It's nice to be able to go and have a refresh after a good few hours walking around (although no need to drop bags as you can leave them at the gate when you enter the zoo if you are staying at the lodge and they are taken to your room for you. The lodge amenities were explained to us and then we were told that the lions would be fed at 5pm and therefore well worth staying around that area for a bit of time. The lodge itself was clean and larger than I had expected. It has an ensuite bathroom (with shower) and a heater (if required, although you are encouraged to have the window open at night if you want the 'full' zoo experience with the noise of the animals). The room doesn't have a TV or wifi, but in my opinion these shouldn't be required. You don't get a lot of time in the lodge as it is and I think it would be a waste to spend what time there is just looking at a screen. There are, however, board games provided in case you want to have one (or as entertainment for the kids!) We were allowed to walk around the zoo ourselves until around 6pm when we were asked to go back to the lodges area and were taken to another area where we were given a welcome drink (either prosecco or orange juice) and an overview of the ZSL and our planned experience that night. The guides were knowledgeable and helpful, they also provided ponchos for those who hadn't prepared for the wet English weather. After the drink we were taken on our first private tour of the zoo. I won't say which animals we went to see, one as I assume they will change the itinerary slightly, each time anyway, but also because it's a nice surprise to see the different areas of the zoo! However what I can say is that the information and delivery of the guys was engaging, and we were given extra experiences by being able to feed some of the animals. After the first tour we went to the restaurant for our evening meal. This was done in a buffet style, but the food was far from 'traditional' buffet and the quality was good. There were two meat options and one vegetarian option, alongside potatoes, vegetables, bread, salad. There was also a dessert and a cheese board to choose from. You were encouraged to go up as many times as you liked and some made use of this! All the food was already included in the price of the stay, but if you wanted any specific drinks (including wine) you had to pay extra. TIP: take some money with you before you go for the welcome drink as you don't go back to the lodges in between the drain, the tour and then the meal - we got caught out. Thankfully we were able to pay by card (contactless) but it was clear that cash was preferred. Prices for the drinks were not extortionate, but were typical for central London, £2.50 for a soft drink, up to £30 for a bottle of wine etc. It was also nice to see that after desserts had been eaten the children were encouraged to go next door and make t-shirts which they could then take home. Not only did it keep them entertained but it gave the parents and grandparents about 20minutes rest to chill out. I think it was a nice touch done by the zoo, even though we couldn't participate! After the meal we were taken for the night time tour. It is an optional tour and you could go back to the lodges instead, but you were encouraged to go on the tour and it is a rare opportunity to see some of the nocturnal animals in a different light - so definitely one to consider. As it was, all our group decided to stay for the tour and I'm glad we did. We visited the aardvarks as part of the tour and did some 'enrichment' with them - making closed boxes of treats which they had to rip open to get the food inside. Lots of fun and just another small insight into he different workings of the zoo. After the torchlight tour you go back to the lodges. We got back around 10pm and it was then pretty much a case of everyone going back to their own lodge and doing as they pleased. There is a small outside seating area with each lodge where you can sit outside, but unfortunately our weather wasn't particularly good so we went to bed instead! We decided not to leave the window open because of the weather and I have to say that, even as a light sleeper, I was only very slightly disturbed by any noise from the animals. My husband slept right through and I only stirred a couple of times - the bed is far too comfy for anything else!! In the morning you are given a wake up call at 7:30am, ready for an 8am leave. We got up a bit early and sat outside drinking hot chocolate on the porch listening to the zoo wake up. Hot chocolate, tea and coffee are all provided free in your room. At 8am you go off to breakfast, again done in a buffet, with PLENTY of food available. There are cooked breakfast and continental breakfast options, and again you are encouraged to go up as often as you like (and even to take elevenses away with you!!) Around 9am we were taken on our final tour of the park before being 'let go' at 10am when the zoo opened to the public and you can spend as long as you like in the zoo. Your bags are again taken to the outgate so no need to lug anything around! Overall, I would say that it is clear the experience is still a fairly new feature at the zoo and perhaps still a couple of teething problems, but we found the guides to be really helpful and informative, the lodges were clean and comfortable and the zoo itself was enjoyable. No matter what your age I think this is a great experience if you have an interest in animals and their conservation. At the end of the day the ZSL is a scientific society, they just happen to have a zoo - the lodges are a way to raise funds to help the conservation of the animals, so you can feel pleased about that good deed alongside your enjoyment too!!

title: Bromwich
text: As a family of 4 adults we have spent the most Amazing time at the Gir lodge and experience. Hannah Nick and Patrick gave us fantastic insight into their important and fascinating roles as well as teaching us much about the lives and habitat of the wonderful animals we were given the privilege to meet. The lodge is superb and the wonderful setting for dinner was delightful. The detail to the structured walking tours brilliant. We heard fantastic sounds of the animals and the cough of the Lions from our lodge,a reminder for the latter, of the power of these awesome animals. I cannot recommend this special experience enough . Wonderful!

title: Unique experience
text: Had a wonderful time with my cousin from Florida. We did not arrive until lateish afternoon due to sightseeing. The hosts were all wonderful, enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the animals. I loved the towels made to look like elephants! We had a twin room, beds were a good size with luxurious cotton covers. Stayed at the Savoy in December, beds as good as there! Dinner and breakfast was very good quality and plenty of choice. Lovely to hear the male lion, sadly he was not loud enough in the night to wake me up! Would love to stay again, maybe when We have lighter nights.

title: Amazing bucket list essential addition!!
text: If you think you know London Zoo think again! Been so many times and then discovered you can stay overnight at the Gir Lodge. What a unique privilege and experience and can't recommend it enough. Private behind the scenes tours after the "tourists" have left with really knowledgeable guides. You get to see nocturnal animals that you would never see during the day and did you know tigers like the smell of turmeric and apparently Chanel No 5? or you get to make up treats and then feed porcupines with nuts wrapped in cardboard boxes? Very comfortable lodges, lovely food, knowledgeable guides, and opportunity to feed some of the animals - what's not to like?!

title: Adults only stay
text: We chose to buy book an adults only stay as a combined birthday/wedding anniversary treat- so between the 9 lodges there were just 18 adults staying the night. We spent the entire day at the zoo before going in to our accommodation at 4.30pm grateful to sit and relax on the verandah with a mug of tea. Our hosts from the zoo were cheerful, friendly and helpful throughout. Only open since May, our lodge was smart and clean and still smelled slightly of new paint. The en suite shower room was supplied with toiletries. There's no tv or wifi, and phone reception was patchy, but that's not a great hardship when you're in the zoo. At 6pm, the zoo closes and the adventure begins with a reception in the Gir Lion Park. The lionesses were much more active than by day. And then a tour of other parts of the zoo. Dinner, included in the cost, was served as a buffet - pay extra for alcohol - and was very tasty. It was served in a room next to the Terrace Restaurant. Then you depart on the the torchlit tour (red torches provided) to see and hear what's happening after dark. As the tawny owl chatted to the Regents Park owls we were delighted to see the aardvarks and porcupines out and about. Worn out, we went to sleep quickly with the flamingoes grunting behind us and failed to hear the lions in the night. We were up early enough to have coffee on the verandah and listen to the zoo waking up for the day. Breakfast was served buffet-style in the Terrace Restaurant and had both cooked and healthy options. And then off for the third and final tour of the zoo. Without the bulk of the visitors, the animals and birds were again much more visible and active. We had taken advantage of the free parking and spent the following day at Whipsnade - cost included in the price if the stay. It was an amazing experience. Not particularly cheap, but you are staying in the heart of London, everything's included and the money is going to a great conservation cause.

title: The best thing we've done in London
text: My husband took me to the Gir Lion Lodge for my birthday. It was the best thing we've done in London since we moved here 7 years ago!! We came straight from work so were one of the last people to arrive at our lodge to check in, but were delighted to be greeted by a welcome drink of prosecco! I don't want to spoil it for others by giving you lots of details about the tours but can give you a flavour of our highlights. - it was such an amazing experience to be part of a private tour of just a dozen people and a guide. Hattie, Jo, and others were so enthusiastic and made the experience so interesting and engaging. We learnt so much about all kinds of animals and it was incredible to have the zoo to ourselves. For example, in the morning we were shown where the brand new baby tiger cubs were being sheltered by their mother. It was hidden from view so quite hard to spot. When the zoo opened, it was amazing to stand and watch her playing with her baby cubs, and the rest of the tourists walked straight past as they didn't know where to look. The night tour was also amazing as it's the only chance to meet some of the nocturnal animals. - the accommodation was very good. I was afraid it would be like a camp site, but it was more like an outside hotel room. Very clean and comfortable with hot water. Also so quiet, considering you're in central London. We slept better than we do at home! - good food. It was amazing to see the transformation of what would ordinarily be a canteen into a dining room with private dining and three course meal. If you like animals, I would highly recommend. It is expensive but we thought worth every penny to have such a close encounter with all kinds of creatures. I'll be back for my next birthday!

title: Overnight stay in the zoo
text: What an amazing experience! The staff who led the out of hours tours were so knowledgeable, friendly and engaging. The evening meal and breakfast were lovely and the lodge cosy. Really recommend doing this trip as it showed the unseen work of what the staff do to enrich the animals lives in the zoo

title: An amazing overnight stay with unique behind the scenes access
text: The team were knowledgeable and helpful, and the lodge cozy - even on a very cold December night. The opportunity to feed the animals was amazing and to see (and hear) the lions vocalize in the dark was breathtaking. We got the BUG house to our self, and an opportunity to see behind the scenes and see rooms you'd never otherwise see. Your donation goes towards your conservation work of the ZSL. It's amazing to be able to stay overnight in the zoo, and being their first thing in the morning before the public arrives is fantastic. We were treated to a hot chocolate as we enjoyed the winter lights at our own pace. All the team were amazing and I can't thank them enough. However food as pretty miserable, and nobody has replied to my email send about a month ago. The food was described in our welcome pack as to be' a delicious 2 course christmas dinner'. This turned out to be in fact some boiled pearl barley, a beef stew (with very little beef) and some rather spicey vegetables. Thank goodness the zoo was open for the light show and we were able to buy hot dogs from a stand. Breakfast the following morning was cold, and the toaster burnt everything that went near it.

title: What A Great Experience
text: We recently stayed for a night in one of the lodges, included was entrance to the Zoo over 2 days, the lodge with dinner bed and breakfast, we also got to walk the Christmas lights which was delightful, we had some behind the scenes experiences, got the Bug House to ourselves and the lions who were good enough to lie down at dusk so we were just on the otherside of the glass, after dinner a talk in the old elephant house and after breakfast a guided tour around several of the animals which included feeding the penguins. Dinner was average and breakfast was good. The staff were excellent and we had a fantastic time in the zoo as I had not been for a while I had forgotten how good it was. We were luck in as much as the weather was cool and a bit damp so the zoo was not at its busiest which for me is a bonus as we were never stuck to see any of the exhibits, all in all a great way to spend a night in london

title: Overnight stay at zoo
text: We had a wonderful weekend at London Zoo. We arrived on Saturday (parking included in price of stay is an excellent bonus) & were able to look around the zoo until 4pm when we checked into our lodge. Yes, it was small (just enough space fora double bed & sofa bed with small en suite shower room) but we only needed it to sleep in so we didn’t need more space. It was beautifully presented. There were 4 of us, 2 adults and 2 children aged 12 & 10. (The only negative was the sofa bed had a hard panel where your feet are when you sleep). The hosts, Viv, Hatty, Joy and Perry were fantastic, they were knowledgeable, great at answering questions from adults and children and made the experience truly memorable despite the rain! The tours were fun and informative. The food, dinner and breakfast, were delicious and plentiful. It was a truly special weekend, one that will become a family memory to be treasured.

title: Exceeded all expectations
text: My husband and I took 8 year old grandson and his friend. This was an amazing experience - the zookeepers who took us on the tours were knowledgeable, engaging and completely attentive to everyone from children to adults. Lodge was spotless if a little ‘bijou’ but you only spend the night there and you have everything you need - heard the lions roaring in the night (scary). This was truly an amazing experience - don’t know what we will do next to equal this experience - my grandson has already asked to go back!

title: Amazing experience
text: This was booked as a birthday gift and it was amazing. The whole experience was above expectations, the facilities were great and the staff were amazing. Excellent value for money and worth what we paid. Perfect gift for any budding vet/zoologist.

title: Fantastic overnight experience
text: We spent a night in the lodges, next to the lion enclosure. The lodges are comfortable with everything you need for your stay, but the main attraction is the zoo, and the insider experience you are given. We arrived around 11:30 to spend the day at the zoo

title: This overnight experience is amazing !!!!
text: I bought the experience for my daughters Birthday - we booked an evening when it was for adults only. We got to go round ZSL all day on the Saturday - which was fabulous in itself despite the rain. We went in to our lodge at 4.30pm - the lodge was lovely , adequate for a nights stayover and in keeping with the lion theme. We were only yards away from the lion enclosure. At 5.30pm we got to look around the zoo with hosts who were enthusiastic and informative - it was good to do things that you couldn’t do on a normal visit to the zoo. We had a delicious 2 course meal in the restaurant. And then out in the dark for another trip round some of the animals and for some of the zoo secrets. At 10pm we got back to our lodges - and spent a comfortable night . We were woken at 7.30am - to be ready for breakfast at 8. After breakfast - with the hosts again we got to go round the zoo before it opened to the public. Again, doing things ie: feeding penguins, etc. At 10am - we were left to our own devices to either go round ZSL again or you go off to Whipsnade for the day. This experience was far better than I could have ever expected - simply amazing. I would recommend to anyone.

title: A brilliant birthday treat
text: So, what does a 70year old want for his birthday? When I saw an article about the Gir lodges, I knew I had found the perfect present. And it was perfect on every level. First and foremost, the staff team at the zoo were just wonderful - friendly, informative and attentive. Other people have outlined the programme and commented on the lodges but we found the tours after hours and first thing in the morning very interesting and we saw nocturnal animals after dark that the general public would not see. The tours included information about the history and architecture of the zoo. (I had no idea there were so many listed buildings on the site) The lodge was basic but that's what we expected and its informality was charming. If you left your window open, you could hear the lions close by! The deal includes free parking next to the entrance and a two day pass to include Whipsnade. A couple of people in our group went on to Whipsnade the second day - it would be about an hours easy drive out of London. Would certainly recommend this very unusual experience

title: Spend the night with the lions!
text: ZSL London Zoo offers adorable bungalows about 100 feet from the lion enclosure and an overnight stay at the zoo. The event begins with an introduction to the lions and continues to a look at the zoo as it closes for the evening. Then it's on to dinner at the zoo restaurant. The food was good and it's a chance to talk more with your hosts for the night. Our hosts were Perry, Nick and Hattie. After dinner, it's another look at the animals, this time including a look at one of the zoo kitchens to prepare an enrichment activity for one of the animals and then a night time tour including getting to give the animals the enrichment you just made. We got to offer nut-stuffed toys for the porcupines and then watch them through night vision cameras as they hunted down their treats. Finally it was back to the lodges to say good night to the lions, knowing they were merely feet a way through the glass. The next morning breakfast is at 7 and then there's another tour of the zoo before it opens for the day. We got to help feed the penguins, do more enrichment (this time with the mongooses) and talk to some of the zookeepers, including Joseph, who told us all about the komodo dragon. The pricing is very reasonable when you realize it includes two days at the London Zoo or Whipsnade Zoo, accommodations and two meals and the experience is unforgettable.

title: Unique experiance sleeping in London zoo
text: I haven't been to London zoo for many years .There have been big changes for the good. you have 2 days and 1 night to explore .Check the map out before you go. 3 small guided tours the staff are great

title: Gir Lodge London Zoo Experience - brilliant!!!
text: Just returned from overnight stay at Gir Lodge in London Zoo. Bought for my husband’s 60th and it was absolutely brilliant! Arrived on first day and left bags with security which were then taken to lodge so we were free to walk round Zoo. Met at lodges and then taken for introductory talk with staff guides with a glass on prosecco. Had 2 evening tours after Zoo closed which was great plus another one after breakfast before Zoo opened. Saw animals up close and even fed some too. Hatty, Nick and Perry looked after us and were brilliant, making our stay really special and memorable. Big thank you to them all! Dinner was really good too and better than we had expected with lovely full breakfast in morning. It was fantastic to see behind the scenes and get up close to the animals. Would definitely recommend to anyone wanting to have a completely different and amazing experience. Worth every penny!

title: What a fabulous night
text: Had an amazing night. Highly recommend this experience to everyone. Lodge very clean and has everything you need for an overnight stay. Loved the guided tours. Big shout out for Vivienne and Joy. Very knowledgeable and enthusiastic. Evening meal and breakfast both lovely. A real privilege to be in the zoo, when it's closed to the public.

title: Fantastic night at the zoo
text: My son proposed to his girlfriend at London Zoo last week and 14 members of both families stayed in the Gir Lion Lodges overnight. The whole thing was a surprise for his girlfriend and the staff did everything they could to make it an incredibly special occasion. The lodges were delightful

title: Once in a lifetime!
text: I was lucky enough to be gifted this experience by a lovely friend. To be honest I didn’t really know what to expect but what an incredible experience. We spent a day in the zoo, checked into the lodge at 4.30 followed by an out of hours tour by Perry and Mary. They were so knowledgable and so passionate about their jobs, they did such a good job of showing us around! Thank you! We then went for a lovely dinner with the rest of the guests which was delicious (drinks were rather pricey though!). Once dark we went exploring again but this time with night vision, so much fun! We then went to prepare some of the animals breakfast and saw some behind the scenes areas, again, very interesting. The next morning we woke up and had a big breakfast. We then got another informative tour and the chance to feed the penguins their breakfast. By the second day we felt like ZSL experts and enjoyed another day at the zoo. The lodge had everything we needed including a very comfy bed! Highly recommend this to anyone who is lucky enough to get the chance!

title: A bit of Africa...
text: A great experience from start to finish. Check in to your lodge was at 4.30pm but you could arrive at the zoo from 10 am that day and wander at your leisure. Free to do what you wanted until 6pm when we met with Joy, Nick and Mary. A welcome drink and a tour of the land of the lions followed. Our 3 hosts were very informative and very friendly, it was obvious from the start that they are passionate about their animals. At 7.45pm we headed for dinner, the buffet was delicious and plentiful. A selection of alcohol/soft drinks were available to purchase. Nick and Mary sat with us and chatted about their work and took interest in what brought us all to the overnight experience. At 9pm, it was explained to us what was going to happen on our night time tour ( I don't want to spoil but it is safe to say it was 'hands on') Back in our lodges by 10pm, listening to the animals as they began to settle down for the night. The lodges had everything you needed - heater, fan, tea & coffee facilities, hairdryer, towels, soap and the beds were so comfy and warm. Checkout/breakfast was 8am, good choice for breakfast including hot full English breakfast. Last tour was 9-10am. You could stay all day in the zoo or head to Whipsnade (included in the price). A very enjoyable experience.

title: Really really good treat
text: OK , first off don't expect lap of luxury , what you get is a cute Wendy house type chalet which is well decorated and comfortable with ensuite facilities . You are kept active and after checking in go out on a tour with the most enthusiastic and knowledgeable guides. Watching the lions close up and at near dusk was just brilliant !. Then after a great dinner which is buffet but good quality you are on tour again and get a great treat with some of the more nocturnal animals. Don't expect a great sleep , nothing to do with the bed but if you do as recommended and leave a window open you will be woken by the Lions at 2 am who are calling to each other , a fantastic sound. After breakfast another tour and we were lucky to see the Tiger cubs at play plus the Gorillas before the crowds came Not a cheap treat , but a great one.

title: Excellent for a special occasion
text: We had a marvellous time at the Gir Lion Lodge. The tours of the zoo when closed were really very special. The food was excellent and all the staff, without exception, were absolutely charming. We have come away with such a different impression of zoos compared to 30 years ago.

title: A really enjoyable and educational experience
text: I went with my daughter and two grandsons aged 10 and 6. We arrived at about 3 p.m. and were pleased to be able to leave our bags in the lockup there so that we could look round unencumbered and know that they would be delivered to our lodge at no extra cost. We started the experience proper with a glass of prosecco and a very interesting tour before dinner. Our guides were young and passionate about the conservation work of the zoo. Dinner was leisurely and there was a special kids' menu so everyone was happy. It was fascinating to go on a twilight tour to see some of the animals who are usually asleep during the day, such as the big cats. We learnt about the enrichment programmes where the animals have to work for their food as in the wild, and the children loved hiding pellets for the porcupines in cardboard boxes. Then we went to where the food was prepared and looked at the various feeding charts. The lodge was comfortable with everything we needed and in the early morning, all the adults heard the lions coughing, while the children slept on oblivious. We had an early breakfast and a final tour, which included some more interesting facts and a chance to feed th penguins and admire the antics of an extremely extrovert gibbon. By this time it was raining steadily and we were all offered ponchos. The children were so enthralled by what they had been told that they immediately wanted to revisit the animals and we ended up spending most of the day there, despite the weather. Overall, a really worthwhile experience, so a big thank you to all our enthusiastic and knowledgeable guides!

title: Great staff
text: We stayed with our grandchildren aged 5 and 8 and we all loved the experience. What made it extra good were the enthusiastic and knowledgeable staff who ran the out of hours tours. They really were fantastic and it felt really special to be in the zoo when the day visitors had left . We were impressed with the evening meal and breakfast as the quality and quantity were better than expected . The evening meal was particularly enjoyable and the children all decorated t shirts with the staff which allowed the adults to have a leisurely end to their meal. Unfortunately we were unable to spend the second day enjoying the zoo as it was torrential rain but that is the English weather for you. If you can spend both days looking round the zoo it is well worth the money when you take everything else you get into account .

title: Really special
text: Just wonderful, my 7 year old daughter and I had been looking forward to this for months and it didn’t disappoint. It was pretty magical to be honest. Staff were exceptional, access was incredible and the accommodation was better than I imagined. It’s no 5 star hotel, but it was really nice and a proper ‘glamping’ on steroids feel. For my daughter and I to have a special bonding experience it was the best money I have ever spent. Recommend very highly.

title: Surpassed Expectations
text: We stayed in the Gir Lion Lodges on Good Friday (30 March). Our visit was to celebrate our 10th wedding anniversary (we had had our wedding reception at another zoo), but because we're now parents, we stayed on a family night. The night we stayed there were 2 lodges with only adults and the other lodges had 1 child each. All of the children were very well behaved and asked interesting questions on the tours. The hosts did a great job of giving the children attention, but also not forgetting the adults. We were able to ask questions and get in-depth answers too. The whole experience was AMAZING. It surpassed our expectations. We learned so much about the animals, but also how the zoo (and zoos in general) operate and work, all of ZSL's hard work toward animal enrichment and conservation, of course. It was really clear that the staff love the animals. The day of our arrival we attended some of the animal talks during regular hours. Then we visited some of the same animals on the special tours and WOW: both were good, but what you get from the Gir Lion Lodge experience is a completely different level. It's like how a medical doctor might explain an illness to a patient, versus how he/she might explain it to a colleague. It was great to be able to make that comparison and know that we really got something extra. The weekend we came it was raining very hard for most of the day when the zoo was open (but happily dry for our tours). We were already foot sore by 4:00 so it was great to check into the lodges for a break. Our torchlight tour included making enrichment items for two different animals and that allowed us to see some of the "staff only" areas in the zoo. I don't know if this is the normal routine or if the staff improvised because it had been cold and rainy and the animals might have been taking more shelter. We also did our proseco at 6pm instead of when we checked into the lodges. This experience is does cost a fair amount of money and the staff and hosts seemed to respect that. Our dinner was in a side room of the Terrance Restaurant (not where it usually is). The food was delicious and there were plenty (it was a buffet). I didn't expect this, but they did ask each family if they wanted something different for their children. Our son ate the adult food so I don't know how good the children's food was, but everyone seemed happy. The atmosphere was great (nice lighting, tablecloths). The next morning our breakfast was also very tasty and there was plenty. We were even offered additional coffee to go. (Also in the Terrance Restaurant there is a station to re-fill water bottles). Some reviewers have complained about the price of the food at the zoo, but I expect food at places like this to be the same price I might pay for hot food from a family-friendly chain restaurant and those are the kind of prices we had. The prices we paid and portion sizes for our lunches (not during the experience time) seemed reasonable to me. The lodge itself was comfortable, warm and clean. The sofa pulls out into a bed, but it is a little "backwards" that the pillow is supposed to go on the end away from the back of the sofa. Our son was 6, so about 115cm and was very comfortable. The ensuite was also very clean. We used the kettle as well and that worked nicely. We tried to use the chairs in the little outdoor area after our son was asleep, but the night was too cold to last long. (We booked before a half-term break so our child could stay up late and then get back to regular bedtime before school resumed. Some families did not participate in the night tour.) In the morning I discovered that flamingos are loud! So are gibbons! And we did hear some lion coughing before we fell asleep. Who else can say "I know what lions sound like at night"? All three of us continue to talk about this months later. Our 6yo son has remembered so many details about the animals. I fondly recall being able to touch special items I wouldn't have touched before. And we all learned so much I have been recommending this to so many friends, family and colleagues. We loved it so much that we booked to do the Lookout Lodge at Whipsnade next week!

title: If you love animals give this a go!
text: Stayed here on New Years Eve 2016 with my husband and daughter, we had an amazing time! Lodges are very cute, warm and cosy (sofabed and shower not so great but I've given this feedback so hopefully they will improve) with the beds being really comfy. But you're staying here to see behind the scenes at the Zoo and have a much more personal engagement/view of the animals. Particularly good for seeing the nocturnal animals as clearly they are out and about during th twilight tour. Also you get to see other animals, e.g. lions and tigers, at the 'right'times so we were able to see the tiger family at play just after their breakfast (and before the Zoo is open) and as the Lodges are in the Land of the Lions you say them pretty much all the time. The staff were excellent, really engaging and charming, they couldn't do enough to make your stay enjoyable. Really lovely touches too such as games for the children and cups of hot chocolate to take on your twilight tour. We've been to London Zoo many times but this trip gives you a much more involved and personal view of both the animals and how the Zoo operates. We'd all highly recommend this trip.

title: Great Experience
text: Wonderful night spent at the lodges. Our hosts Hannah, Mary and Perry were exceptional. The lodges are basic but comfortable and had fans which were a godsend as the heat was ridiculous! Dinner and breakfast plentiful and good quality. The after zoo hours/pre zoo opening experiences not to be missed. Thoroughly enjoyed every minute

title: A unique and tremendous experience!!
text: As many of these reviews have already identified, this is an amazing experience!! The tours are just awesome and unique. The staff are so lovely and passionate, sharing their knowledge and insight of the animals. The evening meal and breakfast were delicious and plentiful, whilst providing a good opportunity for socialising and chatting with other guests, as well as the staff. Again the staff are just terrific, supportive and friendly, assisting with special requests and engaging in general chitchat. We adored our visit and have memories that will last a lifetime.

title: Great stay at Gir Lion Lodge
text: My mum and I stayed at Gir Lion Lodge for 1 night on Sunday 10 July, and thoroughly enjoyed it, Arrival: you can arrive at any time on the day your experience starts. Bags can be left with security (the gate is to the right of the member's only entrance (look for the driveway)), and then taken to the lodge for you. The experience started at 5pm, with a glass of prosecco at the terrace restaurant

title: Special out of hours zoo experience
text: Wow! This trip was incredible and worth every penny. I booked it for my partners 50th as a surprise and he was thrilled...as was I. The hosts are very welcoming and knowledgeable too and their passion for the animals is obvious. We had three private tours after all the guests had gone and it was so quiet except for the animal noises including the lions, gibbons and peacocks! We had access to the kitchens where they organise and prepare the food and learnt about the enrichment techniques they use and the breeding/conservation programmes. We even got to feed some of the animals and each tour showed us something different. You won't be going there for a rest as there is a fair bit of walking involved and an early start, but tours are optional. I was really impressed with the dinner and breakfast provided...really high standard of food and service too. The lodges were perfect, functional and clean too and in a lovely setting right in the heart of the zoo next to the lions. Ideal for 2 but a squash with kids too I would imagine. Mel, Nick and Joy were entertaining and so knowledgeable it was a pleasure to listen to them and we learnt so much. It was an unforgettable experience and recommend to all.

title: Amazing experience
text: My daughter's and I stayed in the lodges in the land of the Lions area of London Zoo. It might look expensive at first but you can spend all say at the Zoo before going to the lodge then the next day up until the Zoo closes and you get free parking. Although you cant can't leave the zoo and come back. Lodges were clean and comfortable with tea and coffee provided. Beds really comfy with crisp white sheets and a duvet. There was even a elephant made of towels when we arrived. I stayed in the leopard lodge which is disabled accessible, two twin beds and a very large wet room. If you bring a carer with you they stay for free. My other daughter stayed in the lodge next to us which had two twin beds and a fold down sofa bed so ideal for families. Previous reviews said the shower and toilet were small but she didn't have any problem There are 9 lodges in total want a smaller lodge for the member of staff that is on hand through the night. If you have mobility issues you can reserve a wheelchair, highly recommended as there's a lot of walking. When you arrive at the lodge there is a welcome drink at 6pm then a tour.the zoo is now closed to visitors so there's only you and the other people staying in the lodges. There are 3 tours a torchlight one after dinner where you go behind the scenes and a final tour after breakfast. During the tours there are opportunities to feed the some of the animals Meals are served in the Terrace Restaurant and are buffet style. You have to purchase drinks which seemed expensive but water is available. There is a no alcohol policy outside of the restaurant. Our guides Mel, Jo and Nick where friendly, helpful and very knowledge Due to the heat the lions stayed in their quiet area but we did get to see them. Previous reviews said they were woken around 3am by the male lion he didn't wake us it was the very vocal male peacock that served as our morning alarm. It was lovely to sit out on the veranda and listen to the gibbons calling to each other. Breakfast is early but then you get to see the popular areas like the penguins before the Zoo opens at 10. Would love to go again in the winter.

title: Amazing After Hours Zoo Experience
text: This is an absolutely fantastic experience for anyone who loves zoo's and animals. The price is expensive, but worth it for for such a unique opportunity to see the zoo after it has closed to the public. We spent the day looking round the zoo as normal. At 16.30 we went to the Gir Lion Lodge in the centre of the zoo. We were welcomed by three keepers who would be showing us round the zoo during the evening and the following morning. The accommodation was very comfy and clean. It has everything you would expect in a small hotel room such as en-suite, tea and coffee etc. At 18.00 the tour begins outside the lion enclosure. A lot of the experience depends on the animals themselves. The lions were mostly sleeping in the evening so we moved on to the camels. There are lots of opportunities to feed the animals during the experience. The keepers showing us round were extremely knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the animals and the conservation work the zoo does around the world. They offered all sorts of information and stories. The food was great. The evening meal consisted of a buffet with meat and veggie options. Alcoholic drinks are available but are quite expensive (4.50 for a beer). Breakfast was also very good with a buffet including full English and continental options. The absolute best part of the trip is the animals themselves. It's impossible to see all of the animals during the tours, but we learned so much about the ones we did see.

title: AMAZING EXPERIENCE
text: Our visit to the zoo could not have been better. Included in the price was....free parking, entry to the zoo, evening meal, breakfast, three guided tours when the zoo is closed to the public and cosy comfortable accommodation in a delightful little lodge only a few yards from the lion's enclosure. The three girls that met and greeted us , a,d guided us through the various enclosures were fantastic. Very personable, very attractive and very knowledgable too.

title: Lovely enthusiastic staff, but all in all, a disappointing experience
text: We recently stayed overnight in ZSL London Zoo, in the Land of the Lions, in a Gir Lion lodge. Our fist impression was that the lodge area itself, is very poorly signposted within the zoo. We were greeted by the staff hosts who were wonderfully friendly and helpful. We were shown to our individual lodges at 4:30, where we were given time to unpack and freshen up before beginning our zoo tour at 5:30. When I say lodge however, I am afraid I have to use the term loosely. To be fair it was more of a large 'Wendy' house. Time to unpack, would have been helpful, had there been any room TOO unpack, or anywhere other than two hooks on the wall to hang anything on. Our twin room had beds so tiny, that my husbands feet dangled from the bottom. They were also quite narrow, although the bedding was soft and comfortable. There was a small kettle and a selection of tea bags/coffee etc. The bathroom had a sink, toilet and shower. However there was no running hot water in the sink, and the shower (if you were small enough to be able to actually fit through the shower door) went from the extreme of freezing cold to scalding hot every 10 seconds during your shower. At 5:30 were met our fellow 'campers', had a glass of prossecco and a began our tour. The zoo closes to the public at 5:30, so there was only us and the staff there. We had expected a tour of the majority of the zoo, but were disappointed to learn that we would no be having a tour of the bigger exhibits. So no gorillas

title: The most amazing Birthday present!
text: I was bought this gift for my birthday and stayed on the 7th June 2018. To say this is a ‘tour’ or a ‘private stay’ is a gross understatement! This was a once in a lifetime experience. The staff who managed the experience were passionate, energetic, engaging and made you feel that you were being introduced to members of their family. You may decide after reading this review, to read some others. A popular theme seems to be the accommodation. If you are looking for 5* accommodation that has a mini bar full of champagne then this isn’t for you. If you want to stay somewhere which is in the middle of London Zoo (take a minute for that realisation to hit you, you are inside London Zoo when nobody else is there!) and want to stay in comfortable accommodation (with lion bodyguard) which is great value for money, then I highly recommend this experience. The only fault I can find with the entire experience is that you have to adjust to other visitors being there when the park reopens at 10am. I will be honest, I really enjoyed having my own private Zoo experience!

title: Amazing, lodge plus Zoo lates adult only
text: I can’t rate the whole experience enough! We visited on Friday 1st June, mooched around the zoo then checked in at 4:30pm to the lodges within the gir lion area of the zoo. Superbly clean & well maintained summer house style lodge, comfy bed, pillows, sofa, ensuite, tea/coffe & water plus towels & hairdryer. Main zoo closes at 5 then we got a tour until 6, went to the zoo lates adult only where there we at my best guess 25+ food/sweet stalls to choose from. We were given 4x £10 vouchers between the two of us, I’ll review the zoo lates separate. We got to feed the giraffes inside thier overnight enclosure/building & the bearded pigs. After zoo lates we went by torch light & fed the porcupines. In the morning we had a wake up call at 7:30 then buffet all you can eat Brekkie at 8. From about 9-10 we had another tour that covered several animals & more feeding plus some behind the scenes bits. The zoo then opened to public again at 10. Totally worth it! A* 5 stars. I believe the usual family version of this is similar but a meal in the terrace restaurant which one of our group had done & said was also good. Any questions please ask x

title: A perfect experience
text: This is a perfect experience for anyone that loves animals....the lodges are very comfortable and well equipped and your staying right next to the lion inclosure...only had a slight problem finding the lodges as it wasn't sign posted. The hosts were fun and had lots of knowledge about the animals. You get to fed some of the animals and also go behind the sciences.Dinner was ok but no variety hope you like Chicken. Fully cooked breakfast in the morning with another tour before the public come in....which is fun seeing the zoo come alive with the sounds of the animals.....perfect

title: Lovely visit
text: The lodge is very tiny and adequate

title: Expensive but worth it
text: We arrived at the zoo at 10am and gained entry through the East Service gate where our overnight cases were left with a security guard. Entry through this entrance avoided the queue at the main zoo entrance. Our luggage was taken to our lodge later that day and was there when we checked into the lodge at 4pm. We spent the day looking around the zoo. The lodges are attractively painted and situated within a small compound within the lion enclosure. The lodges are small but are immaculate. Our lodge had 2 single beds, a bed settee (children said that this was not comfortable), en suite (with toiletries), teas, coffees, hot chocolate, towels and a hairdryer. After we checked into the lodge (4pm), we were left to our own devices until 6pm, although you could not leave the lion enclosure. During this time, we were offered a glass of prosecco and orange or apple juice for the children. At 6pm, we had our first tour of the zoo. We saw the Pygmy hippo having food as they fed him for us and we could see him through the night vision googles that they provided us. We also saw the fruit bats, tortoises and otters. We were then taken to the restaurant for our evening meal and it was buffet style. The choice was pot roasted chicken, grilled squash with chickpea and roasted leg of lamb. There was also a selection of vegetables. For dessert, it was Eton Mess or cheese and biscuits. Water is provided but other drinks have to be paid for. We had 2 soft drinks, small glass of white wine and a small bottle of beer and it was £15.50. After the meal, we had another tour of the zoo, where we fed the porcupines and aardvarks. We were back in the lodge just before 10pm. Due to visiting in December, we left the heater on in the lodge whilst we were out in the evening. On our return, the lodge was lovely and warm. In fact, we had to turn the heater off for the rest of the night as it was too hot and this was with the window slightly open so we could hear the lions during the night. We heard the lions from about 6am. At 8am, you need to be checked out of the lodge for breakfast. Luggage is given to the hosts and this is taken back to the gate and locked up securely, ready for collection when you want to leave. Breakfast was a selection of cereals, fruit, pastries, juices, toast, bacon, sausage, scrambled egg, bacon, tomorrow's, baked beans and mushrooms. There was also a selection of hot drinks. After breakfast, we had another tour before the zoo opened to the public. We saw the penguins. We were then took to an area behind the scenes where they prepare the food for the primates. It was amazing seeing the 'menus' and all the food. We then spent some time at the tiger enclosure watching the tiger cubs playing. We left when the zoo opened to go to ZSL Whipsnade.

title: A most wonderful birthday present
text: I have just come back from spending a night at the GIR Lion lodges and can’t praise the whole experience highly enough The lodges are lovely - we stayed in Sunbird. Twin beds, separate bathroom with shower, tea making facilities and a fantastic view. Laying in bed hearing lions chatting is amazing!! The London Zoo keepers who were our hosts were amazing! Such lovely people and brilliant knowledge about the animals we saw. We were able to leave our bags when we arrived so we could immediately walk round the zoo until we were able to get in to our lodge at 4.30. Once we had a welcome meet up with our group and the lovely keepers who were our hosts, we then had a complimentary glass of Prosecco while we walked around the area that was set out to represent a street in Gujarat - very well done! Once the zoo closed at 6pm we went on a tour hearing all about the beautiful lion/lionesses as well as many others such as the gorgeous penguins, camels, Komodo dragon, my favourites the pigs 💗 We were able to help feed the pigs 🐷 and the camels We then had dinner - a buffet style meal which was lovely! There were 16 in our group and we were very lucky to have a great group to share the experience with. You pay extra for your drinks After dinner there was another tour which I didn’t do as my poor feet were in need of a rest 😊 I think you got to go behind the scenes in the food preparation area to see how that worked and helped prepare a meal for the pigs breakfast After a very good nights sleep hearing wonderful noises of the zoo while you rested - we met for breakfast at 8am. You had lots of choice - cooked breakfast, muffins, croissants, cereal. After breakfast we were heading off on another tour before the zoo opened at 10am. It is such a privilege to be able to walk round the zoo and see the animals without other members of the public being there and once again I want to praise the zoo keepers - wonderful and so knowledgeable At 10am the tour ended but we were able to enjoy another day at the zoo Overall highly recommend this experience!

title: Amazing experience
text: We visited as part of a larger group and had booked four lodges. We gained access to the lodge at 4.30pm. It is not that easy to find the lodges as there is no signposting to them and we were not given any instructions when we arrived at the zoo. The cabins are small but nice and clean (except the shower head but more about that later). There is a double bed, a small sofa and a compact shower room. There is WiFi access as well. We noticed that the shower head had mouldy on it and was overall disgusting. We mentioned it to one of the hosts who came straight over and cleaned it. The experience started at 6pm with a glass of fizzy wine and juice for the children. We were given a guided tour and a chance to provide enrichment for the porcupines before dinner. Dinner was plentiful and buffet style. There was another tour after dinner with a chance to get a look behind the scenes. The tour ended around 10pm and we went back to the lodges. We met at 8am the following morning for a walk over to the breakfast buffet. Another private tour followed after breakfast and we had the opportunity to provide the enrichments we had prepared the following night to the bearded pigs. We had an excellent time and would recommend it for both families and couples who want to get a look behind the scenes at ZSL London Zoo. It is not cheap at first sight but considering free overnight parking, entrance to the zoo for two days, three private tours, two course dinner buffet, staying overnight in a lodge and breakfast makes it very good value indeed. Plus you make a contribution to the work and research at ZSL London Zoo.

title: Brilliant Experience
text: Had an amazing time staying at Gir Lodge at London Zoo. Great staff with so much knowledge. Excellent breakfast. Nice lodges, staff keep them heated for you especially if the days/nights are cold. Was amazing to hear the lions roar during the night.

title: Got lion lodge
text: Just got home from gir lion lodge at London zoo what a wonderful experience the lodges are clean and warm just right for an overnight stay at the zoo all the staff are fantastic and very knowledgeable can't say enough about it just 10 out of 10 thank you

title: What an experience!
text: Myself and seven friends have just returned from a weekend at London Zoo and a nights stay at Gir Lion Lodge. What an experience! From the moment you arrive the team at the main entrance make sure you can leave your luggage and have as much time as possible exploring the zoo. Check in at Gir Lodge is 4:30pm upon which we were given a little bit of time to settle in and warm up - we happened to be staying on a weekend when it snowed. The lodges are immaculate - clean, tidy and although small, have everything you need for a night’s stay. A glass of prosecco marked the start of our experience and a trip to see the Lions. This was then followed by an amazing dinner (the food, hosts and atmosphere was really impressive), a visit to the camels and some tours back of house. The knowledge and passion of the team is incredible. I believe tours can vary a little depending on time of year, the animals etc which is understandable so our tour finished at 9:30pm. It was also snowing and we were all extremely cold so I think everyone quite welcomed going back to our warm lodges and settling in for the night. The following morning after breakfast we had another tour (before the park officially opened) visiting the tigers and penguins, as well as a few other animals and reptiles along the way. Then we were left to continue our day. Highlights: when else do you get to sleep in a zoo??! The team only add to this experience with their knowledge and passion. And the food, simply wonderful. Great evening meal and fabulous breakfast the following day. Generous amounts of food and a good quality and selection. Wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this experience.

title: Amazing experience in London
text: I had booked the Adults Night experience for my fiancé’s 32nd Birthday and it was truly amazing. The lodges are really warm, comfortable and clean, the dinner and breakfast provided was delicious and the guides were lovely- super enthusiastic and really knowledgable. We were greeted with a glass of prosecco on arrival and then after the zoo had closed got to go behind the scenes to see how some parts of the zoo work as well as put together some breakfast and entertainment for the animals and hear about the conservation work ZSL take part in. Would recommend as an alternative overnight in London. 🦁

title: Excellent night at the Zoo
text: Everything we could have wanted and more. The hosts for the evening and morning were amazing and very knowledgeable about the Zoo, the Animals and ZSL in general. Getting to spend time in the Zoo after hours is an amazing experience and slightly odd when walking around in the Dark. You soon forget your are in London.

title: WOW - an amazing adventure
text: My 6 year old son and I stayed on a family night (the same as the adults only but children are allowed to stay as well). This was an amazing trip and I think great value for money. We arrived at the zoo around 1130am and entered quickly through a side entrance where we got to leave our bags. We parked in the car park which is just across the road and easy to find. We thoroughly enjoyed our day at the zoo and then checked into our lodge at 430pm (and warmed up as a very chilly day!) and our bags were there waiting for us. The tours, guides, staff and experience were amazing. The food was delicious (there is a kids option so ask about that as it wasn't made clear when booking) and extra activities which we weren't expecting like t-shirt designing for the children and making enrichment for the animals. The shower was a little slow but who cares when you are sleeping feet away from lions and get woken up by their roars! The lodge was clean, comfortable and warm. The evening meal was nice, only one main option and one option veggie, but I enjoyed it all. Breakfast was delicious. I can't recommend this trip enough and will definitely be staying again if I can. Wrap up warm if you go in the winter- take a camera- enjoy!

title: Best Thing to Do in London
text: This is one of the best things I've ever done on a trip. The staff, Hattie, Joy and Laura, were AMAZING and so fun. During the tours at night and the next morning, they gave us insights into the lions and other animals, their personalities and behaviors and inside scoop on what they are really like. Nothing a regular visitor to the Zoo would ever get to learn. They told some wonderful stories about the lions and tigers and others that made me want to stay and learn more and brought me closer to the animals in a unique way and made the experience ever more special. The meals were very good too as were the cottages. If you have 1 night to spend in London, spend it with the lions of the Gir Lion Lodge.

title: Enjoyable
text: I agree with the mainly positive reviews of this experience. My wife and I stayed on an adults only night and as there were only 8 of us, it made the experience intimate and nicely manageable. The whole thing is well organised. We arrived at the zoo at about 3pm and gained admittance through the East Service gate where our overnight case was left with a security guard and which was waiting for us when we later entered our lodge. As we had time to kill before check in, we had a stroll through the zoo which in winter closes at 4pm which is also check in time for the lodges. At about 4.10pm I had a call on my mobile from one of the Gir team (as our overnight case had been delivered by security, the team obviously knew we were somewhere in the zoo) concerned as to our whereabouts as we had not yet checked in. Good customer care. The lodges are attractively painted and situated within a small compound adjacent to the lion enclosure and designed to replicate an Indian village, the lions being Asiatic as opposed to African. It is true that the lodges are on the small side and can best be described as functional. They are clean and bright, en suite, with soaps, body wash, shampoo, lotions etc, different variety of teas, coffee and biscuits. Our lodge was called Oriole and was set back and accessed over a small wooden bridge which led to a small veranda with tables and chairs. Very charming. The young girls who looked after us in the evening and the morning were extremely engaging and pleasant and were perfect hosts. They were full of enthusiasm and clearly enjoyed what they were doing. After being shown to our lodge we met up for a safety talk and then had a glass of prosecco whilst watching the three lionesses curl up next to each other on a warm spot in the enclosure. Wonderful. We then set off on a guided tour for about an hour before arriving at the main restaurant where we had dinner in a private room. The food was acceptable, not great but ok. Drinks were available to buy. After dinner we had another guided tour of nocturnal animals which was quite a treat. We were shown back to our lodge about 10pm where you are "locked" in for the night or at least within the confines of the compound. For obvious reasons you are not allowed to wander unaccompanied around the zoo at night. Also, for similar reasons, no alcohol is allowed within the lodges. Sleep was comfortable enough and from time to time in the early hours we could hear the lions roaring their exchanges. We had to vacate the lodge by 8am and made our way to breakfast in the main restaurant where there was a varied selection of hot and cold food. After breakfast and before the zoo opens to other visitors, we were taken on a final guided tour and were entertained by the penguins and caught a glimpse of two tiger cubs and their mother. After this my wife and I made our own way around the zoo for a couple of hours before taking a short cut to the East Service gate to collect our case and head home. We thoroughly enjoyed this experience.

title: So much fun!!!
text: My stay at the Gir Lion Lodge surpassed all my expectations. Exploring the zoo at night was so nice, quiet, and being taught all about the animals by the guide was so interesting. Also got to get involved with feeding/ enrichment activities for the animals which was good fun. Dinner was lovely (i had the veggie option), buffet style and plenty of it. The actual lodge was small, but really cosy, spotlessly clean and had everything you needed. Very comfy bed! Again, the morning activities were really fun and interesting. Special shout out to Hattie and Kerry who were great hosts! Really different experience, would highly recommend - for all ages! :-)

title: A real treat for animal lovers
text: My wife and I had the pleasures of staying here on 4/11. The lodges were simple but very comfortable supplying everything needed in terms of towels, toiletries, refreshments etc. Considering how cold it was they were warm and cosy Our hosts were friendly and knowledgeable and ensured everyone had a good time. We arrived around 4pm and had a tour before dinner and another after dinner. Having the zoo to ourselves after dark was truly memorable and feeding some of the nocturnal animals was great fun A good night’s sleep was broken in the morning to the sound of the lions coughing (sounds like a steam train and has to be heard). A hearty breakfast was followed by another private tour before the zoo opened to the public Definitely recommend to anyone who likes animals and wants to learn more about them without having to contest with a multitude of families with children who have little interest in the animals themselves

title: Amazing and unique experience
text: Our visit was part of my husband's 40th birthday celebrations and it was fantastic. The zoo keepers made this amazing experience, they are so knowledgeable and passionate about the animals and it was really a privilege to learn from their expertise. We found the lodge to be small but perfectly formed - the reality is that you only sleep in it as the schedule is rather busy so you don't need anything bigger. The bathroom was immaculately clean and we enjoyed hot showers. We found both meals to be really tasty and there was a huge choice of breakfast items so something for everyone. Eating with the zoo keepers and host was also great, we loved hearing their stories and they were very helpful in addressing some of our questions. This was a key part of the experience for us. Yes, the price is a lot of money but you simply can't compare it against hotel rooms at a similar price-point - you are paying for the experience. We liked the fact that the money we pay goes to conservation projects. If you have a special occasion coming up I would definitely recommend this.

title: Amazing experience, birthday with lions.
text: Anyone who is remotely interested in animals could not fail to love this experience. Informative, joyous and entertaining. The hosts are wonderful, there knowledge boundless. The whole thing excellent. The lodges are pristine and comfortable. The great work the zoo is doing here and around the world is shared with you in great detail. A charming alternative of a trip

title: Amazing experience
text: I have been telling all my friends and family what an amazing time we had at Gir Lion Lodge. There were so many highlights to our visit it would take too long to list them all. We were made to feel like VIPs throughout. In particular it was such as huge privilege to be so close to the lions and have a chance to see them after the zoo was closed, and learn about them in such a relaxed environment. The hosts are so passionate and knowledgeable and it was great to be able to ask them questions and hear about the conservation work that ZSL does. We also enjoyed seeing the other animals in the zoo and waking up to hearing the gibbons and lions. The lodges are really comfortable and we were really warm despite it being October. We thought that all three tours were awesome and different. We also took advantage of our lodge experience allowing us access to Whipsnade zoo the next day. This was well worth the hour drive. The zoos really complement each other… and it was great to see the African lions in Whipsnade, and the baby hippo with its mum. We hope to do the lodge experience at Whipsnade next time.

title: Hatty, Kerry, Joe and Joy are amazing! Gay penguins too cute.Loved it!
text: The staff running this experience are amazing, warm, friendly and knowledgeable. After dropping our bags at the East Gate, we wandered around until 4.30 when we were able to check in to our lodge. There are 9 lodges painted in different colours and each named after an animal or bird. These cute little lodges are like a summerhouse. Spotlessly clean inside and new smelling with pure white bed linen and towels and a small sofa as well as the bed and a separate shower room. The shower worked perfectly for us. There was also a small table and 2 chairs on the veranda. We found the accommodation just fine, unlike some other reviewers and after all, that is not what this is all about. As well as making it fun and telling us loads about the different animals and conservation programmes, our hosts said a huge thank you to us for supporting ZSL and their work and it's good to know you're doing that by staying here. After settling in with a cuppa we met the rest of the group at 5.30 and were taken to view the lions in their authentic setting based on the Gir forest in India, and it was amazing to be able to be so close to these beautiful creatures. We also got to feed some of the animals before dinner at 7pm. Dinner was excellent. Afterwards we had another tour in the dark which included the aardvarks and porcupines. Some people heard the lions around 4am, although we didn't. The next morning we had to be packed up and out by 08.30 before having breakfast and one last tour including the lovely penguins being fed. We were told that penguins are monogamous and mate for life, including the 3 sets of gay penguins. We could have stayed inn the zoo the entire 2 days if we had wanted and it also includes Whipsnade zoo.

title: Birthday and Proposal memories that will last forever
text: With my girlfriend's birthday approaching I decided to book a night in the Gir Lion Lodges at ZSL as a special treat and decided to use the venue to propose to her. Prior to the trip I contacted Olivia at the experiences team and she couldn't have been more accommodating in helping make it as an amazing experience as possible. On the day we arrived via the separate East Gate entrance leaving our luggage in the storage giving us a few hours to explore the always great London Zoo prior to checking in at the lodge at 5pm. The lodges themselves are great and located right next to the brilliant new lion enclosure. The are all well decorated with good bathroom facilities and a comfortable bed and an additional sofa bed if required. We were greeted by Joy, Viv and Hannah who explained the itinerary of the night and got us checked in very easily. The first tour of the night began at 6pm with a glass of prosecco while they showed us around the land of the lions enclosure and gave us a great insight into the lions living at ZSL. We went onwards and got opportunites to feed some of the animals in the zoo prior to our own dinner. Dinner was great and we got to quiz Joy and Viv on their work at the zoo, food was a good quality buffet with plenty available (do note alcohol drinks had to be purchased separate). We then went on to the night time tour which was great and got to see some nocturnal animals rarely seen out in the day. After this while most headed back to the lodges the team took me and my girlfriend back to a secluded part of the lion enclosure where they had set up candles and 2 glasses of prosecco. Here I was able to propose to my girlfriend (happy to say she said yes) with 3 sleeping lionesses on the other side of the glass. It was such an amazing moment that was only possible thanks to the thoughtful and accommodating staff looking after us. Neither me or my now fiancee will ever forget how special it was. During the night we could hear the various animal noises across the park and we were actually woken up by the sounds of the lions roaring as they woke for the day. A very unique experience. We were given a tasty breakfast at 8am followed by our final tour before the zoo was open up to the public. This was especially enjoyable as we got a peek behind the scenes at some of the food prep for the animals and got to see the Zoo slowly coming alive for the day. At 10am with the Zoo open we were able to stay as long as we wanted and even given the chance to enjoy ZSL's other zoo in Whipsnade as part of the package if we wanted. Overall an amazing experience that is well worth the admittedly steep price thanks to the uniqueness of the setting and great work of its staff.

title: Memorable Experience
text: My hubby, my 7 years old boy and I spent a Family night at Gir Lodge in early August. Unfortunately, the weather did not like us and it kept raining non-stop for the first day, including our free time at London Zoo in the morning and both tours in the evening. Nevertheless, the experience was memorable. The three ZSL education staff (Hatti, Hannah and I am so sorry I forgot the other girl’s name…) really made a difference for the experience. Although we had a full group with poor weather, they were attentive to each of us, and nobody felt left out in the tour. They were very enthusiastic to share the zoo animals’ fun facts and the conservation works that ZSL involved. Please help me to say thank you to them and congratulate them on the job very well done. Three private tours were included in the price, and I found that each tour was better than the previous one. I felt privileged to visit animals at night time and was able to provide enrichment items to them. My family loved the morning tour with the visit to the back-of-house, as we could actually see how keepers prepare food for the animals. We also got to see the big old toothbrushes that the pygmy hippos we visited the night before used to use. The weather finally turned sunny the next day. We stayed at the Zoo till 2pm and visited majority of the exhibits. Yes, the charge was not cheap at all, but that included two days entry to the Zoo, yummy dinner & breakfast (my boy also got to draw his own t-shirt to take away as a souvenir after dinner), a night stay and three private tours. Plus, it felt good that profits that ZSL made would contribute to the great conservation work they do.

title: A birthday to remember
text: Looking for something unique to do for my birthday, my husband found this zoo experience and I have to say it made for the most memorable birthday. When you book you are given access to the zoo from opening. As check in to the lodges isn't until 4:30pm, we left our luggage at the entry gate and were told it would be at our accommodation for us later. That gave us the day to enjoy and explore the zoo to ourselves. All guests are asked to arrive for check in at the same time, which makes it easier for the hosts to be able to give housekeeping instructions and issue keys. We were allocated Flamingo Lodge which was tucked into the corner and felt very private. The lodges are small, but comfortable and well equipped for a single night stay, which when you calculate the time spent inside, I think it calculated to only a few hours awake! They are also spotlessly clean, with good quality linens and large bath towels (nothing worse than a tiny towel that doesn't go around you!). Inside the lodge is an information folder detailing the itinerary so every guest knows exactly what to expect and the system works like clockwork. Our two hosts Joy and Hannah were fabulous, both friendly, fun and very enthusiastic and clearly loved what they did. After the zoo closed, we were all gathered and taken for welcome drinks in the Land of the Lions. Drinking prosecco whilst a pair of sleeping lions are the other side of a pane of glass was a first for sure! The evening tour then commenced and took us around several areas of the zoo, including feeding some of the animals. I think our tour group were a bit spoilt as, due to a function being held in the usual restaurant, our evening dinner was held in the Mappin Pavilion

title: A night with the animals!
text: My daughter (aged 16) and I stayed on an adults only night and with a couple of lodges empty it made the experience a bit more intimate. The whole thing is well organised. We arrived at the zoo at about 1pm entered through the East Service gate where we left our overnight case with a security guard. It was waiting for us in our lodge when we got there. The lodges are nicely painted and decorated and situated within a compound next to the lion enclosure and designed to replicate an Indian village as the lions are Asiatic. The lodges are on the small side but they are clean and bright, en suite, with soaps, body wash, shampoo, lotions etc, different variety of teas (brownie points) hot chocolate (big thumbs up) and coffee. Each lodge has a small veranda with tables and chairs. It's all rather lovely. So while it is compact, you're staying for one night and essentially you are just sleeping there... so what do you really need.. Joe, Hannah and Joy were out hosts for the evening and morning and were very enthusiastic, engaging and utterly charming. After being shown to our lodge we had a brief safety talk and then had a glass of prosecco whilst watching the three lionesses curl up in the railway station in the enclosure and the male lion being given very little engagement by them. It was an extraordinary moment We then set off on a guided tour for about an hour before arriving at the main restaurant where we had dinner in a private room. Everyone sits round a big table - it worked well everyone was chatty and the food was fine, plenty of it and you could help yourself and go back for seconds etc if you chose. Drinks were available to buy - It would be nice for the bottle of wine buyers if the unused bottle could be returned to the appropriate lodge to enable a night cap... (just a suggestion). After dinner we had another guided tour of nocturnal animals which was my personal highlight - there's nothing like preparing a treatbox for the Aardvarks and watching their snout get stuck in it. We were shown back to our lodge about 10pm and then "locked" in for the night. Sleep was comfortable and it was thrilling to be woken in the early hours by the lions roaring their presence. We had to vacate the lodge by 8am and made our way to breakfast in the main restaurant where there was a selection of hot and cold food. Hot didn't appeal to me - but there was plenty of other stuff so no problems. After breakfast and before the zoo opens to other visitors, we were taken on a final guided tour and were entertained by the penguins, the gibbons and the tigers who were just a perfect finish. We took a couple of hours to hit spots of the zoo before it got busy, gorillas first thing is lovely, as is the night house and the rainforest. We finished off with a final treat of feeding the meercats some treats and had a total blast.

title: 20th Anniversary stay
text: We had our wedding reception in the Reptile House at London Zoo, so when we read in the FT that it was possible stay overnight at Gir Lion Lodges in the zoo, we jumped at the chance. The hosts are very friendly (and also very young, but that maybe just the fact that we are very old). The lodges are well built summer houses with en suite facilities. All very new and clean, if a tad small. We had our two children with us and the sofa bed they had to sleep on took up pretty much all the available floor space when it was open. Things to improve on? Some biscuits with the tea and coffee stuff would be nice and the towels are pretty thin and scratchy. That said,it is a magical experience and one we'd highly recommend. We had a Silent Cinema session on the night we stayed and it was awesome. Best bit? Feeding aardvarks at 10:30 at night. Beyond special.

title: Great Gift, room for improvement
text: I purchased this as a gift for my parents. They really enjoyed their stay but because they knew it was expensive, held back on their criticism. This following are improvements i think ZSL could make customers more happy! :) 1) Allow guests to have access to the lodges throughout the day. If not, atleast earlier than 4.30pm would be better! Would allow guests to make the most of their day at the zoo. 2) Seating area at meal times to be more comfortable for elderly guests 3) a free soft drink with the evening meal!! Would have been nice for my parents to to have to worry about other costs once relaxed inside! 4) More vegetarian options for both meals. Very limited menu. 5) Have the option of reducing the ticket price for those that do not wish to have access to the Zoo on the following day. Many, like my parents, would be tired after the 1st day and given their long journey home- they missed out on going around the zoo the second day. Atleast give them a voucher so they could come back on a different day ?!

title: Unique stay at Gir Lion Lodge
text: On arrival at the East Service Gate, our initial impression was not good as the man on the gate was abrupt and did not direct us accurately to our lodge. However, when we finally found our way there, the Lodge staff were incredibly apologetic and said this would be looked into. They immediately told us we would receive a complimentary drink each at dinner in way of an apology. The lodge was immaculately clean and looked like brand new. The single beds, although somewhat narrow, were extremely comfortable with very cosy bedding and pillows. The bathroom, towels and toiletries were good quality and faultless. We thoroughly enjoyed all the evening walks. We enjoyed dinner and again the staff went out of their way to ensure that my dietary needs were met. The dynamics of the group meant that we would have preferred the option to sit on our own table as certain people loved the sound of their own voice and dominated the conversation. This is maybe something that could be looked at by the organisers. The early morning walk was again both enjoyable and informative. At breakfast, I had to wait for a suitable breakfast to be prepared for me, despite having written all about my needs on my initial application but again staff profusely apologised for this oversight and delay. We stayed at the zoo for the rest of the day and were very impressed with all the keepers' knowledge of their animals and the animals' environment. As always, there is so much to see at London Zoo that we know we will be back. A recommended experience with enthusiastic and friendly staff who really want you to have a good time.

title: Adult night
text: We stayed in a Gir Lion Lodge for our 30th wedding anniversary and are so pleased we decided to celebrate with something fun. We arrived around 2pm and left our case at the gate to be delivered our lodge for check in at 4. We spent a couple of hours enjoying the zoo which has changed enormously and for the better since my last visit 25 years ago. At check in we were given a very friendly welcome and settled into the lodge with a cup of tea on the decking. The lodge was very clean and lovely and light with themed decoration and lovely bedding.
