It's compact but has everything needed for a nights stay. At 6 we were given a safety briefing and taken on a tour of the new lion enclosure, prosecco in hand. Dinner in the restaurant followed

title: Excellent! You may even get a chance to feed the animals.
text: This experience exceeded my expectations. It may sound weird but I enjoyed packing a box full of maggots and beetles to feed to the Aardvark! (You don't have to of course). The staff are fun and enthusiastic giving you the chance to enjoy the night to it's full potential. The meal was excellent (you can buy a wine or beer) and the breakfast would set you up for the day. Be prepared for a 4.30 am wake up call from the lions next door! Up in plenty of time to go to the kitchen and watch the preparations for the animals dinner. It may seem expensive but compare that to the cost of a London hotel, meal and a show.

title: Good guides, accommodation less than basic
text: The sheds (please they are not lodges) had en-suite, but were simply not big enough,and nowhere near what you could call value for money. The food was adequate. The real plus point was the enthusiasm of the staff/guides, which was hugely infectious and very welcome indeed. They were so very knowledgeable that the negative points were totally outweighed. We now need to find how to get a sloth as a pet - they were really great! Would not do this again, the price is far too high for the accommodation supplied. In real terms - one star for accommodation, two stars for food, at least five stars for the guides - average = average!

title: Walk on the Wild Side with Experts
text: A sleep-over at the zoo has never been so educational. My husband had to be convinced to attend this outing with me, but has not stopped talking about how much he learned on our walks with zoo staff. The accommodations are very nice, with clean, separate lodges that include bed, bath, and a front porch. We happened to reserve our lodging on a Friday night in summer, so we had the extra benefit of entertainment from the "Zoo Night" event. The lodging has a heater and extra blanket for cold evenings and a fan for warm evenings, but not air conditioning. We enjoyed the towels folded as swans on our bed upon arrival and also the tea and coffee station in the room. The enthusiasm of the staff is exceptional, and for anyone interested in learning more about animals, or what goes on behind the scenes in a zoo, this is the place to be.

title: Having the zoo to yourself!
text: On holidays from Australia we booked this experience as a fun way to experience the zoo and have a different sleeping experience in London. The staff were extremely friendly and willing to meet our needs especially when my traveling companion wasn't feeling well and had stayed in the cabin, allowing us to bring him a doggy bag of dinner back for him. Feeding the animals at night was fun and waking up to a lions roar isn't something you would expect to experience in the middle of London! Yes it is expensive... but hey we were on holidays!

title: Fascinating Experience
text: We spent a wonderful night at Gir Lion Lodge. The four hosts were so enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the animals. It was a magical experience being able to stroll around an 'empty' zoo, with the opportunity to feed the animals. It was an amazing experience being woken up at 5.30am with Banu making his early morning call. The security guard was extremely enthusiastic, even at 5.45am and it was a great pleasure to spend some time talking to him. After breakfast it was lovely to spend some time looking at some other animals and discovering how and what they were fed. On the subject of food, both our evening meal and breakfast were of a high standard. The overall experience was superb, our only regret being, that we weren't able to stay longer. We do intend to return in the future bringing our granddaughter along for the experience. Karen and Andrew Wrexham

title: Wonderful!
text: A perfect night away for our wedding anniversary. Lodges were attractive and comfortable, staff were knowledgeable and friendly and the food was good. The out-of hours tours were fun and informative, loved being able to participate in the animals' enrichment. Absolutely wonderful, would highly recommend.

title: Lion Lodges - Fantastic experience
text: We wanted to celebrate my husband's 60th birthday in a special way and we thought we would all love to spend 2 days together, seeing all the animals, have dinner and breakfast and have tours round too - it was an amazing experience. We had a brilliant time at both at London zoo and Whipsnade-the guides were really informative and helpful. The downside again was my shower in Flamingo Lodge-either freezing cold, or scalding hot-not pleasant and this has been mentioned on other reviews, so needs looking into asap.

title: Fantastic Experience
text: What a fantastic experience, the lodges are excellent and the people who look after you are brilliant , very knowledgable, friendly and nothing was too much trouble. You see the animals in a totally different and much closer way when the Zoo is closed. Totally unforgettable.

title: Great experience
text: I won't go into too much detail as previous guests have pretty much covered it but would just like to say that this was the most enjoyable visit to a zoo I have ever experienced. The guides are passionate about the animals and their welfare and really bring it home to you how much these creatures need our help. The lodges are compact but are spotlessly clean with all that you could need provided. The food provided is plentiful and tasty and if you don't want to pay extra for alcohol or soft drinks then both still and sparkling water is provided. As for value for money is concerned I can only say that I recently stayed in a hotel in the Cotswolds for a similar price, no meals were included and no guided tours, Gir Lions knocked this into a cocked hat,, plus you have the warm fuzzy feeling that contributing towards ZSL s conservation programme gives you . Well done all concerned!

title: Birthday treat!!!!
text: What an amazing experience. I gave no idea why another reviewer was so down on it. The lodges were lovely. Spotless and with REALLY comfy warm beds and bedding. Ensuite shower/basin/toilet all great. Nice touch with the toiletries and tea/coffee things in the lodge. The lions sprung into voice around 4am and continued to be very vocal for a good 90mins, all added to the experience!! Both meals (dinner/breakfast) were buffet style and the food was good quality with plenty there. There are 3 tours, before and after dinner then again after breakfast. We saw a lovely variety of animals and got to interact with them by making up their enrichment boxes!! The hosts were lovely and incredibly knowledgable about both the animals and the zoos history. I absolutely loved it, thank you to my two main hosts Hannah and Joy, they made us welcome, kept us entertained and are a credit to the team at ZSL.

title: Great value for money and really interesting. Fantastic experience
text: Had an amazing time with my partner at the Gir Lion Lodge. Spent a lovely day looking around the zoo until check in time. The lodges are superbly furnished and comfortable. Being able to see the lions from the lodge enclosure was brilliant. The guides were very helpful and knowledgeable. 3 tours are included in the package. A pre-dinner tour and a post-dinner tour after dark includes feeding some of the animals. A 2 course dinner and full English breakfast is included. Another tour is provided after breakfast before the public is allowed in which includes behind the scenes. I will recommend this experience if you have the money.

title: Over night stay - excellent!
text: A great weekend. The food supplied was lovely, but most importantly the guides were helpful, friendly and knowledgeable. They provided a lot of interesting background information about ZSL which helped make a special experience. My son got to feedsome of the animals, which he loved and the animals almost seemed more relaxed after hours. Seeing behind the scenes in some areas was fascinating. A brilliant day, with the added bonus of Whipsnade the following day. Would recommend without hesitation.... if you like animals!

title: Fantastic experience and worth every penny
text: I bought this as a birthday present for my boyfriend because I wanted to do something different. We had an amazing time. Spent the day at the zoo and checked into our lodge at 4.30pm. The tour starts at 6pm so we had time to relax and sit on the veranda first. It was very exciting being the only people allowed in the zoo after hours. Seeing the lions close up was fascinating. The tour guides were very friendly and informative and passionate. The tours were brilliant, the food was way better than I expected it to be. Breakfast was delicious. Hearing the lions roaring at night is something I'll never forget. The morning tour was my favourite as we got to see the kitchen where the food is made for the animals. Overall this was a brilliant experience. It was very expensive for one night but I would say it is worth the money for what you get included. And of course the money is for a very worthwhile cause.

title: Fantastic experience
text: Stayed overnight at Gir Lion Lodge with my husband and had a wonderful time. On the day of arrival, you can check into your lodges at 4:30pm, but if you want to spend the day at the zoo then you can arrive anytime after 10am, and ZSL will store your bags for you, which is very useful. The lodges are fairly simple, but very comfortable and nicely decorated, with a small deck to sit on as well which is nice. Only slight issue was that the temperature on our shower (Flamingo lodge) was a bit hit-and-miss, and might need fixing. You get 3 tours as part of the overnight experience - a pre-dinner tour, a post-dinner tour in the dark, and a morning tour before the zoo opens. All of these were wonderful, and our tour guides were very knowledgeable. Of course you do not cover the entire zoo during these tours, but we saw lions, pygmy hippos, painted dogs, warthogs, tigers, the komodo dragon, penguins and tigers, amongst other animals, so covered quite a lot! And you have 2 days to explore the rest of the zoo at your own leisure, so I'd much rather cover fewer animals in detail whilst I have the experienced guides on-hand to share their knowledge. Dinner was nice, although given the price of the experience it would have been nice if soft drinks at least were included in the price. Breakfast was also good, nice seleciton of cooked breakfast, fruit, pastries etc. All in all, a wonderful experience which my husband and I both thoroughly enjoyed. Yes, its not cheap, but if you're interested in animals then this is a fantastic special occasion gift.

title: Awe-inspiring
text: A mesmerising and awe-inspiring 30 hours at a beautifully managed zoo

title: Brilliant gift
text: Santa gave our grandchildren and their parents a night at Gir Lodge, it was the best present ever. Both parents loved the facilities and the food while the children were captivated by the whole adventure. The dawn and dusk tours of the zoo were "awesome", the lions could be seen very close to, and the roars heard from inside the lodge, they also loved the tiger cubs and too many others to name! Our grandson aged 10 told us it was the "greatest time of my life" and our granddaughter wants to be a zoo keeper! It also taught them a lot about conservation and protection of endangered species. A special thanks to Joe and all the team who made it such a wonderful experience.

title: Superb view of some fascinating creaturess
text: Earlier Reviewers have provided plenty of information about this marvellous experience. Suffice to say we endorse their superlatives. OK the rooms are small but very well planned with all mod cons. The price seems high but for 2 days entrance for 4, plus meals and private night and morning conducted tours it is very good value for a very good cause. Four medium price tickets for a Top musical cost £300, no contest.

title: Gir Lion Lodge
text: Overnight stay with lots of close encounters with the zoo animals once the park had shut including an Easter egg hunt. The lodges are small but perfectly laid out and comfortable as well as being very close to the lions and their roars! Dinner was excellent and the night tour was fun with unexpected nocturnal encounters! The morning included a pre opening visit to the penguins and back room areas which was led by the keen and informed zoo staff. Really special treat.

title: Great treat
text: Just returned from our night in the zoo and felt compelled to leave a review. OK yes, it's a big treat price wise but I felt that not only was it worth it but that I was donating to the charity/research as well. The lodges are small but comfortable and let's face it you're not there for the accommodation. The staff looking after us were excellent, as were all the staff throughout the zoo by the way. They were enthusiastic and knowledgeable and fantastic with the children. Remember this is not a petting zoo, nothing is going to "do tricks for you" this is about educational experience as much as being amazing. The food was good and plentiful. We spent 2 days at ZSL and it was well worth every minute. 2 tired children after walking over 13km each day.

title: My Very Own Zoo!
text: Having read some of the reviews I have to agree, this Gir Lion Lodge experience was fantastic, Joe & Hetti were great, so enthusiastic about the animals, the zoo, the conservation of ZSL's future. The Lodge was clean warm and tidy. We stayed in the Flamingo Lodge. Initially I thought this was an expensive treat, however, realising that every penny goes back into the zoo, training and ZSL's conservation here and abroad was worth ever penny. I found London Zoo ZSL's Enrichment program very impressive, the zoo is balancing the viewing pleasure of the public and the physical & mental needs of the animals. Well done ZSL. The 1st tour of the zoo was great, it was still light and you feel special knowing you are the only members of the public still there. The evening meal was lovely, with a vegetarian option too. I do agree the soft drinks and alcohol should have been included with the meal. Even if for just the first drink. The evening walk was very special indeed. No spoilers, but I loved seeing the "surprise" animal. The highlights of the evening walk for me: - the sound of the zoo residents was incredible, namely, the tweeting' of the Owls, the amazing roar of the Lions. I woke up at 6.30am on Saturday morning, I got to see the handsome lion all to myself, first thing, no interruptions. For that alone, worth every penny. As agreed, Joe & Hetti should have the opportunity to go to India to see the hard work ZSL are achieving over there..... could you imagine their enthusiasm then, off the scale 🤔 Highly recommended

title: Best neighbours ever!
text: Ok, so when they are 'speaking' they are a bit louder than most but you will find that you really don't mind! All of the other reviews have done a wonderful job of telling you all about the experience and I heartily agree with all of their positive comments. Our hosts, Keri, Hattie and Hannah, could not have been more friendly and helpful and we were made to feel so welcome by everyone we met, from the security guard at the gate, the teams in the restaurants and shops and the keepers who had the patience to speak to us about 'waking up' the zoo even though they obviously had so much to do. We were very lucky and the animals all came out to see us. The hosts work so hard to make sure that you see as many animals as possible. However, please do bear in mnid that sometimes the 'stars of the show' decide that they are having a night in! Go ahead-book and create your own memories

title: Highly recommended
text: If you are looking for a London weekend break with a difference and have at least a mild interest in animals & conservation this is highly recommended. You are looked after thoughout your stay by friendly, welcoming guides who are very knowledgeable & passionate about the zoo. The lodges are cozy, clean and comfortable (reminded me of the sort of facilities you find in a caravan), this isn't meant to be a 4 star hotel, its a working zoo, after all you only in there to sleep as the rest of the time is taken up with very interesting & informative tours. The cost of the stay was easy to justify, even with 4 of us, as it included overnight stay/food/parking/day in London/private zoo tour after hours/behind the scenes/day at Whipsanade etc.. On top of all that, knowing that the proceeds from this are going back into ZSL worked for me.

title: Great stay
text: Would highly recommend gir lion lodge, we had a fantastic time during our adults only stay.Joe, the keeper is brilliant, he made us so welcome and his passion for the animals shines out, thank you Joe and the lady keepers too, you are all a credit to ZSL. Our lodge was clean,a very,very comfortable bed and came with linen, towels,toiletries and a hair dryer, complimentary tea,coffee,hot chocolate and water.It also has a sofa and small veranda with table and chairs so you can sit out and listen to the night animal sounds, magical.We both had no trouble at all dropping off to sleep and were not disturbed even with the window open ( we turned heating off ). Be aware the bijou bathroom does not have a window so be careful when using spray deodorant, hairspray or perfume, it's easy to set the smoke alarm off!.If it does go off ( sorry once again Joe ), just open the door to lodge to let the fumes/steam dissipate and it turns off...it happened to us!. For the smokers, you can have a ciggie by the gate in fence surrounding the lodges, there is an ashtray on fence.You can watch the lions if they are up and about as their compound is mere feet away!.All lodges, in and around are non smoking. The evening tours were wonderful and we thoroughly enjoyed meeting all the animals and learned so much thanks to the keepers knowledge.Torches are provided so no need to bring one. The evening dinner was very nice,tasty and plentiful, vegetarian option too.Wine and beer available to buy, complimentary water, tea and coffee with meal.Breakfast the following morning is help yourself, (make your own toast,tea,coffee ),choices of cooked breakfast, cereals, pastries, fruit etc, as much as you want,and very nice it was!.This is before your morning meet the animals tour, so you will walk the calories off. Wrap up warm, wear comfortable footwear because you will do a lot of walking around.If you are planning to spend the day before and after your sleepover at ZSL, don't knock yourself out rushing round to see everything.Take your time to savour all the wonderful animals, what you don't see the 1st day, you can see the 2nd day as we did.There is a LOT to see and enjoy. You can leave your bag/s at the entrance east gate when you arrive and they will be delivered to your appointed lodge, they will also be taken back the following day for you to collect when you depart zoo.They are kept in a locked storage shed. Once again, many, many thanks to the wonderful folks at ZSL who made our stay a fantastic experience, would we do it again?,YES.I bought this as a Christmas present for my partner and it was worth every penny!. If you are not an early to bed person, take a book or mag as no tv etc in lodges, but after all the walking you will do, you probably won't want to stay up too late.Its an early start the following day. ps....you can go into your lodge at 16.30 so just walk to the lodges and your keeper will let you in.The meet and greet with complimentary drink takes place in the village at start of 1st evening tour before dinner.

title: Unique birthday treat
text: Took my husband for his 60th birthday at the end of February. Accommodation is compact but very comfortable and cosy. Really enjoyed the out-of-hours tours with knowledgable guides, and learning about how hard the zoo works to enrich the animals' environments. The visit to the kitchen where the keepers prepare the vegetarian food for their charges was particularly interesting. It's an expensive trip but I think value for money considering it includes (if you wish) two full days in the zoo, overnight accommodation, and a unique experience - and you know that the profits go to excellent conservation work.

title: Gir Lion Lodge
text: Once in a lifetime unforgettable experience to see behind the scenes at London Zoo. Our hosts were the perfect mix of knowledgeable and sociable ...none of the standard corporate word perfect spiel here. From the guard on the entrance gate who checks you in, to the restaurant staff, all went out of their way to make us feel welcome and looked after. They all seemed to have genuine wide smiles. The sound of the lions making their presence felt loudly from 4am was really special and standing centimetres from the large male was breathtaking. The tours show you a range of nocturnal animals you'd never normally see, and take you behind the scenes into places you wouldn't know you'd be allowed to go so I won't spoil the surprises. Night vision glasses and infra red torches help you to see a whole new side of the zoo and as the ambulances wizz by on the local roads you feel like you're in a little world of your own away from city life. If going in winter I'd take snuggly extra throws, fluffy socks and hot water bottles if you are a chilly soul and to make the place homely but it's by no means necessary as the lodges have heating and a good en suite with large walk in shower. Food was plentiful and lots of choice. Thanks Hattie and the rest of the team, you really did make a little girl - and two big girls! - dreams come true.

title: Not what 'it says on the tin'
text: Sadly this did not live up to the hype, description and expectations. The lodge cannot be described as a lodge, more a big shed with a bathroom. Don't take the cat as you will not be able to swing it. As some reviewers have said, at best a glorified Wendy House. All very clean but very tiny. We booked a double bed in a 'large family pod'. We were greeted by twin beds. No big deal but oh dear, they are tiny. Don't roll over for fear of falling out. Cannot see any reason for such a late check-in 4:30 pm. It would be nice to have use of the facility earlier. Particularly on a cold wet day. When considering the cost, in excess of £530 that is the least one would expect. The girls were great. Friendly knowledgeable and great with kids. The night tour was a big disappointment. Standing in the cold of night watching a Pigmy Hippo eating, for 15 minutes plus was too much. We were then taken to see bats, then a sleeping otter. The surprise animals (will not spoil it) were not great. And it's dark so you share one pair of night visions between the family. Dinner which is private with the guests was ok. Decent food after a long day. Much needed. Surprised to be charged £2.50 for a kids apple juice. Can understand charging for alcohol but soft drinks? The morning tour was an improvement. But this tour thing needs attention. The blurb tells you that you will have a 'zoo tour'. That is not the case at all. You see only a fraction. Breakfast was basic. Nothing special. No cornflakes! Everyone provides cornflakes. The cost for what you get is extortionate and considering it's all about the kids, somewhat unfair on parents and grandparents. Not worth the money for the experience. Would better to spend the £530 and stay in a 5 star London hotel and spend the day at your own leisure and see everything. Will say it again, despite everything the girls were great. Give them all a pay rise.

title: Great experience. We felt privileged to have the Zoo for just our small group.
text: We took this experience as a surprise anniversary gift for my husband who used to be a 'young zoologist' at the zoo as a little boy. You are taken to the small but functional lodge to leave bags and freshen up before having complimentary pre dinner drink on the terrace above the restaurant and to meet your fellow members of the group. We were on an adult only evening in July and the sun was out for both days. We had a short tour of some of the animals before dinner and then a more intensive visit to the Aardvark enclosure where we tempted them out with tasty Aardvark treats which we hid in small boxes for them to find. We were given interesting information about the work the Zoo does and the animals we saw, the staff were very informative and enthusiastic. We then went back to the Gir Lion enclosure to see the Lions and retreat to the our lodges in the human enclosure! We could here the animals as night fell. The morning arrived and we were roused by a member of staff about 7am before breakfast and further visits to some of the animals. At 10 when the Zoo opens we were left to explore on our own. The viewing of the animals was more geared to the smaller ones that people might not see or know much about rather tha the big favourites but you have plenty of time to see them prior to the start of the experience or after it finishes the next day. The lodges are small but have everything you need for a night, the single beds are comfortable and have nice linens. There is tea/coffee making equipment in the lodge. The ensuite provides shower, toilet and basin with plenty of hot water. There is a small deck area outside for having an evening drink or early morning cuppa. The evening meal was a buffet and was tasty and plentiful. You could purchase alcoholic drinks. Breakfast was plentiful and the usual buffet cereals or cooked offerings. The cost looks expensive but if you factor in dinner, b&b, a welcome drink, 2 days at the Zoo, parking and the overall experience of having the Zoo for a small group viewing I think is reasonable. We thoroughly enjoyed the experience.

title: Excellent experience but quite expensive
text: Firstly, I have to say that I was aware of the cost when I booked this so I can't complain about this and if you compare it to an evenings entertainment, accommodation and food in London, it is not that different. That aside, the experience was incredible, the staff were really informative and I would strongly advise this to anyone who has a passion for animals. The accommodation was warm, comfortable and good quality and the catering was exceptional.

title: Fantastic Family Experience
text: We stayed at Gir Lion Lodge on a Family night over a cold weekend in February - I was concerned that we'd be cold at night sleeping in a wooden hut but I needn't have worried, the lodges are so toasty and very well appointed, I was pleasantly surprised. Being so close to the lions was a once in a lifetime experience, and such a treat to see all the other animals in the evening that were fast asleep during the day (such as fruit bats, pygmy hippos and the adorable "mystery animal" (I won't give away what it is and spoil the fun but we all fell in love with her!). In the morning you'll be woken early by the male lion roaring and the parakeets in the trees, not something that happens every day! The staff that run the experience are fantastic, we were looked after by Joy, Hattie, Viv & Hannah and they were all so helpful and knowledgable - they seem to love their jobs and we all learnt so much about the animals and the conservation work that ZSL do. If you're thinking of booking this experience, don't hesitate, it really is worth every penny and you won't forget it in a hurry!

title: Awesome stay at the zoo!!
text: Who knew you could stay at the zoo! Stumbled across this unique stay while looking for a special 40th birthday present for my other half. The Gir Lion Lodge only opened in May 2016 and is a stunning attraction. This overnight stay is only available on specific days/dates and some of the time is specificity adults only and others are family times. (But couples are welcome on these days too) Price wise this is not cheap but on the plus side it's well worth the money for what you get included. I felt as a special present it was worth the money. And he blinking loved the surprise. When you arrive they take your bags from you and deliver them to your lodge and they also keep them the next day till you go. We arrived early so we could have a day at the zoo before we checked in to the lodge and started the adventure. I don't want to give too much away as I felt not knowing what was going to happen was exciting. I would say wear good comfortable shoes/trainers and pack a jumper or a cagool as you will be outside for a good amount of time in the evening and you'll be walking lots too. The accommodation is really lovely like sleeping in a wee chalet in a wood. It also has a nice ensuit, the shower is amazing and they provide shampoo conditioner and body wash, so it saves to carting that with you. Do note no tv (not that you'll need it) This was an amazing overnight stay and I'd highly recommend it to anyone who loves animals/zoo's Only suggestion is that if your not a big fan of hyperactive children then perhaps go on a adults only session, as on our trip a few of the kids really didn't behave well and spoiled parts of it for me.

title: The best way to experience London Zoo.
text: We visited in early February on a very cold Sunday. The lodges were cosy and warm with all mod cons. Other reviews explain what to expect, which, in summary, is an excellent tour by very enthusiastic zoo keepers. Thanks to Kelly and Hannah for the Sunday nighttime tour of the nocturnal animals, Jay (or Joe, we didn't work it out) for the Bugs tour and also Jay/Joe for the early morning tour and for looking after us. Sunday night into Monday morning was great because it was just four guests, on the previous night, I understand, there had been 30 people including children, which would have been a different dynamic. The food was very good, both the evening meal and the breakfast. In short, I thoroughly recommend this excellent experience.

title: The best New Year ever!
text: We booked this as a New Year's Eve treat on January 1st - as soon as the email appeared in my inbox. We have been to Lookout Lodge in Whipsnade twice and really enjoyed those visits so thought we'd give Gir Lion Lodge a try. It was just an amazing experience, we were a couple but the visit was enhanced by the excitement and enjoyment of the children in the group so would choose a family-friendly night for future visits. From the first glass of prosecco (there was an extra one at midnight) to the last goodbye and thank you Olivia and the team were great, enthusiastic, informative and helpful. It felt very special standing in the dark surrounded by fireworks and drinking fizz, especially as it was their first New Year. We loved the torchlit tour, throwing nuts for the porcupines and making enrichment boxes for the aardvarks and the sight of Bhanu, the big male lion, upside down on his hot rock, pressed against the window with his (huge!) paws in the air was remarkable. Lovely staff, lovely food, lovely warm, comfortable acommodation. Thank you to all at ZSL London, especially the team whomade this such a unique and special experience.

title: July stay
text: Small room, very small breakfast area, but excellent location. Clean. London is a beautiful city, enjoyed my stay. had a good time. What more is there to say? Ok - I have got 42 characters to go - this should be enough???

title: Great Locality.Convenient & Clean
text: This Hotel is located ideally in London,just around the corner to the nearest bus stop & subway,staff was friendly & helpful. Breakfast room very small & crowded however fit the bill.A very cute cafe"Lady Diane Cafe" just around the corner with photos of Lady Diane plastered over the walls,very unique.

title: Great Value for Money for this Location.
text: I stayed with my wife here for one day and we were not at all expecting anything more than a basic accommodation. We stayed here after staying in Crown Plaza London where we payed 150 pounds for one night. After booking the hotel from the hotel website we called up the hotel as My wife has booked it for one person instead of two by mistake ( Prices were same on the website ), But instead of solving the problem operator has hung up the phone. We were disappointed. But when we reached in the hotel which is very conveniently located less than 5 minutes walk from Notting Hill Tube station and the bus stops, we were surprised by looking at the room. It was a big room with television , coffee maker and very cozy temperature in the room. The bathroom was very small but designed in a way that you will not feel congested, I a toilet freak but toilet was nice and clean. yes hotel does not have new carpets but what could you expect in the heart of London in 42 Pounds. The hotel was really every penny worth if you are visiting this historical city. check out timing is 11 am and if wish to leave your luggage, till 1 pm it is free and after that they will charge you 5 pounds. All the attractions and Buzzing night Life of London is Close by. You can take bus number 94 all over the night if you want to party late in London. extremely great Location. Breakfast is very basic continental breakfast but you will get everything what you want. The Breakfast room size is very small but we got the table as we were there by 8 am but I suppose later it will be difficult to find the table. It was all Italian young people staying in the hotel. Will definitely return back to save money.

title: Basic but fine
text: We stayed overnight at the Notting Hill Gate hotel, it was basic but clean. There were numerous stairs so people with young children / mobility issues may struggle. The room was compact but was cheap and clean. The breakfast was basic but was plentiful. Staff were polite. Good budget accommodation for an overnight stay.

title: Perfectly okay
text: Good location close to bus and tube, room was fine but the bed wasn't very comfortable. The bathroom was very small but actually really nice(!!) and looked as if it had recently been re-done. Stayed in the room up by the first flight of stairs from the reception so a downside was having everyone in the hotel passing by my door on their way out and me overhearing all conversations had by the reception. But they probably heard me snore so we're even. Would probably come back here if I'm ever in London again!

title: Great location in the middle of Notting Hill
text: The hotel is small but very nice. The simple rooms are very clean and are kept in good condition every day. Price performance far exceeded. I had indeed a Disagreement about a damage in room no.8, which I didn't cause, but everything has been cleared up. I'm sure I'll get back to this great location in the middle of Notting Hill for carnival.

title: Just about acceptable!
text: Recently stayed at this hotel for one night as a single traveller. Single ensuite room I stayed in was very compact, basic and somewhat noisy what with locals talking outside the window and the constant buzz of cars. The room however was cheap and was a late booking so if you take all of this into account it just about did the job. Hotel also offers free wi-fi which should be commended but on the downside charges a whopping 4% charge when payment is made via credit or debit card. Personally I would only consider staying here if you are a single traveller who doesnt want anything fancy price wise and justs needs hot water and a bed to sleep in.

title: small everywhere
text: The first thing you do when you arrive is paying the bill, and then they explain you about the facilities of the hotel. Internet wifi is free and works very well. The rooms, or at least my room, were tinny, I’m used to be in small hotels but this one was really tinny, there was only one double bed, and that all. do you want same place to put your luggage? Well put it in the bathroom that the only place left one you are inside the room! Breakfast was included, well if we can call breakfast only same cafe, toast and juice, and guess what? Yes this room was almost as big as my room!! the people in the reception? Well we asked about the time table of the metros because we had to leave very early and we wanted to know if the metro was open, the only answered we had was go the metro and ask them... oh did i mention the best thing? There was no lift!! And the stairs to go the rooms were not event of the same size: the more you went up the smaller they became!

title: I'd rather sleep in Hyde Park
text: This hotel was so bad, it was comical. Firstly it's not a hotel

title: Best deal in this great location
text: The staff at this hotel is very welcoming and very helpful, the room we stayed (2 adults and 2 children) is very clean and is not bad size, no carpet in the room just wooden floor, which was very good for us. Free Wi Fi and works very well. The continental breakfast is ok (tea, coffee, milk, chocolate nutella, egg, cheese, croissant, bread, honey jam etc). The hotel is 5 minutes walk from Notting Hill Gate Station, 10 minutes from Hide Park. There is everything nearby (exchange offices, restaurants, grocery stores, etc ...).we loved this location and hotel, we will be back again. I recommend this hotel.

title: Rubbish ......do not stay here !
text: This property is a joke ! We arrived, and were told our room was on the 4th floor .... Two 26kg bags plus 2 backpacks and NO lift ! Advertised as 20 sqm, air conditioning and it’s a safe, However, ......much closer to 10 sqm, no air conditioning see the attached pics ... Further, there was no safe, no glasses, no ice available, no hot water in the morning, Intermittent internet, and the toilet didn’t flush properly, no good enough and NOT as advertised, something Agoda needs to fix !

title: Value for money
text: A cosy hotel located in the very central part of London. 3-minute walk from metro station (Notting Hill), 24-hour reception, very friendly and helpful staff. Breakfast and wi-fi included in price. Small but clean rooms with private bathrooms. Best choice for those who travel alone or in a couple and looks for a good hotel for a short period in central London with no frills at a reasonable price.

title: Great Eating Area
text: Quiet hotel with very friendly welcome. Good size and standard of accomodation and a continental breakfast included in the price ofn the room. Smart, clean, tiled en suite toilet and shower room.. Very handy for buses and underground travel into Central London.

title: DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY HERE!!!!!
text: Rude staff who mess up your booking then call the police when you complain. Don't waste your time or money here

title: Very very nice place
text: Went there for a 4 days trip with my boy-friend. Really nice, quite hotel, unluckily at the last floor without lift, but it was worth it. Clean, quite, we were lucky: we got a 4 persons room for 2, so the room was big enough... but the guy at the reception said we were lucky as the rooms for 2 are small... The bathroom was completly new, there was a flat TV in the room, a kettle and so. Nothing to say, really nice, some restaurants around, a Tesco at 5 min walk, as far as a metro station. I highly recommend it !!

title: very good!!!! AAA
text: I travelled in February 2010 with my mother on a shopping trip to London. The service was excellent and the hotel staff were very helpful with any directions we needed. We were given Room 10 which we were very lucky with because it was more than enough for two people. the hotel's location is just 6 minutes walk away from the Undergroud station, which in turn is just 3 stops away from Marble Arch, very central and especially ideal for shopping. there are also number of restaurants in the main street just off the hotel's location. the hotel is very clean and breakfast is also enough.

title: Nice little hotel
text: A small hotel near the Notting Hill area with only about 25 (?) rooms. We (three adults) stayed there for 5 days. We got the room on the 5th floor and there was no elevator so the trek upstairs with our three luggages was not fun. Location was very convenient - about a 3-5 min walk from Notting Hil Gate Station or the Queensway tube station. Just steps from the hotel is a bus stop, so you are only a bus ride away from places like Oxford Street and Picadilly Circus (take bus 94) and the British Museum (bus 390). It's also within walking distance to Kensington Garden and Portabello Road. Breakfast was provided in the morning but don't expect anything fancy. It was hard boiled eggs, toast with jam/butter, milk, fruit juices, coffee and tea. Breakfast room is really small, and depending on when everybody else gets up, may get a little crowded, so you may have to line up to get into the room. And even if you get sick of their breakfast there are decent places around the Notting Hill Gates tube station (ie. Pret-a-manger, EAT) just down the street. The room was a little small, but at least everything was clean. We were mostly out and about and was mainly looking for a place to crash after a long sightseeing. Staff was friendly and helpful. The street was a dead-end street so there isn't as much traffic as a main street, so it was pretty quiet at night. Our only complaint was there was no remote control in our room on our arrival and it took a while to figure out which remote control worked in our room. Overall we are satisfied with this place and would recommend this to others.

title: Feeling fooled
text: We are a family of 5, came in late with tired children. Our booking was for a 3 night stay at the Notting Hill gate, but upon arrival we were told that because of a leak, you had to drive us to their sister hotel Linden House in Paddington. We had specifically chosen the hotel because of it's location in Notting Hill and no one tried calling us to inform of us if the suggested change. We were given no option. It felt very pre-planned. The standard of the room we were given was nothing in comparison to what I had booked over booking'com. In a very small room of approx 9m2, in which was crammed 2 double and one single bed. The double beds were 1.20 and not a fullsize double bed per definition. The room was small, leaving no room for luggage and the shower room (because one can't call it a bath room) was so small that when sitting on the toilet you had your knees under the sink, touching the shower cabin door. I went back to look at the photos and I now see that they are shot in an angle to make room and beds look bigger, decoration is non exesting, but moreover we ended up in a hotel we didn't even choose. We have requested reimbursement, but had no answer to any messages. Feeling very fooled and deeply disappointed.

title: Not a place to stay but very friendly staff
text: This hotel is a dump, smells like sh.. And not at all a place to stay but in the other hand very very nice and friendly staff. They tried hard to make up for the hotel but ... Rooms are so bad you can hear next door person snoring, crap breakfast that I had to leave every morning and eat out.

title: A cupboard for the price of an Hotel room
text: We've booked for three night but we cancel the last one as soon as possible when we enter the room. A very small room, smelling sewers with a poor bed, and with a gum on the wall?? The breakfast room is underground and don't expect for an english breakfast, you will only have the bred and the marmalade. Yes it's in a good location, close to the metro but for this price we found a better place for our last night.

title: Notting Hills gate Hotel
text: Very small rooms and breakfast hall apart, the Hotel is good situated, no noise, confortable and very clean. People are friendly and everything was OK.

title: Not worth the money
text: Tiny box room in the attic up four flights of narrow stairs. Our bed was on casters and moved around in the night. No hot water and breakfast was terrible. All for the bargain price of £105. Don't bother.

title: Frustratingly small
text: I think my review is going to be pretty much the same as the others. Didn't have any problems to make me hate this place but there are issues. So I'll start with the good points: Great location - Notting Hill is a lovely picturesque area. Portobello road is amazing, Hyde Park starts just down the road, Notting Hill Gate Underground Station is 3 minutes away, it's also a walk away from Queensway & Bayswater which has alot of nice restaurants, also I found the staff in the hotel nice and helpful. But....Now the bad points: The first thing we discovered when arriving was that the front of the hotel was covered in scaffolding. As we walked into the hallway we could see this place was small. This place is basically a converted town house. They have crammed as many rooms into this building as they can. Our room was 2 flights up but i saw rooms on the basement level (wouldn't've liked one of them). When we got to the corridor where our room was there was a hoover outside the door which was there for the entire stay. The room was tiny. There was 2 single beds pushed together with a sheet on top. The right side of the bed was pushed to the wall and the left side had a 2 foot walkway. There was no wardrobe, just a rail on the wall but had we hung our clothes there, we would have blocked the space leading to the side of the bed so we had to live out of our suitcases for 4 days and with nowhere to store our suitcases, this made the room even smaller and more claustrophobic. The TV pixelated when you plugged something in, touched the wall it was attached to or even simply walked past it. The bathroom was actually fairly big considering the size of the room but had absolutely no surface to put your toilet bag. Workmen outside our window banging on the scaffolding in the morning was pretty annoying too. 2 Stars would be more appropriate in my opinion.

title: 2 night-stay
text: I was with my family (we are 4) 10 days ago in this hotel. We chose this hotel because we wanted to be together in the same room, a central place and also a good value for Money experience. The hotel is near the tybe station. However, it has no elevators and if you come early and want to leave your things in the hotel (in a luggage room, for exemple), you need to leave it in the breakfast room, very accessible to others and because of that, very unsecure. The room is very small and the bathroom is the smallest one I have ever seen. The room was apparently clean. However, in one drawer we found a peace of underwear, which means that the standards of this hotel are not that high... The room was also very hot inside and we weren't able to turn the heater off. You need yo leave the room keys at the reception, which is something I don't understand. It wasn't a big deal for us, because we stayed most of the time out of the hotel. The best thing is the localization, but I am not sure if it will be enough to come back.

title: Great location, basic hotel
text: Stayed here 11th til 14th of May.Great location 2mins from tube. very basic room. we were in roon 1 and the path outside the hotel was jus above our heads when in bed so was bit noisy but bearable.great price for such a well located hotel.glad we comprimised standard for location.we didnt spend much time in room as were out sightseeing whole time. wouldnt reccommend if planing on bein in room a lot.staff werent that friendly.they werent rude but just werent the friendliest.breakfast was included but didnt have it any of the mornings as got up too late but because price so cheap didnt care.

title: we enjoyed
text: I read some of the previous reviews expecting very little when I went. But seriously, it is great value for the amount of money I paid.The staffs were friendly and helpful when needed. the location's is excellent.The room was clean and tidy and was pleasant,I will recommend this hotel to others.

title: never will stay at this hotel again!
text: Booked a single room. When I arrived, it turned out there is no toilet in this room! The administrator kept telling me, but it has a shower, like it is enough. The single room itself bears no critic. I canceled my reservation and found another hotel nearby.

title: Charming hotel in Notting Hill
text: Nice location, near underground and buses. Close to Portobello Road. Nice restaurants in the nearby area. Clean rooms, our room was very small but still ok for three The breakfastroom was very small and the breakfast was mediocere.

title: Comfortable beds only
text: The reception staff were very friendly and the room and en-suite very clean if very cramped. Although continental breakfast is included, again, the breakfast room is extremely small and uncomfortable. One cannot move or see what's on offer, the pastries were stale and the selection was very limited. The staff spent more time chatting than taking care of residents needs, you had to seek them out if you needed anything. The uniform made me feel as if I was back in hospital. Ward sisters Blue tunics!

title: Half-term trip to London
text: Whilst the website refers to a recent refurbishment I feel it would still benefit from a tidy-up. The location is great with underground and Hyde Park on the doorstep but due to the large number of stairs I would avoid if your party has young children or elderly members. The breakfast room is tiny with a basic spread, our room slightly tired - the beds probably needed replacing - and like some of the photo's the 'aircon' was provided by a desk fan fitted to the wall. The tv and wifi worked well but you got the impression some of the furniture had been thrown together. Would I go back? Its a so-so hotel with a great location. If you are looking to visit London on a budget then I am sure you can do worse. One major concern however was overhearing one of the receptionists suggesting a 4% credit card charge on a newly arrived foreign couple, I do not think that this was right or proper.

title: Not recommended!
text: The manager was rude. The rooms tiny, the beds were made, but the sheets were not changed. It's a five-floor hotel without lift. We had to carry our luggage for five floors. The Wi-Fi was not working properly on the top floor and the staff refused to check it. The breakfast room was tiny, one had to wait in a queue to get a table. The breakfast itself is very basic and the coffee horrible.

title: Not luxury but fantastic price and brilliant location
text: Second time we've stayed, it's a place to dump your bags and go. The location is superb, right in the heart of Notting Hill and within walking distance of loads of restaurants, Portabello Road Market (5 mins walk round the corner), Notting Hill Gate station etc. I can understand why some people would expect luxury, I have stayed in both the top floor room others have complained about and also in the pokey downstairs room. However, first time we paid £45 and we just paid £38 for a Sunday night at the weekend. For that money, I have no complaints. Two night previously, we stayed in nicer and much more expensive apartments in Southwark. As nice as they were, and walking distance from Borough Market, they were down a side street and it took 10-15 mins to get to the nearest tube walking through a slightly dodgy looking area. In conclusion, if you want luxury, put your hand in your pocket. If you're looking for an acceptable place to stay in a great location in London for a very cheap price, stay here.

title: WARNING!!!
text: Please check when you book this hotel that your room is not described as a double on the ground floor. We booked a double ensuite, what we got was a single with a double bed in it, no room to move, a shower that was impossible. It was so hot that we had to have the window open, there was a nest of pigeons flapping and cooing all night and the family below who had no regard for guests, i had to shout at them to be quiet late at night. Pillows (one each) were rock hard. The room itself was spotlessly clean but unbearable, no storage for luggage. Breakfast was included ,a selection of a boiled egg or cereal or toast but with all guests in one 'breakfast' room the size of a shoebox, we ended up eating out. The other rooms may be fine but just be warned about the ground floor doubles.

title: Horrible hotel and staff
text: This hotel is not somewhere you want to stay. Was going to stay but walked out with no refund or understanding/help to fix issues. The rooms are extremely claustrophobic, the staff are not friendly or want to help out. Rooms are clean but rest of hotel is filthy.

title: Excellent location, value for money
text: We spent 5 nights in February, and it was a great option. We read all the reviews and found them to be exactly true: the room wasn't so small but we booked a triple, because we saw that the rooms were very small. The breakfast room was tiny, so we tried to go as early as we could. The location is excellent, the room was properly cleaned every day, and the staff was friendly and helpful. The neighbourhood is gorgeous! Close to Kensington Palace, and the V&A and Natural History museums. The hotel is two blocks from the underground and there are suoermarkets, drugstores, souvenir shops and restaurants really close by.

title: Okay, but with some flaws
text: Stayed here with a friend late January for a couple of nights. The hotel has one good thing going for it: location. And one major downside: cleanliness. Pros - Location: near Notting Hill tubestop (5-8min), a 10-15 minute walk to High Street Kensington with a lot of shops (M&S, Whole Foods, New Look, H&M..) - Lot of shops nearby - numerous restaurants and small shops - The staff were always friendly - The bathroom looked all new or newly renovated Cons - Noisy! There was a LOT of noise all through the night. Our room was located downstairs, below street level. All evening and night you could hear water running and/or dripping, doors slamming etc. Especially the fire door outside our room made a lot of noise when people entered and exited through it. - Cleanliness: no bugs were observed, but the room somehow felt a bit dirty. There were a lot of hairs that did not belong to either of us (dark hairs - we're both blonde) on the carpet, the sheets and pillows. Not very appealing, and worrying, as they always appeared even though the cleaning crew did our beds every day. All in all: It's simple, conviently located, but don't expect too much (even if it's Notting Hill). It's okay if your plan is to sleep there, and if you're not a light sleeper. The breakfast (included) wasn't all that, and the room (we ordered a triple room, but we're only two - and I can't imagine being three in there) is cramped and gets stuffy when someone takes a shower. But- there's air-condition, the breakfast is included and we were in London to see London, not our hotel! :)

title: Great location , good value.
text: I must say the position of this hotel is great. Notting hill is B-E-A-utiful , and I love the fact that you have a park that it's so close to you. Tube and buss accessible . I must admit that they don't have an elevator which is a big NO - NO for those(girls/women) with big luggages because it is almost impossible to carry it (if you have a room somewhere upstairs). There is no one to help you with it. Breakfast room was very very small. Overall it's ok for younger people that visit London with friends and just need a place to crash and have fun and visit London.

title: Great Location, great value for low cost!
text: Before we went, as usual I read the reviews and prepared myself for small rooms, flights of stairs to walk, rude staff and compact breakfast room. We did get the compact breakfast room, it's too small for a hotel. It felt over crowded and could hardly move when you are sat down. The food was ok though, what you expected for continental breakfast, it's just a squeeze to get to! However, the other negatives I read about didn't happen. We were greeted by friendly staff and our room was on the ground floor so no stairs! Our room had two double beds and single bed in, still had enough room to walk around in...my daughter actually managed to dance around the room! The bathroom was tiny however fine for one at a time. The TV didn't work at first, my husband had to fit the Ariel and change the language but it was fine after! The location is great, few mins walk from the tube and a few stops to central London for sight seeing. Restaurants within walking distance and right by Kensington Palace, Hyde Park for a stroll to the sights. I would return to the hotel for the cost, location and comfortable stay.

title: Cheap yes...
text: I think we were not the only ones trying to have breakfast in the ridiculously small breakfast room (chairs piled back to back) who regretted our choice. Cheap in all ways. Unfriendly "staff", noisy and small rooms. Etc. Etc...At check-in, we were told to pay in cash or get an additional 30£ fee if we paid with credit card. What could be the reason for this? Choose a different hotel.

title: Convenient for tube and perfect for overnight stay
text: Had a single room which was small as I expected. Width about size of 2 singles but enough space. Turned off plug-in radiator as room warm enough. No wardrobe but plenty of hooks behind the door. Tiny shower, toilet, but very clean and shower was great. Tea and coffee plus kettle, which I filled with the cup as kettle awkward to fill from washbasin in bathroom. Breakfast room was small but I got a table. There was great coffee, ham, cheese and hard boiled eggs plus bread and toaster. Reception staff were lovely and helpful. Good wifi in the room plus TV at end of bed, which was very comfortable and I slept well. I would stay there again as it suited my needs.

title: Great location and customer service on a budget!
text: Have to say, wasn't expecting a great deal when booked for just £47 per night per room including breakfast but have to admit i was pleasantly surprised. Staff were very welcoming and the hotel was very clean. Decor looked a little tired and breakfast was a tight squeeze and limited in choice. Overall, for this kind of money, and 15 minutes away from central tourist attractions by tube (station 5 minutes walk from hotel), it could only be considered great value and i would not hesitate in returning.

title: Good enough
text: Room was a bit too hot, but over all clean. Breakfast is served in tiny room, and was difficult to sit in same table our five person group. Maybe would not return. Also could hear neighbour room noise by nights and a lot of traffic noise.

title: Smallest Breakfast Room In The World
text: If you just want to stay close to the West End and don't want to do anything more than sleep at your hotel, then this might be for you. However, it you don't fancy carrying your bags up 4 flights of stairs, and if you actually want to be able to sit down for breakfast, then you might want to choose somewhere else.

title: Brilliant
text: For the price and location this place is a bargain. Not fancy but clean and service with a smile . People will moan but you get exactly what you pay for and a little bit of brekkie for your bucks. Close to Hyde park.

title: issues
text: As everywhere in the core parts of London this place is overpriced and undersexed. The bathroom is accessible only via the hallway and weekly cleaning service did a less than proper job. None of this too bad if The Collective organization had been honest and open about issues and a few other things. Furniture looks new on photos, but desk was basically junk and mattress more of hostel quality. Rooms have giant TV screens but basic service in other areas is lacking or very poor. Basically a place were they want to make money real fast without providing the service for it.

title: Too many problems, too little service
text: Well, there is so much to tell: the managers were extremely impersonal and unfriendly. When we drew their attention to the fact that our bathroom doors had no locks and no hooks, they said they had had the locks removed intentionally to improve the security and safety of its guests! Can you beat that? The breakfast area was totally cramped and horrible. Guests kept clashing into each other. The food was so-so, but the seating area was terrible. The family room we had for four adults was completely unsuitable for us. There was no room to walk about, and the window faced a wall. I suspect strongly that the good reviews are not genuine. There was nothing to like.

title: Great location
text: We just stayed for three nights. Pros Great location 24 hour reception and very clean small but functional room. Fresh towels were left everyday. Cons Like some others have said the breakfast room is very small and feels claustrophobic. Some people had to queue to get a seat which made me feel uncomfortable as I felt I had to hurry my food. This was the same everyday. Cornflakes,toast, croissants, sliced cheese and ham. Plenty of this though as it was topped up and there was plenty of butter and jams on the tables. Next big one for me was the stairs. We were only on the third floor but being a larger person I found it difficult to get up 70 steps two to three times a day which puts me off returning. We were in room 20. I believe that there are 5 floors in total. The bathroom was small but very clean. Only problem I had was a large step into and out of the shower. Again this is due to a problem I have with my knee. Perhaps the management should consider a grab handle in the shower to help with this. Having said this don't let this put you off staying here. It's a great base to visit Hyde park. Marble Arch and it's just round the corner from Kensington. The bus runs right past the end of the street two mins walk away and the Notting Hill Gate tube station is about a 5 mins walk away. we used a visitor Oyster card to get around. Had I been more able bodied I would use this hotel again. For our evening meals. We found a great pub a couple of streets away the old swan. I would recommend it after a full days sightseeing and shopping. Food was fantastic. See separate review

title: decent hotel
text: Good location and neighborhood, nice exterior, inside carpets, clean and quiet, friendly staff and at the time of booking was very good price. That people would most likely not like is narrow stairs to 5 floor and very small room (they have also bigger rooms, so it is lottery). Also breakfast is continental and served in so small place, that there is no place to sit and eat, especially if there are more guest, who are so fat, that sit on 2 chairs (this is not hotel to be blamed). Luckily or unluckily for us we got some kind of food poisoning in London so breakfast was not any more a problem, but I missed really english breakfast I had in my previous trip to London 10 years ago as there is so poor eating opportunity in London nowadays and mostly is only junk food available or good spicy asian food, but not an option for kid... Wifi was good, rooms were clean and service was good.

title: nice accomodation
text: nice location next to Hyde Park, cozy tiny rooms with very small bathroom, breakfast everyday the same, there is possibility to leave laguages for some time during last day, close to Sience and Natural History Museums

title: great stay
text: my family went to London for a couple of days to see Shrek the musical. this hotel was perfect for our two night stay. The staff were pleasant and very helpful. the room was very comfortable. we had a family room which was perfect for our family of 5. Breakfast room was a bit small but it got the job done. at the end of our stay we was able to leave our luggage at the hotel all day for a small charge of £5 which gave us an extra day to look around. Overall we really enjoyed our stay.

title: Good position and clean!
text: We've stayed in this hotel for 6 nights and our room was cleaned every day, towels changed every day. Excellent! The 2 cleaners were very kind and efficient! The hotel is close to the tube station and you can reach every part of London very easily. The only negative things are that the rooms are really too small... our room even didn't have awardrobe. We had to leave our clothes in the luggage or hanged around... Also the breakfast room is too small (only few tables) and almost every morning you have to wait to be seated... Finally it's a good hotel if you go to London to sightsee and you use it just to sleep.

title: Inattentive service, cramped conditions, poor ventilation
text: The rooms stayed miserably hot as the windows barely opened and our fan was constantly turned off by cleaning staff. The front desk wouldn't give us the wifi password before check in so we could find things to occupy our time. Also, the wifi cut out every thirty seconds. The breakfast was very limited and the dining room was horribly cramped. Thankfully, there are a few cafes nearby that have a reasonable breakfast selection. Of the four times that I've traveled to London, this was the worst stay that I can remember. The water pressure and temperature were good, aside from all of the things I didn't particularly care for. The ceilings/floors were thin and I could hear everything that our upstairs neighbors were doing throughout our stay. On the bright side, it forces us to spend less time in the hotel and more time in the city. The location was very close to two different underground stops and was a prime location for easily getting around London. That alone warrants three stars.

title: NOT 3* no window in room loads of steps paid £311 could not stay for health reasons NO money given back -
text: Checked in at 01.30am to this hotel due to delayed flight with my daughter. Paid £311 given key and man on reception pointed to stairs. Four flights with doors to tackle and suitcase as no lift. Dusty carpet and so many steps I think about 80 had my daughter needing her inhaler as she is asthmatic. Got to the top and found the room with difficulty. Top of hotel went in and it was a tiny room with a very small bedroom and NO WINDOW. My daughter burst into tears and being asthmatic needing air could not stay. I went down to speak to the man to ask for another room and he could not care less said no other room I said I couldn't stay but he said there was nothing else. Eventually he said I could sleep in the breakfast room. He pointed didn't take me to the downstairs room. It was very small and again no window and was untidy and unclean. I asked for my money back so that I could find somewhere else to stay. He said no. We sat on the hotel steps until 4am During this time I asked booking.com to help us and was told they were hopeful we could get our money back. We didn't want to stay not only because of the steps and the room without a window but that as we sat there for those hours we saw the bread on the floor for the breakfast and the eggs and cheese left out. I have received an email from the hotel who took my money very quickly and have said due to their cancellation policy no refund will be given. I didn't expect to arrive at such a poor hotel otherwise I would have cancelled. So BEWARE - its a great location BUT there is NO customer service at this hotel the steps are AWFUL there is no visible fire escape and the room at the top of the hotel has NO WINDOW. and goodness knows what breakfast is like. I could not afford to lose so much money but it was better to sleep on steps. NOTE TO SELF: read trip advisor before booking anywhere!!

title: Good hotel
text: We had good access for our family, good price. Looks clean and healthy inside. It has great convenient location. We came back to stay again. Shame I haven't booked this one for 2016, as I booked another one more expensive and quality was terrible!!!

title: Excellent location, all you need
text: For my first time in London, this was a great place to stay. Very basic (and small) room, but complete with a private bath. Close to tube and a nice walk to many local amenities and attractions. Staff was friendly, and hotel was quiet.

title: Excellent location, good value for money
text: Walking distance from Kensington gardens & Hyde park and portobello road. Close to metro station and bus stops . The room and the bathroom are small and essential. We had no wardrobe. Ideal for a short staying. And for those who are used at sailing boats. Breakfast is also essential. Ideal for a short staying. Close to the hotel many coffee shops and bakeries.

title: Not recommended
text: Where do I begin? First I will say we didn't book this, our now former Tavel agent did. Secondly we are from the USA so I suppose a touch of cultural bias towards our ideas of what a hotel is should be noted up front. Rooms small and not well appointed at all. Very uninterested front desk person(s). Bathrooms small, and I mean SMALL. No ventilation short of trying to open windows. Says wifi available, still scratching my head on that one. Five floors, steep stairs, no lift or even a hint of assistance in dragging our bags all over the place. The plus side is the young lady cleaning the rooms and working the breakfast room

title: Romantic long weekend in London
text: Everything worked very smooth. Nice staff that was very helpful. The room was a bit small but it had everything we needed for a weekend. Perfect location very close to the underground station which took us to London in just 10-15 minutes. We had a great experience and would gladly choose this hotel again if we were to return to London!

title: Basic Value
text: Although the room was clean, there are rooms in the basement, which is what I had. These rooms are extremely small. The breakfast is very ordinary and the breakfast room is also very tiny. Often you have to wait to have a table. Be prepared to bump elbows with other people who are trying to help themselves to the continental breakfast .

title: For the price we paid, we loved it!
text: It was a last minute grab of any hotel since I was running out of time. Thankfully I made the right choice! The rooms were cozy with a touch of class. The place must have been newly refurbished since everything was just clean and in place. I think for the price we paid, we had a good deal. Did not expect anything close to this since the previous hotel we stayed in Paddington wasnt up to mark. Just less than 10 mins walk from Notting Hill tube, u can grab Starbucks on the way and dont even realize you've reach the hotel. The guys manning the front desk were helpful too and accomodated our requests. I'd recommend this hotel anytime to my friends!

title: Apart from the position ... This should be completely review.
text: This should be a budget hotel for the poor quality of service offered, old rooms, small toilettes, old furnitures, old windows you cannot even close ... But I paid 100 pounds for a single use room. Hotel gave me a quad room but most probably because they did not have single rooms ... Breakfast is very very poor in a small room of 9 square meters, a continental breakfast very bad served ... Butter left on the tables with no ice, chees standing on a table to the air not protected from bacterial .. Receptionist are very kind and offers good service but I cannot promote this property at all. Price should be the half, breakfast should be reviewed and management should look better about many things like staff lefting cleaning products and instruments on the entrance to the bakfast room near the food! Location is good and easy to find just 300mt from Notting hill tube.

title: RIP OFF!!! BE CAREFULL!
text: Tried to book this hotel with a debit card and was told very adamantly that they were unable to reserve a room for me with this type of card as they dont accept debit cards!!! - then to my astonishment they charged me (yes on the same card!) half the full price for not turning up! After reading other reviews, seems they can charge whenever they like for whatever they like even without your premission then refer you to some dodgy small print on their website!! Staff rude and accused me of lying when I tried to discuss the issue with them - stay away!

title: Stuffy and cramped
text: We booked a room for four people and there were two beds in which we barely fitted. The room was very small, there wasn't even a space to open your suitcase. The twin beds were so small that we had to sleep adult+child. There was only one bedsheet for both who slept in the same bed, we had to ask for more bedsheets. The room was really stuffy, even though we had the windows open all the time. Bathroom smelled moldy. There was only an overhead shower in a very small shower space, making it impossible to shower without washing your hair. Breakfast was very basic and didn't include anything fresh. Breakfast room was very small and very crowded. We had to wait in line to get a table. The wifi in the room didn't work well enough to send, open files or upload anything, so basically it was like not having wifi at all. The area is very nice, but the hotel is not.

title: Tiny but good position
text: I had book a single room and yes I have to admit that the size was very much like a closet. The hotel though it's clean enough, breakfast room tiny and used to store luggage too but the location it's great! If you get a reasonable price it's OK. Ah they charge you to leave the luggage...not very good customer service, it should be for free even if it's not The Plaza!

title: Value for money
text: The breakfastroom is to small.

title: Surprisingly good
text: I needed a cheap place to stay in central London for business (mine, with a small profit margin!) for one night and came across this on Late Rooms. Given the low price for a pretty central location I didn't expect much but was very pleasantly surprised. I had a ground floor room (7) which was actually a triple. Now, I have to say it would have been distinctly "cosy" with two people and I certainly couldn't imagine three occupying the two bed AND wanting to move around. But for me alone it was just great. The bathroom was spotless and obviously new, wioth a lovely shower. (As others have said, there was an odd lack of hanging facilities in the shower, though!). The WiFi was excellent which was handy and it really is a fantastic location, a minute form a major bus stop and less than five from the Tube (Zone 1, too). I didn't have breakfast. I was leaving very early but as others have said the breakfast room is tiny and £4 bought me a breakfast elsewhere before my job. The breakfast room was also where left luggage was stored, which wasn't brilliant, although my suitcase only had my dirty shirts and underwear in it, so any thief would have had a bit of a let down to say the least! I wasn't asked to pay for left luggage, either, as some have mentioned. The positives much outweigh the few negatives. I paid more for much less in London in the past. Would use it again.

title: Not fully convinced I didn't share the room with other living creature.
text: I stayed there during a business trip to London in February 2014. Whilst the location was fantastic, everything seemed to go downhill afterwards. My room was up four flights of stairs. The further up the stairs we went, the thinner the carpet was. By the time we finished our ascent to the top of Everest (4 flights felt like 20) I was ready to end my day without attending my meetings but what greeted me motivated me to begin a quick descent. The local cats in the area all breathe a sigh of relief in this establishment as none of them will be swung in here. The curtains had a stain which wasn't quiet brown and wasn't quite red. Perhaps I'll leave those closed, I thought. Until the cold London winds greeted me through an open window. This very old building was non negotiable and the window was wedged open. I left ASAP. When I returned later that night, our hotel had transformed into a discotheque for all sorts of wildlife. My quite room peaked with the movement of multiple creatures running around the floor. Possibly looking for their relative who had died some time ago , in the bathroom by the smell that lingered in there. Eventually when I drugged myself to sleep, the size (or lack there off) came back as my feet rested on the radiator which was left on (probably by way of counteracting the always open window). The next day I left ASAP. The staff were friendly but this hotel needs a good cleaning and a renovation.

title: Easter 2016
text: Very nice small hotel from outside, but inside with a lot of rooms. Small rooms but enough space to be and sleep, very small bathroom but still clean. Small room for breakfast but if you come early there are room enough. It's not the last time I book room here.

title: No help when baby split head open!
text: First of all, I will say that the room was okay, it was cramped but there was room enough for myself, husband and baby (11 months at time of stay). There were fans and windows in our room so the temperature was fine and while the breakfast room is small, it does the job. However, both nights we stayed, our bathroom was absolutely filled with the smell of cigarettes, I can only assume from the next room, and my main point : My daughter slipped on the laminate flooring. She fell into the bed side table and split her forehead open, which as you can imagine is very scary for any parent. My husband ran down to reception while I tried to stop the bleeding, and was given a plaster and an alcohol wipe, and told the nearest hospital was 20 minutes away on the bus. We called Nhs24 and we're sent an ambulance. The man at reception was completely disinterested, had no sense of urgency and didn't even enquire as to whether my daughter was okay when we went out to the ambulance. Appalling behaviour, no excuse whatsoever. I realise this is an unlikely circumstance, but to have a stocked first aid kit and a little bit of sympathy for worried parents, is not a lot to ask. We spent the evening in A&E.

title: good and affordable
text: Location was close to the tube which really is the way to get around London. Its a bit far away from central London but if your looking for an affordable option its a great one. Be early for the breakfast as it is always PACKED. *** Be aware they will take money as a security that you wont get back for a few weeks ***

title: Tiny prison cell
text: The tiny room reminded me of a prison cell. There was no space for my suitcase except under the bed. I could hardly turn around and I could not close the door of the super tiny bathroom behind me. There was no real window, you could not see the outside world and the sky. Depressing! The room is very close to the reception and I heard everybody leaving / entering the hotel. The breakfast room was too small for all guests and very uncomfortable. My only positive remark: The bathroom was quite new and clean. If that had not been the case, I would have checked out of that hotel right away and looked for another one.

title: Worst Hotel in Notting Hill
text: This hotel had many things wrong with it. First and foremost the Hotel staff were completely incompetent and unwilling to help or solve any of the problems we encountered on our stay. The top floor of the hotel suffered dreadfully from the stench of Sewage. The room did not have a window, and the plumbing in the room was awful and every time a tap was used or the toilet flushed the stench of sewage swamped not only the room, but the top floor as well. There was a constant noise wiring throughout the night which prevented us from sleeping. There was one thin bed sheet and no duvet provided and we stayed at the begging of November.
