The room did not even have the basic amenities, something you would expect for £90 a night. The continental breakfast consisted of a bowl of boiled eggs, a small container of cereal or the option of toast and Nutella – absolutely awful! When we complained to the hotel staff about the stench and the fact that we were quite possibly breathing in raw sewage the only answer we received was that there was nothing they could do - except hand over a bottle of 49p value bleach and cheap air freshener. They had no spare rooms and apparently knew of no other hotels in London in which to move us too and were unwilling to give us a refund or pay for another hotel room. After over half an hour of complaining and getting nowhere we had no other choice but to stay in the hotel room. The manger was apparently incognito and could not be contacted and coincidentally the ONLY member of staff authorised to make any sort of decision regarding everything.

title: If it wasn't for the great location, this would be one to avoid
text: My partner recently stayed at the Notting Hill Gate Hotel for 2 nights, having booked fairly last minute and it being one of the only hotels in the "right location" within our £150 budget. It really is a bit of a mixed bag: if location on a budget is your only concern then you'll be happy

title: Visiting our cousin in London
text: Very good located location wirh very good service and cleanliness. Maybe the rooms are too small but very comfortable. The breakfast room is very small too, but compensated by the breakfast quality. In conclusion I suggest this accomodation.

title: Nice basic hotel with good location
text: Very simple hotel, room was very very tiny but I didint mind. Location was the best

title: Excellent value for money
text: Excellent 4 nights, paid 45 punds per night including brekfest, location is very good, rooms very clean and service good. Breakfest included bread, eggs and cerials, but that was just extra for the price we paid. Recommend to everyone!

title: Everytime I come here I fell at home even if I'm so far away from home....
text: I saw so many bad comments, most of them left from people who should have a break and reflect before they say something. FIrst of all, you spend like you were in the Hotel of a little town in South Italy, considering that you are in the Center of London and moreover, the new Terravision Bus line from Gatwick stops 100 meters from the hotel. 2nd: you complain about the fact that the breakfast room is little, this means you go on holiday just to stay in the breakfast room. I came 4 times in to this hotel and I will always come here, everytime I come to London......

title: Small room
text: You get what you pay for when staying at Notting Hill Gate Hotel. The rooms are tight and on the limit to uncomfortable. Staff is polite but maybe not the brightest. The price included a western breakfast but we never tried it. There's a lot of other places in the area were you can have breakfast. The hotel is located 1 min from the Notting Hill underground station and from there you can everywhere. Hyde park is very close and the luxurious Kensington is not too far away. The hotel is good for 3-4 days of stay. If you are planning to stay longer I would look for something better.

title: Great location for visiting London - value hotel (double room means 1,5 size of bed = great value)
text: + 24 hrs recption + cleaning service, clean towels every day - room no.8 ground floor noisy and no view from the window. No A/C, No fresh air. We booked as room for 3 pers., but it has only 1,5 size bed + 1 regular size bed. - hotel say: Breakfast include

title: tiny but cozy hotel
text: small rooms, no elevator, breakfast area was so small only that 4 people could eat breakfast at the same time...but charming and cozy and clean rooms. not far from Portabello marked or the underground.

title: Dont stay at this hotel
text: i have just recently stayed in this hotel, june 2010, and i wouldent want to stay at this hotel again. From their website the rooms looks clean and nice. The hotel price was a bargain and the location is perfect, but i should have known that for a price like that, you get a pretty lousy hotel. The breakfast area was in the reception room. small, tiny and they has absolutely nothing to offer. Only jam and toast, but this is not the worst thing about this hotel. The house has approx 4 levels, and we got the room on the top of the house. With no elevator we had to carry our own suitcases through all the narrow staircases. Noone asked us for help, so the service was realy bad. Also we had to change room beacuse the room didnt have a window and NO aircondition!!!!!! i mean come on! a modern hotel needs aircondition. it was 30 degrees outside. it was hell! finally we managed to get a new room which was better, but the hotel staff said that none of the rooms had airocondition. realy bad! we were also charged an extra 10 pounds if we wanted to pay for the room with a visa card. that is just crazy! i have never experienced that before. They also dident allow us to pay by the end of the trip, like hotels normally do. Apart from a great location, i wouldnt want to bother to ever stay at a crap hotel like this ever again.

title: A Good 3Star hotel....we'd return!!
text: We chose this hotel after searching online, because they could accomadate two adults and three kids. We were a bit dubious due to some of the reviews online, but I can honestly say it was a really nice hotel. Our room was a good size, and very clean. It looked like the hotel had recently been refurbished. The bathroom was a good size, and clean. Staff friendly and helpful. It's located in a great location near the tube station, shops and restaurants. There was free wifi Only negatives were the breakfast room was small, and we had to que for 10 mins. Breakfast was either cereal, toast or a boiled egg. But it was ok There was no parking near by due to resident parking permits required. But we booked two days parking with JustPark car parking. , prior to leaving. The cost was £34, and the electric gated car park ( Melbourne House, Kensington Place) was just ten minutes walk away, and was excellent!! We received a text from the concierge that morning asking what time we would arrive, he came out to meet us when we did arrive. He gave us instructions on where to park, and a key fob for the electric security gates. We would return!,

title: Extremely small room
text: In the room there was only a queen size bed, supposed to be for 2 people. No possibility to walk around the bed, no wardrobe, no room to put the luggage, just the bed and a very small bathroon. A complete disaster we paid more than 70 £ per night. Payment @ check-in!!!

title: No consideration
text: I booked a room for business, but found out at 15:00 on the cancellation day that there will be a tube strike, so I couldn't make it. I contacted them immediately and they wouldn't waver the penalty, even though it was still on the same day (Penalty for cancellation after 10:00). I understand the necessity for penalties, but it wasn't on the day I needed to book in. They still had enough time to rebook the room. It was completely out of my hands i.e. tube strike, so they should have been a bit more considerate. I can understand why they have such a low score on all the websites!!

title: As expected
text: A great location that made it easy for us to reach the whole city fairly easy. The staff was very friendly and helpfull both before and during our stay. The room was very very small but since we only used it as a place to sleep and shower, it was great to the price. If I was going with children I'd book something bigger but for the two of us (my husband & I) it was as expected. Yes the breakfast room is very small but we came at 7 when it opened and had no problems.

title: It is a good hotel
text: I stayed for one night in this hotel. It offers a good value for money. My room was good. It is ideal for singles or couples.

title: It has location going for it!
text: I stayed at NHG Hotel from 6th-11th September 2013. The location was close to NHG tube station, Kensington Palace, a good street nearby for all sorts of food, close to Portobello Rd Markets. I was staying on the 3rd floor. No lift, no porter to assist with luggage. Room smelt like mould or mildew however I kept the fan on in the bathroom and the window open my entire stay so the smell dissipated. The room was small, had a queensize bed, a single bedside table and a hanging rack on the wall. Clean towels everyday albeit thin and about 20 years old. No bar fridge however there was tea & coffee facilities. The shower had no water pressure however was hot. Breakfast provided was a choice of muesli or cornflakes, toast with jams/marmalades, hard boiled eggs, tea/coffee and apple or orange juice. It was enough to kickstart the day to explore the city. If you just need a place to rest your head and nothing more then this hotel for price is ok. If like me at the end of the day you want to relax a little, enjoy a glass of wine before bed then probably not the best option. I did leave some plastic wine glasses in the top drawer of the bedside table for the next guest

title: Looks nice on the outside but paper thin walls and windows
text: I travel for work and need a place to relax at the end of the day and a quiet hotel. This was not my experience. 1st night - mid week, I stayed on the 3rd floor with a courtyard and it was quiet for the first 20 minutes until my neighbours came back and turned on their bathroom fan and left it on while they went out for 3 hours. Then they kept opening and shutting the fire doors and talking loudly. I was angry but knew there was nothing the hotel could do because of their lack of insulation in the walls. By 2 am the loud neighbours left and then by 5 am they were back turning on the bathroom fan. The next morning, I politely asked my neighbours were going to be back and if so could I please be moved. Sure enough, they claimed they did not hear the loud party and did not understand why I did not register a complaint. Ok so if I were to register a complaint, most likely they would not be able to stop the noise, esp. if they are renting their rooms to college age students. They kindly moved me and put me in the basement in a room facing the street with a single pained window so I could hear all the cars driving by, slamming their doors, and the click clack of people walking. I can hear my neighbours pacing their floor and slamming the doors even the fire door that squeaks open and shut. I hope to go for a run in Hyde Park before my long 10 hour day ... we shall see if I can pull off at least 4 hours of sleep.

title: Two Day Break Away
text: This hotel is ideal if you're looking for a short stay. It's close to NGH tube and on a FAB bus route to the centre of London, although we walked from Kings X then back again on our return, enjoying Kensington Palace and its gardens, Royal Albert Hall and strolling on to Buckingham Palace etc. The traffic was pretty tricky on Constitutional Hill, the taxis don't give an inch, but I highly recommend the walk, it was well worth it. We had an overnight stay sharing a triple room (3 generations of girlies, 20, 50 & 73) which was spotless. It had a large tiled bathroom and walk in shower.The breakfast was basic but there was plenty of it, including an abundance of fresh coffee. The dining room was in the basement but very tastefully decorated (a new stair carpet is needed though). The staff were very friendly and obliging. I would stay here again.

title: Worst part of our trip.
text: The best thing that can be said about this hotel is that it had an amazing location - just down the street from Hyde Park. The free breakfast consisted of bread/toast, croissants, or Danishes. Deli meat, cheese, coffee/tea,corn flakes and canned fruit. The room to eat in was small and cramped with five people. My husband went down to eat at 8:30 and it was packed with over 10 people and a line headed out the hallway. The bathroom was tiny, as was the room. But this is common in London. You had to return the room key to the desk upon leaving the hotel everyday. The most frustrating however was the fact that the window didn't lock. Being on the ground floor (which we did request) and not having a secured window don't leave peace of mid while we were away. Add to that the fact that people would stand right outside our window to smoke, this making our room and belongings stink, and that when my husband turned on the shower for the first time the shower head fell off (it was promptly fixed the next day), and this place left much to be desired - especially for the price we paid. Luckily - the weather was beautiful and the city made for a fantastic trip.

title: It's ok
text: Service was friendly enough. The room was very small, the very minimum possible, but very clean. Toilet was ok, only they probably have some issues with the plumbing since the water in the sower and the sink went down very slowly at times. If you're planning on leaving your luggage inside for the last day of your stay, be aware that they will charge you 5 pounds if you collect it after 2pm, although no indication was given beforehand. The luggage storage room is the breakfast room which is the smallest I've ever seen. Overall average/good value for money if you don't really care about high standards facilities. The location is excellent, 2 minutes walk to portobello market, three tube stations one/two blocks away, hyde park is just round the corner.

title: Great Hotel
text: I stayed here in February 2015 with friends. Our room was a good size with a gorgeous balcony overlooking the main street. Our beds were very comfortable and the room was really clean. The location is brilliant and for the price we got, it was definitely worth it. I would definitely stay again if I was returning.

title: short stay in Notting Hill Gate
text: We were in London visiting our daughter, stayed in a couple of flats for 8 day periods, this was just a fill in after returning from Paris late the night before our departure back to Australia, cost and location were important to us as it was just a bed for the night, we were very pleasantly surprised by this Hotel, we knew it was a great location but found it to be very clean, quiet and well fitted out, amazing value with a good breakfast included, had we known we probably would have spent a bit more time there and saved on the flat costs as we were eating out most nights and didn't require a kitchen.

title: Don't take the promo offer
text: They have four rooms downstairs, in the basement. Small, no windows, no air, terrible bed / shower, it's either too hot or having the air conditioning blow all night. That's what the promotion offers.

title: Average hotel. Get what you pay for.
text: We stayed in London for a few nights for a quick break away, but only stayed for one night in this hotel. The location was great. Plenty of convenience shops and tube station only a 2 minute walk away. We were on the top floor which wasn't a problem for us but for those who struggle with steep narrow steps then this isn't ideal for you...especially if you have heavy bags to carry, as no help was offered! I didn't go for breakfast as I don't usually eat first thing but my partner did and he was satisfied with the cereal and toast which was provided. No cooked breakfast was on offer. The room was extremely hot and had to have the window open all night, even after making sure the radiator was off. There was a fan on the wall but I found this only blew dust around which irritated my nose so I turned it off. The room was tidy and what I expected. There was a bad foisty smell in the room which was coming from the shower room. There is no window and only a small extractor fan. The beds described as "double" beds are only slightly bigger than a single. Overall it was an ok stay. We got what we expected so no complaints. I would suggest that the hotel gets a refurb as it is slightly dated and it needs more space for guests to have breakfast. Also as its quite obvious that a stair lift / persons lift cannot be put in, due to the small space and narrow stairs, help offered to carry bags up to the rooms as part of the customer service would be appreciated.

title: Few good points
text: The best point of the hotel would have to be the location, with restaurants and shops just steps away, and a 5 minute walk to the tube. The decor in the rooms is very nice and modern, and the rooms are cleaned well daily. The rooms however are tiny, we had a room with two doubles and for four people there is just no room to move. The space issue is a big problem at breakfast as you have to get up very early to get a seat, the breakfast is pretty poor (its really just toast) The rooms were very hot and stuffy when we visited and it would be really helpful if they could provide a mini fridge in the room. We were surprised that we were not able to make use of a communal fridge or even get an ice bucket. This hotel is suitable as a base at the most but I don't think it is worth the price as there are better budget options about.

title: Beware! You are worth more than this place!!!!
text: Our room was up 100+ stairs, top floor, no lift, extremely hot. The room was crammed with a single and a double bed. My son refused to sleep under the covers for fear of what might lurk beneath. Carpets filthy, walls filthy. Light fittings hanging off the wall. Big holes gouged out the walls too. Bathroom was tiny but better decorated than the bedroom and cleaner. I was embarrassed to take my family here. Would never use again. The price may sound inviting but come on guys, you are worth more than this place!!!!

title: Ideal location for London Tourists. Nice, cute neighbourhood near Kensington Park
text: We paid about 45 Pounds per night (late May2009) which included a continental breakfast. The hotel is located at the heart of Notting Hill. Only four minutes to Subway Station Notting Hill Gate, 5 minutes to Kensington Park. There are plenty of restaurants near by. Don't expect too much. It is a cute little hotel in a street like in the movie Notting Hill. It was clean but we had a room downstairs. You can see that the personell is trying to keep this place clean. For people that do a London trip and just need a place to sleep this hotels is perfect.

title: Awful!
text: The only positive thing I could say about this hotel is its location which is perfect. On arrival we were told our room was "up the stairs" but how many stairs! over 100! 6 flights, the last two of which were so steep and narrow we struggled with small suitcases. We asked for a change of room due to health issues but were told no. There are no lifts and this is not mentioned on any booking site. The room I would say was "compact bijou" to be polite, the ensuite provided interesting negioating skills (reverse in, drive out), the shower had 2 temperatures (boiling or freezing), and 2 speeds (flat out or dribble), and the easiest way to get dried was to reverse out of it and into the bedroom! I question how this hotel was ever given a fire safety cert as the room we had had no window other than a velux skylight that an agile cat would have struggled to get through. The breakfast room was compact bijou also, we had to wait for others to finish in order to get a table! the "fresh fruit salad" was freshly opened out of the tin! We were asked for £5 to leave the cases at the hotel after checkout, but the staff at reception had no change and proceeded to count out change from £10 in coppers!! He looked horrified when we suggested waivering the charge as we had struggled with the stairs! Yes the room was clean, and tidy and was cleaned daily. I'm struggling to find anything more positive to say! Give it a miss

title: Basic but good location
text: Reception staff not too friendly...effort to speak at all. Room on 4th floor so counted over 70steps to it as no lift. More steps down to breakfast area that was far too small and squashed together. Not good if mobility problems. Boiled eggs, slices of cheese and croissants only so not much choice. Hotel fairly clean but in need of updating. Location good..close to tube and bus stops. Short walk to bayswater. Across from hyde park. Hotel should be 2star.

title: Mixed
text: A Fullers pub and so should be good. Went for a late lunch and so fairly quiet. Unfortunately my chicken and mushroom pie was served with glutinous gravy and microwaved peas - not good. My son's fish and chips finally turned up when I had finished! Beer - good. Service - indifferent.

title: Like sleeping on the train tracks
text: The hotel is conveniently placed next to the train station, which is great, however this also has its downsides. The room was fantastic, modern and clean, great facilities, but when it came to sleeping there wasn't much of that. I slept for probably only 3 hours due to the fact my room (room number 4) was practically on the tracks. I could hear every train/tube train that went past. In the morning, I welcomed the wide choice of options for breakfast with open arms. The American pancakes almost made up for the loss of sleep, but just be careful when booking here that you end up on the other side of the hotel. However, if you're not overally fussed about noise then this is still a good hotel - although, walking through the pub with your suitcase and checking in at the bar feels slightly odd!

title: Cannot fault this hotel
text: We have just returned from another fantastic stay at the Wellington. We have stayed here a number of times and each time has been fabulous but now the rooms have been refurbished it's even better ! Mark and the staff cannot do enough for you, the hotel is in an ideal position for anywhere you want to go in London, lovely pub downstairs with great atmosphere and good food. Cannot fault and will definitely be returning again, would definitely recommend!

title: Excellent location, nice room, friendly staff
text: Stayed in the Wellington last week, for one night. If you arrive at Waterloo station on the Bakeloo line(like I did from Paddington) make sure you follow the signs to Jubilee line and then exit the station as this will exit you right opposite the hotel. That was a real bonus when I realised the proximity. So location, definitely - check! Check-in was quick and efficient and the hotel does offer to store your luggage before check-in or after check-out. There is no lift and there are a few stairs to climb to the first floor and even more past that(not sure how many as our room was on the first floor). For us that we only had one small carry-on it was ok, however for someone with a bigger and heavier luggage it may be a bit of a problem. The room is small, so is the bathroom. However both room and bathroom were very clean, sufficiently stocked and nicely appointed. Some people may find the shower cabin,the double bed and the sink a bit on the small side however for one night we were more than happy with everything. Also the bed and pillows were super comfy with very soft beddings. I won't lie, there is traffic noise coming through even with both sets of windows shut, however it didn't bother us as we are used to it. For someone who is used to quiet locations though, it can be a bit on an issue. The room temperature was quite high when we initially walked in the room but turning down the radiator worked a treat and kept a comfortable temperature throughout the night. We had both dinner and breakfast in the pub and I can't fault either of them, very tasty and nicely presented. The only thing I noticed that I didnt quite like was the musty smell on the corridor from the pub dowsnstairs to the rooms upstairs. Not much of an issue but is not really a good itro to someone going up to their rooms for the first time. All in all, a nice little hotel for one/two nights in London.

title: Great value, great service, great welcom
text: To start, lets get things clear, this is a 3* hotel (in fact the manager refers to it as a B&B). Having said that I've stayed in 4* and 5* hotels which could take lessons from The Wellington. The welcome can't be faulted and like other reviewers we were guided to the stairs to the rooms. I was expecting some rickety garret like staircase having read some reviews, but this was not the case. OK, it's not marble, glass and polished brass, more like your average household staircase, painted white banisters, neutral carpet etc. and the number of stairs aren't that excessive. We found our room (second floor twin) easily and were pleasantly surprise. Compact and bijou is probably a good description, one window with a desk and chair under, wardrobe, beds, 2 bedside cabinets, shelf with tea making facilities and a compact shower room what more do you want? Ok the view isn't great - we got the side of an office block and if you look sideways, the entrance to Waterloo station but we weren't there to look out the window. What struck me most was how clean it was - spotless white bedding obviously freshly laundered and made, massive fluffy white bath and hand towels - first time ever I've been tempted to pack the towels to take home with me (I didn't). Bathroom spotless with good quality complimentary soaps etc. Decent hairdryer with diffuser, tea, coffee, milk and biscuits, good mirror in room and another good one in bathroom, plenty of hangers in wardrobe and enough storage space for a week or more's stay and two sets of ear plugs on the bedside cabinet. Oh and a large flat screen tv on the wall. We ate at the Wellington before going out for the evening and the food was good quality, fast service and generous portions. It's one big bar but in 2 sections, one having lots of comfy sofas and chairs. What struck me most was how welcoming the pub was with a real cross-section of clientele from business men, to workmen, to foreign students, I'd quite happily make it my local if I lived in London. Being a rather light sleeper I was a little concerned about the noise, but I didn't need to be, unlike some hotels I've stayed in there was no banging doors and creaky floors outside the room in fact if we hadn't seen more guests at breakfast I could have believed we were the only guests. Outside there was some traffic noise but nothing excessive, in fact I looked out the window just after 8 and was surprised to see rush hour in full swing outside. Breakfast was good, freshly cooked to order and certainly set us up for the day and they are happy to store your baggage until you're ready to leave. The cons? The staircase and corridors are a little tired and could do with a spruce up (but I understand that Fullers have relevantly recently taken over the place so it could be in the pipeline) and there were a few minor maintenance issues - curtains wouldn't close (but then I'm pretty sure apart from Spiderman no one could have seen in) and the lid on the bin in the bathroom hinge was broken. I really can't believe our luck on finding The Wellington. I would certainly stay there again recommended for good old fashioned service, welcome and value for money!

title: we will be back
text: first of all i want to tell you that we arrived 2 hours early and with no where to go we phoned the pub/hotel whilst stood outside on the street. The pub was not open but the staff very kindly opened the door and let us in and were more than happy to relieve us of our luggage, then we were given our room as it was ready! Also on checking out they lock your belongings up if your train is later in the day so you can sight see bag free! This pub hotel is within hopping distance of waterloo station, we were in room 26 on the top floor and you looked out at the station! superb for the tube, the london eye is 5 min round the corner as was westminster bridge. You cross the bridge nd theres parliament not to mention big ben! anyway, the room was cosy but we only slept and showered there. The beds were so comfy and CLEAN. The shower super, and we all love a good shower. The brekkie was delicious and im a fussy customer. The room had a plasma tv, hairdryer and kettle with tea,coffee etc. Plenty of clothes space, extra pillows. If your not looking to swing from the lights then this is a great room and location for all of london. We managed to see most of london on foot by walking the length of the south bank, occasionally crossing to see things like st.pauls, the tower ,and we crossed the millenium bridge. Covent garden was close too. I never knew i cuold walk so far. All the places seem to link up and we found piccadilly next to leicester sqaure and soho. The boss is genuinly interested in you and is a jolly nice bloke. I cant think of one reason why we would stay anywere else, genuinly. At 5p shy of £90 for two adults on a saturday night in a prime location of London with en suite and full english preceeded by croissants, cereal, yogurt, fruit and juices, where will you get that? Good honest clean accomodation.

title: Horrible staff
text: Been there with my mom and boyfriend and asked for 2 peroni and a coffee: total amount..£15. Not enough, coffee horrible, cup filled up to the top, no milk could be added so we asked for some help to throw some coffee away in order to get some space.. Bar staff moody, frustrated and unprofessional refuses to do so. Just after 5 minutes another bar staff decides to be helpful and do what has been asked. Sticky tables, stinks of vomit everywhere, definitively not anymore in the life!

title: Short measures all round !!
text: This review is only about the pub not the hotel side. Ideally sited for Waterloo station and with large open bar areas and a good selection of ales make for a good meeting point. My gripe is that I had to wait about 15 minutes to get served due to the lack off staff. Then the drinks all came up well short of measure. As I was part of a large party the first few I let go ,then I had to start asking for each one to be topped up as it was getting a bit silly. These were not oversized glasses. I don't know if this is the norm or just poor training of the bar staff but as you are paying London prices you expect a full pint. It's a good job I don't work for weights and measures.

title: A budget hotel ........but done nicely!
text: The Wellington is remarkably good value. It would be cheap in this location at full price but is amazing if you get a late booking reduction. We only paid £50 and that included an excellent breakfast served by pleasant attentive staff! You are most likely to get a reduction on Sundays. The room was clean. The bed was very comfortable and the bathroom clean and functional. The location next to Waterloo Station is very convenient. The only down side is the noise. Contrary to some reports there is little noise from the station but there is lots from the busy road right outside particularly buses pulling away from the bus stop. Just when they finished for the night we were woken by a group of drunken yobs... not from the Wellingon. The bar was long closed by then. I should have used the earplugs provided but I don't like the things!

title: Pleasant stay in a great location
text: I've been by the Wellington many times and had to opportunity to stay in September 2015. You cannot beat the location - directly across the road from Waterloo Station. But, that plus is also a minus. The room was a bit noisy with road and rail traffic, but since I never travel without my earplugs, all was well sleep-wise. I had a lovely, clean room (just like the picture on the website) with a comfortable bed, safe, and nice bathroom. The bathroom was small, but the shower had great water pressure and all was very clean. The breakfast was stupendous with cereals, yogurt and a large cooked meal. I was thoroughly stuffed afterwards! The staff were really lovely and helpful. There is a private entrance for hotel guests, so you can come and go without the pub crowd. Would definitely stay again.

title: Fantastic location and an amazing place to stay
text: Stayed at The Wellington with a friend in their bunk bedded room!!! It was a lovely room on the first floor, please note, there are 2 more floors and no lift!!! The room and shower room were extremely well presented. The breakfast was included and very good and very large!! The Wellington is in a great location about 5-10 walk to the Southbank and The London Eye and we found it was about a 20 minute walk to Covent Garden. All in all a great place to stay for a reasonable price in a good location, I would definitely stay here again, and would recommend it as a place to stay.

title: As expected, small rooms above a large pub, very conveniently located to Waterloo station.
text: Summary: If am again in need of business accommodations close to Waterloo station, I would stay here again. I would not bring my wife here for a leisure visit as the room/bathroom is just too tiny. It is near the rail lines and above a pub—there is some noise from both. If you need to be close to Waterloo station (National Rail or tube), The Wellington cannot be beat in terms of proximity--it is exactly across the street. I arrived on a Sunday, from the US, at around 1:00pm. I was told rooms aren't available until 2:00pm, which was fine, and I had a meal in the pub. Once checked in (they collect the full amount for your stay upon check in), I walked up the stairs (there is no lift) to find my very small double bed room. Very small, but serviceable as I was on my own and traveling for business, so didn't intend to spend much time in the room. The bathroom is *tiny*. I am a big guy (6 feet and about 300 lbs/137kgs) and just barely fit in the wee little stall shower. Again, it was OK, but just. The rate includes breakfast, which is comprised of a continental buffet and a choice of made to order hot items, including a full English breakfast. I also had a couple of evening meals in the pub. All the food is absolutely standard London pub fare, which is to say completely OK, but I wouldn't go out of my way for a meal there. The pub is very popular with the after work crowd and, I assume, many people coming from, or going to, a train. It's busy, bordering on crowded, most evenings. Lots of TVs and game machines, and quite loud. Again, as expected, but by no means a "charming" pub (although these are nearly impossible to find in the city any more.)I did not find either the train or pub noise to be a problem, but I sleep soundly. Light sleepers might be disturbed. There is no laundry service available, but I used an app based service, Zipjet, which picked up from, and delivered back to, the hotel: brilliant. Pros: location, friendly staff (thanks, Kiera!), adequate desk, ample power points all over the bed room, good clean housekeeping. Cons: The wifi is a bit dodgy for business use. It's the Fuller's wifi, which is targeted at consumers in the pub, and it's fine for casual use, but I had some frustrations getting to some sites, and it was at times dreadfully slow.

title: real british
text: It's my first time. Fantastic experience ! Great atmosphere, good price. Very good location, just opposite the tube station., and very closed to south bank bars and pub. Nice crowd in the pub, very polite staff. The hotel offer a very good english breakfast. The single room to much little.

title: Just the ticket
text: Stayed with husband and 6yr old son. £105pn incl breakfast can't be beaten. Location was ideal with most places within easy walking distance. Rooms basic but spotless and comfortable. Excellent choice at breakfast and VERY tasty. Good choice on bar menu and 2 course kids meal with drink for less than £6 was great value. Pub gets very busy and even though we were over front entrance we werent bothered by bar or train noise, just general city noises. It was great to be able to return to bar for a few drinks knowing we didn't have to go out again for food with a tired child before going up to the room (unlike some featureless budget chain hotels). Final word has to go to Markk and his team for making us welcome and we look forward to seeing you again next year. Thanks

title: Decent Hotel
text: This hotel is priced fairly for what you get in a city like London. The staff was more than friendly and the accommodations were clean. You get a full brekafast as well where they will take your order and serve you. There is quite a lively pub on the bottom floor so families with small children beware. Overall I rank this a good find in London and it has a sort of charm that you wouldn't find in a big named chain.

title: Bad - Worse - Wellington
text: The Wellington Hotel takes the term 'dump' to a whole new level. Before I ever would spend another night at that place I'd rather sleep on a parkbench. ...which would most likely offer more relaxation. The railway tracks were located hardly more than 5 meters away from the bedroom window (see pictures, unfortunately couldn't upload a video to demonstrate how incredible noisy it was). As Waterloo Station is a pretty busy place, at least every five minutes a train was passing by which felt like it was going right through my room. That the room contained a bed folded up against the wall, no airconditioning, a bathroom so small that an overweight person probaby would have severe problems using it, moldy smelling stairways and a 'reception desk' where you got to register next to drunk people in a Pub, were small add-ons I got for spending 139 Pounds/night on that dosshouse.

title: Loved this place!
text: We were looking for a centrally located London hotel and stumbled across The Wellington when I typed in my daughter's address (she is studying abroad there.) What a find! After a 12 hour trip from California, I emerged from the Waterloo Underground station (on the Jubilee line, after transferring from Heathrow Express) and the hotel is across the street: perfect! A lively pub is on the ground floor, filled with locals meeting after work and to watch football (soccer for Americans). We took one cab all week because everything was so easy to get to from this hotel. Rooms are recently remodeled with modern and luxurious bathrooms, hard wood floors, and crisp white linens, daily. Staff is friendly and responsive, greeting us each morning with smiles & a menu of several delicious breakfasts, all included in the room price. Worth every pound ... I woud definitely go back.

title: Really good ...
text: I've stayed at The Wellington twice in the last few months and overall it is a really good hotel and value for money. The rooms are clean and spacious (for London), well equipped and comfortable. Single paned windows make for a noisy sleep, but that is the only complaint. The staff are incredibly warm and welcoming, nice selection of breakfast and a really nice pub. It is directly across from Waterloo Station, so easily accessible and a very short walk to Southbank. Will definitely book again when in this area of London.

title: True English pub
text: We didn't stay here, but had dinner here. Football(soccer) ,( Olympics) was on the telly and the fans were singing. You had to order your meals at the bar. The fish and chips and chicken pie were quite tasty.

title: Decent enough for the price !
text: Great location across from Waterloo . Busy pub , but I knew that when booking . Staff very friendly . Double Room was clean and decent enough size . Shower bathroom seemed recently re-done and was a lot better than I expected . Yes it will be noisy across from Waterloo and above a pub but that will be obvious when booking it ! Great breakfast served by friendly staff .

title: Could be a lot better
text: First impression is very good, you enter the Hotel's main entrance and you are greeted with a superb and very impressive bar, with paintings, Muriel’s and wood panelling, we arrived at 13:00 and had a drink in the Bar while we were waiting to check in at 14:00, the gentleman behind the bar was very helpful and polite. We were given our room swipe card and given details of how to gain entry to the Hotel part of the Bar, we were told what room we were in and shown the door that we needed to use, once through this door that’s when it went downhill, first of all No lift, stairs very narrow and very creaky, it was quite a climb to the second floor, on arrival at room the floor was making a lot of noise, we went into the room which at first view seemed quite pleasant, until we noticed the curtains on the main window only had one curtain hook holding one end of the curtain up so curtains would not close, I had to take 1 hook off the other curtain so we could close them, the wardrobe only had 1 hanger inside, and as we were there for three nights we had to leave our clothes in the suitcase as we could not hang them, also there were cobwebs around the celling other than this the room was ok, bed was very comfortable except for the noise from the trains, I know that other reviews have said about the trains noise but they do not give it justice, believe me when I tell you that the trains are so close to your window you can see the driver and the passengers and the trains go buy your window from 05:00 to 01:00, yes they do supply earplugs but they are no good. The most positive part of our stay was the breakfast in the morning which is first class, if you want a meal in the hotel at night then my answer to you is have it about 3pm as the pub gets very, very, busy from about 4pm till it closes at midnight, on our second day we came back to our room to find the door had been left on the latch by the cleaner all lights were on, so anybody could have walked into our room and taken what they wanted, also after the second night we only had bath towels no hand towels were left in the room, all in all we will not be staying in this hotel again, we are frequent visitors to London and thought that we would try somewhere different this time as we normally stay in the same hotel every time, this has taught us to stick to what you know, we will be in London again in May, we will be here for three nights again we will also have 2 other people travelling with us, and we will NOT be staying at the Wellington in Waterloo again. I hope this helps

title: Surprisingly good food
text: Stopped here for a drink with my girlfriend whilst waiting for our friend and we were struck by the food menu - very wide range of foods, good veggie options for her and some variations on standard pub fare that made us decide to stay and eat there. Food was as good as the menu promised, I.e better than most pub food! Close to the station so location is good.

title: More pub than hotel
text: We chose this hotel for location which was close to Underground, walkable to London Eye, Westminster Abbey, Tower of London, shopping, pubs & restaurants. The "reception desk" was a window at the end of a long bar. There are no elevators (lifts) to the rooms so you'd better have small bags or large muscles. Our room was on the 3rd floor after climbing up dark, narrow winding steps while dragging our luggage (challenging!). When we met other guests on the stairs one of us would have to back up to another floor because the stairwell was so narrow. The room was too hot even with being able to slightly open one window. It was rather noisy from outside noise but that's part of being in a central location so not complaining just making note for other travelers. Our friend made reservation 2 months before so he could meet us there. At check in they said they had no room for him. He finally got a room but it took quite a bit of time & negotiating. The plus side, (other than location) was the friendly staff (despite our friend initially being told he had no room) and a lovely complimentary breakfast. This is a VERY popular after work place for drinks. It was mobbed every night and we really felt that The Wellington catered more to their pub than to their hotel. In the end we just laughed, enjoyed the pub, the sights and limited how many times we climbed those stairs!

title: Welcoming stay at The Wellington
text: We was staying at this hotel due to being over in London for the NFL game at Wembley. We had researched the location and found that this was perfect for the underground (literally just across from Waterloo station). Upon arrival, we were checked in quickly and shown to our room. We were on the second floor, and there is only stairs to walk up. The room was well presented and modern with two single beds, tv and wardrobe. There was coffee and tea making facilities, with two packets of cookies. The bathroom was nice, however we did find wet toilet roll stuck to the seat, which I find unhygenic. The rest of the room was clean, there were a few marks on the wall, with felt tip pen, however this can not be removed. Location and value for money was key for us and both were really good. We got this room for £70 for the night, which is considerably cheap for London. We had a drink in the bar which came to a total of £8.50 which for us and coming from up north were we are used to £2.00 a pint was very exspensive! After talking to some locals they told us this was actually cheap haha! Breakfast was really nice, there was a choice of cold buffett alongside a full english breakfast, or you could have pancakes, breakfast baps etc. The full english breakfast was all fresh and gorgeous! The sausage was beautiful, and you also got bacon, egg, mushrooms,beans, hashbrown and toast. Upon checkout we left our luggage in a small cupboard were there was plenty of space. Overall a great central location, with a comfy bed for a over night stay.

title: Brilliant little hotel!
text: We stayed here as a couple for one night in April. We arrived quite late (around 9.30pm) but as this hotel is also a pub this wasn't a problem. The pub was packed when we arrived which made checking in extremely difficult. you have to check in at the bar area which you could barely get to there were so many people, and so loud you couldn't really hear what the staff were saying. There is no lift. We were on the top floor which you had to climb a very steep spiral staircase to get to. The room was small but perfectly formed. Very clean and neat. The bathroom only has a shower as its so small but again very clean. The room was stiflingly hot but if you open the window the train line right outside is disturbingly loud. The breakfast was pleasant enough, we got the full English which wasn't tiny but wasn't exactly big either. The staff we encountered in the morning were all brilliant. So friendly and happy.

title: Little gem in Waterloo
text: Despite my initial reservations at having to climb three flights of stairs to my room, I was welcomed to a delightful space with luxurious linen and towels, quality personal care products, ample tea and coffee and enough accessible power outlets to satisfy the most connected traveller. I appreciated my bags being brought up to my room on arrival and departure, this made the room location manageable. I found every staff member I encountered (from Reception to bar and hospitality staff) friendly, kind and helpful. Although the railway line runs a mere arms length from the building my light sleep was not disturbed once during the night and I did not need to use the earplugs thoughtfully supplied. The good choice of generously portioned cooked and buffet breakfast on offer with great coffee (I’ve been enduring European hotel machine coffee for the last 3 weeks so this was outstanding!!!) was a bonus. Due to a wearying chest infection, I did not feel up to anything much on my last day as I waited to depart to the airport. Although I sat around the bar for a number of hours waiting for the time to depart for my flight home, I was made to feel at home and particularly appreciate Mark’s care and attention to my comfort and welfare. Will definitely stay here again on my next visit to London! My thanks to all at The Wellington for a great stay.

title: Excellent location for tourists
text: We arrived early and staff helpfully stored our luggage behind the bar as the cupboard was full. Drinks were fairly pricey but there is a busy pub atmosphere in the bar. The room was cleaner than expected (the hall and stairs are a bit grotty) but we didn't get hand towels or ear plugs whereas our family in another room did. The room (17) was noisy but I didn't mind as it was good value and a central location for travel and tourism. Niggles: cups did not match and TV kept switching itself on. Our family down the hall were woken at 4am by brawling men in the room nextdoor but of course not the fault of the hotel. Food service was terrible. Forgotten orders, late side dishes, waiters that couldn't care less. Food was acceptable pub grub but don't expect restaurant standards.

title: Mid Week Break
text: We stayed for 3 nights. The room was immaculate, bathroom was sparkling. Many thanks to the bar staff who were efficient and friendly. They even knew us after the first night there and welcomed us each morning for breakfast. Bernie, responsible for the cleaning has a very helpful and friendly manner and goes out of his way to make you comfortable. Mark, The Landlord, is the friendliest landlord I have ever had the pleasure of talking to. His aim is to ensure that your stay is memorable in the best possible way. A wealth of tourist information and a very well respected landlord with locals. Thanks to Mark and his team, we had a very enjoyable and memorable stay and will certainly stay again on any future visit to London. Great service and it all comes so naturally to his team. Thanks. Rita (Margaret) McLeod

title: Affordable South Bank hotel with personality
text: British by birth, but resident in the USA, I return to London twice a year, always staying on the South Bank. There are 4 reasonably affordable Hotel options: the 2 Premier Inns, the 2 Park Plazas (County Hall and Westminster) and the Wellington Hotel. If you do an advance/prepay for the Park Plazas it puts them in approx the same price range. Reading through earlier reviews, many are very fair - clean and fun/funky underground themed rooms, substantial breakfast (choice of hot meals plus continental buffet included in price) and a young energetic team running the place. The pub is extremely popular, and I don't know if the noise would be an issue on the 1st floor of the rooms. I stayed on the top floor which is a bit of a hike up a good number of stairs but could only faintly hear the trains coming past as they have installed double glazing. Windows will open for those enjoying air and the sounds of the city (the only hotel of the 4 that is not hermetically sealed). The top floor was however a little warm, even in cool autumn temperatures, but there is a floor standing fan in the room so you can adjust to your preference. Best of all, there is no more than a 50 yard walk to the Underground at Waterloo, so the Wellington is a brilliant place to use as a base. It won't be the best fit for everyone - some might prefer the predictable design of the Premier Inns or be able to get a cheap deal at the Park Plaza (which is still my favourite due to mini-kitchen facilites in the room) - but take a look and make your own decision. I loved staying at somewhere with a bit of personality and overseas visitors might like to experience a bit of real London.

title: Weekend break
text: Value for money is excellent, its a short walk away from Big Ben, & literally over the road from the tube, which gets you to anywhere, very quickly, Its a pub, with rooms! the room was en suite, with a good shower, clean & tidy, it was not very big, & could probably do with a lick of paint, but thats my only moan! its only £95 a night, bang in the heart of London, & the breakfast is great, the staff are friendly, polite and helpful & It is a proper English pub with a great atmosphere, I cant really rate this place high enough, I've been to plenty of budget priced hotels in London, over the years, and this is definitely the best, by a country mile. Foreign visitors, would get a proper feel of London staying here. And check out the ceiling murals!! excellent.

title: Beautiful characteristic hotel in the centre of Waterloo!!
text: I stayed here with my wife when seeing a show in the area, the hotel is beautiful with amazing art work throughout. The bedroom was really well laid out with all commodities (TV, kettle, fan, toiletries etc). Really atmospheric area of town with lots to see and do and tube and bus stations around the corner. The freshly prepared breakfast was excellent and I actually struggled to finish it which is saying something as I can eat. The Wellington Hotel is a perfect place to lay your head if you want to stay in the area. We will stay again!!

title: Busy traditional pub
text: The Wellington was a great location for our hotel for a last drink before bed. This pub was big and busy, London pubs always become busy once the office is shut for the night and this is no different. The football was on, so it was a struggle to find a seat, but we did. Great pub though.

title: Great for football
text: Popped in for a quick pint on way to somewhere else, the football was on so the pub was busy but they had so many screens you could always have a decent view from where ever you stood. The food looked quite good so may have to go back at another time.

title: London trip
text: Fantastic location right by station. Good pub with solid menu. Included breakfast ok. Nothing fancy just basic. Family room on 3rd floor with lots of steep steps to climb and no lift is a challenge with anything beyond light luggage. Overall good value for a good location. Would consider staying again if visiting central london.

title: Great Hotel
text: Stayed for a long weekend, great location, facilities, atmosphere. Staff were very helpful and accommodating. Spent a night in the pub before retiring to bed and it was a great atmosphere. Breakfast was good the next day with cereal and full English available. Would definitely recommend , with easy access to the underground and the main attractions of London.

title: Weekend Visit to London
text: My husband and I had a most enjoyable stay at The Wellington Hotel. The location is fabulous, being so close to the heart of London. The pub was beautifully decorated and historic. A great unique pub with its own character which suited us better than staying in a faceless chain of hotels. The staff were really friendly and helpful. Our room was a typical double room, very clean with new bathroom facilities and a very comfortable bed. We were concerned that the noise of the trains would keep us awake, but with triple glazing and great black out blinds we had no issue at all. There was a fan in the room which was a great thought. We didn't have an evening meal, but the menu looked great and varied. The breakfast was delicious, with lots of choice of fresh fruit, breads and cereals and a varied hot selection to chose from. I understand from the staff there is a family room and would not hesitate to stay there again. If you would like to stay in a typical English pub with character and interest I would highly recommend it.

title: Great room + free Wifi + Great breakfast!!
text: We (Myself and Husband) booked a 2 night stay to do some touristy things in london. We booked direct on the pubs website, its run by Fullers brewery. This Pub is really easy to find, you leave waterloo by the east exit (come off the train and go down esculators towards mac donalds, pub is ourside on the left) Enter the pub and at the end of the bar on the left is a 'Hotel reception'. We were checked in promptly and given our key cards to enter our rooms, and they let you access the pub via a side door so you can come and go as you please after hours. Rooms are easy to find, the place has lots of signs to tell you where to go (not that you need it) the rooms have key card entry which is easy to use. The room we had (No.7) was well equipped, double bed, wardrobe, desk and chair with a large mirror. Shower, sink and toilet. Room was clean and decor was really nice. The bed was hard but im fussy so cant really complain about it. You are provided with a kettle, two bottles of water and a selection of tea, coffee and couple packets of cookies. The bathroom has a couple of shampoo bottles and a bodywash for you to use. We had fresh towels every day and the staff made our bed and cleaned our room every day also. (not sure if the bed was changed, but it was made for us). Week days breakfast is between 7.30-9.30am and its a fully cooked english breakfast, and the bar is also laid out with croissants, cereal, yogurts, fruit and a selection of juices and tea/coffee. The breakfast made the stay perfect, healthiest cooked breakfast i have had, good quality food is used, and they make it to order. A++++++ To them for the breakky! We had some food before we left to come home, and the lunch was lovely as well, The wellington Burger was about £10 and my husband said it tasted really nice, and was really filling. I had a Cheese and pickle sandwich with chips, which was really good and cost £5.95. Points to mention are: This is a nice hotel for the price, and you are really central (we paid £124 for 2 nights, and were opposite waterloo) But you can hear the trains, dont get me wrong, i did sleep, but i woke up at 5am and was drifting on and off due to the noise. It wouldnt stop me staying again though, i would just use ear plugs. :) Also we were on the 2nd floor and there were alot of stairs, were used to stairs but if you are not able to climb them, then maybe ask for the 1st floor! The whole pub has free WIFI and all rooms have free wifi as well.

title: 50/50 for our stay
text: Good aspects

title: Warm, caring staff at the Wellington
text: I recently went on a solo trip to London from the US, and stayed at The Wellington for 3 nights. On my first night, I was taken with extreme vertigo, and had to be transported to the hospital via ambulance. I was sick, scared, and alone in a foreign country. The staff at the Wellington could not have been more incredible. They made me feel safe and cared for. They checked on me constantly, and even went to the pharmacy to buy me medicine when I was unable to get out of bed. I will never forget the kindness, warmth, and compassion they showed me during my stay. I am forever grateful.

title: Great location but noisy .
text: Great location as across waterloo station.swipe key card are a nightmare to work.room clean and on small side and back room close to railway so can be really noisy.pub very busy.breakfast ok.indian restaurant down the road=little gem(bangalore).bed very confortable.

title: Good Value, Great Location
text: I agree with previous reviewers that this place needs a bit of TLC, but it was an ideal base for a couple of days in London. We stayed in a family room on the 3rd floor facing the road and the noise didn't bother any of us. In fact we all slept very well. Noise would be reduced further if the windows closed properly! Room and linen we're very clean, towels soft and fluffy, beds comfy. No bath, but FANTASTIC shower. Yes, we had to climb a few flights of stairs, but this wasn't a problem. Breakfast was great. Option of cooked, cereal, yoghurt, fruit, tea, coffee etc. Set us up for the day. There was a nice atmosphere in the pub itself. Felt really welcoming even with a very tired 7 year old! Free WiFi a bonus. Location is ideal for Waterloo, South Bank & the West End. Walked to the London Eye, over Waterloo Bridge to Covent Garden. Direct tube to Bond Street to hit Oxford Street and to North Greenwich to the O2 Arena. Overall The Wellington is good value for money in a great location and I would certainly stay again.

title: Meeting place
text: We met here prior to going to a concert. The food was fair and prompt considering how busy the place was. Bar staff helpful and although busy cleared tables quickly. No doubt that we will all meet here again. Toilets clean always a bonus! Thanks

title: A delightful stay at The Wellington.
text: Having stayed at The Wellington on a few occasions, we were delighted with the refurbished rooms. They had been carried out to a very good standard and fashionable. The bed was very comfortable and we had two good nights sleep. The breakfasts were excellent too with plenty of choice. Mark, the manager, and his assistant, Roger, gave us an enthusiastic welcome which contributed towards another super weekend. We find that the location is ideal as we enjoy walking around London rather than taking the tube. We will definitely be making a return journey in the future. Thank you Mark and your wonderful team.

title: Option for a pint right in front of Waterloo
text: Went this place to meet some friends and it was nice and not so crowded despite the crazy business day. The location is quite handy. One negative point is the price of beer. Expensive for a pint (£5).

title: Top location top staff great value
text: I have stayed here on numerous occasions when in the area. The rooms are spacious and come with complimentary tea coffee and bottled water. The pub below, a fullers pub sells 4 real ales and a wide a varied selection of bottled and draught lagers and ciders. Great bar menu with a wide selection of choices for all pallets. Location - you can't fault the interchanges for tube and buses and also the mainline into Waterloo. Staff - very polite, very chatty and always available to offer sound advice on what's on in the local area. Nothing was too much for the staff during my last stay. Check out in the morning was easy - but first a top breakfast cooked to order and you could mix and match anything off of the menu. I love this place and would willingly travel out of my way to sample a drink or to stay

title: Fantastic Hotel
text: This is the second time I have stayed here and I did not previously leave a review as I felt the rooms were somewhat tired, although the experience was good overall. However, they have clearly spent a substantial amount of money because the rooms now are incredible. The theme throughout this refurb is obviously "London Town" with underground station signs and London landmarks decorated everywhere. You are in the heart of London when you are here and it is nice to recognise this within the rennovations. I will be looking to stay again in the future.

title: Earplugs !!
text: I booked this hotel for a business trip to London. The price was reasonable and the location excellent for central London. The room was pretty basic but satisfactory, and the bar downstairs served good ale, and the food looked good. What let this place down for me was the noise. If you reached out of the window you could practically touch the trainline out of Waterloo. Trains start running at 05.20 and don't stop till after midnight. I can see now why there are earplugs supplied in the room !! If you want somewhere central to crash after seeing the sights and a show, then this place is fine. If you want to relax and rest, look elsewhere.

title: Lovely hotel run by lovely people
text: I stayed a couple of weeks ago for one night only whilst I was in London for my son's graduation. The staff were very helpful & even upgraded me to a double room at no extra cost. This was much appreciated as it meant I was at the other side of the hotel from my ex-husband & his parents! The owner was really lovely & when I told him my reason for visiting, was very interested & didn't seem to mind me rambling on about how proud I was.........I just wish I could have stayed longer to find out more about the hotel & its history. I would definitely recommend The Wellington to anybody visiting London. Hope to go back some day. Mandy Stuart x

title: Great hotel location and service
text: I stayed overnight at the hotel for a work trip. It is very centrally located and has plenty of restaurants, bars etc within close walking distance, with Waterloo station just a few minutes away. My double room was comfortable and well decked out with contemporary furnishings. The morning breakfast was also a hearty offering. There is a pub downstairs which is quite big and was really busy the evening I got there, however, hotel patrons can access the hotel from it's own entrance down the side. I went out for dinner so didn't really have much contact with the pub, apart from at breakfast, where the service was very friendly. I would like to point out that the reason I have given this hotel 5 stars is for the exceptional service provided to me by Roger, who checked me in. In line with most central London hotels, there aren't parking facilities on site. I had equipment that I needed to drop off at the hotel before parking my car at the car park around the corner. I called the hotel and Roger kindly offered to go out of his way to assist in taking the equipment from my car and bringing it to my room, which would otherwise have caused me much difficulty in such a congested traffic part of London. Roger was both kind and courteous, leaving me with a great impression of the hotel, which I would gladly stay at again if I happen to be working in the area. He showed an exemplary level of customer service and is an asset to this establishment.

title: Perfect for sight seeing trips
text: This was the first time we have taken our children to London (aged 6 and 9) and for our overnight sight seeing trip, the hotel was perfect. The location was spot on as we traveled up by train to Waterloo, so crossing the road to drop off our luggage (which was safely stored until we could check in) enabled us more sight seeing time. The room was small but as we only planned 1 nights stay didn't bother us ... tea/ coffee facilities available in the room and when we asked for more ... that wasn't a problem. The breakfast was laid out so that you could help yourselves to cereals, yogurts, fruit and crossiants and then you had the option of a full English, porridge or pancakes. Great hotel, Great location (yes can be noisy but so can 2 kids! But you are in London!) Would go back or recommend to friends.

title: Convenient Location and Great Hotel!
text: We had to check in late on the day of arrival and we informed the hotel ahead of time to make sure that we could still check in. Roger was there and stayed up past the late check in time to make sure that we could check into the hotel! Throughout our stay, they were very accommodating. We also had lunch once at the pub and it was delicious! Definitely recommend the pub on the first floor of the hotel! Not to mention, the location is right across the street from the Waterloo station, which has both tube and national rail access. We were able to go everywhere right from Waterloo! You can't beat that!

title: Pub with rooms - adequate for the price
text: We stayed here for one night due to proximity to Waterloo station. It's a pub with decent rooms, though they are compact but with good features. Don't expect the usual things you'd get from an actual hotel though - we arrived a few minutes earlier than check in time but were told we couldn't check in until the appointed time - fair enough but there was no effort to see if rooms were ready. We didn't eat in the pub as didn't fancy what the menu had to offer - but there are many places to eat on the embankment just 5 minutes walk away. We were disappointed not to be able to have the breakfast included in the price as it was Bank Holiday Monday it wasn't available any earlier - again no effort to help even though we only needed to eat 15 minutes earlier in order to get our trains. If you are a light sleeper this isn't the place for you - Waterloo Road is busy and noisy and while the double glazing helps it doesn't cut down noise that much. The bedroom doors slam loudly when let go and other guests aren't that courteous about keeping the noise down - fitting slow closing doors with dampers would help. Having said all that the bed was comfortable , the shower powerful and the rooms of a good standard for the price - I guess you pay your money and take your choice. I'd probably stay again and hopefully get breakfast next time!

title: Good location for South Bank
text: Like the previous reviewer, we too booked for one night as we we were going to the Festival Hall. The bar was packed with rugby fans when we arrived but we were booked in quickly. A kind member of staff took our bag upstairs for us and it was on the second floor. As my husband is 77, it was a good job we were only there for a short time. However, the room though small, was very clean and quiet, which considering the crowds in the bar, was amazing! Breakfast was really good with plenty of choice and the staff were very helpful. We would stay again, but on the first floor next time.

title: To many little faults, sorry
text: Rooms upstairs above a traditional pub. Stair case restrictive, steep and very musty, coughed everytime, banged my head on awkward ledge while passing others on the stairs. Room, considering the proximity of the train track, was very quiet with double glazing, however, with this closed, room was unbearably hot, needed fan on full blast all weekend. Very small room, better as a single, we both banged legs on the corner of the bed numerous times, leading to small bruises. Funky modern decor. Tiny toilet/shower room, clean and modern but poorly finished. Bed, very very comfy. Complimentary tea, coffee, water and biscuits in room. Well positioned decent sized TV. Breakfast poor, bacon tasted like it'd been cooked on the steak grill, first morning normal bacon, second smoked, tasteless baked beans, horrid coffee but tea ok. Husband loves a full English but declined it by the third morning. First morning, came downstairs for breakfast to find a bar full of drinking rugby fans watching a match, not what I want while eating my breakfast, total conflict of interests between bar and hotel there. Location, perfect for waterloo station, suited us great as within walking distance of the places we were here to visit. Really wanted to like it but the bad added up too much. Sorry.

title: Great position for the Festival Hall
text: Room, bathroom, meals, service all very good. Access for Festival hall excellent, no more than a 5 minute walk. Staff very friendly. Only issue is access to bedrooms which are up steep stairs - not surprising when one considers the building, but something you may want to consider if you are travelling with elderly, disabled or children. Would certainly stay again but probably not take 87 year old mother next time. (To be fair manager gave mother a free upgrade in room - unprompted - to save her walking up as many of the stairs). Some people will complain about the trains but what do you expect if you stay next to the railway???

title: Great location, poor service
text: The hotel is in a great location and is ideal as a base for sight seeing. The family room was adequate for our 1 night stay and I was surprised how quiet it was given the busy rd outside. The downside was the attitude of the staff and repeated errors with the serving of our food, on arrival we ordered lunch which took 45 mins to arrive in 3 batches, one of the orders was incorrect. At breakfast the selection was really good however again it was the service that let it down, we waited an hour for 3 breakfasts and a bacon bap! Again one of the orders was wrong, I was informed I ordered the wrong item! The waitress was very rude and unapologetic. I wouldn't recommend staying there due to the unhelpful staff, which is a shame as the hotel is in a great location.

title: Not Impressed
text: We booked the Wellington so that we'd be able to get to the London Stadium easily and then have quick access to Waterloo Station for our journeys to work the following morning. The room was nicely furnished and comfortable, if a bit small and hot (but there was an electric fan). However, it was up several flights of steep stairs, so not suitable for anyone with poor mobility. It was also right next to the railway tracks from Waterloo East - not good to be woken up by trains at 5 a.m. Earplugs were supplied, but they weren't very effective! Breakfast was OK at best - undercooked bacon is not nice (though we didn't have their Full English, so can't comment on this) and the buffet wasn't being replenished frequently enough. It all seemed a bit chaotic. The staff are pleasant and helpful, but given the other issues, I wouldn't stay there again.

title: Great Location in the City
text: My wife and I enjoyed our stay here. The hotel couldn't be any closer to the Waterloo station which is extremely convenient for traveling around the city. It is also close enough to walk to several tourist attractions. We walked from the hotel to the South Bank, the London Eye, and the houses of parliament The guy at the desk was very friendly and helpful with our luggage. The room is very small, but it was very clean. The bathroom was very small, but we had no problems using the small shower. We both found the bed to be comfortable and the outside noise did not bother us. We stayed in room 4. You can hear the trains and activity through the window, but with the white noise from the fan, it was easy to ignore and sleep through. The loudest noise was the slamming of some door. It may have been the door to the outside of the hotel, we aren't sure, but it definitely needs some padding installed to quiet the door. It was extremely loud in our room. We didn't realize we were staying above a bar until we arrived. It was always packed in the bar in the evenings, which made eating in the hotel difficult and uninviting. The breakfast was great. A full hot breakfast made to order, eggs, hash browns, sausage, English "bacon," beans, pancakes, and black pudding. Along with several cold options. We would stay here again.

title: Return visit
text: We returned to the Wellington Hotel with friends after staying here a year ago. I tried to get a room here again after the refurbishment, but unfortunately it was fully booked. We came for dinner with our friends after enjoying the food so much the last time we came. The food was just as good as our last visit, the service was great despite being very busy for the world cup and we all enjoyed our visit.

title: Don't let the noise reviews scare you!
text: We stayed in London for 6 days during May 2013 after a transatlantic cruise and were looking for a "reasonable price" hotel in Central London as close to a tube and train station as possible (not an easy task!). This hotel could not be closer unless it was in the Tube/Station lobby! The noise reviews had me concerned so I emailed the hotel before our trip to see if they could accommodate us on the street side rather than the train side of the building. Hotel management responded and was VERY forthcoming about their noise issues (a total surprise!) and were also very accommodating about keeping us only 1 floor up (no lift and we had 3 heavy bags) and on the street side. The room we stayed in (Room 15 on the street/alley side) was no worse (noise wise) than hotels we have stayed in near airports, freeways or train tracks. The windows are dual-pane and unless you require absolute silence, the noise was there but it was nothing to worry about especially after returning exhausted after a full day of site seeing. THE HOTEL POSITIVES: 1) Closeness to Waterloo Tube AND Train station (directly across the street) 2) A mini-super market 100 feet up the street for snacks/water/drinks etc. 3) Very good wi-fi interned and FREE! 4) Flat screen TV's with lots of channels. BBC and SKY but no CNN and FNC. 5) A smaller but comfortable room. Armoire for hanging clothes, room to store 3 large suitcases, walk around bed, desk and chair and your own toilet/shower. 6) A great hot breakfast cooked to order INCLUDED, which offered all the standard continental breakfast cereals, juices, fruit, yogurt AND prepared to order eggs, English bacon, pancakes, toast, butter and jellies. (A 9 GBP breakfast included free with the room!) 7) Separate hotel/stair access with key card entry so you do NOT have to go through the pub to enter and exit the hotel rooms 8) Misc items like a powerful hot shower, key card locks for door and outside access, daily maid service, monster size bath towels, and a great staff including the manager who was at breakfast every day and served as a local sightseeing guide! THE NEGATIVES 1) This hotel is part of the ground floor pub. The hotel registration is at the pub bar so you go to the bar to check in which can be a challenge during drinking hours. We were on the floor above the pub but did not notice any noise coming up through the floor. 2) No elevators/lifts, so if somewhat narrow stairs are an issue for up to 5 flights, ask for 1st floor (above ground level). There is a trade off as higher floor are probably quieter on the street side. 3) The keycard door locks are older and we had a problem getting in our room one night but the hotel night manager immediately gave us access and repaired the lock in short order. 4) No ice machines or mini-fridge in our room, but I am sure if I had asked in the pub, they would have provided ice if asked. I would stay again in this Hotel in a heart beat! It was so central to London we did not even need a tube or train to see many of the sights. We had a short walk to London Eye, Big Ben, River cruises, Parliament, Westminster Abbey, Churchill war museums and more. We spent easily 6 days on the internet trying to find the best value with the best price and the Wellington Waterloo was it for us! Charlie and Pat San Diego

title: great stay
text: we booked the wellington on Late.rooms.com at a bargain price , we stayed one night b&b all the staff kind and friendly , its a pub and do great meals, the room was at the back no20 the window looked out on railway lines, you expect noise when you stay next too waterloo st the room was clean and comfortable, they supply ear plugs, but it wasn't that bad,well the breakfast was really good hot much as you want too eat

title: Best breakfast, enjoyed so much,
text: Me and few friends of mine visited the pub foot breakfast and we enjoyed it a lot But Many thanks to the chef for lovely breakfast. It is also in very good location easy to reach. English breakfast is my fav choice to go for.

title: Hotel above a big pub directly opposite Waterloo Station. Rooms are tiny, bathrooms are even smaller!
text: Unusual hotel rooms above a pub. The rooms are clean but tiny and the bathrooms are too say the least compact. Prices are reasonable for London standards and the pub is very centrally located directly opposite Waterloo railway station. Breakfast is the usual fare of full English with cereals and fruit juice. Coffee is not great so opt for the tea.

title: Breakfast
text: Best breakfast by far eaten in Birmingham. All freshly cooked. Unlimited tea,coffee etc. Served by friendly staff. Shame didn't discover this gem of a hotel beforehand. Next visit will stay at the place if this level of service runs through the place.

title: A pub with rooms ... but quite a decent one
text: I was looking for a hotel close to the Oxo Tower, and the Wellington seemed an appropriate price and is less than ten minutes' walk away. It was also handy that I was able to book through Booking.com, as I wanted to be able to pay on the day rather than at booking time. The hotel's pretty easy to find: leave Waterloo Station via the Waterloo Road entrance and it's bang in front of you. Check-in is at the pub bar - there's a little area set aside at one end.
