Ordered room service and wished it was better.... if you never be in Asia, it would be the very good modern Western n Asian in London to stay.

title: Urban cool
text: Great location in heart of Shoreditch in quiet side street. Cool design, super comfy beds with stylish bathrooms. Nice free WiFi and friendly staff. Nobu bar and restaurant in double height basement is amazing. Staff were superb, hip design, incredible food. Welcome opening offer rate must be best value in London.

title: Lies about room service hours
text: As a business traveller on a tight schedule, I rely on the posted hours for room service. The alleged service hours (until midnight each night) were a significant positive factor in selecting the hotel, despite the expensive cost of ordering from Nobu for room service. However, I just placed an order at 11:50 and was told that the menu had been shifted to Late Night, i.e. only Bento boxes were available. If I had known, I would have eaten outside the hotel. I don't appreciate being lied to by a hotel I rely on for food, and I will not stay here again, nor can I recommend the hotel.

title: Citrus Essence with the Mindful Touch facial - top facial in London (from a Londoner)!
text: I’ve had a few facials, many can leave you feeling fresh, better than a wash type thing, but this experience really did leave me feeling SO much better about my skin (and mind). The Mindful Touch is a VR experience (with accompanying massage) to relax you - really put me in a great place before the facial. And then every element of the facial basically just felt like the ultimate goodness on my skin, whether it was cleansing, toning or moisturising, nothing felt harsh and I have genuinely left feeling like a new person, my skin healthy and alive. The massage touches between applications are always an definite plus, and there were plenty here. I’m a sucker for a scalp massage - definite thumbs up here. I’m sure they are all great, but my technician Rebecca was superb, and definitely worth a shout out! Can’t wait to come back.

title: Awful hotel - never go there
text: This hotel is very badly run. There are events going all night with full music and wired people . All is very dark. Intense music all the time. Nobody to lead you to your room. Bathrooms are not convenient. Lighting in the room does not work nor does the heating. Staff is unhelpful and quasi rude .

title: East meets West Chic
text: Enjoyed my stay at the newly opened Nobu Hotel, situated on a quiet Shoreditch street (facing The Hoxton). It's pretty much as you'd expect from the brand - Japanese aesthetic, all very linear & feng shui but with an edgy little nod to the EC2 location. Check-in was fine but I was a tad miffed that pre-arrival emails took upwards of 24 hours to be answered. Staff in general are willing but clearly still learning the ropes. The lobby is nice enough with a casual café/lounge area & grand staircase leading down to the cavernous 240 seater restaurant. Dinner was excellent - the usual Nobu staples plus a handful of dishes exclusive to this branch. I didn't take breakfast but the menu is imaginative, what a previous reviewer refers to as being thoroughly Nobu'd!! Rooms are sleek & zen like - dark wood, clean lines, slatted screens with everything concealed that possibly can be, including the bathroom (which took some finding under the shadow of sexy mood lighting!). Bathrooms are compact but opulent with golden basins contrasting starkly against the otherwise all white surround. My premium room was generously proportioned with a seating area & floor to ceiling window. Sliding wooden slats leave the room pitch dark by night making for a restful sleep aided by a very comfy bed, luxurious covers & solid sound proofing. The gym is due to open later in September & a rooftop bar scheduled for 2018 I believe. Recommended.

title: One of the best Asian restaurants!
text: We always visit Nobu when in London. The Asian plates are very delicious. Beef tataki is a must. And the makis and the miso soup were outstanding. The sashimis were fresh as the rest of the dishes.Very recommended.

title: Another fav in London
text: Big fans of Nobu food having previously eaten in Vegas and Monaco Restaurant s Wanted to try London so booked new shoreditch Restaurant and a stay at this hotel . On arrival booked in quickly and went to room on 5th floor room is stunning with big comfortable bed , room decorated with industrial feel with lots of different textures and diming lights making it feel cosy , all amenities in room you need , room also very quite making you have excellent nights sleep , turn down service prepping you for good nights sleep . All staff encountered efficient and welcoming and making sure things we booked went ok lady whom checked us in come down to spa when we were waiting for a massage too make sure we were happy nice touch . We will definitely rebook this hotel

title: AmaZing new London hotel
text: You can’t go wrong with Nobu . Stayed a few weeks back and also dined in the nobu restaurant INCREDIBLE MEAL! Highly recommend this hotel and restaurant . In such a cool location also, value for money perfect

title: Harmonious and stylish hotel with few glitches
text: There’s no question that Nobu isn’t a well-designed concept. Rooms are beautiful, well-appointed with elegant and bespoke furnitures. The bed and linens have a luxurious feel. I had a room on the 1st floor but the green garden behind the window gave the room a nice atmosphere. Bathroom has enough light and the room lighting is easy to use. The hotel has a relatively nice fitness facilities, although I would add a cable machine, bench press and few more sets of heavier dumbbells. The steam sauna was unfortunately out of order. I had a breakfast packaged room rate so I expected a sumptuous morning treat because the content wasn’t described in the reservation confirmation. Instead, I got one small plate of my choice from the menu, house bread and black coffee and juice. I felt the value wasn’t enough. Especially, when the breakfast wasn’t busy at all on both mornings, it seemed that many guests chose to eat somewhere else. The food itself was tasty and when you have such a nice overall concept, I really hope the management consider the breakfast context once again. However, overall experience was very good and in London especially the value is great!

title: Good comfortable stay
text: Stayed in Utagi Suite for a few days with my husband and daughter. The room was very comfortable with a lovely terrace although I would have to admit the bathroom is a bit small. The staff in the hotel were accommodating as they can be especially with a baby with us. I didn't enjoy the breakfast very much and room service gets boring really quickly as there was no other options other than the Nobu restaurant (it would be nice to expand the room service menu to include items that are different than the menu at the Nobu restaurant). The housekeeping staff were excellent. Overall it was a comfortable stay with staff that were trying their best to be very accommodating.

title: Modern and stylised
text: Some confusion on arrival - receptionist advising my company hadn't prepaid (as they always do) so I had to contact the office to get them to confirm things. Very modern and highly designed hotel with Japanese influence. Room fairly small but comfortable. Design meant it took a bit of time to establish how to work lights, find electric sockets, shutter the window, etc Breakfast good. Staff friendly. At breakfast I was told it had been pre-paid (food not drinks). On checking out I was told my employer had in fact pre paid the room, but not the breakfast. Because of the confusion they waived cost of breakfast (but not drinks at breakfast). Was unable to get best room rates advertised. Good location and likely to use again if I can get a decent rate.

title: Great Hotel and a better experience
text: I stayed at Nobu Hotel Shoreditch for 3 days during a business trip in London. From the beginning everything was amazing, the building was incredible, close to the Old Street (underground) and in the heart of Shoreditch. At Front Desk the staff was very professional and polite with a very Nobu's Style. The room was in the second floor and was quiet and very comfortable. Moreover, we had two options for dinner, the in-room dinning or the restaurant. However, the bar at restaurant is from other World, it is compulsory to drink something there. Definitely, the experience was perfect and 100% recommendable. I am sure that if I have to come back to London, I will stay there.

title: Great hotel
text: Generally this is a great hotel with a lovely service. I loved everything especially the Japanese touches in design and tea pots etc. The one thing i did not like was the size of the room, if was small for 2 persons it was good for 1. My friend has joined me for 2 nights and it was a bit too small for us. There wasnt enough sun light (personal opinion). The concierge and especially Michael were excellent and so helpful! Michael was kind enough to walk with me to find my uber with my luggage. Thanks for an amazing service!

title: Amazing xmasdinner
text: I am a huge fan from Nobu unfortanetly I was a bit disappointed from the reserve but I loved the food as always!! Yauatcha and Nobu are in my top favourites and please believe me I went to a lot of restaurants! The tacos are amazing, the misosoup as well and the black cod mmmm as well both oysterdishes and lobster njammie

title: Nobu delight
text: Stopped by for lunch mid week with friends. We have a mix of starters and bento boxes for mains. Food was simply delicious, try the black salted cod! This is a restaurant I’m coming back to try more on the menu, a Hoxton winner!

title: Great addition to Shoreditch
text: London's first Nobu hotel doesn't disappoint

title: Great Room, Bad Service
text: Room is good on the overall, especially the bathroom, comfy bathrobes & the minimalistic well designed space is the plus part of our experience. However the service is a really nightmare ! I had my glasses damaged during room service & only discovered it before resting at night ( changing out of my contacts into glasses ). When I feedback this to the counter staff, she mentioned to come back to me. Upon following up with the counter staff the next morning, I realised nothing was done about my feedback. Another staff took down my contact details and claim to reach out to me - again, no reply the next day when they claim to reach me within 1 day. After waiting a few more days, Nobu finally reached out to me with a poorly done investigation claiming they had done a check via the CCTV & it has nothing to do with their turndown service staff - by common sense of course this was by the day staff ?! After I emailed them about this logical deduction, they again denied it... The specs was just less than 46 pounds but they refused to compensate me & reply my email ever since. I can't understand how it happened till this day when it didn't occur in other lower tier hotels I stayed in my trip to Londpn

title: UNREAL!
text: literally unreal hotel... after having the most incredible food downstairs... we got a free upgrade of our room. spacious, beautiful furniture... unreal little extras... scattered about. The bathroom was beautiful and there was even a walk in wardrobe. Sofa... arm chairs. Huge TV. Huge bed. Beautiful view. Breakfast was incredible... served on a white table cloth trolley. best served breakfast in a hotel ever. Unbeatable! Literally one of the best experiences of my life... from start to finish. and we have stayed in a few good london hotels... but this...... WOW :) :0

title: Birthday weekend!
text: My boyfriend and I recently stayed two nights at this Nobu Hotel in Shoreditch for the weekend. First of all, the design of this building is very unique and beautiful. When we arrived at the check-in desk, we were greeted politely. They told us that our room is not ready yet but offered to store our luggage for us. We did gave them our luggage and pop downstairs to their Nobu restaurant for lunch while waiting for our room to be cleaned. When i made the booking online, i did put a note in the booking that its my boyfriend's birthday. After lunch, our room was ready and they gave us the key to our room. We booked a Deluxe room which is a good size room. I know some people complaint that it is too small but not for me maybe because we only had two small cabin size luggage. I guess if you are international guests and travelling with large suitcase, then yes it can be abit small for you. Anyway, when we got to our room, there was a birthday card and a plate of dessert with Happy Birthday written on it on the table for my boyfriend from the hotel. It definitely made my boyfriend feel very special. The room was very clean with a huge TV. My favourite was the bathroom which is beautiful with gold sink, gold taps and a rain shower head. I love everything about the hotel apart from the location as theres not much around. I think if you are looking for a quiet weekend away, this could be the one for you. Although we stayed at this hotel but we spent both days taking the underground to Knightsbrige and London Bridge Station. The nearest underground station to the Nobu Shoreditch Hotel is called Old Street and it is less than 10 minutes away. Highly recommend this hotel to everyone :)

title: Nice hotel. Great location.
text: This hotel is located on a very quiet street in the heart of the happening neighborhood of Shoreditch. It’s a brand new hotel, very modern and a good value for the cost. Room size was fairly large by London hotel standards, and the staff was nice also. That’s the good. What’s bad or to be desired at least: 1. Room keys are some funky key we’ve never encountered before and it unclear how to fully utilize it in the room. A tutorial upon arrival would’ve been nice. 2. The bed was a bit too firm for our liking and the sheets could’ve been softer. 3. CAREFULLY REVIEW YOUR BILL AT CHECKOUT! They added £10 Pounds in food costs we didn’t order and tacked on a “voluntary community donation”. Hmmmm adding it to my bill without asking isn’t a voluntary donation, it’s a tax. We got them to remove it. 4. We got breakfast included with our booking, (which was quite good), and check in we were told ‘we could either enjoy it in the dining room our our hotel room.’ They lead us to believe there was no additional charge for room service, but there was £5 per occurrence added to our bill. The bad taste this left in our mouths could’ve easily been avoided had they simply told us there was a £5 surcharge for room service. 5. The toilets...there’s no other way to say this other than they just don’t flush well, or at least the one in our room required 3-4 flushes for a #2. All that being said, we’d still recommend this hotel, as most of the issues we experienced could be resolved with a bit of employee coaching.

title: Lovely Hotel just some minor imporvements
text: First of all the hotel decor was beautiful, the rooms were spacious enough and the staff were very accommodating and welcoming. My issues were the following

title: Needs to find it feet
text: Stayed here for a night in London with mixed thoughts. When we arrived the systems were down and we were invited to have a drink in the bar while we waited for them to reboot - the assumption was these were complimentary but were then charged at checkout the next day. Some of the hotel is still under construction so I would suggest waiting until it's complete to stay as it looks like it will be stunning. The rooms are great and the bed extremely comfortable. I was offered a free upgrade upon arrival but this meant I didn't get the use of a walk in show which was a slight disappointment. I'd definitely revisit when it's finished to be able to give a fair review of a hotel that is complete.

title: Food is great, hotel is complex and complicated for business travel
text: I have eaten at many Nobu restaurants around the world - London (both Park Lane and Shoreditch), US (Miami, New York, San Diego, Las Vegas) and the food has always been top notch. Under that assumption, I thought the hotel would be as well! First, they charge you for your room + 80 pounds a night in advance when you check in. Only club hotels do that in Miami and places like that as they are scared of runners. Not a trait of general luxury hotels. I ordered food from the restaurant when I got in late. I ordered an appetiser and small glas of wine. When the food hadn't arrived after 1 1/2 hour, I called and they mentioned they forgot to put it in. Then when I got upset and asked them to send it up immediately, the man answered " I cannot guarantee a time", I was furious. The hotel comped the meal but it was a bad experience. Second, the room is complicated. I understand it is supposed to be modern with the lights, the sliding doors for the windows but it was dark, hard to understand how to use everything. Also, the hair dryer cannot be used in the bathroom as their is no power outlet to support. Again, not business travel friendly! The room doesn't have a desk either so it is hard to do work in the room. Again, business travel. When I left in the early morning Saturday, there were a bunch of club goers in the lobby (at 7:00 am) minimally dressed and the alcohol smell was so strong. It was like the after math of a hard night out! Not what you would like to be welcomed by. So I would recommend dining here, but not the best place to stay while on business travel in London.

title: Full of nasty surprises
text: Won’t try my luck again. From rude front staff to surprise unsolicited morning calls - this is the last place anyone wants to be in London. Checked in early (10am) from a red eye flight (they don’t care even you emailed them in advance) - no rooms. Took all my bags claiming to be safe but didn’t give me a key or receipt for the bags/room. Never bothered to tell me when the room is ready either. When you go back they will ask for ID like a club bouncer (smart - who got my luggage and personal belongings?). Threw some hotel policy in my face and didn’t think any of this is an inconvenience and only after a round of complaint they reluctantly apologised. Next morning a surprise call at 7:20 - did you order an Americano? Hell no - I ordered some sleep. Called back again in 10mins again and hung up. They probably had this in their hotel policy too! One more night to go - ready for more surprises! Don’t pay to suffer! These guys don’t belong to the hospitality industry.

title: Gorgeous Room. Gourmet Food.
text: I stayed at the Nobu Shoreditch on a quick stopover in London last August. My first trip to the neighborhood started out rough but turned out top notch. Upon arrival at Heathrow, I realized that my brief stay in the city was going to be cut even shorter thanks to incredibly long lines at the airport. The weather was also slowing down traffic. My ride from Paddington station to the hotel took longer than expected. I had dinner plans in the neighborhood but by the time I arrived at the hotel I had long missed my reservation and the restaurant was closed. It was after 10 pm. I was soggy and kind of bummed. However, as soon as I stepped into my room - all that faded away. The zen ambiance and gorgeous fixtures of the premium room were enough to instantly win me over. I did consider grabbing a spot at the Nobu restaurant downstairs. But knowing that room service was from the same skilled chefs, I was more than happy to stay in and enjoy the space. So, instead of exploring the new neighborhood or joining the buzzy crowds below, the rest of my night included an insane in-room meal with short ribs and rock shrimp, a wickedly warm bath and piping hot Japanese tea to lull me to sleep. Yes, I’m officially old now :) After a great night’s rest, I woke to enjoy another delicious meal - this one included in my room rate - of parfait, pastries, miso bacon and fried chicken with matcha waffles. I was also able to squeak in a morning of exploring Shoreditch shops and cafes before heading back to the airport. The trip was quick, but enough to whet my appetite, literally and figuratively, for more. The only reason I’m not leaving five stars here is that I wasn’t overly impressed by the service. Nothing went wrong but with a five-star property this slick and food this delicious, I expected more polish and personality from the staff. This could have been because they had just opened. Maybe by now, they have their A game on. I certainly hope to have the chance to see it if so.

title: Pleasant Surprise
text: I have to admit I was skeptical about choosing a hotel that is better known for its restaurant, but I was so wrong. My two night stay in the Nobu was pure comfort and luxury. My room was modern and quiet, with lots of nice little details like a heated bathroom floor and a custom lighting system. The clean lines of the hotel are a nice contrast to the grittiness of Shoreditch and the whole thing leaves a very memorable impression. And of course, dinner at the restaurant downstairs was stellar. Would return in a heartbeat. One note - i wasn’t 100% clear on why, but taxis and Ubers will not come to the hotel door to pick you up, so staff send you over to the main street. Not a dealbreaker, it was just odd and a bit inconvenient.

title: very Zen!
text: awesome hotel located on a quiet street. the decor is incredible, the service is top notch and the F&B at the hotel is done by Nobu so it is top notch as well. I first want to highlight the Nobu Shoreditch team, from Henrick, Xenia, Christian, Bertrain, and Matthew. They were always professional and courteous and even accommodated a last minute late checkout for me. The housekeeping team was on point as well and the turndown ladies were lovely! My kudos to the Nobu team and i would definitely recommend and would stay there again!

title: Weekend one night stay
text: For our 10th year anniversary we decided to stay here for a night. Check in was at 3oclock but we decided to arrive early and they accommodated us with our room. The staff were impeccable! The room was spotless, my Fiancé worries about hotel beds, but they were more than comfortable and so where the chairs in the room. The bathroom was to a high standard and we had a wall in shower. Also a walk in wardrobe! Couldn’t fault anything. The food was A* Would recommend to everyone, the location was perfect for us also being so close to all the places we wanted to go to. Thankyou for an enjoyable stay. Spencer Ellis

title: quality beyond belief
text: I was fortunate enough to stay here as I was attending a seminar the next day. The reception staff could not do enough for you. I popped to the bar for a beer and the ambience was "buzzing" and lively. At the conference the next day I had a platter on no fish/seafood Sushi which was excellent - followed by Sake tasting All round, not cheap but quality food, service and an exquisite room. Only "faux par" was a shower above the bath

title: Food & Cocktails to Dine For.
text: We've heard great things about NOBU, but the Shoreditch restaurant was our first experience and it exceeded our expectations in almost every way. We were treated like royalty from the moment we walked into the hotel. It was only a short walk from reception to the bar and restaurant. Sometimes a large group can often be a challenge for most restaurants due the sheer variety of personal tastes: spicy, not spicy, fish but no shellfish, no meat….requests. However, the personal service from our waiters was excellent, with multiple food and drinks orders handled with easy, and some very helpfully guidance when we were conflicted on what to order (just too many good things to choose from). The food from beginning to end was worth every penny, and the taste sensations were terrific - I recommend the black cod and the vegetarian dishes (I’m not vegetarian, but couldn’t help trying my friends dishes). The menu is very eclectic, so there is something for everyone to enjoy. The drinks service was exceptional

title: Rollacoaster
text: A very hard hotel to rate. On the one hand it was fantastic, the rooms from a spec point of view, bed, tv, bathroom were first class. The rooms though were very small, I was told that was upgraded, so i hate to think what the room I'd paid for was like (hotel didn't do itself any favours there). Went to the bar in the evening, great atmosphere, very sophisticated, and expensive, 3 beers were £28. Breakfast was fussy and hard to communicate with the staff over what it was that was on the menu, they were trying to be nice, but then just brought things i didn't order and made the table full. Would I go again, yes i would.

title: Excellent coice
text: I spent couple of days at Nobu Hotel Shoreditch, and it was my first time. I travel quite a lot in London mainly for business and this time I wanted to try Nobu as accommodation. I was surprised by the architecture and atmosphere of the place, calm and intimate. I had a late check in and everything went smooth and without any issue, the room was ready for me and a relaxing music welcomed me. The room, located in the 2nd floor, was quiet and cozy

title: Another excellent stay
text: Second visit here and we were very impressed. A few issues with drinks prices at the bar on happy hour and draft beer not working on a Saturday / unforgivable

title: Lovely hotel let down by the food
text: The hotel itself is lovely, large clean room with a very comfortable king sized bed. Only a 5 minute walk to an NCP car park, which is just outside of the congestion zone. My husband and I have visited Nobu restaurants in the past, which was the main reason that we stayed at this hotel, being able to order room service. The website states that you can order from the main menu shown on the website, however this is not true, and the room service menu is considerably smaller. The quality of the food here is definitely not up to par with the other Nobu restaurants. The wagyu burger sliders were raw, I think that there needs to be a warning on the menu about this, as this actually made me sick. I don’t mind paying extra money for a really good meal, but the food bill (no drinks) was over £130 for 2 of us, half of the food we couldn’t eat, and we were both left very hungry! Tried to speak to someone, was told a manager was not available and would call me back - never did. We were in a rush in the morning so just had to pay the bill and leave. £75 for the robe, although very nice just seems a bit extreme. I don’t think that we will return.

title: Great hotel
text: I really liked this hotel. Very nice decor and everything in the room was top notch. It's hard to explain why I didn't give this hotel 5 stars. With the price you pay you expected more. It is as said a gorgeous hotel but it lacks some ambiance and personality. It could have been a hotel in any part of the world - there was nothing personal or Nobu like. The shower was awesome, the beds were very comfy. More pillows than you needed - which is a good thing in my opinion. The staff needs to loosen up a bit and smile more - that would make it a 5 star hotel.

title: Spa
text: Had an aromatherapy massage at the spa and the whole experience was incredible start to finish. Best massage I’ve ever had and the staff were great. Couldn’t have been better! Will definitely be back.

title: Wonderful food
text: Excellent hotel and fabulous food . The black cod and sashimi are wonderful. Great location and restaurant. Another ' go to ' in London I would recommend in a heartbeat ! Excellent staff and rooms with a great vibe

title: Can’t get there
text: Was a nice enough hotel and service was very good but having to walk due to taxis not being allowed into the zone didn’t empress the wife , how can she be expected to walk to this establishment when she’s wearing hills , also it’s in hackney which isn’t the type of area where it’s safe to walk around with its crime epidemic . 1st and definitely last visit for me

title: Nobu willow street
text: Hotel seems ok but very hard to get to. Taxi drivers can not go there at certain times so drop you as near as they can and you have to walk the rest of the way and when you have luggage it seems a long way. If you want to book this place I would phone them first to find out which is the best time to arrive otherwise you could have quite a walk

title: Chic and sexy
text: Stunning new hotel. Rooms are well designed, compact and everything has a place. Very chilled zen environment in the hustle and bustle of Shoreditch Staff are polite and professional Only downside is the bar closes at 1am, which you expect to be open longer especially in such a location as Shoreditch. Bar and restaurant are very cool and brunch on the Sunday is an absolute must. Amazing food and lots of it...it’s the only meal you will need that day.

title: LUXURIOUSLY EXPENSIVE MEAL.
text: I was invited to dinner at the Nobu Restaurant located in the Nobu Hotel, Shoreditch, by family members who stayed at the hotel for four nights. Finding the hotel was quite difficult as it was certainly off the beaten track. The nearest station which is a good 10 minutes walk away, is Old Street which is serviced by the Northern Line and London Overground. On arrival, I entered into a nicely lit foyer with very well dressed, young staff in attendance. A call was put through to my hosts, who then came down to get me. I was taken on a tour of their room and other facilities and I was really impressed. They stayed in the Executive Room which mirrored the description on Nobu Hotel's website. Pure luxury and aesthetically pleasing Japanese inspired tranquillity welcomed you. Design wise, everything was carefully thought out and nicely executed. Every detail, right down to the slippers and toiletries, was exquisite. We then made our way down to the restaurant which is located in the basement. On descent, we were greeted by an impressive bar area, which extended over the back wall. Our party of four (which included a 14-year-old) were led to our table by a beautiful, tall waitress (I believe her name's Sherrifa - real asset to the Company), located right in front of the kitchen. We decided on a selection of dishes both on and off the menu... at one point, my host spoke to the main chef and asked him to surprise us. When the surprise arrived, I wasn't too blown away by the chef's selection. It was hardly that different from what was on the menu anyway. Our food was very well spaced out in between courses and the wine selection was good. I loved how the food was presented and enjoyed the narrative from the waiting staff. In all honesty, I wasn't too wowed by all we ate... I guess it was mainly because the final bill was soooo hefty. I couldn't justify paying almost £1000.00 on sushi, sashimi, small portions of black cod, shellfish and vegetables. I would gladly recommend this Hotel, but would advice that you look locally for other restaurants. You will be spoilt for choice in the local area, which is now gentrified. Shoreditch, Hoxton and Liverpool Street are all foodies mecca and major players in the restaurant/Street Food revolution. Don't miss out on the eclectic mix of cuisines available within arms reach.

title: What a modern piece of art!
text: I was ending my vacation with my partner in London and stayed at the newly opened Nobu hotel and it was fabulous! Loved the style, decor and ambiance of the hotel as well as the Shoreditch area. We were only there for a night but we had a blast!

title: Amazing Hospitality and Decor!
text: I stayed at the hotel for two days for my birthday and it was amazing. The spa is very clean and treatments were very relaxing. Staff were very helpful particularly a member of staff called Alfio who went above and beyond to ensure a comfortable stay. The resturant was also of a high standard and food was amazing

title: Shocking level of service for a five stars hotel and extremely rude and untrained staff
text: My partner had booked nobu Shoreditch hotel for our anniversary and I have to say was a very poor experience. First of all, I was greeted by very disenterested and rude staff (extremely busy looking at their phones but not paying much attention to guests) and me being there half an hour earlier than my partner they wouldn't allow me to check in without him as it was booked under his name. Understandable (although poor customer service from a five stars hotel), they asked me to contact him so he could email or call them to confirm I could check in without him which he did a few minutes later. At that poiny even though I was seating in the (cold) lobby two meters away from the check in desk, they never got back to me to allow me to check in so I had to wait until my partner got to the hotel, bit a good start. The room was nice but very dark with temperamental lights andbquite noisy ( could hear music outside the room). Overall a bad and disappointing experience and definitely not up to the standards of a five stars hotel in London. I would not recommend or book again. Advice to management : train your staff as the standard of customer experience or professionalism is very poor.

title: Spectacular
text: Such a great hotel. The design and service is amazing. The front desk people are so helpful - Mona and Rocio are awesome. The restaurant is also incredible. And there’s a great gym as well. Can’t wait to come back!!

title: Brand new hotel
text: Stayed for one night with a friend. This is a brand new hotel - it has only been open 2 weeks so everything is sparkling and fresh - there is still the lovely smell of new carpets everywhere. All the fixtures and fittings are of the highest quality. Staff were friendly, helpful and professional and the room was lovely, although the view was just the building that is being renovated across the street. Bathroom was great as were the toiletries and the other amenities. We had a suite which would have had a sofa in but as I asked the hotel for twin beds, the sofa became the 2nd bed but that was fine. The hotel is about 10 mins walk from Old Street tube on the Northern Line. We had every intention of having a drink in the bar but it was empty both when we came downstairs to go out for the evening and also when we returned so we passed on that. It does look lovely though, and I'm sure when more people realise it is open, they will get more custom. Lots of people were turning up in taxis etc early evening so I guess they were coming for dinner at the restaurant. This is London - hotels are expensive here of course, but i do believe you get more bang for your buck being away from the main tourist sites - a room like this in Covent Garden would be twice the rate I suspect. I have no idea whether the price we paid was reflective of the fact that the hotel has just opened and room rates here may well rise in months to come, but this is an excellent addition to the Shoreditch hotel market. Walking distance to Spitalfields - quirky shopping and good eating options.

title: Fabulous anniversary
text: Beautifully designed hotel with great ambiance. Slightly odd location in terms of its immediate surroundings but easy to get to and loads of places to go within walking distance or hop on the underground. The room was high spec with a large comfy bed, smart TV, designer bathroom with loads of toiletries and supplies. Fantastic bar with a huge range of wines and spirits, DJ and attentive staff. Unfortunately we didn’t have enough time to use all the facilities on offer

title: The best hotel In London#Trendy place#Place to be!!!
text: This is the most amazing hotel in London, the food was incredibly delicious!! (européen and Japanese influence) Spacious and comfortable rooms with a big tv's , Wide choice of food and beverage in the bar, plugging everywhere, big dressing, hairdresser, furnitures care and the workforce I will come back for sure

title: Nobu Hotel Shoreditch Spa - Aromatherapy Massage
text: I had the most wonderful aromatherapy massage in the Nobu's spa. The treatment was perfectly tailored to suit my back pain and the oils were selected as per my personality and my stress levels. A really great experience

title: Anniversary
text: Amazing one night stay amazing 8 course dinner. Luxury hotel you can’t ask for more with great service from every section of the hotel. The only thing I would change is the lighting its extremely dim in the rooms not too everyone taste.

title: Nice hotel - wrong location
text: The hotel in general is nice although the service was at times not at the level of what you expect from a 5 stars hotel. Staff friendly but a bit junior (the didn’t even know about Simpson’s in the strand)... For instance when I checked in I asked whether the restaurant was still open to serve breakfast and the answer was “it is not included in your room rate”. That wasn’t my question... I am happy to pay just let me know if it is open. But perhaps what bothered me the most was the location. My bad not to research more about Shoreditch but it is really far from the classic attractions I.e. Piccadilly, Buckingham Palace, Knightsbridge... If visiting London’s landmarks is your main purpose of your trip ... perhaps you may want to reconsider your stay unless you are ok with a 30 minutes trip in the filthy London tube. Overall It has not been an awful experience but it did not leave in me the willingness to come back. Location and lack of wow factor didn’t make it for me...

title: Complete relaxation in a hotel that's thought of everything.
text: If you are looking for compete relaxation with a high end hotel with the buzz of London on your doorstep then this place is for you.Nobu have mastered relaxation in this classy hotel chain with a fabulous bar & a restaurant that is too good to miss.Everthing is thought of with a great selection of toiletries, bath robes and the 360 huge swivel tv at the end of the bed.Lovely modern rooms with good sized balconies to sit & people watch.Lovely mood lighting.The staff were wonderful & couldn't do enough for us.We were celebrating an anniversary & the hotel staff left us a tasty plate of chocolate dipped strawberries which was a very nice touch.There is a place to get a coffee,tea or juice or a slice of cake located near to reception.Downstairs you will find the bar and the restaurant.I can definately recommend both as we got to enjoy both.Happy hour is 5-7pm.This hotel is located within walking distance of Old Street Station.The only reason I didn't give the full five stars was because the balconies only had a very partial covering so if it rains you can't sit out which was a shame but it was the only negative we had during our stay.If I could have rated this at 4 1/2 I would have & I would certainly return again.Wonderful place to stay!

title: Terrible Customer Service
text: Pros first! Nice check in staff, nice comfy room, delicious dinner and food in general however..... Bar staff hadn’t a clue, it appeared they were all on their first day, literally organised chaos and extremely rude with it, the bar staff in particular need a course in customer service. Actually got shouted at when I tried to get out to the terrace for a cigarette...’closed, it’s closed’ in a very loud voice! Asked for some bar snacks in courtyard to be told they can’t serve in smoking area, I said that’s fine I’ll come down and collect them. A kind member of staff bought them to me anyway then his ‘manager’ came and berated him in front of our table! Took 4 different people to serve us 4 drinks then none of them collected our payment! Dinner was delicious but the service haphazard at best, sometimes waiting 20 minutes between dishes leaving our rice to go stone cold, very, very expensive for what you get. Breakfast service similar, ordered extra toast which turned up 20 minutes after we had all finished our food. Had to ask for ketchup 3 times! One member of our party had an issue with the lights in her room, meaning the service guys couldn’t get them to turn off until 2am....a good hour after she wanted to go to bed! All in all not a great experience and we won’t be returning, they need to sort the customer service issues and teach their staff how to talk to paying guests properly. No doubt the duty manager will post his standard copy and paste reply.

title: Nobu for 4 nights * COOL & TRENDY & DIFFERENT new modern London hotel
text: Stayed here with my daughter for 4 nights in July. Decided to stay here a bit out of the center of the city due to decent pricing & curiosity. Easy pleasant enough walk to the tube & loved being near the trendy Spitalfield market. Location was fine- I would stay here again when visiting the city. Service was friendly and attentive but too many guido type bouncer men on staff. Also one creepy man kept cleaning the same spot on a wall in the hall. Too many staff members without that much going on yet IMHO. Room was small & I wish it had a king bed instead of queen. Room was COOL though. Modern and very comfortable & plenty of space really. MY YOUNG ADULT DAUGHTER LOVED IT. Bathroom was LOVELY. AC worked well- that's a big priority for us. Great Asian style slippers, excellent toiletries, beautifully decked out mini bar. Thoughtful & gorgeous built-in Asian furniture & window screens. We slept well. We had breakfast included in our room charge and opted for their version of traditional English breakfast twice and skipped it twice. Presentation of the food was beautiful & tasty. LOVED the butterfly drinks at the hotel bar. The staff was outstanding late night at the bar putting TWO butterflies in our drinks because we were so excited about them. Very thoughtful touch. These life-like edible butterflies are amazing. IMPRESSIVE. Cool and trendy vibe here. Staff makes a concerted effort to please. I would recommend it.

title: Excellent stay at Nobu Shoreditch
text: We had a great 2 nights stay at Nobu Shoreditch a minimalist modern architecture hotel in a funky area in London. The area is really worth a visit as is the hotel. A very hip crowd. The room, a suite was not very big bit had a lovely balcony overlooking the Nobu bar & Restaurant underneath. Great bed, modern shower room, very minimalistic, Japanese style (pity no Japanese loo). Concrete, light wood, very slick. Breakfast was OK small portions and only à la carte. Very poor juice quality, not fresh for sure. Only regular coffee/tea included with breakfast, cappuccino etc is extra. But that was the only issue we had otherwise a great stay. Pitty a pool was not designed on the roof of the hotel.

title: When was the last time you did something for the first time?
text: Very elegant - contemporary design, great location, very nice bar and great restaurant. However, the staff was very young and amateur like - from the check in to the check out. My husband and I had an issue with a room next to us where there seemed to be a party going on until 7 am (many people coming in and out throughout the night and early morning and slamming the door) which resulted in no sleep at all for both of us and the hotel stuff was unable to deal with the situation even though we made a call down the reception at 4 am and a personal visit an hour later. At the check out, I asked for operations manager, but only had a chance to talk to one of the girls at the reception whose apology was inadequate. We were offered a special care on our next visit, but assured this young lady that there was most definitely not going to be another visit to their otherwise trendy establishment.

title: Great Design
text: I confess to owning a commercial building opposite the hotel, so have watched it being built, it’s a great building and looks stunning. I normally use the Hoxton but I thought I should try the Nobu. To be honest they are like chalk and cheese and it depends what you look for in a hotel. Firstly the rooms are great, loved the design and the beds are super comfy, nice bathroom and great that shutters give you complete blackout. Good heating/aircon very quiet, needed on the coldest night of the year! There are some problems with sound from other rooms, which should not be in a new build. I could hear a man coughing through the night. It’s a Japanese styled hotel this is reflected in decor, lighting and amenities. You also have a branch of Nobu Restaurant in the hotel and in fact it’s the only restaurant. I am not really into the cuisine but Shoreditch has many restaurants so not a problem. The Japanese cuisine also runs through the breakfast and room service menu, with everything having a twist. This might not suit everybody and I confess to popping over to the Hoxton for more traditional fare at breakfast. The lobby lacks atmosphere and was not warm on the night we were there. All in all pretty satisfied, little improvements would be some coffee bags and Earl Grey tea. Fresh milk in the fridge like the Hoxton should not be difficult. I hope the Fire Notices which should be on the back of the bedroom doors are on order! Plus a guest info folder in the room would be useful. It’s not been open for more than a few months so still time to tweak the offering.

title: Weekend at the new Nobu hotel
text: I agree with the other review that the rooms are small but decent size for hotels in London! bedding, towels and toiletries are nice. Staff was very friendly. We were there for one nigth celebrating my husband birthday without out toddler! so I did wanted to choose a nice hotel with a nice restaurant and I went for the Nobu instead one of the Morgans group which are always our preference. The hotel its very cool, I really like it, but our room was facing the neighbourhood with not a lot of privacy, on that aspect im glad we were there just for one night, i did not fancy to open the window and i like natural light!.. The telephone lines were not working and I had to phone the reception through my mobile. Then we went to the restaurant, same really cool, the music and the service, the hotel manager came to apologise for the telephone not working.. In the restaurant we waited 30 min for the wine list, just the list! then another 15 for the wine, then the food came before the wine! I really don't know what was happening with the wine list/wine but you don't leave your clients waiting for a drink for 45min!! The food was really nice and our waitress was very helpful, he knew and described every single dish we asked for. Overall we had a nice experience but I think management has to be improved in the restaurant, we noticed many staff moving around/standing around.

title: Wonderful property, great stay!
text: I absolutely loved my stay. The property itself is amazing and Shoreditch as an area is so cool. Great restaurants and bars, I was entertained every night I was there (and I stayed for a week) The style of the rooms is very minimalist and chic. The bathroom is the best part with the beautiful gold sink. Service when I was there was top notch at both the front desk and the restaurant. I had breakfast there every day and their "Full English" was a great mix of everything. Dinner service was sometimes a little slow, but the food was great. Will definitely stay again when I return.

title: Great
text: This was our 3rd visit in 1 year , the hotel is very relaxing Great rooms , clean comfortable and stylish Nice staff Good breakfast , lots of variety caters for all nationalities Will be back Parking outside the hotel if your fortunate, Saturday night Is free

title: Great boutique hotel
text: We have been 4 nights at Nobu Hotel Shoredict in a Deluxe room, facing the street. Great location in a very quiet street. The hotel is very tastefully decorated, with a modern japanese style. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The Nobu restaurant is amazing! We’ve eaten the most delicious gyozas and sushi. I truly reccommend both the hotel and the restaurant!

title: Stick to food not hotel
text: Stayed here last night - one night stay as part of a large group. Arrived at 515, told room wasn’t ready (check in normally 3pm). Whilst waiting for reception staff to deliberate how they could rectify the situation, another guest came along and was given a room immediately. No assistance available to help with bags etc so receptionist helped carry therefore leaving front desk unattended. Room so dark make up was a challenge. Weird lighting and a brown tinted mirror in bathroom. Reception staff extremely poor English which made for complications with other guests. The breakfast was amazing though (and the restaurant food which I’ll review separately). Look these are first world probs but that’s what trip advisor is about! Would we stay again. No. Would we dine again. Absolutely yes!!

title: Birthday celebration
text: Fabulous stay at this quirky hotel Room is modern and comfortable, with a big bed. Lighting could do with being brighter to put on make up but other than that no criticism Very good value and not too expensive

title: Excellent stay with a surprise
text: Stayed for 2 nights on business. Check-in was swift. Got an upgrade from my standard room. Room was nice but indeed a little small. The hotel is quiet, clean and the staff is really very friendly. My shirt was pressed without asking and free of charge -nice. Had an amazing dinner in the restaurant - and next morning at breakfast (which is excellent) was seated next to Mr. Nobu! The manager of the hotel Ms. Vega arranged for me to have Mr. Nobu's newly published autobiography sent to me - autograph and personal message included. Impressive. In short, great choice.

title: Nobu Hotel not for me!
text: I am actually sitting in my hotel room at the Nobu writing this review. Room 228 to be precise. So this is my last night of a 3 night stay and I can’t wait to get home. I am here with work as I am attending a company conference nearby. I never chose this hotel and would never do so. I am an Executive PA and have a wealth of experience and knowledge of booking hotels and venues. This hotel is pretentious to say the least. Low lighting everywhere which makes it impossible to see menus etc. Bedrooms are small and claustrophobic but credit where credit is due, the beds are comfortable. The pillows on the other hand are awful. One being too low and two being to high. Also the fact that my room is above some service door with constant banging throughout the night does not make for a good nights sleep. My view from my window is a horrible back street full of graffiti. The bathrooms have heated floors but because they are so small resemble a sauna every time you go in there. I actually had to ask for the heating to be turned off in there because all my toiletries were melting. The complimentary toiletries in the bathroom do not have the best smell either, so opted to use my own. The breakfast is grim and rather odd and if you are not in a hurry and don’t mind waiting 30 minutes for a coffee and 45 minutes for some porridge then the Nobu is for you. This morning I had to ask for the coffee to be put into a take away cup because it was served too late and I had to leave. I left the porridge after one mouthful. FYI the toast is safe! Tonight we had the private room booked and again it was small, too warm and claustrophobic. The food was awful but then again I do not eat Japanese food, so maybe ok for those that do. They waiters tried their best to bring me something I could eat and I ended up with chicken skewers with sticky rice. I was struggling with the chop sticks but gave up anyway when I came across some under cooked chicken. I actually gave up and said goodnight to my work colleagues and had a protein bar I brought with me and some warm water in my room. I would like to make a standard cup of tea but faced a Japanese tea pot and 2 clay cups with no handles displayed in a back lit square box (so not sure if for display only). Yippee I’m checking out first thing tomorrow morning, never to return and certainly never to book or recommend.

title: In the new trendy area
text: Nobu in Shoreditch is the new destination for those posh but understated looking for a new hot destination in town. The hotel offer a different perspective of luxury in which ‘green’ and ‘conscious’ seems to be the definition. There are a lot of positive and negative sides in this hotel. Rooms are nice, decorated very minimal, dark colors, with bamboo floor, but the bathrooms are excessively too small. I loved the natura bisse amenities, but honestly it was impossible to have a proper shower avoiding the steam room effect. The space is really small, with no opening outdoor but also the impossibility to keep the door open the result was terrible. Having Nobu food as room service a true privilege, but the room dedicated to the breakfast was really cold and impersonal. I did not like the corridors to the rooms, the have the feeling of old and used. The hotel misses a proper lobby, very useful if the reason of your travel is business

title: Pleasant stay, slightly underwhelming, some pitfalls..
text: We often book 1 night boutique hotels when we attend events in London - usually around East London, and the City as thats where we tend to go out. Nobu is a small building, tucked away from the main road and easy to miss. The new building itself is quite striking, and forms the home too for the popular restaurant. However it's not a brilliant location for tourists - whilst it's in the heart of a trendy nightlife area for locals (Hoxton) if you're new to London this may not be for you - it's a good 10 minute walk to a tube/ station, along a shabby street (which most of Hoxton is...) For heading out for a late night, in this area , it would be perfect. The entrance and welcome is fairly minimal, pleasant but everything feels a bit 'small' . There was a delay checking in, but this was no issue - and we were given free drinks whilst we waited - there is a very small bar area to wait in, and the bar tender was superb. The rooms are small, perfectly formed, but underwhelming. Japanese inspired - all the dark wood and minimalist features - including small shower room, made everything feel a bit cramped, and i'd imagine more than one night would be tough. However a big shame for us (and we're not cheap but...) was that several drawers in the main unit, and the mini bar were jam packed with extortionately priced snack items and drinks. Including wine, and 2 glasses laid out in a drawer in the dresser (warm by the way - there was no room in the mini fridge for anything to chill..!) We thought this was so funny we took a photo - I cant remember exact costs but they were easily 5 or 6 times that which you'd find at the corner store nearby (and even they were inflated for London!) I know hotels stock mini bars with high priced drinks, and sometimes we take advantage of the convenience - but this scenario was ridiculous, because the hotel we were in is certainly not 5 star luxury... Also as it's a small place don't expect a view - we looked over some garages. This is fine, it's East london. But a shame nonetheless. So i've given 3 stars - staff were nice, we got comped free drinks on arrival, and the room was clean. There are very few perks to staying at the Nobu - and it's very high priced compared what you find at Citizen M, the Hoxton, and the Montcalm - all favourite boutique hotels that do similar things nearby, but much better in our opinion - they're more fun, nearer transport and if you shop around can be had for much better prices..

title: New Hotel Just Opened Some Problems!
text: Stayed at This hotel for one night for my wife's birthday. While I knew there were still some minor things happening in the hotel I felt a little let down with some parts. Check In was good they let us check in early and the front desk staff were nice. Lobby is a nice lots of dark wood ect. Room- was ok very small considering we went for the middle range not the entry level (hate to think of the size of the entry rooms) We were facing the back of the hotel so you have to have the shutter closed otherwise the people opposite can see in your room. Mirrored glass would have work well here. Bed is very hard!! And there are no slippers in the room. Other Nobu hotels I have stayed in give you complementary water all you get here is rice crackers, the air con in our room was broken and was giving out a terrible small (drains) Upon check out this was mentioned and while the staff member was sorry there was nothing offered to put it right! Would have been nice to been offered at least some breakfast or something. Restaurant was nice food was just like every other Nobu restaurant. Service could have been better we ordered two cocktails we waited 20 min in the end I had to go to the bar myself to asked where they were. I was told that there was a problem with the ticket machine!! Have to say the fact that we were the only people in the restaurant the waiter should have seen that we never had our drinks!! Again service is key!! Overall nice hotel would be nice to go back once they have been open for a while to see how they performed I am a big fan of the brand. 5/10😞

title: Lovely hotel but out of place in Shoredich
text: I really liked this hotel, it feels very tranquil and the rooms are well designed and comfortable. It was exceptionally clean and nice and stylish as you would expect from Nobu. A couple of things could be better in the room such as softer pillows (couldn’t find a pillow menu or get an answer from reception to address this) the corridor noise and next door noise is louder than I would expect in a new hotel. The service could have also been a little better, I waited on the phone for over 10 minutes when trying to order room service and was cut off twice. Also check in and out was slow. The staff didn’t go above and beyond by any means. Although they were friendly. The reception and bar area are very nice and feel very relaxing and chilled . The rooms have no view and the surroundings don’t match the hotel style at all. I like Shoreditch and I like the area however Nobu feels out of place here and therefore cannot make the most of any outdoor space or views. I got a very good price for the room so it was exceptional value so on these terms I would stay again and recommend as my few petty gripes are probably an exception rather than the norm.

title: Love this place
text: The food at nobu is consistently great and shoreditch has its own special vibe. The hotel is great.. great toiletries, comfortable bed and delicious breakfast but the rooms are very warm and the AC not very effective.

title: AVOID AVOID AVOID! Dirty, horrible, smelly, worn. Yikes!!! Run!!!!
text: It was really one of the worst hotel experiences I have had recently. Dirty, worn, smelly and did I mention dirty? The restaurant is fine but whatever you do: do not stay at this hotel. Run - don't walk!! Don't stroll. Sprint!!!

title: Amazing Albany
text: I have been a regular guest at The York & Albany over the years and can honestly say that the service is excellent. The staff are so attentive, paying attention to personal details and requests. The rooms are always exquisite and beautifully furnished and the hotel have always made a special fuss over birthdays, anniversaries as well as looking after me so wonderfully. An absolute pleasure to stay.

title: Lovely meal and stay
text: Was given a Red letter experience by our son and daughter in law. Great welcome by staff and checked into our room, had an amazing room The Stable number 4 and it was huge great furniture and the bed so comfortable although on the main road didn't really hear any noise. Could have done with somewhere in shower to put the gel/ shower ect. Great smellies to use complimentary and water left in room no tea coffee but did have room service. The meal was amazing and the atmosphere in the restaurant was lively and enjoyable, had drinks in the bar after the meal before retiring to our room. All in all a great stay would return if in area.

title: Truly wonderful stay
text: Highly recommend this wonderful spot in Camden! Exceptional staff, especially Karim in the restaurant - he was amazing and a very friendly face to greet us each morning. Perfect service and outstanding food. Managers very visible each day and very friendly....room was awesome and clean. A short Uber ride to downtown. We will be back!!!!

title: Disappointing
text: What a shame. We wanted to take my mother for Sunday lunch and I happened across the York & Albany knowing it was Gordon Ramsey the food should be excellent having been to the Maze, Savoy grill room and others. I am sorry it was OK but tough beef is not good. The limited roast selection was disappointing so we left after the main dish to get desert somewhere else. Maybe an off day but once is enough. We loved the atmosphere and decor. Pitty!

title: Restaurant Review Not Hotel
text: We booked the York and Albany for a special family meal and let them know in advance we would be bringing a baby. Brilliantly they seated us on a large table with a huge sofa and also plenty of space to hide the buggy and a high chair already in situ. Although I initially thought the waiter was disappointed he had been landed with the “family” table rather than a nice tidy business lunch perhaps he was just keen to remain extra attentive?? The food was good and I tried the pan fried mackerel and the pork belly – which was lovely but a bit too much for lunch. My 12 year old son loved the scallops and his fish pie was excellent. My sister enjoyed the goat’s curd and beetroot salad followed by a generous portion of perfectly cooked cod. And finally the 1 year old baby thoroughly enjoyed the generous and tasty sausage and mash and then thankfully fell asleep a very contented little man!! Only my son had enough space for an amazing sticky toffee pudding – although we all helped him out. Only one niggle which is that we were not offered the bar menu which had some lighter meals.

title: Dissapointing stay for my 40th Birthday, poor disabled access. Worst hotel stay ever.
text: My partner surprised me on New Year's Day on my 40th birthday with a stay at the York and Albany and a visit to the near by Jazz Cafe in Camden. I was excited to stay as I shot a wedding at the York and Albany in 2013 and was very impressed with the place, particularly the food. I have spinabifida and since my last visit have developed severe walking problems. My partner was careful to book somewhere that had a good sized bathroom and normal disabled access such as a lift. We were very disappointed when we arrived to find the lift was not working, with no idea when it would be operational. Our room was on the second floor, which meant walking up four flights of stairs. Not good at all. The receptionist tried to find another room for us, with no luck, so we had to walk up the stairs. This was obviously very difficult for me, especially carrying my suitcase, as no one offered to help take it to me room for me. When we got in the room, we were very surprised to find it looked entirely different from the picture on the website. The floor was carpeted instead of bare floorboards, the nice decor behind the bed had gone and was replaced with drab plain wallpaper. Even the teddy was missing from the bed. The floor also very strangely was not level, sloping up towards the outer wall from the door. This meant the head end of the bed was lower than the foot end, not great. We then discovered that the shower door was broken and couldn't be closed and the rest of the fittings in the bathroom looked very tired. My partner complained and again, no alternative was available. We then made our way out for the Jazz Cafe (which was amazing btw) and asked about the bar, looking forward to some cocktails on our return, we were really surprised to find there was no bar service after 11pm. Very odd and disappointing in a central London hotel. I then remarked how 'at least we have a fine breakfast to look forward too'. I should have known we'd have no such luck. When we arrived for breakfast in the morning we were seated to a very tired looking table, with laminate trim hanging off the edges of it. The waiter (who was working alone) handed us a sticky menu card that shared no resemblance to the breakfast menu card we had in our room. Consequently we had no idea what was included in our complimentary breakfast. We made our order of eggs benedict and salmon with scrambled egg. I must say, being Gordon Ramsay's hotel, I was expecting the eggs benedict to be fantastic. I was sorely disappointed. The muffin was stale and the hollandaise sauce was tasteless. We asked for toast which never arrived, coffee, which never arrived and when we left, we were shocked to see that we had to pay, as it turns out these items were not included in the complimentary breakfast, even thought the waiter said they were! I was even more shocked when after paying and complaining about the breakfast, the waiter held his hand out for a tip! Unbelievable. We packed up and left to go home. We made our complaints to the receptionist who did nothing about them, no discount, no offer of help or of taking anything further. We then proceeded to leave and found that the bins had just been emptied and the entrance threshold just outside the main door was covered in rotten vegetables and dozens of broken egg shells. All in all, a complete disaster. Room not as advertised, shocking disregard for disabled accessibility, no special complimentary touches for my 40th birthday and a train-wreck of a breakfast dining experience. To say I am disappointed would be huge understatement. After my visit in 2013 I was left with an impression of excellence. I don't know what has happened in the intervening 5 years, but Gordon Ramsay should be ashamed to have his name associated with this fiasco. In all sincerity, I can say this was the worse hotel stay I've ever had.

title: Pleasant Stay - but seriously overpriced.
text: I have never written a review before, we travel a lot staying in lovely places around the world - most recently the beautiful Babington House in Somerset. I am not mega fussy but do like a nice hotel!! I felt compelled to pass on my thoughts of this 'hotel' as I normally have a good nose for finding a nice place to stay...and this one was a stinker! We booked for one night as meeting up for a birthday celebration in the restuarant. I thought it was a no brainer as have eaten in Gordon Ramseys other restaurants and stayed at Castell Monestero in Tuscany (which he is associated with and consults on the restaurant). We have always had a good experience and high standard of servce. We stayed in a deluxe room priced at £300 per night inc VAT and breakfast. Which is pricey but we enjoy staying in London a couple of times a year, previously spending the same amounts on rooms at Browns, Haymarket Hotel etc...and have always felt we have recieved excellent service and value for money. We arrived at about 4.30 on a Friday afternoon having luckily found a meter opposite to park on (which is free after 6.30 all weekend.) We struggled to find the entrance to the 'hotel' which is has no entrance signage and is tucked behind the pub. Its is also next to the stairs which lead to the noisey and smelly restaurant kitchen, with bins, old boxes and staff bikes in front of it - not very glam! Having found the entrance we then had to find a member of staff to check us in, after an awkward few minutes hanging around we went into the bar and a rather unfriendly woman said she would be with us shortly. We checked in and she seemed rather irrated that she had to show us to the room,she let us in and disappeared! The room was pleasant, a little shabby and unloved and very cramped. Everything looked like it could do with a paint or bit of polishing, but it was clean and as only staying one night it was fine. We had asked for a quiet room as knew the hotel was on a busy road, and the room was in a very quiet part of the building, but as the hotel backs onto the main line going into King Cross Station you still get the trains going passed - but the noise level was acceptable. The TV did not work and just said 'no satalite signal' we tried in vain to ring reception several times but got no answer it.....just rang and rang - so turn the TV off! The bathroom had under floor heating which was SO hot that you could not walk on it without shoes which was crazy, ended up putting towels over the floor to walk on. The products provided are supposed to be Miller Harris but the hotel had obviously ran out and had provided the little mini bottles you get from Boots of Tresemme and an odd make of Shower gel in bright yellow (not sure what is was) Although the floor was red hot the towel rail was cold and coming off the wall. You do not get any mini bar or tea making facility in the room, as no answer at reception for room service we went down to the pub for a coffee. We are not tight at all, and know London prices are high but do feel a litte uncomfortable paying £5.00 for 2 warm (not hot) coffees in tiny grubby cups which are just plonked in front of you from a very unfriendly waiter....charming! Anyway I think you probly get the idea....Could go on and on. This is not a 'hotel' by any stretch of the imagination it is a B&B above a pub/restaurant on a busy junction on the edge of Regents Park. Great if you want a room for the night but definately NOT worth £300 a night!!! When we checked out (by someone who didn't even know how to work the chip and pin machine!!) we feeling well and truely turned over having fallen for the glossy marketing and clever PR. The restaurant was nice and we had a loveley meal...wished we had just paid the £300 to get a cab home instead!

title: Unique but essentially rooms over a restaurant.
text: This is essentially a restaurant/bar (more restaurant than bar) with some rooms above it. The location is excellent - 5 minutes walk from the buzz of Camden yet in a quiet area very close to Regents Park. Thankfully it is in a quiet area because the windows are not double glazed. Without the excellent restaurant below this 'hotel' wouldnt be in existence. The restaurant is part of the Gordon Ramsey brand and has a warm atmosphere with very efficient and friendly staff. The breakfast has to be one of the tastiest that I have experienced. We had evening dinner there and chose from a reasonably priced set menu. However the set menu was a choice of 2 choices for each course only. A la carte was fairly expensive eg 9 oz rib-eye steak was £32 plus the additional cost of vegetables etc and service charge on top. There is a very small entrance hall which is the reception but consists of a stand where you check in - if a member of staff happens to be passing! It is not manned even throughout the day. That presents to me a security risk as you can enter and be upstairs in less than a minute without any intervention. I appreciate that can be done in a large hotel but at least there are staff employed and present in those larger establishments. We had to wait nearly 5 minutes before someone came to enable us to check out. What really concerns me is the flies. Our room was very comfortable and homely preserved in traditional style but had several flies flying around. Despite my best efforts I couldnt get to them all but I reported it to the staff when we went for a walk. An hour or two later the friendly lady member of staff reported that they had been removed/killed. Not so, or perhaps more entered, as there were 4 when we went back in the room. We had to use copious quantities of fly killer to manage the problem. There were several flying around the reception area which was blamed on the fact that they fly in when the front door is opened. I would guess there is more of a problem with air conditioning as that would explain the existence of the problem in the bedroom. The rooms are very well equipped with tea & coffee making facilities, slippers, dressing gowns and well stocked with toiletries etc. The bath is retro style but would be difficult to get in or out for elderly or infirm. The bed was extremely comfortable and the room had an appealing fireside to one wall. We struggled to get many channels as the signal seemed to be very limited - that didnt bother us but thankfully the free wifi was efficient in our room. Overall a pleasant stay but I remain undecided on whether it merits a recommendation. Yes, its unique and different but to describe it as boutique in my opinion would be wrong as that to me conjures up an image that would be misleading.

title: Surprise Party
text: Organised a surprise party for my wife in the Regency room and stayed the night in the hotel. Venue were very helpful, food was fantastic. Room was nice. Breakfast the following morning was lovely. All in all great experience.

title: The best way to spread Christmas Cheer, is not to go here.
text: Took clients to the gingerbread house recently and it’s quite underwhelming. The premise is good but they haven’t invested enough in it. The inside is laid out like a fun gingerbread house with sweets glued to the wall and it looks cute, however, food wise it’s very sparse (I was glad I’d eaten before, just in case!) a tiny platter of mini food with one savoury selection and one sweet. They then give you gingerbreads to decorate which would be cute except we got minimal decorations to put on the gingerbread men so they looked a bit cr*p! Then they rushed us out with no warning, saying that we knew we had a two hour window. (Technically true but it’s supposed to be fun and a little warning would be helpful when you know there is still half a bottle of Prosecco left!) We asked for little boxes to take our gingerbread men home and when they came back they’d actually broken them up to fit in the boxes! (We did laugh at that but if you actually cared you’d be really annoyed especially if you’d brought kids!) There are a lot nicer Christmassy things to do in London than this..

title: Fantastic stay, wonderful area.
text: Excellent stay at the York&Albany. Lovely staff, great location and nicely sized bedroom. We stayed in a superior deluxe double and it was perfect for two people. Nicely sized bathroom with tub and shower. Breakfast is included even to your room. And they replenish bottles of water each day. A nice touch!

title: It was the bomb.
text: Staying here was set up as a surprise for my birthday and it is a lovely place to stay. We were in the primrose suite. 4 poster bed, chunky bed with marshmallow pillows, fab decor, modern tv. Lovely candle holders underfloor heating in the bathroom. Just generally a very warm and relaxing place to stay. Breakfast menu was huge. Our package was a continental breakfast which was a massive bowl of fresh ripe fruit, a bowl of granola with compote and yoghurt, and a pastry, all very yummy but I was too full to enjoy it all :) The team here who serve and who are at the bar and FOH are very friendly courteous and clearly enjoy their job. Definitely will be staying here again.

title: Not really worth money we spent...
text: We stayed there in November 2011. I have booked the suite which I thought would be suitable for two adults and one child. When I called the hotel, nobody asked me for the age of the child - assuming that its a newborn! When we arrived it appeared that our suite is REALLY TINY! There was a double bed in the middle, and for my little one -they wanted to put a cot near our bed! When the receptionist saw our child, then immediately assured us that it will be sorted. It was, they put a tiny metal framed bed in our bed end. This tiny metal bed was incredibly uncomfy and noisy, so we ended up with the little one sleeping with us, not really something you dream about paying so much money for a 'luxury' hotel. Tiny bathroom, 'antique' smelly furniture, not something I would like to see and use in a 'boutique' hotel. I am not sure if the room has been cleaned before we arrived, I found old packet of cookies in the drawer of the bedside table. After we went out to town and we get back, cookies have been gone, so somebody definitely searched through the drawers, I had strange impression that our stuff habe been searched through too... No comments for that... The strangest thing was that when we got downstairs, the receptionist had completely NO IDEA where The Maze Grill is. We wanted her to call us a cab, but she had not a clue where this restaurant is located! Shame, Mr Ramsey should check maybe from time to time if his people do know who is he? That put us off, but after the night in the tiny bed, located just nearby the train passing by, we ate the worst breakfast ever downstairs. First of all, we have been ignored by all staff for first 30 minutes. I could not stand waiters and all the same people passing us by, not even asking what would we like to order. Shame, I had to go and ask the waiter to PLEASE finally bring us coffee and eggs benedict. Not really tasty, I think the worst I ever had. I was wondering if ham used to make this dish has been bought from the cheapest supermarket...No smell and plastic taste. Disguisting English muffin, not worth it! And then we had to pay for it, because BREAKFAST IS NOT INCLUDED when we paid £250 for the night. Ridiculous! Overall impression for the York and Albany downstairs restaurant - filthy, the curtains have never been washed. Definitely not worth the money wespend, please Mr Ramsay, pop in sometimes...

title: Lovely Stay, Wonderful staff
text: I found this hotel after searching for ages for hotels that didn't cost the earth for a Sunday night, and it included breakfast! The room was beautiful and breakfast was fabulous. We upgraded £5 for a full English, such good value for money. I felt the need to write a review as having stayed in a chain hotel the night before where the staff simply couldn't have been less interested, the staff at York and Albany were all so welcoming and friendly. We will definitely stay again the next time we're in London!

title: maybe Gordon should have his own properties on his show and fix them !
text: I statyed here about 10 months ago, and have only decided to write reviews after a terrible experience at another hotel, unrelated to this one i booked one of the executive rooms, which unfortunately was next to the function room, and there was an event, the shouting and singing finished at 1am.... the bed was Ok, but no working wifi. my biggest issue was how unhelpful the front desk staff were.. when i checked out, the printer was not working, so they could not print my bill (I was on business, so needed it for my expenses), they promised to email it to me that day. nothing was received within a week, so i emailed them, and emailed them, and emailed them 6 times, eventually they replied, with my receipt cut and pasted the email, i replied, and said this was not what i needed for my expenses, and can they send me the proper VAT invoice, 10 months alter, still no reply, so I gave up, paid for it myself, and vowed never to stay here again.

title: Could Improve On Service
text: We had booked Sunday lunch for ourselves and two friends we were meeting in London. The greeting service was mediocre, we waiting a long time to be seated (we had booked about three weeks before). The food was excellent, we all had three courses, the only thing I could fault was the plate of cheese and biscuits, very meagre portion, and nothing about it looked attractive. The main problem was with our server, she was miserable, slow, and didn't seem to have a clue about taking food orders.
