We were not checked on any of our courses, and although the food was really good, the service definitely let the restaurant down. Not sure if I would go back.

title: Great location and a good atmosphere
text: pThis hotel is in a good location within walking distance to the tube at Camden Town. It has a good bar and restaurant offering a great choice of food and drinks. The rooms are well equipped with a very comfortable beds with lovely linens and pillows. There is all you would expect . The shower room was great plenty of towels and hot water . We stayed with some friends from Germany and they were impressed and thought the ambience was very good and both our evening meal and breakfast were very good. We would all stay here again . The staff were friendly helpful and made our stay very pleasant .

title: Cosy hotel in Camden
text: We stayed one night at the "York and Albany" with 2 adults and 3 children. We enjoyed it. We had 2 really cosy interconnected rooms (antic furniture ...). Service was very kind and helpful. The situation is almost ideal: near Camden market and Regent's park, 10' from St Pancras Station. Breakfast at the restaurant is really excellent. The best americano in a hotel.

title: A wonderful stay
text: We stayed at the York and Albany for our wedding night and we were not disappointed, I did mention in our on line reservation that it was our wedding night and we were treated beautifully. The room was beautiful, tastefully decorated and was the one we has seen in the pictures on the website which had made us book in the first place. We were greeted with a bottle of champagne in the room cooling in an ice bucket with a little card saying 'congratulations' from V&A. The room was clean and the bed was extremely comfy and very high!! The only negative I can say was that it was a little too hot during the night but fortunately it wasn't too noisy with the windows open. We ate in the bar area, as we had eaten well during the day we didn't have a full meal but what we did have was stunning, service was good and extremely friendly. We also had breakfast in the morning which again was of good quality, the best egg Benedict I have eaten. We then had a further surprise as they did not charge us for breakfast and put it in the room price. I did not book this hotel due to its association with Gordon Ramsey, I didn't even realise until after I booked it but his staff and hotel are a credit to him.

title: Great Value night out
text: Good location near to Camden Market and a lovely venue. Food superb and the staff were very friendly. Asking for a finger bowl after eating Tiger Prawns seemed to cause an issue

title: PERFECT 5*
text: We booked the York and Albany on 22nd June for the evening of our wedding. We booked all the rooms apart from one as this had already been booked in advance.. The hotel was PERFECT, I got ready in the suite which has a separate entrance around the corner, it was big and extremely clean. The bathroom was also spotless. All our guests complimented what a gorgeous boutique hotel it was and they would all be recommending it again. All the rooms were great, no complaint of loud noise etc. The staff were exceptional, we all had drinks when we arrived back after our wedding (at a different venue) at about 2am. They couldn’t have been more helpful! Breakfast was also perfect, a good selection and very polite and efficient staff. We can’t wait to stay here again! Thank you again!!

title: Gordon Ramsay is about food, not hotel
text: stayed for 1 night, for business. was early, so couldn't check in - fair enough. asked to change my clothes

title: To much salt
text: Had lunch at the York and Albany starter a artichoke soup which was excellent followed by a ragout with tagliatelle which unfortunately the chef overdid the salt making it inedible , a dessert of rhubub and custard was very nice. The staff were very attentive. The drinks were on the expensive side. Parking was ok street about 100 yards away

title: Horrible
text: The service in this Restaurant is terrible. It took 15 mins for me to get a glass of water. I was jammed in a corner between 2 tables to the point I and the staff had to squeeze between them to get at my table. Got my starter handed to me and didn't see any member of staff until He came to take my plate away. I ordered the roast beef special which was supposed to have horseradish sauce but no sign of it and no sign of a staff member to ask for some. The beef was half grissle and unbeatable fat. They then had the cheek to try and add 12.5% service charge to my bill. Gordon Ramsay should be asshamed to have his name on this place.

title: A true gem in the heart of Camden Town!
text: Honestly perplexed by some of the reviews left here. We had a late night dinner in the restaurant before a stay at the upstairs hotel. Amazing food, powerful wines & and beautiful rooms. The only thing that tops all of that was the incredible service we received from Aneta. A true hidden gem in Camden Town, that I’d thoroughly recommend!

title: Wonderful
text: My husband and I live in London, but decided to celebrate our anniversary by staying a night at the York & Albany, as we had heard such good reviews. We had a lovely time, the suite was very special, huge room, comfy bed and a wonderful wet room. Very efficient room service delivered hot coffees to our room and breakfast was also fantastic, the dining room so Cosy and the staff very attentive. For a tourist visiting London, I think the location is just perfect...20 mins walk into the West End,the bustle of Camden 5 mins away, and then the loveliness of Regents Park, Primrose Hilll, Hampsted and Belize park also on the doorstep. We would highly recommend.

title: Great location and lovely room
text: Great building and well designed ! Very clean and ideal location . Some areas looking a little tired and a refresh required for such a price eg bed linen frayed and ceilings water marked in restaurant ! But that said a lovely stay ! Get the paint brush out and it's perfect

title: Lovely dinner
text: The food here was superb, as were the cocktails. A little on the pricey side but that was expected. There was a nice ambiance to the dining area as well as the bar at the front for drinks. Good place for dinner dates.

title: Daughters must do list
text: My daughter is a big fan of his majesty Gordon the first. Our meal did not disappoint. Our waiter Micheal made a recommendation for a two course seafood that I would not have picked but thoroughly enjoyed. Service just right. I'm sure I've typed 200 characters by ow but trip advisor says I have to add more.

title: Wedding Anniversary
text: A lovely greeting and great service. Our Anniversary surprise from hotel was a lovey gift of food products from their deli .Our room was delightfully homely with lovely comfortable bed and so well appointed ,slippers ,robes, great coffee machine and free wi fi for those who are not romantic ! lots of thought in a guests needs. The view of the park and John Nash's elegant houses was exquisite . The food on set menu is tasty and breakfast choices are great, ( we didn't eat again until the evening) Room 7 named Camden Market, is situated at side of hotel and I'd recommend a stay here regardless to it being romantic or just in need of a descent nights stay. We would go back tomorrow , we went to Buckingham palace and the British museum during our stay both fab and hotel isn't to far from Camden underground. Nice area .

title: excellent reception, pleasant but noisy hotel
text: As per previous comments, the reception staff were very friendly and helpful. The same cannot be said for the restaurant, whislt they were not unhelpful, the service and food were average. the place is trendy and has a good atmosphere and the suite (room 4) was spacious. The main drawback for me was that it was very noisy due to traffic and street noise, not something the hotel can avoid, but not great for a restful night. the locality is ok, nothing close by of noteworthiness but not run down. Nice boutique hotel, but not outstanding. Slightly bitter taste left by charging me for the postage of a t-shirt left behind, but hey,times are tough!

title: Lovely experience
text: The building from the outside looked like it needed some tlc, inside whilst retaining some original features it looked worn. The bedroom was nice, the bedding was lovely quality. I was disappointed that there was no tea or coffee making facilities but we could have used room service. Complimentary water was a nice touch. Our evening meal was superb , a full English breakfast was also of good quality and nicely cooked and presented. A good service was provided. My husband remarked that it was great to see his pint of bitter served in a named glass. Check in and check out was efficient. Be aware there is a constant traffic flow throughout the night, but hey it is in Camden. A great base for exploring and the town was extremely interesting.

title: York and Albany - FOUL
text: We have been visiting and staying in the York and Albany Hotel literally since the night it opened. We have had lovely dinners there, great fun at the bar, and enjoyed staying in many of the rooms. Over a reasonable period of time sadly we have noticed standards slipping, but our most recent stay really was awful. On arrival the receptionist was dismissive to the point of rudeness. Our room was not dirty as such but certainly not clean - the rug had clearly not been vacuumed and the headboard had grease stains from other people’s hair (yuk). But worst of all was our experience at breakfast. We waited 30 minutes after ordering and still no breakfast arrived

title: Never again , and I told them
text: 4 businessman for lunch on a Tuesday and the place is empty. Reading the menu as we are cramped into the round table in the corner although there are only a couple of other tables with customers, Im thinking what am I going to eat !. Starter, ducks heart on toast is tasty but not worth £8.50 . Mains is a problem so little choice. A flat iron steak at £24 without anything is rejected by us all. 2 of us go for English lamb , but when it is served I see the look on the Hosts face - is this it ! And it's not cooked 2 x £50 , what a joke ! The desert menu is rejected by us all, and as we give verbal feedback to the staff as we leave , there is a look of disbief on their faces , yes thats right we won't be be returning again. Mr R , how did you cover the rent on that place, but then again that's not my problem

title: Very comfy bed - lovely decor
text: Stayed here for our anniversary and were upgraded to a suite - room 4 with complimentary prosecco and fruit. This was a large room with a vaulted ceiling with huge antique mahogany wardrobes and drawers. The bed was incredibly comfortable and the bathroom was fitted with a big walk in shower. The room faces onto a main junction by regents parks and with no double glazing the traffic was a constant noise - this was mainly a problem when there were sirens or hellicopters ! The windows also faced onto the seating area at the front of the bar which was noisy in the afternoon but quiet when we returned later in the evening. I would have liked tea and coffee making facilities in the room but otherwise we were very impressed with the quality and decor. The hotel reception is very difficult to find as it is round the back of the bar/restaurant and not signposted. The hotel reception staff were very helpful and friendly on check in and out. Unfortunately the same cannot be said regarding the bar staff - we were ignored in the evening when we wanted to order some cocktails then service was very slow. The breakfast was delicious however we felt that again the service could have improved hence my rating of very good not excellent

title: Lovely food, hit and miss service
text: We stayed at the York & Albany recently as part of an experience package. We were upgraded upon arrival, which was an unexpected plus, and our room was lovely. The rooms aren't large, but have bags of personality and individual touches - definitely beats your typical generic London hotel room. The only problem we had with the room was slow draining water in the bathroom sink - but that wouldn't deter me from staying again. Our package included dinner at the restaurant, which is where the service slightly fell down. As I had (correctly) assumed that we wouldn't be able to order anything we wanted off the a la carte menu, I had ask the waiter a couple of times which dishes were included in our offer. It would have been a nice touch if the maitre de had already known we were on a Red Letter Day, and given us the correct menu to start with. It's a bit embarrassing to have your menu taken off you! Once we had the correct menu we ordered water and wine - the wine came immediately, but we had to remind our waiter that we'd ordered water as well after a 10 minute wait. There was a similar delay for our bread, which only arrived once my partner was half way through his soup - after we had had to remind our waiter again. I understand that there's a fine balance between rushing diners and allowing time between courses to digest and chat, but as a general rule the food took quite a long time to arrive for every course (we waited at least 25 minutes for our starters). Each course was delicious however, and we had absolutely no complaints about the taste of the food. The couple on the next table to us obviously knew the manager, and had attention lavished upon them throughout the evening: recommendations for food and wine and lots of questions as to whether they were enjoying themselves. It would have been great if every diner in the restaurant could have been treated to the same level of exceptional service. Breakfast the day had a similar delay in service, and my eggs royale arrived cold - although they were very tasty. The hotel is beautiful and in an excellent location: I would only say that the level of service in the restaurant could be improved.

title: Ramsay give up Hells Kitchen and get back to England Pronto
text: Bought this as a Christmas present for my partner and my sister and her partner. The deal was overnight stay with dinner. On arrival check in was a bit sketchy. With confusion over the red letter codes. However we went and had a drink in the bar before dinner and found the bar service was pretty good although they forgot our olives. We then had dinner we ordered drinks after a 20 minute wait and then ordered food. Our food arrived before our drinks so we had to remind one of the waiters. It was explained to us by the waiter that we were entitled to three courses off the menu that was presented. The food was pretty good. Disappointingly the ladies toilets downstairs from the restaurant were in an awful state with only one working toliet the others were hideous. On returning to the hotel room we found there was no remote for the TV and in the morning discovered there was no hairdryer. Had breakfast which again we had a choice of various dishes that was included in the deal and that was actually pretty good. However on revisting the same toilets from the night before they were in the same condition. Checked out and was then given £147 food bill as from the choice provided for the evening meal they all had supplements. Overall it needs attention the staff need more training and although its not an expensive place to stay or eat at with Gordons name attached you do tend to have higher expectations.

title: Great location
text: Stayed here for one night as it was local to where I need to be that night and the following day. Everything was great at the beginning - friendly staff, very nice room, etc, but was disappointed the following morning. I had breakfast (one slice of toast with half a small avocado, one slice of bacon and half a grilled tomato), with a glass of orange juice. All fine. Came to check out and had to wait ages for the the reception person to appear. I rang the hotel to see if that would bring anyone forward, no luck. I went through to the restaurant area to ask for someone. Waited about another seven minutes before the reception guy turned up. Same guy as night before, but was very surly this time - bordering on rude. Told me that as I had had a 'hot' breakfast, I would be charged an extra £5 in addition to the amount included in the room rate! I pointed out that I had had one item but was told that I could have gone 'hog wild' and would still 'only' have been charged the extra £5. As I was now in danger of being late for important meetings, I didn't take it any further but it left a bad taste. A little flexibility given that I had only had one item off the menu would have perhaps been better customer service. Also, the way I read the menu seemed to imply that you could only have one item! Other than that, the room was fine, great shower, the bed was really comfortable - although I would debate it being a 'quiet' room!

title: A Right Gordon Fest!!!
text: As the lucky recipient of some Gordon Ramsay vouchers for Christmas I went on to Gordon's website to book dinner at Restaurant Gordon Ramsay BUT to my sheer delight discovered that he has a townhouse in Regent's Park. No question what won! We checked in a bit too early but not an issue as we were given a table in the bar. The menu is so diverse and as we had a dinner reservation for the dining room and I wanted to save myself for the Rib-eye we happily shared a pizza at the same time enjoying a cheeky glass of Prosseco. After lunch the lady on reception checked us in and we were delighted with our room. I travel on international business so the room was perfect for us as it was a home away from home as opposed to a carbon copy of one modern room does all. I understand from Holly our receptionist that all the rooms are different which is very me. A beautiful Regency building and it honestly felt that we were just staying in a very rich friends townhouse! We went for a bracing walk in Regent's Park, laid on the bed watching afternoon TV and then back to the bar for cocktails. Dinner didn't disappoint and we had an amazing table on the rich red velvety banquette opposite the pass. Outstanding mussels would you believe cooked in Camden ale followed by the Rib-eye. I was in food heaven and full so I only had room left to share a super treacle tart with clotted cream. It was really nice actually because it was clearly Gordon's level of cooking BUT the service was really grounded and informal. Rolled on upstairs and slept very well

title: I'll be eating there again, lovely food!
text: We had a great, attentive waiter who made the whole experience lovely, contrary to recent reviews. I highly recommend the lamb, cod and tuna, all delicious. Mixed with the 'Tin Hut' New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc a perfect combination!

title: Average food and below average service
text: I had a high hopes for this restaurant. The building is lovely. The decor is lovely. Unfortunately the experience was pretty poor. Meals delivered to the table incomplete and then the remainder of the dish was delivered three quarters of the way through the meal. Staff forgot to order parts of our meal, we waited a long time to have drinks delivered, when we ordered a further dish to eat, that was forgotten about and we had to remind them again. All up the service was poor and unfortunately the food was decidedly average. Management did give a discount and apologised, so that was to their credit but I will not be returning. Real shame.

title: You must stay here. The staff are fantastic!!
text: We booked in for our anniversary and were so well cared for. We had been upgraded to the suite on check in and things only got better from there. The staff couldnt do enough for us. The food was marvellous and the heated bathroom floor was good enough to sleep on. Well done Y&A - loved every second!!

title: Lovely atmosphere, very very varied service - not sure if worth the ££££
text: York and Albany promises quality, atmosphere and of course, fantastic food......being under the wing of Angela Hartnett in the Ramsay collection. Well......When you arrive at York and Albany, don't be disappointed, it's not a 'pretty' setting, particularly next to the tyre shop! It's also appallingly signed, particularly for hotel guests, you really have to take a guess at how to get in.........However, when you pass through the door, class and elegance hit you in the face, the decor is beautiful, stunning victorian refurbishment, mixed with ultra modern fittings. When you find the hotel check in desk, it is intimate and the staff particularly attentive - I was very impressed. The room....I booked the four poster deluxe double that is featured in the images on the website....it is stunning - beautiful antique furniture, stunning high ceilings, what's missing is the fire to give it the cosy finish and to be honest, the settee is a little 'shoved' in at the end of the bed. The bathroom is a little clinical, but is full of quirky features, but with the original windows is particularly draughty!! A lovely glass of champers on arrival was particularly welcome as I settled in, but alas, to no avail, whatever myself and the 'concierge' tried, we couldn't get our satellite TV to work - when we had booked the York and Albany 6 months before for a romantic laze away weekend, this was of particularly annoyance as we wanted to laze in bed and chill, read and watch TV, not go out and sightsee. Luckily there was another room available in the same category and after a quick look, we arranged to move. This one was much less traditional, but still as luxurious and had a bigger bed.........Lovely!! The Restaurant on valentines evening, was of course busy. The service though - BEWARE, is appalling. We were seated at 20:30 in time, but were not given a menu, or asked if we would like a drink for around 20 minutes. NOT what you expect from the reputation of Angela Hartnett and Ramsays. The food, was particularly good, the wine choice was also really satisfactory. Again though - despite liking the length of time to sit and eat for a valentines dinner (we ended up leaving at around 2330 - 3 hours later!), it was the attention to detail and the atmosphere that lacked from our less than interested waiter. Luckily for us, the company was great and we weren't in a hurry, but it wasn't necessarily that, it was the lack of interest as I say. Hence when checking out we refused to pay the 12.5% service - £25 quid in all for lacklustre service is just not on. The building inside is beautiful, the bar area surprisingly relaxed and not full of pretence. The food seriously good, and the deli offers lots of options adjacent! All in all a lovely, romantic weekend, but not quite up to the price tag is our verdict! Angela still has a lot to overlook if it's going to stay as busy as it currently is in its' early days........

title: Couldn't do it justice but a home-from-home stay
text: I arrived late from work and left early, so didn't eat in the 'gastropub'. I was showed my bijoux but lovely room with an open window for fresh air (unusual) and a good bathroom. The man at the front desk was super helpful. I had a speedy Waldorf salad in my room which was delicious, complimentary fizzy and still water and a bottle of fizz. Beautifully decorated in muted, warm tones. My room needed more lighting - would have been helped if bedside lamp worked. Comfy bed - alot to be said for somewhere with only 9 rooms. Nice and quiet.

title: Comfortable rooms - Great location
text: My husband and I stayed here for one night in August '12. We also dined in the restaurant downstairs, which I would highly recommend. Staff were polite and helpful, the room we had was very spacious with a large comfortable bed, it has a traditional homely feel, this is obviously what they were aiming for when designing the rooms but I felt it lacked any 'wow' factor. Breakfast the following morning was good. I would recommend this hotel based on convenience of its location and there being a fantastic and reasonably priced restaurant and bar downstairs.

title: Character hotel with exceptional staff
text: We stayed in a superior room for two nights over Christmas. Our room was full of character with beautiful windows complete with working shutters. Large complementary bottles of water both days and a tasty Christmas gift on arrival. The bed was extremely comfortable with soft, good quality pillows. The hotel is a listed building so expect character rather than logically planned facilities - but the space is used well. We had some minor problems - no waste paper bin in the bedroom and varying temperature in the shower - but what made this hotel really stand out for us was the quality of the staff. They were exceptionally warm, friendly and helpful from the moment we arrived until they waved us off when we left. Nothing was too much trouble. Some real stars in their excellent restaurant at breakfast and dinner. We'll definitely stay here again when we next visit Camden.

title: Excellent Hotel In A Great Location
text: This hotel is located close to both Regent's Park & Camden Town High Street. The hotel itself is a lovely old building. Given that the hotel is on a busy road we were surprised at how quiet it was in our bedroom. Quirky is a good way to describe it. Although we didn't have dinner, we did have a fantastic breakfast. The staff were friendly and very helpful. We'd stay here again definitely.

title: Nice but not as nice as we'd hoped
text: We stayed here for my husbands birthday and booked the Suite . The room was large and bed was comfy but we both felt the room lacked the luxury you expect when paying these rates and didn't feel like it was anything really special . Shower was also disappointing . I wouldn't say there was anything wrong with our stay it just lacked the wow factor and the little luxuries . It's also quite noisy with traffic . Breakfast was lovely and enjoyed our drinks in the evening at the bar .

title: Romantic Bedroom Suite
text: Lovely place to stay - easy to find, looking out over Regent's Park, and well located for public transport. Beautiful bedroom suite - four poster bed and spread over two levels with the bathroom down a small flight of stairs. Good quality bedding, pillows and mattress - decor leaned towards the shabby chic feel but still very nice and extremely welcoming. Amenities in the room were very good - there were even a set of GHD hair straightners in the drawer with the hairdryer. We worried about being able to hear the street at night, but our room was towards the rear of the property, so was very quiet. View from the window was out onto a roof garden. Excellent breakfast, as you would expect - freshly cooked to order and plentiful. I went for eggs Benedict and my partner had a full English option, and we ordered pastries for the table. All delicious and well presented. Staff were friendly, smiley and helpful - all you need. Prices were typical London hotel rates for this type of establishment, so you do pay for the celebrity chef name - but we thought it was worth the slightly higher charge to stay in such a nice place.

title: Disappointing Facilities, Friendly Satff
text: We stayed in a 'Deluxe' room (5AA* - apparently) and we were very disappointed. It was not a cheap overnight stay and we were expecting better. There was a dead orchid in the room, TV remote did not work, cords to open/close curtains were broken, No easy to access place close to a mirror to plug a hair drier, lukewarm water for the morning shower, disappointing food. I am a little frustrated as I have stayed in cheaper places in London with better facilities...

title: Great Hotel and Restaurant
text: This is a small boutique hotel with a great restaurant. The staff was very well trained and the person (I am sorry I can't remember his name) who handles all the hotel check in and check out was so wonderful. He was so accommodating, helpful and kind! The restaurant is very cool and the food was delicious. I would recommend going to dinner there if you are in London. The fresh Pea Soup was perfect!

title: What are you thinking?
text: This hotel could be good - unfortunately they staff it with people who are quite challenged. Simple requests become complicated and "complicated" requests belong in another hotel. On the positive, the location is great and facilities ok.

title: Comfortable designer hotel by Regent's Park
text: The York & Albany is a designer hotel with a good restaurant, both owned/run by the Gordon Ramsay franchise. The building is fantastically convenient on the north east corner of Regent's Park, close to Camden Town, and is a conversion of a small terrace of Georgian houses. The overall scheme is 'shabby chic', but it has been done exceptionally well, with as many of the period features of the buildings retained as possible, whilst at the same time delivering comfortable, air conditioned space. We found the bedroom a generous size, with a large four poster bed and a cute bathroom accessed by a little staircase. Dinner was excellent, and the staff were welcoming and friendly. A great little hotel for tourists, overnight business stays or like us just a family visit.

title: Hotel and Restaurant
text: Stayed overnight and ate in the restaurant, staff very pleasant and helpful, room very comfortable, food was well lovely and the service excellent. Would certainly return either on business or as a couple. A really nice place. Only 10 minutes from a Euston station and close to Regents Park.

title: Enjoyable but flawed
text: It's a great value proposition - a boutique hotel attached to a well-known (but fairly empty on a weekday evening in January) restaurant owned by a celeb chef. Stuff yourself and then cut out any inconvenience of having to go home by just climbing the stairs (or waiting for the very slow lift) and tumbling into bed. The rooms are well appointed, everything is new and good quality. Just don't expect a peaceful night in room 6 - it seems to be above the very noisy central heating system for the building, or something equally as noisy - which provides continuous low-level background noise. It wasn't a deal-breaker for me but did take a bit of getting used to. Other than that, it was a home from home, felt much more cosy than your usual soul-less hotel chain. A good find and I'm hoping to be back if the price is right. It's a bit off the beaten track as far as there's no Tube slap on the doorstep, but there is the 274 bus to Baker Street and you're not that far from Camden Town or Mornington Crescent tube stations. The wifi isn't that fast, but it's free.

title: Average but good ambience
text: We ate on a Sunday evening. The server was one of the worst I have encountered. Sullen and uninterested. As a coeliac I was pleased they could help me navigate the menu and the manager did that well. The food was average for all diners, not one of has was impressed. My main course was wrong but rectified quite quickly. For a Gordon Ramsey restaurant it was below expectations and overall quite expensive for an average meal. Unlikely to return.

title: Avoid if you are serious about steaks.
text: it's our 2nd visit to this restaurant. our first visit in 2009 filled us with warm memory of good food and nice ambience, so we popped in for a 2nd visit when we dropped by camden town. Upon arrival we found the set menu for lunch has been scraped, and replaced with a new a la carte menu. i expected to be told what today's special was, but the friendly waitress made no mention at all when we placed our orders. strange, i thought. marinated olives and almond was nice, and salt and pepper squids was crispy and tasty. those were the only highlight of the entire meal. starter i had chicken liver and foie gras parfait, which tasted only of chicken liver and with a texture of melted ice-cream. scary stuff. when my sir-loin arrived i couldn't believe what i saw. it was charred and the meat was very dry and grainy. i tried half of it and both i and my wife thought it was overdone (i ordered medium). i made my comment to the waitress but she was adamant it was medium when it arrived at the table. the chef sent us a free dessert to compensate, which was ok, but the damage has been done. we paid a premium for this lunch, but the quality of the food was only on par with any gastro-pub. incidentally, the table next to us made comments to the waitress about their fish being overdone. i looked around and noticed the restaurant was less than half filled (it was 2pm when we arrived), so i don't think the kitchen was too busy at that time. my fond memory of this restaurant from our 2009 visit was tarnished during this 2nd visit, and i would definitely not recommend this place to anyone.

title: Needs some tlc.
text: First impression of the room was good. However, the more i looked the more things i noticed that were not of the standard i would expect. The furniture is gorgeous, all antique style. But the lights in the wardrobe didn't work and one of the doors didn't shut properly. The bed was comfortable and the bedding was lovely. But there was no valance sheet covering the divan base. The rug was tatty and was a bit of a trip hazard. The plant in the room had dusty leaves. The bathroom wasn't cleaned to a high enough standard as there was grime on the tiles. The complimentary toiletries were lovely but the packet of cotton buds had already been opened and one was missing. The bath robes were rough and heavy. There was a tassimo machine in the room which needed descaling so we were unable to use it. This hotel is expensive and i was only able to stay here because of a special offer. Had I paid the full room rate i would have been very unhappy with the standards here.

title: Lovely stay
text: We stayed here for a night as a gift from our children. We opted to upgrade the room which meant we were in the room with the four poster bed. It was a lovely room with lots of charm, the bed was really comfortable although being only 5ft tall, I could have done with a step to get in and out of it! The standard of the room varied greatly, there was sky tv, ghd straighteners and hairdryer, luxurious toiletries, fluffy white robes and towels, plenty of space to store belongings. We were however disappointed that the maintenance let it down, there were stains on the carpet, scuff marks and dents in the walls, broken tiles in the bathroom and a real lack of electrical sockets, especially one to plug in the hair dryer in front of a mirror. That said it didn't detract from our enjoyment of the room and the staff were all delightful. We had a great night's sleep and would definitely stay here again.

title: Run down, shabby in need of refurb
text: The room we were given (Room 8) was run down and dirty, the furniture had scuffs and stains, every corner you turned there was something below expectation. We immediately complained to a nice American chap who apologised, but nothing more was done. Later on we requested an iron, which upon inspection had cracked and broken wires to which you could see the copper within. The air con did not work and the room was constantly stuffy and hot. The room we were given was a disgrace and the public area of the hotel and restaurant were run down. We were expecting a special evening away, unfortunately it didn't turn out that way!! Please consider spending you hard earned money elsewhere, you will be disappointed I promise you!!!

title: Chocolate cake not fondent
text: We came as a big group for a hen party. we were all dressed as Disney characters. Staff and service was impeccable. Our starters came quickly and were really scrummy. Next followed mains witch were also quick and delicious. We waited quite a while for our desserts, and some of us couldn't wait it cut in to our chocolate fondants and get a guey chocolate centre. They arrived and we were waiting in anticipation as we cut in to them, only to be disappointed massivly it was more like a school chocolate cake.

title: Chic hotel overlooking Regents Park
text: Overnight stay in London, York and Albany provided competitive rates for a lovely location. Popular dining spot providing a busy atmosphere but staff polite and prompt with their service. Room was clean and modern with all the necessary amenities, good breakfast menu in a relaxed atmosphere made it an enjoyable stay. Shall use again and recommend to others

title: Food tasty but service was poor
text: We ordered a starter to share and six main courses. After waiting a while we asked the waitress about the starter and she said quite abruptly it was just coming. Clearly she had forgotten as the main course arrived before we had finished the starter. She also took away the starter plates and had to bring them back when she brought the starter but didn't bring enough plates so we ended up sharing plates. The portion sizes were very uneven as one of our party had a lot less on her plate and there was hardly any gravy on two plates. They brought some extra carrots and gravy after we requested it but we were charged for the gravy which we objected to. Again the waitress was quite stroppy when my husband reduced the 12% service charge by a couple of pounds as a protest at being charged for a tiny pot of extra gravy. The food was tasty but the experiences was tainted by the surly service and attitude - wouldn't expect this from a Restaurant that Gordon Ramsay has put his name to.

title: Best Week in London!!!
text: My husband and I had a 3 week holiday in Europe and for our first week, we stayed here at the York and Albany. One word - FANTASTIC!!!!!! - from the moment we checked in, which was very early in the morning after a long flight from Australia, till the day our week there ended.. We were lucky enough to get a room upgrade to the Fantastic Townhouse, which had a great bed to collapse into each night, very spacious, warm and comfortable suite with plenty of room and storage so you can "unpack" and actually feel like you live there for the week. Love the glass roof sections with opening windows (totally private) and the luxury of the heated slate tile bathroom floor. It would have been nice to have a jug/kettle to make your own tea/coffee, but it was easy to have tea/coffee sent to your room. It has its own little deck area with an ashtray! which was fantastic if you are a smoker like me, nice and easy to nip in and out for a quick ciggie in privacy and without upsetting anyone! Every single staff member went out of their way to make sure we had a great time, and were friendly, attentive, and were a pleasure to meet and talk to each day. The restaurant was great, we ate there for four out of the six nights we stayed and the salt and pepper squid was tasty, tender and the BEST I have ever had. We sat outfront of the serving area on the red lounge one night and it was great to watch the kitchen staff in full swing. Each meal they put up looked fantastic, and to watch the finishing touches and fussing that went into each plate, made you appreciate the meal even more. A big thanks has to go to James the chef for our wonderful "packed lunch" he made for us on the day we were leaving to catch the train over to Paris. I loved the tall backed chairs in the bar area which we sat at each morning and enjoyed the Full English Breakfast with juice and coffee,which kept you full till lunch time. The location is great, near the park and a stroll to the camden markets and underground train station. Overall, we could not fault the York and Albany, I highly recommend it as a Hotel and as a Restaurant, we will definitely stay here again. It really was a highlight of our holiday, and it was so nice to have staff that actually CARE if you were enjoying your stay and making sure you did!! 100% thumbs up!!! Janet Wood - Wollongong - NSW - Australia

title: Through the Looking Glass
text: Stayed at the Hotel for one night. Had breakfast day before and after. It was an Alice in Wonderland experience, complex, sublime an occasionally absurd. The Hotel is lovely with much ambiance. The beds were very soft and cushy. I slept like a jet lagged infant despite a banquet party going on next door. The hotel is aged so we had issues with a broken toilet that was resolved in no time. The hot shower was a complicated procedure requiring instructions with later clarification of said instructions. (Thank you White Knight). The TV in our room 5 was not working at all. Alas not even the White Knight could fix it. The Hotel is in a solid location. Easy walk to crazy Camden Market. The York and Albany hotel is quirky, romantic and a tad overpriced. The bizarre restaurant experience however whisked us down the rabbit hole. I asked to sit at the two top table by the fire but was encouraged to sit by the window instead only later to be apologetically re-routed back to the fire side table due to a reservation confusion. On day one we ordered smashed avocado and salmon on toast, York forgot the Salmon. Day number two we ordered streaky Bacon and eggs. York forgot the bacon. It seemed as if everyone was in slow motion save for one French manager that was as busy as the March Hare. It took over 30 min and four separate orders to get our first cup of coffee. My daughter and I would place our order then watch the chess pieces that took it just walk off and start rolling silverware or stand at the hostess podium continually checking a laptop whilst attempting to look elegant and European. See if you can spot the Red Queen! Staff seemed happy to take our order however actually fetching it was apparently not part of their job description. Although totally unable to think outside of their personal boxes, York employees were super nice and happily messed up orders with a big smile. Most were good looking young foreigners that held a reasonably sturdy grasp of the English language. I can't help but wonder if the lack of communication is perhaps a guest worker thing? The coffee when and if it arrives is genuinely superb while the Panna cotta with pear compote is to die for. I suspect ones experience with the York and Albany Hotel and it's restaurant may waiver somewhere between hell and perfection. If you are bothered by little things best stay away. If you have a great sense of humor and are as adventurous as Alice then go for it!

title: Lovely room and lovely staff
text: Stayed one night on a Birthday Red Letter Day Voucher. All the staff were delightful, very helpful and keen to make ones visit special. We were upgraded to a deluxe room which was large, comfortable and with views towards Regents Park. It is a great location being just a few minutes walk from the underground (Northern line). Breakfast was very good with a good choice from the menu. What did let the Y and A down was the very mediocre set price menu. I think I expected a little more from a place headed by a 'Celebrity Chef ' than 'Soup of the Day' and 'Cottage Pie'. We opted instead for the a la carte menu and enjoyed the (very expensive) food. I suspect that most visitors do decide to take this option.

title: wouldn't stay again
text: we stayed on a thursday night. the meal was good, we only has pizza because we had been out for lunch. service was a little slow. the bed was the comfiest bed we had ever slept in. worst night sleep though, door beneath the room slamming closed every time someone went out continued til about 2am, staff putting out bottles, rubbish etc. also a hissing sound like a systern filling again til the early hours. such a shame lovely room, size , decor etc. breakfast was ok however not the best lincolnshire sausage! very draughty too, sat in the front windows looking across regents park, lovely location.

title: Wonderful Hotel
text: My wife and I stopped overnight 30th August. The room was very clean, lovely decor and the bed was one of the best I have ever slept in. The staff were excellent, every member of staff was attentive and always smiling. The food was excellent and again great service. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: What a lovely stay!
text: We stayed at York & Albany with my partner for couple nights last weekend. Hotel is very cozy and full of spirit. We had a deluxe room on a second floor with very comfortable king size bed. We really loved classic room style with modern equipment like hair straightener, coffee machine, Sky TV or bluetooth radio. Staff is very helpful and friendly, made us feel like at home. Great location, just few minutes away from Camden Town tube station. Definitely recommend and will came back again.

title: Amazing
text: Dear Joanna I am sat with my cup of coffee still going over what an amazing weekend we have had. We have stayed in many 5 star hotel around the world but this was one of the shortest stays with the biggest impact . My husband just mentioned to a member of your team it was our anniversary and you went out of your way to spoil us. I have to say that all the staff work so well together and you can see that your customers are the most important thing to each and everyone of your team. This is refreshing these days. Joanna made sure we were brought belinis to start celebrating once we checked in, when we arrived for our dinner reservation John the barman made a glass of champaign so special with his orange zest and flower petals. He took time to chat about his home in columbia but constantly checking to see if anyone needed serving such a lovely young man,who also makes the best g and t i have ever had! The food in the restaurant was not pretentious and plenty of it soooo lovely complimemts to the chef and his team. The end of our meal was so lovely when we were brought a special happy anniversary truffle platter omg done so tastefully thank you. Your head waiter was very complimentary and i do hope his wife likes his new perfume choice for her ha ha ha. Thank you again to the chef for my breakfast as i asked for something not on the menu and it was made perfectly. Our first visit to camden although we visit London 8 times a year or more, we will definately return to this hotel and camden. Dont change what you are doing you have it right. Joanna you are a fabulous manager right to the end making sure you said goodbye,

title: Helpful staff
text: Decent sized room, well appointed. Comfortable, with good A/C. Helpful staff. Although the kitchen doesn't open for breakfast before 07:00, but they'll do an earlier continental breakfast if you request it.

title: Friendly and charming
text: We organised my wife's 40th in the downstairs function room and stayed the night too. All of the staff were very friendly and professional and the hotel were eager to make sure we had a excellent time. We did. Thanks.

title: Enjoyable stay over Christmas
text: We arrived on Christmas Eve and checked into the suite for 2 nights, we got parked down the side street of hotel for free as it was Christmas, but I believe if we had booked at any other time we would have had some serious issues with parking as most of the streets nearby are resident permit only and the hotel has no parking at all which is quite poor. The manager of the hotel was very friendly when we checked in and showed us to our suite and was more than helpful with anything that we needed. The wifi in the room was good when it worked but was too intermittent. The suite was really nice and they added 3 beds for our children, even with this there was still loads of room, it was really spacious, the decor and furniture was lovely and the room was old fashioned yet modern. Our bed was big and was seriously comfortable, the tv was good sized and there was also a DVD player which was handy for the kids. There was a nice welcome note in the room and a plate of fresh fruit, cookies and water which was a nice touch. The bathroom is lovely and the shower is really good, the only downside is water escaped through a gap in the door and floods the bathroom floor which runs to a drain at the door but this slightly soaks the edge of the carpet, this wasn't a major issue our other slight concern was the room only had single pane windows so listening to the police helicopter on Christmas Eve wasn't nice and the cold breeze wasn't nice for my wife but me personally I enjoy sleeping in a nice cool room so it wasn't a problem for me, the children said their beds were nice and comfortable. Overall we really enjoyed staying in this room, I think it was well priced for this time of year. The breakfast in the bar area of the hotel was lovely, we enjoyed porridge, eggs Benedict with ham and scrambled eggs with salmon, the kids enjoyed their pancakes, the orange juice was really crisp and fresh. We eat in the restaurant Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, this was lovely and we have left separate reviews for this. Overall we would we stay again if we were in London.

title: Stylish Boutique Hotel in Perfect Location
text: The rooms in the hotel are gorgeous--traditional decor with modern touches. The bed is huge and we loved the wetroom in the bathroom. The hotel is attached to a great bar with amazing cocktails and a Gordon Ramsey resto. They offered us a table when we checked in which is impossible to get at the last minute on a Friday night. The location is excellent as well--just a two minute walk to Regents Park, Camden and Primrose Hill. A brief walk through Regents Park takes you into the city centre. My only complaint was that the bathroom didn't have a bathtub (room 8).

title: Very disappointing
text: We stayed one night as part of a wedding party and we were very disappointed with the quality of the service and of the amenities. The presence at Reception was patchy, we were given no instructions when we checked in (about check out time, breakfast, ....) and the hallway on the way to our room was strewn with workers' tools. It looked like a construction site. (We were given no apology for this.) The room was nice but the air con was not working (during a London heatwave) so we had to sleep with the windows open and we baked! Again, we were offered no apology. We were looking forward to breakfast and were quite disappointed to see there was a £5 supplement for anything other than granola and 1 SINGLE pastry (as the menu pointed out). The staff were also pretty inadequate unfortunately and I struggled to get through to them 2 days later when I called as I had left something behind. I spoke to someone at the restaurant who said there was no one available at receptions so 'could I call back later?'. Overall, it was a chaotic place, with poor management, poor customer care and inadequate amenities. A real disappointment! PS. I also know to now expect a generic 'We are sorry your stay did not match expectations' message, as per all the other complaint messages. This is also disappointing as you clearly don't take the complaints seriously.

title: Reasonable food but slow service
text: We ate here September 2015 Sunday lunch for two £90 including service Both of us had a starter and a main and a glass of wine The food was reasonable but not outstanding by any means. What was irritating was the service. The staff were pleasant but delivery was very slow. Food was slow to arrive but the drinks still only came at the end of the starters despite reminders ping the waitress. I ordered a second glass of wine, but if didn't come. Then they forgot our coffee order, so another wait. Luckily the bill arrived quickly! I think there is better food to be had with better service elsewhere.

title: We had a really good experience!
text: We stayed for 1 night at the Y & A and had a great time. The room was lovely, clean and really comfortable. The staff were really helpful and let us check in a few hours early because we had a wedding to get to. Would definitely recommend it.

title: Great taste but some improvements can be made
text: We had a dinner for two, we decided to try the combination menu and really liked the taste of the food and the wine. Nothing to complain about it, you can really notice that they've paid attention to it. The staf was friendly, but one of the waiters, might be the host, is really present in a "direct in your face way" which I found annoying... I don't know how to describe it better, but you'll know exactly what I mean when you visit the place. Furthermore there was some confusion about the menu caused by the waiter, the bill had some small errors and after paying it, they said bye, thanks, goodevening and left our table where they could also be more polite, help us with our jackets and walk us to the door. So summarized, food is great, service is not what Gordon wants it to be and can be improved ...

title: Super afternoon tea
text: Lovely afternoon tea. Food was yummy, particularly the mini desserts. Creme brûlée was delicious as was the moist brownie. A shame the server didn't tell the kitchen that we don't eat meat, however the ham sandwich was swiftly replaced. We received this as a wedding gift, so didn't pay for it. It did seem very expensive, but the food was beautifully flavoured and worth it if you're feeling flush!

title: Great service
text: The most efficient and professional service we've ever had , just walked into the restaurant recommended by our friend and been served by this amazing Brazilian waiter Tales ,who answered all our questions , we are amazed by place . We didn't plan to spend a lot but this casual night out turned into most romantic dinner so far ,great dinner, atmosphere , highly recommended , will be back and ask for the same service .👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻thumbs keep it up and Tales and your colleague Michael who was also supportive on arrival .

title: Overall very poor
text: Arrived at hotel and building defenately needs a lick of paint. Picture on internet is very misleading. Room very clean and beds are extremely comfortable. Considering it's a Gordon Ramsey restaurant, myself and my girlfriend had very high expectations for the quality of the food. We were highly disappointed. Food was oily and tasted worse than what you could get at your local wetherspoons. Food and drink way over-priced, two single rum and lemonade and what we thought was a free bottle of water for the table came to £23.50. So overall our £200 package was in our estimations worth about £70-£80 maximum. Staff were brilliant and very friendly. The breakfast was okay but again not what we expected. It's almost like the more you pay the worse the quality. I've stayed in hostels with more appeal than the York and Albany.

title: Excellent restaurant and service
text: I have visited here a number of times and the food here is of very high quality indeed with a constantly changing modern British menu in a lovely and well designed setting with beautiful lighting throughout. I read the last review from someone who made a comment about the bathroom - all I can say is that I do not share this impression whatsoever and have actually considered the opposite that the bathroom was in excellent condition. Although hard to select one aspect, the true star of this place has to be the service. Particularly notable for superb service has been Anthony, but actually everyone here at the York and Albany, from the bar staff to the kitchen is great and deserves congratulations for going out of their way to make coming here such an enjoyable experience.

title: What happens when a restauranteur moves into hotels.......
text: Stayed here for two nights on business so this is about the hotel and the restaurant in the evening. Food is ok though for someone so downright rude about food quality and standards, GR might want to start putting his own house in order before criticising others. Room was odd, it was outside (Room 4 - The Stables) and by the time you'd walked by the appalling 'Winter Chalet', the dirty walkway, the kegs and the grey fake snow, up the stairs I was hopeful for a reasonable room. In fairness the quality of the room itself was ok but had the smallest double bed I've seen in a while (I'm over 6ft so if there was two of you, it would be very cosy) and one of the most bonkers bathroom arrangements. No bath but a very good sized shower which leaked incessantly through the bottom of the door as the shower floor didn't slope towards the drain? No ventilation meant there was a stale musty smell in the bathroom and the window didn't operate using the control. Wifi was abysmal in Room 4 and kept falling off but assumed that was because it was so far from the main building. In keeping with one of the other guests who has posted here, there is a really irritating mechanical noise which kicks in at 5am and I think is either the kitchen fan/air con/heating or a mechanical digger but I think its the former. I travel a lot and had hoped to have a slightly different experience than the usual business hotels which can be rather anodyne and boring. This was prohibitively expensive, the staff were helpful but badly trained and quirky so you'd better like back chat with your order which I don't mind. The only high points were Michal (I think that was his name) and the venison which was lovely. I can't work out if you arrive thinking because its got his name on it, you are in for a reasonable experience or whether you think the price will see to that (£300+ a night)

title: Gordon Ramsay might need to visit
text: While to food was quite good, I was a little shocked by the condition of the place--specifically the bathroom. The sink was very water damaged and looked terrible. According to his shows, I'm surprised this is allowed in a place that bears his name. That aside, however, the food was quite delicious. The steak was extremely tender and cooked perfectly and the Anna potatoes were scrumptios. The coffee selection was amazing and the Columbian selection took me back to my days in Armenia. Would definitely visit again.

title: Intimate Luxury
text: I found this Gordon Ramsay owned hotel via Mr & Mrs Smith, who Hand-pick the best boutique hotels and luxury hotels to ensure one can find the perfect romantic getaway. And what a pick this was.Superbly located to get to the West end, right next to Regents Park and walking distance from the bustling Camden Market. Described as a Town house - I would suggest converted pub. - The ambience is relaxed, yet refined - with a high level of service. I stayed in a Deluxe Room - with a 4 poster bed! The only thing to say about this room is 'WOW', but it is not an idea to stay in this room, if you intend to have too much to drink, or if you have mobility issues as there is a number of steps down to the bathroom and a step up into the bath/shower. Yummy thick cotton bathrobes, luxurious toiletries, even nail file. Wonderful touches, such as a map showing you a number of jogging circuits round Regents park in the Welcome pack are really thoughtful. Free welll working WiFi - however if you wish an Ipod dock in your room you need to request this - understandable, as some guests seem to have thought that they are there to be taken with them. I was spending the evening out (attending the European Hospitality awards) - and was pleasently suprised to return to my room with the curtains closed, soft lighting on and a card on the bed telling me what the weather was supposed to do the following day.

title: Great service, great restaurant
text: Wonderful. We stayed there for 5 nights, and had three dinners at the restaurant...that was in addition to breakfast every day. The location was great for us, close to Regents College/park, and close to St. John's. It is a short walk to Camden market. The staff was wonderful, in particular Lucy at the front desk, and the host of the restaurant. On a Saturday night, we made a last minute decision to have dinner at the York and Albany. Amazingly, the restaurant made it work, since we were hotel guests. The banquet room looks like the perfect place for entertaining a group of ~20. We stayed in room #1, which was a tad modern, and in need of sprucing up. Good news. The room is scheduled for renovation in June, 2012. We will certainly stay there again.

title: Really good team meal
text: A really good "high end" gastropub with a very reasonable wine list and great service and atmosphere. Couldn't complain about any of it. I'm a fan of the Ramsay chain and love Maze Grill. If you like honest, smart but not pretentious food of a real quality then this is a winner. Will go back with family and friends.

title: Not bad at all
text: I was brought a red letter day gift for this hotel & having read all the bad reviews on Tripadvisor I was more than a little apprehensive...... I needn't have been! I think the other reviews on here are a little harsh! We arrived early on a Saturday to drop our bags we were immediately greeted by a very nice receptionist who stored our bag for us and we went off to enjoy a day in the city. Upon our return we checked in and our bag had already been put in our room. We were in room 7 which was very nice, a little small but all you need for an overnight stay! It was clean and comfortable, my only slight quibble is that there was a tassimo with plenty of coffee pods but no tea bags! Not so great for a tea lover!! There was a little street noise but not enough to keep us awake and it's to be expected in London. We had dinner in the restaurant and chose from the set menu, the food was very nice although the service was a little slow. We also had breakfast the following day, in the cold light of day the restaurant was a little tatty, ripped curtains and dusty light shades and again the service was slow, which would have been infinity less frustrating if there had been some Sunday papers to peruse! I do feel that this place could be improved with very little effort but it is fine as it is. I think that because Gordon Ramseys name is associated with York & Albany some people expect it to be Michelin starred which it isn't, it is a gastro pub (a very nice one at that!)!

title: Managed to completely ruin my entire wedding lunch.
text: I can honestly say that I am very happy for the past reviewer who had a great day / meal in the Regency Room... Unfortunately ours was the polar opposite... From beginning to end an absolute disgrace. As it was only yesterday, I am too upset to write what happened in full detail now, but will return later to do so. If you want snarls from staff, meals taking over an hour to arrive, meals served while half the guests are not at the table, mains served at different times (by 30 mins), guests having to leave before dessert (3 hours after starting the meal).. and having to make apologies to all your guests for the whole balls up, just to begin with - you have found your spot.

title: The Y&A breakfast may have spoiled me for all future hotel stays....
text: Highly recommend this hotel. First of all, the breakfast. The phrase "Have breakfast like a king and dinner like a pauper" springs to mind. Thankfully breakfast was included in our price but even if it's extra, you should treat yourself. Everything about it was fabulous and delicious and the surroundings (the bar/lounge) were beautiful too. We didn't eat anything in the York and Albany apart from breakfast (we hardly were hungry enough to eat any other meals anyway!) but the standard of the breakfast menu is certainly what you would expect from a first-rate eaterie. The location of the York and Albany is also excellent. We used Camden tube station but Regents Park, the zoo and the tranquility of Primrose Hill are also on your doorstep. The room itself was gorgeous - no tea/coffee making facilities (all the more reason to get yourself down to that amazing breakfast!) but there was sparkling and still water. Great bed linen, towels and robes. Very good shower. The cleaning lady was helpful and efficient. Likewise for the rest of the staff who were all more than happy to help and make us feel welcome. Most people aren't going to come to London to stay in their hotel but it's still a treat to stay somewhere like this.

title: Attention to detail?
text: Stayed didn't have a chance to eat. Comfortable bed. Pleasant room but at over £200 a night I wouldn't have expected lights out in the bedroom and bathroom. Also problem with coffee machine. Very noisy kitchen extractor under room 6 switched on very early. Public areas looking tired. Continental breakfast a little mean. Croissant cold and raw in the middle. Overall falls a little short.

title: Great Gordon Ramsay restaurant
text: We had a great experience at Gordon's Regent's Park adjacent restaurant. Although fairly empty at 7:30 mid-week, it filled up very quickly. The menu is small but we found the best option in the cote de boeuf for 2 which was amazing. It is served beautifully, on a large wooden board, beef perfectly cooked and cut with the side dishes also placed on the board. Wine list was good and our waitress was knowledgeable enough to help us choose. We were underwhelmed by the dessert options but were too full anyhow. On our way out, we glanced over at the gorgeous bar area and were then drawn to it for another drink. The bartender was so great and really into his job so he expertly made me a cocktail off the menu and made the most precise 'old fashioned' for my hubby. It was a perfect post-dinner experience. Can't wait to go back next time we are in London.

title: Amazing stay and delicious food!
text: Unfortunately I only stayed one night but will definitely be back the next time we're in London. The room was small but very comfortable. The best bed and pillows in the world! As for the restaurant, we net this lovely Italian waiter that explained the menu to us, suggested a few nibbles and drinks and made us feel very comfortable. Well done to all! We hope to return very soon.

title: Not as good I expected......
text: I spent a weekend in London with my wife for a wedding and one of the options was York & Albany Unfortunately I was a bit disappointed.... The room was fairly comfortable with nice furniture but......A/C was not working and being on the top floor it was pretty warm (we were told no maintenance until Monday), two lights in the bathroom were not working and even if we requested no one came to fix them. The room was a bit "beat up" The only good note was the breakfast included in the rate and very good!

title: A special Night in London
text: I had selected this place as it appeared to be something special. I had read a few reviews and was prepared for a few little things but generally thought it might suit us well. We needed to be in Camden for a meeting during the day and loved shopping in the market so location was ideal. I booked the suite even after reading the review which described it as a waste of money. That reviewer is correct you do have to walk to it around the back of the hotel past the kitchen entrance and the empty beer barrels but once up the outside stairs and into the room it is a real secret hideaway. You sit up above the rest of London in your loft space hidden away a perfect romantic location. It is beautifully furnished and full of a different sort of charm, fits well into the Camden vibe. A few grumbles, the room had not been cleaned very well before our stay, whilst trying to get the desk lamp to work, which I was not able to do, I was searching around on the floor and found what I at first thought to be an empty condom packet but my female companion assured me was an empty sachet of a special hair product. Stepping into the shower without my glasses on I stood on something sharp, that turned out to be a clear plastic gum shield. The bathroom is merely adequate which for us was not really a problem but with the room being so special you do kind of want it to tick a few more boxes. They are hardly generous with their showerstuff we soon ran out, perhaps our fault it had turned into that sort of experience we needed several showers each. A quick comment on the restaurant. Had booked a table but when we went down it was full and only table they had was so low and the chairs so big and comfy we sank into them so ended up eating our food on our laps. Which kind of spoilt the food, eating a full sunday roast turned into a real challenge. So sadly cant really recommend. Breakfast was fine and served at decent table but felt a little cheated being asked to pay an extra fiver for the cooked breakfast felt they could have put that in with the room rate. For the whole package and experience good value for money, would I stay again maybe

title: Very disappointed
text: I went to the York and Albany for a Sunday roast, which was very nice but that was about the only nice thing I can say. The person I was with asked for well done beef and the waiter said are you sure and started saying it would be horrible and started banging on the table. All of the waiting staff could hardly talk English and was very hard for them to understand my friend has a very bad nut allergy. The worst part was the dessert! The sticky toffee was bad I've had a better dessert from wetherspoons, the waiter went to check if it had nuts in for my friend and came back to say on the packet it does say nuts. Sorry PACKET sticky toffee! Would never go back, such a shame that Ramsays standards have gone so low

title: Fantastic Sunday roast
text: Lovely service and ambience. This was probably the best roast I've had in London, the horseradish butter was a delicious accompaniment. Definitely worth the money! I would highly recommend it. The squid starter was outstanding and cooked perfectly.

title: Gordon - top notch
text: Booked a two night break via voyage Privee - excellent hotel with exceptional service - check in restaurant staff stand out Had dinner from a la carte menu - very busy in the restaurant but food and service excellent throughout - Wine Sommelier in depth knowledge and spent some time recommending lovely wines to suit our budgets Great vibe - very cool - must return some time soon

title: A family Wedding
text: We had a wonderful family wedding at the York and Albany in London this weekend. The staff all worked so hard. They were kind, friendly and professional and nothing was ever too much trouble. The wedding meal was fantastic, small courses which were all delicious. The children were taken off to make their own pizzas in the kitchen. This was a fabulous venue for a wedding because of the quality of all the staff working together. Many thanks for a lovely occasion.

title: Excellent hotel
text: Definitely we will come back here in the future. The location for us is perfect because our daughter lives in Herne Hill. Very good transport to get into London centre. The next stay for us will be in summer 2018 and we are already looking forward.

title: Wonderful find...
text: Great hotel... love the building and the way it has been renovated keeping the original but updating by leaving bare floor boards and rustic bits with interesting colours and textures. Really clean , comfy bed and good breakfast- (just a slight bit off for that). The staff was really friendly and the neighbourhood where the hotel is, is out of rush and bustle of the more tourist areas and is residential- just a bit noisy though. We will stay again, as it is a short trip by train to any of the London attractions. And the price for a London hotel is really reasonable. Overall, highly recommended!

title: Brilliant stay at the Half Moon Hotel
text: Excellent stay for 2 nights in preparation for a wedding. It was very comfortable and when I realised I'd left my purse at the hotel the following day, the staff couldn't have been more helpful and we succeeded in finding it!

title: Nice rooms and good service
text: The room was nice but just near the station, you could hear the trains and traffic. A little far from the city of London. But good if you want to stay in a more green environment. Bus and train to the city was easy.

title: Great rooms with an interesting theme!
text: Stayed in this “pub with rooms” this week. Very pleasantly surprised by the quality and size of the rooms. It is a busy pub with a great atmosphere. We didn’t eat here so can’t comment on the meals, but if you want a decent room you should consider this place. Very nicely themed too. 2 minutes walk to Herne Hill train station. We would definitely stay again.

title: Half Moon Heaven
text: We initially chose the hotel based on its location. The staff were very welcoming and room was clean. Breakfast was exceptional!! Our server was helpful and made sure we were comfortable, unrushed and well fed.

title: Great location and comfort
text: Our third visit. The hotel is perfectly located for visiting our family in Norwood and Kennington. Also it is so easy to reach from Kings Cross - about 15 to 20 minutes on the overground train from Herne Hill. Couldn’t be better. Enjoy having the family to dinner there too. The food is great. The chef Michael was really helpful and served me with a fantastic flat iron steak. Everybody enjoyed their meal. The beds are brilliant and the linen is top quality. We had a room at the back (Conrad) which had a much bigger bathroom than our previous rooms and with a window. The lighting is hopeless for putting on makeup, but the bedside lights in this room were good. Annemarie who welcomed us again is great news. The young breakfast waitresses clearly haven’t been remotely trained but they are all quite pleasant. The eggs Benedict are fantastic, as were all our breakfast choices. Can’t wait to return for our fourth visit.

title: Not coming back
text: This is our third visit but sadly we won't be returning. The Sunday lunch we had in April was excellent but have since been back with friends in May and again last week to give it a second go, as in May they were very busy. Frankly, if they can't get fish and chips and burger and chips right then there's not a lot of hope, not least the chips aren't right! The fish is ungenerous, battered cod looks great but if the fish inside is mean it's very disappointing it should be thick and flaky. Six of us (out of seven) ordered it and all were disappointed. It's such a shame, as it's a great location and we were so pleased when it reopened after the flood.

title: Family wedding party
text: We were very comfortable here when a big group of us stayed here for 2 nights. The rooms were quiet despite facing the street and extremely comfortable. My daughter was very happy with the suite which was big enough for the bridal preparations on the morning of the wedding - quite something as she had 7 bridesmaids! I would happily recommend the rooms and pleasant bars downstairs.

title: Heading for stardom
text: I was privileged, along with my wife and friends, to attend the soft opening of the now Fullers Brewery owned, much anticipated, Half Moon's new restaurant today, following 3 years of refurbishment. 10/10 for décor and ambience – they have really done a good job on that. 8/10 for food on the Sunday roast menu: the starters all got top marks, particularly the carpaccio of venison

title: Delish!
text: We have been on a number of occasions to enjoy the old pub with great history. Having recently been for dinner again, after initially popping in when it first opened, we weren't disappointed. They're clearly after consistently good food which is a bonus. Service can sometimes take some time but I think that's been sorted out since we initially went in. Excellent to have another good pub to go to locally.

title: Great!
text: (I'm from Holland, sorry for my English) We really enjoyed our staying in The Half Moon. We really liked the style of the pub, restaurant and hotel with a lot eye for detail. Our room (Duke) was small, but it gave us a warm feeling and there was everything that we needed. The staff was warm and breakfast was good. Also there was a nice place outside to sit in the sun with our breakfast and with a glass of wine in the evening. We would recomment it tot everyone :)

title: Friendly staff
text: I stayed at the the Half Moon hotel for 4 nights. I haven't met more friendly staff before. You feel really welcome in there. I loved the decoration of the room and how clean it is. The location is also great. it is at the centre of the town. It is very close to the park, the station, the supermarket, and to a number of resturants. The hotel however, doesn't have an elevator and in order to go to your room you have to go through the pub. It was awkword as I had kids with me. every time I entered the pub people starts staring :)

title: Good but several teething problems
text: The bed was really comfortable. Be prepared for no privacy from the street outside. Lovely big windows open onto the street. You have to keep the curtains open in the morning as the bedroom lights are as good as non-existent! The food, breakfast and dinner, was excellent. There was a feeling of nobody being in charge which was somewhat disconcerting. Loads of friendly staff, but there didn't appear to have been much training and certainly no management. We would go again definitely, in the hope that some of their teething troubles have been rectified and that there might be a good manager in situ.

title: It’s a Full Moon by all means
text: Pub food, very well cooked, not oily, large, huge portions. We had fish and chips and nioki pasta along with draught beers. For desserts I had the brownie cake with vanilla ice cream. The service was very fast Although Saturday night the staff was very kind and eager to assist. Thank you Sofia, you are such a gem. Looking forward for the next time

title: Great experience at the New Half Moon last Sunday
text: We had an impromptu trip to the New Half Moon pub ( Fullers House ) last Sunday and found it to be a great experience. The waiting staff were very attentive and there's a great choice of Ales.. would definitely recommend for a traditional Sunday roast.

title: Half Moon
text: The front rooms are noisy so ask for rooms towards the back of the hotel. Staff very accommodating and helpful. Management and Ann Marie were particularly great ! If you want to experience a London Pub with great rooms and friendly staff this is the place for you.

title: Perfect experience
text: Everything about this place was brilliant. The decor, ambiance and staff made for a wonderful stay. The room was individually beautiful and well equipped. A giant, comfortable bed provided a great night's sleep. Breakfast was delightful. We shall be returning!

title: A Brilliant Weekend in London
text: We chose the Half Moon as the venue for our son's naming ceremony, as it was a stone's throw from my best friend's house and she recommended the workshop private space. From the word go the staff were very communicative and helpful, and on the day they made sure everything was set up just as we wanted. Our bar man was charming and the event went without a hitch despite the guest of honour arriving late thanks to London traffic! Afterwards we went into the bar with a group of friends and family, and some time later when we decided we wanted to eat we were accommodated with a table for ten despite it being Saturday night and us not having made a booking. On Sunday we had a gorgeous cooked breakfast and in the evening had a shared roast in the restaurant which was just delicious, and the perfect way to end the weekend. Our room (Irwin) was delightful and perfect for us and our son, especially as it was a bit further away from the other rooms. The staff were helpful and courteous, we really felt well looked after all weekend. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend and will be back!

title: Had a great time!!
