You're bound to end up with a rather chaotic arrangement of your personal items even if you've only packed for a weekend, and chaos within a rather confined space is even worse. the room looks very lovely and stylish but has more disadvantages: the window, as others have mentioned, lets in loads of noise from the road. the blinds do not keep out the light. after two days, a "sleep kit" randomly showed up on one of our night tables (only ONE for two people, mind you), containing an eye mask and ear plugs. lucky we had both brought these items with us anyway. seriously, if you're going to invest in revamping a victorian building to turn it into a stylish hotel, the windows should be your first concern. the bed was small (yes, it is technically a king size in UK measurements), about 152 cm. on to the bathroom: the shower has no handheld otion, water only from above. which makes it more difficult to get clean - especially in the (yes, again) rather confined space of the bathroom. hardly any space on the tiny shelf over the sink. if you bring more than a tooth brush (e.g. face soap, face tonic, face cream, mouth wash....) you better bring it in tiny sample sized bottles. the pantries on every floor, even though i loved them (great taps for filtered or boiling water), offer no milk, cream or even coffee whitener ("milk is available in the lounge"). for the room rate, even though it is on the inexpensive side for london, these are still heavy disadvantages. for very little more we can get a room at indigo in the same street if we book early. the single best thing about the room was the marshall bluetooth speaker. playing your favourite music lets you forget momentarily that you have been fooled by what looked like an extremely cool new hotel concept but is really designed for instagram only.

title: Noisy, disorganised and pricey. A triumph of form over function, but close to the station.
text: The addition of some magazines in the room and a rather good blue-tooth speaker did not alter the fact that the room had a single-glazed window onto the street, where pubs had outside crowds until late. St Mary's Hospital is close-by and it's the major trauma centre for west London, cue: ambulance sirens at several points during the night. The blinds did not keep out the light from the street during the night. £199 in order to wear a blindfold and earplugs (provided in the room by the hotel). Really? Our £199 did not include breakfast, which was just as well, because no table was available! After waiting 15 minutes, we went to the nearby Garfunkel's in Praed Street and got a reasonable breakfast. Avoid.

title: Got to be the smallest room I have ever stayed in
text: Totally ridiculous. Takes small to whole other level. One suitcase in the bathroom, two at the bedroom door. God help us if there is a fire, we will never get out. Forget this place. Impossible to unpack a bag, no hanging room. Took my money months ago as soon as I booked. Very disappointed

title: Stylish
text: Really enjoyed our stay - loved the style of this hotel, mix of modern and old/quirky - very well done. All the fittings, bedding, shower etc of v good quality. Great location. The breakfast was good, cooked options but also a nice simple but more than adequate continental offer too. Staff friendly and helpful. Only downside is even though we booked a larger room the rooms are small and there are no drawers for clothes and limited hanging space so more suitable for a weekend rather than a longer stay. Also can be a bit noisy at night as central London and maybe windows not well insulated.

title: Great location, lovely hotel.
text: Just a minute from Paddington station, this hotel has great style and ambience. The bar/cafe area is great- lovely bruschetta snack and a drink. Our room was small but the well thought out design made great use of the space and made for a comfortable stay 👍🏼😃

title: It should be good, tries hard, but fails badly in places
text: The hotel looks good. You walk through the door and there's a small Workshop cafe in reception and you're given your key to the room almost immediately. We had the Large room which we expected a full and spacious bathroom. How wrong could we have been. Tiny. The sink was in the bedroom, too. Barely any wardrobe space and the room was warm, in September, even with the window open. However, the biggest issue with the underground noise and parts of the room shaking whenever a train went underneath the hotel. Incredible. Starts up again early in the morning. On checking out - despite asking for a quiet room when checking in - the receptionist told us that room M12 was notorious for underground noise! Breakfast was basic. You pay £10 and receive a continental choice, which is bread, croissants and some cheese, hams and cereal. It's cheaper and easier to walk 100m to the McDonald's around the corner or Garfunkel's. Better breakfast, too. The bed is decent, staff friendly and the hotel looks pretty good, but it's also small, too. With no aircon in the rooms, I'd dread to stay there in mid-summer.

title: Good news & bad news
text: The good news: The Pilgrm is very close to Paddington Station, where you can catch the Heathrow Express to the airport. Very convenient location. The bed was very comfortable and the linens were lovely. The staff was very friendly. The cost for a one night stay will not break the bank. The bad news: The Pilgrm is very close to Paddington Station, so people are coming and going all night. The room and bathroom were really small. Noise is the biggest issue in this hotel, both from outside the windows and from inside the building. Lots of pubs nearby and on a Saturday night it was pretty rowdy out on the street. Windows are not double-paned, so street noise will keep you awake. Within the hotel, there are lots of rooms, stairwells, and corridors, so doors are slamming all night. The walls between rooms seem thin-- we heard our neighbors talking loudly in their room after the pubs closed. Bottom line, if a good night's sleep is important to you, then this hotel is not a good value.

title: Lovely hotel but some improvements needed
text: Firstly let me focus on the positives. The hotel itself is lovely and has been done to a good standard and the staff are really friendly and helpful and a credit to the hotel. Now the unfortunate negatives. It was possibly one of the worst nights sleep I have had in a hotel. I was in room Y42 facing onto the busy main road and the window in this room was not fit for purpose. It provided absolutely no sound proofing from the noise outside, my bed may as well have been on the street. It was a wooden framed single paned sash window. In contrast my parents room, which was at the back of the building away from the noise, had a proper double glazed window. My next issue would be the fact that I paid for two large rooms and I'm not convinced that the second room I was given was a large. I was told that it was, it was just a smaller large than mine, however the website states that the large rooms have a chair in them and the second room I booked definitely did not, which makes me think it was possibly a medium. My only other negative is that the following day I had no hot water in my room due to a plumbing problem - that said the hotel compensated me for it and had I asked, they would have provided me with another room to shower in. Had I not been in the room I had, this would have likely been a 4/5 star review. I would definitely consider staying again, but only if the window issue was rectified.

title: Great Hotel in good location
text: We stayed at the Pilgrm Hotel for three nights and booked a large room which was a decent size . The bed was very comfortable with lovely clean and soft bedding. They do not have tea/coffee facilities in the rooms but there is a pantry on each floor which provides an endless supply of good quality teas and coffees with fresh milk in the fridge. The staff were friendly and polite and the check-in was easy and relaxed. We tried the Continental breakfast twice and its was excellent. Fresh yoghurt, fruit, delicious pastries, sour dough bread and a nice selection of cheeses. All the food was of a high quality. the coffee was excellent as well. We really enjoyed our stay there and would not hesitate to book it again. We frequently visit London to catch up with our daughter who lives in Australia and has business trips twice a year. It was good to find a hotel in London that is a bit different to the average, reasonably priced and a pleasure to stay in. Well done Pilgrm. We loved the quirkiness of the building as well!!

title: Convenient & stylish, but some compromises
text: This hotel is a convenient location for tube and train travel, being next to Paddington station, however the area itself isn't great. The decor is nice, apart from the faux distressed carpet. The layout of the hotel is pretty confusing. The lounge is lovely, with attentive staff and an interesting menu. The rooms are very very small, the shower wasn't warm enough and the single glazing isn't great for cold or noise. For one night it was fine, but the lack of space would deter me from staying any longer, despite the central location.

title: Lovely staff, small rooms, good overall
text: Had a 3 day stay at the Pilgrm (no typo). The staff could not have been more friendly and helpful. We had a “medium sized” room, filled by the bed. This wasn’t a big issue, nor was the ‘white noise’ that Paddington generates 20 hours a day, once you got used to it. Very convenient for Paddington and the tube - advise you book through the hotel

title: Comfortable Trendy Hotel a stones throw from Paddington
text: The Pilgrm is in a great position right next to Paddington Station. I stayed here at the weekend as I was going to Proms in the Park, only a 10 min walk from Hyde Park. The rooms are great and comfortable although a little compact, but what else do you need for a few nights in London. The rooms don't have tea or coffee making facilities but there is a pantry on each floor with tea and coffee making facilities in here which is great. Fan in the bedroom was needed, I was in a room facing the street and I am a light sleeper and managed a good nights sleep....the bed and pillows were so comfortable. The lift is small and it is a rabbit warren of corridors and wings and stairs but its great accommodation at a great price. Breakfast was really great too and the coffee they serve is among the best I have tasted. Would recommend and would stay here again

title: Amazing concept
text: A newly refurbished hotel with a remarkable decor and concept! Stayed here a couple of times when it was called the royal norfolk so I am able to compare both properties! Located next to the paddington station is always a perfect location especially if you are traveling to heathrow. The staff here are also very warm and friendly. Special thanks to the manager Eleni and her staff member Szsannna for assisting me with a minor issue I had with my flights. The beds. This is one of the most comfy beds I have ever slept on. The room itself was very clean so thanks to the housekeeping team for doing such a great job. The restaurant

title: very disappointed
text: I did not like this hotel. The rooms are tiny (even the large ones) , hot and very noisy at night. The windows cannot open for air circulation ( there is no aircon or air filtering system). The check in was casual , slow and unprofessional. The breakfast was the only nice part.\ of the stay.

title: Boutique hotel that is very clean and cozy. Great stay.
text: This is a small hotel without the usual reception desk and concierge services of the large hotels. It is extremely clean without any smell of cleaning fluids. The elevator is tiny but we simply made 2 trips instead of one. The small staff is very pleasant and helpful so we really felt welcomed. It is conveniently located with a coffee shop on location. There are various dining options right on the block or around the corner. Transportation is just several yards away.

title: Not worth the price
text: I stayed at the Pilgrm with a friend in one of the bunk bed rooms which is tiny, like very tiny. No space to move around or keep your suitcases. The location is good and the staff friendly but for this price you can definitely find a better option.

title: Everything you need. Nothing you don't.
text: This quaint hotel was just what I needed for a single room. Small but so comfortable and very friendly staff. Don't be put off that there is no formal reception area--rest assured there is someone available 24/7. Some rooms have vintage hand pull toilet flush and others more modern 'small' of 'large' flush options. Lots of stairs and intricate passageways but still worth the money for clean quarters and helpful staff. Highly recommend.

title: Convenient, clean, and friendly staff.
text: Stayed in the Pilgrim for two nights. Very convenient location off of Paddington Station. Walking distance to lots of pub (I recommend Sawyer's Arms). Staff was friendly and welcoming (at all hours). The facilities are chic and the decor is amazing! We had two rooms, one with bunk bed and the other a double. The bunk bed room was tiny, but clean and had everything needed.The double room was roomy and comfortable. No A/C on premises, but rooms do have a fan. Rooms also have a Bluetooth speaker, USB plugs, reading lamps, stationary, and REN skincare products. Cleaning staff also kindly folded my clothes nicely while cleaning (sorry for the mess!). Elevator is tiny, can fit two people with two roller bags. There is a pantry on the third floor where you can get hot water, tea, and coffee. Bonus: free water foundation (still and sparkling) on ground floor was a godsend!! Regrettably, we were not able to use the cafe on-site but the prices looked fair and the seating area in the second floor was very cute. The only real downside to the place is that the bunk bed rooms are extraordinarily tiny. Would definitely stay there again.

title: Quite ghastly one to forget
text: A really poor experience which left me feeling pretty sad about life and the lack of value one so often finds in London. The room was tiny, smelly and noisy and lacked any redeeming features. After a really poor night's sleep I politely and quietly mentioned that I didn't want to stay for the second night of my booking as would prefer to actually sleep. They said they would refund my second night, they didn't, I chased them up, still no refund. Super poor value, one to swerve.

title: Super Cute
text: I didn't have a lot of preconceived notions before coming to The Pilgrim but the little hotel really surpassed any expectations. The only issue I had was arriving the address from the website didn't show up on the cab drivers GPS so we had a little trouble finding it but once I arrived it was smooth sailing. There isn't a formal reception, its very causal in the entrance is a lounge chill space with a coffee bar. My room was on the top floor a crossed a "bridge" which sounds complicated but in reality was pretty cool. My room itself was pretty small but that's the hotels whole concept, so as expected. Everything was stylishly designed and impeccably clean. Finally, I opt'd to get the breakfast included which was huge/impressive/delicious. Overall I would definitely recommend staying at the Pilgrim, just don't bring more than one suitcase

title: Lovely hotel with a personal touch!
text: This hotel was a charming little gem in busy Paddington. My wife and I booked a large room for an overnight stay and we were impressed by the service from the moment we walked in. Check in was quick and easy and the young lady who helped us was very polite and informative. The Pilgrm is quite a quirky hotel with a nice cafe on the ground floor offering free bottles of water as soon as you arrive. The first floor has a lovely lounge where you can eat and drink in a wonderfully relaxed atmosphere. Our room was very comfortable, spotless and spacious. The bathroom and shower in particular were of a very high standard. The retro bluetooth speaker in the room was also a lovely touch. The bed was a lovely size and extremely comfortable. Before going out for dinner that evening we stopped in the lounge for a couple of drinks, again the staff were very friendly and service was quick and prices were very reasonable. Breakfast the next morning was lovely, you could help yourself to juices and pastries at the bar and there was a lovely menu with lots to chose from for your main breakfast. All in all I would highly recommend the Pilgrm and would most certainly stay there again.Its nice to see hotels pay attention to detail and I would always prefer to stay in hotels such as the Pilgrm as opposed to the larger chains. Thanks so much for a lovely stay, we will definitely be visiting again soon.

title: Boutique Feel
text: 100m or so from Paddington this is a find. Staff are excellent, decor modern and a little qwerky and there some really nice touches. I especially liked the fizzy water on tap in the foyer! The small rooms are really small which I actually liked - but it won't be to everyone's taste. There's no air-con, but fans are provided. The bathroom was clean and well done. My shower provided a lovely blast of hot water. Breakfast was a treat: great service, fresh ingredients and real leaf tea in a pot! If you need to be able to cope with stairs - there are alot of them, though there is a lift to get you most of the way up to your room. Nothing in London is cheap but comparatively, this is good value and recommended if you like something different from the big hotel chain.

title: Hip, but Tiny and Noisy
text: Sure this hotel has great looking stylishly furbished interiors and rates top marks for cleanliness, but the rooms are teeny tiny. You could not swing the proverbial cat in my room. I was solo - attending a conference - and I felt cramped. If two people were sharing, with only minimal luggage, it would be uncomfortably constricting. Access is also problematic. The lift is very small - at most it would fit two people with baggage - and does not go to the upper floor. My room was situated some distance from the lift and to get to the wing where my room was I also had to climb stairs, cross an external metal grid, then shuffle down a very, very narrow warren-like passageway. During my stay here I was anxious about how I would get out if there was a fire. Probably best to be aware that wall insulation is minimal, and you can hear other occupants coming and going and opening and closing the doors to their room. As well, you can hear when they use the shower and tap water. Worse though was the street noise and lights. In my room the (single) window was not double-glazed and I could not close it all the way. The first night the nocturnal revellers seemed to be up all night - my room faced onto a lovely tree in a small park with the streets facing onto it lined with restaurants, shops, pubs... so I had an unpleasant night not being able to settle into sleep. In addition, the roller blind did not effectively block the light: at night allowing the street lights in and in the morning the sunlight, so no chance of a sleep-in. London was beautifully sunny during my visit. I was unimpressed with the situation because when I made the reservation online and then again at check-in I specifically requested a quiet room. Things did not improve on the second night, so sleep-deprived and grumpy I complained. The woman on duty was apologetic and efficiently organised my move to another room. She also had someone help move my suitcase. Happy to report that I had a quiet third night, and by positioning the extra pillows and bedding against the window blocked out the light so as not to be woken at the crack of dawn.

title: small but perfectly formed, quality fittings and very handy location for Paddington
text: What a lovely place and so close to Paddington station. Grotty area of Paddington however this is a shining gem. Whilst the room is small, its homely and cosy. Super staff, quality fittings, free Ren products. Great shower, spotless and v comfy bed. Very stylish common areas. Highly recommended!

title: Spot on!!
text: Wanted nice hotel, not a large chain, near Paddington. This is a real gem and find which I loved and will return!! Brilliant location 1 minute ( really!!) from Paddington station exit on Praed Street. Welcome was outstanding. Left bag for night but, before I went to LOrds for cricket, they made me a lovely tea and I sat in downstairs cafe. Waved me off then greeted warmly later in evening. Booked large bed room

title: 4 for idea, 2 in reality. A balanced review.
text: Room: large room facing London St. The concept and design of The Pilgrm was what swayed us to book. Light grey walls, deep navy carpets and shadow tones, with crisp white highlights appeal to the (minimalistic) style conscious. Accent items such as cast iron heaters, utilitarian lights and compact open wardrobe are pleasantly functional. Perhaps unsurprisingly the old sash windows are single glazed and leak both sound and wind (they do look great though). The wind was welcoming on the hot evening, but the noises from the busy street really not great. No handmade cotton mattress, Egyptian cotton bedding and ear plugs could change the fate of a tossful night's sleep. But still the room looks great, lit by the evening streetlights coming through the edges of the blind. Shower-room: The shower is powerful, the best thing. Toilet characterful, strong flush. Sink splashes a lot, could do with a hand towel hook to just help the function as form is well taken care of. Suppose minimalism doesn't mean absolute essentialist living. Around the hotel: the staffs are eager to help, but perhaps this new concept of hospitality is also a bit confusing for them at the minute. Some items promised, such as the Larder for snacks, are not yet a reality. Shame. The breakfast is decent, perhaps is the best in the area but not so in London if you are willing to travel a little further. All in all, in some areas the Pilgrm is trying hard to be different but maybe it's best to keep eyes on something more important such as air-con and some soundproofing to the windows. Eco-friendly probably also doesn't mean having the fan on all night. The whole concept of forgoing the reception is not (yet?) a reality. To be honest, I'm not entirely sure why they wanted to remove the reception, or why it's not simply part of the coffee bar. Like many lightbulb idea before it this place gets a balanced 3 from me in practice.

title: Relaxed and friendly place to stay
text: We frequently visit London and I would say this is one of the best hotels we have stayed in over the last ten years.warm friendly staff with no fussy uniforms or long drawn out checking in process. The young lady who greeted us was an absolute delight and was very kind and caring. Ok.. So the room was small.. But when you're asleep that really doesn't matter! The bed was so comfy we didn't want to get up.. The cleanliness was the highest standard I have ever encountered not just in the uk but overseas also. Will definitely be returning cannot say enough good things about this place. We absolutely loved it. Thank you so much to all the lovely people involved.

title: Reasonable price, great services
text: We spent 5 days at The Pilgrm and the staff is very welcoming, the services are complete and they pay attention to the details. The lounge offers great choices, the breakfast is good but not a lot of options. The room was clean, the bed confortable. The WiFi works great and I was able to streamed some movies. However, there was no air conditioning in the room and it was really hot. The location is a bit noisy but it stops around midnight. Overall we had a great time and I would come back

title: Unique rooms nestled in a prime location
text: The location of the hotel is a minute walk to Paddington station, where you can get onto the Heathrow Express and be at the airport in less than 20 mins. The hotel is nestled a few minutes walk from cafes, pubs and restaurants and only a 20-minute walk to Oxford Circus and Hyde Park. Friendly staff and easy check-in. The hotel offered a unique, clean and easy stay. I will definitely be going back to stay there again. The small room is perfect for single travelers or business. I stayed in the Medium room and had no issues with the space (even with 4 suitcases). If you want that extra room I would suggest the medium or large room. There was no aircon BUT, a fan was provided and I honestly did not think it was an issue as for most of the day we were outside exploring the city and at night the cool breeze and the fan made it a comfortable sleep.

title: Very small rooms, and no air-con
text: This is a nice enough hotel and well situated, however if you book a small room, be aware that they are very small, almost shoebox size. The room size, excluding the shower room is about the size of two double beds side by side. Given that there's already a double bed in the room that doesn't leave a lot of floor space to move about in. We were there in 30degree heat and with no air-con the only ventilation was provided by a small window hopper and a floor standing fan which was not sufficient. Had we been there at a different time, i.e. not so hot, and had book a larger room, then I may have given more that 3 stars as the staff were very friendly and the food was acceptable

title: Lovely
text: If you want a generic hotel that you find anywhere in the world, with no soul then this is t for you! We went for the medium sized room and were pleasantly surprised at the size of it. Yes there was a zigzag corridor to the room but that was fine. Gorgeous bathroom. Spotlessly clean. Comfortable bed. Excellent linen. Excellent pillows. Endless cold drinking water. Good food. Large tv. Good WIFI. USB ports. Great music. Very relaxed place. Excellent location beside Paddington! The only reason I didn’t give it 5 stars was the lack of aircon. The fan helped but we were there during a heatwave and it was pretty hot. If you like something a bit different then go there! But I understand that it is an old building and it is t possible to deliver everything. We will be back...

title: Smallest room with no air con, wouldnt recommend
text: Dont be deceived by the pics online, they are all real but just art directed very well. The rooms are tiny, I couldn’t fit in my bed, it was summer and no air con, total nightmare it was super hot throughout the entire hotel, who doesn’t have air con!!!!!!

title: A bit too small
text: Full disclosure - I felt that I understood the philosophy of The Pilgrm before I booked a small room and was prepared for the confined quarters. Just not prepared enough. There’s just not enough space to feel comfortable. There are no shelves to put spare change, no space to open a suitcase, your toiletries bag has to sit in the sink. There’s no bedside table for your phone and a glass of water. It’s a bit too small. On the positive side, the room was really clean and the bed was comfortable. Service was OK. Very hands-off. I think the care factor is pretty low. It wasn’t a bad place. But behind the trendy veneer, this was a more budget experience than I was expecting. So on the whole “small, but all you need” philosophy, there may be some way to go on the execution.

title: quirky and fun one night stay
text: Stayed here with my daughter for one night (one of the hottest in London recently!), in room H22, a medium sized room. After reading all the reviews, we were pleasantly surprised by the size of the room which was more than adequate, with space for luggage, a perfectly designed bathroom, a window that opened (for some much needed air) and a great bed. A fan was already going in the room when we arrived. We were at the end of a mews, so no street noise at night. We loved the concept of this hotel, all very informal, however the one negative was the chaos at breakfast on Sunday morning. The waiting staff and the kitchen were completely overwhelmed, so after waiting over 30 minutes for my breakfast we had to cancel as we had a train to catch. Shame, as I was really looking forward to it having read all the good reviews. My daughter had ordered the continental breakfast, and had some yogurt and dried apricots, there was no fresh fruit and no pastries left, but some good orange juice and coffee good too! We weren't charged for what we had had and staff were apologetic, but think it would be better to be upfront with guests when ordering and tell them it might take 30 minutes, so you could choose, as some people might not mind waiting? Loved the pantry idea, being able to make tea/coffee and get cold water, just meant having to get dressed to make a morning cuppa! overall loved it here, and would definitely return, such a refreshing change from the normal corporate hotels! It wasn't particularly cheap either but think that weekend in London was particularly expensive everywhere!

title: Nice hotel - excellent location
text: Nicely designed hotel with quality furniture and decoration. But very small rooms and too limited space to move inside’ not even a table to put computer or stuff. This is relatively expensive for just a bed. Otherwise good welcome and service and overall positive atmosphere.

title: Interesting, mostly good
text: Curious Paddington hostelry offering superior design nous - comes off as a kind of hipster Travelodge. Greeted by friendly, hapless staff overawed by a sudden rush of check-ins and hampered by what is supposed to be a trendy lack-of-desk. Room generally good - cleverly thought out minimalist offerings featuring various vintaged fixtures in black, white and gray, not unlike the set of a peculaliarly noir-ish Wes Anderson movie. Comfortable beds with cool bougie sheets, very much appreciated in melting London summer. Very clean, and sound proofing clearly more substantial than in comparable, crumbling Victorian terrace boarding houses just around the corner in Norfolk Square. Irritating lack of amenities papered over by strong Shoreditchian branding, marketing and comms. Claims lack of aircon for "environmental" reasons, and pushes communal, out-of-room (often up or down stairs) tea and coffee stations as an innovation. Actual rationale for both increased profit margin, although sharp on-brand marketing bod sure to deny this by reply. Breakfast superb - similar lower priced offerings can be found in the vicinity, but unlikely to match for quality. Roomy and hip Eurocafe feel to eating area, rare for pub and chain saturated locale. Worth shelling out for at least once. Could be superb, but hobbled by amateurish oversight (example of reply to another guest "As discussed in writing and on call, in order to investigate any claims made during a guest’s stay, we needed the full team to be present on a Monday morning to look into the matter" - any hotel that can only provide a satisfactory managerial response once a week is in dire need of introspection). Still, perfect for unfussy one night stopovers, or temporary Central London based events. More than three nights likely to be cloying for all but the hardiest.

title: Best brekky of our London trip
text: Really should listen to locals. Went here on the last morninh we were in London. Brilliant. Great breakfast. The hands down best black pudding I have ever had, and I have had A LOT of black pudding. Great sausages and beaut big mushroom. Do go there. You will not be diappointed.

title: Quick stopover
text: My wife and I had a quick overnight stop as we headed back to the states. The beds were wonderful, the food at the bar was great and we slept awesome. This place has a ton of charm and is right by Paddington Station. We plan to stay here again.

title: Spot On!
text: We booked 2 large rooms through the hotel website & stayed for one night B&B (22.06.18). The hotel is a stone's throw from Paddington - perfect if traveling into London from the West Country (or Heathrow). ALL of the staff were brilliant - friendly & professional. The breakfast was delicious with an excellent choice. The bedrooms & bathrooms are thoughtfully designed (someone has a great 'eye'), the bed linen wonderful & the beds very comfortable. Our rooms were on the side of the building on the first floor, we wondered if it might be noisy at night but it was NOT! Hooray to the free water. The team who has put this hotel together deserves much applause, as does the team/s who run it for them - do hope they keep up the high standard! We'll be back!

title: Worst service ever. Do not stay here
text: We stayed here for 2 nights with our parents to celebrate their joint 60th birthdays

title: Finally a great place to stay in London
text: Part of me doesn't want to review this as it's newly opened and once people realise how great this place is and they are fully up and running, I doubt I'll be able to book again. I'd read the excellent review in The Guardian newspaper and we'd booked to see exhibitions in The Serpentine (10 minute walk), the Barbican (25 minute tube) and shows in Leicester Square (20 minute tube), so it was the perfect location to stay. On arrival all my expectations were met, firstly the staff were excellent, all of them from management to cleaners were helpful and welcoming. Secondly the detail and design is top notch, everything had a quality to it, from the light switches and fittings to the wonderfully comfortable beds, they really have spent a lot of money on fine, quality decor. We were at the back of the hotel and had a great night's sleep, there was a low murmur, but as we live on the coast it was no different from hearing the sea. Finally, a delicious breakfast and perfect coffee and teas, all in under a 4 minute walk from Paddington train station and tube. We can't wait to return, thank you.x

title: A nice place to be!
text: It couldn't be any closer to Paddington Station, but once you walk through the doors it just feels so chilled. It has a really nice vibe and the building is quirky and interesting. Yes rooms are small, it was a bit hot and you can hear noise from outside, but everything just works and it's a nice place to be. Given the location it's also very decent value. Will definitely use again.

title: Great location, but Room is too small
text: Stayed 1 night late May. Put up request for 2, chose a double room. We were allocated a room in Y block. I was surprised to see how small the room was - the double bed was tugged end to end snuggly within 3 walls, and there's a narrow gap (perhaps about 20cm) between the bed and the entrance to the shower room. Thankfully the shower room is sufficiently big for a toilet bowl, a sink and a shower corner. We ended up having to store our luggages in the shower area after our baths. To sleep I have to curl up against my partner (I am about 6 feet tall

title: Hot and noisy, great decor!
text: Stayed one night after arriving late in to Heathrow and catching an early train the next day from Paddington. Decor is really nice and staff friendly, but I was on the 3rd floor in room Y38 over looking the main road and the windows are single glazed and paper thin. I could hear everything going on overnight, conversations outside the pub opposite, all deliveries to local businesses and any vehicles passing, the emergency alarm being tested at 0500 in the tube station opposite and the tube trains. So safe to say that most of my 8 hours stay was not spent asleep. The room was hot, they have no aircon and this did not help either. The room was small, fine for a single person for one night, but no more than that. Great decor and staff, poor quality sleep.

title: Great location, breakfast, and value. Smallest rooms ever!
text: Good value. Clean, friendly, and charming. Convenient to Paddington Station, Hyde Park, Kensington, etc. Helpful staff. Excellent breakfast. Rooms of various size-class category available. The “Small” rooms are so small you bump into each other, and knock things over. If you travel light and don’t need much privacy in the bathroom, it’s fine. I’d stay in our W32 again, knowing what I’m in for. Look for the free coffee stations around the hotel.

title: Over all nice stay
text: Great hotel, very Nice interrior and decor. Laid back staff and very helpful. Rooms are a bit small if you are staying longer than 2 nights (we booked a big room and were there for 4). The walls were a bit thin but it was very quiet.

title: Simple, clean, straightforward, convenient
text: I have stayed in lots of hotels near Paddington station (connecting to early flights, or when I have missed the last train). Most have been horrible. As bad as any I have stayed in beyond student hostel. PILGRM (why the odd spelling?) an exception. It is not glamorous and has minimal functionality, but nothing wrong with that. It is simple, clean, straightforward - everything I want from a hotel. Staff were friendly & helpful. It is very convenient for the station. It is a bit of a labyrinth - my room was quiet but I expect some will be noisy It was very reasonably priced (though of course prices always vary)

title: how to take the luxury out of london hotelling
text: I stayed here last weekend as a last minute BH getaway with my other half. Was a very strange experience, they've obviously tried to be different and cash in on simplicity but it's not right, if I wanted a simple hotel I would go to premier inn.. No reception, just a lady not in uniform, with a laptop on a stool..No actual restaurant, even though the food actually saved the day! Only a plush, squishy lounge area which is a multi-functional room of bar/function room/dining area/breakfast. No AC, ANYWHERE, this is a 2* hotel... The stairs to our room were not finished and could smell chemicals. The moment we opened our door I was disappointed, I think my skin age a decade from the heat. I looked around for a table for my bag, no table. I wanted to put my toiletries in the bathroom, no bath and only floor for storage. I wanted to open the window to get some air, the window opened on the the hotels extractor fan...this was blasting out hot air at a rocket blaster volume. I thought the TV would be able to drown out the noise, the freeview digital TV, nope! Only 3 channels "had signal"...We asked the pretend reception (by foot by the way as no in room phone) if there was any other room, no was the answer. We found a fan in a cleaners cupboard on our floor and had that and our room door open all night, talk about a private night. I honestly I couldn't wait to get out of there.

title: Wonderful Central London Hotel
text: I booked the Pilgrim as a birthday treat for my sister when she visited London. I live round the corner. She thoroughly enjoyed her stay. The room was great and had some great design features. The breakfasts were varied and delicious. We had some fantastic cocktails in their lounge. Overall a wonderful hotel

title: Minimalist & Awesome
text: The Pilgrim is a really cool hotel - it's rather minimalist, in a good way. Surprising it houses everything I need! Great magazine selection - it has cereal, good quality tv, a bathroom with dehumidifier, nice Bed ! would have been perfect if the lift was working at that time. But it's ok because the staff were really nice and helped us carried the luggage up and down ( we stayed at level 3.. ) If we had more time, would definitely explore the lounge.

title: Clean, friendly staff, right by Paddington Station
text: Difficult to get closer to the trains at Paddington Station, don't be surprised by the informal and narrow entrance - it is up a few steps and most of the rooms involve some steps to access although there is a small lift. It is spotlessly clean and has lovely beds and linen with rain showers and compact traditional en-suite toilets. My bedroom was double glazed and overlooked a mews - you could just hear the Underground trains as they stopped at the adjacent station. Staff are friendly and informal

title: Last Minute Solo Trip To London
text: I have always wanted to stay at the Pilgrm and was excited to check it out. Knowing I was alone for the night the bunk bed room was suggested online and I took it. After having to walk to the second floor to ask someone where I could check-in because the lady at reception was not the most welcoming I gave my details and with shock she said, “Oh you have such a cheap room!” I felt put on the spot feeling I had to give an explanation as to why I had booked it. Afterwards I thought, yes it is cheap but I am still a guest. I dropped off my bags and after not feeling particularly welcomed wanted to get out... The hotel at first is higgledy-piggledy if you want to be conscious and not use the lift. I got a little confused as to what floor I was on and was greeted with a stern, “May I help you,” directing me to where I needed to be. I entered my room with a feeling of just not being welcomed. Do I look too young? Is it because I booked the cheap room? Hells bells, I don’t know! Having always stayed at the The Hoxton when I come to the city I certainly understand now why hotel engagement and atmosphere is equally important when rating a hotel. Check-out was worse OCD me had thrown my card number away and only checked out with the room card. I said I had forgotten it. The lady whom was not so welcoming started tapping her foot getting impatient with me. I started giving my name and with attitude she said, “I can’t hear you,” followed by “Can you not even remember what floor you were on?!” Having to almost shout I said the floor number and my name. I could see my name on the page she had in front of me and had only seen her the day before checking in. So much for remembering your guests’. I have never felt so unwelcome in a hotel before. Such a pity as it would have been the perfect setting for coffee, however, I left upset after the treatment. If I owned a hotel or managed one I would treat everyone with respect despite who is booking what room. I would be grateful that someone had even visited and welcomed them warmly and with sincerity. I was going to book again for a solo trip in July to see a gig but sadly I will not be coming back. I am not one for reviews but felt I had to share.

title: It has its quirks but I loved staying here
text: I stayed here for four nights whilst attending a training course at Paddington Central (an easy 10 minute walk). The hotel is a great antidote to your bland corporate experience and is very well located within a couple of minutes walk from the main Paddington station entrance. There are plenty of shops and restaurants right on the door step. I had a very friendly welcome and they kindly stored my bag for the day to save me lugging it around. My room was a “small double” and the clue is in the “small”. It was fine for a single occupant but any more and you’d struggle. It is pretty much just the (double) bed and a small area for hanging clothes, there was a gap at the bottom of the bed where I could store my luggage and the room safe is cleverly hidden under the bed. Looking on the fire escape plan there were clearly much bigger rooms available, mine looked like one of the smallest. I had a large window with a lovely view out over Norfolk Gardens. There was no (room for a) desk so if you’re expecting to work you’ll be stuck with the bed. A 32” Samsung flat screen TV is provided with Free View channels but no smart functions (you can get to the HDMI sockets if you remove the panel from the back, it worked fine with my Xbox) and a Marshall Bluetooth speaker which sounds ok (it’s not a BOSE but...) and is certainly a nice touch. Wi-Fi is free, reliable and was super quick (circa 75Mbps up+down). There was no fridge in my room (difficult to see where they’d put it!). The bed and pillows were super comfy and the room (and hotel) has a quirky off-beat decor which I loved. There are nice options for playing with the lighting to make the room cozy. It was immaculately clean and the bathroom had a decent overhead show with good pressure and temperature. As with the bedroom there is very little storage but it did me ok (I put some things on the toilet cistern lid - an old fashioned style one with the cistern high up on the wall) A few points to note. The windows are single glazed and Paddington is a fairly noisy area so there was quite a bit of noise, even late at night. I ended up using ear plugs so it didn’t bother me. My room (W32) was up and down lots of stairs so if you have mobility requirements I’d suggest flagging these at booking. There is a lift but it doesn’t reach all parts of the hotel without involving stairs. The 1st floor has a cafe/restaurant serving a small menu and with the large windows (luckily open when I was there, given good weather) its a great place to chill out. My all day breakfast was very tasty with high quality ingredients. There is also a small cafe area on the ground floor/reception with tables where you can work. In short, if you can manage the noise, space and want a change from a corporate hotel I’d highly recommend this hotel, it was an enjoyable rather than transactional stay which is rare. I’d definitely stay here again but opt for a larger room.

title: Pros outweigh the cons...
text: Pros: Characterful

title: Very Average
text: Firstly the staff do seems to care and try hard, in particular the kitchen for breakfast was accommodating of a vegan diet and made me some lovely food, so a big thanks you. The room was very very small and we had a large room apparently, we were not shown to the room so spent ages looking for the safe and its beneath the bed and also we didn't find out until we left that there are allegedly tea and coffee making facilities in a central location on each floor? We were in room 41 on level 4 which looks out over the top of the flats opposite so the view was good, unfortunately the noise from the road below was too much for me and both nights of our stay I was awaken several times by shouting, sirens and general 24 hour city noise, the issue here is that the window as an old single glazed sash, this room desperately needs secondary glazing. On Sunday we were greeted by workmen in the stair lobby banging and still essentially finishing the hotel, not great but I guess it has to be done? I liked the decor, the staff and the service but I would not stay again as I can get better value and I can't deal with the road noise. I hope this helps. James

title: London experience
text: One word

title: A must-stay!
text: Clean, well-equipped, spacious, friendly, modern apartments (fully fitted kitchen, too) just minutes away from Tower Bridge, London Bridge, Hays Gallery...Supermarket, Coffees and pubs close-by. We absolutely loved it and will come back next year!

title: Great Location!!!
text: We booked our room via booking.com. The location and price could not be beat! The staff was super friendly, and the room was very clean. We stayed for a quick trip to London-3 overnights. A quick walk to the London Bridge (10 min. max) and tube (10 min). Again, best location!

title: Really good option in London
text: My husband and I stayed here 8/31 - 9/3. I had found it on Expedia and seemed like a great option for the location, amenities, and price. I had been to London once before and stayed in Mayfair, but my husband had never been. The rate was 130.68 US per night and offered a 2 room suite that was perhaps a bit tight on space by some US standards, but was thoughtfully laid out and had absolutely everything you would need...even a kitchenette. There was also on site laundry, though all were occupied when we tried to use them. We loved the ability to get fresh air in the room with the large sliding window / door and how the hotel allows fresh air to flow into the corridors as well. Also, the common lounge allows you the option to get a drink even after other places have closed. We also really loved the Bermondsey neighborhood...lots of restaurants and businesses populated with local professionals and away from lots of tourists, close to London Bridge Station, The Shard, Tower Bridge, and Maltby Street Market. I would definitely consider staying here again. The negative comments I have are very minor. One is regarding the front desk staff. Perhaps it comes from my experiences in the US, but as we came and went no one ever greeted us or even acknowledged us. They were not rude and were available if we needed something, but not terribly warm. Also, the lobby bathroom was out of paper towels for the length of our stay. Lastly, the air-conditioning unit is in the living area and not in the bedroom area, so it doesn't cool the bed area quite as well I would have liked...but I like my bedroom very cold at night so this is probably only an issue for me and not most people. Again, these are very minor complaints, but were the only things keeping me from giving a 5 star rating.

title: Best value for money in central London
text: This was the first time we stayed at this place and I doubt if we'd stay anywhere else in London now we've discovered it. The room was superb. It was clean, modern, everything worked as it should, and it had a very well equipped little kitchen area as well as a living room and a sleeping area. It was an example of excellent use of space. The location, close to London Bridge, was very convenient. Despite its central location, it was quiet so we had a great sleep.The staff were very helpful and friendly. It also had the best shower I've ever experienced in a hotel anywhere. The breakfast was OK but it's optional so we'd give that a miss the next time. There are lots of extras on offer such as complimentary laundry facilities. We didn't have the need for that as we only stayed for one night but that could be a money saver for other travellers. Top marks for this place - highly recommended.

title: Amazing!
text: Out stay was brilliant, the room was clean and tidy and the staff went out of their way to make the night perfect for us. We had a few minor issues such as the toilet door not locking and the plastic seal on the shower coming off but they were not problems for us. Our main issue was breakfast - Its not amazing, there was little choice and the cooked food was mostly cold with poor layout. but other than that amazing, absolutely amazing and i will be staying again.

title: Excellent location
text: Stayed in this hotel to visit family for the weekend, excellent location right near London Bridge and tube stations. Staff were friendly and welcoming, room was small and compact but as it was only one night it did the job. Bathroom could have been cleaner, the shower screen seal also kept falling off when being used. Unfortunately the pull out sofa bed was also not very comfortable which resulted in a bad nights sleep. Breakfast was excellent, lots of choices to choose from, we did enjoy the food. The hotel tried to charge us a higher rate than what we had booked it for through their own website. Fortunately a confirmation email resolved this situation. Would definitely recommend this hotel due to its location, friendly staff, excellent breakfast, and convenience. Would also recommend not using the sofa bed.

title: 7 day stay - very recommend WSET course
text: Very centrical, well communicated (train station London Bridge) Borough market walking distance, charming neighborhood with boutique cafes and shopping. Rooms are ample, clean and quiet. Kitchen a welcome plus. Staff very friendly and helpful. Breakfast selection correct. 5 min from WSET central office in London. Highly recomendable. Would happily stay there again.

title: Great Suite for a good Price
text: Comfy, stylish, clean, great location, great price, would recommend and stay here again. Near borough maket and some nice cafes and restaurants. Near the tube and bus routes. The breakfast had a good selection and was ok.

title: Outstanding
text: Staff helpful, polite and courteous. Rooms fully equipped, couldn’t have asked for more. Complimentary breakfast excellent. Highly recommend these suites. It is a 15 min walk from Borough tube but pleasant walk and located near to pubs, restaurants and supermarkets. Will definitely return next time we come to London

title: Great, clean and good location
text: We stayed here once night and found it was only about 15 minutes walk from the underground by the Shard. Lovely a clean. Good reception staff and a nice room in the middle of London. Would definitely use again

title: Great hospitality !!!
text: This is a fabulous place in a beautiful part of London. I am staying here for business and it has been a fantastic experience. The team at reception are an asset to the service apartment. This is the place to be if you want to be surrounded by friendly, helpful people. You will go to work with a smile on your face when greeted by OJ. Dwayne and Stefan will always ask how your day is going. I can't speak enough of how much the team adds value to the experience of the service apartment. Apart from the excellent team, the rooms are tidy and beautiful decorated. Plus the bed is very comfortable!

title: My preferred London place to stay
text: I like to make my own food as I’m vegan too and this is the best equipped apartment hotel. Good internet and windows opens good bed easy walk to London bridge and Broughton market. Plenty of bars and cafes

title: Charming hotel in charming neighbourhood
text: We loved South Point Suites and loved Bermondsey too! Trendy hotel with very comfy beds. Excellent location. Only 10 minutes walk to the Shard and Borough Market. Lots of nice cafes, restaurants and shops nearby. Easy to travel to the other parts of city.

title: Your own city pad
text: Great for a few nights stay in the city on business. Clean, well-equipped apartment with friendly reception staff. Good location for coffee bars and cafes, local shops, restaurants and bars. It felt like having your own city pad to come back to.

title: Good value for money!
text: Spacious well equipped room! Very good for a short stay! Good bed, great location. Breakfast was quite simple, food was not tasteful as promoted by the hotel. The shower was good but the water was not flowing properly. Amenities were water inside, not suitable to use.

title: Superb
text: Excellent facilities - well positioned and made for a convenient stop over place. Close to London Bridge which is ideal for both my airport (Gatwick) and access into London Only shame was that I wasn't staying for longer

title: A little Bermondsey St gem
text: Stayed at South Point Suites over a weekend whilst visiting family/going to a gig in Borough. Extremely happy with the experience. Decor very fresh, with attention to detail. Room with separate bedroom area had everything I needed. Bed was amazingly comfortable, room temperature easily controlled and shower room was immaculately clean, with quality toiletries. Soundproofing was great

title: Good space but don't try to do laundry...
text: We were in town for business but traveled as a family. The suites were a comfortable size for our family of three and the price was very reasonable. The layout of the room was nice as we had a separate space from our young child who slept on the pull-out couch. The staff was friendly and the breakfast was generous. There was a nice variety of items and always hot breakfast offerings alongside the usual hotel breakfast. The location was a bit of a hike to the tube but it was manageable. There were a nice variety of restaurants nearby to explore as well as a few little shops. The price was definitely worth the slightly less convenient location. On a side note, as we were waiting for our Uber in the dark on a very early morning, we saw a small fox walk right down the sidewalk. That was quite a surprise and very surreal! My primary complaint was the laundry situation. As we were toward the end of our travels, I had some laundry to do for the family. If that's your plan, you're better off making other arrangements. If you only want to wash a couple of items and hang them to dry, you'll be fine (but then hand wash and you can stay anywhere). The dryer did not work (I had to hang many things and it took repeat visits with moving laundry to other dryers in order to dry things such as socks and underwear) and based on the amount of laundry lying around, that's the norm. There were clearly people who resided there somewhat long-term who just left their laundry all around and didn't worry about swapping it out right away. It was most annoying. It also seems as though cleaning people would wash their cleaning cloths there as they were lying around as well. I had flashbacks of college dorm life and it was most frustrating. Overall, if you are booking a stay for a family and wanted some decent sized space that includes breakfast, I would recommend this hotel. If you are willing to pay a bit more for more comfort/intimacy and easier access to transport, I'd look elsewhere. I personally would choose another spot next time we return.

title: Solo business traveller
text: Excellent stay, the room was clean, comfortable and quiet. Perfect for solo business travellers. Good value for money, friendly and welcoming staff, excellent location as lots of places to eat very close by.

title: Superb!
text: Lovely one night stay. You won’t get better for the price in London. Very reasonably priced breakfast (£8 in advance, £10 on the day) of a very high standard with loads of choice, all fresh. Rooms (suites) large, modern and of a very high standard. George was an absolute delight. So professional, friendly and welcoming. Little touches like remembering our son’s name and welcoming him when we got back after a long day with a smile and a conversation mean so much and he should be very highly commended for such a brilliant attitude. Well done, we WILL be back!

title: Great facilities, location and cost
text: Great location in the heart of London Bridge but also tucked away. Apartments are clean, spacious, stylish and have everything you need for a stay (hair dryer, iron, toiletries etc.) Gym in the basement is of a reasonable size and wasn't particular busy first thing in the morning. There are a handful of cardio machines, cable machine, dumbbells, some weight machines and exercise mats. Breakfast was included and provided a range of continental style options. Overall a great stay.

title: Very pleased
text: Very pleased with our stay. Staff were very helpful, polite and friendly. Room was clean and comfortable. Good value for money. Tube station was only 10 minute walk away and the area was clean and quiet.

title: Excellent All Round
text: We have stayed at a good number of serviced apartments in London, particularly around London Bridge and Tower Bridge - these are the best we have found. Fitted to a high standard, very comfortable bed and couch, excellent air con, other fixtures and fittings good quality and a decent sized kitchen. It has a nice ground floor lounge area and an option for breakfast. Staff are really excellent - very warm and welcoming on check in and throughout the stay - Stefan on the front desk in particular deserves a mention - lovely sunny disposition and informative. Will definitely be back for both business and leisure. Excellent value for money in central London.

title: Came back for more!
text: We flew in London to celebrate a milestone birthday and staying in South Point Suites made the trip special. We stayed in the deluxe studio suite for our family of 4 and we were all amazed by the size, comfort, and service the hotel provided. They even had a special treat when we arrived.... such a nice touch! Breakfast was lovely and the Tuesday Happy Hour was marvelous! It was our first time to stay in the Bermondsey area and it was such a pleasant surprise to see how vibrant and fun this place is with lots of restaurants, pubs and cafes nearby. On our way back from Paris we tried to make reservations at South Point Suites again but they had no rooms. Thank goodness I persisted and we were able to book a room in this fabulous hotel because we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. I don't usually write reviews and initially wanted to keep this gem a secret, but I do have to give a shout out to the amazing staff - Denise, OJ, Angel, Tabitha, and Kasim for making us feel at home and always going the extra mile! Thank you! We will definitely be back!

title: Beyond Expectations
text: One of the best hotel experiences I've had. Top notch on every area. I like to stay in new hotels and this one didn't disappoint! The property is stunning, and the service was exemplary. I'll definitely be back.

title: Great Place to Stay in London
text: I stumbled on this property earlier this year and thought it was great. I went back with the family in October and took two rooms and was not disappointed. This is a fabulous place to stay. The rooms are great, free laundry, great lounge room on the ground floor and sensational staff.Really close to lots of funky restaurants, Borough Market, London Bridge and Tower. IT really is a must try

title: Very comfortable
text: Excellent stay and services. Room was spacious and comfortable . Nice looking . Very well located from the London bridge station. Easy access to all facilities around. Great stay . Didn’t try the food here but all provisions in the room were sufficient . Microwave , fridge and all utensils . Also a coffee machine .

title: London for a weekend
text: Hotel is on great location 10 minutes from Tower Bridge, we were satisfied with the service. Suites are bigger than our other London experience, everything clean and equipment on high standard. We can recommend this hotel for a weekend stay.

title: Great overnight stay in a lively yet quiet street South of the River!
text: Stayed here with my Cousin for an overnight. Small yet perfectly formed suite on 4th floor. Good Reception service, including storing our bags until our suite was ready. The lounge area was cosy and welcoming, with tables to eat at and a degree of privacy. The fact that the building is down a pedestrianised lane area off Bermondsey Street itself, means that a degree of quietness is added. Bed very comfy, shower room and facilities great, lovely well equipped kitchen and dining area and everything to make your stay enjoyable, comfortable, stylish and a home from home - well I wouldn't call my home stylish, yet hey! My only slight issue was that the air con in our suite remained "temperamental", even when one of the Reception staff tried to re-set it. I mentioned it when we checked out. Bermondsey Street has a range of interesting one-off shops and places to eat and drink. Very characterful and not too far from London Bridge Station either. I'd definitely consider staying again, should the opportunity arise.

title: Great place to stay in London
text: Modern, cosy, comfortable and convenient. Well equipped suite, good functionality, nice little kitchen and good shower, snug beds, ac in room, clean and pleasant overall. Loved Bermondsey Street, great atmosphere with lots of restaurants, cafes, food shops. Borough Market and London Bridge Station 10 min walk away.

title: Good location for London Bridge Hospital
text: My wife had an operation in The London Bridge Hospital which involved a 5 night stay. Most of the time I was the only occupant so the room was fine for that. The 15 minute walk to and from the Hospital was fine.

title: Love love loved it!
text: Stayed here last Tuesday for a business trip! Smooth check in, great staff, room fantastic with lounge kitchen area and bed other side with bathroom in between! Found various gems along Bermondsey Street such as Jose Pizarro’s original tapas bar (amazingly authentic) and 10 min walk to borough Market and the Shard! We will be back !!

title: Excellent!
text: Stayed here for 3 nights - fantastic find. The staff were helpful and accommodating. Rooms well appointed and spotless. Good location and great restaurants and bars nearby - maybe make a reservation wherever possible at restaurants as the area is popular. We'll definitely be back!!

title: charming hotel
text: best service for acceptable price - although the room wwas quite cold at the end of october (heating could be optimized), very friendly and helpful staff, cosy lobby :-) breakfast excellent, quite close to tower bridge but 15 min walk to the underground - many stylish restaurants shops and pubs nearby but not the best surrounding for children who won't eat anything unfamiliar

title: 5 stars!! Best deal and quality in London!
text: I travel extensively and this hotel is absolutely 5 stars. Our stay was for a family trip and this checked all the boxes. To top it off, the room had two full bathrooms! Room quality was fantastic and the breakfast was stellar. This hotel also has gym and laundry facilities. The only down side is you may have some increased cost for the tube or Uber to see the sites. If you are coming to London with family, don’t miss this one! Your future traveling self will thank you! :)

title: Excellent purely excellent
text: Great place to say at a very reasonable price close to everything. Try it you will not regret your stay.the room was clean,superbly decorated,everything you would need is in the room. Very quiet for the middle of London

title: Great place to stay
text: Stayed 8 nights for business and personal reason and really impressed with the space, service and facilities. Amazing place to stay. Clean and relaxing. Helpful staff. Great location. Only a 10 minute walk to Borough market and London Bridge. Lots of great local restaurants around. Loved that there was complimentary coffee & tea in reception, complimentary laundry facilities and 24 hours gym made stay very easy. Most of all, the bed was so comfy!! Would definitely try to stay here again on my next visit to London.

title: Great Location
text: This accommodation was fantastic, from the great location off Bermondsey Street to the room facilities. A great choice if you are looking for flexibility and the amenities are great if you are there for a longer stay as they have a laundry room and gym facilities.

title: Amazing
text: The staff are amazing. Tabitha, Stefan, Georgia & co have made this long term stay a home from home. Here since January 31st. The rooms have all of the mod cons and are extremely comfortable. Can’t wait to visit and come back already!

title: Really like this place
text: Stayed for one night and would have liked it to be longer. Staff are great, the place has a smart and relaxed vibe that is very appealing. The room was a delight, great coffee maker, spacious and quality everywhere. This could become my favourite place to stay in London

title: Christmas trip
text: Came here the week before Xmas for two nights. Wonderful hotel and have booked to go again! The hotel is tucked away and has the friendliest and helpful staff. The rooms are like mini-apartments which we loved, the idea we could make our own breakfasts and lunches etc was awesome. The locations is good, about half a mile from London Bridge station.

title: Excellient hotel
text: Excellient hotel,we stayed here for a birthday weekend. our room was very clean and well equipped with everything you need for your stay. The staff were very friendly and helpful. I would definitely stay again

title: New Year’s Eve stay (two couples)
text: Myself, my partner and two friends stayed for 1 night on New Year’s Eve. We arrived to a quick and easy check in after a long drive. We were in room 401 on the 4th floor, room was well spacious, clean and had everything you could need. Only downfall was that the beds were opposite each other which we found a bit odd - not a problem but not much privacy. Tea/Coffee downstairs is complementary, cold drinks or alcoholic drinks are an additional charge. The following morning we had breakfast which we took back up to our room, great selection of hot and cold food/drinks. All staff are exceptionally friendly, polite and will help with anything you ask. A great location and a real home from home feel in the rooms. Thank you!

title: Very good hotel
text: Two things decided: good opinions about the breakfast on the site Booking.com and good location. My family emphasizes that the breakfasts were great. Only 10 minutes walk from Tower Bridge and only 2 minutes from the bus stop.

title: Welcoming staff and felt like home.
text: Great service. Location was great and the room felt like a homestay. 2 tv's and complete with everything you need during a busy conference. Peace of mind, slept great, and the staff was flexible. I had to check out over phone in the taxi due to hectic morning. Will definitely book again for next one.

title: Quality Accommodation
text: Room - not huge, but well designed, and space used to the max Staff - excellent Breakfast - very good Distance from Tube - 0.5 miles/10 mins walk Euston to London Bridge - 30 mins In 20 years + of going to London, I can honestly say this is the best we’ve stayed in, and the first that we’ll be going back to! Everything you need, nothing you don’t.

title: Weekend break
text: Great weekend stay at South Point Suites - excellent service and amenities and convenient location close to London Bridge station. Bermondsey Street with all it had to offer is right on your doorstep. Highly recommend this accommodation

title: Brilliant place to stay
text: Stayed here October until July and couldn't ask for anything more. Room is great and staff are really friendly. Location great too. Near to the tubes and some excellent places to go nearby. Definitely recommend.

title: Smashing stay
text: Newly refurbished place, which doesn't feel like hotel. Room was very well equipped with great entertainment screen containing more I could look through during my stay. Bed was very comfortable with lovely fluffy beddings. There is no typical hotel 'oppressive' reception desk just a lectern with standing receptionist. Very cozy lounge with variety of seating options. Feels very homely. WIFI first class as it should be. Kitchen section in the room has all the equipment you have at home but new. Did not use the Gym but will do next time. They serve great coffee. Congratulations on beans selection.

title: Great stay
text: Arrived late at 1am to check in for the night and received a warm welcome. No problem that I arrived late. Suite was excellent, spotless, bedroom separated from the living space. Nice big bed with a big TV. Usb chargers next to bed for convenience. The living space had a sofa, and small dining table and chairs, a big TV, fridge, hob, microwave/grill, kettle, toaster, Nespresso coffee machine, sink. Room was very quiet, some building works nearby but didn't start until after 8am at least. Breakfast in the morning was fine, continental with some hot food, sausages, scrambled eggs, beans, pancakes. There was a coffee machine, yogurts, pastries, etc They took a £50 deposit on check in but was immediately refunded within 5 mins of checking out. 5 minute walk to tower bridge.

title: Very Good
text: To whoever wants or plans to stay in this hotel, i just want to let you know that the staff, hotel experience, food and hospitality was fanatastic and their supervisor Angel and their whole team catered to me all he could and i would highly reconnmend this hotel to you.

title: Fab Hotel/Apartment in a vibrant and beautiful part of London
text: Just finished my second week at South Point Suites and I'm very happy indeed. The place is clean and tidy, the staff always friendly and helpful. The rooms themselves have all you need

title: Excellent
text: Found in a quiet turning off Bermondsey Street. Walked in to a smart reception area which smelt beautiful. Staff, welcoming, friendly and helpful. A lovely comfortable lounge area with free hot drinks. Room lovely. Very clean and bright. Good, powerful shower. All amenities including a oven, microwave, dishwasher etc should you wish to self cater. Lots of things to view on tv. Wi-fi excellent. Breakfast, plenty of choice. In short I’ll definitely book again.

title: GREAT stay over New Years!
text: Wonderful staff. They don't clean rooms on weekends, but they let you know that they will upon request, so previous complainers either don't listen or read. (There, I said it because the hotel can't) It was very clear. Room was spacious and very clean. It had a boutique feel. The lobby was gorgeous and modern. The neighborhood was fun and atmospheric. If you uber, tag the church across the street as a lot of uber drivers were confused by the location. Fun things not to miss are The Shard - expensive but worth every penny. I've been to London 16 times, and this was my first time up the Shard, and I loved it, and you will too. (Make sure it is a clear day). Also, if you walk just past London Bridge Station about a block or two, you will find Borough Market. Grab a few snacks to keep in your room, as it has a little fridge, cutting board and plates. In a nutshell, I highly recommend this hotel, and hope that you will, too.

title: Great stay
text: I stayed there on a Fri night with my husband as we were celebrating my Birthday. The room was decorated with lots of Birthday touches and a bottle of Prosecco! Such a lovely touch and so thoughtful.The apartments are location in the heart of Bermondsey street, very close to all the bars, restaurants and coffee shops. It was very clean, nicely decorated and super cosy. I'd stay there again for sure!

title: Outstanding
text: Great Hotel, ideal location, nice atmosphere, home from home rooms. The area has a wonderful cluster of bistro's, restaurants and pubs, perfect to complement a memorable London experience, with Borough a 'must do', right on your doorstep.

title: Great stay! Quiet setting.
text: I stayed there Thursday through Sunday for leisure. My wife and mother were already there from the day prior. I was expected to sleep on the settee and found that it pulled out for a bed. Pretty comfortable with no middle bump from the framing. The suite had a double bed, nice bath (shower) room and kitchen area with a dishwasher, microwave, small fridge, small cooker, and sink. Plenty of dinner ware to use. Also included, but not used, were hair dryer and an ironing board (with iron.) Adequate storage for hanging clothes with drawers for storage. Breakfast was included (possibly built into nightly rate) with unlimited coffee and tea through out the day. The spread for breakfast was fresh and had a decent assortment of choices for hot and cold. There was an abundant selection of beverages/snacks that you can purchase, but we did not buy anything

title: Great Accommodation
text: Stayed here at the end of June and it met all of our requirements. We arrived at London Bridge (only 30 min from Gatwick) and walked with luggage in just 7 minutes. Check in was quick and friendly and we were very pleased with the one bedroom suite There was a bedroom area with ample space and a toilet/shower room. It was great having a kitchen area and sofa separate from bedroom. The area was nice and felt safe and Sainsbury was just around the corner for decent quality microwave food for the night we were tired and couldn’t be bothered going out. It was great having cooking facilities and fridge London bridge is excellent location for getting around London and we got Oyster cards in the station which also had an underground station. There are some nice shops and a M & S Simply Food in the station which just opened the day we left. It was a 20 minute walk to excellent sky garden which was a great free view across the city (we booked the slot online in advance). It was 15 minute walk to London Bridge and Tower of London. We also walked to St Paul’s in around 30 minutes. Breakfast was very decent This was our fourth visit to London and we will definitely stay here again when visiting The city.

title: Pamela Walters
text: Myself and my partner visited over night for his Birthday celebration which was perfect from beginning to end, my stay was booked by a very polite and informative Mr Stefan Latty.The accommodation attention to detail and surprise left in the room for my partners Birthday was excellent all staff were polite. I will definitely visit again and would recommend to anyone.

title: Love this place.
text: This is not out first stay and i can't remember if I've reviewed this place before. If so... It's worth another. Always clean, always welcoming and I always feel safe with the kids here. Safe are always lovely and helpful. I enjoy staying in the city of London when I'm without the kids. When they're with me... This is the place to go.

title: Broken heating
text: Aircon providing no heat , huge draft in room on colder at night of year . Then aircon came on during the night pumping out more cold air. Told staff, who bought me a heater, no offer of different room. So no sleep .

title: Lovely and affordable!
text: The suites are lovely, the location is great (very peaceful even though it's only a 10 minute walk from London bridge station) and the price is really reasonable. We ended up staying an extra night and will definitely be returning!

title: Awful
text: Not cleaned at all. I stayed 4 nights and even if I placed the towels on the floor they didn’t give me new as the soap. They didn’t put in order the room (Hair dryer, as well many other things in the kitchen), they didn’t clean the table, the bed was settled I think in 2 seconds.For 2 nights the heating wasn’t working in the night.

title: So sad to have left
text: I stayed here for two weeks as I was doing exams in London. It was so so amazing

title: Great Hotel, super friendly Staff
text: One of the top Hotels in London by our opinion. Walking distance to the Tower, and Tower Bridge. Nice neighbourhood. The hotel and rooms are clean, wel maintained and spacious! The staff is friendly and made this a special stay!

title: Highly recommended
text: Having never really been the biggest fan of London, staying here allowed me to see a really lovely part of the city. There are lots of lovely cafes on Bermondsey Street and it's an easy walk to London Bridge / Borough stations. The accommodation was perfect - a great space and very quiet so it was easy to get a good nightsn sleep. Highly recommended .

title: Impressive...
text: I can't say enough about this hotel, if I'm honest I could easily live here!From the amazing staff, to the well designed and thought out suites, amazing breakfasts, great facilities such as the gym, laundry room, etc - this is as perfect a stay as I can attest to. Plus, it's in one of the coolest neighbourhoods in London and an ideal vantage point fir exploring the city.

title: Wanted to like the hotel
text: Was very impressed with the suite (larger than most in London). It was tastefully decorated and designed. However, we were placed in a handicap accessible room which was slightly inconvenient as there were red pulls everywhere and no shower curtain or shower enclosure so water spilled everywhere in the bathroom. Not sure if this is standard or specific to the room. I was anxious to do laundry after 9 days of travel but the dryer was horrible. I had to run a 40 minute cycle 4 or 5 times before it even seemed to dry my clothes. This was frustrating and annoying as we had to take time out of our day to go back and forth to the hotel to check on our clothes. Only 2 elevators that we could find and 1 was out of service for the entire stay. Breakfast was very average (hot food not very good). Not the closest to the tube/train station. Probably wouldn't stay here again.

title: Good place to stay
