Nowhere in room to put anything No ironing facilities in rooms (there is a single ironing station on one floor) I could go on. Probably all correctable but currently missing the mark.

title: We did not sleep a wink
text: If you are going to price yourselves in the same bracket as hotels like The Hilton then deliver a room which is fit for the price. The sound insulation was terrible, the noise from the road was so loud we could not sleep. Sirens, people talking outside, car alarms the lot might as well have been in our room. We used this as our first night away from our twin babies and ended up having a worse night’s sleep!

title: Very Authentic, Original and Different Hotel
text: Visited this establishment today for lunch, and I must say I was utterly impressed with the quality of food, the atmosphere of the place and the blend between old/new decor throughout the place, which was achieved with ease. The food was absolutely delicious with great spices and sauces, truly impressed by the quality. I definitely recommend the restaurant, bar and hot tub.

title: Excellent stay
text: We booked one night using a Travelzoo deal and were really impressed by the hotel. It was easy to find -just off Whitechapel high street and 5 mins from Aldergate East tube. Getting around was easy & we felt safe-we walked to Shoreditch/Brick Lane and caught the tube into Piccadilly Circus. Nearby pubs Urban Pub, Good Samaritan & Hoop & Grapes were really good with great selection of beers. Staff were friendly and our room was a good size & immaculate with no noise at all & a really comfy bed. Breakfast was all fresh & cooked to order and the bar was chilled. Great value for money & would stay here again if visiting London.

title: Amazing Mocktails
text: Had a girly get together it the restaurant on Saturday 11th August. Loved the food and drinks. Marie created an amazing Mocktail for me. Mauro and Marie took such good care of us. A really nice relaxing environment to catch up with friends after work.

title: Quirky, friendly, excellent
text: I admit I got a great deal on Lastminute.com. Interestingly, the hotel said they could better it next time. I’ll definitely be staying again so I shall put that to the test. I was a little apprehensive with the hotel being out at Whitechapel. I needn’t have been. It’s less than five minutes to the underground station. The hotel is über modern, incredibly friendly and quirky in its design. The rooms are smallish, but cleverly laid out so as to utilise the space to maximum effect. The bed is comfortable, the shower really good in a compact but adequately spaced bathroom and all spotlessly clean. The blind achieves a total blackout with just a small blue safety light, which is a clever thought. The electrics are good as is the WiFi. On each of the four floors there is a treat. A library, a games room, an ironing station and a yoga area on the roof. Each floor also has a complimentary drinks station. Breakfast (included in the incredible price) was almost excellent. My partner’s vegan sausages letting the meal down by being hard and heavy. The choice is good and varied catering for all tastes. The staff are lovely from reception to the restaurant and made the stay even nicer. I’d definitely put this hotel at the top of my list next time I visit London for one or a few nights.

title: Really great hotel
text: My husband and I had an overnight stay prior to catching the Eurostar and it was such an enjoyable stay. The hotel had only been open about 3 weeks when we visited, so some of the staff were very new and still learning, so the restaurant and bar service was patchy.....that said, our waitress was delightful and the food was really very good. 2 very well espresso martinis and then we played pool in the games area which was brilliant fun and completely unexpected from a trendy London hotel. The communal areas on each floor were actually a really nice touch and added to our enjoyment. Our room was described as “pocket”, and we were offered an upgrade to a bigger room...but we stayed put and were not in anyway disappointed. Spacious, really well thought out, very quiet and with a great shower and fabulously comfortable bed!

title: Outstanding 💕
text: We booked this night away to cheer us up after having a rubbish few months with family bereavements and we cannot thank you all enough for making our stay so amazing from start to finish you couldn’t do enough for us. The rooms, decor, atmosphere, food and cocktails were incredible. We came as strangers and have left as family, see you all soon xxxx

title: Beautiful and stylish
text: We were greeted in a friendly manner after a long trip and day and found our room with ease, which was helpful. The room was unlike any other we've stayed in, with the bed taking up the whole width at one end of the room, and a walk-in shower/bathroom area. The air conditioning was effective and the very large, high-quality TV with all sorts of local information was great. The decor (strangely, for a converted factory) is very sleek and modern while still retaining much of the original features - our personal favourite was the brick wall. There are communal areas on each floor: a library, ironing station, games room and yoga station. They are all quite minimalist and quite nice to sit and relax, although it is a cut-across for some of the rooms so the peace can be disturbed quite frequently. Location-wise, it's quite literally 5 minutes' walk to Whitechapel tube station, just a turn right and across the road. You can launch any tourist excursions with ease from here, and there's a variety of shops and restaurants within 20-30 minutes' walk either side if you fancy going by foot. We had complimentary breakfast included and it was of a very high quality and wonderfully-presented. We didn't get the chance to try the food or drinks from the bar as we were too busy out and about in London. All-in-all, though, an excellent experience and, if we're in the area again at some point in the future, we will definitely be giving this place another serious look. Would thoroughly recommend.

title: Pearl Anniversary
text: Booked this hotel as liked the idea of being away from the hustle of bustle of central London, but close enough on the tube. Did the Motown musical and was surprised as how quick it was to get to the shaftsbury theatre. On arrival staff were brilliant, knowledgeable and friendly. Booked a small double room and was as expected. Bed amazingly comfortable, the shower and toiletries perfect. Loved the old original features, yet the modern feel. Would definitely book this again. The architect and designer spot on. The free pool table lovely if got children, breakfast Abit pricey so ate out, but loved the anniversary cake in the room, nice gesture. Perfect stay

title: Great hotel but be wary if a light sleeper...
text: Stayed here at the weekend as part of a birthday celebration - the communication from the hotel in the week leading up to our stay was very good and they were quick to respond to any query. They also gave us a free upgrade to celebrate the occasion which was a nice touch. The hotel itself is really quirky, clean + modern and although we didn't have an opportunity to eat in the restaurant as we had dinner plans, we did have a really nice coffee and a sundae in the morning. Other particular highlights included the games room, a very comfy bed and fantastic shower. The only negative for me is that I'm a very light sleeper and our road facing room was too loud for me and I simply couldn't get to sleep which was immensely frustrating. I did contact reception during the night but the receptionist wasn't overly helpful or sympathetic and unfortunately, there were non-road facing rooms available to switch to. Any dissatisfaction I felt was remedied by the brilliant customer service I received from Emma the next morning, she really was great and was very understanding - a big credit to the hotel. I will definitely stay at The New Road Hotel again but will be sure to request a non-road facing room.

title: Very good new hotel in London
text: Very well located (3 min from the Whitechapel Underground station) and 24/24h bus (n°25) connected to the major attractions in London. Very helpful staff. Rooms are tiny but well organized. Very good breakfast with some choice.

title: Lovely, welcoming staff
text: We stayed for a weekend in the NRH and enjoyed our stay from the first minute. The hotel is easy to find and not far at all from public transport / tube. The staff welcomed us in a very friendly manner and gave further advise on what sights to visit, aside from the touristy areas. The room itself was a little small but for a stay of 2-4 days it seems perfectly fine. It was all spotless and we had nothing to complain about (no noise whatsoever) Absolutely loved the massively comfy pillows!! Another nice feature is the cereal bar in our opinion :) We liked the design of the hotel in general as it didn't come across as a stylish design hipster place but created a welcoming atmosphere in a building which brought even further character. We would definitely stay here again on our next visit.

title: Close to everything, perfect quality/price ratio !
text: If Whitechapel might seem an unexpected choice while staying in London, it has excellent qualities and the New Road Hotel is one of them. The Hotel is located nearby the underground station and therefore close to any part of the city, in just a few stops. TFL bikes are just 50 meters from the entrance, and Shoreditch and Brick Lane Market are at walking distance. The Hotel in itself is brand new, staff motivated, extremely kind and helpful. Our 'pocket room' was practical, functional and full of natural light. Each floor has a dedicated space (ironing, playroom, library,...) making it fun to discover. With an excellent price/quality ratio, it's definitely an address to keep for further trips !

title: Great hotel, friendly staff but area slightly run down.
text: Couldn't fault the hotel, the room was clean, comfortable & quite it was exactly as described. The staff were very friendly and helpful, slightly disappointing that we couldn't get a drink at the bar on arriving back after the theatre as it was 2 minutes past 11pm when it closed but apart from that the staff made a lot of effort to make our stay special putting a mini cake in our room as it was our wedding anniversary. The only thing that stopped me putting a 5 stars rating was the area was a bit run down with rubbish on the streets but very close to Whitechapel tube station and some nice areas within a short walk from the area.

title: A fabulous all rounder
text: I stayed here with my teenage daughter this weekend and found it to be most enjoyable. The welcome was friendly and unimposing. The staff could not have been more helpful and the hotel itself was spotless! Trendy design ensures that my daughter was impressed and I got some cool Mum points!!!! Bed was comfy and everything in the room was top quality and nothing there that did not have a use or purpose! Plenty of complimentary hot drinks available and the bar prices were not unreasonable given its central London location!!! All in all, ticked all the boxes and I would not hesitate to stay here again and recommend to others. :)

title: Great choice!
text: Lovely hotel at one of the most lively spots in London. Close to all means of transport with excellent service. Beautifully decorated making the most of space. The best part of the stay has been the bed! Extremely comfortable and spacious! Great breakfast choices, good restaurant and bar. The Staff are very friendly, always eager to help and serve but also totally unpretentious. I loved the clever and practical idea of the communal rooms (library, games). I travelled by myself for an educational event and also to visit and see friends in London. Negatives only minor: although the beds are generous, the rooms can feel rather compact if two people are sharing or if they are staying longer than a couple of days and have more luggage. It did not bother me but the neighborhood can be a bit noisy. Some guests may have preferred tea and coffee facilities in the room although it was very easy to get some from the communal rooms. I would definitely go back again and recommend it to friends.

title: 4 nights in a Gem of a hotel.
text: My wife and i stayed in this new hotel for 4 nights in July. It is in a great position if you want to visit all the attractions of the East End. It is only a 10 mins walk from Brick lane, a must to visit. The hotel is a converted warehouse, very ,very well done. This is a quality place to stay. Marco -Pierre-White ihas his name above the kitchen. Breakfast was 10/10 . All the staff were very helpful and polite. The rooms are small but very well fitted out. Even with a large safe. very large tv. The only poor point in or whole stay was the " free teas/ coffee ...this came from a vending machine in the corridor , which would be fine if it was not served in horrible paper cups !! with powdered milk, instand coffee , truely horrible ! .However this was the only poor point in our stay. We loved this hotel and would reccommend it to everybody....... just avoid the coffee/tea machine at all cost :).

title: Business trip stay-over
text: Short business trip to London which involved a one night stay. Hotel is conveniently located near Whitechapel tube but also only a short walk from Aldgate and I did both to take in the area. Whole experience was fantastic with an attentive and friendly Reception team and a well equipped, trendy and quality room. I didn't eat in the restaurant in the evening as I was watching a football match on TV in the bar but the aroma coming from the restaurant made me wish that I did - breakfast was an absolute delight and the best I've had in a long time. Will definitely return the next time I'm in the area.

title: London Business TRip
text: Great hotel. Very friendly staff, great room, nice food. I liked the work space in the library. Room very clean and comfortable bed. Food nicely prepared and staff very attentive. Location very handy for tube.

title: Quirky, comfortable room with lots of little luxuries and great food
text: The small room was bigger than expected and the waterfall shower was great. Highlight of the room was definitely the Hypno bed, comfiest bed I've ever slept on. Breakfast was delicious and the coffee machines on each floor was very convenient. Games room even had a retro fighting game, lots of fun. The only downside of the property was the surrounding area. It was very noisy at night and the surrounding area was not very nice. Luckily there was an underground station a few minutes walk from the hotel, so the rest of London was easily accessible.

title: Tiny rooms
text: London is expensive and finding a room in your price range for 2 adults with a adult son is tough. This place presents well and was very clean. Location is at Earls Court tube station 4 stops from Victoria so easy to get to and from Gatwick Airport. Location is great. Restaurants and grocery stores are a stones throw away. We had a room with three twins. It was so tiny but understandable given the price. The room needed some hooks on the wall for wet towels and perhaps a small narrow depth stainless rack to put the towels when you arrived. They lay them on your bed but there is no where to put them once you get into bed. You could barely open your suitcase the room is that compact. The internet connection was almost non existent in our room which was our biggest disappointment. We had to go to the lobby to download what we needed for our flight home. It was frustrating to be on vacation and looking for timetables and things to do without good wifi. The tv signal was intermittent too. Staff did try to fix the tv and were helpful. We were disappointed that a room discount was not given for the inconvenience. Breakfast was lovely and great to have it available early to start your day of sightseeing.

title: The tiniest hotel room ever known to man
text: Although the rates are almost unbeatable and the hotel is well located, I really expected a little bit more from this place. The room was really small, I could touch both walls if I spread my arms. The bathroom was minuscule, imagine the toilets in a plane. Breakfast was just ok. The noise from the trains bothered me a bit, but it subsided at night. I recommend the Italian restaurant STRADA, which is 3 blocks from the hotel, direction the tube station.

title: Friendly and helpful staff. Great Choice while in London.
text: The Trebovir will not disappoint you. The room and hallways were clean. The location, just a 2 minute walk from the Earl Court station, was fantastic. Breakfast was very good. The best part however was the staff, especially a gentleman named Joy. He was extremely courteous and helpful and although always busy, made us feel as if we were the only guests in the hotel. The only negatives were a very small bathroom and the wifi service was not working when we were there. Highly recommended.

title: Nice central location
text: From the outside this building looks fabulous very elegant looking ..Check in was very easy, nice man on reception very helpful. ..The room was very small situated on the first floor.Bathroom was like aeroplane toilet very compact, complete with a shower ..Three beds in a small room overlooking a shed which the staff sit and have breakfast outside,smoking..not my ideal room !..Breakfast 2 slices of processed cheese.2 slices of processed ham ,3 pieces of small toast and a yogurt , Tea or coffee and small orange juice ,on the 2 days were stayed here {weekend] there were no croissants left at all..when i questioned why there were none left i was told other guests have eaten them .. and they had no more !..The breakfast staff were quite abrupt, This wasn't a cheap hotel and i thought the breakfast was rubbish for the price we paid....on a positive note its very central to everywhere ,earls courts tube station is a 3 minute walk to this hotel, you have MC Donald's KFC Nandos all within 2/3 minute walk , shops and restaurants also within close walking distance..Definitely visiting London again but wont be staying here ...

title: ok for a one or two night stay
text: Excellent location of this hotel for Heathrow travellers. Take the Picadilly line to Earls Court and then walk about 4-5 minutes from the tube station to the hotel. Very easy - even with luggage. Also great is the price - hotel is listed on most hotel budget sites. Now - rooms are very small and bathrooms are even smaller. This is a hotel where the shower is so small that you can't imagine that you'll fit inside - even with an average body size. Breakfast was (for me) a disaster - room was so tiny and filled with people that there was nowhere to sit. I went to a nearby coffee shop instead. Staff was very helpful and friendly. I stayed one night - two would be my limit for this hotel due to room size.

title: Damp and smelly
text: Disgusting hotel with outrageously rude staff. Ended up in a damp dungeon like basement room. The smell of damp hits you as soon as the lift opens even the bedding was clammy. They insist on scanning your passport and there was something very dodgy about the way my card was processed, to the extent that AMEX recommended cancellation of the card.

title: Great location, good value
text: Great location - 2 minutes walk from tube station on Piccadili line Breakfast - prety well, doesnt have too much variety. The room with single bed is very small , with very smal bath. I've heard every noise in near rooms which was pretty annoying. Staff is OK.

title: Excellent location
text: Excellent location, just around the corner from the Earl's Court Underground station, which is very convenient for the Piccadilly line if landing at Heathrow . Nice, clean, quiet hotel. Efficient staff, good breakfast, we had a room with toilet and shower, ok it was small, but we didn't expect a spa! I was travelling with a friend, but it was ideal for families as well. Very good value for money, I'd definitely stay there again if back in London.

title: Great value
text: We were very satisfied with the Trebovir Hotel. We booked here at the last minute after the Barkston Gardens Hotel cancelled our reservation the day before we were supposed to arrive. The location is excellent....about a 2 minute walk to the Earl's Court Tube stop. Earl's Court is on the Picadilly and District lines. Talking the Picadilly line directly from Heathrow to Earl's Court was extremely convenient and inexpensive. The room was basic, but clean. It was an extremely small room and small bathroom, even by European standards, but we only needed it for a place to sleep at night. We weren't in the room much other than that so the size didn't matter. There was enough space to put a suitcase down and a separate closet to hang some garments. We had a first floor room where the window faced the street. We had no problems at all with street noise. Any cars or people we heard didn't bother us. I was pleasantly surprised that our room at air conditioning. I didn't see that detail when I booked the hotel. Even though the temps were not hot at all during our visit, the room did get stuffy at night. So we used the AC and it made the room much more comfortable. I'd stay here again any time!

title: Stay at Trebovir
text: Stayed here as I like the area it’s central and in a relatively safe road in amongst some very nice residential properties. I was travelling with my daughters and we were going to the theatre. Very close to Earls Court Tube. Room was a triple with 3 single beds. Linen spotless, beds reasonable though mattress could probably do with turning each time. Room cleaned to a good standard and en-suite was spotless. Tv worked, kettle in room was clean with no lime scale inside. Sound proofing was good given the close proximity with other rooms. Hotel was unsurprisingly full. Breakfast was good only negative was we had an awkward few minutes waiting for a table with no real system for seating guests. Bit of a free for all. Continental breakfast was fresh, croissants fresh and warm. Cutlery reassuringly spotless as were the plates and the staff cleaned the tables properly with anti bacterial spray before the next guests sat down to eat. I was particularly reassured by this. Good value for money. Only downside was lift was out of action and had to struggle up 2 flights of old stairs to reach our room with luggage. Would stay here again. Compared with premier inn a lot cheaper and cleaner actually for a night in London. Get the lift sorted though!

title: Value for money
text: Though the room is smallish, overall it’s still value for money as compared to other accoms which I have tried. The place is close to the tube station and breakfast is pretty decent. Hot shower is working well. Rooms are clean

title: Rude
text: Booked (Thursday)through a popular website were no payment was needed till arrival. The hotel went to charge my card and it was declined ( not enough in there) I had an email today to say it had been cancelled. I called and it was explained that they take money beforehand. I offered to pay in full to be told the room was no longer available. The male receptionist was rude and not accommodating in anyway. We now have a few days to find a hotel!!!

title: Clean Budget Hotel in Good Location
text: Location is prefect, next street of Earl Court Exhibition center and 3 mins walk to Earl Court subway station. There are lots of hotels & B&Bs located in this street. I was been there in Apr 2010 while there was volcanic ash disaster . During my this London trip, I stayed in 3 hotels in this area, West Western The Boltons locates for 4 nights, Trebovir for 4 nights, and City Continental London Kensington for 3 nights. My personal comments : The Boltons - the best but most expensive (about GPB 150 per night during exhibition period, booking made in month in advance) . double comfort bed, nice room decoration with nice amenities in bathroom. iphone & ipad speaker available in a room, free wifi anywhere in a hotel. Full English breakfast is good enough. My room located in the top floor which is more space and quiet than my friend's room in lower floor. Trebovir - budget B&B with clean and tidy small single bed room. free wifi, comfortable bed. better than my expectation at not more than GPB50 per night (walk-in rate during volcanic ash). Breakfast is alright at this price range. Breakfast is simple and ok. City Continental - rather high price for simple setting double bed room, I have stayed here for 1 night (GBP100, booking made a month in advance) and 2 nights (GBP60 per night, walk in rate during volcanic ash) after few days later of my 1st staying. 24 hours free wifi only. smelly and rather old finishing room during my staying (in 2010). lift is available, but not every single floor. clean bathroom but with spotted. Breakfast is simple and ok.

title: Small, quiet and practical Hotel
text: The Hotel is small, reasonably clean and most important: it's quiet at least the room on the last floor I had. I didn't check the breakfast. The bath room nhad a shower and a toilet and was rather modern, I'd say less than 6 years old. They have credit card size access cards for the room, very practical. There is a 24/24 presence at the entry. Checkin was quick and easy, checkout was superfast.

title: Very Small Room close to Earl's Court Underground
text: My wife and I stayed at the Trebovir Hotel in London very near Earl's Court Underground on August 22. It was very close to the Tube stop, it is clean and well maintained and did have air conditioning, as advertised. The front desk has an attendant 24-hours. It has a small elevator.We booked it as a double bed for 2 people. We were disappointed in the following: The room was VERY small, with the comfortable bed against 2 walls, with only 2 feet next to the bed and about 3 1/2 feet at the foot. There was not room for a chair, and the TV was on the side wall, only visible if you sat crosswise on the bed at the foot and propped up against the wall. There are no telephones in the rooms. The TV stopped working, saying weak signal, after about one hour. The front desk person came and did something by manipulating the wire into the wall (which was taped). This helped. Soon it recovered and continued to work. There are only medium-small bath towels and no hand towels. The modern shower came with no instructions and was not obvious, but it worked. The bathroom is very very small, but has shower, toilet and sink. The breakfast was from 7-10, with a warning at check-in that it was quiet from 7-8, normally busy 8-9 and very noisy 9-10. We went at 7. The freshly baked rolls (3 types, quite good) were not ready until 7:35. It is a continental breakfast with a multi-function brew-by-the-cup machine. The coffee was good. We would not choose to stay there again because of the extremely small room and discomfort except when sleeping. It would be just right for one person with minimal luggage. We were two with only one large and one small bag plus carry-on bags, and it was tight. It is expensive for its size. Lee Kohlenberg

title: Value for money hotel in a great location
text: Stayed here for one night. What I liked most about this hotel was its location. It is very near to Earl's court metro station (which has elevators - so no worries about baggage!), from which you have easy and cheap access to London Heathrow Airport (This metro station is on the Piccadilly line and since it's just outside the busiest sections of Piccadilly line, you dont have to bother much about carrying your luggage in metro - something which I consider as important!). Most tourist parts of the city are also easily accessible by metro or bus. The famous natural history museum can also be reached by foot. There are also many fast food restaurants nearby. Though small, my room was comfortable (in spite of the fact that my room was in the basement!) and had a reasonably comfortable bed. Both the room and the attached toilet were also very clean. Breakfast was also okay, though not excellent. They also have luggage storage, which I could use on the check out day. I must also mention the negatives: There was a strange smell of pesticide in the corridors (but no smell inside the rooms!). To avoid people taking key outside, they have put long and heavy threads as key chains. It was very uncomfortable and strange to carry that to breakfast halls. If loosing keys are the concern, the proprietors could easily address that problem by shifting to electronic entry modes. In spite of the minor negative aspects mentioned above, I will say that for the price I paid, it was a value for money deal and I would certainly consider it for my future stays also.

title: Very Good
text: All are good, but only very thin wall (you can listening all what your neigbor is doing) and the bathroom in single room is very very small.

title: A Hidden Gem
text: This was my second stay. It was still a nice experience. The location is hard to beat. I used the Piccadilly Line Tube (subway) from the Heathrow Airport one-way ticket cost only 5.5 pounds to get to the hotel. The hotel is only 100 meters away from the Earl Courts tube station. There are a few supermarkets including Marks & Spencer in the area. The bed room was not very big but the size is reasonable for the price. Hot shower was great and the air conditioner/heater worked ok. Wifi in my room was fast. Staff was very friendly and helpful. On my first day the heater and the wifi did not work properly. The staff responded to my request very quickly and fixed the problem promptly. Breakfast was ok. It comprises ham, cheese, toast croissant, jam, cereals milk, tea , coffee. I have stayed in other hotels in London during my other visits. I found this Trebovir Hotel decent and best value for money. It is a hidden gem.

title: Convenient, clean and cosy but some issue with noise...
text: Right round the corner from Earl's Court Stn. on the Piccadilly Line (with lifts) to Heathrow - couldn't be better located at a reasonable price. Room was cosy and very clean, especially the bathroom, and strong, silent air-conditioning, being recently renovated. Was worried about noise from trains but no problem there - instead it had rather porous walls common with most 3-star re-modelled terrace apts-turned-hotel, in London - and my luck to have chatty neighbours who return back late or a father whose rapping on the door, to get his family up at 5.30am 3 straight mornings, felt like a fire alarm in my room - he did apologise and eventually found alternative way(s) to get his family up... BTW, staff were friendly and accommodating.

title: Really small, bad experience with left items.
text: The room was small, but I expected that from other reviews. The bed was narrower than I expected--apparently 'single' means 30 inches (a twin is usually about 36). The module bathroom is a good idea but too small (I have had rooms with them before where the size was fine). I could not use the shower--I did a rough measurement and it seemed about 30 inches long and less than 20 inches at its widest point. I'm 25 inches from elbow to elbow, so could not turn around. I think any man average size or larger would have the same problem. I was running late when I left but snapped a photo as I was going out the door to show my friends the size of the room. Later that day I discovered I was missing a hat and a small bag of clothes that I apparently left behind. I called the hotel and was assured nothing was in the room, but when I later looked at my photo the bag was in plain view on the bed. I called back again and was again told nothing was turned in by the housekeeping staff. I found this a bit disturbing.

title: Clean & Comfortable
text: I looked at the reviews before booking this hotel so there were no surprises. The bathroom was super small but the shower was hot and the pressure was good so I have no complaints. The hotel had been renovated a few years ago so wasn't tired looking. The beds were very comfortable. We were on the front of the hotel so we could look down the street.It made the room feel larger. Staff seemed nice. We really didn't need anything one we got our room. I would definitely recommend. I would like to mention that Pret a Manger is a great place for soup & sandwiches. Think we had lunch everyday at one.

title: Great Value
text: Room was spacious. Shower was hot. The price seemed right $226 USD which is in line with most hotels in the area. Free Internet and boy is it fast, 60x90 which is very nice for business travelers! We enjoyed the bar at boys in the lobby.

title: By far the worst hotel I have ever seen
text: Small, dirty rooms, small toilet, no safety locks, awful service at the reception desk. The only polite people were in the breakfast room. I want to forget it as soon as possible. Friend was given room in Lower ground. That was even a bigger nightmare. All night she heard the elevator announcement (you are on the lower ground floor, or so). Room smelled like petrol, bugs, unclean. Just try to avoid this one. The only positive thing was the location. Do not be fooled by the website pics and the front of the hotel. Just awful.

title: Nice and well-situated
text: This hotel is just a few steps from Earl's Court station, where you can move to everywhere in London using Piccadilly or District Line. The room was small but comfortable, the bathroom was clean and breakfast is adequate. Just a bit too much dust in the room, if you could work on this, your future customers would appreciate. Nonetheless, I would choose the hotel if I were to visit London in the future.

title: Location, location, location
text: Good hotel in an Excellent location, very reasonably priced. Pros: Location, free internet (not wireless) Cons: Small rooms (but normal for the city), service, breakfast, hvac This is a really good hotel, especially for the money. It's less than a 2 minute walk to the Earl's Court Underground station, shops, restaurants, and pubs. The rooms were really small (the bathrooms are sort of cool - they look like some kind of prefab pod, maybe you'd see it in a stateroom on a ship) but very clean. We were a group and people in rooms on the non-street side of the hotel had heat they couldn't turn off. The rooms on the street side couldn't get any heat at all. Luckily the weather was moderate during our stay and the duvets worked out well for sleeping pretty comfortably. The only issues we had were that if something was wrong (heat, missing towels, hair dryer) calling and asking for assistance got you nowhere. But, if you went down to the desk and asked for something you could always get it. Also, the included breakfast didn't work out very well for us. At the times we could go there was always a large line and we didn't want to spend the prime morning time waiting for a lackluster meal. It wasn't bad, just nothing to write home about or stand in line for, and it's funny that in a country where we had more excellent pork products in a week than we've had in months at home the breakfast included sliced lunchmeat style ham. Not huge issues and all in all we had a very nice time. I'd definitely consider staying here again.

title: Basic but nice hotel!
text: The hotel itself is not bad but it is expensive for what it is (Maybe It's London). Very small rooms, small beds, regular breakfast with ham and cheese toast, coffee and orange juice with some french viennoiseries and Yogurt, there is cereal as well. The location is perfect near earl's court undeground station and there are many restaurants, pubs and snacks nearby. 24h reception and you need to leave the keys at the front desk. The keys are chained to a huge thing which is inconvenient. The staff are nice and helpfull. I stayed in similar hotels in other european countries and the prices were a lot cheaper (I think it's London and the high season). I would stay again in this hotel as you don't have many other choices with similar price.

title: Warm Hotel!
text: Trebovir Hotel is a Warm Hotel, Ubicated in a Good Zone in London... The Rooms are Really Comfortable... I Recommend It!

title: Ideal Location, Affordable
text: During a recent trip to London, I stayed for 3 nights at the Trebovir. I was pleased with my choice. The location is fantastic with the Earl's Court tube station around the corner and many restaurants/pubs and shopping so close. The rooms are small, but if your main goal is sightseeing, then the room offers exactly what you need in terms of a comfortable bed, cleanliness, and hot shower. I opted for a double room which was decent for 1 person, especially if coming from the American perspective of being used to more space in a hotel room. The tiny bathrooms may be a challenge for a very tall or heavier weight person but was fine for me being a shorter and smaller frame. The staff was decent and helpful when I asked any questions. The on-site included continental breakfast was adequate to start the day, but if you want a more substantial breakfast, you should go elsewhere. Also, they have a luggage storage room, which is handy if you arrive before check-in or need to leave your luggage for a bit after you checkout. The room prices were affordable. Overall, it was a decent stay.

title: centrally located clean and modern
text: Great location.takes only tube for GBP 1.70 with oyster card to arrive from LHR. Rooms are small but efficiently furnished and clean. Personal very helpful.storage of luggage free after checkout (other economic hotels do charge these days) tube around corner plenty of coffee shops and restaurants as well. My favourite in London!

title: This is a better hotel than my rating suggests
text: Why do we still in Britain undervalue the importance of good service? It's said that what happens in the U.S.A. eventually filters its way across the Atlantic. For example, no-win no-fee damages claims). However, 'great customer service' has been a long time coming although I don't deny that many businesses have realised its importance. On arrival at the the hotel at 17:45 the reception was unattended. I waited for 5 minutes and then rang the front door-bell. Nothing! I them phoned the hotel. The phone on the reception desk rang but no one came to answer it. By this time, another would-be guest had arrived and repeated my attempts at summoning some attention. Four more people then arrived and we all waited for the appearance of a receptionist. Eventually, sometime just after 6:00 a young man appeared and asked if we'd like to check in. Hmmm. I could have been sarcastic and suggested that we were all standing there to improve our health but I resisted the temptation to do so. What ever happened to: "I am very sorry to have kept you waiting". So easy to say. It costs nothing and it immediately relieves the tension that a frustrated guest would have been feeling. But no, not even a smile or some welcoming words but a perfunctory check-in service. I'll accept that this was a one-off but I cannot or will not give more than two stars to any hotel, even a 5 star hotel, which keeps me waiting for 15-20 minutes to check-in. As for the hotel: it is part of the same group of hotels as the Coronation Hotel (which I have also reviewed). The rooms are on the small side. Once again I was allocated a lower-ground-floor room. It was clean, comfortably furnished and painted in dark pastel colours. The TV was on the small side - okay it was tiny - and the bathroom was of the modular type and even my small size had trouble maneuvering in the confined space. Breakfast, as with the Coronation Hotel, consisted of a soggy warm croissant, a slice of cheese and meat product pretending to be ham. I declined this although the waitress tried to insist that I should indulge in its dubious culinary delights. She also poured me coffee when I had asked for tea. But no matter, these minor problems can be successfully negotiated and I managed to breakfast adequately on muesli, fruit juice,tea and toast. This hotel is okay for a short stay and my visit was tainted only by the lack of customer service. I paid £65 for the room which I think is slightly too much but not extortionate.

title: clean and nice
text: we stayed at the trebovir for one week. the room and bathroom were very clean, they changed towels every day. breakfast was good, with coffee, tea, milk, cereals, yogurt, croissant, butter, jam, toast, ham and cheese. the hotel is less than 5 minutes walk from tube station. room and bathroom were very small but we had no problem at all (btw, imho you can't find big rooms in london unless you're going to unreasonable expensive hotels). I'm definitely going there again!

title: Good location and helpful staff
text: I liked my stay there and think it is good value for the price I paid. The staff was very helpful but could have smiled more. The breakfast was good. Small room but I do not mind I just needed room to sleep in. The location is very good as the underground is just around the corner 4 minutes walking. I think I have never walked through so many doors in as little space as in this hotel, 7 doors to my room and it was 50 steps away from the front door of the hotel. But nice stay, good location and helpful staff. Thank you

title: Room got burglarized
text: Stayed here for 2 nights before my room was broken into. They said this has happened before and honestly I don’t see how it hasn’t happened more. They don’t protect the building. You should have people show you their key cards when entering. The policeman showed up hours after I had left and supposedly the cameras “weren’t working” but my room was the only one broken into. Manager wasn’t very cooperative or sympathetic to my situation. Staying here would be a mistake. I would advise against it. I almost feel like it was an inside job

title: Small and loud
text: The room 312 was so small you couldn't but your luggage down anywhere. You had no place to put the contents of your luggage either. There wasn't a chair in the room to sit on. We had stayed there 4 nights before our cruise and had to move from room 404 to room 403 as room 404's ceiling made it so you couldn't stand up. We were guaranteed room 403 on our return. They did not keep their promise and gave us room 312 which was horrible. There was a party next to us that went on until 2am and the hotel didn't do a thing about it. People were stopping in the streets and taking pictures of the party as it was so loud. The following morning Mark the owner/manager said he hadn't heard anything about the party or any problems from Edwin the employee working that previous night. We concluded Mark's way of refusing to accept responsibility was to deny he knew anything about it. I believe Edwin did tell Mark as Edwin told me when I had complained that evening after 11pm about the party other guests had complained as well. Hector another employee was wonderful to work with. Our advice: spend a few extra bucks and get a room you can move in, set your luggage down in and have a chair to sit on. Any hotel that allows their neighbors to have loud parties and keeps theirs guests up until 2am doesn't care at all about their guests. You get a hotel room for sleep not to be kept up until 2am.

title: Comfort, convenience and value for money
text: This hotel has been fully renovated and is a great place to stay. The day manager was exceptionally friendly and helpful. My stay at the hotel was broken by some time in Paris On my return I was welcomed back like an old friend. It was my first trip to London and he was always very happy to give me really useful advice in relation to getting to various destinations in and out of London. It is so close to the tube station that getting around London was quick and easy. Make sure you get an Oyster card at Heathrow if you are coming to London by air and hop onto the tube which will take you straight to your hotel which is just around the corner. Couldn't be easier. On Earls Court road (just around the corner) there are plenty of shops, a laundry, post office, grocery shops, restaurants, fast food and takeaways - everything you need. The room I had for the first part of my stay was on the first floor and overlooked the Earls Court tube station. I did not find that a problem. The noise of the trains was no more than a low rumble occasionally. I certainly didn't find it disturbing or lose any sleep. When I returned from Paris I was allocated a ground floor room facing the street which was a little more noisy with the sound of people talking as they passed the building. The only thing I would criticise would be the breakfast. Stick to the toast, cereal, juice and coffee. Give the croissant, ham and cheese a miss - it is served on a plate that is straight from the fridge and the croissant is stale and cold. For some people the bathroom may prove a challenge because of the size. It was fine for me (I am on five foot) but I think taller people may find it a bit cramped. If I am in London again the Trebovir will be my hotel of choice.

title: Small room but decent value
text: Stayed for 2 nights: Pros Excellent location very close to earls Court and access to the picadilly line to Heathrow Clean rooms Polite and professional staff Good value for money Cons: The room we had was very small - looks like the original rooms have been partitioned off although we did have a small window Bathroom was one of those plastic all in ones similar to what you find in easy hotels. Very small but everything worked and shower pressure was good. Breakfast was fairly simple Overall I would recommend this for budget travellers and I would stay here again

title: Nice hotel
text: 4 nights in this hotel and I recomend. Metro station on the corner with Earl's Court Road. Very quited because even with Earl's Court road near, the Trobovir Road is quited. Very clean and a nice breakfast. Modern WC and room forniture. For London is a good quality/location/price hotel.

title: Never Again...Highly Not Recommended
text: I stayed at the Trebovir Hotel for three nights during a recent business trip to London. What a disaster. I arrived at the hotel at 11:15pm to check in. After chugging up a large suitcase, hand luggage and a briefcase I tried to enter the hotel attempting to get through the door with my luggage. There were two staff members standing at the front desk watching me. They made no attempt to assist me by holding the door open. The check in was quick, as the room had already been prepaid. There as no “welcome to the hotel”. Just a “can I have your passport”. This was not followed by a please or thank you, or a “enjoy your stay”. I was allocated Room 202 on the 2nd floor. If you decide to stay in this hotel ask for a room very far from the elevator. For three nights all I heard was the very loud voice coming from the elevator announcing the floor number and to stay back as the doors are closing. Upon entering the room I was confronted with a tiny room and a single bed. There is no desk in the room to work on, so I was forced to kneel on the floor working on the bed. There is a chair and a very small wardrobe. So with luggage in the room you are not left with much space. When I entered the bathroom I was shocked to see this tiny place they call a bathroom. The bathrooms were obviously added as a late addition. The basin is tiny and there is hardly any space to place your toiletries. The shower is a joke and you can just stand in the shower. It is impossible to move in the shower. It has a flimsy curtain and the entire bathroom is flooded after a shower. The worst part was opening the toilet. I was shocked to see what I found inside. I leave the rest to the reader’s imagination. I found the same thing when I returned the next night. I am not sure if the hotel has a back flush problem with the toilet water system. After flushing the toilet it runs water the entire night. The walls are made of thin cardboard, needless to say, you can hear the neighbours coughing, sneezing, talking on the phone as well as people returning to their rooms very late at night walking down the corridor. At least the bedroom was reasonably clean. The mattress is very soft, although the pillows are relatively comfortable. Breakfast is served in the breakfast room in the basement and is only open between 7:00 to 09:00 weekdays. This is ridiculous especially if don’t want to get up so early as you did not have a good night’s sleep. The room is very small. Upon entering there is nobody to welcome or greet you. The room is packed and you are forced to sit at tables with strangers. The breakfast is very basic and nothing fantastic. The hotel claims to have free Wi-Fi, although the Internet works intermittently. On one night I needed to send urgent emails at 01:00am and the Internet was not working. When I went down to the front desk to complain, the night porter told me it’s working as he has Internet on his iPhone. I did not find this very helpful or the solution I was looking for, as I needed to send emails on my laptop and not on the night porter’s iPhone. And considering the prices this so called three-star hotel charges, it was certainly not the money’s worth. In fact I was booked into the same hotel on my next trip to London next week and I have cancelled my booking and booked another hotel. On a last note the hotel’s website says it offers a “Hospitality tray”. Not sure what this means but there was no tray in the room. The rates advertised on their website are not actually a true reflection of what they actually charge. Definitely a very disappointing hotel and stay!

title: Convenient location
text: Within short walking distance of Earls Court tube station and exhibition centre. All room are newly refurbished, with flat screen TV and freeview channels. Shower room was very small. Continental breakfast was OK.

title: Handy for Underground, close to City centre.
text: Excellet hotel,nice room which was clean and tidy on arrival. As I arrived by Public Transport Im not sure if theres any car park for this hotel. Breakfast was nice, continental style with plenty of choice. Very helpful and friendly staff. A really nice experience and I will be back there soon so I recomend the Trebovir Hotel.

title: London Excursion
text: Hotel location is excellent. From Victoria station it's approx. 15 mins to the hotel. We took a taxi from the station to the hotel and paid 12 Pounds. Also, the subway, Earl's Court is 5 minutes away. Hotel staff is friendly, helpful and when asked will provide great suggestions. We stayed in the Family Room, small room, but hardly noticed it because it was clean and well maintained. Also, breakfast is good...

title: Acceptable, nothing glamorous
text: I have stayed for 4 nights there with a husband. 4 nights is too long, for such a small space, to stay. 1 or 2 nights would be just OK. The best is its position, very near Earl's court tube station. That is ideal if you are in hurry and have lots of things to do during the day. The room is small, but the so called bathroom is so tiny that the person hardly can turn around. The price is acceptable, the stuff very friendly.

title: Great location, clean and efficiently run
text: Great location, near Earls Court and Underground with direct line to Heathrow. All arrangements and requests courteously and efficiently handled. Hotel in good condition and very well maintained. Room size was tight and bathroom tiny, but adequately equipped and in excellent condition. Breakfast room busy and breakfast just adequate. Left luggage was very useful.

title: Good quality / price ratio
text: This Hotel is placed very close to Earls Court Underground station, and It's very close to pub, market and MacDonald's. It's clean, with daily change of towels. Bathroom is in the room, but it's small, bed is comfortable. Breakfast is not english breakfast, but it's a continental breakfast, with coffee, tea, marmelade, croissant, bread, ham and cheese. There isn't a buffet for breakfast, but the waiter asks you what you want. The receptionists are quite nice and friendly. It's a good choice for a 3-4 days holidays.

title: Great Location – But . .
text: The hotel is a few hundred metres from the Earls Court station. But the rooms are small with even smaller shower / toilet. The room we had certainly could do with a new bed (which was up against the wall on one side). Breakfast was fine. Overall, was not impressed.

title: For people on a budget
text: I choose this hotel based on other reviews I read on Trip Advisor. When we arrived at the hotel we were given a room at the lower ground, which scared us a bit, because we imagined that it would be dark. We were relieved to find that the room was not that bad at all. We asked at the front desk if there was another room available, they said that probably on the following days we could move to another room, but we got used to it and never changed. Actually, having a room on the lower ground had its advantages: it was closer to the breakfast room and to toilets we could use. They asked us if we wanted to pay for all the nights we had booked when we arrived and hadn't even unpacked, but we chose to pay only at the end of our stay. I found this attitude a bit unpleasant. We booked a twin room, but the room we stayed in looked like a single room where another bed was added. This other bed was simply not as comfortable as the "main" bed. I found the place very clean and the staff polite. Near the hotel you have the Earl's Court station that can take you directly to the main attractions in London, without having to change lines. Yes, you can hear noise from the trains at the hotel, so if you are easily disturbed by this, don't stay there. For me it was a bit of a problem because I could only rest when the trains stopped (half past midnight), but for the other person that I travelled with this was not an issue at all. The toilets are very small... I managed to use the shower, even though I am above my ideal weight. Perhaps the toilet is the most negative point on this hotel. The area is safe and full of tourists. You have several restaurants on the main street and also supermarkets for all your needs. If you want to avoid the line at the breakfast room arrive there before 8:20. When we were leaving for our day out in London, we noticed that it was around this time that a line began to form.

title: Great
text: Great value hotel in a great location, this hotel is spotlessly clean and would stay again! Staff friendly and free breakfast great even if it was slightly hetic. Hard to fond good value acomodation in london but this is a hidden gem !

title: DON'T TRUST THEM - I DON'T!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
text: I booked my stay with Trevidor on the the 25th of April with my Cheque card. When I arrived the next day to book in they asked me how I was going to pay even after my confirmation. I said I had already paid and they said NO, it's only pre-authorization and that my money would be paid back after 10 working days. I paid AGAIN in CASH - 388 British Sterling Pounds. I stayed 7 nights and 8 days and it is now exactly 12 working days after I have paid on my cheque account and they tell me I have to speak to my bank!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! My bank has advised me to get the money from Trevidor and now they do not even get BACK to me!!!! They just keep on telling me to speak to my bank!!!!!! I believe it is fraud as I have read on tripadisor that other hotels do the same!!!!! WHAT NOW - NEARLY R5000-00 GONE!!!!!

title: Clean, comfortable and convieniently located
text: Being situated 2 minutes walk from Earls Court underground station makes this a winner however, it is somewhat compact, I booked a double room and when we arrived my wife and I were allocated a room on the lower ground floor (basement), as a double it was small to say the least, if it was for a single occupancy it would have been fine, but for 2 normal sized people it was far too small, the shower cubical was almost impossible to shower in with any degree of comfort. The tea and coffee making facilities were on a specialist shelf screwed to the wall in such a way as to render it again almost impossible to use with ease and as for the quoted "generous" breakfast enough said really (2 slices of "ham" 2 of cheese 1 piece of toast and 1 croissant plus tea or coffee 1 cup). Having said all this the room was air conditioned, clean and warm. The bed was old but reasonably comfortable and the room was serviced to a good standard. The reception staff were polite and courteous and as we needed extra towels helpful as were the staff serving breakfast, at a push I would stay there again if I couldn't find somewhere else of a similar price, solely because of the location and a very nice restaurant within easy walking distance for breakfast.

title: Customer service leaves much to be desired
text: Stayed in this hotel 21-23 January. The room was small but did not expect much more for the price we were paying for it. The room was clean and the bed made for a comfortable night's sleep. The main issue we had during our stay was with breakfast on the second morning. Having been told on our arrival that breakfast was from 8-10am, we headed down to breakfast at 9.40am, only to find that the breakfast room was closed. We found this quite confusing and headed straight to the reception desk to ask the receptionist on duty about this. He then informed us that breakfast on the weekdays was between 7-9am. We then told him that this was not what we were told at check in. He then proceeded to inform us that all the staff are instructed to inform guests of breakfast times. We argued that this was not the case and while I can accept that it was possible that the receptionist on duty might have overlooked that fact that we were staying 2 nights and not 1 and had failed to inform us of the breakfast time for the second morning of our stay, the receptionist we were dealing with handled the situation very poorly. He said there was nothing that he could do, no amount of refund nor vouchers for breakfast at any of the nearby cafes could be offered. Obviously, it is very disappointing to hear such a response and we pressed him for an acceptable resolution. His response did not change. Finally, I suggested that he send one of the other staff down to put out some breakfast cereal and toast for us, and he said "why didn't you ask for that in the first place, if you only had asked nicely I would have done that straight away" I found this response to be quite rude and insulting. He claimed to be the manager on duty at the time, but could not have come up with solution himself, instead throwing up his hands and saying that there was nothing he could do. Customer satisfaction should be a priority for anyone in the hotel business, and in his position, he had a duty to resolve this issue, and not leave it up to the customers to suggest it themselves. As a final note, while I was happy with the quality of accommodation, all things considered, perhaps a more time and resources should be spent on training all the hotel staff in providing quality customer service.

title: Small but value for money
text: This is a small "budget" hotel that is well located, clean and comfortable. I had one of the attic rooms that was perfect for an overnight stay. A good deal, especially in central London.

title: Cold Staff
text: Hotel is good by location, by cleanliness but just too cold behaviour of staff, not at all friendly, all of them working there as if they are forced to do that and do not enjoy their work, horrible staff, horrible breakfast.

title: The Trebovir experience
text: Arrived from a long trip and were not able to get room until later in the afternoon. The hotel is well situated and easy access from Heathrow. Safe and very nice neighbourhood. Call ahead to book room and floor. When you arrive you might have some surprises.

title: It's cheap, location is good, but it's not a find.
text: This hotel is in a great location to get to and from LHR on the Picadilly Line. The tube stop is Earl's Court which is equipped with elevators and ramps, making it loads easier to deal with luggage (not all tube stops are this convenient). The hotel is very inexpensive and it has WIFI that worked most of the time. I found the hotel staff to be cheerful and accommodating - I didn't bother with the breakfast as there are a tremendous amount of cafes about that will most certainly be better than whatever a hotel chooses to serve. If you are on a business trip and really only need a place to sleep, then this is a decent choice. Or if you are on a tight budget holiday and can put up with the challenges of a cheap hotel, then you might be fine here. However, if you are on vacation and want to be pampered then you best give this one a pass and spend more money. The negatives were: - No safe in the room and the key must be left at the front desk. I didn't have an issue at all but I never really like these arrangements. - The shower curtain was pink with mildew which made the whole room smell musty. - The bathroom was comparable to one on a sleeper train. Just enough room for one person, no way that two could use it at the same time. - The building is a converted period home and my guess is that all of the rooms were as small as mine. There were twin beds in mine but again, two people in my room would have been a nightmare. The second bed served as an excellent spot for my luggage. - There is a nightclub right up the street and so people returning to their cars at 3am are VERY loud. Bring earplugs if you stay here. I stay in London alot and while this was fine, I probably won't rebook. There are too many other choices that might do things better. The search for "the find" continues.

title: Overpriced budget hotel, great location
text: Had I paid £80-£90 for my stay I think I would have thought the whole experience was fair for Central London location, but sadly I booked the day before & paid £144, for which I expect a certain level of product/service. Whilst the 'Grand' Hotel does have a fantastic location and in fairness it does look quite grand from the street, just around the corner from Earl's Court station, the room was not what I would describe as a 'deluxe' double (I stayed in room 408). Unless deluxe is a nice way of saying bog standard. It was a very compact room with two single beds pushed together up against one wall without a headboard, and a beaten up futon in the corner. The room could definitely benefit from double glazing as was quite noisy too, plus in the evening I could hear pipes in the walls gurgling and others guests' doors being slammed. People had obviously been smoking in the room previously (or in nearby rooms) as I could smell it every time I re-entered the room and there were fag buts just outside the window, which was quite unpleasant. I was staying on business so the fact there was free wifi was great, however, it didn't work in my room, which meant I had to use my phone as a personal hotspot. Not what I expected. Overall the room was clean enough but could certainly have been better. It's a fairly minor point, but the TV was the size of a microwave and it might have been better not to have one at all and invest the money in a light fitting about the bed that actually works (mine didn't)! The continental breakfast would have been fine if I was in a cheap hotel on the continent - two squares of cold cheese and cheap ham with white toast (it would have been nice to have been given an option here as I'm actually vegetarian and tend not to eat white bread). There was also luke-warm yoghurt pots already on the table, an OJ dispenser, range of average-looking pastries and the choice between plain oats or cornflakes. I think this was quite disappointing, again considering the price I paid. Receptionist was very friendly and gave me a good impression before I went further into the hotel but sadly, the waiting staff spoke very poor English and just repeated 'cheese, ham and toast' to every customer in the breakfast room, which felt a bit robotic for first thing in the morning. The room keys and hilarious - massive curtain tie style jobbies, that mean you have to leave them at reception everyone you want to pop out. Very dated, simple changes could make this is better hotel and more enjoyable stay for guests (starting with a bin in the bathroom!)

title: Good hotel with perfect location
text: The Trebovir is just around the cornor from Earl's Court Tube station, with several good restaurants and a post office in the vicinity. Yes, the room is small and the bathroom, too, but perfectly OK. The beds are comfortable, with the luxury of two pillows each. The continental berakfast is not only tea and toast, but also yoghurt, ham and cheese. The breakfast room is small, but if you arrive around 8 o'clock instead of 8.30 there is likely to be free seat. Staff is very fiendly and efficient.

title: Ideal for transit passengers to Heathrow.
text: We were in transit to catch a flight the following morning. Situated near Earls Court Railway it was easy with our suitcases to catch the tube to Earls Court and walk just round the corner from the Station. The hotel was cheap for London and although very small bedroom with a capsule for bathroom/toilet it wa sOK forf 1 night stay.

title: Small and expensive
text: Let us start with the positives.. Good location very close to Earl's Court tube station and good customer service. And now for the bad.. The room was the size of Harry Potter's room under the stairs. However, we did complain and were upgraded to a larger cupboard (the larger cupboard did have a standard bathroom compared to the spacesaver bathrooms). Breakfast was great if you like cold pieces of toast cut up for you + room temperature yoghurt and week old ham and cheese. In addition, each day is an adventure to find the front door through the maze of doors (you can get lost). Overall very expensive for a small and very average room with no additional services or facilities.

title: So convenient, so noisy..
text: At the mouth of Earl's Court Underground Station, lies this jewel, on calm street to the left.The room is not big, but very practical, with integrated furniture, and good products in the bathroom. The staff seems to be Croatian, very kind, but too noisy: the ladies walk strongly, and slam doors, after cleaning the rooms. Upper classes of Rio de Janeiro hate noise. The elevator is awesome, a gift in a small hotel.

title: Good Value, Clean
text: I stayed here for one night in September on my way up to Edinburgh. I had a single room with a bathroom. The room was small but very clean. The bed was comfortable. Restroom small, but clean, newly modern and appointed well. The shower door handle was broken though, not really all that important though. My only complaint room wise was that the wireless signal was difficult to receive in the room. I had to go to the cafe down the street to print out my flight reservations. Complimentary breakfast was good. Desk staff courteous. Air conditioning worked well. I found the key policy a bit strange though. It is in a great location for food and night life. Tourist attractions a short tube ride away. I would certainly stay here again.

title: good value for money
text: A very nice and clean hotel. The rooms are a little bit small, but nice and clean. We book this hotel on a late booking and it was a very good deal. It's 2 minutes away from the tube on a quiet street. Sheets and towels were changed daily, good breakfast. Overall, a very good choice, saved us money and time (just 4 stations on District line from Victoria). Recommended!

title: Superb Location, Nice Staff & Clean!
text: I stayed there one night and I was quite happy with almost everything. The location of the hotel is fantastic ... a few minutes walk from Earl's Court Station. Every member of the hotel I met was pleasant and helpful. The hotel was clean and my room was spotless. The breakfast was simple, but tasty enough. My only negative comment would be concerning the washroom in my room. It was speckless, but it wasn't much larger than one found in an airplane. I literally have bruises on my arm from bumping into its walls. Overall, I enjoyed thoroughly staying at the Trebovir Hotel.

title: We stayed here two weeks ago. Pros were...
text: We stayed here two weeks ago. Pros were that it had a good breakfast included and was very near the metro station... The staff were helpful and friendly and the street was quite charming. Cons were that the rooms were super small and super basic. The location was not ideal for seeing the sights but being so close to the metro made it okay. I would reccomend as a place to crash on a budget...

title: My worst hotel experience ever
text: I made this booking for a twin room in good faith based on the hotel website and information found via the Hotels link on the hotel website that I reached via Norwegian airlines. The experience however turned out to be so bad that I need to share it to help other unwary travelers. I have written to the hotel and they have not even responded. I was booked the 13-15 of June, two nights, non refundable, at this hotel. On walking into a dingy lobby that looked nothing like the picture on the hotel website I was given a room down a filty corridor with open doors to dirty toilets and reeking of cigarette smoke. I was almost vomiting by the time I got to the room, which looked nothing like the picture advertised. The room was down below the main street level, a window showed a dirty stained wall half a metre away and the carpets and sheets looked so unwashed and dingy that I could not bring myself to sit down. The room itself was a little hole in terms of size. It was NOTHING like the descriptions given by the hotel. I walked out of the room and returned the room key to the clerk at the front desk and asked for a refund which he could not give, he said the manager must be sent an email. I simply walked out of the hotel and booked and stayed instead at the Ibis London, thus paying another 350 pounds on top of the 200 pounds I had already paid via the Norwegian website. I have still not gotten my money back or any response whatever from the hotel. Terrible.

title: The best
text: I come from Egypt and I am really I have good time here in London hotel so nice and staff so good and I will comeback here again thanks for every one to look after 100%very good and give me big welcome and room very clean and food nice inshallah wish for them all the best

title: Poor value, poor sleep
text: Basement room was small, with access on one side of double bed only - awkward for a pensioner. Sleep disturbed during early hours by employees moving wood and stuff around outside bedroom window and chatting. Bright light also outside window shining in. It was a hot night and had to close window to shut out noise and allow for curtain to be drawn. Disturbed again early next morning by cleaner running water and mopping outside window. Price was very high as during Chelsea Flower Show period, Twice the normal price. Breakfast was minimal - one slice each of cheese and ham and some toast and coffee/tea. No hot food offered. Coffee served at table but then had to carry full cup to other side of room to use milk jug. Toilet fittings in bathroom missing so flushing was problematic. Overall very disappointing and poor value.

title: Poor value for money
text: Tiny room in a basement a double bed in a single room accessible from only one side not useful when you are pensioners. . Staff talking and moving stuff outside window after midnight and in the morning staff filling buckets of water and mopping at 7 in the morning. had to keep window shut so very hot and little sleep. Toilet flush mechanism incomplete push panel missing had to poke finger in innards to flush toilet. television remote didnt work , thats not a major issue but added to everything else was frustrating. Breakfast was very very limited. Considering what it cost overall it was poor value for money.

title: like a crew cabin on cruise ship
text: I don't know where all the good reviews I read stayed but WOW. Worst bed ever. Single room is 5ftX12, including the toilet/shower cubicle (don't even think about having a shower if you're overweight, you won't fit). If you have ever seen a crew cabin on a cruise ship, you've seen this room, except the bed here was even worse. No TV remote. Trains right outside the window. Clean, though, and staff were pleasant.

title: great location
text: Great location took train right from airport. Great central location to all sites. Hotel was clean staff was nice. Awesome city easy to get around! Got to see all sites easily by train. Neighborhood has lots of good restaurants.

title: Great staff-tin rooms
text: I visited the Trebovir hotel during Easter,and all in all it was a good experience. To be honest,the rooms were indeed tiny,especially the bathroom,the breakfast was the worst Ive ever had,but what I loved was the staff-so much fun,well trained and very helpful! I don't think I'd visit again,since it was too expensive for what it has to offer,but the location is perfect,and many congrats to the staff! Free internet was a plus!

title: Great hotel
text: This year was my second time in this hotel. First the location is the best. 2 minuts walk from earlscourt train station. Second you can find every thing you need around the hotel like restaurants,supermarket. Third the service is great the stuff are very kind. Hotel is very clean.

title: a great little find
text: Stayed for two nights and was happy with the room. It was on the lower ground and it was very quiet. I read previous reviews where people complained about the noise from the underground, I have to say I was not disturbed by it at all, it was just a low rumble now and again, nothing that could keep you awake at night (tubes stop at 12 or so anyway). The enuite, was rather small, had to wash my body in two halves, left and right, but it was no real chore. Towels were clean and smelled fresh. The tea/coffee making facilities were slightly less then adequate, I always go prepared to make my own coffee but having the kettle in the room was a bonus. The TV, was a bit strange. had freeview but couldnt get the usual BBC/ITV programmes but not really bothered as we were out most of the time. The air con worked just fine. There is internet in the room, we didnt use it but the information says it requires a £5 refundable deposit, it made no mention if there was any other charge for it. The bed linen was clean and fresh, pillows were comfortabe and so was the bed, if rather squeaky. The staff, very pleasant, but had very little to do with them. Now to get to the breakfast, complimentary? no, there is no such thing as complimentary, we all know that. We only had breakfast there the one day, as the second day we didnt bother. It was the weirdest process ever, we went in for breakfast, no clean tables, which was fine as it was very busy and a small resaurtant. We cleared a table and sat down, ignored by staff, but when another couple came into the restaurant, a table was cleared immediately for them and breakfast, such as it was, was brought to them immediately. I am not picky, so waited a few minutes for the waiter to come to us. They did eventually, and brought us tea/coffee and ham and cheese and toast, not bad I thought, but looked over at the other couple and they had cereal, toast, croissants, ham, cheese and yoghurt being brought to them. When i looked around, others had the cereal and croissants, so i asked for croissants, i was brought one, rather stale one. So the breakfast is a bit of a mystery. The second day, we didnt bother to go for breakfast we were checking out anyway. The area is great, the hotel, is just 2 minutes walk from Earls Court Station, when you come out on Earls Court Road, turn left and the road the hotel is on is the first left. loads of places to eat and drink, Mcdonalds, KFC , Nando's, pubs, even a supermarket and a post office. A great central place to stay in london and dont forget to get your oyster card for travelling.

title: Perfect location!
text: After reading some bads reviews before going there... I was kind of scared of what I would find once there. But I was surprised by the hotel. My room wasn't as small as I thought. Yes it's not big, but it's big enough to get sleep, eat, and take a shower. The bathroom isn't big but it's enought for what you need. This isn't a 5 stars hotel people, but it's was ok for a 3 stars. As for the breakfeast, there's not much choices but enough to get your day starting. And if you're sick of it, there's plenty restaurant in the area to get breakfeast! The location was PERFECT. That's the best part about the hotel. 5min walk for a tube station between Zone 1 and 2. We had a problem with our heater in our room, but they've put another heather to keep us warm. I would recommand a room on a higher floor like I had. The ground floor, where's the breakfeast room can be quite loud. The only 2 negatives points I have.. I've asked for a double bed and I got 2 singles bed. It's not a big deal but as a couple, I was a bit disapointed by those. The other thing is there's no insonorisation in the room. Meaning.. you hear everything that happen in your neigbourgh room. If they sneeze, you can hear them, if their tv is on, you can hear.. I would recommand the hotel, only if you get a room on a higher floor and you have earplugs to not hear your neighbours!

title: brilliant, again!
text: stayed at the Trebovir three years ago and the place is still wonderful and good value. We had a triple single room which was huge and the bathroom fantastic! Close to the trains and bus, this is an excellent venue.

title: Shabby...but not chic!
text: Booked this hotel by mistake..should have chosen The Mayflower next door! The Trebovir is cramped, tired and certainly not value for money. For £155 per night, I at least expect the TV in my room to work and for the bathroom to be bigger than one in a caravan! I requested to be moved from my ground floor 'cell' as the noise from the street kept me awake all night. My alternative room on the 3rd floor had walls so thin that I could hear my neighbour combing his hair! My advice...avoid at all costs

title: Nothing to recommend it
text: I stayed at the Trebovir for 2 nights in order to be close to Earl's Court. It is. That was the only good news. The initial experience of the reception staff was one of rudeness to the point of hostility - that was once I got them to come in from the step outside where they were smoking. The room is very small and the bathroom beyond belief. It was so tiny I had to stand side on to the shower! Being relatively cheap does not make this hotel good value. Seriously, find somewhere else.

title: Trebovir disappointment!
text: Myself and two friends travelled to London from west cork for a mid January break. We decided to stay in the Trebovir hotel at Earls Court which was in close proximity to the tube station. On arrival at the hotel, we had specifically asked for a three bedded room, something we found difficult to locate in London. To our disappointment we were given a room with a double and a single bed. When we informed the receptionist of this fact, he told us to check a different room ourselves to see whether it had three single beds or not, even though he was not busy at the time.
