The room did have three single beds although it was an extremely tight squeeze. To make adequate space to move around the room with comfort, we placed the two bedside lockers on top of the wardrobe. When we went to sleep, we were woken repeatedly throughout the night by the incessant snoring of the guest next door. The ironic thing is this gentleman had warned me earlier "to keep the noise down" due to the thin walls!!!!! The following morning, when we arrived for breakfast, which is served in the basement we were given two slices of processed ham and cheese with a croissant, tea and toast. We found this breakfast unsatisfactory. Furthermore, the hotel does not have a bar and lacks modern hotel amenities and has the feeling of a rabbit warren.

title: Convenient location, clean, tiny room but good service for money
text: I used this hotel as a hub while I traveled to other countries. So I stayed here 3 times, in different rooms, the total of 7 nights in 2.5 weeks. Rooms were very clean and well maintained though the room were tiny and bathrooms were airplane bathroom size. 2 times I had upper floor with nice street views and I actually liked them. Last room was on the first floor, had tiny window and had moldy smell-I did not mind because I only had a night and left early in the morning but I may not like it if I need to stay this room longer. Although tiny , room has everything you need-dryer ( ok it was broken in 1 room), flat TV with remote & coffee maker. Breakfast included was good with cheese and ham, orange juice, warm croissant and toasts with jams, butter & full service. Staff were very nice and offered me to keep the luggage while I took a trip to Paris ( for a fee), and also made arrangement for cab to go to the the airport at 5am. Location is super. It has 2 underground lines, and it was especially convenient when one line stopped the service for 1-2 days. You can go to/from Heathrow w/ big luggages no problems because this station has the lift. If using Eurostar to go to Paris, it goes straight to go to St Pancras. There is DHL service at the corner which I used to send accumulated stuff back home. Starbucks, which has Wifi is around the corner, post office is in front o the underground station which is 2 min away, restaurants of all kinds are all in walking distance.

title: Great location, basic accomondation.
text: Steps away from Earls Court Underground, local and fast food chain restaurants. Very basic "cruise ship" sized rooms. I could almost touch both walls in my single with my outstretched arms. Shower is not for "persons of size." Thin walls meant I heard a snoring neighbour all night. Staff is nice and off season meant no line up for the breakfast room.

title: Good value, good location
text: There are many small hotels like the Trebovir, and finding a good one can be hit and miss. What I like about this hotel is that it is newly refurbished, so rooms and beds are comfortable and clean. It is close to the Tube and there are a lot of restaurants nearby. OK - the rooms are small and the hotel can be noisy with guests arriving late, but for tourists, or a business traveller staying one night this is an excellent choice. Nice coffee at the complementary breakfast too!

title: An unexpected affordable oasis in central London
text: Nestled within a few paces of Trafalgar Square, this refurbished "grand" old lady exceeds expectations. Booked through an Expedia special offer, from start to finish the experience was beyond expectations

title: 방이 너무 춥다 My room was so cold.
text: I couldn't sleep. Because my room was so cold. The air conditioner can't be controlled at your room. If you feel cold you have to tell receptionist. But it was cold even they turn up the air conditioner to 29°. 방이 너무 추웠다. 첫날은 온도가 22도로 되어 있어서 올릴려고 이것저것 눌러 보았지만 내 방에서는 컨트롤 할 수 없게 되어 있었다.그래서 기다리면 따뜻해 지겠지 라고 생각하고 잤는데 너무 추워서 일찍 잠이 깨 버렸다.안그래도 비행기에서 잠도 못 자고 왔는데 호텔에서도 잠을 못자서 힘들었다.다음날 직원에게 말하니 내가 리모컨을 잘못 건드려서 그렇다고 내탓을 하네~근데 직원이 리셉션에 있는 리모컨을 누르니 온도가 26도로 올라와 있었다.직원이 얼른 온도를 올린거다.역시 내 방에서는 컨트롤 할 수 없는 방식이었다.근데 26도로도 너무 추워서 29도로 올려 달라고 했는데 그래도 밤에는 너무 추웠다. 이불 하나 더 달라고 해서 계속 이불 두개 덮고 잤다. 그리고 직원은 친절한 직원도 있지만 불친절한 직원도 있었다.여직원2명이랑 빡빡머리 남자직원은 친절했다. 조식은 크로와상,햄,치즈,요거트가 맛있었다. 위치는 진짜 역에서 너무 가깝고 찾기 쉬어서 가장 맘에 드는 점이다. 그리고 냉장고도 없음.

title: Great location and service, but minus points for not functioning WIFI
text: Plus: you can't go wrong with the location of this hotel. its perfect for all the popular tourist spots in London. Just 1min walk to the underground station at Earl's court, lots of restaurants around and laundry shops too. Breakfast is provided every morning and room service is proper. Ask the reception for a taxi booking to the airport or booking for Evan Evans Tours (I highly recommend Windsor, Bath and Stonehenge) and its done without much hassle. Cons: The toilet is somewhat small (I'd estimate it to be just twice the size of the lavatory in an airplane) During my 5day stay, the WIFi wasn't working and I wasn't the only one complaining about it. Router signal was strong but absolutely no connection to any webpages. I made my complaints from first till last day and aside from restarting the router, the internet connection was never fixed and its a huge hassle not being able to contact hotels, friends and make early affordable rail bookings for my next destination. For its poor response on this, Trebovir gets 1 less star.

title: Lovely hotel, great location, friendly staff
text: I stayed at this hotel in October 2016 - and I loved it so much, I immediately felt at home there. My room was located on the third floor and offered a beautiful, unobstructed view and natural light. The neighbourhood is quiet and pretty, and there are plenty of good shops and restaurants nearby. The Tube station Earls Court, which is connected to the District and the Piccadilly Lines, is just around the corner and hence travelling through the city is easy

title: Good value and excellent location.
text: I have only positive comments about the Trebovir Hotel. The location is great, only two minutes walk from Earls Court tube. The desk staff were friendly and helpful and the room itself was fine: clean and comfortable. There was free wifi and a good continental breakfast was included. I would definitely stay there again.

title: Inexpensive, Convenient, Friendly
text: I don't understand the negative reviews on this site. Partner and I stayed SEVEN NIGHTS in the hotel on TWO OCCASIONS in TWO DIFFERENT ROOMS and we had ZERO PROBLEMS. PROS: We dealt with Edwin, Arpet and Mark on the front desk, which was always manned professionally. Edwin took our reservation and there was no problem checking in. Mark is supervisor extraordinaire and took special interest in making sure our 1st time in London was a good one. The hotel is *extremely* conveniently located (40 min from Heathrow) on the same Underground line and a short (5 min?) walk that involves TWO turns upon reaching the Earl's Court exit. Earl's Court is in ZONE 1 (i.e. cheap) and is also a "super station" with several important lines converging = extra convenient and if you have to change stations you only have to do so ONCE. Typical travel time is approx 20 min to 40 min to everything interesting (Museums, Trafalgar, Picadilly, Tower, City). Absolutely no complaints. Broad choice of chain pubs, US fast food and other local restaurants within 5 min of front desk. absolutely no complaints. Room turned over fine and amenities OK. Most North Americans are going to find the rooms serviceable and the bathrooms laughable. Our first room featured a "pod" bathroom that had been retro-fitted into the room. It was like stepping into an airplane bathroom. Once you get used to the postage-stamp size of the think and figure out how the shower works, it's all OK (NOTE: As travelers in this cost echelon we do not care about the room in terms other than (1) cleanliness (2) safety and (3) quiet sleeping, which this hotel delivers on in spades). CONS The breakfast is simply awful - 1 slice cheese, 1 slice ham, 1 slice salami, 1 terrible croissant, terrible coffee, toast, yogurt...but once you understand that there are literally 20 better options within a 5 minute walk who cares about the breakfast! Go out to eat! We'll stay there again as the room rate of 78 pounds per night was unbeatable and the laughable breakfast is not a higher concern to us than cleanliness, security, quiet and helpful staff. This hotel delivers where it really matters. ....now, if they'd only fix the breakfast......

title: Fantastic
text: I stayed in the hotel one night, on a business trip. The location of the hotel was fantastic, literally a minutes walk from Earl's Court tube station. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the check in desk was open 24 hours. My room was a single ensuite, and was small but absolutely adequate. I never understand why people rate hotels such as this badly because rooms aren't huge. It's not the sort of hotel for spending lots of time in the room. Its a hotel which is in an ideal location for visiting London, and getting a good nights sleep. It was also very clean, and the free breakfast was nice.

title: Worst hotel experience ever!
text: The rooms are small, the baths extremely small, the staf rude, one of our two rooms was in the basement smelling old, damp cellar and was extremely unpleasant to sleep and breathe in. Woke up by the staf removing trash, long queue to get in to the breakfast room but not food available there! Would never go back, this is a frawd of a hotel.

title: Much disappointed
text: I changed the habitual hotel in Earls Court and just after a while I realised what great mistake I made...An incredibile small room and tiny toilet, a nasty smell in the corridor and the personnel rude to complete the picture. Forget the breakfast: thawed croissant and pastry and no other choice... The only advantages are the reasonable price and proximity to the tube.

title: Except for disappointing WiFi, perfect accomodation for price
text: I stayed at Trebovir for 2 days/2 nights in September. Let me get the 'bad' bit of the review out of the way first. Trebovir advertise free WiFi in the rooms, and whilst it is available and it is free (both ticks in my book), it was a very slow and patchy connection. There were times when the connection dropped out or I couldn't find the station. The only other minor bad bit was the noise in my room (G4). My room faced the Earl's Court tube station and during the day you could hear the trains arriving and departing. I hesitate to call this a negative, because inside the room, the noise sounded a bit like the wind and so it never really bothered me. Plus, it's still a very quiet location evetn with the train noises (you can't hear any car traffic noises for instance). Now having said that ... the rest of Trebovir is fantastic. The rooms are not huge, and the bathroom/shower/toilet is like a ship bathroom - tiny and compact. However, the rooms are modern and very clean and whilst compact, I never felt squashed or cramped. The location is perfect - Trebovir being 2 minutes walk to Earl's Court tube station which is itself 10 minutes on the Picadilly Line to the centre of London and 30 minutes to Heathrow. It's also within the Zone 1 ticket region and Earl's Court has plenty of bars, pubs, fast food outlets, restraunts and small supermarkets in the immediate vicinity which is incredibly handy to the traveller. The staff were friendly and helpful at all times and the office has a storage area for those arriving early/departing late. Best of all, the accomodation is *very* reasonably priced. So overall, despite the disappointing WiFi (come on Trebovir, it's not going to cost much to get a faster Internet connection nor wifi repeater stations), Trebovir is still a great place to stay and one that I would return to.

title: Basic hotel in a quiet area.
text: The hotel is near Earl's Court station, which made it accessible from and to Heathrow International Airport and central London. It is situated in a quiet area with some nice restaurants and shopping nearby. The hotel looked better in photos, and we were disappointed with the cramped double room, which was given to us on the ground floor. The room was dark and cold and expensive considering what we got for it. The rooms on the upper floors are probably better.We could certainly have found a better and more centrally located hotel for the price.

title: Closed!
text: The Grand Hotel on Trebovir Road closed unexpectedly and without notice. When we arrived there was a repossession notice on the door so we were forced to drag our suitcases down the street in search of a room. If you have reservations at the Grand, you won't get in.

title: Afternoon Tea
text: I went with friends for tea admittedly with a voucher offer. The staff were very pleasant and helpful. Prosecco at start was lovely. Excellent range of teas, sandwiches fine and most of the cakes. The scone stand mini muffins were not. Tasted very stale and were extremely hard. Think the cook might need some lessons in how to make.

title: Pleasant stay
text: Stayed in a family room. Clean room & bathroom. Friendly & helpful staff. Breakfast can be improved though. Great location. I do wonder why there are so many doors to pass through...thank god our room was on the ground floor. The air condition remote in the room was not functioning and we had to call the reception each time we wished to adjust the temperature. Quite bothersome! Enjoyed our stay. Will consider staying here on my next trip.

title: Great location. secure & clean, tiny room & bath- good value
text: As a thrifty solo traveler in London for the first time, I must say the Trebovir suited me perfectly during my recent 6 day visit. All I really needed was a safe and clean place to sleep and shower. The Trebovir provided that and more for about 65 pounds per night. The Trebovir is around the corner (150 meters) from the Earls Court tube station, which has direct service to the Heathrow terminals on the Piccadilly line. Would you rather spend $2 on the tube or $100 for a cab? The proximity to the tube is a huge plus which puts all the historical sights and museums only minutes away from your room at the Trebovir. The room is small but adequate and fairly clean. The 16 inch wide shower compartment requires some getting used to. see photo. The heat & TV worked well. Didn't use the phone or require internet. Leaving the room key at the front desk when I came and went seemed odd at first, but it definitely made the hotel more secure. The breakfast was mostly as promised, but I never saw any sign of the fruit or pastries. Corn flakes, yogurt, toast, cheese and mystery ham & salami, coffee or tea & OJ. I found it helped energize me for days of walking in museums and galleries. If you require eggs Benedict or tofu omelets, you won't get it here. Basic morning nourishment here. All in all, the Trebovir provides very good value for the modest cost by London standards.

title: not so Grand!
text: Minor problems with room showed a lack of overall care for the details, added to which the sad excuse for 'breakfast' was the worst effort I have ever experienced at a hotel or B&B... but to cap it all, the luggage storage we'd been promised was denied us on the day we left, due to lack of space but with such rudeness in the handling of this by the so-called reception manager that I am left without a good word for this hotel. Why he couldn't have handled this in a more professional manner I have no idea, his person skills were awful - fair enough if there was no space and that it may not be guaranteed (although suggested as available in their advertising) but he could have been more helpful and suggested a lost luggage facility such as the one we ended up using at Victoria station. To end on a positive note, though, the Earls Court location is very convenient for travelling within London - just try another hotel!

title: Service with a smile. A few niggles.
text: On the few occasions I need to be in London have stayed at the Hilton Kensington , always a good experience. I needed to meet up with friends ,they messed me around over the dates and I missed out on booking the best deal available at the Hilton. I spent so many hours searching for an alternative only to find bad reviews on Trip Advisor for places I thought looked good. As it would only be for one night I honed in on the most important thing for me, would it be clean? The Trebovir came up time and time again as my best choice. I was not disappointed in this. Booked via booking.com, no additional charges, quick and simple transaction. I stayed for the one night on 19th. August, arriving in the afternoon and checking out the following day. During that time I met 3 receptionists , one breakfast room attendant and a gentleman who was , I believe , a “ general manager “ for this hotel and the others under the same ownership. Without exception every one of them were welcoming, polite and helpful. I was well aware of the size of room I could expect as this hotel, unlike most others, actually posts pictures of ALL it’s rooms. Your experience of any hotel does depend so much on the actual room you stay in. Mine was on the first floor front, just above the entrance., overlooking a side street. My room was very clean and had better storage than I expected, very clever use of space . Did my own thing before meeting up with my friends so was able to come back to my room and shower. In London you can always feel hot and gritty but this time was worse, only 25C but the humidity was a killer. Tried to use the ECO setting on the shower but only got a dribble of water so had to go for the full on shower, lots of hot water so no problems there. I used my own bath products as I do not like scented items. I did sniff the ones provided but they would have been too scented for me. My room overlooked the street so I did pull the curtains before showering. They were full on black out style and great at keeping the light out at night but, in full daylight , I found my room was like a black hole as two of the room lights were dead. I am a medical electronics engineer but even I could not find a setting that was comfortable for me on the multi function digital controller for the air con at night. Yes I am the person who would read instructions if they were there ! Knowing all the nasty bugs that can be in A/C units I suggest that if this worries you take the pillows to the end of the bed and sleep so the A/C blows onto your feet. I did not do this as I am sure the units were well maintained. Knowing from Trip Advisor that there was a queue for tables in the morning rush for breakfast I did ask if it was possible to collect my breakfast and was told this would be O.K. Breakfast room was full the following morning with a few people waiting. Helped myself to juice as I explained to the very charming blonde lady that I was in a hurry and would be happy to take my breakfast to my room. Within about a minute my tray was loaded for me and she even helped me carry it to the lift! Bigger queue outside by now and I did get a few glances ! The hotel may ( or may not ) thank me for this but I really think it could help the situation if this option was made clear to people who don’t mind where they eat their breakfast as it would free up tables and make it speedier for all. If you opt for this be considerate, do not make extra work for the people who service your room. I left no mess and took my tray back , with a small tip for the good service. My check out was hassle free and my luggage ( to be collected later, about 7 pm ) was stored in a secure room. Would I stay again ? Yes if it was for one or 2 nights. The price was very good (£20 cheaper than HK ) for what it offered and not much difference in “ room “ size between the 2 hotels. Trebovir has better proximity to the underground. Hilton Kensington on a best deal rate would however be my first choice due to the fact you get a full size bathroom. Not so close to the underground but if you have a travel card you can get the bus to Notting Hill tube station. Cannot understand why people insist on walking to the nearest tube ! Finally thanks to eveyone at the Trebovir that I met, you were all so helpful , polite and charming.

title: Clean but tiny
text: This is in a good location and is clean. Breakfast is good (continental). Has an elevator which is also a plus. But understand what you are paying the somewhat low price for so don't be surprised or annoyed with the staff when you get there. It's an okay hotel for one or two nights for two people max I would say. You are booking into a remodeled 4 or 5 storied terrace house that has been chopped up. The rooms really are tiny. The bathrooms are manufactured fiberglass rooms only a tiny bit larger than a 'port-a-potty' or 'johnny on the spot'. They have a toilet, shower and sink all squeezed in there. The double bed is against the wall so that you can walk down one side and reach the wardrobe. All perfectly clean but very tiny. Staff are very helpful and friendly and the location is great for museums, tube, restaurants.

title: Leaking Air conditioner and musty smell
text: Booked a single room, which turned out to be a basement room with a musty smell. The air conditioning unit dripped water through a light fitting. I reported it to reception in the morning bit nothing had been done. Unfortunately they could not move me as the hotel was supposedly full. The ensuite was compact, I had to sit at an angle on the loo otherwise I knocked my knees on the basin. Breakfast was a unique experience with unlimited supply of cereal accompanied was a rationed croissant, two slices of cheese and two of ham. I won't be rushing back there

title: Small but tidy !
text: It was small though very clean and tidy.Gorgeous breakfast.However,I wish wi-fi connection was free for everyone in everyroom and not have to pay 15 pounds!I thing Trebovir hotel is a typical English town hotel in the very hospitable neighborhood of Earls Court.Moreover,price was very good and the service excellent!

title: A Great Stay
text: We stayed in this hotel when we visited Hackney for Radio 1's Big weekend. We arrived at the hotel at 10am & needed to leave before the person still in our room had checked out. The very helpful waitress sat us down & offered us a free tea or coffee whilst we waited for the manager. He was just as helpful & found us a spare key didn't have to wait around. He Took our case to store in the office & place in our room when it was available. Also we had a complementary drink each included in our stay so we took him up on the offer even though it was still quite early. When we arrived back to the hotel at about 11pm we went up to our room, it was decorated really nice with a settee & Plasma TV, nice comfy bed, clean bathroom with two little bags full of complementary show gels, shampoos etc... The next morning we went down for breakfast which was buffet style, we had plenty to eat which set us up for the day & all of it was nice too. The room cost £99.95 which if you ask me is a bargain.

title: Dodgy
text: Well where to start? Upon arrival I was asked despite having paid online already to pass over my credit card. Of course I had to question this: told in order to allow a £50 charge that would be refunded after 5 days if the room I had stayed in was not damaged. This is very odd and as I was to find seemingly a way of paying for the damage that in fact was already there! This was not featured in any terms & conditions of the booking via their own website which itself was very basic and lacking information about other things like check in/check out times. Upon going through a door leading to the stairs I was faced with the unfortunate nature of them being steep, windy and totally ridiculous in being expected to take any luggage up. The nice young man on the desk however agreed to carry it upstairs eventually. This was after my initial check of the room on the top floor. I got to the door to find it unlocked & ajar. I started to enter in order to access the situation when a foreign woman who spoke not one word of English appeared behind me in a hysterical manner . I deduced this must be the cleaner. After 2pm the rooms on the top floor where not ready when the guests where being sent up to them. Its not a large hotel with hundreds of rooms so I think there is no excuse for this. When I was finally in the room I was able to see the many points of damage & lack of cleaning. The walls were marked all over and dirty, the blind damaged, a large chunk of marble missing out of the worktop in bathroom amongst these. There were no tea & coffee making facilities. The only water offered: a dirty old glass bottle filled with tap water. A simple bottle of 50p water from the corner shop would have looked better and at least I could have drank it. There was no soap in the bathroom. A little gift bag with a mini shampoo and conditioner..laughable. The added unnecessary supposed luxury of hair straighteners amused me. Lacking in the basics and trying to impress people with crap. The t.v was OK actually when you worked out how to switch it on the ability to swivel it was useful. There were cigarette buts and ash on the windowsill. THIS IS BAD. I have smoked in the past so I'm not entirely foreign to it, but that even disgusted me. There was constant noise from some sort of expellar system from the hotel kitchen downstairs. Some people don't mind this but at £80 for a single room Its not great. Also alot of mold on light cord!!! Security is appalling, after 11.30pm ish the desk is unmanned and no one at the hotel at all. The door from the street has a big gap in it & not properly secure at all. Its a swipe open door system. I have lived in hackney previously so I am familiar with it. Which is why I know that having no security light at entrance or anyone manning the desk till 2am on a Saturday which would be more appropriate in hackney is a bad idea. Hackney is not immune to crime despite the development of the area. And the entrance to this accommodation is basically down an unlit alleyway. WHAT I FOUND TO BE TOTALLY APPALLING AND DANGEROUS IS THE FACT THE LIGHTS ON THE STAIRS DO NOT WORK & AT THE BOTTOM TO GO UP THERE IS NOT ONE AT ALL..PITCH BLACK. I had to use my phone and carefully meander my way up as though I were in a horror movie. I had being informed upon checking in that check out was 10am. When I went downstairs for breakfast before this I was told along with everyone else I was going to be charged 'a fee' for not checking out in time for 9am. ON A SUNDAY. When they were running breakfast till 11am. On a Sunday they do breakfast in the actual pub downstairs. I only worked this out from a leaflet in the room, upon checking in I was told it was at a cafe nearby. The menu in the pub claimed there was soya milk as an option. Which lets face it in this day and age it should be..coffee shop chains provide it why can't a place charging this much a night do so. Well there was no soy milk, the owner apparently according to staff doesn't see the point. Having food allergies there is a big point & Ive paid for a full breakfast I can't have. Now cereal, porridge & hot chocolate are all off the menu because they cant be bothered to provide what they advertise. Not impressed. Various shops next door that actually sell it. See where I'm going with this. So I asked what the hot breakfast would be was told sausage, egg, bacon, mushroom that's it. In-fact in turned out there was more, other guests asked for it. The actual omelet I ate was nice. The green tea was cheap and tasted naff though. The eating area is pleasant to sit in. Although people walk in and out off the street when its not open to the general public which I found to be inappropriate. The fact they leave double doors to the bar open is it any wonder. I am a well traveled & reasonably fit young woman in her twenties. Not a fatty or disabled. I have raised some major issues here that would greatly affect people of an older age. In fact anyone over 50. I actually have a high tolerance for many things after traveling alone to many different countries since I was a teenager, therefore in context for some things to be a problem for me means they really are a problem. I would say this place certainly has some dodgy ways of trying to con you out of more money to pay for their costs and former damages perhaps? Or just plain greed? Who knows. They are obviously unorganized, lazy & just ripping people off. I was happy to get out of there. Some of the staff are nice..the young man upon checking in, the day bar staff but that doesn't make up for the dirt & lack of security. £80 a night more like £10 and £2 for breakfast. This is a honest review where I have complemented on positive points. Its just there are not many. Don't go. You will feel cheated.

title: Food and Drinks with Friends
text: Came here with friends for some food and drinks before heading to an event nearby. Really nice venue, friendly bar staff & great food. I had the shredded chicken burger topped with mac n cheese and fries, which was really delicious. Would definitely recommend this pub and will return.

title: Hidden gem!
text: We stayed here for the night when we were visiting the Hackney Empire. It was a 30 second walk from the hotel to the venue, could't have asked for it to be closer! Although the bar was busy with people ordering food, the bar manager still immediately took us round into the check in lobby to give us our room key/instructions etc, everything we needed to know for our stay. He also mentioned that there was 20% off food and drink for hotel residents. That made our mind up that we would eat our evening meal there. The food was really good chicken with choice of 2 sauces out of about 6(the jerk was excellent), with sweet potato fries and coleslaw that was homemade. The staff were all friendly.polite and attentive even when the pub was bustling.The room was just what we needed, a comfortable bed and what looked like a brand new bathroom. We had to leave early to catch a train so can't comment on the breakfast but the bar manager also said he would refund us the breakfast charge. A real great find, will go back. Thanks

title: Good Sunday lunch
text: Quite evocative styling downstairs, light and open upstairs. The food is pretty decent and the prices good. Popular when the rugby is on, with a great bunch of characters passing through it. Good for kids on Sundays.

title: Great food - especially the rotisserie chicken
text: Just got back from our second Sunday lunch visit to the Old Ship Inn, hidden down an alley by the Hackney Empire. The food was brilliant - my family and I had fried squid with aioli mayo, an outstandingly good dirty burger (with chorizo, avocado and bacon) and a melt in the mouth rotisserie chicken (with curry butter). Washed down with a good local bitter... The service was friendly, helpful and full of good humour. You can’t want anything more on a lazy weekend. Even played darts with my boy in the bar section. JK

title: Short weekend break
text: I stayed at the Old Ship Inn for a couple of nights last weekend, while visiting my niece. My single room was decorated beautifully - loved the bright green Dalsouple rubber bathroom floor & having real tea-leaves on the breakfast tray (and at breakfast downstairs in the bar) was a nice touch. Staff were really friendly & helpful. I will be back! Regards, Jo R

title: Lunch with friends
text: Casual lunch with friends. Food acceptable although bit on the pricey side for what it is. A quarter of rotisserie chicken including two sides around the £13 mark and the chicken was dry. Very welcoming, pleasant staff although I object to the practice of adding a £1 charitable donation on my behalf to the establishments charity of choice. If the Ship inn wish to give to charity they can do it from their profit, I prefer to chose when donating rather than it being done/ added to my bill without even asking. To clarify I do give to charity but when I chose to not when I’m eating out.

title: Nice stay - shame about the bed
text: I was a little uneasy about having booked at the Old Ship as, having made my booking, an e-mail I sent asking about booking for dinner went unanswered. However, My initial impressions of the Old Ship, when I arrived in Hackney, were very positive - it's close to Hackney Central station, easy to find, the staff were very friendly when I checked it, and while I quickly found there was no milk with the tea and coffee, and no bag in the bin, staff were happy to provide both when I asked. The room I had was a single - it was small, but perfectly adequate (although like so many hotel rooms, the wiring is not well thought out. The only power points are at the foot of the bed, so although the tea & coffee making stuff is all laid on on a shelf you have to put the kettle on the floor to boil it, and have similar problems if you want to plug in a phone or other item.) The complimentary toiletries in the shower room were nicely presented and good quality, and it was very nice to have leaf tea and ground coffee available rather than sachets of instant. I was pleasantly surprised to learn that the room rate included a complimentary drink, and was able to book a table for dinner when I checked in so the fact that my e-mail had not received a response didn't cause any problems. Both beer and, when i came to eat, food, were good (and good value, for London) and although the bar became very busy during the evening , the staff all remained very cheerful, polite and helpful. Unfortunately I wasn't given any information about when breakfast was served (and no information is available either in the rooms, or on the Inn's website) so I came done too early, but once it was available, breakfast was very good - cereal, fruit and yoghurt, freshly baked bread, and cooked breakfast - sausages, bacon, eggs, mushroom and tomato, although these did not seem to be replenished as they were used, and I am not sure that those coming down a little later got the full selection of hot food. However, despite all the (very) good points, there was one major problem - the bed was the most uncomfortable one I've (tried to) sleep in for a very long time - the mattress was obviously past it's sell by date as every single spring could be individually felt. Fortunately it was a warm night, so I ended up using the duvet as a mattress topper and sleeping under the throw, instead. The sheet seemed to be directly on top of the mattress with no mattress topper or underblanket, which no doubt made the problem worse. There was also a lot of noise from rats or pigeons - very disconcerting as it sounded as though there was something scrabbling around under the bed. I think it must have really been in the walls or somewhere, but it was very disconcerting. In the morning when I wanted to check the news I discovered that the remote control for the TV didn't work properly - it turned the TV on, but didn't alter the volume or channel at all , so was a bit of a dead loss. The Inn is VERY convenient if you are seeing a show at the Hackney Empire, and the Bar and food are great, as are the staff, and I could see this as being a good place to stay if it were not for the bed, but as that's such an essential part of a hotel stay I have to rate it 'Poor' on this occasion. Unfortunately by the time I went to bed and found how bad the mattress was it was too late to speak to anyone about changing to a different room, so I don't know whether this is a one-off problem (I was in room 7) I wound up only getting about 3 hours sleep. I'd be happy to eat here, or hang out in the bar, but I'd be reluctant to stay again.

title: Great for dinner before a show at Hackney Empire
text: We stumbled across the Old Ship Inn before a show at the Hackney Empire, and thank goodness we did. It was so warm and intimate, great staff, great gastro pub style food, and really good drinks menu. I would highly recommend if you're looking for a really nice 'gastro pub' style restaurant before a gig at the Empire.

title: Such wonderful staff and customer service. Highly recommend!
text: We stayed for one night at the Old Ship Inn at the beginning of October. It is very close to train stations and bus links, which is perfect if you want to explore the whole of the area. Although the rooms are above a busy pub, we were on the top floor and heard no noise at all. In fact, we had a wonderful sleep. I should mention that there is no lift to the rooms, which could be a problem for anyone with limited mobility. Although we arrived quite early, our host was welcoming and we only had a short wait before we checked in. Some minor issues were dealt with quickly and we were able to get some rest before we headed out. Due to a problem with our booked taxi, we had quite a stressful afternoon, but on return to the Old Ship, the staff were so kind and we quickly relaxed again. With a 20% discount on all food and drinks in the bar for hotel residents, we decided to stay and have our evening meal there. We were not disappointed! The staff reserved us a table and we enjoyed a delicious meal in friendly and cosy surroundings. I wanted to try the craft ciders on draft, and I was offered samples before I made my decision. ( I ended up buying a glass of each, they were both so delicious!) I have read some reviews about small rooms and creaky floorboards in the hotel, and these are fair points. However, I think this adds to the sense of history in the building, which you do not get in larger, chain hotels. The customer service is probably among the best we have ever had. In my opinion, that is so important. Rooms were clean, there is free Wifi and the beds and pillows were so comfortable, that I made a note to ask what kind of pillows they use. A delicious cooked breakfast in the morning set us up for the flight home. We will definitely stay here again. I have given five stars because I think the amazing customer service makes up for the tiny 'quirks' like the creaky floorboards and the absence of a phone in the bedrooms. Thank you so much to everyone who made our stay so wonderful! We look forward to returning soon.

title: 2 night stay
text: The Old Ship in is along the main road in Hackney close to the central station and lots of shops and restaurants / takeaways. Entrance to the accommodation is via a side road which was not that easy to find. My room on the second floor was clean and comfortable with tea and coffee facilities and lots of hot water for the shower. The staff were very friendly and helpful and nothing was too much trouble. I had the full English breakfast the first morning, very large portions and help yourself to unlimited toast, coffee, cereal and juice. The following morning, I had the granola which was also large and delicious. The only downside to staying here is the noise, but that was too be expected on a Fri. and Sat. night. Overall, I was very impressed and would definitely stay again.

title: Not a great sleep
text: We stayed here for one night mid-week in May. The hotel seems newly fitted and we were pleasantly surprised with the room. It is small but has everything you need as well as HD TV. A welcome drink on arrival was a nice touch. There were some problems though.. the room was incredibly warm and we couldn't cool it down without leaving the windows open. The room backs onto a flat roof so this wasn't an option. It wasn't even warm outside so I don't know what's going on there. Next was the uncomfortable bed, the creaking floorboards in the corridor and the slamming doors of the neighbouring rooms. It didn't go on all night so wasn't a major issue, but it's a shame because it could be fixed so easily. Other than all that.. I'd still recommend this place - it's the cheapest place near the City by a long way.

title: Chicken wiiiiiings
text: Hackney's best chicken wings. Probably. Why has it taken us so loooooong to try this place? Friendly, responsive staff. Great food. If there's anything that could be improved, it's swapping Neck Oil for Gamma Ray on the draught. Anna enjoyed her Moscow Mule which they kindly cooked up even though it wasn't on the menu.

title: Great Staff, fab room, good stay
text: I stayed here overnight to attend an evening course held locally. What a great little place....we entered via the passage way from main street which was fresh and clean (see previous review) and the pub was lovely, well decorated and cosy. The staff took our bags despite being 11 am so I was free to explore London in comfort...was given complementary drinks when returning to check in and enjoyed a lovely vibe whilst waiting...room 5 was compact but extreamly well designed to offer everything you needed for a breif tip, very good bathroom, but just in need of a minor touchup (general wear and tear) Would have eaten in the evening but their was a party, which was quite noisy however noise didn't carry to the rooms and buisness is buisness in these economic times. There were some hitches but it was how these were addressed and resolved by extreamly good staff which made the difference ...wish there were more urban inns because I would always hope to find such good places to stay at their reasonable price

title: Fantastic Staff and Lovely Food
text: We stumbled across this lovely place when we were looking for something to eat before going to Hackney Empire. The entrance was hidden away but we decided to take a look. The staff were amazing. Although we hadnt booked and they were busy they found us a table and made us feel very welcome. We werent rushed at al. The food was lovely as was the house wine. We will definitely go back if we are ever in Hackney again. We have had bad service many times but all the staff here were polite, friendly and very helpful.

title: Great location,reasonable price
text: Spotlessly clean pub with easy walk to Lardo restaurant and London fields/broadway market area.reasonably priced with friendly staff. Character pub which we would highly recommend to friends.didnt eat here but food looked fantastic.

title: A Very Pleasant Stay Indeed
text: All in all a lovely stay. Excellent welcome (including complementary drink). Room was lovely, not particularly big but well appointed and nicely decorated. Staff were very attentive throughout my stay and very friendly too. The whole place had a really nice, friendly, relaxed atmosphere. The evening meal was excellent too, a good variety, very well finished and tasty. Breakfast was great too. Everything that should have been hot was hot and there was a good selection. I will definitely stay again when I am next in the area.

title: Great value for money
text: I stayed here for a night as part of a party of three in April (one single room and one double). We stumbled upon the hotel whilst looking online for somewhere to stay close to the Hackney Empire Theatre as we were going to a concert there. We got a lovely deal on the rooms, dinner and breakfast. We arrived somewhere around 2:30pm, check in was nice and efficient and the free drink for each member of our party was very welcome as it was a fairly warm day (which it wasn’t when we left Wales so we were rather overdressed) and we’d had a bit of a frantic dash across London. The bar actually closed for staff training whilst we were sat having our drinks but they were perfectly happy for us to continue to sit in the corner and relax after our journey. As others have said the stairs aren’t any good for anyone with mobility issues but it’s an old building so what else do you expect? The rooms were what you expect for London – small but adequate. Let’s face it, how much time do you spend in your room anyway? They were perfectly clean and modern looking. I’ve paid more for bigger rooms that weren’t anywhere near as clean or modern – I’d much rather small and clean. We ate in the restaurant – the food was lovely and the service was very efficient as they knew we were heading on out to the concert. It was very busy due to the concert and so people were being turned away – including people who were staying at the hotel who hadn’t thought to book a table. I don’t know if it is that busy every night but if there is a concert on at the Empire Theatre you do need to book. There was a good selection for breakfast the following morning. I only have one negative – the floorboards. I know it’s a very old building but they are a bit of a problem – and I work in an old building myself and we’ve had the floorboards sorted for the same reason. It wasn’t because someone else was keeping me awake but because I was the one making the noise - the ones under my single room were the worst out of our two rooms – I felt awful whenever I moved around even a tiny bit because it made such a massive noise (even when I turned over in bed). I had to be annoying other guests whilst I was getting ready for bed at 1am. Other than that quibble I can’t recommend this place enough – great value for money with lovely, helpful staff. A hidden gem.

title: Do not stay in this hotel in winter!
text: I stayed in this hotel for two nights and I would not recommend it. When I checked in, my expectations were good as the staff were friendly and I'd read positive reports on here. I then got to my room which was a decent size, TV was ok, bathroom a tad small but sufficient. It was already quite late so I decided to settle down for the night- only to find the room was freezing and the heating was not on. I put on a few more layers to deal with the cold as staff had already finished for the night. The next morning when I went to breakfast I mentioned it to a member of staff who said she would tell the owner who was in later that morning. I went out, came back where the aforementioned member of staff told me that the whole hotel had no heating and it was due to be fixed that day. Come that night, it had still not been fixed so another freezing cold night in the room. Trying to find staff was tricky as the reception is not manned, you have to go to into the pub 99% of the time, the stairs are steep, there was no bin in the bedroom, only a small one in the bathroom. Oh and ladies, be warned, no hairdryer!

title: Good Value - Perfect for College Students
text: Traveled from London to Paris. This was our London Hotel. It was nice, great service and food. The rooms were tiny but compared to a dorm it was fine, especially for the price. We took the tube into the city everyday, but it isn't that long, definitely not a hassle. I liked it and so did my boyfriend. It was cute and had character. Hackney has a few bars and it was an interesting scene. Only con is that the bed was ridiculous firm and uncomfortable.

title: Great value for money
text: In London for training with 4 of my colleagues. We had a mixture of rooms types - singles and doubles. After reading the Hotels good reviews on a number of booking sites, our Company decided to book with them direct. Upon arrival we were greeted with a free drink then shown to our rooms. All the rooms were immaculately clean and very well appointed. The staff were very polite and went out of their way to help us. The breakfasts were really nice with a great selection. We ate in their restaurant most nights and were pleasantly surprised - delicious well presented food and the prices very reasonable. We go into Hackney often for events at the Hackney Empire - we definately would use this Hotel again. Great find for the prices charged.

title: Unreliable
text: This may be a nice hotel but they are incredibly unreliable. My parents and friends were supposed to stay here when I got married - they booked months in advance, and it seemed like a perfect location - but just a few weeks before the date they said there was no availability because of renovations, leaving everyone with a last minute rush to get a room elsewhere. Do not trust this hotel.

title: Rude staff at the pub
text: I hardly ever go out of my way to review a bad experience but the rudeness of one of your waitresses earlier today left me no choice. My boyfriend and I came into the pub at the Old Ship to see the rugby match and since there were no tables free we sat on bar stools at the end of the bar, ordered a couple of beers and started watching. From this point onwards, one of the waitresses (blond girl) pushed me pretty much every time she was walking past, at first I thought it's just by accident, but she didn't say sorry once plus there was plenty of space behind me at all times. She also hit me in the arm with her elbow while taking some drinks from the bar and later on deliberately came out of her way passing me to push me again (which my boyfriend saw coming back from the bathroom). I then decided to confront her about it asking whether she's got a problem with us sitting there and if so then she should have just asked us to move somewhere else. She wouldn't even listen to what I said and walked away saying she does not have a problem, but somehow that's when the pushing and barging in have stopped. I would have fully understood if someone have asked us politely to move somewhere else if we were somehow in the way of the staff working at the pub, but this sort of behaviour is just unacceptable. The management should really rethink who they hire. Needless to say we won't be coming back even though we live in the area.

title: Great pub, poor hotel
text: We stayed at The Old Ship Inn in Hackney for one night on the 16th Dec 2017. When we checked in we asked what time breakfast was served on a Sunday morning as we had early trains to catch (back to Suffolk). We were told that breakfast started at 8am and we said we would be down at that time. We had a lovely evening meal in the pub and the rooms were good. Sunday morning we went down for breakfast at 8am and there were no staff and all of the doors were locked. The four of us were joined by another couple and a man. We then let in a relief member of staff who had no keys. We waited in the corridor for 30 mins..... but no one turned up to unlock. In the end we had to leave to catch our trains. I left my phone and contact details on the desk as we were unable to check out. Next day I receive an email apologising for our lack of breakfast and that they had debited my card for the cost of the two rooms but not charged us for breakfast..... but absolutely no explanation as to why there was no staff on duty. Personally I find this outrageous especially as breakfast was an extra cost anyway. We have previously stayed at this hotel annually at this time of year. Unfortunately this will be the last time.

title: Nice room, disappointing service
text: Lovely room, nicely decorated but a little on the small side. We stayed for 2 nights and breakfast on the Saturday was at the cafe a few doors down which was very nice. Unfortunately breakfast on the Sunday was in the pub/restaurant itself and was served earlier than on the Saturday. We had not told about the change of procedure on the Sunday and walked down to the cafe as we had on the day previous to find it shut. Went we got back to the hotel we were informed that the chef had gone home and missed breakfast. When we asked for a refund as we had paid for bed and breakfast and had not been told that it was earlier we were informed that the breakfast was complimentary so no refund would be given. This unfortunately this left a bit of a sour taste after what had been a pleasant stay.

title: Lovely boutique hotel
text: The old ship is a hidden gem in Hackney - 2 minutes walk from tube sation. We were given a free drink on arival and booked in very promptly from helpful staff. The hotel has a nice bar and restaurant. The breakfast in the morning was lovely, latte, juice and good produce. We had the top floor room which is a steep cimb, but the room was very comfortable quiet, modern, flat screen tv, sofa, nice bathroom and tea/coffee/water. The only negative was a lost/stolen remote to tv, the mattress a bit springy and the shower only warm at its hottest

title: Burgers
text: I went for my last night in Londond with a friend. We ordered a cheeseburger that was really nice and the fries were on point. The waiter was really friendly and the prices reasonable. The only things I would criticize are the toilets (they smell) and the tables (there were sticky).

title: Cool bar.
text: This place is cool. Staff were lovely. The food was really really good and well priced. The chicken was delicious. Drinks were a little on the expensive side but good - we appreciated the significant wine list.

title: Good food after work
text: I came to this pub after work with my big sister. We ordered the veggie made from sweet potato fetta along with a brownie and fruit pie. Try the veggie burger 🍔 fantastic. All was good. Nice food for a pub. Only bad thing is fix your toilet! Leaking not good.

title: Best in London I reckon
text: The friendliest, most accommodating hotel I've ever stayed at. If you have to spend time in Hackney, this is the place. What a pleasure.

title: Quirky but great!
text: My wife and I had tickets for the Athletics at the London Stadium so needed somewhere near to stay after the last evening performance. We found the Old Ship in on the internet and decided to book a room. When we got there it was attached to a pub where we had a friendly greeting. We were shown to a room early that was freshly decorated and full of character. Everything you could want in a room in this day and age. My title calls it quirky as it would not be every bodies cup of tea. The wall over the bed had a photo of a man giving a donkey a glass of stout, which we thought was very amusing. The only complaint we had was a creaky floor board, but what do you expect in an old London pub.#We also stayed for a roast Sunday lunch which was as good as Mums.

title: What on earth was THAT???
text: My husband and I popped in to the Ship for a quick bite to eat before heading across the the MOTH Club. We ordered simple food and a couple of Bloody Marys. The food was no frills basic "competent" does what is says on the the tin

title: Mixture of Highs and Lows
text: Another hotel that makes an excellent first impression with a free cold drink on arrival after taking the tube from Kings Cross to Hackney Central. I was then shown to my room (family room) which I found well appointed with all I needed for a one night stay. TV was a challenge to work out with a mains switch hidden under a shelf but this was soon clarified by a member of staff after puzzling over why it wasn't working. Offer on my bed enticed me to take advantage of a free glass of house wine with a main meal. Downside they charged me afterwards and I am awaiting a refund to be put back on my card. This was made worst when I called later (when the charge appeared on my statement) and I was questioned about where sat to qualify? Customer complaint handling lessons to be learnt here. On the night I was placed at a table for my meal and then quickly moved again - apparently it was reserved (waitress wasn't aware of this and I certainly didn't see anything on the table) so this didn't make me feel terribly important. The food was excellent and the `free' wine was most welcoming. Breakfast arrangements were a little strange - you walk around the corner of the block to a little cafe (not too far) however the positioning and the service were excellent so no complaints on this front. Finally the sleep quality was not great due to a bagging noise outside that sounded like a garage door being slammed in the early evening before stopping at a reasonable time. Sound proofing to the street needs improvement for me to return to the Hotel - you seem to hear a pin drop so when a noisy group of people having a great time about 2am decided to make alot noise I was naturally awake until they passed down the side street.

title: Good food friendly staff
text: Stopped at the old ship inn during our 5 mile Thames Path walk, great food good portions and very friendly staff, beautiful setting overlooking the Thames. Visited other pubs nearby so far this is the best.

title: Friendly and convenient
text: I wanted a base for 2 days in London that I could get to by car and then commute to the city on public transport. The Old Ship Inn fitted the bill perfectly. Convenient to overground trains, but also on a great bus route there is no problem getting around North to South or East to West. Easy to get to on the A10 from the M25. That leaves just one challenge which is parking, however, there is a small carpark at the train station 1 minute away for that. You can park for under 10 pounds a day, and you can renew your parking fee each day by phone. The staff were all very friendly and attentive. Our room was lovely and clean, modern and considering it's above the pub, surprisingly quiet. The pub itself has a relaxed atmosphere and serves great food with some very good values specials. It was 2 for 1 burgers on Tuesday. These were very tasty and excellent for the budget. We also tried some of the appetisers which were also very good. Not a fancy place, nor does it claim to be. It's good value, with hardworking staff committed to providing a pleasant stay. I'll be back when next in London.

title: Great place for the cost of the room
text: For the cost of the room we found a great place to stay the room was big enough for me and my wife to get changed at the same time without getting under one another feet. the food was ok but the friendliness of the staff always makes a difference and really went that little bit further than i really expected we knew that the rooms were above a public house so did not expect it to be an oasis of quiet but neither i or my wife were woken by noise either from the pub or from the alleyway outside. For under a £100 bed and breakfast in London you really could not fault the place i would definitely stay there again no problem at all

title: Wonderful dinner
text: We stumbled upon this place walking through Hackney looking for a place to eat. HIGHLY recomend it, the food was really well made and the ambiance was both relaxed, progessional but still unique :) Come here if ever in Hackney!

title: Nice little b&b
text: Visited London for a weekend for a couple of concerts. Decided to stay in Hackney as it's walking distance to Victoria park, the Old Ship inn is a trendy pub with 10 rooms above, close to shops and tube station, all staff were friendly & helpful, rooms & bathroom nicely decorated, breakfast very nice. Had to have the windows open in the room as it was a very hot weekend which made it a bit noisy, but that's understandable in the town centre, would recommend staying there.

title: Great Place and a Great Team of People !!!
text: I was on bussiness in the area and was srugling to find some were to stay at short notice. I was walking passed and noticed the sign. I went in and I have to say the welcome I recived was very good. The manager came over while I was booking and asked me how I was and was I having a good day, I explained I was on bussiness in the area, I was delighted to have found some were to stay at such short notice I was also asked would I like a drink a very nice touch. Something about the place makes it feel like home it sure doesnt feel like a pub.My room was amazing Clean ,very up to date with all mod cons I was very impressed. I back in that neck of the woods soon with some of my Team and we will booking here for sure !!! looking forward to it !! Oh I forgot to mention Food is great in here to !!! I also had a great sleep bed was very comfortable.

title: OK
text: I stayed here for two nights and although I wouldn't put anyone off staying here I just didn't like it as much as I thought I would looking at their website. Firstly there is no parking so the first night as it was Sunday and I was out at 7am the next day I could park on the street nearby. 11.30pm till 8am is free on the street. The next day though I parked at hackney railway station car park for £8.40 day rate. As I was up early the first morning I didn't have breakfast as it doesn't start until 7.30. My fault for not checking the times on the website before paying for two days breakfast. I did have it the second morning though and it was nice but I was told they didn't have any poached eggs when I asked. Full English (with scrambled eggs) plus cereals toasts and juices are all available. The room was clean and tidy. Single bed was on the small side and the TV couldn't be turned over physically on the set or by the remote so I hope you like E4+1. I stayed in room 6. The pub it's above is great. I had a nice beer there one night and the staff were really pleasant and food looked nice. Free WiFi throughout the building. No noise from downstairs once you're in your room. I would have given it a 4 star rating instead of 3 but I paid £186 for two nights. Although this probably isn't expensive for London I'm just a simple northern boy. I wouldn't put anyone off staying here but check they've fixed the TV and stocked up on poached eggs first.

title: The kind of hidden gem that makes hackney special
text: Wandering up hackney high street looking for somewhere to watch the rugby we didn't expect to stumble on somewhere as good as this. Well tucked away from the high street it has a lovely vibe, great gin selection and fantastic food. The menu is by no means extensive, but if you can do a few things really, really well then it's worth sticking to them - and the Ship certainly does this. Best rotisserie chicken in a longtime, with great sauces and sides. Would highly recommend even if only for the chicken, but a great place to chill and/or watch a bit of sport as well.

title: Lovely hidden gem
text: Great little boozer ! Visited on a Wednesday afternoon, pub had a good atmosphere and nice ambience. By 6pm there was a good buzz to the pub, few people playing darts and lots eating. I had the cheese burger, added some guacamole which was bangin. Good options for additional toppings, considering it's a relatively small gastropub. Very reasonable price wise too. Staff were very friendly and had good knowledge of beers - the selection of which was also refreshing. All in all, recommended ! Will be back J

title: Awful barman, and there were mice!
text: Chose this pub as we'd just been to the cinema over the road, and on first entering it is a nice place with plenty of space to sit down. Unfortunately this is the only good thing I can say about the place. The barman (tall guy with dark slicked back hair and facial hair) didn't seem to be on this planet. He ignored us when we went up to the bar, told my friend they didn't do house red wine and didn't suggest anything else. Then conversation went like this: Me: Can I have a sauvignon blanc please? Barman : No. (blank stare) Me: Errrr, why? Barman: We don't have any. Me: Do you have anything else then? Barman: We have the house white wine. Me: I thought you didn't do house wine. Barman: We do but it's really bad. Me: Do you have anything nice then?? Finally got our drinks. Sat down next to the kitchen, and the area where they were putting the food out for the B&B guest brekkie the next day. Lo and behold a couple of mice were running about. Told the barman who responded "What do you want me to do about it? It's London there are mice everywhere." Then he bizarrely came out from the bar (looking annoyed that we'd disturbed him) and took pictures of the mice on his phone. But did nothing. Really gross that there were mice around the food prep area. I wouldn't ever come back here!

title: Excellent pub with amazing food
text: I came last weekend to watch the rugby having never heard of this place before. I was so pleased that we dropped in. Really nice staff and great atmosphere in there. We hadn't intended to stay for food but it looked so good that we had to give it a try. We were not disappointed- delicious food and really reasonably priced. We will definitely be coming back again and again. This review would have been 5 stars, the only thing that let it down were the toilets- one of the cubicles was flooded and the door didn't close properly.

title: Mean spirited staff at Christmas.
text: We had our xmas works meal here, the food was dreadful the turkey was out of a tin, the pigs in blankets were burnt, there were no chestnuts as promised the whole meal was like a pre packaged meal from the frozen section in your local super market. The staff were cold and unfriendly there was no interaction of christmas spirt. We spent lots of money for nothing. Not one member of our staff would eat at this second rate run down establishment. And I certainly would never ever return here. there are a million and one beautiful places to eat out in Hackney. We only went here as a last resort as we had left our booking too late. Now we know why they were the only ones available at such short notice.

title: AMAZING!
text: In the U.K. from Australia and dropped in for dinner before a show. I was surprised that most of the tables were reserved (I know why now!) as it's tucked away from main road. Service was quick & hospitable. Food was excellent. Very small menu because what they do, they do extremely well. Serving size was very generous. If you're in the area, I highly recommend but call & book a table.

title: Wandering around Hackney looking for somewhere to eat
text: Staying just one night at the Kip Hotel and so looking for a place to eat that evening. Wandered down Mare Street, the main shopping street, and literally stumbled across the Old Ship Inn. If you're looking for it, it's at the end of a very unprepossessing passage stuck between a couple of shops, about 3 doors away from the Hackney Empire. Slabs of fried chicken and enormous burgers dominate the menu together with a range of salads. I chose a shredded chicken burger and it was.....heaven!

title: a genuine hidden gem!
text: I had the pleasure of staying at The Old Ship Inn last night (14th September) - infact I am writing this review sat at a dining table having enjoyed a delicious and relaxed breakfast - and i am very happy to report that Ive rather fallen in love with the place. I am a frequent business traveller and I can honestly say I've enjoyed my stay here more than the vast majority of 4/5 star pit stops that I make. The staff are friendly, efficient and very accomadating. I saw lots of smiles and the conversations felt genuine and unforced. The room was clean, modern and stylish. The bed comfortable. The shower powerful. I had dinner, breakfast and lunch and all meals were excellent and reasonably priced. The atmosphere in the bar was great too with such a refreshing mix of people from all ages and walks of life.

title: Quite a find! Let down a bit by breakfast!
text: Stayed for one night when attending a concert. A bit out of the way but with very good public transport to central London. Room 10 on the top floor was fine and excellent value for money. No problems with noise. Breakfast buffet a bit "tired" and sparse by the time we were eating. The tiny bit of scrambled egg left was completely grey and best avoided!! I think the young lady in attendance could have made a bit more rather than keep stirring in a bit of milk. But we would probably stay here again.

title: Great hotel, great location
text: Perfect for empire or town hall. Room was lovely, staff great. Food (lunch and breakfast) delicious. Parking wasn't too bad cos it was weekend. My only criticism would be that I emailed before I booked and the reply I got was of a tone that nearly put me off all together. Instead I booked through late rooms. I don't know who answered my email because the staff I met during my visit couldn't have been more helpful.

title: Great for the Arcola theatre
text: I was pleased that the hotel has taken up my recommendations to improve one's stay. I found the members of staff very helpful and friendly. The chef I met when I returned from the theatre and he was chatty and helpful. In the morning my milk had turned and I cam down to find a very helpful cleaner who did not speak English but very kindly gave me fresh milk for my early cuppa. Breakfast was great and enjoyable with umpteeen papers. I also struck up cpnversations with a guy who has stayed there for many weeks while awaiting work on his property and a couple over from Israel for their son's wedding again staying for 10 days or so.I would not hesitate to recommend the hotel as a single female.

title: Charming Place
text: Hotel rooms and bit minimal - but the place has a lovely authentic vibe to it. Great food and cocktail deals - make sure you're there on the right night! Awesome friendly bar staff and Mare st at your door step! Love it.. will stay again.

title: Great atmosphere
text: The Old ship is really hitting its stride as a pub and hotel. Great enthusiastic staff, always willing to help. Great atmosphere - and away from the hustle and bustle of mare st. A fun reliable food menu too, but still wouldn't mind some more variety/veggie options.. Be sure to check out all the street art in the tunnel on the way in. I'll be back time and again.

title: The Old Ship - nice place.
text: Wondeful place to stay in London, pub and small hotel with a good english breakfast. We will absolut say you must try this. Located near the Town hall with good buslines to city. Good restaurants around the pub.

title: Rude bar staff
text: My partner and I have just come into this pub for a drink and food before a concert, having had 2 drinks my partner tried another beer that in his opinion tasted off, he approached the bar and asked if it could be changed, he was told theres nothing wrong with it !! My partner said he thought there was, the Boris Johnson look a like bar man said after 5 minster of disagreement I will give you half a pint at this stage I got up and informed them I run a pub the gave him a pint very very begrudgingly, how dare they accursed us of telling lies. NEVER AGAIN.

title: Not for business trip
text: Restaurant/Bar with rooms up-stairs. Difficult access to rooms. Only possible to sit in the bar/restaurant to work, and it was very noisy. Staff was very kind. Rooms are small, beds are OK. Bathroom small. Everything is outdated.

title: Very good inn in Hackney
text: This was our 3rd stay at the Old Ship . We always get a clean bright room with a comfy bed. Breakfast is fine and all the staff are incredibly helpful. Great value in the capital with the overground station a short walk away.

title: Nice Pub and Hotel
text: We found the Old Ship Inn for our first visit of London. Located in Hackney the Pub serves simple but very delicious food, there are 241 burgers available... 😉 Trendy people, good drinks. The hotel is lovely too, the rooms are clean and modern, but not the biggest ones... There is only one thing we missed: a hairdryer.

title: Great value for money
text: Stayed here as a couple while visiting our daughter. Upgraded to evening meal. Clean, comfortable, quiet. Good service. Will stay again. Steep stairs. Great atmosphere in the bar/restaurant. Very friendly staff.

title: Good in parts, pity all the parts were not there.
text: The Old ship Inn is obviously popular and because of that dining is a noisy experience. Staff tried to be helpful but were under pressure ( I am medically allergic to dairy and after explaining this was presented with a salad scattered with Parmesan!) Portions were huge but the cooked veg were grim. I had the ham hock terrine which was good but it was sold as coming with pickles and onion jam, both of which I was told had run out, so no spare jars in the cupboard?

title: What a fantastic alternative to the impersonal, drab london hotels
text: After being continually disgusted at the value of hotels in London and the quality you receive I was recommended this as an alternative. What a refreshing change - human, friendly staff, comfortable room with space and a wonderful bed, tasty, well presented food from an interesting menu, served with a smile and personality. Staff you value your custom and enjoy what they do.

title: didnt even get through the door!
text: my boyfriend was given a "red letter day" voucher for he's birthday at the beginning of august. their was a huge choice of things we could do but we thought we would go to London and stay in a hotel over night. at £170 for a Saturday nights stay, dinner and breakfast included, we thought we got a good deal! we planned to see a show and tour London both Saturday and Sunday. the week before staying at the hotel i checked trip advisor reviews to see what i was letting myself in for. after reading numerous horrific comments i was slightly concerned and told my boyfriend. he reassured me we would be fine! i asked my boyfriend to ring up and ask what time dinner and breakfast started so we could get organised prior to our stay. my boyfriend rung red letter day to find out and they gave us the hotel's number and said we would have to ring them. my boyfriend rung the hotel and they had no recognition of our booking, which we had booked 3 months ago!!!! we rung red letter day back and they said that cannot be possible as they have the confirmation of the hotels booking. the girl my boyfriend was on the phone to from red letter day told us she rung the hotel to explain and they were rude and uncooperative to her and refused to take blame for anything. i know its the hotels fault because of all the muck ups iv seen on here with other people! thank god we didnt turn up on the day because that would of been our whole weekend ruined! red letter day have found us a better hotel to stay in right in the centre of London and have apologised plenty, which is more than i can say for the old [--] inn! if you ever plan to stay here ring hotel prior just incase this happens to you or just avoid it all together

title: A great find
text: A weekend in Hackney visiting relatives found us peering curiously down the alley which leads to the The Old ship Inn. The passage way is dark, edgy and little a discomforting however worth getting through to enter the Old Ship Inn. Rustic and comfortable and atmospherically lit, the pub/restaurant has a great buzz about it. the Music was excellent, however not everyone will agree! and the volume just right. The menu is limited however we went for chicken with jerk, lemon and thyme and dunston chilli marinades with fries, onion rings, avocado salad and coleslaw. All excellent, the chicken was succulent and well flavoured without being over powered. The accompanying sides were equally delicious. all the food was fresh and prepared well by chefs who enjoy delivering great food. A good selection of wine and local ales added to the evenings pleasure. Service friendly, prompt and considerate. A great find and worth the effort

title: Don't stay here
text: After staying here for a few nights, we couldn't take it any more and went somewhere else. The bedroom was extremely hot, stuffy, noisy, claustrophobic and uncomfortable. The windows are opaque and cannot be opened more than a crack. This was the only time I have ever forfeited £120 for cancelling a stay. Earlier, it had started badly when they told me I couldn't have the room I had booked because it was still being renovated. I later found out that they had actually double booked the room and didn't have the decency to tell me, so they made up the renovation nonsense. That hotel hasn't seen a renovator for decades. To be fair, they did put me in another hotel for that particular night. There were a whole host of other negatives as well, but there isn't much point in describing each one in detail.

title: Great place to stay
text: The hotel was great value and very handy for where I was visiting. The staff couldnt do enough to help when I checked in. The only things that let it down were I came down from my room about 1115pm to get a drink but couldnt get one even though there was people still drinking in the bar. This was bit disappointing especially as was staying in the hotel. The hotel manager said next morning he would have still served but it is up to the staff. The other thing was that the bacon and scrambled egg were a bit cold. Overall though the hotel was very nice and the room was well appointed and clean. Would stay there again

title: Hidden gem
text: Great rooms, fantastic selection of lagers and ales. Manager is a fantastic guy, surpassed all expectations. Burgers are absolutely fantastic. I'll be back here again. Stopped here for business bit would highly recommend to anyone in the area.

title: Just what I needed!
text: After an arduous 36 hours non stop travelling across several timezones I landed at the Old Ship, 3 hours too early for check-in but just glad to have arrived there. Was welcomed with a complimentary drink and room was made ready as a priority. Took a fabulous shower and had very long sleep in very comfy bed, room was well appointed, nice decor. Wifi signal not that fast/strong but still worked. Had heard about creaky floors but didn

title: Paralympic stay
text: We stayed one night with our 8 year old. We chose The Old Ship as it was near to the Olympic Park (just two stops on the train). The staff were friendly and welcoming, both on the phone before our visit and on our arrival. We were very pleased with our stay, all the staff were exceptionally helpful with our requests (e.g. providing an early breakfast to have in our room, storing our bag while we were at the Paralympics). The room was clean and comfortable, a good size, good shower, nice tea, good toiletries. The floor was very creaky, and while that didn't bother us I did worry that, as we had to get up so early, it may have disturbed other guests. We were pleasantly surprised to be given a complimentary drink on arrival, and a free glass of wine with dinner too, and the food was very nice. There were no children's portions, but our son enjoyed his meal so much he ate it all anyway. This pub is good value for money and a good place to stay.

title: The Old Ship Inn Hackney
text: It is quite difficult to find a decent small hotel central to Hackney that is both well priced and of a good quality. The Old Ship Inn has both. We stayed here as we were visiting our daughter for her birthday and her house was full to overflowing. So after doing a lot of research we decided to try here. It was a great choice. The booking system was welcoming and easy. It was friendly too. We had a lovely double room, that was clean and tidy with a good en suite. The TV was excellent and the room was warm and quiet, given we were in a very busy area of Hackney. We were a little early to check in, but were treated politely and given a complimentary drink while we waited. We slept very well in the comfortable bed and had a good, generous breakfast the next morning. My slight niggle was that breakfast started at 9.00 am and that is a little late for those of us who like to get up and out when we are in London, I left that comment on the hotel feedback form and have since been contacted to say that this matter will be considered. A very nice small hotel that we will return to in the future.

title: It made an "old man" feel hip again!
text: A one night stop over for a business trip in East London prompted a search for hotels in an area that isn't overrun with hotels, especially the well known chains. So a break from my rule of not staying in a pub because of the noise from the bar downstairs needed to be broken on this occasion.
