title: Still as quaint and welcoming asnthe first time
text: When we got married all those years ago,we spent our wedding night here. We visited again to celebrate our anniversary. We rang the hotel direct and got what I thought was a good price for our night's stay. The person I spoke to when making the booking had a good knowledge of the hotel. The place has changed a bit since we were last there, changing ownership at least once. On arrival we were greeted enthusiastically and the receptionist made us feel at home. The room we had was on the top floor. It was very nicely decorated, the bed was comfortable and it had aircon. We explored the local area, taking a cab into town. The room we had was just right for the two of us, with nice views over the garden. Breakfast was relaxing, with plenty on offer to eat. Any negatives, not really. We took more in on this stay (our wedding night was more of a blur). The hotel is not particularly cheap but we enjoyed our stay.

title: Still as good after all these years
text: This was a bit of a trip down memory lane for me - I used to stay at the Portobello regularly on business many years ago and always loved it - quirky, comfortable and very peaceful in a beautiful part of London. I came back with my wife to use it as a base when going to Wimbledon (ideal as it turned out, 20 minutes direct on the District line from Notting Hill Gate) and found it every bit as charming as before. We stayed in one of the basement rooms with a small outside terrace - this was spacious and comfortable, although some may not like the somewhat quirky plumbing in the bathroom (we did). The staff members were lovely - friendly but discreet. Breakfast in the drawing room was great. No restaurant but plenty of choice locally.

title: Gorgeous Boutique Gem in Notting Hill
text: We had a wonderful stay & adored The Portobello. It’s a small boutique hotel with just 21 rooms spread across 2 handsome neo classical townhouses. The immediate vicinity is awash with great restaurants & the nearest tube a 10 minute walk. Reception staff were wonderful - it’s a friendly, personal little pad. We loved our room, a generously proportioned top floor bedroom with space for a sofa. It looked out over private garden & was spacious & beautifully decorated with fine period furnishings. Nice bathroom, very powerful shower & lovely full size Spring & Garden products. Rooms have a good coffee machine & chocolates & biscuits are also supplied. Continental breakfast is included in all room rates, a small spread including pastries & cereal with cooked items chargeable. It’s served in a quaint old school styled sitting room which also operates as an honesty bar. Breakfast can be taken in-room for no additional charge, a necessary provision as the intimate parlour couldn’t possibly cater to all guests. The only thing the hotel lacks is an outdoor space, though some rooms do have a terrace. There is a lift & rooms have air-con. The hotel has a really nice feel, decor throughout is classic but boho with its delightfully chintzy furnishings, portrait clad walls, Portobello antique finds etc. It’s characterful & infinitely British. I’d definitely stay again. The hotel is now part of the Curious group which includes other bespoke lovelies like Cowley Manor & Canal House in Amsterdam. A fab find.

title: Small Room but great location and quiet
text: This is a gorgeous little hotel. The room I stayed in was a standard and was small, with the bathroom even smaller. I didnt mind at all but others might. The rooms were quiet, staff was brilliant and beds comfortable. Walking distance to markets, hotels, shops and underground (all about 5-10 min away) I think if you were to stay maybe take a larger room although I didnt see them so cant advise.

title: Beautiful Luxury
text: Stayed at the Portobello during September 2006 and it was a fantastic stay. There are different themed rooms, and I am glad we chose the 4 poster bed room -with a bed so high that you need a step to get into it! Room was perfect with fresh coffee, cookies etc. Room came with a massive square tv, large lounge and a private balcony overlooking the shared gardens below! Bathrooms had both a large bath and a separate shower, and lots of room. Service was great at every stage from when we first checked in, to ordering us numerous taxis, to the breakfast the next day. While the Portobello is slightly expensive (between £240 and £300), is it well worth the expensive, and I will definitely be returning.

title: My favorite small Hotel in London
text: Wonderful, fun, funky rooms, great staff, got a wonderful upgrade, great brunch, accomodating, just plain awesome. Would stay again in a heartbeat.

title: Wonderful Stay!
text: Thank you for a lovely time! The service and rooms were fantastic and the hotel is in a fabulous area. I really fell in love with the area and London in general. Thank you so much for a memorable experience. By the way, I believe I left my robe there...maybe I'll pick it up when I visit next time :-)

title: Weirdest approach to us as clients
text: The price and the quality of this hotel is too high for what you get. We booked a superior room with a bathtub. It was my birthday (I came with balloons from my earlier celebration so it was also very obvious to the reception) and I was super excited to chill out in a hotel. When we arrived it was, in a London fashion pooring outside and even though they were two in the tiny reception, no one came to help us to open the door. and to help us with our bags. The approach from the lady in the reception was the weirdest ever. First - the room that we got wasn't locked and the other help went with us to the room to put chocolate on the pillows and checking the room (a bit last minute don't you think?). The room was super small, the bed is a double bed and suitable for one normal size adult. And no bathtub. I go down to ask if it's possible for us to change the room for the one that I actually wanted and paid for (with a bathtub) and that was a big negative. No rooms left, besides from the extra luxury rooms "but then you need to pay extra". And when I kindly asked about the fact that the room didn't have a bathtub, I was just told that "they were out" of that room and that they asked me to contact hotels.com if I wasn't satisfied, so all responsibility on the customer. But Hotels.com couldn't be contacted at this date (January 1:th). The hotel offered us a bottle of prosecco, but by that time we just wanted to go out and enjoy the Notting Hill surroundings and have a birthday meal far away from the hotel. That night I didn't sleep at all. The bed were way to small for two adults. In the morning there were nothing for me to eat but fruit even though we'd paid for breakfast and we told them the day before that I'm coeliac. I'm writing this review almost six months later because I have been reminded of this horrible stay though spam e-mails about their great hotel. I never signed up for a mailing list. And I have opted-out twice. No change. I hope the GDPR law will change that now... I really don't recommend this hotel seeing that what you see on the images is not what you get in reality.

title: Poor quality, bad service. Will not return
text: My husband and I were very excited to stay at this hotel. We stayed in the "Japanese room" which was described as "one of the larger rooms in the hotel, which has been recently added". Modern and minimalistic were also used by hotel staff to described it. The room is in the basement, next door to the hotel kitchen. To get to the room, one must walk down the stairs, go past the door-less kitchen and you then arrive at the front door of your room. There was a constant smell of food in the corridor. The room was not large, it was average sized so if this is the largest room in the hotel, I hate to think what a small room is like. If you are used to luxury hotels, this hotel is not for you. We arrived at the hotel in a taxi. There was no one to help us with our bags outside or inside the hotel (we had 3 suitcases and a set of golf clubs). I asked if someone could help us and the women behind the desk looked at me like I was crazy. The staff were not terribly helpful. We went to use the computer in the lobby area because no one could provide us with the password for the wi-fi. The hotel porter/bell person was surfing the Internet ! There are much better places to stay in London. The location is good but value for money and service are terrible. Needless to say, we will not be returning.

title: What a unique stay!
text: I cannot say enough good things about this hotel! First, it was fairly convenient to get to Paddington Station or the Underground by walking just a few blocks, which made it an ideal location to center our stay in London. It was in Notting Hill, but we liked that because the neighborhood was quiet and residential. The hotel itself was super unique! We had this awesome green room in the basement (but it had a little patio - so it didn't feel like a 'basement' room). The room was giant and had the coolest decor and bath. The bed was out-of-this-world comfortable! The best part of the experience though - aside from the incredible staff - was the breakfast. Oh my croissants! These things were pure heaven! Hot out of the oven, and all buttery, they melt in your mouth! There was this incredible local yoghurt served too that we couldn't get enough of. It was such a beautiful way to start our day and prepare to go explore London. I highly, highly recommend this hotel!

title: Lovely lovely lovely!
text: We stayed here for valentine's night and it was just perfect! The reception staff were welcoming and friendly and nothing was too much trouble! Our room was very large with a lovely sofa in it and a glorious selection of teas and coffees. In the morning we were served breakfast in bed which was great. Cannot recommend this place enough a true taste of London in a great location only a few mins from Notting Hill tube and Portobello Road Market.

title: Filthy and tired
text: Avoid at all costs this hotel which is trying to live on past glories.

title: Cute Boutique
text: This was our 2nd stay here. The Portobello holds a special place in our hearts. Very friendly reception staff (sorry didn’t get her name). We stayed on lower ground floor, Room 2

title: Just beautiful...
text: This charming little oasis in the middle of metropolis is just fab ...you hardly feel you are in the city it’s so quiet . The rooms are beautiful with hand crafted antique furniture and the most comfortable beds ever . The staff are attentive and friendly with lots of information about the local attractions . The breakfast is lovely located in a beautiful drawing room ...we opted to pay extra fir cooked ,but the continental is very good . Overall I would definatly stay here again ...in actual fact I wouldn’t stay anywhere else . Thankyou to the Portobello for such a lovely stay .

title: Great Hotel
text: Stayed here for 2 nights in mid February. From start to finish was a great experience. Loved the hotel, old world with great character, very friendly staff, couldn’t do enough for you. Room was perfect, fab shower, turn down service with beautiful chocolates on the pillow. Nespresso machine in room and they even had fresh milk in the fridge. Bed was luxurious, great nights sleep. Breakfast was lovely in a beautiful room, so classy with high ceilings and creaky floors. Have stayed in many places in London and the Portobello is without doubt the best. Location in Notting Hill is great too, walking distance to markets, pubs and restaurants. 5-10 min walk to Tube station on Central line with only a few stops to Oxford Circus. Couldn’t recommend high enough

title: Charming Boutique Hotel In Notting Hill
text: The room was most comfortable, and the hotel overall attractive and convenient. But what distinguishes the Portobello was the attentiveness of the staff. I had come to visit a local and she felt most welcome by the staff every time she came by. The front desk was cheerfully helpful in planning shows and museums, and the room service staff took initiative to respond to my preferences. Warmly recommended.

title: Lovely tucked away in Notting Hill
text: A little gem within a stones throw from Portabello Road. Staff were polite and very helpful. Rooms were lovely and quiet. A very agreeable two days. Would definitely recommend this place. Parking outside after 1.30 was a bonus.

title: Unique
text: This is an utterly charming hideaway located in the increasingly popular Portobello area of London. The hotel offers a thoroughly unique experience with every room being enchantingly different. We stayed in two rooms, one at the top of the house which was tradtionally decorated and very comfortable, but the second room really hit the spot. It featured a raised window seat, a gloriously comfortable bed with art deco mirrors both behind and above it, a rolltop bath in the bedroom and the smallest but most marvellously designed bathroom ever. We felt completely luxuriant for our two days in this room and the only regret was that they don't serve breakfast in bed! The breakfast room was a bit of a disappointment and also the fact that there is no restaurant on site. We would have happily spent most of our time in the hotel if the facilities had been better. But then again when you're within walking distance of many wonderful restaurants and sights, perhaps it's enough to just return to a wonderful bed at night.

title: Quirky and fun
text: Great location in a quiet street and free parking after midday on Saturday. A one-night stay whilst attending a function locally this hotel is quirky but tired. First the poor stuff: The hotel needs some decoration as everything is looking tired. The balcony rail is rusty and peeling and the hotel needs a new concierge arrangement as the lobby was literally filled with other guests bags when we arrived. A bit of friendliness from the reception staff wouldn't go amiss either - no offer to help with bags just "here's the key and there is the lift!". Ok. Room service was apparently 'no problem' except that it arrived with only half the order. We weren't charged for the missing half at least. Although the bath is a centre piece the closet sized shower looks like it was reclaimed from a 1970's council make-over. The room was great. The round bed doesn't quite fit in the middle of the room but was extremely comfortable and the bizarre Victorian bath was a ral talking point. Very large and very deep for multiple bathing if you wish! It's worth a night but I probably wouldn't stay here again until it was refurbished.

title: Colonial decadence in Notting Hill
text: We stayed in the Colonial room at the Portobello hotel to celebrate an anniversary. The room was lovely, a really good size, fantastic decadent bed and lovely bathroom with huge victorian bath, with all its original fittings. Staff were lovely, couldn't have done more to help. I would definitely recommend for anyone wanting a romantic stay somewhere a little out of the ordinary.

title: Love this
text: It’s my first choice always to stay in the Johnny deep suite This is the finest boutique hotel in London surrounding eclectic shopping & choices of fabulous restaurants The design & the antique furniture is sublime Also love the staff

title: Fun Friendly Excellent Hotel in Perfect Location
text: A truly original boutique hotel with warm, welcoming unpretentious staff. The rooms all vary but they are invariably well done up and the beds are super comfortable. Breakfast, which can be brought to your room, is delicious. Location is quiet yet easy walking distance to Notting Hill and Portobello.

title: Lovely hotel in a great location
text: I recently stayed a the Portobello, made a mistake with my standard room, which was lovely, but wanted something bigger. The staff were great and rearranged bookings to give me a lovely large refurbished room. Both rooms had great beautiful beds and lovely linen in bedroom and bathrooms. Breakfast in a lovely sitting room overlooking a garden, wonderful. For me the staff made the stay, good so helpful, ready to accommodate, just great

title: Charming hotel with great location and service.
text: The rooms and bathrooms are not to the standard of modern hotels however the friendliness of the staff compensates for any shortcomings of the facilities. It is a great place to stay and highly recomended.

title: Never again
text: The website for the hotel could be for a different hotel!! The rooms are very very tiny and the bathroom was hideous...the toilet and shower room was more like an aeroplane toilet. God help you if you are carrying a few extra pounds. I love shabby chic hotels but this hotel needs a complete refurb,from the bar in basement (which is as big as Del Boy Trotters bar) to the breakfast room, bedrooms and bathrooms.I think the hotel thinks they can charge the room rate they do due to being in Notting Hill but the rate doesn't reflect the hotel. They need to become aware of the fact that people expect a great service and atmosphere for their money not just be in the right postcode.

title: Lovely british hotel!
text: Stayed a few days at this hotel, situated nearby Portobello Road in Notting Hill. Beautiful rooms, lovely breakfast and very friendly staff! We will return for sure! I can recommend it for couples, families and anyone who want to explore and feel the Londoner atmosphere!

title: Quirky, different and lovely friendly staff.
text: If you are looking for luxury and decadence don't go here, but if you want interesting and different then this is the place. We stayed in the Japanese room and it was fairly large with a comfortable bed and super bath and shower. The staff were very helpful and it was a lovely quiet location. I was disappointed by the breakfast, the croissant was stale, the toast cold and the butter rock hard. However this was my only real complaint. The hotel is a bit expensive but it is really quirky and I loved my stay here and found it very romantic.

title: Perfect
text: Stayed in room 16 last weekend and can highly recommend this boutique hotel. Perhaps we were lucky with our room because it was not too tiny and did have a nice bathroom! Breakfast basic but very good. Bed extra comfy. Great location and very nice staff. We will return if we need a hotel in that location again.

title: Big Expectations, but no warning about the toilets
text: To be fair, THE PORTOBELLO has a good location, in a quiet lane, exceptional beds and nespresso ! But it ends there, it is a boutique hotel, meaning there is lack of space everywhere, in the lobbies for your bags, in the rooms for your bags and worst of all their GOOD ROOM toilets where we were occupying must not even be 12 sqft., i'm sure they should be getting an award for the smallest toilets in the hotel industry! You do not have place to move, change or shower properly. No tubs, none of the hotel travel sites warn you ! When we requested for a change of room with a bigger toilet we were denied unless we paid for the upgrade, So be warned, if you do not really expect to use the washroom or gym, you should be just about fine !

title: Where Penny lived.....
text: They say in order to be unique, you have to be irreplaceable. The Portobello hotel is most certainly both. Situated in the middle of the perfectly alligned homes in Stanley Garden's, we parked up behind a pristine vintage (two-tone blue!) Rolls Royce. The car definitely mirrors everything about this boutique hotel

title: Quirky, hip, with potential but also a little tired!
text: A hip and quirky hotel in a quiet but well placed street near the Tube, Buses and Market. Unfortunately, it is also a bit shabby and in need of a make over. My room was full of furniture that was in need of refurbishment, frayed curtains,and a bathroom that was 60cm x 210cm with broken floor tiles. Small TV, no real desk and a lack of convenient plug sockets. If you are paying good money for a room, then the room should be up to standard. Shabby-Chic only goes so far! Could be a great place... when fixed!

title: Very private
text: A perfect place if you want a private but central location. Ideally situated near Portobello Road and Kensington High Street. Rooms imaginatively decorated Hiving a sense of decadence and calm ...lots of interesting items including roll top baths, circular beds. I love the idea you can open your balcony doors and still have complete privacy offeted by the trees beyond. It's a pity there didn't seem to be access to the park beyond. For a hotel of its reputation the things you normally cast a fleeting glance at eg sockets, curtain rails, wooden blinds etc all seemed a bit worn. Not that I mind this at all but it didn't reflect the price paid. That said I would definitely visit again for the seclusion and fab location next to the huddle and bustle.

title: Some things really matter.
text: The hotel certainly doesn't match the photographs on its website but I arrived ill after a trans-Atlantic flight so I just wanted a bed. I got one in a small pumpkin-colored room with 1970's furniture and construction going on outside my window. I feel that it was outrageously overpriced but I stayed in a B&B the last couple of times that I was in London so I can't be sure. This is not an appropriate hotel for anyone who has trouble walking. The "ten minute" walk to a main street was a forty-five minute uphill crawl for me. Look for a hotel in a busier area. The reason that everyone should avoid this hotel until the security issues are resolved is as follows: There are no safes in the rooms. There is a safe in the front desk area. I take narcotic painkillers so I don't carry more than a few with me. When I left the hotel, I turned over my pills, passport and extra money to be held in the safe. The items were sealed in a stretchy envelope and placed in the safe which is operated with a key that I assumed was kept in a secure place. On the morning that I was scheduled to leave, I went downstairs to eat breakfast and told the man on the desk that I needed my items from the safe. He couldn't find the key. From listening to his subsequent telephone conversations it became clear that there is no one secure place where the key is kept. The desk clerk rifled through the desk area as if he were looking for a pen. When he could not find the key, he told me that I would just have to wait until the owner arrived to open the safe. When I told him that my plane would have already left by then, he shrugged and told me that there was nothing that he could do. I requested that he call the owner and ask him to come in immediately. He refused. I then requested that he call the other more competent desk clerks to ask them where the key might be. As it turns out, the Portobello Hotel desk does not have a list of employee phone numbers - or the owner's number. By that time, I was less polite and the desk clerk was useless. I finally had to tell him to call the number that he had and ask that person for the owner's number and to keep calling and asking for the number until he got it. When the key was located, I was beyond upset. I waited to write this review because when I got home I found that my thyroid was not working. That is mostly why my trip was so awful. I wanted to make sure that I hadn't overreacted to the hotel's issues. But it's seven months later and that last horrific morning still makes me angry. And I spent an enormous amount of money on that trip. Since I was in my room more days than I was out of it, it would have been really nice if the room had actually resembled the website photos. Not everything was awful. The women who worked the desk during the day and evening were very nice. The people who delivered room service were very good, too.

title: An oasis of charm, quiet and utmost attention to detail
text: My daughter and I just returned from an absolutely wonderful week stay at the Portobello and it was the hotel highlight of our 3 week vacation -- beautiful crisp linens, attentive staff and beautiful furnishings await you -- after our stay we went to another country for a week and returned again to the Portobello for an overnighter (and unbeknownst to us an upgrade!) before heading out again -- while we were gone, my 17 year old told me she couldn't wait to get back to the Portobello as she loved it which is high praise coming from a 17 year old -- !!

title: May be good may be not
text: This small hotel is very weel located near Nottin Hill gate subway station. It is in a typically London street. It is very clean and the staff is good. But for the price (572 € for 2 nights) he bed room is not very large and the bathroom is so small : as small as in a boat and the washbasin loks like the one we have in our restroom !!! The continental breakfast is very correct but if you want an englis breafast you have to pay. It will be good if the price was less expensive.

title: Hidden Jewel
text: Tucked away on a side street off Portobello Road in the very trendy neighborhood of Notting Hill Gate lies a hidden jewel. If you’re not looking very carefully, you may miss Portobello Hotel London. The building is very much like the other mansions on Stanley Gardens. Once inside, the warm décor of the lobby is just as inviting as the lovely ladies waiting to greet you. I was directed to room number 2, which is located beneath the main floor. The elevator is a bit tight and has a mind of it’s own, but you’ll get used to it. Room number 2’s furnishings are sensual and reminiscent of colonial India. Windows and back door open onto a cute hideaway patio that’s perfect for fresh air and afternoon tea/coffee. The pièce de résistance, however, is the amazing king size bed with Kama Sutra figures carved in the wooden headboard. Great room service, great in-room amenities and a bathtub for two makes this hotel the perfect getaway for lovers, poets and anyone who wants to take the road less traveled.

title: A charming place to stay in Notting Hill
text: This is a quirky, charming hotel . It is infused with character and we found the staff to be very helpful and friendly. Lovely personal touches too....chocolates laid on pillows plus a surprise departure gift. Highly recommended.

title: Fabulous hotel with excellent service
text: We stayed for 6 nights. Hotel just fabulous. We had room #6 which overlooked the beautiful garden. Room large with separate room with a claw bath & then a separate shower room. Perfect location- short walk to Portobello Rd with heaps of restaurants. Plenty of photo shoots for all the sights from the movie Notting Hill. Staff wonderful, helpful & served breakfast every morning. Short walk to tube station which was only 4 stops to centre of London. We had a wonderful stay & would recommend to anyone

title: All that glitters is not...............
text: I had been invited to a very special friend's birthday party. One of those '0' ones so i knew it would be a late do, so sensible to stay over I thought. Checking around I came across the Portobello, which just happens to be in the next street to where I was going, Have a look on their web-site, I did, it looks great. About 3 weeks before the event I rang to book a room, now I should point out that they aren't cheap £145 (ex VAT) for a single up to £315 (ex VAT) for the best. The cheapest double works out at £234 inc Vat, but the 20% offer mentioned on the website apparently only applies to bookings made on the day, a novel way of pricing thought I! I found another bookings site which actually showed the number of rooms available and tracked that so I did book on the morning of the day I was staying and got the room for £200 inc. You have to look for it in Stanley Gardens, but the ubiquitous 2 Bay Trees gave it away so I pulled up on the yellow lines outside (it was a Sunday) and went in to check in. The young lady on reception was having a blazing row with some other guests who seemed to be having a row themselves, but that's life, so when she gave me that look which sort of implies that I had no right to be on the same planet as her I put it down to her recent experience. How wrong can you be! The welcome is neither warm or polite, but check in I did and then asked (because it wasn't offered) if someone could help me in with my bags. Someone was (after a very audible tut) summoned. I went up to the room! Small didn't come into it, how 2 people manage I'd love to know, then I looked at the bathroom! Tired would be polite. It had a toilet, facing the shower room with a washbasin in between, not so much a room, more a corridor! Having driven for 2 hours I made use of the facility, but I could not get the flush to work. I knew I had to move my car so I went down to reception and explained about the problem with the flush, only to be told that 'I had to push hard' Not sure she was happy when I said that for £200 per night I didn't push hard on anything, but she said she'd get someone to look at it whilst I sorted my car out. On my return I was assured that someone had been up to the room and was again advised to 'push hard' On the plus side this Hotel does have complimentary wifi and that was easy enough to get connected too. Early October this year was unseasonably warm, the hotel doesn't suffer from air conditioning and my little room was getting hotter so I thought I'd have a shower. That was a challenge. Firstly you have to climb into it, secondly to get to the tap you have to close the door, thirdly the cubicle is so small you can't avoid the water, end result you either get very cold water or very hot! Not bad for over £200 eh! It's impossible to dry yourself off in the bathroom so back into my now even hotter pen where I changed into my party outfit, sweating profusely and I set off for the party. On the way through reception I mentioned the heat and without a smile I was told that they could put an air-conditioner in my room and, fair enough it was there when I got back. These portable units could not be described as quiet and to use it you have to open the window and doing that lets in the loud traffic noise from Kensington Park Road, a bus route and hilly at that point too. So the choice was sleep cool, but be woken by the noise, or sleep warm, I opted for warm, although as they haven't yet found double glazing the noise element is still very much there. I watched some tv, marveling at the way the wiring to the wall mounted set had been done in black with no effort made to conceal it, sent down for a glass of wine which was served by the same guy as sorted out my luggage so I assume they run the place on 2 people with some chambermaids in the morning. Continental Breakfast is included in the rate and you can have it served in your room, but as there was nowhere to sit and not being a breakfast fan I skipped it, maneuvering round the shower was challenge enough! There is a mini-bar, they charge for water which is not stored in the fridge. Wardrobe space is at a premium, if you are staying more than one night and there are 2 of you, you'll struggle They do use duvets on the beds though which I thoroughly approve of. Would I go back? No Would I recommend this hotel, no unless you really do want to be in that particular part of Notting Hill and your stay is short.

title: Intimate and Amazing
text: We booked this hotel for an overnight stay for a 40th birthday. From the moment we arrived they could not have been more friendly and helpful. The room overlooked a central garden in a Notting Hill terrace and had a 4 poster bed, roll-top bath and loads of space. Each room is unique and charming and decorated to a high standard. There is an honesty bar in the living room that is quiet and truly relaxing. We had a fantastic time. Without doubt the most enjoyable stay we have had in a hotel. Highly recommended.

title: Decent stay
text: Decided to try this hotel for business trip instead of the traditional faceless chains. It is certainly very quaint and charming. Quiet location although there were building works around. You can definitely hear the traffic with the open window. Rooms are quite small but extremely adequate. No issues although you need to take care with the steps. Quite steep at times. My room 21 was tiny but bright and airy. It is definitely not a business hotel but still full of mod cons. Had lunch in the hotel and it was really nice. They serve breakkie in the lounge and really good. Certainly recommend this place.

title: Nice location
text: This is a simpatic hotel, the room was nice, the breakfast can be better. The location is the best, is quiet and you are close to every shops and porto bello market. You have a tube too no very far. I can recommend this hotel to my friends.

title: Exclusivity in a Perfect Location!
text: I was taken to the Portobello Hotel for my birthday last year and had the most romantic experience. The hotel is situated on a quiet road just away a short walk from the buzzing Portobello market. It has the character of Nottinghill coupled with the sophistication of a top class boutique hotel. I was impressed with the bedroom (Colonnial Room) which had a raised level bathroom with a sauna and jacuzzi. The bedroom furniture was totally original and gave the room real character. The breakfast experience was a memorable one, in a large sunlit room with high-ceilings and excellent service. In the evening we dined at the restaurant "Julies" which was a few minutes walk from the hotel but had great character and style. I would highly recommend this hotel and look forward to returning myself one day...!!! charming sophisticated hip romantic

title: Very nice quiet location, good hotel
text: This is a nice little hotel in a very nice and quiet area of London. Many shops around but not as stressful noisy and polluted like the other areas in London. We loved the Location. Within walking distance of Hyde Park. The hotel has a once flair, you have to like antiquities though. The bed i had made quite some noise because it was old and wooden. My friends bed was very soft. Both our bathrooms were on the super small size, this is what we did not like. What we liked very much: Location, the view outside my room into the nice little and quiet park, the wonderful and delicious , relaxing breakfast. Friendly staff. The good quality linen and bathroom amenities. The honesty bar. Cleanliness of the room. The nice keys, not to have a card can be really nice... No issues with that The good working easy to access wifi Thanks for a nice stay!

title: Quaint hotel with exceptional staff
text: This is a charming and quaint little hotel. From the minute we arrived we were treated warmly by the staff. Since it was our first visit to London we were not familiar with the area. Alex was a gem! She made excellent recommendations on what sights to visit and made sure we knew how to get there. When we returned from a long day she had a smile on her face and wanted to hear all about our experiences. The 2 rooms we had were very small but adequate. The bathroom in Room 11 is very small and it is hard to maneuver and the shower was very hard to adjust but the staff made up for the inconvenience. The location is lovely-quiet residential area and a short walk to restaurants and stores. You will not be disappointed if you stay here. So glad it was our first experience with London.

title: Nice hotel
text: Nice hotel in a nice location. We just stayed there for one night at the Japanese Room which is underground and has its own patio. The bed was super comfortable and the furniture in the bedroom very nice. The spa bathroom in this Japanese Room is amazing!!! Only one bad thing that coincides with another review. The staff has some kind of weird arrangement with a taxi company. The taxi wanted to charge us 75 pounds to Heatrow when a black cab charges you 45 pounds including luggage. Bare in mind that this is an expensive hotel that will cost you 240 pound per night including continental breakfast.

title: Charming boutique hotel
text: Most charming boutique hotel in the fashionable Notting Hill. Staff very helpfull, kind and attentive to their guests. Yes, rooms are small, but very very nice and charming decorated, bed is absolutely perfect and when you in the evening return to your room, the bed is made and slippers and kimono is ready for you. Breakfast in your room is an option without extra cost - otherwise served in the "library" where you also can have your afternoon tea and/or the "before-going-out-for-dinner-drink". I absolutely can recommend this place, and will certainly return (hopefully very soon). Thank you to all the staff at Portobello Hotel for an excellent stay :-) I am now addicted to your good service. PS - good luck to Douglas with his new job :-)

title: Beautiful little hotel
text: Stayed in newly refurbished room 1, lower ground floor but plenty of natural light (no photos on their website yet). Gorgeous room with little courtyard with incredible sea shell decorations, open bath and 2 sinks (separate loo!), big comfy bed, indulgent bath products, creative and eclectically decorated. Perfect stroll back from an evening at Holland Park Opera. A great London find. And they even gifted us a bottle of Prosecco as it was our 15th wedding anniversary. Can't fault it.

title: Boutique luxury
text: We stayed in room 16, a gorgeous room with a circular bed and amazing bath. The staff were lovely and welcoming and the breakfast delicious. We loved the unique and friendly feeling with touches like the honesty bar. A fab hotel and great value for money. We will return.

title: Gorgeous hotel, great location!
text: This lovely hotel was located just a few minute walk (or 2 minute taxi ride) from the Portobello Road Tube Station, and a few minutes to all the funky Portobello Road shops and cafes. We loved the hotel design which gave the rooms and hotel an intimate yet cozy feel, and the service we received was 5 stars, right from our check in to check out. Our room had a large desk and fast wi-fi, both which were comfortable enough to work from. However, my highlight was the wonderful bath in our room, which felt really romantic and indulgent. We especially enjoyed the relaxed, yet delicious buffet breakfast each morning. I highly recommend this hotel if you are looking for either a hotel to work from in West London, or for a wonderful and relaxed romantic escape.

title: Old, Tired and so Over Priced - Not like the photos
text: This hotel looked lovely on the site, but the reality was very different. It is not charming, but old and tired and ridiculously over priced for what you get. The rooms are all tiny as on arrival we were so disappointed and asked to be changed (£300 a night and no room to put a suitcase) but found all the rooms were of the same size and comprised of the same tired old furniture and fake dusty antiques. This is a tourist trap to be avoided.

title: Fabulous
text: We absolutely loved this hotel. It's faded elegance is such a refreshing change from many other London hotels. We had a gorgeous circular bed with a sweet balcony and a huge bath in our room. Beautiful, a little bit expensive but just lovely. Staff were kind and pleasant but not intrusive and I can't wait to go back!

title: Amazed
text: I am amazed hotel management have not responded to the latest review nearly 2 weeks after it was posted. I sympathize with the poster and hope all turns out well, but it says something about the vigilance of hotel management that they don't care or are still unaware how important these reviews are to their business.

title: AVOID
text: Our stay in the Portobello Hotel was the first night of our honeymoon before we flew out to Florence and my husband had emailed the hotel to inform them of the purpose of our stay. When we arrived in the hotel we were not welcomed warmly, a member of staff was hoovering the hallway and the gentleman on reception asked him to turn the hoover off in quite a demeaning tone. Not a good first impression! The man on reception asked the purpose of our visit, we said we were on honeymoon and that we were going out to Florence the next day. We were excited and still on a high from our big day, however he responded with an aloof 'interesting' which somewhat burst our bubble! The room was very small, however, we expected this from previous reviews. The bathroom was tiny but clean. After an afternoon of walking around the area we returned to the room for a late siesta before going out for dinner. Unfortunately this was disturbed by a huge amount of noise coming from the basement of the hotel. This included noise from a kitchen and also building/renovation work. We were staying on the ground floor (room 5) so this was right below us. Breakfast was decent and the beds were comfy enough, but this is what you would expect for a near 200 pounds a night. We left the next morning and found that our greeting and service in our hotel in Florence were above and beyond the Portobello Hotel. We didn't expect upgrades etc, but we did expect to be congratulated on our marriage when directly asked the purpose of our stay. All in all the Portobello Hotel really disappointed us. We had chosen the Hotel carefully for the best possible start to our honeymoon, but it did not deliver. AVOID.

title: Amazing Hotel, great backstory and fantastic service
text: I stayed here in February of 2015 as we had a bad experience with another hotel. We booked a room here last minute and boy oh boy am I glad we did! Not only did they fit us in without problem, last minute on a Saturday night, but they also upgraded us to a premiere suite as the guests had stayed on longer than expected in the room that was meant for us. We arrived in our room on the top floor after the receptionist had carried our bags up the stairs while we went in the lift. The room was absolutely beautiful and the design was very quaint and, without sounding completely cheesy, quite delightful. There was an array of snacks and a minibar, all reaonably priced considering the quality of the products. The free standing rolltop bath was gorgeous and, if that's not for you, then there was a shower and bathroom, albeit a tiny bit pokey. We talked to the staff about the hotel and discovered that Alice Cooper, amongst many other celebs, had stayed in our room and kept his python in the bath!! We had breakfast the next day (continental) which was perfect, presentation was amazing. The stay was great, and the memories even greater, not sure I ever want to stay anywhere else now!! The rooms are not the biggest in the world, but the quality and charm of the rooms was more than enough to make up for it. Location is fantastic and the hotel lounge/bar is a stunningly beautiful room.

title: Unique experience
text: In this hotel you feel at home. Excellent staff, excellent breakfast, wonderful ceramic services (old style / vintage). Very high evel of cleanliness and attention to detail. Fresh flowers changed daily. And before leaving the final embrace .... something unique and rare! Thanks The Portobello Hotel!

title: An hidden gem in Notting Hill
text: Fabulous hotel wonderful room overlooking garden with a huge bed that allegedly came from Hampton court. Couldn't believe I was in the hustle and bussel of lively Notting Hill. An Honesty bar that stocked Jordans wines from the vineyards in South Africa couldn't believe my luck. Douglas the Manager was very attentive and made sure that every detail was perfect. Only niggle was the lounge could really do with a redecoration.

title: Great hotel, let down by breakfast
text: I've stayed here three times before and have had a seamless experience each time, but alas on the last occasion the experience was soured by a chaotic breakfast experience blamed on 'lack of staff'. Forty minutes to wait for a coffee? An hour for a full English breakfast. Need to sort out the fundamentals. It's a beautiful, well-appointed hotel, but with chaotic service, the whole thing doesn't work.

title: Weekend Stay
text: Organised and pleasant staff at the Portobello. Our room was clean,spacious and tidy and was equipped with plenty of toiletries etc. We had a Continental Breakfast, plenty of choices and if you requested a Full English Breakfast was available. However, the continental breakfast was lovely.

title: What a great hotel!
text: This is a charming hotel! The decor is warm and inviting. Though the rooms are small, they are lovely and ultra clean, and a fresh comforter is put on the bed daily. I was thrilled to return to my cozy nest each evening. The staff was very helpful, the service great, and the neighborhood is terrific. I plan to return and can't wait to try one of the special rooms!

title: Comfortable townhouse hotel in a smart corner of London
text: The property - a set of townhouses in a quiet residential street in Notting Hill, five minutes walk from the tube. Decor is smart, quality, homey. Staff welcoming and cheerful. Dining/sitting area very like a house drawing room. The room - a lesser grade room on the first floor front. About 180 sq feet, dark red wallpaper, two double floor length windows that opened for air. Clean, smart, comfortable. The bed - excellent super king sized bed, soft and welcoming, first class cotton sheets, excellent duvet, all round top quality. The bathroom - a minute shower-only space, barely room to turn around, but functional. Powerful shower, quality soaps, towels OK but a little tired. Ambient noise and light - on the street side of the hotel so steady but low level traffic noise from the busy road at the end of Stanley Gardens was audible, and slightly intrusive. Thick curtains, but not light-proof so bring a sleep mask. Overall - a cosy comfortable and welcoming stay.

title: small single but great service
text: I stayed at the Portobello for weekend and was very impressed. The staff was very nice and room service was excellent. The breakfast is your basic bread and jam but the avocado salad I ordered for dinner was delicious. The hotel is well located in Notting Hill and has rooms overlooking a very charming garden (the birds wake you up - not traffic!) The only downside, if you request a single, is the size of the room. The space is quite small but the hotel makes up for it. Oh, if you don't feel like lugging your laptop, they have a computer in the downstairs lounge where you can check messages.

title: Mansion Hotel in the middle of Notting Hill
text: We were attending a friend’s wedding nearby and did not fancy staying in the ‘usual’ hotels nearby. If you decide to stay west side of London I would highly recommend this Hotel. It is quite, one minute away from the Portobello Road, great restaurants nearby, and easy access to the rest of London. But the great thing is the rooms!! Enjoy

title: Lovely but shame about Mrs Moody Chops
text: We stayed here for a couple of nights in the Round Room with the "Victorian Bathing machine". Everything about the stay was wonderful - except one incredibly stroppy woman at the reception desk who seemed to think you were taking up her time just by checking in! I think she may even be the owner!! I vowed I would mention it in a review because it was made the difference between a wonderful stay and one marred by that memorable disappointment. In this service oriented business I just dont understand how staff can fail to understand the importance of ATTITUDE.

title: A truly romantic hotel
text: We stayed in the victorian four poster bed room. Wow what a room, just beautiful. The whole place has such a lovely feel to it. Its romantic, classy and decadent. It was my birthday when we stayed and we had lunch at their sister company "julies restaurant" when we arrived, the lady that worked at the hotel paid for a glass of champagne for us as it was my birthday. A lovely genuine touch. A wonderful weekend inc the restaurant which was out of this world. Really love this hotel and would stay again!. Lovely breakfast, good service, clean and comfortable.

title: Great Hotel, Great Area
text: We stayed for 2 nights at the Portobello Hotel and we're really glad we stayed here. The first night was my birthday and we went to Julie's Restaurant which is only about a 10 minute walk away - highly recommend it. The room was lovely and I disagree with some of the other reviews that it needs updating, I found it all added to the charm of the place. The only thing that my partner and I didn't like about this hotel was the breakfast. The Continental Breakfast is included in the price, but the Full English is not - they charge £15 each for this. At £200 per night, we found this to be a little cheeky, to say the least!

title: Lovely spot
text: Krisztian and Alex were so lovely to us. Room service is no extra charge which is excellent for lazy mornings and weary nights. Complimentary biscuits, coffee, and water in the room + cushy robes. The rooms are all unique and adorable. Victorian decor (and sometimes teeny facilities- one of our rooms on the 4th floor was slanted at the roof like an attic

title: Happy honeymooners
text: My husband and I stayed at the hotel for one night in August 2016 - and it was an amazing experience! We mentioned we were on our honeymoon and they upgraded us to a beautiful pinky/lilac-coloured suite with a four-poster canopy bed and a stunning old Victorian tub. We were so impressed and grateful! After ten days of traveling through Europe it was actually the first upgrade we had gotten. The room was comfortable and had a beautiful view of the park out back. It was in a great location with cute shops and pubs only a short walk away. And the room had AC! This was my 5th time in London but I've never been in such a nice hotel - we will be returning for sure!

title: Great room, fantastic bed! Place to stay to discover Portobello Road
text: We booked the hotel as we needed somewhere to stay for Saturday night as we were visiting the Ginstitute on Portobello Road. We also wanted to treat ourselves to a boutique hotel so were prepared to spend a bit more on the room and we were not disappointed! Although the best rooms are not cheap, we were given room 13 on the 1st floor which is located at the back of the hotel. The views out of the windows are stunning looking out onto trees and private gardens and it is also very peaceful too. Sadly the back windows and doors are locked due to health and safety but the view is great. Room 13 has an amazing four poster bed which has a mattress that sits around 3-4 feet off the floor so you are provided with a set of small steps to allow you to climb into bed! It feels like you are sleeping on a cloud when you go to bed...quite magical. I did ask the hotel the provenance of the bed and they informed me it had come from Hampton Court in the past. I'm not sure whether that is folklore or fact but it is romantic to think that Henry VIII may have once slept in the bed with one of his 6 wives! What fun...and it is worth the room just for the bed! You won't forget it... The room was well equipped and spacious. We did experience a small issue with the lighting in the toilet & shower area which the hotel was not able to rectify. It didn't spoil our visit though, it was just a little inconvenient but the hotel were quick to suggest alternatives to use another room, another bathroom but in the end we decided to stay in room 13 as we loved it so much and they took £40 off the cost of the room and also offered a free 'hot' breakfast in the morning. Continental breakfast is offered in the room rate and you can have it delivered to your room free of charge or you can go to the breakfast room on the ground floor. We decided to take breakfast in the breakfast room, which had a peaceful atmosphere with a good selection of food and drink. The scrambled eggs and salmon on toast was done to perfection, would definitely recommend that! Service in general was very good, people were on hand to help when requested and Keith on the front desk was most helpful in addressing the issue of our lighting outage. I expect parking could be an issue during the weekdays as it is mostly resident permit holder parking in the surrounding streets. But if you visit for a Saturday evening I think you will have no issues as resident parking is suspended from 13:30pm Saturday afternoon and free all day Sunday. We were able to park right outside (arrived at 12:30 Saturday) the hotel at no charge which also added to the experience. I would recommend the Portobello Hotel if you are planning to visit the general area of Notting Hill and of course Portobello Market. Portobello Road is approx 5 mins walk from the hotel and there is plenty to see and do in the local area just minutes from the hotel. A great place to stay and we would stay there again.

title: Notting Hill
text: Good hotel to stay at in Notting Hill area. Shower facilities are small but clean. Ask for room on first floor with walk out patio. Elevator was not working great and they don't have a lot of people to help with luggage More like a B&B

title: Charming with Reasonable
text: After staying in Dublin, my beau and I flew to London to spend his Birthday in the Portobello Hotel, in Notting Hill. It is very small, quiet and felt like staying in someone's house rather than an hotel. Our room was bright and cheerful, the bathtub in the middle of the room. Definitely for couples only!!! We ordered breakfast up to our room every morning and the coffee, fruits and croissants were delicious as was the presentation of all silver service pieces. It was fun to walk around the area, go to the Portobello Road antique market, look in to all the lovely shops, and some cozy and delicious restaurants. We could walk to Kensington Palace, and the bus stops to everywhere were a block away, and taxis bountiful. I highly recommend to people who want to avoid the hustle and bustle of being in heart of London, and want to hear birds chirping in the morning and flowers blooming everywhere.

title: Pure Class and Beauty
text: When you arrive in Stanley Gardens, you discover that The Portobello Hotel is a magnificent beautiful Georgian building, and you can't help thinking of Mary Poppins and the Banks' family home when you look along the terrace. We travelled as a party of three (two adults and an eleven year old), and we were kindly assigned two rooms opposite each other. In the 'grown ups' room we had an exquisite four poster bed, beautifully ornate and so incredibly comfortable. Pure luxury! Another fabulous feature was the view out of the bedroom sash windows, in front of which was a seating area, across the private gardens behind the hotel. Add to this the luxurious bathroom accessories - dressing gowns and towels that are super soft, and another lovely touch - full sized bottles of top end bathing products. I was also particularly taken by the fact that the staff had clearly anticipated the needs of our eleven year old's room - he had a mini bar and snacks that were age appropriate and safety locks had been activated on the windows overlooking the street. A small gesture, but it meant that our child's safety had been considered. The vibe and ambience of the hotel is that of a home away from home, there is an honesty bar in the drawing room complete with snacks. We had our breakfast in our room, just as we would as a family, but there is the option to have breakfast in the drawing room that looks out onto the garden. The General Manager, Douglas and his team are the greatest asset. They are very discreet, very professional and nothing is too much trouble. If you are looking for modern and minimalist, The Portobello is not for you, because this is a property that has been lovingly and sympathetically restored to showcase Englishness at its most quintessential. I just adore it and can't wait for the opportunity to stay again.

title: Almost 5/5
text: Quaint hotel in a great location. Probably best to ask for the garden facing room as mine was noisy. Breakfast is good, coffee in the jug best, lunch a disappointment. Room cleaning and bed turning down service excellent! Front desk so helpful!

title: Not sure how this is a 5 star property
text: Booked through Mr & Mrs Smith the 'better room', our flight was delayed and we ended up coming in just before midnight and the lovely guy on duty was very helpful and took us to our room after the receptionist came to sign us in: we were apparently upgraded to the 'great room' - not sure how this was an upgrade, mind you it looks nothing like the photos. Like most properties in London, space is limited, but when you're in a 5 star hotel you expect a bit of space, what they do have in space they didn't really know what to do with, the furniture is awful, tired, outdated and in a great need of a revamp, even though apparently this room has been renovated!! Not sure adding a large bathtub in a room the size of the bedroom with wasted space: leaving literally an inch for the shower and toilet (having to leave the door open to be able to use it) qualifies as a renovation! The interiors just hurt my eyes, the TV awkwardly placed on the wall, I can't believe this place is on Mr and Mrs Smith and highly rated as well! The 'breakfast' is a dingy grey drab sitting place that's more fitting for a student dorm! Don't get me started on the breakfast, there's no toaster, forget the food, it's literally old bread, microwaved croissants and juice, ooh and the only decent thing there: fruit yoghurt made for the hotel, along with the chocolates they leave in your room (again made by a local nearby shop). This place seriously needs a decent investment to revamp everything, the corridors are ridiculously narrow enough for only one person, you have to go through 2 fire doors to get to the red lift (that looks more fitting in a brothel). The room doesn't get cleaned as I noticed a pile of combed hair on the bathroom floor when we came back the next day post lunch. For the price and location you expect way more - I don't recommend staying here at all. Shame because the reception staff are actually really lovely - Alexandra is very helpful, genuinely sweet and offered places to check out in the area.

title: Loved it there!
text: First of all, the excellent staff at Portobello hotel made my stay so very pleasant. No exception, they all were very friendly, smiling, and always willing to help. The hotel itself is really lovely, with attention to detail, my room was really nice, with a comfortable bed, and a bath, breakfast was excellent, and last but not least, the location is good. Only compliments!

title: Expensive and Average
text: Our room was small and the bathroom was tiny- far too small for 2 people. The first night a 'humming' type noise woke us both every 2 hours and although the hotel fixed the problem there was no offer of compensation- a drink on the house would've sufficed. In fact it was suggested that if we had to move to a 'better' room we would have to pay the difference. Good location in Notting Hill but I wouldn't return.

title: Thank you to the wonderful staff at the Portobello hotel
text: I had an amazing (but too short) time at the Portobello hotel a few nights ago. The staff was so warm and friendly and made my boyfriend's surprise 40th birthday stay very special. The Exceptional room was large, quite comfortable bed and nicely equipped. Good amenities. The wifi worked well during the stay and the hotel is in a great location within walking distance of many nice shops, restaurants and the famous Portobello market. I highly recommend this hotel!

title: A wonderful stay in the Portobello hotel
text: Just on my way home for a 1 night stay in The Portobello Hotel, as I was in London for a friend's birthday. What a brilliant experience! The hotel is in a beautiful part of London, which is very pleasant to walk around, and easy to get to from Notting Hill Gate tube station. I stayed in the recently refurbished room 34 which was absolutely stunning. The bed was superbly comfortable and I had a wonderful night's sleep. The bathroom is something else - it has and enormous walk in shower and a free standing bath tub, as well as beautiful toiletries and decor, Overall the room had a real feeling of luxury about it. This morning I ordered the complimentary continental breakfast in bed which arrived very promptly and was lovely, it has everything I could have wanted. The hotel is clearly very well managed and the staff couldn't have been more helpful, especially Alex on reception who was very friendly and welcoming and went above and beyond to sort out transport for my evening's plans. Overall I can highly recommend this hotel and look forward to a return visit.

title: Perfect location and great staff
text: I just came back from an awesome trip to London and loved my stay here. The room and accommodations were exactly as advertised and the reception service was great. They were super friendly and accommodating. Breakfast was also a pleasant surprise, beautiful presentation and just the right amount. Tips on getting there: After arriving at LHR, I took the heathrow express straight from terminal 3. It was a quick trip to Paddington and then a short tube ride to Notting Hill. Just be aware there are some steps involved so make sure you can carry your luggage. Exit the Tube to the portobello market and a few blocks later you're there!

title: Lush
text: If you are in London, then stay at the Portobello, whose rich rock & roll history is well-maintained by the gallantry of Giuseppe. He tended to my every wish and made sure I was safe and comfy. His knowledge of the interesting history of the legendary hotel is vast. Giuseppe's manners are impeccable, too. As are Ken's, the lovely gent who greeted me with amusing charm and bid me adieu with friendly style! They make me want to visit again! Oh - and it's true what is said about the beds: they are outrageously comfortable and sumptuous. I am looking forward to my next visit!

title: Excellent hotel
text: Quiet hotel with great staff and lovely rooms that are very clean with all mod cons,hotel has a lift but also has steps to main door so not ideal for people with wheel chairs,very close to portobello market witch is great,also close to bars and restaurants,I will go back again.

title: Very nice and cozy hotel
text: It was very nice that they left some chocolates and a note of weather information on the pillows. The hotel room had a high ceiling and tall window with a little terrace to come out. One or two paintings on the walls inside the room. Nice amenities of normal bottles of shampoo, hair conditioner and body wash, which I felt the finest on my hair during the trip. The bed was very nice and clean. Free wifi without pass word or anything. Staffs were very nice and helpful. We would visit here again.

title: Always welcome here
text: Second time we have stayed here, asked for same room as before & we were assured it. I have stayed in big 5* hotels as well as tiny guest houses, The Portobello is the least pretentious place I've ever stayed. I'm sure whether you are famous or Mr & Mrs average like me & my husband, you're treated the same. Warm welcome, nothing is too much trouble & the rooms are eclectic & very comfortable. A joy to stay there.

title: Relaxing boutique style
text: After a long flight from Melbourne Australia, the family of five arrived Wednesday morning to be met by the friendly staff at Portobello Hotel in Notting Hill. Beautiful rooms, quite and private in its own way. Well equipped room with a home cozy pantry. We loved the breakfast and a tip is to reserve time and order the breakfast from the menu the night before. Our friends stayed the hotel two weeks later and they had the same positive experience as us. Thank you to the wonderful staff and management, we will definitely be back.

title: Stylish and stunning
text: This is a lovely townhouse hotel just a short walk from Notting Hill Gate. It was like staying in a private house

title: Perfect for a romantic getaway
text: The Portobello is a small boutique hotel, perfect for a romantic getaway. We got room 16 which was really lovely. Lots of space, great garden view and amazing four poster bed. The bathroom is tiny, really tiny. But there's a wonderful tub outside of it. The breakfast's croissants are delicious and service is very attentive. Lots of nice restaurants very close to it and Portobello road is steps away. Not a place I would go with kids but definitely a great choice for couples.

title: My favorite Hotel in London
text: The warmest hotel ever ! All the staff are extremely kind and I feel to be at home . Every room have a different style , the atmosphere is unique. The Hotel is very closed to Portobello Road and Notting Hill Gate. I used to stay there every two weeks since 9 years ago and is actualy my second home !

title: Keystone House ~ Review
text: I stayed there last night ... £63 for a 4 person room for one night (so £16 for me as we booked as 4 persons) ... Very clean ... Adjacent bathroom facilities were immaculate ... Very friendly staff ... Recommended ... I was there for the football and live in Hereford ...One night stay ... Two times bunk beds that we stayed in are as per the photo ...

title: class place
text: Loved the location of it and price of it. Staff were friendly and loved the pub next door. Beds werent as comfy as they could have been but you get what you pay for. I definatley would recommend it. :)

title: Keystone House
text: Stayed here for one night in a private room. It was very decent for the price. The room came with en-suite, lockers and air-con. Staff at the front desk were very friendly and informative. You get 10% off at the pub next door by showing your room key. I didn’t rate it as excellent because there was mould growing on the walls and there was a lot noise from the outside. However £44.50 for a private room in central London is an excellent price so I would recommend staying here.

title: Great location, fair price
text: As everybody says, Keystone House is located conveniently just a few meters from Kings Cross station. We stayed at a double-bed private room. We were worried that this room has no windows. Actually it had two windows, but one of them is impossible to be closed 100% and lets cold air in, a bit. But there is an electrical heater to fight this issue. The bed was comfortable, but other than that the room is pretty small. Not even a space to put off your jacket or trousers. But price is very good.

title: Great location - that's it
text: For one night in London, it sufficed. I wouldn't do it again. Two (one male and one female) stayed in a 8 bed dorm in Dec. 2014. I'll list the pros and cons of our experience below. Pros: - Excellent location near Kings Cross - Somewhat cheaper than alternatives - Easy access to a Starbucks. Which you'll need for wifi if you stay here. - Free luggage room prior to stay (not after) Cons: - No elevator (we had 50 pound bags, as London was the first stop on a two week extravaganza) - Wifi only in reception - No age limit (there seemed to be a lot of people well past their 20's) - Rooms were cramped and while not dirty, didn't exactly seem updated or fresh - Limited outlets (I had to charge my phone in my travel companion's bed) - No under-bed lockers (I'm partial to the cages under the bed that hold luggage) - Malfunctioning door (while we were there, the door was broken so the reception had to buzz you in or out every time. Annoying.) - The staff weren't bad but it just seemed like they didn't really have everything together. They seemed understaffed (especially with the door situation) and they couldn't find or key for the first two hours and we had to use a house key without a fob, requiring us to knock on the door to the reception to be let out of the stairwell. Not the end of the world, but not great either. - Security: while I was asleep, my travel companion says that a man who was not staying in our room stumbled in, muttered something, and then left. So there. It worked for a night but I wouldn't go back.

title: Great location
text: We only stayed one night in an ensuite room, it was ok & met our needs for the night. We were on a budget but getting our bags up the stairs was painful but the location made up for anything else & the staff were more than helpful.

title: This is why I keep staying here.
text: Very friendly staff. Very good prices compared to most of London hostels with female dorms. Clean. Warm blankets in cold London winter :) Enough space for each person. Dorm that fits 16 still gives enough privacy by having a thick wall that splits 8+8 and a side panel to each bed. Keeps renovating. Ground floor has all changed. Painters painting the dorm just while I was there. Didn't bother me and it means they keep taking care of their guests actually, trying to improve things year by year. Great location. What else? The only kinda negative thing was the breeze in the shower/toilets area. Which is good to keep air clean and dry but water should be slightly hotter then or you freeze unless you are under the shower :)

title: Funky little hostel near Kings Cross
text: Myself and a band-mate booked Keystone House to stay in after we'd played a show in St Pancras. It was very cheap (£60 for a Friday night, for the two of us, I think it was) and frankly we just needed somewhere to sleep after rockin' the bejesus out of our devoted audience. *cough* Anyway - after* booking, I started reading the reviews on TripAdvisor and felt a bit faint. They ranged from 'Thank God I only stayed here for one night' to 'The worst accomodation I've ever had the misfortune to stay at' and everything in between. It was a fairly narrow spectrum. So it's fair to say I had low expectations. Which meant I was pleasantly surprised to find a perfectly adequate hostel when we arrived. No blood on the sheets, as described by another reviewer. No bed-bugs. Nothing that really gave away the fact that this was a cheapo hostel. Except maybe the smell in our windowless box room. There was an eye-watering funk in the air when we arrived. It smelled a bit like someone had washed a St. Bernard and popped it in the laundry basket to hang out later - then forgotten about it for a week. A damp, musty odour. Maybe with a touch of sewage? I'm not sure. Let's just say it wasn't something you'd want to bottle and sell. Frankly I'd had enough to drink** that I just collapsed on the bottom bunk (we'd booked a private room with en-suite) and slept like a baby - except with less crying and only the occasional toilet-mishap. The (single) bed was comfy and the en-suite shower was alright, too. Worth noting that they didn't provide towels or shower-gel. Luckily we're resourceful chaps and used the bedsheets to dry ourselves. If all the guests did that, perhaps that'd explain the wet-laundry funk in the room. Anyway - it was cheap, I slept well, showered well and didn't pick up any serious diseases that I'm aware of. Would I stay here again? Yeah. I think I would. *Yes, I read the reviews AFTER booking. Yes, it IS ridiculous to do it that way round, but you've got to live on the edge sometimes, haven't you?.Don't judge me. ** We stumbled to The Scottish Stores pub next door. Good music (if you like 80s pop classics), good booze (if you like booze) and a buzzin' atmosphere. Recommended.

title: Not great
text: I'm used to hostels but this place wasn't great for the price we paid. Even though we paid for a two-person room (bunk bed), we might as well should have stayed in a dorm. Walls were thin, we could not talk in our room because neighbours could hear us. There were no windows in our room and it felt stuffy. I have to say great location and convenient for public transport but that's the only plus point. Just know what you're getting yourself into before booking this hostel.

title: Glad my travel plans changed and i only stayed one night
text: Easy to locate, despite the scaffolding - but warning folks - they may be working on the outside, but they BADLY need to work on the onside. The staff are friendly enough,but this is basic beyond belief. The room was tiny with two old changing room lockers as wardrobes (they didn't lock). Single glazed windows allowing the workmen on the scaffolding a room with a view. Beds have poor mattresses. I ain't no Princess, but I felt the bed springs all not long. The sheets were clean, Overall the room was not to what I would call basic standard - the same pillow case littering the stair case the day after I arrived with dust and dirt ingraining the very old paint work. Be warned - you do not get towels. You can buy one for £5 - that you could split peas through - but you get to keep it! I ended up showering the next day and using my bed sheet to dry myself. The shower room - I had a private bathroom. Where do I start - the hairs on the paint work, the shelf that is too low to the sink, the rusting metal work........I could go on, but I think you get the point. Now, before people go thinking, but it's a hostel....yes, it is. And yes it is cheap. But there is no excuse for a lick of paint and a bottle of bleach. Had I been staying longer than the one night I would have needed to find alternative digs. On a plus - there is a deal with the cafe two doors down for breakfast. £4.50 for a full English, toast and tea/coffee. Best part of the visit, but then I had left the hostel by this time. I won't be back.

title: Awful smell, not as I remember it...
text: Myself and my boyfriend stayed in the hostel for 4 nights. I had stayed in this hostel with some friends 6/7 years previous and remember it being a very positive experience - unfortunately the place has not been well kept! We arrived in from our late flight to find that the room was small, run down and uncomfortably warm (aircon did not seem to be doing much!). Like many of the other reviewers, we too found a suspicious stain on the bedding and when we reported it to the cleaners they did not seem that bothered about this and said they will "see what they can do". By far the worst part of our stay was the horrendous, overpowering stench coming from the bathroom - we asked to move rooms immediately and were told we could do this in the morning - but this never ended up happening. We were told this was coming from the ventilation system, again staff did not seem that bothered. We booked via booking.com and were told we would have breakfast included in the price - we had to fight for this to happen as staff claimed this was out of date and did not offer this anymore. We were eventually allowed a basic breakfast in the café next door. The main draw of this hostel is definitely location, it was very easy to access most areas of London via Kings Cross. Apart from that, it is a real shame they have let this place go dramatically....

title: Total disgrace
text: I did have enough time to wright my review the day I returned from Keystone and I hope that something changed. All started on the 21nd of November 2015. We were group of 4 male friends having a late night flight to London. We reserved 4 bunk beds in a room with 8 beds. In the reservation form I let them know that we’ll arrive at 1 a.m. on the 22nd of November. We arrived at the hostel exactly at 00:54. There were two guys in the reception TOO BUSY to get their eyes out of their laptop screens and look at our way. I came up to them and said that we had a reservation, to get the response from the blond guy "Check in is at 14:00". He didn't even ask the name that the reservation was on. Nothing! Then I tried to explain to him what was going on. Then we had to pay for the whole stay in advance but they asked for cash because the credit card machine was broken but HOW to pay in cash we just arrived from the airport! After a long process they guy handed us 2 pair of keys (we were 4) and he showed us which way to go. He didn't show us the facilities nor our rooms. We sneaked in our room after a long search and at 02:35. The room was on the top floor and there is no elevator. In the room were 3 guys who were working nearby and living there for many days. There was also an elder man living by himself there. He was having some trouble with his health because he was receiving medication. In the second night he PIED NEXT TO MY BED. Yes, he did. I was not there but my friends saw him. We immediately informed the reception and the only thing they did was to tell us that they were fully booked. They didn't offer us refund and we couldn't afford to book another hostel so we stayed there. We kindly asked to look after the problem and the hateful odor, but the house keeping never showed up. At the end I want to say that it's not good for the other guest to have people in a long stay. The other guys that I told you were living there. One of them brought his girlfriend for a few nights and there were squeaky noises

title: Noisy construction, dirty sheets, awful mattress, not as advertised
text: I’ve been staying in hostels for the past 2 months so I’m not new to this game. I know to expect simple accommodations, but this was just unreasonably awful. We arrived to find the room was much smaller and shabbier than advertised on the website. Pulling back the blanket revealed a sheet with several gross mystery stains on it (see photos). The mattresses were worn and lumpy making it nearly impossible to get a good nights sleep. The rooms had no air conditioning despite the website stating otherwise. In order to keep from over heating, the windows had to be cracked exposing us to the loud street noise below. The next morning, Sunday at 9 AM, we were awoken by constructing workers hammering and drilling right outside of our window! The workers were even opening our windows in order to paint them! Completely unacceptable to have workers opening windows while guests are inside!!! We left after the first night of our scheduled four night stay. My back hurt from the mattress, I was tired after getting no sleep and being rudely awoken by workers opening our windows, and was absolutely disgusted by the state of the sheets. Some extra minor complaints: They don’t allow alcohol on the premises. The WiFi is not very fast. Don’t stay here. There are plenty of other cheap accommodations that are not an insult to human decency. This place is disgusting.

title: Very bad experience ever
text: I experienced lost luggage in this hotel. Totally irresponsible staff and people in charge. My check in time was 17/9/2018, my beg was red large size fabric material baggage. I hope it was mistaken by someone and please contact me huikeem_lim@yahoo.com or huikeem@gmail.com. Really appreciate if you could return my baggage.

title: Not too bad
text: Stayed here with a friend for 3 nights in November. Not much to do or see near the hostel but it was right across from an underground station and right next door to a sainsburys which were both nice. Most comfortable hostel beds I have ever stayed in. Staff was generally not overly helpful or pleasant. Wifi was spotty at best for most of our stay. Reasonably priced.

title: Great Location, Comfortable Beds, a bit worn and tired
text: This is the second time I have stayed in this hostel, last time being early June 2012. I would say the hostel has gone down somewhat since then. I stayed in the 16 bed female dorm for two nights. +ves: The beds and duvets are very comfy, everything is clean including the bathrooms, lockers are included (but bring a padlock), everything feels quite safe and there is breakfast included.
