The location of this hostel is by far its best asset. It is only a few steps from Kings Cross which has fantastic links to the rest of London, a great base to have. I never had to wait for a shower. Staff were very friendly. -ves: The beds creak a lot, if you have a wriggler above you then I guarantee that you will wake up every few hours. The traffic noise is quite bad if you aren't used to it (bring earplugs), ask for beds 1-8 in the 16 female dorm, as these are a little quieter, although you will still be plagued by sirens at all times of the night. One big thing when I was there, there was a 4am fire alarm. There seemed to be no procedure, no one knew what they were doing, so I dread to think of the case there was a real full blown fire. At the time I stayed, the upstairs green bathroom with the decent shower was out of order. This was a huge huge negative. The other female toilet/showers are cold, drafty, there is mould all over the ceiling, and the shower is an automatic sensored one which does not stay on for longer than 10 seconds. Not good if you want to wash your hair. It does for a very quick wash but no more. Breakfast is an issue in this hostel, on a weekday get there before 9am. On a weekend when the hostel is busier I recommend get there at 8am. One of the days there was no bread left, no cooked food, the milk was sour and off, and the fruit was lacking - I had to go out for breakfast. The breakfast is also worse than Tesco value/Sainsburys basics, the quality of everything is extremely poor. Although, for the price you can't expect much. Overall: I preferred my stay in June, I felt the hostel bathrooms especially have gone downhill and the hostel is in need of a bit of work. I was disappointed with the breakfast quality, however pleasantly surprised at the comfy beds, just a shame they are creaky.

title: Good for budget travellers
text: They are very cheap. We walked there from the street, looking for a place to crash for one night. We have paid 60 pounds for double. Very small rooms in a basement, no bathroom, no window. Free breakfast with lots unhealthy choices but it is enough to start the day. What was ridiculous, WIFI ia not free and they made us pay for storage room. Great location for sightseeing and transportation. Hostel good for one night.

title: Nice chip place to stay in center of London
text: Stayed there for two days, nothing fancy but the crew was very helpful, the beds where comfortable and the room had good temperature. the showers are OK, nothing to write home about but you have your privacy even that there where 3 showers in the same room and never had to wait in line. we where in a room for six and the other peoples where very nice and considerate. bottom line, if you want to stay at the central and not pay too much this is a great place.

title: Worst place of my trip
text: I am no stranger to hostels and don't expect them to be perfectly comfortable, but we absolutely hated our time here. This was the worst hostel I have stayed in in over 4 months of travelling. I think we had a particularly bad experience of this hostel. Our room absolutely stank of sewerage, coming from the bathroom

title: Average hostel
text: The beds were really comfy and the security screen were nice. The dorm room was a little squishy with all the beds and not much room for luggage but it wasn't unpleasant. What was a little annoying was how far the kitchen was from the rooms and the tiny common room. The location was ideal for quick and easy access to the train and underground stations. Staff were also very friendly.

title: Great location and value for money
text: Keystone House is located just a few minutes from Kings Cross Station, so you could not ask for a more convenient location. Due to its popularity, the only room available to us was downstairs and had a bunk bed in it. It was very small with no windows but the air conditioner worked well so it didn't get too stuffy in there. The room was clean and we were close to the shared bathroom facilities. The bathrooms were a bit tired but adequate and there were also laundry facilities that were very handy. The common areas were very neat and clean and the wifi was good (though not available in our room). Breakfast was basic but fine for what we required. Overall I have no hesitation in recommending this hostel for its value for money and great location.

title: Above Average Hostel
text: This hostel is one of London's better ones. The bright spacious common areas, clean sheets and comfortableness of the bed all contributed to a great stay. However the cleanliness of the bathrooms could definitely be improved and the size of the lockers as they were not big enough to fit a standard 50L backpack. Also, be aware that there is no stove or oven in the guest kitchen.”

title: Oops!
text: Booked this as it was close to the Eurostar station and cheap . On reflection it was a mistake and I ended up with an unhappy wife . I’ve stayed in hostels before and on the whole they are ok but this was dirty and grubby with no hot water and a bathroom that should carry a health warning . They did have a roof type terrace so I thought maybe it’s not all bad and it was a warm night however in the window above was the silhouetted figure of someone wiping their bum so I gave that a miss ! My advice unless you’re skint or kinky give it a miss

title: Close proximity to Kings Cross St. Pancras
text: What was good - Very close to Kings Cross, cheapest private room option offered on Hostelworld, air-conditioning in my private room, room and bedding was clean and shared bathroom was clean (and it was cleaned during the day), the wi-fi worked well in my room and the kitchen area. I was given a key and fob so that outside doors could be accessed. I felt my room was secure and there were lockers in my room if I needed them. Room for improvement - There are areas including my room that could do with some modernisation or at the very least sprucing up. The room I was in was noisy with outside and indoor noise, the breakfast situation was never clear and it was not offered everyday. Also, there was a very friendly man who checked me in but I found that generally the staff were not particularly friendly which was a shame. It was very cheap for central London and if you want to be in the heart of the city with excellent transport links, knowing that the accommodation is basic, then it would be a good place to base yourself for a couple of days.

title: Less-than-average Hostel
text: I stayed a night over at Keystone. Reached the place at night and had to rush out of the hostel to catch the morning train. Some quick thoughts: - The staff was friendly and ready to greet us and help us with the late check ins and really early check outs. However we were separated at the 2 ends of the room. Other than that no complains about the service - The toilets were not up to the mark. The water heater handle was broken and the bathroom on my floor basically had one temperature. The nearest bathrooms were two floor down. Overall, the hostel was very average (cramped but clean conditions & friendly staff with the usual amenities listed). The toilets were a turn off which brought it one notch down.

title: Great value, very well located
text: A really good hostel, quiet (but not silent) at night so my sleep wasn't disturbed. The biggest draw is probably the location - extremely close to Kings Cross and St Pancras stations, and either next door or just a few doors down are a small Sainsburys, a cheap fast service pizza place (Pizza Union), McDonalds, Starbucks, Pret a Manger and more. The quality of the showers differ but the more updated looking ones were lovely, and there were always plenty of toilet/shower facilities available.

title: Unable to sleep!
text: Booked a double room

title: Awful
text: Where do I begin... we paid for a private twin room with ensuite. The young hip Hugo was very impolite and seemingly uncaring for the amount of stress he was about to cause giving us the key to what could only be described as a shambles of a room. That was after we witnessed nobody help a young women with two huge suitcases and a backpack struggle to make her way up the stairs. The room itself was bleak, I know its a hostel.. but the window was wide open on a subpar day leaving the room unbearable cold. I carefully climbed up the broken bunk bed ladder to close the window, and then the blinds to find out the blinds were also broken. After about 10-15 minutes I decided I needed to go to the toilet, I opened the door to find out the toilet was actually 2-3 steps down and at the end of narrow opening. I used the toilet, with an awfully weak flush as I had to flush the toilet a few times. I then proceeded to wash my hands to then notice there was nothing to dry my hands on but toilet paper, I reluctantly did so and then went to walk back up the 2-3 steps

title: Good hostel in city center
text: My friend and I slept there for 3 days in a 8 beds room. Pros : Location - Just next to King's Cross, supermarkets and shops. Common room, plugs everywhere, wifi connexion. Beds are comfortable. Cleanness : We were very surprised by the cleanness of the shower and toilets. Immediate hot water. Cons : We were on the last floor and it was freezing in the bedroom ! The windows let cold enter the room, hopefully the duvet was warm. Noise - Located next to King's Cross, it's normal if there's a lot of noise. Just put earplugs and everything's allright ! Wifi - Wifi only available in the common room on the last groundfloor. You have to pay to have it in your bedroom. Good place to stay for one or two nights max. Good and clean hostel for London.

title: Good position and cheap price
text: The position was really Good and also The price But no elevator and i was At The fourth Floor, no plugs near my bed so i couldn t recharge any battery, The lockers were Very Small and unconfortable so I usually needed to use The lockroom downstairs to leave My luggage in a safe piace. They have a Nice Small rooftop and a bar, enjoyable for solo travellers but not really The Best hostel in town.

title: Love it after checking out several in the area
text: I need to stay 1 or 2 nights a week from next April so this weekend's trip was to find somewhere I felt safe and comfortable with wifi as a more mature than average hostal user travelling alone. This is the third place I stayed at and love it. Beds in the dorms are separated to give some sense of privacy. Locker by each bed - not present in other places. Good free wifi - albeit with restricted hours but I knew this when booking. Friendly and helpful staff. Looking forward to spending time here. I don't mind the steps - good exercise. For what I have paid this is fantastic value for money.

title: Cheap stay in a great location
text: Booked Keystone House for a recent trip to London. Just three night stay but have to say it was a great location! So close to King's Cross Station and you can get pretty much anywhere you need to be in London from there. There are also plenty of cafes and restaurants around. Found the staff to be extremely friendly and accommodating - was able to hire and towel and a hairdryer very quickly and easily. The rooms were basic, ours was in the basement so no windows but for the most part the hostel was clean. We were close enough to the common room that we could avail of the free WiFi at all times which was a bonus! Didn't really have the breakfast but the kitchen facility looked adequate too. I didn't really notice much of an issue with noise and overall for the price you pay for accommodation in London I'd have no problem staying here again.

title: Perfect location and great staff
text: Good prices, GREAT location and super-friendly staff. Not a crazy party-hostel, but still quite a good spot to meet people. The staff in the reception were always really helpful and the rooms were clean and nice (once you found them - this place is a maze!). It's not luxuries, but based on the location, staff, free breakfast and price it is still worth a top review!

title: Great Hostel
text: Stayed for two nights. Staff were friendly and professional and free luggage storage was available the morning of arrival and afternoon following check out. Rooms were very comfortable. 8 bed dorm was non-ensuite however bathrooms were clean and there are plenty of showers with no need to queue. Hot Breakfast was free and very good. Location is excellent, opposite the Pentonville Rd Exit of Kings Cross St Pancras- accessed from the Victoria Line platforms. Supermarkets are nearby as is Starbucks and McDonald's which both offer free wifi. Only improvement required is the lockers which are too narrow for suitcases or large rucksacks. They are sufficient for the storage of laptops, suits and other small valuables though.

title: Fab for one!
text: I came down to visit friends and needed somewhere cheap and central to stay. I'm not one to sleep in a room with strangers so got an ensuite to myself which was perfect! I never thought about getting a hostel for one but it worked out great! It was basic but clean and that's all that mattered. It was of course slightly noisy at times but it's a hostel what do you expect? It never affected my sleep. Bed was comfy, shower was good. Would stay again!

title: Location is Perfect
text: Pretty good if you're looking for a cheap place to stay. Wifi in room isn't great but works well downstairs. The showers/bathrooms are a full floor away which is a bit frustrating. Overall fine place if you just need a bed to crash in. However, you can’t get a better location for travel around the city.

title: Noisy
text: check-in very fast with a receptionist very smiling but very difficult to reach the room it looks like you play labyrinth, the arrival of the room the total disappointment, carpet infects, bad smell, a disco bar under the hostel that gives too much noise, breakfast very modest and shy. The only good thing is that the hostel is in central London 100 meters from King's cross st pancras station.

title: Holidays
text: Very bad! We payed 150£ per day for the new year's eve and the double room was too small and without any comfort (no desk no towel no windows, anything!), breakfast was free but it looked very bad. Good position near the station and nothing else.

title: Perfect base if you don't want to miss a train from King's Cross / St. Pancras
text: The location was perfect, very close to King's Cross / St. Pancras station, and there were several mini-markets around this hostel. The receptionist was very informative. The DIY breakfast was very good.

title: Misery
text: We were told at reception to wait and see if our room still had electricity. We were informed that there had been a flood in the basement where our room was. We then had to wonder though a completely dark corridor with water dripping down the walls. Our room was very damp and stuffy and as it was underground we could not even open windows to air it. I started to develop a very sore chest after only a few hours sleep in that room. We asked to be moved but none other room was available. Staff seemed very incompetent and indifferent. Workmen were constantly present during our stay, leaving side doors leading to the rooms open all day. We also had to walk over massive holes on our way kitchen. Generally we found it a very unpleasant place. On our last night there was another flood this time right outside our room which we has to walk under every time we left. Absolutely terrible, will not return!

title: Not friendly, But clean atleast.
text: Considering I have paid infinitely LESS money for hostels in Asia where I've had a pool and beautiful surroundings, my hostel expectations are often unfairly high, however saying that, whilst the room was small, and I don't love bunk beds, the room was very clean, the bed comfortable and the shower pressure excellent (if not the shower space itself a little snug) Noise was okay, we were unfortunately next to a fire exit to what I assume was the smoking terrace, so suffered with a lot of banging doors however nighttime noise was minimal. Having a skylight that we could open electronically was a nice touch, as was the electronically blind. Location is excellent, literally a 2 minute walk straight down from Edgerton (or whatever E name the road is....I cant remember) road exit at kings cross. Security also decent. Biggest failing is the staff and friendliness. There was no "Welcome to London" for us! We didn't care too much as I was born here so....however for tourists this isn't a good first impression. We intereacted with several staff, none of which were overly polite, wished us a nice trip, or ever actually said anything other than the bare minimum. At one point one staff member was talking to us and then turned to deal with someone else, no apology or acknowledgement, and we waited several minutes for him to continue helping us. Rude. I would consider staying here again as the facilities were acceptable (please note here that we didn't use any of the kitchen facilities, so can't comment on those. We literally came trough reception and up to our room, too much to do no time to stop and socialise!) however the rudeness of staff does mean I would look for an alternative out of sheer stubbornness. Prices were similar to a travellodge level of pricing, so if you're not gonna be a "ten quid a night hostel" you need to really up your game.

title: Adequate
text: For a 3 night stay with friends we booked an ensuite room but were not given an ensuite room and no explanation was provided for why not, and we weren't offered to switch when we became aware that an ensuite room was available. It seems that they use two separate booking companies and tend to overbook/double-book certain rooms. Some girls were supposed to have checked out of our room and their belongings had been moved before our check in but they still had the key to our room and let themsleves in later, which was alarming. Building is currently under renovation and getting to the small common room where wifi is provided is like trying to get through a maze of hallways and stairs. There also appears to be no age limit at this hostel, so if you are under 30 and looking for the fun backpacker young folk crowd that you might expect from a hostel, it may not be the case. However, beds were comfortable and rooms and bathrooms were clean, and there was 24 hr reception so for the price it is about what you might expect. Towels are £5 for purchase, but you can borrow hairdryers for free. No breakfast was provided, but I believe this is all advertised by the hostel upfront. The location was good for transporting to other areas, but not much to do in the immediate surrounding area. Also- If you need a cab here, just flag down a black cab and don't bother with the local cab companies, they aren't as dependable when you're trying to leave the King's Cross area.

title: For families, not young travelers
text: Very comfortable beds and the rooms had air conditioning. Breakfast was satisfactory but nothing special. WAS THE LEAST SOCIAL HOSTEL IVE STAYED IN. Was expensive and wasn't really near the touristy areas that you would want to see if you haven't been to London before. I wouldn't go back if I were backpacking with my friends again.

title: Good location, but kinda gross
text: Good points: good location, clean beds and room. Bad points: disgusting bathrooms (often no toilet paper or soap), rude staff that barely looks up at you when you arrive, really cramped rooms, bad wifi.

title: Uncomfortable, not accurate pictures, good location
text: This hostel is located in a central and easily accessible area. We were quite disappointed in our room. The pictures made it seem much nicer than it actually was. The room was tiny, the bed wasn't very comfortable, the shower was not very good and the whole place seemed dirty and cheap. We were not too impressed with these accommodations.

title: Horrible, nobody has to go there
text: In the hostel broke the bag when leaving in custody and slept both nights were horrible. The receptionist was terrible with me and the rooms horrible without good lockers. The bathroom was horrible too, and the people who go there is very violent. The worst staff ever!!!

title: Best hostel I've ever stayed in
text: The hostel was in a great location, directly across the street from an Underground entrance (Kings Cross/St. Pancras station), and a five minute walk from Kings Cross and St. Pancras. The staff was so helpful and friendly! The hostel itself was VERY clean. We stayed for two nights and had a private room with its own bathroom and bunk beds. This is definitely my favorite hostel that I have ever stayed in (and I've stayed in loads). I HIGHLY recommend this hostel to anyone visiting London. The hostel does not provide breakfast, but there is a nice café two doors down that has a cheap breakfast. There is also a luggage storage room with CCTV, which you can use if you have large bags or arrive at the hostel before check-in time (2:00pm). Do be aware that if you are staying on the lower ground floors, that you can hear the underground trains going (which I found to be quite soothing, actually, but if you're a light sleeper you might want to book a different room).

title: Not 100% self-catering. No cooktop or oven. Noisy and Dungeon-like room
text: Good location (super close to a main train station), rooms are clean, air conditioned with a NOISY aircon, and super comfy beds. Our double room was underground with no windows. Noise from the common room always travelled into our room clearly, with other guests still using that area well after curfew, sometimes even past 1am! This hostel was also advertised as having 'self-catering facilities'. However, it was only equipped with a fridge, microwave, kettle, and toaster. We ended up spending ridiculous amounts of money on outside food... As one of our main reason for booking here was to be able to cook it SHOULD NOT be advertised as 'self-catering', luckily we were only there for 3 nights.

title: Friendly staff who made my London trip memorable
text: So I flew into London without any reservations and as it turns out all the hostels were absolutely full. I've wandered for 5hours around London searching for cheap hostel accomodations and was about to give up and sleep at Heathrow airport. I went into Keystone and their staff were so friendly that they truly tried to accommodate me even though they were fully booked for that day. Because of them, I've had a wonderful time in London. I've gotten to know a handful of their staff and they're all really helpful and nice. One of the nicest staff I've met after having backpacked for a couple months around europe.

title: Unhelpful staff
text: I stayed about a week ago and was very disappointed with the staff. Checked-in around 10pm after my flight from Athens. Walked into reception and although there were 2 guys manning the desk they both ignored me because they were watching videos on FB -_- After a few minutes one finally asks if i'm checking in and apologises. I'm easy going so i still smile and make convo about the crappy cold weather. Check in takes about 10 minutes. Cool. I'm given my key, room and bed number. I go up to my room and someone is sleeping in my assigned bed. woohoo!! lol I would've taken another bed but its full house and not sure which bed is free, so i head back downstairs. The shorter blonde guy tells me i have to wake her and tell her to get out of my bed. Not wanting to be on the receiving end of a possibly ugly scene i ask if he can do it. He pokes the girl awake and tells her she's in the wrong bed. Turns out she wasn't. They made a mistake and assigned me the wrong number. lol The real downer of my stay was the storm that supposedly happened a week ago which knocked out the wifi in the street. The staff informed no one of this and we were just meant to accept the fact, there was no wifi/internet. One of the girls staying for an extended period in my dorm said the wifi has been down for a week. I booked a night before my stay, if i had known there was no wifi i would not have stayed here! No warning posts or anything on the website. Ridiculous!! Staff at reception didn't even tell me until i asked. The not so funny thing is, Mcdonalds down the road had perfect wifi. Two girls who live in london who stayed at the same time said there hadn't been a storm in London. Stop with the lies yo! I reckon it might be time to hire new staff, preferably ones who smile and are eager to help. The current ones make you feel like your a hindrance if you ask them a question. Good points would be the location. 2 minutes away from the underground and Mcdonalds lol Beds were comfortable and the view into the street from the girls dorm was pretty cool. The individual bedside lights were good and showers & toilets were clean. Oh and there's a grocery store right next store. The fresh croissants are yum! They also need thicker sheets because it got too cold at night and lastly... fix your dam WIFI!!!

title: Alright Stay In London, But Not Best.
text: Don't get me wrong, the staff was great. Very friendly and accommodating...the next morning. I stayed at several hostels in my jaunt across Europe and I have to say this might have been my least favorite. There are things that factor in that should be said on Keystone's behalf: 1) It's in a crazy popular area, so the security is good. 2) It's in a crazy expensive city, so for the price vs. the value, it actually is a decent hostel. 3) It probably gets crazy ridiculous guests, so that might contribute to the rating. I'd like to think I'm not one of them. So now why is my rating so low? I stayed in another hostel in London for around the same price. Actually, maybe it was even for a little lower, and I'd like to think the location was even more prime, being just a few minutes walk from such famous attractions as Eye of London, Big Ben, Parliament, etc. Also, that hostel was directly across the street from Lambeth North Underground, an unassuming, not too busy metro stop. Keystone House was a few blocks walk from Kings Cross, which is a crazy busy and congested metro and train station. The other hostel I stayed at previously also had an attached restaurant and bar, so while meals weren't included, they were discounted. There was no attached bar at the Keystone House Kings Cross, but there were several bars in the nearby vicinity (back to 'it's in a crazy popular area'). So you couldn't unwind and eat at the hostel itself, but you could unwind and eat nearby. The showers were on the first floor only. My dorm was on the third. Said showers had individual deep stalls, 3 shower curtains deep for separating the stall into compartments. Each stall had a first shower curtain that revealed a sink and rack for hanging towels and such. Behind the second shower curtain was the shower, which was initiated by pushing a button and a shower stream would go for about 10 or 15 seconds. Behind the third curtain in this stall was the toilet. So it was nice to have each piece of a bathroom compartmentalized in each stall

title: Would stay again
text: Upon arrival there were some problems with check in due to loss of Internet, we could not get our rooms due to this. The showers and toilets are in individuals cubicles, this is good for changing but if you just want a wee and all the cubicles are full you may have to wait a while. Our room was very clean, the beds were comfortable and we had a good nights sleep. The location is great right next to Kings Cross. The communal areas are a little squashed, at checkout time it was rather full. There is a free breakfast ( toast and cereal) but the kitchen is small and it's hard to get in and out to make breakfast/ wash up etc... Overall ok and would stay again.

title: Hotel Hostel Kings x
text: Hi Being an older Traveller at 66 and never ever stayed at a Hostel before in my life I did not know quite what to expect to find. First of all the property is located very close to Kings x rail station in Pentonville road just around the corner. The first problem was the stairs since they gave me a room down stairs partly due to my fault arriving 1 day early on the 12th April last week and so on the second night it was on the street level. I have Arthritus in one hip which did not help on the stairs. I was not prepared for no towel for the shower so I bought one for £5.OO from the hostel, the beds are basic being metal bunk some with upper bunk with a ladder, I found the bathroom one night a bit difficult with the door not opening fully because of the ladder and me having a few pounds extra to get though. For the price of £49.9O overall good for teens and for people on a budget.

title: Mr
text: I've stayed in keystone several times and return here due to the fact that it's the best all round hostel in inner London bar none. The staff are friendly and the ameneties are great, the rooms are not so tightly packed with beds that you can't move and the showers are always hot and well looked after. The travel links are amazing and it's very easy to find, there is a key fob system so no curfew and the free breakfast is a bonus too. Never too busy and always friendly people staying. Highly recommended

title: Cheap and cheerful
text: We stayed at The Keystone House hostle underground for a week in June, It was clean and tidy. The staff were really helpful (especially at night). Very safe and free luggage storage was available too! Lockers provided for valuables. The rooms were clean and the bed's were comfy, Toilets were clean and always checked, Although the shower was a little bit small as i'm claustrophobic but bigger ones are available up stairs. The breakfast was lovely and fresh! Sausage & bacon etc along with cerials toast, tea facilities, juice, milk and fruit all included!! This hostel is in the perfect location if you need to be close to the overground or underground as right next to Kingscross station. Also easy bus route outside to Angel, islington etc-Lovely area for business,shopping etc. We booked a 4 bed dorm for the four of us so was just perfect for what we wanted it for - sleep after partying in the city. The roof terrace is also really lovely especially as the weather was hot & there is a bar which is fairly cheap too!! :-) And a good chance to meet some lovely people too! We will defiantly be staying here again next time we come to London but this time up stairs with air conditioning & windows as there was no fans available due to nice weather. Many thanks to Keystone house for a lovely stay and see you again soon! JCG Artists

title: Feeling like at home
text: I've been in this hostel while I was working in the City. First thing first I must say is that the team (all of them) is amazing, they letterally treated my like I was at home. At the reception aside being professional, the staff has been superfriendly, always helpfull (during my stay I also lost my credit card and on the same day I had to pay my stay, at the reception the manager Carley, Paula (Paula the most) and Orla seeing me desperate hepled me calming down saying I could stay there till I could resolve the issue.) Orla has been an Angel, after asking her some suggestions about nice cinemas around the area, the next day she called me at the reception giving me some vouchers she took on the way home (yes, she letterally did something for me afterwork) as well as Amandina and Paula again, always there at the reception to help. All the girls Alex, Nora, Moni and Dorryta evry morning, every single morning came in my room and when seeing me already awake they always wished me goodmorning with a shining smile leaving my room clean and tidy as well as all the cummon areas of the building. How can I forget the "night shift receptionists" Michael, Mark and Nik, always welcoming me after work, asking me if everything was ok when yes, everyting it was more than ok. To all of you Thank you so much for making my stay..like at home...

title: Good location, Average stay
text: Picked this place for it's location. Just steps from Kings Cross/St Pancras. Overall, staff were quite helpful, though they could have used some more during busy check in times. They seemed a bit rushed and overwhelmed. They allow you to check your bag if you get there too early or need to check out. -My son and I took a double room. The room was small but functional. Bunk beds. We didn't expect too much. Mattresses were comfortable. The room was located above the Flying Scotsman Strip club. This was only an issue on our first night and we wanted to get some sleep early. Otherwise, it closes down at a reasonable 11 pm (10pm on SUndays). Music can be kind of loud, but the strippers had good taste in music! -The shower on our floor was broken the week we were there, so we showered in the basement. They were generally hot and with good pressure. They were, though quite small. Barely enough room to turn around. There was also a stark lack of hooks or places to set things to avoid getting wet. The floors could have been helped with some rubber matting to keep out of the puddles better. -The kitchen was inadequate by their own admit. There was a microwave a kettle and some empty shelves and counters. There were no utensils or containers. It was not useable as cooking space. -They did serve breakfast which I did not know about before hand. I've never had a british breakfast of baked beans, toast and sausages. Not sure how they were supposed to taste. Beans were tepid. Sausage was crisp on the outside, mushy and rather flavorless on the inside. Is that how british sausage tastes. There was a good supply of toast, spreads, juice, tea and coffee, plus fresh fruit. All is included in your price. -The main lounge is rather tight during busy times. Nice TV and some computers for internet. Internet rates were 5 pounds for a week, unlimited. The people there when we were there didn't know how to clean up after themselves so sometimes it was a bit untidy. Really, people. Be considerate. -The bar in the back is cozy and has a good selection of drinks. There is roof terrace which would be nice in the summer. Buy and drink and get internet access. -All in all not a bad stay. Some simple add ons would make it much better

title: Not worth the money.
text: I chose this hostel because of its location to Kings Cross Station but I wish I hadn't! The place was sooooooo cold. I had to walk down three flights of stairs to use the large bathroom because the light had broken in the single bathroom closer to our room. The bathrooms steemed very dirty and you had to keep pressing a timer in the shower. I had very little sleep because even with the windows closed you heard every word on the street below. Never again.

title: Not if you want to sleep
text: Stayed in one of the rooms in the basement. The rooms were ok, quite cold but that's always in the UK. It wasn't anything special, just a room with beds, but it was clean. The staff was friendly and helpful and the location was good right next to the underground. The breakfast was quite poor. What we however really hated was that there was a pub "flying scotsmen" or something similar right above our room. So we could hear people partying until 1 o'clock at night, which was ok because we weren't in the room so much during the night, but the cleaners arrived at the pub really early, like at 6 in the morning and started (what it sounded like) throwing chairs and tables everywhere. We did not get a single good night sleep at the Keystone House. Would not stay there again just because of this.

title: Perfectly fine stay, nice location
text: I only stayed here for two nights but I had two good sleeps. The beds are comfy and have privacy boards up, and each bed has its own outlets and light, which is nice. Each bed also comes with its own locker, not big enough for suitcases, but definitely big enough for all your valuables. Everything seemed clean. The only thing I wish there was a way to control the temperature in the showers. It was warm enough, I just prefer it a bit hotter. Nice location to Kings Cross, as well. I'd stay here again.

title: Pub With Rooftop Terrace
text: While we didn't stay at the hostel, we frequented the Backpackers Bar. Great drinks at the best prices in London, and a fabulous rooftop terrace! Everyone was friendly and it's a great place to have a pint or 2 and meet people from all over the world!

title: What a mistake!
text: What can I say about keystone house! What a disgrace! We arrived at 2pm for check in and we were told to wait for half an hour! Don't make check in 2pm if you can't let them into their rooms. When we finally got into our private room, I could not believe my eyes! The mould on the room was disgusting and the room smelt like a nursing home. Very damp. When we asked if we could move rooms as it was a health and safety hazard the guy at the desk couldn't give a damn and didn't move us. Even after I told him I am an asthmatic and the mould was affecting it. The next day, someone came into our room and took one bag of rubbish, left the rest and didn't change the toilet paper. So we were left without toilet paper. We also went downstairs to purchase the wifi password as they have wifi all throughout their hostel (according to the information on the wall and when you click onto the internet) however when we went to the desk and asked for it, the guy at the desk said no they don't offer it. Why advertise it then!? And if you love a top bunk with a half broken safety rail, you will find that here too. I understand hostels aren't 5 stars, but basic health and safety is not that hard. If you couldn't give a damn about health and safety then keystone house is the place for you. Such a disappointment for the price paid. I will never recommend it to anyone ever!!!

title: Friendly and convenient
text: Stayed in Keystone for one night in early December. Hostel is a couple of minutes walk from Kings Cross station. Staff very friendly and helpful overall. Nice internet cafe and separate pub / cafe area as well as roof terrace, so plenty of room to hang out. They run entertainment events (which I didn't go to, but seemed fun), and you got a voucher for a free cocktail when you checked in. Slept in 4 bed dorm with en suite which was fine and comfortable and clean. They had a good breakfast buffet included with rashers sausages, beans, fruit, cereal, bread etc. Overall friendly, convenient and good value.

title: Excellent Budget Accommodation
text: As we all know accommodation in london is horrendously expensive, but this place was surprisingly cheap. The best thing about this place is the location - 5 minute walk from Kings cross station, which basically means with a connection to just about all of the tube lines, you can be anywhere in london within 20 minutes. We caught the tube to the West End, The Oval, Tower of London, Hyde Park and all of the trains made it back to kings cross no worries. seriously it was amazing. As to the room itself, the twin private room we had (Duchess room 5) was very small, basically enough room for a bunk bed, locker, and doorway, but the sheets were clean and the beds were comfortable, which is all you can ask for really. The room also had its own split system so temperature was not a worry. It was relatively noisy outside but we didnt really notice, probably because there is so much to see we were very tired when we got home every night. The bathrooms and breakfast were just okay, but reception was very friendly I would definitely recommend this place to others, both on price and location

title: Great location and amazing staff
text: We came here with some friend for the week end and really enjoyed our stay there. The location is perfect, you can litteraly walk everywhere and its only 2mns from the Eurostar. Staff was very helpful and it was very handy to be able to book tour tickets from reception (it clearly saved us some times on our short trip). The room was clean and quiet. We will definitely come back here again.

title: Good Value
text: I stayed in this hostel for 1 night. This hostel is near to King's Cross station. A very convenient location!! The room was clean and tidy. Staff are friendly. Wif-Fi is accessible everywhere, including underground rooms!! Highly Recommendable!

title: Would NOT recommend
text: Maybe it'a because I'm a new hostel traveler and don't know how these things work. What I will say is I expected a different experience. The ONLY benefit to this hostel is the location. I was surprised to find multiple women basically living in the women's dorm. While some may be ok with this, I was surprised. I never wanted to go back to the room, and tried to stay away from the hostel as long as possible. I actually really dreaded returning to the room. There was only one bathroom that I felt was clean enough to use. While in some places I may be able to escape to a common area for some solace from the odd dorm situation, I would not even attempt to use the common area, it was not clean and had an odd smell. Would definitely in the future pay more to stay somewhere better.

title: Almost perfect, but no cookers!
text: We spend there with my boyfriend in a twin room about a month in the first half of the year 2014. The location of the hostel was great

title: Average
text: “We stay in a private twin room, which was tiny, cleanliness-average, the carpet would do with the cleaning, couldn't open the window, but there was an air con so that's a good thing. What's more, our room was located near the stairs and the bathroom, we could hear every step and ... Word. Not good if you want a good 6-7 hours of sleep. We paid £20 each, it was too dear for the standard of the property. The staff were excellent, though.”

title: Great location and budget hostel
text: Good thing about this hostel was the location,5 min walk to King's Cross station. The private room ensuite was basic and clean. Room had a roof window for some air which has remote control to shut-down. air conditioning and decent size shower and toilet.. Friendly staff and helpful ... Overall the stay was great, only thing I was concerned was to pay £5 to store your luggage for the day. which was bit expensive. where other hostels has free storage facility. There was lot of coffee shops and restaurants near by which is good sign... Free wifi available need to ask for password at reception.

title: Good place to stay
text: Good location, not to far away from train station and close to tube. Clean room with compfy bed. Air con definitely a benefit in humid city :P Nice communal kitchen with free coffee and tea. Good value for money. Worth coming back to:)

title: Conveniently located - steps away from Kings Cross St Pancras
text: Stayed here for four nights. We had one of the Omega rooms which are located at the top of TWO flights of stairs. Not a good thing when you overpack. Steps are very very narrow. Bathroom was good but shower is super tiny and floods if you run water at normal flow. Room had three beds. One person reported a horrible bed but the rest of us had no problems. It is noisy at night. AC worked great. Easy check in and check out. Pleasantly surprised.

title: Good location that's all
text: This hostel has perfect location just 5 min walk to Kings Cross Station but in my opinion it's was the only advantage . Our room was really expensive (£84 something like that private room with private bathroom) but was very disappointing. Our sink was clogged not any towels ( only if you buy at reception) and this ridiculous bed ladder from right side a bed( couldn't open widely doors to toilet!). Really never again,sorry.

title: Great location but could do with a clean
text: The hostel is only 2 minutes walk from Kings Cross station and is in an ideal location. I stayed in the London Underground room with a private bathroom. The room had no windows and I could hear the trains from my room through the night however this was included in the description before booking. The bathroom was rather old and could do with renovation. The room was quite cold and the heater didn't work. The floor could have done with sweeping and the bed linen had dust and hair on it. The staff were friendly and for the location the price isn't too bad. Overall the hostel is ok for one or two nights but if you are staying longer it might be worth spending a bit more.

title: chill stay in the UK
text: as much as loud is kingcross london, this hostel was chill quite n the bed was quite comfy compare to the rest of the hostel, the recptionist Almondi, Carly was super nice , they have light breakfast as well. great location right next to tubes

title: Does the job!
text: This hostel is in a great location, 2 seconds from Kings Cross Station and a 10 min walk from Euston and with a nice bar across the road. The hostel was clean and basic, it's quiet which is what we were looking for. However, the underground rooms are not only underground (I knew that when I booked) but also really airless and musty. There is very little ventilation and the whole basement floor smells a bit like a gym changing room. If you need a cheap-ish place to stay for one night, this place will do, but it's not particularly comfortable or atmospheric.

title: WORST HOSTEL EVER
text: Filthy place, smells like crap, and staff are rude ! Especially the front door individuals. Rooms were small, we booked a 3 bed room and they gave us a two bed room. Bathrooms are in the hallway and showers are too. The rooms smelled like old, moldy, rotten crap. At night all we heard was loud music that didn't let us sleep. We had NO windows and it was basically living in a dungeon. We were only there two nights but that was more than enough.

title: Over night stay
text: The hostel is about 5 minutes from the tube station and surrounded by an array of fast food places. The staff are lovely and it's quite quirky in the reception area. The room was okay. Very plain. Booked and en suite double and had a bunk bed. Double on the bottom single on top. There are no towels (bring your own or rent one for £5 a towel) there are no tellies in the room and our light was broken so had to switch the bathroom light on and leave the door open. I had quite a good nights sleep. The hostel is about 10 mins from London central. Get the Piccadilly line which is dark blue to Leicester Square and other areas of attraction. Also new tip: if your card is contactless or you have Apple Pay you don't need a tube ticket. Use your card/device to swipe in and out for the day and it caps the charge at £6.50 All in all if you don't plan on doing anything but sleeping at a convenient location out of the congestion charge I'd recommend this hostel.

title: We wouldn't recommend this place
text: Pro's: - the location was really good, only 2 min. walk from St. Pancras / King's Cross (metro)station, cool pubs, nice coffee places and supermarkets - Real cosy roof top terrace - nice decoration in the common room Con's: - they didn't provide an adapted socket for other European plugs to charge your phone or camera so you had to buy it somewhere - the bathrooms were quite dirty with constant wet floors, hair all over the place and other dirt - The staff wasn't really helpfull and it seemed like they didn't really know how the place worked - The room was extremely tiny (for 2 people, we couldn't even stand next to eachother, the full room was 2x3 meters) - We couldn't close the window (it was stuck) so it was quite cold and really noisy from the traffic downstairs in the street - Twice we came to the common room on time to have breakfast, twice they said we couldn't have breakfast anymore without further explanation - We had to pay 2 pounds per pag after we checked out to keep our luggage safe for an hour or two (never seen before) We wouldn't recommend this place.

title: Problem with the booking
text: When I arrived at the hostel I was told that they were fully booked so I would have change rooms twice during the stay (4 nights). We were 3 friends traveling together and started by staying two nights in a 3 person room called Omega 5. The room was really nice but we had to check out before 10 o´clock on Saturday morning and could not get the other room until 2 o´clock (had to take the luggage down MANY stairs and then back up again later that day). The second room we got was extremely small, one bunk bed, but apparently 3 persons accommodation. We stayed there one night and had to check out again the next morning and again we could not get the other room right away Then they put us back in the room we started in. We talked to the manager (and probably all the staff) many times and asked why we could not stay in the same room the whole time and the other group (apparently also 3 persons) could take the room we had to stay in for one nigh before changing back to the first room. No one could do anything about the matter and all the answers we got were "the computer says no" answers. We talked to the manager many times and asked her if she could compensate us in any way because we would never had booked this if we would have knew that this would happen since we were planning on going to a concert during Friday night and hadn´t planned to wake up early like we had to do in the end. The manager dismissed everything we said, denied all responsibility and blamed it on Hostelworld (which we booked through). She even tried to blame it on us since it was "such a long stay" - Who in their right mind would say that a 4 night stay at a hostel is abnormally long? She wasn´t even willing to let us keep our luggage in the storage room for free after we checked out for the third and last time (2 pounds each). And we even asked if we could have towels for free because of this trouble and had to ask her four times because she just pretended not to hear us and talked about something else (but of course she denied us the towels since this booking fiasco was not their responsibility). This is such a shame since the hostel would otherwise get a good/ok review from me. The location is good, only short walk from Kings Cross station. The common room was nice and tidy and had free wifi access. One of the two rooms we got was really good: three single bed, big space and a nice bathroom. The other one was really small (only one bunk bed an two closets) and had a funky smell in the bathroom. The general staff was really nice and helpfull. But this booking fiasco was really annoying and we had to spend a lot of time trying to solve it so it cancels the good things out. Ohh. I almost forgot to mention that we were waken up the first morning at 8 o´clock because there was some constructions going on at the hostel...

title: Great Location, Staffs, Rest are just Average
text: We ( Me n my friend ) stayed here for the 2 times, first for 1 night, and the second for 3 nights., in different rooms. First of all, i must say, this hostel's location is a great plus and its very near to king's cross staion/under-ground and bus-stations. I would say its pretty easy to find even if you walking in darkest hours. Reception desk staffs are kind and helpful, and the check-in was fast, took less than 5 min for the first time ( due to filling of forms, and scanning passports ), and less than 2mins for the second time ( as our details are already in the system ). Hostel providing luggage storage, but with a charge of 2 Sterling for a day, if you are checking out. Though, it was still helpful for us to leave our bulky luggage here for one week, so we dont need to carry all things to all those other destinations. Storage room is near to reception, so we had a confidence that, its pretty safe there. Shower rooms are another plus, easily adjustable, separate shower rooms ( far from toilets ) are cozy. And the shower was great, water-flow was just perfect. Toilets are good too., found clean almost all the times. Basement Corridor, where our rooms (LU - Londer Underground rooms, with no windows ) located are nicely painted and decorated. Kitchen are is another plus, arranged properly with neat tables/chairs and a big TV, in there. Wifi is accessible in all areas, including rooms. Our first, room where we stayed for the first, ( twin shared room with shared bathroom ) was with double bunk bed, with softer and cozy mattresses, and nice and thick quilt blanket to get warm quick. One chair and thin and long steel wardrobe, separated for 2 person's belongings, was provided. Sleep was great with no issues. For the second time, when we were staying for 3 consecutive nights, the room setup and decoration was same, though there was some serious trouble with ventillation, as it was blowing with cold air all the time. Receptionist did helped by sending a maintenance staff on checking the same, but couldn't help much on that. Then we noticed something on the corner of the room, which turned to be a portable heater. I guess the previous party staying at this room had the same issue, and may requested for this before. When we turned it on, voila.. room got warmed up in time. Overall, experience and satisfaction by staying at this hotel is "Above Average". And would happily choose this hostel again, if im about to go london again.

title: Fantastic for a group of friends
text: Myself and two friends booked a private 3 bed dorm. It had 3 single beds and our own bathroom which was very modern with a great shower. It was very quiet, particularly at night time, with the only daytime noise being traffic. Very clean, our rubbish was removed daily. The place felt very secure with access only by fob at main door and key at bedroom door and there were staff members on reception 24hrs. Staff were very helpful and provided a mattress bed for the floor for a last minute addition of a sibling to the mix. They also provided luggage storage for the price of £5 on the day that we checked out. They also offered breakfast in next doors cafe for a very reasonable price Great location as close to kings cross underground which serves multiple underground lines. We spent a lot of our time in Camden town which was only 2 underground stops away and the city centre.

title: Avoid unless you have no choice
text: Keystone House Hostel has surprised me on many levels. First, everything went wrong with booking a bed. When I emailed first about paying upon arrival because I don't own a credit card, they were very strict and said no. After two weeks I accidentally emailed the same hostel with the same question and now it was possible. But after reserving the bed, I called in after a week and they had no record of me whatsoever so I had to book again. I chose the hostel because of location and that's almost the only good thing about Keystone. They were however able to book me into another room so I could have a floor bed. Pros: Friendly lady at reception Location - just outside Kings Cross mcDonalds and large Tesco supermarket just around the corner Cons: Other staff was unwelcoming and not really willing to help with questions Showers are horrible. They are cold, dirty and you constantly have to press a button to get it to run. Seems to have no age limit - anyone can sleep here and the people in my room were a little creepy and old. They say you can rent a towel for a "small fee" but it turns out you can only buy one for 5 Pounds. Extremely small and boring rooms. Extremely noisy - you can really only sleep if you're very very tired or dead. Kitchen is too basic, funkily lit and very boring. Sitting there is very awkward and no one talks to anyone. No elevator I'd avoid this hostel at all costs unless I was really desperate and didn't care about hygiene.

title: Did what we wanted it to do
text: A group of us stayed here as we were going to egg nightclub. Rooms were a good size. We had a 6 bed private dorm. Beds were reasonably comfy. Room clean. However the fire exit door was unlocked so other guests could still walk in to our room and this happened. So you may want to bring your own padlock or rent one to store valuables in lockers. There was also a fair bit of noise throughout the night however kind of expected given location and it being the weekend.

title: Don't stay in the rooms without windows!
text: Stayed here once during a class trip (I'm a teacher) and will definitely not do this again, although the staff was very friendly and helpful and the breakfast was good for a hostel. All the rooms I've seen were simply nightmares, even for London standards, where cheap accomodation always comes at a certain price. The dorms for 16 students were simply too small, no room to store the suitcases, there were holes in some of the walls, the bed sheets were stained (don't really want to know what the staines actually were...). The showers weren't any better either, some of them were extremely mouldy and there were simply not enough for so many people. Worse even than all of that was my room - located in the basement, it didn't have any windows, some kind of air-con which didn't do anything apart from being very noisy, and the worst bit was that I could hear every single Tube train going to King's Cross (even though the website of the hostel said that these rooms are "said to be more quiet" - ha bloody ha!). I didn't have a good night's sleep there for one week and woke up every morning with a splitting headache. Don't go there, spend some extra quid and go to nearby Generator Hostel instead!!

title: Go to the rooftop balcony
text: The pub isn't anything special and I don't fancy the beer options they have. Strange microbrews. However the rooftop patio is fantastic. It's like a small English garden. Definitely worth a stop if you are in the area.

title: Ughh don't recommend.
text: Keystone was a mistake- while there were some positives, the negatives far outweighed them. Don't recommend staying here. Pros first: 1) Loved the bed and bedsheets- clean and very comfortable. 2) Great location- less than a 5 minute walk from King's Cross Station which is connected to a ton of lines and also to St. Pancras International where we took our train to Paris. 3) Lots of good affordable restaurants and grocery stores within a 5 minute walk from Keystone. 4) Staff is nice, the receptionist charged us a couple less pounds to store our luggage because he noticed how frustrated we were with all the extra charges. 5) The bathroom's paper towels were nice and thick, but they don't restock it fast enough. 6) Room have A/C Cons: Keystone charges for pretty much everything! I was surprised they don't charge for breakfast. 1) Wi-Fi: If you want wi-fi in your room or use the internet on the the computers in the front, you have to pay. In all my recent years of traveling I've never been to a hostel that charges for Wi-Fi. There is free Wi-Fi in common room but Keystone tells you at check-in that the common room is open 7-11PM. Get with the times! 2) Leaving your luggage after checking out: 2 pounds per bag. This is the first and ONLY hostel I've ever been to that charges for this! We were shocked. 3) Late checkout- 5 pounds per person if you check out at noon instead of 10AM. The night before the receptionist told us it was 5 pounds so we thought it was per room, but when we checked out they said, "No, its 5 pounds per person." Great. Thanks for being so clear before. We also were woken up by housekeeping when we wanted to sleep in. 4) Feet smell: When we walked in the Duchess Deluxe Twin Room, the fresh smell of feet hit us in the face. This is a permanent fixture of this room so please make sure you don't get this same room. 5) The room was small so I can't even imagine what the NON-deluxe rooms were like. 6) Although being "deluxe," there are no mirrors and the window curtain fell off while we slept. 7) The three floors of duchess rooms have to share the toilet and bathroom on the first floor. 8) The shower is not continual, you have to keep pushing a button to maintain water flow and you also cannot control the temperature, there are seconds when you get a bit burned from the shower. 9) There is absolutely no personality at Keystone, bland walls, very ugly and smelly kitchen and medicore common room. 10) Breakfast is very minimal and bland. We ended up getting food from Tesco and leaving it in the fridge- at least Keystone doesn't charge for that either thank god!

title: Decent for price and location
text: Booked 2 beds of a double room - inside no windows and bunk beds, but they had some sort of green halogen nightlight that gave just enough light so it was not pitch black. Small room but adequate. At £50, you can't beat the price or location. Wifi was ok to skype.

title: Good location-that's about it
text: The first impression of Keystone House wasn't great, the front desk manager (Hugo) was extremely rude and abrupt-I don't think this is the industry for you. Once checked in we found our room, it was nice and clean-very basic but we fully expected that anyway so no drama. We had a bathroom immediately to our left which was very handy-until we realised that it was never going to get cleaned, the first use was fine as no one else had used it but thereafter it was not a pleasant experience. It smelled pretty bad, the floor was drenched, the bin started to fill up, and the hand towels ran out. The location was amazing-about 5 minute walk from Kings Cross Station, plenty of restaurants round and about so don't have to walk far for anything-handy as it was torrential when we were there! Luggage storage seems overly pricey bearing in mind we were guests-fair enough if we had come in off the street but seems harsh charging a premium to guests. Probably wouldn't stay again, however if you just need a base to sleep at and don't need to spend any time there then I guess it's ok

title: Decent Accomodations
text: I stayed here for two days while I was in London and my only major issue was that it took about 30 minutes to check in because there was only one person working the front desk and about 10 people needed help. I could have just arrived at a bad time...who knows? Aside from that, the facilities were not anything to write home about, but clean. There are lockers in the rooms, but if you want to store your whole bag you have to leave it downstairs. Overall, not fantastic, but not terrible.

title: Fantastic Hostel!
text: This was a great hostel! Rooms were very clean. I shared a 16 bed female dorm, had a wall separating half the beds. Own small kitchen in room, sink fridge microwave some cups and plates. Heater and own bed light, own powerpoints and a small bedside table that is a locker also. Staff were great, very helpful and nice people. Roof top bar and restaurant. Downstairs bar. Attatche to a great reataurant called The Brill. Free breakfast. Location was great. Showers good. Shower and toilet are in the same cubical, but shower curtins cover toilet. If any anything the showeres could of been hotter and not timed every 60 seconds you have to press the button to start the shower again. But that is if I had to pick anything! Theres an Internet cafe, with computers and Cafe style set up. Location perfect. Highly recommend it. set up like a small cafe. Cafe style coffee machines for us to purchase from.

title: Difficult experience all around. But good location.
text: From check in to check out and on a daily basis, this was a complicated (unnecessarily so) stay. If I actually listed the details, you wouldn't believe me. The person at check in was not friendly. My daughter and I trekked around the place (from the 3 floor down to the basement-all stairs) on a daily basis due to switching rooms b/c they had us in a shared bathroom though I reserved a private. They insisted I received an email that I never received. One night, 11:30pm in a basement room w/ no windows, I was looking for another place to stay. The kind young man at the desk offered another room...but it had someone else's clothes and trash still in it. Finally, we did get our private room & bath. It was fairly clean. It was not a positive experience, unfortunately. I think if I were traveling alone and could've done the dorm rooms, it would have been a good stay. But I don't recommend this for families traveling. For the same cost I could've stayed in a nearby hotel.

title: Fine for a night's sleep
text: I needed a place in London for a night's stay at very short notice so booked this. I was a bit disappointed that there weren't any male/ female separated rooms, at least not when I booked. Also it was very very loud at night. The location was awesome, tube station just across the road and Kings Cross/ St. Pancras within 3 minutes walk and free wifi is always good but I probably wouldn't stay again.

title: Had a great experience!!
text: My partner and I stayed here for 4 nights in a private room with a private bathroom. We had never stayed in a hostel before and i'm so glad we had such a good experience here :) This hostel is in a fantastic location! You get off the train at a major station which is kings cross and the hostel is a 1 minute walk down the road. When we arrived it was early in the morning and couldn't check in yet, but the staff were friendly and there was somewhere we could store our luggage while we went out for the day. All staff were helpful our whole stay. We booked this hostel a few months back and at the time there were no horrible reviews on TA so when I did a double check of it before we got there I was really worried. But when we checked in I was extremely surprised. There is no elevator and there are narrow stairs to carry your bags up - not complaining just informing. The room was very small but i didn't expect anything grand. It was all extremely clean, didn't smell and the linen was clean and tidy as well. There were no windows on the wall but there was a skylight in the roof which did let in a lot of light at all times of the day and night but it really didn't bother us. There was a remote control to open and close the skylight so natural air could come in too. The room had a proper airconditioner on the wall with a remote. The bed was super comfortable, the only thing I would say is at night time it got hot - even with our air conditioner on. The shower was lacking some water pressure and there was no floor mat so things in the bathroom did get a bit wet. And there's not a lot of shelving in the bathroom to put things on. The hostel was not noisy at nighttime at all, and the surrounding area is pretty quiet also. You see people walking in and out of the reception area during the day but that's about it! The common area is so far out of the way - down the hall, down some stairs in the basement right at the back. It felt a little bit dark and dungeon-like and quite a small room as well. We felt safe at all times and we loved the conveniency of this hostel. The only thing I would recommend is that upon checking out if you need to store your bags there's a 5£ fee per bag. It would be better if this were cheaper or even free!

title: Only good thing about this place is the location!
text: My first night that I arrived , I was a little in shock , I had a private room all the way up the millions of stairs, I didn't feel to safe. There was a man laying on the bathroom floor in the co Ed bathrooms all the way upstairs , which I personally do not think it is a good idea, it is not safe , especially in its location all the way up far from the reception area. I told the staff and he went to check the bathroom , which made me feel better. The hostel smells, like mold and sperm. My private room was small, the bed was very comfortable but the blanket was ripped, defiantly not what I was expecting for a private room. I had stayed at the wombats hostel a few days prior and it was amazing! It was luxurious I felt safe and it was huge! This hostel , keystone, needs an update really bad, it has stairs which make it very hard to carry your luggage , I can't imagine someone disabled or not in good health having to constantly climb up the stairs. The common area was cozy but very basic . The only great thing about this place was the location, it is literally close to everything you need. The staff was also very friendly , but I highly Recommend updating this hostel, get rid of the mold that can make you sick !! And also get rid of the co Ed bathroom , unless it's in a safer location within the hostel. Please invest in an elevator . Other than that , thank you for the stay.

title: Small but neat
text: We were looking for somewhere neat, but affordable on a big budget. While this was not the cheapest hostel, it was very well located right near King's Cross. The rooms were very small, but clean. My husband and I had a 2 bed room with a private bathroom. It was relatively quiet most of the time. I would not recommend it for anyone wanting to be romantic though! The beds were quite comfortable, but small, and they are bunk beds. I recommend getting up early for the breakfast as it gets extremely busy from 8am on. All in all, not bad. Oh, and take your own towels!

title: Overall Decent Experience
text: This hostel was cheap and clean, but aside from sleeping, it did not offer much opportunity to interact with other travels. There was one common room in the basement, but it was difficult to find and rarely used. The location of this hostel was not ideal in accessing the city. The benefit to the location was that it was very close to the train station. Although this hostel didn't have anything to do besides sleep,there was good service and comfortable sleeping situations giving me an overall decent experience.

title: Good location. That's all.
text: Me and my partner stayed in a private room with an ensuite. The one good thing with this hostel was the location, extremely central. We had mould on the wall (which was then attempted to be hidden by the mattress), the mattress had springs broken on one side and one of the nights when we came back to our "private" room, we found a big black bag of rubbish which wasn't there when we left. When we explained this to the staff they just took the rubbish and didn't intend on acknowledging it. 4.0

title: Small but convenient
text: We stayed in a private double room without a bathroom. Our room was so small and the window was small so it got pretty stuffy at times. I was not too uncomfortable however my boyfriend did complain about it being hot at night. It was quiet, and and clean. The staff was helpful and always at the front desk. The location is fabulous-- right near kings cross station which can take you pretty much anywhere. We came home around 2 am a few nights but I never felt like I was in danger-- safe area. The pizza place a little past the hotel is amazing!!

title: Everything You Need
text: Keystone House is in a great location for exploring the city by foot or when using public transport. It is a huge hostel but the staff was really friendly and very helpful. There was a service to leave your bags after checking out, although it would be great if this service were a bit cheaper, or even free! We stayed in a very small private room with our own, very small, private bath! The bathroom was cleaned each day during our stay. We had to purchase towels for 5 each. We didn't get a chance to check out much else of what the hostel had to offer, but were happy with the experience we had and would definitely recommend Keystone House.

title: Heaven
text: Booked in for few nights last month. This hotel could not be better. Staff could not be nicer and rooms are beautifully decorated, so cosy. I felt like a princess! Great location. Tube very close. Great restaurants. Easy walk to Brompton cross for superb shopping. The only thing I didn't like was having to leave. Could live here.

title: Just Gorgeous
text: Had such a wonderful weekend away at Number Sixteen in South Kensington. The location is perfect, the hotel is beautiful and the staff are so warm and friendly. My new favourite place to stay in London and I can’t wait to get back there! Same room but for longer next time. X

title: Relaxed luxury
text: Simple, relaxed and intimate luxury. Beautiful rooms, great service, excellent food. The attention to detail is relentless. Wonderful chain too. I have stayed at two hotels now in the Firmdale chain and you rely on the quality in each one.

title: Wonderful Hotel
text: This hotel and its staff were phenomenal. I stayed with a group of 10 in this hotel for four nights. The rooms were exceptional, the staff goes out of its way to accommodate, the food was very good, the included breakfast was more than enough and the coffee is spectacular. The office is able to call a cab at a moments notice. Help is given with directions and any other kind of suggestion. The rooms are clean, comfortable and very pleasing to all the senses. Although I didn’t have tea here, It looked amazing. The South Kensington tube station is a 5 minute walk away. I would definitely stay here again and suggest the hotel to all my fiends.

title: Avoid rooms in the "basement"
text: Beautiful renovated rooms but...some are very noisy. We were staying in room no 1, located in the basement below the corridor going to the elevator and the dining room. We could hear EVERY steps above us, late at night when guest were coming back to the hotel and VERY early in the morning when the staff was setting breakfast. We did not expect that from a hotel of this category! After 2 nights, exhausted, we asked to be moved to a room on the second floor. After, we start enjoying our stay in this beautiful and well located hotel.

title: Stay here
text: Recently completed my fourth stay at Number Sixteen and highly recommend. Located near the South Kensington tube station, the hotel is a true gem. When you enter the immediate feel is small and exclusive, quiet, comfortable, and beautiful. The staff is friendly, the sitting areas plush and inviting, and the rooms are large and well designed. The lower levels find rooms with access to the garden, which seems like an oasis in central London. I will stay at Number Sixteen in the future. Restaurants, shopping, museums are an easy walk, and with the tube a quick walk, the hotel is at London's doorstep. Stay here.

title: Fabulous way to end long trip away
text: After travelling for over a month, Number 16 was the perfect way to spend my last couple of nights. Staff were so helpful from the time of booking, preparing for my visit and during my stay. Gorgeous furnishing, the most comfortable beds and lovely common shared areas. I had high tea with a friend and enjoyed all the hotel had to offer. The little touches make a big difference here, just lovely. I'll definitely be back!

title: Great location, design & quiet - but very small rooms
text: Very nice place to stay - warm and relaxing interiors, good & helpful staff. Very pleasant lounge aera and high quality breakfast. Rooms are well appointed but small for what you pay - so this is not a hotel where you can stay at length in your room as it get claustrophobic. Noise proofing is also not very good.

title: Slightly disappointing
text: We were looking forward to trying another Firmdale hotel to celebrate our 25th wedding anniversary with our teenage children. We have stayed at two others in the group and liked them very much. This hotel was a very mixed experience. Good - good location, lovely decor, great artefacts, nice afternoon tea in the conservatory, pretty building and garden, nice man went to car park when we forgot some items in car, complimentary drinks at tea for our anniversary Poor - unfriendly welcome (no mention of anniversary), very small superior room with minute bathroom, £45 car park charge, partly inedibleand slow late night room service (refunded), slow service in the conservatory for breakfast and tea, breakfast not included in the room rate and prices are ridiculously high and complicated to work out - small portion of baked beans £3.50, croissants £4 on top of the rate for English breakfast, extra sausage charged for etc. Every item was charged for individually even though we asked for English breakfast - this was refunded on request but duty manager was not happy about this. These little trivial incidentals matter when you stay in a hotel as service can make such a difference to your overall impression. Nobody wants to have an argument over baked beans as they leave the hotel. We will not return because of the ridiculous breakfast charges - this needs amending and should be included in the room rate. See my review of The Grove for how to do things differently and still be hugely successful.

title: Charming!
text: I am currently obsessed with the Firmdale Collection of Hotels in London. They are all decorated so beautifully with such great attention to detail. Every room is different and very interior designed. The PRO's of this Hotel - If you like the South Kensington Area then this is a perfect location for you. If you don't know the area it is very central with the Piccadilly Tube line taking you straight to all the tourist spots. This is also a good area for museums - Very beautiful interior of rooms ] - Attention to detail e.g. water next to your bed, sleep spray, coconut water in fridge CON - The size of the rooms are not the best! I stayed in room 106 which was beautiful but I felt it was a little too small with my partner. - The bathroom was tiny with no bath - Banging doors in hallway - I mentioned this to the reception upon leaving as it was a little irritating and they should look into having some sort of silencer on the door.

title: Townhouse charm with excellent afternoon tea
text: Number Sixteen may be small but is perfectly formed. Our room on the second floor had a roadside view but with no roadside noise. The furnishings were exquisite and the bed the best I've slept in for years. The breakfast in bed service on Sunday was a little slow but a minor point in comparison to the overall stay. Do treat yourself to afternoon tea if possible. Would happily return and thanks to all the team for a lovely stay.

title: luxury price but no luxury services
text: when paying £360 (incl. vat) for a room, I expect at least a coffee/tea facilities in the room and free WIFI (they charge £20/day)! the staff was very nice and efficient and location is great though. and apart from the ants in the bathroom there is no complaint about the room

title: A gem in South Kensington
text: If you've never been to London the first coscious choice you have to make when selecting a hotel is the neighborhood. South Kensington and Chelsea are posh yet multicultural quarters, brimming with bars, cafés,restaurants and boutiques. Personally I like South Kensington as it is closer to Hyde Park which is a boon if you enjoy running. Number 16 is smack in the middle and offers casual, goutique luxury. The staff is friendly and helpful, the breakfast in the garden is great and the rooms are nice without exuding the stuffy elegance found in many other five star hotels in London. If you check prices online, make sure to verify if VAT is included so you don't compare apples with oranges.

title: An intimate townhouse hotel...
text: This intimate 40-room townhouse hotel is located in the heart of South Kensington on a beautiful one-way street. The unique touch of Kit Kemp turns this property into a sophisticated personal place, full of character and charm... The staff is helpful and kind and the garden is the perfect place for a breakfast in a sunny day...

title: Lovely short stay
