text: Stayed here with my husband for two nights. We found the all of the staff exceptionally friendly and welcoming. We were given room 203, which is at the front of the hotel over looking the street. The room was lovely but perhaps a bit pink for my personal taste! Although it did have a comfortable large bed, walk in wardrobe and lovely bathroom. The small garden is a peaceful setting for breakfast or early evening drink. Good selection of breakfast cooked dishes, great bacon sandwich and healthier options of fresh fruit and cereals. Excellent location for the V&A. We would recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

title: Afternoon Tea!
text: I am so glad that I found this place in London! I pre-booked to come here for Afternoon Tea with my friend last week! The place was beautifully decorated and all the staff were very welcoming! Everything was clean, tidy, beautifully presented and nothing was too much trouble for the staff! We were seated in the dining room which was gorgeous and over looked the pretty garden, away from all the hustle and bustle of London life so was completely relaxing and enjoyable! The food was amazing for such a reasonable price! We both went for the full afternoon tea which came with a selection of sandwiches, mini savouries, scones, preserves, cakes and pastries! They were fresh and exceedingly tasty! We even struggled to finish! There was a wide selection of teas and refills were at no extra cost! The staff were polite and attentive! We were there for over two hours and at no point did we feel rushed or pressured to leave which I have encountered at other places! It was an extremely enjoyable afternoon and I would certainly recommend it, and will be returning! Thank you number sixteen for such a pleasant afternoon!

title: No better hotel in London
text: Delightful boutique hotel in the ritzy South Kensington area of London. Two blocks from the tube station. Great service from attentive staff. Free WIFI. Positively charming parlors & garden so you're not stuck in a hotel room.

title: Perfect for Solo Travelers
text: Spent 2 nights at Number Sixteen in March 2015. Proximity to South Kensington underground station made this hotel the perfect location for exploring London. Stayed in a 3rd floor room, but it was well appointed and spacious for one person. Staff was very friendly and helpful.

title: Feels like you are walking to your own house....
text: Number Sixteen is a small and friendly hotel where you feel you could actually live. Great location, with local restaurants and pubs and the underground all within easy walk. Rooms are typical Kit Kemp style, although beware of very small shower room in room 307 (like a small cupboard) and not all rooms, including this one, have an in-room safe, which I feel is expected for this standard of hotel, so I would suggest checking if this is important to you when booking. Great continental breakfast and very helpful team, all make this another winner from Firmdale.

title: Great place
text: Loved this hotel. We liked the location just south of Hyde Park. The staff was lovely and helpful. Our room was clean and quiet. I felt like we were staying at a friends very nice home. We only ate breakfast there so I can't comment on the restaurant. Their breakfast buffet was nice with the typical choices. But it seemed fresh. I think you could order cooked to order breakfast but we were always up and on the go. Lovely spot.

title: Wow! It was great!
text: My husband and I were surprised by the hospitality and comfort that "Number Sixteen" offered. From the beautiful linens to the lovely warm towels, Number Sixteen was "top notch". The marble bathrooms were also a treat! We would recommend this B&B to anyone!

title: not our cup of tea
text: Unfortunately, the evening before flying to London we realized that the room I had booked (booking.com) only had 12 sqm (superior room 864 GBP, incl. breakfast 3 nights). So I called the hotel to ask if they had a larger room and was able to switch to a luxury room (936 GBP). When checking in the next evening we were given a room on the ground floor (nr. 17) right next to the reception (we heard every question and conversation) with the window facing the courtyard (this is not a garden, rather a quite small courtyard). The next morning we packed our bags to move to yet another room (Deluxe). A women drinking her breakfast tea in the courtyard politely moved behind a plant so as not to see into our room. We came back in the afternoon looking forward to our new room and tea. Unfortunately, there was a wedding reception so both rooms, orangery and courtyard were full with guests and a band playing outside. We skipped afternoon tea. Our room was finally to our liking (40 GBP upgrade per night)

title: Very nice high tea
text: My wife and I had high tea in this lovely hotel's dining room. We made a reservation and enjoyed a traditional tea in a non-traditional yet tasteful room with a lush garden just outside (you can have it served there if you like). Trimmed finger sandwiches, fresh-baked scones with clotted cream and jam, of course, but also some unusual additions that worked perfectly, a layered mango pudding and a dark-chocolate brownie. Delicious. Best quality tea. All served by friendly and helpful staff who observed the traditions without a trace of stuffiness. Very reasonable, too. Highly recommended.

title: A boutique hotel with real character
text: Another of the Firmdale chain that is smaller and more individual. Perhaps not as well located as it is just off the busy South Kensington area and some distance from the West End, but handy for the museums. Just undergoing a refurb that keeps the Firmdale style to the fore. Some rooms are on the small side but a great conservatory for breakfast and the big advantage of a secluded private garden.

title: Wonderful and cozy
text: The hotel could be best described as a bed and breakfast. The staff let us check in early because our flight arrived around 7:00 in the morning - they were most friendly. The area is very quiet, it is a residential area but close to a market and coffee shops for convenience. The room was fantastic and comfortable. Nothing bad could be said about this hotel. Relaxing and beautiful. We enjoyed our first stay in London. We will return to this hotel again!

title: Fabulous boutique hotel with amazing staff
text: We stayed for the first night of our honeymoon and were absolutely thrilled with this place. We booked a Luxury Double Room and requested a rom with a patio - well worth doing as the patio was beautiful. The staff were really friendly and so helpful. The room was on the small side but really well laid out and had everything you would need.

title: Perfect choice. Better than the SOHO hotel.
text: Best hotel in London!!! We were here for a three day stay, originally booked another hotel for the next five days, but couldn't resist extending our stay, that is how perfect it was. The hotel is in a very nice and expensive area, the hotel in a residential street, and just around the corner is the South Kensington Underground, plus many nice restaurants. Reception area is very warm and cozy, feels like home with the big smiles that the staff gave us. We had the room number eight, which had a small balcony outside. The room was not very big but considering that we are in london, it is not too bad. Room was clean and bed was very comfortable. Decor was very classic london-ish, loved it. Room service was available two shifts a day, so you need not worry about getting up late in the day (unlike many other european hotels). Breakfast was in the cutest room ever, we felt like we were in some english home, overlooking the terrace. Too bad we were in winter, if not we could have the loveliest breakfast outdoors. Food was wonderful too, breakfast eggs and bacon were included in our room price. The service was what won us over. The staff was friendly and helpful, as we needed to get tickets to several shows and needed other information, they weren't once annoyed and tried to help us get everything we needed. On the other hand, our friends stayed at THE SOHO HOTEL of the same firmdale hotel line, which was much pricier, but they got comparatively poor service. We felt very welcomed at number sixteen, and i think that is what makes a hotel stand out from others. p.s. we loved the complimentary olives that they gave us on our arrival.

title: Faultless
text: Probably the nicest hotel I've ever stayed in: lovely design, friendly and helpful staff, great location, the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in and fab breakfasts. Have stayed here twice now and would move in if possible. Perfect!

title: Beautiful and cosy boutique hotel!
text: We stayed at Number Sixteen in October 2011 and loved it. The location was perfect with a number of nice little restaurants around the corner and the tube station a couple of blocks away. Our room was really nice overlooking the beautiful garden. The breakfast room was lovely and the staff very friendly. It was very nice to relax in the library after a busy day and the honesty bar is a wonderful feature. Hope to stay there again soon!

title: Great atmosphere, pricey but worth it
text: Very good service, polite up to good London standards and generally in line with what I expect from Firmdale hotels. The room was small but very comfortable, excellent bed ! Great location close to South Ken tube a lot of excellent restaurants and all possible services nearby. Liked best - ambience Liked least nothing to dislike Didn't try the breakfast (busisness breakfasts both days) but looked very ok when I peered into the dining room.

title: Great hotel
text: Let's get the negatives out of the way: 1. If you're unable to walk up steps, you need to ask for a room on the 1st or 2nd floor. The elevator goes to the 2nd floor and then you have to walk up very winding and narrow steps. I injured my knee and wanted to avoid the steps, so changed my room upon arrival. (I don't think I was told about the steps before booking, but may have been.) Thank goodness there were rooms available! 2. The rooms are super small. I mean super small! Now for the positives which are many: 1. Staff are EXTREMELY accommodating and helpful. They listen to you when you have a casual comment and react to it

title: Fabulous in every way!
text: Number Sixteen is an absolute dream. My mother and I could have moved in. Located on a quaint and quiet street in Kensington, you are walking distance to everything you need. Perfect if you are looking for the picturesque London location. The staff was amazing, and the hotel itself was fabulous. The interior and exterior design is a dream. I immediately bought Kit Kemp's book for style inspiration/

title: Nice hotel, but TINY rooms and some outrageous charges
text: The hotel is very clean and has modern, stylish decor, but the superior rooms are so small, they look they were literally cut in half. Some of the rooms have bathrooms so tiny, you can barely fit one person in them and taking a shower with the door closed is an exercise in extreme claustrophobia. Room rates are, I guess, in keeping with London prices and the current value of the pound, but $40 U.S. for internet service? $60 for continental breakfast for two? An honesty bar that charges something like $25 per drink? That is just INSANE. Staff is friendly and helpful, but also sort of clueless. Can't make recommendations or give information without looking it up. Very few of them are English and/or seem to know the city very well.

title: Fabulous Town House Hotel
text: Absolutely perfect in every way. First experience with Firmdale Group and will definitely stay in one of their hotels when I'm next in London or New York. Bedroom with juliet balcony overlooking street, superbly comfortable bed, linen, etc. Lovely breakfast area with garden and interesting decor throughout. Public areas small but it's a hotel with not many rooms. There are two lounges with a self-serve honour bar system. Walking distance is many restaurants and shops in South Ken. Close to station. Went to a sold-out show at V&A but overheard concierge getting tickets for another guest at a little over face value. Best London experience ever.

title: Please Stay Away from this Hotel So I can Keep it to Myself
text: I had been to Number 16 once before, more than 20 years earlier and had loved it then because it really is a kind of non-hotel, and was curious to see how it had fared. I was not disappointed. It has changed and modernized, but it is still a wonderfully civilized and pleasant refuge in the big city. Number Sixteen is actually a collection of several townhouses on a quiet but extremely convenient side street in South Kensington. Because the hotel does not advertise itself as such and it doesn't have a public lobby per se, the atmosphere is quiet, relaxed, like being in your own home or the most elegant Bed and Breakfast. I found the service impeccable. We stayed in one of their larger rooms that opened up to the private, large, peaceful garden in the back. They still have an honor bar but also now have proper restaurant service. (when I had been there earlier it only served breakfast and tea.) Because there are two proper sitting rooms that are for the guests only, this is a hotel where you could comfortably stay in one of their smaller rooms, which I plan to do when I return in the fall. In short, I really didn't want to write a review because I want to keep people away from "my hotel."

title: Stylish
text: Very clean hotel, staff were very friendly. Our room was very tastefully decorated, bed was very comfortable. This hotel is in a lovely location. There is an honesty bar but this room was very quiet, all in all a very pleasant stay

title: Charming for a slower paced visit
text: We stayed here one night when we had a layover (late arrival at Gatwick and early departure from Heathrow). I had read good reviews on TripAdvisor and was curious about the hotel. Normally we stay in the West End, but I like Firmdale properties and the location of Number Sixteen looked very convenient for both airports. (Using the airport express trains, coming from Gatwick into Victoria station your'e 2 stops from the South Ken tube stop

title: Number Sixteen
text: I was moved to Number Sixteen from the Knightsbridge Hotel due to a scheduling conflict. I spent one night there and enjoyed it very much. I had a small, very comfortable room on the 3rd floor at the top of the narrow, winding stairs. It was very quiet and had a window I could open. The staff could not have been better, greeting me so pleasantly when I arrived and showing me around the property and in the restaurant where I ate both dinner and breakfast. The location is excellent, just a few blocks from the South Kensington tube station. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Lidia
text: Today we had our Afternoon tea at the Number 16 hotel. The staff on the front desk and in the restaurant were friendly, efficient and attentive to all our quiries and request. Espetially the waiters and the waitresse in the Restaurant. The food was amazing. We enjoyed in the garden our Afternoon tea. L♡ A♡

title: Comfortable Beds, and Quaint Rooms..
text: Just returned from a 5 night stay at Number Sixteen with my husband. My husbnand has stayed there a few times before for business so the staff knows him well, and are very friendly. The rooms are tastefully decorated, and the beds are so comfortable. The location is really central, and a short walk to the tube station. It was too cold to enjoy the garden, but it looks like it's very well kept. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel to anyone who enjoys a boutique hotel.

title: A gorgeous boutique hotel
text: My husband and I stayed here on the first night of our honeymoon, before going abroad. It was a complete surprise for me - to be honest, I though I would be staying at an airport hotel. How wrong I was! It was the first time I had stayed at one of the Firmdale Hotels (I've wanted to for some time), and I wasn't disappointed. What a gorgeous little gem of a hotel, just perfect. As it was our honeymoon, they kindly upgraded us to the best room - and wow... it was gorgeous. The decor was beautiful, and all of the little extra touches in the room just added to it. We ordered room service, and it met the standards of the rest of the hotel - the food was great, better than other room service meals that I've had. The breakfast room is like a little oasis of calm - I only wish that we had the time to experience afternoon tea there. I will definitely be staying at Number 16 again - it really is one of the best hotels in London.

title: Excellent.
text: This as already my second time in this hotel and I really liked it. Wonderful stylish rooms and the quality in general is great. Breakfast is delicious. The staff was very friendly and I will return for sure.

title: My seventh time at this place and still amazed!!
text: Not only this place is gorgeous, but the staff is one of the politest and friendly ones. It is a Very Small boutique hotel, located 100 meters from South Kensington underground. Breakfast is served at their cuttest garden of the townhouses that were transformed into the hotel.

title: Comfortable, Chic and Friendly
text: Truly a charming, intimate (39 room) hotel, that you feel right at home in. We had several different rooms during our 7 night stay last week and all of them were spotlessly clean. Beautifully and tastefully decorated with a staff that makes you feel at home the moment you arrive. They are friendly, helpful and never too busy to ask if you need directions, or call for tickets, etc. There is a small kitchen which specializes in 24 hour room service. The rooms are small but elegant and no smaller than any other European hotel. Beds were very comfortable. Try to get rooms on the first or second floor as these are a bit larger than the third floor. Also the third floor does not have a lift. The hotel is situated along a beautiful upscale street, one block from the South Kensington tube stop, and from there you can explore every part of the city. We travel to Europe often and are picky when it comes to hotels. Number 16 is a gem in all respects.

title: Conventional and just OK
text: This hotel is superfically attractive, but lacking any real character of its own. Decorative accents, such as piled wooden garden baskets, feel self-consciously chosen--somewhere between quaint and "good design". When we arrived, the desk clerk was unhelpful and curt, bordering on rude. The first room we were given was in the basement, not where we like to be, but we were told we could not have a room on another floor. We accepted the room, but while unpacking noticed a large, wet stain on the bedspread--about 10" x 20". I lifted the cover back and the sheets were damp as well. When told, the desk clerk grudgingly directed us to another room which was fine. Her attitude suggested that she thought we might have been responsible for the wet spot ourselves. Other staff were friendly. Breakfasts were pleasant. The V & A is nearby.

title: Afternoon tea indulgence
text: Haven't stayed at Number 16 but have at The Haymarket and so we decided to have afternoon tea in the garden at No. 16. You certainly don't need dinner after tea at 16. Fantastic cakes and pastries with a excellent choice of teas.

title: Great venue for a party!
text: We hired this venue for my partner's birthday party. I was perfect! The staff were friendly and efficient - attentive but discreet. Very professional. And the canapes were delicious! The garden area is beautiful and perfect for a small gathering (around 30 people). This venue really has the WOW factor - perfect for a special occasion. It almost lost a 'star' as the toilet could have been nicer, but it was nice enough not to deter anyone from wanting to come back. We didn't use the bedrooms but were invited to look at some examples and they looked AMAZING - though a bit on the expensive side! While there isn't a restaurant in this hotel it is in an area that has plenty of nice restaurants to suit every budget.

title: Excellent stay, comfortable and very clean
text: We had a lovely night away in this quirky, stylish hotel. Our room was spotless and the bed was so comfortable

title: Perfect boutique hotel!
text: Small, elegant and quirky as well. This hotel is even better than the last time we stayed there. The staff is amazing, from my Skype call to the emails and theater and restaurant and shopping recommendations. The rooms are large and perfect- with great mirrors and lighting. But the best is the garden- for a leisurely breakfast ( included), high tea ( dinner before a show) and just relaxing reading a book. I could envision a wedding party there! Location in South Ken is great- close to Tube and in a wonderful neighborhood- and away from the huge tourist crowds- and close to walking to the V and A, Hyde Park and even Harrods. My fourth time there- and love it more each visit.

title: charming south kensington place to be
text: I discovered the hotel via a recommendation and felt at home from the first time. Since I am welcomed with personal attention every time I return which makes my trips to London a particular pleasure. Rooms are small but offer all amenities you need

title: Delightful Stay, Minus the Construction
text: Number Sixteen is an intimate, quirkily designed boutique hotel tucked away on a quiet side street of the ideally located South Kensington. Each room has a ton of character and yet all the modern finishes you need from a luxury boutique hotel. The public spaces are similarly stylish and welcoming, and the staff is friendly and accommodating. My only complaint is that there were renovations, inside (changing the wallpaper) and outside (some sort of scaffolding) that were incredibly disruptive starting from around 8 am. There was no notice of this construction on their website, and I found it particularly irritating since I was on a conference call and could not escape the incessant banging noises and reverberations. The staff handled my complaints professionally, but I do think it's a matter of courtesy to notify guests in advance of their construction plans. I would gladly return but would have to call ahead of time to inquire about any expected noise.

title: Outstanding Hotel in London
text: I recently returned from a 5-night vacation in London. I booked my reservation for the Number Sixteen based upon the reviews on this website. Everything you read here is true! The hotel looks exactly as it does on their website (finally truth in advertising)! I was traveling alone, so I stayed in a standard single room on the fourth floor (third floor in Europe). The room was small, but who spends all their time in the room anyways. The room and bathroom was impeccably clean, as was the rest of the hotel. The library was a nice place sit and read while enjoying a drink from the honesty bar. The staff was extremely polite and helpful. The room service food is also good. As a woman traveling alone, I never felt unsafe in the hotel or while walking in the surrounding neighborhood. The hotel is about 2.5 blocks from the South Kensington Tube stop. Anything you could imagine that you'd need is along that walk (bank, post office, pharmacy, restaurants, cafe, etc). I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone planning a trip to London. No hotels are cheap in London, and if they are you have to wonder why. The Number Sixteen is a bargain for the level of accommodations and service it provides.

title: Beautiful hotel let down by the service and food
text: My husband and I stayed here for the weekend with another couple and their baby. We have previously stayed at the Soho Hotel and the Knightsbridge Hotels which we couldn't fault. Number sixteen is very similar in furnishings and rooms. However, the service was not what you'd expect for the price. They seemed to be very short staffed. We had dinner on the first night and it took nearly 2 hours to get our food and they got one of the orders wrong. The food was very hit and miss and not of the same standard of the other Firmdale hotels. The room service was very slow as well and the food was cold and not of the quality you would expect. I think the staff were trying hard but obviously were not properly trained. We ordered some cocktails from the honesty bar and the waiter insisted on making them but they took an hour to come. The room we were in was right near the reception area and so it was a bit noisy. We paid £220 a night which included breakfast. Be careful what type of breakfast is included as we were charged extra. They also tried to charge us for an additional breakfast. Also watch your honesty bar charges as these are quite high. Having said that the hotel itself is beautiful and I love how the rooms and public areas have been decorated. The location is very handy for shopping. The rooms are well appointed although the bathrooms were a little bit small (especially the doors) compared to other Firmdale Hotels we've stayed. The lounge areas are probably the best things about this hotel. They are so comfortable and you can just sit and relax and help yourself to the honesty bar and order snacks - but be prepared to wait a while and your meal might either be pretty good or not good at all. Would we go back? Probably not unless they had a discounted rate. We'd rather go back to the Knightsbridge which I'd give 5 out 5 and the Soho 4.9/5 as it is down a bit of a back street.

title: Great Alternative to London's Top Hotels
text: Number Sixteen (and its sister hotels) are a great alternative to London's luxurious and overpriced hotels. It has a enviable location in South Kensington, just a 3-minute walk from the Underground station. The hotel's decoration and fixtures are both high-quality and tasteful at every corner. Even though the rooms are small, they're comfortable and well distributed. Just right for London, a city in which you pay for location rather than for size (unless you plan to stay in for most of the time). Number Sixteen's staff is very accommodating and helpful, so feel free to call ahead and get ask for help or guidance if you need it. Breakfast is tastefully served and portions are generous and delicious. A great way to start the day.

title: Just brilliant
text: Recently stayed with my partner and it was just great. We had a Deluxe Double which is their largest room category and the room was just amazing. It just felt like we were home! Friendly and attentive reception staff and cosy drawing rooms to chill out with a glass of wine in the evening. ideal for shopping as the hotel is close to Fulham road, Knighstbridge and Kings road. Will definitely return.

title: Afternoon Tea
text: I have passed this hotel many times in the past two years. Finally, in January of this year, I entered it as glimpses through the large ground floor windows had intrigued me. I was welcomed by the friendly staff and was shown the Public Rooms, each one of which is decorated with exciting artistry. The walls and ceilings are hung with modern art,which in themselves, are worth a visit. I was shown the garden and stayed for tea. It was the garden and the memory of that first afternoon tea that made me cross the road again yesterday. The garden is green, cream and pink, with accents of red and orange. It is quiet and shady. The trees protect one from the rain. The sound of water from the carp pond is relaxing and the planting is beautiful: a mixture of beds, plinths and huge pots. Even the tables have little trugs of planted flowers on them. As before, afternoon tea was a real treat, served with care and friendliness. This time, I had champagne! Freshly made sandwiches, home made scones, a selection of little cakes served on chinal familiar from my childhood, were delicious. The whole experience made me very happy.

title: one of my favorites
text: I have stayed at number Sixteen several times when traveling to London. It is like staying in someone's private home but with the amenities of a fine hotel. It is small, intimate and beautifully furnished. But the true charm of the place is the staff. They bend over backward to make your stay comfortable. From securing a reservation to a cup of tea no request goes unanswered. If you like large, glitzy and bustling this may not be the place for you. Number sixteen is a quiet oasis in the city of London.

title: My home in London
text: I have stayed at Number Sixteen a number of times over the years. It always feels like I'm returning to my London residence. Boutique style hotel, wonderful staff, very comfortable rooms that are spotless. Some rooms are quite small. So do opt for a larger room. Continental breakfast is very good. If it's included in your room cost it can be a value. The back garden is lovely. Always try to have tea. Even in your room it's very nice. South Kensington is very convenient. I look forward to my next visit.

title: We loved staying at the Number 16!
text: We stayed for two nights on a weekend and appreciated the quiet location in South Kensington. The Tube station is closeby (2mn). We had room #303 under the roof. Nicely and apparently newly decorated, very quiet, even when we opened the windows. Very comfortable bed. Small but very well thought bathroom. The Breakfast room is bright and close to a small courtyard. We would have preferred a bigger buffet with coffee machines but the staff was here to help all the time. Gluten free and alternate milk available (soja, almond)... if everything was organic, it would have been just perfect!

title: My favorite place in London
text: I love so much this place, the location is perfect, it's very calm and relaxing. When I am there I am feeling at home. The decoration is very nice, warm and charming. The staff is always very kind and helpfull. For me, my London paradise.

title: So lovely!
text: Very cosy and beautiful hotel. It feels like you are in a private home . There is lots of art in all the rooms.The staff were super friendly. We enjoyed traditional English tea in the fabulous conservatory served on their dainty customised Wedgwood china. The portions were delicate: scones finger sandwiches and bite size mini cakes. There is also a nice little garden where you can sit in good weather.

title: Wonderful!!!
text: Number Sixteen was a wonderful place to stay. It was conveniently located near major museums, delicious restaraunts, and the tube (5 minute walk). The staff was very friendly and they went out of their way to make you comfortable. The rooms were charming and clean and very well done. The overall appearance of Number Sixteen was very eclectic with interesting art pieces displayed in the common areas. They also had a beautiful outdoor garden patio where you could sit and relax after a day out. I would definitely recommend it to anyone I know who is going to London.

title: Great Little Boutique Hotel
text: We stayed at Number 16 the first weekend in April 2012 and had a great time. The staff are truly professional and welcoming. Room quite small but very well appointed and comfortable. Bathroom with double basin good size. Afternoon tea is great in the courtyard garden, breakfast buffet also top notch. The drawing rooms are wackily decorated but have a great feel. All in all a truly memorable place to stay in London, beats the anodyne large so called luxury hotels, Number Sixteen exudes so much more style. We will be back.

title: Gorgeous hotel
text: Everything about this hotel is wonderful ... The location, the rooms, the garden. But most importantly the staff who are all delightful. I especially want to thank those who were on duty on the evening of the 30th of April when I was struggling to get to the airport for a long haul flight (tube strike, my cab did not show). They were very very helpful and calming.

title: Afternoon Tea at Number sixteen
text: This afternoon tea was amazing! Excellent sandwiches, scones, and pastries. The place was very beautiful and service ''5 stars''. Possibility to have vegetarian sandwiches on demand. 20 pounds per person only! Good to know: the water is charged (5 pounds for the bottle).

title: Real home from home loved it
text: beautiful townhouse in quiet road in south west london. This hotel is more like staying at a friends house than staying in a hotel. That is meant as a complement as you feel completely welcome and as if you've become one of the family. I was met with a friendly welcome at the reception desk and then given a tour of the house its public areas and up to my room. The hotel has a very contemporary almost boutique funky feel to the decor which may not be everyones cup of tea but i loved it. Room was a good size with a nice large bathroom. bed was really comfy and had a wonderful relaxed 3 day stay. Staff were friendly and helpful. If i need to stay in this part of london again this will definately be my first choice

title: cosy and chic
text: located in a quite street of S. Kensington, this hotel remains a nice and cosy solution in town. some of the rooms are really small, but all of them with a nice decor and personality and miller harris amenities. Breakfast is a nice moment to share, good organic food served in a nice dehor...to try

title: Charming boutique hotel
text: Number sixteen is a very charming boutique hotel in South Kensignton. excellently located close to the tube,Restuarants and shopping. It feels more like staying in an elegant B and B.-- a home away from home. It is delightfully decorated in true Kit Kemp style. staff are friendly and helpful,breakfast just delicious.The room was comfortable and beautifully appointed. My one complaint would be the charge for Wifi .At the room rates ,and given the clientele and the way the world is connected ,Wifi should be complimentary. I would definitely return again to number sixteen.

title: Good but not exceptional
text: I enjoyed my stay at Number Sixteen. As many reviewers state it is in a beautiful street, close to transport and restaurants. It has a lovely feel. The breakfast is plentiful and fresh. The staff are helpful. Downsides? If you have to pay for wi fi it is very (unnecessarily) expensive. Ground floor rooms are noisy as people pass your door continuously and the floors are wooden. My room was nicely decorated but starting to look a little tired. Overall I enjoyed my stay but would probably go for Edgerton House next time.

title: Nice Weekend
text: Good location in central London, beautiful rooms- each one different. The garden area was delightful, a great place to sit in the afternoon to catch the sun. Pleasant staff. The breakfast was great a nice selection of everything. iPod docking station in the Rooms needs updated though.

title: Absolutely amazing stay!
text: Just returned from a wonderful stay at Number Sixteen. Our room was lovely, luxurious and comfortable. The entire staff was exceptional and they made us feel welcome and special. The location is ideal for museums, shopping, dining and sightseeing. The hotel has a luxurious and homey feel with a several magnificent drawing rooms to relax in. Breakfast was great and we were able to enjoy it in the lovely garden. I can’t wait to go back!

title: Feel at home with premium service
text: This place is located in a hot area for design shopping and brunch places, and only a few steps from South Kensington tube station (3 major lines across London) The venue is composed of a few british style homes linked together which keeps the area look like a residential street rather than a hotel. Rooms have been decorated in a typical british home style, just like the guest areas and dining room. This place is a MUST go for those who are sick of large hotel lobbies and frequent passage of people around you while reading peacefully around the fireplace. Also, the many living room style invite you to engage in conversation with local customers while at the same time keeping a feeling of privacy.

title: Perfect Tea for 2
text: Traditional or not? That was the debate about what type of afternoon tea we should have while visiting London. We wanted somewhere with the right mix of modernism and traditionalism. Number 16 provided just that. The new and clean, but cozy and comfortable atmosphere was perfect. The food was delicious and just the right amount, if not too much, for an afternoon tea and lunch. LOVED the scones and the mini egg sandwiches. It was an afternoon that I'll always remember

title: Very good hotel
text: We spent one night here recently. Great location, beautiful garden in the back, quiet, tastefully decorated, kind staff, healthy delicious continental breakfast. Tasteful touches such as linen spray provided. Rooms on the small side and rather expensive but overall very pleasant experience.

title: Number Sixteen
text: My wife and i stayed at # 16 for 7 nights in July while visiting our daughter in London. I can't say enough about the hospitality and comfort provided us by the staff. We were there during the bombings and I cannot even imagine the issues we would have had in a Hyatt or other large chain. The staff was very friendly, very helpful and kind of felt like family after several days. They accomodated our every request. The setting is is very residential, do not even blink about not having a restaraunt - there are 25 within a few blocks and all very good. We would definately stay again!

title: beautiful and well located
text: Number 16 is a relaxed and charming base in a great location. The staff are incredibly helpful and the rooms bear the inimitable stamp of Kit Kemp - whose talent and attention to detail is a privilege to enjoy when staying here.I am looking forward to seeing the new garden which is in progress and will soon be complete.

title: Work trip for the wife
text: This was a work trip for my wife, so I was the spouse tag-a-long. The hotel was expensive, compared to US standards. But our room was paid by work. So we may not have stayed here, if we paid for it. Loved the location, because it was close to the Tube. Rode the Tube everywhere, so the location was great and the neighborhood is really safe. Walking around all times of night (i.e. 3am), so I felt really safe. Overall I would recommend the hotel, if you are staying in London. The only complaint is that the bathrooms are really small (I am 6'7). The bathrooms are for really small people.

title: Beautiful decoration and excellent service
text: Number Sixteen is in a fantastic location for Knightsbridge, South Kensington and the museums on Cromwell Road. A great plus point is the proximity to South Kensington tube station - so very easy to get around London. Great check-in. Very nice receptionist called Helen who couldn't do more to make me feel welcome. As soon as you enter the hotel you feel like you're walking into a very special house. It just doesn't have the "hotel" feel of anonymity which made me feel, as a single female traveller, safe and welcomed. The room was beautifully decorated with bright pinky-red wallpaper which even my husband liked when he arrived on the second night. Important point to note when booking: if you want to have a bath and not just a shower, you have to book a grade higher than the superior double which was what I booked as my bathroom was absolutely titchy to the point where I had to open the bathroom door to dry myself after having a shower just so I could stretch my arms! I haven't honestly been in such a tiny bathroom. That was the downside of my room. And as I was on my own there on the first night I wanted to take advantage of a lovely long soak in the bath which I couldn't do :-( My room was 307 which was on the very top floor only accessible with steps (the lift only goes to the second floor) so I wouldn't recommend it unless you had hand luggage like me. I didn't order room service breakfast which cost £16/17 because it simply wasn't worth it when you have Hummingbird Bakery right around the corner and Carluccio's nearby for a lot less. Plus, I was dying to have a croissant at Patisserie Valerie on Knightsbridge so I walked there instead. Check-out was very smooth. We left at 6.45am and paid up and left very swiftly. P.S. When you check in, they swipe your card and add 40% to the total room charge for "additional incidentals" as a deposit. Very strange, I thought. I was a bit worried when I had a sign a credit card slip for £650 for a two night stay. They have assured me that it hasn't gone through, but I am awaiting my credit card bill with some trepidation....

title: fabulous gorgeous hotel
text: Simply the perfect place to stay! Exquisite, reasonably priced, well-located, utterly comfortable, everything excellent. Gracious friendly efficient staff, lovely breakfast--I just loved everything. I'll always stay at No. 16!

title: Very disappointed with the customer service
text: I have have stayed many times in the firmdale hotels and a few times in Number Sixteen. My last stay however, was very bad as I woke up several times due to faulty air-condition making a loud noise. I phoned down to reception and the gentleman very kindly came up and heard the problem, however could not do anything. I asked to move room, unfortunately it was full and I had no choice than to stay with the noise. As a result I had a very bad sleep and as they are so nice in reception I felt bad about complaining. However, I did say I had a very bad sleep and the AC was making noise throughout the night and the very early morning. They where very sorry and charged me for breakfast. I find it very strange when the obvious a hotel should provide "a good night sleep" has not been met and a customer complains and nothing is done. A nice gesture would have been, breakfast is on us at least or let me offer you a stay next time. The GM wrote me an email later, saying to contact her on the next stay. I did when I stayed in their sister hotel and nothing was done. I arrived very late and he said he thought we where coming yesterday and then said it was a mistake. He then said I had only one person inclusive for breakfast in my booking and he would have to charge me for by partner, although I had written to the GM and said I was coming with my partner. I guess its not a good start when you had a bad experience last time. I remember staying in the Rosewood in London and the keycard was not working and as a result they sent up a bottle of Chablis with cakes and fruits. It was not necessary, but a very nice touch and a good memory. I recommend you check into one of these hotels so you can see 5 star service delivered well even when things don't go as planed. I will not be staying again, as I feel I have been short changed and not been looked after how I would expect to be.

title: Small comfortable and friendly
text: We stayed for 3 nights on a business trip for me and a shopping trip for my wife with some seeing of friends thrown in. Number Sixteen was a very convenient base for all elements, very central a few paces from South Ken tube but in quiet side street. The staff were friendly - the nice man who showed us to our room was exceptionally determined to show us everything on arrival. Reception staff and others were unfailingly pleasant and helpful and cheerful. The deluxe room was well-appointed - very comfortable and large bed (exceptionally comfortable pillows), large enough room to be comfortable but no more, hanging cupboard with real hangers you can actually lift out and put back (one of our hates the chain hotel type you now get in many quite reputable hotels) good polished granite style bathroom with bath and shower and space to set things. No extractor fan, and a tap that made getting cold water a challenge. Air conditioning in the bedroom but as always a bit noisy so we vacillated between leaving it on and off all night, as the room tended to be too hot even in cold weather Minibar and safe. Good drawer space/ Third floor is probably quietest but lift only to second floor and then narrow steep staircase unsuitable for people of limited mobility. There is ready assistance with luggage so this was not a problem for us. Courtesy laptop downstairs for residents. Wifi available for 20 pounds a day which we thought exceptionally expensive and didn't take. Staff willingly printed off a small document transferred to them by email from the residents laptop. Honesty bar, which is always a charming touch, and was well-stocked and easy to use., whether for taking drinks to the room (minibar stock less well chosen) or consuming downstaris, and a pot of tea or coffee always readily available anywhere on request. The two downstairs rooms quickly felt quite small when even one of two small groups of people were present (and their conversations intrusive), but wonderfully like being in someones living room when you more or less had them to yourself. The breakfast room is also quite small, overlooking a pleasant garden space, the room a bit pain quotidien in table style and layout. Excellent breakfasts with fresh fruit (some tinned thrown in for the addicts), greek yoghurt, fresh individual coffee and of course english breakfasts available. Expensive of course but all decent London hotels seem to be expensive and this one no more than you would expect for such a location and this standard.

title: Defenitely one of the best Boutique hotels in London
text: Number sixteen is defenitely one of the best Boutique hotels in London. A very quiet neighbourhood - easy to reach by the tube. Easy waking distance from the central streets. Brilliant decor, Brillant rooms, brilliant food - a perfect place for Tea - they also have a garden. Loved our stay at this brillant ! we will be back again for sure!

title: Beautiful hotel, great staff nice room limited food
text: I stayed in room 204 for two days. The room itself was spacious and nicely presented the hotel is designed boutique type hotel. How best to describe more Home from home than hotel. I really enjoyed stay however be warned no restaurant and very limited room service menu. Plenty of restaurants on fulham road but would have been nice to have the choice. Nice selection of bathroom products and the spray for the pillows was a really nice touch. I slept like a log.

title: As good as ever
text: We have stayed at Number 16 a number of times and really enjoy the boutique nature of this hotel. Wonderfully situated in South Kensington in beautiful Sumner Place yet just around the corner to the South Kensington station and lots of shops and restaurants. Since our last visit the owners have rebuilt the breakfast room which is not a light filled pleasure - unless of course you want to have breakfast in the garden. Great team, very helpful and professional. We will be back !!

title: Lovely cup of cha!
text: Tucked away from the hub-bub of London. Pretty garden with a fish Pond. The fish kept coming to the Surface asking for food! Afternoon tea Is delicious. The mini home-made burgers were a modern twist on a traditional theme.

title: Wonderful room. Fabulous staff
text: Great experience. Would stay here again. Staff were very helpful and pleasant. Room beautifully appointed. Close to South Kensington Station. Walking distance to museums and restaurants. Wouldn't stay anywhere else in London.

title: A sixteen out of ten!
text: I have stayed at the Number 16 several times and it never disappoints. It is a lovely boutique hotel in a wonderful location, close to the South Kensington station, as well as, several amazing restaurants. The beds are extremely comfortable and I particularly love the decor and charm of each room. It's also worth mentioning that if you are coming in on an early international flight they have been known to have a room ready for you as early as 7am (if they have availability.)

title: loved this hotel
text: my daughter and I stayed at number 16 in late october and absolutely loved it. the service was fantastic, the hotel itself is lovely, we had the safari room looking out to the street and we loved being able to look out to see what was happening each morning. It wasnt noisy at all. the breakfast room is lovely with a little garden to look out into. the area is great just around the corner from the kensington tube. we asked the hotel for a recommendation for dinnner and they suggested Bumpkin up the road which was delightful. I catn think of a single thing wrong with the place and cant wait to stay there again.

title: My review is long over due but this shows I'm delighted to still talk about Number sixteen
text: I stayed here weekly for years up until I recently had my second child and as a result I travel less to London. I was a regular for about two years week in week out and firstly this is an amazing gem of a hotel, boutique in all the best ways. Design of the hotel and style is excellent, I wish I owed it. The staff were always amazing and consistent and as they got to know me they made me feel more and more comfortable, in fact as someone travelling on their own, they could not have looked after me better. Great hotel and I miss seeing them on a weekly basis. I have had the pleasure of staying not only in this Firmdale hotel but quite a few within the group and each one greet you with that special personal touch. Love the hotel, love the location, love the staff, love the help they provide, love the attention to detail, love that nothing is too much trouble and I miss staying there.

title: Like staying in a luxurious private home in South Kensington
text: Number Sixteen is so charming and restful that my husband and I, exhausted from jet lag, didn't even bother going out two of the 5 nights we were there, and just had dinner in the casual and very pretty dining room. Then crawled back into our very cosy bed. The hotel is made up of several townhouses put together (one of which is number 16!) It is a Firmdale hotel, so the decorations have that quirky and elegant feeling that all Firmdales have (we've stayed in the Knightsbridge many times, and no two rooms are ever decorated the same way in either hotel.) The hotel was full when we were there but it has a very quiet feeling, with no bustling lobby. There is a lovely sitting room, where you can read the paper or have a drink, or take something from the honor bar, and downstairs a skylit dining room where we had the BEST breakfasts. Lots of choices at the buffet, or you can order a specific breakfast. It seemed to be a very international clientele - different accents and languages at every table. There was one family with young children, but it's not an ideal place for families with kids, because they can't run about much. We were there in January so we didn't use the garden outside the dining room, but it was beautiful even in the winter, and would be a lovely place to sit and have breakfast or tea in warmer weather. This is a residential neighborhood, so it is quiet and the hotel is surrounded by private houses. But very conveniently located two blocks from the South Kensington Tube station. The staff are superb - friendly, accommodating, eager to help. Now that we've found this hotel, I will always stay here when I'm in London. I felt as if I lived in London while I was there, in the best of circumstances.

title: Gem in South Kensington
text: Stunning boutique hotel that's small enough so staff knows you after second night. Our room and the common areas were an absolute wow visually. Plus, it's a great location. Great restaurants in the neighborhood, the "tube" is two blocks away and Short walk to Harrods, Hyde Park, Natural History and Victoria and Albert museums.

title: Charming and Cheerful
text: Stayed at this delightful and characterful hotel on a "girls" trip to London and consistent with its sister hotels, it proved to be a real winner for service, style and comfort. The location is ideal for cultural activities as well as shopping. Easy access to theatreland via underground. Delicious breakfast with great variety. The garden is quite charming and an oasis of solitude. The staff are exceedingly helpful and professional. I was impressed with their enthusiasm and I felt like a really welcomed and valued guest. My room was immaculate and stylishly decorated. Well done yet again to this small hotel chain for providing an exemplary hotel experience!

title: Cozy and so sweet
text: I think it's almost the best place to stay in London- near the South Kensington station. Even if the rooms are small, it's absolutly wonderful.

title: Boutique luxury with a warm welcome
text: We stayed here over Christmas 2013 and I realised I never reviewed it. What a great stay we had - complete with a lovely and thoughtful gift from the hotel on Christmas morning! The rooms are beautifully decorated. Comfy beds, fluffy robes and Molton Brown products. Breakfast is delicious - healthy, tasty. Staff welcoming and helpful. Lounge areas relaxing and comfortable. This hotel has the best of boutique luxury in an excellent location. We will definitely return!

title: Excellent!...but breakfast a let down...
text: Stayed at this hotel with my girlfriend just before Christmas 2004. This hotel is beautiful, warm and cosy and very tastefully furnished. The staff are generally polite, overly helpful and cheerful (a bag of good qualities) and the location can't be beaten. They just let themselves down on breakfast which I thought was a real disappointment. The service was unattentful and the choice was a little limited. I understand it is described as a continental breakfast, but I have had far more imaginative continental breakfasts in Scandinavia for example (and I'm not Scandinavian by the way, no bias intended). However, just a small gripe, if they sort the breakfast out they would get five stars from me in future (hint...hint)...

title: Oasis of Quiet and Luxury
text: The 3rd floor rafter room (superior single) was quiet, clean and beautifully decorated. The room is a little on the small size - to be expected in London, but the bed was absolute Heaven! Just steps away from South Kensington tube station (on the Picadilly Line - direct tube line to Heathrow) and easy walking distance to the Victoria & Albert museum, Knightsbridge (Harrods) and Chelsea shops. Loved it! Would go back again & again if the exchange rate wasn't so lousy.

title: Adorable !
text: I liked everything about this hotel. The pleasant and helpful personnel, the welcome, the great breakfast, the unusual, pretty decor in the rooms, the incredibly comfortable big bed, and the lovely interior garden where you can have breakfast in summer. It is close to the tube and within walking distance of the V&A and Natural History Museums.

title: Boutique hotel par excellence
text: This is a boutique hotel which simply gets it right on all counts. Superbly located for starters (in Kensington) this is a small and extremely comfortable place to "come home to" whilst staying in London. Having 2 lounges in which to relax (one of which is an Honesty Bar) helps enhance the stay - as does the restaurant with its delightful view over a very pretty garden. The furnishing of rooms, both public and private, is pitch-perfect. Add to the foregoing extremely friendly and helpful staff and all boxes are ticked for a perfect stay.

title: My home away from home
text: I have stayed in this hotel several times a month for over five years and it almost always genuinely feels like a home away from home. Service and attentiveness is exceptional, almost all the rooms are large enough, beautifully decorated and bathrooms well appointed, the occasional double glazing challenge and underfloor heating absence in the beautiful marble bathrooms can mean they are at times a little fresh, but the beds are super comfortable, and between room noise mostly fine for a Victorian house! First choice in London always. The Hotel Manager is always present, attentive and caring.

title: Good Hotel near the Subway!!!
text: We have stayed at the HOLIDAY INN EXPRESS LONDON CITY last week, the Hotel offers a pretty good location considering that is only 2 blocks away from the London Underground (Subway) "Old Street Station", this Hotel offers decent rooms with nice showers, good internet and also 110V outlets in the rooms for American travelers which is a plus! The breakfast is included and pretty decent, the attendants are always there! Perhaps the area is not the best due I saw a lot of homeless people nearby but I also police surrounding and some clubs that were decent! My son and I were hungry and next to the Hotel you have choices that open late at night, a place named American Pizza and also another place where they make some nice Kebahs!! If you travel to London and want to stay on budget, this Hotel will be fine! rooms are clean, people are professional and friendly and is worth every penny!

title: very clean, near Underground station
text: It was hard to find a single room in a London Hotel for 2 adults, & 2 older teenagers, but we had a double bed & double fold out couch & it worked for us.. Room was very clean & small by US standards,but ok size. Staff very helpful. Continental brkfast convenient, but same thing every day. Lobby had AC but not rooms. Ok if we closed blinds & left window open during day, otherwise very hot at night. Street very noisy with windows open at night but we quickly learned to sleep through it & I slept well most nights. Room & bathroom very clean but staff didn't clear away used dishes from room. Hotel is close to convenience type stores & some small but good restaurants as well as a Tube stop.

title: Budget Hotel
text: This hotel is very convenient to Old Street Station and Moorfields Hospital. It charges for wifi. It is almost completely re-furbished thus providing good clean and practical accommodation. The main problem is breakfast...if your needs are simpleeg toast, cereal, fruit juice ...its OK but the cooked components are best left alone. In comparison with one or two adjacent hotels it is a little pricey. Very well situated for bus/tube access to central London. It is in a student area and probably the area is not too savoury. For a simple short stay it has to be a candidate.

title: Good city hotel.
text: We stayed a night at the hotel in October. The room was small but perfect for just one night. On arrival we were placed in a room on the road side and there was a party opposite. Having two children we asked if we could be moved and this was no problem at all for the staff. Breakfast was very good and enjoyed by all.

title: First time in London
text: Holiday inn is a cheap choice to the centre of London. It is in a highly growing area with many restaurants, markets and bars. The period we went it was very quiet though. There are bus stops outside of the hotel and the tube is very near. The room is very clean

title: Complicated
text: Standard Holiday inn hotel in terms of quality. The main problem it was the location. We arrived at 1h30AM at hotel and the was Police inside... The breakfast is very simple. No cheese and ham. The Old Street metro station is close to the hotel.

title: No frills and a great location
text: It was clean - good hotel, good value and a great location in a very trendy district of London. Its great for business - looks awful from the outside but was friendly and cheerful. All in all - it was good enough.

title: Good base, easy access into London
text: Spent 3 nights here. Old st station is a 5 minute walk away so great for access into London. Rooms are comfortable with coffee, tea and a handy smart phone in the room for guests to use. Hoxton Square is a 2 minute walk away with a few nice restaurants and a great cocktail bar which I would definitely recommend. Breakfast was nice, all the basics do great to set you up for the day. Lifts are a bit rickety but did at least work! All in all a great base for exploring London a reasonable price.

title: Would stay again & recommend
text: I usually stay at Premier Inns and decided to try a Holiday Inn Express for a change. The room was as expected (practical, everything you need), the bathroom was nice with a double shower cubicle no bath. Good to have a double set of towels despite being a solo traveller. The bed was surprisingly soft but comfy. The breakfast was basic with just sausage, bacon, beans and scrambled egg as the hot choices. It was included. There was also fruit, yogurt, ceraels, bread, croissants. Location good being 3mins walk from Shoreditch High St and probably the same in the opposite direction to Old Street underground.

title: Very nice place
text: I was there during my visit in London in 2019 and it was excellent! Reception, breakfast (fits various cultures) and then there was everything excellent about the rooms. More than value for your money.

title: Horrible place even for 1 day only.
text: A door separate your room from your neighbour (not a wall)... Rooms are noisy. Poor breakfast. Staff incompetent. Price high. If you're going to reserve here...change hotel. Holiday Inn is no longer guarantee of good balance price-quality.

title: Great service and room
text: Stayed in this hotel before and will definitely return. The reception staff were very helpful and took their time to pass the time of day with the whole family. Even though the room is basic it was beautifully clean, especially the bathroom. Great shower too! Breakfast was busy but still plenty to choose from. Superb location for Spitalfields Market. Overall I would recommend this hotel.

title: good value base for a london trip
text: Weekend holiday with friends. Didn't want to pay extortionate prices and this hotel fits the bills. Clean rooms and modern facilities with all the basics you need. Not the prettiest location and no great view from your window I agree but within short walk from old street station and makes a great base for sight seeing London. Very busy area at night with lots of bars and nightclubs in the neighboring area but I wasn't disturbed by noise and slept really well. Don't expect all the extras you get for free at the more expensive hotels as you pay for them in the cost of your room.

title: Xmas shopping trip
text: Nice hotel in great location just a 5 min walk from tube station ( old street station, northern line ) great bars and restaurants in the area...... well worth a visit. Shoreditch within 5 minute walk. Car park available if needed, good breakfast and very comfy beds.

title: Not the Ritz, but good!
text: Got a good rate for this hotel... Rooms were ok.. and all was ok. The Northern line of the station was closed and did cause some trouble but the rest was fine. The hotel is comfortable, though the rooms are not very large.
