title: Looking Tired
text: Stayed here Saturday 23rd June for a wedding close by so the location was ideal! The reception area could be better, as i walked in the door, it was obvious a coach had arrived before me and people were in the way of others as there was no one to take charge of the situation very hectic! The staff were lovely but had no reservation for me when I had arrived, fortunately I had my booking.com receipt but still there was some problem with the booking. Got there in the end and found my room. The room was clean and tidy as was the bathroom however when it came to sleeping the beds were so comfortable and bedding fresh that I was so looking forward to a relaxing sleep, wrong! two guys outside decided to have some kind of heated discussion, at first I thought they were in my room as I could hear them so clearly but we were on the second floor! Their conversation went on for a good hour or so and if I could open the window and tell them to clear off I would have done! I think some serious double glazing would not go amiss here as this was three in the morning! Breakfast was hectic to say the least and we sat in the bar area to eat it (near the reception area) this is where I noticed that it was very lacklustre and could do with a good wash down on the marble and also the paintwork! It is quite pricey for what you get but then again London prices! not a lot of work needed to make this looking a great place at a good price in my opinion, just a bit of general cleaning, washing down paintwork, tables, bar marble and paintwork here and there and it would look good.

title: One night theatre trip
text: Chose this hotel as it was a good price for London and included breakfast. Travelled in to Euston by train and it was really easy to get to, just three stops up on the Northern Line and then a 5 minute walk. Check in was efficient, although the lady checking us in could've been a little more friendly or given us a smile. We arrived at 1 and went straight to our room, although we had been informed check in was at 2 so this was pleasing. Our room on the first floor was clean and nicely decorated, the bed was comfy, air conditioning good (which was needed as it was extremely warm), bathroom very nice and a good, hot, powerful shower. I had asked for a quiet room at the back, as previous reviews had said the rooms facing the front could be noisy, and that was what we received, slept very well. Breakfast was good, plenty of choice, well stocked and although it was self service buffet style there were plenty of staff around cleaning tables and replenishing food and drink. Check out was 11am but we were able to leave our luggage, free of charge, until we travelled home in the evening. All in all it ticked all the boxes for a short, reasonably priced stay in London and we would definitely stay here again.

title: RECEPTION & HOUSEHOLD STAFF UNHELPFUL
text: nice stay in the hotel, clean and basic. long queues at reception, and staff under pressure. Within minutes of leaving hotel, i rang to advise i left my new glasses on the bedside locker. advised housekeeping had not yet finished the rooms and I would be called back when manager on duty. Rang consistently every day for 5 days to be told glasses were not found and were not in lost property & phonecall was never returned.

title: Clean, tidy, well located
text: Stayed here as part of a business trip and it was ideal. The location is great, near the tube, easy access to the city and Islington where my conference was. Staff, friendly, room clean, IHG points, located perfectly. What's not to like? Holiday Inn Express could be improved with a better breakfast offering (the same in all of them), but other than that, excellent and good value for money

title: Don't Stay if youre hoping for a quiet hotel for a good nights sleep
text: We stayed here for two nights. The first night was on a bank holiday eve. The hotel was extremely busy and full of kids who ran up and down the corridor, sat in the lift area yelling and abusing other guests. When I raised this with the manager he seemed a little too blaze for my liking after I hold him I had been abused by one of the groups of kids who were ' hanging out' in front of the lift. Also you could here people yelling from the street below even though the windows seemed to be double glazed. The only shinning light and the reason I am not giving it a terrible rating is the other staff were nice and breakfast was good and served piping hot. Also located close to Old Street station which is handy

title: very poor customer service
text: Im not a very picky person, but customer service must be improved!!! The guy at the front desk couldnt even lift his head to welcome us, not even talking about the simple smile. Im working myself at the hotel industry so was very disappointing to experience such a bad customer service. Otherwise, the hotel was quite ok, but my stay at the Holiday Inn Express Croydon was much much better. Nights sleep wasnt great either as you can hear the noisy street outside as you would sleep with an open window.

title: Good value, good service
text: Hard to fault this hotel for business travel - fast, efficient check in and a clean, comfortable, quiet room. Very reasonable price too, I'll certainly stay here again when next in the area. The only downside is parking but thats not unusual for a central london location. If you're leaving early in the morning save yourself some money and park in one of the sidestreets & avoid the expensive car park.

title: Can't Get Any Better
text: Great location, excellent room, friendly staff, great price, and unexpectedly great hot breakfast. Rooms are spacious & very clean, and loved the shower. Can't really say much for the staff. At check-in, they accommodated me although I arrived early without warning. Night shift staff was very helpful with ideas about where to eat.

title: Awesome Location
text: This is an average 3 star hotel. Nothing fancy, but overall a decent stay. The breakfast is typical English breakfast and was plentiful. The staff was friendly and accommodating when necessary. The location is the selling point for this place. Taxi services were easy, two busy stops 50 steps away and very close to the tube. There’s even a small, quick stop market next door. My only concern would be the mold in the bathroom. I’m sure the room was cleaned to it’s best ability

title: Dissapointing
text: I booked this hotel as a surprise and my husband was definately surprised when the hotel took over £1000 from my account instead of £350. This ruined the surprise for him along with the theatre tickets that I had purchased. I was given some IHG points as an apology which would not get me anything. I work for a hotel group so these points were not really what i was looking for. I needed an additional room and called to see if they would offer another one at the same rate as i had paid, i was told no. I offered to give the points to cover the difference, I was told no. I asked if i could use the points for car parking, i was told no. The customer service that i received was not good at all and due to this i would not stay or reccommend this hotel. The bedroom was ok apart from very noisy air-con and very lumpy bed.

title: Reliable and comfortable London hotel
text: This is the hotel I normally use when I'm in London for work, and I've stayed many times now. It does everything I want for a business trip - comfortable, clean, quiet, and relatively spacious rooms with enough space to do a bit of work if that's what you want. Breakfast included, it's not spectacular, but absolutely fine to get you going in the morning. Location is good to walk to good bars and restaurants. Old Street tube stop a few minutes away. Staff have always been friendly and helpful. Can't fault it!

title: Great customer service and a good place to stay for a London trip
text: We stayed at the hotel in October for two nights. It was a great place to stay in London for a quick visit to the city. It is not far from the London underground and is opposite the bus stop to the city. So it was indeed a good place to stay. The staff are excellent and very helpful to find your way around London. A sufficient breakfast as well. Superb quality and value for money. Keep up the good work.

title: Great sleep adn friendly helpful staff
text: I stayed 3 nights here with a bus trip and it was a wonderful place. Good beds, modern bathrooms, good breakfast with lots of choice. Lots of business travellers during the week and families on the weekend. The front desk staff was helpful, one of our group had trouble with making an overseas phone call and the desk was fast and efficient in getting the problem straightened out. I would love to stay again. Close to restaurants and tube stop but as we travelled by bus, I'm not sure how far it would be to major attractions.

title: Not such a quiet night away
text: The hotel lobby and bar are immaculate but the rooms are a little tired and very small when you have a the pull out bed up and I had shower fittings that fell off when you tried to dispense soap. The noise was terrible as it was the start of half term and some parents thought it would be okay for their little cherubs to play football in the corridors and lift lobby's. I was greeted by a very busy reception team who managed to get my room ready 45 minutes early which was nice but the informal way of being greeted needs work as I was referred to as "oh your a reward club member" . the staff were friendly and helpful.

title: Weekend in Shoreditch
text: Stayed here last weekend as had a night out in Shoreditch, I requested an early check in as was arriving on an early flight, got the the hotel about 11am and was granted the early check in and also given a late checkout until 14:00 along with a welcome letter and free drink & snack voucher as a platinum IHG Rewards member. Hotel included free wifi which admittedly was a little slow but it was free after all so I didn't mind at all! The staff were great, I asked at reception for directions to the venue we were going to on the Saturday and not only did they tell me but actually printed me a map too, I thought this was a great touch! Room looked brilliant and the bathroom was lovely! Black tiles in bathroom and a blue colour scheme throughout the room, was really modern and looked recently renovated. Included with the room we also had breakfast, sausage, scrambled egg and beans great to start the day! All in 5 stars for a great stay, will definitely stay again!

title: Nice Hotel at a convenient location
text: This is my second stay at this hotel and my experience has been consistently good ! The hotel is a nice value for money. Rooms are good. The staff were exceptionally friendly! Lots of restaurants around that place that are open till late in the evening! The Old Street Tube station is nearby. Overall , a nice experience staying at this hotel !

title: Not good
text: We chose a non-smoking room, but when we cheked-in they give us a room that smells cigarretes. they change our room in the next day, but the phone was broken.

title: Very good value for money
text: This hotel is very good value for money! Perfect location in a lively neighborhood without it being disturbing. Clean rooms with comfortable beds. Even the bed sofa is OK. Nice bathrooms with a good shower. The breakfast was surprisingly good. And the hotel has got a friendly serviceminded staff! I will definitely recommend this hotel and I will absolutely consider it for my next London Weekend. Takk for oss

title: Overpriced and noisy
text: Staying here for a week, wi-fi is 10.5£ PER DAY (with special offer 45£ per week, that's amazing) payed on top of 150£ per noisy night (every time the heating system turns on it's like a rave in the room above and every fart from the other rooms is like a bomb). I'm staying on the 1st floor and people on the upper deck of the buses can see me naked out of the shower. Rooms are always tidy, the hotel staff is very professional and will kindly help you out with everything but I don't think this is worth the money you'll pay. If you want some breakfast go to the Breakfast Club a few meters towards the City on the left.

title: Wow was this a pleasant surprise!
text: OK so my client books me into a Holiday Inn Express - not very good I thought! Well was I ever wrong. Let me start by where the hotel is located. It is about 3 minuteswalk from Old St tube station which is just so convenient. There are quite a few restaurants and pubs within easy walking distance. The check in staff were really friendly and SMILED! Something sadly lacking in a lot of London hotels. The room was very contemporary with a choice of pillows and quite well appointed although a little basic. Temperature control was excellent - again often sadly lacking. Breakfast was complimentary(as was a newspaper) and was perfectly adequate with the breakfast room staff absolutely delightful. Again they all smiled and also engaged with you. Check out was efficient with the ever-present smile. The only reason I am not giving this hotel 5/5 is that the bathroom was a bit small and the corridors had an "office" basic feel to them. I would DEFINITELY stay here again.

title: Good bed, poor menu
text: I stayed here as part of a Newmarket coach trip - a switch from the advertised "Docklands" hotel. We were booked in for bed and continental breakfast, and both were acceptable. The bed was very comfortable with a choice of frim or soft pillows. The room had TV , tea and coffee, and several mirrors! the shower was a good size and the towels good. There were tissues in the bathroom but only bottled gel was provided - so if you don't like that for washing bring your own. The breakfast was more than is usually supplied as "continental". -As well as the usual hot drinks, there was a variety of cereals, juices, yogurts,. bread including m.y.o. toast, and sausages and scrambled eggs. The BIG disappointment was the provision for an evening meal. The location did not look safe for a woman to go out on her own so I was stuck with the bar offering. -One area was designated a "restaurant".! from a limited menu starting with a burger @£13.50 I ordered "Steamed salmon with broccoli and new potatoes".@£18.50. Immediately I was told they had neither broccoli or new potatoes! and was offered chips. I refused the chips having had some at lunch time, and suggested carrots instead of the broccoli. I was then offered cauliflower and roast potatoes - which made it clear that the food is bought in ready cooked! I had no option but to accept. The Salmon was very good - adequate portion and well cooked. The cauliflower and potatoes were definitely NOT!. The cauliflower was defrosted and warm but very hard - I ate it because I knew raw cauliflower was not harmful. The "roast" potatoes were hard boiled with a brown mark about the size of a £2 coin on each. I managed one only, as they were almost raw. No comment was made when I pointed out that I had been unable to eat them. I had wanted a Cinzano but the bar did not stock it so paid £3.50 for a J20. Other members of the coach being in parties fond very good Italian restaurants nearby, but on the first night of a trip it is not clear who is alone.

title: Saturday night stay
text: On the plus side reasonable price for reasonably Central London. On the downside, lots of noise from outside with all the people going to and from bars and nightclubs plus traffic. Breakast choice was very limited compared with similarly priced competitors such as Premier Inn. Room itself was quite nice although smaller than Premier Inn rooms.

title: Holiday Inn Express wins for best breakfast at a tourist-class hotel.
text: I am a big fan of Holiday Inn Express. They tend to be modern, clean, and comfortable, and this location is within easy walking distance to the Tube. Delicious breakfast and coffee. The only caution I have is that it's not the best part of town if you're traveling with young kids.

title: Not quite sure what the negative reviews are all about??
text: I booked this hotel for my partners birthday as we wanted to be close by to shoredittch brick lane spital fields and the coolest ever bikers heaven The Bike Shed the location was simply perfect...........The staff are very friendly and attentive without being intrusive and our room was exceptionally clean as for the bathroom it was faultless as for the bed it was like a gigantic marshmallow a perfect nights sleep. Breakfast was plentiful and a great choice I suggest saving some room as the culinary delights of the street foods nearby is not to be missed either. All in all I recommend this hotel to anyone first time in a holiday inn and certainly not my last if they are anything like is one!

title: Two night stay
text: We have stayed in this hotel before, but last time the air conditioning was extremely noisy all night - this time it was much quieter thankfully. The room was clean and spacious but very dim, and definitely needs better lighting. The desk light was a joke. The desk/dressing table needed to have a mirror above it on the wall, as the bathroom didn't have much space for make up etc. Breakfast is a buffet and it would have been nice if the croissants had been warm, and although there are scrambled eggs and sausage it would have been nice to have had some bacon. All very basic and not inspiring, but it was included in the price.

title: Does what it says on the tin - functional
text: I booked this hotel for a city break for my wife, daughter and myself. The hotel was probably better than I expected insofar as there was less noise from street traffic etc. Room was clean and big enough (it was only a base after all) although more storage space would have been appreciated. My daughter slept well on the sofa bed and the air conditioning in the room, although perhaps noisy, was effective. Breakfast was functional, not a great choice of options, but plenty of what was there. Check-in was quick and easy and the reception staff were always polite, helpful and smiling. Old Street tube station (the nearest station) was closed for the Saturday/Sunday while we were there. However, the no.55 bus stops across the road from the hotel. This bus terminates at Oxford Circus and also stops at Holburn which is very close to the Bristish Museum and is about 100 yards from Holburn Tube Station. Hoxton Square and its environs offered a range of dining options. The three of us ate at a noodle bar just outside the square on the first night and also used the 'real' burger restaurant in the square. Both were excellent and child friendly.

title: Enjoyed our stay
text: We stayed Sept 1. We had a family room which was excellent, spotless, beds very comfy except for the "firm" pillow which seemed to resemble a block of wood. Was too tired to go back down to reception so they may well have changed if requested. We arrived before noon and the duty manager rang housekeeping and our room was made ready for us within 30 mins, which they didn't have to do. We asked for more milk & coffee and were given them with a cheery smile. All reception staff were very friendly and helpful. Air con was very efficient, only problem was the noise from outside the hotel (sirens etc), which I would expect almost anywhere in London to be fair. Breakfast wasn't the best but was adequate. Was reasonable value for money altho the prices were inflated everywhere because of the Games. Location wasn't really what we wanted but we booked so late there was little choice. Having said that if using public transport it would be very good.

title: Great stay.
text: Expected the Tripadvisor rating to be higher than 3.5, the hotel in our opinion certainly deserves it. Staff on reception were very friendly and helpful and check in was quick and efficient. Our room was spacious by London standards and well appointed. Some nice touches including free Smartphone to use during your stay with free telephone calls and internet and iron and board hanging on wall in wardrobe area. Bed was reasonably comfortable but was just a standard double size. We had requested extra pillows via their pre arrival e-mail and these were in our room on arrival. Very nice modern showeroom with a good shower. Breakfast was better than we expected, cereals, croissants, muffins, fruit etc. and a nice hot selection of bacon, sausage, beans and scrambled eggs. Even though busy it was kept well stocked and tables cleared quickly. Will definitely return, thought it good value for money and location also great, lots of restaurants in easy walking distance and a bus stop opposite to take you to Oxford Street.

title: Great location!
text: My husband, 2 daughters (7&9) stayed at the hotel for 7 nights. Since all we did was sleep there, it was a very nice accommodation. The bathroom was very clean, and so was the room. The beds weren't the most comfortable and the room was small (but since we didn't spend any time other than sleeping in it, it wasn't a big deal). Location was great! There was a little grocery store across the street which was great for buying water bottles, snacks etc. The tube station was an easy 5 minute walk from the hotel. Breakfast was the same everyday, but very good! Wifi was free, which was also a great plus for us! There were no toiletries in the room, but there was a sign offering them, if needed. Overall we were happy with our stay here! (Getting to Heathrow airport from the hotel was an easy tube ride, once you know your way around)

title: Great Location, not such a great hotel
text: The staff were excellent. My room was small and stuffy - Aircon was making quite a racket, and my bed had been slept on so much that it just flopped to the side when i got on it - very uncomfortable. The Breakfast was TERRIBLE! I have never had such a terrible breakfast from a hotel in my life - eggs were runny on both mornings I was there, they shouldn't even be allowed to call whatever was in the machine Orange juice. I ended up eating cereal both days. The staff were very accommodating and friendly, the bathrooms were great - nice big shower. Free WIFI is a big plus. I would recommend for a short one night stay, but would rather look elsewhere if you are planning on staying in London for a while.

title: Average
text: My wife and I visited London for the New Year's Eve 2012/2013 and stayed for 2 nights in this hotel. The room is clean and I think it was recently refurbished.The bathroom is nice and we got fresh towels every day. The best way to move from and to the hotel is by bus (there is a bus stop just outside/ line 55 and 243) We preferred to take the bus and change at Holborn station, as it is a central line station. The Old city tube station is a bit far from the hotel and appeared a bit inconvenient to me. What I didn't like? First of all the a/c was making an irritating noise from times to times. It is a bit annoying when it happens in the middle of the night. Secondly, breakfast is poor and overcrowded, as it is served 6.30-10.00. It's even worst than in other Holiday Inn hotels I've experienced. And lastly the internet service is very expensive - as in all Holiday Inn hotels. Overall, if you can book it in a fair price it is a moderate choice for a low budget getaway to the beautiful city of London.

title: Very clean bathroom
text: Stayed one night while working in town. London hotel prices always make me wince and at £199 inc breakfast for a double room with a sofa bed this was the cheapest I could find near to where I needed to be. 10 minute walk from Liverpool Street station. Good size room at the back of the hotel (so away from the busy road at the front). Very clean, especially the bathroom which was sparkling and had a very good oversized walk-in shower. Comfy bed, squishy pillows, big fluffy duvet. Very good night's sleep. Would definitely book again.

title: In the heart of it, but there is better
text: This was my first visit and still not sure if it will be my last. It is a basic, functional hotel that is looking a little tired, but is close to Moorgate, Liverpool St etc, so ideally placed. Like others I reckon there is something up with the air extraction in the bathroom - could never turn the thing off, so ended up packing a towel in the gap to reduce the noise (like a jet taking off!). On the plus side, the staff were happy to help, bed is good and shower looked brand new. If it's a good rate - try it!

title: Ok for London While with work
text: Wasnt overly impressed with this hotel. Was clean enough, rooms could do with getting updated. Was in great location for where we needed to be - which was why we booked it! Places to eat/drink close by! few parking spaces which you have to pay extra for, reception staff were great and very friendly!

title: Not 10 out of 10 but good.
text: When booking one of the Holiday Inn Express hotels I usually don't worry. I know what to ecpect. Basic room, good bed and and a good breakfast. Worldwide the same standards for a reasonable price. Quoting a management reply to a review last month on Tripadvisor

title: Friendly, clean, quiet and a great night sleep
text: In a perfect location with a two minute walk to the tube station in the centre of the roundabout, including lots of bus stations that go in every direction, buses run frequently. The hotel was very clean and tidy. My room was very quiet compared to most hotels I stay in before around London. I couldn’t hear anything from outside even with a joining door to the next room, which is lockable from the inside so no panic hear. Friendly staff with big smiles on their faces. Breakfast was great, tasty and fresh. The comfortable beds and the quietness are the two main things I want from a hotel stay, so big props. I loved the hotels iPod/phone style hand held device which you can take and use on your travels around London. It uses a 4G connection and has a lot of info on events, shows and attractions in the city. Nice little feature. Free to use on you stay if returned. Freeview tv, air con, great bathroom and shower. Stayed for one night and my experience was very satisfying. I’ve stay in more expensive and upper market hotels and not always had a great experience despite the glits, glamor, fame and theatre. Will stay again later this year.

title: Not too bad but still not impressed.
text: After reading many of the other reviews, I wasn't looking forward to staying in this hotel. I had come over for a knee consultation, so unfortunately didn't get to pick where my own accommodation as the states of guernsey pay for it. The room was £260 just for one night - so I was expecting something really nice, despite the fact it's in an expensive area, spending that amount of money, you would expect something really upper class. When I checked in, the woman on reception had no idea what I was saying - and I'm English. This is a "Holiday Express Inn" where you would've thought foreign visitors would stay when they visit the mainland. If this woman couldn't even understand me - someone without an accent and who speaks perfect english - how on earth was she meant to understand someone from Germany or France or even Scotland? Another thing that really got on my nerves was that I woke up to the sound of building in the room next to me at 7am! The people that are staying in the hotel will have probably been travelling throughout the day or night and are shattered! I was absolutely raging that they had the audacity to have people building so early in the morning when I'd been on planes and trains all day, and was extremely tired and looking forward to a nice lie in! I wasn't even warned that these people would be working so early in the morning! I mean - DRILLING at 7am?! Really?! Who does that?! So when I eventually got back to sleep, I was woken by a knocking at the door. It must've been about mid-day, so I was confused as to why someone was knocking on the door. I answered the door to find one of the receptionists at the door - demanding money! When I checked in, I asked the woman who checked me in if it would be ok if I had a lie in and checked out late - she said it would be fine. She never mentioned anything about having to pay £30 just because I checked out a little later than I was meant to! My charming visitor even told me that if I didn't pay he'd have to throw me out of the hotel - IN MY PYJAMAS! Talk about customer service?!!?!!! After I quickly packed my belongings and threw some clothes on because I was told to get out - even after paying THIRTY POUNDS (which I would've thought would guarantee me time to even make myself decent!) I started my long journey home (4 hours on the first train, 30 mins on the second train and a flight for 2 hours home!). By the time I got home I realised I'd left a necklace at the hotel that I'd stayed in the previous evening. I called up the hotel as soon as I realised this and was put on hold about thirty times and transferred to numerous people. I then spoke to a woman who couldn't really understand what I was saying but understood that I'd left my necklace at the hotel. She said they'd found the necklace and that she'd email me regarding my address and payment for postage. That's right - they expect me to pay for my own necklace to be posted back to me. And not just 50p - £7.00!!!!!!! I STILL haven't received an email from the woman I spoke to, despite saying I'd be happy to pay the cost for postage - and I spoke to her over a week ago now. The necklace I left in the hotel is very sentimental to me - it's the last thing I have from my Mum, who I no longer have contact with, so I think it's fair to say I'm very upset, as I doubt I'll ever get it back :( The only good thing I can say is that it wasn't actually as loud as I expected reading the other reviews, despite being on a main road in London. Also, the male member of staff that worked on the Tuesday evening (the ninth November) was extremely friendly and helped me find a McDonalds for my dinner - he was really very lovely to me (and pretty hot too!) so that was a rose in a bed of thorns. Would never recommend this hotel to anyone. Ever. I'm never going to get my necklace back and I'm absolutely gutted about it as I'll most probably never recieve anything from my Mother again. :'(

title: Great Experience
text: My partner and I stayed for two nights here. We were warmly greeted and check in was swift. Our room was clean .bright and airy. The location was perfect for our needs only a five minute walk to nearest tube station. Breakfast was ample and included hot and cold options. The staff were all friendly and professional. Great value for money. Will definitely be returning.

title: Standard Holiday Inn Express
text: This hotel is a nice, clean, standard HI Express. The staff are very friendly and efficient, the hotel is very clean and it is only 10 mins walk from Bishopsgate and therefore a great value hotel for when you need to visit firms in the City. It's probably not a great location for tourists though. The other bad point is the street noise. Whilst the bed was very comfortable, the noise of sirens on police cars driving past during the night woke me a couple of times. But then again, you are in a big city!

title: Mixed Bag
text: The rooms are well decorated, much better then a premier inn to a certain degree. What I love. The walk In Shower. Why cant all hotels have walk in showers? Free wifi. Free Breakfast. What I don't like. No restaurant. I didn't even think to look to see if there was when booking as I would have booked elsewhere. The 2night room service" that's Offered is a bit of a joke to be honest. Food was cheaper on Just Eat at the same place. By a good margin Also. It's London, and very noisy. The area is very run down in general and wasn't nice to be out in the dark. The dated TV interface and channels don't work. Ended eating crap every night ! Just not what I was expecting. Last thing i wanted to do after a 10 hour day is end up going back out to find food. The rooms are clean and well looked after. but the corridors and bar areas need a good deep clean and a bit of a refurbish. The lifts are very dodgy, they are 20 years old and need a overhaul. I gave them a miss for coming down as it was quicker to walk. Parking outside is £40 a night, i don't recall seeing this when booking, luckily I left the car at work. But ended up with a PCN cause of TFL's hatred of cars. To sum up. Location okay if you like it busy. Expensive parking. Free buffet breakfast. Wouldn't stay again, the lack of restaurant being the decider rather then the rooms.

title: Holiday Inn Express need to up their game
text: It comes to something when I'd rather stay in a Travelodge than a Holiday Inn Express. While the former have improved lately by refurbishing and installing comfortable beds, as well as improving the breakfasts (part from the terrible croissants!), Holiday Inn Express have stood still and been overtaken. The bed here was positively uncomfortable. Lumpy mattress and there seemed to be no difference at all between the "firm" and "soft" pillows" - they were both very firm. And they still persist with the bafflingly small range of hot breakfast items - sausage, scrambled egg and beans. Also, despite our room being at the back of the hotel away from the main road, we were still plagued by late night noise as on this side there are student halls of residence, with students returning noisily from their Friday night out well into the small hours. On the plus side the staff were fine, the price not too bad and the location good, but I think next time I'd rather stay a little further out at a (cheaper) Travelodge and get a better night's sleep.

title: A good base to sleep and shower...
text: I was very conflicted and still am regarding this hotel... I had both truly excellent points and real detractors, but overall it's a good average value to see london from a convenient location at a great price with a buffet breakfast. First, the good points - Location! Right in the center of everything with easy access to the Underground and a 24 hour front desk. Super convenient and also has a sainsburys next door. They offer a pretty nice buffet breakfast with a few hot items among the breads and cereals, which was a pleasant surprise. The coffees and juices served are good qualities and not watered down. The front desk staff is helpful and, in fact, changed our room when we complained about a cigarette smell in the first one (non-smoking hotel). Also, they do offer a free wifi service. And, the "A/C noise" that is a big topic of complaints in reviews is seriously not that bad... Yes it clicks on in the middle of the night, but that's because it maintains a baseline temperature that you get to set. The negatives - Not the best street with a bar, a skeevy looking club, and several liquor stores. The elevator makes really weird groaning sounds. The beds were not comfortable at all and were super tiny (my husband and I shared a double bed that was the same width as my son's pull out couch bed). And the wifi, while free, had a tendency to be super slow, hard to log into, and unreliable at busy times. Overall, I'd stay there again - just be aware of the negatives and look past them for the positives.

title: Nice hotel, conveniently located
text: My husband and I spent two nights in London as part of a longer trip in the UK. It was a nice hotel with very friendly, helpful service. I went to wash my hands when we first got to our room and no water came out of the spigot in the sink or shower. The toilet flushed just fine. We left the taps open and the water came up after a couple of minutes. That's the only negative thing I can say about our stay and that's not even negative. Oh. That and the tough croissants at the breakfast buffet. The buffet has a very good selection: eggs, bacon, sausage, pastries, cereals, yoghurt, fruit, etc. We didn't care for the sausages that much, but that could be because we really like USA style sausages so much better. The croissants were tough, which was a disappointment. The scrambled eggs were really fresh and good. I put a slice of cheese on top of mine and that upped the flavor quotient. The location is good - close enough to walk to the Spitalfields and Brick Road Markets. The Tube is about a block and a half away. St. Dunstans in the East is also walkable - it's in the Spitalfields area. It's the shell of a church that predates the 1600s and was bombed in World War II. It's been turned into a lovely park.

title: Good Location
text: On a recent trip to visit my daughter in London we made reservations at Euston Square hotel. The location is great (a little noisy as it is near a hospital so sirens were the norm) and having tube stops close by as well as St Pancras train station (we took the train to Paris) was a bonus! The room was small but comfortable for the two of us. Having housekeeping service daily with fresh towels and bed made was nice. Continental breakfast was good and the bar/restaurant was nice to have for an evening snack and cocktail. Wireless was a little touch and go but all and all it was a good place to stay for the affordable price.

title: Handy location, small but immaculate room, ok breakfast
text: I stayed at the hotel whilst in London for work. It is very conveniently located about 30 seconds from Euston Square station and around a 3 minute walk from Euston station, meaning various train and tube routes are available to you. The check-in was prompt, professional and courteous. The room was very small but had everything you would need for a short stay, reasonably comfortbale bed, tv, tea/coffee facilities, heating and air conditioning, lovely bathroom, good quality shower, decent black out blinds etc. The bed was a small double perfect for one person, but the room would be too small for a couple. The only other downside to the room was it was facing out the front of the hotel and despite double glazing the road outside is fairly busy on a Saturday night with traffic and police etc, so noise was a small issue, but this can be said of so many of London’s city centre hotels. Breakfast was basic, but well presented, and ticked enough boxes to be satisfactory. In short I would stay here again due to the cleanliness and location of the hotel.

title: Great hotel for the price
text: I stayed for a single night whilst accompanying a family member to the Univercity College Hospital right opposite. I was able to check in early as I was desperate for a nap after travelling long hours. The room was newly refurbished, both room and bathroom were clean. Although the bathroom cubicle was small the power shower was strong and really hot, Unlike most hotels. Would happily stay again if i was In the area.

title: Lovely hotel very close to Euston Square Tube and Euston Station
text: The room was large with a very comfortable bed and a nice shower. The staff were friendly and we could leave our luggage, which was very helpful and saved the steep cost of leaving luggage at Euston, which allowed us to really enjoy our last day in the city without lugging our bags around. It is a very short walk from the station, just a few minutes, so is very convenient. There was a little noise as it is on the main road so you could hear traffic during the day and some sirens at night but it was not distracting at all for us.

title: The smallest room in all the land
text: i stayed here mid-week and only booked it as it was the 'cheapest central hotel' option i could find. for £160 i had a single room which was quite honestly the smallest room i've ever stayed in. It was well equipped in terms of a comfortable bed, TV, mirror etc but i'm not sure it was the cleanest ever, the carpets were a bit dubious and the room could have done with another lick of paint. The bathroom was essentially in a cupboard but it had everything i needed and this was definitely the cleanest part of the room. I wasn't really in the room for very long so my niggles weren't too much of a problem - but i'm not sure i'd rush to stay here again. It is in a very central location though, just 5 mins walks from Euston. Friends have since reassured me that there are better deals to be had in other hotels (some chain hotels) which are equally central. Lesson learened for next time.

title: A Nightmare
text: I have just returned from a 7 night stay at the Euston Square hotel and I can honestly say that I never slept during the nights I was there. The hotel is located right on the main road with sirens going off all night. To make it worse they are renovating and there were power saws going by 7 am every morning. The hotel is small and the rooms extremely tiny and you can hear every door banging throughout. On the up side the hotel staff was very friendly and the place was clean but I'd never stay there again.

title: Visit of London
text: Nice people, comfortable room, excellent breakfast, very good location. The hotel is not far from Euston station. It is located in the center of London, close to the British Library, the British Museum and UCL.

title: Good location, pokey room and no curtains
text: The location near UCL and Euston station was excellent and that is what lead us to choose it. The room was too small for the double bed. You could hardly get around it, although the bed was fine. There were ineffective Venetial blids on the windows and lights outside. Unless you…

title: Room buzzer alert!!!!!!!
text: . the hotel was great, however, the most bizarre thing that has ever happened occurred whilst staying here.... During the night when the hotel has locked the front doors and guests need to buzz to enter, for some reason, the buzzer was linked to my room on the second floor, meaning that every time someone pressed the door bell, an extremely loud buzzer went off in my room! This kept me awake from 3am - 6,55 am when the front door was unlocked. this was so annoying and meant the next day I was a wreck... The front desk had no idea how this could happen, so I would advise avoiding room 217 at all costs!!!!!

title: value for money
text: easy to get around,very clean,nice staff,room a bit small but breakfast is really good.

title: Ended up being disappointing
text: Location is brilliant and for the price I got the room I shouldnt be complaining. However the niggles were couldnt get any BBC TV channels (so bang went half of what you could get), access to plugs was difficult e.g. to use the kettle it had to be placed on the floor and generally you just wished someone paid more attention to what they were providing.

title: Clean room but poor breakfast and miniature room
text: A very disappointing hotel . The room was so small that when I opened the door it hit the bed, I am only 4 feet 2, and a size 10 so the fact that I could,only just fit in the shower is somewhat unusual! The breakfast was very poor, all carbohydrate , no fresh fruit , the "full English" was actually boiled eggs only. The staff were friendly but had very little English, this meant lots of mistakes, as they struggled to understand what customers were asking. I asked for a map and was told that they only had 2 and they had gone! I paid £180 for one night. The bed was very hard , pillows were so hard that it was impossible to sleep.

title: Ok place...no communication
text: If you are onto small rooms, you'll love this place. It's clean and neat. However, I checked in on Tuesday night and straight away there was the usual london screw up. I find it really hard to understand how service and communication seem to be totally void in this huge international city. But london is what it is and if you go there you know what you're in for. Bad service, arrogant people and a total disregard for any inconvenience caused to the customer. This hotel has all that and in spades.

title: Comfortable but for the traffic noise
text: Staff friendly & check in straightforward and the double room was clean & comfortable. Adjacent to a Costa. Location is brilliant but the downside is the 24/7 traffic noise even with windows etc all closed in our room fronting on to A501. Could be improved with better soundproofed glazing.

title: Love the place
text: I travel to London every three months and stay at Euston Square. I don't need a full service hotel with every amenity. I basically use the hotel as a place to sleep. The staff know me and treat me well and go out of their way. The hotel has been going through renovations, but have not really been an inconvenience to me. The rooms are small but clean and serve my purpose. I will continue to stay at Euston Square.

title: You get what you pay for.
text: I stayed here for four nights with my boyfriend at the time. The lift was tiny and we had a struggle to fit in with our bags. The room was equally as small, containing two single beds, a table, a dresser with a T.V., and a wardrobe. Our bathroom was fine, although the shower felt cramped, and was a bit leaky. At first, we couldn't find the tea/coffee making things, but soon located them in the cupboards of the dresser. We were slightly disappointed to find we didn't have a double bed, but we pushed the two singles together on our first night. By the third night, housekeeping was pushing them together for us which was nice. The walls are thin, and the noise level could be an issue, however we didn't find it too bad, and the central location more than made up for it! As we arrived at Euston Station we were delighted to find the hotel a few metres down the road, and we enjoyed some meals in the area. We only made it to breakfast on the last day, but it was enjoyable with tea, coffee, toast, juice, cereal, eggs, etc. All in all, don't stay here expecting luxury- it's budget accommodation at the end of the day.

title: Not good at all
text: This is a very, very, very bad hotel and extraordinarily overpriced. The room cost £87 per night and I'd have been disappointed paying £7. To summarise: - extremely noisy all night throughout hotel - guests not loud but hotel so cheaply constructed, every footstep can be heard - broken air conditioning unit in 2 rooms on 2 separate occasions, making a loud buzzing noise every 10 mins - breakfast - stale bread and hard cheese - tv not working in first room - tv fixed on wall facing away from bed with no chair so therefore no ability to watch tv

title: Does what it says on the tin....
text: We spent a very comfortable night at the Euston Square Hotel recently. Our twin room was spotlessly clean with good WIFI and very impressive shower room. Location is its greatest asset but friendly staff and attached Costa made it a good all round experience.

title: Great location
text: Great location - it took me 4 minutes to walk from London Euston, and that was including waiting at the pedestrian crossing. I would estimate it is a 10 min walk to St Pancreas and another 5 mins to Kings Cross. Euston Square Underground Station is literally round the corner. I only stayed one night. The room was clean, modern and surprisingly quiet despite being on a main road. Staff were friendly and welcoming. I preferred having the option of booking breakfast when I arrived or on the morning itself rather than booking it ahead. There is an option of a full English (£10) or a Continental (£7.50) depending upon your preferences.

title: First time stay but not the last.
text: With an air of trepidation I booked this hotel through HotelTonight at a reduced rate (useful tip there). Found the hotel and was surprised how it looked from the outside (it looked high quality) the check in was akin to Ibis/CitizenM. Speedy and a 50% voucher off food before heading to the room. Okay first of all the doors have been designed for Hobbits (other little people are available). The room is what I would class as functional clean and perfect for a single person or a very friendly couple.

title: Great City Hotel
text: I was a bit apprehensive on arrival at the hotel after reading reviews on this site but I really needn't have been. Location wise you really cannot get any better than this hotel. We arrived into Euston station and the hotel was literally 5 mins round the corner. Outside the hotel restaurant is Euston Sq station and a 2 min walk away is Warren St station - great if you plan on doing alot of sight seeing. Our check in was smooth and uncomplicated. The concierge was both friendly and polite and we were checked in within 5 mins. The lobby is clean, bright and very modern. A great indication to what the rest of the hotel is like. However the price of drinks at the bar is ridiculous.....avoid! Our room was a little on the small side but then again it did have 2 beds, a tv and wardrobe in it. It was very clean and bright. The bathroom again was perfectly adequate and clean, aside from the problem with the hot water on our last day. I think that this is a great hotel for people who are looking for comfort on a budget, a place situated centrally and really just a place to sleep and store your things while you sightsee.

title: great hotel
text: the hotel was comfortable ,satisfied all my expectations, the place was central, and clean.The breakfast it was very good ,i just found it the the hours for the breakfast were too short,untill 9.30.My opinion that is possible to extend it untill 10 am.Price and quality are matching.

title: Good value for money
text: Just came back from 6 nights in London. The hotel is located just above Euston Square Tube station, and there are 2 more tube stations within 2 minutes walk. Rooms are small but clean. Clean towels every day. Breakfast- basic continental. The hotel located on very busy road- heavy traffic 24 hours. Try to ask for high floor room and not on Euston road. Very easy to get anywhere in London, many restaurants and pubs nearby. Free WiFi in rooms.

title: Mr
text: Very comfortable decent sized room with nice modern ensuite. Clean and comfortable and very cool with the AC. Staff are very nice and friendly. Very convenient for Euston tube and train station. Would stay again(which I think will be when Wimbledon is on). Would recommend.

title: Perfect location, clean & well put together
text: This hotel is spot on if you are just staying a night or two in London and you don't need much if any time in your hotel room. It's clean, fresh, and the staff are pleasant and helpful. It's round the corner from the Tube station and a three minute walk from Euston station. Location couldn't be better. We booked through hotel tonight which doesn't allow you to choose room type, but when we asked for a twin room instead of the double they gave us, they couldn't have been more accommodating or helpful. The workers were all kind and pleasant. Breakfast was really good and an excellent price - one of the better continental breakfasts I've had with fresh breads , meats and cheeses, fruit and cereals, etc etc. No luxury stay, and the rooms are small, but absolutely solid and I would stay again.

title: Great hotel
text: I stayed for one night while I was in London visiting friends and it was lovely. Rooms were spacious and clean, nice big shower and extremely comfortable mattress. I’d recommend it. I didn’t book to have breakfast so I couldn’t comment on that but the coffee machine in the room was a nice touch.

title: Reasonable value for Central London
text: We stayed two nights just before Christmas. We got one of the renovated rooms (not all rooms are renovated). The room was small --- you must make full use of the closet if you're staying several days --- but I've seen smaller. Really liked the LCD TV and the free internet. Windows are double-glazed so road noise not an issue except in summer. Staff were helpful and friendly. Excellent for transport (use Warren Street tube for most travel).

title: Clean but small rooms
text: I stayed at this hotel for three nights in September 2015. Location is good staff is pleasant. Breakfast was extra 10 pounds for english 7 for continental. Room though was very small as well as bathroom. I was up at 3rd floor so noise from was not a problem. I won't stay again just because rooms are very small. If you are on a business trip you might want to sit down to do some work but there is no space for that.

title: Great Breakfast!!
text: Small boutique style hotel. Our room was on the front so quite noisy at night but apart from that - all good. Superb freshly cooked full English breakfast. Would stay again but ask for a quieter room.

title: For business trip perfectly fine
text: This hotel is very conveniently located if you have to visit UCL. It sit just on top of Euston Square station. The rooms are small but have everything needed if you stay no too long. I was pleasantly surprised that I had a wardrobe - that is not always the case of hotels in London. Compared to many other hotels in London the room was in very good condition and clearly had been renovated recently. I was a bit concerned about the traffic noise, but the windows isolate well if you also close the inner window. The breakfast was nothing special, but quite a nice choice for a continental breakfast. All in all I would recommend this place for short visits to London.

title: Great location. Middle quality. Good value for money.
text: Right next to several tube hubs, and a short walk to Kibgs Cross makes this hotel an excellent location. Quality is mid level, certainly better then the low end, not the quality of five star hotels. Fair value for money. If you don't spend much time in the hotel and want to run around London and only use the hotel as a base this is a very good choice.

title: Small, clean, good location
text: Plenty of upsides and good value for money. Clean, modern and fresh. Ask for a room at the back, as those at the front are almost on the Euston Road and very noisy. Free wifi works well, although requires constant re-registration. Don't rely on staff for directions or advice, as there's not a single Londoner amongst them, and their local knowledge is poor.

title: Small but nice
text: Recently refurbished rooms, actually still undergoing refurbishment! The rooms are tiny with no room for luggage or any storage but perfect for an overnight stay for business. Comfortable bed - double only. Excellent shower and clean nice bathroom. Very good location for Euston station - 5 min walk

title: Good location, average hotel
text: Stayed here for an overnight stay, very good to get to from Kings Cross station, just a couple of stops on the tube. The hotel did what we needed it to - provided a base for the visit. The bedroom was clean enough, but very small and the hotel gives a feeling of being in need of makeover and the overall experience just average.

title: OK for the Price
text: Checked into Euston Square Hotel however room was unacceptable due to size however staff were more than happy to assist and upgrade to a larger room. Travellers should be aware of London Hotel rooms being small so we were not too bothered. Room was clean and tidy however a little noisy but we were advised of this prior to accepting the new room. Excellent location and a short walk down Tottenham Court Road to Covent Garden and Central London. Staff were always helpful and friendly.

title: Excellent location but the tiniest rooms
text: This is a budget hotel which has a very nice location right on top of the tube station. Like all budget hotels the rooms are very small with hardly any space to move and open your luggage. The washroom is extremely tiny as well. The hotel has limited listed facilities. However, the room was clean and staff is smiling, helpful and attentive to customer requirements. Recommended if you need to be around Euston Square, on business, solo traveler and are on a budget.

title: Clean, tidy and great value for money!
text: Stayed here while in london for 2 nights. It was clean, tidy, and great value for money. Its right next to euston square and euston underground. Really nice indian restaurants next to the hotel too. Would definitely stay here again.

title: So glad I followed the trip advisor advice on this one!
text: I was planning a weekend away with my friends and wanted somewhere to stay that was friendly, good value and with good access to public transport. This hotel seemed to tick all the boxes and I wasn't disappointed... We checked in on friday night, we had driven over and were very pleased to discover we could park right outside the hotel for free for the duration of our two day stay! The girl on check in was helpful and efficient. We went up to our rooms, my friends had a double and I had a single. My room was compact but clean and had plenty of storage space and plug sockets. My only complaint would be that I had to plug the kettle in on the floor. The room could have probably benefitted from some bedside lamps too. The bathroom was nice and modern and the shower hot and powerful. When we got back wanting the buy a bottle of wine later on the staff were very helpful and were happy to let us sit on the nice cosy sofas in reception to drink it. Breakfast was a continental one with nice fresh fruit salad, ham cheese, pastries, yogurt, breads and a choice of cereals and fruit juices. You could have a full english cooked for you for an extra charge but we were more than happy with what we had. The bar was well stocked and not too expensive and we thought they had a great selection of very affordable, drinkable wines. The only issues I had during my stay was that my friend was coming to join us on the second day, I wanted to leave my key but the receptionists said not to worry, just to leave her name and they would give her a key to get into the room. Unfortunately the staff changed shift, the information was lost and they new staff wouldn't let her into the room. Luckily we weren't far away but it could have been a bit of a disaster if we were. The other issue I had was with getting the cleaning knock at 9am on our checkout date. It is a bit of a pet hate of mine, we are booked in until 11... We haven't checked out yet, please leave us to enjoy our sleep. The beds are lovely and comfy by the way. We all slept really well throughout our stay. The girl that cleans the rooms was very sweet, I wanted extra milk, tea and coffee and she very kindly fetched more for me. I highly recommend this hotel, the staff are lovely and friendly, they did their best to really look after us throughout our stay. The hotel is clean and modern, the rooms small but comfortable and great value for what we paid. They also have free wireless which was good too. We all enjoyed staying here and I would definately recommend this hotel if you are staying in London.

title: Super place in center London
text: A really nice hotel in the middle of London. Friendly and helpful people to help and answer questions. Really good breakfast and lovely coffee. The only thing missing was a bigger desk in the room as I needed to do some work. The room was super nice, good beds and with a really large shower. In addition water and coffee in the room for self service. I'll get back here!

title: Comfortable but lots of traffic noise
text: Comfortable room, reasonable cost for meals. Very heavy traffic noise. Convenient location

title: Perfectly adequate
text: If you are looking for a top class hotel in the centre of London, this isn't it. However, if you are seeking reasonably priced accommodation that is clean and safe and conveniently located, pick this hotel. My room was pretty small but it had a good sized, comfortable bed and a tiny but great shower - in fact it had everything I needed in a small space. The continental breakfast is nourishing and there is plenty to choose from. The staff were helpful and it really is a fine place to stay. A bit noisy.

title: Super hotel - trendy decor - highly recommend
text: Close to St Pancreas & Euston Square. Very clean tidy & comfortable. All the facilities are fairly modern and a reasonable sized room for London. Handily located to the Eurostar terminal. No fridge in room which would have been handy in the heat to keep water cold.

title: Great location. No hassle
text: Great modern hotel. Easy check in. Spotless room. Tea and coffee making facilities and bottled water. Fantastic location. Good WiFi. Friendly staff. Luggage storage before and after check in. So handy for Euston station.

title: Nothing to write home about
text: I had to stay overnight on business so booked into the Euston Square Hotel at the last minute and paid £125.00 for a small clean double room with en suite. The hotel was described as "boutique." A big exaggeration in my book. I arrived at about 20.00hrs and asked if they served food. (I wanted room service, but was told food was only available in the bar area). The only problem with the menu was that half of the choices listed were not served after 17.00hrs. I decided to eat out! The room was fine and the hotel is very well located, right next to tube station and only 20 mins walk to Oxford Street. I would booked it again as it does the job for me when I just need to rest my head on business but wouldn't want to book a romantic night away with the wife.

title: Location, Location, Location!!!
text: If you are looking to stay at a hotel which can get you easily to practically ALL the highlights of central London without burning a hole in your pocket, this is the one to stay at. The hotel is just around the corner from a pedestrian subway which will lead you comfortably to Euston Square Tube Station, which is across the road. If your want to take trains from the Warren St Station, you just need to walk about 3 - 5 minutes from the hotel. If you have heavy luggage and need to get to King's Cross, there is a bus stop right outside the hotel and you can take 3 different buses which will drop you right in front of the train station. No need to drag your heavy luggage up and down the tube stations! Yes, I must admit that our room is small - it has a double bed which is pushed against the wall (hence only 1 side to get down from the side of the bed), a writing table and a wardrobe, which take up almost all the space of the room. If you leave your luggage unpacked, you will have to move it every time you want to pull out the chair to sit on or open the wardrobe door. The shower cubicle is rather tight too but the water pressure and temperature is fine. Wifi is free and fast from our room on the first floor. The room has an air-conditioner and an adjustable radiator which worked very well to keep us warm and snug during the cold winter month. Yes, like some other guests have complained here in their reviews, the walls are thin and you will be unlucky if you have noisy guests staying next to you and inconsiderate ones who do not know how to close the doors quietly. But hey, we did not come to London for rest and relaxation. We were there for the adventure, sight-seeing and shopping!! Due to this reason, we can easily get used to the small room (which we only use to sleep after a very tiring day out and about!) and ignore a little noise in the early mornings. The buffet breakfast was simple and sufficient and our room is cleaned very well on a daily basis. We will not hesitate to recommend this hotel to visitors to London. The location is perfect and very convenient for those who travel with heavy luggage.

title: Tries really hard
text: Stayed here overnight and found the staff to be extremely friendly and helpful. check in was quick and easy. The room wasnt great, this place needs a big injection of cash to get it into the 21st century, It has the feel of a 1970s type hotel. However, the room was clean and the bed very comfortable. Close the blinds and shutters and there is no outside noise and there is the ability to control the temperature in the room. The shower left a lot to be desired and there was paper hanging off the wall. We needed to eat here after a work conference and we asked how late they would do food. We were told food finished at 10pm but we could ring and order if we were going to be a bit late. Despite the obvious neglect of the place we found the food to be really nice, fresh and tasty. We ordered dessert after 10pm, the chef said this was ok and it was brought to us. Unfortunately all of the beers and lagers had 'gone off' so we had to have a drink from the fridge (which cant have been on as nothing was cold!) I would say that this place is really tired and doesnt do justice to the staff who have to work in such a sub standard hotel. I would certainly not pay full price to stay here, but with a huge discount its absolutely fine for a one night stop off.

title: All-rounder
text: Great place and great service. It was right for what myself and my sister needed at the time of stay. Good central location making it an easy place to get from A to B. Adam at the frontdesk was especially helpful.

title: Already booked to stay there again
text: I only needed a single room, preferably with its own bathroom, to stay in while I was on a four day course in the Euston area. This hotel was clean and comfortable, the staff was friendly and the location was great. It's literally on top of two coffee shops and a tube station. It's a five minute walk from Euston Station in one direction and Tottenham Court Road in the other. I have to go back to London in August for exams and November for another part of my course and I have already booked to stay there again.

title: amazing!
text: Excellent experience from arrival... nicely appointed and tech-savvy rooms, friendly service and great location! Really happy that we found this hotel last minute. Just a few steps to Euston Station and minutes from Kings Cross.

title: An average hotel!
text: Euston Square Hotel is an average hotel.The hotel has very good rooms,although they were small but was maintained very well.The staff is friendly and helpful.But the breakfast was not so good.Even the hotel did not have much facilities.Even I found the tariff of the hotel to be a bit pricy.

title: Too minimalistic
text: Stayed on a hotwire reservation. Fairly good location - Euston Square Tube station next door, but a good walk from Oxford Street. Rooms not too bad for a budget hotel in London - clean and with duvets - no blankets, but very minimalistic. Safe in room was a bonus. Corridors very run down and gives impression of a youth hostel. Reception area modern but totally soulless. Would staybagain provided price was Ok - but paying more than 30 pounds p.p.n. would make we search elsewhere

title: Good location but downhill from there
text: Had two overnight stays during the last week, before and after a holiday in the Dordogne. The hotel is not good value for money: location is excellent for both Euston Station and St Pancras. Twin bedded rooms adequate, bathroom needed an urgent and more importantly a good clean. Television didnt work for more than 5 minutes at a time. When Receptionist was asked by me what the problem was,she informed me the Manager was dealing with it - it was the same the previous week. On the plus side - the food was good.'' June T

title: MY WORST HOTEL EXPERIENCE EVER
text: I paid a lot of money for this hotel and so expected a high standard of it. The room was tiny, only just space for the bed. There were no bedside lockers, no fridge (no room} and the bathroom was minute. The staff were really unhelpful and the walls were paper thin so we could hear everything that went on next door!! The busy Euston Rd is right outside and we were kept awake all night with sirens and drunken antics. I would certainly never go to this hotel again as it ruined our weekend.

title: Superb Central and Friendly
text: Travelled here for business and the place is central, good value and although my room looked a bit tired in places it had good facilities, was clean and excellent value for money. The cooked breakfast over the road in UHL also recommended!

title: Good experience
text: Clean and tidy place ,helpful staff ,the rooms (typically London) are small ,but place is great value for money ,and comfy beds .. I will use it in future ,as it is very handy ,and the rooms were clean ,fresh ,with a very comfy bed . Didn't use the restaurant as had early meeting ,but would recommend this place .

title: Awful treatment, terrible customer service
text: We were supposed to stay here on the first Friday of June. Everything was booked and paid for in March and on the morning before our stay at the Euston Square hotel my husband brought our suitcases to the hotel, and was told our booking was fine but we couldn't check-in until the afternoon. At 5pm that evening I went to the hotel to check-in and was then told we couldn't stay because the hotel was over-booked. Only when I protested that we had booked in March and that my husband had been there this morning did they inform me that our room was flooded and we had been booked into another hotel. They booked us into the Royal National hotel which is the dirtiest and noisiest hotel I have ever been to (and the Tripadvisor reviews confirm this)! We duly checked-out, and after an incredibly stressful evening of trying to find a hotel in London on a Friday night, we finally found a room in a nearby Holiday Inn. We made a complaint to the Euston Square Hotel 2 weeks ago, and have so far received no reply with an apology. They completely ruined our evening and tarnished our stay in London. While the hotel may be ok if everything runs smoothly, they clearly do not care to help when something goes wrong.

title: I would NOT stay in this hotel again!
text: Problem 1. Our room card key did not work the first five days of our six-day stay. On the last day someone who was competent listened to our complaint and solved the problem--a bit late, in my opinion. Problem 2. Breakfast was just okay--basic boring ham, musty-tasting rolls. Problem 3. The room was itsy-bitsy. Compliment 1. The hotel was extremely clean. Compliment 2. Location was good--close to St. Pancreas and Kings Cross train and tube stations, and to the Euston, Euston Square, and Warren Street tube stations.

title: Pretty Good Budget Hotel in Central London
text: Located smack in the center of town, right by Euston Sq station and, a 5 minute walk to the Warren St. Tube stop and bustling Tottenham Court Rd. further down the road, Euston Sq hotel is a good choice for accommodation in Central London without having to break the bank. The facility has a more intimate feel as it’s on the smaller side. Right off Reception is a no frills lounge area (with internet access) and adjoining restaurant and bar where guests can enjoy complimentary breakfast and other meals to order through the day. Rooms are decent enough--size-wise--by London’s standards and appear to have been recently renovated. They come with make-your-own coffee/tea service, flat screen TVs, safe and, extra bedding, etc. Bathrooms have showers and feature H2K toiletries (which I thought was a pretty good touch), and other basic necessities. Certainly recommend Euston Sq Hotel. Offers good value for money in Central London.

title: Nice but room very small
text: Good location for Euston station, friendly staff, clean/comfortable etc, nice shower. However, the 'double room' we had was tiny! Hardly any room to move, store belongings etc. Ok for single travellers for 1 night but not ideal for couples visiting London for weddings etc.

title: Cramped and Hot with outdated decor.
text: We booked this hotel as we were down in London for the weekend and wanted a hotel close to Euston Station. The location is good and within 800 yards of the station but I'm afraid after that there isn't much positive to say. Our hotel room was cramped and in need of good makeover, the shower although efficient had a damp smell and even opening the windows didn't help. The air conditioning had a setup where it would turn off after 1 hour which given that this weekend was very hot meant we didn't get any sleep as we were getting up to switch it back on during the night at regular intervals. It was also rather inefficient and noisy. Fortunately we only booked for one night and stayed at another hotel close by (part of a large budget chain) for the second night that cost less and was 100% better value with a large spacious room, clean and modern furnishings and fully working air conditioning. I cannot recommend the Euston Hotel and even though we expressed our dissatisfaction on checking out the staff were uninterested and stated that they had heard about the air conditioning comments before but obviously nothing has been done to rectify this!! Do yourself a favour and book elsewhere for less money.

title: Excellent spotless hotel ideal for Euston and Kings Cross Stations
text: Spotless hotel, room well furnished, bed very comfortable staff very welcoming. Housekeepers should be very proud of their work, as should the boss. Can not find any negative issues, only 200 metres to Euston and half a kilometre to St Pancras and Kings X

title: Really good location
text: I wasn't sure what this hotel would be like and was pleasantly surprised. It is in a really useful location and very easy to get around via the Northern line from Euston or Gower Street, buses or walking if you want a longish walk. My single room was very comfortable and had everything I needed. There are cafes in Euston station but I bought stuff from the Sainsbury's local and ate it in my room.

title: Good location, clean and nice rooms
text: The location is great. 10-15 minutes walk to Oxford St and 15-20 minutes walk to theatres. Lot of buses going too around this hotel and ofcourse, tube runs everywhere. Rooms are very nice and updated, but kind of small. A/C had an odd sound couple of times, but that didn't bother us. Internet connection was good, it's free and you get a access codes from reception. Breakfast was a small disappointment, there were absolutely no vegetables (like cucumber, tomatoes etc) and cheese ran out every morning. And the waitress was the slowest ever to put new cheese to the table. But still, one of the best hotels I've visited in London and I'm going there again. Thumbs up.

title: Just what I expect
text: this was my first time in london everything was amazing there. Arrived Hotel at 12pm but the checkin time was 2pm it didnt bother us at all coz the reception was very helpfull in storing our bagges and guiding us the direction towards london eye. wokeup next day to have breakfast in restaurant, it was continental breakfast with various choices of pastries and great selection of fruit yoghurts and several diferent kind on breadroll, fresh fruit salad and the list goes on. i would say it was very healthy breakfast and all staff performed well. my whole trip was just what i expect from everyone and everything. I will recommend this hotel to everyone and will definatley come back for more.

title: Would recommend, lovely hotel
text: I work for a charity and we have a corporate rate with this hotel. The rooms are always clean and tidy and there are never any problems whatsoever. I always use their lugguage room in the mornings, as I always arrive too early for check -in. They always provide a high level of service and nothing appears to be too much trouble. The only fault I can possibly find with the hotel, is on a few occasions I have had a room which has been a bit noisy with the traffic pasing by, but if I was staying more than one night I would probably ask them to move me. I would recommend this hotel to busines travellers as it is quite close to Euston Station and usually I drop my lugguage off before heading into London.

title: Not the room we booked
text: We were told at time of booking that the room was a little larger than most London Hotels, with a sofa on one side of room, however those rooms were sold out on arriving in for 4 days, bathroom that tiny you could honestly sit on toilet and vomit in sink at same time, shower was unreal, standing upright room only, open shower door to wash back or lower extremities, step down from shower dangerous, my husband fell badly as a result. Room a big disappointment.Otherwise very clean, nice continental breakfast, Very close to the Underground, bus network, and walking distance to St Pancreas Station.

title: Dreadful place - NEVER to be repeated
text: Useful location - that is the only positive. Noisy, dirty, tiny rooms and even smaller bathroom and outrageously expensive! No bar. I don't know about the breakfast room, I just wanted to get out of the place. Getting on the train from nearby Euston was like pure luxury!

title: Dingy and cramped
text: The hotel is located only yards from the tube station. That is the good bit. Beyond that it is hard to find anything good to say about my stay. The entrance is worn and shabby. The stairs is narrow and worn with marks on the walls. The room was very small and while the bed was ok the room was very shabby. The bathroom while small was clean. Oh and there is alot of street noise. For what I paid (£365 for two nights) there are many better options.

title: Good value but noisy
text: Central London is expensive so finding good value is tough. Invariably you end up in the 3 star converted grand old houses that vary in standard hugely and some are quite frankly grotty. Euston Square Hotel thankfully is not as bad as this. The room I had was a good size and the decor and en suite acceptable. Room was clean(ish). Some small stains on the duvet cover. Biggest issue was the noise. The room was facing the main road and the secondary glazing just wasn't enough to keep the noise out. So despite a comfortable bed didn't sleep very well. For the price can't really complain as it is half the price of a very run down travel lodge I stayed in nearby a while back.

title: My Turn to Set the Record Straight
text: I'll keep this short and sweet: 1) This hotel is LOUD! No excuse and no other way to put it...it is so LOUD. I've been living in london for years now and the hotel is located on a major/busy road that runs through central London. I did not sleep well at all. My room was 001, on the first floor. I could constantly hear people going to and from the lift all through the night. Our window was overlooking the street, where all the maintenance trucks and workers were parked outside. If you don't know this hotel is located DIRECTLY next to Euston Square tube station. If you aren't familiar with London, starting around mid-night (until 5ish AM) workers do maintenance/repairs on the tube. So luckily for me their trucks were parked next to my window. Even with the window closed, I could hear them speaking, yelling, and banging from their equipment. 2) The walls are paper thin. I could hear everything my Italian neighbors were saying, doing, and I could hear them coughing at night. 3) My room was for disable people and I am not disable. For some unknown reason they placed me in this room. The bathroom was designed for a person in a wheelchair, and it looked exactly like the bathroom in my grandfathers nursing home. There was no shower curtain and it had a special seat in the shower. 4) Hotel staff was nice and friendly. 5) Our A/C did not work. Conclusion: If you want location, yeah this hotel has got it. But there's about 5-10 other hotels in the King's Cross area. It's a plus the rates come with breakfast and free newspapers. Overall, I'm warning you the hotel is soooooo loud at night.

title: Nothing to shout about...
text: Stayed for a weekend trip to London. The first room they provided was little more than a box and to be fair after a complaint the staff who were very helpful moved us to a slightly bigger room.
