text: Good place if you come in to Paddington train station room smallish but most London hotels are.Breakfast was good. Shops nearby good place to base yourself. Clean rooms. Has a lift for suit cases which some older hotels do not. We arrived early and were able to leave our bags to go sightseeing. I would stay here again

title: Mr Haitham
text: Really very bad hotel .. Room very small if u r little bit fat u can't take around in the room and will be very difficult to enter the bathroom and close the door . AC is fixed over the bed with cold air and u can't stop the aircondition even if u take off the card key to stop all the electricity... It was a horrible day and I can't sleep all night .. And I was sorry that I didn't ve time to make a legal problem with them .. It must be a 1 star hotel max

title: Small quaint hotel
text: We were a party of four. The hotel was clean. The staff were a "bit stuffy" upon arrival. After speaking with the front desk manager the staff seemed more friendly. The bar is a great place for drinks - the bartenders were the friendliest people in the hotel. Biggest complaint -- the elevator was out for the entire visit. Had been out since March 8th and when we left on the 21 was still down. The stairwells were wide enough for one person and very steep. No attempt was made to advise us ahead of time, nor to compensate for this in any way. I would only stay again, by calling ahead and making sure the elevator was working.

title: Really good, which is unusual for London
text: I'm always fascinated when a hotel has 5 star reviews and 1 star reviews - who's right? Well in this case I was really pleasantly surprised. Admittedly I did have a suite (they upgraded me without me asking - THAT never happens!) so I was down the stairs, in what I guess is the new bit. Really nice and clean and smart. £139 which includes English breakfast. Check out the photos - good attention to detail, great big TV, free wifi, nice area with lots of restaurants etc just outside - what's not to like?

title: Gem of a hotel
text: Just returned from a 2 night stay for London fashion week.tube station just around the corner.fast check in, very friendly staff,rooms spotless also bedding emaculate. Rooms cleaned each day with fresh towels.not the biggest of bathrooms ...but how many do you want in a bathroom at same time,plenty of mirrors in room.had the continenta breakfast first morning it was excellent with a vast variety and choices.went for full English second morning and could not fault it very tasty, staff on hand for teas, coffees,top ups all with friendly smiles and attitudes. The hotel was spotless.if in paddington again would not hesitate to book here again.great pub at the end of the road ,fountains abbey.

title: Couldn't fault it for a one night stay.
text: Hotel is located, approx. 5-10 min walk from the tube station & is located ideally in Paddington. We were here for one night only as we had tickets for day 1 of the final test at Lords v the Windies. Check in was quick & efficient, staff were very polite & welcoming, they also upgraded us from an executive room to a suite of some description. Suite was a good size, with a large bed, sofa & fridge in the room. Bath had a TV at the end if you can't miss 5 minutes of the television. Didn't use the bar, nor the restaurant, although we were given a coupon for a 3 course meal in the restaurant for £17.95, we had a dinner reservation elsewhere.# Room & communal areas were all clean & well kept, genuinely can't fault this hotel nor the staff & would stay here again in a heartbeat...

title: Great staff
text: Stayed here one night, it was a lovely hotel. The first thing that strikes you is how incredibly friendly the staff are. They do everything with a smile. The food is so tasty and very reasonable priced. And then me and my sister sat in their bar at happy hour and had the best cocktails ever! Singapore sling, pina colada, White Russian and a blue Hawaii. By that time we was very merry so up to our room we went. If I had to say one teeny negative is that the bathroom is a bit snug, But I'm quite shapely so perhaps it would be snug for anyone else.

title: Amazing hotel, excellent staff, perfect location, shame we were sleeping in a cupboard.
text: We arrived early and our room was not ready yet, the staff dealt with us perfectly, friendly and helpful. The bar was nice and the breakfast was pretty good too. We went for the second cheapest double room, 'executive' they called it. For the money paid the location and quality of the hotel is exceptional. The room size would have been funny if it wasn't me who had to sleep there. There wasn't even enough space in the room to open our suitcase without putting it on the bed. I understand that central London

title: very good stay
text: Sixth visit every thing was good .from reception to the restaurant very good service. The quality standard is high Some rooms are small but are clean.very good location for getting to places.will visit again

title: Rude receptionist
text: It was a good and amazing hotel for few nights all went good from the beginning until the last moment when we were checking out they were not so flexible like the check in receptionists. They were arguing a lot and annoying ,rude specially the lady I'll get her name and I'll contact the manager regarding disrespecting guests on the new year 1 January huh what an amazing check out.because they didn't give me a bit time to prepare myself and luggage and make sure that all my belongings are with me , that was not the issue the thing is they been DISRESPECTFUL I wouldn't even mind to pay more even though at the check in they were so so flexible big heart for them ,that shows how is that hospitality has to be lead by professional staff. And just to be honest all other things was really really amazing the bartender from Brazil and the concierge , housekeeping, late night receptionist 100% keep it up all of you and thanks for your hospitality.

title: Amazng expeeience
text: The Norfolk towers hotel is very conveniently located and is a 5 minutes walk from Paddington Station.. We took the Heathrow express from the airport and reached within half an hour. The nearest bus stop is 1 minute away! Lots of convenience stores are located close by. As far as the hotel went, it was comfortable and clean. The hotel staff was very polite and helpful. We stayed here for 8 nights and thoroughly enjoyed our stay as the room was well lit, spacious and comfortable with all the amenities. The continental breakfast was sumptuous even though the items served were the same. On the whole it was very good and I would recommend it if you are looking for a medium priced hotel with lot of plus points!

title: Wonderful service
text: I stayed at this hotel for four nights, and the experience was really good. The receptionists were so polite and helpful whenever I was in need of help. The cleaning ladies did an amazing job every day and the breakfast staff made breakfast an loving experience. Will definitely book here again when I'm in London again!

title: Location Location Hostel
text: This hotel has a brilliant location the staff are very friendly and helpful but the hotel is tired, dated and depressing. I expected more for the price but you are clearly paying for location. I did not enjoy the breakfast either and was desperate not to spend any more time than I needed to In this hotel.

title: You get what you pay for
text: Overall the rose court is a cheap hotel with a good location. It is a bed for the night if you are out in the city or visiting to see the sights, etc The bed was clean and comfortable but the bathroom was lacking. All of the facilities were there but we're just a little 'faded'. The room was very small but it did the job as we were rarely in it.

title: Creepy
text: This is the worst hotel on the planet. I wouldn't stay here if it was free. I came with 8 of my best friends and we all thought it was a nightmare. We had 4 couples so we had the luxury ( LOL) of visiting all the floors. The basement was old and molded, that's why the extra heater was provided and it wad a 100 degrees upon arrival, to try and dry it out. My friends on the second floor brought in candy and woke up to mice eating in the middle of the night, which makes you wonder about the complimentary breakfast. My other buddy, they barged in on when he was taking a shower, and ask him to keep the water in the tub because it was leaking down below, which was a impossible task (which he did) they realized it was a leaking pipe. We called our travel agent and requested a new hotel after 2 days and ate the difference for the remainder of our 10 day stay. The only place this might be a descent stay is for a guy who's been in prison or some hobo of the street.

title: A good hotel to stay away from
text: Rude receptionist, poorly kept rooms, a lift that can only accommodate one person, lousy breakfast. The only good aspect is it is centrally located with easy access to Oxford street. Never stay here!!

title: Avoid
text: Although the welcoming staff were very polite and friendly- this was the only redeeming factor of our stay. The room was directly next to the kitchen and I was kept awake until 1am in the morning by the staff shouting and even hoovering in the room above. This then began again at 6am. 5 hours sleep before a meeting is not something I was planning on. In addition, the bed sheets had staining, and the overthrow has melted chocolate stuck to it. The hairdryer didn't work in it's allocated socket, wired up through the desk. I wouldn't feel comfortable recommending this hotel to anyone- especially at the price we paid for our stay.

title: The hotel where I am going to stay again and again!
text: I would like to thank from whole my heart the management of this lovely hotel for being so nice, so attentive and so kind to me every time when I just decided to book my stay in London. A month ago I again stayed in "Rose Court Hotel". It was my sixth stay there. I had my room that I liked from the first time of my stay. Into room I had TV, big bathroom with a bath and comfortable bed. Also there was the electric kettle, cups and as much tea, coffee and sugar as I wanted. What else do I need to relax after a busy day? I could use Wi-Fi in my room. But the security system of my tablet didn't want me to. I don't know why. Even without using Wi-Fi I felt good and comfortable in my room. The staff of the hotel from the reception to the restaurant was nice! I would like to thank every one who is working in my lovely hotel for good hospitality! Next time for sure I am going to stay in "Rose Court Hote"!

title: Theatre trip
text: We stayed at Rose Court for a theatre break. Its location is perfect right next to Marble Arch on Oxford street. There is an Ncp car park virtually next door but remember to pre book your space here on line. After reading the reviews we weren't expecting a lot but it was really good value for money. We were met on reception with a polite welcome and they were very happy to store our luggage as we were early and give us directions to the theatre. Our room had 3 single beds and plenty of room for one night. The bathroom was clean and everything worked. The breakfast was continental with option of eggs beans and toast included in the price. Yes the room could have done with a lick of paint but it was clean and comfortable. If you want a high class hotel book somewhere more expensive but for a budget break this is ideal.

title: Cheap but fine
text: For the price you mustn't grumble. The staff were super friendly and helpful which made the stay fine. Ok the rooms are a bit shabby and could do with a lick of paint for the price and location it's fine. Breakfast was basic and we did not choose the fried option as there's plenlty of good places to eat close by. For the price - it's great

title: Good value for money - great location
text: Spent 5 nights here on a trip with friends. Keep in mind that this is a budget 2-star hotel and adjust your expectations to this, and you will be satisfied. I loved it. It´s clean, rooms are cleaned every day and staff is friendly. The location is almost unbeatable, close to Marble Arch tube station, buses that go practically everywhere and all kind of shopping (Primark is really close). Beds were comfortable, two pillows each, small and large towels. A bit on the cold side, espescially as I am not used to just blankets in bed. Bring sleepwear if you get cold easily. We turned up the heat, and let the curtains down all day to keep the cold from getting in. A bit windy from the windows! Also the noise from the streets is quite loud from early morning. Breakfast is just ok, as can be expected really. Patisserie Valerie just down the street had great sandwiches by the way.. and coffee

title: Minutes from Hyde Park
text: I would only stay here if I needed to be in the area. Our group found the rooms to be quite small for the price. The staff was very helpful but this facility needs some serious renovation. There are much better hotels within minutes of this place.

title: You get what you pay for
text: When in London I want a room close to everything, it doesn't have to be fancy, but it has to be clean, Rose Court is clean, the rooms are small the hotel old, the lift is a experience, the staff are pleasant. Breakfast is also nothing fancy but it starts the day. This hotel is cheap, if you want grand pay more, go elsewhere. For me the convenience of being close by to so many good tourist spots out ways any thing else. My last three visits to London I have stayed at Rose Court, I would certainly book I again .

title: Perfectly situated
text: We booked a family room, and ended up in the basement! If we had been anywhere else in UK, we would have paid about 30 pounds for the room, not the classiest place, the beds were comfy though, and that's the main thing. The Hotel is in a perfect spot just near Marble Arch, not far to walk through the parks to Buckingham Palace etc The staff were helpful, the rooms could do with some $$$$ being spent on them.

title: Okay hotel for the price
text: I found the hotel pleasant enough, the staff worked very hard on a low budget. Peaceful location just off Marble Arch is priceless. I relished my quiet room, it was clean, the bed was comfy, the bathroom was all fine and the shower had a good water preasure. Breakfast was on a very low budget, but I didn't expect better for the price I paid.

title: Disgusting!
text: Rose court had is excellently placed for the local amenities. It is a old property that no one can either be bothered to, or have the money to bring into the 21st century. It would be ideal for blind people to visit as they won't be able to see how disgusting this place really is. Definatly not worth the money I paid to stay here. It's the kind of place you would bring your co- worker to for a cheeky bonk on Monday lunch time behind your partners back. I'll be making sure to wipe my feet on the way out as I'm sure the street is cleaner than the carpets. There was urine on the toilet seat, dirt in the bath, hair and a used nappy in the bin, dirt and damp patches in places, completely different to the pictures advertised. Unsuitable for children and not pushchair friendly at all! Our door didn't even lock properly, the main light didn't even work and the walls are scuffed and dirty. Do yourself a favour, save the £83 and £40 petrol and stay at home, at least you won't catch anything there.

title: my second business trip
text: this was my second stay in Rose Court Hotel, I guess I will always choose this amazing hotel whenever I visit London. It's really best value for money. It's central location serves you best in reaching all places. Marble Arche underground station is round the corner, 3 minutes walk. Same for buses too. The hotel staff is very friendly, they are there for you 24/7. The hotel is very clean and the rooms are spacious compared to other hotels which I used in London, even those which were more expensive. The wifi is free & is excellent in all hotel & all rooms too. Great breakfast with welcoming smiling staff to serve it. I recommended it for my Boss & his family and his wife actually thanked me for it. I will always recommend it to all my friends. Special thanks to Jale, the manager, and all the staff, I wish I knew all their names to thank each and everyone.

title: Worst place to stay in all of London
text: This hotel was booked for us through our travel agent. When we arrived the desk clerk was sleeping on the sofa in the lobby. The elevator up to our room only held one person and a suitcase. No AC, one window opens to the noisy street. Bathroom was from the dark ages. We were booked for 4 nights. After one night we left and went to another hotel. Would not recommend this place to my dog.

title: A trip back in time
text: I wanted somewhere cheap to stay in walking distance from my meetings. I stayed one night and it fitted the bill. I was not there more than eight hours. The decor is something out of the seventies. It was well priced against anything else available and yes, under the same circumstances, i would go back. I did not stay for breakfast, but the breakfast area was very busy when I left at around 8am.

title: Stay well away from this hotel
text: I was given a room on the fourth floor of this hotel. It was only accessible by taking a small elevator up to the third floor and then the steps to the next floor or by taking the steps all the way. The room was tiny and had a musty smell. The only way I could get the free wireless internet was to stand out in the stairwell with my laptop or go down to the lobby. It is a very old hotel and does not in my opinion warrant the price they charge for a room. I was booked in to this hotel for three nights and after seeing my room I checked out and vowed never to return. It is far from value for money. The local tour office booked the hotel for me and I did not read the bad reviews until after it was booked. I would certainly have stayed away if I had read them before hand. The only good thing about this hotel is its location.

title: rose court hotel for city trip
text: This is the 2nd time ive been back its got a great position only 2min walk away from oxford street its really the best spot. OK its not the most fancy of hotels but its clean and thre staff are friendly free wifi. I went bymyself so i had a single room it was fine had everything i needed in it. Will be definately booking here again.

title: very nice place to stay
text: This hotel was good for a three night stay. Staf were helpful and friendly. The hotel is minutes from Marble Arch tube station on Oxford St and it makes easy to get around for shopping and sightseein plus custo is reasonable. I willl recommend this to my friends and family.

title: Terrible experience
text: The condition of the rooms is terrible, especially the showers Some of the staff are really bizarre Wi-Fi does not work properly even though it's one of the things the hotel is committed to provide according to the information on its Website Great location but it's not worth it at all I will not come back there in a million years

title: Jackpot
text: A great hotel for holiday makers and business trips. Right in the centre of London, 2 minutes away from oxford street and Marble Arch Station. Reception was 24 hours available, all staff were friendly and helpful. Lift available. Room included a private bathroom with all necessities. Towels were changed everyday. Room was clean and spacious enough for our luggage. Breakfast includes toast and eggs and beans, croissants coffee tea, and juice which are all included in the price of the booking. To round up, the greatest asset to this hotel is its location, perfect for the bnb personnel who will be visiting all the great sights of London or will be out during the day. Definitely my first choice if i return.

title: Great location, friendly reception staff and amazing price
text: Booked online for this hotel and got a right bargain. Upon arrival I was greeted by a cheerful receptionist who checked me in promptly and showed me to my room. The room itself was well presented, if a little dated (but in a way this just added to the charm of the place) and very clean and tidy. It also had the best water pressure I've ever had from a shower. So lets face it - we all know it's not the ritz but for its fantastic location it's really quite a good hotel.

title: Homely, safe and familiar at start, central location, Economic with worth services
text: I was new to UK and not knowing any thing here. By chance i took this place first time when i came in july and stayed for three days. I felt quite familiar and homely from day one. It's in central London and most of things are in easy approach from here. The nearest tube station is at walking distance and so also nearby markets,restaurents etc. Its quite economic priced with worth hotel services. The staff and Managers are worth special mention who always are polite and helpful. The breakfast was free and the rooms though not big are comfortable and cozy. There was 24/7 free Internet inside room(WIFI). If you are planning comfort and economy together, then I suppose this could be the best choice. I liked it so much that NEXT TIME I CAME AND STAYED WITH MY WIFE HERE IN SEP., 2009. It was again a nice experience.

title: The worst hotel I have stayed at
text: The only positive thing is the excellent location in Central London. The room is overheated and you cannot moderate the heating. Room 103 is equipped with a window door that opens on a shared balcony. The window does not lock properly so it is the first time I feel unsafe in a hotel. You can ear everything from the street as well. Hopefully I always have some earplugs. As for the bathroom, there is NO space at all for your toilets amenities. And I didn’t mention the 40 year old decoration and carpet ... I would not even put my dog in this hotel Breakfast is very average, not even an English breakfast. The staff is very corteous. Keep in mind breakfast starts at 8am so not a place for early birds

title: Special present
text: Went to London for a birthday celebration. Arrived back at the hotel very late after meal and show, and went straight to bed. In the morning my wife found the tea and coffee in the bedside table, together with a used condom. What else is there to say.

title: Past its sell by date
text: We were given room 300 which was disgusting with rotten window frames (which couldn’t be secured)and dirt due to ineffective cleaning. We were moved to room 101 where the window frames were also rotten and dust hanging on the walls. The windows were single glazed with bad sealing so the room was noisy. On the landing, there were dirty marks above the heater from dust being convected and not cleaned.

title: Rose Court
text: We stayed last week for four days, We found the hotel to be in a great location, hotel was clean and satisfied all our needs. Some of the furniture was a little tired but overall a good experience. Would definately go back.

title: 2 star gem!
text: The hotel is located in central location, minutes away from Oxford st, Marble Arch and the beautiful Hyde Park. The staff at the hotel are very friendly and extremely helpful. The reception is available 24/7 and there is always someone there to answer to your questions. The rooms are reasonable, quite small but the beds are clean and comfortable. Would definitely stay here again!

title: Awful!
text: I was booked in for a night on a business trip. If it hadn't been late on arrival I would have turned and left right then. The hotel is tired and dated, with marks and dents an the Walls. My room was furnished with a twin bed , complete with a blanket with holes in. Breakfast was very woeful and consisted of the option of two cereals and toast, branded up as a continental breakfast. All in all i cant believe they charge what thye do. Honestly don't bother, there are better places in the area for the same or less.

title: Terrible!
text: This is without doubt the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. It may have been owned by the Churchill family in the past but I doubt it has been redecorated since they left! The bathroom smelt of damp and the window in the bedroom wouldn't shut. Having read the reviews, sadly not until after it was too late to cancel, I decided to give breakfast a miss. Take my advice, book somewhere else, anywhere else...

title: Worst ever
text: I visited this hotel for two nights in a weekend stay, my friend had already booked it, did tell me the reviews were mixed but you take a chance sometimes, we certainly did. We were too early in arriving for check in so left our bags and called back later in the day, I was shown my room up a dirty stairway that had carpet on it that was out of the ark , room was just as bad, tiny, more like s cupboard with a window looking out the back to other buildings that were similar. Very unattractive. Small bathroom with a shower tray which was The tiniest I've ever seen you kept hitting yourself off the sides when using it, a wardrobe and set of drawers that had seen better days and smelled fusty and robe was damp, awful looking. We had been given the continental breakfast option but immediately decided not to eat anything in this place. The location of hotel is excellent, close to Hyde park, Oxford street and tube station, but the hotel is ancient and badly needing upgrade, it looked more like a DSS establishment, definitely would not return here if you paid me . Worst I've ever encountered.

title: Shocking
text: Went to London to see bat out of hell. Needed a cheap and cheerful hotel just to rest our heads for the night. How wrong were we. Outside looked nice and i felt i made a good choice for £144. But i couldnt be more wrong. Got to reception lady just looked up give us our key told us second floor but there was a lift (broken of course!). So stairs it was...narrow and dated really just needed a lick of paint and for the £144 we gave alone could have done the trick and made it more pleasant. Got to our room thought the door was already open...turns out the doors were not even on properly and locks were old. Got into our room, boiling. Window hatch broken so it kept shutting. They put tea and coffee in the draw and left the sugar in a tub not even wrapped so dust etc would settle into it. Fan fitted to the roof looked like it was going to fly off the ceiling and massive crack in the ceiling too. Bed looked okay room was dirty and poor, wardrobe smelt of damp and musky, curtains really outdated and wouldnt shut, small door half the size of a normal door to get into the bathroom. Went in, cramped so badly. Toilet paper like sandpaper and the bin hadnt even been emptied from previous stayers. Round the bath was going mouldy and the shower kept leaking everywhere. Only good thing bout the bathroom was that it had dove hand soap. Back to the bedroom, the floor was covered in blonde hair that kept finding its way over all my stuff (such as my bag etc on the floor). Again only good thing is that it had a brand new TV in there that we did not watch. Towels were okay, didnt even stop to have breakfast and was out the room by 8 the next morning. I asked for thw wifi and the map to london which was supposed to be included, but again nothing received. I didnt want a 5* hotel for the money i was willing to pay but i wouldnt even pay 44p to stop in there again let alone £144. They are in dyre need of ringing the hotel inspector in to redecorate the whole place as it has potential to look beautiful (as not far from tubestation and attractions) if i didnt laugh about the stay there then i would of cried. Staff were not helpful or friendly and when asked a question just blatantly got ignored. Will NOT be returning.

title: Not great, but clean and comfortable
text: Cheap and cheerful, rooms are tired but clean and comfy, tv, tea and coffee, hot water and extra pillows and blankets all provided. But a good location, very helpful and friendly staff, and you can leave luggage there too. The breakfast is pretty standard, but the pastries were dry, starts at 8am, and you have to pay extra for cooked, but there is a great patisserie just up the road, which is recommended. Beware if you have a room facing the street- no double glazing means that it is noisy, especially late at night when the bicycle taxis go round and round with their music blaring!Good for a few nights for sightseeing.

title: The worst hotel I've ever booked
text: I've booked this hotel for 3 nights, during this time I couldn't take a shower because the bath is broken, my room was so dark because the main light didn't even has a light bulb, there are some kind of suspicious hairs on the bed sheet【Thank god I've brought my own】. Plus, the entire room was cold as an ice. I ask the reception to fix those problems as soon as I could, but HE REFUSED to fix them【yes, even the light bulb】after I said I will be here for 2 other days!. ....After all, at least I've got the light fixed in the before my second night, but it didn't work again the third night. I don't even bother to fix it. I'm so tired in this hotel _(:з)∠)_

title: Avoid.
text: Plenty of better hotels in the area. The hotel is old and mostly dirty, but at least the bed sheets are clean. The radiator was always on even when switch turned to min, the room was boiling and the window was broken so couldn't be opened. When asked if could be turned off the person at the front desk said there was nothing that could be done. Doors were not secure. Although shower was hot and towels provided were clean. Good location near oxford street. But would not stay again.

title: Avoid
text: This hotel enjoys great location. Yet, it needs lots of improvement and renovation. Everything is exhausted. The elevator, the furniture, the bathroom. The intercontinental breakfast is the worse i have ever seen. Only the heater was working very well. Never again

title: Smalll Quaint London Hotel
text: We stayed at the Rose Court Hotel while sight seeing in London. 4 blocks from the Marble Arch Tube station. Several restaurants are near by. Just blocks from Oxyford Street shopping. Room was very small but adequate. Bed was comfortable. Bathroom was tiny, but did have a tub/shower. It was difficult to regulate the temperature. The temperature would go from warm to hot very quickly. Black mold in the sealant around the tub needed some attention. Lift was small holding only two people. Wifi was slow, only allowing access to Facebook. Breakfast included cereal, croissants, rolls, OJ, milk, tea, coffee and made to order scrambled eggs with toast and beans. All in all a good value for the money, since we were only sleeping.

title: Great Location
text: Great location, close to Marble Arch. Very clean rooms and great value for money (for new years eve period). The breakfast was very good for a continental level. Helpful staff! The only negative thing i could think about was that the hotel was listed as free cancellation and pay at venue but a charge was taken from bank account from the moment of booking confirmation.

title: Don't bother
text: Don't bother with this hotel, although the staff are pleasant enough, I can't say the same for the rooms or food. We were given a basement 'family room' One double bed shoved against the window , a single popped in the corner, a wardrobe that had seen better days and a small table with a kettle on all squashed into a room smaller than some student accommodation I've seen The radiator was on full blast so I opened the window to let some fresh air in. Bathroom door stuck and my son got stuck in the bathroom ( needless to say we didn't shut the door again), sink didn't drain but when it did it leaked over the floor so had to brush teeth using the bath tap instead! Curtains had obviously been put up when walls were still wet with paint as they were covered in emulsion but that must've been a good few years ago as room definitely needed a spruce up! Beds were very hard and only given 1 pillow per person but found a lone one in the wardrobe Being in the basement we could hear all the goings on regarding water (toilets being used and flushed and all sorts of drainage) No bedside table or lamps Nice TV though ! Breakfast isn't totally included as they suggest Continental is included but you have to pay fir a fry up Only supplied cornflakes or branflakes for cereals but cornflakes ran out and never filled up Ran out of plastic cups for juice and again never replenished All in all I would not want to pay £149 for that night again ,it's definitely not worth it. You have been warned

title: Solid value
text: I've stayed here twice. The staff is friendly and quite multilingual, 24 hr. desk. The location is excellent - less than five minute walk from Marble Arch and airbus to Heathrow, neighborhood good. Clean. I believe all rooms are en suite (= bathrooms in your guest room for my fellow Americans.)

title: Big dissapointment
text: Terrible experience . Old and dirty , no cupboard doors, torn and dirty curtains. My window could not close. Dirty carpets. Internal telephone lines don't work. Can only eat breakfast from 8 in the morning , does not work if you are in London work or any conference. No fridge facilities. When you open your bathroom taps you compete with warm water with the apartment next to you, if showering at the same time. Will not recommend this hotel, many more hotels in this area for same price, that will provide you with much better services.

title: Worst hotel I have stayed in but serves a purpose
text: The vast majority of people using this hotel are going to the USA embassy for visa applications. As many people have stated the hotel is in a great location but is in need of a total revamp. But the owners probably dont care as it " serves a purpose " for clientele wanting somewhere close to the US embassy. The rooms are clean and ours didnt smell, but it was well pass its sell by date and worn out but The Wifi worked just fine and there was a modern TV on the wall. But the whole place is utterly tired and I had the most uncomfortables night sleep ever in a hotel on a very lumpy matress. I cant have any complaints about the breakfast, its just the overall appearence of the place, the sort of hotel used by councils to accomodate homeless familes. There are many other budget ( remember this is Mayfair though ) hotels in the area that are worth checking out by using google maps. The Rose Court was £144 for one night for a twin so not cheap cheap but cheap for the area.

title: A surprise - Rose Court Hotel
text: Arranged by a travel agent, an expensive way to go, with the price I paid, I was expecting a four star hotel. It turned out to be 2 star. Some rooms were small and others were not. It pays to specify what you require at the time of booking otherwise you may end up with something not to your liking. Direct online booking is better and less expensive. The location is great and so is the hotel. It is maintained at a similar level to many 5 star hotels, and the breakfast is very good with efficient service. Reception staff are very good.

title: smack in the heart of London!
text: This is my second visit to the hotel, which is for me in the best location possible in London, a minute walk to marble arch and oxford street, yet tucked away in nice and quiet great cumberland place, hard to beat! Ok it doesn't have the high end decor, but the beds are great and the rooms very clean, and so are the bathrooms, everything works well. Great size rooms for my family.The staff are always really kind and go out of their way to make you feel as if at home. And they have also upgraded their breakfast which now offers eggs and beans as well.

title: Clean and friendly
text: The location is great. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The rooms are ok and clean. I think it is a nice place to stay if you want to be in the center of the city and don't want to pay much.

title: Cheap Yes Great No
text: We were looking for a cheap hotel in a good location in London, not something easy to find. Next time I will pay more and stay somewhere Nicer. Don't get me wrong the location was great, just off Oxford St near Marble Arch, the staff were friendly. The room however was on the top floor up some very creaky stairs, you can hear what time people go to bed! The room was clean but very small. wallpaper was starting to come away from the wall and the curtains could have benefited from a wash. The breakfast was toast and cereal, hot breakfast extra - fair enough for the price paid, but please just put the nets at the dining room window through the washing machine. This could be such a quaint homely hotel should it have some money spent on bringing it up to date, but for one night was ok.

title: Great value for money
text: If you don't want luxury hotel, but value more location, this hotel is great option for you. Old, but still in quite good condition this hotel is situated just few steps away from Marbel Arch. Staff was very welcoming and helpfull. Familyroom was quite big and bathroom was clean. Onlything that bothered was that air condition was only in one bedroom, so we had to sleep windows open and the hotel is situated on a quite busy street, so time to time the traffic bothered at nights. Breakfast was quite good. I didn't expect that much after reading comments about it, but I was suprised: coffee, tea, croissants, toast, scrambled eggs, cerial, different marmelades and orange juice.

title: hurry up breakfast
text: Date 28 June 2007 Just returned from 3 nights at this hotel. As a 2 star hotel, the location was great:-10 mins walk from tube (Central Line) and buses. Room, as expected form other reviews, was small and bathroom tiny . Also dark . Glad it wasn't hot weather as might be stifling. Had requested a larger room but this was hardly that!!! Main complaint was about breakfast. Scheduled for 7-9am, went down at 8.50 to find only allowed 1 cup of coffee , toast that had barely winked at the toaster and to be told to 'please eat quickly' as the servers were finishing at 9 ! When I queried this, i was informed that the servers ' were only paid until 9 and had other work to do.' Needless to say, did not bother the other mornings. If you want a cheap convenient hotel, this is OK but certainly no frills and not particularly hospitable staff

title: Everything up to my expectation.
text: We were in this hotel for 6 nights from 21st Dec and checked out on 27 Dec 2012. I do admit that this hotel is not the best among 3 star hotel in london but the price that we paid is very reasonable as the location is great and very suitable for those who want to go for shopping along Oxford Street and Regent Street. We stayed in quad room and definately will stay here again because to us location is the most important thing to consider when we choose accomodation in London. Maybe the management of this hotel should do some upgrading as the furnitures are a little bit outdated and repaint certain walls along the corridors. But overall we are satisfied.

title: Would NOT stay here ever again!
text: So many cons to this hotel--No air conditioning, the room was dirty, the carpet made my feet dirty, had a day with no hot water, the bathroom was tiny, phone did not work, internet was weak and intermittent, the breakfast is some cereal or croissants with jam or butter, or you can ask for scrambled eggs--if you are late don't bother trying to get a table-not worth the wait. at night there are people driving little rickshaws/three wheel bikes that haul passengers and they blast music. the street is noisy and you have to keep your window open in the summer or it is too hot. The absolute most shameful thing that happened was that some staff (I assume cleaning) went through our luggage in our room and stole over $100 dollars. It was hidden so we know someone went through our luggage. There were very few pros for this hotel--had a ceiling fan, the linens and towels looked like they had been washed and were changed every day, there is an electric kettle under the nightstand with some instant coffee and tea bags and the staff at the front desk seemed pleasant enough If you choose to stay here--buyer beware and please do not leave anything in the room that you value.

title: great stay
text: Myself and five freinds recently stayed in the Rose Court during a recent trip to London (feb 28 - march 3 2007). I can honestley say that the hotel was far better thn any of us expected it to be. The rooms were clean and comfortable and the staff couldn't have done any more to be helpful towards us. The hotel is situated very close to marble arch tube station and from there it is a short journey to anywhere in the city, alternativley it's great location allows you to walk almost anywhere you might want to visit.

title: Just wow.
text: If you hate cleanliness, touchable surfaces around the bathroom and the room, if you're not that much into warm water, or decent sized rooms, book now! Perfect for people who love sticky feel on their fingertips and appreciate a good ol' moldy bathtub! Absolutely superb city views available through torn, dusty, and, once upon a time white, curtains! Your foot will never slip on those well-gripping 1970s carpets -- in fact your shoes might come off of their own! And at £ 126 a night, it's a steal: you'll also get a definite feel of the Saw / Hostel film sets -- only grittier! Why wait!?

title: Not bad
text: I had two nights here in August 2016. A couple of positives: very well located. Easy to find off the tube if you're new in London. Basic but comfortable. The staff are friendly and the single bed was comfy. The negatives : continental breakfast is ok if you show up first on a quiet morning. It consists of croissants and tea:coffee on tap and cereal. If you come on a busy morning, it's not worth it to wait around for a table to get a cup of cold tea. Fried eggs and toast cost a grand total 2 pound so very inexpensive and filling if you're on the go. I had hot water the morning of my arrival, but only cold that night which was a bit disappointing after being rained on in typical London weather. The phone in the room did not work so I could not buzz reception to sort out water and didn't fancy going to reception in my towel. WiFi is unreliable at best. Could not get it to work at all on first day. But worked intermittently on second day. On the whole : comfortable with a good location but zero luxuries. Not bad.

title: Great place to stay!
text: This year while visiting England I once again stayed at this B&B. They had done some more painting of the inside and are still working to get it up to par. But it is the friendlist place that I had stayed in london. Fair prices and very,very nice people. They all treat you like a friend and were so pleased that I had returned. Even gave me a bigger room for less money.The owner is there much of the time and a very caring person. The desk clerk,Sondra is wonderful and always willing to help with what you need. Stay again next time,Oh yes.Four stars for the Rose Court 35 Great cumberland Place, London

title: Beware of the Room
text: A friend booked this hotel for me. Initially there was a mix up with my booking which finally got sorted(long story which is for another day). Here I just want comment on the room. As I approached it via the 2 person lift , the narrow hallways and stairs, alarm bells in my head were already ringing. It had grubby and unkept appearance. As I opened the room door I was prepared for the worst and so it was. The room was an unusual shape, longish and narrow. The wallpaper was dull and ancient. My attention was then immediately drawn to the bed. The blanket was very old and dirty looking, as was the headboard. There was an old wardrobe at the foot of the bed which looked like it was ready to fall over at any moment. The room had a real dark and depressing feel to it. I had a quick glimpse into the bathroom which was bigger than the room itself before I decided to go back and investigate the sheets on the bed. As I pulled back the old top blanket the sheets underneath surprisingly looked cleaned but then the lights went out and I was in the dark. Maybe that was the best way to view the room. After ten minutes I had enough so I picked up my back, walked down to reception, returned my key and left. Stayed in a much nicer and cheaper hotel about 15 minutes walk from there. It is amazing what hotels like the Rose Court ,Great Cumberland Place can get away with.

title: Decent, great staff
text: The location is excellent, and for the rates it is a pretty good deal. We had a few issues and the staff, especially Miss Julie was very accommodating. (jale?) Recommended for sure.

title: Crazy but great!!
text: This hotel is crazy. It's like a warren. Basic but clean rooms. The best location you could imagine. Check out it's neighbour hotels!! £50 per person per night B&B.I wouldn't bother with the breakfast. Eatern European at it's worst. Pop round the corner to Deli Valerie! Have no expectations and you'll be pleased.

title: Excellent business stay
text: Great stay, excellent location, good room and nice staff. I've stayed in a few hotels in London and this is by far the best!! Staff were courteous, polite and went the extra mile to make it special..

title: A little gem in the centre of London!
text: We stayed here Friday night it is a lovely hotel for the price we paid, round the corner from marble arch tube station. Nice rooms, nice staff, nice breakfast :-) Staff are very friendly and able to assist u which makes a nice change, good base with a hair dryer, tea and coffe facilities in room. Just ask at reception for iron And ironing board . We will be staying again Mr & mrs Lacey

title: Good location but very basic

title: The worst hotel I have stayed in
text: In April this year I had cause to make a trip to London for a Conference in the City that I had known about for several months, but for which I had not made appropriate arrangements. What do you do under those circumstances ? I needed a hotel that was (a) accessible to preferably the Central Line, (b) would not cost me an arm and a leg, and (c) had rooms available at less than 48 hours’ notice. I know central London reasonably well, having worked there in the 80’s and again in the 90’s and early 00’s. I have some favourite spots but I am disappointed to report that with shabby damp and smelly rooms, even for £60 via lastminute.com this place is expensive. Yes I was appreciative of its location, the cheery chappie on the front desk when I arrived, and the short walk to the tube station, But to describe it in a single word, think “jumping into a pool”.

title: Holy Moly! I've been scalped!
text: I should have guessed there might be an issue when the taxi driver grunted in response to the address I requested. This seems to be a small family run hotel but really the price for what I got was outrageous. A narrow twin bed, stained coverlet, and furniture that was badly chipped and stained. Walls and doorways covered in handprints and the tiny black-and-white TV. Depressing. This was a 180 pound room that should be more like 50! (If you can endure the funky bed linens.) I switched to a major chain hotel for less the next day.

title: Friendly Hotel
text: Having read the reviews concerning bedbugs, surly staff and threadbare carpets, I couldn't wait to try this hotel. I was sorely disappointed. The sheets were clean, there was a generous supply of clean towels, the bed very comfortable, more than adequate milk cartons (something hotels are usually very mean on) and the staff were, without exception, helpful and friendly. There was always a smile for you upon returning to the hotel. Upon arrival, a young man was summoned to carry my small suitcase up to my room - an old fashioned practice not found in some more expensive hotel. It is true the carpet was worn in places and the paintwork has seen better days. There appears to be some renovation taking place in the area of one of the main staircases as modern wood panelling had been placed on the lower part of the walls. This was, I fear, a mistake and out of keeping in a town house such as the Rose Court. The restoration and decoration of these elegant houses, even when used as hotels, needs to be researched. The hotel appears to lack a housekeeper and a DIY man. Traditionally, the housekeeper's job was to check each room, etc. for any fault (however slight) and get it fixed (this is where the DIY man came in). In my room, the housekeeper would have found the basin plug did not fit and that some wretched child, upon entering the room, had left their sticky finger marks on the wall . I would think these two jobs could be absorbed by the current staff. The small lounge had a supply of tourist leaflets, large TV and two comfortable settees. Some magazines would have been nice. They do not have to be up-to-date or expensive - just something to while away a short time. Some fresh or potted flowers would have been nice. Again these do not have to be expensive. The dining room could have been the original dining room and had two large windows which made the room quite light. The basic breakfast was included in the price. However, a cooked breakfst was available for an extra charge. The UK and London in particular is now expensive and the cost of maintaining these town houses is high. People seem to forget that the bill they pay is not the hotel's own turnover. There is VAT at 17 1/2% and the business rate. I suspect that, of the £75 I paid, the hotel received maybe £60. Then there is the burden of implementing the never ending legislation which now emanates from the EU . This always includes a healthy dose of paperwork which nobody ever looks at. I hope the above points will be helpful to the hotel in developing their trade and I only wish that some of the other commentators thought before they put key to computer screen.

title: Cheap not cheerful
text: I booked this from a last minute hotel booking website for me, my partner and a work colleague. We got two rooms in the hotel after our work Xmas party. We just wanted somewhere clean and cheap, and are generally not fussy when we stay in London, which we do often on a budget. The room my partner and I stayed in was surprisingly large with high ceilings and a big window, and so has the potential to be really lovely. Unfortunately though the decor and general state of repair let it down. I'm not sure of the room number, but our room had a large mirror right opposite the bed, which was really disconcerting and gave you the feeling of being watched which wasn't pleasant. There was a double bed in the room and an extra single, the bedlinen was clean but looked old and the bed was incredibly uncomfortable and creaked every time you moved, making it near impossible to sleep. I tried sleeping in the single and it was the same. The en suite was very small, but I expect that for the price and it was no problem for us. It was quite grubby though and the whole place could do with a refresh. The final test of a good hotel is always the tea and coffee making facilities, but they provided whitening instead of milk and the kettle wasn't clean, so we didn't go there! We didn't want to stay for breakfast and when we met up with my colleague in the morning, she was equally unimpressed and had left her room at 6.30am because she didn't feel comfortable there. It did the job for one night, but I wouldn't stay there again.

title: Great location for the price
text: This hotel is in a great location, right by Marble Arch so ideal for tube access and, shopping on Oxford street and even Hyde Park for a stroll. Considering all this, i was surprised that it was so reasonably priced. I was in London with family to see a show, so was only staying one night. The hotel is undergoing renovation, so the family room that I stayed in was a little tired, but it was clean and had all the facilities that we needed for a night. A basic breakfast is included, but get there early as the breakfast room is small so you will end up waiting for a table, as the staff did not seem eager to clear them. ou can have a full english for en extra £4, portions are small but it was well cooked.

title: location and staff are perfect

It is situated in a perfect area 5 mins walk away from the marble arch tube. The staff there are very nice and friendly. The breakfast is good,reasonable price and it has a small lift.....will definatley stay here again........

text: Booked an overnight stay here through late rooms. £36 total for bed and breakfast. Considering its location Marble Arch, and less than 5 mins walk from Oxford Street this was amazingly good value. The room was warm, clean and had everything required. The staff were helpful, the breakfast was more than adequate and the whole place was well looked after. It's not a high end establishment and the price reflects this. I would stay here again. For an overnight stay in central London I doubt you could get anything near the price we paid.

text: I have stayed here for business last year in 2011. since then I have been coming back everytime my work takes me to central london. A great location and only a brief walkaway from the colourful edgeware road with its lively cafes and eataries. very good value also, definatly 'my' hotel for business.

text: Cheapest hotel I could find near Marble Arch and it showed. The room was pretty small but luckily I hadn't brought my cat to swing around. Walls and fixtures were tired and worn. The bed felt like a plasticky hospital bed and the noise from the traffic outside made it difficult to sleep. The bathroom was quite cramped and on the positive side it did have a bath, on the negative the drains stank and I had to keep the door shut. If you can put up with the above fora cheap price I'd still recommend it as the staff were polite and helpful and you're only 2 mins walk from Oxford Street.

title: Old hotel at a good location.
text: Me and my family, four of us stayed here for 3 days. I was disappointed at first to see the room because with the price, i was expecting something fancier. It must be a bit on the pricier side because of the location and it was peak of summer vacation! We got the basement room, with 1 king bed and 2 single bed. We're happy that the room is big. It is a really basic room with electric pot, cups, coffee, tea, hair dryer, wifi, lcd tv, and shower foam / shampoo. Though the furniture was old, the room is clean enough for me. The lift, we were looking for it at first, not something you will notice right away. Looks like a regular door and it's small. Exactly 2 adult can fit in and no more. Might be the original lift they had since 18**'s maybe. The staff was really helpful. The breakfast starts later at 8am but we always have to get out earlier since most of the tour starts before 8am. The hotel staff allowed us to have breakfast earlier but we can't order hot breakfast since the kitchen staff will only starts working at 8am. I think they should start the breakfast time earlier because a lot of tourists stay here and most of the visit tour starts early. I give 4 stars for the convenient location and the helpful staff. The hotel can improve so much better with a little facelift.

title: Great value for money.
text: Everyone giving this hotel bad reviews are clearly expecting to much from a 3 star hotel. It's a fair priced hotel with breakfast included, the rooms are a little dated but out of the two rooms I've stayed in both bathrooms have been refurbished and we have never experienced any problems apart from the usual hearing people in the morning but that's only because we like to sleep in. This is a perfect hotel for a cheap weekend away in London, especially if your not looking for too much.

title: Good, especially for the price

title: Survival shelter In the very center of London
text: Located surprisingly well, three minutes walk to the place where the famous Oxford street begins, this hotel may have been nice in a passed era, if ever. The building interiors could actually be nice due to some generous interior staircase, but the "decorator" was so cheap that spoiled this possible advantage. In the lobby you can see the safe boxes, apparently not usable because they are always obstructed by luggages. And they are not free. My room was, luckily, big. A triple room by London standards, which is almost a normal sized single room in the rest of the universe. But the furniture and the blankets and the carpet and the walls were so worn-out and stained that you hardly wanted to be in contact with anything. At some point I could realize that the sheets are actually clean. They were really clean. The bathroom also was ancient, poor, but clean. Don't expect too much from the breakfast. It's rather limited, but you can eat enough to start your Oxford street adventure in the morning. Probably you'll avoid to come back at the hotel until evening. You can also walk opposite to Oxford street. There's the Edgeware road and its surroundings. Here you'll find a very different London - it's worth to see it.

title: Cracking!
text: Weird but hilarious hotel! We walked in and were greated by the Receptionist who informed us we were early in a very polite manner (and yes we were by about two hours) we asked if we could leave our bags there and nip out for lunch, we were told, yes just put it in the corner over there (the corner of the large reception room), had we had anything valuable we would have maybe felt a bit dodgy about this but it was just clothes as we were only staying a day so happily obliged. We popped down to Marble Arch (which you can see at the bottom of the road) and Oxford Street less than 5 minutes away! When we returned our items were still there and we were promptly checked in and directed to our room. The room was big! We had a double(ish) and single bed in our high ceiling room with plenty of floorspace, a desk, two wardrobes and a bathroom. We noticed a kettle but no coffee/tea/cups - no issue as we weren't overly bothered. Fun begins - toilet seat would not stay up unless jussst riiiight which resulted in many loud bangs scaring the poop out of ye! The shower took some technical know-how to operate and once I was in I realised the bath was quite high and as such could only really shower if you were about 5ft as my head was over the tap and screen! I did have to laugh! The hairdryer was as good as any hotel dryer. The TV was a decent size with plenty of channels which we enjoyed after our shopping trip and evening meal. Problem was our room was on the ground floor in quite a high traffic area with a set of lights right out the window which was not glazed to a high standard. As we were clearing out the next morning we found the tea/coffee/milk/sugar in the bedside cabinet - doh! Please do not take the above as saying this is a bad place at all! It isn't! We paid £60 for one night to stay in a hotel 5 mins from Oxford Street, we were expecting worse and it was actually quite fun with its quirks! We would definately go back but maybe see about staying in a room not on street level!

I bit irritating with the resepsjonist who was more oqupied with playing videogames on ihis lap top than paying attention.... but when we first got his attention - he was all ours :-) so: if yore lookiing for a cheap - no nonsense stay over - saving money - and you are not to pickey - just perfect.

title: Grim
text: First impression of outside and reception - good. We had a room on top floor - carpets are very grubby on all floors. To get to our room we had four sets stairs - last set were extremely narrow and steep. The room had grubby carpet and walls

title: Very basic but doing the job
text: I stayed at Griffin House Hotel for one night - I basically chose it for its cheap price (finding a room in Central London for less than 100 pounds is quite difficult...). I had a single room which was super small but clean, however it smelled weirdly in the morning -- might have come from the street but I am not sure. The breakfast was very basic, and variety not too extensive -- no plant-based milk, which was a pity. But wifi was for free and the bed was quite comfortable. All in all, it is an OK option to stay in but really nothing fancy at all.

title: This place is awful
text: The rooms are in very poor condition. There was plaster falling off of the walls and large dirt patches above the headboard. The quality of the accommodation at the prices they charge is absolutely disgusting.

title: Wat a dump!!
text: Overpriced and in very poor condition ! Quite happy to take your money and definitely don't care as regards to condition of the rooms ..the most expensive and the worst place I've stayed in in London 😭

title: Good 3* hotel with great location
text: Just few steps from busy Marble Arch in a quiet location. The hotel itself is bit vintage, poor furniture and very small bathroom. The room was ok, nice view. Lot of stairs to the top, but ok. It was clean but smell it like an old hotel. Continental breakfast was ok, but nothing special.

title: Better than sleeping at the airport.
text: London is an expensive town, so I was glad to find a hotel in the center of town for only £119 following a two week trip to Scotland. However, as they say, you get what you pay for. The "room" was on the fourth floor up a steep flight of steps (good thing I only had a backpack) and was small (about the size of a walk in closet), stuffy, and dingy with signs of recent water damage and had to prop the window open with a coat hanger. I am not a picky traveler by any means, but the unwashed, recently soiled sheets on the bed were just gross. A stripped the bedding and slept in my sleeping bag. I would give the place a one star rating except for (1) wi-fi, (2) its good location in the heart of Little Beirut with numerous great Middle Eastern eateries, (3) proximity to the Marble Arch underground station, and (4) the very helpful late night staff who let me borrow their personal UK to US converter to charge my phone. Still beats sleeping in the airport.

title: More than awful....but they don't care!
text: Stay away from this place! It is a dump. I doubt that this place could possibly meet any industry health and safety regulations. The location is good, but that is not enough. If this accommodation cost a quarter as much as it did, it would still be far too expensive. For an extra 50 GBP per night, for a triple room, we found a beautiful 'luxury' hotel metres from Paddington station, including full English breakfast! So look carefully....read all of these comments....I wish I had! Like so many others, we had a horrible stay. We booked and paid for a triple room. We arrived very late at night and could not look for alternative accommodation. The room is no.3. It was disgusting to say the least. It was in the basement next to their kitchen. Tiniest of rooms, could not move. Three people could not even stand up at one time, the floorspace was so small. Worse than this the walls were damp and mouldy with peeling wallpaper. The double bed and single bed (a makeshift trundle-type of structure) had stained linen. The dirty shower was literally in a cupboard and stank of mould. The toilet was dirty and unflushed. I could go on and on about one awfully tiny revolting space. We e demanded a full refund for the two nights booked, but they don't care. We left as early as possible the next morning, not daring to eat food from there. and after much following-up and argument, we received a refund for the second night's booking.

title: Filthy - Tiny Rooms - Fire Trap
text: Room 7 was up one flight of stairs that were covered in a filthy beige carpet. The room itself was grimy and the decoration was poor. There were no curtains on the 2 eye level windows. There was a large amount of dust in the room especially the radiator. The sheets looked grubby and there was no headboard on the bed. There was plaster missing from the wall behind the bed. The carpet was so disgusting that I decided against walking on it in bare feet. The ensuite was accessed by a sliding door and was home to a colony of silverfish. The toilet seat was loose and the shower door was rusty and loose. It was late when I arrived and I was unable to find alternative accommodation that night. My booking was for two nights but I found another hotel to spend the second night in. Overall a truly grim experience. AVOID.

title: Where not to stay in London
text: This is no 3-star hotel - trust me on this. The single bedrooms are extremely cramped and the TV is practically in your face. They have about 17 rooms in a place that can't support more than 8 max! Plus, their service is terrible - they pulled a fast one on me by charging me extra days when I checked out early - never happened before!

title: Don't go there, you can book better!!!
text: This hotel is definitely not the best place to stay. It is located in a very central area, but the hotel itself is no good. The double room we booked was extremely small with the bed taking up most of the space. The matrass was very old and I could feel the base of the bed. The bathroom is smaller than small with the wash basin tucked away in the one corner and hardly wide enough to wash your face in. The towels were really old and over used. There wasn't even complimentary shampoos or anything! The sky-box cables were haning lose and looked terrible. The room was located on the street and was so noisy I had to use earplugs! The breakfast room was just as bad. It it located in the basement and very warm and stuffy. Not a friendly breakfast feel to it with staff that could hardly understand what I asked for in English. It was suppose to be a continental breakfast but I was terribly dissapointed. All in all, you can find a better place to stay at that is even a bit cheaper!!!

title: Excellent Value for location. Clean & Comfy with Sky & Breakfast. Perfect.
text: I cant understand what everyones on about in the earlier reviews! Maybe the hotel owners have had a spruce up since. I was nervous because of the reviews but it was the best I could get in that area at a budget price. I had no reason to worry! Alright its a small double room with small bathroom but perfectly adequate and very clean with new modern sheets and sky and a fan for a weekend trip. I wanted near hyde park with our own bathroom (many hotels were charginh more for a shared bathroom!) and I got it for a reasonable price (£170 for two nights with breakfast) The breakfast room is tiny and breakfast isnt big and a bit limited for my appetite but absolutely perfect scambled eggs - not microwaved! Also this is a VERY safe and secure place as Tony Blair lives literally across the road and has 24 hour armed guards! All in all a very pleasant stay. Would definately recommend this place if only for the short walk to Hyde Park.

title: Great location
text: Fantastic location, really helpful friendly staff. Small room and bathroom but very clean and functional. Great price for the area. Breakfast was available but didn't have time to have it. Stairs were something else ( Had room 15 on top floor!) Over all had a good experience, would stay there again and certainly recommend. : )

title: Great location, fantastic staff
text: Have stayed in this hotel 3-4 times this year on short business trips. Clean and tidy, excellent breakfast cooked to order. 3 mins walk from all the amenities of Edgeware Road incl. Supermarket nearby. Less than 10mins walk to Marble Arch and Oxford Street. Highly recommended

title: Ok, if you are not planning to spend too much time at you room.
text: Perfectly located in walking distance to oxford street and hide park. Friendly staff, but the rooms are very small,dirthy and the walls are paper thin. The beds are also small, but comfortable. Simple breakfast with eggs of you choice and toast.

title: Solid 3 stars. Great for the price and location.
text: Stayed for 5 nights. I'm used to the small size of the rooms in London, but this was one of the smallest. The bathroom was tough because I am a larger than average person, but it was usable. The water was plenty hot and I took my normal 10 minute shower no problem. The room could definitely use a little more storage space. The rack that is available for hanging clothes was okay, but I couldn't unpack my entire suitcase onto it, and I'm a light packer. The bedside table was fine for holding my books, water bottles, snacks and c-pap machine, and there were plenty of outlets thanks to two power strips provided. The television reception was patchy, but I wasn't there to watch TV, so it was not a problem. I found the bed to be quite comfortable, surprisingly - I am used to them being uncomfortable but this was okay. The carpets and paint left a little to be desired, and could use some updating. I never felt like I was in a "dirty" room, though. As for the noise level, I was on the 2nd floor, and the bed was right up against the window, but it wasn't that bad. The people that I dealt with (only 3 of them) were very pleasant, they helped me with my luggage, and the front desk girl even let me use her personal cell phone to call my friend (a local call) to let her know I had arrived safely. Over all, it was a pleasant stay and I would go there again.

title: The room was definitely bad
text: A room located underground, exactly under the lobby (so that each time somebody entered the hotel, I heard their steps loudly) without speaking about the toilets of the reception also located above the room and which made a huge noise each time they were used... No table nor desk (of course) A very tiny bathroom Really a bad room. Otherwise, the hotel looks nice from the outside..!

title: Hideous hotel experience
text: We booked a triple room and were given the room downstairs next to the dining area. The window was directly opposite to the hotel kitchen windows so it was noisy in the morning. The room was far too small for a triple. There were large damp patches all over the walls

title: Very disappointing clastrophobic single room
text: Booked for 7 nights as single adult traveler. I got tiny single room, about 2*2.2m where the toilets were outside the room under the stairs. The toilets were very small, where one should have a flexibility of Chinese rubber girl in order to sit and relax there. obviously there no place for towel in the toilets. After one night (actually 12hr upon arrival) I paid a fine, and run away to different hotel.

title: Excellent value.
text: I dont know where the moaning critics were staying, not here! Fantastic location and incredible value for a hotel 5 mins walk from Hyde Park and Marble Arch. The MOST friendly and helpful staff. The room and bathroom were small (impossible to sit on the toilet without crushing your legs on the shower cubicle), the corners, paintwork and carpet were not clean but the linen and bathroom were immaculate and the bed was comfy. Perfect for a one or two night visit. Breakfast was good but I would have liked tea and coffee making facilities in the room.

title: 3 Stars is generous!
text: Our stay at Griffin House Hotel was more than disappointing. With a group of 3 we were given the downstairs basement level room with 1 double bed and 1 single bed. The amount of space in the room was perfect for the three of us to use with 3 carry on sized bags we were comfortable. The beds were extremely uncomfortable and hard. The mattress was covered by only a flat sheet which moved throughout the night and no top sheet was given the Doona was the only blanket provided. Linen appeared clean however a pin was found in the single bed. The room smelt damp, most probably due to it being on the basement level. The bathroom was the most disappointing aspect of the room. The shower head was filthy with a massive build up of limescale I'm not sure it had ever been cleaned. The shower drainage was terrible, we had to have extremely fast showers or the water would overflow and flood the bathroom (forget trying to wash your hair) the plumbing made the sound of a jack hammer every time we (or anyone else) flushed the toilet ( we did record the sound but we couldn't upload to TA) The hotel has been renovated since some of the other photos on trip advisor however the walls in our room were dirty and looked like they could use another coat of paint . The floor length mirror was also dirty. The roof in the shower looked like it could use a fresh coat of paint with the paint flaking off. Breakfast was standard with croissants and muffins although these didn't quite taste fresh and staff were available to make eggs and toast upon request. Some of the staff were lovely whereas others seemed like they would rather be anywhere or do anything else other than help you. We would have been more than happy to stay at griffin house hotel but paying over 960 AUD was a joke.

title: Perfect for a one night stay
text: I needed a small room in the centre of London as I was meeting friends for the evening and then had a short drive to another location in Westminster the next morning. I wanted no frills, somewhere to lay my head and considered hostels etc, but stumbled across the Griffin House Hotel and I was impressed. The hotel is located on a quiet street just off Marble Arch. You are really in the thick of it, but just a street away so you are no disturbed by the throng of shoppers/party goers/Police sirens etc. As I stayed Saturday into Sunday I was able to park for free outside. Please be aware there are some resident's spaces that require a pass and you will received a ticket if you park in them at any time. My room held a single bed and was small, but it was exactly what I expected. It had a en suit with a decent shower and the whole room was very clean and well decorated. The front reception area and breakfast room were also very clean and well decorated. The breakfast was a selection of muffins, cereals, fruit, croissants and a hot breakfast could be requested. Due to my hangover I tried pretty much everything they had and it was excellent. I paid £50 for the night and breakfast was included along with free WiFi. I would not necessarily stay here for a fancy weekend away, but I will definitely be visiting again when I need somewhere just to crash. Exceeded my expectations and would recommend.

title: Who Said Small Was Beautiful...................
text: Single rooms in this day and age - only in Mayfair, London I guess. How they fitted the actual bed in the room was the only mark of excellence but god forbid the cleaners who have to try make the bed or even open the window! Three floors up and no lift, a lock on the door that was older than me and when you sit on the toilet your feet are in the shower. I guess it was clean enough as really, other than the 100 year old carpet, there was nothing in the room to get dirty. The sink being blocked added to the experience. On a good note the ladies downstairs did fry me some lovely eggs with a great coffee and yes they were very pleasant indeed. But hey one might say what do you want in that area of London for £85 per night - personally I want MORE!

title: Cheaper over night stay in London
text: Clean,welcoming and friendly. We stayed in a very small ground floor bedroom. The bed,floor and bathroom door squeaked and we did feel uncomfortable to think people in reception could hear us. We only wanted a bed for the night and it was fine for that. We didn't have the breakfast option or use the shower.

title: Disapointing
text: Tiny rooms, cleanish, no information packs in room,location good. Appreciate it is in a "good area" but leaves a lot to be desired. Breakfast area again tiny with poorly arranged seating arrangements.

title: Cheap and cheerful hotel in great location
text: Stayed here for 3 nights. Great base 5 mins from Marble Arch. Rooms very small but clean and warm. Bed ok Breakfast included was fine and enough to set you up for he day Staff were friendly and helpful. Fine for a budget break to London with no frills. We left the room after breakfast each morning and didn't return till bed time so didn't need anything fancy.

title: Urine smells, moldy showers, and cramped rooms await you...
text: We had a 4 night stay planned in London so we chose our hotel based on price and location. We found the Griffin House on a budget travel site and agreed that it fit our criteria. It looked decent from the on-line photos as well. When we checked in, we were giddy from its location and lovely surroundings. These feelings were instantly nixed as we headed towards our dungeoness room toting our massive luggage down a rickety flight of stairs. The desk staff was greasy and unsmiling. Not a great start. When we opened our door with our ancient room key (this took 5 minutes) we were smacked in the face with a wafting smell of fresh urine. We booked a double room for 2, we got a triple with a tiny bed for children, I suppose. I sat on the bed to look around and take in the hideous surroundings, and as I did the pee smell became stronger. It was then that I realized this bed was the culprit. Some child had probably peed in the bed and the staff just put a fresh set of sheets on and threw over a comforter and this was their solution. Nice. That was just one of the problems. Only one of the 4 lights in the room worked, the shower was covered in green mildew, the toilet was cracked. The towels were like the shammies you wash your car with. Ick. There was also no room to walk or turnaround in your room. Just a long, small hallway from the door to the room. We begged for a room correction at the front desk and by that evening they finally moved us upstairs to a smaller, but cleaner room. Our second room was equally cramped with a bonus! The only source of ventilation was a window that we opened, and outside were 2 apartment dwellers smoking like chimneys. Of course, all of this smoke blew into our room and added to the ambience. We stayed 2 nights total in this place. It was disgusting. The other guests were equally as miserable and we would commiserate over breakfast each morning at the condition. The one up-side is that the staff swore to us that they were about to do some major rennovations to the hotel in the fall. I hope for everyone's sake that they do. It was the moldiest, stinkiest hovel I have ever stayed in, especially in Europe. Budget or not, I know you can find better in London. Really unfortunate stay.
