title: If Location Only Is Important - This Could Be Right For You.
text: Before making a week long reservation at this establishment, I read a less than complimentary report on your website. I discussed this with the Reservations Manager of Griffins who expressed surprise at the comments, assured me that the hotel had been completely refurbished and would meet my requirements admirably. To cement the deal he offered me a deluxe room for the standard room price of 70 pounds per day. On 24th September 2006, my wife and I arrived to move in. Full payment on registration was required and paid. The reception gentleman seized one of our bags and set off up a flight of stairs as steep as a hen's face, leaving 82 year old me to carry an equally heavy one. By the time I hove into view at the door of the room, reception was on his way down, leaving no opportunity to re-act to the state of the room. A quick survey confirmed it was clean. It had one towel available for the use of two people and a T.V. on a stand so high up on the wall, it could not be viewed from any comfortable position. No chairs so the only option was to lie flat and try to catch an angle of the screen. We reported these matters three times before another towel arrived the next day and the Television was taken off its stand and dumped on our bedside table. The room was described as DELUXE. This term should be expunged from Griffin's promotional material. At best it could be described as a STANDARD room- leaving their standard rooms with the title SUB-STANDARD. Breakfast was included. A set of stairs downward that would be better approached with alpine equipment, took us into a room with four tables. CONTINENTAL breakfast was on the menu- in fact that was the menu. A bowl of cereal swimming for its life in far too much milk, arrived promptly. Almost simultaneously came two slices of slightly toasted bread on a large plate along with the usual butters and jams. By the time we had excavated the cereal from its milky hideaway, the toast was cold and leathery. This pattern was repeated each of the seven days we appeared. The only releif offered was eggs scrambled or boiled with no supporting luxuries such as bacon. The word CONTINENTAL should be deleted from all Griffin brochures and replaced with the word-SUB-CONTINENTAL. Griffin House Hotel should never be called a Hotel. It is at best a B&B. there is no lounge or Bar-nowhere to be except in your room. GRIFFIN HOUSE HAS ONE VIRTUE- IT IS NEAR OXFORD STREET.

title: Only plus is the location
text: Spent only one night at this hotel, but that was plenty. The room was the tiniest room I have ever stayed in and the cleanliness left a lot to be desired, as did the maintenance. Thick layers of dust everywhere, the hardware around the mini sink was loose and it took a good 5 minutes to get the first warm water to flow. The location close to Marble Arch was the only good thing about this hotel.

title: Just for a couple of days!
text: Griffin house hotel is located only 5 min on foot from Marble Arch!!i guess this is the only reason for someone to book this hotel!!!the rooms are too small even for London's stardards,you can hear everything that's moving outside the door!!!Staff is unfriendly i never saw them smile!!anytime we asked for something the answer was no!!the only decent guy is the one serving breakfast!!!!the receptionists' behavior was unaccepted!!!go there only if you are spending a night or two, but no more than that!!!!!

title: Terrific, Cozy Hotel nr Marble Arch, London
text: Griffin House Hotel, Connaught Street London. I have stayed in this charming Hotel on two seperate occasions and have just confirmed a third stay for May 2007- in my opinion it is very good value for the money. This is a delightful small B + B in a wonderful location off Edgeware Road, just a 5-6 minute walk to March Arch and Oxford St. The rooms are clean and comfortable, with decent en suite bathrooms and Cable TV.All the staff are wonderful, extremely courteous and friendly, as were the other guests at the time! I needed to have computer access on several occasions and the staff allowed me to use their front office for that purpose. A very good hot breakfast is served downstairs and I had access to the kitchen for a "cuppa" whenever I needed. I think of it now as a "home from home " whenever I am in London and would not consider staying anywhere else.

title: reasonable for short business trips
text: It was just right for my businesstrip, because the location is within easy reach of all important stops in London. I would not recommend this hotel for pure leasure trips with your partner. The room was very tiny with no proper storing facilities

title: Welcoming house, simple 3 star hotel, great location
text: The hotel is a welcoming house with cool modern decoration from London and British heritage. Friendly staff, clean, simple service, competitive price (3 nights were almost the same price as 1 night in a 4 star nearby). Asked for a single room and had a very small single room, with a very thin single bed, but enough for 1. When I opened my bag, I had to jump over it to reach the toilet, and when the door was closed, I could unfold the chair and use it to place my toiletries or other items on top. Internet worked well everywhere, always handy these days. Breakfast was a nice surprise for a 3 star hotel, more complete than expected. Fresh fruit, variety of cereals, bread, juices, jams, etc. And then we could ask for eggs, fried, scrambled, omelette… with a great location 5min from Marble Arch, Hyde Park and Oxford Street, I would definitely stay there again!

title: A five minutes walk from Marble Arch and a place to sleep- that's all!
text: I can handle four floors without an elevator. But when I and my daugther saw the last stairs up to the attic, we wondered if we were able to get up there with our suitcase! IT was so narrow and steep that we almost were leaning backwords! My imidiate thought was: How will we get out suitcase down again after 5 days in Oxford street?! And even worse: nobody offered to help! But we managed! We got info a small room, filled up with a bed. Fair enough - we were just going to sleep there! But IT would have been nice with a warm shower- that was impossible! Plenty water, but cold! The continental breakfast was also disappointing, we tried it just once. We can however recommend Paul two minutes away - with "l'amour de pain". But it shouldn't be necessary when you've already paid for breakfast. Anyway - London is great- Marble Arch is a fine place to start the day- and life is too short to let cold water and steep stairs affect your holiday! But I think we paid enough for this hotel!

title: Dont waste your money
text: Where do I start with this review, very friendly n polite staff on entering, thats the good points over with now to the rest. If you do decide to stay here, there is no lift so ask for a room lower down as we were in room 15 and it was in the attic, very steep stairs, but seriously dont stay here. Our room had dust lying on all flat surfaces, the beds were well made but very uncomfortable, we also asked for a double bed we got twin singles. The room itself was small and only 1 of the 4 electric sockets worked, the main light fitting was loose from the cieling, and the bedside lamp did not work, Oh and the small table between the beds had a randomly opening draw throughout the night. very annoying, the TV was working though. In the bathroom apart from the 1 inch rise on the floor, there was a 3inch triangle of ceramic tile missing infront of the basin very sharp edges, but this was repaired when I mentioned it to the very nice receptionist. The shower was a waste of time no hot water and very low water pressure even after 15 mins nothing and also the noisiest Ive ever had the displeasure to switch on, The basin was far too small and again there was no water pressure and no hot water, on a rare plus point all 3 mirrors in the room worked fine. Breakfast was continental and tasty and again the receptionist was polite and pleasant, I will increase my rating to 2* as all the staff were very nice in our all to brief meeting, This hotel has a great address ................and nothing else going for it.

title: A lovely hotel
text: First fell in love with the hotel because of the interior and atmosphere. The room was certainly spacious and nicely designed. But I was disappointed by some points. Note that the building has no lift.. And ironically the staff was not quite welcoming, despite the friendly atmosphere of the hotel. It becomes little noisy in night time, and the smell from restaurant or kitchen come up even to the top floor.

title: Dirty and a fraud
text: Dirty, old hotel, if you can call it that. Tiny rooms and bathrooms, no elevator, unfriendly staff (they never greeted you and you always had to wait until they would talk to you). The stairs are not safe and the breakfast is more than disgusting! Not recommended at all!

title: Don't believe the nice reception pictures
text: 1 night stay for business, location great and online picture looked modern and clean..... Not the case, really poor, dirty room not on suite as toilet is down the hall With a separate key and tiny. As was the room, Zero hot water in shower, street noise very bad, yes it London but decent windows would help. Value by London standards but still £90 so expect better with hot water and clean! Wouldn't go near it again.

title: Not so bad as other reviews imply!!
text: Okay its true that the breakfast is not great, the breakfast room is also tiny but Griffin House Hotel has got a great location, just a stone's throw away from all the hustle & bustle. The area is very safe even at night & the two reception ladies are adorable especially the foreign one! Can't say the same about the male one though! The room & bathroom are small but very cosy. Many of the reviews here are old from when the hotel was under previous management so please ignore the old reviews!

title: OK hotel on good location
text: We stayed one night in this hotel in august. We choose it because of the location and that is indeed very good, just 5 minutes from Marble Arch, Oxford Street and Hyde Park. We had booked a double room, but when we arrived we got a triple so we had some extra space, which was very nice. The room itself was ok, altough the bathroom was tiny en the sink was the size normaly used in toilets only, not handy when you are brushing your teeth! The only real thing that kind of bothered us was the fact that the room ws in the souterain and right beneath the reception. Lucky that I'm a deep sleeper, but before going to bed we could hear every step above us. Breakfast was not big, (2 pieces of toast with butter and jam an a egg) but I liked it and for my it was enough. All things taken in account I would recommend this hotel for person who are traveling to London and have to keep an eye on tje price.

title: Perfectly acceptable for a nights kip
text: positives

title: OK for a short trip
text: Positives: Close to Oxford street, close to subway station and busses. No problem in finding food, its all around you. Service was good. Breakfast was good, the lady made fresh omelette for us with freshly toasted bread. Good for short stay if you intend only to come here to sleep. Negatives: Not the best hotel i have stayed in. Small room, tiniest bathroom i've ever seen, and even more tiny sink. Couldnt even wash my face. Windows not good, can hear all the noise from the street. No good blinds, woke up early due to all the light spilling in the room. No elevator, so be prepared to carry all your luggage up and down. They charge £3 for each bag to be kept in the hotel after checkout, never seen that before.

title: A quick trip in london (petit sejour a londres)
text: The hotel, room, bathroom are small, but for a quick trip it's enought because you spend all your time outside. The service is good, the personnal is kind, the room clean. I was in room 8 for three. The location of the hotel is good, near marble arch. There are a a lot of bus we can take and there is also a subway station. I recommand this hotel.

title: Okay for short stay
text: The hotel is located very close to Hyde Park which is great. I was in Room 14. A long way up the stairs until somewhatth floor. The service is acceptable, everything is clean. But the room is small and it has no closets to put in the clothes. Although, the corridors were quite narrow, they gave me free WiFi. The breakfast is okay, but the space for people there is quite small. Overall, I would recommend to people who are traveling individually to London and for a short stay.

title: Basic stuff for younger travellers
text: On the positive side - location in a walking distance to Marble Arch and Hyde Park. Low price for that location. And here is where positives are ending. Con's include: 1. poor layout - small room with no seperation from the corridor, so throughout the night there is light around the door, not to mention noise if somebody is coming back from hanging out. Lavatory separated with wooden wall only. No cupboard, forget the ironing desk. Extremely steep stair to the fourth level without elevator - an elderly person would not make it with a travel bag. 2. location in the loud street with poor, old-style window 3. deposit for a Euroeap-style socket adapter, extra charge for Wifi

title: London base
text: Great central location, perfect base for Central London Staff very friendly and helpful, always willing to assist. Good choice of light breakfast, dining room compact, Bedrooms compact, we had a triple room. no tea/ coffee making facilities but these are available to purchase. Beds comfortable and very clean, nice white bedding. Not suitable for disabled Stairs very steep and numerous ( nicknamed them cardiac arrest hill lol) despite these would definitely stay again. Good value.

title: Stay Away Please!
text: Please stay away from this hotel. I stayed in a single room that was supposedly an en-suite. This meant a very small shower cubicle with a door you couldn't open without bumping into the tv. The toilet was a shared one in the corridor. The room was very small even for London and smelled really badly. I have stayed in a lot of hotels but have never felt so cheated before.

title: Nice place to stay in
text: Location is excellent, rooms are nice and clean, staff friendly and helpful, we stayed for 7 nights and enjoyed our stay. Nice place to stay for long time. Breakfast is continental which can be improved but i think its worth the price we paid...... i will stay at the same hotel next time......

title: Recommended !
text: I enjoyed one night stay at Griffin House hotel,while my business trip to London.My room was small,bur cosy,with a view to the street,which was not too busy.The only downside was that my room for one person had a shower,but not toilet /as I know there are toilets in the bigger rooms/,but there was one for me in the corridor near the room.The breakfast was "take as much as you can" continental and the hot food option was different variations of eggs.I met Roberto,who was at the reception that time - a polite guy,who gave me some advices about my stay and the surrounding area.In two words-Griffin House hotel is a good place to stay if you want to be near Hyde Park and Oxford Street.See you there next time you visit London...

title: Had a lovely time
text: Room was small and at top of the stairs, but it was perfect for me. Breakfast was lovely and close to everything. Perfect for a solo traveller. The shower was really small and I wish a bit bigger, but other than that I would recommend. Staff was great too.

title: Small but clean and cheap hotel.
text: This hotel is small but clean, cheap and very close to Central London. If I had to name a negative it would be the small dining room where only breakfast is served. To eat at noon or evening you have to go out, but again, that's no trouble, it's 15 minutes walking from Soho anyways

title: Small but convenient!
text: Stayed a week over there... They offer you with good hospitality and good customer care. Room was pretty small but was just perfect for my stay. Clean and perfect! Only thing bothered me was that there was no lift.

title: Do not stay at this hotel.
text: On arrival the hotel had allocated the wrong rooms for our party of five. The receptionist was less than helpful and made no apology for their error. They managed to fit another 'bed' into the twin room and discounted the cost of the room by £5. When we got to the room they had put a camp bed between the two singles, there was no space to actually get into the bed unless you crawled up the bed from the bottom end. The rooms themselves were poorly funished and very knocked about. There were mutiple faults with the room e.g. door off the hinges, sharp cracked bathroom tiles, wires stretched across the rooms and plastic bags tied around the smoke detectors. When I returned to the reception to make the staff aware of the faults they said that they were already aware, but again offered no apology. Luckily our party were only staying one night and we spent minimal time at the hotel. I would strongly advise that people avoid staying here. The hotels website is very misleading and the room are not recognisable against the photos they have used on their web page. The hotel is in a good central location and is relatively cheap but still offers very poor value for money.

title: Cheap and cheerful
text: Booked for one night and the only drawback was the radiator had been left on a high setting so the ground floor room had got a bit too hot and I didn't feel safe enough to leave a window open as it didn't appear to have a security catch. Otherwise the room was very clean, the ensuite bathroom small but very nicely fitted and for the overall price and location this was an excellent find and I'd definitely recommend it and stay again.

title: Not good.
text: I keep looking for a clean, friendly, quiet, affordable small hotel in central London (if anybody knows one, please let me know). This isn't it! It's a rickety old place, where the staff don't know the name of the nearest tube station, and the room was so small, that there wasn't enough floor space for my bag. Give it a miss.

title: Excellent Staff.. shame about the rooms
text: I required a hotel in London for one night in February ( 2009) and used a well known website which lists lots and lots of hotels. The price was acceptable and the description was really good, below is a copy of the websites description .... "Rooms With excellently designed rooms, quality pine wood furniture, central heating system and multilingual satellite TV channels in every room, your will stay at hotel more comfortable and enjoyable. Restaurant Griffin House Hotel has a very clean and modern dining area where delicious breakfast is served" The outside of the Hotel looks nice, but the inside I found to be tatty and poor. I will let my photos speak for the quality of my room. My bathroom had a lipstick stained glass in it. In front of the wardrobe doors was a gap of about 3 feet to a wall where what looked like a small plastic piece of pipe was sticking out..for what I do not know. Breakfast was very basic, and mine was a glass of orange juice, cup of tea, a fried egg and slice of toast. The bed was most uncomfortable and although it was February, the room heat was excessive..which must have bothered others, as there was a fan in the room which I had to use.....and this was February remember Location was excellent for my requirements, but would I stay there again .. no way, if for no other reason but the totallly false claims about the quality of the room and especially the furniture ( see my pictures )

title: I enjoyed my stay.
text: I had to go to a weekend seminar and just needed somewhere close by that didn't cost a fortune - this was at the cheaper end of the scale but looked nicer than others near Paddington. The area is lovely, and I really enjoyed the short walk to Lancaster Gate in the morning along the quiet streets of Surrey Gardens and past the Hyde Park Stables. I received a very friendly welcome when I got in late at night and they were kind enough to give me extra towels (I later realised I had missed the towel on my bed). The breakfast started a bit late for me at 8.30am but when I appeared early at 8.15 they cooked me eggs regardless. It was extremely clean and I slept in room 14 (sounds like others have had an awful experience in the shared loo) but they said I wasn't sharing it with anyone. I know this is true because I blotted my lipstick in the morning and dropped the tissue in the loo (didn't want to flush one sheet away) and it was still there in the evening. It is nicer to have your own loo but you know when booking that this is the situation and that is what makes it cheaper. So all in all, I had a good stay here, it suited me well.

title: Thrown out of room for visiting a friend
text: A friend of mine stayed in this hotel for 2 nights. On the second night I went to visit her in her hotel ( I live a 15 min walk away), I'm British and have lived in London for 10 years. Upon arrival I was told I was not allowed to go to her room as no visitors were allowed after 9.30 pm?! In all my years of staying in hotels I have never heard this before. I tried to reassure the porter I had no interest in staying there as I was a local...but to no avail. DON'T STAY AT THIS HOTEL! Really weird

title: Worst hotel ever stayed in
text: On arrival and shown our room (downstairs on a narrow, twisty stairway) to a triple room which would barely accommodate a single human being, we said we could not possibly stay 2 nights here (1 night was pre-pd & 2nd pd on arrival). We were told there was no refund and we had to live with it, but after more complaining were offered 1 extra room on main floor (for the 70 yr olds) at no cost for 1 night and adult son slept downstairs. This was much more like a Hostel! There was no phone service, inadequate towels, ok juice, etc for breakfast but a disaster. After having traveled 2 wks (Ireland/England) this was a terrible way to end our last nights. However, Richard did arrange car transport from there to the airport direct - which helped.

title: A traveller’s nightmare
text: I’d love to provide you with a full review of the Griffin House Hotel experience but I can only take you as far as the reception, as that’s as far as we got…despite a confirmed booking with the Griffin House Hotel, we found ourselves in London on a Saturday with no accommodation. My friends and I booked 2 rooms with the Griffin House hotel over a month in advance of our trip, we called a week before arrival to make an amendment to the booking and confirm our reservation. However, upon our arrival the thoroughly unhelpful lady behind the reception (I use the term loosely) not-so-politely informed us that ‘our names weren’t on the list so we weren’t coming in’. This is despite the fact that we could provide written confirmation of our booking. Defying the tradition of customer is always right, the lady behind the desk blankly informed us that the hotel was full and our predicament was not her fault. After some huffing and puffing she finally presented us with two equally under whelming options

title: Better than expected!
text: I booked this hotel very last minute, thought the position was great and it looked good. After I booked it, I read all the reviews on this site.. and there were many, and got increasingly concerned.. a vast proportion of the reviews were terrible, frankly. But I thought, hey ho, I

title: Not the hotel we were expecting...
text: This is more like a 2* guest house than a hotel. There are no tea /coffee making facilities in the room and the T.V didn't work, but there was a hair dryer. The beds had seen better days and were on a slight tilt so it felt like you were going to fall out. There was a slight drain /sewage smell coming from the bathroom, but the water was nice and hot and the shower did work. The radiator was absolutely red hot so you had to have the window open constantly , ok if you like saunas. Its only bonus points were that it was with-in a 10 minute walk from Paddington station and about a 5-8 minute walk to Marble Arch tube station. The breakfast provided was not what I would class as satisfactory. It consisted of tea/coffee, cereal or scrambled egg which was served up on a plate on its own and then your toast was bought to the table. We found a great pub on the way to Marble Arch tube station that served a great breakfast for £1.99, so I would skip what they are offering if you choose to stay here. I'm glad we were not staying here for more than one night, it was a last minute booking and it was ok as a base room, it was clean and tidy that is the only good thing I can say.

title: a disgrace
text: booked a double deluxe room , got 2 awful single beds pushed together ,carpet old and threadbare, mould in shower , generally disgusting . breakfast bad , just cereal juice , toast and eggs . no one claimed to be in charge so no one to complain to . i rang the owner once home . no real apology , he promised to refund £10.00 on card , wow . it never did arrive of course . please do not go to this hotel ever

title: Easy and convenient stay
text: The griffin house is a very nice hotel for a short stay in London. The down side is maybe the noise, you hear the other people quite a lot. Otherwise very nice stay and a good price for a romantic weekend.

title: Short weekend Stay with great location
text: Stayed here 8th-9th December and for a good price, the hotel is in a great location off Edgware road, close to Marble arch and ideal for Hyde Park and for the shoppers next to Oxford Street. I stayed on the top floor which was for single person, room was very clean, with tv, en-suite shower and basin(small), the bedding was clean and fresh fluffy towels, the toilet is on the landing of which i knew about when i booked that didn't bother me. Reception was clean and tidy and very helpful staff, most of them are foreign workers with good English, you can leave your luggage at £2 per item was great for my last day of visit. Breakfast was Continental with bread,jams, cereal, tea, coffee, fresh juices etc...included in your price, I feel hotel is more suitable for couples, business people and singles, i didn't look at any of the family rooms so can't give any feedback on them. To sum up my stay, great hotel, clean room, friendly staff, great location would book again next time i visit London.

title: Don't Stay Here!!!!!!!!
text: They made me pay in full on arrival without even seeing the room, then the room was so full of a mildew smell my allergies immediately acted up and could not stay in that room. The room was under street so no fresh air. The sheets looked and smelt even worse, and the bathroom was a 'closet' with loads of mildew on the roof of it as it had no air in it... GROSS! After telling that I couldn't stay there, they told me no other rooms were available and that I couldn't have a refund. I paid for a room for 5 nights and couldn't even stay there. Don't stay here!

title: No Room booked!!!
text: Booked to stay at the Griffin Hotel at the weekend over from Ireland booked with Travelstay, got all the confirmations booked 2 single rooms for 3 nights, on arrive told they only had one room available so very disappointed, so spent the rest of the day, trying to find somewhere for the 3 nights, eventually found one in Holborn not where we wanted to be, not sure if it was down to Travelstay or Griffin House Hotel, but they did pay for the taxi to take us to another hotel as by that time we were very tired, and just wanted to get on with enjoying our stay in London for the weekend, so felt terribly let down. My suggestion to all is even if you do book through an agent ring the hotel direct yourself and confirm that they have the rooms booked that you require do, not assume all is ok.

title: Good for the price
text: We stayed here for the second time and was again pleased with what we got especially for the price, the location was brilliant (we were at the proms in the park) for Hyde park , the bathrooms are very small and need attention ( the receptionist when we arrived told us they are shutting down probably in January 2013 to update all the bathrooms), the rooms have been updated since we went last year and are all very clean and well fitted out. We will chose this hotel again and yes the breakfast isn't a full fried , but cereals, toast, eggs and tea or coffee is good enough choice for us and if you want bigger and better then there are plenty of places around this hotel. Staff are all friendly and willing to help.

title: Opinion of travelers
text: The location is a strong point, it is very close of the main tourist areas and of the transports. The receptionists are friendly. Our flight was only at the end of the day and they kept our luggage. The room is small but for those who only go to hotel for sleep, it is acceptable. The bathroom is really small. Weaknesses: We slept five nights and they didn’t change the towels. The breakfast is very weak, it should get true bread and have more options. We think that the price of the room with breakfast does not pay. It is preferable to book without breakfast, and eat something tastier in cafes, bakeries and supermarkets.

title: It's fine
text: Tripadvisor reviews are becoming more troubling. You can't figure out what really is going on. I start to think there is something more wrong with the reviewer than with the hotels. Griffin is a budget hotel -- on a quaint street, next to some great places in London. If it weren't for places like Griffin i'd have nowhere in London to stay. I paid 50 pounds for a basement room. It was clean. The towels were a bit worn

title: Great choice
text: This hotel is à very good choice. The staff were friendly and serviceminded. À great location and it's was clean. The breakfast was surprisningly good . The only remark we have are that the room are little to small to have an extrabed in.

title: Great, cheap and cheerful.
text: I have just spent one night at the Griffin House Hotel and thought it was great for the money. It has been refreshed....hastily and the paint job wouldn't pass close scrutiny, but now it is clean, bright and contemporary. The local Ikea must be rubbing its hands in glee because all the rooms feature Scandinavian styling. Our double bedroom was quiet, bright, small and comfortable. The refurb hasn't stretched as far as the bathroom but the shower worked well and there were good fluffy towels and complimentary toiletries. I was amazed the breakfast, cereals, yoghurts, selection of bread and cheeses, jams, eggs and tea or coffee was included in the price. The hotel needs to update its own website to reflect the changes.For a short cheap stay in London, close to the tube and shopping you can't go wrong.

title: Fair price
text: The hotel price is very good if you think that it is located less than 5 minutes (walking) from Oxford street. The room was clean and new! The breakfast was simple but enough!!

title: Small rooms but clean and close to london attractions
text: We stayed at griffen house hotel, it is colse to all attractions and Marble arch tube station, Rooms are small but have everything you need. Breakfast was not the best but there are cafes in walking distance which do breakfast. For the price i think this is a great stay. But you get what you pay for.

title: SMALL AND ANTIQUATED
text: rooms, very small access for disabled people very difficult beds unbroken, and bedding old and broken bathroom equipment broken good localization near Hyde Park unoisy

title: Good location
text: Hotel in itself was not tremendous but the location is a real advantage! Right in the city center, walking distance from Buckingham and Westminster, tube station very close. Well, just perfect for a short week-end of tourism. Apart from that, rooms were small, busy and wall paint needed refreshment. Bathroom was cold, the sink was ridiculously small and shower was degraded and not very clean (old soap bar was left on a side...) Breakfast was really simple and disappointing (only toasts and eggs, no bacon or sausages).

title: low cost, not very nice.
text: low cost with good location, terrible beds, small , boring rooms. Service was fair. Breakfast low quality.

title: Ron @ Celia From Bonnie Dundee. Opinion Of Worst Dump On Earth.
text: If this is the general standard of English,and more so,London Bed and Breakfast establishments,then,NO THANK YOU. This has to be the worst experience of a Bed and Breakfast Establishment, in my entire 62 years of living on this planet.I can `only speak for myself,and not my wife.As a Major Organ Transplant Recipient,and also a double below knee leg amputee,this is most certainly the last sort of establishment that i should within a mile of.My chances of catching an infection from this lot,was very very high.On arrival,we were asked to pay the remainder of our 2 night payment up front.We were then ushered into a back room,along beside the reception area.The first thing that met us,was an extremely vile,ghastly smell,from a burst main sewer pipe,directly outside our bedroom window.The toilet was no more disabled friendly than fly in the air.There was no room to open 2 suitcases,unless you used the top of the bed.No kettle in the room to make tea or coffee.There was not even 1 seat on view.But of course the room was too small for one, anyhow.Then there was the dangerous,steep, filthy,stairway,down into what they describe as the breakfast room.Quite frankly,our 2 wee staffy doggies eat in a far superior eating area, than what we had here.My wife asked for corn flakes.The young man who served us,must have emptied the entire contents into her bowl.He maybe thought that we were staying away from the premises for a month.She also asked for toast,which surprise, surprise,she is still waiting for,and we have been back home in Dundee now for 5 days.I asked for scrambled egg and toast.It was in front of me within a minute.This must be a world record.But alas,the bread was barely lukewarm,which can hardly be described as toast.The scrambled egg was barely edible.We were planning a 2 night stay,as we had laid down a deposit for it.But,we decided to head back to Bonnie Dundee,Pronto.I demanded a refund for the night we cancelled.After a bit of discussion with the receptionist,who eventually telephoned the owner,i was then handed the refund. What is even more unbelievable,is that Ex-Prime Minister,Tony Blair,lives within a stones throw from this pathetic place,with a 24 hour armed guard !! My advice to anyone planning to book up, in this run down premises,is,LOOK ELSEWHERE.

title: Great location
text: I have stayed here twice when travelling to London to go to concerts at Hyde Park. This hotel is in a perfect location for Hyde Park / Central London. The hotel is cheap and I'm afraid it seems quite run down, needs money spending on it to attract repeat business for people who need it for more than just sleeping in, which is all I needed. I would not recommend this hotel unless all you need is a great location and not bothered about size of rooms, or pristine cleanliness. On subsequent trips I have now found better hotels not far away in Sussex Gardens which are not much more expensive and definitely better run.

title: Griffin house london- A complete tip!!
text: This is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in!! It was absolutly filthy and grubby. There are 57 steps in the hotel which is completely useless for a disabled person like myself.When at the top of the narrow stairs to enter my room there was a decorators ladder blocking the passage way! Furthermore the road outside the hotel is extemely busy and hard to get across.The paint in the hotel was peeling and plaster was falling from the ceiling!! The webiste is very misleading as the hotel does not live up to the pictures posted and makes a false claim that the rooms have tea making facilities, which it does not! This hotel should be closed down by the trading standards, as in my eyes and i am sure in a lot of other previous guests eyes this hotel is not fit to be trading or putting up guests! J.A.

title: Best to avoid
text: We are small, but we couldn't move anywhere in the room without knocking into something. The bathroom must have the tiniest sink I've ever seen! We had the basement room - fabulous view (see photo)! Breakfast was until 09:30. 1st morning, we presented ourselves at 09:15. They weren't very happy. No sooner had they given us the breakfast (rather pitiful!) than we were told to hurry up! The 2nd morning, we went early, but we had to wait (they only had 3 tables!). Then, they had the cheek to tell us to hurry up again! When I told them it wasn't our fault that we had to wait, I was told to try to understand them! On the final morning, a guest obviously couldn't put up with the breakfast any longer, so he asked if he could have 3 cups of tea to bring up to his room. Well, the lady attending to him wasn't very happy, to say the least. The conversation, bordering on argument, lasted about 10 minutes! And the reason? They didn't have enough cups! Conclusion: Go somewhere else!

title: We love London but not this hotel!!
text: First of all there shouldn´t be any room in the basement. We had a triple room (no 1). The view from the window was to stairs leading to the street above. The stairs were used by the staff and we couldn´t get the wooden blind down, needed some help with it, and it was all covered with dust. It couldn´t be kept up if you wanted to keep your privacy. During the night there was noise coming probably from the reception and we couldn´t sleep well after about 5 am. The smell coming from the airfreshener in the toilet was awful. It was perhaps trying to keep away the smell of the mould without succeeding to do so. Luckily we got another room from the second floor (no 11). It was a bit better. The toilet basins were too small to be able to wash your face without wetting the whole toilet. The carpets should be cleaned properly and it would be nice if the walls were painted. The stairs are so narrow and steep and I think that to elderly people they are too much to handle. No tea-making facility in rooms as was mentioned in booking.com -pages. Also you´ll have to pay in advance the whole stay. The positive things are free internet access though it didn´t work always, TV, which didn´t work properly either, clean beddings and warm water in the shower. The room was also very warm (if not too warm) during the night (stayed in April). The window could be opened in our second room which was great after staying in the basement. The location of course was great!!! You ought to do something to the breakfastroom also, not very practical and the kitchen didn´t look very hygienic at all. Breakfast was ok. The staff was nice though the lady in the reception didn´t seem to like her job very much. The hotel is ok for a short visit cos you aren´t really spending your time there but if you are going to stay a bit longer we recommend another hotel.

title: Griffin House - more like doss-house
text: My daughter and I have just returned from two nights stay in room 9!! Wish we had read reviews before we went. Felt slightly ill at ease when asked to pay balance on arrival at the somewhat scruffy reception - why oh why didn't I ask to see the room first!!! This "hotel" is absolutely dire - I hope they use our £85 per night charge to buy a new bed and some desperately needed paint. I take issue with some of the reviews which justify the disgusting conditions at this hotel because it is cheap - firstly I don't think it was cheap and secondly soap and water don't cost much so there is no excuse for this hotel to be so dirty. The only reason we stayed was because the sheets were clean and we were only there for a very short space of time. Furniture was old, grubby and damaged - we didn't even unpack - as the drawers were very grubby inside. Paint and plaster coming off the walls dirt on the skirting boards inches thick, the bedside lamp was vile - even after a shower you felt grubby due to the surroundings. There were no tea and coffee making facilities - probably just as well really!!! We used the deli on the corner for a late cuppa. Looked into the breakfast room on the first morning but turned tail and preferred to go and pay for breakfast - bit annoying really when you have already paid for it. Second morning decided to brave breakfast - well cup of tea really before heading off. When I say cup of tea I mean half a cup of hot water with tea bag on the side - no pot or top ups here - half a cup that's your whack. A bowl of pre-poured cornflakes was planted in front of my daughter (you didn't even have portion control) and two slices of "toast" was plonked in front of me - don't expect a toast rack or your toast in nice triangles. Don't expect "would you like anything else, is everything ok for you" - they don't ask because they really, really don't want the answers!!! It's location is extremely good and for London the price is competitive, however I have stayed in places far cheaper with excellent breakfast, friendly staff and delightful rooms - there is no excuse for this place - it is an absolute disgrace, Big Issue sellers would turn their noses up at this one. Come on Griffin House - clean up your act and give your guests a decent experience - you put London and the rest of the UK to utter shame. You should be ashamed of yourselves what an impression to give travellers - disgraceful. DO NOT STAY HERE NO MATTER HOW DESPERATE YOU ARE - THIS PLACE IS JUST AWFUL.

title: worst hotel ever stayed in
text: very small dark room, room was dirty and smelly, shower was hanging of the wall, loose broken tiles on floor and walls. Needs updating. Electric sockets not working would advise anybody not to stay here, or you will regret it!!!!!

title: Shabby chic it wasnt - just shabby!!
text: We only stayed one night thank goodness. The hotel was very shabby, noisy and the room was incredibly hot and very small. No tea/coffee making facilities in the room and not even a glass for some water. The shower fittings were hanging off the wall and although the room wasnt dirty the shower was mouldy and the hand basin the size of a tea cup!!. Breakfast was an interesting experience - warm orange juice and a choice of scrambled, fried or boiled egg (yes one egg!) cold toast and coffee (I think it was coffee) For the £115 we paid for the room we definately wont be going back again. Alot of TLC is needed by the owner and a course in customer service would be worth the investment for the staff!!!

title: be aware of hanging/ trailing wires....and that's just to start!
text: My my.... what a place, and i sincerely wish I meant that in a good way! After finding the hotel, which was central to Marble Arch and pretty much ideal, our group of 5 arrived to check in and our reservation had been messed up, instead of a triple and 2 singles (this was all they had available at time of booking) we had been reserved a double and 2 singles. The best they could offer was to put a 'camp bed' into the double room (i suggested the possibility of upgrading a single to another double and was met with a very un- friendly huff). Seeing as we had no- where else to go and needed to be at a theatre show for the evening, we agreed. No lift and 3 flights of stairs later- 1 flight to the top floor was steep and very un-forgiving with suitcases and wearing heels, we arrived to our rooms. The 'now' triple was cramped and to get into bed you had sit at the bottom of the bed and crawl up, the bathroom door was off the hinges, cracked tiles and a sink you could barely wash your face in. One single was not actually that bad, except the shower knob came off in your hand and the other single room was hysterical... a shower in the cupboard (literally), wires hanging from the tv around the satellite box (that fell off onto me) leads across the floor and of course the bag over the smoke alarm. Receptionist as apologetic as ever... yeah right! Didn't even attempt to try and figure out what was on the breakfast menu! Thank goodness we were only staying for 1 night... oh, and for great friends that made the whole escapade hysterically amusing and a great night out!

title: Not that bad to be honest.
text: After reading some of the reviews on this site I was a bit worried about what we were going to find when we arrived at the hotel, but I was pleasantly surprised. Basically my girlfriend, myself and one of her friends needed a hotel room fairly close to Hyde Park so they could do the Walk The Walk Moonwalk for charity, since they would be walking at night only myself would be sleeping in the room overnight but they still needed somewhere to get ready during the day and when they returned from the walk. Our room (number 8) had one double bed and one single bed, it was on the first floor and faced out towards the rear of the building, view wasn't brilliant but it's London, if you want a fancy view pay two or three times the price!! The room was clean and tidy, bit cramped for three people but it never caused an issue. The double bed was extremely comfortable but I never checked the single bed. Due to time pressing on we couldn't make it to breakfast so I cannot comment on that either. Yes there wasn't tea making facilities in our room but since I don't drink the stuff it didn't bother me at all. If I'm being hyper critical the toilet roll holder was missing from the wall....but is that the end of the world? No. Given the price we paid for a 3 bed room in London on a weekend and it's location I cannot see what all the fuss is about with other reviews, and I didn't see anything that would put me off using this establishment again in the future.

title: Good Budget Priced Hotel
text: For the price we paid it was good value for money, the rooms were clean and cleaned each day.The location is excellent for sight seeing of London

title: Enough for a one week City Trip
text: The Leisure Inn is a small Hotel close to the Hyde Park in the Bayswater area. It is clean and the breakfast was ok. For a one week city trip it is absolutely enough. I spent one week there in May and I would go back to this place. From this location you can reach a lot by walk.

title: Fulfilled all our needs
text: Location was brilliant, nice continental breakfast, room was fine with piping hot shower and comfortable beds. Highly recommend if you're looking for a low cost stay near the centre of London. Wifi was available for only £5 per stay.

title: Perfect budget break
text: Booked this as part of a theatre package with lastminute at truly the last minute. I stayed by myself. It's in a great location (near Paddington and Hyde Park) and in a pretty pleasant area (lots of other hotels) away from busy roads. Was slightly unnerved by the need to leave a £30 cash deposit on check-in (in case of damages / thefts) and half expected to come back to the room to find the towels had "disappeared" and would lose the deposit Thankfully that was just my paranoia and I got the deposit back without any problem. The room (number 15) was in the basement but had a window. A good triple room. Furnished a bit like a travel lodge, i.e. modern and functional

title: Comfortable
text: We stayed in this hotel it is located very central rooms are small but comfortable breakfast is very basic we had a problem with the first roo we were given but we had no problem with the staff we were given another room which was beautiful with hesitation

title: Smallest rooms ever.
text: When I mean small I mean it. You have to step outside to change your mind. I think my laptop screen was bigger than the tiny tv. Maybe it was the cocoon or womb like feeling but I did have a terrific sleep there. The bed was good and the pillows soft. Lots of hot water but nothing pretty and not the cleanest. We left our luggage while we explored more of the city for the day and came back in the evening to collect it. The luggage lockup is close to the desk but they give any one the key so you know. It was half the price of the other 3 hotels in the area so we picked it because we only needed a place to sleep for the one night. If you're looking for a cheap place to sleep, it works.

title: Room 308- tiny hot double room -good for smaller people & max 2 days stay
text: Room 308-3rd floor -room facing south-good for those who alre always cold because this room is so warm (no airconditioning) that we slept with a wide open window, in our underwear and only covered by a bed sheet and it was still warm (even if it was cold and raining outside) The room itself is the tiniest room ever (probably because they built in a bathroom) The bed is too soft and too small (narrow and short-not advised for anyone taller than 180cm) , but bearable for 2 days. It is said that the hotel was refurbished but it looks a bit run down. I saw two tiny ants in the bathroom but that did not bother me. The water in the shower was warm but if you want to cool of with cold wather after walking hte whole day in 25C it is not possible because it never goes cold (again good for someone that is always cold Breakfast was very asketic-you get couple of warm toasts, have 3 different cereals, boiled egg and few spreads. coffee and tea. Not good for people who like to eat a lot in the morning. The elevator was ok. The staff was robotic, no emotions-probably on minimum wage. Room cleanliness was ok.

title: Avoid this place like the plague
text: My partner and I wanted somewhere close as we were going to Nottinghill Carnival. All I needed was a clean room with a bath . Not much to ask . That room was a box with curtains hanging off , dirty bedding not to mention dangerous lighting as the lamps by the bed were falling off the wall . One was even stained with what looked like blood from the last visitor . When we didn't see any bath we thought "that's it , they put us in the wrong room " . When we try to sort it out we are told there are no baths in the whole "hotel " and it was booking . Com fault for confirming something they don't have. The continental breakfast was bread, plastic cheese and tinned fruit cocktail. Not a croissant in sight . Barring the amazing Carnival I've never been so glad to get home and bathe after sleeping on our towels for two nights . This place should come with a health warning!

title: Acceptable
text: The hotel is acceptable for a short stay, location is very good. Good restaurants, ATM nearby and Underground station Queens Way (central line) within 7 min walk. Not very expensive and it is good value for the money. Nice people in the reception

title: Family from Sweden
text: This was the Third time we visit London in a year, and gave this Hotel a second chance in oct 2011, as we wasnt so happy after the first time a year earlier. The first time the whole family of 5 people had to wait nearly an hour for the taxi that the hotel was suposed to send. The kids got a drafty room, from the window, and we, the parents, where every morning woken by the kitchen staff one floor down. Anyway the next time, april 2011, we asked if we could have a specific room, the answer was NO ! = Bad service, so that time we found a good price on a Hilton Hotel and at the same price as this hotel so look around before you decide. In october 2011, we tried again, = BAD idea. The New Mercedes that the Hotel then showed on the homepage as their new Taxi, was instead a old Volkswagen with old papers on the floor, and you guessed right, again we had to wait for it for one hour on Heathrow airport. Got another small room then the one we had before, lucky us :-( , and the bed placed in a room suited for a single bed, was in the form of an old hammock so the back wasnt any happy after the nights. Asked the manager of a refund of the Taxifair, because of the waitingtime that could have taken us in to the hotel by the tube and a lot cheaper, and because of the bad advertising on the class of transport. But the manager since many years couldnt care less and the bad offer he gave isnt worth mention (and we didnt take it as it was more as a big joke) ! So find another Hotel in London, this isnt worth your money!

title: Not impressed
text: I was planning on going to BST concert in Hyde Park and booked a single room well ahead of time. When I arrived I was told that there was a problem and they didn't have a room for me but they'd booked me into another hotel near Earl's Court. I was tired, hot and sweaty and in no mood to journey across London to another hotel when I'd specifically wanted one close to the concert as I was travelling alone. After much arguing I was eventually given a room with two single beds, French doors/windows which couldn't'be closed/locked and one of the curtains was hanging off the rail so they couldn't be closed properly. Bathroom was tiny but decent enough. Room was very stuffy and I was awoken at about 5am by light streaming in through torn curtains. Didn't bother with breakfast - there was a nice cafe down the road - and staff hardly bothered to acknowledge me when I checked out. Oh, and there were a load of old mattresses in the stairwell too which were probably a fire hazard.

title: Great hotel for a cheap price!
text: I stayed here in September just for a leisure trip with my mum! This is a great hotel for money the rooms are clean and bedding. Quiet and peaceful. The hotel is just beside Kensington palace and right beside the station. We found it a really good location hotel and value for money :)

title: Lucked out
text: When we got there, there had been a leak the night before and one of the quad rooms were out of commission. We were given the choice to staying at the hotel or at a 2 bedroom flat nearby. Well, we chose the flat which was beautiful and very large. (Only the kitchen needed some work, the rest of the place was great) We had a terrace, huge windows, and great comfortable beds. With 2 boys, aged 15 and 12, the space was appreciated. We walked to the hotel for breakfast, which I enjoyed, my kids found the food a bit boring. The location was great. We were right near the tube, the rail station, and many conveniences. The famous Peter Pan statue was right inside the nearby gate to Hyde Park. All in all, I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: Slightly better than London's Victoria Hotels... I think.
text: Ahh London. One of the worlds most beautiful & EXPENSIVE cities! Perhaps the best advice I can give is that you typically get what you pay for in this city. To get what would be your average no thrills hotel in most cities (aside from Tokyo) expect to pay about $200 plus per night. Keeping that and the exchange rate in perspective you can see why these hotels usually get such terrible ratings... that and the fact that they would probably be already have gone out of business in most other cities. Location wise its fantastic. I typically stay in the Victoria area and as my hotel experiences couldn't get much worse than there, I decided to give the Paddington area a try. Paddington Station is a 5-10min walk. Paddington Station is where the Heathrow express arrives (15min journey from Heathrow to Paddington Station for about twenty pounds one way) and the regular Heathrow Train (25min journey for about 9 pounds one way). The walk to the hotel is very simple if you take down directions or a cab fare would probably be about 5 pounds, maybe less. All tube stations seem to be a 5-10 min walk (Paddington or Queensway) and Kennsington Park is a 5 min walk or less. The hotel receptionists were friendly enough and check in was fine. The hotel does provide free and reasonable safe locked luggage storage in a cupboard adjacent to the front desk. You can purchase internet for an hour or a day at the front desk. Think it was around 8-10 pounds for 24hrs. The ensuite room was located in the basement (as most cheaper expedia bookings seem to be) and is a typical tiny London room. The room comes complete with a wardrobe, desk and chair, tv with a few channels (the typical tv remote that apparently works for a tv in some other in the building but not the one in your room) double or twin beds, night stand and barely room to move. The room did come with a small safe and seemed reasonably clean. Bewarned the walls are thin in this hotel! You will hear your neighbors if you have any and they will hear you. On my first morning there I had the pleasure of bring woken up at 530am by a drunken lady screaming into her phone to her mother about helping the children of Egypt after what apparently was a great night out on the town. How do I know all this about a phone conversation having nothing to do with me you ask? As I said the walls are very VERY thin apparently. I am not sure who was more relived when her credit ran out... her mother or myself. I am still not sure if this woman was screaming outside the bedroom door, in the room next door or if she had somehow snuck into my room and was standing with a megaphone at the bottom of my bed. But you get the point. If this woman isn't still around for your 530am wake up call, never fear the many children in the hotel will be up screaming and tearing around the place slamming doors by about 730am. And if this still doesn't rose you out of bed the silent knocking maid with the ability to open a door faster than the speed of light will surely have you up by 10am latest. And yes she did this both days. I was beginning to question if she has a side job with Inquirer to try to get surprise photos. The ensuite bathroom was better than most I have seen in London, even despite the cracked tiles in one area. It apparently had been recently renovated and is refreshingly clean. Plenty of warm water and water pressure. This is not something I am used to in London. Typically I feel like I am attempting a shower out of a frozen garden watering can. So that was a pleasant surprise. Also the shower drain actually drained. Another first in a cheap London hotel for me. Often I emerge from the shower to make my way across a swamp only to find it flooding into my bedroom as well. Do be sure to keep their towels tidy as the sign says or they will happily charge you a 10 pound fee. After the cracked tiles on the floor stained the bathmat towel I had a note awaiting me in my room informing me of a 10 pound charge for replacement. Upon showing the desk clerk that their floor tile was cracked and that is where the stain came from (and that I don't infact wear industrial strength rust on my face as makeup) the charge was dropped. It is a bit comical that they would charge 10 pounds for their towels as even in their brand new towel days I doubt they ever saw 10 pounds. I never tried the hotel breakfast but there is a great little cafe down the same street heading towards Kennsington Park that had a great 4.99 pound traditional English breakfast and other delicious choices as well. So overall location is great, the hotel is better than many I have experienced in Victoria area and just keep in mind you get what you pay for in London and many of the buildings in this city are quite old and cramped which is part of what makes it such a great place and makes finding a descent affordable room so challenging.

title: Excellent
text: Superb value for money. Very comfortable, very clean, great bathroom. I had a single room which is quite small but larger than other single rooms in the same area. Very quiet and staff were great. I can totally recommend and will be staying again in a couple of months.

title: the worst!!!
text: I booked this hotel last minute, I was looking for something closer to Paddington Station. The priced they charge for 2 nights was $753. I know hotels in London are expensive but for this hotel, it is NOT worth that at all. The room is dirty, and old! The mattress is very old and sagging. I can feel the spring inside! The small refrigeration they advertised online was not working. Breakfast that was supposed to come with had 2 kinds of cereal and toast. By far the worst hotel I have ever stayed at.

title: Average hotel/nice neighbourhood
text: The hotel is in pretty decent place - near Hyde park. A 25 min walk distance from Victoria Coach station. The reception staff is nice, room was average, the windows don't open up properly and you can hear your neighbours talking all the time, TV was lagging all the time. Breakfast was very poor. Just some toasts, eggs and peanut butter. So if you want a place just to crash at night - it's a decent option. If you want a good breakfast and quiet surroundings - better choose another hotel.

title: worst ever

Bathroom is so tiny you could,nt shower & then dry youself in the bathroom without hitting the walls & basin.The room also smelt damp. Tv did,nt work properly.

title: Not fit for purpose
text: Visited the leisure inn for a three day trip with family. This hotel is not fit to be open. There is numerous building work going on, with carpets torn, plaster on the floor and holes in walls. Stay clear of this place, it’s cheap for a reason. Pay a bit extra as this is one of the worst hotels in London.

title: Nice, just needs some TLC
text: Nice size room downstairs. Room was mostly clean and tidy but carpet needs fitting properly and tiles in bathroom on floor are broken and sharp on edges. Otherwise perfectly adequate room for the need & budget. Will be staying again soon, also excellent location to underground.

title: Do Not Stay Here!
text: Worst hotel experience i've ever had. I booked the room with a double bed within a weeks notice. When I got to the room it was tiny, and they'd given us a twin single room. I went back to the reception to complain but they didnt have any double rooms left. The receptionist was extremely unhelpful. There were stains on the wall above the headspace on the bed, and the room was very shabby and out-dated.

title: dont be fooled
text: Dont be fooled by the entrance of this property. It looks so modern when you come in off the street.The rooms are digusting, the carpet is filty, and the price was ridiculous. The bathroom was cleanish, but towels old and stained. We paid $600 for 4 nights and only stayed for 2, We were given a basement room with the lift next to it, noise from the motor was awful. We were moved, but that room didnt have a fridge, and was just as bad. The location is quite good, but that doesnt make up for the condition of the place. Had two weeks in different hotels every night, most were cheaper than this and 10 times the quality. Very very desappointed.

title: Cheap, cheerful, clean and convenient
text: This hotel s pretty much what you'd expect from this part of London. Above all it is good value. The location is very convenient and walkable between the Bayswater and Paddington underground stations. The rooms are small but clean and newly painted. The WiFi worked well...

title: Acceptable if you’re just looking for a place to sleep
text: Not very good, the customer service wasn’t the best, and it seemed old and little tended to. The room was small, and their definition of a twin bed was two single beds with two inches of space between. Didn’t even try the breakfast, it didn’t look very inviting. A bit of a distance to walk to the underground, but the area was okay. There is a nice bakery to have breakfast at close by. And the bathroom was nice.

title: POLICE HAD TO BE CALLED
text: Where do I begin? This hotel has to be the worst ever. Booked online and paid the whole amount for 6 nights. When I got there, staff said - You have only paid for 1 night and you now have to pay the rest. They asked for my passport to hold in the safe while I sorted this out. At the end of the stay, I arranged a payment online and they still refused to give me my passport back. One of their directors 'Micheal' who told me on the phone 'I am a lawyer' told me your passport has been removed from the hotel. Thats when I called in the Met Police. They came at midnight and demanded to know where the passport was. After 1 hour of being mucked around by the management and staff, police threatened to close the entire hotel down, arrest the staff on suspicion of theft and call in the Anti Terrorism squad as a UK passport had gone missing. One of the directors said his son was in possession of the passport and could not be awoken, because he had been studying for his A levels all day. Suddenly, my passport appears after all this. I am now considering legal action against this company if I do not receive adequate compenstation for the removal of my passport from the hotel. I will also be applying to have this companies licence to operate a hotel removed. The management of this hotel is a joke.

title: DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL, (DISGUSTING)
text: this hotel is disgusting and the service is terrible the staff dont give a [--]. when we booked this hotel through lastminute it showed some really nice pics of the hotel we got a shock when we arrived, the room we got given was so small and dirty it was unreal i woulnt keep my pet rat in that hotel, when we tried to complain the staff just said there was no manager to speak to. absolute shocking service this hotel wants shutting down!!!!!!!!!!!!

title: Husband and I like this hotel - we always stay here when we visit London
text: The Leisure Inn is in a great location - near Hyde park, tube. transport, etc. It's my first choice when we stay in London. Okay, the rooms are small, the bathroom teeny, the decor a little shabby, but we always manage to get bargain prices, and we enjoy our stay - the breakfast is decent, and everything is satisfactory and value for money.

title: Poor Customer Service!!!!!!!!
text: So we arrived and the receptionist was unbelievably rude, made us feel unwelcome. Everything was too much hassle. It seems that booking.com had booked us in without taking our card details (not our problem) so the receptionist told us off like a head teacher speaking to children!! The room was very basic which is what we expected considering the price. The price included breakfast, wish we hadn't bothered!! Breakfast is surreal. Cold, hard boiled eggs placed in a basket on top of a microwave, cold toast and a choice of cereal, that's as far as it goes. Anyway, we started by getting some coffee and orange juice, which was removed from the table when we ventured over to the 'buffet'. We were looking for a cheap place to stay. If you're looking for somewhere to stay for more than one night then seriously don't bother. The lady on reception ruined the whole experience from the word go, if she hadn't been such an issue I'm sure the entire experience would have been different.

title: Good location and very cheap
text: I stopped here for one night with my Dad when we travelled to London for a concert. It's in a great location and was very cheap. We booked a twin room but we had one double and a single which was a bonus for my Dad who stretched out in the double! Our room was clean and modern - although we didn't inspect mattresses like other reviewers, but the bedding was clean and fresh. Our TV didn't seem to work but we weren't fussed (we may have just not been able to work it!). We didn't spend much time at the hotel as we just needed a place to sleep after the concert, but the time we spent in the room was pleasant. The bed was comfy, I slept well and the room temperature was good. Breakfast was disappointing, though it's included in the price so understandable. It's not a cooked breakfast or continental, but just some cereals, tinned fruit, cheese slices, toast, jam, chocolate spread and some hard boiled eggs, along with tea, coffee and orange juice. The staff were polite and helpful, they allow you to store bags for the day after checking out too. Unfortunately the wifi in the rooms costs, but in reception it's free. It's good for what it is. I wouldn't recommend it for long stays or if you're wanting to spend a lot of time in your hotel room. But it's great for a short break and it's in a good location for tourists. Glad we came here over the Travelodge and it was a fraction of the price!

title: Spend a little more and get something else
text: I booked this hotel as I wanted something central and cheap, as I knew I would only be in the hotel a few hours. The 'Leisure Inn' however was noisy, dirty and the workmen started the noise of drills etc. outside my room quite early in the morning. When I asked if they had wifi I had to buy a £5 card that didn't work, when I asked at reception they told me to wait for the manager and only he knew how to work it. For budget accommodation next time, I would probably travel out of central London if this is what you get!

title: The worst hotels I have ever scene
text: We had to drop our stuff and go so when we got back to the hotel I checked the mattress and it was so disgusting, it was alll yellowed, had stains, and was torn up and when I told the from guy he refused to call a manager because they don't answer and then he told us after we decided to check out because on top of the mattress all the pillows had stains on them, he wouldn't sleep in them and that we'd have to come back the next day somewhere between nine and ten to catch a manager. title: Horrible.
text: After staying in many hotels, b&bs and hostels this dump needs to be closed down. Faulty tower Inn! Staff were rude, poor English, no electricity in 1 of our rooms so a friend had to be moved to a different hotel and not as much as a sorry. Smell of gas or sewage around the basement floor was disgusting. Breakfast room had ants everywhere. Was never so happy to check out after 2 nights of torture! Save yourself and stay somewhere else.

title: Too hot and get the decorators in.
text: We stayed here due to its proximity to Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens as we were attending the BST music festival. It was very handily placed in that respect. It was also handy for the shops, bars and eating places on Queensway where there are also two subway stations On the plus side the staff that I encountered were friendly and helpful where they could be except for when we asked for morning call which never came, fortunately we had woken in time but in pools of perspiration and were wringing our pillows out. After seeing photos on review sites I feared the worst. We had room 204 at the front on the second floor. It had double opening bay windows but you had to stand on the bed and reach over the headboard to open them. The weather was very hot but it was impossible to sleep with windows open due to outside noise, a fan would have helped as there is never going to be air con. Our room was at least cleanish with a decent sized bed and just enough room to swing a cat without bashing its brains in on the walls. The carpet had a few marks but nothing too suspicious. We also had a spiders web on the corner of the front and side walls which was there for the whole of our stay, perhaps it was a permanent resident with immunity from a duster. There was what appeared to be newly tiled bathroom with a good shower, new sink and loo but that had to be sat on sideways due to a large towel rail. There is practically no wardrobe space just a small rail with 3 hangers. There is a kettle and tea and coffee things and a small TV. The breakfast was cereal or toast in an inadequate basement dining room. The self service area was in the worst possible place and needs moving next to the small kitchen. The seating is woefully inadequate when everyone descends on it. I know that these places get a lot of traffic but it needs an urgent overhaul in decorating and re-carpeting in the corridors and please discard the filthy settee in reception. I doubt that I would ever return.

title: A DUMP!!!
text: DO NOT stay here!!! I stayed at this hotel as it was in close proximity to Hyde Park for the BST Festival, because I was on a fixed budget of less than a £100 to spend on a Hotel room and this hotel, if you can call it that, was nothing short of a dump!! I had a very small pokey room, of which none of the lights worked, no air conditioning considering it was extremely hot weather, the breakfast was disgusting(there was orange SQUASH instead of JUICE!!) and I almost broke my neck on some steps!! DO NOT STAY HERE!!!

title: Disgusting
text: I have never written, a review on trip adviser but after my experience here i had to. My mum booked a family room for her, i and my two daughters 11 and 7. The first room we were given was freezing cold and the wall surrounding the window was covered in mould! We wanted to leave straight away , but after a long journey and with two children we decided to complain and get a different room....the customer service was poor but just about acceptable at this point and we were offered another room that 'would be warmer' this room turned out to stink of drains to the point of making us gag and the heating was obviously turned up to full...we obviously left but the customer service was shocking never experienced anything like this and both myself and mother have stayed in many bed and breakfast's in London. Do not book in!!!!

title: Not Very Nice, Avoid Room 18 At All Costs !!!
text: This hotel is in terrible condition and despite being a budget hotel I think some of the issues that we encountered may have even bordered on health and safety / environmental health issues. Everything in the bathroom was supplied with red hot water, I don't even think there was a cold water supply to the room, even the toilet cistern was red hot ! Massive damp patch outside the toilet door that looks like it’s been left neglected for a long time as the door / door frame has started to rot. The room itself was red hot although for a budget hotel I don't expect AC they could have left a fan in the room at least. The hotel is very outdated and felt very dirty, there are marks on every wall on all of the corridors and in the room. Thankfully we only really needed somewhere to get our head down for the night and left promptly the next morning as I didn't fancy breakfast after spending the night with the cockroach. I've attached some pictures of the defects and the cockroach. Hope this helps you make up your mind when booking a budget hotel in London.

title: good location and that's it!

Breakfast should be between 7:30 to 9:30 a.m., but you have to reserve just 20 minutes in the night before. And it was so bad and poor, it resumed to some grains, yogurt, coffee, tea, toast, jams, cheese and boiled egg. I'd like to not have at all. The cleaning as well wasn't good. I drank tea one night and the cup wasn't change in the next day. I advise to NOT choose this hotel at least you don't have other choice. Terrible!

I would never stay here again if my life depended on it.

title: Shoe Box Room.....
text: Assumed room would be small as space is at a premium in London, but was shocked at how small. I had a double and was staying by myself but still had to move things out of way so I could navigate around room. Wasn't sure if I was overreacting so went and had a mosey at couple of other hotels in area as will coming back to London later in year, and rooms I looked at were far superior for about same price. Great location near bayswater tube and stacks of great eating places close by, but that's about it. Went down for breakfast twice and didn't eat either time, just wanted fruit but was big bowl of canned fruit, and dining room was packed despite having to book in each night prior to make sure there's room....,

title: Just what i needed
text: Great location, staff really friendly. Price is really good , I really liked a room , all clean and in really good condition. Breakfast was simple but that what i was expecting. Will return again and recommend to my friends!

title: Great value! Excellent location and everything was perfect!
text: I stayed here on recommendation as I took a couple of days off to go sight-seeing. The hotel was clean, comfortable and the staff were helpful. For the price, it was excellent. Queensway is about 1 minute away (superb choice of restaurants for dining out, or for breakfast) and it was an easy stroll across Hyde Park to the museums. Wonderful!

title: Pleasant hotel in the heart of London
text: At first glance, seems like a pleasant and decently priced hotel close to Queensway. Room a bit small, no bedlamp, need an extra pillow, but it will hopefully be quiet.

title: Small single rooms and sub-standard breakfast
text: Stayed at this place in September 2016. Good location as it’s in Bayswater and near Hyde Park, Marble Arch and Oxford Street. Breakfast is sub-standard and there is a charge of five pounds for the Wi-Fi password. If you have no choice, only then stay at this place.

title: Worst Hotel Ever
text: Don't stay here. My room was underground. No air conditioning. Sticky floors. I've stayed in a lot of outback hotels across Australia and am pretty hardy but this hotel was disgusting. Spend your money elsewhere.

title: Bad hotel
text: Stayed at the Leisure Inn in the Bayswater area of London. Pretty poor hotel. Minute rooms and totally cramped facilities. TV didn't work, no proper wardrobe and dirty. We checked out after our first night and lost several hundreds of pounds, as any refund was totally refused. Asked for the owner, Mr Ali, but he was never available.

title: A Pleasant Surprise!
text: Upon arriving to the Leisure Inn my mom and I were impressed by the reception area (which was nearly twice that of the other hotel we'd just come from and very modern looking) as well as the comparatively "spacious" elevator! The hotel was very clean and the staff were friendly and helpful. The room was, as always, rather small but for two people it sufficed. Breakfast was satisfactory as well, consisting of toast and cereal as well as coffee/tea/juice. The only negative was the shower. Not only was there no pressure but the actual amount of water that came out of it was very little. In fairness, it appeared the showers were in the midst of being replaced so perhaps this problem will no longer exist. Overall though, a cozy little hotel in a quiet neighbourhood but still quite close to Paddington Station. This hotel is a steal of a deal!
