title: Only for sleeping
text: To be honest, we just slept and took showers in this hotel. It was the only purpose of our stay. We spent two nights, left really early and came back late. We booked last minute, so we were in the basement room and definitely payed too much, but well, London is expensive. The bathroom was tiny, but bed was comfortable. The neighborhood was gorgeous, very safe and the hotel is located a few blocks from the tube station. Service could definitely improve. Wouldn't stay here again, just save yourself and book early in a better hotel for the same price.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: Our friend booked this room for us via another site, laterooms.com. It was very last minute so according to that website the room we got usually goes for 300 pounds and we got it for 85 pounds. The receptionists were friendly, the room was small with 3 single beds and a small bathroom but it was all very clean . There was a tiny hanging area, a small tv and tea and coffee making facilities which I thought was a nice touch. Continental breakfast was included which was quite good (toast, cereal, boiled eggs, coffee and juice etc). They have a pay as you go internet kiosk in reception. It was conveniently located, easy walking distance to Bayswater Station and lots of convenience stores (SPAR, Tescos) as well as Boots, Superdrug, a post office and lots of places to eat and a couple of pubs. Having stayed at Lords Hotel which is on the other side of the tube station I would prefer this place (see my other review) for the price. I've read the other reviews of this place and am surprised as I don't have anything to complain about so I guess we lucked out!

title: Clean, large room for the price
text: Stayed here once before, and this time it was just as nice, if not better. The room was clean, the beds were nice, breakfast was fine. overall, for the price, which was less than £50 a room, it was great. The location is good as well, as it's so close to the circle line, where most things are. The only bad thing was that i though the batheroom was tiny.

title: Clean and a good price
text: For London, this was a very good price - £206.10 for 2 people in a twin-bedded room for 4 nights. `So the fact that there were drawbacks was to be expected - the room was cramped, and the bathroom tiny. But it was clean and serviced each day - and we were out most of the time, so the size didn't really matter. Breakfast was hostel-style - grab your own cereal, cheese, toast, eggs, coffee and so on. The eggs and the cheese were probably the best part of the meal. While there is a lift, it is pretty rickety, and I was glad to reach my floor each time I went in it. The only real complaint was the noise made by people coming in in the early hours of the morning - our room was next to the lift, and the walls must be paper-thin ... Oh, and there is no free wifi, and the available service wasn't pay-as-you-go - it was quite an expensive rate per 24 hours - whether or not you used it. (I used Skype on my tablet, which was a much cheaper option.)

title: Cheap but poor
text: Great location, horrible small rooms, poor breakfast, but all at a great price. Close to the underground station and retail store. Wi-Fi not available at rooms for free, though there's a computer you can use in the lobby. Smoking area is actually a table on the street.

title: Sets the standard for budget hotels in London
text: A real gem - and the rarest of things - a genuine bargain in central London. OK - so I got a 'credit crunch' bargain price in the middle of January, but even if I'd paid 3- 4X what I did, there would have been no complaints. Having booked a double room, I got a huge (for London) 4-berth room (double and two single beds). The room was spotless, the linen clean and fresh and enough little touches (recessed spotlights/pictures and mirrors/a small fridge/tea & coffee facilites) to make it feel like a higher star rated room. The bed was one of the most comfortable hotel beds I've ever slept in and although the bathroom was small (1metre by 3metres), it was also spotless, nicely tiled and the shower was hot and powerful. Not only that - the television has a decent selection of channels and a remote control that actually worked. A miracle. Breakfast was included in the knockdown price - basic but the toast was freshly made on arrival, and the staff were friendly and helpful. In short - this hotel is EVERYTHING that a budget hotel should be

title: Not a great experience
text: First impressions from the website and front reception - great. It went down hill when I left the reception to go to the room. In need of a good paint was the first impressions before getting to the room. Room was small but adequate. Bed had collapsed on one side so spent most of the night trying not to fall out of the double bed. Noise from next door at 4 am didn't help! Sink had no plug so not much use to someone who has a wet shave - managed just. Breakfast was toast and cereals - adequate but what happened to a offer of a full English Breakfast ? Maybe I ask for too much ...

title: Our showering skills were questioned when we told we were from...
text: Freezing cold (no insulation), smallest room ever. Hot water for only a few minutes than it stops. The shower practically showered into the bathroom floor. When asked to change the room explaining our difficulties we were asked where we were from. When we said from Istanbul, we were given a lecture on how to take a shower, in order to stop it from going on to the bathroom floor! So no changing rooms!!! Thanks to our lucky stars the receptionist in the morning was Turkish and she helped us and changed our room. Much larger, no bad shower and warmer than the other. But the hotel is very central, due to insulation it should be preferred for travelling in warmer seasons. The beds were comfy and room was clean. But the staff (including the receptionist) is in desperate need of a communication skills seminar. Our door was knocked for cleaning in the morning since there are no "do not disturb signs", we said we were in the room. In the next 30 mins. the door was probably knocked 10 times if not 15!!!

title: Not recommended
text: Do not believe the photos shown on expedia. This place is not nice. First, it is not very clean. The bathroom is very small and there was dirt in the corners. The bed linens are of poor quality. There is a gap in the double bed. Don't think you are getting a good deal because breakfast is included. It was a hard boiled egg and corn flakes. The staff is rude and not helpful. Would not stay here again.

title: Don't go if you're tall and/or claustrophobic
text: This hotel scarred me. I only stayed for one night, yet my experience there was pretty dire. The staff were fine, accommodating, helpful when needed to be. But the problem is that I'm 6"7. Nothing wrong with that, I hear you say. However, I didn't expect the room I was going to stay was *that* small. The staff member I saw warned me before I was given my key but honestly, I wished I was warned before I booked my room. I was a victim to false advertising. The small room made sleeping a nightmare and there wasn't much walking space because it was covered by my small suitcase I brought with me. The lowlight for me had to be the shower room. I don't suffer from claustrophobia, however, I was very close to suffering from it that one night. The shower room was so small. I slouched all through my cleaning process. And the room was stuffy, no air coming out of the extractor fan. On the bright side, you can have pizza delivered to the hotel...

title: Cheap and cheerful
text: My husband and I have just returned from a London City break. We stayed at the Leisure Inn because it was cheap ( we only paid £90 with lastminute for 3 nights B&B). The hotel was in a brilliant position right next to Hyde Park, and within walking distance of all the main attractions. The room was basic and clean. All we wanted was a base to sleep and shower. It was OK.

title: On a scale of one to ten, it's a five
text: Because this hotel was recently rennovated, everything may look good at first. However, at second glance, it appears as though the hotel is gilded, as they try to make it look better than it is. In the rooms, the carpets look nice, but they have stains. The bathrooms look great from afar, but up close one can see cracks in the mirror and the flaws in such a small sized bathroom. All the problems would be excusable, if the room rates were not so high and the hotel weren't so far from paddington station or any tube station. Also, costs of access to a computer if a traveler didn't bring one increases as the minutes go by, and the only way to earn free usage is to write a hotel review such as this one. This hotel is recommended as long as the traveller knows exactly where it is.

title: Never again
text: This is the most unfriendly hotel that i have ever visited. Good morning, Good evening,... are unknown words in this hotel. And the rooms : We've got a room in the basement with a plexi glass roof (which btw is not allowed by the building law) and almost no ventilation. The leaking bathroom was a very nice surprise ( the shower water came back up next to the beds), the nice Tv with only snow on it and the breakfast was verry simple. conclusion : never again grz

title: A very nice hotel
text: I went here for holiday with my friends in February. This hotel is very nice. The collocation is perfect, in a beautiful area very close the the beautiful and magical Hyde Park and there are a lot of stations of the underground to go to the nerve centers of the city. The staff is very kind. Our room at the groundfloor was, in our opinion, big enough for us and for all our things

title: Not what I was expecting
text: I read the reviews on here after I had booked and I was prepared to have to find somewhere else at the last minute! However I was pleasantly surprised especially for the price we paid. For three of us plus breakfast it cost only £60 and being central London I couldn't complain. Our room was not huge but plenty of room for three single beds and with room to walk around. The room was very clean and looked like it had been recently refurbished. Beds were comfortable and we had a great nights sleep. We did hear the odd noise from other rooms but nothing loud enough to disturb us. The bathroom was lovely, really clean and again not huge there was adequate room. The shower was amazing and plenty of room for my 6' son. The room has a flat screen tv, hairdryer and tea/coffee making facilities. Breakfast was fine, not a big choice but enough for us. Cereal, toast , boiled eggs and I think there was some cold meat. We only stayed for one night but I would have no hesitation in returning to stay for longer, the nearest tube station is about 5 minutes walk away. The hotel might not be the most luxurious but I don't know what people expect for the price. There appeared to be families, couples and a few groups of friends staying and the staff on reception were very helpful and friendly. We didn't pay for the Wi-Fi do can't comment on how good it was.

title: Relaxing Stay
text: I have stayed in this hotel quite a few times now and each time got a really good deal paying no more then £60 a night. ( I would not pay more then £60 a night tho ) Great Location within a 5 Min walk to 2 Tube stations and surround by lots of shops and Restaurants makes this Hotel a perfect place for a short stay. Rooms are very basic but have all you need for a short stay. Breakfast comes free when staying at this hotel and this is also very basic. Hotel is clean and staff are helpful. I'll be coming back to stay at this hotel again soon.

title: cheap and cheerful
text: This is cheap, 2 star budget hotel. IT IS NOT THE SAVOY, so don`t expect it to be as such. There were 7 of us going ( 2 adults, a 15, 13, 7, and 5 year olds plus a 6 month old baby), so we booked two triple rooms (numbers 3 and 6). They do have 1 cot, but couldn`t guarantee a pre booked one, so we took a small travel cot. Room 3 had 3 single beds and room 6 had a double and single with room for the T/cot. We were staying for 3 nights and there was enough room to store our bags and baby stuff...including a pram in the rooms. At one time all 7 of us were in the one room (not to sleep) and there was just about enough space for us all (so those who say the rooms are microscopic were obviously expecting a suite!). My wife (in room 6) did say that she could hear EVERYTHING that went on in the next room though, my room (3) we didn`t. This a hotel that is basically for you to sleep/wash/refresh. It isn`t the place for staying most of the time in your room. The rooms have keycards, clean linen, clean towels (although some were wearing),. tea/coffee making facilities. The carpets are a bit dated, but I don`t spend my time studying carpets. The ensuites were good for our needs, though some tiles were cracked and some grouting was stained by mould (not fresh mould though). The staff are foreign, but very friendly and helpful. The only exception being was that they hadn`t a clue where the nearest doctors was. We didn`t try the breakfast as one of our kids has lots of severe allergies to certain foods and we all try to eat together, but they did ask us to book a time if we wanted it. If you wanted a full English breakfast, the internet cafe (200 yards up the road) does a great one. Talking of food, the Leinister Arms Pub (200 yards away) does great food and if your like sausages, theirs will be like nothing you`ve ever tasted before!!!!! The location is perfect. There is parking on the streets, but beware that they seem to have a traffic warden standing by your car, 2 minutes before your time is up!! There is a multi storey about a quarter of a mile away (in the main street near Bayswater Underground station) and it`s relatively cheap....for London. After I read some of the bad reviews, I thought there was a few snobby people around, after reading a lot of bad ones, I really didn`t want to go. After arriving, I really can`t see what people expect from a hotel of this price and rating PLUS SIDES: All we, as a family of 7, wanted. Clean, friendly, cheap. good location DOWN SIDES: room 6`s walls were very thin

title: Bug infested dump!
text: I stayed here because I got a great rate through Expedia. When I got the key to my room, I went upstairs, only to walk in on the previous occupant who hadn't checked out yet! He was very gracious, but when I went downstairs to tell the staff, they acted as if I was crazy, because check out time had been an hour before. After much arguing, they agreed to store my luggage, and I had to go hang out at a Burger King for 2 hrs. while they "cleaned" my room. When I returned, I found stained floors, and bugs crawling all over my shower. At this point, I was too exhausted to care, so I tried to take a nap. Unfortunately, I was rudely interrupted when two employees walked in on me! Also, the walls were paper thin. This place is a dump, and the staff is incredibly rude and unhelpful. The location was great, but that's about it. STAY AWAY!!!

title: So much better than expected
text: Given the low price of staying here and it being central to everything I wasn't expecting much at all, some backwater hole in the wall maybe so you can imagine my suprise when I showed up outside to see it looked like any other hotel. I strolled it to be greeted by a very friendly young man with a giant smile who made me and my friends feel at ease the second we walked through the door, cracking jokes which made the start of our weekend. We went down to our room which was a basement room, having had read reviews on here before hand I had again expected the basement rooms to not be the worst in the building but yet again I was left pleasantly surprised, in fact I couldn't say a bad thing about the room, it was well decorated, the beds were comfortable, the bedroom was clean as was the bathroom, in fact the only thing I could say negative was that my mobile phone got absolutely no signal down there so whenever I needed to make a call or connect to the internet I'd have to go upstairs. Other than that this hotel was comfortable, clean, well decorated and for the price I'd say you couldn't get any better especially for London so it would appear the people of this website are unnecessarily cruel and expect far too much for the tiny amount of money theyre willing to pay. If they want the ritz, this obviously isn't going to be the hotel for them but you can't expect the ritz on a two figure budget. It was only one road away from the high street, tesco, mcdonalds, boots.. everything was close as was the underground station to get to anywhere else in the London area. I would highly recommend, I will be staying there again and if ever friends or family are going to stay in London this is where I shall be sending them.

title: very disappointing ,travelled 4 london parade.4 2 day trip .
text: 1 good point central location, arrived on friday and had booked group in jan for march 43 people with selection of rooms all of these confirmed by the hotel b4 we left only to arrive and they were nt available totaly different to what was booked . we had 3 married couples 1 single which they tried to put in a room that was as small as hot press in ur hse wit no bathroom , and 3 teens not related to any of them ,when we arrived at hotel there was no rooms 4 them and hotel coulnt understand why they coulnt share and why we couldnt put them in quads when we requested doubles .took 2 hrs to check in 43 people and we had to book theese guests in our group without rooms in another hotel ,totally unacceptable and stressful especially with 22 children wit us all tired and hungry ,manager wd nt see us to sort this out and doesnt wrk sundays so earliest was monday when we wd b leaving this says it all .walls are like paper rooms very small even 4 london.never again stayed in hyde park towers last yr totally diffferent experience wd return there again .

title: london hotel Faulty Towers
text: Room was in the basement clean and tidy. Hoteli n need of some redecorating. Breakfast was cereal and toast cheese and jams. Hotel was good for Kensington Gardens and visiting the museums and walking to Oxford street. On last morning check ot was 11am. Just finishing of getting my thing's together when there was a knock at the door and a voice announced check out in 2 mins. Went to reception to ask who had knockedo n the door and the receptionist said it was her and she justw wanted to remind guest of check out time. I said that that was very rude. Would not stay again.

title: Better options elsewhere.
text: Have stayed at this hotel on numerous occasions in the past. In the past it was what it was...clean, basic but affordable. It had no pretentions of being anything other than a reasonably priced budget hotel in a decentish location. With a splash of paint in the communal lobby this hotel now believes it is something more than it really is. The room price has also gone up quite considerably with little or any evident improvement in the experience. The staff are pretty surly and unhelpful as well. Certainly there are better, cheaper and more friendlier hotels around to stay at. Wifi is £7 a day but wasn't even working in the rooms when I stayed. Will not be returning....ever!

title: Disgusting
text: This is by far the worst hotel I have seen. Absolutely worthy to spend more money for a better hotel as part of your experience while on holidays. I am not talking about the size of the room (barely space for the luggages) and bathroom, about the lack of cleanliness and so on you can read in other reviews. The worst thing was to find a kind of slug (or similar animal) on the headboard when I was about to go to sleep. Staff service was terrible. We asked the night receptionist to take the slug out of the room and we had to move all the furniture just in case more slugs of different animals were around. We asked for a new room for that night but unfortunately the answer was no. Next day we got a new room. We tried to make a complaint to any manager and NO ONE wanted to speak to us. We were told that "this is not a 5* hotel, that this is London". After 5 nights there and £800 bill no manager had the decency to come and apologize. The answer was "this is not a 5* hotel". Absolutely terrible service. Of course we are in the process of making an official complaint to booking.com (where we booked the hotel) and to the London authorities.

title: Sentral, quiet but dirty
text: Good for those who is only looking for an ok place to sleep during a stay in London. Easy to travel to, a close tube (actually two!) and a quiet street, which fives you a good night sleep. But the room was dirty, the bath terrible with water leak and an awful smell, the breakfast can't be described (who does the dishes by hand at a hotel in 2011???)... But thanks for making our beds every day and giving us fresh, clean towles!

title: Correct place
text: We had a 4 rooms persons witch was really a 2 bedrooms with 4 beds so it was very small, But I recommand this place because of the situation... Close to everything. The thing is... how staying in a so small room

text: Family of 4 travelled Europe for 4 weeks June/July 07 and compared to similar priced accommodation this was average. Room small but compared to other family rooms we stayed in was not too bad. title: 4 Rooms in 2 Days!
text: So, we arrived after booking online for a double room with double bed for two nights and we checked in and went up to our room to find 3 single beds in a room. Okay, their mistake so we headed down to reception and they changed us to another room. This time the room had a double bed and two singles, hrmm, a little unnecessary for two people but okay. However, the wall had a MASSIVE, and I'm talking MASSIVE, amount of water damage on the wall. Laughably, they had a crooked painting trying to cover the large hole in the wall but the damage went from the middle of the wall to the roof. By this time we were too tired to complain so we just went to bed, but a small child cried from 3am til 9am when we went for breakfast (admittedly not the hotel's fault but annoying nonetheless). Breakfast was pretty standard, toast, cereals, juice and perfect for the budget traveller looking to get some grub in before they start their day. After breakfast we asked to have our room changed because of the water damage and annoying kid and they gave yet another room. Open the door, and BAM, 4 single beds. Why 4 singles for a couple? Asked for a double bed room as we'd asked for when we booked and were told one wasn't available til 1pm so we went off for the day. Finally at 1pm we got a room with one double bed and it was pretty perfect for what we need. Overall, this hotel was pretty good for budget travellers (although at £97 for two nights we've paid a lot less) looking for somewhere close to good restaurants and tube stations but not all rooms are great (we got to sample 4). Buyer beware, be specific when you check in that ask for what you want bedwise or you may get shafted.

title: Much better than many local cheapies
text: Had a really nice stay here for the night. It was quiet and comfortable, just what I needed after a long day grafting. Don't know about value as work paid... I had a small double room on the 3rd floor, lower rooms might be noisier

title: Damp, noisy but great location
text: Stayed here one night - room was in the basement. The first thing that hit as I walked into the room was the smell of damp. You could see damp on the walls. The carpet was not put down properly and cables ran underneath. The ceiling level windows let in good light but they were 'plastic' conservatory style and so when it rained or a gutter leaked it was so very noisy - I had about 2 hours sleep in total - not good when you are working the next day. Breakfast was a OK apart from the bread - this was damp - I think that it was part baked and should have been cooked before serving. Definitely would not stay here again

title: the worst!! - dont waste your vacation and money here at all
text: i lived in room#205. it s really the worst hotel.. room is just about 12 sq.m. with narrow ceiling. it has bad smell and there are many fly & insects in the room. eventhough the price was attractive but it did not value for money at all.

title: would not rush back
text: Not badly located but more than basic, did have a good deal on lastminute but would not pay more than 50 pounds a night! The room was clean and the bathroom modern but no decoration or comfort even though the mattress was okay. The breakfast was cheap and tasted cheap, still believe that having powdered with water instead of orange juice, cheese that taste like plastic and smelly yogurt was quite poor...staff unfriendly, quite a disappointment after all It is the kind of hotel that you don't remember the name of after a little while and would not suggest to a friend or go back to.....overall, unless you get a cheap deal, book somewhere else!

title: Bedbugs bedbugs bedbugs room 207
text: We stayed in room 207 quadruple room. My 2 children stayed in the beds near the window. My 10 year old son started complaining of itching then my daughter, by the time got back home, both of them seriously needed to visit a dermatologist to treat the bites. Carpet is also not vacumed the whole time we stayed, sheets were not changed till we checked out, bed was only made but not changed. Would have forgiven them for the terrible breakfast they served everyday, boiled egg, cold toast, jam and butter.... everyday!!!

title: Really run down, old style hotel. Budget blown on entrance!!
text: I hated this hotel SO much. It didn't take away from the brilliance of London but seriously me and my mam were stuck in a double bedroom aka broom cupboard. Had an ensuite shower..more like en suite closet with a shower head stuck in..you couldn't swing a mouse in it let alone a cat!..you could barely swing a cut in the entire rooms proximity! We were on third floor above stairs..room not really even fit for one person! The decor is SO dated..and that's fine but not for the price the charge...creaky old stairs wake you up everytime someone comes in..shared bathroom was minging..nice warm shower but some blokes must have been on our floor peeing all over the place blurgh!! Breakfast wasnt too bad..could have had a bit more on..some yogurt and cppachino machine or something would have been great but..its passable..but dont stay here..you can get nicer for the same price...seriously if you do stay make sure you ask for a room not over and above the stairs or you'll be stuck in something probably smaller than your fridge!...no lies!!

title: Never been in a worse 'hotel' in my entire life
text: Stayed here for a business trip. Actually had paid for another hotel who overbooked and I was passed onto this 'sister' hotel. This 'hotel' is not fit for purpose. The room I received was at the very top of the 'hotel'. It had a single bed, a broken wardrobe, a wash basin that didn't have running water and a hole in the wall where a window pane should have been. That's right people - no actual window just a 3ft x 3ft hole in the wall - which led out to the fire escape - so anyone could have come and gone into my room if they so wished. I checked in, went and got terribly drunk and came back at 3am and stayed awake in the room and left at 6am for Heathrow Airport. Never ever staying here again.

title: disgusting
text: We found this hotel disgusting badly in need of a good clean and decorating children refused to eat breakfast it was so bad.would not stay there if paid to do so.Only good point was staff were very nice.only stayed the one night and that was more than enough.

title: Too many cons!
text: On the positive side, location was great and price was good for London. Staff were helpful enough but that`s about it. On the negative side hotel needs a total refurb before you could actually call it a hotel. Low grade hostel would be more accurate and honest.

title: one night of horror
text: I stayed in single room one night. It had a shared facilities between 4 -5, i am not sure maybe more. The fact that it would be shared was not mentioned anywhere, the advertisement was very misleading. the room was like a shoe box, probably smaller, damp.Tthe toilet was opposite the room, but the shower nowhere to be found, apparently it was one flight up or down...they also demanded $20.00 deposit in case if a guest decided to steal sth- not clear what. The breakfast should have been booked in advance, but it did not help avoiding the queuing in a very narrow passage in order to get something on the dirty tray and then find a chair and sit at the wobbly table spilling the content of the cup. At 5 a.m an incredible noise woke me up, people walked up and down the corridor and there was the feeling that the wall between the corridor and the room did not exist at all. There was no light in the room even in the morning. The stuff kept reassuring that it was a good value, but it was too expensive for such an indescribable place. I think the owners should pay people to stay in that "HOSTEL" and it should not have any star at all, since it can be dangerous for health. it was the worst hotel I had ever stayed in my life. if you want to spoil your holidays you should book a single room for a couple of nights and you will easily achieve the goal!

title: A joke!
text: Horrible place in the middle of London! I wouldn't leave my dog there! Dirty carpets, horrible shower! Please avoid! Breakfast was horrible as well! I would rather pay extra £50 and stay in Travelodge. Lesson learnt to read the trip advisor comments before booking hotel!

title: lovely staff and brilliant location for a good price!
text: my family and i needed a place to stay in central London for a weekend and we thought this was the best all round deal, we were not disappointed. The location is deffinatley the best feature of the hotel, it is very close to Bayswater/Queensway underground stations and there are bus stops at the top of the road. It is also about 5 minutes walk from Hyde Park which was great for the kids as the weather was nice so we visited the park almost every day! The rooms were a reasonable size, clean and well furnished. My wife was worried about the reviews we had read, but it seems that others may have had a bad experience as we saw none of the same issues. The staff were really helpful, the receptionist Eda booked a taxi for us to go to the airport as well as selling us tickets for a bus tour during our stay. The price was also a major factor, its a good deal. Next time we stay in London we're coming back :)

title: good location, but all the rest ...
text: I will remember this hotel for a long time. We stayed in the room for 4 people. The first room we stayed was a bit small, but OK ( as we first thought) On the second night of our stay a little accident happened : probably someone who lived upstaires dropped smth heavy on the floor and that something made a lot of noise and ... 2 holes in our rooms's ceiling. it was pretty scary . So, they moved us to the other room ( 3rd floor) : the other room was a bit smaller, than the first one and the water pressure was really bad. When we asked to fix it - got the answer - that it is not possible. The lights were also acting weird - they were going out in 15-20 minutes, so we had to switch them off for approximately the same time to get the light again. Well, the location of the hotel is really good :)

title: Convenient Location.
text: The hotel is close to Paddington station and Lancaster station and that makes getting about easy. The hotel however was very basic. The breakfast served was less than satisfactory. Service was poor. Wouldn't recommend this to anyone who wanted to stay for more than one day.

title: Only for those on a tight budget
text: The initial 'Kerb Appeal' of the exquisite Georgian façade quickly fades on entering the shabby (no 'Chic' here I'm afraid) reception and I had the immediate feeling that there was probably an 'S' missing from 'Hotel'. We had been told by the online booking site that this place was 'Good' and 'Refurbished'

title: Dirty Hotel with poor breakfast
text: I would not recommend this hotel. The bedding looked like it had not been changed and had what I could only describe as white body fluids on it. Generally dirty. Utterly appalled and the staff were completely unhelpful, uninterested and displayed no customer service. Breakfast was poor with very limited selection and I ended up chosing a cheap brand of corn flakes.

title: Nice location, poor conditions
text: We made a last minute booking for 1 night stay in London and we ended up choosing the Leisure Inn due to its location. It stands near to Bayswater shopping area and tube station and a short walking distance from Hyde Park. The area around is very nice, quiet and safe to stay on your visit to London. Apart from this, it does not justify the price of £50 to stay in a very small bedroom where you can easily hear everyone walking and chatting every single time of day and night. The breakfast is OK but I doubt you will end up having a great rest.

title: DO NOT think about staying here!
text: Stayed at this guest house for approx 7 nights in Sept 2013 - it immediately struck us for the slightly shabby appearance (e.g. cracked floors), but for the cheapest rates avb we had found (abt £100 per night!) this was acceptable. However, POOR MAINTENANCE & HYGIENE marked our experience - discovered a mouse lurking in our bathroom since hole under sink was not appropriately covered + bed frame had missing wheel + maintenance were called in to check status of room after our incident rather than what one would expect before guests arrive into the room! Although a partial solution was offered in terms of being shifted into another room and a miserable compensation offered, a little less arrogance from receptionist in charge and direct contact from hotel manager could have made the situation better (No matter how busy a manager is, serious complaints/ incidents should be tackled directly, not through receptionists !!). Indeed, no effort in pushing customers away!

title: Harry potter eat your heart out!
text: I travel to London on a regular basis in order to accompany an elderly relative. When I do this I spend a couple of nights in London to do some theatre so need to find convenient but affordable accommodation. I knew when I booked this hotel that I was in a single room with a shared bathroom which I did not mind as I only use the room to sleep, I did not however expect to be in a converted cleaning cupboard under the stairs without even a small wash basin. I knew that things were not going to be perfect when I arrived at the hotel (which I must admit was in a fairly good location) and went to check in. The receptionists (one French and one far eastern) both seemed as though English was far from their second language and seemed not to understand the simplest of questions. I eventually was given my key to room 107 and was told it was on the first floor. I went up in the lift as advised only to find that rooms 101 to 106 were signposted but no 107. I searched for several minutes but eventually went back to reception only to be told 'it is there somewhere'. After a second futile search I went back to reception and insisted that one of them show me where the room was! I then realised why they did not show me in the first place

title: misery in Bayswater
text: Bayswater is a good safe location. Close to 2 subway stations and buses, a short ride from sites, good inexpensive shopping on Queensway (5 mins walk). As for the hotel itself, the teapot in the room worked great. And that's about the only compliment I can pay. This "triple" room was so small that even with minimum luggage (1 per person) we had to do a regular Swan Lake to get to the bathroom or out of the room. The bathroom: you better be anorectic to negotiate the space between the toilet and the sink. At the same time you should have strong hands to pump the flusher. And be patient with the sink that thinks it is in an airplane and empties ever so slowly. The carpets have not been vacuumed since WWI (my wife says). She is an expert, I can't tell, between luggage and beds I haven't seen enough carpet to draw conclusions. TV: broken - complaint - fixed - broken again a day later - complaint - fixed - broken (repeat ad absurdo). Overhead light: broken - fixed. Shampoo: none. Hotel-provided outlet converter - worked after manymanymany attempts and returns. The hair dryer overheats and turns itself off after 30 seconds. Orange juice - none (if I call the vile liquid they serve at breakfast OJ, Tropicana will sue my butt off). Add the sheer misery in the "restaurant" manager's face, the furniture and the decor, and you have an average Polish factory cafeteria circa 1970. The report would be incomplete w/o mentioning the reception staff. These young girls were as charming and kind and friendly and helpful as they could be. Unfortunately, they couldn't do much. Maybe in London in summer you cannot expect better for $195 a night. Maybe. Still: this is an hotel you can survive, but not much more than that. If the option is a night at the station, take it. But beware.

title: Great Stay, Great Service
text: I actually signed up to Trip Advisor to leave a review for the guys at SDH as a thank you for being so nice. I can't understand other reviews criticizing the hospitality. I was very happy with every aspect of my stay but especially by the personal and polite service that I experienced from everyone at SDH. I feel they went over and above their duty and especially what I would have expected. Obviously location, cleanliness, and room were perfect. To be helpful and give a balanced review there was a little street noise (room 101) but nothing major and a bit of noise one morning from the room above us walking around and then being hoovered, but again not major. All in all it couldn't have been better really. I would recommend SDH to everyone.

title: Fabulous and characterful base in London!
text: If you want to return as soon as you leave then that says it all about this charming and quirky mini hotel in Chelsea. The staff were all absolutely lovely and genuinely helpful, we experienced no language difficulties at all, nothing was too much trouble. The hotel is in a wonderfully quiet and peaceful street, no noise from anything despite our windows looking out into the street, it was very restful. The bedroom was a deluxe mini suite with galleried landing with sofa and table, bathroom was spacious and felt luxurious, overall we had a feeling that we had lots of space. Room service was extremely prompt with a huge tray of tea, toast and preserves priced at £8 for two,would be a bargain anywhere in Europe we felt! The location is perfect, 2mins from Peter Jones/ Sloane St/ Sloan Sq/ Kings Rd/ Tube etc...there were gorgeous restaurants in walking distance - you must try the prawn & courgette linguini at San Lorenzo on Beauchamp Place! Overall, the hotel made our trip very special, we felt as if we had stumbled into a little secret world where we were being looked after!

title: Good but watch out for breakfast
text: Located in one of the best addresses in Central London. Everything that one needs is near. Good service , very comfy bed, the room was nicely decorated and well presented, The staff were very friendly . Turning onto costs, I feel that it could be a bit overpriced but bearing in mind that its the most expensive part of central london you would expect the pay such prices. Do not have breakfast there it is truly expensive, there are so many other places within a few yards to have a better cheaper breakfast. Having said this, looking forward to rebook next Autumn

title: Amazing Location & Interior but disappointing checkin
text: I would have given this hotel 5 stars based on the location and interior. It is really like staying at someones home. I had two issues, one breakfast was expensive in my opinion for what it was. GBP 18 for 4 slices toast, 1 croissant, coffee and juice. Two we asked for a baby cot when I booked. On arrival at 4pm we checked that the cot was in the room, it wasnt. The reception called room service to get one, but they had already left, so our 12 week old baby had to sleep on the sofa...

title: Perfect hideaway
text: I spent one night on business at the San Domenico House. The location is great - close to the tube but in a quiet side street ( I was able to sleep with an open window without too much noise!). The hotel is very personal with lots of antiques and it feels more like a privat guesthouse than a hotel. Service, though, was impeccable - extremely friendly staff. Since the hotel is owned by an Italian family, most of the staff has an Italian background, which is quite funny in London, but definitely charming. The room I stayed in was very large for London standards, individually and luxuriously furnished (loved the Louis Vuitton vintage suitcases) and very clean. It even had a nice roof terrace which I can imagine to be really nice in the summer. Breakfast in the morning was served either in the room (mine had a nice seating area) or in the breakfast room in the basement, which I thought at first to be strange but turned out to be quite cozy. And they serve good coffee!! Even if I try hard, I can't find any downturns.

title: Disappointing.
text: I organised this boutique hotel for my girlfriends birthday. Spent a bit more to get a gallery suite as on booking.com it says it has a bath as we both prefer to have a bath to soak and relax. Turned up to the hotel and it’s very clean and decor lovely. Was first given a room without a bath and questioned why and was told not all gallery suites have baths. I had to explain that on the booking.com website it stated that the room would come with a bath and is the reason I booked a gallery suite. The lady then said that I hadn’t requested a bath. In the end they managed to give us a room with a bath. The bed was really comfortable and the air con brilliant, Was a nice room with nice furniture but was not worth what I paid. The bath was tiny And everything rough around the edges with plaster missing from the ceiling in the bathroom, mouldy patch where the wall was constantly damp from the bath, tap on the bath awkward to use and the label missing, the plug socket wasn’t fixed on the wall properly. I can’t see what makes this hotel 5 star. Just felt the hotel didn’t live up to my expectations.

title: Overpriced
text: Beware this hotel is a complete rip off £36 for two very average G&T's why take advantage of guests , we expect to pay a bit more than normal in London but that's just ridiculous for a single Bombay sapphire Breakfast was meant to be included but they still tried to charge us! We won't be returning

title: Not a five star for sure.
text: Certainly not a five star hotel. The shower is only over the head at the ceiling so if you want to wash you hair only it is impossible. No coffee machine in the room. No cutlery at all. I ordered coffees with room service and they brought sugar and milk with it but no spoon to mix it. The lights were so dim that I could not apply my make up properly. We asked to pay cash and get refunded to our credit card as they had already charged us before our arrival there and the answer from the lady there was a NO as she was new and she did not want to make a mistake to the refund procedure. Also before our arrival we had sent them two emails to arrange a cab for us to pick us up from the airport but they did not bother to reply at all. In general it looked like they are totally amateurs there. There was only one person at the reception. There was also no bar at all in the hotel. Definitely not a five star service. Out room was simply ok. Nothing extravagant. The only good thing is the proximity to King’s Road. I don’t think we would visit again. Even a four star hotel has better service.

title: Special!
text: San Domenico House is infused with charm. From the moment you ring the doorbell to enter into the intimate, plush library/registry room and adjacent sitting area, with a fireplace that bring the room to life, you feel you've made the right decision on your hotel stay. The staff were professional, yet friendly and could not have been more helpful. The small elevator took us up three floors where we then walked up another flight to our room. Fine for us but could be difficult for older guests. Our room faced Draycott which is a somewhat busy street but being on a higher floor helped with the noise. The room was large, with a comfortable bed and hardwood floors. There was an armoire for hanging our clothing but the one drawback was the safe, which sat on the floor of the armoire, so you needed to sit on the ground to actually use it. Silly! The overhead lights were supposedly on dimmers but when dimming them they provided us with disco lighting, fading in and out until you adjusted them back to full strength. Fortunately we were not there to spend time on the internet which was patchy and required you signing back in each time you went off line for a few minutes. The small bathroom, with one sink basin and shower, was adequate but everytime you flushed the toilet strange noises creaked through the pipes for a few minutes. The bathroom was exceptionally clean, as was the entire room. We were never able to enjoy breakfast but did have tea in the sitting area, which is absolutely beautiful but small so the two children playing a game, without a parent in sight, did cause us to spend less time than we would have liked lounging near the fire. All in all, a lovely hotel and a wonderful Chelsea location.

title: Very pleasant
text: Stayed here because the place I usually stay was booked, San Domenico was on the same street so I took a chance because of the location. Now I have two fine hotels to choose from on the same street in my favourite part of London. Really enjoyed my stay, quiet, charming rooms in a beautiful period building, the staff were great, the bed comfortable and the breakfast was excellent. I look forward to staying there in the future.

title: Hidden little gem in Chelsea
text: This little B&B was the perfect find. After many attempts with boutique hotels in London, we were thrilled that San Domenico House offered large rooms with excellent service and a real "home away from home" ambiance. Ideally located wihin a stone's throw from Sloane Square and Kings Road, what better spot to spend a few days. The staff bent over backwards to help and no request was too much for them to handle. Normally, this kind of service in a big city comes with a hefty price tag.... not here. This will definitely be our first choice from now on for every future stay in London.

title: Hidden gem
text: Me and my partner have stayed at the Milestone, IHG at O2 and others in London and we are both in agreement that this is the best hotel we have stayed at. Fabulous room and service. Will be looking to stay here again when we come back to London.

title: Cosy hotel at nice location
text: San Domenico gave us a pleasant stay over a weekend in London. Spacious room (404) on top floor with our own private balcony facing south and nice airy view over the Chelsea area. Bed was quite hard - but that’s our taste and perhaps you’ll find it just perfect by your taste. Super friendly and polite staff eager to help you with whatever you might need. From the hotel you have just a short walk to Sloan Square and access to London Underground (circle/district line) or in the other direction you’ll find South Kensington and access to Piccadilly line. Perfect! Many shops, designer brand stores and restaurant/bars nerby. You’ll find your favourite close by for sure or travel by underground to wherever your favourite is located. Overall this is a highly recomended hotel BUT breakfast should definatly be included in the room fare regardless where you make your booking. £18 p/p (Continental) and £24 p/p (full English breakfast) is more than double the price you’ll pay at a proper café a few steps away from San Domenico House.

title: Little italy in a great London location
text: This is a quite interesting boutique hotel, in a very good London location. Love the fact it is run by Italians which for me makes this a lovely place to stay at. The hotel itself looked great with the christmas decorations. Hotel room very quirky but that is the italian style, which I prefer to any modern hotel chain's hotel rooms. Staff was very friendly and helpful.

title: A lovely peaceful hotel with attentive service
text: The San Domenico proved to be a wonderful find. The hotel is well located just a few minutes walk from Sloane Square tube station. Set in a quiet and picturesque red brick street the hotel is lovely from the first entrance. Service was very attentive from the first welcome to our departure. Our room, a Junior Suite, was very stylish with a certain traditional flare. There was plenty of space, the room offered good facilities and was well maintained. The bed was comfy, the bathroom smart and it was all very clean. Only a couple of things detracted from the otherwise faultless experience. The lack of tea and coffee making facilities in the room was disappointing. Likewise no iron was available in the room and upon requesting one we were told that the only option was for the hotel to press items at £3 a shirt. Despite these slight negative points it was still a very positive experience and a lovely stay.

title: Disappointing
text: This hotel is in a great location and I understand they are sorting out a few issues but to be honest I found it a rather strange place. Firstly the breakfast was a total rip off. There is no need to have breakfast at this hotel as there are wonderful cafes nearby serving much better food. The choice of cereals was woeful and by the time I had selected some miserable cornflakes, yoghurt and fruit it cost more than a fatty English breakfast. The toast was cold and like cardboard, the coffee the worst Ive probably had anywhere in the world. We were the only people in the breakfast room (should have taken that as a sign) and the service was slow (although the waitress was very sweet). The room we had requested was a twin room and beautifully decorated but totally impractical. I had to ring for an extension cord as there was no power point near the mirror to blow dry your hair. The room was very stuffy and the internal stairs in the room meant you were up and down constantly to access the wardrobe. No ironing board in the room and they would not provide one but instead said I could send out my shirt at a cost to be ironed...hardly satisfactory if you want to wear that blouse that morning and judging by what the breakfast cost very expensive exercise. The bathroom was incredibly small with no storage space for cosmetics (are all these hotel bathrooms designed by men?!!) and the shower not great. I would definitely not stay here again but I do believe they are trying to resolve some of these issues....or so they say. I just found the whole vibe there very odd but as I said, a beautifully decorated property but a long way to go to making it a great hotel.

title: Nice hotel. Good Service
text: I have vacation with my family, 11 person, 5 rooms. In first we have problem with air conditioner. But it complete in 30 minute. The hotel is good service mind and clean room. if we back to London. We will book this hotel.

title: So Italian, so Brit, so charming
text: Italian taste and warm care of details in a perfectly British location. Quiet , yet in the very heart of the city, easy to reach , absolutely charming and elegant . Don't miss breakfast ! Just perfect

title: Inconvenient bathroom
text: Although the hotel is small & beautiful, the shower in the bathroom didn't work. I tried several times. I decided to wash my hair in the sink next to the shower. I got only extremely hot water...burnt my head...They said the showers were a little bit complicated....They should have told me when I checked in! I got peanuts and pringles for free and an apologize. For this price I had expected much better.

title: Charming
text: I come here every year when my family comes to London to see me so I always spend some times with them here! The place is small, charming, the details and the design are the ones of a topical aristocratic British house! Good food and perfect location, right next to Sloan square and not far from harrods! Unfortunately They raised the prices in the last period but the place is always nice!

title: Aniversary stay
text: Just getting round to writing this. The hotel was lovely, although quite shabby around the edges. Great location but needs furnishing and bathrooms changed little things. I can't comment on the breakfast as we checked out before it was served. There was an issue with our booking which really soured our experience. The management were completely disorganised and rude. Upon getting to the hotel there was no apology for the incident that took place (a member of staff shouting down the telephone at my partner) We wouldn't stay again. The staff really could have won us over but just lacked any charm. Such a shame as the building and the Inteior are lovely.

title: 5 star price, 4 star trimmings
text: I stayed for 1 night as a last minute birthday treat. I had one of their junior suites. This place does not have a restaurant, so you mainly rely on room service, which was quite pricey. The room had a minibar and complimentary but no tea/coffee making facilities - usually come as standard in 5* hotels? The room was clean and very comfortable. The staff were friendly and helpful. And it is in a very convenient location.

title: Mixed feelings
text: Stayed here for two nights with my husband for short a Christmas break and have mixed feelings about our experience. First impressions were pretty good: the reception area was decorated beautifully for Christmas and had welcoming open fire. The member of staff who checked us in was not quite so welcoming, we felt they made no attempt to create any air of friendliness. This was something we experienced with all of the staff but having said that they were efficient in their roles. We were given room 203 which is at the front of the hotel. The room was large and decorated in an opulent style. It was clean but some of the wallpaper looked slightly grubby in places. The bathroom is the part of the stay that disappointed me the most - didn't like the shower and tiles around the bath did not look thoroughly cleaned. Molton Brown toiletries - shower gel and shampoo but no conditioner. No tea or coffee making facilities and no alcohol in the mini bar! Room service stops at 9pm. We didn't have breakfast at San Domenico House so can't comment on the quality of that. We preferred to go out - the Botanist is a few minutes walk from the hotel. We had a great breakfast there. We found the location excellent for what we wanted to do - mostly a bit of Christmas shopping. Overall, I think the hotel is good value for the location but for me it was the bathroom that let the quality of the room down. I think it is unlikely that we would stay here again.

title: excellent boutique hotel
text: very nice rooms...good sized. bathrooms a litle small. neighbourhood is excellent and so is the service.

title: This Is My Idea of Luxury
text: The San Domenico House Hotel is exactly what I think of when I think of a 5 star hotel. First, the hotel is set in a perfect location on a quiet street that is just a minute from the Kings Road, and about 5 minutes from the Sloane Square tube station. There are a number of good restaurants, cafes and shopping nearby. This is a very safe neighborhood, and I always felt comfortable walking back to the hotel after an evening out. At night, the staff set out lanterns on the porch, which is a lovely touch and very welcoming. The hotel is fashioned out of red brick townhouses built during the late Victorian period. Everything inside speaks to comfort, peace and tranquility. The materials used from the drapery to the antique furniture to the carpets are of the highest quality. Each room is individually decorated with fine art and antiques and the bathrooms, while perhaps small, have everything one could want from marble floors and counters to high-end fixtures. Every day the Molton Brown toiletries, which are not only provided on the sink surround but also in the shower itself, are refreshed. The staff were always attentive and cheerful. I must admit that my arrival at the hotel was not what I wanted as I came in soaking wet from a sudden downpour. Not only did I look like a drenched rat but my bags were soaked as well. When I arrived, another guest was in the midst of being checked in. Check in is taken care of at the desk located by the fireplace, and the fire on the grate was burning brightly adding to the sense of welcome and comfort. The young lady working at the desk asked me to sit in a chair while she finished the first guest's business. When that guest left, the young lady apologized for making me wait. I was then asked to take a seat by the fire so that she could check me in. My first thought was that she'd look through her paperwork and claim that they did not have my reservation. But no, instead I was told that I'd been upgraded to a suite. Suddenly my day was looking sunnier! The bellman took my bags and I travelled via the small elevator to the second floor where I was shown to my suite. The room is located behind two doors with a small passageway situated between the fire door and the suite's door. There was no question but that the room would be quiet. As one enters, there is a small table with two chairs, a desk and an armoire and yet another chair and lamp. From the huge windows, that I could open, I could see a beautiful house and garden across the way. The bedroom and bathroom are located down a short flight of stairs and so the ceiling height of the bedroom itself was double height. The king bed was covered with a snow white duvet and European Square pillows. The slight bow windows gave onto a similar view as above. Once I'd settled in, I was then able to enjoy the red and green grapes that had been provided for me. Two of the three nights I stayed at the hotel, I had friends in for a glass of wine in the beautiful lounge. I can definitely recommend the house red and white wines. With our drinks came bowls of crisps and nuts, which was a nice extra. The couches are deep and comfortable and the décor lux. What a lovely way to spend the evening before going out to dinner! I definitely want to return to this beautiful hotel that is so English in feel and so Italian in style.

title: Beautiful and charming hotel - feels like Italy
text: My husband and I stayed here just before Christmas for a weekend of shopping and catching up with friends. Firstly the location is fabulous, just behind the Kinds Road, short walk to Sloane Square station if required. Nice and quiet street and easy to find parking in the neighbouring roads. The welcome was fantastic, warm, friendly but not over bearing.The gentlemen at Reception was helpful and we were escorted to our room. The bedroom was beauitful, it really felt like we were in a hotel in Italy, full of charm and character. The bedroom was red and oppulent, I loved it!!! I was a little aprehensive about the bathroom having read a few reviews online about them being tired...our bathroom was fabulous, really spacious and great water pressure....not at all dated, it felt and looked brand new. The only small issue we had was that the room was very warm (both my husband and I are always warm, so I think this is more a personal issue than a problem that would affect everyone), a gentlemen came up and put the air-con on for us which was brilliant, problem solved. During our stay everyone was friendly and helpful, a great little bolt-hole for weekends in town and we will stay here again and again and I would highly recommend.

title: Perfect little boutique hotel for a romantic holiday
text: Stayed three nights including New Year's Eve. Warm fire blazing on check in. We wanted to have a nice dinner to bring in new year, but had no reservation anywhere. The hotel staff went all out to get us a reservation last minute the eve of, at a wonderful restaurant in walking distance. This hotel is first class all the way! Great location for walking and shoppping. Thank you to everyone at the hotel for making our stay a complete joy!

title: Overrated, horrid value
text: Wanted a romantic hotel in the heart of London. We stayed for 2 nights. Paid £264 per night not including breakfast for a Junior Suite . Ended up feeling as if it was a huge waste of money with really bad value. Here is why: 1. Room way too small to be categorized as a Junior Suite. We stayed in room 303 2. Bed was two queen mattresses combined - not one big king. How is a huge uncomfortable gap in the middle of the bed considered romantic?? and especially in a Junior Suite! 3. Room service managed to mess up our order, providing a salad instead of a sandwich, and without even providing the cutlery to eat the salad. 4. Disgusting smell of fried eggs in the morning from the kitchen . We were on the 3rd floor (!!!), and it came from the stairs inside of the hotel! Every morning the most horrific smell all over the room. made us both feel sick. again, how is this romantic?? 5. Bathroom was tiny, with a shower in a bath that was for one dirty with black marks in corners, as well as a really nasty shower head and with no curtain, resulting with water all over the place and feeling really disgusted by the whole state of the room. Again, is this supposed to be romantic? At the rate we paid we could have ended up with way better value for our money than this place. As it was a short stay, we decided to keep our thoughts to ourselves and simply make the best of what we were offered. We will not be returning, and I can not recommend this hotel to anyone. stay away if you value your money and want real quality!

title: Absolutely divine, my new home in London
text: San Domenico House gets top marks from me for old world elegance. Feels like a private mansion rather than an impersonal hotel. Could probably do with a refurbishment next year. There are some visible signs of wear but nothing to ruin my overall impression. Very nice to have both The King’s Road and Sloane Street literally a stone’s throw away

title: Charming hotel with attentive lovely staff
text: We stayed in room 102, gallery suite o 5th November 2016. Great room with very comfortable 4 poster bed. Lovely to be in a residential area in a hotel with all Italian staff. Very good full English breakfast. Excellent coffee. Good views from roof terrace. Next to King Road but far enough away to be very quiet. Very good restaurants nearby.

title: we just loved it!! perfection
text: location perfect. Concierge's so helpful and professional. You knew as soon as they met you at the door that this hotel was a cut above. We just loved every second of our stay and we will be re-booking. We are very picky but this place is faultless!!!

title: A 5 star hotel with a few issues
text: I have to say that we loved our stay at San Domenico House. We would definitely stay there again and recommend to anyone looking for a small boutique hotel in lovely Chelsea. Everyone at the hotel without exception was extremely friendly and helpful before and during our stay. We had a 2 level suite. I think it was room 204. It is the red room on their website. Our room was clean and had a good amount of storage space. We had a view from the back of the hotel down to King Street. The elevator was very small but sufficient. They have a deck on their top floor which is only accessible by stairs. It is a very small deck but you get a nice view of the surrounding area since most of the buildings in Chelsea seem to be no taller than the hotel. Now to my slight qualms. Many of the rooms require you to go up or down stairs to get to them from the elevator and the stairs are fairly narrow. If you have any issues with walking up stairs make sure you ask for a room that is directly off of the elevator. In the bathroom there was no outlet where you could hook up a hair dryer or a curling iron. We travel with adapters but there was an unusual plug in the bathroom that we were told was for electric shavers. It had 4 holes so I thought it would fit the english plug with 2 prongs but they were not the correct distance apart. When we told them about this at reception they had no answer for this. I'm not sure if only our room had that type of outlet in the bathroom but my wife had to do everything in front of the mirror in the bedroom and the light was barely sufficient. Again, I would stay there again but with those few caveats in mind decide if this is the right hotel for you.

title: Good hotel in most respects but breakfast and tea were very disappointing
text: This is a quirky place! The location is good and quiet and the bed was comfortable and room clean. I think it is intended to be quintessentially ‘English’ but suspect the owners aren’t so this is a non-Brit’s take on what is ‘typically English’, and probably appeals more to those who are not natives unless you appreciate an eclectic mix of pictures everywhere and high-camp style with sprigs of lavender on the pillows and rose petals down the loo on arrival for example. The picture of a Madonna and grotesquely obese child over the bed was a rather bizarre juxtaposition and there was an odd chair that was too wide to fit under the writing desk so was both annoying and a health and safety issue. Staff were polite and efficient but they desperately need to learn how to make tea properly (given there are no facilities in the room). I have to put up with being served a pot of hot water and tea bags on the side when overseas as they don’t know any better, but in my own country I do expect when ordering a pot of tea that is exactly what I’ll get and not a DIY job. We were advised to book a table in the sub-terranean breakfast room the night before and when we did, were then expected to say exactly there and then what we wanted. At 11pm and suffering from a tummy-bug I had no idea what I might feel like 9 hours later! This is the only place we’ve stayed for years that didn’t do a breakfast buffet so ended up having to have fruit salad/cereal/yogurt etc afterwards (because of course we'd had to order the night before). Hot water and tea bag job again was their idea of doing a pot of tea. Too be honest we found it so much hassle (and at more than £20 each, not exactly cheap) that we decided to do our own thing the next day and would suggest that anyone else staying Mon-Sat do the same – we walked 5 mins down the road to Peter Jones were you can have breakfast in their spacious skyline cafeteria at reasonable prices from 9.30 onwards and where of course you get a perfect cup of tea!

title: Great Hotel
text: Room was really nice and spacious - I had a balcony with a lovely view over Chelsea. Bathroom was great, spacious and clean. Location is great, right in the middle of Chelsea! Staff were very helpful, and really couldn't do enough for me.

title: A night in Chelsea
text: Certainly the location is not to be faulted, just steps from Kings Rd and. Sloane Square tube. Checkin was efficient and speedy. The room, a deluxe at the rear of the hotel was spacious. Disappointingly the TV was very small, and too far away from the bed to facilitate viewing once au lit. To watch it comfortably required moving the small chairs to the centre of the room. The bed could have been bigger, and poor quality pillows with no substance gave me a stiff neck. The bathroom was functional, but needed upgrading in terms of decor. The flooring looked as though it was unfinished and was somewhat harsh on the feet. The decorative finish needed sprucing up, as did the chipped doorframe paint. Breakfast was fine, although the room was a little chilly in atmosphere with an overwhelming chintziness not to my taste. In short the accommodation was acceptable but somewhat characterless, lacking that warmth that would make me feel I would return. One tip if staff prefer their office messy, best keep the door shut so guests can't see it.

title: Beautiful small hotel, excellent localization
text: Quite close to Sloane Square this esqusite small hotel used to be a house in Draycott Place, Chelsea. The localization couldn't be better: metro and buses, King's Road a few metres away. The place is very beautiful. Our room was on the 2nd floor and although giving to the main street not very noise. I guess the rooms that give to the other street are even more quiet. The room was very nice. Beautiful decoration and quite spacious. It had a living room area. There were two flaws: mattresses that were too soft (same with the pillows) and no ventilation at all in the bathroom, which after a shower was like a steam house. The staff was excellent. I suppose the place in run by an Italian family from Puglia. Everybody was very nice and courteous, Don't forget to go to the terrace on the rooftop, it has an amazing view. There was a full moon even! All in all, an woderful experience. Go and see for yourself.

title: Lovely hotel, shame about the staff
text: Beautiful hotel, lovely room (we stayed in a Junior Suite). However, the reception upon arrival was unfriendly, and my partner and I felt as though we were cold-calling at the Royal Family's weekend residence. We went out for the evening, and upon our return we received a slightly better reception, but had to show our room key to prove we were residents. The minibar in the room (no alcohol in sight) charged £4.50 for a can of Coke, and £3.00 for a Mars Bar. Continental breakfast for one person was £14 (plus VAT) and not fresh. Or warm. Really nice room, but not value for money.

title: Home from Home
text: I thought I would try something different to my usual hotel in London and I will now stay here every time I am in Town as our stay was perefect. Only minutes from Harrods the hotel offers a really good location. Our room was fantastic, as soon as the porter opened the door it had the 'WOW' factor, with a very comfortable four poster bed. We really did feel like we were at home. The staff were very attentive and service was impeccable. The breakfast was better than many 5 star Hotels I had stayed in. This is a hidden gem.

title: Beautiful, quiet hotel full of character in the heart of London
text: San Domenico House is a beautiful hotel in a very convenient location. For those arriving from Gatwick Airport, Victoria Station and the Gatwick Express is an easy walk away. I loved the comfort and character of the room, and the staff were all very helpful. The quiet, elegant rooms felt like an oasis in the middle of London.

title: Loved this Hotel...so central and just across the street from the Underground Station..
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times over a period of years and have recommended it to friends and have only gotten raving reviews about the location. What is so pleasing is that one only has to walk across the street from the Underground station to the Hotel. I find that the price is great for the calibre hotel. As a travel agent, I will always recommend this hotel as it is so close to everything.

title: A gem of a hotel
text: Brief one night stay in Chelsea with my wife. Early business meeting the next morning so we decided to treat ourselves to some luxury. This is a wonderful hotel just off the Kings road, Sloane Square end. My wife, whose in the know, describes the interior as Italian Ate. Lots of special paint finishes and old world art. Made a very refreshing change to modern decor favoured by so many establishments. We had a mezzanine room, so split over two levels. Four poster bed. We did not opt for breakfast in the hotel but did have time for an evening cocktail on the roof terrace. Great view over looking the Royal Chelsea hospital. We were in the middle of a rare heatwave and so a very welcome start to he evening. Staff were all delightful . We had a lovely time, but too brief. NB family event next week so we booked 3 rooms!!

title: London's Best Kept Secret
text: Where does one start when he enjoyed everything. The property is one of a kind in london. I have stayed in my fair share of hotels and I loved that property. The exquisite attention to detail was unrivaled. I loved the homey feel the room had to it. Location was super ideal and the service was impeccable.

title: Perfect Location
text: I would love to give this boutique hotel/bed and breakfast 5 stars but although certain aspects were perfect, such as the location (just off Sloane Square) which is really great, the quirkiness of the hotel, the great decoration and the lovely room we had with a little balcony there are a couple of reasons for me not to. The first is that there are a lot of stairs. No problem for us but could be if stairs are an issue, even with the small lift. We were on the top floor and there were a couple of flights after the lift. Second the breakfast was not the best value and being down in the basement a little small. The service was fine and everyone tried hard. The fact you have to ring the bell to get in adds a 'country house' feel to the place. We had tea brought to the Library and it was perfect. We stayed for two nights and would stay again. Slightly high in price but you are paying for the location.

title: Great boutique hotel in the best area in London
text: i have had a great and memorable experience in this wonderful hotel. it is a charming boutique hotel in my favorite part in this world. we were allocated to a great room on the last floor with a balcony with views to Kings road the room was so beautiful that it made our stay very special and romantic the staff were so nice and helpful in our reservations and answering our requests i would definitely without thinking twice to book myself here once back in London. You made our stay magical thank you!

title: What a difference staff makes
text: The courteous staff was outstanding. Everyone was friendly and helpful, from the reception to the cleaning staff. Homely and tastefull decor. Cleanliness. Attention to detail. With 17 rooms, small is beautiful

title: A small quite charming hotel
text: The hotel is very well located a step off kings road ... the hotel is Italian style and owner is also Italian as well as the staff who are very friendly and helpful. Furinature is very elegant , rooms sizes is very convenient and cozy, I think each room has its own colors and decoration . Breakfast is in basement but In a cozy small room and wonderfull selections. The area is very nice and the street is quite although you can easily flag a taxi. Or call for a ubar. The small details that has been taken care of .... shows how owner and managment are treating their clients. .. I strongly recommend it for any couples .

title: A very unhappy experience
text: This was meant to be a “treat” on a recent trip to the UK – it unfortunately failed to live up to everything it promised! The hotel is located in lovely, upmarket Chelsea, about 10 minutes’ walk from the Sloane Square Underground Station. The reception when we arrived was lukewarm and we were not offered any assistance with our bags which I would have expected in a 5 star property. We were also not shown to our room. Finding our way was a bit of a challenge as the hotel is something of a “rabbit warren” with rooms leading off from several mini staircases (3 or 4 steps each). The room was large, even by non-London standards, with interesting Victorian decor. It was however a lot older than it looked in the pictures and was badly in need of maintenance (I have attached a few pics of what it really looked like). The carpets felt sticky as though they had not been cleaned in years. The bathroom had only a bath with an overhead shower, not a separate one has come to expect in a 5 star property). The enamel coating on the bathtub was cracked and peeling and the showerhead was so blocked with rust / limescale that the shower was little more than a trickle (see pictures). There was a rust stain on the floor tiles presumably from a water leak from the radiator. The formerly white and now greyish towels were hard having the texture of cardboard, rather than being soft and fluffy. There was no tea/coffee station in the room which is also standard in most UK hotels. For what this experience cost, it was sadly lacking in so many ways and we left feeling completely unhappy at having been ripped off!

title: Very good
text: Staff were really helpful, the position was fantastic.close to many attractions or a short bus or tube ride from the others. The room I stayed at was on 2 levels, extremely comfortable and clean. Good breakfast.

title: Lovely
text: Great staff, a very different and boutique hotel in the heart of London. we had a lovely room on two levels and a four poster bed. it has a very Italian feel and the service is excellent and very personal - they had even scattered rose petals in the loo!!!!

title: Very nice
text: We liked this place. It is small, cosy and tasteful. A refined mix of Italy and thoroughly British. If you like Chelsea, this is a wonderful hotel. We asked for a ground floor room/suite, which was confirmed after some effort (from our side). We were upgraded to the master room on the first floor, and that was of course a wonderful place. Personally, i would not like to stay on the high floors because everything (lift, corridors) is quite narrow, including the tiny roof terrace. Our conclusion: not cheap, but tasteful!

title: this is not a 5 start hotel...avoid!!!!
text: i would not recommend to stay in this hotel walls and carpets were dirty! the front desk is not helpful at all. (None was in the from desk the day we left, we had to ring the door bell to get someone to check us out!!!)) no elevator access in some floors very expensive for what they offer! the only plus is the location

title: One night in Chelsea
text: Arrived at San Domenico House on a nasty rainy day. We had a lovely warm welcome from from the concierge. The hotel had a firecrackling, antiques and large paintings on the walls. We were shown to our suite, which was in two floors. Very cosy. Lovely bathroom products, enticed me to have a huge bubble bath. Bed and pillows were comfortable. Breakfast was continental, served on our room. Croissants were excellent, very French in taste not like cheap supermarket ones! We thoroughly enjoyed our stay here and the position, near the Kings Road, was excellent Will be back .......

title: Nice hotel
text: Nice hotel loom like a home clean room and good to pass a days there But the breakfast is poor for the price that we pairs for Receptions they are goo but there is some attitude from one of them and that make it bad to said all not good There is many think to see around the hotel just take a chance to walk around

title: Nice hotel
text: Our second stay here. Nice rooms and very convenient area. Helpful and polite staff. Did not eat breakfast there. We wanted to stay in the area and in a small hotel. This suits the bill. I would come back again.

title: Potentially amazing, actually average
