text: The place is absolutely stunning. Location as well. Service can definitely be better. Issues with the reservation system forced me to change 2 rooms in 2 nights

title: a dream hotel
text: This little gem is situatd in the kensington/Chelsea Borough and has only 19 rooms. They are all differently styled but in a most chique and elegant way. The staff was very friendly. This hotel won the bet B&B 2008/2009 award and rightfully so. Many of the room interiors can be seen on the virtual tour on the hotel's website. The King's road is at 1 minute away with lots of café's and restaurants.Even the sloane square tube station is abt 2 min away. An ideal spot where we shall certainly return.

title: A sumptuous stay!
text: We stayed at San Domenico House for a special birthday treat and it didn't disappoint. The decor is traditional Italian antique and our room was beautifully appointed with a balcony overlooking Draycott Place. I loved the extra large comfortable bed. The service was excellent, understated but friendly. The location is perfect for visiting the King's Road, Sloane Square and attractions such as the Natural History Museum and the V & A. There is a wide variety of restaurants nearby, such as Bibendum which we enjoyed very much. This kind of luxury doesn't come cheap, but it was worth it for the special occasion. Very memorable!

title: Lovely in all but one way..........
text: This is a beautiful, unique and splendid hotel from which to explore Chelsea and the King's Road. The decor is stunning and the Italian styling throughout delivers a venue which is a joy to stay in. All but one of the staff are welcoming, warm and charming. The one sore thumb is the young Italian chap who is manning Reception. He gives the distinct impression that he really doesn't want to be there, is curt in manner and doesn't seem to understand that good service is something which is integral in an exclusive Hotel. As the front of house face of the hotel, he really spoils which would otherwise would have been an outstanding experience. With a new great front of house face who is interested in customer service, this hotel would be outstanding.

title: My first boutique hotel experience
text: I wanted to review this property while staying in it. This is how much I loved the experience at San Domenico House. We were hesitant before we booked this property as we are used to big hotel chains and never took the risk of trying something different. If anything, it was the best hotel choice I have done so far this year. I have learnt that staying in a boutique hotel will give you more attentiveness from the staff, more personalization and much better service. The staff were incredibly sincere and nice. They loved their work and it shows. The room was spacious and every detail was attended to. It is as if you were at your own home. Free wifi and a nice balcony gave the stay a better meaning. I would give his boutique hotel a 110/100....

title: One of the best boutique hotels we have ever visited
text: Ideally located near Sloane Square. Very friendly and helpful staff available 24 hrs. Room was stunning with private balcony. Bathroom surprisingly large for Europe/England. Would not hesitate to book again.

title: Feeling like home
text: Service kind, excellent localization for reasonable price rates. It's a good choice in price efficient terms. If you do not like street noise avoid room front view!Eventhough they offer a little more space,however if you don't mind with street noise front view suites are very good. The food is very honest you also have excellent restaurants close by.

title: For the price we expected better ...
text: Well, it's Cheslea so what do you expect on the price. The rooms are quirky but spacious. We were "upgraded" when we booked but to be honest some of the double rooms are better than the junior suites. The reception staff are brilliant and helpful. The rooms are packed with extras - bathrobes (although mine was woefully too small), slippers(again too small), good toiletries. What was most disappointing was the breakfast: the service was incredibly slow and the staff had to be reminded what had been ordered and chased up to get it, bits arrived in an odd order and there was no attentiveness from the staff. As the phrase goes "everything was too much trouble". We only stayed one night and were committed for dinner elsewhere so cannot really comment on the other dining facilities. In short, if you like quirky Italian styling, are skinny with small feet and have all the time in the world for breakfast you'll love it.

title: Very nice...if you like this sort of thing.
text: We chose the San Domenico House as it is very convenient for Sloan Square which is where we needed to be on this occasion. First impression was "this is odd" as I had to ring the doorbell to get in (at 3pm in the afternoon). The next odd thing was reception wanting photo confirmation of my ID and address and taking a photo copy of my driver's licence. It's lucky I happened to have it on me as I don't make a habit of carrying my passport around in my home country! I've never been asked for this before at a UK hotel...Anyway on to the room

title: A beautiful getaway.
text: Located in Chelsea, this amazingly beautiful boutique hotel is definitely a hidden gem! It's interior is impeccable and the bedroom we were in is quite cosy and spacious. Every bedroom has its own unique design. Breakfast room was also beautifully set and decorated. San Domenico also has a lovely terrace on the roof which is spectacular!

title: A home away from home
text: Head over heels in love with this tiny hotel. A hidden gem in the heart of Chelsea with the most beautiful interior and an impeccable service. The bedrooms are spacious and cozy

title: Beautiful Boutique Hotel
text: We stayed eight days in a Junior suite at San Domenico House. It was just perfect. We had an active schedule in London, so this Chelsea hideaway was a great balance. The room was beautifully decorated, in good condition. The all-Italian staff were very friendly and helpful. If you want an intimate, tasteful and quiet retreat from the London bustle, this five star hotel is ideal.

title: Excellent boutique hotel
text: This was a lucky find! My first time to stay in a small boutique hotel. I admit, I loved it!! Location is nice and staff was excellent. The only thing I don't recommend here is food and probably the room was a bit noisy at night, but what helped was that we are on a small street with not much traffic anyways. Otherwise rooms are perfect, clean and very nice like rooms in a French palace. Me and my wife loved our stay in this hotel and will do it again if we come to London. Look at the rooms in the virtual tour on the hotels web site.

title: Perfect...
text: I am going to start off this review with my only complaint... It's that I have to write a review!! I really want to keep this gorgeous hotel a secret from everyone else... And enjoy it, selfishly, for whenever I want to treat myself! My partner and I booked this hotel in the lovely Chelsea area of London as a Christmas/Late Valentines present for ourselves. I can't remember how we came to find out about it, so I will just put it down to fate and fortune. We were greeted with a beautiful front facade which was looking onto a narrow London side street, it was full of character and once inside.. The grandiose yet homely interior was just so nice, we sat next to a roaring fire as we were swiftly checked into our room by our friendly host. The family run nature of this hotel was evident, as polite children played around in what seemed like their family home, family being a strong word for this hotel. We were shown to our room, up high on the third floor... In an elevator... Up some stairs and then down some stairs... Through a narrow corridor... Some people could find this hassle, we found it amazing and just added to the experience and character even more so.. Our room door opened and we were just so happy with what was in front on us. We had booked out a double deluxe room, with a balcony. The bed was clean and the linen was crisp and well tended to. The bathroom, yet quite small, was perfect. Black marbled surfaces worked well with the White floors and furnishings and kept in tune with the vintage theme of the building and rooms. The room had everything you'd want and expect, with gorgeous furnishings well placed, old pictures hung from the walls (which were sloping inwards, just another quirky feature of this old beautiful building) a small table in the centre had a plate full of grapes and a letter welcoming us to our room. We plonked our bags down and took some pictures, before going out to the balcony to take in the lovely view of the Chelsea rooftops, the buzz of London could be felt... But wasn't overwhelming. We ordered some champagne to the room and enjoyed a few hours of leisure before heading out for dinner. We arrived back late and we were still greeted with a smile, more drinks were ordered to the room and we took in some more of the fantastic balcony views... This time the London skyline lit up the horizon. We slept like royalty and woke up to our breakfast, which we had ordered to our room! We put on our San Domenico Robes and Slippers and basked in the crisp February morning sun, once again, on the balcony. Croissants and preserves went down a treat with some tea, coffee and juices. Check out was at 12, so it was lovely to spend the morning relaxing before we had to leave. Check out was swift and again done with a smile. Credit must go to the staff, all were so kind and polite... And none of them ever seemed like employees, they did just appear to be a part of a great working family that enjoyed and took pride in their jobs. This place is going to be our come to place for a stay in London whenever we treat ourselves. If you're thinking of booking a room... Don't ask for 404... It's mine!! 10/10 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

title: A little "Italy" in the middle of London
text: Since Sheraton Belgravia closed down a couple of years ago, I have not had a favorite hotel in London. I prefer staying in the Chelsea/Knightsbridge area and have tried out several places. The Sydney House hotel was my favorite until I discovered San Domenico House in Draycott Place, a minute or 3 from Sloane Square. A dream fulfilled - the best hotel in London. Clean, charming, individual décor of rooms, - and an unbelievable staff. All staff my wife and I got in contact with was all Italians, service minded, helpful and polite.

title: Huge rooms.....
text: I stayed here with my son in a magnificent twin room

title: San Domenico House, London
text: This is an excellent, well located, boutique hotel near Sloane Square. The service is exemplary and the staff go out of their way to assist. While the accommodation is comfortable and reasonably commodious by London standards, my bathroom was small and quite cramped. The bedrooms are not particularly well set up for work purposes or storing clothes, but are quiet and well appointed. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: Good atmosphere in great location!
text: Good atmosphere in great location! Very kind staff and good atmosphere. No bar which kind of is ennoying. Beds are really good and nice balcony with a view if you have a room in one of the upper floor. If you want to stay next to Sloane's square it's a good choice with charme.

title: Service and staff are excellent.
text: We spent two nights here and have to say the staff are very very welcoming. Opened the roof terrace for us out of hours and bought us drinks and refreshments, recommended and booked a table at an impressive local restaurant nearby... Too many "above and beyond" instances to mention them all but the staff really made our stay special. We stayed in the split level room- the rooms are a little theatrical and in the traditional Italian style- minimalists beware- but the venue as a whole has a romantic feel that you often get in the smaller boutique hotels. Really enjoyed and would love to return.

title: Classic Italian in Chelsea.
text: Stayed here five nights. First impressions, "wow this is different". Greeted by very friendly Italian staff, in what felt like the lounge of a 19th or early 20th century town house of an Italian aristocrat. Plush soft furnishings, heavy curtains, patterned wallpaper and no shortage of antique furniture, art works and curios. Up the slightly narrow staircase to my first floor room, generously sized, similarly decorated. All one expects was present, flat screen TV, fridge, safe, etc, and the eclectic interior design even extended to two Louis Vuitton antique trunks at the foot or the oversized bed. Everything was very clean and well presented, the only thing that stood out was some slightly scuffed paint on the woodwork here and there....Bit like some of the old palazzos I have seen in Italy, so quite authentic. Bathroom was small but clean and with all the quality toiletries one could want. I did not try the breakfast, but the afternoon tea in the cozy, comfortable lounge I can recommend.If you want a little bit of traditional Italy, friendly and efficient service, in a quiet street, close to Sloane Square, this could be for you.

title: Romantic, private and top drawer
text: We spent several nights at the San Domenico House in mid-June, and it was a real find. The location is perfect-- between Hyde Park/Buckingham Palace and Chelsea, just on the west edge of Belgravia, a couple of blocks from Sloane Square and the Saatchi Museum, near to several tube stations and many sights, all within walking distance. Lots of good food and great shopping nearby. The hotel (once a pair of converted townhouse mansions?) and its decor were wonderful-- beautifully and comfortably furnished, classical Italian antiques abounding. The Junior Suite was spectacular-- spacious, sumptuous, quiet and private, with a wonderful little patio for breakfast, overlooking the street. Paolo, Manuel and the other staff were warm, welcoming, very helpful, and responded promptly to all inquiries and requests. We were so pleasantly surprised that upon leaving, we cancelled our reservation for the Ritz (the last night of our trip a week later, back in London before flying home to the US) and booked that last, romantic night at San Domenico House. We have recommended it to all our traveling friends, as well as those in the UK, and will definitely be back next time we are there. The owner's other resort properties on the Italian coast look every bit as spectacular, and we look forward to staying at one of those when we are there, next, as well.

title: The nicest staff ever
text: This boutique hotel located in Chelsea, has nice rooms and suites. In walking distance you are at Sloane square and Sloane avenue with all the nice shops and restaurants. The lobby is very cosy and you can have tea in there. It looks like a private house, with books and furniture giving the nice impression that somebody lives there. The view on the back of the hotel is better as it points on the King’s Road on south. There is a small two tables lovely terrace on the roof where you can have breakfast. Just ask the front desk. The best thing about this hotel is the kindness, the professional and good attitude of all the staff. Will be back just for them. I recommend suite n°304, a Dupleix.

title: Spacious room in a great location
text: Spent two nights here before Christmas with my husband. We loved the spacious room (we took a Junior Suite) - always a bonus in cities like London - my only complaint would be the bathroom, which was small and didn't live up to the standard of the room. Room service for breakfast was good, prompt and of a high standard. When we couldn't get a reservation at the fabulous Indian Restaurant around the corner called Rasoi for our second night, the Receptionist was successful - please go there if you can - the food is outstanding. Lastly, the location was perfect - so convenient for the shops. I would recommend this place and gladly stay there again

title: Paradise in London
text: I have stayed at some absolutely lovely hotels over the years but San domenico house exceeded my expectations. When we arrived the staff were fabulous and very welcoming. The interior was incredible, there is so much to explore. Our room was stunning and I was bowled over at just how perfect it was. The attention to detail everywhere at this boutique hotel is stunning and cannot wait to go back and stay again.

title: Beautiful Boutique Hotel that felt home!
text: What a find! Arriving at the great ,central location ( just off Sloane Sqaure in Chelsea) one is welcomed by the glow of lanterns at the entrance .... Reception is warm & inviting & sets the tone for your stay! The room is very spacious & luxurious with a huge king size bed ,large marble bathroom with Molton Brown Toiletries & everything you need to make your stay a pleasant & comfortable one! The staff are all incredibly warm,friendly & helpful ! The Coffee,Italian of course ,is delicious! Go on,treat yourself & enjoy a fantastic time in a trendy part of London which offers some of the best retail therapy in the city!!

title: What a little gem...sch... Don't tell anyone else.
text: Just a fantastic boutique hotel, short walk to Sloan Square station. If you are there over the weekend, they even have a food market every Saturday near by. They have an amazing communal terrace with great views. Assuming your room does not have a private terrace. A great hideaway. There is an fantastic designer ice cream parlour close by. All shops on your door step, beauty of Chelsea. A great characterful, charming a little quaint hotel, with flair and personal service.. Understated classy place, very welcoming and such helpful staff. You can't go wrong staying here. It will forever be our favourite. A May

title: Nothing too much trouble
text: The Hotel is very convenient as it is in Central London. A short walk Sloane Square Tube Station.The Kings Road is just around the corner. The rooms have a lot of character and are very spacious. would stay again

title: Luxurious private hotel in the heart of Chelsea
text: In comparison to major 5 star hotels this is lacking in certain modern facilities such as aircon high,speed lifts,duvets,power showers etc It is convenient to Sloane Square with reasonable on street parking within 100 yards.The atmosphere is of a smart Chelsea Townhouse,although the check in process was unnecessarily laborious and pretentious. However,as romantic settings go this has lovely intimate small suites,a roof terrace overlooking Chelsea rooftops and charming if small public rooms but with only 17 suites this was not a problem. Overall at about £300 per night on offer this seemed fairly priced with decent if not spectacular standards of service etc. For a private intimate night away it is much to be recommended but would be a little bit lacking for busy business people.

title: Lovely room with the boyfriend <3
text: We only stayed for 1 night for the price of 165 pounds excluding VAT (pretty good for a 5 star hotel, found deal on trivago). I have to say this hotel is one of the bests I've ever been in my experience, It started with me and Luke (boyfriend) turning up at around 12:50pm at the door knocking to be let in by the staff, they were really nice and helped us show us the room, we were let in earlier than 2pm which I really liked. when we got to our room (204) it was absolutely lush, it was also a good size, they even had sprigs of lavender on the bed pillows. the bathroom was stunning (I've uploaded pictures to show) and the bed was actually delightful to sleep in, the covers were soft and you can tell they were good Egyptian cotton. We were given an upgrade room which is the Junior Suit to what we had before which was the Gallery suit but me being me I wanted the Gallery suit as it was 2 floors. They upgraded us because our room had a light to be fixed, I didn't mind that being done as the electrician came down in like 20-30minutes and was finished in wouldn't say more than 8 minutes. Once that was done the cleaners did pop by to clean the small mess the electricians had made. (didn't take more than 5 minutes to clean). I wouldn't say these are issues for us as we did turn up earlier than expected but they made our stay absolutely perfect, this hotel is also 5 minutes from Sloane square station and kings road. I would definitely come back here. San Domenico House watch out for us 2 again! :)

title: A little gem
text: I've stayed in this hotel three times now and think that it is one of the best value hotels in London. The rooms are spacious and comfortable and ther location is perfect being so close to the Kings Road. I haven't used room service or had breakfast and my one critcism would be that when ordering a drink in the lounge it takes a long time to be served. Other than that it is a small but perfectly formed bolthole. I will certainly continue to use it when I visit London.

title: Great service
text: Wonderful stay in a great location. The views from the foor top was amazing. Helpful staff and friendly staff. Large room size especially for centre London. A small hotel good if you prefer service and style to modern large hotel.

title: Great value
text: London is expensive, very expensive, and it is more expensive even to stay at districts such as Chelsea, South Kensignton or Notting Hill. San Domenico House is not cheap by some European standards, but we have to put it in the perspective of where it is located and the offer you get from other accomodations in London and specially in this area. San Domenico House is a rather small boutique hotel located in Draycott Place St., a small street parallel to the fantastic shopping street of King's Road, very close to Sloane Square and to Victoria Railway Station (almost walking distance). If you travel to Gatwick Airport, you can use the Gatwick Express train to get there in a reasonable time for a good price. The hotel itself is located in front of the Spanish Consulate (as a Spaniard myself, that is a relief in case of trouble). But insignificant details apart, the street is usually very calm despite its closeness to King's Road. The two rooms I've been two (a Junior Suite and a Deluxe Room) are fantastic. Usually London's hotels (including 5 stars hotels) sport very small rooms that are torn by time. Although the hotel and the furniture might look ancient, it is in the good way, ancient in the sense of antique, and well equiped, clean and with big rooms (very big indeed for British standards). The bathrooms are not really big but are very confortable. Water pressure must improve, but water temperature was perfect, even when the hotel was full. Beds and pillows are very confortable. I only had king size beds in my two stays, the matress was extraordinary and so were the sheets. Mostly all expected amenities were available, ranging from complimentary water bottles, all stuff you might need in a bathroom (except for shaving) including hairdryer and showercaps, and so on. Not only it is well equipped, but the quality was very good as well. It is quite improvable the WiFi reception. Depending on the device you use, you might have some trouble in most areas of the hotel. Good to say is that the WiFi was complimentary, with no added charges. It has a limited room service throughout the whole day. The last night of our second stay we ordered something to eat and (despite being a bit steep in price) the food was excellent. The food offer is limited though. However the Hotel does not have a restaurant itself, although it does have a dining room for breakfasts, magnificently decorated. The breakfast is in general quite good. It has no buffet but instead an "a la carte" breakfast. It has some areas to improve, including the lack of a wider offer, but you may have here either a varied English breakfast with good produce or the more classical Continental breakfast. Last but not least, the personnel were extremely friendly. They are a bit like a family like customer service, but with all the care of a 5 star hotel. Undoubtfully an alternative to (usually) more expensive 5 stars hotels around the area.

title: Best option in the area
text: Not an usual hotel. If you have seen already a lot of places in London and you would like to stay like a Londoner please stay at this hotel. Best location, good service, nice rooms and a good rate. It will be like stay at home.

title: 5 Star Service!
text: Wow! What a fantastic hotel! The service was fantastic! The Room was excellent! The value for money was supreme! The staff was flawless! Great hotel in a very good location. Convenient to tube stops, great restaurants a short distance away. The atmosphere was very nice. Antiques in the lobby and rooms. Nicely appointed but not over the top. The staff went out of their way to make sure our stay was enjoyable. Any place where I'm greeted by name both on arrival and throughout my stay is tops in my book. The rooms were nicely sized. I highly recommend a stay here. I'll be back even if it means traveling a bit further. Very convenient to Sloan Square an on a major bus and taxi route so always good transport options. Great job, kudos to the staff.

title: "fabulous San Domenico House "
text: Only had the one night at the San Domenico House,what a shame it wasn't more. The room was beautiful,luxurious and spotless. Big bed, very comfortable with soft pillows. Staff were lovely and nothing was too much trouble. The other big plus is the location just round the corner from Five Fields restaurant ,another great find. Next time I will be staying longer.

title: The home you always wised for in London
text: What a find! Thank you to my fellow TA community for your recommendations. San Domenico House is what one wishes one had for a home in London. Just spent two nights at this lovely glorified B&B/luxury hotel. The location is perfect, a stones throw from Kings Road, over looking Five Fields Restaurant (currently ranked as in the top five restaurants in London) and a 3 minute walk to Sloan Square and Sloan street tune station. If you are looking for a hotel with all the usual amenities (multiple restaurants, gym, gift shop…etc.) this is not for you. If you've been to London many times and you are sick of the run of the mill hotels and are looking for a home in London then please give this exceptional hotel a try. It's as if you own a luxury flat in London in one of the best parts of the city. The service is wonderful, polite, professional and non obtrusive. The room (I stayed in room 304) was clean, comfortable and luxurious. Yes, there is no tea/coffee maker in the room but there are ample places just around the corner for one to go get ones cup in the morning. I had breakfast one day and the quality of the fry up was excellent. I will certainly go back the next time I'm in London and I will certainly recommend this jewel of a hotel to my friends.

title: Wonderful experience
text: We just came back from a 5 days trip to london. This hotel was a great surprise. We had a junior suite. It was big, very nice and clean. Very comfortable big bed. Only small down side is the bar: not many choices for wine and too high prices. They should give more options. Other than that just perfect! We certainly be back!

title: Beautiful hotel room 103
text: Lovely location a few minutes walk away from sloanne tube station Stayed on New Year's Eve 6mins on tube to Westminster for firework 103 is top suite and has balcony One thing is the floor and walls are thin and you can heard people in other rooms and floors creek

title: A spur of the moment treat!
text: I didn't mean to stay here! I had booked somewhere else but didn't like it and fortunately managed to get their last room here at the last minute! What luck. This is a super place to stay, just off the Kings Road in Draycott Place. It is Italian owned with charming Italian staff and elegant decor. On a cold, wet London night a roaring fire and candles makes for a great welcome. The gallery bedroom was large and comfortable with everything one could wish for. Good selection of toiletries in the bathroom. Only thing missing for me was a make-up mirror! Unfortunately I did not get a chance to have breakfast but I'll be sure to rectify that on my next visit. There definitely will be one. What a great find.

title: Nice Stay
text: Very conviently located on a side street between Sloane square & Kings Road perfect for visiting Chelsea area. This hotel is owed by an Italian family and you could tell with all the nice little touches scattered around amongst the what would be a classic historic English building. Not a great check in though, the receptionist, never stood up while going through the usual formalities,not even when we left her desk with the bell boy as a matter of coutesy. The room was ready on time & was very nice, crisp bed linen,with turn down service & a Ferrero Roche on the pillow, niche.Wasn't cheap but ..in central London....in Chelsea??? I would revisit again we didn't have breakfast at San Domenico,but Tom Aikens Kitchen restaurant is near by,with celebrity & their security included

title: A hidden gem
text: A beautiful and impressive small hotel that is in a great location. The rooms are large, particularly by London standards, with tasteful decorations and excellent furnishings - it certainly feels like five star luxury accommodation. The staff were excellent, very efficient and friendly. I did not stay for breakfast so unable to comment. Only very small drawback is that there is no tea and coffee making facility in the room, however room service is excellent. Useful also to remember that all prices for accommodation, food, room service etc does not include vat so be prepared for 20% onto the bill at checkout. Still great value for money, however!

title: A nicely styled hotel marred by slack customer service
text: We booked this hotel to stay in for our wedding night as the location was convenient and we loved the style of the hotel. However our stay was marred by the fact that despite booking almost a year in advance and confirming closer to the date the room we had specifically booked wasn't available when we turned up after the ceremony to get some professional photos taken. Unfortunately the photographs were dependent on this room so we never got our shots. A real disappointment on a near perfect day.

title: Well worth a visit, though not perfect.
text: My first impression was whether the scaffolding which covered half the building would affect my room. It did not, but it did block the view of my friend's room despite being told that it would not. The Junior Suite Deluxe was a special room and worth paying for (though find a special rate if you can). As others have reviewed. the whole experience would be better if there were newspapers and tea/coffee available. Having said all that, the staff were exceptional, especially when the sad news came through of a family bereavement and my friend's plans were disrupted. The staff were helpful in every way and even provided some complimentary refreshments. The toiletries were especially good, but be aware that if you require an evening turndown you should either request it or make sure you leave your key if going out.

title: Great hotel in Chelsea
text: We stayed one night in our honeymoon trying to avoid the typical big chain hotels and discovered this great alternative hotel in Chelsea. Location is just fantastic, 2 mins walk to Sloane Square in a very nice and quiet area. The rooms are very nice, with a classic touch and great attention to detail. The staff, friendly and professional, made us feel like at home just by walking though the door. The terrace, if you´re luck enough to catch a sunny day (and we did!) is great for breakfast.

title: Treat yourself to a lovely nights sleep
text: The location is great, 5 mins from the tube and situated down a quite side street. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. The room was a four-poster suite and was lush. Decorated to a high standard and with some gorgeous furniture. The bathroom and toiletriies were also lovely although the shower head leaked and was coming away from the wall slightly. There were no tea/coffee faciliities in the room which was a disappointment but other than that, the room, the hotel and staff were great. Would definitely recommend.

title: Treat yourself-will be back.
text: Stayed for 2 nights in room 201 and had a wonderful time. The hotel was intimate and welcoming with an eclectic mix of furnishings creating an elegant relaxing 'house-guest' atmosphere. The friendly staff were always available and ready to help in any way. The continental breakfast we had in our room was very good.The large room was beautifully decorated with rich fabrics and paintings. Beds were very comfortable. There was also a settee and armchairs,good TV and air-con too, if needed. Ensuite was well equipped with everything you might need. Location was ideal, very close to Sloane Square tube, also walking distance to shops restaurants,Saatchi gallery Only two points which slightly marred our visit and can easily be changed:- Inform guests in advance if windows of their room will have no view and be covered in plastic with workmen walking past on scaffolding early in the morning!(we were kindly offered another room but we wanted twin beds and had already settled in) Please provide tea and coffee making facilities in the room-it's a little thing but makes a massive difference to a worn out tourist.

title: Very good value for money
text: I've been at the Gainsborough for a business trip and I've really enjoyed my stay in this old fashioned but friendly hotel. The reception staff is very helpful but the rooms are a little small, check on the website the room's dimension if space is a concern for you! The location is fantastic and it's worthy the price it self. They should revamp the premises as some room looks a bit lumpy and the beds are old fashioned English style-like but not really comfortable. Overall it's good value for money.

title: The smallest room but then only £70 in central London
text: I guess that you get what you pay for but I still feel very let down by this hotel. I booked a room at short notice on www.laterooms.co.uk and found a "special deal" at the Gainsborough near to South Kensington Tube. It was described as 4* with a room reduced from £220 to £70 excluding breakfast. It sounded too good to be true.... Firstly the good points: The Location And now some of the bad ones: The room (no 308) was only about 6'6" x 11' (2m x 3.4m) plus the tiniest bathroom I have ever seen. The bathroom door would not fully open because it banged against the bed.. Decoration was very poor with mould in the shower, door knob falling off the bathroom, filthy windows, paint falling off and strange circular stains on the walls. The temperature in the room at midnight was 89 deg F (30 Deg C) with no air con and only a portable fan to try and keep cool. The shower door was a corner unit where I had to squeeze my body through the opening (No, I am not an obese person!). I had to run the water for 10 minutes to get warm water. There was no indication of how to work the shower controls with no H or C labels. The window overlooked aircon units on the roof of the next office block and had windows from another building looking straight inside my room. This meant that i had to make the choice of opening the window and curtains to get some airflow and being overlooked lying on top of my bed, naked directly in front of the fan trying to cool off. It did not bother me unduly but I imagine that this would be a big problem for any ladies staying here. I DID NOT SLEEP A WINK ALL NIGHT. This was a horrid little room and I advise anyone reading this to check the room size before booking. There is no way that this is a 4*hotel!

title: You can't beat the location
text: This hotel is a bit tired and needs some updates. We had an enormous fan/dehumidifier in our room, which was helpful in keeping the air moving but took up a fair amount of valuable space. The beds were fine and the bathroom was clean. The service was average, most of the staff were friendly and attentive for answering questions. We paid 135 GBP per night which was a reasonable price and for that I would absolutely stay at the Gainsborough again. The location is what makes this place, around the corner from the Natural History Museum and nearby loads of great restaurants as well as the South Kensington tube stop.

title: Some pros and cons
text: The hotel is well-located near South Kensington tube and bus services are very convenient in the area. There are pubs, restaurants, cafes, delis and supermarkets within a minute's walk. There's also a French Adult language-learning institute, high school, French cinema and bistro complex right next door and French is widely-spoken in the area! The hotel itself is in an old house of several storeys and the foyer and reception is welcoming and pleasant. I found all the staff I met to be very courteous, helpful and friendly and the continental breakfast was most satisfactory for me. You can 'upgrade' your breakfast to a full cooked English breakfast for an extra 5 pounds if you wish - and it was a very good cooked brekkie! However, the rooms themselves are a bit drab and jaded and in need of a makeover. Still they are spacious and quiet with comfie beds and a decent desk and chair. Everything works well in the bathroom and it is all nice and clean despite looking a bit tired! Depending on what you are there for it may or may not suit you! 24 hour reception as well.

title: Gainsborough Hotel - Fantastic location for museums, needs refit
text: Our small group, meant we booked three rooms in this hotel a double, twin and single. The entrance to the hotel is well presented with good maintenance unfortunately the rooms are not as good. All three rooms we booked required maintenance attention, with decoration very tired and in room fittings also requiring replacement due to their age. The overall appearance of the rooms was OK but everything was very tired. Definitely not the 4 Star rating that was promised. All our rooms were on the small side especially the single which had only a narrow gap to the side and end of the bed. Rooms are hard to find and have unusual layout to fit them in the building. On opening the door to the twin you are presented with a stair case up to the room with the wardrobe at the bottom of the stairs. None of the rooms had a dedicated space for tea / coffee facilities with the equipment being located in cupboards / wardrobes etc. The Staff were a mixed bag and all bar one we encountered were mixed foreign with less than ideal spoken English, causing confusion and making explaining details in both directions hard. Some of the staff were particularly rude in attitude, however this may have be due to the poor level of their English. The continental breakfast (standard) was OK with no real complaints, albeit a little limited, ham and cheese provided was of poor quality but acceptable. Upgrade to full English cost £5, whether this was worth it is debatable, personally I would say not. The location of this Hotel is excellent if visiting the museums with the Natural History almost literally across the road (2 Minutes) and the others commensurately close. The nearest tube (South Kensington) is about a 5-10 minute walk. Overall the hotel is tired but acceptable, I would rate it high 2 star, definitely not 4 star. I would stay again but not by choice, as it would be quite far down my list. If we had not have got very discounted rates I would have been quite annoyed but for the price we paid and level of accommodation versus the location this was OK, but not much better than OK.

title: Good accommodation good value for money
text: room was dated but larger than one close by that I had previously stayed at. was very clean. Tea coffee etc plus complementary bottled water.Within walking distance of Brompton hospital and museum. Good value for money.

title: Cheap & Cheerful
text: I booked a single room for 2 nights, mainly for it's location and price. The room was a proper single - just room for a single bed with a small table and chair, small wardrobe and bedside table. I had arrived early and couldn't check in straight away, but the very helpful staff took my bag in and eventually let me check in earlier than usual. I went up to 3rd floor as instructed and could not find my room - finally saw a door marked stairway and opened it and my room was there. Had a bit of trouble with the door key card but again, staff helpful and sorted it promptly. Bed comfortable and room clean, but dated. The shower room was tiny and you had to sort of go sideways to enter the shower cubicle. For breakfast you had to go across the street to another hotel. Breakfast was slow. I was shown to table and brought a hot drink and ordered a cooked breakfast. The food was good, but the wait for it was unusually long. People that came in quite a while after me were served before me. Good selection of fruits, juices and pastries. I decided to have dinner "in" on the 2nd night and again it was across the street. They only had a snack menu and it was very limited in choice and I ended up only having a bowl of soup. I did not enjoy the soup and only ate a small amount of it. While the servers were very nice, the service was again very very slow. I gave this hotel a 3 as average only because the staff were very nice and the price was very reasonable for London. Usually I pay twice the amount for a room in London, so even with the problems, it was value for money. All of the staff that I encountered were excellent and very helpful and friendly. Just read the question below about hairdryer - make sure you bring your own - the one in the room functions, but it is not the best and I had a very bad hair day while there.

title: Noisey
text: On arrival we were told that we had been upgraded to a 'Delux' room free of charge. All was fine, although for a South Kensington Hotel I would have expected a bit more from a 'Delux Room', until we got back in the evening and tried to sleep. Be aware that there is a night club next door and the music kept us awake until 3am. When we complained in the morning we were told that they didn't usually put people in that room on a weekend. We had stayed on a Thursday night!!! We were offered no apology or compensation. The room was 111 so if you book in and are allocated this room I would enquire about the noise.

title: Needs a good revamp
text: Whilst the staff were friendly and it is really convenient for the Royal Albert Hall and museums our room was awlful. The bed creaked, there was a cracked window pane, the tiny bathroom needs a refit and to top it all there was blood on the curtains ( probably from the person who broke the window pane) but I suppose £113 for London what did I expect?

title: 3 not 4 star, but redeeming features
text: I stayed here on business and the location was chosen primarily on distance from work and price. It's very well situated and easy to find being right next to the natural history museum. on arrival I was offered a complimentary drink which after an eight hour trip was very welcome, although it probably would have been better for them to bring this to your room as I felt a bit awkward standing in reception while the receptionist and the bellboy waited for me. They carried my luggage down to the basement room which was very small and involved the bellboy putting my case on the bed and us shuffling round each other as there wasn't really enough room for me to have followed him in. The decor was chintzy, but the bed was comfortable enough, there's a floodlight on the building right outside the window so the curtains stayed tight closed. Nice toiletries in the bathroom and a sewing kit which is always handy. I didn't have breakfast so can't comment as it seemed a bit pricey when there's dozens of cafes right outside. All in all not bad, more of a three star than four but well priced and good central location.

title: overpriced but handy location
text: I stayed for one night, arriving early evening after an easy and relatively short journey. Hotel is in a quiet side street, about 6 minutes walk from the tube and about 3 from the Natural History/Science Musuems & Albert Hall etc. First impressions: nice, well cared for frontage, attractive, reassuring, no dodgy feeling about area. On checking in, was greeted by a smile but really slow service

title: Very good location
text: We were greeted by friendly staff. The room was adequate and clean. Breakfast was another matter altogether, and I wouldn't recommend spending the extra money. There are far too many good breakfast places nearby to justify what proved to be one of the worst breakfasts I've seen in London (service was slow, the order wasn't written down, the wrong order was served, the food was cold, the bacon was repulsive...) Still, the location was excellent for what we wanted to do.

title: Happy to be home safe
text: We booked two rooms in this hotel for two nights. On the first night my mother in-law couldn't find the hairdryer in her room so I went to look for it. I found it attached to the inside of the drawer and when I turned in on it EXPLODED in my hand! This in turn tripped the electrics in both of our rooms. I tried calling reception but the phone wouldn't work. Reception were nice but it took time for the electrics to work again. The wiring is below standard. After getting such a fright it was hard to sleep. The pillows were uncomfortable also. My room was at the front of the hotel and there was a lot of noise from the street which couldn't be helped. My mother in-laws room was quiet but the emergency exit door wouldn't close so she had to tie it with a pair of trousers. The toilet did not flush and when we went out the room was not cleaned. The do not disturb sign was on the door and a letter of apology was left on the dresser of my mother in-laws room. I contacted Hotels.com on the first night as this was a prepaid booking and we wanted to leave but they did not reply until I was home and only offered a voucher for €50. I am not fussy, all I usually look for in a hotel is a nice clean room. At the price we paid €515.48 I certainly did not expect to be electrocuted.

title: Location, location, location
text: I chose this hotel for its proximity to the Royal Albert Hall and it certainly is in an ideal spot for the museums of South Kensington. Other positives - clean comfortable bed, friendly reception staff, complimentary coffee on arrival. Negatives - very tired decor particularly in the bathroom where a serious revamp is overdue. Old tiling was discoloured and the shower seals and ceiling were mould stained. Power sockets are not ideally placed, down to the sides of a very solid desk or on the skirting board under the tv. In looking for a socket to plug in the kettle, I noted that dusting is clearly only done in the places that show and the net curtains were horribly grubby. One bedside light had an old-fashioned small round pin plug! Is that even legal these days? The room was excessively hot and it was impossible to reach the radiator thermostat (behind same heavy desk) to attempt to turn it down. The air con remote did nothing. The guest info book said to ask reception to assist with room heating issues, which I did, to be told that it is controlled centrally and couldn't be adjusted. The receptionist on check out said the opposite, that I could have turned down the thermostat on the radiator (see above!!). Whatever the truth, it was uncomfortably hot all night and the window didn't open. That said, this hotel does have it's particular style, the room itself was comfortable and the shower nice and hot. We didn't eat breakfast there, preferring to head to the amazing Muriel's Kitchen just round the corner by theTube station. This place needs some serious money spending on it

title: Great location and great service - reception
text: close to subway, great location

title: Good location - rooms variable
text: This has become my favourite base for occasional overnight work-related stays in London. It is very convenient (close to South Kensington tube), and in a pleasant area (near the French Quarter, the Museums, close-ish to Hyde Park, and with lots of eating places within five minutes walk (I've started going regularly to the large Pret a Porter near the tube station but there are plenty of places for a 'sit-down' mea nearby). Breakfast is a good buffet in rather a nice room with constant classical music. The problem is that the rooms vary hugely in quality and size. Last time I had a large room with no window, which was odd but OK. On other occasions I have been at the front, which is just too noisy once the deliveries start in the early morning. However at the back it is quiet and some of the rooms are really very pleasant.

title: It gets the job done
text: I booked this room due to its location – which is great. The bed wasn't the best bed I slept on but nothing to complain about. It was a small room, again nothing too bad there. The room was old, but was overall nice. The issues I had were this: 1. Wifi – When we checked in, we were told that they had two wifi networks, free to use. This was great because I had a project to work on for that night. However when we tried to sign on, we could get no connection. It wasn't until our last night there that we were finally able to get any type of connection. 2. Breakfast Deposit – When they checked in, they took £20 off my card for a "breakfast deposit" in case we were to eat at the hotel. I specifically chose the package I did to avoid paying for breakfast because I knew that I wouldn't need it. They never refunded my card or mentioned anything about it. I was ripped off £20 (plus more because of the fees on my card for international usage).

title: NIGHTCLUB AND NO SOUND PROOFING - DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!
text: We had a truly awful night staying here. There is a nightclub in the basement of the hotel and no sound proofing. It was so bad that we were kept awake until 2am when the club closed. Local residents have also complained because of the noise. The earlier reviews on this site do not include comments about noise because the club was not open then! If you want a good nights sleep in London, STAY SOMEWHERE ELSE!!!! When we called reception at 1.30am to complain we were told there was nothing they could do. We left two nights early and stayed elsewhere which was quiet, clean, modern and had excellent service - the direct opposite of the Gainsborough. If you are reading this and thinking, I might still stay there - DON'T!!! There are plenty of nice hotels in London and this is neither nice nor cheap.

title: The Gainsborough hotel london
text: I long weekend away with my friends. Very very pleased with hotel, small but very clean. hotel staff very helpful. reception staff very helpful they provided transport maps and advised on transport links hotel 5 minutes from the tube station (green, yellow or blue line). There is no restaurant but the continental buffet breakfast is very yummy with a wide selection of food. I will definitely go back.

title: More like 3 star
text: The Room was in basement and was tired. My colleagues room was also in basement backing onto a basketball court giving him no chance of a pre dinner nap. The receptionist was uninterested When we tried check out and even worse AWEFUL undrinkable coffee at breakfast.

title: Superb service and position.
text: My second stay. Perfectly positioned for the Albert Hall, 5 minutes fro South Kensington station. The service from Reception was exceptional. Nothing too much trouble, and I didn't leave once workout them smiling and speaking - makes a huge difference to feeling valued. My single room was, as expected, small, but very comfortable, the shower hot and powerful, and the towels and bed pristine. For te price, it is surely the only place to stay in that area.

title: very disappointing
text: The room was clean enough and there ended the good points. Beds poor and pillows smelly. Shower was scalding or freezing (we opted for freezing). Furniture shabby and drawer falling off. One bed had stained sheet. Air conditioning unit with tube hanging out window ridiculous and noisy. Reception staff dismissive and unfriendly - eye contact would be a good start. One night only and the position suited us for our 24 hour visit to Imperial College but could not recommend and would not return. in spite of the area this was not a good deal.

title: Dårligt dårligt
text: Jeg var der og skulle bruge hotellet for fire nætter. På grund af deres dårligt hygiejne valgte at annullere min bookning. Fik ingen penge tilbage men fik en sur mail som jeg vedhæfter her. ((Good afternoon, Unfortunately to get your money back will not be possible, as my colleague explained to you previously that your booking was an advanced purchase booking in this case this is not refundable. if you wish please speak with booking.com If you have any further questions please do not hesitate to contact us. Thank you Kind regards, Nicki))

title: Needs complete overhaul, don't waste your money here!
text: The ONLY good thing about this hotel is the location. We have travelled around the world extensively and know what to expect from a 4/5 star hotel. This hotel is rated 4 star but clearly should be graded 2 star or less - a budget hotel would no doubt provide similar. Don't be fooled by their 'fake' stately looking reception or the hotel's website promising a stay to make you feel as if you are in an English Country House - the owners obviously have never set foot in one! We stayed for two nights, the first night having to endure loud music until 2am from an adjoining building. As a result, the second night we were given another room. The furniture in both rooms looked as if it had been found in a skip, the carpets/walls were grubby with holes in, and the bathrooms were dirty. The appalling breakfast is served buffet style, with the sound of classical music playing in the background to delude you into thinking you are living the 'stately home' life. Food served is the cheapest bulk buy stuff on the market, which I'd be embarrassed to serve up to a pet dog, eg, slabs of sweaty tasteless cheese and slices of thin mass produced ham - awful! The staff, some pleasant enough, are all foreign and speak limited English. If you want a memorable stay in London, stay anywhere but this hovel - a truly dreadful experience and like throwing money down the drain.

title: OK for my two-night stay- comfortable and great location.
text: I decided to pay a little extra for a single room with double bed, as I thought that the room would be larger than the average single size. It was fine for my purposes- enough room to move around in, comfortable bed and, above all, very quiet, as it was on the top floor. There is a lift. The decor was reasonable, if faded

title: Lousy hotel
text: Worst hotel ever used in last 20 years. Wallpaper falling off. Room had 3 different carpet colour patches, stapled to floor and cutting your feet. Bathroom light not working, ventilation so noisy it sounds like a jet engine all night. Mattress so worn , you can feel every spring. Loose extension leads around the room trip hazard. Furniture with half the handles missing. Rooms so tiny you can't get a cat in, never mind swinging it. Dreadful hotel and definitely one to avoid, at all costs

title: Checked out after 10 minutes
text: Title says it all. The only plus points are the post code and the entrance. The room was just under 100 pounds for the night. About 8foot by 5 foot and very shabby with a small corner cupboard housing a shower. Please don't stay here.

title: Tired
text: Hotel looks great from the street view and the location is excellent but the experience is downhill from there. Rooms very tired and bathroom was third world. No bar and restaurant across the road...not a hotel. Back to hotel chains for quick London visits in future where you get exactly what you pay for. Very disappointing.

title: OH WHAT A NIGHT
text: Arrived to be told I couldn't have an early check in, but it was passed the check in time. When we went back the receptionist who's English was poor, rang and shout down the phone at a college. She then proceded to tell me there would be a £20 per head fee for extras. At this point she tappped her head and repeated per head as though I was stupid. I was told I must say my nationality even though the form said it only applied to non British residents. Bedsheets ripped Table cloths dirty Out of order toliet, the other was dirty in reception area. Breakfast, "How long will a cooked breakfast take?" "Only Five minutes" I was still waiting 25 minutes later! I was told there was mix up with the orders that came to our party of 6 one plate at a time. We knew they had forgotten one of us as the microwave had not pinged! To top it off they couldn't give me a recipt when I left and I had to call back later. Never deserving of 4 stars.

title: Not pleasant
text: Stayed for 1 night and will never return. Room smelled mouldy and damp (and was subterranean). TV didn't work because no aerial connections. Shower somewhat dilapidated. Could hear children crying in nearby room. This is frankly not a nice hotel, rather a partly refurbished and tired house.

title: No sleep!
text: Next to a nightclub, I didn't get to sleep till after 04:00! Sheer torture. Avoid like the plague.
