title: perfect location but could do with revamp
text: This hotel is perfectly placed for the museums and is a beautiful place. The hotel is situated in a very quiet street close to the underground and local cafes. The staff at reception were very polite and helpful and we were offered complimentary drinks on arrival. The only problem was the room and corridors could do with bringing up to date. We stayed in a triple room at the back of the hotel so no view but very quiet. One of the beds was broken and was very wobbly and noisy. One of the double wall sockets was also loose and some of the bathroom floor tiles were cracked and ingrained with dirt. There were plently of towels and toiletries for the three of us and the bedding was clean. We didn't have breakfast as it wasn't included in the price(£169). If the quality of the inside had matched the location and the building as a whole I would have given a higher star level.

title: Dark and unwelcoming
text: I felt that we were put in the worst room because I had a child. We were put in the far depths of a dark basement room. My child is very quiet and causes less noise than most adults.

title: A bit tired and dated
text: I chose the Gainsborough hotel because of its close proximity to the V&A, Science and Natural History Museums. I knew of this hotel and had thought that it would be really good, especially as it is 4 star. I have come to realise that the star rating of hotels can at times be mis-leading as I found that this hotel was more comparable to a 3 star hotel. The hotel itself was clean and cosy but the decor was very old and tired. By my estimation I would say that it had not had a refurb since about 1987. The room was functional, with the usual guest toiletries but the bedding was a little uncomfortable, especially the pillows.That aside, the location was fabulous and made visiting the museums and going elsewhere in London very easy. Restaurants are plentiful in the South Ken environs and the station is extremely close to hand. I chose to have breakfast out so I can't comment on the food.

title: Poor, poor quality
text: The lift was broken, out of service, the woman who checked us in eventually, was almost rude sometimes, and was most certainly, unsencere, and seemed to like being awkward, there was no dinning area in the actual hotel, we were instead sent over the road to your sister site, to eat, and I seems that if we had eaten there, you would have charged an extra premium on top of there posted prices. The chair in our room had a threadbare cover on it, the tv remote barely works, the room was dirty, the hair dryer made a noise like it was working,but actually produced very little heat, the aircon machine was noisy,and didn't seem to work properly either,the room in my opinion was in a very poor state of decorating,in short I was very dissatisfied

title: Booked 6 nights stayed 1
text: A horrible experience. The staff were nice but the room was filthy, shower had no pressure and worst of all the pillow we were given had someone's blood on it. We stayed one night out of the 6 we booked.

title: Not worth the money
text: We stayed here over the weekend, using it because of the prime location and it was the only one available in the area. The staff were very helpful and professional, however they were working in difficult circumstances. The lift wasn't working, neither was the complimentary coffee machine in reception, unless you wanted espresso. Our room was on the ground floor and was functional at best. The A/C was broken but there were fans, however the window faced the piping and had no view of the street. The pipes were also quite noisy with rushing water. There was a kettle and tea and coffee facilities, but a lack of plugs to plug the kettle in. The room could have been cleaner as well. Breakfast was over the road in their sister hotel, but it was an extra charge and was expensive for what it was, so the next day we ventured towards South Kensington tube station and had a cheaper and more substantial breakfast in a cafe. If there's nothing else available and you need something in that area for the museums etc, then ok but bear in mind you don't get a value for money venue. It's saving graces were the location and staff, but that alone couldn't justify the price or 4 star rating.

title: Very disappointing
text: The best thing about our room were the curtains! The Georgian high ceilings are lovely but the whole place is tatty. The reception area looks good but looking past that the stair/landing carpet is old and stained, the wall paper is faded and peeling in places. There seemed to be some wall paper stripping in the next bedroom to ours as there was paper all over the carpet down the landing so there might be some redecorating plan going on, i hope so as this is a lovely area of Kensington and being this post code you expect something nice and also for the price! The room was clean and the bedding immaculate and nicely presented. We slept well with hardly any noise and the lovely very long and sumptuous curtains eliminated any light at all. It was hot and humid outside but we had air conditioning which worked very well. Wifi was £5 per hour or £10 for 24 hours, not really what you expect when many provide it for free. Breakfast was not wonderful but adequate. No fresh fruit sald only tinned peaches and tinned pears swimming in lots of syrup. No fresh milk, only UHT, not good when you're dying for a good cup of tea. Not much choice on the menu. One saving grace was that they did find some gluten free bread which was much appreciated. The staff were helpful and very polite. It was very convenient for all of the museums being at the end of the road and many lovely eating places in the area.

title: Cramped and uncomfortable
text: This is a so-called 'boutique', and four star hotel. Do not be taken in. It looks OK from the website and from outside, but it is not anywhere near four star and is very poor indeed inside. Be warned, it is cramped, uncomfortable, the beds are truly awful, and your money is much better spent elsewhere then completely wasted here. However good a deal you think you've got it will still be far too much to pay to 'sleep' here. Anywhere that makes so much of a point of its location and little of the state of its rooms and service is best avoided.

title: Amazing location!! Very friendly staff!!
text: I booked based on the location and was really pleasantly surprised!! They provided nice shampoo & conditioner & body lotion, the shower water pressure was strong, the bed was comfy and the staff were super friendly and very attentive! I would definitely go back.

title: Listen to the reviews
text: I didn't listen to the reviews and focused instead on the cheap price and location. Well, I got what I paid for, the room was sweltering despite it being chilly outside (so I can only imagine what it is like when its hot). The "air conditioner" a bulky unit that was a serious fire hazard as it got hot after I had shut it off!! It was blow cold air for about two minutes and then make a loud banging noise and then blow only hot air.The tube coming from the unit through the cracked window made it impossible to open the window. Yes the room was a little shabby but what I couldn't understand was the scrimping on amenities that wouldn't have cost them anything. Why must we share one spoon to stir our tea? Why can't there be conditioner with the hair products? Location was amazing but there were other hotels which I enviously looked at. Beds were hard as a rock and same with the pillows.

title: Great location but small, worn and noisy
text: Check in went well and the reception area was lovely, however it went downhill from there as we were led to the basement to the room!!!!! We were offered no help with our luggage even though I'm mid 70's and had a large case, however the man did hover for a tip, which was not given. On entering the room we were not so shocked at the size, as we were expecting that but the lack of upkeep is scandalous for £182.00 per night with no breakfast. The walls looked as though they had been damp at some point and the paper was lifting and had dirty marks. The paintwork was peeling and the shower is in need of grouting as black in places. Obviously no bath as very, very small. Our main concern however was the noise, as outside our room was a school yard with screaming children and later this was used for a football match, so obviously this will allow for no lie in in on your stay. Overall a very expensive night in a small, worn, noisy room!!

title: Good value and location
text: I stayed one night at Gainsborough and was pretty good stay. The room was clean and it seemed freshly refurbished , new TV and comfortable bed. Upon check in the receptionist offered me a complimentary cup of tea , a rare gesture from hotels I've been. Great location and fare price for what you get. However I'd say was nice stay and I would definitely come back for my next trip to London.

title: Good hotel for a weekend.
text: Fine hotel, close to South Kensington metro station. Rooms were clean, personel friendly. WiFi was not very good, often no access and slow. Breakfast was ok. We had a room at the back which was very quit. Also close to Royal Albert Hall. Good pub and several great diner locations very close by.

title: Excellent Location - Extremely small single room
text: The personel was helpfull. The single room I stayed and the bathroom were very small.There was no space in order to open my suitcase. But it was clean and quite.The bed was very comfortable. The elevator was out of order for 4 days and I had to use the staircase to the 4th floor. The location is excellent.Very close to the South Kensington tube station which is directly linked to Heathrow. The neighborhoud is very good with many shops and it is possible to have meals until very late at night. Museums and Parks are close by. I would stay again in this hotel.

title: Thumbs Up for the Gainsborough
text: My husband and I stayed at the Gainsborough in March 2004, and we enjoyed our stay. The room was tidy and nicely decorated, if a bit small, and the bathroom was a decent size, very clean and included a tub, not just a shower as you often find in lower-priced hotels. My only advice is that if you like to sleep late like we do, you might not want a room at the back

title: Not a 4 star hotel!
text: This is not a four star hotel - or at least our room in the basement was not! Check in was chaotic, we had been sent away as check in was not until 2pm, which is fair enough, but came back to a queue of unhappy people and we did not get our room until 2:40pm. Our room, what can we say, faded and mouldy. The glass fronted wall picture had its own condensation waterfall and black mould and there was water/damp damage on the wallpaper and curtains. The bathroom ceiling had black mould growing on it. Our view was a broken cleaning cupboard door in the outside stair well. The walls of our room were paper thin and we were kept awake by the family in the room next door who were extremely noisy and excited! The only good things were - the staff were friendly and the location was good. We will certainly not be going back to this hotel and we were very surprised, based on our experience, that it was still classed as a 4 star.

title: Stayed here for work
text: Following a week travel, I chose the single room option here instead of looking elsewhere for a different hotel with a larger room, the decision was based on previous reviews from another site. What a mistake! The room is dirty, the bathroom isn't usable, apart from the damp musty smell there is black mould between the sink and the shower. The window made of plastic, has a round hole cut into it to allow air to circulate. On the bedside table there is a sign that stated ' Do not change the linen'! I am leaving the room itching and scratching, the thought of someone else using the same linen is bothering me. I also haven't slept and will be attending a meeting tired which is really what I was trying to avoid by staying over in a hotel. The room is cheap, but that doesn't excuse the way this room is, they shouldn't be selling a room in such bad condition. I will be talking to the manager before I leave and talk to the company that I booked the hotel through, hopefully they will take the correct action.

title: Great Stay
text: Stayed last night at the Gainsborough and was very impressed. The room we had was very nicely decorated and very quiet. We arrived late at the hotel and they could not have been more helpful. Fo us it was a great night and very good value.

title: Over-priced, Dirty and the rudest staff I haveever met
text: I recently paid an atronomical price for two nights in a (so called) deluxe suite. I am a man of quite high standards and expect the highest of ettiquette from staff in a four star hotel and based in South Kensington. However i received none of these I could go on forever with issues with this hotel and room. Its disgusting and i will never return

title: Avoid like the plague
text: My room was 32 degrees, no additional da to help cool it down, and all this despite the fact that room is advertised on booking.com as having air conditioning. Dated room too, dusty, with cracks down the wall- not sure how this qualifies as a 4 Star hotel at all!

title: TERRIBLE
text: 4 Stars? no way. We booked a double and a twin for my wife and son & daughter. They wanted to give us 2 doubles ( my kids are 30 and 28 ) They said that the fault was our travel agent. We had a prepaid voucher. The first day they sent us to the basement where the rooms don't have windows. The next day we were moved to the 1st floor ( the window looked out at the kitchen air pipes ) and my sons went to a 3rd building. The double beds are 1,50 m wide!!!, the safe didn't work, burnt light bulbs, the doors of the shower blinds fell off. No free wifi. They asked for an £80 waiver. No help to carry bags or catch a cab...and so on...I'm writing a letter to the London Tourist Office, E.Bell Argentina

title: Location, locaction, location
text: Great location, but the hotel needs an update - at least the rooms. They are tiny, but clean, but looks aged, and the walls in my room looked really worn. A bit more of an effort is needed for the breakfast. The staff however was A+!

title: One night stay
text: Straight of the bat, never in a million years a 4 star hotel. Really a 2-3 at best. Room was very dated, not vintage just old and in need of a refurbishment. Cracked tiles, light bulbs blown, stains on the wall from the air con, curtain hanging off, shall I go on? On the plus side the staff seemed nice from the little interaction we had. Certainly not worth the money. One to avoid.

title: Very well mannered and helping Staff
text: My special thanks to the staff of the hotel they were friendly , happy to help always, ever smiling and cooperative. I specifically would like to thank Zita , Ivan , Lorrela, Bogdan . Enjoy the hospitality with them . Keep smiling always. Cheers

title: Disappointing!
text: I stayed here in April when visiting London with friends.. There were 5 in our group, we had boooked one double room and one triple room. The double room was marginally better than the triple room which was frankly awful! It had no windows and the decor was enough to give you nightmares. The rooms looked nothing like the pictures on the website and to make matters worse there is a nightclub directly below the hotel. (The rooms are not soundproofed!) The staff were rude and unhelpful, any request was met with disdain and disinterest. The only saving grace for this hotel was the location and the breakfast.

title: Don't stay here if you expect a decent bed
text: Very nice people stuck in a bad situation - welcoming tired visitors to stay on their ancient lousy beds in a wonderful location in London. If they could purchase some new mattresses and put some fresh paint on the walls and fix other maintenance issues they would have a gem. We had to literally tape the curtains closed to block the morning light from waking us, and found the torn wall paper, worn paint and lousy beds hard to ignore. On the bright side breakfast at their sister hotel the Exhibitionist across the street was very nice. I'd look there for a room next time, as I was told they have better beds.

title: One Night Stay
text: A good hotel. Could have been a little bit cheaper. Not good that you have to walk over the street to eat breakfast which was very very expensive and the service was not the best. The best service at the hotel was from the great Receptionist Alessandra. Stayed at the hotel just for a gig at the Royal Albert Hall on the 16th of May.

title: It is London, what else you expect?
text: The location of this hotel is just great, walking distance to V&A and other museums, great restaurants and cafes. So there you go, if you get an inexpensive deal go for it. However, -and this really is a general comment- it is a hotel that has all the drawbacks of staying in London. You know the feeling, when traveling I usually enjoy the pampering and comfort of hotels

title: Four star apparently but rooms are small and cramped
text: The standard double room has a standard double bed (UK size) which means one only 2ms long x 1.27m wide. The bed was also very hard, and pillows were flat. No duvet, only sheets and a blanket. No spare pillows. Our room was on the ground floor at the back , so had no view. It was cramped, and hot, with furniture which was way out of date. A room deodoriser was plugged into one of the sockets. I wonder what smell it was trying to cover-up! The bathroom was very small in deed. The pipes made a terrible noise when the loo was flushed and the noise of loos flushing in adjacent rooms was enough to wake one. However is is a great location for the Albert Hall, the major museums and South Kensington generally.

title: Overnight stay
text: We arrived at the Gainsborough yesterday which is a great location for all the museums and the Albert Hall. We had a triple room which was quite spacious and clean but a little dated decor. Overall happy considering the price however the beds were awful!!! Next day not your traditional English tasting breakfast but ok.

title: 100 Quid for an Executive Broom cupboard!!!!
text: Yep,100 quid for room 401, which you get to via the fire escape. it was obviously never intended as a guest room, but has been converted to make a bit more money. OK, at this location I accept it will be either pricey or small. But a tiny room with barely enough floor space for a suitcase, a falling-apart bedside lamp, no heating (they did send up an electric heater - which didn't work), mould in the shower, breakfast extra and 10 pounds a day for wi-fi? But credit where it's due, the 12.00 checkout was nice. Not recommended.

title: Fair price, good standard in excellent location
text: I stayed here before and I like this little hotel because of its great location (5 min walking distance from the South Kensington tube station) Of course there are better hotels but especially in London they are hard to find for a reasonable price. I think this hotel is lovely and got a fair price. the staff is very friendly, the breakfast room cosy. I had a meeting there with a colleague during my stay and we even got complementary coffee on the house. I will come back here

title: Location good but that's it.
text: I have just returned from London where I stayed with my wife in room 103 at The Gainsborough. Our stay was not a good one for the following reasons:- There was no plug in the bath or hand basin, no shower curtain over the bath, the window blind was broken as was one of the window catches, the toilet seat was loose, there was only one bedside table and lamp and the TV electrics were very poorly done. The décor was very shabby and there was paint peeling from the walls in the bathroom. We ordered room service on the night of 13th May to be told shortly after that one of the items was unavailable. We made another choice so had Cajun Chicken, Salmon and a bottle of Red Wine. When the meal arrived we opened the wine and commenced the meal. The chips were almost cold, the chicken raw in the centre and so I called to advise the room service staff. When the butler arrived I explained the situation and as I was unhappy with the quality of the food asked him to remove it all including the remaining wine and bottle and said I would not be reordering. He suggested quite rudely that as we had already drunk some of the wine we would be charged for it. I said I was not happy with this as it had spoiled our evening and I would be making a complaint to the Manager. I made my point clear at check out and was not surprised to hear several other guests also complaining. I have complained to the management at the Gainsborough and Hotels4you who I booked it through but as yet I have had no reply from either.

title: Concert at Royal Albert Hall
text: Good location for visit to the Royal Albert Hall. Clean nicely decorated and furnished twin bedroom in keeping with the age and character of the building. Breakfast adequate. Friendly staff. Will visit again.

title: Very small, well situated but insufficient
text: Well situated in South Kensington this somewhat worn hotel is a little disappointing. The internet didn't work, and that really should be fixed. The friendly staff tried their best, but it was a frequently occurring event. That's not good enough for today in a city like London. My single room was extremely small. I had to climb into the bed in order to get into the bathroom.

title: Comfortable and convenient
text: A small and cozy hotel, which looks more like a private home, can be quite a comfort in the heart of London. And like odd guest rooms in a home, everything is not super smart all the time. But the breakfast is ample, the room service fairly adequate, and the location certainly the great plus point. A few minutes from some of the best museums, Victoria and Albert included, and Harrods for fancy shopping and the South Kensington tube to get you anywhere are wonderful conveniences. The days are so easy to organize from this hotel, and when you return to the room, its quiet and not unwelcoming. A bit pricy, a little shabby chic, but on the whole, a place to recommend to friends visiting London.

title: Needs to be in the 20th century.
text: A comfortable hotel in the heart of West Kensington. But you can't boil a kettle or plug your laptop in without having to shift furniture. The decor in the rooms needs a lot to be desired. Plenty of cracked tiles, age distressed bedroom fittings and drapes. The money has been spent on the downstairs public rooms, must remember that once in your allotted room the guest is free to inspect and absorb there surrounding. Comfortable well priced and near to museums, shops, underground, buses and Restaurants.

title: Great Hotel, Very English
text: We stayed at the Gainsborough for two weeks in May 2005. We had a triple room on the third floor, it wasn't as small as all the reviewers say there rooms were. The only problem we had with the room was the quality of the mattresses. The lobby was nice, the breakfast room and food were great, and the staff was friendly. However, the 'sister' hotel right in front, The Gallery, has a much nicer lobby, I would check that one out first. The location is simply unbeatable, two blocks away from the South Kensington Tube stop and surrounded by fantastic restaurants. Make sure to try Kuality Indian, near the tube stop.

title: Adequate
text: Hotel looked somewhat dated and when I arrived another guest was complaining about the size of the single room he was given. He was given another room although the receptionist did try to charge him another £20 but he held out and she cleared it with her manager and he was given a larger room. I wasn't feeling very confident by this time so when the receptionist asked me if I would like to see my room I said yes. Room 308 was small, but this is London, and the tiny bathroom looked clean (complimentary shower gel etc) so as it was only for one night I took the room. One of the window panes was broken and had been covered with plastic. The bed was comfortable and had a blanket rather than a duvet and the pillows were rather thin. The room was very hot even with the window open and the portable fan on. When I went to bed I could hear a humming outside the window sounding like a central heating/aircon motor. Fortunately once I'm asleep I'm asleep but if you are a light sleeper this could keep you awake. I didn't have breakfast so I can't comment on the food. I'm surprised at its star rating and I think the single rooms are certainly overpriced. On the plus side it was very convenient for museums and transport. I don't think I would stay there again.

title: Five star location. Three star interior at best!
text: For the first time ever, I booked a secret hotel via Expedia. They lied. I will never book a secret hotel again from any company. It will be a very long time before I book anything through Expedia. The promise was a four-star hotel in South Kensington at a 40% discount. I booked for three nights. The price was £133 per night, breakfast being extra. This is not a four-star hotel. Since Agoda sold the same rooms for the same nights at £152, without there being any kind of special offer, my understanding of maths can't work out where the 40% discount comes from! If you are offering a four-star hotel, on a so-called secret basis, you have to be upfront about those things which are not four-star. In 2014 no four-star hotel still charges £10 per computer per day for Wi-Fi. No four-star hotel has got away with charging £1.42 for a one-minute call to France since the 1970s. Four-star hotels do not have holes in the curtains. The curtains in four-star hotels are hung properly. Four-star hotels offer more than six hangers for a couple staying for three nights. Four-star hotels offer a choice of a double bed or two single beds to couples. Four-star hotels have quality beds and do not use the cheapest possible quality bedding. Four-star hotels have air conditioning. They do not feel uncomfortably hot even on a cool April evening. The electrical wiring in four-star hotels is immaculate. Four-star hotels have enough space for all your cases and enough space in their wardrobes for all your clothes. Four-star hotels have a proper,spacious, bathroom. They do not feature a seriously pokey shower cabinet, with no bath and with one tiny hand basin for a couple! The location of this hotel is extremely convenient for all sorts of places, with good transport links as well. That is all the hotel has going for it. There is not the tiniest bit of style in the upstairs areas. The only way it could conceivably merit the description four-star is if the whole interior was to be gutted, at a cost of millions of pounds of course.The same space would end up providing something like two thirds of the numbers of rooms currently in use in a modern, stylish fashion. I do not get the impression that the ownership has any intention of spending any money at all on the property, let alone that amount. Unless they do, avoid this hotel like the plague!

title: Mr
text: We stayed there on Sunday 28th Feb for 2 nights , we booked a four star deluxe room we stayed in room 306 on the 3rd floor , well where do I start !!! 😂 the room was very poor , stained carpet , cracked sink shower head broken , that was fixed when we complained !! Windows rattled at night in the wind , we decided we would have a full English bfast for the extra £5 each , they have no kitchen in the hotel they go across the road and collect the food from another hotel !!! We didn't eat the breakfast and refused to sign for it too as it was s-it !! , please do yourself a favour and stay somewhere else 😂😂😂😂😂 it's not an expensive hotel and it's never a four star either more two star

title: Neither good nor bad
text: A friend and I found this hotel on the latebooking.com site for half the normal price which I think is just over £180 a night for a double room. The hotel itself is very quaint, is in a brilliant South Ken location for the the V&A and the Natural History museum and the rooms are quite nice if somewhat ragged around the ears. The hotel is ultra warm in April so we had a portable air conditioner. The bathroom is also a bit tatty but I wouldn't give this place a terrible rating. With a bit of tarting up it could be wonderful.

title: Brilliant hotel.brilliant location.
text: What more can i say. An excellent hotel with great staff. On arrival we were given complimentary drinks whilst waiting for our room!..they also checked us in by 11.30!..now that by all standards is amazing. Room was small but lovely and clean and decorated really nicely. Staff were great and couldn't do enough for you. Would i return?..most definitely. Ps. If you're into your museums..there literally all on your doorstep. Fantastic weekend. Thank you Gainsborough!

title: Terrible
text: We booked a double room for 2 nights. On arrival the receptionist was polite but seemed to struggle . When we got to our room we found we had been given a twin instead. We returned to the reception to basically be told it’s tough and the other rooms are fully booked. After a long debate we were put in a family room. Terrible. It was small.. carpets stained.. broken tiles in the bathroom.. doors on the corridor to other rooms were broken... it’s was dingy... soul destroying.. at nearly 200 pound per nite I would expect a bit more. So that same day my partner booked us into another hotel..the baglioni in Hyde park.. more expensive yes but pure luxury.. one nite in the Gainsborough was enough for anyone

title: A nice place to stay
text: The Gainsborough Hotel is perfectly located within London's inner city for a holiday. It's only minutes walk from the South Kensington tube station. And is literally across the road from The Natural History Museum. We were impressed with the facilities at the hotel. Our room was larger than expected and very comfortable. The breakfast in the morning was also very good. Staff were very friendly and helpful all the time when we needed something. We were more than satisfied with our stay.

title: Great location and wonderfull staff
text: Very good sized rooms with beautifull decorations. Convinient hotel for exploring the surrounding musea. Staff isvery friendly and helpfull, especially Nuria and Marco from reception who went the extra mile to deliver an excellent service. Good breakfast service with also very helpfull staff We surely will be back.

title: Disappointing hotel
text: Stayed here recently and would not bother again. Prime location for all Kensington attractions with a very classy and welcoming reception area, however once you venture to your room it is shabby chic gone wrong. Dated, tired looking decor with a broken toilet seat, staff who can't understand you and bad admin skills. Over priced. You get a better experience in a Travel Lodge! The rooms were clean although they didn't look it. Didn't fancy breakfast here.

title: Cheerful
text: This little hotel tucked away on a side street was perfect for a night in London. The staff were incredibly helpful and friendly and really couldn't do enough for me. The room was tiny but clean and breakfast included yummy French pastries hot out of the oven. The hotel is well situated for museums, Hyde Park, Kensington and Knightsbridge.

title: A nice place to stay
text: My wife and I just returned from the Gainsborough. We were greeted by Tessa and our room was not yet ready due to we arrived an hour early. The staff did everything to get us into the room as fast as they could. We sat in the lobby and were given a free drink. After reading all the reviews I admit we were a little bit apprehensive. Our room was just fine. It was very clean and the typical English decor. Nothing great but also nothing to complain about. The bathroom is very small, and the shower took a little getting used to. I am tall so I had to conform to it. That being said the staff excellent,. They were very friendly and helpfull to all our needs. If you need to use their computer you have to go across the street to their sister hotel and pay a service charge. The hotel is located in a great location and very nice area. The metro is only a short walk away. We took it to the South Kensington stop from Heathrow, with our luggage and walked there. We would stay here again without any hesitation.

title: Very handy location - very small rooms
text: I was in a single, which was very small and allowed no room to layout the suitcase. But it was clean and compensation was the central location for a reasonable price. Cannot comment on the catering as I chose to take breakfast in local cafes.

title: A seedy weekend in the 1950s
text: I don't think I used Tripadviser before booking - big mistake and I think I was swayed by its proximity to where we were visiting. From the outside it is an anonymous hotel in an anonymous street in South Kensington. The staff are very helpful and checking in was no problem. We walked through a door and then went up a narrow wooden staircase to a half landing where we found our room. The first thing we noticed was the smell of damp. Then the peeling wallpaper. We threw ourselves on the double bed we had booked and found it was a double bed cover hiding two single beds made up as such. Somewhat disappointing, although to be fair they were comfortable beds, despite being springy enough for my grand-daughter to trampoline on, and we had two good nights sleep. The small window, covered by grimy net curtains, opened onto a little flat roof which was a maze of central heating and drainage pipes. To see the sky we had to crane our necks and look up. The room size was typivcal cheap central London, ie just room to get around the bed. The bedside lights did not work and the kettle needed to be plugged into an extension lead on the floor but then didn't reach up to the table. The small shower room had some exposed wiring, surprisingly still covered by it's protective covering. Interestingly there was an ordinary switch in the shower room to turn the extractor fan and over-sink light on. There is a note by the bed telling you not to change the linen. What exactly does that mean? Are you sleeping in someone elses dirty linen? It is far from ideal for a romantic weekend, but if you wish to take your loved one and experience a seedy hotel from a 1950's Graham Greene novel, this is the place for you! It is however in a very convenient location and the staff were very helpful.

title: Very poor value for money, not that great.
text: My husband booked this hotel via booking.com (in advance). The deluxe double room cost £165 (inc. continental breakfast). This is far from a salubrious hotel, the location is great, but there is no bar (walk across the road to the sister hotel, The Exhibitionist). The “deluxe” room was small with a comfortable bed but a very temperamental shower over the bath. The focal point of the room was a very large air conditioning unit at the foot of the bed, with the attached hose going out of a broken plastic pane in the window. Continental breakfast was nice but only with yesterday’s newspaper to read. For the price we paid I would rather go the The Ampersand Hotel round the corner or as another visitor suggests The Millennium Gloucester Hotel. I’m sure much better value for money.

title: Good location but a bit tired in decor and soft furnishings.
text: Broken tap, frayed and stained bed spread, poor freeview channels, mostly pay tv, and hard pillows but the location was great. Simple things that could be fixed and make a much better impression and a more enjoyable stay for guests. Staff were very helpful but need to improve on attention to detail. Jeni at http://www.letsrentinedinburgh.co

title: Thanks to the Gainsborough Hotel
text: I booked this hotel very last minute as it looked gorgeous on the website and I was not disappointed. As soon as you hit the door everyone is helpful and trying to meet your every need. All public areas are stylish but my room was a bit small comparing with the Italian standards. Bathroom was lovely with raindance shower. The roomservice provided a better value for the price. Unfortunately I did not have time for breakfast, which looked delicious. This hotel was really nice & I would definitely recommend it.

title: Worst hotel ever
text: Someone has stolen from my room 300Pounds cash and my mobile while I was having dinner yesterday evening. The same happened to another guest. The manager, a blond lady, never appear to help me even when the police came. DO NOT GO......worst place ever......worst manager ever.

title: Terrible!!
text: We booked this hotel through hotwire so we did not know what we were getting into. We were very disappointed. What was described as a 3 star hotel can only truly be described as shabby and in need of updating. I'm sure this was once a lovely hotel but now all of the furnishing and décor just look well worn. The entire hotel smells musty and stale. There was so much mold in the bathroom in our first room, I had trouble breathing throughout the night. We were allowed to switch rooms and the second room was marginally better. There is an air conditioning unit in each room but they are so loud it is hard to sleep with them on. The front desk staff was not knowledgeable or helpful. The only thing that this hotel had going for it was it was in a great location. The neighbourhood is lovely, close to restaurants and transit. Many museums are near as is Hyde Park. We will not be returning to this hotel.

title: Brilliant!
text: Stayed here with my partner for 1 night in July, the hotel was lovely. The reception staff were very helpful, complimentary drink on arrival and they even kept watch of our bags while we explored London until Check In time. We stayed in room 40 and couldn't have asked for better. It looked very recently refurbished, brand new bathroom, 2 windows, a TV bigger than mine at home!! We used it as a base really as it's within a 5 minute walk to South Kensington tube stop, Lots of cafe's around too. We didn't have breakfast so can't comment on that. Would definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: Never a 4 star hotel
text: From the outside the hotel looks pleasant and the entrance lobby is quaint in its period decor, but from there its a rapid decline! The rooms are tired, in need of some basic maintenace, decoration and the bathroom, well, not sure where I should start! No shower curtain, broken plug chains, leaking shower hose, no openable window, decoration tired, bits missing and generally appalling. How a hotel of this standard can get a 4 star rating is beyond me. If this is right the whole rating system needs a overhaul. Be prepared to be disappointed if you intend staying there. M

title: An excellent hotel
text: This small boutique hotel nestled in the heart of Kensington offers good value for money and helpful staff. When my luggage was inevitably lost by Garuda, the staff were extremely helpful and kind. The hotel is old-fashioned, hence the price, but my room was a good size and very comfortable. This is high-quality accommodation for very reasonable rates.

title: very dissapointing
text: You get what you pay for - and less - at the Gainsborough. I stayed here in the family "suite" with my wife and two daughters for 280 pounds ($560). It was a glorified closet. The shower was poor, and the in room internet did not work. We would have been much better off (and spent less money) on two doubles in another hotel. The staff was pleasant but not well informed about tourist queries (no info on the hop on-hop off bus tour eg). The breakfast was nice - it was included in our room charge. London is crazy expensive with the current exchange rate - still I think we could have done better than this. We won't be back.

title: Strategic place, nice breakfast, friendly service
text: Although the room seems a bit old, especially the carpet needs to be replaced (it felt dirty even though maybe they cleaned it) and they didn't have any slippers to wear inside the room, overall it was nice to stay there. The breakfast was nice, and the staffs were very friendly too, especially the afternoon staffs, Virginia, Amy, and also Adam who helped me with many things, and the two breakfast lady staffs who remembered my preference of tea during my 4 days stay there. The place is also strategic to go to famous spots (Victoria and Albert Museum, etc) or take the main route of bus tours in London.

title: Great staff - helpfull and friendly people
text: I would like to thabk Nadia and Elena for the great care they took of me and my business partner. They were extreemly kind and helpfull. They guided us and took care of all our requests in the moat friendly , kind and professional way. People like these make my stay an absolute pleasure. The rooms are small but excelent for spending a night or two on a budget.Thank you Nadia and Elena and i hope to see you next time. Kind regards Andrei Clanetaru (Andras)

title: Great stay!
text: I stayed with my parents in a family room and our stay was fantastic. All the staff was really friendly, specially Nuria the receptionist who made our stay unique and helped my parents with all their questions in Spanish. Javier

title: The price was right
text: Although this hotel is advertised as a four star it is not. It is however, a solid three star in a great location for the money. It is in South Kensington and centrally located to most London attractions. There are shops and restaurants nearby and the tube station is a 5 minute walk. Our room was clean but small, and the bathroom was very tiny. Having said that, we did not spend much time in the room. I found the staff to be accomodating and helpful. It was basically what I expected for the money.

title: Disappointing visit having been here before
text: We stayed here last October and came back as we enjoyed the stay. It started badly with the receptionist being unable to find the booking so she had to manually at the booking in. We were given one of the last rooms and it showed. The room was very small, we had to shuffle around the room as it wasn't big enough for 2 people to move past each other. The tiles on the bathroom floor were cracked, the basin had a huge chip in it, the cabling for the TV was off the wall and the paintwork was chipped. When I said to the receptionist that I was disappointed I was pretty much told there was nothing they could do. Not value for money and I won't be back again. I'd book somewhere else if I had to choose again.

title: Awful!
text: THis is the worst hotel i have ever stayed in, and have stayed in a fare share of bad hotels as a poor student. It takes about 20 minutes to get hot water in the morning, one of the employees told me they have bedbugs in most rooms and in general it is old and dirty. They even have a room without a window, which is probably illeagal as ther is no emergency exit. They claim they are an elegant english hotel, which couldn't be further from the truth.

title: Great location and friendly staff
text: I stayed at the Gainsborough Hotel over the weekend and I have to say the location is great, the premises are kept clean and are well equipped. What I think stands out the most is the friendliness of the staff, it was always a great pleasure to see and speak to Nuria at the reception, she shined with positivity!

title: I’d stay here again!!
text: I really enjoyed my 4 night stay at The Gainsborough! It was a bit tricky to find as it doesn’t have the typical hotel look, but is part of a block of row houses. The room was absolutely adequate with a very comfy bed and good linens. The breakfast buffet was good, staff were consistently helpful, particularly Nadia who worked at the front desk during the day. The location was excellent with easy access to the tube, trains and the hop on hop off bus.

title: Good Location but rather tired decor
text: Good location - walking distance to South Kensington Tube station. National History Museum just around the corner as well as the V&A and Science museum. Looks like an old Victorian house from the front - in a street with similar white fronted houses. Rooms are OK for sleep and washing and are therefore ideal for sightseeing. Rather pricey £310 for two nights for two people)- but all London hotels seem rather expensive - this one was probably priced more for the location than standard of accommodation. Could do with an upgrade of decor/ new bathroom fittings etc. Everything we wanted was functioning. Tea and coffee facilities in bedroom. Rather large air conditioning apparatus in bedroom with a tube to a hole in the window. Did not test this as it was October and not very warm. We would stay again if the price was right as the location was ideal for what we wanted.

title: Great hotel
text: Stayed here while on our trip to the tennis at Wimbledon. Hotel convent to the tube station. The rooms were comfortable if a little dated however the air conditioning wasn't great. All staff were very friends and helpful.

title: Loved the 'local' pub
text: Have just returned from The Ibis Earls Court. Can't fault the place. Fantastic breakfast ... buffett style ..... plenty of it ..... hot or cold. Cereal, fruits, juices, tea/coffee/chocolate, hot cooked bacon eggs sausages tomato's hash browns and they didn't rush you in and out. The rooms are basic (as are Ibis hotels) but will tea and coffee making in the room was all we needed. We needed extra pillows which were duly delivered to out room withing 10 minutes. The bar .... the "George and Dragon" was a lovely place to finish off the evening and it was like being in a country pub. Really convienient for the tube and all connections in and around London. As I say basic but all you need is a base and this is one of the best.

title: Nice hotel
text: Nice hotel. Could use some renovation. Location is perfect underground station nearby and ideal for a visit of Stamford Bridge. The home of Chelsea Football Club. King's Road with it's nice restaurants nearby

title: Great location, good value for money!
text: Fab hotel 2 min walk from West Brompton tube Station & one stop from Earl’s Court, so very central and easy to get to attractions such as the Royal Albert Hall and Fulham/Chelsea. There are many shops and bars close by although the area its self is very peaceful. Hotel was clean, check in very quick, great bar and was extremely good value for money, it was less than £200 for 5 of us to stay in one twin and one family room. Would recommend and would stay again!

title: OK 3star
text: The good. - got a great rate online, - not far from most attractions - bus stop at front door - clean & comfortable - quick seamless checkin - good selection and quality at included breakfast buffet - free Wi-Fi that actually worked well in the room The bad - air-con temperature was not adjustable - room was always too warm - no toiletries are provided - have to bring your own - no gym pool or anything like that The ugly - staff at information desk unhelpful to the point of being rude

title: Good value hotel although a bit dated
text: Stayed here a few times. Good value for money. Rooms clean and good size although a bit dated. Breakfast is fresh and plentiful, although can be busy but well organised. On bus route and underground stations nearby.

title: Clean, safe and good value hotel in London.
text: This hotel is actually at West Brompton Tube not Earl's Court. It is clean, comfortable and great value for London. The room was a little warm (like many similar hotels, it had air conditioning that seemed to make little difference) but the beds were comfy, the bathroom clean and contained a shower and bath. The lifts were quick and staff friendly. A bus stop right outside takes you straight to Kensington/Knightsbridge (you can use your Oyster Card). The buffet breakfast was great and very good value. Ask for internet log-on details and you get free unlimited wifi! In summary, although it is a little further out than I would like, this hotel is a great alternative to the more expensive but less comfortable hotels closer to the centre.

title: Good location, easily accessible.
text: Stayed here with my partner as we had a gig in Camden and dinner in Chelsea

title: Location
text: Location is excellent with parking on site. Ok prices for the area. Check in staff friendly and efficient. Rooms nice size, could be updated a little. Shower room again needs updating, but was clean. £17 per 24 Hours is the parking rate.

title: Brilliant for the price
text: I was a bit skeptical about booking this hotel due to a number of negative reviews on here however, I was very happy I decided to book this hotel anyway as it turned out to be very good especially given the price. It's not the most amazing hotel you could stay at but I'd say you would get very good value for money here. The rooms weren't too small especially when considering hotel rooms tend to be quite small in London. Hotel and room were clean and maid service was quite good. The bed was comfortable, and we had everything we could possibly need. There are 4 lifts available which is very convenient and I loved the fact that they had a vending machine with basic everyday stuff you may need (toothbrush, toothpaste, paracetamol, etc), this was very convenient. Apart from this, the location was excellent as it's super close to West Brompton station so you can get around London very easily. There were plenty of lovely restaurants around the area and it was also a nice and safe neighborhood and was very quiet so we had no troubles sleeping, which is something we had experienced previously when staying in other locations in London. We also had dinner at the restaurant on one of our evenings and were very happy with the food. All in all we had a lovely stay at this hotel and would definitely stay again :)

title: Big hotel with nice room and nice breakfast
text: The hotel is big (ten stairs), near from the London tube (district line, which allow to go to museums, Big Ben and tower of London without any change). The room is quite correct for a London hotel price (80 $). You have a TV, a double bed and a desk. The bathroom is big, with a phone (!) and a speaker which transmits the sound of the TV. My room was at the 7th floor, and I had a good view on the town. The reception was a bit unpersonal and the people there were not very helpful. They just wanted my credit card. The breaksfast cost 7 £ per person and is very correct with a large choice of meals (continental and english breakfast). You can eat at the hotel but I didn't try the restaurant. I didn't see any restaurant around the hotel. It is better to eat downtown. Around the hotel everything was calm and I didn't have any trouble. I will certainly come back to this hotel the next time I come to London.
