title: OK
text: No real problems. Washbasin waste was blocked. Car park is useful. Fairly handy for West Brompton station on district line. Full breakfast is good but cheaper rates may include only a less substantial second class continental breakfast buffet in the bar. Check.

title: Comfy Hotel
text: A fantastic tower building hotel with full service, large room, helpful staff and good customer service. Also the speceous ILEC Conference Centre could accomodate people for different events, exhibition and and occassions.

title: Sixth visit
text: We chose to stay again at this hotel, over the Easter break. Still very happy with it. The rooms and breakfast are good value for London and the location by West Brompton underground/overground station is very convenient. Although a large chain hotel they had made the place appropriate for Easter for the large number of tourist families staying there.

title: Good hotel with nice pub attached
text: We arrived early, but our room was already available. The staff are quiet friendly, even gave a tour of the dining room buffet, but we chose to try the 'pub' next to it, which was great. There are also other real pubs in the area which are good for eating at. Our room was on the seventh floor, so was quiet. There is a new lift near reception, which is quieter than the main lifts. The hotel is near a tube station, so London attractions are not far away. Would stay there again, the room of reasonable size and clean. The only problem, was the hot water in the shower was sometimes not so hot!

title: For the price it is a good deal
text: The hotel was basic but ideal for a short trip in London, if you're not going to be spending a lot of time in the hotel it is fine. Bed was comfortable, had no problems with our room. Airplanes flying overhead weren't a problem at night, other doors do shut loud but at night time it wasn't too noisy. At one point a couple in the next door room were arguing and it was a little irritating but that isn't the hotels fault. Bathroom was good and provided soap, toilet paper and shampoo. Overall a good stay, nice staff and would stay here again for a short trip!

title: Very Good loaction - decent 3 star hotel.
text: Hotel is in a great location - within 3 mins to Earls Court Exhibition Centre. The hotel has good facilities with a nice bar and decent restauraunt. The rooms are small but well kitted out - they could do with a bit of updating though! The bathroom did look like it had been refurbished and was really nice - overall I would say that this hotel is a decent 3 star hotel.

title: Good location, spacious room
text: Located just minutes away from West Brompton underground, very convenient. Room is spacious but rather old. Still a good choice!

title: Excellent Ibis in London
text: This hotel has to be the most well appointed Ibis, carpeted floors, decent wooden furniture and comfortable bed. Spacious marble effect bathroom with towels and soap/gel dispensers provided. Tea/coffee making supplied. Room was air conditioned, and quiet being on 11th floor. Good bar in the style of an English Pub, also with traditional cask ale on tap. Extensive selection for breakfast in a large and always busy breakfast room. Efficient and pleasant staff on reception. Location 5 mins walk from West Brompton Underground and Overground station. Usually good value rates here so is a regular stop off for me.

title: Very dated, but ok for an overnight stay
text: Good location, very close to West Brompton station. Service at check-in was fine, agreed to what I thought was a deal for a cheaper breakfast, but the following morning this had not gone through to the breakfast reception and I refused to eat there because of it (not keen on paying for expensive hotel breakfasts). They did at least sort this at the main reception by making sure the breakfast charge was removed from my bill. The room was ok, just looked very dated. Wifi worked well.

title: Decent hotel
text: The room was nothing special, but it was clean and had enough space. Wifi was free and reliable and we got a good deal with the room - between the two of us, it probably would have cost us the same to stay at a hostel! The front desk staff were helpful. The Hotel has a convenient location. It is within easy walking distance of two tube stations (different lines) and there are bus stops right outside. It is also within fairly easy walking distance of several London tourist attractions (such as Buckingham Palace) if you want some exercise. Unfortunately the hotel doesn't have a fitness room which is a shame as it's such a big hotel. Our only problem was with the breakfast which we opted for on one day, it was overpriced and poorly-organised. We had to wait for a long time to be allocated a table as it was full. The food was average at best and the staff were completely useless in terms of organising people, replacing the food, and dealing with requests.

title: Good hotel
text: Good hotell Close to the tube. Large rooms and very silence. nice and friendly staff. Really good cleaning of rooms. Restaurang in the house too. Only bad thing was that the bed was little hard. ´Nice area close to the lobby.

title: Good Location
text: I stayed at the Ibis with my mother recently. The room was alright, it was clean, there was room to put our suitscases and hang clothing up. The heating worked well and the bathroom was clean. I thought the staff were quite helpful. I was frustrated, however, that there was no bar fridge to store food in and a tiny, almost useless hair dryer. The Ibis is a couple of hundred metres away from the West Brompton Underground Station. This is the best thing about the Ibis, it was just so convenient. I was also never concerned about returning back to the hotel late at night, the road you walk along between the Station and Ibis was a main road, well lit and always very busy.

title: Clean, performing, close to center and a true bargain
text: I often use Accor Hotels when I travel because of their quality/price balance. This hotel is near West Brompton Tube Station and it is a perfect place for sleeping. You get a standard international service for good money. I sugest you to ask for rooms on higher floors to avoid the city noise.

title: Ethics
text: The most important to choose the hotel is the ethics and no need to change it when use ,they can serve you in an easy way with no need to pay. Comfort room , any kind of room you can reserve , full room service.

title: Concert Trip
text: Really nice location and hotel rooms were perfectly adequate. Value for money and staff were helpful and pleasant which always helps in a hotel situation. Enjoyed the breakfast following morning. Will stay again.

title: Decent hotel in a good location
text: Ibis Earl's Court is just your average hotel where you can get a good night sleep after tiring day touring and walking around the London. HIGH POINTS 1) Good Location close to train station and everything else 2) Clean Bathroom 3) We got it a a cheap rate before prices started to rise 4) Breakfast to get your day started but I would suggest to have hard boiled eggs too

title: WORST HOTEL SPECIALY THE NIGHT MANAGER
text: DO NOT COME TO THIS hell HOLE with he worst behaved staff. They are biased towards the white and don’t respect the customers. The night security manager is the worst and does not have the slightest sense of courtesy. He threatens and acts as if he is the gangster of the hotel ! VERY BAD EXPERIENCE

title: Conference booking
text: Stayed for works conference room clean bed comfy. Not the smallest room for London rooms let's face it all London rooms are small and I could swing a cat in it and that's a good judge. Plenty of hanging space and not far from west brom tube. Reasonably priced so no complaints quick check in and check out. Only compliant cleaner banging on door at 8am to clean is a bit much

title: Breakfast could be a lot better
text: The location is good, although the pavements between the hotel and tube are very uneven, bit of a struggle with a case. My room was acceptable, nothing special. The staff were on the whole very good and helpful. Breakfast was a huge disappointment. This Ibis would benefit from following the example of the Ibis hotels in France and Spain, who are providing an exceptional continental breakfast at the moment.

title: Horrible rooms
text: Really horrible, small, dated room. For a chain like Ibis, this unacceptable. The pub is awful, so dated, needs complete refurb and, the microwave menu is as disappointing as the decor. Not even a small gym in a 4 star hotel. Restaurant closed at night. I would not recommend ever.

title: Affordable budget hotel, great location.
text: Great location, closest tube station being West Brompton on the district line, however Earls Court tube station is also within walking distance, occupying both district and Piccadilly line. All main areas of central London with easy reach. First impressions of the hotel itself are very welcoming, clean, spacious and friendly. Easy, quick and convenient check in/out service. We stayed in a triple room (3 single beds) the room was very basic as expected, though had everything you needed to hand. Clean with enough space for 3 people to move around in. Bathroom was a relative size with working bath/shower. Beds were ok, though not the most comfiest of beds, however were fine for a 1 night stay. Good working Wi-Fi within the hotel grounds. Would recommend for convenient budget hotel stay.

title: Very pleasant stay
text: Chose this hotel through Air Canada Vacations. The room was very clean and bright. Good service by staff. Close to West Brom station. The all-you-can-eat breakfast was spectacular - fresh and tasty! Would return to this hotel.

title: Functional, location and value for money
text: London can be quite expensive - we all know that. Ibis Earl's Court gives us the opportunity to stay in central London without breaking too much from the budget. It offered a room spacious enough to rest and accommodate this solo traveller, with facilities that one might need for a convenient stay (tea-making facilities for instance). The receptionists at the front desk were very efficient and warm. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Great weekend
text: A basic room but good value. An extremely comfortable bed. There was a problem with the door lock but they sorted it out very quickly, giving us another room. The staff were very friendly, if a little inefficient in the restaurant. The location was very convenient, within walking distance of Olympia and close to a tube station. A very enjoyable stay

title: Ibis earls court london
text: My husband, young daughter 2.5 years old and I stayed at hotel ibis earls court London from September 3-6 2014. Rooms were neat and clean the only small critique we had was there was no bar fridge which would have came in handy. The buffet breakfast was plentyful with an option for everyone. The hotel is located close to the tube, bus stop & convience stores. The information desk in the foyer was happy to help with any queries we had! All in all a pleasant stay at this hotel for our first time in London!

title: Happy! Happy!
text: This is the surprisingly the best of Ibis Hotel i have ever stayed so far! The room is big. There is an electric kettle in the room with complimentary tea/coffee. Toiletries as with other Ibis Hotel are just soap dispensers. Just bring along your shampoo & body lotion. There is a clothline in the bathroom for you to hang your wet clothes. Breakfast was brilliant. Staff very helpful. Location is good. You can easily get to central London via public transport. I stayed here for 5 days & used bus no 74 to get to & fro the hotel (didn't try the tube but I'm sure easy as well). There are various tour agents at the concierge should you want to tour England. Overall, I was happy. Will stay here when I'm in London.

title: Ibis a Little Staid or Just what Tourists want
text: This Hotel is a large facility from a major hotel group, location is good with an eclectic surrounding area that will entice tourists to investigate and enjoy the area. Because the hotel is part of a large group, they have lost that personnel touch, which is reflected in all areas from the rooms to the public areas. The meals I attended were self help, with good choice and prepared to a good standard. The staff were there, but could not say they were attentive. For purpose a good choice, however and with a little planning, better places are available.

title: A week in a comfortable setting
text: A basic hotel with everything you would normally require. We would stay again without hesitation. With West Brmpton tube station within an easy walk, you can get anywhere in the region quickly. Staff were friendly and earnestly helped when asking for reviews on local nearby eateries. We really enjoyed our full breakfast buffets. The Pub here is good as well.

title: Great stay...Certainly haunted...
text: I had a fantastic stay here, however I was a little unnerved by a shadowy figure that was wondering the halls during the night time and I came back to my room to find all the wardrobe doors open and bath running. I spoke to a member of staff who said that this figure has been spotted over the years, apparently it's the ghost of a former staff member who fell to his death in the elevator shaft in the early 1900's, he wanders the 11th and 12th floors and stays close to certain guests of the hotel. CREEPY! But still an enjoyable stay!

title: Decent No Frills Hotel
text: If you just need a place to lay your head at night this hotel will meet your needs. It's quiet and clean and has all of the essentials, but could not be described as luxurious in any way. The restaurant and pub are well kept and serve decent fare (the fish and chips are pretty good). The room decor is a bit dated and sparse

title: Can't understand why people have left bad reviews...
text: Stayed at this hotel last night and I cannot say anything bad about it! The staff were so friendly and nice to speak to upon arrival and they were so helpful the parking facilities are a bonus and overall the hotel is lovely! Would definitely stay there again!

title: Excellent!
text: Stayed at this hotel on 17 November 2012 for 1 night with my husband. We arrived early and checked in without a problem. We had a room on the 10th floor, it was small but comfortable. We got the tube into the centre of London from West Brompton Tube Station, which, if you come out the hotel and turn left is almost straight up the road in front of you (over the bridge). Coming back to the hotel we got off the tube at Earls Court and had a 15 minute walk back round to the hotel! The bed was comfy, in fact, I had aa great nights sleep! Air conditioning in the rooms, plenty of towels in the bathroom. The TV was a bit dodgy, sometimes the remote would work it and other times it wouldn't, think it just needed new batteries! All in all a very pleasant stay, excellent location into London. Although arrive as early as possible as the hotel car park isn't that big and quite tight to manover around in a big car. It also costs £17 which is quite expensive but it is very convenient.

title: A Good Base
text: The Ibis Earls Court is a good base from which to explore. It's a short walk from the Earls Court (Piccadilly & District) and West Kensington (District) Underground stations - and from there London is your oyster. The hotel rooms are comfortable and clean. Also, the higher your floor the better the view across West London. The "George & Dragon" bar is designed to be jolly old London pub -- which it isn't. It is also really busy when Chelsea FC play at home (Stamford Bridge isn't far away). The restaurant is buffet style, has great food with a differing selections each time. And they have really helpful staff that have helped my out on more than one occasion.

title: Great value
text: Took the hotel as a package tour and stayed an extra week. Clean , curious staff. Breakfast is fantastic allow might have been better with pot cereal or oatmeal. Great assess to the underground a block away. Area is Ok but again everything is so close. I'd stay again

title: Ok
text: The hotel is within a five minute or less walk to the West Brompton tube station, so is close to public transport. The rooms are clean, but nothing special. In fact, my room was quite small and really had no where to open my suitcase (hard case style). I can't imagine two people in the room. Also, the walls are paper thin and you can hear everything. The hotel is used by a lot of tour companies which can be a detraction as well.

title: Outstanding Customer Service and Cleanliness
text: As an almost weekly visitor to this hotel, I cannot recommend highly enough. The key areas for me being Service and Cleanliness are exceptional in my opinion. This is a credit to Ioannis Koletakis and his excellent team. An extremely friendly, efficient and welcoming environment!

title: Great start point
text: If you are looking for a great starting point to explore London,this is it. The hotel is well located within a half a kilometre from West Brompton tube station. Walk out the front door and turn right and keep walking to the tube station. The hotel has a great buffet breakfast and should be taken advantage of. The rooms are small but livable. Careful watching the TV, I received a bill for 5£ for watching the BBC news. The hotel pub is not very realistic so go out the front door, turn left,walk about 500 metres to the stoplight and look left. The "Moose" is a pub that offers good lagers and ale and....two for one meal deals for £7.95. There is a fabulous Italian restaurant with a patio that serves excellent food. All in all good value. It's a shame very few of the hotel staff speak English but they managed to be very helpful.

title: Chain hotel in convenient location
text: My twin room was comfortable and quiet, and provided what I needed for a business trip away from home. Clean, friendly staff and WiFi that works. Not much character, but wasn’t expecting it! Breakfast ok too. Convenient location, about 15 mins walk from Earls Court tube and 5 from West Brompton.

title: Average, no more no less. Uninspiring dated hotel.
text: We stayed at the Ibis Earls Court as we got a good price and were in London to attend a gig. Although part of the Ibis chain it is clear that this hotel had a former life, and ibis have done little to update it, and it lacks the efficient and clean appearance of its other hotels. The hotel is close to West Brompton Tube Stop and a short walk away from Earls Court station. The area felt safe at night, and there are a selection of takeaways near by. Check in involved the minimum levels of politeness, and although we got a room straight away, there were a lot of angry people who were being told to wait - apparently check in and check out are both at 2pm for some rooms!! We passed on the breakfast due to the negative reviews on here, and instead went to Wetherspoons. Rooms had dated furniture, although did have a flat screen tv. Cleanliness was average, although the shower head was covered in an unknown orange substance - looks like it could have done with a good clean! The hotel is open for anyone to walk in and there seems to be little security features. On the back of our room door there were four screw holes where a security chain had once been - I am not sure if this was removed by the hotel or by someone looking to break in in the near future! Bed was ok, although as I had been on my feet all day I would have probably been able to sleep on a floor! All in all, I would return, only if there was nothing else going and now I know exactly what to expect. Still the price was good for London........

title: Nice-ish hotel, if over-priced
text: Stayed here whilst exhibiting in the exhibition hall downstairs, so highly convenient for my own purposes. Location close to the tube is spot on. But rooms are pricey. I predict that when Earl's Court Exhibition Centre opposite closes, prices may soften a little..... Bedrooms are excellent and very clean. I was on the top floor so had stunning views over London. They have a very dated "pub"-style bar on the first floor. I stayed at this hotel years ago and this bar hasn't changed. It is very down-market and jaded and badly needs updating. Bar staff do very little to give extra service. When the bar closed we all had to troop downstairs to the reception foyer area where there was a limited bar service at top prices, which didn't go down at all well. Why not just keep the bar open?? The restaurant looks very new and has a real contemporary feel - only had breakfast but it was excellent. The exhibition hall is five-star (if anyone reading this is interested!)

title: Value and convenient
text: The lobby is large and inviting. Rooms are a good size and fresh. The bed and pillows were really comfy. Check in was smooth. We ate in the restaurant and the on site pub, but would probably try the pub across the road next time as the food was quite bland. We used the tube to get around which was really easy ( even for first timers) from the West Brompton tube station just down the road. It cost about £8 for a day ticket.

title: Thumb up for ibis earl's court
text: The hotel was just a few minutes walk far from West Brompton tube station. The room was clean and comfortable. The staff was really helpful and kind. Ideal location, near to the citu.I higly recommend this hotel.

title: Great hotel great location
text: visited over November. great hotel with efficient check in staff. great room on 12th floor with great views of the city. windows well insulated to keep out the heavy traffic outside and inside hotel is lovely and not noisy although it is a big hotel. only disappointment was pizza which promised to be thin crust but was just a tortilla base. Otherwise would definitely reccomend to other travellers and well worth the money.

title: Not sure why it's a three star!
text: Although the location was great, the hotel was definatly lacking. Had to change room as our 1st was flithy and had not heat. Had to argue with the front desk that heat was important. Second room was marginally cleaner, but very small and atleast had heat. Fortunatly we did not spend a tone of time there. Breakfast was good. Very busy hotel. Should not be advertised as a 3 star, should be listed as a 2 star.

title: Average
text: Overall average experience. The elevators and general appearance of the hotel could be improved. The TV was a bit cranky and there were intermittent noises that indicated electrical leaks, which was disturbing, as was the fact that people(misguided guests) tried to enter my room while I was obviously in there.

title: Great value for london
text: Stayed only 1 night. The staff were very helpful & the rooms were very clean. Breakfast was quite adequate with plenty of choice. We stayed in room 930 which had a huge 7ft bed I don't know if this is the same in all the rooms but we didn't pay any extras. Would stay again if staying in this part of london

title: Good-ish.
text: The hotel is conveniently close to West Brompton tube-station, wifi is fine, rooms are nice and clean, and as such, its nicely worth the money. However, there were some odd things: the bar had a system where you have to find your own table and order your edibles with table number. Several customers didn't seem to be comfortable with that. Also you might want to skip the pizzas that appeared to be picked up from freezer of nearest Tesco. And oh, bath towel left on the floor wasn't replaced.

title: What a pleasant surprise
text: We booked this hotel purely because it was near to the venue we were going to that evening. For the price we paid we were amazed to find a large reception area which was beautifully decorated for Christmas and had a concierge desk. Room was good, breakfast delicious. The only slight problem was a chilly room, but a top up radiator was provided which helped.

title: ok for the money...
text: Booked in through Trafalgar Tours, was not impressed after staying in 2 different rooms. No A/C so you sleep (in summer) with windows open to street noise below. Beds are hard and pillows are even harder and flat. Bathrooms were musty-smelling, tiling grout was missing. The continental breakfast was meager. Due to high tour traffic, check-in can be an arduous task. On the plus side, Marta at the front desk was very professional, even when facing an ocean of people checking in. And the walk to the nearest tube was very easy. The neighborhood is not the best, not the worst. There are several shops and pubs nearby where one can get a quick sandwich or a hot meal. After staying in Ibis hotels in 2 countries (on a tour), I can say that I won't stay again unless I have no other choice.

title: Our first stop on a Trafalgar tour, July 2016 (Costsaver)
text: This hotel is way out of the city centre, with very little nearby to do or see. It was booked for us through a coach tour. It was clean and comfortable. Breakfast was continental and fine. Kensington gardens and Hyde Park are walkable, but about 40 mins away. Its about a 5-10 min walk from the subway. Would I stay here again? No, due to location.

title: Below average, wouldn't go back
text: Stayed here for one night in May on business. I had the same problem that others have had with the key, twice I went down to reception before someone came up and sorted it for me. Checking in was awful. When I was finally seen to, the process of checking-in took a good 10-15 minutes. I had dinner at the bar and ordered a steak. I was stood at the bar waiting well over fifteen minutes to be served, I was the only one waiting and there were three members of staff. They weren't busy at all, just painstakingly slow. My steak arrived very quickly but at £13, I would've sent it back if I wasn't claiming back on expenses. The steak was rubbery and the chips tasted undercooked. Room was OK, bed was comfortable enough. I was surprised that there was no mini shampoo in the bathroom and the drain in the bath was blocked so the bath filled up as I was using the shower. Checking out was also a disaster, my employer booked the hotel direct online but the card wasn't charged and they asked for another card... My employer then sent a fax (twice) to confirm they could charge the original card for the stay, which took the receptionist ten minutes to find. Overall the hotel is in a convenient location, rooms are good and there is free wifi, but it's ruined by haphazard service

title: Ibis Earls Court
text: Excellent two day stay. Room was super, on 11th floor, very spacious and had two bigger than usual single beds. Beautiful views towards The Shard in the distance. Staff very polite and extremely helpful. They knew everything we needed to know about buses and tube services and where to change to get to the London attractions we were headed for. Breakfast had everything you can think of and was well presented. Our stay was excellent value considering we were in central London, would certainly use this one again.

title: very good
text: I would book again, its not the cheapest, but it is very value for money. The food is good, location is good. Staff are very helpful, parking is excelent. I would book again, its not the cheapest, but it is very value for money. The food is good, location is good. Staff are very helpful, parking is excelent.

title: Average Hotel
text: You just get what you paid for. That's it. They need to send some of their staff for Customer Service training as they are not very friendly and not so helpful. Overall experience is average, was okay.

title: Dodgy Mini cabs
text: Stayed at the Ibis last month and was extremely unhappy when i asked for a Taxi but was sent a mini cab. I asked to be taken to Saint Pauls Cathedral but the driver had never heard of it and asked for a post code!! I exited the car and hailed down what i wanted the first time around. A Black Cab. The driver obviously knew where Saint Pauls Cathedral and i got me there quickly and at a reasonable price. You can always rely on a london Taxi

title: Do not book any tours with Ibis staff
text: We were in Ibis Earl Court for 8 days. Good things: Clean, comfortable, close to public transport and market Bad things: We had booked two trip with Ibis court and both were booked wrong. We ended up paying more on our first trip. The driver was very good and drove us to a different destination instead and second trip was completely cancelled by Evans and Evans touring company and we were not informed about it and ended up spending a full day in the hotel room. Ibis court manager was not considerate to give us a refund or any compensation to us when our tours were wrongly booked and cancelled. Only explanation we got was it was mistake of the touring company. That was very disappointing. There was one more family in the hotel who had problems with Evans and Evans organized tour. The supplies in the rooms were not replaced unless reminded every day.

title: nice rooms same about door key
text: I loved the hotel it was nice and clean BUT the door cards are a nightmare it took me 10 mins before i had to go back down 10 floors to tell the desk and they gave me anothe card and told me to swip it slowly so i went back up 10 floors and tried again but still couldnot open the door so i went back down and told them it wont work so the lady who was very nice followed me back up and she then swiped the card very very very slowly and it worked so it took me about 20-25 mins before i could get in my room so i suggest to any one who stays there to ask a member of staff to open the door for you.

title: Very handy for Earls Court and Stamford Bridge
text: Stayed at this hotel on Saturday 30th November for the Chelsea v Southampton game the following day. Very clean and friendly hotel, but looking a bit old in places. The hotel also has its own pub on the first floor which is really handy!

title: Be aware before you stay!
text: This hotel was booked for me through a travel agency as the starting and ending hotel for a 2 week motor coach tour. We stayed a total of 4 nights. After arriving late due to weather difficulty, we relaxed for some time. We had theater tickets for that evening (which we had been planning for many months), and I went to the concierge/information desk. I asked for the quickest and easiest way to get to the West End for our show, explaining that I did not know London, nor was I familier with the subways. Expecting them to say they would fetch us a cab, they instead directed us to the tube insistang that the stations were very near where we needed to go. Well, the 2 minute walk to the first station was not 2 minutes, especially for someone dressed up in heels. After getting turned around in the West End, we missed the first part of our show. At the conclusion of our trip, I again went to the concierge and asked for them to arrange transportation to the airport. The concierge was obviously incompletely trained, and told me numerous times that he did not know how to do it. After finally finding the books for reservations, he couldn't find the right numbers. He called his supervisor (I assume at home) and was told to tell us that 1) the hotel doesn't do this (even though they had a book of reservations), and 2) I would have to make all the calls myself (even though the sign on the desk says that they would arrange pick-ups). After getting the concierge to talk to the hotel manager, he called a number for transportation and was placed on hold. After 30 minutes, I asked if there was another way to get to the airport, he suggested a cab which would have cost us another 2 GBP! He supposedly scheduled this for us. The next morning a cab pulls up in front of the hotel. He tells us that it is normally 45 GBP to the airport (not 32) but that he would be willing to take us for 32. Furthermore, he had no knowledge of us needing to go to the airport. One person in our group was advised to take the subway to the airport (lugging 50 pound suitcases up a hill to a subway station with no elevators) when she clearly asked for a cab! The rooms are very small. Alone, this would not disappoint me, but we found that the carpets were stained and patched together, the beds were very uncomfortable, and the sheets smelled. While Accor advertises breakfast until noon, this is not the case, as breakfast ends at 10am here. While this is fine for most business travelers, this is less than helpful if you are coming from US time zones, or are trying to get back to US sleep schedules (where 10am in London is 2-5 am in our time zones) If you are familiar with London and understand the subway system, this facility is reasonably close, and may serve your needs. If you are an unfamilar traveler, be warned. The concierge desk does not listen to your requests, they will give misleading advice, and are less than helpfull.

title: London Stay
text: Old room (no renovation for furnitures / floor) Kettle not clean No coffee stick refill Good location (near a metro station) Rapid Check in / out No other comments for this stay

title: Good Hotel
text: I stayed here for 4 nights on this occasion but have stayed here twice before. I stay here as it is very close to West Brompton tube station, which is only 5 stops from Wimbledon. It is also easy to travel to London Centre. From our room, we could just about see the London Eye! It is a basic hotel, with no room service etc but that is to be expected for the price. However, the rooms are clean and the beds are comfortable. The only thing I'd say is that the curtains do not cover the whole window area and during the summer, the sun beams in at 6am waking me up. An iron in the room would have been nice too. I know a lot of people have said the breakfast was great but I personally did not like it, but I guess that's just a personal preference. Overall I would definitely recommend it and I will return

title: Good value for money
text: Stayed here in a twin room whilst at the cake and bake show in earls court exhibition centre. Staff friendly and helpful, allowed us to check in at 9 am which was great after 3 am start! Close to earls court and west brompton station, we travel in from heathrow, took around 30 minutes and cost £3 ish great value. Room was clean, basic, just as you would expect from 3 star hotel, breakfast was very good, great choice. Only complaint, the lofts must have been the slowest in London and the stairs not well sign posted, meaning we ended up in the bowels of the hotel trying to get out!! Concierge very helpful. Would definitely stay again if going to exhibition centre.

title: VALUE FOR MONEY
text: Next time I travel to London I will book this hotel again ! The location is just perfect : the Easybus from Gatwick stops exactly in front of the hotel, the West Brompton tube is just 5 minutes walking from the hotel and the bust stop to reach Fulham is just next to the hotel! The lobby is very big and always clean. The reception staff is efficient and attentive. We had a superior room on the 12th floor: very nice view, very spacious room, very comfy beds with the chance to get an extra pillow from the guardrobe, TV, radio, kettle, tea and coffee,very quiete, pretty clean (a bit too dusty the carpet under the curtains),big bathroom. We had to buy a bar of soap and shampoo as they don't have any courtesy set but that's fair enough for the price you pay. We did not have breakfast in the hotel but we went to the pub which is on the 1st floor of the building and it was a very nice experience: they serve good food until 11.00 pm.

title: ok...
text: The hotel beds were comfotable, rooms were clean, but there were a couple of things I did not like. Continental breakfast got old, quick. There were no clocks in the rooms, or directories or pen and paper (things that are normally there). Also, I did not enjoy the food in the restaurant at all. Everywhere else I went in London had great food. Location is good, close to Tube station. All in all ok, but lacking some basic things.

title: Nicer than I expected from an Ibis
text: Was wowed with a lovely reception area, that was as good as it got. Room was a double bed with a little walkway to each side of it, but only wanted somewhere to sleep so that didn’t concern me. Only problem was it was hot on a night but couldn’t have windows open due to the air conditioning system been on roof below our windows, which was too noisy with window open. Full cooked buffet breakfast was £17 so had it as a treat on my last day.

title: we didnot like it and will avoid it in future
text: hotel was a kind of run-down...staff a little indifferent. Room was no great ,with fixtures coming apart.Breakfast which was included with room tariff was a big let down...same stuff every day and of mediocre quality. At $95 per day /per person ( we were charged $180 for two of us ) , it was a rip-off.

title: not as good as usual
text: been to your hotel a few times lately as we do not spend lots of money on a hotel, that's why we use you....your lifts were not working properly, took us over half an hour to exit your hotel after already giving up on breakfast as it took us too long to get into the restaurant due to the lift problem. we followed the staircase down as far as we could but spoke to a contractor, not your staff, who told us there was a lift problem but no signs had been put out. your location is excellent for what we need but we are already looking for somewhere else. spent over 20 mins in a lift from the 2nd floor to the ground level, up and down to the 12th floor and back. your hotel/bar staff are very pleasant but struggle with english, it'sbritains capital and we expect more from a so called leading hotel.

title: Great location and excellent price
text: We stayed here as part of a flight and hotel package. When we checked in and went to the room, and discovered two single beds when I'd asked the package seller for a double bed. I went back and asked the front desk whether we could have a double and they happily changed it and had it remedied in less than a minute and explained that the package seller noted 2 single beds. Room was small but clean and had a great view! The bathroom had a tub in it and not just a shower. The tv has a good selection of channels for relaxing in the evening. Breakfast was included in the room and was fresh, hot and had a good variety of foods. Parking was affordable and convenient. The tube station is a couple minutes' walk away, as was the car rental place. We will likely return again.

title: Room OK, but watch out for service charges in bar
text: The room was fine and the hotel is in a handy location for tube and train stations. However, we were a bit shocked at the prices in the hotel pub which were not only very high, even by London standards, but also included a 10% service charge! Considering that drinkers have to go to the bar and colect drinks themselves, adding on a service charge seems out of order to me.

title: Poor Staff but great location
text: Slight walk to West Brompton station, makes it very convenient. This is my second time here. Rooms are comfortable and well maintained. Good quality AC. Bathroom was roomy for 2 people! Surprising for ibis!! Service was slow - I specifically requested the room to be ready by a particular time during booking. But no heed was taken despite acknowledgement from the hotel. & they gave a rude response and not ready to listen. Wifi was fast and easy to connect. Would stay again provided service is improved.

title: A very good place to stay
text: It's the third time I come to Earls Court, London and the third time I sleep in the Ibis Hotel Earls Court : a great hotel, employees always charming people, no problems, rooms kept cleared everyday without any kind of problem, a good place to stay a few minutes only from the Earls Court Centre which is ideal place when exhibiting there and the proximity of West Brompton and Earls Court tube is just perfect. I recommend it !

title: Good Location
text: The hotel is well located, very near to West Bromptom tube and close to Earls Court tube. It caters for the big bus tours so breakfast time is a frenzied meal. The beds are comfortable and we had a great view over London. The soap and shampoo are dispensed via a dispenser so bring your own shampoo. The tea and coffee supplies (no biscuits) were limited in the rooms, but the concierge was happy to supply more. Staff are efficient, some are friendly some are not. I was very happy at this hotel as it was easy to get home to.

title: Ibis Earls Court
text: Rooms were quite small and basic. Room only had one light switch which meant when going to the bathroom you had to switch on all of the lights! This was a nightmare during the night! TV was state of the art wish this could of been said for the poor quality hairdryer!

title: Good Hotel & Handy for Earls Court
text: Just 5 minutes walk from Earls Court & West Brompton station, this hotel was really nice for a short stay. The room was small but not too small. It had plenty of drawer & hanging space. Very clean throughout, comfortable bed, nice bathroom. We don't usually eat in hotels preferring to venture out but the 'all you could eat' evening buffet was too good to miss at only £10 each (usually £15 apparently!). We didn't try the breakfast buffet, preferring to go to The Coffee Shop up the road (worth a visit!). I noticed a previous review that said the lifts were rubbish. They were in the process of being refurbished when we were there (1 at a time!) and we had no problem with them. Would we stay again? Definitely.

title: Good hotel for London
text: We stayed as a family of four adults

title: conveniently located tourist hotel
text: Just down the street a couple blocks to the West Brompton tube stop, this hotel was quite convenient for our explorations of London. A few blocks farther on, lots of small restaurants and pubs. The rooms are small, but comfortable. Breakfast was included with lots of variety to choose from. We started our tour here and the desk folks were knowledgeable and helpful getting us started exploring on our own before meeting our tour director.

title: Convenient Hotel
text: I booked this Hotel as I was in London on business and it was reasonably local to where I needed to be. The big advantage was it had a car park with residents discounts! Good clean hotel with friendly staff. Breakfast was extra but also good. Room was high up with a great views, I could see The Oval plus most of South London.

title: Good Bargain Hotel
text: Stayed 5 nights over at Ibis and was glad we made the right choice. Hotel lobby looked considerably modern and they have comfortable seating area at the lobby. Despite the hotel had alot of tourist buses, they managed to arrange their guests professionally in order not to make their lobby looking chaotic, plus point for that. Their hotel rate was reasonable and location wise, it was located not too far for the tube station, about 3-5mins walk away, however it's not on the main line. You might need to change lines abit to get to the tourist spots but no complains because the hotel was located in a safe neighbourhood, so it's alright to walk back to the hotel late at night. We booked a standard queen bed room and it is abit small but good for 2 person. Nothing luxurious but it was clean and had bits of modern fittings such as the light fixtures and lcd flat tv which offers quite a number of channels. Bathroom was alright, considered acceptable size compared to some other london budget hotels I stayed before. Breakfast was included in our booking and we find it a good selections of hot and cold dishes offered. However it will be advisable to confirm with the check-in counter whether your room rate includes full breakfast or continental. If it's only continental, then it's located at another section of the dining area where there's only few selections of breads and pastries offered. You will find quite a number of small restaurants over at Earls Court station which is about 5-8 mins walk away. Definitely a good choice for budget travelers.

title: What a joke, this is not a no smoking hotel
text: This place is joke. They advertise as a non-smoking hotel but the scent of smoke runs rampant in the halls. One cannot even open their window because every window that is already open is being used by smokers and the smell drifts into the room. Obviously my neighbor is smoking because my bathroom smells like an ashtray. I complained numerous times And I was told, nothing we can do about it, the hotel cannot control people. Well, I can control my actions and I will never stay in an ibis hotel again. The customer service response tells tales about the state of this place. This is a real shame because the hotel is in a nice location near the west brompton and earls court tube stations on the district and Piccadilly lines. And there are some great restaurants nearby like 222 vegan veggie and lily tandoori. Not to mention a really good breakfast in the hotel. So, the hotel is what you'd expect from an ibis and is a solid three star in a good location at a great price. So if you are a non smoker who is affected by smoke do not even think about this place. If you are a smoker you can book here no problem just bring your own ashtray (byoa) because apparently there are no real rules against it.

title: Great location, good amenities
text: Stayed here for 6 nights during October 2012 for our first visit to London and we were not disappointed. Very convenient location near two Tube stations (West Brompton - 3 min walk and Earl's Court - 10 min walk). Rooms are small but clean and modern. As Canadians we are used to faceclothes and luckily we brought our own as none were provided. We had the buffet breakfast included in our package and it hit the spot with lots of choice and a good way to start each day before hitting the tube/city. Lots of pubs and stores in the neighbourhood (check out the Troubadour and the Blackbird). Good pub in hotel with decent menu. Free and fast wifi in room and pub.

title: My stay in London
text: The room and the services offered were ok and the rooms were well cleaned, the location was very good - near to restaurants and underground. The only exception is the breakfast, that isn't good at all.

title: Well it's got the bare necessities
text: I believe Ibis is primarily a business hotel which is fine. My husband and I were traveling to London in order to eventually get to Barcelona so we stayed a few days in Earls Court. For the most part Ibis has a decent location, I didn't expect anything fancy. It's literally 2 min walk from the West Brompton District line station which was quite convenient. There are a few pubs, restaurants and convenience stores nearby so at the very least if you're coming back late at night you could still get something to eat. So about the hotel...for one person the room would have been comfortable, for two we were a bit cramped with our 4 suitcases but that could probably be overlooked, after all the bathroom felt like it was half the size of the bedroom. I felt like Ibis was skimping on the towels though, and no facial tissues. Also no bar soap, just wall dispensers. So if dispensed liquid soap bothers any traveler, walk with your own. I had an allergic reaction to the soap at the hotel so perhaps that taints my review but only a little. Our room didn't have a safe which really bothers my husband because we don't like to leave valuables in our suitcases. No mini fridge

title: Good hotel fir the price, but really not near Earl's Court
text: I've stayed in Ibis hotels in other cities and countries, in my opinion Ibis Hotel Earl's Court was slightly better than other Ibis hotels. Rooms were nicer, air conditioning was relatively silent and effective and the rooms were actually soundproof. There were so many elevators you never need to wait too long. The free wifi worked well. The name of the hotel bothers me. Earl's Court is quite far from Lillie road. The Ibis chain has also named their Hotel in Prague Wenceslaw Square, even though it's a mile away. Even though I'm able to check to location on a map I still think this is misleading and deceiving, they are trying to make the location to appear better than it is. Location is quite good, if you have no luggage or you are not handicapped. This, of course, is not the hotel's fault in any way, but I have to warn all you fellow travellers: the nearest underground station West Brompton is only partially wheelchair accessible. The train coming from central London uses the easternmost tracks. There is no lift or escalator, you have to carry your suitcase all the way up. I had to carry a 20 kg suitcase when there was an exhausting heatwave in London. I was not very happy. In my country this would be considered a human rights violation, because a person who uses a wheelchair could not use the tube. Aren't there any kind of organizations, advocacy groups or legislation in the U.K. to protect the rights of disabled people? If you are planning to arrive to the hotel using the tube, please make sure you have no luggage or your suitcase has those amazing stair-climbing wheels. I also visited the hotel's pub. It was quite crowded and didn't understand the order system. The barmaid told us we have to know the number of our table to order anything, which was really weird. Beer was good, but the pizza I had tasted just like a low-quality, frozen pizza from the supermarket. The pub is ok for drinks, eat somewhere else. For it's price the hotel was otherwise quite nice. Staff was always friendly and helpful. The view from the 12th floor towards Wimbledon was really nice. Room was well equipped, only thing missing was an en-suite safety deposit box. Rooms are equipped with tv, kettle, iron and ironing board and hairdryer.

title: Spacious hotel
text: The hotel is conveniently located 100 m from the West Brompton metro station. There is a bus line 74 to Hyde Park and the view from the second floor of the bus is comparative to the tourist buses but costs only 1.30 pounds. The rooms are spacious and clean. The staff is friendly and responsive. The breakfast is lavish and if you manage to benefit some good offer, for example "3 for 2", this hotel is great deal. The area seemed quite safe and generally this is an expensive quarter - 30 m2 were sold for the price of half mio pounds eveident from the numerous real estate agencies boards. According to me this IBIS is one of the best within its brand. The only drawback I experienced during my stay was the lack of shampoo but to be honest I did not mentioned it to the staff. I suppose they would correct it.

title: Nice hotel
text: The hotel is quite convenient, close to West Brompton Station. There's a restaurant inside the hotel, which make the stay easier. However, there is one bad thing which is there's a cemetery near the hotel.

title: Good value hotel
text: We wer in this hotels almost two years ago, but we enjoyed our stay. Clean and quiet rooms. The room we stayed had a nice view and it was clean. We opted for the breakfast option, which was excellent and the breakfast room was very comfortable. This Ibis hotel is located in a quiet neighbourhood, good to rest.I would recommend this hotel to visitors/ tourists.

title: So expensive
text: It was so expensive and not overly impressive. Breakfast was unclear- two areas one was terrible one was extra but really nice. The beds were too hard. The location is a fair distance from the main attractions because of traffic. It cost about 25 pounds to go into town via taxi because of the terrible traffic at all hours of the day. The train station is near but found that to be expensive too, I may have been doing that wrong though

title: Good location - Lacking in Good old fashioned service
text: Called the Ibis a day or two prior to our arrival date tFo organize an early check-in availability of getting a better room as I had worked as Front Office Shift Leader at this hotel property many years ago when it was still the Ramada West London. As we were celebrating our 2nd honeymoon, I was very excited to show my husband where I used to live (around the corner in Redcliffe Gardens), play (at The Troubadour) and work! To sum up the experience - very poor communication especially with consierge and management. Lacking in warmth and hospitality. I get that it is a budget hotel and it is predominantly staffed by foreign workers but there are cheaper hotels out there that make you feel welcome and will go out of their way to ensure you have a good stay. If you want a quick basic, head down on pillow, in/out experience this is probably the place for you.

title: Nice place to stay for a citytrip in London
text: Location: the hotel is located in the centre of London. Underground station (West Brompton) is at about 300m from the hotel. The hotel is located in front of the Earl's Court exhibition center. I was there during the Games so the street was quiet. There are a lot of airplanes flying above the hotel but in the landing phase so it is not such a big issue. Count about 1 big hour walking from the hotel to reach the touristic center. the room: it was ok but nothing WAWWW. The room was clean but for example there was no fridge in the room (and so no mini bar). Painting was quite old. I read some people complaining about the noice but in my case it was ok. breakfast: it is ok, quite a big choice for the English breakfast. Restaurant room is standard with nothing special. It looks like an company restaurant. You receive a tray and go to the buffet :) Reception area is good. Employees are very friendly. There is an information desk to answer all your questions. PS: I gave a bad rate for the price/quality as I was there during the games and paid a lot for my room....

title: Perfect for single traveller
text: Enjoyed my stay here very much. Had a single room -- it was tiny, but that was part of its charm. It was cozy, clean, comfortable and quiet (my room overlooked a quiet residential street behind the hotel). All the staff I encountered were very friendly and helpful. The hotel is in a good neighbourhood and very close to the Underground. The building is old, but well kept, clean and quite modern. There is an Internet cafe directly across the street. Breakfast was decent -- croissants, cold cuts, cheese, yogurt, cereals, etc. Overall, a very good value, considering the hotel's good location within an expensive city. Would definitely stay here again.

title: Great hotel!
text: This is possibly the most comfortable bed I've ever found in a hotel! Our room was in the basement and so was very quiet and easily darkened although the windows allowed a lot of light during the day. Breakfast was a very satisfactory buffet. The location is exceptional in that it's 3 blocks to the tube which takes you anywhere in London.

title: Good hotel, shame about ongoing refurbishments
text: I don't know how value for money applies, as we booked through a discount site, but we booked one night stay in a twin room for £95, and it was in the run-up to christmas. The entire front of the hotel is covered in scaffolding, but our room was in the basement, so although we didn't have much of a view, the scaffolding didn't obstruct our view either. The included breakfast was nice, but fairly limited. I would definitely stay there again. I may post some photos of our rom if I get a chance.

title: Excellent location in a nice area
text: I had a five night stay at the Park International Hotel last week and thought it was excellent. I stayed in a standard double room as my friend was joining from Sweden for three nights. The room was a bit small, but very cozy and comfortable and all we needed as we were out and about all day, however, the bathroom and shower were very spacious. The cleaning staff did a great job and were in everyday to tidy up. The breakfast that is served in the mornings is very good with a variety of different options. The staff at the front desk were very friendly and helpful. I had actually booked the hotel for only 4 nights but then ended up staying for the extra 5th night and they easily accommodated my request even though the hotel was fully booked and gave me a very fair price. Even the bar/restaurant staff were very friendly I found, and the pianist that is there a few nights a week is fantastic. The location of the hotel is ideal when travelling around the city by the tube. The Gloucester Road underground station was about a 3 minute walk from the hotel and had three different lines there, (Picadilly, District and Circle lines) making it very easy to get around the city. Also made for a very easy departure back to Heathrow Airport as the you take the Picadilly line west, right from the Gloucester Road Station and takes only 35-40 minutes to get to the terminals. Cromwell Road (road hotel is on) is also off of a main street filled with lots of great restaurants and cafes, but also only a block away from very quiet streets in Chelsea and Kensington. I will be back in London shortly for business and plan on staying here again, based on the experience I just had.

title: Nice hotel for vacation
text: Great location, very close to Underground Gloucester Road station. One can take Piccadilly Line from Heathrow directly. In walking distance to Earl's Court Road where many restaurants and cafes locate. Also in walking distance to Kensington Palace, Hyder Park, and High Street Kingsonton. Nice and polite staff. Good services. Clean and comfort rooms and facilities.

title: Ho hum
text: With the dollar being so weak, we decided a 3 star hotel was all we coult afford if we were going to be able to also enjoy the sights. This hotel was really not more than a 2 star. The location was wonderful, a very short walk to the Underground and within walking distance of many famous museums, parks, etc. However, the lodgings themselves were bare bone. Front desk and concierge were adequate at most

title: Bit of a dive, actually
text: So I picked this hotel last year as part of a package when I visited London in late November of 2005. Price seemed right (though everything in London is overpriced) and the reviews didn't seem too bad, so I went with it. Well, it was not a completely disastrous experience, just not a good one. I got a dungeon for a room (there are two rooms on the ground floor that are quite dark and dreary, with no view). At night, there were plenty of weird noises and sounds emanating from all kinds of directions. The advertised wireless internet didn't work at all (and attempts to fix the problem fell on deaf ears). The appointments in the room were okay (if a bit drab), but certainly clean. The bed was typical English fare (e.g. hard and lumpy) but passable. I did not have the breakfast, they wanted too much for it. They also nickeled and dimed you for everything (if you arrived early, if you left late, and so on.) Its location is good (Cromwell Rd is a main thoroughfare out fo the western end of the city, and it's a 40 minute ride to Heathrow on the Piccadilly line) but that's about all it has going for it. Shops and restaurants are nearby, but none are all that fantastic to write home about. In the end I would not stay at this hotel again, because I think there are better deals to be had in London. That said, I can't warn others to stay far far away because I think this hotel has its good points too. Perhaps if I'd gotten a better room...

title: IKEA prison cell
text: I found very few aspects of this hotel likeable. It's not a purpose built hotel, but instead a series of Victorian terraces that have joined together and bashed through. That's quite common in the lower price categories of West London hotels and involves all sorts of compromises regarding oddly sized rooms and differing ceiling heights. The problem is this hotel bills itself as a higher quality offering, when it's blatantly not. Specific criticisms: - All of the decor is cheap and nasty. It's modern looking and apparently fresh, but on closer inspection, it just looks like they have raided a B&Q or IKEA home store - this cheapness meant in my room a soggy uncomfortable bed, two cracked bathroom tiles, a loose toilet seat, poor soundproofing, the cheapest polyester filled duvets and pillows etc - the hotel is noisy internally and externally. Towards the front you face a hugely busy main trunk road. To the back (my room) I had the 24/7 whir of air conditioning units on the roof - my room was small and poky and the bathroom was tiny. The space for the actual loo was so small the toilet paper holder dug into my leg. The 80cm square shower enclosure was as small as it gets (though water pressure was good). The single bed meant I felt like I was back at home sleeping in a children's bed - breakfast was basic: a few cereals, some cooked items, and a cheap canteen feel to the place. The juice was however of good quality - Swisscom provided wifi was free in the lobby (though it cuts off after an hour) and incredibly expensive and slow in the rooms. I paid £48 for a week's "business access" which gave speeds of 0.8 Mbps with a pathetic 250MB total upload limit. That means forget sending a lot of emails. The download was unlimited, but so slow you can scratch watching Netflix etc during busy times. On this basis I assume the cheaper but still expensive "economy access" is all but useless for even light surfing - staff would score about 2/5 on a charm/friendliness scale. Nothing specifically bad, but nothing great either. Colleagues complained about black hairs all over their bedding and this took an inspection by the receptionist to resolve, rather than an instant apology and room change as a properly run quality place would have offered All in all how IKEA would design a Swedish prison cell. My top room tip is to "go somewhere else". If you like this relatively handy location for good access to the National History Museum, South Ken, Heathrow, Harrods etc then for example try the Holiday Inn next door. It's purpose built, has a great breakfast, is better decorated and professionally run, and it's even a bit closer to the tube. Not recommended.

title: Comfortable room - don't go for the food
text: The room was fine and the bed very comfortable - I had a good night's sleep. Not too noisy even though my room looked over the Cromwell Road. The bar is a bit weird - patio-style furniture arranged in front of a big TV. The breakfast was not great - bit of a free-for-all at the buffet and the cooked breakfast was not nice. Great for a quick stay but go out for breakfast.

title: Lovely, great location
text: This lovely older hotel has just gone through updating and renovations. Hallways and many rooms are small, but very nicely decorated. Staff were wonderful and helpful. Our room was "itty bitty". My 6 foot plus husband had a bit of trouble in the small double bed, but the rooms are sweet. Our only glitches: rooms lacked sufficient information on the amenties of the hotel and surrounding area. We are used to a notebook of information as a resource. For example, we had to ask for restaurant hours (menu is posted in lift, but not hours), we had to ask if there was room service. We were told 'no room service', but I think this person meant there was no room service when the restaurant was not open. I was never clear on this answer. There is a fitness area but no information on it. We had to ask about surrounding area and restaurants. They were very accommodating with answers, but could avoid having to answer these questions redundantly by providing information in the rooms. We had two rooms. In one the shower only went from real hot to extremely hot. The cold valve didn't work. These are newly decorated rooms with new modern fixtures. This was a slight aberation. Other than these minor points, all staff were extremely helpful. The lobby is beautiful, the restaurant and bar are beautiful, good menu. Breakfast has many choices from fruit and cereal to full English breakfast. The hotel is lovely.

title: Great location, price and accommodations
text: During our stay in London during the volcano disruption our stay at The Park International was very enjoyable. The rooms were comfortable and clean and the service was first rate.

title: An Excellent Stay in London
text: Stayed at the Park International Hotel in London on my first stop on an 8-day European getaway. While, I had never stayed there before, I had been to London before and knew the general area where I wanted to be. The Park International is a perfect re-modeled hotel in the heart of a booming and exciting part of London. From the moment we entered the hotel to the moment we left (2 nights later), we were treated with such respect. Anytime we needed anything (For instance, how to turn off the light behind the bed, or a dinner reservation), the staff was more than accomidating to our needs. They have a great little bar in the hotel, which also serves as a sports bar some nights, and is great to go in and have a pint and just relax. I would strongly reccomend this hotel to others who are new to London or returning and want a hotel that is reasonably priced. Great staff, service, and hotel rooms! By the way, the showers in the newly renovated rooms are HUGE., which is such a treat for a European hotel!

title: Good location, comfortable beds, excellent double glazing
text: Spent one night here when spending girly weekend celebrating a friend's birthday. Good location near to Gloucester Road tube station and museums such as V&A. My friend had booked and paid for 3 rooms requesting twin beds. The room we were sharing did not have twin beds when we were shown it so we asked to be moved. We were then shown a room in the back of the ground floor which was very small, dark and smelled strongly of disinfectant. We told the front desk that we would revert to the original room and the girl on the front desk did not hide her expression that suggested that we were irritating and unreasonable. While we were out at dinner the hotel separated the double bed into twins so all was fine in the end. The room was a good size and clean. The bathroom did not have a bath which was fine with me but others may not be so happy. The beds were firm but comfortable which is important to me as I have problems with pain in my hips and back. We were at the front of the hotel and were really impressed at the double glazing as there was really very little noise from what is a very busy road. Breakfast was very busy and we did feel that the staff found it difficult to cope in terms of clearing tables and providing tea and coffee - we had to ask both initially and for refills especially as we were only given one pot of tea between six of us! We had a drink in the bar before we went out to dinner. The bar is relatively modern and seemed to have a good selection available.

title: Great Location
text: I recently stayed here as a chaperone during a school trip. The hotel was very clean and well kept. The beds were comfortable. Our room was fine, not tremendous, but enough space for 2 adults. Although I do know that some rooms were extremely small from other chaperones. The breakfast was ample with a wide variety of choices. The breakfast room was cute as well. The location was great! A 2minute walk to the tube and walking distance to museums. My only complaint would be the wifi. Although it is free, you can only get it in the lobby and even then it's spotty at best.

title: Ok.....
text: One night business stay for me here. I had a standard double. The room was quite small but not extreme by London standards - a bit barren. But the bathroom was another matter

title: Great Hotel
text: We stayed at the Park International for 2 nights this week. The staff were very welcoming when we arrived and our room was 105, on a mezzanine floor. The room itself looked out onto a another building, so limited the light but this made no difference to us as we didn't spend much time in our room. The room was a good size and very clean. The hotel is a 2 minute walk to Gloucester Road tube station which is ideal and only a couple of stops from the theatre district. The breakfast was delicious and again the staff were extremely friendly. There was a great variety of food, particularly for my vegetarian husband. We would absolutely stay at this hotel again.

title: Rude Staff & No customer serice
text: Despite receiving a poor quality room of such a hotel that has had such good reviews, I was ectremely disappointed in the service I have received since. I am currenty attempting to have a phone charger returned from over 3 weeks agao and despite contacting the hotel on more than 5 separate occations, to be either told call back or someone will call back I have had no response, I managed to eventually speak to their scarlet pimpinel manager who was extremely rude and as yet no details of where my property is. This is unacceptable behavour by anyone never mind the manager of the hotel. Such bad service

title: Fede_italy
text: Very confortable hotel! Clean, quite and good position to visit London! You can reach museums and the center in few min. Hotel staff is friendly and the breakfast amazing! I would recommend this hotel

title: Decent hotel in good location
text: Pros:Location,Cleanliness,Breakfast buffet Cons:Is not a 4 star as advertised.Maybe a 3 +,rooms small and bathroom very small, like a yachts wc😏 Internet in room only when booked through hotel website,otherwise 7 pounds/day. Mattress old fashioned coil style.

title: Great hotel and location
text: Stayed 2 nights at end of October. Excellent check in staff. Lovely clean hotel with good quality furnishings. Good breakfast.d Food in Chequers bar on the evening was excellent, although service was somewhat slow. Excellent location very close to Gloucester Road tube. Would definitely return and recommend to others.

title: Everything ok
text: Was a great hotel with great staff ...the only thing we had a problem with was the size of ourgency room which was on the top floor ..it felt like an attic room and was very small as was the bed .....saying that the breakfast was great and the choice in the bar was ok (if expensive..bit it is London)...all in all we enjoyed our stay ..just wish we had a bit more room

title: Great location, but would look elsewhere
text: First, the location of this hotel is terrific. It's just a short walk to the bus stop or the underground which connects to 3 different lines (Circle, District and Picadilly). There's a Boots and a Waitrose right at the Underground, which is handy. You can easily walk to the Victoria and Albert Museum, and I even walked to Harrod's, just 2 short subway stops away. Lots of restaurants in the area too. You will need them. The lobby is shiny with marble floors and looks like an upscale hotel. The front desk staff was pleasant, and the concierge was helpful about directions and maps, etc. The room was spacious with a large King bed, which wasn't super comfortable. Our room overlooked the street, and you could feel the rumbling from the traffic at night. The bathroom was adequate, if you only use a shower and not a tub. There's a safe for valuables and a small fridge for drinks or food, which was nice. For what should have been a luxurous hotel, the management has really cut back. No pad of paper or pencil by the phone. Cheap toiletries with a Portuguese shampoo so harsh, I went to Boots and bought my own. No shower cap or Qtips. No bottled water. There's a desk, but no lighting over it for work or a make-up mirror. In our room, we found an flyer inviting us to Happy Hour in the bar. Besides half price on the drinks, there was a half price offer on some appetizers. We ordered drinks, but when we asked about the appetizers, we were told there was no such offer. We thought it might be something new, so they weren't informed yet. But 5 days later, when we asked again, the waitress said she would have to speak to her supervisor. She was in no hurry to do it while we were there, because it never happened. They have little ottomans in the bar, but whenever anyone put their feet up on them, they were asked to take them down by the waitress (so don't make yourself too comfortable). The drinks were expensive enough that I thought they could have given us a small bowl of crisps or nuts, but there was nothing. Breakfast was the exact same buffet for 5 days. No variety. No omelette station. And they ran out of things constantly and seemed to struggle to keep up. All in all, I'd say, the renovations were done to make this look like an upscale hotel. But the only thing upscale is the decor (minus the plastic flowers which are tacky) and the price of $400 a night. The gracious hospitality does not exist, nor the amenities to make you feel relaxed like this is your home away from home.

title: Quick autumn London trip
text: This was a nice hotel for a quick London get away with my wife. The location was good, one block from the Glouster street tube stop. Any hotel you get in London must be near a tube stop. It is very easy and convenient to travel via the underground around London. The room was small but clean. Our price included breakfast which was very good. A Lot of hotels in london did not include breakfast with the stay. The staff was friendly and helpful but we really did not require much from them. There are several restaurants nearby. Also, a well stocked supermarket is within one block. The room has a small refrigerator to keep snacks and drinks cold. The only downside is that internet is NOT free.

title: often stay here when working in London - no complaints
text: I often use this hotel when I am working in London, it's very conveniently located near shops and restaurants, and Gloucester Road tube station. I've only had cause to complain once - I was put in a room underneath the piano bar - but as soon as I queried this I was moved to a quiet room. The rooms and bathrooms are always clean, sometimes I am lucky enough to get an upgrade, there are really some superb rooms in this hotel, but even the most basic rooms are fine. I've always found as I do everywhere - that if you are polite to the staff, they are polite back.

title: Safe choise
text: Basic rooms, basic breakfast with hot and cold assortments. Nice bar and restaurant. Very difficult/poor Wi-Fi. Do not expect luxury, safe choise if you are looking for a clean basic room near the subway line.

title: Excellent location and service
text: Good quality/price. Good and efficient service. Great location, near the underground. There are several interesting museums walking from the hotel, especially for children. The room was a bit small but with good facilities.

title: Great location and quality for the price!
text: I chose this hotel based on the reviews on this site, and I was not at all disappointed. I'm a young female who was traveling alone, and a place that felt safe was my biggest priority. The only thing I can complain about was that my room key didn't work when I first checked in, but they fixed the problem within an hour, and I spent that time wandering Kensington. The staff are very helpful and friendly. The breakfast wasn't bad, not a typical US hotel breakfast, but enjoyable and convenient. The location was amazing. 2 minute walk to Gloucester Station, which is on the Circle Line and will get you to most of the attractions in London in 10-15 minutes. 15 minute walk to Kensington Palace and Hyde Park. Single room was a bit small, but I expected that, its London, and it really wasn't an issue since I was only using it to sleep. Great little fridge and a safe in the room. I found the hotel to be in good condition. Next time I'm in London I will stay at this hotel, and I would recommend it to anyone planning a trip there. They will store your luggage until check-in time for free, and after check-out for a £2 fee per bag. If you want a taxi to the Train Station/airport, I suggest calling a taxi company yourself. When I asked them to arrange for a taxi, they actually called a chauffeur service they use, and while it was a good service, the trip to Paddington was twice as expensive as a taxi. £15 versus £7. If you're coming in from Gatwick to Victoria station, a taxi to the hotel is about £10.
