title: Would recommend!
text: Stayed for 2 nights with mother and daughter. Ideal location close to Victoria with bus route within a minutes walk. Hotel staff all helpful and pleasant. Room very clean, smallish but good value for money being in London. Have stayed in various hotels overnight in London and will definitely return here again, as my first choice.

title: Good: location, clean Bad: tiny, no frills
text: We got a room at £80 to go to a gig at brixton academy. The location was round the corner from pimlico station and the room was clean. It was however, about the size of a ferry or train overnight room, and the bathroom/wetroom was so small you could pee and take a shower at the same time. Could be as we got the very top room, so it was an attic room. Good for one night where you have to stay over - a bit depressing if you took a holiday there! View was nice - could see milennium wheel. Breakfast ok , nothing facny, cearal and toast. Coffee was not coffee, but we got one elsehwhere after.

title: Nice, Clean and Good Value For Money
text: I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights. We had a twin room and a single room. The single room was quite small but well equipped. The twin room was very spacious. We booked this hotel as we were on a budget and this seemed like the best hotel for what we could afford and to be honest I wasn't expecting very much. But I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is in a great location, close to the centre of London and close to Pimlico tube station. There were also some lovely restaurants very close by. The staff were all very friendly and helpful. The only downside was that the breakfast room was very small, very hot and very busy. There was not too much choice of breakfast items. The croissants were lovely but we were unable to heat them up. I would definitely recommend this hotel and hope to stay again in the future.

title: Excellent position
text: The position of Victoria Inn is excellent. The rooms are small but nice and comfortable. The staff was so kind. The breakfast is international and the food is good. I would recommend it for a trip in London

title: A good hotel on the Belgrave Road (London).
text: I took my chance to test this hotel one day in London, as I needed to be near the Victoria railway station for an appointment, and I was pleasantly surprised by the hotel. From the outside the hotel is not attractive but the hotel room I requested was spacious and clean, which was the most essential criterion for me on any hotel that I visit. Breakfast served is average but good. I would certainly use this hotel when I need to be near the Victoria station again!

title: Great Location & price
text: Great location for Buckingham Palace, Houses of Parliament etc. Lovely hotel, rooms are small but very clean. all the staff were very nice and extremely helpful. The breakfast was better than I expected. I would recommend this hotel.

title: look elsewhere! NASTY
text: We arrived and the lobby looked nice and clean. When we got to our rooms we were shocked at how small they were. The rooms were clean, but hadn't been painted in a long time and looked more like a college dorm than a hotel room. The place charges for internet acces (you can find a free hotspot if you browse around). It also offers breakfast, when we went down to breakfast it was like 1OOdegrees down there and smelled like something was burning. So, we had to go elsewhere. The bathrooms are deplorable. They smell like sewers and don't even have doors on their showers! STAY AWAY!

title: Good value hotel.
text: Good value a good value. Reasonably priced hotel. The hotel was very clean and airy. Pleasant staff. Well placed for central London. Pleasant neighbourhood. Would recommend to people wanting a good value hotel. Enjoyed our visit. Had a recent weekend stay

title: clean but not for me
text: Yes it was clean and in a handy area but I can't think of much else good to say about it. My double room faced the noisy road so best to take ear plugs as there is no double glazing. The room was small with high ceilings, ok for one person although it did mean that it had an odd loud echo to it when I was trying to make a business call. The lighting was bad, either a really bright light or really dim bedside lights which made it hard to relax. Breakfast was poor but in fairness nothing served was to my taste as I don't like cereal or beans (and I don't eat sausages). The croissants were shockingly bad. As the breakfast is included in the room rates it should be better quality as everyone is forced to pay for it. I would rather have paid less and not had the breakfast. The worst thing about the room was the 4cm gap under the door to the corridor, I tried to block it with a rolled up towel but it went straight underneath. This meant there was no real privacy and I didn't feel particularly safe as a lone female traveller. The door to the room next door was the same.

title: Would have been great if we werent in the basement
text: First impressions of the hotel were good: clean reception, friendly receptionist, nice area, ideal location. I was a little disappointed with room 5 as it was very small but the sheets were clean and the shower was amazing so overall felt we had got a good deal considering location. I noticed we were directly opposite the breakfast room but didnt think anything of this at the time as it was a closed off space....How noisy can tea and croissants be anyway???.. VERY is the answer. What we werent told when we checked in was that a door in the hall next to our room which we thought was a cupboard was infact a makeshift kitchenette and the staff began noisily clattering crockery and cutlery at 7.30 on SUNDAY morning right outside our bedroom door!! that was bad enough but when the breakfast room opened inconsiderate guests were running up and down the hallway shouting about the lack of bacon. I was really looking forward to a good nights sleep after a great night out on the tiles but sadly after being woken up i couldnt get back to sleep due to the high levels of noise. Even after complaining to reception the kitchen staff continued to be noisy and after an hour we could take more and checked out in a rage - all this before 9.30am - not the chilled out morning i had been hoping for. I am still so disappointed with my stay as it started so well and this experience did make a bad ending for an otherwise brilliant weekend away. I would still recommend this hotel to friends as it is good value BUT i would suggest if, like me, u like lazy sunday mornings, avoid the basement at all costs especially room 5.

title: hotel under renovation and my room was new!
text: The hotel is under important renovation: plus: during evening and early morning no any problems, the workers were quiet. The room I had was very nice, simple, clean cons: the smell in my new room needed window open all night Other things to say: - breakfast room is simple with average choice. - at the reception one more smile could be a welcome to have a nice stay... - the hotel is central: short walk to Victoria Station (easy to reach Gatwick apt). - area is quiet

title: Decent
text: The location is good - close to the Tate Gallery, Westminster Abbey, and the London Eye. It's a 5-minute walk to the Pimlico tube station

title: Terrible !
text: Room tiny and cramped, no seating or dressing table. Wardrobe space was laughable! No information pack in the room. No safety fittings on 3rd floor window. Most worryingly was the lack of fire evacuation procedures! The only upside was the great location. Stayed at the Days Inn hotel directly across the street, at just an extra £10 per night it was a far more pleasurable experience.

title: Reasonable hotel for short stay
text: If you need a hotel in central London for a short stay at a reasonable price, this is a good choice. I have stayed here twice so far, both times for one night. The rooms are relatively small, but very clean. The staff is friendly and helpful - although not the most motivated in the world. The hotel in general is not very noisy, however, the doors are everything but sound proof, so you do hear other people coming and going. The location, price and cleanliness are the crucial aspects, why I would consider coming back a third time.

title: Convenient Location
text: Convenient location to central London, with a bus stop a short walk away with a direct 24 hour service. Ample breakfast and a good price with friendly and courteous staff. The lift could be claustrophobic for some people.

title: Okay for a night...
text: Room was clean and airy but very small, and so was bathroom. Everywhere was clean, and towels were provided. Bed was extremely uncomfortable and we only had one pillow each which was hardly an pillow! Extra pillows should be provided. No noise from outside except from other people in rooms, we were right near the breakfast room so was very loud at 7am! Good location easy and quick to hop on a tube to main attractions!

title: Great Location!Great value for money!
text: I stayed with a friend at the Victoria Inn and was pleasantly surprised.While its nothing special our room was extremely clean and comfortable.The location is so central and such good value for the price you pay.The breakfast was fine and the staff were lovely.I will definetly stay here again!!

title: great location, average stay
text: close to tube, only 10 minutes walk. Ok for a short stay. Rooms a bit small but it was clean and affordable so can't complain.

title: London Weekenders
text: Took my mam for birthday treat. Hotel was lovely, room was very nice and complimentary drinks and cake was a nice surprise. Good location next to Warren Street tube. Our only complaint was the breakfast. On the Sunday morning the turins need refilling with beans and eggs and was a bit cold, on Monday the bacon was very very salty. However the toast was lovely and we cannot fault the service. The service was excellent, the staff could not do enough. Would we go back yes we would. This was a very nice hotel with a lot of nice touches, free apples, water in reception and luggage room free of charge. The bar on the night was nice and reasonable priced for London. reception staff very polite and professional. We had a great weekend.

title: Clean and nice hotel
text: Stayed at this central hotel in London people and staff are friendly and helpful the rooms are clean and a decent size. It's a noisey place at night but for it central location it's perfect. Breakfast is pretty good and normally included in your room rate

title: Great place to stay in Central London
text: I've been staying at the Grafton Hotel on Tottenham Court Road once or twice a year for the last nine years on business trips to my company's London office. The location is great and the hotel is comfortable at reasonable rates.

title: Great place to stay in London
text: We stayed here again on our 3rd trip to London. The hotel is in a great location with close to 3 tube stations with lots of good and inexpensive place to eat close by. Also close to Regents Park - a hidden gem. Staff are friendly and helpful and rooms are quiet. Highly recommended.

title: Great location!
text: Enjoyed my stay at this hotel because of its convenient location. 10 mins walk from Euston London. There's a Mcdonalds right at the corner, a supermarket right opposite the road, 1 pharmacy right beside as well. And a cafe too. It's also just 1 minute away from the tube exit. I recommend rooms that face inwards however. Rooms that face the main road can be noisy. I can occasionally hear people dragging their trolley bags across the hotel when I'm inside the room.. sound insulation can really be improved.

title: AWFUL
text: Air conditioning not working, window falling off, noisy traffic , Staff couldn't care less. Trouser press falling to bits, had to change rooms twice. Reception night stuff totally disinterested. I hd the worst nights sleep of my life and I travel extensively on business

title: substandard quality of TV/Internet/Breakfast
text: I've stayed in many Radisson hotels in the world, this one in London should not be carrying the name Radisson!Substandard quality of TV/Internet/Breakfast/Room/Bathroom/Personnel.Good only for a one night stay, only reason I stayed here longer is the location.

title: Handy for shopping and the West End
text: I regularly stay in Radisson Edwardian group hotels in London and the Grafton showed itself clearly to be one of that family with its cheerful and courteous staff, range of facilities and breakfast quality. Handily placed at the top end of Tottenham Court Road, and within 50 yards of Warren Street tube station, the hotel is well placed for access to shopping or transport to the myriad of London sights on offer. Although not as plush as its sister hotel, the recently refurbished Bloomsbury Street, or as well sited as the Kenilworth (both of which are at the Oxford Street end of Tottenham Court Road), the Grafton nevertheless represents value for money when compared with many of its 4* rivals.

title: Handy for Euston and Kings Cross
text: Only stopped the one night for business trio but I was impressed with the Hotel. The room I booked 140 was well laid out with a massive bed and well presented, quite a luxurious room with adequate bathroom TV etc. Breakfast was of the buffet type and very good. It is so handy for the main stations and a good base for touring London. The staff are very friendly and efficient and make you feel special which is good, so I will use this again

title: Great Hotel
text: We stayed once again at this hotel due to the fact we have used it previously and it is in a good spot on Tottenham Court Road right next to Warren Street Underground. We stayed for 1 night with a twin and a double room before going to Southampton for a cruise, rooms were very good and roomy for London, I had requested rooms at the back as the front is very very noisy ( Beware ) and our request was met no problem. We returned 2 weeks later after the cruise for 3 days and arrived at 1030 am from Southampton and our rooms were ready, both of them which was a welcome surprise and we checked in right away. The Concierge staff are excellent and very helpful and knowledgeable, we were going to a Chelse game and their directions were superb, getting us taxis as and when required which is a great help as the London Taxi Drivers must be the rudest in the world!. On both stays breakfast was plentiful both Hot and Cold and the restaurant manager is a very nice guy and always has a smile. Would not hesitate to go back. Well done Radisson Grafton

title: A noisy shoebox
text: I booked this Hotel fairly last minute as in London 2 nights in a row and had a lot to do at work. I got what i thought was a good deal which wasnt as I slept badly and had to work in my tiny room. The room , bathroom and bed were ridiculously small. If you are booking here just for one book a room with a double bed so hopefully the size of the room and bathroom will be better. The room also was not very well insulated for sound and Tottenham Court Road is a very busy thoroughfare with constant lorries unloading , traffic and people shouting . Also the inevitable noise of people chatting loudly in the corridors seemed to echo and be louder than normal. Room service was reasonable in cost but Chips were undercooked and the salad drowned in dressing. The staff were friendly and efficient enough, well the catering staff were. Check in/out efficient enough but very functional , no real warmth from them. I wont be returning but it hasnt put me off Radisson as have had much better stays elsewhere.

title: Everything you need
text: Close to Warren Street station, it is in a good location and good value for the money. It’s clean, friendly, but the breakfast is a bit expensive! There are plenty of shops near by and about a 20 minute walk from the British Museum and St Pancras station.

title: Smallest bathroom in London?
text: Stayed here 2 nights 16-18th September. Staff were polite and efficient, Hotel is well located. Bedroom and bathroom were clean, and the bed was comfortable, but I have never stayed anywhere with such a tiny bathroom! It was not possible to open the door fully as the loo was in the way and we had to squeeze through a narrow space to get in.

title: A pleasent nights rest in Central London
text: We just needed somewhere to lay our heads for the night after attending a family party and have a night away from the kids

title: Room was stifling hot and small
text: Room was tiny - when they say small room it means barely space to squeeze my pregnant-self down the end of the bed and the wall to access the other side of the room and I'm not even that big yet. Also dangerous if there was a fire I would have struggled to get out quickly. The room was stifling hot as well. My partner and I both were far too hot and felt overwhelmed with the temperature. We used the air conditioning to cool it but it was fairly ineffective and very noisy so a very disturbed sleep for both of us ahead of an important day. The rest of the hotel itself was very nice and breakfast was delicious with plenty of choice but expensive for how little we ate. Maybe if we were staying on a leisure trip instead of business we could have chosen our own room and it may have been better but not sure if I'd risk it after that experience.

title: Excellent location, very small rooms
text: On arrival I was glad that is was literally a few steps away from warren st station. Reception was swanky and clean, staff were polite. Lifts were tricky and seemed to take a while so I took the stairs to my room. Unfortunately my room was booked as a single and it was like a cell, the bed was against all three walls and the tvwas as big as the room was. The windows were frosted so could not look out which made me feel very closterphobic. I called reception and explain but they had no single rooms left and refused to do a free upgrade. Luckily my colleague swapped with me. Still a small room but the windows weren't frosted so felt less hemmed in. This one though had a crack in the sink. A lot of water went down the crack when used. I hate to think where it was going to! Good facilities in the room, tv, free wifi, toiletries etc. unfortunately I was at the front of the hotel and the noise of traffic was loud and consistent throughout the night. I did not feel fresh the next day where I was to attend a very heavy course! I asked at reception and they said that they would have a quieter room for me by the end of the day. When I came back that evening I had been moved to a much quieter room still quite small though. Breakfast was delicious plenty of fresh fruit and cereals. Would have been nice to see some yogurts though not just natural.

title: Both good and bad
text: I really like this hotel chain and am usually very happy. This time it was the longest check-in I have ever had in any hotel and I could see no reason for it. The room was quiet and clean, but there are no plugs near to the bed so you can't plug your phone in and have it on the bedside table. There was a message left in the room for us, but it was clearly meant for someone else. The shower was powerful but I had to stoop to get under it, and I'm not tall. The drinks in the bar were a bit pricey but I guess you would expect that in London. The breakfast was a bit chaotic. There was no-one there to greet us so we simply hunted for a table that was made up and there weren't many of these. They kept running out of various food and my partner didn't get any bacon. I had to keep asking staff for things and not once did any of them simply come to our table and ask if we needed anything or whether it was any good etc. The staff at check-out were efficient and friendly.

title: Nothing to fault
text: I stayed here for 2 nights as I needed to be close to the RCGP. The hotel was a perfect location-extremely close to Warren St and Euston Station. The rooms were lovely, comfortable and peaceful. The staff were friendly & helpful. The pre-checkin service offered was great & saved time on arriving at the hotel. We did not have breakfast as thought £20pp a little pricey. Overall I enjoyed my stay & would highly recommend this hotel.

title: OVERNIGHT STAY
text: We stayed here on Saturday evening and even though reception was busy (a football match and the Jubilee) it was very efficient. We had a family room which was spacious and the decor was really nice. The breakfast was really tasty with lots of choice. The leisure facilities were out of action which was a bit annoying as we had brought all our gear - it would have been nice if the hotel had emailed us about this beforehand. This hotel is five minutes walk from Euston and is a few doors from Warren Street underground station. Charlotte Street is close by and has quite a lot of independent restaurants which made a change from all the usual chains.

title: Let down .
text: Stayed here for a quick getaway with the wife . Rooms are ok & location is great. Bed was comfortable with great pillows however what let this hotel down was the inclusion of mice in the bar / restaurant late on that night. On notifying the staff they didn't seem to bothered or alarmed which was surprising. So we let the reception staff know the next morning & we got routine answers with no real apologies , still waiting on an email that was promised but I gather that customer service or feedback isn't important to these people.

title: A regular
text: I stay her regularly, certainly over the past few weeks, and then weekly for about 2 years a couple of years back. The service is impeccable, the lounge / bar area, toilets, gym, reception are all spotless. Breakfast is first class, although I cannot vouch for the restaurant as there are so many eateries around the area, that I never had cause to eat lunch or dinner in the hotel restaurant. Rooms and facilities have good touches and are comfortable, with the exception of single rooms, which based on experience I would avoid. These are far too small, and have showers only, no bath, which for me is a big downside. Some of the showers too are narrow, and if you drop your shower gel or sponge, it is a struggle to pick up. A small thing maybe, but overall this is my preferred stay in London as all round, it is a great hotel and nicely situated for getting around London.

title: Convenient location but
text: I was there for a 2 day training and stayed one night. The location is convenient and easy to reach. The hotel is nice: lobby and restaurant are really nicely decorated. The meeting room where my training took place was sufficiently isolated so we could concentrate and stay focused. After all that I said above, I was a bit shocked when I entered into my room. I felt almost claustrophobic: there were about 4 pillows on my little tiny bed. The desk was too small, although well equipped with several kinds of plugs. I could hardly open my suitcase to unpack my clothes. Moreover, the room was noisy because of a continuous whistle coming from the bathroom (although its door was closed). On top of that, the phone had a very sharp sound in the middle of the night (maybe half past midnight) then 5 min later again. My neighbours had the same trouble, as I could hear people moving around. The mattress was also very hard. Not a good experience in terms of stay.

title: Great Hotel in Central London
text: I have had the opportunity to stay in this hotel on many occasions while in London on business and vacation. This hotel is a hidden gem. The staff are always friendly, there is a nice ambiance, the rooms are comfortable and nicely furnished. I would recommend this hotel. While only a short walk from Oxford Street, it is also located near two tube stations, "Warren Street" & "Googe Street", therefore if is easy to get all over London.

title: Comfortable but rooms fairly basic
text: I stayed here for one night for business and overall my stay was average and wouldn't rate the rooms as 4*. The room I stayed in was fairly small and basic and was also very hot and I ended up sleeping with the windows wide open. I was pleased I was only staying one night. Although the room was disappointing I cannot fault the breakfast which had lots of choice. The staff were polite and happy to help.

title: Nice hotel in great location.
text: This is my go-to hotel when staying in London. Very close to Warren St tube so you can get there for just 6£ from LHR. Lots of restaurants, pubs, grocery stores, and coffeehouses nearby. Breakfast buffet is 19£ and if that is too serious for your budget, there are several other options nearby.

title: Perfect location
text: Nice and warm atmosphere. The rooms are great. Good beds gave me a good night sleep. Nice an spacious rooms and a great bathroom. Lots of nice restaurants nearby and if you need to work all that food off, you can do it in the hotel gym:) Short walk to the underground. Recommended

title: Very disappointing
text: The hotel lobby was fabulous but misleading! To say my room was 'dated' would be an understatement, dingy, old and in need of TLC. I was here on business and definitely willl not be coming back.

title: Small, good location. OK for stopover but not thst special
text: We booked for one night, whilst seeing Hamlet in Islington. Good location, right by Tube station. Looks nice, friendly staff and good pre service/emails etc. Room was small (London average ?) Standard room booked through hotels.com for £135 - but clean and well laid out. bathroom, again small but fine. Room was a little warm, but we could open windows, and despite being 4 floors up at the front, wasn't too noisy. *Nice comfortable bed*. Good facilities/iron etc and the usual mini bar options- though expensive. Free wifi- and quick check in/out. Stopped in bar for coffee- lights in both bar areas were FAR too bright, almost fluorescent- and didn't make us want to stay long. OK for an over night stop- but not special enough for a return (or an overly excited recommendaton) I'm afraid

title: Comfortable room, close to Warren Street tube station
text: I stayed here for a one night stay whilst on business and it was a very pleasant stay, very comfortable room. I didn't get a view at all and got quite a small room (but as a solo traveller that was OK but if I was part of a couple I would think it's a little bit small), so that wasn't the best but was still very comfortable and OK for me. Nice flat screen TV and lovely bathroom, shower, etc although again a bit on the small side. Breakfast was very tasty and if I stayed here for a trip to London, I would count myself lucky as it would be a great place to set as your base. It's right next to Warren Street tube and so you would be able to explore London very easily, as even Euston Square and Great Portland Street tube stations aren't that far away either.

title: Excellent hotel
text: Excellent service and great location. Ask for room situated on the alley and not the main street (too noisy). Public transportation at the front of the hotel and "tube" one corner down, and near Kings Cross Station. Great for getting around by foot or public transportation.

title: Perfect for theatre
text: Lovely hotel, very friendly service with good service. Although the room was quite small, it was fresh and clean and had everything I needed for a business trip. Other advantages are that it's very close to the tube station and the theatre for We Will Rock You

title: Saturday night stay
text: Check-in staff were good. They were happy to change a tiny room for a bigger room. The bedrooms and bathrooms were not huge, but they were clean and with lots of nice toiletries. Enough choice of breakfast however the "warm" plates were cold so the food went cold very quickly. There is a good bar for later drinks and all the staff were friendly and helpful.

title: Great hotel and location!
text: We booked this hotel to use as a base for a two night stay for sightseeing in London. The location was ideal, 5 minutes away from Euston station. Out of the way of the crowds while at the same time right next door to Warren Street tube station which is three stops from Leicester Square. Attentive friendly staff and a great breakfast (buffet style). We would definitely use this hotel again.

title: Cheeky weekender
text: Stayed at the Grafton after staying at several other Radisson Blu Edwardian hotels. Reception service was good, standard room was a little small and a touch dated. Breakfast service was shocking. No cups for coffee, when they brought coffee it was cold. My wife had to wait 20 minutes for a pot of tea and the milk was curdled.. you just don’t expect this from a 4 star hotel with Radisson name. No matter how busy they are. They did knock us some service charges off but it put a bit of a dampener on it. Shame will stick to one of the others next time.

title: Beware the Sunday breakfast
text: Decent hotel, small rooms with nice stuff in etc etc. Friendly staff. But - beware breakfast at 10am on a Sunday! 15 minute queue to get seated, ten minute queue at the buffet. The eggs were so far overcooked and also turning blue (?!). The rest of the food was decent, though the 'new' tray of beans I had to wait for were lukewarm, while the new sausages were scalding hot. Confusing! So yeah this is a decent hotel, but I did have a bad breakfast experience (along with lots of other people!).

title: Not the jewel in the Radisson Blu crown
text: I stayed here on business for 3 nights when my usual hotels were fully booked. Will only return if preferred options are not available and because there are some good restaurants very close by. + excellent location for West End and great restaurants close by (see review for Del'ish). + breakfast was efficient, well stocked and service was a credit to the staff. A special mention should go to the manager who was extremely nice and courteous. - on check-in I was not not pointed to where breakfast is served, nor was I given info' on timings. - my Gold Elite member fruit bowl was not provided on arrival. - room 360 is so far away from reception it's not fun with lots of luggage. - the shower water temp would occasionally increase to an unbearable heat.

title: Beautiful stay
text: Cannot fault this hotel! We where greeted by a lovely member of staff who spoke to us as if we where the most important customers in the hotel, even as a young couple! The rooms where beautiful and the facilities where faultless! The time in our hotel really made a difference to our short stay, loved it!

title: Very good hotel
text: The hotel is centrally located and close to all transport links- Warren Street underground rail station is next door, the bus stop is almost at the lobby exit and taxis ply the main road every minute ! The hotel is just a short walk to shops and restaurants. Service level by the hotel staff is excellent, and hotel facilities work well but the room tends to be on the small side.

title: A Touch of class
text: The Radisson Blu Edwardian London is a nice Hotel. It's a little chic in its styling with a touch of class running throughout. It's got to be a decent Hotel in anyone's opinion and not too badly priced. Nice rooms, restaurants, and public areas. Bang opposite Warren St Station and 100 yds from Tottenham Court Road stn. It's a well placed.

title: Great location next to warren street underground
text: Myself and my wife chose this hotel for four nights. The hotel is a reasonable price in London terms, the hotel is in an ideal location for what we wanted, as warren street tube station is 30secs away. We only paid for a standard room but this was clean and we'll maintained. Staff were helpful and easily approachable. I have an issue with hotel beds as they all seem to give me a dodgy back, but myself and wife both commented on the comfortably of the mattress. We will defiantly use the hotel again.

title: Very Good Visit
text: Can't really fault our visit ! Only there for a one night quick tour of the City. Check in was extremely professional and the receptionist courteous and took time to ask what our plans were etc. Our room was situated at the front of the hotel overlooking the hospital and therefore the road was busy through the night with sirens etc. But in all honesty and in a strange way helped me to sleep. Bed comfy, bathroom well stocked my only gripe was the air con isn't upto standard. Otherwise breakfast was well stocked with a good array of produce and staff attentive but not obtrusive. Checked out with the same receptionist and again could not fault the ladies approach to us. She was a true ambassador for the hotel. Good stuff !!

title: Great hotel, great location
text: The hotel is great for location - clean and well-appointed, with all the facilities one needs. Rooms were spacious, and the price was reasonable. The electronic check-in and check-out were new to us - this worked well, and enabled us to choose our room rather than simply have one assigned to us. We would definitely consider staying here again.

title: Close to British Museum and Warren Tube
text: Central location to British Museum and Library - can walk ( if you like) to other areas like Soho and theatre or jump on the tube at next door Warren Tube station. Excellent breakfast selection, compact but functional room, non street facing room was very quiet ( no street noise), and comfy bed.

title: Stay here regularly good hotel very close to the tube
text: I stay here regularly for business. Its well situated for the tube at Warren Street just 1 minures walk. Staff are very friendly and helpfully. Particularly Hasan at breakfast in the dinning room. Always happy to see me with a warm welcome. Rooms are good to very good. Can be nosiey if on the front of the hotel. Lots of pubs and places to eat nearby. I'd recommed it. Have a good stay. Brian

title: wonerful location
text: location is extremly convenient❗️Access to any interesting places are walking distance. Check in tooks quite long, but stuff is friendly and tried to solve quickly. It was PC problem. Room is clean enough and comfortable bed.

title: Fantastic Hotel with excellent rooms and service near everything worth seeing
text: This is the second time I visited this Hotel and I really like the rooms and the atmosphere. The service is excellent and so is the full Breakfast in the morning with complimentary newspapers. It is one station from Oxford Cirkus and you can easily get right into the shopping area. I warmly recommend this Hotel and will definitely come back again.

title: Over Priced for the room
text: We stayed at this hotel Saturday 7th July. We are not normally people to complain and I have to say the hotel on the whole was clean and we received a warm welcome and also the breakfast was good with a lot of choice. However we had paid £150 for one night and I do not feel room wise we had value for money and we were actually quite disgusted in what we received for the cost. We did try and say this as we checked out but it was quite clear we were not being listened to and as they were busy with other guests we did not try and discuss the matter further, we were ushered out the door. The room itself I found quite dark and stuffy, we over looked another window and quiet obvious we were over a shop or the kitchens as all night long we were kept awake by crates being dragged and people banging around downstairs (I know it’s the middle of London and space is scarce but for £150 we expect to at least be able to get some sleep). We had to keep the window open as it was so hot and stuffy in there, we tried to turn the heating down but it didn’t work. The TV didn’t work it kept switching itself off, we were told this was a widespread problem and none of the TV’s worked, ours however had switched itself on at 3am, to which we couldn’t switch it off causing more disturbance to our already disturbed sleep. Not only this, the cleanliness of the room I found rather disappointing, there was dust all over the side tables next to the bed and also over the dressing table. As I mentioned we paid £150 for one night and chose to pay extra to stay in this hotel choosing over another hotel as we thought we would be getting a better room and more comfort as it was a 4 star (my friend who paid less on the same weekend for the hotel we were going to originally choose had a far better stay and rooms were much nicer). We were bitterly disappointed our extra money did not give us a more comfortable stay. I have emailed twice about this but not yet had a response even though requested one which i think is poor business. Will not be reccomending this hotel to anyone due to this experience.

title: Consistently good
text: Probably our 5th visit over a number of years. Hotel is well located near Euston and Warren St tube station. Rooms are plush and well equipped. Staff on reception in the bar and on reception are always friendly. Nice touch of £15 complimentary drinks voucher for each day of stay.

title: Such efficient and friendly staff
text: My wife and i stayed this week end at this hotel which is close to places we wanted to visit.. including visiting our daughter at University College Hospital. It is so handy and only 100 yards from the hospital. Room was spacious and comfortable. Staff were so good and helpful... Sainsbury's was right opposite and there is a Mcdonalds and Cafe Nero next to the hotel. Warren Street tube was just 2 minutes walk. Euston was just 10 minutes walk and Kings cross St. Pancras station 15 minutes.

title: Great weekend trip
text: Yet another visit to one of my favourite hotels in London. The staff are all so polite and friendly. The rooms spotlessly clean and the location couldn't be better a 10 second walk from Warren St Tube station on Tottenham Court Rd. So very handy for anything you wish to do in the city. Amazing hotel. Thank you.

title: Nice location, reasonable room size, but could use a good cleaning
text: The hotel is very close to a tube station and also in a good walking distance from Soho, China Town and museums like the National Gallery (20-25 minutes). Rooms are comfortable, good size, but bathroom is a bit durty. Bed was very comfortable. Wi-Fi is free but you will have to pay for the TV. Personnel is very kind.

title: Great Stay
text: Found a great deal on this hotel at a very reasonable cost including breakfast. We arrived early not long after midday. Welcome very friendly & we were able to check in straight away. Room clean, modern & average size on a par with similiar London hotels we have stayed in. Really great location just a few steps from Warren Street tube served by two different lines. Also only 10 mins walk from Euston. Tesco & Sainsburys right next door for any bits & pieces you might need. Just 5 -10 min walk are a selection of different restaurants (mostly on Charlotte Street). Customer service notable at hotel. They had a great diverse mix of staff of a number of nationalities & throughout our weekend all the staff we came into contact with were friendly, polite & helpful. In fact it was probably this factor that prompted me to write a review. At the end of the day there are many hotels to choose from & always a deal to be found but a good welcome & friendliness go a long way. Would definately use this hotel again.

title: LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE
text: This is the best London hotel I have ever stayed in! Hotel staff, lovely an can't do enough for you, hotel room, compact but everything we needed and a great sleep. Hotel is right next to a tube station and everything is easily accessible through this. Great value for money. PERFECT STAY.

title: Always made very welcome
text: The hotel suffers a bit from being in Central London - the rooms are quite small and there is often some noise from outside. However, that is more than countered by the welcoming, friendly and efficient staff. I am a fairly regular guest at the hotel, and it is great to always be greeted by name at reception and in the restaurant. It is the same whether I am there on my own for business, or with my wife for a weekend in London. Last time I stayed, some chocolate covered strawberries arrived in the room as a happy birthday gesture for my wife. For me, the difference is that the welcome (Katarina, Trevor, Hasan, Edna, etc., etc.) is genuine, it's not just people following a script. I have stayed in many London hotels and this one, on balance, is the best.

title: Good Central London Hotel
text: Great hotel, great facilities, exceptional staff - friendly and helpful. Get a room at the rear of the hotel though, its on a busy road opposite to a 24*7 emergency hospital so lots of siren and traffic noise throughout the night.

title: Great for a short weekend on London!
text: The room was fairly small but comfortable and clean. I asked for a quiet room, and that's what I got. This is where I normally stay when I come to London for the weekend to visit friends - the location is very central and the Warren Street tube station is right next door!

title: Central location, good staff...beware of small single room!
text: Stayed on Friday night as visiting friends. Got single room and breakfast for bargain of £72. Check in excellent - nice friendly staff. Reception very welcoming. Complimentary juice/water and sweets on desk. Hotel excellent location - right by Warren St tube (Northern/Victoria lines) and ten min walk max from Euston. Got allocated Room 426. BEWARE....this is a very small single room and if you have mobility issues it may be a problem esp in the bathroom. The sink is literally at your face if you are seated down....if you follow! Shower also very small but nice toiletries provided. The wardrobe is also a little strange. I had to remove the ironing board and iron out of the wardrobe to get my clothes in and even then the hangers still hang at an angle across the rail! The roof cuts across the room at an angle by the window. Tea and coffees provided but these were in the bottom of the desk area so again if you have trouble getting to low level areas it would be an issue. Nice touch though is complimentary bottles water provided. Breakfast is good - standard choice of hot food buffet style. I seemed to wait while for my pot of tea to arrive and I heard other guests muttering similar things. All in all I have mixed feelings but I think I would stay again....BUT.....I would get the room issue sorted prior to staying and would NOT want room 426 again. Hopefully ALL single rooms aren't the same!

title: Nice cosy room - Nice restaurants and shops around
text: I stayed one week. The room was confy and quiet. The hotel is nice. It's a chain hotel, so it's not very charmfull. But I would recommend it. It's not very central, but there is a subway station nearby and some good small restaurants and shops and chains like M&S, Le pain quotidien, supermarkets.

title: Stay Away
text: Very expensive for the prices. If your room class is not ready when you check in, they will trick you to an expensive upgrade. At the end. you will pay extra to get what you actually paid for in the first place. You need to come to this hotel only if you run out of options.

title: Uninspiring and confused staff
text: Stayed here for a 5-days course. The room was tidy and dark, so course facilities were all in the basement with no windows, so it was 5 long days. The staff in the reception had the best intentions, but appeared rather inexperienced why the service level on some request lacked a bit. The hotel restaurant has a good deal for either steak or lobster, but also this place is poorly decorated, lacks atmosphere, and there are of course no windows. If the price happens to be really good, then it's okay, if not I would go elsewhere.

title: Stay elsewhere
text: Bed was uncomfortable, breakfast was poor quality with cold egg bacon and slow coffee service, Room and bathroom were too small for comfort. Poor value for the tariff I paid. The upside is the location close to all the good stuff in Central London + tube and bus

title: Expensive
text: An expensive hotel with things to address. Breakfast service slow for no apparent reason and whilst a concierge service is offered it is seldom available. Location is good for major train stations in London and tube locations nearby. Rooms at the back are quiet.

title: Good atay
text: Stayed at this hotel for one night with work and was impressed with all aspects. Service was great from moment of arrival, room was clean, tidy and comfortable and breakfast was great. Big selection, fully stocked and fresh. Desk area with plenty of power points made it easy to work and location of room was very quiet despite location on busy road

title: Room no bigger than a shoebox
text: This is the second time we have stayed at the grafton after reading good reviews at trip advisor. The first time we were upgraded to a suite. Not massive but big for London. We booked again for 1 night in August. The room was 10x7 and was then cut off on an angle. My wife actually became claustraphoic. Would have been OK if you are paying £50 a night but not acceptable at nearly £100. The bathroom was nearly as big. Was clean and functional. Would not stay there again.

title: A great location and friendly, helpful staff
text: Stayed to celebrate my husband’s 65th birthday. We had two nights during a real heatwave in London, the air conditioned rooms were just brilliant, a little in-room fridge with bottled water on arrival and ice dispensers on each floor meant we were able to keep cool. Communications before, during and after our stay were excellent. Online check in and check out saved time and was very efficient. Kajsa Schultz ensure we had a memorable stay with special birthday treats! Thank you. We were impressed with the staff they were polite, attentive and friendly. The location is central with a tube station a few yards away. We will definitely return for our next celebration. We had a fantastic trip and enjoyed our stay.

title: Very friendly staff
text: We booked at last minute but still got a fine room. The hotel reception area is spacious and all reception staff are a credit to the hotel. It is next to the tube station, within walking distance of town centre and there are several convenience stores nearby. Room was clean and of reasonable size. Good value!

title: Nice hotel with an international standard, but with some potential for improvement
text: This was my second stay at this hotel in two years and once again, it was a successful stay. I paid some 75 pounds a night, which is reasonable in London. You can get some good weekend rates at this hotel if you book in advance. The standard of many hotels in London is generally below average and you rarely feel you get value for money, but in my opinion, the Grafton delivers as promised and at a reasonable rate. There’s an international feel to this hotel. It may not be typical of London hotels, but that is a big plus. Rooms are a bit small, but not smaller than in other London hotels. Service is welcoming and professional. It is close to Euston station and within walking distance of most attractions. I did not sleep well. The room was small (-ish) and there was no ventilation (for some rason the aircon-system was off). I opened the window, but got little fresh air. Adding to that the bed and pillows were hard. The breakfast is OK (mine was included in the rate, but don’t be tempted to buy breakfast in the hotel – it’s a rip-off) and served in a beautiful dining area. If I’m going to be picky I’d say that the toast machine is unsuited for a hotel (slow and with low capacity) and that the scrambled eggs are more suited to a refugee camp than a four-star hotel, but as least it fills your stomach. I might stay at this hotel again.

title: Perfectly Nice
text: I stayed here previously and gave it a five star – it was purely for the bar staff, due to circumstances. I stayed here again recently and now I have seen it through calm eyes. I have an update on the actual hotel itself. The staff are still pleasant and friendly. The room itself was good for one night, although the carpet was absolutely filthy and threadbare and needed replacing, there were no black out curtains just roman blinds, so the sun shone through in the morning. This time we had a room at the back of the hotel, which is a lot quieter. Other than this, the hotel is a perfectly nice three star.

title: Enjoyable and well looked after
text: We stayed at this hotel for a Christmas shopping weekend, all the staff were very attentive and could not do enough for us. It was a second birthday treat for my Mums birthday, so she enjoy the bit of luxury and the extras. The breakfast was great, and my omelette cooked perfect. My only criticism if any was the downstairs bar was very very busy with works functions and there was only 2 bar staff on duty, one was making waitress drinks so that only left one for the bar. The poor guy never stopped but a 20 minute wait was excessive for a drink. We had had a problem on our last stay but the Manager rectified this on this stay and was there to greet us on our arrival to ensure everything was correct this visit ... and it was. Thanks

title: Most comfortable bed ever!
text: Brilliant Location, most comfortable bed ever, gorgeous pillows, could have slept for a week! Room lovely and clean and quiet as requested. Breakfast not as well organised as other Radisson hotels i've stayed at, but it was ok.

title: Poky, noisy & with the smallest bathroom I've ever seen! Breakfast was good though.
text: This was a last minute booking following a late flight, the hotel was picked because of the proximity to the railway station. The reception is very nicely done, the staff were very helpful, but the room ... it was seriously tiny! The bathroom was a squeeze, there wasn't room to sit on the toilet properly (evidenced by the crooked seat!) and the shower was just big enough to stand in after squeezing past the sink. The decor was pretty dreary and old fashioned, and I really feel for the person in the room underneath mine as the floor was very squeaky. I had earplugs, so was able to get a good night's sleep, but without them it would have been impossible because of the street noise. The high point was the breakfast, it was excellent! The breakfast room was really quite nice & the service was prompt and efficient. The choice available was very good covering full english, cold meats & cheeses, fruit, yoghurt, cereal & pastries. Wifi was free here, which is always very welcome.

title: Great location
text: Great location (close to British Museum, British Library etc.). I was there for 4 nights in summer (didn't use AC). The room was spacious. Design is kind of "old school", but i liked it that way. I had a view to the street, however - the noise level was acceptable. WiFi functioned well and it was for free. Bathroom was clean and comfortable. Check in-Check out was uncomplicated. I would lodge here again.

title: Surprisingly good
text: Got this as a last minute deal for a night out in london. Right next to the tube, so location couldn't be better. Lots of shops, coffee bars and pubs on the doorstep. Friendly welcome at reception, everything very straightforward. Smoking rooms available. My room on an upper floor was large, spacious and nicely decorated. Bathroom was a little poky, but for one night, it wasn't an issue. Bed was comfy. This hotel could be a problem for light sleepers as Tottenham court road is noisy 24/7. On an upper floor it didn't disturb me, but I can imagine it may be an issue for some. Didn't eat or use any services, so can't comment, but overall, the hotel impressed this ex-Londoner. Not incredible - but a solid choice for business or pleasure.

title: A very good choice at London
text: I chose this hotel through Hotels.com basically for its placement near to Euston station. However, once there, I was greatly surprised with the quality of rooms, the warmness and efficiency of personnel, the internet service and the pretty convenient surroundings including an Underground station (Warren St) and a Sainsbury store. Even though that was the crowded summer station and the hotel was full, the personnel were always opportune, kind and efficient. I deeply recommend the Radisson Blu.

title: simple but inexpensive overnight stay in London
text: This hotel is conveniently located directly above Warren Street tube station, and within 10 minutes walk from the extensive Regents Park just north of the city. The single room was small but adequately presented. A discount prices was obtained from web based hotel booking service. Breakfast was the classic English breakfast of bacon sausages mash eggs and the lot. Juices are adequate, but the muesli had run out when I got there. Wifi was available free in the room on an unsecured network, with no problems with connection or speed.

title: Great hotel for week-end visit to London
text: We have just had an overnight stay in London and stayed at this hotel for the first time. It will certainly not be the last time. The hotel is located very close to Warren Street underground station - turn right and it is within 50 metres. Although the official check in time is 3pm we arrived at midday and were given a choice of rooms that were ready. We asked for a quiet room and given one on 4th floor at rear of building. Very nice room and bathroom. Didn't eat in hotel but had lunch in pub almost next door (out front door and turn right - pub on corner across side road - very good food) and on Sunday morning had breakfast at a cafe a bit further along Tottenham Court Rd. The hotel cooked breakfast was about £20 which is a bit steep. On checking out on Sunday morning we were allowed to leave a case with reception and collected a few hours later. Reception staff really good. As said this is a great location and when next in London will definitely look to stay here again.

title: Fawlty Towers
text: Just back from a family break, 3 nights. Positives are location to public transport. Negatives. Rooms very hot, air con doesn't do much. Too many trainees on reception at peak times. Biggest farce was breakfast when it degenerates into a free for all, after 09.30 forget it at weekends as nothing left and if you find anything it resembles slops. Too many rude people crammed into very small lifts.

title: Sadly not as had hoped for.
text: I was looking for a hotel near Warren Street station, looked at the reviews and noted a few comments about small rooms. As our stay was for my daughter to relax and the rest before travelling home as having a procedure nearby I wanted a relaxing comfortable room, I emailed the Guest Relations Manager Direct to explain the reason for the stay. I then booked a deluxe room direct rather than go through a third party. The room has good views through the small windows and the room has double aspect, however as on 5th floor it is an annex style with sloping walls. It is a little like a cave and to get around the bed you have to lean to manouver around, difficult after an operation. Also boiler type noise coming from ceiling in bathroom is rather constant and noisy. I was going to request a change but my daughter just wanted a quiet time without upheaval of having to move as had unpacked. Considering my efforts at contacting hotel direct prior to booking to explain the situation , I would have liked to think our requirements would have been considered, sadly they have not been. All in all nice hotel, close to underground, but not really ideal for us on this occasion.

title: London Theatre Break
text: The Radisson Blu Grafton was a fantastic hotel. Would highly recommend and will definitely be staying here again. The staff are very obliging and will help you in every way they can. Food highly recommended also.

title: not worth the money
text: My room was extremely small and contained two steps to get from the minuscule entrance to the sleeping area. In such a small space they were borderline a safety hazard, particularly if wanting to use the toilett at night. There is no shelf in the bathroom to place your toilettries, no hair dryer, no full length mirror and no working heat in December.

title: Brilliant Stay
text: We booked our room late on New Years' Eve due to staying with friends falling through. Room was small but perfect for our needs which was getting ready and heading straight out. Courtesy call from reception moments after we arrived in our room to check all was okay which was a nice touch. Excellent location, Warren Street tube station just moments away. Lots of good cafes and pubs nearby. The best thing was that the hotel allowed us a late checkout at no charge which meant that we could enjoy a lie in on New Years' Day, great with a hangover! We would recommend this hotel and definitely stay again.

title: Aston Bar and Restaurant
text: As someone who had walked past the Graftoh Hotel for years without going in, I was more than pleasantly surprised, together with 25 other colleagues, to find an excellent restaurant and bar in the hotel. The staff were friendly, professional and very efficient, The food was first class. Highly recommended.

title: disappointing
text: I stayed here for a conference in central London. Although the location was very convenient, being just outside Warren Street tube station, the hotel was less than I expected. The paintwork in my bathroom was (an executive deluxe room) was yellow, and was in desparate need of a new lick of paint, the TV was a tiny 16" old CRT model, and the safe kept refusing to open, necessitating daily trips to my room from the hotel manager on duty. The food at the bar was really nice, though. I had a very fresh smoked salmon on a toasted bagel and the gym was petit but functional with three treadmills, a few free weights and a machine which functioned as a general all body toner. I would only stay here again if I really needed to stay within walking distance to the conference venue that I was at previously. I originally wanted to stay at the Mal Maison in London, but that was fully booked, so I stayed at a four star close to the venue. Next time, I'll stick to the Mal Maison and book earlier!

title: Poor service!
text: My experience with the Radisson Blu splits into two: the one started with Radisson Blu on Grafton and the 'corrective' experience ended at the Radisson Ble Bloomsbury. I arrived there close to 22:00 pm after a long flight and bad traffic getting there. The receptionist was a guy working at the concierge. When I handed him my hotel voucher he apologizes saying that the hotel has been overbooked, and that they transferred me to a sister location, which is about 12 min from there. At first he said it was my travel agent's mistake, then the other lady at the reception explained that it was their reservation dept that overbooked them. They said they will take care of the taxi payment and that a taxi will get there in 5 minutes. They also promised that there is a room for me there and that everything has been sorted. It took the taxi almost 40 min to get there, as the roads to there are under construction. (There was another guy from Belgium who also had the same issue and was sent to another hotel) Finally the taxi got there and I was drove to the other location on Bloomsbury. When I got there I approached a very kind guy called Manciej (excuse me if I misspelled his name). He is the night shift manager. He immediately tried to help checking for my booking. He could not locate any reservation under my name in their system. He then called the Grafton reception and apparently, the guy who answered the call there did not know what he's talking about. He let me speak with him and this guy explains that he does not understand why I was sent there, as there is a room waiting for me there. There were only 4 receptionists at the Grafton when I got there, all of them knew I was sent away, and this guy dares to lie to me on the phone, ignoring the fact I was sent away from there few min ago. I explained Manciej that I am not leaving anywhere, and he was so kind deciding he is not sending me back but fixing a room for me there. And so he did. He arranged a room for me there and from then on, it only got better. The hotel was nice. I have no complaint at all but to the fact that the Grafton team has to learn how to service their clients. And if they make mistakes, listen and try to solve. Room was great, clean and convenient. Location is perfect for people who want to say close to the center. I stayed at the first floor, so it was a little noisy from the main street, so stay away from the first floors.

title: Good hotel in an excellent location
text: I've stayed at the Grafton a number of times on business and I'm very impressed with it. The staff are friendly and helpful, the rooms are very clean and it's virtually on top of a Victoria Line tube station. Highly recommended

title: Never Ever Stay at this Hotel
text: Never Ever Stay at this hotel. The customer service is disgraceful and you will not have a silent night sleep as promised in all of the marketing material. Due to the floods in Berkshire, my wife and I decided to stay here on a Friday night before heading off to Paris on the Eurostar for Valentines weekend. Having experienced a hard week at work, we were exhausted and found ourselves in bed by 11. Unfortunately, we we're woken up every half an hour from the moment we fell asleep until the moment we woke up at 7am due to various noises within the hotel (buzzing/door bell noises/bathroom/lift/more buzzing doors)We rang reception 6 times over the night which we have since found out weren't recorded and were told each time they would "investigate". A simple room change may have sufficed but this was not made available. In the morning, we were tired and entirely dissatisfied with our hotel night from hell. On speaking to Ken the "customer service manager" in the morning, he refused to give us a refund and shouted at and abused my wife in the middle of the lobby in front of other guests when we asked why we couldn't agree compensation for the entirely awful night we had experienced. Ken said that there was no "evidence" to suggest we had made any calls to reception in the night. Nordine, the concierge also contributed to making us feel uncomfortable by asking if we know of any other hotel that would offer any kind of refund after they have purchased a nights stay regardless if we had any problem or not. My wife, was and still is rather upset by the ordeal. Without any compensation, we have left the hotel and now feel that we should share this so you never have to go through it. We have been told that the manger will be in touch but rest assured, I will be contacting head office and every other review site to share this ordeal so that no other customer ever has to go through this or meet Ken or Nordine and we are reimbursed. The Radisson seems like a good brand but they have employed some of the rudest and most incompetent people I have ever encountered at this joke of a hotel. Please don't waste your time or money by staying here until they improve the hotel unless you like being shouted at and abused in public for raising a complaint. To the manager - please contact us when you are back at work. We have left our details with Ken.

title: Good base on the north side of the city centre
text: The upsides: clean rooms and public areas

title: Good value
text: The room that I used was very nice and very clean, everything was in very good conditions. The location was lively - with the result that my room was a little noisy as it faced the main road. I enjoy to sleep with an open window which was not possible. But everything was fine when I closed the window.

title: Excellent upgrade of this hotel since last visit!
text: I have just stayed 3 nights here after some years since the last stay and am very impressed with the extensive upgrading that has gone on. We had a Deluxe Room which was large, airy, quiet and comfortable. The marble bathroom was the largest I have seen in Central London. The restaurant did not attract me as it was restricted to 2 main dishes - steak or lobster! I expect their research has told them that is what the majority of their guests would like but I found it a very restricted choice and went elsewhere to eat. Otherwise - excellent!

title: Employees need more training
text: Good hotel, the building that is, but the employees need more training. When the reservation system doesn't have your reservation upon arrival (after confirming online two days prior) and was told that the headquarters system hasn't synced up with the local system, then that is an employee problem, not a technology issue.

title: Excellent location by Warren St underground - great breakfast, nice rooms
text: Rooms are not overly large but very nicely fitted out with shower rooms, toiletries, water provided etc. I have stayed here twice in recent months and would happily stay again. There is a good selection of food available at breakfast and no long queues to get a table. Friends have used the bar and found it good but there are lots of places to go for dinner and drinks nearby too.

title: barely adequate
text: we had a typical boring tiny room usually provided for cheap business stay. the air conditioning could not be controlled, but opening the window meant roaring noise from the air conditioning machines outside.

title: Well located. Small room
text: Very well located hotel with tube station at just 100 meters. However, my room was small, the bathroom was even smaller and uncorfortable, and there was no space enough to work in the room. The room was clean and the concierge service was nice. I am afraid I will not come back as there are other options more confortable around too.

title: Perfect location near Warren Street Tube
text: high level of service, very helpfull and friendly staff, clean hotel, breakfast: all you can dream for, spacious accommodation, very attentive staff, fresh apples on every floor near the lift, complementary small bottles of water in the room

title: Single bedroom don't even fit a desk and chair!!!
text: Single room was so small the desk could not be moved to sit on. The single bed was tight against it. When queried I was 'helpful' told, "yes our single rooms are very small!!" As if that made it ok!! Not very good and very noisy.

title: Nice stay
text: Hotel looked lovely. Rooms look lovely, bathroom very small, and room we had was situated on the front of the building so was very noisy over night so didn't sleep well at all! Good location just next to warren St station,not too far from All flagship stores.

title: Birthday Treat
text: Husband booked this as a birthday treat. It is extremely close to Warren Street underground and within easy reach of Oxford Street. I had read previous reviews and was fully expecting a small room, however on check in advised that we had been given an upgrade. The room was on the fourth floor, and overlooked the internal courtyard - but I could see the Post Office Tower (as it was once known). The view was immaterial, and I can confirm is was quiet. The room was quite large (as large as the London Hotel we stayed in two weeks ago), a huge bed, a sofa and coffee table, and still room to move around. Slippers and a bathrobe were provided 9but for two guests only one robe!). Yes the bathroom was small and the toilet was right behind the door, however the shower was large enough for two and the toiletries were really nice, not the small bottles but large bottles in the shower and over the sink. The heated towel rail was really hot but how nice to snuggle into a warm towel after a shower. The bed was comfortable and warm and our temperature controls worked very well. I do wonder sometimes about the number of objects that light up the room at night however and are they all really necessary? I thought the small card with the name of the staff member responsible for our room was a nice touch and made it more personal. The bottle of water was really appreciated. Yes biscuits with the tea would have been nice and perhaps more than 4 milks but these are nit picky things personal to us. In our view breakfast was plentiful and well presented. Signs were posted around the hotel to advise of the busy times at breakfast, so guests could plan when to eat. Staff were extremely pleasant and I would like to say how lovely Trevor on front of house was. Again it made us feel a little bit more special. All in all a lovely weekend and we would return to this hotel.

title: Very Small Room
text: We stayed here overnight coming from the Lake District and on our way to Gatwick in the morning. We chose this hotel due to its location- walking distance from the train station. We arrived here late at night from a long train ride.The staff were very polite and professional. Check-in was fast. However, the room was very small

title: Perfect all round hotel
text: The location is perfect and the staff are friendly and welcoming. The rooms are very comfortable and clean with the added bonus of opening windows for fresh air. Breakfast choices were excellent and the Green Juice is a must. Overall fantastic experience.

title: Adequate close to St Pancras
text: I was so concerned about noise as we had a 4.30 am awakening the next day (Eurostar) that I splashed out on one of the better (top) rooms. Well not exactly like the pictures, it was still very small and cheap looking. I think my first impression was that the hotel had the feel of a backpackers lodge, lots of young people, worn carpets, a little noisy lower down. Definitely felt out of my comfort zone but surprisingly slept well probably due to being at the back and on a higher floor. The bathroom even in the more pricier room was still the smallest I have ever seen, was not much bigger than an airplane toilet and the shower was smaller than regular. You wouldn't want to be a big person or you'd never fit. As for location, it was handy. The supermarket was close by, lots of pubs for meal choices and of course the reason for our stay, St Pancras was very close by. So it did the job but I don't think I could have stayed here for longer than a night. I spoke to a few other people of similar middle age to us and they felt the same way. That it had a real backpacker feel to the hotel and a little out of our middle aged comfort zone in that, but overall turned out okay for the one night.

title: Compact accommodation in a great location for central London
text: The rooms are very small, but great if you don't plan to spend lots of time in them. Very compact loo/shower room, not enough room to swing a cat but again ok for a short stay. All very clean and they've tried to get the most out of the space available. We were in a basement executive room with a small kitchenette as we wanted the option of eating in occasionally. Quite noisy as you'd expect for London so take earplugs if you're a light sleeper! Also the bed in our room was awful (sunk in the middle like a hammock!). There was also a bin area outside our room window with an annoying slamming door that it took 3 complaints about to management before they fixed it, which was a little frustrating but at least it was sorted. It's also near a shopping centre with a supermarket so handy for supplies on your stay. Overall, I'd recommend for a short break base in London, lots of nice pubs nearby too (recommend the friendly Mabel Pub up the road). We'd go back again, but would try to avoid the basement rooms due to street noise.

title: great location/ well equipped
text: good quiet but central location, I had a basement room which while small was well equipped and had a tiny but useable courtyard which was nice in summer when I stayed. My friend had a balcony room which a nice outlook and a large opening window which was lovely in the morning. the location is handy to the picca.dilly line so direct to heathrow is easy. Handy supermarket and basic cooking facilities . Pretty good value

title: nice, clean, great located apartment
text: very close to Euston and King's Cross stations. Nice and clean rooms, not very big but comfortable and definitely enough space for two people. Bathroom clean. Heating worked excellent. Would definitely recommend it and stay there again next time.

title: Great location
text: Location was fantastic for transport either wanting the buses or trains. The room we had was verysmall and also the bathroom. But it was fine for our stay as most of the time we were out sightseeing, it was very clean and was handy having washing facilities downstairs which were spotless.

title: Affordable no hassle London stay
text: We stayed here as a couple in early January. Having stayed a month earlier at the Radisson Edwardian on Bloomsbury St, I would recommend these studios way and above the Radisson. First off they are what they say they are. Excellent value £91 for a double studio. The staff communicate effectively and show you to your room - which are based in a number of attached buildings on Cartwright Gardens. You have a front door and studio key. We didn't see other guests or hear anyone, which was bliss. The studios are very compact but you know that when you book . They are clean, well kitted out and a friend even lived here when working nearby. Nice fully tiled bathrooms, loads of hot water, radiators and air con which you just adjust to your own wishes. The added value for me : location, just a few mins from Euston and Kings Cross. Near local pubs, cafes and restaurants which are quirky and have good atmosphere. If you like walking it's only 20 mins to stroll to Covent Garden, the theatre district and Seven Dials. In advance the property offers on line check in and asks you to say what time you will arrive and would you like a room preference. This worked brilliantly for us as we got our room early , but in any event the property texts you to tell you when your room is ready. No checking in or out issues. It just works and they've thought about what the customer needs is our impression. As a regular traveller to London , I am delighted to have found an area, and property which I will now use each time I visit. No hassle and good value for money. Eat your heart our Radisson Edwardian .......you could learn something about valuing your customers if you followed this model.

title: Suited my purpose
text: I needed a place to stay near Kings Cross for one night and this studio suited my purpose. The place is easily in walking distance from either Kings Cross or Euston. Check in was simple and straight forward and the staff were most helpful. I'd paid a bit extra for a superior studio and I'm pleased that I did as had I not I may have left with claustrophobia. My studio was in the basement with a window that looked out into a shared yard and someone else's front room which resulted in me keeping not only blinds closed but the window too as their cat had a tendency to try and jump into my studio, The place was very clean, though this can't be too hard when the bathroom is so small with an innovative layout to fit a sink, shower and loo in I had to keep my toiletry bag outside so the bathroom didn't feel cramped! If you need a place to put your head down when traveling then stay here, it's clean, convenient and the staff are nice. If you're looking for a studio where you can chill out after work, maybe cook yourself something and stretch for a bit then even paying for a superior room will not help you here!

title: Lovely room closed to King's Cross Station
text: The room is close to Kings Cross Station. The location is very convenient. The room is tidy and has everything we need. The staff is very helpful and kind. You can keep your luggage before or after checking-in.

title: Not for me!
text: Arrived to check in which appeared to be a room full of staff members having a meeting, no other guests very strange. I was given a room in the basement which was not good, located next to the laundry room and maintenance room so I could hear staff talking and walking in front of the window. The room was a good size and well decorated however when I opened the bathroom door I was hit with the most disgusting smell and a wall of heat! The smell was coming up from the drain and the heat appeared to be coming through the wall of the bathroom. Leaving the building the following morning to check out the entrance hall was lined with at least 10 large bags of laundry it was a lovely site!

title: Great location, but rather small
text: We had a very nice stay at Studios2Let. The room is rather small but big enough. It was very clean and looked very nice. We were on the 4th floor and there is no elevator so it can be difficult for some to get up there. It was great to have fridge and small kitchen in our room. The location is great, short walk to Euston or Kings Cross, and from there you can go almost everywhere in London. I probably would stay here again next time in London.

title: Cheap accommodation, but...
text: Six flights of narrow stairs to negotiate with bags, no lift. Unable to open and use the wardrobe without first sliding the bed to the far side of the room. No desk to work on. No iron or ironing board in room. Five day stay without a single service of the room/change of towels etc. Price was good but I wouldn't stay again.

title: Good option in quiet area
text: We stayed here recently for 8 nights. We had a room (Number 11) overlooking the rear courtyard. The room as others have noted is compact, with a kitchenette in the main room. We had a good sized double bed, two fridges, sink, cooktop, TV and all other requirements. Wifi worked well in the room and was free. The room was very quiet other than occasional footsteps on the stairs. We also were bothered occasionally by voices from the courtyard area. The room was serviced once through our stay which was fine. The kitchen sink is in a silly location under an overhanging cupboard, making it hard to use. The bathroom is very small, but quite usable. Mind you, taking sips from the basin when cleaning teeth requires contortionist skills to avoid water spilling all over the floor. Also there was a bothersome orange flood light on at night that lit up our room - better black out curtains are needed! Staff at reception were helpful when they needed to be. The place has a free laundry for guests. Cartwright Gardens is very quiet and it is a short walk to Kings Cross and Euston Stations, as well as Russell Square tube. All our expectations were met at this place - convenience, value for money, quietness and comfort. If you are a place to stay a week or so in London, close to action but not overwhelmed by it then this is a great option.

title: April 2019 Trip
text: Fantastic location. Small shopping centre, resturants, pubs etc 3 minute walk away. Five minute walk to either Russel Square Station or Kings Cross Station. Room was tiny, but we'll equipped. Prior to arrival customer service was outstanding - not so much, once there. Free washing machines/dryers were a bonus.

title: Great place to stay
text: We stayed there for 4 days and enjoyed every minute.Its only 500mts from St Pancras Station and busy Euston road, and yet you cannot hear any traffic noise it was so peaceful the only complaint we have is that the bathroom was very small the shower was great if you were a 10 year old child but as an adult it was near impossible to pick up the soap if you dropped it.The unit itself had everything that you needed and was spotlessly clean. If I ever go to London again this is the place I would stay.

title: Perfect Location!
