text: Hotel has a great location for shopping and some sightseeing. The staff was professional and the breakfast was good. What was utterly disappointing was the size of the room. We were two people and could not both move about in the room. One had to sit on the bed if the other wanted to moved about. The bed is also a standard double bed. For the price we expected better.

title: Great serivce, great location
text: We have just returned from a short break in London and had a lovely stay at the Mostyn. The location is great, just off Oxford Street and close to Hyde Park. The room was a good size with a lovely big shower, tea and coffee making facilities and complimentary bottled water. Good quality linens, towels and a choice of pillows. The only negatives were that you needed to be about 6 feet tall to use the heated section of the mirror in the bathroom and our room (802/Kensington) was next to the gym which needs soundproofing. All the staff were friendly and service was excellent throughout. The breakfast selection was very good with the tasty cooked options arriving quickly. The waitress even remembered our choices from the previous day.

title: Fantastic hotel
text: We have been to several hotels in London, but this is one of our favorites. The hotel was great, with nice, clean and large room, great service and excellent location. Lots of nice restaurants close to the hotel. A really nice sup price with the worm cookie when arrival. It is a hotel I will recommend for friends and family. Great value for money.

title: Disappointed overnight stay
text: Arrived after long train journey to find room that was not what we paid for was also cramped & musty smelling We requested twin told nothing left asked why we did get what we paid £ 220 for one night we then were shown to cramped twin stained carpet room spoiled a birthday treat

title: My Oxford Street home from home
text: I stayed here for 1 night in December 2015.It's very close to Marble Arch tube and just off Oxford St, the location is excellent. Arriving early – around 11am – I expected only to drop off my bags at the hotel. The reception staff were very friendly, gave me a welcome cookie and said the room was available now. My room (called Mayfair) was on the lower/basement level, but there was no noise from the street and good coverage from the curtains. It was clean and nice, the bed too soft for me (but this is personal preference). There was a great toiletry selection in the bathroom. When getting ready for the evening I discovered that the iron was broken. I reported this and the staff brought a replacement in literally 1-2 minutes, very speedy and attentive. The breakfast was a real selling point for me

title: Review of July, 2015 Stay
text: Enjoyed our stay

title: Good stay with courteous staff
text: Stayed here for one night whilst on business. Staff were unfailingly courteous and helpful. Breakfast was on a par with most business hotels with a good choice of hot and cold food but the melon was tough and inedible. Room and bed were comfortable but something seemed to be wrong with the lights as there were many of them and they were difficult to operate. Some instructions would be good. The decoration is in good order but too much dark brown which makes it gloomy. Some lighter paint on the next redecoration would be good Overall a good experience with some minor issues

title: My week in London
text: My sister and I spent a week in London - May 18-25. Our stay at your hotel was excellent. The beds were very comfortable, the room, though small, had a refrigerator and a safe and plenty of drawer space. Tea and coffee making plus the cookies were great, also the "rain" shower in the bathroom. Your staff were more than helpful and we enjoyed the daily breakfast which was included in our package. One small problem was there was no free access to a computer to print our boarding passes for our return trip. We had to pay 10 pounds for about 5 minutes use of the computer in the business center. Overall, I would rate this hotel as excellent and the location near the Marble Arch was wonderful.

title: Christmas City Break
text: Everything was excellent, the men at the main door made you feel welcome, even once checked out they were running to find us a taxi, there was one problem, when I checked in the receptionist asked if we would like to give him credit card details, to add any items to the rooms, drinks, etc. Which he put a hold on £50. the first night we went for one drink when returning to the hotel, which came to £24. five minutes after returning to the room there was a letter came under the door asking to contact reception as there was no credit card details given, which was a mistake by the staff member on reception, this is not good practice

title: Poor Bar staff at night
text: Wouldn't serve beer late at night even though residents were supposed to be allowed all night. We weren't drunk and as we were entertaining customers this was a poor show. They were clearly being lazy.

title: A Week In London City
text: The hotel is in a great location - handy for shopping but also good connections for the tube at Marble Arch or Bond Street. We were on the Hilton Honnors floor which was very quiet. Would stay again. Room had A/C which could be adjusted to suit your needs

title: Ideal location and value package
text: Stayed two nights in Club Room. If you arrive with your own car Club room is good package as it includes full (english) breakfast and parking in multi-storey car park opposite hotel. Room was compact/cosy but was comfortable, modern and clean. On first floor, noise from the street not a real problem - this is in Central London after all. 2 minute walk to Oxford Street - Primark or Selfridges depending on your wallet! Front Desk - friendly helpful and efficient. Breakfast - good choice and staff coped well with a busy spell. Would highly recommend and would use again.

title: Microcosmic Doubletree
text: I can't remember the brand, but Doubletree bought this hotel from a competitor. It was always fairly forgettable as an operation and the new owners have managed only to drag it up to average i.e. way below Doubletree standards elsewhere. The rooms are well-equipped, but tiny, viewless and dark. Someone sold them on an electronic switch system that would defeat Stephen Hawking and, in ours, Housekeeping failed to turn up at all on the first day. Complaints about this and a failed safe, caused the management to respond with free water and fruit, but it was all disappointing, given visits to the brand throughout the world invariably have been very favourable. I'll forgive Doubletree for this poor experience, because of better experiences elsewhere, but the management control in this mini DT needs a shake-up, especially where room size is concerned and the unappetizing gloom of the public area, which caused us to take our feeding arrangements to a nearby pub.

title: Close to Oxford st
text: Lovely clean hotel friendly and helpful staff. Arrived an hour early but was able to go to our room. Lovely large bath sheets with ample toilettries, over head shower. Good quality heavy blackout curtains, decent size t.v with sky. Again ample supply of tea and coffee also hot chocolate and biscuits in the room with bottled water. Bed very comfortable like sleeping in a marshmallow. only stayed over night but could easily have stayed longer. Nice size room. Literally a road away from Oxford st so an ideal place to stay for shopping. We were in the basement by the road so there was a little noise from the traffic above but nothing major and apart from the usual closing of doors from other hotel users there was no other noise. The down side is that there is no parking but across the rd is a car park where you can park for 24hrs (maybe longer) which was ideal. Cost of car park was £36 for 24hrs. A bit pricey but because of location we could just walk everywhere. So parked up and left the car until it was time to leave. English Breakfast expensive at £19 each although i believe your key card gives you a 15% discount but still expensive. There are other options for breakfast that are less expensive. Did not have any meals in the hotel so unable to comment. Would definately stay here again. Stayed across the road a few years ago at the Thistle but the rooms are not a patch on Best Western.

title: Close to Oxford Street
text: Chose this hotel due to it's close proximity to Oxford Street, Regent Street, Hyde Park and the West End of London. We have stayed here before and weren't disappointed. If you don't mind walking it is easy to get to Regent Street, Piccadilly, Kensington, Covent Garden... Otherwise there a number of underground stations in Oxford Street.

title: Excellent Hotel
text: Having used this hotel for the last 12 years I can say that even with the change to the Hilton brand this hotel still gives excellent service and reasonable prices for this area of London. The staff give excellent service, the rooms are better than most other hotels in the area and the breakfast being exceptional. I would recommend this hotel with total confidence.

title: Great location, shabby rooms
text: The location is excellent - close to Oxford/Regent Street shopping, Hyde Park & many sights. It's tucked back on a bit of a side street so pretty quiet. Costa Coffee across the street. Overall, though, the rooms are shabby and outdated, not what I'd typically expect from Doubletree. The room is small, but it's a large city so I was expecting that. But the details are older & the room and hallways worn. I stayed on the top floor and at one point in the hall you have to walk up and then down a bunch of stairs (???) Wifi was slow to nonexistent. Perfectly serviceable, but with a little updating could be 4-5 stars.

title: DoubleTree Hotel by Hilton Marble Arch London - For Those Who Like Shopping At Oxford Street
text: It took quite sometime to search for a hotel along Oxford Street London, this time to experience the atmosphere at Oxford Street famous for its shopping and a hit with tourists. We ended up with DoubleTree by Hilton Marble Arch London which is quite expensive but most decent in terms of its nearnest to Oxford Street and it is the only factor driven us to take this hotel. Unlike many DoubleTree hotels we experienced before, this hotel has slightly different concept as the owner exert a great influence on the outlook of the hotel and the moment you step into the hotel, you will know who own the hotel. The hotel is located in an old building and there constraint as it has stairs in certain floors which makes it difficult to carry heavy luggage up or down, considering the concierge service starts at 7.00 am. However, once concierge is operational they are very efficient in handling all issues. The room is OK but not up to the standard in comparison to many other newer DoubleTree brand hotels. The Receptionist are well trained and handled check-in and check-out very well and met with our expectation. Breakfast is also good and you can still leave your luggage with the concierge upon checking out to continue with the tour of London. It is about 5 minutes walk to Oxford Street and to Marble March Underground Station and this is a plus point for ease of travelling. From here you can walk to Selfridges, to New Bond Street, Picadally Circus and Trafalgar Square without the need of a taxi. Overall, it is still a good hotel but we would prefer to choose another hotel given the chance to come back to London the next time around. Saha & Yam Stayed April 2018

title: ideal for a tired runner ...
text: i stayed here for one night after completing a 100 mile running / walking race - which meant i'd been on my feet for 33 hours. i'd booked a single room and was delighted with it - by far and away the nicest single room i've ever stayed in. not small or dingy or badly furnished, like so many others. i was so relieved when i opened the door and saw how smart, clean and modern it was. perfect. it was high up - on the 6th floor? - and quietly tucked away. the bed was extremely comfortable, the bathroom luxurious with a very welcome powerful shower and plenty of towels. i didn't stay for breakfast, but was delighted with the location. after a stroll to selfridges in the morning i was able to collect my luggage from the hotel then catch a bus directly opposite to kings cross. i loved this beautifully presented hotel with its helpful, professional staff and would happily stay here again.

title: Business
text: Good Location. Easy access to tube. Ask for the upgrade room. Still very small. Scared to see regular room. The wifi is the worse. This needs to be upgraded. I cannot. It was a clean hotel. The hallways very small feel like you are a boat. Overall would come back if wifi upgraded

title: Excellent Hotel
text: Excellent and perfect stay with this hotel. As overall, the hotel was a good selection for the whole family, and it was an ecellent experince for our trip. This is my good experince, and I would recommend as a good facilities for all my family and friends.

title: Great location, good price
text: We booked for a pre- xmas chill out, leisurely visiting xmas events, hotel 2 mins from Hyde Park Winter Wonderland which was fantastic, hotel was spotlessly clean, beds soooo comfy, polite staff, would stay again

title: Horrible Room, Service, & Staff
text: The room was not ready for an hour after my check-in. They gave me no updates so I had to continuously check-in at the counter. The check-in staff was also very rude and unhelpful. When I got to the room, the room was unmade with the sheets and blankets completely stripped. I had to call maid service multiple times to come up to clean. The refrigerator was also missing and the bathroom was disgusting.

title: Those Little Touches
text: What can we say to those little touches that enhances the time we're working away from home. It was not just the cleanliness, decor, TV - It was the Working Air Con, the fluffy pillows (different choices depending on preference), the Iron and Ironing Broad, the slippers, the decent towels, A complementary ltr bottle of water renewed daily! and last, but certainly not least the chocolates left on the pillow. Thank you for a lovely stay

title: lovely stay
text: from the minute we arrived the staff welcomed us all with genuine kindness, the room was spotless, comfortable and very pleasant, all the staff were polite and helpful and nothing was any trouble at all, breakfast was unrushed and delicious!!

title: Clean updated property in excellent location
text: This property is clean and modern and made for a very comfortable four day stay. The rooms are a bit compact - to be expected for London - but stylishly decorated, and the bathroom is newly updated and spotless. The breakfast was standard, even if the service was a bit slow. I had one dinner at Indigo and the food was really good. This hotel's best asset is its location, just a block off of Oxford street and some of its best shopping. Its really easily accessible for public transportation and there are plenty of places to eat in the area. I'd certainly stay here again!

title: small room
text: hotel location is excellent, next to Oxford street. Room is small so is the bath room. There was no shower hose in the bath room, only rain shower. Mattress was soft for old people, internet only can be used for one device and quite often disconnected.

title: 2 Nights stay
text: Stayed for 2 nights , was given a basement room and if the curtain was open could see the streets level above. Could hear slight vehicle noise coming in especially when high performance car like Lamborghini race through. The room was spacious and well maintained. It's slightly aged in some areas. Customer service was nice n pleasant. Location was splendid. Excellent location within 2 min walk to marble arch subway and right next to Oxford street , near to Hyde park also. Overall was a good experiences.

title: The Best Hotel by All Standards
text: This hotel is by far the best I have ever stayed in. The rooms are overall small but that is normal for Europe. What made this hotel so great was the above and beyond staff. I have never experienced the kindness and helpfulness they gave me. They far exceeded my expectations!

title: Overrnight Stay for Business
text: Had to travel to London for a photo shoot for my daughter. Booked the DoubleTree at Marble Arch, due to its location. Very clean, very modern and really nice hotel. Staff very friendly, welcomed professionally. Breakfast was buffet all you could eat and was really nice, quiet hotel that you can relax in.

title: good location, fair price
text: For a couple of nights in the heart of the West end of London this hotel is great for shopping(Oxford St.) Shows and food. Some rooms are basement level and lack light but are very well appointed. Not a great deal of space for relaxation,lounge area and bars very restricted.

title: Worst Hotel I have ever stayed at
text: They put me in the basement room. Lights went out and couldn't be fixed. They were sold out and had to put me in another hotel. The consergie new nothing and was terrible in helping us find a restaurant and a tour. the service was terrible! The rooms old!

title: Always surprised
text: It was interesting reading other reviews as I personally found that it was the staff that was the saving grace of this hotel. They were text book good. Very polite and recognising HH Gold. The room I stayed in (G8) was very large. Badly cleaned, you wouldn't want to eat in there, and noisy. Light streaming in unless you used the blackout curtains. Breakfast was 'OK'. Brilliantly service. Faultless. But orange squash kind of says it all. Location is excellent. My surprised is why people don't use Airbnb or other alternatives until Hilton makes staying at its hotels either more affordable or more desirable?

title: Great location, very nice hotel
text: Located in the middle of literally everything, you will not go wrong by picking this hotel for your next personal or professional trip to London. it is clean, accommodating and friendly and did I mention amazing proximity to shopping, dining and entertainment.

title: Good hotel near Hyde Park
text: Rooms are typically small in this part of london, no exception here, but the room was clean and relatively comfortable. Doorways are short, so if your tall remember to duck going to the WC. Bed was comfortable. Noise from street was a little higher than expected but not bad. If you have any any issues with stairs, the only way to the breakfast room is down a long flight of them. Staff was friendly and helpful.

title: Great time near Marble Arch at the DoubleTree
text: I had to extend my stay in London and needed to be close to Gloucester Place and Oxford. With the Rugby world cup going on. I found comfort at the DoubleTree Marble Arch for 3 nights. The hotel is fairly Modern and my room was comfortable. The queen sized bed was very comfortable. The bathrooms were a bit small. After staying across the street at the Thistle. I found this hotel had less traffic of people. It was more relaxed environment. However to my surprise on the first night. I awoke to jack-hammering and building demolition going on right next to my room. This will only be a temporary event. But i felt safe and comfortable at this hotel and the staff was very friendly.

title: Great Location
text: Great location - close to bus, tube, pub, restaurants, shopping. Staff very friendly and helpful. Room smaller than american hotel rooms, but very comfortable and clean. I would stay there again. Could hear street noise but did not interfere with sleep. Ate at Fire & Spice Restaurant twice - food was very good.

title: A very good, comfortable and convenient hotel in central London
text: I spent two nights in this hotel for business trip on 7-8 May 2012. The service was good and the staff were cheerful and helpful. Although the room wa on the Ground Floor, it was clean and comfortable. Enjoying The breakfast there is a prefect start for the day. Its location is great: close to the underground station and next to the Oxford Street. I had been to London several times and this hotel is so far the best one. I will certainly book again. Chi-choi YUEN

title: Small Rooms
text: Very Small rooms. the service wasn't outstanding but okeyish Expensive for the utilities and type of rooms provided. the hotel would not be my first choice when staying in marble arch. transportation arranged is also not the best nor cheapest around.

title: A relaxing getaway
text: This was one of those holidays that you need another holiday to recover once you have returned home :).The hotel was simply amazing,even the lift smelled like heaven. I would highly recommend this hotel to everyone.It is within reach of everything you need to see around London.

title: Double Tree Marble Arch
text: Very good hotel, comfortable rooms and staff are very friendly. The location of the hotel is very good with direct access to Oxford Street. Rooms are spacious and comfortable and the services of the hotel are good.

title: Great Service & Location
text: The hotel's location was great being near to Paddington where one arrives by the Heathrow Express. It was also about 8 minutes walk to Bond Street Station where I took the Jubilee Line to Canning Town for Excel where I was here on business to attend an exhibition. When I had the time, shopping at Selfriges and Oxford Street was wonderful! The staff was most friendly and helpful. What I appreciated the most was that they gave me a complimentary early check in when I arrived early in the morning after a long overnight flight! The only drawback was that the room is small and I couldn't see out of the window. However, housekeeping did a great job in keeping it clean & tidy. All in all, it was a great stay.

title: Niec hotel , very well located
text: Nice stay, even for business trip, Associate very friendly, helping to make you stay comfortable and relaxing Bedroom offering all amenities , and well designed Business hotel, having nice gym as well. Definitely to recommend

title: Perfect location and great service!
text: I really enjoyed my stay at DoubleTree Hilton, Marble Arch! The hotel was only 30 seconds away from Oxford St and was really close to Hyde Park. The service was fantastic! The room we stayed in was also really nice. It was nicely decorated and bright although the windows were covered. I will definitely come back!

title: Location and cleanliness in the City
text: I have stayed at this hotel a number of times now and it has always been a pleasant stay. The location is excellent if working / visiting the Fenchurch Street, Bank, Monumnet area, with plenty of nearby places to eat and drink. Rooms have always been spotless, reception helpful (I actually like the cash-machine style check in and check out machines) and whilst the lowest cost rooms are fairly small, they are perfectly adequate. The second size up though are pretty spacious for a central London hotel.

title: London stay
text: Well located clean hotel. A lovely feature is the free snack and coffee bar located in the lobby as well as a cupboard full of coffee, sugar etc on all guest floors. We also appreciated the fresh water station on each level. The things we found lacking was that there is no hairdryers provided. I did not bring mine as other travellers told me that I would find one in all hotels. Also a mini bar fridge would have been handy as often we saw lovely deli items we would have bought but we have no refrigeration. Overall a comfortable stay.

title: Nice city break
text: Lovely clean hotel. Great snacks in the lobby, refillable water bottles on each floor. Good location for tube stations. Very quiet at weekends and some shops around closed but easy access into central london

title: Good Perks - Average Stays
text: Stay here on multiple occasions mainly to collect the night on the house points. 2 stays and there's a free weekend night for you. Generally the front of house staff and facilities are pretty good, welcoming and comfortable. I've noticed they've started putting out complimentary chips n dips with wine in the evening plus some breakfast bars and fruit in the morning. In between these bits you have to sleep here - or try, Rooms are clean but tired. Slamming doors all night, paper thin walls, echoing toilet usage above your bedroom, I even had a joyous rendition of office party overindulgence i.e. all night pukeing next door to me last time I stayed. Sorry folks - if it wasn't for the perks I would spend my £180 a night elsewhere.

title: London visit
text: This hotel is ideally situated for a visit to the City.The room we were given was described as a double, the bed was a double, but the room was furnished for 1, 1 easy chair, 1 bed side table. The room would be ideal for somebody working in the city, it is set up with a fridge and microwave. Or would suit if you wanted to be visit he heart of the City.

title: Very much satisfied!
text: Convenient location and nice hotel service. Such a spacious room with air conditioning. You can walk to Tower Bridge in 20 min. Their purified water service was super good! I would stay next time again.

title: Only ok for business,worse for pleasure
text: Location is amazing for a lot of business visitors and close to London and tower bridge as well as Liverpool street. However staff not great,mixed up my business and personal cards even though I had a booking for the week and another for the weekend. Also don't order from the delivery place. Really bad!

title: Not very pleasant and lousy customer service
text: I will get to my experience of the hotel, buty mainly I'm now writing because I can't get hold of the manager at the hotel after several attempts of calling and e-mailing - I forgot my engagement ring at the hotel, and they don't seem to bother to answer me properly about their (lack of) effort to give it back to me. It's now more than a month ago I stayed here. I find this completely arrogant, and I am certainly not used to being treated like this when travelling. The bad thing is that I had the impression all the way from checking in that this wasn't a hotel I would like staying at. Normally when I go to London I stay at Conrad hotel (which I will go back to after this bad experience), but I booked CQ Gracechurch due to the good location for the meetings I would be attending. I regretted my choice as soon as I arrived to the cold reception area where a not very helpful staff pointed to the check-in machines - and the smell of mould as I entered my room. I think if you're a businessman looking to stay at fairly low budget, or tourists looking for good location for decent money, this is just ok. But if you're a businesswoman(like I am) travelling alone or someone who expects as a minimum a pleasant atmosphere, I would recommend to stay away. I would also urge the manager of the hotel to come back to me regarding the ring, which of course has some value more than money for me who lost it.

title: Good base for business in the city.
text: I commute to London every day but I stayed in the hotel as I had an early-start event the next day and didn't want to risk the trains being late. The location was perfect, the room had everything I needed and it was quiet, so I had a great night's sleep before the event.

title: Club Quarters Gracechurch was Excellent
text: Great location and really quiet nights sleep. I booked a basic room which was excellent room with a huge bed and lots of facilities at the hotel which were free, the staff were always around to help also

title: Comfortable accommodation in London
text: I stayed in the Club Quarters in December 2011 after bidding for a hotel for the night on Priceline. The price for the night was reasonable although I could have booked online with the Club Quarter's themselves for very much the same price. Prices did seem to vary though depending on busy it was. I had a twin room with my daughter which was a reasonable size for London. Had a nice bathroom, a good size desk if you want to do some work, some interesting references books to use in the room (as the place is really designed for business people)TV, ipod dock and a fully functional clean bathroom. We only stayed the one night but would have been happy to stay a few more as was in a very convenient location for the tube, buses, Docklands Light Railway etc. Leadenhall Market is just across the road. The hotel, which is more like an old club, has a small lobby/lounge area as you come in off the street where you can sit and have a coffee or tea, or read a book. There is a coffee machine where you can make your own and is complimentary. There is also chilled water on hand and bottles to fill and take away. We didin't have time to worry about breakfast, but I believe it may have been possible to have this next door in an adjourning steak house - evening menu for the steakhouse looked quite nice, but I belive it is not open till very late for dinner if you are rush - am not sure about the opening hours for weekends. I think there was a Wetherspoons as well - open weekdays. However, if you don't go off to eat elsewhere and left with nothing else, there was a menu in the room from which orders can be delivered to your room from local eateries they had made arrangments with - we didn't try them as we had made arrangments to go out to eat. Some of the rooms had a small kitchenette for which you pay extra (these were advertised on our stay to upgrade to) - which is handy if you don't want to eat out all of the time, as eating out in London can be a bit pricey at the best of times. As every one always wants to know about what the experience was checking in, although it was a self check in via an automated machine that you use your card with, we got immediate assistance without having to ask from a very friendly and polite receptionist. I'd also telephoned them as beforehand to request a twin room as I didn't know what we'd get as I had booked just a room via Priceline, and they couldn't be more accommodating when I rang. Checking out via the machine on leaving was very quick, which was handy as we were a bit short of time to get our train home. As the place is so near a couple of tube stations, bus routes, without having to resort to taxis you can travel almost anywhere in London and outer from there, as long as you planned your journey before hand, particualry if you don't know London and can walk to a number of places as well depending on your interests.

title: Excellent Venue for short city break
text: Location was excellent, rooms were very clean and spacious. Facilities were very good and the staff were really helpful. Transport links to the city and beyond are on the doorstep or you could even walk.

title: Pleasant Stay
text: My husband and I stayed here over the weekend as we were part of a wedding party. We found the Hotel to be very efficient. The receptionist was very helpful when we arrived and sorted out directions for us to help us get to the Church on time, as we only arrived 20 minutes before the Wedding was due to take place.!! Thankfully the reception was at the Oyster Shed, just 5 minutes away,so we had no trouble finding the Hotel after. The room was pleasant, and the bed very comfortable. We decided to have breakfast in the Hotel the next morning, and this too was adequate, although we thought the full English was a bit pricey at £14.00 plus. However, it was a good choice of hotel and we would definitely stay here again.

title: Excellent service and location
text: The Club Quarters Gracechurch hotel has a great location, close to the Gherkin building, two blocks away from Monument Metro Station, and within walking distance of the Tower of London and the London Bridge. Besides, the service was very friendly and helpful, the rooms were clean and well kept. I would definitely stay here again in the future. Oh, and WiFi is complimentary, without password stuff!

title: Very Good Stay
text: Have just returned from a 3 night leisure stay here. I booked this hotel through hotwire and paid just £280 for 3 nights - fantastic! The hotel itself is in a fantastic location for the tube, buses even walking distance to so many things. Wasn't sure what to expect from the hotel due to some mixed reviews however I was more than happy with everything. Our room was small but adequate, likewise the bathroom

title: Could be better staffed
text: The room itself was good, spacious and clean etc. The set up of the hotel was a little strange, basically self serve. I checked us in on a computer at the reception area. Drinks are self serve, more pillows etc have to be brought by yourself to the room. The bed was slightly uncomfortable as the mattress was rock hard.

title: Location is the only postive
text: Great location if you are in the City, otherwise a drab, old fashioned hotel with very little to recommend it for the price. Rooms need updating and correct bills would be helpful - was charged somebody else room rate, but the guy on reception would change to the value on the booking I had actually made. I lost money on it!

title: Superb
text: Great hotel! Reasonably priced for London and close to the tube. Great touches in the room make your stay really comfortable. Everything you would expect from the higher premium end, with comfortable beds, refillable filter water and soft drinks and snacks all included. Would definitely book again!

title: Perfect weekend break
text: The hotels amenities were just excellent. There are complementary tea and coffee making facilities in the lobby a place to relax fruit biscuits nuts all complementary. Free wifi throughout the hotel including in bed rooms. Small room is very spacious newly refurbished and you can open the window or control your own air conditioning. Location is perfect with lots off shops and cafes around and tubes and busses on each corner. Staff are so helpful and welcoming. There are guest lockers on each floor offering guests extra tea coffee sewing kits etc. water dispenser and bottles on each floor provide convenience and that extra little touch. Would definitely recommend this hotel. 10 out off 10. :)

title: Lovely hotel in the city
text: My partner and i have just returned from a lovely weekend in London. My partner found this hotel on Lastminute as a secret hotel. After copying and pasting the description of the hotel through Google we discovered that it was the Club Quarters on Gracechurch street EC3. On leaving Bank tube station from exit 4 the hotel is only a 5 minute walk along Cornhill then turning right in to Gracechurch street and the hotel is located opposite Leadenhall market. On entering the hotel you instantly feel like your in a grand bank. The staff upon arrival were friendly and helpful. When we reached the 5th floor we could see that free water was available and that there is a cupboard for guests to help themselves to extra pillows, blankets, toiletries, iron, ironing board and refreshment refills. The decor of the rooms is smart and of a standard you would expect from a 4 star rated hotel, although a little on the small side. The room was clean and tidy and the hotel information guides handy and informative. The view from the window was disappointing as we looked out on to a building that was under renovation. Noise came from the site all weekend but not at night. See the picture provided. We arrived on the Friday and the area was busy with all the city workers with the shops open as usual. On the Saturday all the shops in the area were closed and the streets very quiet. On the Sunday the area was deserted with nothing open not even the pubs. We did not have breakfast included in the deal so used the Cross Keys pub next door on the Saturday morning which was another stunning former financial building now a whetherspoons pub. The cost of the buffet breakfast at the hotel was approximately 13 pounds at the Gaucho Restaurant which we avoided due to the price. On the Sunday the Cross Keys is closed so you would have to explore the area to find alternative breakfast dining if not willing to pay the high prices of the hotel restaurant. On walking back from nearby Brick Lane after a curry one night we tried the cocktail bar in the hotel. There was only 3-4 other people in the bar, which appeared brand new and with cowhide everywhere! The hotel is in a great location for the Tower of London, which is walking distance and exploring the City area of London. Overall we enjoyed our stay but would reinforce that at the weekend the area is very quiet with little open.
