This was one of the cheapest hotels that I found and we both thought the facilities were excellent, plenty of space and comfortable beds. There were only 2 of us in a triple room so may have been more cramped if at capacity and obviously had more luggage but it was more than sufficient for us! Breakfast was nothing special but with cereals, toast, croissants, fruit juices and hot drinks - you'd be fussy to eat nothing at all! We are already thinking of returning for another London trip later on in the Summer and would definitely return to this hotel.

title: Very good for the price
text: I stayed one night at The hanover hotel.The good points the place is decorated really nice colour schemes. The rooms was a little on the small side but it was clean and really good value for money. We had a triple room and I really can't complain. We had breakfast it was simple but that's all you need on a short break. The hotel was close to Wicked threate and BIlly ELliott. When we check out of the hotel we said bye to the member of staff on the reception and he didn't say any thing back.which I didn't think it was good customer service. I would stay at this hotel again if your a budget this is a great hotel

title: Cozy, but comfortable.
text: We stayed 4 nights and found the hotel to be clean and comfortable, although a bit "cozy" for three of us! Staff were very helpful (they carried our luggage all the way to the attic room where we stayed!!) , food was good. As there is no elevator and there are four floors between you and breakfast

title: Tiny room, overpowering smell of mould in bathroom
text: This is the first place that we stayed in England, not very impressed especially due to the price we payed for the 2 night stay. The room was tiny, could almost touch both walls when I stretched my arms fully out, could barely fit both of our bags in the room and the bathroom had the most sickening overpowering smell of mould (couldnt find the mould though). Positives about this place would be the location, central to almost everything and its in a fantastic wealthy suburb of Victoria with excellent public transport nearby. Hotel staff were friendly, carried our bags all the way to the top for us and the reception area waa quite nice and friendly.

title: Dirty and Unsafe Hotel
text: I had the misfortune of staying at this hotel in November 2004. When I arrived at the hotel the two 'gentlemen' in reception were so rude

title: London visit
text: This hotel has both positive and negative points but overall it is reasonably comfortable and I would stay there again. Negative points include a general shabbiness , redecoration should be a priority as my room has paint peeling from the wall. Also no lift, although the receptionist did offer help with my case. On the positive side, the location was perfect for me as it was just five minutes walk from Victoria station and fifteen minutes walk from Knightsbridge. The staff were outstandingly helpful and friendly and the hotel was clean. The room was small by Spanish standards but actually quite a good size for a hotel in central London! The double bed was quite small but very comfortable

title: average
text: average budget hotel set in a good location , handy for the theatres and good links to the uhderground

title: Outside vs Inside
text: We all know the saying 'don't judge a book by its cover.' The same can be said for the Hanover Hotel Victoria. Although this hotel sits in the heart of Victoria, surrounded by upmarket style homes and a good deal of shops, the inside is more like a rundown budget nightmare. Personally, after my 2hour journey from my home in Wales to London, I was expecting to have an easy walk to my room. However I quickly found that there was in fact no lift, only 5 flights of stairs to climb (each growing steeper and smaller going up them). I warn you, if you are unlucky enough to be like myself and get a room on the uppermost floors, you will need a good 5 minutes to recover from the gym-style workout you have just endured. What do you expect from a hotel room in upmarket, central London? Well I expected to find a spacious and modern room where I could comfortably put my bags(and head) down and then go back out. As you may have figured out, this was not the case! The walls and ceiling had paint missing from them, while the small curtain had black stains visible from all corners of this cramped room. The floor had a blaring orange stain by the door, while the desk was barely usable due to a lack of space. Moving onto the bathroom situation, the cramped room boasted a dated shower cubicle with a horrible smelling toilet and stained sink (pictures attached). Breakfast was a tremendous letdown also, as the so-called continental breakfast was a massive joke since there was only a fraction of what you would expect to be found there. Overall I would advise anyone looking for a hotel in London to avoid this nightmare at all costs! The area may look good and the price attractive, but looks can be deceiving. Have a good stay in London (just not here)

title: Very average
text: Extremely small room, very small bathroom not very modern and not especially clean looking. We were on fourth floor and as no lift was a real hike getting up the stairs.....staff were more than happy to help getting baggage up and down but don't think I would ever choose to stay there again...

title: Adequate for our needs
text: I stayed for one night with my 11 yr old child. I found the staff to be very helpful - allowed us to leave our bags before check in and again after checkout, so we didn't have to carry them round. No lift, so a walk up a couple of flights of stairs to our small twin room, which was clean and tidy. Not much space, but we only needed it to sleep in so didn't matter. Had t/v and kettle with tea/coffee etc. Got free Wifi as we booked direct on their website (which also gave us a discount on the room). Shower was not fixed to wall properly but did stay up! Beds were very comfortable. No air con, but a large fan in room helped keep us cool. Fairly quiet area and we didn't notice any noise at all, even though we were at front of hotel and had to keep window open due to mini heatwave! Breakfast was a bit of a sad affair, with a selection of 3 cereals, tinned fruit, toast and croissants, packet ham and cheese, apple/orange juice and a coffee machine. It is only 10 mins walk from the coach station and the tube at Victoria, which made it handy for popping back to freshen up.

title: Tough to rate but liked
text: This is a tough place to review. If i give 5 stars the Americans will expect a Hyatt which it is not. 3 stars would make the place seen like junk. So i rate it a five for what it is, traditional London b and b. Staff Very helpful, room clean, bathroom clean but all small Europe standard. We were in 2 separate rooms. Breakfast was cereal, bread, fruit, juices and tea coffee. No hot options. 10 minute walk to Victoria Station. Easy food options in Pimlico 7 minutes away. Staff was great. Only issue was we got hot at night, would have been nice to have a sheet and not a duvet.

title: Not that bad!
text: I inadvertently booked this hotel without reading the reviews on this site. I booked it through a last minute accommodation site. We find England (London particularly) grossly overpriced for the quality of just about anything. I say this as in our country you can get a room in a five star hotel for the same price that we paid for this hotel! The Hanover Hotel, compared to a couple we have stayed in previously in London, was a welcome relief. This could have been because we were expecting it to be REALLY bad after reading the reviews. A porter carried our suitcase to our room for us and the staff were very friendly and chatty unlike a previous one where we were lucky to get a grunt. So all in all not that bad.

title: Haven't stayed but booking process rubish
text: Booked a room months in advance trough booking.com on a flexible rate as we were unsure if we going to make it. Just to receive an email from booking.com week in advance that hotel true to preauthorised my card and it's declining. Hmmm wondering what's the point to book a flexible rate if they going to block money on my control week in advance. For those who doesn't know how preauthorisation works hotel is holding money on my account and even after thy release it in case I cancel or something liner still will be held for about 5 working days. But anyways since we already decided that we are definitely going I rang the hotel to ask them to try my card as well as it shouldn't decline. Well it did. Then I provided them different card which also declined. Strange. But anyways while all that I asked the girl on the phone what is the reason for such a police as it doesn't make any sense considering that I've booked the flexible rate. The answer was that I should have read t&c before booking and if anything I can always cancel the booking and go somewhere else. Hmmmm nice customer service. At the end I've cancelled my booking... And don't think I'll ever going to consider it for my stay again.

title: Faulty Towers!
text: I`ll keep this brief. The floor in my room was on a slant so when i laid in the bed my feet were higher than my head. Thats actually quite funny but thats as good as it got! The bathroom door did not close or lock. The hot tap would not turn off. The balcony was used as an ashtray by prior guests and not cleaned up. The continental breakfast consisted of 2 slices of toast and a bowl of cereal. But for and additional charge of £3.50 you could upgrade to the English breakfast which was made up of 1 sausage 1 rasher of bacon 1 fried egg and half a dozen baked beans. The front door is supposed to be open 24hrs but on returning back late one night at the unsociable hour of 12.30 it was locked. I know its a budget accomodation but i expected more for £89 a night.

title: close to victoria train station, great service, great value
text: stayed there for only one night, was perfect for me, great service, close to the train station and the reception is open 24 hours. breakfast was not good at all - only one star for that! but the rest was fine!

title: Perfect Location
text: We stayed here for one night, and we could not fault it, The staff were very friendly and welcoming, and also very helpfull. We stayed in room 101 on the first floor, it was spotlessly clean, comfortable mattress, it had tea/coffee making with plenty of everything, free wifi, and A/C, in one word very comfortable. The shower /toilet/room was on the small side, and so was the bedroom,but for us it was ample for what we paid. The breakfast was continental, 4 types of cereal, fruit juices, fruits salad, cheeses toasts jams and marmalade, the dining room itself was basic,but clean. All in all a good stay.

title: Dirty and cramped room. Breakfast depressing
text: I was put up here at the last minute on business. I had a room supposed to sleep 3 (double & single beds), but the space was cramped with just me and a small suitcase. The bathroom smelled badlly and there was visible mould on the tiles, whicb could be wiped off with a tissue (see photo). The carpet was stained and dirty. The continental breakfast was ok, but the slightly unclean tables and the views of what was going on in the kitchen made me pleased to get out. At £107 a night it made me ashamed to be British.

title: My wife had nightmares.
text: Let's do this chronologically. The hotel was very hard to find, but that is London's fault, not the hotels. The check in process went smoothly except they charged us for a map, and informed us that coffee and danish were served at 7:30 am for $14. British Airways left one of our bags in Rome, so I asked the front desk to check in with the airline, to see if it would be delivered that night. They said that I could call the airline from their phone at $.60 per minute. After a few minutes navigating the British Airways automated system, I was informed that my call would be answered in order. At which point, I hung up and paid the phone bill. This is a family owned hotel and all rooms with air conditioning had already been taken. We were given the last available room. There is no elevator so it required significant effort to climb the dark stairwells. As we climbed to the 4th and top floor, the stairwell got darker, narrower and slanted. At the top, they were little wider than our luggage. Some steps sagged as we stepped on them. I felt fortunate that neither my wife or I were injured ascending and descending the narrow, dangerous, stairs. Our first impressions, of the room, were stinky, hot, stuffy,dirty, run down and SMALL. After a while, you get used to the smell. But every time you open your eyes, you see the broken furniture and the horrible excuses for drapes (rags), carpets (threadbare), blankets (hand me downs), bed spread, and walls. The room was a filthy little 8' x 8' storage room in the attic.The linens were the only thing that was cleaned regularly. As soon as you get there, I recommend opening the window, pushing the bedspread and blanket onto the floor, and not walking in your barefeet. I cannot guess how many weeks or months it had been since the room had been cleaned properly.The bathroom was expectantly small and dirty. There was poor water pressure and the toilet flushed occasionally. You should really keep the toilet lid closed. And to prevent injury, take short showers which is easy since there is no soap or shampoo. The bed was tiny, hard, uncomfortable, and had awful pillows. We had just spent 16 exhausting days travelling Italy, Croatia, Spain, Sicily, and France. We were only able to sleep a few hours in this bed and my wife had nightmares about bed bug infestations. Since there was a chance that our luggage might be delivered after we checked out, we stayed quiet as we left and did not complain.

title: fantastic value for money with great views
text: we (myself , 3 teenagers and a child ) stayed at the hanover hotel for one night in may whilst visiting the sights and the theatre . after reading some not so good reviews i was unsure of what to expect!! i had nothing to worry about the hotel was decorated very tastefully and the room was plenty ample , with clean sheets and towels, complimentry tea and coffee and even freeview to the boys delight ! the bathroom was compact but clean and ample , even for my 6.5ft brother ! the views at night were fantastic looking out onto a floodlit houses of parliment and london eye (room 27) . breakfast was served up until 9.30 which is ideal when your not such an early riser , with as much tea ,coffee ,juice ,toast and preserves as you can eat , along with a full english or cereal . everyone at breakfast was tucking in and i saw no complaints . We were able to leave our bags in a left luggage room until later on the day of departure giving us another days shopping without carrying the bags with us . the staff were friendly and accomodating . if you want imacculate accomodation with five star service then this isnt for you .(and will cost you far more in this location ) if you want extremely reasonable rates with comfortable rooms clean sheets and a more than ample breakfast , close to londons attractions then i highly rercomend the hanover . it was a fantastic experience and will be booking again when we return to london .

title: If your on a budget......
text: Cheap and cheerful. Rooms tired, dinning area cramped. Building works going on in main reception so dusty mess awaits your arrival. Wifi very slow. If you can spend the extra money to stay elsewhere Id strongly recommend it. Apart from that it did the job.

title: hated, worst hotel ever, if u can call it a hotel
text: Where do i start, the directions firstly, sent us every route but the hanover hell hole, staff dont speak a word of english, are rude and ignorant. rooms and hotel spelt damp and un clean, When arrived the rooms were still un made. For the £90 we paid we were given a 10ft x 10ft room in the attic with two single beds joined to make a double both at different heights, We chose not to return to the hotel to shower and change before our theatre showing as we couldnt have it ruin our night as it was appauling, and would of felt more dirty than having been walking round london for 12 hours. When we got back from the show we found that our beds had been made but with the dirty sheets from the visitor before,We slept in our clothes on top of the sheets. In the morning we braved a shower to find that the ceiling had fallen down, no soap in dispenser and damp towels left on the side from the unlucky previous vistitors. Breakfast, "full english" by the time they managed to say the two english word i think all they know, it was in front of me, cold and not quite a full english, one hard fried egg, spoon full of beans, a sausage of meat that i wouldnt give to my dog. so u can guess that we didnt stay there any longer, we upt and left and never to return again. word of advice cancel before dissappointment, else youll be writing the same review as this when you return from your weekend away,

title: Nice hotel
text: We stayed at this hotel for the one night we were in London. Close to Victoria Coach station (and train station) once we knew where we were going. The stairways and hallways are small in this hotel (which is what to be expected in the city). The major problem we had was to carry our luggage up the 4 flights of stairs (we only had 2 bags but they weighed about 40lbs each.) If they had a small elevator that at least our luggage could have gone in would have been better. Breakfast that was included in the morning was very nice. Nothing special (cereal, yogurt, toast, coffee, juice) but it was just what we needed.

title: Fair stay for a fair price
text: Pleasant hotel with the basic necessities needed for a stay, the bed was comfortable and everything was clean. Breakfast was a standard continental - although I did notice they only had a 3 out of 5 stars food hygiene rating! Overall not bad for the price you pay considering the location.

title: Ms
text: Close to Victoria stations, restaurants and theaters. Clean and nice bath. Great staff offered to carry bags up and down stairs. And when I left phone charger there, they graciously agreed to mail it io me the very same day. Reassuring to stay in such an accommodating hotel! Definitely will stay again!

title: Good Value for the Price
text: Our 3-night stay here was fine. Room was small but clean, beds comfortable enough, great shower. Breakfast was fine, with plenty of choices available. Staff was helpful and friendly. The location was convenient, on a quiet street about a 10 minute walk from Victoria Station. Not sure why the place has gotten bad reviews from others. It's a good deal for the price and I recommend it.

title: Location fabulous, trains, buses and passport office!
text: First of all, staff on front desk extremely helpful and polite. The area was clean. Room was 201. Clean and dust free. Bed linens clean and ironed. The only gripe I would have is the shower stall, the cleaning staff need to bleach the heck out of that to get rid of grime and mould. I slept like a baby. There was tea making facilities, hair dryer, international adapters and tv with loads of channels. For location it is fantastic! 5 minute walk from Victoria station, 5 minutes from HM Passport office. Lots of different eating places. This hotel is basic however if you don't mind that and like to be somewhere quiet, this is it. I won't have any qualms using this hotel again because the location is great and the front desk staff are helpful. They just need to insist to. Their cleaning staff to do the proper cleaning of a shower stall to get rid of the mold. Breakfast I would give a miss but for cash conscious travellers its cereals, breads, cheese and cold cuts, juice, coffee, tea and yoghurt. Still better than no breakfast. Great location!

title: One bad experience
text: Decided on a weekend break to London with Canadian relatives. Booked in. Money taken off the credit card straight away. Climbed lots of stairs to get to the rooms. A very hot summer. Saw AC in the room. tried to operate it but it did not work. Enquired and was told extra £15/ day charge. We commented that we was not told about this during the booking. Anyway, argument ensued and at which point the manager got abusive over the phone. Never experienced anything like it in my life. Even stayed in India, China etc.. but this takes the biscuit. The owner was just as bad. Had to spend 1 night otherwise would loose one night's deposit. That's blackmail. DON'T DO IT!

title: Filthiest room I have ever seen
text: Late check in. When the sun came up, some sort of brown smear on carpet near bath room... black fuzzy stuff growing in the shower. All reported to staff who said they'd report to management. No other room was available. I spread towels over the bad stains and kept my shoes on. For three days the towels were removed but the stain remained. Given the filth, I did not eat the breakfast... room rate quoted was 20% lower than charged. When queried, staff replied that the rates are flexible depending on days. Tiny room with steep stair.

title: Comfortable but a dangerous shower.
text: Hotel staff and location were great. The room was comfortable for the price. The breakfast was free and not too bad, but the breakfast room was too crowded. The scary part was the shower. It took a long time to heat up. Then you would adjust it. While in the shower it could get cold or dangerously hot.

title: Good location and great value
text: My family and I visited London last week and chose to stay at this hotel because of the practical location. Overall we really enjoyed our stay, the service was flawless, the rooms were very clean, there was not a vast choice for breakfast but at least it was quickly prepared. Thank you to all the staff, they were very helpful and I hope to return to this hotel in the near future.

title: Good enough
text: 1. The water in the shower was just about warm enough. 2. People arrive late at night and the closing of the doors kept me up a bit, but if you're tired enough, you'll soon become immune to it! 3. The door entry cards need a direction of insertion printed on it. I spent over a minute trying to open the door without success and had to ask the guy in reception to do it. Of course, you have to insert it correctly, with force! (So maybe it's not entirely their fault?). 4. Upon walking to Victoria Station, I passed a Comfort Inn, so maybe I'll check their prices! 5. I've chosen 'Very Good' as the rating because I got what I paid for....I got a nice view of the London Eye from my room...so maybe I was lucky!

title: avoid it, below standard hotel
text: The hotel was very dirty. the bedding was smelling and damp.The bed cover was dirty colour and stinking. bathroom drain was dirty. Bedding was not changed and made for 3 days stay. Staff was very unhelpful and argumentative. Breakfast was just toast and butter. you can better hotels than this in the area. Just avoid it. Not recommended at all.

title: Perfectly Adequate
text: Managed to get a good deal for three nights on Last Minute.com. Perfectly adequate,and close to the station. Clean, comfortable bed,with TV, kettle and hair dryer. Breakfast included ,.Could have done with a sink plug in the bathroom! Not bad.

title: A great hotel
text: It was my second travel to London and the hotel left warm memories. The location is just perfect, all the sights within the walking distance. Unfortunately there were queues to have breakfast. But in general I would recommend this hotel and I would return to it.

title: Pleasantly surprised by the Hanover
text: We had actually booked the Airways Hotel across the road from the Hanover, and so were at first a bit put out to be told they were full up and we would be put up at the Hanover. But it WAS only just across the road, in the same kind of tall handsome terraced building as the Airways. The streets are quiet, and though they're very close to the Victoria coach and train stations, you feel you're going back to Regency times. I don't know if the hotel is family run, but it felt as if it was, and the staff were polite, friendly and helpful at all times. The decor was attractive and freshly done inside and out, and the rooms were comfortable and had everything we needed. We'd been put right at the top of the building - presumably because we were a last-minute booking on a busy weekend at the beginning of July. It was very hot weather at the time - but the room was cool enough thanks to the fan and open window. So if you're not good with stairs, mention in the 'special requests' that you'd like to be a bit nearer the ground! Most of the guests seemed to be tourists from all over the place, and they all got a good English breakfast, quickly and efficiently served, before going off sight-seeing - they didn't have far to walk to Buckingham Palace et al. We were there the night England played Portugal - we could have watched in the lounge downstairs but decided to opt for the TV in our room instead - just as well, in view of the inglorious result!

title: bugdet and convenient
text: The hotel is a prime location for the tourist, we stayed in hanover hotel on 2nd november.The staff is quiet helpful. The hotel is a old georgean buildings with a very good moden furniture and facilities.The room in which we stayed had a very good balcony and view of the city. i liked the very simple but traditional english breakfast.All sightseeing bus tours and tickets, advance entry to all major attractions are available in hotel and we enjoyed the wi-fi during our stay. In my room there was nice air-condition and new LCD Tv. Nice traditional food and pubs around the area. one thing i would say the break fast room could have been bit bigger as lot of people wants to have breakfast early in the morning and go for a day plans. Small reception very efficient in serving guest. we enjoyed london and especially Hanover Hotel as we dint not expect this big surprise of a cozy room in small money.

title: Very good central location
text: We visited this hotel for 4 Nights and enjoyed it very much. The location was perfect for daily trips for sightseeing and the are a lot restaurants nearby for having lunch and dinner. Breakfast is standard and not very special not so much variety but okay to start the day. The rooms were modern and cleaned very good every day. Only during the nights it was a bit too hot but there was a fan we used a lot. Sadly we couldn't turn off the heating. Allin all we would definately recommend this hotel.x

title: Convenient Lodging within Walking Distance of London Attractions
text: We stayed at the Hanover and had a very good experience. The staff was very pleasant and helpful and breakfast perfectly met our needs. The hotel is within walking distance of many of London's most popular attractions. It as our home base during our visit to London and we primarily used it for sleeping and breakfast. I would recommend it to other tourists who are looking for an affordable place to sleep and a quick breakfast before heading out for the day.

title: Ok hotel for what i paid £49 p/night
text: Cheap price in good loaction. There is no lift, I was on the top floor, the stairs got narrower as you went up making it hard to take cases up the stairs. The petite room is very small, very crampt. Basic room and in working order. Breakfast Ok. Room was cold and drafty so didnt get much sleep. Storage room has no lock on the door unlike other hotels like the comfort inn and was uneasy leaving my stuff in it.

title: Average hotel, good location but room not great
text: Stayed at this hotel for one night recently for work. Pros - good location short walk from Victoria station, good price for London...43 pounds for one night in a triple room, place to leave luggage for free on leaving day, also were accommodating with early check in, bed comfortable, quiet area Cons - freezing shower you could not stay under the water! Needs a better clean...dusty behind TV, no view of out window just a wall

title: London trip with friends
text: Hotel us great location for Victoria Station a bit of a walk but ok, Hotel is clean carpets could be better. Rooms we had on Third flour nearly killed us with the luggage as no lift🙁But it was a case if we wanted separate beds. Continental Breakfast was good so over all we were happy.

title: Good price and location
text: Rooms were fine, staff friendly, near tube station, breakfast was average. We had a room downstairs next to breakfast room so was a bit noisy in the morning if u don't get up early. ....................

title: Small rooms but clean
text: We stayed here for 2 nights when we arrived in the UK and the night before we departed. Both rooms were quite small, with very small bathrooms. Both bathrooms had problems with damp. Our second stay was on the underground floor with plumbing running down outside our window, which was noisy every time someone upstairs went to to toilet. Breakfast is basic but good. I would stay again, but I would look elsewhere first

title: business
text: didn't think much of the hotel as I was placed on the top floor which is a lot of steps to get there and if you have luggage near impossible. It is not a hotel for people who struggle with stairs. Breakfast was poor at best. I found the rolls dry as if they were from the day before. I was down at 07:30 when it starts so there was no reason for this. The other items at breakfast didn't come to much either. There was stains on the bed sheet as well. Positive points was close to station.

title: pleasure trip
text: The hotel was quite easy to find and once there we found the reception staff were polite and friendly.. The room however was not very clean, the carpet needed cleaning as was badly marked by the bathroom doorway and the toilet failed to stop running. We were moved to another room which was much better and cleaner and we had a good stay in this room. However, a little more attention to detail in cleaning the rooms would have made for a better all round experiance.

title: I would not stay here
text: I only gave this hotel a 1 ratings as it offered free breakfast. We were very disappointed with the room as plaster was coming off the wall, they offered an alternative but this had a really small window which made it feel even smaller. It was clean, but the pictures of the hotel do not reflect the hotel as it is very tired..Then 2 couples moved in next to us and kept their doors open chatting. We could not stay here so left and booked another hotel, we lost £120 but we made the right choice in leaving...

title: Value for Price/Location
text: The hotel is nothing fantastic, but for the price was really a good value - clean, quiet, comfortable. The room was small and we were on the top floor, which meant a LOT of stairs with our heavy bags, but we're fit and were only there for one night and considering our harrowing experience at the Nanford Guest House in Oxford (THE worst accomodations on the planet - read the reviews) it was really very nice to stay in this quaint little room and enjoy an adequate breakfast in the morning. I'm keeping this hotel on our list of places to return when passing through London.

text: The bed was very small. The street is busy, also at night. It was very warm. Breakfast was very bad.. only a slice of bread and some Jam.

title: NEVER AGAIN

The bathroom was dirty and smelly the system lid was broken and held together with black tape. The tea cups in the room had to be washed before use. Beds had clean covers but was I afraid to check under the bottom sheet.

title: So many choices, don't choose this!
text: I was very concerned prior to our trip about state of hotel following tripadvisor reviews. So much so that I contacted the hotel before our visit. I'm glad I did. The rooms we were given were acceptable, but I got the distinct impression that the hotel is being renovated one room at a time. One of our rooms was fine, the others- barely acceptable. The reception were helpful, putting additional beds in rooms (I complained that doubles were not acceptable for a school party). We were very spread out, not ideal for a school party. THERE ARE HUNDREDS OF HOTELS IN LONDON, MANY LESS EXPENSIVE AND FAR NICER. If you want to pay over the odds for what looks, feels and smells like student digs- stay by all means. My advice is stay elsewhere!

title: Good choice!
text: The hotel is very good located. The trainstation/underground is not far away but you can also walk into the city center. The rooms are good and the price is cheap. The person at the reception are very helpful and friendly. Breakfast is okay as well. I can recommend it to travellers that don't want to spend too much money on the hotel but want to stay close to the big ben (which we could see from out room!!!!) :))

title: Disappointing.
text: We were booked in for four nights over Christmas. Chosen for it's location which I can't fault. The level of cleanliness and breakfast however were not what I had expected. Towels were grey and smelt unwashed. Beds were comfortable but We found the carpet dirty and the it was impossible to control the shower temperature. To be fair when we complained we were offered another room but by then we had found another hotel on the same road which was of higher quality so we got a refund and moved after one night at the Hanover.

title: Best in the Bed & Breakfast
text: Stayed here for a month while i was on a business trip for over 15 days. Enjoyed my stay .. the breakfast is good. The tube is close by for my daily commutation. The people were helpful in planning my weekend sightseeing. You will be at a walking distance from Buckinghum Palance and you can pay a daily visit to the queen

title: Good location and good price!
text: I've been in this hotel for 3 nights on the beginning of June 2010 with my girlfriend. The room was small, as almost everyone in London but it was what we expected. Small, but clean and suficient for everything we needed. There was some noise during the night because our room was next to the elevator. We heard lot of noises coming from the floor of the room upstairs. The noise was really what we disliked more. The best was the location. We could go by foot to 2 metro stations (victoria and pimlico) and we could go by foot to central places like big ben or buckingham palace (20 minute walk). Belgrave road is full of hotels and it's a very good place to start your trip in London.

title: A very poor value of a hotel.
text: I had the misfortune of staying here for a week. Check In/Out was quick. Room was quite small for what I expected. It's located mid way in the block so when cars or emergency vehicles go passing by at night, the sound literally gets channeled down street. It quite literally sounds like you are sleeping on the street. The staff were less than helpful. I had issues with the internet connection several times. There were a fair number of people in the lobby complaining about it so it wasn't just me. The cleaning staff were very rude. I felt like I had to work around their schedules. All around a very poor value of a hotel.

title: Value for money
text: Stayed at Corona back in August. Rooms are very small but were modern and clean. Hotel is in a great location and was perfect for a couple of days break in London over the weekend. Breakfast was great, couldnt have asked for better. Service was ok, only criticism would be the lack of an iron/ironing board in the rooms. But these were available from reception upon request.

title: Lone Traveller
text: The room I was in was very snug but clean and had everything I needed. Staff were very efficient and friendly. The hotel is situated in a very central area so good for sight seeing. Street of hotel was very nice too. Unfortunately I had a road facing room and while I appreciate London can be a busy place feeling as if I was sitting kerb side all night isn't acceptable. Very ill fitting doors/window with no double glazing meant a really noisy and horrendous nights sleep as well as a bit crafty though there was a heater. If you do stay here ask for a room at the back anything is better than what I had to listen to all night

title: Basic London Mid Price Hotel
text: We were just looking for a mid range priced hotel in London. Just somewhere to "crash" after a days sightseeing. We booked this hotel as it was extermely handy for Pimlico Tube Station & Victoria Train Station. The Tate, Buck Palace,Science /Nat History/ & the V & A Museums are also just a 20 minute walk away. As stated before we only wanted a basic room. The room was clean, BUT, the Air Con was broken & it was extermely hot. They had placed a fan in the room, but this was not much help. Also the TV was nowhere near suitable. Just a basic 18" portable with every channel not set up properly. AGAIN, You get what you pay for & it was just a place to collapse in at night. Plenty of extermly good placed to eat around that area. Thia/Chinese/Indian, you name it it was there. If I had to choose again I would look elsewhere, but all in all it was OK.

title: Above & Beyond.
text: Fantastic little hotel. Clean as a whistle. Reception staff very friendly, helpful & polite. Breakfast was lovely & breakfast staff just as nice as the reception staff. Room had everything I needed. Very comfy bed. Amazing power shower. I was in room 111 for 2 nights. I would recommend it & I would definitely use this hotel again.

title: Staff make the hotel
text: Me and my boyfriend endured a 2 night stay here the weekend of the 15th February. Upon arrival the hotel staff were very friendly and helpful, as we had arrived early they stored our bags until we came back for check in at 2pm. A negative is that the rooms are very small and cramped, we were having to step over our suitcase throughout our whole stay. The bathroom was also very small with doors of the shower that didn’t completely close and the shower itself constantly dripped although being off. Despite this, the bed was very comfy and the staff were extremely helpful. On a few occasions we asked for an iron/ ironing board as well as a hairdryer and the staff brought them up to our room without a problem. As well as this we ordered a takeaway to our room as soon as the food had arrived we were informed by reception. Breakfast was mediocre but substantial. Also bottled water was £1.50 per bottle and as there was no other way of providing us with water, we had to buy numerous bottles during our stay which isn’t very good. Overall the staff make this hotel, very helpful and lovely apart from one exception. Our stay was very enjoyable, hotel is located very well.

title: Nice little budget hotel
text: We are pleasantly surprised by the value of this hotel after staying there for a week in September. It is located within walking distance from Victoria Station, which makes it convenient if flying into Gatwick and taking the Express to Victoria. The closer Tube station to the hotel is Pimlico. If you don't mind walking, it is possible to walk (albeit a long walk) to all the major sights such as Westminster, Parliament, Buckingham Palace, Trafalgar Square, etc. The room, although small is clean and has all the essentials including hair dryer, kettle, pant press. The shower is wonderfully large with lots of hot water. The sink is strangly small but the bathroom appears to be recently renovated. The hotel is situated on a main street but we were never bothered by street noise. There are quite a few reasonably priced (for London) restaurants in the surrounding area. Breakfast is continental buffet style with the normal cerals, juice, breads, toast, croissants, cold meats, cheese, and fruit. Staff members are friendly and accommodating, allowing us to check in as early as 10 am in the morning.

title: Pleasant little hotel in a good location
text: We spent a week in London at the Best Western Corona in late August and ultimately decided we had made an excellent choice. Americans used to the unlimited expanses of the great plains might find the compactness of the rooms at a moderately-priced big city hotel surprising, but as residents of New York City, we did not. If we were judging the Best Western Corona as a trendy luxury hotel for jetsetters, well...it's not, nor does it pretend to be. But by the typical and reasonable standards of this type of city hotel, the Corona came out well and gave us a pleasant stay. Here's our experience: We arrived late in the evening and at first were given a room on basement level -- this one *was* tiny, airless, and so close to the breakfast room that we feared excessive noise in the morning. Gentle reader, do remember: one doesn't have to accept the first room any hotel offers! We immediately asked for another room, which was cheerfully granted. The room we were given was on the 4th floor and actually had a lovely distant view of Big Ben, the London Eye and the Swiss Re building. It was small, but a bit bigger than the other one -- and those few extra square feet made all the difference. Like all hotels on Belgrave Road, the Best Western Corona is comprised of what were once Georgian houses, now connected as one structure. Although perfectly modernized, there's a bit of an old-timey hotel experience in staying in an antique building that is not made of concrete and steel. The neighborhood is wonderful

title: A wee gem
text: We booked a two night stay in London to go and see a show and were lucky enough to get two nights for the price of one in this hotel. The room was comfortable enough. Some may see it as being a little cramped but lets face it, you don't go to London and spend time in your hotel room! There's plenty of storage and wardrobe space. The shower is brilliant, lots of room and really good power. I was really impressed with the bathroom all round. The only downside to this hotel is the breakfast. The dining room is small and cramped and if you go at the wrong time you'll have to queue for a seat. If you aren't up for breakfast when it begins then you are unlikely to ever see the selection of foods on offer. This hotel does continental breakfasts only and the variety of food available is poor. The pastries run out very quickly, the toast will be cold when it arrives and the restaurant staff are very unfriendly. In fact, the head waitress gets quite uppity if you don't hear her shouting across the room whether you would like tea or coffee! We didn't let this put us off though, for the price you are lucky to get breakfast included and there is no short supply of places in the vicinity where you can get a full english breakfast for next to nothing. We did this the second morning of our stay as we couldn't face the breakfast room again. I will definitely stay at this hotel again, although I won't be having breakfast there!

title: Short stay
text: Hotel is perfectly located near major attractions and Victoria station. It is an old Victorian building converted into a hotel. Unfortunately the single room I had was way too small. It was little uncomfortable for me to move around, especially if you have a big luggage. I had clean sheets and towels, overall everything looked very clean. Ok for short stay.

title: Good value great location
text: I stayed for one night on a business trip, really pleased that the hotel was near to the underground and within walking distance of Westminster, lovely walk to my meeting the next day by the river. The hotel was small and in an old building so a bit rickerty . The room was small but had everything needed for a comfortable stay. It was spotlessly clean , bed and pillows comfortable, pleased that there was a mirror over the dressing table as many hotels don't bother with this now and I like to sit comfortably in the morning to do my make up and hair. The TV reception was a bit hit and miss but that didn't bother me too much as I was only staying one night and i used my ipad as they had free wifi. My room was at the back so nice and quiet and I could control the heating so wasn't too hot at night which can be really unpleasant. The breakfast was fine, plenty on offer and good value at under £6. Staff were friendly and helpful. I would gladly stay again , bit of a bargain for the location.

title: holidays
text: Hi, i don't have so much things to tell, because we just slept in, all the things i can say are written in lines before. We didn't stay enough to tell many things. The breakfast was nice too, with the service.

title: Average, not bad when compared to others in the area
text: The rooms are generally clean, it has free wifi (but only in the lobby area, which extends to rooms on ground floor and perhaps 1st floor) and free wired Internet. However, there is no central heating or air conditioning although they supply heaters and fans. I've stayed in summer and winter and been uncomfortably cold and hot at times. The breakfast is mediocre, bread, ham, cheese, cereal, toast and coffee and some orange stuff that resembles orange juice. The biggest issue I've encountered is with the water - many times there has been no cold water! Warm water comes out of the cold tap, and it's impossible to regulate the shower temperature! Overall, it seems overpriced for a pretty low standard hotel but the location is great, and other hotels in the same street are worse...

title: Very Small Room
text: This hotel is fairly close to the Pimlico tube stop and a fair walk to Victoria Station, although we usually chose to walk to Victoria. There is shopping district between the hotel and Victoria that has a Tesco, KFC and other small restaurants. The staff was friendly and helped us book a day tour to Stonehenge and Bath. The room was clean but one of the smallest we have stayed in. We asked for a double and should have requested a twin because we got a double bed that was uncomfortable for two people. The room had a/c that worked. Having stayed in several previous hotels and B&B's in London that were noticeably shabby, we were pleased that this hotel appeared better maintained, neat and clean. We did not eat breakfast at the hotel. It is within walking distance of the Tate Britain museum and Victoria Station.

title: Great Staff, Small Rooms
text: I was met by a friendly smile and efficient booking in process. I had a double room with no view and when I opened the curtains the air vents were stuffed with toilet paper? The room was very small but reasonably well laid out, the odd stool was stuffed into the only available space for it, it couldn't really be used unless you put your feet on the bed?? Room rate was reasonable for the area. Good access to a couple of pubs and restaurants. Breakfast was ok, nothing to write home about but again friendly service.

title: Adequate hotel in good location. Rooms small.
text: Had a stopover in London, so booked the Best Western Corona with air miles. Most of the previous comments are valid. The single room that I booked was really small, and when they say single, they mean it. I can't figure out how they would have placed another person in this room. The room also faced Belgrave Road, which is pleasant, but loud, even on a Sunday morning. This said, the hotel is about a 5 minute walk from Pimlico Tube stop, or a 10 minute walk from Victoria station, with the major coach and rail services in the area. Location is pretty good, and this part of Westminister is safe and not dodgy at all. Room came with free Internet access (wired or wi-fi for laptops), and a TV that did not work. The bathroom is small, with a shower stall only, and (yes) a very small sink. And surely, they could pitch in for a face towel? That said, the room was perfectly clean, the foyer is tidy, and the hotel ambiance was clean and well-maintained. Since this was a booking by points, I don't know if this was good value or not (though easyhotel is just around the corner), but this part of town is relatively safe and centrally located.

title: New Years Eve in London
text: We couldn't have asked for more helpful and friendly staff!! Such lovely people, throughout our stay they were more than accommodating! The room was lovely and clean, bigger than we were expecting and the bathroom looked brand new! Room service was available at an extremely reasonable cost it saved us a lot of running around so we ate while we were getting ready for our night out I would happily go and stay again, they are central to all the main areas you'd like to visit Thanks to you all for an excellent service

title: Excellent
text: Great location ! Small rooms, small hotel, but clean and New refurbished. Victoria is a great area , close to good restaurants and other attractions . I Will not hesitate to stay there Again on my next visit to London

title: Very small room and no air conditioning
text: We stayed here for one night in August in a double room. It was clean and comfortable but very small. It was a warm weekend but there was no air conditioning, which made the room uncomfortable. There were doors opening onto a small balcony but they were locked. With no other windows in the room the only thing we could do for some air was too climb up on the bed to reach a small window above the balcony doors. The bathroom was so small the door couldn't open fully. It hits the toilet bowl on opening. The shower door was broken and came off its runner. Breakfast is over priced so we ate nearby in a lovely place called Kazan Kitchen. We won't stay here again. It's a good location for what we were doing but very overpriced even for a London hotel.

title: Don't expect to feel welcome.!!!
text: Arrived early in the day and was almost trampled by a costumer who wanted help with a flooding room!! receptionist couldn't care less.! Rooms are small for the money. In the morning.. went to ask for a bit of tea in the kitchen as there was noone in the restaurant and no food worth eating avalable.. Met by polish girl who looked like she had a sour lemon stuck in her mouth and it had been in place for several years.. NO SERVICE WITH A SMILE HERE..!!! Was left feeling awful for asking the misserable sod for a cup of tea. She then proceeded to bring cold toast which she dumped unceremoniously on the table .. NO SMILES HERE..!! Wouldn't go back and wouldn't recommend. Go somewhere else for your hard-earned cash.

title: Best of the Best
text: Stayed here on several occasions and have always received a great welcome and great stay. Will definitely being staying again and bringing the family along, a great place to stay if you want to visit sights of London, not far to tube station or walking distance to London Eye.

title: It is ok for a short stay
text: This hotel is near Victoria Station, which makes it convenient for getting around the city. Of course, it isn't really close to Victoria Station. It is at a distance that makes it annoying to walk to the station when you are tired. The room I stayed in was very small. Not enough room to put a suitcase down and the noise from the street is a bit much until later at night when it quiets down. They did provide a fan which was essential as there is no AC and it was very hot! The bed was not comfortable and the pillows were extremely flat and not soft at all. I did not have the breakfast so I can't comment on that. Wireless was free, but very poor. It was not strong enough for a skype call as it kept dropping the call. The hotel is overpriced for what you get. I would not stay here again.

title: Not worth staying at
text: We stayed two nights in this one. I have spent many nights in best western hotels, and this one should be classified as an economy hotel. Room was small, bed rolled around on an uneven floor, the shower was in a bad state, the loo seat was loose, and the supposedly free wifi did not work. The room was so hot, that although it was freezing outside, you slept with the window open to keep the room cool. Breakfast is only a continental, and nothing special at that, so no good cooked breakfast to get you going for the day. All in all a waste of the 64000 points I used up on the hotel.

title: Smallest hotel room in London...
text: I chose this hotel for it's location as I was running an event nearby. I really think they should make it very clear when booking how small the room is - the term 'couldn't swing a cat' comes to mind and it felt a bit like a prison cell as the windows were high up. In saying this though the room was clean and the continental breakfast was adequate, however I won't be booking to stay here again though.

title: Broom Cupboard with a Bed
text: Visited for business, nice welcome but this is where the quality stopped. My appointed room was tiny in the basement. The bathroom was poor - no bigger than a wardrobe - toilet was positioned under the sink such that it was impossible to sit normally on it and the seat was stained with years of ingrained use. Shower door off its hinges. Next to a fire door to rear of hotel which guests/staff were using as some sort of smoking area til late at night with commensurate disturbance, further compounded by the constant drone from the hotels aircon units attached to the outside wall at the back of my room. Breakfast was adequate. Only saving grace was outstanding little Italian restaurant up the road called o sole mio!

title: Worst Best Western we have stayed in - Shame
text: Room and shower room very small, old style television on top of wardrobe. No hot breakfast, cheese had slightly curled up edges and I was horrified that when the couple next to us left the waitress left forks on the table for the next person to use! Cold water ran hot in room, basin plug could not be popped up - Good job my husband knows plumbing. Reception staff were polite but I would NOT stay there again. And how they got 4 AA * I can't guess. Oh and my back might stop hurting, the mattress was so sloppy my husband said he thought it was a water bed and I had to hand on to the edge all night to avoid rolling into the middle - Room 201

title: Location...and that's all
text: Excellent central location in a typical londonian street, 1mn walk from Pimlico metro station, this hotel is a shame for the Best Western brand... A 12 m² "family room" from the 80th, a 2 m² bathroom, no air conditioning, no double glazed window, no blackout curtain, no safe, no need to unpack your luggage as there no space for your clothes and for your toiletries. Poor breakfast open till 9:30, no storage room. In one word...NO!

title: Nice little hotel
text: Nice little hotel rooms pleasant with a nice breakfast clean and comfortable would stay here on business again easy location for Pimlico tube ...will recommend this hotel to colleagues and friends a wee bit expensive £125 per night staff very pleasant and helpful

title: Not up to Best Western standard
text: Very simple hotel acceptable only for sleeping. Beds and bathroom OK, continental breakfast acceptable but othervise has nothing to offer. Limited TV-channels with bad quality, minimal monitor. Very hot during warm weather, no ventilation or A/C. No general spaces in the hotel, you have to be in your room sitting on the bed. The surrondings are calm but have not much to offer.

title: better than expected
text: As two mature ladies we stayed for two nights 11th /12th ofJune in two single rooms,both really good and they provided us with everything we needed and very comfortable beds.Ignore all the silly comments about noisy Belgrave Road,yes it is on a bus route just close the window.Best location, bus stop on the doorstep and Pimlico station 3 minutes walk .10 minutes walk to the Tate Gallery and another 10 to the Houses of Parliament.Staff very helpful and we would use this hotel again.

title: Compact Hotel.
text: Stayed for 3 nights, 1 double room with breakfast. Had breakfast 1st morning and decided to not bother as it was very basic, but this was not a problem for us. Yes the rooms are compact, and bathrooms are tiny only room for 1 person. Overall very pleasant stay and the front office staff were very welcoming. The only thing that was very annoying was the chamber maid kept slamming, the entrance door to the tiny corridor outside the bedroom, and well we were only 20 minutes pass check out time. Would stay again providing the price was OK...
