title: At the heart of the city
text: We stayed at the Best Western hotel for 4 days the past weekend. The hotel was extremeley close to Victoria, next to bus 24 stop (to Leicester square), and had around all type of facilities, from nice, cosy restaurants to have breakfast to Sainsbury's and Boots. The staff was really kind, helpful and proffessional! We almost forgot a handbag on our leaving day and the cleaners took it to the reception so that they could warn us about the situation! They were awesome! The room (we stayed in a triple) was very comfortable, nice, clean and it had all the services needed, from a nice,equipped bathroom to complimentary tea,water and buscuits. The only bad thing about our stay was the fact that, on our first morning, they had to repair the window of the room next door, so we had a noisy wake-up alarm. However, everything else is far worth a slight trouble and we recommend the Best Western Corona for London stays!! We most certainly will be coming back for more!!

title: Great location
text: Stayed one night for work,really easy to get to. Plenty of places nearby to grab food and drinks too. Don't expect luxury this provides clean base in very central location and no more. I have stayed at holiday inn over the road as well which is identical but on average 50% more expensive. Only big downside to corona is no a/c.

title: Hot, friendly, cramped and uncomfortable
text: One night in this hotel was enough. It was one of the hottest nights of the year, and my single bedroom at the front of the hotel was one of the smallest rooms I've ever stayed in. It faced the street, was extremely noisy and, with no air conditioning, was like a small furnace. The original sash windows are very attractive, but wouldn't stay open so I had to ask the receptionist to fix it for me (which she did). They thoughtfully provide a fan, but it was fighting a losing battle against the heat. On the plus side, the bed was comfy and with good white linen. The bathroom though was something else

title: Great Staff
text: This hotel isn't anything out of the ordinary. It delivers what it says it will - a budget end offering in central London. That said, it is clean, tidy and staffed by a very friendly and efficient team of people. The rooms have recently been refurbished and although on the small side, are perfectly adequate for a couple of nights when in town on business. Breakfast is okay for the price paid and again, served by welcoming staff. Maybe this wouldn't be my first choice if visiting London for leisure but as a business hotel, you could do a lot worse.

title: Best location at budget
text: The hotel is located near Victoria train station which is best suited for connectivity to all across London. The hotel rooms are OK for double occupancy and provides complimentary breakfast. Breakfast options are good. Must recommended for short business trips.

title: Excellent Base
text: This hotel can't be beat on location, cleanliness and service. After two days of travel from the states we arrived at the hotel at 9.00am, check in is typically 2pm. We were imediately checked in to our room 5 hours early. The rooms are small but modern, clean and comfortable. You don't go to London to sit in your hotel room anyway! The bathroom is brand new with excellent water presyure. I am a British citizen now living in the U.S. and have stayed in tons of these boutique hotels when visiting home. This is by far the best ever. Easy access from Gatwick express, 5 pound cab ride from Victoria train station and Pimlico tube station 5 minuites walk away, central to eveything. Highly recommended.

title: Decent Enough
text: We booked a girls trip to London for a week. There were 4 of us in 2 different rooms. We stayed on the ground level and found the accommodations to be okay. The rooms were small but workable. The one issue we had was lack of electrical outlets. Halfway through our trip, one whole set of plugs stopped working, which meant some juggling when it came time to charge. There was a hairdryer in the room, which was awesome. No one told us breakfast was extra and not included when we booked our rooms. The hotel did have an iron that they let us use. We didn't spend much time in our room so it was okay, but next time I visit London, I will probably upgrade to a slightly nicer hotel. The location was fabulous, we heard no noise at all when sleeping (with windows open), and the staff was nice. However, there aren't a lot of extras, and the bathroom shower is very, very small, so that's why I would upgrade next time.

title: London Corona
text: I want to use less than 200 characters for chicken-coop rooms and plumbing which appears to connect like in our stays in Tanzania. There you would turn the hot and cold water on and the hot water would flow to another room. They blame the whites for teaching them plumbing although it was the Russians and East German political appointments sent in the '60s who did the incompetent work. Is this 200?

title: good hotel for not close to any major landmark
text: This was a good hotel if your trying to see a different part of england, although there is no AC in this hotel and if you are trying to get on wifi it only lets 1 person on from your room at a time and it kicks the other person off. Beautiful area around but just wasn't what we were wanting to stay by.

title: Great for short city break
text: Good location for Apollo Victoria Theatre, Victoria and Pimlico stations - all within a short walking distance. Reception staff very friendly and helpful in getting taxis, helping arrange trips. Breakfast was continental with a hot option as well. Not a five star breakfast by any means but was fresh, warm and very good for the price. Dining room pleasant and staff attentive and friendly. The hotel is currently being redecorated. We had a refurbished room. Although the room was small, the room had everything we needed - it was clean and the beds were comfortable. There is no air conditioning, so the rooms are very hot but there was a fan and you can open the window - manage at home like that every night and after all, you only sleep in the room! Overall, this hotel is a good 3 star for London. This is reflected in the price and what the hotel had to offer. If you are expecting more, book a five star hotel and pay the price!

title: Great location, small room
text: Hotel is located in a very quite area few steps away from Pimlico tube station, within walking distance of Victoria Station. Typical Victorian style street of white houses, many of which are hotels as well. Very fast check-in and check-out, my room was very small, but that is what you expect at this kind of hotels. As most Best Western hotels, only basic equipment, i liked marble floor in the bathroom. Toiletries provided every day. The only thing that needs improving is their WLAN access system. Each day, you have to get a new printout with username/password for the network, which is pretty annoying if you stay from three days like I did (and always forgot to ask for a new one on my way back). Giving one code for your whole stay would be much better.

title: Basic, but reasonable for the price
text: In central London, with reasonable transport links, a few minutes walk from Pimlico Tube station, 15 mins walk from Victoria station, and on major a bus route (No. 24). My room was fairly basic but included most requirements, and the bed was comfortable. Free wifi was included in the room rate. Negatives included a window with a slightly broken lock, which for a lower-ground floor room was of a little concern, and lacked a mini-safe for valuables. Service was good and polite, but the breakfast was basic, comprising mostly cereal, bread, danish, fruit, cold ham and cheese, but no hot food. Only a very limited room service menu was available. Overall, fairly basic accommodation for this price range, but given London prices was reasonable value.

title: Good Hotel
text: Hotel is near London landmarks. it's not a big hotel but enough for what you need. Rooms are somewhat small but is good enough to rest. Bathroom area is also small but I think it depends on the type of room because the other room that our kids occupied has a spacious bathroom. Staffs are nice, approachable and helpful from reception, to housekeeping, and breakfast staff. All-in-all it was a good and satisfying stay.

title: Horrible
text: Too too expensive for the price, with nothing much in the hotel. The rooms are very small, And the breakfast nothing much......

title: ideal location small room
text: my wife & i stayed here for 1 night on new years eve the location was excellent not to far from the houses of parliment the eye etc but far enough away to be not to noisy. when i booked in i asked the receptionist how far it was to westminster & the london eye she said that we would have to get a bus as it was to far to walk, we decided to walk anyway we got there in about 3/4 an hour along the thames (dont people ever walk in london) we had a great time watching the fireworks at the eye, we walked back but a word of warning make sure you know exactly where your hotel is as all the roads look the same especially if you have a load of beer inside you also if you are a bit of a bloater like me make sure you have a skinny wife cos the bed & the rooms are small lol

title: Couple of days in London
text: We chose this hotel as it seemed to be within easy walking distance of Buckingham Palace, before we knew about the tube strikes! On check in the staff were pleasant and helpful, with complimentary newspapers on the counter. Free London maps etc also provided to help us get around without tubes. Our room was compact, but had all the usual facilities, e.g. Large TV, coffee/ tea making facilities, en suite shower room. The shower enclosure was quite generous, but the sink was in one corner, and there was no "work surface" to place items near the sink. The room did seem to have been recently decorated, re carpeted etc. the bed was comfortable. We stayed during a hot spell, and the small room became quite warm with no air con. We opened the window on to Belgrave Road, which did have the odd loud motorbike, and "shouty people" late at night, but it was no big deal. reception managed to book us a taxi at short notice, to take us to Theatreland in the evening, as there was a tube strike. Breakfast was self service continental style, with a selection of cereals, scrambled egg, beans, yogurts, pastries, toast, rolls, ham, cheese etc. again the staff were pleasant and helpful, serving coffee and toast. Plenty of empty tables during our stay. The hotel is well placed for walking to Pimlico underground or Victoria Station. There are plenty of pubs, restaurants and shops ( Tesco, Sainsburys and Waitrose) within easy walking distance. There was free wifi, but in our room it was a bit patchy.

title: Small but perfectly formed
text: One night stay in April with work and what a lovely little hotel it is. Whilst appreciating for the cost you will not get a big room and even though I literally could not swing a cat in my single room it was clean and warming, Lovely comfortable bed, clean bathroom with lovely shower and in a great location on Belgrave Road. Lovely friendly reception and breakfast staff always smiling and willing to help a hand with tourists not used to the area. Breakfast was lovely and lots of it if wanted and the hospitality was brilliant. If you want t cheaper London city centre hotel that is affordable this is the one. Whilst its not luxurious and is very basic its clean and friendly basic which suits me.

title: Great value, great staff
text: I stay here regularly for business as the location is great for eating out, staff are very welcoming and always remember you. The rooms whilst small they are very clean and yes outside can be noisy in the front rooms but not always and as hotel manager has said, it's not something they can control and it is a busy city. Breakfast is basic but more than ample and always fresh. I've stayed in lots of hotels in London and for the price and location of this 3 star hotel, you do get good value

title: a bit out from Oxford street, but great small hotel
text: nice tourist hotel a little out of town, but with a metro near the hotel, not big rooms but still cosy and space able, we were almost thrown the hotel deal in the neck from our trip organizer for 800 DKK on top of our plane tickets for 4 days in London including breakfast. this we had certainly nothing to complain about, and we were more or less only at the hotel to sleep eat and throw our purchase of . But a real and efficient hotel which lived up to it's reputation as a best western. And we must admit we have lived in a part through time in both the United States, France, Germany, Spain. and certainly not the last time we get to their hotels

title: Horrible
text: It was the worst hotel I've been in a long time. Shower did not drain the water, the room was really small, horrible WiFi, terrible breakfast and the guy on the reception did not help us at all. The girls were nice and helpful, but the guy that received us didn't make us feel welcomed here. Don't waste your money here

title: Great service
text: What makes a hotel stand out? Cleanliness and service. The Corona on Belgrave in London, aced both of these categories. Pleasant, helpful staff, clean room and nice continental breakfast included. Plus internet service was excellent. I say this because oftentimes internet service is spotty in hotels if working at all. Highly recommend this hotel.

title: Not bad, but basic!
text: We had 2 double rooms and 1 triple. Doubles were tiny - bedroom and bathroom, very basic dated, but adequate for an overnight stay when all you'll be doing is using it to sleep, triple however was at least 4 times the size and like a suite in comparison. Not your typical best western.

title: Very Happy to Stay there Again
text: The Corona Hotel is situated on Belgrave Road, London where there is plenty of competition for similar hotels. Some very good and some very poor. It is in a great location for Central London if sightseeing with lots of bars and restaurants nearby. The Corona is certainly very comfortable and perhaps at the better end of the range. A few steps to negotiate on entry but a very warm welcome at reception and easy check-in. My room was on the ground floor at the top of the stairs that lead to the breakfast dining area. The room was a good size, comfortable and well reasonably well equipped. The bathroom was clean and modernised although space was at a premium when using the toilet as one has the sink almost on one's lap forcing a slight sideways manoeuvre when seated. Ihad to be up relatively early for work however a lie-in may not be possible for all as one can hear noise from the breakfast guests as they descend the stairs outside my hotel room door and eat their breakfasts. Neither were a particular problem to me and I would not hesitate in staying there again on my frequent trips to London.

title: Hotel Corona- The Crown of London
text: Great experience in this centrally located hotel. There are single rooms so you don't need to get lost in a double room if your travelling on your own, family rooms are also available. Clean hotel and well presented staff and good for local attractions and transport links. Staff at the breakfast even remembered that I liked brown bread, so really made me feel welcome and at ease. Overall good value for money and I'll definitely be back!

title: Adequate
text: Just been on a business trip to London. The tube to Pimlico took 10 mins on the Victoria line and the hotel was a 5 minute walk. Outside this hotel looks elegant and there are a number of lovely bistros and pubs nearby. The staff are friendly and helpful and you get free newspapers. Breakfast was good if u don't want a Full English with only scrambled egg and beans by way of hot food, but there was a good choice of cereal, pastries, cooked meats and cheese, food and yogurts. It was clean. Unfortunately the rooms are extremely disappointing. If I hadn't been on the company funding I would have been gutted.....but it wasn't, cheap! My colleague text me to describe his single room as a childrens bed in a cupboard, and it painted a perfect picture. I could nearly touch both sides if I'd Have stretched my arms out. The room was extremely tired, with holes in the walls where paintings had once hung and toilet paper stuffed in the window to plug holes in the woodwork and keep the draft out. My heating did not work and the large heater placed on top of my broken one would only work if I lifted it onto the dressing table due to the location of the plugs. As such I didn't use it as I needed space to work, which is limited in a shoe box! I was freezing and slept in a jumper. I had no hot water at 1st and on complaining the receptionist albeit extremely friendly condescendingly tried to tell me how to turn the taps from hot to cold....at 45 yrs old I worked that out many years ago! Nevertheless I located a red switch next to the broken heater and having turned this on it solved the problem. The bathroom was tiny. I was on the 4th floor and due to ongoing work in the hotel I could go up to my room, but coming down it stopped at the 1st floor. Breakfast was on the lower ground floor so if you have mobility problems you will struggle. The charm of this hotel has to be its location, but I would be reticent to stay here again.

title: A good location hotel
text: Very friendly staff welcomed us for our stay. Avni and Ana were very helpful and kind. Ten mins walk to go to London Victoria station which is full of shops and locations to eat.Our room was clean with gd wifi and coffee facilities. Breakfast was very good.I would recommend this hotel to other clients cause we had a very comfortable and lovely stay. I would surely come again!

title: Good location
text: This was a decent hotel for the price we paid. It was in a good location...we could see the London eye from our room, it was just a few minutes from the Plimlico tube, and pretty close to other attractions. The hotel did provide breakfast which helped saved some money, however, their selection of breakfast items were slim pickings. The receptions were very helpful, the only negative thing I have to say is that the hotel rooms were tiny. Also, wifi is free at the hotel

title: Fantastic staff!
text: We stayed on the 8th March to attend an awards party. We decided to walk to the hotel from the station as it wasn't very far at all. Ana on reception was very welcoming (thank you for the nail polish remover!) Bedrooms were basic but clean, had everything we needed. Breakfast was lovely and there was plenty of it. The general manager - Anvi was very friendly and helpful too! We will definitely be back!

title: One night in London
text: I stayed at the Best Western Corona on the 15th Dec. The single room was small but clean and comfortable and the breakfast perfectly good. The hotel is central to where I wanted to be. The staff were cheerful and friendly and at £95.00 for the night very reasonable for Central London.

title: Good for the Price
text: My daughter and I stayed at the Best Western Corona from July 1 - 3. It was clean, friendly and in a great location. It was only 2 blocks from the Pimlico tube station, and taking the #24 bus was even easier to Buckingham Palace, Westminster Abby, the Tower of London, and to the West End theatre district. The room was quite small, but my daughter and I could both put our suitcases and dress at the same time. As other reviews stated, there was no cold water (really odd). When you called the desk, the staff would quickly bring a pitcher of cold water. The TV was quite old, but the picture was OK (no satellite)

title: no investments in hotel, just earning money with...
text: Breakfast worse than last time. Shower was very dirty. Room, especially the floor was not cleaned sufficiently and carpet was very tidy. At check in the recepionist did not find the reservation... At check out they charged breakfast extra although I changed the rate shortly after I booked the stay. Could not argue about that cause I did not print out confirmation of reservation because I thought at BW it is standard to be charged correctly. No help with problems with CC although preauthorisation was correct.

title: Disappointing
text: We stayed 3 nights over the August bank holiday weekend and booked as it was close as the Oval. The room was in need of a refurbishment and depressingly dark. Breakfast was limited as there are no cooking facilities, no boiled eggs or similar - straight forward cereal, ham and cheese, after day two very limiting.Breakfast staff more concerned if you joined tables together that clearing tables. Location is good for stations etc but there was a whole street of hotels providing better value - having stayed at many Best Western hotels this was the most over priced for facilities by far.

title: Small but friendly
text: Good points Clean, good view over london from the high floors at the back Friendly staff Baked beans at breakfast Did the job for a short stay Modern fittings and decor Had a good fan Short walk to Tube Disappointments Small room and bed Small shower No air con Got coffee when I asked for tea

title: Friendly London Hotel with Lovely Staff - you could be in Yorkshire
text: My colleagues Pippa Swanton and Andy Dowell recommend this hotel to anyone needing a home from home in London. I don't think they let Dead Goats stay but they knew Flippant and Epic Uncle Andy by name and always made them welcome. Some small rooms and some big ones. Too clean to take livestock in. Plenty of oats for breakfast and lots of choice for Ewemans to eat round about. Couldn't recommend it more highly unless they let me inside xx

title: Lovely Staff
text: Great location, clean and good value for money. You don't get much for your money in this area, however the hotel is a good standard and a safe bet. Most importantly great staff, polite, helpful and professional. I will stay there again,

title: Basic hotel, small rooms, clean and close to tube
text: The room I had was small - particularly the bathroom. shaving wasn't easy in the corner sink behind the door. Very high ceiling gave a sense of space. I found it quiet enough and it is close(ish) to Pimlico Tube and a reasonable walk to Victoria. Free WiFi. Otherwise average in every way. Which may be what you are looking for.

title: Overpriced for the size of rooms
text: I am sorry to say that the price I paid for one night stay at this hotel was seriously overpriced, for the size. The room was very crowded, I couldn't ever open the bathroom door. The room was overly warm, I couldn't turn off the heater. There was no breakfast service

title: Corona
text: Staff great very helpful close to Pimlico underground breakfast needs improving. Rooms not huge but perfectly adequate. Bed comfortable. Laundry used uses strong chemical cleaning products that permeate the linen, needs looking into.

title: Ear plugs required
text: This hotel has all the promises of being a good hotel however the upside is the location. The room could be comfortable but u couldn't swing a cat in there! Due to the age of the building it sounded like elephants above me and noise of traffic would be reduced if they got double glazing. Basically a poor nights sleep and then only a continental breakfast - rubbish. One good thing the staff were very friendly and helpful although could not provide ear plugs!

title: A mixed bag that I wouldn't recommend
text: This hotel is really a mixed bag. First, the pros. The location could not be better. Absolutely superb. It's about a block away from the Pimlico Tube station, which is a few short stops from everything you'll want to see in London. It's in a nice, safe, residential neighborhood w/ several pubs and convenience stores, plus an internet cafe. The service is good too. The front desk staff is nice and helpful. They gave us a map that gave us discounts to lots of stuff, which they didn't have to do. The rooms are clean and the bathrooms are fine. A breakfast buffet is included w/ limited hours every morning. The food is standard fare, nothing fancy, but decent and nothing to complain about. Now, for the cons. This room is small. I mean, tiny! It's small by european hotel standards. There was literally no room for the suitcase on the floor. The double bed took up the entire room. There's no closet, just an open armoir. The bathroom door opens up toward the bed instead of near the doorway like most hotels. In fact, you cannot open the bathroom door all the way, b/c it hits the side of the bed. It's that small. Secondly, the amenities are quite lacking. They provided shampoo, but no conditioner. The hair dryer was not located in the bathroom, so it was two days before I found it. And when I did locate it, I found it to be damaged. There was no refrigerator or safe. There is also no room service. The bed in our room was very uncomfortable. Neither of us slept well the entire four nights we were there, and my spouse actually awoke in pain most mornings. But the biggest negative to this hotel for me would have to be that the walls in the rooms are painted ORANGE!!! I don't know what the management was thinking when they did that! It is nearly impossible to sleep well in a brightly painted orange room. I literally couldn't sleep w/o Benadryl. Overall, I wouldn't recommend this hotel. there are some positives, but they are unfortuantely outweighed by the negatives. I do recommend that you find this hotel on a map, research the area, and then book a different hotel in the same neighborhood, because the location is spectacular!

title: Long Weekend in London
text: We came down to London for a trip on the Orient Express as well as the London Eye, a tour of the Houses of Parliament and to see the West End Show 'We will Rock You'. The hotel was only a short walk from Victoria Station where we caught the train. Reception was very friendly, efficient and competant. All rooms and areas of the hotel were very clean and in excellant decorative condition. We did not know that there was only a continental breakfast and not a full english breakfast until we arrived at the hotel. On two mornings there was a shortage of milk and they had to send out for it and on the first morning they ran out of orange juice. The hotel appeared to be full and very busy but we would definately use it again in particular du to its excellant position.

title: Glad the company paid!
text: I would never have chosen this place...but it's one of a few my company will allow people to stay in and was near where I needed to be for work...and that was its only redeeming feature I'm afraid. First it's in a bit of a dodgy area..I was propositioned as I walked back after my evening meal..before 9 pm! When I arrived to check in I was told the water was off for essential maintenance .I was a bit peeved but they said it would only be half an hour.....It was an hour and a half later before it came back on .As I had got caught in the rain on the way there by this time I was feeling v grimy. the rooms are small and painted the most hideous orange. No proper wardrobe or full length mirror.Essential things for the business traveller. The worst thing was the squeaky floorboards on every floor. this meant I could hear every step of the people above me. I cannot understand where they were walking to, given the fact that the rooms were so tiny, but nevertheless I heard them pacing around for a big part of the night.The corridors are very narrow too so as people were leaving the rooms opposite it sounded as if they were coming into mine! I didn't sample the breakfast and to be honest I couldn't wait to get away. thank God I didn't have to pay for it..The poor bloke checking out in front of me was stung for an extra £5 for the continental breakfast which meant he paid over £150 for one night.I know it's London etc etc. but there are far better places to stay at that price .

title: Warm and comfortable.
text: After a day out on the cold and suffering from a heavy cold, it was a pleasure to arrive here with a warming welcome and a very snug, warm room. The single bed was very comfortable and I got a good night's sleep as the room was to the rear of the hotel, so no external noise. Bathroom was quite small with a compact shower and small washbasin. Toiletries and towels supplied. The breakfast has improved since my last visit with more hot items on offer and a good continental selection. The hotel is in a good location for Victoria, with Pimlico Underground being a short walk away. The staff here are welcoming and friendly and with good value rates in winter this is a hotel worth returning to.

title: Truly excellent hotel
text: This hotel is perfectly located in the walking distance to many sightseeing places. The hotel staff is very helpful, friendly and highly professional. They made our stay unforgettable and pleasant. The Family Room size is enough for 3 adults, it is spotlessly clean and cosy, the hotel is renovated. Surely we will come back here again and can recommend this wonderful hotel as a real gem in the heart of the city.

title: My stay at the Corona
text: Stayed at this hotel whilst on a course for 4 days. Clean and tidy room, breakfast was continental adequate but nothing to shout home about. Lots of other hotels on the road but nothing much more than that with a pub down by Victoria station. The price was expensive for what you got, but having said that it is London.

title: Alright Hotel!
text: Stayed for a weekend in January. Bedroom layout badly designed. Couldn't see the TV from the beds! Breakfast was a little disapointing, not replenished when there was still guests coming for breakfast. A place to sleep and handy for tube and walking into town.

title: Good location value hotel
text: We booked this hotel last minute as we got Olympic tickets for the final saturday evening and wanted to stay in London to see the marathon on Sunday. We booked a double that could have a cot bed and were plesantly surprised to be put in a family room (double and a single) with room for the cot bed. There are plenty of reviews saying the rooms are on the small size, well we found it adequate. The reception staff were efficent and pleasant and we were in and out in no time. We didn't book breakfast but continental breakfast was included. The hotel is a 5-10min walk from Victoria station, alternatively Westminster is around the corner. The road was quite and there was no real noise in the hotel at all at night. For £135 I thought it was very good value.

title: Tiny tiny room
text: Hmmm, well all I was looking for was a cheap place close to Victoria station before an early morning flight from Gatwick. Price was £50 for the night which is cheap for London but outrageous for places like the USA. My room was very very small - more like a student room than a hotel. This is travelling at its most basic. However, location is pretty good for Victoria station which was a 10 min walk with suitcase. Main problem was that the hotel is on a noisy main road and there is little sound insulation. Similarly, I could hear my neighbours pretty intimately! Bathroom was also very small and basic. All in all - exceptionally basic but close to the station if all you want is a place to put your head.

title: Good base!
text: Stayed two nights in February. Room is basic and spotlessly clean. Good water pressure and hot water in shower. Convenient location, close to Pimlico tube and great little restaurants and places for breakfast and coffee. Staff is professional and helpful. If you need a place to stay that is safe, clean, and reasonably priced and you don't care about breakfast or other amenities, consider Best Western Corona.

title: ANOTHER PLEASANT BEST WESTERN HOTEL
text: We booked the only Family Room in this hotel as we needed twin beds & it was small but comfortable, however, over-priced for what you get. The staff were extremely pleasant & helpful and attentive to your every need which makes a big difference to any hotel stay. Breakfast is greatly over-priced at £12.95 but there are a few local cafes within walking distance. A point of concern is that when booking this hotel the price shown did NOT include the 20% VAT & I'm not sure if this was due to Best Western or OPODO, the site it was booked on. In any event, the final price was a shock & very misleading. The No.24 bus does NOT stop outside the hotel, as some reviewers have said, but is a few minutes walk on either side of the road. This is a great bonus when needing to get to Westminster, Victoria, etc. A big thank you to Reception Staff who made our stay very pleasant.

title: Very good price/quality hotel
text: My son and I spent there 5 days, on holiday. We've highly appreciated the reception staff, very friendly & helpful. The hotel is very well located, close to Victoria station and also nearby to bus-stops. The room & bathroom were clean (the bathroom a little small).

title: Great triple room
text: Spent a girls weekend at this centrally located hotel. Triple room was very spacious and very good value for money. Hotel very clean and pleasent, and staff helpful and friendly. Short walk to Houses of Parliament or Buckingham Palace. We will definately use this hotel again.

title: London Leisure Trip
text: Fully coresponds to three star hotel category. Good location (Victoria station is in 7 minutes walking distance), nice and welcoming staff, but room is very small. From windows comes cold. Special offers in web page are good.

title: Rude, unhelpful staff and the worst coffee and tea ever!
text: The selection at breakfast was extremely limited with no option for a full English breakfast. Apparently, fresh lemon for tea was not available - I quote "not at this hotel". I feel that the cost did not reflect the service and I will be very wary aout using a Best Western again.

title: Good Location
text: This was a conviently located clean hotel. However, the rooms are miniscule. You can roll out of bed into the bathroom. You have to go out to change your mind. Wifi was worthless. As I said the location was near Victoria Station and about 1 1/2 miles to Trafalgar square. Good bus service.

title: Clean, comfortable room in central London
text: A no frills stay in central London for business. The staff were polite and courteous. Stayed in a single room with small bathroom. Free Wi-Fi. Breakfast was a few warm items, plus the usual selection of cereals, toast, yogurts and fruits. Overall a pleasant stay.

title: Excellent location, friendly staff, nice room
text: I spent four nights here with my mother. We arrived before check-in time so our room wasn't ready, but we could leave our luggage at the hotel, which worked fine for us. When we got back in the evening, the check in process went smoothly. Our room was in the lower ground floor, close but not next to the breakfast room. The room was compact but very nice, safe, clean and quiet. The room had free wi-fi, which worked fine. There was also a coffee maker in the room, which was a nice touch. When traveling, I don't need a large room because I'm mostly just going to sleep there. The location of the hotel is excellent. Pimlico is a very nice area with plenty of restaurants. The Pimlico tube station is about five minutes away and the larger Victoria Station is only ten minutes away. It takes about 20-30 minutes to walk to Big Ben and Westminster Abbey. The breakfast was good. There were croissants, pastries, fruit, cereal, and eggs, beans, and bacon... The breakfast staff also asked if we would like some toast (white or brown), and whether we would prefer coffee or tea. On the day of our departure we had to leave very early, before breakfast time, but the staff was kind enough to bring a limited but very satisfying breakfast to our room. Overall, Best Western Corona is a nice, clean, safe hotel in a beautiful area with exceptionally friendly staff. I would definitely come back to this hotel.

title: Amazing hotel
text: Very nice hotel. We stayed here for a night it was lovely very friendly helpful staff. Comfortable beds very clean everything you need for a short stay in London. Pimlico underground 2 min walk away ideally situated for exploring London. Very reasonable price and lovely breakfast to start your day. We will be staying here again for sure. Highly recommended.

title: Good location
text: Upon arrival we knew we were early, the gentleman at reception was very friendly and we left our bags with no problem at all. Checked in later and we were directed to our room which was modern, comfortable and clean. All staff very pleasant and helpful. Only downside was housekeeping knocking on the door at 8.15am on a Saturday morning! Breakfast was okay, limited choice but suffice. The location is great within walking distance to an underground station.

title: Adequate for most purposes
text: Given that all one needs is a comfortable bed and hot shower the fact that I could touch opposite walls at the same time (which means I have very long arms or the room is exceptionally small) has little bearing. It is given 4 stars, a push but again clearly the rating doesn't include the square footage of the room or the size of the TV screen. Clean yes, helpfulness at reception, mixed but generally ok. Squeeky floorboards from the room above and considering their room was no bigger than mine there was an awful lot of walking about being done! Continental breakfast - no sleeping in, breakfast finishes at 10am sharp!! For a business traveller with an entourage of paperwork, laptop, files, there is precious little room to work, but the internet was free, one just had to pick up a password from reception every 24 hours, no biggie. Handy, a range of pubs to choose from with reasonably priced food and good beer (if you like British beer). Everything within walking distance, Victoria Stn handy too. Stay there again, probably if I had business in that part of town... on the other hand the Grosvenor on Buckingham Palace Rd looked appealing...

title: ok for budget hotel
text: Stayed here for 2 nights due to being on a course nearby. I had booked a single room, which turned out to be a triple with a double and single bed in it, so plenty of space - although would have been very cramped with 3 or even 2 people in the room. The room was ok, basic and small, with a strange musty smell! There were tea and coffee making facilities along with a portable TV and useless hairdrier. The bathroom was very small, but clean with a decent shower. This hotel is on a busy main road, normally this wouldn't be too much of a problem, however, the hotel does not have double glazing, therefore it is very noisy - all night! The breakfast consists of fruit juice, tea/cofffee, toast, cereal, a bit of cheese and ham and stale croissants and bread buns. The best thing about this hotel is it's location, which for the price probably can't be beaten. It is a 10 minute walk to Victoria and 5 minute walk to Pimlico with plenty of bars and restaurants nearby. In all, this is a basic/budget hotel in a great location - you get what you pay for. I've stayed in worse but also stayed in a lot better!

title: Oh dear same again
text: Our company continues to use Best Western to my dismay I am holed up for 3 nights in this place again 18 months ago I stayed here and it was exactly the same. Scolding hot water noisy rooms or should I say boxes and they charge £140 per night daylight robbery good bit is there is plenty of nice places to eat and drink to keep you away from the dreadful place

title: Good value for money
text: Great location The room is very clean, small but enough. the area is quiet and near the hotel there is Victoria station-central station for bus,train and tube. The staff is very polite and kind. Good value for money. Check in 24 hours.

title: Good for the price
text: A little far from the main sights but not bad if you can walk everywhere. It is right next to a station on the tube so if you are public transit savvy it's a good location - you get what you pay for. Biggest disappointment was the wi-fi, it didn't work in our room and they couldn't get it fixed for the duration of our stay (3 days) but really not the biggest deal... when I'm on vacation, wi-fi is not life or death.. we just had to walk to the lobby to use it which was inconvenient. For a budget hotel, not bad at all. I'd stay here again.

title: Small rooms and bad value for money, no air con
text: The hotel is well situated within easy walking distance of Pimlico tube station and is clean and well presented, and the staff friendly. Pimlico is a nice area and there are loads of restaurants with easy walking distance. We all had double rooms on the 3rd floor, and being there on business meant I had this to my self which was just as well as two people in there would have been crowded, for example the bathroom door opened on to one side of the bed so if there’d been anyone sleeping there they would have been hit by the door. The room was decorated nicely and there were ample supplies of tea, coffee and a good size TV. The bathroom stocked well with shower gels and fresh towels. However, there is no air con and only a desk fan for air circulation so in the recent heat wave, was I uncomfortable all night, fortunately being so high up you could leave the window open all day and night. I don’t know what was up with the floor boards but it sounded like a herd of elephants where moving about upstairs, my colleague’s also complained of the same thing. Breakfast was continental an ok selection, cereal, tinned fruit and yogurt in bowls, croissants, bun’s and Danish pastries and apples. The staff brought you toast and the tea and coffee which was barely warm at best was from a communal pot, no individual tea pots here. The first day we went down at 8:15am and didn’t have any problems with the availability of breakfast items. We went down at 8:45am on the second day and there was no fresh fruit ( there’d only been apples anyway) and they had run out of Danish parties and some cereals when we asked about this we were told that they didn’t restock so once it was gone!. On our third day we again went down at 8:15am expecting everything to be there and again no fresh fruit, no Danish pastries and a certain type of cereal were absent, considering they serve breakfast till 9.30am and at £100+ a night this is really not good enough. I’ve had better value in a Travelodge. The other issue we had was the day were leaving. Being on a training course meant we had to leave luggage on the day of check out to collect later, we were told to leave it in reception under the bay window but were not asked for room numbers or given any ticket so anyone could have walked in and just taken any case (not that I had any valuables in there). We were only there because of its proximity to the college. I’m pleased I wasn’t paying for this as I defiantly don’t think it was worth the money, when you consider you can get a larger room with air con in a Travelodge for less than £100 in West End of London

title: Very comfortable stay
text: A five-day stay in a quiet area of London. Corona hotel is close to Pimlico underground station and the fundamental bus route n.24. Hotel very clean, excellent and kind service, surprising view of Central London from the back side of the hotel. Very nice experience.

title: Friendly and helpful staff, plus centrally located
text: Stayed for 6 nights. Close to buses and trains (Victoria station coach tours 15 min walk away). Very nice Italian Restaurants and old style English restaurants within 5 min walk. For those that go on vacation, the hop-on-hop-off start their tours at the Victoria station. Shuttle from hotel to airport available for 15 pounds. Hotel has very small rooms, but you are not in central London, to stay inside a hotel anyway!! Hotel services are very good, and friendly. Quick laundry services same day return available. Unfortunately only cold breakfasts, but a good one is available near Victoria Coaches departures. Surroundings safe during night. No noise. My room had a view over the front street. Ps. A smallish shop with long after hour opening times 7min walk away.

title: Small room but served needs for night.
text: Had a small single room but big enough for 1. Staff were friendly. Breakfast was adequate without a massive choice but had everything I would normally eat. One issue if you can ask for a room facing the back as my room had a lot of traffic noise despite the window being shut. I guess the age of the building means that double glazing is not allowed. Handy for my meeting near Westminster.

title: Best place to stay in Mayfair
text: The staff is very accommodating and polite....one of the best serviced apartments I have stayed in....so centrally located that everything is at a stone throw distance....strongly recommend for those travelling for the first time to london as it will make your trip easier

title: Plenty of room, great price
text: Spent 9 nights at the Ascott Mayfair with mother and sister. Great apartment with great view. Very quiet neighborhood and residence. Felt very safe even walking the streets at night. Apartment had large kitchen/dining area with refrigerator, cooktop, oven/microwave and combo washer and dryer. Plenty of dishes, silverware and glasses. Washer and dryer hard to figure out and took hours to dry clothes, but was a really nice convenience. Spacious living area with sofabed, desk and 2 chairs, TV with plenty of channels. If you are traveling with children, remember that nothing is censored on the TV! Entryway had very large closet. Bedroom contained a KING size bed, large closet, dresser, 2 nightstands, safe and TV. As mentioned by others, the bed is firm, but I was so tired at night it really didn't matter. Sofa bed was acceptable. Marble bathroom had large tub/shower, towel warmer and plenty of space to move around and for storage. Water pressure and temperature were variable, but after the first shower you kind of figured out when the water was going to change temperatures so you could get out of the way. Apartment cleaned daily. Initially maid was kind of stingy with the towels, but after a small tip, we had more towels than we needed. The room was very clean. The hotel itself was very comfortable, clean and pretty. Breakfast was included which was good enough to get you going in the morning. There was a selection of cereals, fruit, yogurt, assorted breads and muffins, juice, tea, coffee and you could make a soft poached egg. Very interesting place to sit and visit with people from other parts of the world. No problem getting a table. Honor bar and snacks available in the lobby at night. High speed wireless connectivity was not available in the room, but readily available in the lobby areas or business center after obtaining an access code. There is an ethernet connection in the room, but I had no luck with it. My only complaint about the residence itself is that the front desk staff wasn't very friendly or overly helpful and really was not able to answer questions about where things were located in the area. Not a big deal. We had also asked for a car to pick us up at Heathrow. The residence arranged it and we were charged 90 pounds! We arranged for a car ourselves to take us to the airport for our flight home and it was 30 pounds. There were not many restaurants in the immediate area, but 2 food stores were within a couple of blocks. Short walk to the tube and easy walks to Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey, Trafalgar Square and Picadilly Circus. Ascott is also very close to Hyde Park and if you want a beautiful but lengthy walk, you can cross Hyde Park to Kensington Palace. The neighborhood itself was very upscale and very quiet. Cabs were readily accessible just by walking out the front door. Once you figure out how to get to Picadilly which is about a 10 minute walk, you can find anything you need or getting anywhere you need to go. I would definitely stay at the Ascott Mayfair again. It was much better than expected and fairly priced.

title: Just Misses
text: We stayed one week at this property. The location is terrific and the staff congenial. The rooms have mostly been updated, but continue to need attention (e.g. stained bathroom ceiling, stained carpet, etc.). The washer/dryer was difficult to use and the staff could not help figure it out. The bedroom was poorly configured and had a tiny TV that could not be viewed from bed. There was only one bedside table (so only one person could read in bed) & the bedroom was too small to accommodate a chair. The freezer door wouldn't close so our ice cream melted. All of these things prevent this property from being A1. Still, it is very well located, clean and has an friendly staff. If the price were right, I would stay again. With a bit of attention to detail, it could easily be a 5 star property.

title: Has gone downhill fast!
text: A year ago, I had a great experience at the Ascott. This year was anything but. The front desk staff were incompetent, at best, and I thought dismissed my concerns in part because I was a woman travelling alone. After seeing three rooms either at street level and/or full of cigarette smoke, I finally agreed to stay one night in the third, with the understanding that I would be moved to another room the next day. I was assured that this new room would have a dining table and be non-smoking. Neither was true. Basically, they lied. The hotel was full, so switching to yet another room was not possible (I had had it by then anyhow). The rugs were badly spotted, the duvet was well past its toss-by date, the shower sometimes worked and sometimes didn't, the kitchen was ill-equipped and some of the dishes not clean, and I was aghast to discover they charged for teabags and biscuits provided in the room--these routinely are complimentary in even the cheapest British hotel! The staff in the breakfast room appeared to be equally incompetent, claiming that the coffee/hot water machine was broken and would not work "for several days," but making no attempt to provide an alternative. Another member of the staff later fixed this "broken" machine in about 10 seconds. This has gone from a classy, clean, well-appointed and pleasant apartment hotel to a dump.

title: Lovely Place!
text: Our family of 4 (kids 13 and 11) thoroughly enjoyed our 8-day stay in the 1bedroom deluxe apartment. This hotel has so much charm--not a new, modern feel, but a historic, comfortable feel. The location is wonderful: it's a 1/2 mile walk to either the Green Park station or to Bond Street station. That allows you to access almost any tube line you need. I had read the reviews from the last 12 months, and was a little hesitant. But I would stay here again in a heartbeat. So glad we made the decision to stay here

title: Great Location
text: My husband, teenage son and I stayed in a 1 bedroom superior (corner room on the first floor). In general, we were happy with all aspects of this apartment and the service. The kitchen was well appointed (although small) and we made use of it nearly every evening (after two weeks on the road -- staying in at night was a welcome change). The TVs were a bit small and certainly not up to premium hotel standards but this is England after all and there in not much to watch anyway. I agree with others that the breakfast room is crowded but if you adjust your schedule so as not to arrive when everyone else does -- finding a table is relatively easy (i.e. don't eat at 9 am). The sofa bed was not up to the standards of many extended stay hotels -- our 16 year old son sunk to the support rails -- but we did not find the main bed to be hard or uncomfortable (as some others have noted). The bathtub/shower is very, very slick (had to put a towel down after I almost fell -- no mat provided) and about every two minutes a 10 second shot of cold water was 'provided.' The air conditioning in the living area worked quite well but the bedroom unit was putting out only slightly cooled air. We asked them to look at it but they said nothing could be done on the weekend and by the time Monday rolled around the weather had cooled a bit. You cannot beat the area -- our son was happy just walking around and looking at the very expensive cars parked on the street. The walk to the Green Park tube station was less than 10 minutes. Lastly, the front desk help was knowledgeable, friendly and willing to help. We accidently left our souvenirs from St. Andrews in a drawer under the TV in the lounge. I called less than 24 hours after we checked out and was told that the room had not yet been occupied but that there was nothing in the drawer. Three days and multiple phone calls later, the golf towel was found but the golf ball and ball markers were not with it. We were thankful for what they did find and just received our package in the mail. All in all, we would return to this property but would make sure the a/c worked in all rooms before we unpacked.

title: Well located and good for short stays
text: This apartment block is part of the Ascott group who also own Citadine apartments dotted around cities all over. We stayed here as a family group of 5 for an overnight stay in London for a 21st birthday weekend to use it as a base. These are serviced apartments in the heart of Mayfair. We had a 2 bedroom apartment which has lounge, small kitchen, and two large bedrooms with a large sofa bed in the lounge (so sleeps 6). The lounge was quite small, but the bedrooms, hall and bathrooms were large. One bedroom was ensuite (so 2 bathrooms in total). The outside of the building is unimpressive and showing its age a little. When you walk in the reception area is warm and welcoming. Optional continental breakfast is expensive at £15... But why would you eat in when there are so many places on your doorstep? Wifi is free for up to 4 devices, but they will give out additional codes. The staff are pleasent and helpful. The rooms have tea/coffee making which they will restock for you, and the kitchen had a washer dryer too for longer stays, a microwave and hobs (no oven). The rooms are traditional/contemporary (not modern not old), clean and cozy but are showing wear and tear, mainly on wood floors and wooden surfaces in bathrooms etc... Varnish peeling. It didn't put us off much, but there are better to be had in Mayfair if you want to impress and prepared to spend more... However if you need to sleep 5-6 there are not many other well located choices. Overall I'd say it need a little bit of talc as a building. If you become a free member of Ascott/Citadines on their website you automatically get between 10-15% off their direct rates. The apartment block is about 3 rows back from the main Piccadilly road in Mayfair, close to the Ritz, Hyde park, and Knightsbridge. It would also be convenient for Leicester Square or Covent Garden/Soho. Green Park tube is the nearest at a 8 minute walk and has good central routes. Parking: The apartment block is inside the congestion zone!... There is parking just around the corner at Audley Square which is about £39 per day and also inside the congestion zone. However if you park in the very clean and modern underground Qparks parking in Park Lane this is outside the congestion zone (just) and we got this for £32 for 24 hours from time of entry(which is better than pre booked time), and it is a 10 minute walk to the Ascott from there. Also if you signup to the Qparks newsletter on the website they often do discounts of up to 50% off for Mother's Day etc. Tip: We went to breakfast at the unique Wolsley restaurant on Piccadily 2 doors up from the Ritz... It is like going back in time and is impressive. If you want a special treat got there, forget Claridges and all those. Many stars eat at Wolsleys because not many tourists know about it. Prices are from about £14 for eggs Benedict or a cooked breakfast, so a little pricey but nice for a treat. By the time you add coffee/tea etc it would be £20 per head... But considering the apartment charges £15 for continental I know which I would rather do. Overall for short stays this apartment is good, but if you want to impress someone then there are better (for more money) Staff and cleanliness are good. location to Mayfair/Piccadily is excellent. Can't give it a 5 but it's a 3.5-4 stars really for short breaks of say up to 3 nights as it is starting to show its age in a competitive market. It's really all about location.

title: Safety box theft
text: This is my first review i have written about an apartment and hopefully it's my last.. Let me start by telling you how my money gotten stolen.. So i said no there is nothing missing. title: Perfect Home Away from Home
text: We just returned from a wonderful 5 night stay at the Ascott Mayfair July 1-6, 2006. This is a lovely full-serviced apartment hotel. I travelled with my husband and two young children, ages 2 and 4. We had booked a standard 2 bdrm apt but they upgraded us to the superior which was bigger and had an added pull out sofa. The apartment was beautifully decorated. It felt very homey and spacious. The kitchen had everything we needed included a washer/dryer which came in handy. I thought the beds were fine, unlike a previous reviewer. Our two bathrooms were also very nice. Because we booked with our citibank card, each child received a welcome teddy bear and we received a box of chocolates and a bottle of wine upon arrival. Also, there was a HUGE fruit basket waiting for us in our room. After 5 days, we hardly made a dent in it. The location could not be beat. It's in an upscale, quiet neighborhood but just an 8 min walk to Green Park Tube which is a very central line. Also, just 2 blocks from Hyde Park, 20 min walk to Kensington. Since we had 2 strollers, we walked more than we took the tube. This hotel is very conveniently located. The service of this hotel was impeccable. I thought the staff was very attentive and helpful. The breakfast buffet had a nice selection: fruits, breads, yogurt, cereal, juice, coffee, meat and cheese. Loved the coffee/cappucino machine. I wanted one in my home until the server told me it cost 7K! The only problem was that the size of the breakfast room was just not big enough. There were only about 6 tables and only 1 waitstaff to help clear the tables and refill the buffet. Every morning we had to wait about 10 min just to sit down. But don't let this small detail keep you away from this lovely hotel. This was not a deal breaker for us. We would definitely return to the Ascott Mayfair!

title: Much much much better than expected.
text: I wanted to give this hotel a 4 and a half star rating in this review, but since i can't do that on this website, i decided it was leaning more toward a 5 star rating. Postive Things: -The staff were excellent-- warm, friendly, and always cheery, i would like to give a big thank you to Marguerita and Franscesca. -3 minute walk away from some nice breakfast eateries. -More than anything, this hotel is really like a home away from home. Although we often stay at other hotel brands such as Ritz Carlton, Four Seasons, Hyatt, etc. we decided to stay here due the scandalous price of hotel rooms and suites in London and also the tiny size of the rooms even after paying such a high price. And i have to say that some, and only some, of these hotels are a bit too posh to the point of feeling uncomfortable, and the Ascott Mayfair really made us feel at home. -The blankets and quilt was amazing. -Taxis pass by the hotel often. -There is a church right around the corner. Negative Things: -The room, we stayed in a double bedroom apartment. We have a few complaints about the room. First of all, i don't see the point of having such a lovely thick blanket/quilt when the room itself only has a tiny and completely useless aircon. Secondly, there were just a few tiles missing in the floor. Thirdly, the TVs, which they have now changed to flat screens, are tiny, a bit too tiny. -Location, although this is in one of the most expensive areas of London, it is nearly a 7 minute walk to the nearest Tube station(Green Park Station)! And we had to take the Tube very very often because taxis in London are very expensive. -Although one of our rooms had a view of a lovely park, the other room had a view of a brick wall. N/A things: We didn't eat at the restaurant because for breakfast it was 24 Pounds for one person. Overall: Although the room was just a bit disappointing, the staff were great.

title: Good location but property run down
text: We stayed for 6 nights in early September this year. We were emailed prior to our departure from Australia asking for any special requests so we asked for a quiet room on a higher level. On arrival we were given a room on the ground floor, near the lift and when I say ground floor I mean street level with people walking past and the Council man who ate his morning tea on the brick wall outside our apartment every morning. It is lucky the street is quiet in general but after around 6am you do start to get traffic. Thank goodness for the double glazed windows. The apartment itself was meant to be a deluxe. It was run down and many things like the wands on the venetians simply did not work so we had to open the blinds slat by slat to let some light in. There was no electricity outlet in the bathroom for the hairdryer so I was doing my hair in the kitchen as it had bi-fold doors with a mirrored finish so that basically fixed that problem. The parquetry flooring had seen better days with bits actually loose or missing and not being able to turn off the light in the room foyer was annoying to say the least. I noticed in another review that someone mentioned a complimentary drinks machine. I haven't seen that yet. The staff were always pleasant and helpful. To be fair when told our room was on ground level we were offered another room in a day or so but moving rooms once I have arrived is a pet hate so we stuck it out for the duration of our stay. There was also a constant drip from the light above the bath for the first few days but just as we were about to complain it magically stopped. Also the tap over the hand basin wasn't installed properly so wriggled around all over the place. All in all it is not the worst place we have stayed but it certainly wasn't the best. The location is good with some quaint little pubs around for eating at night. If you are into flashy cars then you may like the location as well. There certainly was a king's ransom of super expensive cars parked in the street. A little joke between my husband and I was that we should get t-shirts printed "We stayed at the Ascott Mayfair and survived". Considering how much we were paying for this stay, we expected a hell of a lot more. The property is roughly the equivalent of a 2.5-3 star hotel.

title: Large apartment and well situated
text: We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We were a party of 4 adults and 2 children, had plenty of space and were well looked after. We were a short walk away from public transport, some great restaurants and some key London attractions. Breakfast was also very good and staff were attentive. Can thoroughly recommend.

title: Wonderful week.
text: We had a very enjoyable stay at the Ascott. Family holiday with two teenage sons. The two bedroom appartment was on the top floor with views over London. It was very spacious, clean and comfortable. The staff were friendly and courteous. Complimentary drinks machine a nice touch. Great location, easy walking distance to Green Park tube and Buckingham Palace. Shepherds Market very close for restaurants and pubs. Would definately stop again in the future.

title: Convenient, classy gem with great staff
text: My wife and I stayed at this hotel for four nights while touring London. We ate breakfast there each morning, The hotel is in a great part of town (Mayfair) which has some fine shopping , food, sight-seeing, and parks (even gambling if you are into that). It is also reasonably convenient to the Tube (either by foot or cab). It is not a large hotel by any means (part of its charm) but provides a comfortable experience with very good service. The lobby is small but opens into an enclosed courtyard (with garden) and attached breakfast room. The room, the one we had was a suite, was very comfortable with a small kitchenette and even a clothes washer/dryer. There was free internet. The small TV was attached to a DVD player which was handy to watch during downtimes. The HVAC system worked well. If possible, you may want to take a room on the top (seventh) floor. The view, breeze, and noise levels were better there (other family members were on lower floors). All in all we left feeling well taken care of and refreshed by our visit there.

title: Poorly run and overpriced
text: I am very surprised at the other positive reviews for this hotel as our experience was negative. Whilst the location is good, the public areas well presented and the buffet breakfast quite good, at £180 for a studio room this hotel was very poor value in September. This is not a hotel for the discerning business traveller. On arrival the check in was very slow (25 minutes) and disorganised

title: serenity in the City
text: I loved the experience at the Mayfair. I have stayed many times in the past and I am always taken with the accommodations, the sense of calm in the middle of London. The windows open, which is wonderful. At night and in the early morning one hears the birds in the green spaces around. The rooms are spacious and the staff is welcoming. Having a mini-kitchen is perfect so one can avoid extra expense by having breakfasts or evening snacks or even larger meals in. Truly, it is a great place to stay.

title: Quality of room disappointing - G04
text: Great location! Lobby nice and modern with a quaint outdoor seating area. The issue we had was with the room which badly needs to be updated - carpets old and worn looking. The curtain in the bedroom was dirty with black marks on it. Air conditioning in bedroom did not work properly as it did in the living area. The vents were situated under the curtains so I had to find books to prop up against the curtains so that the air would circulate within the room. If you didn't, the air was blowing up at the curtains causing them to blow outwards. Couldn't find any glasses or cutlery in the kitchen! Called housekeeping the next day, guy shows up and proceeds to go through the kitchen not finding any so he tells me that sometimes it's kept in the desk/drawer in living area!! Why? Makes no sense. He looked there and still no cutlery or glasses. He then proceeds to walk to the cabinet that the TV sits on and voila there is everything. That is the strangest place to put these things. I would never think to open those cupboards. There were 4 of us, yet only 2 sets of towels were available. As for trying to use the blowdryer, you couldn't in the bathroom and we were stumped as to where the outlet was. Finally, by the bedroom door, lower on the wall almost floor level was an outlet. On a whim, I plugged in the blowdryer and it worked. Again, who would have thought that and then, you didn't have a mirror to do your hair because the cord wasn't long enough!! For the money, was disappointed.

title: Worst apart-hotel evet
text: The staff at this apart- hotel simply do not respective their clients, I just checked out today, I asked last night for a black cap to take us to st-pancars station ،to my surprise they booked me a van without telling me either the price nor the fact that the transport they booked was not a taxi at all, I had to take it because of time shortage only to be surprised that it cost £50, while the taxi from hethrow to Ascot cost me only £70. The member of staff who did this was named, salim, I did complain to the manager as soon as I arrived to st-pancaras, unfortunately she was so rude. Also they lost my pyjama shirt that I sent to laundry, also their A/C does not cool at all

title: 4 star apartments
text: Location is the only plus for this property. Didn't find anything luxurious in the two bedroom apartment. It's quite basic and should be under the 4 star deluxe category . didn't have any problems during our 15 days stay here except there air conditioning doesn't work so they gave table fans ! That's not 5 star ! So at 30 degree .C with a table fan. You can imagine this 5 star !

title: Reasonable
text: Pros: Location, kitchen facilities, room sizes, clean-ish, free internet, privacy, quiet. Cons: Very hard beds, a little worn, poor aircon, no hotel switchboard If you insist on staying in Mayfair and you don’t mind foregoing full service luxuries: the hotel bar, doorman to hail a cab, in-room breakfast, messaging etc then the Ascott is a reasonable choice. Good value: some full service hotels in the area can offer similar prices (before the extras: such as internet, room service etc) but the Ascott rooms - even the smallest - are usually a tad larger. Having a kitchenette to make a cup of tea without calling room service, is a big plus. Bathrooms are small but work well, showers are fine with good pressure. The breakfast area is small and overcrowded, the breakfast itself is marginal (no cooked items i.e. scrambled eggs, soggy croissants etc). Meeting facilities minimal. A little out of the way and takes a while to get to know your way around the area. Best for non-business travel, longer stays without too many expectations.
