title: Luxury Apartment .. very well located.
text: Stayed here second time in a row in June 2015. We were in a two bedroom apartment. Very comfortable size by London standards. The building is very well maintained with a very helpful concierge. The location is superb in the heart of London. 5 minutes walk to Oxford street. An expensive and popular property so try and book well in advance. A little downside was that the property is air cooled and not air-conditioned so in peak summer it becomes a bit warm. However we were at higher floors both times so as long as we kept the windows open it was comfortable.

title: luxury apartment in a heart of London
text: stayed here in May with big families. Got an upgrade for one bedroom suite which is lovely. the bed was quite comfortable, the furniture is well maintained even though some of them looked quite old. there are some construction work undergoing, therefore the lift is not working and we have to use the service lift which was very uncomfortable. one of other guest that it has not been fixed since one month. hopefully it is completed right now. Location, in the heart of London. 10 minutes walking to tube station and bus station. quiet and posh area. didnt try the breakfast, because quite expensive compare to other's. i would recommend to stay here if you can get reasonable price!

title: Too bad really...but beds are important
text: Beautiful place, great location, good breakfasts, quiet area, fantastic bathrooms...have nothing bad to say except it has the HARDEST beds known to man. I actually hurt my elbow from leaning on it for too long, it's that hard. A slab of marble is softer.

title: Very nice apartment in a good area of the city
text: We booked a studio apartment for one night before a trip abroad. I hadnt realised that it was an apartment / studio at first, until I checked the booking for directions but the price was very good against other hotels at the time we were travelling. Although we were late checking in (nearly 11pm) we were dealt with quickly and professionally by the gentleman at reception and were soon on our way up to our room in the (albeit very small) lift. When we walked in I was surprised to find that we had actually been checked into a one bed apartment, which was a lovely surprise. We had a large entrance hall (easily big enough to store suitcases in if need be) with a good sized storage cupboard, a kitchenette (which we didnt use but was fully functional with plenty of cupboards, kitchen/microwave, kettle and toaster etc), lounge room with settee, writing desk, sideboard, TV and other electronics (DVD, satellite etc), and a large bedroom with en suite. The bed was a good size - a Queen I believe) - and comfortable. The bathroom was well equipped and provided dressing gowns and slippers as well. We had a really good night's sleep and wished we'd known (although there's of course no way we could have) that we would be having an actual apartment (as opposed to a studio) as we would have spent more time in it! The apartments are in a good location at Mayfair, surrounded by other residential buildings and are very quiet. Berkeley Square was a short walk away (two or three minutes, even with suitcases) straight down the road and Green Park station would be only another few minutes from there. We jumped in a cab from St Pancras to get there and the taxi fare (black cab) was around £15

title: comfortable place
text: comfortable place, the recieption staff are helpfull and friendly the house keeping is good, the only problom was the main elevator not working ..the location is great ..we stayed in 2 bedroom appartments and the showers are very small as per london standered

title: A comfortable stay amidst a luxurious milieu
text: We have been staying at the Ascott during our London vacations since a few years and are very happy with the spacious rooms, general cleanliness, toiletries etc. This year we had the opportunity to stay in three different sized apartments due to changes in our travel schedules and our midway visit to Sicily. Turning off the light in the hallway is certainly a problem as mentioned in one of your reviews. Another issue was that there was no cooling facility in the apartments. It was very hot during nights and when we tried to turn on the cooling it did not work. The reception informed us that they only had heating facilities not air conditioning. They promptly provided us with table fans but we had to leave our windows open[which opened just a few inches for supposed security reasons]. Besides that, we had a comfortable stay as always in Mayfair, which is quieter and posher and close to Central London. Overall the apartment block especially the elevators, hallways and most of the apartments needs refurbishing since it looked jaded.

title: Good location, furnishings a bit dated
text: Obviously these apartments are in Mayfair, so they are expensive. You are paying for the location. It was nice to have an apartment, which gives you a bit more space. We had a two bedroom apartment. The L'Occitane toiletries in the bathroom were a very nice touch. Our main bathroom was small but clean and everything operated efficiently. There is a shower within the bath tub. In the second bedroom, there was a very small shower only, which did not have great hot water coming through. It is roughly a 7 minute walk to Green Park Tube, or a minute or two longer to Bond Street tube/Oxford Street. We walked to our Theatre in Picadilly in 15 minutes. The furnishings and TVs appear a bit dated. The king size bed in our bedroom was extremely comfortable but the air conditioning unit appeared to struggle to cope. We stayed here in September and the room was quite warm, so I wouldn't like to see how the air conditioning dealt with summer. I was not able to utilise the free internet service to check my flight times because it crashed everytime I tried to get into the Singapore Airlines site. It was extremely slow and I gave up using it. The female staff member who greeted us on arrival was friendly, as was Alex and the other male staff members. My husband experienced an unfriendly attitude from a female staff member. Whilst things feel a bit dated, I felt quite comfortable here.

title: In room safe broken open!!
text: Imagine your plight when you keep all your cash and valuables in the in-room safe of the hotel, and it literally is ripped apart. Who could do such a thing when my room is on the 3rd floor of the apartment, and the entry points have a receptionist who has to buzz in and out every visitor?? The most impossible aspect is the sheer negligence of responsibility by the management and entire staff of the hotel, who when we informed of this incident( we were out for 2 hours in the evening) told us to call the cops ourselves as they had nothing to do with it. No insurance for in room safe? Beware.

title: Not worth the price! Terribly Disappointing!
text: We are a family of 2 adults and 3 children. We had planned to stay at the Athenaeum luxury service apartments, but due to a lack of availability we had to use an agent knowledgeable about "comparable" accomodations to find an alternative place to stay. We ended up at the Ascott Mayfair, London. Price tag per night was 387 pounds (about $650) per night for the 2 bedroom apartment we rented. We were assured that it was at the same standard as our initial choice. The size of the apartment and its rooms were disappointingly tiny. With the king size bed, there was no room left on the window side of the bed since the bed was up against the heater. Had to climb onto the bed from the foot of the bed. The so-called kitchen did not have an oven or a dishwasher. There was a 12 inch television in one of the rooms (who puts a 12 inch in ANY hotel room), and the other room ("Master bedroom') had what looked like a 15 inch or so TV. The strings on the blinds did not work, and so we could not raise and lower the blinds without drama. The slats on some of the blinds could not be closed with the rotating rod intended for that, because it was broken. A slat was missing from one of the window blinds so you could not keep the daylight out. One night, the hot water stopped running and was not fixed until the next morning. The shower in one of the bedrooms was the ancient type where you have to HOLD the shower head in your hand and point it at various parts of your body where you wish the water to go. The shower stall in the other room was so narrow that you had to step out of it into the cold (also small) bathroom to dry yourself. Some of the knobs on the bathroom sinks had the labels missing, so that we were looking at disgusting looking grout or glue that previously held the label in place. We had to change rooms one night because the power outlets were not working and we could not recharge our electronics or use our computer. The furniture is old, and unimpressive. The interior decor was saddening. Extremely poor lighting in the rooms and living room, may be to force guests to use less electricity. The brightest light in the apartment was the hallway light. The only advantage of this place was the location within walking distance to many shopping places, and to many restaurants. For the price per night, this place is extremely poor value for any traveler from the United States. An equivalent place in the U.S. would rent for somewhere in the $90 to $175 per night range depending on the time of the year.

title: Love the Ascott
text: great hotel, loved the apartment we stayed at very clean and spacious the best investment made on this trip. they have a good sauna room and the place is great, service is really good, staff are very helpful and mannered. breakfast there is superb! if you can pre pay your breakfast fees with your room fees do so because it will be worth it for 12 pounds for breakfast you have all you can eat and great quality as well! will come back again! and thanks for the previous posters to help us find a wonderful hotel in the middle of london couldnt have done it without YOU GUYS!

title: Comfortable accomodation in the great location
text: We were really delighted to find this very comfortable aparthotel in the heart of central London. First of all it was very good deal in terms of price. Second it was great comfortable accomodation for the family. And third the location is really perfect with easy access to all central London attractions. We really do hope to return there.

title: Comfortable in London Mayfair
text: Lovely helpful staff, pleasant reception area with bowls of red apples and an honesty bar. Booked 1 bedroom apartment - for up to 4 people. 1bedroom and a bed settee in sitting room. Funtional kitchenette - well equipped. Dining area with beautiful orchid on table.Large comfortable bed,lovely towels and waffle robe. Continental buffet breakfast plus can boil eggs.Situated round the corner from the Dorchester Hotel. Only criticism is that the bathroom while adequate, is in my opinion, due for a refurbishment. Shower difficult to control.

title: Comfortable apartments to stay in London
text: These apartments are decent in size for a short stay in London . Very close to Oxford and Bond Street . Great part is that although very close to major attractions the area is quite peaceful through out the day . Lots of upscale restaurants nearby like nobu . The reception and concierge were always friendly and helpful . Housekeeping was good . Some people might say that the room are compact but don't get confused by these reports . These are absolutely comfortable apartments to stay in . Will recommend to everyone

title: Ideal Location For Our Visit
text: We have just had a two day break in London and chose these apartments. We booked a one bed apartment, but on arrival we were one bed short. After some negotiation we were upgraded to a two bed apartment, but we were told we were "lucky" they had one free. This was their mistake not ours, so I don

title: Perfect location for London attractions
text: The hotel is situated within walking distance 2 mins of the American Consulate also 2 mins of Oxford Street and 2 mins from secure underground parking. The service is excellent and the breakfast was very reasonable, my only criticism would be the bathroom is a little out dated and could do with a make over. There is no restaurant at the hotel but there are many close by, I would recommend this hotel over and over.

title: Don't bother as the high price charged doesn't come close to what you would want or expect
text: Although a fantastic location in one of the most beautiful areas of London, this hotel fell so far short of expectations that it wasn't funny. At almost $1000 US per night we were charged a full day extra to check in early as our flight arrived in the morning after a long haul trip from Australia. We arrived at close to 11am and was frustrated that it took almost an hour to check in and that as we hadn't arrived the night before, (they HAD been informed of this), our room wasn't ready for us. Once settled into our room, (with no assurance with luggage etc), we found that the suite, (although initially attractive), was very poorly finished. Of the almost endless list of things wrong with it the most annoying was 1/ washer/dryer didn't work, 2/fridge didn't work, 3/ heating didn't work, 4/ door handle to my daughter room was broken thus locking her in, 5/ taps in bathroom were broken 6/ microwave didnt work, 6/ tv was faulty 7/ safe didnt work etc etc. Of course we complained and were met with complete apathy from the reception staff. In the end, under sufferance, they said that they'd get someone to fix the problem. After returning from a day out, nothing had been fixed and in fact the reception staff had no idea if it had been even looked at. She just said.."you go up and tell me if it hasn't!" Later we were told that they wouldn't be able to get anything seen to til the next day. We requested that they at least see to getting our clothes washed which they did very reluctantly and although we gave them to them at 7pm they delivered, (tossed a bag of unfolded clothes at us), at 12:55am!!! The next day nothing was fixed again and we had to push them to put us in another suite...this was almost as bad. Under circumstances would I ever recommend this place to anyone!!!

title: Hotel for the winters
text: We stayed at the Ascot in mid November 2014. We pre-paid our stay at the ascot which I advise against as it was available for a similar price when we got there. Reading reviews increased our scepticism, however we were proved wrong by the homely ambience. We stayed for 10 days and it was a pleasant experience. We were with family in the two bedroom deluxe room and it was of good value. The nearby (5 minute walk) supermarkets were helpful. The WiFi was fast and the kitchen amenities were sufficient. The AC did not work and the lights were far too few in the rooms. There were no plug points except in the bathroom and there wasn't really a grand lobby. Also I wish they serviced the room on Sundays. All in all a good experience and worth trying again.

title: Best Kept Secret in London
text: This is by far the best kept secret in London. We stayed for a month at this amazing apartment-style hotel in Mayfair London and cried when we had to leave. The staff is lovely, the hotel is relaxing and the location can not be better. Our suite was well appointed with everything you would ever need ... we could live in this place! Give it a try, we found that the rates were very good, worth every penny!

title: Comfort in the heart of the West end
text: A comfortable hotel with helpful staff. We liked its location as it was away from the major traffic routes and yet within easy walking distance of public transport. It was a fine base for the museums, theatre, the parks and shopping.

title: A home in London
text: A property that you may choose to stay with family. We stayed there as a family with our 5 years old twins. Comparing the price that you pay for and the service you get, I am not sure that's a jewel. 10 minutes to the closest metro station which makes it very difficult to see around with kids, unless you are a taxi user. The rooms were OK, but really old,I would not choose to stay there again with the family (and alone) would rather rent a place much cheaper and convenient via airbnb.

title: Central location beautiful apartment
text: Stayed for 1 night in an executive apartment in the October half term. Took 5 of us comfortably. Clean, and roomy, 2 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and all kitchen amenities, and very comfortable beds. Lots of wardrobes, and drawer space, much better than your average hotel. Everything you would need. Also very warm, but unfortunately it was warm outside also! With windows open, comfortable, and surprisingly not a lot of noise for Central London. The location is the best part, within walking, not strolling, distance of everything, so no tubes or taxis needed. Shoppers dream! Wish we could have stayed longer.. Understated and discreet, definitely use again!

title: Great Find
text: I booked this through Secret Escapes, thinking the ability to have a "picnic" around our theatre trip, rather than rushing a meal out would be a good idea. We bought our picnic at Euston and checked in early evening. We were told we had been upgraded from a standard to an executive apartment. A nice little hallway into the apartment kept corridor noise at bay, a well equipped bathroom to the left, bedroom straight ahead and lounge to the right, leading through to the dining and kitchen areas. We had everything we could have needed for our stay from robes and slippers, l'occitane toiletries to washing up liquid and an ice bucket! Our stay included wine and chocolates - which we didn't expect much from, but they were both very nice - thank you. After eating, we walked to the the theatre (Queens for Les Mis) and back after. The area is very safe and quiet - unlike theatre land. A wonderful sleep in a comfortable bed, in a very quiet area. I didn't expect much from the continental breakfast included, but was really impressed. The breakfast terrace is a pleasant room they they have included everything you could imagine for a continental breakfast (toast, pastries, muffins,meats, cheeses,fruit, yogurt, juices, tea, coffee), plus they will boil eggs to order and have a make your own fresh waffles machine. I think my husband had it all and all very good indeed. We left our case with the concierge and went off to explore - collecting it later. Lovely space and location and I would recommend it to others.

title: Shabby and expensive
text: We had to transfer to the Ascott because of a muckup with our accommodation. The hotel was rated as 5 star and I was very disappointed with it. The rooms were shabby and the air conditioning didn't work which was hopeless in 30 degree heat. For the amount that we paid I would have expected a true 5 star hotel.

title: Mayfair hotel London
text: What a great hotel in a great location for our visit to Buckingham Palace. We had two gorgeous rooms, My friend stayed in a Queen suite room, everything she could of wanted. I had a King size suite with my son who is disabled and uses a wheelchair, access to the bathroom was a little too tight and not really suitable for a wheelchair user. The breakfast was just perfect and the staff throughout the hotel were very helpful and professional. Access for the wheelchair in the breakfast room was good as their was plenty of room, and a good plus was that the wheelchair could go under the table, this way my son was not a mile from his plate! :) We would all definitely stay here again :)

title: Good property for family holiday.
text: We had the one bedroom which was a comfortable size for 2 adults and 2 kids under 12. We had a newly renovated room and we were pretty happy with it. Great part of town to stay in and good location (although if you are planning to use the tube its a bit of a walk ~ 15 mins to Green Park).

title: Fantastic stay!
text: Extremely friendly, helpful, accommodating staff. The apartment we stayed in is well furnished and maintained. We love the coffee from the lounge. Breakfast was good, not a wide range but of good quality. Although the nearest tube station isn't that near but the walk to the nearest tube station (around 10-15 mins) is a very pleasant walk. The bed is a bit small though and we agree with Marianna15 that the hot and cold water in the bathroom is very hard to adjust. Overall experience

title: cheated by their cheap!
text: We were fooled into staying at this premise by the reputation of the Ascott group, located in Mayfair and managed under the name of Ascott Group I would expect the real cozy but luxury accommodation but it tunred out that the picture in the website is far more alluring than the truth. The room is old, breakfast is lousy and the towels they provide in the room is the worst quality must be made from pure syntatic cause it won't abosrb any water from you (if I pay to stay in 2 stars hotel that will be understandable), but the worst part yet to come is - we stay in the double room but they provide only 1 bathrobe and 1 slipper when requested for 1 more set I was told that it will be additional charge! And when requested for extra blanket becuase it was cold..was told again that it will be another addiotional charge. I felt I was cheated and Ascott Mayfair has no respect for their loyal customers. It will not be a repeat experience for me.

title: Comfortable stay
text: Spent the second week of July here with my wife. The apartment was comfortable and roomy. The kichenette was adequately equipped. The only drawback was the kitchen faucet leaked when turned on. The apartments are located very well in the heart of Mayfair. A 10 min walk got you to Oxford Street and 15 mins to Leicester Square. Will definitely consider staying here in the future.

title: Wonderful Service
text: Our room was on the 7th floor - a two bedroom, two bath. We traveled with our three teenage grandchildren. The staff was wonderful. Any request made was fulfilled. The room was quite comfortable if not a bit dated and needing to be refreshed. No complaints on the beds they were comfortable. The location is great and in a quiet area. The weather was very nice and warmer than normal. The air conditioning is not turned on until summer so they gave us a fan. Worked just fine. Our only complaint was the instructions on the washer/dryer were very difficult to understand.

title: excellent stay at Ascott Mayfair
text: My husband and I stayed at the Ascott Mayfair for one night in Feb 2005. We managed to get a special deal (£120), and it was incredible value - we had a small apartment with a sitting room, kitchen, bedroom and bathroom, elegantly decorated, in a brilliant part of town, 2 televisions, a DVD and everything you could want. A good buffet breakfast and friendly staff as well. I'd definitely stay there again.

title: Much better than Hotels
text: We, as a couple with a son, stayed at two bedroom superior for two nights. Our reservation was made for one-bedroom but they kindly upgraded on the arrival. The suite has a spacious living room and fully equiped kitchen (even with a laundry machine). High speed internet which you can use in the living is free of charge. The room rate was GBP233 per night including tax. I cannot imagine we can stay in such a spacious suite at the price level in the very expensive city, especially in Mayfair area which is walking distance from Bond St., Piccadilly or Oxford Circus. Highly recommended.

title: Nice but a little thought would help!
text: Nice place booked 2 bed apartment for 6 people to be given 2 apartments that linked so a bit weird. Having said that there was plenty of room and it was nice. They didn't give us enough towels though and also didn't give us access to the connecting door so if it shut we would have been locked out. After going to reception and explaining this a few times they sorted these issues out. They did give free bubbly for inconvenience though!

title: In need of attention
text: Before I start this review, this is the fourth time I have stayed at this property and the staff were all polite and did their utmost to help. However the place is falling apart. Simple things that the hotel management should be on top of are just not happening. These are the things I can remember we're wrong and this is supposed to be a five star property. Heating too high, thermostat broken, even in middle of feb place was like a sauna. Shower not working. Both plugs in bathroom sinks not working, beside lamps not working, floor in kitchen falling apart, lift broken, both exercise bikes in gym broken, step machine broken steam room alarm would not go off, blinding broken in one room, could not close them. We complained and were offered another apartment but we had waited an hour for the heating to be sorted and were late for our Sons 18th birthday dinner, so we decided to stay put on the basis that everything would be fixed that evening, which it was except for the plugs in the bathrooms and the blind which stayed shut all weekend. All these are minor things but when added up make a big problem and all should be checked. Additionally the whole place just looks like it needs refurbishing. Lastly there was nowhere to sit in either rooms, so my wife and daughter could not do their hair and make up without standing up and the location of the plugs is bizarre. This is a £350 a night hotel and is in a great location, but the senior hotel management of this chain have let this property go to the dogs.

title: Great location
text: We had hired a 2 bedroom executive apartment at the Ascott Mayfair which is very conveniently located in central London with key shopping areas of Piccadilly, Regent Street and Oxford Street within easy walking distance. The rooms are tastefully appointed but require refurbishment and the gymnasium needs to be totally revamped. Staff could be more attentive as well.

title: Luxurious, Well equipped, Amazing location
text: Stayed at the Ascott Mayfair for the first time.. and its definitely not going to be my last! Superb location.. 2 minutes walk to Hyde Park, Oxford Street and Picadilly / Green Park all within easy walking distance. Good housekeepng, pleasant front desk and great wi-fi connectivity all made our stay even more comfortable. Elegantly furnished and very well equipeed apartment make this one of the nicest apartments to stay in Central London.

title: Reasonable accommodation
text: Perfectly functional accommodation in a good location. Reasonable size. Not great price wise. Service depends on who's on duty- really friendly guy at night or an easily confused lady by day ( not unpleasant but frowns at every request!)

title: Lovely place to stay in London
text: Stayed here for Marathon weekend. All the family rooms in the decent hotels were well over £400 and managed to get this much cheaper (although watch the VAT which they charge for separately - cheeky blighters). This is perfect, the room was massive, two huge bedrooms and a separate living area and kitchenette. This has a real home from home feel about it, and given you never eat in a London hotel anyway, the lack of restaurants is not a problem. And the honesty bar is a nice touch. Only reason it didn't get an excellent was that the room was a little hot and the member of staff was a little sniffy about me using the gym shower facilities after a) agreeing this upfront and b) having run in the marathon! Final niggle was adding the Vat on at the end - need transparency on pricing please. Nevertheless would still recommend highly - great place and brilliant location for getting around London.

title: Not worth the price for me
text: For the price I paid, I don't think I got the quality I was expecting. I paid £165 per night for a studio and stayed for 4 nights. The hotel is supposed to advertise free high-speed internet connection (wired) and also a wi-fi (wireless) connection. However, there was no wireless signal in my room on the 4th floor. The the wired internet in my room did not work. I made a complain but the wanted me to be in the room to fix it. I was here for work, I did not have time to sit around in the room during normal business hours. I ended up coming down to the lobby to use their really slow wireless connection. - For one morning, Wednesday, the shower failed to produce hot water. - The hotel controls heat/AC centrally, and has no ability to adjust the temprature if the temparature outside changes. For e.g if today it is 9°C, they will call a technician to change the thermostat centrally to start the heater. Say, in two days the teparature rises to 18°C, the heater keeps running, and you end up sweating in your room. Then they recommend you open the windows, which I did, and had to cope with the street noise from passing traffic. The place is about 10 min walk from nearest Tube station Green Park or Bond street. I prefer to walk to Bond street in my case. The area is expensive, so I will not complain about smaller room size. Staff is polite but not much use and were unable to fix my problems mentioned above. The shower gel ran out but they did not bother to replace it. I called it to their attention. Good hotels make sure they replenish that. I did not like the towel quality either. The shower runs nice and hot, but difficult to operate. Room was clean. Had this place cost me £78, I would say it was good hotel. But for the price, you need to get quality which was missing. My previous stay at £199 per night at Langham was very pleasant. That place is more professional and well managed. But they do charge £20 extra for the internet. So thats extra £50 per day, I saved here, which I guess makes it all worth it. I would try Club Quarters at St. Paul next time. Its only £120. For that price, I can live with slightly poor quality, if at all.

title: Great Apartment-Hotel, Great Location, Very Good Service
text: In the past I have stayed at The Ascott on business (a number of times), but this time I stayed with my wife and two small children (5 & 1 years old). We were joined by my mother-in-law. We took a 1BR apartment which proved more than adequate for the five of us. The staff at The Ascott are ever helpful. It is only a few minutes walk to Picadilly and the Tube and there is a largish Tesco (?) at Berkeley Square. One thing worth noting is that the sofa-bed in the lounge is superb. Most hotel sofa beds seem to collapse if you look at them, but this one was of very high quality. In a similar situation, I would definitely go back there again.

title: good location value for money
text: what can i stay about the ascott,, everything you expect when you stay in a service apartment you get it. good location 5 min in a cab your in oxford street, piccadilly, 10 min soho tottenham court victoria and harrods... nice staffs ready to help when needed ,, building is quite old will with referblishment,, good continental breakfast and self service bar...

title: 2 night city break
text: Apart-hotel brilliantly located in Mayfair, just over 5 minutes walk Green Park tube station. Small lounge, small bedroom, kitchenette & ensuite, nicely furnished but just slightly tired within the suite. Continental breakfast was far more than that and all staff were very friendly and helpful. We booked on an offer and it was amazing value. Recommended

title: Overall superb hotel
text: I was very pleased to spend my 6th year anniversary at the Ascott. Set in the heart of Mayfair, this hotel provides the best customer service making you feel like a VIP. Upon arrival I was a little disappointed with the one bedroom executive, the decor was out-dated, lamp shades were out of place, toggle on the blinds in the bathroom was broken. I made a small complaint and was shown another one bedroom executive which surprised me with it's modern furnishings and large bed. Ahmed was an extremely helpful staff member and always went the extra mile. Overall great hotel!

title: Excellent
text: Excellent apart hotel, rooms are very comfortable and the people are very nice and helpful we felt at home. The zone is very good only a bit far from underground stations but great for moving in taxis

title: Wonderful quiet property just off the beaten trail
text: We stayed at the Ascott Mayfair during the London Olympics and were very satisfied with the property. It is a classic old style property with a modest front entrance and kitchenette suites available. It was perfect for our family of five to stay in and be together without being on top of each other. The location is very good and just off the beaten trail so on a quiet street and about a 10 minute walk to Green Park Tube station. The staff was very polite and courteous. We didn't use the hotel amenities so can't comment on food, workout room, etc. Would certainly stay there again.

title: Great place to stay
text: Stayed here in January 2014. The standard 1 bedroom is quite comfortable. I would have liked the exterior of the building to be more fancy considering the amount you pay here per night. We did face a problem with getting hot water and had to repeatedly call and ask them to get it sorted but the staff was quite prompt so that's a relief. The breakfast selection i felt was quite limited so we did not opt for the 15 quid breakfast package at all during our stay. We woke up late and mostly did Brunches at some local cafes around the place.

title: Avarage but pricy
text: It is located in one of the closed end, one way, narrow streets, difficult to describe it to the taxi driver. The building is not very charming from outside, looks like an old army barrack, brick work walls and small windows, typical old social house building. The lobby however is warmed by the welcoming East European staff, check in was easy but explanations of the building were a little. Starting from the dark, low ceiling corridors look very depressing and pressurising, going up with a slow motion noisy elevator, feared to be stuck in the elevator any minute. One bedroom suit was adequately furnished and layout, however the bedroom was small compared to the spacious bathroom. It is quite but old, and dimly lit, one can have the feeling of energy deficiency of Europe is around the corner, even if you have to pay for it. It may sound as if suitable for families with children but it is expensive and may be more appropriate for professional couples and business-like travellers. Its location is very convenient to all kinds of transportations and the city centre attractions, some of them are in walking distances.

title: Great location, but too expensive - a bit old!
text: Very nice location. Nice but old rooms. We had 2 bedrooms, 2 baths, living room and a small kitchen. The kitchen had everything necessary, but no knife. When we asked fior a knife tu cut bread we were told that there was no knife because of security. So we went out and bought a knife.... How can you operate in a kitchen without a knife?

title: Very Nice Stay
text: We had a very nice staying at Ascot. The staff is very polite and helpful and really helped us in everything we needed. We have a baby and I request a bathtub for him, what was promptly arranged, I also needed a doctor and they found right away. The hotel is in a great location, you can walk to Piccadilius Circus and there are lots of restaurants close by. The room was big, two bedrooms and a small kitchen, what is great when you travel with kids. I will never forget how warm and cozy the hotel was when we arrived from the outside tours. The only thing I did not like: there was no food in the fridge, only water, and some coffee and tea bags, we all arrived tired from a long flight and I was expecting to have something to eat available for the kids, as it is a hotel residence, my husband had to go right away and buy something for the kids. I recommend the hotel and will be staying there again for sure:)

title: A VERY disappointing experience.
text: Arriving at The Ascott Mayfair, although in a great location, it was disappointing to find no air conditioning, with hot stuffy rooms, despite a 5 star rating. Even one of our toilets was Malfunctioning.The staff were inexperienced and had a poor command of English . They offered no solutions, but when pushed sent a single old-fashioned fan. Despite its expensive cost it failed to deliver on all levels. I would avoid this hotel.

title: High price shame about the experience.
text: The apartments are in an expensive location, in Mayfair and so have a high price. We stayed in a studio apartment, which was fine. The washing machine and fridge were yellow from old age, I believe they were meant to be white. If you show pray no one turn on a cold tap, this seems to cut the supply of cold water to the shower - the water became VERY HOT. This would definitely burn anyone not fast enough to get out of the spray, very dangerous. The room was warm so I examined the dial on the wall for air-con, turned it to minus and we got hot air being blown into the room, thank god the windows opened. The blinds they have in the windows do not have the stick like device so you can change the way they face, we had a building opposite and so wanted the slates facing up so you could not see in, I had to adjust each slat by hand it was just bizarre. We telephoned the front desk, we asked them to order us a taxi. We gave an hours notice for the taxi, got down stairs and no taxi. We were told they have been trying to get one - rubbish. I work just around the corner from this place, you phone a black cab and they arrive maybe 10 mins early or late. We walked outside in the rain and hailed a cab. On returning to the apartment, outside the building is a sign that states press the button. The sign looks like a button, I pressed it and of course nothing happened. Yes, it's my mistake, but the guy on reception just sat there staring at me. I gestured I could not get in, he just yelled press the button. After staring at the area that is mat metal I notice what looked like a metal stud and pressed that, service what service? We were asked if we wanted breakfast at £15 each, I asked three times what type of breakfast it was only to be told "yes - between 7am - 11am" ????? A continental breakfast for £15, no thank you. I would rather stay at a 4 or 5 Star hotel next time, for £200 - £300 a night. Upon checking in they wanted to photo copy our driving licence, the room was already paid for and they had an imprint of our credit card, I felt more like a criminal than a guest.

title: Great Location and spacious
text: Only a short walk to the tube (direct from Heathrow) made this is a good location to start with and as time passed this proved to be a good location for most things. Walking distance to Oxford Street, Hyde Park etc. We stayed in a one bedroom apartment which was well kept though some of the furniture was aged. It was spacious though as it was an apartment you should expect this. Several supermarkets/pubs and plenty of restaurants all within walking distance. Service was not over the top though by and large covered our needs.

title: Lots of room but old
text: The Ascott is a charming apartment hotel in the heart of the May Fair. We had loads of room and we could get to every where easily. BUT the air broke down two of the first nights we were there and London was having its hottest summer ever. Not too good to come back to a sweat box after slogging around castle all day. My older sons loved having their own rooms and Shepards market is close by for meals and there is easy access to Green Park, Picadilly Circus and Kensington.

title: Pure Luxury
text: The apartments are like your own little house, beautifully furnished and great views of Mayfair from the windows, the location is perfect, close to everything, I love it, it is a beautiful place to stay and the receptionist and concierge are very friendly, the only thing is the WI-FI connection is quite poor but overall a fantastic place to stay x

title: Great Location
text: Having booked this hotel via Lastminute the day before arrival I was concerned to read the reports on Tripadvisor. I had wanted somewhere central for my partner's business meeting and my trip to the Royal Academy. The location is fantastic, 5 mins from Picadilly and the area of Shepherd Market is a hidden gem of little streets with pavement cafes and charming shops. As you walk around look up at the rooflines to see the many different types of architecture that make up this area. It is a perfectly safe area too to walk around in the early evening. The room was very comfortable, with Molton Brown toiletries, clean and quiet and looking over the rooftops from the top floor was a Mary Poppins experience, you really wouldn't know you were in central London. The staff at the front desk were charming and helpful so I would thoroughly recommend this hotel and plan to return. I truly do not know why it has has such bad reviews.

title: Great Staff
text: The rooms are a bit tired, and the plumbing could definitely use some updating, but the staff is extremely accommodating. Vijay was very generous in giving us tips for getting around town, as well as being a most genial bartender. The woman at the front desk (sorry, can’t think of her name) who gave me advice on where to find a toy taxi for my mom was also great. And a special shout-out to the housekeeping staff, who cheerfully and efficiently responded to plumbing trouble. Very professional.

title: Small and dated but great location
text: Stayed here for two nights recently. Thought the location was fantastic right in the middle of mayfair and close to the underground and some lively pubs. But the rooms were small, dusty and not the nicest decor i have ever seen. The breakfast was very poor also. For the price we paid for the hotel i wont be staying here again.

title: DO NOT STAY HERE
text: How this hotel can say it is a 4 star is a disgrace - suggest it doesn't deserve 1 star. We decided to try a boutique hotel for a change & this place gives boutique hotels a bad name. Dirty, v v v tired, cold water - if we hadn't needed to be in London we wld have gone straight home. The management / owners should be disgusted with themselves. The one time we didn't check TripAdvisor and look what happens. WARNING TO EVERYONE -DON'T STAY HERE ITS APPALLING AND SHOULD BE STRIPPED OF ITS STARS!!!!!

title: 2nd Visit - its got a little better...
text: Visited Park Lane Mews Hotel again, was sceptical as my last visit was awful. This time we took a double room and found it a little better but just not worth the money.. its still shabby and run down and is in need of some TLC. Not bad for a quick over night stop.. no more. Service is good, value is not.

title: Bit better than just average
text: Booking in was quick & efficient very nice lady on the desk also very pleasant staff in the Bar and restaurant in the morning, the breakfast was surprisingly very good as my expectations were not high when I saw the Buffet Warmers but I have to say it was very good. The rooms are quite small but the bed was very comfortable and bathroom again small but quality shower. The hotel needs a bit of TLC the doors to the rooms are quite poor tatty in fact they need a painter in to varnish the Doors and paint the corridors. As I said it's above average but "not very" good shame you can't give 3.5 stars although the staff rate 5 stars for me.

title: Not as expected
text: I recently stayed here with my husband for a night in London - I normally check trip adviser comments before I stay in a hotel or resort etc. But I didn't on this occasion as my husband had booked it. .. I wished I had. The location was fantastic however and the outside looked smart enough. The reception staff were welcoming and polite and we took the offer of paying extra for the breakfast which was around £11 ish. This included cereal, fruits and cooked breakfast. Sadly the hotel itself was in need of decoration and updating. Most paintwork edges and doors in the corridors have paint chipped from them. The bedroom itself was nothing special and had a plug in heater and a double sized bed. Glad I was only staying 1 night.

title: Dirty room and bedding. Tiny room with no place to put a suitcase without tripping over it.
text: We chose this room for its location and that's all the good I can say about it. It was cramped and nowhere to put our smallish suitcases without stepping over them. The air conditioning was very noisy and did not work. It was so hot in the room that we got very little sleep for the three nights we were there. When I told the girl at the front she said "well you did ask for twin beds" as if that was relevant. While the girls were friendly, they spoke very little English so were hard to understand. They also did not know enough about London to be able to answer the usual questions about getting around. The wallpaper was peeling off the walls and the trim-work was scratched and scuffed. It did not look anything like the pictures on the website. Nothing like the "boutique" hotel they advertise. We would not come beck there again!

title: 4 Stars - Are you serious?
text: This hotel has a quaint lobby, but that is it. The room had no A/c and we were told it had been a few days since it worked.... and..."in London we are not required to have air conditioning" was the comment from the gentleman at the front desk. There was a fan in our room, but it was so filthy, we could not turn it on. The window wouldn't stay open, so we had a rolled up towel in it to keep it up. The rug was also quite dirty and worn. It was so bad, we slept in our clothes for the one night we were there. Faded and scuffed wood in the halls. To top it all off, wi-fi was advertised, but it was only available in the lobby if it worked at all. Very bad.

title: Good place for the right price
text: Booked on line for a 3 night deal (just less then 300 quid for a double), the hotel turned into a pleasant surprise. It's a great location, close to great parks, Piccadilly, Mayfair and walking distance to many of London's attractions if you have a bit of energy. We walked...and loved it. It's not the most glamorous or up-to-date destination but we found the staff helpful and cheery, we liked the lobby area with its lounge and library and our rooms were okay. Comfortable bed and adequate facilities. Just around the back is a lovely area for dining - lots of options for breakfast, lunch and dinner, from cafes to pubs to restaurants.

title: Not what we expected
text: I guess 198 pounds per night for a hotel in London must be cheap because this hotel is tired, needs some TLC and needs to be more accurately described on the website. Our room was two single beds, end to end with no room either side of the beds for luggage. I paced it out. 12 Feet by 10 feet in the living area, small hall way and bathroom that was two outstretched arms wide and not much longer. No safe in the room, beds as hard as concrete. All in all no great but I must stress that the tariff might equate to what we got. On the positive side, the staff were friendly and the breakfast very good. Would I stay there again, no. Disappointing.

title: Helpful staff, great location
text: We found everything was good, from first to last. Staff were very efficient and helpful. Room decor was fine, and really clean. Just what we wanted for a night away, close enough to walk to restaurants, theatre, and Hyde Park.

title: Tired shabby hotel in ideal location
text: Selected the hotel location as my Husband needed to get to Buckingham Palace to receive a business award from The Queen, the location was ideal for that and for walking round the City. We rejected the first room allocated as the TV didn't work and we refused to stand under the disgusting shower head. The second room was marginally better with working air conditioning but had tired shabby decor and a bathroom which could be considered dangerous as due to its tiny size, one had to practically climb over the toilet to exit the bath and shower. The room overlooked the rear of the hotel and as we had to have the window open as the air conditioning was too noisy to sleep through, we were subjected to crying babies, noise and pounding music most of the night. The only redeeming factor was the pleasant breakfast. One other factor that concerned us was the insistance on removing the entire cost of the stay from our credit card on arrival, on querying this, we were informed that this was the system employed by Travelodge..? This obviously made it very difficult to leave early.

title: Don't waste you money it's really grotty
text: We spent £200 on this double room. It is tiny, all the decor is chipped, doors are missing from the furniture. There is no aircon so there is a free standing unit. It's really not nice so suggest staying anywhere else. The service is awful with big queues checking in and only one person serving. Has the feel of a hotel that has no cash flow to invest.

title: old English charm on a small scale..
text: The location of this hotel is fantastic

title: Expensive for what it is!
text: I have stayed at the Park Lane Mews a couple of times for business and dont think i will be heading back. For where the hotel is based it seems cheap. But i would say there is a good reason for the price and in fact it is very expensive for what you are getting if you take away the location. From the outside it looks like a lovely hotel and has been well kept, however the rooms are a different story. Small and very hot and stuffy rooms with see through net curtains that mean you have to close the main curtains if you wish to get changed to ensure that everyone on the street cannot see you - making the rooms even more hot and stuffy. TVs and plug sockets that don't work and air conditioning that if it does work will deafen you or may only blow out hot air. If your lucky you may get an extra air conditioning unit taking up plenty of the little floor space the room has with a hose going out of the window which will also ensure you cannot hear your TV (if it works and if you manage to find a channel that doesn't skip and jump around). At over £180 a night minimum i wouldn't recommend the hotel to others - although i have to say the reception staff were very helpful.

title: Great location, but in serious need of refreshing
text: Ideal spot for West End, quiet mews location but only seconds from Park Lane/Piccadilly. Looks quaint, but on any kind of close inspection, the decor is knackered! Rooms are small, but it's about half the price of anywhere else within half a mile. The bathroom is very compact but functional. Unfortunately, several other things were not functional - the bathroom extractor and heating/cooling system in particular. Glad it was a mild spring day, not mid summer. Cheap option if all you want is a room for the night near the Hilton/Dorchester/Intercontinental, I wouldn't go back for pleasure, or with family, or want to stay for more than a night though.

title: London visit before Northern lights Finland
text: We stayed at this hotel due to the location and value. The location was the only positive thing about this property. They were very rude and condescending at check in. The hotel is not only dated but it’s not clean. All it would take is a fresh coat of paint or stain. It’s obvious that they are not proud of their hotel and could care less if its a positive experience. All they want to do is connect you with a tour that they get a kick back. Breakfast is very expensive and you’re better to go to the cafe down the street! Great little restaurants close to this location. The bartender also didn’t know how to make a martini or a margarita.

title: Dump
text: The friendly front desk staff do not make up for the pitiful condition of this hapless property.

title: Amazing
text: location is amazing for the prize of the hotel, the room were clean but the hotel need a bit of refurbishment. The breakfast was amazing for the prize we paid. The receptionist Nasir was very presentable and helpful.

title: Location good for Park Lane and Mayfair - rooms OK
text: This hotel is a good choice if you want a reasonable cost stopover right on Park Lane or need to be in Mayfair. It is in the street directly behind the Park Lane Hilton, and you can access Shepherds Market directly from it. It isn't grand but service is reasonably good. The room we had was small (as was the bed). The bathroom was tiny. Not much wardrobe space so I wouldn't recommend the room we had for more than a night or two. Decor in the room was generally a little shabby (the carpets were a bit worn and stained here and there) but it was clean and the shower worked well. But don't let that all put you off - clean, comfortable and low cost accommodation in the centre of town is hard to come by - that's why I have given it an overall 'very good'. We didn't eat at the hotel (it was room only), there are some great places to eat out the back of the hotel in Shepherds Market. Free wifi was an unexpected bonus.

title: Good......... But it's not Carling
text: Stayed there from Sunday over to Monday, the location is second to none. A 5 minute walk away from Green Park tube and then you're on your way. Stayed here to go and see The Jersey Boys and we were only 3 stops away on the tube. The room was slightly on the small side but clean and my wife liked the shabby chic decor and the curtains (although the shabby chic is becoming just shabby now, a return is underway I think and it's probably overdue). We we were staying in room 311 at the rear and it looks out along Shepherd Street. You can see one of the mews houses which belongs to Stirling Moss (the one with the balcony that has classic racing cars etched on the balcony glass), and the pub further down the road which is decorated so Christmassy it could be something out of Dickens, is where Wendy Richards out of EastEnders used to live above. The bed was comfy and the television large, wardrobes and cupboards provide plenty of storage space. But (and this is a big but), the shower didn't work properly and probably not safe - it was either lava setting on number 7 or no water at all. The dial on the shower to reduce the temperature of the water simply turned the water off - I think it was too hot to use because we simply could not use it, it was unsafe because it could have burned us. I reported it to reception and admittedly they did offer to send someone up, but it was quite clearly a fault so I'm not sure what could have been done and by then we'd had to have a cobbled together a bath (we had to hurry to get down for breakfast), which was not ideal for me because I have epilepsy and I don't have baths. Breakfast was good, the cooked breakfast was very good, very tasty - but......... there were three food containers heated from underneath by Liquid Chafing Fuel. Well at least two of the three were, one of the containers only had one tin underneath and that had burned down. Which meant my cooked breakfast was hot except the sausages and bacon which were just warm. The guy who checked underneath the food containers, must've checked on the underneath of these food containers two or three times, but made no effort or attempt to replace the warmers under the sausages and bacon. And what's more, when breakfast had ended at 10am when people were still coming down, he blew the flames out of the Liquid Chaffing Fuel, and I could clearly see clouds of spray or mist coming up from the fuel and settling on the food - he'd left all the lids open and the fuel settled on the food. And people came afterwards and helped themselves from this food with the fuel on - eww! Despite the fault with the shower and the sloppy attitude towards the food, I would have felt churlish to give this hotel 3 stars because the room was comfortable, it was excellent value for money being on special offer of the week on another website, and its location is excellent - the back street really is so quiet and it's so close to the tube. I would have still given this hotel 4 stars if it was not for the following - I took my wife to London to see The Jersey Boys as a special surprise as it had been her birthday the day before on the Saturday - it was a total surprise for her. When we left the hotel we didn't realise that my wife had left a pink satin coat hanger that she'd had her party dress on from the Saturday. She is absolutely gutted because she'd had this coat hanger for 40 years and while it might sound silly, it does have a certain sentimental value to her - it wouldn't mean much to anyone else, but it means a lot to her. I have just called the hotel to explain this and I spoke to someone who gave me the impression he could not care less if he tried, and that is hugely disappointing. Although I received thanks when I pointed out the fault with the shower, I can't help but feel another hotel would have offered to knock something off the bill, not at all what I was looking for admittedly but the gesture would have been welcome. And the lack of interest in taking something seriously as I explained the coat hanger means something to my wife is disappointing, I wasn't expecting him to break into tears at the news or anything, but I was expecting a response better than just beung told to call back in the morning to see if it had been handed in to lost property - seriously?! So all in all a very very mixed review of this hotel indeed and I cannot in all good conscience give more than 3 stars under the circumstances.

title: Haven of Peace !
text: Ideally situated just off Hyde and Green Park the Mews is an ideal place to stay with easy access by foot to many places including Buckingham Palace a mere 10 mins at most . The staff are very customer focused , the rooms are comfortable and all is quiet . I hate to finish on a low note but ...........our only disappointment was breakfast with the staff not particularly interested - the food offering was bland , tasteless with scrambled eggs inedible + if you want smoked salmon its an extra £10.00 .......no way !

title: EXCEPTIONAL VALUE FOR A REALLY LOVELY HOTEL
text: Just returned from this delightful hotel. In the heart of Mayfair with very helpful staff, lovely full English breakfast, clean rooms, and so close to the West End. Definitely will stay there again and recommend it 100% we both really enjoyed ourselves. Only one fault, the pillows were not too good, very thin and hard wouldn't stop me going again.

title: I couldn't imagine that bad experience for £300 !!!
text: Extremely old. Everything around (carpet, furniture, bed, etc.) is amortised. Last revamp seem to happen 30 years ago. Toilet not working. Can hear voices from neighbour rooms. Wouldn't pay even £50 for this room.

title: 4-Star my ****
text: Planned a special 2 day break to celebrate a 50th birthday - obviously read the wrong review website! Arrived at the door and my immediate expectations were far beyond the reality which awaited. Staff on reception very pleasant, location turned out to be better than expected - then we went to the room. Dated, drab, the decor needed returning to the wall and the quiet room requested was immediately adjoining the lift shaft. The twin room requested was a double, the heater broken, Satellite TV not worth having, mould around the bath seals. Second morning the simple act of taking a shower proved too much - no hot water! This followed a night of a Spanish couple deciding to keep the entire floor awake for two hours whilst they indulged in a 'domestic' which everyone could hear, though not neccesarily understand, and which the nioght staff could not manage to calm. Breakfast

title: GUTTED, UPSET AND ANNOYED
text: I booked two rooms on the 7th June 2015, as it is my best friends 40 birthday. Since booking these two rooms in this hotel, my husband has been told that he has a rare form of cancer, I phoned the hotel to explain this on Tuesday 25th August to say that we would not be able to go as my husbands blood count is 0.5 which means he has no immune and he can not be round to many people as he could catch any infections going and could end up straight in hospital. This was suppose to be an amazing weekend for the 4 of us, We feel bad enough not being there for my best friends birthday, without this hotel being so rude to me on the phone THIS HOTEL DOES NOT CARE AT ALL, WILL NOT GIVE US A REFUND OR MOVE OUR DATE TILL NEXT YEAR. ITS NOT OUR FAULT MY HUSBAND GOT CANCER, BUT IT WOULD OF BEEN A BIT EASIER FOR US TO THINK THAT THIS HOTEL MAY OF MOVED OUR DATE TILL NEXT YEAR OR OFFERED US A REFUND. TWO VERY UNHAPPY PEOPLE.

title: All show, little substance.
text: Looks nice from outside, bur very worn and dated interior. Carpets, cupboards, decor and paintwork all need an upgrade. We'll positioned for Mayfair restaurants and nightlife. Rooms very small but are clean.

title: Great Location
text: I had not booked a hotel ahead when we came in early July this year. It was the only place we could find in central London, and very expensive but beds were at a premium and we were glad to find somewhere. Its a fabulous situation and good transport from Park Lane. It was quiet and there is a nice restaurant area which has HUGE potential if they get it going with good food. The room was small and decor is "tired" but the very nice Manager Soda, I hope I spelled this right, assured us its going to be done up. I also thought perhaps coffee and a croissant could have been thrown in. However there was tea coffee and a biscuit in our bedroom. We would come again, and prices would be better if I had not left it till the 24th hour.

title: Dated rooms
text: We spent one night here on the 07/03/2017 the main reception and dining room are both very nice but the rooms are very dated and not all that clean it could do with a good clean. On a plus side the breakfast was excellent.Also the noise in the night from something being moved about in the adjoining room to which we think was some kind of store room was terrible.

title: Good value for Park Lane Hotel
text: Good value for Park Lane Hotel - I was upgraded to the Mayfair suite which was very nice with all the facilities expected. Bar prices were outrageous out of hours £16 for a Budweiser and a Vodka/dc! Didn't have time for breakfast but it looked basic. Very close to Hyde park tube for connections into town All in all, don't have big expectations and you will not be dissappointed

title: Good experience
text: A good breakfast , but very old rooms .. we can’t open the windows. A good experience with one of the bar staff santi a good man attentive and helpful. Hotel installation very old , but it is a good price for this area.

title: A great find
text: This hotel was booked on our behalf so we arrived feeling a little unsettled after reading some of the reviews. We shouldn't have worried. Check in was efficient with pleasant, helpful staff and our request for a quiet room was granted with no problem. The room was of a reasonable size - it's a mews property after all and although the decor was a little tired it was beautifully clean with a super king bed which was very comfortable with fabulously clean linen. The bathroom although on the small side had a bath with a powerful shower over and we weren't lacking in any of the essentials. Breakfast was great with all the normal items you'd expect. I don't know how much others have paid but we paid £130 a night including breakfast - what more do you want for this price it's a lovely small hotel in Mayfair not a faceless chain hotel. We will certainly return. Excuse the rating for fitness centre - there isn't one so the question doesn't apply - I couldn't cancel the rating.

title: Charming and inexpensive in a great location
text: Sometimes you just need a nice room near to where you need to be, and you'd prefer not to pay over the top for it. That' why I'm glad I found the Park Lane Mews Hotel. It's right in Mayfair, nestled in behind some of the great hotels of London, where you'd be paying twice as much. This trip, I just needed a place to lay my head for the night- I arrived after eight, scooted off to a function, and left at seven the next morning. This hotel is just the place for this type of trip. The entry is welcoming, and the staff are friendly and helpful. The rooms are on the small side, but are well appointed, clean and comfortable. The bathroom I had was one of the smallest i've seen, but it was clean and tidy, and for the time I was there this was not a problem. I didn't have time to try the breakfast, but I will next time, for I am certain to stay here again.

title: what a rip-off!
text: Dont bother with this hotel. It is not 4-star. It has some of the rudest staff on reception, i have ever come across and it's sub-standard in just about every way you can think of. From shabby decor, cheap loo paper, no mini-bar in the bedroom, coat hangers falling to bits in your hand, lights not working, i could go on and on! Thank goodness the show we saw that night, was fabulous and the restaurant we went to beforehand, as otherwise the trip we had been looking forward to ,would have been a huge let-down. I do not recommend this hotel in any shape or form, dont go there !

title: Never 4 Star!
text: We stayed here last night, in room 211. Sorry, but this was no more than 2 Star standard. Why were we charged £294 for a tiny room with a hard bed, broken socket, very tired, tatty decor, stained carpet & a bathroom door hanging off it's hinges?(You had to lift it right up for it to close!) I have never written a complaint before, I really am very easy to please, but this was insulting. I believe that some of the rooms have been refurbished and these are the photo's that are used for publicity. Surely people will then assume that the whole hotel looks as lovely as this? We realise now that we perhaps,should have dealt with this at the hotel but had a very late night and left early without breakfast, to get to work. I would love to have written a positive review (Hotel looks lovely from outside and the position is fab) but I have to speak as I find! Please have honest pricing for the different standards of the rooms,it is the only fair way.

title: Good location. Tiny rooms. Even tinier bathrooms.
text: This is a wannabe boutique hotel in the center of London. The location is very good (very close to to Green Park tube station). The structure seems old, but overall clean and tidy. It's funny, if you look closely everything appears like falling apart, but if you don't, everything seems fine. There is no minibar in the rooms and the range of temperature varies a lot according to the room. There is no heating system (there is one but it doesn't seem to work and it looks like a leftover from the past) but there are radiators. We were 7 in 7 rooms, and some of us complained that it was cold, and some others that it was too warm. Included breakfast was very basic but decent. A couple of time our key cards would simply stop working and we would have to go back to the lobby. I would recommend this place for a 1/2 days stay, but not for longer.

title: Not up to par
text: My wife, 2yr old boy and I recently stayed here for what should have been 4 nights... I had noticed the hotel on a previous trip to London where I stayed at the nearby Hotel (also sub par, but better than this place). Long story short

title: Tired beyond belief!
text: This hotel has seen zero investment in recent years and it shows. Suffice to say almost any alternative at a comparable price will be better. It simply trades on its excellent location. Had to insist on changing rooms as the allocated one stank of smoke.

title: Capitalises on it's location
text: Stayed at this hotel a handful of times over the last couple of years. It is in a great location but on closer inspection is a little tired and shabby. Most recent one night visit found me on the top floor in the tiniest but functional bedroom with a single bed (!) for the princely sum of £254 - breakfast extra. Breakfast buffet does the job, but the restaurant is small and you have to time it correctly or you may well have to wait for a table. It is an easy walk into the bars, clubs, and restaurants of Mayfair. Very close to Green Park tube for wider excursions. Quite simply, you are paying for the location. Having said that, I will probably return.

title: Great location but needs some work
text: The hotel is very nicely located in mayfair - very close to walk to attractions. The hotel is needing some TLC and refurb especially to the bedroom and corridors. The room we stayed in (standard double) was small and basic and for the price is not good value - however is anything good value in Mayfair ?. The service was excellent at the reception and at breakfast with really helpful and chatty staff. Overall the hotel dispointed us - we felt we deserved more for £210 night.

title: a good experience
text: Just a one night stay in a single room, but nevertheless a very pleasant experience. True, it's tired-looking in places and a refurb is overdue, but I've had worse in London for twice the price. It's exceptionally good value in a great location. I'll be using it again.

title: NOT fancy
text: park lane mews? park lane EWWWW. i would have rather stayed almost anywhere else, including a park bench. staff is incompetent and rude

title: A wonderful break in London
text: I stayed at the Park Lane Mews Hotel for 3 days. The price for a king deluxe room was a bargain. The room was deeply clean and the bed very comfy. The position of the hotel is amazing. All the London landmarks are walking distance and there are plenty of nice restaurants in the area. Breakfast was ok, staff pleasant. Special mention to Jade who assisted us all over the stay.

title: Musing on the Mews
text: I reviewed the Mews in Oct. 2009 and noted that despite its obvious shortcomings, I would return because of its location. I returned for a 5 night stay in May 2011. Its location and room rate are still outstanding. The small hotel is near many restaurants in Shepherds Lane. The choice of restaurants in the lane has increased with the stand out being Sofra, the Meditteranean restaurant where we had an exceptional evening meal of mezzes. The staff at the Mews still lack the finesse and training of better hotels. Their personalities range from that of Basil in Fawlty Towers to remarkably efficient as in the case of the young woman who remembered my name so she could forward a phone call to me while I was in the lobby. The rooms are still small and need major refurbishing. We could not close our windows and the noise during the night from hotel workers changing shifts resulted in some sleepless nights (and we weren't in Seattle!). As women travelers, the location meant we could walk to and from the theater safely despite the late hour. Dine comfortably in good nearby restaurants and walk easily to Fortnum & Masons on Piccadilly, shop at Marks & Spencer's convenience store, have breakfast at Pret a Manger or even walk to Harrrod's or the Victoria and Albert Museum. The rooms are clean and comfortable enough to overlook the shortcomings of the staff which I now consider part of the ambiance of the Mews.

title: OK, Definately not 4* Standard, would look elsewhere next time
text: Booked through lastminute.com as a "TopSecret 4* Mayfair Hotel". Was very excited and researched a few 4* in the area and was hopefull for one i had seen. Was advertised as a 4* Boutique hotel in Mayfair. Arrived at Park Lane Mews Hotel and was a little dissapointed with the outside, then more so inside. The Check in was smooth enough. The room was pretty small. The Window did not close/lock properly. The Tv reception was not clear, All 5 channels were not fully received, The TV services did not work at all. The Water pressure was VERY VERY POOR, the extractor in the bathroom was a hole in the wall next to the shower head with a pipe...very bad and dusty! The positives were: Nice (Small) bed, Nice Sheets & 2 pillows!!

title: Got a great price for a very good London hotel
text: My wife and I stayed at Park Lane Mews Hotel in October. We stayed overnight on a Sunday as we needed an early start on the Monday morning. We booked this hotel through Lastminute.com and only paid £76 which was an absolute bargain considering a Travel Inn is £85 in London. The hotel was one of their 'Top Secret' room only hotels but was easy to work out considering the normal B&B description was only a couple of hotels down on the list (and even this was only about £90 including English breakfast). The hotel is about one minutes walk from the Hilton and so very close to Hyde Park and a not over distant walk to the museums or Oxford Street. There are excellent bus links and the tube isn't too far away at Hyde Park Corner or a hike (with luggage) from Marble Arch. The rooms were very good for London hotels, we have stayed in a number over the years and this was a good size room with a 42 inch plasma screen on the wall! The bathroom was adequate although not luxurious and the hotel facilities looked okay although we really only saw the lobby and our room. We were offered the opportunity to have breakfast when we checked in (at a supplement of course) but they didn't start serving until quite late (08:30??) so we didn't have time even if we did want it. I thought this was quite unusual to start serving so late, so check this out when booking if you need an early start. Overall I would thoroughly recommend this hotel if you can get anywhere near as good a deal as we did. This was an above average hotel (especially for London) and well located for a quick stop over or a short break in London.

title: Better location than expected
text: We booked this via Expedia and got a lower rate - approx £50off the published rate but this was for room-only. The hotel was behind the Hilton in Park Lane so nice and central for shopping and theatres - approx £8 by taxi. The Hard Rock Cafe is about 3 minutes walk. Because the hotel is shielded by the Hilton and Dorchester, it is a fairly quiet location and you can hardly hear the Park Lane traffic. We stayed in a room overlooking the mews but at 4am the bins were emptied and for 20 minutes it was chaos. Ask for a room at the back of the hotel if you dont want to be woken up. The room-service breakfast for 1 is enough for 2 easily, and costs £22. Breakfast down stairs is eaten at a low table in reception - not good enough for a 4 star hotel in my opinion. The room was small as all London hotels are, but not a shoe-box. and there was plenty of storage space. The bathroom had Moulton Brown toiletries but no robes and the bath was too short for my 6 foot husband..
