title: Its the end of my shift
text: On arrival one member of staff said she did not do reception, which meant unfortunately we had to interrupt the other person behind the desk. He gladly informed us that it was the end of his day and that his day was going to get better. After handing us a key, but not informing us where our room was or if we wanted help with our luggage we made our way to the room. Having got a good rate via booking.com and only staying for one night we didn't expect to get the best room they had but the pictures on the website do not look anything like the room we were given. Our room was dated, mouldy, noisy from the lift and tiny. We asked if we could change rooms but the receptionist could not authorize this, but made no attempt to find a colleague who could (as he was going home soon !!!). From various websites at least 6 other rooms were free at the time of asking. I would not stay here again or recommend it to anyone. Not even water available in the room. Thank goodness we didn't pay full room rate !!!

title: Unimpressive hotel, good location
text: The pros: very nice location, bathroom clearly recently refurbished. The cons: The staff seemed entirely uninterested in serving the guests, and were generally miserable

title: 5 star boutique - I don't think so
text: Tired washed out hotel. Location superb but sadly hotel needs redone top to bottom. Room smelled strange. Plug in heater as radiator obviously not working. Bath plug would not seal so a bath was a quick affair. Huge stain in middle of carpet. Curtains dingy and woodwork bashed. Hall doors outside rooms looked as if a stampede had passed by. Staff friendly ish but really felt we were to be suspected rather than welcomed. Won't be back.

title: Good but dated
text: This was a good hotel that was very clean and had everything that you needed. Bar was very expensive as was room service, but the customer service skills were excellent, from bar staff to hotel staff. Overall a good stay. Also good walking distance to London attractions.

title: Fabulous and friendly :)
text: Just had a fabulous weekend! Location is great

title: Thanks Vijay
text: After a late night/early morning celebrating an Award, I missed breakfast. Thanks Vijay for bringing me a plate of lovely cooked brekkie and some much needed coffee. Great location, every comfort in room

title: Cold water, no heating
text: The hotel looks nice from the outside & great location BUT beware. The heating wasn't working which meant the rooms were cold & the water barely warm. My colleagues room had torn wallpaper, dirty carpet & the bed wasn't great. This really isn't a 4* hotel!

title: great location but service a little to be desired!
text: I have recently returned from a long weekend in London-I have stayed in lots of hotels in the UK & abroad however it really is more 3 Star quality than 4 star -I was checked in on the Saturday by a lovely receptionist Called ANGEL -she was being professional & polite but was being interrupted by her colleague a male receptionist Martyn -he was off putting & his sense of humour not appreciated as he clearly thought a bit of banter is considered friendly but in my mind most unprofessional -I have worked in the catering industry at a senior level & found his manner towards his work colleagues quite uncomfortable -he made himself look unprofessional & stupid (reminded me of a scene out of Fawlty Towers not Mayfair London) -Over the course of the weekend he was at reception & I had the mis -fortune to listen in on a couple checking out & wanting to leave their bags until later -this was clearly a problem for martyn @ reception as he was quite rude & not initially willing to accommodate the guests wishes -He made a joke saying that 'anyone would think this is a hotel'!!! following on from this guests were coming in to check-in although it was late morning Martyn was clearly not happy about this as made several comments which were rude & un-welcoming -The Receptionist on that day another lady called Katalin was lovely & helped me with my enquiry to print off a confirmation of tickets required but each time Martyn would interrupt & say they would try but if a PDF DOCUMENT then may not be able to print!!!I was surprised as again he had tried to take over & made his work Colleague look very un-comfortable -I was also surprised that the hotel details state that the hotel caters for Business meetings & it seems that most word docs are PDF ?he clearly doesn't understand computers or software & clearly been in the job too long to show sincere enjoyment & empathy to customer needs -I have never complained about my hotel experiences before as I know how difficult customer services is in the real world but think it only fair to the reputation of this centrally located & perfectly positioned hotel to be saved of further embarrassing situations -The 3 star quality also refers to the Twin room we stayed in the carpet clearly needed replacing as it had stains & looked dirty so let the whole quite cute ,cosy & boutique hotel look shabby .If it wasn't for the fact that the room prices are good for the area & brilliant location this is what keeps customers coming back & just a shame that the points raised will be stay with me as an experience as a lesson how not to deliver excellent customer service on the front line ,

title: great location, but small shabby rooms
text: My wife and I have just stayed at the Park Lane Mews hotel to celebrate her 30th birthday. As I read previous negative comments about the hotel, I decided to call ahead of our arrival, and request a nicer room if possible as it was a special occasion. The staff were courteous on the phone and when we turned up, we had a free upgrade to a deluxe room. Very kind! Off to a good start. The staff at check in were lovely and the gent helping with the bags was also very nice. We arrived to the room, as considering it was an upgrade, it was tiny. I actually had to call down to see if she had made a mistake. The only way the room could have been classed as larger, was because we had a narrow long walkway into the room. The room was small at best. The paint had chipped away in may places and carpet was shabby in places. Saying that, beds were clean and cleanliness was overall good. Bathroom again was tiny (sideways sitting on the loo as bath was in the way!). Location for our activities was superb! Parking is expensive (£40 for 24 hours on weekdays) but I suppose you expect that in the centre of London. Now to the two problems we had. The main one: I had booked the theatre as a surprise for my wife, and therefore went to the front desk 2 hours before departure, to book a cab. No problem, its coming at 6:45. Ok, so we turn up at the front door at 6:40 to be safe, and 6:55, still no sign. I went back inside, and they called the firm, and they said they were still struggling to find a taxi for us! I booked over 2 hours in advance! I recommended the hotel they use a different taxi firm in the future, and I was told that is who they use, and I will just have to wait. Who knows if we would have got to the theatre on time! I managed to run to the hilton in front, and they got me a cab. Not great service for a 4* hotel! Second gripe (more of the hotels fault). On saturday morning we were on our way out, and bumped into an elderly couple having a very difficult time getting their 3 huge cases and suitor downstairs. I of course helped them with all their luggage. When I took them to check out, I asked where the bellman with the trolley was to help these people. They said that he does not work saturday morning. Simple as that. No apology to the old couple, or to me. What 4* hotel does not have a bellman on the busiest part of the week?!? SHOCKING! So not massive issues overall. If you are looking for a pleasant stay in a central location for a good price, and are not bothered about a large or up to date room....This is your hotel.

title: Good location
text: The hotel has its issues but we did not find it as bad as some reviewers. It was very convenient for our two-night stay as my husband had meetings in Mayfair. It is close to Green Park tube but also walking distance of pretty much everywhere I wanted to go. Yes, the room was small and our rate was not particularly cheap but not outrageous for Mayfair. The bedroom had plenty of storage space and the bed was comfortable. Like other reviewers, we were initially alarmed by the plug-in radiator, but at least it worked. Yes, the TV was dated, but we didn’t really use it. The bathroom was tiny (as was the bath) but I’ve seen smaller in London. The problem was that the layout hadn’t really been thought through so it was hard to get into the bath without kicking the toilet or to dry yourself once out without knocking the loo roll off. However, at least both bedroom and bathroom were clean. Overall, for London it was a great location and not too bad a price. We didn’t bother with breakfast as there as so many nice cafes nearby, likewise we didn’t drink there with so many pubs and wine bars in the area.

title: Needs attention
text: If you just want to sleep it’s ok. The rooms are clean. Booking in is a hastle. Pay for room. Then pay for breakfast. Then pay a deposit should I break something! Maybe that’s normal? The heating is broken so no aircon just portable radiators. Room was on the small side but since only me it was fine. Good shower. Wash basin plug leaks so have to keep filling. When you want it to drain it takes far too long. One interesting point was the tv. The picture and sound track were out. Best just to listen. It must have been 5-10secs out. I wasn’t that bothered so let it go. Usual tea and coffee. Could use complimentary bottled water. Breakfast was ok. A tad more expensive than I expected. It’s a buffet so at least I could get what I wanted. The decor is scratched in corridors at the same height as the cleaners trolley which has bolt heads exposed. So that explains that. A decent trolley would have saved wreaking the place. Overall not as good as a premier lodge but does serves a good breakfast and has a bar. I would have preferred a premier lodge.

title: Average to low average...
text: Room on the 4th floor did not meet our expectations... Stains on the carpet, stains on the wall and cobwebs did not give a neat impression... Room was in desperate need of freshening up. Receptionists were friendly and location was good for us (close to family living in the same street) but unfortunately this does not weigh up to the room. Would not go back...

title: A little disappointed.
text: I chose this hotel because it was within walking distance of where I was due to attend a luncheon. From the outside the hotel looks good, set back in a quiet street off Picadilly. I checked in and went up to my room. The room was very small with just the basics, flat screen tv, coffee/tea tray etc. Looking out of the window all I could see was the back of other buildings, and a view very reminiscent from the old opening scenes at the start of Coronation Street. There was a stand alone air-con unit running in the room which was extremely noisy. The room was clean with en-suite bathroom, the bed was comfortable. There was a list of cocktails that could be ordered incurring an additional 12% service charge. I filled in the breakfast card and requested breakfast in my room for 0800hrs. This incurred a further 12% service charge. I was woken during the night by doors banging somewhere in the building, and people moving around the hotel from 0600hrs onwards. Breakfast was finally delivered at 0840hrs and I was asked to pay there and then. I said that I would pay when I checked out which was finally agreed. Breakfast was plentiful, but the bacon was overcooked as were the fried eggs. The staff were polite and helpful throughout. My overall impression of my stay was that it was overpriced for what I got for my money.

title: Value for Mayfair
text: Firstly, you have got to consider how much you are paying to stay in Mayfair. Its a real bargain. The hotel has a lovely presentation walking to it. This is a boutique hotel, so is not a massive entrance but not cramped by any means. It is welcoming. I was a bit sceptical as I had seen poor reviews and also stayed in many 5* and more hotels in London but obviously at 3-6 times the price. All i needed was a warm room that was clean for one night. The staff were warm and friendly and informative (even at 1am in the morning!), the room was perfectly clean and presented. It was not a massive room but i did not find it squashy at all for an overnight stay. The curtains perfectly blocked out the street lights bed was firm but I like that. Slightly flat pillows but there were extra so that made up for it. Coffee and biscuits in the room ready for the morning. Breakfast was £11 if you paid on checking in. Hubby and I had a lovely full english breakfast. Again staff were great, including cleaning staff that greeted you and wished you a pleasant day. I would definitely stay there again.

title: London hotel
text: Hotel locality is very good. Walking distance to Oxford street, Picadilly street, Chinatown, Hyde Park, Buckingham Palace and to take a hop on hop off bus tour. Nestled in a quiet enclave and safe area. Staffs and management of hotel are fantastic friendly n helpful people. However, hotel pricing is not cheap . For the room is very small with no proper Aircon service. Toilet is very small too. Lightings in room not bright enough.

title: Disappointed
text: When we arrived the check in was very quick and the staff member was friendly. We went to the room we were very surprised how small the room was and the size of the bathroom. The room was very "old fashioned" and the carpet was dirty, covered with stains. We wanted to open the window however it did not open. Our room did not have a very nice vie of the dustbins opposite. The room felt very gloomy and very enclosed. I don't think that this hotel was worth the price of £160. One positive is that the air conditioning did work quite well letting out cool air. On arrival we were offered breakfast for the Saturday morning, apparently it was on special offer (£11.95) compared to £17.95 online which I would have defiantly not paid and is not worth this amount. Overall I don't think me and my partner will be returning due to us being a young modern couple and this hotel is very much the opposite. Dark, enclosed and old fashioned.

title: Park Lane value
text: Booked this hotel for when we were going to the Radio 2 Hyde Park Concert in a Day. Good location, just behind the Hilton. Hotel very comfortable, had an executive king room, the bed was large enough for three, but there was only two of us! Bathroom was smaller than I would have thought for an 'executive' room but perfectly adequate for our needs. Only had breakfast at the hotel which was good, plenty of choice, all buffet style except the tea & coffee, for some reason the waiting staff poured one cup at a time and took the pot away, but they refilled without delay when we requested a top up. Walk down the side of the hotel to get to several pubs and eateries, I was amazed just how much choice there was at decent prizes so close to Park Lane. Ye Grapes serves Everard's Tiger and London Pride, the Tiger was excellent, and also serves English and Thai food, we had a Thai meal and it was very enjoyable.

title: Dissapointing, Uninspiring, completely Heartless and Unsympathetic!!
text: As a 40th birthday gift we were treated to dinner and a cruise in London by very good friends who had booked to join us too. Along with our friends we decided to stay at Park Lane Mews due to its location. Since this was booked in early June our friend found out he was suffering from a rare form of blood cancer

title: Very Pleasant surprise
text: We stayed at this little gem of Hotel did not expect to find a wonderful place that surrounds this lovely Hotel. The food,, cleanliness, comfort, were first class and the staff very professional but very friendly and extremely helpful. The location was great for all the sightseeing we wanted, plenty of bars restaurants and shops. Look forward to our next stay. Rodney Sandra Northwich

title: Lovely little hotel in heart of Mayfair
text: I had to go to London and stop for one night. I found the Park Lane Mews hotel on the net. Not expensive considering it's location. Very friendly staff. Comfortable room, great to have 'tea-making' equipement. Always plenty of hot water. Great English breakfast in a nice, old fashioned dining room. Get the impression that time has passed by this little gem of an hotel by, hidden away behind the great eye-sore of the London Hilton. Some people think it needs refurbishing, perhaps there is some oldish carpet and chipped paint, but I rather liked that, lived in, homely feeling. Quiet, comfortable, friendly and very well situated. Perfect!

title: Ideal location and good value for this part of London
text: We stayed at this hotel recently and found the staff very helpful and pleasant. The location was ideal and good value considering this part of London. The rooms are a little dated and could do with some work, nonetheless we had a comfortable nights rest and enjoyed our stay. I would recommend the hotel to family and friends, only thing I would say is that it would have been nice if the rooms were a little bigger.

title: Very good - great location
text: 3 nights stay in this hotel, very enjoyable. The price reflects the excellent location of the hotel with it being minutes from Hyde Park, Park Lane, Green Park, Piccadily and Buckingham Palace. Staff were very helpful and friendly and breakfast was good. Hotel is situated to the rear of the Hilton Park Lane, with good restaurants only 5 minutes away in Shepherd's Market. With it being at the rear of the hotel there is a small amount of noise in the evening/early morning with deliveries etc but this was not significant nor did it cause a problem. Room was good, exellent shower. Maybe could have done with a new coat of paint in places and there was no safe for valuables.

title: Get away
text: Great hotel, located in a great area, quiet hotel and quiet area. Close to near by attractions! Room service was lovely. Friendly happy staff, exspensive for sizes of rooms. All in all a good stay! Will recommend to friends and family!

title: Worst hotel in London (and possibly many other cities)
text: £184 for a dingy, worn out, tired excuse for a 4 star hotel. Holes in wall, chunks out of the doors (i think someone’s tried to eat their way out). The last time this brown carpet was changed there was a king on the throne!

title: Quaint hotel. Good prices and decent rooms. Great location for Mayfair
text: Good standard of hotel, a bit tired in places but good location for Park Lane. Staff are very friendly and helpful. Breakfast is very good _ full English recommended. The hotel is an easy walk from Green Park and tucked in behind the Park Lane Hilton with pubs and restaurants in easy reach

title: A little gem
text: Very convenient location and reasonable price compared to other hotels in the area. Room was compact but had everything you want and was perfect for a one night stay. I have seen some of the pictures on this site, but the room I was given was fine, and I had no complaints. Staff on reception and in the restaurant were welcoming and friendly. Breakfast was buffet style with a good selection of hot and cold food. My only suggestion for improvement would be to include some sachets of hot chocolate on the tea tray!

title: Proms in the Park
text: We stayed at the Park Lane Mews with our daughter and son-in -law because it was only a short walk after Proms in the Park in Hyde Park, and they had stayed there previously. We found it to be a charming, cosy, old style hotel, with courteous and helpful reception staff. Our rooms on the fifth floor (there is a lift) were not huge but everything necessary was there, including tea making facilities

title: Stay way from this uncomfortable mess, it might ruin your trip
text: We had reserved and confirmed a Deluxe king room with a king size bed. Upon arrival we were given double room with a queen bed. As soon as we walked in the door we noticed: Filthy carpet. Dirty floors including particles of food and other foreign material. I do not think the place had been vacuumed. Broken and bent light fixtures, burnt out bulbs on two lamps.. Then, Bathroom: No exhaust fan. No lock on door. [ Apparently the door lock had been broken some time before and, rather than repairing it they removed it and put a roller bearing inside the door mechanism so that the door would close. It's a lot cheaper for a hotel owner than to hire someone who actually knows how to repair things properly ... door locks and toilets. ] Cracked and broken sink porcelain

title: Park Lane Lose!!
text: I booked the Executive Room and what I got fell far short. Looked amazing on Hotels.com however its far short once you get into the lift. the room was grubby, carpet stained, bathroom minging and the carpets were not only in need of a jet wash they additionally required refitting to the floor. Gutted really as it looked a treat from outside bar the two cigarette bins on the wall each side of the entrance which appeared not to have been emptied for a couple of days. the staff in reception where polite and curious and assisted with getting taxis.

title: My advise is stay away This is not a four star hotel
text: We booked this hotel as my husband had stayed on business 2 years ago and said location was good and hotel was ok....HOW WRONG COULD HE BE!! upon arrival we checked in early and the front desk were very professional and welcoming although he told us the room for 3 people that we had booked and already paid for was really small and the 3rd bed would only just fit in the room with no space to spare...that was very true. The room was really shabby, dirty and torn wallpaper, Stained bath tub which was so small a bath would have been almost impossible unless you are a child and the beds fitted side by side with no extra space between at all. The room had obviously had smokers in it as it was very unfresh and smelled of tobacco. When the chambermaid came to make up the third bed she brought a duvet which was covered in dried in blood and i mean it must have been a stain of about 36" by 24" - HOW DISCUSTING!! obviously we would have complained but before we got the chance she said it was no good as it was a double duver and the cover was only single....no mention of the dried in blood stain. The airconditioning did not work and as it was around 25degrees we woke up tossing and turning all night as we were so so hot. Usually we would have complained but as we were only staying one night and its the high season and getting somewhere else at short notice would have been almost impossible we decided to stay put. The location of the hotel is ok but there are many hotels closer to the action of london. Saving grace was breakfast which was very nice, full english and the staff were most polite. in a nutshell i would not ever stay here again even if it was free. Please do yourself a favor and book something else.

title: London faded grandeur
text: Attractive hotel in an excellent location. The bad bits..... very small room. No hot water for bath, tiny summer duvet for a chilly winter stay, flimsy pillows, two lights did not work in the room, tatty fixtures and fittings in room, heater not functioning fully, bar is really non existant (it involves asking a member of reception to dissapear into the kitchens if you require a drink!). The good bits.....quiet but central location all within walking distance of some excellent restaurants and pubs, clean rooms, friendly staff. I really hope the hotel sorts out the fixtures and fittings in the rooms. It is such a shame the small things seem to have been forgotten about as they are exactly what the customer looks for and expects! I would stay again but only because the location is fantastic and not because of the quality of the hotel.

title: Worst hotel
text: Terrible hotel. From the outside it looks nice and the reception area seems appealing however this is where it ends. Rooms are shabby and tired looking. The bed clearly hadn't been changed as there were numerous hairs under the duvet and on the sheet. Upon telling reception about the state of the room we were told there were no other rooms to change to and instead were given a change of bedding to make ourselves... Very noisy room also. Constant noise throughout the night as the rooms are on a road next to the refuse collection entrance for another hotel. Overall terrible experience. Very grubby hotel and for the price definitely is not 4 star quality.

title: Great location, and that's pretty much it
text: In a neighborhood of great and expensive hotels, like the Dorchester and The Metropolitan (where Robert De Niro's Nobu restaurant is located), the Park Lane Mews tries to compete with an impressive lobby. The minute you set foot in it, you start to expect the Earl of Gloucestershire to appear at any minute, puffing on his pipe. However, the rooms leave much too much to be desired. Old dirty carpets, beds not too comfortable, not a lot of space. Shower water took about 10 minutes to warm up, which can be tricky if you're in a hurry. Wireless internet did not work most of the time even though they had two servers in the hotel. So it's your call. If you want to stay at a chic location, close to Oxford Street and Picadilly, fine. The price is reasonable for London, very expensive for pretty much everywhere else on the planet. Staff are nice and courteous, except for the over-tanned girl that does the morning shift in the lobby. She is one of those women who probably think that her good looks are an excuse for not being polite or corteous, whereas most guests couldn't care less about it and would rather have nice manners before tanning salons.

title: Don't be fooled by the location - rubbish
text: It may be in Mayfair but it is a squalid little place that is run down and is really 3 star. The descriptions are misleading and the service poor. There is no doorman to assist with backs and one cranky lady in the desk. It's a joke! Anywhere else it would be below best western. As a well travelled person, I would recommend you stay away. Unfortunate I have to wait until tomorrow to check out

title: A little tired
text: The hotel is small and cosy some might say bijou! The Reception/bar area is pleasant a little dark, or was that the dreary weather outside. Nice fireplace, comfy if a bit tired looking sofas and chairs but nice atmosphere. Two small lifts to bedroom floors. Our bedroom (409) was a rather small double, but not too small, we did think the bed was a small double rather than a standard double. The room smelt musty, perhaps it hadn't been used for a few days or maybe it was because an electric radiator had been left on in the room, which was totally unnecessary, the room wasn't cold. Once we'd put the air conditioning on the air cleaned and the room felt nicer. The room was adequate for our needs an overnight stay, but I do think the room needs to be refurbished and is in need of some TLC, it felt very tired and old. The bathroom was tiny, although everything worked fine, nice selection of toiletries and plenty of good quality towels. The bathroom also needs some love, plaster work by corner of bath had been badly repaired but having said all that it was very clean - just tired. We didn't eat breakfast as there is a very good cafe serving fantastic full breakfast for £7.95 just a 3 minute walk behind hotel. We had a good stay, staff friendly particularly chap who worked at the bar in the evening. The hotel has a brilliant location and I guess that's what you are paying for. Hilton Park Lane car park 5 minute walk from hotel.

title: Fair Review.
text: After reading many reviews we were a little dubious about staying at Park Lane Mews, so after staying for two nights for my birthday I thought I could give an honest review. Firstly the location is very good, walking distance from Green Park Station and situated behind Hilton Park Lane. There are lovely mews in the surrounding area with lots of independent resturants and pubs to visit (turn down the alley at the left of the hotel entrance.) The hotel- Unforunatley we were at the front of the hotel on the second floor and as mentioned in other reviews, it is noisy. Sports cars racing around, staff from opposite hotel having thier cigaret breaks all hours and general loudness from people on nights out. Fortunately I had earphone so I slept with them in and finally got to sleep. We didn't make the hotel aware of our disturbance as this sufficed. Yes the hotel is dated and it could do with upgrading. Our room was tired but it was clean. We didn't have air conditiong but we got a fan from reception with no problem and room service brought us an iron and ironing board when we asked for one too. We didn't eat at the hotel so I can't comment on any of the food, we ate at the independent eateries as it was cheaper. The staff we met where pleasant, not the welcome you get when staying in a group hotel but that's not what you are paying for so you get what you pay for. To be fair, we have stayed in several 4* hotels in Mayfair, Park Lane Mews in my opinion should be a 3* in it's current condition and the facilities it offers.

title: Location very good - main reason for this choice.
text: Rooms and bathrooms in general very tired need upgrade . carpets in the rooms very worn look very dirty ,big issue to walk bare foot in the room. Reception staff / Jenny very good in her job, she assisted us and found solutions in all needed. Heaters very noisy ,in fact in our room we found a portable heater probably for this reason. Top location.

title: My birthday
text: Stayed 4 th to 6th August .. absolutely gutted . Having done a lot of research on hotel in the area i picked this one because of the Hotels Official Description. None of it true .. run down .. shabby.. dirty.. Should be reported to hotel grading body for misrepresentation of star rating . 4 STAR no way try a 2 STAR.. They charged me £5 .04 for a bottle of luke warm water on Friday night to take to the room.. absolute disgrace.. total waste of my hard earned money.

title: Great location, outdated furniture
text: The location is great.. steps away from the bus stop.. there is an elevator but a small stair should be climbed to reach it.. staff is great espcialy wajed, ayman & jenny.. glenn was rude and made a silly joke about spending too much money on shopping.. this is not acceptible in my culture as I was not getting money out of his pocket to shop.. it happened because I was preauthorized of a one night before I arrive and when I arrived they took the whole amount from my card which nade the preauthorized aum hold in my balance for about two weeks before it was released again into my account.. another annoying thing that they do is holding an amount of 100£ as an insurance for every room that is released after we leave the hotel.. The hotel is suffucient.. beds are comfortable.. rooms was warm (we visited in the fall so I don't know about the summer time).. title: PARK LANE MEWS
text: i made a wrong date booking but the lovely reception team Sofia and Tee were able to help me sort out my reservation. The room wasn't that great but i was here for work and needed to stay only for one night.

title: Look at the pictures I posted. A picture is worth 1000 words.
text: Cons. Old. Run down. Not worth what you pay for. No safety deposit box. Although it states that one exists on the website Pros. Location is fantastic. They’ll probably tell you what they told me. That they have newly renovated rooms, and that is what you see on their website. Just none available at the time. I was there for 5 night and asked to move to one of the renovated rooms when they became available. They claim that all the renovated rooms were fully booked.. I don’t think they exist.

title: Lovely area, good room.
text: I noticed this Hotel had been subject to a lot of bad reviews which I belive it does not deserve, during my stay at Park lane Mews Hotel there were no unsatisfactory aspects whatsoever. The surrounding area is lovely and there are plenty of places to eat, the hotel exterior was very aesthetically pleasing. The standard double room was spotlessly clean and well decorated with contemporary furnishings, we had a large Television and a comfortable bed. We visited on a very hot, muggy day but the air conditioning in the room kept us very cool during the night. Overall this was a very relaxing, enjoyable stay and this hotel and from my experience does not deserve the negative reviews it recives.

title: Dcamp
text: Nice hotel at the back of the hilton noise of dustbin wagons at 6 10 in the morning but nice area everything handy resteraunts chemists shops newspapers nice food at sofras if we go again we would ask for a room at the back of hotel a lot guieter staff very nice and breakfast ok

title: Bad hotel - great location
text: People keep telling me that in general London hotels are bad, even at 300 pounds a night, so what can you demand when you pay less than a 100? The room is shabby and damn cold. They give you a small electric heater which is not sufficient. The wool blanket carries 10 kilos of dust and is unusable. Over all - not a great experience. Will return only at a gunpoint.

title: Nice cousy place
text: I stayed at the hotel, it was nice and homely environment, the internet did not work properly but otherwise was great stay. The hotel duty manager Nigora was extremely helpful and pleasant! Looking forward to stay here again in future!

title: Thanks Sandya
text: Excellent service and very safe and clean hotel. In addition, very friendly staff and helpful reception especially ms Sandya. I was happy to stay in the hotel and I advice tourists to try it. Thank you

title: What a gem
text: A small hotel which is so well situated for Mayfair and Sheherds Market, Great personal service, has the ambeience that only smaller well run hotels can achieve. Thoughtful staff,a management out to provide a real service. Loved it,will be using it in future.

title: Short Break
text: A most enjoyable stay at this small boutique hotel located directly behind the Hilton on Park Lane. It was easily accessible from Victoria Station (form Gatwick flight) and a very short walk to the bus stops on Park Lane and Hyde Park Corner Underground Station. The room altho' not large was maintained to the highest standard by the maids. FlyBe managed to lose a case on our inbound journey. The staff at Reception could not have been more helpful particularly Angel.

title: Poor standard of room spoiled visit
text: This hotel had been selected for us to be situated close to the start of the Vitality British 10k and avoid travel on the day so that I could have a relaxed start to be in the best possible state for the race. The hotel was indeed right where we needed it to be and for location I give 5 stars. That's were it ends. The hotel is very dated and our standard room was tiny. All I needed was a comfortable bed and a good nights sleep to be refreshed for my early start and race the next day. The double was a 4ft bed, not big enough for two adults, even skinny ones!! The air con unit was archaic and blasted out cold air underneath an open window, incredibly noisy, right at ear height when in bed. when switched off the room was like an oven. I managed an hour and a half sleep all night and felt exhausted the following day. For £200 a night, no breakfast (additional £17.95 cost) it was NOT worth the money. In hindsight it would have been better to travel early and arrive on the day having slept at home........in the Midlands!!! We were travelling light, the hotel details hairdryer in the room. There is one, but evaporation would be quicker. Such a shame, but if you need your hotel for a good nights sleep and seek value for the money you are paying, this one is not for you.

title: Gigantic Bed
text: It's taken me so long to write a review... (June 2008): Got the room for a significant discount through the internet, and was tucked away from Park Lane, but just a minute's walk from Piccadilly (A4). The bed was enormous. Never had such a good night's sleep. Room was small, however, and the bathroom was interesting. Doubt larger businessmen could use the bathroom with the door closed. Staff were very polite, and the communal areas were very well-kept, something you would obviously expect at such a hotel.

title: OMG........... Terrible
text: Stayed thankfully for just 1 night. Room filthy, damp walls, paper hanging of the wall, bed as hard as rock and I dare not look at the mattress. Website makes this look like a 5 star but maximum is 1 star and that's being generous. Go here only if it's your last hope of finding somewhere to stay. I can confirm all photos posted are correct and even those photos make it look good. Good luck

title: GREAT LOCATION
text: Very lovely hotel, perfect location to have a nice break and relax, Spot on for Simone Migliardi for the best customers service ever always ready to help!!well done thanks for everything! See you soon 😊

title: weekend girls from scotland
text: Hi there everyone, just to let you know that had a quite relaxing five days at the Leonard. The room was on the fifth floor so after getting in the elevator had to carry our luggage upstairs a flight to our room. The room was clean, the beds were comfy, the air conditioning was not working very well so quite hot at night so we left the window open all the time . We had only breakfast in the hotel which was ample and lots to choose from. The hotel itself very old worlde looking but keeping in character with the hotel and looks like what foreigners would expect of quaint english styled hotels. The staff were all friendly and helpful and we had a laugh as they could not understand our scotch accent sometimes and us theirs..... Oxford street 1 minute nearby so shopping trips meant going back with bags and re-filling up again. Bus journeys and tube journeys you can buy a pass to get you on both modes of transport although this time around we used taxis and walked but all within easy reach of the hotel. Marble Arch tube station is less than 2 mins away Great pub right across the road called the Grazing Goat . We went there on our second nights visit as the drinks (2 vodkas and lemonade) was £18......? pence in the hotel . Very pricey and the same drinks only £10.00 across the road, so hence doubles all around in the Grazing Goat...... Checked out other hotels in vicinities which are Radisson Port Blu which is the same price yet more modern and the pricey Marriott Churchill across the road from the Leonard which is obviously superior yet not too much of a difference in price if you really like your comfort. The Mostyn Hotel is around the corner and lots of airline pilots staying here and also a busy hotel. Next door to the Leonard is Maylebone Police Station but I might add the gansters in this part of the woods very quiet.........not a lot of action going on........ Well this about sums it up for us, we are down in July again but going to try out the Radisson Port Blu which is less that a minute from the Leonard so hope it is as good, we will let you know. bye for the noo......................

title: Review Yvonne Madureira
text: Whenever I fly from Porto-Portugal to the UK, I always stay at this Hotel because of the very good quality of service they provide, all members of staff are very friendly and very helpful. I strongly reccomend them.

title: Charming
text: Back in the Leonard. Such a charming, comfortable small hotel. I slept like a log last night. Friendly and helpful staff. Great location. The perfect place for a woman to stay in London for business or tourism. The only gripe I have is that I am working too hard to be able to enjoy it to the full!!

title: Not bad for the price, but...
text: Overall my experience with the Leonard hotel was average. I checked in on a Friday morning, and discovered that my room wasn't ready. Ok, it was a bit early in the morning, but the receptionist told me that the room was already available, but needs to be cleaned. That would take 4 hours, she said. Quite amazing for a 10 feet room. I sure expected it to be very clean... When I was finally let in, I received room number 16. I did book a single room, but this one was quite awful. It was located in the middle of two floors, without a proper elevator access. You either had to climb up from the first floor or down from the second. I did got help with my luggage, but not a pleasant experience to say the least. My next discovery was that the room's AC wasn't heating the room. It was December and it was freezing! I called the reception and they have changed my room to a different one, this time on the second floor - number 20. Now, number 20 is a much nicer room. Roughly the same size, 10 Square ft. but looks better. The AC was working well, and the little flat screen LCD television had lot's of channels. Two major problems bothered me in my short stay there. The first, after the first night I discovered that the next-door elevator makes the most horrible sounds at night. Apparently something is wrong with it, and it just purrs all night. The second problem was with the room's dimensions. You can't really do much in the room other then sit on the bed. There is a small chair, but no real table to work on. The chair actually blocks the way to the tiny cabinet and if you have any luggage you will have to hop above it to get to your bed. The bathroom isn't grand either. It's a tiny space with a tiny shower and a corner sink. Another point worth mentioning is the wireless internet charges. I couldn't find online any mention of it being a paid service, but apparently it is. The hotel charges roughly 4GBP per wireless hour, and 10GBP per day. Not the end of the world, but again, I couldn't find this information on the hotel's website so here goes. On the good side, the staff was very nice. The location is amazing, and the hotel's public areas are beautiful. With a fair price of 80GBP per night excluding VAT (from the hotel's website), I guess this is a fair deal, but I'm not sure I will return to this hotel.

title: Excellent location, clean, friendly staff
text: This is an ideal location if you want to be close to Oxford St/West end attractions/tubes/Victoria. It is in a safe area to get to at night - there is a doorman outside. The staff are very friendly. They didn't have wheat free bread, and the staff were surprised at the request.

title: Charming British Style Hotel next to Oxford street and Marble Arch
text: My two teenage daughters and I stayed in a spacious One room suite(one bedroom- one living room) in a lovely British atmosphere with refilling of biscuits and tea every afternoon. We ate breakfast in our living room, but big English breakfast in a cosy restaurant is available, even brought to your room. Located on a quiet street 150 m from Oxford street gave us nice sleep after hectic shopping, sightseeing and musicals.The reception guided us in an efficient and friendly way weather to take the Tube, taxi or walk depending on time, price and distance. Outstanding hospitality, lovely warm reception area ,quick check in and out, luggage keeping, nice cleaning and everything you expect from a four star hotel. The hotel helped with booking all big sightseeing events so we did not have to wait in line as well as confirming on line bookings done in Sweden with the theatres.

title: Location, Location
text: The Leonard is in a great location close to Marble Arch, shopping and the parks. The staff is friendly and helpful. The furnishings in the rooms are each unique with a variety of antiques in most rooms and very modern in others. The bed in our room was somehow two mattresses bagged together to make a king size. the gap in the middle was noticeable. Were we staying another night would have asked for another.

title: A bad experience
text: Very bad experience,every thing is bad,the staff are careless and uncooperative. We are live in 4th floor and no elevator. There was a leakage of water from the ceiling and after that the room was changed to a worse one.I strongly advise everyone not to book at this bad hotel.

title: Superb afternoon tea
text: I came here with my mum for afternoon tea one Sunday afternoon and we both thought it was superb. When we arrived we were shown to our table and asked what teas we would like straight away. There were roses on the tables and they were set out nicely. The decor was a bit to be desired but it gives it that old Victorian feel. Service was a little slow but I could not fault the hotel in general. I would come back here and have recommended it to friends. I said that it was one of the best places I have been to for afternoon tea.

title: Nice Hotel with an Outstanding Staff
text: This hotel exceeded our expectations - good location, large and comfortable rooms (Deluxe room) and the staff was great with their recommendations and overall helpfulness. Special mention to Abdul in the restaurant and Hussein at the front desk. Abdul went as far as to lend us his personal converter until we were able to purchase our own. Some great restaurants are close by, and the Marble Arch station is right around the corner. Definitely will stay here again when back visiting London.

title: Afternoon Tea
text: My partner and I had a lovely afternoon tea at The Leonard hotel, good selection of sandwiches, and lovely warm scones with clotted cream and jam, and a selection of cakes and of course plenty of tea. The service and staff were excellent. Very enjoyable afternoon.

title: Do not go for afternoon tea as you will be shocked with what you get for your money.
text: I went there with my wife,I assumed that you would be well looked after due to the location but I was totally wrong. Firstly they give you one pot of tea and that is it,they put one tea bag in a large teapot. The sandwiches are prepared and same for everybody,as we are vegetarian ,I asked for vegetarian option but they refused.We shared one little quarter each.the rest were meat but they refused to change. So whilst it is a 2 for 1 offer ,I rather go to a cafe as they the surrounding are dated and worn and it is not worth it for money. They came only once to take the order and that was it,it is not a special dining room . Will not go again

title: Champagne Tea
text: My daughter booked afternoon tea with champagne as a birthday surprise. The room is lovely, with lots of interesting photographs and cosy traditional decor. The staff are polite, friendly and helpful. The crockery is stylish. We had two pots of English tea, sandwiches, cakes and scones, all fresh and tasty, and two glasses of good champagne. I would recommend it to anyone looking for an atmospheric treat.

title: Fabulous
text: Very welcoming staff. They really go out of their way to make your stay enjoyable. I visit London once a year and have done so for many years I have finally found a hotel i will be re visiting for many years. Family friendly/ welcoming only a few words to really describe the hotel

title: A real mix of experiences
text: A good deal through Last Minute for a suite at this hotel. An old-fashioned hotel, friendly enough, but slightly dated and a little scruffy round the edges. A delightfully vague receptionist, a lift that issued minor electric shocks - perhaps it was just me - but, most importantly, a suite that was very comfortable. The most impressive point was that things worked - a proper iron and ironing board, a shower that was simple and easy to use, a TV that just switched on, provided a good picture and didn't want to give me unwelcome welcome messages to navigate past. A comfortable bed. Brilliant in that respect. And a day's wi-fi for £5. Take note, Le Meridien, Crowne Plaza, etc. The downsides, to the extent that there really were any? A tiny lift (licensed to carry six - that would be entertaining) which was ponderously slow and narrow corridors with various steps along the way to trip up the unwary. The point was it did what a hotel is required to do - comfortable, easy to live in and pleasant staff. The acid test - would I go back? No hesitation. Its not pretentious, just very very good.

title: Relaxing Sunday afternoon tea
text: 6 of us we went to the Leonard hotel with a groupon deal on sunday the 15th of January at 5pm for afternoon tea and wow it was worth it. We actually arrived early but the staff were very accommodating and asked if we'd like to eat when we arrived.at 4.45pm. There was a wide selection of teas to choose from and for the non tea lover beautiful filter coffee. Then came out the selection of cakes and sandwiches - ranging from cucumber, salmon, ham and egg & cress (suited to all people if you're a bit fussy like me) each were fresh and well presented. We had 4 finger sized sandwiches each, two squares of carrot cake and chocolate cake and 2 miniature scones (which were warm from the oven on arrival) each with fresh cream and jam. The staff were polite and reassuringly asked if everything was ok and if you need anything frequently. Cant recommend here enough, superb service, wonderful staff and fantastic food.

title: Great location, great staff
text: Excellent hotel, the staff were amazing, by far the most friendly, helpful and professional in any hotel I have used. The room was well equipped, the location is ideal. The hotel is well designed and furnished. The street is central to London yet just of the main roads, so quiet and restful at night.

title: Wonderful afternoon tea
text: I bought a voucher for an afternoon tea as a gift for my mum on Mother's Day. We finally got a chance to use it last weekend and it was wonderful. I had booked the royal afternoon tea so we had a glass of champagne to start. They then brought out the sandwiches and cakes. We had salmon & cream cheese, cucumber, egg and ham & mustard sandwiches which were all delicious. Followed by scones with jam, lots of lovely little cakes and some salted caramel cupcakes. Everything was great and my mum enjoyed her treat! :)

title: awful experience
text: I arrived at the hotel at 1.00pm. I was told that my room was not yet ready and had to wait until 2.00 pm. I waited at the bar in front of the reception and at 2.30 pm given nobody was coming, i went to the reception desk and only then they said the room was ready. I was in front of them and nobody cared to advise me that finally the room was ready. Room was the smallest one i have ever had in my life and was also very remotely located, not easily accessible with trolley and taking some walking up and down from the lift. I had real difficulty in moving around the room as the bed was occupying almost entirely the space, Shower separated from the bathroom and throwing humidity straight into the room. TV not working. WIndow not closing properly and furniture and carpet which both need strong renovation. On top of this i found the staff not helpful at all. They couldnt care less. For a 4 star hotel with pretty high price, this experience was awful and extremely disappointing,

title: Central location, wonderful staff, excellent room, solid pricing (for London!) - a TRUE winner!
text: This is our second stay at the Leonard, and it was once again simply perfect. The room was spacious, clean, and warmly decorated, the staff were exceptionally helpful and kept volunteering to help and assist at very turn, the location near the Marble Arch was the perfect setting for our needs. For business or holiday/vacation, this is a truly wonderful hotel, and we look forward to returning again. Thank you once again for a perfect stay!

title: Quiet haven
text: We visited the Leonard with an open mind after reading some bad reviews but were pleasantly surprised. Good location, pleasant staff, and a lovely room. We were on the top floor, room 510, a quiet haven from the noise of the city. The bed was incredible-so comfortable, and the bedding was luxurious. bar prices were a little steep but that would not stop us from staying there again. definitely recommendable.

title: Afternoon tea
text: We had a deal for afternoon tea for two with champagne, fantastic service very enjoyable! Definitely worth the value for money. From the moment of entry to end the staff were friendly and tentative. Would defiantly go again. Cakes were delicious.

title: Could have been better
text: When we arrived the receptionist advised us that our rooms weren't ready but we could leave our cases, the receptionist was very informative and helpful.When we eventually got into our rooms we were advised that as requested two rooms were close to each other, rooms 7&8 which are downstairs next to the dining room. The rooms are very large and clean, the down side was that the rooms didn't smell very nice, not sure if someone had eaten an Indian meal in both rooms the previous night. Both rooms were very dark and decor very old fashioned, dark drapes and bedding makes the rooms appear darker, we had to use the lights most of the time during the day. The bed was comfortable, but pillows very flat! We hadn't been in our room very long when the door bell went and in walked a cleaner, we were shocked, she didn't wait to be invited into the room which I wasn't happy about and could have caused embarrassement to all concerned, all she wanted to do was flush the toilet, stated that she had been teaching a new member of staff, this intrusion was not neccessary and she should have waited to have been invited in to the room. We tried the food in the evening, we were going to the theatre and felt eating in was the best option, big mistake........staff were very nice but disorganised, they were unable to tell us soup of the day until chef came down some 15mins later. I had fish and chips with mushy peas and at £12.95 I felt that fresh chips rather than frozen should be used, wasn't convinced that the fish was fresh either. The eating experience could have been better if the TV over the bar was switched off and the cleaner wasn't hoovering the floor. Felt very sorry for one member of staff as he was told off in full view of us for something trival, very bad management which made us feel uncomfortable. Breakfast in the morning was lovely no complaints. The positives of the hotel are location, price and staff. I'm not sure whether I would use the hotel again as I have stayed in better hotels in London for similar price.

title: Average afternoon tea
text: We went here for afternoon tea on a Friday afternoon. Having booked over a month in advance we were surprised to find ourselves on a pop up table that didn't match the rest of the furniture in the dining room. I had also called a few days ahead to ask if they could cater to the dietary requirements of a celiac, they assured me that it was fine and they would ensure there were gluten free cakes and sandwiches however, they only provided her with 4 tiny sandwiches that were presented on the same plate as the normal sandwiches, they told us cakes were not available, so for the money paid all she had was a glass of champagne and 2 slices of bread! They tried to charge is extra for coffee instead of tea and the staff just weren't very attentive. The scones and champagne were lovely however that was all. A shame really. After looking around there are much better afternoon tea deals you can find so would advice going elsewhere.

title: Nice hotel
text: We have been coming to the Leonard for years and have stayed in the classic doubles , the grand suites and the 1 and 2 bedroom apartments, we have always had a good experience the staff always very willing and friendly and a wonderful central location.

title: Classic, quaint and incredibly friendly
text: We stayed here for one night after a recommendation from friends who stayed previously. This hotel is gorgeous, clean and secure. The location is perfect for tourists who want to be close to the action. The staff are incredibly friendly and the breakfast buffet was extensive. This will be my first choice for my next London visit.

title: Convenient Location
text: What I liked most about this hotel is the convenient location

title: Spacious Hotel Rooms
text: Stayed here for 2 nights at an end of a 11 day trip through London and Paris. Great location a block away from the Marble Arch tube station so close to all the shops on Oxford, but on a relatively quiet street. Very friendly staff. The room was extremely large compared to the other two hotels we stayed at during our trip. The room reminded me more of an American hotel room with the amount of space available. The bathroom was also quite spacious. The room was also very contemporary in decor with a nice LCD TV. The biggest CON to the room was the fact that you will need to walk up 2 flights of stairs to get to the room. Our room was located on the top floor and the elevator did not go there. I'm sure if you were unable to climb the stairs, the staff would provide service, but it was annoying dragging even our carry-on bags up the stairs after a long day of traveling. Granted the front desk did ask if we needed help which we declined not realizing it would be 2 flights. I booked the hotel through travelzoo.com with a 50% discount making it a more reasonable price. I would stay again for that same price, but would not if I had to pay full price.

title: Needs some TLC, great location for shopping though
text: Hotel was ok but in need of decorating. Room was quite large. Staff could have been more helpful -alhough in their defence it was hard to be chatty as all the staff we met could only speak broken English. They were polite and tried but it left us feeling as though we were in the middle of a foreign country rather than London. Rooms needed decorating but you could tell they were basically good rooms - just needed freshening. The saving grace for this hotel is the location - straight out of the hotel, turn a corner and then onto Oxford Street. Great location for a shopping trip.

title: Excellent choice
text: Location is great, next to Marble Arch tube station and Oxford Street. Rooms very comfy, staff is very helpful. Food is very good. Across the street from one of the best restaurants in London (Locanda Locatelli). Definitely a choice to recommend and visit again.

title: The leonard Hotel
text: Great hotel being close to Marble Arch, which is a brilliant location, the hotel has excellent freindly service, who really do all they can to make you feel welcome. Lots to recommend it a great Hotel.

title: Room in need of updating and adjacent to the lift
text: Where do I start. The room is in pretty rough shape. The wallpaper is ripped and could use a facelift. The room is pretty small too. The worst part is the fact that it is immediately next door to the lift. Wouldn't book again.

title: No value for money
text: The location was good and the fact that bathroom wasn't as small as it was in many hotels,those were the only things we liked about the hotel. The staff was welcoming as well Hotel was very in need of refurbishment, the wallpapers were getting off and dirty in some places. The furniture and things like alarm clock, phone, iron and ironing table (it was broken actually) were very old. We were given a room in the 5th floor..where we had to take elevator untill 4th floor and stairs then. With 2 suitcases and tired after a loong travelling day that was not what we wanted. There was no value for money! for that money there were better hotels and even apartments where we could stay.

title: Great location
text: Friendly staff :) rooms are lovely but a bit old. We had a problem with the safe box but the staff tried their best to solve it . Food is average in my opinion. Bus stops are with few minutes from the hotel.

title: Afternoon tea
text: I had a great time with my family for afternoon tea, in a very peaceful place and the service was great. I would like to thank Khan who has been amazing. In fact, I made a mistake with my groupon and so wasn’t able to use my voucher. But, he did all he can for us to still use and we had a great time. Thank you so much. It was a lovely moment and the food was DELICIOUS. Only thing: the size of the scones, they should be bigger. But beside this EVERYTHING WAS GREAT. I RECOMMEND IT.

title: My London home away from home.
text: I have been staying at the Leonard for 10 years and I hope that this Hotel will never change. The staff are warm and friendly and really eager to help in any way. The rooms are furnished in traditional English style, very cosy and the beds very comfortable. The location is excellent with great shopping and cafes a short walk away. Hyde Park is nearby for those who love horse riding or running. For me it is one of the best kept secrets in London and I hope it remains that way. I highly recommend The Leonard to anyone who is visiting London.

title: A fabulous place to stay
text: I just returned from staying at The Leonard Hotel and I can't say enough nice things about it. It is located on a quiet street which is very close to the Marble Arch Tube stop, bus stops that will take you anywhere in the city, and Oxford St. The staff were all extremely friendly, helpful and knowledgable. The decor is welcoming and warm. You feel like you are at home as soon as you walk through the doors. There is a quaint dining room and bar, and the front room has several comfy couches and the fireplaces were always going. The room was a good size and had a large bathroom. I have been going to London for years and have stayed at many hotels around the city. The Leonard Hotel will have my business from now on.

title: Jaber almutairi
text: My stay at the hotel was pleasant, All services and facilities was as good as it should be. The big plus was given for location and staff services especially Mr. Abdellah, he was so helpful. Defenetly i will stay here again ,, abdellah Thnks :)

title: Something a bit different
text: After many years staying in hotels all over London I discovered the Leonard and immediately became a regular guest who has stayed at this hotel every week for many years now. This says it all really - The Leonard is my home for home in London.The staff here are superb. The level of customer service is consistently good and has remained so over the years. The staff are friendly, quietly efficient and create a calm, unhurried atmosphere which is greatly appreciated. The hotel itself consists of a series of town house which gives it a quaint feel. I love the size and space of many of the rooms which are all individually decorated in that shabby chic style which shouts English country house. This type of decor is so different from the bare, modern beige minilism of many of today's hotels where every room is identical. But, it does mean that some of the rooms may look a little tired at times. All, however, have excellent beds. Another plus is that you rarely hear noise from other rooms but, it has to be admitted, the floor boards do creak. Having said that this is only a nuisance if the guest above decides to use their room to train for the London marathon at midnight. The style of this hotel gives it a warm, cosy ambiance which, coupled with its quiet but central location and superb customer service makes it a hidden delight.

title: my stay in the hotel
text: the only good thing in this hotel is the friendly staff and the management is not flexile and the hotel furniture is very old. I did not enjoy my stay in this hotel. I tried to cancel my stay from the moment I entered the hotel but unfortunately they did not accept since I made my reservation through booking.

title: A faded gem
text: Had 3 nights here for my weekly stay in London. The website looked good but the reality was that the hotel was really quite tatty. Obviously a lot of money had been spent in the past as the furnishings were quite opulent but once you looked further there were scratched surfaces and worn paint. The hotel is very welcoming with an open fire in the reception/ lounge area and very friendly staff. I was given a huge and comfortable room which in a smarter hotel would have cost a fortune but the downsides were, no bottled water, other than that for sale at £2, no free wifi, air on that had to be paid for and windows that didn't open. The staff were very good, helpful and responsive. I also had a very nice bowl of pasta late back from work one evening as room service which was very fresh and tasty. A good location and possible to park outside. I would go back but it is all very dated - the one lift is so slow - and needs a facelift.

title: Fantastic!
text: Just waking distance from Oxford Street. Super clean. Staff was friendly. Advise- they have a tie up with a mini cab company for airport pick-ups and drop-offs. It cheaper than hiring a black cab. We didn't have break fast at the hotel cos it just wasn't worth the price. However, what we did do was eat at KFC which was down the road which costed £6.00 for two people.

title: "Afternoon Tea'"'
text: We visited the 'Leonard Hotel' last week for afternoon tea. I came with teenage children and we had a wonderful time. The ambience was lovely, quiet but a lovely atmosphere. I love the décor and the crockery! The food was amazing and particularly the scones were the best I've ever tasted! Loved it and we will definitely recommend and come again.

title: A real mixed bag
text: Rooms are a good size - we ordered 3 suites, and all had good sized bedrooms, with seperate loung/kitchenette, and seperate bathrooms - overall really good size and value for money for London. As everyone says, great location too - really good wine shop in street opposite, great cafe for breakfast/brunch just across the road from hotel front door too. Reception staff very friendly and helpful, and bell boys try hard too. However, bar/restaurant staff appalling - don't seem to have been trained, Luke warm wine, and appealing breakfast. I'd come back to the hotel, but i wouldnt use the bar/restaurant, but the breakfast across the road on the first day was really one of the best ive had for a long time - so no real need to stay in. Bed's were really comfy, and super kings, despite being described as smaller on web. Lots of creaky floors though, And some road noise on lower floors. To be fair to the hotel, when i mentioned the poor experience, they refunded the breakfast, and took on board the service comments - so i cant ask for much more than that, accepting it had already happened.

title: Almost Perfect
text: I've stayed here countless times and have found everything pretty much perfect - great breakfasts in the Cafe Bar (Cosy, homely restaurant), helpful staff available at all hours, spacious rooms, comfy beds & linen, excellent showers, nice toiletries, air-con. However, one thing I noticed on some recent visits - arriving late on a Sunday (10pm ish), there's no chef available, so room service was limited to pizza / panini. In fact there was no menu available. There are some supermarkets nearby, so I picked up something from there - can't say I'm happy to do that after a flight. This was a real shame as their own menu (short but good), if available, would have done the trick This not withstanding, the hotel is fantastic and in a great location

title: Afternoon Tea
text: The afternoon tea was really nice, the tea room is quite big and traditional. They serve a good variety of cakes and sandwiches. The waiters are very helpful and welcoming ( they couldn’t find our reservation but they were so nice and solved the thing as fast as possible). A nice evening out!

title: Great traditional English hotel
text: A great hotel old fashioned it may be but so much better than the modern alternatives the staff are great the location is good and the room rate is reasonable would not want to stay any where else in london

title: The Leonard Hotel is a little hidden gem of central London
text: The Leonard Hotel is a little hidden gem of central London, located just round the corner from Oxford Street and Hyde Park. Hotel has a warm and welcoming décor, full of old English charm and character. Friendly reception staff willing to help with any request you may have. Those of you who have stayed in central London hotels before will know that you can’t expect too much space from a standard double room. However, my colleagues and I were pleasantly surprised to find the rooms at the Leonard to be very spacious. The Deluxe room had an enormous bed (with a very comfortable mattress I must add!) as well as a lovely "relaxing area" with a sofa. The Suite was larger than I expected, not only did it have a separate lounge area, it also had a dining area and a huge bathroom. To sum this up – great hotel! I will (and have already) recommend it to my friends and colleagues. Very well priced for what it offers. p.s. I didn’t have a chance to sample a breakfast there myself but I've been told that it was just as good as everything else at the Leonard.

title: Great stay
text: Excellent hotel close to Hyde Park and Marble Arch station. Nice and calm area, good restaurant nearby and for shopping you have Oxford street around the corner. The staff is friendly and always have a smile 😃 Good rooms, plenty of space and big bathroom. Beds are okay, and a good breakfast Recommend

title: Location, location, location
text: Great location for Marble Arch / Oxford Street / Marylebone. Hotel a little tired in the communal areas, but room was great (we were in a classic double on the top floor). Very friendly and helpful staff.

title: excellent hotel
text: We really loved the location-2 minutes from Marble Arch underground and just off Oxford St. The recption staff were exceptionally staff. There was a porter to bring our bags up. The breakfast was served in a beautiful dining room , so elegant and relaxing with white table cloths. All orders were taken at the table . No standing in line for anything.Very relaxing experience . Worth every penny. Can see why they had a tripadvisor reward framed at the reception. Will return.

title: Great Hotel.
text: Stayed for three days after Christmas and loved it. If you want well-done traditional, this is the hotel. Got a great rate thru www.travelzoo.com on a standard room and then was upgraded to a deluxe! Deluxe room was huge and included a working gas fireplace. Front desk was very helpful and friendly. Free internet access was a plus. Only negative was the cost of using the phone. Spoke with a friend who was in a hotel five blocks away for 11 minutes and was charged 7 pounds. Travelling alone, I found the area very safe at night. In fact the hotel is on the same block as the police station.
