title: Lovely, relaxing afternoon tea with excellent service
text: I booked afternoon tea through a Groupon offer and received excellent service from start to finish at the Leonard hotel. Excellent selection of cakes and sandwiches, and scones. Lovely, relaxing and cosy environment. We loved the fact we could have unlimited tea (which is not always on offer in some venues) and we were allowed to stay as long as we wanted and enjoy the environment and ambience. We would like to say a very big thank you to Khan who I dealt with from the start and who helped to arrange a surprise little treat for my fiancee, who's birthday we were celebrating. Thank you very much to Khan and your colleagues for making our afternoon tea even more special! Would highly recommend.

title: A much better revisit
text: My wife and I had a bad experience when staying here earlier in the year. I commented to the management and was actually surprised to receive an e mail from the General Manager apologising and asking for us to give them another chance. We had cause to stay in London this weekend and decided to give them another try. we had a deluxe room which was excellent spacious air con and very clean. The breakfast was excellent and the staff were all very friendly. The décor could do with a revamp, but that said everything else was great will be going back. Thanks Danny for making our stay a memorable one.

title: Very small room
text: Stayed here last night.Pleasant enough hotel, secured cheap last minute deal on a single room at £76.The site warned the room was small.No exageration there,it was very very small!Nicely furnished,but very noisy with window open due to air conditioning unit of adjoining building.OK for a 1 night stay at £76 but would not wish to pay a penny more. Staff very pleasant and effecient, not a bad location, behind Oxford Street.The rack rates made my eyes water, i would never pay them for this hotel in this location, but at the right rate all in all a nice boutique style hotel.

title: Royal Afternoon Tea
text: Had the Royal Afternoon Tea at The Leonard quirky hotel hidden away behind Selfridges perfect end to a day in London for anyone seeking a little bit of old London and maybe somewhere to go back & stay

title: Great afternoon tea!
text: We went to the Leonard Hotel for an afternoon tea - as we managed to get some vouchers. The service was really nice and friendly. The atmosphere is really cosy and intimate. We had a traditional afternoon tea: the quantities were good, and the sweets were nicely prepared. The only minus was maybe the filling of some sandwiches that a bit "thin" to my eyes. A good experience overall, will recommend it.

title: Lovely English style with great service
text: We had a one bedroom suite which was like an apartment- nice English style. The staff especially Hussein at the front desk made our stay very enjoyable. They were helpful and accommodating (booked our theatre tickets as well). The breakfast was freshly made every day and the homemade jam was amazing! Location was ideal very close to Marble Arch underground station and walking distance to Oxford street. Overall a very enjoyable stay

title: Good Location Good Service
text: The hotel was in realy good location , few mins walk to Oxford Street and Marble Arch tube station. We have booked deluxe room ,the room and bathroom was big , clean , warm and nice , all the facilities were working proparly . The only problem was with the bed . They put 2 single beds together to make one double bed and in the middle of bed was very unconfortable , it was hurting our boddy .As I expalin this to reception they have changed our room to suit room wich was even better than our deluxe room . There was a kitchenette inside of room . We didn't use the kitchenette but it seemed it has plenty of stuf inside .

title: Loved the Leaonard
text: When entering this hotel a feeling of calmness overtook us. The check-in/check out was fast and efficient. The room (we had a suite) was magnificent. The bed linen was superior and the towels very white and fluffly. No shower gel but plenty of shampoos etc. Great shower with good water pressure. Well stocked mini bar at reasonable prices. Public rooms interesting with wealth of pictures, hangings, antique furniture etc. Breakfast was intimate and the food superb. Juicy sausages, thick bacon and fluffy eggs. Coffee in cafetieres and lovely toast. Very quiet hotel, lovely staff and when the barman didn't know what a shandy was, it was treated with humour on both sides. The waiters were attentive and discreet and all the staff seemed happy. We will definitely book this hotel again. It was once of the best we have stayed in and the location for Selfridges and Marble Arch is excellent..

title: Afternoon tea
text: One of the most delightful afternoon tea I've experimented in London so far. Lovely atmosphere, welcoming and warm staff, delicious cakes, scones, pastries, sandwiches and tea of course. Great value for money and I rejoice in going back there soon.

title: If you like traditional style/old world
text: Over all a fine hotel. It is aged which is good and bad. Good because the hotel has a style of old London and charm in many ways. Bad because they need to update and spruce up a few things along the way. The rugs are worn, torn and stained. But can be overlooked. I am not sure I have ever stayed at a hotel that offers so many TV channels - extraordinary. The Wi-Fi is good... The housekeepers are not that welcoming. The front desk staff are certainly fine and friendly. Location is excellent. There are better places to stay and far far worse.

title: Charming boutique hotel right in the city center
text: The service from this friendly hotel staff was excellent. From the front door concierge to the receptionist, they are all young, welcoming, and accommodating. We stayed here several times and had very positive experience. The rooms are comfortable and decorated in traditional European/English decors with updated bathrooms. The hotel is walking distance from the Marble Arch station and close to shopping, restaurants, cafes, and pubs. Is a nice home base for a short London stay. Thanks guys for a great stay!

title: Good visit to a nice hotel
text: Had booked a double room but got upgraded to a junior suite which was very nice. The hotel is situated in a very convenient location close to an underground station and two minutes walk to Oxford Street.

title: Shabby
text: shabby and not convinient hotel - steps everywhere what is not convinient when you got bags. Would not call it value for money. Liked to have two complimentary bottles of water in the room, breakfast was also good

title: An oasis of calm
text: This hotel scored highly for us on all counts: convenient- a two minute walk from Oxford Street / Marble Arch a peaceful retreat from the bustle of London very friendly staff clean tastefully furnished well equipped rooms (we had a suite so can't comment on standard rooms- it was much cheaper than booking a second room for our teenage daughter) so much more pleasant than the rooms offered by the hotel chains lots of little extras that just added to the experience The only slight annoyance we overheard from some guests was that as the restaurant is very small some people had to wait for a table at breakfast.

title: Good value - as long as it is not the rack rate
text: We have stayed at the Leonard twice in a junior suite. The extra space afforded by having a sitting room as well as a bedroom is great if likely to be spending some time in one's room. It would also be excellent if three are staying as there is a sofa bed in the sitting room. But book well in advance through one of the early booking sites for good value. Go for room only and have breakfast out. There is a slightly worn feel to the rooms and the beds are a bit squashy. Staff very welcoming. Location excellent for the Mayfair and Marble Arch.

title: Afternoon tea
text: We went to Leonard Hotel for an afternoon tea. The hotel itself is quite nice and cosy. I loved the room where tea was served. It had a fireplace which was the best thing on a cold day. The location is perfect as it's just a few min away from the main street. The afternoon tea wasn't great though. The choice of sandwiches was very limited and they were the worst ones I've had so far. The little cakes were not my favourites either. Scones on the other hand were delicious. It was ok but i wouldn't go there for an afternoon tea.

title: A very nice stay!
text: A nice hotel with a perfect location near Marble Arch! I was at The Royal Park Hotel 3 months before, and because of that The Leonard have to be a "number 2" for me. The Leonard was great, but The Royal Park is perfect. Nice hotel, nice, big rooms, great staff.

title: Excellent place.
text: LEONARD Hotel is at an excellent location behind oxford street. The röoms are very nice ...and the bathrooms so beautiful never seen before in the most luxurious hotels. The management has taken care to give every amenity in the room you can think off. Location is marvellous. Reception staff was very helpful. Would love to stay here again.

title: Good Location for Shopping and Siteseeing
text: Stayed here with my two daughters in a junior suite. Rooms very clean and bathroom. Staff very helpful, had breakfast one morning, quite expensive when service charge added, but seems the norm for London. Would stay there again as location was great for tube, shopping Oxford Street and siteseeing.

title: A beautiful place to stay!
text: I just got home after a short visit to London and my third year of staying at The Leonard. It is a hotel just a couple of blocks off of Oxford St at Marble Arch. Very convenient to the busses and Tube, and yet it's on a quiet street. The staff are all very friendly and accommodating and the rooms are all different and cozy. It is more like staying at a bed and breakfast, yet you're in the heart of the city. Seymour's, the restaurant tucked inside, is warm and inviting and offers all meals as well as an afternoon tea. There is also a bar. I visit London at least once a year and I have stayed in many other hotels, but I don't think I will stay anywhere other than the Leonard!

title: Warm and homely stay
text: Excellent location if you want to be right next to Oxford street and still be far away from the crowds. Very helpful and friendly staff. Warm, comfortable hotel. Hotel rooms are small and in room dining menu has limited choices.

title: poor and tired
text: for my pounds I was expecting more.The room looked fatigued and tired and uncared for It was minuscule, next to the elevator. The only things opulent was the mini bar which did not interest me whatsoever. The mattress had springs I could feel so I had to use the coverlet as a blanket since there was no extra blanket in the room as there was no space to put it, it was that tiny. The entrance looked good and the staff was friendly but a good inviting night they do not make. I felt short changed for my 124 pouns.

title: Very beautiful
text: The place is just magnificent, cozy and a home away from home. The make over is a totally different outlook from my first visit. Just simply elegant and friendly. A home for the kids when on holiday. Especial position for shopping on Oxford. This is just shop till you drop.

title: Lovely stay at the St Leonard
text: We stayed just one night at The Leonard but were delighted with the hotel despite the quirkiness of the internal architecture viz uneven and creaky floors! Very courteous staff. We had a suite (bedroom, lounge with bed settee and kitchenette & bathroom) and on a very cold night it was very snug. We were at the front of the hotel but were not disturbed by traffic noise. Lovely large fluffy white towels and all the shampoo etc one could possibly need. What a brilliant position - just two blocks away from M&S & Selfridges and three minutes to Marble Arch tube. Our thirteen year old particularly liked the front door being opened as he left and returned by the two porters! Yes it's a bit tired in places but good value - I'll be back! Thank you St Leonard.

title: Comfortable Stay & Great Location for Shopping
text: The hotel is located Seymour street, very near to the Oxford Street and the Edgware Road. The nearest tube is Marble Arch (Central Line). I stayed for 2 wonderful nights. I love the room and location. My room is at 5th floor, the lift is only up to 4th floor, so if you carry a big luggage, make sure you get some help from the butler. Checking in and out was very quick. I particularly love the lobby, very cosy and warm after a long tiring and wet day. They serve free delicious cookies at the reception desk and you can eat them all you want :p For Muslims, there are plenty of halal restaurants along the Edgware Road and it is not far from the hotel. Wifi is not free and my room was without breakfast. The hotel is perfect if shopping is your main agenda in London. Anyways, Marble Arch station is just around the corner, and i find it easier to travel anywhere using the tube. Apart from WIFI is not free, this hotel is very comfortable to stay and it is conveniently located in shopping area.

title: Dinner
text: Victorian style hotel, beautiful for who likes the style. Lovely quite dinner, very good food, very good steak compliments to the chef. Excellent customer service by Khan and Samona, thank you. We would return again.

title: A pleasure
text: Just perfect! I'd like to see more places like that. Very cheap for the comfort and the location near a beautiful known park. Th not so far museum of natural history gave me the scientific end of trip that I needed. God save the queen!!!!

title: Good Hotel within reach of Heathrow
text: we arrived and given a room without fridge,(required for medication) moved to another with fridge but carpet was .well lets say had seen better days. The Manager went above and beyond call of duty and moved fridge to another excellent room, Thank you Enjoyed our stay, restaurant excellent

title: Excellent Traditional London Hotel
text: I booked this hotel as part of a surprise weekend for my partner's birthday. I managed to get a good deal from Travel Zoo, and communication from the hotel was very good. The Leonard is in a quiet road just off Marble Arch so very central to everything. The hotel is very traditional in design and furnishings so makes for a relaxing break. Upon arrival we checked in and were advised we had been upgraded to a suite which was lovely, 2 bedrooms, 1 luxurious bathroom, together with a living room and kitchen diner! The hotel was lovely and quiet, we didn't mind the creaky floorboards at all and the bed was very comfortable. If you are in a hurry for breakfast get up early or leave it until after the rush. We had a ten minute wait in the lounge, which was no problem as there are plenty of papers and magazines to browse. Breakfast was included in our deal but otherwise nearly £20 each for full English. However, it was very tasty with loads of choice. Although the staff didn't rush us I was aware of other guest waiting for tables so perhaps not as relaxing as it could have been. On the plus side we didn't waste any of our day and got out and about at a respectable time. We only stayed one night but we would have been happy to stay several and will certainly return to The Leonard again.

title: Never disappointed!
text: My husband and I plus my sister,daughters and their families have stayed over the years solely in the Leonard.It is extremely well located,minutes from Marble Arch ,Hyde Park etc. The staff are friendly,helpful and remember your name! We travel a lot but believe me the best English breakfast EVER you will be served at the Leonard.I find it a welcoming, warm ,charming place to stay whenever we are in London

title: Nice hotel for an overnight stay
text: We just stayed the one night and the hotel was perfect for that. The rooms were nice. Breakfast was really good. Staff very friendly and accommodating. Had to get a public bus to the hotel was a little awkward..

title: Great Hotel In London
text: Great location and atmosphere. Nice, old world hotel. Friendly staff. Large rooms for London. Warm and cozy lobby and bar area. Near the Marble Arch tube so easy to get around London. Comfortable rooms, if not a bit dated, but did have new flat screen TV. Elevator a bit scary (it's old). Food was average and very pricey. Better bets around the neighborhood (excellent Egyptian food a few blocks up).

title: Home away from home...
text: Great location, moments of Selfridges, Oxford Street, Marble Arch tube and Hyde Park. Highly recommended not only for families but also for business travelers. Great value for money, although in the heart of the busy city the Hotel is an oasis of relax and quietness. I enjoyed the professionalism of the staff and their will to make the most of the guests stay.

title: A unique hotel!
text: This is a beautiful place to stay when in London. The room was big and lovely. Breakfast was served in an amazing room which was like from another era.The hotel's location is really central, it's very close to Bond Street.

title: Just Great
text: We spent two nights over the weekend at this hotel. From start to finish we could not fault the staff, the location, the food. Particularly the staff who seemingly could just not do enough to help. The location is ideal for Central London with the tube station and Oxford Street buses just around the corner. When staying in London again we will definitely use this hotel again.

title: Outstanding
text: Without doubt one of the best hotels I have ever stayed in while visiting London. Best for several reasons. Such a refreshing change from the ultra modern streamline corporate establishments we have so many off these days. The Leonard is a Boutique hotel. Atmospheric, filled with charm and class. Decorated throughout in traditional style with original period features and array of antique art work. The rooms are outstanding. Complementary water in room. All amenities including tea/coffee and biscuits as well as flat screen TV. Warm, friendly efficient staff who do their upmost to make your stay an enjoyable experience. I would highly recommend breakfast. Plenty to choose from including healthy options. Very hearty breakfast which won't disappoint. The hotel is based in the centre of London yet set behind the hustle and bustle of the city in a quite street. A two minute stroll will take you to Marble Arch, Hyde Park, Bond street and Regents street where the designer shops await you. The theatre district is 10 minutes walk. A perfect hotel in a perfect location for anyone visiting London. Highly recommended.

title: Lovely historic boutique hotel in great location
text: We spent 4 nights at this wonderful hotel in Marlebone. The service was exceptional with friendly and helpful staff, the food tasty (although we only ate two meals here), the rooms were comfortable and the decor was charming. The location was excellent, being only a couple blocks away from Marble Arch tube stop on Oxford St., Hyde Park and a good starting point for many a walk around the city, yet it was still very quiet. It was also a short cab ride from Paddington station and hence the Heathrow Express. We highly recommend this gem and will certainly stay here again. Fresh baked cookies for the taking on the concierge desk!

title: We loved the hotel
text: Like they say proper location maketh the difference! The Leonard is located hop, skip and jump from Oxford Street and is a boon to all shopaholics and Oxford and Westend enthusiasists like myself and my family. Located on Seymour street just 4 minutes from Oxford street was ideal for us. We (my wife, my 3 daughters aged 13, 10 and 11 months, my aged mother and me) stayed at The Leonard hotel for 2 weeks between 11 and 26th May 2006 in a 2 bedroom (one large sized and one small sized), a large living room fitted with liveable furniture, nice antiques, a 6 seater dining table, a fully fitted kitchennete, 1 ensuite bathroom, 1 detached bathroom for GBP 200 pounds +VAT per day and we felt that this was money's worth. The staff was very helpful -whether it was the porter who helped us with our 8 heavy suitcases, the room service staff (whether you asked for a bucket of ice, a wine opener, extra cutlery, a baby chair...anything was delivered in a matter of minutes), the receptionists and their managers (always smiling), I think the staff made the difference. Yes I do agree that they could spruce up their maintenance (saw paint peeling off in many areas and the air duct filled with dust and debris) and their housekeeping staff (this is agreeable that tehir housekeeping is not as good as it could be and on more than two occassions we had probelms with the housekeeping staff)...but overall, we loved the hotel and we would stay there again in a wink

title: Lovely hotel, great location
text: Great hotel. Stayed for one night on business and staff were super attentive and had a small suite at a good price for the quality and location. An NCP is very near (although £45 overnight) and I'd certainly stay here again.

title: The quirkiest room ever!
text: To tell you the truth I don't have too much to say about the hotel as I was always into my room and then directly out. The position is perfect, one minute from Oxford street yet still quiet and peaceful. As many people have mentioned before me the hotel is a bit worn down but perhaps in a weird way this is part of the charm....My room, yes my room (17 if I remember correctly) was the quirkiest room I have ever seen but I loved it! The stairs lead directly into the room (yep, private stairs, one and a half flights worth directly into the room. Separate wc as you enter with hanging chains instead of a door and then a couple more steps up to the room with a shower in the actual room. Although it was a bit worn down it was clean and fresh. Loved it! Highly recommend for fit single travelers.

title: Old world charm & service
text: We stayed in the guest suite for 3 nights. They were very accommodating to all requests and very prompt. They provided us a cot for the toddler and were happy to heat up his milk for us even though we weren't dining in the restaurant.

title: Great English Breakfast
text: We stayed at the Leonard for a night . The room we booked was clean but small, typical of London hotels. The floor arrangement / plan was like a maze. This hotel is a 3 minute walk from Oxford street and Marble Arch. They have a late (up to 10:30 pm) room dining service.They have a bar and restaurant which serves very good English breakfast : sausage , poached eggs, baked beans , toast , bacon . the staff were very kind and helpful .

title: Great Location for tourists, good value for money!
text: This Hotel is a very good hotel with reasonable prices, for London. We have stayed for one night at the 5th floor, and the fact that the lift does up to the 4th floor, and then you have to use the stairs did not bother us at all. The room was big enough with enough facilities for its star rating. It was also clean, and the decoration, although it is not my style, was very interesting. The big plus of this hotel, is its staff

title: Excellent location
text: Very quiet, good night sleep, but still in the heart of everything. Just a few steps from Oxford Street, Marble Arch tube station, restaurants and shopping. Staff is friendly and service-minded. Breakfast very good. Rooms are OK -average level, but location really excellent.

title: disturbing incident with staff
text: Rooms were ok, but it's a hassle getting to the top floor as elevator doesn't go up that high. I had a very disturbing incident with a night manager: he barged into our room about 10:30 PM without knocking. I was getting ready for bed and was undressed. He tried to explain why he was there...made no sense (as I'm standing there trying to cover myself). I called down to the front desk and received only an "I'm sorry." Talked with manager the next morning who promised to look into it...didn't hear back from him before we left the next day. When emailed after our return, he merely apologized. I will never stay here again, nor will I recommed it to anyone. The staff is obviously not trained in proper hotel etiquette, at least as far as US standards go.

title: New Year's Eve 2012
text: Nice and clean rooms ...although on small side ...staff helpful an friendly ...service received good...dinning room was busy on mornings some people having to wait for tables clearing...but excellent breakfast couldn't fault it....would return again

title: Good small hotel
text: When we travel we always look for hotels that have breakfast included and this was one of the hotels that had that option. However, they served the same thing every day which was tiring after 5 days. Room was small and clean. It had a fridge and blow dryer. Staff was friendly, however we had to call few times to order a taxi to pick us up from the airport. But overall good hotel with friendly staff.

title: Tiny rooms, basic facilities with poor maintenance
text: We stayed twice at this hotel - once for a week in August and the second time for a week in September - the rooms are very tiny - no space between the bed and the wall to even open a suitcase. Showers stalls are extremely tiny with no space to keep your soaps or shampoos. The lift was not operational for more than two days during our stay in September. Buffet Breakfast is served in a congested dining area in the basement - the limited choice for breakfast is set off by excellent service from the staff who are very attentive, and remembered my choice of bread everyday. During our August stay - London was facing a sweltering summer - and the rooms with poor ventilation were unbearably hot. The hotel provided a small fan and an air cooler which basically recirculated hot air in the room. The room windows only opened two inches and didn’t provide suitable ventilation. The only thing going for this hotel is it’s central location. Apart from the excellent staff in the dining area, the management & front office of the hotel don’t seem to care for the hotel guests- the narrow hotel corridors are congested by cleared garbage and fresh towels and sheets left carelessly right in the middle of the corridors. Although our group booking was made by Thomas Cook, and we gave the hotel a lot of room bookings for over two weeks. They were totally inflexible in offering us even a single courtesy room for 4 hours for four of us who had to depart later in the afternoon on a long international flight. I hope Thomas Cook takes this hotel off their list of approved hotels - this is an overpriced hotel with poor maintenance meant for backpackers but sold to business travellers and touring families - most of the room doors need to be slammed shut due to the poor maintenance.

title: Bad service
text: We stayed for 4 nights in what we think was a single room al though we booked a double room and the bed was in so bad condition with a big whole in the middle ,we complained at once and they promised to change our bed or room the next day but nothing happen,then we complained again the next day but still nothing happens,also the third day we try again but it was the same results. One of the mornings we was served 2 pots of cold coffee,and when we told the servants the didn't even bother to change our cups we have to do it our self.Only positive thing was the lokation near Paddington station and the weather those 4 days.peter@10mb.dk

title: No complaints
text: Reading other reviews on here I’d thought I stayed at a different hotel?! I was given room 002 in basement which worried me to start with as I hate basement rooms, this was modern, looks like it was recently refurbished. Comfy bed, excellent aircon, there was a heatwave and my room felt like a fridge. Perfect. Lovely modern bathroom with powerful shower. My only slight complaint would be to have a chair in the room but probably not enough space. Big tv, fridge, coffee naming facilities etc Location is great, nice area. Staff were wonderful, particularly the girl with the headscarf who checked me in. Breakfast was very busy and is only continental, didn’t like the look of the sausages and eggs but plenty of cereal, toast and juices.

title: Had to abandon
text: We visited in what was I admit a heatwave but the twin room was the smallest twin I had ever seen, it was stifling hot, no air conditioning (apart from a portable thing that actually super heated the air). If there was a breeze outside you would be lucky to benefit from it as the only window is restricted in opening to just a few inches Have a look at the cupboard they call room 203 to see for yourself I have to say that the only other thing that I can compare it to was a sleeper train across Italy and France which was awful. The staff seem fine and the hotel is not their fault.

title: Nice small hotel in a great location
text: The hotel is small but clean and nice. Although it is quite basic, you still have everything needed and the room (and bathroom) were clean. The breakfast was also nice but nothing special. The staff was friendly and the location is super (near to the parks and Paddington station). The only really negative thing was that as it was very hot in London during our stay, the room was also too hot.

title: Location, location
text: As a low cost hotel well situated in London, the Brunel has a lot going for it. The location is a couple of hundred metres from Paddington Station - ideal for the Heathrow Express airport link. The room was very small, but adequately equipped. Staff were friendly and breakfast in the basement cafe was excellent. Unlike some other low-cost properties this one does have a lift, albeit a tiny one. I'd happily stay there again if in London on a bidget.

title: horrible hotel
text: The hotel rooms are very dirty, old and extremely small. My partner and I couldn't even stand at the same time and couldn't even find room for our luggage. The window was broken, the air clima control that they write about in their presentation is an old fan. They also said that it would be minibar in the hotel room which it wasn't. Will never stay here again!

title: Location
text: If you are a tourist and don't want to spend your time in a hotel room this is a place for you. Room was very very small (just bed and a small table) and so bathroom with the shower, but it was clear. What is the best about this hotel is the location. It is just 100m from Paddington station on the Circle line which can take you to all the sights in London and there is also the first bus stop of many bus lines so you are the only passenger on the stop and you can take a place right in front of the upper window and have a sightseening tour nearly for free. Yes, it is a little bit noisy place because the hotel stands on the crossroad and above the tube line (so you can hear it while passing under :) but it is not so bed. I think it is a good offer for that money. And if you just want to have a bed and breakfast it is a great place to stay over night. Martin

title: Perfect
text: Best fair priced accommodation I´ve ever had in London! Nice rooms. Fresh towels and cleaning up every day. Friendly service. Avoid rooms in the basement - tube might be heard. Fair rates and good service wanted? This is the place to go!

title: Average hotel
text: This was an average 3 star hotel booked without my choice by a corporate company for a business trip. Location was good near Paddington station. Rooms were tiny with bed occupying most of the room. The bathroom was small with a shower that will suit a thin person only. Breakfast was basic with the essentials. Beware that some rooms require steps to get to as there is a tiny single person lift that doesn’t reach all floors

title: Shame about the poor reviews - renovations finished in 2 weeks time.
text: I wasn't sure about booking as I had read the poor reviews so I emailed them to confirm we would get a nice room. I read that the top ones had already been renovated so we chose one of those. I didn't realise quite how many stairs we'd have to scale but the room was worth it. It was clean, nicely decorated and had a hairdryer and safe which was handy. At first I thought the lights weren't working but it turned out you put your room keycard into a slot which activates the electricity. The lift was not in use due to the final renovations downstairs. The staff explained there's only 2 weeks to go and all the rooms will be finished with lift back in use. With this in mind, I will definitely stay here again. It has nearby both Paddington and Lancaster Gate Underground stations which was great. Also very close to Hyde Park if you fancy a stroll. Plenty shops and restaurants nearby. Staff were professional and friendly. Breakfast was fine for our taste. Coffee/tea and toast are brought to your table then the rest is help yourself. Chipolata sausages, poached or scrambled eggs. Crossants or chunky bread you cut yourself. Fruit Salad, pieces of fruit, yoghurts, cereal, cheese, tomatoes, fruit juice, spreads/sauces, other stuff but I didn't take it all in as I knew what I wanted. All in all, we enjoyed our stay and for the price we paid, I'd say we got a bargain. We shall definitely book here again.

title: Avoid this hotel
text: Please avoid this hotel if you can. The rooms were absolutely tiny and were visibly filthy. It's incredibly noisy being on the junction of two major roads too. The staff were actually quite friendly as I requested a change in room but they are all the same. It's cheap, but unhygenic and I would not recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Nice little hotel.
text: Really easy to find from the centre of London, 20 minute from marble arch and about 40 mins from Buckingham. The staff where really Nice, helpful. Had my room upgraded from a double to a double/twin. Lots of room, clean and very comfy beds. The breakfast was very nice with alot of choice, fresh fruit salade, pastry, cereal, yougurt, ham cheese and some cooked food. Nice hotel, good location would def book again

title: Below average
text: In the basement bed hardly fitted the room. Shabby, grubby, noisey, need I go on! What shock me most was Thier insistence that they photocopied my credit card after they had taken payment??? Needless to say that didn't happen. They also insisted they copied my driving licence, armed with them two documents, the mind boggles! I stay at five or six hotels per month in the UK, never have I encountered such an outrageous demand?? Needless to say I won't be returning!

title: They took off the curtains!
text: The hotel is simple but clean and organized. Everything was fine until, in our last day, they just took off the curtains of our room, leaving us with a huge window, in front of the street. They said they do that every 6 months for cleaning. Except for this unacceptable inconvenience, the hotel would be ok.

If this place has a complete makeover I would definitely stay here again, but until then...

title: Was much more better than I expected....
text: I stayed in Brunel in the beginning of July 2008. After reading all these reviews here I could say I was a bit nervous! Location is perfect, staff is friendly, even very friendly ( they will find an answer to all your questions no matter what Your gonna ask ) and helpful and for that mony it is perfect place! After all you dont go to London to spend all time in the hotel, aren´t You?! Yes, there were problems with elevator and breakfast wasnt the best one, but still its not a 5 star hotel, so dont expect anything super. Its a normal hotel for a person who wants to stay in the centre of town with low budget. And all these reviews about the cleanness and staff beeing unpolite -totally wrong!! At least my room was totally clean - and I was staying in standard room.... So, if you have booked a budget hotel then I´ll think theres no need to complain after even if you had some problems! I can totally reccomend it!!

title: Fabulous location with a great buffet breakfast!
text: Great location, not far from Paddington station or Hyde Park! Very friendly & helpful staff! Breakfast buffet was always excellent with very quick & efficient service. Room very tiny, which I understand is normal for London, but clean & tidy, with tea, coffee & biscuits provided daily. However, more hanging rails are needed in the bathroom to hang up hand towels. I would definitely stay here again & I would recommend it to friends & family!

title: Would book again
text: I stayed at The Brunel Hotel for three nights with a friend in September 2017. We took the bus from Stansted, and the hotel was only a short walk from the busstop, which was nice as we arrived late and left very early. The hotel is also close to Paddington station, which will take you pretty much anywhere in London. The reception is open all the time, even during the night, and even though we arrived in the middle of the night, the man at the front desk was very friendly and made us fell very welcome. The rooms are small but nice. It's clean and nicely decorated, there's a Tv (which we didn't turn on, but it was there), cookies and tea that you can have if you want to. Breakfast is fine and includes bread, yoghurt, cereal products, fruit, scrambled eggs and sausages. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Don't stay here
text: I stayed here 2 separate nights on my way to and from Rome. The only thing it has going for it is location. Other than that, it's a terrible hotel. The lobby area is a smoking area. On my first day there, I didn't notice it (i guess there weren't alot of people smoking that day). However, when I went to check in on my second stay there, I was overwhelmed by the cigarette smoke in the lobby and I started coughing and felt like I was choking (I have allergies). I even had to step outside in the middle of signing my reciept cause I couldn't take it. When I told the man at the desk that the smoke smell was bothering me, he just looked at me like I was the weird one and said nothing. I had a single room which was so small. You could feel the springs in the bed. The first night the sheets looked clean. On the second stay, they didn't look like they were changed. I slept on the top cover. The bathroom was tiny even by european standards. The fan in the bathroom was loud and didn't do anything to clear the steam. It was only May and the room was so hot. I had to sleep with the window open which was on a street side. Didn't sleep well either night. I left early in the morning both days so never had breakfast. If you like hostels, I guess you wouldn't mind this place. I know that I will never stay here again.

title: The basement experience continues with another traveler
text: Oh dear, the basement story continues with another poor unsuspecting customer. Basing my booking on well angled photographs of a popular hotel booking site, the name itself, and the location we selected a twin room for three nights. A lift that has seen better days struggled with just one person and two bags groaning under the strain. Hoping to be dragged upwards we were unfortunately delivered in the opposite direction to a pitiful cramped room deep in the basement with little light and comfort. To me a twin room means two people with at least two bags each so at least give us some space to move around and store our bags. And to top this there was only one plug socket. So a twin room means two people with at least two devices each to charge, you get my drift. So where do we plug in the fan and where do we put it? Forget trying to iron at the same time. Breakfast okay but not nice in the basement. Sorry would never stay here again. I hope the other rooms are better! Great location for Paddington and tube but I would gladly walk further for a better hotel!

title: Close to Paddington Station
text: This hotel is quite close to Paddington Station, just a 4 minute walk away. Room rates are quite affordable compared to other hotels in London. However, these are all advantages this hotel can offer. The doubleroom I got was very tiny and in desperate need of decoration. Staff was not unfriendly, but far away from beeing nice as well. Continental breakfast was ok. If you do not expect that much and just would like to have an affordable bed for one night close to Paddington Station this hotel might be an option. It was not that bad that I would never stay there again.

title: Excellent location
text: + Hotel is very well located in Bayswater. + under 5 minutes walk from Paddington Station + Several convenient stores around the hotel + Rooms are spacious and clean + Free Oyster card was great + Great value for money Cant fault the hotel

title: Dungeons
text: When I booked I wasn't expecting to be put in a very small room in the basement, the room was smaller than my kitchen and that included the shower room which was the same size as my cloakroom. The bedroom had two beds each against the wall with a gap of 12 ins between them. The wardrobe was about 15ins wide and 4ft. High. The plus was it had a kettle tea and coffee . And the bathroom provided shampoo and shower gel. I must say the beds were comfortable.

title: Worst staying ever
text: It was the worst experience I even had in a hotel. The first day they gave us a room at the basement (which was not mentioned in the hotel cite). We demanded to change room and the second day they gave us a renovated room on the 2nd floor. The breakfast was awful with 3 hot dishes, cheese and cherry tomatoes. The cleaning was terrible too. The towels had an awful smell like they had been stored for a long time. In addition, we were robbed by 50 euros from the suitcase in our room and at the same day my credit card account was charged with the amount of 420 euros while it was in the same suitcase in my room. Protect yourselves and never visit that hotel!

title: Certainly nothing special
text: Room was about 10C hotter than outside temperature and the fan provided was rubbish. That's pretty much enough to make anything else irrelevant although the decor and beds were fine. Bathroom tiny but all clean enough. Breakfast not worth bothering about. Very expensive for what it was, but then it was a busy weekend in the city... wifi didn't work either.

title: Good holiday
text: Overall was a pleasent stay. Excellent, supported, kind reciptionest. Kind resturant staff. Left going to the rooms in levels1, 2&3 only and level 4 you halve to use stairs,, left is very small where it occupy only 2people of wieght 150kg total, bags as well may be requied to be taken one by one. Room is very small.and rest room.

title: Awful
text: Very scarce breakfast which doesn`t change even a bit any day. But main surprise was a room in a basement level (this wasn`t mentioned while booking on a hotel site) with old interiors, extreme small windows and square about 15 m2.

title: Not again in this lifetime!
text: First of all the address is misleading. The Hotel is NOT on Gloucester Terrace. It is on Craven. We walked from Paddington Station with our bags and couldn't find the hotel until we asked a taxi driver. Whlie the lobby is very nice (and air conditioned) the room was VERY small, VERY hot, and VERY much not worth the money. It was the most expensive room in which I stayed over my week's visit to Great Britain and was least worth the money. Although we had intended to pay cash everywhere we stayed (and did everywhere else), the Brunel took the liberty of charging the credit card with which I had secured the reservation via an online booking service for the first night of our stay before I arrived. WiFi was 5 pounds per day. Use of a computer was 2 pounds per half hour. There were 4 (sometimes 5) channels from which to choose on the small, outdated television set. The best thing about the staff was that they ignored you unless questioned directly

title: Good location, small room - missing jewellery!
text: The location was good, rooms were very small but clean. We stayed before and after a trip overseas and they stored our luggage. Very disappointing though as I left jewellery (2 bangles) in the bathroom and as soon as I realised called the hotel. I regret not going back to the hotel when I realised...After waiting 1 day for a call back, I was told they weren't there. I am 100% certain they were left in the bathroom (and have triple checked my bag to be sure) but unfortunately was told they weren't found - very disappointing!!!

title: First time in London!
text: Nice outside and reception view, but very small and dirty rooms, wasn't possible to move in 4 inside it or open the wardrobe's door without move the bed away. Very defective and noisy lift, and for the 4° floor you had to go upstairs by walking bringing your suitcase by yourself. Staff was very helpful but unkind, we had to greet first otherwise they didn't greet us, the breakfast service wasn't bad but you had to pay an extra supplement for typical english breakfast, it's a little bit of shame because if you plan a trip to London you expect english breakfast to be a standard!....

title: very small
text: The hotel is right next to Paddington station. And that is maybe the best thing about it. I stayed 5 nights with my son in a very small room. There was no place for the suitcase so we had to left it next to the bed. The room was clean and the toilet also very small. Breakfast is ok no more.

title: Good,basic hotel
text: Stayed 2 nights in this hotel. The hotel was an easy,level walk less than 10 minutes from Paddington Station .Our room was small and pretty basic but also clean and the staff were friendly and helpful. The continental breakfast was good and there was plenty of it for £5. We didn't try the full english breakfast but it looked good. There's a small room to leave bags if you don't want to drag them around with you after you check out. While we were staying at the hotel we went to a concert at Wembley Stadium and used Brevet cab company based in Wembley to take us back to the hotel. They provided an excellent service even phoning us after the gig to make sure we could find our way to the pick-up point.

title: Jo-Ann G
text: This hotel was booked as part of a package deal. I booked weekend trip with my son, staying two nights in single rooms. I read the reviews and was concerned about the number of complaints about noise and in particular noise from kitchen in the basement rooms. I therefore sent an email prior to visit explaining that I have a noise aversion due mainly to cancer treatment both in the past and now presently and asked to be placed in a quiet room and definitely not in the basement. I received a reply that this would be accommodated. We arrived at hotel at 7pm after a very tiring day and although the rooms were very small and outdated they were clean and beds seemed comfortable which is good enough for me. Unfortunately I was wakened at 8am by very loud music and at first I was not aware of where it was coming from. At breakfast I found out it was from the restaurant and kitchen and the speakers were in the ceilings and my room was directly above. I asked at reception if I could be moved and was advised that there were no other single rooms available apart from one and it was beside the lift and it would be worse. I didn't want to go from bad to worse but I explained my concern was that the next day breakfast was to start at 7am and I did not want to be woken even earlier. The receptionist said she would speak to kitchen staff to turn music off and would also mention my complaint to the manager. I was satisfied with this, until 7am the next morning when I was again woken by music!! I rang reception and after nearly giving up as it took so long for call to be answered I was assured that the music would be turned off. It was turned down but I could still hear it and I was unable to return to sleep. I do not sleep well and when I do manage sleep I hate for it to be disturbed which it was on both mornings at this hotel. The rooms were small but were adequate however if you were a big person the showers would not suit as I could hardly turn round in them. There also was no one to put your shower gel shampoo etc in shower and no towel rail in bathroom. Also the wifi in my room did not work unless you sat at the door of the room though it did work in my sons room. There was a towel rail in his bathroom but no where to put toiletries in shower or bathroom. The staff were friendly and breakfast was sufficient. Location was good only a 5 min walk from Paddington station which had links to everywhere else. If the problem with noise had of been sorted I would consider staying here again but not to be woken twice despite having tried to anticipate this problem before I had arrived.

title: comfort, economy and location, location, location
text: Hotel is quiet, clean, comfortable, with excellent, friendly staff and generous continental breakfast. Being just minutes from Kensington Gardens, it's convenient to that gorgeous park, and a good walker can continue through the equally beautiful and tranquill Hyde Park and Green Park to such destinations as the West End, South Bank, Buckingham Palace, Victoria and Albert Museum and many other attractions. It's also minutes from Paddington Station, and from the Central and District and Circle underground lines. Rooms are compact, but efficiently arranged, with private bathrooms, 7 channels on tv. I've stayed for long periods over several years and always found the same dependable and aggreeable accomodation.

title: Not impressed at all
text: Two Friends and I stayed at this hotel in the febuary half term, as it was cheap and had a tripple room.When We arrived at this hotel I was told i could not pay by Cash and card had to pay by one or the other. We were then given a room on the 1st floor which was absoultly digusting a funny smell in the bathroom ( which was tiny) and in the wardrobe. Costomer service was decent was given a new room on the 4th floor which to be frank was too small for 3 people although was much cleaner but also hotter and the lift wasnt working.. which isint great for 3 girls carrying alot of shoes. I will never return to that awful hotel.

title: I called a week before to cancel and received poor assistance
text: I called a week before my stay to cancel the reservation but the hotel was not very helpful and kept giving me the runaround. They said call Booking.com I called booking.com who said call the hotel. I went back and forth between both parties and both said they could not help me. So what is the point of having customer service if you don't assist customers. So please do not ever reserve a stay at Brunel Hotel they charge your card before you even get there the minute the reservation goes through and there is zero cancellation. This is bad for business if they plan on getting more people to stay at their hotel they might want to adjust this. I only used this hotel because it was beyond cheap but now I know why. Avoid Brunel Hotel at all costs.

title: Clean, friendly staff, efficient
text: The hotel was decent for the money. Upon arrival they couldn't find out confirmation but the issue was quickly resolved. The rooms are small and you can hear everything outside your door. Try to avoid a room on the 4th floor if you have big luggage. The lift only goes to the 3rd floor and then you have to carry all your stuff up a narrow staircase. The location is great, especially if you're taking the Heathrow express (although I would highly suggest taking an unlocked phone and buying a sim at the airport. £20 for 700 minutes and 10GB of data! Then taking an uber to your hotel. You really only pay for convenience/saving time with the heathrow express £74($90) for two round trip tickets to paddington and back) the breakfast was okay. The food is enough to fuel you for the morning but it's not very tasty. We stayed for 4 nights and didn't have any issues. Overall a decent place to stay and would probably come back if I had to.

title: mould in the bathroom
text: We stayed at the Brunel Hotel 18 months ago and was quite impressed, this time however, the stay was a disaster, could not believe how the hotel had deteriorated, stains on all the carpets, the paint work was tatty, and we were put in a 4th floor room, with a filthy bathroom, chipped bath and mould on the ceiling. The beds were hard and worn. We could not sleep because of the couple arguing all night next door, the walls are like paper. Our room looked out on to a grotty back yard one way, and the other, straight into next doors room. The receptionist was quite indifferent. They did offer us another room, but this was worse. Never again.

title: School trip
text: Is an average hotel... the room are tidy and clean, bathroom is very tiny, no frigobar, very good and confortable beds... when we arrived the room wasn't ready, so we changed..... it's near the Paddington's underground... staff was friendly and helpful... clean towels were left in the corridor's floor...

title: Xmas weekend away
text: By London standards it's a cheap and cheerful place to lay your head for a night or two. Little broken in places, for example in particular the en-suite needs some maintenance work as there slot of temporary fixes, but does the job. Breakfast isn't anything to write home about but it's ok.

title: Suited for what it was for
text: Stayed at this hotel to be close to Hyde park, perfect location. For the cost the hotel is decent, breakfast included. Room was small but adequate, clean enough. Staff were friendly and helpful. No complaints here!

title: Below standard
text: Only good point is the relatively close location to Paddington Station. I was given a room in the basement right next to the kitchen. Tiny room and bathroom. Old furniture. Very noisy, both from the road and the kitchen. The room was cold in the morning as the heating is off. Not even the kettle worked. Staff friendly but unhelpful. Price €140 incl breakfast. NOT RECOMMENDED.

title: Location and Budget Friendly
text: I recently stayed at this hotel with my husband.The hotel is easy to find and not far from the Paddington Station. The service staff is nice and helpful. When needing transportation to the local airport the staff was very helpful and gave us a few options for the cheapest way to get to the airport. Downside was the lift only went to the 3rd floor and you have to walk to the 4th floor (which is where our room was). Being 7 months pregnant those stairs are a bit much with luggage. However the room was nice and clean and there wasn't a lot of noise to deal with besides a bit of the road noise. Our hot water had some issues and was quickly fixed. Breakfast was quaint and quick. I thoroughly enjoyed our stay and recommend this to anyone whom wants a centrally located hotel in London. It's a decent walk through Hyde Park to Buckingham Palace and there are several restaurants nearby.

title: We wont be back!
text: We were 2 female friends on a weekend break. We had read the negative reports about this hotel but could find nothing else for the two days we wanted and so booked and decided to keep an open mind. The location cannot be faulted and from the outside the hotel looks just fine, but our room was like a shoebox, old and very shabby. Peeling paint, one plug that could not be used as it was so close to the table top. The bathroom was tiny,dark and had cracked floor tiles that moved when you walked on them. When we turned the shower on there was a small trickle coming from the shower head, it looked as thought it was blocked with limescale. As we were only staying one more night we stuck it out but just wanted to inform potential guests that the awful reviews on here are very right! On our final morning we paid £2.50 more for a full english breakfast, the sausages and tomato were rock solid, and the bacon was some sort of processed meat that was shaped like but certainly not bacon. Before we had drunk our tea the staff were vaccum cleaning the floor around our feet! We have stayed in many London hotels and this was just appalling.

title: Good location for reasonable price
text: I got the newly refurbished room which was very nice. Double bed room is very small, not enough space for two person. In spite I was on the 3rd floor and the restaurant is in the basement, the smell of the toasts and scrambled eggs could be felt. Also the floor is very noisy as only the wood floor is covered with a carpet and it was creaking.

title: Not a bad hotel
text: Stopped whilst briefly working on a commission in London. Ideally situated for Paddington station. My room was recently refurbished and clean. One downside are the windows and you can hear everything outside. So loud it drowned out my neighbors having a good headboard banging session almost. The breakfast is ok apart from the awful sausages. Really friendly staff. Liked the classical music made for a nice atmosphere. Recommended and used it a couple of times

title: Great staff but a poor hotel
text: Firstly I must say that the staff were excellent and the hotel was very clean. Unfortunately everything else was a minus. Very small rooms. We changed after two nights as the walls were very thin and between that and banging doors, we were awake early. The picture went off on our TV after an hour. We had sound but no picture. My side of the bed had protruding springs which hurt to lie on during the night. The bathroom had no more than 18" between the bath and the wall. That 18" accommodated the loo and basin. A squash was an understatement. The wifi went down after the first day and we were without it for the following 3 days. The plug in the second bedroom was installed upside down unbeknown to us with the result that having plugged in my iphone to recharge it and switched on, I had really switched off with the result that the phone was flat for the whole of the next day, so no navigation app. The decor needed a definite spruce up Wish I had spent a bit more and gone to our usual Premier Inn

title: Within walking distance from Paddington Station
text: The hotel is located about 10 min walking distance away from Paddington Station. When going to the airport, I just lugged my luggage to Paddington Station to take Heathrow Express. Very easy to walk along the way, no stair case, with ramps. I was being transferred to another hotel nearby on my first night as the hotel had oversold the rooms. The next day, the hotel arranged transport to send me and my luggage back to Brunel Hotel. The single room I got was very small, under the staircase. For the price I paid, thiss is the downside.

title: First time in London
text: I was in London for a school stage from 16/01/2013 to 20/01/13. The hotel has a great location, close to paddington station and several restaurants. The staff at the reception is helpful, the rooms are very small but clean. We were four males in two double beds and one single, it was very unpleasant. The bathroom was very small.From the windows of the room coudn't keep hot inside. The breakfast was very little and disgusting. In the morning clean towels were left on the floor by house keeping staff: not professional at all The carpet was dirty. The elevator get stucked easy, do not use it. I do not reccomend this hotel.

title: Very dated hotel
text: We stayed here for 3 nights, room very dated, although bedding very clean, fresh towels every day.. Room on ground floor, at front of hotel, can be noisy as traffic goes by.. Breakfast was awful, the scrambled egg was watery and tasteless.. Not much choice at all.. We ended up just having toast and yogurt, plenty tea and coffee offered.. The staff was very helpful and nice.. But, wouldn't stay here again I'm afraid..

title: Seriously Dissapointed
text: Really Wishing I'd checked TripAdvisor before booking this hotel, I booked through a theatre package website and really wished I'd gone for the much cheaper Travelodge option, I was treating my wife to a nice weekend away for her birthday and thought that this place might be nicer given that it was more expensive!! Good points were location and friendliness of two members of staff.Bad points far outweigh I'm afraid.Street noise, hot and cramped room made for two nights very broken sleep, after waiting twenty minutes for a table for breakfast we gave up and went elsewhere, second day only had to wait ten minutes and were then disappointed by the lack of space in the tiny room, (chairs being bumped every time anyone got up) and the snappiness of the staff when they got our drinks order wrong.(One member of staff was quite helpful there though eventually). Back to the room, the kettle lead was coming away from the wall with wires exposed,(did not use it just in case), TV had little or no signal and the WIFI was so slow my 3G phone worked better. Could not move in the room without the floorboards creaking or sit on the bed without it moving. Overall would not stay here again or recommend it.

title: Good Value for Money
text: The room felt bigger due to high ceiling. Great access to Paddington Station and Lancaster Gate Station. Hyde Park is just minutes away. Great services by the hotel staff. Breakfast included. Option for further discount with 'crystal1' promo code.

title: Worth paying more to avoid the Brunel
text: Friends had stayed here and they recommended the location. But when we arrived the room was grubby and the staff curt. Strange how this hotel is always offering deals???? because it has to. For the money I would rather have paid another £30 for a comfortable clean night's sleep.

title: Hated it
text: Stayed here at the spur of the moment after following the world cup through Germany. Did not realise that wimbledon was happening in London and needed to book a hotel a day before arriving in London. Unfortunatley for us because of Wimbledon the Brunel was the only hotel available with a 2 night vacancy. The room was located on the 4th floor and the lift only takes you to the 3rd floor. My partner had to carry our very heavy bags up a steep flight of steps that seemed to be located in a small atic area. The room was small and the bathroom the size of a linen cupboard although the shower worked and the water was hot. The linen was clean and the tv very small. The lock on the door was broken which forced us to put our luggage against the door before we went to sleep at night. We did not have breakfast included. The staff on the front desk seemed friendly and on check out we asked if we could leave our bags in the luggage room for a couple of hours. However we soon changed our minds when we saw the room as it looked like a small outhouse in the backyard with not much room for anything. We retrieved our bags and made a hasty retreat never to return again I promise. At the rate of 65 pounds for the first night and 70 pounds for the second night there are much better rooms available in London.

title: Avoid at all Costs!!!
text: AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!! We had planned to stay 4 nights at this Hotel or should I say Hovel! The rooms were extremely small, the bathrooms dirty and the staff unhelpful to say the least. Air conditioned rooms, no - the windows would not close and the noise was terrible. The doors looked as though they had been broken into and seemed unsafe. When we asked to be moved, they said they were full and could do nothing. We did something - we moved to another Hotel. I would never use this place if it were the only place in London.

title: Oh my god!
text: My family (parents, brother and I (18)) stayed in this hotel for 3 nights and I can say that I would NOT come back for another stay or recommend it. We had expected that the rooms would not be too big, so it was ok and I have to say that everything was clean, BUT the bathroom can not be called room, because it was smaller than a wardrobe!! Water in the shower was hot and everything, but the drain was not really good and one had to wait about half an hour till all the water was gone!!! The double-bed was really VERY small and furniture in general was quite used and a bit shabby. The elevator was old and it took ages to get on - PLUS - one was able to go till the 3rd floor - what about the people on the fourth?? We had to carry up our luggage on this narrow stairs. Breakfast itself was ok, but the room in which it was served was totally HORRIBLE!! No windows, down in the cellar, cold ... one felt like in prison!! The staff was unfriendly and not at all helpful! One had the impression that you should do something for them and not the other way round. As somebody else mentioned in another statement on this hotel, we wanted to leave our luggage in the hotel for some hours, after the check out - the room they showed us was a simple catastrophy!!! Dirty, full of old, damaged stuff ... have not seen anything like this before... One or two good things about it - close to Hyde Park, tube and everything and not noisy during nighttime.

title: Awful - never again
text: I didn't expect a lot from a hotel of this price in London, in fact I just wanted soemwhere to sleep, the small rooms didn't bother me. Upon checking in I was asked if I'd like to pay, said I'd rather pay on checkout, no - they wanted the money up-front, this worried me a little as they had my CC on file from the check-in... anyway, checked in, dropped my bags off and went out for dinner, basic room, but you get what you pay for. Upon returning to my room I noticed that the lift (next to the room) randomly opened and closed every 5-10 minutes, so I was kept awake by the noise and the announcement 'Doors opening', after a very bad nights sleep, I was woken at about 6 to the sounds of the cleaners and (presumably) the breakfast guests, I decided it was time to leave and hopped in the shower to freshen up and prepare for a days work, only the shower didn't work - clearly broken. I debated complaining and breakfast and decided to cut my losses and got something at the station. The worst place I've ever stayed, I'd never go back, un-interested staff.

title: Not where it claims to be.
text: The Brunel is actually on Craven Road, Bayswater, not in Gloucester Terrace as it states on its adverts. The rooms are extremely cramped, and the lift only takes two people, or one person and luggage. Worst of the hotels I used in London by far.

title: Weekend in London
text: Very good and nice small hotel.very clean and with good breakfast.no problems with WiFi.conformable bed.good housekeeping.helpfull staff. Good service.good location in walking distance from Paddington tube station.good connection to busses.

title: First time in London!
text: Brunel hotel is suitable for school trips, great location, central, five minutes from Paddington underground. Rooms were quite clean but very small: bathroom had to be clean a little better, and there was only one power plug in the entire room. We were four males and we had to move as they put us in double bed room. receptionists were unfriendly and the breakfast was short of choise.

title: Never again
text: I don’t normally write reviews, but feel I have to about this hotel. The room was tiny, consumed mainly by 2 beds. The bathroom was ridiculously small

title: Very disappointed
text: The hotel rooms are very dated. Stains on the bedsheets and we were put in a basement room which was tiny!!!! Could hear everything going on from reception including the receptionist scrapping the chair on the floor. Walls extremely thin. Not good if you want a lie in as opposite our room was the breakfast area. Not unless tables to cater for all the hotel had to wait 10 mins both days for a table.

title: So So
text: It will not be my choice again if I have to go back to London. The hotel was just good enough for sleeping over the night but as I said the facilities in the hotel is not very good. I could smell cigarette in the hall way. Practically, I am not impressed with the hotel.

title: Great location, basic and good hotel!
text: i have stayed in this hotel twice and was quite pleased with it. it is located in a very good area, very close to an underground station (Paddington), which is one of the most important things for me, when searching for a hotel. i have to be honest and say that i didn't expect a 5 star hotel when paying a low price, and this hotel is very affordable (another important thing). all i wanted was a good location and a clean room to bath and sleep in, and that's exactly what i've got. the staff is very nice, the rooms are small but comfortable and clean, and the breakfast was not bad at all. all in all - i would definitely return to this hotel, as i already did.

title: Small rooms reflected in the price..
text: The hotel is clean but basic. Our room was on the small size but acceptable. Equipped with personal safe, TV and fridge

title: Excellent Budget Hotel
text: We booked to stay here for 2 nights, we had a do at the Grovesnor Hotel to go to and this place was idealy located for that, yes the rooms are small, but to be honest we weren't coming to London to speand all our time in a hotel room!! there was pleanty of space for my self and my husband and he's 6'3", the room was nicely decorated and very very clean, the staff were so polite and helpful and the whole hotel in general was kept really clean and nice. The breakfast was a littel random and yes the only hot options were scrambled eggs and sausages, but there was also a wide range of breads, croissants, cereals and a very fresh fruit salad, if i'm being honest the worst thing was probably the sausages, I prefer proper meaty, juicy sausages, these were the little cocktail sized sausages that you normally get on the contintent, but there was so much else there that there was no fear of going hungary. The location is fantastic, you are just a short walk away from the beautiful Hyde Park, Paddington station is about a 5 min walk away, Lancaster Gate and Marlybone under ground stations are also with in walking distance. So in summary if you want somewhere clean and pleasant to stay, with very friendly helpful staff but want to keep the cost down then this is a great place to stay, a lot of peole are complaining about the room size and yes they are cosy but to be honest I have stayed in smaller and paid more in London. The bed was very comfy and we had 2 great nights sleep. Would definatley stay here again.

title: Its fine!
text: Good location being close to Paddington and near Hyde Park. I was transferred here as my other hotel was full. My room was spacious and comfortable. Room and beds more like 4* but bathroom let it down a bit, a shade small and not particularly modern, although nice toiletries were provided. Generally speaking this is clean and comfortable. Not much more to say!

title: Unimpressed, not going back
text: If you're put on the 4th floor, there's no lift going that far and the only staircase is tiny and steep. We were in the smallest room - 401 - which had just enough room to edge around a normal double bed. The bathroom was too small to sit on the toilet comfortably, and neither of us was big! It would have been better to do a wet room rather than try to shoehorn in a conventional shower etc. The basin was incredibly awkward, and only provided hot water. The water temperature was either boiling hot or freezing cold, with very little pressure. After all that, the air con unit directly above the bed decided to spew out scalding hot air at around 3am, so hot we had to move out the way to avoid being burned. It took a good 10 mins to sort it out again, not great when it's already really hot outside. As for the wifi, don't bother. You'll be waiting ages. The location is great, but there are better hotels in the area, so we won't be visiting this one again.

title: If you know it, you avoid it
text: We were a group of 12 and visited this hotel fron 29 dec. 2006 till 2 jan. 2007. Only one of the five rooms that whe rent was accettable: the two triple bedded were little also for two bed, and my double (room nr. 101) was a single room with a bed a little more large than a single bed. In another room, water fell from ceiling on the bed, when the guys in the chamber of the superior floor used their shower. The forniture in all the rooms was old and damaged. The bathrooms are absolutely little (and in bad conditions too). The personel unprepared The elevator was constantly out of order.

title: Run away as fast as you can from this property!!!!
text: We were conned into this hotel by our travel agent (whom we have since stopped using). Claustrophobic and cramped room with an airline cramped and tight bathroom. We could touch the opposite walls, it was that small! It was supposed to be a triple room. We had a view of an alley with dustbins! How wonderful. Rude insensitive staff at the reception. Had to go down into the basement for a very mediocre breakfast. The only positive thing about this place was Paddington station which was a 3 minute walk and Hyde Park. We have travelled to more than 17 countries around the world. This is the hotel that nightmares are made of. AVOID this place!

title: Friendly hotel good location
text: The location was very handy, the reception warm and welcoming. The reception staff was extremely helpful and really made our stay. We enjoyed our stay, but the room was quite small and the shower was not very strong. Would stay again if I am in this part of london

title: One to avoid
text: Staff were completely incompetent, had communication problems and were very unhelpful. Our rooms were not available despite booking well in advance. They had contact details for us but failed to give us any notice of a problem. The staff made no genuine apologies and made us wait an hour and a half for a management representative. We were transferred miles away from the venue we were attending and they failed to organise adequate transfers, despite promising this. We were late for our awards night and did not get back until 4.15am (the event finished at 2am). We were then woken at 8am by Brunel hotel staff wanting payment cleared.

title: BE CAREFUL!
text: The great staff on reception, and in the kitchen / breakfast room were the only saving grace during my recent stay. The room I stayed in was unlike any image I could find on the website and was very dirty. Bathroom was filthy. A carpet of hair and dust lined the sink area. The sink was too small to shave in, or brush teeth. Shower was broken as were the tiles that lined it and the furniture. Bedroom Carpet was an ill fitted scrap. Bed Linen was very worn, with stained pillows and a valance that was caked in dust. Mattress was also very dusty and rogue hairs were apparent in the bed too! There was a safe in the room, but wasn't bolted in, so pointless. Windows were old with a fan that didn't close properly thus letting in a harsh draft. And as a parting gift, I awoke on the final morning with red bites on my arms and legs after an itchy nights sleep. Very slow / intermittent wifi. I stayed with 4 colleagues. 2 ended up with bites also from their stay. None would return. Would i recommend? Absolutely not. There are a lot of hotels in London - look around, and don't be caught out by the pictures on the website. They aren't always a reflection of the 'whole' property. The Brunel unfortunately for the nice staff, falls into that category.

title: Nice for a quick visit
text: Came for 2 nights at this place. The guy in the reception. Rana was very welcoming and helpful for the rest of my stay(first time in London) The room was pretty small, but that was no problem for me, just me, kind of expected that. Wifi there, awesome. Great location, easy access to the subway. The breakfast was fine, except the milk which was horribly warm for my cereal. Fine place if youre not looking for some luxury

title: Great value for money in a good location - more than adequate for a brief stopover!
text: This hotel, in my mind, was good value for money. Room was clean, shower ensuite was small but adequate and shower worked well, towels and bed linen really lovely. All mod cons, I guess, squeezed into as small a space as possible but very adequate. We had a family suite, 2 TVs one in the sitting area, the other in front of one of the beds. Would have no problem staying there again on another brief stopover in London for the theatre. A mini cab was arranged for us to get to Piccadilly and was cheaper than the black London cab we came back in. No complaints from us. Oh, yes, there was no sign of mold or damp in our room and there was an air conditioner (portable kind) with external flu on it - we didn't try it out. I suspect the reason there is no double glazing could be due to restrictions on altering the outside of the building...

title: Well placed
text: Stayed here for 3 nights. The hotel is very well placed, and the reception and room were nicely decorated. However our particular room was far too small. The bathroom was decorated nicely but the shower was poor and the hand sink was in the corner and the size of a shoebox, which made it difficult when trying to brush your teeth! The staff were pleasant enough and the breakfast was OK, although the breakfast room is not big enough for the amount of guests. Its situation is great and it states that Lancaster Gate is the nearest tube, however Paddington is probably nearer which gives you a choice of different tube lines.

title: Utterly disgusting not fit to be called a hotel!!!!!!!
text: We actually booked in to this hotel and left after we had gone for dinner and located somewhere decent. It was absolutely gross! The room was the size of our utility cupboard at home, and very smelly. In fact it smelt of poo very badly and the entrance to it smelt of tcp. The bed was tiny, and the mattress filthy. The walls were very dirty, and burnt above the light fitting. The bathroom scared me, and I didn't want to even go in there, but upon inspection it was dirty, cramped and the stink was unbeliveable. Do not stay there!!!! Not fit for my cats, let alone humans!!!
