The buffet breakfast used to be super nice with great varieties of hot and cold food with a great price and smart and nice staffs.But don't understand why recent years the choices of food was reduced and the staffs so robotic-by just keep clearing your table! Ive tried couple of times being cleared the table right after my appetizer!Even cleared everything Ive just put down!And after told them to give me back a new set of cutleries and drinks.They generally gave a long face back to me!! And,the quality of the toilet and tissue paper was poor!Alots of dark spots and some wood residues were seen clearly!I felt not so comfortable to wipe it on the skin. That's why I always bring my own toilet roll if stay in this htl! Can I claim the money back for the toilet amenities?

title: Quality London hotel
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times over the past 3 years whilst attending courses. If I had been choosing a leisure hotel in London I would look elsewhere as I got a discounted rate as a conference customer. That said, there are many lovely things about this hotel. It's very clean, I've always been given a spacious room, the lobby has a nice spacious feel to it and room service food was good and for which there was no extra service charge. This year though, I felt the menus both for restaurant dining and room service were more limited which was difficult as I did need to eat in the hotel most nights. If you are taking a leisure break though, Hammersmith is just a 5 min walk away has lots of venues for eating, plus a number of highstreet shops including M & S, Boots etc so is a convenient location. The buffet breakfast is wonderful, one of the best I've had. There is a hot buffet, fresh fruit, yoghurts, pastries, cheeses, breads - all of it fresh and tasty. Expensive though if you don't get it included in a booking deal. If you are on a breakfast inclusive you can also get room service breakfast at no extra charge which is good. I liked this hotel but I would be choosy about how much I paid to stay here . The location is about 5 - 10 mins from the tube so you can use it as a good base for sight seeing and also have the convenience of the town locally.

title: Fine hotel...except for the internet (or lack thereof)
text: I stayed in this hotel almost a week. It’s a basic business hotel. Here are the pros and cons. I’ll come to the internet in a minute: – Nice lobby/bar – Stark/boring rooms (no art or charm). – The rooms have plenty of space, but no drawers to put your things. You’ll be living out of your suitcase. – Confortable Bed – Stained carpets in the room, although it was clean – Friendly staff – Good breakfast, which is quite helpful if you're on the go. It's probably the hotel's best feature, along with it's location if you have business in the Hammersmith area. The issue is the internet. Internet is offered in two forms. The first is a wireless internet, provided by a big British telecom called Orange. The signal didn’t reach my room. I called them up to get a router placed near my room. They told me quite directly that they couldn't be bothered. As for the ethernet internet offered in the rooms, which is offered by a different provider – it’s quite slow and often stops for 5 to 15 minutes at a time. If you want to use Skype, forget it. Not only can’t you use video, but often you can’t use audio. Also, if you were to try and send someone a file of, let's say, 5mb, you might not even be able to. And as I mentioned, the internet service would frequently stop all together. The manager told me that they’re stuck with their current internet service until some time in 2013. This order has come down from the hotel owners (Accord) in France. He was quite frustrated by the situation. He provided me my own conference room so I could make Skype calls – but the wifi in that room was also to slow for Skype. In summary, I've stayed in hotels that were better and I've stayed in hotels that were worse.

title: Good Value in Hammersmith
text: Booked several months ago, as we had tickets for Hammersmith Apollo If you do this it's a great option (rack rate is high) Breakfast was excellent good cooked selection and also continental Room clean and comfortable

title: unstable water temperature in the bathroom...etc
text: I've stayed in Novotel London West Hotel for 6 nights 1. The water in the bathroom sometimes becomes very hot and scalded my skin. 2. There seem to be no slippers in the room. 3. Bottled water is ONLY available on the first day when you check-in. 4. Breakfest is NOT nice and varied at all. 4.

title: It's Good
text: Hotel is in a good location (tube, bus station, & TESCO ). Employees were professional in general. However, there was no one to carry the luggage to the room. The food was good. The room was nice & clean.

title: Lovely!!!!!
text: Flew over from Jersey for a gig at The Apollo so stayed here for the one night. What a lovely hotel. Friendly staff,clean rooms and comfy beds!!!! The breakfast is mahoosive........eat all you can buffet!!! I will definately stay here again as its so close the The Apollo and across the road from the bus and train station so very easy to get around. We will be back!!!! Thank you x

title: Perfect for a business trip
text: I stayed in this hotel during my business trip to London in Feb 2018. The hotel is huge. Those who look for natural English authenticity will most probably hardly like it. But its really convenient. Everything is on a large scale here, and the hotel is strongly associated with business activities. Room was quite spacious, all necessary equipment available: power socket above the bedside cabinet (really important for me), small refrigerator, safe, tea kettle, iron. There is a small fitness center. Wide variety of food for breakfast. Self check out is available. Infrastructure around the hotel is rich and convenient. London tube is just couple of minutes walk, and its Hammersmith, several lines junction (Including Picadilly line which can be used to get to/from Heathrow)

title: A great base for wide range of activities
text: I didn't know this part of London well but as Hammersmith is on the direct tubeline from Heathrow I decided to try this hotel on a recent visit to London. From the outside it's not the most prepossessing place but the accommodation was excellent and a great range of foodis offered at breakfast. The hotel is a 5 min walk from the underground and has 3 bus routes to the centre of London nearby. We walked to the Albert Hall and to Fulham Palace (well worth a visit) and there are a large number of ethnic restaurants nearby. Would be happy to go back anytime.

title: good price excellent service!
text: I was in this hotel a week ago for three nights with my familiy and a couple of friends with 2 kids. The hotel is absolutely new and comfortable, (very beautiful decorations for Christmas, also!) cleaning was absolutely accurate, comfortable beds and bathroom and delicious, well cooked and well served breakfast ( by the way for the 4 children the breakfast was offered by the hotel). I want to spend some more words about the hotel staff: they were very very kind and helpful with us and withthe children and helped us a lot. The Hotel was barely full ,I think , but all was managed smoothly and I was very happy for the perfect silence during the night (few months ago we had a bad experience in a business hotel in Dublin, very noisy)...a few steps from Hammersmith tube, absolutely recommended!

title: Never again will we use Novotel
text: I would like to start by saying that over the past 10 years my wife and I have used Novotel in various countries around the world and even had our wedding reception in a Novotel. We travel a lot for both business and pleasure and this was probably the worst experience of a 4* hotel we have ever had and we have stayed in a lot of hotels! From arrival through to departure, we were made to feel like nothing in this hotel. Service was shocking, the hotel room poor and the layout of the hotel left you lost with no one to assist most of the time. As we planned to be in Hammersmith for an event on our second night we decided to stay at the hotel as it was a short walk to the venue and a quick taxi ride into the city for dinner on the first. With parking, this was ideal. Whilst they advised that parking was available for a charge, we were surprised to see find out on arrival it was going to cost an additional 75.00 for just over 2 days’ worth of parking (Charging 3.50 per hour I believe). On top of the 450 for two nights in an executive room this was a little hard to believe as there was no indication on the website of the fairly significant cost. Being a public carpark, residents receive a small discount to the list price when paying at reception. We pull into what we believe is the reception area to get our bags out of the car (it is also the entrance to the carpark). Two staff walking around dealing with bags, but obviously too busy to assist me with our 3 bags. My wife took the car to parking and I struggled into reception with the bags. First desk, sign to advise they had just popped away and will be back shortly. Looking around, finally see a member of staff who tells me I’m in the wrong place and need to go to the first floor. Strange that he watched me walk in and stand next to the desk for a minute or two and only when I walked round like I was completely lost did they point it out to me. Get to reception eventually with bags still in tow. Que for the 1 receptionist that seems to be doing anything and eventually get to the lady. Who then proceeds to walk off and deal with someone else???? Trying to work out if they want our business, someone finally comes and registers us by which time my wife has parked and found me waiting and enlightens me to the cost of the car park. Checked in, we head to our room, still dragging our bags. To say it is an executive room is a disgrace, the room was poor although there was a little space which was nice in what was a very dated room (they are in the process of updating rooms). Having spent some time travelling, we need a shower. My wife goes first and on coming out warns me the shower seems to be playing up. So with this advice I take a shower and sure enough, the water runs at a normal temperature for 32 seconds then goes scalding hot, then cold then back to normal for another 32 seconds. Yes, I did count the time as I really needed a shower and just kept having to try and dodge getting scalded. I would also like to say this is the shower in a bath and there was no shower mat so very easy to have slipped… We were heading out for dinner so went to reception and advised of the fault and would someone kindly fix it or move us to another room so we don’t get burnt. To which we were told it would be fixed before our return around 10 to 11pm later that evening. After having a lovely evening, we returned to reception and asked if the shower had been fixed and to my amazement, we honestly got the following response: “How would I know, the shift’s changed? You will find out if it has been fixed when you have a shower in the morning.” I would like to point out that only 3 weeks earlier the headlines in the national press were about a certain hotel chain that had lost a lawsuit for the death of a resident after being scalded in a shower. Go figure, I guess hotel chains don’t take these things seriously or the profit from us mere customers is enough to cover the cost of the occasional death by negligence lawsuit???? Anyway, true to form the shower wasn’t fixed so down to reception in the morning to speak to a manager or supervisor or anyone that gave a damn! Nope, no one in sight. Reception were very apologetic and advised a maintenance person would be with us shortly and that the duty manager was busy and despite advising we will be there for another 24 hours and would like to speak to someone about this, were advised, they are always busy so won’t be able to assist us. The maintenance man turned up and was apologetic having worked out the thermostat had broken and the shower was dangerous so we would need another room for the remainder of our stay. He advised he would tell reception straight away and get us moved. We came down with him to reception to confirm the move and were told if we would like to go back to the room, someone will be with us in 15 minutes to move the bags 1.5 hours later and several calls, what looked like a cleaner with a laundry basket turned up to move us. Despite being told they would move us, he was sent without any room keys which we had to go and get from reception. Something we had asked when we were at reception and told no, they would move us. Move to one of the newly renovated rooms which to be honest was a lot smarter than the original but felt much more cramped due to a table and chairs and again practically nothing in the room you would associate with an executive room??? Surprisingly they didn’t even offer to upgrade us but since when has customer service been a priority in this hotel? Good news is the shower and bathroom was all new so no need to climb into a bath to get burnt. Generally, the hotel felt like it was just playing host to lots of conferences and general guests were a bit of a nuisance. The bar was in the middle of an open plan lobby area so really noisy later on in the evening and difficult to get served drinks or beverages (tea or coffee) as this is the only place open to get anything when you get back from a night out. We were unfortunately there when there was a rowdy conference so couldn’t even get into the bar at 10.30pm. In the morning when I went to the smoking area, you could see where the cleaners had simply left broken glass under the chairs in the smoking area from the night before and even pointing this out to reception, there was still broken glass on the floor in the area when we checked out 2 hours later. I am guessing from other upset guests we meet just waiting at reception the multiple times we were there

title: clean modern hotel
text: We stayed here for one night as part of a short break to London, the hotel is bright , modern & clean, we found the staff to be efficient , pleasant & helpful, the rooms are a good size & well presented , we were a party of 2 adults & two children (11 + 5) we had a double bed , with a very adequate sofa-bed for the kids, the room more than met our needs. The buffet breakfast had a larger than normal selection that I imagine would cater to most peoples tastes, the only small niggle is I found some of the hot items to be a bit undercooked, but in general very good. As for the location of the hotel ,it is a fair way out of the centre but the nearest tube station is an easy 5 minute walk and we found no problem with it. The exterior of the hotel is a bit nondescript & is set back from the road, you get to the main entrance via a flight of steps or a ramp you then cross a plaza to the hotel, this area lets the hotel down as it is not in a good state of repair, they have tried to make the area by the doorway more attractive but in all it does let down what is an above average hotel down, this said I would recommend it & would use it again myself.

title: Typical Novotel room and as I didn't have to pay :-)
text: Located very close to a metrostation you can get here quite fast from LHR and the city centre, very busy hotel, lots of places around where you can have meals, shopping area close by, this being London I never expect much

title: Do not stay here
text: I recently stayed here with two other adults. We had booked and paid for a triple room and as such expecting 3 single beds. We arrived in the room to find a queen size bed and one sofa bed and not enough room to open a suitcase. We enquired at reception as to the availability of a triple room as booked and was told that their family room was a triple room. We then had the dilemma as to how to work the sleeping arrangements as we had three adults, none of whom had shared a bed before. The staff were completely uninterested in our dilemma and refused point blank to move us to another room. On enquiring re the cost of taking a further room, we soon realised that we had paid a premium price through our wholesaler in Australia and paying more money was not an option. One concession the hotel did make was to offer to store our baggage in the baggage bay in the basement, we were on the 5th floor. I believe this situation is completely inappropriate and I would not advise anyone to stay here if they need a triple room.

title: Brilliant front desk staff!! Very helpful!!
text: We were thrilled with the wonderful service at Novotel London West. Nice spacious room. Great wifi!! Front desk staff was efficient and very helpful. Nice location in the greater London area. Only s few minutes by taxi to central London attractions. Conveniently located within walking distance to many great pubs, etc. We started our European vacation here with Cosmos and extended our stay here for two extra nights when we returned to London. Loved it!! We plan to return again!

title: Busy bar and restaurant
text: I ate and drank here with colleagues the bar was busy and service a bit slow but it was OK the staff were working flat out it wasn't there fault there was not enough of them. Menu varied staff professional and helpful. Happy to revisit.

title: Surprisngly good location
text: Stayed for weekend for the Proms and Book of Mormon. Walked to and from Albert Hall from hotel

title: Good Hotel with great location !
text: I stayed here for 4 nights and I enjoyed my stay, The check in staff were friendly and thorough as they let me check in early because I had arrived in London very early in the morning. My room was tidy and clean had a good size bathroom, My bed was comfortable. The buffet breakfast was included and had a great selection. The location of this Hotel is really good not all that far from London Central using the tube and the hotel is within walking distance of many Pubs, Restaurants, Shops and very close to transport 3-5 minute walk to Hammersmith station and buses if you go via the shortcut which is hard to describe in words so just ask either at reception or the baggage handler as you walk in trust me you will save 5-10 minutes if you go the shortcut route. Also if you intend to keep fit ask the reception about their Gym as they give you a different card for that, The gym is very well equipped. Overall my stay here was great and I would stay here again, Plus I will recommend staying here to my family and friends !!

title: Very good value for money
text: We were a family of four staying for four nights. The hotel has a good location and offers very good value for money for holidaymakers. Visitors are a mix of tourists and business people. Large, nice rooms, especially for London. Very good breakfast buffet. Wireless Internet in room was fast, but I would have been even more satisfied if wifi was included. This hotel is a large, but smooth operation.

title: Location good, everything else mediocre
text: Like a lot of other reviewers, I chose this hotel because I was going to a concert at the Hammersmith Apollo. The location was great for that - easy walking distance. I would probably not stay there again though. I stayed with a friend and we checked in separately. When I got there, my friend had already checked in. When the front desk checked me in, it completely invalidated my friend's electronic room keys. Front desk people seemed very distracted during check-in and check-out, even though there were no other guests waiting. The air conditioning dripped to the point that a spot in the carpet directly underneath the unit was soaked and squishy by the time we checked out. The shower/tub floor was elevated several inches above the bathroom floor, with a very high tub wall, and nothing on the shower wall inside to hang onto. Made getting out very precarious. On the good side: gift shop was nice, concierge was very helpful (front desk was not even helpful in pointing out where the concierge was located) and the location was great for my purposes. On the whole though, not at all worth the money.

title: Loved the Novotel London West in Hammersmith
text: I recently stayed at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith. The building itself is new and modern, and my double room was very large, very comfortable, and very clean. The white walls reflected the natural and electric light giving the room a kind of cheeriness. It's about a five-minute walk from the hotel to the Hammersmith underground station, where you can take either the District Line, the Piccadilly Line, or the Hammersmith & City line to virtually anywhere in the central London area. If in the future I visit London again, I will definitely stay at the Novotel London West.

title: Good location for westfield and central london!
text: Stayed here back in August. Was pretty good for access to central London (with several tube options since Hammersmith has 2 separate stations!) The hotel was nice and comfortable and nice since we had an executive room! Unfortunately we only had one bathrobe and were celebrating my girlfriends graduation, we rang reception several times to have another one delivered and this didn't materialise till fairly late on! (which was a bit of a shame, only thing stopping a 5* review) Breakfast was decent too with plenty of selection. There's also two restaurants, a decent bar and even a little shop Overall a decent stay and likely to use again if need somewhere to stay in London!

title: Very nice
text: Overall very nice hotel. Staff were pleasant especially Emmanuel on the front desk who was very helpful. The hotel is clean and modern and the food is ok (the mushroom tortellini is fantastic). The bar has a nice atmosphere and there is also a small shop which is handy. Cons: The heating seems to get turned up quite high late at night making the cold drinks in the minibar seem a lot more appealing, adding approx £15 onto my bill for just a few cans of britvic. So it might be a good idea to open the windows before bed!

title: Nice hotel in great location
text: I stayed in this hotel for one night, attracted by the proximity to the tube station. As I would be flying to and from Heathrow, and would be spending most of my time in Central London, the proximity to the Piccadilly Line is ideal (it's only about a 5 minute walk to Hammersmith tube station). This is a massive hotel. There must be well over 500 rooms. But it never felt busy - perhaps it was a quiet weekend, although with the Wimbledon Finals and various other major events in London that weekend, I can't really imagine that being the case. The concierge service is fantastic. Check in was really simple and I didn't have to wait long at all. I was given a room on the 8th floor, overlooking the courtyard behind. I was really impressed how quiet this hotel in the heart of West London was, particularly being adjacent to a major road junction and under the approach paths to Heathrow airport. I had a fantastic nights sleep on a comfortable bed. It is a huge chain of hotels, so the room is rather generically designed. But the facilities were above average. The free wi-fi was excellent (you can pay for premium wi-fi, but the free internet was still more than functional). The television was good. The bed was very comfortable, and there was plenty of space in the Superior Room (which I think is the most basic room offered in this particular branch, despite the name). Price was on a par with similar hotels in London. On the down side, the room did feel a bit tired in places and the plug next to my bed wasn't working. I also felt that breakfast was a bit overpriced at £17.50 for what seemed to be a very generic hotel breakfast - I didn't partake. There are plenty of places nearby where you can get a much cheaper breakfast. I also resented being awoken at 8am on Sunday morning by housekeeping - sure I should have probably put the "Do Not Disturb" sign up, but 8am on a Sunday seems a bit early! But I'd certainly return. It is in a fantastic location for most of London via the tube, and is particularly ideal if you're flying into Heathrow.

title: Good hotel in a decent location
text: In general this is the standard Novotel hotel. There are 9 floors so if you are lucky, you can get a good view of the city centre. The service is OK meaning the reception desk, maintenance, restaurant and bar. The hotel is huge so it takes a while to get to the reception if you have a room quite far away from the lifts. When it comes to lifts there quite a few of them, so at first glance you have no idea where to go when you leave them. Next to the lift there is an ice machine so a good option if you want to have a good time in your room. One thing that really surprised me is that for the three consecutive days there was a stripe of paper lying on the sixth floor and despite being passed by housekeeping staff it had not been picked up. The bar staff really friendly and breakfast rich in choice. You can actually get a variety of food if you are selective. There is a subway station just 5 minutes from the hotel. There is also a car park underneath the hotel yet this is really pricey. For hotel guests they charge 1.50 pounds for one hour so it makes 36 for a night. We found a decent private car park for 29 pounds for 2 nights nearby (just use the skills to find it). The air conditioning was working perfectly if you like mild conditions. All in all a good and safe location with accessible amenities around with not high prices.

title: Worst night sleep ever
text: For £275 we got a double room with air con that would blow out only hot air... a rock hard bed and if we open the window the noise of the main road below. I am a bit of a fussy sleeper but even my partner struggled and she can fall asleep in the floor normally

title: Perfect for Eventim Apollo
text: This was our first stay at a Novotel, and we found it to be a slick operation, where quality counts for something. The reason for our stay was to see Kate Bush, at the Eventim Apollo, which is literally 5 minutes walk away. Check in was easy, and we found our room had a king sized bed, topped with a memory foam mattress, which as anyone who has slept on one will know, is very comfortable. There was the usual small LCD TV, which worked fine but kept on defaulting back to an enticement to buy paid channels. The room included basic free wi-fi, but again extra payment was required for more extensive service. The bathroom was excellent, aside from the choice of a flimsy door with opaque glass panels, which cut down on privacy. A small issue which we believe is it be addressed. The bathroom also boasted a small speaker in the ceiling, which was handy for keeping up with whatever was on the TV. Despite being in the middle of a very urban area, the room's triple glazing kept things very quiet indeed, and we could not hear anything going on at street level. Hotel food is at London prices, which may seem excessive to those who live elsewhere, but we were tempted to a pre-gig meal, which turned out to be the best bar food we'd eaten in a long while. As it should be for the cost. The service was friendly, fast and efficient. For wine lovers, the Pino Grigio here is better quality stuff, At no point did we feel rushed, and the surroundings in the bar area were nicely open with plenty of space between seating. After the gig we walked back to the hotel, a trip which felt quite safe despite the late hour. The two available routes are both well lit, and for most of the way are in plain view of other travellers. The next morning I was slightly confused at check out, due to the bill apparently being £50 more than I had expected. Until I was politely informed that this charge is automatically levied when guests check in, to cover extras. The charge is taken off if no extras were added to the bill. Novotel is a cut above, and a classic example of getting what you pay for. It isn't cheap, but as we were attending a once in a lifetime event, we thought it worth the small luxuries provided by booking an executive suite.

title: Our second time here
text: We stayed at this hotel on an earlier visit to London in 2010 and were very impressed. Things did not start so well this time. A few days before arrival I received an email offering a room upgrade "from 15 pounds per day". Apparently they have some system called "eStandby Upgrade" which I sincerely hope is not becoming a standard at all Accor properties. One of the attractions of silver Le club Accor membership is the possibility of a COMPLIMENTARY upgrade, which has happened on numerous occasions over the years including (ironically) at this very hotel back in 2010, but most certainly not on this occasion. Our Superior room was typical Novotel with a comfortable bed and a rather dated bathroom with shower over a ( quite slippery) bath. The sign in the bathroom said " bathmats are available" and we quickly got one. Breakfast was of an excellent standard and the busy area was very efficiently organized and maintained. The bar was a pleasant place for a drink and some nibbles despite the building work going on outside. The hotel is an easy walk to the train and bus stations and is a great place to base yourself when exploring London. In summary, a good mid range hotel with a great location and breakfast, but this business of Accor "selling" upgrades is quite concerning.

title: Good Value
text: We stayed here 3 nights as our tour left from this hotel. Rooms were comfy and beds spacious. Restaurant for meals was good value and breakfast was big and a huge selection Close to transport which made it easy to get into the city and only 30minute walk to Kensington Staff were helpful, however more knowledge on the bus system and Oyster cards would have helped us immensely

title: Novotel in Hammersmith
text: This hotel is a compromise if you don't want to stay around the airport or in central London. It is located approximately half way between the city centre and the airport, so it will take you approximately 20 minutes to get to central London for sightseeing, eating out etc. The hotel itself offered a very good room with a great view from the top floor. We twice had a problem with the room safe but it was resolved swiftly. The bed was good and we even had a Nespresso machine in our room. The lobby bar is alright but lacks atmosphere. The breakfast was fine, altough a bit pricey. One can always go to Hammersmith Broadway, where you find a variety of breakfast options (3-4 minute walk). Finally, there are 4-5 excellent riverside pubs just minutes away from the hotel. You can also go for a nice walk along the river all the way to Chiswick if you feel like.

title: Excellent value, great location
text: The room was a little tight, but the service was good, the room clean and modern and the value excellent. The buffet breakfast was a highlight also! Location wise it is excellent, with a 2 x min walk to the local tube station within zone 2 and restaurants are also within walking distance, as are shops and the local theatre. Highly recommended

title: I was taught to sit at the table!
text: Having been appalled at a previous hotel / meeting complex serving up their wonderful lunch without a single table and chair available - you can imagine my disdain when this occurred again - this time at the Novotel! Why do London hotels think it's acceptable to serve lunch like this! Do we have to pay extra for the tables and chairs !!!!! Idiocy.

title: adequate
text: I stayed at this hotel for the easter weekend with my 11 year old son, the hotel was ok for a short stay, the rooms were cleaned every day and bedding and towels changed. The view from our room was poor to say the least, it just looked out onto a lower level flat roof with a variety of different metal vents, ducts and that sort of thing on it. The breakfasts were ok and for £15 each they should be, with hindsight I'd have prefered to have gone to a restaurant, I'm sure I'd have got better value for my £30.
