title: loved the london town hotel
text: My 12 year old son and I were on a fixed budget and needed a clean place to stay in London that was reasonably priced and close to the tube station.We booked a twin room and were very happy with it. It was clean, bright and cheerful, a good size, had a nice bathroom and a decent continental breakfast. The room was also well heated(it snowed when we were there!) very quiet and the staff were nice. I had read other reviews about this hotel on trip advisor before we left and all I can say is some people may expect to much for what they are paying.

title: A great welcome to London!
text: I arrived early in the morning and came straight to the hotel to drop my bags off as I knew I wouldn't be able to access the room then. I checked in, the night porter told me where to put my bags and I was able to use the wifi too. Night porter wasn't very friendly but then the next lady came in to take over and saw me sitting on the ground using my laptop and let me know where the guest lounge was with couches... thanks for telling me night porter lol! Bags were in my room when I came back after a day of sightseeing and the room was everything I needed - a bed, ensuite with a nice hot shower with good pressure and a tv to provide background noise. Bed was very comfy and hotel generally very quiet. Breakfast was ok - cereals and tinned fruit and coffee... you had to ask for toast which I found out AFTER I had eaten my cereal - a sign would be helpful. Would definitely come back - great hotel, great location.

title: Third time at this hotel
text: I have stayed here three times now and can only say that it is a basic hotel with small but clean rooms. The breakfast and internet connections are both good and the location is perfect only a couple of mintues from the tube. Very helpful and friendly staff. They have a lounge that compensates for smallness of the rooms.

title: DISCRACE
text: very thin walls u can hear everything,dirty matress,towels and sheet never changed,rude personell,tiny smelly rooms and the list is endlese stay away for your sake

title: Great Location lovely hotel
text: Spent 9 days at this hotel and enjoyed my stay. Rooms are a little small for 3 people but they are clean and safe. Lovely lounge on the first floor. Staff were friendly and very helpful. The location of this hotel was great pop around the corner and you are at Earls Court station with access to the District and Piccadilly lines. Lots of pubs and restaurants in the area. Nice neighborhood to walk around. Tesco located within walking distance.

title: Value for money
text: This hotel is very good value for money compared with other London hotels that I have stayed at. Very polite and effective staff. Good breakfast, No traffic noise. Good choice if you are on a quick visit to London and are not looking for top class luxury. Tube station just round the corner and reasonable resaurants nearby.

title: Lovely Hotel
text: We had a lovely comfortable stay in room 205. Everything from check in to check out was 100%. All staff were very helpful and friendly. Plenty to eat at breakfast.A 2 minute walk to the high street, tube and buses. Looking forward to staying again on our next visit to London.

title: Very convenient location and good quality/price ratio
text: Best At only 100 m from the earls court underground station but in a very quiet street Clean and nice double room with convenient bathroom Good continental breakfast Nice staff Least You could be disturbed by noisy neighbours because of not very well insulated walls between rooms (but this risk exists quite everywhere)

title: My Dirty Bed!
text: Two friends and I came in from Italy and didnt arive at the hotel until near midnight, when we had setteled in and about to go to bed to my Horror my bed sheets where so disgusting I started freeking out. There were stains on the top bed cover when you turned it over and when I pulled back the sheet there was alot of dirt and hairs, I have photos to prove it! So at around 2am I went to compain no chance would I sleep in that and it was a bit earlie in the morining to look for another hotel. I told the night porter it was a discrase and I wanted new sheets, it was well I wasnt cold I only got a sheet, he didnt seem to care. I complained in the morning to the receptionest who said the sheets were changed EVERY DAY, dirt dosnt just get there by itself, the sheets were not changed from the last person, horrible! I enformed her we would be back by 1pm to change, then the cleaning staff said they were about to go in and when we returned, angry as I was I told her I had enformed the receptionest she continued to moan so I closed the door. (We returned for 10min) lack of communication & not listening to your paying customer. The top sheet was still dirty but seen no point in complaining as nothing was getting done about it. A bottle remained under my bed for my stay that was not our's, not to much cleaning done and not checked regulary by manager. The breakfast was awful, at 8.30am there was no where to sit, the boiled eggs were cold and so over cooked so it was toast, an apple or a choice of two cerials no English Breakfast in site but would forigners no how to make it? Dissipointed as I work in the Hospitality area.

title: Will stay there again!
text: This is a low cost hotel so definitely don't expect luxury. However, from my experience it obviously has good management - everything was very clean, well stocked and well looked after. The staff were welcoming, smiling and helpful. The location is a two-minute walk from Earls Court underground station with both the District and Piccadilly underground lines. There are plenty of supermarkets, places to eat and pubs close by. The continental breakfast was plain and simple. In fact, I found it better than other hotels of the same grade. I liked the fact that there were camomile teabags as well as the usual tea or coffee, a plentiful supply of bananas or tinned peaches, and also yogurt. Here again the service was excellent. There is a lounge on the first floor with a kettle so you can make your own tea or coffee at other times. It was lovely to sprawl here at the end of the day or just make cup of tea and bring it back to my room. Again the camomile or peppermint teabags were appreciated. As you can see from their website, the rooms have phone, TV and hairdryers. Basic toiletries are provided but remember to bring a shower cap if you need one. Like everything else, the bathroom was basic but very clean and my shower had good power. And now for the negatives! As you will read in other reviews, rooms at the front of the hotel get noise from passersby/revellers (experienced by my travelling companion), there are thin walls between the rooms, and the noise of doors closing can be loud. I had a room at the back, stayed for four nights and only had noisy neighbours on the last night. My advice if you're a light sleeper is (1) definitely ask for a room at the back of the building and (2) keep an iPod under the pillow and listen to something relaxing to get you back to sleep if you're woken! I am a light sleeper but I'll definitely stay there again. I liked the caring atmosphere created by the staff.

title: Really unsure
text: Seemed more like a B&B than a hotel. Arrival was odd, I was asked to provide photo ID and a credit card, both of which were photocopied. I am quite well traveled but as a UK citizen I have never experienced this at home before. The door to the room was so narrow that I had to walk through sideways and the room itself was tiny. No tea and coffe in the room but apparently there was a coffee lounge for guests on the first floor. I didn’t have breakfast.

title: Excellent price-performance ratio
text: I booked one night at the London Town Hotel on a short notice for a business trip. I found the experience to be mostly very positive: * The staff was exceptionally courteous and helpful * The room was small but very clean and cleverly furnished so that it was possible to work at the desk for a few hours * The internet connection was very fast * The breakfast was satisfactory * The location near the Earl's Court tube station was very convenient Executive summary: a more than adequate stay for a very attractive price - especially for London - with very friendly staff as a pleasantly surprising bonus.

title: Cozy, quiet, and convenient
text: A lovely hotel centrally located in the Earl's Court area. Just minutes from the Earl's Court tube, you have everything (restaurants, convenience stores, and things to see) right at your doorstep. The hotel staff are all very nice and the rooms are kept very clean.

title: Great location and friendly staff
text: I stayed at the hotel on two occasions as part of my Olympic Volunteer duties in London (stayed for 1 night and 16 nights) I found the room size fine as was in there on my own, staff were all great, friendly, helpful and always happy to help. Location was great for everything as was based in Earls Court for my volunteer role, just round the corner from the underground to get anywhere in London. Would recommend and defo go again if back in London for another visit in the future.

title: Pleasing!
text: I stayed here five nights. Staff were always helpful. Free tea and coffee available. Internet I had to pay for, and did not always get my money's worth. Breakfast was not a great range, but I was always satisfied. My room faced the main street, and it was clean, and nice. Not big, but as I was on my own, it suited me very well. I was very happy with my stay here. Location was brilliant - tube round the corner, bus stop round the other corner, fast food, pubs, bank, post office, etc all round the corner. Everything was in close range. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Not my first choice next time
text: The hotel was well located at Earls Court station. The cleaning was good. The staff was very nice. The rooms were very poorly soundproofed. One could hear conversations and snoring from several adjacent rooms, and much creaking of the floor above. It was also a drawback as a tourist that the breakfast was finished early. Was also ukonfortabel that there was no fire drawings and that it was not tight around the fire doors out to the only staircase.

title: Family weekend break in London
text: We have really enjoyed our stay in this hotel. Location was very central and easy to get to. The staff were very friendly and helpful, and the buffet breakfasts were lovely.The only slight negative was our bed was very hard, but I do have a back problem so may have felt it was harder than other people might find it. We would love to stay here again, and have already recommended it to other family members.

title: Nice Little Hotel
text: Me and my friend stayed here during our trip to London for her birthday. At first we were kind of wary, especially after reading reviews of how old and cramped London hotels can be. However, we were pleasantly surprised when we turned our key and found a cute, cozy room waiting for us. Now mind you, the room was definitely small by American standards, but we had already mentally prepared for that so it was no big deal. We checked in close to midnight, but didn't have any problems doing so. And, they have a LIFT!!! The next morning, we went down to the breakfast room and had our choice of cereals, yogurt, fruit, sliced cheese, boiled eggs and toast. My advice is to fill up on the eggs, cheese and toast - it will get you thru most of the day. The staff was very friendly and the neighborhood was quiet, yet very close to the tube station. At one point during our trip, we checked out to stay with a friend and also to travel to Amsterdam. We knew immediately that we wanted to stay at this hotel for our last night in London. We requested our old room (on the top floor), and when we returned to check in, not only had they held our old room, they also offered us a room on the ground floor instead so we would have to take our bags upstairs. Needless to say, we took the ground floor room! The staff was helpful and courteous. And don't worry about leaving your bags at the hotel if you have to go out of town. We uses both secure and unsecure storage and didn't have any problems.

title: Fair quality & rates, close to tube station
text: The hotel is just 4 mins walk from the tube station (Earl's Court, use Warwick road exit). The room was fair, and the equipment was correct, with a new TV and phone set. There is no sound nor thermal insulation, so just pray for the next room to stay quiet during the night... The bathroom was clean, but very cold as there is no heating and it was December. The girl at the desk was smiling and very open to provide informations on the city. The breakfast has a quite low choice of items, but good french croissants. Breakfast maids were very nice and tried to do her best to please the customers. There is a computer in the lounge for the hosts, but its use is not free. Lots of hotels in the same quiet street.

title: Decent Budget Hotel
text: The London Town Hotel is a budget hotel and is located on Penywern Road which is 50 feet west of the Earls Court Tube Station. To find the hotel, exit the station via the Earls Court Road exit and then turn right. Take the first road on the right (Penywern Road). The Hotel is on the left side of the road, 1/4 of the way down. There are several hotels on this street and they all kind of look the same. Earls Court tube station is only 45 minutes from Heathrow Airport on the Piccadilly Line. The place was full as the Chelsea Flower Show was going on while we were there. I stayed in a triple room (one double bed and one twin bed) with my wife and youngest daughter for 5 nights in late May and generally liked it. It is a budget, 3 star hotel and we paid 155 Pounds per night plus tax. We had a basement room near the breakfast area. I liked the location as it was close to the Underground and we were able to go anywhere in London we wanted without any trouble. The hotel was in a quiet location and I did not hear any noise from the street. The hotel Reception Staff were very efficient and friendly. I felt very safe in this area but I did not really walk around after 11 PM (so I am not sure what the area is like late at night). This location had a lot of restaurants close by on Earls Court Road to choose from. Our room rate included a free breakfast but we really liked the nearby French bakery (Paul’s) and we ate there every day except for one. It is just across the street from the underground station Overall I enjoyed staying at this decent budget hotel as we saved a lot of money and it was close to a convenient tube station. My only complaint was the bathroom. The shower was very small and the bathroom light switch and the fan did not work properly (no main light one night and I could not turn the fan off on another night). If you are expecting a luxury hotel, in a fancy part of London, this is not the place for you. If you are OK with a clean, budget hotel then I recommend this place.

title: Mixed Bag
text: First, I want to be clear, I have stayed in much worse places for more money. This Hotel is your typical London Budget hotel but it does have some nice features. The Location is great and the Staff is really friendly and nice. It is small and the beds are less comfortable than I would like, but I knew this beforehand given the price of the room. There were two issues that really did bother me though. I didn’t like the fact you didn’t have control of the heat in your room during the daytime. It switched on at 630 pm. I was sick in my room and froze during the day. Maybe it’s just me, but I think if you pay for a room you should be able to heat it anytime you are in. The other issue is slightly more delicate so I won’t go into great detail here but the Hotel took it upon themselves to block a certain kind of content from the WIFI Network. I really don’t believe a hotel should have the right to do this without some kind of notification beforehand. I couldn’t very well go down and complain to the nice lady at the desk. Overall, there are better options in that price range but in a pinch, it’s much better than some places maybe even most places.

title: The worst hotel ever
text: London Town hotel is the worst and the most overpriced hotel that I have ever stayed in. It felt more like a hostel than a 2 stars hotel. A toilet in my room didn't flush properly – you had to pull it ca 20 times each time you used it, to make it flush. When I complained about it, I got a response from the reception girls that "there is no problem at all. We had the men to check it out and they said it was OK, considering it was a very old building." I found their response insulting, like they were implying that I was imagining problems. The problems with the toilet flush continued for days, until I asked for another room. In another room they offered me, the toilet flush worked, but there was a curious notice from the manager on the bathroom wall, saying: "Important warning. Please make sure that the shower curtain is in its tracks all the time." I examined the shower curtain closely and it looked fine, so I moved to that room. I discovered what was wrong with the shower cabin the very first time I tried to take a shower. The shower was fixed to the wall at such an angle that when you turned on the water and tried to fix the right temperature, the water sprayed right onto you, standing in front of the shower cabin, and on the toilet seat behind you. I guess the idea of the manager who put that notice on the wall was that a guest should enter the shower cabin, close the shower curtain, and then wait and endure a few minutes of cold water running over him/her, until it warms up. How very considerate and kind advice, thank you very much, manager, but I don't think so. Then there was no hot milk available for my breakfast cereals for a couple of days, because the microwave in hotel's kitchen didn't work. Then I found a hole in the towel I was using, as well as a long black hair (I am blonde), and it all made me feel very sick.

title: Good place to stay
text: We stayed for 6 nights recently and found the Hotel clean and comfortable. the rooms are small but as we were out all day sightseeing it was good. Our room was at the back of the building so no street noise. Breakfast was good and there are plenty of Pubs and fastfood places to get meals. Earls court tube station is just around the corner and bus stops close by. we found the staff to be friendly and helpful. one night we had some loud tv noise from the room next door, we spoke to the desk staff and had no other problems after.would stay here again.

title: A great find!
text: I booked this hotel in a hurry for a last minute trip. Thankfully I was pleasantly surprised. The staff wade me feel welcome and were happy to help me with my many questions. I was given a room on the lower floor, before seeing it I was a little worried. However the room was exactly as I had seen in the pictures and the bathroom was new. No complaints from me. The was not a great view but that didn't matter for me as I was out all day.

title: Excelent staying
text: I felt very satisfied having stayed here...clean and comfortable room...the hotel is very quite at night for good sleeping..., good location (only 100mt from tube station)...the staff is both friendly and helpful...and reasonable price...I highly reccommend this place... Sergio (Argentina)

title: a very cozy and familiar hotel
text: I stayed at London Town Hotel for a few days and from the beginning i found it very cozy and familiar. The staff was so friendly and very helpful. I had an ensuite single room, a bit small , but very clean

title: A Great base in London
text: I've stayed at this hotel twice now, once in 2007 and once in 2009. I can def say that its probably been the best overall hotel in London that Ive stayed in. Its a short stroll to Earls Court tube station, which is located on the Picadilly Line (very handy if you are coming in from Heathrow) its close to pubs, shoprs, fast food outlets, ATM's, post office and a few cafes. And its only a short train ride (or pleasant 30min walk to Westminster, Buckingham Palace etc) The hotel itself is well presented, the rooms are not huge by any stretch of the imagination but they are also a bit bigger than many I have seen in London. The bathrooms have always been clean and well kept. The decor isn't super modern but isnt dated either. The bed has always been firmish but thats how i like it. I found the dinning area to be roomy and well lite which makes a chnage from dark, dingy and crowded as I found some other Hotels in London to be. My only 2 gripes are: that there is no tea making facilities in the room (not the 2 i stayed in) and i find this a must. Having tea making facilities in a common area isnt what you need when u feel like a tea at midnight and you are in your jim jams already! Almost all hotels ive stayed in in the UK have this and so should the London Town Hotel. My second gripe is that Ive twiced asked to check in around 10am (as I have been arriving from Australia) and have twice been flat out refused. Now Im happy to pay the extra day, half day or whatever but they havent been accomodating. Both times I have made booking well in advance of my stay so I felt with that amount of notice they should of been able to accomodated me. Nohing worse than walking around London waitimg to check in after a 23hr flight. All in all though a very good hotel. All being well I will be staying there again in 2011 when I next visit, hopefully checking in at 10am for a good sleep too :) As an aside, i also stayed 1 night at the Lord Jim Hotel, which is in the same street as the LTH, I found the Lord Jim to be more expensive and vastly less impressive.

title: So convenient!
text: I stayed here with a friend after finishing a tour around Europe, and definitely enjoyed the convenience of the place! Was so close to everything, especially the tube which i became a master at in 2 days, and Earl's Court is a great place for anything you need, restaurants, pubs, laundromat, nail/massage salons etc. London town hotel were very accommodating when rang to upgrade and book an extra room the day I was due to arrive. The only problem was that during the weekdays breakfast was over by 9am so we either missed out because we wanted a sleep in, or had to rush for breakfast. It was simple, but the boiled eggs were yum! The staff were very friendly and always there no matter what hour we would roll in. I would definitely recommend this place to others.

title: Very Helpful and friendly staffs!
text: Wonderful stay for a family with 2 children. Very friendly and helpful staff. Allowed us to leave our baggage after check out so we still have time to roam around London. The reception staff also helped in booking a private car for us to go to the airport. Great location. Very near the Earl's Court Station and bus stops. Lots of shops and supermarkets around. Free WiFi. Highly recommended especially for family.

title: Great staff
text: An old victorian town house, we stayed for 6 nights, my girl friend and I we had a lovely, relaxing stay there, all the staff we encountered were welcoming, friendly and attentive from checking-in to the moment we left. The room was clean and tidy and very comfortable, breakfast was quite good (not cooked though). Some refreshing of decorations required but not an issue. We recommend this hotel .

title: Tired, soulless, but clean & a decent breakfast!
text: I commute down from Chester to London for work 3 days every fortnight, where I work long hours and just want a quiet, comfortable & preferably friendly place to get my head down. Earls Court is perfect for me because it's a pleasant 2.5 mile walk to our office in Victoria and right on a bus route, and there are lots of better-priced small hotels. First impressions weren't good. I arrived at 10.30pm to a disinterested welcome and a tired, musty-smelling reception. Having asked for a quiet room, I was then disappointed to find I had the room next to reception and the main entrance overlooking the street at ground level - but, as my wife would say, that's what you get for turning up so late! The room was also tiny, although I know that this is normal in this area for a single at "just" £75 a night! And at least it was clean and the bed comfortable, with a very clean & perfectly functional en-suite shower room. In the morning, breakfast was a perfectly adequate continental with choice of cereals, fruit juices, fresh toast & coffee, boiled eggs & sliced cheese, and a croissant that could have been fresher! Service was again disinterested although efficient. I hope I won't be back, but I know what to expect next time if the price is right!

title: Good value for money
text: Room was quite small but had all one needs

title: A Pleasant Surprise on the Queen's Weekend
text: We booked the London Town Hotel based on location and tripadvisor reviews. It's on a street of Victorian small hotels, and our room overlooked the garden (which, since it rained a lot, we didn't get to use). The staff was helpful, even storing my medication in their refrigerator. We arrived on Jubilee weekend, though not because we planned to. We enjoyed the excitement. The room was smallish, but certainly serviceable, and it was clean and well-maintained, though could probably do with some upgrading. Breakfastt was fine. AND it has an elevator! We'd come back here -- London is an expensive city, and this location and hotel made it seem more reasonable.

title: Solo traveller
text: This is my first stay at the London Town Hotel I stay in London every week for work purposes The hotel was cheap, you never know what you are going to get on a budget and I was pleasantly surprised with this hotel I booked a single room for one night, the room was spacious (which is unusual) it was spotless and had a lovely bathroom and decent shower. Bedroom had a desk and wardrobe, bed comfy and spotless Tv had free view and the offer of a communal lounge up to 11 pm If you don't want to be in your room on your own Free wifi available although I didn't access so can't comment on speed Excellent value, basic but clean, comfortable and met my needs Gentleman on reception was polite, friendly and welcoming Right next to Earl's Court tube Will use again Many thanks

title: Eighth Ring of Hell!
text: Would not recommend. Love Earl's Court, but hated hotel. Not clean. Staff not knowledgable or helpful. AVOID! AVOID! Locks on doors did not work.

title: very good place to stay !
text: i have been to london town hotel 5 or 6 times...that says everything!!! a very good place to stay!!!! a nice location, and very good saff !!! hope to go back soon.

title: Good value
text: I stayed here overnight and for what I paid I think it is good value. The staff were welcoming and helpful. The room, as expected, was a little basic but clean and comfortable. There is fast free WiFi. I didn't have the breakfast so can't comment on that. Earl's Court tube station is two minutes away on foot so there are excellent transport links nearby. I would definitely stay there again.

title: Poor intoductiont to Europe
text: I trusted our travel agent to book three night's London accommodation for us, on our first overseas trip. The London Town Hotel in Earl's Court was our point of arrival in Europe. We arrived, very weary, early in the morning and as it was too early to check in, asked to have our bags minded while we went out for the day. "Minding" meant leaving them in the corner of the public corridor. We were worried about our things all day. The room was very small and stuffy. The floors creaked, so people above disturbed us and the walls were so thin we could clearly hear the people speaking next door (at 2am!) The shower was blocked. You had to shower quickly as it filled up with water and nearly overflowed every time. We had to ask for toilet paper. The staff pretty much ignored us. The breakfast was fine. I got a few itchy bites which I suspect, after doing some research, were bed bug bites, but not certain. As our room was at the back of the building, there was little traffic noise. We were hoping for better than this for the three star rating and the price.
