title: A good budget hotel in Central London
text: This is a well-kept budget hotel with clean rooms and professional staff. The location is very good - transport zone 1, near the Earl’s Court tube station (and the EasyBus stops from Gatwick) with many eateries around. The continental breakfast (basic) is included in the price. The rooms are small but functional. The shower cabin was even a bit larger than can be expected (though not too much water from the shower).

title: Nice British style hotel in good neighbourhood.
text: Clean rooms but bit small. Enough breakfast but same things every day. They could have change it every day as small boutique otel should do. Great back garden to have tea.. Very close to metro station.. Use website for booking to get best price..

title: Location, location, location
text: We spent a week here and would do so again. It's location is perfect, being so close to the Tube. The room, on the ground floor, was small with thin walls. Our neighbour of a few nights seemed to endure wracking early morning coughing fits. The bed was comfortable and the shower worked well. Breakfast, at an additional cost, was pretty poor but we found, just down the road, an early morning opener which served great cheap meals. The 24 hour office staff were most helpful. In summary, this is one of the cheaper hotels within easy reach of Central London. Accommodation in London is anything but cheap so it would be unfair to have high expectations in this price range. That said, I think you get more than you pay for. I recommend it.

title: Location, location, price
text: Very convenient location. Five minute walk to the Piccadilly line Earls court and Heathrow. Six minute walk to easy bus to Gatwick. Very reasonable price, and an EXCELLENT front desk staff, always helpful and friendly.

title: good quality budget hotel
text: On arrival was greeted by friendly smiling receptionist. My single room had a good standard of fixture and fittings and my window overlooked a pleasant patio area which must be great to use in the summer. The breakfast room was bright and cheerful and the staff efficient in clearing and cleaning tables. This is the second time I've stayed in this hotel and again was not disappointed. Also the room was quiet and I had a better nights sleep than when I've stayed in more expensive hotels.

title: Decent stay
text: My one night stay went fine. The room was compact and clean, and everything worked. There was strong wifi, decent water pressure in the shower, and a lounge with coffee/tea. The location is great with the tube a block away and plenty of pubs, restaurants, and shops around. Suggestions for improvement: 1) Please provide an early check in option. I arrived at 11:40am after a red eye and would've loved to freshen up, but they wouldn't allow checkin until after 2pm. The person at reception didn't even bother to look. The hotel advertised vacancies in the front window so it's not as though there was zero availability. 2) Please do away with the separate charge for same day bag storage and include it in the room rate. Sure it's only £1 (or £5 for the secure option) but this extra charge stuck out. It's only the second time I've seen a charge for this service.

title: We recommend it to everybody!
text: We stayed at London Town Hotel during last summer and our choice was perfect. The hotel is very nice and cozy, it has a lucky position because it's situated at few step from Earl's Court Underground Station: from you can catch Tube trains and visit the entire city of London easily, without using cars. The staff is very helpful and polite, above all Ms. Diana (what a nice coincidence with Princess' name!) in the breakfast room. Our room was very quiet and clean, the entire hotel is very clean: those reviews like "London Bedbug Hotel" are nor credible at all, you know the world is full of frustrated troublemakers and bad hats, so don't believe them and don't let them deceive you. Stay there, you will not regret it!

title: Friendly service
text: The London Town Hotel has very friendly and helpfull staff. Location is perfect: 2 minute walking distance to the Earl's Court Metro. Clean rooms, free wifi. I would definitely recommend staying here.

title: Recommended Budget Hotel
text: This hotel did all the important things well for the price. I paid 65 pounds for a single room. It was clean, quiet with a good continental breakfast and facilities (eg TV, newish bathroom). Its 3min walk from the Tube, which is itself about 30min from Heathrow and 15 min from central London by train. OK the room was a bit small and floors a bit creaky but hey this is central london so buildings tend to be oldish. Earles Court the suburb is fine with lots of well priced food options. I quite liked the 'Blackbird' pub on the corner.

title: nice hotel
text: friendly and helpfull staff clean room. my room was facing the street, the noise was okay, even with open window. breakfast was ok. nice little terrace to hang out location is close to public transport. .

title: Cosy
text: We had a night here during our London stay. The rooms were very clean & the bedding was comfortable. We picked a triple room & it was a good size. The service was fantastic. The gentleman on reception was very pleasant. The location was great - just around the corner from the underground station. There was a laundromat nearby (a huge plus). This was just a short walk from the hotel. The walls are a little thin (we could hear everything from the rooms all around us), but do not let this deter you from staying here. Once 10pm came around, it was very peaceful and quiet. We would definitely consider staying here again in the future.

title: Excellent location with good facilties and service
text: I stayed here for 9 nights in the summer. Location: Excellent. Barely 2-mins from Earl's Court Tube station. Easy access to banks, restaurants, drug stores. My favourite is the M&S Food Hall. Accessibility/Facilities: a lift is available although my room was on a landing so I had to walk up/down a few stairs to reach it. Not a problem for me as I only had 1 suitcase. Room: the perfect size for a solo traveller. Bathroom had a separate shower stall which is good. My room was on the first floor, facing the main road but it was quiet with hardly any sound from passing traffic. Breakfast: good, standard fare provided daily consisting of toast, cereal, juices, spreads, fruit, yoghurt. Wifi: good service in the room and dirining area in the basement. I noticed several hotspots located on the first floor itself which all gave off strong signals. Lounge: located on the first floor with free coffee/tea served throughout the day. There is also a TV. Computer and printing facilities are also available (pay per use). Room amenities: safe, TV with popular British channels, basic toiletries. I only wish there had been a small kettle for making hot drinks and a minibar for us to keep drinks and snacks in. Overall, I enjoyed my stay here. The staff were all pleasant and helpful. The room and public areas (dining room, reception) were clean at all times. Earl's Court is a very convenient area to stay in London and I would definitely recommend the Hotel to my friends and families who visit.

title: Best Location, Best Staff...
text: First of all the Location of this hotel is amazing, having read other Trip Advisor reviews I decided to book this hotel for me and my friends and we sure weren't disappointed. The Hotel is situated a mere 5min walk from the Earl's Court Tube Station which will then take you to anywhere in London you want to go. The staff was very helpful from the day we checked in till the day we checked out. The receptionists were very helpful on many occasions, with one in particular giving us insights on the best shopping locations and attractions. The Continental Breakfast is not very lavish, but you get what you pay for...and in London with that price, it definitely is a Good breakfast. Our triple room was quite roomy and very clean. The bathroom was cleaned and stocked with fresh towels each day. The room isn't that spacious but if like us you are planning to go to as many places as you can possibly fit in, this is definitely the hotel for you! Thanks to all at the London Town Hotel :)

title: Travelling in style
text: Rrrrrrreally loved my stay in this hotel in London. Kensington and Chelsea is an amazing area of London by default - the number of shops, pubs, the proximity to the centre and all touristic attractions and museums yet to all gorgeous houses (real houses of real people lol!) and parks - oh, that's just bliss! The tube station "Earl's Court" has a step-free access so you won't have to carry your heavy bag all the way up and down the stairs - the same with the hotel, it does have an elevator. Single rooms are small but cosy, VERY clean and with a nice view - windows face a quiet street. Brekfast is alright - fruits, eggs, toasts, tea and coffee. Good to grab something early in the morning and start your adventures!

title: Dissapointing
text: The hotel is in a good location on a quiet street in Earls Court near the tube station and many options for meals. Half of the staff is very friendly (Mohamed at the front desk in particular was extremely helpful), and half I would say grumpy, especially the guy who was at the desk Sunday morning before 7 AM. There is no air conditioning so you need to leave your windows open but there are no window screens. The bathrooms are really small, about the same as a cruise ship. There is one small elevator that seemed to be enough. Breakfast was about what I expected for continental, but it never changed. The breakfast attendants were very efficient and after breakfast they doubled as room attendants. The rooms offer no dresser or chest of drawers to unpack in so you are basically working out of your suitcase.

title: Perfect for the budget
text: Couldn't of asked for more out of this hotel. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The lounge area was a nice treat with free tea and coffee. Breakfast was nice too with enough to start your day. The room was clean. It was a bit warm due to no air on but the window did open enough to let in a nice breeze. There is a lift which stops on certain floors. Our room was on the 4th so you got the lift to the 5th floor and walked down a small flight of stairs. They were helpful with tips and advice for London etc. Just a short walk to earls court tube station which is a fantastic tube and can get you straight to most of the main areas of London from the one line. Will definitely be visiting this hotel again. Also has a smoking area off the lounge which is a bonus personally

title: A good location, helpful staff and a good start to the holiday.
text: We chose thishotel because of the positive reviews and we were very happy with our selection. Our room was quite big and very comfortable. The room and bathroom were very clean and the location very quiet, could even hear birds singing in the early mornings. The hotel was located very close to the Earl's Court tube and this made getting around extremely easy. Breakfast was wonderful and catered well for the whole family. I did have a problem with the lack of hot water, but as soon as I repported the problem, the staff quickly fixed the problem by giving my family access to another room and I noticed there was a serviceman fixing the problem within half an hour. We were very happy with this hotel.

title: Good value and well located
text: This is a value hotel and room sizes reflect that. It is well located near the underground and buses. A decent buffett beakfast is included. The free wi-fi can be erratic during the day but early in the morning or late at night the internet connection is adequate. The staff are friendly.

title: would return....!
text: My friend and I recently stayed in a similar priced hotel within minutes of this and vowed we would never return there. We booked 2 nights here with a bit of trepidation, but the price was inviting. We had booked 2 singles for 2 nights, .The London is ideally placed 5 mins from Earls Court tube, in a quiet side street (apart from the council cleaning the drains at 7am on the Sunday morning..but no fault of the hotel...!). Our rooms (502 /503) were on the 4th floor at the front of the hotel. Nice clean comfy bed and pillows, nice white towels in the shower ensuite, essential toiletries provided and hairdryer. Flat screen TV ... and contrary to other reviews on here I picked up the wi fi on my smart phone without any trouble in the room. Missed a kettle - but the lounge on the first floor had help yourself tea/coffee at all times. Breakfast was continental, served in the light, bright basement dining room. Adequate selection of juices, fruit, yogurts, cereals eggs cheese etc, and fresh toast to order. Unlimited tea and coffee. The staff were all pleasant, welcoming and helpful... All in all a pleasant 2 nights stay, for an excellent price by London standards. I think we have found our little oasis for our future visits to London !!!

title: Nide hotel in convenient location
text: Near to Earls Court Tube station, restaurants etc. My room on the top floor had no window but a skylight. Quite OK. Staff was friendly and breakfast perfectly OK. Pleasant stay for one night only, in and out from Heathrow and a short visit to a bookshop! Will be back.

title: Great value and location!
text: We chose this hotel based on value and location. It's a quick, easy walk from the Earl's Court station. This makes an easy trip from LHR and also to most places in London. We were in a room below street level, but had large windows and lots of light. As with most triple rooms, there wasn't a lot of available floor space, but we spent six nights with no problem. The bath was also small, but new and clean. The beds were comfortable with good linens. There was no noise at all from other rooms and we faced the back and had no outside noise. Wifi in the room was spotty, but worked well in the lobby or lounge. We didn't spend a lot of time in the room. Breakfast was typical: cereal, toast, juice and coffee and tea. Some days there was meat and cheese and pastries and fruit were varied. The staff was friendly and knew us after a few days. Front desk was very helpful with suggestions. The neighborhood felt very safe and there was a selection of places to eat and buy food supplies. It's not central London, and it's not five stars, but it was a great fit for us.

title: Alright
text: For the price it was alright, a bit noisy as the walls are not thick, so you can hear the neighbours. Free breakfast and it is not too bad. Free wifi. There is a nice lounge with a garden where you can hang out. However the staff could be a little more pleasant.

title: Standard Hotel, Good Location
text: Standard hotel in London. The rooms are basic but very clean and were at a fairly cheap cost. The staff are heaps friendly and the desk is 24/7. Very close to earls court tube station so location is good, although the rooms can get quite hot in the summer

title: Excellent Location but Beware of Room Choice
text: Pros: Excellent location with very short walk to Earls Court tube station which is served by both Piccadilly and District lines. This station also has a lift (don't have to go up stairs if you have luggage coming from Heathrow). Many nearby restaurants. Friendly staff and clean rooms Lounge area on second floor with coffee/tea Breakfast decent but never changes. Serving staff really nice. Negatives Sketchy WIFI Single room so small, no where even to put your suitcase. Additional hooks for hanging clothes would have been useful. The rooms in the basement (where breakfast served) also not recommended. Very hot and stuffy, noisy, dark, also a sewer smell.

title: Nice place to stay!
text: Friendly and welcoming. Clean and tasteful. Convenient for all west london attractions. Plenty to eat at buffet style continental breakfast. I would stay again. Ive been told to use 200 words so I have to repeat myself: Friendly and welcoming. Clean and tasteful. Convenient for all west london attractions. Plenty to eat at buffet style continental breakfast. I would stay again.

title: Highly Recommend, Great staff, Great location , Very friendly vibe
text: We greatly enjoyed our stay at the London Town Hotel, the staff were very friendly and helpful with any requests we had. The room was very comfortable , everything we needed and a very relaxed feel. The first floor lounge was a great idea, with tea making facilities and large TV and also great info on local shopping , markets etc in Hotel visitors book, it was also a great way to meet other travellers. The breakfast was basic continental , and delicious .I would highly reccomend this hotel to anyone staying in this area. Very close to tube station, and local resturants and supermarkets Very, very happy. Thank you

title: Good location
text: I had a small room with single bed, a small closet with 4 hangers, no shelves, just a shower. All these things were sufficient for the 5 nights I stayed. I stayed in a room facing street on reception level. Location was perfect, close to everything: Staff helpful and clean hotel. Appreciated free Wi Fi, TV with lots of stations, a good selection for the continental breakfast. Liked the offer of tea or coffee in the lounge. I didn't need air-con because it was cool out so I was able to open a window for fresh air. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Very good and clean hotel when on a budget.. close to Earls Court tube
text: Spent a week with my wife at LTH and have to say that we were satisfied in almost all aspects. Had room 401, which is a double room and compared to the London standards it is of a fair size and very clean indeed. The hotel is graced with an elevator too, which most of the other London hotels of its class does not. We had comfortable sleep. Towels were changed whenever we left them out of the bathroom. The staff were also helpful and gave us all the information we asked for including some tips how to get around too. If I had to remark about something, it would be the breakfast. There was nothing really wrong about it, as all the things were fresh, but I would have preferred some more selection. I don't really know the London standards for continental breakfast as I always had English breakfast the times I visited before. The wifi in the room was also a little week at times but it was ok in the lounge.. but hey .. it was free. All in all, it was a a good hotel which helped making our London stay more enjoyable

title: Overall, OK
text: The location is great. The elevator ("lift") slow and small, the room very small, the shower incredibly small with conservative water pressure. Nice that wifi was in the room. Relatively quiet. Service at desk ok except for this one rude gentleman. For example, they ran out of cups for coffee/tea on the 2nd floor gathering area a few times when I was there. I asked him if I could obtain a coffee cup and he rudely directed me to walk to the basement like I was some kind of idiot for asking to ask the breakfast people for a cup. When I went down there it seemed like they were looking at an alien as I took a cup from one of the tables (I tried to explain why to no avail). He was also rude to my GF when she left a few minutes after me and I had already left key at desk (he wanted her to leave the key). Other than that, great!

title: Clean and affordable
text: I have now stayed at the London Town Hotel for the second time in between my travels from Europe to the Middle East. I returned to the hotel because it offers clean and simple rooms at affordable prices for London. In addition, on both occasions I have found the staff to be friendly and willing to help with any queries I had. I have previously stayed at another hotel at a similar price on the same road to which I will not be returning. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for somewhere comfortable, clean and welcoming to stay at a decent price.

title: Convenient and Friendly
text: This was our first hotel experience in Europe and I was expecting a small room and bathroom and I was not disappointed. The beds were extremely uncomfortable and the street noise was pretty significant since we had to leave our windows open due to the heat. But....all of the front desk receptionists were very helpful and friendly and the location was wonderful. I can't compare our room to similar London hotels, but all in all I think we got a good value - which was what we were looking for. I would recommend this hotel for a budget conscience traveler looking for a clean, safe, friendly small hotel in a good location.

title: very good would highly recommend.
text: My daughter, granddaughter and I stayed here for 2 nights in a triple room to see the london sights. With earls court so near we found it very handy for travelling. room was clean, breakfast sufficient to start the day and staff at reception and breakfast room all very pleasant and helpful.would recommend.

title: Good value for money
text: The hotel is conveniently located a few minutes walking distance from Earl's Court tube station. Rooms are simple and clean but good value for money really. Breakfast was good also. There is free Wi-Fi but connection can sometimes be tricky. All in all, a good hotel as a base for three nights whilst in a course.

title: Great value for your money, extremely good location.
text: This hotel turned out to be better than we expected. We booked a double room, but was given a room for four, so we had lots of space. The hall and room was quite narrow, but I have learnt that is to be expected at London hotels. It is situated in a quiet street just around the corner from the underground, so perfect location. From that underground, it was easy access to the largest attractions in London without even changing the tube. At first glance, the hotel seemed a bit suspicious and cheap, with it's blue sign welcoming us at the door (they would be better of without it, to give a better first impression), but it turned out alright. The staff was pleasant and helpful, and we didn't experience any problems during our stay here. The breakfast was a disappointment, as all they had was warmed up croissants, cheese, eggs, jam and some cereals, and served toast at the table. Me and my mother decided to buy crackerbread to bring, as we are used to more fiber and nutrition for the first meal of the day. But either way, it was very welcoming to receive food at the hotel, so we didn't have to rush out each morning to get something to eat. It's a nice area, with several shops and pubs as well. The walls were a bit thin, so one could hear if anyone walked the hallway or were talking in the reception, but that didn't bother us as we brought earplugs.

title: Convenient and well run. Optimal location
text: Had a superb stay, very cosy and convenient. Inexpensive considering location. Management was extremely helpful and knowledgeable. Breakfast served to your room. Small room but adequate for ones purpose. Comfortable bed. Would stay there again every visit.

title: Good service
text: Pobyt jsme si užili. Obecně od hotelu očekáváme, že je čistý, útulný a za rozumnou cenu máme kde si přes noc odpočinout - jinak jsme pořád někde pryč. Tento hotel to splňuje - kousek od metra, se snídaní, čistý a velice milý personál. Doporučujeme. What do we expect? Clean and comfortable room where we can rest after a long day... This hotel fullfils everything we need - near the tube station, with breakfast, clean, nice and friendly staff. We recommend it!

title: Good hotel in a good district
text: Liked: 1. Very welcoming & friendly receptionist 2. Really very good big room (double) & bath-room (with real bath!), clean, warm 3. Good location - 2 min to tube, supermarket, cafe, 4. Free wi-fi Dislike: 1. A lil bit poor breakfast 2. Toilette was out of order - problem with water

title: Repeat guests who have found our home away from home in London
text: Great staff. Mohammed at Reception remembered us from our stay 2 years ago and could not do enough to make out stay enjoyable. The other staff Ins & Ali were very helpful too as are the breakfast/housekeeping crew. Very happy with our stay and will be back

title: Good value for money
text: I had a room under the roof was clean and with a comfortable bed. The reception was very friendly. The hotel is is in a good location and offers free wifi and a lift to higher floors. Compared to similar hotels fair value for money and a place I will book again.

title: Great Find
text: Found Hotel at short notice after being messed about by Booking.Com and was not disappointed, the staff were very friendly and helpful and the hotel room [quadruple] just what we needed. The Hilton it is not, but also not what we were expecting for the price, importantly the room and bathroom were clean the linen fresh and beds comfortable, and was large enough for us all plus our luggage for two days, in fact we all had a comfortable and quite nights sleep, Continental breakfast was plentiful and service good. What did impress me was that the staff had a genuine desire to make you feel welcome and went out of their way to help. Hotel location was great too just a few minutes from Earls Court where there were plenty of places to eat out etc. we would defiantly use again in the future.

title: Only OK
text: This is, at best, a very average hotel. I was in London during August, when the weather was quite warm, and there was no air-conditioning in tiny room. Fortunately, I was given a fan. Breakfast was very bland and basic. I had to get the management to ask the kitchen staff to stop smoking directly under my window during their early morning break. My room stank of smoke at 6am. The reception staff, however, were friendly and helpful.

title: Family Friendly Hotel in Great Location
text: The location of the London Town hotel is fantastic

title: 5 Stars Had The WIFI & TV & Hot Water Being Working Better
text: The location of the hotel is ideal for being close to Earls Court underground station, as well as the shops and places to eat and drink nearby. My room was facing the road and I stayed on a Saturday night, but was never woken up by any noise. The night receptionist was very welcoming and the small single room was ideal for one night and for single occupancy. The room was super clean and the bed was very comfortable. I paid only £60 which was a generous price during high season. The TV needs sorting out (Room 304) as hardly any of the channels work. The WIFI reception was week and the hot water took a very long time to heat, thus wasting water from the tap. But I would stay again.

title: Clean but that's all.
text: The good news:Very close to tube station,good room service,peaceful neighbourhood,good breakfast, friendly staff (the room maids were friendlier though). The bad news:Very small room for the price (nothing like the photos, which make it seem spacious),tiny bathroom that can only fit one person. The bed bust have been 1.70cm in length, so we didn't really fit. Room service (towel refreshing, sheets etc) does not have a set schedule, so the maids might have to knock on your door and practically kick you out so they can clean up. You also notice that the whole street line is comprised of the exact same hotel buildings, so you wonder why some are more expensive than others. These are all Victorian buildings with tiny spaces, creaky floorboards, and bad insulation. Don't expect these type of B&Bs to be practical and comfy.

title: Perfect affordable hotel in London
text: Fantastic stay at this hotel for three nights in August en route to other places in Europe. Room was ready as soon as I arrived, staff was friendly, and room was comfortable. Very close to the Earl's Court station, which made getting around town very easy. Was great to find an affordable hotel in London - a notoriously expensive city. It doesn't have the in-property amenities of a five-star hotel, but it isn't charging five-star prices either.

title: Short break
text: The hotel is excellently located being just a couple of hundred yards from Earls Court Underground on the Picadilly lIne. The rooms were small but comfortable. Continental breakfast was substantial and to a good standard. The only downside was that it was very hot and there was no air conditioning. The staff were all helpful and pleasant. We wouldn't hesitate to stay again.

title: Great value for solo travellers - bring ear plugs for the ground floor rooms though!
text: I paid £55 per night for a single room, 3 night stay. The room was really clean and very comfortable for the spend. The room I stayed on was on the ground floor, adjacent to reception. Unfortunately, a nearby rattly old door to other rooms was slammed constantly at all hours, morning and night, making one hell of a bang and shaking the room. While this was the fault of other guests, the hotel really needs to address this issue. This was my only quibble in an otherwise comfortable stay and I'd have no hesitation in staying there again.

title: Don't expect much at this hotel
text: This is not a bad choice if you want to stay in the Earl's Court area and you're not fussed by quality, however, the hotel is quite old and it shows. When we were there it was not good value for money, although in fairness it was a last minute booking and not much else was available. The hotel is really more like a lodge or backpacker accommodation (minus the dorms and shared bathrooms). The breakfast wasn't particularly good, suggest you eat out unless you're getting breakfast as part of the deal.

title: London Town Hotel - great location!
text: We arrived at the hotel early in the morning after an overnight flight from the Washington DC area. We couldn't check in yet, but they held our bags (four of them) and we walked one-half block down the street turned a corner and walked about another half block back to the Earl's Court Underground Station. The location is terrific - located a very easy walk to the Underground, and the Earl's Court Station is on both the Piccadilly and District/Circle lines providing easy access to all areas of the city. From there, we went all over the city as well as to Wimbledon and Windsor Castle - both of which are outside of the city. We had no trouble getting anywhere. We had bought a 50 pound sterling visitor Oyster Card for travel in zones 1 and 2, and didn't need to "top it off" (i.e. add extra money to cover travel outside zones 1 & 2), except to get from Heathrow Airport and back. The Oyster card can be used on the buses and some of the rail lines, too - depending on which kind of Oyster card you get. We also read that you can mail the card back to get a refund of unused credit on the card, which we'll be doing in the next few days. The hotel itself had an unusual arrangement that I've never seen this in the U.S. - a family room- which had a queen size bed and two twins. We have two college age children - one male and one female - and two queen beds don't work out for us any more like they used to when the kids were younger. The room was small, but it had an en suite bathroom with a shower, sink and toilet, and there was wi-fi throughout the hotel (a must have amenity for our college age kids). The room was a little small - but typical of European rooms in individually operated hotels. They served a "continental" breakfast with cereal, small danishes, toast, hard boiled eggs and ham, canned peaches, apples and bananas, yogurt and coffee/tea, apple & orange juice, milk and water. The menu didn't change at all in the 7 days we were there, but it was sufficient to get us started each day. The staff was very friendly and helpful, and the room was cleaned each day. It was a little bit cheaper to stay a little further away from the downtown area, and the underground is so close, we didn't find being a little further out an inconvenience at all. We'd recommend staying at the London Town Hotel, especially if you are traveling with your family. There were also a few good restaurants/pubs nearby, and a grocery store at the end of the block.

title: Medically unsafe temperature on hot day and unbearable even after it cooled down outside
text: It's midnight and I'm currently in the room covering myself in cold water to prevent hyperthermia and wondering what to do. It was an unusually hot day when we arrived and the room, on the fifth of six floors felt noticeably hotter than the 93 degree outside temperature even with fan on and windows wide open as suggested by the very friendly but sweat drenched staff. We took cold showers and kept our children out of the room during the day but decided to stay because it looked like the temperature was due to drop to the 60s overnight, we had prepaid on Expedia so refund chances were iffy and everywhere else was booked up (Wimbledon week). Regretting that decision now. Still literally a sauna and we are a family that has travelled extensively on a budget in hot third world countries and normally don't complain about stuff. Otherwise small but clean room and good location. Utterly miserable right now. Avoid in hot weather at any cost

title: Nice clean, Great location!
text: I was a little apprehensive after reading a few of the reviews on this hotel on tripadvisor. I am so glad that I did NOT change my reservation. Charming small hotel! All employees that we met were extremely friendly. Our room was small, but so were the rooms in places we stayed outside of London prior to arriving at London Town Hotel. I think small rooms are just a fact of life in the UK (unless you want to pay a fortune). The room was clean, the bed linens were fresh, and our room was extremely quiet. The location was great, close to the Underground, and several good places to eat close by. One note - if reading the other reviews and notice the negative ones, take into consideration the LOW number of negative ones....... the positive comments FAR outweigh any negative comments.

title: Convenient Location
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel for two nights at the beginning of our vacation and we returned for three nights at the end of our vacation. I chose this hotel based on the price, its reviews on Tripadvisor, and its proximity to the Tube. The hotel is very, very close to the Earl's Court tube stop, but on a quiet side street which is great. There are many other hotels on the street but London Town was one of the lower priced options. The room décor is outdated and lacks any character. The walls have dings in them and the bathroom ceiling fan had A LOT of dust in it. The shower itself was extremely small. I couldn't bend in it without hitting the wall and I am not a large person. The water pressure and temperature was good. We had a bit of trouble getting the Wi-Fi to work upon arrival but had no problems with it once we were connected. I was not a fan of the breakfast so we only went down to the basement to have it one morning. Overall, I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is looking for a decent place to stay while exploring London. My husband and I are not the types of travelers who hang out and relax in hotel rooms - we'd rather be out and about. If you are looking for something more than a convenient place to stay, you may want to look into other options. That being said, the price is probably the best you will find for a small hotel close to a main Tube stop in London.

title: A comfortable and friendly hotel
text: Excellent value and a superb location. Very easy to get to all the sites, especially the National History Museum and Science Museum. Very clean and the staff are very friendly. Will return next time I visit.

title: Nice hotel, great location!
text: Nice hotel, great location! Kensington/Notting Hill is just beautiful. Excellent location for a nice walk after dinner. Beautiful shops nearby and lovely restaurants. Our room was cramped for 4, but it was very clean and nicely kept. It is not luxurious but is well maintained and it has an elevator/lift so one does not have to lug the luggage up stairs. Only 2 fit in the lift on every trip so it takes a while to get luggage up if you are a party larger than 2. The staff is very friendly and very efficient. They will watch your luggage for 2 euro per bag if you leave it under the bulletin board, or store it for 5 euro per bag. We had it stored and it was worth it as they do not guarantee its return and they will not be held responsible for stolen items. A quick walk to the tube and shops and restaurants. Our room was very warm and we called down for a fan which was delivered promptly. We set it on an open window and slept soundly - no noise to bother us. The breakfast was awful! Limited to tea, coffee, apple juice, orange juice, water, peaches in syrup, cereals and toast. That's it! Not great but we took it because it was included. Free wifi, very fast.

title: Great location, friendly hotel... would 100% stay again!!
text: Stayed at the London Town Hotel for 2 nights, Friday and Saturday. Arrived before check in but we were able to have our room which was great so we could freshen up and our bags were safe. Staff were very friendly and helpful, we dealt with a young woman most of the time who was very pleasant. Room was for 3 people but there was plenty of room. Comfy beds, clean bathroom and very powerful shower. Breakfast was great, plenty of choice for continental. Check out was 11am but hotel kept our bags free of charge until 2pm. Location was excellent, 2 minute walk from Earl's Court tube and in Zone 1 for the underground. I would 100% stay here again, great value for London!!!

title: Holiday Trip to London
text: When I decided to book and stay at this hotel, it was done solely on the basis of price, convenience of location and also what I looked on what was shown on their website. I am glad I did not make a wrong choice. In fact, I am really very happy with this hotel. In the first place, I had done my research and had wanted to stay at a place where I do not need to change too many Tube Stations from where I was travelling from. I was able to get onto the London Underground tube station at Terminal 4 and travel direct on the Picadilly line to Earls Court Station. This meant I did not need to lug my luggage all over the place. What was even better was that I found that once I got out of Earls Court, there is a lift too, so again that meant minimal straining of muscles. Once, I took the lift and got out on ground level, there is also a ramp meaning I do not need to lift my luggage up the stairs. The hotel is literally just around the corner. I turn right, walk up a few yards, turn right again into Penywern Road and I can spot the hotel straightaway. I am also happy with the fact that there are plenty of eateries like Prets including a Marks and Spencers Food Hall. Once at the hotel, you do need to go up a few steps. The hotel is small but comfortable and I was actually given a really small room as I was travelling on my own. To be honest, I really do not mind as there is still room for me to put my luggage to and to walk about a bit. There is even a balcony but it's not exactly clean outside, so I kept the door to the balcony locked.The bathroom was really nice, just renovated, modern and clean with excellent water pressure for showering. This is an important point for me as I do shower everyday. There is a also a small TV. The room is kept very clean, again another plus point. Wifi is supposedly free but the signal was so weak, I gave up doing anything with it. Again, I am not too worried as I do have a smart-phone, that I can use. The room does not come with a kettle or drinks but the hotel provides this service on the first floor. Any hotel guest can make use of this for their coffer or tea, etc. Breakfast was provided as part of my hotel bill which is great and again the kitchen and seating area has just been recently renovated. It's lovely and bright with about 10 tables or so - very cosy. The menu selection is the same everyday but again no complaint here. The kitchen staff does a great job with their service. The hotel Reception Staff is also very efficient and will assist with advice, booking of taxis etc if so requested. They will also keep the luggages if needs be after the hotel guest has checked out for the day. I find the afternoon receptionist to be really friendly. Once you are there for the first two days,the gentleman can recognise you. He always has a ready smile unlike the morning staff who has a stoic look all the time although if you care to greet him first, he will reciprocate. I am very pleased with this hotel and not only will I highly recommend this place, I myself will certainly stay at this place again when I am in London soon.

title: Great location
text: Close toEarls court station and close to main strip. Rooms was clean, bathroom rather small when getting out of shower need to have to door open bit of a squeeze. Breakfast was very bland and the only hot food was toast and boiled eggs. Very small room so you have to get there at the right time otherwise you have to wait. Four at a table is very small. No tea coffee making facilities in the room only in the lounge.

title: Tiny Shower to the level of a joke! It is close to the Exhebition Center
text: The plus is that you get to be very close to the Exhebition Center. This hotel was chosen for me by a company I was working with. The room was very small but suitable to the price they paid. There is launge in the first floow which serves free tea and has a TV. Cons. 1. The room was not clean! FYI. 2. The shower was too small. If you are above 1.80 you night have a problem. If you can - I would avoid this place. If you must go there make sure you fit in the shower and that you get a double room.

title: Simple and cosy
text: Very close to the tube, and 2 lines go from Earls Court. Direct train (Piccadily line) also comes from the airport, making it at a very convenient location. Quadruple family room was quite small, but cosy nonetheless. Room was very clean, and worth staying if you want a base and good night's rest to view the rest of London. Breakfast was simple, and service was good. Very good value for money, since the rate was so reasonable! Lift is not the fastest on earth, so be patient :)

title: Location!
text: My first time in London and so happy I chose this hotel. Location is perfect! Less than 5mins from Earl's Court underground station. I stayed 3nights in a single room on the 1st floor with a view of the street:) The street is lined with hotels and safety is not an issue. The staff were very polite:) The coffee and tea making facilities are at the lounge area on the 1st floor. The smoking area at the terrace outside the lounge. For the price it was very decent - clean, breakfast included, had a private bathroom, wifi, a lift (Quite small but very useful if you have heavy luggage just as I did:) too! Earl's Court station is also a very convenient stop. There are plenty of cafés,restaurants (try Nando's at the corner!) pubs, money changers and convenience stores.

title: Great service and location (metro-Earl's Court)
text: I stayed there for 2 nights and enjoyed my stay. The service was great and the room was cleaned! i only paid about $130 for two which I expected to get a small room. What I really liked about it is that it's a block away from the train station. I stayed in Victoria area in the past and it's too crowded - if you're looking for a family or to get away from the city center (which is only a 10 minutes tube ride) then I strongly recommend the place.

title: Surprisingly good.
text: For an economy hotel, this place is very good. Stayed at the hotel last night. The hotel was busy. I had booked a single room but was given a double room which was very clean, comfortable and had pretty much all you could possibly need. The staff are friendly as well. This hotel is very popular with the tourist brigade who are on a budget. The only little nag from me is that they charge for wi-fi (£7 for 24 hours). Not massive but still annoying.

title: Good to visit London
text: The hotel is in a perfect position to visit London, very close to the yellow, red and green tube line (I think this is the strongest point of this structure). Rooms are old (wooden flat, old moquette) but sufficiently clean and spacious. The quarter is lovely and very quiet

title: Ok for the price
text: First of all, bear in mind that Umi website is a lot better than the hotel itself :-) That said... the hotel is good for it's price. I got a double room, and stayed for 4 nights with my girlfriend, and for our needs it was good. We only would sleep there and leave right after breakfast, so it was ok. We didn't have any noise problems because our room faced the back of the hotel... and the heating worked fine. Staff was nice also!

title: Wouldn't recommend to a friend, but ok for the money
text: Stayed here for two nights at the begining of October with my boyfriend for his birthday. I chose the hotel because it was the cheapest yet the best reviews for a 3* hotel i could find. The room was an ok size, (at the end of the day your only sleeping in it) the sink was in the bedroom, and the bathroom was so tiny you litrally couldn't swing a cat in it. The bathroom was full of black mould and absolutly stank of foust, but, it was clean to use both shower and toilet, just didn't look very nice. I'd read reviews before staying at this hotel, and a couple said about creeky floorboards..that didn't stop me booking. BUT, seriously, were talking LOUD creeky floorboards from the room above that kept us up until 1am! And our room was next to the lifts so that was noisey too! So if you are sensitve to noise, do not stay at this hotel, or ask for a room on top floor away from lifts. The breakfast was good. It def filled us up til lunch. You had 4 options to choose from including toast, muffins, cereals, fruit, teas, hot chocolate, orange juice, apple juice etc. Was very nice, no need for a cooked full english. It was about a 6 minute walk to bayswater station, and a 12 minute walk to Queensway station. They are the nearest stations to the hotel. You could obviously get a much closer hotel, but this was ok if you can be bothered to walk.....in the rain. All in all, it was an ok Hotel, wouldn't stay here again or recommend it to a friend really. It was good for the money tho, I piad £150 for 2 nights including breakfast, so in London, that isn't bad. The staff couldn't have been more friendly either.

title: So much potential - great location and great front of house staff.
text: Thankfully on holidays you don't spend too much time in your room. If you did you'd have concerns about mould in showers! Front of house staff are great. Contential breakfast great too - and sooooo handy to Bayswater station.

title: old furniture, dirty bathroom, cold, not value at all.
text: old furniture, dirty bathroom, cold, not value at all. will never stay in the hotel again

title: Don't stay here if you want to sleep
text: The reception staff were helpful and friendly, and the location of the hotel is great, just 5 mins walk from the nearest tube station, and close to central London. BUT..... The hotel is a tired old terrace building, the paintwork needs attention, the sofas are worn and scruffy, the lifts are a bit rickety with the old name of the hotel still on them, and the floors creak like hell. This was the main problem we encountered - our room was on the 4th floor, and from entering the room in the afternoon to leaving the room in the morning - RIGHT through the night, the people on the floor above were walking around constantly and the floorboards creaked so loudly they could still be heard with earplugs and with your head under a pillow! To add to the disruption, the room was so hot we had to leave the window open all night so the volume of the city noise also kept us awake, not to mention thin walls so the general milling about within the hotel could be heard. We chose not to complain about the floorboard issue to be moved to another room, as it was late at night and we didn't want the hassle of packing everything back up and moving. Besides, I would imagine all the other floors to be the same?.. The bed linen and towels were clean, and the room was also, but again the decor and fittings were tired, and the shower was awful (had to take it down to use it as there was zero pressure). Fittings old fashioned. We certainly wouldn't recommend this hotel even though it is in a good location, as it wasn't really even good value for money at £80 per night. We didn't use the restaurant or bar so can't comment on those.

title: Good location but...
text: I have stayed here many times over the last few years on visits to London - because of its location, it's fairly good price (considering the location), and because I know I won't be spending much time in the room. I have always found the staff friendly and helpful, but the rooms vary depending on which part of the converted terrace houses you are in, they can be very hot during the summer, and it can be very noisy with student/school groups. Also the single rooms can be very small. I choose to stay here because of the location and am prepared for the reality - but it would not suit many people.

title: Thieves
text: This hotel is absolutely dire in its customer service. I booked a room for one night for when I needed to be in London for business. I'm a busy man so I booked it online. Come the day before I looked for the email confirmation and could find none. I then emailed them about this and they took nearly the whole day to get back to me for at which point I had got another hotel because it was urgent and because I had received no confirmation I was under the belief that the booking for whatever reason had not gone through. I have never not received a confirmation and I have stayed with many hotels. I then got a confirmation as a reply to my email late in the evening with the cancellation policy. This was to cancel with 24 hours notice to not recieve the charge. Fair enough but UMI hotels failed to give me this in time for me to carry out the cancellation without getting charged. It was their failure and I only had to cancel in the first place because of their complete shambles of customer service. I work in customer service and getting back to someone with an urgent matter in such a rude and late way is not acceptable. They have now charged me £84 which is my grocery bill and electricity for the week. They then try and insinuate that this is my fault. They have two choices. To offer me a full refund asap and i shall take back this review or I will leave this review as well as taking this further to the hotel regulator and chase the money up through all possible channels. This is unacceptable behavior and your staff emailing me bullying and insulting content won't work either.

title: Good Value London Hotel
text: Stayed here in Feb 2005. Good and quiet location, 15 minute walk to Paddington, 5 minutes to Bayswater Tube Stop. Tiny room, but it was clean, the bed was comfy and it had just been decorated. Breakfast was adequate, we had the continental breakfast included in the price and we paid an additional £3 each to also have a fried breakfast. Staff were indiffernt. However as we payed £61 for the two of us, can't really complain.

title: Best to find somewhere else!
text: This hotel is in a good area and in easy walking distance to Bayswater station. The really small room was simply awful - down a flight of (dirty) carpeted stairs, broken window, handbasin awkwardly placed in room, written instructions not to leave food unsealed! Dreadful smell (dead rat?) in passage and lift area. Staff were helpful but not friendly and access to the internet is expensive. Avoid laundry down the road or make sure they rinse clothes well! Found Pret a Manger in the main street for breakfast - free wifi, wonderful hot porridge and honey: see [--]

title: Average English hotel
text: We went for a weekend, a friend and I and had booked this hotel after many considerations of price and location. It can't be defined a three star level hotel, more a two stars one, rooms and bathrooms need a good refurbishment as they are old, paint is cracked and it's peeling off, size of the room is on the small side, sheets were clean and so were the towels. In the bathroom, dove soap and shampoo are provided, you can find a hair dryer, tea and coffee set, a flat LCD tv on the wall. Breakfast is ok, tea, muffin, toasted bread with jam and butter, yogurt with cereals, for me it was enough!location is excellent, it is 5 minutes walk to the Bayswater tube station and 7 to queensway station. Bus stops are even closer if you go to westbourne grove, which is just around the corner.staff is helpful, we asked for the room to be changed when we got there, because there was a horrible reddish stain on the carpet, it looked like they had killed somebody in there and they had given us what I called the "cellar-room": to enter the room you had to go down some narrow steps as the room was on a lower level from the main corridor!they couldn't change the room that night, buy they did the day after and following day room was better, on the fifth floor, nice view of london from the top! All in all this is an average hotel, price was ok, location was good, at the very end we only were there to sleep and shower!

title: Will return on next visit to London
text: I stayed here for one night in a single room. Reception staff checked me in quickly, room was small but for £50, suited my purposes perfectly. Enough room for 1 person and a suitcase with a desk and wardrobe. My room over looked a lovely gated garden. Excellent location, easy walk to Bayswater or Queensway tube stations. Basic breakfast was included and free newspapers provided in the lounge area. I will return here for my next London trip when I need a centrally located, budget hotel

title: I would rather have stayed at the hostel from Quentin Tarininto's movie.
text: Most of the people who work at this hotel are incredibly rude and unprofessional. Expect to be woken up by yelling maids at 6 AM or the weekly fire alarm. The beds move a lot and the floors creak to the point that you will be surprised not to have fallen through the ceiling. I would also like to add that the hotel staff called an unmarked taxi for me and my friends. Despite some nice workers, I found a lot to be incredibly rude. In addition to this, maids will attempt to wake you up during your naps and try to convince you to get out of bed so they can clean. It is not until the 5th "Please come back later" that they will leave. Also, the toilets do not flush.

title: Good value for London
text: I liked the location of this hotel

title: small but cute
text: You need to ask for a room in the front of the hotel and then you might get a balcony (small but it adds character). The men at the front desk were great. We played cards in the bar and met very interesting people. Its just a short scenic walk to Notting hill where you can find just about everything. And Hyde Park is about three blocks away!!!! Great salad and toast for breakfast :)

title: Great value and location
text: I was looking for a good value for money hotel for a solo stay. The Umi Hotel London has updated reception and dining facilities but the rooms and corridors need a new coat of paint and carpet. The bed was comfortable, the room was otherwise clean and I really wasn't there that much during my exploration of London. I had both breakfast and dinner in the hotel dining room. It was all beautifully cooked and great value in pleasant surroundings. Umi hotel is within easy walking distance from Bayswater shops and cafes, Hyde Park, Kensington Palace and the Hop on-Hop Off Tourist bus. If you're looking for value for money the Umi Hotel has it and with new paint and carpet in the hallways and rooms I would give it a high rating. Be aware that there is no fridge so you can't make anything more than a cup of tea or noodles in your room. I'm an Australian traveller who had a fantastic time in London with Umi Hotel as my base.

title: Budget Friendly with Great Staff!
text: I stayed here for one night with 2 girlfriends. We just needed a place to sleep and really weren't fussed about luxury. We were greeted by a lovely friendly receptionist when we arrived in the evening, who seemed genuiniely pleased to see us. Our room was very basic, just 3 beds, a shower,and sink and loo, and it was a little shabby, however everything in the room such as the loo, the shower and the beds were absolutely spotlessly clean. Another good thing about the room was the mirrors, more than enough room for 3 girls to get ready for a night out! The reception, lounge and dining room areas were really nicely decorated and obviously new, and although we didn't eat there the breakfasts looked huge! Another great bonus to this hotel was that they do really, really good coffee! It's rare to find a trained barista in a budget hotel, and as a barista myself, I really appreciated this. So all round, you do get what you pay for, but the staff make it!

title: An average quick stay prior to topdeck
text: I stayed here for three nights prior to starting a topdeck trip. The hotel is quite old. Steps are creaky, floor is uneven everywhere. Bathrooms cramped. However overall its not a bad place to stay if all you need is a bed and shower. Staff were quite helpful though.

title: PLEASANT HOTEL, EXCELLENT VALUE, GREAT LOCATION - BARGAIN!
text: My friend and I stayed at this hotel in November for two nights to do a bit of Christmas shopping in London. The location was fabulous - good tube links and about a five minute walk to Bayswater and Queensway tube stations. It was also amazingly close to Portabello market which was great for us. We got a really good deal for the room which ended up having four beds in (strange but we weren't bothered) it was clean with a decent bathroom, nice shower and the usual TV and amenities. Didn't deal much with staff but they seemed friendly and helpful. We got free continental breakfast which was perfect for our travel needs. There were only two tiny negatives - one being the security of the locker facility. We left our bags on our last day and anyone could have got in there. They were not very careful with the key. Also the curtain pole in our room was a bit old/bent and the curtains didn't fully meet so some light did come through. Overall, an ideal hotel/hostel and an absolute bargain - I am hoping to go back with my boyfriend in the new year. It is just ideal for a cheap weekend away for young friends/couples. Not luxury but a great stay for a great price!

title: Good but......
text: We paid £70 per night for our room which for London we were rather pleased with.... On arrival we were extremely pleased with the location, only a 5 minute walk from Bayswater Tube Station which is on the circle line so really we were in the hub of activity so in a nut shell the location was faultless. The hotel reception was pleasent, well maintained and had a super coffee bar and dining area. It offered a selection of free newspapers and magazines and a wealth of info on London such as maps and guides. Check in was painless however there was an issue with holding money on our credit card for the room which on departure would be released, however this takes 3 days to clear with the bank so was a bit of nightmare. We had reada previous review by someone else saying this so we made sure we budgeted for this. Our room..... On a positive the room was clean, the bed was comfortable and there was tea/coffee making facilities and lovely buscuits which were replentished daily. On a negitive the bathroom, whilst clean, was of a poor standard. The shower screen was siliconed to the bath so it wouldn't move making it difficult to get in and out, I almost slipped twice andade reception aware of this. The carpet throughout, again whilst clean, could do with being replaced but this is only cosmetic and wouldn't prevent me from staying again. I would definately stay in this hotel again and would recommend it but only of you are open minded and aren't expecting The Ritz but want a central location.

title: Umi London - Perfect Location and Price
text: I recently stayed at the UMI on business whilst exhibiting at Earls Court for 4 days. This hotel is brilliantly located in a quiet square near bayswater - loads of good restaurants and pubs on your door step. The hotel staff are incredibly helpful and efficient, the rooms (while a little dated) are very clean and spacious and offer excellent value for money. Reception attended to all my requests and the breakfast and bar staff in particular were very warm and friendly. Recommended base for London. This is a busy and vibrant buzzy central london budget hotel. Karen

title: Excellent Location
text: We were looking for an older English hotel in a great location with friendly staff and we certainly found it with the Westminster Hotel. The Hotel is older so there was a musty odor in the stairwells, but it has elevators that can be used to avoid this. There is a trick to flushing the toilet but the bathrooms are very clean and if you're on the fifth floor, they are very large and have a tub. The bathrooms on the second floor were small and only had a shower. The staff was VERY friendly and eager to help us with directions, bus tours, etc. There is a breakfast room downstairs that served cereal, breads, fruit, yogurt, and coffee. There is a small bar upstairs. The Bayswater Tube Station is a very short walk away and the neighborhood is surprisingly quiet for being in such a great location. We went exploring the first day and ended up in Kensington Gardens... and eventually Oxford Street. It was a nice walk, although we just took the tube back to Bayswater from Bond Street. There is a mall just around the corner, complete with Starbucks, Burberry and a movie theater. There are many cafe's and restaurants all within a couple of blocks. Lots of souvenier shops and many western fast food places like KFC, Pizza Hut, McDonalds, etc. all within a few blocks. As I said... Excellent Location.

title: Family trip to London - Umi is ok
text: Very British standard, anyway clean hotel in the beautiful old building. Renovated but in the British way. Not for the people who want big hotel chain standards. Quite a good situation (Bayswater and Queensway underground stations in 5-10 mins walking distance). A lot of teenager guests who were having fun on the hotel door steps during the night on Friday / Sunday -> very noisy two nights of our five nights. The floors of the old house make noise as well. Have your ear plugs with you :). Beautiful small park in front of the hotel. Good breakfast in nice restaurant. During the breakfast you could see the quiet guests (couples, families) as well. Very international. Umi has a concierge service and for example Mme Tussauds & sightseeing bus tour tickets can be bought in the hotel without queing. Overall: ok.

title: GVFM!
text: OK, this is no five star hotel but it does not advertise itself as one. I got a great rate on my room for a one night stay on a bank holiday weekend (paid just over 40 pounds for a single room). The room was pretty basic to say the least and could have benefitted from some refurb but having paid alot more for London accomodation I was happy enough. There was an en suite with shower facility, again pretty basic but all clean. The location is pretty good with Bayswater tube station a few minutes walk away and some good place to eat very close to the hotel. The hotel itself is set in a quiet square with gardens in the middle making it very quiet. One word of warning though...... this is not the place to be making international phone calls. A quick flick through the hotel brochure brought to light that a three minute call to Australia costs over 23 pounds in this hotel!!!!! No excuse for this nowadays when you get low cost call companies that only charge 3p a minute to Oz!! I would stay here again if I needed a bed for the night in London and did not want to be seriously out of pocket. The staff were pretty friendly and all in all it was good value for money.

title: Theme hotel
text: We stayed the 3/1-3/2003. Little did we know that this was a theme hotel! Think ocean, think ocean liner, think cruise ship. You can imagine yourself on the ocean as you walk to your room. The building is actually several old townhouses that have been connected together to form a larger building. The halls have a distinctive wave in the floor and a step is appropriately placed between the townhouses to sort of level the floors. Speaking of floors, the room floors were so uneven and creaky, not only did you hear the people above you everytime they walked around their room, but you had to be careful about walking in your room. While standing at the sink, make sure you bend one knee so that you can be level at the mirror. The desk drawers had a tendency to open, so we placed a chair in front to keep them closed. (You had to wonder if the floors weren't about to give way. Was this building structurally sound? Who knows!) The cruise theme was carried through to the bathroom. It was the size of a bathroom on a cruise ship. Shower stall and commode in a 3'x6' space! The sink was in the bedroom. The breakfast room is the best part of the hotel. If the rest of the hotel looked like this room, I'd go back again. Breakfast is typical European continental -- yogurt, cheese, meats, breads, cereal, fruit. Don't believe that other reviews of this one!

title: Not a Bad Spot, for Convenience
text: We stayed here before and after a bus tour, as it left from this hotel. I thought it was overpriced for what it was, but all in all we had a comfortable stay. Would stay again under the same circumstances. Pros: - excellent front desk staff, very helpful and friendly - good selection at the restaurant for breakfast and dinner - water supplied in-room free of charge - around the corner from a street packed with restaurants and cafes - several laundromats within walking distance - short walk to the subway - close to Hyde Park - comfortable bed and pillows Cons: - very noisy/creaky floorboards in rooms and hallways - a bit tired around the edges, didn't use shower because it looked a bit scungy - expensive for the quality of the rooms, but you're paying London prices after all

title: Expensive for what it was.
text: The hotel is located in a quiet area close to the tube station and the staff were really friendly. We paid extra for a superior room which apparently had super comfortable mattresses. Ours was uncomfortable with springs poking out. We were expecting a bath but only had the world's smallest shower and it was impossible to watch the TV in bed due to the wall it was attached to. Perching on the end of the bed was the only way to watch it. The floor boards creaked throughout the hotel which kept us awake also. We paid £159 for 2 nights and in my opinion that was far too much. But it was clean and easy to find so if you are looking for only one nights stay this may be ok.

title: Not a bad stay but wouldn't recommend
text: Chose this hotel for its location but to be honest it's not the easiest place to access. If travelling in to Euston you have to change tubes so it's not particulary convenient. It's also not surrounded by much so finding somewhere to eat and drink meant another tube journey. The hotel itself was clean and sufficient for a nights stay but was a bit run down and tatty. The staff were very polite and helpful!

title: Brought back memories of student hall of residence...
text: The check-in area does not look bad at all, but once I got to my room (206 - single room) I opened the door and got a shock. I thought I was back in a student hall of residence. The sink was part of the room, paint was stripping from the walls and the bed in a corner by a window. As I walked towards the bed on a scruffy carpet, the floorboards creaked. That night was pretty windy and even though the bed was average (spring mattress - not foam), the window was rattling and between the rattles I could hear the person next door snoring (could have been worse). Next morning, the breakfast was good (full english served at table, not buffet - 10-15 minute wait though) - and newspapers and magazines (eg Timeout) were free. The following night, I did sleep alot better - as I had got over the initial shock of the room. There were school trippers in the hotel - so it does get busy, and there were not enough tables for breakfast. For £75 a night, midweek, it is not cheap - and I was surprised I could not get a better offer, but there must have been alot happening in London that week. In summary, the room was pretty poor (needs refurbishing) but breakfast is good - and location is excellent. Great for students.

title: Decent budget hotel - good location and friendly reception staff
text: Stayed here before my topdeck european tour. Hotel is a bit old and worn out but overall a v.good location. Room was decent and had all the basics, only negative was the screecy floorboards whenever i stepped on certain areas in the corridors. Great reception staff - was checked in by Jason who was v.friendly and once he realized I was a newbie in London he gave me all the vital information I needed in regards to transport and local attractions and made sure me and my girlfriend were happy with our stay. Good takeaway breakfast for the tour during check out and overall everything was organized between the hotel and topdeck in regards of meeting time and tour departure times. Would recommend for a short stay because of location - about 20 minutes bus to oxford street and the tube stations are a short walk from the hotel too.

title: Great hotel, o.k rooms
text: The hotel is in a great location with two tube stations,restaurants,and shopping close by. The rooms are very small but for a budget hotel, that is to be expected. I didn't spend much time in the room anyway so it didn't bother me. My only complaint would be the en suite bathroom. There was almost no space between the shower and the toilet which made it very difficult to move around. If your looking for a no frills budget hotel than this is a great place to stay.

title: Third rate-avoid unless you're a poor student and can't get a loan from Grandma !!
text: Not as nice as we would have thought. Very hot rooms, very little space. Charged like wounded bulls for wifi. Toilets took some effort to flush. Beds saggy and wrecked my back! The carpets were worn, the floors creaked and the smell of cleaning fluid abounded. A very tired, cheap-feeling place. Avoid if you enjoy decent accomodation.

title: Stay away
text: Old and run down, extremely hot room with windows that can only open 5 cm. Claims to have air conditiong on hotels.com, which is a lie. Filthy pink carpet. Woken up at 8am by someone entering the room after having knocked just once. Couldnt go back to sleep due to a constant noise from the cleaners in the corridor. Shower didnt work when i arrived. It was fixed on 2nd day, but come on... The whole thing was loose and clearly didnt work... did they even clean my shower before i arrived? Big + for helpful and professional staff in the reception. Provided me with a fan that helped on the heat. (its not their fault the hotel is in the condition it is). Having stayed in 10+ London hotels at a similar price level the past years, this was the worst experience.

title: Nice hotel, great location!
text: Clean, basic and really good service. Nice breakfast (you can choose 5 items in a list) that may include capuccino, fruit, muffins and croissant. Near to 2 metro stations giving access to the main subway lines. Nice and safe neighborhood. I certainly reccomend for families and group of friends. Pay attention if you book a room in the top floor... the elevator goes until the 4th and you have to make one by stairs... Not a problem if you dont have heavy luggage.

title: The room smelled badly!
text: The first room we got, smelled badly and had damp/humidity in the walls. The window didn't work properly - and was some places it was covered with mold. :-( We asked in the reception, to get a new room - but the hotel was fully booked. Our first night at the Westminister hotel, was a bad experience. Because of the smell, we had to sleep with the window open all night. The next day, the housekeeper moved our luggage to a new room, with was mutch better. More generally: Good breakfast, but we missed a darker/more heathy bread alternative. The service was ok. The nightguard was really nice, the rest of the staff could have smiled a bit more. :-) The standard of the buidling is poor. The lobby and restaurant is ok (newly renovated, it seems), but the rest of the hotel is a bit shabby. We had problems with the toilets and the shower - everyting is quite old. Awoid room 204!! Next time we visit London, we will try another hotel.

title: Nice hotel, but avoid it in hot weather
text: I stayed at the hotel for a night, on an extremely hot day. In the lobby the temperature was even hotter than in the outside, as well as in the room. The room was nice and clean but very noisy. Breakfast was OK and everybody in the hotel was very kind. Excellent location.

title: Very Good Location
text: I stood four nights at UMI Hotel in London and I was very pleased about its location. The underground stations are near and it is a very quiet area in London, although close to restaurants and cafés, perfect for a night walk. I agree with the other customers about the noise and the flushing problems, but our room was cozy and I slept very well. I will surely come back.

title: Too noisy
text: Stayed in a superior double for five nights this November. The room was a good size, a bit shabby and worn down, but acceptable. No sink in the bathroom, this was kept in the room beneath the TV, which seemed a bit strange. The bed was comfortable, but the floor (and consequently the bed) was slanting so much that I had trouble not rolling off it throughout the night. The floors were also extremely creaky and the walls thin, and as our upstairs neighbors seemed to be a group of young students on a school trip who were not particularly loud but liked staying up until 3 a.m. talking and moving about a lot, this was a rather unlucky combination. I could also mention that there was a problem with our booking when we arrived, the internet company that we had ordered through had only forwarded two of the three room reservations we had booked to the hotel. While I realize that this was not the hotel's fault, and did not blame them in any way for the mix-up, I do wish the staff had been more helpful and welcoming. The young woman that we encountered at the front desk was rather arrogant and rude, but reluctantly let us use the internet without charge to double check our reservation and get the number for the booking company to get the problem sorted. Could have done without her snide remarks, but her colleagues all seemed nice.

title: Great hotel to stay
text: I've just come back from 2 nights at the Umi hotel and I would definitely recommend this hotel to any of my friends and am planning a return visit next year. Its a lovely hotel in a beautiful area only 5 mins from Bayswater tube station. There are plenty of restaurants, bars and other amenities in the area. The staff were extremely pleasant and helpful and we were always greeted with a smile. The continental breakfast was included so helped us to a good start to the day and breakfast is served til 12 if you need a lie in. Our rooms were spotless and were a good size.

title: This Place Is *Very* Hard to Describe"
text: I read the other reviews below, and I can understand how there is confusion about this place. It seems unusual for one small hotel to have so many different price points for rooms. There are business rooms (and business people) here. These are the rooms pictured on the hotel's web site. During my six-night stay, there were groups of American high school students traveling with chaperones and some American college kids. They seemed to all have been placed on the upper floors. Families and regular tourists seemed to have been placed on the lower floors. That's where my room -- room 224 -- was located. Some folks I chatted with stayed here because (1) it is very safe (2) it is bug-free (3) there is a not-too-bad free breakfast that lasts daily until noon (4) it is within walking distance of dozens of restaurants of every possible cuisine (5) the #70 "red bus" stops at the corner (6) two different underground lines are within easy walking distance (7) there is a "we're all in this together" camaraderie among the guests -- some of whom moved out after a 4am fire alarm we had on May 28th. This makes up, somewhat, for the small rooms, the squeaky floors, the cramped ensuites, and the smell of burnt timber noticeable in some parts of the hotel -- and even the broken window sash in my room that I propped open daily with a coffee mug. The nicest things I can say are that this hotel is filled with 'personality' and that I met some really great people here. I'm sure some will be back for another stay. Me? I'll have to think about it.
