title: Spoilt At The Last Moment
text: We stayed at this hotel for 2 nights in one of their superior double rooms and initially were very impressed. The room was spacious, well presented, warm and clean, the bathroom was also clean and had bath and powerful shower. We had complementary dressing gowns though they weren't exactly fluffy, there was also a freeview TV, kettle with tea, coffee and biscuits and 2x bottles of water. The bed was comfy but our nights sleep weren't great. The floorboards in the hallway were very creaky, this was funny at first but then you can hear people up and down at all hours. We were lucky we were at the end of the corridor so I dread how it must have sounded for people further down. The windows are single paned so you can hear everything outside which whilst we were there included some kind of roadworks and what sounded like children trying to kill each other. We had a continental breakfast inculded which included selecting 4 options from a set menu and was very nice. The reception and dining area are well presented and staff seem friendly enough. We had a pleasant stay up until the last moment when we found that under the window where we had left our suitcase for 2 days (still with some clothes in) had soaked up a large amount of damp through the carpet. When we mentioned this to the receptionist on checkout the lady just stared blankly and asked us what we wanted to do about it rather than offering any recompense. Then to top things off the waitress forgot our crossiants at breakfast! The hotel location is great near to a couple of good pubs and casino if you like that kind of thing. Bayswater tube station is a 5 minute walk away. I would have stayed here again until our stay was spoilt by leaving with musty smelling clothes. Also on seeing some of the other photos the standard rooms appear to be a lot less desirable.

title: A cut above
text: Umi definitely provides better value for money than many similarly-priced London hotels, especially if you are able to arrange a favourable rate by booking ahead. Last things first - the room is small, or at least, mine was. But then, what else does one need to do there when in London, other than rest, change clothes and maybe enjoy a cup of tea? My room, Nº 224, had a large window with a VIEW - not something you'll get at every London hotel. The room overlooked an idyllic garden where one could catch sight of squirrels playing

title: Great service and staff
text: I stayed at this Hotel for visting London the service was great from start to finish. Jimmy from the bar was great, breakfast was very good and quick service I have stayed at alot hotels and this breakfast was one of the best. The staff are very helpful. The only bad comment I have is the bedroom they need to be refurbished to make this hotel even better. Thank you for a great stay, I will be coming back!!!!

title: Awesome Location, Friendly staff
text: Stayed at Umi for 4 nights and really liked this hotel. I was originally staying for 2 nights, but added 2 additional nights the week before I arrived to have more time in London. I had booked a quad room, which was not available for the 2 additional nights, but the staff was very helpful when it came time to move to the new room. They got the room ready early in the day for us, so that we could move in right away. Both of our rooms were nice and clean. The hotel was close to the tube. I would stay here again

title: Great location, Good price
text: My girlfriend and I wanted a cheap place to stay in London for 5 nights and Umi was great. Easy check in and the receptionist gave us a map of all the POI around the hotel and where the restaurants were located. The rooms are basic but clean and big enough to not trip over our two large suitcases. The location is great with three tube stations within five minutes walk and lots of cheap restaurants and shops just down the road.

title: Budget as they come
text: I choose this hotel becasue it was cheap but in a nice area. The hotel was a little hard to find even with a taxi driver. I was warmly welcomed by the staff. My room as smallish and the bathroom was small as a cuboard but was decently clean. The furniture was a bit old looking and the window was hard to close and 1 of the staff had to come and give me a hand with it. The breakfast price was a bit pricey, I decided to get breakfast elsewhere for less. The staff are nice and have some good knowledge but most of them are forginers and most live in the hotel as well. No free wifi and have to buy a card to get access to the computer and wifi. floorboard were creaky so you could hear people walking around.

title: Great value
text: Great location and accessibility. Room was nice and comfortable nights sleep. We had a superior room and had everything you need for an overnight stay. Breakfast was great quality and very fresh. We liked the umi logoed coffee! Would definitely stay again.

title: Disappointing room but good location
text: We upgraded to stay in a Grove Room for a few nights but were very disappointed. The towels were stained and bathroom was small, and the 'quality' coffee and tea were basic. The bathrobes didn't match and overall the room was quite shabby and needed work. The bedhead was attached to the wall by two short screws that didn't hold when leaning on it to watch TV. The location was good - being walking distance to Metro station, restaurants, pubs and other essentials like pharmacy and groceries (but there's no fridge in the room so don't buy anything that needs refridgerating!). The hotel has a cafe and restaurant but we chose to eat out as there were lots of great options like Thai and Indian and fast food options if you're after something quick.

title: Decent budget hotel
text: Decent budget hotel. Very good service... friendly and helpful. Decent free breakfast (although not buffet so not as filling as others). Full English available though for modest charge. Bed was comfortable. Rooms clean. Carpets in rooms a bit worn and in need of repair but overall room was pleasant. Located on quiet square a couple blocks off street with tons of ethnic eateries. 10 minute walk to two tube stops and Kennsington Park. Stayed here for 7 nights.

title: Great friendly service and brilliant location at brilliantly reasonable prices
text: The title says it all but to expand this is my 2nd stay here and everything you need for a business tourist trip to London is in walking or rental cycle distance. Excellent public transport facilities too. Great range of reasonably priced restaurants especially Middle Eastern on Queensway and surrounding area.

title: Didn't quite live up to its advertising, but still a good choice
text: We stayed for one night only (as planned - we didn't walk out!), wanted somewhere inexpensive, convenient for an appointment the next day, in a nice area and not depressing, and it ticked all these boxes. The decor of the room was a little odd, I think they'd taken over another hotel and not yet redecorated. It didnt fit their young and groovy image, and was a bit tired and old-fashioned, though it was pleasant and inoffensive. I would guess the main new additions would have been the bed (very good, though not big for americans) and the flatscreen digital TV with freeview, a nice touch. We had the executive room, not sure it was worth it, though it wa a good size so maybe the standards are tiny. The bathroom was minute - just a toilet and shower - but was freshly painted. As well as the reasonable price and fairly nice room, the best thng was the great location - on a lovely and very quiet square with a park in the middle. But a block away from Westbourne Grove, with more restaurants and shops than you could shake a stick at. Frankly I can forgive the odd loose floorboard for the beautiful old building we were in - if you want standardisation, go to a Holiday Inn (the hotel does have a lift, though) I wouldn't come here for my honeymoon, but I'd happily stay again.

title: Very disappointed
text: We decided to use this hotel following high recommendations from this site however I was extremely disappointed. The initial entrance and reception was very pleasant and the staff were very friendly. On entering our room, 116 at the rear of the hotel, the first thing we noticed was it was in dire need of modernisation. Although it was fairly large, the sink was in the main bedroom (which took up a quarter of the room), and there was very little room between the bed and sink.., how this passed a health and safety check, I will never know. Thank god we didn't need to get out in an emergency. The taps in the sink both ran hot water so we had to buy bottled water to clean our teeth. Despite being at the rear of the hotel, there was noise throughout the night, (from inside the hotel), ie creaking floor boards and doors banging and if you want a lie in, well forget it..., the hoover starts at 8.30 am. Despite all the negatives, the hygiene was of a very high standard but I would not wish to go back. Also on a positive note, it was situated in a very pleasant part of London and within a couple of minutes from the hotel, you had all the shops and restaurants you could wish for.

title: Conveniently located
text: This small little hotel is conveniently located close to several tube stations and portobello road. I stayed here while on a spring break trip with my college class. The place was fairly clean and quiet. We had our own bathroom and shower, television in the room, armoire for our clothes, iron in the room, tea and coffee, etc.... They provided complimentary breakfast for everyone staying there and had a fairly reasonable little bar area with a few TVs in it. The only complaint is that the mattress was a little funky. Whenever i would lay down the end of the mattress would pop up into the air haha. All in all i would stay here again though.

title: Great location, nice for the price
text: We stayed here for 4 nights at a fabulous rate I found through the UK tourist website. I agree with a lot of what the others have said. The rooms are clean (staff seems very hardworking) but a lot of things are old and a little run down. Rooms are small and bathrooms are tiny but servicible. We did notice noice from upstairs neighbors, but I've had the same problem in lots of hotels this is extremely difficult to fix and in an old building like this one probably next to impossible. The service was very good and we liked the simple breakfast. The neighborhood is beautiful and quiet, while being only a couple of blocks away from the underground, shopping, restaurants, and of course Hyde Park. Our three teens liked their room and the flat screen. Only real complaint was no air conditioning. It was pretty stuffy at night, and we had to leave the windows open all the time. The windows opened very wide but we were on the fourth floor and there were no screens. If I had young children I would have been seriously concerned this is a real safety hazard.

title: Great value in a great location
text: I spent two nights at Umi and found it a nice, no-frills hotel in a great location. My room was small, but comfortable, and looked out on a nice park across the street. The bed was comfortable, the shower hot, and the hotel quiet. I don't ask for a whole lot more. The staff were very friendly and helpful, and the internet computers were reasonably priced. When I arrived, the lobby was sweltering (it was a hot day), and my room had no air conditioning, but it was still comfortable. Less than 10 minutes' walk to the nearest Tube station (Bayswater) and some nice restaurants. I'd definitely stay here again.

title: Can't really compare it to other hotels in London
text: Because it was my first visit and the only hotel that I've stayed at in London. The staff were nothing but friendly - and I mean every hour of the day. Even the maid was pleasant and gave me extra towels. (By the way they don't supply washcloths). They would smile and acknowledge me every time I walked in the door. I had a single room, being that it was only me. They placed me in a room that was midway between two levels so there weren't any rooms on either side of me. I arrived at 7:30am and they immediately had a room for me. Likewise for my parents who had arrived at the same time 3 days earlier. Neither of us had booked an extra night for this, they just gave it to us. The single room is very, very small. Compare it to an elongated cubicle. There was a single bed with a down comforter and a fleece blanket for the cover. No top sheet, but the comforter was to die for! Pillows were feather but hard as brick and flat & small. Reverse cycle airconditioner along with a separate furnace heater, so I could run the airconditioner at night - which I did every night. The rooms were at a comfortable temperature, but it did become a bit stuffy due to the size. TV has seven local stations. And it was clean - something that I check at every hotel. They don't vacuum daily though. Bathroom is extremely small and you sort of have to rotate the handle on the toilet almost 360 degrees to flush. That was amusing but time consuming. There's a shower stall, but you can't bend down to pick up your soap. I'd say if you're bigger than a US size 12, then you'd have trouble navigating around the bathroom. I kept hitting my elbows and I'm not a size 12. My parents' room had a bathtub that was so deep that my able-bodied dad needed help getting out. In other words, you need a step ladder. Two workstations with internet access in the lobby. Payment by credit card. My stay there overall was quite pleasant until New Year's night when they put someone in the room above me at 4:30am. The floors must be wooden because the footsteps came through loud and clear. Smoking was another issue for me and it was a constant annoyance every night. My parents ate at the continental breakfast most mornings and was surprised at the end to be presented with a bill for 13 pounds for each breakfast (that's for each person). Location is about two blocks from Victoria Station (providing you come out at the right entrance) and I felt extremely safe walking back and forth alone both night and day. Victoria Station is nice to shop and eat. The Station has KFC, McDonalds (I think I counted 3 altogether), Burger King (don't forget to ask for condiments though), Pizza place, steak restaurant and other eateries. Has nice dress shops for men and women, grocery market, electronic store, record store, several small pharmacy type stores, health store, hair accessory (Claire's I think), jewelery store, Avon, book store and many many more. Pick up the bus tour (Big Bus was better than Original) right at the Station. A hint

title: Great Value
text: Stayed here for one night while attending a concert near by. Seen the reviews here and for the price it is one of the cheapest in London so wasn't expecting much. But have to say I was surprised room was clean and big enough staff on the desk friendly and was in a nice neighbourhood.

title: Good value
text: Good value hotel in a convenient location. The lobby and public areas are very nice but the rooms are a bit outdated. Breakfast could be better. Overall, a good address in London if budget is a concern. We were there with a group of 16 people and the hotel was perfect for the needs of the group.

title: No Aircon!
text: Would be fine to stay there anytime outside of summer but pretty much July, August, September I would not advise it. The staff were helpful and the location is very good but it is difficult to appreciate any of that when you can't sleep. We stayed here as our Top Deck tour left from there the following morning, would be ok for one night but no more than that.

title: Value for money in the heart of London
text: A group of 10 of us stayed here for a friends hen weekend. We chose this hotel as it was close to where the restaurant was, and it is also close to many Tube stations - Bayswater, Queensway and Notting Hill. The hotel is situated off the main road in a quiet leafy location. The hotel also has a restaurant bar on the groundfloor, together with a party bar in the basement. On the night we stayed they were holding a karaoke night there. As there was a large group of us staying, we had a couple of quad-rooms and a triple room. They were able to locate our rooms together at the end of the 5th floor. The rooms varied in size but all had bunk beds, toilet & shower, tea/coffee making facilities, hairdryer, flat screen tv etc. The only downside was that the windows only opended about 3 inches, We arrived on what seemed to be the hottest day of the year so it was a bit warm. However, the staff were very friendly and provided us with as many fans as they could lay their hands on. The price included a continental breakfast. You choose four items from a list, I chose a fresh fruit salad, yoghurt, toast and tea. Very nice. I would definitely stay here again as it was affordable, good quality and in easy reach of London's attractions.

title: Beware!
text: My friend and I stayed at the Umi once at the outset of our trip before flying to Italy and also at the conclusion before flying home to the US. The first room had the sink in the bedroom. The sink had two faucets, one for hot and one for cold, and neither worked very well. There is a trick to getting the toilet to flush by repeatedly pumping the handle. The carpeting had huge stains and the bed gave me a backache. The shower was impossible to turn off and you needed to grab a towel in order to get a strong grip on the shut off valve. When staying in the second room, all the same problems remained except now our crummy sink was in the bathroom. What amazed me is that, on one hand I was worried that I couldn't flush the toilet, yet I could watch a flat screen tv. I'm not sure Umi has its priorities straight. I'm not used to luxury when I travel but this was a little too much for me.

title: AVOID!
text: Avoid this hotel. It is horrible and expensive. The photos lie how this hotel is bad! There are others in the region much better and cheaper! Reception at first glance seems to an interesting hotel, but when you take the key and lift the nightmare begins.

title: Disappointed
text: I expected an average 3* hotel with good quality/price. But... The 1st room, was over-heated +++. i had to have the wondow wide open all the time. The TV didn't work & the only way I could watch was by sitting in the sink (yeah the sink isn't in the bathroom). I changed room. The 2nd was just between the stairs & the lifts and above the entrance of the hotel. I didn't sleep for 3 nights. A real nightmare.

title: Westminster Hotel
text: Good priced hotel with a nice location. The room was a bit shaby and needed some repair, but was clean and everything worked.

title: Great Location and Service
text: Stayed in this Hotel for 1 night. Hotel is well organised and clean. I paid an excellent rate via Booking.com and honestly expected a lot less for the money paid. Yes the Hotel is showing signs of age but the location is so good that it really does not matter. Bars and restaurants really close by and tube stations to get you to central London in 5 mins makes for a relly good experiance

title: disappointing...
text: This hotel has been renamed as "Umi" and I booked one of their "Grove Rooms" which was billed as their best rooms, with bathrobes, teas, welcome snacks and mineral water. (No mineral water or welcome snacks were provided in my room!) The room was shabby, but they had tried to dress it up as a more modern "boutique style" room. My biggest complaint was the shower. I expect a power shower in a hotel, not a domestic white plastic shower. The water pressure was appaling. I've never known anything like it! I didn't feel clean, after standing under the pitiful trickle and I wouldn't book this hotel for this reason only. It seemed like an old-fashioned, chain hotel which was well past its sell by date had tried to fix itself up a bit and relaunch, but the main areas they should have concentrated on were neglected. I'd rather they replaced the carpet or installed a decent shower as gave flavoured teas and bathrobes. The hall areas were dowdy and dull, a bit creepy actually. The lift was tiny and rather 70's in style with wood panelling. The girl at reception who checked me in was really nice, and all the staff was pleasant enough. There's computers with broadband (fee) in the reception area, and a coffee shop and nice lounge area with newspapers. It seemed like a lot of students and tour groups were staying when I was, but I didn't hear any noise.

title: Not what we were hoping for
text: The reason I booked this hotel was its fantastic website promising ' a new concept in hotels...to offer you some of the best London hotel accommodation, with excellent service and facilities, all at a value price.' As a young couple this really sounded up our street! I kept an eye on the price of a Grovsner Room as it fluctuated right up to £165 per night and after finding it for just under £80 I jumped at the chance of a 'great deal' expecting a fresh, vibrant and funky hotel with comfortable, contempory rooms (again a reflection of the website). On arriving at the hotel we werre definatley impressed with the location and the hotel building (it really was a Notting Hill setting). The staff were helpful as promised and everything was looking good! The only problem was on enterering our room... The furniture looked like something you would pick up at a car boot sale and the bathroom was so small it couldn't even fit a sink in it which subseqently was in our bedroom. It definatley was not the type of room we had been promised...and paid extra for as a Grovsner Room. I even had to call downstairs to double check we had the right room. I know that finding a room in London for under £100 a night can be a challenge but I really believe that Umi Hotels are promoting a false idea of what the hotel has to offer.

title: Cheap & convenient but could do better
text: Stayed at Umi twice

title: Great find!
text: Did alot of research before booking at UMI Hotel London but have had a great 4 day stay with them! The neighbourhood is quiet and friendly and a short stroll to Bayswater gets you directly on the London Tube to everywhere! (Picadilly, Kensington, Westminster). The hotel and the room were small and old but everything was clean and nice. Staff is friendly and would def book there again.

title: No frills, good value
text: I stayed for 2 midweek nights. The hotel is best described as shabby with flaky paint and temperamental plumbing. That would be unacceptable in a more expensive hotel. It also would be unacceptable in a cheap hotel however the UMI's saving grace is that its staff are polite and helpful and will rectify any problems. In my case I requested a room change due to the shower and WC not working which was dealt with immediately and without fuss. I would stay there again for these reasons as well that the location is excellent

title: More hostel than hotel.
text: More like a hostel than a hotel. Room tiny. Floorboards really old so squeaky. Toilet practically in the shower as so small.Staff were friendly at reception and in the bar area. Located near Bayswater tube station so that was handy.

title: A cheap place to rest your head in London
text: Basic small accommodation, great for cutting costs in a big city. Ideal base to see the sights. More suited to friends travelling together who are not too worried about luxury. Choice of breakfast. I would use again.

title: Expensive, no AC, and not very clean
text: I stayed here before taking a bus tour. I paid way too much money for the room which did not have AC. It was about 90 outside, granted the hottest day of the summer, and there was no relief staying inside the hotel. The space inside the room wasn't too bad considering London standards. The location was pretty close an underground station so that was a plus. The bathroom sink had cracks in it and the shower stall had not been cleaned since who knows when. Would not recommend unless you can get it under $40 a night. And that's dollars not pounds.

title: It was Amazing i give it a 5 star!!!
text: It was a very tidy and very relaxing. In the rooms they lay out tea with biscuits and a kettle! We payed £40 and it was worth the money!!! The food there is very nice eg. the breakfast. You get alot of channels on the television like CBBC Entertainment and much more.There very kind at the desk and help you with your luggage so therefore i recommend this hotel for you.

title: Great Location and friendly staff
text: We stayed here at the beginning of Sept 2012 as a family of 2 adults and 2 kids under 4. We had a triple bunk bed room with a crib as well. The room was crowded when we had our stroller in it but without that or the crib, there was plenty of room for the price. The elevator only goes to the 4th floor but for the price I didn't mind hauling our stuff up an extra flight. The hotel does attract a lot of students and got loud on a couple nights. The restaurant was very well priced and had good food for dinner. We also had the continental breakfast included and this was enough food for us to make it to lunchtime when we were out and about. The internet was 2 pounds per 20 minutes. Or you could go around the corner to the Starbucks and use their wi-fi. The location of the hotel was great. Close to 3 metro stops and about 15 minutes from Paddington station which we used to arrive from the airport directly. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The only negative was the rooms were a bit grungy and the towels one day looked dirty. Overall, if you're looking for a reasonably priced place to stay that is close to attractions and metro stops, then I'd recommend Umi hotel.

title: Nice stay
text: We were 3 persons who stayed 3 nights in May in a double and single room. Very good service in reception and breakfast room. Good breakfast apart from tea and coffee which did not taste very much. Big double room, but very small single room. Comfort in beds could have been better. Otherwise great location in quet surroundings

title: Tread the creaky boards...
text: Found the hotel (eventually after some wandering!) in a relatively nice bit of London, fairly conveniently located near Bayswater Tube station (maybe 10 mins walk if you don't get lost). The walk to the room down the corridor was bizarre... most lumpy floor I've ever seen, hilarious really! But the room (by London standards) was pretty big, clean enough and not too noisy. OLD but ok. Staff were nice, wifi has a fee (don't pay... head down the road and use it somewhere where you eat). It's not too bad for the price.

title: Not a great experience
text: This place was a bit dodgey. The rooms were dirty and carpets and walls were stained. The toilet the didnt flush and the shower was horrible. We didnt complain as it was just for a night but definitely not a place i would recommend anyone stay at. The people working there were, however, extremely helpful and friendly.

title: Small room but good location. Bad for car parking.
text: It was ok. The room was very small which i knew beforehand but it was clean and good enough for a couple of days. I had big hassles getting out of the hotel though as there is no where to park and load up the car and i had to park down the street and try to ring up and pay for parking even though i was leaving and only wanted to grab my cases and go. I tried ringing and ended up spending a heap more $$ on the phone call than the parking fee. I was really annoyed as all i wanted to do was go and i thought it was all ridiculous. They should get special permission for a drop off/pickup bay. it is in a good location, near Hyde park and Oxford St.

title: Sub Standard
text: Warm water runs from the cold top Rooms are hot with no air conditioning Noise from the surrounding streets is appauling (loud music from residents to the early hours) Poor maintenance of rooms Showers run at a trickle No mineral water provided in rooms even though the website indicates this is provided - perhaps it evaporated in the heat! Cleaning staff make to much noise and have no consideration for guests or do not disturb signs. Walls are not very thick between rooms you can sometimes hear next doors TV!! All the rooms are in serious need of some updating.

title: Umi is okay but ...
text: I stayed at Umi hotel for six nights a week ago. The information given in other reviews was quite accurate so I knew what to look forward to and expect. The service is very good the concierge was more than helpful. The breakfast – You can choose from 4 items. One can also ask for extra toast to add to the croissant. The fact that the sink is in the room didn't disturb me at all. The mattress on the other hand wasn't even & not hard enough. In another review it said that biscuits and free water were provided - I didn't get such addition but I did get a small fridge at my request. My room faced the leinster garden – there was no disturbing noise and I slept with my window open as far as it was able to open. I want to add that it is not permitted to smoke in the hotel and smoking was one of the reasons I chose this hotel (out of others as location, price & information I read in the reviews) – it said in the description there are non smoking rooms but not that smoking is not permitted at all. This made me stay at the hotel as little as possible and as a solo traveler I intended to return not very late in the evenings and watch television in my room. There is a problem with the television – only 4 channels and not even BBC1. For a traveler that wants to see the news – it is a disappointment..

title: Great Hotel!!!
text: I will deifintely return to this hotel. It is situated in a safe neighbourhood with all the amenities one could need. The hotel staff were friendly and very informative. They even booked my London bus tour from the hotel. They have a great cab service which is reliable and reasonable. There is a restaurant and bar in the hotel if you are up for a nightcap before bed. The nearest tube station is Bayswater and it is very central (on the central line) so not far from anywhere you wish to go. The rooms were clean and comfortable. I would stay here again without question and their rates are fantanstic in comparrison to others in the neighbourhood. I highly recommend the Umi!!

title: Pretty Average
text: First of all, I wasn't expecting anything amazing for this price in London. The location was good for me, easily within walking distance from the Bayswater tube with a hand luggage wheely case. The room was very small, the bathroom was smaller still. It was very hot, but if I opened the window there was some noise, although not really enough to keep me awake. Although I am a heavy sleeper! Breakfast was nothing special, but served in a very friendly manner, so that was good.

title: Won't go back
text: This was a disappointing hotel. The room was tiny, the beds were the most uncomfortable I have slept in for a long time. My young daughter and I swapped beds after the first night as neither of us could sleep - we had both hoped to find some respite in the opposite bed but unfortunately both beds were equally bad. The mattresses were hard and lumpy and the beds were really very small. I was disturbed by noise from the adjoining rooms at night which made matters worse. The whole place is looking very tired although I have to say it was very clean although the carpet in our room was so thread-bare it was hard to imagine it would ever be really clean again. The breakfast room needs a thorough re-fit, and the selection of food was not at all inviting. The staff seemed to be young and inexperienced although they all did their best at being professional. I definitely would say this hotel is over-priced and I won't be going back.

title: Nice Hotel Small Room Very Little Storage Space
text: Hotel was really nice but room was small and very little storage space for clothes it had a nice bar restaurant on site

title: All Location and not much else
text: We paid £60 for somewhere to stay on a week night. The location is brilliant, a short walk form Portobello and the reception were very helpful at 12am. The hotel and hotel rooms though have seen much better days. It is a great cheap place if you just need to ut your head down for the night but do not come expecting too much.

title: A great bargain
text: Just back from several nights at the Westminster. I'd reserved a double "Grove" room for my husband and I, and it was fine - definitely one of the rooms that HAS been recently refurbished, and very quiet both day and night. It was a bargain at 69pds per night. All furniture and fixtures were new, the bed was very comfortable with plenty of pillows and a great new comforter/duvet, and the bathroom was newly redone as well, with plenty of hot water and good water pressure. The size of the room was perfectly adequate - certainly not huge but I've had smaller rooms for much higher prices both in London and the continent. It's true that the staff wasn't very personable but they dealt adequately with what few issues we had. For example- the computers they have for guests to use (for a small fee...1hr for 3 pounds) were not hooked up to printers. When I needed to print something the staff let me email my documents to them, and they printed them right out, with no extra charge. Apparently the breakfast has recently changed from some sort of continental buffet to ordering off of a limited continental menu, still included in the price. We never attempted the cooked breakfast as the cereal, fruit, juice, coffee and croissants were enough to hold us until lunchtime. The location was excellent and we didn't experience any of the problems with the neighborhood mentioned by others. Close enough to the Bayswater, Queensway and Nottinghill Gate underground to get anywhere you want to go, but away from traffic and clubbing noise. Lots of good restaurants all around, from pubs to any kind of ethnic you want to try. All in all, we would stay at the Westminster again, it was a real value for the price.

title: Two star.
text: No way a three star hotel. The building and the rooms particularly were very tired. The girls at the reception were very nice and helpful. Thank you! Also waitresses serving the breakfast were professional and nice. Thank you! Breakfast was good. The location of the hotel is excellent. Nice neighborhood and easy access to basically everywhere. Could stay here again.

title: The indian guy at the reception is very rude and unprofessional
text: Hotel well positioned, rooms very small but not bad... Never met a guy at the reception more rude and unprofessional...I asked to the indian guy at the reception an information to get Luton airport and he didn't support me...he had been very rude...never met a person from the staff more rude and unprofessional

title: Well situated, clean quiet with enthusiastically helpful staff
text: Umi is near 2 tube stations, unlimited buses and 2 or 3 ? bike stations. Good accessability. The number of eating choices available in Queensway and particularly Westbourne Grove nearby made this a good choice for my business stay. The room was spacious (London standards), clean and comfortable. There was a lot of charm covered up by recently applied paint. Nothing classy but hey! The staff was, without exception bright, cheerful and, above all helpful. Still do NOT enjoy having to pay for internet access, but at least it worked and the weekly rate was OK. In all, well situated and did the job.

title: Cute!
text: Charming! Stayed at the Westminster last week on vacation with my wife and found the hotel to be much larger than I had imagined. Great size room (Grove Double) with robes! The lobby/bar area is recently renovated with plasma screens & a coffee/alcohol bar where a delicious breakfast is served each morning from 7-11. Also a great spot to unwind after walking all day. Pros: location (Notting Hill), charm, decent size room, price Cons: small bathroom, a bit smokey (for families), kind of hard to find initially (all the building are in the same style) Would definitely stay there again for the price and the location.

title: Wonderful stay with great staff.
text: I recently stayed at the UMI London hotel this October. Me and my husband had travelled to London to visit our daughter. Whilst he went to pick her up I decided to go to the hotel to check in. I'd arrived around 1:00pm but was too early as check in time was at 2pm. I was greeted by two very welcoming receptionist. One of them named Selay was very helpful during the whole stay. She made sure I could check in at 1pm by moving things around as I looked completely tired out and needed a lie down. After checking in I wasn't very happy with the room as it was too small for my liking. So she also managed to move me to another room even though it was completely busy at reception. It was definitely a very pleasant stay after that. I'd recommend anyone to stay here considering how friendly the staff is. The two receptionist Selay and the trainee girl at reception that day definitely made it worthwhile.

title: Nice enough for a wee break.
text: Stayed at the Umi hotel for 3 nights in a double room in mid June,the place has the look of an old hotel that has been done up on the cheap,but at least its trying.The staff were all helpfull and happy enough and the "tick your own breakfast "order cards were ideal as most seem to have little spoken English.I dont think there is one straight wall or level floor in the building but hey, its not my mortgage!The nights were very stuffy and the rooms could do with a fan,(I`m sure Ikea has a range for you Mr Umi )apart from that we had a nice stay.Ideal base for a few days

title: A Great Spot
text: If you want a room in a lovely area of expensive London that won't break the budget, I highly recommend the Umi for every reason stated in previous reviews. Staff is very friendly and helpful, the public spaces - lobby, bar and restaurant - are charming, warm and welcoming, location is great. Our room and bathroom were very tiny as is often the case in Europe so this did not trouble us. As others have said, the room was in great need of some attention to aesthetics, but both the room and bathroom were clean and fresh and that counts more for these budget travelers than schmancy surroundings to sleep in. If you are getting on an early morning tour bus as we did, the restaurant will pack you up a little breakfast to take along. We did not want to pay for Wi-Fi so the concierge pointed us to Starbucks for free Wi-Fi just two blocks away. We will definitely return to the Umi on our next visit to London.

title: It had bunk beds!
text: I unfortunately had to travel with work last minute and couldn't find a hotel under £200 so went to late rooms and found the Umi hotel. It was located in bayswater so this was perfect for my requirements. When I arrived, very hot and tired having travelled from Scotland, I was made to wait until 2pm as this was the check in time and the rooms apparently weren't ready prior to this. When I got assigned my room I was informed that it was on the top floor (6th) and the lift only went to the 5th floor so I would have to carry my luggage up the stairs. When I eventually got to my room I was greeted with black metal framed bunk beds and a single beside it. After I managed to squeeze my way through the door and past the beds I discovered a rather unpleasant bathroom with dirt in the bath, a very smelly shower curtain and limited toilet paper. When it eventually came to having to use the bedroom I found that the curtains were hanging off the rail at both ends. The weather necesitated opening a window only to find a noisy air conditioning unit right outside. All in all not a great nights sleep, especially as the vacuum created by other guests opening and closing doors forced my room door to rattle loudly. Hope to never stay here again...

title: Delightful and cosy
text: Great hotel- the staff is friendly and the rooms are clean, warm and welcoming. The bed was very creaky and at imes uncomfortable, but still one of the better rooms I have encountered! Shower was too small for my spouse.

title: Good hotel for the price
text: This weekend I spend 2 nights in this hotel. I stayed in many hotels in London and this hotel was a real surprise when I arrived ! The hotel is located in the lively neighbourhood Bayswater, few minutes walk from Starbucks, all kinds of restaurants, shops, supermarkets, the Whiteley mall and 2 undergroundstations Bayswater and Queensway. The hotel is located in a quiet street so no noise from the busy streets. The hotel reception and lobby were really nice and all the staff was friendly. Breakfast was very good too ! Buffet style but with lots of things to choose from ! The hotel has 2 elevators and the hallways are ok. My room no. 222 (twin room) was small but clean and everything you need. Coffee and tea making facilities and iron bord and iron. Good small room. Overall this hotel is a great hotel for this price !! (I booked through the hotelwebsite 49 GBP per night for a twin room).

title: Never again....
text: I only stayed there because the tour I was doing did most of their departures from this hotel. The staff were very friendly and helpful and it was a great location but they were the only good points, certainly wouldn't stay there again but you do get what you paid for. There was always noise of some sort, fair enough they had a club downstairs but after a certain hour, say 1am, they could have at least turned the music down. The rooms were very cramped and are in desperate need of a refurb. Depends on what money you want to pay but I'd rather pay more and have a good nights sleep next time!

title: Over priced.
text: I stayed at this hotel in July, and found it to be considerably overpriced. I stayed tonights and was quite disapointed in the general up keep of the hotel. The outside looks amazing and it fits in well with its surrounding area. The reception and breakfast area is also quite enjoyable. The rooms however are out dated. The bed was not very comfortable, and the window did not open very far so the room was quite stuffy. Its location is great if you intend on staying in the area of Bayswater, there are alot of local business. overall the hotel is reasonable, its is just overpriced.

title: Non trustable hotel with bad service
text: I stay 2 nights and on day 2, they do not clean the room and no change of existing 2 towels. When I ask the front desk for help, the assistant FOH manager Jason Dominguito and a guy tell me that they change their policy that only will clean the room after 2 days stay. And they point out that “ I notice you now, this is our new policy ” and there have a letter in your room mention this policy and “this is your matter do not read the letter”. When I ask the place of the letter , their reply is “inside the drawer”. And I find the letter and even mentioned that the bed sheet will be changed after 4 days stay. I really feel doubt that whether everything is really changed on the date I stay. Although I request them to change room for me but they say fully book, I still can find room available on Online booking on same room type at that moment. And they lie on me that they inform the agency and online platform about this new rule but I know it is not true because all online booking website information is uploaded by the hotel. Don’t stay in this hotel. Bad attitude to the guest.

title: Awful hotel
text: Me and my wife booked this hotel as we were attending the nearby tabernacle notting hill for a gig. We arrived quite late so checked in without really seeing the room or hotel the staff were friendly. When we got back to the room later we were shocked it was dated but worse than that it was dirty. We were considering leaving then. But stayed the night as it was late. Too make a bad situation worse the next morning I found a cockroach in the bathroom. Worse hotel I've ever stayed in.

title: Would not recommend
text: Arrived to the hotel at 3pm to be told our room would not be ready for 10 mins, arrived back 15 minutes later to be told they did not know when the room would be ready, pretty unacceptable when check in is 3 and considering check out is 11! We ended up having to tell the rude receptionist as much so she eventually called house keeping to be told the room was in fact ready!! On getting to the room we were extremely disappointment with its state, the decor was extremely dated, wallpaper was falling off in areas, there was different colour plaster in area, we only had 2 towels even though 3 of us were staying, the mould in the window was shocking and the paint was very flaky, bathroom was just as bad, was extremely small, mouldy,cracks in the sink and bath and could barely use the dial to change the temperature of the shower, please see pictures, would love to add more to show the full extent but could only upload 10. The next day house keeping never even came to the room. The room was extremely warm and with the location of our room, at the fire escape we were unable to keep the window open. On the morning of check out we tried to get the hotel to call us a taxi to be told the hotel had no taxis and we needed to walk around and flag one down, horrendous attitude at 7am in the morning. The hotel is in a good location but would definitely recommend anyone to pay more and look elsewhere,it would be worth it.

title: Good location but not a relaxing hotel
text: We booked this as a one night stay before heading to the airport. Run down, needs sprucing up. Wifi cuts out a lot. The room was very dark & could hear anyone who was in the corridor or the staff office. They also seem to start cleaning very early. Probably wouldn’t stay again.

title: Practical, Not Fancy
text: Pros. Hotel is just a 100 meter walks from Bayswater tube station, with Circle Line you can reach to almost all attraction in London. Room has a heater air con, not plate type, it warm up the room pretty quick. Surrounding has a lot restaurant, Asian, Italian, convenient marts. A few hundred walk away to Hyde Park, beautiful park. Bed are hard, but it suits me, sleep comfortably. In room has a couch,l and coffee table although make up desk area is a little bit tiny. Hotel has a little small lift. Very small, but it is better than No, especially if you have a big suitcase with you. Reception are good. Cons. From Paddington to Bayswater, there are no lift or elevator, a few fly of stairs you need to climb. To get into lobby a few steps of stairs you need to walk up. Wall, some furniture and toilet fitting show sign of aging. But it still works well.

title: OMG!!!!
text: What can I say but I have never stayed in a hotel as poor as this. I had been booked a single room for 3 nights. When I saw it, I couldn't believe it. It was ridiculously small approximately 8' x 8' with what could only be described as a child's bathroom. I complained and was changed to 404. It is slightly larger with peeling wallpaper, damp on the ceiling, scum on the bath and taps and is excessively warm. Avoid!!!!!! Time to find somewhere else.

title: COMMENTS
text: Good overall nice hotel and friendly staff able to find shops near by and can find lots of restaurants .great location .value for money and convenience for the transportation. even some of my friend I recommended did enjoy it .well done

title: Great location but.....
text: Very, very small room. Very, very small elevator. One tiny, tiny bar of soap for four nights. People at front desk knew NOTHING about navigating area, recommending restaurants, etc. Breakfast at the hotel restaurant was horrible. Dirty cups and plates. It seemed that the hotel was not prepared for guests. HOWEVER, the hotel was in a good location, around the corner from two different underground stops and near both the hop on and off bus stop and several local trams. Bottom line is......this place is all about location, location, location. If you can deal with the other inconveniences, you CAN get a decent night's sleep and a hot shower to set you off for a day of touring!

title: Do not expect luxury but worth staying...
text: My son and I spent 5 nights at Berjaya Eden and we enjoyed every moment as the hotel was just half a minute away from the Underground and all the local food stores. You can't imagine how important this is after a very tiring day. It is almost easier than staying in a luxury hotel with a big entrance and hallways where we would have to walk more. It is a typical big London house with narrow corridors and modest sized bedroom converted to a hotel. If you are planning to use the hotel facilities, there is only bar and restaurant available. If you want to spend time in your room and enjoy the view then you must ask for rooms facing the street as our room 510 was facing to a church next to the hotel but we did not mind at all as we left very early and came late.

title: Very well based but poorly managed hotel
text: I arrived at the Berjaya to my prebooked double room and found it to be in the shape and dimensions of a mouse trap. They changed my room. In the new room the shower water temperature was unstable, and the niagara (flush water of the toilet) was unable to remove residual feces - the stream was too weak. I asked the plumber, who came over and apparently fixed both problems - only to reappear in no time. I asked him again, he came again (I was covering my nudity with a towel), and again it was no use. I gave up and did my best to manage keeping my grievances to myself. I fought with the niagara by pouring hot water into it, i.e. was cooking my dungs, with the inevitably resulting smell. Later on, I was expecting a visitor who came to be interviewed for a job. The girl in the reception told him I had checked out. When he insisted on being connected to my room, she told him the line was occupied. Later, when I inquired into these peculiarities she narrated, with ever-increasing enthusiasm that a guest whose first name was identical with mine had really left (the poor chick was not taught to check for the surname as well) and the line, well the line, ah, she asked the technician to see what was wrong about it. This gentleman, invited to be interviewed, kept waiting patiently in the lobby (he needed the job) and I was waiting for him impatiently in my room for a long whole hour! When we did meet at last, I felt ashamed for having humiliated him. In my desperation I yelled at her, which only helped to encourage her to add fresh excuses for her unbelievable inability. None of the many employees staring amazed at the appalling scene bothered to intervene or assume professional leadership. They charged me for leaving my luggage with the hotel after having checked out! I could add more regrettable examples of this repulsive phenomenon, but I'd rather not. In conclusion - this hotel employes too many workers, but no responsible adult MANAGER with authority and initiative. Most of the employees are mere frightened third-world work-immigrants, with minimal (if any) English, no preparation at all for their jobs, and evidently too poorly paid. Keep away from this hut imported from the banks of the Ganges river!

title: Mediocre hotel, excellent location
text: My wife and I spent a week at this hotel recently. The best part about the hotel is obviously its location. It is literally around the corner from the Bayswater tube station, and a short walk to the Queensway tube station. Banks, restaurants, pubs, shops, malls and laundrettes are all within easy walking distance, and Kensington High Street and Portobello Road are slightly further. As for the room, we were in a basement room which was very noisy (no double glazing and very thin walls and floorboards!). However, we got used to the noise by the 2nd night and thereafter it didn't really trouble us that much. The room and bathroom sizes were OK and not as small as I had expected based on other reviews on this site, although I also saw another room that resembled a broom closet! The bed and pillows were not great, but the room and bathroom were always clean. The hotel was almost full throughout our stay, and is obviously popular notwithstanding its deficiencies. Practically, I suggest that anyone intending to stay at this hotel uses it merely as a place to bathe and sleep, and a well-situated base to explore the wonders of London. By minimizing time spent in the hotel, and maximizing its excellent location, the hotel is worth the money spent.

title: Avoid this hotel
text: This is the third time I've tried to review this hotel but the negative reviews seem to go missing !! Dirty beds , one lift that held 2 and was constantly used by staff . Broken furniture , torn wallpaper , damp smell . Horrible experience and owners are not interested in complaints . I've stayed in many London hotels and this one is the pits !

title: Great location, to expensive...
text: the location is GREAT! very close to the Bayswater tube station, walking distance from the Hide Park and Marble Arch and a lot of restaurants in the area. however, my room was very very old, not renovated at all. the smallest bathroom i've ever seen in my life, but with good pressure and hot water. the bed was not so comfortable and the TV is like 10"... the worst was the cold wind coming from the window, even when it is shut. the radiator was not enough. there was no free internet in the rooms, only in the lobby. in rooms it costs 6£ an hour(!!!!). in 2013, having free wi-fi in hotel rooms is a must! the staff are really nice and great, breakfast was good but not more than that.

title: Better service at Mcdonalds
text: I work in a hotel. I have done for a year, Before that I waitressed for 7. So I know a thing or two about good customer service. Now I know some of you will say 'Oh stop moaning' or 'here we go, she knows best' but honestly as I work for a budget chain hotel I really didnt care less about the room or anything as Im not fussy, not now due to the ridiculous complaints we get where I work. Im fairly laid back. Ill start with the good points. Location - Brilliant!! Couldnt have got closer to the tube station. Thats it!! Staff - We got there early and walked in. We knew full well the room wouldnt be ready so asked to drop our bag off until later. Now the prices listed on the wall was £200 double room per night. We booked 2 nights for £158 bargain we thought. Clearly the man behind the desk thought we were riff raff because he started to check our booking then PICKED UP THE PHONE halfway through a sentance!!! Who does that!! We left and came back later and a different woman checked us in. We had no welcome, no smiles and no directions to rooms or amenties. This I could deal with, however whenever we left the hotel or returned from a day out we would get dirty looks from staff and no greetings. I know this was because we didnt look 'the part' because we shared the lift with a buisness man, he let us out first and we were ignored, as soon as he walked round the corner it was all smiles and they even ran to hold the door open for him despite the fact that i was stood there being polite and doing it myself. Like I said I wasnt bothered about the room at all but seeing as this is a £200 a night hotel, its disgusting. We were right opposite the lift and you could hear every word. I also woke up the first morning with a horrible rash across one cheek, a doctor said it could ne the linen powder they use to wash the sheets or BED BUGS!! great!!! For 2 nights at £158 for a bed to sleep in this place was fine but for £200 a night I wouldnt bother. Its grim and in need of a facelift .. and im not just talking about the hotel!!!

title: Nice location
text: Stayed here for two nights. The room was grand, there was enough space for us. The hallways tho could do with some touch ups. The location was great. Bayswater Underground was right around the corner and Queensways station is on the same street but a 2 mins walk down towards Hyde park. Plenty of restaurants and grocery shops along that saw street. :)

title: Needs Overhauling
text: I chose this hotel because of its amazing location but in actuality, the downsides outweigh the positives. The nearby tube stations can't make up for a lift that broke meaning I had to carry my bags up the stairs to the top floor. They did temporarily fix it but it broke down again with me in it! It never worked properly the entire time I was there. The room wasn't much better as it was so cramped and the washroom needed re-doing badly. The bed also needs changing - it was really springy and bouncy, like lying on a jellified water bed. It was clean, though, but my room came without the tea/coffee facilities they promised. The décor throughout the hotel (other than the reception area) is sub-standard: it need new paint, carpets and fittings.

title: Room a good standard location amazing.
text: Really close to Hyde park and only a couple of minutes from tubes on two different lines. The room was renovated. The shower water pressure could have been better but all in all a very well priced stay in central London.

title: Beware What they Copy
text: Hotel is in an excellent location for getting around London - walking and underground. Facilities are quite good and it is in a quiet location. Our concern was that reception staff photocopied our passports without our initial kniowledge or any approval to do so. When challenged, staff refused to return the photocopy stating English law required them to photocopy the documents. A few days later the manager advised no such law and apologised.

title: Just the location is good
text: I was tempted to stay at this hotel for its location - and surely it did not disappoint. Enjoyed morning walks in the Hyde Park. But then that's about it - in terms of rest of the facilities, room and bathroom size, cleanliness, privacy, restaurant etc. - I will rate this hotel fairly average. Will recommend the hotel only if you get a great deal and do not have to stay inside much.

title: 3 night stay - good value
text: I stayed for 3 nights while working in London. The welcome was friendly and I was shown to my room. The room was a double and was a good size for London. Ensuite was shower and not bath but was quite modern and well maintained. View was not amazing and the room was adjacent to the back of one of the nearby bar / restaurants so there was a bit of noise into the night. On the second night I was very aware of other guests who were noisy throughout the small hours, having arrived back to their room after midnight. The walls are thick but the doors are really thin and not at all soundproof. A good base for a few days and a decent sized room. Good value for money and a friendly welcome. I would stay again.

title: Strategic Location.
text: Best place to stay due to location. Though the rooms may be a little small especially the bathrooms but a comfortable night is good here. The staff were helpful. This hotel is in between 2 subways which is so helpful. Further down you have Hyde Park. Lots of cafes, grocery shops and a mall nearby.

title: Rabbit Warren
text: Stayed at this hotel mid-september 2011 and would not stay again. We actually changed our booking to this hotel as it had a better write up on TripAdvisor. We were booked into a double standard room but they gave us a deluxe room, but it was very tiny so I wouldn't like to imagine what the standard room was like. To get to the room it was like a rabbit warren and flooring very uneven. The decor was nice, no airconditioning, had to leave the window halfway open all night as it wouldn't go lower. No refrigerator (is this so that you buy drinks from the bar). The bathroom was modern but the shower very small and shower head not working properly (even though we let them know twice). The located was good though, close to Bayswater Tube, Kensington Gardens/Palace and Hyde Park easy walk to Oxford Street. There were only 2 people that understood English properly, so this made it difficult. Buffet breakfast was ordinary, in fact we declined the breakfast and went up the street - much better and not too expensive. Plenty of restaurants in the area.

title: Run away as fast as you can!!
text: Without a doubt, the worst hotel room I have ever stayed in! Actually correction, I did not stay in the room, but immediately left once I located the room (through the narrow, maze-like hallways) and felt the steamy air hit my face as I opened the door. Luckily, I was travelling alone so I could easily relocate and the room was not pre-paid, so I only lost money for one night. I did ask the reception staff to change my room, but was repeatedly told there was not another room available for that price. Even when I offered to pay more for a different room type, there was still nothing available. I was only offered a different room after I asked to checkout. By this point, I was dripping sweat and had no desire to stay in the stuffy room without a window that opens. I agree the location is great and the price was good, but not even that was enough to make me stay in this lousy hotel.

title: Room review
text: We stayed there some years ago and its an absolute dump...should have be demolished years ago. The room as about the size of a snooker table,we couldn't close the shower door so water went every where.a complaint to the front desk went completely ignored as did a request for a room where we could actually find somewhere to store our luggage apart from against the door-no fire escape-no air con.without any doubt the worst hotel we've ever stayed in

title: The very first stay
text: I had my very first stay here in 1994 september... it was a small single bed room with a fairly low rate... narrow corridors, typical british carpets... i will stay again to remember the old days... next time in a bigger room...

title: What a dump
text: I was relocated to this hotel due to an overbooking at Kensington Town Hotel. They wanted to place me in a room in the basement with a terrible smell and the carpet was wet! Totally unacceptable - if you have these kind of rooms don't sell them its just a no go and they wanted to charge a 110 GBP for it. The original reservation was made through booking.com and they did nothing to compensate - be careful with online reservations in London especially when big events are going on as the hotels don't care at all they just want to be fully booked at any price - customers loose and are faced with severe problems. There was a Chinese executive with me that had exactly the same experience I had. It shows again that many London hotels are not professionally run.

title: All $ goes to Location
text: Excellent Location - between Bayswater and Queensway Room - we booked the Deluxe one so is pretty new and modern Don't expect anything except these. Showering was our nightmare everyday.

title: So good we walked out.
text: When we walked into the elevator it should have given us cause for concern, they were so small, this was after a two hour wait for the room to be ready. We walked down the narrow corridors, one at a time, as you couldn't walk side by side. We opened the door and saw the small room with a brick wall view, as it was in the basement. My Fiance opened the bathroom door, just in time to see the bath regurgitating it's old bath water. We complained and went out. When we returned we enquired about the bath, to which the receptionist had not been informed of it's progress. When we got to the room, the bath still looked dirty. There was toilet paper supplied, but not put on the toliet paper dispenser. We rang room service for a bottle of Muscadet and two glasses and 15 minutes later they still hadn't delivered it. While we were waiting we noticed the bed had hair on the sheets, and had obviously not been changed that day, despite this being our first day in the room! The room was also cold with no visible means of heating. We then asked to see the manager, who never came! At this point we had enough and found a better hotel around the corner. We then came back, finally saw the manager and attained a full refund. Avoid with your life.

title: Excellent Location, good value
text: Well located only 2 mins from either Bayswater or Queensway Tube Stations and plenty of local bars, cafes and shops. Hotel room was adequate for a short trip but many of the areas need redecorating. This is currently being done so decorators were in the corridors will be much improved once complete. Staff were friendly and helpful, we had booked a deluxe double and I would not want anything smaller. Overall I would stay here again once the redecorating is finished.

title: Deceiving website photos
text: Stayed in a single room for 2 nights in Nov 2005, paid GBP41 per night inclu tax and continental breakfast. Good value for a central location. Baysway tube station is only 1 minute walk away. surrounded by good restaurants and shops. Lobby, dinning area, bar are ok but tired decor. lift only fits 2 people. average service from staffs. helpful conceige, super small-sized room, similar to a student's room in residence hall in the UK. single bed fits to the wall like a coffin, have little room to open a standard sized luggage, very small shower room with toilet, have to walk around toilet to get to shower, smallest shower even used, whole toilet became wet after shower. tv received 8 channels with remote control that is working. trouser press worked but not very effective. clean carpet, bed linen, towels that are changed everyday, smoking room but smell fresh, comfortable bed, quiet. ordered dinners in room, fish and chips for GBP7.50, steak GBP9.50 plus GBP2.0 for room service. very good quality freshly made food, good presentation and still hot. again good value for money too. but room service only available after 1700. tea and coffee making facilities provided in room, little milk sachets tasted horrible. Bar downstairs made horrible tasted cappuchinno, so ran across the road to Tesco to get tea and fresh milk. the room was not warm enough for cold days. staff bleeded the radiator and turned on full power, yet for such a small room, it was still not warm enough. i am still in 30s and came from nearby city, not Hawaii. will NOT stay there again.
Great location - very close to tube, shopping and Hyde Park. Had an evening flight home, got to leave our bags for the hole day at the hotel (50p per bag). Great:-)

title: Ok fore a night or two
text: Booked and payed extra fore a dubbel room, and got a room with a dubble bed. But it was very very smal. The closet was also so small that you had too curle youre shurts and dress jacket to get it inn. The bathroom was old With Paint falling off. The shower was a old fashioned one with no shower hose, just a stuck shower head up on the wall. The hot or Cold regulater was broken and just did deliver hot water.
