The free wifi did work very bad in the room. Thw positive parts was

title: Disgusting & dirty
text: This is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in , walking in the the actually reception area which is beautifully decorated you would think wow , until you go up the tiny lift that hold s two people with baggage at a squeeze , to your room , then you see this hotel for what it is dirty ,shabby , broken windows which are taped with cello tape , worn out carpets , wall paper peeling of walls ,brown stained ceiling very hard uncomfortable beds only 3 sockets in room to charge our phones plus try to keep the room cool coz it was like a oven with fans , The only plus with this hotel was the reception staff who didn’t look at all stunned when I complained and showed them the pictures ,and the hotel is very close to bay water station ,but there are plenty of other hotels on Inverness terrace to choose avoid this one at all costs

title: Pre-Diamond Jubillee London Trip
text: Love the location of the hotel. Just next to the Kensington Palace, made me feel I stay with the Roayl family:). The hotel is quite simple, but perfect for the London visit, all you need, in great location. I would definetely recommended for city visit - planning to come back for the Olympics. Love London:)

title: Quick Overview
text: Location is good, but transportation with underground from Victoria station is not so fast. Room is not very small, but there is not enough free space for two people. Bathroom is extreme cold and tiny. Stuff are Ok.

title: Great Value in London Bayswater
text: Getting value for money in London is not easy. I stayed at the Malaysian-owned Eden garden Hotel just before Christmas, my third time to stay here. If you are just looking for a clean bed to sleep in and your time in the hotel is minimal - and you want to save your money for shopping or taxis - then the Berjaya Eden Park Hotel is the place to stay. One constraint is that the hallways are narrow and the lift very small - a potential irritant if you have lots of luggage. But staff are efficient and courteous. There's wireless internet available through t-mobile. A continental breakfast that includes great ham and bread. And my single room had a bathtub long enough to soak in comfortably! Location - just around the corner from Bayswater tube station - which is just one stop away from Paddington Station and the Heathrow Express! Hyde Park is just a block away. For GBP40/night, I'll stay here again!

title: Good location but others just so-so
text: The best thing about this hotel was the location as it was in between two subways that provides better way of touring London. My personal opinion is bayswater is relatively more catered to asian as there had a lot of very nice, budget friendly asian eateries here and a lot of choices as well. Its the best mixture for a short trip. *relatively good/simple hotel *Near two subways *a lot of food options *A few convenience store /moneychanger/simcard/topup and etc. The slightly down side *very small rooms *small walkway *small 2person(bigsize) with no luggage or 2medium size with 1huge luggage lift. (literally very small lift, so either come and go at off peak hours ) or sit while waiting for the lift to be available as theres only 1 small tiny lift that the customers and staff uses. *Breakfast was ok i guess but worth it to pay a buffet breakfast for . Unless its included , its best to get breakkie in other cafe/shops/bakery nearby .. PS: When checking in early . Best for one person to go check the room first . As hubby and i walked in with people still sleeping in bed. Shocking us and them to bits.

title: O pior quarto de hotel onde já estive! The worst hotel room I ever stayed!
text: Until last week was difficult to me to elect the worst hotel room I ever stayed. Thanks to Berjaya that isn't true anymore. I have no words to describe the room at the ground floor. How can it have 4 stars? The staff at front office don't even speak english and they don't know what Customer Care is!

title: Hot Fun in the Summertime
text: Other reviews say it, and it's worth repeating: this place has a great location, but inadequate room facilities. I've stayed there before and thought the trade-off was worthwhile. After my most recent visit I'm not so sure. We got a room on the fourth floor (nice and quiet), but with no air-conditioning the summer heat made it VERY stuffy. The small fan in the room did little to remove the heat of the afternoon sun. (The room would have been much more enjoyable in a cold winter, I think....) We could only sleep by getting naked and letting the fan blow on us. Not a comfortable experience. Other than that......older building.....amall rooms......so-so room furnishings. Continental breakfast buffet adequate. Staff efficient. Internet quite expensive for a day's use. People should book with open eyes, to decide if all the trade-offs are worth it.

title: Don't Bother!!!
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at this hotel over Valentines weekend, 13th & 14th February. We chose it because the website seemed to indicate that it was a stylishly furnished modern hotel – how wrong we were! We arrived about 1pm on 13th hoping we could check in an hour early but the receptionist told us a very firm no so we had a drink in the bar. The bar and reception areas are very nice so we still had high hopes that the room would be as per the photos on the hotel website. When we did check in the staff didn’t show us to the room or offer to help with our bags (bearing in mind you cannot fit in the lift with a bag as it is so small and our room was up 3 flights of stairs) which was disappointing. On entering the room the stench of stale cigarettes hit us instantly, it was vile, I’ve never smelt anything like it. I went back down to reception to ask if they could move us, the answer was a point blank no! I explained that there was no way we could sleep in a room that filthy and stank that much and asked if he could either let me speak to the manager or give us a refund and we’d find another hotel. After a lot of huffing and puffing (from the receptionist, not me!) he eventually agreed to move us. The room we ended up with (and the first room) was no bigger than a box, there was barely room for the bed and although not dirty it looked tired and dated, evident in the mould on the bathroom tiles. Wasn’t exactly what we were expecting for a romantic valentines weekend away, particularly when they tried to charge us for the room we moved to when we’d already paid, the receptionist was intent on arguing with my boyfriend about it even after he showed him the receipt! We found the staff unhelpful, rude and quite miserable. Also don’t bother asking them for any London information, we asked if one receptionist could confirm the road a restaurant in Covent Garden was located on and she gave us completely the wrong address in a different part of London! We didn’t eat in the restaurant as the menu looked completely uninspiring and fairly expensive for what it was. The only good thing about this hotel is its proximity to Baywater and Queensway tube stations. All in all if you want a basic hotel with good transport links then this hotel is ok, but there are probably better hotels out there for the same sort of price

title: Well placed budget hotel
text: 7th time here. Its easy placed for 2 tube lines and on a quiet street. Yes the rooms are a little small but we always book classic double and the beds are very comfortable. We stay here because its value and easy to get to and from. Its a good quality budget hotel.

title: Nice n Clean
text: Visited London last week. Small room but clean. Adequate space for 2 adult. Very unfortunate of us to have a room with heater not working but room was just warm enough if window was closed. Very helpful staff. Hotel just 100meters from Bayswater tube station. For Muslim- a lot of shops with Halal food nearby.

title: Good value for money
text: The Berjaya Eden Park is in a fantastic location in Bayswater, super close to the Bayswater and Queensway tube stops and all the shops and restaurants along Queensway. It's got a very cosy, English feel about it and is a more than decent option for the price you pay. It was really lovely to sit in the downstairs bar with an open fire going in the winter. Pros: Good location, good price, decent sized room (for London standards), can book a single room. Cons: Walls are quite thin, breakfast is average.

title: Fantstic Location, Great Food, Good Service
text: We stayed at the Berjaya Eden Park Hotel for four nights in early June and were very happy. LOCATION The hotel is very close to Hyde Park and Bayswater and it is actually cheaper to take a taxi from the Paddington tube station than take the train. It cost just over 5 pounds while two tube fares would have been 10 pounds! Major tourist attractions are also close to the hotel. These can be reached by the tube (two tube stations are really close) or by taxi. FOOD There is an excellent choice of buffet breakfasts with an option of an English breakfast or a Continental breakfast. Lots of fresh fruits and yoghurt as well. The hotel specialises in Asian cuisine and the two dinners we had were excellent-the prawns fresher than one normally gets in five star hotels. Everything was light, fresh, flavourful. ROOM The room is small, and a bit dated. The bathroom sink is so tiny, it looks like it would be better off in a doll's house! There was no heating nor cooling in the room in June, so we were lucky that the weather was good, not really calling for either. The room and bathroom are clean and comfortable but not plush, but the view of the street, and trees etc means that it is pleasant. The lobby, and restaurant are full of character though the floor under the carpeting is just a little uneven in the dining room. SERVICE Mostly very good. The only member of the staff that I could fault was the receptionist who was on duty when we checked in on 3rd June. She unreasonably did not agree to a packed breakfast we requested on one day of our visit when we were to go on a day tour insisting that this could only be done on the day of departure. Fortunately, the next day there was a different receptionist, the charming Mamata, and she organised a most excellent packed breakfast. IMMEDIATE ENVIRONS There are very good eateries and shops just two minutes walking distance from the hotel. Just turn left as you exit and walk for a minute!

title: Good Value, Great Location
text: The hotel staff were wonderful, very nice and very helpful. The location is perfect. It's close to Bayswater and Queensway tube stations and we could get to most locations from one or the other without changing trains. Also, there were a lot of restaurants on the street behind the hotel as well as a Sainsbury (where we got breakfast every morning) and a Tesco Express. The street with the restaurants stays pretty busy even later in the evening, making it safe to walk around after dark. Our room faced a quiet street, so noise at night wasn't much of a problem for us. The beds were very comfortable and clean. Also, we didn't get breakfast at the hotel, but we did eat at the hotel's restaurant for dinner and it was very good. The hallways, elevator, stairways and rooms are very small. This is an older building, so don't expect the same size as modern hotels. It's small enough that a wheelchair might not fit. Also, the bathtub is very high, so if you have mobility problems, you might want to find another place. The bathroom is small, though not as small as other places I've stayed in in Europe. Again, the building is old, so the doors, windows, floors and walls are worn and a little dirty, but there's only so much you can do with these old buildings, especially in a more humid place like London. The floor in our room was a little uneven, and some of the wallpaper was peeling, but nothing major. Overall, this hotel is great for it's location and price. If you're looking to just stay the night in a hotel and spend the rest of your time sightseeing, then this hotel is definitely a great choice. We would love to stay here again if we ever go back to London.

title: Convenient Location, Small Room & Bad Bath Room
text: Located at nearby Bayswater Train Station, with just a few minute walk away, it is a location that many traveler would like to stay, as London transport is very convenient and you can almost get to any part of London with train. The hotel lobby is designed using quite a vintage feel, though it is quite small in size but the theme is quite fit with the local English theme. The lift for the hotel is very very small, only enough to fit two person with an average luggage. The room is quite clean and nice, we are given a welcome fruit plate (With some banana, apple and peach) There is also two bottle of mineral water given on the first day, the following day, no free water or fruit is given. Shower is quite a nightmare, our room water is too hot as the cold water tab is not working. We tried to call in the technician but the problem does not go away. The other room also suffer problem with their shower, some is too hot, too cold or too low water pressure, the general feedback is quite bad for the shower room. Breakfast is serve on daily basis, on the ground floor. Everyday we are serve with the same food, their breakfast consist of bread, milk, some coffee and ham. Overall the service given by the kitchen and service crew is good, request is being attended to on time, and they are doing their best to serve the customers.

title: london business
text: Not all impressed. Starting with the positives, it's within 100 yards of a tube station (Bayswater). Other than that I can't think of any else to reccomend . The room had a stale odour of smoke and the full English breakfast was rather dried up. Won't stay again

title: GOOD LOCATION AS NEAR BAYSWATER TUBE WITH HALAL FOOD AROUND
text: Room: I give 3 star as I felt that the room advertise was not the one I book. The room was tiny and old. For two men staying at the same room, felt like bromance moment as the room really limit our movement after we put down our luggage. However, excellent wifi provided. Minibar: Coffee/tea for the room. No mineral water. Bathroom - Bathroom was tiny but clean. Bath and shower gel available. Water pressure good. Location: Located at Inverness Terrace, just a stone from Bayswater tube station. Many halal certified restaurants round the hotel even Tesco and Sainsbury's. Service - Check-in was fast and their receptionist was good and so politely answering my question regarding the hotel. Value: Affordable booking via Agoda. F&B: Halal-certified dining at the hotel. Not worry about halal food if you staying this hotel as the owner is Malaysian company.

title: Too Small for Big Money
text: I don't think they know that they are over priced. One night 100.00 BP. Small room. Small Bathroom, Can't even bend in the Shower. Have to pay 6.00 BP for one Hour of Internet. Two night is enough as I can get double of the size with same rate. Only advantage is near to Bays Water Underground.

title: Don't let the bad reviews put you off.
text: After booking, I read the reviews and was worried it would be awful. It's not. Location is amazing, a stones throw from Kensington Palace. The building and street are impressive and well kept. It's an older hotel so yes, some creaky floorboards and small doorways and stairs, but looked after and possessing character. Staff were smart, friendly and helpful. Immediately we were upgraded without asking, and free of charge. The room was clean, airy and modern, with a comfy bed, desk and small dining suite. Aircon was convenient as it was 25c outside. Breakfast was plentiful with a large and varied selection of cuisine that catered for many nationalities. Generous check in/out times of 2pm / 12noon. Its not the best, but for £88 in the city its fantastic. (most others in the area are £130+). Shame it has some bad reviews, we shall certainly consider it again.

title: Great Value for money!! Staying again next year!!
text: We stayed here for two nights at the start of the trip and couldnt believe the location, wow its amazing its a short walk to the tube, parks,and internet access. We found the serivce accommodating, and helpful. The hall ways are a little narrow and long, but the rooms are newly renovated( ours was). The room was clean, comfortable, and the bathroom was lovely!. There was a litlle noise outside in the evening, but when u have been travelling for ages you become quite exhusted quickly and dont notice it!. Breakfast was amazing so much food, its a great start to the day!!!We are staying here again next year! we really loved it!

title: Dated
text: Terrible condition bedrooms, the lobby space is acceptable. The lift is ancient. The bedrooms leave much to be desired. Holes in the walls, doors, bathrooms outdated. Terrible condition for a rated Hotel even in london standards. Only stayed as london was full, avoid if you choice in the matter.

title: Never judge a book by its cover
text: Room very small Very cold breeze coming through closed window Mattress was terrible. Old and lumpy,had to ask for extra duvet just to lie on top of it. No iron Poor hairdryer Paper thin walls,could hear conversation from next room! Major makeover needed,bathroom ceiling needed paint Drinks in the bar was poor,overpriced and clearly not knowing how to make cocktails. Hotel staff were friendly. Location was good. Close to tube station,restaurants and walking distance to Hyde Park ( winter wonderland )

title: Mid-week break
text: We have previously stayed at this hotel so we knew what to expect. It is an ideal location for the underground and minutes away from Kensington Gardens. Plenty of local shops and restaurants nearby. Reception staff are friendly and helpful. We had booked a standard double room, it was comfortable, but basic. We were a bit disappointed to find that the bar is no longer in use although they still advertise it on the web site so beware !!! Breakfast there was plenty to choose from .

title: Extremely Disappointing
text: It pains me how tourists are ripped off in London. Don't let the attractive reception or exterior of this hotel fool you, nor the photos you might see on the internet. When I arrived at this hotel, everything was going well until I got into the cramped 2 person lift and ascended to my room. The corridors are incredibly small and the rooms are tiny. When I tried my cardkey in the door it didn't work so I went back to reception to tell them. They informed me that my room was 'dodgy' and the porter would let me in. After the porter let me into my room I was surprised that, even though the sun was shining, I had to turn on the lights because the window was so small it didn't let sufficient light in. The bathroom was so small, I could barely wash my hands in the tiny sink without getting water everywhere. The shower was also stained and everything about the room just seemed cheap and unfinished. Already dissappointed about the price i'd paid for such a dissappointing room, I realised that I wasn't happy with having to fetch the porter everytime I came and went so I complained at reception. Thecustomer service skills of the staff were little to none, and they told me there was nothing they could do about my faulty door. They weren't even understanding or apologetic, and didn't offer me any kind of compensation. The next day when I was due to check out I got a knock on my door at 2 minutes past 12 and a voice telling me I was due to check out. Never in my life have I come across this in a hotel. I got an online discount but the hotel rates are £130 for a twin room. I'm glad I didn't pay the full price as what I paid was already enough. The staff are useless, the hotel is a total rip off. People should get their moneys worth and this certainly doesn't apply at the Berjaya Eden.

title: Does just enough to cross the average barrier
text: Spent one night at this hotel on a work-cum-mini holiday trip, and while it wasn't the worse, there are certainly some areas in need of attention. Room: For starters, I was actually given a complimentary upgrade from the Classic Single to the Deluxe Double, which was much appreciated. Unfortunately, my room was located on the ground floor, with my room window directly facing the road and walkway, thus making it impossible for me to open the curtains without being seen from the outside. Additionally, there was a small seating area just outside my room, so close that I am able to hear their conversations clearly in addition to the noise from passing cars. To make things worse, there were people spending time and chatting there throughout the night, which was rather unpleasant as I could hardly get a good night's rest. I can only assume that this may bother most people. As for the room itself, it was decent and sufficiently spaced, although I must say that it might be slightly tight for 2-3 people. Cleanliness was maintained, both in the room and bathroom, although it does look tired and aging. The toiletries were good however, and the shower functioned perfectly. In general, the room is not spectacular, but offers you what you need. Location: In my opinion, this is the hotel's greatest strength. Extremely accessible to a variety of eateries (close to a very popular asian/malaysian food place called Goldmine) and to many express supermarkets such as Sainsbury and Tesco. Most importantly, it is a mere 3-5 minute walk away from Bayswater Tube Station, which is excellent for connectivity. Hyde Park is around the vicinity, a place I personally would recommend visiting if you haven't done so. All in all, its location is as good as you can get in its price range. Restaurant: I had their continental buffet breakfast for one morning, and I regret to say that it was quite disappointing and underwhelming. I certainly expected more from a hotel in the heart of London. I personally felt the spread and quality was not up to mark. My humble advice - you'd be much better off booking your room without breakfast and save yourself some money. After all, I guarantee you'd be able to get better breakfast options within walking distance for far less cost. If I ever returned, that's what I would do. Staff and service: Front desk staff weren't the greatest, but decent. Helpful, responsive, and quite welcoming. Restaurant staff, on the other hand, could probably use a bit more help. I'm not sure if they were understaffed at the time I was there, but I noticed they were struggling to keep up with the guests, and weren't exactly the most fluent in speech. That being said, no major complaints. Just offering some constructive criticism. Others: For some reason, the corridors/hallways to the rooms are extremely narrow and full of stairs, making it quite tricky to navigate. The journey to the rooms are literally like a trek, going up and down and up again. For my room in particular, I had to walk up a tall flight of stairs, go down, and slightly up again just to reach the elevator which brings me to my room's floor. Bear in mind that one needs to do all this whilst walking through tight corridors which can probably only fit one person (with luggage) per way! While I understand this could be typical for hotels in London, I just feel that it would be rather difficult for senior citizens to get around, let alone carry their bags. I would certainly not recommend this hotel for large families and especially senior citizens. Conclusion: While my review seems to slant towards the negative, I honestly do feel that this hotel is quite value for money for the average traveler, especially if you are on a relatively low budget. I can only assume it would be hard to find anything substantially better than this hotel at a similar price range within London

title: Highly recommended for middle income.
text: The deluxe suites room is very comfortable for couple. Hotel staff are very helpful and polite. I will stay again in this hotel. 3 mins to to Bayswater Underground station..Plenty of eateries and souvenir shops nearby..Location is very good, morning walk to Hyde Park and Oxford Street. Highly recommended. Good value for money. Stayed in for 25 days..we enjoyed the food, the staff & the environment. I like the hotel interior deco.

title: location & staff, hotel a bit tired
text: I found the staff very helpful and the location excellent. My room was clean and though small, was adequate. However the decor was tired - the net curtains grey, the bathroom in need of a refit. Balance this against a very reasonable price and I think it was good value - you get what you pay for. I made a comment about the chipped sink and received an e-mail to say that it was being dealt with, which impressed me.

title: Avoid!
text: I spent three nights in London, and I choosed the Eden Park Hotel because of the offered price (GBP 49,- or approx. EUR ~70,-). London is really expensive, this location was presented as 4 star hotel, thus I thought the price would be okay. !!I have never been in such a small hotel room!! The room was located below the ground floor, but it was equipped with a window. The corridor was so narrow, that two persons were not able to pass by. The bathroom was extremely tiny. Breakfast was okay, but only offered limited choice. Location is excellent, it is just a few blocks to the next tube station. In my opinion this hotel (and many other hotels) does not deserve a four star rating . I would give them only 2 stars. Additionally I was surprised by the fact that such hotels (small rooms, narrow corridors...) are allowed to be operates. Aren't there sufficient laws which force the management to make their hotel safer?

title: Shopping trip.
text: This was a good Hotel situated in the Bayswater/Edgeware Road district. Malaysian owned Hotel from a very reputable Group. Decorated with Chinese Lanterns at the entrance due to it being Chinese New Year. Going left out of the Hotel and across the road is the Tube station.The other end of the road a good bus service direct in to City centre. I was able to check in before the said time of 2.00pm. My room although small was adequate as this was just me occupying the room,siuated on the first floor.The room was spotless with tea coffee making facilities, flat screen television/ hairdryer/ Single bed a bit on the small side. Bathroom with bath and shower.toiletries etc. The bar area downstairs had a lovely lounge small and comfortable with a lovely fire, making it a very snug place to have a glass of two of wine, which we did of course. I went with my friend to Whiteleys Shopping centre for a buffet meal at the Real China Restaurant. Very good. Just round the corner from the Hotel where there is also a wide choice of all types of cafes and restaurants. The following morning I opted for continental breakfast in the Hotel at a very reasonable price with plenty of choice and as much tea and coffee as you could drink. I will certainly stay here again when I return for a stop over with my husband. . . ..

title: Great location at budget prices
text: Small budget hotel, with low price but a friendly staff and decent breakfast, just one block from the Bayswater tube station. Ideal for a familly week-end in London, or a shopping trip on your own. The rooms are small, clean, and overlook a very calm street. The neighborhood is nice and rather residential, but some decent restaurants for an evening meal are available on the main street, on both sides of the tube station.

title: Never again!!
text: We were five people who traveled to London for a nice week, all good apart from the hotel. Extremely small, dirty room where the shower did not work on one of the rooms. The first night had one of us stay in single rooms as they had not managed to fix beds in the other rooms. Never ever again!

title: Adequate Hotel. Honest staff.
text: Stayed in this hotel just for a night. It is literally just outside Bayswater Tube Station so location is very convenient. Queensway Tube and Bus Stations are just around the corner as well. Check in was a breeze. The room was small but adequate when you just need a decent place to sleep in. The halls are really narrow and there are staircases involved as you make your way towards the room so big/heavy pieces of luggage can be a problem. The walk to the rooms is like a maze and can be confusing. Staff guided me thoroughly though so I didn't have a hard time. You just have to manage your expectations. A friend of mine dropped a £5 bill and a staff member chased us to the corner of the street to return it. Got an honest staff right there, whose name I believe, was LENO. Breakfast looks interesting but I didn't get to try it. Be warned that there is no potable water in the room. There are, however, a lot of restaurants and stores in the area which makes the location even more awesome. Will probably stay here again.

title: Convenient location
text: The actual building fronts two roads and is quite impressive. Public areas - reception and bar - are OK and initial impression is good. Going by some of the other reviews we were lucky to have a good sized room facing the road. The road is one way and not everso busy so neither traffic nor pedestrian noise was a problem. Our room had all we needed but there's no two ways about the fact it was tired. What a difference a coat of paint would make!! The room was clean and the beds comfortable. Bathroom was small but big enough to have a bath with shower, toilet and sink - what else do you need??!! Location was good for us. Convenient for Paddington Station, Hyde Park, Little Venice, Underground and buses into the city. Nearby restaurants catered mainly for Middle and Far East clientele. It's not the Ritz but it's not Ritz prices. Berjaya is fine for a base to visit the city, just take it for what it is: an good average hotel.

title: Fantastic stay
text: After reading mixed reviews on trip advisor i must admit i was a little apprehensive about our stay at the Berjaya. I've always thought that some people have exceptionally high standards and ignore most bad reviews and this proved to be right in this case because we had a fantastic stay and couldn't recommend it higher. After checking in we were told we had been given a free upgrade to a deluxe room and to be honest we were really impressed. The room is finished to a high standard, comfy bed, nice furnishings and it was spotless. One of the main selling points of this this hotel is its location, literally a minutes walk from the tube station and a high street of shops including tesco, sainsburys, macds etc yet still manages to be on the quiet side with no traffic noise. Also worth mentioning the bar as well, after watching the first half of a football match elsewhere we came back to the hotel to find the drinks much cheaper and staff polite and friendly. My advise is to ignore any bad reviews, we were chuffed with the deal we got and thought it was great value for money. I genuinely would recommend this place to anybody and we will definitely be coming back.

title: Nice but.....
text: The room was small, the bed was not very comfortable, but it served the purpose. The staff was very good, very nice. The bad part about this place? The NEIGHBORS. Across the street, there can be up to 20 or so people out in the street, whooping it up til all hours when you want to sleep. The location is pretty good, near to several underground stations, but the selection of restaurants could be better. The restaurant only serves a Malaysian menu, which I don't like, and the breakfast was not very good at all. Overall, its a pretty good place.

title: Good, comfortable hotel in London's food paradise
text: A good hotel with friendly and knowledgeable staff. Located in London's food paradise Bayswater. Easy connections to central and circle line underground (Bayswater station is within 100 meters). Hydepark is just around the corner, and even the V&C and Nature History Museum are within walking distance. A 10-15 minutes walk to Nothing Hill and Portobello Road. I will definitely stay with them again.

title: A Hidden Gem!
text: This is one of the most cost efficient, excellently located hotels I have stayed in. It's a 1 minute walk from Bayswater tube station (circle line/district line) and very close to Kensington Gardens/Hyde Park. Very handy for the V&A/Natural History museums. The rooms are well designed with the usual mod-cons except tea/coffee facilities. I guess they want you to buy downstairs! No matter, there's a "Caffe Roma" (not the chain) place round the corner. Great staff, good breakfasts. Along the main road you have everything from fast food to great restaurants (Royal China especially good) with Indian/Italian/Halal and more. There are Tescos/Sainsburys/souvenir shops all within a minutes walk. The staff are friendly but not intrusive. The bathroom was always clean and the bedroom was well maintained. I will definitely stay again.

title: Great location, Single rooms don't have AC
text: I made the reservation very sure that this was not a 5 stars hotel, but what I got was kind of disapointing. I booked a single room and I found out at the hotel that single rooms don't have AC and it's a hotel policy that's not showing on the web page. The room needs renovation, the wallpaper was peeling off the walls, the bathroom had accumulated dirt on the borders of the tub and sink. On a brighter note, the location was great, it's one block away from two Metro Station. Bottom line, if you don't care about these details, this is a place to stay while in London.

title: Very Nice
text: Having just spent Valentine's evening staying at the Eden Suite in this hotel I would like to share my experience. Our suite wasn't the biggest I'd ever seen but there was plenty of space for two people and featured a "livingroom" area with TV, sofas, minibar fridge etc, plus a small dining table with 4 tub chairs - all the furniture looked new and good quality. In the bedroom area we had a spacious, comfortable double bed, 2 wardrobes and a dressing table - again all good quality and attractive dark wood. We also had our own private patio which we didn't use due to the wet weather but it looked very nice. The bathroom was well fitted and spacious with marble tiles and white fittings. The complimentary toiletries were also very nice! The decor of the room was very nice with a dark green wallpaper accented with red and gold accessories. The hotel staff were friendly and efficient, plus the bar and dining room were very nice. The continental breakfast was plentiful and of good quality. Only minor criticisms would be the lifts are tiny and the corridors are very narrow too but this is a general feature of Victorian London buildings in the city centre. Living in London myself I know about small spaces in buildings! All in all my partner and I enjoyed our experience at the Eden Park Hotel.

title: Good location but wouldn't stay again
text: As heading to Wimbledon for the tennis I picked this hotel for its location with easy access from Euston and also to the championships via district line. The hotel is "budget" standard

title: Avoid - not as advertised. Very poor
text: I had been in London at meetings throughout the day. Trains were cancelled due to an accident so I needed to find somewhere to stay. Hotels around London Euston and Kings Cross were full so I reverted to the internet to find something as close to the station as possible. Up popped the Berjaya Eden Park Hotel in Bayswater. Rooms looked quite large, clean and equipped with a TV. How misleading that was. I paid £150 for a 1 night stay (London is expensive - no problem) but it was nothing more than a hostel. I was put in the lower basement floor in a tiny room, TV didn't work, boiling hot room but couldn't switch the heating off, dirty carpet, chipped paint, ancient furniture......it was horrible. The hotel was not as advertised, it was overpriced and under equipped. Dirty, cramped and generally not a nice place to be. Avoid if possible.

title: Five Days In London
text: We stayed in the Berjaya Eden Park hotel in London from 18-Sept through 23-Sept this year. Our room was a Deluxe Double room on the second floor. The people in the hotel were very helpful, polite and friendly and helped us with some of our arrangements in and out of London. The room was nice and the only reason I would give for not allowing a better rating is that being so close to the Tessco Market on the corner, we were awakened by the mandatory nighttime deliveries at the store. Know this hotel is a converted row house as are many of the hotels in and around London. The building is old but well kept and our room seemed to be recently remodeled. There are some real dumps in London that are also remodels and we actually stayed in one prior to moving to the Berjaya. The Berjaya was less than a block from the Bayswater Underground station and is very convenient for travel around London and we did a lot of travel around London. As I mentioned the staff there was extremely helpful to us during our stay and I would recommend this hotel to my friends and family. The only thing I would have done differently would be to make my reservations further in advance for a better rate but our situation would not allow for that on this trip. The food in the hotel was just average but then, so is most of the food in London. Worth noting, WiFi access is not free with the room and a bit expensive if not traveling on an expense account.

title: 35-39 Inverness Terrace London W2 3JS England
text: Disgusting!!! We didn’t have many expectations. A clean and dry room would have been totally enough. They gave us a room in the basement which was cold, dark and musty. The carpet was dirty. The staff was working just next to our room so it was very loud. We changed the hotel.

title: Okay for a short stay
text: Stayed here for one night whilst sightseeing. On arrival it was good. The staff were nice and efficient and shown us to our room. The room was nice. Has everything we needed for the night, tea, coffee, towels, soap, shampoo, conditioner, tv. Our main problem was the noise from outside! I understand it's not going to be quiet given its location but we had a fairly sleepless night due to the noise coming through the windows! And draft! The windows are terrible and need replacing!!!!

title: Convenient Place
text: Nearby to Bayswater tube station and very convenient located at Hyde Park. The hotel is clean a bit small but just enough stayed at the Deluxe queen. Equipped with coffee and tea facilities. The staff is very helpful. Easily to find Halal food nearby.

title: They organised a surprise birthday dinner party
text: Well organised, even at such short notice, went there in the morning to arrange a surprise birthday dinner later the same evening. Job well done, food was good, very generous portions, everything turned out as planned and everyone happy. Only comment for improvement is they need to serve the food promptly. It was quite a long wait for all 6 of us to get our food. Thank to Puan Azlina for the services rendered. Will definitely come again with family and friends insyaAllah. Thanks also to Danish & Shikin. You guys were great. Compliments to the chef.

title: a horrible experience
text: We booked two rooms for two nights and when we checked in late on Friday night and went to our room we were extremely disappointed. The lift only held 2 people, how do you manage if you have children, the corridors were very narrow, the room was very small and hot and the bathroom was a joke. I grazed my knee on the hand basin when I sat on the toilet and when I got in the shower I could not bend over to wash myself. No fans or air conditioning in the bedrooms which were unbearable. Breakfast was continental and we would be charged £5 if we wanted a cooked breakfast. We found the staff not at all helpful or friendly. We moved rooms to the basement which was a little larger and cooler. Our friends who remained on the 4th floor were woken at 6 a.m. on the first night and 3 a.m. on the second by loud music being played in the adjacent room. The staff only agreed to go up and listen to the noise after my friend went down to the lobby and threatened to spend the rest of the night sleeping there. Definately a hotel to be avoided at all costs.

title: A pleasant stay at a good price
text: It was a really pleasant hotel with a homely historic feel of welcome reception. The staff were outstanding! Helpful and very positive! An interesting labyrinth of getting to my room. The room for 1 man is small and limited views, but adequate. The windows however, do need to be more secure as it feels a bit thin and easily opened. I would stay here again however as it is super easy to reach and service in general was very good!

title: Paying for the location and not the hotel
text: I stopped at this hotel overnight with my wife for the Take That concert at Hyde Park... The 'Classic double room' cost £149.99 and I was very disappointed with the room. There was nothing classic about it, worn tired furnishings, walls that needed some paint on them....an uncomfortable double bed (more like 3/4 length double)..... The bathroom was tiny and the shower was pretty useless and not powerful at all...... Could be a little gem but I have stopped in lots of premier inns with work that are so much nicer and cheaper.... Unfortunately folks your paying for the location....close to tube stations and Hyde park.... I won't be staying again....

title: Great hotel
text: Berjaya Eden Park is a really nice place to stay during your visit to London! In a great location, close to the metro station and biggest attactions. As for London, rooms are spaciois and clean. Prices are decent, and service really nice! Hotel has its "old" English climat, which makes the stay even nicer :) Hotel restaurant is ome of the best, and even if you would like to try different cuisine you can do it in nearby restaurants. Recommended!

title: "DISGRACEFUL" First and Last time Ever
text: We stayed at this hotel for 6 nights in September and had the worst time ever at any hotel we have stayed at in the many years we have travelled. We booked through our travel agent a Classic room.Well it lived up to it's name "classic" alright. Headed off to bed after a 12hour flight only to be woken to the fire alarm at 11pm. On our arrival at reception we were told it was due to someone having a shower the heat from the shower set off the alarm.... yeah right... we then headed back to our room but couldn't sleep so decided to make a cup of tea guess what the jug didn't work so off to the reception again and they didn't want to know.The next morning I demanded we be shifted to another larger room. When we arrived at that room the carpet was wet and the tiny shower that you couldn't move in only provided HOT water and the paint was lifting on the ceiling. This is not fit for accommodation. This hotel is sub-standed and we are making sure we tell as many tourists as we can NOT TO STAY THERE.

title: Avoid at all costs
text: Absolute dump - the decor looks like it's from the 80s and the fact that the wallpaper is peeling off the walls and that there are cracks in the painwork, would suggest that it is that long since it's been touched. Furthermore, the TV is antiquated, there were no tea and coffee making facilities (as stated), the staff are inefficient and unhelpful, the bathroom was disgusting with poor facilites and levels of cleanliness. Thank goodness it was only for one night, I feel sorry for anyone who visits the UK who booked this for their stay. I can honestly say it's the worst hotel I've ever stayed in and couldn't wait to leave.

title: Good location, poor rooms
text: The shower was horrible, very little water. The whole room (410) need to be refreshed. Very noisy because backpakers sitting outside the hotel on the other side of street. The windows was in a bad condition and you could put all your fingers under the door. Too hot, no aircondition, no mini bar. Good service. Free wi-fi.

title: Before you Book....
text: .....work out what it is you want in a hotel. If you intend spending a lot of time in the bedroom then this possibly isn't the place for you. Like a lot of London hotels, they make use of every inch of space and therefore bedrooms and bathrooms are small, however, if like us all you want is a clean, reasonably priced hotel that is perfectly placed for a base to explore or go to the theatre then it could be for you? We had no problems with checking in, checking out, sleeping or getting a shower. Any staff we encountered were pleasant enough. We would definitely stay here again if we could get a similar deal.

title: Filthy place
text: Very expensive as its a very tiny hotel like a maze you will never know how to go to your room. Rooms are old and in a very bad condition with unpleasant odor , I've got a room in the basement where there is no view at all with a filthy smell and the there was a leakage on the wall , reception staff are very rude and unhelpful, I won't recommend this hotel for anyone

title: Worst hotel ever!
text: This is the worst hotel for the price that I have ever stayed in. We had booked a few days there either side of further travels in Europe and when we arrived for our first visit we were given a twin, rather than a double. Upon request we were then moved to a double room in the basement. The bed occupied most of the floor space and was reminiscent of our broom cupboard at home. We requested that we be assured a double room for our return (we had already paid for both visists before leaving home) and were informed that this would be possible. When we returned we were once again given a twin. The desk manager, arrogant and dismissive like most of his staff, blamed the wholesaler and then told me that as there were no patrons either leaving or arriving in the next few days, he could not move us. He had no record of our previous request. As I sat in the foyer the next morning I witnessed a procession of arrivals and departures. If you enjoy being lied to and paying exhorbitant rates for the priviledge, sobeit. Otherwise, don't go there!

title: location is the key
text: very good location situated near 2 subway station (less than 5 mins walk) and 10 mins walk to Hype park and Kensington Garden. not the highest standard in room and clealiness but super location.

title: Very Unprofessional Management!!
text: I made my booking through www.asiarooms.com on September 2010 for my holiday in UK on December 2010. According to the hotel's policy ~ "there will be no cancellation charge if a booking is cancelled before 10:00 hotel local time 1 day before your date of arrival. If the booking is cancelled later, or in the case of a no-show, the first night will be charged." However, i have cancelled the booking due to a better option. I cancelled my booking on October, which is more than 2 months of notice. I even got my cancellation email from www.asiarooms.com. But to my surprise, on January 2011 when i got my bank statement, the hotel has charged me for 1 night as a penalty. It forced me to made so many calls & write so many emails in order to get my refund. Finally, the hotel has refunded me £94 (one night charge). But due to the currency fluctuation, I have to bear another £5. I sent in the email to complaint, but they never seem want to pay me back which i think it is so unfair to me as i have to bear the cost for their mistake. I try to liaise with www.asiarooms.com too, but they seem to pushing the responsibility around. Honestly, £5 is not really a big figure to me, but as a customer, i am definitely not very happy & satisfied with their service and certainly not impressed with their professionalism. Now that i have to bear all the costs because of their silly mistake. As a tripadvisor member, I think i have the responsibility to write a review here to alert & inform all the members/readers about this issue, i really do not hope anyone of the reader here to have such an unkind experience. Just to be sure to double or even triple confirm your booking cancellation if you do not wish to pay for any cost that caused by someone's mistake. Hope this info helps.

title: DO NOT STAY HERE
text: I was a late arrival around 11pm and was given the key to a room. When I got to the room it was already occupied. They then told me it was fully booked and put me to another hotel. Whilst waiting another couple had also been overbooked and been moved to another hotel. When arriving to another hotel Berjaya had booked the room in another guests name, and more problems arose. Staff were rude and inconsiderate. I picked this hotel due to ideal location for hyde park and ended up quite far and hence having to pay tube fee. I would not recommend this to anyone!

title: Not happy!
text: The room was not very nice there was no hot water, the room was in the basement and it was very dingy looking I would not recommend this hotel even if it was cheap I expect a little bit more from London I will not be rebooking, I would not recommend to friends. Spend an extra 20 pounds, 30 pounds and get a better room in a different hotel the only good point was that the location very near the metro.

title: Good location.
text: We stayed here on a fleeting visit, and I have to say, for the price, it was good. The rooms are small. However, I liked that they were very modern. Nice big glass shower. The best bit was the location. Very easy to get to most places, either by tube, or to walk. (oxford street etc. ) Overall...would come back.

title: My room wasn't that bad....
text: ... but reading the othert reviews on here it seems I was lucky! As most of the other reviews state, it was a bit of a maze to get to the room after a straight-forward and friendly check-in. My room looked newly refurbished. It was very small though with a double bed, with good quality and clean bedding. The bathroom was lovely - new, spotless and with a good walk-in shower instead of the usual dingy bath. The water pressure was decent enough for a good shower. The main problem with the room was the lack of aircon. Even in October, it was absolutely boiling. I opened the window but it looked out on to a flat roof, so did not dare to leave it open for sleeping. The corridor was very tired looking, despite the refurbished room. Breakfast was 2 out of 5. Not much choice, very poor service by the staff, and unless you are getting it free, I would not recommend it. Overall, the hotel was good for what I wanted it for. However, I probably would not stop here again.

title: Overall hotel ok,
text: Overall hotel was ok. Rooms small and in Heatwave in London from June 11 to 20th with no air con or fans in room it was just too hot. Even with window open. Beds were not in good condition although clean linen etc. Just that pieces of fabric pulling off sides of bed supports. Mattress's needed replacing. All this sounds negative, however the location and general stuff were fine.

title: Absolutely horrid.
text: This hotel has a fancy facade but inside the place is decaying, possibly from age, possibly from neglect, possibly from the occupants smoking in their rooms I am unsure. In a nutshell for the price you pay you expect it not to be great. Its in London. In a good location. That is all. The rooms are tiny, dirty and smelly. But you do have a place to rest your head in the night and a short walk to two tube lines. I would say go for it due to its location if I hadn't stayed in Hyde park suites on the same street two doors down from Berjaya and paid less for a room that was bigger cleaner and had cooking facilities. And this was one of their budget rooms..

title: small and run down...
text: My fiancee and I stayed here two months ago. We found the reception area to be not overly friendly. In fact I felt more of a nuisance being there! The room is approximately 2.5m x 4.0m (8ft x 13ft) and that includes a bathroom and unneccessary cupboards which were run down and just took up space. We asked for a double room and recieved a twin room. The bathroom is pretty run down and the shower curtain is terrible. We couldn't have a shower with out the bathroom being flooded. The location is ok. Its close to Bayswater Road and you can catch the tube or the bus to major sights. Or stroll through Hyde Park to your destination. The next street is Queensway road with restaurants and a mall. But the area is dirty and loud at night as there is a hostel up the road and its a lively night spot. The breakfast is average. Not bad not great but oh well. I would not recommend this hotel. If you have a booking try and change it. I understand that its only a place to sleep, but its so hard to relax when its loud and your not comfortable. It wasn't dirty. I will give them that.
