title: Wonderful!
text: Perfect place to stay! Quirky, quiet and pleasurable hotel to stay.. loved every aspect, felt your room was hidden away from everyone. Close to underground so was very convenient. Plenty of amenities around too! Staff were all very helpful and friendly 👍

title: A disappointment
text: I was visiting London on a solo trip. I expected a small room, having traveled through Europe a number of times previously. but this room (216) was little more than a closet. The front desk staff were helpful but begrudgingly so. No a/c . A small section of the window opened for some fresh air. No safe for valuables. The bed was a poor twin size mattress on a piece of plywood. The bathroom was probably no than 6 sq. feet total, so picture a shower(with little pressure and poor temperature control) toilet and sink, which didn't drain very efficiently. in that area. There was shopping and restaurants nearby but mostly ethnic fast food. I did eat at one Chinese restaurant nearby that was interesting. Near Kensington Park and two underground lines, which was convenient.

title: Not any more
text: location near Queensbay & Bayswater station walking distance at different line. Free WIFI but always intermittently disconnected all the times, management claim many guests using the WIFI. Room are small, carpet are smelly and dirty, recommended carpet shampoo are the best solution. the hotel should have a facelift everything looks needed a repair. Daily breadfast no changes you get bored. Menu display is optional, as mentioned you can get a good meal outside Bayswater. Staff are friendly & helpful.

title: A decent, budget hotel.
text: This hotel is just like the ones that Americans are warned about in the travel books. It is not what you are accustomed to by American standards. The rooms are small and none-too-modern. It's just generally an old-fashioned place. That being said. I would certainly go back there again. It's cheap (we paid about $110 per double room in March 2004) and has a great central location. The breakfast consists of boiled eggs, corn flakes and toast, but is well presented. I've gotten less at more expensive London hotels. You hotel is not posh and you will not wish to hang around your room, but you'll be out seeing the sites. The staff is competent and helpful and the clientel was fine, mostly younger folks and Europeans. I stayed three nights and was never disturbed by unruly behavior. One hint, you will likely arrive via Earl's Court tube station, which is the closest station. The route from the station to the hotel is a little dreary. Keep in mind that the area just north of the hotel is much nicer and you can walk to Kennsington High Street in less than 10 minutes. In closing, the initial impression of the Hotel Oliver can be a little disconcerting to Americans used to American style motels. But the place is fine if all you are looking for is a place to rest after a long day of site seeing and theater. Save your money on the hotel bill and spend it elsewhere.

title: A small room for a reasonable price
text: We stayed for one night. The room was quite small but it had everything we needed. Thin walls, we heard everything from the hallway during the night. The breakfast was okay, but nothing special. On the plus side, the staff here was very friendly!

title: Fabulous place.
text: I needed a reasonably priced hotel in London for a weekend trip to London. I found this hotel and I have to say I had a better experience here than in some 5* hotel I have stayed in. It’s very near to Earls Court Station, 2 minute walk. On arrival the reception staff were lovely and welcoming. We were taken to our twin room, which had two small doubles instead of singles. The bedlinen was crisp and white and there were extra pillows in the wardrooms. The bed was very comfortable. There were nice white towels and toiletries in the bathroom and it was very clean. There was a hospitality tray which you don’t often get anymore, even in 5 star. We slept well and it was very quiet. The free breakfast was lovely and they served you at the table, bringing coffee, toast, egg, ham, cheese, yoghurt and cereal. The waitresses were lovely. There was also free tea and coffee all day in the dinning room. Unbelievable value for money. We will definitely return and I will recommend it to everyone. Perfect stay.

title: Nice
text: Staff are so lovely, breakfast was basic but filled us up til lunchtime. Room and bathroom were both tiny but we paid £100 a night so you get what you pay for. It was very central, underground was 5 mins away and there are some really nice pubs and restaurants if you venture off the Main Street. Only issue was dust on lockers and top of wardrobe! All in all it was fine for a 3 night stay in London 👍

title: Well appointed budget hotel
text: We Stayed for one night, the hotel was well appointed and furnished, the shower/bathroom was lovely and they have obviously refurbished recently The only real sticking point for me was we asked for twin beds, don’t get me wrong my business associate is a dear friend but I prefer not to spoon with him especially as we’re both 6’4” There were two beds but they were together as one double with a postage stamp sized Duvet over each and as they have obviously tried to cram a bed (or beds) in every available space there was no room to move them apart so just a double bed with two kids size duvets The room was far two small for two people in twin beds Saying that it was incredibly clean and not expensive and the staff we’re lovely 😊

title: Great price and location
text: I was lucky enough to find Hotel Oliver at the londontown web site. I was looking for a budget hotel, and Hotel Oliver was the only real choice I had for the length of time I stayed. I stayed for 5 days. Each room had a private washroom facility with shower. The rooms were clean, the staff were helpful. I had 2 burnt out bulbs the first day I go there, I let the front desk know, went out for dinner to find them replaced. Breakfast was served every morning and included in the price. The hotel is located in Earl's Court, close to the tube, restaurants and attractions. If you're looking for a budget hotel, this is the place. A++++

title: Great price in Kesington
text: My father and I had a great Dad-Daughter trip and we stayed in this hotel, Centrally located at a very good price and the breakfast (English not American) is included so be prepared to feast and with a full stomach go on to conquer Londinium.

title: Poor
text: The hotel is very old, rooms haven't seen paint in a really long time, holes in the walls and ripped wallpaper.Very loud as the windows don't shut properly and there is no stoppers on doors so you can hear slamming doors all the time.You have to pay deposit for the tv remote control which don't work anyway.The pictures on website don't reflect the true conditions of the rooms.I get it's central London but the price is well inflated for what you get.The continental breakfast is bowl if cornflakes, hardboiled egg, yoghurt, toast, processed cheese ( the square burger type)oh and some jams.Pretty disgusting if I'm honest.Wouldn't stay there again.

title: Bed Bugs!!!!
text: This hotel looked nice and wasn't daftly cheap, so i thought why not? I'll tell you why not. The sink and shower were both broken on arrival, the heating was stuck on, so the room was roasting! The breakfast consisted of 2 toast, 2 slices od processed cheese and a boled egg

title: Dated, small rooms and poor breakfast
text: This hotel is just about manageable for 1 night but I do not recommend. The room we stayed in was small and dated. The beds were uncomfortable and it was warm at night, so I had very little sleep as there is no air con. The breakfast is awful as it includes 2 slices of toast each, a boiled egg and a yoghurt which for the price it's disappointing.

title: Weekend
text: Clean friendly hotel a little dated and the rooms are small but enough for a long weekend could do with air con in rooms as I was quite warm on the top floor although there is a fan you need cool air for it to be effective the road outside is busy night and day so expect traffic noise and the occasional sirens but that’s London life breakfast was basic but pleasant in a clean well serviced dining room I didn’t have to wait for a table but a few did at peak (8.30) time

title: Poor hotel in a good location
text: We recently stayed at the Hotel Oliver for 5 nights. Most members of our group did not get a single warm shower over the 5 nights, but the hotel refused to provide us any compensation for this. The free wifi internet was very spotty. The rooms & bathrooms are very small (even by London standards) and have an old, musty smell to them. The hotel is in an excellent location on Cromwell Road near Earl's Court, but there are many other hotels in this area that would be better choices.

title: Real pictures
text: Pictures you can see on their website are not what you can see in real life! Someone probably edited them to show how nice this hotel CAN look like. Also do not forget about deposit for TV remote (in case you will take it home with you). Someone mentioned air conditioning. Yes there is one--screwed fan to the wall. Bathroom was just shocking but you can judge it by (not edited) the photos I took. Advise from me: pay few pounds extra and stay somewhere else...

title: Avoid where possible
text: We made a booking here out of necessity. But I’d recommend looking elsewhere as I don’t think this hotel is value for money. Our room was small and the furniture was dated - I think this is obvious from the pictures available online anyway so no big deal, you can live with that for 1 night. But the worst part was the HEAT in the room. There was a fan attached to the wall but it didn’t help at all, and it was almost impossible to sleep. Advice to management: invest in air conditioning!! We didn’t eat the breakfast but I don’t think we missed much. Also the night staff at reception were very brash and, to be honest, just plain rude. Overall it’s fine for a night if you know what to expect. However this hotel is not on par with others in this area. Avoid where possible.

title: Central location but the photos are misleading.
text: We booked this hotel because it was reasonably central and close to a tube station so we could spend the evening in central London. Parking was a bit of an issue and we ended up a 15 minute walk away. The photos on here unfortunately make it look better than it is. Not being a negative person I am struggling to find positives. The receptionist was lovely although you are charged the full cost as you book in. Too late to leave then when you see your room. Our £100 room was so tiny you wouldn't be able to have a suitcase in it and there were no facilities in it. The double bed was tiny and difficult for the 2 of us to move about in it. We had to laugh or we would have cried. The curtains didn't come low enough to cut the light out and to top it all having paid £10 deposit on the tv remote control the tv wouldn't work. At breakfast the staff wanted us to share a table with another couple so they didn't have to clear another table. We all refused. An apple, yoghurt and toast were literally plonked in front of us then we were tidied up as we ate. I assume to make us leave faster.

title: Thieves, Renovation a Lie
text: We originally booked this hotel for a few reasons, but the most important one being the in-room Wi-Fi service, as my partner was completing an online master's course during our stay in London. After we checked in at the Oliver, the first thing we did was to test the Wi-Fi. It didn't work, so we went downstairs and they said "it might be working in 2-3 days." Then the manager came out and said "Oh, my guy is coming in tomorrow morning and I guarantee 75% that it will be working tomorrow." We decided to check in (our mistake, admittedly) and took our bags upstairs, left them and went about our business for a couple of hours. While wandering around, we really decided that we had to have the Wi-Fi for my partner's coursework and that a 75% "guarantee" just wouldn't do it (turns out it was still not working the next day either). Before going out to dinner with friends, we went back to the hotel and informed the person on duty that we would be checking out, as the lack of Wi-Fi was a deal breaker for us. His solution to the problem was to call a hotel across the street and ask them if we could use theirs and have us pay the £5 for the service. That's right, he wanted us to pay for the Internet service he couldn't provide us with. After a considerable amount of discussion/arguing, the man told us that the manager would be in the morning and I would have to talk to him about having our charges reversed, as he had no power to make this type of decision. Frustrated, we set out to find another room in the Earl's Court area and were lucky enough to find one a few blocks away with in-room Wi-Fi and nicer rooms. We booked five nights and went out to dinner with our friends. After booking the other hotel (at a considerable premium), we went back the next day to talk to the "manager." We explained the situation to him and he told us "the terms and conditions state that you will be charged for two night's stay unless you cancel 48 hours in advance." We told him this was unacceptable, as the room did not have the amenities that were promised to us when we booked the room. I told him that there really was a simple solution to the problem: refund the £320 he had charged my card, I walk out the door and everyone's happy. He refused. He then called Laterooms.com, who we booked the room through, to have someone tell us the terms and conditions. I told him that I didn't need someone to tell me the terms and conditions and that since he failed to provide us with a room that had the promised features/amenities, I was due a full refund. He continued to refuse to credit back my credit card and insisted that I pay for two night's stay. At this point, I asked him if the Wi-Fi was working. He said no, it was still broken. So here we have a hotel owner trying to charge me for a two-night stay in a room I never occupied and didn't have the promised services. After arguing with him for about an hour, we finally gave in and paid for one night's stay (£49) for a room that we never even slept in. Of course they never saw a cent of it, as I contested the charges with my credit card company. Absolutely mind boggling and the worst customer service I've experienced in my life. Lastly, the hotel touts "renovations done in 2009." This is a lie. They did nothing more than replace some furniture, fix up the lobby and slap some new paint on the walls. The rooms are about as big as a shoebox. Stay away from the Oliver Hotel

title: Basic but Good
text: Me and A friend travelled from Aberdeen Scotland to London and stayed here for 1 night. we asked for directions when we left the tube station and asked a shop worker and when we said the name of the hotel they man just looked at me and said "oh the hotel oliver oh" which made me panic a little bit as he didnt make it sound a very good place to stay. Anyway when we got there we were surprised that it quite good. it looks nice from the outside and when we went in the man at reception was very helpful. we arrived before the check in time and it wasnt a probelm we paid for the room and went to our room. The room was a little small and the window was really small which made the room really warm and a little airless BUT there was a fan in the room which sorted that problem. The toilet had a shower in it and it was very clean. The only disappointing thing was that in the website it says they have luggage storage and they dont we had to leave our luggage in the dining room and the female receptionist wasnt very helpful she was more interested in flirting with the pizza delivery man.

title: poor quality
text: the location of this hotel was fine for us but it was poor value for money...the room was not very clean at all...when i pulled the bedside out i dont think the cleaners ever had, it was filthy...although we hate being cold' the heating was that high we felt like we were boiling in our sleep and had to open the window on a busy road so there was lots of traffic noise!!!!!and we wasnt sure wether it was the cleaners or not, but all morning you could here every door being opened and closed very loudly and constantly...definately dont stay here if you want a lie in!!!!

title: Such a good location and such a bad quality
text: The location of the hotel is very good, so close to the centre and museums. I stayed in a double bedroom, which was very, very small, I could barely turn around. The bed was also small, there is no chance that 2 average people can sleep normaly. The room had view on the street, that is quite nice, but you cannot sleep because of the noice. We had no warm water for 4 days and they told us that there is no problem. Breakfast is poor, you have to keep asking staff to bring you more. The towels were disgusting, stinky, wet and gray, already used. They change it every second day. Reportedly. Bedclothes had been used, there were hair all over the bed. Such a shame for a London.

title: Good budget choice
text: I spent 10 days at this location, so I had lots of opportunity to experience problems, of which there were none. Staff were friendly and helpful, breakfast service was very fast and efficient with a decent breakfast served (and I was always asked if I wanted an extra of anything). The room was clean and tidy, and although small, it was what I expected and did not find it cramped. The location is good, very close to the Victoria and Albert Museum as well as the Natural History Museum (the are basically side by side). The underground at Earl's Court is the closest, with lots of pubs and restaurants in that area, although one can find that in nearly any direction without too much work. That stop includes the Picadilly line which runs to Heathrow, and that is very convenient. I would stay here again.

title: Rude receptionists. unclean bedrooms - beware of room 18....
text: this is really an hotel on a budget. the people are not friendly. the breakfast is hard swalled. Is nonetheless conveniently located but the way they treat you does not make you whish to return. never again no.

title: medium satisfaction stay with enough facilities
text: good things: - complementary breakfast and 24hr tea with coffee - accessible location - nice towers - hair dryer negative things: - room is incredibly small with small window - bed and pillow are uncomfortable - toilet makes annoying refilling water after flush - very noisy as window, walls and door are not able to block the noise

title: Ideal budget hotel
text: Spent 1 night here with my mum so we had a twin room on the first floor. The reception is welcoming and spacious. Staff are friendly at the front desk and in the breakfast room. Was a little dubious after reading the feedback but you get what you pay for when staying in a budget hotel which is ideal for us as we were out for most of the day and evening. The room was adequate and importantly clean and warm. There are extra blankets and pillows in the wardrobe. There is a hairdryer. Kettle didn’t work so we make our brews in the breakfast room. The shower was very hot and couldn’t turn down the temperature. The windows are locked upwards and not downwards. I would take your own shower gel and shampoo as they give you 1 sachet per person which is for hair. We had a good nights sleep and breakfast was good for what you pay and is served to your table so no hanging around waiting. There is boiled egg, toast, jam, cheese, ham, tea or coffee, orange juice, apple each, yoghurt each. I would stay again but maybe not in the summer as this place I think would get hot in the rooms.

title: Very good value
text: This hotel is very convenient for public transport, in a safe and pleasant area. The staff was pleasant and helpfull. The room was small but clean and had a safe, a television, a hairdryer, a trouser press and plenty of storage and overlooked nice quiet gardens behind the hotel. The en suite shower was the smallest I have ever seen, you could not bend down to pick up the soap if you dropped it (but other hotels at the same price only had shared bathrooms so I didn't mind). There was a nice lounge with large television and comfy chairs. The breakfast was nothing exciting but quite adequate. For the price I paid, I will definitely stay there again.

title: Would not visit again
text: There are so many things wrong with this hotel it wold take ages to write it all down so let's start with the few positive facts. Staff is friendly and service minded and without them it would have been a disaster. However, the room is tiny, dark and has a worn brown wall to wall carpet which looks like it's been in place the last fifty years. The floor underneath the carpet is wobbly, uneven and sort of clicks in areas, I wouldn't be surprised if there is water damage beneath it. We had booked a room for two and found a room with the single beds separated by a bedside table fixed to the wall. Since the room was cold and drafty and the window couldn't be closed entirely (with the help from staff) my fiancé and I had to sleep in one bed due to the cold. Also, the other bed was lumpy and uncomfortable. The sound from the road makes it hard to sleep as the before mentioned window doesn't close properly, add to that a wet flag advertising the hotel flipping in the wind all night. The walls are thin, the door have a gap between the floor and you can hear your neighbors talking in other rooms, not much privacy. The bathroom is even tinier, the light over the sink doesn't work and the shower is a plastic box which has seen better days. The shower head is mounted overhead and there is no handheld head. Some pieces around the pressure and heat controls are broken. Moving on to breakfast. Eggs, an apple, toast, jam, gross single serving cheese in plastic, juice concentrate and tea. It works if you're hungry but this is certainly not what one would expect of a hotel breakfast. Oh, and single serving yogurt from Tesco. The stairs and corridors leading to the rooms are wobbly and have another type or worn wall to wall carpet. This hotel is a good option if you simply want a bed. It's close to the subway, Hyde park and some other places of interest.

title: Perfect location
text: I stayed here for 8 days in April on a business related trip.. Perfect location nearest train station is earls court and the bus stop is just 30 meters far.. Rooms are a little small but then in central london in 90 gbp you can't expect anything else .. The breakfast is typical English.. you get to meet so many new faces ..as mostly tourists stay .. Super markets, restaurants are nearby I think this is a very good value for money hotel .. as the adjacent hotels are too pricey.

title: Perfect as a stop over
text: My husband stayed here this week while my daughter was in the Cromwell hospital down the road. We only wanted a base as he wouldn’t be there much and didn’t want to pay much. The staff were unbelievably friendly and helpful they even got in the car to show us to the car park which given how nervous we were with the hospital appointment it was a godsend. The room was small but given the price what would you expect! It was clean and the breakfast was all you needed it to be. I would recommend this if you want a cheap base in the heart of London. Thank you to the staff for making a hard time much easier.

title: Good location but not satisfied with the room
text: They gave me a room which is located by the street. I arrived late and was really tired, but I was waken up at 6:00 in the morning by the traffic. I asked a quieter room or higher level and they said they didn’t Gabe Sigle room. I can only change the room with higher price. In addition, the provided the soaps which seem to be used by the previous guest!

title: budget option with low standars
text: we stayed for 5 days and the rooms were not very clean and they did not provide you many facilities. For examble they didn't have brush and hangers for towels in the toilets .Also room had in some places dust. But the breakfast was nice.

title: Olive Hotel Not Good Value
text: Very disappointed by the standards in this hotel and it did not reflect good value for money. Not happy at all with the bedrooms. The first one was shocking and I would have left but it had been prepaid. The room was old and smelt and bedding was sheets and blankets I told reception I could not stay there. Then she showed me to a slightly better room and we suffered it but again I was not happy so we went out and came back and went to bed. Surprisingly, the bed was comfortable, but my companion had been bitten by the morning. Breakfast was not very inspiring and the service was not good nor the quality of the food and bevereges. Coffee was spooned out of a large can of Nescafé Instant and the waitress growled at me when I asked for a drink after a 10 minute wait. The proprietors should take a walk up to the Coronation Hotel in Neven place to get some idea of simple but good standards of hotel keeping and service, as currently the Olive Hotel Cromwell Rd reflects very poor value for money. Do not mistake his hotel with Olive Plaza Hotels which has high standards.

title: horrible and fleas!
text: Came down to London with young people who I work with and some workers. The staff friendly and nice and from the outside really nice to look at. However, when we got in, you could smell the damp and it was really old fashioned and grim. Ordered three rooms - one single, two twins. The twins smelt of damp as soon as you opened the door. Ther was not a proper shower in the bathboom. The bathroom did look modernised but I felt nervous about having a wash in there and so did the others as did not look clean. The rooms were boiling even though the raditors weren't on so we had to leave the windows open which caused alot of noise from the traffic which went on all the night. The beds were hard and it had an awful rough blanket on which didn't look or smell clean so that was off putting. Came back from a show wanting a cup of tea went into the coffee/breakfast room and the cups were dirty, the kitchen was unclean, the kettle was dirty and the tea and coffee were left in maragine tubs which did not look attractive or like I wanted to drink from it. So I didn't have a cup of tea which I was really disappointed about Managed to sleep relatively okay despite the TV next door being contanstly on and the noise of the traffic. Was really looking forward to my breakfast as it boosted of a contential breakfast. Which in my mind is croissates, smoked ham, yogurt, selection of breakfast cereals. No, we got an apple (no choice) slammed on the table, rubbish and vile orange juice, was offered cereral which was really cheap and was left unopened over night as I saw it in the kitchen the night before. The tea and coffee were in old fashioned and dirty teapots. I hated the breakfast and so did the young people. You had no choice. We also was offered an egg. I think in total the breakfast per person was £1 worth of the money you paid it was really poor! Overall, I was really disappointed because for the young people it was there first time that they went to London and stayed in a hotel. These young people are homeless and there hostel and standard of living is better than that living in a YMCA than the hotel. Also myself and my work collegue had flea bites when we got up so we have to get some ointment. It was from the hotel because we did not have them before we entered there!!!! I am itching as I am writing this If you are looking for something cheap and nasty and this is the place. The staff were nice but terrible hotel

title: 2 Star Hotel with a High Star Service
text: Looking for a cheap place to stay for the night, we found Oliver Hotel, a budget hotel with a fantastic location. Having read the reviews on here, and ultimately deciding to take a gamble on it, I have to say there's many things we definitely did not expect. From the minute we walked through the door, having seen the view from outside, we immediately assumed it was going to be a run-down place with bad service. However, our assumptions were wrong as the lady at check-in was very helpful, very kind and well-mannered. She had us sit in the canteen/kitchen area for a few minutes as our room was still being prepared. The room itself was much better than expected. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom, slightly cramped but still visually appealing and even though there wasn't a lot of room, there was still enough space to move around. The only downside was the noise, as our room was next to the patio outside, but it didn't bother us much in the end. Breakfast was another surprise. Having read reviews of how terrible it was, we were half expecting to go into the canteen and stand in a line to grab a bowl of cereal. However, it was better than that. We were taken to a table where we received toast, eggs, ham, cheese, fruit, yogurt, tea/coffee and were even asked if we wanted more when were finished. I think a lot has to been taken into consideration when people come to a 2* star hotel but frankly, if you expect the service to be 2*, you'll be pleasantly surprised.

title: Never again
text: If you want to stay at a really terrible hotel go to the Oliver. Every time coming back to the hotel room was a nighmare. Everything is dirty, damp and absolutely depressing. You will save maybe a view Euros but loose all hapiness being on a holiday trip. Therefore my recommendation - stay as far as possible away from this hotel!

title: False advertising & sleazy night porter
text: Firstly it is not 24 hour reception. If you arrive after midnight you have to knock on the door as your key , even if you happen to sneak it out, does not open the main front door. If you can wake somebody up they will let you in at their discretion. My female travel companion arrived back around 2am and was initially refused entry. When he finally let her in he had to escort her to the room for some reason as I had the key and thought it ok to actually attempt to fondle her from behind. She spokento management next day who appeared not surprised yet no real apology or remorse. The matter is now with police. So not only is it not really 24 hr reception it advertises that its only 15 to 20 minute stroll to Oxford st , Harrodsburg etc. This is laughable, we wondered why walking and asking people the directions they looked at us weird. It takes approx 90 mns to walk to Oxford st and that's at a great rate of knots. Avoid this hotel, the rooms are rabbit warrens, staff shonky and sleazy and basically have nothing to offer what they advertise. The breakfast btw is stale toast and hard boiled eggs. Simply a joke.

title: bad experience
text: Stayed there for 3 nights after they messed up our booking and we were put in the basement very old, smelly and the beds were hard, the rooms tiny and dirty had my children and was not happy would not recomend it to anyone but did love London and can't wait to go back

title: Basic but enjoyable
text: Stayed here for two nights with my girlfriend at the start of our European Vacation. Not expecting much as we're looking for a budget type hotel we were pleasantly surprised with this hotel. The rooms are basic but clean and the reception staff were very helpful. Breakfast daily was nice with toast, ham, fruit, yoghurt and cereal provided. The location is great, very close to Earls Court Road which contained numerous restaurants and close to the tube stop Earls Court. Also just a short 15 minute walk to Harrods and a little further to Buckingham Palace. Would stay here again when we come back to London.

title: Oh dear!! This is not good
text: This is my first stay at this hotel, I stay in London each week and I'm well used to budget not luxury so I feel well placed to state this hotel is awful £75 single room, not expensive I agree, however I've stayed in much nicer budget hotels The room is tiny, tired and could do with some maintenance work The bathroom is literally a shoe cupboard although it has an en suite so it's something Checking in easy enough, went to my room, no TV remote, went back down, yes you can have a remote for a £5 deposit ??? Why didn't the reception lady tell me when I checked in. I only had a £20 note, I wasn't offered any change just given a hand written receipt The window has no view, however even if it did, you would not be able to see out of it as its thick with filth and bird poo The hotel does have a TV lounge if you don't want to sit in your room and rock in a corner Room key really awkward to use as you have a huge plastic tag on it No tea making facilities, not that I would use them It's unloved, shabby and is not a 3 star hotel, this is a 2 star at a push If I was here for a trip not work I would not stay here tonight, however it's work and I pay my own travel so I can't justify it to myself. I will not return 😩😩😩

title: Can it get worse?
text: Apart from the very polite and friendly lady who checked me in there was nothing I liked about this place. They say rooms ready from 12.00. Not the case. I was put in a box on the ground floor very close to reception and the kitchen. The door was made of plywood with a 1970's lock. The bathroom was like something I once experienced in the USSR. You couldn't sit on the loo as the toilet roll holder was in the way. The noise from the corridor was unbearable. I popped by head into the restaurant for breakfast and decided to leave immediately for somewhere more decent. And to have been charged £100 for this experience was simply rubbing salt in the wound!

title: Good location with easy access to buses and tube station
text: Pleasant location with Earls Court Tube Station about 5 mins walk. Room was a good size but did smell of stale tobacco. Room was clean with good size shower. Breakfast was adequate with choice of cereals, fruit, yoghurt, eggs, bacon, cheese and toast. Receptionist was very welcoming but breakfast staff rather surly and abrupt. That said, would stay there again.

title: Very basic
text: Location - quiet neighborhood, very close to the Earl's Court Tube Station. Few restaurants and supermarkets are in 5mins walk distance. Night bus stops in the front of the hotel. Room size, cleanliness, sleep quality - probably even below average but nothing more can be expected for this price in London. However, breakfast is okay and the staff is polite.

title: Nice hotel
text: Spent two nights here. Hotel basic but clean. Staff very friendly and helpful. We were on top floor room was small but okay for us as we were out only used room to sleep. Bathroom clean and tidy with shower and bath. Plenty of hot water. Breakfast was cereal, eggs, ham, cheese as much toast as you wanted, and yoghurt s also apples which staff served to you. We would go back again. We did enjoy our stay.

title: Great for work
text: I had a course in the area so thought I'd try this hotel despite the reviews! They were right it is a bit dated and very small rooms but very clean and the staff were so lovely. I stayed on 3rd floor and with the tiny window open it was very noisy from the road and even though there's a wall fan no aircon in summer you would bake but it is only a 2 star hotel in the end so yes there s no nice toiletries or big t.v. or tea and coffee in the room but if you need a bed for your head in a great location it's fab. So easy for the tube and train and airports plus a nice walk to Kensington palace and all the lovely shops at that end of london. I didn't try the breakfast as I was meeting friends at a local cafe but it looked fine on passing the dining room. I saw toast and cereal and I'm sure there was more.

title: No thrills but good location
text: The hotel lacked much hot water in the showers and breakfast was raher basic but it did he trick. I do not have any way to judge hotels in the UK but I had thought I would at least have a more visually appealing room for nearly 100 pounds. Location was superb, though, and the staff tried to help out when possible.

title: Location
text: We stayed for 2 nights as we were visiting an exhibition at Olympia. The hotel is within easy walking distance of both Earls Court and Gloucester Rd tube stations. It's an easy 20 min walk to Olympia. Plenty of eateries and pubs nearby. The hotel is basic and clean. The room we had was adiquate for 2 nights. We had a ground floor room near reception, which meant other guest's passed our room making it a little noisy, we could also hear breakfast being prepared in the morning. Breakfast is basic and not buffet, even the Orange juice is brought to your table. No problem with additional toast or coffee though. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. For London this is a reasonably priced Hotel and we would probably stay again.

title: Ok for a couple of nights
text: Stayed here for 2 nights whilst attending event at Olympia, not a far walk. I was weary after reading the reviews however it's not that bad. The rooms are small and the decoration does need updating however it is clean and our towels were changed and bed made. Quiet hotel not noisy at all staff were friendly. Breakfast was just toast, jam, sliced cheese in a packet, a yoghurt, Apple or banana and a boiled egg... Probably could do with some cereal. No kettle in room but it does say you can help yourself in the dining room however we didn't do this. You need to put a deposit down for safety box and remote for tv if you want to use. The shower temperature was quite hot and hard to withstand at times however better than cold. Location is good, right near earls court station and a few pubs and takeaways in the area.. right near Kensington high Street plus a large tesco nearby. If you are looking for budget, good location, somewhere that you're literally just using to get your head down then this hotel will do the job.

title: Hotel Oliver, not bad
text: This hotel is basic, but its location and reasonable price are both pluses.

title: Too many issues for just one night stay
text: I didn't book Oliver Hotel originally, but had to stay there when the hotel that I had originally booked said that there were "health and safety" issues with my room and they had to move me to a nearby hotel. The first problem was with the phone line. My friend could not call her family to inform about the hotel change, as there was simply no phone line available. We later found out that the phones were actually working, but the hotel did not allow people to use them, because they did not have a way to control the length of the calls and charge them later. That's ridiculous! Second and worst issue: my friend arrived before me and made the check-in first. When I arrived, the receptionist gave me the room keys and told me that she had left for a while. After about 20 minutes, I started to get worried that she hadn't come back yet. Then I realised that some of her things in the bedroom were in Italian and we do not speak any Italian! I was given the key to the wrong bedroom! As soon as I realised this, I ran to the reception with all my stuff. The receptionist did not admit that he sent me to the wrong room until I saw the correct room number in the form that my friend filled in at check-in. The receptionist did not apologize for this unacceptable mistake. Thirdly (as if it was not enough), our room was in the basement, located under the reception. We could not sleep due to the sound of steps from the reception and from people on the street during the whole night Other issues: the water in the shower was not hot enough and the breakfast was very poor. I definetly do not recommend this hotel.

title: Lovely, comfortable, clean and friendly
text: Came to this hotel after an awful experience. The price is excellent, the rooms are comfortable, bright and very clean. The staff are very friendly and very helpful, and you have 24 hours coffee, and the night staff was also willing to make you food when coming in late. Very good service for the price. Will definately stay here again.

title: Great night's sleep
text: Booked here to stay in town after some Xmas drinks as it was under £60 B&B for a single room. I often stay in budget hotels for single nights and this was one of the best. Clean, friendly and basic, with a reasonably-sized room. Great location to get to most places in London. Will definitely use again.

title: Great staff great value
text: I stayed the night here with a friend of mine. The room was a little small but clean and functional. Very good value for the location. I enjoyed the breakfast and give a special mention to the blonde girl I think her name was Lumi who was very helpful and friendly. For anyone looking for a basic clean room in a central location I can highly recommend hotel Oliver.

title: Ideal for London
text: Well located for Earl's Court Underground and therefore all of the city. Cosmopolitan area, wide choice to eat around there. The hotel is clean, simple no frills, but helpful staff and emphasize clean. Simple breakfast, the front desk is manned 24/7. What more do you tourists need.

title: Average Hotel for an Average Price!
text: Great location for Earl's Court Exhibition Centre & Earl's Court Tube Station! There were plently of amenities, bars, resurants and supermarket close by. Hotel room was a bit dark (basement) and the window had been left open, so it took ages for the room to warm up a bit!! Room was clean, bathroom could have been better (hair on the floor!) Carpets a bit worn and net curtains definately could have done with a wash!!! Bed was like sleeping on the floor, it was so hard that I woke numerous times feeling very stiff!! Very uncomfortable!! Reception staff very helpful and pleasant throught stay and Breakfast Staff a bit surly!! ( A smile wouldn't hurt girls!!) Continental breakfast was adequate, but I would have preferred a cooked breakfast!! I think tea and coffee facilities in the room would have been preferrable, but was available in the Breakfast Room at any time. The stay was ok just for one night, but for more than that, Hmmm!!! No definately not!

title: Basic but solid.
text: Used this hotel on business trip and all that can be said is that you get what u pay for. Used it as a place to crash at night. you get solid personal service from owner/manager as is hands on. Treat staff with respect and one will be treated as such.

title: Never ever
text: I stayed here two nights from October 1st to October 3d 2013. The hotel is old very old, the room was quite dirty and smelled of smoke. The problem occured one morning on Thursday 3rd : usually when I'm in hotel and I leave for the morning, afternoon and night , I prefer not to leave the key at the reception, and I dindn't have any problems in every hotel I stayed all over the world. That morning a very rude person asked me to leave the key at the reception, because of '' the rule of the hotel''.....and .when I told him '' ok show me where this kind of rule is written and i leave the key here '' he simply told me '' is written somewhere ... but I cannot show you know''... WHAT? Umbelievable..

title: Great hotel even better price
text: My father and I stayed at Hotel Oliver, we had a delicious English Breakfast in the morning, then walked to Kensington Palace, had a lovely tour, we took the tube and also visited the wine library for lunch and after that walked the London Tower at night went to the Royal Opera house, I loved the hotel it was clean, nice, I loved the old house where it stands, the terrace etc. I do not understand ugly reviews, I do not at all! I will stay over and over again, I highly recommended.

title: Not good value for money
text: The hotel is well located and cleaned but it is very outdated. For the price we paid for that room there would have been much better alternatives in the area.

title: Great location but not the greatest hotel
text: Stayed here when we saw take that at Hyde park which were fab. However although we were out all day we were disappointed when we got back to the hotel. It was one of the cheaper ones around at the time as the F1 etc was on the same weekend Receptionist was lovely however the staff at breakfast were awful. We had a 10-15 min wait just to have our table cleared and when we did we got toast , a boiled egg (no cutlery), a yoghurt, an apple, cheese slices wrapped in plastic and a couple of slices of ham. And jam on the table. Paid £120 for an exec room but it was more like a standard room to be honest. Bathroom was lovely though but the beds were uncomfy. I wouldn't recommend other than location is excellent. And didn't ruin our stay. Bonus it had wifi which worked in our room.!

title: Damp rooms
text: We stayed the Oliver Hotel as it was nice and close to Earls court. Unfortunately the rooms were extremely damp the bathroom was disgusting and none of the electric sockets worked, not that it would have been safe to use considering the dampness. Even though the closeness to Earls Court was great and the Hotel was nice and easy to find. I would most definately NOT recommend this hotel to anyone!!!

title: It is a cheap clean hotel in heart of London.
text: I think my title speaks for it self. It's cheap and clean, 24 hour staff and we only paid 70 as a couple for the night which was perfect for the gig. Breakfast was a nice added extra as I'm sure saved us £10-15

title: Get what you pay for....
text: The place is pretty easy to find from Earl's Court station and looked lovely from the outside. Inside was quite dark but was clean. The receptionist was nice and friendly and let us check in early. We had a single and a twin booked and got told we had been upgraded.... I'm glad we did as I dread to think what the classic rooms are like! The room was functional and did the job, beds were clean and surprisingly comfy however there are a few things that need addressed.... The tea bags on the tea tray were just loose and had hair on them (not our hair as we just checked in) this is pretty unhygienic, they really should get individually wrapped tea bags!! We just settled for coffee in the morning. The shower door was off the rails at the bottom and was a bit awkward. Apart from this everything was fine. Probably wouldn't go back but for what we paid we can't really complain! It's a basic hotel but I believe if you want luxury then your gonna have to pay for it!

title: unfriendly staff
text: I was in this hotel with my mom between 19-20.11-13, it is ok if you just want to sleep. Staff was very unfriendly, reception persons tried, but the others...no good morning, no goodbye no nothing and when we try to ask some advise to some place and shop, they criticise our choises and so on..breakfast was ok, but the åerson who worked there...you cannot be and look more unfriendlier, it obviosly was not personal beause they behave like that almost everyone and two ladies table next to us wondered that have they done something wrong because no one didn¨t even say good morning, same to us. I work my self in the customer service and accomodation services and I don´t aloud anyone in our company to bahave like that with customer, unfortunately we felt ourself not wanted.. Room was smelling very damped and we kept windows open almost all the time when we were in the room. I visit London many times a year and have use same price range places and I would not use this hotel twice, places where I have been were fullybooked and i think for reason, this was my moms first trip to London and that is the reason why I am so sad about that, but this is not her last, so better luck next time.

title: ABSOLUTELY APPALLING
text: We booked this hotel for my birthday weekend away. This hotel was one of the worst I have ever stayed in. The welcome from Reception was rushed, we were kept waiting whilst the receptionist dealt with answering the phone, dealing with other members of staff and even got the wrong booking and said our card had been declined!!! not the case as she was looking someone else's booking details. Our room was small unclean and cramped. No tea or coffee facilities, no complimentary toiletries, no hair dryer. If you expect breakfast then think again.... we had to clear our own table with left over food and plates. The food that was on offer was cheap and basic, white toast a boiled egg, sliced ham, cheese slices !!!! This hotel is dated, old and dirty and the service is appalling. Very disappointing. I will not be staying here again.

title: Would never recommend
text: I have read other good reviews about this place but I'm not even sure if they're about the same hotel. Our stay here started bad and only got worse. We arrived to check in more than half an hour after check in begins and were given our room key. We made our way up to our room to find that it was still being cleaned and were told to wait in the hall. Once we got into our room we found it stank of cigarette smoke. It was also really hot so we tried to turn on the fan - didn't work. The next problem was when we wanted to shower. We had to leave it running for 7minutes for it to be anything other than freezing. Once it warmed up it was scorching and wouldn't even go back to cold. We left it and tried again in the morning, but had the same problem. It was too hot for any of us to be able to shower - this is disgusting. Besides all of this the service was appalling and the breakfast bar was not even worth visiting.

title: Very good value for money
text: We stayed in this hotel for a long weekend. We arrived early, but the receptionist very helpful finding a room ready for us. Although small it was clean, with lovely soft towels and crisp Cotten sheets. The shower room was also small, but adequate enough. There was a TV with DVD, hair-dryer and trouser press. Considering the cost, I was very pleased. Location is great, close to Gloucester Road tube station, Sainsbury's and Waitrose supermarkets, 15 minute walk to the museums, a further 15 minutes walk to Hyde Park or Harrods. In the other direction 10 minutes walk to Kensington. The hotel is a lovely old Victorian building, the TV lounge has lovely stained glass window. There is a courtyard garden. You can help your self to tea and coffee from the breakfast room. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise. Cereals, ham, processed cheese and boiled egg, orange juice, yoghurt, hot toast and choice of jams and marmalades. Fresh, tea, coffee or hot chocolate. We found staff were very attentive and helpful. This is a good little 'budget' hotel, good location and great value for money. We look forward to staying here again later in the year.

title: Nice
text: A very small but perfectly functional room, with an equally small and functional en suite bathroom (shower, sink, toilet). Ours was a room looking towards the back of the building and a wonderfully tall tree where birds were singing (you may not like this in early mornings though)

title: It was like a real life nightmare!
text: On arrival the receptionist (who i believe could be the managers daughter) was rude and spoke to us like children, she was the one with the language barrier not us! We were not shown to our room (which was in the basement). We had to drag our suitcases down a horror movie starcase or squish into the tiniest lift in the world. When we entered our room through a tiny door it was like stepping into a lunchbox. The wardrobe and dressing table space was adequate but then we got to the bedroom. A window with bars on with no light coming in so it is hard to tell what time of day it is, a double bed and a single bed squished into a space that you couldn't swing a cat in! We don't want to mention the stains on the bed! Bathroom-don't even ask, just beware of sticky floors and an ancient shower head. On to the full english breakfast...WHAT full english breakfast? Cornflakes, Branflakes, boiled egg or (processed) ham was the question our lovely receptionist (now waitress) asked us. Plastic cheese, a random yoghurt, a not so fresh apple and toast are placed in front of you and you must choose from the other delicious items! No sign of bacon and fried eggs anywhere. To sum it up this hotel is the worst i've ever stayed in, it shouldn't be allowed to be open!

title: Mr
text: My son and I stayed there for 4 days. By far the smallest room ever. Comfortable linen, Wi-Fi non existent, very noisy due to very thin walls! The location is good, next to Earls Court station. The cleaning and kitchen staff was very efficient and friendly. The breakfast is a typical low budget continental but this is expected.

title: A week in the capital
text: A weeks stay in this hotel was very pleasurable. The hotel is five minutes walk from Earl's court tube station, situated on Cromwell road . The room was comfortable, en suit , Tv,trouser press, double glasses , And virtually no noise from outside. Breakfast was very good and well served at the table, 24 hour reception, safe,good WiFi, Will defo stay here again.

title: Over priced tiny double room with bad quality
text: Me and my wife stayed at this hotel for 4 nights during a conference at Imperial College London. Pros + Good Location + Breakfast Quality (not the quantity) + Free wifi with good speed. Cons - Too Little space in the room and in the toilet - Asked for a kingsize double, but didn't even got a full double bed. It's kind of or bit bigger than semi double. - Not cheap compare to the facilities. - Hand written Invoice. - Quantity of the Breakfast: It's not buffet, it's served by the staffs. - Old fashioned furniture and window - Not Soundproof. You can hear the sound/talk from the other rooms. Overall Not recommended.

title: Horrendous!
text: Stayed here and the service was very poor, the sheets were torn. The breakfast was disgusting stale bread to make toast and a nasty yoghurt with water! besides that i left my tablet in the room and they claimed they could not find it until i threatened to inform the police and it miraculously turned up.

title: Basic good for a couple of nights
text: The hotel room was very small and basic much like a hostel room the breakfast was ok the receptionist was really great. The total was centrally located and was great for the one night we stayed there as we spent the whole day out and didn't get back until midnight so all we needed was a bed and a shower. I wouldn't suggest it for a swanky hotel visit or honeymoon or such like but for cheap and cheerful it was ok. Not sure if i would go again though but would if couldn't find a better option

title: Overnight stay
text: Stayed at the Hotel Oliver for one night recently whilst down for a rugby match, found the hotel staff to be very friendly and helpful, the bedrooms were clean and relatively comfortable, the hotel itself is showing day to day wear it suited our needs.

title: Centre hotel es with the basics on it
text: We went there as soon as we arrived to London and the rooms where really normal and clean with the basic in it (shampoo, clean towel...). the only thing was that they cleaned the rooms once in two days instead of a daily cleanance. The breakfast was a British one with many things (but not a buffet one) like tea, coffee, boiled eggs, toasts, juice, ham, yogourt... The people working there was very kind and tried to help you when needed. The hotel is very well located but instead of a 3 star one I would put them in a lower category.

title: Aware of Bed Bugs
text: We stayed in this hotel for 11 nights in a triple room . Every thing is going well until the 10th day of our stay, red spots were visible all over our body. Yes, we did complaint to the hotel that they might be ants or bedbugs in our beds. First hotel staffs refused about any ants or bedbugs in their hotel until we show our red spots as the proof to them, They promised to do deep cleaning during daytime while we were going out of town. When we came back at night, our room was clean and smell good so we went back to sleep. The next morning we found alive bedbugs on our bed sheets and pillows. Do not recommended this hotel to anyone. We are every disappointed and suffer from terrible itchy.

title: Good location
text: Handy for central London but stayed in better hotels for the price. Room was ok .. Cold but not the end of the world . As I was only using as a bed for night stay..Staff friendly .. Had to go back down to pay £20 deposit for TV remote ?? More towels and soap would have helped and no coffee tea making in room was annoying . Little basics you expect even in budget price hotels .

title: Good price for extremely good position!
text: We booked last minute.It was the best offer we had.The Hotel is close to Earls court tube station in Kensinghton and it is in a really nice and posh area full of restaurants and some pubs as well.Especially it's very near to the Natural History Museum.(10 min walk).The room was enough confortable and clean with an adequate breakfast.After all we didn't expect nothing more for that price by considering prices in London.I strongly suggest this Hotel..so you can spend money you save by doing shopping and pubbing in London.

title: Little more than a dump...
text: Location is the major plus. They also arranged for a swanky BMW to take me to my conference location the next day which did not cost much more than a London taxi would have. On the negative side : Rusty sanitary fittings, torn blankets, Spartan breakfast, deposit for the TV remote (!!!), seriously shaky elevator, TV screen slightly bigger than a laptop screen, Chinese shampoo (didn't use it), a piece of soap that could not have been any better than a piece of stone...

title: Indian Hospitality
text: Absoulutely nice! The staff has a very good and friendly attitude. This is a budget private Hotel and totally satisfying for what it is. I has the luck to get a Queen size bed and a bathtub, which I asked for in my Booking. The room is tastefully desigend and I loved the high ceiling. Since I always stay in this area of London I will definetely return. And the Bus 74 stop is right in front of the Hotel, which comes handy during wind and storm for trip to V&A or Baker Street! Faboulos.

title: Don't believe the bad reviews!
text: We were almost put off staying here because of the bad reviews however the staff were polite and helpful, the room whilst on the small side was spotless and even though we were at the front of the hotel we weren't bothered by traffic noise. Breakfast was a bonus! Conveniently located and at a good price we would stay here again without hesitation!

title: Good honest hotel
text: A perfectly adequate hotel, pleasant staff, clean rooms, quiet room at the back away from the busy main road. Good secure parking just around the corner. Didn't partake of breakfast, so cannot comment on standard and availability of comestibles.

title: lovely looking hotel.
text: Nice room but felt a bit put out we were told we were in the basement. Lower floor might have sounded better !! Lovely area and the hotel looked very grand and luxurious. Nice staff, but breakfast was a bit frantic. We were told the staff don't normally have it so busy and we had to keep asking for things. Its a continental breakfast. Yoghurt apples, toast and boiled eggs. Tea or coffee and orange juice.

title: Basic but comfortable!
text: Stayed for one night whist visiting Comic Con so wasn't in the room much apart from sleeping. Great air con which we needed, comfy bed, nice big shower, breakfast was ok.. tea, coffee, orange juice, toast, boiled eggs, yogurts, apples, sliced ham & cheese squares all served at your table by waitress. Staff were friendly enough and very helpful when it came to parking (although it's like a maze trying to get out of the carpark!!!) Cleanliness was superb, couldn't fault it! As title says, room was basic for an 'executive double' but was fine for what we wanted. Would stay here again if needed.

title: Average but great position
text: The room I was given was clean but very small, and so was the washroom. Taps need fixing, and probably a bit of renovation. Anyway, the price was very fair for this area, the hotel is close to the tube and 15 minutes walk from Olympia, the city fair, and the staff was ok.

title: Small and cosy
text: We were here in december 2010. The location of the hotel is great - Earl's Court station is a short walk away (6 min), lots of restaurants nearby. Our room was very small, but clean and cosy. We had a clean bathroom with a bathtub, and a small flatscreen tv. In order to get the remote control, you have to go to the front desk and pay a small fee - which you get back if you return the remote control. Breakfast was alright. We were there during the winter, so the heating was on, but it became too hot in our room and we couldn't turn the heating off. That's the only negative thing I have to mention. And we could open the window, so it wasn't that bad after all. Considering how much we paid, I was very pleased with our stay and would definitely come back.

title: Very good accomodation
text: I was looking for an accomodation at midnight of a hot saturday, after a check out from an indecent hotel. The guy at reception was very gentle, i got a very good room at a very good price considering the place. Silent, clean, air conditioning working well. It doesn't achieve the 5 stars because of the private bathroom and the shower (good for children, not for adults). Earls Court Subway at 5 minutes by foot, some markets and self service washing machines really close.

title: Pre-Cruise, Seven day visit in London
text: We chose Hotel Oliver because of its moderate price and excellent location. During our 7 day visit to London we were able to use the tube at a nearby location for several tours. The Hotel is nothing fancy, yet clean and their morning breakfast satisfied our needs quite well. I would recommend this Hotel to anyone who has the needs as we had.

title: Basic hotel
text: I would recommend this hotel if you're not picky and just want some decent place to stay. This is one of the most basic, no-frills hotel, and also the smallest one I've been in. The single room is tiny. Probably just slightly bigger than Harry Potter's room under the stairs in the Dursley's house. The toilet? Even smaller. The doorway to the toilet is just nice for me to walk through normally. And I'm a petite Asian girl. If you're a normal-sized westerner, you'll have to crab-walk your way in. If you're overweight? You should probably just cancel your booking. Receptionist who checked me in was kinda rude. But the other staff like the cleaner and kitchen staff were very nice and efficient. Breakfast was toast, hard boiled egg, ham, cereal with juice and tea/coffee. Not too bad.

title: four days in London
text: we stayed at Oliver Hotel for three night, we were a group of 9 people. Rooms were clean and we got clean towels every day. we had 5 rooms: room n.1 was good, big and with a comfortable bath tub. room n. 4 was the worst small and narrow but clean. Room n. 16, n. 35, n. 46 were not so big but clean. Breakfast was not so rich : yoghurt, fresh apples, tea, coffee and milk. Only boiled eggs and toast. I suggest this hotel for short period in London because the area where is located is perfect to reach every part of London easily.

title: economical with good location
text: Met our requirements of a clean, economical and well located hotel. Room was basic but clean

title: Barely adequate
text: Reasonably smart frontage but idiosyncratic check-in staff, more concerned with controlling their image and being officious than providing genuinely welcoming customer service. Room barely adequate - even allowing for relatively cheap rate obtained through web search. Bed not bad though base material torn. Curtains too short for window, letting bright light through over bed. En-suite toilet superficially clean in appearance but dirty/urine smell in area. Breakfast - hard boiled sulphorous egg with toast and butter no margarine available. Waited at empty check out desk (staff away) and then left keys on desk after a few mins - all of this watched by owner from a distance sat talking to friend(s), did not offer so much as a thank you. Won't go back, ever.

title: OK ish
text: The room was a little basic and the breakfast was rubbish. The male receptionist on check-in was totally uninterested although the female receptionist on check-out was much friendlier - as were the laundry ladies. It was in a convenient place to where I needed to be but I doubt I will be staying here again.

title: short stay at hotel oliver
text: got booked in nice and early and was given a room on the seondfl floor it was a basic room bit tired and in need of refurb it served a purpose but dont think i will stay here again the breakfast was basic really only good part was the closeness to the transport to london i think that if they did it up then it would be better as the room is very small and could do with new carpets

title: Good value and location
text: After reading some reviews about the hotel, we were a little apprehensive about what we were going to be faced with. Mainly as we were off to see Robbie Williams in concert that night, we knew it would only be a base to crash out and therefore, we weren't that worried if the room wasn't up to our usual standards, however we were pleasantly surprised. The receptionist was informative and friendly, our room adequate and clean. Soft clean white towels and crisp linen sheets a comfy room a bit limited on space but fine for our needs. Breakfast included in price started our next day off a treat.

title: Convenient for a short stay
text: A hotel easy to get to and located not to far from Earl's Court station. We visited London for one night with a group of four. We had the executive en suite room in the basement that was quite o.k. Enough space and the en suite bathroom was spacious enough. The shower was excellent. Our other fellow travelers had a standard twin room. That room was small and the bathroom very small. All beds were good. The hotel was quit as our rooms were at the back. The breakfast was simple but adequate. The breakfast room is small for the number of guests and the staff was pushed to the limit but was polite and helpful. Parking is a point of attention. A short stop is possible in front of the hotel and we were told that after seven parking is for free. Although wireless is available we did not manage to get connected.

title: Looked so good. . . but disapointing.
text: We chose this hotel because its close to Earls Court tube station (4 mins walk) which is in Zone . . . and the pictures looked good. However don't believe everything you see because the hotel is tired and in desperate need of a facelift. Holes in carpets, pealing paper and doors with no handles. It was impossible to actually sit straight on the toilet in our room - you had to sit sideways! But, the hotel was a clean as they could get it and the staff were helpful. It seemed to be busy and I believe the rooms in a more modern extension were better than outs. We're still looking for a decent hotel in London without paying the earth - we didn't find it here.

title: Satisfactory
text: Despite negative reviews of this hotel, we were very satisfied with our experience. My Mother, my sister and I stayed in a room together. The facilities were adequate, we had the use of the dining room all day. The staff were friendly, and overall, we were quite happy with this centrally located hotel. I would definitely stay there again as it was great value.

title: What's with the grey eggs?
text: My boyfriend and I were looking to stay in a centrally located Hotel in London for my 24th birthday. On contacting the Oliver, the receptionist sounded "a mess", not entirely sure of whether she could book us into a double room. following various phone calls, she finally manged to organise herself and get us in. 60 quid, not so bad considering the location for a double room. In hindsight, it may have been a large, or should that be enlarged single.. Our room was on the first floor, bonus, but on opening the door I was greeted with what can only be described as a nuclear heat wave. Ah well, I thought, maybe I'll open the window... NO CHANCE! Window was the size of a small child and utterly smattered in pigeons poo. I arrived late at night so didn't quite understand the reason for this until the next day. Opening the barely locked window, I discovered it looked out onto the side of the building. In this alleyway there was not one, not two, but three pigeon's nests and spikes to prevent said pigeons. As well as mounds, and I mean mounds of more pigeons mess. Utterly vile and completely unhygenic. I'm quite surprised one of the little blighters didn't come in for a nose around. Breakfast, we were told was served from 7.30 to 9.30. As our night's sleep was interrupted by various sirens, traffic and the unberably hot room preventing us from getting any rest, we slightly overslept and got to breakfast at 9.20. Reasonable I thought, oh no. We were ignored until 9.35, at which time I had to attract the waitresses attention with a polite "excuse me, can we order some breakfast?" She glared at the clock, about to completely refuse my offer when I again politely informed her that we had been sitting there for 15 mins. She disappeared and slammed down our new cutlery and plates and informed us of the varied and high quality choice of breakfast which was egg or cereal. The manner of this particular waitress was utterly inexcusable, she treated us as if we'd just slaughtered a small puppy. Not 5 mins later, an elderly couple appeared, confused as to what time breakfast was, and at one point it seemed that she was about to refuse them food. Luckily they were fed the same high quality rubbish that we had. And all on my 24th birthday. Utterly disgraceful. Give this place a wide berth in future. Unless, of course you fancy taking home a few pigeony friends with you.

title: What A Dissapointment
text: We booked this hotel to be close to the Stamford Bridge for a match. it was very disappointing, the room was smelly and the covers on the bed were fusty. we had our teenage son with us and his bed was positioned across the bathroom door which had no handle on the outside . every time we need the bathroom we had to move the bed. The breakfast staff all spoke broken english and on the first morning we went down for breakfast and not knowing what was happening we went to the boiler in the corner to pour a coffee and out from behind the hatch this girl bellowed SIT DOWN NOW. we felt about 2ft high. the breakfast was cherry yougart, apples, coffee and toast and if you asked nicely some cereal was provided. this hotel was not cheap . We had to go through the fire escape to get to the lifts and this area was dirty and stinking of smoke were obviously people were using as a smoking area. we will never be back beware
