title: Superb 2 week stay in London
text: Once again I find myself questioning why an establishment has such a low scoring. I stayed here for a 2 week business trip, and I thoroughly enjoyed my stay! I arrived after a hell on earth tube experience

title: Better not
text: We booked just for one day in this hotel near Kensington at the end of zone 1 of London metro. We chosen it for the position, not certainly for the price or the services. Price indeed was not comparable with the service, 100 pounds, for a really small old double room where is really uncomfortable to move, with a small old bath and a not so polite service. Breakfast included Yes, but nothing special if you don't really really love boiled eggs. Maybe with the same price is better to find something else

title: a decent sort of place
text: Once again my wife and I stayed at the Langorf in north London. As usual, the staff were welcoming. The breakfast was still good. But the hotel is a year older, and the comings and goings of guests have made it a little shabbier. Rooms are smaall (but clean) -- and after all it's a London hotel. For London it is good value -- and, in fact, very honest value.

title: The apartment is lacking some essentials.
text: The Langorf is on the outskirts of London in a working class neighborhood. We spent a week in one of the apartments. When we entered, we immediately noticed a musty smell, but we were initially impressed with the roomy living room. We found the beds to be clean but with hard mattresses, and there were only 3 hangers in each of the two closets. The TV had 6 local channels, and we were surprised to see that the only US channel was The Bloomberg Channel with lots of financial news but not much else. Our biggest disappointment was in the kitchen which was lacking in what we consider some basic essentials such as plates, drinking glasses, and hand towels. So, we made our first trip from the apartment to the local Sainsbury's store and bought paper plates, drinking cups, dish soap, paper towels, a cork screw, and a new electric kettle as the one in the apartment looked very old and dirty. There is no microwave, and the fridge is small. The wireless Internet access worked well once we got the correct password from the front desk, but it cost one British Pound per hour to use. The daily maid service was a nice feature with fresh towels, but we were led to believe that breakfast was included with the price of the apartment, but it was not. The guests in the apartment above us came home late and were very noisy. The apartment is a short walk from the Finchley Road subway, and the charming village of Hampstead is just up the road. The apartment did not meet our expectations, and we wished we had found a better place to stay for a week. The price of the apartment was also 10 British Pounds a day higher than what was quoted over the Internet.

title: Nice and quiet location
text: We chose here as it was close to my niece’s apartment and the tube station. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The continental breakfast was adequate to last us through the day. Suited our needs quite well.

title: Nice no frills spot
text: My wife and I needed a nice yet inexpensive place for a London overnight before catching a flight. We found this online and tried it. Was perfect for our needs. Quiet neighborhood. Close to the tube. Free wifi. Free breakfast. Small but comfortable, clean and functional room. Courteous staff. We checked in then took the tube into the city for dinner and some walking. Returned to have a nightcap at the nearby Sainsbury center - nice. Restful evening, good breakfast and we were off. It isn't the ritz but was exactly what we were looking for. About 45 min to heathrow with one change.

title: Poor
text: Nice place, but too old and definitely too expensive. Stuff at reception was good and breakfast as well. I did aspect a bit more cause it seems very small hotel and in a nice location but there are better place in London for the same price.

title: Rooms not as advertised.
text: We chose this hotel based on the location and earlier reviews. Unfortunately I have to agree with the more recent reviews in that the rooms don't match to photos. The hotel itself is very "English" and that is what we wanted in preference to a standard hotel room that look the same regardless of where in the world you are. Our first impressions were tainted by the state of the carpet in the foyer area... Threadbare!! Not a great first impression. Our room was one of the refurbished rooms but not sure how long ago that was as there was water leaking through the bathroom ceiling from the room above plus everything seemed to be done on the cheap sometime ago. It was very hot when we arrived and all the window were wide opened and there were NO insect screens so the room was full of bugs. Our room was on the ground floor facing the street and we had these massive spot lights shining on the facade to the early hours of the morning which lit up our room too. The free wifi is very slow and unreliable. The breakfast was quite nice but if you went late there was not much left and the staff could be a bit on the abrupt side and often stood chatting in the kitchen when their services were required in the dining room. Our bed was less than adequate with the sheets barely fitting the bed. Our room was quite large which was good and the location was handy and in walking distance to trains, buses and shops. We did not experience noise from other rooms or above as had been previously reported on TA and was a concern to me given that we were on the same floor as reception. Reception staff were polite and friendly but I had the feeling that they were telling me what I wanted to hear rather than the truth. Sadly NO we won't be back as it sounded so good when we booked months ago.....

title: Big Disappointment
text: Location was fine, except for the unexpected uphill walk with luggage, but the Langorf Hotel is in serious need of a major refurbishment. The carpets and beds should have been replaced years ago, and the bathroom was in really bad condition. Just because a hotel is old, though, doesn't mean it has to be dirty. The kitchen and bathroom were repulsively dirty. My room was on the 3rd upper floor with no lift, so don't even think of staying here if you have any physical challenge with hills and stairs. The breakfast room was far too small for the number of guests, so the staff quite rudely told people to wait until something was free. Even that is a simple thing: If there's not enough room, try being pleasant with your guests! The breakfast was one of the least appealling I've encountered at even really low-budget hotels in London. Overall, I wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone unless they are simply looking for a low price, the location is really convenient for them, and they don't have any problem with filth and mildew.

title: a wonderful stay
text: This was our second stay in the Langorf Hotel and, as the last time, we were delighted. We had a triple room, which was very, very beautiful, clean and comfortable. Plus: the third bed was a real one. Experience has shown us, that some hotels will give you just a folding bed instead. Our (quite huge) bathroom was amazing, all neat and clean – looked done up. We had sort of a big glass shower, there was absolutely no dirt or mildew anywhere. Breakfast was small but nice. You'll get a continental one with boiled eggs, buns, croissants, cheese & ham, cornflakes, jam, honey, … if wanted, you are able to get toast as well. A member of staff will be glad to ask you for your wishes. The staff is very helpful and polite. You'll never get a rude answer of them and they are keen to help you with whatever concern you have (and provide you with a special map). As the hotel is located a little bit outlying of the main street, you're able to enjoy a quite and peaceful stay. There is a little mall (with a supermarket included) nearby and you can find the next underground station just a 3 minute-walk away. The hotels offers a free charge service to store your luggage if your flight departs after your checkout. So, what can we say? The Langorf Hotel is a really good choice and we will surely come back.

title: helpfull staff
text: We had an enjoyable one night stay to see a show. Although the room was small, it was clean and adequate. Nothing was too much trouble for the staff and all were very friendly. The position is close to the tube and parking at a nearby supermarket is convenient ( £10.50). Breakfast was good and served till 9.30. We would certainly return.

title: Great Stay at Langorf Hotel!
text: Stayed for 6 nights and had wonderful service. Staff was friendly and helpful. Room was clean and comfortable. Very nice stay.

title: Visiting Family
text: The room was very worn. Carpet filthy, sofa worn and old. Bathroom so small toilet roll behind you that fell off wall when pulling the roll. Only shelf sloped so everything fell off! Fawlty Towers! Stayed 3 nights as close to my Aunt and Uncle. Last night people arguing all night and I called reception twice to complain. We did not sleep that night oh and no mattress pad and the mattress was stained. We will never stay again. Room was awful. However front desk staff very pleasant and helpful. We did not pay for our last night Glad to get that off my chest !

title: Short and Sweet
text: We had a short but memorable stay at Langorf Hotel. The hotel is well located in a quiet residential area but very near the main Finchley Road with the tube station 5 minutes away. Though small, the hotel had the bare essentials to make one’s stay very comfortable. We had a bathtub in our bathroom with a nice big shower. Besides, it was well equipped with the necessary supplies like shampoos, soaps, etc. While the room was small, the placement of the bed and sofa-cum-bed gave it a spacious look. There was also a safe in the room which came handy although to operate it, we had to call the front desk. The service was good even though the hotel seemed short-staffed with only one person handling the front desk. The breakfast area was small. Though they served continental breakfast, the spread was excellent with a wide variety of cold cuts, assorted bread, pastries, waffles, cereals, etc. to choose from. For egg lovers, there were boiled eggs available. A major positive was the free Wi-fi that was available. Along with this, there was access to a computer near the front desk which guests could use for free. Overall, we had a good stay at Langorf. It was not like a typical hotel and a nice homely touch to it.

title: Dilapidated, horrible
text: Awful. Threadbare carpets in room and stairs, damp wallpaper peeling off near the ceiling, toilet leaking onto floor, paint cracked in en-suite, lampshades bubbling with age, desk/dressing table, bedside cabinets, coffee table all peeling. Just shockingly bad. Nice quiet street though, actually slept quite well, but then it was a heavy night. No cooked breakfast available - really????

title: Really really needs a refurbishment
text: I used this hotel for many years and put friends and family there regularly. Went back myself this week and while pleased that it keeps the old family atmosphere and the prices are really reasonable, it really needs a refurbishment. The carpets are truly awful and must not have been changed for a very long time. While the sheets and towels were very clean and so was the bathroom the bedcover was also a bit dodgy. Good points was a large safe, good wifi, and the room was really spacious and warm. It wouldn't take much to make it in a really good hotel again but the carpets in particular are a real problem.

title: Overpriced in need of refurbishment.
text: We normally stay in Central London in one of the big chain hotels. We decided to stay here as we were going to Wembley on Saturday night. The hotel is desperately in need of redecoration, with stains on the carpets and seat bases all over the hotel. Bed was uncomfortable, and room was noisy. You can hear doors banging and floorboards creaking all night. Not a patch on the usual places we stay and we thought it would be considering it was £130 a night. I won't stay here again. On the plus side the location is ok.

title: Three Night Visit
text: My family was 'upgraded' to a garden flat on our recent visit, which gave us more space at the same price. Unfortunately, the kitchenette was dirty (and showing the desk manager the dirt did not have any effect on its subsequent cleanliness), there were dirty extra blankets tossed in a closet, the bathroom was unheated (and really cold), the bed was the most uncomfortable I have ever slept in, and the noise from the street was considerable. One evening the fire alarm went off and frightened the life out of us, but it was only someone in one of the upstairs flats frying something. Breakfast was the minimum, but fine. It's not far to the Finchley Road tube station, and close to the buses. The price was reasonable, and the staff seemed friendly. I would say to try to stay in the hotel proper, facing the back. Avoid the flats!

title: Never again
text: I currently travel to London on a weekly basis and the company I work for normally book me into Hilton/Holiday Inn/Novotel etc. However this particular day London was very busy and the hotel agency could only offer the Langorf Hotel. I looked at their website and tripadvisor and thought it looks ok - it was only for one night. What a mistake!! When I arrived at the hotel I checked in and went to my room which was chinzy but clean, however there was an awful banging noise coming from somewhere so I went to reception and was told it was the boiler which was faulty and suggested I turned the radiator knob down as this might stop it - it didn't. Whilst I was at reception I enquired about an evening meal - the receptionist said they really don't do meals but took me to the kitchen and offered to make me a cheese toastie!! being a female on my own I was very reluctant to find somewhere to eat so I accepted her offer. Could it get any worse?? I was awoken at 1.00am by someone hanging around outside my bedroom door. I phoned reception who came and I heard them ask this man to move and get out!!.After trying to get back to sleep I was then woken by the banging of the boiler again at 5.00am - at this point I decided to get up. I was going to have their continental breakfast but it didn't start til 7.30am so I asked for the bill and went to work early. I would not recommend this hotel.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: .As we (me and my adult son) were really only looking for an overnight stay after a visit to Wembley Stadium for an England football match and given that a twin room with breakfast was less than £70 GBP, I didn`t expect too much. However, the Langorf was spotlessly clean, comfortably furnished and service was genuinely helpful and efficient (e.g. when enquiring how to use the safe, a member of staff came up to the room and demonstrated...immediately).The room was small but adequate, as was the bathrom, but what impressed was not only the cleanliness but for an old tradtional buiding (the hotel is made up of converted large formerly residential townhouses) but the high standard of decor. Quality workmanship and well maintained (recently renovated?), it had nice ambience, slightly old school and a nice non-chain alternative. Continental breakfast was fine, fresh and reasonable choice

title: Ideal for Wembley events
text: Discovered this hotel while looking to book a short stay while attending a concert at a Wembley, while avoiding the grossly over-priced hotels within the Stadium complex. The Langford turned out to be ideal. Situated on a quiet residential street on the edge of Hampstead/Swiss Cottage, yet only a 2 minute walk from the bustling thoroughfare of Finchley Road. Very close to the Finchley Road Tube Station which is only one stop from Wembley and a 15 min journey from Central London. Comfortable room, well stocked continental breakfast and friendly, helpful staff. Good value at £115 for a double room incl breakfast (late June).

title: Good service, large studio with baby bed, good location
text: I travelled here with a friend and a baby. We were upgraded to a studio room. Although the decor was from time past, it did the job. The room was large and everything was ready for our 1 year old. The location is PERFECT as the tube is nearby and it was easy access with the Greenline bus from Luton airport (easyjet flight). We enjoyed the short walk to the main area of Hampstead and the assortment of great restaurants lining the street. Breakfast was everything we needed and the service was great. Wireless internet access was available (2 pounds per hour) and they also have a computer in the main hall. All in all - a good choice. We got a 50% discount with a deal with Booking.com... so can't talk about the price.

title: Always my first choice
text: Many times I have happily returned to the Langorf. The staff is exceptional...it is centrally located...it is charming and attractive...the atmosphere is welcoming, warm...it is quiet and one feels at home there.

title: Awful
text: I travel to London frequently with business and I stayed via late rooms in June 2017. The Hotel was advertised as 20% off, it was £93 and I often make a decision to stay somewhere of around £100 mark this could usually be a good 3 star and sometimes 4 star and I expect cleanliness,quality and a comfortable bed. This hotel is neither of those things, it is closer to a hostel than a hotel. The sheets were stained, the headboard was stained, the carpet was stained, there was water ingress coming down the wall, generally the bad reviews on here give an accurate description. The mattress was especially uncomfortable and generally the place was filthy. It is the only place so far that I have felt compelled to take photographs as it was that bad. I was very tired on my arrival and like many others just got on with it as it was too late to get anywhere else and as I had a meeting the following morning I just got on with it, I slept (not very well) above the mattress in my clothes and looked forward to a long and clean bath when I returned home. Needless to say I wont be staying at this one again- eeeww!

title: decent value -- a worthwhile hotel
text: If you are looking for luxury, the Langorf is not for you! If, on the other hand, you want realistic pricing and honest value, the Langorf is your sort of place. The staff are conscientious and helpful. The rooms are comfortable -- but not all that big. The breakfast buffet is quite acceptable. The location is ten minutes (walking) from the Underground. So -- all in all -- this is a good place to stay. We have stayed there for several years -- and would hope to continue doing so.

title: Great stay.
text: Room was amazing, spotlessly clean and enormous.Staff were helpful. Buffet breakfast was great. The only negative thing I can say is the room we had was obviously once a smoking room and on arrival still smelt of smoke, but after a bit of an airing the smell went.

title: Friendly quiet hotel in good location... But REALLY needs refurb
text: Friendly staff on arrival and location and price are great. But the attic room I was in clearly used to be a smoking room as the room really reeked of old stale smoke. Decor is shabby and the bathroom has rusty spots. However they'd clearly cleaned it so can't fault the service! If they refurbished the rooms, this would be a fantastic hotel!! That said I'd probably stay here again if it was possible to request a room that had never been a smoking room.

title: Anywhere else this would be a budget hotel....but this is London
text: In the context of London's vastly over-priced hotel accommodation, where value for money is a rare experience, this place is just about okay. The bedroom was very small (and too hot), but clean enough and adequate for an overnight stay. Yes, it's decor is dated, and the mattress has seen better days, but it's acceptable. Breakfast was good - a generous array of meats, cheeses, fruit etc. - and the staff team members were all very pleasant. The hotel is a five minute walk from Finchley Road Underground station.

title: Good location and pleasant staff
text: I stayed for four nights over the Easter weekend and would certainly consider coming here again. The double room was not over large but far from claustrophobic - likewise the bathroom. Breakfast was Continental (when is it ever anything else these days?) and served in the dining room by friendly staff. I would have preferred to pay somewhat less, but have to admit that, this being London, I did get value for money.

title: Reasonable price if you need to stay in the area, but basic and some hygiene issues.
text: Stayed overnight in a double room on the top floor. The room was adequately furnished, bathroom (with shower) was reasonably clean but in the morning the 'hot water' was only just a bit warm, unable to take a full shower. The bed was a double, not too comfortable, but the bare mattress was covered by a sheet, (no mattress cover) and the top of the mattress quite obviously stained in various places. The management need to ensure that the mattresses are cleaned properly and they should be using mattress covers as well as the sheet. A noisy couple in the next door room kept me awake for some time late at night

title: Good hotel
text: We enjoyed our stay at the Langorf - it was well located and a good price. The breakfast, considering it was a 'continental' buffet was also very good and the staff were friendly. The room was fairly small, but it was quiet and comfortable. Our main complaint would be were that we were denied breakfast after 9.30 on a Bank Holiday Monday, despite it being advertised until 10.00 on weekends and holidays. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Good Points, Bad Points - Overall Very Average but Good Value for Money.
text: A lovely welcome awaited us when we arrived very late and completely exhausted. Our room was large, comfortable and well appointed. It was also clean. Bizarrely, though, there was a notice asking us to close the windows whenever we left the room to prevent squirrels from entering and scavenging for scraps of food!! Prudent? Yes, until I noticed that all the windows were fully wide open when we arrived and the central heating was on - very bizarre. A good night's sleep was followed by an average continental breakfast. With a little thought, and at no extra cost, our 'average' breakfast could have been so much better. Coffee served by the waitress from a machine - why not freshly made? Fruit salad from a tin - in 2017?! I was also less than impressed with having two waitresses in the 'kitchen' next to our table - with next to nothing to do - talking away in their native language at a volume which, although not upsetting, did nothing to enhance the enjoyment of a quiet breakfast The worst point, by far, was the complete lack of hot water. I couldn't have a shower - a basic provision for any hotel. I called reception who, although pleasant enough, had no answer. It was clear that there had been hot water earlier but it had run cold by the time I needed it. They clearly hadn't heated enough for every guest. That is not the sign of a well run hotel. I think my title - 'Good points, bad points - overall very average', sums our experience well. I think, also, that for the money we paid, the Langorf Hotel is fairly good value for money - even excellent value for money if hot water were included!

title: Good quiet location .Excellent value for money
text: Located up a quiet road close to Finchley Road tube station and not too far from Hamstead. The room was clean and comfortable ,reception friendly and a good "continental" breakfast included in the very reasonable price.

title: Better than expected
text: You never know with hotels in this type of area - so really surprised. It seems the rooms have recently (November 2014) been improved and they were large, clean, well decorated warm and comfortable. The reception area is typical small hotel and the staff most helpful. Breakfast was continental but the huge wide range variety so absolutely fine. Hotel was a bit of a walk from the tube but it meant we could have a quick look at the local restaurants for the evening - all in that area. So evening meal was soon sorted within 300 yards of hotel. Delightful place recommended by the person at reception called 'Oregano' Italian trattoria food of the highest standard but in an unprepossessing position. So - good value.

title: Excellent value for its location
text: Stayed here for one night, unfortunately couldn't get a single room as it was fully booked. Nevertheless, it was better than expected I must say. It was an easy and short walk from Finchley Road station, so dragging my luggage around wasn't a problem. But since it was winter, it was really dark around 4pm and it was hard to navigate the hotel as the street it was on didn't have bright street lights. Location was very convenient, with a large Sainsbury next to the station and other restaurants as well. Staff was kind and helpful, very pleased with the service. As for the room itself, it was really spacious and large for a hotel in central London, therefore I was really pleased. Bathroom was spacious and clean as well, however I had problems with the shower as it only seem to had extremely hot or cold water when I tried to operate it for the first 10 minutes. Other than that, it was a pleasant stay and no faults to be found.

title: Dont stay in the apartments
text: Booked to stay 2 nights in Sept after reading the reviews online. On checking in discovered that the resident parking permits as advertised on the website are no longer available, so then spent 15 minutes trying to find somewhere to park. On check in was told we had been upgraded to an apartment, this was not in the hotel but 300 yds up the road, we were shown into a shabby house with stained carpets and wall and paintwork chipped and marked up stairs to an apartment. It was horrible, cheap furniture, pillows like wafers, shabby and grubby. We asked to go into the main hotel but all rooms were taken. We were so unhappy we left in the morning even though we had booked for 2 nights. Nasty, nasty place.

title: Let Down by Poor Service
text: Wanting to stay in North London, in a good quality hotel, we were attracted by both the Tripadvisor reviews and the hotel's own website, appearing to depict a hotel that was striving to provide a professional and reliable service. Although initially reassured, on arrival, by the good location and pleasant reception, on entering our first room, we were confronted by an umade bed, a dirty ashtray and an uncleaned bathroom. Mistakes happen, so we were pleased to be promptly offered a new room, which was fine, even though for the price the worn curtains and battered side table were a bit dispiriting. We would have left the Langorf with a relatively positive impression, had it not been for the what lay in store when we went down to breakfast. Arriving at the breakfast room at five minutes to ten on Sunday, having been told breakfast was available until ten, we were abruptly and dismissively told we were too late and that the kitchen was closed as they needed to prepare for a conference. We were disappointed not to be able to get breakfast, as this was a consideration in deciding whether the hotel was a good deal. However, it was the way in which the hotel staff appeared totally unconcerned by our predicament, making it quite clear that preparation for a conference was far more important to them than treating their guests with civility, that really upset us. On explaining how we felt, the reply was that as the manager would not be in till Monday, there was nothing that could be done. We left the hotel very disappointed

title: Quiet place, nice facilities
text: Close to Finchley Road and the O2 Centre, the apartments have a decente size (we stayed in a triple apart) fully equiped with kitchen and houseware, good dinner table and sofás. There are some supermarkets and tube station close to the hotel.

title: nice staff, good breakfast, quiet spot , needs refurbishing
text: we usually book an airbnb or deal in Camden or hamstead but booking quite late found the langorf. It is in a quiet location which was very good and less than five minutes from the finchley overground and two from a bus to all areas of london. on arrival we found they had given us a double room not a twin which we were thankful to change because the room decor was so tired that it felt like we had arrived at a B+B for the council. The staff were all lovely throughout the stay and when the fault was made acted quickly and politely apologised in a way that exceeded the service you often get in a brand hotel or four star. The new room was in the attic and had a cute round window , with a sign to remind you to close it when going out to stop the squirrels getting in . The tv and wifi access were great, the beds firm , the bedding a little institutional but adequate , but unfortunately the same problem kept coming up for the Langorf , which is a lovely building and that is it needs a full refurb. The rooms and shower were obviously cleaned before arrival well (although the daily clean was badly done , they left a dirty teapot , half full of tea and just left binbags on the floor next to the bin ) they put ion the toiletries and little touches but the room had the smell of stale smoke that is not new but comes from the stale walls, the shower and bathroom had rusty areas , water stained old tiles and other causes which put you off using it ( luckily we were only there two days ) carpets and walls everywhere were all threadbare or scuffed and unfortunately at the time of our visit the ladies toilet near the dining room was out of order so a trip was needed all the way back up to the attic to go to the bathroom. The breakfast and service however were exceptional, a huge choice of continental foods , including quiche , carrot cake , eggs , meat fruit and waffles were available, toast and drinks were served quickly. The staff friendly and helpful , the location was good , so would I stay again? I don't know, its downside was only its building maintenance and decor , not so important on a two day business trip , but this would not be the place to stay if you wanted a treat away from home. Refurbish it and it could be a go to boutique hotel or top class B+B but for now its really its food and reception staff that stop this from getting a poor rating.

title: Tired
text: We booked this hotel as we were going to Wembley to a concert and we left it late to book anything closer at a reasonable price. The location was good, the breakfast was continental only and the breakfast staff glum. The parking is on the road and parking restrictions apply. Unfortunately the staff are all foreign and they simply didn't have a clue about the restrictions. I rang on three occasions and received three differing pieces of advice. Look on line if you are driving there. The interior decor was tired but as we were only staying for one night it was ok.

title: Good inexpensive hotel
text: By London prices this is a good inexpensive hotel in a pleasant, quiet location. Although the room was a litte shabby it was a good size and clean. Heating was efficient (and the weather was very cold). Continental breakfast was good and varied. The reception staff were friendly and helpful. Tube station (Finchley Road) was a less than 10 minutes walk away. Overall a very satisfactory stay.

title: 100yds from holiday inn - quieter, better, cheaper
text: quiet rooms and a great breakfast. well placed for freud museum/anna freud centre etc. use overground for quick access to hackney central and east londons markets- hackney broadway on saturday is great-keep walking via lock 7 bike cafe, hackney city farm ( monster pigs) and columbia rd flowers.

title: Lovely hotel at very good price
text: I really enjoyed my stay here! hotel was very clean and staff was very friendly. breakfast was nice. there were many services and shops within 400m of this hotel. From other reviews I read that tube station is very close however I have to say that the walk from hotel to tube station is not that close! I would definitely stay here again!

title: Great value for money
text: We stayed here one night in a triple room for going to a concert at Wembley arena. The room was spacious and clean. Staff were very friendly. Hotel was great location for Luton airport and getting to Wembley. Was very reasonably priced. Only bad point was it was a continental breakfast rather than a cooked one, that we'd been looking forward to after having a few drinks the night before.

title: Great location and not just that
text: How I miss this place! The hotel is located on a quiet, clean and beautiful street. My room was big and clean, I have nothing to complain about. I also enjoyed breakfast, which has different types of food every day and everything was fresh and delicious(I remember that tasty cookie whith oatmeal and nuts). The location is more than perfect, I had days when I went to the city center by foot. P.S. Next time when I will be visiting UK probably I will choose the same hotel.

title: What you see is what you get
text: This is an old fashioned hotel which I intend as a compliment. It has no airs or graces and staying there is like staying at your grandmother's house. However the staff were very friendly, it was clean, it has a lift, breakfast was perfectly fine and it was not expensive. It is very handy for the Jubilee Line and I saw a coach nearby going to Stansted Airport which could be handy. There are two cinemas nearby and plenty of places to eat in the O2 centre. If you like a reasonably priced, non-pretentious hotel at a reasonable cost then pay it a visit.

title: Couldn't Be Happier
text: Myself and my partner stayed at the Langorf hotel for one night whilst visiting London. The hotel is located in the lovely Hampstead district an was peaceful and quiet all night (I'm a light sleeper and slept like a baby!). The room was clean, spacious and comfortable with the added bonus of teas and coffees! Even a selection of toiletries in the bathroom. Our room was cool as it was a ground level room. Breakfast in the morning was £6 for continental, good selection of pastries, cheese and sliced meats. The train/underground links to the hotel are excellent and ran til around midnight. Staff were friendly. Would definitely choose to stay at the Langorf again when I visit London.

title: Good for families
text: My wife and I stayed with our 9 month old daughter for a week. As the hotel was busy we stayed in both a 1 bedroom apartment and a studio apartment as we couldn't book the full week in either. The staff were helpful and polite, the rooms were very clean and tidy. The 1 bed apt could have done with renovation as was looking a bit dated, but as said was clean, tidy and comfortable. The studio was much more modern, and having seen both rooms would book the studio over the 1 bed apt. Staying with a young child, it was a bonus to have a proper kitchen in both rooms, as it made eating a lot easier as well as dealing with the baby bottles, and both rooms had clothes washer/driers. Baby bed and high chair were provided. My only small complaint is that I was told there was a wireless LAN available, however this wasn't the case. There is internet access available, but you have to go to reception and plug in a LAN cable. Overall I would say that the Langorf is good value for money, good for families and is in a good location to for public transport. Would stay there again. By the way a black cab driver told me that the name of the hotel comes from the street it's in. Frognal spelt backwards!

title: Good service for a good price
text: I went here with my mother for a citytour London. The hotel is in a quiet neighbourhood and near the underground station Finchley road. It's about 20 minutes from St. Pancras and Picadilly Circus. The staff at the reception was very friendly and helpfull. Natalia was our favorite, she gave us good advise for nice spots and for using the public transports. We had a renovated room, which looked very nice and clean. The only bad thing was that the bathroomdoor opened to the inside. There was only a little space left to enter the bathroom. The breakfast was very good! A lot of choise, even carrot cake! We had a good time here.

title: Basic, charmless and in need of a refurb ...but good value and helpful staff
text: We stopped in one of the apartments here - fairly clean but certainly outdated and the whole decor is in need of a full upgrade - easy to get to from the north circular, handy for the tube and central London and if you park on the O2 centre using the hotel voucher it's great value (£60 per day for non users) - a couple of issues were resolved quickly be the staf and they were helpful with moving and storing luggage and very friendly - as long as you don't mind it being basic and are spending most of your time in central London then it's good value - as usual the local parking attendants from the good borough of Camden are very on the ball so don't risk it !

title: A place stay when visiting London
text: I wasn't sure what to expect from this hotel. The last hotel that I stayed in London was terrible. So, my only expectation from this was that it wouldn't be any worse. But I was pleasently surprised. The hotel is located near the underground station Finchley Road where theere is just about 10 minute ride to the city centre. The hotel is about 5 minute walk from the underground station. The staff in the was was friendly and helpful. We were able to check in about one hour early. The room was clean, big enough for two. The bed were comfortable with good pillows :) The safe in room didn't have instructions in i, so we couldn't use it. The room was cleaned daily and the bed lines were changed once during our three day stay in the hotel. The breakfast was average. Nothing special but a good enough to start your day. The only downside was that you could only get continental breakfast wich doesn't include bacon for example. But I was able to live without it :)

title: A Nasty surprise
text: We stayed at the hotel mid January for a weekend break in London. The Hotel looked pretty on the internet but the real life experience did not live up to the expectation. We checked in on the Friday evening and the staff were friendly enough. The room seemed smaller the bathroom was cramped and when i tried to take a shower the water ran hot almost boiling with no adjustment to the temperature. I reported the problem to reception and asked if we could change rooms. They said they were aware of the problem and if i let it run for 5 to 10 mins it would be OK but that did not work. They also said this was not possible to change rooms but i was welcome to shower in another room. I would describe myself as a liberal person but this suggestion if carried out would put me outside my comfort zone. They suggested getting the handyman in but that came to nothing and we were left with a room without a shower all weekend. Breakfast was a very cramped affair and it would seem that the room was not big enough for all the guests. overall i would describe the stay as disappointing.

title: good location- near to stations, bus stops & eating places was the saving grace
text: Helpful reception but inefficient house keeping- never changed toiletries even though we stayed about a week. Small non descript rooms, very small bathrooms. Hardly any space around tbe building to walk around. Same old breakfast everyday morning, served by mostly non smiling professionals

title: Positively surprised
text: We visited London as a family of three and booked a 3-bed hotel room. From the moment we entered we felt the cosy atmosphere, and this was just topped by a recently renovated room which had everything we needed as "our base" during the two nights that we stayed. I especially loved that the room had windows which can be opened instead of being at the mercy of an airconditioner. The staff was friendly and very service minded and we also loved the atmosphere and quality of the breakfast. Surprisingly, the WiFi connection was in fact shockingly good - even more expensive hotels have let me down on this before - which was so nice making planning for the next day very smooth. As others have mentioned, the price is affordable and with two train stations nearby you have good connections to all important places in London. We would definitely choose the hotel again.

title: Not bad.. but wouldn't recommend
text: Lets start with the positives, the staff are very friendly and the breakfast is decent. Also the price for one night for London is quite competitive. The room I stayed in had a comfortable bed and the heating worked very well, it was also quite clean. As for the negatives, the hotel is very tired looking. My shower only had boiling water in the morning and to be fair I was told that I should keep the water running for a while and then I might not get third degree burns but.. who has the time to wait?. In general its an 'okay' hotel but I wouldnt recommend it and I would probably go and stay back at the Rockwell hotel in which I have previously stayed, which is more pricey but worth the extra cost.

title: Excellent Value
text: Stayed here for the cricket at Lords. Yes the hotel could do with some refurbishment but we had a quiet room overlooking the back and in this current heat wave the window was wide open and cooled the room. Quite a small room but had everything we needed. Brilliant breakfast, lots of choice. The hotel booked a taxi, was there when we wanted. Overall excellent value hotel. I would stay again.

title: Extremely noisy and hot with complimentary drugs!
text: Stayed here with son and daughter in law and my two grandchildren for a triple birthday treat which we had saved for and eagly anticipated as a sightseeing break in the capital. Arriving at 8pm on a wet and windy evening to a soulless reception with a receptionist who lacked any charisma or welcome. On inquiring after a night cap we were told there was a shop about a 10 minute walk away which due to the adverse weather we passed on this idea and went to our allocated rooms which were breathtakingly hot and although you could and I had to open the window wide we couldn't leave it open for security reasons as we were in the basement. We had a bath and retired for the night knowing our exacting iteinary the following day. Unfortunately that was completely impossible with the creaking floorboards above and a really loud lift operating just across the corridor from my room and a more worrying sinister noise that sounded like someone was trying the door handle. After some investigating I found the culprit to be it caused by a gush of air pushing through the ill fitting door frame every time someone opened the corridor Fire door to get to their rooms! Terror over with, the creaking continued as so the lift noise which sounded like a noisy old boiler starting up as it was that ancient and dilapidated. I had no option other than run the ventilation fan in the bathroom

title: Dissapointed
text: No hot water - we were told due to the boiler being old and not able to cope with all the guests consumption. We were made aware that we were not the only guests with this problem. Black mould in the shower, although we could not use the shower due to lack of hot water. Breakfast was continental not cooked, and not a large variety on offer. Other members of our party suffered from a blocked toilet in their room, and there was confusion over payments where people were paying for more rooms than they occupied. When we asked to speak to the manager we were told he was not on site but would phone us - we have not been contacted yet.

title: Good place to stay in London at a reasonable price
text: The Langorf has a lovely. old-world atmosphere, just off the Finchley Road. This makes it an excellent location for getting around London, being just 5 minutes away from the underground station (Metropolitan and Jubilee lines). The rooms are well appointed (at least the 2 I have had on two separate visits), and the bathroom has all the required amenities, including a rainforest shower head. I did have a problem with the temperature of the water (sometimes getting only hot water in the sink and tepid water in the shower). Free Wi-Fi and breakfast are included in the price. The breakfast is a tasty buffet with cheeses, salamis, quiches, fruit salad and a lovely carrot cake. Cereal, flapjacks, waffles, croissants, etc., are also offered. The coffee is great, and if you request it when you order, soy milk is available.

title: Didn't Leave Hungry
text: The beds were a little hard, but the breakfasts made up for it. Pastries, Meats, Quiche, carrot cake, hard-boiled eggs - absolutely wonderful. They even let us leave our baggage there while we finished sight-seeing and waited for the Eurostar. It's about 2 blocks from the subway station and a block away from Starbucks and a restaurant mall.

title: Recommended
text: Lovely small hotel in quiet residential area. Ten mins walk to tube and plenty of buses to take you anywhere you want. The decor may be tired but it is a very clean, comfortable and welcoming place to stay. Our room in the basement was warm and the bathroom new fittings and plenty of hot water. All of the staff, especially on reception, where friendly and helpful at all times, nothing was a problem. The included buffet style breakfast was plentiful and and fresh. I could not find fault with anything for the price paid and would recommend The Langorf to all my friends. Well done everyone,

title: Fair accomodations, good service
text: The location is good, a few minutes away for a subway station. I arrived very early on the check-in day and the person at the front desk was able to arrange the room for me within less than an hour. On the next day I was surprised by the decent quality of the breakfast. On my check-out they were also very understanding and let me get rid of many coins I wouldn't need anymore as I was leaving the country.

title: Very Friendly
text: We arrived at this charming hotel at around ten o'clock, and the man who served us at the check in was quite charming. We arrived to our room in a nice lift and when we arrived to are rooms we saw that the descriptions on the website were accurate. There was a lovely bathroom with a nice shower and bath. The beds were very comfortable, and I fell asleep straight away. In the morning we were the first people down and there was a nice buffet. In addition, a waiter/waitress serves you hot drinks. I strongly recommend!!

title: Hotel Staff
text: Many thanks to lovely and always smiled Natalia on the reception. She is very willing and she gave us all informations that we needed. Room was always clean, and breakfast very tasty, especially orange fresh :). The only thing i missed - little bit of vegetables (tomatoes or sth). But really big like for this hotel, we love this place so much! Michal & Kristina (Bratislava, SLOVAKIA).

title: 5 days in London
text: Excellent hotel, near the underground station, very kind staff. Room clean and spacious. Breakfast very satisfactory. I suggest

title: Sustained Standard
text: A return visit to this Hotel, friendly staff (except one) and good clean accommodation in a convenient position a short walk from either Hampstead or Finchley Road tube Stations. The only fault was from a member of staff serving in the breakfast room on the Sunday, I entered the breakfast room at 9.45 (service until 10 am) and asked if they had any more cold meats of a particular variety to which I was abruptly told no we have nothing left - which I find hard to believe of a Hotel, fortunately the other member of staff was friendlier when it came to ordering a hot drink. However the former member of staff on the dot of 10 am started to clear all food from the buffet tables, not really good with customer relations, not even a question would you like anything else before I clear away . I would have given a better rating if that particular member of staff was considerate of the customers which she was not - I think she would be better placed using a vacuum than 'serving' breakfast. The night porter was more helpful with providng addition tea bags, ice and chilled water - he should be promoted !!

title: A very agreeable place to stay
text: A very pleasant hotel with a great location. We stayed in one of the newly refurbished rooms which was spotlessly clean and very comfortable. We had a small issue which the owner of the hotel resolved for us with expedience and a true sense of customer care. We would stay in this hotel again and would recommend it.

title: Terrible experience!
text: I have not received any contact from Langorf hotel regarding the fact the you where overbooked the nigh 04/10/14 It was only when we arrived close to 10 pm I was informed about the need to be transferred to another hotel When we where transferred via taxi the taxi driver asked to be payed directly by us as he was not properly instructed that this would be payed by the Langorf hotel. Therefore we had to return to the hotel for a second time for reception to pay the taxi

title: Just what I needed!
text: Hotel Langorf is the place to stay if you're visiting Anna Freud Center or the Tavistock Cilinic. Rooms are nice and roomy, breakfast is good and service is great.

title: A VERY PLEASANT STAY IN LONDON
text: Very nice hotel in beautiful Hampstead, quiet area (you can just sleep so well!) with nearby subway station. Its style is typically British. The room and bathroom were clean nd comfortable. Rich and tasty breakfast. The staff (in particular Renato, Maria and Natalia) is very kind and ready to give you all tips to make your stay in this wonderful city an unforgettable experience !

title: Fairly good value for a london hotel.
text: Stayed at the Langorf for 3 nights whilst visiting family. In a quiet location on a leafy residential street. Nearest tube in Finchley rd, 5 mins walk, or Hampstead 10 mins walk. Reception area and dining room are clean and neatly decorated. Bedroom had seen better days, was a bit too pink and in need of a revamp, but having said that it was clean (apart from the net curtains, which were a bit grey) , warm and comfortable. Bathroom was fine with a great power shower and plenty of hot water. Breakfast, although continental was plentiful, help yourself to cereals, yogurt, fresh fruit salad, juices, bread rolls and pastries, eggs, and a selection of cold meats and cheese. Can't comment on parking as we travelled by train, but I imagine it could be a bit tricky. We thought that for London, it was good value and would stay there again.

title: spot on
text: We stayed at Langorf Hotel 2 nights in May good location, very quiet, really clean, very pleasant staff, excellent breakfast . Close to tube and overland stations . Don't miss Camden market only a short ride on overland train .Will be using Langorf Hotel again on our next visit to London. Thank you for very pleasant break

title: Good price so close to London
text: This was the last night on our UK trip. The staff was very friendly. We arrived about 11 and the night desk man was so helpful and friendly. I did not notice any problem with the girls in the breakfast room. They were very nice to us. The rooms were updated. We had no hot water at midnight which the nice desk man came up to check and could only apologize. Hot water was back by morning though. There is no parking out on the street. Good luck finding a space if you're driving. Only a reasonably short walk to the underground in one direction (Finchley Rd) and a little shorter to the overground (Finchley Rd and Frognal) in the other.

title: Reasonable value, friendly staff
text: We usually choose to stay in the Hampstead and Belsize Park areas when we are in London - we prefer to be in a quieter locale, and love strolling around the leafy streets and trying out the cafes and restaurants. Not to mention the bonus of having Hampstead Heath to ramble through, which on a summer evening is absolutely magical. The hotel we usually choose had no vacancies so we booked in at the Langorf. It's a bit further away from Hampstead than we'd ideally choose but still easy walking distance - about 15 minutes. The hotel's decor, as others have mentioned, is a bit tired. The bathrooms have been revamped but the surround of our bath had peeling paint. The room next to ours had an ugly water stain on the carpet at its entrance. The sheets and towels have clearly been washed a few thousand times but they are reasonable quality, and in fairness, this is an affordable London hotel so you don't expect top quality. We were a bit dismayed to find a little brass 'no smoking sign under the table, covered in dust and clearly it had been there some time, so nobody has hoovered under there for a while! We left it there to see if the cleaner would find it the next day - they didn't. Breakfast is good. Not Full English, but that doesn't bother us. For a continental breakfast, in England, it's excellent. My experience of 'continental breakfast' in the UK is generally very poor. At least at the Langdorf there is a selection of cheeses and meats, a quiche, hard boiled eggs, croissants and rolls with jams etc, pastries and muffins,as well as cereal, fruit and yoghurt. Coffee is great! From an espresso machine and good flavour. The staff here are very nice. There is free wi-fi which is a bit slow, but not too bad. As other reviewers have mentioned, the floorboards are squeaky and if you have inconsiderate people staying above you, there can be a lot of banging and squeaking. Fortunately this kind of noise did not continue very long. The hotel itself is in an extremely quiet location - no traffic sounds at all. There is no air conditioning which would bother me if it had been any warmer. My partner was very annoyed on our first morning when there was no hot water to be had (I'd showered the night before and it was fine). I phoned down to reception and we were told to keep the shower running for 5 minutes, and hopefully the boiler would catch up! To Australians who are very conscious of conserving water, this was a horrifying thought. We did leave it running, as instructed, but it had no effect. There was no hot water still when we returned to our room nearly an hour later, after breakfast. The person on the desk explained that the boiler sometimes does not cope in the mornings, when the hotel is fully booked. That's just not good enough. You expect two basic things in a hotel - a decent bed, and hot water. If you can't provide the hot water you need to invest in a new boiler. Interestingly, we had no problems on our second morning. There are no ironing board or iron in the room - you must borrow one from reception, and the hotel has no guest laundry facilities. Overall, the Langorf is reasonable value for London and we would certainly consider staying again. The quiet location, the good breakfast and the friendliness of the staff are three very strong factors.

title: Great location mainly
text: The room was small, as expected but clean. Bathroom a little bit old but still acceptable. Breakfast was included and food was ok: savoury and sweet things. Good point is free Wi-Fi. Hotel is average but I would return to this area because it is handy for subway. 5 mn walk, and then 2 or 3 stations away from a stop with many connections. Also, if you keep walking up the street (15-20 minutes) you'll reach the limit of Camden and Hampstead area: there is a nice "village" with Paul patisserie and other original cafes, Still a Tesco express is also available. On the opposite end, when walking towards the station "Finchley road", you have shopping mall and shops on main street with handy Subway for past midnight meal, and a good Korean restaurant. Also, this Finchley road has stops for National Express and Terravision bus shuttle to/from Luton. So overall, excellent location and hotel was acceptable for a long week-end.

title: Friendly staff but old hotel
text: The Hotel is located far from the main streets but has a tube station very close by. The staff is very helpful and guide you well. The breakfast was decent. The rooms are old and need lot of improvement. The kettle in the room was dirty and so was our blanket. The housekeeping really needs improvement. You can get much better Hotels in Main London with the same cost.

title: Very good choice in London
text: Last December my family and I spent a weekend in London. Langorf Hotel has been an excellent choice for a value for money accommodation in London. Very nice hotel in a great location, five minutes walking from Finchley Road underground station. Rooms clean and spacious, staff people have been helpful and kind. We enjoyed our stay at Langorf and we will definitely choose it again.

title: Can't say enough good things about the Langorf Hotel to fit in one sentence.
text: My son was also stranded in London with 27 other students and their 4 chaperones due to the Islandic volcano eruption. The hotel went out of their way to make the group comfortable during their extended stay. The hotel's central location allowed them to get out and see the sights and never be far from "home". The staff was incredibly gracious to our group of teenagers. What more could a mom ask for?

title: Great location.
text: I have been staying in this hotel for the past 18 years and continue to return every year. It is an easy walk to the tube station and conveniently located for evening visits to the pubs in Hampstead. The breakfast is very good.

title: Promised much but ...
text: A conveniently situated hotel near to the tube station that looks impressive from the outside. Sadly the rooms do not reflect the facade. The included breakfast was a key reason for booking for us. However we were not prepared for the speed with which the available food was taken away by staff as the clock hands moved nearer to ten o'clock. We will not be staying here again.

title: 3 days london
text: Good location, near the Underground station, Breakfast was ok.Room,Bathroom and bed ok I will return.

title: Great Stay
text: Great Stay! We reserved on-line and were happy to see that our reservation had been received by the hotel. Location is great (no more than 5 minutes to the tube) and out of the more expensive core of London. Friendly staff, delicious breakfast, clean rooms and bathrooms. Internet access for 1pound (=20 minutes). 24HR front desk, and 24HR Pizza parlour down the street for those suffering from jet lag. :) Our room could have been considered slightly small if travelling with a lot of luggage, but friend's room was spacious. Stayed 3 nights, and would definetely go back. (our only concern was the security - you must leave your room key at the front desk. (unusual for NA hotels). No problems though - had a great experience, although I would not leave valuables in the room).

title: Handy, helpful, immaculate and reasonable.
text: I stayed here with my son, after reading the reviews on Tripadvisor. I always dread trying to find reasonable accomodation in London as it is either overpriced or dingy and shoddy. As the other reviews said it is very handy for the Underground and you can have your choice of 2 stations. We were very lucky and had a room at the top(there is a lift!) which backed onto the garden

title: Good place to stay
text: i often stay at the Langorf because i find it comfortable, personable and excellent value. It doesn't suffer the impersonality of a large hotel and the staff are very helpful and welcoming. Once i left some money and all my credit cards locked in the room safe when i left and the staff was most accommodating in sorting retrieval. Another time, I booked the wrong day but when I turned up, they changed the booking with the booking agent rather than stand on the formalities. I also like the continental breakfast with its fresh orange juice and great coffee. All in all, a good place to stay.

title: All round good hotel
text: Stayed here with family for one night after a music gig at wembley. The tube stop is only four stops from wembley and has very good conections to other areas in London. The hotel is just off the main road so it is in a quiet area and parking is very close by. However having said that the only thing i would say (Not a complaint) Having been at an AC/DC gig my hearing was not great after but i still managed to hear a baby crying from a room further down the corridor (I was not the only one to hear it)... But this was not a problem for any of us as we all slept like babies our selves as the rooms were spacious and beds very comfortable. The brekfast in the morning was welcoming and very tastey and was just what we needed after a night at a gig. I would recomend staying here.

title: Again a very pleasant experience to stay at this lovely,historic hotel.
text: The Langorf hotel is located in the heart of Hampstead

title: Nice place to stay
text: If you plan a week end in Hampstead, this is the place to stay !

title: Great hotel in a lovely area of London
text: We stayed at the Langorf Hotel at the end of our visit to London and found the rooms clean and the staff on reception very helpful. Breakfasts were good but could have included fresh fruit. Hampstead Heath is a lovely residential area of London so it was a nice area to stay at the end of our holiday. There are 2 stations a short walk from the Hotel (Hampstead & Finchley) so it meant that we were able to access the sights of London very easily, although being further out did mean we often had to change trains to get to our destination. If this is a problem then consider accomodation in an area such as Paddington (we stayed there on arrival in London). Shopping is not great but as we headed into the centre of London each day it was not a problem for us.

title: Lovely room and bathroom
text: My husband booked me a weekend here for a present . It's near tube and restaurants. Room big plenty of wardrobe space. Good bathroom clean and lovely towels. Breakfast continental cake cheese and such. Friendly staff. Good value for London and great for us to visit Camden .

title: Homey and friendly
text: The staff made this place for me. There wasn't a great breakfast selection (for a vegetarian anyway!) and I suspect the cups in my room might not have been washed, but I felt welcomed and the building itself is very pretty. It's a mix of modern and aged

title: Langorf Hotel Frognal Hamstead
text: On Saturday 23rd of May I went to London to see Paul McCartney at the O2 Arena. I stayed at the langorf hotel in frognal, hamstead, which I booked through hotels.com, and got sixty three pounds off the price for one night. The hotel is a great place to stay, i was very impressed, the room was clean and tidy, spacious and had everything you would need, Upon my arrival, I was checked in very quickly and recieved polite and helpful service, The contential breakfast was suberb the next morning, I would highly reccomend this hotel to visitors to London, and hope to return there again. The area round there is very quiet, and in a good area with plenty of shops, it is convienient for the underground and overground with stations located on finchley rd.

title: who took the photos for the web site?
text: I have just stayed at this hotel...langorf, we had an appartment...which was described as two bedroom...top floor 5 flights of stairs, no lift , one of the rooms was 'a shoe box' with a tiny single bed in the eaves you could not sit up in it..the tiny kitchen was absolutely filthy....the sink did not work in the bathroom and the grime around the walls, shower and sink was a disgrace, it was the same for the all the rooms. there was nothing good for this the fee was £170 per night. the web site is very clever!!!! I have never in all my life stayed some where so bad...needless to say we checked out early curtailing our stay in london. not recommended.

title: Official photographs are misleading
text: I booked two separate rooms for two couples over two nights during September 2013. On arrival both rooms were in very poor decorative state and did not resemble in any way the official bedroom photographs. Both rooms had sad tired carpets, very cheap mattresses on the beds and wallpaper peeling. In addition the lift floor and lift door were extremely dirty and had obviously had not been cleaned recently. I immediately complained and the reception desk was very helpful arranging a better room right away and the promise of being moved to "the best room in the hotel tomorrow night". Reception were true to their word. Unfortunately when the occupants of the other room similarly complained they were told that as someone had already complained about a room (me) and as they only had one spare room no other exchanges of rooms were possible!!! One other comment, the breakfast time was until 10 am. On the second day we were discussing our plans for the day with the other couple, breakfast was finished and we were simply sitting at our table talking. A member of staff came over and told us that it was exactly 10 o'clock and we had to leave the breakfast room straight away as her staff wanted to leave. Technically the staff were correct but the matter was not handled politely, surely a simple request to move over to the reception area as breakfast time was over would have been much more tactful!

title: Nice hotel
text: A nice hotel in a quite but central location not far from the next tube and bus station Finchley Road Station. Our apartment was located in another building and could need some renovation, but was clean and big enough to stay there with three persons for three nights. It even had a little kitchen so that it would have been possible to cook. Heating was fine (and needed as it was quite cold outside). The staff was very friendly welcoming us as well as during our stay and while checking out. Breakfast was the only negative aspect as on Saturday and Sunday morning there were not enough places for all guests so that we had to wait for a free table and were not able to sit together with three persons at one table. The staff explained to us that they were fully booked so perhaps this was only an exception. The breakfast itself was nice and everybody should find something he likes, I personally missed the hot chocolate. In total a really nice hotel which I absolutely would recommend to my friends.

title: A hotel in need of a makeover.
text: Location is the best thing about the hotel. It is 5-6 minutes from the tube and has a good supermarket and local shops close by. The breakfast selection is limited and i advise you to get to the breakfast room early as when some food stuffs run out, such as eggs, the kitchen staff would not cook any others. In fact, the kitchen staff were particularly unhelpful and spoiled what would have been a good visit. The hotel had no ice, as the ice machine was supposedly broken, and when we asked for an ice bucket we were given a china bowl! Not the best or elegant thing to put your wife's birthday champagne in! The decor and condition of the room we stayed in was somewhat dated and tired, in need of a little refurbishment and modernising. The front desk staff were friendly and helpful. Despite the criticisms the price of the room was very reasonable and its location was handy for travelling in and around London.

title: A pleasant stay - very friendly staff
text: Having stayed at the Langorf hotel for three nights and for the first time, the first thing to say is that every member of staff has been very friendly and always welcomed me with a smile. Especially in London, unfortunately, this is a rarety. The hotel is conveniently situated in a residential neighbourhood in North London, near the Finchley Road tube station. My room was fairly clean and made me feel comfortable (which is not easy!). The bathroom must have been fairly new and offered a great shower (again, this is rare in London). The continental breakfast was certainly enough for my needs. I will be back :-)

title: Budget hotel, average.. but does its job
text: The hotel is average, the interiors are run-down - but then for its price, its quite a deal. It is well located - so thats a good thing, and it includes a hearty breakfast which helps kick-starting your day! I was in London on business, and this hotel did it's job well!

title: A very pleasent stay.
text: A small clean and quite hotel in a good area. we will come again. Nili and Dorith from Israel

title: Enjoyable stay!!
text: We all enjoyed our stay at the Langorf. All the staff were pleasant and friendly. The rooms are a little dated but were clean and comfortable and we all enjoyed a good nights sleep. My son and his girlfriend stayed in the fabled room 101 and had no problems at all, so don't be put off by earlier posts on here. If anyone booking the Langorf is expecting 5 star service then book a 5 star hotel and pay there prices. The location is in a quiet area and having stayed in another hotel on Finchley road you will be grateful of the peace and quiet. Buy an Oyster card and use the local bus service they are regular as clockwork and you are in the centre of Oxford Street within 20 minutes. The breakfast was plentiful but the bar and dining area could do with being a little bigger. A little TLC and this hotel would be a regular for me when visiting London but would stay again no problem at all.

title: Very disappointing!
text: We have just returned from a 2 night stay at The Langorf Hotel and have vowed never to return again! The hotel is very tired and requires a serious refurbishment. Our double bed had been made up with a single bed sheet which obviously didn't fit. We were too tired to complain and put up with it. The next morning I did complain and it was changed. The person making up the bed must have known they had used the wrong sheet but obviously didn't care. The room was small, with a tiny bathroom. We found the shower impossible to regulate, it was either scalding hot or freezing. The door to our room didn't fit properly and light came in around it. The net curtain was filthy. Breakfast was served in the dining room - the curtains are so dirty they are disgraceful. The hotel had numerous overseas visitors and I felt ashamed that their introduction to London was this hotel. I strongly recommend people to look at other hotels before booking this one.

title: Good location but needs modernisation
text: The whole hotel looks very tired and could do with redecoration. The beds were comfy enough but the pillows are the worst I have ever slept on. So thin which makes you wonder how old they are!! The room was clean, the staff were friendly enough and the breakfast was ok. Some fresh fruit would be nice though. The location of the hotel is convenient for the tube and Hampstead is not far away. The hotel is over priced for what you get but london is always over priced. It could be a beautiful hotel if they put the effort in and modernised it.

title: A home away from home in London
text: We stayed at the Langorf in July of 2013 in one of the apartments. The first night we were placed in one of the lower level apts., couldn't see anything through the window except bushes and the place smelled of stale cigarettes and dampness. However a call to the front desk took care of everything. They were booked solid that night but the next day moved us to a nice, clean 2nd floor apartment that we thoroughly enjoyed for the remaining 3 nights of our stay. They even moved our luggage for us while we were out sightseeing. It was nice to have a little kitchenette with stove and refrigerator. Just a few minutes away from the underground and overground, grocery stores, etc. After the first night we really enjoyed our stay and the Langorf. The owner/managers were eager to please and went out of their way to accommodate us. The studio apt was nice and clean, one street removed from the busier Finchley Rd. meant peace and quiet too.

title: Very disappointing
text: Stayed in room 101 - very small, hardly larger than the 4ft doube bed. The window lacked a handle and could not be properly closed. The bathroom is very cramped. The breakfast was very poor. Reception staff were uninterested and unhelpful. Very disappointing.

title: Incredibly convenient for Olympia, decent room too
text: I was going to London Olympia and this hotel could not be more convenient. I was travelling alone, but had got a large family room, which was very nice, so I probably got lucky. Breakfast was very reasonably priced at £7.50, but my only complaint is that it could have been served hotter. Staff were all friendly and helpful. Would certainly stay again, next time I am at an Olympia show.

title: Charged for no reason
text: My girlfriend booked a room for a stay here, she had booked before so her details were on file. She got a response saying that the booking did not go through due to false card details and since that room was no longer available decided not to pursue it anymore after. She was then notified that she was still charged using card details from before and it was her fault by extremely rude and defensive staff who wouldn't even listen and interrupted continuously!

title: Great value
text: Stayed for 2 nights while at Olympia. Received a friendly welcome, good explanation of charges and necessary information. Room is small but perfect for what I needed and more importantly, to me, very clean. found the WiFi to be consistently strong and fast. Breakfast is at taken in a room in the basement. Good selection of food and really good coffee.

title: Small, pokey, no customer service
text: Stayed there on business trip. Disgustingly small bedroom, zero customer service and just plain horrible. Fire alarm went off middle of the night, which was luckily a false alarm, but everyone trundled outside and waited to hear what was wrong. Management tried to sort out alarm panel, but did not know how to operate it.

title: It was a decent stay, it is well priced, but I would rather spend a bit extra for a lot more.
text: The positives: - Staff was accommodating when we requested changes. - Location was great, lots of nearby amenities like a pharmacy, supermarket, etc. - Westfield shopping centre is a pleasant walk away, or 2 minutes by train The negatives: - The lift was broken for half of my stay and I was on the 3rd floor (I have a bad knee), and the reception kept saying they don't know when it's going to be fixed. I felt dismissed when I repeatedly asked about the lift. - The rooms are quite small. - Neighbours are very loud, playing music most nights and late into the night. It's worth the stay if you're only here for a night or two and have earplugs, but wouldn't really recommend otherwise.

title: Still needs work in some areas
text: I stayed at the hotel, since i was heading to a convention across the road. The hotel is pleasant and staff especially reception are polite and always there to help. I stayed in room 104 which is on the first floor and was surprised since found i had a double bedded room and front view. Was shocked to find that when i tried to take a shower that the water was coming through a section of the ceiling, so reported to the dont desk (reception) who popped up and after seeing the issue said they would get it sorted tomorrow, which they did (well done). So next morning i went down to the basement and after confirming my room number and telling them it was for only one, I reviewed the breakfast section, not bad, but my only concern is that most of the cooked products, bacon/beans/eggs were luke warm at best. I had previously enquired about gluten free products and was told they had them as in bread, so after i enquired about this, the staff, who do not speak a lot of English, which isn’t their fault, they got the reception staff to visit and solve the issue, so got my gluten free bread for my toast. Overall the hotel isn’t bad, but will say that depending upon which website you visit and date requested the prices vary and that also includes the free or not free breakfasts, so check around sites if your want the breakfasts includes, otherwise its £7.50 per day at time of writing this.

title: A Great Stay Away
text: I enjoyed my time at the MStay Russell location. The staff was friendly. Corina was wonderful. The breakfast team each morning was accommodating and friendly. no complaints their. The only negative was the size of the room and bathroom. but definitely not a deal breaker. I loved my stay away there and will highly recommend staying here and I will be back for sure.

title: Always a pleasant stay
text: I have been using this hotel since it opened when working in the area and I felt I needed to leave a new review as it is improving. I have always been happy with the rooms, ok they may be a little small but it's only for sleeping and in London this is fairly usual, however they are always very clean, well stocked and most importantly quiet. I stayed in one of the newly refurbished rooms and was pleasantly surprised, the rooms have everything you would expect from a good hotel, tv, biscuits, coffee shampoo etc. And now the addition of an iron is a welcomed improvement. I will continue to rebook and recommend anyone looking for a nice friendly quiet hotel gives this a try.

title: Small but clean rooms
text: Some double rooms are tiny but if you have a longer stay you will get a bit bigger room. Very friendly staff and nice atmosphere though there is no place to sit down in the reception which hardly has space for a couple of suitcases. Conveniently located close to Olympia Exhibition center. We have stayed here several times as close to why we are visiting London.....

title: Do not recomend it. Don't waste your money here, go to hilton just around the corner.
text: They started working with hammers and drills at 8 am, gave us the room that was just below the works. Not only the noises were annoying, but the smell of toxic products, with a very little window... The room was small, no direct elevator, small window and very thin walls...

title: Good hotel, especially if you get upgrade to a double from single!
text: I’ve been lucky enough for this to happen a few times now. Getting a room upgrade to a double from a single is really a treat as the amount of space gained is really good, no need to cram in. Staff have always been very good and happy to help when things haven’t been right. Great location for work when I need to be in London. Even better when you can get a night on a discounted rate!

title: Great location, tiny room
text: The best thing about this hotel is the location. Quiet, central and near a station. Staff were friendly but the room was too small. Hardly any space to walk. I wouldn’t return here as there are other hotels nearby at the same price with better space and layout of the room

title: Great hotel if visiting Olumpia
text: Only about three minutes walk from Olympia so was great whilst I was working there, especially as there was lots of snow on the ground! Room was only small but had everything you needed, Lovely buffet breakfast in the morning. Staff were all very helpful and very hotel clean and tidy. Great little place!

title: Good location for Olympia
