title: Good rather than average
text: stayed with a colleague for a business event. For prices in London it is very very good, the rooms were a small double and en suite small but for the price included breakfast. It is in good position and fairly close to tube station. If you want to see London on a budget it is good choice. the rooms we had were on ground floor and in hindsight I would have preferred a higher floor. staff nice and polite,

title: Great stay!
text: Stayed at the morgan for two nights. Great location only a 5 minute walk to the Holborn tube station-which has a big Sainsbury next door. My luggage was delayed and was delivered to the hotel when i was out, the staff took the delivery and was ready for me when i returned to the house. I had a heavy suitcase and was assisted with it both during check in and check out. The breakfast was filling and adeqaurte, the morgan is definately recommended to those who are looking to stay in central london withouth busting their budget.

title: Fantastic location, breakfast and hospitality
text: Stayed at the Morgan for one night (booked 2 twin rooms). Location was perfect and breakfast was excellent. The owner was a genuine Londoner and we loved the Cockney rhyme. "Rocking horse!" = sauce for a delicious English breakfast, with an assortment of fruit, hot drinks, juices, cereals etc. Would definitely recommend this place and stay again! :o)

title: We would be happy to return
text: We had a room for two for L105 per night. The room was quite comfortable and much larger than I had expected. Almost what i would call a suite. A sitting/TV area set aside from the sleeping area. All perfectly clean and quiet. Our room was in their annex building which is about 75 yards up Bloomsbury Street from the main hotel. That was no problem for us since we had very nice weather, however, if one encountered bad weather, then getting to the breakfast room and back to your room would be a problem. Breakfast and the breakfast serving room were quite nice, not elegant, but nice. Food was good and plentiful. The location is perfect , just right adjacent to the British Museum, and easy walking distance to Covent Garden, SOHO, Trafalgar Square, many other interesting places. The nearest tube stop is Tottingham Court Road about ten minutes walk, and there is a bus stop immediately outside of the door of the hotel. We finally decided that the bus was more convenient for anywhere we did not want to walk. However, given the traffic conditions, we thought we could walk anywhere within a mile, quicker than the bus could get there. We were comfortable and well-satisfied for four nights at the Morgan.

title: Comfy, Comfy, Comfy
text: My hubby and I spent 8 nights and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The location was great -- close to 2 tube stations and directly outside the bus stop. Our room was large and the bed was extremely comfortable. We appreciated that good size bathroom and how quickly our room was cleaned each day. We would go down for breakfast, and while we were eating the staff would have already clearned the room. Breakfast was great. You can have the usual fare -- full English -- but they also yogurt, fruit, cold cereal, juice. In fact, they were kind enough to make me oatmeal when requested. John ( I believe that was his name) was always there each morning, making sure our breakfast was served as ordered in a friendly and efficient way. They have a computer in the lobby, which we often took advantage of. It was a wonderful perk. Our room was the first room right near the front door. We never had a problem with noise from outside (as it was right off the main street) nor did we ever hear any noise from the hallway. They were also kind enough to allow us to leave our luggage on the day we checked out, as we were not leaving until later that day. The Morgan is a great place, a great value, and a wonderful place to come back to after a long day of sightseeing. We would certainly stay there again.

title: Unusual kind of hotel for me but I would return
text: Recent reviews of this hotel have included one very critical review, so I'll say straight off that I am neither a friend of this hotel nor a member of staff, and of course every guest anywhere has their own opinion

title: Puzzled by Some Raves
text: I have traveled to London several times a year for thirty yeras. I decided to stay at the Morgan because of the weak dollar and the rave reviews. I think some of the raves about the hotel are overdone. The hotel is clean, modern for a B&B, a good value and good location for visitors who want easy West End access for the theatre. But ther is no lobby, parlor, resident bar, patio or any other common area other than the breakfast room. The reception area for staff is a cubby hole in the basement so you do not pass them when you enter the hotel. I saw no staff except for maybe 10 mintutes in four days. For any visitor who needs any tourism, travel or other information, there is no one to ask. That is why I think many of the raves about friendly staff are puzzling. Two of the four staff people I did encounter were Asians who spoke very poor English. I also encountered a problem about a late check-out. Normal checkout is at 10 am. I asked three times about staying until noon (even volunteering to pay extra). I was told each time that it was no problem. On check out day, Mr Ward the owner said he knew nothing about it and he was obviously displeased. Breakfast was good but is only served from 7-9 am. Since most people were not going to bed until late after the theatre, cutting of breakfast at 9 am was too early. I would stay at the Morgan again but I think many people who are not in London primarily for theatre would be happier in a small hotel in Kensington etc.

title: Great Stay
text: We rented two rooms at the Morgan winter of 2013-14 and were very pleased with the accomodations. The breakfast was great - choice of sausages, toast, hot cereals, eggs, etc. One room had a private patio ensconsed in shrubery - very nice. The staff were very pleasant and informative. Nice access to the tube and the British Museum is around the corner. Plenty of dining a short walk away on South Hampton Row. A coffee shop is just across from the hotel on Great Russell St. We moved to another hotel in another part of the city after a couple of days, but in hind sight we should have just stayed put at the Morgan. There is no "wow" factor stepping into the hotel, nor stepping out onto the street, but for the price and location the hotel deserves a "very good to excellent" rating.

title: Expected more, but liked it nonetheless
text: I stayed at the Morgan for two nights in early September. The reviews on here were so pristine and the hotel came so highly recommended on TA's London Forum, I think my expectations were too high. That being said, I still had a good time and would certainly stay in this hotel in the future. The hotel was not as close to the Tube station as I had expected but was not a long walk, either, perhaps 10 minutes, max. Our twin room was located near the top floor and there were a LOT of stairs, I got a good workout that weekend! The room was mostly clean and comfortable but a few things were amiss, the bathroom door was missing a doorknob and therefore would not close or lock properly and the toilet took forever to flush and run it's cycle. Our room faced the street which is one that leads to a major hospital so it was rather noisy at night. Closing the windows did help and the room had air conditioning should we have needed it, which we didn't. Breakfast (full English is included) was far better than any other place I have stayed in this price range and the fact that the glasses of juice were sitting on a cooling rack was genius!! I am so used to warm juice when I travel to London. The staff was very nice and the hotel seemed very safe as the front door is always locked (you get a key after you check in.) The price was very good for it's location. It is certainly a budget property, but one that offers excellent value.

title: Great Location
text: We stayed at The Morgan Hotel for 5 nights in March. It came highly recommended on Fodors' website. The hotel is a small 14 or 15 room townhouse style, plus several apartment sized units down the street. Most if not all of the main building units have been refurbished in the last year. Our room was on the top floor and there were many stairs to climb - no lift. This was not a problem for us, if it is for you, request a lower level room. One benefit - the noise level was very quiet. The room was large enough, the king sized bed was very comfortable. The in room bathroom had been recently remodeled. Small but functional with hairdryer. Everything was spotless and kept that way by daily housekeeping. The proprieters were cheerful, friendly but did not waste much time with chit chat. We found the eggs cooked to order breakfast a good way to start the day. This isn't the Ritz, but for 95GBP, breakfast and VAT included, we found it to be a great value. Location is very convenient. We would not hesitate in recommending this hotel and would certainly return again and again.

title: Superb Hotel, Helpful People !!
text: Me and my wife stayed there for 7 days, i read the reviews here before i booked and i should say that i am very impressed. The hotel is in the middle of it all, offering a very good price and service..The people responsible, David and Lou were super helpful..Took care of us quite well.. I would not hesitate going back whenever i am in London.. M. Assad Beirut - Lebanon

title: Friendly family in Central London
text: "John" and his wife and their son "Young John" do a super job of making you feel welcome in their simple but clean hotel in the Bloomsbury district of central London. British Museum, Oxford St and the theatre district are within five minutes' walk and a superb Turkish restaurant, Tas, is next door. At today's prices, 90 GBpounds is good value. They'll arrange a private taxi to Heathrow for 30 pounds.

title: A great spot in the city
text: Stayed over a week at the Morgan. Great location in London near the Museum and UCL. Good dining around most corners.Convenient walk to at least 3 Tube stations. Room was compact, clean and comfortable for one. Breakfast was a big plus. Staff were very polite, friendly and happy to help. No lifts means it is a bit of climb for the higher floors.

title: Excellent experience
text: Couldn't have been happier with the location and service. Basic, clean, comfortable, good breakfast, within easy walking distance of theaters, British Museum and good food and drinking spots. These folks go the second mile. Felt completely comfortable as a solo traveler. I'll go back.

title: Loved the refurbished rooms!
text: I stayed at the Morgan Hotel for 9 days at the end of March and had a lovely time. The room I was given had been refurbished and was extremely comfortable. The English breakfast was fabulous. The location is convenient to the theatre district. Will definitely stay in this hotel in the future!

title: Great value in the thick of London
text: It can be frustrating to find reasonably-priced accommodation in London. Many of the high-rated TA hotels and B&Bs were full even in (I thought) off-season. The Morgan met or exceeded our expectations. Our room on the top floor (59 steps) was spacious enough, very clean, functional bathroom with plenty of stowage space. Shower a bit "cosy" but functional. As another reviewer (cheroman) mentioned, our view was of the side of the British Museum, a 2 minute walk away and a focus of our trip. Breakfast was fine

title: Good location for Theatre and Covent Garden
text: This was a good value for money hotel within easy striking distance of Covent Garden and the Royal Opera House. We had a ground floor room which was at the side of the property. Whilst quiet, it was small and dark. However, it was well appointed and had everything required for our stay. We had an issue with bedding which was dealt with positively after our visit.

title: great value, great location
text: My husband & I have stayed here twice & will probably stay again (unless we can stay with friends :-). It's shockingly affordable for London, the breakfast is excellent, the location is very central, & it has all the basics that the traveler needs. Of course the rooms are small -- this is London! Even London homes are tiny unless you're the Queen. But everything works & is clean, that's all the matters.

title: short walk from theater land
text: very clean hotel spread over 2 buildings, rooms very clean,with nice beds, with a living room and small kitchen. about a mile from euston station, and 10 minutes walk from all the main theaters and shows, covent garden is also about 10 minutes walk away, british museum, is not far, so really central for everything

title: Terrible stay, don't stay there unless you are guaranteed to be upstairs!!
text: The reason I am so unhappy is that I had one of the couple of rooms right by the front door. This meant I could hear people coming in and out of the hotel late in the evening and early in the morning. I think it's not obvious that these are rooms and people didn't stop making noise until they walked upstairs (which I could hear as well, the hotel being very small and narrow). Also, the reception is in the basement so if people haven't got a key already, they have to ring the door bell which once again woke me up. These rooms should simply not be rooms! It should be where the reception or breakfast area is... (Baring in mind I never usually complain to hotel staff and that I have never asked to swap rooms before in my life) - I asked to swap rooms, but the guy said that the hotel was full that night and the following night as well. And he said that the room is a good quiet one anyway! Funny then that later on that same evening, I heard the new arrivers from the room opposite complaining of the same thing. I'm sure they actually get complaints about this all the time. Later, in the night (after midnight), I heard these people having an argument with the hotel's staff who I had spoken to earlier. They insisted much more than I did and in the end he gave up saying that there was actually a twin room available upstairs at the back but that he had been reluctant to do it because it messes up "the system" and he would speak to the manager the following morning. So he lied to me when he said the hotel was full! Note that I wasn't ear-dropping, I was in bed trying to sleep, that's how loud they were talking! I basically hardly slept during my stay! I was woken up as late as 1am and as early as 5am. Including once by a member of staff talking right behind my door! (see above) Anyway - The room itself was small but fine and comfortable. The only thing I would say is that a table was missed, and that the TV was REALLY tiny and far away from the bed in one of the ceiling corners. Apart from that the breakfast was very decent and some of the staff were nice. The hotel doesn't have a restaurant, but there is an independant one next door, and lots of others a block away. The best thing is by far the location for the price, as you're 5 mins walk from the Underground's Central and Northern lines at the Tottenham Court Road station, 2 mins walk from the British museum, 10 mins walk from Covent Gardens, Soho, Leicester Square and Oxford Street. So it's very central, and ideal for visiting, restaurants, theatre, shopping, etc if all you need is cheap (for London) accomodation for the night (although not in my case as I couldn't do the basic you need a hotel for: sleep!). Just ask to be upstairs or pay a bit more and stay at one of the many other hotels around... Oh yes and I forgot: on one of the days my room was not made!

title: Fine receptionist, excellent location
text: Excellent location, not far from a Greek restaurant that I enjoy visiting. Receptionist - Shay - was admirably helpful and solved a series of travel queries with efficiency. He organised an early breakfast as well. Quiet night's sleep.

title: London's Wonderful Morgan Hotel
text: When we visit London, we only stay at the Morgan Hotel. The location is ideal. It is within easy walking distance to the museums, Trafalgar Square and the theatre district

title: Great For The Single Traveler
text: I stayed at the MORGAN hotel from Jult 20th -July 27th. The room was a small single room but contained an in room safe, air conditioner(new), two telephones (one by the bed and one by the shower). The bathroom was renovated with a marble sink and a shower with a detatchable shower wand and plenty of hot water. The room and bathroom were very well organized and faced the back so it was very quiet at night. The breakfast room was cute and the breakfast was filling and delicious(this is included in the price of the room) The Morgan is just steps away from the British Museum. (You don't even have to cross the street-it is right around the corner). There is a 24 hour store two blocks away(walk south two blocks ) and a bus stop about 20 feet away from the front door. You can cath the 73 bus there that will take you to Victoria Station. There are also two Tube stops within three or four blocks of the Hotel. The service at the hotel was excelent - the hotel is run by a family and in the mornings there was always one of the family members there (usually serving breakfast. I was on a theatre going vacation and it was ideal for me as it was usually just a short stroll to the theatre district of the West End -but even when I took in a show at the National Theatre (across the river)or the Royal Court theatre (in Chelsea) it was just three or four stops on the tube to get there. I will tell my friends about this hotel and think it is a great place to stay for the single traveler as Air Conditioning when you can find it in a town house hotels is usually only in a double room -ditto for the high end hotels. Robert

title: Excellent location for price
text: Stayed here for 4 nights in Jan 09 after reading the reviews from tripadvisor... overall a very good hotel... the biggest pro is location... being next to british museum u can walk almost anywhere in west end... and despite what others said the hotel is just 3 minutes walk from Tottleham court road tube and 4 mins from Holborn. For the price it is very decent and we definitely would come back.

title: My new Favorite in London
text: Wow, what a find! Location, value, clean. friendly, helpful staff, the Morgan has it all. London is the best city in the world, but finding a decent hotel at a reasonable price is not easy. Here it is! I booked a twin room and requested a room on the top floor. The stairs are not a problem for me, but could be for some people. The room was not large but fine for the amount of time you spend there. The bathroom was clean, the only tiny negative was the water pressure was a little weak. The beds were comfortable. Breakfast was served quickly, the food was good and plentiful. The location is great for exploring London, on foot or there are 2 tube stops close by. British Museum, Covent Garden, theatres, shopping, and much more all within easy reach. I will definitely stay at the Morgan again. Thanks Trip Advisor!

title: Great location, excellent breakfast
text: Stayed here for three nights in early April 2018. Great location within a block of the British Museum and a 15 to 20 minute walk to the theater district. My room was on the top floor (3rd) and as there is no elevator you need to be able to walk up, which I knew about and was not a problem. As I was travelling on my own I reserved one of their smaller rooms but it actually was larger than I expected and included a queen size bed. The room was very clean, the wifi worked well and the room had an in-room safe. The bed was nice and comfortable. The one complaint I have is that the shower head had very little water pressure and was like a fine spray instead of an actual shower. So taking a shower took quite a while. The included breakfast was excellent with friendly service and included made to order eggs, toast and coffee. Cereal and yogurt was also available. Always much nicer to have breakfast served by friendly staff instead of a self serve buffet with pre-made scrambled eggs! Despite the shower, I would recommend the Morgan Hotel and would stay here again if I get the chance.

title: great value
text: Hotel is located near the metro and helped us during our stay. Room was quite clean with a safe, TV, and a fridge breakfast was also good included into the room rate. The stuff was friendly and helpful any time we request for directions. I recommend this Hotel to any one, notice if you can not walk the stairs ask for a room not in a high floor

title: Great location, very clean, friendly
text: Very nice small (more like a B&B) hotel. I was on the top floor in the front - and it was quiet, with the windows closed. Air conditioner worked well. There was distracting TV noise from the adjoining room, when it was on, so overall quietness depends on your neighbor - but that only happened once in 5 days. TV was small and only had about 4 or 5 stations - all British. There is supposedly free wireless Internet located in the basement, but one of the workers had entered a password and forgot it and did not seem to be trying to resolve this, so there was no wireless Internet. However, that same person was friendly and showed me how to connect my laptop directly to an extra Ethernet cable in the basement

title: Great location and value
text: The Morgan's location couldn't be better from our perspective. Next door to the outstanding British Museum, close to three tube stations, within easy walking distance of London's theatre district and a variety of restaurants were all pluses. Our room was a reasonable size by London standards. It was very clean and there was lots of hot water in the bathroom. Breakfast was very good including eggs, bacon, toast and a good sized carafe of coffee. It was efficiently served in an attractive, clean and appropriately decorated dining area. The only negative may be that the Morgan does not have an elevator. We asked and got a ground floor room so this was not an issue for us. Next time we're in London, our first choice will be the Morgan Hotel

title: Rock-Solid
text: This is a very simple, solid hotel, without many amenities but has all the basics, including free breakfast. Family-owned, the staff is highly accomodating and has a great focus on service.

title: The Morgan Hotel is the place to stay!
text: My adult son and I stayed at the Morgan in separate rooms for six nights in January. He was very pleased with his ensuite room. My room was huge and the bathroom was superb! My only complaint, and it is a minor one, was the fact that my room was right outside the telephone and computer area. At times I was amazed at the rudeness of people checking out early in the morning, bellowing right outside my room

title: Still great after all these years!
text: I first stayed at the Morgan in 2009. Nine years later I returned and found it to be just as good. This hotel won me over with it’s prime location, excellent price, secure building and very quiet location (despite being on a very busy street, the windows really block the noise out). The location is great, between either the Tottenham Court or Holborn tube stops, so you can get just about anywhere quickly. My sister and I shared a twin bed room, which was a tight fit but we managed. The beds are ok the bathroom is small but everything was clean and the building is secure, with key entry by hotel guests only. Breakfast is still included and it’s good to get the day started with that. After two stays here, I’d stay here yet again, and probably will! Thanks Morgan Hotel for showing that some things do stay the same over time!

title: Short Stay
text: This hotel is ideally located for those wanting to go a West end show and other centrally based activities. What stood out was the extremely friendly down to earth staff that were happy to go over and above for you. The room and bed was very comfortable and clean but the occupants in room next to me could be heard very clearly so a bit noisy for a while in the evening.

title: Excellent value
text: Location is great. Walking distance to do many places. Room was clean and comfortable with everything we needed. Excellent breakfast included in the price. Our only issue was we stayed in the 3rd floor with No lift. Not The Hotels Fault as there is no space For One but it Was a bit hard on the Knees . However we will stay here again but will try to be a bit fitter

title: Great Hotel, Great Location, Great Price!!!
text: Great little hotel in a fantastic location. Went with 2 friends so booked a triple room. The room was clean and fairly big. It had a safe that was free of charge to use and air conditioning, which came in handy as the weather was fantastic! The bathroom, athough small, was also very clean and adaquately stocked with clean white towels and toiletries.The staff were very friendly and helpful, and allowed us to leave our bags at the hotel after we had checked out so we could enjoy our last day without hauling our bags around with us. Would definitely stay here again and will reccommend to all!

title: Shouldn't a respectable company check their listings on booking sites?
text: I booked this hotel through a well known booking site. I was heading for London with a speech to make the next day and the site promised me a desk. Tick. The site also promised me a bath. Tick. And, if I had time to spare there was a flat screen TV - half tick. Also have to say that I prefer to stay in non chains because I like to support individual enterprise and there are a number of hotels in other parts of London that I am happy to return to. The visit did not start well as I entered the hotel and a ghostly voice from downstairs "welcomed" me. It would have been nice if he had made the effort to come to the ground floor as I have no sense of direction, was a woman on my own and had a case which I did not want to leave and did not want to carry. Needless to say my room was on the 3rd floor and there was no real offer of help with my bags. On entering the room I immediately saw that there was no desk so decided to check out the bathroom before taking things further. You've guessed - no bath! I called reception and said that I had expected a desk and a bath and was told that that was not confirmed on the booking form - after a very prolonged discussion (during which I was told that they had no responsibility for descriptions on booking sites) I eventually persuaded the poor man on reception (the one who apparently had limited use of his legs) to phone his boss. To be fair to him, he did this. He then phoned me back to confirm that they had no say over descriptions on booking sites. Now, you can call me picky if you want, but I would contend that a reputable company would check the listings for accuracy - and as a punter, I had assumed that the hotel would have provided the description in the first place. Anyway, I was told that the computer had allocated me that room so no change was possible (to this day I do not know whether the hotel was full) So, not in a great mood and decided to have a half hour TV break before tackling work. The TV was a joke. The smallest screen I have ever seen (to be fair, it was actually flat) and tucked, at ceiling level, beside the air con. I was glad that I had not planned to watch TV all evening because I would have had to have visited a chiropractor to sort out my frozen neck afterwards. I ended up having to complete my paperwork etc sitting on the bed, which was not an ideal situation In the morning I tried to have a shower. It was truly the most miserable flow I have ever experienced, and I have travelled on business in third world countries. I was hoping for a redeeming breakfast. Sadly not. I shared the breakfast room with stacks of Xmas decs waiting to be put away (mid Jan) and my expectations were raised when I saw that the breakfast would be cooked to order. I didn't want a full English so ordered bacon and eggs. I received a rasher of bacon and an egg! As part of a full English this is fine - but if I don't fancy sausage - and whatever else was on the menu, then wouldn't it have been nice to have that replaced with an extra egg or an extra slice of bacon? It all just seemed a bit mean.

title: Second stay was just as good as the first..
text: I recently stayed for 7 nights at the Morgan Hotel. This was my second stay there and it was just as enjoyable as the first. The room (single) was quite roomy by London standards,pleasant, and very clean. Breakfast was tasty and the service was excellent. As I was there during unexpected warm weather, the A/C was an added bonus. The Morgan is within 10 minutes walk to three differnet tube stations (Russell Square, Holborn and Tottenham Court Road) and there is a bus stop right out front. Friendly, helpful staff make the Morgan an excellent value in a very convenient area. The only thing I missed in my room was a kettle to have a cuppa. As a solo female traveler, I felt safe and had no worries. I look forward to staying at the Morgan in the future.

title: Terrible disappointment
text: Took my children to see Matilda and the Morgan hotel for locality was perfect, but that is certainly where the good points finished! We was in the front bedroom supposedly for family booked as 2 daughters 1 adult. The room contained one double one single so not ideal, the bathroom was not child friendly at all!! The toilet flush buttons were almost inoperable and needed significant ADULT force, the hot and cold taps were opposite so my daughter burnt herself. The water was not drinkable from the tap so they had put some water in a bottle with a flip top, once opened the rubber seal was blackened with mold so we had to go out and buy water 10 at night. The doors of the room were set heavy so they slammed and as thus room was by the front door all night the front door would keep you awake with the coming any going of the residents. To occupy the children in the room the TV was mounted 6ft up and was the size of a postage stamp!! So to make light of the situation I convinced the girl's to go to bed early ready for the morning, but unknown to me the room is the central point of all the drainage from the rest of the hotel so throughout the night toilet flushing water and showers so ruined any chance of a good night sleep my eldest looked drained in the morning. Breakfast in principal looked good until the tasting, sausage very limp and fatty similar to a boiled Richmond beans had a horribly calcium aftertaste similar to a scaled up kettle and scrambled eggs tasteless. Fried egg and bacon ok as was the cereal , juice and coffee. Service wise I cannot fault, booking and waitress were good. Overall very disappointing for my daughters, I never feel the need to complain but I hope to prevent any other family getting that room!!

title: Very nice hotel
text: My wife and I recently stayed in the Morgan Hotel for 5 days. We stayed in a twin room on the second floor in the back of the hotel. The room had been recently renovated, and was very nice and extremely clean. As I understand it, they are in the process of renovating all of the rooms. The location of the hotel is right at the British museum, and is only a few blocks from the Tottenham underground station. You are not in the middle of everything, but it is still very convenient to the west end and related attractions. We could walk to Covent Garden, Picadilly Circus, and restaurant row on Compton Street. The staff was very helpful and friendly, and the included English breakfast was generous and nicely prepared. Some of the reviews complain about the rooms being small. Be warned that this is a European hotel, and the rooms really aren't that big, and there is no elevator, pool, etc. If you want a Holiday Inn, stay at the Holiday Inn! But you would be missing a very nice experience. The Wards are extremely friendly and nice, and getting to know them was our pleasure. They work very hard to please their customers, and would do anything to make your stay memorable. As a bonus, just around the corner is Munchkins restaurant. The prices are good, and they have a fairly large menu. A great place for afternoon tea when your feet are throbbing from touring the British Museum. We highly recommend the Morgan Hotel!

title: Convenient, clean and comfortable
text: My 21 year old niece and I spent 3 nights at the Morgan hotel and will definately stay there again when we return to London. As some others have written, the rooms are extremely small but once you get past that you find a clean room and very comfortable beds. The host is very friendly and helpful. Breakfast was very good - eggs, bacon, sauteed mushrooms, toast and jam, yogurt, cereal and more. The breakfast area is very cute and comfortable. The hotel was walking distance from the theater district and the Covent Garden area which is full of great restaurants and street activities. It was also convenient for accessing public transportation. The TV only gets 3 channels but my niece and I didn't care about that. Overall, this is a great little hotel for the price of staying there.

title: Ok for London but don't expect too much
text: We stayed here in July for almost a week. The good news--for London, home of the worst hotel values in the world, it wasn't too badly priced (about $200 per night for a double) and decent. The rooms are pretty cramped and the furnishings old if adequate. Bathroom small but decent. The breakfasts are large (if a bit greasy) and the manager and his assistant who serve you breakfast are really great--friendly, helpful, etc. It is also in a great location--right next to wonderful Turkish restaurant (Tas) and very near British Museum. Walking distance to Soho and even to theatres. Has free wifi too,a definite plus. The bad news: Anywhere else but London it would not be a good value. There is no elevator and the rooms go up 5 flights.

title: Great hotel! Will stay here again!
text: After traveling on business on a "start-up" budget, I learned that there seems to be a lot of hotels in the UK at the 65-85 pound range, then it shoots up to 150-299 pound range. Everyone loves a gorgeous hotel - but let's be honest, you really need a comfy bed, control of the heater, a good comforter, and hot water. When in the UK add breaky. I saw the Morgan on TripAdvisor and selected it. When I phoned them two days before arrival they were able to lodge me for three nights if I was willing to move to another room after the first night. I agreed. I arrived and they greeted me by name! The first night I stayed in a flat in the annex (at single room rate). It was really big great for 2 people staying for a long time or a close knit family or a group of friends. It had 2 bathrooms, living room, and two twin beds (that could be pushed together). The next night they moved me to a single in the main hotel (which the owner corrected referred to as a cupboard but was more comfy for me than the flat). I stayed there a total of three nights at 85 pounds per night and I made phone calls back to the US every night for about 45 minutes to an hour. The entire stay cost me about $450 (that's cheap when you include the phone calls!). The décor is older grandma with a touch of bed and breakfast and I was told by the proprietor that all the room will be remodeled by early 2004. The breakfast was excellent! The owner is a great cook. If you are vegan or veggie, you will definitely need to talk with them in advance. The breakfast is typical English breakfast eggs, bacon, sausage, cereal, tea, toast, tomatoes, juice, tea/coffee. It doesn't seem as though they stock any other food products (ie yoghurt, etc). The windows have double-paned glass. The heater worked like a charm. There was hot water at all times. The owners were really, really great. Location cant be beat!

title: You Can't Beat the Morgan
text: Stayed at the Morgan Hotel for the second time 6/2/07-6/8/07. This trip was with my daughters 18 and 22 who had each just graduated from H.S. and college respectively. We stayed in a fourth floor suite which was just up the street from the main hotel. Three years ago I had stayed at the main hotel with my son on his graduation trip. The suites are much larger and well worth the extra money. WIth three of us the extra space was essential. The rooms in the main hotel are small but extremely clean and well maintained. The suites are also clean and well maintained but had a kitchenette and a living area in additon to a powder room, bathroom and a large bedroom with a queen size bed and 2 twin beds. Our suite was on the fouth floor and it is a walk up. For someone with health issues it would be important to request a lower floor, for us it was not a problem. Also the suite had the bedrooms in the back of the building ( very quiet, we could see the side of the British Museum from our bedroom windows) which is important as there is street noise in the front of the buidlings at both the hotel and suites face Bloomsbury. On the last visit to the Morgan my son and I had a room on the street side of the hotel and I experienced some nights waking up with traffic noises. (I am a light sleeper) If you're a light sleeper whether in the hotel or the suites make sure your bedrooms are away from the street. The area of the Morgan is nice and accesible to the Tottenham Court tube stop. It is only a block to the British Museum. It is within walking distance to the West End theatres also. I would say the biggest point for me is that the Morgan is family owned and run by very nice, hard working people. David was there every day of our stay. We had breakfast every morning in the breakfast room and he was always pleasant and helpful. At the end of our stay we mistakenly left a back pack at the hotel and he was very gracious and accomodating in having it shipped to us in Paris which was our next stop. You can certainly pay a lot more in London for accomodations but I don't think you will find more for your money than what you get at the Morgan. I will always stay there as long as the Ward family is running things.

title: Awful
text: Revolting hotel. 8 hours in cramped, musty room with no drinking water. I'm glad we amused the manager with the fact that our luggage would not fit in the room. Rickety stairs, tiny beds pushed together. Rip off. Not the hotel we booked. Meant to be happy with the sub standard accommodation because they offer a free breakfast.

title: Great Value, Comfortable Room
text: Comfortable, clean, warm in winter, great location. This hotel was everything it said it was on its website. A great value for the price. Our room was the twin at the back top of the hotel, a few flights up but just like a continuation of the tube climbs we did much of the day. Bathroom was well appointed and modern. It was quiet all night with very little daytime noise also. The breakfast of eggs, bacon, sausage, cereal, yogurt, juice, coffee kept us filled for a good part of the day. I like the Bloomsbury area for convenience. Plenty of nice, moderately priced restaurants within walking distance in any direction. Nice one on the corner. A little more walking and you are in the heart of Covent Garden. Enjoyed the free wireless internet. I selected this hotel based on Trip Advisor reviews and would stay here again.

title: highly recommended!
text: My mother and aunt currently stayed in the Morgan for a whole week and we were all impressed by how clean and spacious the room was, with a private safe for peace of mind, and extremely friendly and helpful owners and staff. The location is unbeatable, while the traditional b+b style makes you feel quite homey. Highly recommended!

title: Great Location and Service
text: I was looking for a central London hotel for an overnight visit and booked at the Morgan based on reviews I read on this site. Have to say I wasn't disappointed. The staff couldn't do enough to help, the rooms were very clean and comfortable, easy access to transport and a short walk to the theatres. Would definitely stay there again.

title: Great Location and Friendly Owners
text: Our extended family of 5 stayed for 3 nights in June at this nice, family run small hotel. It is located near the British Museum and in walking distance of many sights, pubs, restaurants and train stations (we had an ~25 minute walk with our suitcases from the London St Pancras train station). The hotel is relatively tall and narrow with a nice entrance though without a lobby, with most rooms on upper floors, requiring a climb up several flights of steps. The rooms are small but comfortable, with 2 of our rooms facing the busy, somewhat noisy street and the other room, much quieter and very pleasant, facing the back of the hotel. The rooms have a safe, adequate lighting, air conditioning, windows that provide adequate natural light and air, TV etc...and a comfortable bed. A large bottle of fresh water is in each room and though a small refrigerator would have been nice, extra cold water is provided upon request. The wonderful breakfast is served, starting at 7:30 am, in the lower level of the hotel, with eggs, bacon, mushrooms, tomatoes, toast etc...and coffee made to order by friendly John Sr along with OJ, yogurt, fresh fruit. It was a great way to start the day! We enjoyed a nice pub/cafe close by called Plough for 2 of our meals (and for those in need of a Starbucks, it is a few minutes walk down the street!) One can walk ~20 minutes to the Big Bus Tours Hop on/off bus stop which is a great way to see the city. A ~30 minute walk to the fun Covent Garden area (with its street performers, market, shopping, cafe's...) was also enjoyable for our family. The owners reserved a taxi for our departure to Heathrow which was very helpful. Overall, the great location and friendly owners makes The Morgan Hotel a nice place to stay while visiting London!

title: Reasonably priced London Hotel
text: The Morgan Hotel is in a very good location close to the British Museum. John and the staff run the Morgan very efficiently and provide as much help to their guests as possible. Rooms are not large (as per London generally) but are modern, clean and fresh. We appreciated, as it appeared did many of the guests, the free access to the internet - an example of the thought given to meeting guests needs. The Morgan represents excellent value for money and we would definitely stay there again.

title: Good Location, Clean
text: My and my other half had a pleasant stay at the Morgan on the May Day weekend. The rooms are absolutely fine for those not wanting to "live" in their hotel room. All areas of accomodation were clean and well serviced. The breakfast served each morning was much better than we thought it would be given some previous bad experiences in other "budget" hotels in London. Choice was fine and English breakfast was cooked very well. Staff were friendly and helpful. We used the hotel for a base as it is quite near Theatreland and with a few tube stations within a 5-10 minute walk we found the location ideal.

title: Still a great budget hotel
text: The standard of this hotel is just as good as when we last stayed there in July 2006. The rooms are well furnished,the breakfast substantial, the staff pleasant and the location is second to none. There are no public rooms as in a lounge or bar but they are simply not required in central London in our opinion. There is free internet access in the lobby and many rooms have a patio if you want to sit outside. Price is £100.00 per room B & B per night. Need I say more?

title: Wonderful Place to Stay in London
text: My wife and I spent 19 nights at the Morgan Hotel and found everything to perfection. The location is ideal, within walking distance to Covent Garden and the West End. The Tottenham Rd Underground is five minutes walk and gives you easy access to all the tourist destinations. The owner is a delight and extremely helpful. Breakfast is, without doubt, one of the best we have had in all our travels. The neighborhood, Bloomsbury, is very trendy with cute restaurants, pubs, etc. that are very reasonably priced for London (great Turkish restaurant next door). The room looked brand new and was very comfortable and spotless. There is a computer and internet in the Hotel entrance. All in all the Hotel Morgan is a gem in London.

title: Convenient Hotel
text: Great little hotel conveniently located north of Soho near the British Museum. The free internet in the hallway was very helpful. The room was small but comfortable, and the bathroom was totally modernized. My room was in the back on the hotel and very quiet. Slept like a rock.

title: Loved our stay!
text: My 12 yr old son and I stayed at the Morgan Hotel for 9 nights during the Olympics. We had an apartment on the 2nd floor for 6 nights and a hotel room for the last 3 nights. The apartment was fantastic - it really is an apartment with full size bathroom, separate shower and tub, large mirror etc. There is a separate toliet room. It has a large bedroom, perfect for us with double and single beds, and a large living room with couch, chair, good size TV and small dining table and chairs. The pictures on the website don't do justice to the actual size of the apartment. The "kitchen" is very small, but usable with sink, small fridge, microwave, dishes, and cabinet. Worth every bit of the 190 pounds a night. The hotel room we had to change to was very small as are all rooms in London. (made our reserv. a year ahead but only 6 nights in apt available!) Bathroom still good size but very little room around the bed, and only one small chair. Small TV high in corner of room. Doable for 3 nights, would have been very hard for nine. The owners here cannot be beat for their service and assistance. For our first trip to London we so appreciated having them answer questions etc rather than being in a "no host" apt somewhere. The breakfast was great. John took our order each day and everything was quick and delicious. Many choices, yogurt, fruit, cereal, juices, to go along with your hot order. I'd advise using Russel Square, rather than Holborn for tube to/from Heathrow as there is a elevator rather than all stairs. Try to arrive/depart midday. Overall, great location. Near tube on Central line. Near grocery store. Just around corner from British Museum. Wish we could return soon!

title: Great location, nice place
text: You really can't beat the location of this hotel ... right around the corner from the British Museum and only a few minutes' walk to the Underground. The rooms were reasonably small, very comfortable, very clean. Our room overlooked the garden, which was lovely. The breakfast was excellent: egg, bacon, sausage, beans, toast, grilled tomatoes and mushrooms, muesli, cheeses, whole fruit, juice, coffee, tea. We happened to have some raucous people the next room over, singing Blondie songs at all hours of the night. Finally at 3:30AM I called the front desk, who took care of the situation. Despite the neighbors, a very nice stay.

title: SPOTLESSLY CLEAN,VERY COMFORTABLE,& FRIENDLY.
text: The Morgan Hotel is a familly run bussines of many years,offering smart up to date bedrooms with en-suite facilities,friendly service and an excellent breakfast.The Morgan Hotel is situated in the lovely area of Bloomsbury, minutes away from The British Museum, several diverse resturants,10-15 minutes walk from West-end theatre land as well as Oxford Street/Regent Street shops. Our return visit, for four nights, to The Morgan Hotel did not disappoint. Our room,as exspected, was spotlessly clean with very comfortable beds,quality white bed linen, and lovely soft white towels in the bathroom. We looked forward to our cooked English Breakfast each morning, served with tea or coffee which was excellent excellent and always served in a genuine friendly manner. I think The Morgan Hotels motto should be, " COMFORTABLE,CLEAN, FRIENDLY AND EXCELLENT VALUE FOR MONEY" We will definately stay at The Morgan Hotel in Bloomsbury, when we next visit London again. If it's "small & friendly" you want, why not give it a try next time you visit London.(forget the large, overpriced hotels)

title: Not what we'd hoped
text: We chose the Morgan based on reviews on this site and the links to Fodor’s, and we were not as impressed as many previous readers. This was our first trip to England, and our second hotel in London, and while I’m glad we left our previous hotel, the Morgan was so-so. First of all, TripAdvisor better update it US dollars price range—we paid 98 pounds a night for a twin (2-bed) room—that’s over $180 USD. Although the proprietor was pleasant, we got none of the friendliness raved about. He checked us in, got our bags up to our room and down when we left, and asked us how we wanted our breakfast cooked—that was the sum exchange in a 3-day stay. The best part of the hotel was its proximity to the British Museum, where we could have spent our entire 3 weeks! The room was small but efficient, with a large lovely window (the only one with a view of the 3 hotels we stayed at in London), and the breakfast was fabulous (but I tired of all that protein very early in the trip). We had a room safe and an adequate closet, and the beds were very comfortable. However, I agree with an earlier reviewer that we could have done better, even in that area and that price range.

title: Great stay in the heart of London
text: First time in London and we were a little apprehensive about booking a little hotel. We arrived from Vienna to a older worn out looking city/subway. Took a while to get to the hotel (we took the train then the central -red- line, with a lot of stops) hauling too much luggage. Arrived at hotel and the door was locked, but we pushed the bell and were quickly let in. Very friendly greeting and although it was quite a climb to get to the room (my wife calls it the 'stairs of death'), when we did arrive we were pleasantly surprised. Although quite small by US standards, it was very clean, nicely laid out, and had AIR CONDITIONING. After a two week trip through Austria without any ac, this was great! This whole trip has been quite warm and humid and opening the windows downtown is a little too noisy at night. Breakfast is great - cereal, fruit (limited), yogurt, coffee, tea, hot choc.,orange or apple juice, brown or white toast, and cooked to order: eggs, bacon, sausage, mushrooms/tomatoes. Very friendly host and the rooms were quickly cleaned. Evidently the apartments are even nicer and they offered to move us to one (they were full the first night we were there), but the rooms we had were so nice, we decided to stay and didn't even look at them. The location could not be beat. Right next to the British Museum and close to the Piccadilly line. We didn't get the Oyster card, because the lady at the train station suggested that it would be cheaper for a 5 day stay to get a card that allows underground use in zones 1,2,3 and all buses. Also tried the hop on hop off 'Original London Tour' buses. They were okay, but kinda expensive. Oh yeah, after two weeks in Austria, I finally got a hotel with free wi-fi. Prior Hotels either didn't have it, it didn't work, or charged obscene amounts of money to use it!

title: Fabulous Stay at The Morgan Hotel
text: Stayed for one night on Saturday 10th November - just wish it had been longer! Weekend in London to celebrate my daughter's 16th birthday - super hosts, very welcoming & informative- THANK YOU. Hotel very comfortable & clean. Excellent 'cooked to order' breakfast. Fantastic location for everything & excellent Turkish restaurant next door! (Taz') - a real bonus as we love Turkish food! Hotel very secure and we felt safe. Without hesitation, we highly recommend The Morgan Hotel & look forward to return visits! *****

title: Loved Morgan Hotel
text: My 16-year-old daughter and I had a wonderful stay in the Morgan Hotel. Our top-floor room (2 twin beds) was small but very cozy and well equipped (hair dryer, in-room safe, comfortable beds and a small table and chairs). The staff carried our bags up for us. I was concerned that there would be street noise since our room was on the front of the hotel, which is on a very busy street, but the double-glazed windows took care of that. In fact, the hotel is amazingly quiet

title: ten out of ten!
text: This b and be couldn't be more central, clean , convenient and friendly. I have said in 5 star hotels and ended up in smaller , dirtier rooms. I recommend fully!

title: A great little hotel in London
text: My husband and I stayed at the Morgan Hotel in September 2011 and loved it! First of all the location is perfect, in walking distance to shopping sites, the theater district, and best of all - right next door to the British Museum! We also found plenty of good restaurants within walking distance. Tube stations are close by and we went wherever we wanted very easily. As for the hotel itself, the people in charge were very friendly and helpful with advice when we asked. The breakfast was served in a very pleasant room and was very good. Our room, though small, had everything necessary, and was spotless. The towels in the bathroom were so thick and soft - what one would expect in a 5-star luxury hotel! We asked for a taxi to the airport on our last morning, very early, and the taxi was ordered and showed up on time, and for a reasonable price too. This hotel was recommended to us by friends who have stayed there on numerous visits over the years, and now I can see why. We will definitely try to stay there again if we visit London in the future, and will recommend it highly to our friends.

title: Clean and secure.
text: It's nearly impossible to say anything about The Morgan that hasn't already been said. The rooms are small and so are the beds, but things are tidy and safe ... there's free internet access in the lobby ... a tasty breakfast is cooked-to-order each morning ... and the proprietor is friendly and charming. These folks have been operating this hotel for many years and they know how to make their guests feel at home. This is a nice, affordable place to stay in the heart of Bloomsbury.

title: Location Can't Be Beat
text: Fantastic location, literally around corner from the British Museum. All of the major tourist attractions are within walking distance, as are several Tube Stations. There are a number of pubs and a few restaurants within blocks (Tas, the Turkish place next door is very good). There is no elevator, so getting to most rooms requires climbing a fair amount of steps. The rooms are on the small side, without a lot of amenities. They serve a typical English breakfast in a comfortable breakfast room in the basement.

title: Nice hotel in a great neighborhood!
text: I was looking forward to this hotel for some time. It was right near my favorite spot in London, the British Museum. Pros- The management was very nice. They helped me a lot with having breakfast and checking out (at five in the morning). John helped with my luggage. It had a double bed. They put me right by the basement with a patio in the back. It had two or three steps down to my level and a number of them down to the breakfast area. But, it wasn't in one section of the hotel. The cleaning crew was also nice. I had a head cold and they didn't pressure me to get out of my room so they could clean it. Cons- The shower was too small. They had a soap dispenser in the shower and by the sink. You will need two hands to use this. (And, most people will not have a problem.) But, I had to go to Boots and pick up soap for the nine days that I was there. The bed had a big lump in it. You would have to pick a side and sleep on it, or you were going to get a lump in the middle. The tv was small and was right by the ceiling. The room was cramped, with two chairs, two bed tables, a wardrobe and a tiny bathroom. (I am assuming that they usually have two people in that room. But, egads! I felt cramped with one person in the room.) All in all, I had a nice time. And, if I didn't have the nasty cold, it would have been much better.

title: Great value, friendly hotel
text: Stayed one night in the hotel in one of their large singles which was effectively a double. Room was clean and quiet despite being in central London. Breakfast was excellent. Plenty of cereal and toast as well as the full english. Stayed in plenty of upmarket hotels in London with up market prices to boot. They weren't a patch on this one.

title: thanks Morgan!
text: My mum and I stayed in the morgan hotel for 3 nights in the middle of january. We had a twin room at the front of the hotel on the very top floor. This must have been one of the smaller rooms but was perfectly adequate for us as we were out all day touring the London sights. The outside street noise which has been previously mentioned was not really a problem, although i did wear ear plugs at night just in case! The daily assent to our room up sooooo many stairs served to keep us fit, however if stairs are a struggle for you then make sure to ask for a lower level room - my legs are still hurting now! The shower did take about 5 minutes to warm up the the mornings but was fine when it had got going. The full english breakfast was great and served to keep the hunger pains at bay until way after dinner time which is just what is needed when attempting to cram in all of the sights of london in just three days! Perfect location, a stones throw from the underground circle line, and all in all a pleasent stay in a wonderful city! thanks Morgan!

title: Excellent location, WiFi, friendly hosts- would 100% stay here again
text: My partner and I (both under 30) recently stayed for 3 nights at the Morgan Hotel for our trip to London. We arrived early on Saturday and the gentleman at the hotel allowed us to leave our bags until our room was ready (only an hour wait). We stayed in room 209 which was a double bedded room with an en suite bathroom. The window overlooked a small court yard. The hotel was quiet, and at no point was noise an issue. The bathroom was clean for my standards (I am a neat freak). The water pressure was good, and it was nice to be able to wash a day of traveling away in the comfort of your own room. There is WiFi available (no charge) and there is also a computer in the entrance way on the ground floor for guests to use. There are lots of maps and brochures downstairs as well. Breakfast is served downstairs in the morning - it consists of a full English breakfast (eggs, toast, sausage or bacon, mushrooms and a tomato). Coffee and tea were served and there was fruit and cereal available for those who did not want a full breakfast. Near the hotel is the Holborn station, as well as Tottenham Court Road Underground stations. Both are about a 10 minute walk from the hotel. The hotel is on the back side of the British Museum which makes it very easy to locate on a map. Also near the hotel are a few supermarkets. The biggest one I found was just a few blocks down by Holborn. There is a little cafe called the Forum nearby which has a decent menu of sandwiches and coffees for a meal. We went to the Museum Pub which was about 2 minutes from the hotel for our night-cap pint of Guinness. For pizza nearby, we walked to La Porchetta. Decent pizza at a reasonable rate. If I were to come to London again I would most certainly stay in this hotel. I would suggest this hotel if you are looking for something at a decent price. The owners were friendly and helpful.

title: Location, location, location
text: My friend and I stayed at the Morgan two nights at the beginning of a two week trip to Great Britian and four nights at the end. Each time we shared a (different) satisfactory twin room on the first floor facing the street. The rooms and bathrooms were a decent size for London and had good storage, were clean, and had nice towels and bedding. The beds were comfortable but we needed ear plugs for sleeping (okay with us) because of the traffic on Bloomsbury Street. The breakfast room was large and pleasant

title: Great for the price
text: The property needs some updating but everything seemed clean. The room was bigger than I expected for London. We walked everywhere in the city from our room. Nothing spectacular but definitely serviceable. I would recommend to a friend.

title: great location
text: clean and friendly. Perfect location. Comfortable beds.

title: Did us well for two nights in London
text: We stayed here because we had stayed many years ago with our parents. Its quaint, Victorian (so yes older) yes rooms are tiny - very tiny, and be prepared to walk up stairs. We stayed at the top so it was 50 plus stairs up, but part of the adventure for us - we are both over 50 and enjoy a good workout. Thankfully the fellow checking us in carried our bags up for us! The full English breakfast was delicious. Wi-fi service is a bit spotty, and soundproof rooms are not going to happen. Snoring of the guests next door was quite annoying. There are no in-room safes, We shopped around for better value rooms, but for the price we paid we were happy.

title: A Real Find if You are in London
text: Great little hotel. Nothing fancy but clean, super location (you are right next to the British Museum). John goes out of his way to make your stay enjoyable. One small glitch: When we arrived, late in the afternoon, we were "greeted" by a member of the night staff that was borderline rude, curt and not very accommodating. He told us the manager would be in the next morning. Once we met John, everything turned around quickly. We had been warned about security in London but the Morgan keeps the front door locked at all times with video monitoring. We never felt insecure at any time, so I wonder if the warnings about London weren't a bit of an over reaction for this part of London.

title: Really nice and convenient hotel
text: Hotel in London, it was my second or third time there and on to my forth stay :D

title: Came through for us when BA left us stranded!
text: Thanks to British Airways, we were unexpectedly stuck in London in May and had to scramble for lodging late in the day. Luckily, the Morgan had a room for us. There are plusher options, but this hotel affords a central location and value for your £ rare in pricey London. I had to print out new boarding passes using the clerk's computer, and he was both patient and helpful in navigating RyanAir's intentionally will-to-live-sucking website. [Neither BA nor the circus-like RyanAir earn any stars from me, for what that's worth. Terrible.] We arrived at (or after) dinner time and left before breakfast was served the next morning, so we didn't have time to enjoy the room (very nice sized) or breakfast (which was quite good on my last visit). We hope to return for a longer stay in less-difficult circumstances and were relieved to find a room at the inn, and staff willing to go the extra mile after a long and difficult day in travel-hell.

title: The Morgan
text: What a great hotel. So close to Central London and so close to the London Museum. I loved this hotel, a family owned hotel, with warmth and friendliness and a great breakafast.. I will stay there again and again. Susan New Zealand

title: A nice and affordable stay at a great hotel in central London
text: Staff was quite helpful. We got a room at the very top of all the stairs and they helped us carry our bags all the way up. Room was small but cozy and felt neat and clean. Downsides to the room was that there was no drinking water in the bathroom. However, there was a new bottle of fresh water provided every day and if more was needed you could just head down to the reception/kitchen and they'd happilly give you another bottle directly from the fridge. The room smelled strongly of some kind of (I would assume) cleaning liquid which I didn't enjoy at first but it got better after we opened the window and vented the air in the room for a while. Sleeping quality was very good. Breakfast was alright allthough I found the rule about how the fruits from the fruitbasket in the breakfast/dining room were only allowed to be taken for eating then and there to be riddiculous.Still, the hotel had the British Museum, Covent Garden and various restaurants/supermarkets and Underground Stations within easy walking distance which is a huge plus. Overall it was a nice stay for our modest budget and we'd definately stay at this hotel again.

title: A GREAT place to stay in London!
text: GREAT location......GREAT staff....... We very much enjoyed the complimentary Full English Breakfasts, and the location in Bloomsbury is excellent for getting around the city. Comfortable room, and everyone was very helpful to a couple of "first timers" to London. Be sure to check out the Museum Tavern around the corner for a pint!

title: Very pleasantly surprised
text: Ideally placed within a short walk of Tottenham Court Road tube, the Morgan is easy to find. The passage to my room was narrow, but the room itself generous by London standards and everything was clean and in good decorative order. I couldn't see any tea & coffee equipment in the room, which is my only criticism. I'd booked a "large single" which had a comfortable double bed in it. I was only in overnight so didn't see if there was a guest lounge or similar. The breakfast room was spotless and service brisk and efficient. I was given a cooked breakfast which, while not huge was perfectly cooked to order. Near the hotel there are plenty of places to eat and you're a few minutes walk from Soho for nightlife. There's also a supermarket and Boots chemist nearby for anything you've forgotten. It's not the cheapest tarriff, but if you wanted a reliably pleasant place to stay this comes recommended.

title: Great location and breakfast
text: The location is fantastic so that you don't really even need the tube to travel to theatres, oxford street for shopping. The breakfast is wonderful too. Rooms are comfortable although room 210 may suffer from some noise from the street if you keep the window open. Overall, a very nice stay.

title: Great B&B, Great Proprietors and Staff
text: Stayed here for a total of 9 nights. We spent eight nights when visiting London and then a final night upon our return from Edinburgh before heading home. We had a wonderful large room in the second building for our first stay. It was much larger than the regular rooms, but not quite a suite. The french doors lead out to a little private garden. With tea/coffee making facilites and a fridge, it was wonderful for our stay. For our last night, we had a regular double room on the third floor of the main building. Smaller, but still very comfortable. The staff carried luggage up and down, so that was not a problem. Best thing about this hotel were the great staff: very helpful and always cheerful and friendly. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. The breakfasts were good and gave a great start to the day. Great location in a good neighbourhood. I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: VERY GOOD VALUE
text: This hotel is in an excellent position. It offers good clean accomodation and efficient, friendly service. No complaints. Cost was £130 b&b for a spacious twin room, good valu for this part of London. Walking distance from a lot of interesting places.

title: Great small hotel, close to British Museum
text: We stayed three nights at the Morgan, due to its proximity to our daughter's school, and the British Museum. The rooms are small, but very tidy. There is no lift, but the staff is very friendly and helpful, and the breakfast is a very nice treat. Excellent value for a great London location. Highly recommended for the value conscious traveler.

title: Wonderful stay in London, wouldn't change a thing
text: The hotel is centrally located on a busy street literally over the side wall of the British Museum (the walk to it is about 2 minutes, tops). It was about a 5 minute walk to the Tottenham Court Road tube stop (and Boots and some theater) and 10 minute walk to Holborn tube stop. I had a large single room with a queen bed for ₤85 a night. This included a full English breakfast of cereal, yogurt, fruit, eggs your way, bacon, sausage, tomato/mushrooms, coffee/tea, toast and juice. The room had two layers of windows, which kept the cold air and the street noise out sufficiently. The room was also sufficiently warm for an unusual cold snap the city was experieincing. I was hesitant about a room overlooking the street like that, but really didn’t hear the traffic at all at night, also did not hear any other guests other than when they came and left their rooms nearby. The bathroom is small but very clean. I had no problems at all with either the shower, the hot water or the toilet as others have mentioned. The bed was new and comfortable and clean as well. There was secure wifi in the hotel that I think I would have had to pay for but I picked up the free wifi from the Radisson across the street no problem. TV in the room had about 5 channels. The hotel is secure, with a locking front door that only guests with keys can access. There are no elevators but the staff helped me up and down from the second floor with my luggage, as well as out to the corner to meet my taxi when I left. There are plenty of pubs and a Starbucks around the British Museum. I had lunch at The Plough, which is nearby, one day and it was really very good. No complaints at all from me and I would return in a heartbeat.

title: Good value near the British Museum
text: We stayed at the Morgan Hotel for 3 nights in their first floor triple (a double with a single bed). Our room was a very reasonable price compared to others we looked at, but it was certainly not super spacious for three people. This hotel is very conveniently located to not only the British Museum, but to two Underground stops: Holborn and Russell Square. The Holborn stop is on the Piccadilly Line which runs directly from Heathrow to central London. It is about a 10 minute walk to get to the Morgan Hotel from the Holborn stop -- quite convenient, even with luggage. We loved being right next door to the British Museum (a must visit!), but found the restaurants in the area a bit lacking. The breakfast (included in the price) is unfortunately nothing to rave about -- same thing was served each morning and the eggs were quite dry. Nonetheless, if you are on a budget and you are hoping to be close to the traditional London attractions (Big Ben, Tower of London, Museum of Natural History, Buckingham Palace), the Morgan Hotel is a great launching point.

title: Great place to unwind after finishing the Coast to Coast walk
text: I wanted to spend a week in London to relax after 13 days hiking across England on the Coast to Coast walk. I'd requested a lower floor to please my sore feet and a quiet room to please my tired body. I had both. Perfect. The large single room opened onto a small patio, which would have been very nice in the summer. The location of the Morgan Hotel couldn't be better, and the price is hard to beat for expensive London. All in all, a great stay. Perhaps one word of caution: Bloomsbury Street is pretty busy. I suspect a room on the street side could really be uncomfortable.

title: Excellent location
text: I stayed with my parents in a triple room and it was more than I expected. Location excellent as well as the breakfast. The room was of a decent size but the toillet was really small and with no window nor air extractor. The carpet was a bit dirty and worn out which gave the room a poor appearance. Anyway it was good value for money

title: Excellent service, we´ll be back =)
text: What a nice long weekend trip we had! We enjoyed nice warm beds, excellent breakfast and so pleasant service located so near Covent garden comedy shows =) And my teenage son was so fascinated by international student athmosphere =) Thank you so very very much. Next time I will remember to take with me my own adapter for hair dryer

title: Excellent price quality!
text: Pro: + Location + Thick quality mattress + Spacious room + Clean showers and toilets + Price is really good for what you get - The lights in the hallway (toilet and shower) are with sensor and really strong so you're wide awake if you want to take a leak at night

title: The location was faultless
text: This accommodation is situated in the London school of Economics student accommodation building on High Holborn. The place is quite new and modern and your key is electronic. There were a lot of young people staying over the summer (obviously), however my wife daughter (adult) and I stayed here to go to a couple of shows. It is an excellent location and we had less than 10 mins to walk to our theatres. Leicester Square and Covent garden are around a 10 minute walk as well. The location was faultless. The breakfast was very good, even though it was continental, I was very full when I left. Cereals, plated meats and cheeses, yogurts, croissants, toast, tea, coffee, orange juice, boiled eggs, and all sorts of fruit. The only issue we had was the ablutions were outside our room! (The there is a sink in each room.) However they were right across a narrow corridor, but you are sharing them with 4 or 5 other rooms. No great hassle for us, but something to bear in mind! Overall I would definitely recommend this hotel for the money and location.

title: Unprofessional
text: As a person that works within the industry I have to say that staff is completely untrained on customer service, no confidence whatsoever on problem solving, state of shared bathrooms absolutely disgraceful (you would think if they are shared they would pay extra attention to the state of them), no feel of management giving direction to staff at all in fact I don't think there was any management or supervision present during our stay which would be normally fine if there was the sense of leadership in any of the staff, place is super messy in all areas including the canteen where it wasn't being cleaned consistently during breakfast. I understand it is hard to keep a nice smell in the building while it is so big and there is no windows in the halls however even a simple air freshener would work and make such a difference! Rooms were fairly clean during check in however after the experience in the bathroom you definitely look at everything in more detail hygiene-wise. The reception is super messy- you can see papers, boxes, everything out in the open which obviously doesn't give a great welcome especially when you see none of these things were well organised. Not to mention the keys to the room are really easy to get lost or are being left in the room - if they are this small they should at least attach some kind of card with room number or hotel information so that they are easy to spot. Not to make it all seem bad..the location is absolutely great! In between two underground stations. You can walk around and find super dinner/bar or shopping locations. The stay is not super cheap or not super expensive which is good especially for only a few days stay and especially with London Accommodation prices, breakfast choice is nice but there was items of English Breakfast missing for sure which was a little bit disappointing. Even if there is more domestic tourism involvement to the place... come on! Who wouldn't want to have a full on English Breakfast in the morning? Concluding: - Staff means well and is helpful enough but need more training in most areas of customer service. -Cleaning and organisation of public areas needs improvement. -Great location for short stays. -Cheap enough accommodation.

title: Cheap and Cheerful
text: I've stayed here twice now - once for a necessary trip to London and another for pleasure. Both times I was satisfied with my stay and it does exactly what it says on the tin. These are student halls, meaning you get a nice, basic room in a fantastically central location (often with a shared bathroom). Both times I didn't encounter any problems with noise (I stayed for two whole weeks in 2015 as well) and there are plenty of facilities on site too (I did my laundry here). I should also note that the breakfast is an excellent spread. Recommended.

title: Unexpectedly awesome!
text: We booked this room with clear expectations that it was pretty basic but excellent location. Hotels.com disappointed with their vague description & incorrect advice (breakfast incl: it wasn’t

title: Dirty!
text: The location of this hotel is really good, as it is close to the tube stations, Oxford Street, Covent Garden etc. We felt lucky at the beginning, but when we checked in to our rooms we saw that the sheets were dirty (there were short male hairs on the pillow), and the bin wasn't emptied. We told this to the receptionist in the evening (expecting that he would give us clean sheets), he only said that he would get the room cleaned the next day. However, the next day, after coming back, we saw that the bin was emptied, but the pillow cases were still the same! The breakfast and the location are good, but I won't be staying here again.

title: functional
text: great location, close to tubes and covent garden. check in was simple and the reception ok. a bit of a rabbit warren internally, but simple enough. room was clean tidy and bed comfortable. shower was good. bathroom could of been cleaner. breakfast was very good and well presented.

title: Excellent as a central base for London
text: Rooms basic but clean and perfectly acceptable, interesting newly refurbished showers with automatic light and sensors to start the water, buffet breakfast plentiful and healthy with a good choice of food. Useful to be able to leave luggage safely before the checkin time and on the day of departure. Three of us booked together and asked to be in nearby rooms but we were all on different floors, wish there was a way to book rooms close together. Very convenient for theatres and galleries.

title: Perfect location, excellent breakfast, great value!!
text: We just spent 2 nights at High Holborn LSE residence, with our children (10 and 14), and this was great value for London. For a family of 4, large rooms are hard to find, and 2 rooms usually blow the budget! In summer, High Holborn was available, and came to about GBP23 per person per night incl. 'continental' brekafast, which was a lot more than what you can expect, with fresh fruit, eggs, ham and cheese, yogurt, good juices, cereals, yogurt, etc... We had booked 2 'basic twin' rooms, which were clean and simple. The showers were not that clean though. The lounge dowstairs is nice to eat in, or just play snooker/air hockey/table tennis. Security is guaranteed with a couple of card swipe locations. Staff was very nice, and check in smooth. We were about 10 minutes' walk from Covent Garden/Leicester Square, perfect! Lots of shops, small restaurants/chains in the immediate vicinity. The 'Big Bus Tour' hopon-hop off stops at about 10 minutes' walk (Aldwych). Parking: we drove to London. DO NOT PARK at the NCP parking garage opposite the High Holborn residence (Travelodge hotel). Just go to Southhampton Row about 500m away, and park at the Imperial Hotel parking garage: it is half price (GBP 18), and you can stay 24/7. Note: The Bedford Hotel nearby will not allow you to park there on the week-ends! So pick the Imperial. It is expensive, but for London, a very good price. All in all, an excellent stay, we will be back!

title: Hotel Review
