text: I was in London for summer school at UCL and reluctantly decided to stay at their accomadation as my parents were not willing to pay the extra cost for 5 star accomadation. Well what a surprise! breakfast was great customer service was good, there was one guy in particular, tall, black I think his name began with the M? Really very polite, helful and smiley. I was so impressed, would definatelty recomnend this accomadation.

title: Great location and price but with trade-offs
text: The positive: location, location, location - right square in the middle of central London, 5 minutes to the British Museum, 10 minutes to Piccadilly - you can walk everywhere and save a ton of money on the Underground. Furthermore, it's decently priced for central London. The negative: Even though the building appears to be modern and renovated, the windows are your usual British/London nightmare - no sound or temperature screen at all. Expect to hear cars and drunks all night and be cold in winter. Due to the recent renovation, the building has been equipped with ecofascist features (don't get me wrong, I'm all for saving the planet but some things go too far). You cannot drink the tap water (I guess they use filtered rainwater or cleaned sewage). The shower is your classic "how does this work - oh, this way - wait, is this all? is this a pressure problem? aaah, it's a water saving shower" type of experience. We did not experience any room cleaning but we were staying only 2 nights so maybe that's common. Changing the towels would have been nice. Breakfast is included in the price but during our stay, breakfast was actually not available. Could have gotten a discount but didn't. The verdict: I've stayed at other LSE properties before. There are always some trade-offs but you can't beat the price and the location. For this reason, I mark this as 3/5.

title: great location, half the price!
text: Stayed here in May as I was attending a gig nearby. The property is student accommodation, but with a difference. I had a single room, complete with wardrobe, desk area and sink. I had use of a shared toilet and shower and fully fitted kitchen area, with crockery, cutlery, fridge, freezer and microwave. Great if you want to save some money and not eat out so much. There is a supermarket over the road, so easy to buy bits, rather than take them with you. The rooms were immaculate and great condition. It is within 5 mins walk of two tube stations, so position wise, really easy to get around London. The location is quiet and travelling alone, I felt safe. Will be staying here again.

title: Good low budget accommodation
text: I stayed for 3 nights and have no reason to complain. Of course my room wasn't pretty, but it was clean and practical. The shared toilet and shower were ok. The horror stories about student halls were not confirmed. But if you have very high standards this type of accommodation may not suit you. The breakfast was extremely good, way better than expected. All in all, for so little money you get satisfying accommodation in central London. It was very easy to get to all the major attractions and it is a nice area. Next time I am in London, I will go back.

title: Incredible value for location
text: First of all, this is a dorm and not a hotel. But I love its value and I'm not looking for luxury! I had a basic but clean single room for 4 nights and would stay here or any of the LSE accommodations again. OK, the bathroom's across the hall, the closest shower is on a timer (just press to keep water going) and breakfast didn't start until the day I checked out. None of that matters in the long run. The Holborn location is fantastic, close to great cafes (Drury Lane) for breakfast, right by the West End theatres, Seven Dials, Covent Garden and the British Museum. The front desk staff is fantastic and this is a great base for a stay in London.

title: Great breakfast and cheap accomadation
text: 2nd time I have stayed here and would definately do it again. In the heart of london, about 5min walk from oxford st and not much more than 10min to trafalgar sq. etc. Rooms very basic, a bed, table and small onsuite but what else do you need if going out all day sightseeing or theatre. They do this fab continental breakfast which goes from hard boiled eggs, cold meat, fruit of every discription, (kwiwi, pineapple, strawberrys, grapes, bananna etc), to yoghurt, choc au pain, toast and hot drinks and fruit juice. Talk about setting you up for the day. I would definately recomend this as a budget place to stay. If only for the breakfast. The guests tend to be very international and a mix of students( being uni rooms) and tourists. Out of all the accomadation the LSE supply to tourists this would be the one I would choose every time as its just so central.

title: Superb Value
text: Great value no frills accommodation in a very central location including a great breakfast buffet

title: Bring your own crockery
text: We stayed a week and it is very convenient for central London and very good value. That said, the kitchen was very ill equipped and I had to go out and buy a mug. The kitchen was clean , but had a strange smell. The light in the bathroom was on a timer and went out every time we used the shower so that was quite entertaining. There was a lot of building noise during the day, but most of central London is near some building site or another. We were separated from our 15 year old son as he was not just in another room, but on another floor and we could not access his room for which he was grateful. This was not made clear on booking and might matter to families with slightly younger children.

title: LSE = Location Simplicity Economy
text: It seems impossible to find an affordable hotel room in central London, especially when you're on your own. I'm too old to take my chance in hostels - and London ones don't seem that cheap to me anyway. So university accommodation is a godsend - stayed at LSE HIgh Holborn for the first time this summer & couldn't believe the location - reckon you could walk for 10 minutes in any direction and see most historic/cultural sights ! It was a treat to leave the theatre, walk back and be tucked up in bed with a cup of tea by 11 o'clock (simple pleasures....) Only stayed one week-night in late August and maybe I was lucky as I had no noisy groups for neighbours (didn't see anyone else on my corridor, in fact). I always take earplugs anyway but there was only a distant traffic hum with my courtyard room on 6th floor. (I asked for quietest room possible when I booked online) Room was clean and basic

title: Better than expected.
text: I booked a room here for one night prior to a flight from Heathrow. Being on the Piccadilly Line it's easy to get to the airport yet it's in the heart of London. I did not completely know what to expect but the experience was better than I had anticipated, and nobody could complain about the value for money, especially as a good buffet breakfast was included. The room was clean and although I did not use the kitchen (shared between about four or five rooms), I can see how useful it could be for some visitors, especially as there is a large Sainsbury's just a couple of hundred yards away.

title: Good benefit–cost ratio (for London´s patterns)
text: Hotel easy to be reached by Tube. High Holborn Tube station is the closest, but only for disembark (station in refurbishing). To embark, you should use Covent Garden Tube station (close to the LSE, too). I LIKED: confortable bed, breakfast, localization, no keys to open the door of the room. I DON´T LIKE: too many doors to reach the room, few bathrooms.

title: Good value for money
text: For such a low price its difficult to find anything to criticise. Room very basic but clean and bed surprisingly very comfy. Good variety of food for breakfast. Central location in Covent Garden but inside rooms very quiet. Overall very good and would stay there again

title: Location, location, location
text: This budget accommodation in the heart of London couldn't be beaten on location - it is perfect for tourists as you can walk or tube to the wonderful sights of London. It's located in Covent Garden so there is excellent shopping and places to eat, it's also close to all the theatres and the British Museum. Highly recommended. Our room had a double bed and was part of a 'flat' so there was a shared bathroom, shower and kitchen. The kitchen was excellent, unfortunately there is no drinking water in the room (sink with non-drinking water only) and the shower only runs for a very short time before you have to press the button again. There is also no air con. However, for the price and excellent location these aren't too much of a problem. The rooms are otherwise very comfortable, it's quiet and the breakfast is generous and very good. There is a laundry downstairs but you have to buy a card and credit for it.

title: Excellent budget accomodation in very central location
text: Stayed for 1 night in double en-suite room mid week for £88 B & B. The room was basic in that no TV, hairdryer etc but for the money was excellent value

title: One week stay in standard single room
text: I was in London for an internship so didn't really need much but a place to sleep and to be central as well. Paid about £200 and had breakfast included, sharing toilet. The room was very average, as you would expect. I was on 5th floor so not much noise going on. The shower room was separate from the toilet, but I suppose you don't need much luxury when you're barely living there. Had towels and room cleaned every other day. The breakfast was very nice, of a wide selection. The location is perfect for tube stations and even 20 mins to Oxford Circus, so really good! If you're looking for a place to crash after visiting/work and do not wish to spend time in the actual room then this is a great option!

title: Nice location!
text: The hotel is fine, clean room, good breakfast, eggs, good fruits, yogurt, cereals, good variety. Near British museum and oxford street, walking. Close to restaurants and china town, good location. 1 thing I didnt like, you can hear the slamming of the doors everytime someone exits the room, because doors are heavy and they close automatically, so that noise is very annoying when you are trying to sleep, other than that the rest is fine.

title: Location great, bed literally un-sleepable
text: Everything about the High Holborn Residence was what we expected. You're staying in a college dorm. The arrangement of rooms into "flats" was actually pretty nice. I think we would have enjoyed staying here if the mattress hadn't been such a horrorshow. We unfortunately did not even make it through one nap in this place. We arrived a bit early, waited for check-in, and then got our keys, eager to grab a nap. Upon laying down on the bed, my girl sank about 8 inches into the mattress. She weighs about 110lbs. When I got in next to her, we both rolled to the middle and bottomed out the mattress. I'm not overweight either. It had to be the cheapest, least supportive mattress I've ever laid on. We're not posh

title: Cheap and cheerful with great location
text: 4 night stay with my friend (we're in our mid 20's) We had a twin room. It wasn't the Ritz by any means but was a place to sleep and shower. Shared bathroom facilities with about 4 other rooms. Fantastic location near Holborn tube station and our room rate included breakfast which was a great selection of foods. For what we paid, other hotels in the same location were way above what we paid. Has a laundromat onsite which was great to clean our clothes. For the time we spent there and being in central London couldn't complain. We stayed there month of September and our room didn't have any air-conditioning which was a bit tough at nights however. However don't be put off if your after a great location and somewhere to sleep and shower.

title: location best tip
text: the bedroom was extremely basic just single beds an no tele or no wifi in rooms but it did have a nice kitchen on every floor for every 5 rooms, fridge/freezer, kettle, microwave etc, on lower ground floor there was plasma tv with sky channels, 2 pool tables, table tennis, breakfast was cold continental type, toast, cold meats/cheese, cereals, fruit .............. location very good between holborn an covent garden, next door oasis sports centre has 2 pools an gym very recomended, pub on corner doing great drafts beer an cider £5 a pint opposite a theatre too all left out hotel , for holborn tube an sainsburys/bank etc take a right out of hotel, 5 min walk

title: Cheap and cheerful
text: Good price, 5 minute walk from Cambridge theatre. Very obviously student accommodation in term time and seems to be run by students but very friendly reception team. Not keen on the shared bathroom facilities but clean. Continental type breakfast but plenty of choice.

title: Excellent value for money in the heart of London
text: Check-in was swift and easy, our room (a twin) was clean and had fresh linen and towels. Beds were comfortable. We had the use of a kitchen if we wanted. The room was a decent size, we had a sink and plenty of storage for clothes/bags etc. This is the perfect place to stay if you are spending a weekend sightseeing or are visiting London for business due to its central location and excellent value for money. The 24/7 hotel access via swipe card was extremeley useful as we were attending a festival that ran late into the night most nights. Individual 'flats' are swipe card access only too with meant i felt very safe. Breakfast was a good choice of fresh fruit (kiwi, strawberries etc..), cereal, meats, toast/crumpets/croissants etc and hot drinks. Im definately staying here again and have already recommended it to friends and family.

title: Clean up your act
text: I stayed at High Holborn in 429 from August 23rd - left 28th morning. The staff were entirely excellent and helpful, no complaints there. 429 had one operational shower instead of two. One working toilet in stead of two. The kitchen had a large pile of *used* crockery and cutlery piled in one corner which smelt. I though it was disgusting and put me right off even thinking of using the kitchen. Fortunately I found the J D Wetherspoons are good caterers. Breakfast was served on paper plates with plastic cutlery. Are we children? Try cutting a piece of pineapple which is hard, with a bendy plastic knife. What is this doing for your eco credentials LSE? Please wise up and get proper crockery and metal cutlery. Would I recommend this hotel to a friend. Not likely. In the room was ok, beyond that I gave up breakfast by later in the week and stuck with Wetherspoons. I couldn't face that kitchen except to heat water for coffee and feel sorry for the students. LSE, please clean up your act and get green. Otherwise it was fine for the money.

title: Great Location, Basic rooms
text: Had a girls weekend in London and stayed here. We couldn't check in until 3 but were able to leave our luggage in a room downstairs. Checked in and went to our room. 3 single beds and a bathroom. Comfy beds and pillows but basic room. No mirror, curtains were falling down slightly. It was cheap and we only spent time in there sleeping and getting ready. Great location and lots of shops and restaurants nearby. Walking distance to Covent Garden, Leicester Square, Charing Cross. If you aren't going to spend a lot of time in the room and just need a cheap bed with friends then I would recommend as location is so good. Staff friendly too!

title: good place for the price
text: I spent 7 days at High Holborn. I booked a Superior Single room. They are flats that you share with 3 other people (this is not very clear from the description) but the toilets and shower stay clean so I did not mind it at all. You have to use your key to get to the restroom and shower and another key to get in the hotel and other doors. Security is very good. There is always somebody on duty. All guests have to register but can not stay in the room with you. Breakfast is continental, with cold meats, fresh fruits, a variety of breads, boiled eggs, yogurts, juices, coffee, jelly. The location is perfect, two blocks from underground, Picadilly and Central lines. The Picadilly takes you to Heathrow airport in an hour for 5 british pounds. The low points are: no air or television in rooms. Sometimes it got hot and windows can not be open much in London

title: Fantastic location at affordable price
text: Use opportunity to return to summer school by staying at London School of Economics student residence. Be prepared for shared bathroom and for rich choice at breakfast. The place is perfectly managed, clean and modern

title: Excellent accommodation if you don't mind a little sharing
text: One night bed and breakfast for a single bed room in central London for under £80 is attractive. The photos are true to life as the quality of the rooms is excellent, although the bed is fairly spartan. No telly or tea-making in the room, but free and fast wi-fi is available, so you could watch or listen on-line. The shared toilet and shower is a bit cramped but clean - free toiletries are provided. Breakfast was healthy (i.e. no fry-up) and plentiful - fresh fruit, pastries, dairy produce, cheese, meat and drinks. The fruit juice was too sweet for my liking though. As many sharers are young students, the noise levels can be quite high and intermittent with running, giggling and doors banging encountered. There is also shared kitchen if you want to do your own thing.

title: Perfect location, good for the price!
text: The most important thing of this place is its great central location. You have the underground close, walking you can get to Convert Garden, London eye (20 min walk), etc. The place is quite and clean (at least the room I got), also the shared bathroom. The bed is a little short, so consider that if you are tall. The only bad thing, is that they only provide breakfast in the summer. I actually picked the place because I wanted breakfast included. Non summer travelers be aware of this! The people at the front desk are really nice and helpful, that is a plus. You can leave you luggage on the front desk for a day, without any charge. The internet works pretty good, and it is included

title: Completely Brilliant
text: I have paid out a hell of a lot more money to stay in hotels and have never had such a great stay as I did at HHH. The rooms were great, the staff were lovely, the breakfasts were fantastic, local was perfect, it was very clean, it was just brilliant. I will be going back the next time I need to stay over in London

title: Cheap, clean, central, no frills
text: I stayed here while down in London visiting friends. The room was very clean and basic but comfortable enough and it's excellent value for money given the location. The shower across the corridor was absolutely tiny and there's no wi-fi, but generally fine.

title: Excellent location
text: I stayed here recently with my daughter on a theatre trip. The location was fantastic only being 5 mins from Covent Garden and having lots of shopping and dinning opportunities on the doorstep. We had a decent room with new fittings which had a fresh, clean feel to them. The shared bathroom was clean but rather small but it was quiet and cheap so we were both happy overall! You are only a 20min walk from Euston station which takes you straight past the university and the British Museum. I would highly recommend this place.

title: loved it- its clean, safe, and absolutely unbeatable location
text: stayed there 2 nights

title: Tremendous Value
text: Great accommodation, great location, great price and the sort of breakfast you would expect in a 5 star hotel, I would recommend it to anybody. I will definitely be booking again. Only downside, the rooms are a bit too warm.

title: Great location, easy to access.
text: Convenient location for central London

title: Gloomy.
text: Book this place with your eyes wide open. Prices are cheap, sure. Location is fabulous, and covent garden is a few minutes away. But the tap in my room dripped constantly, the maintenance staff didn't turn up upon notifying the reception. The housekeeping staff were cheerful and friendly

title: Very good value for the location, but basic rooms and shared bathrooms.
text: I recently stayed there whilst on a business night out. I wanted cheap and convinient, and for £45 this was a good choice. Yes, the rooms are basic. Yes, it is a shared bathroom. But the rooms are fine, the bed/s were comfortable. The location was fantastic. Just on the edge of Covent Garden, and walking distance to all the tube stations such as Tottenham Court Road etc.

title: Basic, some problems but price and location made up for it
text: I was surprised when I found that LSE meant London School of Economics but London was full and it was cheap so I booked it. I was attending a course in Holborn and the location was perfect - 10 minutes from The City but also 5 minutes from Seven Dials, 50 yards from The White Hart, very, very central. The room was a basic student room with a sink, some drawers and a bed. A shower room, toilet and kitchen were a 10m walk up a corridor. The building was busy and well lit and had a good 'feel'. Bed was OK, it was quiet (I WAS on the 10th floor) so sleeping wasn't a problem. Now the downside. The tap in my room didn't work and neither did the shower down the corridor!!!! So not so great from a hygiene viewpoint. Breakfast was basic but all-you-can-eat. So some significant problems but overall OK for 40 quid. Luckily I could clean myself up at the training venue. I think with a less phlegmatic approach a complaint was in order but I wanted to get out and back to my course. All in all a pleasant return to student days with facilities to match.

title: Great location at a great price
text: Stayed for one night before catching a train from London and the single room was perfect for an overnight stay at a special offer price. Location is great for theatres, shopping, British museum and Covent Garden. The room was understandably spartan but clean enough. It was through a door also accessing the toilet, bathroom and kitchen and the door banged a fair amount but not late at night fortunately. I was very impressed with the continental breakfast considering the price - don't think I've stayed at any hotel with quite so much fresh fruit on offer! I'm not sure if I would stay for more than a day or two for a proper 'holiday' with family but the price could persuade me and for a night after a theatre visit or for passing through I certainly recommend it.

title: Great value, great location.
text: At £45 a night complete with breakfast you can't really go wrong here. I was working in Soho for this trip so the location was bang on. The room I had was extremely well maintained, clean and modern. The shared bathroom and shower on my floor was spotless too. As for the included breakfast there was plenty to chose from. We are talking continental style here, not a full English, but that is not a complaint at all as this type of breakfast is perfect before work. My main recommendation would be to request a room in the upper floors to reduce volume for the street level. However I can't speak for the lower floors as I was at the top!

title: Cheap and great
text: We found this place excellent in almost every way. The room was spacious (not common in London) and clean, the bath/toilet/kitchen facilities clean and tidy for the most part. Breakfast was simply superb

title: Great value and ideal location
text: Stayed there for 4 nights. Breakfasts in the morning were very relaxed. Room service handled everything perfectly. The shared bathroom/shower had me nervous at first but no trouble at all. A lot of shampoo's and conditions get left behind by guests so feel free to use some of that rather than buying your own. Managed to lose the key to my room and had a replacement key within 5minutes at no additional fee. Staff seem very helpful and understanding. Overall a great experience.

title: FIRST STAY, WILL BE BACK AGAIN SOON
text: We stayed for two nights at the weekend, and were allocated a room at the rear on the second floor, on arrival we were left our luggage in a room in the basement. At 3.00pm we went to our room and it was as anticipated a basic students room, we had two beds, cupboards and bedside draws along with a vanity sink. We had two windows overlooking a garden consisting of wild grasses. Four rooms shared a kitchen, toilet and shower which worked out just fine as most of us were short stayers and just used the room to sleep in. Breakfast was included in the price - £44 per night – which consisted of ten different fruits, bagels, croissants, breads, cereals, cooked meats, eggs and as much tea or coffee you can drink, in fact, enough to keep you going all day. It was our first visit and will certainly not be our last, all staff were helpful and courteous from front of house to the breakfast staff, in particular the man dealing with the luggage store. Well done and looking forward to my return.

title: dorm- perfect location
text: I actually live at this residence but I thought I would post a review to help travellers. This is a LSE student accomodation that turns into a hotel come summertime. Sinks in each room with telephone and high-speed ethernet connection in each bedroom, although I am not sure if this is available to hotel guests during the summer. Composed of flats of between 4-6 rooms. If you can, try to book a room on the Mezzanine floor as these have been recently renovated with brand new kitchens. Couldn't ask for a better location as is it three minutes walk to Covent Garden Tube, four minutes each to Tottenham Ct. Road and Holborn and walking distance to Soho, Leicester Sq., Piccadilly Circus, Waterloo bridge, British Museum etc. It's not luxury but if you want budget accomodations in the heart of London, this is your place. I consider myself fortunate to live here...I would pay triple if I wanted to stay in this area and rent a flat. Hope this helped!

title: Bit expensive
text: Stayed here With one of my friend for 3 weeks... The property was clean and the staff friendly .. However i found it a bit expensive and the cleaning service was also provided only twice a week.. The property is located in a very central area and places are easy to access.. Nice option for people who plan to study at LSE

title: Good value, but i was charged twice
text: Excellent value rooms, with a generous breakfast. Location is perfect for central London. However, i was double charged for one night of my stay. Be very careful when checking in or out, to make sure the details for your stay are correct. Also, when you return home, check that no overcharging has taken place. I really liked this accommodation, but after 3 weeks back home, am still waiting for my refund - be warned!

title: Great location!
text: We stayed at this residence hall for two weeks during the school break period in August-September 2005. The location is fantastic being a short walk to the theatre district, restaurants, and Covent Garden tube stop. All of the rooms are furnished with typical dorm style furniture (single beds). There are 2 ensuite rooms per floor which share a kitchen with the single "apartments" on each floor. The 4 or so singles all share a bathroom and shower room in the "apartment". Floor maps are available if you need a better idea of how this works. The building is run in a secure manor with a helpful front desk staff. Breakfast is plentiful but rather utilitarian--think dorm breakfast. Linens are changed each day. There is no high-speed internet access in the dorm rooms during the vacation periods. We used a phone card and slow phone connection. The price per room and location are the best features of this alternative accomodation in the center of London.

title: Theatre District convenient
text: I stayed at High Holborn Residence for 1 night in September 2010. It was well placed to go to Covent Garden and the Theatre. Room was small but comfortable. Continental breakfast included was full of variety and unlimited in quantity. Staff were helpful. Security very good - given swipe card to access building, room and shared bath & toilet. I would definited stay here again.

title: Good Value and Central Location
text: Sentimental value as I lived here for a year when I attended the school. For summer travel though, it is central, relatively cheap at 100 pounds a night (2 adults and a 4 year old), and comes with a decent breakfast. Would recommend it for location and for price.

title: Bottom line - great location and value
text: We arrived here with mixed expectations, based on the reviews. We were very surprised in a good way - our en-suite room on the 10th floor was completely new, very clean, large and comfortable. Unfortunately we asked for a double bed and the room had three singles, but we joined two of them together to fix that. The location is prime, a minute walking distance from the British Museum, Covent Garden, Oxford Street, and lots of theaters. Breakfast was generous and diverse and mostly tasty. Warm (even too warm) and strong water in the shower. Luggage holding services were great and felt pretty secure, and front desk guys were helpful. So basically, we had a very experience from what some of the reviews here describe, and I believe it's because we had an en-suite room in the upper floors, which are probably new. So if you have a chance, make sure to request that. Now for the bad: two elevators to service twelve floors and probably a couple hundred people is NOT enough. Each morning on the way down to breakfast, back up from breakfast, and down again to go out, it would take several long minutes to catch an elevator. Also, the bathroom was quite tiny (unlike the room itself), and the soap provided was less than adequate. The automatic on/off faucets were a pain to use and way too fast to shut themselves off. Other than that, if you can get a room at a high floor, and don't mind waiting for the elevator a few minutes a day, this hotel represents an excellent value for money option at a pristine location. Enjoy!

title: Pretty awful
text: To date, this residence is my worst experience in what would be defined as speciality lodging or something akin to a hostel (which essentially I compare it to). Firstly the positives

title: Never Again
text: Very disappointing stay. There were several issues – the only shower I had access to didn’t work, and there were no communal showers, certainly not on my floor. I was awoken at around 4am every morning by either roadworks, streetcleaners or both. The noise was absolutely unbearable. The card machines to work the washing machines did not work properly….at one stage I put in £4.60 to get a card to cover a wash and dry, however that button didn’t work but still took my money. I then had to get a £1 card to top up online, to find I could only top up a minimum of £5 – despite a wash and dry only supposing to cost 3.60. A very costly experience. Towels were not changed despite leaving them on the floor by the sink as requested. Also my key card was very hit and miss at getting me back into the building. Reception staff wouldn’t believe me when I said I had problems, even whilst demonstrating it in front of them!! Breakfast was cold buffet style but was very good, with a good variety of fresh fruit and amazing fresh porridge. The only good thing about my stay. All in all I was left shattered from barely any sleep in 8 nights, and certainly will not be returning.

title: Affordable Location in Central London
text: Rooms are basic dorm style. Breakfast is fine but nothing to write home about. But you can't beat the price and the location. Easily accessible from the Piccadilly line and a five minute walk for Oxford Circus and the British Museum. A great value for the money.

title: great budget stay
text: breakfast and location fabulous basic room matress and pillow could be better shower cubicle / toilet very small

title: Don't think it can be beaten
text: I've been in 3 different LSE locations and all of them are great. In fact, I plan my stays in London based on LSE availability. I travel on my own which make accomodation prices almost 2 fold in most places, so I can't afford/it's not really worth for me a Hotel, and my experiences with London Hostels are terrible, so LSE is like a savior for me. Rooms are simple but clean (same as bathrooms), secure and I really appreciate having access to a kitchen. Location is unbeatable, and breakfast is really good (I really can't understand the negative reviews below). All in all, best value for money.

title: Great Value
text: I have stayed twice at . High Holborn for 7-8 days each time. Clean safe, location convenient. Breakfast a little so so this past trip (Sept) adequate and included in price. But definately recommend. If u r an American lower your expectations. It isn't the Ritz. I stayed in one of the renovated rooms 1st floor it was very quiet. Enjoyed my stay. Staff very nice and helpful. lpful

title: I was scared for my safety.
text: I realise this was probably the cheapest option for staying in centrel london on a friday night but it really was very poor. The electrical plug over the desk was no longer attached, shower was freezing no hot water and with people walking around all night I was very concerned and barely slept. I spoke to the counter staff about the hot water and they did apologize but took no action. Glad I didn't choose this at my university.

title: Excellent location and affordable
text: Friendly and efficient staff and quick check-in. Clean room with the kitchen/shower room/W.C/bathroom opposite along the corridor. Breakfast is decent and the 24 hour security makes it stress free if returning after a late night. I stayed in two different rooms over two separate nights and the bed on the first night gave me back ache.

title: terrible service and dirty
text: I'm an LSE alumnus and used to stay in this student dorm a couple years ago. A few days ago, I was here for a conference at the LSE. The staff at the reception is incredibly rude and after a while one just gives up asking any sort of questions. All other travelers I met had the same problem with the staff as me. At the reception, they just don't want to help and they make fun of the customers, laughing sarcastically among themselves after any question and their "witty" comeback. Besides, there is supposed to be wifi in the communal area but one needs to know how to follow the simple steps to access it. The information they give you at the reception is incomplete and they do not care to try and understand the problem or ask an IT specialist about the proper way to inform the clients (fortunately fellow travelers help themselves...). The room was not very clean but the worst was the kitchen with its discusting plates and cutlery and the common shower (never washed by the cleaning staff apparently). the shower temperature can also not be changed and it's boiling. I will never go back to this dorm and feel ashamed to be an LSE alumnus after witnessing this appalling level of service and the image this dorm gives of the LSE.

title: absolute value for money
text: for 42 GBP it was a clean place to sleep for a night in Central London (a bus stop is right to the entrance that takes you to a major tube station, though one of these stations is currently under construction : "150 years London Underground"). the pros and cons: PRO: - flexible arrival/departure (though this does not appear on the hotels booking webpage) - high security : strong fire doors and 2 keys (one classic key for the room , the second one, a modern RFID system for the associated 5-room unit with common kitchen,toilet and shower). - I used toilet and shower , everything was clean. - quiet (at least during my stay) - modern lift (talking) - vending machines and large TV in breakfast/meeting room - luggage storage section in basement - 5 minutes foot-walk to a supermarket with relatively moderate price-labels CON: - you can only open the windows (at least in the 9th floor where my room was) for a bit: Depending on the selected opening angle (and wind speed outside) you get a wind noise that might disturb your sleep. - no house internal WLAN (but from the reception situation on the 9th floor there seemed to be at least one external commercial WLAN service available)

title: OK
text: Stayed here before and it left good impressions but this time much more average. Hair on pillows and duvet and room semi-clean but bathroom and toilet could have done with a proper clean. Breakfast was pretty good.

title: Great location, inexpensive, no thrills
text: I stayed at this residence (open to public thru LSE Vacations) in Sept 2013. It was exactly what you would expect for a university dorm: inexpensive, but noisy and no thrills attached. The rooms were tiny, as were the bathrooms, but it was definitely what I anticipated for only paying about £30 per night. Fantastic central location won me over. If you're looking to save some money and be in a great location -- fully understanding the tradeoffs -- I recommend it.

title: Good budget option for staying in London
text: Because if the location and price I found it OK for a short stay. The room was small and a bit worn out, so I don't think I'd like to stay there for more than a weekend. The location is convenient for theatres and sightseeing. Great choice of food for breakfast. The whole place feels secure and hassle-free, would recommend it if you're travelling alone.

title: Good value
text: For central London LSE High Holborn is a great deal. Simple but clean rooms. Good breakfast. Friendly, responsive staff on reception. Only very minor quibble: there were some dirty pots in the kitchen when we arrived which were still there when we left 6 days later. The communal kitchen could be good for people on a budget though as there is a Sainbury's 2 mins away with a good range of food inc ready meals. Fellow guests, friendly and well behaved (no drunken loonies). So, all in all, a big thumbs up.

title: Noisy inhabitants.
text: Kept awake until 2am with noisy neighbours who couldn't care less about the noise they were making. The toilet was dirty which was obviously used by these noisy yobs.The breakfast was excellent and made up for the lack of sleep.Staff couldn't be better.

title: Excellent location & cost
text: Fairly basic accommodation but for the price and location it cannot be beaten in London. How much time do you spend in your room anyway? You want somewhere safe and clean and comfortable. London is literally on the doorstep for theatreland.

title: another big hostel
text: Good location for tourism, which is I believe the only advantage of the Hall. About the other points, I have to agree with negative reviews. Wifi connection in the communal area was always unstable (mostly unsuccessful at least for me), and it seemed that the staff never bothered about this. And in the same area young people were always being noisy and making the place nasty, which amounted to the unbearable level. I believe any good youth hostel would allow this kind of behaviour. The way of serving breakfast was totally awful. They offered guests disposable cutlery and plates. Soon after the breakfast time began, dustbins became filled with used dishes and other materials (I would like to know how LSE think about the concept of sustainability). Besides, I never enjoyed the food itself, which didn't taste fresh.

title: It does what it says on the tin - practical, clean and cheap
text: This is a student residence with student style rooms and shared facilities, unless otherwise stated. The front desk very helpful, room clean, bed reasonable, large desk (compared to reasonably priced hotels), walls bare and showing many signs of previous adornments. You should note that there is no radio or TV in most (?) rooms, but if you make a booking with that in mind then you won't be disappointed. The shared facilities were right next to my room and I did not see or hear anyone else using them. A previous reviewer who talked of queing for facilties must have been unaware there was a map by the lifts showing where alternatives were located. The in-room information was very useful, even for someone who visits London reasonably regularly. If you want to self cater you have a good student kitchen available. The breakfast was continental style but extensive and of very good quality for what it was. There were plenty of staff around to keep the stocks replenished and the facility clean. In my view you could compare this to a Youth Hostel BUT with private single rooms. I have marked sleep quality as average because despite the fact my room did not overlook the road there were a lot of loud bangs and crashes from outside during the night which seemed to be concentrated by the building exterior shape and relationship to neighbouring properties. But this is London. In terms of location it is excellent for the West End - at the top of Drury Lane.

title: extremely enjoyed will be back
text: I stayed at High Holborn Residence from 29 August to 5September 2011. The Room was clean and there was hot water everyday. Large conti breakfast was provided every morning. All the staff were very helpful and friendly at all times. The weather was wonderful it rained only twice for a short period.Other days just wore a t-shirt.

title: Great value for central London
text: Reception staff were very pleasant and helpful. The building and the room were very clean as were the shared facilities. It's a 5 minute walk away from Holborn tube station and plenty of restaurants, bars and fast food outlets in the vacinty. Also, LSE is next to Oasis pool and leisure centre if you fancy some exercise. Covent Garden is also a five minute walk. Fantastic value for central London. The room was light and airy and had a wardrobe, desk, single (fairly comfy) bed and a sink... all you need if you just want somewhere to lay your head. Electronic key fob entry to the building, corridor and room felt very secure.

title: fantastic
text: Great location, close to 2 different tube stops (so various lines) and about a five minute walk to Soho, Oxford Street, and a tad longer to Trafalgar Square. Continental breakfast was fantastic, the rooms, facilities, and communal kitchens were clean and comfortable. Reception open all night, and everybody working at High Holborn (reception, cleaning ladies, breakfast crew, etc.) were all super nice and friendly. Truly an ideal place to stay

title: This accommodation is absolutely wonderful for central London, the service was second to none!
text: I have stayed at High Holborn several times and can't say enough good things about it. The location is fabulous and the breakfast is superb! The staff are very friendly, helpful and very knowledgeable. If you're looking for a great place to stay in the heart of London and are on a budget, High Holborn is the place to go if you want a warm welcome and fabulous service during your stay.

title: Generally disappointing...
text: Generally disappointing - shabby room (1109), kitchen and toilet facilities, uncomfortable bed, unclean pillow, noisy doors, had to ask for a cup and spoon for the kitchen as nothing supplied. I booked this as it said one step up from a hostel. In my opinion it is definitely one step down from the last hostel I stayed in in London. Only redeeming factors were good breakfast with lots of fruit, helpful reception staff and the location but would definitely not book in again. If there are two of you, you can get a discounted hotel room in the area for the same money.

title: Spend your money somewhere else.
text: The rooms have shared bathrooms disgusting, I got a room that had it's own bathroom for higher price, when I got to the room the Bed had been slept in and not changed, there was a dirty towel hanging on the shower door, the bathroom lights did not work, part of the ceiling was so full of mold that it was falling down, the room had no amenities, no TV no Radio nothing. I went back to get my money back and go somewhere else, this was Saturday was told could not get it refunded until Monday or Tuesday, got it refunded but was not full amount, Take Your Money and spend it somewhere else of course all of the LONDON HOTELS ARE OVER PRICED CRAP.

title: Excellent location - great price
text: I stayed here twice within a two week period. The first time was better than the second

title: Surprisingly good value
text: I had booked my daughter onto a Pre Law course on a Saturday and didn't fancy getting up really early to travel by car or train on the day. I visited laterooms.com and saw the High Holborn residence. The location from Euston and the University was excellent, in walking distance. We couldn't check in until after 3pm (which we knew about) but we went along to see if we could get in earlier. Unfortunately we couldn't but the staff were very helpful and friendly and offered to store our backpacks. When we checked into our room we were surprised how spacious and clean it was. I was a bit surprised we had a communal shower and toilet but it was fine (I've never been a student at Uni so it was a bit new to me!). Towels and soap were provided, another surprise, and breakfast was excellent value and catered for all tastes. All in all, a very positive stay and surprisingly good value for money.

title: Great Location & Price Despite Dorm Style Accommodations
text: We're the type of travelers that don't spend much time in the our hotel room and don't like to spend an arm and leg on hotels for this reason. We want clean and safe accommodations in a terrific location where we can walk and take in the locale instead of mostly traveling by taxis and subways. High Holborn meets these qualities. It has efficient and basic furnishings - we don't usually watch tv, and happy that we did not see one in our twin-beds room. There are no alarm clocks, so use your smartphone or bring a travel clock. You'll share showers, bathrooms/toilets, and kitchen (there's a grocery store - Sainsbury - nearby) with about 6 other people in your suite. We only had one other person in our suite, so accessing facilities weren't a problem. One more tip about the showers, just like a college coed dorm, you may want to bring your shower supplies of shampoo, condition, travel wash cloth or whatever gets your clean. You'll be provided a body and a hand towel, shower gel, and a small bar of soap. Loved that we were in the West End/Theater District. Everything is walkable (Convant Gardens, Leicester Square, Oxford Street, etc)! The all-you-can-eat continental breakfast is more than enough. Get to breakfast early to have dibs on the chocolate croissants! We would come back.

title: Great location and very reasonably priced!
text: The location was perfect for sightseeing in downtown London. We were able to walk everywhere we wanted to go, and felt safe on the streets, even after dark. The price, considering the location, was extremely reasonable. The room was a typical dorm room... sparsely furnished, but clean and adequate, it was fine for our 3 night stay. We were gone all day, each day, so being able to lounge in the room was not something we desired to do, anyway. (The room only had a bed, desk, bedside table, sink ... there was no chair). The breakfast was very good, with many choices. The large selection of fruit was amazing. We found the staff to be very helpful and friendly. Sharing the bathroom and shower, although not ideal, was not a problem. It seemed as if everyone was in and out in a timely manner. We plan to stay at High Holborn, again, if our travels take us back to London.

title: Great room and location for Central London prices
text: Cleanliness: The room and building are very clean. Room: Of course you should note that this is not a hotel room. It's a college dorm room that LSE rents out during university holidays but a pretty nice, relatively large one (at least my corner room was). Rooms are in flats so you share a full kitchen and bathroom with 4 other people (no common area in the flat although the building does have a pub and other common areas). Location: Excellent location. It is centrally located on High Holborn and equidistant from the Holborn and Covent Garden tube stations. The British Museum is maybe 5 blocks away. Safety: I felt completely safe at all times. Service: You get what you pay for so you should expect that everything is basically self-service although they do clean the common area. CONCLUSION: A great option for those in the moderate price range of Central London lodging (above a hostel but not quite a hotel). Location is unbeatable and you have access to really great nightlife in Covent Garden.

title: Stayed for Summer School. Met my needs
text: Elevators were kinda crummy. Otherwise, this was perfect for my needs. Nothing fancy, but totally functional. And great location if you like theater or clubbing. Almost all clubs and theaters are within a 10-15 minute walk. I stayed for 6 weeks for London School of Economics summer school and I was very happy, although I wish there were more common areas on each floor to socialize with flatmates and floormates.

title: What more can you ask for in this location?
text: Excellent area to stay in at low prices, though there's been a 10%increase recently and that will encourage me to visit London using this accomodation less frequently.Anyway with the prices at the time I stayed, breakfast included, a place to cook your own food, a student style area to relax, play pool etcetera and the proximity to the West End, really there can be no complaints. It's not luxury exactly, but it is a luxury at 28 pounds a night.Not your thing however if you want en-suite and won't instead use the wash basin for a night.

title: Very reasonable prices for great location!
text: I greatly enjoyed my stay at LSE High Holborn, and intend to stay there again on future visits to London. One thing to keep in mind when booking is that this is a student dorm, and thus you should not be expecting hotel-style accommodations. That being said, I was pleasantly surprised at the size of the room - there was a sink, closet, desk and chair, and bed. My one caveat is that the mattress in my room desperately needed replacing - I dipped down so far in it, that I ended up sleeping on top of one of the pillows to make it more comfortable! That is the reason I am giving four stars. The rooms are set up in suites of six

title: Great Location Terrible Rooms
text: We were actually pretty lucky to stay in such a great location. But I must say we were very disappointed with the rooms. The sheets on the beds were dirty, the trash wasn't emptied out, and it was so dusty we couldn't stop from sneezing all the time. Breakfast wasn't too bad.

title: London High!
text: Had stayed in High Holborn during my course in LSE.. Stayed there for a month or so... Great location and amazing value for money.. If you just a bunch of guys travelling in UK then such places are excellent.. Just 5 mins walk to Oxford Circus and Covent Garden!! Well connected from tube station where the red line works.. they charge you aroun 45 pounds a day and has great view on the front side! Have their own canteen, Gym, Bar, etc

title: Pleasant stay at LSE High Holborn
text: The rooms are nice and clean although it's a little small for twin sharing. Breakfast was great. Strategic location in central London. Good security.

title: Great location
text: While the room (superior double, shared toilet) was small, it was a great price given the location, within walking distance of British Museum, Trafalgar Square, etc. Besides, we only used the room for sleeping. Wi-fi never really worked for us, which was frustrating. We'd log on to webmail, and wait 5 minutes... Breakfasts had lots of choice, although the disposable dishes meant lots of garbage.

title: Lousy WIFI
text: Wifi is dodgy in the common areas, weak signal, password/login changes seemingly randomly, which means a trip to reception for current codes,when they have time and inclination to help. NO wifi in-room, although the wired LAN can be hacked. The rooms facing the street are NOT noisy, unless you fancy yourself a descendant of the princess in "the princess and the pea". Good kitchen with some cutlery and crockery, large refrigerator and an iron. Breakfast was diverse and copious, absolutely no complaints about the food. Ten minutes walking time to the British Museum,twenty to the National Gallery, thirty to Parliament or Buckingham Palace. Great location and value for money.

title: great location, excellent value for money
text: the location was fantastic, 5-10mins walk from the tube station. possibly another 15-20mins to Oxford Street. we even tried walking from Chinatown back to the hostel (which took us about 20-30mins) so that was how convenient the location was. room was clean. it had 2 single beds and a sink. there is a wardrobe cupboard too but there weren't any hangers so it was kinda pointless really. would have appreciated a hanger of some sort to hang the wet towels after we showered. the communal toilet and shower was clean

title: good location
text: good location but breakfast not all that good cold buffet not what one is looking for in a cold and damp london would be nice to have warm breakfast

title: Good location, no-frills accomodation
text: Was here for a couple of nights in August. The location is excellent, really close by to the British Museum, Covent Garden and other attractions. The 'economy twin room' I stayed in was essentially a single room with an extra bed put in. Pretty no-frills standard cheap mattress and all, which was okay for a couple of nights but would have been a bit uncomfortable had we stayed longer. The shared kitchen was convenient - we used it to heat up takeaway meals. Their 'eco-friendly' fancy shower was a bit odd as it was poorly ventilated and I was getting short of breath after taking a warm shower inside. Breakfast food was alright, but do agree with other reviewers' sentiments regarding the disposable cutlery -- the trash stacks up really quickly. Luggage storage was useful.

title: Perfect location
text: I found this by chance and was not disappointed. I stayed one night as I went to see the musical Rock of Ages which was across the road. I paid £30 and it was excellent value as breakfast was included. The room was very basic as you would imagine and the toilet and bathroom separate from the room but that was fine. I slept very well there. Check in was great and the guys on Reception were very helpful. I would highly recommend it and definately stay again.

title: Excellent service,excellent location
text: I spent two nights at this hotel for business in London. I have used it before prior to recent refurbishment. The improvement is significant. The service is impeccable and it is a clean and attractive hotel. The staff are well trained,courteous and friendly and it sits on a corner of Trafalgar Square. The rooftop bar has fantastic views all over historic London. A great choice for business or tourism.

title: They are getting it right all round!
text: Absolutely fabulous! I love The Trafalgar! This was the first time I stayed here and won’t be the last! You feel happy as soon as you walk in. The team is all smiles and all so ready to help and make you feel welcome. The people at the top seem like they got it right and are keeping their team happy, enthusiastic and motivated. Everyone is SO friendly. They clearly enjoy what they're doing. Well done guys. Keep it up! I loved everything about my room – décor, cool Tom Dixon accessories and coffee table books, lush Molton Brown toiletries, the view of Trafalgar Square, fresh milk in the free mini bar! It’s all in the detail! The food and service at the Trafalgar dining rooms and bar is tops. Really tasty and fresh. Needless to say, it was service with smiles all round. Really cannot fault anything! Thank you Trafalgar Team for making my stay such a great one. I cannot wait to be back next month! Ingrid x

title: 2nd Stay - Same Fantastic Experience
text: Again, the staff was fantastic from the waitstaff at the rooftop restaurant to the helpful concierge (especially Ippy) and bell staff. This hotel has every detail figured out and the location across from Trafalgar square is tough to beat. Highest recommendation.

title: Classic luxury in a great location
text: This hotel is very well situated at the corner of Trafalgar Square. The checking desk is a bit hidden away in a back corner behind the restaurant, if you enter from Cockspur St, but trust me it's in there. The rooms have an opulent feel with modern amenities: your own personal nespresso machine and tablet! There is also a lovely, very small, roof top bar. Concierge service was excellent but I would advise avoiding the restaurant on street level. Breakfast buffet was serviceable if you don't take into account the not easily accessible bar counter but the a la carte menu was a total disappointment. With these prices you would expect some basic culinary skills and use of spices but sadly all flavour was absent. Luckily there are other shops and restaurant in the immediate vicinity. I do recommend the hotel, however.

title: Great Hotel in center of London
text: Great Hotel, location, staff, amenities! Wonderful six days of vacation in heart of London. High quality hotel, wonderfully quiet rooms and truly excellent staff in all areas of this hotel. Excellent value and quality was consistent for our entire stay!

title: Top-Notch Service and Location!
text: I planned our 10th Anniversary trip and narrowed it down to one of two hotels (the Trafalgar St. James - and the Sofitel down the street), ultimately choosing the St. James Trafalgar based on location and the fact that we are Hilton Honours members, and I'm so glad I did! We were greeted by Andromahi at front desk. She was very pleasant and we were lucky our room was available a tad early as we were exhausted from the long flight and wanted to freshen up before venturing out. Upon returning we had a note from the manager with a bottle of wine and some incredible dessert to celebrate our 10th Anniversary. What a wonderful gesture and truly made our celebration that much more special! We had the St. James Family King Room. It was very spacious with plenty of extra room. The Nespresso Coffee machine was excellent (admittedly I couldn't figure out how the pods dropped in at first, since my machine at home is different) - but it was delicious coffee for a great start (and end!) to the day. The bar fridge was also complimentary, offering water, soft drinks as well, which we did use a few times. We had a tub and shower with good water pressure. There were robes, slippers, ironing board and hair dryer available to use as well. There was also a separate seating area with a couch and a small table. The room had a good sized safe, and enough drawers and closet space to unpack our clothes. We didn't have the greatest view, but I didn't care much as we were barely in the room. Location was excellent. I always felt safe day or night, it was steps to Trafalgar Square. Most of our day tours would have their starting points within a quick walking distance from the hotel which made it that much more convenient as well. Subway was nearby - but we truly walked everywhere! (or cabbed it back when we were too tired!). It was so easy to venture back to the hotel as it was in the middle of everything! Staff is incredible. They truly made us feel like we were part of the family. Ibby was always helpful, always greeting us with a huge smile. Helping us when we had some concerns with our transfer back to the airport (as roads were closed for a marathon and we were worried about our car hire getting to us!). You were always greeting with a smile from everyone, which was well received after an exhausting day of touring! They even brought our uber eats up to our room for us one night as we were in our pyjamas already (and truthfully could barely move our legs after 8 hours of non-stop walking around the city)! The uber driver would not be able to come up to our room, since you do need a room key to activate the elevator for security! So we appreciate that the hotel staff brought our order up for us! We didn't eat too often at the hotel as we weren't always hungry when we woke up with our time change and all. There's a Pret-A-Manger next door as well as a café Nero if you're in a rush. Although we did manage to eat our last day at the restaurant and we ordered a Traditional English Breakfast and it was truly delicious! I'm so happy that we stayed here - everything was perfect! Don't question it - just book!

title: Lovely wedding anniversary visit
text: Already thinking about our next visit ! Came across the Trafalgar and was drawn in by the rooftop bar, general look and oh yes the sale offer!! Despite a bit of a bumpy interaction to get a bottle of bubbly in the room on arrival (phone don't email) everything else was spot on - room upgrade so we could just about see Nelsons column, chocolate congratulations cake, rooftop bar and food was great, breakfast continental more than enough but didn't stop us having extras both days - haddock omelette especially good. My only niggle was that on both nights there were private functions in one of the bars delaying service and preventing access all areas - the staff looked after us but its just something for the hotel to remember they are a hotel and to always put the residents first. Looking forwards to coming back in the summer and testing out that rooftop bar again!

title: Superb!
text: Superb hotel. There couldn’t be a better location in London for me than Trafalgar Square. I walked almost everywhere I wanted to go. The room was beautiful, clean, very quiet, high quality furniture, bedding, accessories, free drinks in mini-fridge. I loved that I could choose my own room so I could select one with a separate tub. Staff was wonderful. In room dining tasty and convenient. WiFi flawless. Just a perfect place to stay. But, of course it is pricey. I will happily stay here anytime I can afford it and will be on the lookout for great deals. A+

title: Great location
text: This hotel is in a great location and hotel room is extremely comfortable. Most importantly there is air conditioning! It was hot when we were in London and this is a bonus. Overall great place to stay but staff is a bit stuffy.

title: Fantastic Location
text: We stayed at this hotel for three nights. We had booked online via Expedia a King Room (St James) based on the descriptions they provided of the rooms. The staff who greeted us when we arrived and assisted us with our luggage were very welcoming, helpful and friendly, as were the staff at reception. When we arrived just prior to 12.00 pm we were very fortunate to find they had a room of the category we had booked already available. The room to which they escorted us (with our luggage) was lovely (number 406) but contrary to the description provided for this room on the Expedia website, it did not have a deep soaking bathtub but rather only a walk-in shower. After we had checked in and found that the room had no bathtub, I reviewed the information Hilton provide on their own website about this room, and they state that the room category has a walk-in shower. Given that we specifically booked that room to ensure the availability of a bathtub, we made a call to reception and chose to pay to upgrade our room category to a Family Room (St James) in order to access the facilities we were seeking. A room of this category was not available at the time, but we were told if we would like to go out, we could leave our luggage in the original room and it would be moved for us upon a room becoming ready. Our new room (419) was also a lovely, clean and spacious room and as advised, our luggage had already all been transferred over to it for us when we returned later that afternoon. As far as the location of this hotel, we found it to be exceptionally convenient to major attractions, eg the National Gallery, the National Portrait Gallery and Trafalgar Square as well as very close to the Charing Cross tube station. In addition, it was within easy walking distance of St James’s Park and Horse Guards and is also close to many London theatres. We had a continental buffet breakfast in the restaurant on one morning, but decided that we would prefer to avail ourselves of other facilities in the area for breakfast on the other mornings. Although there is a reasonable range of foods available, we felt that it was probably better value to dine elsewhere. All in all though, because it was so centrally located and the room was modern and clean with air conditioning and access via elevators, we would be happy to stay at the hotel again in the future.

title: Beautiful hotel, but expected more
text: I had such high expectations of this hotel. It was very clean, our room was nice and the beds were comfortable. It is ideal if you're looking to be centrally located. Unfortunately, we had booked this hotel in part for the rooftop bar and view and we didn't really get to utilize it. I would recommend asking if it will be open your entire stay if you want to spend time there. There were private some private events during our stay closing off a portion of the roof. The front desk staff did not realize that we were guests of the hotel so they were not accommodating until we noticed they let other guests upstairs and we re-approached them. To be honest, my friends and I did not feel very welcome at this hotel. We were often mistaken for public coming to the bar instead of guests and were stopped every time we entered the lobby before being able to proceed to the elevators. We stayed for 3 nights and this happened throughout our entire stay. Despite this, I did want to mention that I had a great experience with the concierge team when I had a package mix up (I had been traveling and a phone was being delivered to the hotel, which arrived after I checked out). I greatly appreciated their help forwarding the package onto me!

title: A phenomenal hotel in the heart of London
text: This was my first time overseas and this hotel was absolutely incredible. My wife and I decided to go to England for our 10th anniversary and we had the best trip we’ve ever had. My brother and his wife had stayed here in 2014 and they said how wonderful this hotel was. They were definitely right by saying what they said. That made our decision in where to stay so much easier. The staff at this hotel was wonderful. The room was big and spacious and clean. There are a lot of restaurants and sightseeing attractions within a close proximity to this hotel. And we paid a rate that was affordable. We will definitely return again if were ever London bound again. A+ stay

title: Excellent Room & Location
text: Pros: Excellent Room. Very Well-Styled & Bathrooms looked chic. Location is right beside Trafalgar Square Near Tube Near Cafes & Restaurants Mini Bar Goodies were free and were refilled daily. Cons: Breakfast buffet had the most limited selection compared to any 4* or 5* I've experienced. Ate only ONCE during our 8 day stay, and selections never changed. Ate dinner at the restaurant, and the steak I ordered was served close to well done, as opposed to medium rare, and tasted bland. But the waiter was excellent! Definitely would stay again, especially if rates are reasonable. Hopefully they would fix the buffet spread!

title: Best location and beautiful room for 4 adults
text: We all loved the Trafalgar. The location is unbeatable, the roof top bar is spectacular. They even had blankets for your legs if a bit chilly. The room was large enough for four adults and very comfy beds. The free mini bar was a plus. You can walk everywhere to sightsee with no need for a car or parking. The bar waiters were fun and made excellent gin and tonics. We booked for 2 nights but extended for a third it was that good.

title: A hotel with difference
text: This is a hotel with difference.Although 5 star hotel but one notices many differences. The rooms are spacious with 2 chairs to sit,the directory of services is on a tablet,the TV is very quiet but modern,even the shower has an on/off like electric switches rather than a turning handle or a knob. The electric kettle is a china tea pot which is pleasant and we are thinking of buying one for our home ! The safe is hidden in the drawers,the storage space is adequate for clothes and belongings. Soft drinks and chocolates are provided in the room bar and included within the price. The breakfast had usual good choice in the continental but also had the unique feature of offering one cooked dish even for vegetarians it was great! One unique feature was 6th floor open space bar which is well worth visiting,it has good seats in the open area and the blankets are provided. The view is excellent specially around X mas with lights. The staff are really helpful. Overall, a different hotel with refreshing experience.

title: Very Good
text: I visited this hotel for a business trip for 6 nights with 6 of my colleagues, while 2 of us had bad experiences, the rest of us loved the hotel. The rooms are very comfortable, mine was on level 1 and I could not hear a THING and slept soundly every night in a very comfortable bed. It is a great location, close to Piccadilly and st James, with great food and shopping nearby.

title: London ,Hilton Curio
text: One of The quietest rooms i ever slept in. Mr. Howard at the concierge desk was the most helpful person I have ever worked with. The whole staff was helpful and professional. How else do you describe the feeling when 4 staff members walk you out to car and say goodbye and hope you return soon.

title: This is the place to stay.
text: I took the red eye from Dallas. They let me check in at 9:30a and sleep. Great place. Near everything. Cool roof. Great room. Go to the play “Come From Away”. Go to soho. Ride on the London Eye. All in walking distance.

title: A Royal Treat
text: Booking this hotel was the best decision of our family trip. Working with Ibby, the concierge, helped make our stay memorable. He helped secure theatre tickets and reassured us of our plans and gave us plenty of options. Adrian was also fantastic as was our breakfast waiter. The breakfast was delicious and what a way to start our touring looking over London from the rooftop. It was our anniversary and they acknowledged our special day! Best part for our family was the room. It is almost impossible to find a two queen rooms abroad yet this hotel has it all. Large comfy beds, spacious bathrooms and the view of Trafalgar Square. We think the hotel is in the greatest location for touring the city. Close to everything and walked everywhere. We definitely stay there again!

title: Five stars
text: Location - right where you need to be for shows, sights and anything else you need to do in central London. Service - staff are amazingly hospitable, welcoming and friendly. A gentleman on reception who helped with our bags particularly stood out to us - he had a Thai bracelet on - hope that narrows it down a little - he’s a great asset to your team. Facilities - felt like there was no expense spared. The rooms are of the highest quality I’ve seen. Minibar is complimentary and replenished daily. Fresh milk for tea/coffee. Molton Brown toiletries. Duck down feather duvets and pillows. Egyptian cotton bedding. You name it, it’s there! Rooftop bar - arguably worth the higher price tag for the view - around £70 for 4 cocktails! We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and would definitely stay here again - thank you.

title: Ravishing Revamp
text: Top marks for a much needed and expertly executed refurbishment! Just what this iconic building required. The rooftop bar is a hidden gem in this city and the lobby bar is worth a visit in itself. A perfect hotel in the perfect location for a central London visit.

title: Great location, clean rooms
text: Very well located hotel, walkable distance to many attractions, shopping and restaurant. Rooms was clean and spacious with complimentary mini bar. Very modern and chic hotel. Must visit the rooftop bar where you can have an overview of Trafalgar Square. There's a parking at the back of the hotel but parking is quite expensive, if you are driving in city area do remember to chk for a congestion charge fee in London. Would recommend friends at this hotel! Thank you for the wonderful stay!

title: PHENOMENAL
text: I simply cannot praise this hotel and its staff enough. Whilst being a member of several hotel programs I have never experience such service, courtesy and exceptional attention to detail. The service is unrivalled, you will not find staff with a greater desire to help than you do at the Trafalgar St James Curio Collection. Nothing is too small, every little detail is significant to staff. Two member of staff who need recognition are Dafne and Westley, they pulled out all of the stops and made my stay the most memorable I have ever had, I cannot thank them enough for this magical experience. Further thanks goes to Elodie and Federico as well as the rest of the wonderful team for their efforts and attention. The location is perfect with many rooms having direct views onto Trafalgar Square, which is such a satisfying and beautiful view. If your room doesn't have this phenomenal view then the roof top bar certainly does. Sensational views. The food is delicious and the restaurant service was great. One of the best starters I have ever had, (try the Italian beef). On one occasion there was a slight delay with my main course. Nevertheless, it was a minor delay and given the quality of the rest of the stay this issue did not ruin it in anyway. The Landseer suite itself, was one of the most beautiful accommodations I have ever seen. Open plan suites are far superior and inclusive in my opinion than segregated room suites. They provide the guest with a much more grand and satisfying experience. A slight issue with cleaning, a couple of missed areas and a couple of minor maintenance issues but again nothing on a scale that could not even come close to dampering the stay. On the whole the stay was wonderful, and even though there was a couple of MINOR MINOR issues, it is still the best stay I have ever had in any hotel. Furthermore, many thanks for the extra support and efforts in celebration for making it to Diamond membership! I will clarify that these minor issues I mention are only down to the rebranding and reopening of the hotel. It is entirely natural and expect that a hotel in its first year of rebranding/opening occur some minor issues (teething problems). Being someone who has experienced a lot of hotels, it is natural. My opinion of this hotel is NOT diminished in anyway by these tiny setbacks. I cannot thank the team at The Trafalgar St James enough. It is an incredible hotel with exceptional staff and I encourage EVERYONE to visit this phenomenal establishment! THANK YOU CURIO TEAM! A wonderful stay!

title: Fantastic hotel, great location, great amenities!
text: Perfect hotel for our short stay in London. The hotel itself is beautiful and the staff are beyond helpful. The restaurant/bar, rooftop all exceeded our expectations. And the gym was great. Will definitely be back next time we’re in town.

title: Very Nice
text: We stayed here for 6 nights for a family vacation in London. Terrific location, very friendly and helpful young staff. Well appointed with nice rooms and facilities, including nice small gym. Very clean with exceptionally fast room tidying. The breakfast in the restaurant is excellent but the service in the restaurant is pretty horrific despite a lot of wait staff. Baffling for an otherwise very well run place. We were very happy.

title: Fantastic location and Great Staff.
text: Great rooms and amenities. The staff is extremely helpful. The hotel is perfectly located for access to the buses and tube. Make sure to go up to the rooftop bar and have a cocktail in the evening. The view is great.

title: Wondrous - As usual
text: The Trafalgar St James ceases to amaze. Once again, truly wonderful service, product and staff. The Trafalgar St James truly creates a wondrous place in peoples lives. Special mention to Fabrizio, Adrian, Miklos and the entertaining Irish man milling about the lobby. Can’t wait to go back...

title: Perfect
text: So big news for visitors to our Capital-here is a hotel which is as good as you had always hoped. No rudeness, tiny overpriced room and sloppy service here. Praise be! In fairness to Hilton they are getting a lot right here-their Southwark and London Bridge venues are great too. Location is movie location ideal. Main door Trafalgar Sq and the magnificence of Nelson and his column. To the left Mayfair, to the right Theatre Land, Soho and Covent Garden. Tourists’ Position A. Check in and Check out personal friendly and attentive. In London? Oh yes. Concierge so good he gave vital heads up on the non running of Heathrow Express the day of our departure. Life saving. Certainly flight saving. Forever in his debt. Rooftop bar to die for. Residents’ privileges too, as it should be on a busy holiday weekend. Lunch and evening drinks great. Service just bedding in here. Easily sorted. No fuss Room my partner described as “the best and most thoughtfully appointed room”. Everything you could wish for, where you want it. Ask for room with view. Not those that look into opposite office block. We moved. Once again. No fuss. Customer satisfaction matters. Yay!! Finally!! These customers will return. That’s what it’s all about right?

title: Faultless
text: Visited in March with my sister. We had a great time and this hotel is absolutely faultless. The staff are friendly and very helpful, rooms are spotlessly clean and comfortable. We could not ask for more. We look forward to visiting again.

title: Fantastic!!!
text: Truly amazing and perfectly located. The staff did an amazing job taking care of our every need. The room was the perfect size and amenities were fabulous. We will be back and strongly recommend staying at this Hilton property!!!

title: Awesome location
text: Great property with amazing location .The rooms are large and clean . Really nice rooftop bar.Staff are great .We had issues with a/c and they were very responsive and got us a fan to help. The rooftop bar is really very good.

title: Wonderful
text: My husband and I booked here for my 50th birthday celebrations, we had an amazing time, the staff were very professional, not only is the hotel chic and leaves you wanting for nothing, they also gave me a lovely birthday surprise of the most amazing chocolate cake and macaroons beautifully presented along with a bottle of wine - this lovely touch really added to my special treat. We will be back, already looking to book in December, this is a must for anyone who likes to feel a touch of luxury, central and ideal for anywhere

title: Classy
text: From the moment we walked through the door until we left we cannot fault this lovely place. The staff were very friendly and helpful, we got there really early to leave our bags but we were able to check in there and then, aided by an excellent front desk lady. The room was just lovely, two very comfy doubles for hubby, me and 5 yr old and the bathroom was lush with a tub deep enough to swim in and a power shower. Room was spotless too.
