Its very convenient just down road from British Museum and taxi rank right by museum. Very central to London. Will definately stay there again as its very reasonble. They have a general lounge with a tv so no tvs in rooms but we were never there so suited us.

title: Will stay again
text: I just wanted a clean place to stay in the area as my usual place was full. It was clean, cheap and good value. The staff were friendly and the breakfast good. It a good location for tourists on a budget (I'm a Londoner living in exile!). The area has good transport links and was handy for the events i was at, including the TALF meeting!

title: London Weekend
text: We wanted a cheap but decent hotel in the centre of London's attractions and that's just what we got! We stayed three nights - the staff were all VERY welcoming and helpful - room was sparse but VERY clean and tidy. 15 min walk from Euston train station, next to British Museum, 10 min walk to Covent Garden, 20 min walk to St Paul's Cathedral & so many other great areas, most theaters walk-able from here too. We will most certainly use this great value hotel again in the future.

title: Spartan.
text: Good location, nice quiet street, friendly staff. Elevator malfunctioning, maybe fixed later. Breakfast quite generous but standard. Rooms small and basically equiped. Beds comfortable but small. We had a family room with private bath. Suppose rooms with common bath may be less satisfying.

title: Functional, little character, but good location
text: I booked this at short notice to stay after a friend's big party near Euston and wouldn't stay again if I had a choice. It's functional and clean but a bit shabby (the communal areas) and lacking in any charm or sense of character. My room was clean and the bed fairly comfortable but there were no spare duvets or blankets, the bed cover was thin and the pillows were poor - didn't sleep that well. No pictures or decorations at all, the lighting was pretty stark, and there was only one bedside shelf: if my wife had been with me (she was ill and couldn't come), one of us would have been pretty fed-up - she or I would have had to climb over the bed to get out as the double bed has to be pushed up against the wall to be able to open the door. Just one (hard) chair in the room so nowhere to sit - I wouldn't have wanted to stay in the room for long. The bathroom was functional, had been modernised and the shower was good, but there were no toiletries provided (is it really too much to expect?) and no towel rail to hang towels to dry. Breakfast was just about adequate - cereal, a limited cooked breakfast, a couple of thin slices of toast (made from a sliced loaf), choice of fruit juice, coffee or tea - but no fruit or yogurt, no cold meat or cheese, the kind of things we take for granted if we travel abroad, as we do a lot. Surely London can offer its visitors better. On the plus side it's relatively cheap for London, the staff are fairly friendly, and it's in a good location if you want to visit the British Museum, Bloomsbury, or want to get to Euston or St Pancras. Personally though I'd want to go somewhere else if I could: London can offer much better than this.

title: Weekend in London
text: Got this hotel off Booking.com for only fifty nine pounds. Considering it's within walking distance of the West End it was remarkable value. The room was very clean and the staff were very friendly so all things considered it was excellent value

title: Very nice stay
text: I've been in a single room with shared bathroom for 2 nights. The room was tiny, yet well furnished and very clean. Ben linen, towels and a selection of coffee and tea was offered by the hotel. It was very useful to have a luggage storage, available from the 08.00 of the arrival day, until the 21.00 of the departure day. Check in was a bit late, 14.00, yet it is a common use nowadays. The staff was very nice, and a very good breakfast is served every morning. The traditional English breakfast is good, and there is also a selection of cereals, marmelades and juices. Wifi is available in common areas, yet you could be able to get it even in some rooms, when you're lucky like me! To sum up, a very pleasant stay. I'd come there if I'm looking for a good place in the heart of London.

title: Well placed gem
text: We booked a room here on a spur of the moment decision to stay overnight and we weren't disappointed. Compact but clean rooms, brand new shower room and a great breakfast in the morning with exceptional service. We'll definitely stay here again

title: Room with a view
text: The Ruskin is located in the vicinity of Russell Square, Bloomsbury, a stone throw from the British Museum, in a safe, clean and quiet neighborhood. Within walking distance of three underground stations which make use of the tube quite practical.There are also bus lines that run near by. It is centrally located which makes sightseeing a breeze. I walked to most places and used the tube on occassions. The reception staff is excellent: friendly, helpfull and informative. The staff is knowledgeable about the sights and the surrounding neighboorhoods. If you have a specific situation ask and they shall find out for you. The hotel has a contract with a local taxi company which provides service for the guest at reduced rates. I used that service twice during my stay and I recommend it . I had an early departure from Heathrow and had no clue as to which terminal I needed to check in. The reception inquired as to which terminal I was to depart from at Heathrow and arranged for a cab to pick me up at 5:00AM. The complementary English breakafast is excellent and the breakafast staff is very nice, friendly and polite.I had a single room (G24) with a lovely view of an English garden. The room was quiet and very clean.Confortable single bed and clean linen which was changed regularly ( I stayed 5 nights).Room has a sink inside with clean towels included. There is a space heater in the room and an electric tea pot. I had a shared bathroom which was located near by and kept clean at all times. There is a WIFI connection available if you have your own portable PC. I strongly recommend the Ruskin for someone looking for an affordable, friendly hotel in the heart of central London that satisfies the basic necessities. If you want luxury and frivolous frills the Ruskin is not your kind of place. I would definitely return to the Ruskin.

title: Just like home.
text: This hotel is really good if you're looking for somewhere quiet but still central. The staff are very helpful and friendly, and were eager to answer any questions we had, and even doing a bit of online searching for us. The wifi, although strongest in the communal lounge area and stated in the description that it's only available there was still weakly available in our room on the 3rd floor. The location was perfect for everywhere you could want to go, and also on the direct line to all Heathrow airport terminals. I couldn't have been more comfortable if I'd been home. The bed was a good firmness and the shower pressure was perfect! It really was a lovely place to stay!

title: Location and Friendly Staff
text: Just returned from another trip to London and have been staying at the Ruskin on Montague Street for many years. This is a great little hotel located across the street from the British Museum and a five minute walk from the Russell Square Tube station. The staff is very accommodating and friendly. If you arrive before room is ready luggage can be left or you can wait in the lounge area - the choice is yours. On most visits, I am an independent traveler so request single room which means you share a toilet and bath, but these are always well maintained and very clean, most often located just outside your room or only one or two doors away. I have never experienced any problem with cleanliness at this bed and breakfast hotel. On occasion, I have shared a double room with a friend and have never had any complaints. Full English breakfast is offered in the breakfast room located on the lower floor, along with a selection of cereals and juices. Speaking from a North American point of view, this may not be what some folks from our side of the pond are used to, but hey, if you want what you have at home, stay at home. Single rooms are small by North American standard, there are no televisions, radios in rooms, but I have never gone to London to spend an evening in front of a TV. There is a lounge just off the Reception area which offers wi-fi and television, for those who are so inclined. This is a great little gem, at a great price in a very expensive but incredible city, something the British and Europeans are very good at offering. I have no hesitation recommending the Ruskin on Montague to anyone.

title: Cheap for London
text: We are a family of 6 trying to do an inexpencive London trip. This ofcourse is not possible, but this hotel made it more possible. We booked 2two family rooms, one with a bathroom and one with shared bathroom. The total price for both rooms was 184GBP. The rooms were by no standard particularly nice, new or clean, but it did provide a place to sleep. It is located in London with a selection of resturants and bars around, but it is not in walking distance of any of the attractions we wanted to see(Tower of London, Big Ben, The London Eye, Buckingham palace, Piccadilly circus, Trafalgar square). It is however right by the British Museum. The breakfast was good and, breafast cereals, juice, coffe and bacon, sausage and egg. Parking is not provided, but there is a parking garage nearby where we could stay for 18GBP for up to 24hours.

title: perfect place in town
text: The Ruskin is a beautiful old building in Bloomsbury, the opposite of the dull corporate box. The staff are incredibly friendly & helpful, finding my partner's mislaid gold watch in a shared bathroom & returning it to her promptly. Breakfast is a proper feast to set you up for a day's business or leisure, cooked to order plus the usual cereals & fruit juices, which would cost an extra 6 or 7 quid at a chain hotel. If you want modern decor, TV sets in every room or wipeable formica, you won't like the Ruskin, but if you want Georgian charm, original features and great views of a private square from the back windows, the Ruskin will suit you to a tee. All areas are very clean, even if the decor is worn. We will now use The Ruskin as our pied a terre in town.

title: great location and value
text: Last minute booking, read reviews, most are spot on. Our room on ground floor had a huge window looked out over a garden with green parrots in the trees! After 4 days in paris looking at scaffolding in an air shaft for 3x the price this was a welcome surprise! Location just cannot be beat, near 2ntube stops, between russell square and bloomsbury parks and across from the FREE British museum, walk to soho for nightlife.

title: Very friendly at the Ruskin
text: I stayed two nights at the Ruskin. The hotel stuff was very friendly. And the breakfast was very tasty and British. The location is perfect, in a beautiful quiet neighborhood and just behind the British Museum and a close walk to the underground. The rooms are very basic, but clean. The showers and toilets in the hallway are also clean. Each room contains a hairdryer and complimentary tea and coffee. This is a good solution for a budget and basic hotel in London. There is a fun TV room on the ground floor.

title: Good for the price
text: We stayed here during the Olympics. We got a double room plus full British breakfast for £45 Yes the room could be considered in need of decoration Yes the room only has a sink and the bathroom is down the hall Yes there is no tv What is lost in the above is made up in with location. The staff were all attentive and we were made to feel most welcome from the moment we arrived to the moment we left. There are tea and coffe making facilities in the room. The room we were given was at the front of the hotel. There is secondary glazing to keep out the minimal street noise. We left this open though to enjoy the cooling night air. It's not the ritz, but never had pretended to be. We booked direct and it clearly states this is a 1 star property. Going here with the right expectations is preferable. Thanks to the hotel team for a good stay

title: Excellent location, but rooms are small and walls thin
text: The main advantages are the excellent location and friendly staff. However the rooms are small, with thin walls (hear snoring next door), lack facilities (no TV) and you may have to share a bathroom. The Breakfast is good but limited.

title: Beware - human beings in all their glory
text: For the first time in years, and because everywhere else seemed impossibly expensive on my dates, I chose a shared bathroom option. Never again. The contented comments on same, above, are beyond me,. Perhaps I shared time with a convention of Disgusting Human Beings, because most times I visited the toilet it had been left in a revolting condition. Perhaps if I had waited longer, the facilities might have been cleaned but unfortunately as one shares the floor with at least 6-8 other rooms (not the smaller number suggested above) one can't afford to wait! Also, as people were aware of queuing issues, many chose to shower at night and in the early hours. Being close to the bathroom was therefore a disaster, sleepwise. In addition, one of the DHBs above returned (from his convention?) at 4.30 a.m., shouting into his phone at top decibels. In this hotel one is inescapably close to fellow human beings in all their glory. The only plus is the location, obviously. The room itself was perfectly clean, if tiny. But sadly, never again.

title: Amin
text: Negative: No wifi in the room No 24 hrs reception Shared shower and bathroom Positive: Good location (just cross the street from British Museum

title: Ruskin: location, location, location!
text: The Ruskin B&B is simple but efficient. Location is great, from walking distance to Covent Garden and further, little shops surrounding, lovely parks such as Russel Square Park around the corner, Holborn tube nearby and several restaurants all to be found in this wonderful part of Bloomsbury. Rooms are small, but that is London for you, clean and convenient, and so were the shared bathroom and toilets on the third floor, no frills. English breakfast was included and sufficient as well, staff polite. So to explore London, and you don't rely on luxury too much, this is the place for you. And yes, British Museum is right around the corner....

title: Investment opportunity !
text: Anyone out there with a spare £250,000 wishing to finance a complete renovation project of what was once undoubtedly a fine Georgian building need look no further than the Ruskin Hotel. I use the word "hotel" in its loosest possible sense - furniture and fittings which should have been consigned to the skip in circa 1965 still adorn the rooms, carpets so badly worn and stained that any attempts at establishing original colours are rendered impossible, no televisions in any of the rooms other than the one in a communal lounge next to reception. I could go on as the snagging list appears to be endless. A few words of advice - whilst the location is pretty good (as far as sightseeing and the West End is concerned) and the rooms at circa £50 are certainly cheap, do yourself and other family members a huge favour - save up your pennies and loose change and spend another £20 or £30 and secure yourself somewhere decent to stay. Until that mystery benefactor comes along with his spare £250,000, I for one, will not wish to spend another night at the Ruskin.

title: good trip
text: had double room on top floor, double there means 2 singles. Long cell but very clean and neat and all i needed. nice view of garden and with no screens and the window all the way up cool breeze at night slept like a log. Room with tolit just to the left of my door and shower just to the right closer thean at home. there was a tub and tolit just down the hall but did not venture there. i am 6ft 2 and 250lb fit everywhere with no problem. I walked to Buckingham palace by way of Big Ben set on the steps of St Martins in the field then on to the palace took about an hr to make the stroll. Breakfest was fine and the staff nice but what the English call sausage and bacon is mighty slim to a southern boy. dont see how you could beat this location and this price, there are at least 2 hostels near by for the younger bunch one a little pricey right next door and a less expensive and very large one that my daughter and friends stayed at 2 blocks in front of the tube station

title: Very Basic
text: Staff is very friendly and helpfull, good location and cheap. There's a hair dryer in the room which is a bit bizarre since you don't have a private bathroom. Room was located next to the shared bath room and we could enjoy the nightly sanitary activities of other guests. Breakfast was ok but only served for a limited amount of time meaning: 1° don't stay in bed too long 2° the depressing breakfast room was overcrowded. The elevator is a real adventure: it sometimes starts to move after opening the doors and sometimes it doesn't move at all when a guest didn't close the door properly on the ground floor. But anyway: we just needed a bed close to the center and that was wat we got....

title: Great location and reasonable prices
text: We booked our hotel last minute for a short weekend trip to London and were pleasantly surprised by the Ruskin B&B. It's not a super fancy hotel, but that's not we were looking for either. The room was small, but we had everything we needed: clean sheets, comfortable bed and nice bathroom (which for some reason did not have a lock nor a handle...). The wifi did not work in our room, so we had to use the common area for surfing. For a short trip this was not a problem as we were not spending that much time in the hotel any way. The breakfast was good and the staff there really friendly. Also the receptionist was super friendly and provided us adapters and tips for sight seeing. The location was the best part! The Ruskin B&B is located on a walking distance from the Oxford street and the subway stations are close by. Great value for the prices!

title: Well located lower end option
text: I took an ensuite room for one night. It was small but clean & entirely adequate for a few hours of sleep. The bathroom was tiny but new, towels and bedding were perfectly adequate. Decor is somewhere between quirky and tired, but the staff are good and a fresh-cooked breakfast was a bonus at the price. This is essentially a B&B, not a hotel, and with that in mind I would consider returning for a low cost option, very centrally located. One occasional night would probably be enough for me though....

title: central hotel
text: Good clean hotel, very central. Room was small but clean and tidy. Staff were friendly and helpful. Breakfast was good. 10 mins walk from Covent Garden.

title: Great value , convient location
text: Stayed here as I booked late and it was the only hotle with rooms free for 5 nights , glad I did ! Nice clean rooms ,comfortable and tidy . The added bonus of breakfast in the price was good , and this was well cooked and served with a full English breakfast available plus juices cereals coffee or tea . The staff were lovely anf friendly . The location was excellent with the BritishMuseum litterally opposite and Oxford street less than 10 mins walk away , plus you are4 close to 2 tube stations . I would def return .The bathrooms are sgared but lovely and clean so taking night attire is a good idea . There is a lift which makes getting to the rooms easy and the value is excellent ( I paid 353 a night for a single ) . A great find .

title: Top Value in London
text: cheap, clean, friendly staff and a really central location, this is top value

title: Excellent Value under £90 for adjacent to Oxford St
text: Stayed in an en suite room and the hotel had recently been refurbished, it was excellent value good friendly service and clean. My expectation was for a low budget hotel and expected the worst due to bad reviews but noted most of them were pre 2014 and before the refurbishment, but was pleasantly surprised and would definitely stay again. only small gripe was no tv in room but had laptop which was fine. The location and price is what sets the hotel apart and warrants 5 stars.

title: Great little hotel cheap
text: Nice standard hotel, cheap and cheerful in walking distance to west end etc. Room was fine and bath room seemed recently fitted clean and fresh, great for the price. Will stay again! Many thanks A****

title: Excellent location, great value
text: My partner and I had a very comfortable stay here. Our room appeared freshly renovated, and while cosy, was well organised so you could make the best use of the space. The window let in a lot of light, but the blinds ensured the room stayed dark till you opened them, and the window was sound proof. We had a shared bathroom and even though one toilet on the floor was out of order, we hardly ever had to wait for toilet or the shower (and the hotel was booked out most nights we were there). House keeping always did an excellent job. Its location next to the British Museum was perfect for us - we walked to Trafalgar Square and the area around Parliament to do the attractions there, but also found it easy to catch busses and trains to other attractions (e.g. to the Tower of London, the Victoria and Albert Museum, and Camden Markets), as there are many bus stops and underground stations nearby. There was a convenience store on Bury Place open 24/7, and several pubs and other restaurants within walking distance, plenty of choice. Also a Laundromat on Boswel Street, around a 7 minute walk away. It is around a 20 minute walk away from St Pancras (where the tunnel trains leave from). The breakfast was a delight, with cheerful service and yummy food. Although I found the hot food quite plentiful, you can fill up on muesli and cereals if you are still hungry. Compared to the ridiculous prices of other accommodation in London, this place is value for money.

title: Good Budget Option in Bloomsbury
text: My wife and I have just returned from a week in London where we stayed at the Ruskin Hotel. As there are a wide range of opinions of the Ruskin on this website, I thought I would add my own comments. The hotel had been recommended by a friend of a friend as a clean, budget B&B near the British Museum. We booked a double room with shower for ₤84/night which was considerably less than the other places we were considering. There are also less expensive rooms available, some without private bath. The price included a full English breakfast every morning. Our room looked out over a small garden in the rear of the building and was very quiet. Rooms facing the street might be more noisy, but it was not a heavy traffic area. The room was immaculately clean, although dated, and included only a telephone, coffee maker, and hair dryer. There was no radio, TV, or toiletries in the bathroom. There was, however, a TV in the lounge on the ground floor. We thought the bed was comfortable, about the size of an American double bed. The bathroom was small but adequate. There was always hot water. Our only minor complaints about the room was the fluorescent lighting and that there was no shelf in the shower for soap and shampoo. The hotel is located in a prime location within a 5-10 minute walk of three Underground stations and numerous bus routes. The British Museum is around the corner and there many pubs, restaurants, etc. in the area. The hotel is a 20 minute walk from most of the West End theatres. The hotel had an international range of guests (Americans, Canadians, Japanese, and Spaniards) as well as a number of English. The staff was very friendly and tried to be accommodating – for example as our room was ready, we were able to get into our room several hours before the official 1pm check-in time. There were a few things I would change – I thought the two nights non-refundable deposit at time of booking to be a bit restrictive, it would have been nice if there was a alarm clock/radio in the room, and it would have been nice if the breakfast room stayed open a little later (it closes at 9:15 am) for the tourists staying at the hotel. In short, The Ruskin is not the place to stay if you are looking for a hotel with TV, room service, afternoon tea, concierge, etc. However, if you are simply looking for a clean, budget accommodation in central London I would strongly recommend the Ruskin.

title: You won't find better value in this area
text: I stayed at this hotel for 5 days in October/November 2012. As others have mentioned, the hotel decor is dated but everything is very clean. The rooms are simple, they have full length mirrors, a sink, a window (mine had a nice view of the British Museum and the pretty street below), a wardrobe, tea and coffee making facilities, and most importantly, a comfortable bed. The shower rooms were immaculate and looked newly refurbished (cream marble floor/surfaces and modern fixtures) and there were a couple of shower rooms on each floor. The shower itself was powerful and stayed hot. The staff at this hotel were remarkable. Upon returning late at night back to the hotel, I was sitting at the bottom of the stairs using the wifi on my tablet. A member of staff came out of a nearby door and nearly died from fright at the unexpected sight of me sitting there, but promptly recovered, laughed and then offered twice to open up the lounge area for me so I could sit comfortably. On the day I was due to leave, I woke up late for checkout (I assumed it was 12pm, my booking said 11am, I woke up to a maid knocking on the door at 10:56). I called reception to ask if I could pay for an extension, and was told that this was not possible but I could have an extra twenty minutes. I thanked him, and when I asked downstairs how much I owed them for the late checkout, he told me that I didn't have to pay anything. He was then kind enough to let me use a shower room to freshen up, after I had checked out. Lovely staff. In short, I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is staying in London on a tight budget for any amount of time. If you don't mind leaving your room to use the toilet/shower, or slightly dated decor (I found it charming) then you will have no problems here. The closest underground station, a shop, Bloomsbury Square and the British museum are just a short walk away, and as the title states, you really won't find a private room cheaper.

title: Great Hotel for the price
text: The hotel was very clean, the location was great & the staff were friendly & helpful. The hotel is old and the rooms are small, but in Europe most rooms are small. We had a triple room with private bath. The room had one double bed & one single. The breakfast was good. If you want a hotel that is cheap with great location this is a good place to stay. If you want a nicer hotel with all the amenities you will need to spend more on the hotel.

title: It does the job!
text: The hotel is very outdated in terms of colour schemes and 70s furniture, which were falling apart in some places, but the (shared) bath room was very clean and surprisingly modern...I did chuckle at one review which said "well tiled" but I'd have to agree! The single room was basic with an odd pink and white colour scheme and dirty looking carpets. However, the bed was clean and the room was warm. The WiFi signal was normally strong, although did drop every now and then. The staff are friendly and polite. The breakfast is simple, but it'll see you right for while. Not a bad location, close to Holborn and Russell Square underground stations. An ideal base for those on a budget. 3/5

title: Small room
text: We have a triple room there, the room is very small, especially the toliet. Everything is so simple, no tv. The bed is ok and average clean. The location is good. It is near the Bristish Museum. It has many buses and 5 minutes walk to the underground. The staff is nice and the breakfast is fine! You can have internet access in the lobby.

title: The right place at the right price!
text: The Hotel Ruskin is a very nice hotel. The staff is attentive and the environment is always clean and well kept. We have stayed here on a number occasions and will try to make reservations in the future. It's location is hard to beat. It is very close to the British Museum and within easy walking distance to the west end theaters and a variety of resteraunts.

title: Nice hotel
text: Staff very friendly nice and clean room and shower.breakfast very good,all round great place and a good price.Great location within walking distance to covent garden and Leicester square 10 -15 min walk.

title: fantastic location
text: We often go to London for theatre, museums, galleries and bookshops. We prefer to spend our money on theatre tickets rather than a pseudo luxury hotel. For this purpose the Ruskin is a fantastic choice. Situated opposite the British museum, is within easily walking distance from major museums and theatre venues. Clean, private with very friendly staff and a cosy living room. Our room had a beautiful view of some gardens. Would recommend it to travelers that are in no need of fancy hotels, prefer to spend their money on other things but do appreciate a clean, comfortable room. Would definitely go back. The only problem when we were there, was that the lift was not working and there are some very steep stairs for the third floor.

title: Great value for an overnight stay.
text: The staff here could teach a thing or two to the bigger hotels in the area. Room had a shared bathroom but that was made clear on booking and basin in the room was therefore a bonus. Nice breakfast included in the price which makes this a real bargain. Why pay double or more elsewhere if you are only staying overnight.

title: Well....
text: I think this hotels best advantage is the location. In comparison to other locations such as Bayswater, Paddington or Sussex Gardens I found it a little bit overpriced.But then again, I didn't spend a lot of money on taxi's or buses, I could easily walk home after visiting theatres or restaurants in the West End. Everything was OK, it was clean and the staff was very friendly, but yet, it was more of a very simple B&B than a hotel which you might think when you see the price. My biggest question mark is about the breakfast, even though it was a bit amuseing to watch the very cumbersome ritual, when you finally get the breakfast it's as everything else with this hotel, it's OK. Having said all this, I can easily recommend Ruskin Hotel to everyone, just bear in mind that it's a simple B&B which you pay a little bit to much for, but maybe save taxifares on.

title: Great Location, Great Staff, So-So Room
text: This hotel is located in the heart of London, across the street from the British Museum and a quick 10 minute walk from the Russell Tube station. Being so close to this tube stop allows you to be at any of the landmark tourist attractions in no time at all. Also, there are shops, restaurants, and a Tesco Market near by. The cost per night is unbeatable for the location. The staff at this hotel is amazing. From the guy at the front desk, to the cleaning staff, down o the staff in the breakfast room...all amazing. My sister and I stayed here for three nights in a twin room. While our room was spotless, the furniture and decor was tired and worn and a bit depressing. I had to continue to remind myself what a great value it was. There is no way I could have stayed in th same area without paying almost double. The shared bathroom was very modern in decor and spotless. I'm not 100% sure that I would book this hotel again. Understanding that when you travel to a city like London, the goal isn't to spend lots of time in your room, but the room should feel comfortable.

title: History at its BEST
text: History at its BEST! Excellent tourist location, make sure you have a whole day as it's large with lots too see. Parking close by also served by public transport. Audio guide is a must, a Great help. It has something for everyone. Families,couples,groups also young children are welcome with adults. I was so impressed by the whole experience and will return.

title: WARNING WARNING WARNING!!!!
text: ******WARNING******* We were looking for a cheap hotel near to public transport and as world wide travellers we understand the risk with booking cheap hotels..but this was something else! We were prepared to overlook the broken windows, very large, body shaped, pink stain on the carpet, blood stains on the wall, 1 lightbulb in a 8 armed light fitting and a bed with wafer thin pillows and a big dip in the double bed! However when the toilet didn’t work we had to ask for help. I went to the front desk and asked the only member of staff available (called himself Daniel) who asked if i had put toilet paper down the toilet. When I said yes of course he got extremely agitated and said that we had broken the toilet as you couldn’t flush toilet paper in London! When I challenged this he said that 99% of toilets in London were the same and that you had to put tissue paper in bins!!!! Having lived in London for 8 years I then realised that anything coming from this mans mouth was not going to be credible. I asked to be moved to another room with a working toilet but he refused, he refused a refund and when I asked to speak to the manager he asked me to leave the hotel! I was travelling with my 2 children and my friend who (quiet obvious to look at) is having cancer treatment. I spoke to Beth at booking.com after we realised our hotel room was baited with rodent poison and suspected the hotel was being used as a half way house as people were drying there clothes in the corridors and landings. Beth put me on hold whilst she called the hotel. I was standing at the reception desk when “Daniel’s” phone rang and he had the conversation with booking.com. He denied all knowledge of the phone call even though I was standing right there..it was just surreal! After being told by “Daniel” that I shouldn’t worry about the small stuff like a broken toilet as much worse things could happen to me within the hotel like rat poisoning I got myself and my family out of there pronto and have left it in the capable hands of booking. com for a refund and environmental health to deal with. I have no idea who has been paid to right these reviews but for a true picture of what its really like I URGE YOU TO LOOK AT THE REVIEWS ON Tripadvisor or Facebook.

title: Survivor, does not deserve to be called hotel. awful service
text: Not even clean,, no elevator,no proper shower, dirty chairs in the breakfast area. rude manager. If you like to be insulted, I think you should book a room otherwise look for something better as this was worst ever night in UK.

title: Disgusting, would never visit it again even if it was free.
text: I have been in different hotels over the world in the last 30 years. I can tell you Hampton Court Palace Hotel should not be called hotel. The owner was extremely rude and just was interested in your money. When we arrived, the receptionist presided us to pay for the whole 3 days we were going to stay. I tried to take a shower but was not possible you either burnt yourself or too cold. I wanted to cancel our next 2 days cancellation but they did not let me o it that evening and refused to refund the money and told us to talk to the manager/owner. In the morning I met the owner, who refused to refund the money and just gave us one day refund as he needed 48 hours cancellation. He was just interested in your money and would not accept common sense. I would not even take my dog to this place.

title: Laugh or your cry
text: You know what this place is as described by other reviewers it's tatty doors been kicked in and repaired no parking anywhere and it's a shut down old pub. the service was terrible... however we did really have a laugh you have to or your break down and cry however the bonus was we survived the night

title: Worst Hotel Ever!!!
text: I'm actually quite taken aback that the owners of this hotel would let these rooms in the state that they're in. I paid £75 and quite frankly I wouldn't stay there again if it was free. The carpet was stained, the ceiling mouldy and dripping. Wallpaper peeling off and the room just felt sticky and had a sour smell. I have travelled the world and stayed in 100's of different accommodations and I have never felt so dissatisfied.

title: Our stay.
text: I would like to start by saying it wasn't all bad, it was simple and easy to book however, our stay was not as pleasant as £79 per night would have you think, the receptionist/manager was incredibly rude and reluctant to help, we had multiple issues such as

title: It did the trick.
text: Quirky old fashioned pub in a council estate. A bit tatty. Good access to Southbank and the river. Breakfast is basic. It worked for us on New Years Eve. I'm glad the building can be put to use rather than demolished!

title: Cheap and Cheerful
text: Stayed for 1 night whilst out on my works Christmas party, the location was good, the price even better. Had no problem with the facilities like others seem to have. The rooms and ambience are not going to win any awards for style and the carpets are dated but quite frankly the price I pad was half that of any premier inn, in London and this hotel is better than the large majority of travel lodges so would be happy to stay again for 1 night.

title: Terrible. Go elsewhere!!
text: List of pro's and con's below: Pros: Reasonable nice staff. Right next to Elephant and Castle Tube station. Con's: Room 8 smelt of feces. Minimum space. Moved to Room 10 slightly better. Inconsistent facilities provided. One day 3 soaps, next day 0 soaps?? Not enough pillows. Cleaner cleaned rooms in bear feet which is disgusting! Shower did not work, had to use adapted shower head running from the taps. Old, outdated, rundown, spend a little extra elsewhere!

title: Fortress,Palace and grounds well wort the visi.t
text: I have been to London five times, but this is my first visit to Hampton Court. Unfortunately, my friend had her dogs with us so we weren't able to go into the palace, but we were able to walk around the Fmfortress, grounds and the neighboring park. It is a large property, so you must be prepared to walk. Even though I wasn't able to go in the palace, I enjoyed the visit to the Fortress of the neighboring Park. And now I know I want to go inside the palace on my next trip to London.

title: Dirty, dated, broken fittings, and poor breakfast
text: Location is at end of dead-end street. Carpet is badly stained and dated, mildew in bathroom exacerbated my asthma. One window no longer opened, the blind could not be raised on the other. Toilet seat was broken and pinched at each use. Mattress was very old and bumpily firm. Breakfast was nothing like the photo - not that anything else was either.

title: Not the best, but ok.
text: We booked the family room. the sheets and towels were nice and white and the bathroom was clean. It could do with a refurbishment as carpets and decor left a lot to be desired.Breakfast was a little disappointing, It was continental and was laid along the bar (it was previously a pub) with no where to place your used teabags etc.

title: Good Value for Money
text: Excellent Location and good value for money. Staff could not have been nicer or more helpful. Accommodation is a bit dated - small rooms, creaking staircase, but spotlessly clean. Convenient for Heathrow Airport, right next to Hampton Court Palace and Thames. Attached restaurant looked nice but we ate along the main street and found an nice Italian restaurant Casa Mia on Bridge St. 3 course meal offer fantastic value.

title: Hampton court palace
text: Visited via boat trip along Thames, magnificent building, plenty of amazing beauty of painted ceilings and wall hanging. History of Henry v111 and plenty of pictures of his family, horse and carriage rides available. Good selection of restaurants and cafes and great day out. Entrance price a bit steep but they do have concessions for children and oaps.

title: Very dated
text: Had to book a hotel last minute near waterloo. This place short walk from Elephant tube and in a residential area of real London...lots of shops bars and food venues around nearby . Was a quiet neighbourhood and I had a comfortable stay paid 89. Hotel itself is very old fashioned run down and disappointing. Carpets worn decor old fashioned bathroom clean n functional . This place is like buying a cheap house at an auction and the 1st thing you would do is rip everything out n start again lol...it did the job but I won't come back.

title: Please find a better hotel to stay in London
text: We stayed there for 4 days in June and the hotel is just old and not great! The front of the hotel looks creepy and the front door is REALLY squeaky! It is located close to the subway, but away from all the sightseeings and attractions. I wish we had found a better location. There is no AC in the room and the water in the sink is either really hot or really cold. Ridiculous! The breakfast is the same old same everyday. I would really eat somewhere else.

title: OK TO CRASH FOR ONE NIGHT
text: I think that this place is undergoing change currently. Staff are pleasant & we stayed in a nicely proportioned twin room. Beds were comfortable & the linen/towels clean. Our room was on the first floor accessed by quite steep stairs & even steeper steps to the room door. The room was nicely decorated & the shower room with toilet & basin looks like it has recently refurbished. Tea & coffee making facilities & a tower fan/heater were provided. The place was very quiet when we stayed but the location is good. The breakfast room is quite small, however I suspect if it were busier the function room can be used. The car parking area is limited but was adequate during our stay. Continental breakfast was included in the room rate. We found the quality of all of the products on offer were of good standard.

title: old and toilet in hallway
text: Small and a bit old hotel near elephant & castle. We had room nr 26 with our toilet / shower in the hallway, expected it to be in the room. Staff and service is ok. Has had a pub on ground floor but closed since 2013, now used as breakfast room. Small breakfast with bread & marmelade and 1 type of youghurt.

title: Hotel ok but breakfast was awful
text: The breakfast was less than satisfactory. All on offer was some cheap croissants with only butter and jam, boxed cereals and the cheapest yogurts loaded with sugar. There was no fruit, cheese or meat. A so called continental breakfast, half of which my husband with diabetes couldnt eat. The most ridiculous aspect was that there wasnt even enough spoons to go round with the poor overworked, non-english speaking worker was desperately trying to wash each one to hand it to the next person. Definitely the worst hotel breakfast we have ever had. We had to go elsewhere for breakfast, not good when we had already spent a lot on the hotel.

title: Terrible
text: I wish I read these reviews before I went! It's run down and just awful. Walked into a man slobbing on the sofa! Went to our room but felt like something out of a horror film. Then when we went to go out we were asked to leave the hotel key! Why would you do that with your belongings in the room??! We were in London to see a show and the hotel was so bad that we deduced to drive home after the show! 2.5 hours and getting home around 2am!! Complete waste of money but you couldn't have paid me to stay there!

title: Disappointed
text: Very disappointed with this hotel. It advertises as a quaint cosy London stay but it is shabby, in need of a lick of paint and a bugs upgrade and overhaul and overall a huge disappointment to us. Holes in the wall, paint flaking off walls, toilet dripping and giving off a very unpleasant smell in to room. Taps and shower broken, blinds visibly dirty, the list goes on. We booked looking forward to a hotel with a bar to be told on arrival it was closed due to poor business. Very poor customer service from staff. Since our stay, have emailed the hotel twice with a complaint for various reasons and nearly a week later have had no acknowledgment or response. A very poorly ran establishment. We will certainly never return and would recommend anyone looking for a reasonably priced London hotel, avoid this one and stay elsewhere.

title: An odd mix...
text: I looked forward to a cheap night in a pub with rooms, but found the bar had been shut through lack of trade. There's no doubt the place is showing it's age quite significantly. The bedroom on the other hand was OK with a comfortable bed. For less than £70 within 20 mins of Trafalgar Square it's good value. Will put it on my reserve list for cheap London hotels but won't rush back.

title: Get what you pay for
text: I can't even list all the negatives, it would take too long! Pros are it's very close to the tube station, is quiet, wi-fi worked in room on top floor, and we had clean bedding and towels. A few of the cons: I don't call a tray of cold cheap croissants a selection of pastries, Customer service didn't exist, everything is tatty, shower barely worked, poor selection at breakfast. My 8 year old son cheered as we left...That sums it up .

title: Not the best stay
text: We were placed in a quite wierd room with bathroom in the common hallway. In addition the door didnt close all the way so it was quite noisy if people were talking in the hallway, so we didnt feel like there was much privacy to get. When we asked to switch room there wasnt much help to get.

title: Economical overnight stay
text: Cheap and excellent value, yes a little dated but clean, comfy beds and pillows, decent breakfast. Bathroom was new and spotless. Quiet location, no traffic noise. Easy access to tube. Would definitely use it again

title: BEWARE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! STAY CLEAR
text: This would come at a -3 * if it was possible! Looked this hotel up and thought it would be OK having checked the photo's This was not the place i looked at in the pics! The hotel needs a complete overhaul walls dirty carpets need changing tripping hazard is not the word in some places, Room was a joke drawer's could not use as radiator in the way draught from windows as lock was broken held together with cellotape, bed had a great dip in middle which then made me look at the bedding which is where we found the duvet was so dirty that we did not sleep in the bed, did not even bother with breakfast as didn't want to risk it? Staff Rude carried on conversation whilst we were trying to flee the place!!!!!!!!!!!!!! This is not exaggerated believe me!!!!!!!!

title: Cheap but not much else going for it
text: Ok, so firstly I'll say that the staff were very friendly at the front desk. Secondly it was cheap for a last minute night in London. Other than this I really can't find anything positive about the experience. The room was tiny (i'm glad I paid another tenner for a double room because lord knows how small the single is!), the window wouldn't close so I had the local soundscape to buzz me to sleep. Both taps were scalding hot in the evening (so I bought bottled water to drink from a local shop) but everything was ice cold in the morning so no shower for me. The area isn't too bad and there's a cracking local pub between here and Kennington station called the Red Lion. Not sure I'd leave the main road on foot at night though. All in all, it's a cheap hotel in London.. What do you expect?! I would probably not stay here again unless another emergency last minute need arose but that's my own preference for a travelodge as a minimum.

title: Great location saves the
text: ....day! The hotel is a disused pub situated amidst a Southwark Council Estate. The place looks and feels tired! The carpets are worn out and the room looked bruised and battered. It did have a kettle and limited coffee and tea. The bathroom had soaps and shower gel. The 1st night of my stay pipe sounds of flushing water kept me awake. Saving grace friendly staff who dealt with it. By night three, a itchy rash appeared on my body and there were ants in the bathroom. For what it is, it's terribly expensive. They should NOT be allowed to charge hotel fees. It's more of a run down hostel type place. Check out is 10am, which considering the price you pay for a room is a massive rip off! I checked out Breakfast one day and it is simple and does kill the initial hunger. I dare say stay there only if other local options are taken and for some reasons you have to be at the Elephant and Castle. Transport links to the busses, tube and overground train are all within 5 minutes. Other than that wait that they lower the room rates!

title: Avoid at all costs
text: The hotel is located on some shabby council estate in a run down old pub, the interior is outdated, the whole place was dusty and mouldy and in serious need of a deep clean, my bedroom had mould and cobwebs,the price is an absolute joke and a rip off for such awful conditons

title: Day out
text: I went on a coach trip with friends great day out right by the Thames you can even go on a boat trip. Plenty to see in the palace lovely kitchens and rooms also an exhibition of Egypt very good . Gardens are lovely you can get a coach drawn carriage with shire horses . Lots of places to eat but our fish and chips were cold and a bit hard . Cream tea lovely would have liked a proper cup though not paper . Go to the maze it's very good . If you have children there is the magical garden which is great for them there's aerial walkways dragons, slides .and under ground grotto .

title: Avoid: disgusting customer service.
text: Didn't stop at the hotel but we made a booking which we had to cancel due to unforseen circumstances. We booked on a free cancellation basis and cancelled 2 weeks at least before the stay. It subsequently took them over 3 weeks to use the card machine to refund me. When I rang to query it I was told a friend would take a week. Not too happy with this but hey ho. A week later I still hadn't been credited so rang them again, to be told it takes 3 weeks to refund and the week previous was the processing time to send it to the accounts department. Because I'm upset at this and make the known the staff member shouted down the phone at me told me it was my fault for cancelling and I shouldn't of. I've had to ask booking.com for proof of the refund because they can't deal with me. I would hate to of stayed here and to of had a complaint. TRULY AWFUL CUSTOMER SERVICE.

title: Lunch
text: Had an excellent lunch time meal during the very busy lunch time. Place was full. Located in the tourist area. Food was excellent, service was excellent. Prices were average for the area. Had the wild boar sauces with mash. The lamb was also great.

title: Good Base
text: My husband and I wanted to stay the night in London following a concert at Wembley. The next day we had booked a Royal Afternoon Tea at The Shard. This hotel (more B & B really) was both affordable and a good location to the elephant and castle tube station. It was clean and comfortable but very basic. They were friendly, polite and accommodating. Would have like something more up market but you get what you pay for.

title: Nothing Close to What is Advertised
text: At first they tried to give me a room with a bathroom outside the room claiming it is still a prvate bathroom. When I said that I will complain about at booking.com they changed my room. The breakfast was just packed stuff nothing hot (not even eggs) at all. The staff was not friendly. I dont recommend you to stay there.

title: Excellent gardens
text: I visited the Hampton Court Palace in the spring (April) and all of the spring flowers are blooming - tulips and narcissus. The gardens are really spectacular. Inside the palace is also very impressive. The Palace is very easy to reach via train from the Waterloo station in London.

title: Disastrous
text: Hotel is above what seems to be a derelict pub. Man on reception rude. Dirty smelly horrid place. Carpets Freighing. When I got to the room it was all of the above and worse. Wallpaper hanging of mouldy walls. Paintwork chipped and dirty AND BLOOD ON CARPETS SKIRTING AND WALLS . Neither myself or my daughter felt safe and went to speak to man on desk he was just RUDE

title: Will look for better place next time
text: I just stayed in this hotel for only 1 night, however it wasn't comfy at all, I'll mention the Pros first then the Cons. Pros: - Not expensive and within the budget. - Clean - Friendly staff Cons: - Bed mattress was not good at all, I couldn't sleep all night - Break fast is only from 7:00 to 9:00 am - Check-out at 10:00 am max. - WiFi coverage is low

title: Complaint
text: On arrival the hotel looked old and uncared for, the woodwork hadn't seen a coat of varnish or paint in years. Inside the carpets were worn and frayed and after check in we had to carry our own bags upstairs ourselves. The room had brown damp stains in the ceiling and on the bedside table lamp-shade. The toilet sounded like a pneumatic drill when flushed and the floor had an ominous lump in the middle. Definitely not to be recommended. Needless to say we left immediately.

title: So so
text: We only booked it to have shower because our boiler was broken. Price wise is ok but the decor is extremely outdated. Good points despite being ancient it was clean. I had white socks that was still white after walk. Bad things - horrible water pump noise all night long. Heating not working. And horrible horrible decor. If hotel reads my comment - thanks for keeping it clean but guys, please take down these shameful curtains! !! Are they 30 years old?

title: Southwark stay
text: Very Large room, great price, found a parking space close to hotel as long as you move for 8.30am. Breakfast was self serve, cereals, toast, croissants etc. If you are a family visiting London or a group of workers on a budget its fine, my room had a double bed and two singles with plenty of room.Bathroom needed a bit of work ie shower head holder broken.

title: Horrendous
text: Terrible hotel in the middle of a housing estate in an unsafe area. Graffiti on the front of the hotel. Rooms were very shabby, door in room didn't close properly, the staff were unfriendly (bar the older man at reception) Out of date boxes of cereal for breakfast & a toaster that didn't toast. Only plus was the bed was comfortable. Would not return.

title: Basic and tired
text: A basic, cheap place to stay for an odd night in my opinion but I wouldn't want to be coming back there night after night. Creaky floorboards, erratic water pressure and temperature. My room also smelled a bit sewer-like (the stink pipe casing was found to be wrapped in brown packing tape - not standard décor!). Breakfast as expected but the member of staff on duty was clearly not fluent in English, which is not something I'd expect in my own capital city. Décor and fittings are tired.

title: Charming little hotel
text: This isn't a standard chain place. Nor is it the Ritz. But for what you're paying it's surprisingly good. The rooms were clearly appointed at a point when this place had ambition: the bathroom was almost palatial with a lovely tiling scheme, and there was even a trouser press hidden away in a cupboard. There are paintings on the walls and strange corners. At some point this place was shown a lot of love. The bed was comfortable, the place was kept clean. Breakfast is served in the (sadly closed) beautiful pub bar downstairs. It's not great but a darn sight better than 'continental' breakfasts I've sampled in similar hotels elsewhere in London. Location-wise... well, someone got murdered just around the corner while I was staying here, but it's superbly located right by the tube/train station. Really, for this price, in Zone 1, you won't find much better.

title: Terrible
text: Never ever again would I give this hotel my money I have stayed in YMCA's that are better than this place. no plugs because they had a flood and no sorry but you can have one but bring it back either. The wall paper is falling off I don't know about a refub I think knocking it down and starting again would be the best option. The breakfast leaves a lot to be desired overall the worst hotel I have ever stayed in

title: Average
text: Correct. Clean. Outdated in need of improvement. Breakfast is basic but this is what you pay for. This is a convenaient place to crash for the night and be out all day long. The location is at a walking distance from a tube stop. So this makes it convenaient.

title: Awful service
text: The location is nice but that is about all that the hotel has to offer. The breakfast that is included consists of small boxes of cereal milk and coffee. While we were there we had to place a call to the airport. At the lobby we were greeted by a young man who said thwy did not extend that courtesy to their guests to go use a payphone. The iron they loaned us did not work. We have stayed in london before and loved it. Definitely would never stay here again and DO NOT RECOMMEND!

title: Wouldn't book again!
text: Stayed at the Hampton Court Palace for a weekend summer getaway. I was visiting London for the first time and got a good deal on the place (or so I thought). When I arrived I was immediately appalled at the location. The neighborhood did not feel safe at all. When I checked in at the desk I was handed an old key and was told my room was on the third floor. While walking up the stairs (no lift), the place smelled of old mildew and was sour. When I arrived in my room the carpet was stained and the room was unpleasantly TINY. I had a twin bed in the corner and had virtually no room to move. It was like a room converted from a closet. The bathroom was disgusting with black all along the tub. I've stayed in budget hotels filled with hookers and drug addicts that made me feel more comfortable than this place. The only bonus was that it was close to a tube station so I could stumble home from Covent Garden at 4AM after a night out. Avoid this place!

title: disappointing
text: On arrival hotel looked very run down with handmade signs directing you. The inside was very dated and in need of renovation. Room was clean but bedside lamps didn't work and WiFi was poor. Very hot in the room even with the window open. Staff at breakfast wasnt very friendly when we asked for cutlery. Orange juice was warm and only cereal and toast available. Staff on front desk very helpful and pleasant. In easy access to the tube and elephant and castle.it was OK to stay for one night but i wouldn't reccommend or revisit.

title: Not a pleasant experience
text: On a positive note its a cheap place to lay your head and if that is your priority this might suit you, the outside of the hotel does not look welcoming and signs for the hotel are handmade. The room was ok but elements of it were not well looked after, the TV signal wasn't strong enough to run the TV and reception were not interested. Behind the TV cabinet was thick dust, the walls were dirty and the mattress cover torn. The handles on the bath had been broken off and filled with silicone, the shower door broken off and left unfinished and the hall carpets were very worn. As a woman on her own I didn't feel safe in the neighbourhood and would not go back despite the price. Wifi not strong enough to do anything other than send an email. The breakfast was good and overall it is clear the owners are trying to make a go of this as a business but you have to work a bit harder in my opinion.

title: "No Frills" budget hotel with character
text: This hotel is over 100 years old and retains many original features. The pub has been permanently closed, but bottled beer and sodas may be purchased by guests at the front desk. Wi-Fi is only available in the lobby and the rooms do not have telephones or clocks, but if you need a wake-up call staff will knock on your door. While the curtains, carpet, and lobby furniture badly need refurbishment, our room was nicely cleaned and fresh linen was supplied every day. The front desk staff were very helpful and went beyond the call of duty to help with some problems we had. The continental breakfast was simple but plentiful and well-presented in the old pub. The hotel is a few minutes walk from the Elephant and Castle tube and bus stops, although in May 2015 there was so much road construction around this area that we found it easier to get off at Kennington and walk two extra blocks back to the hotel. There are only a couple of sit-down restaurants near the hotel but there are several take-aways within 2-3 blocks, serving a variety of ethnic foods. The nearby Elephant and Castle Shopping Center is quite run down, but has a small Tesco store and the area around it has many small vendors that give it a bazaar-like atmosphere. We would recommend this as a basic, budget hotel with a good staff, in a fairly convenient location for public transportation.

title: Conveniently located budget hotel
text: Stayed for 3 nights. Location is good, with easy access to many buses and Elephant & Castle tube station. The street is quite isolated, specially at night .... The hotel is quite old, needing urgent refurbishing and maintenance. But it was clean and the staff were correct. No wi-fi in the rooms, just in the reception are. Right value for money.

title: Nice hotel
text: Excellent location, 2 min to Subway. Quit area. Very nice staff, even at night they are super helpful. Tasty breakfasts, small but still ok. Croissants and toasts. Old style, but clean and and friendly

title: Disgusting - Avoid at all costs!
text: I stayed here with a friend back in March and the only good thing about it is the location. Situated a few minutes walk from Elephant & Castle, meaning commuting to and from the hotel was nice and easy. Upon arrival we found that the pub below was closed and signs pointing towards a side entrance, which led us into a rather dated, but clean reception area. The furnishings in the room were of a high quality, but the uneven, squeaky floor dampened the mood. Speaking of damp, the bathroom was in a disgusting state. The ceiling had been severely water damaged, with a consistent drop of water leaving one of the spotlights every 2/3 seconds. We alerted the guy on Reception and asked for a different room but was told that the hotel was fully booked (doubtful but we rolled with it). Later that evening, we went off to bed and all was well until a gust of wind blew open the window. Initial thought was that the previous guest/maid didn't lock it, but nope, the lock was broken. Back down to Reception to complain (at 1am). The guy followed me up, took one look at the window and proceeded to try and slam it shut (apologies to all those other guests staying that night who were sleeping) before asking us to bare with him and he'll be, "back in a minute". You guessed it, he never returned, so we slept with a broken window all night (it was very cold!). The following morning at check-out we asked to speak to a manager and got told to email a generic address - one week on, we're still yet to receive a reply. An absolute shambles of a hotel. I wouldn't stay here again if you paid me.

title: Nice place but most likely won't book again
text: When I arrived I was greeted with notifications that the pub was closed for good. The hotel entrance was luckily the entrance was clearly visible by some paper sheets that where put up. The whole hotel was clean and made a good first impression. Unfortunately that was vanished by a lot of details. In the bathroom door was a dent as if somebody tried to use an axe to get out of the bathroom. The toilet was squeezed right between the shower and the wall, so that you had to get up to clean you bump after doing your business, no chance to do it while sitting... well maybe if you are size zero. The thick carpet was clean but couldn't prevent the floor from making a lot of noise. The wall sockets where far away from the night stand and also loose in the walls. The room doors had the ability to be opened with a key card, but I got a proper key for them. When I came back at 2am in the morning I saw the door locket with a heavy chain and I was ask to come through the fire exit door same next morning at 1am. As I said the place was very clean, even the party plastic cup for cleaning your mouth after brushing your teeth, was sealed in a bag. No dirt on the floor and the trash in the room was also cleaned daily. I didn't had a chance to try the breakfast as I prefer some local stores over any breakfast, but it was available and included in the hotel price. So if you want just a place to crash at night and have a good sleep. Go for it. But if you are easily turned off buy some dodgy things, then better book something else.

title: hmmm
text: arrived to a scarey looking location. Quiete handy near tube only good point!! no hot water... hello how are u meant to shower ridiculous... arrived for "breakfast" which we wer told wer 15mins late and it was only continental. wuldnt recommend this place

title: Hideous
text: We had booked into The London Court Hotel in Earls court, when we arrived they said there had been a leak in our room, but it was ok as they had another hotel we could go to and they would get us a taxi and pay for it. When we arrived at the Hampton and saw the room we were shell shocked it was horrible. We didn't even stay there the night we refused, we didn't feel safe the area wasn't nice either. The man at the front desk was quite affronted that we had a problem with the "hotel", he was rude to us and said well you won't get a refund!! We just wanted to get out of the place and quick!!

title: Not as advertised
text: Me and my partner stayed here for 1 night as a last minute thing and wasn't impressed. The room was very dated the tv was miles away from the bed. As for breakfast included?? Well cereal and toast was on offer but no hot choices quite disappointing when you pay extra included in the price. No parking available and when I asked where to park the man behind the desk said he didn't no. Very helpful. Not for us.

title: Horrible
text: We stayed for the weekend, at 150 pounds a night, felt completely ripped off. The first room we were given had the smallest "double" bed ever and the lumpiness mattress. Signs in the hotel are paper, everything is rundown and threadbare. The area is awful, the breakfast was awful. After demanding another room, we were moved the next day, but I would have preferred to have myself away completely, unfortunately we had already paid the exorbitant price.

title: A quick weekend in London
text: Oh dear, first impression from the outside, run down, inside it doesn't get any better. Everywhere you look, it's shabby. Tread bare carpets, lamps missing from lights, table lamps that don't work, toilets that take 20 mins to refill, doors kicked in, tread bare curtains, taps with tops missing, glass shower screen about to fall off the bath, shower with a dribble of water. Shall I go on !!!! Breakfast was poor, the one and only staff serving never even made eye contact, no morning, no good bye. We did not book this because it was cheep, we booked it because it was close to where we wanted too be and it had a bar, so as we could relax. The pub underneath the rooms is closed down and has been for some weeks and yet they still advertise on the web it's open. Budget doesn't have too have basis poor quality, it usually means you pay for the add ons. Here you have a run down hotel, that is desperate for some TLC.

title: When is a pub not a pub?
text: The location of this ex urban estate pub is less than 10 minutes from the E&C roundabout, and my single bedroom on the top 2nd floor was very shabby and threadbare. The suitcase rest frame was no longer usable, since 2 of the 3 material straps were completely worn through. The toilet seat was missing hinge, and the cobwebs were much in evidence. Nevertheless, I had a good nights sleep, room 6 overlooking a basketball court at the rear. Breakfast was a poor affair, really. Toast, tea and coffee, fat free yoghurt that was full of sugar, a spooky feel to a bar area that was as quiet as the grave........ £82 for bed and breakfast represented very poor value. I walked to Lambeth North tube station and bought a freshly cooked breakfast and mug of tea for £5.50' at an Italian deli near the Days Hotel. I tried to get into the Days but they were full.

title: WONDERFULL
text: Stayed for 3 nites , was really worried as we read the review by dangif after we booked but can only say was he / she in the same hotel as us? Staff were friendly, room was clean and fresh and breakfast was fantastic !

title: Reasonable hotel, despite first appearances
text: This is not the best part of London and its location above a pub is worrying. However the pub is closed and the hotel is a short walk from Elephant & Castle tube station which is well connected to most tourist spots. Downstairs does not create an immediate good impression with well worn furniture and carpets. However the room, once you get there is very good compared with most in London in this price range. The bedding and towels were spotlessly white, the floor area is exceptional for London, the bathroom is spacious and well maintained. Trouser press, hair drier, tea and coffee. toiletries, TV - these are not common in sub-£100 London hotels. I was perhaps fortunate in having a back bedroom and despite having windows open I was not disturbed by noise. Overall, I can understand why other reviewers have been disappointed but I stay in a lot of budget London hotels and this one is better than most - once you get into the room!

title: Old victorian pub
text: I stayed here for one night and found the hotel to be a pub with rooms. The reception area looked like a bar and was dimly lit. Check-in was easy and I was given my key. The door looked to have a key card entry but there was a key hole beneath it. It's an old pub and the decor reflects this, orange curtains and here pelmet - lovely! Creaky floor boards and poor reception on the tv. But it was clean and quiet and the bed was comfy and the shower was hot. Breakfast is a simple affair cereal toast yoghurt etc.., I wouldn't like to spend a week here but it was okay. The staff were happy and friendly so I have no reason to complain.

title: Stay away for your own sakes!
text: This hotel is hideous, and what the advertise is complete lies! 1) The Area. If you want to stay on a street where cars rev their engines and blare music out all night, then this hotel is perfect for you. Its not a nice area to be in, and is very intimidating as a woman on her own. It was made perfectly clear that this is not a street you walk around in at night, unless you want trouble that is? 2) The Full English Breakfast (Included in the price of a room). The choices for breakfast included... Stale bread that you could toast yourself, croissants that had seen better days, plastic cheese that was hard around the edges or cornflakes. That's your lot! 3) The staff. There was one younger guy who seemed fairly nice, the rest of them barely spoke English and were completely uninterested in helping or having any kind of conversation with you. 4) The room. The room was a reasonable size, basic TV, shower over bath etc. BUT I would recommend cleaning the bath before using it (there were water marks all over the bath I was expected to use). The rooms are old fashioned, but if you like that sort of thing, then great. 5) The Location. Its near a shopping mall... tired and run down shopping mall. Other than that I would say jump on a tube to anywhere... as far far away from that place as you can get! Overall... Hideous trip! Would never return to that part of London, or that hotel EVER! Stay away for your own sakes!

title: Cheap, but still not good value.
text: The only redeeming factor of the cold-water shower in the morning was that it fully woke me up after a poor night's sleep on a mattress that could only be described as spring-bare. What I don't understand is that attention to detail had been provided in some respects, like vanity supplies, toilet rolls folded neatly, but none of it took away from the fact that the basics were missing (hot water!). And it was only surface-clean – I could see marks on the bath that resulted from it just being wiped, rather than properly cleaned. I actually went to bed dreading what the mattress underneath the sheets would look like. Someone here commented that there was almost no window. I had the opposite experience – far too much window in the bathroom. Only the bottom half of the tall sash window was frosted

title: No. No. No.
text: Very rude, unprofessional staff. Dirty rooms...unpleasant odours. Very evident that the management haven't run a hotel before...quite scary really. Only marginally better than sleeping rough on the streets.

title: Horrified experience
text: NOT a very cheap hotel for 99GBP per night. I had a horrible experience staying one night at the hotel. THERE WILL BE NO RECEPTION NOR ANY STAFF AVAILABLE AFTER MIDNIGHT, guests will be left alone to themselves in the hotel.There was almost no window and no phone in the room. Free Wifi was said to be provided in the room, BUT the reception was too weak to even just to connect to the internet. One thing was right about other review is that the bathroom was clean, the entire room was moderately clean. HOWEVER, there was a spider of a size of 2euro coin on the room's wall that kept me up all night!

title: The Pink Finger nail!!!!
text: Stayed a single night and loved it, proper London Pub!!!. Superb staff/Managers, basic but clean room and a great full English breakfast. Arrived Sat afternoon and instantly felt at home with the locals and staff, manager even ordered us a takeout and let us eat whilst enjoying a few shandy’s!!!!. Be warned thou, the Phantom Pink Finger Nail drinks on the premises, you know who you are Geoffrey!!!!!!!!!.

title: An urban oasis
text: Very last minute I found this place on line and booked a family room for myself and my two young children while having a treat visit to London. Five minutes walk through the eclectic 'Elephant' part of town we found this old Georgian building in among a housing estate. The reception was warm and friendly. The inner decor was tired but somehow comforting. The feel of the hotel was relaxed and easy, amplified perhaps by the contrast to the harsher outside environment. The room followed suit. Breakfast was distinctly fry-up but went down well. For the money I would definitely recommend this little place if on a budget.

title: Good little spot, clean and friendly
text: Booked this on laterooms.com where there are many reviews. Then saw there was only one review at tripadvisor, and it was quite damning. Still I'm not fussy so carried on, but was pleasantly surprised. The Hotel, (or B&B may be more accurate) is over a pub on a side street a short walk from Elephant and Castle tube station. Room was bright and clean, as was small but nice bathroom. Staff were casual and friendly. I mentioned the bad review and was told the management were recently changed and they have now upgraded the rooms. Breakfast was down in the bar next morning, a good hearty breakfast from friendly staff. The walk from the tube was quite short, shorter than it looks on the map. Pub is in a residential district, quiet in the daytime, was back too late to know what the pub crowd is like. I would definitely use this again as a cheap base from which to do things in London for a few days.

title: This Hotel keeps it real
text: Just returned back to Manchester with my family after staying at this unique hotel.We all loved it.The rooms were clean,comfortable and had everything we needed.The staff are pleasant and respectful,making us feel welcome at all times.The pub has a free and easy atmosphere with no airs and graces.London is an expensive city.Take into account the price of the room/full English breakfast/parking near hotel was free at weekend/walking distance to the west end 30 mins/reasonable prices for drinks/friendly locals and this hotel suites.Make no mistake this hotel is in way the Ritz but I would stay there again without hesitation.

title: A local Pub.
text: A typical South London pub with friendly staff and reasonably priced rooms. Well located for the South Bank and the West End. No food,but plenty of good restaurants to suit all budgets in this up and coming area.

title: Friendly and Fun
text: Stayed here as wanted to be in this part of London, and was looking for a good deal. This place fitted the bill and i was more than happy with my room and the facilities they had to offer. Spent some time in the bar during the evening and got to know the staff and even some of their family. was recommended to go for dinner at the Tai Tip Mein, the cheapest chinese buffet i have had anywhere i think! Clive the manager at the hampton court palace is a great host, and Shamus cooks a blinding breakfast. They even sorted me out secure parking which i had missed when booking! Thanks guys i will return soon.

title: Clean but depressing
text: The bedroom was mainly clean (apart from the edge of the carpet near the skirting board which had that grey mark you get with old carpets), but I'm guessing it was last furnished in the early 1990's. Same for the bathroom

title: Rather ramshackle but good value for central London
text: Despite the rather grand name this is not really a hotel. It is a pub and the rooms are on top of the pub and your breakfast will be served in the pub. The location is not brilliant: it's on the edge of the Newington estate down a fairly dodgy looking road that I guess is safe but I would not want to walk down there at night of I were a woman on my own. Everything inside is in need of an upgrade: my window didn't close properly, a cupboard door handle came off in my hand, a tile had fallen out of the side of the shower and the carpets are a bit threadbear. BUT..... it's clean,safe and comfortable and the owners seem very friendly. A large cooked breakfast is on offer the next morning which sets you up for the day. So it's not perfect but for central London it really represents good value for money. I've stayed in far worse places in the city for this kind of money.

title: Relaxed and so friendly...........
text: If you're into relaxed, cosy and friendly and not bothered about sticking your little finger out - you will love this place. So friendly and that includes the locals, cheap beer, less than a stones throw from the Elephant & Castle tube. Excellent base for your London break..

title: Juliet
text: I was greeted by warm and friendly staff. Had a very welcome by all. As it is a pub as well I had a few drinks in the bar and chatted to the locals who made my stay even better. Had a great time while I stayed there. Bedding was changed every day. The rooms are clean. Beds are very comfy. Had breakfast which is include in the price, and what a breakfast (very nice indeed). I would defiantly stay here aging. I loved the place and it was like home from home to me... Thanks to Clive for staying up!!!

title: Lovely Staff, Good Clean Rooms
