text: We are a family that 9 times out of 10, are on a budget. We're stingy and always look hard for a good price. After arriving in London Victoria, we hailed a cab and gave the directions to the Hampton Court Palace Hotel, the taxi driver looked a bit confused and said "..That's an old Pub!! What do you wanna go there for?!" after discussing it with him, he assured us that he goes there frequently and it's actually not bad. Once we turned the corner, we could see why he was so astonished at our decision, it was a real old-school pub, not exactly what I'd expected (but then I didn't book it and didn't see the pictures beforehand). When we got inside, there were a couple of locals having a quiet drink, and a nice man behind the bar who directed us to Reception. The Reception is nice and spacious, with pictures of Royals and the like on the walls. Now, after coming home, I read the reviews to see if they are similar to how we enjoyed our stay. Ok, so the carpet on the stairs up to the rooms is tired and needs replacing, but it isn't doing anyone harm being in the state it's in. The room (Number 22, consisting of 1xDouble bed and 2xSingle beds) was clean, and roomy. We had an LCD TV, Large windows, pictures on the walls and a large bathroom. The beds were comfortable (which is imperative for us as I have problems with my back), the linen was spotless and we each had 2 pillows. The area, although not ideal, caused no problem for us, we frequented the local shopping centre and underground stations and had no problems at all. As someone else has mentioned on here, there is a basketball court near-by but there was only as much noise as you'd expect children to make in the summer holidays, which dissipated at a decent hour. The noise some people have mentioned coming from the bathroom is the sani-flow system which they have in place, it didn't cause us any nuisance. The entire time we were there, Clive and Seamus were helpful, polite and informative. We hadn't really planned our trip, as it was on a bit of a whim, but they told us about places to eat, visit and enjoy while we were there, they even gave us helpful tips with regards to the area. The breakfast was lovely, with a large choice for the cooked option, and a selection of cereals and fruit juice, teas and coffee. Served from 7:30 - 9:00, but Essentially, if you're looking to get the Ritz, or the Hilton.. then go THERE, this place is good value, but if you're a snob, you probably won't like it, so pay more and stay somewhere else. This place is clean, tidy, spacious and friendly...what more can you ask for, for this price? I wouldn't believe for a second that these guys would steal, from anyone, or accuse anyone of doing something unlawful without a just reason. My guess is that the person who wrote that review is the competition, or just a really deluded tourist. We will certainly be returning on a regular basis.

title: Great breakfast
text: Little worried when we arrived because the pub is not in the most desirable area but we were made to feel very welcome and enjoyed a friendly drink in the pub. Close location to the Elephant and Castle Underground station, room was very spacious for my husband, myself and two teenage children. Bit noisy outside but beds clean and comfortable. Great breakfast in the morning with good service. Bit too far out to leave our luggage so paid to leave it at the train station so that we could make the most of our day in London. At the end of the day you get what you pay for. Good value.

title: Nice pub B&B
text: Got to say that when the taxi pulled up we were a little worried but this is a London Pub with B&B rooms above so don't be as surprised as we were! However, you're made to feel really welcome and the rooms are clean and tidy. I feel that if you get a comfortable nights sleep then it's worth the money you pay and that's exactly what we all got. Yes it's in the middle of a housing estate and clearly it's a good local for a number of people. We stayed on a Saturday and karaoke was on but we didn't hear a pep. When we arrived we were welcomed nicely and made to feel like we were locals anyway. When I went down for a beer, everyone was welcoming and chatty. In summary a bit like the Old Vic of the telly but that actually made it nicer than a chain hotel.

title: disappointed
text: I had booked this hotel for me and my husband and two small kids for two nights. I arrived in london and stayed at a hotel near legoland for the first night and was due to stay here for the next two nights when i recieved a call from the hotel to say our room had a leak in it and that they couldn't offer us the room as simple as that. They didn't even recommend another place to stay, We were really annoyed as we had no where to stay with two small kids but they didn't care, in my opinion id say they double booked! Definetly wouldn't ever consider booking here again as they COULDN'T CARE LESS!

title: Won't get a good night's sleep here
text: I stayed for one night at the Hampton Court Palace hotel. Generally I thought it was an OK place to stay for just one night. The room was very clean and tidy with a nice bathroom, good shower and a colour TV. It's also conveniently just a short walk from Elephant & Castle. On the downsides my room was very hot even with the windows open which made it hard to get to sleep. There was also some kind of loud noise from the water pump or something going off intermittently through the night. This sort of noise doesn't really bother me but other people might find it annoying and difficult to get to sleep. The worst thing was that I needed to be somewhere at 8am and I went down to check out at about 7:20 only to discover that the door into the bar was locked and I couldn't get out. I tried knocking on the door and pressing the buzzer above the door but it wasn't unlocked until 7:30. This meant that I was really rushed and ended up being late for where I needed to be. Also breakfast isn't served until after 7:30 so if you need to leave early like me you can't have breakfast. And be warned if you stay in room 10, you might get a surprise when you go to close your curtains and see a fat old man cooking in his underwear across the alley! I wouldn't mind staying here again but not if I needed a good night's sleep and had to be out early and not for more than one or two nights.

title: Never go to this place!!!
text: WARNING!!!!!!DO NOT STAY AT THIS HOTEL!!!!!!!!!!! This hotel is absolute joke, the worst place i have ever stayed in my entire life!!, please learn from my mistake and never go here just go to a travel-lodge or something seriously!!, me and my partner went down to london for the weekend and stayed at the hampton court palace and believe me this place is the opposite of a palace!!, it's an absolute dive run by the most despicable kind of people on this planet who will accuse you of stealing pillow cases, single and double bed covers, hand towels and so on, YES hand towels and charge you £50 without even consulting you about it and treat you like common criminals oh yes and call the fuzz on you, and due know what the police actually went with our story because we didn't actually steal a thing as they searched our bags and found nothing and who the hell will go all the way down to london from liverpool and steal old pillow cases and bed covers that looked like were purchased from a red cross shop or something. So anyway the police went with us and then the hotel people gave us the money back which they had already taken out of our account, yeah i know what your thinking the audacity right? but get this they only went and helped themselves to £60 out of our account by direct debit when we left and got the hell out of that hellhole , which i am seeking legal advise over because thats not even legal to take money out of someones account for no reason thats called fraud and thats what they are fraudsters, i really have no idea why they done such a thing to us maybe there business is going under and they thought they could take advantage of a young couple, and due know what thats the tip of the ice burg really, the actual hotel itself is sited in a very rough neighborhood me and my partner actually felt really unsafe walking round there during the day never mind at night i just wouldn't!, many hooded youths around very unfriendly, it's on top of a pub aswel where many local drunks situate and shout things at you, aslo it's right next to a council estate with roaming gangs and a basketball cage about 20 feat away from the hotel were kids blast footballs all night. Plus the hotel itself is literally falling apart as when you flush the toilet or take a shower the pipes make very loud noises and the electrics are all faulty if you leave a lamp on at night it will make an incredibly irritating noise and the room itself was in very poor condition the pillows had no cases on, there was dirty cups around the room with coffee still in them, even though they said they have house keepers really?? they can't even remember what roomed they cleaned and due know what we got charged £70 a night to stay in this dive but take my word for it this place is not worth £70 a week!!!, and what else oh yes the so called hotel manager did not even know when his own breakfast times finished as it said on the leaflet the breakfasts finish at 9:30 but he said 9:00 what the hells all that about like?? so yeah i have been staying in b n b's and hotels all round the country as i really enjoy trance events and the hampton court palace is by far the worst place i have ever stay in and run by the most miserable most unprofessional people and they need to just tare that place to the ground and go and die for what they done to us!! but despite there best efforts and the poorness of the hotel they did not ruin the weekend for us we had an amazing time at the trance event we went too but i hope that people take note of this review and stay clear and this hotel!!!!

title: Fantastic stay would definitely return!!!!
text: When we arrived at the Hampton Court Palace we were warmly greeted and given the run down of what room and things we were in, we were happily surprised to find out we had been given a family room for my and my friend! When we got to our room it was very clean and were really happy with the room! The staff were all really helpful and friendly

title: Avoid
text: I unfortunately left my hotel booking until the last minute when staying away for work last week, so I was clutching at straws, and this was one of only a few hotels still available at a reasonable price. It isn't in the greatest area of London, but not as bad as some reviews suggest. My welcome was friendly and the bar area seemed ok, not threatening or anything. My main issues upon reaching the room though were as follows: 1. The room absolutely stank of smoke. There was a big laminated sign up saying that those caught smoking would be ejected from the premises and fined, but it is a bit late for that. I might as well have smoked 50 B&H and left them lit overnight as my suit and all my clothes stunk by the morning. 2. There is a noisy water pump that I know another reviewer has referenced that went off, loudly, at random intervals throughout the night. I just couldn't get to sleep for very long despite wearing earplugs (which I always take with me just in case being a frequent traveller). 3. The temperature in the room was stifling. I wasn't necessarily expecting aircon, but a fan is very much needed. 4. The bathroom, whilst spacious, had a shower that was impossible to control the pressure of and the water came out in directions of its own will, and insisted in soaking the floor rather than me standing under it. The temperature was also variable. Having had a pretty average night's sleep, I went downstairs for breakfast at 7am, only to realise that nothing was open. I checked breakfast serving times, and realised it was from 7.30, not great for a business traveller. The other issue was knowing where to leave the key as there was no sign of life, so I had no option but to leave in the room and then head out the fire door exit. I was disappointed as I thought that the breakfast might have been a redeeming feature. Overall, not a shocking experience, but even though it was reasonable for London, (£90 last minute), it wasn't worth £90. I won't be returning.

title: Top Hotel
text: Booked at last min ,but only stayed one nite,and they was soooo helpful as we didnt know london at all ,they booked our taxi,sorted breakfast for us as we he too leave before breakfast was served.rooms were very clean......NO rodents lol ,and really friendly and soo friendly & helpful staff.....and CLIVE WOT TOP GUY !!!......deffo use again,sooo cheers guys :) ,.

title: GREAT weekend
text: Booked at last miniute and then saw the review from Kategordon! Arrived expecting some rat infested hole but found a lovely although a bit tired victorian pub. Rooms were spotless and breakfast to die for so can only think that Kategordon didnt stay at the same place. And as for the BAD ATTITUDE from Clive what rubbish he was like all the staff at the hotel friendly, polite and helpfull .

title: Olympics
text: We stayed for 5 nights during the Olympics. Nice friendly staff and good value with an excellent fry up for breakfast. It is slightly shabby but clean and has not had all its character erased. We expected to see Del Boy come in the door some night but alas he never showed.It definitely beats an anonymous hotel and we hope to go back again. On the Sat night there was music and a sing song with the regulars.Dont go if you like everything neat and tidy but ideal if you want a bit of local atmosphere.

title: Rodents!!!
text: Shabby foisty rooms & a barman owner known as clive has a bad attitude & claims to be a falklands vet paratrooper! also the worst problem is the RODENTS scurrying around the bedrooms to wich when complained to clive was met with the reply 'bollocks' wich means they refuse to acknowledge the RODENT problem in their slum! also was moved room 3 times due to MICE problems And toilet blockages. Avoid avoid avoid.

title: comfortable stay
text: staff were very friendly and helpful. The accomodation was good value, especially for london. Quite location for saying above a pub and near the railway line also in a built up area. Handy being 5 minutes away from elephant and castle tube station. Good breakfast and the room very clean and tidy and accomodating for a small child.

title: Rating is well deserved
text: No idea what dangif is on but I don't want any. Stayed here before a meeting, You get what you pay for and a bit more. For the cost its a straight forward, very clean, friendly B and B. Breakfast well cooked, slept better here than I've slept in £130 a night hotels. Quiet and safe neighbourhood. The pub bar has friendly locals, what more do you expect?

title: Must see!!
text: Hampton court was fabulous. You need the better part of the day to see it all. Audio tours are fine but spring for the real ones if possible.

title: A good value, comfortable stay
text: A corner pub - 2 adults 2 kids in a 4 bed room on 1st floor was quite comfortable. Good Value accomm. Staff were helpful and the hotel patrons friendly. Cereals & cooked English breakfast were good and mother/daughter team were very helpful. Handy to Elephant & Castle tube stn and to several buses (which we used more as they provide a view and go to many places from the nearby main road). Enjoyed an ale or two in the lounge at night, and there was music on Sat nights (which we could not really hear upstairs). Coffee and Tea etc provided in the room, but staff were happy to help with additional requests where they could. Downsides: as it was summer, it did not get dark till late, and so the outside noise could be heard easily (when kids are trying to sleep) - but not a big problem. The pub is close enough to the city, but chatting to a local cop, she suggested I don't walk around the main street talking on my cell, as I'd be a candidate for it to be stolen - although we did not encounter such incidents. Pub does not do lunch/evening meals, and no local restaurants of any note at all, so we ate out before returning at night, or simply jumped on a bus to somewhere else.

title: On the way up
text: Although this hotel does not appear to be in the most salubrious of neighbourhoods, do not be put off. It is extremely convenient for the tube and for the town centre - the greek restaurant around the corner and the Columbian with the shopping centre are excellent (try guava and home made cheese at the Columbian). The hotel is in a former victorian pub - wood panelled bar with booth seats and feature original fireplaces in the bedrooms. Clean, tidy with all the facilities you would expect. Breakfast was cooked to order and of good size and reasonable quality. Tiny moans - noise from the bar and outside til 1.30am - blisteringly hot so windows had to be open. Toilet roll holder set so far behind the toilet (and over the bath!) it required a degree of contortion to use. We were left with the impression that the current owners really care about this place and are working towards an upgrade where there might have formerly been accusations of shabbiness. For £110 per night it was a good deal and is one to watch in the future.

title: Henry nice steal!
text: What a great palace, it has it all fine building, chapel and kitchen. The grounds are massive with a few hidden small gardens. Don't get lost in the maze, put your camera over your head to see who is across the hedge. Nice to go outside the grounds to the river with its locks and traffic, picnic by the side of the river

title: Very nice place to stay
text: We went for a weekend, it was lovely, the staff and locals were very friendly. Close to tube station which only took 15 minutes into central London. Breakfast was lovely, room was very nice and comfortable, Overall a very good experience, will definitely go there again and will recommend to anyone.

title: Good value b&b in the heart of london
text: This hotel is a pub situated 3 minutes stroll from tube and bus links to central London. Do NOT be put off by location at the Elephant and Castle, it is literally 20 minutes walk from St Pauls Cathedral, right by a massive shopping centre and bus links. The breakfast is a huge and I mean huge Full english as many drinks as you want, served by charming young ladies in olde worlde genuine english pub bar. Any tourist from abroad would be impressed by the rooms and decor of the pub which is just what England should be portraying to the world. The staff could not do enough for us , the bed was one of the most comfortable I have slept in, the facilities where clean and adequate. I can not recommend this hotel more and will stay there on future visits to the capital. Value! £150 for two nights for two cannot be beaten in this class of hotel for what you get. One tip if on foot from tube don't follow gps instructions will take you longer route via other entrance to hampton street. Exit left from tube past e&c shopping centre straight to first roundabout over crossing past arcade of shops to join A3 (newington Butts) main road and about hundred yards opening on left leading to hampton street and hotel. If you are unsure Google earth will show the area.

title: Comfortable, basic accommodation with a great welcome and breakfast
text: I stayed here alone after a night out with friends and it was just right. No problems finding it on foot from Elephant & Castle tube. Check-in was friendly, quick and easy before heading out again. Room was fine, not enormous but not expensive either. Clean, quiet and decent-enough shower. Breakfast was great, warm welcome and good fry-up.

title: OK, but would not stay there again
text: I stayed at this hotel in September of 2004. I decided to write this review because I wanted to let the people know that since September of 2004, the ownership of this hotel changed, and definitely not for the better. I agree with previous travelers that the location of this hotel is perfect, however, for this kind of value you can find something better in London. The rooms were very tiny and the new staff was not friendly at all. So if you read previous "perfect" reviews, keep in mind that things changed, and you might not find the hotel you were hoping for. Be careful.

title: Location - O, noise level - X.
text: Booked thru Orbitz, great price. Got there too early, (2.5 hours before check-in) but were kind enough to let us check in at their sister property, Kingsway Park Hotel. They told us that the rooms are identical, and anyways we will be coming here for the breakfast, and the reception is only here, none at Admiral, so actually staying here might be better for us. So I guess my review will be about Kingsway. Pros: 1) LOCATION! - Less than 30 minutes away from Heathrow Airport by using the direct line to Paddington Station on the "Heathrow Express". From there only a 5 minute walk. Paddington Station connects you to many national rail lines (to Bath for example) along with the 4 underground lines (Bakerloo, Circle, District, Hammersmith & City Lines), not to mention the many bus routes that run nearby, so get yourself an "Oyster Card" in advance and have it charged for easy access to hop on and off to change lines/buses without standing in line or losing time trying to understand their currency! 2) free wifi -was ok, but slow at times 3) free english breakfast- from 7-9am, I believe consists of juices (orange, apple), cofffe, tea, milk, water, cereals(oatmeal & raisin, cornflake), bread (white, wheat) on the buffet table. They will ask you if you would like "an English breakfast" (free of course) and that comes with a boiled tomato, fried egg, sausage, bacon and beans. On the first day, I ordered all, but from the next day on, I chose just what I felt like, and they are very flexible about it! Also, be careful, because the breakfast space has only about 6 tables, fills up fast when they are busy! 4) overall, friendly staff Cons: 1) the noise- the walls are paper thin, and so you can hear conversations of your neighbors, someone taking a shower & flushing the toilet, and people walking around above you! However if you plan to be out and about and not spending too much time in the room, perhaps having ear plugs might help you to get a good night sleep. 2) the stairs- there are no elevators, so if you have heavy luggage, that will become an issue hauling it up and down those narrow stairs. The building itself is very old, and not easy to add-on elevators because of the building codes they say. We were on the 3rd floor, but its more like "the 5th floor" with all those stairs in between the floors. 3) small bathroom space- I guess if you are european or travel around in europe a lot you are used to it. I personally was amazed at how they can utilize such small space!

title: Fab location and friendly staff
text: I have just stayed at the Admiral Hotel, after being recommended here from a friend. I felt compelled to write a review after seeing all those reviews from those of you who haven't even stayed and wrote terrible reviews based on the C4 programme! When I checked in I was greeted by both Kevin and So, who were both very hospitable, and even offered to help with our bags as we were struggling a little. Kevin was extremely polite and went through a few things to do in London, walking distances to local attractions etc. I must also say the photos really don't do it justice! We were given a recently refurbished room, silver wallpaper, USB plug sockets, and comfy sheets. We also booked in for £260 for a triple room with a lovely view over the weekend,which worked out at £40 pp, much lower than advertised on four in a bed! Not sure why it was advertised at that price. 🤔 Would recommend and will be back for Winter Wonderland! 😀

title: Not one for families
text: Really disappointed in this place, had very high hopes from the pictures we saw of it and my 2 young boys really excited for their first trip to London have both given thumbs down to it. If I was travelling alone or just as a couple then maybe my opinion would be less critical but travelling as a family I have to review it in that context. Welcome/Hospitality - Despite having to check in at the hotel next door (bit of a pain when dropped at 1 place then having to drag kids & bags elsewhere) the fella on reception at arrival was friendly and welcoming and very helpful. The man on reception in the morning however I’m not sure should be the face on reception, not very friendly, very unkept look and despite making aware of an issue in our room didn’t really seem to be paying attention to us. Room - Very Clean and tidy but for a family room its tiny. Beds are right on top of each other so not much room to manoeuvre either. Take out one of the singles and got a decent triple room. Shower room is nice and newly fitted by looks of it but you can barely swing a cat in it so very tricky when it comes to putting kids to bed. Hope you don’t want to watch TV as you never get a signal which is a shame coz for once a hotel has a cracking sized TV in the room. From big TV (albeit not working) to the worlds tiniest tea cups - I mean come on!! We are in London capital of the Brits and famous tea drinkers and you give me a cup which holds a mouthful of brew!!! Get some mugs in for the love of god and a decent size kettle, the TV is forgivable the tea cups most definitely not as thats a crime against humanity!! Hotel/Lounge - lounge looks lovely but shame we didn’t get to use it firstly because it hadn’t been cleaned from builders being in to them being short staffed and breakfast being done next door. As said there are builders/decorators in so in my opinion the place should not have guests in it but it does (just us though I think) and we are having to walk past decorating supplies (bags of plaster etc) as we go up the stairs and it has the protective sheeting down all the way to our room - not a bad thing with us raising Damien and the trail of carnage he can leave behind him but still it doesn’t give a very relaxed, homely, holiday break feel if anything we feel more of a nuisance and in their way. Breakfast - Dropped a ball here again sorry guys!! Firstly you have 2 hotels sharing a breakfast room of just one of the hotels, here’s a clue - 2 doesn’t fit into 1. So first up as trying to fit double guests into half the capacity of breakfast room you’ve got guests (including young, hungry & impatient kids) queuing and waiting for a table, then you have staff looking over stretched and stressed which then transitions into the food and what we got was a very sad looking cooked breakfast!! We come from Scotland and there you get the full works its like the law to send your guests out with fully stomachs and ready to take on the sights - We are in London and I got beans, 1 sausage, 1 bacon (cold & overdone) and a very sad overcooked egg thats it!! Wheres the black pudding, the bubble, grilled tomato, mushrooms and some toast that you don’t have to make yourself which again is not good enough, a four slot toaster for 18 hungry guests to wait on. So much potential but sadly lacking in deliverance of the final product. Maybe give up on trying to accommodate families and just stick to couples, get a decent TV signal, don’t overcrowd your breakfast rooms and serve a decent breakfast and get some proper mugs & kettles in your rooms if you do nothing else at least do that!!! I don’t like being critical really, always look for the good and this place could be very good but sadly the verdict is a thumbs down and not one for families., I’ll maybe give it another shot in a couple years (without kids in tow)

title: Mr
text: Wonderful stay,staff are fantastic and very friendly, and the owner what a loverly person she made me feel at home, I would recommend this hotel to all my friends and I will be coming back again and again 💯

title: Not at all as advertised
text: The Admiral hotel at 139 Sussex Gardens is desribed by Orbitz when I booked as "a dedicated staff providing an exceptionally welcoming and friendly atmosphere. (08/05RP) Built originally in the 1850s, this elegant Victorian listed building has recently been thoroughly refurbished to a high standard, combining charm and character." When I arrived I was taken instead to the Kingsway at 143 Sussex Gardens assured it was the same hotel. My room was definitely not to a high standard, had NO charm, NO character and the owner/manager was rude and snooty. When I requested my orignal booking at 139 address, I was shown a hellhole in the basement, no window, next to the kitchen and smelling of kitchen grease. The only bright light was one of the workers did haul my heavy suitcase up the the 5th!! floor - almost vertical stairs.

title: A friendly London hotel in a great location at a very reasonable price
text: Our family of three stayed at Admiral Hotel for a full week in September 2018. It is hard to imagine a nicer and more convenient location to stay in and the hotel staff were friendly and helpful at all times (special thanks in particular to Kevin and Ali). OK, so the room was not the most fancily decorated or spacious we have experienced, but the value for money more than made up for that. The rooms are also being progressively renovated and ours was one that was still waiting to be upgraded. Even so, it had everything we needed for our stay, was clean, plenty comfortable enough ... and the point about being in London for us was more about getting out and seeing sights than hanging around in our hotel room. A delicious, hearty breakfast was served every morning that kept out motors running until well into the afternoon. We were very happy with our stay at Admiral Hotel and would have no hesitation in booking it again for our future visits to London.

title: Cosy accommodations, great location and breakfast!
text: We were very pleased with our stay at the Admiral Hotel. As is to be expected with these old buildings, quarters were tight and the bathrooms were tiny, but the bedding was very comfortable and the service was great. We started each day with a great breakfast, great service, and a short walk to Paddington Station to take us anywhere we wanted to go. Not wheelchair accessible.

title: Great location
text: Recently stayed 1 night, I booked mainly for location & fact cooked breakfast was offered. Location is fantastic, close to tube & Hyde park which is my favourite spot in london. Kevin on the front desk, was so helpful a really pleasant Guy. Our room was available when we arrived which was earlier than we expected, so that was fantastic. The room was spacious and comfortable looked recently decorated. However Carpets were filthy & bathroom was quite dated. Room was on the basement level with no aircon heat in the room was horrendous, heating system was outside the bedroom window. noise from heating was unbearable so couldnt open window @ night. Breakfast was pretty poor, tasted extremely cheap, 3/4 of us ate egg & spent all day running to the loo. Not the worst place to stay in this area @ the price range but not the best place either.

title: Very good location, 24h reception, Friendly staff
text: Hotel has excellent location and 24h reception which was very important for us as the plane had a delay and we came in London at 3am. The employee on the reception was really helpfull advising us where to go and what to see in London city.I also forgot one of my items in the hotel room when leaving back home and the staff was so nice and shipped me the forgotten item back to Slovenia. Great customer expiriance!!

title: Good location but very outworn premises!
text: This hotel is really good located. One can find that its just a few minutes walk from Paddington Station and a short ride to the city center. On the other hand, you do not have to expect a lot from an old and barely refurbished building and the rooms. The rooms are quite small (but to be honest we were 4 there), the furniture is really outdated and needs immediate replacement (chest of drawers is a bunch of firewood). A bathroom is small and needs renovation. Breakfasts were ok, but I would love some more quality to be added.

title: 10-Oct
text: Great location with friendly welcoming staff. Transport links are excellent - bus stops and Paddington station are nearby so traveling in/around London is easy. Places like Marble Arch and Hyde Park are a pleasant 15-20 minutes walk away so definitely recommend doing so (especially in the upcoming summer months!) Will definitely be coming back to this hotel in the future. Thank you to the Admiral Hotel team for making my stay enjoyable!

title: A+
text: Admiral Hotel ticked all the boxes for me... fairly priced room, great location, amazing breakfast, staff and management were very welcoming and helpful, really couldn't have asked for much more. I'll definitely be returning.

title: Don't Bother !!!
text: OMG !!! Don't bother ... Very dirty, rude staff, very noisy and very overpriced. Dirty property and rooms need TLC ... sooo overpriced !!! Most of the staff are rude including management. Very Noisy property ... not good if you want to relax. So overpriced !!! (there are many properties locally which are much better and are value for money) I suggest looking at the Best Westerns if you are looking for value for money or any other hotel if you want a good experience. At the prices they charge and the experience they provide ... Don't Stay Here !!! Location is good but definitely look at other properties in the area. Total Rip Off !!! Unfriendly !!! Dirty !!! Don't Stay Here !!!

title: Good start - wouldn't use it again
text: Stayed for two nights - on arrival, the night receptionist was very helpful with the room, finding us parking, and was generally pleasant. Location is convenient for Hyde Park and it was expensive but not massively extortionate (for London). That's the good stuff. The room was on the top floor (OK for me - but wife didn't like the climb). Inside the room we had one double bed and two singles and no additional space (see photo). The shower room was tiny - with a toilet and sink. So small that the shower doors wouldn't open fully (see photo) and I had to get in the shower sideways - bending over in the shower was impossible, retrieving a dropped soap required a yoga squat :). When we got there, the room had two old pizza boxes in it - so it can't have been properly cleaned. The window wouldn't close properly and the temperature changed from cold to hot and back again randomly over the days (the radiators never came on). Breakfast was basic but OK - once we had managed to get our instructions across to the waitress who seemed to speak almost no English (we had several false starts and sat waiting for over 20 mins one day until we checked with the waitress and discovered that she had misunderstood us to have said we didn't want any - so umm.. why were we sitting there ?!?!). However, I will definitely not return - because guests in the hotel were so noisy on both nights and our sleep was therefore very poor. The layout of the hotel was such that when our neighbours decided to shout at each other and one (apparently called Mordecai - or at least that was what they were shouting at him) left the room and stood in the tiny corridor outside our door shouting at 3am - he was directly outside our door and a few feet from our heads. Next morning, Mordecai and mates were sitting on the stairs glued to their phones while we tried to get past them with luggage. I prefer my hotels to be a little more spacious, with rooms better separated, and with less noisy and intrusive neighbours. I don't care how convenient the location is - bad sleep is a deal breaker. To cap the experience, on checkout I went to the reception (different person - this was an old guy) and stood patiently to check-out (he was on the phone). He was clearly trying to sort out a guest with a colleague as he was randomly going through a looooong list of nationalities asking what they were (which seemed pointless). This took ages and then another phone rang and he excused himself to the first phone to address the second one. At which point I gave up politely waiting - put my room card on the desk, said the room number and walked out (we had prepaid). What a very rude man... So no, we won't be back.

title: Simple and convenient
text: Stayed 3 nights in Admiral, luckily I got room upgraded with a city view and it was pretty big for one person. It’s located in perfect location, very close to Paddington Station and Hyde Park. What I appreciated more was staff wonderful service with such a good price! Happy to come back again.

title: Disappointing
text: I had read about the Admiral in "Let's Go" and expected it to be a "beautifully run family B &B" as they described. Unfortunately, the hotel changed management on our arrival and we had to go next door for our keys, etc. The new manager or concierge stayed in the front lounge watching TV with some other men and at first was not particularly friendly or helpful. I am used to small rooms and baths in London hotels but this one took the prize. As my daughter said, it was like an airplane bathroom. The shower was a tiny plastic triangle in the floor bordered by a thin curtain. Although the location is great, I would not return to the Admiral.

title: Admiral is a dump
text: This is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. Don't be fooled by the photos. I was stuck in what seemed like an attic with only a skylight and holes in the wall. Please book a well-known brand name hotel. It is worth the extra money. Staying on the street would have been better than this dump.

title: Very disappointing
text: The first thing I found very disturbing is that the actual hotel is two doors down called Kingsway Hotel - don't expect an explanation from anyone for that one. Our room was clean but tiny, on top of a neck breaking stair case! Bathroom was appalling, minute and it smelled like a sewer, probably coming from the shower drain. Staff not very friendly, I've never heard a "hello", "thank you" or "you're welcome" from them. Breakfast is ok but the room itself is a joke. Tables and chairs are crammed together so tight that there is basically not enough room to sit if there are several people in the room! I know that the price is considered as cheap for London standards, but it's still way too expensive for what you're getting out of it ! The only good thing is it's location, very close Paddington Station. Over all - not recommended !!

title: Very basic, but useful due to location
text: Perfectly placed for our trip between Paddington station and Hyde park. The hotel room was dated, simple and small. The wardrobe door was blocked closely the bed. The bathroom was fairly horrific and not clean. However, we spent almost no time there apart from to sleep and so would probably stay there again for a similar trip as it compared well on price.

title: Very Disappointed.
text: We arrived late in the evening to a room that had water leaking through the light fixture in the bathroom which shorted out our electricity. They have since moved us into 2 other rooms, unpacking and settling in has not been an option because we have now been moved to a third room. The furniture is broken, the bed coverings are torn, the carpet is worn and dirty and the bathrooms are so small that you cannot turn around in them. The rooms themselves are not large enough to fit three people, even if you have reserved a triple room. The breakfast included barely resembles something edible. Overall it feels like a run down hostel and is not worth the price that is paid nightly. This has been an absolutely terrible experience and I would suggest staying at a holiday inn or something well known

title: Ok - but
text: Initial correspondence with this hotel was great. Arrived late but had given advance notice. We had requested two adjacent rooms for two couples and off the street based on advice by other previous guest. We got one room on street on third floor and one in basement. There are no lifts and no AC. Wifi did not work except in the hotel lobby two doors down. Phones in rooms did not work. On the plus side, they did say they were sorry and gave us same rate for credit card as cash which was a small concession. Manager was nice but we only met him at checkout. Rooms were small but clean and breakfast was good. Location is short walk to Paddington Station and even closer to hop on off bus stop. For London price is great. All in all it was ok.

title: Good location
text: Stayed for a couple of nights in Feb , 2 adults , a 12 year old and a 18 month old. Great location , 5 minute walk to Hyde park in one direction, 10 min to Oxford street in the other direction and lots of restaurants and small shops 1/2 min walk away . Check in at the hotel a few doors away was quick and friendly. We were able to park the car out the front for a small charge which was an advantage. Given a room on the 1st floor , it was clean and quite pleasant for the cost . There were 4 beds , large tv , tea/coffee making facilities, vanity table , wardrobe and a small but clean and functioning shower room . Breakfast was nice in a modern dining area and the ladies that served the breakfast up were very friendly . My only complaint was that we enquired at reception regarding an highchair for breakfast and we were ensured one was available, this turned out to not be the case . This made breakfast times rather difficult. I shall return in the future but only with my 12 year old as I don't think the hotel is suited to small children.

title: Do NOT stay here - horrible!!
text: We booked this hotel based on proximity to Paddington Station. That is the only thing it has going for it. The desk clerk addressed me by first name and then tells me he is the manager and his name is MR. "whatever". Put your nose down buddy, you work in a dump. We had more than one room. The "free" internet never worked (one computer in reception). They charged us additonal 5% for using a foreign credit card. Be warned the bathroom pic appears to be the one in the hotel made just for pics. Others in our group had to come and use our bathroom as theirs were so small and awful - two of the bathrooms seemed like they were taken from old motor homes. One reeked of urine. One shower curtain was barely hanging due to being torn. Some of the towels looked like rags and had holes. Two of the shower gel dispensers were broken or empty. The beds are so old the springs poke you.The window handle/lock in one room was barely hanging. The wiring is exposed and seems unsafe. The morning desk clerk was snoring (we there 15 minutes while waiting for all our group) and then woke up and was rude when we all were walking out the door saying we had to pay which of course we did upon check-in. There were parts of tvs or something just thrown next to the sofa in the reception area. Horrible horrible hotel. It should be condemned.

title: Bathcloset not bathroom
text: The Admiral is cheap and in a good location. BUT you have to check in at the Kingsway hotel a few doors down. I guess they own both hotels. The room we stayed in had twin beds and the prefab thing they call a "bathroom". If you are over 5 feet tall you can't close the door when using the toilet and if you're over 6ft tall your head hits the ceiling in the so called "shower". Also there were always friends of the owners hanging out in the lobby and front porch area. I wouldn't recomend staying there to anyone.

title: Location, Location, Location
text: The location suited me very well - just a couple of hundred yards from Paddington Station. And at the price paid (£80 for a single for one night in London), I anticipated quite a small room and dated decor. But what I found wasn't "quite" small - it was very small indeed

title: Great hotel in central London
text: My fiancé and I were in London for a week on a recent trip to Europe and couldn't have been more pleased with this hotel. We even had a bottle of wine waiting for us when we checked in to our room. Our room was clean and the hotel's location in London was perfect. The gentleman at the front desk couldn't have been more helpful with suggesting activities for my fiancé and I. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting London!

title: Wonderful Stay
text: Right on the door step of London! The location is fantastic and was certainly one of the reasons we picked this hotel. From the moment my wife and I arrived we made very welcome by all the staff. The hotel manager Mr Jankunas helped us arrange our day around London and was very knowledge and helpful. Would certainly come back again.

title: Mold in the Bathroom
text: We knew that the hotel would not be top line but mold in the bathroom!! The beds were not even beds but matress stacked up on top of each other. There was no alarm clock and no hand soap in the bathroom. The carpet was old and looked like it hadn't been vaccumed in months. The breakfast was OK and the staff was helpful.

title: Location
text: Good location, close to tube station and Hyde Park. Free wifi but it can get slow, breakfast included (you can order English breakfast) and very basic rooms. The first I got was the tyniest I have ever been in - even for London standards. It was a single room, in the basement, just a window in the ceiling, no air conditioned and courtain in the shower which means the floor always got wet. Then I was moved to a double room on the 2nd floor. In comparison, it looked like heaven! Window to the street and glass shower doors. So run away from rooms in the basement and if you can afford it, pay a little more for a better room.

title: Scary
text: Scary hotel. My room was in the basement and it felt like I was in the cabin of a very small boat. There was a weird skylight/ceiling hatch that let a small amount of light in. There was a ceiling fan that made so much noise you would think it was nuclear-powered. And at night lying in the bed - it almost felt like you were being buried alive. But it was cheap and in walking distance to many good areas - so if you're up for adventure and you plan on not staying in the room more than sleeping hours, I guess you'll be ok.

title: Holidays
text: Arrived at Hotel on the 13TH June, We were given a room on the 4th floor no lifts, we carried our luggage up and tried to adjust but been in our seventy it was to much of a struggle. returned back to the reception desk and asked for a different room, which they did change. Today I had to ask after 8 days could they please change the sheets, I was so disappointed the shower is so small we have to stand sideways. This is our special holiday for a month , the photos we saw looked okay our room is not like that so small.The ladies at the breakfast are lovely.

title: Awful - rip off
text: Avoid, avoid, avoid... Booked this hotel as a place to rest our head after a gig. We weren't expecting much but for £100 for the night we expected more that we eventually got. Will not visit again. Firstly the Admiral Hotel's reception is actually two doors down at the Kingsway Hotel. Not a problem in itself, but it took us a good few minutes of walking through the Admiral part of this joint venture to realise there was a small sign on the door the door pointing us to the Kinsgway. This immediately raised some concerns as to security as we were able to fully explore the Admiral Hotel without seeing any staff. When we got to our room it was still being cleaned so we waited outside for 5 minutes while it was finished. When we were left alone in the room we realised that it had been a while since this room had been given any TLC. Lights did not work, sockets were broken and the bathroom was tiny with a dirty and cracked sink. We hadn't planned to spend any real time in the hotel so we dropped our bags off and headed out. On our way from Paddington Underground Station to the hotel we unfortunately found that the end of the road was an area where prostitutes gathered. Admittedly the hotel can do nothing about this but I think that families and lone female travelers should be aware of this fact. Again the hotel front doors were wide open. There was a member of staff smoking in the doorway though. The road noise during the night was not too bad and the rooms are double glazed. However the bigger issue is noises within the hotel. At around 6

title: Awful
text: I spent weeks trying to find a reasonable hotel in London for my little boys birthday. The Admiral looked clean, fresh and the price was good, according to their website! The location was very good too! But when we arrived the reception showed signs of a run down hotel, grubby and tatty. We were given our room card and went next door as the Admiral does not have a reception. Our room was upstairs, I have to say my heart sunk it was awful, the radiator and paint work was caked in dirt and the cupboards and doors smeared with dirt. I sat on the bed and the mattress was that old I could feel the base. I peeled back the sheets to find hairs and a stain which was coming from the mattress protector, I peeled back the bottom sheet to find a huge blood stain. The cleaner was working in another room so I went to see her, she came and looked and said 'its not dirty its just a stain'!!! Oh my God what kind of people think this is acceptable? The receptionist did offer to change the whole bedding but I was too disgusted to stay. We left and got a room across the road at a B&B, a family of 3 had to share a double bed but this was better than a night at the Admiral!

title: Don't bother!!
text: Booked in for one night this week. Reception is not in this hotel, but 2 doors up the street. Given a double room on the 4th floor

title: The Adrimal Hotel is one of London's Best kept Secrets!
text: We have stayed at the Admiral Hotel, on All of our Visits to London. The Hotel is a Fantastic Location, in London. Within easy walking distance to both Paddington Station, and Lancaster Gate Tube Underground. The Hotel is Family Owned and Opperated by a Superb Couple named: Frank & Gloria. They go out of their way to make each Guest feel at home, while staying with them. The hotel is a converted Victorian Townhouse, located on lovely tree lined Sussex Gardens. A Traditional English Breakfast, Welcomes you each day of your stay at the Hotel. The rooms are very Comfortable, Quiet, and all are insuite Bathrooms

title: Gobsmacked
text: Only good thing is hotel is 5 minutes walk from Paddington tube and nice restaurants near by. After thinking someone was being helpful showing us where hotel was but then asking for money for a cuppa for being helpful (yes I know not the hotels fault) but just be on your guard as this guy kept touching my arm so watch if round that area! Booked into reception which looked messy and all I could think of was faulty towers! Given a room key and told to go to a building 2 doors away. The room was up one floor with creaky stairs and an unsafe bannister that if you fell on it could be an accident waiting to happen. The bedroom you could hardly move in. Carpet looked about 30 years old, dust all over. Furniture dated and draws broke. Telly on wall and wires hanging down all over the place. Bedding should have been ditched many years ago and it makes me wonder if it had been washed as the pillow had been turned inside out. The bathroom was tiny! You had to sit on toilet sideways as was pressed up against the dirty shower. Was meant to stay there 4 nights but moved after the first night.

title: Good value
text: I needed one night accommodation without paying more than £100. This room cost me £90 for bed and a really good breakfast. Good size room plus a good shower. Tea and coffee in room plus a selection of sweets. I recommend this place as good value.

title: Good stay
text: This is the 2nd time we've stayed at the admiral and found all the staff helpful, the rooms are lovely and clean we booked a twin and a single but was offered a family room with a double and two singles, there was plenty of room and the beds were comfy, breakfast small but edible plenty of cereal and toast to fill up on also coffee tea and juice, will stay again

title: Delicious dinner
text: We had one of their speciality pies and it was lovely. We were not that happy with our table and the very nice wait lady moved us to a better table. We were on the upper deck. It is a pub designed like Nelsons ship the Victory. Would highly recommend.

title: Convenient and Clean
text: We were only staying in London for a handful of days and found Admiral Hotel to be a perfect fit to our needs. It was a small room but it is also London. So given that it was perfect, a clean bed and a place to shower. The point was not to relax in a resort but to explore the area all day and sleep in peace at night. It was about a mid range hotel as far a cost but the convenience factor was perfect. Two blocks from Paddington Station to the airport. One block to the nearest city wide bike rental station and only a few blocks to Hyde Park area. The Staff was friendly and took care of our room perfectly during our stay. The breakfast was always fresh and the two ladies that take care of it are worth a million dollars for all the effort they give to make the stay comfortable and peaceful. Well done and money well spent on our part Thank You Annette and John

title: Budget
text: We arrived and had to go to another hotel 2 doors down to check in and get the key. When trying to use the keycard to enter the hotel we were staying, it would not open. Had to get management to open the door for us. Explanation for this was a new keycard system was in place. We got to the room which as of an ok size and room to move about. TV was a 32" which is surprising as most hotels offer a 19-24". Cupboard doors were broken as well as the bottom half of the bed. The bathroom itself was small, especially as my legs were tightly placed under the sink. The showers water would not get hot nor would the sink. There was free wifi to log into. Breakfast provided was a "full English" with 1 egg, 1 bacon, 1 sausage, 1 peeled plum tomato and beans. You could make your own toast, tea, coffee, cornflakes or muesli. Orange and apple juice were also on offer. The waiting staff were very friendly and polite. I think that with a few repairs, updates and adjustments, this could be a gem at the price that it is, especially the location about a 3 minute walk from Paddington tube station.

title: Awful, avoid at all costs!
text: Brought the wife and 18 month old baby to London for 3 nights whilst visiting the UK. Spent £446 for 3 nights. Got put on the 5th floor (no lift, 5 bags, small child). Would not give us a different room when asked. 28° outside, we were in the attic room with only a tiny window for ventilation. No air! Rats in wall cavity. Breakfast was awful. Cocktail sausage, one bit bacon, fazzled egg, beans. Two choice of cereal, cheap tea bags, coffee rubbish.

title: We Booked The Admiral But Got Put In The Kingsway Park Next Door!
text: My partner booked this hotel aftering seeing it online, and calling up the owner. It was my birthday so we wanted a nice weekend away in London, something basic, not too far away from the main attractions and not too expensive. The hotel we booked was called the Admiral Hotel. It says on the website that you have to check in at the Kingsway Park hotel, which was situted a few steps away. This was fine. The Admiral looked nice on the website pictures, showing a nice modern bar, and clean rooms. It was this hotel we had booked! Once into the Kingsway Park hotel, we where then told thats where we would be staying. It seems that's where everyone stays! It appeared the nice clean Admiral Hotel was not having guests! This was indeed empty! We checked in early, and where told where our rooms where. As other reviews say, the stairs where very steep and there was no lift or warning which didnt help someone in my party that had a knee complaint, but i havent let that interfere with the review, as i could of enquired upon booking. My room had a terrible smell as soon as i walked in. I wasnt expecting anything less though, as the hotel upon entry was tired, shabby, had a smell to it, and had dirty woodwork and walls, and frayed carpets. The divan bed was 2 singles together, with a badly stained base. The lamps had stained and burnt lampshades. The furniture was dated and didnt fit in the room. There was no fancy chairs and furniture like the i've just seen on the Kingsway Park Hotel website! We kepting hurting ourselves when walking around the crammed room on the furniture. The portable tv did work, but the picture wasnt quite viewable, i felt like i had double vision after looking at it. The main critisim is aimed at the toilet which was a portocabin shower and loo in one type of thing, which was placed in the room, but then was incorporated into the paintwork. It smelt, had mould on the shower, and when sitting on the loo, your foot was in the shower area, which was very small. The bottom of the door was also covered in rust. I did not use the shower at all, as it was very off putting. My partner did, and he was fine with it. The other room we booked, for other parties, was very similar but they had a bath, and a more normal bathroom, which had a terrible smell of damp in it. I didnt sleep well during my two night stay. The bedding was a sheet, and then an extremely 'itchy' blanket, with a floral throw over the top. This was covered in stains. Me and my partner had one small pillow each, there was no other bedding to use. Breakfast was included in the price described as a 'full english' we went down for breakfast which was served in small room crammed with tables in the basement. Two ladies, whom we saw cleaning rooms served breakfast. The option was cereal, toast and the cooked breakfast was a boiled slice of bacon, egg (scrambled,fried or boiled) plum tomato and a sausage. I did not recieve what i ordered for breakfast on both mornings, and didnt rectify it as the person serving breakfast could not fully understand my english. Our bed was made while we where out, and there where towels left in the room. The manager/owner was around for most of the time, and there seemed to be approx 6-7 other guest there, excluding my party. There was no problem returning. The front door was unlocked and there was a gentleman on the desk. The latest we returned was around 11pm. The area of this hotel sussex gardens, has a whole host of hotels similar to this one. They all had vacancies in there window, but did look a lot cleaner and friendlier. I do not recommend this hotel to anyone. It did us for the weekend, because we had no choice once we got there. Location was great for us, lots of restuarants, and paddington station near by, but for the price, which can seem cheap, im sure there are others for the same price in better condition. In my opinion, it wasnt clean, wasnt comfortable, the food wasnt good, so it was a huge let down for me. Luckily the great company i had, and London being so fantastic didnt make my weekend a complete let down. I have written this review within 7 hours of returning as i would hate anyone to have a weekend ruined, and this hotel would do that! Don't be fooled thinking they put you up in the Admiral hotel, when infact your staying at the Kingsway Park. The website for the Kingsway Park Hotel says it has recently been refurbished! Id of hated to of seen what it was like before! Both the Kingsway Park and The Admiral Hotel have individual websites, the pictures on both are extremely different to what you get, so there not worth looking at! Please look at reviews for the Kingsway Park when booking the Admiral as thats where you will probably stay!

title: Great Location!
text: We stayed at the Admiral for a week at the end of July and found the location absolutely perfect for our sight seeing needs. The room was clean and neat if blandly furnished. The ensuite bathroom was of the prefab variety and definitely on the small side. Breakfast was very good and we were happy to have a choice between full English and continental. Our room faced the street and traffic noise was pretty loud since we kept our window open (very warm weather while we were there). I would absolutely recommend the Admiral to others.

title: Great central location, nice hotel, friendly staff
text: We stayed in this hotel for one night on a city break to London. Its walking distance from trains/tubes and near nice pubs and restaurants. They offer baggage storage before and after check in/out and they staff were extremely friendly and helpful. They also have onsite parking. The rooms were small, but clean and very good value for money. Beds were comfortable and they have coffee/tea facility in rooms as well as TV and free WIFI. Very nice hotel and i will definitely recommend it!!

title: OK but, comments on specific rooms
text: I stayed there with 4 of my friends. We originally had booked two doubles and a single, but when we saw the rooms, we changed to a double and a triple. The single we were shown was in the basement down a small, twisty staircase . It was a tiny, dark room with an even tinier shower stall/WC and none of us wanted it. So two people ended up in room 3, and three of us ended up in room 9. Room 3 wasn't bad. It was the easiest room in the hotel to reach: it was up the first flight of stairs: a straight shot. The room had cross ventilation, and a decent sized shower stall/WC. Room 9 was up a floor or two more and you had to go around corners/landings. 9 did not have cross ventilation, and it was hot! The bathroom was very small, probably like what you would find in a recreational vehicle or a boat. I've included a photo of the bathroom in room 9. Both 3 and 9 looked out the back of the building, really not much of a view, but probably quieter than if we had been fronting Sussex Gardens. The staff was nice, and the breakfasts were fine. The rooms were acceptably clean. The staff did help us bring our bags up when we arrived. You still have to check in with the hotel 2 doors down (same management/ownership.) One possible problem in the future: apparently they have applied to have a bar/club in the evenings on the ground floor. I got the feeling it might be open to the public, not just the people staying there. Not sure how that will work out as far as noise, and security.

title: Cheap and cheerful. Got what we payed for.
text: We stayed here for one night as a family of four. Reviews weren't good but we thought we got what we payed for. When you pay less than a hundred pounds for a family of four in the city centre within walking distance to lots of the sights then it's great. Paddington tube was 2/3 mins walk. Hyde park around the corner. What more can we say. The breakfast is not a full English, it was bacon beans egg and a tomato but it was close at no extra cost. It was clean and pleasant. We even got to park the car for 24 hours for £15. Bargain. We would recommend to friends and stay again.

title: Breakfast staff outstanding
text: We stayed there 4 nights from November 25-29th. While the ensuite bathroom is tiny and the shower smaller yet, we always had hot water, even with 4 of us sharing a room. If you do the hokey pokey and wash one side and then another it works. The room felt very warm, and we ended up opening a window to cool it down even in November. Three of our four nights were very quiet. One night we did hear the bell ringing at night and stomping about and doors slamming despite a sign on the door telling people to go to another hotel at night to get a key. So your stay as in any other hotel anywhere depends upon the courtesy of others sharing the premises. Susan in the breakfast room served us each morning with a bright smile and cheery disposition. Full English breakfast consists of toast, tea or coffee, eggs cooked to order, Canadian bacon, beans and tomato. Oatmeal or porridge, orange juice and cornflakes are also available. With that meal to start the day, the ladies often skipped lunch. Paddington Station is a couple of blocks away which was great. While not perfect, the hotel is clean and the staff friendly and I would stay there again.

title: Nightmare
text: Worst hotel I've ever stayed in my entire life. Did not get the room I paid for, cracks on the wall, smelly very old style furniture and beddings. Did not get the room even on the second day. I got a very small one no space, no windows, very smelly very broke down. The roof fan almost fell down, it was noisy and just above the bed. I told the staff that this is not what I've paid for, they told me that I'll get a complementary wine next day morning. Not acceptable. Worst staff, worst hotel. NEVER AGAIN

title: go elsewhere!
text: checked in at sister hotel 2 doors down, then sent to another sister hotel across the road ( large family!)..booked this hotel because it had a triple room ( £120.00 p/night) really small dated rooms with the smallest toilet/shower rooms ever, so small the sink was in the bedroom ! breakfast (after the queue) was basic and a free-for -all... top tips...pay more and stay elsewhere! simple

title: pleasant experience
text: I booked 4 rooms at this hotel based on the admiral write up and photographs. On arrival, I was told that 1 room had been cancelled because I had made 2 seperate bookings (an extra person joined us so needed extra room) they assumed I had mistakenly booked my fourth room. They only thought to ask on the day of our arrival. So we had to split up, two of the 4 rooms ended up in the next door hotel, kingsway,. This was no the best start. The staff were very pleasant and helpful, with advice and directions. My sister had a bottle of wine when her room key didnt work and she was up and down 6 flights of stairs to sort it. Which was nice of them. The hotel was nice and clean. Comfy sofa in reception at kingsway. Breakfast is basic but tasty. Dining are is trendy. My room was on the top floor, absolutely knackering climbing all the stairs. The room was very small for a double, no room to walk around the bed, toilet door closed but was a struggle to get it passed the toilet. Shower was small and not strong enough, could have done with a notch more power. On the plus side, the bed was very comfy, big tv with great picture and range of channels, a fan which was a life saver in the warmer months.very clean and tidy room. I wouod stay again because its good value for money on the whole-just unfortunate to get top floor bedrrom.

title: Avoid
text: Hotel booked well in advance. Group of six ladies. Not checked reviews until the day of travel and as all others,we were kept waiting and not put in the hotel stated on confirmation. We were told that the manager was not available and after a while relocated in to a hotel near by!!. The breakfast offered at the Lancaster was continental so we complained and went back to the original place for breakfast the next day, which to be fair was good. The area was eclectic and lots of cafes and bars nearby as was Hyde park and paddington station. I would not revisit thus hotel but area was good.

title: Disappointing
text: I had some problems with this hotel. I booked months in advance - June to stay in September - and even then they put me in a room downstairs (should I say basement?). Kind of claustrophobic as there was no window, only a hatch that could be opened or closed depending on the weather! Then the TV remote control was not working... the bathroom box (closed with a plastic curtain) had not a single soap dish or any other place where to put the soap while you were taking a bath (unless you put it on the floor)... Details that may cause some discomfort. The good points were the location, at lovely Sussex Gardens, a few steps from Paddington Station (express train to Heathrow) and the complete English breakfast.

title: Customer service better than 5 star hotels!
text: Stayed here for a few days with my girlfriend to celebrate her birthday, and our experience exceeded all expectations considering the price we paid for our double room. Check in was swift, and the reception helped us with our bags to our room on the first floor. The room was a nice size and very clean, with a little balcony, which was a pleasant suprise! On the night of my girlfriend's birthday, we returned to our room to find a bottle of champagne and a happy birthday note!! Never experienced anything like that before and my girlfriend was chuffed! Also, I thought I knew London very well, but the receptionist recommended some great attractions which we visited during the day, as well as booking us a table at a nice little Italian restaurant nearby where he got us a 20% discount! The only dissapointing part of the stay was having to leave! Will definitely be staying here again in the future :)

title: Good but more bad
text: Recently stayed : bathroom door hanging off , room door would not lock from inside , walls so thin that I had to ask couple in room opposite to keep the noise down , room key cards not working , tv not working , had to really push night porter to change room as fan in ceiling above kept us awake , 5% charge for paying bill by card On the plus : manager found us a room to sleep in when night porter said they were full and he did come to try and sort the noise out , guys in reception did come up and help with the room swipe key card .

title: beware - bed bugs
text: i stayed in this hotel in March, and never ever again. I was covered in bedbug bites the next day - unfortunately had an allergic reaction as well so had visit to doctor as a result. The hotel promised to refund my money but after months of emails and getting Trading Standards involved, they finally sent me a cheque but only for half the cost. I also reported them to Environmental Health on advice of my doctor who confirmed bedbugs in the room when they visited about a month later - so no commitment to health and hygiene and subsequent visitors.

title: Very Disappointing
text: A strange set up with the hotel reception in a different hotel a couple of doors away. The hotel was chosen for its location and the double room was reserved 5 months prior to our stay, our excitement on arrival soon turned to disappointment when we entered the room to see twin beds waiting for us. Although the room was clean, there was no soap or shower gel in the bathroom... When we asked about changing rooms we were informed they were fully booked, and the person on reception started looking through desk drawers in the hope that some soap might appear....hilarious really!! Thanks, but no thanks...look elsewhere!

title: OK, but no more
text: I just got back from spending 5 nights at the Admiral Hotel. I have decided to write this review since according to the previous reviews there is an image that the hotel is perfect. It is not the case. Disadvantages: 1. Shower and toilet are REALLY SMALL, about 1 meter x 1 meter size, and the water pressure is very weak. 2. There are a lot of staires. 3. The breakfast is: 0NE pease of bacon, omelet from ONE egg and toasts. 4. The rooms is not quiet, there is the bell at the entrance of the hotel that alarms all visitors of the hotel. 5. The staff is not friendly. Advantages: 1. Good location, (one minnute from tube (paddington)) 2. Clean enough. 3. Low prices (about 65 &) I will not stay at Admiral hotel again.

title: Ok "hotel"
text: The room was too small for 4 people and defiantly not enough space for luggage and shopping bags to place. The bathroom was quite ok everything functioned very well! The sheets were not exactly cleaned out since we found that they were just flipped over to cover the makeup stains on the pillow case since I could see the same stain on the other side. It also bothered me the fact that there is no lift and no one in the hotel would help you with the luggage. Breakfast was okay not that big of a deal but for a small hotel it was good. Would not return if I had too since it was too much if a struggle for all the family with all the luggages.

title: WOW!!
text: This is the best hotel i have been to in years if you like being in a nice hotel that has good service and is not so expensive come here its really good!

title: Very good service :)
text: Went there in november and had a great time! The hotel manager told us about amazing things to do and showed us bars and great asian resturant! If I ever go to London again I will deffinetly stay there again :)

title: Cheap and Cheerful
text: I was looking for a cheap place to rest my head which was not going to break the budget of the Not-For-Profit organisation I was there on behalf of. Staff were ok, room was clean but smelt a little musty, and the bedroom was a little noisy (I was at the front) The location was perfect however and was only a 3 minute walk from Paddington Station, and a 4 minute walk to Lancaster Gate underground. I was looking forward to my inclusive english breakfast, but alas it was OK, but microwaved to get it to temperature - not the best combo. Still there was also cereals and copious quantities of toast. Steer clear of the coffee however and report back if the tea is any better.

title: Customer service unheard of!
text: Stayed here for the night. Chaos, didnt seem to expect me, disappeared and left only me in reception!(thought it was a set up,looking for hidden cameras) Finally came back, not friendly or welcoming. Given room after prompting and long wait. Given key for room on top floor! OMG bring the oxygen!,left luggage half way up and sought help. Small room, stained bedding and double not twin! On raising issues his manner inferred he was doing me a favour. Offered to split beds and make myself, said no bedding could have alternative room in a few hrs. Gave up,just didnt get the point!! Did offer to refund which was pointless on the Marathon Weekend in London and i questioned how i was going to find an alternative. My daughter arrived later and attempted to obtain pillows same prison officer approach and if he ignored long enough and kept talking in native language to others she would go away. Positive is location and breakfast and waitress smiley and pleasant.But dont go there. Twin for well over £100 but what for?? Sorry folks one of the worst! Dont rush to this one.

title: Unprofessional
text: Quite a badly run hotel. Reception is now 2 doors down in another hotel. When checking in new guests they open your door to see if your room is free. Renovations are happening and sanding, painting and whistling go on until midnight. They moved my belongings to a different room while i was out without telling me. Room and bathroom sizes are standard london small and breakfast was reasonable. There are so many hotels in this area, which is a very handy area for transport and restaurants, others must be better.

title: a bog standard hotel with great location
text: booked on the day and managed to get reasonably cheap (£58) for a double, didn't actually book this hotel but the sister Kingsway-doesn't state that you will be in a different hotel as I hadn't read reviews! its got simple cleanish room, freshly painted but still a bit tatty round edge's. if you want a cheap hotel in a very good location then this will do for you. Be warned there are a lot of stairs!

title: Cleanliness clearly not a priority
text: On arrival we were told we had been upgraded to a larger room and upon entering the room we realized why!somebody else had obviously asked for a new room!!straight away we noticed that you could hear every footstep on the hardwood flooring above us from the bar/dining room and as u can imagine this is a busy area in the hotel.this made for a very disruptive sleep and then first thing in the morning when they started to serve breakfast!but this was not our main concern,they hygiene in this hotel is very poor and our room and in particular the bathroom was horrendous,so bad in fact we never showered the next morning as the smell coming from the shower cubicle was disgusting.the whole hotel is very grubby and in need of a paint job and the carpets steam cleaning!if we needed to stay more than the one night then we would have cancelled but luckily we literally just neede a place to sleep.the FULL English breakfast is also something of a phenomenon,u get 1 very tiny slim sausage,1egg,1bacon and some beans it wasn't quite ur typical full English....all in all if you want a place to stay for a period of time and enjoy your stay then look for something better as u will not enjoy ur stay here.if u just need to get ur head down for a night then I guess it's ok

title: Warm and freezing
text: We stayed 3 nights at the hotel. First We arrived we needed to wait for our room 15minutes after 1.pm. The hotel reception is in an other hotel which is 2 doors away so it's close to Admiral. As soon as we got the room we went there wich was at the 3rd floor and had no elevator so we carried our heavy bags to the 3rd floor, where the stairs were so tiny. At the first night there was no heating out there was only 5 degree. I got cold. The second and third night the heating was repaired but than it was so hot that even the cleaning lady (during tha day) opened the room window. The room was so small that we couldn't move. The room is not that clean as I can read from the rewievs. We were told that there was free wifi included at the price. We got the password but at our room we hardly could use the internet. When we went down to have breakfast we could catch the wifi. The breakfast is quite good. The english breakfast is served by a waitress and there is continental breakfest too. The location is excellent. The Paddington undergraund station is 4 min. walk, there are 3lines there and there is also a railway station. Around the underground there are many restaurants. There are steak houses and fast food restaurants as well. Once we walked throw the Hyde Park to the center of the city it took 20 minutes. I did not expect a five star accomodation but a clean and nice room with a good service which we unfortunately did not get.

title: Does The Job
text: To be honest, I have stayed in many hotels in London and its not generally the individual hotel that is bad but simply the value for money obtained in London as a whole. Infact the Admiral was above average for many of the hotels I have visited although I did read its reviews before booking and was to my surprise that it did not hold the weight of those reviews and the reason I proceeded to book was of a reccommendation. Staff just about give you anything you need and have a 'family' type attitude toward you. During my 8 night stay there I did encounter regulars whom frequented the hotel on a weekly basis and due to the abundance of hotels near by, took this in as a good factor of the place. The stairs can be a teaser if your on the upper floors however. As I brosed with the help of the receptionist, I saw that some rooms had full bathroom/tub and tiled rooms and some were a unit waterproof styled based cabin bathroom. I guess its a matter of preference where mine would not sooo much be the size but more the cleanliness and they, at least mine, were cleaned well daily leaving that antibacterial smell that you would expect from a toilet which had been cleaned well. Breakfast great though you should pop out for one or two days to a local cafe to get an altered taste.
