title: I would not recommend
text: No air conditioning. Our room was small and we had to carry all of our luggage up four flights of stairs. The breakfast however was good and good service for breakfast. There was a step up to the bathroom that was NOT fun to negotiate in the middle of the night. Also, our shower drain took about 20 minutes to drain. The area the hotel is in in great though.

title: good location
text: We stayed 3 nights in this hotel. It has a good location but it the rooms were very small and the charged us for a extension night much more as we paid the other nights. We were to lazy to look for a new hotel thatswhy we stayed. But we had the feeling we got ripped off.

title: Great Choice - Friendly Service
text: We have stayed at the Admiral during two trips to London. We have found the Hotel to be neat and clean, with a very friendly staff. An excellent breakfast awaited us each morning. The hotel is centrally located in London, with easy access to many famous attractions. We will surely want to stay at the Admiral during our next trip to London.

title: good hotel in a pleasant area
text: First trip to the city for many years and very pleased with our hotel choice . The hotel was as advertised ..room was comfy very clean,great breakfast each morning served by pleasant staff. Great area, just a few mins from paddington , local shops,cafe,restaurants. each day we walked through Hyde Park to our destinations. We enjoyed our few days, felt safe and well looked after by all the staff we met .

title: Fantastic Service, location and friendly staff.
text: I have been in this hotel more than 10 times. Perfect location for London Sights. 300 meter walk from Paddington Station. The rooms are small, but nice and very clean. There are two hotels - Kingsway Park & the Admiral. I had a triple room this time at the Admiral and the room was very good. Cleaned every day and new towels - perfect. The whole staff were extremely helpfull and the manager Mr. Kin in very kind, very helpfull, and he gets us to feel very much at home at the hotel. If you have a problem Mr. Kin will sort it out for you at soon as possible. English breakfast served very quickly and it was super. I will definately stay there again. This it a very good value for your money .It will be difficult to find a better place to stay in London on the same level.

title: Triple Room
text: We arrived at Heathrow Airport and quickly hopped on the Heathrow Express which took us to Paddington Station. This hotel is a 300m easy walk from the station. Our room had a double and single bed which suited our needs. The room was small but adequate. We liked the fact that the hotel was small and quaint and typical English style. Breakfast was good - a cooked breakfast was made as you ordered. The staff were extremely helpful with information on where to go. We walked to Hyde Park from the hotel which was easy. It is also on the Big Bus Hop on Off route, which we found to be a great way to get around. This hotel is a fantastic place to stay for the price you pay - great location, comfortable rooms.

title: Admiral Hotel is a great choice
text: If you want to stay in a friendly, clean Bed & Breakfast hotel in London, this is a perfect choice for you! Everything was great. A good personally served and cooked breakfast, clean rooms and friendly staff. We payed £56 per night for our twin room which was good value for money. You live close to central London, Hyde Park and Paddington Station, just a few minutes by tube or a 20 min walk to the center parts. Perfect! One note, though. If you're having trouble with stairs then this place may not be for you. A narrow (carpeted) staircase and many floors (4?) may be too much for some people. No lift/elevator available.

title: Good Service, friendly staff
text: Fab loc Near Pad Stn Good staff Great site Good bkfs Walk to oxford st Clean, mod linen- many rooms quite well furnished Nice decor, mod paint works Mr Kin and Mr So very friendly n helpful managers David nite manager v friendly n helpful

title: Great Value Hotel!!!!
text: Arrived to a friendly welcome, clear and full explanation of hotel entry, breakfast times, checkout etc. ( not unlike the larger chains!!!!) The room was clean, and welcoming, with good quality linen on the beds. This included, complimentary chocolate, soap, shampoo and a rather nice bottle of sparkling Rose wine!!!!! Along with a handwritten note welcoming and wishing us a pleasant stay. The bathroom was compact, but clean with adequate shower, good quality towels and plenty of hot water....good extractor too, that worked...... Breakfast, although served in a limited seating dining room was adequate and served quickly and well presented. A limited selection of cereals, plenty of tea and coffee, plenty of 'self serve' toast.....one 4 slice toaster may not look like it can cope.....but......it does!!!!! A few minutes patience and everyone gets their toast......( the dining room was full when we had breakfast....and I only waited for minutes.......seriously it was stress free!!!) We've stayed here twice now, and will stay again!,,,, The over and above helpfulness when I realised I'd forgotten to bring some e-tickets......the staff were really helpfull ( I don't think it's a regular service from the reception) and printed them out with no questions asked and just the whirr of the printer. The hotel has two buildings, just a step from each other, so DON'T be put off by the thought. Deffo worth a try if you like the cunningly disguised B+B....that has hidden HOTEL features!!!!!

title: Great Value for Money
text: I am shocked by some of the reviews here of the Admiral Hotel. Yes, the reception is in an adjacent building but the staff were excellent and very friendly. Our bathroom was absolutely spotless - much cleaner than the 4star hotel we stayed in the night before in Bournemouth! Shampoo and soap were provided along with clean towels and clean bedding. I agree that this is not a luxury hotel but I've stayed in much worse for a lot more money. The next time we stay in London this will be my first choice!!

title: Location is the only good thing about it
text: Good location for accessing London shopping and sightseeing, but pokey small room with limited facility and bare minimum breakfast.

title: VERY SMALL ROOM
text: We stayed there 5 nights as a family of 4 ..no lift ..2 storeys of stairs with heavy luggage ...room is very very small especially the bathroom ..was not suitable for 4 persons ..breakfast is very poor in 2 days we were only given 1 sausage 1 piece of bacon and 1 egg ...not worthit for the money paid ..1 good thing is that is central and close to station and shops

title: Better than expected!
text: This hotel was better than expected! The room was nice and clean, the value is ok, the location is excellent and the staff is very friendly and helpful! It's not a luxury hotel but it's a perfectly ok hotel. We will not hesitate to use this hotel again.

title: What a spoiler especially after a 13hr flight!!!
text: With a jet lag and arrived at an early morning we just want a comfortable room to relax and recover our energy To our surprise we got to carry our 2 large bags through staircase to level 3!!! Maybe I had a wrong perception that all hotels in London have lift...our first day in London ended with back spasm and cramps!!! The room can hardly fit three pax.. I am sure glad that Malaysian budget hotels are world class!!!

title: Small- that's my only complaint...
text: I stayed at the Admiral from Nov 5th to the 11th of 2007. I kind of understand the less then positive remarkes made about the hotel in some aspects but not all of them . it's location is great and the staff is friendly. Mr. So and Maria you went out of your way to help and I appreciate it immensley! i guess because I don't travel too often and I don't stay in that many hotels I don't have such high and mightly standards, but my room which was at the very top of the hotel as neat and clean as it could be and I just considered the staircase good excercise! The daily breakfast was delicious and the beautiful Hyde park was a short walk away as were all the prime tube stops. It's no big problem to me that the check in is too hotels away. it's like ten steps people, not a huge in convenience! The day I checked out my cab arrived early and on time. A good experiance overall, and I may come back again. My only advice is don't call past 9 pm UK time. The night porter is a total box of rocks!

title: Excellent Hotel and Staff
text: Very good service and friendly welcome from senior managers Mr KIN and Mr SO Very good location close to paddington station and hyde park area Very good value for money and attention to detail with good range of information for tourists

title: Over priced.
text: My husband and i recently stayed here for 5 nights. The hotel which we booked thinking it was a quaint b&b as it was advertised was clearly not the case. Although it does have a fabulous location with a quick walk to Hyde park and paddington train station. The room was clean and comfortable but have had better for the price we paid. The front desk staff are not very friendly or helpful unless your a female travelling alone and it seemed you got undivided attention. Breakfasts included in our price and was very very simple and the breakfast lady is quite rude. As it is a 3 star hotel i didn't expect anything flash but was over priced for what it was.

title: Avoid going to this hotel, for your own safety!
text: My friends and I made A RESERVATION THOUGH BOOKING.COM quite in advance before our arrival (it was the beginning of September and we were supposed to stay in this hotel at the beginning of October). Just to be sure the reservation ended well, I ALSO WROTE AN EMAIL TO THE HOTEL. The owner, Mr. So, reassured me that everything was fine and he was looking forward for our arrival. Before flying to London, I wrote a new email to Mr. So to let him know we will be arriving to his hotel at 11 pm. He replied to me that the rooms were ready and, again, he was warmly waiting for us. So warmly that WHEN WE ARRIVED THE ROOMS WERE NOT AVAILABLE!!! Only the doorman and another couple experiencing our same mess. Of course, the "poor" doorman could not explain what was going on...he tried clumsily to find us another accomodation. In his opinion we should have paid for the price difference. While the couple agreed, we spent more than an hour fighting on the phone with booking.com: at the end, they find us a hotel in the neighbourhood (the pleasant and perfectly-managed Tudor Court Hotel) without paying any extra. The owner of the Admiral hotel was unreacheble when we arrived

title: Good value - Clean - Comfy Beds - Central location good well licated hotel for great price. NR Hyde Park /Paddington tube
text: Stayed at Admiral hotel 18-21st Oct '12 in triple room - which was small but adequate for our requirements and good for the price we paid. It was much better than the 3 of us expected Its a well located hotel if you wish to enjoy London for a few days Rooms/sheets v clean. Comfy beds and breakfast good. Helpful courteous staff - what more can you ask for Got a great rate for 3 night stay Thanks to Kin, one of the management staff who was very courteous, friendly and helpful Sadly not enough people give positive reviews - usually people only write complaints, which is a shame for some hotels. If you want to visit London on a budget but still have the benefit of a good clean B and B - visit the Admiral Can Recommend ASK Rest. 5 mins walk nearby for Italian meals/ Really nice Rest /Meal at reasonable price CAROL BAILLIE. LESMAHAGOW SCOTLAND

title: Admiral Hotel
text: Well equipped room, spotless and comfortable. Quiet yet minutes from Paddington. Staff were extremely polite and helpful, in particular Kin. Would definitely recommend - good value for money for a London hotel. Keep up the good work!

title: Good value, great service
text: Had a 2 night stay. Room very clean, comfortable and quiet. Nice breakfast. Excellent service. Great location for exploring London. Mr Kin was very hospitable and helpful. Would definitely use this hotel again.

title: Not good
text: Just back from 2 night stay at Admiral hotel London but there was nothing admireable about this place. We had a triple room on the third floor up steep stairs. There is no lift. Our room was tiny, very hot with a very pokey shower room. I was disappointed with the bathroom there were hairs in the shower ! The shower was more of a dribble than a shower, pathetic ! Beds were ok. Light bulbs missing, broken dressing table door very old coffee sachets which I was afraid to try. The heat was unbearable, we had to try to sleep with the noisy fan on all night, but it didn't help much. Breakfast was an experience...we had to queue for a table and the waiter was run ragged, poor guy. It did have a good point though it was close to Paddington Underground which was great. Don't buy tickets from reception for "big bus tour" they promise 20% discount but there is none. Get them online. Definately needs a visit from the Hotel Inspector!!!!!

title: Admiral, Paddington continues to impress
text: Was back in London again recently and glad to see that Mr Kin, Mr Su and their team are keeping up their high standards. The great advantage of this hotel is its central location and proximity to Paddington- the fastest gate-way from Healthrow into London and the mainline station for nearly 30% of the long-distance trains arriving at the capital. A very good bargain choice for London and staff really do work very hard to make you feel welcome. Strongly recommended!

title: Stay away!
text: I can only be thankful I just stayed for one night! the bathroom was unbelievably small and really uncomfortable to use. The only good thing was that it was relatively clean. there was no space to put your luggage, so we struggled with this. The people in the reception aren't very helpful so don't expect much help from them. It was January and the heating wasnt working, and neither did the phone or the wireless. There are better places in London for this same price so be sure to book somewhere else.

title: Pleasurable stay
text: Admiral was a great deal in terms of pricing and location in comparison from other hotels I have stayed in the area. The front staff were very attentive and helpful with a lovely gift they gave me a free bottle of Champagne! I believe they randomly pick some guest and give free transportation and meals and drinks :) interesting. Recommended!

title: Don't stay there!
text: I stayed here in March/ April 2012 on my own for 3 nights then with my daughter for 4 nights. My single room was about the size of a cupboard and next to the dining room and toilet. Apparently I could have had another room but it was up 8 flights of very narrow stairs. It was clean but very noisy early in the mornings. It was in the Kingsway Park Hotel and not in the Admiral for which I had a confirmed email. When I complained about the room I was told I was given this one as it was the best one. There was no fridge in the room. When my daughter arrived we were moved to a twin room in the Admiral. I was informed that it was a special room on the second floor. Up 4 flights of narrow stairs the room was not much bigger than the single room but it did have a fridge. There is no-one to help you with your bags!!!! If I could have found another hotel to stay in I would have but it was over Easter and all of the hotels in the area were full. I have stayed in other places in London and I know about the size of the rooms and the stairs but I felt they could have done more for their guests. The breakfast was good if you like an English Breakfast every day. No fruit, yoghurts or water were available. As the rooms are so small you can hear everything from the other rooms especially when people come home at all different hours. The only advantage of these hotels is their proximity to Paddington Station. I would not recommend these hotels to anyone and I will never stay there again!!!

title: Pitch a tent somewhere before you think about staying here!
text: Before you book a room here, pitch a tent in a park somewhere. You will be a LOT more comfortable. I booked a single room, which was like a closet. Now I don't expect a mansion, but I'd like to be able to turn around without hitting a wall. The stairs up to my room were almost vertical and there was no one to assist with the luggage. The woman who checked me in told me that I should not have brought so much stuff! I was in the UK for over a month, did she think I could get away with less than one suitcase?? Breakfast was a disaster. You could not request to have your egg made the way you wanted, it was her way or no way. I only ate there two mornings, then gave up and went a couple of blocks up the road near Paddington Station where I found a nice restaurant. I also received a phone call while I was staying there from a friend that I was meeting up with and we needed to discuss travel arrangements. After 5 minutes, she knocked on my door and informed me that I had been on the phone too long!! They advertise that staying there is like staying at home...yea, if your home is a prison! Stay away from this place!!

title: We had a problem with this hotel!! Please read this!!!
text: we stayed at this hotel in November 2011 (three persons). Although we paid the full amount of our stay, they unfairly took another 142 pounds from our bank account. We informed the hotel management immediately and they still did not pay the money back. It has been more than 4 months already and no one is answering our emails. This hotel is very poor in terms of management and service. They are really ignorant and disrespectful. I will sue this company.

title: Excellent manager, superb location and good value
text: I recently stayed at the Admiral, 143 Sussex Gardens and cannot comment on its sister Hotel Kingsway Park, although the reception area of both hotels is inviting and the staff are extremely welcoming. I found the Admiral to be very good value. It is just a few minutes from Paddington Station and the fact that the hotel is located on a pedestrian frontage away from the main road means that it enjoys a quiet location and gets little street noise. The manager of both hotels, Mr Kin is excellent. He is friendly, welcoming, professional and very helpful and deserves all possible accolades for the charming way that he manages a busy hotel operation split across multiple buildings. He is an enormous asset to the business and a consummate hotel professional. He is the star of these businesses. The Admiral's rooms are very clean, tastefully decorated, modern facilities and are of a very acceptable standard. The ground floor bar and breakfast area would not be out of place in a boutique hotel that could easily charge x 2 times the price. The design concept of the area is very good and the breakfast service itself was perfect. The one draw-back is that the Admiral does not have a lift and the upper stair floors are a bit narrow which would be difficult for guests with challenges or heavy luggage. That said, the main reception at Kingsway has a large storage area and welcome lounge with comfy couches and travellers could easily leave their main luggage there so that they did not have to take heavy luggage to the upper floors. In summary the location and management is excellent and this hotel offers very good value for money. Over 20+ years I have been coming for short stays to London and the Admiral is one of the best places I have seen recently and with the care taken by its manager Mr. Kin I would certainly be persuaded to stay there again soon.

title: Awful. Very dissapointing!
text: After much concideration I booked this hotel and sent them a message as it was my husband birthday weekend and I wanted to pamper him a little.... NO response! I should have realised how poor this place was going to be when we had to check into this 'family run b & b' 3 doors down the road! reception was shabby, when i asked what time the bar opened he said it was closed because it cost them money to have someonw serve! they advertise this hotel and family run with bar etc etc... what a crock! our double room was a tiny triple, no hot water and no toiletries (not even loo paper) really really dissapointed. My husband was livid. We handed our room key back and left within 20 mins. I managed to find a best western a 4 min walk away. they were £196 for thur, fri & sat night. £16 more expensive but a million miles away from the Admiral! Do not reccommend this 'motel' unless your a dirty old man wanting a room for the evening! Chaps in local bar said its well know because you can rent a room for a couple of hours! need I say more. Not our sort of thing. Happy to sacrifice the first nights cost so I could leave!

title: friendly staff and good location
text: after reading the reviews on trip advisor i was a bit worried about going to this hotel. It was very nice, clean the breakfast was excellent and the staff were great. Mr kin the manager was very helpful and polite and so were the rest of the staff at the reception. The room was cleaned every day. I recommend this hotel and the location is perfect.

title: Great Location,Great staff,great value.
text: Recently stayed for two nights, celebrating our wedding anniversary. Great location,asked for room overlooking the square and got it. Clean room ,(if somewhat small),decent breakfast and very attentive staff. Had evening meal included in our deal,which we had in the Pavilion Roastery at the Royal National. this also was good food and very attentive staff. The only negative thing to say that there was no air conditioning in the room and we were experiencing some of the hottest weather this year.

title: Good value
text: Excellent service from Front of House. Restaurant staff varied in their friendliness but the breakfast was excellent with plenty of choice. The decor was a bit tired in places but very clean. Such good value for London in a popular but not too noisy area.

title: Great value for London
text: Spent 2 nights with English breakfast. The hotel is convenient for Kings Cross station being a 10 minute walk. Check in was quick and pleasant and our room was clean and large enough. The hotel is convenient for buses in to Trafalgar Square. The bar in the hotel is pleasant and wifi there and in reception is ok. Breakfast is very busy but was good and efficient with pleasant staff throughout. After checking out my wife discovered that she had mistakenly thrown 1 of our rail tickets away in the bedroom. The 3 cleaning staff on the 2nd floor were marvellous and spared no effort in finding the ticket-brilliant! They would not accept any recognition-they said they were just happy to have helped. For that reason alone we will return.

title: A surprising eating venue
text: We were 5 friends meeting for a chat. We needed a good restaurant that was relatively quiet, not TV's or loud music. Surfing the net I found Jacques wine bar in Tavistock Street within the Tavistock hotel. The menu is not extensive but had specials. We all chose the English lamb chops, not often sourced in Australia where we live. We all chose the chops with vegs. No hard carrots or cauli. New potatoes, aubergine, red and green peppers and tomatoes. We followed with 2 plates of cheese and biscuits. When we saw the size one would have been quite sufficient with a cheddar, camambert, blue with a choice of bread or crackers. We talked a lot consuming 3 bottles of french bordeaux. All for 89 pounds. Pleasant light oak tables overlook Tavistock park. Perfect for our evening together. A further surprise when we exited via the hotel door into reception. beautiful original art deco columns, mirrors and signage led through to another restaurant Poppadoms. Its a self service Indian eat as much as you like for 13 pounds ninety five pence. We can't say what it is like but we will certainly try it soon.

title: Well priced hotel in good location
text: I stay here every time I am in London. The rooms are a decent size, clean and there's breakfast included, if you want it. It's a very convenient location and easy to get around, either by public transport or on foot. I do have two issues that I always experience with the hotel though

title: Lovely hotel
text: Stayed for one night. Nice clean room, it was quite warm and we couldn’t find anywhere to turn heating down, once windows opened it was bearable. Breakfast nice, very friendly staff. Great central location. Will definitely return.

title: VERY GOOD LOCATION
text: It is perfect hotel if you want visit London. It is central location in front of tavistock square. 5 minutes on foot from the Subway RUSSEL SQUARE. The room is clean and quiet. The breakfast is very copious (buffet) The restaurant staff not very friendly, we cannot have everything....

title: can't sleep well cos bed & noisy environment
text: I stayed there for 4 nights, location is good, but room is so small and not clean. don't like it. it is not value for money.

title: tiny but clean
text: A friend staying in a hostel in London said her single room was larger than our double. We were tucked into an inner quadrangle which in some ways was quieter except when the restaurant staff was recycling or putting the garbage out. We needed to keep the window open to cool down the room even though the radiator did not seem to be on. The staff kept the room exceptionally clean every day. My partner traded up to the full English breakfast a number of times. As a vegetarian, what I chose for my continental breakfast consisted of grapefruit and orange sections and musli. Good but repetitive. It was difficult to get more than one cup of coffee. This is a very basic hotel. Next time, I would try for the hostel.

title: Basic Hotel for London
text: Good location in the Center of London, the Russell Sq. area is always our first choice. This hotel will satisfy your basic needs of a bed, a shower, a closet, a dresser and breakfast. I usually stay in the Royal National hotel (just next door) but this time we went for the Tavistock (the Royal National was fully booked), I must say that I preferred the R.N. – but the Tavistock is good enough. The view from the window was nice (Tavistock Sq. all nice and green) and the lobby looks like out of a Jeeves and Wooster episode (very 20’s), but the R.N. is a bit more updated. Our bed sheets were torn, and so was the mattress itself. But all together – for the low price – it’s sufficient.

title: Typical London hotel close to British Museum
text: Arrived Eurostar late in afternoon so did not want to take tube during peak hour to our airb&b on the other side of river. Have stayed in Russell Square previously so decided to try the sister hotel we stayed in previously. It was a 15 minute walk from St Pancras dragging our bags through heavy foot traffic. Hotel as expected small room and bathroom but luckily with a double bed. We knew the area well and enjoyed revisiting pubs and restaurants along with the museum for two days before we moved on Breakfast simple but OK to keep us going for the day. Hotels in London even budget hotels are expensive, but we enjoyed the Tavistock, but our preference in our return visit next year would be to go straight to an airb&b much cheaper, which means you can stay longer in London.

title: Great location, great price, very much in need of refurb
text: Good location as 5 mins from euston station, 10 from Oxford street and Russell square tube 5 mins. However, room was not good (I believe their is a renovated floor but I hope this was not it!)...uncomfy pillows and blankets (nb blankets not duvets!), stained towel, rusty shower curtain rail and mouldy shower curtain. Scaffolding work going on outside...started banging at 8am! Smelled very strongly of curry for some reason on the floor we stayed on?!!!! However, very good price for London and breakfast was also good. Would pay a little more and stay elsewhere next time though...

title: Weekend in London
text: Stayed here previously and just as good this time round. Able to check in early as room was ready so plenty of time to sightsee before evening show. Clean room, comfortable bed, lovely breakfast, friendly staff. Can leave luggage for just 50p per bag after checkout. Will definitely come again. Highly recommend

title: Has maintained its standards
text: My last visit was a comfortable one on the rather faded elegance of the 4th. floor facing the quiet western aspect. This time I was on the more modern 1st floor facing a much more noisy eastern aspect. However, the room was very comfortable with a bath and shower, and separate WC. The breakfast was ok but I nearly mistook the porridge for the scrampled eggs!!

title: 1930's style hotel
text: My wife and I had a very pleasant room on 3rd floor at the front of the hotel overlooking Taverstock square gardens. The hotel staff were pleasant and helpful with advice and directions. We ate out so only had breakfast there and this was very good, again with helpful staff in attendance. We have stayed here before when visiting London, and will no doubt come again.

title: cheap and cheerful
text: Overnight stop in the Tavistock on a little trip to London. So close to Euston, and at £100 odd a night for a twin room it was cheaper than many travel lodges. Easy to find. Great staff. Clean and serviceable. Old fashioned, and not too generous in the toiletries, teabags etc, but had everything we needed. Our room was on the 2nd floor above the bowling alley underneath and there was loud music playing till the small hours that meant I was glad of my ear plugs. My parents have stayed before and said it's no where near as bad in different parts of the hotel and doesn't always go on too long. Breakfast was included and despite queues (which the staff warned us of) was perfectly acceptable. The coffee was pretty awful though! Stored our bags for the day and they only charged us 50p each - which beats a locker at Euston. Really happy. Will stay again. It's not the ritz, but at that price, you'd be mad to expect it!

title: good location
text: Stayed here 1 night for a work function nearby, room was clean and adequate for our needs, excellent powerful shower. Speedy check in/out, friendly staff, breakfast is continental only unless you pay an extra £5 .Plenty of pubs/ restaurant nearby, would recommend for a short stay, its within walking distance of soho, leicester square and oxford street

title: Very basic but clean!
text: Have stayed at the Tavistock several times and each time I leave I hope it will have been updated by the next time I go. Sadly not... The rooms themselves are very clean, if a little small. However, many basic expectations are sadly lacking: no air-conditioning (and in this area of London it is impossible to sleep with the window open), no fridge in any room (I rang in advance to ask if we could have a room with a fridge, but fridges only provided on request and for medical purposes only!!!), no hooks in the bathroom for towels (yes there's a bar, 1 bar, but you don't want to share this once towels have been used, and surely not hygienic. But not even a small hook for the hand towel!!!), the 'continental breakfast' was seriously disappointing and I feel for those who don't eat the 'full English', just rolls or toast, no fruit (fresh or dried), no croissants or pastries. And the television in the room had shocking signal and picture, yes I know you don't go to a hotel to watch television, but it's nice to have on whilst getting ready. However there was soap provided and a hair-drier, and tea/coffee smoking facilities, but no hot chocolate (I don't drink tea or coffee). For the price, it isn't bad but there are some basic things which desperately need attention.

title: Convenient budget hotel
text: Not too far from Russell Square tube station. Next to Tavistock Square Gardens. The rooms are basic, but spotless. Cleaned daily. Soaps and shampoo provided, which was a pleasant surprise. Wonderful, soft and fluffy towels. Beautiful Art Deco features. Our only complaint, although that is too strong a word, is that the pillows were very tired and need replacing. Breakfast wasn't spectacular but perfectly adequate and lots of it. Will certainly use this hotel again.

title: Pleasant Surprise!
text: I booked this hotel for two nights for me and my fiancee for my birthday weekend in London. When we pulled up in the cab I was very happy with the look of it, considering the reviews and some of the hotels I had looked at, this one was a palace and great views of Tavistock Gardens. The reception area was pleasant and clean, although very busy which I took as a good thing. We were early and went straight to reception to ask to store our luggage in the designated area why we plodded on with sightseeing. We were told that our room was available (3hrs before actual check in) we were given our key and went to our room. I have stayed in London before in a more expensive hotel and the room was just big enough for a queen bed...this one on the other hand was suprisingly large. There was room to walk al l the way around the bed, a TV, dresser and wardrobe. We even had a very clean bath with overhead shower. After a long day sightseeing we stopped by the onsite bar for a quick nightcap which the staff were very pleasant and accommodating and the drinks cheap (£2.50 for a glass of house wine - 175ml). We then retired to our room before starting all over again the next day. The bed was very soft compared to our orthopaedic one we are normally used to however, it was comfortable all the same. The only problem we found with it was when we sat up to watch the TV the bed is on wheels and you started to roll away from the wall. There was also a lack of extra pillows but it didnt bother us too much or we would have requested more. The location of the hotel is fantastic. It is within walking distance of the busier Russel Square and Russel Tube. We were also around 20mins walk from Covent Gardens. We would both recommend this hotel to anyone and we have actually just booked the Royal National (sister hotel) for January. We wanted to be a little closer to bars and restaurants and also closer to Covent Gardens for the winter weather.

title: Really good hotel
text: This hotel is in a good area, walking, easy places to get to. The room was immaculate and clean with excellent bed and bedding. Very reasonable prices at the bar, very nice breakfast. Number one the staff! They were all so nice and looked after us.

title: Great location and good value for the money
text: Couldn't be better for the price! Central location - within 10 min walk from Euston Station. Nice clean room, comfortable bed and full breakfast in the morning! Perfect! Some rooms may be a little small but are comfortable and warm in winter. Staff are very friendly.

title: Good at what they do
text: This was my first visit to this hotel. I have stayed serveral times at one of the sister hotels. I was delighted to find that my room was equiped with lovely blankets instead of a duvet! This alone is a great reason for me to return. I was grateful to have been upgraded from a single to a twin-bedded room. The room was compact and they have done the best they can in that constraint. Everything in the room worked and looked to be well maintained, however, still having an old fashioned big box of a TV occupying one third of the desk space is an example that modernisation is overdue. The breakfast buffet contains quite a reasonable selection of items. This hotel is good value for money.

title: Poor customer service
text: The hotel refused to supply us with a hot beverage, said they cleaned the machine at 22:30, this was at 23:30, I said we were residence of the hotel but was told so what. Ask for a manager and was told none on duty. What an absolute joke.

title: Impersonal
text: I've stayed at this hotel a few times and thought it was OK although it is quite large and impersonal. There's nothing special about it but it's usually quite reasonably priced and it's only a short walk to the nearest tube station.

title: Too noisy at night
text: I checked in again at the Tavistock on the 7th July with no problem by a friendly helpful member of staff. I made the mistake of asking for an upper floor room at the back - bad idea ... Its an enclosed courtyard with roofs of kitchens / a health club underneath and a constant noisy air conditioning unit outside which gets louder the quieter the rest of the place gets. My only other complaint is that the shower above the bath which is protected by a shower curtain ends up flooding the bathroom as it cannot stretch to the wall due to an overhang on the wall.

title: Surprisingly Good
text: The purpose of the visit was a one night stay for a football match via Superbreak which covered rail travel from Newcastle and one night in an allocated Imperial Hotel which in this case was the Tavistock. For those arriving at Kings Cross its a twelve minute walk up Euston Road turn left at Upper Woburn Place and hotel is on the right.Alternatively you just get the tube to Euston and its three minutes again along Upper Woburn Place or the tube to Russell Square.On arrival at just after eleven first impressions were very good reception very plush.We were surprised that the rooms were ready but had they not been there is a secure room to leave your bags at no charge next to reception.The rooms were fine twin beds with room well decorated.While the room was a little hot their were windows which opened securely to let some air in.Yes their is some noise from the nearby disco but not to bad at all. The hotel has an excellent bar well furnished with prices a staggering one pound fifty LESS than nearby bars.There was also a wine bar and the hotel has its own nghtclub with bowling alleys open late. The breakfast was fine self service except tea and coffee which was brought to your table on request.The only downside no mushrooms for some reason but everything else in a relaxed atmosphere. For those wanting a night out nearby get the tube from Euston on the Northern Line to Camden Town only two stops very good and saves going into the city. As I said we had a rail deal which was just over hundred pounds which was great value.Anyone walking up to this hotel will pay ninety one for a single or one seventeen for a double so pays to shop a round.Another tip is that if there are three of you some of the Imperial Group just add twenty one pounds which brings the rate down to forty seven pounds per person. So all in all a very good hotel and relaxed considering it ws so busy.

title: Good location, room small and hot.
text: The Tavistock hotel is in a great location for a short stay in the centre of London. As mentioned in earlier reviews it is close to the rail and underground stations. However when we arrived I asked for a quiet room and was given a room on the 8th floor. The room was like an oven it was so hot. We turned the radiator off and opened the window to cool the room down, but the room never cooled down and we had to sleep with the window wide open and only a sheet on the bed as a cover. With the window open (our window looked into a central open area which must be above the kitchens) we had a constant noise of extractor fans and smell of food wafting into the room. I would hate to think what it is like in the summer as there is no air conditioning and our stay was in February!! The room was small which you can expect in London but so was the double bed and my husbands feet hung out of the bottom of it. I have to say that the room and bathroom were clean. Only 2 coat hangers in the open wardrobe area but plenty of drawer space. Small bars of soap in the bathroom but no shampoo so bring toiletries with you. A kettle is provided with only 2 packets of coffee so again if you like a cuppa after a long day sightseeing bring extra coffee and coffee mate. We only had continental breakfast offered with our booking and went down to sample it the first morning but only had a slice of toast and disgusting strong coffee which practicaly took the enamel off your teeth. So after that we found a cafe to have breakfast. Giraffe is very good, located in Brunswick centre which is close to hotel where you can have tea or coffee and bacon, eggs and toast all for £5, this centre also has high street shops (Coast, Hobbs, Joy, French Connection, Benneton) as well as Restaurants such as Strada, Carluccio's, Nandos, Yo sushi and GBK and a Waitrose. Would I stay at the Tavistock again, probably not I think I would shop around and get something a little better.

title: Enjoyable stay
text: I have stayed at the Tavistock for many years, it provides good basis accommodation at a reasonable price in central London. After my last couple of visits I was becoming a little perturbed as the place was becoming quite shabby and tired looking. However, I have just spent 6 nights in one of the refurbished single rooms. The bed was comfortable, the double glazing worked (keeping out traffic noise), there was adequate space and I had a great view over the park. Breakfast was fine and staff were ok with the exception of some of the restaurant and portering staff who were abrupt and not very helpful or communicative. In summary, a pleasant stay, I'll definately be back.

title: Great value, friendly hotel.
text: This hotel has everything you need for a stay in London at a budget price. Rooms are clean, beds comfortable, en suite facilities with tea and coffee making facilities and hair dryer. Shower gel is provided and rooms are serviced daily. The staff are very helpful, very friendly, and there is plenty of them. Breakfast was plentiful and well cooked and served, continental full english, including steamed fish. The evening meal was a slight disappointment - plenty choice but very salty. You do not however have to eat in the Tavistock but can take your free meal in any of their hotels. You also do not have to take it on the first night - we arrived after 10.00 pm and so had our free meal on the next night. The hotel is only 5 minutes from Euston and just off a main route into the centre of London so there will be traffic noise - no air conditioning in rooms so take ear plugs if you need to keep the window open. The concierge staff were amazing - could not do enough to help and they will look after your cases for 50p per case after you check out. It is easy to walk to the centre of London or you can get taxi, tube or hop on hop off bus from near the hotel. Hotel bar prices are really cheap for London. The decor in the common areas is art deco and very chic. The hotel is light, unlike many modern hotels with dimly lit corridors and rooms' I was very pleasantly surprised by the Tavistock and would stay there again.

title: Never again
text: Our experience with this hotel was not good. We stayed in a room on the second floor which backed on an area that had something to do with ventilation. There was some kind of vent noise emanating from the area which lasted for two or three seconds every 10 seconds all night long. Not to mention the dumping of garbage or whatever . So you could not leave the window open because of the noise. This was nice because it allowed us to hear the TV in the next room going till after midnight. The free continental breakfast featured kippers, or at least some kind of smelly fish, as well as toast stored under a heat lamp, which was a new feature to me. Left it with a kind of rubbery texture and with no chance of burning yourself. The one good thing is that it certainly encourages you to stay out as long as you can and enjoy London.

title: Getting a bit better
text: This was our third stay in two years at the Tavistock and yes we are particular where we stay but it's not so bad! The staff at reception and housekeeping staff have improved even quite pleasant compared to our previous visits. We had requested a room facing front but did not happen not sure what one has to do to achieve this. Room is basic but clean been to posher places where they don't change linen and towels everyday Please Oh Please do something about the heating in the rooms far too warm when getting ready to go out for the evening my wife struggled to put on her makeup it was running before she had finished. Still same choice for breakfast but it set us up for the day. Unlike previous reviewer our TV worked fine no you don't get all cable channels but your not in London to watch TV.

title: Sadest hotel I ever stayed at
text: Anywhere in North America this would be a $49.00 room. Here's why: -Deadbeat staff except for a few of the underlings who serve at the buffet breakfast. -Creepy doorman who checks your valid breakfast paper (we called him the Undertaker) got into a nasty verbal spat with a female breakfast server right behind us. -male bartender from perhaps Malaysia should not be working around people, he might make a good garbage collector. I got to know each coil spring intimately each night, barely slept 2 hours each night. -bathroom has no shampoo, no facecloths, no hair dryer, the bathroom air vent system doesn't work. They just left new towels and removed old ones. -no kleenex provided -no alarm clock/radio -back side room was quiet other than hum of HVAC system outside. -new window was good and could be opened to refresh room -breakfast was OK but ham slices were the saltiest ever. Don't stay here. There must be better places. -

title: Cheap but pretty central
text: Been there on new year eve, central position, 5 mins away from two tube stations (Russel Square & Euston). Real estate is pretty old, room clean but really tiny. Breakfast acceptable, staff polite but in fairness didn' t deal much with them. Heating always full steam and the radiator didn' t have any proper kmob but strange taps to activate it. Not realized whether there is any aircon for summertime. What really pissed me off was the lack of room wiFi: free wiFi was only available in the lobby. Unacceptable in 2015 London. Would I come back? Maybe yes if all the above isn' much of an issue for you.

title: 3.5/5 - Cheap, central and good breakfasts.
text: Stayed here a number of times. Its central to London so it's easy to walk to all the main attractions from here. The costs is low considering its location, but you do get what you pay for. It's slightly dated, and rooms are small and dark. There is a restaurant which is attached which is small and food isnt great, but the breakfasts in the hotel are really good. In london, you have such a choice of great restaurants I wouldnt want to be eating in a hotel anyway in the evening. If you want to iron any clothes you'll need to go to second floor laundry room and do it there. They dont bring irons/ironing boards to the room. so bear that in mind! I like to go for morning jogs when I'm away, I'd recommend heading towards Regents park in the morning. its beautiful and also nice to hear the roar of a lion during a morning run (from London Zoo!). ha (its about 1 mile away)

title: Does the job
text: A very clean if tired room but for the price and location couldn't go wrong. Separate loo and bathroom - which could be v convenient I think. However this made both feel small. Bed was comfy. Sheets changed daily. Staff all v good and attentative in bar area and rooms. Odd ticket system at breakfast overseen by the most miserable looking chap but all was edible and plentiful. Lovely Art Deco bat area with plenty seating and room to meet friends and chat. Staff remembered our order so when we went back to the bar just said "same again" Excellent location - only 10 min walk to Euston and 15 / 20 min walk to theatre land. We had a great stay and would recommend this hotel for anyone just wanting a base to stay close to the west end etc.

title: Mix feelings
text: I stayed on tavistok 8 nights. First night was awful. I checked in at around 22.45 and they gave the worst room i have ever lived in in my whole life room 845. I could not sleep from the noise of the ventilation the aircondition compresors and the elevator machine. Because i could not sleep i came down to reception and asked for a room change. The guy there told me he could do nithing beacuse the hotel was full and i had to wait until morning to talk to the morning shift. I stayed down to reception all night and in the morning i told the morning shift about the problem.they said that they will change my room by noon as they did and i was transfered to room 817. Which was nice and quite. If i choose ti atay again at tavistok hotel i will definately ask for thesame room. All staff were very helpfull from day 2.

title: Never ever again.
text: Its 1.10 am and I have an early start tomorrow. But I can make out every song from the music being played in the bar two floors below. Seriously? Clearly they value the bar spend more than the satisfaction of residents. That and the three star food hygiene rating on the door are enough for me. Might skip breakfast. Oh, and the newish double glazed windows that are supposed to keep noise out and heat in, are clearly warping in their frames, and doing neither well. Won't be back.

title: Good value - v good brekkie.
text: Lovely Art Deco Entrance Foyer & Bar and the staff were excellent - despite many drunken RL fans. Beds rather uncomfy and the room a bit noisy. But we would definitely stay again. The location is also excellent for stations, the tube and many tourist sights.

title: Worst hotel I've stayed in for a while - will definitely not be back!
text: I stayed on business for one night in July 2011, having booked through British Airways website with flight from Scotland. The hotel certainly did not live up to the description on the website. The hotel overall was run down and the room was basic to say the least - my bathroom had no cold running water. At least the sheets seemed clean which is more than can be said for the rest of the room. The room door looked like it had been forced in the past as had bit broken off around the lock. Continental breakfast was a joke - stale rolls and cheap jam, cornflakes and tinned grapefruit segments. I will definitely be avoiding this hotel in future and it wasn't cheap - B&B cost £79 through BA although the walk in price advertised for single room is £69, which in my opinion is still too much.

title: Good Location
text: We stayed for 7 nights. The hotel is clean, great location, very good breakfast and very good service from the personnel. We had a small problem with the bathroom sink, the staff was polite and offered us to change our room, but we decide to stay and in general, enjoyed our stay very much.

title: New year stay
text: Our favourite hotel, Me & my husband always stay here when we come for New Year’s Eve 👍🏻 I genuinely carnt fault this hotel as it’s very clean in all areas & the staff are always polite & ready to help no matter how small the query.😀 The breakfast is my favourite part as there’s more than enough to choose from. I honestly feel this hotel doesn’t get the credit that it’s due. I would highly recommend this hotel.👌🏻 Also it’s only a bus trip away from all the main attractions & shops 👏🏻

title: Great Hotel
text: Larger budget hotel with friendly helpful staff. Have stayed a number of times in this and other hotels in the Imperial London Hotel chain and have been pleased on each occasion. Would highly recommend this chain both for the excellent service, staff and price but also for the location, very easy to reach all the sights both by foot and public transport. One small comment not sure but believed the chain did in the past have shower caps in their rooms but not now.

title: Good Location
text: This is our fourth visit to this hotel, we keep returning because it is good value for money, good location, clean and comfortable and friendly helpful staff. There is a complimentary meal on the first night (the chilli is hot) and plenty of variety for breakfast. They also do an 'all you can eat' fixed price curry option in the dining room but we didn't have this so can't comment but it's an option to their Jaques restaurant. There is a nice bar for a night cap before bed. Our room overlooked Tavistock Square so we had a nice view, can't comment on the traffic noise, this is London so you'll always hear traffic! The location is perfect for theatres and restaurants, tubes or buses or a 20 minute walk to Leicester Square (about a mile so if you stroll it'll be a longer walk!). We usually stay midweek as can't be bothered to run the gauntlet of weekend repairs to the train lines but also because last time we stayed here the disco at the back of the hotel was too noisy for us and could be heard in our room at 3am. Obviously this isn't a problem Monday to Thursday. We would certainly recommend this to friends and family.

title: We loved it
text: We loved staying at the Tavistock! The first thing you see when you arrive is the lovely Tavistock Square across the street. Then you are greeted in the charming deco style lobby. I'll admit, I was a little disappointed when I first saw our room. It seemed so small and had twin beds! But it didn't take long to get over that initial disappointment. We weren't here to hang out in the room, so who cares if it's small? Besides, the view overlooking the square was beautiful. I read another review here that said the street noise was too loud. We didn't have that problem at all. We slept with the windows wide open and our sleep was never disturbed.The location is great, just two blocks from the Russell Square tube station. Of course, if the tube isn't for you, it's very easy to catch a taxicab in front of the hotel. The British Museum is just a short walk away

title: Don`t be put off by bad reviews
text: The Tavistock is situated about 10mins walk from Euston .We picked it for a base for our Ruby wedding treat to see a show.The staff on the front desk were very friendly when we booked in , as were all the other staff , from the cleaners up. We were on the 7 th floor and the room was basic but very clean , with tea making etc, as well as a trouser press and hairdryer. Although the bed was harder than what we`re used to but that did`nt spoil our stay.The breakfast was really good, a full english, all cooked nicely .Right across from the hotel is Tavistock Square which is a really peaceful little area, well worth walking round to see the flowers etc, and as we had nice sunny weather we sat there a couple of times. Hoping to book a couple of nights nearer christmas for shopping.

title: Great food, staff friendly, idea spot to stay, so close to Euston, walking distance.
text: If you are looking to visit London near your arrival station of Euston, this is the place to stay, walking distance about 5 minutes, accommodation clean, well presented, reasonable price, look out for offers stay 2 nights get free meal, full english breakfast included as well as continental if you prefer. Can also walk to west end or catch bus or tube.

title: Ok for 1 night
text: Stopping in London on a business trip the Tavistock was fairly cheap for this area of London

title: Affordable stay in a prime location
text: The reason we stayed there is that this was the hotel we used on our first visit to London, back in '98. Nowadays, I would have chosen something a tad fancier, but I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel is situated in the middle of the West End, within 3 mins. walk from the British Museum and 7 mins. walk from the Oxford street. Its facade looks upon a park, and the place was very quiet throughout our stay. The rooms are rather small and basic (only one towel per person, no shampoo etc.), but the rooms are clean, the room service - thorough and efficient, and there is a tea/coffee kit, which is replenished daily. Through an oversight, we had a continental breakfast ordered, and had to upgrade to the English breakfast (4.5 pounds per person). The breakfast itself is also rather basic - no vegetables, cold meats or cheese, but is nicely served and is nutritional enough. To sum up, for the price you pay, this is as much (or more) than what you'd expect.

title: Philipino Philipino Philipino
text: I was so proud that i was going back home to london for a short holiday. i was happy with the hotel room but the service was terrible. The staff which was all philipinos who kept talking in their language and kept ignoring the guest. They kept disturbing my sleep by banging on the walls while cleaning and disturbing me despite the sign on the door saying do not disturb. this is because the 90 % of the staff who were philipinos could not speak or read english. Staying there felt like i was in philiphines not London extremely disapointed and will never stay there again on my visits in future I recommed a staff mix would certainly be a bonus for this hotel as the rooms are very nice but the staff were terrible. The hotel has all beautiful facilities and its a shame that the staff gives this wonderful hotel a bad name.

title: Best kept secret in London!
text: I have stayed at this hotel most weeks since January 2018. Booking is best done direct on their website and the hotel is one of about 6 in a group who operate in the same general area of Holborn and all at fixed rates for the rooms, highly unusual in London. The Tavistock offers a single for £85 and a double for £111 this includes free wifi and breakfast. There is usually last minute availability, which I tested during weather disruption and got rooms on the day no problem. The location is excellent 5 minutes from Euston Station, about 10 minutes from Kings Cross and Holburn tube is about 10 minutes away. Close to a range of restaurant's and shops, you couldn't ask for a better location. Breakfast is excellent, good choice, rooms are a little dated but always very clean and they are refurbishing some rooms. The room service is exceptionally good value with a £2 tray charge and a burger at just £8, quality again excellent. What really makes hotel though are the rally lovely staff, so pleasant and helpful, and genuinely offering excellent hospitality. I will be staying here until August and look forward to having this as my second home for that period. Recommended for tourists and business travellers alike.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: Despite quite a few negative comments about this huge hotel, I found it rather pleasant. Although small, my room had obviously been recently refurbished, it was clean and all equipments, notably in the bathroom, were in working order. Although on a busy street, it was quiet at night (efficient double-paned windows). Friendly staff and a good English breakfast included in the room rate. Good location close to St Pancras Station and tube stations, too. Good value for money for a short stay in London.

title: Excellent Value Hotel in London
text: Excellent Value Hotel in London.Close to Euston Station.Clean Room.Excellent Choice for breakfast.

title: Beautiful Art Deco hotel, good value but room for improvement
text: Some reviewers have said that the décor is dated but this is a hotel built in the 1930s in an Art Deco style and that shouldn't be changed. There are some good Art Deco features such as the lovely wood veneered modular 30s bar, the lighting, door surrounds to the bar and restaurant entrances, some original 1930s style doors at the tops of the stair wells and some lovely Art Deco touches in each of the guest rooms. The problem is that it hasn't been decorated for a little while, the wallpaper and paintwork in the rooms are obviously due for renewal and this does make the guest rooms look a little tardy. One big problem is that the hotel sits on a busy road junction which means that traffic noise is a real problem in the front rooms (take ear plugs as I did). However. the pros are that it has a great location close to the Victoria Line tube and central London and if you love Art Deco then it's well worth a look in. The rooms were clean and the staff at reception and breakfast were friendly, although the coffee at breakfast was the worst I have ever tasted and was only lukewarm, but the breakfast room was beautiful and tables nicely laid out and clean like a restaurant. Breakfast is buffet style with an excellent selection of cereals, continental and cooked. It is great value for money for a hotel in this location. Great for one night stay overs for business, as I was on, but I wouldn't want to stay for any longer than a few days. Although the hotel website says WiFi, it is only available in the hotel lobby which is a big oversight on the hotel's part and a great disadvantage if you plan on staying for more than one night and need to keep in touch. Also note that if you are allocated a front room in the hotel that you are overlooked by offices and you have no net curtains for privacy!

title: wonderful mid week break
text: 2 friends plus my wife and I booked a mid week break at the Tavistock Hotel in Russell Square, London. A 5 minute walk from Euston Station and a 5 minute walk to the nearest underground station. We had an evening meal on our first night and breakfast for the next 3 days. There was a good choice on the evening menu and although the breakfast was self service there was a plenty of variety. The food was well cooked and plentiful. It set us up for the day so we only needed a snack at lunch. The hotel was very clean and the staff were all friendly and helpful. The only complaint I had was even on the 7th floor the rooms were very hot, even with the windows open. One guest referred to it as the sauna floor, after our stay I now know what he means. The hotel was well placed as we found out during the 2 day underground strike and the roads being gridlocked we ended up on foot. I know where we will be staying on our next visit to London.

title: Tavistock Hotel
text: A friendly, efficient and clean hotel. Minutes away from Euston Station and within easy walking distance of many interesting areas of London. Jaques Bar, within the hotel is pleasant and has good food

title: Hotel Nice As Always
text: Having traveled to London five times in three years I have never had to book another hotel since. The Tavistock Hotel was recommended by a friend who knows London quite well & as a keen walker I wanted to stay somewhere within ten to fifty mins walk of local attractions. Tavistock Hotel near Russell Square is within walking distance of Shaftsbury Avenue, Euston Station, Oxford St & Covent Garden to name a few places. ten to twenty mins walk at leisure. I prefer to fly & using the tube from Russell Square to Heathrow Terminal 5 is only a few mins walk from hotel. Inside the hotel offers comfortable lounge space & fine bar area. The atmosphere of the friendly staff & breakfast staff is extremely pleasant & sometimes amusing when dealing with the usually busy morning rush. Breakfast is very good here. The rooms I've been in were all comfy & basic but you can always ask for a room on the Woburn Road side & preferably on upper floors seven & eight. At night the views are nice especially the BT tower that brightens up the skyline. Noise at night can't be avoided in busy cities like London & you will have to endure many sirens up to nine or ten a night at the least on average. Also just around the corner is a handy Internet cafe & Toscana a splendid Italian deli / cafe that is open till 11pm. The food there and service is wonderful and good for say families or late eaters. Tavistock Hotel has struck a cord with me over the last few years & the affordable cost is a bonus when visiting London no matter how rich or poor we travelers are. Top marks again for this handy hotel & the best part for me is I feel I know my way around the surrounding streets quite well. Knowing I'm not going to get lost again that's a big step forward especially in London.

title: You Get What You Pay For!
text: When I first arrived at the hotel, I was unimpressed about the furnishings of the rooms which were very basic and looked very 60's in their design. The wallpaper and fabrics were also very dull and for some unimaginable reason, the bedside lights were fluorescent tubing which gave the room a very stark and uncomfortable feeling. At first, I was quick to blame the management of the hotel from their apparent lack of imagination but as time went on I realized that I was being unreasonable in my expectations. We had after all, only paid £84 for two people, bed and breakfast in a very good location in Central London. It is a true saying that you get what you pay for. In terms of value it could have been far worse. The rooms were clean, the food was OK, the staff were helpful and we were only there for one night (more would have been too much)! What really surprises me is that, being part of the Imperial Group - a name which suggests grandeur and top quality, that they have not developed this hotel to a much higher standard. It is in a great position and in my view, deserves more.

title: Good location
text: Good location, room was quite small but was clean and served our purpose. Room was quite warm but given the time of year this is not a complaint. Staff were polite. Euston station is only five minutes from the hotel with Covent Garden close by.

title: Good location.... so is the adjacent park
text: Room OK, quiet enough for my 3 night stay.Suppose it's typical of a central London hotel. you stay somewhere because you have to. Don't know what they use for tea in the breakfast beverage! Poor poor breakfast, forsook it on the final morning and enjoyed far better fare in an adjacent cafe.

title: Good value and location
text: I recently spent my fifth stay at this hotel. This time a single night but I have stayed for a week on a couple of occasions. The hotel is great value for the location and is clean with everything necessary for a comfortable stay. Over the last few years the rooms have been redecorated. Breakfast is served buffet style, there is a very wide variety of food available and I've always found it delicious! Staff are helpful but sometimes seem rather too busy! On this latest visit I needed to borrow a hair dryer (none in the room) and had to make a £20 deposit which I consider to be very steep for something most hotels provide free of charge, I also had to make my own way to the housekeepers room on floor 8 to collect it. This is the only time I have ever felt that service was not good. I always just walk from St. Pancras and Euston is even closer, access to the underground is also easy so the location of this hotel could not really be much better.

title: Utilitarian but good value
text: A comfortable room at a reasonable price. No luxury toiletries but essentials such as soap. Tea and coffee in the room I liked the fact there was a wardrobe, not just an open hanging space that is usual in business hotels these days. Lots of very hot water. Towels thin but effective and always changed. Good lighting in the bedroom. Downstairs, free wi-fi in the lobby and bar, none elseswhere. Concierges excellent, rushing out in the rain to find taxes etc. Breakfast room hot, tables small, buffet breakfast with the usuals, but tasted better than it looked. Toast already made which is good for time and turnover so fast that it was still crisp. This hotel is part of the large Imperial group and other than breakfast, food and coffee was only available in a small bar. You were directed to the other hotels for a variety of resteraunts. It was very adequate for a stay where you were out all day, and for London, very reasonably priced.

title: Everything fine except really very unfriendly reception staff
text: I stayed here December 2014 to attend a course the next day. Just needed a bed for the night and that was adequately provided - room comfortable and well appointed, no complaints there. However, I was left feeling pretty shaken by the manner of the reception staff when I arrived and when I left. I often read negative reviews of hotels that seem extreme and I don't want this to be one of those. I am quite easily pleased really when it comes to hotels and don't expect some subservient bowing person to treat me like royalty when I arrive. However, my experience at this hotel was something else. Be warned that you have to have a hard copy of your hotel confirmation on you or you will not be checked in. I must have missed this in the small print and only had the confirmation on my phone - that wasn't good enough. I was tired and stressed after a hellish ride on the rush-hour Piccadilly Line but was treated as if I was some sort of disgusting creature who had wandered into the hotel lobby, and I was apparently deluded if I expected to be granted my (paid-for) room because I didn't have the requisite leaf of paper. Long story short, they in the end accepted my confirmation as an email and I was begrudgingly given the card for my room. The staff on checkout were equally unfriendly and left me wanting to leave as soon as possible. I've never been to a hotel where I've been made to feel like I didn't deserve to be there, and honestly found the whole thing pretty upsetting. Should just mention the concierge staff, at a separate desk, were perfectly helpful and friendly. Don't know what was going on with the reception staff but they couldn't have made me feel less welcome. Will definitely avoid this hotel for that reason in the future. Oh, and be warned you'll need to pay a £20 deposit if you want to borrow a hairdryer.

title: This hotel has seen better days - but then again, so have I!
text: The bellmen are what make this hotel. I wish I could remember their names but they had a wealth of info, terrific senses of humour and were truly entertaining. The front desk staff ladies were a little grumpy at times - the rooms adequate. They were certainly clean and basic but one has to remember the age of the hotel. The restuarant for breakfast is quite nice with decent food. The whole hotel has certainly seen better days but I liked its character and feel - it was certainly affordable (40 pounds). The subway is just around the corner (Russell Square Station) and if you take the stairs to the train - BE CAREFUL. I go back!

title: Difficult to deal with
text: The Tavistock is cheap for central London, and in a good spot. We stayed in a room which was clean and comfortable (own bathroom), but the reception and other staff were difficult to deal with. Long waits to check in and out, and I twice waited behind travellers having heated conversations with reception staff about overcharging, room keys that wouldn't work. Breakfast is decent but supervised by cranky staff. They told us there was Internet connection available in rooms but there wasn't, which caused a lot of inconvenience. Would probably stay there again if we didn't need to work while there.

title: Good location..average hotel
text: I recently visited London and stayed at the Tavistock hotel for 3 nights. The location of the hotel was pretty good. The tube was just a short walk from the hotel and there were several bus stops around the hotel. The area where the hotel is located was very pretty and had quite a bit to offer in terms of parks, restaurants and shopping. The hotel itself however, was not my favourite. There was no air conditioning in the bedrooms which made them very uncomfortable during the summer time. The bathroom in the bedroom was well cleaned however the bedding had many stains on it. The wifi connection was not very good and you could only have access to wifi in the main lobby. The breakfast food was not very good, there were limited options and they served the same food everyday. The hotel is very outdated and could use some touch ups here and there. Overall the hotel itself was average but the location was pretty good.

title: great value
text: We have used this more times than I care to remember the lobby staff know every bus route and are so helpful nothing is to much bother and no hand out looking for a tip breakfast the gentleman on the door of the dinning room remembers you from your last visit must have been there when the hotel was built what a selection of things to eat even smoked haddock don't take that off thanks staff at the tavistock. have in the wine bar excelent

title: Perfect location, exceptional value.
text: This hotel is in the perfect location for easy access to the city attractions. Covent Garden is a 10 minute walk away, the British Museum is a 5 minute walk, Russell Square tube station is on your doorstep and Kings Cross & St. Pancras railway stations are only a pleasant 10 minute walk from the hotel. The spotlessly clean rooms have comfortable beds with crisp, white sheets and pristine, functional bathrooms. The public rooms have retained their beautiful, art-deco period features, the staff are friendly and efficient and the plentiful full English buffet breakfast is as good as you'll get anywhere. There is admittedly some noise from the streets but that's to be expected in central London and overall the Tavistock offers exceptional value for money. I wouldn't hesitate to book this hotel or one of it's sister properties when staying overnight in London.

title: Capital City convenience
text: Attending a Conference near the Mall, we found the Tavistock Hotel which is no where near, but is on the number 91 bus route and takes one from outside Starbucks in Tavistock Road on a scenic trip through the City to Trafalger Square and close to Carlton House Terrace where the meeting was being held. The Tavistock hotel is a sort of retro art nouveau design mixed with modern touches. Just as well since the lifts take forever to arrive even though there are several. Fortunately we were on the first floor so walked. The Staff were incredibly helpful and utterly charming, and our check-in was done with speed and efficiency and when we lost our breakfast card, simply issued us with another without any complications. Remember this is a city centre hotel in the heart of London and in spite of this there was very little noise, although the rooms are small, but well appointed and the bath and shower had gallons of lovely hot water. The small soaps were a bit mean and it is as well that I take my own supply of toiletries, but this is countered by the ample supply of tea and coffee making facilities. Breakfast was a bit chaotic but with hundreds of guests, the dining room was vast with food piled high in a central galley area. The fruit juice was awful, thin and cheap as was the coffee, but the selfservice food including cerails, fruit, toast, eggs, bacon, beans/tomato/musrooms, fish etc etc meant a hearty breakfast was had by all. So here in London, we had a capital time. Jan, Ledbury

title: Reasonable, overall - but not without issues
text: Giving a single whole-figure overall grade for this hotel is difficult, because there is a real mix of the good and the not-so-good. Three and a half stars out of five would probably be a more accurate reflection of our experience. Firstly, the good stuff. The hotel is in a very convenient location for people arriving by train from the Midlands and the North, as it's about a 10-15 minute walk from the major railway stations of Euston, St Pancras and King's Cross. Being also only about five minutes at most on foot from Russell Square underground station, most popular areas of London are readily accessible. The cleanliness of all areas of the hotel is also very welcome, and there are plenty of staff on hand to deal with questions, etc. With eight floors to the hotel, the lifts were also quick and efficient. Now the "middling" elements. Our room was adequate - reasonable ventilation, clean, but distinctly "compact" in size, with just enough storage space for a short stay. The television on the wall matched the dimensions of the room. The food at breakfast was acceptable - not the best we have ever had, but a long way from the worst. Now to the not-so-good. Although there were four staff at Reception, it took a while to get checked in. There seemed to be a problem with the IT system and one of the keycard issuing machines wasn't functioning. We had been assigned a twin-bedded room, and both single beds and the associated pillows would have to rank on the hard side of "firm" - it's a question of personal preferences, I know, but we didn't get a comfortable night's sleep. There's no wi-fi in the rooms, but that didn't matter to us. There are "tea- and coffee-making facilities" in the room, but a total initial complement of two tea bags, three milks and a couple of sugars must be rated as miserly. Table allocation at breakfast was a bit hit-and-miss. The sign on a stand, with the instruction to wait to be seated, wasn't prominent enough, and some guests just ignored it. Also - even though there's no dress code - it is off-putting to have people turn up to breakfast still dressed in pajama tops and in one case pajama bottoms (I kid you not ...) Staff coped as best they could, but the fear of offending individual guests seems to over-ride other considerations. So - would we go back? Yes for a short stay of a couple of days, no for anything longer. For what we paid, it's reasonable value overall (considering what you can be charged in London), and the convenience of the location is also welcome.

title: AVOID AVOID
text: Dreadful, absolutely dreadful. Old, dirty, room temperature cannot be regulated. Bed very uncomfortable, like old army cot. Wallls very thin so you hear everything. Bathroom small and not well appointed. The toiletries consist of carbolic soap. This hotel proves there are no star hotels.

title: Very nice
text: This was a lovely hotel within walking distance of Kings Cross (10 - 15 mins). The staff were very quick to check us in the room was smallish but very nicely decorated and spotless. ,my only complaint about the room would have been it was very warm but that would be a plus for some. The breakfast was excellent. All in all we were very pleased with the trip

title: Wonderful
text: Lovely stay. Check in was swift and everything I needed to know was explained. Every staff member I came across within the hotel was very welcoming, polite and couldn't do anything more for me. One exceptional member of staff, who was a trainee in the restaurant (Bindu, I think her name was) was particularly attentive, could see I was alone and made the extra effort to make conversation with me, which made my stay more exceptional. I got a free evening meal (buffet) on my first night, I went down towards the end of service due to my late arrival, so there was limited choice but still plenty and of good quality. Breakfast was also buffet and pretty standard. My pillows were hard, asked for softer ones but was informed that the hotel only had one style of pillows. The night porter then arrived with a soft blanket to see if that was any better for me. They went above and beyond. The last shout out goes to the housekeeping team who were the happy smiling faces I saw as soon as I left my room each morning. Room was spotless and perfect for my stay in London as it was close to Euston and where I needed to be for business.

title: Great hotel on a budget
text: Can't understand bad reviews on this hotel, its a lovely hotel when on a budget, can't ask for more, we got a great deal direct from hotel, 2 nights bed and breakfast and a 3 course meal on the first night, for around £190.00, which if your looking at London prices is really good.
