The location is great, we went to see a great west end show and had a lovely leisurely walk back to hotel, (not a long walk by any means), you can walk to convent garden, british museum just round the corner, oxford street easliy walked too as well. If walking isn't your thing a tube station on the Piccadilly line is a few minutes away, to take you directly to convent gdn, oxford st, west end down to knightsbridge etc, with easy changes to other lines. Yes, the rooms are'nt spectacular, but for the price, the're very clean and well maintained with more than enough room to enjoy a few nights stay, you really will not be in your hotel room for that long anyway in London, if you are, stay somewhere else. I requested a quiet room and we had no problems at all with noise. Check in was swift with no problems as was checking out, found the staff very pleasant at all times, room/bar/reception/breakfast staff, all very helpful and friendly. The bar downstairs had very reasonable prices, (more so than we have at home, which is unusual in London), but really no complaints at all, the breakfast was very good, as was our 3 course meal, which was in Jaques wine bar attached to property, again very reasonable wine prices too. If you want a great value, comfortable hotel with very nice staff, within reach of the most of London tourist spots don't hesitate to book, no complaints at all for our needs when on a London trip. Hope this helps anyone hesitating, great location.

title: More than adequate
text: We stayed at The Tavistock for four nights, having requested a room overlooking the Square and on a high floor. Both requests were granted. The in-house bistro was chosen for our first night complimentary dinner and it didn't disappoint. Good food and pleasant service. Our room was on the small side but it was clean - the bathroom exceptionally so. Top marks here! Oh, and towels were changed every day - a nice touch. Breakfast, buffet style was as good as we've had in any similar establishment - wholesome, plenty of choice and hot. No shortage of pleasant staff too. Now for the only pitfall. If you enjoy a pint of well kept draught bitter, avoid the hotel bar. My Marston's Pedigree was as flat as a fluke and even the lemonade in my Wife's shandy failed to produce a head! This apart, this hotel is reasonably priced and in a great location for the West End. We will visit again next time we're in London.

title: Great value for money
text: Me and my family booked this hotel expecting it a basic hotel for the price we paid. When we arrived we were suprised to find the hotel was much nicer than expected. Staff were very polite during our whole visit. I shared a twin room with my younger brother and the room was very spacious, not cramped. The toilet was in a separate little part in the room than the bath tub and sink which me and my brother preferred since there's no more waiting for each other to get out the bath to use the loo. The breakfast was great, fry up, cereal and toast. Also, we got a free three course meal included on our first night with the price. We chose Poppadom Express but didn't enjoy this as much. The starters and deserts were great, the mains not as much and I found there wasn't much choice for me personally. We visited the downstairs bar a couple of times and bar staff were polite. Near lots of transport to get to most of the attractions, apart from Harry Potter tour which took us an hour and a half on underground, overground than a shuttle bus (we didnt realise how far it was out of Central London) Overall, great hotel and I hope to be returning next year! ☺

title: Hot, hot, hot even in November!
text: I have been in this hotel a couple of times for business trips. Clean and well located hotel, if not a bit outdated. Overall staff is very friendly, but sometimes it depends on how busy they are at the reception. At my final visit the welcome was not very warm. The rooms are clean and basic. Frontside is a bit noisy, in particular since you have to sleep with your windows open, as it is utterly hot in many of the rooms. Central heating works on overdrive, apparently. My heater was turned off, but I guess that the heath comes from the piping and adjacent rooms. This is not pleasant,

title: Very friendly and helpful people
text: The staff were very friendly and helpful. The meal on the first evening was excellent! Within easy walking distance of Kings Cross and the West End. Very good selection for breakfast. The room was small and a little tired but adequate for three nights and very clean. Only soap provided, no toiletries. We would consider staying again in the future because of the kindness and friendliness of the staff and the convenience of the location.

title: Good location
text: If you stay two nights you get a free evening meal. This is taken in the adjoining bistro/wine bar and we were pleasantly surprised when it was really nice. We ate there the second night too and a bottle of wine was reasonable. But what a grumpy guy in charge of breakfasts! Food was OK but he was a bit frightening!.

title: Good location
text: Tavistock is an older hotel , it is clean and well kept. Euston and Russell Square tube stations are within walking distance. Easy access With the underground from Heatrow to Russel Square, and a two minute walk to the hotell. Small but ok rooms,a lot of noice from the street. Breakfast is very simpel.the bar is cozy. Hotell staff is nice and very helpful

title: Tavistock Hotel in Bloomsbury
text: Big and impersonal. Breakfast is good but very difficult to get a second cup of coffee. Rooms are simple and clean. In the heart of the Bloomsbury neighborhood, which in my opinion is the best neighborhood to base a tourist stay in London. Room on west side can be very hot on sunny days. Could not open the window because of the very loud party at the bowling alley - until 3AM! Quietest rooms are located in the interior service well area - white noise from the fans.

title: Good budget hotel
text: Check in could have been more welcoming, the foreign staff seemed disinterested. I had previously telephoned to request rooms on the 7th floor and that was dealt with in a very helpful manner. The Art Deco reception area is very nice and the hotel is generally clean. We were allocated a "refurbished" room but the refurbishment had not extended to painting the window sill! The room was very hot but this was not the fault of the hotel, just the gorgeous weather. Difficult at night when the window had to be closed because of traffic noise. The breakfast was adequate with helpful and pleasant staff but the bar staff all appeared to have been subject to charisma by-pass procedures. Not a smile or pleasantly to be seen. A complete contrast was the Jaques Wine Bar, food was good, prices competitive and the staff were brilliant - so helpful and friendly. The Tavistock Hotel is a good budget hotel for seeing London with convenient tube station and bus stops. I would be happy to return.

title: Fair but could do better
text: An excellent location

title: Good location
text: My third visit in this hotel. When you book make it directly through their web-page so you can get the English breakfast included and if you stay more than one night you can get free three course meal. The price is a bit high compared to the value, but that is normal in London. Rooms are tidy but worn. The double bed we has was really small for two normal sized, so it is better to have twin room. Since my last visit they have wifi-covereage in the rooms and that is good.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: I was apprehensive about staying here after reading some of the negative reviews. The room was clean and comfortable, the staff very helpful and polite. Breakfast was good. Very central. Will be booking again next time I visit. The hotel is ideal if you only need somewhere to sleep which I did. They also will hold you bags after departure for 50p each which is so much cheaper than £11 at the train station.

title: good value in a convenient location
text: Providing you are able to get one of the recently refurbished rooms you will get value for money staying here. Breakfast was OK overall with the hot food good quality. Staff were friendly and helpful.

title: great location
text: This was booked by family member for 50th birthday. myself and wife found hotel easily accessible by public transport. Either by train.(Euston station) underground(Russell square) , and by bus. Hotel staff very friendly and helpful, Rooms were adequate size, clean and bright. we had Evening meal which was excellent and reasonable priced. Breakfast which was full English or continental very good and staff more than helpful. Would recommend this hotel for short stay or longer.

title: perfectly adequate
text: This is one of a chain of Imperial hotels in London. I've stayed in the nearby Royal national with pupils and it was fine for the purpose, but must be horrible if you're a private traveller. The Tavistock is much nicer. It is a fairly bog standard London hotel. The bathroom wasn't spotless, but ok, and it did have a very good shower - a bonus! The bed was comfortable, and it was pretty quiet. Breakfasts are always a bit nasty in these places: watery scrambled eggs, cold hard toast, greasy fried eggs, dubious sausages, tinned tomatoes and so on, all kept tepid on a buffet. We struggled to get the waiter's attention for tea, then there seemed no chance of a top up. The waiting staff generally were a bit grumpy. The front desk were great, however. I was in town for a conference, and my husband came along. He asked if he could stay in the room until midday, and they agreed without a fuss. So, not a lovely experience, but good value for money and you can do a lot worse in London if you just want a bed and a base.

title: Convenient, great staff.
text: Regular visitor, always staff helpful, food good selection. Rooms adequate, clean and fresh at all times. Convenient for central London shopping. British Museum close, Very good value, especially weekends. A warm welcome assured.

title: Nice hotel with good location
text: We were 3 couples in Tavistock hotel near russel square in london , Hotel is very nice and clean with small rooms and comfortable beds , bathroom is very small but clean , the shower is very old ..... Location is great , 5 min walking to the russel tube station.

title: musical trip to london
text: my daughter and I are just home from a 2 night stay at the Tav. What a great place to stay.We arrived from Scotland at 8.30 a.m walked 5 mins from Euston station and we were there. The girl on reception checked us in straight away, no messing about with times. room 351 was more than we were expecting from previous comments, the shower alone was worth the money. we don't know London so armed with out wee map off we went. We found all the hotspots all within walking distance of the hotel, so much so we were walking around for hours and kept finding somewhere else of interest round the next corner or over the street.We booked seats for THE BODYGUARD and already had tickets for THE JERSEY BOYS both of which were BRILLIANT. next morning buffet breakfast , all the usual stuff, which was very nice and hot. So all in all the tavistock hotel was fantastic and would have no problem recommending it or using it again for any future visits to London.

title: Value for money
text: Within 15 mins walking distance of King's Cross/St Pancras and/or Euston stations and a similar distance from Oxford Street/Leicester Square/Covent Garden. Also within 5 mins walk from Russell square underground station. Room excellent, breakfast good with option of full English for an additional £5. Will stay here again.

title: Worst sleep ever!
text: Although the location is really good the hotel itself needs a really good rennovation. The staff was rude and uninterested and the bed awful. We woke up tired and with sore necks. Although the price is good, I would definitely prefer to pay more and have a good night sleep.

title: 1975 called - they want their hotel back!
text: I've worked around this area for many years, but when a project required enough overtime that we had to stay in a hotel, this time we stayed in the Tavistock... What a disappointment! The faux art-deco reception looks pretty tired - Not a good start, genuine art deco looking old, fair enough, but fake decor looking tired should just have been replaced. The lifts appear to be ancient and are glacially slow, the hallways appear to have been decorated 20 years ago and the rooms are similarly tired. There was great pressure in the shower and an abundance of hot water, and the bathroom was clean - the bath felt like the enamel had completely worn through, no danger of slipping, but you wouldnt feel comfortable having a bath with the somewhat abrasive bath floor. Luckilly I had brought shower gel and shampoo with me, because there were only several cheap looking bars of soap provided. The room was pretty small and also looked tired - there was a small flat screen TV which I didnt use also an elderly looking kettle with a pack of tea or coffee - no biscuits or bottle of water. There was a single plug point in the room by the kettle - nowadays there should certainly be a point by the bed for a mobile phone, but I think the Tavistock was decorated well before mobile phones were invented.. evidently there is a club nearby - perhaps the bowling alley under the hotel, because on Saturday night the noise was incredibly loud and if I hadnt been so tired it really would have stopped me sleeping. Wifi in reception only, not the rooms... Not so good! A drink in the bar at night was complicated by a broken credit card machine, but breakfast was a real shame - if you like an English breakfast there is a reasonable selection, but the "continental" selection was a fruit salad, some cereal and coffee (as advertised by some grubby signs). I should say that staff were generally friendly and while I stayed for work, if you are a tourist, this is certainly a very convenient location - but please dont leave London thinking that this is what we consider to be a good hotel - this is a pretty average hotel, but if you dont pay too much for it why not?

title: Good Value and Location
text: We booked this as part of a Superbreak deal, which included Train travel. The hotel is close to both Euston and Kings Cross railway stations. Check In was straight forward and staff were polite and helpful. Our room didn't have aircon and sleeping with the window open was a little noisy. Will ask for an even numbered room next time. That said, nothing else wrong with the room, which was cleaned every day. Plenty of choice of breakfast. Some dishes not as hot as we would have liked, probably down to the dated lamp heaters. Nothing wrong with the food itself, or the choice. Very helpful staff in the dining room. Superbreak deals include free first night dinner at one of Imperial's local 4 hotels. We stayed at the Tavistock for the Indian Buffet. It was terrible. My wife complained to the manager, who seemed genuinely sorry and who thanked my wife for her comments. A replacement meal voucher was offered for our party of 4 and we ate at a very good carvery in another of their hotels. This hotel is what it is - competitively priced, dated decor in the bedrooms, nice public areas, but in an excellent location for transport links, Underground and walking into "town". Nothing in life is perfect and the pros clearly outweigh the cons at this hotel. For those reasons we will be staying here on our next visit. If you want luxury then use another hotel and pay the extra for it. From our experiences, there is nothing wrong with this hotel that a traveller should be put-off by.

title: lovely hotel
text: went to stay for 2 of the hottest nights in London 31deg!! arrived at 10.30am check in not until 2pm but our room was ready and we checked in with ease. room was nicely decorated a bit small but very clean. great location for all sights 5mins walk from Russell square tube station. had our first evening meal free in the hotel it was very nice. good choice on menu. staff very nice. Breakfast was a help yourself set up excellent choice of cold or hot food presented nicely.staff a little grumpy! but it was very very hot. The hotel itself was a lovely art deco building with lots of character we would stay here again

title: Excellent value
text: This hotel is not luxurious, but has an excellent location. Many places are walking distance, like The British Museum, subway station, shops. The room is basic, but very clean, white crispy linen, comfortable beds, clean bathroom with a good shower

title: basic but friendly
text: Room basic and could have done with a lick of paint , but as we used it just as a base to sleep it was fine for that purpose , cooked breakfast buffet average, Staff were very friendly and were a credit to the hotel . Very near to russsell square underground (less than 5 mins walk)and bus stop at side of hotel.The £7or £8.40 all day travelcard (price depending on what day you travel) covers all the major sites in london and was a godsend as could be used on underground and buses.

title: Handy Location
text: Clean, comfortable and centrally located this hotel isn't luxurious but is reasonably priced. We had 2 nights here and had a complimentary 3 course meal (which must be taken on the first night), not gourmet, but good so we ate there the second night as suited our time limitations to get to a show. Good breakfast, all the staff were polite, friendly and helpful. Nice bar for night cap. Only small soap bars are provided in the bathroom, and one towel each, one coffee sachet and one tea bag supplied each per day, if we were staying longer than 2 nights I would have asked for another towel and one more coffee sachet each but we were out both days so wasn't an issue for us. This is our third visit to this hotel and we haven't been disappointed. Would recommend as reasonably priced and centrally located

title: Great location
text: Stayed here for two nights 17th/18th May 2016, great location, clean hotel, it was dated but hey you get what you pay for!! Included in the price was a three course meal on the first night and breakfast both mornings. You could choose to have your evening meal at any of the sister hotels and we chose to go to The President Hotel along the road at Russell Square. The meal was okay, just an average carvery, the service was very intense, there was more staff than guests and they seemed very on edge which seemed to rub off on the guests, if you moved they were there asking if everything was okay or if we needed anything, don't get me wrong they where very nice but it was a bit like being in a doctors waiting room, everyone was whispering, it was silent and no atmosphere. Breakfast back at our hotel was nice, lots to choose from, my husband said it was the best bacon he'd had in a hotel! There was no internet from us arriving to us leaving. On our arrival we where told the internet was down but engineers where working on it and would be back on after about an hour and a half but it never was. Day time staff where very nice, happy, polite and ready to help you in any way, from reception to porters, they all greeted you with a smile and a hello. Now the bar staff on a night was a different story!!!! Totally ignorant, miserable and downright rude!! We went back to our bar for a night cap, got served off a girl with long blonde her in a ponytail who never even managed a smile, or a hello, never mind a please or thank you, all we got was a nod of the head instead of a "yes please"! We sat a little table at the end of the bar and as we put the drinks on the table, it wobbled and quite a bit of wine ended up on the table, asking for something to wipe it up with she flung us some serviettes over the bar with a stern look, there wasn't enough to dry the table so my husband asked for some more, she didn't answer him just came round with a cloth and a spray bottle and sprayed the table along with my husband and myself and told us someone had moved the table so she picked it up and moved it where it should have been leaving my husband and I sitting on chairs with glasses in our hands and no table, I actually laughed, I think more out of embarrassment, we got up and moved back to the table and the next thing she was back with a mop and bucket so we had to get up so she could mop the floor, to say the least she was fuming. The next night we thought we had escaped her as there was an older man serving but he was no more happier or politer than the barmaid.... Then she arrived!! To close the bar without announcing she was shutting it and then had some guested asking for another drink to which she just waved her hands at them and said "SHUT" One man got really upset at her behaviour to which point we thought he might have been asked to leave as he got that mad. It never spoilt our stay and yes we would go back for definite and maybe the barmaid might have been taught soon manners!!

title: Bed bugs!
text: The title says everything. To make it worse, when confronting the owner, we were told that we were lying until we showed her video taken with phone. Even after that, no apology! Considering that husband had bites covering arms, legs and back, I would say that we are never going back and recommend no one visit this establishment! By the way, we were still charged for our stay!

title: Small and no lifts - but there were positives.
text: The hotel is in an old building, Sussex gardens were family houses in the 19th century and so the rooms are small because that is the way they were built. The hotel was in fact immaculately clean because it was recently decorated, the bed was comfortable and I have to say that we got posh biscuits in the room which is quite rare for less than 4 star! The hotel was very well situated for Paddington station, places to eat around - especially breakfast because the hotel breakfast stopped at 8.30 which if a bit early if you have had a good night out. The reception staff were helpful - Spanish speaking which might help some. It might be a good idea to ring the hotel directly for their rates. The Balmoral House Hotel was an annex of Balmoral Hotel and we had to cross the road for reception and breakfast. This was not actually a problem - I have been in bigger hotels where I have walked further to get to the dining room!! If you have a large suitcase (and certainly if more than one large suitcase was being used in the room I had) you may find the rooms are much too small and really struggle on the stairs, but if you are on a short trip to central London or are staying over night and you are using the Heathrow Express from Paddington it is a good choice.

title: great location, spotless rooms, good breakfast
text: 1 block from the train/ Tube, clean spotless rooms, nice friendly staff

title: Serves a purpose
text: The room is good, pretty spacious for a London hotel. Warm in February! Hot shower, wifi good too. 5 minutes walk to Paddington so a great choice if you are passing through London or here for a weekend. Breakfast .. sorry .. not good! My bacon was like cardboard and the eggs were .. solid! But, coffee was really good.

title: Not what I expected at all
text: First off, I should point out that this hotel has two buildings across the street from each other. I really wish someone had told me that in the first place so I hadn't gone over to the other side with all my luggage and then have to cross back over. Now you can tell that the hotel really isn't designed to have a 10-day guest, who is single. Yes they have a few single rooms, but the dinning area really isn't meant to have a single person eating in there. All the tables are for families except the one couple table. Breakfast is served between 7-8:30AM, which for me personally is way to early for someone on vacation. If you do stay here go earlier, there are less people in the dining room and you are less likely to have to wait for breakfast. You are only given one key which unlocks both the front door and your room. It's not a key card that is coded for both, but an actual physical key. Which meant that anyone could go into your room if they really wanted to. There was also no way to let housekeeping that you didn't want them to come in. For me there were only two upsides to this hotel. The mattress I slept on was better than my own at home, and the service the first and last day I was there. On the first day I had the guy at the front desk offer to bring my bags up to my room and then on the last day the owner walked me out and held the doors open for me. So will I recommend this hotel to anyone? Most likely not.

title: You get what you pay for......
text: There was an initial mix up when we arrived as the hotel had double booked the family room. As a family of five we were spilt into two room on different floors. Not too much to complain about though as they did admit their mistake. We managed to get in to our original room that was in the hotel over the road. Breakfast served btwn 7 and 8.30 but we were advised to be there for 7.45 to avoid queueing. Rooms are of a reasonable standard and clean. Great location for short breaks. Owner, receptionist and breakfast staff very friendly but watch out the grumpy old bloke who covers reception in the early morning. Easy for Lancaster Gate & Paddington and Hyde Park just 5 mins away

title: Bargainstay
text: Want somewhere cheap, comfortable and central? Then Balmoral hotel is the place for you and your family (unless you don’t like narrow stairs). A few minutes walk from Paddington Station makes it ideal for travelers. It’s also close enough to walk to Hyde Park and a quick hop on a bus and you’re in Central London. What’s not to love? We stayed in the hotel opposite the main reception building. Yes the facilities are basic and older, TV small, hairdryer didn’t work and shower head broken and shower/toilet very small, but the room was large, water and heating warm, very quiet (away from the street) and my single bed was comfortable. But when you’re paying less than £40 a night, it doesn’t matter. Aside from price and locality, the free full English breakfast was a major plus. Just expect to get up early for it as the kitchen closes at 8.30am. Will definitely return!

title: Absolute joke!
text: All I can say being in the same trade and knowing how stressful a family run business is, this hotel standards is the worst I have seen. My wife rang a few days before to see if we could have have mini fridge because of my insulin. She was rudely spoken to when she questioned why they couldn’t supply a fridge In our room even if it cost more. The older women then (apparently the owner) told if you don’t like it don’t come. Arrived there and was given a room with 2 single beds, even when we booked a double. Was given another room straight away. 👍 We had booked for3 nights and our room was not cleaned for the first 2 days. Breakfast was like herding sheep in a small room cramped as if we were animals. The old lady who runs it on behalf of her daughter needs to step down and realise we live in 2018 and London is part of England not Spain as majority of the guests staying there was Spanish. So I suppose from my point of view the older lady has issues and that takes effect on the staff, hence why the problems. Parking £15 a day was told, but apparently had to pay cash? I wonder why when we paid for rooms on card they have card machine? Dodging tax? Authorities will be informed. Don’t stay here! Look somewhere else if you don’t want bed bugs.

title: Avoid
text: We booked through booking.com and had confirmation of double room with en-suite shower. After climbing six flights of stairs found a dirty twin room with shared shower on landing. Ad has claimed price reduced from £150 to £79! Not so. Was only ever £79 and too much at that. Did however give immediate refund. We will not be returning.

title: Returning to our home away from home!
text: Our family just returned from our week long stay at the Balmoral House Hotel. We have stayed there many times before and the owners make us feel like we are part of their family. They have done so since we first met them in 2001. Some things never change and it is best that they don't. You always know you will get a clean and tidy place to stay and a wonderful English breakfast made to your liking. It is always a treat to come back to Balmoral House, conveniently located near Paddington Station. Lots of wonderful restaurants nearby. We can not wait to return on our next visit to London.

title: Avoid this hotel at all costs.
text: Family break to visit the Winter Wonderland in Hyde Park. Check in was easy with our booked parking bay available early. The room was small but the bed was clean and comfortable. toilet and shower en-suite. That’s the good bits. The hotel is split over 2 properties either side of the road. The balmoral house is the “annex” with no staff on site. So the noise level is very high with shouting and drunken groups. During our stay room 7 had around 8 people in it still going strong almost until breakfast with loud music animated full volume drunken conversations slamming doors and trying to get into our room as in their drunken state could not work out which room was theirs. Complaints to reception made no difference. this went on from around 4pm until after 1:30am. The hotel owner said we were lying as the group only had the room to leave cases in while they went to a show. The rooms all had very thin walls so when our neighbour used the toilet it was as if they were in ours so if you object to hearing someone else using the toilet think again. Breakfast was included in the price. The staff were friendly but they seemed to only cater for Eastern European visitors as English was a problem. Breakfast choices were egg bacon? Coffee? And that’s exactly what you got. Over cooked egg and burnt bacon. In all fairness the coffee was very good. The staff that cleared the table was able to ask “I bring now” to see if we had finished. However on checking out we spoke to the reception about the issues we had the owner said we were lying and nothing had happened overnight the guy who answered the phone admitted that we had called to complain and he had come over to ask the party to be quiet. But again the problem with a lack of english being spoken by the staff just ended up with a shouting match from owner of the hotel. The location of the hotel is fantastic but in every other respect go somewhere else.

title: Not worth the money - one star!!!
text: The hotel is located in a great location near the Paddington Tube Station ... Unfortunately that's it's only good quality. Let me start off with my introduction to the front staff. The guy working the front desk assured me I only booked for one night. After I showed him my confirmation email he said, "oh okay - looks like you are booked for 3 nights." He then wrongly informed me bfast was from 0630-0830 (although all the signs around the hotel indicated bfast was from 0700-0830). Check-in was at noon and we arrived at 1215. Our room was not ready yet. So we waited. Then at 1315- they told us our original room was not ready but they had a room at a higher level that was ready. I said, "I will take it." (Considering my husband and I had tickets for a matinee show). My husband carried our suitcase up 5 floors of narrow stairs. We entered our room only to find someone else's suitcase in our room!!! Seriously? We then called the front desk and the lady owner said - I'm sorry the boy who checked you in is in the bathroom and I don't know what he did. 5 minutes later a lady showed up w a key to our new room (which had not yet been cleaned). We entered and it was 2 twin beds separated by a nightstand. We dropped our luggage and left. Needless to say my husband felt like my freshman college roommate all weekend! The next day we were booked for a Stonehenge, Bath and Salisbury Cathedral tour and had to wake up early to catch the bus. We went to bfast around 0700 and were greeted by really nice ladies in a small dining room in the basement with a few tables that could only fit at maximum 20 people at one time. Since we were the first people there it was great and the traditional English bfast was nice and filling. Things were looking up for the hotel. Unfortunately (this hotel is full of unfortunate moments), we weren't so lucky the next day. It was our lazy day and we slept in a little bit and went to bfast around 0815 (bfast closes at 0830) to only see a line for bfast. Remember the small dining room I described? It bit us in the bum. The line was long (from the basement to the entrance of hotel) and the staff was rude. They actually expected you to come earlier than 0830 (even if you were standing in line before that time) for bfast. We were disgusted by the wait time and rude staff, so we went to McDonalds conveniently located down the street near the tube station. Bottom-line: if you want hotel bfast, you need to get there around 0700. No sleeping in on this holiday! Later that day we needed to print our boarding passes and asked the front desk if they could print two pages for us and the old lady running the front desk said no because she told us that she didn't know how to work the computer and the other guy was in the toilet, but directed us to a nearby Internet cafe (nicest thing this staff did for us). The next day my husband and I decided to go separate ways (so I could go shopping)-I asked the staff to let me into my room because my husband had the key (and they told me No). After some reluctance by the staff, I showed them my passport and finally the guy let me in. Finally, checkout was smooth for me - but not for the family ahead of me. The lady had accidentally left the key on a table at the entrance of the hotel (this hotel consists of two spaces across the street from each other). The staff member (the same guy who checked me in) - proceeded to become very upset and he started huffing and puffing. This hotel has been the worst hotel I have stayed in. Besides the great location to Paddington Tube station this hotel has nothing going for it. It's old and not the cleanest. Definitely do not recommend this hotel. And if you do decide to book - do not pay extra for breakfast unless you want to wake up at 0630. Wifi is poor also. Only worked 15% of the time.

title: Proceed with caution
text: Well, the pro is the location, a few minutes’ walk from Paddington and easy to get to London attractions. A few other things may be worth mentioning, concerning the owners, the room and the service. Upon arrival, the female proprietor offered me and my friends a tiny triple room (which would have involved two of us sharing a small-looking double) but as the family room wasn’t booked, we were able to upgrade. Bizarrely, we were instructed not to use the double bed, as we hadn’t paid for it. The male proprietor clearly wasn’t happy about giving us the larger room. During the entire check-in process, a third member of staff sat and stared stonily at us, which was really uncomfortable. The room itself was an odd layout, as if it had previously been used in a different way and then knocked through to create a family room. The toilet and shower were hidden away behind what looked like cupboard doors, and the shower was tiny. Bigger/taller people will have problems using it. There was no sink with the toilet and so you had to walk through two sections of the room to wash your hands. My friend’s bed was dusty and during the night, she used her inhaler for the first time in years. The bed I slept in was beside a draughty window and also had a draught from behind from the doorway into the section of the room housing the double bed. But the worst thing was that, although the heating was on when we returned in the evening, it didn’t come on in the morning and the room was absolutely freezing. When we brought this to the attention of the owner as we left, she didn’t believe us – insisting that the heating had come on that morning – and unusually, no apology was forthcoming. Breakfast is only served until 8:30. The small dining room isn’t equipped to deal with the fact that everyone will obviously choose to have breakfast as late as possible at the weekend, and so we had to queue up the stairs for a table, eventually returning to our room before trying again. Then the plates of food were brought out immediately

title: Nice hotel. Poor and rude staff
text: When i arrived i was checked in by a quiet young a moody guy who didnt seem interested in the job. Bad start. I went to my room and was disapointed to find i was in a twinmroom when i specifically asked for a double upon booking. But as it was just one night i thought its fine it will do. I went to pick my girlfriend up from the airport, as was purpose of trip and later that evening went for dinner. When we came back we has not been in room more than 2 minutes when a older lady knocked on the door claiming there had been complaints from the noise of the tv which i found very hard to believe and that we should also turn out our lights!! The next morning was just terrible. At 1045 house keeping knocked the door and without waiting for a reply opened it straight away. My girlfriend confronted them and they told her we should be out already when check out was at 11. Then soon after they came again and once again told us we should be out. When we told them once again its not 11 the house keeper replied 'yes it is' waving her phone in our face with the time clearly stating 10:58. The hotel it self was nice enough but after this experience we wont be visiting again.

title: Dreadful customer service
text: Everything could have been better. The room was actually in a different building across the street. I tried breakfast one morning and had to get let in by another guest, after ringing the bell and standing on the doorstep for 5 mins, as my key did not give me access to the main hotel. The food was poor and some other random guest was placed on my table when most of the other tables were empty. The wifi worked for about 5 mins at a time and then threw you off, each time forcing you to put in all of your details again in the sign in page. The TV didn't work - I was there there for a few nights and was advised a technician would come to fix it - my continued complaint was just met with "a technician was meant to come, but he didn't". No apology, no offer to move room, nothing. The bed & pillows were so hard that sleeping on the floor would have been more comfortable - and it was an old fashioned place with a dozen sheets and blankets rather than a duvet, so way too hot when you mixed that with the lack of aircon. I'm in London a couple of times a month and this was by far the worst customer service I have ever received. Most disappointing.

title: What a disaster!!
text: Was put on fourth floor. No lift. 74 steps. Tiny room. Felt like we were staying in someone's attic. Room way too small. bathroom unbelievably cramped. Told manager that we only wanted towels and did not want our room disturbed. This request was ignored and they serviced our room anyway. Two nights here was waaay too long. Just a really bad experience.

title: Not bad for an inexpensive London hotel
text: Just came back from a long weekend staying in Balmoral House Hotel. My husband made the reservations without checking the reviews ... so I was a bit leery. We choose twin-bedded rooms -- for us, generally it's easier to move around the room that way. Yes, the rooms are small and so was the ensuite bathroom (the shower is almost claustrophic small), there is no lift and the staircase is exceedingly narrow. But overall ... it's a decent place. Quite close to Hyde Park, the Underground and Paddington Station (easy to get to-from Heathrow on the Heathrow Connect). The rooms were kept clean other than a small patch of mold on the shower ceiling. Pots in the room so you can make yourself a cup of instant coffee or tea (from a bag) (both are provided as well as sugar packs and creamers). Our beds had valleys worn into them .. but we were still able to get decent night sleep. All our pillows had a really funky smell ... we wadded up the coverlets and used them for pillows. Breakfast was eggs, bacon, toast and beans ... as well as a scone or croissant. We enjoyed most of the breakfast ... the oj was clearly from a can (metallic tasting) and two of the three mornings, the scones and croissants were obviously reheated (tough). For the price and the location, we'll be staying there again. It was clean and close to transportation so we could enjoy our visit to London. Please be aware that you will be sharing tables at breakfast since there are not many tables...and the tables are small for four adults, but fine for two adults and two kids. I made sure to check both beds for bugs when checking after reading some of the other comments ... we lucked out and there were none.

title: Beware - bed bugs!
text: Stayed in Room 15. Wish I'd read the previous reviews beforehand as we too were attacked by bed bugs. Horrible! We killed one and caught another, but suspect there were many more, judging by the state of our bodies the next morning! Woman manager initially agreed to refund us but, on departure, had changed her mind. She had decided that we might have brought them with us as a way of getting a free night's accommodation! I suspect the 'fleas' reported by another reviewer were also bed bugs, so I suggest you keep well clear of this place.

title: CRAP B&B NOT A "HOTEL" WITH VERY RUDE WOMAN MANAGER
text: Booked for 3 nights for a family room with private bathroom , was given 2 separate rooms with the bathroom and toilet outside the rooms and shared with other guests on the same floor. Rooms were small and beddings looked and smelled dirty. No elevator. So very hard to carry luggages to the 4th floor (Thank God for Valerio) for helping us carry our luggages at 1am arrival. HAS A VERY VERY RUDE MANAGER. Ask if we can check out early 8 am not stay for 3 nights because our problem was we were not given the room that we booked . (Good I only paid for the reservation and opted to pay the rest at the hotel)Manager said she's busy and will moved us to the 2nd floor once she's done with breakfast and just bring our luggages on the 1st floor. Got ever mad at us because we (my cousin and I) were discussing how to move our 3 luggages from 4th to 1st then 2nd floor with NO ELEVATOR ,no good sleep and have an early commitment to do. This place is not easy to cater needs of their clients . Good thing booking.com was contacted and only paid for 2 nights. Why? Beacuse the stupid manager said it wasn't her problem, it was ours. BUT. We checked our voucher and it said EXACTLY: "For more questions about the property, contact The Balmoral House Hotel." We moved out early and did not stay for that 2nd night. We were not persuaded to stay even from the pleading front desk and a very nice man Flavio Martinez (Good luck on your career) We were just happy to run away from this place and from the very RUDE and UGLY MANAGER to our new hotel ( Hilton Paddington). If you have options, do not dare to stay in this place... manager needs to change her ATTITUDE.

title: Awful - AVOID this place!!! A lot of fleas - if you want disease this is your place.
text: Unfortunately our annual vacation is RUINED by this hotel. The hotel is full of fleas that stang us and made us itchy and upset. Pictures are attached. As this is a serious issue we asked the manager to take care of it but they don't want to do so. It's too expensive to do it. In addition, you hear everything that happens the next door. I don't mention that the room's size as it is it normal in London to get a tiny one. They asked all of the money when we've just arrvied. Later we've grasped that they demand it in advance because they don't want you to check out early. AVOID this place!!!

title: BED BUGS
text: Host did not think that bed bugs were a problem, just said everyone has them. Well I am sorry but I do not have them and hope that I do not carry them with me. We stayed in August and it was hot, there is not any air conditioning.

title: Bad, checked out early after 1 night
text: Tiny rooms, family friendly yet no lift so had to carry prom up stairs for 1 year old and no high chairs at breakfast. When I gave the feedback to the manager she said in her day women sat babies on their laps to eat and so they can do that. I explained that this is more difficult to eat and feed baby but she wasn’t bothered and got defensive saying it would be more mess if the baby is in the high chair. We also wanted to iron some shirts but had to in the hall of the main building as the manager believes gusts would use the irons to burn holes in carpets and chairs and started aggressively asking me how much I think carpets are worth and would I risk it. I had only calmly asked why irons were not allowed in the room when I had seen ironing facilities advertised. Finally we arranged parking but had to park in front of the main building when we were in the building across the main road. When you have a baby, prom and all your luggage, this made it difficult to navigate logistically, and then after crossing the busy road with all our things, having to Cary them and baby up stairs to a tiny room was not comfortable. In the room the tv remote didn’t work, the phone didn’t work either so we had to use our mobiles to call reception and there were problems with the WiFi. When we called reception from our mobile to ask to use the iron, the manager seemed to admonish us not to leave it to the last minute for breakfast and to come soon for breakfast...this was at 7am when breakfast is until 08:30. Don’t stay here unless you have no other option or the manager changes her attitude.

title: Nasty
text: Arrived an hour before check in for a two night stay and was asked to pay for the second night upfront, OK? Then said I’d wait the hour in their lobby as I’d been travelling all day but was told no that’s not possible and I’d have too leave and come back later. Not a good start. Wifi is atrocious although it’s just outside my room on/off constantly and when it was working it had poor strength, OK to view emails but that’s about it.The restaurant isn’t a restaurant it’s a cellar that they cram as many people as they can in after you’ve lined up for half an hour. Asked the boy at reception for an iron and got told to come back in an hour. No I need it now. He sat there and did nothing. I went and found the infamous owner who after I asked for an iron called me inconvenient. Lovely Lady. I just hope the bites I got overnight are from mosquitoes not the bed bugs that everyone else seems to have fallen victim to

title: Felt like cattle at breakfast
text: Nice room for what we needed for. Breakfast was very average, not great if you’re a vegetarian! Only eggs and bacon, or toast, cereal. Daughter wanted sausages but not a part of breakfast. Not enough breakfast room for size of hotel. Tea bags must have been used a few times as tea pot was extremely watery, not worth drinking unless you get down by 6:30am? Staff friendly but felt rushed to eat and get out so others could eat! Shame, if breakfast time was more comfortable and welcoming I would give a better review.

title: "Very happy with our room"
text: Just returned from a short break. We had a very pleasant stay. The room was spacious and clean with a compact bathroom which had a good shower. Breakfasts were very good, varied and well cooked you could have toast and croissants and scones, a selection of cereals and also fresh orange juice and fresh fruit. All in all it was value for money. the young man on reception was also very helpful. Would definitetly stay there again.

title: Not a good experience
text: I have stayed twice in this hotel. Once in 2004 and again this year. The first time I stayed I had been warned about the grumpy rude owners, so I was prepared for it and just ignored it. This year I went back again and found the husband his usual grumpy self but the wife was just downright rude. I went back simply because I knew it was clean and the breakfast not bad. The first day I went down to breakfast at 8.45 and she was so rude to us saying we were too late because the breakfast was served from 7.30 to 8.30. There is no indication behind the room door saying hours and rules (just instructions in case of fire). She insisted on being paid immediately for the length of stay. I said OK but I expected a receipt. She made a big story about it, that the hotel was cheaper than others around (which I found not to be completely true because I made a few rounds in the neighbourhood) but the next morning she reluctantly gave me a receipt when I gave her the money without my asking for one again. I personally like to be welcomed with a smile not somebody who looks down at the carpet and says come in with a scowl on their faces. I will never go back there again, clean or not clean. But London is a great swinging city.

title: Wonderful
text: This reveiw is long over due. We stayed at Balmoral House in late April 2004 and unfortunately had an unexpected death of a parent back in the states while we were visiting London. We were notifed of the death late in the evening London time after the airline offices closed so we could not make plans until the next morning. We were visiting with our college aged son who had been studying in the UK and had different travel plans for after London so we had a very complicated trip with out the unexpected death of my father-in-law. Even before the bad news the host and hostess had gone above and beyond to accomadate our needs(giving us a quad room so we could store our son's semesters worth of luggage which we were taking home with us so he could continue his trip unencumbered) without being asked. The host and hostess of Balmoral House were sympathectic, helpful and understanding. They provided a breakfast for my husband after the dining room closed the morning after our bad news and they helped us make arrrangements to leave as soon as possible. The hotel is clean, the bathrooms are more than adequate but most of all the staff is kind, generous and went out of their way to help and provide support in time of great distress. We will never forget the kindness and helpfulness of the staff to strangers visiting their city. My thanks to them and we would never consider staying any place but the Balmoral House if we return to London.

title: Clean, tidy, functional, but!!
text: I was staying in London for one night and couldn't get accommodation with my friends, so I tried the Balmoral House Hotel. I didn't expect much for £65 per night, but when I arrived, I was greeted well by the staff. They said that they hadn't received the booking, so had to put me in a double room. Great, I thought, but it was on the top floor 5 sets of stairs up!!. Now I am 63 and not as fit as I once was, but the staff never offered to help me with my overnight case, even though they knew that I was going up 5 flights of stairs. The room was fine, with two single beds in an attic room, washbasin, tea/coffee making facilities. No ensuite but a shower/toilet just outside the door. This was shared between three rooms. No trouble for me, all clean and tidy. Breakfast was fine, it was described as a full English by the waitress, but was actually two eggs, two bacon and beans, with toast and fruit juice. Perfectly adequate for me. All in all, you get what you pay for and as long as you don't build your expectations up too high, you won't be disappointed.

title: Well located and spotlessly clean
text: Easy to access from Paddington Station with plenty of choices for eating out just a step away. The hotel was spotless, the breakfasts were great and the staff friendly. Yes, the room was on the fourth floor but clean and quiet. They arranged a staff member to come in at 5am to carry down luggage for another guest. Pleasantly surprised as it is relatively a cheap hotel in London. Would recommend.

title: Balmoral is Great
text: We spent 6 nights at the Balmoral House over Thanksgiving and had a very pleasant experience. The entire facility is spotless and excellently maintained. The owners are very attentive to the needs of the guests, including providing a tray of ice every night at our request. Includes an individually prepared full English Breakfast. Location is great: two blocks from Paddington, wonderful Italian restaurant (San Marcos) a block away, as is a very reasonably priced internet cafe. Only downsides: no lift (we requested and were given a room on the ground floor), bathrooms are VERY small. Also, be sure to clarify the rate you will be charged if you are going to pay by credit card. We had some miscommunication about that, although the owner resolved it in our favor as soon as we questioned it. We'll stay there again without hesitation!

title: Could be better
text: Stayed here in May 2004 and found the room to be clean and comfortable. The hosts are nice and the location is very convenient - close to the underground station and sightseeing bus stops. Yes, the bathroom was small, but I was more bothered by what seemed to be almost no water pressure in the shower. I am not sure if there are non-smoking rooms at this hotel but if you are bothered by the smell of smoke I would recommend asking. I did not ask so I am not taking points off for that. My real problem with this place was the breakfast. They stop serving breakfast at 9:00 so the small breakfast room was often very crowded after 8:30 and my last day here I ended up standing in line for a place to sit. When I did get a place, I was given toast that had been offered to someone else ten minutes earlier and was cold. The eggs had been getting more overcooked every day and that last day they were practically hard-boiled. I will probably stay someplace else next time, but if I did stay here again I would get breakfast elsewhere.

title: Friendly and attentive
text: We stayed at The Balmoral House Hotel as a family of six. We arrived after staying one night in a hotel nearby, that being a very poor experience. We found the staff very welcoming and friendly, the rooms really clean, the breakfast big and English (yum) and the security excellent. I have recommended the premises to friends and I look forward to going back.

title: Ideal budget stay
text: Stayed 1 night when on a training course. London hotel prices are ridiculous in this area so at £67 for a twin room, this worked. You get good value with a small, but neat breakfast included. The room was clean but won’t suit modern taste. If you have issues with stairs, be sure to ask for a ground floor room. Staff were all very pleasant at reception and breakfast. Recommended for budget traveller and short stay.

title: One Night Stopover
text: This Hotel was ideal for stopping over in London on our way from Plymouth to Cleethorpes. Travelling by train it was an ideal stop only a 5 minute walk from Paddington Station. We were in London to see a show on Thursday 31st October 2013. The welcome that we received was excellent. The customer service was second to none. The room was very clean and we both had a very comfortable night's sleep. The only negative thing for us was that we had to queue on the stairs for breakfast. When we eventually got in for breakfast we felt that we had been rushed. Before my wife could finish her cereals the cooked breakfast was put in front of her. But I must say that other than that the breakfast was very nice. We will definitely be booking this hotel again when we visit London in the future and I will be recommending it to our family & friends.

title: The Balmoral House Hotel
text: The reception of this hotel was located at the other side of the street. Location was good, near the London Tube. Very basic hotel but nice. The staff was pleasant. The only negative thing is breakfast, only possible till 8:30 AM.

title: mixed feelings
text: The hotel itself is conveniently located very close to Paddington station. It's nothing special, but pretty clean and well kept. They can also give you discounts. Breakfast was not the best I had in the UK. Bacon was very salty and toasts were cold at times. And the old couple of Spaniards who own the place (Audi and her husband) were not very friendly. They have certain attitude problems and it shows. Guys, maybe it's time for you to retire and pass your business to people who enjoy running a hotel.

title: Disappointing
text: Told at check in that one of our rooms was in Balmoral House hotel and the other in Balmoral Hotel across the road. The receptionist had a flippant attitude to the matter, saying "I think you are only here to sleep". Told us that we would have to pay an extra £15 if we wanted to leave the car there for an hour longer, when there was free parking right outside on the single yellow lines due to it being a bank holiday. Receptionist did not advise us that there is free parking outside on a weekend. Arrived for breakfast at 7.45 to find a huge queue coming all the way up the stairs from the 'dining room'. Took a look inside to find people crammed into two rooms like sardines with hardly any room to move. Opted to go out for breakfast. Room was decent, with a clean bathroom.

title: London Hotel
text: Nice hotel, bit dated but for the price we paid it done us well. Nice clean rooms, TV and tea and coffee facilities in the room also a hairdryer. Comfy beds and small on suit. The booking came with breakfast included in the price and there is plenty to chose from, the staff were friendly and helpful. The hotel is very close to the tube station and there are lots of restaurants, bars and shops right on the doorstep. We enjoyed our stay.

title: alot of stairs
text: stayed here for 2nights.the room we had was no18 and unfortunately we had to climb 7flights of stairs(72 steps) in all.thats the only gripe.the room was warm,clean and tidy although not massive.Breakfast was brilliant,we had cereal of our choice followed by a full English.very adequate.

title: A family place
text: First off, one must understand that the owners are very particular about t he guests that stay at their hotel. They don't want hooligan types who are distructive and disruptive. I too had a negative first impression of the older lady at the desk. She is the mother of one of the owners and does need a bit of work on her people skills. However Harry, her son in law and owner and his wife are unbelievably kind. I was there for four days with my young son and could not have been treated better. Hotel is tiny with no elevators (we were on the top floor) but very clean with extremely comfortable beds. Our en-suite room had a small bathroom with shower

title: Spotlessly clean and perfect location
text: Perfect for transport links , plenty of excellent restaurants and pubs very close by , but best off it's spotlessly clean , comfortable , friendly family service and a good breakfast served from a open kitchen that was also sparkling clean .Perfect for a base to see London , much better value that a big chain , will be back

title: Great Hotel
text: This hotel is lovely, relaxing, very clean comfortable beds and the staff are very amenable. The full English breakfast is a good start to the day. It is situated very close to shops, restaurants and of course Paddington Train station and cube which can take you all over London and all tourist points, there is also a good bus timetable at the bottom of the road. We have stayed many times, lovely people.

title: Not what we expected!
text: Nice from the outside, rooms large and clean. The en-suite however was the smallest cupboard I have ever seen a toilet, shower and sink shoved into! You could sit on the loo,brush your teeth and shower your feet at the same time! The tv had unwatchable reception - someone came to look at it but it was obviously just the way it was in that room. A full English breakfast was toast, eggs, bacon and tomato but the waiting staff were nice. Wouldn't stay there again as the location was extremely noisy and no double glazing.

title: Excellent location and spotlessly clean..........but....
text: what a strange reception!!. We arrived to a reception area full of guests and had to navigate our way through heaps of cases to the desk to me met by an elderly gentlemen who just stared at us. I handed him our booking confirmation and he continued to stare at us. Not a word! Finally a lady appeared who took over but didn't seem to know what was going on. She even asked me to find our name in the book!! Fortunately it was there and although our room wasn't ready we were able to leave our bags and continue with our day. The rooms are split between two properties which is also a bit strange so we had to walk across the road for breakfast which wasn't a problem but is a bit disconcerting to start with and would probably be best if it was mentioned when booking. The bedroom was of a reasonable size although it was on the fifth floor with no lift so definitely not suitable for anyone with any mobility problems. The en-suite, although squeaky clean, was tiny and the handle inside the shower had fallen off which could have proved embarrassing had I not been in the bedroom to let my wife out. The entire premises, both buildings, were immaculately turned out both in cleanliness and décor. I don't know if they had been recently refurbished but we could not fault any aspect of it. Breakfast was OK although a little lacking if one is a Full English purist (eggs, bacon and a scattering of mushrooms) but in line with other reviews it is served too early (7.00 -8.30) and the dining room is tiny so you have to queue up the stairs outside for a table to become available. The staff (with the exception of our arrival experience) all appeared friendly and helpful and had our admiration for how they worked in such a small space without falling over one another. All in all we enjoyed our stay and we would happily go back and perhaps would not be quite so phased by the oddness of the character(s). Our room rate was £105 which I guess is about the going rate but the hotel does have its own parking spaces which was a bonus for us and at £10 is much cheaper than the surrounding public car parks- a definite plus point. If we were able to select a "good" that would be our rating but since Trip Advisor goes from "average" to "very good" then we have chosen very good as it was certainly better than average.

title: Very clean, quaint hotel
text: i stayed in this hotel for 3 nights. The check in was across the street from the hotel but the people were very friendly. The room was very small (especially the bathroom) but the room was extremely clean and maid service was provided every day. We stayed in room #6. There's free coffee, tea and cookies provided as well - replenished every day. There a free breakfast and I suggest going on an empty stomach. The "English breakfast" they provide is delicious and you won't leave hungry. There's juice (the best orange juice ever), coffee, tea, toast, scones, croissants and that's only the beginning. The English breakfast consists of 2 eggs, bacon and toast. They also provide more toast in a toast rack. Although you can't order from a menu, they will cook scrambled eggs in the traditional English style with bacon and beans if you request it. The servers are extremely professional and very friendly. The location was perfect....a 3 minute walk from Paddington station and within a 30 to 45 minute walk to Hyde Park, Piccadilly Circus, Trafalgar Square, Harrods and many other attractions. This was definitely a fabulous hotel for location, cleanliness and service and I highly recommend staying here.

title: Disappointed....maybe?
text: We arrived at Balmoral after travelling more than 30 hours from rural Australia. They had booked us into another hotel, Olympia, a few doors along. It was mentioned several times 'you are just staying 1 night'. We had booked in early 2917. We got a basement room at Olympia and they had a lift. Noisy fan right outside window, clean room, tiny but comfortable. They had a nice continental breakfast in the morning. In retrospect it sounded better than Balmoral, however, we consider Balmoral should have asked us about changing our booking to another hotel and it should have been our choice. Lack of proper communication re our Booking. Young men on front desk at both hotels were excellent.

title: Weekend in London
text: My partner and I only stayed for one night as we were just visiting London for a weekend. We arrived to the hotel 8.30pm and finished our stay the next day at 11am (latest check-out time). So this review is based on that. Check-in Got confused as there are two buildings across the road from each other and there were no CLEAR signs to let you know which building is has the main reception. At check-in, Emmanuel the receptionist is very friendly but there was an elderly lady who also runs the business told me to not make any noise. Room My room was on the fourth floor and the only way to get there is to climb steep stairs! I was slightly concerned about emergency access. Luckily it we didn’t have our kids with us otherwise it’ll be exhausting to carry your kids and bags up to the fourth floor. Probably best to request a room not so high up if you have kids or cannot go up many flights of stairs. The room I stayed on was just a normal double room you would get in a standard residential home with small standing shower & toilet ensuite but the sink is outside the ensuite just in the bedroom. Towels provided but you would have to bring all your usual cosmetics. Nice built in single wardrobe, comfortable beds and tea/coffee making facilities available. The TV is just a little bit bigger than my iPad

title: Great location, terrible attitude with regards to security.
text: We stayed here for one night after reading good reviews about it. It was really easy to find from Paddington Station and we checked in with no fuss. Our room was on the 4th floor and was clean and well equipped. We decided to head out for the afternoon and on our return we discovered our bedroom door was wedged open as the decision had been taken to paint our door whilst we were out. All of our belongings were in the room and anyone could have taken anything. The painter told us not to close the door however, as we were going to shower and change for the evening this was not feasible. My friend politely complained to the man on reception who seemed to believe we were making a fuss about nothing. There was an older lady in reception, who could possibly have been the owner, who simply said 'move her over the street to make her stop complain'. My friend was not impressed! I then went to speak to the guy who advised he didn't know the painters had left our door open and that he had spoken to them. I explained that a room that smelled of fresh paint and a lax attitude towards the security of the guests' belongings was not very good customer service. He was silent until I prompted him to apologise. It was a shame, the location was great and the street was beautiful but I would choose from one of the other hotels on this street next time.

title: Perfect location, super clean and nice hotel.
text: Perfect location, close to restaurants, pubs, Paddington tube station, Hyde park and London city. We stayed in the four bed room with four people and although it was a bit small it was perfect for two nights during our city trip. The room was very clean, as was the ensuite bathroom. The breakfast was really nice and everyone was very friendly. I would definitely recommend this hotel to everyone!

title: Terrible and Disgusting AWFULL is not the word...
text: The worst hotel I have ever had the misfortune to stay at, yes it's cheap yes it's close to Paddington but if you like being spoken to like dirt and threatened then by all means stay here. booked in for one night and when arrived was greeted by a very pleasant gentlemen at reception not a problem. It was later when I returned from a evening out with friends that a accedently locked my self out so I went to reception to get a spare key the women there would give basil fawalty a run for his money she was the most vile and deplorable person I have ever met she went berserk at me shouting and cursing i was dumbfounded by her reaction she went on to say she was the owner and had been in business years God only knows how, in the end she relented and gave me a spare. I went for breakfast in the morning and it was good surprisingly, went back to the room and next thing I knew she was at the door with two men from a building site asking me to leave. on asking why she had bought these men she said for here protection I said I had given her no reason for this, I felt threatened by there presence so decided it was best just to leave all the while these burly builders were looming over.My whole trip was ruined by my stay at this terrible hotel there a reason it's cheap I was not surprised to find very similier reviews about this lady on trip advisor.

title: alot nicerplaces for same price
text: manager was horrible, never spoke or gave us eye contact, guy on reception was great, really helpful, hes wasted working there. don't bother waiting for breakfast, served 6.30-8.30. big queue to be seated, ate each morning in local cafes.

title: Did the job!
text: Stopped there last night as needed a cheap hotel in easy and quick reach of Stamford Bridge. Only a few minutes walk from both Paddington and Lancaster Gate Stations. It was clean and welcoming. That's all I wanted!

title: The Balmoral Hotel is *very* clean and very good value and one of just a few places that still do full English breakfast
text: The Balmoral Hotel is located next door to a hotel my mother used to own in Sussex gardens in London. I have been going there for many years, since we no longer have my mums places. I have tried other places in this area for the same price and *none* can even come close in value for money, or (which is very important to me since my mum's places were spotless). There is in my opinion (and my husband and friends), no place better for the price. The people who run this business work like dogs day and night to keep this business to a very high standard for many years. The rooms are newly decorated, have tea/coffee making facilities, tv, and air conditioning in some rooms also. The beds are very comfortable and the bedding very clean and fresh. I do recommend this B&B highly. Once booked in, give them a call a couple of days before to make sure of your booking and then enjoy a great location, a great breakfast and a great city of London!

title: Bed bugs! Please, watch out for them!
text: Became ill from the many bed bugs bites. Management offered no compensation only a weak 'sorry for the inconvenience' and 'we miss money because we cannot rent the room'. Looking back on this site, it's clear that they have had this problem many times before. Unfortunately I had not checked this. Blankets obviously not cleaned properly. Sheets had black spots (old blood?). It looks clean, but looks can be deceptive. Watch out here! Having traveled around the world, I have never encountered a place so infested that I became ill.

title: Great hotel, friendly staff,ideal location.
text: We stayed for 5 nights in october, very friendly reception, always spoke when we came in at night ,the older lady and gent were very good with my son, the breakfast was very good staff worked so hard if you had to queue, it was not for long,room was ample for our needs, my son left his d.s.behind and they so kindly sent it back to scotland for him, also location was brilliant, near paddington tube 1minute walk also near hyde park, will be returning next year and will be going back to The Balmoral and would recommend to anyone. The Elliott Family.

title: Balmoral house for London visit
text: On our recent visit to London with aged parents who were returning to australia, we primarily looked for accommodation near to Paddington station. After sifting through the lists of places to stay we plummed for"The Balmoral house hotel" in Sussex square. Not knowing the area, the location of hotel and lugging 4 cases around we jumped in a taxi from outside the station on Praed street , only to be getting out of it around 400 metres away. We decided that it a was manageable to walk to the station when departing for the airport. Check in was easy and efficient, although our rooms were across the street in the other part of the hotel, on basement and top floor, after explaining that my parents would not be able to climb the stairs the hotel sorted out a ground floor room for them. The location and ease of accessing the underground at Paddington was great, a short walk and the grandure of Hyde park is at you feet. Oxford street is easily reached on foot. There are plenty of places to eat and drink around this area along London road. The hotel room was clean and well presented, it was a good sized double by London standards with en-suite shower and toilet, tea and coffee making facilities and plenty big enough for a weekend break in the big city. Breakfast is plentiful, with cereal, toast, croissants and cooked breakfast of eggs, bacon, etc all that are produced at break neck speed from the kitchen, with fruit juice and hot tea and coffee. This is a place I would highly consider using again if visiting London.

title: Don Anderson
text: We stayed here 15 years ago in 2002 and had no hesitation booking again for this visit to the UK. We were not disappointed. The hotel is very well run by a family who make you very welcome. Rooms are comfortable and well equipped even though a little on the smallish side. Breakfast (included) is very good and no one leaves the breakfast room hungry. This hotel is conveniently located, minutes from Paddington station and is well serviced by public transport to all areas of London.

title: Good value, good location, great staff
text: Stayed 2 nights after Christmas. This hotel is a short walk from Paddington train/tube station, very easy to find, very convenient. Also only a short walk to Lancaster Gate entrance to Hyde Park, took a lovely stroll through park over to the Victoria & Albert museum. Reception staff were very helpful and friendly, and the breakfast dining room staff cheerful and efficient, made a very nice start to the 2 days there. (Thank you). This is not a luxury hotel by any means, but room was clean, comfortable, warm, quiet and had tea and coffee making facilities and biscuits, and is very good value given its London. We would stay here again for sure.

title: excellent hotel
text: fantastic hotel well worth a return,,, the staff made us feel so welcome ..1st class service,, excellent location close to paddington tube..easy to get to central london and all the sights, excellent breakfast,

title: Infested with BED BUGS.
text: Literally the worst hotel stay I've ever experienced. Booked one night and after waking up found the room was full of bed bugs! On further inspection there were several blood stains on the bed sheets which were obviously not new, anyone cleaning this room should have seen these and not ignored them! I managed to catch 3 of them and brought them to reception and the guy working there did not seem to be shocked at all. When I asked to speak to the owner / manager, they were nowhere to be found. I demanded a refund to which he did process but at no point did I get the impression the staff member really understood the gravity of the situation. Bed bugs are incredibly difficult to get rid of and once we got home we had to spend hours quarantining and cleaning everything we had with us. Several items that could not be cleaned properly had to be binned! After looking back through reviews for this hotel, you can see they have had a pattern of complaints regarding bed bugs spanning back over a year so clearly not properly resolved the issue which is a serious health hazard. I will be reporting them to the local Health and Safety Executive. Who knows how many guests have unknowingly brought bed bugs back to their homes!

title: Beware- They didn't honour our booking , and rude attitude
text: I booked 2 rooms in February through booking.com as 4 of us were going to see the Killers in Hyde Park. We arrived at 1pm to be told we didn't have a booking but after showing our confirmation email and insisting they rang booking.com the story changed. Eventually, acknowledging that booking.com had sent through the details we were told there was nothing they could do with a very unhelpful tone and no hint of an apology. Unfortunately I couldn't get reception to ring booking.com so we had to stand our ground as we had travelled to London by train and you can't bring cases to Hyde Park. Eventually after some conversations they had between themselves in Spanish a lady (again saying what can we do and me saying that is not my problem, they have failed in their contract) brought us across to another hotel where we were told our only option is for all 4 of us to share 1 room. What could we do but accept it. As it turned out the Albro Hotel across the way was spotlessly clean with a lovely breakfast. Needless to say we didn't get to stay here but I would not recommend this Hotel by virtue of their attitude to their mistake. Go to the Albro Hotel across the road where Dave will look after you.

title: Value clean and a great location
text: Staying here for the weekend to watch phil Collins in concert at Hyde park and Sunday at Lords cricket ground.. great location for both with a 20 min walk.. smallish rooms but spotless .. good breakfast , if not a little too quickly served!! Helpful reception staff and overall brilliant value for what paid and what received

title: Great value for money
text: Six of us stayed here overnight and we were very pleasantly surprised at the top quality of this hotel given the Price we paid. It was central for what we needed and the main reception welcoming and staff knowledgeable about the area. The rooms were bright and clean. The bathroom was small but manageable and the bed had a slight dip in it but nothing that would stop you sleeping. Breakfast was plentiful with a choice of full English or continental and the hot food was actually hot and served quickly. The staff were very helpful and friendly and allowed us to keep our bags there for the day when we checked out so we could enjoy our time without dragging our cases around with us 😁would definitely use this hotel again.

title: Great place to stay The Balmoral House Hotel
text: I was in London with my family of five from Singapore - 7th to10th Jun 2017 on our way to Paris. Booked the Balmoral House hotel early and was happy to stay there. Good service and very convenient as it is near to Paddington Central Station. Its located just behind the hotel about 5 minutes walk. Paddington station u can connect to all around London and to airport too by Heathrow Express When you reach there, you have to walk across the road to the reception counter to check in and breakfast is also served there. Simple English breakfast and with good service staff. Francisco and Emmanuel great staff and they will also help with any info on how to move around. Many food and cafes around. Great places to visit as its my second visit there. But for my kids and wife its their 1st visit. Go to Primark shopping from there only 4 bus stops from Paddington.
