Visit Tower Bridge, Big Ben, Buckingham Palace, Hyde Park, Kensington Park, Tower Of London ..WestMinister Abey If u are a soccer fan visit Wembley Stadium and Emirates Arsenal Stadium. Visit Harry Porter Warner Bros Studio its a must. All by train. Booked a day tour to Stonehenge and Bath. U can take a train trip to Manchester United Old Trafford too. Buy the Oyster card to move around. Big thank you to Francisco and Emmanuel and all staff of Balmoral House Hotel. Rafik and Famil

title: BEWARE! EXTREMELY RUDE OWNERS!
text: dont bother staying in here! the owners treated me and all the other guests EXTREMELY bad!!! they treated us like pure c.r.a.p! worse customer service ive ever seen in my life! dont think: ohh it cant be that bad! TRUST ME IT IS!!! i serioulsy hope that places shuts down because guests cant be treated like rubbish like the owners treated me and all the other people that have stayed there! Read all the other bad coments! its a waste of money and it will drive you nuttssssssss!!!!

title: not happy with the owner
text: Bad experience with the owner. When we got there the owner had given our room to another family and put us in a larger one. The owner said, that we didn´t have to pay anything extra. When checking out, she had forgotten, and we had an argument. After we went back to our country, the owner made a bank transfer and paid us. The hotel itself was good, not the owner.

title: Best Budget Hotel
text: Budget hotels in London are hit and miss, and we've missed on a few. Balmoral House Hotel was a real find -- super clean, quiet, very well run.The bathrooms are small, as you would expect, but sparkle with cleanliness. The beds were very comfortable -- we actually slept well the night before travel back to the States. Breakfast was very adequate and they began service early enough for us to check out by 7:00 am. Francesco, who runs the desk, was very helpful.This place stays on my list for inexpensive London stays.

title: Standard English cooked breakfast .......... when you actually get to sit down!
text: The positive points of this hotel are the great location, it is very close to Paddington Tube Station. The room was clean and the beds/pillows comfortable. The staff are very friendly. The negative points are the bathroom was extremely tiny, so tiny that it was impossible to get dried in the bathroom. The wifi was non existent, (I gave up trying in the end and use 4G) There is no lift in the building which is ok if you are not at the top and finally the hot water is switched of during the day, so no showers during the day! The worst part of this hotel was the breakfast fiasco. Breakfast was from 6.30 - 8.30 so no chance of sleeping in! However, it gets worse. The dining room is so small that there was a queue every morning of my 3 day stay. At one point there was 15 people in the queue. Once seated (up to half hour wait) we felt under pressure to finish our food as you could see the others waling outside the door. The breakfast consisted of cereal, toast (white bread only) scones & croissants. Fresh fruit and cooked English breakfast, but the wait to be seated overrode any positive experience of staying in this hotel

title: Perfect
text: I just loved this hotel, friendly, helpful and warm staff. Cosy clean rooms... the location it is just perfect. I definitely will come back. Thank you!!!! Para los españoles, no lo dudéis ni un minuto, perfecto, el trato, la localización y el precio... Un 10! Gracias!!!! Volveré pronto!

title: OK but Landlady from Hell!
text: I only had to read the previous review to know it wasn't just me. This hotel is recommended by Let's Go, and I contacted the property directly. When I arrived the same grumpy landlady described by the previous reporter from Irvine tried to reneg on the price quoted. She indicated she'd quoted me wrong and didn't realize how busy they were, which is irrelevant to me, of course. When she finally relented she demanded that we pay in cash for the entire 5 days by the afternoon of our arrival. After checking in and unpacking I went to settle the bill. The landlady went psycho went I requested, rightfully, a proper receipt indicating that I'd paid for a 5 night stay in cash. She threw my money in my face, claimed I was "being difficult" and then said she was going to charge me for her burnt lunch that she'd had to leave in order to tend to me. If my party hadn't already checked in and unpacked after a stressful journey we would have left and sought other accomodations. THe landlady, who described herself as the owner (and, yes, she was in charge of the kitchen), was way out of line. I've never been treated like this before in my life by a proprietor. It was unsettling to say the least. It's a shame, because the accomodations and food were fine. I liked the fact that this property had satelite TV so I could catch some Champions League football matches. But nobody should have to receive the abuse I took. This property should be taken off any list of "recommended" properties.

title: Great budget hotel in great location
text: I booked a family room on booking.com for this hotel a few months ago, and it worked out about £30 with breakfast per person. Now when your only paying this it can mean a couple of things - 1) not the most desirable of locations or 2) it's going to be rather run down and unpleasant. This place was neither. On the downside the bathroom was a little small, and the hairdryer was held together with electrical tape, and there was a short queue for breakfast, but, let's get that into perspective. The staff were pleasant and courteous. The location was fantastic. We were 10 minutes walk from Marylebone station, two minutes walk from Paddington.underground - and there was an eclectic choice of restaurants in the road where the hotel is situated. The breakfast was quickly served, and the eggs, bacon and beans was support d by an ongoing supply of hot toast. The room was clean and functional, no its not The Savoy, but neither is it the same price. Would I use this again, yes is the answer, so there's your answer. In summary, easy to find, nice location and excellent value for money.

title: Excellent value
text: My husband travels regularly to London and often has to stay overnight in budget hotels. Usually he makes no comment but this time he remarked on how he had a vey clean and comfortable room . There appeared to be new carpets and fresh paint everywhere.The breakfast was freshly cooked and he considered he got excellent value.

title: Great stay at Balmoral.
text: l stayed at the Balmoral House Hotel, Although the rooms are small, The Breakfasts are great. l will stay again. Pjacobs @bishopamat.org

title: Good location
text: Met our expectations fully. Good place for a weekend stay with friends. Nice and clean. Easy to get around from Paddington station. A couple of good eating places nearby, The Victoria and Garfunkles among them.

title: Good Sightseeing Base
text: This hotel is in the Paddington area, close to Bayswater Road and other tourist areas, including excellent shops and restaurants. The Hotel is split into two parts opposite each other in Sussex Gardens. There is no lift. We were told to go across the road and up to the 4th floor for our room. There are 70+ steps. The room was an attic room, small but adequate, as was the shower/toilet facilities. Our room was very clean, beds were comfortable, a bit stuffy as no aircon. Staff were not exactly helpful. We were told that breakfast was served from 7.30am until 8.30am, when we got there the young man at reception was 'surly', he pointed to the stairs when asked where breakfast was served. We looked down the stairs and saw several people standing waiting for a table, more people were sitting on the stairs, we did not wait.

title: Minus 100
text: Balmoral House Hotel Our reservation was made via booking.com on 27th of January for one evening 29th January.We chose this as the most convenient hotel for St. Marys Hospital as a family member had to attend at 7.00am.We also reserved parking at an additional charge of £15.00 After a two and a half hour journey from the midlands we arrived at 11.20pm,parking temporarily outside the hotel in a private road, until I found out where to move the car for my reserved parking. Leaving our luggage In the car we rang the doorbell twice,the most rude woman I have ever met opened the door and stared at us as if we were dog dirt, we held out the booking form and said we had reserved a room,"who has reserved it." "When." We explained through booking .com "You have no luggage" I explained it was in the car until I knew where to park as I had paid extra for parking ,and enquirer as to where I should park the car. On the road she yelled I pointed at the main road at a white van she again yelled yes out there this is a private road. I went to move the car my wife horrified went inside. I parked on the main road went into the hotel and my wife just looked horrified. No booking no reservation but she said she would put us up opposite, I then asked if my car was okay on the road during the day as I had paid she said "you pay me £50 and I will park your car" I began to explain I would have had a better reception sleeping on my sons floor explaining that we had chosen this "hotel " for the convenience of the hotel and that I had never met anyone so rude.She then shut her book and y Told us to get out I said trip adviser and I am almost certain she told me to "bugger off" when I challenged her on her language she denied it saying you people go on get out.You people are not as good as me. Looking back at her first reaction to us with no case we think that she thought I had picked up a prostitute for the night. Half hour later we checked into premier inn Kensington £30 more and money well spent with free parking. Disgusting welcome, disgusting service, disgusting in every way. I would not use this place!

title: Not a good experience
text: We booked this hotel mostly because of its location close to Paddington Station. Sure enough, getting there was quite easy! We were quite excited for our stay, but that changed when we arrived at reception. The lady checking us in was quite unfriendly from the start, and this got worse when it turned out our booking wasn't what we expected. As far as we knew, we had booked a double room ensuite, but what we got was a twin room without a bathroom. Apparently we would have had to book the more expensive room to get the bathroom, but the provided pictures on booking.com definitely showed a bathroom for our room type and so did the additional information. The lady got very angry at us (as if we were just trying to get a better room for a cheaper price) and told us to just take this room or pay for the other one. In the end we gave in and got the room we apparently paid for. It seemed okay at first glance, but when we woke up my friend was covered in bed bug bites. We went downstairs to complain about this and the (much nicer and infinitely more empathic) guy at reception immediately offered us another room (with bathroom!). Right at this moment the lady from the night before came in again and, without asking after the situation, started to get angry because we were asking for another room again! When she heard about the bed bugs she understood, but remained very irritated, as if all this was our fault. Not once have we heard an apology from them for the inconvenience, even though because of all this we were never really able to enjoy our two-night stay in the hotel. Apart from all this, the English breakfast was quite all right, even though we thought it was very early (7am - 8.30am). The facilities seemed clean, but the tiny sink in our bathroom was clogged so we could only turn on the tap for a couple seconds at a time. The free WiFi is nice, though at the top floor we couldn't get it to work. The tea and coffee with biscuits in the room are a nice gesture. But all things considered, I would book something else next time.

title: Home away from home
text: This hotel never disapoints. We are a family of 4 and have stayed at this hotel many times. It is clean, neat and tidy and the location is excellent, only minutes away from Paddington Metro / train stations. The hotel serves a nice breakfast - English (eggs, bacon & sausages) or continental (cerial, toast, buns etc). The hotel price is reasonable for London. The hotel is in the process of being renovated and is even more comfortable than before. Stay here, you will not be sorry.

title: A very basic hotel
text: Hotels in London are expensive, and that's just the way it is. i knew what to expect because I had read other reviews and basically they all said the same thing: we wish we got more for our money. This hotel is very close to Paddington station, and was clean, the bedding adequate and the towels and toiletries fine. The wifi worked for the most part. On the negative side, the room was small, with out of date decor and the walls were paper thin. We carried our luggage up 75 steps to our room (no lift). We didn't try the breakfast so I have no comment there.

title: Good convenient hotel
text: We enjoyed a two night stay here. The staff were friendly and helpful. The family room was clean and tidy, although the shower room was a small as it could possibly be. Be prepared to queue for breakfast, which needs to be eaten between 6.30 and 8.30. A little early for teenagers!

title: Zero hospitality
text: I stayed here less than 2 months ago for 2 nights, prior to taking a cruise to the Baltic Sea coming out of yhe port of Harwich in England. I chose it for the location and price, but sincerely I did not know what to expect due to the mixed reviews in different sites. I also chose it because of the four beds in one room for my family of four. I expected a small room since I have been to big cities in Europe before, and this is the norm. When we arrived, with four 24" suitcases and 4 small carry on suitcases, the ownner said that we would not fit in the room. I told her to give me a solution, and all she did was insist that we did not fit. I asked her to show me the room, which was across the street from the main building in the Sussex Gardens region, which is a nice location. When I got to the room on the fourth floor with no elevator , which I also expected, I saw what I expected, one double bed and two single beds, a wood armoire to hang clothes, a small bathroom, and no air conditioner. There was enough room for my family and my suitcases, and I was ok with that. So here is the worse part... She said that we did not fit and that my suitcases would damage my room!! She treated my husband and I so mean and as if we were disconsiderate persons that I had to tell her that she was being disrespectful. She said that I was the one being disrespectful!!! She ended up giving me the key and the gentleman in the front desk escusing himself for her. I have never had this kind of treatment in a hotel while travelling. Just for that I would not recommend it. That who,le street is full of similar conveniently located hotels.

title: Clean, compact, old fashioned
text: We stayed here this week...I was hesitant after the reviews....Maybe should take more notice of them. Staff were friendly, it was also clean and freshly decorated however it's quite old fashioned inside. I didn't like the room set up for 5 of us...walk through one room to get to back 2 bedrooms ( no doors) 2 sinks in 2 back bedrooms. Shower on its own in compact space. Toilet on its own with no sink. We also had to wait in a lengthy queue for breakfast in the morning. Budget hotel approx 5 mins walk away from Paddington tube and railway station.

title: Good Hotel in great location
text: A tidy, neat hotel which is situated across both sides of the road that is well located for Paddington Station which gives access to the whole of London very easily and quickly. Reception staff friendly, helpful and efficient with very clear and concise explanation of facilities, breakfast location etc. Room was clean and well appointed although no air conditioning which would have been extremely welcome during my stay as it was on the hottest day/night of the year so far which means it was stifling in the room but I'm English and we always complain about the weather 😉. Places to eat and drink are plentiful and very close, a supermarket is located on Paddington Station so all your needs can be met easily. Price was also excellent for central London in July. Personally I'm not able to comment on breakfast as my departure was very early to catch a flight from Heathrow which was also very easy, 90 minutes from bed to duty free in T5 via Heathrow Express. All in all a fabulous hotel that I will definitely use again.

title: Budget Hotel and Feels Like It... Experienced some dishonesty too.
text: Stayed here last fall and this review is long overdue. Maybe things are better now, but I kept thinking about our experience here, which kind of put a damper on our whole family trip. Basic budget hotel, old beds, not super comfy, bathroom so tiny you can hardly turn around (and I'm a 5'3" thin girl). I could tell they try to keep things clean, breakfast is decent, and I loved the little teas and shortbread cookies they provided in each room every day, but the fact is that my parents found 3 bedbugs in their room over the course of 3 days... one bug a day. They finally bailed to the hotel next door after the third one. There was no sign of bug residue on sheets or mattresses, but once you see one you know you've got a problem and you will have to be very careful with thoroughly cleaning every item you brought on the trip, including suitcases. These bugs spread ridiculously easily. I know it's hard for hotels to deal with travelers from all over the world going in and out constantly, and it can be costly to pay professionals to come in and eradicate bedbugs. We spoke to the owner about the issue and she ranted about how the professional bugkillers overcharge and take advantage of them. However, this is an unfortunate fact of the hotel business and we felt she just did not seem to take the matter seriously enough. Our family owns apartment complexes, so we have dealt with this matter before ourselves. She thought she could just clean the rooms herself, which is not realistic. We were very understanding with her, but the thing that really made us unhappy with this hotel was the observation that after my parents moved to the hotel next door, my brother and I (who had not found any bugs in our rooms) spotted the hotel putting new guests into their old room THE VERY NEXT MORNING. Anyone who does their research knows that you need to give a room a couple of weeks to be sure all bugs and eggs are gone. This hotel not only did not do that, they wasted no time whatsoever in just putting some other poor sod in the room in question. It was just about money to them, not the wellbeing of their guests. It's hotels like this one that help to spread the worldwide bedbug problem with travelers. I now regret not saying anything to the unwitting new guests in that room. I hope they didn't end up with a bedbug infestation that they took home with them.

title: Bed bugs, food poisoning and a rude owner
text: Myself and my friends arrived on a Friday evening, before we were shown to our room we were told we have to pay for the next night in advance, this was strange to us but we went along with it. We were shown to a triple room which was ridiculously small, with a tiny bathroom! Tired from our journey we went to sleep and to our horror the next morning the beds were riddled with bugs. We were devastated and started to instantly pack our clothes away in our suitcases. We decided to throw our pj's in the bin! The bugs were crawling on the walls, mattresses, sheets, we were disgusted that we slept there for a night. We went downstairs instantly and told the man at the front desk, he didn't even seemed surprised and said he would give us a room in their sister hotel across the road. Reluctantly we said ok and went for breakfast, I use the word breakfast lightly!! It was the smallest breakfast room, with rude staff, they brought us eggs out of the kitchen, so who knows how long they have been stood there. I have never been so ill after having eaten the eggs! We knew it had to be the eggs because 2 out of 3 of us ate the eggs and only us 2 were violently ill. After a long ill day out, we returned back to the hotel at our new room. It was a 5 bed room, it had 3 singles and a double. The double bed had dirty linen that was instantly noticeable. To our absolute devastation within 20 seconds of being in the room, we saw a bed bug crawling on the bed. We went and got the guy from the front desk who was so lovely, he saw the bug and looked upset. He further asked us if we slept in this room last night, in which we explained we hadn't, he then dragged the sheets off the double bed and said "this is dirty, i am so sorry". We said we didn't want to stay here, the man said that he knew only one clean hotel on this road and he would try get us rooms there. We dragged our suitcases up the street and the new hotel happily obliged. The man said they would foot the bill and pay any extra it would cost. We asked about a refund for our first night and he said come back tomorrow morning. The next morning was by far a demoralising experience. We knocked on the door and was confronted by this little angry woman that was shouting "what you want now", "you got what you want", "go now". It was a horrific experience, we paid money to stay at a hotel riddled with bed bugs, a skeleton key for all the rooms in the house and no latch on the door, so you never feel safe! Worst wifi ever, a disgraceful breakfast and the rudest, angriest owner who's people skills are clearly lacking! This place needs an inspection and shutting down, do not stay here!!!! There is a reason you have to pay upfront!!!

title: bed bugs and food poisoning
text: Myself & 2 work colleagues booked this hotel for a weekend away. We stayed one night and could not face another. The tiny room we shared (double and single bed, with tiny shower room) was riddled with bed bugs. What was interesting was the acceptance from the gentleman at the desk (as if to say 'oh yeah..THOSE bugs..'). We were promissed a 5 person bedroom in the same named hotel across the road. For breakfast my 2 friends had the cold fried eggs (with solidified oil), I stuck with some coffee. Not long later we spent the day running to find them toilets and medication. Returning to the new room we saw a double bed with DIRTY sheets and 3 single beds... and more bugs. Te young gentleman working at the desk was horrified and took us to another hotel, which was clean and beautiful. The next day we went back to the hotel to find the female owner not let us in as she stood by the door with a broom shouting 'what you want from us!'. She was a horrible person and uncaring! We didn't get the money back. Nor did we get the clothes back that we binned the first night. We are from the UK (Yorkshire), we know our rights and will report accordingly. We understand the law and will be taking further. I highly recommend you pay the extra money to go better! A mistake we will never fall for again. I also recommend dont look for the high stars and good reviews, but the reviews that warn you of fleas/bedbugs etc.!!!!!!!!

title: great location
text: Just come back from a two night stay in London for some business and pleasure. I have to stay that this is a fab little place to stay in a great location you are so central to everything. We drove up by car but Paddington is literally a 2 minute walk away. The room was small but it was spotlessly clean, towels were changed the following day. I cant comment on the breakfast as we did not try it due to it being a very early sitting but the spanish lady who I think is the owner was very pleasant and greeted us on arrival. There had been some confusion over my booking (booked through booking.com) but it was sorted immediatley. Yes there are 2 buildings to this hotel on either side of the road but its no hardship to get to the other side. I will definatley stay here again.

title: Poor choice - you live and learn
text: Poor choice on my part. I paid £115 for a night stay with breakfast. I stay in Paddington regularly on business. There are far, far superior hotels in this area for the money. It's actually more of a guest house than a hotel. It's clean, which is my top criteria when staying away. I had an issue when I found the kettle wasn't working however reception was closed (it was 11pm) so I couldn't have a cup if tea. I also couldn't have breakfast as the queue was too long - I had a train to catch and only allowed my self just over an hour. The gentleman that booked me in had no personality whatsoever. Bordering on ignorant. I won't be staying here again

title: Compact & clean
text: Stopped over for 1 night, I found it very clean and snug. The breakfast was great just what I needed before my Triathlon, the only downside was I had to pay for parking which was £15. Would I stop there again, yes I would, maybe for no longer than 1 or 2 days. Top tip, Don't be a snob..!!!

title: Clean tidy ok for an overnight stay
text: Booking in was not the friendliest of affairs. We got told we were across the road at the other part of the hotel. Five sets of stairs later we found our room. It was small but functional. It was very hot despite the window being open. The room was ok for an overnight stay but would not want to stay any longer. Had to go back across the road for breakfast and join a queue. The breakfast room was far to small for the number of rooms in the hotel. Wish we had not bothered to take breakfast as it was not worth the wait. First and last time at this hotel.

title: Spotlessly clean
text: My daughter and I stayed in a twin room for 1 night in July. Given the very reasonable cost (£110) for such a central location, I wasn't sure what to expect but I was delighted with our room. Although small, it was spotlessly clean from décor (which looked fresh and recently refurbished) to bedding and en suite shower room (also all brand new and sparkling clean). The beds were really comfortable and the room had everything you need - tv, tea and coffee making facilities, hairdryer, 2 large mirrors and free wifi. The accommodation is spread across 2 houses on the opposite side of the road but this was explained clearly by the friendly staff when we arrived and not a problem at all. The breakfast was good and the lady who cooked and served it to us was also welcoming and friendly. Warm croissants followed by plenty of toast were followed by eggs and bacon on toast and plenty of tea, coffee and orange juice Despite all of these excellent qualities, by far the best quality of this hotel is the location. It was just minutes from Paddington (on foot), and only 5 minutes from Hyde Park where my daughter and I were attending a concert. The perfect location for our event and for any London visitor wanting easy access to all the sites. I will definitely be back, really impressed with what is a really clean, comfortable and friendly B & B!

title: Good location for a B&B but.......
text: We were disappointed on arrival in our Family room, to find it was not ready - beds that had just been slept in (despite being given the key by reception over the road and not being advised that the room was not ready, we arrived at 1pm, check-in 12noon). However we were leaving our luggage in the room and going straight out so this wasn't really a problem, just not expected.When we returned our room was spotless so we couldn't fault the cleanliness.The beds were comfortable, the en-suite EXTREMELY small, however for one night we could manage. The breakfast was delicious (2 rashers of bacon, 2 fried eggs, mushrooms and toast), there was also cereal and fruit if you wanted this too. The location is near to Paddington and Lancaster Gate tube station, there are also a few pubs and restaurants within a few minutes walk. We would recommend for a short stay, but not a lengthy holiday.

title: Good Location, Poor Management
text: We booked this hotel for an overnight stay as we had a morning flight to catch and the hotel is conveniently located close the the Paddington Station. While booking I requested for a late night check in and a ground floor room as we were at the hotel for only 5 hours. I also called on the day to reconfirmed the details. However, when we arrived late night after a full day of travel, we were given a room on the 3rd floor and since there aren't any elevators we had to lug our 3 heavy suitcases up. I do understand sometimes they aren't able to fulfil the room requirements but the reason for giving us the room on the higher floor was that since we checked in so late, they gave away our room to someone else. After confirming and reconfirming the same, I'm sure why they would give the room away. The wifi is very poor and didn't work at all. The rooms were clean and the, the bathroom is really tiny. The wash basinwas outside the bathroom in the room, I found this arrangement quite inconvenient.

title: Singles beware!
text: After reading other reviews, I was wary of the staff at this hotel, but was pleasantly surprised by their friendliness and service. What I wasn't prepared for was the size of the single room. Don't know what others in the hotel are like, but mine was on the attic floor across the road from the main hotel and was small, no tiny! The single bed fitted snugly - bedhead against one wall and the foot of the bed against the other. The width of the narrow bed was half the width of the room. This room would better be described as a cupboard. I put my suitcase on the floor beside the bed, and that meant that it blocked the opening of the door to the room! No windows either! There was a skylight but as it was raining that couldn't be opened, so if you have a fear of small spaces, stay away from this place!! £70 per night to stay in a cupboard was a bit rich for me!

title: Clean & Tidy, but compact
text: Stayed here for 2 nights during half term. Room was very clean, being a very central location the rooms are compact. Breakfast, Would say it was a basic English breakfast, all fresh and loved the warm croissants and scones the ladies did a very good job and we were looked after very well. Good accommodation in a good location.

title: full breakfast included
text: 'Tis rare to have a full breakfast included in the price of a "budget hotel" in London. Fry up and toast and croissants and cereal and fruit, tea, coffee, juice etc. The only reason this does not have 5 stars is because the toilet and shower room were tiny. All very clean. Nice staff. Very close to Paddington tube. Very close to Hyde Park.

title: Don't stay here!!!
text: After reading some of the previous reviews on expedia prior to booking, I was under the impression that the hotel was of a decent standard. Oh how I was wrong. I arrived and was informed that the room was not available but I could leave my luggage. I arrived back late night and had to ring the bell to get let in. I had an encounter with a rather rude woman who had told me the room had been available from when I had arrived and I could have easily been provided with a key. As for the standard of the room at £65.00, it was deplorable. A matchbox sized bedroom with a broken headboard and not even my own toilet or shower. I found the shower in the communal shower had only two temperatures, freezing cold or scalding hot. This did not represent good value for money. If you are planning on staying in this area, I would suggest the Lancaster Gate hotel where my friends advised me they had a much more pleasant living experience.

title: life savers
text: after booking into the haven hotel in sussex gardens which was like a youth hostel in bangkok .probally put up with it had i been on my own but having my wife and two young children ,seven and three we just couldnt stay three so we walked up the road to try and find an alternative as it was 21.45 we were fearing the worst but we came across the owner of the balmoral hotel and told her our predicerment she then showed us a familly room which was like a palace nice and clean tidy. and for the same price as the haven.the breakfast was realy nice the service was exellent we will definatley be returning

title: Very close to Paddington station
text: I stayed one night for stopover. Really close to Paddington station, and can use Heathrow Express. Also the metro station and Hyde Park is near at some walks. Room was tiny, but I didn't care.(other rooms may be larger) Breakfast is served with good taste. If anyone want to find the hotel for one-night Heathrow stopover, The Balmoral Guesthouse can be in your list.

title: Hoosier in London
text: Stayed here with family for two nights. Great value hotel. Clean and comfortable. Quiet sleeping even in front of hotel. Breakfast was cooked to order and bountiful. Kettle in room. Bathroom very small. Daily service. So civilized! Very short walk to Paddington and the Heathrow Express. Not as convenient for touring London.

title: Excellent location
text: Could not be closer to the earls court underground station. They happily stored luggage for me for a couple of days which was very much appreciated.

title: An affordable family-run hotel in an otherwise expensive city!
text: We are so happy to have found this amazing hotel in London! The location is incredible, the building is beautifully kept and inviting, the rooms are clean and comfortable, the breakfast is plentiful and delicious, but best of all, the staff are some of the kindest and most welcoming people you will ever meet! We fell in love with London years ago and feel fortunate to have found this gem of a hotel that offers top quality at an affordable price. Thank you so much, we will be back!

title: Beautiful boutique hotel
text: Central located hotel less than 2 mins walk from Earl's Court station. Lovely, friendly and very helpful staff, we stayed here twice with a few days break In between to visit Rome. Spacious clean and pleasant rooms and staff on hand to help with bags as their is no elevator but this did not hinder our trip. Close to many great places to eat and a small sainsburys for groceries. Cannot comment on breakfast as we were up and out early most days so did not sample. Pleasant hotel I would stay again

title: Warm and welcoming
text: We only stayed here for an overnight stay as we're seeing a local show. The hotel is a 5 minute walk to the local underground station which was ideal. As soon as we walked into the reception we were warmly greeted and the staff left my Daughter a little birthday gift in our room. The room was clean, comfortable and met all our needs. Will definitely stay here again and recommend to anyone.

title: Good value for money
text: I (1 person) booked a 2 person rooms for 2 nights in this hotel for a little less than 100 pounds. The room was spacious, aproximately 20 m2, clean and comfortable. The hotel is located 100 meters from subway station Earls court (border zone 1 and 2), which is 3 stations away from Victoria station. A continental breakfast and free WIFI internet was also included in the price. If you compare this with other hotels, I think they offer great value for money. Ps: the hotel has no elevator and I think has 4 floors. If you are in good health this should be no problem.

title: Great location, friendly staff
text: Stayed four nights late April. Very happy, would return. Staff very friendly and helpful, excellent location (many restaurants, bars, food shops within a few minutes walk) and only a couple of minutes from Earls Court underground (direct links to Kew Gardens, Piccadilly Circus etc). Yes, quite a few stairs to room, but great value for money in London.

title: Special Ideal home exhibition visit and stay
text: Pleasantly pleased with this hotel, although I did find that it may be a problem for those with mobility problems due to the stairs. Room was compact, dated but comfortable, the ladies providing the morning breakfast were accomodating and always cheerful. We even had a nice balcony that overlooked the road. It was a fantastic base, very near the local tube station with a small supermarket around the corner and restaurants both quick and easy and sit down more or less on your door step.Would definitely use this hotel again. Myself and my partner stayed. Most comfortable.

title: Recomendo
text: my family and I stayed at this hotel twice: room 01 and 02. very comfortable, spacious and clean. Breakfast with several items. Staff very attentive. And the locality is wonderful, close to the subway station, quiet neighborhood with many dining options.

title: Clean, good price and good welcome
text: I booked 1 night at the Rushmore having been let down where i usually stay. I was a bit apprehensive as the deal was very competitive on Booking.com. I arrived about 10pm and was greeted by a very pleasant receptionist who explained the facilities, gave me a wifi code and told me about breakfast. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. I would say The Rushmore is trying to be a boutique hotel and does very well for the price. The shower is a little small - I think it was 90*90 and I am slightly larger than average so it was a tight squeeze but I made it. I would stay again.

title: We love it!
text: The rooms are very clean and nice, the staff is super friendly and helpful. The breakfast was just perfect. Everything was fine. Thank you! We will come back! A szobák gyönyörű tiszták és szépek voltak a személyzet hihetetlenül kedve, segítőkész. Bőséges reggeli volt, minden szupi volt, ajánlom! :)

title: Perfect place for short stay. Great location and tidy room!
text: Stayed here for one night after arriving in London and heading out of the city the next day. Nice tidy room, only small but two people would still be comfortable. Cheap, clean and quiet but central location. Only 2 minute walk from Earls Court tube station on direct line from Heathrow.

title: Tiny bed, claustrophobic shower and ants everywhere!
text: The good: The hotel is located near Earl's Court tube and bus stations and all the restaurants around Earl's Court. The room is relatively clean, and there's a little balcony outside the room which is really nice. The bad: The tiny "double bed" (120 cm!) is very uncomfortable. The rooms are poorly sound proofed, so you hear everything your neighboors are doing, and if anyone gets up early, there's no need to try sleeping in, what with the sounds and killer (not in the good way!) bed. The shower is the smallest I've seen (and after years of trips to London I've seen some small bathrooms before)! Now I'm not the skinniest person out there (size 16), but someone bigger than me would seriously not fit in this shower. Had I been pregnant, I certainly would have had serious problems cleaning myself in there. In addition to this, a colony of tiny black ants lived in the room with us. We tried to speak to the staff about the ants, and they said someone would spray the room. Not sure if they ever tried to do something about the problem, as the ants marched happily around everywhere in the room the whole time we were at the hotel. With all the other hotels in this area, I would not bother visiting Hotel Rushmore again, and I'm certainly not recommending it to others.

title: Excellent place
text: The hotel is beautiful and the staff is very kind and friendly. The room was for 4 people and was quite big (expecially for being in London). The bathroom was new and they changed the towel every day. Continental breakfast included, free wi-fi, 24h reception and luggage keeping even for a long time (all the day long) without any additional cost. It's close to Earl's Court tube station, where Piccadilly and District line stop.

title: Management should have better policies
text: I made a reservation for two weeks on a Thursday night comencing the following Monday. I had to cancel and called the next day - Friday. The manager never told me there would be a cancellation charge. And she charged me for 2 nights. She could have filled the room over the weekend. What a bummer. Bad business.

title: Very helpful and efficient staff
text: Right from day one we felt very comfortabe. Martina helped us with an early check in. We stayed for three nights. Wish we could stay longer. Carmen and the Polish lady at breakfast were very efficient. Preeti and Manmeet answered our emails promptly. Check out was carried out by Preeti who also arranged a taxi. Room was well lit .we will certainly return and also recommend to our friends. Wish the hotel and staff a bright future. Mrs Ramanathan

title: Lovely spot
text: The hotels location is excellent, very short walk to the tube station, makes it easy to go out and see the sights of London. The room was cosy but nothing really to complain about especially given the very reasonable price. The shower was lovely and warm. The staff are very friendly and are there 24/7. The hotel is good for people looking to explore London yet having a comfortable stay and a good nights rest.

title: Amazing location & great value
text: I stayed in the hotel for 5 nights. It was super close to Earl's Court tube station and the area around was really nice. There were many shops, bars etc around the hotel. It has 24/7 reception and people were very friendly. I had my room on the second floor. As others have already said, then there is no elevator, so you have to carry your bags. My room was quite small but it was enough for one. Also had a balcony which was nice surprise. Bathroom was super small. If you want to take nice showers etc I suggest taking a room with a bath. The room and furniture looked old but it was mostly clean. Only thing what bothered me was that there was very creaky floorboards. So, when people started to have breakfast early morning I always woke up. I think it's a good value when you have a budget friendly trip where most of the time you would like to move around.

title: Our Home in London
text: Its been 11 years since we started using Rushmore Hotel...with each year we have found the facility more comfortable than the previous...the Management and Staff, both have been very caring and ready receptive...its our "home" in London and we highly recommend the use of this outlet...it has also got the added advantage of a very good location.In its category of Hotels we would give it 5 stars.

title: We loved this place and would stay again
text: The Rusmore, while small, has a lot going for it. Great location amid tons of amenities and only a block from Earls Court tube station. Our room, located on the main floor, was clean, quiet and cute. Breakfast was included in the cost of our stay and always included cereal, toast, fruit, sausage and cheese plus juices, milk and coffee which became a bit monotonos but always appreciated. Our room had a small kettle and the fixings for tea and coffee too. The front desk was staffed 24 hours a day and had a small internet staton available there. The restaurants in the area were very diverse and we especially enjoyed the Masala Spice.

title: great location ..
text: Rushmore Hotel is in an excellent location. this area of london is amazing for places to eat ..close to the tube station close to markets ..drugstores etc etc .. The hotel is very clean and the bathroom is small but has everything you need. The staff were helpful and the front desk has someone there 24 /7 ... it is a walk up and we were there during the heat wave with no ac and the nights were very HOT .the hotel was good value .We found the breakfast was o.k not great next time wouldnt go for it would grab something from one of the markets near by ... the baked goods were very dry and uneatable almost like they were day olds or over baked ... it did have toast,yogurt,cereals and some kind of fruit which was cut into tiny pieces .. the staff in the breakfast room were friendly but were always getting in the way of people trying to get there breakfast ..it was a little strange . would stay again but maybe not during the summer months

title: Excellent hotel and location
text: We stayed here in freezing Spring (single digit temperature) for 5 nights, and it was wonderful! The rooms were up a flight of stairs about 20 over steps, not suitable for those with mobility issues. The shower was very tiny, but brilliant pressure. The staff were always friendly and helpful. The free wifi is fast and much appreciated. Excellent location to the tube and eateries. Breakfast was a little simple but efficient. The room heating was also excellent. I have marked this as a place to stay again for future trips.

title: Tiny but clean room
text: Hotel Rushmore´s situation is just perfect: just a hundred meters from Earl´s Court tube station. That was the main reason we chose it. We (I, my wife and our 18-year old son) got a room for three persons on ground floor. The room was really small. We have stayed in Kensington before, but this room was much smaller than what we had e.g. in "London Lodge Hotel". And there wasn´t storage place enough, just one coat rack, one shelf and one little drawer. That´s not enough for three people! But all the beds were "normal size beds" (the third bed wasn´t some kind of smaller extra bed) as they had promised. The walls were like paper, sometimes we could hear what the receptionist talked... The room had seen better days, but now it really is time to update it! Fortunately the cleaner made her best and the room was so clean it could be! Because there was no double glassed windows, you could hear everything that happened on the street. Fortunately there wasn´t busy trafic! Breakfast was included in the price which isn´t typical in bigger hotels and although it was quite poor, you could manage with it ´til lunch. I would like to give Rushmore Hotel two and half points, because three points is too much and (thank for the cleaner!) two points is too few, but because there´s not that alternative, let´s say that it is three...

title: Great deal -- very accommodating!
text: I stayed at the Rushmore for 3 nights from the 26th of December. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. I was in a single room and there was plenty of space. The bathroom was more than adequate and the location is great. I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a good deal in London!

title: Good value
text: Nice hotel in a traditional old english house. Good locations near Earls Court U, from where you can go to central London and Heathrow. Lots of restaurants nearby. Rooms medium size, but all you need for a night or two. Our bathroom small, but okay. Streetview, but not noisy. Be aware of stairs, narrow and steep. No elevator .Breakfast okay, not anything special.

title: Great value, very comfortable.
text: Good value hotel. Rooms were basic, but clean and very comfortable. Excellent location, and friendly staff. Would nt reccomend to people who have trouble with stairs, as we were on the top floor, and were out of puff by the time we got to our room, however, would reccomend to anyone.

title: Good location
text: I stayed here for 2 nights. It's just around 5 mins walk from Earl court underground train staion. There are many restaurants and convenience stores nearby as well. Breakfast is good. Staffs are helpful and going extra miles to help me. I'm really grateful. :)

title: Good value for money
text: A group of 16 of us stayed at this hotel for 5 nights at the end of April. The rooms were big enough for our needs and the bathrooms were in very good condition. Breakfast was more than sufficient and the nearest tube station was a 1 minute walk away. Staff were very helpful and we will surely stay there again.

title: Great location.
text: We stayed in the Rushmore Hotel the last weekend in February. The hotel is in a great central location with Earls Court station just around the corner, plenty of shops and restaurants nearby. Our room was in the basement so it was nice and quiet. Room was clean as was the rest of the hotel. Beds were comfy. Breakfasts weren’t great, but good enough to fill you up till you had a hot meal else where. Staff were friendly and helpful. Though the hotel only has one key per room, which isn’t handy. Not sure if this is a standard thing to expect in London. Would visit again though.

title: Good location but bad breakfast
text: Our room was at the top (the attic) and we had to walk about 10 flights of narrow stairs with our heavy luggage. Every morning we had to wait for a free table for breakfast and our family would be split up and eating on a table with strangers. Food was ... no comment. The hotel was near the train station which was great.

title: Close to Earl's Court tube station and good value for money
text: I stayed here on Friday and Saturday 15 and 16 December 2017. I had flown over from Belfast to see The Sweet play in Nell's Jazz and Blues club and this hotel appeared to suit what I was looking for in terms of quite close proximity to the venue. Upon arrival I was greeted by a very warm and friendly receptionist who knew my name straight away! She helped me find the best route to get to my rock gig venue, showed me my room and I was off to the gig asap. This is the way all receptionists should be all the time. My room was warm and clean with fresh linen.The toilet and shower room were ideal. Plenty of clean towels too. The double bed was very comfortable and I had a great night's sleep over the two nights. The breakfast was a good choice of cereal/cheese/yogurt/toast and coffee /tea in a conservatory style area that was well laid out and welcoming. On leaving Rushmore, the same receptionist wished me a happy Christmas, all the best, and a safe journey home. I had a super time in London and this hotel simply added to my stay. To summarise, a great hotel and a warm, mannerly and genuinely inviting receptionist means a lot. Thanks for a lovely stay. Maybe see you again next time I'm in London! Regards, Robin.

title: Great location and comfortable stay
text: I stayed in Rushmore hotel for 2 nights as a solo traveller in the double room (wanted a double bed, but got a twin bed, but this was not an issue for me). I arrived close to midnight and was greeted by a very friendly receptionist who made my check in process very quick and easy. The room was very nicely decorated and the toilet looked like it had just been renovated so it was very clean and nice to use. They served a continental breakfast with a wide selection of bread, cheeses, cold cuts and yoghurt. So I didn't have to worry about getting breakfast in the morning. However, if you have bad knees and heavy luggage, the stairs might be a bit of a problem as they are steep and old. Location is great as it is 2 minutes from Earl's court station and 15 minute walk to High Street Kensington which then takes you to Kensington gardens. There is however, a club two doors down from Rushmore hotel which gets quite loud. So if you're travelling with young children I would not recommend Rushmore hotel. Overall it was a comfortable stay and I would go again.

title: Very low standard
text: TripAdvisor team, please indicate that the hotel has no elevator. I found about it when I arrived. I was promised that the next morning I will be transfer to a room in the ground floor, as I had difficulties in climbing these steep stairs. Apparently, it was a lie, as rooms in the ground floor were occupied for the whole duration of my stay. The room itself was tiny, matress was stiff. Front desk lady on my check out was rude. keep away from from this establishment.

title: Convenient location
text: This hotel is conveniently located a few metres away from Earl's Court Tube station but in a quiet street. Room was tidy and clean but for 3 people (2 adults and a teen), a bit small and shower even smaller! Continental breakfast was fine and staff was nice and helpful. We would stay here again!

title: Great clean value hotel in central London
text: It's hard as a regular visitor to London on business to find somewhere close to the centre at a reasonable price. This hotel is great. For just an overnight business stay it's clean, the staff are friendly and breakfast while DIY was just enough for my ever increasing waistline!

title: Ticked all the boxes
text: I stayed here on a hen weekend with 3 friends. Lovely spacious clean room and friendly reception staff who couldn't do enough for us. Very well located just a minutes walk from Earl's Court tube station. Fairly priced for a London hotel.If I had to pick one fault, the pillows could do with changing as they weren't the usual plump ones most hotels have. But I would definitely return and recommend.

title: A gem of a hotel with friendly staff and a convenient location
text: A special thanks to the staff at Rushmore for making our week's stay perfect! You were all so very friendly even taking our luggage up the stairs. You were very helpful with information about what underground line or bus to take to get to our daily destination. Both the tube and buses are a few minutes walk from the hotel. The beds were comfortable, the bathroom was very modern with lots of hot water for showering. Breakfast always included cheese,meat, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, yogurt, cereals and breads. We looked forward to returning to our home away from home in this safe neighborhood after a long day of sightseeing. We enjoyed our room with a street view but they do have rooms facing the back for those who maybe sensitive to normal street noise. We had great meals at Bistro Benito, a family owned Italian diner and the Earl Court Pub

title: Okay but not that memorable
text: The reception area was quite welcoming and the staff were efficient though, I thought, a little frosty. Away from reception and they room I had clearly needed some refurbishment. However, it was of a decent size but the decor and furnishing were dated. The bathroom has obviously been upgraded at some point and, although a bit cramped, it was okay and the shower was decent enough. I stayed here for only one night and I thought it was a little overpriced and certainly didn't have a comfortable or welcoming feel to the place. Three star is probably a little generous. I think 2.5 stars is more appropriate.

title: Convenient location, reasonable price, clean and friendly.
text: A great little hotel for the price, we had 2 rooms for 9 nights, both were quiet, clean and a reasonable size. Shower in one of the rooms was very small, the other was a good size and had a bath. Continental breakfast was in a charming room downstairs with a glass ceiling. Owner has 2 Brothers with their own hotels, The Amsterdam is 2 doors away and a little more upscale and The Henley House is also very close by and also a bit more luxurious. Both are more expensive. All are only minutes from Earls Court tube. The Rushmore is fantastic for the price. We would stay here again without question.

title: Really small bathroom
text: I had read the reviews so I knew I would have a small room, but the size of the bathroom was still a surprise to me. It was placed in a former closet and could only be described as tiny. I dropped the soap down and had to close the shower and open the doors before I could pick it up. The room was dark as the ceiling was covered with draperies and there was a dusty smell in the room. The location is however excellent with the Earls Court station only few steps away (direct connection to Heathrow airport as well as Piccadilly Circus).

title: Quaint and Imperfectly Perfect
text: My husband & I stayed here the final 3 nights of our 3 week holiday around England. We were late for check in by over an hour after driving from the British Grand Prix, and the lovely staff never mentioned it. Our room was on the 3rd floor, and there is no lift, which was no problem for us as we only had backpacks and are only 35. The staff at the front desk was always very friendly, no matter what time it was, we were always greeted with genuine smiles and pleasant hellos. In a very beautiful part of London, and seemed like a posh area. I recommend staying here!

title: Great Value For Money
text: For the price, I was expecting a "pension" style accommodation and was really astounded by the high level of cleanliness and comfort given. The staff were very friendly and helpful. With buffet style breakfast included which is constantly being topped up at the selection bar. This suggested to me that it was fresh and yes, it was. The dinning area was bright and spotlessly clean. I didn't see any cooked breakfast but there again I prefer continental style. The shower and toilet facilities in the room were very clean and well decorated (Tiled ceiling to floor) albeit a little on the small side in the room I occupied. The double room I had wasn't spacious but it wasn't small either and I didn't feel claustrophobic. In all, this hotel is extremely good value for money for it's location and they haven't cut corners. I'd definitely stay again.

title: Great service in a great location
text: Thank you and well done Rushmore Hotel on your staff, all of the people I met there were so helpful and friendly. On arrival much earlier than check-in time, the young lady on reception was very welcoming and made it easy and comfortable to leave my luggage, when I returned later in the afternoon the hotel staff had lugged my heavy bag up to my room for me - three flights of stairs so I was very grateful for this. I was supposed to leave London the next morning but unfortunately got sick (nothing whatsoever to do with the hotel), I’d already moved out of my room but couldn’t get any further. The new young lady on reception (sorry I didn't get your name) was lovely, she moved me to a sofa in the breakfast room to rest and see if I could recover enough to continue with my plans for the day and in the background reserved a room for me for the night in case I needed it - which I did, once again my luggage was managed for me by the hotel staff. I really appreciate the concern showed by Rushmore staff, I was feeling pretty awful and they were just lovely, thank you. Both rooms I had were lovely, very clean and comfortable, both quite large so not sure if they were really single rooms. The hotel location is great, just off the Earls Court Road, lots of pubs, restaurants etc and the underground, easy walk to High Street Kensington, South Kensington and Knightsbridge. The price for the area was very reasonable. I would definitely stay here again, highly recommended.

title: Great Location in Earls Gate
text: We just spent one night in the Rushmore, it has a great location right off of the Earl's Gate tube, not far at all to haul luggage until you get to the hotel and a room 3 levels up and no lift, a bit of a struggle if you have large bags. The room itself was clean and linens were nice but the entire hotel looks like it could use a spruce up, still we found it to be fine. We did enjoy the included breakfast in the morning, nice spread of options and all was very fresh. There was good wifi in the room as well. Really I'd rate it a 3.5. Staff was very friendly.

title: Clean basic hotel, 2 minutes from underground
text: The Rushmore is an excellent location, literally 2 minutes walk from London underground. My room was 22, a double on the second floor (unfortunately no lift) so had to climb stairs, not a problem personally but could be a problem for someone elderly or disabled. The room although not the biggest was cleaned daily to a high standard and included tea making facilities, a comfortable double bed and a bath/shower in the bathroom. The continental breakfast was downstairs and was prepared by two friendly hotel staff. "hey Mr... do you have your room number! :)" With the positives the only problem I experienced was the mid July heat in my room made sleep difficult, the hotel to their credit provided a fan inclusive with the room. Overall, the staff are friendly, helpful and a credit to the hotel!

title: Great location, cheap, good continental breakfast
text: The hotel is located on the first road on the left to Earls Court station, so it takes about 2 minutes. The staff on reception were pleasant. I had a room with 3 beds which worked out at around £85 for 3 nights. The breakfast is in a conservatory in the basement, there's a good choice of bread, hot drinks (fresh coffee!), juice, cereal, cheese, yoghurt and fresh fruit. The only down points is that some of the furnishings are worn. The rooms in the basement are very noisy too, no lift. One of the better budget hotels in this area.

title: Would come again
text: Stayed at Rushmore during Wimbledon week. Fist impressions were good as the hotel is just around the corner from the Earls Court tube station and so excellent for all London travel. We were greeted by very friendly girls on reception and allocated a room on the third floor. There is no lift at the hotel so those with problems should ensure they book lower level rooms as the stairs are exhausting. The room itself was compact and in need of a little decoration but was very quiet and comfortable. There was plenty of wardrobe storage and drawers with desk and chair, hairdryer and large good TV. The bathroom looked fairly new and was a pleasure to use. A fan was supplied and this was very useful as the hotel did not have air conditioning. Breakfast was a buffet style, a little limited in selection but all very nicely presented in a light airy conservatory in the basement which is reached by a series corridors . Adjacent to this room is a pleasant lounge/reading room. Also in the basement is a left luggage room that can be used free of charge. However be careful what you leave in this room as the entrance door is not locked. Also when I deposited my cases the external fire door was propped open by a mat so anyone from the street could enter and help themselves to the contents. This hotel is all about location and as well as nearby transport there are dozens of shops and restaurants with a few steps so couldn't be more central for a London visit. I would use this hotel again without question and thank you to the lovely staff who couldn't be more friendly or obliging.

title: Disappointed
text: Having seen the pictures of the bedrooms on offer I was extremely disappointed with ours, tiny, very old and dated with the smallest shower I've ever seen. The hallways and stairs were also old and neglected. On the plus side it was clean and the staff were pleasant

title: Very convenient
text: Just came back from a weekend spent at the Rushmore Hotel in Earls court road. The hotel is right next to the tube station which is extremely convenient! We were on the very top floor in a quadruple room which was nice and modern- there are lots of steps though so if you have difficulty getting upstairs- this is the wrong room for you. The staff at the reception were lovely- especially teresa! Breakfast was nice although you want to get down early as they do run out of the 'nice crunchy bread'. There are lots of choice of cereals along with yogurt, eggs, ham, cheese, crackers and fruit. Good value stay for a nice clean hotel!

title: Provides the basics at a good price
text: Being American, I will try and point out some of the things that I experienced staying at the Rushmore Hotel that may not be typical of a hotel in the US

title: We've had better experience in third-world hostels in both cleanliness and amenities
text: We stayed in this hotel for 3 nights. After the first night we had to change rooms because the bed we were in was on a slant and so during the night I had to sleep with a pillow underneath me to stop me rolling off the bed! After complaining at reception we were allowed to change rooms. The change was to a smaller room (no change in price to reflect this) with a bathroom that you could barely rotate 360 degrees in. My girlfriend is only 5-6" tall and average build and even she had difficulty fitting into the shower. The simple act of washing your hair resulted in banging your elbows on both sides of the shower stall. The bed linen looked like it was over 10 years old. One of the covers we were given had an unsavoury stain on it. Thankfully it was warm at the time so we could get by without using the offending items. The drapes on our window were similarly dusty, yellowed wallpaper and stains on the walls made you wonder if you were going to be attacked by bedbugs in the middle of the night. In general, we would not recommend this place, and especially not to people with allergies. Breakfast was ok, not a great selection of food and staff were vacuuming the surrounding area well before breakfast was due to end, which seemed inappropriate. The location was excellent, just a short walk from Earls Court tube station, which is then a short journey to most major attractions. This and the comparatively low price (which was obtained by booking over the phone, direct with the hotel), were the only positive factors. To be honest, we've had better experience in third-world hostels in both cleanliness and amenities.

title: Nice, good value
text: We (a german family) stayed at Rushmore Hotel in a nice, spacy 4-bed room in the 5th (!) floor, no lift (!!), which makes this hotel not so good a choice for older or disabled guests. This is yet the only critical remark we have to make. The place is clean, the staff very friendly, and the breakfast buffet is good. The surrounding (Earl´s Court Tube Station) is perfect for sightseeing in London. Very good value!

title: Stay away!!
text: I have staying in that hotel for two nights. The room is very small, old and neglected. The shower is like 1 sq.m. There is renovation beside the hotel next to my window causing a massive !! noise and preventing rest. No one mentioned that when i booked (they should have as i could consider the "adventure"). The tv did not work, and when i apply the receptionist about, their nothing she can do. The breakfast was very poor, very unpleasant and thick dining room. no service sing so the cleaner just "jumped" into my room. I have complained about all in front of two separat receptionist and demand for compensation, but they did nothing due to the weekend manager off, they even did not call him !!!. If you care about your money, stay away !!!

title: Fabulous.
text: I stayed for six nights. Location is brilliant, staff are just gorgeous and so helpful. Room was perfectly adequate for one person. Would highly recommend and will definitely use again. Thank you so much!

title: Great for getting around
text: We stayed there to do some sightseeing in London and it was great for that. The rooms were clean but pretty small and the breakfast was average. The staff were really nice but on our last night there was a leak in the room above us we couldn't be moved as they were full. We weren't offered a discount for the inconvenience.

title: Poor service, poor staff interest, poor facilities
text: Can't recommend this hotel to other travellers , unfortunate but true. The facilities were extremeley basic, the shower ridiculously small, the staff apathetic. We left this hotel after 1 night even though 3 were paid for , our concern was of a saftey nature(someone entering our room ) the staff were not interested and offered an inaudible "sorry" for our experience and a shrug of the shoulders. No refund was offered, no conversation to try and keep us as guests.Also no lift in this hotel so not easy for people with limited mobility or heavy cases. Very noisy guests, smelled of cigarette smoke so strong , we put a towel near the door to stop it coming in. Breakfast reasonable. I could go on, but there are plenty of hotels in this area,, go to another one.

title: Good basic accommodation without a great deal to complain about
text: The Rushmore Hotel is well-situated in a quiet street around the corner from the Earls Court underground station. The hotel is a white terraced building, which looked suitably inviting in its night lights on a cold January evening. I was welcomed by a receptionist who deserves top marks for warmth and chat, something rarely experienced in London hotels. As I mounted the stairs to my room on the second floor, I wasn't sure whether the staircase and corridors were in need of re-decoration or the hotel had simply gone for the distressed look (I suspect the latter). On entering the room, the lock on the door didn't strike me as particularly secure (although the reception desk is manned 24 hours per day, which was reassuring). Although a lone traveller, I had paid an additional £5 over the price of a standard single room to benefit from the extra space and luxury of an 'executive twin' room. The room size was reasonably generous for a twin, with high ceilings and two tall windows looking out towards the rear of the building. There was, in fact, minimal traffic noise, which was excellent for central London. The room was furnished with an assortment of non-matching pieces of fairly basic quality, and the overall effect did not conjure up the word 'executive' in my mind. For example, there was only one bedside cabinet and lamp for the two beds. In terms of facilities, the room had an ancient 21-inch TV which could receive only the five basic analogue channels with a grainy picture. A tea/coffee tray was provided (but with no biscuits). The ensuite bathroom faired better - in fact, I was quite impressed. It was a relatively spacious bathroom with a full-size bath/shower, and was tastefully tiled on the walls and floor. However, there was some evidence of mould on the ceiling above the bath. The 'executive' label is probably justified for this room. Breakfast was included which was served in a conservatory on the lower-ground floor. This was a bright, nicely presented room. The breakfast staff were not much in evidence and the meal was completely self-service. Only Continental breakfast was on offer and the choice was pretty much restricted to a selection of cereals, breads, crackers and cheese (I didn't see any yogurts, croissants or pastries). The breakfast was just about adequate for this type of hotel. For a price of £64 for bed and breakfast, I'd say that I got pretty good value-for-money for central London. The hotel provides a pleasant base for a short stay in London but I think they should drop the word 'executive' from the room description.

title: Misleading Website - very disappointed
text: We have just returned from a 3 night stay at the Rushmore Hotel. We had checked trip advisor before booking and despite the general consensus that the rooms were small the impression we got was that the hotel was very clean and most people enjoyed their stay. The hotel's website, depticted beautifully decorated rooms and stated that it was suitable for families. However, it omits to state that there is no lift and that the family room (aka the hotel attic) is on the top (4th) floor with 5 flights of steep stairs to climb to get there (and a further flight of stairs to get to and from the Breakfast Room). At 5 months pregnant, this was a bit of an issue, particularly with children and luggage to haul up. The room itself was very basic and very stale and tired looking with the previous guest's dirty sock still in one of the drawers. The bathroom was tiny although very clean but the roof sloped so much that we couldn't actually stand straight up in the shower. There were two attic windows with no view of London and the bedclothes were torn and stained. The carpet was also very stained and dirty and the floorboards horrendously creaky. The hotel lobby was dirty and the whole place looked shabby and in need of a lick of paint. Whilst the staff were very friendly and helpful, overall we were very disappointed in the hotel and felt the website was very misleading. We certainly would not stay there again nor recommend it to anyone.

title: Great location, wonderful people, good breakfast
text: Really great value for your money. Personal is super nice. Breakfast was better than I expected, good variety. Location is amazing. No lift was inconvenient when bringing bags to the top floors... Overall very good experience. Would stay again and recommend others :)

title: Great location and value for money
text: Stayed in family room for family tourist trip to London Staff very welcoming with welcome drink on arrival , arrived too early for check in but kept our bags while we went to National history museum a short walk away Room clean and adequate size for 2 adults and 2 teenagers only small downside is bathroom tiny Had a balcony to sit out and watch the world go by , considering near main road very quite , fan in room for hotter weather Late night and theatre trip so typical too lazy to make breakfast for 9.30 but continental on offer in conservatory . Such a great location , nando's , KFC , Costa and McDonald's at end of road Would highly recommend and will return

title: Nice, good value, but some problems
text: Nicely decorated, very affordable hotel in a great location. The rooms are comfortable and stylish. The bathroom had a weird smell but seemed clean. However, they want you to leave your room key with the reception desk when you leave. Then, once you return, they give the key back to you without checking identification. Made me nervous. There were several other minor annoyances--none of which would have bothered me by themselves, but added together I did get a bit frustrated. So, a mixed bag.

title: Great value for money!
text: Stayed one night here in March 2016, before my flight home. This hotel is a great deal! It's hard to find a decent place for this price in London (about $70/night). The room was small, but clean, well-stocked, and with private bath. Free continental breakfast. Amazing location in the heart of London, and one block from Earl's court tube station. I would definitely stay again!

title: Very accomodating staff, rooms quiet and clean, not too shabby.
text: I booked this hotel because it looked fairly decent for the price and the room came with a balcony, according to the booking site. We got there about 20 minutes before check in and they still let us check in early, which in hindsight was a good choice. At first they put us in the attic quadruple room. It was decently presented but it didn't have the balcony I had booked and the shower head was a bit low. The staff in reception didn't seem at all annoyed when I asked if it was the right room as I was expecting a double with a balcony. Luckily there was an available quad room with balcony overlooking the front of the hotel and because we were there early, let us swap to this room. I suspect the booking site was incorrect as they only have 2 rooms with a balcony anyway. Of the two double beds in our room, one of them was reasonably comfortable, the shower was tall enough but quite narrow (ok for us though) and the balcony made it nice and bright, and I got to people watch in the morning, although it could have benefited from a bistro-style table to match the 4 chairs. The breakfast was a reasonable continental breakfast and again, the staff were friendly and helpful. The hotel was quite quiet, I only heard an occasional squeaky floorboard and other guests once, which is a lot quieter than some newer hotels that I've stayed at.

title: Loved the neighborhood
text: Our family (two adults and two teens) spent 3 nights here at the beginning of our European vacation. It was very easy to get to from the tube station and is in a great neighborhood. The streets around the hotel are charming and there is a main street very close that has everything you might need. We were on the 4th floor with no elevator and knew that going in so it wasn't a problem. The room was good size for the four of us. Breakfast was in a nice room in the basement and the staff was very friendly. Leaving the key (as others have mentioned) is a little unusual but we didn't have any problems. Our only drawback was that it wasn't air conditioned and usually in London that wouldn't be a big problem but we were there for the hotest day of the year so it was a bit uncomfortable. They had one fan and we ended up buying another one and we did just fine. For the price and location, this was a good place to stay.
