title: Great Location
text: While this hotel is not 5 star and a bit dated, it is clean, staff very friendly, helpful and room cleaned everyday with fresh towels. The room was very hot (there was a heatwave at the time) but a fan was provided. We also had a fridge in the room which was great. The heat made it difficult to sleep. Room was a good size for 5 of us. The bathroom was very small but was perfectly adequate. We did not spend much time in the room so it was fine for what we needed. The location is brilliant, a few minutes walk to Hyde Park and Oxford Street. Well serviced by buses so everywhere is within easy reach. Would stay here again if visiting London.

title: Smallest room I've ever seen
text: Excellent location and clean enough but rooms extremely small and size of beds in a doubleroom way too small for two adults!!!

title: nice place concerning the price
text: Old and small hotel with very good location and friendly staff. We were seven persons who stayed three nights in three rooms. Two of the rooms were a bit noisy and wifi worked properly only in one room.

title: It's alright
text: I stayed for two nights in November, room was clean,bed comfortable.Quite noisy with guests walking past my door plus the entrance buzzer for reception to open main door going off all the time.Handy for central London, the tube and Heathrow. Some of the staff quite abrupt,but why should they care,as it is very busy thankyou. I didn't like paying for the room up front but I suppose they had had trouble in the past. I quite liked it.

title: Great place to stay
text: Just spent four nights at the Marble Arch Inn, great little place to stay. Very central with easy access to most places on foot or tube. Friendly staff, clean and children friendly. .....Certainly will be back!

title: Great place
text: We stayed here for 4 nights with our 3 children this week. Family room was spacious, clean and pleasant. Hyde park extremely close and a couple minutes walk to the tube. The hotel was lovely and staff were very friendly and helpful. Central and nice area. Will be back!

title: Super
text: Hôtel very well located (near Marble Arch-Oxford street... shopping area). Staff very friendly and helpful. I will certainly go back again.

title: Basiic But Central
text: This hotel is very basic. There are no dining facilities. Breakfast comes in a large bowl with boxes of cereal, coissants, yogurt , milk and orange juice. The rooms are small and a little cramped BUT the hotel is cheap and cheerful and also very very central. If you want to be five minutes walk from Marble Arch/Oxford Street/Park Lane , this is the hotel for you. It was also incredibly quiet. Granted our room was at the back of the hotel but there was no traffic noise whatsoever and we slept with the window open all night. I found all the staff to be very friendly and welcoming . You definitely get what you pay for but since most people use hotels in London as somewhere to lay their weary heads at the end of a hectic days sightseeing , this hotel fits that bill nicely. I would reccommend it to anyone travelling on a budget.

title: Good Hotel
text: We were a group of 5 friends and stayed in the hotel for 5 nights. The hotel was ok it was always clean and the location was perfect 2 minutes walk from oxford street (main shopping area) and 2 minutes walk for the underground. The only two drawbacks were that we had to upgrade the room from a 5 person room to 6 person so we could have some space cause the first was extra small. And the wifi is horrible. all else was up to standard for the price we have paid. If I will visit London again for shopping I will consider to use this hotel.

title: Bad experience
text: Hotel at first seemed like an ok low cost budgett hotel although very small rooms (3 stars). But going to bed i found my bedsheet had some very creepy stains on it and the fire alarm went of 3 times during the night and a dog was barking outside. So my basic need of sleep was not satisfied at all. Very disappointed. Plus for nice reception person and renovated room.

title: A dreadful place
text: The location of the hotel is great, but that is about the only good thing about it. Me and my friend stayed there for four nights and I would not set a foot in there ever again even if someone paid me. Not only was the room the size of a shoebox, but it was at the bottom floor, so the view from the window opened to some kind of concrete pit that was several meter below ground. The only way to check the weather for example, was to stick your head out the window and see if the sun shone somewhere high up or not. The breakfast basket was an ok idea, but the croissants and pans au chocolat they offered were stale every day so it wasn't exactly enjoyable. The walls around the little sink had started to mold so the whole room smelled very bad. The toilet and the bathroom were two floors up, and one could barely squeeze into the shower and turn around in there because it was so small. The worst thing though, was that after coming home my skin started itching and after a trip to the doctor found out I got scabies from this establishment. My friend also found fleas in her clothes. So no, I wouldn't really recommend this place for anybody.

title: careful !
text: I made a reservations, then cancelled it after reading the comments regarding this place on this website (a very useful website, I might add). Though they were canceled before the 'penalty period' this "hotel" still charged the credit card - and am still trying to get them to credit this unauthorized charge. Beware! - the reviews here appear to be accurate.

title: OK
text: Perhaps you could install new toilets and reduce the noice from the water flow. There is a lot of noice from the toilet now. The handles to the windows could be more solid.

title: Good location and service
text: The location is perfect close to hop on hop off bus, buses terminus, metro. Restaurants and Oxford street for shopping Stuf is very nice and accomddating Room is clean all time and like all Eurpeen hotel rooms are smalers than Nord Amsrican's I recommend this hotel . I spend a nice week this march

title: Nice stay
text: A small bed and breakfast in central London, very close to Marble Arch underground station, and closer to a Tesco and Sainsbury's. The location was the greatest thing about this hotel. Then it was super clean and the staff was very helpful with all queries. The only slight negative thing was that space was very limited, but we were expecting that from previous reviews. We had a room for 5 with an ensuite in the basement and it was very good for 5 nights. So, if you are looking for a central hotel in London and you're on a budget, I would definitely suggest this hotel.

title: Accommodations just okay, but staff.....way wonderful!
text: Everything is small and modest about this hotel...except the staff and locations! Pick what is important to you, then decide if this small but caring hotel is right for your! The location is great, there is a wonderful cafe across the street, and the staff go out of their way to help make your Britian experience nice!

title: Cheap and cheerful!!!
text: This place is hardly going to be the Four Seasons!. It is only a 2 star hotel and for that it is excellent. The location is unbelievable, everything including oxford strret, hyde park, marbe arch, tubes and buses are at it's doorstep and with the low price, i was able to afford to get my shopping done! I stayed for two nights. The room's are small, but there is tea and coffee making facilities and the breakfast basket isn't too bad either! Also, the lady at the 24 hours reception has a very high pitched voice and it is very entertaining!

title: Good location, hotel ok
text: I stayed here last September and will come back again. If you want to stay in London in a good location with out the expensive price then this hotel is right for you. I found the rooms clean and the staff willing to help me out. The only thing wrong with this hotel is the breakfast. Its a bit disappointing!

title: FLEAS
text: This place is disgusting. Me and my partner both woke up with flea bites. title: It´s close to the main streets!

The interiour was not uptodate but the rate of the room was low so it´s was nice. The only thing that i can complian about is that you didn´t serve breakfast but it´s so so close to coffe shop and restuarants so it was ok. I enjoyed my stay in the Marble Arch In.

title: Amazing
text: Very confortable and realy near to services. Friendly, clean and right for couple or family. Reception open 24 hours. Good WC, good Quartet. Staff very friendly and helpful. very convenient and strategic location.

title: London short stay
text: Very convenient many restaurants nearby. Near tube station. Near Hyde park. I even get to go to the Christmas Wonderland. Shopping are within walking distance. Primak.. Selfridge etc. Glad that I choose this hotel. Makes my stay very convenient. Staffs are very friendly and helpful. Safe area. Very quiet too. I really had a restful night sleep while I'm there. Recommended to all

title: Hotel with rooms smaller than 8m2
text: Probably the smallest room in the world for 85£/night !!! without breakfast. True, we are in Marble Arch area, but not in the chique part of it though. True, it is 5 min walk from the famous Primark megastore, but that is the only positive note, together with a friendly reception. For the remainder, if you like to sleep in a 8m2 double bedroom WITHOUT toilet nor shower (and like to go upstairs therefore), then this is your pick. For us, never again.

title: Clean and comfordeble
text: I spend 2 nights at end of March in marble Arch Inn, Clean and comfordeble room,the hotel is perfectly located and everything at a walking distance, room is bit small but nicely painted with new carpet, the best thing about the breakfast is no time restriction as you would collect it in the evening and can have it whenever you want. i got discounted rate as i reserved through their own website,

title: Good value of money minus the hot rooms
text: We stayed 4 nights in Marble Arch Inn. Location is very good, near Oxford street and all shops. Marble Arch tube station is only 5minute walk away so it is easy to move around in London. There is also cafes near by where you can grab something to eat. Tesco is also near. The rooms are quite small. We stayed in a 3 people room and with all our luggage there were almost no floor space at all. Anyway we know what we were getting because the price was low compared to other hotels. Rooms are clened everyday and you get new towels too, it was nice. You have to leave your room's key to the reception every time you leave the hotel, that was little bit strange. Also notice that the rooms are super hot. There is no air conditioning. During our stay weather was sunny and it was +25 degrees outside. The room was so hot it was almost impossible to sleep in there. The lack of airconditioning was the worst thing, everything else didn't bother us that much. Still it was great value for money since London is quite expensive and the location of the hotel is very good. Staff was always friendly and helpfull.

title: A disappointment.
text: I chose this inn for it's location. When approaching the inn, bags of rubbish in black plastic bag was lining the pathment, rubbish collection day, anyway a bad omen. The front of the inn was pretty which was good to see. It was early evening and dark in October, the front door was locked, so I had to ring the bell to gain entre. The inn is 2 adjacent house join together which means narrow staircase, small rooms and shower room more suited to caravan or boat. My room had a wall to wall bed. The pane of glass in the window was too small for the frame, so there was a natural flow of fresh air. The included breakfast was a bun in a plastic bag, portion size cereals and small box of long life milk. I decide to have breakfast at the nearby MacDonald. In short, not worth the money. Better off going to branded budget hotel like Travelodge .. basic, but clean and warm !!!

title: Great Stay, Close to Oxford Street
text: I stayed here when I had to attend an interview in London the next day. It was great value for money (£35 per night-online price), and the breakfast in the basket was an excellent idea as it meant breakfast in bed!! Room was quite small, but I had reserved a single and got a double bed. It was also better than some hotels that I have stayed in. It was clean, had a fridge, hanging space and tea and coffee facilties. I didnt book a room with a toilet and shower in, but it was just on the next floor which wasn't a problem. Clean towels were provided. I had a television and hairdryer in my room as well. The staff were very helpful and cheerful. It is situated round the corner from the beginning of Oxford Street. I would stay here again, and have recommended it to some friends who come to London often. Might not be to everyone's taste as the rooms are small, but by all accounts so are most rooms in London. I could not have asked for better for my money.

title: STAY AWAY
text: DO NOT STAY HERE. title: 2nd visit & remains very good
text: My 2nd stay here & it is still excellent. Very good value for money considering the great Marble Arch location. The hotel is currently undergoing a large refurbishment with all rooms being completely modernised. My room had already been finished & the improvements are very good indeed. Very comfortable bed, lovely new bathroom & very pleasent decor throughout. The completion date for the refurb is March 2017 so expect works to be ongoing until then if you stay here. I had no disruption during my 2 nights here & I continue to recommend the Marble Arch Inn.

title: Amazing value for money.
text: Myself, my son (4) and his dad needed somewhere close to winter wonderland. Being so near Christmas we thought we might struggle but this hotel is perfect. Close to everything you need. We even visited London eye. Close enough to walk or jump on the underground. Very clean and tidy. Clean bedding and towels. Room was small but we only needed to sleep there so perfect for us. :)

title: Great Service from Reception
text: The three of us stayed in Room 1 in the basement from 30 Nov to 3 Dec 2014. We were pretty apprehensive about the size of the room after reading previous reviews on TripAdvisor about how tiny the rooms at the inn are. Although the room was indeed small (esp the bathroom - there was hardly space to even towel ourselves dry) and the decor was dated, we found the room adequate for our needs. The beds were comfy and the room was relatively well heated. Thankfully, there was also a fan to keep the room well ventilated or it could have been very stuffy. Housekeeping was efficient in keeping the room clean and tidy during our stay. While we could hear people moving in and out of the rooms, the noise was tolerable and we slept well on all four nights. The location was excellent as it was near the Marble Arch Underground (less than 10 minutes' walk) and there were supermarkets like Tesco Express & Sainsbury Local just 5 minutes away), major department shops like Primark and M&S in Oxford Street and restaurants (mostly Middle Eastern) nearby. What is perhaps the selling point of the inn are their hotel receptionists who were attentive to our needs. They helped print out tickets and boarding passes for us and also booked a private cab service for us to the Heathrow airport at a reasonable rate (esp when we compared it to how much we would have had to pay for 3 persons aboard the Heathrow Express). We truly appreciated the top-notch service which made our stay at the inn a rather positive experience in general.

title: Marble Arch Inn
text: Staff was very helpful and friendly. Location was very convenient to transportation links and a variety of restaurants. However, room furnishings were basic and rather shop-worn. Since mid-April, the hotel is undergoing renovations that we were not told about when making reservations. That meant a lot of unpleasant noise and construction dust filtering into our room every day. One night, a fire alarm went off and beeped until the next morning when an engineer was able to turn it off. Although billed as a "bed & breakfast," we were informed upon arrival that breakfast was not included at the BudgetPlaces rate. We were offered a pre-packaged box breakfast for 4 pounds.

title: Not recommended
text: My family of four stayed in the hotel for 5 nights in a family room for six. I had booked a family room for five three months ahead, but upon arrival, we was suprised to learnt that the family room we booked was not available, we were given an alternative but it was not suitable for us. We ended up paying more than what we should and not getting the value for money. Even when I pointed out that stains were found on the bed covers, the staff won't do anything. The female receptionist was horrible

title: Only location counts

The rooms are very, very noisy, because it's a very old building and when someone walks on the room above, or even down the hallway, you wake up. The room is TOO SMALL, me and my husband nearly don't fit in. Also, no elevator or anyone to help with your luggage.

title: Don't

title: Excellent Value for Location!
text: The staff were very friendly and helpful, the room was comfortable, and the value was excellent, especially considering the location! I think that people complaining about relatively minor issues at this inn need to take into account just how economical their prices are, considering the incredibly high rates at most nearby locations.

title: absolutely appauling
text: this is without doubt the worst hotel i have ever stayed in , the room was set behind reception , the bed was approximetely 4 foot square , the shower and toilet room absolutely stunk of the drains , there was no hot water for the shower , it was like a step back in time and completely spoilt our weekend , we even had to take turns to get dressed owing to the lack of space .

title: DO NOT STAY HERE!!
text: This place is NOT a bed and breakfast, and is more like a hostel. This place is NOT kid friendly and I would avoid it at all costs!! They wanted to put us in a basement room with no windows. When we said it was unacceptable the night manager agreed that this establishment was not suitable for kids!!

title: Good Hotel, Great Location
text: My friends and I absolutely loved our stay at Marble Arch Inn. The staff were friendly and certainly helpful. The room was, as expected, small, but comfortable and the location is brilliant (couple of minutes away from Oxford Street and Marble Arch underground station). Housekeeping was great

title: Great value
text: Fantastic location being only a couple of minutes walk from Oxford Street in the heart of London. My room was small but it was clean and well decorated. The shower was just outside the bedroom door and the toilet was a couple of doors away. But for central London this was the best value for money place I have stayed. A great idea is the breakfast that is served in the evening in a basket for you to put in your own bedroom fridge overnight and to eat when you want to. It will not be everyone's cup of tea (great English phrase), but it is ideal for keeping costs down and making the hotel affordable. This is not somewhere to stay for a romantic weekend away if you want to stay in the hotel and enjoy the facilities. However, in terms of location and affordability it can not be beaten. I will definitely stay here again.

title: Good value budget hotel
text: Ok i'll say it the rooms are tiny!!! But London is a expensive city and if you are looking for a cheap hotel in a fantastic location this is it. Very close to Marble Arch station and easy to find. The reception staff are mostly very helpful and friendly with one exception. Breakfast was provided the night before and eaten in the room and was quite adequate. There was WiFi internet but it was pretty hit and miss in our room although it worked better at reception. We had a room with a shower and basin but no toilet, which was close by in the hall. The shower is straight off the room, but it was clean and there was plenty of hot water. There was a fridge and a very handy shelf to put stuff on. Overall we liked this hotel, yes the room was the smallest I've ever seen but it was big enough for our 2 night stay and it was cheap and clean. Will stay here again.

title: Hotel fine not as bad as some reviews
text: We stayed for two nights booking a twin and double room, yes these were very small but perfectly adequate for a short stay in a very good location. The staff were very helpful and our rooms were nice and clean, Kids said their room was rather noisy with squeeky boards but the buildings are old. We shall return.

title: Clean room

title: Second stay
text: This was my second stay at Marble Arch Inn, and it won't be the last. Me and my friend arrived a little early for check-in but the staff managed to give us a room right away. We actually got the same room as my last stay and I was happily suprised that they had read my rewiew and had put up shower curtains in the room. An extra credit for listening to the guests. The rooms are very small, but since we weren't spending that much time in the hotel we didn't mind. It's clean, have a good price, helpful staff and excellent location if you want to shop since it's just a few minutes walk to Oxford street and tube stations. I also like that they have TV in the rooms, it's nice to relax in front of it after long days out in London.

title: Nice hotel in a wonderful place
text: Good hotel, location is very convenient. Five minutes to the subway, Oxford Street, Hyde Park and other attractions. The staff is always ready to help with advice, rooms are clean and cleaned every day. Comfortable bed. The only drawback - small and uncomfortable bathroom. I will recommend this hotel to friends.

title: Great for what we needed
text: We stayed 23 may 2012 for one night , hotel less than a 10 min walk from marylebone train station, we were able to leave our bags at reception on arrival , we arrived about 10.30 am, and went to explore london , we arrived back at 5.30pm we had rooom 12 at the top of the hotel and at the back , no street noise just a lot of helicopters flying about ! we had a triple room loads of room for the 2 of us and very clean, clean towels and an on suite shower room , rather small but did the job, had to jiggle about with the taps a bit to make the shower work but did and had a nice shower after one of the hottest days in london this year . Then we went out for the evening . Managed to get a good nights sleep (we took our ear plugs ) and left the fan on all night so room was nice and cool . We were able to leave our bags at reception on checkout (very courteous staff) and collected them on the way back to marylebone station in the evening. For breakfast we walked to the weatherspoons pub at marble arch about 3mins walk away and had a traditional breakfast for 3.99 not bad for central london. When we go back to London we would definatley use the March Arch Inn again no problem .

title: Pleasant stay!
text: Nice B&B for a very cheap stay. Clean rooms and shower/toilets. Nice staff, open 24 hours and the location is perfect. Close to everything. You hafto pay extra for wifi. Stores near by for breakfast. Absolutly ok!

Thats what we want.

title: Clean, great value for price, nice staff

title: An accommodation for tiny people

title: Happy stay at the Marble Arch Inn
text: We are a family of six, 4 kids from 4-13 and 2 adults. We stayed in the "family room", which is a large room (~20' x 20') with two double (queen size) beds and two single beds and a very small bathroom tucked into the corner. It was cozy but clean with towels for everyone. After long days seeing the sites, it was fine for just crashing for the night. The Inn is three blocks from the Marble Arch Underground station and the beginning of the Oxford Street shopping district, so the location is pretty good. There is also a small market across the street that is open late for those late night snacks. The only minus would be the wifi access: the free wifi is slow and won't access secure sites, but OK for checking email. If you want faster internet service or need to access secure sites, you'll need to pay for that. Last, the service was fantastic. The staff were very helpful and cheerful. Overall, the Marble Arch Inn is good value for the money. We'll look into staying there again next time we're in London.

title: A place to sleep
text: A budget hotel with a basic set up and friendly staff. Good location for Oxford street. Could do with a refurb as a bit dated and tatty in places but beds were comfy and linen and towels clean. Room was small and bathroom also a bit too small. I would only recommend for a short stay but it's ok for a place to lay your head at the end of the day

title: Nice budget place
text: Budget hotel but nice. Place could do with a referb but its very clean. I stayed on the top floor. Room had a single and double bed, very small room but so comfy. Very warm, window was already open on arrival and was not needed to be closed. The shower is very small but served its purpose. Staff extremely friendly. Close to Hyde Park, marble arch tube station and Oxford street. Would definitely recommend.

title: Physically the owrst hotel I've experienced (former employeed in travel business)
text: Worn out hotel. No toilet in the room. No shower in the room (1 floor up) Very narrow and little space. All in all the worst hotel I have ever experienced. Service is good - so is the central location. The only reasons this hotel might survive.

title: Good location
text: Good location with walking distance to the center and all museums. Kind staff. Quiet in the nights. Not good breakfast, just a box with prepacked cold things. The shower was no good. Not enough hot water.

title: Faulty, not fun
text: The Marble Arch Inn hotel in London is by far the worst I've seen in Europe - and I've stayed at hundreds of hotels... The room was out of order when we came, so we couldn't check in. When we came back hours later, we were given a smaller room without WC for the first of three nights. This turned out to be extremely crammed, even though the double bed was too small for even one adult person there was almost no floor space. The "breakfast" advertised consists of some cereal and youghurt which we had to carry up to the room before going to bed. The youghurt wasn't chilled so it had turned sour, but the Frost Flakes were actually still edible. The window was impossible to shut completely, so the night turned into a cacaphony with street sounds from one end of the room, and the unmuffled noises from other guests from the door end. There was probably some kind of bugs in the room, both I and my wife had small bite marks in the morning. We were woken up in the morning by the noise of lots of water dripping. It turned out to come from the room above, their shower cabin leaked and the water went through the floor to fall down onto our room's shower cabin. (Yes, it had a shower but no WC...) We then decided to dodge this hotel, check out prematurely and leave. Then the receptionist said that "you can have the bigger room you reserved, as soon as it's cleaned up". Cleaned up - it was supposed to be out of order due to "an accident"? No, apparently the cheeky --- had handed it to some other guests... We declined, paid for one night + another nights fee due to the late cancellation, then we went straight to a decent hotel in a major international chain. That hotel turned out to be only about 15% more expensive, even better located, much better rooms and services. So the conclusion is, try to avoid the smaller, local hotels in London with their poor building style - and whatever you do, don't even think of making a reservation at the Marble Arch Inn! The value for money given at "real" hotels is definetly much better.

title: Marble Arch Inn
text: Smaller than expected room, no room for luggage and 2 adults, too many flights of stairs to take large pieces of luggage, no help at all from Front Desk. This was not good value, not comfortable and definitely one of the worst places we have stayed at. OK for back packers but probably not at these prices. Room did not have a standard of basic appearance or inclusions. Small room was stuffy and claustrophobic, no toilet in room. Very disappointed. Great position however, very close to Regent Street shops.

title: Good Budget Hotel (for London)
text: Great location for our Hyde Park event. Close to tube and Oxford Street. Our double room was small, but did the job well enough. It was quite a warm room, hence a good wall fan fitted. It was clean enough and the bed was reasonably comfortable. There was a TV and a kettle etc. The shared toilet and the seperate shower room were small and basic,but functional. The 24 hour reception was very good. The 3 people we dealt with were friendly and efficient. Breakfast was not included. The hotel suited us, but may not suit everyone. This is a budget hotel, even if it seems a little pricey. This is London after all. We would stay again. Hope this is helpful?

title: Best Location!
text: My sister and I have been staying at the Marble Arch Inn twice now, and we are very satisfied with the place. The location is great, it is pretty much close to all of the major attractions London has to offer - such as Oxford Street, Hyde Park, Soho, Baker Street, Big Ben etc. The staff at the hotel is also very friendly and they are ready to help you whenever you find it necessary. However if you are picky your hotel rooms you might want to look elsewhere. The rooms are very tiny, and the bathroom facilities leaves much to be desired. But all in all the hotel is a great place to stay for a short holiday in London.

title: Overpriced and pretty grim
text: So expensive for what it is! Only thing going for it is the location but even that is a stretch since Marble Arch doesn't really have many good restaurants and bars... Close to Hyde park and tube so easy to commute. Shared bathroom and toilet. Small bed, little floor space and weird vibe. Would not recommend.

title: Good for a budget accomodation
text: The Marble Arch Inn is a cosy little hotel. The location is terrific, about a 5 mins walk from Marble Arch tube station. The refurbishment seems good to me. Of course the rooms are quite small, I've never seen big rooms in London! But it's good value for the price. Yes, the breakfast consists of a basket full of goodies, but I found it far better than breakfast in other hotels. I'd recooment this hotel if you want a budget accomodation, and if you don't expect the Grand Hotel.

title: Never go to this place!
text: Do you call this hotel? if you do, I don't! the only good thing about this hotel is its location which is few minutes away from the Marble Arch (Central Line) tube station. the interior is terrible and overall quality is poor

title: Hostel NOT Hotel
text: We arrived here as a family of 4 for 3 nights. The reception staff are really helpful and friendly. The location is excellent for Oxford Street, Madam Taussads and Marble Arch. Our room was on the basement floor which faced out to the main street, although the windows are double glazed the noise is ridiculous, sleep??? the song insomnia comes to mind

title: Good location, small rooms
text: My stay at the hotel was four nights with my sister. The room was so small - barely space for other than the bed. But it was only five minutes walk to Oxford st. and the staff was helpful.

title: Great location, good for sleeping
text: Marble Arch Inn has a great location - 3 minutes walk from underground, Hyde Park and Oxford Street. Rooms tiny but clean, no elevator, bathrooms really small. Good for sleeping and weekend stay. Pubs and restaurants in neighbourghood.

title: WE in London
text: Very good emplacement to visit London, near all the points of visit. Very pleasant personnal Expensive for a room in the basement with a poor confort for the price

title: Basic, well priced and central
text: Stayed here with my wife while visiting London for 2 days sightseeing. As we only had one night in the city, we were just looking for somewhere to dump our bags and rest our heads after a long day on our feet. The Marble Arch Inn was perfect for this. We spent the whole day we arrived sightseeing, and checked in at 11pm. There was someone at reception 24 hours a day so the late check in wasn't a problem. Our room was rather basic, but we weren't expecting the Ritz for what we had paid. Overall we were more than happy with the hotel, it was reasonably priced, and an ideal base for seeing London. The hotel is a 5 minute walk from the nearest tube station, which can have you in central London within minutes. I would stay here again without hesitation

title: Nice Bugs in my room
text: Pretty nice location for shopping and sightseeing. Pretty small rooms. If you have a room with a shower there really is just a shower and a small basin in your room. Yes in your room! There is a little space in the wall where they build a shower cabin into. Breakfast is a small basket filled with cornflakes, milk, orange or apple juice and some kind of croissant in a plastic package. But around the corner is a Starbucks - so breakfast is not necessary. The worst experience I got was after my return back home. The second day back I got red points everywhere. First I thought I've got a gnat in my flat. But they became more and more.. My doctor tells me that it seems that this are bug bites - so I've got a cheap souvenier from my holiday. The only thing I can say to everyone: don't stay in this hotel!!!

title: IS THERE WORST THAN THAT?
text: I don't know from where to begin. They charge GBP75 per night for double room instead of begging people to stay there. The only possitive thing is the people who work there and the location. The room has 2 beds next to each other and a small place just to stand to put your clothes on. Suitcases must be on the bed if you want to open them. A piece of wood on the wall with 3 hangers is for hanging your clothes. An other piece of wood - on which i heard my head on twice due to luck of space -, just to put your things on (don't get too excited, enouth place just for some makeup things). Bathroom was so tiny that there was no way to fit 2 people together on the same time. We arrived there at night so there was no way to leave immediately. We went to bed and from the noise we slept only for 2 hours and on 6 am we got up. My husband slept next to the window which didn't close well the heating was on and off every one hour, so we got freezing the whole night. This was our first time to London so you can imagine our dissapointment. We booked this hotel becuase we thought it was ok 100 euros per night. But unfortunately i didn't see any reviews before. Now I got my lesson. Any way first thing in the morning we left, found an other hotel just one minute from Oxford Str., paid the double money but at least that was a proper hotel. The full amount I paid for Marble Arch Inn was non refundable so i didn't get any refund. If you are planning visiting London don't even think on choosing this hotel. Is the worst that i have ever seen in my whole life. And i have been to other europe countries. Is better to stay a little bit longer from the center instead of staying here.

title: A good nights sleep
text: Very basic but this is just what we needed. The beds were comfortable and our room was clean. I've seen complaints about how hot the rooms are, but we didn't have that problem. We had two large windows that opened fully and a fan. The only downside was the bathroom was very small and when showering it was hard to keep water from going everywhere. Staff were friendly and helpful. Location is ideal. 3 minutes from Oxford Street and a small walk to Marble Arch tube station. Also accept under 18s. Great for a trip with friends who just want a place to sleep and be close to all the London action.

title: Four night stay - 2 adults and 2 kids
text: The location is fantastic - situated close to Oxford St and Marble Arch. The rooms were very basic, small and fairly clean (aside from some mould), although I was aware of this prior to booking. The bathroom was tiny, which wouldn't be an issue except the entire floor and toilet got soaked when someone had a shower (the shower curtain directs the water out of the shower). There was also nowhere to put luggage, nor hang wet towels, which is an issue in a single room that sleeps five. The room we had was under the 24hr reception and got a lot of noise from reception, front stairs and bell, and the street. I was also disappointed with the 'free wifi'. The signal was virtually non-existent in our room. What was even more frustrating was the response from staff - it is a known and existing issue with the room we stayed in, yet there was nothing they could do (I suggested they could fix it, which would be a good start!). I would have preferred they not advertise they provide this service, that way I wouldn't have wasted so much time trying to get connected to look up information for my holiday. If you are looking for cheap accommodation Ina good location, this place is ok. I personally won't stay there again.

title: Stay away from this place!
text: I recently stayed here for three nights with my husband and daughter. We were extremely unhappy. The room was very tiny for three people and was so hot we had to keep the window opened with an ashtray. There was not enough room for our luggage...to open it or store it. It was difficult to get up and down the stairs with luggage and the halls were so small you couldn't open the door without disturbing a neighbor's breakfast bowl of prepackaged cereal, bun and yogurt. There was no place to put clothes and the linens, rugs and furnishings were very shabby. The bathroom was tiny and annoying difficult to use. For the price we paid we got very little. I discovered too late that there are many nicer places costing the same or less. Would never go here again!!!

title: I night stay at the Marble Arch Inn Great location in Georgian Conversion.
text: Stayed only 1 night, Great Location but rooms very small not ideal for any longer that a couple of nights. Our room was right up the top. The guy on the counter was great helping us getting our rather heavy luggage up the stairs. It was great however to stay in a authentic Georgian converted house not in in the usual boring hotel rooms that all look the same. We where advised however if we where to stay again to ask for a ground floor room, as we are not as young as we use to be.

title: Okay..
text: Room was not too small and very clean, however, TV did now work, shower was too hot all the time, and room was too warm.. Continental breakfast was also not bad, but not lovely. I stayed at this hotel for business and it was one of company recommendation, so I did not pay by myself. But 150GBP per night is too expensive.

title: Nice and easy
text: Arrived to a nice welcome from the staff. The staff were just friendly on my departure. Room, although a bit on the tight side, was clean and had everything as per itinery. Perfect for my one night stay, too allow me to attend my Christmas party. Location was nearly as close as you could get to the wonderful British Museum, which I browsed around (late opening Thurs and Fri till about 8:30pm-ish). I booked this room with a voucher (less than £100) and probably received a service/room worth £180.

title: Good location..but rooms are a sauna in summer
text: This hotel is located next door to the British Museum and has a lovely secluded garden at the rear of the property. Its within easy reach of the tube stations and shopping. As for the hotel, the reception staff were very helpful and the hotel is clean and tidy. It is an older property and consequently air conditioning is not available. It does have an elevator to all floors. The room I was in was well presented. But the lack of air conditioning meant the room was very hot. I had to have the window open and a fan running all night just to try and keep it cool. My room was street facing and its on the main Russell Square bus route so it was noisy. Breakfast was ok, it had the right ingredients but the delivery failed. The cooked breakfast was luke warm. They piped classical music, loudly, in the breakfast room. I certainly didn't feel the urge to stay there very long. Its a good hotel for its location, but average for everything else.

title: Disappointing
text: Initial impressions were good - excellent location with helpful and efficient staff on the front desk. The room , however , was a let down - dark , with a small double bed and cramped bathroom ( although the shower and toiletries were good ). Perhaps I was unlucky , but the lower ground floor facing onto the street was particularly noisy both from passers by and heavy vehicles whose engines running as they waited in the street set things vibrating in the room. Breakfast was included in my rate , but small plates for the buffet ( too small for toast , scrambled egg and a hash brown ) and a single cup of coffee seemed mean with much better value available nearby.

title: Left early
text: Stayed here last weekend. Well, not for the entire weekend. We left early. The stay was ominous from the start. Two hours after we booked online, almost an hour after official check-in time, the room wasn't ready. We were left to wait in the bar, without so much as the offer of a cup of tea. When we did get in, it was a little disappointing. Basement room, dark, little wardrobe space, bathroom not spotless, small, overly soft bed. Still -- we were paying less than rack rate, and the British Museum is right next door. Who cares where you lay your head when you're in London, right? Wrong. En route to the bathroom that evening, I stepped on a squeaky floorboard and, as I did, there was an even louder squeak from the bathroom. Then the sound of scuffling, and even louder squeaking -- squealing, really -- from behind the tiles. However, despite being a little freaked out by this, we simply decided to leave the bathroom light on all night, as a deterrent. But neither of us slept very well. And my husband had a very bad back as a result of the very soft bed. Then the TV went out -- the last straw for my hubby. No one seemed to be able to fix it. We checked out. To be fair, the woman on reception was very nice. Quick to point out no refund would be given, but very pleasant. She offered to get us another room, but by that point we just wanted to get the hell out. She took my husband's email address, and the next day he received a stock email. I suspect that will be the extent of their response.

title: Booked this hotel was fobbed off with another !
text: We booked a room at The Blooms Hotel as we liked the look of the decor and old charm Was very disappointed to be told at check in we were in the sister hotel next door - no apology or explanation - Gutted !!!!! Was a special weekend away so didn't want to spoil it with a confrontation But the Hotel we got wasn't what we wanted, booked. White Hall Modern boutique style room ( very tired and tatty decor) when we wanted traditional. Room was quiet overlooking garden which was good. But so disappointed feel totally ripped off that booked hotel in good faith and didn't get it

title: Not 4 star
text: Stayed at this hotel as part of a theatre break in room 108, located next to a very noisey lift shaft. The room was very small made worse by the dressing table being too big, restricting access to the wardrobe. It was hot evening so with no air conditioning we had to have the window open and was woken up by refuse collectors at 6.30 on Sunday morning. On the positive side the staff were very friendly. I have stayed in much better London hotels for the same tariff. If you do stay I would suggest you give the offer of 2 for 1 afternoon tea in the sister hotel, The Grange Holborn a miss, £24 per person very average.

title: Good service and location, but old-fashioned, small rooms with no A/C
text: Stayed here for one night in July 2011 and while the hotel is ok, there are better in London, so wouldn't rush back to this one. The location is the best thing about it - 20m from Russell Square and a 2 minute stroll to the British Museum. Good service, and very nice continental breakfast in a bright breakfast room looking out onto a pleasant garden, which had picnic tables and would be a great spot for a quiet drink in the sun. In general though, the hotel itself has an old-fashioned feel - it's a comfortable place that does the job, but lacks the level of luxury that you can get in a more modern place for the same price. It could do with a bit of an update in most areas but is probably surviving just fine without given its location. To the room: uneven floorboards creak under aged carpet as you go down the third (top) floor hall. No. 305 was rather pokey and had no air conditioning, which in London in July proved a big problem. The desktop fan they'd left on the table for us helped a bit but was far too noisy to leave on all night. And the bed was the smallest double I'd seen in a hotel in some time. We didn't get much sleep at all. The bathroom was fine though - clean and bright, and the rooftop view was lovely. All in all not bad, but very much let down by the size and lack of A/C in the room. And they charge for the internet which always comes across as plain greedy. (£5/hr

title: Noisy small room near lift and above entrance
text: The hotel was in an ideal location close to the british museum and a short walk away from Oxford street. The hotel was very clean but the room we had was right next to the lift which caused a lot of noise, all we could hear all night was the lift going up and down and with the noise outside we hardly had any sleep for our two nights stay. The room was tiny but clean, i requested an iron and ironing board and once we had these you had to climb over the bed to get to the bathroom. I paid £17 each for a breakfast thinking it would be full English, well it was for continental only, which had stale cheese on display. You had to pay £6 each extra for a full English, which makes it £23 per person - daylight robbery. I would not stay here again.

title: Cosy but tired
text: I liked this hotel, yes it is ‘tired’ and could do with a touch up but I enjoyed my stay. It’s in my favourite part of London, Bloomsbury and very near to British Museum. Our room although a ‘superior’ was small and the furniture was scratched and chipped but it was comfy and cosy. It overlooked Montague Street but was quiet and had lovely large windows. Staff were friendly enough, breakfast buffet style and perfectly adequate. Despite the furniture a bit battered I’d be happy to stay again as I couldn’t help but find it charming.

title: Good location. Crummy hotel and staff
text: The area is great and the price is decent. They put us in a room which is obviously a meeting room, with a Murphy bed! The woman at the desk literally rolled her eyes at us for asking for two teaspoons. The breakfast is ridiculously expensive and of poor quality. Yes the price for the area is good BUT it is too expensive to be this poor. Spend an extra 20$ a night and get yourself something worthwhile.

title: enjoyable 2 night break
text: Just got back from a 2 night break , the hotel is very clean with extremely comfortable rooms ours overlooked a pretty terraced garden, breakfast was really nice with very pleasant staff, in all the hotel is in a very nice area with great accessible tube stations within easy access to explore London very easily , it is also in a walkable distance to Covent garden , theatre land and places of interest ,would definitely stay at this hotel again , brilliant .

title: Definitely not a 4 star hotel
text: I stayed in the hotel very short but I got a pretty good idea of its quality. First the positives: excellent location just behind the British museum, coffee and team amenities in the room and some cookies. The rest of my experience however did not much the 4 star rating of the hotel. Room basic, television did not work (it was all red and blurry when I turned it on), tiling in the bathroom and wood work in the room ready to fall off. Room did not give me the feeling of being clean at any moment and the bedlinen smell gave me serious suspicions of not having being changed. The hotel is old hence you can hear everything outside your door, above your room etc at any point of day or night. I did not try the breakfast, but I wanted to make a last remark about the reception staff, all of which seemed to have come from some Eastern European countries, basic English, really bad make-up and not a smile or any true feeling of being welcomed. If I can avoid in the future I definitely will.

title: Loved it
text: Wonderful.. If you choose ask for ground floor room w/ doors to patio. We had G1, perfect. Rate was 69 (pounds), and location was perfect for British Museum..next door, Bloomsbury and theaters, bus and tube. Most of west end in easy walking distance and i hate walking. Large and lovely room, staff were very helpful. Parking was a bit of a bother, but we were there overnight and left before parking charges were enforced.
subratings_json: {"service": 5.0, "business service (e.g., internet access)": 5.0, "location": 5.0, "check in / front desk": 5.0, "value": 5.0, "rooms": 5.0, "cleanliness": 5.0}

title: Never Again
text: Our room on the lower ground floor was next to the lift shaft and the lift creaked and groaned up and down all night. The bed was 4 foot wide, one side of it was against the wall and it sagged seriously in the middle. It was obviously intended as a single room because there was only one glass and one set of toiletries in the bathroom. The view from the window was a wall and we could hear every passing piece of traffic and every footfall from the street above. This was on our way out to a holiday. On the back we stayed at another hotel with a 6 foot bed, views over London, a peaceful night's sleep and breakfast for £10 less! Such a shame because we have used LastMinute's Secret Hotel deal before and this was our first disappointment. A pity it had to be on such a deplorable scale.

title: More than enough
text: Cozy and warm townhouse hotel behind the British Museum The staff was good enough, the room clean and confy enough and the overal experience was quite good although it was used just for sleeping. I had a room overlooking the back garden and the walls of the British Museum. It's location is really good and convenient for visiting the city's main landmarks.

title: A quiet oasis in Bloomsbury - right next door to the British Museum
text: Booked at a special rate with lastminute.com. Bang next to the British Museum, with a nice quiet garden to the rear. Room very quiet and well-maintained. Staff efficient and well-meaning (mainly Eastern Europeans) Good facilities in room.
subratings_json: {"service": 4.0, "business service (e.g., internet access)": 4.0, "location": 5.0, "check in / front desk": 4.0, "value": 5.0, "rooms": 5.0, "cleanliness": 5.0}

title: Fantatsic!
text: I stayed in the Grange White Hall Hotel the weekend just gone. It was utterly fantastic!! The Welcome and service was excellent as was the room (which we had been upgraded from on arrival, even though we paid what seemed to be an extremely reasonable price through the hotel's website!). the location of the hotel was superb, within walking distance from Euston Station (approx 10mins) and two stops on the underground to Oxford Circus. Everything was in easy reach. We did not sample the breakfast so could not comment on this section of the stay but overall had everything you could have needed, ideally located and excellent service. Would definately recommend and use this hotel again for my next stay in the big smoke.

title: Overall pleased, but...
text: Very quiet location and our room was overlooking the garden, so no problem with noise whatsoever, and the room we were given was very large with a flatscreen TV. Breakfast was nice , offering continental, and we didn't realise we were also allowed full english until we asked on the last day! The location is OK, you need to walk a fair bit to get to the underground stations (Holborn/ Tottenham court rd) But we ended up using Boris Bikes (there is a depot on the road of the hotel). I would have given more stars but in the night we were rather cold as the bed covers were thin, and there were no additional covers in the cupboard. Also, when we went to turn on the heater, it was a very old oil one and made alot of noise when heating up. Also the Bathroom was a bit dilapidated and needs renovating.

title: Grange blooms hotel
text: Stayed here mid Feb for one night on business although we were supposed to be in the Grange White Hall next door. When we arrived, five of us, we were told we were actually in their sister hotel next door. This was no great problem as the hotels along this street and the street parallel are all very similar as I have stayed in several of them. This hotel is fine and the only downside is that there is no bar in this hotel and you have to use next doors. The staff at these establishment were friendly and helpful and I would have no problem staying here again.

title: Homely stay
text: We have state at the Grange hotel on 2 occasions now and both have been most relaxing and enjoyable. staff are professional and friendly. Rooms comfortable an continental breakfast is good. I like its proximity to Kings Cross station. The horse is well placed for the British museum and easy to access the West End.

title: Very Good London Hotel
text: We were on a Theatre Break and after trawling internet for a good hotel, decided on the White Hall. When we arrived I straight away asked for a back room as I hate traffic noise. After a little diliberation the Supervisor changed our room (we had booked Executive as write ups seem to favour these). Lovely glass elevator took us to the 3rd Floor. We had room 301 at far end of corridor. There appeared to be new carpet and decoration in the hall way. Our room was very well decorated and the bathroom was spotless. New tiles and NO horrible black mould round bath. We had twin beds which were very comfortable. Plenty of Tea Coffee etc only complaint no biscuits. We overlooked the garden and the British Museum and the only noise was a hum from the Museum air conditioning which wasnt too bad. Breakfast was very tasty with beautiful fresh rolls, cheese, hams and coissants/danishes. Plenty of tea. Only downfall is if you leave it until 9.00am you may have to wait as the dining room is very small for a hotel of this size. The staff we found all to be very friendly and polite. Our suitcase was kept locked away on the Sunday morning once we had vacated our room and we collected it later on that day with no problem. Monday morning I realised I had left my phone charger in the room, so I rang and they had it recorded and offered to post it directly to me ( charge to be taken from my Credit Card). It arrived safely Tuesday morning, so I was impressed and relived. Overall this hotel is definately one we would return to in London as on previous experiences this was by far the best we have stayed at in London and I AM Fussy. Try it for yourselves.

title: This is London
text: Our room was tiny, but clean and decently furnished. It was overheated. Opening the window solved the problem. We looked out on a quiet garden courtyard. The staff were very nice and accommodating. We had dinner in the hotel 3 times over 10 days. We were usually the only patrons or among a few. Service was excellent and the food was very good for the price compared to places where we ate out. We also had high tea which was much better than one we were given at the Wallace. Fantastic location.

title: A lovely place !
text: The rooms are tiny. The windows of ours had a look on the garden and on British Museum ... The staff was very competent and nice. Rooms were small ... And Montague Street is really where we like to be for visiting London

title: Never a 4 star hotel
text: We stayed for one night with friends. Upon arrival, one room was ready which our friends took. We were told that we had a room on the same floor. when we arrived back later, we were told that our room was on the 3rd floor so not where they had told us earlier. The room was directly outside the lift entrance so anyone waiting for the lift were standing directly outside our room door, which made it noisy. Also, as it was directly next to the lift, there was a loud noise each time the lift went by our floor. Upon entering the room, we were amazed by how small it was. The bed was literally next to the entrance door and around 2 feet from the far wall. The wardrobe could not be opened properly as the dressing table was in the way of the doors, which shows how small this room is. I phoned down to reception who advised that they would call back in a few minutes. True to their word they called and said that if we go back to reception they would transfer us to another room. We went down to reception and were given a new room in the basement. Although there was a slight damp smell, we took the room as it was at least bigger. After trying to switch on the TV it appeared not to be working, so I tried to call reception. On picking up the telephone handset I found that it wasn't even connected to the phone! I plugged it in but it didn't work. I then made another trip to reception to convey my utter disappointment, but when I asked to see the manager was told that there is no manager in the building until the next morning. I gave them my mobile number and asked that the manager call me when he/she arrives. It is now 7PM and I still haven't received a call. Hence the reason that I will never be going back!!

title: 1 Mom and Two Teenagers in One Nice Ensuite Room Worked!
text: Instead of renting 2 rotten rooms....this Single Mom rented one very nice room and Daughter and I shared the large bed and my son slept on a cot. It is worth the price as you can walk to all the major sights and have the Tube station close by ( as well as Scotland Yard). Decent breakfast not steller but nice environment. I found it really interesting that foreign dignitaries would be milling around the lobby as Parliment is around the corner as well. Read up on the History of White Hall Palace to tell your roommate. Also there are cheaper rooms in London....but you will end up paying more for transportation. To save money print Tube maps before you go!

title: Convenient, comfortable and very welcoming
text: The staff could not do enough to help. Comfortable rooms in a lovely part of London. Facilities, reception and bar available 24 hours. I cannot recommend this hotel enough - the only slight issue were the bin lorries collecting very early each morning, but closing the windows blocked out most of the noise.

title: Sweltering with no air-conditioning and poor decor
text: We were told on checking in that there was no air-conditioning, but we could have up to 2 fans! It was a sweltering hot day over 30 degrees, and the room we were first shown was airless, with one window that didn't open and another window with a cracked pane of glass which we hesitated to open. There was a standard 4ft 6in double bed with four metal posts and a canopy of dark material over it. The mattress was saggy. This was supposed to be a de-luxe room. Heaven knows what a standard room would be like. We asked to change. We were shown a room on the floor above, again no air-con, but a bigger bed with no four posted and canopy so it looked and was a bit more comfortable. The decor was poor, faded carpets, chipped dark painted furniture. The windows in the second room did open, but the window ledge was so rotten that you could put your hand through it. Continental breakfast was adequate, but not good. However, the positive side was that the staff were immensely helpful. We did discover that they do have air-conditioned rooms on the ground floor, but we weren't told about these.

title: comfortable clean and as a lone woman traveller very safe
text: the location is great for Covent garden and all the fabulous restaurants. the British museum is right on the doorstep and the hotel garden overlooks the museum. breakfast is hot and tasty and the staff are very professional and friendly

title: Perfect Respite from busy city
text: This hotel and its sister hotel The Holborn are located on a reasonably quiet street near the British Museum and the Russell Square and Holborn Tube stations. Their rates are reasonable and the staff is extremely pleasant and helpful . We appreciated their willingness to keep our luggage safe until we could check in and to serve drinks and tea from the bar at odd times of the day. There is an elevator available and a lovely small restaurant where breakfast and dinner are served at reasonable prices. The staff was also very helpful with sight-seeing and transportation suggestions.

title: Top stay
text: We have stayed there for the London weekend out, and it was lovely. Nice rooms, very convenient location, not far from Euston station! Perfect. We even went to British museum which is back-to-back to the hotel itself.

title: Very helpful, and great location
text: I booked a stay here using the "Top Secret Hotel" feature at LastMinute, and so paid just 75 pounds for a double room. I arrived late in the evening, and the only room available was in the basement. Because of other reviews on this site I was reluctant to take this, and explained that I really wanted a view of the garden. The receptionist (who was both friendly and helpful) took this concern seriously, and arranged for me to stay in Bloom's (the hotel next door, run by the same company to the same standards). My room there was an executive double, and was great: elegant furnished, comfortable, and even spacious!

title: Nice stay
text: Just returned from a four night stay. The hotel is in a great location for shopping, visiting the British museum and the west end, and with it being close to a number of tube stations, it makes getting around very easy. The room was clean and tidy, and our room (back of hotel) and no street noise. The staff were friendly and though the hotel is in need of some refurbishment we enjoyed our stay.

title: Good hotel, excellent location.
text: I was there for 4 days with my father in the beginning of May. Let's cut to the chase. The hotel is good. Not spectacular nor poor. Very british design. We stayed in a double bedroom on the first floor, backyard view. I think our room was the only one with a balcony - which wasn't very useful as the weather was rainy as usual. There were 2 comfortable single beds with nice and clean sheets. Carpet all over the floor. The size of the room is perfect for two people. Don't have any complaints about it. Room service was good as well. Now, we did not have breakfast at the hotel as we found it a little bit expensive (something around 17 pounds). Not a big problem. You can walk around and find a good one easily. There are plenty cafeterias walking distance from the hotel. The surroundings are great. Very nice area to stay in London. You are close to all the West End attractions. We occasionally had to take the tube to meet some friends at their houses. They charge 5 pound an hour for internet access in the rooms. You can pay for the whole day if you like. I never checked how much was it anyway... If you are ok with it, they have a PC that guests can use and get online for free. Basically we were there just for a good night of sleep so it met our expectations. Hope this helps.

title: Radiator would not turn off
text: We stayed here 2 weeks ago. Checked in, all seemed lovely. Room was good size and clean. Went out for the evening and when we returned, the room was much too hot. I looked at the radiator and checked the setting, it looked like it was on low but I turned it all the way off. This had no effect at all on the amount of heat pouring from it. I called Reception, they sent someone up to look. He looked at it, opened the window a bit further and said to give it 15 minutes. 15 minutes later it had not cooled at all, almost seemed to be getting hotter. I called Reception again, someone else came up. Twisted the control valve and said to give it 15 minutes. This was at 11.30pm and I had my 9 year old son with me, we needed to get some sleep. They said they would have moved us but the hotel was fully booked. At 11.45pm I called them again, it was still pumping out heat and they basically said there was nothing they could do. We did not sleep at all well, with the window open we could hear all the deliveries and street noises from 6am. I complained at check out and recieved an email from the head office which basically said sorry my expectations were not met (!) and sorry for any inconvenience and embarrassment. I was not embarrassed, I was cross and upset. So it was a lovely hotel in a good location, but not at all a comfortable night.

title: Nice Room Forget The Rest !
text: We booked here because The Megaro (Kings Cross) was full. The room was nice although the walls were clearly made of paper mache (we may as well have shared a room with next door), the bathroom was horrible (needed a re-furb 10 years ago), the staff were average as seems par for the course (Megaro excluded) in London, but my real gripe was the food. We were told whilst phone booking that our price £124/night included a Continental breakfast. This turned out to be true for the Monday morning and not for the Tuesday ?, confused, I was. Not only was the breakfast incredibly poor it cost us £69 for four!!!!!!!!!!!!, WHAT!!!!!!. How can the Grange group justify that ?. The cooked breakfast is £25/head, what a joke. Stay at The Megaro the full English is £12 and brilliant. Never again, don't stay.

title: Quaint and lovely
text: Quaint little hotel just around the corner from the British Museum -- the location can't be beat! Also a quick walk to Kensington cafes and Chinatown restaurants. The rooms are small (typical UK) but overstuffed with charm -- ours had a lovely canopy bed! Breakfast is lovely and adds to the experience. A delightful little charmer -- you'll feel like you've stepped into the times of Downton Abbey.

title: Ideal location and nice rooms
text: Stayed here for a weekend while visiting the city. The hotel is ideally located as it is 200m from the British museum! Close to the animated parts of town yet in a very calm street. The rooms are quite spacious especially for a Londonian hotel and very calm. On the downside I do not recommend asking the staff on tips for restaurants as there best recommendation for breakfast inn the area was Subway! :) Overall a very pleasant stay I would recommend .

title: Never Again !
text: We had booked a room at Blooms Town House Hotel but on arrival we were shunted into the sister property - the White Hall with no explanation. although i cannot fault the staff the carpets desperately need to be replace and the smell is nearly unbearable. The bed was tiny, and the red wallpaper made the room seem even smaller and somewhat claustrophobic. The breakfast was downright disgusting, cheap sliced meat, eggs that had been boiled for at least half and hour, terrible pastries and croissants but worst of all. Two women from the street came into the hotel, helped themselves to the buffet and left before anyone had even noticed - one of them even tasted the fruit salad from the serving spoon before replacing the spoon in the fruit. Needless to say we felt somewhat queasy after witnessing this.

title: Standards maintained, but TV drove me mad!
text: Stayed here again on business, two nights. Pleasant enough, if rather subterranean, room with all usual facilities. Excellent, powerful and hot shower!! Breakfast very pleasant, reasonable choice and quality. Breakfast room is small so a bit of a squeeze when busy. One gripe: the TV system us a right pain. Far from logical, it comprises a rather dated digibox affair, with generic remote which is a frustratingly imperfect match to the Tv/decoder. Expect to wrestle with this combination frequently! In this day and age, shouldn't be too much to ask for a tv that works without fuss! That said, when it works, great to see the sky sports channels on offer.

title: Shopping Trip
text: This is my 3rd stay in one of the Grange Hotels in Russel Square , and is in a quiet area and ideal for getting about in London ,as everything is close by. I come here with a friend for some retail therapy and the staff always make you feel welcome and the rooms are clean and very comfortable. The continental breakfast is very filling and sets you up for the day. We shall be back soon .

title: Spot on!
text: I decided at the last minute (2 days notice) to take my girlfriend to london for a couple of days for her birthday. Going to watch a show in leicester square I needed to find somewhere near by on a reasonable budget as I'd rather spend the money on her than somewhere to sleep! At £69 for the night with a continental breakfast the grange white hall was one of the cheapest and pretty close to where we needed to be. Spending this amount in this location was a bit of a worry but we were both pleasantly surpised at the room, service and breakfast, all spot on!!! Would highly recomend at twice the price!!

title: What A Disappointment
text: Having stayed at other Grange Hotels with great pleasure, and to which we'll undoubtedly return, the White Hall was out of that pattern. That said, let me say straight away that we stayed for one night on a £72 Bed AND Breakfast Superior Room package, which represented fantastic value for a hotel just off Russell Square Gardens and so close to the Underground network. This though purports to be a 4 Star hotel, and it's standard room rates are priced much higher accordingly. Against those values, it can only be a disappointment, and represent poor value. Check in was easy and conducted by a very nice young man, who informed us that we had received a complementary upgrade to an Executive Room, which was obviously an excellent start to our stay. Imagine our disappointment therefore when we got to our room that there was little Superior, let alone Executive, about it!!!! In fact, as the young man subsequently confirmed, we had obviously not been upgraded - whilst of course we still got the room we paid for, raising our hopes was obviously a bad move. Over and above the small size of the room, and the poor condition of the furniture and drapes, one particular aspect of the bathroom was almost comical. The toilet was next to its long window of clear glass looking out on to Montague Street, and so in clear view of passers by!!! Of course the remedy was simple in drawing the curtains, but I'll bet that I was not the first to almost be absent-mindedly been caught out. The Continental Breakfast was pleasant enough, but very basic in its range, and everything, except toast, was buffet style, so one was constantly up and down getting juice, coffee (and refills), cereal, etc, etc. That may seem normal for a buffet style service, but with everyone doing the same thing, it felt congested and somehow pressured. In conclusion, it's only fair to re-emphasise the fantastic value that our stay represented @ £72, but I wouldn't want to pay any more, until after it's been refurbished.

title: Not of the expected standard
text: Stayed one night on business this was my second stay at this hotel. The reception area and staff are pleasant and there is a well stocked bar and nice garden outside where you can enjoy a drink or snack. My bedroom was a double on 1st floor and tiny, you could barely walk around the bed. It had two large windows that opened up from the floor, great ahi thought as the hotel has no air conditioning or fan, however the heavy curtains stopped any breeze and my room was positioned just above the outside beer garden, it was very noisy. I just thanked my lucky stars that it rained so the drinkers abandoned inside and I got some peace. Bathroom also tiny but well stocked, room not very well laid out, the kettle lead for example was not quite long enough to reach the plug ! Breakfast is not included in the rate but was provided by my company, the price is expensive over £15 and not particularly good value for money, not a great selection of cereal, the cold buffet looked quite appetising but the hot food was not that hot, the egg yolks were smashed, the sausage undercooked and it was not particularly tasty. There was however a steady supply of tea and hot toast. I would not pay that much for this breakfast and would advise missing it and eating out. I would stay here again but I would be asking for a much larger and quieter room and skipping breakfast. The location though is superb, just around the corner from The British Museum, near Coventry Garden and near the tube.

title: What a great location and nice boutique hotel!
text: My nine year old son and I visited London during April 2004 and stayed at the Grange White Hall. The location of the hotel is outstanding - right next to the British museum, right on Russell Square and 2 blocks from the Picadilly Line. We took the Underground right from Heathrow to the hotel for $10 - no switching . It was easy to walk everywhere from the hotel and the neighborhood was really lovely and relaxing to be in. Our room was nicely sized for London, with a very pretty marble bath and nice appointments. Our room faced Montague St, which can be somewhat noisy with cars, but there were insulated windows which muffled the street sounds very well. There was a delightful absence of cigarette smoke throughout the hotel. Breakfast was typically European (e.g. tried to be nice but was YUCKY), but the ambience of the breakfast room is lovely. Next time, we'll just have coffee in the breakfast room and then have breakfast in one of the nice local coffee shops. We would return to the hotel and recommend it to anyone.

title: Fabulous. A real gem
text: This hotel was a real find. Really central, it backs onto the British Museum and easy walking distance of theatre land. Lovely large twin room with comfy chairs to sit in so perfect oasis to retreat to after busy day sightseeing. Great view over garden so very peaceful. Beds really comfy and large bathroom. Kettle and wide range of teas. Up to date magazines to read. Great breakfast in classy dining room. All this for £80 for the 2 of us. Much cheaper, much comfier and more central than very dull chain hotel we usually stay in. I am converted.

title: Great location, friendly staff
text: Stayed here for four nights on business. First night I got a room next to the elevator which was a nightmare. However, next morning I got another room which was perfect, even spacious for London hotels. The location is excellent, you can reach lot of key attraction on foot but two underground stations are nearby. A big plus here is friendly and well trained staff. You will feel welcome and appreciated. I would definitely come back.

title: Something Amiss
text: Looking at the Grange White Hall website it is advertised as a 4-star boutique hotel with Spacious guest rooms either Superior or Executive with Concierge services that include sightseeing requests. First the Good: - great location in Bloomsbury directly behind the British Museum - good breakfast (if it is included in the room rate, otherwise it is very expensive) - nice garden views (from some rooms) Bad: - Superior rooms are grossly mislabeled, these are Standard rooms at best. Also, "superior" rooms are located on all levels, including the basement below grade. Requests for a Garden View room even though booked well in advance and paid for prior will not be given more than a passing glance. We only got a Garden View room after 3 attempts and finally involving the Manager. - Executive Rooms after viewing are not much bigger than their "superior" rooms and at 30 GBP, not worth the upgrade in my opinion - Staff are not given adequate training on handling requests for sightseeing tours. Although they have a Concierge service, not once were we transferred to speak with the Concierge when we made inquiries about a sightseeing tour. We were dismissed by the front desk staff and forced to handle matters on our own. - were given keys to our room only to enter and find the room turned upside down, beds not made, linens and pillows thrown about. Asked to be moved to a room that was ready. - Upon being told to return at a certain time were told to wait while room was being prepared only to find out from a returning front desk clerk that the room had been ready for some time and wondered why we had been told to wait. - that being said this is not a 4-star quality hotel and should not be marketed as such My recommendation if you are set on staying at this hotel, make sure you phone ahead and specifically ensure you are getting the room and services you requested prior to your arrival.

title: Lovely little hotel
text: A wonderful discovery! Fantastic location just around the corner from the British Museum (2 minute walk), on a quiet little street. Breakfast and evening meal were tasty. Rooms extremely well furnished and maintained, and very very comfy beds. I will be back!

title: Good value by London standards
text: Stayed on a weekend break with a friend. We'd booked a twin room but were actually given a family room with one double bed and one sofa bed which was small and would have been more suitable for a young child. The room was on the ground floor and although quiet, it looked out onto the garden / outside tables so it was not very private. On the plus side, the hotel was clean and the continental breakfast which was included in our package was good. The hotel was well located for West end theatres and central London attractions. The bar was staffed by concierge and when I asked for a cider one night I was greeted with a blank stare and asked what cider was - a fellow guest had to explain to the concierge that Magners was infact not beer but cider!! Overall the hotel was reasonable value by London standards and served it's purpose

title: Lovely hotel and full of character!
text: Myself and two friends found ourselves on a last minute trip to the UK which required us to spend the night in London. We booked into the Grange White Hall Hotel and were very pleased. The character of this building is abundant from the entrance, to the check in space to the rooms - this includes the ceilings. Our room was located on the second floor and accomodated the three of us easily. I'm picky about bathrooms and I'm pleased to say this one has rated highly. The place was clean and the shower was very nice. The service was excellent as well. When we arrived it was late morning so the room wasn't ready. We wanted to get out and about in London so the girls at the front desk took our luggage to a holding room. You don't get this at every hotel....and you don't always get the friendliness either. The staff were excellent. The location is also very convenient if you need the train...this was one of the reasons we selected this hotel in the first place. The overall visit was great. I would love to stay there again.

title: Comfortable stay. Great location.
