text: Choosing Hotel accommodation in London is a veritable minefield, and endless hours trawling the internet and reading reviews can sometimes only add to the dilemma given the huge differences in hotels which carry the same star ratings. Having stayed in several London hotels and usually looking for a reasonably priced, central location (not always an easy combination to find), I decided to stay in the Grange White Hall. Website pictures can often mislead but in this case everything was pretty much as described. This establishment is in an excellent location being only a five minute walk from Tot Ct Rd. and all the necessary transport links. The British Museum overlooks the Hotel's garden. While the decor is a little tired compared to other four star hotels in the area, and the exposed lift shaft looks raw and out of place, I could not fault this hotel. From the moment of arrival at the small Reception / Bar, the staff were excellent, allocating rooms to the rear so we could avoid any possible traffic noise. Windows are double glazed to minimise this. (Find me a hotel at full capacity that does not have SOME level of noise!) Rooms, bathrooms, and general areas were very clean with every facility in place to make the stay a pleasant one. The continental breakfast was ideal even if there was some delay due to limited capacity in the small dining room. Staff did their best to accommodate guests quickly. Luggage storage is available as check-out is 11 A.M. At £69 Bed and Continental Breakfast per double / twin room on weekend nights, and a late drink at hand when every bar in London is closed, (Did none of the City Centre bars take the 24 hour option in order to give non-clubbing holiday guests an extra beer or two??), this is good value in a great location. However, for a little extra expenditure the Radisson 4 Stars up the road have a definite edge and this would be a factor for future visits to London. For the price paid this was a very enjoyable stay at the Grange White Hall.

title: Great Location Lovely Hotel
text: We have just returned from a trip to London to see 'Warhorse' Wonderful Show - break out the tissues in the second half!!! We stayed at the Grange White Hall Hotel,Montague Street in Bloomsbury. Lovely hotel, Helpful and welcoming staff. Pretty room overlooking the hotel garden and the back of the British Museum. Lovely breakfast. Great, quiet location, walking distance to Oxford Street, Covent Garden and theatreland and of course for the British Museum.

title: very disappointing stay
text: We were given a basement room, very small, no room for a bedside table or even to swing a cat. Obviously no view from window. Altogether too cramped for two. I would avoid this hotel

title: Small things could make this so much better
text: Just back from a long weekend in London. Nice room, nice beds and bathroom at the Grange White Hall Hotel, but several minor things that pull down the general impression. After checing in (friendly staff) we went to the nice little bar for a drink. Nice TV Screen on the wall "entertaining" us with BBC full mumbeling coverage of the stirling architecture prize 2013 - interesting? Not! Could not put the drinks on my room since I had prepaid for the room and I therefore might leave without settling the bill - a possible thief amongst the guests.... Left for a pub. Nice day in London the following day, returned to hotel - room was not made up (at 6PM). Forget the breakfast - bloody expensive. Want to check mail? 5 pounds for an hour on the internet is close to fraud - wake up management - it is 2013!! Go to any pub near Holborn and have a nice beer and free wifi access!

title: Let down
text: Initial room (paying over £100 per night) was in the basement with no natural sunlight and exceptionally cramped. The television did not work, the control battery had ran out and the cushions on the bed were dirty and stained. As we had arrived late in the evening and were tired, we had a lot planned for the weekend and so just accepted the fact that we would not be spending much time in the room. However, after a night of ridiculous levels of noise, it became unacceptable. We had only a few hours sleep as the noise of staff moving and setting up for the next day above us was absurd. Our window was directly underneath a staff entrance/smoking area and so could hear every word said. When we approached reception the following morning to express our dissatisfaction, the moment we said we were unhappy with the room, the receptionist on duty did not even ask what was wrong, but instantly offered a room change. We accepted the offer as we were in a hurry to make an appointment, but were unnerved at the readiness to offer the change. This does lead me to think that the hotel management are perfectly aware of the inadequacy of the initial room provided and hope that the guests placed there will accept it and pay the full price. We were offered no explanation or apology for the disruption, resulting in two very tired people trying to enjoy a well earned weekend in London. The alternative room offered was nice and would have been acceptable as an initial room. Unfortunately, after this experience, we do not feel that we will ever return to a Grange Hotel again. The location was perfect and the second room was perfectly reasonable. Unfortunately, we felt as though we were an "inconvenience" to the staff after requesting the change as not once were we asked what the problem was or asked if we were happy with the replacement room.

title: Wonderful stay
text: This hotel was just wonderful, staff were so pleasant and helpful. The hotel itself was very clean and smart and very comfortable rooms. Staying at this hotel help make our trip to London special, it was really lovely. Having tea in the garden was a great way to get out of the bustle for a little quiet time, beautiful.

title: Good location, uneven quality
text: Booked a single to meet up with family for a long weekend. Excellent location between the Russell Square & Holburn tube stations, at the side of the British Museum. The weather was quite warm. My room (room 4) was in the basement. The bedroom window was frosted for privacy and wouldn't open, while the bathroom window opened into an areaway, and was totally overlooked by staff & patrons on a terrace, so not exactly discreet. It would have been nice to open a window during the heat. I booked through booking.com, and although I had the same price as others in my party who booked separately, their rooms included a continental breakfast, while I would have been charged £17 or £20 for the same thing! so off to the nearby Pret for breakfast. I didn't mind too much, but it seemed a little unfair. The staff were very pleasant and helpful, but seemed extremely confused about when people were checking in and out, repeatedly trying to get my family out before their stay was over. The bed was comfortable, the room was clean, but the bathroom sink drained very poorly (basement?) which I reported to the desk to no avail.

title: Unfunny Fawlty Towers
text: Arrived 11am Sunday, rooms weren't ready as to be expected. Checking in was extremely difficult and took an age with the check in assistant trying to retrieve our booking. We had suitcases with us which they offered to keep in storage so we could explore London. The staff kindly offered to take these to the rooms when they were ready, I tried to explain that there was 4 of us, so 2 different rooms so it may be wise to write on the labels which room each item of luggage needed to go....which I gave up explaining after 5 minutes. We then arrived back at the hotel in the evening, went to the room....no luggage!! We then had to go back down stairs to reception to ask for our luggage, which we were greeted with a totally blank expression. After numerous phone calls by the receptionist and 15 minutes of waiting our luggage finally arrived. There was no offer to help take these items to the rooms. The rooms were the smallest I've seen anywhere, very dated, cracked tiles in the bathroom, windows were secondary glazed so were unable to be opened and generally run down. On a positive note they were very clean. The service from start to finish was poor and totally bizarre, the hotel was run down and in urgent need of refurbishment. Would never return.

title: Excellent Location and nice room, a bit noisy
text: I was giving a conference talk at the School of Oriental and African Studies and I wanted to stay close. Finding the hotel from Russell Square was easy and stress free. They let me check-in early due to the nature of my flight. Service was excellent. I would suggest a room not facing Montague street and/or not near the elevator for the lighter sleepers

title: Clean and Comfortable
text: This hotel was very authentic and charming. Long hallways and twisty turny layout, so be sure to pay attention where you're going. A cute garden outside and a sunny breakfast room. Breakfast was good (full English) with plenty of variety. The rooms were small but clean and comfortable. The staff were very kind and helpful.

title: Quaint hotel but a little old
text: Nice little hotel. However the interior looked dated. Needs quite a bit of refurbishment soon. The hotel is rather quiet. Most of the rooms are of different layouts and furnished differently even though they are of the same grade of rooms. I was a little luckier to get a large room with high ceilings and full height windows. My colleagues were not and their rooms were dark, stuffy and with small windows. The rooms are not air conditioned. And there wasn’t a fan in the room. Room is really stuffy during the warmer days and the English windows were stuck, can’t really open them. I probably will pick another hotel the next time I visit London.

title: Lovely hotel with great service
text: We stayed at this hotel for one night using a Buyagift voucher, meaning we only paid £80 for B&B. We had originally boked theGrange Blooms hoel next door but on arrival were told we were stayingnext door. Great location in a quiet part of london. % min walk to Holborn tube, behind the british Museum. The hotel is in an old georgean building on a quiet street. Staff were incredibly helpful and receptive.Our room was quite small, on par with London though. Large bathroom but no obscured glass so it had a great view of the street (and the neighbours!) !! Our only complaint would be that the room was very warm, caused by water pipes in the walls apparently. The bed was also quite small. Breakfast room was nice with a good selection. It was a bit pricey though if not included in the room rate.

title: A Grand Old Dame
text: A well situated, moderately priced hotel in Bloomsbury, London backing onto the British Museum. There are elevators which was definitely an attraction in this area of gracious old townhomes converted to hotels. ( Most are walk ups! ) As expected, the rooms are small but quite adequate. Some rooms do not have safety deposit boxes so be aware if this is important to you. Breakfast is not usually included in the room tariff but there is a restaurant on site that was surprisingly good. Breakfast however was pricey at 20£. There is also an intimate bar area. I would return.

title: A pleasant stay
text: I have stayed here before. In the summer months I had rooms overlooking the back which were always nice, if rather warm. This time I faced the street and enjoyed seeing all the lovely Christmas lights outside. Lovely room with sofa and space to walk. Really comfy bed. Breakfast was okay, there is choice but I prefer a pot of tea rather than having it poured from a shared one. I was using the Conference facilities, the help and support was outstanding!

title: Repeat visitor
text: Check in was smooth and I had included a full English breakfast as part of my booking. This had generous portions on both days. The allocated room was facing the front of the hotel which I would not choose again and also it was next to the lift, so noisy at night. Considering I have a membership loyalty card, I expected better. The staff were very pleasant, the room was neat and tidy, the bedding was clean and next time I would opt for a garden view, away from the lift.

title: not worth the money!
text: I was given a room on the first floor directly next to the elevator and it felt like the elevator was running through my room. As a result, from 6 am onwards, I had no chance to sleep. The room is tiny (so small you can use the desk sitting from the bed as there is no space for a chair), but clean, and with a good wifi connection. Bathroom was ok, if not for the fact that the balcony window is directly next to the toilet. Thus to you the choice to use the bathroom in full view of the street and neighbors or use the unhygienic heavy (cloth) curtains... For almost 200 GBP a night you'd expect to have breakfast, but no, breakfast is not included...

title: Clean hotel but room needs a make over
text: I only stayed at the Grange for one night & it was paid for by a large corporate company, I was the guest at the law society & sir Ranulph Fiennes.The staff on the front desk were very friendly and helpful booking in only took about five minutes, I was told everything that I needed to no i.e breakfast times and number to call if I needed room service. I got to my room which was at the back of the hotel overlooking the garden,I think the room was a family room as it was huge, everything looked clean but the bathroom was a bit dated.The toilet was right next to the radiator so when sitting on it if it had been on you would burn your right leg,a lot of the furniture had big scratch marks over it.Also the sash windows did not open properly and this day was very hot and the paint work on the windows well it was more wood than paint, the blinds had broken so was unable to pall them down.we got back to the hotel and had a few drinks and very expensive but nightman very polite and friendly. I was woken about 7am by a member of staff thinking he was arnold schwarzenegger with a leaf blower which added to a ranging hangover did not mix very well,was unable to get back to sleep after that .I did not go down for breakfast so unable to comment on that.I booked out and again the member of staff was very polite and friendly. I forgot to say the bed was very comfortable only problem two singles put together but as it was only me not a problem .In all the room needs a jolly good makeover

title: great base for london sight seeing
text: This was a lovely hotel not far from euston station. We requested a quiet room away from the road which was granted. The room was comfy and well equipped. Bed and pillows nice and comfy. Tea and coffee facilities provided. Staff extremely nice and very helpful. We arrived too early but were able to leave our luggage and went for a bit of sightseeing and lunch. At 3pm we returned and our room was ready. Luggage was brought to us within 10 minutes. Will return to this hotel for our next visit. We didnt use the restaurant so cant give an opinion on it.

title: Worst bed out of 100+ hotels, on a slanted floor in an overly hot room
text: I travel a lot and have probably stayed in over 100 hotels in the past five to six years. This by far had the worst bed of the lot. The mattress was so soft that you sunk in and fell to the centre, colliding with your partner. I hardly ever have complaints about my back, but I woke up the first night with my lower back in spasms. I ended up having naps on the hard floor because that was better than the bed. Complaints about the bed and a plea for a better mattress prompted the dull response that "it's a standard mattress" (whatever that means) and so they thought there was no point in offering me another room. By the time they did agree to a change, it was the last night and I said to forget it. I'll never stay there again. I think the mattress started out as a standard reasonably firm one, but collapse and died in the intervening years, and they haven't bothered to maintain the bedding. Combined with the floor tilting significantly from the window to the door, and the room being unbearably hot despite the heat off and the windows open, it was not a comfortable night. I've stayed across the road at the Montague, and it is a far superior hotel. I would have stayed there except that the hotel had been arranged and paid for by a conference, leaving me no choice in the matter. It's not a four star hotel

title: Wonderful place to stay
text: This place was wonderful! You get a beautiful room, nice location, curteous staff, and breakfast!! If you are looking for a wonderful cozy place to stay that's extremely close to anywhere you'd want to go in London - listen to me and stay at this wonderful place!!

title: Basement room a bit dingy, but unbeatable location and good service
text: Our first impression it has to be said was not good we were placed in one of the basement rooms which was a bit cramped, very little natural light, practically no view and frankly in need of a good refurbishment, my wife was not happy and the hotel agreed to move us to another room on the third floor. This was much better. Without doubt the best aspect of this hotel is its location, its a £5 taxi ride from Euston and literally at the back of the British Museum and a mere 5 minute walk to the start of Shaftesbury Avenue and most of the theatres. Despite this central and convenient location, the hotel was so quiet and you almost felt you were in the countryside, with a pleasant garden and beautiful green squares near by this is probably the best location i've ever stayed in London and will go back for this reason alone. The hotel itself is satisfactory and breakfasts were of good quality, not much going in the hotel but as a base its really unbeatable.

title: Friendly staff and convenient location
text: This is the second time my Mum and I have stayed at this hotel. We had stayed in another Grange Hotel previously also. Do not book this hotel if you want something big, businesslike and impersonal: what we love about it is that there is no air conditioning, but have opening windows and radiators which respond immediately when you turn the thermostat - yes the room is warm when you get in, but you can change it to a suitable temperature. The windows are sash and original, so can be drafty if closed, or may require a book to wedge open, but there are heavy blinds and curtains to block out any draft. And as with any old building, some of the floors are not level, causing furniture to lean a bit, which meant we had to keep closing one bedside drawer which automatically opened whenever we walked past! In both of the rooms we have stayed there have been plenty of spare sockets, and a trouser press. We have stayed both times on the 3rd (top) floor in a room overlooking the garden at the back, and it is very quiet in the nights with the windows open. We have stayed in a quite large room, and one slightly smaller, but more than enough space for us. The staff are fantastic - very friendly, and at breakfast the first morning, they took one look at my Mum and her walking stick, and sat us closest to the buffet, and whilst I was getting us some juice, one staff member asked my Mum if he could fill a plate at the buffet for her if she told him what she would like. This was a lovely touch. When we arrived the machine to programme the key-cards failed, so we were taken upstairs by the concierge, who let us in, and asked to pop to reception later to collect our key-cards. As it was, someone brought them up to us about 10 minutes later. As some other reviewers have stated, the hotel backs onto the British Museum, and is really conveniently placed: on the tube you can get off at Russell Square and walk through the square itself to the hotel and if you are shopping in Oxford Street, the number 7 bus (can be caught from outside Selfridges, just up from Bond Street tube station) takes you to a stop immediately outside the hotel door, and takes about 10 minutes. I did book the hotel early to get a good (non-cancellable) price, which worked out about £200 for the pair of us for two nights including breakfast. We will definitely be staying again next year.

title: Good choice for a short stay
text: I visited London a few days ago for business reasons. Grange White is located in a quiet and nice street, just behind British Museum. Access to Holborn tube station is less than 5 minutes and to Tottenham Court station 5-7 minutes. You can reach Soho area in 15 minutes on foot. Hotel personnel was quite kind and helpful in solving any issues. Wifi is free and of good speed. There are several drawbacks such as the narrow corridors, lack of air conditioning. Room space is, to my opinion, inadequate for families. In conclusion, this hotel is a good choice for a short stay and sightseeing in spite of rooms' moderate quality.

title: Good location and good service
text: I like the location in a quiet street and near to cafes, shops, restaurants and The British Museum. I arrived in the heatwave and was surprised that my room had no air con, so I had to try and open the window using the rubbish bin to wedge it open. But, a comfy and clean room helpful and friendly staff, a nice breakfast room and really pleasant conference facilities. Conference manager was charming and helpful.

title: Cute English Hotel But Dated
text: Very traditional style London hotel with beautiful design elements. Friendly and efficient service. Small room. Unfortunately poor noise insulation. I heard the street and people walking in the corridor and in the room above me. Also the room was warm and I couldn't turn off the heating. The mattress wasn't great either. I didn't have breakfast. The free Wifi worked well. Overall 3.5 on my personal scale. As quiet is important to me I am not likely going to be back.

title: Good location
text: Nice hotel, very good location for Leicester Square. The room was small but lovely and the staff very helpful. Our only problem was our room was right next to the lift which was a little noisy. On the whole it was a nice stay and I would recommend it for short visits at a reasonable cost.

title: OK really
text: The hotel does nothing badly but nothing really well. It is straight down the middle. The location is reasonable near 3 tube stations in a quiet location but still central. The rooms are small but clean and functional. The staff are friendly. I paid £87 per night which was good value. Breakfast was included on our last day. Other days there was a charge of £15 which is expensive. I suggest eating in the Cafe in the park for £5. There is no air conditioning and the rooms can get hot in August. The hotel ask you to pay for your stay on arrival which is unusual and they do not take payment by switch which may be a problem to some people. Overall cheap, clean but not really 4 star.

title: 4-Star prices for 2-star establishment
text: We all know that London is one of the world's most expensive cities, and nobody expects hotels to be convenient. However, the standard of this structure is really low compared, say, with similar establishments in Berlin or Paris. The rooms are clean but tiny, often without natural light, and the furniture is visibly past its prime. On the positive side, the wi-fi connection is extra fast, the bed is reasonably comfortable and the furnishings are good quality. Wardrobes are cramped with trouser presses that can't be used if you need to hang your clothes. The restaurant was sadly empty when we had dinner there with our guests, which didn't surprise us unduly, given the offer and the prices. The staff was however kind and helpful and the hotel is in the same block as the British Museum, a wonderful bonus.

title: Cold breakfast
text: Booked for me by my organisation. Well placed for my close by business meeting. Room was on second floor and was fine. Could not get the tv to work but as I spent little time in the room and I was only there one night this did not bother me. What did bother me was the cold buffet breakfast, plenty of it but cold, cold, cold. Hopefully it will be back to the Hotel Russell next time.

title: Clean and functional, but below average
text: Spent one night on a business trip there. Got an excellent rate through an internet consolidator site - booked less than 24h before arriving there - but my guess after the night is simple: you might get a fantastic price, but you'll get a fairly bad room for that. The room (108) was very small: I was not able to use the desk, because the bed would impede the chair to retract enough to let an adult sit on it. On top of it, the room was placed right on the side of the elevator: everytime the elevator moved, I heard it. I had a late checkin (10pm) and asked the very friendly Lady at the reception if the restaurant was still open, which she denied. I went for a walk to eat something - losing 1h - just to notice when I got back how the hotel offers a 24h room service. If only she told me. In morning I found how heating in the bathroom was off, with temperatures like outside (something around 15 Deg). On the good side, I had a water cooker and a good choice of newspapers in the room (Newsweek, Time, etc). I would had given one star less, but for the price I paid that's probably what I should have expected.

title: Will find a different hotel next visit to London
text: Have stayed twice before and the rooms were fine. This time the room, though large, was not up to expectations. It backed onto the Museum on the ground floor. It had a pulldown double bed, no bedside tables and no bedside lamps therefore anything like phones, cups of tea, etc had to be placed on the floor. If you had to visit the loo during the night you had to make your way across a pitch black room with arms outstretched should you bump into anything - dangerous!! There were two old shabby bed settees in the room. There was a door opening into a 'store cupboard' which was storing old ornaments. The bathroom was fine and the shower was really good. I have a feeling this room was opened up at the last minute, previously used as a store room. There was no trouser press or luggage holder. The kettle had to be placed on the floor to boil up as there was no socket available at desk height. As with previous reviewers, we were not asked about our stay or our room on checking out - probably afraid that we would complain. I have complained by email to the management. Not good enough for an 'Executive' Room paid for over the internet weeks before. In favour of the dining experience, breakfast was excellent, as were the staff in the dining room. The staff in Reception need further lessons in customer service!

title: Highly recommended - **** Stars.
text: Very friendly and helpful staff although I checked in at 2:00 AM. Almost all wishes are fulfilled. High ceilings, walls and windows because of old building and nevertheless everything is clean and almost as new. Here the bathroom was bigger than my whole room in another hotel. Rich breakfast. And bus stop right in front of the hotel.

title: Excellant location & service but small rooms
text: A great hotel. It is easy to commute. Close to all main shopping centres. A warm hospitable welcome. We were given room facing the museum. Quite room, but it was very small. The furniture looked dated. The staffs never walks by without a smile in their face. They made us comfotable even though we were dining alone. For the breakfast as we were waiting for the glass for the juice, a managment staff (Restaurant Manager I guess) stepped in asked us what we need and he himself served it to our table. A good & professional gesture. The staffs in this hotel has made it a gem of a place and we would visit this hotel in our near future

title: The worst deal in all of London
text: To preface this review, I originally booked the Grange Holborn Hotel and when they were overbooked, they sent me to this hotel. I would never have booked this personally. To begin, the staff was friendly and courteous. The facilities, however, are horrible. The bar is very tiny and does not seat very many people. The room are the worst I have have ever paid USD $250 a night for. I got - a double bed that wasn't big enough to sleep two people. The windows would not close completely and the street noise was incredible. I couldn't get a good night sleep. On the other side, all of the noise from the hallway filters into the room. I mean ALL the noise. It is like sleeping in a paper box. The room wasn't big enough for two suitcases. No internet. I didn't even stop for breakfast - I just wanted to get out of there. I have stayed in Motel 6's that were quieter and bigger. Avoid this hotel, at all costs. Believe me - the costs are high. I would have paid USD$40 for this room. Not $250. Complete rip off. Grange Holborn is probably the best deal in London.

title: Definitely not four star
text: I think I've now stayed at all the Grange hotels in London, and this one lets the side down. Really small rooms, and pokey bathroom. Not impressed. The position is great though, and the staff were helpful. Free wifi is irritatingly slow. Grange hotels - get this sorted please! WiFi almost everywhere should now be fast and free.

title: No air conditioning and bad service
text: I arrived at the hotel reasonably late. There is no air conditioning in the hotel and the weather was warm, so the room was stuffy. I ordered room service and it took ages. In the morning I asked for an Iron and Ironing board and again it took ages. Other Grange hotels are much better and I highly recommend them, however, this and it's neighbour the Blooms charge more in the pretence of being some kind of luxury boutique hotel and they are both the same.

title: Superb!!
text: We visited on Saturday 5th August and stayed for one night. This hotel is situated in a lovely are of London. Formerly a Georgian town house it has retained any original features and even has a rear garden where guests can relax...Very rare in London. The reception staff were helpful and courteous as indeed was every staff member who dealt with us!!! I was very impressed..so professional. The hotel and room were spotlessly clean. The street where the hotel is situated has retained many original features and is like a street scene from the film "Oliver" The hotel..staff..food..scenery are fab and we will definately be going back for more Sincere Thanks to all of the staff who work so hard to make your stay special

title: London Business Trip
text: At first glance this hotel is quite grand looking, however on closer inspection is somewhat dated and threadbare. There is no air conditioning, the hotel is onto a relatively busy road, always ask for garden view so you can open the windows. Breakfast basic but edible. Pillows could use replacement.

title: Good location good hotel but some improvements needed
text: As regular Grange Hotel users was slightly disappointed in our one night stay for a birthday treat. Room very small, including the executive double we were upgraded too, no air circulation or air conditioning in room and fan just moved warm air around. Noisy street throughout night, including bin collection at 7am on a Sunday! Limited choice compared to other Grange hotels at breakfast On a positive note staff were friendly, welcoming and helpful, room clean and location good for exploring London.

title: Lovely hotel
text: The Grange is a lovely hotel and our room overlooking the garden to the rear was delightful in a very old style way. So if you like a modern funky hotel it would be best to choose elsewhere. We ate at the restaurant on our first night and were pleasantly surprised by the good quality of the food. Unfortunately breakfast wasn't included in the tariff and was very expensive so we gave it a miss. There are many cafes close by. The location was very convenient for the British Museum and in general we found getting around London very easy from this hotel.

title: Great location for business or pleasure
text: I stayed here for the first time early April. I thought this was a good small hotel that is truly a 4 star establishment. The room was nice and faced the rear garden on the second floor. It wasn't large but was well appointed. The room has free wifi (on my corporate rate) otherwise it is £10 per 24 hours, the bed was soft and comfortable, the toiletries and towels are high quality but there is no air conditioning. My room was exceptionally quiet which is a bonus in central London. The breakfast was excellent - the buffet was top class and very fresh. I would not hesitate staying here again.

title: Slightly disappointed
text: Having stayed at various grange hotels in and around Holborn I have left rather disappointed by this latest stay. Ok it was a rather hot July day but the room did not have any air conditioning. There was a fan but this didn't work and there was no replacement to provided despite informing them minutes after arrival into the room. TV didn't work for a period of time. Room was ok

title: Peaceful hotel in great location
text: Booked for an overnight business trip and the location was fantastic, just 5 minutes from Holborn but in a nice quiet street next to the British museum. Check-in was quick and friendly and I was told I had been upgraded to a king bed which was nice but a bit superfluous for just me! Room was very large with decent size tv with good selection of channels, tea making facillties but sadly no bottled water. The bathroom was well decorated with a bath and good selection of toiletries. The room service menu was rather limited with nothing I really fancied so I went down to see if the restaurant menu was any better. However the room which looked like the restaurant was all set up for breakfast and there was no-one around so I assumed they weren't serving dinner and went back to order room service. The food came quickly and was good. Although there was no air-con there was a big window which opened widely and although it overlooked the street there was very little noise so I slept well (until the morning when there was a rather loud fan noise coming from somewhere!) Breakfast was a bit of a shambles. When I arrived there were no tables so I was offered a cup of tea while I waited. Then a couple came in after me and were found a table by another waitress who moved a table away from another one! Perhaps sensing my annoyance at this I was asked if I would like to sit outside in the garden to which I agreed. By the time a table was laid one was free inside but I sat outside anyway as the garden was lovely. Does beg the question - if there are more quests than tables inside and it is a nice day then why don't they have some tables outside already laid?! However they then forgot me so I wasn't offered any toast. The breakfast selection and quality was generally good although they had run out of scrambled egg and there was no fresh fruit. Checkout was quick and easy and overall I had a good stay and would certainly consider booking again if they address the issues mentioned.

title: just behind the British Museum, a very nice place where to stay
text: Exciting position, indeed. A quiet, nice street at the corner of Russel square, a few meters from the British Museum, which means that you can pop in and breath its inspiring air whenever you like. The Grange Hotels have their own style, which is pleasant and welcoming, the White Hall is one of them. If you find a good offer and you make sure not be given a room in the ground floor, you will find an ideal place where to stay here. It has some character and the staff is kind. Clean, good beds and satisfactory breakfast, in a cozy room. There also is a lovely garden in the back that must be very nice in the summer.

title: Good location for visiting the British Museum. .. otherwise best to avoid this one
text: This hotel was disappointing on do many levels that it is hard to know where to begin. So instead I will point out a positive feature. It has excellent free wifi service. The negatives include being unbearably hot and stuffy with no a/c and windows that only open 3 inches. There is a small portable fan in the room which is the only reason that sleep is possible. Perhaps this is a blessing in disguise as there are great crazing sounds outside at various times during the night when yeah is being collected or drunken rowdies are matching by in full voice. The shower is configured in a way that only high hurdlers can manage comfortably. There is no ice machine. The hotel will deliver buckets of ice to your room. .. except when they run out. The room is on a slant so that drawers fall open randomly and the safe will not stay closed unless locked. The reception desk crew is helpful and fairly friendly.

title: Comfortable hotel. Great location. Very reasonable price.
text: The staff were friendly and helpfull with finding info on our departure flight. The room was tastefully decorated and clean with a reasonably sized bathroom and big windows facing the street. Our room was on the ground floor, so we had the curtains closed most of the time. Better lighting would have been nice, as the ceiling light was very bright and cold and the bedlamp a fluorescent bulb. The aircondition unit didn't work, but the radiators was sufficient. However, we were not told this when we checked in, and so we had to figure out how to adjust the radiators ourselves. The location is excellent. The hotel is situated in a beautiful, quiet neighborhood, just a short walk from Oxford Street and SoHo. In conclusion: The room was not flawless, but the hotel is great value and the location very good.

title: Disappointing and rather poor
text: The website mafe it look quite promising but the hotel is only mediocre, if even. The staff is rather uninterested in servicing. We had an extra bed in, and the mattress was completely inappropriate for use: That is just the way it is, said the concierge. I guess he was just right...

title: Good hotel and location, very small rooms & beds
text: Stayed here in December 2003 and thought the hotel was very nice and in a good location but the room was small even by London standards. I had booked a double room but ended up there on my own and to be honest there would have been no room for my husband in the bed! It was adequate for me - I would call it a queen size bed, slightly larger than a single and no way coudl accomodate two people, so beware when booking. The staff and location however I can not fault, they were great.

title: Terrific Check in and location
text: Last minute decision to stay in town for an additional 2 nights and I got a great deal on this hotel. Fast and efficient cvhevck in - also very friendly. Lovely single room - much bigger than your average London Single. Room 10. I have NO hesitation in recommending this hotel. Clean, friendly, chic and very central.

title: long walk to some rooms
text: long walk to our room on the 4th floor, up 2 lifts but worth it. lovelly robes, slippers & the bath was fab. nice products & staff very helpful. checking was quick & check out easier. We were starting our VSOE trip at 9.30 in the morning & the bell boy carried our bags through the hotel entrace direct to the platforms & then round to the VSOE check in across the station. great place. will use this one again

title: Brief stay.
text: Quite a lovely place to stay with excellent location suitable for a quick visit to the heart of London. Had some problems with my room as the window arc in the room was a potential danger as it knocked me on the face. See picture "Room 619". Will avoid the last floor next time.

title: CHRISTMAS TREAT
text: My daughter and I visited the Grosvenor for a pre theatre dinner in the grand imperial which was outstanding. The grosvenor entrance and staff was wonderful and the bar just added that something special. Beautiful and elegant surrounding. Really beautiful hotel.

title: recent weekend visit
text: The Grosvenor is a wonderful old hotel, the entrance is amazing, and the staff are extremely polite and helpful. The beds are very comfortable, the en suite bathrooms a reasonable size, and the other room facilities to an excellent standard. But unfortunately if you are put in a room that has the view of Victoria Railway Station, you will hear the announcements even with the window closed. This despite the website advising you that all rooms are fully sound-proofed. Be prepared for a long hike to your room too, and it may involve some unavoidable stairs. It probably isn't surprising that the food is rather expensive. I didn't eat or drink at the hotel, as having seen the menus provided in the room I could not briing myself to. And be advised that as well as the meals costing a great deal more if you want them in your room and not one of the restaurants, they also add aa £5 tray charge on top as well. A full English breakfast for one could cost you over £30.

title: Simply Fantastic
text: Have stayed in quite a few hotels all over London but the Grosvenor is my favourite. Fist timer in this hotel and WOW was I impressed, The service at check-in excellent, staff efficient, professional and quick. Nice guy checked me in, listened to my requests and acted accordingly. Room was great - big by London standards. I got a deluxe and was surprised no noise although being in central London. Comfortable huge bed with lots of pillows, fast internet and free. I had a room on the 6th floor (603) so was fantastic being away from noise, no view but that isn't important to me. Space and quite is! Situated almost next door to Victoria Station so convenient for trains, although I arrived at Kings Cross it was well worth travelling the five stops on the tube to stay here. Starbucks, M & S, etc all just outside, and a better option for a quick breakfast as the price tag is a bit steep at £15.00 a go. I didn't have breakfast nor did I eat in this hotel but am sure the food would represent the ambiance. You can tell that they pride themselves in customer service, and am already checking dates out for when I am back in London for business.

title: Convenient hotel at Victoria
text: This was my third visit to Grosvenor. It is extremely convenient. It is situated adjacent to Victoria station. Therefore it is easy to hop on the Tube or take the train to Gatwick. The rooms, sometimes, can be small by US Standards, but the staff and the facilities are first rate.

title: Wonderful stay at a wonderful hotel
text: The stately hotel is down the street from Buckingham Palace and a longer walk to Westminster. The rooms were incredible, the staff very helpful as we were there to sight see and watch a soccer match. The food was very well done, as good as some restaurants in New York. When I go back to London I will stay at the Grosvenor again.

title: Great Hotel and Staff
text: I had a really great stay at the Grosvenor Hotel. I stayed for one night and had a fabulous Time. The Staff was really welcoming and helpful, from start of booking till when I left. I tried the Bar and it was lovely and the prosecco great. The room was spacious and the bed was comfortable. I had to get up in a rush to go to the embassy and didn't had time for my breakfast, but when I came back later, the reception organised some coffee, toast and cakes for breakfast, complementary of the hotel, so I didn't had to go hungry on my away home. What was really nice The Hotel is in a great location, for a city break. Victoria Station has its own entrance to the hotel. All in all loved it and would recommend it anytime

title: Very good and convenient london hotel
text: Stayed here last Friday with another couple as part of our wedding anniversary celebrations. Really convenient for Buckingham Palace (about 400 metres), which we toured in the afternoon, before checking in. Our friends were allocated room 668 and ourselves 704. Room 704 was a tiny attic room just big enough to fit a bed in, with a miniscule bathroom. We called in our friends room for a drink, only to find it was at least 3 times the size of our room! I went straight down to reception to enquire when a booking was made for 2 rooms there were such disparaging differences between those allocated. Samir was most helpful and offered to move us to another room. Apparently Room 704 isn't normally allocated to paying guests, rather being used for trainee staff. I mentioned that we were there for our wedding anniversary and we were moved to Room 113 which was lovely. Thanks Samir. Breakfast in the morning was good, witha good variety and quality of items. The only minor issue is that all of the food, both hot and cold is collectd from a small horseshoe shpaed area. This is a big bottleneck during busy times!

title: Great hotel, good price, good location
text: We had a last-minute meeting scheduled for London during the week of Wimbledon. The Grosvenor was the LAST reasonably-priced hotel in central London. The hotel was immaculately clean with small room, typical to Europe. It sits above Victoria station making it accessible. The conference room was full of IT gadgets, though we brought paper. The staff at reception, breakfast, concierge, and conference rooms all took an extra step to make sure we were looked after properly. This isn't where we normally stay when we travel to London, but it is now on the short-list of places to check when we do have to go back.

title: Fab cream tea.
text: Such a wonderful cream tea experience. Service was stunning, very attentive and friendly. A lovely place to go with friends or family. We had a Fab time! A lovely place for a celebration or just a get together.

title: Good Location
text: Spent three nights here and traveled about London. The hotel was very neat and tidy and the staff were very helpful. The room as a single supplement was a double and worth staying in. Attached to the Victoria station it was easy to get on the underground. The breakfasts were substantial.

title: Excellent location, very happy stay.
text: The hotel is in a great location just a short walk away from Victoria Station, "Wicked" and Buckingham Palace. A little further to the Mall, Westminster Abbey and The Houses of Parliament. The hotel has been renovated which makes it fresh, clean and very well maintained. The hotel staff very efficient, knowledgable and polite. A range of bedroom options from suites to basic. Our room was a decent size with a very comfortable bed and the amenities you now expect when travelling. The breakfast was very good. English overall but with a good continental breakfast if you wanted. Lunch was ok. Slightly overpriced for the quantity and average. The chicken on the dry side. However the hotel cannot be faulted overall and we would stay here again. Minor inconvenience which is awful to admit but the wifi was impossible to get in our room on our phones. Very sad reflection on us !!!

title: On the station
text: We overnighted between coming into Victoria Station and going out the next day. There is a door right onto the station, and the concierge staff will arrange for luggage to be brought in and out. We had a room in the newer wing, which was a bit of a hike but worth it. The room was large and very comfortable. Even though it looked down on the forecourt of the Station, it was very quiet (triple glazing). We had dinner in the Brasserie. The street side was buzzy but we opted for a quieter room on the other side of the corridor. The menu is straightforward but the food was fine. We didn't have breakfast so can't comment. Jamal at the concierge desk was very helpful.

title: Best hotel in London
text: My husband and I stay a lot at the wonderful hotel, the two Jamie's who greet you at the front of the hotel are amazing, they are always very polite and happy to help with anything. The service in the hotel is the best and the rooms are really nice and the bonus is the location you can walk anywhere. It's a must to stay at the hotel, far better than the Dorchester.

title: Great Location
text: Stayed for one night on Boxing day, you can not fault this hotel on location its perfect!!! We parked on Victoria station 24hrs for £15.00, you can access the hotel from inside Victoria station so it makes it ideal! The hotel is beautiful and I honestly had the best nights sleep I've ever had at a hotel, we stayed in room 161. The only complaint is the room service is very poor, we waited well over an hour for soup of the day described as "soup of the day with crusty roll and butter" we received 3 slices of white bread no butter or spoon, we didn't complain as it was gone midnight and by then just wanted to sleep and it make us laugh but the for the prices you would expect much better service. We had a sharing platter before we went to a show at the Apollo in the Grosvenor Arms which I couldn't fault it was perfect and staff very helpful. My tip for the hotel manager would be to leave some information in the rooms/your website as to where to locate door to station, and other places within the hotel as we were forever asking where's this where's that! and would never of know if we had not read trip advisor before hand. All in all a fantastic stay and will be paying a visit again in the new year.

title: Quality hotel and great value for London
text: I stayed for one night on a business trip. I had a single room booked and expected a small room after reading reviews on here. I was offered an upgrade for £20 but as I was staying for only one night I declined the offer. The room I was in was small but adequate for one night. It had a 3/4 size bed which was fine and really comfortable, a large bathroom, large wardrobe, safe, lcd tv (not a great signal), tea/coffee and an iron and ironing board. There is also free wifi. The room furnishings were great and contemporary/boutique style. I ate in the Brasserie, which is not cheap, but on a par with other restaurants in the area. The food was very good, but if you have a big appetite, the portion sizes are small. The gym is good and breakfast was excellent. The reception staff were very efficient and helpful. Restaurant staff could have been more atentive at breakfast, as it was very hard to catch their eye to get coffee, as they seemed to deliberately not look around the room to see if people wanted anything. That is my only minor criticism. Overall excellent value for London and I will be back later this month and in January.

title: Thoroughly Enjoyable Stay - Highly Recommended!
text: I stayed with my family at The Grosvenor Hotel for 5 days whilst we were visiting London. It provides an excellent base from which to explore the sights of the Capital especially as it is adjacent to Victoria Station and there is also a bus stop close to the front entrance. We had an executive king room. The bed was huge and extremely comfortable. The bathroom (and the room itself) were spotless and the bathroom came with soap, shower gel etc which was replenished daily. Fresh fruit was also provided and there were tea and coffee facilities. We had a fridge which was stocked with a variety of soft drinks and mineral water. For the business traveller there was also an iron with ironing board and a shoe shine kit together with a safe. We were also impressed with the friendly and helpful staff and would definitely stay here again.

title: Amazing stay
text: I stayed at the Grosvenor Hotel for 2 nights and was thoroughly impressed. The main foyer is breath-taking, the bedrooms are very impressive and the breakfast was delicious. My room had a very comfortable bed, good size bathroom and plenty of closet space. The finishing touches in the room made it a very friendly/homely stay. I will stay here again without hesitation.

title: Almost luxury
text: I picked the Grosvenor for a stay for my daughter and myself having wondered through on a previous visit with my husband. The lobby is impressive, the room was well decorated, clean and comfortable beds. Extremely small bath with just enough linens. No robes and no view (even from the top floor). In-room tea service was nice, but instant coffee. Staff pleasant, but difficult to understand. Or, they didn't understand me. I didn't seem to be the only one with this problem. Every time I went through the lobby, it seemed to take several employees to decipher a reservation as 2 or 3 would regularly be huddled around a computer with perplexed guests trying to "explain." I am grateful that Nate, the evening manager, was able to help us when several before him would not. Some language barriers, lots of rules, and limited flexibility in their job scope, apparently. Customer service does not seem to be the number one priority. You can't beat the location next to Victoria station, down the road from Buckingham Palace, and within walking distance to so many sights. We enjoyed our stay and though it was all very pleasant (with the exception of check-in), there was never the feeling that they would be willing to do "more" for you, if needed. Pretty on the surface, limited on the inside.

title: Beautiful Tower Room
text: Fantastically Victorian in decor and wonderfully clean. Sunday breakfast was a huge disappointment but management rectified the situation promptly. Dinner was amazingly tasty and superbly presented. Friendly staff.

title: nice hotel
text: I liked this hotel. It's in a great location - near Buckingham Palace and Victoria tube station, and close to the Google offices. It has an old, elegant charm, but the rooms are modern and clean. recommended!

title: Decent hotel, nice rooms, friendly service, perfect location for Victoria station
text: Pretty much what it says in the title. The whole hotel is nicely decorated and the rooms are clean and comfortable. The staff are really friendly and it couldn't be in a better location for Victoria station which is the main reason I chose the hotel.

title: FANTASTIC HOTEL AND SERVICE
text: Went for the afternoon tea and it was so amazing,They were so accommodating,Out of a kind of tea we wanted to try but the earl grey was great,scones and jam and clotted cream were incredible! They came warm and everything,They also will bring out more food if you request,The staff are excellent and i would recommend you give it a try.

title: Fantastic Stay!
text: We arrived The Grosvenor on 28 Jul 2016 at approx 7:45 AM. Since the rooms were nowhere near ready, they held our bags at the concierge desk and helped us book a tour on the Big Bus hop on hop off service. A great way to get your bearings on your first day in town. The hotel staff was extremely friendly and Sarah Jane at the concierge desk was magnificent all week, helping us with tours, trains and busses. They could use a bit more staff to assist with tours as the concierge desk was typically overwhelmed with people like us asking for help. Food was very good in the Grosvenor Arms. The daily buffet breakfast had everything one could want or you could order from the menu. The afternoon tea, left a bit to be desired in our opinion. But, that could also have been our tastes. The room was very comfortable. Bigger than I expected compared to other hotels I've experienced in and around the UK and Europe. Only problem we had was the toilet took a very long time to refill. So, consecutive use could be problematic. The location was superb! Victoria train station is attached. So, day trips out of London were a breeze. Some people have complained they could hear the loud speaker announcements. Yes, depending on room location, this is true. But, we found it to not interfere with rest and after 9:30PM, the announcements seemed to stop. More annoying were the inconsiderate guests that let doors slam, yelled down the hall or let their kids carry on a racket! Luckily, they were only there one night! The hotel was beautiful..absolutely beautiful! I will gladly stay here again and will recommend it to anyone going to visit!

title: Perfect hotel
text: Just returning from our trip to London and stopped overnight in this gorgeous hotel. Had an amazing time, we were greeted by Nate on reception who was very friendly, we mentioned to him that I was staying for my birthday and later on after returning to our room, a slice of cake and birthday message had been left. We were pleasantly surprised by this thoughtful gesture. The room was very cosy and the bed was so comfortable, also it was very quiet, perfect for couples. Location was brilliant, we came to see Wicked at the Apollo theatre which was just round the corner and the hotel is situated right at Victoria station and only approximately 40 minute walk from the main attractions of London. Would definitely stay at this hotel again

title: Great location but everything else average
text: The location of this hotel is perfect. It is located right next to Victoria Station, so ideal for getting the train or the tube. There is even an entrance to the hotel in the station. The concierge we came into contact with were rude and unhelpful. They preferred to talk to other people than help. They made us feel like we were putting them out, when we asked for our luggage. The reception staff were OK but not that friendly. The hotel is very dated though and the bedrooms are in need of renovation. The mattress was extremely hard and uncomfortable and the pillows were either hard or lumpy. Neither me or my husband got any sleep in the two nights we stayed. The bathroom was an OK size for a central London hotel but there was a massive crack in the sink and the shower did not work properly, we either had to have a cold shower or a scalding hot shower. So we ended up having to use the shower connected to the bath and hosing ourselves down. The TV was barely watchable, all channels were really fuzzy/snowy and not that many too choose from. Now I know we were not there to watch TV but it is not the point, when we were in out room

title: Really good hotel
text: The location of this hotel is excellent - right next door to Victoria station. Room was not very spacious but more than adequate for our one night stay. Reception staff good, we booked in really early and this was no problem and booking out simple. Breakfast was excellent, good choice of food and service very good. Would recommend it for a short stay in London.

title: Great Grosvenor
text: Excellent Hotel. We were made to feel very welcomed and appreciated from the moment we entered. All the staff are so polite, friendly and professional. We were given an upgrade on our room,as we had stayed with them on previous occasions. This was a lovely touch! Service was outstanding from start to finish. Thank you to the staff at the Grosvenor for helping to make our weekend stay special.

title: Excelente experience
text: I stayed at The Grosvenor Hotel, during a business trip, for 10 nights (february/march 2015). The location is perfect, the decoration is unique and the attention of concierge (Mr. Jamal), reception (Mr. Nabil) and breakfast teams (Mrs. Carina) was fantastic. Despite some noise coming from the roof (6th floor) some nights, the experience was excelent. London is an incredible city, but visit London and stay at The Grosvenor Hotel ir something that I would like to have again.

title: Lovely, lovely hotel, which we loved. But breakfast manager was not nice to his staff, which we didn't love.
text: This was our second visit to this hotel. The room was quite nice but rather small and the floors were slanted--but i expect that. The staircase going up to the second floor was beautiful. Wifi was complementary, which was nice. The breakfast was lovely as always, but the manager of the breakfast place was rather abusive to the staff--who worked very hard. He was condescending and would loudly chastise them in front of the morning crowd of patrons. One morning he physically pulled a woman into another room. As I said, the servers worked very hard, nonstop, actually. I was upset as my granddaughter witnessed this. It ruined the breakfast experience for all of us. We reported this to the day manager the morning we left, so hopefully he is no longer there. The concierge got us front row center tickets to Lion King, which was incredible. She was absolutely lovely.

title: Enjoyable stay
text: Lovely room. Lovely check in girl Cristina. Only thing that let our stay down was breakfast. Taken to our table with no explanation. Had to ask 4 times for a cup of tea. Clearly not enough staff on duty. Otherwise very enjoyable

title: Quality Victorian Hotel
text: My wife and I stayed at this hotel as part of an inclusive theatre trip. It is a beautiful Victorian building right on top of Victoria station and even has its own entrance from the concourse. The architecture is true Victoriana and the interior grand and impressive. Perhaps the most impressive feature is the huge chandelier in the main entrance and this lights up the tiled and wood panelled interior which has been expertly refurbished. Staff are friendly and helpful and we had a good welcome. We had a drink in the Grosvenor bar which has waitress service. You can also get light meals here. There is a large tv thankfully without sound but with sub titles. We had two ciders which cost £10 plus a 12.5% service charge added automatically. There is a Chinese restaurant which looked good on paper. Our room was smart and had everything you need for a comfortable stay – tv, safe, aircon, kettle with tea / coffee, plenty of cupboard space and a comfortable bed. We had some initial problems with the aircon and lead for the kettle but these were sorted out by maintenance. There was a very ancient chair which had been recovered in a grotty vinyl out of keeping with the décor and standard of the room. It really needs replacing. If you are a fitness fan there is a gymn on the 7th floor. Breakfast was really good. Scrambled eggs, fried eggs, beautiful herb sausages, and lovely smoked salmon plus all the other things you would expect in a cooked breakfast. Cereals and fruit are also available plus different flavour teas. We enjoyed our stay and would stay again. The hotel is very well placed for transport links and access to the west end.

title: BEAUTIFUL BUILDING & COURTEOUS STAFF
text: Stayed here recently for 1 night on business due to its location right in/on Victoria Station. Entrance and reception are stunning and welcome from staff was warm and efficient. Breakfast was not included by my booking agent so had to pay extra - employer was equally tight by booking me a standard single room - and I ended up in the tower - that said it was perfectly adequate and had everything I needed. Would recommend.

title: Has seen better days
text: After going up the steps with our bags we were not greeted by anyone to help us. The lobby is very grand but only has two chairs! The check-in was long and painful. Not sure if it was the receptionist or the computer but it was inexplainably long. We had two rooms, one on the 4th floor(which was neat but small) and another larger room on the 6th floor with a nice view. No one bothered to tell us that the 6th floor was only accessible by one elevator. The room was very hot and if we turned off the heat the air vent would vibrated and make a loud noise. Also there was no hot water in the morning and the tv reception was very poor. Overall, it was expensive ,very average hotel with a good location very near Buckingham Palace.

title: Excellent Hotel in an excellent location
text: I had cause to call a few times for various reasons before my stay and got all the info I needed. Location right in Victoria Station, excellent for the Gatwick express and Tubes. Hotel very clean and comfortable, breakfast delicious. Made a surprise birthday treat for my daughter when we entered our room

title: Just Lovely!
text: We stayed at The Grosvenor for just 1 night (sadly), but what a wonderful experience! From the doorman when we arrived, to reception, the concierge and the room--everything/one was lovely and very helpful, friendly and courteous. We arrived an hour before check-in time and because we only had one afternoon to enjoy London, we were anxious to get out and about. They let us pre-register and took our bags, which were later waiting for us in our room when we returned. The room may have been a tad small by US standards, but due to the high ceilings and tall doors and windows, it didn't feel small. Everything about the hotel felt very elegant. The doorman that day was particularly helpful with our bags and giving us directions to and tips about our sightseeing destinations, as well as suggestions for dinner. I wish I had gotten his name. I would highly recommend this hotel for your stay in London.

title: Right at Victoria Statio
text: The entrance hall is magnificent and grand, staff very friendly and as mentioned in the title, the hotel is connected to Victoria Station making it very central. Buckingham Palace is only few minites walk away. Westminster Cathedral (Catholic) is less than 5 min. away. All in all, it was a pleasant stay.

title: Great central location
text: Went with three friends to visit the Chelsea Flower Show, The Grovenor proved to be a good choice of place to stay. The staff were helpful, friendly and polite, the public areas are quite spectacular and certainly make an impression. The sweeping staircase is lovely, it leads you up to the champagne & cocktail bar, very inviting. We had booked two twin rooms and were allocated wing rooms on the fourth floor, a bit of a trek, but we didn't mind. The first room was large and had a double and single bed, all very nice. The room my friend and I stayed in was smaller with twin beds, but was fine, although the unit with the tv etc.. on was a bit worn and knocked about a bit. We were only there for one night so wern't too bothered. Breakfast, the next morning was great, we were pleased to find that they were giving special vouchers out at reception that knocked £10s off the price, so we enjoyed it all the more. All in all a good stay at the Grovenor and I would recomend it to anyone who is looking for a reasonably priced, central London hotel.

title: Great Vacation Thanks to the Grosvenor Staff
text: We spent a great week in London, thanks to the wonderful staff at the Grosvenor. The hotel, was clean and elegant and the staff was always friendly. The concierge was very helpful a couple of time and special thanks to Sabina at the front desk for making sure our room request was met and for checking with us through out our stay!

title: Fabulous
text: I took my daughter to for her first trip to London for her eighteenth birthday We stayed at the Grosvenor primarily because we were using the gatwick express and it meant we didn't need to manage the underground with suitcases We had the most fabulous time, the staff were fantastic, the room was fabulous, the food was brilliant We will definitely be back and highly recommend this hotel

title: Wonderful hotel, great location
text: This is a beautiful hotel, with extremely helpful and friendly staff everywhere. We had a basic room but was quite spacious( even though we had taken a fold up wheelchair). The room was well equipped and spotlessly clean. The bed very comfortable. We were worried when booking a London hotel that the room would be noisy but it wasn't at all. We had a wonderful nights sleep. Would definitely stay again.

title: Birthday visit
text: Well this was a great find ,we were going to see wicked at the Apollo theatre just around the corner and thought we would pop in for a quick drink as a treat for mum's birthday ,it was fabulous and not as expensive as I would have thought,we had an amazing margarita in the bar that made me walk sideways when I stood up ,the staff and service was so friendly and not stuffy ,I would definitely pop in again as it made our day special ,a really lovely hotel xx

title: Very average stay at an upper end hotel
text: Great first impressions on arrival as lobby and reception staff were excellent. Two twin rooms booked for the same price at the same time. First room was fine, however second room was so small we didn't have space to move round the beds while our suitcase was on the floor. We tolerated this on the first night of our stay as we had flown in from overseas however requested a move the next morning. After a deal of discussion we were finally moved to a room that was of an acceptable (not exceptional) standard. Food service in the hotel dining areas for breakfast (on both days) and dinner (one evening) was something like an episode out of Fawlty Towers! The service, or lack thereof, required that I go to the bar on several occasions to request drinks service. When the waiter eventually came to our table he did not apologise but did inform us that he was very busy and would take our order when he had time. He promptly turned and walked away. I then sought out the on duty manager who whilst unapologetic found an alternate waiter to provide service. Drinks were ordered, arrived after 20 minutes, incorrect drinks provided! When a friend arrived to join us we had to move to another table for dinner service and unbelievably whilst our drinks were being moved from one place to another they were actually returned to the bar and disposed of! You can only imagine what it took to get them replaced! Food and coffee service at both breakfast and dinner was shambolic overall. There are very obviously some serious issues within the food/beverage services at this hotel. Wifi reception in the bedrooms was minimal at best and more often than not non-existent.

title: Convenient location with impressive foyer
text: I chose this hotel because of the convenience as it is on Victoria Station and I was catching the Pullman the following morning. The foyer is magnificent and check-in easy, though I had to take my bags up to my room myself, which was a bit of a surprise. My room was adequate with good facilities, including tea/coffee making items and a large, well-appointed modern bathroom with a bath and good shower. It was very well sound-proofed A good choice in terms of price and location. I would stay again if I were travelling from Victoria.

title: very central to everything
text: going to theatre as well as sights and sounds of greater London was very convenient. Close to Victoria Coach station with all its traffic, room was small but very nicely decorated. Good service from front office personnel.

title: Walked a maze to find our room
text: We stayed here with a bus tour. Prior to our checking in, a number of our tour said what small, hot, crowded rooms they had there previously. Some of them didn't have enough room to open 2 suitcases. Several of them had to change rooms and were not happy with the hotel. Another one said he'd never stay there again. We were dreading staying there. When we checked in, I asked for either 2 twin beds or 1 bed, whichever room was larger. I am so glad I did, because the lady checking us in booked us in a room with more floor space. Our room was great. It was very clean, bed & pillows were excellent, plenty of space. Modern and clean. Food at hotel was very good, too. The reason I didn't rate it higher was because not all rooms were as good as ours and because of the "wings" of the hotel. The elevator only went to a certain floor, then we had to lug our suitcases up or down stairs to get to the "wing" with our room. The hotel is laid out like a maze and you should allow plenty of time to get to the lobby, if you are on a time schedule or catching a cab at a specific time.

title: Excellent Hotel
text: Could not fault this hotel. From the excellent location to the stunning service we received. From check in to check out, it was a wonderful stay. Staff are so well trained, polite and attentive. Room was spacious and very clean. Perfect hotel for a couples break or a sightseeing visit.

title: Superb customer service!
text: For me, the staff really *make* this hotel! I have never become as fond of a hotel as quickly in the past 20 years.... And I travel most weeks for business. The staff are friendly, efficient and really seem to have been schooled by a crack customer service ninja

title: Good touristy location, average hotel
text: This hotel is all about location if you are a tourist and want to see the Buckingham palace area. The hotel itself is slightly garishly done - loud furnishings, dark colours and big chandeliers. Minimalist and modern it's not! The rooms are tiny and the bathrooms are super tiny as well.

title: Complementary
text: great staff,good food and service. I had such a wonderful time.that I made a new reservation to arrive on and check-in on March,17th. What better complement can one give.I look with delight to my stay and enjoy the wonderful breakfast provided,along with the professional staff.

title: Use to be called Thistle Victoria.
text: Only a mile from Victoria Station. Neat Trafalgar Square, St.Martin-in the-Fields. When you go for a walk don't be surprised to see the Queens Guard pass you by on horseback. Near many shops in London. The inside is gorgeous and the staff friendly and helpful. My cousin Gina and I could not help but pose on the staircase in the hall. Around suppertime people come in from all over to sit on the couches, overstuffed chairs in a huge lounge. The walls are lined with rowing things other sports items. People relax with a drink of liquor or coffee or tea and just talk. By far I had the best breakfast I have ever had in my life at this hotel. Tables and tables of foods. Thought the hotel was just wonderful.

title: Nice stay overall.
text: This hotel is beautiful inside and out. We were on a tour with Globus and would be staying here at the start and end of our tour of the UK and Ireland. Let me start with our first night (05/24/2013): My boyfriend and I were traveling with my mother and she was to be staying in a separate room from us. We arrived at around 11am and our rooms were not ready (which is understandable given how early it was). My boyfriend and I left for a few hours and my mom hung around the area and my boyfriend and I ended up getting back at around 2pm-- we were told rooms would be guaranteed by 3 but could possibly be ready sooner. We checked, and my boyfriend and I's room was ready, but my mom's was not. So the three of us went up to the same room while my mom waited on hers. We were told they would call us when her room was ready, but they never did. I ended up having to call down to the lobby to ask. This was about 5 minutes until 3. Turns out her room was right across from ours. Now, the room. It was nicely furnished and clean, and a good size. It had a nice view of the Victoria Train Station and the road. However, instead of giving us one bed big enough for two people, the beds were simply pushed together to create a larger bed. Not comfortable and not practical for a young couple... We were starving before dinner so we wanted to order a 'snack' from room service. The prices for everything were astronomical so we ended up ordering some bread with oil and balsalmic for about 4.50. We also ordered two bottles of still water--which we thought would be the normal size bottles of water. The bottles ended up being huge (one bottle would have been enough for us to share), about the size of a wine bottle. And all of that with the service charge and tip was over 15 GBP...for some scraps of bread, oil and water! That's about $23 USD. !!! Overall, the room was comfortable. The reception on our television was a little fuzzy despite it being a newer model tv. But I don't have a lot of negatives to say about this particular stay. Our second stay on the last night was better. While our view from the room was not as good, the room had a full size bed instead of two smooshed together. Thank god! The room also seemed to have more space. But it was just as clean and furnished as the first night we stayed. Both rooms also had a micro fridge which included sparkling water, but we did not partake. Pretty nice stay overall.

title: Traditional
text: Good traditional Victorian railway hotel. We enjoyed our stay though it was all a bit impersonal. It's a fantastic old building but if you want something more contemporary this is not the place. The area around the station is not that great.

title: It was ok, not as high standard as expected.
text: Great location and service on check in. Issues with the hot water in the shower, maintenance were called twice but still never got it sorted. The mattress was far to firm and pillows were a bit thin. Can’t fault the staff though for their helpfulness and friendliness.

title: Fantastic
text: Just returned from staying 3 nights at this lovely hotel ... I booked this as a birthday treat for my husband. Checking in was very quick, our room/bathroom was lovely with lots of space. Breakfast was lovely,lots of choice for a full english, if you pre-book this you get a reduction. My husband received a fruit bowl on our first evening and a birthday card from the hotel, which was a lovely touch. The staff could not do enough for you, making sure you had a map,knew which bus/tube you required. The hotel has an enterance into victoria station which is great for access to the train/tube. The location is fantastic, short walk to Buckingham Palace,Westmister,Harrods and lots more. I would use this hotel again on future stays in London.

title: Will be back again ...and again....and again!!
text: Myself and my son stayed in the Grosvenor while attending the League Cup Final at Wembley and having travelled from Ireland through Luton Airport, with bus direct to the hotel, we were delighted with our stay. Location couldn't be more perfect for visiting the sights of London and its location beside Victoria makes every part of the city equally accessible. The staff are lovely, pleasant and extremely helpful and the rooms are first class. The price of the accomadation was very affoardable and represents great value. Thank you to all at the Grosvenor

title: Great location and service, awkward room
text: My room was as small as a closet even for London standard and it was about a mile away from the lobby. However the location made it up, next door to Victoria' station. I would repeat but ask to look at the room before hand.

title: Location for sure!
text: The location, the staff, the building are excellent! Although it was a little confusing to find the room which was in a separate building which communicated with the basic, but it was fun and was adventure. I would go back!

title: Grosvenor hotel Victora
text: We had a wonderful stay at Grosvenor hotel. The hotel is located close to Victoria station, underground and bus and is ideal for getting everywhere.. The staff and hotel atmosphere was really nice. The room was fine, although the toilet flushing was a bit noisy. The only meal we had at the hotel was breakfast. The breakfast was not huge but the food was good and the atmosphere was pleasent.

title: The Perfect Proposal..... Amazing!!!
text: I booked the Hotel for my partners 30th Birthday and on booking made the hotel aware I intended to ask her to Marry me. They took care of the rest. It was perfect!!!! Everything about the Hotel was fantastic, location couldn't be better,the 'Grandness@ of the Hotel is spectacular making it exceptional value for money. The way the staff treated us made the stay extra special. Relationship Manager Jackie Small made contact to discuss my plans and with the help of Executive House keeping manager Eva Slatter and their team pulled out all the stops and made it a stay to remember. I was blown away! A truly fantastic hotel with remarkable staff. Thank you!!!! We will be returning with our two children once we are Married.
