It was refreshing to meet down to earth people in an up market place.

title: Overnight stay
text: The hotel is nice, clean and very well positioned . We were upgraded to a deluxe room for free but I can't say I was impressed with the size and outlook however the beds were very comfortable and the bathroom had nice white towels ,

title: show and shopping
text: a a great hotel and a very clean room also nice and quiet the staff also friendly and helpful breakfast could be better !! in as much as the coffee far to strong an bacon cold and could be of better quolity

title: 5 star
text: Beautifully decorated and absolutely great food. I would definitely return in the near future. Reasonably good service and also a friendly, tranquil ambience. Even the sandwiches were so delicious. Perhaps quite high priced but definitely worth it.

title: Lush hotel.. great location
text: Lush hotel.. lovely helpful happy staff and amazing brekka. Defo stay again. Great location, right next to Victoria and tube station great line. Tesco m&s Starbucks all preety close next to station. Overall great

title: Excellent weekend in London - Compliments to Hotel Staff
text: Just back from a weekend at this hotel. Excellent service. Location was brilliant, direct access into Victoria station for links all over the city. A nice walk alternatively up to Buckingham Palace and onto Picadilly. Upgraded to suite which was nice and private - although we had to take a seperate lift to get to our room. Recommend to couples - though not for kids!

title: Great hotel central to verything
text: Thge hotel is righ above Victoria Station. If the trains are running it is easily accessed from the airports or any other part of the City. If the trains are not running the busses will get you there. Only once could we hear the station announcment in the 3rd floor room. Most of the staff were helpful watch out for one of the concierges he gave us bad information and seemed upset we did not want to buy theater tickets from him.

title: Beautiful hotel, great location
text: The Grosvenor Hotel is lovely. Our room was beautiful and spacious (two adults, and a child who used a sofa bed) and we loved the attention to detail throughout. The location, right next to Victoria Station, Buckingham Palace, theaters, etc...was very convenient and the staff was gracious and accommodating. We had access to the Executive Lounge, which had adequate choices for breakfast, snacks/appetizers and drinks. The tea room was beautifully decorated and comfortable. All in all, a wonderful experience!

title: Reunion Bar
text: We went to the Reunion Bar last night - fantastic bar - well worth a visit - cocktail menu great and staff helpful and attentive. Only downside we wanted to Rose Petal Champagne cocktail but they didn't have the ingredients to make it - had to have two Peardrops instead which were fab.

title: London weekend visit
text: Good quality hotel ideally located and staff were very helpful and polite. Breakfast choice is fair but hot food sometimes not very warm however overall we thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Grosvenor.

title: Excellent
text: The hotel was amazing the staff helpful and polite the room spotless. Location perfect. This hotel is 5 mins from Buckingham palace and seconds from Victoria station. Hotel is easy to find. Thoroughly enjoyable time.

title: What a transformation!
text: I stayed here 10 years ago and again 2 weeks ago. What a difference. The magnificent lobby has been returned to its glory and looks amazing. We stayed in one of the refurbished rooms (103) with a big comfy bed and great bathroom.The brasserie is very good and not too pricey and the staff are great. If you need to travel through Victoria,I would thoroughly recommend the Grosvenor

title: Mark W.
text: Hotel was centrally located within walking distance of Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey. Bus service was in front of the Hotel. The room was spacious and clean. The staff was very helpful and friendly. I would stay here again.

title: The great room
text: Had a great night at a charity black tie ball in the great room of the Grosvenor hotel. The tables were set out beautifully and the food was amazing. The serving staff were very helpful and so polite. The drinks were a little expensive but your in London so I expected it.

title: 4.5+ Star Hotel!!
text: We loved this hotel! Just stayed first week in August 2014 for 4 days. The hotel is stunningly beautiful on the outside and inside. Very grand lobby. Our room was very spacious, with two twin beds - very large bathroom. Room was very grand and beautiful - super clean and updated. We would definitely stay here again. The location was at the Grosvenor Victoria, was excellent - beautiful area, close to Buckingham palace, westminster abbey, plus great pubs around the hotel. Very easy to get a taxi and the costs weren't too bad since the hotel was so central to all the areas we toured. Staff was warm and attentive. We had dinner several times in the Lounge & room service, which was quick & delicious. they make a great, huge cappuccinos! Highly recommend this hotel if you're visiting London!

title: Business Trip
text: I stayed at the Grosvenor for one night. The room was very clean, albeit a little small. my room was at the back of the hotel, so there is a lot of ambient noise from the train station, especially early in the morning. The reunion bar is fantastic. The hotel staff are excellent. Hotel is a little pricey, but that's London for you.

title: Pretty good!
text: Pros: - fantastic location - right next to Victoria station - entrance hall is amazing! - staff were all wonderful - breakfast was awesome! - rooms were clean - good wifi Cons: - bathrooms were a little tired, need a bit of TLC - the room we were in overlooked the station, and you could hear the announcements until about midnight and then from about 6.30am (was ok for us as we were up!) - TV was rubbish Overall I would recommend this hotel, only had a couple of minor issues!

title: Great location for Victoria Station
text: Very busy and reception a bit confusing but staff seemed friendly. Room on - no mirror so hair blow drying a challenge. Don't like showeres that are fixed in the ceiling as I wear contact lenses so husband had to hold hand attachment so I could shower!!

title: Location, location, location!
text: Clean rooms, nice service. Most important feature is the easy access to Victoria Station. Since I travel mostly by train in the UK, this made my life so much easier. It is a rather large, maze-like hotel, but worth it. Will stay there again. Beds were very comfy.

title: Wonderful old world building
text: stayed here for 4 nights in May - the foyer is magnificent and truly from another era. Staff were friendly and helpful. If you are an older person or someone who has trouble with stairs, you really need to mention this as some rooms are accessed by many stairs. In my case, staff mentioned I and a few steps to go down - I envisaged 4 or 6 steps. In my views I was confronted with a flight of stairs - unfortunately I had declined the offer of taking my case to the room so had to negotiate down the stairs with a heavy case. Bathrooms have shower over the bath, again an older person may find that difficult. From my room on the 2nd floor (246) when leaving I was faced with 4 flights of stairs to go down or up a flight and along a long passage. For someone younger and fitter none of this would be a bother - I am older and was having problems with my knees during the stay so I did find the stairs a problem. Buffet breakfast, just your average buffet but the food was cold every morning and the orange juice warm. From my room I could hear announcements from the station but this wasn't a bother and certainly later at night with the curtains shut I couldn't hear a thing. A quick walk to Victoria coach station, hop on hop off buses out the front as were other buses. Great location and an easy walk to many other places. Loved the old world charm of the Hotel, although the stairs were a slight problem for me, if I was in the area again I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again.

title: Great Stay
text: This is my second time staying at the Grosvenor and each stay has been great. Hotel is in a great location, very close to Buckingham Palace and right next to Victoria station. Rooms and public areas are very nicely decorated and the breakfast was also very good. Would definitely return to this hotel!

title: good location
text: I booked a single room here for one night including breakfast. I specified a quiet room on a high floor. The single rooms are advertised as spacious and quiet. My room (511), admittedly bigger than the one photographed on their website (bedside table either side of the bed, and a little lobby affair on entering) didn’t particularly have a spacious feel to it although it was by no means the smallest single I’ve stayed in. It was well appointed, with tea/coffee making facility, complimentary bottled water, a decent hairdryer, fab walk in shower (instant hot water) with glass door - no nasty shower curtain, and a heated towel rail that worked. The bed was a small double and very comfy with 2 great pillows. However, traffic noise was very intrusive despite the secondary glazing (My trusty earplugs to the rescue.) – and it was not on the main road either, so where are all these quiet rooms located? Be aware that the fifth floor rooms are in the eaves and so have tiny windows making the room quite dark. I was only staying one night so neither the noise nor the lack of light was vital but for a longer stay it would have bothered me. Breakfast was busy – but a good selection of food. Toast delivery was a bit erratic

title: Refused a room even though we proved we booked it!
text: Booked a double room with an online estate agent, paid for it with Barclay card well in advance, received email conformation for our stay at the Grosvenor, upon arrival we were informed they did not have a room and were asked to leave. How is this for customer service?????????? This has never happened in 29 years of travelling to London every month, except here.

title: A week in London at the Grosvenor hotel
text: My best friend and I decided to cross the North Atlantic on the Queen Mary 2 this past December. Since neither of us had been to England we decided to stay a week in central London before embarking from Southampton on the cruise. Needing a place to stay, a bit of research suggested that the Grosvenor hotel would be a good central location to see some of the sights of London. My travelling partner arrived a day earlier than I did and didn't care for the "deluxe twin room" that we had booked. Rooms in these older hotels are a lot smaller than we would expect in Canada. We were able to book into what must have been the largest suite in the hotel and were very pleased with its amenities. The suite was on the seventh floor and was accessible by its own private elevator. The suite consisted of two relatively large rooms separated by a bathroom with tub and shower and each room had its own thermostat which was a nice touch. If you are heading to London, the Grosvenor is located right at Victoria station, a central transportation hub for buses trains and taxis. There is a convenient shopping mall right there and one can enter the hotel directly from Victoria station without even needing to go outside. One thing is for sure in London. Things are EXPENSIVE! The hotel offered a breakfast buffet with a good selection of food and a really nice touch was the "executive lounge".This facility if open from 5-pm and offers hot appetizers and free liquor. Had lots of other comments but no room.

title: Five Star Service
text: I was very impressed with the service we received from everyone. I was expecting Four star, but it really is Five star. The front desk people, the restaurant staff, the concierge, the doorman, all were exceptional. It's location is ideal for getting anywhere. Buckingham Palace right down the street. Harrods about a mile away. It is on a busy street so be prepared to always encounter tons of people going in and out of your hotel. All tours will pick you up at this hotel. They have a pot that makes hot water in your room, so you can make tea or instant coffee in your room. If you get the cheapest rooms, they will be small and you will have to first take an elevator and then stairs to get to your room. I would not stay in one of those rooms. If you can afford it, I would strongly recommend getting an Executive Level room. The Executive Lounge has a full English breakfast from 6:30-11 every day, and evening drinks and snacks from 5-9 every evening. During the day, you can come grab a soda or Cappuccino at any time. The snacks are decent enough that we would have a big breakfast and late lunch every day and the snacks in the evening. The Executive Lounge staff is outstanding! You will not be disappointed if you get this service. You can also check out with them instead of the front desk. They will order room service for you if you want to eat supper here and drink. Some nits: the shower is only partially obstructed so water splashed on the floor every morning. A local call was 8 pounds to make. I would certainly stay here again. Go to Bag 'o Nails half a block away for their fish-n-chips and a pint of their Carling Lager beer. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Good Hotel in a Central Location
text: First, I'd like to echo all those who came before me: the Grosvenor Hotel is in a great location. It's just a block or two from Buckingham, very walkable to Westminster, and sits right on top of both a train station and an Underground station, and from here you can get to just about any part of the city very easily. It's a huge selling point for this hotel, and we never had any complaints about getting to and from the hotel to where we wanted to go. In fact, since we flew in to Gatwick, the train took us right to the hotel's doorstep. It was all great. We booked a smaller room through their chooseyourroom.com website, last minute, which means the price was good but the room selection was not. But it was fine, as we were out and about for the most part, the only time we really spent any significant time in the room is on the first day when we were both very tired from the trip and wanted to call it an early night. There wasn't a lot of storage options, so most of our clothes remained in the suitcase. We also received complimentary breakfast which was a good selection and nice to receive that for free. In addition, we had late night drinks at the Champagne bar one night, prompt service with good drink selection. Unfortunately didn't get a chance to eat lunch or dinner at the restaurant. Everyone was always very friendly and any question I asked was answered by the staff. We didn't have any major issues but I would have complete confidence in their ability to handle it should something have happened. Free and easy wifi is also nice. The bed was comfortable, but taking a shower often resulted in lots of water on the bathroom floor, as the shower door doesn't even go halfway down. It would be nice if the door blocked more of the water. The towel heating rack was a nice touch, however. Our room overlooked the station and we could occasionally hear the announcements down below, but it never woke us up or kept us from falling asleep.

title: Regular Visitor
text: The most comfortable bed in London? Great hotel for working in Victoria area. Noise from railway station almost inaudible from most rooms and never an issue. Good menu in Brasserie. Highly recommended. I stay every week and am now a Gold Member...with great benefits.

title: Afternoon Tea
text: Newly decorated tea rooms with the theme of travelling first class, the afternoon tea at the Grosvenor is a lovely way to spend an afternoon. The staff at the Grosvenor are incredibly attentive and friendly.

title: You get what you pay for
text: We used London as a base staying at three different hotels. This was the grandest most opulent but based on our room we would put it last. This raises the question.....Is it better value to book the best room in a 3 star hotel or the worst room in a 5 star hotel? We got the latter. As a couple in our late seventies we struggled to get our cases up the flight of stairs just to enter the hotel. After a couple of hours we were given our key and directed to the second floor. They are short staffed and the guy helping with luggage was busier than a one armed wallpaper hanger. On exiting the lift we needed a GPS to find our room in this massive hotel as we made our way with luggage down long corridors. We paced the distance to our room and it was 150 meters. As we approached our room the second floor split in two with a flight of stairs going down and a flight going up. There is a second floor upper and lower. Our room was tiny even by London standards barely larger than the balcony cabin on Pacific Princess. As we looked out the window we saw we overlooked the massive roof of Victoria Station that abutted the hotel. Through a half meter gap we could see folk walking on the concourse below. Right next to our window was a series of maintenance walkways on the roof. We laughed at the notice on the wall advising guests of the danger of walking on the station roof. The public spaces and atrium are jaw dropping and I'm sure Queen Victoria herself would have loved it. We normally have our travel agent book superior rooms and I'm not sure what happened here. So if you intend staying here make sure you cough up for a suite at least. Service was a problem and we overheard a supervisor tear verbal strips off a housekeeper in a way that made us squirm. The poor lady walked past us in tears. We wanted to give her a hug. As we left the hotel we actually met a member of staff who spoke with a native English accent as most staff in London hotels are from other EU countries. Apart from the supervisor mentioned we found them to be delightful and helpful. Remember...You get what you pay for.

title: Lovely ambience
text: Love this hotel as the location is ideal for the stations. Lovely ambience and room was deluxe so nice and spacious. TV sound poor, BBC2 unusable. Vibration felt in the room but did not stop us getting to sleep. Huge comfortable bed. Breakfast was delicious although choice Nora's good as when I stayed there a few years ago. Waitress did not approach us with coffee, had to ask her and she wasn't very friendly. The lady on the desk was much more helpful. I would recommend the hotel as the highs outweigh the lows.

title: View from room was roof of raialway station
text: our travel agent booked this hotel for us. When we arrived we were faced with a lot of steps, if you needed help a sign said ring the bell. Bell was rung 3 times waiting about 10 minutes - no answer. So struggled up stairs with our cased. Checkin then was told we had to get left to 2nd floor and walk about 150 metres then down steps and then another 100 metre walk. Went to window to see outlook it was roof and concourse of railway station. There was a promotional older in the room for dinner in the dining room, tried to take advantage of this offer and was told the offer had expires. Room was small, clean The only way to stay in this hotel is a very costly upmarket room. Location was good if you were using the train.

title: Stay over after the theatre
text: Chose this hotel as it was close to the theatre, it was supposed to be an upgraded room, the AC did not work and we heard Train Announcements for most of the night. Other than that the hotel seemed to be fine

title: 7th birthday trip for my daughter
text: I took my daughter to see Wicked for her birthday and we stayed in the Grosvenor for the night. My daughter was very excited to be staying in such a prestigious hotel. I had emailed the hotel prior to arrival to let them know it was a birthday surprise and they went above and beyond to make it even more special for her. We were upgraded upon arrival and once inside the room there was a knock on the door and my daughter was presented with a birthday plate of macaroons and fruit with chocolate ‘happy birthday’ and a lovely postcard of the hotel with a personalised message from the hotel! She was thrilled! Nothing was too much trouble for the staff and my daughter enjoyed breakfast in bed the next morning! It truly is an beautiful hotel with excellent staff and we will most definitely stay again soon.

title: Great hotel in a great location
text: The hotel is in a great location to visit most of the major sites in central London. It's only a couple minutes walk from Victoria Station in the Underground train network. From that station you can take the Circle or District lines to the Tower of London or Westminster (the same stop for the London Eye) or the Victoria line up to Kennsington. The included breakfasts are well presented with the usual fare and some surprises as well. The staff is very friendly and "politely eager" to help. The rooms were well tended to and the building itself had a classic feel with the typical expected comforts.

title: Great location and nice staff
text: We spent 6 nights here for Christmas 2016. It is ideally located within easy walking distance to Buckingham Palace, Big Ben, the Eye, Hyde park and so many more sights in central London. And it has an entrance in the back to Victoria station. Though our shower wasn't working when we arrived and it was never fixed while we stayed there (I know it was the holiday but 6 nights without a shower to use is a bit much) Overall though the staff were friendly and helpful and the rooms were nice and the hotel is very classic. I have to say again it was an excellent location to get around. Though I also heard the calls from victioria station but it isn't as prevalent on the higher floors. I would recommend this hotel for anyone wanting a nice comfortable stay ideally located for sight seeing.

title: High Tea
text: We enjoyed High Tea in the Park and Library Room. The staff were very courteous and accommodating and we had a lovely view over Hyde Park as the sun set over the fair ground. The atmosphere was enhanced by the wonderful pianist playing gently in the background. our tea was good

title: Perfection
text: Our room was completely spotless and I can't remember the last time I said that about a hotel. They had made a real effort when I told them it was my husbands 30th win cake and wine which was a lovely surprise. We paid for an executive double and I'm glad about that as it felt luxurious despite the very reasonable price as we chose not to include bteakfast, we also asked for a room on the top floors following advice online and the view was lovely. I work in the area but this still felt like a romantic holiday. Loved it, recommend it to everyone and we will be back. Amazing.

title: Lovely
text: We stayed at the Grosvenor during the first leg of our honeymoon, and couldn't have been more pleased. The rooms were comfortable, and the location can't be beaten. But the best part of the place is the wonderful, friendly, helpful staff. Highly recommended.

title: Overwhelming from start to finish
text: From the moment we stepped out of the taxi we were overwhelmed by the grosvenor. Beautiful inside and out. We stayed here overnight for our silver anniversary everyone was helpful and from the check in to the bar where we enjoyed cocktails after a night at the theater watching the lion king. Our room was only a standard double but was beautiful and comfortable. Our bed was the most comfortable I have ever slept on.my only complaint was that I couldn't stay longer. Definitely will be coming back next year for my 50th birthday

title: Nice hotel, clean but WiFi expensive
text: Quite comfortable but bed not as good as Premier Inn. Room very clean, fresh, and good size for a central london hotel. Parking a bonus but £38 / night. WiFi very expensive so use tethering! A little stingy on the milk and sugar in the room. For what it costs they could have put a few more in but luckily there is a Sainsburys Local opposite. Breakfast very expensive so didn't have that although I suspect it is standard for London. (Just went to Sainsbury Local opposite for Croissants and danish for a fraction of the cost :-)

title: Nice location
text: I stayed there for 2 weeks. First I got an upgrade to executive room ( because I have a platinum membership) and the room was small! No wireless Internet but they have a cable which is not free of charge! One more problem was that they have a smocking and non smocking rooms in the same floar and the smell is every where! Location is great, 2 minutes walking to the metro or the park and 12 minutes to Oxford street. It was average but not like any holidayinn I visited.

title: Excellent Value.
text: Paid £159 in advance for a double room on a Saturday night including full buffet breakfasts the following morning. Walk-in rate is £300!!!!!! Hotel modern and clean, staff all polite at all times. Breakfast buffet excellent. Just remember to book in advance. Basement car park £36.10p for 24 hours - great value in London as no congestion charge at the weekend.

title: Unexpected stay
text: Having been sightseeing in London we decided on the spur of the moment to stay the night. Hotel staff were very friendly and the room was a good size with a very comfortable bed. We had a drink in the bar on arrival. Can not comment on dinner as we ate out but breakfast was very good and again staff very good. A special thank you to the duty manager who found us a phone charger to borrow. Would we come back oh yes.

title: Great Location (Oxford Street and Tube Stations)
text: I returned to the Holiday Inn Regents park and this time around it was a 10 day stay (as opposed to the 2 days stay previously). Continue to be impressed with the location / proximity to Oxford Street, Regent Street, Soho etc and tube stations. I was originally allocated a room on the 5th floor and when I complained about how small the rooms were, I was offered a room on the 3rd floor (old executive floor) and was informed this floor had free water and a couple of other freebies. I would recommend checking the location of the room before accepting it as there are many rooms and some of them can be a very long walk from the elevator.

title: Don't book a standard room
text: Stayed at this hotel for 3 nights Booked with lastminute and when i arrived I was asked to pay for the room however trying to explain to duty manager it as pre paid was difficult and this took ages. The check in was poor not even polite and when I said no offers of wake up calls or newpapers which I know is a standard at holiday inns they just looked at Me The room was small and the bathroom so small u could not turn around in it and at a cost of 500 for 3 nights it's not good I spoke to staff the following morning and in all fairness I was upgraded This hotel is overpriced for the rooms you get as they are even smaller than the St giles but at least that is cheaper and service standards are higher As an ihg reward member this compared to other holiday inn is not as good

title: Great hotel - clean and tidy
text: great hotel - quiet location yet close to tube station and withn easy walk of oxford street. Breakfast was buffet style and a good selection. Room a little on the Small size but clean, tidy and warm yet had air con if needed.

title: Very Pleasant Stay
text: I stayed at the Holiday Inn, London Regents Park for one night on business. The hotel is ideally located being only a couple of stops on the underground from Kings Cross/St Pancras and then a short walk to the hotel. It is also only a short stroll from Oxford Street. I stayed in a standard room on the 4th floor (Room 456). The room was a good size for central London and had a comfy double bed, desk area, tv, tea and coffee making facilities, safe, hairdryer, iron and ironing board and a small table and arm chair. Plenty of wardrobe space is available and the room is finished with a full length mirror. The bathroom is compact but fully functional. The power shower was very refreshing and complimentary toiletries are available. The bathroom is lit with spotlights. This coupled with the large mirror makes it ideal for applying make up. I didn't eat dinner in the hotel but did have breakfast there. The restaurant is on the 1st floor and you have a choice of the usual cereals, bread, fruit and also cooked breakfast options. You can also order poached eggs and omelettes to be cooked to order. The food was well presented and hot. The staff were all very attentive and I would happily stay at this hotel again.

title: worth the price
text: first time we have stopped in a Holiday Inn in London, it was very good value for money. There was everything you needed except there was no main ceiling light so although there were quite a few side lamps , none were very bright and I found I struggled to see in the mirror, also the bathroom was compact. However the staff were all excellent, nothing was to much trouble, the room was immaculately clean and the fridge to use for your own food was a lovely thought

title: it's not 4 star !!!
text: hii, we, me and my colleagues, stay in this hotel for exebition on may 09 for a week. the hotel is located at the best place near to oxfort street and near by there is a lot of bars and resturants. but.... the rooms are all same and very very samll !!! we can't even moov in the room in the same time. the brakefast was very standart. the price for internet are 15 pound for 24 h.... the service in the lobby is not frandly and thay don't help you to get a place for the evening....the taxi drivers help you a lot more... search another hotel to stay in london !!!!

title: Great location!
text: A well situated hotel near to tube & beautiful Regents park. We had an executive room, clean, very comfortable & with air conditioning which was most welcome! Friendly staff & a good breakfast

title: Very expensive Wifi, poor service.
text: When local coffee shops offer free Wifi I don't expect to pay £70 a weeks for Wifi when paying to stay in an Executive room. This is what some people might call rip off London. The exec room was much smaller than some of the other hotels locally and service was very poor. I had to queue twice to leave a case for later collection -if you don't do this via reception a poster of note on the desk explaining the process would help. When I went to collect it I had to ask for it twice before anyone bothered to get it for me. Nothing will induce me to return and I've now booked my next two trips with another chain.

title: Perfect!!
text: I stayed here in July with my sister while we were on a girl's trip to London and we both agreed that it was one of the nicest hotels we'd ever stayed at! The place was well laid out and easy to navigate, the rooms were really comfy and the staff (usually the biggest let down of hotels) were SO NICE! Staff were always checking on how we were doing whenever we passed, were more than happy to help with any questions (and were angels for accepting our delivery take aways and bringing up to us)! It's a really nice location - and the BT tower being so nearby made it so much easier to navigate back to when we got lost! The rooms were really swish and having control of the heating and air con was nice! I've found in the past that Holiday Inns are usually pretty noisy but, considering how busy this one was, the rooms seemed miraculously sound proof! Only down side was that we had to go home again! Definitely going to choose this place again next time I visit!!

title: Return Visit - Unrivalled Evening Meals
text: I stayed at this hotel for a whole week and it was most enjoyable. The food in the restaurant is just heavenly. I had some fish dishes, vegetable dishes but the best were the delicious curries made by an Indian chef in the restaurant whose name is Mohandas. All the curries were truly authentic, bringing back memories of the home made curries I used to have in my childhood. Mohandas uses the finest spices, herbs and each meal is made according to your individual taste. If you have an allergy, Mohandas takes every care to make his guests truly authentic meals free from any ingredient that causes allergy. It is worth booking a room and enjoy your evening meal at a reasonable price surpassing some very expensive local restaurants. If you are bringing a group of friends it is well worth alerting Mohandas in advance as he makes sure that your dinner becomes a memory to treasure.

title: Good hotel with a comfy bed in a great location - near to regents park and soho
text: We had a great stay at this hotel. Room nice and clean with all basic facilities and for location priced pretty well compared to many other nearby hotels. Plenty of tube stops nearby and frequent black cabs into the city. Great for a weekend away. Good comfy bed too and no real noise as off the main road. Staff friendly and helpful and left luggage service available. Were able to check in early at no extra cost as room ready. Definately worth paying that little extra over a travelodge. The hotel is just round the corner from Regents Park and Radio One and close to all main train stations.

title: Friendly
text: The Hotel was in a very good position for our weekend in London. Very close to the tube with easy routes to where we wanted. The hotel staff were friendly and very helpful. the room was adequate for what we wanted. Only complaint is that there is never enough tea, milk and sugars.

title: Theatre break
text: Great hotel very friendly staff always doing their best to help. Room was very clean, not huge but the bathroom was very tiny. This is not really an issue as everything else in the hotel is first class. The breakfast was great, a very well set up buffet all food fresh and kept hot and once again the staff very focused and help full.

title: Unfortunately disappointed this second visit
text: This was my second time staying at the Holiday Inn London - Regent's Park. The last time was for business and this time for pleasure with my wife. My previous stay experience was excellent but I am sorry to report that the current standard room did not measure up to the room provided during my business stay. My wife and I were very disappointed. The room interior was old and somewhat worn…especially the bathroom. The lobby, restaurant and common areas have been upgraded but apparently some rooms need to be refurbished. Hopefully the hotel management will recognize this and make the upgrades soon.

title: One night stay
text: My wife and I stayed here for one night the (5th of April ),the location is central and close to very good transport links. Check in and out was very quick and the staff were very friendly. The room was London average and a little bit tatty, damaged lampshade , chips and scratches on the woodwork though more importantly the room was was clean. The bed was comfortable and we had a good nights sleep.We are not sure if it was a language issue but I think we were told that because we booked the room through last minute dot com and we only paid £80 (as it was a mystery room ) we would have to have the disabled room because the rest of the hotel was fully booked.the car park was pretty empty for a fully booked hotel, mentioning the car park it's just over £36 for twenty four hours . To sum up relaxing break hotel good, still not sure if because we had a deal we had a lesser room?( though it did remind me of the comedy sketch "what sort of a hotel is this." Answer "a fully booked one sir"

title: Good for an overnighter
text: Hotel is conveniently located just a few hundred metres from a couple of Tube Stations in a nice quiet area. There are a few good bars and restaurants within a very short walk. The room was nice and clean although the shower was not up to expected standard in my room. Breakfast was excellent and all the staff were really friendly and helpful. I'd definitely stay here again.

title: Great Location
text: Stayed here on st Patrick's weekend. Very pleasant staff who were very helpful. It was very nice inside and food was good too. We had room service for lunch one day. The location is so central with multiple tube stations nearby. I will say to beware that parking is no included in the price or even a discount. I was quoted 120£ for 2 days. Best to arrange an alternative or use public transport.

title: Location and staff good, rooms average
text: This hotel was chosen for its location and availability on BA website using Avios points. If you're visiting Central London this is a superb location - 5 mins walk to Oxford Circus and Regent's Park, but in a fairly quiet residential area with some nice cafes and bars close by. Also fairly near 4 or 5 tube stations on several different lines, so easy to get around. We stayed for one night as a family (me, wife and 3 year old). The hotel is, as you can see from the pictures, a 1970's bunker but it's fine inside. The reception area, restaurant and bar are of standard modern decor, some of the corridors on the upper floors are a bit tatty. There was a problem with our room allocation - we had called the hotel to specifically ask if our room was suitable for 3 people, and had been assured that while most of the rooms were small, we had a larger room allocated to us which could accommodate an extra bed. The room we got was not big enough for 3 people. On asking at reception, they were baffled as to why we had been told about being allocated a larger room. Finally they offered us one of the 'accessible' rooms designed for wheelchair users (no 407) - it was much bigger and was fine. A lot of messing about though! The room itself was fine, quite new and clean. Aircon seemed to work, windows opened too, and noise was not a problem (apart from a few rowdy guests across the corridor). The bathroom was huge - but standard rooms have tiny bathrooms as we witnessed from our initial room allocation. Good choice of TV channels, but we only 'watched' CBeebies ! A very nice lady set up our extra bed which was comfortable enough, as was the main bed in the room. Unfortunately the fire alarm went off at about 9pm, and we had to evacuate ! Luckily it was not cold or raining, and we only had to stand outside for about 30 minutes. Staff seemed to have everything under control. As usual, it was a false alarm and there were no further incidents. In the morning, the shower was a bit feeble but was at least warm. The bathroom was spotless. Breakfast in the morning was very good - it was extremely busy but we were seated quickly and the choice and quality were great. Waiting staff were very efficient and friendly, as were staff overall. We checked out with a minimum of fuss, and the hotel was happy to store our luggage for the day. I would gladly stay again if in the area, and if I could get a good rate online or using airmiles.

title: Small room ok for a night but not a holiday hotel
text: Room clean and good location for hotel but shabby small bedroom, huge crack in bathroom sink and bathroom small as you could get

title: In the Executive Room 626
text: My wife wanted to do some shopping in Regent Street and Bond Street while I visited my taylor. We decided to stay at the Holiday Inn, Regents Park. It was just 5 minutes walk to the main shops. We travelled by car to the hotel and it was a little difficult finding the hotel with all the one way streets around this area. I'm a disabled driver and although I asked for a "Disabled Parking Space" there are only 2 spaces immediately outside unless you park in the street on yellow lines. Staff were very helpful and friendly. Our room was on the top floor, nice and quiet with complimentary WiFi for 2 devices. The bed was the best we have ever slept in as far as hotels go. The Bathroom was clean and bright. Breakfast the next morning was brilliant. We then wished we had booked for a few more nights. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at this hotel in the centre of London. Next time.

title: Decent location, clean and comfortable room
text: We stayed at HI Regent's Park on a Saturday night, the hotel is clean and comfortable and very quiet so a very good nights sleep. It's In a good location near Regent's Park but still only 15/20mins walk to Oxford street and Soho. The room rate was a bit lower than some hotels claiming to be closer to the action but the same walking time in reality. There was free wifi if decent quality.

title: I wouldn't recommend
text: <in my previousl 4 tripadvisor hotel reviews, I gave 3 times 5 stars and 1 time 4 stars> My wife and I stayed in the Holiday Inn Regent Park hotel between the 4-8/6/2008. We have encountered numerous times when we were told false information by the staff: 1. we asked for a double bed room via email and got confirmation. When we got there, no double bed room was available. 2. The receptionist (named Jude) told us that this is only temporary and someone will move our belonging to another room with double bed, the next morning, while we are out travelling. This was not done. 3. We asked for a wakeup call at 7:30 and received it 20 minutes later. We complain and were told that the wake up list says 7:50. 4. the concierge told us that all events start at 11:00 on Sundays, which is simply not true. On the other side, John, the receptionist was really nice, professional and helpful. I'm describing this as this seems like a pattern, and not a random mistake. We saw another complain earlier in the reviews and wondered about the odds that this will happen to us. Well...it just did. Besides that the hotel location is great. Only 100m from the tube, tesco and pret a manger. In addition, if you go to this hotel, 50m north to the hotel, there is a construction site. We haven't stayed in a north room, so we're not sure about the noise coming from this site, but this should also take under consideration. In addition, the hotel is very clean (so say my wife) and provide all the needed facilities - safe in the room, minibar (cost money), TV (not LCD), playstation (cost money), ok bed and shower. All in all, I wouldn't recommend going to this hotel, just because the problems we had with 3 out of 4 staff members.

title: Great Breakfasts!
text: Stayed over Jubilee weekend with my daughter for a theatre break, birthday treat. Having read numerous negative reviews I was a bit apprehensive, but was pleasantly surprised

title: Good location
text: The location of this hotel is great, it is easily accessible to lots of London attractions, the breakfast is very nice and staff are friendly, the rooms are nice but we did have a broken window handle and there was limescale in the bathroom and I think our room did need painting over, i'm not too sure on hotel prices in this area as we had our hotel booked for us as my husband was donating stem cells near the area but the room price did seem quite expensive for what you get, however again it is a fantastic location

title: Couldnt believe how badly we were treated
text: Booked 2 nights stay in double room for my husband and I as a birthday treat. We left our children with family and looked forward to the 2 day break . On arrival we were given a twin room. When I requested a move to a double room, after a long wait, was told it wasn't possible, hotel was full and no apology was given. Asked to speak to mananger/supervisor, after a wait spoke to supervisor, repeated the story to her again she said she could do nothing, and still not apology for their error. After some time she suggested a free drink at the bar , after some time again she suggested upgrading us to the "Executive Package". We moved rooms the following day and did not get either the free drink or executive package. Contacted reception again and explained the whole story again after which they sent up to our room the following: 2 bottles of water, one kit/kat, one Bathrobe, one pair of slippers and some bathroom shampoo and sewing kit. It could all have been sorted out by a proper apology at the beginning, we just wanted to be treated as customers who had paid for a service that we had not recieved.

title: Quiet location but handy for West End
text: We were given this 2 night break by my Father for a xmas present who booked it via Saga and managed to get a superb deal. If we had payed full price then this hotel is expensive, nonetheless it was very close (2 tube stops) to the West End. The area around the hotel is quiet but there are a few nice restaurants and pubs in the vicinity. We also enjoyed a walk in Regents Park which is close by. The breakfast was really good, excellent choice of cooked and cereal. A great weekend in central London and we hope to return.

title: Quality and courtesy
text: The staff was very friendly and courteous. The hotel in the whole was very clean, comfortable and very close to the tube station. The area was quiet and easy to reach from the city centre, just fifteen minutes walking to Picadilly Circus. I will come back soon.

title: Hidden gem in central London
text: I stay regularly at this hotel and am made to feel very welcome and its easy to unwind

title: Average holiday inn
text: The hotel is only a 10 min walk away from Oxford street and other attractions so its location is good As an ihg member wifi was free and if you do decide to stay just join at reception I had an executive room and although it was clean it was smaller than most other holiday inns My initial room had no TV working and when I rang down it took them 11 times to answer the phone which is an issue I have raised before The front of house manager came to check the TV and I asked him to try his own reception to get an answer it was so good that he rang twice and could not get a reply He is in charge of this or maybe the general manager maybe they will give another excuse on the reply to this The hotel is not as friendly as many other holiday inns and although I don't think this is the fault of the staff it could just be the layout of the hotel I would return again but hope they improve customer service

title: Comfortable stay
text: Stayed here overnight as my 1st choice was fully booked, however after staying here I may have to change my allegiance. Hassle free stay. Executive room was spotlessly clean as was the bathroom. Even though I had a front facing room it was very quiet both inside and outside the hotel. Didn't eat in the restaurant in the evening but breakfast was excellent, food well presented and the cooked food was hot. Check in and out very easy thanks to front desk team (Stefan and the lady who checked me in - sorry can't remember he name) who were very friendly and cheerful. Would not hesitate to stay here again

title: Unexpected issues for a 4-stars hotel.
text: We stayed in the Holiday Inn Regent's Park for one night in December. The standard rate for our room is £305/night and this review is written with this price in mind. First, I'll pass on the petty but usual issues: no free Wi-Fi and the £15 breakfast (and that's only if one pre-books). Next, while the room in itself was fine (short of the mini-bar being locked, which was weird), the bathroom had some real issues. First, it was really cramped: fine for one person but impossible for two. Second, the toilet brush was missing. Third, the toilet seat was cracked. Someone had tried to fix it with glue, but was unsuccessful. The net result was that every time one of us sat up, the crack would pinch our buttocks' skin. Ouch! We checked in late, so we did not report the issue until checkout time. At this time we were offered a free breakfast as compensation, which was nice and unexpected, but at this time we really to go. The location is quite convenient so I might stay again, but certainly not at the official price...

title: Pretty good came to see a football match
text: Hey, So that's my 2nd time first time was a romantic vacation 6 years ago +- and was very good. and i have promised i would come back when i have had a chance to. So i did this time with a friend and to a two singles room. If you are a cell phone junkie before going to sleep there are no charge spots around the bed so you would have a problem. room was a bit small as well breakfast was pretty good like in the past even though i remember that in my first time there were actually cereal boxes all over. why there are no some sliced vegetables for breakfast i am not a vegan but that's the a better option for them i am sure you have some vegan clients. oh there is a free Wi-Fi. hope for a better visit next time.

title: Great hotel, location and price!
text: After reading many negative reviews I began to regret booking this hotel for a weekend away with my husband. However on arrival I was pleasantly surprised. The hotel was large and modern with polite and helpful staff. We were upgraded to an executive room and I have no complaints - the air con worked, the bathroom was clean, the shower was superb and the bed was nice and comfy. We had managed to secure a fantastic rate - £105 for 2 nights room only - and I believe this hotel was more than worth this. We were offered breakfast and when we declined there was no problem. Great Portand Street tube station is only yards away and a walk to Oxford Street is only about 10 minutes. Well done Holiday Inn!!

title: Great Stay
text: Stayed at the Holiday Inn, Regents Park for the weekend. Nice room very clean and modern. My Sister forgot her toothbrush and two were promptly put in our room at no extra charge. A card has to be presented and number taken in case there were extras bought. The first morning we were going out early so were given a breakfast in a bag which consisted of 3 croussants, a babybel, apple plus butter and jam a bottle of water, strangely glass, but all were acceptable. The next morning we had the normal breakfast there was a lot of choice and the staff were very friendly and helpful. I would recommend this hotel and if I make the trip again I will stay here, good location we walked to Oxford Street and the theatre lovely hotel.

title: Great hotel
text: I stayed in this hotel a few times already so I guess it says it all. it is just right. nice friendly staff, decent rooms, great location close to the tube and minutes away from the center. great for value.

title: Great last minute choice
text: We had rented an apartment in London which fell through literally as we were arriving in the city. This hotel was around the corner so we thought we'd take a chance and see if they had anything open, and were pleasantly surprised that they had 2 rooms available for us at a very reasonable rate. I also have to say that the front desk staff were extremely helpful and welcoming when we suddenly appeared in front of them in a complete panic. They even had the concierge take us upstairs and show us rooms, then agreed to hold the rooms for us while we figured out what to do. This was excellent service, they really went out of their way to help us. The rooms were not large, but very comfortable, clean, seemed recently renovated, and had everything we needed. Yes, wifi had a charge, and the breakfast was expensive (we only went there on Sunday because not much else was open), but this is central London. I feel we got good value, comfort, and an unexpectedly high level of service.

title: I would say is a 3.5 stars rather than 4
text: Very close to Great Portland Street underground station. About one km from Oxford street in a quiet part of downtown London. Rooms are spacious and modern. Safe included and boiler to make a tea and cups is available. Refrigerator included but is empty. Room service prices are quite high. Bathroom is modern, only shampoo and soap provided. TV in room. Heating knob regulation is located by the radiator, however our's was not working properly. AC is located separately in a control on the wall. An office building is located directly across the street so they could peak in our room in the morning. Don't walk around naked unless you are an exhibitionist. Lobby area not that big, but still OK. Breakfast area was suitable and comfy and breakfast was rather good. Only cheese was not offered, but we felt quite full from the variety. I would rate it as a 3.5 stars rather than 4. Overall it was a comfortable stay. Not much of common areas. Lobby is rather limited.

title: Great hotel, great location
text: Just returned from a 4 nights stay at the Holiday Inn Regents Park. The hotel was recently refurbished so it was nice to walk into a hotel that wasn't falling apart. Our room was extremely clean with a queen size bed, desk, tv, coffee area, closet, and bathroom. I will say the room was a bit small for the 2 of us -- but we're used to small European hotels. The benefit of this hotel is definitely the location. It is literally a 2 minute walk (1 block) to the Great Portland Street Underground Station. There are also a host of buses within a short walk from the hotel. We definitely had no problem getting around. My only warning is if you do not have your breakfast included in your rate, do NOT eat at the hotel. The breakfast buffet is 15 pounds per person! Don't get me wrong, the food is good, just not really worth the price -- especially when it converts to about 30 US. There's a great cafe right by the Underground station (Cafe Meze) that serves a full English breakfast for 4.95. There is also a pub right nearby (can't remember the name) that serves a great lunch or dinner for a reasonable price. Overall, I would definitely stay at this hotel again. The rooms could be bigger, but we didn't spend all that much time in it anyway.

title: Standard rooms but excellent service
text: The hotel was fully booked and had not upgraded the room as expected but the staff went out of their way to apologise and look after me once checked in. The rooms are very small and standard size for London, nothing special but the service is very good. Well located hotel and great bar for meeting with friends.

title: Business trip
text: Stayed here while on business in London. Location is great but would agree with other posters that it is a 3* hotel. Room was fine. My main issue was the wifi costs - £16 for 24 hours and very poor quality (v slow).

title: Expensive for what you get
text: Clean and tidy but not the best of places. quite small rooms and a bit dated. location is good for Tube and Regents Park area / Euston Station Conference facilities were quite good. The bathroom was a little small as well, shower being an above the bath job with the head fastened to the fittings so it was impossible to shower effectively.

title: Clean and good service but serves a purpose as a business hotel
text: I have stayed here many times for business, all without problems or need for complaint. The rooms are of a good size and breakfast is also pleasant but it doesn't offer any added value. Where as I don't expect bells and whistles in every hotel I stay in, for the money, so additional luxuries would be nice. I would stay again as the location of the hotel is excellent to get to the regents park area.

title: Consistently Delivers The Goods
text: We've stayed here on countless occasions through our jobs over the years and it always comes up trumps. We were relieved to find that our recent stay was on a par with other stays. The location is outstanding. You are within walking distance of some of London's most famous attractions - Oxford Street, Regent's Park, China Town, etc (Cafe PT in Wardour Street is without doubt the best Chinese restaurant in the area - you MUST try the bubble tea!!). The hotel is close to most major tube lines. If you want to avoid the crush of Oxford Street, we would recommend walking to either Great Portland Street, Goodge Street or Warren Street stations (unless you really need a line that these stations don't cover of course!). Can't comment on the food at the hotel, but there are some excellent little restaurants and cafes down the side streets in the area (I love the "Ultimate Bacon Roll" from Kiko's Cafe in nearby Clipstone Street!). Very clean and highly recommended.

title: APPALLING CHRISTMAS LUNCH
text: My wife and I attended a club Christmas lunch at the Holiday Inn, Regents Park, and paid £27 a head despite the event being heavily subsidised. This price included a main course (turkey or lamb), a dessert (crême caramel or Christmas pudding), a mince pie and a small chocolate with four bottles of wine between ten people. The main course was one of the worst meals I have ever eaten! The turkey was overcooked and came in slices a quarter of an inch thick . I almost choked on one of these slabs. The potatoes and vegetables were overcooked and barely warm. Whilst I appreciate that providing food simultaneously for 100 plus people may well affect the overall quality, chefs manage to do it perfectly well at every meal, every day for hundreds and sometimes thousands of people on cruise ships. Had this appalling dish been served in any restaurant in London, they would be out of business in a couple of months. My wife, however, said the lamb was 'quite tasty' and 'not too tough' (a year ago it was so tough it was inedible). The rest of the meal was good. The individual Christmas puddings were succulent and tasty, the mince pies were ... well, average mince pies and the chocolates were... well, small and probably the cheapest available chocolates wrapped in gold foil . Thankfully, the meal did not detract from the enjoyment of the occasion, which emanated from meeting former colleagues and friends rather than the hotel's input. I cannot vouch for the quality of food served in the hotel's main restaurant, but any company or organisation considering a lunch or dinner for a large number of people would be well advised to think carefully.

title: Clean and comfortable.
text: We stayed overnight after attending a wedding at Marylebone and the reception was held in the hotel. We had an enjoyable time and the staff were friendly and helpful. We had a discounted room because we were relatives of the bride and groom. The room used for the wedding breakfast was very well set up and there was plenty of room to accommodate all the guests. Breakfast was good, with plenty of variety.

title: Weekend Away
text: My wife and I had a weekend in London recently and needed a Central London Hotel. For the price this place is excellent, nice clean hotel, friendly staff, nice restaurant, buffet breakfast was good and an underground car park if needed.It is easy to find , just off the A40 at Great Portland St Tube Station. There are also local amenities :- nearby tube station, Sainsburys on the corner and numerous cafes. Alot of people have complained about thin walls and cramped rooms. We didn't notice any significant issues. If you want to pay double the price then you you may get a bit more for your money. For us this place was more then sufficient. There were also alot of families staying at the hotel so the family rooms should be ok also.

title: Not worth the money, and watch out for the elevator
text: My husband and I booked this hotel after a good experience the night before at another Holiday Inn in Nottingham. We asked them to book us a Holiday inn near the St Pancras station as we had a very early Train to catch the next morning. The price was very expensive at 160 pounds, but we thought it would be at least as nice as the one we stayed in, so it wouldn't be too bad. And it was London...We were wrong! They got the booking wrong and had us in a twin room, (happened a few times on our trip so no worries) Rang them and we had to go back down and get another key, we ended up with a room (604 I think), which shared a wall with the smaller elevator which was the noisiest elevator I have ever heard. We went down for dinner on the town and got in the large elevator, very scarey, moved and shaked all over the place, and didn't use it again! We came back for an early night, as we lay down we heard the elevator groaning and creaking so loudly we lay there for the next three ours until it finally stopped being used. We wanted to call and complain but we were so tired we didn't want to think about moving everything to another room. We were glad it wasn't a Saturday night and it didn't go all night! We'd booked a wake up call and asked to book a taxi for us, but that ended up being a "transfer" to the station which was a flat rate about 10 pounds more than the taxi fare was (because he had the meter running!), which they told us when we were downstairs and it was already there. Felt very ripped off. I assume there was a cost to book a taxi, but not that much! The room itself was very old and worn out really, carpets were lifting and stretched so they moved when we wheeled the suitcase over it, everything needed a tidy up. We should have looked ourselves and got a backpackers for about the same quality but cost much less. This hotel was the worst one (in value for money terms) in our 4 week trip but also the most expensive and we stayed in everything from a backpackers in Singapore to the Sheraton in Edinburgh! If it was about 100 pounds I probably wouldn't mind so much but when they're charging that price, it's not worth it.

title: Wife's Birthday Trip
text: Used my points to give my good lady if and I a few days in London to do the basic Touristy type thing. The staff as always, were very good and friendly and made us feel very welcome, (even though we weren't paying them) The room was clean and comfortable, and most importantly, very quiet. That said, it was probably the smallest Holiday Inn room I have ever stayed in. I didn't use any go the facilities like the restaurant etc as we dined out every day. A further small niggle was that I get free Wi Fi as an IHG member, but they withdrew the facility before I had checked out which was very slightly annoying if I was honest.

title: A second home
text: My wife, daughter and sister (40,12,26) just returned this morning from London. This is my wife's 3rd visit to this hotel. Once she found this hotel it became the first and only selection in London. It is clean and have a great location. In addition to that, Unfortunately, on this trip, we had to check the warmness of the personnel as for my daughter became sick (no relation to the hotel…). We received all the help we needed and far more. Especially we can point Mr. Anil Umrit as our great helper. Counting the hours to the next visit of this hotel.

title: Good location, very pleasant staff
text: We stayed for three nights during very hot summer weather - the air con was a blessing! Good location, handy for Oxford Street. Clean room, excellent choice of breakfast. Staff were very pleasant and helpful. Lots of restaurants nearby.

title: A good central London Holiday Inn
text: I tend to stay in Holiday Inn's on business as you know what to expect but this is not the case in London where the standards can vary. This hotel is really good and has especially friendly and helpful staff. It's in a very good location next to a tube station and 15 minutes walk to Oxford Street. Only downside is rooms are a bit on the small side but comfortable. Food is good as is the service, However, breakfast can be very busy. I've stayed here often and on one occasion had to leave 10 minutes after I checked in due to an emergency at home. I would have expected them to charge (it was at 7pm) but the receptionist didn't which was a really nice gesture.

title: business trip
text: Costing over £650 for 3 nights, this 4 star??? hotel certainly disappoints. Rooms are small and barely furnished and the bathroom was so minute you could hardly get into it. WiFi was chargeable!!! - ridiculous given the cost of the rooms.. I left the hotel and returned home to discover my i phone charger had been left behind - when I rang they said it was not handed in by cleaning staff!!?? suggest they need to have a word about this as I definitely left it there.............. so be careful with belongings. Staff very indifferent and unhelpful in the main. will try to avoid this hotel in future

title: I liked this hotel
text: First of all, let me thank all those who make their contributions on tripadvisor because I booked a single room with the Holiday Inn Regent's Park based on the previously submitted reviews I read. I had to have a stop over in London due to jet lag and I did not want to fly all night long, so I was happy to make a reservation with Holiday Inn Regent's Park. Though the room I got was rather small, it was well equipped, absolutely clean and offered me all what I needed, especially a very comfortable bed you may wish to see from my photos. Provided for free by the hotel a welcoming bottle of sparkling water was awaiting for me on the working desk, tea and coffee making facilities were at my disposal, too. I spent the evening walking along Oxford street that could be reached by walk in 15-20 minutes. These days London experienced very heavy fog, I worried about my next flight from Heathrow

title: Can Location
text: One night stay to see Ed Sheeran at Wembley. Few stops down from Liverpool Street, few stops up from Wembley Park. 24 hour tube and five minutes walk from the tube station. Reasonable breakfast. Helpful staff. What is not to like.

title: Nice Hotel in Central London
text: The hotel is close to Regent's Park and a few underground stations, which is a nice neighborhood if you are travelling in London. You could also walk for 10 minutes and get to Oxford Street to go shopping. The hotel itself is small, but considering that it is London, you would appreciate the fact that they have a generous lobby and relatively big room. The bathroom is very clean, with plenty of towels. Stuff like shampoo and toothpaste is also provided daily. The TV is small and old, though. There was no view from my hotel room, and I don't think the view would be great anyway... There is a small Sainsbury store right downstairs, so if you'd like something to eat or drink , it is convenient. A breakfast was included in my room rate, but I woke up super late because of the jet lag, so too bad I didn't get to eat it... Overall it is a hotel great for solo travellers, friends travelling and business.

title: A decent hotel if you get an online price
text: Myself and my partner stayed here for 4 nights recently, as a theatre trip to London for my partners birthday. Overall the hotel is clean, well decorated and staff are friendly. They will try and accommodate any request you have and were very helpful. We were in one of the executive rooms, on the 6th floor (room 631) with street views. It was quiet, clean and tidy with good decoration and was spacious enough for two people to "live" in without being on top of each other. The bed was noted as a double, but seemed more spacious than a normal double. I would say the only 3 (small) negative remarks we have about the hotel are: 1) the door to the room didn't open all the way, which meant getting luggage in and out was difficult. It was also difficult for room service to get in and out with trays of food. 2) The water pressure in the shower is non-existent. It was like showering under a dripping tap, rather than a shower. 3) The mini-fridge in the room is weight sensitive, so you can't store anything else in it to keep it cool. This was somewhat disappointing as a lot of hotels now have fridge space for you to keep drinks/snacks cold. In terms of furniture and layout, we had: a very spacious wardrobe (in the vestibule area), with lots of hanging space and cupboards and right next to it a mini fridge with snacks and drinks. Then you go into the main room and there was a very large double bed, a comfy chair with coffee table, an office desk and office chair, two bed side tables, 2 bedside lamps and a TV. The bathroom was small but adequate with enough space to store our toiletries. One nice feature of the executive rooms is that each day they give you 2 free bottles of water and 1 free candy bar (KitKat chunky). A nice suggestions ma be to find out what type of water your guests like. We could only ever use one of the bottles as we don't like sparkling water. The breakfast was not bad. It cost £9.99 per person if you booked in advance, or (I think) £14 if you turned up on the morning and wanted breakfast. Honestly, for the price, in London, you couldn't really go anywhere else and spend less than that. The food was typical hotel breakfast food, but not bad. Hot buffet of the usual eggs, bacon, sausage, has browns, mushrooms, beans and tomatoes. Cold selection of cheese, meats, fruit and yoghurt. There was various breads, toast and pancakes (which you make yourself). There was also a good selection of cereals, fruit juices and hot drinks. I will also say that one morning when we turned up late (we mixed up the weekday/weekend times) they accommodated us as best they could and brought out some of the food that they had started to clear away, so that we could still eat. We really appreciated that. The hotel is a 5 minute walk from the local tube station. Across the road from the hotel (2 min walk) there is a sainsbury for snacks, etc. Sainsbury also leads onto the main road area which has various places to eat, Starbucks, etc. There are always cabs available around the hotel or on the nearby street, so it's easy to hail one down. You're also a 5-10 minute walk from the start of Regents Park, which is you carry on up for another 20 minutes, takes you to ZSL London Zoo. We paid around £800 for 4 nights including breakfast and we booked online, through the Holiday Inn website. One tip though, always book online, never just turn up and book. The "rack rates" for just turning up, were £450 per night for the executive room that we were in, so we saved around £1000 just by booking online. Everyone has a smart phone these days, so even if you were stuck in London and needed a hotel then and there, you're better off whipping out your phone, booking online and then walking into the hotel. You'll save yourself a lot of money. Overall, this was a good hotel, decently priced for London, good location with good transport connections and we would definitely stay here again.

title: Good food, courteous and friendly staff, good location
text: Spent one night here as part of a Newmarket Holidays trip to Olympia. Room was clean and spacious. Appreciated the choice of pillows. Warm shower and good toiletries provided. Breakfast was excellent and the staff very pleasant. Our guide was given our room keys earlier in the day so we didn't have to queue up on our arrival after the show (at around midnight) which was much appreciated. Our only criticism, which is a serious one, is that only one lift out of three was working which necessitated us walking down several flights of stairs carrying cases the next morning in order not to be late for the coach as the hotel was very full.

title: Overnight delight
text: We could not fault our recent overnight stay at this hotel from reception to breakfast all first class, except for the teapot poured badly! There was even a choice of pillows and the hotel is so local for the West End.we would go there again

title: Reasonable for Central London
text: I stay in London on business fairly regularly and I use this place occasionally if its rates are decent. I like the location. It's very close (next door!) to the BT Tower and just set back of the main roads so not too noisy. The rooms are fairly basic and the bathrooms a little tired, but I find the staff generally helpful and breakfast good.

title: Great Location
text: My sister and I stayed here at the weekend for one night. We were visiting London , sightseeing and shopping. We have stayed here before and have found this hotel an ideal location. The reception staff are very friendly, helpful and efficient. Rooms are clean and comfortable . We liked that you could open the window slightly to allow for fresh air - which in a lot of hotels you generally can’t do. The bathroom was on the small side but adequate with nice fresh towels and a selection of toiletries. Breakfast was excellent. We were greeted by lovely staff who were friendly and very welcoming. Lovely selection of hot food and continental choices. We especially love the pancake machine! We are already planning our next stay.

title: London again
text: Initially we had difficulties with our booking but this was more attributable, I think, to the booking agent Expedia, rather than the hotel. Anyway by way of apology the hotel's reservations manager upgraded us to an an executive room - a gesture that was greatly appreciated. My only grouse was that the only way I could make telephone contact with the hotel was by using a premium rate number. Otherwise we were very pleased with our accommodation. Our room was clean and comfortable, had complimentary drinks including bottled water and nibbles and was quiet. All the staff were welcoming and friendly. This hotel is well located for central London with easy access to tube and bus. If the rate was right we would certainly use it again.

title: Terrible value for money
text: I stayed in the Holiday Inn for a business trip and at a rip off price of £279, I will not be back. Breakfast was terrible. Cheapest quality food that was dry and unedible. Room was tiny, and had dirty carpet smell. Not even bed linen smelled fresh but musty. Dated cheap decor and carpet looking curtains. I’ll be sending my review and the rip off experience to our corporate travel team.

title: Very good hotel, great location
text: We booked to this hotel due to two main reasons : its location and a trade name. The hotel's location: near four underground stations and nearby to Oxford street and also this hotel is a part of Holiday inn network. When we arrived it was a very cold day, the reception was quick and we went to our room, which was very cold. Once we heated the room with their local heater, we went to the first of many days of "hunting days" in the Oxford street (less than ten minutes of slow walking). Due to our location we could travel every mall (Wembly, Westfiled {both}). Their breakfast was very good, as well as their service. So, if you like shopping (especially this sale season), i suggest you to come to this hotel and enjoy the reputation and location.

title: Good value for money
text: An excellent place to stay. Friendly and helpful staff, good choice at breakfast, could maybe do with more choice for evening meals but could still find something for everyone. Rooms were clean and had everything you need. Hotel was in ideal location, 10 minute walk from Oxford Street for shopping so not in centre and noisy but able to get to everything quickly. There was also a Sainsburys on the corner for anything urgent you needed/ forgot. Be careful if choosing to drive as although there is parking 'onsite' this doesnt belong to hotel and there is a charge. Though hotel does offer duscount to guests at end of your stay. Will definitely be back!

title: Overnight stay
text: Hotel is located in a quiet side street close to Regents park, approximately 4 minutes walk to Great Portland Street Tube station. Check in was great - I arrived at around 08.30 and was very fortunate to be given a room straight away, especially after a long haul flight. Rooms are fine, bathroom is not the biggest in the world, however adequate for one. Breakfast in the main restaurant was good, great selection and helpful staff - tip - go early or the place is very busy. Check out no fuss no problem. Acceptable for an overnight - close to the West End - but a nice quiet location.

title: Does what it says on the tin.
text: Good clean rooms, no view, nice breakfast although extremely busy at weekend, handy for the city, and friendly staff

title: Small room, big breakfast
text: This hotel was perfect for our needs, and although the rooms were rather small, they were certainly adequate for our 2 night stay in London. The location was good and the breakfast was wonderful with dozens of choices, including make-your-own pancakes. Especially noteworthy were the gentlemen at the Concierge Desk, who gave us excellent recommendations for dinners both nights (Jamie's and Ping Pong), and assisted us in getting tickets to a show while we were there.

title: Good Central Hotel
text: This is the second time we have stopped here and would go back again.. Great location, good/ helpful and nice staff and good facilities. Just what you need. Hotel is very convenient for the tube station (Great Portland Street is close) from which you can quickly get to everything. We walked from kings cross (about ½ hr) and again the same to Leicester sq, so very easy and enjoyable if weather ok. It was also very good value for central London. The rooms were clean but small and basic, but all you needed. Also very good Italian restaurants close by, after eating we did go to the bar, but there was a dreadful smell… we think it was the pumps so did not drink the beer and went onto shorts (quite expensive, but you are in a hotel in London) again the staff were good. Our only problem was that we did have a late night and room service knocked on the door then opened it at about 8am on the Sunday morning, she did apologise and said she would come back. (put you do not disturb sign on!) this did not happen to us before. Breakfast was great again all you could ask for. We would and do recommend this hotel.

title: Comfortable hotel
text: Stayed for one night, really liked area hotel is situated in. Stayed in very busy parts before but this was quiet and still lots of choice for cafes/restaurants and mini supermarkets. Hotel room clean, no frills but we were only sleeping there! We were Too busy out and about in London. Very near tube stations, so convenient for travelling to tourist areas. Regent's Park just down road was amazing, beautiful scenery! Did not eat in hotel so can't comment on food. Would come back definitely if back in London.

title: Great location, clean, modern
text: The hotel is nothing particularly special but is really centrally located, well kept, modern, clean, and a good value. Only 5 minutes by tube from Paddington/Heathrow Express, only a 10 minute walk from Oxford St. We had a glitch at check in but the manager made it right.

title: pleasant stay
text: Checked in for one night, receptionists very efficient and great customer care. Room was lovely with air conditioning, blackout curtains, fridge and comfortable bed. We also ate in the restaurant and the food was nice. Great service by Monika, very attentive but not obtrusive. Definitely be back

title: Great location and staff
text: It’s a Holiday Inn, so you know it’s going to be formulaic, but perfectly acceptable and they don’t let you down on either front. I booked a surprise dinner for my wife with 14 people, and the staff went out of their way to make it a great event for all. The restaurant has a great menu – lots of different cuts of meat and a good selection of side dishes. After dinner, they kept the bar going as long as we wanted to without complaint and ordered taxis for us as we needed them directly from the bar. The breakfast is huge and was very busy on the Sunday morning. We chose the hotel as it’s walking distance from Madame Taussauds and London Zoo. Very good stay.

title: Great Hotel - Ugly Building
text: Visited this hotel for one night and the hotel is situated just down the road from Great Portland St. tube station and is easy to find. The building externally is an ugly grey monstrosity situated amongst many beautiful buildings.
