The hotel is perfectly situated for Regents Park and other London attractions either on foot or via the Tube. We found the staff to be pleasant and friendly and our room,although slightly small was perfectly adequate and had a tv,safe,fridge,tea and coffee and an iron. The buffet breakfast was very good with a great selection of hot and cold food,although it would be better if the plates were hot rather than cold. We will certainly return here on our next visit to London.

title: Convenient
text: My daughter and I stayed here for one night over a weekend as part of a birthday treat to visit the theatre. The hotel is large and our room on the second floor looked out to the other half of the hotel. This didn't matter as we only slept there. The room was large, very clean with a fridge and kettle. The air-con was brilliant as we stayed over a very warm weekend. We chose not to have breakfast on site as the cost of £20.00 each seemed exorbitant - even for London prices. Our room was quiet and we didn't hear a soul all night. This is exactly what we want in an hotel and I would thoroughly recommend it.

title: Good value London hotel
text: Very clean, appeared to be recently refurbished. Upgraded to executive room, small but very well equipped, with mini bar, iron, hairdryer, toiletries, tea and herbal tea, coffee bags and chocolate. Staff very helpful and friendly. Good location, easy walk to BBC, Oxford St and Regent's Park.

title: Nice modern, well equipped and friendly staffed hotel for London.
text: Friday & Saturday nights. 2 minutes walk from Great Portland Street Tube Stations allows ease of travel to Paddington and all other destinations throughout London. Modern design to the Reception Area - You receive a friendly welcome from Concierge & Reception. Check-in was efficient. Rooms, in common with most London Hotels are not spacious, but my room was comfortable, with a desk, complimentary tea/coffee etc.. acceptable in-room tv entertainment and quality bathroom accessories. A couple of small issues - kettle did not work, and needed to be replaced. Wake-up call booked for 7am was never received. Junction Bar/ Restaurant/ Big screen tv - Relaxed atmosphere, chairs are comfortable, and evening staff were friendly and attentive. A good range of meals and a reasonable selection of drinks. Special mention for Concierge. We wanted to watch some rugby & soccer on SKY Sports. Without hesitation, the guy asked us to wait in reception as he went upstairs to the Junction Bar to enquire whether such a channel was available. It was, we relaxed for a couple of hours, had some beers, some snacks and a lovely afternoon. He's a credit to the hotel! Same story re: getting us a taxi - No hesitation, fast and efficient. Thanks an enjoyable stay!

title: Good hotel, welcoming staff, clean and well run
text: We stayed on the weekend of the London Marathon. We found the staff to be very welcoming and helpful. The rooms were clean and comfortable and the food was good. We will return. On the question of Wi-Fi, I there should be free access throughout the hotel for all guests. Holiday Inns are behind the competition here.

title: Nothing really wrong nothing really spectacular
text: If you need to stay in the area, I can't say it would be a wrong decision to stay in this hotel. The rooms are rather small but clean, the bathrooms tiny but sufficient for a quick shower and to brush your teeth. The breakfast buffet is very good and tasty, some of the staff extremely friendly, some don't really care too much.. A typical average hotel for one or two night stay

title: good hotel
text: I travel London for Pleasure with My sister. This hotel had great price include WIFI The rooms are small but clean The Hotel is in good access to tube and by walking to Oxford (10 min) It’s not a new hotel so don’t expect to get a new room. I have upgrade to the renovated rooms and they were only o.k. If you know you will go out in the evening to the SOHO area this hotel is not for you. The taxi is very expensive and the way to the SOHO by Tube is not easy.

title: A Hotel that looks distinctly tired
text: Stayed here for one night during a brief business trip to London. Whilst the bed was comfortable and the shower decent, the room definitely needs a refurbishment and whilst you can get free wifi by signing up for the rewards programme, charging for wifi is a pretty good indication of how outdated the overall impression of this place was. Staff were helpful and efficient but I won't be rushing back.

title: Curious loos
text: WARNING - not for the squeamish. With a rack rate for the room of £450 one would at least expect some nicely fluffy loo paper rather than paper which is more like the infamous Izal ("Rough or smooth side for you?") which we used for tracing at primary school. Getting to it was an interesting experience. The two holders are placed below the seat level and under a shelf. In order to reach the paper, this makes it necessary to almost put your head down the loo, a none too pleasant experience. The suggestions for the hotel is to reposition at least one of the holders up the wall, perhaps to beside the redundant phone socket. The suggestion for yourself is to remove the roll of paper from its holder before you sit down. Good luck! The bed is decidedly firm. Remembering the high rack rate for a basic room (B&B = £450), I was surprised to discover that there is no free Wi-Fi and that the rates for going onto the internet while in the hotel are extremely high.

title: Clean, nice place great value just not as good as they claim
text: Stayed at the Holiday Inn in regent park when we were in London two weeks ago. The rooms were nice and only a block and a half from the tube. My biggest issue is that I thought I had booked a 4 star hotel and this holiday Inn is a 3 star at best. Besides the aveage beds and small bathrooms I was really disappointed by what they called a business center which consisted of one operaitonal computer to be shared by all the guests in the hotel.I would recommend the hotel and would stay there a again but I would have to adjust my expectations

title: AWESOME!!!
text: The receptionists were very nice! The concierge was very helpful! I loved everything about my room! Room service food was absolutely delicious!!!! Best room service food I have ever had! I had the chicken masala with naan bread. The guy who brought it up was very nice also. Only thing is they claim WIFI is super fast but was very very slow for me and kept logging in and out by itself and most of the time didnt load the pages at all :( (I was in room 526)

title: A comfortable hotel near Regents Park
text: The room was very comfortable and had everything we needed including a fridge and tea/coffee making facilities. The bathroom was well equipped. We dined one night at their first floor bar and their "posh fish and chips" were very good. The staff were very welcoming and approachable and quickly helped us out with taxis etc. The hotel is very near bus stops and the Great Portland Street Underground station. I would stay there again.

title: Great choice!
text: For the New Year 2007/2008 I have spent four nights at Holiday Inn Regent's Park, which was not my first stay at this hotel. Location of the hotel is great. The crossroad between Oford Street and Regent Street (one of the main shopping areas) is just 10 – 15 min. walk and it is 20 min. walk from the Madame Tussauds. But, if you don't want to walk Great Portland Street underground station is just 2 min. walk. Warren Street underground station, which hes better connections, is 5min. walk. The hotel is typical London 4* hotel. In rare cases you'll get better. Reception desk staff at the hotel is efficient and wellcoming. Concierge can help you a lot with planning your stay and sightseeing. There is the cash machine (1GBPcommision) and the charging point for mobile phones in the lobby. The rooms are of medium size, which means large by London standards. They are not brand new but comfortable and clean. Beds are heavenly comfortable and are true blessing after the long day of walking. For the winter stay at the hotel, it is good to know that the central heating is very good (unlike the Holiday Inn King's Cross). The breakfast room is beautifuly and modernly decorated. I always take full English breakfast which is very good with lots of choice. I didn't eat other meals in the hotel which is understandable with the choice of restaurants in London. There are couple of acceptable restaurants close to the hotel, in Titchfield Street. I always recomand this hotel to my friends.

title: Fantastic 2 night stay
text: Arrived on Monday evening for a training event at the hotel & was met with a very smiley & friendly receptionist. My room was on the 2nd floor & whilst it wasn't a huge room it was no way small by London standards. It was well equipped with: iron & board, safe (which was on the top shelf of the open wardrobe, so only being 5ft 2 meant I couldn't reach it!) hairdryer, tea & coffee facilities, an empty fridge & toiletries in the bathrm The bed was a good size double & super comfy. It also had a good size TV. There was a small table & a chair. The restaurant staff were super friendly & helpful. The restaurant was really nice & the food was great

title: Hotel ok, great location
text: I stayed at Holiday Inn for 4 days during the month of may. I had a smoking room, it was ok, clean but the furniture was quite old (the arms of the arm-chair were scratched). The food - I only had breakfast and it was good. Anyway, the location is fantastic

title: Nice location, good breakfast and a very quiet room
text: The location just 10 min from Oxford Circus and just a few blocks from the tube station is very good. The reseption and breakfast restaurant is modern and nice. The room we had the first night was OK - even though the tap in the bathroom did not function properly and the bathroom door didn't close without use of much force. When the TV broke down the second day, we were transferred to another room and had no more trouble. The rooms facing the inner courtyard are very quiet - I have stayed in London many times, but have never had a room where sleep is not desturbed for four nights in a row. The choices for breakfast is wide, and almost everything tasted nice - but skip the scrambled eggs. They're made from powder and tastes awfull. One negative - the charge for WIFI is very high. We got a very good deal on the price for the room with about £510 for four nights in a twin.

title: Expensive, tired, noisy
text: Very tired carpets, decor, communal areas. Room basic but OK. Standard breakfast. Location is fine, but for this money you should be able to expect a lot more. Very noisy in the morning from trash and building works. May be best to ask for a high room to minimise this.

title: Great hotel
text: The group I travelled with stayed in 2 rooms here during the Easter break for 4 nights. We booked through the Mystery Hotel scheme on Superbreak which got us around £50 each off the usual price. The hotel is in a fab location - just 2 mins from the nearest tube station (Great Portland St) and 5-10 mins walk from Oxford St. The staff are very friendly and greeted us in the hallways and upon returning each night. The room was always clean, had all the essentials and the beds were surprisingly comfortable! The only thing I didn't like was the cost of WiFi each day if you want it - expensive! Breakfast was included for us and featured a wide variety of common breakfast items -hot and cold - to suit everyone. I would stay here again and would recommend to a friend.

title: Clean, modern, bright, excellent location
text: My husband, two year old son and I just got back to Canada from a weekend in London. We stayed at the Alhambra Hotel for the first night and then at this hotel for the second two nights. We staying here for free because of a British Airways promotion. After staying at the Alhambra Hotel, this Holiday Inn was a delight. The whole hotel was very clean. The hallway had some wear, but they were painting and working on it while we were there. Our room was very clean and spacious. For London, the room seemed very large. There was plenty of room for a cot (pack and play) for my son. The restaurant was nice looking, but I thought the food liked pretty greasy. I ended up only having continental breakfast. There was plenty of cereal, toast, fruit and pastries. My husband liked the breakfast. He had eggs, bacon, sausage, beans and the "continental" breakfast I had. The staff in the restaurant and at the desk were very efficient and helpful. They were very nice to my son especially. The location was excellent. It is very close to two tube stations: Great Portland Street and Warren Street. Warren Street station is only a few stops away from Buckingham Palace and the House Parliament area. If you have lots of time, you could probably walk to most locations. We were only in London for a couple of days, so we took the tube mostly. Internet access was not free. I had to pay 10 pounds for wireless internet access. I needed it for some work I needed to do while I was there, or else I would have not paid for it. Overall, it was what I expected, very similar to other Holiday Inns I have stayed at in North America.

title: A nice place to stay in central London.
text: A very good value for it's price. Very clean (they change the linens daily) but extremly small bathroom. If you are above average weight, you must look for another place. The quantity of the Shampoo reminded me days of austerity. The breakfast is rich and tasty. Two remarks. There is no gym and even at the lobby you must pay for WiFi, looks strange in 2013.

title: Very nice experience
text: I have visited the Holiday inn at Regent Park, and liked it very much. She service was great, rooms are clean, very good location. The only weak part is the internet service

title: Good stay, not outstanding
text: I was here with a colleague back in June 2012 for a business trip. The hotel was more than average, friendly staff and the location was good for us as it was not far from our office. The room was very good but the bathroom was too tiny in my opinion. The breakfast was very good and the hotel was quite busy, so it was nice to have a drink in the evening to watch some Eurocup matches with some of the guests. It was a few weeks before the Olympics so the prices were quite high everywhere but we could have a good fare in this Holiday Inn.

title: Tasty British Tapas
text: Met family here for a quick get together before going out for the evening. Great location and very comfortable bar/dining area. Loved the British Tapas - some tasty ones on the menu. A little understaffed as we had wanted some extra Tapas but couldn't alert the waiter as he was busy elsewhere and had to wait a while for the bill. But overall very good. I can't rate the accommodation as we didn't stay, just stopped in for snacks and drinks.

title: Dinner of exceptional quality
text: If you're looking for somewhere off the beaten track yet in the centre of town with exceptional food then this is the place to head for. Just off St James's and 2 mins from Piccadilly we have been delighted with the diversity of the menu over repeated visits. Lamb done four ways has to be a favourite with different textures and exquisite flavours bouncing off the tongue. We've eaten here a number of times over the past year and have never failed to be impressed with the presentation and the balance of the different courses to make us truly contented diners. Would recommend to friends.

title: Great location for boutique beauty
text: Business trip had me at the St. James for 2 nights. Excellent rooms - very comfortable bed and nicely appointed. We also used the meeting rooms which were perfectly suited to our group (15 people). The location is perfect for the centre of London and all the attractions - Buckingham Palace, Jermyn street, Piccadilly etc.

title: A superb and discreet luxury hotel with a London feel
text: The St James, that I use regularly in London, has been superbly refurbished and the rooms are small but extremely comfortable and well attended. The staff is feiendly and helpful and the restaurant is surprisingly good for a hotwl in London. The atmospere of the hotel is a combination of modern amenities and design with the classic London club feeling.

title: a wonderful anniversary surprise!
text: My husband and I had the pleasure of staying at the St James Hotel and Club to celebrate our 32nd anniversary. Once the staff learned of the special occasion, they went out of their way to help us celebrate. The staff is beyond professional and the hotel and its location are superb. I left a note for the management upon departure, something I don't normally do, to let them know how pleased we were. A return visit is definitely in order.

title: Amazing service
text: I can't say enough about this fabulous boutique hotel. The quaintness and service are impeccable. The rooms are small but very nice. Everything is thought of when you enter. I would recommend this hotel to everyone.

title: Superb experience
text: We stayed for one night as we had a christmas party in London. We had stayed before and the staff must have remembered us as we booked a junior suite, but were upgraded to the terrace suite. The hotel is just superb, staff is very friendly and quality and service are top. The location is excellent as well. It is a smaller hotel and it makes you feel very much at home.

title: QUIET, BOUTIQUE UPSCALE HOTEL
text: On our return second visit to London from Edinburgh, we stayed at this hotel. Our previous London stay was at the St Ermins Hotel in Westminster. The St James is another nice boutique hotel that is in a great location for walking around and enjoying restaurants, shopping, historical sites, etc. It's located down a side street at the end of a cul-de-sac. It's really quiet. We arrived via taxi and were nicely greeted. The front desk/reception area is small, but the staff were very professional. I would be remiss if I didn't mention that the room we had was larger than the St Ermins. The bathroom area was also nicely appointed as well with modern amenities and a nice walk-in shower. We did not feel cramped at all. So, if you are looking for room size, this hotel has it beat over the St Ermins in that respect. We stayed several nights during our second visit and would definitely return. The only meal we experienced there was the breakfast buffet. It was very nice, but the room and variety is smaller than the St Ermins. Again, the front reception staff are quite knowledgeable and helpful with where to go or where to dine. They made a nice recommendation for us on our first night. We wanted to have Italian food and did not want to walk far to get there. They recommended Al Duca and it was a very good choice (more on that in another review). We would definitely return and stay again. Next time we would probably explore the Mayfair and Piccadilly areas more, also within walking distance.

title: Wonderful staff and hotel
text: From the second you pull up outside St James you know you are going to have a great stay. The two door men instantly had umbrellas up for us to get to the hotel without a single rain drop hitting us. I abandoned my car with the doormen who took it straight away for parking. We checked in at reception and was given a selection of rooms to look at and decide which one we wanted. We looked at 4 rooms and everyone was perfectly decorated and furnished, the bathrooms are very contemporary and have everything you would expect even down to bath pillow and designer dressing gowns and slippers. The beds are really comfortable and the sheets and duvet are soft and inviting. The food here is out of this world, but be sure to book your table at the restaurant when you book the room to avoid disappointment. Breakfast is an event all on its own, the second you walk in you are looked after by the staff with nothing being to much trouble, the full English is a very hearty meal enough for anyone, however there are numerous other choices to suite all tastes. Check out was very simple no fuss and my car was returned perfect with no marks or scratches. The hotel is really close to Buckingham palace and St James park and only a short walk to Trafalgar Square etc. I cannot recommend this hotel enough, yes it is not a cheap hotel and I can tell you why. Because it's worth it.

title: Great location, friendly staff, bad basement rooms but amazing suites...
text: My family (8 ppl) stayed at this hotel 2 years ago and we were given an upgrade to their Westminster Suite. This suite was amazing and probably the coolest I've ever seen. The suite offered a huge private balcony and was very spacious. The services in the hotel was excellent and everyone from the reception staff to the door man was friendly and forthcoming. This year we revisited the hotel and booked 3 superior rooms for 2 nights. Unfortunately 2 of the rooms were in the basement and this sadly totally changed our previously great impression of the rooms. The rooms smelled and the air-conditioning was so noisy, which made sleeping impossible. The service and staff was still very lovely and absolute what you expect from a place like this. The bar was also very nice, offering great cocktails. However, the service there was a little slow. We had to wait 20 minutes for the drinks to arrive, but that was due to only one bar man working and he was very busy. We are probably going to give this hotel another try soon as the overall experience was still very good. Make sure you don't get a room in the basement.

title: Meal in the restaurant
text: 6 of us including visitors from Australia had a wonderful meal. The set meal had a few things that we do not eat and our daughter is pregnant so a few more things for her. No problem. The meal was outstanding and so was the service. The restaurant if very intimate. We had a great evening.

title: exquisite stay
text: The St. James’s Hotel and Club is the home for the elite of the elite — a five star boutique hotel connected to a Michelin Star restaurant. Even as an exceptionally young looking, casually dressed traveler, I was warmly welcomed by a sweet and accommodating staff who was expecting my early arrival and treated me like Ms. Meghan Markle herself. A lovely personal note, fresh fruit and bottled water were waiting in our impeccably clean yet comfortable room. Plush robes and warm embroidered towels were ready to be snuggled in. The best shower on earth was waiting to wash away my hangover from the many glasses of champagne I didn’t know I was going to indulge in that evening. All was well at St. James’s Hotel and Club and we were ready to explore London. The area is obscenely convenient to anything that you want to do or see in London, but the hotel itself was tucked away off the beaten path in what seemed to be their own private alley. We walked for hours, stopped for multiple pints, shopped around Piccadilly Circus and I enjoyed 2 full English breakfasts at the recommended cafe down the street with no regrets. Dinner at Seven Park Place by William Drabble was something I’ll always remember. The service was unforgettably perfect - we were greeted with a cocktail at the bar before heading to our seats. We were treated to a 3 course meal with appropriate wine pairings. I was left speechless. Our server was more polite than I deserved but also playful enough to make me feel comfortable. Here’s a run-down of what we tried (by tried, I mean completely devoured). I forget what these were called, but they were the most scrumptious little snacks of all time. Accompanied with (another) glass of champagne, the crostini had some cod deliciousness in it, the center item was burrata with a red pepper and olive over a delicious crumbly crust, and the last was a tiny duck spring roll. We knew we were in for a treat after this tasting. After that, I regret not having a photo of the fantastic trio of butters and bread selection available. I wasn't ashamed to ask for some butter delivered to the room -- it was THAT good (they talked me out of the butter delivery). Starter: Poached Native Lobster Tail with Cauliflower and Truffle Butter Sauce Starter: Assiette of Foie Gras... Seared, Mousse and Ballotine Main Course: Grddles Fillet of John Dory, Celeriac, Apple, Mussels and Chives Main Course: Assiette or Rabbit with Langoustines, Young Leeks and Rosemary The last items we ordered were dessert. Unfortunately, I didn't remember to take a photo of the menu thanks to my wine intake, but mark my words: the dessert itself is worth the visit. I cannot suggest a stay at St. James’s Hotel and Club highly enough.

title: Feeling Duped!
text: We are currently staying at the hotel and checked in yesterday evening. We had booked directly with the hotel and reserved a deluxe room for two nights, which includes a king size bed 25m2 room and breakfast. We have stayed at least a dozen times over the years but still feel as they don't recall us. We were given room 407 and were told this was the highest floor deluxe room available, I had emailed ahead requesting fifth floor away from elevator and a particular room but the reply came that it wasn't possible to prealocate rooms. We went into the room and it looked small and had a queen bed and thought this can't be right. We went back down to reception and were assured that this was a deluxe room, but I mentioned that the bed was only a queen and he said that was correct. He seemed surprised when I showed him his hotel website specifying the king size bed in deluxe room, we were then shown a couple more rooms and decided to stick with the first (all queen beds). Reception insisting that it was still a deluxe room. Feeling disappointed I brought up the website again to have a look and noticed that our room 407 was in fact pictured in the category below deluxe, it was a superior. Ordinarily I wouldn't have minded but for the substantial price difference and the fact reception had convinced us that it was a deluxe. Feeling duped and ripped off, my husband then hot footed it down to reception to explain where they begrudgingly admitted that we were right. So here we are now in room 412 with a bigger bed (required because of husband over 6ft) but only for one night because someone has prebooked this room, which I was also told earlier in an email wasn't possible. And we have to move! We are only here for two nights! We have been left in no doubt either that we have to move as we were reminded again when we came back from our evening out last night, what do they think we are going to do.....barricade ourselves in! My moan is I don't like the feeling of being duped... Give us what we have paid for and I'm fine. There has been no apology or anything. Come on St James Hotel, get your website and room categories in order. "A misrepresentation is a false statement of fact made by one party to another, which, whilst not being a term of the contract, induces the other party to enter the contract". Will we come back.... I'm not sure, we were trying to build up loyalty with one hotel on our visits to London but after this episode I'm not sure it's worth it. We like the location of the hotel and when you get the room you pay for its very nice.

title: Amazing service and location for honeymoon
text: We stayed here in January for 4 nights for our honeymoon. First of all, the location is perfect. It is close to everything and we walked everywhere. Second, the service is beyond words. Everyone knew who we were, addressed us accordingly and were incredibly helpful. The bellmen were amazing and we chatted with them every day for tips. Our last night my husband saw a supermodel leaving the restaurant so it must be great as well. Within location of all the great cigar and tailored mens shops. Just amazing experience and we will always try to stay there upon our return.

title: PERFECT, but...
text: This place is IT in London! Great location, beautiful rooms, wonderful concierge services, lovely staff, well-appointed, quiet. Then we checked out... £13 for 2 cups of coffee that we wanted to have in our room (not allowed to just take a cup from the included breakfast

title: I felt like I was being pampered in my own, luxurious home
text: I have stayed at this hotel several times, and have hosted dinners in the elegant dining room, which is a standout on its own. Even if you don't stay at the hotel - go to the restaurant. Perfect for business breakfast and for late evening snacks at the bar, in addition to regular dining. The rooms are a little small, but have every amenity, including great service. I particularly compliment the Reception Manager, Jonathan Hennessy, who is one of the best in the business

title: Absolutley stunning hotel, where nothing was any trouble.highly recommended.
text: I stayed at this hotel on a stop over in london. It was in a perfect location, just off of London Picadilly. Really close to Green park, lecister square, hye park and the mall. The decor is stunning throughout. The staff are friendly and extremley friendly. The rooms are luxurious and homely. There is also a wonderful restaurant and lounge downstairs.

title: A most luxurious treat, quiet, lovely staff and setting was perfection
text: The orchids were sensational and the bathrooms sparkling with lovely smelly things for the bath and fluffy towels. The bed was the most comfortable bed we have slept in together for 40 years!!! Thanks to the staff for making it so nice for us, respectful and polite and we were very struck by that.

title: Top Hotel in a great location
text: One of our favourite Hotels to stay in this part of London. Warm welcome by all staff, who can't do enough to help when needed. Love the art deco feel of the Hotel and its rooms. Great value compared to many in and around the area, location is tucked away but convenient for excellent shopping and a wide range of entertainment. Have stayed before and well most definitely stay again.

title: An amazing place where staff go above and beyond.
text: We booked the St James's for a business meeting for the day and 10 of the attendees stayed at the hotel too. Right from the initial contact with Silvia the Meetings and Events Manager through to the day of the meeting everything went really smoothly which is down to the professionalism of all the staff we came into contact with while making the arrangements and also on the day. So a big thank you to everyone that helped me. Everyone that attended the meeting was very impressed with the surroundings, the superb service provided and the amazing food too. Both Tim and Daniel who looked after us on the day couldn’t have been more attentive or have done more for us than they did. They're experience shone through and they are really nice guys too so we were very lucky to have them. We would definitely use the venue for future events so I hope we’re lucky enough to work with the same people again when the time arises. Words can't really express the quality of the hotel or the excellent service of it's staff so all I can say is if you want a central location with these qualities the St James's is the place to go.

title: Fun Vacation
text: I was only there for a few days, but St. James really made my short stay unbelievably memorable. The staff is extremely friendly, helpful and accommodating. The hotel offers quaint views of London Town and gives you a good look into the beautiful, homely streets of the city. I would gladly stay at St. James' hotel again the next time I visit London, as the ambiance is warm and inviting. It's like home away from home!

title: Elegant Hotel in Great Location
text: The St. James is located in a quiet cul de sac around the corner from the Green Park Tube Station. The hotel is elegantly appointed and has quiet and convenient lounges and dining areas. The rooms, while on the smallish side, are well appointed and the beds, most comfortable. The baths are rather small! The service is efficient and polite. A definite return visit.

title: January Visit
text: This was my first stay at St. James and I will definitely return. Great location near to Picadilly St. where the shopping, entertainment and dining are great. Concierge service is excellent and the facility goes overboard to accommodate business meetings.Overall great experience!!

title: First - Class Superior Accommodation
text: Tucked away behind the Ritz is a gem of a hotel, having stayed in a number of 5* hotels in and around the Mayfair area, The St Jame’s Hotel & Club tops them all. The recently refurbished interiors ooze opulence and the beautiful artworks add a distinctive flair. The welcome upon arrival is warm and genuine and the service we received throughout our stay was impeccable. Our Junior Suite which included a beautiful terrace was quite simply flawless. The Hotels fine dining restaurant and bistro don’t disappoint! The location couldn’t be better with easy access to Green Park, Bond Street and the West End. We would highly recommend this hotel.

title: My Review
text: Again the room service which is a treat for us when we travel was not good. The service was very poor. They guy who answered and delivered did not listen to what we were ordering and got the order wrong and forgot items so he had to go back and get them. It felt like he didn't care. I think if you get a better routine down on this to double check before leaving the kitchen it would save the hotel time. It didnt just happen once it was every time we ordered.

title: A quiet reserve in the bustle of London
text: My husband and I are contemplating staying in the next few weeks as a result of the lovely experience I had as a reciprocal club member from the Arbutus Club In Vancouver BC. When having a quiet glass of Champagne travelling solo in January and awaiting the arrival of friends to head off to a show staff could not have been more accommodating Right around the corner from the Ritz and Hyde Park- the lounge is intimate and lovely

title: Lovely hotel
text: I was impressed by the moment I saw the hotel's building. Very elegant and charming. this is just the beginning. When you walk in, every detail impresses you. A very elegant staff and friendly. Rooms are cozy, decoration very elegant and all the technology one might need. Location is fantastic, quiet and and at the same time close to the hot spots. For runners, a secret passage will take you to the lovely Green Park.

title: Very nice, very expensive
text: GOOD: We stayed in the Executive Room and we loved it. Our stay lasted a few days and the front staff were exceptional. The doorman knew my name from day 1 and the rest of the staff were very professional, pleasant, and accommodating to our needs. The free umbrellas out front were a nice touch as well. The room itself was amazing. From other reviews, I would say you want to spring for the Executive if you stay here. True, the shower is small, but the tub is an amazing way to relax at the end of the day. Room temperature control was easy and reliable. Walk in closet has plenty of space. Location is awesome, as others have said. A great central place where you can walk to most of the main tourist attractions. It's also a really nice area to to walk around in and see what shops you discover. BAD: There is a 5% "accommodation charge" added to the room rate, which adds up quickly in addition to the 12.5% service charge for any food. We had tea (excellent!) and took it in the back lounge but service was rather poor, almost as if we were forgotten about. TV is small for the room, but we didn't watch it, so no issue for us. Breakfast was not cheap at ~18 pounds for a conservative layout of yogurt, dry fruits/nuts, jams, and a few meats.

title: What a way to celebrate a 50th
text: From reservation, through arrival, welcome, stay and farewell on departure the team at the St James spoiled us rotten. The suite was spotless with wonderful fruit and champagne on arrival, a surprise at every turn down, luxurious toiletries and fluffy towels. We want to move in....breakfast was freshly prepared and hearty and everyone with a warm and genuine smile. Thank you for making this special birthday even more special.

title: Great Small Hotel
text: Recently spent 5 days here with the wife and kids, 9 + 11. My overall impression is very favorable and I would definitely recommend. We had two adjoining, though not connected, rooms. Mine had a bit of an awkward layout making it hard to access the closet, but this is really my only minor complaint. The furnishings were contemporary, the beds very comfortable and the rooms spotless. The front desk staff was top shelf. Very friendly, very helpful. We did not make use of the bar and dining are much. The location is great, set back on a quiet cul-de-sac. Around the corner is the Green Park tube station and the hotel is walkable to tourist sites like the War Cabinet rooms, Buckingham Palace, and Westminster Abbey. It is also smack in the middle of some very ritzy shopping, including the Jermyn street clothiers.

title: Good Central London Retreat
text: Nicely situated in St James. The staff are excellent and very well trained. We booked a deluxe room which was in the basement and very claustrophobic. After complaining we were upgraded to a superior on the 1st floor which was a big improvement although as with most London hotels cramped but very nicely furnished. Ordered lunch and it was well presented. Ordered room service in the evening and the cheese and cucumber sandwich was two quarters of a sandwich and the Welsh Rarebit = one slice of bread. Chips/French fries arrived as crisps with a hefty charge for this poor supper thus only 4 rating from me overall. Annoying that service charge was levied on all services even though I had put tips on each receipt. We did not take breakfast at £24 a head but had it around the corner for half the price and it was excellent. Only stayed one night

title: perfect
text: this place is perfect in every way, the staff is very nice and accommodating, the concierge is well-trained, the food is delicious, the rooms are very luxurious with attention to detail. the beds were comfortable and softest

title: Comfortable 3 nights
text: Had a nice stay. Hotel in nice location. Our first room had a noisy air con outside so had to move, but this was dealt with professionally, the rooms are, as expected extremely clean and well furnished, the beds very comfortable. We had continental breakfast which was fine. Any staff we encountered were very helpful and friendly. The hotel does charge an additional 5% which is clearly stated on the website, but they also charged us an additional service charge for breakfast, which I felt was unfair as we served ourselves, so this was removed. Also on check out I had a receipt through my online booker that I had paid a deposit and I informed the reception staff but he said I had to pay the full amount to the hotel, I did this but knew I would have to double check when I arrived home, therefore I did have to email the hotel and confirm to them that I had in fact paid a deposit, the hotel corrected their bill and refunded me the difference, no big deal but could have done without this. All in all we had a nice stay but not sure I would choose this hotel again as I like to stay in different locations.

title: As central and as 'boutique' as it gets.
text: This hotel is as nice, if not nicer, than its pictures. The location could not be better, in my taste. Just a stone throw from the fashionable Ritz, but in a much calmer and cosier part of the neighbourhood. And a fashionable neighbourhood it is, yet with a tube station 2 minutes walk away. Not that you need to go with the tube to access shopping and sights, but if you want to it is there. The room was impeccable and above expectations. The main area a bit on the small side, but that was well compensated by a generous bathroom, a walk-in closet/amenity section, and of course the balcony accessible through the room. Bathroom with jacuzzi, an amazing shower, the kind with the 'I'm standing in a heavy warm rain sensation'. The breakfast was really good, but if you are on the hungry side and want something warm in the mornings on your platter, the buffet is not going to cut it, but you'll need to order something off the menu. The quality of the coffee, omelette and freshly squeezed orange juice was right on par - tasty and added to the whole experience of quality.Almost fogot to mention the beds in this hotel. Can't remember sleeping this well in a hotel, ever. (reminds me that I have to write them and ask about the make!) The two things I would have opinions about in this hotel was the elevator and somewhat inconsistent level of service. The elevator is small (rooms 3 people comfortably), slow, old (but with modern interior), and there is only one. The reception we got was not relaxed and the girl behind the desk made an uncomfortable face when my credit card did not go through for a pre-charge for restaurant and minibar use (turned out that since my pin was inactivated on this card she would need to wait for a signature charge, but she did not know this, and behaved strangely. Then she proceeded to tour-guide the room after the check-in was already done, which felt really odd and intrusive. First time I've experienced this, and I hope the last time. After having checked in, I just want to go to my room all by myself and have that space to use, and not see someone who already looks at me strange strott around telling me where the toilet is (how did she think I made it all the way here if I need those kind of instructions?!). Most of the other service redeemed this first negative experience, expect the last day when they seemed to forget our company in the morning and did not serve us until we had been trying to get their attention for some time, attending to later arriving guets first. The kind of guests that seem to chose this hotel is on the 'pocher' side, the suite and tie kind, if that is of importance to you. Most in the personnell were very friendly and attentive though, but on the typical british 'stiffer' side, if you know what I mean. Overall, I highly recommend this hotel.

title: Very nice hotel situated in an excellent area of Mayfar
text: Wonderful hotel in excellent area close to Greenpark with friendly service , nice rooms and very good service in bistro and bar and very good food. Rooms are sometimes a bit loud . All front desk manager are very engaged and friendly. Very close to important places.

title: Central Boutique Hotel but nicely tucked away !
text: Stayed here on a Sunday & Monday night getaway, we usually stay at the Sofitel St James and wanted to try this, it's nicely tucked away off the main St James area which made it pleasantly quiet but very accessible to Regent & Oxford St, the staff are instantly welcoming, we stayed in a terrace suite on 6th floor, the room was very nice had everything for a comfortable stay except... Tea & Coffee facilities ! I don't understand why these are not provided in a five star hotel, it's a small thing but essential in my book, we didn't really mind paying £12 for 2 teas via room service, but would have preferred to not have the room service interruption in the morning. The rooms are well equipped otherwise, the Penhaligon toiletries are a very nice touch, along with the abundance of towels, shower fabulous, the bed was comfortable, obviously a well sprung mattress if I was being very picky....the pillows were a let down, small, flat not the big fluffy cloud like ones you normally expect. We didn't use the bar or restaurant as it was closed on the two nights during our stay, but the menu looked inviting. We had breakfast in our room, if I am honest I have had better English breakfasts but do try this little gem it's a nice alternative to the big boys and the staff make you feel very welcome.

title: Very Lovely Stay In A Very Lovely Hotel
text: St James Hotel is in an excellent location. In a quiet side street but not far from Green Park Tube Station, The Ritz, St James Park, Buckingham Palace and Fortnum and Mason, to name a few. Concierge were very helpful and knowledgeable. Reception staff were friendly and efficient. Public and private areas were spotlessly clean and well presented. Breakfast was delicious and the waiting staff were friendly but professional. Rooms were small but had everything in that i wanted. The bed was very comfortable. I didn't sleep as well as usual as the lights on the light switches and the light coming in through the bathroom door made it harder for me to fall asleep. I know the bathroom window is frosted but i would have personally have liked a black out blind or similar. I really did not like the hair dryer. It had all the usual functions but it took ages to dry my hair, maybe a bigger wattage would be better. I also didn't like the pillows, there was absolutely nothing wrong with them, they were just not comfortable for me, i would have loved a pillow menu. We like to stay in different hotels in London every time we visit so may not be back to this hotel soon but we would definitely recommend this hotel.

title: Nice townhouse hotel close to the Palace. Lovely restaurant.
text: Well located for sightseeing. Rooms nicely decorated with lots of high tech.

title: New Years Eve 08/09
text: So I lived and worked in London, so am aware of what NYE means as far as crowds/prices are concerned. Location. Couldn't be beaten. Just off Piccadilly it was a 10 minute walk from Big Ben across Green Park. For people new to London this is n ideal location. The quiet back street meant there was no traffic noise. Rooms. Modern, maybe too modern... We only stayed for the one night and it took us some time to work the lights and the steam shower... However great bathroom, and a walk in wardrobe. A wonderfully comfortable bed. Breakfast. Morning after NYE so palates were a little weak...Breakfast was adequate, fresh products - other than the fruit...but the tea....awful. Service. Very friendly. Car Parking. expensive, but then it would be for anywhere else in this area - £48 for the night! Special occasion so quite pleased, but would probably not stay here again simply because of the price...

title: Beautiful…but a tad too pretentious for my taste
text: I’m a bit conflicted with my opinion of and experience with the St. James’s Hotel. On the one hand, it’s a beautiful property in an excellent location (Jermyn Street is a block away and the lovely Green Park directly behind the hotel). Shopping, dining and landmarks like Buckingham Palace are all a short stroll away. Our “deluxe” room was sizeable, spotless and very well appointed with all the amenities you would hope for at a hotel of this nature. All-in-all, on paper it’s a great property. The singular downside – which will keep me from returning anytime soon – was the air of condescension my wife and I experienced from several members of the staff while visiting recently. It’s hard to put into words, but while some of the staff were very pleasant and cheery (we sincerely thank YOU), others very overtly gave off a feeling of “you’re not welcome here” or even outright disgust by our presence…and at $500 a night, I had hoped for (and would expect) a bit more hospitality in that regard. (Side note: this wasn’t my first trip to London, so I know the difference between British formality and condescension.) Even a slight smile or tip of the hat can be polite enough, but I can only experience so many scowls before I start taking it personally (especially when the person you greeted moments before got quite a cheery “Good morning sir!” while I get a look of “thank God, it looks like they’re leaving for the day.”). Quite frankly, it’s been years since I’ve felt this awkward and unwelcome while traveling. A shame. Put perhaps it was us. Granted we were there on vacation, so instead of formal attire we opted for designer jeans and a more “causal” dress overall by London standards (and being from California, casual is about as dressy as we get). Then again, maybe it was our age (we were probably half as old as the rest of the clientele we saw, most of whom appeared in their 50s, 60s or 70s). Or perhaps it was because we arrived on foot instead of via chauffeured Rolls Royce (call me crazy, but I enjoy taking the Underground and feeling more connected to the city). I don’t know what it was, but despite a lovely hotel, we did leave with a bit of a bad taste in our mouths. Accommodations: Excellent Overall Experience: Below Average Bottom line: If you’re like us, you’ll probably feel more comfortable in a less “stuffy” hotel.

title: Super place
text: Great location, great people and a really quiet room with a very comfortable bed The air conditioning was perfect and the room was at a very good temperature when we checked in Breakfast excellent was in a very nice room Very good people who didn’t rush a thing and lots of attention if you need it

title: Nice Boutique Hotel in Fantastic Location
text: We stayed at the St. James for 5 nights in January 2011. Great location in a quiet pipestem 3 blocks from St. James Palace (and Buckingham Palace across Green Park) and 3 blocks from Green Park Underground stop. Very well-appointed, small boutique hotel, which was exactly what we were looking for. Service wasn't perfect (we were incorrectly charged for items that had to be taken off the bill at check out), but overall a great stay - we'd stay here again.

title: A favourite but standards not the same.
text: We have stayed here twice before and also visited for cocktails when in London for the day. Each time has been a pleasure in an oasis of luxury and calm. On this occasion we went for New Year. The room we had was 109 which is downstairs. Reasonably spacious but a little dark as windows are below ground. It was a little musty too. However, we were only there for a night so decided not to bother too much. The staff were generally attentive as always. Interestingly unlike previous times there was no ’welcome back’ at reception. The bar staff were great getting us drinks. Good range of cocktails served well. We didn’t eat dinner at the hotel as we had made other arrangements. In the morning we had breakfast and ordered the full English from the menu. All fine until we were advised that we would get our poached eggs and the items we would need to get from the buffet! Rather strange and not what you expect in a 5 star hotel. Alongside that at £25+ I expected more! Not sure I’ll be back.

title: Bad for events - over priced
text: Had a hen party here in the Library and the service was just terrible. The waitress we had was very rude to my guests, which they complained about. As soon as time was up I was told we had to get out, despite their being no one after us in the Library room. We went up to reception and they said we could stay in the room for drinks- it was just a total mess really. Ruined our event, which we spent a lot of money on. The afternoon tea itself was just TERRIBLE. We had 16 guests and many of them complained they did not even eat anything. So I ordered more sandwiches, which of course we got charged for. I've been to afternoon tea before and usually it's unlimited tea/coffee- but we were charged for extra drinks. Wouldn't call it afternoon tea then. I was however happy with the room itself- the Library, which was stunning. We stayed over night at the hotel - average stay I'd stay. Could find better for the amount you pay. The event organizer I spoke with was also quite nice, he met my friends vegan requirement. Issues with payment though, he told me I couldn't pay on the day- but when I called I was told I could. I asked kindly if I could use our own champagne on the day and she said she charged me £200 if I did, I didn't pour my own but she came round quite rudely and inspected all of my guests glasses- felt like I was in school and being told off, not relaxed- wasn't "private" with the waiters trying to kick us out and charge us for everything. Overall, for an event I wouldn't host it here - the price isn't what you ask for and for a 5* hotel not accommodating. Afternoon tea, was the worst bit about it. Left hungry- not enough for everyone. Not much flexibility, charged extra, unfriendly staff, not relaxing. Thought I might add we kept getting told to be quiet, even though they knew we had a hen.

title: Wonderful location, clean and spacious rooms, very good service
text: We had a great time at the St. James's hotel. It is in a perfect and central location, although we had very peaceful and quiet sleep both nights as well. The staff are very accommodating and polite

title: Intimate luxury in a quiet corner of St. James
text: This former club is a perfect oasis in a bustling city. The staff are professional and competent

title: Tanktroop
text: Hotel room very tiny we had to get dressed one at a time breakfast was an experience orders were coming out wrong on nearly every table and then they asked us to use buffet and they would bring poached eggs out no conserves on table toast wrong twice everything cold very disappointed will not be going back they brought out kippers for next table and they had put scramble eggs and mushrooms on the wrong plate so they said would you scrape it know your partners plate and she replied that they will have the fishy smell on them and she refused point blank and they huffed and had to make fresh waited 10 minutes minimum then they got up and walked out very disappointed

title: Very Satisfied
text: I have stayed at this hotel many times and always find a welcoming and consistent service. We were welcomed and permitted to check in early which was very helpful. My business matters were will handled and the restaurant service was friendly and accommodating.

title: what a beauty
text: From the moment you enter, until you say goodbye, you will love this hotel. The service is excellent, the rooms very nice. Location is in the centre. Walking distance to Regent street. We had dinner at the restaurant and this is also very good. It does not come much better than this.

title: Wonderful place to stay in London
text: I had a wonderful stay at the St. James. The staff was excellent and this hotel is perfectly located in London. I highly recommend the St. James for you next visit to London. I will stay here again next year.

title: Superb
text: We arrived at lunchtime and had a beautiful lunch. Our room was lovely and we loved drinks each nite downstairs. We had one nite loud drunk women who were not staying in the hotel arrive who should have been chucked out. Otherwise great stay.

title: A little gem in the heart of London
text: Tucked away in a tiny dead-end street this gem of a hotel offers quiet and efficient . ...plus one gets a good night's sleep . The hotel is a stone's throw away from sights, the palace , Piccadilly , the theatres, and businesses in the west end. Will return !!

title: Great location in central London
text: A great location in central London with friendly, efficient staff. The rooms are a standard European size but efficiently organized and the beds and linens wonderful- like sleeping on a cloud ! Very clean .

title: An Outstanding Hotel
text: What a truly marvellous hotel. The service was exceptional as were the rooms . The staff friendly and helpful and what can I say about the food .. absolutely outstanding. Exquisite infact. I have stayed and eaten in many hotels in London and around the world for that matter and class the St James as one of if not, the best. I enjoyed every minute of my experience and would without a doubt recommend it.. I look forward to my next visit.

title: City Stay
text: I chose the St. James Hotel and Club because it is a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World and because of its convenient location for my business meetings. The hotel did not disappoint, the room was clean and comfortable, the bed divine and everything was of the very high standard I would expect from an SLH property.

title: Bijou but excellently laid out
text: Late night arrival, early departure. Shown to my room. Had an excellent Negroni at the bar from the Italian barman. Location is excellent, service too. Rooms are clean and not as small as feared. Would recommend...but not on a budget.

title: Great Rooms and Location, But Staff Makes the Difference
text: Our family has been staying here on business and vacation trips to London for over 20 years. More recently, there have been many modern upgrades to the rooms and amenities, and the restaurant remains top-notch, but the reason we continue to stay at and recommend the St. James Hotel and Club is due to the close personal attention by the staff in ensuring we thoroughly enjoy our time there. My wife and I are very picky in our hotel choices, which in most cases is a very costly standard to maintain, but the St. James is probably the best value in London for quality at a reasonable rate. On our most recent stay this summer, there was a slight problem with our room reservation, and without us saying anything, but sensing our disappointment, John H., the Front of House Manager addressed the problem immediately, and with a total commitment to making our stay a memorable one. Can't wait to return.

title: West End, walking distance to all the shops, excellent service, a treasure!
text: Amazingly accommodating staff. Be sure you book the executive room for comfort and space. We will definitely visit again.

title: SUPERB!
text: The Hotel has been recently beautifully refurbished to a very high specification. Our room was amazing. MASSIVE bed. Beautiful bathroom - huge bath and walk in drench shower. Service was impeccable as was the food and bar. Brilliantly located for nightlife and shopping. Highly recommended.

title: Fantastic Birthday treat
text: Right from the start the reception by the staff was both attentive and very welcoming, the decor and atmosphere was comfortable and the whole effect was calm and quiet. The Serving staff were amusing and wholly professional, the experience was excellent and I would thoroughly recommend this as a gift or a quiet romantic meal.

title: Quiet Spot in London
text: I recently stayed three nights here for business. I've pretty much only stayed at the St. James's Hotel & Club for the past few years, having tried a number of options previously. I love the location, how small the hotel is, the breakfast, and the friendliness of the staff. This time didn't really disappoint, though the overall experience wasn't as great as before. My room had kind of a weird smell, like they were masking water damage? It didn't bother me so much, but it was noticeable. I'd also corresponded with folks before arriving - I wanted to be able to check in early - and the front desk wasn't really clued in to this when I arrived. No big deal, though, my room was ready. Breakfast remained awesome. My room was quiet. Obviously the location didn't change... I'm sure that I'll be back!

title: Great Boutique Hotel
text: I stayed in St James during the last leg of my honeymoon. Overall, 5 star service and rooms. Can't really expect more than this for a boutique hotel. You won't be getting a big Ritz Carlton type of feel, but the hotel is very cosy yet top notch. You have to check on the size of the rooms though. Alot of london hotels have very small rooms, so if you want something bigger make sure you upgrade and get a bigger room. If not you should call to check the size of their rooms. 30m square should be very comfortable for most people. Location is great, short walk to the heart of the city. Basically a very good hotel without having to pay the ridiculously high prices of the brand name hotels.

title: Serene hotel just a heartbeat away from the West End
text: This hotel is located on Park Place, literally five minutes walk away from Piccadilly Circus. More importantly, however, it is a haven of calm amidst the hustle and bustle of London. St James's Park is just around the corner from the hotel. It is also adjacent to Jermyn Street, home of some of the most elegant shirtmakers in London town. Further down Jermyn Street, you will find a bistro called Rowleys (which serves a sizzling beef entrecote of the tenderest disposition direct to your table). And, for those of you with flights to catch, Green Park tube station on the Piccadilly line is only about a three minute trek away from the hotel. I was allocated room 602 in the St James's with access to the rooftop terrace. Given the warm temperatures in London, it was pleasant to return to the hotel in the evening and - from the rooftop - watch the world go by down in Park Place. The bedroom was of a modest size with a highly comfortable bed and effective air conditioning. The true jewel in the crown, however, was the spacious marbled bathroom which hosts both a capacious bathtub as well as a separate shower compartment. The hotel is very close to most of the central London venues. The Royal Academy is just around the corner from the hotel and it is currently hosting an alluring exhibition of paintings by Waterhouse. I was also able to walk to the Donmar Warehouse in Covent Garden (in the space of about 15 minutes) to see Rachel Weisz play Blanche in "Streetcar Named Desire". And there are also a couple of good arthouse cinemas quite close to the St James's Hotel. The hotel breakfast is a bit pricy, coming in at £16 for Continental, £22 for English. We are in recessionary times. So I eschewed (if that's the right word to use) the hotel breakfast in favour of a couple of neighbourhood bistro restaurants which serve tasty breakfasts for less than a tenner. Finally, the staff of this hotel give the place something special. Great people who made every effort to ensure that I would enjoy my stay there immensely.

title: Boutique style in superb location
text: Stay here several times a year and have never been let down .Staff are excellent ,rooms beautiful,wonderful design andd so comfortable with stylish black granite bathrooms. normally book through small luxury hotels of the world and given 2 upgrades to executive suite on last visit . Only one niggle to be wary of - they add a 10% ( or was it 15%?.) service charge to your bill which you are not obliged to pay ,though I wonder how many guests actually deduct it . On querying it they tell me it paid as a tip for their staff ?! I just hope this is not attend that other hotels follow..

title: Fantastic boutique hotel
text: Really enjoyed my one night stay at this unique boutique hotel. The bar has a wonderful atmosphere as well as thoughtful and informed staff

title: What a gem!
text: This is a beautiful small hotel situated in the best part of London. The service is among the best I have encountered. We booked an Executive Room but were upgraded to a luxurious suite - just a stunning space with a fabulous view of Big Ben from the lovely terrace. The breakfast (included in the weekend rate) was delicious and plentiful. My only complaint is that we weren't able to stay longer. I would enthusiastically return to the St. James's.

title: Amazing Comfortable Stay
text: Loved the stay. Everything from the service to the room was great. The entire family got a good night stay and and made the trip to London worth while No hassle, and very easy going staff, and the rooms made it feel like a home away from home.

title: Very good but with some minor drawbacks
text: Great hotel but rooms and in particular bathrooms are small for the price. I frequently stay in London hotels so am aware that rooms are generally small and expect them t be so (particularly if not staying in a suite), but these rooms do not justify the price, especially when factoring in the additional service charge at check out (which I find unusual and a little greedy). Our bathroom in a deluxe room was so small that I had to walk sideways to get from the sink to the toilet and shower and even that it was a squeeze! Also, whilst on the subject of bathroom, the shower screen is so small that it means that it is inevitable that the bathroom will be flooded, which in our case made the bathroom unusable after two consecutive showers, unless you have wellies with you! Serious (and perhaps dangerous) design flaw. In this category of hotel (small, boutique 5*) there are other hotels that are better value for money, with decent size rooms and well designed bathrooms. Having said that, what it can't be beaten on is location and the service and friendliness of staff. Location is excellent being within walking distance of piccadilly, regent street, oxford street, leicester square etc, yet tucked down a quiet street away from any noise. The staff were very impressive in their professionalism, yet warm and friendliness, particaurly the door man - the best I have ever encountered and an asset to the hotel. Also the overall look and feel of the hotel is good, with good quality fixtures and fittings and an understated luxury feel. Others have commented on breakfast

title: Perfect location in London & great service
text: My mom and I recently returned from a week's stay at St. James' Hotel. The location of this hotel was perfect - walkable to Buckingham Palace, Piccadilly, St. James' Park, Trafalgar Square, the Westminster Area, and Hyde Park. The hotel is small upon entry - more of a boutique hotel. Our room was very nice and very quiet. We never had any noise issues during our stay. The housekeeping staff was very prompt as well and usually had our room cleaned and ready to go while we were at breakfast. What made the hotel stand out to us was the service - the front desk day managers, the daytime concierge, and our friends at the hotel entry were all extremely kind, professional, and willing to go the extra length to help us. Once, the concierge even showed us his "secret passageway" to Green Park and the front doorman even helped us carry our luggage several blocks to get a taxi when there was an accident blocking the hotel street. Would recommend this hotel for a London getaway.

title: Another Pleasant stay at my second home!
text: I regularly stay at the St James's Hotel and club and consider it a home from home. The hotel is located on a very quiet street in a fantastic part of the city ideally located for sightseeing and shopping! I don't know how big the rooms are exactly nor do I carry a tape measure to work out the square footage like some sad individuals on trip advisor. I have always been extremely happy with all of the room categories I have tried however I am lone traveller and being of a slight stature I don't need a great deal of room unlike some shall we say big boned individuals!!!. The service is always great and I am treated very well, in fact like an old family friend.

title: Lovely hotel but give the bar a miss
text: Had a good overnight stay at the St. James's. Service from reception and Porter was very good and friendly. Twice used bar for drinks. Service in the bar very poor, drinks take long time. Not offered milk with tea, plus the house white wine was disgusting. My fault should have checked first but did not expect a poor riesling! Room good - spacious for London and both room and bathroom immaculate. But spoiled by being "under" bar so noisy!

title: Very British
text: A lovely lunch with business guests in the restaurant. The duck egg and asparagus was a delight followed by the plaice and the Boone Estate Pinot Gris was very good. Service excellent and the overall price was reasonable.

title: great hotel in the center
text: Its a beautifull hotel, with great service, and excellent restaurant, located in the center, behind the Ritz. it's indeed not common to find such a nice place in the center of london, combining service with top food :) A must!

title: Treated like Royalty
text: We went for a weekend to this wonderful hotel.The weekend included my Birthday and the hotel and Restaurant made this a Birthday, I will never forget.I have stayed at some amazing hotels but the level of service here surpassed everything I have experienced.We were treated as though they had always known us and nothing would be too much trouble.The whole hotel is beautifully decorated the beds so comfortable the bathrooms a divine Art Deco style and the William Drabble Restaurant served the best meal I have ever had.I can still remember the fantastic taste of each dish and all the extras that come with the meal. This is the only Hotel I will now stay in in London. Thank you for such a fantastic experience.

title: Great location
text: Stayed three nights while in town for business. Great location. Staff was very helpful and the bar was great. The only negative was the noise. On the first floor you could hear a lot of movement from the lobby above and then to the sides from staff area (kitchen, etc.). Next time I'll request a higher floor.

title: Earrings went missing from hotel room
text: I'd have loved to have given this hotel a better review, but unfortunately my property went missing from my room and the hotel management did not deal with it very well. Earlier on the day of my stay I had purchased 2 pairs of earrings from Harrods. I was going to an event that evening and tried them both on with my dress. Having decided on a pair I left the other in a small velvet pouch on my bedside table. After the event, I went straight to bed. The next morning when I was packing my bag to leave I realised that the earrings I had left on the bedside table were no longer there. I rang reception immediately to report it. My friend who was also staying in the hotel helped me thoroughly search the room and all my bags to make sure that I hadn't misplaced the earrings. But to no avail, the earrings had somehow been removed from my room. When I went downstairs to follow up on the matter (as I had not been called back as promised), the duty manager was not particularly nice to me. His first response was "well, you should have put them in the safe". I explained that I didn't think they were expensive enough to really warrant that. More to the point - that's victim blaming. I left my property in a locked room - it should have been safe. Now, I'm not claiming that the earrings were stolen. What is entirely likely is that when housekeeping did the turndown service in the evening, that they got knocked into a housekeeping trolley, or caught up in the linen, or fell into a crease of someone's uniform. It doesn't really matter what happened - the crux of the matter is that somehow the earrings left my hotel room and it wasn't me that took them out. I emailed the hotel to ask for some sort of compensation - in other similar scenarios such as if staff had damaged my property or spilled wine on me I'd have expected a gesture of goodwill. But no, they flat out refused. During the entire complaint process I have been made to feel like they think I am lying. That I have made the whole thing up. Given the amount of money I spent on the room and lunch it would be utterly ridiculous and a huge waste of my time to lie about the whereabouts of a relatively inexpensive pair of earrings. As a hotel they have a responsibility to ensure that their guest's property that is left in locked hotel rooms stays there. Not only did they fail to do this, but they treated me like dirt when I complained. If you value your property then don't stay here.

title: Fantastic stay in St. James area
text: I stayed here for three nights in November 2013. This is a fantastic boutique hotel nestled in a quiet side street (Park Place) near St. James Palace, the Ritz Hotel, Pall Mall, etc. It's about a three or four block walk to Green Park tube station, so it is very conveniently located. The bellmen kindly permitted me to borrow a hotel umbrella on two days (which I never needed much). Room: This was like staying in a fine home away from home. My room was extremely comfortable and quiet (even though I was on the main level). My en suite bath had both tub and shower and very nice amenities. Food: I had three meals at the hotel, which were all very nice, and the staff were very professional and accommodating (and friendly!). The breakfast buffet has an excellent selection. I found drinks after dinner to be very pleasant, too. Value: This is not cheap (after all, you are staying in a very posh section of London), but I found the experience to be a great value in light of the service, facilities, and comfort provided. I was working in the City. I frequently stay in a serviced apartment in the City, because it is closer to Lloyd's and my clients, but I decided to stay elsewhere this time (in part to scope out a nice place to bring my wife when she joins me next time). I found this location to be excellent for movement about London. I was here solo on a business trip this time, but I will definitely be back with my wife next time!

title: Amazing hotel and location!
text: We booked an over night stay here and were upgraded to the Kensington suite which was amazing. The suite has a large lounge area, a huge dining table, a separate bedroom, with a large bathroom... The views are lovely too. The service was amazing one of the best we have had in the uk, the staff are extremely friendly and helpful. The breakfast was lovely we could order anything from the menu which we had all bought up to our room. The location is brilliant as you can walk to Buckingham palace, green park, and really close to bond street from which you can walk to Oxford street and further. I would highly recommend and hope to stay there again in the future.

title: Superior Accommodations
text: St. James's makes you feel like landed gentry from the moment you arrive. Friendly staff, with no pomposity or pretension, just courtesy. Both the junior suites and the executive rooms I have stayed in are luxurious & comfortable

title: Good, but some staff are too snobbish
text: We have stayed more than four times at St. James which clearly scores in terms of location and decor. However, depending on who you meet at reception, you can get a nasty surprise. Generally speaking, the older staff are polite, polished and professional whilst the younger staff, especially at reception, are mostly incredibly aloof and snobbish. Basic standards of politeness, such as greetings and good byes, appear to be too much to ask of some of the young ladies. I have rarely come across such unprofessional behaviour. Rooms offer a nice decor, yet the windows do not insulate from cold air or outside noise. The same can be said of the doors, which have gaps to the floor. The German hotel management is reflected in the fact that the hotel is cleaner than most five stars in London. The beds are of fantastic quality. The bathroom plumbing needs sorting out as the water - both in the sinks as well as in the tubs - flows down very slowly (and were were on three different floors). Breakfast is good, but not amazing with a buffet that covers the basics of a four star hotel, yet nothing more. A huge disappointment actually and certainly not in line with British or German luxury standards. Overall, most reception staff do not make you feel welcome and many lack the professionalism displayed in other Althoff properties. We have been to Bensberg and Lerbach many times for the spa and dinner (since part of my family comes from Cologne) and St. James is not in the same class. Indeed, it is average within the luxury bracket of London's hotels. I feel the Andaz and the Connaught are better.

title: Perfect Stay in ideal location and so quite
text: Fantastic staff so helpful and welcoming. Lovely room and incredibly comfortable bed very luxurious duvet and pillow too.A treat having Penaligans toiletries and homemade biscuits. We had the English Tapas in the cocktail bar highly recommend. Thank you all for a perfect stay

title: Great value for great location
text: This hotel is perfectly located for enjoying London, just walking distance to best restaurants/clubs in green park/oxford street. Rooms are quite small (in line with UK standards) but very nicely equipped, clean and quite. This is for me the best choice when travelling to London. Please consider that gym/spa is not provided inside the hotel premises due to lack of space, though you are entitled to use the one of the Mayfair Hotel which is nearby (they have an agreement).

title: Great location
text: Nice hotel in a great location, but the bedroom was VERY small. Once our suitcase was placed onto the luggage stand there wasn't enough room to move around the bed, this was the smallest hotel room I have stayed in while in London. The lighting system in the bedroom was ridiculous, it took us 5 minutes every time we tried to turn on/off the lights due to the fact you have to hold the switch down while the light dims and brightens and if you don't catch it in time you have to go through the whole cycle again! The staff were all friendly and helpful and the hotel itself is very beautiful. The afternoon tea was actually very average, the sandwich selection was delicious but the cakes were quite bland and scones were so dry we could not eat them.

title: Brilliant!
text: I stayed at this hotel last night, and was really impressed. The staff are so friendly, and can't do enough for you. Fast, friendly, efficient. I had a lovely room in one of the "turrets" - really quiet location considering its in the heart of London. Great bathroom, super-comfy bed. Amazing food on room service. Really recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Spectacular
text: I was bought a lunch by friends to celebrate our Golden Wedding anniversary. I did not expect the quality of the lunch. The Food was as good as I have ever eaten. Every course was so tasty and presentation was just beautiful. The service was immaculate and the knowledge of the Sommelier Andrew was breathtaking. I will go back at every opportunity..

title: Very good but could be outstanding with a few simple 'Tweaks'
text: Most other reviewers have commented on location, rooms and general aspects, so I will add nothing to their comments. There were a number of things that would make a stay more pleasant, and herewith my thoughts

title: St James Hotel & Club-Nothing but the best
text: I recently spent two nights at the hotel in February. I also reserved a meeting room which was luxurious to say the least. Everything was 1st class especially the staff. I simply can't say enough about the sense of warmth and helpfulness. The room although not huge by US standards, was kindly upgraded from Superior to Deluxe and was wonderfully appointed. When I checked out of the Hotel and went for lunch on the way to the airport and realized that I had left my passport in the locked safe , the management was immediately responsive and cooperative. Top notch time, great location - and wouldn't hesitate to recommend to my closest friends.

title: Get Personal
text: I love this place. Its small and intimate, simply beautiful . The staff is helpful and very friendly is like I've knew them for years. Breakfast is included with a good selections on various foods . The bar and restaurant are great . The rooms are clean and cozy . I felt at home . Great location . No fitness but the park is just around the corner , even better.

title: My new favorite hotel!
text: The St. James's Hotel is my new favorite hotel. I have no complaints. From our arrival to departure I have no complaints about our stay. The hotel is located in an absolutely superb location in London. Walkable to all of the shops, restaurants, and Buckingham Palace is almost in your backyard.
