As we extended our stay twice while here, we ended up using three of Grosvenor Property Management's serviced apartments, each of which was very clean and comfortable. This is in a great location too, 3 mins to the DLR, 5 to tube.

title: Very nice stay
text: we really enjoyed our stay in the aparment, the cleaning was very good and the location is great....the only inconvenience for us Was the sofa bed, it is uncomfortable....I really recommend these apartments When you visit London.....I hope to repeat soon....

title: Families who need space
text: Stayed in the one bedroom apartment for 5 nights. The apartment provides the needed room for families staying in London. The Wifi worked very well which was important to us and apartment was spacious, Tessco Express 30 second walk, Starbucks 1 minute walk, Aldgate Tube about 5 minutes walk. Felt safe and was quiet. If traveling as a family, this is a good option since the lounge is large and the couch pulls out to a full size bed. The bedroom is a comfortable size with a comfortable bed. Plenty of room for 3-4 people. Rooms are not cleaned daily unless requested but clean towels are provided Monday-Friday. This was not a problem for us but be aware if this matters to you. Good price for the amount of space. Apartment 210 needs new tile or something similar as the carpet has many stains. The carpet may have been clean but the stains made it appear and feel otherwise. Air con in bedroom only so the lounge was stuffy in July. Air con is uncommon in London apartments so at least it did help in the bedroom.

title: Excellent Experience
text: We had a fantastic stay. Everything was well organised on an auto mode and the accommodation was very good. There was slight problem with the lock of our apartment i.e. we had to really struggle to open it but that could be one off lock. Location was ideal for us and overall it was a great experience.

title: Marlyn Apartments
text: Apartments are in a great location. Less than ten minute walk from either Aldgate or Tower Hill tube. Comfortable accommodation, good local facilities including the rare presence of a pub in the City or nearby open on weekends! . No hesitations to book again.

title: Needs Renovations
text: I stayed in the Marlyn Lodge unit 210 for a week with my wife. Unit 210 was a 1 bedroom unit that's needs to be renovated. The bathroom was old and the tub was peeling with rust. The kitchen was adequate but had no dishwasher and had older appliances. We did not use the washing machine so we do not know how that work but there is also no dryer. We arrived on a Saturday when there is no one to leave bags with if arriving before 2pm. We were told to leave bags in Liverpool Street train station which is 1 mile away if we got there early. I am not sure if all the units are in the same condition but this unit needs to be updated. The good things about the Marlyn Lodge are the wifi and good location with access to underground, trains and grocery stores. I would not stay here again

title: Best ever return for the money in the City of London
text: For the ones that need to be close to the City of London, close to subways and a supermarket just some steps away, Marlyn Lodge is a great option. Actually I stay there for the last 10 years with no bad surprises.

title: Warm and cosy accomodation during a cold week in London...
text: Very good and safe location. Clean and large room, good for 4 persons (1 good twin bed and 1 foldable sofa = twin bed, pretty confortable). Good heating system for the cold spring week we had in London... (individual regulating system). For summer days there is an A/C unit, but we have not tested it. Two elevators. Reception only during weekdays. Had a problem with the bathroom sink, it was solved the day we annouced it. All you may need in the kitchen and bathroom. Clean sheets and towels. Every day maid came to pick up litter. Very honest (we even let money in the room, although there was a safe box). Tesco market downstairs. Good communication on-line. Street view (you can here the ambulances though through an air vent in the room wall... )

title: Lodging in a great location!
text: We booked a studio apartment for me and my husband for one week while visiting London. The space was great and we loved having a couch and a kitchen! It was much nicer than staying in a hotel and felt more homey. Everything was easy -- the directions given by the management were excellent and the booklet in the room was helpful. Marlyn Lodge is so close to the Tower Hill Station and we could go everywhere from there. We could even walk to several attractions from the apartment and there were plenty of pubs close by. The only criticism I can make is that the apartment could use a little updating, but still it was clean and fully stocked with everything you would need. I would definitely stay here again and refer my friends!

title: Another fantastic stay!
text: My colleagues and I have been staying at Marlyn Lodge for years during our business trips to London, and the accommodation cannot be beaten from both a value and location perspective. Having returned from our most recent stay a few days ago I can confirm that the standards are as high as ever and highly recommend the location for both professional and personal visits to London.

title: Terrific location at a good value
text: We spent 7 days at a one bedroom flat at Marlyn odge and had a wonderful time.The owners communicated with me frequently about the checkin and checkout process and it was very easy. The apartment was clean, well furnished and the kitchen was well equipped. The appliances worked well. The fold out bed was a bit uncomfortable so we took the matress off and placed it on the floor which was way more comfortable. The best part of the apartment is its location. Less than 5 minutes tothe Tower tube station and the Tower of London. There is a Tesco just around the corner of the building and very good pubs in the area. Incredibly convenient. We will definitely stay there in the future.

title: Great location in the center of London / super dans le centre
text: Location was great: big enough for 5 (2 parents and 3 kids). well equiped, clean and very well located. Direction send by the owner were very detailled and helpfull. We got a trouble with the payement and before we ahve notice we got an e-mail and the refund of the cash overpayed. We will come back as soon as possible. Bref, Adresse à garder!

title: Ideal Base for London visit
text: I stayed in a studio apartment in Marlyn Lodge for 6 nights and was delighted with the convenience, comfort and value for money. The management gave prompt, efficient and friendly service and the housekeeper, Maria, was very pleasant and helpful. The warm, cosy apartment was really appreciated on cold, windy London days and the proximity to Tower Bridge, numerous transport links and the City was ideal. Some quite good restaurants nearby at St Katharines Docks. It was great to have a super comfortable bed. The only negative for me was the lengthy journey to Heathrow - allow plenty of time if you book a car!

title: Pretty Dirty place to stay
text: We spent the week of Oct 22 2016 at this place in Flat 101. It was quite dirty. The bathroom looked like it wasn't cleaned in years, the carpet is stained with filth and the towel service only came three time as opposed to every day. The room had a constant mildew smell and the management on duty really could care less about things.

title: Apartment with hotel services in central London
text: Comfortable apartment just five minutes walk from Tower Hill. Safe stay with cleaning service (three times per week) and all one could need. Easy check-in with clear instructions and lockbox. The only thing is that they say the washing machine is also a dryer, actually has a spin function but it is not a true dryer.

title: I only want to stay at Marlyn Lodge!!!
text: This place is fantastic!!! Location, cleanliness, the ability to assist when needed, is all at this property. I like too, that there are different apartment configurations as sometimes I travel with my family and sometimes on my own. It truly is the only place I want to stay at when I visit London.

title: Central location and comforetable
text: We stayed in one of the apartments for 9 nights and it was great! We were a 5 minute walk from Tower Hill underground station and felt safe walking in between. The bonus was the Tesco supermarket, which was located below the apartments.

title: Ideal!
text: We stayed at Marlyn Lodge for six nights and were very pleased. The flat was large, spotless, well equipped and very comfortable. The internet was speedy, and the clothes washer was great. The flat is located less than ten minutes from the Tower Hill tube station, which services both the Circle and the District lines. The DLR is right across from the Tower Hill station. Mass transit connections were excellent. Grocery stores, pubs and restaurants are literally just around the corner. I'd stay here again when in London for sure.

title: Convenient and comfortable
text: We arrived late on our first evening, and although we got a little turned around by the directions to the flat, we found it without too much difficulty. The flat was not as modern as expected, and based on the pics in the advertising, we expected to have a view of the tower. Nonetheless, the bed was extremely comfortable, as was the single cot, but the pull out was so uncomfortable that our son ended up folding it back and sleeping on the couch. It was clean, the shower lovely and the location very convenient. Not many restaurants in the near vicinity for a family. There are two grocers close by, although it would be nice if there were more supplies on hand. We have stayed in several vacation rentals in which guests leave behind what they don't use so others can use them (spices, sugar etc..) for their cooking, as it is difficult to stock a full pantry for a handful of days. Plenty of towels and the owners responded to our one request immediately! Overall great location and I would recommend it.

title: Better than hotel
text: We stayed at marlyn lodge two adults and two children.Very clean property with separate bedroom,bathroom, kitchen and sitting room with flat screen tv with english speaking channels and wifi was very good. .Rooms come with double bed,fold out bed in sofa and extra single fold out bed,fully epuipped kitchen which also has a washer/dryer which helps to keep airline baggage to a minimum.The property is a three minute walk from tower hill tube station which runs every few minutes.Very easy to travel around london from this property.There is a tesco express at the rear of the building and other supermarkets very close also.Lots of local restaurants in the immediate area while the tower hill tube station running every few minutes makes all london restaurants easily accessibile. Strongly recommend staying here if you dont want the expense of london hotels,but you want central location,clean accommodation,easily accessibile and quiet at night for sleeping. No complaints very enjoyable stay

title: Good choice
text: Apart a little issue at arrival (we didn't find the apartment key), promptly solved by the landlord, all was quite fine. Nice location: 5' by foot from the Tower Bridge, very close to underground and to a lot of restaurant, pub and market. The apartment is OK, well organized, but exposed on a noisy road. All things considered I recommend it.

title: Hard to Imagine a Better Value London Flat
text: In my 45+ year experience I'd always found London hotels shabby, overpriced, and inconvenient, so when my wife booked Marlyn Lodge for 9 days through VRBO I was apprehensive: based on the pictures the price looked too good to be true. It wasn't - it was better! Our unit was spotless, smart, and had everything one could ask, like being in someone's home. The kitchen and bathroom were superbly fitted and the bedroom had more storage space than our own. Our 4th floor unit was quiet, even though we left the windows open often. We especially appreciated the blackout curtains. The Wi-Fi worked just fine although it was a bit poky at times. Location? Couldn't be better. Access to tube (Tower Hill or Aldgate), bus (15 or RV1) & train (Liverpool St.) excellent. Tesco in building for supplies. Lots of eating / drinking options at all price ranges. Even a quiet little park just down the street. Next to a 1937 landmark streamline moderne office building still well maintained. I include the few nits just for accuracy - nothing is perfect. While the shower is brilliant, the extractor is useless, the bathroom steams up and stays that way. A rubber mat for the tub would help. The washer doesn't dry and the dishwasher takes way too long. The street gate is broken. Construction noise, detours and road work weren't the fault of the owners, but were just annoying. In sum, this is the best value lodging we've ever enjoyed. 7 stars if that was possible.

title: Very pleasant flat, well located.
text: The flat easily accommodated two adults, and George was very helpful. The building was very quiet whenever we were in the flat. Location and easy walk to the tube, Tower Bridge and the Tower. Air conditioning would be helpful during a London heat wave, but with windows open and fans operating, we were comfortable.

title: Great location and comfortable space.
text: I very much enjoyed my stay here, it was in a great location for all of my work meetings and the space was very comfortable. Kitchen and bathroom were both in great condition and very clean. The independence I felt while working in London for the week was great, I preferred this greatly to hotel living. Two grocery stores just around the corner and several great restaurants both quick service and formal dining. Looking forward to staying here again on my next trip.

title: Best value for great accommodations in London central.
text: We rented a one bedroom apartment and a studio apartment for our family visit to London. They had everything we needed to help cut costs. Full kitchen, grocery store just around the corner, and a tube station just a few minutes away. There are also great economy restaurants just a block away and Starbucks on the corner. Would recommend this place to everyone.

title: My son and I took a Dad/Son vacation to London
text: This room was perfect for us. We added a roll away bed for my son and both were very comfortable. The kitchen, bathroom and bedroom all met our needs. The price was fantastic and the location was convenient to the Underground (we used Algate station) and many of London's best sights.

title: Perfect accommodation for visiting London
text: We were 3 families staying in those aparments. The property is located just 300 meters from tower Hill underground. Is just 5 minutes walk from Tower Bridge, Tower Hill, TAmesis River... Just in the corner there is a 24 Tesco small market, a English Bar, Italian Restaurant, and in front of the building there is also a Starbucks....so you can cover your basic needs. In terms of facilities...2 out of the 3 aparments rented were pretty new... 1 kitchen, 1 bathroom, 1 spacious saloon-bedroom in which there were 1 doble bed, 1 sofa bed.. both of them news and comfortable. We had a table with 4 chairs, stereo equipment, new flat TV... Microwave, new refrigerator, free wifi (quite powerfull) everything ....full equipped. So the listing description of this accommodation is totally accurate in terms of location, layout and facilities. Just lo let you know that 1 of the apartment sitting in the four floor was not renew as the other, although it was ok but not as new as the other and that at night there was a noise coming from the TESCO market, perhaps some machine ...air conditioner or refrigerator machines. Customer service support was fantastic. Easy to contact with them any time, any day of the week. From Monday to Friday there is conserger in the building. His name is Jorge and it was very kind with us, keeping our suitcases until our department time. As a summary..quite convenience location and I would strongly recommend to travelers. Regards, Juan Carlos

title: The ideal place
text: Surprising at first sight opening the door. Well-finished flat, accessible to disabled (bathroom might be not perfectly suitable due to bathtub), clean, widescreen Sky TV, high speed Wi-Fi and a well equipped kitchen. A Tesco market just at ground floor, a Sainsbury 100m far. A 5' walk from the Tower of London and the Tower Bridge, 15' walk from the Liverpool St. Station. Many buses stops and Tube stations in a few minutes walk. Surely recommend this place whether short or long period holidays. Surely will be our first choice the next time we'll be looking for some days in London.

title: A perfect stay in London
text: The location of the apartment is perfect and the owner and his staff are very helpful. Although not every corner was perfectly clean, there are five points. In the apartment is everything you need and the price / performance ratio is fully OK!

title: Fair price in a very good location.
text: The pictures look a lot better than the actual place but everything was in order and clean. We noticed that the DVD player was not working and it was replaced the next working day. Very nice and helpful management staff. We had clean towels every day and overall, the apartment was well looked after. Heating and Internet worked well. Very good experience with flat 206. I would stay there again and recommend it to my friends.

title: Great location and excellent communication
text: We staid at Marlyn Lodge for 8 days. At 300 meters from the Tower of London and the Tower Bridge. At the same distance is Tower Hill Metro, which brings you directly to the city center with its monuments. In a quiet area, the appartment is very clean. Check-in was very easy with the instructions send by mail. Defintely a good choise in London!

title: Excellent location and Nice appartment
text: Clean and comfortable studio!it was exactly what I expected and what was described! It is walking distance to the Tower of London and Tower Bridge, near two Tube stops Aldgeit and Tower Hill. Jeorge and Maria very friendly people!

title: Absolutely Wonderful
text: I stayed twice at these apartments – once for a week in September 2017 and again for a month in November and December 2017. On the first occasion I travelled with a companion (occupying individual apartments) and on the last I travelled solo. The booking process was simple and efficient and arrival/check-in information is emailed regularly to guests prior to arrival. (NB: Marlyn Lodge operates “self check-in”, however if you check in on a weekday before about 16:00 the caretaker, Jorge, will help you to get your keys if he is around.) Situated very close to three tube stations (Aldgate, Aldgate East and Tower Hill) as well as a number of handy bus routes (205 to Paddington, 15 to Trafalgar Square etc) the location is wonderful. There are two supermarkets nearby – one (Tesco Express) is located underneath the apartment building. The other (Sainsburys) is only a few minutes walk up Mansell Street. A larger Tesco is located in Eastcheap (about ten minutes walk). A Post Office is a few doors away from the latter. For those fans of Marks and Spencer the nearest Food Hall (that I could locate) is about fifteen or twenty minutes walk away in Fenchurch Street. There are a number of pubs in the area however I only visited the Wetherspoons diagonally opposite the apartments. That’s the location dealt with

title: Love!
text: Have stayed here for years and is a fantastic value everytime. Management is always responsive and helpful whenever anything is amiss which is not often. Fully equipped kitchen is great after a trip to Burrough Market or after a night of curry that generates leftovers. Solid TV, great aircon and heating units and plenty of space, even in an efficiency. The price can't be beat for the location and amenities!

title: Spacious, comfortable apartment in the center of London
text: The cost-benefit of this apartment is undisputed. In front of the tower bridge, close to all the main London attractions and public transport (although I must say that with Uber, it is not as important as it was in the past). As a brazilian, the heating system is a very important issue during winter, and it worked perfectly! This is not the case in most of chain hotels. Fridge, washing machine and the regular amenities you would find in a flat are also a big plus. It is also a spacious flat. Having a concierge (Jorge) may help you as well. You have a Tesco right by the building and many different eating places nearby. Finally, once in a while I have to go to London to work (City Centre). Marlyn Lodge will be my choice from now on. Why wasn't it a 5 star then? Well, the apartment is in reasonable conservation state, but only reasonable, the location is convenient but not insanely touristic nor breathtakingly beautiful. All in all a great choice.

title: City Trip
text: We were very positively suprised about the Standard of the bokked Apartment - we three felt very well from the first momnent - almost like home. We had enough room, a nice bathroom and our 12year old Girl enjouyed most that we had the open space between kitchen and living room

title: Nice accommodation and very good location
text: The accommodation (room 508) are comfortable and it has all for the pleasure living. The kitchen is are fully equipped, rooms are large enough. The staff are very polite and always willing to help. There is a place to improving cleaning, but generally it is a good. The location is perfect: close to two underground stations, multiple bus stations, stores, good pubs (1-2 minutes of walk).

title: Great location!
text: The location was perfect as its close to everything! Tesco's around the corner, walking distance to the underground and train stations

title: Hostel
text: The most expensive hostel.Not polite,tired reception staff-dirty corridors,and a room looks that nobody touched in the last 20 years Suprisely the food was good in the restaurant.It was quite expensive ,but least value for the money.

title: Perfect Location and Great Friendly Staff!!
text: Hotel is just minutes away from Bond Street for some serious shopping! Just 15 min walk to Chinatown but there are tons of restaurants nearby. And don't forget the Georges Pub just around the corner. Get a half pint and chips (fries)!

title: Unbelievably awful
text: This hotel is brilliantly placed, just north of Oxford Circus, on Regent Street, near Oxford Street. It's rated as a 4 Star, but in reality it's possibly one of the worst hotels I've ever stayed in. You'd think which such a great location and the prices they charge, and the tag of 4 stars, it would be a treat. However, the "Executive room" I booked had paint flaking off the walls and doors, including the door into the room itself which was covered in scuffs. Once inside, wires were hanging from various appliances, including the TV, and the room generally had the shabbiness of a hostel. The sink in the bathroom didn't work, because the plug was stuck and no amount of prising it by one of the hotel staff could shift it. This mean that minor washing and cleaning of teeth had to be done over the bath, which looked ancient and was rusting in places. After complaining, I got a 20 per cent discount, but I felt it wasn't only shabby, but I was worried about the wires, and being on the 10th floor, thought that safety seemed to be at the bottom of their list of priorities. I have to say the staff were extremely friendly, and helpful, and there is a brilliant bar for drinking on the 15th floor with fantastic views across London. Go for a drink, but if you stay, expect the lowest possible standards.

title: great location
text: We want two couples , rhe service was graet , the location is lovely. We come back to london only to this hotel for sure.the view is spectacular. Dont forget to drink a beer in the 15 floor of the hotel .

title: Great location & clean!
text: It's right next door to the BBC! From St George's Hotel: 20 minute walk - Hyde Park 15 minute walk - James Street (lots of restaurants) 10 minute walk - Leicester Square (the heart of West End) 5 minute walk - Oxford St (shopping) 5 minute walk - Carnaby St You really can't go wrong with the location and getting a taxi is very easy in the area - the tube station is a 3 minute walk outside the hotel. Was easy to check in, staff were friendly and the rooms were cleaned daily. If you're not overly fussy about the windowsills being dusty or the shower a little rusted - then this is the hotel for you. Yes, a little expensive but you pay for the ease of the location. The full London experience.

title: Good value for London
text: London hotels are quite expensive - after lots of looking I found this centrally located hotel. Very easy walk to Oxford Circus tube station and just a bit longer to get to nightlife in Soho. I had a full size bed and was really surprised at the size of the room - I was expecting something much smaller. I was expecting some road noise from Regent Street, but the room was very quiet. I was next to the elevators, so I only heard the occasional muffled shut of a door. The staff was nice although somewhat aloof. My room was meticulously cleaned each day - definitely in the top five. I did not like the restaurant. I wanted a full sit down breakfast early in the morning of my last night, so I went up to their restaurant. I was rushed along and really felt as if I was inconveniencing the staff - although my English friends tell me this is normal, I find it unacceptable. The food wasn't anything great although properly prepared and I found it quite expensive. I came out thinking that I should have just stopped for something at McDonalds instead. I would most definitely recommend this hotel to anyone searching for a basic clean quiet hotel room.

title: Good Choice, might stay again but London has soo much choice
text: I read the many reviews before me just like you and decided to go with it. The cons were not all that bad, mostly from people who had too high expectations. I didnt have high expectations but I have standards and this hotel easily met them. Let me start by saying: The halls do not stink. We even took special note of the fact the 12th floor smelt of lavender. The lifts do have a mind of their own. The doors close very quickly and unless you press the open door button your partner or fellow guest is locked out. Putting your foot in the door, I learned, does not stop the door. The lift sometimes decides which floor it would like you to stop at. I figured this was because somebody on the floor it stopped at pressed the call button and got on another lift or stairs but no, its just felt like stopping there or bypassing your floor and stopping further up. Do you know what? They were the only complaints. The bathroom door would not lock but we always knew when the other person was having a "private moment" to not open the door. The main door was a bit broken whereby the lock was slightly askew from the deadbolt. It still worked after a bit of jiggling. The room was a good size, big bed, 28" LCD tv with around 80 channels. Im aware you dont go to London to simply watch TV but with my Fiancee's bad back, sometimes we need to stay in. The bar and restaurant on the 15th Floor have amazing views and the continental breakfast is satisfactory. It does exactly what it says on the tin. I think £15.95 for a hot breakfast is a lot to pay anyway. We never had dinner but the prices seem reasonable with £10.95 a main course + a glass of wine or dessert. The staff are friendly and helfpul and even took the time to answer my strange query on where the 13th floor went. Reason, the hotel reception is on the ground floor but the hotel starts from the 9th floor and up. 13 does not exist and all the way to 15. The BBC occupy the first lot of floors with a canteen on the ground floor next to reception. They have parking out front for 4 cars!! LOL but have a reduced rate in a multistorey around the corner. The hotel does need a facelift but from the inside it makes no difference. It you want a fancy hotel, stay across the road in the 5" star place. Its looked nice but with 3 doormen it looked expensive. Its an old 70's type building. Location: Thumbs up. We walked from the hotel down to the start of the shopping streets in less than 5 minutes. Oxford Circus is the nearest tube on the shopping street 5 minutes. This circle line goes Everywhere(nearly). I have attached loads of photos, well as many as Im allowed to. Would I stay again? Maybe. Its great and all that but there is soo much choice, I might save money and stay out by Bayswater/Queensway again. Questions. Quirke.alan@gmail.com

title: Small Dingy Room 1217, Rude Duty Manager Tony
text: Got checked into 1217 room. It’s a small, smelly & old room. Went back to reception to ask for room change

title: Perfect location
text: Booked this hotel again after staying there in 2015! Location is perfect. Close to Oxford Street and walking distance to almost everything in central London. Hotel is what you need for a visit on London. Recommend it!

title: Didn't meet expectations
text: Good points: the location but that's about it. Bad points: Soulless miserable front of house staff. Wall paper coming away from room behind tv and paint peeling off the bathroom ceiling. Apart from the location I was attracted by the free WIFI in all locations because I wanted to work in the evenings. As anyone knows, free high speed WIFI is the norm in most hotels in the developed world except for the uk where it's usually expensive and slow. One of the reasons I booked was that there was free WIFI. Here's what the website DOESN'T tell you: the free WIFI is slower than dialup from 20 years ago. If you want a faster connection you have to PAY extra. Most of the time my phone on 3G was quicker. If you want to avoid using your data or expensive roaming charges don't come here, or go to a cafe with free WIFI. So the claim of free WIFI is true but grossly misleading. I can't find anything online to show about extra charges. I wouldn't have booked if I'd known and it's not fair to mislead the public in this way. It took me 12 minutes to log into my email. This is totally ridiculous. Oh and the hot water failed on sunday morning so we couldn't shower. They said someone was working on it and it would be restored in 15-20 mins. An hour and a half later and it was the same. I've NO IDEA how this place got fours stars. It's also noisy at night but this is due to the location. Not the hotel's fault but it's a no no if you want a quiet night.

title: value for money
text: Excellent situation just off Oxford Street opposite the Langham which costs three times as much! stayed 2 weeks (on business) First week instandard room that had been redecorated ,recarpeted and retiled bathroom on 14th floor with excellent views and quiet apart from being near to noisy lift. Second week had executive double which had robes toiletries and leather furniture but was on 10th floor with not as good a view and noisier,also cost £30 per night more.Not really worth the expense. staff were much better than in the past when it was French run. victoria in the bar even remembered what we drank each evening (we only had one drink per night) which must be unique for a London hotel. Excellent value for money and position. Pizza Express next door for good cheap meals and the Heights bar for great view and reasonable prices. Will definitely stay there again

title: Good localization nothing more
text: I've been in worse hotels, these one is fair enough, but fake internet service. The staff just after check-in told me " unstable service". These days all the hotels should have at least clean room and a internet service is that difficult? I guess no!

title: St Georges
text: The st georges hotel is a great place to stay in London. It is right off Oxford street and has a central location, near many shops etc. The 15th floor is a brilliant place where you can have an enjoying meal or relax at night with a great view from London. Overall brilliant would really recommend it.

title: student digs
text: Brought me back to my days in the halls of residence 20 years ago Was on 10th floor. Dark narrow corridor with worn room doors with scuffs on them and peeling paint. Had paid for a suite type room, dont think I got one, room was so warm, sweat box. Banging pipes all night. Handy location, bath was big and filled up fast. Unlikely I will return.

title: Good Hotel
text: St Georges is a very good hotel near the Oxford circus tube station and very close to the shopping centre, eating places are near by. Accommodation is good clean rooms. Breakfast is available and good.

title: Cant wait to come back
text: Stayed one night at St George's hotel. The location was perfect for us, just off Regent/Oxford Street and near the London Palladium. Most peaceful nights sleep I've ever had in London. Room was big with plenty of storage. Really impressed with location of mirrors and plug sockets for doing hair and makeup. View from top floor is gorgeous.

title: Stale, requires a good shaking out.
text: Great location close to Oxford Circus tube ststion. After that nothing much of merit. VERY expensive for what we got. A tiny double room with en-suite. Secondary double glazing which worked well but the frsmes were rusty and dirty. If you want to run s bath / have s shower then I suggest you run the hot water for 10 minutes beforehsnd. A complete waste of wster, the wster rates bill for the hotel must be huge. We didn't eat in the hotel as there were a myriad of restaurants nearby. I'll leave s good review on one of them shortly. title: Room with amazing View
text: One of best hotels visited in London, fantastic location right in the heart of West End shops & handy for theatres, historic sites, parks & Oxford Circus tube station. Room was on 14th floor, clean, modern & spacious with large flatscreen tv, fridge & all the usual mod cons, bed very comfortable. Bathroom spacious & clean, thank goodness a lovely bath to relax in after traipsing streets & shops of London (shower over). Room service food menu appeared reasonable & good choices, although did not stay long enought to try it out. Bar & Restaurant on 15th floor, breakfast was excellent, plenty of choice & staff very attentive. Would certainly stay at this hotel again as a previous reviewer mentioned, would look no further if wishing to stay in this part of London & all staff very friendly & efficient.

title: Good Location & Old
text: This is a good place in a pinch but should not be your first choice. Room was clean and shower was great. Bed very firm for a bad back like mine, so appreciated that but others may not. Restaurants close by and shopping. Recommend Wahacca Resturant just up the street , as was amazing. Internet worked well. Only real negative was a need to refurbish carpet in hallways and the lobby , lamps etc.

title: Great Hotel
text: A very good service. Very clean and nice rooms. Amazing view from the restaurant. Very good breakfast. In the heart of London. Perfect location for those who love shopping. Will definitely be my choice again.

title: Perfect location
text: This Hotel is located in the centre of london, very near to oxford street and it is very nice. Big bedrooms, quite, clean and the breakfast is good. I really suggest this hotel for week-end or few days of holidays ! I really recommend the hotel for the position, near shops, restaurants, bus station and tube .. and it is not so bed also for the price. Good price/quality services.

title: Great staff, service and Location.
text: This is a fantastically located hotel. Close to shopping and multiple tube lines. The building itself is slightly run down and dated but this is more than made up for by the amazing service. The staff are friendly, informative and courteous. The service is impressive with regular room cleanings and well stocked toiletries (always an indication of how good the service will be). Decent WiFi and great views in addition to the above points make a great value package. Some rooms are better than others and so it would be 50:50 whether or not to have a romantic getaway here. If you get a good room and skip the dining facilities it could be a great getaway.

title: Disappointing service
text: Centrally located with comfortable rooms, the Saint Georges disappointed on two counts. The scaffolding erected for major renovation works made the wind howl at night making it difficult to fall asleep. In the morning I went for breakfast at the opening time of 7am to be told that my order would take at least twenty minutes. I don't have that kind of time to dally on a business trip. So a coffee and a bowl of cereal was my lot. Disappointing to say the least.

title: Very Satisfied from the Hotel, will come again!
text: I'm a very picky person when it comes to choosing the hotel we will stay at. It take me like a month to do my survey on the net to choose the most suitable hotel with best location, suitable budget and everything. I was soo worried at the beginning when i chose the hotel from the reviews, but i gave it a try because of the location. I was surprised to see that the hotel was even better than my expectations. The Location and SERVICE was the best. When we first arrived the reception people were very welcoming and friendly, quickly gave us our rooms, though we were a big group of 5 rooms, solved our problems with the rooms, and automatically updated one of our rooms to a suite. I still have some concerns, with some of the rooms at the hotel, some are really not superior at all, and some are excellent and you can still pay the same price, which i found unfair. However, the reception staff all of them especially the Blonde hair woman cant remember her name, did their best to provide us with a special room, especially after having a hot water problem with our settled room. Also, the manager Aisha did her best to explain our concern and satisfy our needs. Really the overall service was excellent a 5 star service people. Another concern, was the queen size of the beds in all the rooms, very small and uncomfortable, i saw this review with all the people and turned out to be really true. Some of the rooms furniture are really old, and some of them are new and excellent, and you still pay the same for both. Didn't try the food, but the hotel restaurant has a great location with an excellent view. The space of the room is very fine for a london centre room. Overall experience very satisfied, and will definitely come again next time we visit london. Thanks.

title: Ideal location
text: We stayed at the hotel for one night to attend a function nearby at Chandos House. Hotel friendly, lovely views from high floors and ideally located for most of London. Situated at the top of Regents street next to the BBC broadcasting house, it is idel for shopping trips and easy to get to from Oxford Circus tube.(5 Minute walk). Rooms spacious and comfortable. Price on Booking. com was £108 for the night. Cant beat it.

title: Great location for a shopping weekend!
text: My second time staying at Saint Georges hotel. This time we were given room 1412. As always the views are what bring us back and the location. The room this time was pretty worn down, carpet should be changed out and walls could do with a lick of paint. Beds were a little on the hard side, clean linen. However, you can't be the location and easy access to shopping. So we would definitely stay there again. We ate at the restaurant one evening. Great views but the food was a little disappointing. Fast and easy check-in and check-out. Cost of cab to Victoria station was approx. £17. I would say this hotel is a 3 star hotel even though the hotel web sight states it's 4 star. You get what you pay for. I will be back.

title: Grim and Depressing
text: Built during the very worst period of architecture in all recorded history, in a style that would have gladdened the heart of Ceausescu, the hotel seems not to have been renovated since the 1970s. To say that the decoration is tired is an understatement. The breakfast recalls British catering at its worst. The staff were pleasant enough, but apart from that one thought one was on the other side of the iron Curtain.

title: Great Location
text: This hotel is in a fantastic location on Regents St, just a short walk from Oxford street and most other attractions. The room was clean a tidy with great views of the city. The room was very quiet and a heater had be put in the room prior to our arrival which was great as it was so cold outside. We had a lovely breakfast and the staff were really good.

title: 4.5* Location. 2* Service.
text: I chose this hotel mainly due to location, apparent quality, and views. As for all my previous hotel bookings, I found no better price than octopustravel. Their site is easy to use and contains photos along with an abundance of information. So upon arrival, my girlfriend and I passed over the details of our booking to the concierge. After repeating the details numerous times, they couldn't find our reservation, but after 10 minutes we finally got the room key (what with the concierge simultaneously dealing with other guest's queries)...Once we got access to our room, we walked in to find a bed un-made, the tv on, and the bathroom with towels on the floor....I guess we were lucky that the current occupants of that room were out !!!! Needless to say, we returned back to reception and explained our situation, where the concierge apologised and gave us another room. This time, we were given a key for a twin room, despite booking a double room!! Yes, we returned back downstairs, and explained the 'new' situation. After a total of 35 minutes to check-in, we were now in a rush to be somewhere, and therefore asked if we could leave our bags behind the desk, and sort it out when we returned. We were told that we could go back up to the twin room and leave our bags there instead (Thanks!!). After explaining that we've had enough of the lift for one day, they decided to keep our bags behind reception. When we returned later in the evening, our key was ready, and our bags were in our new room. Thankfully, all was in order this time!!! This was my first experience of a 4* hotel room, and apart from the additional coffee-making facilities and immaculate bathroom, I found no real difference from a 3*. After finally settling in our room, we decided to go to the bar upstairs. Despite the somewhat hostile bar-staff and £4 charge for a bottle of beer, the bar area had great views of the skyline!! The next morning, we ordered room service breakfast, and despite some omissions from our order (such as toast), it was ok. However, from 9:30 to 10:45, we were disturbed by impetuous cleaners, wanting to clean our room. Ok, maybe we should've hung the 'Do Not Disturb' sign on the door, but after 6 times (later on with feeble excuses such as ''I wondered if you had enough coat hangers?''), we began to feel we were outstaying our welcome (despite the 12pm check out time!). I hope I'm not sounding too fastidious, but after spending a large chunk of my wages on the room itself, I personally expected to feel slightly more welcome....I don't know, maybe it's our age (we're both in our early 20’s)....or perhaps because we were staying there on leisure and not business??!? If it weren't for the location or views, I probably wouldn't stay at St.George's again. Though I would definitely browse elsewhere beforehand. Maybe the Bonnington? Hope this review is helpful. 3* room 4* bathroom 5* view 2* service 4* location

title: Good location but lacks in other areas
text: Booked this as price was reasonable and the pics looked good (for London at least) on the booking site - though still around £120 per night Hotel is well located close to Oxford & Regent Street, with everything on the doorstep. Also nice to have free Wi-Fi, which some hotels in London still try & charge for. Unfortunately, the good things fall away after that - the hotel is tired in the extreme, with frayed carpets, marked walls and flaking paint. My room on the 14th floor had was large, with great views, but also had badly marked and flaking paintwork. There was also two plug-in radiators, suggesting that the heating may not be up to the job. Bathroom had nice toiletries and looked ok until the shower cabinet door fell came off the track (repeatedly). It also took several minutes in the morning for the in the shower to heat up. Ate breakfast once - average buffet choice but at around £16, it's not worth it. Again, the breakfast / bar area would benefit from a refurb much of the furniture was tatty.

title: Average hotel for the price
text: Quite a shabby hotel, I stayed here on business and although the hotel was clean, I was generally disappointed considering the price and what other options are available in the same price bracket. One advantage was it was quiet.

title: Never disappoints
text: Have been staying at this hotel for many years and additionally using the top floor bar and restaurant as a rendevous for business meetings. Service always good and prompt. It's in a great location just a few minutes from Oxford Circus and opposite New Broadcasting House.

title: Poor service, definitely not a 4 star. Deceiving and to avoid.
text: I spent a few days at the hotel early October while I was in London for work. On the plus side, great location, great view, especially if you are on the 12th floor. Great view from the restaurant and bar too. On the negative side, I had a rather dirty and old room. The hotel is currently going through what the management describes a " truly exciting refursbishement programme" or something like that. For guests paying the price of an accomodation, there is nothing exciting to have smell of work in the (already very dark and unconfortable) corridors. The bathroom was not finished ( a few tiles missing from the walls, not sure why), the TV was not working properly (despite the numerous calls to the lobby). The restaurant and bar enjoy the nice view. The staff is sometimes impolite and not very dedicated to customer service. The same applies to some of the staff at the reception. No possibility to call the room service (nobody answers the phone). In summary, I would not reccommend this for travellers in London, except if you need to be in that particular location. On my side, never again.

title: Saint George is a saint !
text: I stayed at the Saint Georges for 2 nights at the beginning of August. I got a good deal for high season in Central London. (booked on the hotels own web page). Superb location, Oxford Circus tube station 2 mins away. Room was spacious, clean & tidy. Can recommend this hotel to anyone wishing good accomodation and easy movement around central London.

title: Location, location, location!
text: I rate this hotel high mainly because of its brilliant location in Central London as well as the beautiful views from the bar and restaurant at the top! The rooms are also ok and staff friendly. Although it is centrally located, it was not noisy. All London favourites are just a few minutes walk away!

title: Great Location but dark and Dingy
text: The location is great, close to Regent and Oxford Street but I'm afraid the hotel itself is in urgent need of a face lift. It is dark and dull. The corridors are dirty and the walls badly need a paint job. Our room was ok but very dark and a bit tired. The carpet was very worn and has seen better days. Bring slippers!!. Everything just needs an upgrade. Having housekeeping knocking on our door at 7.50am on a Saturday morning is a touch early I would think, especially as we were checking out that day anyway!.The hotel is located from the 9th floor up which makes it a bit soul-less.

title: Perfectly Fine.
text: I stayed here after needed a hotel as close to Regent Street as possible (I like to be close to my clients.) Bearing in mind that this was cheaper than a holiday Inn (which stunned me for London) I didn't have massive expectations. I had 5 nights for under £700 Whilst I could gripe about the silly things (slightly cramped reception, some evidence of refurb work going on, flaking paint on a wall corner in my room etc) to be honest these are non consequential. Facts Wireless - free (got told the wireless speed upgrade wasn't worth it). You won't manage Skype or streaming media (VPN may struggle too) but everything else was perfectly fine. Shower - Decent, hot and clean. Ditto the bathroom. Bed - comfortable, clean. Staff - Helpful, quick to respond (Anyone who complains about lack of English in London mustn't come here much

title: I love this hotel and have been coming back for over 20 years
text: I love the hotel, I love the location and always try when in London to return again and again. The hotel is just over time n of the BBC buildings in the area and the room floors are from floor 9 -14. On the 15 th floor there is a lovely bar, dinner and breakfast places. Our room had 2 two beds. They charge £17 for breakfast so I usually pick up a coffee and croissant at Starbucks or Illy or more just down the street. The staff are extremely friendly such a Janus who helped with anything that came up

title: Luxury price budget accommodations
text: I do not recommend staying at the Saint George's Hotel. The king size bed mattress was actually two single mattress pushed together, hallways and rooms are outdated and rundown, room was poorly lit, shower head had no pressure so you had to stand directly under it to shower not to mention the knob to control the water temp was broken and kept falling off so we never able to get hot water. They are doing construction on the building which we had to listen to coming from the adjacent room during the day. Not worth the money we had to pay to stay here. The best thing about the hotel was the view from the 15th floor.

title: Old and dirty.
text: The fantastic location of the Saint Georges Hotel might bring the hotel up to three stars in my opinion. The fourth star must be a joke or a very old review. It is possible the hotel once lived up to it's rating but the hotels former glory is long gone. The furniture in the lobby as well as in the first room we were shown was very worn. The room was dusty, the floor stained, the lamp in the bathroom wouldn't turn on, the windows where stuck and the bedspread had not been washed for god knows how long. I hoped the white stains was from someone ordering milk from room service but I dared not to take the chance. The staff was very friendly and where not at all surprised by the fact that we wanted to change rooms. A very nice man from the reception showed us to a newly renovated room that on first sight looked very nice indeed. But the vomit stain on the bedcover, that I first noticed the next morning, had me thinking differently. Once more, the staff was very friendly and very quickly changed the bed cover. The first morning we tried the breakfast buffet. Expensive, disgusting. Old dry cereal, tinned fruit, reheated buns... The view however was amazing and the staff friendly. The hotel is under improvement so it is possible that the hotel, when restored, is a nice location to stay at.

title: Bed lottery
text: Have stayed here a few times in the past and it was very nice, seemingly those days have changed. It has become very run down and the duvets are now flat and thin as pancakes. Previously I always got a room with twin beds and they were fine but this was my first double bed at this hotel. First one was creaky and I could feel springs so asked to change. Staff were super and took me on a tour to choose a room. The next one I was shown had even more lumpy springs than the first...(they were both futon beds). The third one was not a futon and was just right ( I felt like goldilocks). A lamp in my room was broken and they found me another but rooms don't have adequate lighting. Much refurbishment needed. Staff are lovely and room was made up early each day which was nice.

title: AVOID THIS HOTEL
text: Having reserved a room through booking.com I turned up at the hotel to discover my room had been given to someone else and they were fully booked. I can accept mistakes happen but they refused to pay the difference for any new hotel for me to stay in and so I was out on my ear at midnight in central London with nowhere to stay. The guy on reception was polite and trying to be helpful, there was another gentleman behind reception claiming to be be hotel owner shouting and swearing. A slightly surreal experience. My advise is AVOID!

title: not a 4 star!
text: My husband and I went to this hotel late June for 4 nights. We were shocked when we were brought to our first room. We were warned that London has a different standard for 4 star than North America but we were not prepared for this. There website said air conditioning , bathrobes, irons. Well this wasn't the case. The room was a sauna and when I called reception they advised me that it was central air. The knob fell off the radiator when I tried to adjust it, so they gave us a fan. The room was tiny, the carpet was stained , mirror was cracked, wood was warped and the furniture was getting threadbare. The washroom was a good size though. They moved us the next night to better room. And we found out that they are in the middle of remodelling some floors so depending on where your room is you could be disappointed .Our new room still had no Ironing board or safe. They only have a few safes and even though I asked every day for one they were always with other guests. They also do not supply wash cloths and I asked for 2 days, left notes for the maid. I was told repeatedly they would send some up but it wasn't until I went down to the front desk that I was informed that they discontinued that service. I have to say I was really amazed at how unfriendly the staff was and only one or 2 understood what good customer service was, the rest were rude and unpleasant. We weren't the only ones upset . I was present to hear a few people complain as they checked out regarding shower heads or the restaurant service. The location is great though and maybe if I had received one of the remodelled rooms I would have been happier but again service is everything and if you aren't made to feel welcome it isn't worth staying at.

title: Highly recomended
text: This hotel is fantastic. We came to see a show. The oxford st tube is very close walking distance in fact. Reception staff are very helpful and friendly. Our room was spotless, quiet and comfortable with all ammenities, TV, Fridge , tea and coffee, etc. I cant reccomend this hotel enough. WELL DONE SAINT GEORGES HOTEL 14-15 Langham Place Tel 0207 580 0111

title: Good location, hotel ok
text: I recently stayed 3 nights at this hotel. The best thing about it is its central location: it is in a surprisingly quiet spot at the top end of Regent Street, close to Oxford Street, and the Oxford Circus tube station, so lots of shopping opportunities and a tube station are within very easy reach. The hotel itself, however, is less impressive. While the outside of the hotel looks fine, the inside definitely doesn't match: the decor is old and tired - looking. The corridor on my floor was dingy and in need of attention. My room was ok, but not what I expected of a 4 star hotel in terms of comfort level and ambiance: average to small in size, with old furnishings - apart from the bed, which was fine- and cupboards with hardly any shelf space to put folded clothing, which was irritating. The daily cleaning service could also be improved!! The bathroom looked like an enclosed balcony space, newly tiled and clean, though not particularly spacious or well appointed. The restaurant and bar on the 15th floor has imposing views over London, but as I didn't eat there, I can't comment on the food. The area, however, has the same old and tired look as the rest of the hotel that I saw, and is not particularly inviting. The hotel is fine for short stays or business trips but if you are looking for a hotel experience with a pleasant, inviting ambiance, and attentive service then you may well be disappointed.

title: Great location
text: This hotel is opposite The Langham Hotel and the BBC is close . Oxford street is close by and Leicester Square is a longer walk . It is undergoing refurbishment at the moment but it did not disturb us at all . One of the most outstanding features is the restaurant which is on a very high floor and has tremendous views of the city. The breakfast is value for money enhanced by the terrific views . The room which was not an upgraded one was clean , comfortable and small , but great views .

title: Just another worn out English hotel -- but with saving graces
text: Those who frequent England will know what I mean -- a hotel with the wear and tear of time all too common in England and that many English regard as "character" -- really an excuse to tolerate the "patina" of many years or use. This hotel badly needs refurbishment. But -- there are saving graces. These include an excellent location close to Oxford Circus, one of the best dining room views anywhere in London (on the fifteenth floor and with a panoramic lots-of-windows view) and really interesting bedroom and hallway framed covers and articles from the old English magazine "Radio Times." The hotel is located almost next to the BBC broadcasting building, so the theme makes sense. I got stuck in the hallway several times looking at the fabulous art deco artwork and reading about how to listen to a radio in 1924. The hotel and restaurant staff were very good -- helpful, knowledgeable, attentive, working hard. They seem to all be from Eastern Europe and other places (frequently the best people for hotel staff, and this hotel recognizes this).

title: Tried to save money and got what I paid for
text: When I come to London I almost always stay at the Langham. This time I was on a tight budget, but wanted the same neighborhood, so I tried the Saint George. It does have a great location, and the views are quite good, especially from the top floor lounge, but the place is really tired and not very clean. The hallways are horrible, dirty and old, and the room doors look like they have had an army trying to get in. The rooms are okay, with decent amenities, but I didn't feel it was very clean, I could not get the a/c to work for the first three days, and one day the maid left stuff in the room. The staff were pleasant. Breakfast was pretty poor. I'll spend the money next time and not be so cheap.

title: Great Location, but quite noisy
text: Very centrally located and convenient for theatres/attractions. Room was well decorated, spacious and clean, but the building itself looked a bit like a concrete block. From the 12th floor, we had a great view over the roof tops of London. The public areas looked a bit 'tired'. Restaurant was less welcoming than expected, so we did not eat there. All in all it was 'OK', but would not choose to stay there again

title: Very Nice Stay
text: Spent 3 nights at Saint Georges with wife and 7 year old son between Christmas and New Year and found it met all our needs. Location is hard to beat and loved the view from our 12th floor room. We had a bed and breakfast package and enjoyed the limited breakfast each day. Room was fine but not huge which was not an issue as we only spent the nights in the hotel. All the staff we came across we good and helped us with our queries. Would definitely stay again for a London sightseeing and shopping trip.

title: An overnight stay while seeing friends in Town.
text: This is a great hotel, centrally located, great size room, good bed (if you like it on the firm side) and wonderful views across the city. Having read other reviews of the hotel I didn't know what to expect but booked it for the price and location, especially as it was for one night. I was pleasantly surprised to discover a great hotel! The hallways and doors look a little worn but I would call it characterful. The room had everything I could need including robes, slippers, safe, ironing board, complimentary water and a hairdryer. In London these little things usually come at a greater price. The room was spacious, with a table and chairs and a sofa included. The bed was very firm but I like that, so perfect for me. The shower was a bit old fashioned and the power of the spray almost pinned me to the wall...but I got out of the shower feeling incredibly awake and revitalised, almost like having had a massage for free! So if you want ultra modern, soft sprung mattress and waterfall showers, this isn't your place. However, character, views, everything you need in a hotel room, blast away the cobwebs shower and a nice room in a central location then I suggest you give it a go. I'll definitely use it again.

They were bigger than needed, and you need to push hard to close it... please check door photo. Saint George’s hotel : this has to do with your visitors’ safety !! Question to owners : what’s it that’s making you so confident that people will always book rooms with you even with this waaay too low standards? Location!? If this is it ..WRONG! This is London, competition is high .. your prices aren’t cheap .. with the price I payed you I could have stayed in better places with better standards! People looking at this review..go look for a cleaner cooler place .. سئ جدا !

title: smart and simple
text: I visited there on my business trip to London and Roma. Only two nights to stay made me comfortable. My room had nice view toward east London including BT tower and there was a nice restaurant on the 15th floor that I drank some beer with my co-workers living in London. It is located the good place near Oxford circus and BBC, so I could use the tube from/to Paddington station for the national railways from/ to LHR airport. But I walked down from the 10th floor to the grand floor through the stairs like evacuation training because their elevators were still under replacement from 11 A.M. to 1 P.M. The reception desk was very kind. Free Wi-fi can be used after getting the password from the reception.

title: Weekend stay
text: Great location and friendly staff. Also, very comfy beds! Minus for dirt spots on the walls, ceiling and very dusty inside the window frame. Away from that, there was clean sheets and towels, so we didn’t mind.

title: Great location
text: The hotel is in a great location just off Regent street and a couple of minutes walk to Oxford Street and the underground station. Plenty of restaurants, cafes and bars very close. We had 2 twin rooms on the 14th floor, I'm not sure if ours were one of the refurbished rooms? In my opinion it was not! The room was of a good size and the bed linen very clean, the bed was not so comfortable as you could feel the springs in the mattress. The bathroom was surface clean but could do with a good clean around the back of the loo and corners ect. Towels nice and big. The carpet had lots of stains and by the window had strange lumps in it and was not fitted properly. The hotel offer free wifi which during our stay it never worked. If we returned to London in the future I would stay again because of its location and definitely request a refurbished room.

title: Good central base
text: Location location location! The hotel is in a good place for exploring central London, and the room was surprisingly spacious. The decor is a bit tired and lacking in style, but my room had everything I needed for an overnight stay. Big comfy bed, tea and coffee stuff, massive TV and a clean, functional bathroom.

title: Average at best
text: When I booked this hotel online I thought I was going to be in a decent hotel. I don't need a 5 star hotel to make me happy. Just give me a decent bed and good wifi and a fridge that works. This place offered none of that. The pictures I saw of the rooms deceived me and were nothing like they portray on the website.The bed we slept on was hard as a rock. I even spent £10 extra to get better WIFI and even that was so bad I just shut it off and used my data. Our fridge couldn't even keep our leftovers from restaurants cool, found that out the hard way by smelling rotten food in our room the next day. The only good thing out this hotel was the location and the house keeping staff. Just do yourself a favor and skip this place when looking to book a hotel in London. Very disappointing

title: Convenient location, don't expect a lot.
text: St. Georges Hotel has been around for years. Like generations! It used to enjoy a remarkable reputation in the 80s and somehow, it is still stuck there despite the quick-fix renovations. Location: Everything you need as a tourist is nearby. Oxford Street, Carnaby Street, Regent Street, Subways, Shopping needs, Food... so full marks there. Room: Check-in was smooth but only one problem. We went upto our room and guess what, it was a total mess! I wasn't surprised because they have back-to-back bookings and staff is always on a tight schedule. I got upgraded to a much better room though, so no complaints. Room Decor: Very 80s, retro. It is not a theme, it's just that the Hotel is THAT OLD. If you are looking for super luxury like the Sheratons/Holiday Inn, then you will be disappointed. But on the plus side, you will get used to the room in no time. Tip: If you want to have a quiet, romantic dinner or just want to sit by yourself and get lost in your thoughts or just think about absolutely nothing, head to the restaurant in the top floor after 10pm. The lights are out except for a few lights and the restaurant has a panoramic view of London. It is beautiful! Things to look-out for: -> The layout of the room was weird. -> A/C ducts were dusty, don't turn it on or else you are most likely to catch a cold or some allergy. -> Kettle, drinking glasses were dusty. -> Lamp wasn't working. -> The exhaust fan in the toilet was not covered so when switching it on, it would sound like a factory in there. Things that don't really affect your stay: -> Furniture was broken/chipped. (Not a big deal to be honest) -> Some electrical fault was there but fixed instantly when I complained about it. -> Room service could be better. -> Parking is charged by the hour and there are like 5 slots... so don't even. -> Lift doors are crazy fast, so don't get stuck. Recommended staff: -> Tatiana -> David -> Pakistani Guy at the reception who is also the manager. (Sorry, don't remember his name).

title: Great hotel!!
text: We stayed for 2 nights at the St Georges Hotel in Pimlico in London. The hotel was really good but there were a couple of niggles - the room was quite small but had everything we needed - en-suite, tea & coffee, etc. The hotel is actually two hotels which are at no.115 (which is where the reception is) and at 107 (which is where our room was). Also the room was 3 flights of stairs up - there is no lift. Breakfast was in no.115 - it was really good - well cooked and well presented. The staff were very good and helpful. All in all a really good stay and I would use the hotel again.

title: Great for central London
text: Have stayed here several times when in London. Its position is amazing - its next to the BBC Building on North Regent Street. So for the west end, perfect. We got upgraded to a suite, with lots of space. The views are immense from the upper suites - right across canary wharf and the city. Its comfortable and you can come and go with ease any time. No hassles with big hotel protocols, you can just head in and up the lift.

title: Wonderful hotel
text: My partner and I have stayed at this hotel a few times before and have loved it. This time though we had an end room on the 9th floor and it was absolutely perfect. We could see the Shard, London Eye OXO Building and miles of London skyline. When we arrived the older man on the desk remembered us from last time and was lovely to see a familiar face. Last night we had our complimentary drink in the Heights bar and restaurant it was wonderful. I will most definitely stay at this hotel again.

title: Run down, dusty but excellent location
text: The hotel is run down visibly. The rooms are not well up kept even the more expensive rooms, full of dust under the bed, holes in the wall, cracks old paint chipping, doors look horrific and hallways. Everything is just looks ruin down. While the staff is very helpful and professional. The location is perfect a walks distance to Oxford circus. Overall I do not plan to stay here any more since for this price you can find better places one tube stop away.

title: Good location
text: Excellent location And very pleasant room. Not cheap but comparable with other hotels in the area. Would definitely stay there again just for the location.

title: New Year's Eve visit
text: Only stayed one night , had I been in town longer this would be the place , high up and away from the hustle and bustle of the shopping crowds it is a peaceful haven . Helpful staff ,and a lovely clean room with clean bathroom and nice clean bed linen,towels really fluffy . Although breakfast was not included in the price it was very good value for money with a good choice of food and attentive staff . I would happily return .

title: A good hotel, a little old for its price
text: The location was perfect for me. But the hotel is a little old. A few renovations would help it a lot, and the price doesn't seem to match this state in my opinion. Reception is small and dark, and personnel have an average behavior.

title: great location
text: the location was great. Check in staff were very pleasant and even though we were early we were accomodated. Room was good with a great view and had everything a traveller needed. It was good value for money. The restaurant located on 15th floor again had great views and breakfast good if pricey. I would recommend this hotel to friends and would use it again. The rooms are slightly old but this just added character for me. The beds are comfortable.

title: Depends on your point of view
text: If you are travelling to London and want to be in the cente of things, close to the shops on Regent Street, the Tube (Oxford Circus) and the sights, then this hotel is good for you. If you want to plan a romantic weekend away with everything just so, look elsewhere. If you want 4 or 5 stars in all aspects, its not for you. On the other hand, if you find chain hotels boringly predictable, then the quirky idiosyncracies of St George may add to your holiday enjoyment. We stayed for a few days for the Olympics and it was great for us. Never mind one light in the bathroom not working, one socket with no power, the main room door which stuck and the shower nozzle setting that kept reverting to 'bath'. The wifi DID work and was very good. The beds were comfortable. The staff were friendly and seemed interested in helping with any query. The 15th floor restaurant (and our 14th floor room) provided a panoramic vista over the city. It was easy to get to and easy to navigate around central London from it. So, one to mull over and then decide what you really want in your choice of hotel.

title: Not good enough
text: Well situated and reasonably priced. But there is run-down evidence (bathtub chipped

title: Location Location Location
text: The welcoming staff were wonderful, my room was awesome, okay its an older building but the bed was so comfortable and the sun came streaming in in the afternoon until sunset and overlooking Regent st. Just walk out the door and in the middle of it all, regent park a short walk away the shopping was all around the history, the fashion, the shops the awesome food. Saint Georges Hotel was the best part of my London stay, I would stay there again in a heartbeat if I ever go back to London. It was just so convenient to go back to have a rest and then go again. Highly recommended if you can see beyond the age of the building and appreciate the position, cleanliness of the room and facilities, best comfortable king bed, not when they shove two twin beds together and call that a king like one hotel did on my arrival at Heathrow. If you pay for a King bed you want a King bed. Saint Georges was great.

title: Old-fashion hotel in excellent location
text: First I have to say, the decoration of this hotel and furnitures in this hotel are completely out-dated and shabby, the room what I stay, obviously there is something wrong with the pump of the lavatory, you can hear water coming in and out continuously which really bother me during the night when I want to sleep, but the price for the location, I think that's the priority thought for most of the people.

title: A one and a half star experience claiming to be four
text: Booked the hotel for an overnight layover in London. The place is described as a four star hotel in a central location so it seemed like a decent value for money. My other option was the Langham across the street but this place was a tad cheaper and sadly I decided to save a few bucks. The location is indeed good (right on Regents street close to the Oxford Circus subway) but from the moment you get in you will feel like you’re in a 1.5 star motel. Everything in the building is dirty. The paint is peeling, doors fail to close properly and carpets have stains of .... well I just choose not to think about their origins. Everything (doors, furniture and even the ceilings) is scraped and scratched. This place feels like it was built in the 70s and it’s almost certainly the last time it had a remodel. Virtually any stateside low budget hotel chain (Hampton, Holiday Inn, Fairfield Inn) is a far nicer, cleaner place to stay. The first room I was given had a shower with so much mold in it that I can only wonder how they manage to pass inspections. After speaking to the front desk the hotel moved me to a bigger room without mold in the shower but it too never felt clean. Overall, the most disappointing thing is that this place costs about as much as nearby actual 4 star hotels. I feel totally ripped off. The service is about on par with the premises. A simple request for a US to UK power plug adapter was met with a suggestion for a 10 minute walk to the nearest shop. All in all - avoid this hovel at all cost.

title: Great Location pity the standard is not great
text: This is ideally situated close to the centre of London! GREAT view across London! Unfortunately, the check in was efficient, but lacked friendliness and welcome! The room was accessed through a corridor with carpet secured by duck tape. The room next door to the service lift and housekeeping was noisy first thing in a morning. The room was adequate in size, bed was comfortable, BUT THE FLOOR when was it last vacuumed?? Biscuit crumbs, and other debris all over! The fridge contained a partly drunk bottle of mineral water. The shower flooded the bathroom floor and only a quarter of the jets worked! ( fortuitous under the circumstances). Complimentary mineral water was very welcome, and filter coffee too! Long overdue a facelift! Wallpaper lifting, skirting boards badly marked, and lumps out of the plaster on the wall! A tired room perhaps not used frequently so overlooked! Probably would not visit again!

title: five days in London
text: The hotel has a very good location for city walks. The room was quite small but had an excellent view. We had a very comfortable big bed, very good service. Clean towels, as many and often as you like.

title: Value for money.
text: Given the location, its a great value for money for such a caring service on offer. Rooms, views, breakfast all come with reasonable price and great service. Highly recommended. Staff are helpful and friendly, comfortable, clean rooms with superb views of the city.

title: You get what you pay for
text: Centrally located. However don’t expect anything fancy. The hotel is definitely tired around the edges. In our room the bathroom door did not shut properly and one of the lamps had a bulb missing. The room was in need of decorating. However it was clean and comfy enough. With its location paying less than £90 per night I would stay again but would warn anybody expecting luxury to look elsewhere.

title: Small flaws, but a wonderful value in an expensive area
text: We checked in for our nine-day stay to a cramped room with a cold wind creeping around windows that wouldn't quite seal. The double bed was smaller than the queen-size found in most North American hotels, but comfortable. The bathroom was large. But everything in this tiny, well-equipped room was jammed in, leaving little space to walk, and several lights and other bits of electrical equipment didn't work. However, when we asked to have some repairs done, the reception-desk person who came up said he was shocked we'd been put in this room for a long stay, and that we'd be moved the following day if we just packed up when we left for the day. As promised, we returned to find our belongings neatly arrayed in a much larger room with a spacious queen-sized bed, a great view (looking down on the spire of All Souls Church and across at the Langham Hotel, which costs much, much more than the Saint Georges), with miles of London skyline stretched out beyond). The windows closed properly -- yet could be opened for some fresh air -- and there was room for a couple of chairs. There were still signs of erratic maintanance: the iron and hair dryer didn't work and a couple of outlets had no power, but our original saviour, the polite and efficient Mr Khan, showed up when we called and replaced both the iron and hair dryer immediately. The room was bright and quiet and our stay was very pleasant. When we asked for more covers (we hate sharing) they appeared quickly. The housekeeping seemed meticulous, and the staff was always friendly and helpful. Our bottom line: it's possible to get a bad room in this hotel, but apparently easy to upgrade. And even our bad room was clean and a real bargain in this costly and very central neighborhood, just a couple of blocks from the shopping and services concentrated along Oxford and Regent Streets. There are pleasant and reasonable-priced restaurants and coffee shops nearby. This hotel is housed in several floors of what looks like a 1960s-era office building used by the BBC, and it's apparently undergoing renovation that helps to explain the difference in quality of rooms on different floors.

title: Good location, nice view from room 911!
text: Stayed a short weekend and the hotel was well situated for shopping (both Oxford and Regent). Clean and comfortable, somewhat narrow bed for Mum and daughter, but not a problem. The view from the bar on the 15th floor -a must. Taxi to Paddington £ 10 and a taxi "hub" just across the street.

title: Weekend in London
text: Great hotel. Central in London, close to Oxford street and underground stations. Clean rooms, nice beds, you could open the windows, great bathroom with hot water instantly. Only negative was that you have to order breakfast, there was no buffé. Can recomend this hotel.

title: Good Location
text: Only booked for one night, the views from the hotel room on the 12th floor were very impressive and I would visit again due to the location, but there were some concerns, some of the power points were not working nor was the heating in our room. There needs to be a little more focus on bringing areas of the hotel from looking tired inside to looking more inviting.

title: To noisy!
