text: We stayed 3 nights and got a room over the bar/restaurant😩 Really noisy at night, impossible to sleep at night. We notefied the reception the first night, no real respons or help to get. This is simply not good enough. When you charge that much for a room a night we should be able to get some sleep! So if you book here make sure to check where your room is located, and as far away from the bar as possible. Or save the concern, book somewere else..

title: This is the Worst hotel ever! Absolutely disgusting!
text: This hotel is perhaps the single worst experience I have ever endured in staying in hotels across the world. So poorly dated, maintained and grimy. Dirty, broken glass on the floor, old, decrepit, stuffy, noisy and foul, old stained carpet. The only saving grace was the concierge Paul, who truly is a star! He tried his best to support us into a better room. Honestly, this fleapit needs to be demolished. If you are even thinking mildly of staying here, DON'T! It's a dreadful, example of converted old office into a hotel. Appalling service, crazy expensive prices and the most expensive s-hole I've ever had the displeasure of staying in.

title: Just shocking - absolutely shocking
text: Where do I start??? This is the sort of place I expect you would go to when you have reached rock bottom, and if they put you in room 1117 - you'll realise you have. The place looks like Ritchie and Eddie's flat from Bottom, trunk cabling everywhere and an absolute dive. It does have some distinguishing features - masking tape holding the carpet together on the 11th floor being just one of them. If you manage to spend a night here without considering ending it all the cold breakfast without cutlery delivered to room in the morning will make you wish you had reconsidered.

title: Very friendly service
text: Great location just off Oxford Street. The staff at the Heights Bar - Mahlet and Conor - were very friendly and the service was excellent. The snacks were well priced for the area. A good place to meet with excellent views across London.

title: Returning to an old favourite
text: Yes this hotel is dated and needs refurbished, but the view from the restaurant/ bar and central location more than make up for it. Good to see Anwar the senior concierge still there. Hope to return again

title: Bang in the centre
text: Very good hotel in the centre of London, just two minutes walk to Oxford Street and to the tube station. It is also handy because it is also walking distance to the Opera House and the West End theatres. Good value for money. Will definitely go back.

title: Breathtaking Views Across London
text: I booked a bit late so had to make do with a standard double room. I requested a room with a view and was lucky to be on the 12th floor! Our room was fantastic, comfortable, modest minibar, tea & coffee etc. The hotel itself could do with a makeover. The Sky Bar on the 15th floor shares similar views but really needs updating and the Michael Bolton sings Motown CD they were playing did little to enhance the ambience...BUT... it was a nice touch to have a complimentary drink. The main plus for this hotel is it's location and if you can get a room on the 12th floor overlooking towards the London Eye etc then it pays for itself!

title: Terrible!!!!
text: 1 star because I can't pick 0!! The reception staff are so rude, the hotel didn't charge my works card as planned so ended up paying for the hotel my self. I was then put in a grotty room that had brown dirty water leaking from the lights in the bathroom so was moved with no apologies. Second room was equally as horrible, this time I was woken up by machines being ran at 10:30pm from the next door utility room, bearing in mind it was a business trip I had been travelling since 3am that day! Finally moved to a 3rd room again no apologies. The bathroom was disgusting, felt dirtier after bathing in there.... And to top off the terrible stay the hotel charged my card 3 times for the stay!!!!!! When I called the reception to advise the rude man on the phone was unable to help! WOULD NOT STAY HERE FOR FREE!

title: Very Pleased with Hotel and will be back
text: I travelled to London with my sister and my fiveyear old niece, we were very pleased with the hotel, I booked over the phone, I requested a triple room the lady I spoke to was extremely helpful and advised that they would put an extra bed in the room alternatively they did have a suite would suite us but at that point it was unavailable however she did assure me that if it became available she would keep it for us. We were thrilled on arrival to find that this was room was reserved for us. We were very pleased with the hotel the staff were extremely helpful. The location was excellent close to many excellent restaurants and shops. I would higly recommend this hotel. The one gripe I would have is that breakfast wasnt included in the price and to purchase breakfast it was very expensive, room service was also expensive. But I will still make a return visit to this hotel.

title: PERFECT STAY
text: We have been there with our 2 children.We were so happy that we choose this hotel for our family.Great staff,great rooms and great breakafast.Thank you for making our holidays so perfect.See you next time.

title: good
text: The other reviews which have some criticisms have an element of truth but really for London and in this location the price is right. 1 minute to Regent St and Oxford St. £10 in a taxi from Euston. Reception was friendly, quick and easy. The room was bigish and well equipped except for the 1960's windows which we left open to the noise outside anyway. Aircon was good, good bed, bathroom a bit dated but everything worked great and the towels were clean and plentiful. The 15th floor was brilliant. Breakfast was quite good but a wee bit limited on range of options - ok as it was included in the rate. Drinks a wee bit expensive but worth it for the view. Yes I'd use it again. Super Italian called Bar Remo a 5 minute walk away.

title: Poor Lunch
text: We went to the restaurant on the 15th floor of the St George Hotel for a group Annual lunch. There were about sixty of us. We had pre-chosen our food from a menu so they knew what we were having. The starters were a celeriac and Stilton soup or a crab and prawn timbale. The soup arrived first and the crab and prawn about 15 minutes later. The soup was a strange saffron yellow colour and had no flavour of celeriac or stilton. We ate while it was hot so we had finished when the other starter arrived. The main courses were a choice between turkey, duck fish and a vegetarian option. I chose the duck. Weirdly they served all the turkey first to all the tables. Then 10 minutes later the duck arrived and 15 minutes after that the fish. The vegetarians are probably still waiting. The turkey was on the menu as roasted but was actually char-grilled steaks with hardly any gravy. The duck had been sliced length ways and along with over cooking was tough. It was supposedly served with a Jerusalem artichoke and turnip dauphinoise. Strangely the Jerusalem artichokes had been replaced with tinned or bottled globe artichokes and therefore had a strange flavour in the potatoes. My wife said that the fish (which had been substituted for what was originally on the menu) was overcooked. My dessert was a strawberry and raspberry tart. It was still frozen and so inedible. Avoid!

title: central for walking to shops and large bedrooms for London
text: This hotel is located within seconds of Oxford Street and Regent Street, it is idealm if like me, you hate the tube and want to use foot mainly and bus occassionally. I have to say, I think it is a good place - my room was huge - which I appreciated after the usual boxes in London, my bathroom was bigger than average too and the shower was good. The room was clean and well presented with large flat screen tv and free wi-fi. I think it had been decorated recently because it was all quite modern. The only wear and tear within the room was the external windows - which were encased by secondary glazing and hidden by curtains most of the time. View over the rooftops - nice. It was quiet, and the bed was comfy, so I slept well. Breakfast was ok - the teapot was big and had two bags in! I liked the fact that there was pizza express on the doorstep literally - handy for the lone business woman but there is a Ponti's Italian restaurant over the road and in a short road leading to the back entrance of BHS and they do a good meal and were very pleasant. The only knock, I would give this hotel, is that its lifts were quite mad - but they worked - if you picked the right one! There are dated bits - the doors for instance but they are not such a big deal because the size of the rooms (huge for London) and the excellent location make this a winner for me.

title: A nice stay
text: This was our fourth trip to London and I feel the location of this hotel was the best so far. As we were spending a week to celegrate our 25th anniversary we ordered a Superior double however upon arrival we had been upgraded to the Junior Suite on the 11th floor. (Room 1102). The room was very nice and had welcomed extra room to relax. The double bed was on the small side and HARD. Only some small problems (light bulbs needed replacing). Great view. Cleaning was OK, toward the end of our stay it seemed cleaning (bathroon in particular) was not so thorough. Breakfast was included and enjoyed a full english breakfast every morning. However I must say that I don't think it was worth the paying £13+. Very pleasant staff (especially the breakfast crew). Location was absolutely fantastic. No more than 5 min walk to Oxford street. I would definitely stay again, but I would call ahead to make sure I had stipulated a quiet room with new furnishings.

title: Good choice
text: Good views of London from 15th floor restaurant, really excellent breakfast. Very convenient for London Palladium,

title: Mixed feelings
text: The location is superb & the staff are extremely friendly & helpful. However, I feel the staff are let down by the fact that this hotel is in serious need of a make-over & does not deserve the 4 star rating it claims to have. If you plan on staying at this hotel I would skip breakfast as it was well below par & seriously overpriced. There are plenty of nice eateries in the local so you won

title: Brilliant postion for shopping!
text: I have stayed at this hotel many times as I do a lot of business in London. Every time I am pleasantly welcomed back again and always have a good stay. Plus when I have finished my business I am just a couple of minutes away from Oxford Street - such a perfect location for a hotel! The bar is fantastic - on the top floor of the hotel and a superb view across London - loved watching the sunset from the huge windows all the way along the bar area - you can even see the BBC next door. Very convenient for Oxford Street and Oxford Circus tube station.

title: Would have been one star but the location is great
text: Great location but absolutely no excuse for poor service and smelly bathroom (room 903). The bait and switch with the 'complimentary' drink in the bar was just the last straw. I won't be back even with the location.

title: grubby
text: We are shortly going for a holiday to London. In the past we stayed at the St. Georges due to the location. After our last visit I could not recommend this hotel as it is simply grubby and depressing . It is really a pity that the owners "milk" this location without any regard for their guests comfort or dignity. Look elsewhere

title: It'll do for one night
text: Although the room provided everything that was needed, there was nothing special about the property. The Toilet clogged and we had to move room and also there was no phone in the room so I had to use my own phone or walk downstairs to seek assistance, quite unusual.

title: What a find for London
text: We heard about #63 from a friend. What a great place to stay and given the location the price is amazing. Rooms are clean and comfortable. Staff are friendly and helpful. The breakfast setting is delightful and the choices quite something. When we go back to London, #63 will be base camp for sure.

title: Faultless!
text: Stayed for a week and am happy to highly recommend. Lots of different room types to choose from for every budget. I stayed in the lower price bracket but didn't feel like it. Great brekky...lots to choose from and a very friendly atmosphere with lots of regulars happy to help me with advice and good ideas for my visit. Best of all it was close to tubes, taxis were always going past and Hyde Park is literally across the road so walking was always a pleasure..a real find! Lots of great restaurants nearby and it really is the perfect location By the way there is a very cosy lounge/bar and i whiled away plenty of time with a drink and having a great chat with our receptionists andrew

title: Convenient Location
text: Recommended by a friend. Convenient location for Paddington Station and Lancaster Gate tube. Excellent value for money and the breakfast is nice. Staff are pleasant and helpful. Single rooms are good value. Twin/Double rooms are nice.

title: The best-kept secret in London
text: Number 63 has all the elegance of the regency houses along Bayswater Road. It is a very under-stated, almost anonymous hotel. The only clue that it is a hotel is the AA signs on either side of the door. Once inside, the warm and friendly welcome from the staff made us feel at home right away. It is a 3-star hotel, but the comfort and facilities are definitely 4-star. The hotel does Bed & Breakfast (a very good breakfast in the charming basement breakfast room. The en-suite rooms are very comfortable with T.V. and free Wi-Fi. The hotel is owned by the Soroptimist Society and you feel that their members expect very high standards. It's location, overlooking Hyde Park, five minutes walk from Lancaster Gate Underground station could not be bettered without paying very much more than their reasonable rates.

title: Great location
text: During a recent stay in London at the suggestion of a friend, my sister and I spent four days at Number 63. I was told it was club-like however it had great service, lovely public facilities and full breakfasts. Food was also available until 9:30. The rooms were comfortable. The location could not have been better, accross from the park, walking distance to museums and near the Lancaster tube. The staff was courteous, friendly and helpful.There was no pool or fitness center

title: Very welcoming, warm and comfortable
text: Stayed for two nights and as a female travelling alone, felt very safe in such a secure house. The hotel is right next to Lancaster Gate Underground station and on several bus routes. My room on the third floor overlooking the main road and park was small but adequate, was immaculately clean and had everything one would expect to see in a bigger, more expensive hotel. No problem with noise from the traffic below, I slept well both nights. Great breakfast with plenty of choice and served by a very pleasant lady. Didn't have time to use the comfy lounge or bar, but hope to next time I stay.

title: Priceworthy
text: A very neat and clean hotel in a good location. Singel en-suite with view on to Hyde Park, big compare to others. Clean, although the cleaning during the stay wasn´t so good. Ok breakfast, but I felt overwatch by the lady there. Good Wifi in the room, but not in the basement. I slept with earplugs and didn´t notice the roadnoice which other guests has written about. Compare to equivalent hotels its really good. AND it has a elevator...

title: Fantastic deal
text: Just returned to the States from my first trip to London where I stayed at number 63. Traveled with my brother, but we got separate rooms and both had great experiences. Excellent breakfast each morning included with the room price. An excellent price for the area of town (by Hyde park and just a block from Lancaster Gate tube station). Staff was friendly and always wanted to make sure you had everything you needed. Rooms were small, but that is part of the European experience and if you’re visiting, most of the time is spent out in the city. Would definitely stay here again if I’m in London again.

title: great location at a good price
text: Number 63 is located right on beautiful Hyde park and is only 50 metres from lancatster gate tube station so it was a great base for our holiday in London . We had a twin room which was at the back of the hotel with a rather unsightly view of a brick wall and stairwell . However the room was very clean and more importantly -very quiet as it was away from the road noise. The staff were friendly and very helpful and the hotel had a very peacful atmosphere. The newly refurbished breakfast room was charming and served a great breakfast and the staff were very attentive. All in all an excellent deal in busy, expensive London. Would stay there again .

title: Fantastic Hotel
text: Fantastic hotel. Stayed here for a couple of nights and was really impressed with my stay. It is in easy walking distance of Paddington Station and just across the road from Hyde Park. One thing that struck me was the way the staff really seemed to care about the customer experience. Nothing was too much trouble for them and they really did their best. Bruna and Debbie were the ones that were the shining stars! The hotel is a little dated in places and could be improved, but this didn’t affect the overall experience I had. Just one little criticism- whenever I stay in a hotel I really look forward to a full English breakfast- for some reason Number 63 doesn’t do that. You are offered eggs (that come with a little bacon), and beans but that’s it as far as the fry up goes. Still a great hotel though 👍

title: Stay here!
text: Beautiful convenient location, friendly helpful staff, well managed, park across the street, tube steps away, modern comfortable rooms with great mattress and all needed mod cons. Definitely a keeper, highly recommend.

title: Wisconsin, USA
text: "Very nice, friendly staff, great location." We were very happy with our stay. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Centrally located. Very close to the tube. We will stay here again on our next visit.

title: Great Place in Central London
text: I spent 3 nights in this hotel. It is next to Lancaster Gate tube station, and in front of the Hide Park. The room was a little bit small but very clean, hot water and TV available. A great breakfast is offered by the hotel each morning. Good service, and the staff (Leonardo and Tami) are very helpful...

title: Clean, affordable, secure, centrally located
text: Good, basic, centrally located hotel. It is clean, well staffed, secure, and not too expensive by London standards. Breakfasts are good (a cooked option is available). The carpets are old, and traffic noise can be a problem, but overall it is a good value. I would not hesitate to stay here again.

title: Very comfortable stay
text: We stayed for one night as we were attending a show. We wanted to check in later after the show as it saved us journeys back and forth. The Manageress kindly accommodated this and was there to meet us on arrival. The rooms are small but very clean and bright and well equipped. Also air conditioning! A god send for the hottest day since 1976. The location is great and very central. Breakfast was good. Good Selection for continental breakfast and the choice of Eggs, bacon toast. The staff were helpful and friendly.

title: An Old Lady by Hyde Park
text: It is really difficult to decide the rating for this hotel. Luxury is the last thing I seek in my lodging choice. Still, I was a bit turned off by the interior of this hotel. It felt as if I had stepped into a time machine transported into a time-frozen movie-set. The facility can use a bit face-lift for every decor shows wear and tear. Having said that, the hotel is clean and the service is attentive. The best thing about this hotel is its location, right cross the street from Hyde Park, half block away from Liongate Tube station, and 10 minute walk from Paddington Train station. Yet, the neighborhood is quite and safe, a retreat in the busy and noisy London. As many critics put it, this hotel is a good value in the high-price London, if you like us spent most of the day out and about doing what tourists do in London, only coming back to sleep. As such, my appreciation for this place grew with the length of our stay. Even if the Tube can take you almost anywhere in the metro area, being so close to the actions is really a selling point for tourists. We really enjoyed this benefit on the night we left the theater close to 11 at night.

title: Back after Leaving a Guarded Review
text: I have returned twice, and will be back a third time soon to Number 63 after an experience in February 2018 that wasn’t as good as usual. I have to say that things are are back to what I have experienced as the usual friendly atmosphere here on previous visits. I am so happy to be able to say that because Number63 is such good value and so well located and a different sort of place to stay in London. It was 10 years ago that I first stayed here.

title: Nice little B&B but a bit dated
text: Needed a reasonable place to stay after coming back from a business trip. This was the cheapest hotel I could find close to work, that did not look I would have to be sleeping with one eye open. The location is great, close to everything you would need and a short walk from Paddington station. I arrived late but the manageress stayed up late to greet me upon my arrival, which is a nice touch for a smaller place like this. Room was big enough and the bed was comfortable, although decor and amenities are a bit dated. The bathroom is spacious, nice shower and fresh towels as expected. Tea and coffee, kettle and a small TV, so everything you might expect from a B&B. Breakfast was okay, reasonable selection of things to eat plus cooked breakfast on request, although that was not quite a proper "full english", not a big deal though. I would have given this pace a 3/5 but I decided to go with 4/5 due to the fact that despite arriving very late someone was there to sort me out.

title: Five stars for value
text: I'm rather late to the party, posting this review several months after my stay in this hotel. Sorry about that. It was personally recommended to me by someone who has been a guest there several times. I spent 10 nights at Number 63 late last year and was very pleased. The location was good, with Lancaster Gate tube station very close by, and shops and restaurants also handy. I loved being just across the street from Hyde Park. My room was small but not ridiculously so. It was located at the back of the hotel

title: Excellent visit from Yorkshire Soroptimists
text: 21 Yorkshire Soroptimists enjoyed a wonderful stay at 63 during their visit to the Houses of Parliament. Excellent facility for ladies as all rooms twins or single and a lovely welcoming atmosphere. Taormina Italian and Bel Canto Restaurants within walking distance to provide excellent food in the evening. Hyde Park across the road a wonderful park with many different aspects

title: Cozy, clean, great location
text: It is a small pleasant house, just across the street form Kensington Gardens. Staff is very helpful adn attnetive, rooms are quite modest but very clean and functional - there is everything needed. Breakfast is served in a typical English room and is nice. Great price. On the negative side - not every room has air condition and there is no safe deposit box, either in the room or int he reception. Wiill stay there again.

title: Location, location!
text: We stayed 4 nights and were very comfortable, beds were good and the room, although smallish, had everything we needed, including a nice hot shower! Breakfasts were well cooked and plenty of options to choose from. We found the staff friendly and very helpful, especially with a small unusual request. If the opportunity ever arose we would be delighted to stay at No 63 again.

title: Excellent Location & Value
text: Have stayed at No 63 a few times, this time for Chelsea Flower Show. The hotel has an excellent location, close to Lancaster Gate tube station but also so close to Oxford St (shopping) Hyde Park and the Royal Albert Hall. Rooms are very clean and staff friendly. Will definitely be staying again.

title: Great view of Hyde Park and close to a tube stop!
text: My husband and I chose Number 63 for our recent stay over the Easter Holiday. The room was small (which we didn't mind at all), clean and comfortable. A delicious breakfast is available in a relaxing atmosphere. We found the staff to be welcoming and efficient. Our room had a view of the Italian Gardens of Hyde Park, and although we could hear the noise from the busy street below, we were still able to sleep quite well. One of the best perks is its location--a few steps away from a tube station and a ten minute walk to Paddington Station which has an express train to Heathrow Airport. If you enjoy a smaller establishment, with less hustle and bustle, this is the place for you.

title: Superb single rooms & Interesting Staff
text: Some good reviews on here so I won’t cover commonly covered topics. It’s not easy to find single rooms in London. Number 63 seems to have mostly single rooms. Most are very small but well designed and the shower rooms are especially good. Rooms at the front have views over Hyde Park. Location is outstanding as mentioned in other reviews. It is excellent value with included breakfast, cooked English breakfasts as well as continental style ingredients in a pretty basement dining room. There are a few bookshelves of paperbacks to borrow/donate to. The beautiful receptionist was one of the grumpiest people I have ever met. I stayed for over a week, and she started to really amuse me. I took every opportunity to speak to her and not once did her mood improve, nor did she become at all helpful as we (sort of) got to know each other. Outstanding. She was very pleasant and helpful to the manager who was visiting at the time and a she was also just as rude to men as women I noticed. So not sexist then. A pity really as I have liked the friendly club atmosphere Number 63 has had in the past. The breakfast was overseen and the hot food cooked by a pleasant woman however. I had to return to London a few weeks later and Number 63 was fully booked. I was a bit sorry, but the staff at the place around the corner were so helpful and kind that it was worth the extra 40 pounds a night (without breakfast!). I am returning to London in a couple of months and might stay at Number 63. How can I find out (tactfully) if she is still there? She seemed pretty unhappy, so I truly hope she’s found work that she can enjoy elsewhere. I think it pretty likely. If you recognise her from my description do let me know. This place is really worth giving a chance.

title: Excellent in every way
text: I love this hotel -- the people are so nice, the rooms are sparkling clean and comfortable (though a bit dorm-room size), the buffet and cooked breakfast is wonderful as well as filling and it is about a one minute walk to Lancaster Gate tube station. Lighting is excellent for reading in bed and there are ample electrical outlets around the room and in the bathroom. Wi-fi is complimentary and and stable. The bathroom has a warming rack which is a perfect place to hand things that have been washed out. Water pressure is good and there was never a problem with hot water. One recommendation is to bring two bars of your own soap if you are staying more than a few days - one for the shower, the other for the sink. The soap provided is miniscule - this is understandable as often guests stay just a few days. The hotel is in a listed building so rooms had to be retrofitted. I was in room (single) #311 which faces Kensington Gardens. Though there is air-conditioning available, the rooms facing south may become too hot in summer. Just be aware of this

title: Surprised by Excellent Rating
text: I booked this hotel because of many good reviews, but regret it very much. It is a good value for the price and we were given a happy welcome. After that, the staff was very rude, every day, front desk, kitchen, etc. The breakfast staff was horrible, never a smile. My room was literally the size of a walk-in closet. I was shocked that it would be considered a room - no air, and window completely shut. However, I was upgraded my last night. A bad experience and I cannot recommend it.

title: Great location, great value
text: I stayed here quite a few times when working in this area of London. Its good value for money and the breakfast is lovely. There are plenty of great places to eat nearby and this will always be my first choice when working in this area and needing an overnight stay.

title: to recommand, really!
text: This charming Soroptimist Residential, also open for nonmembers, has a great many advantages: hospitality, helping with all kind of questions about museums/ addresses where to eat etc. And ... the prize of your stay is very affordable and reasonable. The situation is marvellous: view on Hydepark, just cross the street and enjoy a walk to V/A, NHmuseum, Sciencemuseum, Kensingtongardens and so on. Take a taxi just before the hotel within seconds, get your tube 50 meters from the hotel.

title: A Classy Home from Home
text: This lovely hotel takes the stress out of a stay in London! A flat two-minute walk from Lancaster Gate tube brings you to this elegant building. Lovely staff, tasty food and a good selection of drinks make for an enjoyable stay. Rooms are warm and cosy, beds comfy, bathrooms of a very good standard with fluffy towels. To be recommended!

title: Westminster abbey.The london eye.
text: The only complaint for this hotel is that the outside steps would benefit from some lighting. We received a friendly welcome from the staff.Bedrooms were very clean and beds comfy. Breakfast was served in the basement. The service was quick with plenty to choose from. Bus stops nearby for Westminster or Oxford Street. We would recommend this hotel and hope to return.

title: Best in London
text: I've been coming to London for 50 years. The combination of quality, service, price and location makes Number 63 THE best accommodation I've experienced in these last 5 decades. Their standards are impeccable and they try to meet the needs of every guest. Staff bent over backwards to help me with a problem. The rooms are small but certainly big enough for me and have all the amenities expected. The breakfast menu has something for every taste. Location cannot be beat. The tube and bus stop,are steps away--all of London is at your feet.

title: Number 63, Central London
text: This is a lovely boutique 3 star hotel directly across from Hyde Park and 1 minute from the Lancaster underground

title: Always a pleasurable stay
text: I've stayed at 63 many times over the years, in single, twin and family rooms. It's in an excellent position, just accross the street from Hyde park and only a couple of minutes walk from Lancaster Gate underground station. The staff are always friendly, there's a good choice for breakfast. The hotel has a homely, genteel feel to it and feels very safe. I would recommend staying at Number 63

title: Fantastic, friendly staff and great location
text: Number 63 is the perfect location for a London stay. We were travelling for business and the room was a great size, kept very clean and with great tea and coffee making facilities. Beds super comfy and the bath was an added treat. The BEST thing was the included breakfast which was absolutely awesome...its simple but everything was wonderful, from the porridge to the omelette, the Greek yoghurt to the scrambled eggs. We had dinner one evening and this was also great. The location is excellent, very convenient with an easy walk to Monument Square and Oxford Street, and with Hyde Pk over road as well as the tube station just a minute away. Thanks to the great staff for a perfect start to our UK trip 😀.

title: Mrs Elena
text: We would like to thank our lovely hotel Number 63 in London. Stay there for the 3rd time and as always feel secured there and as family guests. It is also great situated near Hyde Park ( we enjoy view from our window) and walking distance from metro and Paddington. Thank You this time for early check in without any problem and looking forward to come again

title: Meeting Room Hire
text: We would like to thank Number 63 for hosting our AGM this year, the staff were friendly and helpful, refreshments were good and the room was clean and professionally presented. This helped our AGM run smoothly in this great location. The room hire rates are very competitive if you need a meeting room in London we would recommend it. The BCMA will be back next year!

title: Home from home.
text: If you are looking for an up to date, cosy, homely place to stay in London rather than a faceless hotel this is great. Small but perfectly formed rooms with all facilities, friendly and welcoming staff, very near Lancaster Gate tube station and a good bus route. Good restaurants nearby but light food and drinks available if needed. No 63 has to be the best value for money in London. I always stay here.

title: Excellent Bed and breakfast
text: I stayed with 7 friends and we all agreed we would gladly return in the future. All could have single rooms at only £75 per night but half price for Sunday on a 3 night stay, which is pretty good for such a great location. The breakfast has most things anyone could wish for including eggs, bacon, beans, toast, fresh fruit, cereals, croissants, brioche, yogurts and more. The staff are friendly and helpful and the location is directly opposite Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens. A very pleasant area, even for someone on their own. The tube station, Lancaster Gate is on the next block and is 4 stops to the city centre. The Swan Pub is almost next door and the Mitre Pub is round the corner, both serving good food at reasonable prices. Kensington Palace is a short walk through the park, as is Kensington High Street. The Victoria and Albert museum is a 20 minute walk away. The rooms are clean but could do with a lick of paint. There is a small licensed bar and a small TV lounge. A lift serves all floors but there are some rooms where there are extra stairs to climb so not suitable for people who are less able. There are a few steps leading up to the front door.

title: Lovely experience
text: Spent three nights (non-consecutive) in three different rooms at Number 63 so I experienced the Bayswater Road side and the quieter rear side of the hotel. All rooms are neat and clean, staff is helpful, and the breakfast in the lower floor dining room was a treat. Talk about tranquil! (Love the green paint and wallpaper!) The breakfast (buffet and made-to-order cooked options included) was one of the best I've had in the UK or Europe. The hotel rates and wonderful location one block from Lancaster Gate and walking distance to Paddington are fantastic. As a note, Number 63 is affiliated with the Soroptimist Club, so it has a quieter club atmosphere and conference room. If you're looking for flash and dash, this may not be the place for you, but if you'd like a quiet, friendly hotel option in a central location, try Number 63.

title: Welcoming, comfortable, safe and great location
text: I've stayed at 63 half a dozen times and keep going back because the staff are really helpful, the rooms are compact but comforable and the location is brilliant. Lancaster Gate tube station- central line - is two minutes away and gets you anywhere and I've never failed to hail a taxi within a minute of stepping out of the front door. Major museums and the Royal Albert Hall are a short ride away. Breakfast is "just right" cooked to order, I've not found anywhere that is better value to money. Finally, as a member of Soroptimist International, there's aways an interesting guest to talk to.

title: Returned visit to No 63
text: We stayed at No 63 again for 8 nights - The staff are excellent, with very clean rooms, serviced daily which leaves more time for discovery of London delights. The Lancaster Gate tube station is only 150 metres from Number 63 so make it very easy to commute from - The bus stops right outside as well. Breakfast is included in the room price which we believe is very reasonable. A pub " The Swan" is about 150 metres which does lovely meals. Walking distance to other restaurants, shops, chemist. Showers are excellent and towels supplied daily if requested. Airconditioning which we needed as the weather was warm (20 - 25 degrees). As our room faced Hyde Park and Baywater Road we found the soundproofing excellent. A new lift has been installed since our last visit - great!! Security is excellent and property well maintained. Breakfast was great - a cooked breakfast (if required), juices, cereal, toast, crossiants, coffee & tea. What more could you ask for. A delightful place to stay thanks to Debbie and her excellent staff. Highly recommend!!

title: Just what I needed
text: I was travelling by myself and felt safe coming and going. My room was small but comfortable. It was warm in London but cooled off in the evenings. I was able to open the window in the room and the temperature for sleeping was fine. Breakfast is either cold items to choose from or a selection of hot items they will make for you. I wish the Lancaster Tube had been open during my stay but the walk from Paddington was very quick. I would definitely stay there again.

title: A lovely B&B across the street from Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park
text: Loved our stay at Number 63! Had a twin room and a double room - both comfortable with great bath facilities en suite. Greeted by wonderful staff, breakfast was delicious, and location fabulous. Arrived from Paddington Station and was a safe and easy walk. Close to several Tube stations. Right across the street from the Italian Gardens -- beautiful. Next door to The Swan for great dinner. Would stay here again!!!

title: Great Location and service
text: Warmly greeted by friendly staff when we arrived. They were more than willing to answer any questions we had. Room was clean and welcoming. Enjoyed breakfast in a beautiful room. The location is perfect. Hyde Park is literally across the street. Could see the Italian Gardens from my mother's single room. Wished we had stayed more than one night.

title: Comfortable little gem
text: I've stayed at Number 63 on multiple occasions when I'm in London for business. It's my first choice when I can get it. As with most London properties, the rooms are on the small side but having said that, the rooms are also well designed to make maximum use of the space and the single beds are comfortable. The en-suite bathrooms are very functional & showers work very well. Location is wonderful for those arriving and/or leaving from Heathrow. As others have written, this is a find within it's price range, including breakfast & an elevator.

title: A great place to stay, friendly and safe
text: Stayed with a friend for a special occasion been here before and it never fails to impress It's so very convenient, safe, clean,friendly and a really great place for a stay in London Reasonably priced it's great value for its location. Staff so very helpful, nothing is too much trouble, and a super location

title: small but perfectly formed
text: Ok, so the rooms are a bit on the "cozy" side. But the location is brilliant, a stones throw from hyde park. Everything is very clean, bed was comfortable, and the staff couldn't be more friendly and helpful. Breakfast is included, great coffee and hot options cooked to order. All in all, excellent value for money, wouldn't hesitate to stay here again.

title: Great intimate event venue in the heart of London
text: I run a small charity called Bread and Water for Africa UK and we needed a small, intimate venue for a donor event for around 30 people. Number 63 provided a beautiful and quiet room for a great price, with projector and interactive whiteboard. Location is optimal as it is minutes from Paddington Station but right in front of the beautiful Kensington gardens. Their catering service was great with different fresh options to choose from. The staff was extremely helpful and accommodating. A great find! We'll use them again in the future!

title: Unbelievable
text: I found this hotel quite by chance on Late Rooms because I had asked for a B&B rather than a hotel. The location was amazing given you are right opposite Hyde Park & Kensington Gardens as well as being almost next door to the tube station. The room was compact although fine for an overnight's stay but the main thing was that it was spotlessly clean. The staff were friendly & the breakfast was excellent. The price for the facilities & the location is amazing. I would definitely consider an overnight stay in future & if I did I would stay here in preference to anywhere else.

title: As a Soroptimist I'm delighted that I have this safe haven in London not just to meet fellow members but all who stay.
text: Excellent situation to all major site s to visit. Caring staff, who will help with anything. Clean, comfortable with good bathroom facilities. I was on the 3rd floor front and because there is air conditioning was able to sleep well with no noise on very hot nights. With key access to front entrance a woman travelling alone can feel quite safe. Taxi drivers used to have this hotel in their knowledge! Dot. Warrington

title: Springtime in London - forget Paris
text: Number 63 - THE very best and most convenient place to stay in London. Very good atmosphere, fine breakfast, nice and clean and friendly helpful staff Walking distance to many things - bus almost at doorstep - TheSwan right next door serves pub food and Kensington garden just across the street. Very reasonable price. What more can you possible need for a long weekend in London Will be back for sure.

title: Surprisingly excellent!
text: For a reasonable price, within 10 mins of Paddington, I didn't expect to be impressed - but this place was faultless. Home from home. Immaculately clean. All the services you'd need for a business overnight stop. Single room, but big enough, with larger-than-average shower cubicle. Charming staff (ciao Leonardo!). Hint: Beware of plastic mattress protectors if you don't like waking up sweaty!

title: Always a pleasure to stay there
text: Simple unpretentious but comfortable and friendly. Room spotless ,nothing is too much trouble and perfect for reasonably priced excellent value accommodation for anyone who seeks a quiet comfortable room without the frills of 24 hour service which most of us don't use nor need.

title: A lovely place to stay
text: I have stayed a number 63 on many occasions. The accommodation is perfect for a short stay in London. It is clean, very comfortable and the staff are friendly and helpful. There is a peaceful ambience at number 63 which is always welcome after a busy day in the hustle and bustle of the city. Number 63 is situated directly opposite Kensington Gardens with its Italian fountain and Peter Pan statue, it is also near to Harrods, the museums and the Royal Albert Hall. On a Sunday you can stroll down Bayswater Road ( again just across the road) and look at the art work. Transport by bus and tube are good, please note that until July 2017 Lancaster Gate is closed for refurbishment. This is a great place to stay, it is easy to book and is good value for money.

title: Great Location
text: Stayed here in a single room for one night after Paul Weller and The Who at Hyde Park. Great little value for money hotel. Yea the rooms are small, yes the Bayswater Road is noisy! But for 75 quid a night you can not complain. Clean and tidy, friendly staff. Highly recommend

title: Great venue for meetings
text: This is an excellent central location for meetings. Room comfortable and facilities very good. Staff are very helpful and friendly. Booking was easy on line. Despite Lancaster Gate tube being closed at the moment there are very good bus connections to 63.

title: Great location, lovely staff and great value
text: Clean, convenient and with really helpful staff, this is a great value, hidden gem right next to Hyde Park. And if you're a runner then you have an easy 5k before your included breakfast - perfect to set you up for a day at work or sightseeing! The staff are also really helpful and kind. Unfortunately Lancaster gate station closed until July but the walk up to Queensway is short or through the Park to Marble Arch.

title: A Great Find!
text: I recently (January of 2017) booked 2 single rooms, one for my daughter and one for me. I have been to London many times but had always stayed in South Kensington or Knightsbridge. My daughter had lived in London during her term abroad several years ago. Neither of us was familiar with this area of London. The location is excellent

title: Single in England
text: 63 B&B was like "coming home" each night. As a single woman staying in London, I felt completely and utterly safe. The staff was more than gracious with providing directions, comfort and security. I felt they genuinely cared about my satisfaction and making me feel at ease and welcomed each time I returned. 63 is PERFECTLY located by a bus station and tube tube station with access to Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens just across the street!! There is a great pub/restrained, The Swan, which made the stay even more wonderful. I will return to 63 in the future. Please consider staying there and say hello to Jessica and Maria. You will be taken care of wonderfully!!

title: Number 63 thoroughly recommended!
text: Wonderful stay at Number 63 where staff were welcoming, friendly, helpful and professional. All went out of their way to help, arranging for me to help myself to breakfast when I had to leave very early three mornings. Immaculate, clean, modern and accessible with good choice of breakfast, afternoon teas, evening snacks etc. Air conditioning was much appreciated especially on the hottest day (and night) for many years. Very good price and being a few doors from tube station made travel easy whilst the park across the road was a delight to visit as an oasis of calm in the bustling city. I will definitely be back and am happy to recommend. Margaret Ross, Aberdeen

title: Debbie Briggs
text: Great place to stay, I keep returning - no reason not to. Ideal location, 5mins from Lancaster Gate tube station, friendly helpful hosts, comfortable bed in a very clean room, great choice at breakfast. What's not to like! Try it & see!

title: Service from the Heart!
text: Debbie, the manager of the hotel, as well as the entire staff are accommodating beyond words. I use their meeting rooms for business and at the end of every reservation, I happily pay them with a huge smile... because they treat me above and beyond what I would ever expect! If this is how kind and generous they are when renting a meeting room, you are sure to be treated as a king/queen if you choose to stay with them during your visit! London sure has "hidden gems" and this is definitely one of them! Thank you Debbie and the entire Number63 staff, I'll only ever sing your praises :)

title: Perfect place to stay in London at a reasonable price
text: I found Number 63 on LateRooms, when looking for a hotel for a night when there wasn't much available for a reasonable price in London. Next time I'll book direct. This was a great find - very clean, friendly staff, good rooms (small - but modern) and great location. Will definitely be booking again.

title: Leisure
text: Accommodation was comfortable and clean. Breakfast was rather enjoyable and not the usual english breakfasts. Location wise it is excellent as it is near a tube station so easy access to shopping areas and museums! The staff was very friendly and courteous. Will definitely come back again.

title: Excellent, comfortable and convenient
text: Everything has been carefully thought of in this convenient and comfortable establishment. Perfect for couples and single travellers alike. Good breakfast and also the possibility of a quiet meal in the evning as well.

title: An Excellent Base
text: I had an excellent stay at Number 63 - a warm welcome, very comfortable room and delicious breakfast with a well presented generous choice of buffet items and also cooked options. The location opposite Kensington Gardens gives easy access to the city and many visitor attractions. There is food available during the day/evening from a limited menu.

title: Perfect place for the solo traveler
text: Number 63 was the perfect place for my stay. As a solo female traveler, I felt so safe being just across the street from the tube station (I used only public transport for my whole trip). The secure entrance to Number 63 was an added bonus. Breakfasts were simple, but very convenient. I dashed downstairs for juice and fruit to-go on mornings when I was in a rush to get to a tour. The location across from Kensington Gardens/Hyde Park is fantastic-- what a beautiful public space! For those traveling from Heathrow, I highly recommend the Heathrow Express train to and from Paddington Station. Paddington is about a 10 minute walk from Number 63, and it was definitely doable with luggage. Number 63 is nothing fancy-- but it is clean, safe, and reasonably priced. A wonderful spot to lay your head down after a day of sightseeing.

title: A hidden gem
text: I stayed here for the first time this week and I will now try and stay at this hotel every time I visit London. It's nothing grand but it is spotlessly clean , in a brilliant location (right next to the tube) - outside the congestion zone on Bayswater Road (easy for the A40) and with wonderful views over Hyde Park. There is also cheap parking available through the hotel next door. Its only small - but I loved it. Highly recommend and I feel like I have discovered a real little treasure.

title: Business and Pleasure
text: In London for a meeting and for my birthday celebrations I spent a comfortable night in a room overlooking Hyde Park, after an easy trip to the National Theatre with friends. Following a delicious breakfast with lots of choice it was an easy stroll down to Notting Hill to meet family for lunch whilst Number 63 held onto my luggage.

title: Pleasure
text: Number 63Bayswater Road,London.This hotel is a hidden gem, the warm welcome received from Manager Debbie plus the superb Breakfast and comfortable, spotlessly clean bedroom made my visit to London so enjoyable. With views of Kensington Park and the excellent transport links just a short distance away were an added bonus.

title: Nice hotel very close to park and tube
text: Lovely hotel. London is expensive! So, for the price, this is a real gem. Very comfortable beds. Slept very well, which was the entire point. So close to the tube station. The hotel is on a busy road, but we still slept very well. With the crowds in London, it felt like an oasis. Staff was very friendly, but not very knowledgable about little things that we would have expected knowledge on--how to get to Heathrow best, how to get from Gatwick to the hotel, etc. All in all, a quiet places to stay that fit our needs. Loved having a toilet and shower in the room. Right on the central line, which made the trip very convenient. Felt very safe as I was traveling alone with my daughter.

title: Clean and close to Hyde park
text: Pros: As previous reviewers have mentioned, the hotel is in a quiet area across from Hyde park and close to the tube. Stayed in a small but nice and well kept room on 3rd floor with a great view of the park. Rooms have tea, tv, and the showers are hot. This hotel also felt quite safe. Prices were good and breakfast was included. Cons: We booked on-line through booking.com and received confirmation. It was not until after we had checked-in that we were told we would have to be moved to two separate rooms for the last night and that the hotel had chosen not to inform us. Not the worst situation, but the front desk really didn't care and were not of much help for anything during our stay. The elevator was also under renovation/ out of service while we were there, which was noisy and could have been a problem for older guests. The single rooms at the back of the hotel were extremely small with no view, and I would not recommend them. Overall, I would stay in this hotel again as it was safe, clean and economical. I just might look at other options first.

title: Warm and friendly
text: Nice cosy room. Great staff - friendly and ready to help. Good service all around but especially on the front desk. I ate there one evening and it was delivered to me room piping hot and delicious. I ll be going back there!

title: A real Gem
text: A few yards from Lancaster Gate Underground, a short walk through Hyde Park to Marble Arch emerging near John Lewis, M&S and Selfridges that's if you don't want to take the Tube. Walk thro the Park to the V&A, Science and Natural History Museums. We walk around the Serpentine in the evening after a hectic day and a good meal. THE HOTEL- wonderful, spotless, friendly, safe the staff are so helpful, like staying with (friendly!) relatives and with a good breakfast. I've stayed here alone and it's the safest place probably because the staff are consistent and caring, this place has non of the anonymity of a much more expensive alternative.

title: great BB in central london
text: When I booked this place I did not expect so much but I was positively surprised when I checked in. Very friendly and attentive staff. I was lucky to get free upgrade to suite room, which was a large room with two separated beds. room was very clean, bathroom a bit small. free coffee and tea sets. very decent breakfast. the elevator was under construction, so you need carry your luggage to upstairs. hotel located about 50 meter from underground Lancaster gate which makes exploring London very convenient. for a very reasonable price, I recommend this place to anyone. I will definitely come back if I need to be in London again.

title: Convenient location and comfortable beds but otherwise poor
text: My room was poor - decent size and reasonably quiet (at the back) but had a leaking tap, the shower temperature (too hot) did not adjust and a broken sash cord meant that I couldn't open the window for ventilation on a stuffy night. Breakfast was ok but served by a rather surly woman. Maybe I was just unlucky with the room I was allocated but they need to maintain the place properly and unless/until they do I won't be back.. Reception isn't manned until 08.30 so if you're checking out before then you have to do it the night before.

title: Hidden gem
text: Perfect little hotel - very attentive staff, very clean, convenient location and great breakfast also. Couldn't fault the place! Would not hesitate to recommend Number 63 to anyone travelling to London.

title: Great value in central London
text: We stayed for 4 nights in June, in twin room on second floor. It was great - conveniently situated, excellent breakfast room, clean and comfortable room. One block from Lancaster Gate tube station. The staff was very helpful and accommodating, especially when I accidentally left without paying - all got straightened out quickly. I especially liked that one could get food and drink on the premises. One night we ordered soup/sandwiches which were served to us in the quiet, comfortable tea room. I will definitely stay here again when in return to London.

title: Home from Home
text: The hotel is immediately opposite the Italian Garden in Hyde Park and within walking distance of Oxford Street and the museums area in Knightsbridge. The warm welcome, good service, comfortable rooms and attention to detail are evident and staff definately go the extra mile to ensure you have a good stay. This hotel is ideal for small families and couples but is particularly suitable for the single traveller. It is very good value for money and far less impersonal than the usual chain hotels.

title: Sue Nichols
text: This was my first visit to 63 and what a find! I visited with 9 other Soroptimist friends from East Grinstead. All old hands! A fantastic central location run by the lovely Debbie and her staff. The lounges are comfortable and relaxing. A lift operates to all floors. The dining room in the basement is modern and airy and breakfasts are cooked to individual order! No platter of fried eggs trying to keep warm on a hotplate! My single room had crisp white bed linen and stylish Roman blinds, flatscreen TV, tea and coffee making facilities, an accessible socket for charging laptops or phones and a hairdryer. The bathroom was tiny but served its purpose. Water pressure in the shower was good. Everywhere was scrupulously clean. On arrival three of us had lunch in the bar - and the best toasted sandwiches ever! All in all a treasure of a place where guests will be made so welcome. Buses and underground on the doorstep and restaurants in adundance. Loads of information leaflets, guided or unguided walks suggested and the staff are so friendly and helpful. Free WIFI.

title: my second home!!!
text: I stay at 63 on average every 7 weeks. I use the conference room for reflexology training and stay over in the safest, most cosy hotel in London. The staff are all very friendly, professional and most helpful in all situations. There are rooms that look over the beautiful park if you want a view or if you prefer a quieter room ones at the back. If you let the hotel know they will do their utmost to accommodate you. It is exceptionally clean, a lovely breakfast/dining room with more than enough choice to satisfy everyone. Special diets are catered for too. And everyone says "Good Morning" to you! I use the cosy TV lounge for relaxing or doing my work of an evening. Sometimes I just chat the evening away with someone I met that day. Many an interesting evening has been spent in this way :) After 12 years of visiting it is my "London" home and would actively encourage you to try it :) The location is 2 mins from Lancaster Gate tube, 20 mins lovely walk to Kensington Palace, 25 mins through the park to Harrods! Plus close to lots of other attractions and very nice well priced restaurants.

title: It was OK
text: I stayed at this hotel because of the good reviews, and I have to say, it was just ok. I had a room facing Bayswater road, which was very noisy. The breakfast was a bit awkward, not enough tables for how many rooms they have. I had to share a table with another guest, which was a first for me on my 5-week trip around the UK in many b&b's & hotels. Check-out is at 11:00, but I already had housekeeping knocking on my door at 10:00. Overall, this hotel was fine for the price, but nothing special. Ask for a room at the back if you don't want to hear traffic all night.

title: My London 'home'
text: Every time I visit London which is four or five times a year, I arrive at Number 63 and feel I am coming home. The staff are friendly, very kind and helpful

title: Best value in central London
text: Stayed here a few times over the years and it is consistently good. Always clean, quiet and welcoming. Staff very helpful, food and drink very reasonable and good choice for breakfast with some hot food. It is a little gem that stands out from the so-so fare too often seen in London.

title: Absolute WOW but it's a secret
text: Just got back from a brilliant 2 days in London. It was a boys 2 day trip. I use the term boys very loosely as it was my sons birthday treat. We picked Number 63 as I had previously stayed there a few years ago when it was a club for Scoroptomists. My late mother was a member. Since my last visit the whole place has kept the culture and ambience the same but brought the accommodation upto date. It is an absolute brilliant place to stay. We couldn't fault a thing. I've stayed in places costing twice as much and they haven't been in the same league. I wouldn't stay anywhere in London other than Number 63.

title: Great B&B by the Park!
text: Stayed with my daughter prior to her going to the University. Location was great, either walking or taking the Tube to various parts of London. Room was clean and quite, we had a great view of Hyde Park. The staff was very helpful in booking our room and offering advice on getting from the airport to the hotel as this was our first time in London. We arrived early and were able to check into our room! Breakfast was wonderful and the staff is very friendly. I would certainly stay again if in London!

title: Don't tell anyone about this hotel! Keep it a secret!
text: I hate to let this secret get out because it will become so in demand I won't be able to get rooms there any more. Everything said below is true: immaculately clean, quiet, centrally located, friendly, helpful staff, free, full English breakfast, late-night meals available, small bar, close to a famous pub (The Swan) and a small convenience store, four blocks from a major international restaurant street (Queensway). Trip Advisor asks really dumb questions that cannot be answered yes or no. "Is it quaint?" What the hell does that mean? It's historic. "Is it good for families?" It has some double rooms, so a family might have to book more than one. But if you have bratty kids I'll get you arrested. "Does it have a restaurant?" Yes, but it's open only for breakfast. At other times you take your meal in the small common room. "Does it have air conditioning?" How am I supposed to know? I was there in March. "Is it a B&B?" Trip Advisor would shine in a contest for most-useless stupid questions. Most London accommodations are dingy, dreary, and expensive. This is the opposite: bright, cheerful, and affordable.

title: So welcoming!
text: I found this hotel on line by chance and I am so glad I did. the staff were so kind and helpful throughout my stay. I arrived earlier than expected, but was allowed to check in and leave my luggage in the room (even though it hadnt been cleaned). This saved me having to trek back and fore across London half way through the day inorder to check in. The room was a single a room, but perfect for me. Everything was designed to maximise the use of space. My room was at the front of the hotel overlooking Hyde Park. The main road was a little noisy during the night, however the secondary glazing (and my ear plugs) made for a good night's sleep. I like a dark room so also wore an eye mask. Everthing was clean and tidy. Breakfast was good - nothing extravegant, but all fresh - and even Fairtrade products available! I travelled alone and have already booked to return later in the year with my two young teenage daughters.

title: Excellent as always
text: Having stayed at Number 63 for over 10 years on regular occasions cannot speak highly enough of the excellent service from Debbie and the team - only downside is not booking early enough and been disappointed when Number 63 is full - well done everyone.

title: A place to keep coming back to
text: Number 63 is a small and friendly hotel. I have stayed from time to time over the past 30 years or so. It is nice to see the care which the Soroptimist owners have put into keeping it up to date but in tune with its original character. It is well connected by bus and tube to the main stations and sight seeing centres and at one of the key entrances to Hyde Park. If you want a choice of breakfast focussed on the continental rather than 'full English" this is the place for you! -Though you can get eggs bacon and beans - together or on their own with toast etc. I had some excellent porridge this morning. Staff -and guests - are friendly and helpful.

title: Very comfortable a "Peace Haven" in a busy city
text: Two of us stayed in the family room at the back of the property, it was lovely & quiet, & felt so safe & so nice to return to after a busy time in London city. The location across from Hyde Park is such a delight. The tube station is just a stone's throw away & so convenient. The staff were all very friendly & couldn't be more helpful & knowledgeable. The half price offer on Sunday night was "the icing on the cake" & much appreciated & allowed us that extra night. All in all a great venue & we will return. This is my third visit here & it is much better than I remember as it has been refurbished.

title: Great Location and Service
text: I thought Number 63 was a great hotel because of its central location (across the road from Hyde Park), close proximity to the Lancaster Gate Station, clean rooms with good views, and caring and attentive staff-it's also good value for money. Number 63 felt more than just another hotel because of the wonderful staff and perhaps the great history behind this hotel (owned I think by the Soroptimist International). I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Great location
text: Spotlessly clean, comfortable beds, gleaming bathroom with good water pressure and wonderfully central - after a 20 minute walk I was at Bond Street. Our room was towards the back so although it didn't have a view of Hyde Park, it was very quiet.

title: A really cozy home from home
text: This is the second time that I have stayed at Number 63 when visiting London. This is more than your typical B&B. Number 63 is like a second home. The room, while compact, is clean, neat and tidy with everything that you may need for your stay. I had a great view across Bayswater Road to Hyde Park beyond. The bathroom is brand new and has a real working, fully mirrored modern ‘medicine chest so that all ones toiletries and paraphernalia is out of sight and where you can get it instantly. Despite the main road the double glazing ensures an almost total lack of outside sound. Even with the December cold outside I didn’t have to resort to the room heating – it was really warm and cozy. Breakfast was more than adequate in a neat modern fully equipped dining room. The staff are friendly and helpful. I really liked the outside security arrangement with access to the property being controlled with your room access card. Access to all London’s amenities couldn’t be better. Lancaster Gate Tube Station is across the road, while Paddington Station is an easy ten-minute stroll away. A really enjoyable stay.

title: Hidden gem at Lancaster Gate
text: Fantastic small hotel - friendly Staff - good bedroom - immaculately clean and great location!! I'd thoroughly recommend No 63 for any business traveller looking for well-priced accommodation in the West End of London.

title: A little gem!
text: Second time we've stayed at 63 when we've been visiting London. Lovely clean rooms, friendly staff and excellent location. Breakfast good - nothing fancy - but good, fresh food. Booking online was easy and reception staff really helpful when we arrived.

title: Home in London
text: I've stayed there several times, and I'm really feel like home in London. Awsome location. The staff is excellent. The rooms are clean . Breakfast is delicius. Great view of the Hyde Park , neat to a lot of points of interest

title: Wanted to keep this info to myself...
text: What a great place. I wanted to keep this info to myself so that it doesn't become so popular, but thought about those whose reviews helped me find this gem so I couldn't be selfish! First, this is not a place for families or romantic couples. I believe the majority of rooms are single. This is a solid place for business people or tourists who want a spotless room, albeit small. Great location, good breakfast to start the day, and a general feeling of safety. My room was very small but very functional. It was spotlessly cleaned everyday I returned tired to my room after a day of touring. The bed was comfortable and, though the soundproofing between rooms may not have been the best, remember these are old Edwardian residences chopped up into BBs, the clientele were so genteel that everyone was respectful of noise that all I heard through the wall was a little coughing. This will be my first choice when returning to London. It is a very reasonable for an incredibly expensive city. Just a shout out to Maria and the young girl who work the breakfast room. Very friendly and accommodating. A nice smile to start the day!

title: An only elevator Beaufort has was out of order
text: We arrived on 12 April 2019 at around 8pm. There was the only 1 lady staff there when we arrived. So we had to wait in front of the front door for quite some time before a kind tenant opened the front door for us. Unfortunately, the only elevator of Beaufort was out of order and our apartment was on the 7th floor when we arrived. And we had around 10 large luggages. The lady staff asked us to wait until 11pm for a male staff to arrive and he would help us carry all those luggages up 7 floors by stairs. We could not wait for that long as we have a 6-year old and a 10-year old kids who need to take a shower and go to bed before 11pm. So we ended up carrying all those luggages by ourselves up 7 floors to our apartments . A staff lady helped us with 2 luggages and then she was then disappeared, but we didn’t mind that. Who would want to carry heavy large luggages up 7 floors anyway. We are the returning customers to this place almost every year. This time was the worst one. My husband and my nanny have got backache from carrying all those luggages up 7 floors. Also, in our reservation form, we have paid for the 3 bedroom and 2.5 bathrooms. But we got 3 bedroom and 2 bathrooms. Other than that, we are ok with everything .

title: Family visit
text: From the first minute of our arrival, we felt we are very welcomed by the front office staff, we felt that arrived in our home, and that was every day. The apartment was always clean, and better than our expectation, the size of rooms and facilities in the apartment was really better than any in London. Location as well, was excellent Thanks to all staff Ali Al Marzooqi UAE , Abu Dhabi

title: The best !!!
text: As always, we finished our trip with a great feeling about The Beaufort House. The staff is wonderful, the location the best and the accommodations are top quality. Thanks to all the staff for making us feel welcome and as being home. See you soon !!

title: London Luxury Apaprtment
text: Stayed in a 3 BR with a family of five in August 2011. Very conveniently located, very clean and luxurious with recent renovation. Thei staff was particularly excellent and very friendly.

title: Home away from home
text: I stayed in Beaufort house for a festive break with my friends and I can easily say this is one of my best hotel stays in London. The hotel is clean and well maintained and the apartments are luxurious. The staff was so warm and welcoming,It certainly did feel like home away from home. Will be returning soon with family.

title: Fantastic
text: Great vacation stay. Location was perfect and all of the staff was wonderful. The rooms were clean and having maid service was great. Staff very helpful with restaurants and car service. I would and have recommended the Beaufort House to everyone who I know is traveling to London. Thank you for a winderful vacation

title: Delightful
text: Two couples shared an apartment for 10 days. Everything was first class. We have stayed in apartments all over the world and the comfort and amenities here are excellent. Not lush and over the top, but clean, and well taken care of, with a great location. My only concern is that smoking is allowed in the apartments. I am very sensitive to cigarette smoke. Our apartment did not have an odor but I would be very upset if I came again and it was a problem. I wish this was a smoke free property like others I have been in.

title: A really good experience
text: This is an expensive and first class property. We stayed a week and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. It is a quality flat in anybody's book and made us feel special every time we entered. The staff is excellent, always very friendly and helpful. The concierge helped us book West End shows and fine restaurants and we got excellent seats. Daily room service. No parking that I'm aware of. Absolutely terrific location in Knightsbridge, almost next to Harrod's. Plenty of very close restaurants and a tube station. A memorable visit.

title: Wonderful easy service, great accomodation
text: The staff are just wonderful. Very easy to deal with and the accomodation is well maintained and excellent. The location is good and quick to all Westerly parts of London. I unable to find any fault

title: After 10 years, disappointed
text: Like many others I have been visiting Beaufort for a long time. First with my wife, then the kids and now occasionally on my own when in London. I think nostalgia for post visits had left me a little blinded to the quality. Sadly it has become a bit worn and jaded. It still is convenient and spacious, but time has taken its toll and London has moved on. I regret to say that I will be staying elsewhere next time as London has too much to offer, considering the rates. Best wishes to the Beaufort I I hope they can recapture that special sparkle.

title: Great Place
text: My wife and I and sometimes our children have stayed at Beaufort House multiple times and will continue to do so when in London. Its convenient location, friendly service, and clean, well furnished accommodations leave nothing to be desired.

title: Home Away From Home
text: I have been staying at the Beaufort House for years and it never disappoints. The staff is wonderful and we were greeted with hugs from Kanny, our long time friend. Kanny, went out of her way to make sure our apartment suited our needs. It was well appreciated. The location is absolutely 5 star and practically next door to Marks and Spencer food store, Waitrose and Nespresso, which makes filling the kitchen so easy. The welcome basket of bread, cereals, biscuits, coffee, tea, milk, juice, butter and much more is amazing. The bathrooms and kitchen are spotless and well stocked. There are wonderful restaurants in the area as well. The beds are comfortable. The living spaces are feeling a little worn and could use a make-over but are by no means shabby. I have stayed in the 2 bedroom and 3 bedroom apts at this wonderful hotel and would never consider staying anywhere else.

title: Second stay not as good
text: Stayed here six months ago and loved it. This time things had slipped. The room we stayed in and our friend’s room smelt very strongly of cigarettes. Staff said there as nothing they could do. The staff all smoke on the front steps of the hotel which makes it even worse. The welcome basket was missing the bread. The housekeeping was also not as thorough as previously.

title: Homey in London
text: We have been coming to Beaufort House for more than 10 years. The place is very homey and well decorated. Nice and warm but slightly cooler for three bedrooms on top floor. Staffs are super friendly and helpful. There is one staff who has been there for more than years. She was very helpful and kind. This is a very nice place very close to Harrods.

title: Great Space for Kids and Thank You Sitara
text: Beaufort House is a fantastic space for children's parties. I wanted to specially commend Sitara who is extroardinarily sweet and has always gone out of her way to be accomodating to our children and is a true credit to the venue.

title: We found a gem in Knightsbridge
text: My husband and I have been for 2 times in the past month in The Beaufort House and we couldn't have been more pleased with our choice. We really felt we had a home in London!! we really prefer to stay in self catering than hotels, because we like more the home feeling. The location is great...steps from Harrods and all the shops in Brompton Rd, the museums, restaurants and M&S. The apartments are beautiful, modern and with all the amenities you need. We really couldn't ask for more. Our apartment had 3 bedrooms (each one with its own bathroom, TV, IPod player and even a own terrace), separate living and dining room and a modern kitchen. Housekeeping was very efficient and comes everyday so the apartment is always clean, very nice ladies. Our many thanks to Juan, the manager, and to the whole staff, they all made both our stays wonderful and we will be back soon without doubt. The are all very nice and helpful, got wonderful restaurant reservations and even got us 2 tickets in a very popular theather play :) Really we couldn't be more happy.....we have to come to London on a frequent basis for family reasons, and this is our new home !!

title: 20 day stay
text: I want to thank Maddy and all the staff at Beaufort house for an amazing 20 day stay. My family stayed here on a recent trip ( checked out yesterday) everything was perfect. Greta staff great location and everything else to go with it. Honestly highly recommend these apartments. A very professional service! Many thanks from Nadia and her Trunkwala Family.

title: Perfect family accomodation in London!
text: We are family of four - including two adult daughters. We wanted something spacious enough to feel "homey" for an extended stay in London -- with separate bed rooms for our daughters. We also didn't want to have to eat out for every meal -- so we wanted a proper kitchen. Beaufort House was a great fit for our needs. We had a three bedroom executive suite -- which had plenty of room including a nice family room, a dining room, a kitchen and two and a half first rate bathrooms. The suite was very clean and comfortable -- and everything worked. The kitchen was a little tight -- but had everything we needed to prepare full meals for the four of us. There is a M&S food store just around the corner which is very convenient for buying groceries. There was also a combination clothes washer/dryer in the kitchen. It worked well -- and saved us a lot of packing. We just washed some clothes every few days. The suite included a free internet -- both wired and wireless -- that worked very well. The location was excellent. We had some great restaurants, shops, parks and museums within easy walking distance. We also had a tube station nearby. The girls quicky got used to coming and going on their own. Included with the suite is access to a fitness facility about five minutes away. This is a first class facility with fitness machines and a swimming pool. We used it a lot to burn off all the "clotted cream" we were eating! The staff were very friendly -- and helpful. We got plenty of help with our bags -- without having to ask for it. The only complaint we have is that the heating/cooling units in the bedrooms are a little noisy for sleeping. So -- we just turned them off at night which didn't seem to effect the temperature very much. Otherwise, the location is very quiet.

title: Home From Home
text: We usually stay in a hotel requiring 2/3 rooms for the whole family. This time we decided to take an apartment at this delightful residence and boy we were not disappointed - this place is beautiful and the staff equally as wonderful. Completely unexpected but 'The welcome pack' of bread, cereal, tea, coffee, juice, water and milk (and more) made us feel instantly at home and in no rush to get out and purchase the essentials.
