title: Great Place to Start and End the Day
text: We came here from the States to visit family in London. A big group of us stayed here and it was a totally wonderful experience. We started everyday with a lovely sunny breakfast, had fun in London and then ended the day at the pub and then off to bed - all in one place. The staff are friendly and attentive, the rooms are clean and comfortable, the food is excellent and the property itself is really cool.

title: Close to Richmond Park.
text: I needed to find a cheap and cheerful room for a quick overnight stay, so I was thrilled to find The Victoria. My room was very spacious and for £108 was probably twice the size of a hotel room in Central London and for half the price. The lady who showed me to my room was wonderfully friendly and absolutely insisted on carrying my luggage for me. Fabulous hot shower and plenty of large towels in the bathroom. Large comfy bed. Huge complimentary bottle of mineral water. Tassimo coffee machine was great. I loved the freshly baked cranberry and white chocolate cookies too. Such a lovely idea. The hotel is located on a quiet side street. If you didn't know it was there then you'd probably never find it. Most wonderfully it is only a few minutes walk from Richmond Park. I used the 493 bus from the main road to get into central Richmond and Richmond station or it's a 20 - 30 minute walk. I'm not able to comment on the food as I didn't try any. I couldn't even have my free breakfast as I had to check out before they started serving and I wasn't offered anything 'to go'. Sadly I was disturbed by noise which has lowered my rating. It sounded like someone in a nearby room was moving furniture around at about 10pm and the noise of what sounded like a thousand bottles been dropped into a bin just outside my window definitely did not go unnoticed. I would be very happy to stay here again though.

title: A great stay
text: Stayed for 3 nights. Was very well looked after and the staff were all very pleasant and helpful. Breakfast was continental with plenty of items to choose. The whole place was very welcoming and I would definitely stay here again.

title: A great find
text: Stumbled on this place by accident on the way to walk round Richmond park. So glad we did! Friendly staff, wonderful food amazing wine menu all at reasonable prices and only a 10 min walk from my house. Will definitely be going back just to make sure it really was that wonderful!

title: Good but not as good as it could be
text: Has the potential to be an excellent place to stay. We were there for two nights. Staff friendly, place fairly well kept although we're slow to clear tables/dishes at breakfast. Rooms were a decent size and bed was comfortable but the bathroom let it down a bit. Shower didn't drain very well (room 5) so you were stood in a puddle throughout and the temperature was temperamental which got a bit annoying. In fact the whole shower unit would benefit from a bit of TLC or refurbishment. Having said that it was all clean which is a plus. Noise wasn't an issue despite being under Heathrow flight path. Breakfast was better than some places but only continental was included for the £85/night - cooked was £8.50 extra if you wanted anything other than cereal, toast, fruit or meats (salami etc). No yoghurts, croissants etc. We weren't disappointed but we would consider other options before staying there again.

title: Lovely family lunch
text: We had a great family lunch here. The burger wash absolutely deeeelish and the service was amazing. We had a lovely blonde waitress serving us who was so helpful and kind. Thank you for such a lovely lunch!!

title: Wonderful Place to Be
text: We stayed at the Victoria because my husband had business in the area. What a delightful inn and pub. It's been located in this neighborhood for over a hundred years and feels like you've stepped back in time when you walk in the door and see warm fires blazing and people visiting. The neighborhood now is very upscale. There is a school behind the building and after school on Friday the pub was filled with Moms and their children. The wait staff were dispensing hot chocolate and crisps right along with the coffee. Such a treat to see everyone having such a good time. Our room was #7 in the small hotel/inn located behind the pub. We were very comfortable there and the staff couldn't have been nicer. Sammy took us under her wing and helped us get to the places we needed to go. She even went to the trouble to write out the train times and exact directions about how to get from here to there. When we asked for a taxi to Mortlake train station, one was called and arrived promptly. The service was exceptional - beyond anything ever expected! The food was outstanding. Excellent presentation! We loved everything we had. Even the continental breakfast was great.

title: fantastic break in London
text: My husband and I were visiting London for a friends wedding and this was close to Richmond park so we decided to come a night early have a relaxing meal and stay over for two nights. On arrival we were shown to our room which was a reasonable size.The welcome we received was really nice, the staff seemed We had dinner reservations and were sat in the conservatory,The meal was fantastic, great choice of dishes with old favourites sat besides new innovative dishes, the scallops were divine, My husbands rib eye melted in the mouth and if I wasn't married i'd have run away with the chef just for the chips! The wine list had a really good selection.This was one of the best meals we have had in a very long time. After our wheel we retreated back to our room for a restful nights sleep, we were woken at 7am, slightly rudely by the noise, banging doors and general noise.Not a huge problem but we were hoping for a lie in.The bathroom in the room was very small and the shower was in need of a refurb as was a bit weak and the cubicle was very small. Breakfast, upgraded to a full English.Wow.Food is very much the Victoria's thing , the breakfast was gorgeous, Well worth the £6.50 extra.We didn't eat again until 6pm! We stayed another night and had another early morning wake up but otherwise everything was great.

title: Delicious food, great service
text: I went to the Victoria for my birthday meal with my family, after being recommended it from a friend. The food was delicious and great value for money (Sunday lunch) and the staff were so friendly, it really made a great lunch. They even put a candle in my bread and butter pudding (without being asked) when they realised it was my birthday. I would thoroughly recommend.

title: Lovely stay!
text: Stayed here over night with my partner on the 21st of Feb 2017. We planned to go into London for the day, we got a taxi to the tube station which ranged between £8 and £12, it was only about a 10 min drive. From there it's pretty much direct to the Centre of London. We stayed here as it is so much cheaper than the centre of London and planned to go to harry potter world the next day which is about a 30 minute drive away. We were both so impressed with the hotel & pub. It's a proper little cozy pub with a great overall atmosphere to it. I have read so many reviews about rude staff and honestly I didn't have a single problem, they were all so lovely and welcoming, especially the lovely lady (which I can't remember the name of) works both behind the bar and sorts out food & breakfast. Also seen a lot of people complaining about breakfast. You get continental breakfast within the price, which is great for the price and location of the hotel. There was a great spread- bread, cereal, cold meats and cheese. We paid extra for a fry up, at only £8 ish, which is totally worth the money as it was lush! Great eggs. Tea, coffee and juices whenever we needed which was also fab. We had no problem at all with the sound of any planes, I am quite a light sleeper and I didn't wake up from the noise of one so I'm not sure why everyone is complaining. With staying in London, you have to expect to hear planes as London is surrounded in flight paths so I think that any complaint about the sound of planes is stupid as it's practically impossible to avoid. The rooms were lovely and clean too. Bed was comfortable and duvet was so heavy (which I love). The hotel leave home made cookies out each day which is an awesome touch. We had lunch at the pub, got Calamari, Chicken wings and the bread and dip selection to share between us, came to £30 which is cheaper than what we would have spent in London. The food was excellent and worth the money. Overall, we had a fab stay and next time we go to London for the night we will definitely stay back in The Victoria.

title: Great food but disappointing service and very noisy airplane traffic from Heathrow
text: We went there for lunch few weeks ago and really enjoyed the food and service so we decided to return for a 2 night stay at the INN. The woman who was working those days was extremely unfriendly and rude. We couldn't believe how someone could allow that type of behavior around customers. The INN was ok but too loud, it's located right underneath the main flight path in and out of Heathrow so you need to listen to airplanes fly low above your room 24/7. Main menu was good but breakfast was very disappointing / low quality.

title: OK but.....
text: Pleasant place right under one of the Heathrow flight paths (expect to be woken before 6 if the routing is not in your favour!). Modest room, comfortable bed, small bathroom. Very basic toiletries and in room coffee. Good breakfast, but this does not make up for the high price for what you get. Friendly staff and quiet (apart from planes) location. Beware of the description on the internet booking form, the rooms are not described separately and you may not get the location or bed size you see. Cancellation terms are extremely confusing. Overall this place majors on the food - which is good.

title: Sunday drinks turned expensive
text: Recently moved to sheen and stumbled across The Victoria for Sunday drinks. Lovely and cosy until we paid our tab with a £5 extra service charge! A bit ridiculous seeing as I went to the bar to buy the drinks and just added to tab... shame as nice pub but enough to not want to go back.

title: I would return in a hurry !!!
text: Three friends and I stayed recently ,we were down for the England ,New Zealand rugby match . We arrived at lunchtime and the place had a real warm buzz to it ,real fires burning ,people eating and chatting away we loved it . We had four rooms which were all of a great standard and spotlessly clean,breakfast was also fabulous,fantastic coffee . The selection of real ales and wines were great,we cant wait to visit later in the year . I wish The Victoria was at the bottom of my road !!!

title: Good Place for Family Pub Lunch
text: We had lunch here on a Saturday before walking in the nearby Richmond Park. The place is also dog friendly. We were struck by how many families there were with small children. The staff were friendly and attentive and the traditional pub food was freshly cooked. The staff were very tolerant of the large numbers of small children and dogs! The interior design is bare floor boards and plain tables, but it has an authentic pub feel . It serves some unusual ales. We did not see the rooms. The pub toilets were spotless. Parking is available both behind the hotel and in the street.

title: Its all down to the room
text: I have to say that I was disappointed. We had Room 1 on the ground floor. It has a window out towards the kitchen, so the curtain needs to be shut all the time. The room had no pictures, prints or anything on any walls and looked really stark. The carpet was stained again (see earlier review) and thats as there is no door mat or the like and coming from the outside straight onto a cream carpet is bound to lead to disaster ! The towel rail didnt work in the bathroom, which was cramped. BUT The staff were all without exception charming. Dinner was good, especially the crab and mackerel. Breakfast was excellent, truly excellent and included in the price. This was the only hotel anywhere in London on the mid week night I stayed with any availability at a decent price, so was a saviour. I fell bad rating it as average, but that's what it was.

title: A little bit of a lottery in the making . . .
text: Like many people, we popped into this quaint pub for lunch after a long walk in Richmond Park. So the great things were

title: Really professional
text: Unfortunately there was an issue with the kitchen not being able to function due to refurbishment. I was informed of this prior to my arrival and told of alternative establishments to eat. They also gave me a reduction on my room rate. The room was brilliant. The staff were attentive and professional. I really can't fault them. I have booked again later this week and will use them when working in the area. Well done......

title: Friendly Pub
text: I called in recently with relatives for a coffee and beer. The staff were friendly and very helpful and the drinks served promptly and brought to our table. The seating was comfortable and although the abience was somewhat muted (the pub was quite empty) the relative silence made for easy conversation. Although we didn't eat the menu looked quite appetising and reasonably priced. I will update you all if and when we do eat here.

title: Hide and seek
text: Hard to find, tucked away in the leafy suburbs of South West London, surrounded by spectacular houses and Richmond park, sits The Victoria. This was our fifth visit in three years. . . and it's still hard to find. . but joy. . . service, quality of food, value for money and ambience have not changed one iota. Great for lunch and excellent for dinner.

title: Sunday lunch
text: For our second visit we came on Sunday and after a few drinks we let the staff convince us to tried the two roasts. And we glad we tried. The roast is as good as the A la carte dishes and we had a very enjoyable meal.

title: Fabulous Find
text: On business in the area and decided to visit Kew Gardens and stay over. What a find. Lovely room, not large, but very nicely done, and amazing garden with outside kitchen. Fab food and lovely helpful staff who found us the nicest driver ever to take us to Kew. Would certainly visit again if in the area, but make sure you like planes if you plan to eat outside, as they are constant, didn't worry us, but may be a concern for some. Couldn't hear them at night though.

title: East Sheen's Hidden Gem!
text: This was our third visit to the Victoria and we have been met each time by warm and friendly staff who go out of their way to make you feel relaxed. On previous visits we have enjoyed the cosy atmosphere in winter months with the fires lit but this time the weather was gorgeous and we were able to sit in their amazing out door area sampling their summer menu. The atmosphere was equally as relaxed and, as on previous visits, the food was faultless. The menu is constantly updated in line with seasonal produce but if you ever get to taste their mussels steamed in cider, they are to die for! The staff are attentive but not overpowering and the whole experience just flowed with no apparent pauses between courses or our conversation! Totally relaxed and wished we could have stayed longer!

title: Wonderful wedding...
text: Greg and the team gave us the perfect wedding reception. The revenue looked fab already and all we had to add were some flowers, storm lanterns and a couple of personal bits and pieces. The food was according to our mate James, "by far the best food I've ever had at a wedding - the cheese board was out of this world". But what really made it special was the service. Everyone from the team got into the spirit of the day and couldn't have done more for us. Thank you again.

title: Room for improvement
text: Utterly delightful pub. Food great and staff lovely... but woefully few of them for which they apologised profusely bless them. Booked an outside table only to be told on arrival that they don't take bookings for outside tables. Bit odd. One thing to be aware of is this is a "child friendly" pub with a play area at the back right next to the dining tables. Sign says it's for use by toddlers until 17.00 but it was still open at 21.00 and far older children were in there unsupervised and screaming to their hearts' content. Don't get me wrong, I love to see children in pubs with their parents, as happens everywhere else in Europe, but we don't seem to have got the hang of it here! Beer was lovely and food gorgeous and will definitely go back but there's room for improvement on the management front as the staff need some support. The main guy running the place was doing an amazing job with the resources available to him.

title: Perfect
text: Had a short stay over night here , was welcoming , clean and a lovely place with nice food , the staff are helpful and friendly and the rooms are priced well clean comfortable will definitely stay again , as the location is close to all attractions

title: Super Stay in Suburbia
text: This is a super place to stay in the London suburbs in a quiet location with easy acess to public transport for London. Staff are very friendly and welcoming and the hotel has pleasantly decorated rooms that have pc's with free internet access. Dinner was fresh and tasty at expected London prices and the bonus was enjoying a nightcap in the bar afterwards before retiring for a goods night sleep in the very comfy beds. Breakfast was a slight disappointment with minimal choice.

title: Friendly & comfortable
text: The Victoria is in a quiet area with no passing noise late at night. A clean, well equipped room with REALLY comfortable bed - I had an exceptionally good nights sleep. This is a perfect base to explore Richmond, Kew, Twickenham, Wimbledon & Hampton Court. Richmond Park is literally at the end of the road - an ideal place to work up an appetite before dinner in The Victoria.

title: Pub accommodation in family friendly area
text: We recently stayed at The Victoria Hotel for 4 nights. Our room was spacious and comfortable, with a compact but spotless bathroom. The hotel has off street parking for guests, which is a true bonus. Continental breakfast, which offered a good variety of choice, was included in the rate- guests could also choose to pay extra for a cooked breakfast. We were assisted by Jeremy on arrival and found him to be extremely friendly and helpful. We also found the weekday morning waitress to be lovely.

title: Nice place, great food.
text: We booked this hotel for a family visit to London . There were 7 of us altogether. We had four rooms all of which were very nicely decorated. Our daughters shared a room on the ground floor which was the largest of the four rooms. It was very spacious with a nice sized bathroom and lovely comfortable bed, the down side was that the window looked out on the passage way to the other bedrooms and was very near the kitchen so was quite noisy if you had the window open and quite dark. The other 3 rooms were all smaller but lighter, big enough but with very small bathrooms with inadequate lighting. The towel rails were on the wall above the loo resulting in one towel ending up the the loo during the course of the weekend! The beds in those rooms were a disappointment. They were wooden frames with very firm mattresses meaning they were not comfortable to sleep on. The mattresses didn't fit the frames properly and the framing at the end of the bed was covered with a throw, which looked nice but because you couldn't see the bed frame which stuck out quite a long way, at least 2 of us bumped in to the frames ending up with large bruises on our legs.The rooms were very warm. In the two rooms upstairs we were able to leave the windows open at night which helped but downstairs we didn't like to as it didn't feel safe, especially as one was accessible from the carpark. In all the rooms, even the upstairs rooms it could be quite noisy, mainly from the kitchen/waiting staff, I don't think they realised quite how the noise traveled. On the upside, the food was fantastic! We had a beautiful 3 course meal on the Friday evening when we got there, everything was perfect, not a single complaint, which is unusual for us! The cooked breakfast was very good too, the only disappointment was the price we had to pay for it. We knew there was a supplement for a Full English breakfast but when we came to pay the bill it was more than we had been expecting (although this was rectified), but not as much as the full price on the menu, however, if you had any other cooked breakfast you were charged full menu prices rather than just a supplement which we doesn't seem fair. Don't get me wrong, we enjoyed our stay, the staff were lovely and very helpful, it is a lovely place in a lovely area and the food (however much we were charged) was beautiful. We would recommend it to friends and family but would warn them about the beds and the overpriced breakfast!

title: Sunday dinner
text: Loved the food and the venue, which is simple yet cosy. The only thing I would do differently is perhaps to visit for Sunday lunch when it'll be busier and therefore more of an ambiance. On Sunday evening it was kind of empty. The food was superb. Go and try it.

title: A surprisingly lovely and modern B&B
text: We stayed here for one night and the room was very clean, modern. Funky prints and carpet up to the 7 hotel rooms. Everything is very compact and cosy but the decor is stunning, bed was comfortable and the free cookies and large section of coffee, tea and water is welcome. I haven't stayed in a pub B&B for years on the basis that they're all bit quaint and old fashioned, but this blew me away. Very impressed. At £135 for one night, it is pricey but as a special treat it was lovely. We only ate in the pub in the morning for breakfast. I had eggs benedict and my husband had poached egg on toast with bacon. The only small gripe was that the food was just not warm enough, I think it may have been left out on the side too long, but as everything else was lovely, we didn't complain. But note to chef - please serve your food hot!! Thanks

title: Great Place
text: Really love this place, the food is outstanding, as are the staff. Great location very close to Richmond Park

title: Very Nice Gastro Pub Restaurant!!
text: Experience: we wanna have a Friday night out for a simple yet nice meal and selected Victoria based on good reviews from others. we were seated at a window corner seat. ordered starter - shrimp on toast (to share)

title: Fantastic Wedding Reception
text: We have known the Victoria for a number of years as a place to have a good meal or a drink after a walk in Richmond Park. We know it as a relaxed gastro pub where the food and service is always good. As a result we chose it for our Wedding reception. Greg, Paul, and the team headed by Marek, did a fantastic job from start to finish. The personal attention we received to make sure that the day was tailored exactly to our requirements was exceptional. They have a long standing stable team of staff who clearly wanted to make the day a success and as enjoyable as possible for everyone. Our guests thought the venue and food was fantastic and judging by the amount of beer drunk - the beer as well! We cannot recommend them highly enough. S&K

title: Superb, friendly place - ideally situated for rugby matches at Twickenham
text: Over a year ago I was looking for somewhere to stay for a number of weekends during the Rugby World Cup 2015. I needed somewhere close to Richmond but given the number of nights I was planning to book, I also wanted more than just a bog standard hotel. I chanced across The Victoria during one of my many Internet searches. I checked its location and it seemed to be close enough to Richmond to meet my needs. When I phoned up, I was first told that the Hotel had not yet opened its bookings for 2015 so call back in January however I was adamant that I needed to get my rooms booked (I have been planning for this Rugby World Cup for a VERY Long time!) so they agreed to take my booking and because of that I booked a job lot of nights for various weekends between 18th September and 31st October. On some of the weekends I needed a twin room as although my husband would be joining me to some matches, my eldest son was joining me for others. This was no problem for the booking staff and my email confirmations were sent within hours. So for our first weekend, 18th September for 3 nights, we arrived and tried to park our car in the small car park at the back. A car was sticking out making it difficult for us to get our car in. The Owner and General Manager were both in the car park at the time and assisted us in finding the car owner to allow us to park. We arrived before the 2pm check-in and our room was not ready. The Restaurant / Pub was busy with lunchtime trade however we were warmly greeted and offered a drink while we waited. We did not have to wait too long. We were shown to our room which on this occasion was Room 1. This is at ground level, separate from the other rooms. We were shown in with the keys explained to us, one key for the room and one for the garden gate to let ourselves in should we arrive back after the pub was closed. The room was lovely, very clean, very well decorated and ample space for the two of us. Having unpacked we waited for our son who was joining us for the match that evening but not staying at the hotel until the following evening. When he arrived we decided to eat in the restaurant - fantastic food, excellent service. The staff showed a genuine interest in our plans for the weekend. Every member of staff we engaged with was very friendly, very professional and accommodating. After eating we walked a short distance to pick up a bus to Richmond - a very short ride with a 24 hour bus service (just remember there is no cash payment on buses, get an Oyster card or use contactless card). The beds were comfortable and both my husband and I had a good nights sleep. The shower was just powerful enough and very refreshing. A continental breakfast is within the price of the room although you can pay extra for a cooked breakfast. The spread for breakfast was superb with a wide range of choice. You certainly could not complain that you were hungry! I have just returned from weekend number two - we were welcomed in the car park by the owner almost like old friends returning. We had a long conversation about the Rugby World Cup and the matches we were going to. It was great to have such a personal welcome. We went into the Victoria without our bags as it was around noon so we decided to eat before checking in. We were greeted by the staff in a similar way - it was great to feel like we were coming back to our home from home. Once again we were not disappointed with the standard of food or the standard of service. Room 4 is equally as lovely as Room 1. It is up a short flight of stairs with very shallow steps which makes it easy to get up them even if like me you struggle a little with your knees! The decor throughout was lovely. Beds were very comfortable and we slept well. Team Victoria has so far helped to make our Rugby World Cup experience as special as we hoped it would be. Noting has been too much trouble for the Team. We have a couple of weekends in Newcastle before we head back to the Victoria. We are very much looking forward to our return. I have already recommended the hotel to friends (two of which also booked 3 nights this weekend just passed) and I will continue to recommend it to all of my friends but particularly those who are travelling to rugby matches at Twickenham. My husband and I have stayed in Richmond and surrounding area on many occasions for rugby matches in a variety of establishments but from now on the Victoria is our first choice! Thank you guys - look forward to seeing you on 17th October - Julie

title: Lovely Gastro Pub but rooms disappointing
text: The Victoria is a really nice Gastro Pub with accomodation at the back of the building. The pub itself is great, well decorated and with a restaurant which is very popular and the staff are generally excellent and friendly. The downside is the accomodation which is not cheap but unfortunately extremely basic. Not much attempt at decor and the bathroom, while adequate in size was dismally lit - surely it would not take much to improve this. Breakfast was excellent, absolutely no complaints there! It would take much to upgrade the rooms and then this would be a really excellent place to stay in the area, it has a lot going for it.

title: One of the best meals I have ever jad
text: I asked the waiter for his recommendation - pork belly ! It was absolutely delicious. It had a smoky flavor that was sublime. I was only sorry that I did not have. Starter. I made up for it with a desert - a boring cheeseboard ! How wrong could I have been. It was without doubt the best cheeseboard that I have ever had and I have had A lot ! It was all washed down with some excellent beer - it was so god I have forgotten what it was !

title: Nearly good, but not quite
text: You won't stumble across the Victoria, but it's a welcoming gastropub with friendly staff, and the restaurant area in the conservatory seems to work as well in winter as summer. The service was friendly, if a little slow, and our starters of game terrine were very tasty, and more bread was forthcoming when requested. The mains however, were a disappointment. My medium cooked steak was only warm, but had been burnt on the underside, while my girlfriend's hake fillet still had a fair amount of bones. It was tasty, but having to fillet a fillet yourself detracts from the enjoyment somewhat. All credit to the staff, when I pointed out the steak to them, they took the feedback and gave us free delicious dessert and glass of wine. So I would give them the benefit of the doubt that we were just unlucky.

title: idyllic hotel with top class restaurant
text: My husband and I stayed here during the first week of Wimbledon. The hotel and restaurant have recently been taken over by new management and although the rooms are still to be refurbished we loved it. The restauarant is very special and the location was lovely, right next to Richmond Park and in a quiet and safe area of South West London. Would highly reccommend

title: Everything But The Room!
text: On an overnight stay for a nearby wedding, I could not have asked for more from a pub with rooms except for the room. Travelling solo at the last minute it came as a relief to have done so when I discovered my room was barely large enough to accommodate me. Reasonably clean and tidy and mercifully with a fan on what turned out to be a sultry London night, its cramped interior was only just suitable for single occupancy. This however was the only disappointment as the evening meal and breakfast the following morning were outstanding. Add in pleasant surroundings and even more pleasant staff and this could so easily have been an outstanding experience. The bar area is complemented by a lovely conservatory and garden dining area. I thoroughly enjoyed their homemade burger and an excellent Portuguese red. The next morning I enjoyed an enormous breakfast in the conservatory before heading back to the west country. I can thoroughly recommend The Victoria but just make sure you check which room you are allocated when booking.

title: Great food makes this place worth staying at
text: Generally the service at The Victoria seemed to be lacking some what. A couple of members of staff were very friendly and welcoming but the majority seemed a bit confused and overwhelmed by the under-taking of the services that The Victoria is offering. The room we stayed in was very nice. It was a good size with nice modern décor and most importantly, it was very clean. The bathroom was small but adequate. The only downside to the room was that it was very hot and stuffy. An electric fan was supplied but it was too small for both of us to get any benefit from it. Breakfast was very nice. There was a continental buffet for guests which had a lot of options including lots of tasty healthy stuff. One morning we had a cooked breakfast (full English) which was one of the best we'd ever had but unfortunately the cooked breakfasts are not included in the price of the room which we found disappointing for a B&B of this standard. We had a three-course evening meal at The Victoria which was extremely good. There was a great choice on the menu and everything was cooked to perfection. The only downside was that some of the waiters/waitresses didn't seem to know what the food was that they were serving and it seemed a little unprofessional. The food itself deserves 5 stars. The location is a 5 minute drive from Richmond high street. It is out of the way in a leafy residential area and therefore nice and quiet compared with other hotels in the London area. Richmond Park is also easily reached on foot from The Victoria. There is the added benefit of a car park at the back of the pub which was a relief to find on arrival. The pub bar and dining areas are very smart as well as comfortable and provides a relaxing environment to spend time. The décor is very tasteful. The garden is also worth mentioning as it is a nice size with plenty of seating and is obviously well maintained. The best thing about The Victoria is enjoying their delicious food in the beautiful surroundings. The service could do with improving though to make the whole experience extra special.

title: Great food, great setting
text: Stayed for a few nights recently: Rooms: Comfortable, clean, in a nice separate block, no frills. For GBP130 a night I would have loved/expected to have seen a bottle of shower gel in the shower rather than the gym style dispenser. Setting: Stunning, temple sheen is a beautiful residential area and you are a v short walk from Richmond Park. Having a car is advisable as taxis are rare (but can be called) in the vicinity, and it is a decent walk to local transport links. The pub itself is lovingly restored inside, with a stunning conservatory and lovely small (partly covered garden with a small childrens play area). Food: Stunning - the chefs are highly skilled and just understand cooking, from a beautiful plate of ham, cheese and honey, to an aged sirlion steak as good as I have had anywhere and cooked to perfection, lamb burgers were succulent with great sides, and a gorgeous tasting pea soup. Scrambled eggs at breakfast were sublime. Also has a great reasonably priced wine list with some real gems on it. Service: Slight disappointment. It wasn't that the staff weren't knowlegable or occaisionally friendly, it just seemed that they were lacking someone with sharper eyes pointing out who they needed to serve, when, and why. Nobody should be left sitting, on their own for 5 mins, or waiting for water for the same amount of time. This happened on a couple of occaision during the stay, so it wasn't a one off. And upon asking for butter at breakfast I don't thing it is acceptable to be given the, partly used, dish from the next table!

title: Dads 70th birthday meal!
text: Chose as location for dads birthday. Ended up with 26 people coming. They were extremely helpful with organising, inviting us to a mini wine tasting before the big day to ensure we got what we wanted. Food and wine both delicious on the day and staff genuinely attentive and friendly. Thoroughly recommended

title: Great place , poor service
text: This came highly recommended and I have eaten before and been impressed. However we just stayed overnight this time. The room was fine, but no coffee machine. Breakfast looked good and there was an excellent menu, but sadly we were in the dining room for 30 minutes, no one came to speak to us , we were offered nothing off the menu and in the end had to beg a cup of coffee. Empty dishes were whisked away, with a curt "Is this finshed" while I was still eating. Come on, you have great place please get the morning service up to scratch !!

title: What a find!
text: We stayed at The Victoria last night. The food was excellent, wine list comprehensive, staff friendly and attentive. The bedroom was large and airy, crisp, fresh linen, bed very comfortable and everything clean and sparkling. Would highly recommend.

title: Continental Breakfast
text: Very nice hotel and clean rooms. However be warned! although I booked B&B I did not find out that it was only a continental breakfast until there. You could upgrade for a fee but apparently the kitchen doesn't cook til 8.30am. No good to me as I had work to get to.

title: What a perfectwedding venue!
text: WOW! We are slowly recovering from our wedding at The Victoria. What a fantastic place all round: absolutely faultless from the early preparations right through to the last drink served. Greg, Natalie and the rest of the team got it spot on. All our guests have commented that it was one of the best weddings they have ever been to: amazing food and wine in a perfect setting. Staff were fantastic: attentive yet relaxed. We wanted a chilled out wedding in a lovely venue and that's excellently what we got. We can't recommend it highly enough - the day was simply perfect (and incredibly reasonable which also helps!). Thank you so much.

title: Hitched without a hitch!
text: It is such a rarity, especially when the two of you already have such high standards, that your expectations are not only met but exceeded! We recently held our wedding reception at The Victoria, where Greg, Paul and his fabulous team looked after us with exquisite attention to detail so subtly performed that they all appeared totally relaxed - real 'swanning' skills! Our guests have continued to comment on how amazing the food was, how great the wine was (we've even had to send out a list to people of the wine choices!) and how fantastically professional and friendly the staff were. We really were treated with such warmth and a genuine desire for us to have a great day - which we did. To everyone at The Victoria, thank you so much, we really couldn't have had a better day.... and the best breakfast I've ever had the morning after was definitely appreciated too!

title: Our Wedding day at The Victoria Saturday 7th March 2015
text: We got married at The Orleans House Gallery on Saturday 7th March 2015 and hired out the whole of The Victoria for our afternoon and evening reception. We had a wonderful day from start to finish. Greg and Paul and the rest of the team at The Victoria were so helpful

title: Top venue for 40th birthday celebrations!
text: We hired out the Victoria for my recent birthday and had a brilliant evening. The Victoria is a great venue as it offers two great spaces - conservatory and bar area and in addition has rooms upstairs so you can crash after the party! Greg Bellamy, Director at the Victoria, helped us plan the party to every last detail - the wine, menu selection, dessert, cocktails, decorations etc, He and his team really know what they are doing and were extremely professional from start to finish. The food at the Victoria is fantastic and our guests were raving about the goats cheese Croque Monsieur canapes, the prawn and chorizo rissotto and incredible dessert selection which came out on a platter with sparklers. The food there is on a par with a top London restaurant which many of our guests were pleasantly surprised about. The staff went out of their way to help before, during and after the party. A really great group of people who love what they do and know how to provide a good service. The rooms at the hotel are perfect for a night away and really handy for Richmond park, Central London and Heathrow. Since it is a residential area, the rooms are quiet and offer everything you need. They offer a good breakfast. I wouldn't hesitate in holding another party or gathering at the Victoria. In the meantime, I have dinner booked!

title: I've been coming here since it opened
text: Great 'gastropub' food in the middle of a residential area outside Richmond Park. Great food. Worth a visit, but it's not cheap. Valentine's Day sharing menu was fantastic - five starters and five puddings with a main course. Wonderful!

title: Love this place
text: Visited The Victoria last Sunday afternoon/evening: great live music (twice a month?), friendly and attentive staff and an absolutely delicious full-works Victoria burger and thrice-cooked chips from the bar menu. Stay over if you can, too: lovely, comfortable rooms!

title: 21st Birthday Party Breakfast
text: These guys really know how to look after their guests. I booked a 21st Birthday Breakfast for my son and 25 other guest at short notice and Paul and his team pulled out all the stops! The buffet idea was perfect with plenty of delightfull choices to fit everyone's taste. The service was attentive but not 'in your face' and there was no pressure to kick us out after 2 hours of fine food. The Bucks-Fizz on arrival was a suprise twist too! Fantastic value for money.

title: Exceptional place to stay
text: The room was very clean and beautifully decorated. Lovely big comfy bed and pillows. The Coffee machine in the room was wonderful. The bar has a great atmosphere and the food is beautifully presented and tastes delicious...I had the steak! The staff are very friendly and helpful. Really enjoyed my stay just wish it was for longer. Thank you.

title: Saturday at the Rugby
text: The hotel is located approx 25 Min walk into Richmond and handy if you do not wish to stay in Richmond or no accommodation available. The room was very clean and spacious with all the facilities required. The Gastro Pub itself was friendly and warming wether you are just wanting a drink or food as well. We only had bed and breakfast that included free continental with something for everyone Cereal, Fruit, Cheese , Meat etc.., but would eat next time. We paid and additional £8.50 for a cooked breakfast that included good ingredients and more than enough to eat and of a high standard that you should expect from a Gastro Pub. Free parking and Wi-Fi was included that you come to expect today. The staff we helpful and friendly and i would be happy to return when next at the Rugby as a great find. I have reflected the value for money based on it is London and £130 per room.

title: Lovely little hotel
text: On business for a couple of days - had a lovely stay here. Rooms are clean and well appointed without being pretentious. Staff are helpful and the continental breakfast was excellent. Ate twice in the bar, and on both occasions the simple food was fresh and well presented. Good value too. Only black mark was that it took half an hour to encourage someone to take my dessert order, then it disappeared into the kitchen and hadn't materialised after another 40 minutes. On pointing it out to them and asking to cancel my order, they were fantastic. A dessert appeared quickly and on the house, along with great coffee. I'm glad I waited - it was superb. That's the way to treat a slightly disgruntled customer! It's the hotel regularly used by the company I was working with, and although it's off the beaten track for central London, I'm looking forward to future visits very much. Highly recommended.

title: Great venue, fantastic food
text: The Victoria is a place that i'd like to get to more although it's a bit of a hike for us - it's always impressed me food wise, and the Valentine's night menu was simply superb. I was also impressed at the value it offered - I felt like Mr Creosote after finishing off the desserts (just a wafer thin mint....). Service was brilliant, and the sense of hospitality really hit the spot. Well done guys!

title: What a disappointment. Rude and unhelpful staff
text: This uses to be a favourite of ours. Have used both the restaurant and rooms many times. It used to be good. But this has all changed After 3 bad experiences, I thought that it was not just bad luck but rather the place has changed. We won't be back The staff are very complacent and te manager is just plain very rude Would not recommend this place to anyone anymore. A great pity

title: 3 nights at the Victoria
text: Had high hopes but didn't really need expectations. Its a cute pub/hotel on a super quiet street but not really walking distance to local trains, You better know the bus system if you want to get around. Breakfast was the high point, served in a nice bright area and the pub looked cozy. Rooms were small and warm but the biggest issue was the bed - so very hard I found myself waking up every few hours. I guess it's London so you can't expect much for the price we paid but unless you have a reason to be in that specific area I would give it a pass.

title: Friendly boutique hotel
text: Had a very long overdue night away from the kids to attend a friends party and from checking in to checking out felt very comfortable and welcomed in this charming pub/ hotel. Although the room was small it was tastefully decorated and contained everything we needed for a relaxing night away. Breakfast was delicious but a very quiet room, or maybe I'm not used to that any more! We would definitely stay here again if the opportunity arose. Either way, we will certainly be back for a drink in the bar.

title: Far from the madding crowd
text: My husband and I spent two nights at Bank holiday weekend in this wonderful small hotel. The décor was absolutely lovely with the décor and carpets looking new. We only had lunch at the hotel one day (daughter living at Twickenham and son in Surbiton) which we thoroughly enjoyed, it would have been nice to have dinner but family commitments called. As our family have small properties we will definitely be booking the Victoria again. I was disappointed at having a shower instead of a bath but can easily cope with this as I loved the hotel and will be back. If you are looking for a lovely quiet location this is the place to stay.

title: A really pleasant place to eat..................
text: We are local and so don't stay but eat in the restaurant from time to time. All in all it's pretty good with excellent food and service. The ambiance is relaxing and the garden a delightful place when the weather is good. Currently a summer menu is in operation and I had the best seabass ever. My wife's salad was OK but not as good. Perhaps a little overpriced.

title: Great!
text: Loved the atmosphere of the place. Close to the park and everything. The rooms are a bit bare but it's very clean. It's is very quite as it is located in a residential area, great if you want to find a remote little place in London.

title: Overpriced
text: I've stayed twice, wouldn't have come back from choice, but have family nearby. Rooms basic, quite masculine, gloomy en suite, thick dust below bedhead and under bed not hoovered too well, though otherwise clean. Breakfast lovely the first time, less so the second, with cheap white bread as the only toast option. Main issue for me was lack of warm welcome and feeling of being looked after, almost like the hotel was an afterthought to the restaurant and bar. It was just about ok the first time, but on my second visit I sat alone at breakfast and no one offered tea or coffee until I got up to go. Planes are an issue too and like another reviewer, I experienced early morning doors banging and noise. Overall, I would probably pay £75 and reckon £120 is over the top for the quality of rooms and service

title: Visiting Roehampton Uni
text: We stay her reg when visiting our loved one at Roehampton Uni. The rooms are spacious and comfortable , and the food - including breakfast is excellent. It has a great atmosphere and outside area and is always buzzing with local residents.

title: A good place in a quiet corner of London
text: The place itself is a tucked away down a few side streets, not that it's a bad thing, probably a 10 minute walk to a train station and 5 minutes to bus routes. This means it was really quiet a night. The room itself was simple and clean, nothing fancy but if you just need it for somewhere to sleep and wash then fits the bill exactly. The real highlight of this place is the food though, it was excellent. The continental breakfast was fine with fresh bread and pastries and the likes and if you fancy being unhealthy then I highly recommend the cooked breakfast, one of the best i've had. Also ate here one night and again food was great, even though the kitchen had been having problems with their electricity they still served us and produced a great meal. The staff were also very friendly and helpful.

title: Wimbledon night
text: We stayed here for a visit to Wimbledon last week as an alternative to central London. The Victoria has a comfortable feel and very friendly staff. As a pub with rooms it provides simple accommodation but comfortable enough for an overnight stay. The complimentary breakfast was good and the diner menu was good value. The Victoria is in a quite location which is good but the downside is that if you are relying on taxis it is quite expensive to get about, £24 taxi fare to Wimbledon. Overall we had a pleasant stay and thought it represented good value for the area.

title: Right under the LHR flight path!
text: The location of the Victoria has both pros and cons. A charming little neighborhood, situated adjacent to Richmond Park would seem to be the ideal location for a few night's stay

title: Best food for miles
text: Food is fresh and delicious. A welcome antidote to formulaic chain restaurants. I had the tastiest ravioli at a recent birthday supper. Welcoming interior, relaxed lounge chairs for morning coffees and at night I'm always comfortable as a lone woman if I arrive first.

title: London break
text: Nice hotel, well maintained and great service, comfy bed which is good for back issues. Staff are friendly and happy to help you with anything. If you want to stay in central London and not spend the earth this place is great.

title: Great location and Great value
text: I stayed here recently for an overnight, between business and personal commitments. This comes up fairly often, so I have tried out hostels, pod rooms, airbnbs, several hotels, before finding Pasha. I found this to be the best value/quality/location/price combo for me. The room was clean, comfortable and warm. It had tea and coffee facilities and a large bathroom. It was quiet. The staff were friendly and offered to help me with bags. There's a busy bus route a 2 minute walk away, making it cheap and easy to get around London. For the first time in months, I have booked the same place back-to-back stays because I think I've finally found a hotel that is cheap, without being dirty/sketchy/having terrible facilities or suchlike!

title: Please read before booking - SHOCKING "Hotel"
text: This is without doubt the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. I know some reviews on here can be unfairly critical i find but if you look back at my previous reviews, most places I rate highly. However this place was absolutely disgraceful, everything about it was as bad as I have experienced anywhere in the world. Where to start? Well first off when we found the hotel it was in an absolutely terrible location, the area was extremely rough and some very shady characters around. I was with my wife and thank God I was with her becasue I was worried for our safety even with me there too so if she was alone, I just dont think she could stay there. The receptionist had a booking for one person for one night for us even though we had our booking form with us of two people for two nights. Ok this can happen but when we got to our room, I can genuinely say I was horrified. When we opened the door it was pitch dark so the first thing you got was an awful smell, a real musty dirty smell a bit like manure to be honest. We found a light that worked (not all did) and saw our room. Like a person cell would be the best way to describe it, a bad prison cell. The bed was a picee of wood ont he floor with a matress on it, no word of a lie, thats what it was. And that was pretty much it, there is a small tv and a press also. The walls had damp in them and paint was covered in dirt. The window which had the curtain drawn over it was a tiny prison cell like window right at the top of the wall so you couldnt see out it even if you wanted to. We thought about going and complaining and asking for another room but then came on here first and read some reviews and figured, the next one could be wrose so maybe we will jsut stick with this one. I had a shower and one positive is the shower was good and powerful with hot water. Thats about it for the good things though. The room felt dirty, well it was dirty. The smell was disgusting and any noise from anywhere else in the hotel was easily heard. The location is one of the roughest areas I have ever been in and it is not close to any tube station and hard tog et around to anywhere else from. And this is the bit that tops it off. The rooms were £90 Sterling a night. That is about €125 and they call it a 3 star spa boutique hotel?!?! If they sold the rooms for 40 a night and called it budget accom, I would accept it and still say it was a poor standard 40 a night but to pay £180 for two nights here with no breakfast, just a bed was astonishing. It was like a very very bad hostel that was in the roughest area of London and charged 4 star hotel prices. i cannot say enough about this place to advise people not to go, honestly, it does not feel safe, it smells and the rooms/beds are the worst I have seen. If there was an option to give it zero out of five, I would. Take my advice and book somewhere else. Anywhere would be better than here.

title: Honest Hotel in a very good location
text: Honest hotel, all the staff very helpful, everywhere was very clean. Breakfast is served on a fantastic balcony. Amazing Turkish themed restaurant. Bus stop just outside so just 5 minutes to Elephant & Castle for the tube. Quite reasonable charges for the location.

title: Avoid
text: - Room was dirty - No lift - Marks on ceiling - Dirt on walls - Stains on sheets - Stains on towels - TV doesn't work - Broken plug socket - Only one plug available - Noisy guests smoking drugs which staff were aware of, who had people going in and out of

title: Very impressed!
text: Just got back from a night in Pasha Hotel with my sister for her 18th birthday. We had a little confusion getting there and we ended up walking from Kennington station (about 20 mins) and the area is a little rough (maybe I'm just a softie!!) but found the hotel very easily. I'm not sure why some reviews have said the front of the hotel looks like a shop or a restaurant. It was clearly labeled and looked nothing but professional from the outside. The receptionist was very helpful, asking where we had come from and what our plans were so she could guide us on how to best get to where we wanted to go. Was seeing a gig in Brixton and the buses (34 or 45) take you practically outside the venue in under 20 mins. The room outside was spotless, very smart. The bathroom was lovely with a walk in shower. We even had two cans of coke and some crisps waiting for us free of charge in our room! The air con was lovely as well as it was a hot night! The only improvements I could suggest is making it clearer on the website that there is no elevator. The stairs are narrow and not well lit so we had a few stumbles (especially after a few glasses of wine!) and I wouldn't want to take elderly relatives there with no lift. Apart from that it was lovely! Thanks a lot for a lovely night!

title: Overnight brief stay
text: If you look at the glossy photos on Bookings.com (the ones Pasha have put up) you'd think you were getting deal of the century. But glossy photos don't transfer here. 3 flights of steep stairs. Grubby carpets...TINY rooms and nothing like the photos. Dirty walls. More hanging space than Johnny Depp's bedroom but why? Tiny bed, dirty 2nd pillow. No curtains unless you call a net curtain a curtain! Right next to a train track!!! Luke warm water. Cold shower full of damp. Basically the worst £62 i have ever spent. Paint and caroet cleaning could go a long way

title: COZY PLACE
text: I stayed at Pasha last week and felt very comfortable. This was my third stay and what i found new was a cafe on the roof top....very nicely decorated. Room was smart and clean with tea and buiscits .. Thanks. See you soon

title: Reasonable hotel for the money
text: I did my research before booking this hotel so it didnt come as a shock to me. The hotel from the outside looks like a shop in a row of shops down the high street and there is no parking outside, so i parked at the small supermarket just 5o yards down the room. Reception and booking in was fine with very helpful staff. I then parked my car in their car park which is at the rear, but be aware it is very small. I had asked for a quite room so i was right at the back on the third floor, it was not too bad but you can still hear the trains and noise from the high street. Room is fairly basic but it could do with some decorating and too many lights had no bulbs in them. Just a shower in my room but on the plus point the room did have air conditioning. For £80 i surpose i carnt complain but i will probably book another hotel next time as i do like a few more luxuries.

title: You get what you pay for
text: We stayed 2 nights mid week. On initial entry we thought, oh no! There was building material all around the place and the fish tank has seen better days! The hotel is in need of updating especially the communal areas. The corridor kept going and then we reached the stair case. We were in a back room with an entry 'cupboard'to two other rooms (it had a strong unpleasant smell). The room was adequate for what we needed it for (place to sleep) as we were out all day and evening. Some bulbs were missing and the bathroom although modern only had one light above the large mirror meaning you showered in the dark even in the day. The room was very warm even in December but the plug was broken on the fan which we were going to use to drown out the thumping bass of a cafe/bar under neath the window. The staff couldn't do anything about this they stated but thankfully it did stop about 11pm. I would recommend taking earplugs as the railway line is right near the window and if the curtains are closed properly you have a disco from the train lights passing through the room. As I said you get what you pay for and we were expecting exactly what we got but dont be swayed by the 3 star rating as it is much lower standard.

title: Filthy and disgusting very poor service and no response from management
text: Well it was a cold wet Friday on the 9th of November when I arrive, my check in was three but arrived late and was rushing. Was given the and got to the room the cleaner hadn’t even started cleaning. I had nowhere to grab a shower and had to just put in cloths. Due to the rush I left whilst the room was being made up. The room felt Dirty and was cold rushed out next morning without opening curtains. Came back in the dark and still at this point hadn’t opened the curtains. Sunday morning got up opened the curtains found the cigarette as per the picture and all the dirty filthy pictures. I asked to see the manger was told no they are busy offered my number was told they might call you a month later still no call, asked to cancel my second reservation for the end of the month told yes but no refund as I had already paid. Asked to speak to the manager was told no. £180 to stay in the filthiest hotel ever. Such a shame as I prefer to use the local then the chains. I feel this is the only way to warn people not to stay here.

title: Holiday
text: Room was grubby. Smelly. Black water odour throughout. Small steep stairs. Gladly surrendered 2 night cost to get out of the place. Attendant was very helpful but did not make up for our disappointment.

title: Do not stay here
text: I am easily pleased so this rating is especially bad. Shower didn't work, dried in blood stain on linen, smell from drains, continental breakfast was literally corn flakes and half a diced apple, constant stream of people outside room, really noisy room beside restaurant, they wouldn't allow us change room, the crowning glory was two non paying guests from the restaurant banging on our door and barged into our room to use our bathroom at 11pm!! Avoid at all costs

title: Excellent Value
text: We arrived slightly earlier than the check in time, the reception staff offered us a different room to the one we were allocated so we could get in and settled. They do have a luggage store so if we couldn't have gotten in we could still have left our luggage. The staff are lovely and friendly. I had researched the hotel before we went, so was a bit worried about what we were walking into as the reviews were mixed, I don't know why. Pasha is situated in the middle of a row of shops so you can easily walk past it without knowing it is there, to my mind that is a bonus - that means there are shops close by. You have 2 restaurants directly over the road and a take away 2 doors up. There is also a corner shop which is open 24hrs over the road too. Transport into the heart of London could not be easier, the bus stop is literally 2 min walk from the door on the same street. The 12 & 148 are 24hrs - within 10min you are at the London eye and 15/20min at Trafalgar square. We had gotten Oyster cards and it was £1.50 each way. If we were getting cabs we were using the Uber app rather than a black cab and from London Eye to the hotel it was only £8. We were disappointed that the terrace was not open, but it was by no means a deal breaker. The room we got was clean and tidy and the beds were better than I have ever had in any hotel. The room also had complimentary crisps and bottled water which was a lovely touch. The bathroom was great with an excellent fixed shower - the only downside if I am picking was that it could have done with some re-grouting in places and a lick of paint on the ceiling. Breakfast is only £5 which was a full English and well worth it. What I did find strange was although the hotel is listed as having a spa - you need to book this well in advance even to use the steam room - we couldn't get a space. Prices start at £20. It is run as a separate business to the Hotel so you can't book at reception. The restaurant is also run as a separate business which means you have to book dinner by either calling in advance or in the morning when you have breakfast. We would go back though if we are ever in London again.

title: Dirty, messy and no WiFi
text: The room was dirty, many things were broken. No WiFi access from the room. The carpet was smelly. The room was very cold and noisy because of the trains. I asked the receptionist to help me fixing the WiFi connection, he said he'd restart it, but the problem was not the Internet itself, but the signal, no signal at all in the room

title: excellent quality of service at decent prices
text: The service is definitely at the level of reliable 3tar hotel, staff is friendly and hospitable. Rooms are clean and well furnished. Bus stop is about 100m from the hotel and takes you to Oxford Circus in about 45 min. I definitely recommend it.

title: Don't Bother
text: I won an all expenses paid night and Spa Treatment for me and my partner. I did not even get a chance to enjoy any of it due to the rude and unprofessionalism of The Spa Manager. No customer care at all, it really put me off.

title: STAY AWAY
text: this hotel is honest to god the worst hotel I will ever come across. In the worst area so far from the London centre, the staff are rude! Rooms are so dirty, broken mirrors and windows are broke. Walls are as thin as paper- could hear people having sex all over the place. !

title: Brilliant
text: Me and my partner stayed here for one night when I needed to come to Kings College Hospital for a specialist appointment. Our room was very clean, the receptionist was fantastic (Julia?) and when the baby has been born we will be back!

title: DO NOT STAY HERE
text: this isn't even worth a one star rating. Me and my girlfriend lasted not even an hour in this sh#thole. In the dodgiest area going, the walls and doors might aswell be paper Thin. Staff are clueless and unhelpful cant even understand what they're saying, if you want a hotel where you feel unsafe and cold then this is for you. Our mirror was cracked, there was a hole in the bathroom floor which was grotty and slimey. The headboard had chewing gum on it, the windows were broken. Do not stay here. This shouldn't be eligible for a hotel!

title: We didn't even get to the room
text: Never ever ever ever ever ever ever EVER consider staying here. The area it is in is dodgy to say the least. The parking is round the back, there are about 5 reallllly narrow spaces, which out car would not fit in, amongst the vans from the M.O.T test center next door. We were weary about even going into the hotel. The back entrance was full of cut off bits of wood and old carpet. You have to walk through the whole of the hotel from the car park to get to the reception. The restaurant is cheap and tacky, with a bridge in the middle, the staff just looked at us gone out! Our baggage was eyed up by a sun bed customer. We went and asked about the parking, and he insisted that there were spaces, but there weren't. We went for a drive around and ended up parking in iceland car park, which felt very dodgy, everybody looking at us. The hotel looks like a brothel, or a cheap tacky chinese restaurant! It is in between a shop and a barber, literally all the shops on the street were barbers and nail technicians. We went to check in, even though my mum reallllly did not want to stay there, but we decided to go and look at the room before making our decision on whether to stay, yes it really was that bad! So we went to check in, and they had got our dates wrong, by a month! Normally this would have been a huge problem but in this case, it was a god send, meaning we could cancel the booking and get our money back. I was soooo glad to get out of this place!

title: You get what you pay for
text: Stayed here for 2 nights in early June. Yes, it could do with a refurb and yes, it is slightly ramshackle but at £50 per night, you can't really complain. Well, you can of course but that would be somewhat churlish I feel. The staff were very warm and friendly. It's almost like a throwback to before Premier Inn and Travelodge turned up

title: Pleasantly surprised!
text: Super cheap room with good transport links (use the bus to get into the city!). Very impressed with the staff - very welcoming and helpful, and room was quiet and clean - even had toiletries and tea/coffee!

title: Fire hazard waiting to happen....
text: Firstly on a positive note I would like to say that the staff are wonderful and really helpful and friendly, however that's where the good stuff starts and finishes. I stayed for the weekend, at the very top of the hotel, in their "deluxe double". Lots of thin stairs to get to the top - but there's only one one route up and down (I even asked if there was an alternative route down in case of a fire or the like - no). Isn't that a requirement these days in hotels? A seriously inappropriately designed building for multiple occupancy if the worst happened this would be a death trap for those above a fire as there's no way down, and the building so far up its impossible to get down safely. That aside, the room was shabby, there were oily "massage lotion bottle" rings on the side table - which was disconcerting, but a clear indicator that it hadn't been thoroughly cleaned ahead of my stay. No phone in the room, no hotel info (restaurant opening times, check out times, local things to do, bus routes etc.) or menu in the room. And as other reviewers have mentioned the train line is very, very close and trains rumbled past multiple times every hour and were very very loud. I didn't mind too much as I'm a heavy sleeper but I'm sure could affect many. The skirting was coming off, the bathroom smelt and looked mouldy especially along the shower seals (I think you get the idea so I won't continue).... We did venture to the restaurant (it was pre-booked, otherwise I'd have given it a miss). Note it is housed partially underneath the railway tracks so shakes periodically as a train goes overhead.... it sounds like thunder (which would be quirky and funny if everythingelse was great, but it wasn't) ! And understandably- as its all effectively underground - its all damp smelling and musty, quite off putting when trying to eat. The food was OK although more warm than piping hot, and I got the feeling it was just re-heated rather than cooked fresh (I may be doing them a disservice), but never the less nothing special... Oh a little thing about reception, its one of the better parts of the hotel however, somebody **please rescue the fish**... There are fish everywhere in a big tank (fine), but also in small vases dotted about. With no grit/gravel, or plants or anything in them, just a vase with water and a solitary fish .. all on their own. How stressful for the poor fish... Fish need places to hide and act naturally, not in a small "vase" in artificially lit conditions day in day out - it was awful to see.... Lastly on the second attempt at getting back in to my room the lock broke, so I couldn't get in to the room, so was given a master key instead... OK. But then realised that my door card with the wireless codes etc on had been taken away, and there but to be honest I was so fed up by then I just wanted to go to bed... In summary, staff a real asset and the only thing going for the hotel, but hotel owner needs to seriously get the standards and H&S requirements up (especially re: H&S) for any chance of this hotel to remain open.... In the mean time, for your own safety and enjoyment, I'd steer well clear.

title: Absolutely disgusting ! Do not waste your money
text: My husband and I stayed here for one night and what a mistake ! We chose pasha as the photos on the website look very luxurious and inviting, however, what a massive disappointment ! We took a taxi to the hotel and first impressions were not good. The hotel is squeezed in amongst shops and looked very strange, even the taxi driver laughed ! The hotel lobby was full of women, screaming children and buggies, so when we were informed that our room wasn't ready for another half an hour, we had to leave the hotel as there was no where to sit and wait. Instead, we headed to the only pub that we had seen in the run down area, which was across the road, where we sat with an old chap watching a film of the tv at full volume! After checking in we were led by the receptionist up 2 flights of very narrow, steep badly lit flights of stairs which had no rails to hold, talk about a health and safety hazard.when we reached the 2nd floor we were shown in to a dark dingy room which absolutely stank of cigarette smoke, and we were told by the receptionist feel free to smoke in here! As non smokers my husband and I didn't really like the idea that we would stink like an ashtray by the end of our stay. The room was hideous ! The carpet was filthy and stained, there was an area near the bathroom that had a loose piece of carpet covering bare floor which we constantly tripped over and had to replace, the wardrobe was falling apart, the window was broken and taped up, there were. Massive gaps around the only plug socket in the room, the door to the fridge did not shut and it stunk, the drain was clogged up so the shower tray filled with filthy water and overflowed, there was a broken drain in the middle of the bathroom floor which I cut my foot on and the mattress stunk and was so cheap and thin. This was honestly the worst hotel we have ever been in, and considering we opted for a more expensive hotel as we wanted a bit of luxury, it was also a massive dissappointment. The staff wrere friendly enough but not speaking very much English made it a bit hard to communicate. I really begrudged handing over hard earned money to stay in the hovel! And at £80 a night, it is certainly not cheap. The hotel describes itself as compact, comfortable and classy! Ha more like dark, dingy, dirty, cheap, nasty and sleazy !!!!! Absolute joke, the area it's in is run down, dirty and there is absolutely no entertainment in the area (apart from the run down pub opposite). I would not pay £20 a night for this hotel, it's an insult. Save your money and find a proper hotel!!!!!!! Photos to follow

title: Pasha Hotel South London
text: Hidden in the middle of a busy street in SE London, not too easy to get to or to find. However, once we arrived we were made very welcome, our room was freshly decorated and spacious by London standards. The staff were really friendly and helpful especially in the restaurant where we had a super value meal. The Georgian house wines - only £13 per bottle were particularly good. Once we found our way around an unfamiliar part of London it was easy - lots of buses right outside and pretty quick access to main parts of the city. There was live music in the restaurant which didn't bother us and a railway line outside the back of the hotel. Again, this caused us no problem. The air-conditioning was great and kept the room nicely cool. We were in London for the Olympics so didn't have much time to use the facilities on offer but all looked interesting. Well worth a look if you want something a bit different at an attractive price.

title: Was a frequent visitor
text: Once upon a time this was a glitzy, fabulous (if quirky and slightly shabby at times) place with a great Kyrgyz/Kazakh/Russian restaurant. Now it's just shabby. I booked a room through booking.com and was given a small shabby room right at the back on the 3rd floor. Far inferior to the rooms on the ground floor which I've stayed in previously. Maybe they keep the best rooms for direct bookings? Anyway the place has lost its charm. Quite depressing now and not very clean. remarkably cheap though.

title: A Really Enjoyable and Friendly Stay!
text: We have a great experience of our recent stay last week at Pasha Hotel, the staff welcome us very nicely and showed our room with taking our luggage feel us very nice. The room was very clean and bed was very comfortable. The WiFi internet was very good connection during all our stay. The location is bit far from the station but we do not have any problem because buses was running 24 hours just in front of the hotel. There is also SPA and Restaurant in the hotel. I will definitely recommend and will come back again.

title: Great Hotel , Comfortable Stay
text: I have stayed in Pasha hotel last month in March and i came back again very nice and clean hotel. Reasonable price and staff is very helpful and friendly. There is good WiFi always Definitely would recommend to my friends and I will surely come back again.

title: Terrible service
text: Despite ringing and booking a month in advance over the phone they booked a single room despite requesting and advising it was a triple room. They were then very unhelpful and refused to address the problem or admit fault. Would never book again.

title: good value
text: if its value your looking for then this is great. We paid £58 for a twin room, no breakfast. Great value for london. The hotel is a little bit out of the way, taxi needed to and from tube station. The hotel is clean and rooms are a good size. There is also cans of coke, and crisps etc that are all complementary. Staff are nice and helpful. There is also a turkish spa, which unfortunately we didn't have time to sample. All in all, good value.

title: Be prepared for the hike...
text: The Pasha is a sweet boutique hotel - and the price was quite good. HOWEVER, please be aware that you cannot walk to the nearest metro (Elephant & Castle) and will have to take a bus from the station. On the other hand, if you enjoy bus rides, the hotel is directly in front of several (about 8 or 9) major bus routes. The neighborhood is fine, but it isn't near any major attractions, but they do have a small and EXCELLENT street market about a 5 minute walk away. Also, there are several very good ethnic restaurants in the area, and they are super cheap!!! Finally, the hotel DOES NOT have a lift/elevator. Be prepared :) P.S. If you book through a site other than the hotel's, please bring your confirmation print out with you. They lost ours and were fully booked until we produced our receipt!

title: Too much dust in the room
text: I had an allergic attack because the dust. The room was very small with a little window, so that there was always little light in it. The staff are very friendly and try to do their best to put you at ease, but unfortunately the hotel itself would need some adjustment.

title: Fine for us!
text: Hubby and I first stayed at this hotel back in Sep 13,I needed to be near Kings College Hospital for work commitments so chose this hotel as it looked the best. Lovely welcome, friendly staff. Our first room was over looking the terrace, lovely big room, and clean. It did however had a nasty smell from the toilet area, and the the side light on the bed kept flickering, we informed them, and they changed the light bulb and gave us a can of air freshener with apologizes...fine. We only stayed for one night,so it wasn't a real problem. Breakfast out on the terrace was really nice,Lovely food with good choice.,Hubby had full English and I had the omelette a lot of food for £5 each! We stayed for the second time this Friday, again friendly same staff. Our room this time was at the side (I think) of the hotel which had the overground outside it, Trains ran every 15 mins or so,but to be honest, this didn't bother us at all. We live out in the country and love the sound of the city life. This was not a problem for us, but it might be for someone who wants piece and quiet. The room was clean, the shower was amazing!! Good supplies, amazing smelling body lotion! Parking fine and secure. Overall lovely hotel, ,

title: A Quirky Place To Stay In Camberwell
text: Stayed at this location many times over a period of 6 months in 2012 and once in Feb 2013 A hotel that many would not like but I enjoyed because of its quirkiness and the fact that all I wanted was a clean bed, on-suite near to the project that I was working on. You enter the hotel via a Turkish Spar & Hammam with a Beauty Salon and greeted by friendly and accommodating staff, the rooms on the ground floor are not suitable for a long stay as they are small, cramped and can be noisy from the passage outside. The upstairs room are comfortable, clean and quiet. There is train noise in the early morning, but I can sleep though that. I like the restaurant where they serve Kyrgyz, Kazakh & Mediterranean cuisine with Russian beer. You can chose to sit at a table or lounge on the eastern cushions at low tables. They also have wifi, I enjoyed the experience staying at this hotel and would recommend it for those that want to try something different. There is car-parking to the rear of the hotel, it is best to ring the hotel for directions to the car park when near by.

title: Painful experience
