text: The window had a hole in it and the heater wasn't working well so made sleeping difficult. The bedding was comfy but the trains made it a little noisy. Its centrality is the advantage and has a bus stop right across the street.

title: The worst hotel i have ever stayed in
text: Well i would say that this is certainly not a Botique Hotel as advertised first of all. As a young couple we reguarly visit London and have stayed in many hotels, I have just discovered that after staying at The Pasha Hotel you cannot do London on a budget and expect it to be remotly ok! We decided on Pasha Hotel as the pictures on the website made it look so inviting with a Turkish Spa, Morrocan Restaurant and 'beer garden' Roof Terrance.. perfect and for only £5 more than what a Travel Lodge would have cost, i think i have learnt my lesson that if somthing sounds to good to be true it usually is... We arrived on Saturday, i could'nt beleive my eyes this well presented front of house was not a stand hotel but nessetled between a convinience store and a caribean barbers on a extreamly busy road in the middle of a rough area on the out skirts of London, there is no where to park and off load baggage at the front of the hotel and parking is around the back of the hotel, the site there is WORSE much WORSE it now looks like we've arrived at a backstreet brothel. Having said this the Turkish staff were extreamly helpful and met us around the back of the hotel to help us park our car underneath the surveailence camera (just in case) and help with our suitcases. From the back of the hotel you arrive straight into the Restaurant and are greeted with a stale smell of somthing horrible, there is a strange pond in the middle of the restaurant and a bird cage (eew) with noisy birds tweeting, is this a Zoo or a restaurant, ??? we certainly will not be eating here during our stay! Next is the 'games room' all darkly lit with spot lights and red carpet 'very seedy' it has a pool table and a games machine, we are now making our way onto the 3rd floor - this hotel does not have a lift so getting upstairs with lots of luggage is a bit of a nightmare. Once we arrived in our room, i was pleased to note that the room and bathroom was quite light and spashious but we were litteraly 2 meters from a train line (GREAT)... everytime a train went past we were woken up. On closer inspection the room seriously needed a good clean, i.e. carpets etc.. Time for a quick browse at that Turkish Spa and roof terrace, no words can describe, the Spa is the smaller than my lounge... you would not want to strip off to get in there! and the roof terrace looks over some high rise flats and the main road... nice view! NOT!! I think its safe to stay we will not be staying at the Pasha Hotel ever again.

title: Excellent value
text: Attended a function in London and had to book accomodation quite last minute and after reading mixed reviews about this hotel decided to try it out. First impression when found the area was that of slight apprehension. The hotel is amid a row of shops and had to dash in to get directions to the car park located at the back of the hotel. You then have to walk through the restaurant (which is also where breakfast is served) to get back to the reception area. I was pleasantly surprised at how well kept and clean the hotel was. The staff are extremely accomodating and will go the extra mile to ensure a comfortable stay. I booked 2 single rooms for my friend and I and expected them to be fairly small and I wasn't disappointed. The hotel has obviously had a recent refurb and the room was modern and clean as was the bathroom (no bath just a shower) but perfect for our requirements. There is a bus stop 2 minutes from the hotel and there are several buses which go to the centre of London - IDEAL!! The No. 12 which goes to Oxford Circus is a 24 hour service. Returned back to the hotel in the early hours and didn't feel at all intimidated by the area, in fact stopped at a 24hr Kebab House and had a Lamb Kebab which was freshly cooked and so tasty (recommended by the owner of the hotel). Added extra is that there is a Turkish sauna and a treatment room. For £5.00, breakfast the next morning was great!! Only regret was not having time to dine at the restaurant which has a Turkish theme. Very colourful with one half furnished with low tables and bright scatter cushions in to sit on and dine in a traditional way. Or you can walk over a little wooden bridge which has a small pond underneath with a few carp, goldfish and a turtle to get to the other half of the restaurant which has conventional tables for dining at. I did peruse the menu and saw the food being served the previous night and it smelt and looked quite delicious. I will definitely stay there again and make sure I sample their food. Well done to the staff and Manager - great service!!! Thank you - Audrey and Mike

title: Pros and Cons!
text: Pros: good price and economic hotel in London center, welcoming and polite staff, tasty English breakfast (try it!), nicely decorated restaurant and delicious Turkish kebab (try it!), spacious and clean rooms nicely decorated (specially upper and deluxe rooms ), near bus station and near park (tennis court), shops (outdo bazaar!), restaurants and ten min to train station. just 10 min to heart of London eye by bus or train. Cons: noise of train backyard of hotel, thin walls ad noise of next room, a lot of stairs (without elevator), crowded and noisy street, family and economy rooms in the first floor do not have a good condition at all. all in all it is precious to try it specially in a very expensive city like London!

title: GOOD VALUE FOR MONEY
text: I stayed for three nights last week. It was a pleasant experience. Staff was very friendly and helping at all times. Room was very tidy and clean. Turkish Spa was some thing very different, which i enjoyed. Will love to stay here again and see you soon.

title: Competitive Rates, Interesting Area, Not Flawless
text: Being a wheelchair user and usually going for the standardized safety of the big chains, I tried the Pasha hotel out of pure desperation over those ludicrous London rates. In hindsight, I don't regret it. My room rate of GBP 75 including cooked English breakfast was reasonable and resembled the hotel's overall facilities and services. I would not consider it a bargain, because the competitive rates also reflects the presence of some flaws that clearly are below standard. Judging the Pasha based on the rates offered, it should be compared to a suburban travelodge or premier inn. Based on such comparison, the Pasha's location is a pro. At the time of booking, I could not manage to find a travelodge that was halfways in central London offering the same rates. Camberwell Road is a lively place with all sorts of shops, a place where real people live, work and shop. It did not feel unsafe, and the bus connections are good. My disabled room offered a small, but functional bathroom with a shower stool in the roll-in shower. The overall impression was a bit uninviting and unsightly, especially as the walls and the carpets had parts coming off and dirty spots to them. Inefficient heating, leaving the room a bit cold. There are odd contrasts all around this hotel with some decorations looking brand new and exceptionally clean while other spots look as though they were left forgotten during renovations. I slept quite well nevertheless, no major source of nighttime noise. The railway line directly behind the hotel does not seem to have a very frequent service

title: Last minute booking
text: Booked this hotel at the last minute for a sudden business trip as limited availability in London that night. Paid £120 for the night, which was way over the top. Taxi driver laughed when I said where I was going. Negatives: Very dodgy area, generally shabby public areas, off hand staff and in room TV showing only Turkish/Arabic TV channels. Positives: Bedroom not bad. If you just need a room for the night and could get it for £70-£80 a night it would be a reasonable deal. If you're looking for anything more forget it.

title: It's NOT a 3* boutique hotel!
text: If you want basic and a good location then it's OK as the bus stop is near enough outside and a bus straight to central London all night long. Check in quite easy, first impressions were OK. The room is where it all goes wrong. So we had a window that wouldn't shut so we wedged a shampoo bottle to hold it shut. The toilet had the most horrendous smell coming from it. The shower had a bath tap in it so you couldn't stand directly under the shower and drainage was poor. The hairdryer was broken front and back. The sink was being propped up by a leg that wasn't even attached. To top it off the smoke alarm in the room was covered by a plastic bag!!!!! We could hear every movement from the room above us. A random light and switch that didn't work. About 50 fag butts just outside the bedroom window. However the bed was clean, crisp white sheets and reasonably comfortable. Would I go back..... No, minor details that are so easily fixed. We reported the window and the toilet, they left the shampoo there and did nothing to the loo and all it needed was a bit of bleach to take that smell away.

title: Prison in London --BEWARE
text: My fiancé has been there on business for a couple of months. I was informed the company he was working for is not paying His bill so I attempted to give them my credit card from here in the US to pay for the bill. They have refused and continue to hold him hostage until he can produce cash. His credit card is not working and the bill keeps growing. Yesterday I couldn't reach my fiancé only to find out today he attempted suicide and when I contacted the hotel yesterday they denied he was a guest. Bewhere you may become a prisoner of this hotel and the only way out may result in your demise.! I will be communicating with management again to resolve this issue. A concerned US citizen.

title: Clean, lovely deco, friendly staff, good Brkfast, great location, perfect.
text: The greatest thing about this Hotel is its location and its rates. Its neighbourhood is not the most beautiful in London, but with over 10 different bus routes going past it, and its within walking distance of Elephant & Castle and Waterloo stations. The reception also has the best map of London including a map of the bus routes, for free ! There is a Chinese 'All-U-can-Eat' nearby. The hotel is a 10-15min bus trip to most attractions, eg. London Eye, British Museum, Westminster Abbey, etc.

title: nightmare
text: Hotel in horrible location always made sure to get back to hotel early as didnt want to be out late in that area room was very small and to hot damp in the windows not all lights worked in the room bathroom lighting very dark tap fell of the sink and shower took over an hr to drain didnt sleep much due to busy roads stayed here as price seemed ok £90 prpn but think that is a lot for what you get next time will pay little extra for decent hotel wouldnt recomend pasha to anyone

title: Dirty
text: I arrived late the first night to find that my bed sheets were full of somebody's hair. They apologised and gave me another room with clean sheets. You'd think that after this they would do anything to make the rest of your permanence enjoyable. The second night again I walked in at 6pm and found that the sheets and towels had not been changed and the room had not been cleaned.

title: Overpriced
text: As we drove up to the hotel our hearts sank at the sight of this place. We tried not to jump to conclusions. We were directed to their 'parking lot', which was a grimy, back-alley driveway. The journey from the back door through the hotel to the reception took us through the hotel restaurant, along dirty carpeted dingy corridors, an out of order lift with creepy dressed up mannequins in it. The rooms were worse than we expected. Dirty sheets, low ceilings, terrible views, noisy floorboards, filthy carpets. Nothing nice to say about this place. Disgustingly overpriced.

title: Avoid!
text: This hotel is a small step above a Guatemalan hostel. The positive was that front desk staff were very friendly & helpful. Although it is on a bus line, it was in a relatively poor & dirty part of town. You get what you pay for.

title: Small, budget, low quality rooms but nice food
text: We had a room for one night stay only. Dirty mattress, not fresh smell, due to cleaning chemical possibly. Wardrobe with a cracked mirror on it. No lift. Restaurant food was ok, but not perfect for a cost that have been paid. Car park for 3-4 vehicles only, next to bin area. Mould in a bathroom shower. Cheap Hotel, not a 3 star rating definitely.

title: I FOLLOWED THE RED CARPET AND WILL COME AGAIN !!!
text: Very nice people warm family atmosphere, helpfull staff , good location , oohhhh very Relaxing Turkish Bath Rooms are clean and room service is quick, reception is very helpfull. Weird but quality and different food yumyy yummyyy :))

title: Hotel
text: Went for 4 nights. You get what you pay for to be honest. Staff really lovely. Room was clean except that there was a lot of tiny black hair in bed so that put me off a little bit. Fridge wasn't working which was disappointing because it was really hot. Air con wasn't working either. Area a bit dodgy so not the best idea to wonder about late at night but the bus stops are really close. And wifi is really bad. But you get fresh towels every day which was really good. Probably wouldn't stay there again but really happy with the price. So would recommend it for anyone with low budget.

title: I paid but never stayed!!
text: I booked the hotel for one night and very clearly out in the correct date that I needed to stay, which I double checked before pressing enter. On making the payment, it came up with a completely different date. I rang the hotel and they said there was nothing they could do and that I should ring the administrators, 'AGODA'! On attempting to ring these people, it was clear that I was being connected to a number abroad and the message facility was in a foreign language. There was no other way to contact them and the hotel couldn't/ wouldn't help so I lost out on £75.00 basically! It is not so much the hotel that deserves a bad review but Agoda, who they use to administer their bookings! Very poor service indeed.

title: Awful stay....NEVER AGAIN!
text: We stayed in this hotel on the 13th and 14th June as we were going to ministry of sound on the 13th and wanted to stay close! We booked a deluxe double room at £100 a night. We got in to our room (number 322) the room was dark and boiling hot. We noticed the air conditioning unit was switched off at the wall so we switched it on for it to blow out hot air...not helpful at all. We opened the windows to let some air in to find a train track right next to our room with trains going past every 10-20 minutes. The floor in the bathroom was dirty, luckily we had some wipes with us so we were able to wipe over the floor. The shower took about 10 minutes to reach a warm temperature and when it was a suitable temperature it would fluctuate from boiling to freezing. We ate in the restaurant for quickness on the Friday and found that the meat was very chewy, service was slow and then they wacked on a 10% service charge, the waitress actually didn't add this charge on when using the card machine, however she soon realised and made us pay it even though we didn't feel they warranted a tip. Our room was also above the restaurant which plays extremely loud music from 8-11 it was getting so loud that we couldn't even hear the tv! When we asked when it was going to be stopping we also informed them about the air conditioning in our room, it was working but they just "forgot" to give us the remote. It seems our money goes on the owner branding the curtains and bedding with the hotel name...they even had their toiletries named after the hotel of which was actually spelt incorrectly...gives you ok hope when they can't get the spelling of their own hotel correct on all of their branded items! I will say that the room and en suite were of a good size and the bed was relatively comfy however these are the only positive comments i have about the hotel. I would never stay there again and would never recommend the hotel to anyone!!

title: Steer clear
text: Let me start by saying the rooms were clean and the staff friendly.... that's as good as it gets. The beds were uncomfortable, the air con did not work and the room backed onto train tracks. The layout of the hotel is very odd almost labyrinth like, and the stairs were steep. There is nothing in the local area to do in the evening and you are limited in your choices for eating out.

title: Clean cheap hotel in London
text: I have to be honest and admit that I almost panicked and cancelled my booking after reading the reviews on here. I'm so glad I didn't. This was a clean hotel with cheap parking in London. It cost 5 pounds to park our hire car all afternoon, overnight and some of the morning (where everywhere else is 5 pounds per hour!). The bathroom was clean, modern and huge. At first we thought our heater didn't work but after reading the instructions which told us to turn it on and wait five minutes, everything was fine and our room was toasty warm for the rest of our stay. There were complimentary packets of crisps and cans of soft drinks in the fridge and all the usual tea and coffee making stuff and of course free wifi! The staff were friendly but we didn't really see to much of them because we didn't have any reason to speak to them after we checked in. There are a lot of winding hallways and steep staircases so you'd need to keep that in mind when booking.There area is very multicultral which might put some off but we didn't have any problems with anyone, they were just locals going about their business. The bustop out front has busses that can take you anywhere in London. Again, I'm so glad I didn't panic and book somewhere more expensive.

title: Oh Lordy!
text: Having been unlucky enough to stay there recently I felt compelled to inform others about this awful hotel. The room was absolutely tiny, and the railway track immediately behind it was so close you could almost touch the passing trains, which would keep you awake every time they go by. The massive construction site just the other side of the railway track was another joy every morning whilst trying to drive out of the hotel "car park" ie blocked in by site vehicles. The passing air traffic into & out of heathrow was a pleasure to listen to whilst in bed on top of being serenaded by police car sirens throughout the night. The local area is also a delight with the dynamic mix of both scum and vilanny just outside the hotel front door. In short, I'll not be back.

title: Felt like a crack den
text: You get what you pay for when you pay very little for a London hotel. Very dingy and not presented well at all looked more like one of my student flats that was a complete s**thole. Fixtures looked like they were bought in a car boot sale and the TV in the room was as big as my left toe nail. Pool table had no black or white balls so had to write on spare red and yellow ones. Which obviously got pocketed so we couldn't continue half way through. No telephones in the room so no way to call reception and cry down the phone about how my pillow was like a bag of sand. Bathroom was ok but in general the whole place needs gutting and refurbishment to look any decent standard. Lastly we got a nice view from our room of one of the premier drug inducing spots north of Peckham. Our window/bedroom wall was attached to the roof of the next building with a kids football and some needles (picture attached). Staff were lovely, spa was also great but short staffed for a couples massage. Our brief encounter with the restaurant was nice and food was good but couldn't overshadow the state of decay of the general hotel. We spent the second night somewhere else. Wouldn't recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Bizarre.
text: This place looks like someone's had a go at tarting the place up then got bored or run out of money. At a glance it's seems ok but then as you delve a little deeper you see the obvious bits that just haven't been cleaned in ages. For example the shower head. The toilet seat also need a wipe. I'm no clean freak but I keep my own place at a far higher standard and having worked in a hotel before understand the basic expectations. On a funnier side the tv is mounted to high on the wall you would need to be standing on the bed to see the picture properly and the last guest appears to have been an elephant as the matteress aint all that flat. Now all grumbles aside it isn't the worst place I've stayed in and the price is pretty cheap. The staff all seem really nice and helpful could maybe just do with a bit more attention on the clean front and some tlc. More something to giggle at then run out screaming.

title: Friendliest most helpful staff anywhere. Great restaurant.
text: I needed to stay as close to Kings College Hospital as possible. The hotel staff could not have been more helpful and supportive. I stayed for about 5 nights. The facilities are fine and terrific value. The restaurant has an authentic atmosphere. I loved the food (try the Carrot salad followed by jumbo prawns) and the restaurant manager was as good as in any 5* place. Thanks for a great stay. Mike, Devon

title: good value
text: for 1 or 2 nights this is ideal, i needed somewhere reasonably priced with good links to central london. Clean no frill room, excellent showeroom and for the price i will definately use the Pasha again.

title: Very nice stay
text: Stayed here for a few days, comfortable room and the staff were very nice and helpful. Great value for its closeness to city of london, on camberwell road close to all the shops and the bus stops right outside, couldnt ask for more!

title: Awful hotel
text: We booked this hotel because of the location, price and parking. When we arrived we were directed to the 'car park' which is a bit of waste ground at the back of the hotel, we were doing London to Brighton bike ride and had a van with bikes, we felt very unsure leaving the van/bikes due to the surroundings. We were told we could get to reception from the back so went through the back door to what looked like an Indian restaurant, then onto a pool room, we noticed a smell but didn't think much of it at this point as thought it may be the food. We then had to go through a maze of corridors to get to reception and there were strange men lurking in the corridors and they seemed to be watching us. We checked in and were told there was complimentary food and drinks in the room, which we though was very strange given how cheap the hotel was. We were shown to our room up some every uneven stairs, again there were men in the corridor that seemed to be watching us. (Two girls) The smell in the room was overwhelming, the window was open and something had been sprayed to mask the smell but it was disgusting, I am unsure what the smell actually was. We returned to reception and asked for another room, the 2nd room was just as bad, when we're asked what the smell was the lady said sanitation, which I presume means it just wasn't clean! But it must have been 20 years of stick it was that bad!! We returned to reception and asked for a refund, as could not stay in this hotel. The only good thing I can say about the hotel is there was no argument with giving a refund and the staff did not try to pretend there wasn't a smell. I have never been so pleased to get a space in a travelodge, however would have preferred to sleep in car than this hotel.

title: Not again
text: As others have said, the staff is lovely, but there is little else to recommend The Pasha, I'm afraid - other than price. Nearest tube is a very brisk 20 minute walk, though there are plenty of buses. My room was small and the bed was hard. The lavatory seat was broken. My room was quiet at the week-end, but is next to a building site, so don't expect a lie-in during the week. I didn't eat dinner there, but the breakfast is not good and the wait for food is far too long.

title: Could easily improve
text: This could be a reasonable budget hotel with a bit of remedial work. Our room was on the top floor (3 floors up) at the front of the hotel, overlooking Camberwell Road. The stairs are very steep and narrow with no handrails so would not suit everyone. The room, though minimalist, was not bad but suffered from traffic noise and light from the street. The double glazing units in the window had broken seals and were full of condensation and the opening vent did not fit properly, letting in noise from the busy main road. The curtains really need blackout linings to reduce light shing through. The bathroom, which looked to be recently refurbished, was quite good but there was a lingering drain smell. The restaurant specialises in Georgian and Turkish cuisine and attracts non-residents. It is quite unusual, offereing a choice of low carpeted seating in the Turkish style or regular tables. We ate there twice and would rate it slightly better than the accommodation. An interesting range of dishes are offered.

title: We will never be back!
text: We booked this hotel as the website was amazing, let me clarify, it was not amazing in anyway, shape or form. We would have been better staying in a hostel. The rooms were revolting, you wouldn't take your shoes off to walk on the carpet in fear of getting stuck to it! The beds were too short had 2 mattresses stacked on top of one another and the duvets were childrens length, the curtains were tied back with string and you couldn't see out of the window. The shower in the bathroom was broken so you had to hold the shower head whilst washing, pretty impossible The stairs were makeshift, the car park was a garage... The list goes on

title: Awful, Overpriced hotel!
text: Me any gf stayed in the "deluxe" doube suite, i can say there was definately nothing deluxe about it. We spent most of the night out enjoying the nightlife, so we didn't spend much time at the hotel, thank god. There was mould above the shower head, large gaps in where the sockets should be, holes in the duvet and dirty walls. The only slightly good thing about the hotel was the staff who were relatively friendly. Apart from that the hotel looks like a cornershop from outside and the parking behind it is horrendous, litter and filth everywhere. Pay abit more and get a proper hotel!

title: Great value for money
text: To be really truthful, I wasn't expecting a lot for the money we paid to stay there. The hotel itself is in amongst the parade of shops along the road and doesn't look too special or different from the outside. But then you step inside and the staff are helpful, the hotel is light but without looking artificially bright (unlike some chain hotels) and we found our room easily. We did have to climb three sets of stairs to reach our room but it wasn't too unbearable. The room itself (We had a deluxe double for £85 per night for two people) was big, spacious, clean, with lots of wardrobe space and a large bathroom. If the saying goes that you get what you paid for, then we both felt that we got a lot for our money. There was no decent view out the window and no nightlife close to the hotel, but we wanted a safe base to leave our things and to sleep in, rather than to spend a lot of time in the hotel. Overall, I would definitely recommend it and would stay there again quite happily.

title: Not great
text: Really didn't like this hotel, the first impression as we came through the back entrance via the restaurant was that it was faded and a bit grubby. The carpets throughout were very stained and dirty. The room was ok, but smelt stale. The area seems a bit rough and didn't feel too comfortable walking along the road at night. We were glad to check out and won't be going back.

title: Husband in Kings Hospital
text: This is what I consider a 'hidden gem' - this is the second time I have stayed whilst my husband was in Kings Hospital. First off - don't judge a book by its cover !!! I have stayed in a single/twin/triple (depending on what family have been up) all rooms perfectly adequate - comfortable and clean - reception staff excellent - very very helpful - restaurant fantastic and breakfast is truly wonderful and served by an extremely handsome and accommodating young man - please give this hotel a try - fantastic as a base for sight seeing and visiting friends - definitely under rated x

title: Somewhere to stay
text: A pleasant but fairly unremarkable hotel within easy reach of central London by public transport. Parking is chargeable in the small hotel car park but local side streets are free at the weekends. Room was comfortable and seemed clean.

title: Outrageous
text: First of all, the hotel is in the middle of nowhere at least a 15 minute walk from tube station and some of the rooms are smaller than my bathroom. The service in the restaurant was absolutely awful and had to wait nearly an hour and a half for my food and 20 minutes for a drink. Beds are uncomfortable and the TV is so high on the wall that you can't see it lying down on the bed which is more or less on the floor

title: Amazing value - superb staff!
text: I was travelling on expenses for a small charity, so booked the cheapest room I could find near where I was to be (The Oval). I was very nervous of somewhere offering a room at £50 per night and expected the worst. When I arrived, the staff seemed genuinely pleased to greet me and show me to my room - much more welcoming that many five star hotels I have stayed in. A bit quirky, limited space, but everything you need (including air conditioning for warmer times). The TV worked with a good choice of channels - a big bonus when you are travelling alone. The restaurant - half Turkish in layout, half western European - was excellent value for money. Good range of near eastern dishes. On the Friday night it included live music. A really great experience in both hotel and restaurant. Do they just employ really helpful staff, or is their training something to be envied? This is only the second hotel where I have felt all the staff are pleased (rather than just willing) to put themselves out for the benefit of the guests, Well done to the whole team!

title: Eccentric, Friendly, Economy hotel
text: It is hard to have the heart to say anything negative about this hotel as the staff are so genuinely friendly and helpful, and are prepared to go out of their way to ensure your comfort. They kept my bag a whole day after I checked out at no extra cost for which I am extremely grateful I think the staff at the hotel are mainly from the former Soviet Central Asian Republics and is a hub for the community which gives it an exotic vibe. The decor is Central Asian with a slight Soviet flavour. More could be done with decor in the rooms, in particular, to make them a bit more boutique-like and less utilitarian. That said the bed was fine and the bathroom functioned well. I would come again for the atmosphere and friendly staff if nothing else.

title: Good hotel and location
text: Good hotel and location near to Tower Bridge..Staff was decent, and rooms were alright.. Water bottles, Chips and biscuits were complementary which was good. Could easily hear the sounds from outside the rooms. Breakfast needs to be included.

title: Noisy stay
text: The hotel is tired and shabby. To get to the rooms there are some very steep stairs, no lift that I saw. After climbing two flights with bags and suit cover it was a relief to arrive at the door. The decor is tired, dark brown paint and wood everywhere. The room was freezing as a window had been left open. The bathroom was, again dated. The hot water took a long time to get hot. The bed was king size, two singles pushed together, and the duvet didn't reach either side of the bed. In fact at two o'clock in the morning it meant a trip to reception to get another one as neither of us could sleep. To add to the ambiance of the room there is a train line running past the room at window level and the trains are thundering past until the early hours. The one ray of light was the restaurant, which has to be expirenced. Finally the restaurant was directly below he room so loud thumping music was heard until late on.

title: Surprised
text: Expected things to be different.... However Staff so friendly and helpfull with parking and making sure I was looked after thanks very much. Small Maintenance needed in the rooms but ok. They need to advertise to there guests better the restaurant and facilities as I was unaware. Nothing in the room. Breakfast :- No Orange Juice and no Bacon on the full english they could charge a little more for breakfast and make it really good. Friendliness made up 100% for any shortcomings ... Come on guys just push a little more and you will be very different to other hotels .

title: Ok for london
text: Near here and there. Reasonable price ok quility. Reception was(the ladies, sorry guys try smile a bit) and helpfull. Could go again. Near to one of the best club in london!! Did not use any facilities thoughso I am not sure about all other spa hammam and restaurant services

title: Well pleased on their attitude to my concerns about reviews
text: Read the trip advisor reviews after booking and was concerned about reviews. Expressed my concerns to staff who happily took me to check rooms over. They were clean, beds clean and comfy checked for signs of bed bugs (none) toilet, shower etc clean and well stocked with no smells coming from drains. Fridge working all fittings in room fine. Staff admitted to having problems in past. All in no complaints and the attached restaurant was adequate and reasonable with very pleasant staff. Would I stay again? Yes I would

title: Really disappointed 😐
text: When we looked on the booking website the hotel at first glance looked worth the 80 pound however when we arrived we were greatly disappointed. The staff were friendly and helpful about the parking but the room was not nice at all. The bathroom was semi clean but when u ran the tap in the sink a smell of sewage filled the room. There was a small fridge hidden in the wardrobe that was hot and filthy and to top it all of the window opened out onto a train tracks with trains running every 7 mins so could not sleep plus the air con didn't work so had no choice but to hAve window open.

title: customer services terrible
text: My wife used the spa, this being her 3rd time there, but on her last visit she wanted to steam room, but there was problems with the steam being the same temperature while we used it. My wife complained but they would not reduce the price want they paid even though she told them many times throughout the session. The only concession was to give her more time even though the steam room wasn't working, so she left. After many calls and texts, he finally replied, very rude and sarcastic!!!!!!!!

title: Would not stay again
text: Friendly and helpful staff Big room A/C fan in the room Far from "Underground" about 2 kilometers walk. Rough area - wouldn't let my wife/kids walk alone Very noisy area, could not sleep first night. Not very clean room - stains and pizza pieces on walls.

title: Glad to leave
text: I was impressed by the hotel website and the convenient location,as I was visiting from Cornwall for a wedding in South East London.On arrival at the hotel,I found the staff very friendly and helpful.I was provided with a large vase in which to put some flowers I had been given ,so it was a good start. When arriving at my tiny single bedroom,it was very cold as the heating was not on and it took ages to warm up.I had to remove a cheap,thin blanket from the bed and a couple of cushions,as they had some rather suspect looking stains on them.(yeurghh! ). The bathroom was unheated and VERY cold.The red carpet running throughout the hotel was absolutely filthy and the management would do well to simply remove it and show off the marble floors. When I gave my comments to the girl on the front reception ,whilst checking out,in particular about the stained bedding,she made a comment about the room only being a standard ( the implication being that if I wanted a budget room ,I had no right to complain about revolting bedding.)In my opinion,the whole place needs a complete overhaul and certain members of staff need to be trained to actually listen to negative feedback and realise that their customers may actually have important information to give them. I would never stay here again and would not dream of recommending this place to anyone else.I'm not in the habit of making public complaints,but feel that other people need to know that this is a place to avoid.

title: Some people are never satisfied - I was!
text: I don't know what some contributors to this site expect from the hotels and restaurants they visit. I'm a food, drink and travel journalist and I stay in many hotels and eat in many restaurants all over Europe which feature on trip-advisor.com, and I think that many of the whingers who contribute should get a life. The Hotel Pasha is easy to find and, yes, it's a bit off the beaten track but handy for the City and possessed of great charm. The interior is quirky and original, the room was small but had the requisite bed, bath and bog, perfectly clean and comfortable, with a telly that actually worked. I loved the restaurant - part Turkish divan, part modern European, with a 'river' dividing the two. Dinner was a complimentary starter and a main course (the menu is eclectic to say the least)... And cost £7 plus wine. For £50 a night, a ten-quid taxi-ride from London Bridge station, it's real find. And as for the standard of service - well, I've stayed in very much more expensive places which were nowhere near as good. I just don't know what some people expect of budget hotels.

title: Great hotel, good location, reasonable price, handy for transport, slept well!
text: Nice place, though wasn't expecting it when we arrived in the area. July 2015 1 night stay with boyfriend, did the job for the night. Friendly staff, comfy bed, nice bathroom, good shower. So easy to get bus outside to London central or anywhere around London, frequent services, cheep with oyster card. We found it much better than getting the tube! Reasonable price for half decent hotel in London £80 for double ensuite room. Would stay again and book in for a turkish bath too!

title: Our stay
text: We were there for 4 nights. Our stay was good, but the food was not our cup of tee. The breakfast was verry nice but with dinner it's a outher story.(tastes differ simply.) If there was a problem, the staff wil do annything to make it good. they were verry nice to the gast. Oure room om the 3e floor was ok. a lote of stairs and no elevaor. Bathroom need more finishing. There is a waredrope but you can not use him. It was to small and there were too much stuff in it, that not belong in a waredrope. overall it was a experience.

title: birthday treat
text: my boyfriend am i stayed here for my bday amazing hotel with high standard good restraunt staff very friendly reception staff very rude n ignorant excellent location and had a comfy 3night stay (bathroom in room was impressive excellent shower!

title: Not worthed
text: The location was good for us, but the hotel is just not worthed, I do not recommend it! The room was small, oldfurnished, the carped was horrible, we could not take off our shoes. The sheets was dirty with stains, the duvet was heinous. The air conditioner leaks on the carpet. The windows was very dirty, the drapes smells. Only the bathroom was ok. Bad experience for us, just not worth the money

title: i will visit again
text: the food and restaurant was satisfying and all staff were very pleasant,making me feel comfortable ihad my first exsperience in the turkish bath which i thoroughly enjoyed

title: Good Value for money...
text: We booked this hotel as convenient base for an anniversary weekend to London to see a gig at Brixton Academy. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. The bus stopped almost outside the hotel meaning we could get to and from the gig easily and without walking far (even at 3am when the gig finished) which was perfect since tubes dont run then. The hotel isnt 5* but it was clean and comfy and the staff even surprised us with wine and balloons in the room! Breakfast was brilliantly good value - cant think where else in London you could get a cooked breakfast, toast, coffee and juice for £5.00!! Thank you and we shall be staying again if we are ever at Brixton Academy.

title: Nice place inside, shame about the water system and noisy trains
text: I stayed here as everywhere else nearby was fully booked. I saw a bad review on TA but there were more positive reviews so thought i'd give it a whirl. I had been warned by friends that this area was quite dodgy, to back this up a black cab that we flagged down from nearby Waterloo refused to brings us back to the hotel and just drove off to leave us freezing in minus 2 about midnight - anyway getting back to review of Pasha, the room was modern and clean, staff friendly and professional but we woke on Sunday morning to discover there was no water supply to our room. I reported this to reception and was told it was a known problem, (turns out the whole 3rd floor was affected by a water pressure issue) "we're sorry" they said. I asked how we were supposed to shower\brush our teeth? The offer was to travel down to the ground floor and use another facility, we declined and left. When i went ot settle up i expressed my concerns and said i wasn't happy to pay, the counter offer was "other hotels would give you 20% off" as the room itself had met all conditions. We agreed to disagree in the end and Pasha made a token gesture by refunding under half the cost. Overall impression Dodgy area Inside hotel is very nice, staff are good. Water pressure thing needs sorting and the trains are noisy Make your own minds up, i was unimpressed

title: Value for money
text: I stayed at the Pasha Hotel lastnight. Reception staff were welcoming. Room (single) was basic but ok. Linen was clean as was the bathroom. General decor needs attention but definitely value for money. If it were spruced up, it would cost more. Dinner in the restaurant was good. Generous portions. Will definitely go back.

title: A little hidden gem
text: We booked this hotel very last minute & we worried when we realised the unsavory location of the hotel, we needn't of panicked though. The staff were extremely friendly & helpful & carried our bags to our room. We had a triple room 1 double bed & 1 single bed, decent tv & free view box. (but if your going to London for a night out who wants to be watching tv?) the room was spacious clean & delightful. There 24hr Turkish bath's & steam room were a godsend for 2 hungover ladies. In the evening the belly dancing was a laugh to join in with & I have to say that in a more suitable location they could easily charge double! Tea & coffee, coca cola, biscuits & crisps in our room was a well received welcome to our room too. A bus stop directly outside was handy & free wifi too. All in all a really good experience, if you want the Ritz then book the Ritz but if you want real London with friendly people & good value for money book here, I know we will be again!

title: Awful
text: I was not expecting much- just somewhere clean near Kings Hospital. Unfortunately I'm still scratching! Hotel is a weird conglomeration of restaurant, sunbeds and, bizarrely, a rather dodgy looking photo studio. The floor was covered in dust sheets which were clearly designed as some sort of trap for unwary feet. My room was oddly shaped and tiny, with a built in wooden bed frame that reeked of urine. Although the sheets were clean the next morning I was covered in bites

title: A weekend in S London
text: This is an interesting hotel and our experience was positive. In fact there are 3 businesses here, hotel, spa & restaurant Our room was great and staff good but we booked a double and not sure that two singles pushed together is the same, we werent bothered. Parking is an issue, only 3-4 spaces, we were lucky, not sure I would park my car in the surrounding roads The restaurant is Mid Asian and we had a great meal Overall, worth a punt but PARKING PARKING PARKING !!!!!!

title: JUST DREADFUL!!!!!.....AVOID
text: I'm struggling to find words to describe just how bad this hotel is...... Dark, gloomy, dirty, and so close to the train tracks that you could almost lean out and touch the trains as they pass....which is every 5 minutes (and makes everything in the room shake - like a bad sit-com sketch...!!).... Paper thin walls so you can hear conversations in the next room, the room had a huge piece of wood simply nailed to the ceiling of the bathroom to cover the hole made where water had leaked through from the bathroom above. I genuinely worried that the whole building was a fire hazard as there was only one tiny wooden staircase as an exit for around 15 rooms - LETHAL! If you are a deaf,insomniac train-spotter with low standards of personal hygeine and a disregard for your own safety and wellbeing and a penchant for the decor and style of cheap brothels....THIS IS THE PLACE FOR YOU !!!.......if you're not.....AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!

title: Avoid!
text: Stayed overnight as was working in the area. My van was broken into in their private car park and all my tools were stolen. Staff were very unhelpful! Key was kept in the hotel safe as I was blocking another vehicle in and there was no forced entry,all a bit suspicious for my liking!

title: Very Good Value
text: We booked a week in the Pasha because our son was having an operation in near by King's College Hospital. We booked a double economy room as our intention was to use it infrequently. The hotel was ideally situated for the hospital - 20 minute walk or 10 minute ride on the number 45 Denmark Hill bus. The staff were extremely friendly and couldn't do enough for us. The restaurant served excellent food. The room was compact but at £65 per room per night was excellent value. We would definately use again.

title: Avoid if you want to sleep in peace!
text: Where do I begin.... To start with, the area surrounding the hotel looks like something out of London gang movie. I wouldn't have been surprised if when I left in the morning i woke up to a murder scene. In the short 20 minute walk from the station to the hotel i felt like i could have been mugged about 50 times. The reception area of the hotel is not so bad. Very chic and not too shabby looking. The staff at reception were a bit hit and miss. One member was very helpful whereas the didn't really seem to want to be there. Upon navigating my way through the labyrinth of narrow corridors to the back of the hotel where my room was and climbing the exceptionally narrow and crooked staircase, i encountered a broken door to my room. After navigating my way all the way back to reception i was given the manual key to use which i was told i had to hand in at reception every time i left the hotel which was annoying. The room itself was... interesting. upon first glance it appears quite pleasant and a good value for what you pay. However upon closer examination i found dirty marks on tables and other surfaces suggesting they had not been cleaned particularly well before my stay. the "double" bed was actually 2 very uncomfortable single beds pushed together. The bathroom was very nice and modern however had no extractor fan what so ever! As a result just 2 minutes in the shower turned the whole room into a sauna/steam room. The only way to clear the bathroom was to vent the steam through the room and out the window. The room itself was also freezing cold. The portable heater sitting at the end of the bed, did little to help and looked like a fire waiting to happen. And then i come to the worst part of all, THE NOISE. MY GOD THE NOISE. I accept that a hotel in London is never going silent but dear lord. My room appeared to be positioned over the restaurant (which i did not visit) which for some reason felt the need to play excessively loud music until the early hours of the morning. considering i had to get up early for an interview i was particularly unimpressed with this. On top of that the trains that go past every 20 minutes are deafening and the constant police sirens never failed to remind me that i could be stabbed in my bed at any moment. I felt so unsafe in this hotel i actually placed a chair in front of the door before i could even attempt to get any sleep. Needless to say i checked out as early as i could in the morning with no intention of ever returning!

title: Surprisingly good.
text: Had to book an economical hotel at short notice and this popped up in searches. Decided to give it a try and was pleasantly surprised. It's not upmarket and be prepared for basic fixtures and fitting but bed was comfy, shower room was good and staff were friendly and helpful. I've certainly stayed in more expensive places which were worse. Note it's not super close to the tube and it's not the best area but I had a reasonable stay.

title: Not awful but not great.
text: I only paid £50 for this room so, in all fairness I don’t have much right to moan and it was good value for money. But that being said I do have a few gripes. Arrived at 11.30am, host was outside the front door having a cigarette, she said hello, put out her cigarette straight away and came inside with us which was nice not keeping us waiting. We couldn’t check in till 2 which was fine and they allowed us to keep our luggage in their office (I did notice on the wall that if you wish to keep your luggage there for more than 2 hours on the day of check OUT you have to pay £10). Arrived back at 2pm & given keys to room 53, top floor. Up (i think) 6-7 flights of stairs STEEP NARROW stairs. So do not stay here if you have difficulty climbing stairs. We are fit and have no issues and we got out of breathe walking up there. The ‘studio’ is basically the size of a small hotel room. Bed was awfully squeaky, felt like it was going to break every time I moved around. The place was incredibly hot- especially after walking all those stairs however the window only opened an inch (for safety I guess) however it didn’t stay open. So we had no choice but to sit and swelter. No room to move AT ALL. They basically replaced the wardrobe with a sink, microwave and cupboards. Hardly a studio. Because they had replaced the wardrobe there was nowhere we could put clothes. So our 1m walkway from the door to the bed was full of suitcase. Way way too small. Very disappointed. Don’t stay here if it’s for more than a couple of nights because you generally can’t move - unless we were given the smallest room there i am not sure). About 10 ish mins walk to padd station, shops and tube & 15 min to Hyde park. When you get to Paddington station. Just keep walking to the right on praed street until you get to the park grand hotel on Devonshire terrace, and then turn right and Dylan apartments is down there. Front door has been smashed and just taped together which is off putting. Didn’t try the breakfast. Woke up at 2 am from neighbours coming home because walls and doors are so thin & floors so creaky. Also someone below us was being loud and annoying and their neighbour started banging the doors and screaming for them to shut up. So was awake for about an hour which was a little annoying. Not the hotels faults but they do stay there & it just goes to show how thin and old the place is. All that being said it is hard to find somewhere in Paddington for £50 a night, they should just replace the kitchen with a wardrobe as it was totally unneeded and in the way. (For most people I spoke to also). The hosts were nice and friendly and it was a great location. Quiet but close to all needs. Happy with the sleep we had but needs some doing up.

title: Totally Remodeled
text: I first stayed at the Dylan Hotel in 1978 when it was family-owned. Over the years, we probably booked here a dozen times because of several geographic advantages. Most importantly, Devonshire Terrace is a quiet street where one can sleep soundly without loud disturbances. There is a laundromat, pub, and small food shop at one end of the block

title: Dreadful!
text: Do not book here. Appreciate it's budget but studio we had was nothing like the pictures or description. Obviously a basement down dangerous steps - very dirty. Double bed squashed in between two walls, two electric rings next to sink!!! Didn't work anyway. No kettle just toaster (which we wouldn't use), microwave only to make hot drink. One plate, 1 knife and 3 forks, 2 chipped mugs. Bathroom awful. We couldn't use shower - curtain was covered in mould and dirty. We spent minimum time (sheets were clean at least but didn't give us much confidence). We left soon as we could next day after a very bad night and noise from adjacent room. Never use again.

title: DO NOT STAY HERE.
text: This is by far the worst places I’ve ever had to stay. It stinks, very badly, I continue had to spray the room with deodorant (all I had on me) and keep the bathroom tight shut, to be able to cope through it. The place was very dirty, the bed sheets didn’t look like they had been changed and it was covered in dirt and dust I wouldn’t dream of eating in there even though that was my original plan. The kitchenette is filthy all the utensils look used and swilled but not cleaned. The decor is very outdated and the curtain allows in a far amount of light. The room is small and cramped but I could have coped with that for the price. I had just done a 24 hour day travel from South America so I thought any bed would have felt better than the plane but honestly I was out of this place as soon as the sun outside glared through the windows in the morning. Disgusting. Decent location, cheap price but definitely not worth it.

title: Very Bad Quality of Room
text: ANTS ... ANTS... ANTS... all over black ants on the room. They dnt hep you clean the room. The condition of toaster was AWFULL. The UTENSILS SMELLED WORST. Not even a 1 star hotel cum apartments. Dirty rooms during check in. OVERPRICED for sure. Only Bathroom and toilet were good. Bedsheets and duvet not cleaned. Bed too hard to sleep. Insects inside the toaster.

title: They are Heartless
text: Do not you ever pay them online. If you will have any problem, they will never refund you anything. There prices for the same room and on the same date varies from one entry to another

title: Good position...exhausting stairs!
text: This hotel is very well situated: Paddington is a good place for visiting London thanks to underground. Rooms are very small but clean and every electric appliance work well. Also the shower and the kitchen are ok. There were many rooms in the hotel but unfortunately our room was on the third floor and the small wooden spiral staircase was really exhausting, especially with the luggage.

title: Okay for a no frills place to stay
text: It was not the cleanest or most comfortable accommodation but perfectly adequate for our needs. The room was small and beds wobbly and bathroom a bit grim but it was fine. There was a small kitchenette with a fridge, microwave and two ring stove. The shower was fine. We were in studio 3 in the basement and it was quite noisy from the guests upstairs. This is a good place if you want cheap and cheerful accommodation with no frills and the lovely cation is quite good with about a 6 minute walk to the tube. Staff were friendly and helpful. The room came with towels, loo roll, linen, big TV and very basic supply of crockery and cutlery. Would definitely go back.

title: not bad for the price
text: ok so this won't be the best place you ever stay, nor will it be luxurious however for central London for that price its well worth it, Clean, fresh bedding and towels each day, and shower/bathroom/kitchen/bedroom its pretty good. lots of steep stairs and not overly spacious but if you need somewhere to just sleep as you are busy doing London stuff i'd say give it a try! ive stayed in worse and paid a lot more!

title: Excellent value for money
text: I'm compelled to write this not because it's a particularly fabulous hotel but because I think the other negative reviews on here are unjustified, or at least certainly didn't match my experience. Yes it's basic but for £35 a night in the middle of central London (what I paid for a single studio), I really don't know what more you could want or expect. Easy and friendly check in with the host who offered to direct me around a bit if I needed it. Yes the room was small, nothing more than a bed and a tiny little kitchenette and shower room but again perfectly adequate for a good night sleep. It is a bit noisy as the rooms are not particularly soundproof and you can hear people above or below and in the stairwells. So maybe bring your earplugs but if your happy with simple, basic and good value then this is a great option.

title: Never staying here again!
text: With these apartments being advertised as being discounted heavily by 70% from £140 my expectation was high and I am reviewing this room against the £140 listed price. Expectations were dashed by the initial impressions, After trying for 5 minutes to get through I concluded that the Intercom by the door wasn’t working, no doorbell so after rattling the door I was met by the ‘no speak English’ housekeeper and directed past the 9 lamp hallway chandelier (with only one dim bulb in it) to the ‘Office’ on the second floor to check in. I was allocated room 41 on the 4th floor up numerous flights of narrow steep stairs – luckily I was travelling light as hauling a large suitcase up that lot would have been an unpleasant ordeal. The room was a tiny bedsit with a smelly bathroom and drains that were blocked. I returned down the many flights of stairs and requested another room. Nothing else available and ‘no speak English’ housekeeper was equipped with a plunger to unblock the offensive drains. The smell and the black filth and hair that came out of those drains were awful – but the drains were still blocked. So back to reception to ask for my money back. Miraculously another room was available 52 on the 5th floor – shocked that there was yet another floor here I dragged my luggage up to the 5th floor to a little larger room with a bigger kitchen area and bathroom. From the front door to room 51 was exactly 82 steps. The bed was uncomfortable and the only good things I can say about this place is that it’s not far from the tube, the TV has a good picture and the towels and sheets are clean. I guess this place survives on one night bookings as no one with any standards would ever return to stay here again.

title: Dylan Paddington
text: The staff were friendly and helpful. The room was tight but manageable, and the shower cramped but usable. Overall clean and comfortable and suited our needs. Cooking facilities were adequate and the fridge was adequate.

title: Worst ever
text: Having stayed in a few apartments this I can say is the worse ever. Dirty, cramped and I didn’t feel safe. On arrival the outside looks ok but the first issue was the bell and intercom didn’t work. Eventually someone let us in. We had a choice down or up. By down I didn’t realise they meant the basement. It was dark and I worried that the only way out was back up the stairs we come which where steep. Every door has a fire door sticker on and I knew they where not fire doors. Some rooms had cupboard like doors on them them. Room was small and you couldn’t open door fully as bed behind. I’m only 5 feet and my feet hung off bed. Bathroom dirty with a leak from the skylight causing a stain down the wall. 2 skylights in room both broken with tape over, thank goodness it didn’t rain. Could hear everyone else’s noise and bad night sleep was experienced. Very basic towels that where the size of hand towels. All I can say is you have been warned by the comments and this is one to avoid. My biggest problem with it was I just didn’t feel safe and wouldn’t of got out in a fire !

title: Not the best for the price
text: Upon arriving I checked in at the office, as others have said I wasn't thrilled about the copy of my passport. In addition to this I was asked for £250 in cash to pay for my room. When I asked to pay by card as I was travelling for business, the gentleman on reception pulled a face. I asked if they had a machine and he said yes but that there would be a 5% charge for the priviledge, he showed me some small print but this was not on my online booking. Tired, I agreed to pay, he then asked for a £250 pre authorisation which was fine but I didn't understand why they then needed written details of my credit card. My room was on the floor level with the road which was by and large fine noise wise apart from when someone used the front door I could hear every footstep, breath, conversation etc. The room was clean but worn, you can definitely get better for £125 per night. It put me in mind of a student bedsit, none of the furniture or soft furnishings matches. The shower room was tiny but adequate, towels are very small though! There was a wardrobe, plenty ofplugs, iron, kitchen, tv, DVD and phone. All fine and in working order. Bed was fairly comfy but no duvet just a sheet and a blanket. The best thing going for this 'hotel' is it's location. A five minute walk to Paddington at most, loads of nice restaurants and bars. Overall I wouldn't recommend it though, it's not an apartment, the staff are quite cold and rooms are worn.

title: Excellent, peaceful placce, centraally located
text: We enjoyed our stay at dylan. Especially having kitchens in the apartments is the biggest advantage. Nice clean rooms and looked newly refurbished

title: Shop around the Paddington Area. Heaps of choice. If going low budget, go to the YMCA hotel. Clean and basic, along same road.
text: Booked on Wotif.com I booked a week here, In June and it was last minute, a lot of places were already booked out mid week and I was on a budget after travelling a month. I took this place as there was wifi and a self contained unit. But on arrival no internet, in fact other guests left because of no Internet during the week before. The room as in the basement. WARNING: The walls are VERY thin. I could heard the lady next door eating chips/crips, people coming in the front door and people walking the stairs. The cleaners are not very good either. I def wouldn't be staying again or recommend especially after not receiving multipal important phone calls, and visitors. The guy at 'reception' even wanted to WRITE down my credit card numbers on paper .. Just in case. No machine. Not a good experience :(

title: It was decent
text: Easy to find and in a quiet neighborhood. No elevator and very narrow stairs to the upper floors. The hotel advertised having free wifi for the guests. Yes it was free but only for 1 hour. I was not informed this when I checked in. The room was small and very outdated. The kitchen area in the room was crammed next to the bed and was uncomfortable to use.

title: Not recommended
text: We needed a hotel for the night following a gig in Hyde Park. We didn't want to spend a lot so we had realistic expectations. The rooms are all 'studio' apartments which meant that there was literally no space due to the fact in a tiny room they had put a kitchen!! You couldn't get around the bed and there was barely floor space to stand. There was nowhere to put you bag or clothes so thank goodness we were only there a night. It was a hot day and therefore night so can't imagine how unbearably hot it would have been if you'd used the hob! I couldn't see any ventilation so not sure how safe the whole set up was. Not the cleanest of places either. Shall not be returning and wouldn't recommend. Definitely better options out there for a similar price.

title: small, but decent.
text: Being that I'd never been to London before I was kinda expecting to be staying somewhere tiny, which is what this place was. I'm a pretty tiny person, so this wasn't a big deal for me. Don't think anyone taller than me would've appreciated the shower though. If I were a few inches taller I'd have to duck. Another thing to note about the shower, if you don't catch it at the right time you will have to suffer through a cold shower. A couple of times I ended up boiling some water to wash my head in the kitchen sink with. The floor was a bit grubby. Could've used a good sweep. You'll be able to hear any neighbouring guests. Other than that though, I found it alright. I didn't have to hand over any ID and my payment online was accepted and I wasn't charged for anything extra. It's located close to Lancaster Gate and Paddington tube stations as well as the Paddington National Rail station. Located in a residential area so it's not as noisey as some areas of London. Over all I probably wouldn't stay here again, but he price was ok and the room wasn't terrible.

title: Pure Luxury
text: To say this is the most luxurious hotel in London would be an understatement, to describe the staff would be an undertaker! We arrived into the spacious reception area with its delightful floral display of four faux roses sprinkled with a layer of finely aged dust, and were greeted by the overly friendly cleaner, or she may have been the concierge? She took us to a private check room away from the riffraff where our attentive hotel manager went through the formalities. We couldn't believe the personalised service. We were told to leave our bags there and they would be delivered to our room and we should just head out as the room would be ready on our return from Hyde park. Fast forward to after our festival had finished and we took the short walk back to the hotel and made our way to the very secure hotel room door that matched the number on our state of the art metal device for opening the door, I think it's called a key? I particularly like the way the door handle rotated 360 degrees. On entering the room our jaws hit the floor. It really doesn't get any better. Everything was like you see in the movies. We made our way through the suite to the sleeping area and there they were twin beds with mattress that must have been 10mm think. I immediately jumped on to see if they were those ones the memory springs that remember every way to dig into your spine. I wasn't disappointed. The sheets were beautifully pressed... up against the grey damp patches on the wall, and don't ask me how they manage to maintain map of London art work made of grease on my headboard. A master piece. After testing the bed I decided to peek out of the window. I drew back the curtain and to my surprise it was a set of those really trendy curtains that don't cover the last third of the window and when you pull them open the pole slides out of its bracket. I can't wait for the price to come down so I can get a set for home. I looked out of the window, and I saw a view that every visitor to London wants to see on the postcard they send home... two step ladders covered in pigeon poo, I could have stared for hours! The suite obviously had a kitchen area for the private chef to prepare you a meal. The highlight here was the standard of cleanliness. I only had to swill the sink out a few times before getting a glass of water. Before making our way to the en suite we decided to pop the TV on. You know the normal TV's you get these days are HD or even 4K, well once again the Dylan Suites push the boat out here too. Again forgive my lack of knowledge on these things. This was a Pixel TV I think. The display is a few random squares that don't make up a full picture, maybe you needed those special 3D glasses to watch it. I couldn't find any? The rooms are so big and spacious you'd expect to have to use a glass pushed up against the wall to hear the room next door, not here, crystal clear Dolby surround sound. The ensuite was bespoke fitted arrangement with walk in trickle of water rain head shower. No cheap plastic bottles of shampoo here my friend, but ultra trendy sachets, about the size of samplers that you get on magazines. Far too much for one person to use! Now I know I've raved about this place but there were a few draw backs... so Mr Manger pay attention: The down pipe that was located in our room could have been a little louder every time someone in the building visited the loo - it was way too quiet. And if you could find away to make the beds a bit more wobbly that way whilst perfecting the poise and balance of Russian gymnast as I slide into the land of zed's my core would get an extra little work out before bed. I think that sums everything up. I can't tell you about checking out yet as it's 5am I'm balancing on my bed with a spring in my coxis writing this review watching what I think is breakfast television in pixel form preparing to be knocked off my feet by the power shower listening to the couple next door decide whether to go to Harrods or Selfridges first. I bet before they leave though they'll sneak one last peek at that view! Pure Luxury. 5 Stars!!!

title: Tiny rooms but clean and great location
text: I stayed at Dylan Studios for a 3 day weekend. I found the reception staff very friendly and helpful. I was on the third floor. There are no lifts, so if you have problems with stairs, this is probably not a good place to stay. I had some heavy luggage, but they sent some staff to help me with it. I was in a double room, which was super small, but it had the kitchen and bathroom, was very clean, and was in about the condition I expected. I even had a view over the street behind. So for the cost of the room, for somewhere safe to sleep and leave my gear, I was quite happy. The walls are paper thin, so you can hear people coming and going all the time, but you can't go past the location and it was better than other serviced apartments that I've stayed in the Bayswater area.

title: Shut your eyes and it'll be ok
text: We knew from reviews it wasn't going to be great so were prepared, and given we needed a cheap hotel for the night we thought it would be ok. We were at a concert at Hyde park so it worked for us. Very rough round the edges, marks all up wall, dirty carpets but just walk fast and look forward. Room was right at top up very steep stairs which was fine but after a few drinks can be a little challenging 😀. Room was small, had THE smallest double I've ever come across which was cosy for me and a friend and the shower whilst clean had no hot water. The choice of window opener was some what questionable though? We found it funny but not sure other would? Overall, if you want cheap and well just cheap! Then you'll be fine but I'm sure you can get much nicer for not much more money. Be prepared.

title: Not as bad as it seems after all the reviews
text: Well, for the price we paid (135 for 2 nights) I was OK with this hotel. The rooms were clean, kitchenette was very convinient: kettle, microwave, toaster, fridge - everything you need if on the budget and prefer to have a quick bite at the rooms. Staff was very polite with us and helpful. Yes rooms are tiny, but in London in such a price range I believe it"s common. We booked a twin room, but were allocated, at first, a double one. After noting this out to the staff, they granted us a key from a single room next to ours. So we've got 2 rooms at our disposal. To compare - both were clean and decent. But a single, of course, was much smaller with a really tiny bathroom. Double was fine with toilet far from the sink :) On the negative side the double bed was really small and the walls were really thin, I've got an absolutely annoying neighbours who conducted a night style of life and that disturbed a lot. At the end we are just guests and lets respect each others rights for the night sleep.

title: London City Break
text: These apartments are in a wonderful location and for the price offer a spacious room that is clean and has all that is needed for a short city break. By using the kitchenette it is possible to save money on eating out, but there are plenty of bars, restaurants and attractions near by. The only issue for some travellers may be the stairs, we stayed on the fifth floor and there is no lift. For us, this wasn't a problem and as we only had hand luggage we managed fine but the stairs are rather narrow and fairly steep (I found this adds to the history of the building in the area). The staff in the building were all friendly and helpful.

title: Never again
text: Old, small and dirty rooms. Not acceptable at all. We've paid before the arrival, at the check in they've "checked" the card charging £0.01, simply unacceptable. Cleaning should be done better, duvet was dirty and broken, dust everywhere, hair in the bed, i guess they don't care, there is no other explanation.

title: Got what we expected
text: We were purely looking for a room to sleep in, no more. And that is what we got. Didn't use the shower or the kitchen, but the bed was ok. My partner had no issues sleeping, although I feel the mattress could do with flipping. Don't expect the Ritz, but served our purpose

title: Great location and great staff!!!
text: I love the Paddington/Bayswater area of London. I have never wanted to stay in any other area of London. I have stayed at many flats in the area and I do like Dylan. The check-in, although there is not a easy access to the area, was quick and professional. I would recommend a ringer at the entrance so people have access to the main desk. But other than wondering want to do at the 14 Devonshiire doorway, I waited and within a few minutes other patorns were leaving the establishment. I found the check-in area on the second floor (US perspective)

title: Ruined our weekend away
text: We checked in knowing that the pictures of the apartment's were to an acceptable standard. First of all, I like friendly smiling people at the reception, and if I give that I expect to have it back in return.

title: I was lucky in this hotel
text: Before booking this hotel, I have read the comments on this page. I was very aware of good and not so good things about this accommodation. Thus I had little expectation. Que sera sera-.... However, I was very lucky. I booked a single room, but I was upgraded into a double bed room, with kitchen, telly, toilet and shower. It was not luxury of course, but more than enough, since during my stay, I left quite early in the morning and I came back very late. There was also room service, thus when I came back the room was tidy and clean. It took some time (around 10 minutes) to get the hot water. The receptionists were very professional and kind. I was not disappointed at all. The location is also perfect, close to the paddington train and subway station, and also bus stop. There are some nice pubs and restos around. Hyde Park is within minutes of walk. Surely I will come back to this place again in the future.

title: Very basic accommodation.
text: Very well located apartments only 5 minute walk from Paddington station. Very friendly staff, check in desk open until 10pm (however late check in fee applies beyond 10pm -£50 til midnight, £99 after midnight). Very basic room, strong smelling air freshener didn't manage to mask the strong smell of damp, worst in the bathroom. No complimentary tea and coffee available which would have been a nice touch. Minimal kitchen utensils, toaster and kettle provided. Hair dryer and iron can be requested from the front desk. Although a cheap option I don't think I would return here.

title: I wish I had read earlier review
text: I have only discovered the earlier review when I came onto the site to register my own dissatisfaction. I had exactly the same experience as Owen. The room was advertised as a studio - it consisted of a double bed with about 1 foot either side, a sink unit, two rings and a white plastic desk. The walls were grubby as was the floor. The shower room was tiny with no room between the toilet and the tiny shower and could only be used with the door open. The public areas of the apartments were filthy with stained carpets, dirty walls and dirty towels on the floor. I was unable to bring myself to stay and left. The young man on duty was polite but very anxious what his employers would do when I would not let him photocopy my ID.

title: Great location, but that is all.
text: I stayed here just for one night whilst visiting London with family. It is obviously reasonably priced for a night in London which is good. The location is brilliant and you can walk most places from here. However the accommodation does need a little bit of love and decorating. I personally would not stay here again and just pay a bit more to stay somewhere a little nicer.

title: ONE NIGHT STOPOVER
text: Booked this place for its close proximty to Paddington Station and the price. Based on that it was first class. Complimenting this was the friendly lady on reception was extremely helpful, even rang me when I left to say my glasses had been found. On the down side, the rooms are small and I mean SMALL. The decor could do with a lick of paint and the carpets on the stairs and good clean. The reality check for guests is that you cannot have champagne on beer money. This place is cheap as chips for London, if you do not like what you get for the price go and stay 300 yards in the Hilton for Double what you will pay here.

title: this place is terrible
text: this hotel is falling to bits, everything is not what it seems, dont believe there website, it all looks so glam, but its completely the reverse, the rooms are so small and the furniture is almost on top of you there no room to even swing a cat, the staff are no where to be seen, and if you do manage to find somebody to talk to, it will be like they are doing you a favour by letting you stay there. The owner hasnt got a clue how to deal with guests and there problems, and doesnt want admit that his hotel has problems, with staff, and management. The Hotel is mis managed and the owners havent got a clue on how to run a hotel. Its not up to scratch, find some where else if you can!!! As you can tell i wont be going back there.....
subratings_json: {"cleanliness": 2.0, "rooms": 1.0, "service": 1.0, "check in / front desk": 1.0, "value": 1.0, "location": 2.0, "business service (e.g., internet access)": 1.0}

title: Amazing!!!!
text: My best friend and i stayed here for 2 night when first arriving to london. They were absolutely amazing! They let us store our luggage and freshen up before check in. The room was small but very awesome especially for the price! The reception lady valentina was absolutely fantastic! She helped us find the cheapest route to our next destination and also helped us confirm our birthday celebrations for my best Friend! Made our first few days amazing and comfortable! Plus GREAT location!!

title: Not luxurious but clean
text: We booked a room ensuite with open kitchen and it was not bad at all. We had read some bad reviews of this hotel, but our room was quite nice and confortable. It had Sky TV and a DVD player, and all the kitchenware. The location is excellent, ten minutes away from Paddington Station, and it has a very good prize. The worse was the man of the staff..

title: Take earplugs & tea bags!
