title: Very small bathroom
text: I was on business trip in London from 11 till 14th of September 2013. While reserving a hotel I was looking for one that was close to my meeting place. Location was good as well in terms of reaching airport from Paddington station (5-minute walk from the hotel). The hotel itself from outside and reception was good enough for me to choose it. Moreover in comparison with what I had at the time of reserving the price (GBP 161 per night excluding VAT) was reasonable. In arriving, reception did not keep me waiting and I was registered within 2-3 minutes. Now I will talk about conditions. It was my first bad experience in hotel. I was very surprised to see very narrow corridors, very old refurbishment, very narrow path to the bed in the room, very small bathroom and finally slow lift (it takes a minute to get 5th floor from Ground floor). I was shocked in the first morning when I switched the light on and saw a black beetle near my bed. I told about this to the reception and do not know if they did anything to this. The bathroom as I mentioned above was too small. In order to sit on lavatory pan, I had to sit sideways just not to hit my head on washstand. It was not comfortable to wash hand and face because of small washstand. The shower cabin was small too. In my next trip to London I will not stay at Westpoint certainly.

title: Great Location, Cheap but in Need of some TLC
text: We paid a £100 for a twin room so £50 each for a night in Central London, this seems reasonable. Great Location, a 15 min walk to Oxford Street, 5 min walk to Kensington Gardens / Park and Hyde Park, also only a 2 min walk from Paddington Tube Station. We arrived into Kings Cross and got the Brown Bakerloo line Northbound to Paddington, came out of the Station walked across the road and down London Street and the hotel was on the corner of that and Sussex Gardens. However the hotel itself is not the best, shabby carpets, Very Small rooms with a peculiar layout in our twin room, no bar or eatery onsite. I guess as expected for the price.

title: Stay away
text: This place has delusions of grandeur. The reception area looks lovely and when you walk in you would think that the rooms would be lovely too but I have never stayed in someone this bad before (and I have been to many countries!) The staff weren't that friendly and when we walked into the bedroom I literally wanted to walk back out again. If it wasn't for us arriving so late at night I would have left. The carpet was full of cigarette burns and many other stains, the bed was so uncomfortable and only had tiny pillows. The sheets on the duvet were turned inside out (I don't even want to guess why!) and the rest of the room wasn't much better. I ended ur sleeping in my clothes as the place felt so dirty. The toilet paper in the bathroom was covered in mould so completely unusable. I would recommend that everyone stay clear of this place

title: Grand as a base to explore London
text: This hotel was perfect for what we needed it for, somewhere to lie down at night. Rooms where quite small with a TV and tea making facilities. Staff where lovely and went out of their way to check us in early. Parts of the hotel where very outdated but I would stay here again.

title: Good value and great location
text: The hotel is located just one block from Paddington and few minutes walk to Kensington Gardens and Hyde Park. You cannot get better location than that especially if arriving by train at Paddington. Our room was small as it is usual the case for most of the hotels along Sussex Gardens but suited us nicely. The toilet/shower room was also small but everything was very clean. The beds were adequate but the pillows a bit on the hard side. Breakfast was exactly the same for the three days we stayed at the hotel and you get tired of it after day 2. It is buffet style and they provide two types of cereal, tin fruit salad, some dry fruit, apple and orange juice, cheese and ham, scrambled eggs, sausage and baked beans, toast (white and brown), butter and one type of jam. They could at least try to vary the breakfast options in consecutive days ( I guess it doesn't take much to change the sausage for bacon every other day or add a different type of bread. Staff in reception were friendly and efficient. The hotel has one computer that guests can use free of charge (don't know if they have wireless). Compared to other hotels nearby, this was adequate and good value. I would stay there again.

title: For the price, great and really handy to everything you need
text: We booked this hotel via the hotel internet site and received a great advance purchase price. The apartment (2 bedroom) was small but expected, being London. Older style but clean with a kitchenette and good bathroom. Each room had heavy doors which shut automaticaly which was a pain, but we propped them open with suitcases which worked. So close to underground, restaurants and shops. The 'Hop off/Hop Off" Bus picks up from the next street. The staff was great, always willing to help. Breakfast was good and included in price. We wanted a budget hotel for our family holiday as we knew we were going to be out all day and late return at night - we would rather spend our money on enjoying ourselves. Recommend this hotel if you are looking for same.

title: Location, location, location!
text: Location is a major plus with plenty of halal food in the area. Easily accessible to Hyde park and Oxford st especially when there was no transport on xmas day. Staff was fantastic as well. What I was really not happy about was staff don't respond to emails. Should look into that side of customer service.

title: Better than expected
text: I was a little nervous from the mixture of comments on here but I just returned from a week's stay at Westpoint and thoroughly enjoyed it. Was in a single room and YES, they are small, as they are all over Europe, but it was clean and passed my "3 check" test......decent toilet paper, thick/fluffy towels & cleanliness. It scored high on all 3. The staff were very friendly & it is in a great location. Would definitely stay there again

title: Average hotel - Great location
text: The location of the Westpoint Hotel. Close to Kensington, Oxford Street and more. Good restaurants and a bakery near by - Big Bus tour stop right beside the hotel. The hotel itself is not bad, but not good either. The free "wi-fi" is ridiculously bad, the phone in the lobby didn't work - the same can be said about the computers at the hotel. The staff was ok. In the lobby there was a man who was selling Big Bus Tours - extremely unhelpful. Be aware that you cannot buy the orientation tour which is the cheapest one - he only sells the more expensive tours. I recommend you just go online and purchase your tickets. Stay at this hotel if you are out all day long and only need a place to sleep.

title: Location, location, location
text: This hotel is conveniently located within easy walking distance of Paddington Station. The hotel is close to the park, and there are many restaurants in the neighbourhood. Finding affordable accommodation in this part of the world is no easy task. This hotel does a good enough job. A map and compass or GPS is required to find your room from reception. The rooms are not massive as you'd expect at the prices being paid per square metre here. The rooms are however relatively fresh, very clean, and tidy. The shelving unit in my room had some minor low quality maintenance/repair work done to it and really that was the only fault I could find in this 3 star hotel. Very clean bathroom staff who like a laugh and a joke. Good hotel.

title: Not bad for the price if staying short-term
text: I stayed here in October 2011 for one night on a quick visit to London for a football match. We were looking for something reasonably priced with parking and access to the tube system. The hotel gives a good first impression with a nice lobby and friendly front desk staff. There is limited (fee) parking just outside the door and spaces are a bit tight but we managed okay. Once past the front desk it seems that your experience might depend on the room you get. There were 4 of us and we had a lower basement room that was probably the most cramped room you could get outside of Manhattan. The beds were extremely tight and the bathroom the smallest imaginable. That being said, as we hadn't intended spending much time in our room and those travelling with me were family it wasn't the biggest issue for me and it served its purpose. It did however mean that the room was very warm and I'd imagine that it could get very hot in mid-summer. This is no doubt a function of the age of the building but a room on a higher floor might get a bit more space. Accessing the room was also a bit awkward with a lift that seemed to take for ever to arrive. The room was clean although there wasn'y much floor space to vacuum. Breakfast was surprisingly good and very popular. This hotel is very conveniently located for the underground with Paddington Station just around the corner. The hotel was also located just outside the congestion charge zone which was another reason for its selection as we were driving to it from Wales. Indeed the area is very accessible from the M1 as its almost a straight road into the area from the motorway network. The immediate area is quite pleasant although we didn't get a chance to frequent any of the bars or restaurants All in all, a reasonable proposition if you are not fussy about space and require convenient access to the tube.

title: Good location and clean, but little else
text: This was our first rip to London and we needed two rooms to accommodate two adults and three teenage boys. The Westpoint had two rooms that would seem to work. The hotel seemed to be in a good location, just a short walk to Paddington Station. And the price was decent. The location was good and the rooms were clean. The staff was also very nice. Unfortunately, this was not enough to overcome the negatives. We knew the rooms were going to be small, but they are tiny. The bed fits in the room and that is about it. If you have more than a small overnight bag it is difficult to fit both you and your luggage in the room at the same time. Our room was so small that my wife hit her cheek on the small night table that hung over the corner of the bed. Yes, hung over the corner of the bed, because the bed was about 6 in. off the ground. The bathroom was ridiculously small

title: Average
text: nice enough hotel best point was its location 2 mins walk from paddington station. rooms fairly small. staff were nice and restuarant for breakfast was ok even though the menu was fairly limited. Old style town house with sash windows looks very nice and sits on a residential street which is fairly quiet even though it is close to Paddington rail station. Easy to access all sites from this hotel.

title: Excellent Location
text: This hotel was perfect for the location super easy to get to from the underground, We struggled to find the hotel as we drove past it about 5xs untill we asked someone lol small mistake but the hotel is called a different name to what we booked it. Very small dated bedrooms but it is expected in London, But not as small as i excpected i even bashed my head on the shelf. Breakfast in minimum. But overall good stay with no other hassle.

title: Could be better!
text: We didn't expect the height of luxury for the price we paid, just needed somewhere clean and comfy. The room we were initially given was awful. back of the hotel, tiny and the miniscule bathroom smelled of cats. We asked for another room and were given one right away. Much better, brighter overlooking the street on the 4th floor. Adequate for a two night stay although the electrics need seeing to. Main light kept going on and off, bedside lights didn't work, telly appeared to look like negative photos but hey ho we only slept in the room. It was clean the bathroom was again tiny but clean. What we expected due to it being an old building and reading reviews. Although we went in July we were glad the weather wasn't hot. The room was very warm and stuffy considering the weather which was quite cool. The location is what appealed to us really good for getting in and around central London, lots of bars and restaurants just around the corner. Staff were brilliant friendly and helpful. Breakfast good for £5.00 - continental - pastries, cereal, yogurt, ham cheese and ok coffee.

title: Great Location
text: I was a bit apprehensive about staying in this hotel as we usually stick to the well known chains. However, the location was perfect and the price was great so we gave it a go. The hotel looks amazing from the outside. Check in was very quick and easy. The desk staff were very friendly. We had a triple room which was a fair size. The third bed was a proper bed and not a sofa bed of pull out. The bathroom was small, but adequate. It was very clean. The hotel staff were happy to look after our baggage on check out day which is a saviour if you're travelling from Paddington. It's only a 2 minute walk. Overall...great location, friendly staff and clean.

title: Clean small budget hotel well siruated for visit London
text: We booked triple room for 3 nights. The room was small but very clean. Towells.change every day. Breakfast good enough especially the eggs. Good situation 2 min walk to Padington station and Hyde park. Walking distance to Notinghill portobello market. Direct bus to Oxford circus and lot more seesights even at night

title: quite hard to judge this hotel
text: This hotel has a great location, it is located quite close to anything, be it the hyde park or oxford street. It is situated aproximately 200m from Paddington tube station, so public transportation is really reachable easily. The main lobby with its statues and a fountaine is trying to impress people entering the hotel, however, creating TERRIBLY wrong expecations about the rest of the hotel's premises. The rooms are very very small. i undertand this is a listed building, however, it was almost impossible to moe around in our room. There was actually space just for one(a very small one) wardrobe in a double room. Next thing that really struck me was the fact that they have just one key per room. In reality this meant that my friend woke me up every night coming from the town latee than I did, not being able to open the door himself. How is this possible? Have you ever heard of programmable entry cards, dear Hotel? The breakast was very plain and static, I tended to go outside to grab something, however, I understand this is normal given the price level. The staff was quie friendly, and also the cleaning lady did her job very thoroughly despite of the fact that the bathroom needed really some refurbishment and I'm thankful for that. All in all, it's quite hard to judge this hotel overall, I guess I am not to come back again to this hotel. Not because I would be entirely disappointed but because I realized I will dedicate more money for accommadation next timeI visit London to get a bit higher standard (especially the room size). thank you.

title: very good for a short stay
text: Location is brilliant 2 mins walk from Paddington underground and national rail station. The street that leads to the station is full of restaurants and coffee shops. The hotel itself is clean although the layout is a little confusing, but i guess they had is extended a lot. i got a room at the first floor and not at all sure if i would have been as happy with one on the ground floor (with reception and restaurant) or the basement floor. The desk is staffed 24/7 and that was good as i got in at 1 am after a flight delay. They also make sure you know to register for breakfast and that you can get a taxi to the airport. There's a tickets stand (concierge?) but i didn't use it. The room itself: the keys are very old school so was never sure if i locked properly, when getting in the bed (room 415) is about 20 from the door so a little difficult to enter but inside there's loads of room. the room has a beautiful tall window to the street but it is not very well sealed and in fact was left open once and there for was cold. The radiator is between the bed and the wall so heats up just that little part of the room. there's tea and coffee things but the kettle can be plugged ONLY next to the other side of the bed and not where it's placed, which is on a tiny shelf under the mirror (really! a little wider shelf and a socket would have done wonders here.) there are shelves for hanging clothes or laying them and that helps a lot to not feel cramped, The bathroom is nice and clean but the are no hooks or shelves in any convincing location. (one above the toilet far from the sink) and no place to put the toiletries even on the sink itself. The toilet handle keeps jamming up and flushing till you push it down and there are noises for other rooms but the door can be closed to stop the noise a little. There were hot waters but the taps in the sink are separated for hot and cold so had to fill the sink to wash my face with lukewarm waters. the TV works fine but had to struggle with remote to turn off. internet is free for 2 hours then you need to pay and there are two computers at the lobby. breakfast was not worth the price. was nice and tasty but for 7/9 pounds (depending if you preregister or not) it's way too much for such a little selection. specially when the street is full of coffee shops. stayed 3 nights in October and would come again but not for a long stay.

title: Rubbish breakfast, rude staff
text: Would have given this a 3 star as the room wasn't amazing, but generally clean and ok for one night. However, the breakfast staff were awful. I was told I didn't have breakfast included and needed to go to reception. Showed them my receipt which proved otherwise and the woman still didn't believe me and had to call her colleague over. Despite their mistake, no attempt was made at an apology. We then had to sit in specific seats and the breakfast was just really really rubbish. As we were sitting down we could hear another colleague interrogating another guest about her lack of receipt showing she had paid for breakfast! Perhaps the hotel should carry the correct breakfast list, even for those who have made non refundable reservations. £10 a head got us watered down juice and defrosted, soggy pastries, bread rolls or cereal. Only good thing about this place is the location.

title: Worst Hotel Experience of My Life
text: Booked this hotel 5 months in advance and the rooms they gave us felt like musty dungeons. No air circulation, the towels were threadbare and they didn't even provide shampoo. Stay far away from this establishment.

title: Total rip off
text: When looking for a hotel near Hyde Park chose this one as it specifically states they had parking, had eight spaces so we had to dump our luggage and go trawling around for parking. Twin room was hot, very small and not at all comfortable.

title: Phil Collins concert
text: Arrived here Friday after not being able to get in the hotel we had originally booked, quite impressive from outside, reception helpful after them saying they could not find our booking, small room 437 and very very hot,told at breakfast we were not entitled which we were and the staff were quite snotty and said they were going to confirm with reception told them to go ahead, now we are fortunate to travel a lot and it is not very often you come across this negativity, but the man on reception was very nice and a credit to the jhotel booked us a taxi back to the station, but the restaurant staff need replacing with some smiley people.

title: Just awful
text: Booked this hotel as was close to Paddington and Hyde Park. Booked and paid for room over 6 months ago, checked in online prior to arrival. Arrived at hotel at noon prior to gig and were assured we could get room key at any time. Arrived after gig and we were allocated room 402b. £167 for one double room, one night. The room was in a basement, no air conditioning or ventilation. Window opened out onto a corridor or room. Electrics were very unsafe. Trip hazard going into bathroom. Shower was lined in lead flashing. Bed was uncomfortable and noisy. Was worse night sleep I have ever had. Worst hotel I have ever stayed in. Don't be fooled. Foyer is all crystal chandeliers and gilded mirrors. Rest of place is a dump. Stays in many hotels in London, and Paddington. This was the most expensive and the worst. Better off staying else where and paying for tube travel..

title: Superb location, value for money
text: Note that due to recent terror attack incidents in London, the hotel says that they are advised not to store luggage. Plan your time wisely, otherwise, you can store luggage at train station with a fee. We stayed 2 nights in triple room without breakfast. The hotel is value for money, just what you need, for shower and a night of sleep. Given that it is London, you get what you paid for, a place to rest and to sleep, nothing more. The location is wonderful, 5 minutes walk to Paddington Station for railway as well as underground. At the station itself there are mini marts like Sainsbury, WH Smith, M&S, Boots, where you can buy essentials like water. The streets nearby has several option of food, from fast food to fine dining. There are also cafes nearby as well as at the train station. There is no AC in the rooms, so it might be a little hot during summer. There is no mini bar, so don't purchase anything that need to be refrigerated. If you have big luggage and can't be bothered dragging around, you can pay to take Heathrow Express. If you have smaller luggage, you can just take the Underground Picadilly line. With the underground, you can just buy a day ticket then the ticket can be used to explore London for the rest of the day with unlimited rides.

title: basement room
text: i have been here 3 days ago wit my two friend and we booked triple room. We came to the hotel at about 4. a.m morning. Building and lobby are very nice, night receptionist was very nice and gave to us our key. Our room was on downstairs with view to laundry and front of the window was wall. One day was there a man who made horrible sound under our window. Our window was possible open only 30cm up! This room was very small and furniture was so old. This room wasnt from 3stairs hotel!!!Our shower was so small and shower flood was very low. When we wanted made a shower it stayes very long so we called to reception and we wanted change a room but recetionist said we must wait till the morning. Ok. In th emorning we came to the reception and other receptionist said it is problem and its possible stay our luggage in luggage room and they try to solve this problem. But we need a shower and she gave us other room and said we can to use this shower.It was horrible, because this shower wass worse like first. So at about 20 minutes came technic man and repair the shower. It was horrible night/morning. Breakfast was very poor. But this hotel has a very good location near the paddington and HYde PArk. Thats all

title: Great value
text: Excellent hotel for price staff very friendly and helpful. Great location rooms very clean. Easy to find from underground we went with a mixed group of friends and family all where happy. Good restaurants close by would visit again and would highly recommend

title: A nicely located hotel with welcoming staff and small, but comfortable rooms.
text: The location of the hotel is absolutely great, even may be called perfect if you are in London for leisure and shopping. It is only 5 minutes walk from Hyde Park, just 2 minutes walk from Paddington Station and (in case you like walking) 10-15 minutes (it depends on your speed) walk from Marble Arch and then Oxford Street. The rooms are not very large, but comfortable. The apartments are quite big and very cosy. They have enough space for a family of 4 with two teenages. Breakfast is included in their room rates. It is rather substantial. The staff are great, friendly, wellcoming and helpful. Moreover, They are multilingual. They speek Spanish, Italian, and even Russian!!!! I would not hesitate to recommend WestPoint Hotel to anyone. Our family stay here every our visit to London and when we come next time, we will stay there again.

title: Frustraiting
text: The worst hotel I have ever stayed. Unreasonable pricing for very poor accomodation. Room with price of 89£ is smaller than Harry Potter's room under the ladder. Staff was polite and helpful during cheking in, but very rude when I have tried to check out. I have requested a late check out, but the hotel refused to meet this condition and did not tell about it in the first place! After that they've charged me double price! Ridiculous!

title: Tried to book for 6 months....it's going from bad to worse.
text: Over the weekend I have tried to book 3-4 night periods of stay for the next 6 months whilst I am based in London. You would think that they would be pleased for the business. However, after booking the initial month I received cancellation notices without a reason why. I called the hotel and was told the card has been refused and therefore the bookings had been cancelled and that we should check with our card provider as it was 'wasting your time and ours!'. We contacted our card provider to be told that £380 had been debited to the card and provided us with the transaction ID. We contacted the Hotel only to be told that 'yes' this booking had been confirmed. I have tried now on 3 ocassions to contact the hotel only to be told that the General Manager is now not available and this morning remains unavailable until 10am. I have never had to complain about a hotel in London but this beggars belief. Proceed with caution, if it goes wrong, it goes very wrong !!!! and we haven't even stayed yet.

title: Two Night Stay
text: Fantastic location for our purposes, Radio 2 Hyde Park picnic in the park concert. Great looking hotel, nearly all staff we met were really helpful, apart from one receptionist, I think possible manger, really couldn't be bothered! We were given a box room, maybe smaller, sure it was used as a shoe box previously, pathetic accommodation. Though I had read many previous reviews advising similar I thought they were joking, sadly very accurate 😱 due to the rooms being tiny and no AC the rooms were red hot, so we opened the window, which then restricted access to the bed as it opened wide into the room, no restrictor on it!! Then the smell of cigarettes from outside the back of the hotel drifted in. Had the room been of sensible proportions I would rated it a possible 4, seriously Westpoint you really need to listen and take notice of the reviews other wise it's pointless leaving feed back?

title: Poor customer atention
text: I stayed at this hotel on my last vacation and only when I got home I realized that I had been charged twice for our stay. I called the hotel and the person who got the call made me wait forever to listen to my complain. She simply told me to send an e-mail explaining what happened. I did so but I never got an answer back, not to mention my Money! I strongly do not recommend this hotel for the lack of attention to the customer and I don't intend to return.

title: Nothing to get excited about!!
text: The big plus of the hotel is that it is near Paddington Station. The negatives are that the rooms are very small, the staff is unfriendly, there is no air-conditioning in the rooms, the wifi is very expensive and it is very noise. It is one of those hotels that you have ticked of and will not make a booking again.

title: Not stay again
text: It's too old, elevator is too old, rooms are very old furnished, bathroom sink too bad, bed is comfortable enough but not clean. There was some dirts in the bed:((( Location is great but hotel is very very old. There are many hotels around, next time i will try another one. For example, Room key is still not digital not key as a electronic card. They are giving very old type of key which is impossible to carry in your pocket.

title: Good location in Paddington
text: Great location. So many restaurants in the area. 2 blocks away from Paddington Station. We are a family of 8 from the Philippines and got 2 Family Rooms located at Basement 1 (4 people per room). Their rooms were not bad but there was no AC and if we opened our windows it was easily accessible from the outside. We were not comfortable opening our windows.

title: Good Experience
text: Was slightly apprehensive booking this hotel after reading some of the reviews but we knew the location was good and could not complain for the price so we went with it. On arrival I was pleasantly surprised. Speedy check in process and the reception staff were pleasant. We were given the Wi-Fi code and instructions on how to get to our room. For what we paid the room was great

title: Just a Bed
text: If you just need a bed to sleep on this is the place, good bed and a tiny bathroom. Service minded and friendly. Walking distance too Paddington station and also near to restaurants and bars. The hotel have a nice frontage

title: Very very very small rooms
text: The hotel is a few steps from Paddington Station, so location is very good. The lobby is nice and the staff very friendly and kind! The room is very very very small, too small! Even the bed is not long enough for a person with heigh 180cm, so no very comfortable. By the way the hotel is clean, very well located, services works well and the price is very good!!

title: Good hotel
text: I stayed here for 6 days in a single room. Room was very small but didn't spend much time in hotel anyway so it was fine because I really just needed a bed to sleep in. This hotel is situated very close to Paddington station so it was very convenient when I needed to take the Heathrow Express. Staff were very friendly but I was disappointed by their lack of communication prior to my stay. I sent a number of emails and I didn't receive any reply. Bed was comfortable and room was very clean. Breakfast was very nice but unfortunately cost 8 pounds.The shower was average and I thought overall the hotel was overpriced for what I got but I paid for location mainly.

title: No air conditioning is a deal breaker
text: After having stayed in a pension and hostal in Spain, then a small budget hotel in Paris, we arrived at the Westpoint Hotel in London. After finding out that the wi fi would cost me around 30£, we arrived in our small room. With the temperature in London climbing to the high 80s, the heat inside was unbearable. Even when the temperature at night dipped into the 60s, our room stayed extremely hot! Even with the window open (and we were in room 17, near the ground, exposing ourselves to someone entering our room) and the door to the hall propped open, there was NO AIR MOVEMENT! The sink in the bathroom was so small that you had to turn your head sideways to spit into it. We were miserable there. I would not stay again!

title: Excellent London Hotel
text: We stayed at the Westpoint hotel last week for 3 nights while I competed in the Triathlon world championships in Hyde park. It was probably the best location we could have asked for. We had to drive there, but parking was easy right outside hotel and reasonably priced. Easy stroll to park. Stayed in a suite with our 14 month old daughter. Excellent size room, with sofa and good space for a cot (all ready set up when we arrived), and we were surprised to find a separate kitchen area as part of our room, which came in very handy for us. Staff were always very friendly. Good access to wifi in room. Altogether helped to make a brilliant weekend

title: Good location
text: Good location as a base for sightseeing in central London. We stayed in a family room, which despite reviews about the size of rooms at this property, was not too bad due to facilities provided to store luggage. Room was clean, however uncomfortably warm at night although the window was wide open (room was not on the street side of hotel). Reception provided us with a small fan but it did not make too much difference.

title: Very pleasant stay. Thank you
text: Room 54, 17 - 19 jan. Me and my friend stayed in west point hotel for weekend. Apon arrival was quick from paddingtion stn as stated. At night the lights outside were beautiful to see and sets the expectation before we entered. Quick check in, which was lovely, when we entered the room everything was clean, tidy, and well presented. As a joke we checked for mould and dust and found none. So the morning breakfast, buffet style breakfast. Loved it as I could go up seconds if needed. Upon arrival to the breakfast area we were greeted with a good morning from friendly team which makes a diffrence. After demolishing breakfast we did our thing, sight seeing and other fun stuff. So we headed back to hotel and to our suprise the room was clean and tidy and smelling lovely. With all the good news spoken about there was only ONE thing. The bathroom we had was very... narrow. Im kind of a built guy and the space was lets say constricting for the toilet activities. As it was our first time here I didnt really think we should complain. But that did not interrupt our amazing weekend at your hotel. So thank you for your service and will be recommending you to friends. From a happy customer glyn.

title: Just an overnighter
text: Westpoint hotel Sussex Gardens London is convenient to Paddington station when planning to go to Heathrow. The area is pleasant and the hotel foyer is very nice. There is also a luggage storage room. The lift was out of order in September and looked like there was no plan to fix it. The stairs were steep, the floor higgedly piggledy, rooms were squeezy and hadn't been refurbished since the fifties. Very grimy curtains and windows stuck tight half open. The sort of place you wouldn't want to stay in long, if at all. I think places like this should be called out

title: Lot smaller than pictures make out. Ok just to crash overnight
text: First impressions seemed really good. Staff helpful and check in went smoothly. Lift sounded like it was going to give up so we used the stairs the rest of the stay. Once at our room was so surprised over the size. I've never seen a room so small. You literally walk straight in and your hit with the bed and just enough walk room each size..that's it. Walls very thin so could here whenever anyone was in room next door or walking along corridors which wasn't the best at 3am when we were woken up. Luckily we only used it as a place to crash. We off loaded our bags and headed straight to winter wonderland and werent back until gone 10pm and left by half 9 following morning. It wasn't the best sleep though as people being noisy in middle of night, it did feel like we in the corridor with them that's how loud it was and the blind wasn't best at keeping light out also the duvet was so so thin not ideal for winter. We booked via booking.com under the policy of free cancellation. Only downside is they look the money at time of booking instead of when we arrived like all other hotels we have booked have done. Personally wouldn't go back, lot nicer places out there and better for comfort.

title: Ok rooms. Not good service
text: Lift not working upon arrival. Not fixed over the weekend. We had 2 tripplerooms. One was of good standard. One seemed old and dirty. The staff was not at all welcoming. Upon breakfast we felt to be a problem as the normal tables were full. The hostess made us seem unwanted as she had to set table in other part of restaurant. Upon leaving we were told to use baggagestorage. When we went to retrieve luggage the room was full and we could not open door. Resepsionist was very rude and not helpful and we had a severe delay to get our flight because of this.

title: Friendly hotel, value and adequate
text: Needed a low cost hotel for one night and the Westpoint was chosen off the web on price and location. As for the latter, it's 5 mins walk from Paddington station and round the corner from shops, restaurants etc. Friendly and efficient service from the staff at check in and at breakfast. They all seemed attentive and helpful. Hotel itself is a warren of corridors and clearly not at the level of £100plus per night ones. The bedroom was small, but clean. My gripe was with the tv, set high on a bracket with no remote! Breakfast ok too and if you go there and don't want to spend too long in your room lounging about it's fine.

title: Thieves
text: Booked a room through Booking.com. Money instantly taken from card although fully refundable/cancellable up to a day before arrival. I cancelled 2 months before arriving. Money not refunded. Contacted booking.com after 3 weeks and got email saying refund will be done the following day by manager. A week later Booking.com emailed saying hotel is refusing to refund so it will take more time as it is clearly refundable and cancellable. I know I will get my money back as Booking.com assured me I would, but shocking how you do not honour terms and conditions.

title: Nice location small rooms
text: Hotel is fine, it is very clean, staff were friendly. Price at London standards was pretty good. The rooms were a bit small but well appointed. The only issue was the heat the room was like a sauna, we asked for a fan which was given to us. Especially in summer maybe fans should come as standard.

title: Clean but compact - shame about breakfast and cust service
text: We stayed here for one night in Mid August. We arrive at 5pm and i wouldnt say we were welcomed exactly. We were told breakfast was until 9.30am which we thought was early for a weekend (and it turned out to be until 10am). The room and bathroom were both clean so no complaints there. The room was small as was the shower room but it was fine for one night. The TV and fridge both worked but the hairdryer gave up after a few mins. The bed was clean and comfortable but the room was hot and there was no air circulating. We did leave the window open and the 'view' was the back of some dodgy looking flats and then looking down onto the dumping area for the hotel - old beds and TV's etc. Breakfast was in a tiny room in the basement that at 9am was very busy (presumably because we had all been told it finished at 9.30!) We had to share a table with other guests which was ok but not really what i expected. A basket of toast and tea was provided and then cereal or ham and cheese or yoghurt was available. No offer of more toast either. Clean and does what it says on the tin but a bit basic is a good summary

title: Arriva Hotel London
text: The best attraction for the hotel is its' location 5 minutes walk from Kings Cross Station. We were using it as a stop over before taking Eurostar to Paris the next morning and made this a convienient hotel to book. The hotel is pretty basic with small rooms which needed a bit of touching up and a a bit of money spent on it. The continental breakfast the next morning was in a small room which had to cope with too many guests so waiting for a table was the norm and again faIrly basic fare. It does what it says on the tin but not much more.

title: If there's no other choice
text: If you have no other choice than taking this hotel, then it's fine....but it is not very good. Firstly when you enter the hotel you are confronted with a step, so forget about wheelchair access, and a door that is awkward to open when you're dragging a suitcase, however it is a old property. Check in was ok, but asking me to leave the key to my room at reception on the way out is not something that I am prepared to do. The room was pretty dated, the wall colour is not the best and the bed is passable. The room needed a good clean and a redecoration as there were scuff marks all along the skirting board. There was more of a set of shelves than a wardrobe. There is a desk in the room, but it is not very big. The bathroom was ok, but a very small low sink. One major issue with the room was ventilation, you could open the window to air it, but when I had a shower there was no-where for the steam to dissipate making the room pretty hot. WiFi is very hit an miss, they obviously do not have enough bandwidth for the entire hotel as on a night it will grind to a holt which is really annoying when you have documents that you need to access online. Breakfast was pretty dire, a few slices of bread, I think it was meant to be deli meat and some cereal. I tried it and it just was the cheapest quality produce that they could find and the taste was pretty bad, so that was a waste. Another strange thing was a sign in the breakfast room saying please do not use your phones as it makes other guests uncomfortable at breakfast: that is a new sign for me! Checkout was: 'yeh thats ok'. Not the best of ways to say goodbye. A note to point you can store your luggage in the hotel at your own risk in an unlocked room for 2.50 which is not the best. Overall, its a good hotel if you need somewhere to sleep at night. I think that there were much better options in the area.

title: Ms
text: Noisy and loud. The night staff were extremely unhelpful when many hotel guests, including me, complained that they were being kept awake by other noisy guests. The night staff confirmed that it is acceptable to have multiple people staying in a double room who are clearly bot registered to that room.

title: Good value for price
text: Stayed here on the Saturday night of the bank holiday weekend. Good central location for a night out in central London. Basic accommodation exactly what was expected for the price paid....room and bedding was nice and clean and slept like a log. Bonus, turned up at 1030 in the morning and was allowed to check straight in and get out on the town.

title: DO NOT STAY HERE
text: Unbelievably bad. The hotel is very basic, and very noisy as the walls and floors are paper thin. The manager/receptionist was incredibly rude and ignorant when we complained about builders working in the room above in the morning. You've been warned. Find another hotel.

title: Good for a short stay
text: This hotel was in the a really perfect location for where I was spending a few days at work. It was clean enough, the reception staff was friendly. It's not brand new or modern but it works. Price was ok for London but that also means you can't have super luxury. I got a really large room, shower had good water pressure. In short, everything I needed at an ok price. I'd go back.

title: Not as bad as some say
text: Is it the ritz? no of course not. Was it cheap and clean? yes. We only stayed one night as we had to catch the eurostar the next morning. Its literally around the corner from the train station so very convenient. All the staff were friendly and approachable and checking in was straight-forward. The room was small but clean and had tea/coffee/kettle, tv, hairdryer and toiletries in the bathroom. It was warm and the bed was comfy enough. Breakfast was good. Continental, with a ham and cheese, fruit, yoghurt, toast and cereal on offer. This isn't a bad place to get your head down for a night, and for the money i'd stay again.

title: Disappointed, would not recommend it!
text: We chose the Arriva Hotel as it is near Kings Cross and the reviews were mostly positive. We had a twin room which was extremely small and basic which is what we expected from the reviews and it was ready for us on our arrival. The room was dirty, there was grit/soil on the carpet which was only evident (due to the colour and stains on the carpet) when you stepped on it in bare feet! Our room was hot and stuffy even with the window open, the fan did not work! The main light didn't work either. The en suite facilities were shoddy and dirty. It was difficult to manoeuvre the door due to the small size of the shower room. Towels were provided and these were stained and well worn. The bedroom had a carpet gripper near to the wardrobe area which was raised and painful to step on in bare feet! The bed linen seemed clean and the bed was comfortable to sleep in. Only one pillow was provided but that was fine for us. Tea and coffee making was provided in our room but we couldn't lie in bed and enjoy a hot drink as the bed moved when we lent against the headboard! We did not have breakfast as the dining room was cramped and the choices very basic and unappetising. We found the staff on the whole to be unhelpful, although the light was repaired and the fan replaced (with an old, dirty, dusty one which was noisy and juddered when used) the attitude of the staff was generally argumentative and defensive! If you are only looking for a bed for the night near Kings Cross and don't care about anything else then this fits perfectly but otherwise we would not recommend the Arriva Hotel.

title: A Great value for money!
text: A small and cosy hotel in a very good location few minutes walk from King's Cross station. There is a couple of nice pubs around the corner and plenty of shops to buy food and drinks. Room size is quite good, and the in-room amenities include tea & coffee maker and a fridge. I was also surprised to learn that such a small hotel has a wireless Wi-Fi!!! But unfortunately it does not cover the rear part of the hotel, so make sure you check with them before you bring your laptop. The receptionists were very friendly and helpful, especially John who would go out of his way to make sure you are enjoying your stay

title: Excellent central location
text: The good point for this hotel is the central location. It is not a budget hotel because the price is relatively high. The beds are old and there is a lack of cleaniness. I had to complain about bed bugs, but I was told that this is not too seldom in London. After my complain the bedrooms were sprayed with insectizide. The staff is very friendly and the WiFi is good.

title: A horrible, noisy, shoe box sized room
text: We booked a 9 night stay based on their Booking.com photos and rating. Unfortunately, the room we were given was on the 3rd floor and was not one of the refurbished ones. Although the beds were comfortable, the room smelt musty, was very stuffy and the noise from the street destroyed any chance of a good nights sleep. The main part of the room is no more than 3.5m square, with another room containing the bath/shower, toilet and sink measuring no more than 2.5m x 1.5m leaving little if any room for a human body to move in. It's so tight you almost have to smear yourself in Vaseline just to ensure you can get in or out. There is much better and more luxurious accommodation for the same money just a few miles from this location and away from central London. The price they charge for these shoe boxes, without including breakfast is an absolute travesty. Only stay here if you are absolutely desperate as it is not worth the money.

title: Short stay in London
text: Was coming home from Man UTD away (Chelsea fan) and after having a few drinks needed somewhere to stay the night. Place cost £48 for two people and was provided a nice little room. You get what you pay for, and I have to say I wasn't expecting it to be as nice as it was. Rooms were nice, and the beds were especially comfy with a good little shower. Only problem I found was the smell of smoke walking into the building as apparently it's a no smoking building but other than that was a good place to stay. Not far from Euston/Kings cross. Probably about 5min walk to KC

title: Small Rooms, Well located
text: The Arriva Hotel is well located, in the Kings Cross area, 5 min walk from the Station, with metro, bus and train. The building is tipically in English vitorian style. Rooms seemed modernly refurbished, small thou', even smaller than expected (only 1 person fits between the bed and the wall

title: Worst Hotel Ever
text: After a 4 night stay at this hotel, the staff admitted they don't change the sheets everyday - they do it every 3 days. DISGUSTING. However the I realised the richness that started after day 2 was as a result of BED BUGS! - BROKE OUT INTO A RASH THAT TAKES 2 WEEKS TO RESOLVE. AVOID AT ALL COST

title: They Know Nothing
text: I've stayed in worse places and the location was excellent -- convenient to City Centre and to Heathrow (via Pickadilly Underground). The housecleaning staff work hard and my room was cleaned daily. The breakfast was okay but basically toast and coffee or tea. The negatives: a lumpy, uncomfortable bed and even lumpier pillow, and a room that was only a bed and small table, with a tiny TV located remotely in the upper corner. The walls were paper thin and the finish was poor

title: Nightmare!!!!
text: 3 days stay in a TINY room for three people. The room was very noisy and it was extremely hot inside! The receptionists were kind, they avoided us to be charged for breakfast or for the last day luggage deposit, but it was the minimum after receiving such a treatment despite the reservation made several months in advance! The walls are very tiny and the floor very noisy as well, so you can easiky appreciate your neighbours' life! It is for sure very close to King's Cross, but sometimes it's better to pay more (it is by the way very expensive for a 2 stars hotel!!) and be able to sleep and enjoy the holidays!

title: Just what you need
text: My girlfriend and I took a chance with the Arriva and we are glad we did. Originally attracted to it's location close to Kings Cross (a major transportation hub) and it's private bathroom in every room, we were then pleased to find out that the rooms were very clean and a decent size. Friends of ours that stayed on the second floor actually had a room larger than my NYC apartment. They provided a free breakfast (cereal, toast, OJ), which was fine. Sometimes the dining room gets crowded, so if you are planning on packing the most into your day make sure you eat early. A quick note about the area, Kings Cross reminds me a lot of Penn Station in NYC. Most of the city's tube and bus lines have a stop at Kings Cross so you can get to any part of the city with relative ease (and within 15 minutes of catching a train or bus). This is a good thing, because Kings Cross has little to offer on it's own.

title: I guess you get what you pay for!
text: My wife and I stayed at the Arriva for five nights, and really didn´t know what to expect. The reception clerk (evening-shift) was certainly not friendly or helpful

title: Just unable to sleep
text: I was aware this was a basic hotel but felt it was worth trying. For the positive, the breakfast area was nicely decorated with London murals on the walls and the continental breakfast was reasonable. I was given a small memento containing sweets which was a nice touch. It was this act, location, along with breakfast that stopped me giving a lower score as I just couldn't sleep. The pillows were like cardboard, the quilt looked very old, there was loud creaking from the upstairs bedroom until 2 in the morning and the toilet continued draining water. There is no point saving money on a cheaper hotel if you are unable to sleep.

title: Avoid this place !!!
text: The booking was made by the office staff online using the M.Ds credit card. I then discovered that payment was NOT taken from the card it was simply used to hold the room. The M.D had to go to the office on Saturday and fax a letter with his signature etc and the details of the credit card. The hotel then decided that this wasn't good enough and the M.D should call the hotel. The Hotel had a problem processing the card as the address on the credit card did not have a house number!!! The Manager of the hotel insisted that I pay for the room myself, I explained that my company was the client and that I did not have the facilities to pay for the hotel, I was told that if I did not hand over cash I would not be allowed back into my room nor would I have access to my belongings. At this point my boss went back to the office, called the credit card company and confirmed that there was obviously something wrong with the new credit card system in the hotel. The Credit Card Company and merchant verification centre offered to deal with the Hotel directly but the manager of the hotel refused to take the call. In the end my boss had to use his girlfriends’ credit card. Strangely enough neither her address details, nor expiry date were required??? I can safely say that this is the worst hotel service I and the company have ever experienced

title: Wont go back
text: Four of us arrived after short walk from Kings cross station. Hotel looked nice from outside . Receptionist was not very friendly and did not seem to care . All rooms were pretty cramped although they did have a fridge in them. In one room friend got woken up every so often with fridge vibrating against the bed. Two of the rooms were front facing \9 onto the street and could be noisy with traffic. The two rear facing rooms were a delight !! If you like to watch drunks fighting and throwing their empty cans about. Two rooms were damp with water running down the walls. Two of the phones in the rooms didnt work as the wires were cut through ? I had an unwelcome visitor in the room in the form of a small brown furry friend yes it was a mouse. It would appear that this is common as when I spoke to reception they shrugged and said things are in place to catch them. One of my friends had two of the same type visitors in his room. The fire alarm in one of the rooms had been disconnected which did not fill me with confidence and some of the lights did not work. We complained but as there were no more rooms available we made do for one night. Breakfast was cereal and toast, the toast was freshly made but the cereal was soft and tasted as if it was out of date. On a plus the bathrooms were nice, I think they were newly installed although the showers were a little cramped. Short walk from Kings cross which was okay. However I would have walked further had I known what to expect .

title: Never again!!!! If this is all that is available - stay at home.
text: My daughter, granddaughter and myself stayed here for one night as it wasa my granddaughter's birthday and we took her to London for a treat. Arrived at "hotel" at about one and was told that room would not be ready until two o'clock, which was fine, so we left our luggage in luggage room and headed out for the day. We returned to hotel at about 10.30 that evening and were given keys to our rooms, or in my daughter's case, her cell!!! It was in the basement with a grille on the window and the fire escape outside (although how she was supposed to get out to this is a mystery with the grilles on the window!). She didn't realise this until next morning as it was dark when we got back. Actually she didn't even know sun had risen as it was so dark and dingy!! My room was on first floor which looked OK, although was in need of a good clean as dust was quick thick on bedside cabinet and the carpet did not seem to have been cleaned very well. Bed was clean and comfortable which was the only saving grace for the room. Shower room was OK but shower was not very powerful and water came out in trickle. In my daughter's room every time they flushed the toilet there was a high ptiched whistle which went on for about ten minutes. Next morning went down for breakfast . Had to queue for table in small room which looked more like a hostel than a hotel (if we hadn't had taxi booked we would have gone out) and all that was on offer was meat, cheese, cereal and toast. We all opted just for the toast which was brought out fresh to each table. The "hotel" is in quite a rundown area and bedrooms either overlook metal grilles, alley or rubbish. I would not recommend this hotel to anyone as I feel it is overpriced (we paid £170) for one night in what I can only describe as less than a budget hotel. Don't mind paying for a good, decent hotel, but this is not it. GO ELSEWHERE!!

title: A needed hotel for hospital
text: Room ok.Ideal for being oppisite the hospital our son was in.We were unable to shut the windows and the fire alarm went off both nights because people did not shut the bathroom door while having a shower.Breakfast was reasonable but very crowded and busy

title: Good value
text: If you want a cheap clean hotel near kings cross then this is it. It is basic but I use the same facilities if I stay in a five star anyway. Ask for a room not facing the noisy main road. Cannot comment on the breakfast as we always prefer to eat out in a pleasant looking cafe on the walk in to the sights

title: Adequate and Convenient
text: A 2 night stay for a bit of London exploring before Eurostar to Brussels so hotel was convenient as close to all travel requirements.We found room quite adequate not tiny or noisy and very clean.Staff were polite and helpful.Shower was ok.Tea/coffee tray in room. However what you pay -London prices-raises more than an eyebrow! Our much superior hotel in heart of Brussels was less than half the price-with breakfast.Arriva you pay extra -only £2.50 -but! However it was better than anticipated the 1 morning we took the plunge. As a base we would use hotel again-if no alternative.

title: Very basic facilities, nothing to be excited about.
text: The rooms are very basic. The floors are dirty and the bedding seems to be clean. The breakfast is very very basic. You can have breakfast with someone practically sitting on ur lap. Beats a dorm but the hotel around the corner seems better.

title: Close to underground, small but clean room
text: We wanted a place near the train station, and this being a 2 minute walk away from Kings Cross was definitely a bonus. The room was a little small but clean and tidy, but the toilet and shower was truly cramped. You could occasionally hear people walking or talking in the hallway but that never really disturbed our sleep. Reception was always friendly and ready to offer advice if needed. Also had to borrow a hair dryer but got that from reception with no problems. Good if you're on a budget and want to be close to transport links in London and just need a place to rest for the night.

title: Bit Rough
text: Stayed in room 88, very hot at night due to the weather. Only had a small fan and the window would only open 6". Stainless steel sink jammed in corner of room over a fridge that had seen better days. Shower had mould all round base.

title: Basic
text: Like many others who have reviewed this hotel there is nothing to rave about. The hotel is basic, very basic. I don’t have a problem with this , our issues were the heat and lack of water in the shower. There is no way I would stay here if the weather was really hot, the room really was ridiculously hot and the window did little to help. The fan simply circulated the warm air. The shower was a dribble ! On the plus side it’s fairly cheap and the staff we’re very nice, it was clean enough and we didn’t find the noise bad at all. It’s proximity to Kings Cross is also helpful. We didn’t have breakfast , far too many nice places around the hotel to visit.

title: It is somewhere to sleep
text: Room very basic... Not very pleasant in terms of aesthetics but.... Bed clean and comfy, hot water and basic facilities that you need. Very very warm room though with only a loud fan to cool the room. Didn't try the continental breakfast.

title: Need a Base not to expensive for London.
text: This is a fairly basic hotel with friendly desk staff who do their best to help. The room we stayed in was tired but clean and on the top floor, this isnt a problem as a lift means the stairs are not an issue. This is a very good base, Euston Station is close by with good access to the underground network, very reasonable fares if using contactless card for anywhere in the Capital. The breakfast which is self service is continental not full English but, the Rat Pack public house which is close by does all day breakfasts is you need to top up. Camden is within walking distance and has a good range of eateries and entertainments available. We were out during the day and most of the evening so as a place to crash out it was really good. THE RATINGS SECTION ON THIS PAGE. ARE NOT WORKING BUT WE GIVE IT A FOUR OVERALL.

title: Very basic
text: Good location...but very very basic, could really do with a Complete renovation. If you just want some where to lay your head for the night...and not fussed about a very basic hotel it would be ok, its also very hot and noisy.

title: Good value and good location
text: Stayed for one night this weekend, budget hotel so you know what to expect. Room was clean and everything was replenished ie, tea/coffee making facilities. Staff were very friendly and helpful and baggage store is a secure and ideal place to leave bags prior to check in if arriving early. Rooms were quite hot but fans were supplied. Showers are not very powerful at all (prob more water standing under a toy watering can) but again, we didn’t expect the world so was pleasantly surprised.

title: Good convenient spot.
text: This hotel is a short walk from King's Cross/St. Pancras Station, taking approximately ten minutes and is easy to find. Every member of the reception staff we encountered, were excellent, very helpful and professional. Our room was a bit larger than you find in other hotels in this area and had a small en suite bathroom. Tea and coffee making facilities were available in the room. We stayed for one night as we had an early morning train to catch and it was good for our needs and was a lower than average price, we found. We could not fault it for the requirements we had. Another good point.....it had a lift, so no struggling with heavy suitcases!

title: Cheap and Cheerful
text: Can't go wrong if you want a quick stopover just for a bed and a wash. In a great location close to Euston station. It's clean and a 24 hour desk. I'd come back if it was just a bed I was after for a cheap price.

title: If you must..
text: Stayed here during Olympics for roughly $500 for a week. Couldn't beat the price, but the hotel is very lacking. It is not the ideal place for us "spoiled" Americans. No ac, meager breakfast, small even by european standards rooms, and a staff that could really careless. It was a good learning experience for a girl who likes her 5 star hotels.

title: Hard Beds
text: Bed was so hard and pillow so soft it was almost non-existent just like my sleep. Breakfast was cheapest of ingredients and could not eat any of it. Even though this was just an overnight stay on way to somewhere else I definitely would not use it again.

title: More hostel than hotel,
text: Book this one in the usual way looking at prices on star ratings for the area. It was only a two star so I wasn’t expecting much and it lived up to expectations. The room was so small and have twin beds but very little space to move around. The sliding wooden door on the bathroom area screeched as you opened it. The general cleanliness was just OK but only just. It was quite entertaining to watch the German coach party struggling to operate the low-quality toasters in the breakfast room. Breakfast with old rice crispy‘s or Cornflakes toast Spamm cheese and some butter and jam. Area cleared away before people had finished eating. Really dont Go there unless you are desperate. Also difficult to get back in after about 1030 as it is difficult to attract anybody’s attention on the front door is locked.

title: Exactly was it says on the tin
text: My wife and I stayed at the Arriva for 5 nights in July. We were looking for a budget hotel, and thats exactly what we got. Thats not to say there was any thing wrong with the hotel. The room was small but comfy. The on suite toilet and shower room was imaculate, it actually looked brand new. The rooms were made every day and fresh towels were always left. There is a fridge in the room which was a little bit big but a good idea. The reception staff were very friendly and the the reception is maned 24 hours , good for a late return from a night on the town. The only disapointing thing was the breakfast, advertised as Continental Breakfast, but was really only Toast and tea/coffee. Also the noise from the traffic at night and early morning is quite loud if you are a light sleeper. The location is good, a few mins walk to Kings Cross and if your feeling energetic the walk to covent garden is about 20 mins. So if you are looking for a cheap "base, ie place just to sleep" for a few nights in London the Arriva is Ideal. if you're the type of person who spends a lot of time in your hotel room I would think again. There is no Bar in the hotel, But Swintons next door is a great place, friendly staff and great food.

title: Don't stay here
text: Stayed here and wouldn't recommend, the only good thing about this place was the reception staff were friendly. The rooms were small , not very clean, had to get them to change duvet cover as was stained, the duvet had seen better days, shabby rooms. The reason we stayed here was that the hotel was in Camden, well that's what it said when I booked it, it's no were near Camden, big taxi ride to camden markets. Very disappointed

title: Absolutely awful!
text: Two friends and I stayed here on the 14th April for one night. Although it was fairly cheap, we felt we paid well over what the room was worth. We were in the basement with a view of a scabby alleyway filled with cigarette butts (this was lit up at night by a bright neon blue light that illuminated our room). The single bed was propped up against a door that had a draught coming from the street through it, and there was a miscellaneous red stain next to the double bed. We could’ve gotten over all of this if it wasn’t for the last little surprise that was in store. Our ceiling started dripping water at about 10pm and didn’t stop dripping all night. We had to get a bin from reception to put underneath it and by the next morning we had a fair amount collected in it. When we checked out the next morning I asked to speak to the manager and was told he wouldn’t be available till the next day. So I rang up first thing Monday morning and was told to ring back the next day. When I eventually spoke to him he was nothing but rude and denied all of our problems. He finally relented into giving us a 25% refund but I genuinely think this was ridiculous. I wouldn’t recommend this hotel to my worst enemy.

title: Great location, BUDGET hotel with friendly helpful staff.
text: My daughter and I travelled to London to spend time with friends having treatment in Great Ormond Street. The Arriva Hotel was the best priced hotel in the area we wanted. We had a twin room on the third floor facing the road. Although there was road noise, to be expected when staying in an urban area, it wasn't unbearable. We commented throughout the stay on the quietness within the hotel. The room was a twin and was plenty large enough for the two of us, the facilities were excellent, including a fridge, kettle, hairdryer, dresser with large mirror a small chest of drawers beside each bed and shelves and hanging space for clothes. Our friends who were staying in a local Travelodge, commented that we had more in our room than they did. The ensuite shower was clean and contained everything we needed including basic toiletries. The room bins were emptied daily, tea and coffee replenished and the towels replaced, at the same time. The staff we encountered were pleasant and courteous. Breakfast was basic but plentiful with a good selection of jams, ham, cheese, tinned peaches, cereal, yoghurt, white and wholemeal breads. As a Coeliac I travelled with my own gluten free bread that I was able to toast without comment! We went down about 8.45 and there was still plenty of food and seats available. Tea and coffee, apple and orange juice and milk were available to drink, no decaf, though! We will definitely choose to stay again at the Arriva Hotel, in the future. * Please remember that this is a Budget hotel it is not luxurious, or overpriced. It's best asset is its proximity to Kings Cross, St Pancras International and Euston stations.*

title: very very poor
text: were given room 30, it had a double bed in it, 3 sides of the bed were touching the walls. pillows were thin. no light in the room, it was like a squat and very dim. i went to complain and was given room 41. this was bigger and brighter, but was on the road side. the noise from traffic was non stop. the toilet and shower room were so small it was very claustrophobic. there were no seats, you had to sit on the bed. no water to make tea or coffee. dust on skirting boards and radiator. went out to watch a show and got back at mid night. could not sleep as the traffic went on and on. i know there is a lot of traffic in london, but there was no sound proofing on the windows. from about 8am til we left at 11 the noise from cleaners was ridiculous. banging doors and speaking loudly. no chance of trying to catch a lie in. Yazz on the reception was very nice and polite.

title: Tarantino-esque hostel
text: The location was really good but the room had a Cold War era dampness and depressive box like quality. If you did manage to sleep in a room close to an A road and with no air con, you might be lucky enough to have your own swimming pool in the corner of your room(carpet was unusually wet). If you stayed the whole night then in the morning you could be treated to a breakfast room that is straight out of a Tarantino soviet movie, somehow for a hotel that has 60+ rooms they only have 6 tables and you feel as though you are in some kind of ration queue. Otherwise great hotel 😂

title: You Deserve Better
text: Pros: - close to Kings Cross for travel Cons: - broken single-glazed window so you hear incredibly loud traffic and partying all night - no air con and a radiator that stays on which means the room is always ridiculously hot - very poor soundproofing to the corridors and other rooms - toilet had to be flushed three times before it actually flushed - toilet sewage smell - WiFi continually cuts out - not very clean in any respects, including dust and grime - breakfast room is simply not big enough for the amount of people staying so you end up bumping into other people or having to wait and queue outside - assured by the mysterious “manager” before my stay that I had a third floor room booked, then upon arrival informed by the receptionist I had a basement room and there was nothing he could do. Receptionist says I must speak to “the manager” for a refund but has no idea when “the manager” will return - even my room key managed to break off the key ring when locking the door! - highly recommend that you do not stay here, even for this cheap price there are much better hotels. Or maybe try to pay a bit more for a somewhere better, where you will actually get a good night’s sleep and not worry about the hygiene.

title: Small but suitable for budget
text: Suitable for the budget. Yes, small, one side entry to dble bed and no table for cases, would suit single traveller or couple going out sightseeing all day - us! Pubs, shops, eats all within 5 mins and transport. Bathroom tight and shower is sml 3/4 with low pressure, so no rugby players. Breakfast is £3.50 but free wi-fi for each device.

title: Good cost benefit
text: Well located nearby King's Cross/St Pancras stations with restaurants, pubs, stores and exchange houses at walking distance. Rooms are small but clean and comfortable. Breakfast room may get crowded so I suggest you don't leave it for the last minute. Night shift receptionist Adrian was wonderful, very friendly, helpful and kind at all times.Wifi signal was not very good inside the room (#3).

title: Ripped off
text: The actual hotel wasn't too bad, typical cheap hotel but they rip you off 100 pounds with their booking system. They charge a 100 puns deposit but they don't take this off your total bill, when I questioned the manager on this they said that it will automatically be refunded to me, it never was. As I live in Australia it is too hard to try and recover this money so I'm down 100 pounds. I would never stay there again

title: Cheap and nasty, dont stay unless no where else available
text: Just got back from stay at Arriva, chose somewhere close to KingsCross after reading reviews and wanted something on a budget as booked a last minute deal. On our arrival, found bookling in to our room ok but a bit slow. Got to our room and yes, it was really basic and very small. There was a phone socket loose from the wall with all the wires showing, not a good sign, but thought not going to be spending much time in our our room. only to sleep in. When checked bed, there was only 2 pillows on a double which were really flat, when we left for our night out, asked the receptionist for 2 more pillows and he said they would be in room when we get back. On our arrival back somewhat 6 hours later, asked if pillows had been put in room, was given a vacant look and answer, after a while, receptionist then went to a basement room and brought 1 cushion back,! saidf there were 2 people in room, he then went back and brought another cusion, not pillow, and it seemed to be our fault that he had to do this!! how any hotel in this day and age does not have spare pillows in all rooms is a mystery. Did not feel very safe leaving valuables as no drawers/doors on wardrobe so everything wide open. All in all cant fault hotel for location, but as an hotel, stay here only if you are desperate, there are much nicer ones located in the vicinity as we noticed when we were walking around.

title: s'alright
text: Close to King's Cross station. Very average hotel. Rooms were average. Breakfast was average. Staff was average. Price, however, was very good. No A/C made it a little warm, so windows had to be opened which made it kind of noisy. Tough to find decent cheap accomodation in London. This is probably as close as you get.

title: Good budget hotel
text: Small, cosy, clean hotel. For approx £50/night in central london it was worth it. Good location, down from kings cross. Room really hot, so wouldnt too too good when weather is warm. Breakfast was a cheap continental (no brown bread). I read the reviews about it and it was quite true. Dont expect the best, just somewhere cheap, clean and good location.

title: One of the worst Hotels in London
text: Unfriendly staff, small stuffy rooms, totally agree with the other comments. DO NOT STAY HERE!

title: Barely a step up from a hostel
text: I was just not impressed at all. The rooms were very small, cheap, hardly maintained. We had a room on the ground floor next to the street - This is very noisy, and doesn't help that the window needed to stay cracked since there is no AC. You best take your shower early in the morning or at night else there will be no hot water by 7:30 AM. The drains were so slow you had to shower at 1/2 throttle to avoid flooding the bathroom. The clerk at the front desk wasn't exactly friendly, but not terribly rude either... Overall, my advice is stay here only if you can't afford somewhere better.

title: Adequate
text: Stayed for five nights on a work training week. Luckily brought ear plugs. Was in a twin room, yes walls very thin. Havent stayed in London hotel for decades, so was great to know bed bugs cleared up from beds. Yes the ones you see decades ago annoying. Good fridge. Kettle dryer, excellent. Clean towels daily, excellent. Breakfast should be 7 and not 7.30. So rushed and crowded, wifi could be better especially when work give u internet work, so had to sit in cold reception. So a lounge or study, or even opening restaurant up to go at night be good. Receptionist is a workaholic and hope he is valued.

title: For a budget hotel this was as expected, would stay again
text: An honest review if you are expexting the Hilton it is not but what it is, is a freindly hotel really accommodating the bathroom and beds were clean and had all the facilities you needed for a short stay a bargin if you ask me for a stay in central London close to station Camden somewhere to lay your head would definately return

title: Room without a view
text: My rating actually lies in between "Terrible" and "Okay" ... there were "terrible" things as no window in our room as well as "okay"-things, like the price and the location. Upon arrival the triple room we had booked weeks ago wasn't available and we had to split up into a double room with ensuite bathroom (shower's drain was blocked) and a twin room with the bathroom accross the floor, through two doors and four steps down, which wasn't overly clean. The next day we were moved to our triple room that was located in the basement with no windows at all. Breakfast was rather bleak, some cornflakes and toast (eight pieces of toast for three people) and either tea or coffee. The dishes weren't overly clean either and the table cloth badly stained. Next time I'll visit London, I'll definitely chose another hotel!

title: Mice
text: This is the worst hotel I have ever stayed in. I was down in London for a two night business trip and, albeit it was a 2 star hotel, but it was not value for money. If I had arrived 5 minutes earlier I would have been stuck in a broken down lift. I felt sorry for the receptionist, who was friendly, however appeared to receive no help via telephone from the manager of the hotel in trying to fix the problem. The only way the young couple got out is because the guy used to work for an elevator maintenance company. The walls and carpets appeared very unclean. The shower allowed for a small trickle of water only. I had to fill up the kettle with the mug as the sink was too small (not a big issue). On the second night, I was wakened in the middle of the night by a mouse. It had found it's way into my open suitcase. When I put on the light it eventually scurried under the bed. I went down to reception immediately to complain, but I had to move room by myself in the middle of the night, which didn't make me feel any better - frankly, if there's one mouse there's going to be mice

title: Choose somewhere else
text: Positive - free luggage room, first receptionist helpful, late night receptionist gave us key but didn’t even explain where room was?? Negative - Tiny cramped room, springs poking through bed, won’t look at breakfast as hotel is below standard - usually book a major chain will stick with one of those in future.

title: London in another way!
text: The hotel location is super! The hotel staff ia very nice and helpful. There is a luggage room for free! There is the USB charger for mobile phones in the room and you don't Need the adaptor. Breakfast is 3.50 pounds and you can choose bread, jam, butter, coffee, juice, tra, yougurt. Nothing really special, but the price is low, so it's ok. There is the bathroom in the room, very small and an hairdryer. The price ia too expensive for the hotel rooms. Very very small and not so comfortable for the price you pay. On the other hand, the hotel is 5 minutes walking from King's Cross station, so Easy to go everywhere. A special Word for the staff at the reception, very kind very helpful, very nice!!!

title: OK for a night or two before the trips from St. Pancras/Kings X or Euston
text: We stayed at Arriva Hotel for two nights in January 2011. We needed a place to stay within walking distance from Euston and Kings X Stations as on the first and second days we had trains at about 5.30 am and 7 am.
