Being there for a city break we found it hard picking a hotel as im fussy were i stay but this one i would recomend for tourist, familys, couples or business use as its not to expensive and has wifi access and also computer in the lobby for guests to use and the staff speak mulible languages. Hope to stay again thanks.

title: Nice hotel, Good Stay
text: We are traditionalists in many ways, we don't like room only when we stay in an hotel, we like B&B. So when we saw this hotel and its reviews and the fact breakfast was included drew our attention, In particular when we got on the hotel website and found there was a further discount for booking direct with them we secured a room for 3 nights with breakfast for under £400. We were not disappointed. We arrived via Aldgate station which was a 5 minute walk to the hotel, reception and check in was easy and our room was ready, even though we arrived early. We had a large spacious room on the 4th floor, the fridge contents were included in our price. Plenty of storage space, big bathroom with an excellent walk in shower, very quite room, no problem with sleep. Choice of continental or cooked to order, I had the eggs royal twice & the bacon bap on the 3 mornings, all were hot and tasty, no issues at all. The only criticism I would have is there could have been more of a choice on freshly cut fruit in the morning. We only used the pub once for a drink, but £16 for a pint of lager and a large Sauvignon Blanc meant we didn't return! There are not a lot of eating options locally, we had a drink in the Minories once but didn't like it, the best place we found for food was The Hoop & Grapes near the station, which was very good & reasonably priced. For the right price we would definitely stay at the Chamberlain again.

title: Changing My Tune About the Chamberlain
text: Previously, I have had great experiences at this hotel (see my earlier review.) Perhaps the double rooms are simply better than the single rooms. This is the first time I booked a single, although it was a "luxury" room. I booked through the hotel website. I was hoping that would put me on a higher level than maybe the rooms they book over at hotels.com. Maybe it was the fact that I got a room that was once part of a suite. In any event, the room was getting tired and not furnished nearly as elegantly as my previous rooms. And this time the noise was an issue. My window overlooked the restaurant's back doors. So when the trash collectors came around at 0600, man oh man, was it noisy. Especially when the recycling people came around.... The room also had some kind of background "hum" which I could not identify but was very annoying. Various other noises made me realize that the back of the house at this level was not the place to be. The maid service was superb. Newspapers, water, chocolates, turndown, etc. All great. The bathroom lighting was horrible. Really hard to shave in the mirror. There is a very annoying trend in UK pubs where one must order everything from a bartender. No table service. This was not the case in my previous visits to the Chamberlain, but I experienced it in other pubs during this trip so the Chamberlain is not alone in this. Saturday night and four other tables occupied. The servers were uninvolved. The food was well presented but not great quality and small quantities. Sunday night I went to another pub a few meters away that was packed with people. Came back to the hotel and the restaurant was quite empty. So there must be other people who find the service and food lacking. It also seemed to be the most expensive Fullers beer in town. With Fuller's buying up all kinds of London pubs, staying here for the beer is no longer an imperative.

title: Better Than Expected
text: Once again a hotel booking due to location and unavailability elsewhere and certainly more than I intended to spend but nonetheless I was pleased with my accommodation. On arrival the exterior of the hotel is nothing special and the entrance of the hotel is rather dark and traditional. Hotel staff at check in whilst friendly I did have the impression that the girl who served me was perhaps new and reading through a check list, particularly when she asked for a credit card to secure in room purchases which I didn't want to do and was advised by her colleague it wasn't necessary and a debit card was not able to be used because of the prepayment option required. The room was both traditional but not old fashioned and spacious and being a Fullers owned property there were two complimentary ales to try in the fridge. With a Fullers pub next door, access through hotel reception or the street created a nice environment rather than the usual often soulless hotel bars. In a street filled with pubs, bars and food options and a Starbucks across the road for your morning coffee pick I would happily stay again.

title: Splendid!
text: My girlfriend and me stayed from December 27th till the 29th in `The Chamberlain`. We had chosen this hotel due to the typical English look and atmosphere, and it did not let us down! I knew that check-in was possible as from 3 pm, but once we arrived we could immediately enter our room. Even better, we got an upgrade from a `Luxury Double` to a `Deluxe king`-bedroom. The room, located on the 4th floor, had several facilities: walk-in rain shower, hair dryer, flatscreen tv, fridge and safe. Also slippers and bathrobes and a personal (free of charge!) Nespresso machine were available. Heating/airco and wifi all functioned well. The main elevator was out of order, so everybody had to use the service elevator. As a compensation for that, we were offered two vouchers to use in the bar on the ground floor. Given the fact a large pint of beer in London reaches the price of £5, it definitely made a difference in our wallets. Staff (both at reception and in the pub) was very friendly and professional and we had a great chat with the Algerian receptionist when we arrived back at the hotel in the middle of the night. Tube-stations Tower Hill, Aldgate and Liverpool Station are nearby. Tower Hill and starting point of various `Jack the ripper`-tours are also within short walking distance. Overall we really enjoyed our stay during this X-mas break and I would recommend it!

title: Nice pub, service a bit spotty
text: My boyfriend and I had a couple of meals at this hotel, although we were staying elsewhere. It had a nice atmosphere and the food is generally pretty good. However, the service is a bit hit and miss in the pub section, but better in the restaurant. The food tends to come out of the kitchen on the cold side, with hollandaise sauce arriving cold and gelatinous, and the sweet potato soup also cold on another occasion. However - we kept going back, didn't we? There are a lot of pub and restaurant choices on Minories, but we went back to this place 3 times. Give it a try.

title: Great stay!
text: I was so lucky to have a room with a large terrace, I just wish I could have more time to spend there. My room was really spacious, great surprise actually in London! Bathroom equipment and all toiletries were excellent.

title: ... a treasure at the right price, and sometimes the price is right.
text: The thing about London is to find somewhere you can afford and hope it stays in business. For years I used to stay at a place in Kensington near the Gloucester Road tube which provided ample bedsitting rooms for 30 pounds a night. Inevitably, five years ago, it closed and since then I have experimented with small hotels at mid range prices, and endured many more appalling experiences than rewarding ones. It’s true

title: Very nice and with a very good location
text: Very good stay in this hotel for a couple of days. Good room, very clean, quiet and a good bed. We have not used breakfast and dinner because good restaurants and pubs are in the neighbourhood. We can recommand this hotel very much.

title: lovely stay
text: I received a very nice welcome and they were aware that I had requested an early check in so my room was ready when I got there. The room was much bigger then I expected and I loved the bathrobe and slippers. Breakfast was delicious it was nice that it was off a menu rather then a buffet as most hotels do now. Only ate in the restaurant in the evening once it wasn't very busy but there was no staff as they were working on the bar but once they knew I was there the service was very quick, the food was lovely especially the ale soaked sticky toffee pudding. Would stay here again.

title: 6 Day Stay
text: My wife and I stayed at the Chamberlain for 6 days in June of this year. The room was clean and comfortable and away from the street so there was no problem with noise. The location was great, a 5 minute walk to the tube and the Tower. It's location in the financial section makes it a little less busy in the daytime, but if you stay during a weekend most of the restaurants in the area are closed, however the hotel restaurant is open and so is the pub, the food here is good. The hotel staff was very friendly and always ready to help. I have read other reviews on the Chamberlain saying it's old, hello, this is London, most everything here is old ,if you want new/modern go to Disney, not much charm there. If we return to London we will stay at the Chamberlain.

title: excellent hotel
text: one of the best hotel experiences i have had in london. extremely courteous and helpful staff, amazingly good breakfast, spotlessly clean. I cannot fault this place. I wish some of the 5 star hotel management came here to learn about customer services and every aspect of comfort provided

title: Good hotel
text: This is in a good location easy access to tube and sights. We had a good room it was a good size. The staff are polite and helpful. It is a clean well presented hotel. We were offered complimentary drinks due to a small inconvenience of the main lift being out of order, it was no hardship as there was a secondary lift. I would stay again.

title: Good stay
text: Double room for 3 nights. Room 109 a good size (and seemed larger than most when we looked at the hotel plan on the fire exit instructions)- well furnished and clean but hardly a good view - out on to the air con and "gubbins". Shaver point and bathroom radio/speaker not working and - on the 1st floor at least - you do hear/feel the underground a bit - but get used to it. If you order a taxi - insist on a black cab - our mini cab was not good -(not the hotel's fault). Staff were very good - particularly the breakfast team. Breakfast was good and plentiful - but we were glad it was in with the room price - £16 odd would have been a lot had we had to pay it separately. Pub food was excellent - as was the beer. Very helpful that we could check in and have our room nice and early - and that bags could be safely stowed all of our last day. Shame the fire alarm went off at 3.00 am - (but glad to know it was working!). An apology from someone in the morning might have been nice. Overall it was a good stay in a nice hotel with nice folks running it and we would use again. Excellent location for the tube, the river, the Tower and the City. Thank you.

title: Location a bonus and a minus
text: We enjoyed our stay at the hotel as it was situated close to the Algate Station of the circle/ metropolitan lines. The lines however were close during weekends which posed much inconvenience. Overall the hotel facilities were great and it’s comfortable. We did not experience any noise from the nearby bars and clubs as mentioned by some viewers here, and we even stayed on the first floor. The hotel even provided a mobile phone though I think most of the time, the travelers already had their own devices nowadays.

title: Great stay!
text: Just back from a weekend in London and a stay at the Chamberlain. I was not disappointed! We were upgraded to a newly refurbished superior room which was a lovely surprise upon arrival! The staff were helpful and friendly. We had a beautiful bathroom and luxury toiletries, fluffy towels and a super comfy bed. We didn't have the breakfast so can't comment on that - although most of the other comments are positive. The hotel is well placed for the Tower of London and Tower Bridge. It is also just a short walk from Aldgate and Tower Hill tube stations and the DLR. The only slight niggle/suggestion was that the mini bar had 2 bottles of beer - maybe a small bottle of wine would be a nice touch for wine drinkers? However, this is a real first world problem and would certainly no stop me coming back. Thank you for a lovely stay!

title: Excellent hotel near the Tower of London
text: The hotel exceeded my expectations: it is close to the Tower and two underground stations, the room big as was the bathroom, we received complementary newspapers and drinks in the room. We enjoyed the full English breakfast.

title: Througout a very good experience
text: Very nice and helpful staff, good and clean room and very nice with the bathtub in our room. The location was quite good, close to Liverpool Street St and other tube stations as well bus lines and last but not least very close to Tower Bridge

title: One night stay in London in transit from Oxford to Brussels
text: Great value for money. Excellent location in just a few minutes walk from the Spitafields market and Bricklane. We had to check out at 6am to catch the early eurostar train and the staff were very kind to prepare take away breakfast! Just a few steps away from Aldgate tube station.

title: Good location and cosy rooms
text: Good location near Tower, Tower Bridge, tube and DLR. Clean and comfortable rooms, we had on facing the back alley, giving us a quite and good nights sleep - even on Friday and Saturdays. All in all a good experience.

title: Great room good service
text: This hotel is 5 min from my office. From the outside all you see is the pub but the hotel and the rooms are quite nice. This time I got one of their larger room and does it ever make a difference. The staff is nice.

title: Very good experience
text: A well presented, slightly quirky hotel. We arrived from Heathrow where we had just been told our luggage for a 3 week holiday had been lost and the host did his best to make our first hours comfortable and also upgraded our room in an effort to make us feel better! We stayed 3 nights and found the room comfortable with an excellent bed. Breakfasts were very good and hot food served on warmed plates. Coffee was awful unfortunately, brewed American style and not at all to our taste. I did however try my first black pudding and can recommend on (in small doses!). Our Bly issue was that the room was too warm. The air con really didn't cut it so we slept with the doors to the terrace open which, being London, was quite noisy. Travellers also need to be aware hat the area is very much geared towards workers and it was buzzing when we arrived on a Friday night. However Saturday and Sunday, all pubs and restaurants were closed apart from our hotel, and one other pub down the road. Overall, a really good experience, and the staff were extremely kind.

title: Fantastic London stay
text: We stayed at The Chamberlain Hotel. We had a great room with a king sized bed. The staff were friendly and made everything so easy. Breakfast was freshly made and delicious. All in all a wonderful hotel with great staff. I would definatly recommend it.

title: Brilliant small hotel
text: My girlfriend and I stayed at this hotel for a blissful two nights last week. It was easy enough to find (although the area wasn't one that I was familiar with). Also, it's only 5-6 stops away from Westminster on the underground, so perfect for those travelling into the heart of the city. We were greeted at reception by friendly and efficient staff, who didn't bat an eyelid at our request to check in 3 hours early. The room was spacious, well furnished and clean. The much vaunted television in the bathroom was in full working order and the only complaint I could make is that some of the hotel furnishings are a little dated (while well maintained!) Great choice of TV channels for those with kids, or those tired after a day of exploring Very quiet for London and slept well. Our rate included free continental breakfast, which was tasty if unimaginative and was served by very friendly staff. Much better than most hotels in London, even those with and extra star and a steeper price!

title: A very nice Hotel :)
text: My husband and I booked a standard double room through the Laterooms website and had a overnight stay for only £84 during the last August Bank Holiday - the usual cost of the room is £325 per night but I guess that's due to the location as it's slap bang in the City of London!! If you stay here on the weekend you'll find it pretty quiet as all the bankers are at home swimming in their cold hard cash - so be warned - none of the nearby shops or restaurants will be open. You have 3 options then, eat at the hotel restaurant or bar (which has a good selection of pub grub and more fancy items but beware of the time as they do not stay open past 10pm), travel into town (Aldgate and Tower Hill tube stations are within easy walking distance as are several bus stops) or get back late and order room service which is available until 7am. The Chamberlain Brasserie has a 2 course set menu for only £13.50 so you may be tempted to eat there before heading out to town

title: Third stay at the Chamberlain
text: We love staying at this hotel. It is about 20 minutes from the O2 and a similar time from the west end. All of the staff are amazingly friendly. The hotel is clean and tidy and the staff are amazingly friendly. The food is good and did I mention that the staff are amazingly friendly!

title: really friendly
text: I have just returned from a weekend in London, we took advantage of the Open House weekend held every year in the capital ,it is a fantastic chance to get to visit buildings not usually open to the public I would really recommend it. we stayed at the Chamberlain Hotel situated a few minutes walk from The Tower of London, the hotel was a fullers hotel which meant a fantastic pint of good london beer was on offer! The hotel has about 64 rooms and is exceptionally clean and the staff were really helpful and friendly, the only problem I encountered was the TV in the bathroom did not work and i was quite dissapointed, I had looked forward to luxuriating in bubbles whilst watching 'who wants to be a millionaire' !! but this was not meant to be!! The only other downside but I think this applies to most london hotels was the price of the breakfast, £15 for a full english we declined this as the Weatherspoons chain of pubs offer a huge breakfast for £4.50 a fraction of the price, apart from that I would definately recommend this hotel.

title: Excellent stay!
text: The Chamberlain is a very conveniently situated low key hotel -- ideal for business or leisure travel. The front desk staff were friendly and accommodating. The rooms were unexpectedly spacious (really loved the bathrooms --shower and bathtub!). Would definitely stay again.

title: Wknd break in London
text: My partner booked this hotel for us for our 2 year anniversary break in London. Check in was swift and friendly and we had room 303. Room was small and traditional in style but clean and bed was comfy. Not like the club doubles that you see online on their website however or on booking.com. Breakfast was ok, very mediocre but you plenty of choice. Hotel is in a good location with Aldgate Underground station very close however they had closed this line for the weekend making getting around a bit more difficult but that's London for you. Not a bad hotel in the main but probably wouldn't choose to stay here again.

title: 2 Good Stays
text: One one day stay and one three day stay in early December. Usual efficient service, reasonable prices and for me ideal location. Floors 3 and 4 have been refurbished and are much improved compared to floor 1. Not sure if there is a plan to refurbish 1 also. Haven't stayed on 2. Note that my rooms on 3 and 4 did not have a bath just a walk in large shower. Come on hotel though the main Lift has been out of action for months. A free drink offered is nice but surely should be fixed by now?

title: Very good Hotel, Value for Money
text: very nice hotel, newly renovated rooms, beautyfully designed. quiet location between financial district and sptalfields. tube aldgate and tower hill near by. pub in the basement nice but a little big for my taste. tower and the lively brick lane and spitalfield near .

title: Very Good
text: We have stayed here several times and have not been disapointed. Staff are very good. Rooms very well appointed and clean. Breakfast excellent & also bar meals Location is 5 mins walk from Tower bridge and the thames (Boat rides ect)

title: Visit to London
text: I have enjoyed staying st the hotel, the staff were very friendly and the room was clean and tidy. Also the location of the hotel is very good were every thing is handy. Train stinks just l00 mtr away and lot of attractions around the hotel

title: Welcome Dinner Location for our United Kingdom Tour
text: Our tour selected this restaurant for our welcome dinner. It was a short walk from the Grange Tower Bridge Hotel where we stayed. We had a private room for our large tour group. We had a fixed menu to select from so I can't comment on the menu itself. I ordered a chicken dish which was quite good. The atmosphere was pleasant and the servers were efficient. It was a fun evening.

title: Great value,good location, spacious rooms
text: The room was huge which was very welcome after 5 nights in a tiny room in a 5-star Paris hotel. The hotel was so charming with an old timely feel, but the rooms were clean and updated enough so you didn't feel like you were in an outdated hotel. Around the corner from 2 Underground stations and down the street to the Tower of London and Tower Bridge. The negative about location - nothing seemed open after 5pm (and it was a Saturday night). All the pubs and restaurants were closed. We had to go to another neighborhood for dinner and drinks.

title: great experience
text: meet exactly our expectation, this was our first stay in the UK,it was a plessure to be in your hotel Room was finebreakfast in the morning and dinner in the evening was fine as wellExtra + point for the daily newspaper and providing a mobile phone during our stay

title: Always a pleasure
text: I have stayed as a solo female business traveller on a number of occasions, plus with my husband. The staff are invariably courteous and friendly and always make me feel welcome and comfortable - even when I brave the pub on my own! The rooms are so comfortable and I love room service breakfast. Public transport is so convenient - the bus to my City office and DLR to City Airport. Looking forward to my next trip in mid March.

title: Weekend break
text: Old hotel but lovely modern room and 2 mins from underground into Oxford street also ideal location for bars we wanted to use. 5 mins walk from sky bar. Breakfast was included and was fine, lots of choice, but avoid the sausages! They were like rubber! Will be staying here again when in London

title: Wonderful time
text: Thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Nothing was too much trouble and the staff were very friendly. Will be back again. Looking forward to it later in year and for a longer period. No complaints at all with anything

title: Covenient location...
text: Easy access and convenient when visiting London... Staff very helpful and friendly.. Good breakfast what else do you need... very close to subway station Aldgate... Overall a good deal and can recommend it

title: Excellent stay, as usual
text: The hotel perfectly suits our needs and interests, central location, excellent service, very good food, a pub to have a good glass of wine in the evening. We will be back next year and have already booked our room

title: Good bed but "sad" room
text: The bed was really comfortable but the room was pretty dark, low lights and tiny kid of windows (horrible sights). The room has a nespresso machine but the rest is very old fashion room not really comfortable. Free mini bar was ok.

title: Wonderful Rooms with Attached Pub
text: As you can see from the title, I was mostly excited about this hotel because it is owned by a London brewery (Fuller's) and had an attached pub. Not to mention I booked what I thought was a pretty good rate for a good hotel 135 pounds a night (a hotel in my home town costs more than that!) on the hotel website. The location is excellent, it is right off the Tower Hill tube stop and that tube station has only a small number of steps to drag your suitcase up. The hotel has a lift. The twin room we were given was fantastic. Messages from the hotel staff (who are all very good) appear on your TV. The bathroom was huge, with shower AND bath. Oh yeah, TV next to the bathtub. Big shower. Bath robes in the closet and a very nice turndown service that leaves bath slippers. If I had used a bath towel during the day and after the room had been made up, the turn down service would replace it with a fresh towel. The air conditioning was wonderful. I have stayed in London hotels with none. But in July and August it's essential to have it. And this one was always nice and cool. In fact, a bit chilly first thing in the morning. Good thing you have the robes! Breakfast did not come with our booking so I only went to the pub for dinner and drinks. The pub had six different cask ales on offer. Which far exceeded my expectations. The menu was reasonably priced - for London. The food, which was quite good, was always delivered in a timely manner. The waitstaff that I interacted with was made up entirely of non-Brits, but all spoke English well and had minimal problems with my American accent. In fact, I found them to be especially curious about the US and we spoke often about traveling in the US. Perhaps that's why over the course of the week I found the service to be very good. But for me it was. My only complaint is the noise level. We had a first floor room (second floor if you are an American). I could hear and feel the subway train and hear some of the road traffic as well. From my room I could hear the water pipes from the nearby rooms whistle when someone was showering. I am a light sleeper, but this noise didn't appear to upset my sleep patterns all that much after the initial recognition that it was there.

title: Really good hotel !
text: We've spent three nights at Chamberlain ( 18-21 May) and really satisfied with the hotel. Helpful staff, quite good location ( close to Tower London), not large, but very clean and comfortable room, nice breakfast. I've booked our room via hotelsrus website. Got a very good deal ( 81 Ł for a double with breakfast ) ! Before booking I checked the reviews about this hotel on this forum. Must tell you, that the reviews are not so good as my experience with the hotel. I think it's a really nice hotel ! And not to speak about the price ! They have special weekend offer. Located in the City of London, which is a very quiet place at weekends. Close to the hotel ( 5 min. walk) you can reach two tube stations ( Aldgate, Tower HiIl ). So, I highly recommend this hotel for anyone travelling to London, either on business, or just for fun !

title: Dissappointed
text: After reading previous reviews before staying at this property we assumed that it would be ok, so here are just our own gripes about staying here! Good things first: Convenient for the tourist and near to Tower of London and good transport network. Staff were friendly and seemed to want to make our stay enjoyable, but lacked some enthusiam! Tried their best. Our room stated as a luxury room, well it had a bed, tv and all the usual accessories but luxury? No not really just a standard room clean, tidy and in need of some updating ie the bathroom, the extractor fan didn't work which steamed up the bathroom also when flushing the toilet water nearly came up through the bath plughole, and the water when we had a shower took time to drain, not a huge problem but one we did needed to mention, as it may be that staff were unaware of this? Also we had little guests in the bathroom as well, silver fish! One was quite big about 3 to 4 cms long! It had a friend too. Bugs don't bother us but not in a supposedly 4 star hotel! Nothing was resolved on this issue and when checking out we told the "manager who seemed the not be aware of the reported issue" but noted it down. The floor tiles in bathroom were chipped in places and some of the grouting needed redoing. Menu offered was adequate but the food never seemed hot enough, breakfast on one morning took a long time to arrive as people came in after we were seated and getting served before us! We don't mind waiting but when it did arrive it was the wrong order, was sent back and then took another 30minutes to be served all that was wrong was the egg order! Petty it might seem, but not what we asked for. Really little niggly things that could have made our stay better,to us we didn't feel we got value for our money, shame as we enjoyed our time in London. Would we come back here sorry to say but no.

title: Great Value, great Service
text: Warm welcome and overall great client-orientated service. Due to a miscommunication there was an issue with an extra bed in our room which was sorted out in our favor without any discussion. I have rarely experienced such courteous and friendly service. We were traveling with our 4-year old son and every effort was made to accomodate him well. The rooms are nicely deckrated, spacious for London and very clean. Breakfast is made-to-order and very good too. Drinks (including beer) in the mini bar are complementary and are stocked every day. Location is close to the tube / buses and just a few steps from tower/tower bridge.

title: Service at the Chamberlain Hotel poor.
text: I arrived at the hotel at 2 p.m. on Sunday Oct. 8 and was told I couldn't check in until 3 p.m. So I went into the pub and had a light meal to kill time. At 2:40 p.m. I returned to the receptionist and told her I had been traveling all night from the U.S. and asked if she could please give me a room. Although it was now only 20 minutes before check-in time, she still said there was nothing available because it was a Sunday. I sat on a couch in the lobby and proptly fell asleep for 45 minutes until a room was available. Of the 60+ rooms at this hotel, I find it inconceivable there wasn't one ready 20 minutes before check-in time. The next morning, I asked to speak with the hotel general manager about my experience the previous day. When the receptionist called the manager on the phone and told her someone wanted to speak with her about a complaint, the manager said she was too busy. I personally will never stay at this hotel again.

title: Debra McCarthy
text: We had a brilliant time here. The service was very good and the staff very friendly and helpful. We really enjoyed our stay here. The hotel is within easy reach of all main London attractions but was also very peaceful and quiet. We will definitely stay here again.

title: Welcome break
text: Great place to stay,the location is ideal for visiting various attractions in London,the hotel rooms are luxury ,the staff are incredibly friendly and helpful,nothing is too much trouble,the breakfast and evening meals were lovely,will not hesitate to use this hotel in the future.

title: London 2016
text: Excellent location, very good service. An ideal solution to stay in London because the hotel is near to two underground stations and one rail station. Near to Thames and Tower Bridgem is also goodfor a foot trips

title: This hotel is awesome there is no more words that would describe this hotel the best I’ve ever stopped in.
text: You won’t be disappointed with this hotel the room was clean and really comfortable. The food was fabulous and I’m normally a Sunday dinner person but I choose the burger and chips and there’s not many words that would discribe the food apart from awesome.

title: The best breakfast I've ever eaten...
text: Beatifull hotel, beautiful rooms and the best breakfast I've ever eaten... They have evan a pub with geat beers.. Hotel is close to the Tower Bridge, the Tower of London, the Aldgate and Tower Hill metro stations and St. Katharines doc...

title: An English hotel of distinction
text: A hotel of distinction particularly as regard to service -- the staff across the board was attentive, generous, interested in being hospitable and professional. The hotel excels in its accommodations, its service, its location near two Underground stations. On a scale of 1-5, I give it a 10.

title: London weekend
text: Friendly welcome helpful throughout stay clean and comfortable bedroom with complimentary water and beer clean and well equipped room with everything you need including a coffe machine nice bathroom with lovely shower

title: Awesome location, great rooms and wonderful staff.
text: We checked into the Chamberlain this week after a long flight from Australia. We caught the train from Heathrow to Aldgate station with two changes, but it was quite easy. We checked in before check in time with ease, the staff were extremely welcoming and explained everything thoroughly. Our room was lovely, oversized fluffy white towels, a very comfortable bed, complimentary sparkling water, beer, tea, coffee etc. A phone to use during our stay which proved very handy for Maps etc when out exploring. We had dinner the first night downstairs in the gorgeous Pub and can honestly say it has been the best meal we have had on our trip thus far. We actually regretted trying other local eateries, they were not bad by any means but The Chamberlain set the bench mark way too high. Breakfast was awesome, spoilt for choice and the nice touch of table service as opposed to your standard buffet was a lovely touch. The location was perfect with three stations all within a stones throw and the Tower Bridge, London Tower, The Shard and and Themes just down the road. I cannot recommend this hotel enough and would definitely stay there again. Thank you to the staff and management for making us feel so welcome. Cheers Dave and Kez Aus.

title: British atmosphere in the heart of Tower Hill
text: There was a LOT of construction going on right outside the windows on the lot next door. The sound was a bit much at times. The hotel should have let us know ahead of time. Despite that, the food was great, very British, the atmosphere was more traditional, which is what we wanted (versus staying in a modern hotel chain that could be anywhere). The beds are small, but comfortable, the bathtub was nice, everything was clean.

title: Not a bad choice for Central London
text: Booked on a London hotel search engine and got a double room for £70 a night. Had considered the usual budget hotel chains, but decided on something a bit more upmarket, and what a good choice. Nice clean lobby, free internet access, and very friendly staff all either English, or speaking excellent English. Room quite small but very nicely furnished and spotless with cable tv, tea and coffee making facilities and air-con, a must for London in midsummer! Bathroom nice, powerful shower and a tv built into the tiles on the wall to be viewed whilst lazing in the bath.... Pity they didn't see fit to change the plastic toilet seat which had seen better days and bore an assortment of scratch marks from previous occupants. But that wasn't a major issue. Minories is a very quiet street, literally two mins walk from Tower Hill Station, bit out of the way of the West End clubs etc, but cheap in a cab, or better and cheaper on the N15 nightbus which runs every 15 mins. Breakfast (decent continental spread) included on weekends, but pricey at £12.95 on weekdays. Don't bother and amble into a nearby cafe for something cheaper. All in all, a very pleasant stay for the money and will go back for more... Dont pay more than £90-100 per double room per night. The advertised "rack rate" of £235 a night is a total joke. No way is it worth that kinda money.

title: Nice hotel in the city near the tower
text: Stay at the Chamberlain hotel if you want to feel a historic atmosphere. We liked it very much. The staff was very friendly and helpful, especially Christopher was very attentive. The hotel is near the Tower, and the tube station Aldgate is only 3 minutes away.

title: Good old British style, with the exact location
text: Great hotel. Extremely well located, precise size, clean, good food (for England), its own pub and a quiet borough. Very good rooms and room service. Excellent for business or family travels. London Tower, Tower Bridge, St. Catherine´s Docks and all the City of London are just a few blocks away. Superb.

title: Great location / Good food
text: Worth the money and a pub just downstairs with good food/breakfast. The internet was very fast and reliable so it did help me as I normally work on the go and that's an important point for most of the places I stay. I would definitely stay there again.

title: Excellent
text: Well maintained building, clean and great location for DLR and tube. Welcoming at check in. Room very spacious and quiet for central London. Good local places to eat and drink. Bar open late and good service.

title: Easy To Walk
text: Great location if you have business in the financial district. Good shower. No noice in the hotel. Great nights sleep. Breakfast was ok. Nice pub off the lobby. Thee are many restaurants and pubs close by. All busy when the business day ends.

title: Great staff
text: This is a very good pub/hotel in the centre of London offering great value and having very good staff. Thank you for a great stay to Chris, Tracey and all staff there. Very professional! Mark, Chesterfield

title: Awesome stay!
text: This hotel was wonderful. Because our room wasn't quite ready when we got there we were upgraded and given two free drinks at the bar. Our booking also included a discounted price for breakfast. I had their eggs Benedict twice! Poached eggs were perfect every time. We had great interactions with everyone. The quality of the room was lovely and the shower was the best! The quality of the toiletry products was very nice as well. The best I've had so far in a hotel. Their concierge services were pretty good. Chris especially was very helpful. All in all, I'd definitely stay at this place again. Plus the location is fabulous. Quiet neighborhood near pubs, metro, free ATM, and a short distance to Tower Bridge as well.

title: Free upgrade
text: Me and fiancé stayed for one night at the Chamberlain Hotel. Friendly receptionist on arrival who told us that we had a free upgrade to the suites on the top floor if we wanted, fantastic! The only problem was that the lift was out of order but lucky for us, we only had a small bag and there weren't many floors. When we got in to the room we were blown away, we had our own terrace with perfect views of the Gerkin building and Tower bridge, the bathroom was immaculate with lots of free goodies. The location was perfect as the Aldgate tube station was only 5 mins walk away, there were also plenty of shops and a couple of restaurants nearby. All in all we saved £200 with the free upgrade, the only bad thing was the lift not working.

title: Lovely hotel in a great location in east London!
text: Faultless in every way, we loved staying at the Chamberlain. We returned for another couple of days at the end of our Europe trip. We recommend it to anyone wanting a quality stay in London. Tower Bridge right around the corner.

title: Everything you want
text: Comfortable room, all the facilities you could want from a hotel room. The bathroom was clean with a walk-in shower and bath, the bed was comfortable and there was plenty of wardrobe space. Coffee Machine, free wifi and a comfortable bed!

title: Quality hotel
text: We stayed here for 2 nights the weekend before Christmas. The hotel is in a great location, just a few minutes from the tube. Our room was absolutely lovely with every comfort you would need. The hotel is clearly well cared for as everything is immaculate. Breakfast was relaxing and plentiful and served by happy smiling staff. Overall a great stay and would highly recommend !

title: The Chamberlain Hotel is the best I've stayed at in London
text: I am paraplegic and use a wheelchair for mobility. I am a professional (legal) and have stayed at this hotel for the last 7 years without a single complaint. I have never experienced such high level of care and attention from all staff members in any other 4 star hotel that I occassionally use when in London. The Management Team at The Chamberlain are in my opinion, exceptional, having a great depth of knowledge of the hospitality industry and are happy to do all they can to make my stay a pleasant one. I often stay more than 1 night and the room is beautifully decorated, always spotlessly clean, well stocked with coffee etc. well furnished and spacious enough for wheelchair maneouvrability. The bed has recently been renewed as part of a refurbishment programme, the linen is fresh, crisp and above all clean, and changed on a daily basis as are towels and face cloths in the en-suite bathroom. Ample toiletries are also provided as are bathrobes. The en-suite is not a wet room but is spacious enough for wheelchair maneouvrability. Free WiFi is also provided. I am impressed with the pleasing, restful atmosphere engendered by the bar staff as I am of the range of drinks available and equally so with the bar food which is of excellent quality, wide ranging and catering to most tastes. The Restaurant is of a higher standard

title: Go here if staying at Chamberlain hotel!
text: We were staying at the Chamberlain hotel and decided one evening to have dinner at their restaurant. The restaurant is very informal – you order at the kiosk and pick your food when it arrives. Yet it has a happy ambiance and felt inviting every time we went in & out of the hotel. Being vegetarians, we had soup of the day - carrot and leek, vegetarian linguini and quinoa salad. We enjoyed the meal but since we had eaten their entire vegetarian menu in one meal, there was no reason to go back. The servers at the bar/ counter are friendly.

title: Katarina
text: Hotel has very good services, hotel is located in center of town. The hotel is clear, the stuff is helpful. You can check in soon as usually. When you check out you can postpone your baggage safely in hotel until your time of departure.

title: Great location and service
text: As I was working in America Square in the morning (a one-minute walk away), I chose this hotel because of it's location.Check-in was easy

title: Perfect for business trip
text: There were all ironing stuff -big ironing table in the rooms. The pub is nice. Rooms are very clean and bed was very comfortable. Location is ver close to train stations and tour buses first stop. The tower bridge is 4-5 minutes to walk. There markets and cafes near by the hotel.

title: Great Hotel. Excellent location. Professional and friendly team to look after you.

Ironing board, iron and a room safe - all supplied as part of the price you pay to stay. The bar is fab and the choice of Fullers drinks is great. Probably the best tasting Pint of Fullers Pride I've ever had.

title: Good Location

title: Weekend stay
text: We had a lovely two night stay. Staff very friendly and accommodating. Rooms very comfortable and added bonus of fresh milk in the fridge. Very close to Tower Hill tube station so easy access to the cits

title: First Class.
text: Location, price, staff service, cleanliness, room, everything was fantastic. The hotel is attached to a pub and this too became part of our nightly routine as the last drink or two of the day. Everything was perfect. Definitely will be returning.

title: Good location but disappoi ting stay.
text: The hotel was in ideal location for the trip. Hotel seemed short staff as was restaurant. Had to wait at reception and gave up twice . No one ever answered phone. Came back at 2.30 pm having been out all day and room unmade and when I went down to ask for towels male member of reception staff brusque.Food in restaurant ok but beer not as expected.

title: Traditional English hotel, good value for such a central London location
text: This hotel was the venue for a family weekend get together - 9 adults and 8 kids. The staff were very accommodating and arranged for all our rooms on the same floor. The rooms were typically English, clean and comfortable, with enough space. Some of the twin rooms were actually massive - bigger than our luxury double. Breakfast was good - particularly the traditional full English, and the staff were attentive. We also had dinner in the restaurant on Saturday night. This was great value at £16.50 per head for 3 courses. As a big group, we had to pre order, but this worked really well, with smooth service and good quality grub. The hotel bar is also a Fullers pub so the atmosphere here was good. One complaint would be that the bar manager's attitude was a bit curt,but other than him, the other staff were very friendly. As residents we were able to stay in the bar til very late - around 1.30 am - which was a bonus. The location is perfect - just a 5 minute walk from the Tower of London, and 1 minute from the underground station. You're also only a 15 minute walk from Spitalfields. There hotel does not have its own car park but there is a NCP one a couple of minutes away, which was fairly inexpensive for the weekend, Overall, I'd recommend this hotel. It was really good value for money for a hotel right in the heart of London.

title: Charming Chamberlain
text: My husband and I stayed here for a long weekend. The location is perfect, easy access by both subway and bus. Nice and friendly staff, good room, spacious and Clean. Excellent breakfast and tasty food in the pub. Could recommend this lovely hotel to everybody.

title: excellent service and nice touches
text: This hotel exceeded my expectations.. Great reception, excellent service, nice extra touches in the room (complimentary drinks), decent toiletries and good bath towels. Very comfortable bed. nothing negative at all.

title: Good location
text: At £299 room only, this hotel felt very poor value for money.There was only one person on reception and she was taking a booking on the telephone which meant I waited for more than five minutes

title: Pricey albeit great experience
text: I stayed at this hotel for a day while my partner had the whole room to herself the the majority of the week. T'was a great place to unwind after a 14 hour flight and 2 hour Tube journey. Can't say the room price was very exciting but I can't fault all else for that matter. While not in central London, the location was pretty good considering the nearby Tube station, Tower of London and our fav Minories pub. Room-wise, thumbs up. It has a cozy feel and comes with a huge bed, bathtub, TV and free Wi-Fi. For service, nothing but positives from their full English breakfast, clean rooms, free Internet and printer at the lobby. Oh yea, and they store luggage if you check in early or check out with a need to put your junk somewhere. The biggest drawback is probably the cost but hey, this is London. Basically, it was almost the total opposite of a nearby hotel we stayed at subsequently :)

title: Home
text: There are those little things that made the difference.A warm welcome after hours of traveling,a small radio in our room and usb sockets.Also our room had free mini bar and an espresso machine. Bed and bathroom where the best !!!

title: Conference
text: I needed a hotel in london with a conference facility, I spoke to the Manager Christopher, who from the very outset was excellent. The Hotel was a perfect location, the staff couldn't have been more helpful and they made the visit for our group very smooth. We used the pub attached and had breakfast there. I would definitely use this Hotel again.

title: Comfortable and convenient
text: Comfortable and friendly hotel and in a convenient location for our purposes. Staff were friendly and helpful, food was good. Near to tube station and being more of a business area, it was quiet during our weekend stay. Would definitely recommend.

title: Not the best value for money
text: The location was OK for what we needed. The room was clean and had enough space but I've stayed in nicer places for less money! The breakfast service and availability could be vastly improved. Overall I would say it was disappointing.

title: Great location & great customer service
text: This was an awesome find at great price for London on Booking.com. The location was ideal. Easy access to three Tube stations and a short walk to the Tower of London. There is a great selection of nearby restaurants

title: Perfect
text: The hotel is well located near Towe Bridge and the City. Rooms very clean and with free commodities. English or continental breakfast, very good both. The restaurant is a very british pub with great variety of beers and wines

title: Pleasant stay
text: I was in London for a business trip and wanted someplace quiet, convenient, but with some food options around. Chamberlain is very close to 2 tube stations and walkable to many areas. Staff was very pleasant. Room was exceptionally clean, and the bathroom was wonderfully large! It was a bit noisier than some other London hotels I've tried, but nothing that kept me from sleeping well. Nice to have the morning newspaper.

title: Good value, great location
text: Comfy bed, good location, everything in the mini-bar was free, which was a nice touch. Would be very happy to stay again. Ate dinner in the restaurant - food was tasty (especially the Vietnamese chicken wings) and good value, and the service was good

title: A nice cosy hotel at perfect location
text: A beautiful hotel at perfect location! Room was very cosy, nice beds and friendly people. Two free beers in the room every day was a nice surprise. Hotel bar is very good with opening hours till 2am. Thank you!!

title: Like a family run hotel
text: We stayed at the Chamberlain for 2 nights with two other couples. This hotel is not one of the big chain types which can be very impersonal and very expensive. We arrived early just to drop our bags but our rooms were ready which was a bonus. The front desk chap (sorry I didn't catch your name) was very helpful and made us feel welcome. Our room was well appointed and had a contemporary feel. There was tea/coffee, biscuits and actual fresh milk in the fridge, along with TV, a good hairdryer ( for the ladies) and a safe. My only slight minus point was that there wasn't any drawer space. The breakfast is a must and can set you up for the day. The food is all cooked to order and there is continental also included. The girls in the dining room were lovely and really professional - a credit to the hotel. This hotel is near the main rail network and also the underground. If you are looking for an hotel that is welcoming, not too big and a nice friendly atmosphere - then this hotel is for you.

title: Good location, nice hotel
text: We stayed at this hotel for three nights in November, after booking our trip at Go-Today.com. I was surprised to find out it was an extended-stay hotel, with studio-apartment-like rooms. Our room was spacious, with a small sofa and kitchenette in addition to the bed. It was flawlessly clean and had some nice extras like a teakettle, a toaster, a DVD player, and a towel warmer in the bathroom. Other reviewers have commented that the hotel was a little tough to find, and I would agree. Street names in London can change block-by-block, so just keep your eyes peeled. Princes Square is a very short block and it just looks like an extension of Kensington Gardens Square, not a separate street. The breakfast at this hotel was good, plentiful, and in a nice bright greenhouse-type room. The hotel staff was very helpful and polite. The neighborhood was nice, with plenty of places to eat and a Tube station very close by. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Better than expected
text: I stayed in these apartments for 4 nights with my two teenaged children and was very happy overall. A slight hiccup on arrival when they put us in the wrong room was rapidly sorted out and we were moved to the correct room within minutes. We slept well and the one bedroom, one bathroom apartment was more than adequate for our needs during the trip. Well located, obliging staff, clean and quiet. The idiosyncracies of accessing our room on the fourth floor were a part of the fact that these are old buildings and no more than a minor inconvenience. Staying in any location sight unseen is a lottery and more than most in London, so I would not hesitate to recommend this venue to a friend.

title: Super family studio, excellent value
text: We stayed for one night while we took our two young boys to various sights in London. Very clean, comfortable accommodation perfect for a short stay. Very convenient to the West End and close to park in Kensington Gardens, children could have a play in the Princess Diana Memorial Playground. Walked to the Science museum across park, beautiful! Wide variety of shops and restaurants in Queensway which are open all hours so great when at 10.30 pm we realised we had no toothpaste. Had fantastic traditional english breakfast on Queensway with freshly squeezed orange juice for £6.00 per head. Highly recommend these apartments and will book again. Staff very helpful and cheerful too.

title: Beware of the small print
text: I booked for 2 nights through Agoda and paid in full. Just before we were due to travel I got an email from the hotel asking me to check in online and give my credit card details again so that they could take a £200 ‘safety deposit’. When I queried this as it was not allowed under Agoda’s terms and conditions they refused either to waive the deposit or give me a refund so I could book elsewhere. I have seen to many instances of hotels attempting to levy charges for things ‘missing from the minibar’ to pay this sort of deposit up front. If there is damage they should seek damages not just take your money and make you the one who has to sue them to get it back.

title: Nice place, great location
text: The location is great - in central london, bayswater train station is next door, hence accessing trains / tube is not an issue. Good market place around the hotel, with various eateries - makes life convenient. Rooms are good - but please ensure that you do not take rooms on ground / lower ground / basement floors - initially we were given a room in the basement - simply horrible. We got ourselves upgraded and got a room on 3rd floor which was nice. All in all was a comfortable stay - but not the kinds where you would want to go again!

title: Amazing hotel
text: The rooms were really big and clean. The receptionists were really helpful and nice. Didn’t add breakfast or the restaurant cause it’s an Asian one and we don’t really enjoy this type of things. The smoking area was great. Bathroom was spacious and well equipped. Very recommend. The location wasn’t amazing but it was close enough to the underground so it’s manageable

title: Good hotel
text: Good location, fair price and helpful staff. The breakfast is excellent. The apartment is clean and tidy, and the kitchenette is equipped with all the necessary things. We only do not like the bathroom because it is too small. I would recommend the hotel to anyone.

title: Friendly n helpful reception staff
text: Rooms n reception area nice n modern. Staff were very helpful recommending attractions for the kids. We checked into a one bedroom apt for six. Location is fantastic n near to eateries n transport points. Very happy check in. Low TH Room G25

title: Convenient for Family
text: Was in GPSA Dec 2011 with my family. We booked the 2 bedroom apt but could accomodate 6 people as there is a sofa bed within the living/dining room compartment. It was very compact unit but I do think that it was a very worthwhile experience. After some checking I had booked the unit via central-london-apartments.com as I believe it gave me the best rate for the period. The apartment also provide other services like booking of shows/theatre and transfers. Very efficient and clean but I believe the front desk personel should be more friendly and smile more..tired travellers like us will definitely appreciate it. We really appreciate the drop off luggage service provided as we reached the hotel mid morning. Another good service provided was the laundry services. I can't remember but for each apartment booked will get free laundy service for a limited kg of laundry. It was really worthwhile. I would recommend Muslim travellers to stay within the Bayswater area as there are some halal food stores nearby (Marble Arch area is also good for Muslim travellers as there are some grocery stores nearby, check out Zabihah.com). Being in this apt makes it accessible to 2 underground station ie Bayswater (blue and greenline) and Queensway (redline) and also the Big Bus Tour (hop on hop off sightseeing bus tour). These are all within walking distance.

title: My friend's property was missing after the cleaning
text: My friend and I spent 3 nights in this hotel in June. The knifes for cooking are not sharp enough to cut any fish or meat. And the worst thing is my friend's accessorise bag was missing after the cleaning. She left her bag, all make-up stuff on the dinning table before we went out and we asked for a cleaning service before leaving. When we came back, the accessorise bag was missing. We did find the whole flat and even phone the reception. They just give apologize and ask us to check the room again. We were quite unhappy with missing personal belongings during staying in this hotel. It never happened before when we stay in other hotels. Untrained staff are a big problem. It's totally a nightmare and we will ever never stay here again.

title: Excellent Apartments, Very Clean / Modern - Recommended”
text: Really enjoyed our stay at the Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments, the staff could not be more helpful and accommodating and the apartment was lovely and clean, it is a nice modern design with eveyhing you could ever need... I would highly recommend this accomodation!!! These apartments are of the highest quality. We didn't want to leave and cant wait to return!!

title: Good Value for Money
text: This property offers clean, modern, bare-bones accommodations that is a much better value than you would find at a comparable hotel. But it certainly does not offer either luxury or charm. Three of us stayed in a so-called triple apartment, and there was just enough space in a bedroom that wasn't much larger than the bed and a separate living room that was furnished with only a convertible sofa bed and a small dining table with three chairs. The sofa bed in bed mode filled the space. Limited clothes storage, but enough. A small kitchen alcove was adequate for light breakfast, coffee and snacks. Photos of rooms are misleading in that wide-angle lens distortion makes rooms appear larger than they are. Long walk down twisty corridors and stairs to get to rooms

title: Friendly Staff and good value for money!
text: It's an ideal location,you have two tube stations within minutes of walking distance, a good variety of good restaurants and shops. It ticks all the boxes that I look for a good hotel: friendly staff, clean rooms and excellent amenities. All in all, very good value for money.

title: Terrible. Don't stay here.
text: This is not a 4 star hotel. It's a 2-3 at best. Carpets are stained, lifts broken, safe didn't work, fire alarms keep going off and the worst beds I've ever slept in and they smelled like body odor. This place needs a scrub. Towels are like dish clothes and there was no aircon. Seriously. I've stayed in a few London hotels but nothing as bad as this for 120 pound a night. Find somewhere better. Only positive is the location.

title: Must read before staying here
text: This is maybe the 2nd review I've left in my life, but the experience here was so disastrous I have to share. I also saw these 4 star reviews on Tripadvisor and thought it should be good / at least ok. However there is no chance this is even close to a 2 star place. I stayed here with a family of 4 total, and had booked a larger room. We were not told there would be NO AC. Let me repeat, do not expect any AC here as a guarantee even over the summer. Once checked in, we were told all rooms without AC should have access to a fan and basic water cooler. We received ours on the last days of our stay, it was a constant struggle to get something this basic. Beyond this there were constant issues that rarely come up during travels (I'm on the road internationally traveling frequently throughout the year). Management tries to help but their hands are tied due to lack of actual things they can help with (not enough water coolers for whole hotel). I expect they will respond to this negatively and explain away, but I just want to share I spent ~$400 usd per night here to take my parents on a trip and it was by far the worst hotel experience I've had over many years. No amount of positive reviews here should convince you to stay here, I made that mistake bc of good location but I'm sure there are other hotels around here can't be that much more money (prob less), so learn from my mistake and avoid at all costs.

title: Great place to stay!
text: The Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments is a great place to stay and is located in a great area. Three of my friends, plus myself stayed in a single room. Our newly reburished room included two double beds and a kitchen that included everything we needed: bowls, silverware, microwave, stove top, etc. The room was spacious, enough for the four of us to stay comfortably. There is a Starbucks very close by, and many little shops (including nail salons- a big plus for us!) we were able to walk to everything, as the apartments are located right next to Hyde Park. Friendly & helpful staff. Clean rooms & lobby. Overall a good choice.

title: Family point of view
text: We stayed four nights in a one bedroom apartment, two adults and two small children. All in all I would say this hotel is of ok value (for London, that is), but with just a little attention to detail, would be even better. First what's great about it: Location. Could not ask for anything better. Nice neighborhood, very close to the tube (Bayswater & Queensway) and even closer to buses. Families with small children will love being next door to Hyde Park and especially the Princess Diana Memorial Playground (less than 10 min walk). Lots of restaurants, supermarkets etc right at hand. Staff. Everyone we came across was super friendly and helpful. Apartment. Very clean and nice, although small. Small bathroom with bath&shower, shampoo and bodywash provided. Coffee and tea replenished every day. We had a double bed and a sofa bead, both of which were fine, and a baby cot was brought in. Child friendly. Our children were welcomed with open arms. I think there were buggies to borrow also. (Not sure since we had our own.) Then the little things less than perfect: Apartment: In our small apartment, there were a lot of doors that were heavy and would slam shut with no way of keeping them open. This was difficult with our toddler and 4-year-old, as we were constantly worried of them being caught between the doors when going in and out. Kitchen: Quite amusingly, there was a kitchen with basic stuff for cooking (oven/microwave, hob, pots and pans), but then a lack of other such basics that would actually make cooking possible. Eg. spatula or such of any kind, any dish that you would actually put in the oven etc. There was washing-up liquid but nothing to do the dishes with (a brush or sponge), we ended up buying a dish washing brush. An inconvenience was also the fact that a fire alarm device was placed directly over the hob, which caused two false alarms while we were there (from apartments other than our own), one of which woke us up in the morning and scared the children. These things being said, I'm sure the staff would have been helpful with any complaints etc, we just didn't bother. Restaurants were so close and we could make our own breakfast that we probably wouldn't have cooked much anyway. We never tried the hotel breakfast but opted to have some in our room or in one of the nearby pubs (for almost half the price).

title: Great apartments for short or long term lets
text: I stayed here on my own for the first time in Sept 2010. I had a really nice apartment. Beautifully decorated with everything I needed. As I was on my own I didn't want to have to eat all my meals out so having the kitchen area was great. I had a separate lounge area to the bedroom so I could relax in the evening and have my dinner but I didn't have to put up with the smell of cooked food in the bed room. The apartments are in a great location near Bayswater and Queensway tube stations so you can get to the rest of London very easily. Hyde park is 5 min walk from the hotel. I liked it so much I went back with my friends in December as it was the perfect location for some Xmas shopping!

title: Grand Plaza Serviced Apartment
text: Great location - very close to Bayswater Village where all the food joints catering to many diverse palettes, supermarkets, Boots, pubs, banks are located. Easy to move around using public transportation as there are 3 subway lines (Central, District and Circle) as well as bus services to South Kensington, Oxford Street, Victoria etc. The rooms are spacious and clean, with comfortable beds for a good night’s rest. Staff are very friendly and go the extra mile to make your stay as comfortable as possible. Breakfast is good, with a great spread of continental buffet. If you love Malaysian cuisine, you can savour Nasi lemak and roti canai for breakfast too! Authentic Malaysian cuisine is also served for lunch and dinner at Selesa Restaurant, located in the hotel.

title: Poor service..racist to foreigner!
text: DO NOT BOOK WITH THEM! 1.Staff at the desk was very rude (Keith) and unhelpful. Poor service. second grade hospitality 2. Rooms are small, too warm and cant turn heating down. 3. Staff wasnt helpful. Travelled as family with small children. Had a few luggages with me. None of the staff offered to help. No porters were about to help. 4. Saw a few customer had their booking changed without notification. Staff were very rude in handling situation. Your money is better off with Travelodge!! Second grade service. They should resign all the staffs at the desk and give opportunity to the mass unemployed british citizen!

title: Big rooms a joy to stay
text: The studio apartments are really big. However the one bedroom apartments are great value. If you get upgraded (arrive later in the day for best chance) then you really get the space. I ended up in a two bedroom once with a massive kitchen and living room. Plenty of space to work at the desk, relax on the sofa and put a few beers in the fridge. Cooking options range from two rings to full size cooker. Khan's Indian restaurant is just around the corner (great Indian-even though no alcohol), Hyde Park a few blocks away as is a Tesco Metro, and Italians. Just behind Whitley's, which in its day was the Harrods of Paddington, a visit to the dual spiral staircase is a must. When in London and if the price drops to £100-120 or so I always stay here.

title: Big Disappointment
text: (Written on the 2nd of a 5-Night stay). Reasonably large apartment, big, bath tub, free Wi-fi, comfortable bed. These are the good points. As for the rest, nobody tells U that the 'free laundry service' doesn't operate from mid-afternood to Monday morning. If U want to cook, bring your own utensils (saucepan lid that doesn't fit, no tea-towels, insufficient cooking utensils). There is a 40 cm strip of sharp tacks leading into the kitchen area (supposed to keep the carpet in place) creating a serious injury/OH&S hazard. We were kept awake from after midnight on night one and 0345 by footsteps from above on the second. Guy at reception desk was particularly unhelpful with lots of pre-prepared excuses but no action ('can't be done now', 'footsteps are created by the security person', 'speak to the manager'). The hotel promises a fruit basket to guests writing an 'honest' review. I wonder whether it will be forthcoming. . .

title: It's nice
text: To my opinion this Hotel is nice. Wonderful beds, nice bathromm, a nice flatscreen and a beautifull kitchen. It's modern and you've got a lot of space. It's not the best hotels I have ever been but it is good if you are here for sightseeing. I recommend it.

title: Great Hotel!!! Will definitely stay here again!!
text: I stayed here in May and was pleasantly suprised. This hotel is very nice! Situated in a great area and the staff was very helpful in anything i asked. Rooms were like efficiency apartments and furnished with anything a traveler would need. Very clean and nicely decorated! It was only 500 ft from the nearest tube station as well! Loved walking around the neighborhood as it was situated in notting hill with many quaint restaurants and shops nearby. The reasonable price, cleanliness, proximity to the tube station and great restaurant and pubs, and helpfulness of the staff will definitley make me want to use this hotel again!

title: Gud place gud location
text: We stayed in the two room apt for 9 nights.. The service was fairly decent.. The location was excellent as it was a walk away from all local provision stores around plus nice restaurants and most importantly the park Kensinghton gardens as we were travelling with a baby. The reception staff was very helpful and the kitchen was well equipped for cooking.. There was service of the room done daily..the train station was also close by. Overall a gud place to stay if u R travelling with family

title: Nice ambience, recommended
text: Finding accommodation in London can indeed be a chore. Your hotel choice will have a large impact on the overall perception on your stay. It's always much nicer to return to a hotel room that is reasonably spacious (by London standards), centrally located and clean. The Somerset Bayswater was impressive by these standards. I paid £99 per night via otel.com which was a bit of a bargain. This was for a twin room with separate ensuite etc. Unlike many 'inexpensive' hotels in London the bathroom was quite modern and comfortable. Shampoos etc. were provided (not always the case in this city). There were many nice touches: free broadband internet via ethernet (more secure and less hassle than wireless), a nice little desk/work area, and a self-contained kitchen which was great for self-catering purposes. The housekeepers even washed up the dishes for me every day which was unexpected. The beds were comfortable enough. The location of this hotel is also very pleasant. It's a very short walk from Bayswater Station, which in itself seemed to be pretty much a large young-tourist area (tip: buy a 7 day Zone 1-2 tube ticket from Heathrow. The queues at Bayswater are extensive in the morning). There are a variety of restaurants, Tescos etc. very close to the hotel which make it a convenient location. Our room overlooked the Princes Gardens which was another nice touch: it was great to open the windows (even in Dec) and look out onto the relaxing vista. Some other good points: - luggage can be stored in the hotel for two weeks, even after you check out - some members of staff were very pleasant and helpful There were a few small problems but nothing that I haven't experienced elsewhere - i.e. giving us the incorrect room, room not ready, housekeeping knocking on my room before 9am, getting lost finding reception from my room etc. but I'm being overly picky here. In the end the experience was both comfortable and positive, and I will most likely stay there again next time I visit London if I can get the £99/night rate.
