title: Well What Can I Say
text: On arriving at the Grantley, we were showed to our room. It was very small and bathroom even smaller. The toilet being practically on top of the sink, no room to move. The shower was so slow wondered if it was ever going to work. The bed was lumpy and flat pillows with no extra ones if needed. The room was on the main road hence very noisy and single glazed windows, so no sleep the first night. The wall between rooms was so thin that every noise could be heard from the adjoining bathroom and I don't mean the pulling of the flush. On mentioning these things in the morning we were asked what did we want them to do about it (not what I call customer friendly). Yes it is close to the tube station but that is about all that can be said for it. The price you pay is not the quality you get. Somebody needs to take a long hard look at this hotel. At the end of the day not a pleasant experience.

title: My Home in London , i like it
text: i was there in last December 2016 , it was a very nice experience there. The hotel location is extremely nice , it is son near for everything i wanted . 2 minutes walking to the biggest shopping mall (West field mall ) , all transportation facilities were available , Bus station , underground station around the hotel . there is a good market for fruits & vegetables . also many souvenirs stores were there . the hotel staff are so kind & very helpful . Thanks a lot for all hotel staff . the breakfast was nice . i have enjoyed my short visit to London.

title: Just right for us
text: we arrived at the Grantly Hotel on saturday 7th sept to a very friendly welcome,my wife was due to have eye surgery at optical express on the sunday so it gave us time to settle in and find where we had to go,the staff told us where to go and told us many of there customers had used them for the same reason,if i had told them in advance they would have put us on the ground floor so my wife did not need to manage the stairs after her opperation,we went to westfield and changed her appointment which ment we needed to stay a extra night,that was no problem for the staff,we had forgot our phone charger once again no problem for the staff to help with providing us with one,we asked for extra pillows no problem they gave us them straight away. After we returned on sunday the staff where concerned that all was well and that my wife was ok after her surgery,i would also recomend the Italian next door for a good meal,the room was small but this was made up with it being very clean and sufficient for our needs so much so that we have booked next weekend there again for the other eye to be opperated on,this time a ground floor room as well look forward to our stay at the grantly hotel again.

title: Average
text: The Rooms at this property were very clean and tidy . The shower was ok and the toilet a bit cramped. The room was very small room . Breakfast was good - continental - which was served in the conservatory out back. Friendly staff .

title: Perfect.............
text: My wife and myself stayed at The Grantly on September 21st while attending a concert at the Shepherd's bush Empire. The location was superb for the venue. You could see it from the Hotel forecourt!. Next door to the venue was a welcoming "o'neil's" Irish Pub which serves pretty good food. The Hotel faces the green and is a short uncomplicated walk down from the tube station. Just cross the road and turn right. There are various convenience stores , a shopping centre and a couple of banks as you walk towards it. The Hotel has a small neat reception area, the staff were pleasant throughout our short stay. We had room 17. If you have trouble climbing stairs or are elderly it would be prudent to ask the staff for a lower floor room. The room itself was spotless, tv included and a modern well maintained shower and toilet room. All were very clean. The noise of traffic at night is minimal, the bed comfy and we both slept well. There is a key for your room and the front door included. The breakfast was continental and the staff were pleasant as they served us. Toast, boiled eggs and warm croissants with a selection of cheese and jams. There was also orange juice and breakfast cereal. Fine for a light breakfast. Tea and coffee too. Just across from the reception is a room where you can leave your luggage on your last day and return for it later. It seems quite secure. We checked out at 11 and returned at 6, no problems. I thanked the staff for a pleasant stay. I will use it again.

title: Not to repeat
text: If you dont have a electric jug clean dont leave it in the room. Terrible! dont offer your clients a dirt one with yellow water...Too much dust. A eiderdown makes a difference for such a cold city. The breakfast room was cold very cold.

title: One night stay
text: Very convenient, clean small room but adequate, comfy beds, lots of road noise all night not possible to leave the window open. Try to get a that does not overlook the green at it should be quieter. Breakfast a bit basic but not too bad. Value for money paid.

title: Weekend stay
text: Staff are very friendly and helpful i have stayed here a number of times now stayed in a triple room this time spacious and always clean ideal location for o2 Shepards Bush and Westfield shopping centre

title: Recommended
text: The hotel staff were friendly, the room was tiny but suitable for one night and was clean and comfortable. The inclusive continental breakfast was adequate. Would book again if we were attending another gig at The Empire as it is just across the road.

title: Great stay !
text: We stayed here for 1 night on 3rd March to attend a concert at the Empire. All communication by email was prompt and helpful. We needed 2 single beds and a double in one room and this was provided for us. I tried several hotels and they all said no, so it was a relief to find the Grantly so accommodating. On arrival we found the hotel beautifully clean and modern. The bathroom was like new. A continental breakfast was provided in a pretty conservatory the following morning. We ate at the pizzeria next door which was also very nice. Highly recommended.

title: Okay for a night or two
text: Short walk from Shepherd's Bush underground, overground, and railway station. Across the street from O2 Shepherd's Bush concert venue. Small (paid) car park in front of the hotel. Lots of stairs. Room size small and bathroom very very small. It's okay for a night or two.

title: Good location and family treat!
text: I used to live in the area where Grantly Hotel is located, and I booked it the first time for my family, to be narby me. They were so happy with the treat and also because of being so close to the Sheperds Bush tube station (2 minutes walking) which is in the Central line, one stop from Notting Hill. The breakfast is average, but very good. Depending on the room, it can be a bit noisy, but the four times we have been there after I left London, they have been very good.

title: stay somewhere else
text: on arrival, were informed we would have to pay for car parking, no previous information on this on their website, or when booking, our room was tiny, bed was tiny,everything was tired and dirty,no furnishings or bedding matched,

title: Good if you expect an experience in line with what you pay.
text: Close to the Tube, clean room, excellent wi-fi and friendly staff. Outside is plenty of small groceries and places to eat. On the other hand the room was too small (had difficulty to place my suitcase and bag). You can only seat on the bed (no desk or chair).

title: Don't Bother
text: The price might be enticing but trust me, its worth paying a bit more money to stay somewhere else. We had 3 nights in this hotel but and would of left after the first night if the hotels policy was not to pay upfront. We knew there would be no chance of a refund and had to stick it out. We had a double room which would just pass for a single occupancy room. The floor looked like i had not been hoovered in months. The bathroom floor and shower was covered in undesirables and the wall next to the bed looked like it had been sneezed on and not cleaned off (which i chose to clean myself using one of the hand towels provided). If you do decide to use the kettle open the lid to check it first. I had a horrible surprise when I opened it to fill. The front of the hotel is on a main road which has ambulances and police cars racing through 24/7 so don't expect much sleep. Unsurprisingly we didn't bother with the free breakfast The only positive to this hotel was its location.

title: Nice hotel for short stay in London
text: We (couple with son) stayed for three day at the Grantly Hotel. We arrived early in the morning. Friendly personnel helped us to leave our luggage at the hotel. Short (5 min) walk to nearest underground was the most important reason for this hotel. Rooms are smal but clean. Breakfast was well too. Price-performance ratio is OK.

title: Good stay at Grantly
text: We stayed at this hotel for 5 nights end of June 2014. Reception was courteous. We had booked a twin room and this is what we received. The room was on the small side but tidy. The bathroom was very small with an adequate sized shower. There was a small fridge for our liquids.We made due. Most rooms in Europe are small. This room is situated at the front of the hotel on a busy street. Wear ear plugs if you are a light sleeper. There are no lifts and the staircase is very narrow. Breakfast consists of cereals, toasts, croissants, cheese, jams, boiled eggs and coffee (instant) and tea. It suited us perfectly. Skipped the coffee and went to McDonalds for coffee. There are several restaurants nearby and the tube station (Shephard Bush) is a five minute walk. You are in center of London in 20 minutes.Lovely park across the street to relax. We enjoyed our stay here and rate it a fair 3.5 stars.

title: Unpleasant experience
text: I wasn't going to bother to waste my time writing a review until I glanced at the Grantley Hotel's website which is an affront to the truth and complete baloney. The banner headline for this hotel is a 'quality bed and breakfast'. Nonsense, you can attach no quality to this place whatsoever. It has been refurbished, yes, about fifteen years ago at a guess but tastefully converted - No! And as for giving you all you would expect from a "good quality Bed & Breakfast hotel, plus that little bit extra"… this is a joke. The only extra is that you have to pay for wi-fi (about £3/day). It is not free as advertised, which these days is outrageous. Furthermore, it was never a former mansion. It's a straightforward terraced London town house over four floors the type of which you will find all over London and which is most unsuitable for conversion into a hotel because this type of house is all stairs and half landings. The rooms are small and cramped and offer no comfort. I have stayed more than once at this establishment and none of the rooms were comfortable. The so-called en-suite bathroom is carved out of an already small room

title: Newcomer
text: First time going to the UK and we thought of getting a descent hotel to stay in because we will be staying most of the time outside so we have decided to get one near the tube station. Me and my family have a lot of itinerary already laid out and stayed for 9 days. We checked the location and it was the one we needed. The location was perfect for travelers especially when using the tube for it has multiple station both over and under. With regards to the room it was small but descent enough. Food stores are everywhere so no need to worry about running out of anything. The place is safe even late evening stroll. The hotel staff are very helpful especially Mr. Ealy ( hope I got his name correctly) who assisted us. Although the room since it was less space than usual, you can hear the neighboring room using the shower and the floor was traditionally made of wood. No big issue as long as you can a have a quiet night sleep which by the way was very deafening especially when late at night. Overall the experience was very satisfying and would definitely recommend this hotel if you are looking for a traditional feel hotel.

title: Cheap but good hotel
text: My son, his friend and myself stayed here for one night. Nice triple room with modern clean bathroom good shower. Staff were friendly and the breakfast was good. Close to everything. 3-4 minute walk to the nearest tube station. Great location, lovely cheap hotel.

title: Great place to stay
text: We booked the family room (no. 20) in this hotel and stayed there with 2 adults and 2 children. We really enjoyed our stay there. Big and clean room, with a fridge, shower and toilet, everything we needed. The room service as well as the breakfast was fantastic. The price is absolutely fair, great location near bus stops and tube station. We have never had such a great time in London before. Thank you very much!

title: Lovely stay
text: I stayed here with two friends on Saturday 7th September. We found the hotel easily and it was just a five minute walk from the Shepherd's Bush underground.We were given a friendly welcome and the room was ready for us.We stayed in a family room with a double and two singles beds. It was well appointed and plenty big enough for us.It was also very clean. It had a very attractive shower room with a powerful shower .The breakfast was plentiful and we were served hot croissants also the coffee was good. The journey from the West End took only 15 minutes on the central line so it was a quick and easy and very convenient.I would certainly stay again and would recommend it.

title: Very good value for London
text: Stayed for four days. Room was small - it is London - and I was out most of the day. Just needed a clean place to sleep. Refurbished bathroom very "tight" with the new shower stall. Excellent wi-fi reception ! TV reception - not so good. Continental breakfast worked for me. Very pleasant and friendly staff. Close to underground and bus stops. A great tourist base. Will stay here the next time I am in the city.

title: Good, No-Frills, Budget Accommodation
text: I booked this hotel based on price and location - at under £50 per night I was expecting a very basic hotel and that is what I got. The rooms are very small - I was given a double as the single I had booked was not available - the room was just big enough to fit a double bed in - there was no space for a bedside table and one side of the bed was tright up against the wall. Obviously this wasn't a problem for me but for a couple this might have presented problems! Storage consisted of a single, narrow wardrobe (mine contained an old phone!) I was only staying for one ight so was travelling very light - i f youhad a suitcase you would struggle to find space for it. The room was very basic - just the bed, a tablewith an elderly tv on it, kettle on the floor and that was in. The ensuite was tiny. My room was at the front and had a view over Shepherds Bush Market. Breakfast (hich is served in a conservatory/kitchen at the rear of the hotel) was cereal, toast and (if desired) a boiled egg. Not exciting, but perfectly adequate and there are lots of cafes in the area if you want something more substantial. The hotel offers WiFi for an extra £3 per night - this is extremely patchy - I found that the signal was constantly being lost and was very very slow - if it had been free then so be it, but not the quality you expect if you're being charged extra! BE AWARE - this hotel wants paying in CASHon arrival - there is a hefty surcharge if you want to pay by card. (I was abble to pay on check out, as I pointed out that this was what by booking confirmation said ) The hotel is very much a budget option - it's in a convernted house, there are no lifts, some of the rooms are in the basement and some up 3 flights of stairs. The entrance itself is up a short flight of steps and you have togo downstairs for breakfast, so if you have mobility probelsm check with the hotel what assistance is available, before booking. I found the room to be very hot (as it is on a main road, leaving the window open isn't really an option) The en suite in the room I stayed in was rather grubby - the showerhead was coevered in limscale, the doors to the shower cubicle were broekn and didn't slide open properly and there was a crack in the shower tray. Good Points: The hotel was clean, conveniently located less than 10 walk from the tube station and close to Bush Hall (the venue I was attending) and very cheap. Bad Points: Reception seemed a bit cluelss. They tried to charge me a higher price than in my confirmation booking and tried to insist on cash upffront (again, contrary to my booking cofirmation, which said cards would be charged on chackout) The lock on my door was faulty and almost impossible to get open from the outside - On all but one occassion, I had to get the receptionst to come up to open it (and it took him about 5 minutes trying - very frustrating) WiFi is very slow & unreliable Towels were incredibly small - the 'bath' towel was the size of a hand-towel! All in all, however, given that the price is so low for a london hotel I felt the hotel was fine

title: Pretty Grim
text: I was looking forward to staying here as the reviews seemed okay and it looked nice from the photos. I arrived an hour after check in commenced, as i took my key off the man behing the desk he grabbed my arm and pulled it towards him to look at my tattoo, he then proceeded to tell me he will single, this left me feeling very uncomfortable especially as I was travelling on my own. I was then told my room hadn't been cleaned yet so had to wait around until it was cleaned. Well - it was the smallest room I've ever stayed in, this one had certainly not been included in their photos. The view from my room was overlooking someone's kitchen! The latch on the window was broken so I couldn't even close it, the 'bathroom' smelt of mould and at night, there was a gap all round the door so the light from the corridor shone in..I didn't even stay for breakfast...I won't be staying here again, that's for sure.

title: Great value for your money
text: The hotel is a 2-minute-walk from the O2 Shepherd's Bush Empire, where I went to a concert, so it was also the perfect location for me and served it's purpose perfectly

title: Very good value for money
text: I stayed at Grantly one night prior to an important meeting and was desperate for a quiet room to make preparations. I was given Rm 14, a delightful single that looks like it may have recently been converted from attic space. The room, although small, was larger than I had envisaged and ample for my needs, with a comfortable bed and solid desk next to a large window. A small set of stairs led to an cozy ensuite that had just been renovated (with the most upscale showerhead I'd seen in any hotel!) This is not a suitable space for those with difficulty navigating stairs, but it was a good enclave for my purposes. Also, the hotel offered a gratis breakfast service, which I wasn't expecting. Staff were very courteous and helpful. I had two difficulties that were both resolved with minimal hassle. The first was that I had booked through an online booking service (Agoda) and had pre-paid but this was not registered on the hotel records, so the clerk requested I pay again. I had arrived late and didn't want to make a bother at that time but then took it up with the manager the next morning. He explained that they had just started taking bookings from that service and they were still working out their systems. He refunded my redundant payment without question. The second difficulty was wifi access in my alcove room. I paid the £3 extra for wifi and couldn't get a signal in my room. This turned out to be a good thing as I then focused on my preparations! The manager refunded my money and explained that he was getting a signal booster so that problem would be sorted. I will definitely return.

title: Great location
text: Arrived late at night. Reception were very helpful.Room was clean and comfy. Breakfast was cooked to order . Location is perfect. Tube station is a 5 min walk and on the central line so you can get anywhere in london easily. A big Westfield shopping centre is next to tube station. Loved staying here.

title: Good Hotel for a gig but nothing else
text: Pro's: -Good location for Shepherds Bush Empire, its just over the road, with a good arm and a strong wind behind you its definately a stones throw away -Clean Rooms -Decent Price Cons: -Bathrooms are unbelievably tiny -Noise from sirens and traffic very loud in room, I'm a deep sleeper and it woke me a few times but didn't bother me too much but my girlfriend didnt get much sleep. -no customer service at all, I definitely don't need my hand holding or the over the top service you get at some hotels but without a lie, the only words that came out of any of the staffs mouths were 'yes' when i asked if the rooms was ready as we had arrived early, and 'thats £153'. nothing else, not even a 'here is your key, you're room is at the top of these stairs' or 'breakfast is served in the conservatory at the back between...' -Breakfast is just toast or cereal I wouldn't recommend this hotel for a sightseeing stay in London or for a visit of more than 1 night, but if I were to go to a gig at the Empire again and were just staying 1 night then I wouldn't bother looking at anywhere else to stay.

title: Family holiday
text: I spent a nice weekend with my family. Very close to the subway. Friendly and helpful staff. Rooms a bit small, but quite clear. The breakfast takes place in a building detached from the hotel, but quite calm and collected.

title: Brilliant!!
text: Hotel was welcoming on arrival, room was ready so no hanging around! Rooms were basic and presentable. Bathroom was spotless no nasty moulds or smells!! Not what I expected. Breakfast was toast and cereals couldnt fault it. A fab hotel near to 02 academy and Subway and Vue cinema and lots of shops!!! A very pleasant stay!!! Will be coming back....

title: My resident hotel in London
text: Great place to be ,great staff very nice , big clean room , i was with my family very comfortable and silent , breakfast was good and close to the tube center line and Westfield shopping center... So my next time in London defiantly ill be there again

title: Great location for O2 Shepherd's Bush Empire
text: Very close to the O2 Shepherd's Bush Empire. Close to Westfield Shopping Centre and tube stations. Small parking area in front of the hotel. Lots of stairs, so if mobility impaired this isn't for you. Breakfast is limited but good, served in a conservatory down two flights of stairs. Rooms are not large, but okay. Would stay here again if attending an event at the Empire. Might not want to use as a base for a longer stay in London.

title: Mixed feelings. Nice staff. Horrible bed
text: I visited this hotel with no great expectations because of the low price. A stones throw away from Shepherds Bush Empire. Very friendly and accommodating staff. Could not fault customer service. The room was small and pokey. Very clean though. The bed was the worst I have ever slept in. The cotton sheets were rough. Blankets not quilts and the lumpyest bed ever. Worst nights sleep I have had in a hotel.

title: Disappointing
text: The room/bathroom were very small which we didn't mind because we were only staying 3 nights. There is a hairdryer fitted to the wall in the bathroom which has to be turned up to maximum to get the full effect but the handle overheats to the point where you can't hold it. The bathroom had obviously recently been half re-tiled (in the shower unit). The tiles outside the shower unit were still the old tiles and where fittings had been changed, they were still dirty and had marks from old fittings. On arrival back at the hotel on the last night after it had been a very cold day, the heating had been turned off. My husband went downstairs to tell the guy on reception to be told "the heating is on!" but he said he would look into it. After half an hour I went down to be told there was nothing wrong with the heating but he did come back up to the room with me. Long story short it turned out there was no heating in any of the rooms on that floor for some reason. They did offer to change our room but as it was very late and we were very tired we declined so he said he would come back up with a heater which he didn't!

title: Ok.
text: This place was ok, no more no less. Its cheap and in a good central location for transport, parks and museums. Westfield shopping center with all its shops and restaurants is a short walk away. You get what you pay for. This place holds no luxury, but it serves as a place to rest your head. You won't walk away feeling spoiled, but it works for one or two nights. It could be cleaner and it has no lift. Breakfast is simple and of the cereal, Tea and toast variety. The breakfast host did offer warm croissants, though!

title: Worst Hotel
text: I have stayed in this hotel for a night. it was worst hotel i have ever stayed. when i made my reservation i have asked for a quieter room. The room i have got was very noisy ventilator in the bathroom was on and can not be turn it off. I talked to the reception she said someone coming to tuned it off but no one came when i go to reception to check if someone coming she was left and there was a guy who pretend does not know anything. Anyway he transfer to me a double room but facing the road. The road is very busy and i could not sleep all night even an hour. Breakfast is very basic and staff does not seem know what they doing.I know it is a budget hotel and i was not expecting much i have stayed in budget hotel before but this one was a nightmare.Truly,I do not recommend anyone to stay there

title: An experience!
text: The hotel is well located for the Westfield & Shepherds Bush, I was allocated a single room in the top floor, mouldy windows, lots of condensation, burns in the carpet... Wasn't great at all. The bed covers consisted of leopard print fleece throws covered by Chinz bedspread. Breakfast was ok, boiled eggs, toast & a selection of cereals & pastry. In need of a serious revamp.

title: Smelly and unclean
text: Very disappointed in the hotel. The bathroom smelt of faeces, even though ni one had even set foot in there! The metal soap wrack in the shower had soap scum on and we had not used soap, and where it hung on the wall there was mould behind it. Breakfast was only toast and croissants, which was not clear on booking. It was handy location wise, but hard beds and sheets n one blanket too made it a bit fawlty towers for us. Also the inside of the bathroom cabinet was revolting.

title: Thumbs up on Location Accessibility - saves time, $ & hassle-free!
text: Given London's unpredictable underground service, this hotel is ideal for those wanting a base that allows flexibility to other public transport and shopping. It's a short walk from the Shepherd's Bush underground and the Westfield Shopping Mall. For 'shopaholics', one can almost skip Oxford Street and the public transport cost to just shop at the Westfield! As I was stocking up on early Christmas gifts, I could make several trips to the Westfield and drop off the shopping within the same day, without spending extra on transportation, even on the day I was supposed to fly off home! The reception staff was helpful and accommodating and the included continental breakfast was good. The impressive thing about this hotel is their staff do stay employed at this hotel, thus allowing repeat guests like myself to experience the familiarity (this is my 4th stay at the hotel). The only improvement that I would suggest for the hotel management is to install hooks in the rooms and their toilets for hanging up coats and clothes, respectively. In addition, it'll be worthwhile considering having family rooms for 4 or more as I would consider staying there if my family should travel with me in the future! Currently, the room sizes are small and compact, just good enough for sleeping, but not much else. The toilets are also smallish.

title: Recent stay for Marc Bolan concert
text: This hotel is perfect for the Shepherd’s Bush Empire which you can see from the steps of the hotel as well as close to a tube station. On arrival full payment was requested, but most hotels swipe a card even if you dont pay at time. we had lower ground twin ensuit which was nice size for our stay and had flat screen TV room being below the road level didnt get any undue nosie from the main road. Breakfast was served between 8:30 in a lower ground floor conservatory and comprised of cereals, toast with preserves/cheeses and also croissants and boiled eggs. Both staff were friendly and asked if you wanted anything else. But no fully cooked breakfast but it is included in the price where as alot hotels charge for breakfast. Although websites does not mention parking i emailed and was told was available, there was space for four vehicles and was only 6 pound so worth ringing or emailing. if you want to take the car. The hotel has good wireless as long as your a bt customer. but not sure if they charge if your not. Hotel was clean and beds fine, towels provided but no soap or shower gel like you get some hotels.But cost of hotel for the location is great. The staff are friendly. You do have to leave your car key with receiption if your leaving car at the hotel when you go out.

title: Horrified
text: Stayed many times before, adequate budget hotel for short term stay, this occasion, Saturday 5th December I woke to find a bedbug heading my way. Here I am sat in work on Monday morning with red bedbug bites on both hands. I will not be staying there again until I hear they have had it fumigated and a clean bill of health is awarded. John Davis Plymouth UK

title: Nice place for a weekend
text: The accomodation is fairly basics but that's all part of the charm, Ideal if you're passing through on the way to somewhere else or you're only in town for a few days. Otherwise you would be better of looking elsewhere for a slightly more comfortable hotel.

title: Cheap and not particularly cheerful
text: A surprisingly good budget hotel. The room was small but it was clean and the bed - although firm - was very comfy for a one night stay. 5 minutes walk from the main Shepherds Bush tube station and about 10 to a huge Westfield shopping mall. It's not 5 star but it's good value for the price and I would definitely stay here again.

title: Close to Tube!
text: I stayed here with my 84 year old mother for 1 night, (was supposed to be 2, but missed connecting flight) Great location in safe neighborhood. Park is right across the street. They put us on first floor since my mom used a walker. We had to leave to catch a flight, & it was raining & slippery out, with 4 suitcases a walker, and a frail Mother, I was worried about maneuvering our way back to airport! The owner saw us struggling & took us directly to nearest handicapped tube station & would not take any money!!! Much thanks for the ride!!! The breakfast was good, but down a steep flight of stairs. Yummy whole grain toast & Nutella! I wish we hadn't missed flight & could've stayed longer. My sister & her family are there now.... Staying 3 nights. Good value for the money, rooms are small, but that's the norm in Europe! Free WIFI!! Free BREAKFAST! They gave us ice, which is also hard to find in Europe. The shower head was hard to figure out, & the hair dryer blows! (No power, bring your own!)

title: Cheap clean room
text: The room and the bathroom were tiny but clean. I wouldn't want to spend anytime in the room apart from to sleep. If you need a cheap sleep with breakfast in that area, well this is for you. Looking for some comfort and quality, well, look somewhere else.

title: Great value for a night
text: My daughter and I stayed one night because the location was perfect for an event she was attending. Other positive points were the spotless room, good bed and breakfast (although the room can be crowded), good value and friendly staff. Although the negative points, tiny room and a lousy wifi, we had a good night sleep and probably would stay in this hotel again.

title: Very small room
text: Good location but very small room and bathroom .Room nr 23 ,there is no place to go in the bath,the TV does not work,there is no place to unload package,I felt as if I lived in a cabinet ,It was not comfortable,the wifi doesn't work

title: Great value - 3 bed
text: Clean reasonably priced. Good location. Internet (wifi 3 GBP/day) friendly staff. big room (3 bed) !!!

title: Amazing service, great location, fantastic staff
text: We stayed for five nights. The staff were incredibly helpful and kind. To me, that was such a treat in busy London. I really can't say enough about how helpful and kind they were. Room was clean nut SUPER tiny. Location was really good. Great park across hotel, metro and bus nearby. A huge mall within walking distance. Shopping and bars nearby. Breakfast was included and really good. Internet was ok but not the best connection on top floor. For the price we paid in London we were really happy. Would stay again. Lots of stairs to top floor room. We are a young couple so no worries for us but something to keep in mind for older travellers.

title: Dirty and noise - one to avoid
text: There are lots of hotels on Lexham Gardens. My advice is book with one of them and avoid this one. This was easily the worst hotel experience I've had in London for some time. The room was noisy - I could hear other guests in their rooms, as well as their plumbing, much of the night, the carpet was filthy and stained, the bathroom floor dirty, the shower was either boiling hot or freezing cold because the tap wasn't working properly, and the furniture basic and shabby. I've had alot better in London for the same price.

title: At least the price is not too high
text: First of all i would like to say that the staff was nice and helpful, the room, however, was far for from great, to be honest it was not even good. With a size of approximately 9 square meters there was not much room to walk, let alone store something, especially as this space was also filled with with a 1.40 by 2 meter bed. The bathroom was also small and the the shower was at most temid, producing a stunning two water drops per minute. We could hear the next door neigbours coughing and the upstairs neighbours moving. When walking through the hallway you could hear the television at every room in which people were watching tv, so the noise problem was probably not just in our room. The hotel itself is downright poor and in need of a fair amount of improvements. Then again the location is good

title: Waste of time dont book this Hotel
text: I am currently sitting in room 001 wends 24th and you see from the photograph that there is so called smoking party going on about 3 my away from the window, which is due to finish at 3am. Music is playing and a considerable level of people are coming and going. I have come to this Hotel after being at a concert at the Albert Hall and was up at 6am so I was looking forward for some sleep which is not going to happen I have complained to the staff and asked for a change of room but they are fully booked I have asked for them to arrange for an alternative hotel and they have refused. Saying that that the party is not part of there business and all they can do is ask them to be quiet which they have done but no one is taking any notice I am now looking for another room but at 1 am on Thursday morning not having any luck. I don't see how any business can rent a room to you knowing that this event was going on and not expect to get complaints. I will look for a full refund but probably won't get it. This is the worst travel and hotel experience I have ever had and it has ruined a gift from my family of a expensive concert ticket and a trip to London. DONT USE THIS HOTEL

title: Great location but very basic facilities
text: I stayed with a friend at 1 Lesham Gardens for four nights. The hotel has a great location

title: Okay
text: Glad that the hotel was close enough to the train station (Earl's Court Stop) to make it easy to get around town. Glad that we were very close to a Sainsburys so we could pop in and get easy breakfast snacks before our day out, and some evening snacks after our big day. The pictures make it look more chic and upscale than it is. The room was not as clean as I had expected, and our blinds did not close all the way. The WiFi was not very good either. If you are on a budget, then this place will do. Otherwise, spend a little bit more and get a bit more.

title: Good enough for one night
text: We stayed here for one night during the London Film & Comic Con (2 x adults and 1 x teenager) and this hotel is within comfortable walking distance of Earls Court Exhibition Centre (as long as you don't have lots of bags). We had a triple room consisting of one double bed and one single. The rooms are VERY small but that's probably normal for the standard of hotel. The room was tidy and clean (apart from a bit of peeling paintwork on the walls) and the en-suite bathroom was very clean. There was single wardrobe with about four coathangers in it and bedside drawers. Bath towels, handtowels and soap were supplied for three people and there was a kettle, mugs and sachets to make coffee with in the morning. The shower is an okay size but the water took ages to heat up, then ages to cool down again to get it to the right temperature. The rooms are quite stuffy in summer so the window needs to be kept open, resulting is quite a bit of traffic noise. The room we had also had no view, just a wall that came up about 3/4 of the way up the windows, allowing space (I assume) to get to the fire escape and a glimpse of sky. We didn't have much to do with staff apart from check in/check out but they were polite, if not overly friendly. We left very early in the morning so cannot vouch for breakfast, however the dinning room and lobby area looked very nice and cosy. This hotel is fine for a flying overnight visit but I wouldn't advise it for more than one night.

title: Not all bad
text: I have stayed in this hotel 3 times now, first under its previous owners when it really was a dump, then last year when it was taken over and again this year. The rooms are small but clean

title: Scary Place-No fire escapes.
text: My wife and I booked this place over the net as a basic type hotel to stay in last December when we visited London from Ireland for Christmas shopping.Cash had to be paid in full upon arrival without seeing our room.Foolishly we stumped up.Then we saw our room!! It was tiny and very basic,but we were content enough with it as we were not planning to hang around only to sleep there.It was in the basement which again was ok but when we investigated the fire exits we found they were welded and did not open.The only exit was back up a tiny wooden stairway.The place is a complete fire hazard and is a tragedy waiting to happen.Chinese guy on reception said there won't be a fire because we don't have a kitchen!!!Had to argue and threaten them with health and safety before we got our cash back.So my advice is don't even entertain the idea of going to this place.Dangerous and hazardous.Yeah you might save a few quid but not worth risking getting burned alive.Hope this helps.

title: More than I expected
text: I was staying on my own for 3 nights at the end of September, so to make my stay as cheap as possible i booked a single room with no breakfast. When i arrived i was given a large family room and also breakfast for the three days. The room was fine with a double and two singles and the bathroom was a good size and clean. The breakfast did not have a big choice but it did its job. Good location only 5 minutes from Earls Court. I would use again.

title: Where do I start...
text: The only reason I am writing this review is to make sure no one else books this hotel. The only good thing about it is the location! It really is great! Everything else is bad. The carpet through out the whole place needs to be ripped out ASAP. I wish I had taken pictures. There are spill stains and dirt all over it. Mold in the shower. The walls in the place are dirty with shoe marks everywhere. The elevator is as old as the building and I feared for my life every time I got in it. The rooms are small and everything is just so old. There was no table or a desk in our room, so we had to leave our backpacks on the floor and as I already said, the floor is disgusting. Save your money and go somewhere else!

title: 3 room changes
text: The hotel from Hell. I still can't believe what we experienced. My husband and I were in London for our 30th wedding anniversary and some American Football. I agree with the disappointed guess. The best part of the hotel was the location. Our complaints: Stay 8 nights, the first room a matchbox. It had kiddie pictures on the wall. 2nd room couldn't get to sleep until 4am because of the night club (Jojo) in the basement. I believe that after the night clubs closed, the owners stayed up until 4am to unwind and smoke Hookah. I think it was room 10. The TV in room !0 didn't work. The room would get overheated, therefore we had to open up the window . Stay out of that room, please . It doesn't has access to the elevator and in the basement. Finally, after the 6 nights, we complained again and was moved to an adequate room.The staff was respectful and most tried to accommodate us. As a returning back home present, the receptionist would not let us leave our bags in the lobby, unless we paid the hotel 3 dollars per bag, per hour. We had a late flight and wanted to take in more sights. He said that the rule had just started. I told him we had checked in before the rule started and therefore the rule shouldn't apply. So my husband and I took turns going out and "watching the bags". Since the hotel accommodations were so bad, we spent most of our time exploring London.

title: Cheap and very nice accomodation
text: Reading previous reviews I was unsure if to book my stay in this hotel. As the rate was cheap and the location was perfect I decided to give the hotel a chance. It was a happy decision. The room I've been allocated was big, clean and with a big flat tv. The staff is very helpful and nice. The lobby area is very beautiful and the entrance is adorned with beautiful flowers. I really ejoyed my stay at 1 Lexham Gardens Hotel. I strongly recomend it!

title: Simple, clean and good value
text: I stayed here for 4 nights in room 207. A clean, simple, restful room. Small but perfectly adequate shower/ sink/toilet. Reception and dining area in very good condition. Continental breakfast which was nice. Staff friendly, especially the blond girl in glasses on reception, she is a credit to the hotel. Great location, central london but not too noisy. Great value for money, would definately stay here again!

title: Great location, terrible shower
text: Friendly and helpfull staff. Location is perfect. One thing that was not good was the shower.....only one temperature....hot & burning and impossible to change! Breakfast was simple but okay. Price is good.

title: Great location and value for money
text: This hotel was very good for me. The staffs were very nice and friendly. The location is brilliant, you can walk to the National history museum and Harrods in just 10-15 minutes. The WiFi was available. However, if you want to use the internet, you need to pay for that.The room was clean and spacious enough for 2 persons. I stayed here for 2 nights and I would come back again. I'd recommend this hotel for someone that is looking for the good hotel with reasonable price in London.

title: You get what you pay for
text: We used husband's last 15 years of air miles to purchase a holiday for 3 nights for 5 of us. Having read the comment about the fire risks, I was terrified when the fire alarm went off at 4am, but I was pleasantly surprised when the evacuation went well, with fire escape(at least from the 4th floor) functional. Fortunately, false alarm.. The hotel is very well situated, meticulously clean, and the staff were pleasant. However this is a basic hotel. Our rooms were small though not unpleasant.Tea and cofee facilities, bathroom v.small, low pressure shower ("like an eye dropper" according to Australian guest - admittedly grumpy at being woken at 4am by false fire alarm). Don't miss the "10 Golden Rules" on the door- Stalinist rather than PC corporate! Breakfast feels pressured due to crowds of hungry fellow guests waiting for a free table. Tea, fruit juice, choice of 2 cereals, croissants and toast- but as much as you can eat, as long as you can continue to ignore the salivating onlookers. But hey, London is a very expensive place, This is not a rip off- you get what you pay for, and we would happily go again.

title: pleasantly suprised
text: After reading the reviews I was resigned to a terrible stay BUT was pleasantly suprised. The hotel has obviously just been renovated and was fresh and clean looking. The lobby was very classy and the rooms very tidy. Beds comfy, lovely fresh linen and plenty of space. The bathroom smelt awful and the window didnt do up, but those were minor compared to what we were expecting! For a budget hotel it was great. Great location, friendly staff and even breakfast provided. Will stay again.

title: Wedding anniversary
text: Thought I would drop you a line to say how disappointed my Wife and I was during our stay at The Lexham Gardens Hotel. The room was basic to say the least we booked a double and was given a family room with no towel rails or hooks, dirty toilet,pile of dust behind door and carpet in very poor condition. On arrival the receptionist was not at all welcoming and on our return later that night she completely ignored us when said goodnight. This spoilt the whole ambience of our stay which was part of our anniversary celebration. We would seriously consider not using or recommending Lexham Gardens Hotel again Yours John Wheeler 12 Drake Avenue Didcot Oxford OX11 0AD

title: basic but nice
text: The hotel itself was very nice and Staff were friendly. The room was clean and had everything we needed but was very small a bit more space would have been good. The breakfast was ok but limited. No full english!

title: Ok for the money
text: We stayed on Thursday in a 2nd floor room. We were visiting the Royal Albert Hall, so location was perfect. Room was very small and cramped, there were stains on the carpet, decor was dated but overall it was ok. Bed was comfortable and although the road was noisy, we slept ok. For the price, it was reasonable and the overall cleanliness was acceptable. Not luxurious by any means but what do people expect for such a value hotel in London.

title: Pretty Bad
text: I gave this an okay, but it is pretty close to terrible. As you approach the entrance, you are greeted with a red carpet and beautiful lanterns. As you enter, the interior paints a whole different picture. Unlike some of the other comments, we found our room clean (but bought disinfectant wipes and wiped down everything we could anyway, but found no dirt). It just felt dirty! The sheets were clean, but the shower was moldy and so was the shower curtain. (How much would it cost to buy a shower curtain? You can get one at the dollar store!) The sink was cracked. There were holes at the entrance and exit to the pipes in the bathroom and my mother and I right away plugged them with bunches of toilet paper to prevent any little critters entering in the middle of the night! (By the way, there was no sign of any little critters.) There was also a hole in the floor in the corner near our bed, which we plugged up too. The lampshades were all stained. How do you stain a lampshade? The TV was not plugged in and when we plugged it in we still did not get a picture because the cable wire was also disconnected. It consisted of 2 copper wires sticking out of the main wire! We finally did get a picture, but did not breath around it, just in case. The TV also had a big crack on the side of it. We got fresh towels everyday, they just didn't take the old ones out. So after 3 days, we had quite a stack of dirty towels sitting there. The breakfast was made fresh as you came in to eat. You got eggs the way you wanted them, hot toast, tea/coffee, cornflakes and juice. We found the breakfast very nice and the cutlery and dishes clean with no spots, which you can't say for the more upscale places. The hotel is situated between 2 tube stops and near a lot of restaurants and a Sainsburys (grocery store) which was open all night. A good place to get your lunch or dinner with sandwiches or a salad bar a lot cheaper than the restaurants. The hotel is in a good location, it's just a shame the place is such a let down. All in all, give this place a miss.

title: Pretty good and value for money
text: The photo's for this hotel on this site are outdated and doesn't do this hotel/Bed and breakfast any favours. The Shellbourne has recently been refurbished, so its really nice and clean when you stay there now. For recent photo's of this hotel check out - http://www.travelstay.com/pages/ShellbourneHotel.htm. I have read some reviews stating the rooms are small, but i have seen one room and stayed in another for one night and can honestly say they are spacious enough. There were three of us staying in one room with four single beds(cosy enough) and none of them were joined to save space and still we had enough room. The bathroom too, newly decorated and clean. Coffee and tea facilities in your room and a plasma tv. Breakfast is nothing special but it's there if you want a quick coffee/tea with toast, cereals and croissants etc. Location is a 10/15 minute taxi ride to main central London i.e Leicester Sq, this might be a hassle for those who want to be close to the main attractions but for me it wasn't a issue for one night celebrating my birthday. There is parking outside on the street outside the hotel which incidentally is free at weekends, again this was handy as we drove into Earls Court and left the car there then caught a taxi into the west end.

title: Excellent Location
text: Excellent location with varieties of pubs and restaurants nearby, underground station (Glouchester or Earl's Court), and it is conveniently on Piccadilly line which means you can take underground directly from airport to hotel. Fair price for breakfast, but I don't fancy eating the same thing again and again, it would be good if they can at least do scramble eggs, half boiled egg, sunny side up on rotation on daily basis. Considered it vegetarian as it does not provide bacon, ham or sausage.

title: Ideal if you only want a bed for the night
text: We stayed for two nights. Room was small but clean and functional albeit a little noisy being at the front. Bathroom small and you had to wait for the hot water to come through. Staff were friendly and breakfast was lovely. Overall you get what you pay for and it was ok for a base for us to explore London....If you want 'posh' then this might not be for you....

title: Below par
text: Although the cheapest hotel we could get near the area. It is in a good location with hotels and royal Albert hall around 10 minutes walk away. The tube stations stated on their website are not as close as stated and the service is shocking. Wouldn't recommend letting your dog eat breakfast there let alone your family. A full fry up consisting of miniature hot dogs, no bacon, burnt toast or bread (no in between) scrambled eggs, lack of beans, cold mushrooms and disgusting hash browns. Rooms were quaint but if rooms 1-10 prepare to be cooked alive. Heating on full power and no way to turn off. Walls with weird stains on (even walk you have to sleep next to) and the bathroom was so small that when you sat on the toilet your feet were in the shower tray! I've heard of multitasking but this was a joke! It was ideal for one night as long as you've had a tetanus jab beforehand! Reception staff were helpful but only after shouting at them in order for them to understand. You won't see me coming back anytime soon. ** if looking to book, spend £20 extra each night and go to the easy hotel across the road!**

title: great hotel
text: we had a great stay in the hotel, the price was fair,we had a quiet room, it was small but comfortable beds. the hotel is well located, close to museums and 7 minutes walking from a metro station. the staff were helpfull and the breakfast wasclassic european . enjoyed the stay.

title: For a short stay, it's ok.
text: Great location, within walking distance from the underground's Earl's Court station, on the same line that comes from Heathrow, so no transfers required with your luggage. The hotel looks nice from the outside, and the lobby and breakfast areas were cozy, like a large old home. One the other hand, the room was pretty awful, they gave me room 010 below the main floor, to get to it, it was a bit of a maze and felt like a "dungeon". Carpet on the stairs so worn that some steps were "fixed" with masking (painters) tape. The room was designed for a very slim person, nice bed, but it barely fit so it was difficult to move around it. The radiator heating was open so it was very hot. I managed to close it otherwise I would have baked there. Two settings, open (extremely hot) or closed, which got quite cool but made it comfortable to sleep. Luckily I could open a window, but could not leave it open since it faced a back alley and had no protection of any kind so I hoped that the area was safe since anyone could have easily climbed into the room, unseen. The bathroom recently renovated but I barely fit in the shower stall, and I'm not big (175 Lbs.) I kept hitting the water tap (faucet I should say) with my elbow and kept turning it to the scalding hot side, and trust me there's no place to run, so you have to be quick with your hands and freeze for a bit untill you found the "sweet" spot again.. The walls were paper thin, and could hear very clearly the couple staying next door... from their regular very early morning conversations to the other "noisier" activities, with every detail, and she wasn't even a screemer! Their WiFi did not reach the "dungeon" so I could not use it there. It was and ok price, and suitable for a teenager backpacking through Europe, or like me, that stayed over the weekend only to attend the ATP tennis finals.

title: Cheap and not so cheerful
text: Check in was fairly quick, Room 005.Bed was rubbish, uncomfortable and had a boingy spring, which loudly twanged on every movement. Bedding was clean. The bed was against a wall and there was not enough room to get around it on the open side.No resemblance to the photos on the website. There were 3 pillows for 2 of us. There were no surfaces to put anything on, one small drawer unit covered by a tray of tea, etc and the phone and a single wardrobe with 2 hangers.. There were no instructions/ numbers for the phone so I had to go in person to Reception to say there was no remote for the TV nor buttons on it. They sent someone very quickly who, after searching the room for it, did get us one from somewhere. The tap appeared to run out of water but the shower was ok! The carpet down to the basement rooms, where we were, was very worn on some of the edges and will need replacing very soon or it will be a trip hazard. Toiletries were plentiful and towels were clean and well presented. There was a small fan, no air-con. It was a reasonably clean, cheap basic place to lay our heads for one night only but I won't be going back. I got what I paid for, I guess.

title: Small but good value for money.
text: This small hotel is in a good location with very friendly and helpful staff. The rooms are very small but clean - and given the price, are great value for money! They don't have air con, and you should ask for one at the back if you are really bothered by noise - we slept with the window open and it was fine, but others mentioned the noise. Limited but fresh breakfast menu. A good hotel all round for the price!

title: Basic, but certainly does the job
text: We paid £65 per night (one) for a double room which is incredibly cheap for the location, and were pleasantly suprised by the facilities. The room was small, but clean and bright, and complimentary toiletries and tea/coffee were provided. The TV worked and the bed was comfortable, but the traffic was a bit of a nuisance - our room was street facing and the Cromwell Road is one of London's busiest thoroughfares so it wasn't the best night's sleep ever. They could do with double glazing! The 11am checkout was a much needed bonus. All in all I'd say it was good value for money and would stay there again.

title: Dirt, mice, and regret!
text: After I paid for a two night stay at this "hotel," I saw the terrible reviews here on Trip Advisor and thought my hubby and I could deal with such a brief stay. I can say that this was IN FACT the WORST hotel I have ever stayed IN MY LIFE. It started in the rickety elevator, whose light flickered every time you stepped on. When we walked into the tiny box of the room, we saw that there were dirt stains all over the rug, there was chipped paint with white spots across the walls. The bathroom didn't properly fit one person, and there was mold inside the cracks along wall tile in the shower. The comforter in the room was stained. I went to the front desk and asked if all the rooms were the same, and the man there said they were the same. On night number two, we are scratching in the dark in the room at 2am. This sound woke us out of our sleep. We turned on the light and a mouse was in our room, scavenging around in a pizza box that we had brought in earlier. Startled, the mouse jumped out of the box and in a hole located at the bottom of the radiator. From the outside of the building, and in the lobby/common area, the hotel looks very nice, but don't be deceived. We heard two other rooms didn't even have functioning showers.

title: Bed bugs and infected bites. Welcome to Lexham Gardens.
text: I work stay in London 3 nights a week , every week, and am used to staying in the cheaper style of hotel and not much shocks me! I was pretty impressed upon arrival. Nice Victorian Façade, lovely looking lounge area and dining room. Things took a dive the second I went to check in. The receptionist barely even looked at me, asked for my passport and glared suspiciously at it, gave me a room card and told me she needed a £5 deposit on the card. I stat I didn’t have any cash on me so she asked for my credit card, which again she started at without seemingly doing anything with it. So after this happy start I went to get in the lift where I waiting and nothing happened after pressing the button twice, so started up the stairs with my heavy case. As I say, I am used to cheap rooms so I wasn’t that troubled to find a very very small room up a set of internal stairs. The single bed was in the corner with a flat screen tv at the end of the bed on the wall. There was plentiful coffee and tea the cordless kettle did not seem to belong on its base, and wobbled, although it did work. The bathroom seemed to belong to an entirely more cheerful room, tiled and done out nicely with plenty of products and a couple of clean white towels. The outlook from the window was truly dismal. A large pipe ran along the window ledge providing a constant background noise of gurgling water. And then the real noise started. I had wondered what the locked cupboard door was for, and then when the high pitch whirring sound started and the clunk click of a heavy door. It transpires the works door to the lift is in my room. Oh crumbs I thought, but I had ear plugs with me and was knock out tired so thought it would all be ok. And indeed it was all ok, until about 12.30am when I awoke to a hot itchy feeling on my arm. I got out of bed and had a look. I had 3 small round red blobs a couple of inches up from my right wrist. I took a piriton and then started taking my bed apart to find out what had bitten me. My window was closed due to the big pipe noise so I knew nothing had come in. I knew then that it could only be one thing….. BED BUGS. As I could not find a creature to squash and present to reception I put the sheet back over the mattress and slept on the duvet cover on the floor. 6am the next morning my arm is livid itchy, and I am not a happy customer. But I need to get to work. That morning at work I phoned and spoke to a very helpful man on reception who said he would call out the pest people to have a look. Without prompting he said he would give me another room. Good stuff, I thought. Then I started worrying about all my clothes etc in the infested room, so asked him to move all my stuff too, and he agreed he would. Later on I worried that I would get to the hotel and none of the above would have happened and I would be sleeping with the bed bugs again. By this point my arm was up like a big pink balloon and throbbed like it had its own pulse. So I phoned again and spoke to the same young man, who volunteered that the pest control had been to the room and had put some “medicine” in the room. He also informed me that they had discovered one “adult” bed bug, in my bed. Shudder………….. Anyway, I couldn’t move hotels as this one was paid for so it was back to Lexham Gardens with my big fat red itchy hot arm. Upon arrival I see the hostess with the mostess from yesterday on reception again. I told her I was moving due to bed bugs in my previous room. She did not apologise or even look at me, just handed me a card for a room on the 4th floor and told me all my stuff had been moved. And, indeed it had, which was nice. So I ended up in a loft room with a radiator on full blast which I couldn’t switch off, a window that wouldn’t stay open so I had to lodge a mug in it, a bathroom with no blind at the window and work men outside it on the scaffolding so I had to put my suitcase in front of it, and a tv which only had shopping channels programmed into it (although this was rectified the next day). All that asides, I would still have stayed here every week because it’s so close to my work, fairly cheap, and room number two was big enough, there was plenty of tea coffee and bathroom products, plentiful hot water, and it was relatively quiet. Another plus was the breakfast, bread, cheese, jams, boiled eggs and beans, with a big basket of fruit. But, as I had to take time out of work to attend an urgent care centre for my inflamed arm and also either chuck out or boil my clothing I had with me once I got home I would never ever stay here again. It simply is not worth risking getting bitten, but worse still, taking the bugs home with you and getting an infestation in your house. It was a horrible experience which could have been a really winner with me. This isn’t a case of attention to detail, it’s an out and out health hazard.

title: good location, average hotel.
text: Just thought give a update of this hotel, stayed here on the 7th nov for the night while seeing the top gear live show. close to the earls court which was really good :) the hotel is nice overall, good reception area with lounge, nicely decorated. The room that stayed in had 2 double beds down in basement, couple of stairs to go down, room was tidy, clean(bed sheets had few marks on them), the tv was bad, reception not good, kept cutting out and skippin back to sky3 lol bathroom is tiny, everything is so close, sink,toliet and shower(shower was alrite tho) noise coming from chairs or tables moving upstairs at around 630am onwards, walls are thin, can hear peolple next door! Otherwise its a average hotel.

title: Compact but pleasantly furnished
text: This hotel is in central London, about 5 minutes walk from Earls Court and Gloucester Road tube stations. It’s just 30 metres from the busy Cromwell Road and as a result is noisy even with the window closed

title: Be careful! Credit card guarantee charged
text: This hotel has charged, on the same day of booking, the rooms. The reservation system is so deceiving that it changes the dates and then immediately it charges the credit card. Travel at your own risk.

title: Great location and lovely staff
text: We stayed here on two different occasions during a recent stay in London and couldn't have been happier with the rooms we stayed in during both stays. The double rooms were of usual hotel size but the extras that the hotel supplied were a very pleasant surprise. Complimentary bottles of water in the fridge & chocolate on the pillow at night as well as the usual good supply of toiletries made us feel well looked after. Breakfast in the dining room offered a lovely and sufficient selection of foods and staff were attentive in responding to any requests we had. The hotel is in a great location and in walking distance to Earls Court and Gloucester Rd tube stations and a lot of tourist sites. There is even a Starbucks in the hotel foyer. The front desk staff were always so warm and welcoming which made the stay even more special after having experienced unpleasantness at another London accommodation place earlier in our holiday. We know where we will be staying and where we will be recommending to others when we next holiday in London.

title: Charged for an extra room
text: Currently sitting in the lobby at lexham gardens hotel. Upon check-in, we were told we only had one room. We proceeded to show Tina, the receptionist, that we had reserved 2 rooms. She said she only had us down for one room. Then we showed her our bank statement where we were charged for 2 rooms. She continued to disagree saying they had only been paid for one room. This went on for about an hour from 11 pm to 12 pm when we had walked all day and were very tired. Finally, we paid for the second room again because she wasn't giving us any other option. She said in the morning, they would try to figure out how to refund us. This morning, we are on the phone with Expedia trying to figure out how to receive the refund for the extra room charge. Tina told us the manager would be here this morning but he isn't. It's been 30 minutes so far this morning with no luck and still on hold with Expedia. No complimentary breakfast or anything was provided for the hours they've had us wait and the extra $70 charge. They haven't been understanding or apologetic for the inconvenience they caused last night and this morning. The room itself wasn't so bad but the customer service is the poorest I've ever seen at a hotel. I'd recommend staying somewhere else.

title: Grand for your money
text: We stayed for three nights. We had a very late check in and a very early check out so we only had dealings with the night staff which were very friendly. We were asked to pay on arrvival without the offer to look at the room first, on seeing that it was clean enough we paid. The rooms could do with painting and the matresses replacing but over all the hotel was not that bad. the bathroom was very clean but I think that they could do with changing their laundry people, the towels and bed linen looked clean but just did not feel it. The TV was a nice addition to the room with many channels. The walls between the rooms were paperthin which lead to us being woken twice. We also recieved a wake up call at 3 in the morning that was meant for the room next door which was especially annoying since this was the night of our late check in. We only had the breakfast one of the days and it was nothing special at all.

title: Very Good For The Price
text: Was worried booking a hotel in London for £60 as usually this means an uncomfortable, dirty flea pit. Had no choice but to get a hotel due to having to be at Hammersmith IVF at 7am! Reception staff were very friendly and appearance of hotel from outside was very welcoming. Lift is small and a little claustrophobic but when you are on 4th floor and are asthmatic it is a better option than the stairs. Room was clean and big (we got the famliy room rather than the double we booked) - TV worked with all Freeview channels, wifi signal a little weak but better than 02's mobile signal, bathroom not big and shower had the very unusual problem of the hot water pressure being greater than the cold water which made having a shower challenging! no aircon - but at the price that was expected. The place wasn't spotless, the bed wasn't most comfortable, no aircon made it hot - but at the price it deserves 4/5. A good place to rest head cheaply in central London.

title: Disappointment
text: After 4 weeks in UK and Ireland this was the worst hotel and what I had dreaded unfortunately on my last night. The staff were indifferent, the lift was tiny, the room was tiny and the bathroom minuscule. The furnishings were old. At 2 in the morning someone had a shower leaving the door open and fan off so the smoke alarm went off for a minute or two. People were still evacuating banging doors long after the alarm was turned off. The room was hot so we had the window open not noticing the heater was on. The bed was against the wall and there was only just enough room to pull a suitcase past it. It wasn't even that close to the tube, a fair hike with a heavy suitcase, overnight bag and handbag ready for the flight home.

title: Sorley Disappointing
text: On arrival from the outside it looked like it needed a good lick of paint. inside and the reception area was well kept and made you think your first thought outside was a little harsh so you give the benefit of the doubt. Then you find your way to your room you open the door expecting a boutique room but no! miss matched furniture.. holes in the wall filled then not repainted.. the window blind broken unable to open and no curtains to keep the light out so you don't get much sleep but with the beds and the waifer thin pillows that have seen better days. after a full day of wondering around the sights of London you want to have a nice refreshing shower but then the shower!! the shower head alone must have years of god knows what on the head of it but you have no other option but use it... the bathroom it's self is beyond small.. the fixtures and fittings have seen better days.. If I could offer abit of advice is that 1 Lexham Gardens is in need of a complete refit or even some money spending on it RC

title: Black mold in both rooms we looked at!
text: My husband and I booked a room with Lexham Gardens at the last minute after our plans changed. We used the Booking app to book the room. When we got to the hotel, we had to pay for our 1-night stay up front. We were told we were in room #1, which was in the basement. The lift doesn't go to the basement, so we had to carry all of our luggage down a very steep and narrow flight of stairs. We almost tripped in the process, as the carpet was loose. The basement smelled musty and dank. When we got into our room, we had a hard time getting it to lock properly. The room was extremely bare in decor

title: Good value
text: I stayed two nights at the Shellbourne. I think the hotel is good value for money. I paid 30 pounds per night for a single room with ensuite facilities and the price also included continental breakfast which I thought was nice.You can buy your own food and drinks and use the fridge in the common room as well as helping yourself with tea and coffee there anytime.The location is excellent, the hotel is very close to two tube stations (Gloucester Road and Earl's Court) and to the lively area of Earl's court. At the same time, the road where it is situated is very quiet, a nice break from London's hustle and bustle.My room was clean and so was the bathroom.It might not be the most modern or fancy hotel ever, but I liked it and would certainly recommend it to those who search for a decent and still reasonably priced accomodation.

title: Great Location, good breakfast, shame about the cockroaches.
text: You can't really expect too much for £39 per night (single). Really uncomfortable beds, really noisy rooms (overlooking Cromwell rd), shower had no water pressure and was luke warm. Nice continental breakfast. 4 of our 5 rooms had an insect problem (what appeared to be small cockroaches). On the whole not great, certainly not for an extended stay (unless a budding entomologist).

title: 5 star service 3 star hotel
text: Very friendly staff, special requests seemed no problem. Room small but comfy you aren't doing London properly if you spend too much time in your room! Continental breakfast included eggs and beans. Great location near Earls Court and a short walk to Kensington Gardens and British Museum of Natural History.

title: Perfect little hotel
text: Great hotel for a couple nights break, we had a convention at the Olympia and it's around a 15minute walk. Rooms are small but you get bottled water, toiletries and a change of towels daily so cannot complain for the price we paid. We will return! Thank you.

title: Not that bad
text: Very interesting price, and good place to visit the city. But there was some little problem in the room, it was really hot in the room, and also the windows doesn't seem to be really closed, so, it was not really secured, but nothing happen so...

title: Nice staff but poor rooms
text: I stayed here before and had a nice room on the first floor. This time I got one in the basement (positively described by the receptionist as the ground floor). The carpets in the basement are dirty and stained and the walls need new paint. My room was tiny with very little room for my suitcase. The heating was not turned on when I came so I turned it on. Regulating the temperature was difficult, so I had the window open all the time / not so co2 friendly :-) The bed was big and nice and the sheets were clean. The carpet in the room needed to be changed. The bathroom was fine but as in many hotels in London the warm water is difficult to get running. I liked the staff / they are all very friendly- but the hotel needs a fix up. I will not stay again.

title: Not worth the money
text: I am a regular visitor to London and this is my first stay here. The carpets were torn and filthy and blinds were very dirty. Part of the ceiling was coming down, lots of mould in the shower - not somewhere I would return to at all. The only positive thing was the location.

title: Regular weekly stay from Feb '15 to July '15
text: I have had the privilege to have been a guest of this fine establishment during the week days from February 2015 to July 2015 whilst staying away from home and working in central London. I have been treated exceptionally well. Rooms have been very nice, clean and well furnished. Rates have been very good and the service received has been second to none. I have received very good customer service from Giorgio, Maulik and Bea. Giorgio has been very accommodating and constantly strived to meet my every request, always with a smile and can-do-attitude. When here always ask for Giorgio as he is highly professional and can ensure you have an excellent stay here. I look forward to my next visit as I now see Lexham gardens a home away from home.

title: Tiny room, tiny price
text: My wife and I stayed two nights bed and breakfast at £115, very cheap. The room was tiny and only just adequate. The window that opened on to a jont balcony with four orher rooms, did not close firmly which meant that whIlst locked, it was still very noisy. I thought my wife had opened it at one point it was sO noisy. We passed on breakfast because it looked so basic. Tea toast etc. hairdryer only available as collection from reception, nOte: collect the night before because they run out quickly. Double bed was lumpy. Probably wont stay here again unless on a very tight budget.

title: Very budget
text: The room was in the basement, through a maze of doors. It was the smallest little room and the bathroom was only for skinny people as it was the size of a matchbox. This room or accommodation would be fine for a single traveller, however my partner and I found it too small for over three days and checked into another hotel. If you're after budget not frills accommodation for one, is a Stella location of London this place ticks the boxes. It was clean and well serviced and staff were friendly. Breakfast was just plain and simple with again no frills.

title: small but clean, good location
text: I spent only one night at the Lexham Gardens hotel. As other reviewers have pointed out, it does feel a bit cramped, even though after reading other reviews I am fairly certain that room configurations vary quite a bit. My single room, while by no means large, was fairly comfortable, and the bathroom had a decent size. Again echoing what other reviewers have said, the big plus is the price and location, and the fact that the rooms are spotless. Indeed the staff was not particularly friendly but that didn't bother me much. One significant (for me) drawback was that wi-fi only works in the lounge next to the reception desk, which was disappointing.
