title: Not bad, Not bad
text: Well located hotel, very small room (as shown in the hotel photos) however it had everything required apart from the tea and coffee making facilities. Our only bug bear was the scorching hot radiator situated at the base of the bed very close to our feet which we could not turn off!! Subsequently we had to leave the window open for the entire night, meaning that we had a bit of a sleepless night due to the high level of traffic noise. Apart from this, we had a thoroughly enjoyable stay.

title: Would NOT reccommend
text: WOULD NOT recommend this hotel to anyone. We had a Family room and to say it felt dirty, was small, cramped and uncomfortable is an understatement. NOT AT ALL like the pictures show you. Open the room door and the armoire is in your face! A small double bed to the left (a half step away) and a hodge-podge of beds, actually 2 different style single beds and a dilapidated couch, three more steps in front of you. There was a narrow walkway to the left between the double bed and hodge-podge for bathroom access. These 3 "beds" were also blocking access to the window. There was NO MORE than 6 inches between the these "beds" and you had to crawl over each other to get in and out of one bed. The TV was not visible from 2 of the 4 "beds: and the only place for the noisy floor fan was in the walkway in front the armoire. The only nice thing about the room was the clean bathroom. Staff members were cold at best and seemed put out when asking for a couple more pillows. Never greeted us as we entered or left the hotel or asked how our stay was going. And when we asked for assistance in printing our airline boarding passes, we were nearly told no but after an awkward pause we were advised to e-mail the passes to them and they could try to print them. Turned out it was easier to go to a neighboring hotel where they were very happy to assist! And yes the neighboring hotel knew we were not staying with them

title: Week stay at Lexham gardens
text: Stayed at the hotel for seven nights with a friend for winter holiday. Hotel is close to Gloucester road underground station and walking distance from the Museum of Natural History, Science Museum and Victoria & Albert museum. The place was nice and room was clean although a bit small. Beds in our room were really bad, we could feel the springs through the mattress. Also the water pressure was really low so it made showering a bit annoying and slow.The staff was a bit passive and not so helpful when asking advice. Wifi was 2£ for 24hours and it was slow and didn't always work. Breakfast was really simple, eggs, beans, toast, cheese, cereal, coffee and tea. Would have been nicer if they had bacon and yogurt too. All in all a decent stay but wouldn't recommend if you planned to spend more time in the hotel room that just sleeping there.

title: An awful place to stay
text: During the last ten years I have stayed in various places all over England, both private homes as well as hotels. Without doubt Shellborune is the most terribel and awful place I have ever experienced. The room was dirty, I had to order the staff to clean the bathroom and there were holes in the wall (to the next room) that were mended with toilet paper. Even though £ 30 a night is cheap, one should expect a minimum level of cleanliness. My recommendation is to avoid this hotel and go for a private accommodation. There are plenty agencies in London that provide accommodation in private households.

title: Good spot, not bad place
text: Stayed for 2 nights while in London in July 2012. The hotel itself is ok and everything I needed and expected for the price. The room is small small small and the bathroom even smaller so if you are after comfort and a place to hang out instead of just a place to sleep and shower etc then you probably should look elsewhere. I am single bloke with no real expectations so it was ok for me for 2 nights but honestly I really don't think I will be back.

title: Really great hotel
text: I am not sure if other people stayed at same place as we did but my 7 year old daughter and I just spent a night at 1 Lexham gardens and loved it. It was great value, lovely room, big, clean, light and with plenty of tea and coffee. Flat screen TV and en suite bathroom. People in reception were very friendly and helpful and allowed us to leave our luggage all day even after we had checked out. We will definitely stay again and have already recommended it to a number of friends. Thank you Lexham gardens!

title: Great customer care
text: We booked into this hotel for 27th August and on arrival unfortunately were told that the hotel had experienced flooding in 9 rooms and that we had been relocated. This was a circumstance out the hotel's control but the staff did everything they could to relocate us. We ended up staying at a beautiful 4* boutique hotel down the road, the cost of which was incurred by Lexham Gardens as the fault was not our own. We had a lovely stay but will look forward to actually staying at lexham gardens next time!!

title: Better than expected
text: After reading rewievs from here I was a bit worried what kind of hotel this would be but luckily it was better than expected. Staff was friendly and helpful. Room was big enough for two and bathroom was working alright. Hot water from shower which was a bit small though. As women we would have had more places to hang out our clothes as there was only one carbord and just few hangers :( Some hooks on the walls would be really nice! Nice to have ketlle and cups and tea/coffee bags in the room. Breakfast was the same every five mornings we stayed there. Could do some changes every other day and boiled egss and fresh veggies maybe..Location was great, only 5-10 mins walk to Earls Court Station and 2 mins walk to nearest busstop. We slept well and did not hear any noice from other rooms or from the street. There is always some noice in the streets in a big city like London! I could go there again :)

title: Cheap but not shabby
text: We stayed here for 3 nights last week Tues-Fri and we were expecting quite a basic hotel for £216 but were surprised at the cleanliness of the place. It looks a little shabby on their website but the room we had was spotless and for the price the size was fine. Very small bathroom but for £72 a night in Kensington we were happy enough. If you have a room facing the road then it's a bit noisy but I use earplugs so didn't affect me. Really close to Gloucester Road tube with a Waitrose, Boots, Tesco and cash machine at the station. Only a ten minute walk to the Natural History Museum and the V&A. Took us 10 minutes to get in to the centre of London and only 30 minutes to get to Euston Station for our train home. Would stay here the next time I visit London.

title: Room Cancelled on arrival
text: Absolutely dismal and rude service. The room was cancelled on the day of arrival without any prior notice - essentially leaving me stranded and to sort out alternative accommodation. Stay far far away and book elsewhere or be disappointed.

title: London
text: Close to two tube stations so easy enough to get to. Grand old building on the outside but the room was a bit tired. All you can eat breakfast for £6.80 was substantial. Plenty of bars and restaurants within walking distance and easy to get to local sites of interest. I would stay here again.

title: Did what it said it would
text: #1 Lexham Gardens hotel is excellently located for the Natural History, V&A and Science Museums, which was why I chose it for my family of 4. The room was big enough and clean and the beds were comfy. Continental breakfast was fine and the lady at reception was polite and couteous. I thought the room rate was fair and I got exactly what I'd expect - good value, great location and a comfortable, clean room to rest the night between Museum visits.

title: Horrendous
text: Visited with my partner for a night and can safely say I will never be visiting again. To start with the carpets are stained and dirty with god knows what, the walls were also covered in stains and peeling paint with also what looked like human faeces smeared down the wall. The tv was hanging off the wall and had wires hanging down from it making it one of the many health hazards. The wall behind the bed where a headboard should have been was covered in dirty marks. The bathroom was uncleaned upon our arrival with hairs in the shower and sink. The wardrobe door was also non existent. There was no temperature control of any sort in the room and when we requested a fan they gave us a broken one which did not work. So we were left to sleep in the 24 degree heat meaning not only were we in a dirty room but we were now unable to sleep due to the temperature. There was also no hot water in the shower. Avoid at all costs.

title: SHOE BOX
text: This apartment stated that it was much bigger then it actually was, there was no room for our suitcase, no towel hooks, no hair dryer, the pillows were so flat. You could hear people in the next room talking, we were missing several blinds from the window which is on the front of the building, no bar fridge either. The ONLY benefit was the location. even on checkout the concierge was asleep on the job. Just very disappointing for the location and price.

title: It's been there for years and is a wonderful option on a budget...
text: I actually worked at the Lexham way back in 1990 as a travelling Australian, I got a live-in job as a porter there. It was my first job in London and lasted about 6 months. It was run by a couple called the Wilson's, I imagine that as they were becoming elderly back then, they might not be running it any longer... I'm glad to see the lift is still functioning, it is certainly beautiful and unique, if a bit wonky, even was back in the 90's so it's positively a legitimate antique by now. Regarding the rooms there, I saw them all as a porter of course, and I remember clearly that there were some great big lovely rooms and there were some REALLY teeny-tiny pokey rooms too. So good ones and s#1t ones. The hotel had rooms crammed in all over the place, and some them are very odd shapes indeed. So if some of the people posting here their reviews, do have unpleasant tales to tell, then I guess they maybe just got one of the handful of bad rooms in the place. Try asking for another room if they try to give you a teeny one... Don't be embarrassed to ask, NO-ONE likes those teeny-tiny rooms there.

title: Central hotel
text: The hotel has a great location, close to Earl's court tube station.The staff is very polite. The room however was extremely small and the mattress awful. Renovation is highly recommended and definitely change the mattress.

title: Cockroaches in the bathroom
text: My friend booked this hotel for us based on the deceiving photos. The room was in the basement, smelled horrible, was dirty with hair on the backboard and what looked to be a blood stain on the bed cover. There was no air-conditioning, the window blinds were filthy, and when I turned on the light to use the bathroom at night, a huge cockroach was crawling along the floor in the bathroom. This hotel was so disgusting that my friend's husband reported it to the health department primarily because of what appeared to be blood stains on the bed covers. DO NOT STAY IN THIS DISGUSTING HOTEL.

title: good location but thats where it ends!
text: rooms were ridiculously small - the towels provided were threadbare -the room was dirty and hot - vertical blinds were hanging down and filthy - carpet also stained - no hot water in the shower - the one window which is all the ventilation the room had would not stay up - I had to place the rubbish bin on the sill to keep it open - the mattress sagged in the middle - the paint on the walls peeling off - unfortunately had 2 nights there - could not wait to leave - would definitely recommend people stay away from this hotel!

title: In defence of the Shellbourne
text: When I got to this hotel, I must admit a was a bit scared of what I could find, after reading so many bad reviews in this site. But let me tell you: I've seen worse. True, the hotel is not the Ritz: the room was shabby, couple of lightbulbs gone off (though I admit we didn't ask they'd changed them), the wardrobe was far too basic and they don't take credit cards. But considering it was the cheapest thing we could find in London with private bathroom in the room (which many more-expensive budget hotels did not offer), it was clean, there was plenty of hot water anytime of the day, good heating, and while breakfast was not too varied (coffee/tea/milk, toast/butter/jam/cereals/cheese), it was buffeted so you could eat as much as you wanted. The staff was friendly and they also have a fridge and a microwave in the breakfast room in case you want to heat your own food. The walls may be thin - but not as thin as the ones of my own flat! The hotel's in a very nice neighbourhood, there are several restaurants and a Tesco nearby. It's closer to Gloucester Road tube station than Earl's Court. So if you don't mind mismatched tiles and dog-eared wallpaper, and you're travelling on a budget, I totally recommend the Shellbourne. We'd undoubtedly come back.

title: Pictures can be Deceiving
text: We booked the above hotel through Booking.com and upon our arrival hotel from outside was very appealing but once we saw the room we were shocked. We requested to move to another room which turned worst. The room was filthy hair on bed sheets dust around the walls bathroom dustbin contained garbage. We had no choice that evening but to leave this hotel and arrange for another hotel. Though the hotel refunded our funds but Booking.com did not bother to compensate us for all the grief of making arrangements for another hotel for five people so late in the evening. So please be aware read reviews on Trip Advisor prior to booking.

title: Great hotel
text: The hotel was clean and great value for the price. The staff were always super friendly and it was generally a great stay for me and my partner. Looking forward to my next London trip - Will definitely stay here again.

title: Worst hotel I have ever stayed in
text: We booked this hotel for a party of 18 going on a hen weekend, and because of the fantastic price didn`t have great expectations. We expected something clean but basic. We didn`t even get that! The hotel was a complete health and safety nightmare due to its building works! There was plaster coming off the walls, electric tools were left on the stair ways and the amount of dust was unbelievable!! Even if that hadn`t been going on the rooms were awful! They were dirty, full of graffit and too hot. Our room didn`t even have hot water or a shower curtain, and the toilet roll holder was made out of a bit of string! On one of the mornings I attempted to have a shower to find there was a massive beattle on the floor! The best thing about the hotel was that it made you want to get up early to either go sight seeing or shopping (anything to get out). This hotel deserves to be closed down and why it is still standing I will never understand!

title: Do not book this hotel!
text: What was good: The breakfast What was bad: There was a loss in our room discoverd when we were going to leave. The receptionist was totally untroubled but promised us that the General Manager should contact us. I had to write two emails and wait two days before the General Manager answered. He did not take the responsibility that we had expected. Don't book this hotel!

title: Do Not Stay Here
text: Like everybody else, I would strongly urge anybody to avoid this hotel at all costs. I stayed here for one night during the Olympics and had booked a single room. I had just checked in and was in my room when in walked another guest. They had allocated the room to two separate people. I was just glad I was in the room at the time or my belongings could easily have been stolen. We both went down to reception and the receptionist gave the other guest a different room. Neither of us received an apology for this. The room was tiny and hot and I could get the window to open. I then discovered that the TV didn't work so as I passed by reception on my way out to my event, I asked for it to be fixed. I returned to find that it had been fixed but didn't have any BBC channels. Any other time this would not have been a problem, however, it was "Super Saturday" of the Olympics and as I was alone I wasn't prepared to watch in a bar or pub. I went back down to reception to complain about this and was told the hotel was fully booked so I couldn't be moved to another room. I found the receptionist rude and completely unhelpful. She then told me they had a triple room available in the basement and she didn't know if the TV worked but I could try it. I moved there and luckily it did have a working TV with BBC1! However, the room was down a dirty, uneven staircase which would be totally unsuitable for anybody with walking difficulties or young children, especially as there was no lift. The room itself had a horrible smell, was really hot and had no window! It also would have been very cramped if three people were staying in there. The bathroom was also cramped although at least it was clean, unlike the rest of the room which looked like it had never seen a hoover. The walls were also really thin, I could hear everything in the room next door, and must have been underneath a corridor because I could hear doors banging and people walking up and down which kept me awake all night. I don't know what the breakfast was like, because I did not want to find out. I asked for my pre-paid breakfast to be refunded because I wanted to get out as soon as possible! If I could give this hotel even less than a terrible rating I would. I would never stay here again, but I refused to let it spoil an otherwise incredible trip to the Olympics. The only positive thing I have to say about the hotel was the location. It is within easy access of Earls Court and Earls Court tube station.

title: Run Down in Desperate Need of TLC
text: I stayed here recently and was told on arrival that breakfast was not included and would cost an extra £2.50 per day despite it saying on my booking confirmation that it was included. Breakfast was minimal and I would have been disappointed had I paid extra for it. I was given a basement room which was dirty, the carpet threadbare and heavily stained. The white bed sheets and bath towels were also very stained. Cracked tiles in the bathroom, dirty grout, no light bulbs, cracked window pane etc etc etc. Please don't book this hotel if you value your sleep, the location means that it is VERY noisy. Cost £150 for two nights and really wasn't worth it.

title: Remember what you're paying!
text: We found this hotel whilst looking for somewhere near Hyde Park, I was pleased with the hotel and the room itself, on arrival the reception area looks nicely decorated and the receptionist checked us in promptly, we had a room on the 3rd floor - theres a lift available. The room was ample sized, with an opening window (unlike premier inns etc.!) the beds were comfortable and the basket of towels, toiletries, water and a biscuit was a nice touch! the bathroom is small but not unusable! Glad to see the hotel uses initiative with the toilet roll too - you don't need a brand new roll for every customer! (but maybe that's just me). Tea and coffee making facilities too. TV. Small travel dryer in the room Would recommend and stay again - near to Earls Court tube station (approx 5 mins) and Gloucester Road tube station (approx. 10 mins) Also near a sainsburys local for any snacks etc.

title: Absolutely horrendous
text: If you want a place with bed bug friends then this is the place for you. Unfortunately for me and my boyfriend we don't like sharing our bed with bed bugs. We checked in 11.30pm Saturday 27th got up to the room which was tiny and got into bed, watched abit of telly only to find at 2.00am Sunday 28th morning that there were bed bugs.... we had a refund and have been walking around London only now (4.45am) managing to book a hotel for Sunday 28th night. Absolutely fuming and would definitely not recommend. Disgusting!!!!!

title: Never again worst hotel ever
text: We booked to stay here on sat 9 July hotel was more of a beds it there were 4 of us staying 1 double bed 2 singles. Plaster was coming of the walls , bathroom window was broke and wouldn't stay open, blinds and windows were dirty, no chains on blinds so light was coming through the big gaps. The Shower was so small you could just fit in it and couldn't regulate the temperature. Sink overflow we were dour teeth and all this brown hinge came out of overflow. Pipe connected to extracter fan was hanging down. I plugged my phone in and socket nearly came out of wall. Very noisy from other guests returning home no sleep. Breakfast all the food was cold I mentioned it to the waiter he had turned the heaters of on the food so beans eggs hash browns and scrambled eggs were cold hard boiled egg was undercooked and was raw . 200.00 a night was awful won't be staying again

title: Value for Money
text: This hotel does what it says on the tin - and it does it well!! we paid about £55 per night for a 4 night stay. We got friendly staff, pleasant lounge and breakfast area, a continental breakfast which was just fine, and a room that was fully appointed, but quite small. Staying in central London, the small room was not an issue, we slept in it!! There was too much to see and do in London rather than spend time in our room. If you want a large room there are plenty of hotels charging 3 times and more what we paid on this "budget" holiday The Location of this hotel was excellent, Earls Court - zone 1 - was nearest tube, a 5 minute walk, no more, and straight onto district & picadilly lines This Hotel was clean, service was good and friendly, and the location was superb!! The price was excellent value for money. will we use again? you bet we will!

title: Loved the Shellbourne Hotel
text: We were eight persons, 4 adults and 4 children, and we stayed at Shellbourne between de 14 of August until the 15th. We were quite pleased with the size of the rooms, who were very good with a lot of space. The hotel had been recently re-furnished with ikea furniture, the rooms and bathroom were very clean, we had cofee and tea in the room, every day at our disposal, they were very nice and professional in keeping our luggage on our last day, after our check-out, until the time we went to pick it up. 2 things they could improve: put some towel hangers in the bathroom and shower gel would be nice. The staff of the hotel, especcially the one that serves breakfast could be more friendly. Overwall it was a very nice stay.

title: More of a B&B than a hotel
text: We spent the night in this hotel as a stop over before flying out of Heathrow the following day. The rate was affordable although probably more expensive than recommended. I booked this through hotels.com and figured that anywhere in London can become "central" via the London Underground, the closest tube stop to the hotel is Earls Court. We arrived before check in and were able to leave our luggage whilst we explored London. Once we checked in we were given our hotel room on the 2nd floor however the elevator was broken. The bedroom was a B&B, not a hotel (even tho it fell under a hotel category). There was 1 double bed and 3 single beds, the bathroom was single glazing so was an ice box and the hotel had basic amenities with luxuries such as 24 hour wifi for £2 and a shuttle bus to Gatwick and Heathrow for a small fee which was perfect. This stay was good for 1 night, the price was affordable and I would probably stay here again depending on circumstances but it is not exactly what it seems via the website.

title: Thumbs down!
text: I have spent two nights here and the so called "standard single room" I was given, was terrible. The room was in the basement, to begin with. Not only there were no windows where I could see outside, but there was a terrible smell of humidity as well. I immediately rejected the room but according to the receptionist, she could have made a change only if I acted within two minutes of me seeing the room. Aside from this incident, in all fairness, the hotel is located 5-6 minutes walk to Glouchester subway station, which is about 1/2 hr subway ride to the center. There are a few restaurants, markets and convenient stotes nearby. Whoever is considering staying at this hotel, please make sure that you do not make your decision base on the exterior view or that at least you will not be staying in one of the basement rooms.

title: Scaring experience
text: I'm used to sleep everywhere, I usually do couchsurfing but I decided to go to London with my boyfriend and we wanted more intimancy. So, the hotel was the worst place to have it. The room was dirty, full of dust on the furnitures and hair on the sheets. The shower was with cold water and the walls were VERY thin. You pay for what you get, but you should have a minimum standard in cleaness!!!

title: $537.10 for a dismal room with no air conditioning
text: My family and I booked a room through Venere at this hotel in London. We read the hotel's website and expected a decent experience. The experience was completely the opposite. The lobby is shabby at best. The room was worse. The bare light bulb hanging from the ceiling in the middle of the room pretty much says it all.The bathroom needed updating. To top it off, the room had no air conditioning and London was in the middle of a terrible heat wave. We have stayed in hotels for less money in Italy, Spain, Canada and the U.S. and they all had air conditioning. It was already late in the evening, but we refused to stay. We found a fabulous room, in a Holiday Inn property, with air conditioning and a great breakfast for about $200.00 less. We cannot recommend this hotel at all. Look someplace else!

title: BEWARE OF THE SHELLBOURNE
text: After a long and tired search for accomodation, I came upon the Shellbourne hotel in Kensington, London which was advertising single rooms for thirty pounds - what a cheap price for what appeared to be a nice looking hotel. I went in - discovered the rooms were actually thirty-five pounds, still very reasonable I thought so I paid and took the key. I found the lift - which was very tiny and as I am claustrohobic that was an immediate concern, I fought my fear and went up, I iniatially picked the wrong room and was seriously concerned on how easy it was for me to use my key to enter it. I then found mine which was very tiny and the wall had obviously been kicked in. For a moment I contempted the affordability of the place versus how very unsafe I felt there - my safety concerns won and I decided to check out. The concierge first offered me an alternative room but I felt that this did not solve the problem, he then moved to show me a sign that stated that the hotel did not give refunds. I argued that I had merely been in the room a minute and that this was unreasonable - but he would not be swayed. So I left with the dubiousness of the place further confirmed in my mind. Is this reasonable behaviour?

title: Expensive for a lousy hotel
text: The hotel is in a generally beautiful neighborhood. The exterior is beautiful, as well as the lobby. Once you step out of the lobby and into the hall to catch the elevator, your dreams are shattered. Tiny, dated elevator that barely fits 2 people with luggage. Everything is very dated, the walls need new paint. Rooms are dingy. You only get one sheet on the bed, no comforter or duvet. There is no air conditioning in the rooms, you have to rely on a 12 inch fan and an open window. The rooms are also very small. I would never stay here again, nor recommend for anyone to stay. If their prices were lower, it would justify the condition of their rooms.

title: Budget hotel budget rooms budget cleanliness
text: We wanted a cheap hotel in central (ish) London, and if you can't afford better, this is what you get I suppose. The room was small but high ceilings, but there were no curtains in the room, only vertical blinds (office style), so there was no way of getting the room dark or particularly private. As the room was also very hot, you had to have the window open, hence the blinds blow around & let in light. The room had all usual amenities, kettle etc but the electrical sockets were poorly located (underneath a shelf) and were no where near a mirror, so drying hair was a bit of a pain. The shower room was compact but a great power shower. Good rating for the bathroom until you notice the cobwebs and dust hanging around the ceiling. Also no sink plug provided. Towels were very small. Breakfast was also particularly basic (buffet continental), with only basic cereal option or (cheap bread) toast. Staff generally friendly, but maids left dirty towels in the hallway near our room. Non smoking room requested, but had obviously previously had smokers in. Horrible smell of plug-in air freshners in all the hall ways. Overall, like I say, if you need budget accommodation in central London this is ok, but not up to the standard of a chain hotel.

title: Does what it says on the tin and good value
text: This is no hotel to shout about but it is a place to stay and is clean and doesn't cost much. The rooms are pretty basic and a bit crooked and the bathrooms small and the TV tiny, but good value for money and i found the staff friendly enough. I stayed here pretty much 3 weeks. And yes the lift is the slowest in the world !

title: A Bargain!
text: I'll defenitely back! 1 Lexham Gardens is a lovely cosy hotel in one of the nicest London areas, Kensington! The room was tidy, continental breakfast, the staff polite and helpful at any time. Comparing price-location-quality I would say A BARGAIN!!

title: nov. 13 2014
text: we always stay in this hotel, its very convenient easy access to all stores in High street as well as Kensington areas.Its clean good breakfast, pleasant people i would recommend this hotel.Its easy to find its near the train station as well as Heathrow airport in fact we are going to Gatwick and they were able to get us a private taxi to send us which we were able to pay cheaper than regular taxi.I still will stay in case i go back in London.

title: had a good stay,
text: room was basic and very small but clean. had TV, drinks making facilities and a free bottle of water. I could open the window to let a bit of fresh cold air in as I do not like a warm bedroom. Everything was clean which was important to me. Reception staff very friendly and helpful. Fairly quiet hotel right on Cromwell Road - really central.

title: Smallest rooms everywhere.
text: Front desk staff were useless. Rooms were so small that 2 of us could not fit in the double with our bags unless you want to climb over them. Our only option was to pay for a family room which cost us another $480 AUD for 4 nights. Beds were lumpy or hard. Pillows the same. Smallest shower. WIFI hardly worked at all and we were told it was because they were busy. Rubbish it didnt work no matter what time of day or night. Buffet breakfast was very small and average. I would never stay here unless you want to be in the smallest hotel room in the world. Only good thing is location but there are many other hotels but it is worth spending the extra cash.

title: Average hotel, Convenient location
text: Lexham garden hotel is conveniently located near the Gloucester road and Earl's court tube station, the bus station is also nearby, #74 bus heads toward central london. There's a sainsbury just around the corner which is open until midnight which is really helpful for buying snacks and whatnot. It's also easy to get to the hotel from Heathrow since the picadilly line stops at Earls court. Hotel: The hotel is very clean with spacious lobby for a 2 star hotel. The family room was very very spacious but the bathroom was on the small side. You can't properly change clothes inside because you'll keep bumping against something. Simple toiletries we're provided but we're simply just too small. The floors of the corridors creaked when you walked on it since the building is an old Victorian house, so do mind your step during late hours, we found that people in a hurry made the creaking sound so loud. There is no air conditioning in the room so you have to open the window, but i suggest that you request for a room not facing the street because if you have a street view and open the window for air, the noise from outside can get loud. Breakfast: It was okay but we would have liked to have more variety. It was the same thing everyday. Overall: I would stay here again, but preferably not in the summer months. =)

title: Terrible hotel
text: Booked this hotel for 1 night, receptionist was unprofessional and incredibly dismissive, instead engaging in chit chat with someone else while we were waiting to be checked in. The drainage in the shower didn't work which caused the bathroom to flood, leaving a rather unpleasant smell. There was no working A/C in the small rooms, which meant I checked out after 4 hours because I couldn't get any sleep. Avoid at all costs.

title: Be aware of cancellation polcy
text: Please be very aware of the canceelation policy as i just lost out of 400 euro after cancelling the booking!!!

title: 1 Lexham Gardens (Kensington&Chelsea)
text: I had a trip to London this March. I didn't reserve a room beforehand. So I was looking for a chip Hotel with good location from the center of London. I have watched a few Hotels in Kensington&Chelsea. In this region the Hotel Lexham was the most chip with very good location near 2 center underground lines. Reception could check in me immediately. So I decided to stay in this hotel. I had a room at the 4th floor. It was double room with 2 bads, small bathroom. There wasn't a refrigerator but there were tea and coffee with hot water. The room was clean but not so clean as you hope. There was a breakfast very morning with sandwiches and tea/coffee/orange juice. This is good Hotel, not expansive in central of London. Just to spend the night the hotel is ideal.

title: Cheap, clean, modern and good location
text: I took a night here during a 2 day trip to London to see the sights. I booked a single room (single bed with en-suite) for £36 The hotel from the outside is lovely, as is the reception/lobby etc. The room itself was small but all I needed really. En-Suite shower, toilet and sink (VERY small bathroom) all very clean and modern. Small TV on wall, small wardrobe and bedside table, again very clean and modern. To sum up the room was well worth £36 The downsides... Thin walls (can hear next door's TV very loud). Room may be too small for some. The hallways and their carpets are a bit scuffed from luggage being dragged around. The lift never works (steep stairs) Location - 10min walk from NHM and Science Museum, 15min walk from Harrods, 25min walk from Victoria station. I walked for the whole 2 days and saw every site imaginable. Overall - Room 7.5/10, Location 7.5/10, Staff 8/10 (pleasant enough) Would highly recommend for a solo traveler looking for a clean, modern, well located hotel as I would begrudge spending twice as much for a travelodge with a double bed.

title: Pros and Cons
text: Really good price, all staff I encountered were polite and helpful. The main body of the hostel kind of smells like an old peoples home but thankfully the rooms didn’t smell. HOWEVER, the rooms get REALLY hot in the evening, the heating can’t be turned off and I had the unfortunate experience of having ‘room mates’ who wouldn’t open the windows. The bathroom and rooms were clean and tidy. (You will need to bring a big padlock for the lockers). Wi-fi had great signal and once I’d cooled down it was a lovely stay. Originally put 3*s but that wasn’t the hostels fault, it was my companions so 4*s in general

title: Stear Clear of the Badger
text: Do Not Stay at the Barmy Badger! We to were fooled by untrue reviews. The renovations have not been done! The place is rundown and needs serious work. The bathrooms are dirty and small. The beds are uncomfortable and dirty the sheets are stained and have cigarette burns in them. Also we returned from a job interview one day and our room had been entered for bug spraying without our consent. They threw our stuff all over the floor NOT HAPPY! The breakfast is great if you enjoy expired milk and stale cornflakes! And the giant tubs of margarine and i think its meant to be strawberry jam are disgusting to say the least. Steer clear of the Badger.

title: Christmas at the Barmy
text: What an absolute pleasure to be at the Badger for Christmas holidays After a short walk from Earls court station was nice to be greeted by the always friendly reception staff my room was a 6 bed dorm with its own bathroom, The hostel had been decorated for Christmas and had a nice homely feel to it as with my last visit The location made getting to central London easy for going to the show i had booked and a last minuet bit of shopping, As we were all returning guests we had planned to spend this Christmas day together at the Badger with the amazing staff and management so our lunch was very special and all cooked by the other guests who were staying This was a special visit to my favorite hostel in London always welcoming,clean and very friendly see you all again soon

title: Not the fancy hostel you expect from the pictures
text: We booked a double room in this hostel after looking at the pictures in bookings. This is not the fancy hostel we were expecting, it is just as any other hostel in London. The bathrooms could definitely benefit from some maintenance. In the bathrooms/toilet it was freezing. The room was minuscule, not even a chair to rest you clothes on. On the plus side, sheets were clean and personnel kind. Still, I won’t be visiting again.

title: Great experience
text: I liked everything about staying there. Staff extremely helpful and nice, great location, clean and convinient. It is very closeby Earl's Court underground stop. I will go back and I will recommend it to all my friends.

title: Weekend stay
text: Stayed for LFCC in July, was looking for a good quality budget hotel/hostel that was close to the venue. Chose the Barmy Badger, not just because of the cost, but also because there was a choice of a room with my own shower. If you have the choice of room 6 take it. Also chosen because just on the door step, you are a short walk away from your choice of restaurants in Earls Court. A little walk away from the Olympia but that is not a problem, it's a very easy walk. Can't comment on the other amenities as didn't take advantage. Greeted by friendly guy on reception, when the heavens opened on the Friday, was giving people umbrellas for those wanting to venture out for something to eat Would I stay here again, yes

title: Great experienc
text: Booking a hostel is always a bit of a nerve-wracking thing because you are never quite sure if it is going to be clean, welcoming, in a good part of town, quality of the clientele, etc. Booking Barmy Badger Backpackers is a no-brainer--it is a **great** place to stay in London. Location is excellent, maybe a block and a half away from Earl's Court tube station. This is important if you are flying into/out of Heathrow--it's on the same REGULAR subway as Heathrow (not Heathrow Express--just the regular line). That means you can get here really easily if Heathrow is your airport. Aside from that, the area is teeming with high/middle/low end restaurants and shops and you are not far away at all from Kensington and more to the east. Super easy to get around from here. There is even a Santander bike stand (rental bikes) that you can use about a block away if you feel like braving the streets of London on bike. The hostel itself is located on a much quieter street than the main area of Earl's Court road. It was hot in London while we were there and had to leave the window open all night, but city noise was not any problem. Staff was super welcoming and friendly. The building and rooms are very clean. Bedding is basic, but clean and soft. Loved having a sink in our room so we could brush teeth, get water, etc. without having to trudge to the bathroom. All bathrooms are modern and never had a problem getting one when needed for showering or other. We stayed in a 2 person room--looked in a couple larger rooms and they seem comfortably laid out. Frankly, the last time we were in London, we stayed in a much more expensive hotel room that was about the same size as our hostel room, including a bathroom that was laid out like it was on an airliner. This was much more comfortable for a lot less money. The common kitchen is clean and large. Breakfast provided is bread and cereal, but you can of course buy whatever and cook (there's a Sainsbury grocery store right at the end of the block). People were very nice. We ended up having many of our breakfasts outside in their garden because the weather was so nice. All in all, you won't be disappointed in this hostel. Immigration officer at Heathrow actually cracked a smile when she saw what we wrote down as our "hotel" in London on the immigration form with a "are you sure that's an ok place?"-look on her face. Glad to say, after staying there, it is a **fantastic** place to stay in London.

title: Solo stay
text: Wonderful hostel with brilliant facilities and AMAZING location. Found all the staff incredibly friendly and helpful. One recommendation (4.5 *s) - for the breakfasts, it would be great to ensure that a communal non-dairy milk is always available, as well as some more fruit. Otherwise, a wonderful stay!

title: Excellent Visit
text: This was such a wonderful experience! Liz was so helpful and welcomed us warmly upon arrival. We stayed in the cutest room with our own shower and sink and we were right down the hall from the kitchen and bathroom. The garden is so beautiful and we had a great time hanging out. Liz was kind enough to give us some great recommendations. Best of all, we got to hang out with Tinker, Liz's dog, who hangs out at the hostel five days a week! We were sad not to stay longer and would highly recommend!

title: Amazing was an understatement!
text: This was my first hostel experience and it was the best.. from the amazing staff, to everything being exactly as described. If you are going to stay in London, this is the place to be! It was quiet, great roommates, superb wifi.. shops, bars, underground tram all real close.. I could go on and on. Go see it for yourself, you will not be disappointed.

title: Just Right.
text: Needed a bed for a night in London without needing to take a mortgage out. The Barmy Badger fit the bill very well. Excellent value for money especially when you consider breakfast cereals and tea and coffee are included. We did not expect the Hilton for what we were paying, but we were really pleased with the accommodation and the welcome we received. We would happy stay here again.

title: Good hostel for all day out kind of trip
text: The hostel is extremely well located, less than 5 minutes walk to ears court subway station, which is a key station because several lines go through it. There is supermarket right around the corner where you can buy cheap food and drinks, this can save you a lot o money, if if store the goods in the hostel refrigerator. Also, about 15 minutee walking to the natural histoty museum. I stayed in room 9, just 2 bed in there, there is sink in the room. This helps a lot. The bathroom/person ratio is good, only once in the 5 days I found all the bathroons occupied. If you are planning walking around the city all day, and want to save save money, this is z great option.

title: Brilliant cosy fun hostel
text: Such a great little hostel in a great location near Earls Court Station. The rooms were nice, the staff were wonderful, the kitchen and communal areas were great and I met some awesome people here. The only thing that annoyed me about this place (and im being very picky) is that there didn't seem to be a great bathroom to guest ratio, a lot of guests trying to use the bathroom at around the 7-9am time which is a very mild inconvenience. Overall, I'd happily stay here again. Oh and there's a dog! :)

title: Very good hostel!!
text: I stayed for 2 weeks and I highly recommend this place to anybody who plan to spend some time in London! 1) Great neighborhood and nice building in the middle of Chelsea 2) Super easy transports access, there is a bus station one minute walk and Earl’s Court tube station 5min walk 3) Sainsbury’s is literally around the corner, and you also have a lot of restaurants, fast foods and coffee shops in the perpendicular street 4) The dorms are super clean, someone comes to clean them up everyday, you have your own plug and a lamp above your head and also your own shelf (don’t forget to bring a lock to close it) with a safe with a secret code inside for your valuables 5) Big and fully equipped kitchen with toaster, microwave, pans, fridge, oven! 6) There are also washers and dryers for your laundry 7) The staff is very helpful, nice and thoughtful. They arranged my arrival even though it was at 2am and they were always there to lend me an umbrella when it was raining :) 8) There is a dog !! I honestly cannot find anything bad to say, I could have stayed longer for sure. It really has everything you could need :) Em

title: Very friendly
text: I stayed in the hostel from 19th December to New Year and have to say how much i enjoyed my stay.There is a large kitchen in the basement with plenty of storage and a large fridge for your food this is also a very social space where all the guests gather in the evening and share stories from their own countries. The hostel is very clean and tidy from top to bottom cleaners work every day. The garden at the rear is quiet with seating which is great for the location so close to Earls Court Road which is busy plenty of shops,cafes,fast food outlets and coffee shops some open 24 hrs I was in a mixed 6 bed dorm beds are very comfortable with own light and charger for your smart phone beds are made of wood so no noise when other guests come back to the room What made my stay was the staff very polite and welcoming with a good knowledge of the area and transport links to places of interest in the area and are always available for a chat There is free breakfast in the morning and free tea and coffee available all day, As other people have stated this is not a party hostel but a very nice family run business if you need a comfortable friendly place to stay in the center of London this is worth a visit i will be back there very soon

title: Barmy Badger
text: If you are looking for a hip, lively youth hostel environment, you will be disappointed. If you are looking for a functional, quite place to stay in a decent area, then consider the Barmy Badger. The facilities are old but get the job done. The staff is very friendly and helpful in you need any tips or suggestions.

title: Welcoming place and near the centre of London.
text: Price was fairly good, for London you're getting a good deal here. I stayed in one of the mixed 6 bed rooms they offer, it comes with an ensuite Bathroom. The beds are comfortable and sturdy with firm mattresses and the rooms come with your own locker and safe (don't forget to bring your own padlock!). the rooms are basic room but it's all you need! Linen is provided. Each Bed has it's own reading light. Free breakfast is a great addition as well as free tea and coffee throughout the day. The owners are very friendly and helpful. The hostel is conveniently located about 5mins from Earls Court station which means you're only about 15/20mins from the centre. Wi-Fi is decent and the people staying often seem very nice. This is not a party hostel, definitely more laid back with their own lounge and garden area to chill in too. This would be my first choice when returning to London. To finish this is a well designed and comfortable hostel run by an experienced traveller.

title: Affordable, clean, central location (private room)
text: Stayed in a private 2-person room here for 2 nights. Prices were affordable for London and big plus was the location: on a nice quiet street close to Earls Court tube, and also a close enough walk from where the EasyBus from Gatwick airport drops you off at West Brompton. The private room had it's own shower and sink in the room, and the toilet was located down the hall with the laundry. The staff here was very welcoming and helpful, and everything was clean. Our private room also had a TV, lots of outlets, 2 USB plugs above each side of the bed, a full-length mirror and a nicely sized armoire with hanging space and drawers. You can rent towels and hairdryers for a refundable deposit.

title: Welcoming and comfortable, with excellent beds
text: The hostel is located about five minutes from the Earl's Court subway station, on a quiet side street in a nice neighborhood near Kensington. The staff at the desk are very friendly, welcoming, and conversational. The four-bed female dorm I stayed in on the second floor was very comfortable, with large lockers (key provided), ensuite bathroom with shower, and excellent sturdy wooden custom-built bunk beds equipped with very comfortable firm mattresses -- unusually comfortable for bunk beds. Each bed had a shelf with a reading light and outlet to charge electronics. Wifi was strong in my room as well on the first floor. The included breakfast was very simple -- not great, but OK -- instant coffee, toast, muesli or cold cereal with milk, bananas (which were green when I was there) or oranges. The kitchen has refrigerator space for guest use and a large table for breakfast. A very well designed and comfortable hostel run by an experienced traveller.

title: Great find near the centre of london
text: Although the prices seem steep, for London you're getting a good deal here. I stayed in one of the mixed 4 bed rooms they offer, it comes with an ensuite shower and sink. The toilet is not in the room but close by which isnt too much of an issue. The beds are comfortable enough and the rooms come with your own locked (dont forget to bring your own padlock!). Basic room but it's all you need! Free breakfast is a great addition as well as free tea and coffee throughout the day. The owners are very friendly and helpful. The hostel is conveniently located about 5mins from Earls Court station which means you're only about 15/20mins from the centre. Wifi was decent and the people staying often seem very nice. This is not a party hostel, definitely more laid back with their own lounge and garden area to chill in too. Would return here if in London.

title: Double room 70 pounds per night
text: We had room number 1. Quick check in no faffing around which we liked. Close to the subway station and easy to find the hostel Our room had a shower in our room, tv, excellent heating and was next to the outdoor area which will be lovely for warmer weather. It's a little worn and tired but offers great value for money. Breakfast provided, great communal areas to meet people in kitchen, garden and comfortable front room. Would have given it 4 point 5. If I could give half scores. :) will def come again

title: Value stay
text: For the money, you couldn't do much better than this place. The dorm was basic. There is no elevator. The wifi was good. Breakfast is pretty basic. The people are friendly and many of them stay there, so they really take care of the place. The neighborhood has a lot of food options, and it is located right by the Earl's Court Underground Station, so it's easy to get around.

title: Should have booked longer
text: I stayed two nights and I should have stayed more. If you are looking for a party hostel this is not it... I mean, yes people go out and drink and enjoy each other's time, but there is no pub crawl and when you do crawl back in, you are aware of the other people. Everyone was friendly and talkative. Overall such a relaxing and enjoyable stay!! Definitely recommend!!

title: Fantastic Experience!
text: Barmy Badger is just fantastic! Ideal location (a short walk to Earl's Court tube, shops, restaurants, and a 24 hour grocery store). The owners were incredibly kind and accommodating. They went above and beyond! The private room we stayed in with bunk beds was clean, functional, and even had a little balcony. Barmy Badger attracts similarly minded travellers so shared spaces were clean, noise levels were low, and everyone was kind and respectful. I would give 6 stars if I could! Fabulous stay!!

title: Good Value
text: Stayed here for a week when working in the area. Suited our needs, staff were nice and friendly but the bathroom could have been a tad better for 6 big men sharing a room. Would definitely stay here again!

title: A Home Away From Home
text: I currently stayed here for the third time, and I have the same experience every time...a fantastic one! I've stayed in several hostels now, and this is the only one that I can say is consistently excellent

title: It's like being at home
text: Every time I come to London, I stay here. The position is excellent, near the center without being too overwhelming and the staff really is friendly and ready to help. There's no elevator, so, if you don't like stairs, this might not be the choice for you.

title: Amazing Stay!
text: Even the most seasoned of travelers will fall in love with this place. It got off to a great start as the staff went above and beyond to accommodate a special request I had made. It was very symbolic of their overall approach to customer service...they will do anything they can to make your stay more enjoyable. Great bathrooms/showers, comfortable beds, excellent location, a family atmosphere and so much more stood out during my time there. I would absolutely recommend staying here and am already looking forward to going back!

title: Best hostel in London
text: Really good hostel,good location,few minutes of walk from tube,nice neighbourhood ,few shops,pubs,places to eat,good and fast free wifi,super clean every day ,free breakfast,very nice staff. Will be back!

title: Hit the spot
text: This is probably one of the best places I have found. It has various selection of rooms.which are clean tidy and great value for money. A light breakfast of cereal fruit toast jam tea or coffee included. Links to central London and main airports are all within a few minutes walk Staff are helpful and friendly. Would I stay here again? Absolutely

title: Super Hostel
text: Super nice and helpful stuff, there is someone for you at the reception 24/7 . In general it is a really homely hostel with a big living-dining room where you can cook your own meals if you want to. In the morning you can get a simple breakfast. There also is a living room with a couch, books to read and a TV. In your room besides a comfortable bed you have a big locker with a safe. To top it all of the location is really nice. A supermarket is at the next corner and the tube station is like 5 minutes away. The borough itself offers pubs and restaurants. Also it is not far from all the sights in the centre going by tube and it is quite nice being a bit out of the busy area.

title: Great hostel, close to Earl's Court Station
text: Friendly, good wifi, clean, good location, room had like eight electrical outlets, quiet, very nice free breakfast (Nutella! bananas, tangerines, cerials, bread/butter), kitchen, TV room, grocery stores nearby

title: Best hostel I've stayed in
text: Being just a couple minutes walk from a Zone 1 tube station I thought this hostel would be noisy, but it was so peaceful and quiet! We booked room 9 which has bunk beds, a balcony, and an in-room sink. The restrooms were up a flight of stairs, but they were the cleanest and biggest restrooms I've ever found at a hostel. The staff were super friendly, and there was even a friendly dog there the morning we checked out. The location is great as Earl's Court is in Zone 1 on both the District and Picadilly lines. If you don't want to take the tube there's plenty to do within walking distance as well. Holland Park is just up the street and the Natural History Museum, Science Museum, Victoria and Albert Museum, and Hyde Park are a 20 minute walk. There are also lots of great and moderately priced restaurants and pubs in the area. The place felt very secure and there were safes in the room if you wanted a place to keep your passport.

title: Fabulous
text: I enjoyed staying in this hostel. Staff were friendly and helpful. Rooms were clean, beds were comfy. Very impressed with the lockers - big enough for large luggage AND a safe for valuables! Breakfast was good. Good location - short walking distance to supermarkets and subway. Would stay here again. Thanks for a great stay! ☺

title: Great stay, great location, great staff
text: This place iw fantastic. I'd been travelling for awhile and mistakenly booked my one week stay here starting one day earlier then I planned to arrive and finishing a day earlier then I planned to leave and didn't notice until the morning I was headed to London when they emailed me about having to charge me for the first night's stay since I didn't show. When I arrived they had cancelled my booking, but when I explained I had made a mistake when booking my dates, they booked me back in and didn't even charge me for the previous night they had held for me, even though it was completely my fault. I was in a four bed, girls dorm and I really liked the layout of the room and how there were stand up cupboards as well as places under the beds for everyone to put things, so there was no luggage or anything taking up floor space. The room and bathroom were kept clean. Breakfast was included and filling. Wifi worked wonderfully. The place had a great atmosphere. The location is great. A few minutes walk from Earls Court station, which is served by two lines, which got me where I needed to go most of the time, and if not, it was really easy to use those to connect to other lines. My only complaint is I felt the heat was on too high at night, but since that was my only issue, I wI'll definitely stay here again when back in London.

title: Friendly staff, clean room and convenient location
text: We booked a twin private room with shared bath. There is no lift and the staircase is quite narrow. Although a little cramped with only one chair, one flap-up table, one wash basin and a double decker bunker bed, our stay was a pleasant one. We had to make our own beds like at home and return the bedsheets, comforters and pillow cases after use. It is a 6 minutes walk to the Earls Court Station (there are lifts to both the tube station and the underground train station). There are many restaurants and eating places around the area. Sainsburys is just at the corner and Tesco Metro is a mere 6 minutes walk so you can also buy your favourite soup and bring back to Barmy Badger to heat up in the microwave. Breakfast is included in our room rates and you just help yourself to the beverages and the breakfast stuff at the dining area at the basement. There are also cooking facilities. So our stay at Barmy Badger was quite a homely one.

title: Good stay
text: The location of this hostel is fantastic. Very easy to come here by sub and the last meters by feet. The staff welcomes you and explains everything u wanna know. Linen are handed after checkin as well as fresh towels if u like and need . For the towels a deposit in cash is needed. Generally cash payment is an advance due to a credit card fee of 3%. The room is tidy and clean (room6) the bath is big enough for British circumstances. The water pressure is acceptable, the light is dim , the shower cabin very small. The bed is comfy, the night very very quiet. The breakfast is foc, and as expected very basic. I took it as a good start in the morning . The kitchen itself needs urgently a handy man . Too many things were visibly damaged and not only for a couple of days . The wifi signal is strong . From time to time it's gone but generally it's working pretty well. Supermarkets, bars and restaurants are on short distance as well as tourist spots and the Hyde park .Recommended place to stay

title: Lovely staff and atmosphere
text: I always get a warm welcome from the lovely people who run and manage here. It's in a prime location if you're visiting to get the most out of your trip to London. They are so helpful with advice on things to do and great places to visit. There are a good range of shops, restaurants and supermarkets wirhin walking distance. You'll also find Earls Court underground station a few minutes walk from here. I always meet great people here and highly recommend staying here. Book early as it gets busy fast.

title: Comfortable backpacker hostel
text: We spent a lot of time in hostels this trip and this was one of the best. We had a private room, which was reasonably priced for 2 people, quite roomy and very comfortable. The kitchen and bathrooms appeared to have been updated recently and were very clean. The staff were friendly and made us feel at home even when we showed up much earlier than the normal check-in time. Only downside, there are a LOT of stairs. On the plus side, you'll get a workout getting to your room.

title: Good people and social spaces make this a great place.
text: Barmy Badger's location is excellent: in very safe feeling Kensington, a five minute walk from Earl's Court tube station, with a small grocery store on the corner. The inside of the hostel feels very worn-in (for better or worse), and the bathroom locations are a bit odd, but you get used to it. Oh, and the wifi worked consistently, better than at most of the other places I visited on this trip. The real strength of the Badger is the people. The owners are welcoming and have a good sense of humor, and the staff can be flexible if a well-meaning guest is a few minutes late in checking out or vacating the kitchen for cleaning. More importantly, the fact that there are two dorm rooms of long-term weekly residents means there's a flexible social group often present in the kitchen, TV room, and backyard and happy to hang out with more transient guests. The kitchen is the type with one long table, which encourages everyone to interact rather than isolating alone or in cliques. All of this makes for a comfortable social environment just as open to joining others at the pub as to heading out for solo sightseeing. That's not for everyone, of course, and if you want to focus on personal adventures the warmly social Badger may not be for you. With my travel goals, it was a highlight of my trip.

title: Home from Home
text: The Barmy Badgers Backpackers Hostel is the best in London. the Owners and staff are friendly and helpful. It's Very clean. The beds are super comfortable and the facilities are excellent. Free breakfast and all-day tea/coffee is a huge bonus. Location is excellent. Even the long-term residents are great, ever time I've visited I've been made to feel like I was part of the Barmy Badger family, they are so nice to include people , even lone-travelers who only stay a night or two can get invited out on a Wednesday to the Kings Head down the road. Can't wait for my next visit to London so I can stay here again.

title: Location, location, location..
text: Just off of Earls Court, this is the perfect spot for exploring down town London. With lots of bars and restaurants on the doorstep and a Sainsburys on the corner if you fancy staying in. In a converted town house the hostel has good space for mingling and a great patio, weather permitting.. Breakfast is included, basic but a bonus anyways, AND the Nutella comes in individual packages = no double dipping! Phew. The rooms are clean and come with storage lockers and safes - great addition!!

title: Very Nice Experience
text: I traveled to The Badger in April with my sister. We stayed for 6 days and overall had an excellent experience. They were very welcoming and gave us suggestions of places to visit. I plan to stay here again at the beginning of September before going to college.

title: HOT HOT HOT (and not in a good way!)
text: On arrival I was early and was able to head to my room immediately. I was given a set of linen and had to make my own bed (not such a big issue) but a first for a hostel, that's for sure. I was in one of the rooms in the top of the house (the converted attic space?). After choosing and making my bed I headed out for the afternoon and evening. I returned back to the hostel and it was fairly quiet as most people were in bed about 10 or 11pm. The room was FAR too hot - not sure if the window opened with it being so high up or not but with it being incredibly hot and the mattress and pillow having a rubber protector on I was sweating SO much and constantly waking up throughout the night. At one point in the night I considered going downstairs to the sofa in the TV room and sleeping on that. Breakfast of cereal and toast was a nice touch. Showers and bathrooms clean although there was no mat for the floor so water was everywhere. If the hostel provided fans for the rooms and mats for the bathroom and gets rid of the horrible mattress protectors I think this would be an ace hostel and would definitely get a much higher rating from me.

title: Quiet, Friendly Hostel in Good Location
text: I was attracted to this hostel because of the price (on the lower end of the hostels in London, but not the very cheapest), location (central) and great reviews, and I was not disappointed. Prior to arrival I was a bit worried about the location (since it's not in the most central Picadilly Circus, or Bloomsbury, neighborhoods), but it worked out well. The hostel is just a few minutes walk from the Earl's Court tube station which is located within zone 1 (where most of the main sights are) and on the Picadilly and District lines (two of the main tube routes through the city) - and the area is very safe so I never felt any qualms about walking around at night by myself. There are several affordable restaurants close by (I recommend Masala Zone for Indian and Prince of Teck for a pint and some bangers and mash), as well as a grocery store just on the corner. The hostel is kept very clean, and the complimentary breakfast was a nice touch. It's a quiet hostel, with a slightly older clientele, so it's better for people who are looking to spend the evening relaxing (that would be me), rather than people looking to party. The staff/owners were friendly and helpful, and the rooms had big lockers (big enough to fit my luggage), outlets and shelves by the all the beds, and comfy mattresses.

title: Great place to stay
text: Pro's - Ensuite bathroom for each room, friendly and welcoming staff, great location (walking distance to tube, main road and Hyde park). Free breakfast was basic but tasty. Con's - Creaky bedroom floor made it hard to be quiet. No elevator. Great value for money in London and I would be go back for my next visit.

title: Welcoming
text: First time visit to any Hostel and at 40 years of age was also first solo trip but any worries were soon gone after being greeted by Spencer on arrival who explained all I needed to know. Comfortable beds every where clean and tidy and added bonus of breakfast. 3 great nights and will be using as a base to explore more of London due to fantastic location. Only disappoint was the dogs where not there during my visit

title: Fantastic location and very friendly atmosphere =D
text: Have stayed quite a few times, and think the customer service is always fantastic/friendly =D Liz & Ken are ever so helpful and can offer you advice on where to go and what to see! From there I booked a trip/tour to Scotland, which was cold but amazing to experience. Otherwise had a Chelsea FC season ticket, so was there on a quite regular basis. The location is not even a 5 minute walk down to Earls Court station and only about 3 stops to Fulham Broadway, the a 5 minute walk to Chelseas Stamford Bridge =D Very highly recommended to all travellers!

title: Great stay
text: It's a great hostel. You easily feel being at home. The staff is friendly and helpful. Also the location couldn't have been better (at Earls Court). You have all you need close by (subway station, shops etc.).

title: 142 countries & this is home away from home
text: I can not imagine staying anywhere else in London. I use this place as if it was my home away from home. The staff are very friendly with a personal touch that a lone traveller needs, information that cuts costs for me being a budget traveller plus breakfast that keeps me going in a heathy way. I just keep going back, thanks guys for another wonderful stay.

title: Everything is so easy
text: For a first time traveller to London, staying at an easy, friendly and central place were pretty much my key considerations (after price). Luckily for me, I booked the BBB which met all of these criteria, with its easy access to everything London offers the highlight for mine. With an easy 5 minute walk to Earl's Court Underground station which has both the District and Piccadilly lines running through it. As it is on the border of zone 1, you can travel everywhere from Kings Cross, Tower Hill and the Notting Hill Gate for a couple of pounds. It also connects directly to Heathrow via the Piccadilly line for the easiest way to the hostel. Included is a basic breaky (toast, fruit, jam, tea and coffee) and wi-fi. the rooms themselves are fairly basic, but you dont need to be there more than to sleep with a couple of good pubs around the corner (Earls Court Tavern basically at end of the street). To top it off, the friendliness of the guys at the front made it easy to get my bearings and get started from a perfect base. Thanks!

title: Friendliest hostel in London
text: Stayed at the badger for only two nights but even in that short time the hostel felt very homey. The staff are lovely and very helpful and the beds are comfortable! Free lockers with a safe inside and free breakfast is definately a plus. Close to the tube station and has a lovely garden area for when the weather is good. Also the bathrooms are just that- proper bathrooms where you have somewhere to put your clothes where they don't get wet! Would definately stay again.

title: Best hostel in London!
text: This was the best hostel I stayed in during my travels. The hostel itself feels like home, is relaxed, and very, very clean. I stayed here for a total of 10 months, originally only planning to stay for 10 days. I was so happy I made the decision to stay. The museums are not too far away, easy to walk to, as is the city if you like a nice stroll through London. The wifi in the hostel is extremely fast, so on rainy days it's nice and easy to access internet! The hostel is very close to both Sainsburys and Tesco, as well as a huge variety of takeaway and restaurant eateries. The tube is only 5 minutes walk away, and services two lines, meaning you can get around London extremely quickly. The rooms are wonderful, everyone gets enough space, even in 6 bed dorms. The double and twin rooms are fantastic as well. If I return to London, this is certainly the place I will be returning to. I won't ever forget my time here.

title: Nice people, but extremely uncomfortable beds
text: I spend a few days here to celebrate new years in London. The staff was really nice and everything was clean. Breakfast was included: toast, jam and some fruits, so basically all you need. We slept in a 6 person dorm with an ensuite bath room. The room was also in a good condition, but the beds were terrible. The matrasses were really thin so you were basically lying on the wooden plank beneath it. Both the matrass and the pillow had plastic on the outside, which also did not really help the comfort. After one night already I really had pains in my back and I did not look forward to have go to bed again at night, which usually is my favorite part of the day. So: great location, nice people but not so great beds.

title: Best place to stay in London!!!
text: I recently stayed at the Barmy Badger and was blown away by the facilities. The bathrooms have been recently refurbished and put most hotels to shame. Each bathroom has all the amenities you'd expect in a hotel costing four times the price. There's free WiFi throughout the Hostel & when I was staying there they were in the process of installing individual power-points and USB charging docks for each of the beds! The back garden is a great place to chill out after a big day in the city, its quiet and secluded. The hostel is superbly located in the center of London. Hyde park is a 10min walk, 30min to Piccadilly Circus (on foot) & 45mins to Buckingham Palace. The hostel also has easy access to many tube lines making navigating the city a breeze. From Heathrow its as easy as a 30- 40min train ride on the Piccadilly Line. The staff at the hostel are amazing!!! All are very friendly and accommodating. There are also two small dogs that regularly frequent the hostel, which for me being a dog person made my stay very enjoyable. I'd recommend this hostel to anyone and I myself would be happy to return sometime on my next travels.

title: Well located and nice hostel
text: I would really recommend this place. The staff was nice and helpful, the location is great. The neighborhood is safe and charming. The room was OK not great, but for me, the most important was to have a secure locker in my room, and as I can remember, the price was good for London... Definitely a good choice!

title: Best Hostel Ever !!!
text: Ok let me start by saying over the years I have had the great fortune to stay in many different fantastic hostels around Europe, but Barmy Badger Backpackers was by far the best I have stayed at yet. The location is superb being just 5 minutes walk from Earl's Court underground station which is served by the district line which also serves the majority of underground stations located beside the main tourist attractions whether it is Westminster or the Tower of London. The staff were so welcoming, friendly and accommodating. We were welcomed by Monika who was full of smiles and information and just made myself and my girlfriend feel right at home and every other team member was much the same. The facilities and common room were fantastic. The common room looked and felt like your TV room and the kitchen was the exact same. They didn't have that "hostel" feel about them rather that you were in your own or a friends home. The bed room was brilliant, clean and comfy and WARM which was a welcome relief as it was rather cold outside. But most importantly the owners are kind and thoughtful....we were staying on Valentines night and as a result were giving a bottle of Prosecco free of charge, it just made the night and was such a surprise.... you would not get this type of treatment in a hotel!! I can't recommend this place enough, stay stay stay stay STAY here :D I will be running back to stay here next time I am in London for sure !!!

title: Cozy central stay
text: I spent one night here, and I'll be happy to book it again on future visits. The staff/owners are very friendly and accommodating, and all areas were clean. I stayed in a female ensuite dorm with 4 beds, and it was good value. The beds were a bit hard, but thankfully that's how I prefer them

title: Home away from Home
text: An amazing hostel to stay at. Relaxing and easy going type place where you can unwind and not worry about the stresses of the real world outside. The owners are friendly and accommodating in all aspects and ensure your stay is pleasant. Was recommended by a friend and can understand why they stayed here. Highly recommend.

title: Fantastic, could not be better!
text: Wonderful, warm room! Comfy beds! HUGE locker with safe. Communal bathroom was spotless. Coffee was delicious, and available at all hours! We just loved coming in at night and enjoying a fresh cup. Free brek was delish: Nutella, butter, huge wheat toast, Musli, bananas, coffee. Perfect. Earls Court is Food Street, and Sainsbury's is 100 feet from this hostel. Big selection of tasty takeaway sandwiches and snacks available there. Badger had very helpful and nice front desk staff/ family and the long term residents were pretty cool. We could not have been comfier here. The Earls Court tube goes everywhere, with 2 Tube lines and direct service to Heathrow. Food on Earls Court Road is all open late, and there is nothing you can't get. Badger had tons of maps and free info at the desk. Wifi was flawless everywhere. We could not ask for anything more. What a great experience, and we had a fantastic time in London.

title: Best local staff in the best location
text: Firstly id like to thank the badger for such a friendly and welcoming stay. The staff were beyond helpful and had some really good advice. The rooms were clean and the breakfast was a good start to the day. Ill more than happyly come back

title: Nice people, a residential hostel near a cool neighborhood
text: Stayed here twice on a Euro-vacation. It was a perfect hostel home base. The bustling tube station is a few blocks away, but to get there you walk past Sainsbury's and Starbucks and Pret a Mange and a few pubs and let's face it you need one of those stores at some point in the day. For my part, the staff and the other residents were very nice and friendly. It is a hostel, with shared bathroom, kitchen, living room and porch. It kinda sounds like planes outside, but from my experience in London, I think London sounds like planes outside. Definitely go to the nearby Troubadour Cafe.

title: good value for the location
text: we stayed for 4 nights in a 6 room dorm. the location was excellent - it is located less than a 10 minutes walk from earls court station, and there are many shops and eateries around. earls court station is located on the piccadilly and victoria lines, and is a few stops away from central london. the room itself is huge, and there is plenty of space for everyone. i love that the lockers have a safe inside. however, the shower space is tiny and the floors creak, but those are small complains compared to all the good things about this place. there is also breakfast provided every morning - bread, jam, butter, cereal, milk, tea, and coffee. we met a lot of cool people during our stay there, and it added on to our positive experience in the hostel. we will definitely stay in this hostel the next time we're back in london.

title: Good location and nice hostel
text: I only stayed 2 nights in the female-only dorm, but the hostel was clean and tidy. Although there wasn't much room in the dorm, there were big storage places under the bed and a large storage cupboard each with a safe inside which was big enough to store all reasonable sized valuables. Breakfast was cereal, toast, fruit and tea/coffee but perfectly adequate to start the day. It's not far from Earl's Court underground which has the Piccadilly, District and Circle Lines. I would consider staying there again.

title: Good Value Hostel
text: Stayed one night while over for the NFL. It was very much what you expect from a hostel in terms of the bedrooms. The staff were friendly, it is located close to the tube so it's easy to get about from here. Also a minutes walk from a main street with plenty of bars, restaurants on it.

title: Clean hostel, friendly staff
