Elvis from guest services went out of his way to help us find our way around the city. All in all a great hotel, in a great location with great service.

title: An amazing London experience.
text: We were traveling as a family for our first trip to London. We book this Marriott because it was convenient located next to the "Tube" (underground metro) next to Canary Wharf, major financial district and close to the Maritime British Museum. We received a very warm welcoming from the front desk, special thanks to Vera, Kormelia and Harold! Excelente hospitality skills! We were tired and we arrived early than the check in time, they were attentive to our needs and offers us water and alternative accommodation (lounge) until they were able to manage an early check in. Vera was very nice to give our daughter a small box with pass activities to make the time go fast. They manage to get us a room and we were able to early check-in. The hotel does not offer a pool, not a deal breaker since we did not care much for it. It has a fitness center, but we never used. The business center was nice and the staff nice as well! The lounge bar was nice too and the staff was great! I do not recommend this place with multiple kids under 8, since this is more of a business oriented hotel, but who know you can change that. There are a few nice restaurants and Pubs, this is a Marriott Apt. so some of the rooms offers a Kitchenette (which it was in our case) we safe good money with the breakfast and there was a grocery in a walking distance of the hotel by the Canary Square shopping Mall. We want to give many, many thank for the housekeeping staff! Thank you very! The Lay Family.

title: Adequate but bit pricey
text: For what you get at the price you pay there are better options in central London. Price is reflective of location. Saying this the hotel is comfortable, I have stayed in over 100 hotels in London so I can be a bit picky as I know what's good and what's not. You won't be disappointed and you won't be overly impressed. Prices at the bar are extreme, again based on location. Right near DLR then one stop to Canary Wharf tube station. Day ticket on tube for zones 1-6 is about £12, pretty reasonable. Some lovely restaurants nearby.

title: Decent corporate hotel
text: Friendly staff, good food and what was an outstanding bar made this a good stay. These hotels all tend to be similar but this one is well run, clean and the room service is very good. Rooms are also comfortable and clean.

title: Nice place and nice people
text: I have stayed a number of times at this hotel and the people are friendly and the food fine and the facilities all work well too. You can plug your laptop into the TV to watch Netflix and the bar downstairs has awesome staff and an even more awesome range of gin though no Australian ones. Will definitely stay here each time I visit my London team. Oh and left my glasses somewhere in the hotel or so I thought and received a welcome email telling me they had been found.

title: Unusual East London Location
text: Canary Wharf/East India Quay in Eadt London is a fairly new financial center East of the tourist areas of London That Marriott Executive Apartments are an excellent place to find over all of London and surroundings if you are staying for more than a few days. We spent 17 days there and thoroughly loved it. We first had a large suite apt complete with a nicely equipped kitchen. Later on we had a guest for three days and switched to a one bedroom apt. Larger than the suite and spacious enough for a roll away bed set up in the sitting room. Nice, large kitchen with everything included. Most days we would return from a whole day of adventuring into town, stopping at the Canary Wharf DLR or Jubilee Line Station and also stopping at the Waitrose Hiper Market store to pick up our dinner. They have excellent organic home-made prepared dinners and soups which we baked in the regular apt oven. Perfevt for all if us. Also ate at the Marriott's Manhattan Grill restaurant which we thoroughly enjoyed.

title: Excellent Service
text: Perfect location for business, great service and attention from everyone. Rooms are spacious. Love the restaurant. Second visit in two years and same pleasant experience. You won't be close to any major attraction.

title: Reasonably priced option
text: The Marriott is a good choice and is usually better priced than the other chain options in Canary Wharf. The rooms are clean and well-appointed and well insulated from the street and rail noise. Every now and again. you can score an upgrade to the serviced apartments which are very spacious. The breakfast buffet has a good variety of food at a decent price.

title: A lovely property with all the conveniences of home
text: We just spent 9 nights over Christmas at the Marriott Executive Apartments, West India Quay. We thoroughly enjoyed all the amenities of home for our family of four. The 2-BR/2-bathroom suite 906 was ideal for us (great view of the Quay-- pronounced "key,"-- as well). Our teenage daughters appreciated their own bedroom, which had two twin size beds pushed next to one another in a king configuration, with a bathroom immediately adjacent to their room, while our master had a standard king bed, en-suite bathroom arrangement. The kitchen was stocked with pots and pans, utensils for cooking and eating, and all the china we needed. We cooked dinner almost every night in our apartment, which was so convenient. The location of the property is excellent. Canary Wharf is on the East End of London, so while outside of Central London, it is a very quick tube ride (the Jubilee Line is literally about a 5 minute walk from the property...we found a shortcut). Canary Wharf is where the modern financial district is and it's very modern and super safe and clean. There are multiple underground shopping malls, with every convenience needed, including a large Waitrose grocery store, where we shopped almost every day. For those who love ramen, we strongly recommend Ipuddo around the 5 Canada Square location (under 5 minutes of walk from hotel). The broth for this ramen is spectacular!!!...the best I've ever had. It's a couple doors down from Notes coffee shop, which is really cute and charming. All in all, this was the perfect location and type of property for our wonderful visit to London. We thoroughly enjoyed the ~1000 square ft of space for our family and all the amenities of home, yet also having the conveniences of a hotel property for whenever it made sense (fitness center, hotel restaurant, etc)

title: Perfection
text: My wife doesn't like to travel. Across the street. So, when she's along it requires a large budget to make sure I have her comfortable. She doesn't demand it, I just want her to enjoy being away from home. The highlight of my year has become choosing a great hotel for the one time she goes overseas with me. We've stayed at some remarkable hotels in London the last 16 years. But this place is off the charts! When we checked in I explained to Verona that my wife was along and I wanted to make it special for her. I had already booked an apartment but Verona gave us a fabulous corner! A killer view!! We were here for 11 nights. The air conditioner was not functioning properly and they fixed it as soon as we checked in. That's important for us. Even in November. This is one of the few times it got so cold for us at a London hotel we had to turn off the ac! Thank you!! The apartments are incredibly spacious. And, it's a Marriott property. What's not to like?? I would love to stay here every time I'm in London!

title: 02 Concert and Overnight in Canary Wharf
text: A good hotel that is good for the visitor to Canary Wharf at the weekend. Lovely breakfast and very nice staff at this hotel. Rooms good and over look the Wharf. You can get a bargain at the weekend if you keep looking. Good for me and the wife.

title: Best place we have stayed at in the UK
text: Me and my family went to this hotel to see a miley cyrus concert, in the O2 Arena, December the 19th - she was amazing! - and we really enjoyed the luxury of the hotel. We are going to see JLS at the same time of the year 2010, and hopefully we will be returning to this hotel. We also might just go to london to do a few things we didnt get round to doing, and we want to stay here. The rooms, bar, and resteraunt is very clean. The service is amazing, as the cleaners and the waiters and waitresses are very friendly and helpful! I wouldnt give the location of the Marriot a 5, because it's in Canary Wharf, which is a bit of a business city so there isnt anything really interesting to do there, so you have to catch a lot of tubes, but we didnt mind. There are quite a few nice resteraunts there though! The rooms were probably the best bit about the hotel. There's a mini bar (but its electronic, so if you take something out and put it back it still charges), a TV, amazingly comfortable beds, a mirror, a desk, a manual about london and the hotel, an armchair by the window, and a wardrobe with a hair dryer inside! In the bathroom there is a toilet, a big mirror, 2 sinks and a shower bath! The beds are so comfortable, me and my mum didnt want to move in the morning. I dont see any need to stay at another hotel, and we would never ever want to! Oh, the rooms also have telephones to contact other rooms and a spy hole on the door which i loved to look out of! =]

title: Another great stay!
text: This is our 3rd time staying at this location and we can't wait to come back. Front desk staff, lobby bar, housekeeping staff all A+. We love the space of the apartment traveling with our 11 & 13 year old. Easy tube ride anywhere we need to go and excellent restaurants around property. Our favorite place to finish the day is the lobby bar where the staff remembers us from previous visits. The food is delicious! Probably the best sticky toffee pudding ever. While the food is great, the staff there makes it our favorite place. So professional and so friendly. We can't wait to come back to see our Quay family.

title: Handy for the O2
text: We stayed here after attending the ATP Finals at the O2. Located only ten minutes walk from Canary Wharf tube station it was an ideal location! Total journey time probably only took 20 minutes as the O2 is just one tube stop away. The hotel was nice, the room was a good size and we had a nice view of the O2. Our room was quite noisy as it was by the tracks but it wasn't too bad. There was a good spread for breakfast in the morning, lots to choose from if you didn't fancy a full English. If I go to the O2 again I would definitely stay here.

title: No longer will stay at this hotel
text: Our travel agent booked this hotel and didn't realize it was an apartment, not the hotel. For short stay, never stay at the apartment as none of the guest services is available. Front desk people didn't even acknowledge your loyalty membership and treat you like below average guest. Nasty front desk woman. Found cheaper room on the Marriott apps at the same hotel, but "it's a system error" excuse and didn't allow moving to smaller from from 2 bdm to 1 bdm for one guest. If I booked one room hotel on my iPhone they would have to honor it, but not this hotel. All about making money and rude service. I am done with this place and will stay at Hilton going forward. I am concerned with SPG hotel as I expect service will be similar with at best average service at Marriott such as Canary Warf location. I night recommend you avoid this place.

title: Great apartments
text: First point is that a lot of folk complain about the location and getting to the hotel. It's a lot easier than many people make it as the hotel is only five minutes walk from the Jubilee Line at Canary Wharf taking you to and from central London very quickly. It's much easier than using the DLR. The apartments are separate from the Marriott hotel although they share a reception. The apartments are a good size with separate living room/kitchen and bedroom with a hallway linking them. Off the hallway is the bathroom. The kitchen is fine with a full size fridge, cooker, hob, microwave and dishwasher. Utensils and crockery are basic but meet most needs. There are washing machines and driers on several floors which are free to use and there's a decent gym. Staff are friendly and the hotel was very clean. All in all a great stay in a great apartment. The location is fine too with some decent local shops and restaurants.

title: Good for Business on Canary Wharf or large families
text: Canary Wharf is a business district. If you're visiting for business in the area, the apartments are fine. For tourists, the apartments are only worthwhile for those who need a very basic kitchen or more than one room to spread out. Otherwise, this isn't an ideal tourist location and there is nothing to draw you here. My overall impression of the hotel/apartments is that it is mediocre and doesn't care to be anything more than that. Hence, the 'go get your own dish soap' attitude referenced by other reviewers, broken washing machines, and generally lackadaisical service. It is NOT a horrible or filthy place. It's a decent place to sleep after your business meetings and don't expect one bit more than that. As far as any visitor is concerned, there is no apparent distinction between the hotel and the apartments. It's all one high-rise building. There is only one main entrance. There is only one lobby. There is only one check-in desk. There is only one set of elevators. Management has commented on several reviews here that they are two different entities. Its a little like the emperor's new clothes. Any separation is only in name. It didn't affect me, but I found the management responses here to be representative of the kind of 'can't do' attitude prevalent at the hotel. If you do find yourself here, it's not hard to get around London from Canary Wharf, just time consuming. The hotel overlooks the light-rail, right next door. You can switch from the light-rail to the tube system at various stops. Alternatively, the Jubilee line is about a ten minute walk, as is the Thames Clipper river bus dock. Depending on the time of day, it will take at least 30 minutes to get into central London on any of these modes of transportation. There are plenty of restaurants and shops in the Canary Wharf area (in fact there's a huge underground shopping mall with a Waitrose grocery story, a Boots drugstore, numerous clothing stores and just about anything you might need).

title: Good not great
text: Rooms and bathrooms are updated and reasonably comfortable. Staff is friendly but not super stars. It is a decent price and if you are a banker then the location is a good one.

title: Reconsidering Marriott as my preferred hotel
text: Apparently at this one Marriott property, there are actually two properties. A hotel and an apartment property. I stayed in the apartment property not really knowing that there was a major difference between them. As a long term Marriott member, I typically get free breakfast and access to the executive lounge. Not the case here if you stay in the 8th floor and above which are called the "Executive Apartments". Quite ironic that if you stay in these, you don't get access to the Executive Lounge or free breakfast unlike the 7th floor and down "hotel" part. I began my quest to understand why I wasn't getting access and breakfast and the hotel staff, managers, etc just kept saying "you are staying in the apartments and don't get that amenity". My business companions, staying in the hotel side, paying about 70 pounds a night less than I was did get all of this. Long story short, they offered me a discount from 50 to 35 pounds to get these two amenities two days before we left, AFTER I called Marriott corporate to complain. As far as the room goes, it was average. Not fancy, not bad. Just a single room with the kitchen, bedroom and living room all one room. This was the worst customer service experience at a Marriott property I've every had. I'm reconsidering my Marriott membership.

title: It was a wonderful stay
text: We had a 10-day family trip with 2 children at Marriott executive apartments West India Quay London. It was a great experience from check-in to check-out. Everything is great. Within the room, we have full kitchen for catering and living room for kids playing around. Very comfortable bed and bath room with hot water. For the location, it is just 5 minutes walk to DLR or Tube station. Both stations equips with lifts which is great for carrying baby with buggy. With DLR and Tube system, you are able to go spots within 20-30 minutes. Overall, we had a great time and will stay here again next trip.

title: Luxurious London Living
text: We stayed on the 12th floor in the suite and it was FABULOUS. The views are spectacular and the suite has everything you could possibly want or need. The beds are super comfortable and luxurious linens in the bathroom. The bar and restaurant offer a great variety of menu choices and we had scrumptious meals with wonderful service. The staff is so friendly and so helpful and make you feel they are there for you at all times.The location is a 10 minute ride on the Jubilee Line (station a few minutes away) to all the attractions in downtown London and the concierge will set you up with all the information you need to make the most of your stay.It suited us perfectly, after a day of sight seeing you are able to get away from the hustle and bustle of crazy downtown. Canary Wharf is a totally remodeled business mecca with high end malls, restaurants, bars and a young and hip professional vibe.It is nice to experience this "other side' of London.

title: Friendly Staff & Great Location
text: Stayed for two nights even though we only live just over an hour away, and would highly recommend. Staff were very friendly especially Vlad who was very helpful. Rooms clean, spacious & quiet. Had a meal in the Manhattan Restaurant on the Friday which was superb and the bar area is a relaxing place to be. Will definitely visit again.

title: Great Hotel with great service
text: This is a great hotel with fantastic service. The breakfast is expensive, but you are given value for money. I love the Executive lounge but it's a bit small. The bar area is nice and intimate with good service.

title: The best hotel we have stayed at - ever!
text: Me and my husband celebrated our second wedding-anniversary in beginning of December 2009. My husband had booked a long weekend at The Marriot... to surprise me. We had wonderful days and nights at that hotel... We recommend this hotel!!!

title: The hotel was blah.
text: I stayed at this hotel on business for 5 days, and was very disappointed. I felt that this place really tries to take advantage of the travelers with their absolutely ridiculous prices! 10 pounds for 15 minutes of Internet is just overly excessive. Also, given that the hotel has only 15 channels and only 8 of them are in English it would make sense to make the movie selection affordable. I do not consider 5 year old movies at 9.99 pounds affordable! Especially when there is a movie theatre next door charging 8.95! The electricity converter was broken, and it was way too hot in the room because the AC wasn’t working properly (to which they didn’t offer a solution saying that every room is that hot). Every day they would leave a breakfast menu on my bed offering me their wonderful American Continental Breakfast room service for 29 pounds. Are they serious? The only good thing about this hotel was that it had a wall of windows. A wall of windows that directly faced a train station! I felt like I was renting a spot on the train platform! Needless to say, I do not think this hotel is worth the money, unless you like to get ripped off for everything. Try the Savoy instead., at least that way you’ll be staying in a decent area with a lot of tourist attractions for the same prices.

title: Not your standard Marriott
text: The ultimate business hotel. I had a one bedroom apartment for a two week stay. The apartment was huge and beautifully appointed. Totally separate bedroom and living room kitchen combination. Everything I needed was there. The view was incredible. Check in was quick and easy. The concierge -Sam - was particularly helpful. This isn't the location if you are on vacation but for a business trip it can't be beat. Many restaurants within walking distance as well as two train stops and shopping. There are also hotel rooms if you don't need an apartment for you stay.

title: Not upto the mark !
text: Went on a business trip and stayed at the Marriot at Canary Wharf having chosen it for its location and reputation. It is a mid size hotel and we were booked at the executive floor with access to the lounge facilities. The room was very large and comfortable with a good view. Despite being a business hotel its room service was quite poor. They needed atleast 45 minutes to deliver and charged GBP 3 as service ! We had dinner one night which was one of the worst meals we have ever eaten ! The executive lounge offered a very limited selection through the day. Not what we would expect from a Marriot.

title: Nice hotel business minded location
text: I'm here for business and was welcome to this hotel most efficiently while the rugby World Cup is going on and half the teams seem to stay here Gorgeous modern hotel away from tourist stuff. Good job Marriott. Snobby US travelled that I am... Bathroom soaps etc could be a bit better. Looks more like holiday inn express

title: Brilliant staff
text: Stayed here for 5 nights while working at a large conference .Marriott hotels always have a high standard and this one ticked all the boxes. Lovely rooms , the best beds ever ! One compliant this is from a woman's point of view the table was not in a position where you can sit and dry your hair in the mirror ! Great breakfast ,restaurant food was nice , the bar menu was ok a little boring and old fashioned ! Great selection of gin and brilliant cocktails What made this stand out rom other Marriott's I have stayed in is the staff They are brilliant from the concierge to reception breakfast staff and bar staff The event staff were brilliant and made our job very easy wit hour customers nothing was too much trouble Thank you all

title: Comfortable family stay
text: Stayed for 5 nights at Marriott Executive Apartments London, West India Quay in a two bedroom apartment. The setting is really nice and comfortable for a family vacation. The adult get a King size bedroom and children get a Queen bed each with a living room and kitchen in between. The room was facing Canary Whraf with nice view of North Dock and commercial building lights. My kids loved to watch the trains each morning as they exit the station. The hotel is near West India Quay and Canary Wharf Light rail (DLR) services which can take you back to central London through connecting Underground. Be cautious that the hotel is about 30-45 minutes away from central London by Taxi and can cost you around 20 pound! We took Uber throughout our stay and cost was around 10 pound to Tower of London and 20 pound to London Eye. If you taking Taxi or Uber, the traffic is horrible any time of the day! Another tip is the airport travel: if you are traveling to London Heathrow, allow 90 minutes travel time since you have to cross London. Gatwick airport is much easier and quick since you will be traveling via highway. The closest airport is London City Airport. The Lobby Lounge Bar is a fantastic place to get a glass of Gin and Tonic

title: Nice place to stay in for longer duration
text: Marriott executive apartments are excellent for longer duration. I stayed there for 47 days on my business visit to London. It was really nice experience all together to be there. Apartment is quite specious and unique interior with super view of canary wharf.

title: Simply Awesome- Lovely stay
text: I have stayed at the Marriott Executive apartments recently this month for nine days for the second time. This was an awesome stay. View from the room was simply amazing. I could see the DLF station and had water view from the room. Access to the executive lounge makes is more attractive. Staff at Marriott is really good. There are many nearby hotels which you can try for variety of foods as well and is again very well connected with DLR. Overall a very nice stay.

title: Could not be better
text: The Staff were exceptional. The breakfast was incredible, lots to choose from, full English breakfast, pancakes,fruit and lots more. The catering staff were very helpful and organised. Our room was very clean and comfortable.

title: Convenient, modern, clean rooms and quiet
text: Very comfortable stay for 4 nights while attending a conference at ExCel, which is only a few stops away on the DLR. We had a one bedroom apartment with plenty of room for an additional foldaway bed for our adult son who stayed with us. The small kitchenette was adequate for breakfast preparation and we stocked up on food at the nearby Tesco. There were no washing up materials so we had to ask for these at the reception. There could have been a complimentary sachet of dish liquid and dishwasher powder provided. (There were no scourers or brushes, either.) We ate dinner out at restaurants in the vicinity and there are plenty to choose from. Marriott service was pleasant and responsive. The bed was a dream to sleep in- wonderfully comfortable. The room was serviced daily. We were on the 9th floor and this was above the noise and extremely restful. There was a guest laundry with washing machine and dryer which was very convenient and a disabled toilet on the floor, which was handy with 3 adults getting ready in the morning if someone was occupying the bathroom! The only real disappointment was the fabulous views of the cityscape were obscured with filthy windows. I mentioned this at checkout and hopefully this will be dealt with more regularly!

title: Truly outstanding apartments
text: Just back from a 2 week stay. The apartments were very very good quality, the location is excellent, and the staff are suberb.

title: Great Hotel, Recommend, few small faults
text: We did a quick overnight with the family. The suite we had catered perfectly for 2 adults, young child and infant. Plenty of room, a cot and fold out bed fitted well. The staff at the door were great, check in with smooth and nothing was a problem. I would stay again but a couple of small things that are annoying

title: Fine overall
text: There is little to complain about a hotel at a good location, with very professional who keep the house in good order and the guests in a good mood. The acoustic insulation between rooms that are separated by doors could be better. The internet in the room is poor at hours when most guest are back from town. Everything else including cleanliness, responsiveness of the staff, and the quality of the beds is just fine. Try to get a quiet room which is away from the train rails. They form a curve around the hotel |North and East facade. Hence, the trains/rails produced a constant noise. Once you keep this in mind this is a very fine hotel. Pricing is like everywhere in London, vous comprenez.

title: Not so pleasant ..........
text: Overall i would say it was not a very nice experience in there. Though the rooms are quite good but the beds are not very comfortable to sleepin. The staff is quite friendly and helpfull. Its a nice place in the evenings with lots of nice dine ins closeby.

title: Visit to o2
text: Wanted a hotel for the o2 and this is ideal, One stop from canary wharf to the o2.Just stay for a drink avoid the rush and the go back to the hotel. On arrival was giving a free upgrade as a marriot member which was a nice touch room was good,bed as always comfortable. The location is surrounded by places to eat and drink but a little quiet at weekends.Good hotel decent bar with plenty of people enjoying a last drink,was a good hotel for the o2 and made the trip a little special. Peter Kay was good also but need to get there earlier on a saturday if you want to use the vast amount of eateries as they were all full. Will stay again

title: Great Location -- good space
text: Great place to home base while in London. We were a family of four and just had two rollout beds in the living area. A little cramped but better space than prior stays in Earls Court and Gloucester Road. Easy walk to the DLR and Tube. Great food and grocery close by. Straight across the river from Greenwich.

title: Very nice
text: I've stayed in these many times particularly if my stay went beyond 4 days which it often did. Its in the same building as the hotel and you have access to most services. The rooms are spacious and have a sitting area and kitchen which beats having room service every night. The executive apartments have a different lounge from the hotel which I don't find anywhere near as inviting or good. There is only coffee there. You can have room service delivered though. But there's no breakfast or pre-dinner snacks like the other lounge. And it doesn't matter what level you are in the Marriott rewards program. I am a heavy Marriott traveler and no offense, but if I can't get it, you wont be able to either. All in all though for an extended stay or a stay with a group, the apartments are very practical.

title: Excellent service and good location
text: I stayed for 8 nights and arrived late from DC. From check in to check out service had been smooth. The room is amazingly spacious for a nice London hotel. The nearest underground tube station is only an easy 5mins (jubilee) and there is a DLR station right behind the hotel as well. The area is fun as well especially at night time with a lot of local young professionals filling the bars, malls and restaurant. The bed is comfortable and big (king) so I slept like a baby especially after a whole day of walking in central London. I also like the 24hrs room service and the bar staying open late exclusively for guests (great for us late check in folks)

title: Excellent hotel, good wi-fi and broadband service - fantastic nights sleep
text: Smart hotel, newly built and well designed. It does lack a swimming pool however there are facilities across the road. Broadband and wi-fi services work well, neat install and easy to follow directions. Food excellent and bar staff attentive during impromptu drinks gathering late in the evening. Staff and hotel GM are doing an excellent job.

title: Excellent Comfortable Family Stay
text: Stayed for 2 weeks in July in a two bedroom suite which was very spacious for my 2 teenage boys. Very clean, large rooms with 2 showers & 2 bathtubs everyone had their own. The beds are amazing, staff is very helpful and location worked out fine once we got our oyster travel cards for the trains. The down side: our ceiling started leaking 2 days before we left and they didn't really fix it. The hotel also collects their fee in advance after holding the whole amount on your card then they take a very long time to release the funds on your card even after you pay your bill. Overall a marvelous stay and memorable 50th birthday experience for my husband.

title: Excellent
text: Spent 11 days here. Was pleased with all aspects of the room. Housekeeping did a superb job of cleaning our room, and service provided by the concierges was helpful and friendly. Would stay at this Marriott location again.

title: Has so much potential
text: Recently my wife and I and our three kids (16, 13, 10) spent two nights at Marriott's Executive Apartments in London's West India Quay. We arrived via the Eurostar from Paris after spending a week there, and we chose the West India Quay property based on positive reviews on TripAdvisor and the fact that the Marriotts in central London were booked solid. The property is located in London's financial district, to the west of downtown London. The apartments occupy 4 floors (9-12 if memory serves) of an attractive, modern highrise, with regular Marriott hotel rooms on the first eight floors and with privately-owned apartments located above the Marriott apartments. Stylistically, the apartments--"villas" in our Marriott parlance--were among the most, if not the most, beautiful of all we have encountered (we are frequent Marriott villa travelers). Our 2-bedroom unit was about 1,000 sq. feet, somewhat smaller by U.S. villa standards but huge by European ones. And everything, from the carpet, to the paint colors and wallpaper, to the applicances and bathrooms, was very modern and new--quite impressive. As was the view (see pictures)--our 12th-floor apartment had a great view of the Thames and some of the other highrises in the area. In terms of location, we found some of the comments re: the property being too far away from London's major tourist attractions, not valid. It is a simple, cheap (15 pounds for five people?) and quick (15 minutes?) Tube ride to London Bridge, Westminster Abbey, the "Eye," and other attractions. Also, there is a wonderful, ritzy, huge mall nearby (less than a block), as well as some terrific restaurants. Those conveniences are welcome after a long day of sightseeing and with kids in tow. That said, it is part of a new development (less than 20 years old), so it doesn't have the same atmosphere as I'd suspect properties in central London might. The downside of the property has to do with attention to detail and logistics. We were unable to get into our apartment until 5:20 pm or so, notwithstanding having arrived at 10 am and placing a request for early check-in. The reason, however, was because a guest in our slated apartment had smoked, and the hotel was trying to abate the smoke smell. The apartment they substituted for the old one -- at our request and without a hassle to us -- was fine, but the cleaning crew had missed a few spots. (We're not that picky, but we do like the prior occupant's refrigerator items cleaned out!) They took care of the cleaning immediately and even gave us a complimentary gift basket. Throughout, they were very nice, and it was never an uncomfortable or stressful interaction. Their staff was extremely respective, kind, and helpful. We really liked them a lot. Getting nit-picky -- because overall it was a very nice experience and we'd go again -- there are still a few bugs they need to work out. Things like an executive lounge that was kept about 60 degrees, was dark, had no food, and the coffee area not kept up. There is free coffee and cookies in the lobby, which the kids liked. The breakfast buffet was also adequate. We don't want to give the wrong impression, it was a wonderful hotel. This property is easily a four-star, but with a little TLC/attention to detail, it could be a 4.5-star.

title: Nice location
text: I was here for business purpose in July 2012. It was a great stay. Canary wharf is walking distance. There are nice restaurants around the quay. Best part was evening walk around the quay on the bridge with cool breeze. Was lucky to have quay facing room.

title: Awesome 10 day vacation- Great Location and Super Friendly staff
text: I stayed here with my family for 10 days vacation. The location is great and the staff is very friendly and helpful. We never rented a car as the apartment is close to the underground railway system. We got a London pass for the family and walked everyday to the railway station/underground fast train for our site seeing trips in and around London. It is also closer to many pubs and restaurant as it is a Financial district and you find lots of corporate folks hanging out in and around the location in various pubs and restaurants. The staff was super friendly. As we planned to cook everyday, we were looking for a frying pan in the kitchen area and not able to find it. I called the front desk and told them that I needed a frying pan and they delivered it immediately. We enjoyed our stay a lot and will definitely come back to this place during our next trip. If you are staying in London for a week or more then this is the place to stay as it is reasonably priced compared to many other locations in London for the size and facility.

title: An Objective Review of MEA, West India Quay, London
text: My daughters and I stayed at the Marriott Executive Apartments (MEA) at West India Quay in London from July 13 through July 21. We had booked a one-bedroom serviced apartment. Note that if you are planning to stay seven nights, you might wish to add one more night as the rate is reduced for stays of 8+ nights. We arrived at the MEA at around 11:30 a.m. and as expected, our apartment was not quite ready and the front desk agent very politely told us so and that she would place a priority on it. They offered to hold on to our luggage and offered some suggestions on what to see and do in the meantime. That was indeed helpful. When we returned at around 2 p.m. the apartment was ready. First the location of MEA. We found it very "peaceful" after the hustle and bustle of the city. It was very nice coming back to the area, which had a surprisingly calming effect. The hotel is almost adjacent - it is connected via a not-too-long foot bridge spanning across what appears to be a canal leading to the Thames - to several indoor shopping concourses. A Tesco Metro (small) and a full-size Waitross supermarket offer lots of choices for food items, both prepared and not. Within the concourses are a whole slew of eating places so one need not worry about being hungry. There is also a row of bar/restaurants on the MEA side of the bridge. The West India Quay DLR station is conveniently located within a 3-minute walk of MEA and the Canary Wharf tube station is about a 10-minute walk. Either the DLR or the tube will connect you to anywhere you wish to go in London. The building in which the MEA is located is rather tall but it appears the Marriott hotel and the MEA occupy only the first twelve floors. We were assigned an apartment on the 10th floor. A corner unit, it overlooked about 60 central airconditioning units and railway tracks. Noise level was minimal and certainly tolerable, a testament to the quality of sound-proofing in the windows which were floor to ceiling. The apartment itself consisted of one bedroom, a seating area with an almost too-small desk, a sofa, two arm chairs and a coffee table. The bed was comfortable. I had asked for a roll-away bed, which unlike the experience of a previous reviewer, had been delivered when we got to the apartment. While I did not measure the bed, it appears to be the same size as what the previous reviewer had gotten, along with the same stained comforter. There is a safe in the room, which was handy. The smallish kitchen is equipped with what appear to be European appliances - dishwasher, stove/oven and microwave oven

title: Not exactly what I expected
text: The rooms are huge, the sight is stunning, but service is to be seriously reviewed. When I checked-in, I was asked to provide a credit card guarantee of GBP 50 per night per room This made it to GBP 300 in my case, which is enormous, considering the only extra is the VOD service (no minibar). The bed was very comfortable. I had asked for an extra bed during booking (5 months in advance), it wasn't there. They sent an uncomfortable 165 cm rollaway bed with two blood stains on the sheets and dirt on the frame. Wi-Fi is 6 pounds. per hour. And it didn't work at all in my room. The "executive room" (basically, a place with TV and a few papers) was closed during half my stay, because the hotel rents them to companies for them to hold meetings. Final word : Good location, stunning view, no service. I would have expected better from a Mariott.

title: Wonderful experience!
text: This hotel was just about perfect. The room came equipped with a mini-fridge, comfortable beds, and a spacious bathroom. The staff were accommodating and friendly, and the restaurant was excellent. I plan to stay there again!

title: NICE HOTEL,BETTER MANAGER....
text: We spent last Christmas there!! the staff were all very friendly especially duty managers!! We needed a apartment for my family to spend,Christmas together!! So we did,it was nice the night duty manager was extra,he went the extra mile to get us on the right track!! did everything to make it work!! It has a nice lobby,and room service from the hotel section can be ordered so that is a benefit!!but, a little further out from the city London itself by car,but train your there in 20 minutes. Now on our second last day, we ran into the front office manager (he was not helpful,at all?being a member you would think he would help to get a reservation for the NEW YEAR,he was more concerned to CHECK US OUT,HE WAS very persistent made house keeping ring our doorbell constantly!! he would call atleast 15times to get us out! he would not listen to me,he hade made arrangements the day before for us to have a later check out,at 4pm due to having pains in my leg,and taking pain killers after surgery of the knee!! we were 10 minutes late,for check out!! but, on check in we came at 12.30 am still did not have the requests i asked the day before?all though i paid for the day before??so the night manager,who did his best to do what should of been done the day before!! SO would i be back?NO!! but everyone has the rights to try it out for them selves!! GOOD LUCK!!

title: Best overall London location for value and activity.
text: I am just finishing up a week at the London Marriott Executive apartments in West India Quay, Canary Wharf. After flying into Heathrow, and then taking the Heathrow Express, and 2 tube trains, then a 8 minute walk to the hotel, I finally arrived. At first, I was thinking this was too far out of range for most things, but soon discovered I was quite wrong. Located in the heart of London's financial district, anchored by all of the major bank buildings, there are more than ample choices for dining and shopping, thanks to the local high-end malls and numerous restauraunts nearby. The hotel is located just across the footbridge from the malls and offices. It is a convenient and nice walk to the pier, where you can easily pick up the Thames Clipper service for a short and scenic 10-minute ride to the London Eye area, and all the other attractions nearby. If you prefer the more frequent and efficient tube service, the Jubilee line is a brief walk from the hotel, and you can be at Westminster Abbey in 10 minutes with no changes. I found the hotel staff to be quite friendly, although you are a bit more disconnected when staying in the apartments than I assume you would be as a regular hotel guest. There are no Concierge Lounge privileges if you are an apartment guest. There is an apartment lounge, but that is only some chairs and tables with no food or drink. I would suggest asking for a room away from the closely connected Light Rail station on the West side of the building. My room was on the 9th floor at that end and you hear every train coming in and out until 1am and starting again at 5am. Not something I didn't get used to, but would prefer to be on the other side for a city view anyway. I have stayed all over London, and this has been the most pleasing accomodations when you factor location and value into consideration.

title: Absolutely faultless
text: My mother and I have stayed in one of the King Executive rooms 2 years in a row, with our 3rd visit coming up in a few weeks. We always stay around late November/ early December time as Canary Wharf around Christmas is beautiful. The apartments are found just moments the DLR which is very useful. The staff are friendly and extremely efficient, build quality and cleanliness of the building and rooms is absolutely 5*. Couldn't ask for more. Apartments are very spacious, well equipped and wonderfully designed. It comes at a high cost of roughly £760 for just 2 nights, but as a weekend treat it suits us absolutely perfectly. Can't wait to be back in a few weeks!

title: Our new London Retreat.
text: Lovely Staff, lovely room. Very comfortable bed. Breakfast was excellent, although tea making could be better.All in all a very enjoyable overnight stay. Location is ideal for DLR. into London central, also for shopping malls.

title: Great location for business. Staff are friendly.
text: This hotel building is connected with executive apartments but they have different entrance. The staff are friendly and service is great. The room is a good size and have a nice view of the wharf. It's worth it to get the executive access. You will get breakfast, afternoon snacks and you can get into the access lounge 24 hours to get bottle of water, soda, coffee,etc. It is right on the financial district but it's a little far from tourist attraction. DLR and underground transportation is walking distance. If you are tourist, I would recommend to stay around central London.

title: Found My Home In London
text: Having stayed at some really crummy apartments which stated they were 4 or 5 stars, for London, these apartments are really great. Quite expensive but well worth it especially if you are a Marriott Rewards member. I have stayed twice in April and May and I enjoyed both stays really well. Very professional and friendly staff, excellent apartments with kitchenette and good breakfast. Well equipped gym and a cinema literally next door. The DLR is also practically attached to the hotel and I loved my stay.

title: Great for families.
text: Stayed in a one bedroom apartment whilst attending a concert at the O2 with my wife and teenage daughters. Check in and out was a bit slow, with little information offered. The apartment was very nice and twin beds made up in the lounge area. Well equiped kitchen. Had a couple of drinks in the bar and the staff were fantastic, very chatty and friendly made up for the miserable front desk staff. We had breakfast sent to the room which was OK. Parking opposite the hotel is £20 as per the website but if you give the reception the token its reduced to £11.

title: 30th birthday treat
text: I went and stayed at one of the apartments this weekend just gone. The check in service was smooth and the lady behind the desk I would describe as an asset to the busy. I mentioned that I was celebrating my birthday to her and that I would like some champagne glasses and an ice bucket brought up to the room. I was cooking a meal for some friends and I found all the utensils I needed,and the room was spacious and beautifully situated over looking the river. When the ice bucket arrived, Bemnet Werede-the lady who had checked me in, had very kindly arranged a complimentary bottle of champagne for me and a kind not to wish me a happy birthday. I felt very special and cared for, so thank you. I had a fantastic evening and found the client care throughout the hotel & staff was impeccable. I shall happily return to this hotel. Many thanks

title: Great hotel but with rubbish room service
text: Stayed here for two nights whilst my partner ran the London Marathon as we wanted somewhere spacious to relax before and after the race. In terms of cleanliness and comfort and facilties it scores ten out of ten. Location in Docklands is great with lots of restaurants and bars and shops on your doorstep. The DLR is too so getting into central London is easy too. For people who haven't considered staying in docklands for leisure, you really should. The hotels out there offer far better value and are much more modern than their central London counterparts. We didn't have breakfast, as the apartment has its own kitchen and it was just easier doing that with young kids. The only complaint was room service for dinner one night which was terrible.... it took over an hour, was very expensive and the food was just pretty average. I would expect better for a 5 star hotel. That aside, I would defintely go back.

title: Nice but could be better
text: I am half way through this stay and I really want to write great things. The location is great if you need to be in CW, it's new, it's a Marriott it should be good. Unfortunately it just continue to be average. The easterly rooms are alongside the DLR so if you suffer from light sleeping this is a disaster. The fridge in the room didn't work, the staff were using the guest laundry to wash hotel laundry- surely there is a hotel laundry for this. The water pressure is limp as is the incredibly expensive wifi! £75 for five days, surely they must realise that this is expensive and if you want to charge for premium Internet speeds in excess of 2mbs should be offered oh and of course if there is something wrong with it the hotel makes you speak to the suppliers call centre, well that's an hour I won't get back and I fear the £75 is gone too. Anyway the room is nice and very clean, although if you are over 1.90 you might find the bed too short. The staff are generally helpful although the lack of English is sometimes an issue. Anyway Ihope the second week goes better as everything should be just that bit better.

title: Good hotel, nice room but .....
text: I stayed from the 13 till the 20 of June 2012. The hotel was great. The appt. was well maintained, cleaned and with excellent in-room dining service. Location wise its ideal. The nearest station is right at the door step. I thoroughly enjoyed my stay with my wife and my toddler. However at the time of check-in the lady took a pre-auth on my card. On the 15 or 16 of June I deposited cash at the reception and asked the person to release the pre-auth. Which he confirmed that it has been forwarded to the bank and it will take 3-4 working days. At the time of checking out – June 20, 2012 I again asked the supervisor about the release of the pre-auth and she said it has been processed. I returned back from London on the 23 of June and checked with my bank. And was informed that its still not released. I send a query on the Marriott International website along with a request for a copy of my folio and was promised that "the hotel will get back to me in the next 3 - 5 working days" (which was by the way on the 29 of June). Till date I have yet to hear from the hotel or Marriott International even after sending several reminders. I spent an approx 2000GBP during my stay at the hotel and I feel that the hotel does not really care about you once you have checked out. I have rated the hotel quite low in OVERALL RATING keeping the fact that my money (approx 1450 GBP) is still blocked and the hotel and Marriott does not have the courtesy to even respond back. Needless to mention that I will not be staying in any of the Marriott Properties in future.

title: BOOK IT WAY OUT!
text: We were in London for 3 nights on our way to a tour or Ireland. This is a real apartment and we had a fantastic corner view 1 bedroom with kitchen overlooking the new olympic stadium area and the bustling Canary Wharf area. The West India Quay area including Canary Wharf is full of shops, restaurants, offices, river boat landing, and several underground stations. This was our base for exploring London and you can't beat the location, value, luxury, and Marriott excellence here. The staff was very professional and helpful. The apartment was very clean. The bedding was high end Marriott quality. Request a free rollaway bed, and you will get a very comfortable extra bed. The restaurant and bar Manhattan Grill on the ground floor was very nice and great for watching sports on large flat screens. The apartment had 2 flat screens with many digital channels. With all the activity you can see from the many windows you would think it would be noisy, but we heard nothing outside of our room. The windows can be covered with heavy drapes and sheers, but you will resist this at night because of the spectacular view. Marriott Gold status members receive complimentary high speed internet service. I highly recommend this hotel, but make sure you book an apartment. Also, take advantage of the Thames River boat service from the Tower of London back to Canary Wharf which is much more pleasant than the Underground.

title: Great room with a very nice view,
text: We had an apartment and lived it! The staff was very friendly and the room was spacious and comfortable.

title: canary wharf
text: good place for business trip. rooms are decent . place is very boring

My husband and I had some business to sort and chose this hotel as we had never been to canary wharf.We stayed two nights 4-6 Jan 2012. Easy to get to as near tube and DLR. Check in staff very pleasant and helpful. Hotel lobby well presented. Had lunch at the fish restaurant onsite, Curve. Only had a choice of 2 actual fish, which I thought was strange for a fresh fish restaurant but what we had was ok. Had access to executive lounge which was well stocked at all times. Numerous magazines to browse. The room was comfortable and we had a river view which was a lovely. Very spacious well decorated room and a nice bathroom. Comfortable bed. There are many places to eat within walking distance. Walked 10 minutes to Gauchos Argentinian steakhouse. 10/10 for food,service and ambiance. Had a few drinks at Via bar next door to Marriott, good cocktails and decor. Transport to Brick Lane and Spitalfields Market was on our doorstep. Also visited the Docklands museum which was free and only 2 minutes walk.

title: Fantastic stay, excellent location..... bit pricey though
text: The Marriott West India Quay is the ideal location for those on business or leisure trips. Rooms are clean and and of decent size with minibar and room safe. There is no complimentary bottled drinks however, and wifi is not free. Toilet is adequately sized with a long bath and WC. We had a king sized double bed which can easily accommodate 3 adults of European built. Pillows are soft and linen is clean, giving a good night's sleep. We had a room facing the plaza and part of the water front. We stayed on the 2nd floor and away from the lifts, so it was rather quiet. The DLR is just nearby within walking distance (7 min) to its nearest station (Poplar). Besides you can take the Jubilee line underground at Canary Wharf station which is about 10 min walk from the hotel. This hotel is hence ideally located with public transport easily accessible. Staff are friendly and ever willing to help out with info. Check in was fairly speedy and so was check out (if you did not use the minibar!). Breakfast was included in the package. There are the usual spread of full English breakfast with breads, pastries, cereals, fruits and juices to choose from. During my stay it was the same food everyday but I have no complaints. Definitely a very ideal place to stay.

title: Fantastic Canary Wharf Hotel
text: Absolutely loved this hotel at Canary Wharf. Attended an evening function in the hotel. Great bedrooms too. Very comfortable beds. Service was very good as well. Would recommend to anyone staying at Canary Wharf.

title: Great for business travel
text: Stayrd in ths hotel for a week on business. Great hotel, neat rooms, good food and nice ambience. Overall excellent experience. Will stay again!

title: The most sophisticated weekend till date
text: I spoke to the hotel a few weeks as i planned to propose to my wife in their Junior suite, which by the way was a fantastic price plus the extra perks from the hotel... the room was laid with roses,bottle of champagne and strawberries with chocolate dips just as my now wife loves them. Great attention to detail and presentation was fabulous. The room, its view... All i can say is WOW even that i work in Canary Wharf, this hotel made me see the best of it Always in my heart ,this hotel got a lot of sentimental attachment needless to say!

title: Very Nice Would Stay Again
text: Stayed at these apartments for 5 days, it's very nice, would stay there again we were in a 2 bed roomed apartment, there are actually three televisions in the apartment unlike how it states on the Marriott website that there are two, nice welcome pack, mini jams in the fridge, two cartons of orange juice and one bottle of red wine, 6 packs of different mini cereals, two alpen bars, large bag of ready salted kettle chips, the oven and microwave are by Neff, everything looked brand new even though the hotel was opened in 2004, there is a washing machine and dryer on the 9th and 11th and 12th floor the executive lounge on the 9th floor is not like a standard executive lounge in Marriott you only get tea & coffee in the morning, no afternoon cakes etc and no canapés in the evening etc, but you have a kitchen so you don’t need it really, and staying in the apartment if you are wanting to get Marriott reward points you only get 2.5 points per US Dollar spent accommodation only (unlike staying in a normal Marriott room where you get 10 points per US Dollar spent) and also you only accrue one night for each three you stay towards your elite profile, and you cannot use the hotel’s normal executive lounge if you are a gold or platinum Marriott member
