title: Good hotel, bit too handy for the rail station
text: The hotel was much better than I anticipated, rooms well appointed and of decent size. The breakfast buffet was comprehensive and service prompt. The two downsides to the hotel are that it does not have it's own car park (you have to use a public car park about 200m down the road) and the rooms on one side of the hotel the rooms face the docklands light railway with trains rumbling past bedroom windows by just a few feet..... That aside I actually liked the hotel.

title: Good central location
text: Good location just off the central Canada Square area of Canary Wharf with all the main banks, Jubilee line tube station, Colonnade shops all within 5-10min walk max. Hotel is on one of the Canals and MUST ask for a front facing room as view good. Avoid back of hotel as looks onto the Docklands Light Rail line and material noise Rooms well equipped with mini bar, aircon, iron, safe etc as expected. The room I stayed in had a bath shower - not great. Part of the hotel also has apartments but haven’t seen these, only hotel rooms There is wifi but charged at c.6GBP for an hour. Full restaurant for breakfast and dinner though suggested that for dinner there are numerous restaurants / bars just outside the hotel. All in, good location, central, friendly service... much like any other Marriott.

title: Great location!
text: We returned to Canary Wharf where we used to live and stayed at the Marriott Hotel India Quay. We were upgraded to the concierge floor and had a wonderful view of the area. The room was beautifully fitted, large flat screen TV, enough room for laptop and free wifi! Very clean bathroom with all the amenities. Very close to tube and shopping. We will definitely return!

title: Great hotel, great location!
text: A great hotel that makes for the ideal place to stay in East London with underground/subway links right by the hotel! Beautiful inside with fantastic staff! Surrounded by Canary Wharf that has a large number of restaurants to choose from and a shopping mall all with a short walk from the hotel!

title: A Blaze of Publicity!
text: My wife and I were kindly invited to The Spirit of Fire Awards on Friday, 4th November and this is where we stayed overnight. It was easy to find, although the dropping off/picking up area was a little cramped. However, the hotel allowed us to park right outside as I was on crutches and had my blue badge with me, so this convenience more than made up for the lack of space. Staff were first-class, from check-in to portering and doormen and our room was a very comfortable twin on floor 3, adjacent to lifts, another useful factor for me. The hotel entrance leads into a vast lobby, with staircases and then two sets of lifts, but it seemed odd to have to go up one storey to get to reception/check-in. Our room was clean, well equipped and comfortable and I appreciated the hand-rail in the bathroom, which enabled me to shower safely. We did not stay for breakfast, as we had to get home promptly, but friends who did said they paid £48 for two breakfasts, which sounded extreme, to put it mildly. Perhaps they had everything on the menu? The doormen and porter really earned their tips, sorting out luggage, taxis and coaches and when we quickly returned because I had left things behind, a porter soon retrieved every last item in double quick time. We would use this Marriott again for the convenient location in Canary Wharf and for the very efficient and helpful staff.

title: Amazing!
text: We chose this property as we have previously stayed at other Marriotts within city center. This is in the financial district and has a great feel as if in downtown Manhatten. It is on the water with great shops and restaurants all in walking distance. The DLR and tube are across the street. The hotel itself is wonderful with great views of the city and wonderful lounge and restaurant. The concierge lounge open for breakfast and early afternoon tea as well appetizers and dessert early evening with unlimited cocktails was a plus. Would stay here again if travelling back to London.

title: Stay Anywhere else
text: I knew all was not well when I asked directions for this hotel, this was necessary as their website has a map but does not show the hotel! Two security guards and one businessman , in the area had never heard of it. The sheets in the room were stained, the paint on the bathroom ceiling was peeling off, the TV was out of the ark, I haven't seen a picture like that since the 70's, the speakers seemed to have ball bearings in them. I am recovering from a broken foot and wanted to use the entrance with no steps, I was told by reception I could only exit by this route, so for two days I climbed the steps at the front of the hotel. Later It was revealed that could enter by the entrance with no steps. I forgot my key card one day, this is needed to use the elevator, I asked three members of staff if they could send the lift to the my floor, their answer was I would have to wait for some other guest to use the lift. In the end I took the stairs. The bar was a joke, screaming kids and load music, in addition I realised when it came to check out that for the privilage of buying a drink at the bar I was charged 12.5% service. This hotel is listed as five star, if this is five star then I am basil brush. Go anywhere but here, if you don't you are going to be very ******* off.

title: Good location if on business in Canary Wharf
text: I stayed in a studio apartment in the Marriott West India Quay for two nights on business. The hotel is just off the West India Quay DLR station, very convenient if flying to City airport. The studio was very well equipped: relatively big kitchen with all appliances, flat screen TV, desk and sitting area and very comfortable king bed. I had read in previous reviews that it can be quite noisy with the DLR, but my room was facing the station and I was able to sleep perfectly ok (I must say that I was on the 10th floor though). The hotel is just 5 minutes walk from Canada Square, so it will spare you the journey from the city centre if you are in Canary Wharf on business. Prices are not exactly cheap, but are in line with other London hotels of the same category. Note: cleaning takes place only once a week for longer stays, and daily for stays shorter than five days.

title: Did not love this place
text: My husband was traveling on business and I was along for the ride. We stayed in a Marriott in London last year and it was fabulous. Unfortunately it is no longer affiliated with the Marriott brand this year. In any case my husband prefers to book with Marriott and has Gold status with them. We were given access to the concierge floor but not actually located there. Our room was right outside the conference rooms as in across the hall was a conference room. The room directly overlooked the above ground railway tracks as well. After a day in the room I called to let them know the room was not cooling off. It was actually a nice temperature outside while our room set on the lowest temp would not cool off. They offered a fan and the opportunity to move. We were moved the next day into a room that had an adjoining room attached and it also overlooked the railway system. Let's just say, I've never had a good experience with adjoining rooms. You can always hear what's going on in the next room. I asked to move immediately and we were moved to the only room available apparently and it had an interior view. Not lovely but at least the room was cool. I feel like this whole review is a complaint but here goes. The bathroom was small and the bathtub was very hard to get in and out of. I'm not an old lady or anything but it was so deep even my husband had to hold onto the towel rack to get out. The shower was barely a trickle and very annoying. The first room didn't have the water pressure problem but I didn't want to call down again. I just took twice as long in the shower to get all the shampoo out of my hair. Usually at a hotel of this caliber there would be robes in the closet. I had to call for those too and constantly remind them that I wanted 4 towels not 2 everyday. We stayed for 6 nights. Let's talk about the free wifi. What a joke! In order to get free wifi you had to connect your device to their hardwire cord in your room. It was a phone cord type which meant only a laptop could connect. Once it recognized your device then you could use it wirelessly. Needless to say there was no way to use my ipad or iphone unless I walked outside the hotel and connected with some other free wifi from one of the restaurants nearby. We decided to try the hotel restaurant one night as well and although the place wasn't even half full we were told we needed to wait 10 minutes. 20 minutes later we walked out and no one even noticed. The only bright spot was the concierge lounge. If you don't have access to that why would you stay here at all? I certainly won't be back. Don't be fooled by the beautiful picture online of the exterior of the hotel. Those waterview rooms aren't part of the hotel, only the corporate apartments.

title: Fantastic stay
text: Stayed here for one night when my husband and I went to see Lady Gaga at the O2. The suite was really fantastic. Very spacious, more than big enough for the two of us, it would have easily housed a family. The hotel was in a great location, very close to the tube at Canary Wharf, and the shopping centre. We took the Thames Clipper service to the O2, which dropped us back at West India Quay on the way back. It couldn't have been a better experience. It was very near Christmas and the whole area was buzzing with people all out on their Christmas do's from work. There was a lovely atmosphere. I would stay there again in a heartbeat.

title: Awesome hotel ..... but not in Central London
text: Strengths: Good location (not central though) Weaknesses: Expensive I stayed for 2 nights in Marriott West India Quay in Aug’07 on a Business Trip to London. I paid GBP 195 per might which is awfully expensive compared to any standards and does not add up from a value for money perspective. In half that amount is you get some other hotel offering similar facilities services but it will not have the Mariott Tag on it. In such 5 Stars you just land up paying for the brand and not only for the services they have to offer. The hotel is in Canary Wharf, which is significantly far from central London. From Heathrow it will take you about an hour and a half to get here and you will have to changeover from the Picadilly Line to the Jubilee Line. In addition the Mariott West India Quay hotel is a significantly long walk from the Canary Wharf Station and if you are tugging along suitcases this may again be a problem. The hotel the is bang opposite the West India Quay station of the DLR (Docklands Railway) so it would be great if you could take the DLR and not the Jubilee Line tube if you have to access this hotel (unless obviously you are coming by cab). For the complete review, visit my travel blogsite on [----]

title: Seven Dials Hotel
text: Great location. 24 hour front desk. Basic 70s decor. Own small bathroom. Simple buffet breakfast included. Helpful staff. A bit noisy on the road side rooms with night sirens. Handy to Covent Garden, tubes and buses....

title: Faulty towers!
text: Where to start! Paid alot for the night our room was tiny had no hot water are toilet was on the landing to share with everyone else, sheets dirty wasnt very clean at all, breakfast was awful good location though if you can put up with such a dump!

title: Theatre Land
text: Hotel has recently been refurbished so the rooms are relatively new, and the hotel is in the heart of theatre land. The nearest tube station is Covent Garden and direct pedestrian route is via Neal Street, as the property is close to the junction with Monmouth Street and Shaftsbury Avenue. I had a room at the back of the hotel, which avoided the street noise, but unfortunately the walls are thin with little sound insulation and the room was also quite small. On the plus side, breakfast was help yourself full English.

title: Location, location, location!
text: As the title of my review suggests, the location of this hotel is it's main selling point. It is right in the heart of the West End and a short walk from Piccadilly Circus and other main attractions. I defy anyone to find another hotel offering bed and breakfast for two people for £85 per night in anywhere near as good a location. The hotel was clean and the staff were all friendly, although the one time we needed directions the Polish woman on the desk had only been working there for a couple of days and couldn't help us - not her fault I suppose! Breakfast was buffet style and consisted of a full English breakfast, but with not a great deal of choice. However, it was more than adequate for us. The room was an en-suite but was very tiny and the stairs to the rooms are extremely narrow. The rooms are so small I would not recommend anyone to stay there for more than a few days unless you like living out of a suitcase - there is very little space anywhere to store your clothes! I would be happy to stay there again (for short periods), however it was my girlfriends first ever trip to the UK and she refuses to let me book this hotel again for a planned trip to London in December. I've tried explaining the plus points in respect of price and location, but she wants somewhere with enough room to be be able to sit other than on the bed and where you have enough space to hand your clothes!

title: Little gem
text: Spent 5 nights here recently, perfect location, Rooms are small but very clean, great English buffet breakfast, very well cooked, and staff were very friendly and helpful, would definitely stay again.

title: Great location for great price
text: We were very happy with Hotel Seven Dials. It was comfty, clean and warm. It offered just enough for the price range. Breakfast was simple but very good. But the best was the location! So many choices of restaurants around and walking distance to everything! We went to see a play in Palace theater which was 4 minutes away. Really, very good.

title: Fab budget hotel
text: This is an excellent hotel if you're on a budget. Rooms are basic but good enough. The location could not be better and breakfast is lovely. The only problem is that the stars are a bit lethal so don't go if you have mobility issues. Staff very warm and friendly..

title: Very good place to stay!
text: We stayed here for ten nights and we were extremely pleased with the hotel. The staff were friendly and helpful. Excellent location, right near the live theatre district. The only let downs we had was that the room was quite small, and when we pulled out the rolling bed we could barely get around. The other problem for us, being vegetarians, was breakfast. It was buffet-style but there wasn't a great selection for vegetarians, and after ten mornings, it became quite boring. But it is well worth it for the price. It covers everything you need for what you pay for. On our check out date, we weren't leaving London until the evening, and the staff let us leave our luggage in the hotel, which was very thoughtful of them and something they definitely weren't entitled to do. I would definitely recommend staying here. We would definitely stay again when travelling back to London.

title: Location, location,location...and that's it
text: I really want to give Seven Dials a higher review

title: Adequate - for short stay
text: You get what you pay for. Clean room, brilliant location and very friendly and informed staff. However, if you have mobility problems then perhaps this is not for you. VERY steep stairs, so steep we did not go for breakfast. Curtains thin so let's light from street in and it is a bit noisy. That being said the location and staff make up for the hotels shortcomings.

title: I almost don't want to write this .....
text: I almost don't want want to write this review. The more people who know about this absolute gem of a hotel, the less chance I have of getting a room whenever I want. I've stayed here twice in the last year. And I'm booked in again next week for a night at Ronnie Scott's with girlfriends. The first time I stayed was with my mother to give her a shopping treat. We stayed in the main hotel in a room directly over-looking the street. My mother is elderly and I was a bit worried about the narrow stairs (no lifts) - but they put us in a 1st floor room and she coped. Let's face it, it's not as if you're going to be going in and out of the room regularly - just once or twice a day - so a little bit of stair walking shouldn't be an issue. Everything is very compact in the main hotel. Small entrance, small reception - reminds me of some of the cute bijoux hotels in the Paris Latin Quarter. Very welcoming reception. The man coped with checking us in whilst answering a seemingly endless string of telephone calls - smiling all the time. The room was clean and bright with plain white linen bedding - no frills, but no complaints here. Yes, the en suite shower room was very, very small - just enough room to get in, shower and get out. Old fashioned sliding door between the bedroom and shower room. You certainly couldn't change in there - but why would it's size be a problem for some reviewers? Change in the bedroom! I see the shower rooms as just an added extra. For the price in this amazing location I wouldn't have been surprised not to have had an en suite at all. Best of all was walking out onto the street (with the intention of meandering down to Covent Garden) to find Monmouth Street itself was a buzzing hive of shops and cafés. We were just zig-zagging across the road popping in and out of Hotel Chocolat, jewellery shops, little clothes shops, gift shops et al. The entrance to Neal's Yard is a minute away. The top of Neal Street leading down to Covent Garden is 30 seconds away in the other direction. Perfect. Yes, it's a little noisy street-side - but you book a centrally located hotel so that you can be just that - central. It's only cafés and shops around - not night clubs and music bars. And they're all closed by midnight - so I can honestly say that having a room on the 1st floor over-looking the street was no problem whatsoever. Slept like a baby - and so did Mum. The second time I stayed was for 2 nights with a girlfriend over New Years Eve. We were given a room in the annexe in Endell Street just around the corner. 2nd floor - over-looking the street - and gob-smackingly amazing for the price. A very large room with 3 beds (2 singles and a double). Basic as before - with a tiny shower room again - but clean and bright with a fridge, kettle and little TV. Don't expect the most up-to-date furnishings - and I agree with one reviewer that plug points are in - ummmm - how do I say this - unusual places - but so what! Come on guys. £50 per person per night or less (we're paying £35pp next week) - including breakfast - in the heart of London between the two buzziest parts of town, Covent Garden and Soho. Don't knock this place for not giving you Claridges luxury. If you want that then go and pay £800+ a night for your room. At the end of the day you're getting the same thing - a clean, comfy bed, a place to wash, complimentary tea and coffee - just not designer bedding, a Nespresso machine and goose down pillows. Oh - one point - you get towels and soap - but no shampoo. So take your own. We were so tired after our New Year celebrations we weren't ready to check out on time on January 2nd. We didn't leave the room til after midday. The hotel were very relaxed about it. No pressure to get out - the cleaning lady just knocked on the door the went away very happily when we said we weren't ready. And reception looked after our bags for the rest of the day while we went off for lunch before going home. Just out of curiosity I went into the reception of the 4* hotel near The Seven Dials Hotel to enquire about a room for the evening. Yes, they had one available - at £425 per night including breakfast. I walked out laughing. I've found my home from home in London. I hope enough of you go to make sure they stay open and profitable - but not too many of you please. I want to know they'll always have a room available for me.

title: brilliant position but very basic
text: This position of this hotel is amazing for theatres, covent garden area and central london shopping. At £120 per night it wasn't cheap but for london it was. Our room was the smallest possible, not even a full sized double bed - and shoved up against the wall so very inconvenient. The bedcover was stained and dirty - inexcusable to my mind. The bathroom was adequate but again tiles + shower curtain were grubby so not very inviting. The furniture in the room was cheap and falling apart - wardrobe didn't close fully, headboard not attached to the bed, that sort of thing. They did provide tea/coffee making so that was very welcome after a day of sight seeing. The included breakfast was fine - hot and colds but no fruit and choice of only 2 cereals. We only stayed overnight, so for that it was bearable but any longer and we would need something a bit nicer.

title: Great Location...Cramped Hotel
text: I stayed here for the location... very convenient to all West End things to do from shopping to museums to shows, but not a place I'd stay away again. Hotel staff are pleasant but the place, including room, isn't very clean, the inclusive breakfast rubbery and the 4 floor walkup on very narrow steep stairs (no working elevator) is hazardous. Evidence of expansion which accounted for a lot of the dust, but no attempt made to seal off the corridors. No lobby to sit in either and there was no way the room was comfortable enough to relax.

title: Small rooms, but good location
text: I stayed there one night for an event which was taking place at Covent Garden. It's located perfectly if you want to go to there or to the theatres nearby, and nicely priced. The rooms are really small and amenities are very basic, but the staff is very friendly and overall it is a very good stop if you treat it as a night harbour during sightseeing or a short stay.

title: Not the best
text: But not the worst... For the price and the location...you won’t find any cheaper. It’s not dirty but it’s run down and tired, they are re furbing so very messy, lift doesn’t work and stairs are very very narrow. It’s noisy (but it’s Covent gardens) fan works and keeps you cool but also looks like it would fly off the wall! Staff are friendly enough. Breakfast we ate on the first day, second day we couldn’t stomach it! Bacon is nice everything else cold....no milk for cereal...toast already cooked so cold and wobbly...scrambled eggs watery. It is included in the price but I wouldn’t eat it if it was free! I would probably stay again as location is fab and after the refurb it may be better. Plus beds are comfy enough..ok for one or 2 nights but don’t expect any luxuries!

title: Best location!
text: I love Seven Dials Hotel. The location is one of the best in London. For me anyway. I LOVE Seven Dials and Covent Garden areas and with this in mind I couldn’t find a better situated hotel in this price range. Standard if the hotel itself is not luxurious, but you have all you need to spend a long weekend in the city.

title: Could Do Better!
text: We needed a cheap hotel close to the theatre that were going to and decided to ignore the negative comments and book this

title: Beyond adequate description
text: This is by some margin the worst hotel we have stayed in. I will add the pictures but even they don't even get close to describing how poor and thoroughly unacceptable the place is. All you will get is difficulty and an argument if you raise concerns and then total blank looks and silence when they hand back your refund that you had to fight for via Booking.com. I will list the facts...not opinions, just plain facts: 1. There is no lift. Up to the 3rd floor and over very tricky stairs...that were covered in dust sheets as the place is a total building site. Stunning. 2. Down the stairs, hands covered in dust from the renovations. Be very careful you down trip. 3. No air conditioning and you will bake, bake, bake. Yes, there is a fan...have you ever seen the film 'Contact' where the seat in the spacecraft wobbles and eventually detaches from the ceiling? Well, that fan threatens the same...laughable and pathetic. 4. A room of dirt and filth on levels we could not stomach...the pictures are amazing. 'We do our best', said the chap. Yeah? Oh really? 5. Noise...oh boy is it noisy...there is a massive vent strapped to the rear external wall and it is like a plane taking off. Shut the windows and...bake some more! 6. The shower curtain...I can't type the monster of a thing...look at the pictures. 7. Breakfast...no plates left, food of dubious quality, cutlery needs throwing away, kitchen door non-existent, washing up lady on full display with her washing up bowl...so not machine-level cleanliness...I couldn't eat, I felt sick. Oh, you'll bake down there too. 8. Service...nope, they have no idea about either basic standards of hoteling or how to manage unhappy customers. 'Well no-one else has complained', he said. I wonder if he has read the feedback...I have and I am amazed I booked...I am an idiot. 9. I was offered a different room. We eventually declined on the basis of basic hygiene. 10. He actually told me he would only refund me for the 2nd night if he could let the room. I was appalled but he wouldn't engage with me, only the booking agent. They were good, to be fair. I should have been handed back every penny of the cost as it was simply an outrageous night's stay. I could write a book it was that bad.

title: Great value for money
text: Have just come back from a 4 night stay at this hotel with my husband. Before booking I had read the hotel's website and comments from people who had previously stayed here so had a good idea what to expect. The room was small but had everything we needed and both the bedroom and en suite were spotlessly clean and there was always hot water and everything worked. One side of the bed was up against the wall but this did not bother us but could be a problem to older or less mobile people. We only once met anyone on the stairs but it did not cause a problem for us to back up to the landing. The staff were all very friendly and the English breakfast was excellent. The location was great and we would definitely stay there again.

title: Great stay, once again❤️❤️❤️
text: We just got back from a 4 day stay at the Seven Dials Hotel and once again it was great. We had room nr•12, which was big enough for the 2 of us! You have all the comfort but just on a smaller scale! The hotel is located in the coolest and nicest area of the city. You are only a 5 minute walk away from Leicester Square and Covent Garden. You can shop till you drop, enjoy great food and drinks, meet awesome people,... I would recommend it to everyone! This is the best!

title: Location Location Location
text: The Good: You can't beat where this place is for the price. Minutes from Covent Garden, the British Museum, and the heart of Soho with multiple tube stops within a 5 minute walk. The Bad: Yes, it is basic, but we stayed in a Quad in the front of the hotel. Basic is an understatement. It was tiny with essentially cots for beds, terrible traffic noise and hot inside regardless of the temperature outside. The breakfast was sub-par as well. The location and price probably may trump the poor conditions, but I am not sure I would stay there again.

title: OVER PRICED
text: the first room we were offered was very small with the bed against the corner, and on the third floor, without a lift. the stairs are hard to negotiate. The manager was very helpful and changed the room to a larger one, which was slightly dated but comfortable, shower good, but no shower gel or shampoo which you would expect for £115 per night, breakfast no choice of cereal, fry up good, toast and tea lacking. OVERALL FOR £115 VERY DISSAPOINTED.

title: Great Location!
text: The hotel was just 5 minutes walk from the Covent Garden tube station. Found it easy with the directions give. We arrived about 12 midday and they allowed us to check-in 2 hours early so that was fantastic! although the room was on the top floor which was not fantastic! Must have climbed at least 50+ steps which is not ideal when you have luggage! The room itself was just basic, double bed, t.v shower etc tea making facilities but no tea/coffee/milk etc! the toilet was shared with others on the same floor - not a problem though. the breakfast was lovely. it was a hot buffet breakfast....bacon, sausage, variety of eggs, beans, tomatoes. toast and tea/coffee. so fill up on breakfast as much as you want! staff were nice and polite, free wi-fi. the location was fantastic because of the trips and restaurants we had booked! 5 minutes walk to the Lyceum and 10 minutes to the Strand - we booked a meal at The Savoy which was amazing. around 15 minutes walk to The Embankment (London Eye etc) so there was no need to use the underground as everything was within walking distance! would definately stay here again!

title: DICK TURPIN IS ALIVE AND WELL
text: Dick Turpin is alive and well and getting away with daylight robbery in Covent Garden,was charged £100 to stay in a room which is of a poor standard,kettle that didn't work,cobwebs in the bathroom.that was also of a poor standard.Breakfast was of also a poor standard only Branflakes or cornflakes the milk was not in a jug but left in plastic bottle,the full english was buffet so kept warm under lights,so the eggs you could bounce,bacon&sausages dried up because of the hot lamps. Only good point is the location to a lot of the shows.

title: central location
text: this is just your basic hotel. no frills but clean, very good full english breakfast,all we wanted was a bed for the weekend and thats what we got, spotless white bedding and towels,a comfy bed, in a central location, (we didnt even use the Tea or coffee thats in the room ) thats how long we spent in the room. so many restaurants + bars in the area,also a hop +a skip to Covent garden .very friendly staff, would stay again when in london.

title: Cosy and Friendly
text: We only stayed 1 night for a Theatre Break but found this Hotel extremely central and reasonably priced for our purposes. The staff were extremely helpful and allowed us to leave our cases in the room before the cleaner arrived. The room itself was quite large and on the first floor and as we were at the back of the hotel, it was extremely quiet. Everything was fresh and clean and the ensuite had a glorious large shower. Yes, the stairs are very narrow, but we only had smallish cases so they weren't really a problem - larger cases however would be more of a scramble, especially if climbing to higher floors. The basement breakfast room is quite cosy with an adequate full english on offer - not so much of yoghurts and fruits etc if that is more your style, but we thoroughly enjoyed our cooked preference anyway. An ideal site if you want to be central for theatres and shops in general and we will certainly be returning in the future.

title: great budget hotel
text: I stayed here with 2 other female friends in March. We stayed in the annexe on Endel Street and ate breakfast in the main hotel. The room was £130 per night. We had no complaints at all. The room was big enough for the 3 of us and the bathroom was small but adequate. All the beds were comfortable and there was a TV and kettle. There is no wifi in this block but there is an excellent 3G signal so Iphone and Ipad users are sorted! The block was located above a letting agency and far enough away from the one or two pubs on Endell street. By central London standards, our room was quiet! For a couple of nights, this place is great. There isn't a lot of space to hand alot of clothes so if staying more than a couple of nights then that might be an issue. In all honesty though, I challenge anyone to find a cheaper hotel that as is great as this little gem.

title: Small & basic - Great location
text: I stayed here with my parents and we shared a 3 people room. The best thing about the hotel is the location. There is plenty of theatres, restaurants and little shops around. Everything about the hotel is small, but we were prepared for that and we also knew there would be no elevator. Our room was clean and everything seemed fairly new. The third bed was on wheels and therefore moved around, which was slightly annoying. Breakfast was basic, there was a variety of bacon, eggs, sausages etc but it wasn't great. The staff smokes outside the door and the smoke wafts into the entrance and dining hall. We told the person in charge about it but she seemed not to care. All in all it seems a bit pricey for what you get.

title: Excellent location
text: This no frills B&B is in an excellent location for theatres, museums,and shops of central London. It is easy to find and has 24 hour reception. The staff are friendly and helpful. There is no lift and the stairs are uneven and windy. This wasn't a problem for us but could be an issue if you have a lot of luggage or limited mobility. The breakfast was adequate, hot and cold items. The room was small but bed was comfortable, husband said that it was one of the smallest shower cubicles he had ever used. The decor of the stairs and public areas was shabby but it was clean. Street lights shone into the room at night making it very light but we were on the 5th floor and it was quiet.

title: Wonderful location
text: Small hotel very centrally located, good rates. My single room was very small but good for a couple of days. Clean and nice staff. Few steps from lovely Neal’s Yard and Neal street to reach Covent Garden square and metro station. Boiler for tea and coffee in room.

title: Great location for a budget hotel
text: We knew this was a budget hotel when we booked but we're only staying one night so thought we'd chance it. Well the triple room (10) was spacious, clean and plenty of hot water. The breakfast was very good and plenty of cereal, toast and traditional English. We were very pleased as everything we wanted was in our doorstep or a tube ride away. We will stay again

title: Could do better!
text: Friendly reception and excellent location. For this price (£110 for the room, 1 occupant), I would expect something much better. Microscopic room without toilet, tiny sink, pathetically poor lighting (I didn't know that you could get lightbulbs so dim) micro shower, adequate if scruffy towels. Not particularly clean, decrepit furniture, broken handles, tiny tv on broken stand, everything shabby and neglected, no attempt at all at decor. Worst for me was the cold

title: Staff and location compensate for small size and limited equipment
text: The location right in West End is great and the street is quite. The hotel rooms are however small, somewhat noisy and not really upmarket in terms of furniture and bathroom. Free wifi, but limited connection on the upper two floors, so ask for a first or second floor room (also no elevators). Full English breakfast buffet and friendly and helpfull staff compensate for the rooms. Not a hotel for a long, romantic stay.

title: Room for improvements
text: The first and foremost positive thing about this hotel is its location... perfect for a night out to a great show. The reception staff is nice and polite, the room was basic but we had a nice sleep, the breakfast is very average and not very well cooked.. really it should be called a B&B not a hotel. The stairs are so narrow they are not easy to climb, one of us fell (sober) down the tiny steps. The bedding was clean but I found a few hair (floor & breakfast table) that seem to belong to the 2 young staff that double up as cleaners and cook. The wifi does not work upstairs! There was a fan on our ceiling which was certainly needed , a small T.V. and a small shower room with no windows and a shower curtains that either needs a good wash or replacing. No frill B&B but it worked for one night, not sure we ll be back again, shame because with a little tlc and attention this place could be a brilliant place to stay due to its location!

title: Perfect location!
text: Excellent location, a good sized room with a fresh bathroom and proper breakfast. Simple hotel but you have everything you need while in city centre London! If you want the extra extra special to come with your hotel it's not your hotel but if you're looking for a great located hotel to a good price, here you have it! I've seen reviews that the rooms are small but our room had three beds, a sofa, a desk and we still had lot of space to move around. Small bathroom without shampoo and conditioner, just soap but that was perfect for us! Very happy with our stay and we will come back!

title: Larger than a cupboard...
text: This is undoubtedly the smallest-roomed hotel I've ever stayed in! Room 9 was, i'd estimate, 11m2. Furniture and fittings were basic and there were no public areas (Other than the tiny breakfast room). I was hoping breakfast would be the saving grace, but with cheap bland cornflakes and inedible sausages, grilled & dried to the texture of leather, even that disappointed. At £105 per night, not even good value (Anywhere else in the UK, it would compare to a £30 per night b&b). Only positives are it's close to the theatres, and it's fairly clean.

title: Great location
text: Amazing location - the best you'll find in this price point. The rooms are tiny (and I mean tiny!) but it doesn't matter if you don't plan to spend much time in the room. Everything was clean and tidy, staff were friendly and the complimentary breakfast was a nice bonus. It's traditional English breakfast (sausage, eggs, beans, toast) so it's pretty heavy (by day five I was really missing my usual yogurt and fruit breakfast) but the coffee was delicious! Seven Dials has a new extension property a few blocks away above a dentist's office on Endell Street - if they offer, definitely go with the apartment (more space plus a fridge and microwave in suite).

title: a few housekeeping items would have made this fab!
text: V comfy bed. Efficient staff. Great location. Broken window latch made it impossible to shut the noise out. Needs black out curtains Poor water pressure in shower Chip and crackss in wash hand basin - needs replacing

title: overnight stay
text: stayed o/night and found it a clean comfortable hotel very friendly staff and helpful.the stairs were a bit steep if you have climbing difficulties we were in the top room and a little out of breath when we got there Location was excellent for the theaters and most other places All in all very satisfied

title: Not for hamster swingers!
text: Very basic but great value in terms of location - right in the heart of Covent Garden. Clean with friendly staff and a good breakfast, this hotel offered all we needed for a short break in London. There was absolutely no noise from other rooms or from outside. Shops, bars, restaurants, Underground stations and theatres are all in walking distance from the Seven Dials. Room was tiny - not enough space to swing a hamster though we did make an amusing video of ourselves traversing the room, squeezing past the bed along the walls, etc. We had a great time regardless!

title: Never Again
text: The equivalent of $185 a day provided a miniscule twin room with a double bed and a single cot-type. I assume it usually rents as a triple, or maybe a quadruple as there is a rollway matrass bed under the cot. Neither the room door nor the bathroom door opened fully. There were no two pieces of furniture in the room that matched and not one piece of furniture that wasn't broken

title: Great location
text: Ok this is a little rough round the edges but it's clean & friendly. It's in a really lovely street with lots of coffee shops & if you are going to the theatre then you are 5 mins from most. China town & Soho only a few mins walk. We walked to Trafalgar Square in 10 mins as well. Breakfast is basic but ok & self service. On the whole good value for London if you don't mind it not being perfect.

title: Amazing Location
text: Spotlessly clean with a hearty breakfast, we found this place to be very convenient and hard to fault. It's very basic - not a romantic choice, but a great place to sleep after being out all day. Construction going on at the building next door right now 9 - 5. 3 min walk to Covent Garden station and surrounded by places to eat and in the heart of the theatre district.

title: The location is great alright, but will not stay there again! bed bugs alert!
text: I booked this hotel because of previous positive reviews of how clean it was and how good the location is. Well the location is just superb, I'd have to admit. Convent Garden, lots of nice shops, restaurants and cafes. Close to all the theatres and nightlife spots. I did not have any high expectations of this hotel, because the price is quite cheap and from the photos I've seen online I just did not have any sort of expecation, except that it has to be clean! But the hotel was not that clean at all. Once I step foot in the small lobby with the dark green carpet, there was this weird smell!!! You will get use to it after a while, but it was not pleasant. The bed sheets pillow case didn't feel clean.. I ended up getting bites from bed bugs!!!!! My bed was next to the heater.. and very close to the wall and the wall had dust and yellow stains on it.. also the heater had stains. It was very gross having to have to sleep so close to the stains! There are no elevators, so you have to carry your luggage up and down those ridiculously narrow stairs. This had been said before so it was expected and I had no probelm with that. BUT the thing I had a problem with is that when I was pulling my luggage down the stairs getting ready to check out. The lady at the front desk did not help me with my luggage (which was expected) AND asked me to be more quiet with my luggage in a rude way! It was 11pm in the morning, and the cleaners were vaccuming so noise was not an issue. Maybe she was afraid I would break their fragile stairs. But the luggage was heavy ofcourse there are gonna be some noise. If she was so concern I think she should come help me instead of just sitting there complaining after the luggage had already been taken down. What's the point? I'm already checking out and that is my only piece of luggage, and I am never coming back again. The washroom was so small, you can only stand and turn, don't even have enough room to change your clothes in there... unless you change in the shower area. The washroom door lock was broken, the door was dented, looked like someone punched a hole in it previously. The toilet paper were crap.. no tissue available.. even if you have to wipe your face or mouth, you'd just have to use their toilet paper. So I had to run down to the corner store to get some boxed tissue. Just not a good experiece, the whole thing looks haunted.

title: Fair play
text: I stayed here for one night. It was very cheap for £110 when I knew Cologne football fans were in London and rooms hard to find. Small but cheap and cheerful. The Seven Dials area is gorgeous and a world in itself. Soho theatres all close by as Shaftesbury Avenue is on the one end of Monmouth Street. Beware Charring Cross at night: full of drug dealers, druggies and people trying to mug you. Good full English breakfast here too. Very polite staff.

title: worst ever
text: This hotel must be the worst hotel I've stayed in, the room was tiny, the shower was broken the whole place stank. I booked for two nights but checked out after one night I just couldn't stand the smell.never again! Joe. Edinburgh

title: Birthday weekend
text: We found this place on Trivago but ended up booking direct as was cheaper, even though Trivago say it's cheaper through them. Location is great as we walked pretty much everywhere but underground station not too far a walk. Room was small but we only spent a short time in the room as was out all day and to be honest if your visiting London you only need that. Breakfast was buffet style and was very nice with cereals on offer too.

title: Location,Location, Location
text: I love this hotel, and have stayed here many times. Providing you can cope with the stairs, and you aren't a major fusspot,you will,too. It's clean, comfortable, and friendly.You walk out right into the middle of Covent Garden. The staff are charming and helpful.

title: Surprising
text: Never judge a book by its cover or indeed a hotel by its frontage or web page pics. Location is absolutely brilliant for the west end and central London For location the price is excellent and believe it or not it's very very quite. The receptionist was excellent, friendly and accommodating We were on a two day one night stay for a big event and were allowed to leave our luggage there in the morning before we checked in and until the early evening after we had checked out which made traveling around London so much easier Yes the accommodation and breakfasts were basic but they were clean (cleaner than some holiday inn express that I have stayed in) and sufficient for what we needed. Unfortunately no facilities for the disabled. And yes I will be staying there again.

title: Little hotel in a big village
text: As you walk along Monmouth street, it has a village feel. You forget you are in a sprawling metropolis. It is so friendly and cosy. The hotel was so small and crammed, it was easy to walk past. Once inside, our room was tiny, with limited essentials and a disappointing view from the window. (No wildebeest walking across the plain, or the hanging gardens of Babylon.) but this was made up with the location, ideal for going to the theatre. The breakfast, although not special was filling and gave you a good start for the day.

title: Horrible
text: Absolutely horrible ceiling fan shaked we went up 5 sets of stairs to get to our one room cracked sink loud air con un hygenic broken bed no room tiny tv chimney horrible view smoke smell breakfast has six things to choose from horrible poor living conditions.

title: Quiet room at the top
text: Friendly welcome and the quiet room I'd asked for was fantastic. Top of the 4 flights of stairs and overlooking the rooftops, well out of earshot of the hubbub round about. Slept like a log with the window open - a first for a London stay! Breakfast in the basement included all at a reasonable price (for London).

title: Location and friendly reception staff
text: Pros Location Clean rooms Reception staff are friendly Breakfast - cooked cereals toast with Jam, tea and coffee Tea and coffee facilities available in the room Cons Small rooms/bathrooms which are typical for London Dated think of early 90s I would stay here again though

title: Not for me
text: Unfortunately booking this hotel was a big, costly mistake. Upon arrival we were shocked at the poor state that this hotel has been left in. We were given a room on the first floor, up threadbare carpeted stairs, with the cleaners materials and dirty bed linked laying all over the landing. Upon entering our room we were faced with someone else's belongings. Having finally sorted out another room we were shocked at the state of the room and it's contents. The double bed is no more that 4feet wide, with a third bed which we had to climb over to get the cup arid which housed a shower and toilet. We were given a wifi code and upon trying to use this we could not log on. We decided that we could not stay in this hotel, due to the state of it and promptly walked put. Yes, it is to each persons taste but there are better hotels in the area for roughly the same money, so why choose this one. I personally had concerns over health and safety, and fire hazards therefore felt unsafe staring at this hotel. The time that we did spend in the room was very noisy, it was claustrophobic therefore the windows had to be opened to allow in some air, this meant that the traffic noise was very noticeable .The only thing I felt in its favour was its location.

title: Great location, great value
text: The location of this hotel is fantastic. It's about a three minute walk away from Covent Garden and about five minutes from Trafalgar Square. It's right in the middle of the West End so Leichster Square and most of the theatres are in walking distance. The hotel itself is nice. The staff are very friendly and breakfast is served in the morning. The rooms are nice, warm and cosy. Some reveiws complain about the rooms bring small. While it's true that there is not a lot of floor space this was not a problem for me as I was staying one night with my girlfriend and we did not have much luggage but I can imagine the size of the rooms being a problem if you plan to spend a lot of time in the hotel. Our room was on the ground floor and we could also hear people walking up and down the stairs in the morning. Again, this was not a problem for us as it woke us up in time for breakfast but I can imagine it upsetting you if you are a light sleeper. These however are minor criticisms put on my reveiw to make it inromative. I think the hotel was excellent value for money in terms of its location and how comfortable I found the room. To summarise, I think this hotel is great if you're planning a short stay in London, especially if you plan to go to the theatre in the evening. This hotel is best for couples or if you are travveling alone. It's probably not as good if you have a family with young children and it may not be the best place to go if you are staying for a long time. Again I have to say this hotel is grerat valure for money!

title: Great location but hotel a little disappointing
text: The location of the hotel was great. Everything is on the door step. We went to see a show in a Palace Theatre and it was only 5 min walk. Loads of places to eat and walking distance to some sightseeing. First time in London when we didn't have to use a tube. Unfortunately that is the only good thing I can say about this hotel. Building and facilities very outdated. Our "double room" was just about to fit double bed! No room to move. However it wasn't a big issue for us as we literally only slept in the room, came back late after show and left first thing in the morning. Breakfast was big disappointment. They offered cooked breakfast where everything was cooked first thing in the morning and sat there until breakfast was over. Unfortunately we came about an hour since breakfast started so everything was cold. Eggs (fried) were rock hard, toast was cold and crusty. No juice available (but you could get cordial with tap water). We couldn't eat it, had to go out for breakfast. If you staying here I would advise to leave the breakfast as there are lovely places just outside the hotel for breakfast.

title: Location, location, location
text: The location I will rate as 10/10. In my opinion, you can't get better for a budget hotel. You are yards away from Neals yard and metres away from Covent Garden. We had a twin room overlooking the street, which was noisy but was expected. The reason why it didn't get more stars was the breakfast, stay at this hotel but don't eat breakfast here, go out for it. WE went down for breakfast at 7.10 am it starts at 7am. There is a buffet hot breakfast, but it is not hot, everything was cold and the toast was cold and soggy. Why they don't just put a toaster out and let you toast it yourself !!! Rather than leave 12 pieces of toast just go cold.. I would stay there again but go out for breakfast.

title: Great value, amazing location!
text: If any of you are planning a visit to London soon and want a cheap place to stay, I highly recommend this hotel! The rooms were small and plain, but very clean. The neighborhood is amazing. It is a 60 second walk to Neal's Yard and 5 minutes to Covent Garden. It was clean, simple, and centrally located— everything a budget hotel should be!

title: Central to everything.....
text: We arrived at the Seven Dials for 2 nights, with a Canadian guest and we were not disappointed. We checked in early, choosing our room on the 3rd floor facing Monmouth St. It was clean and recently had been renovated. It was a basic reno, the bathroom door wouldn't close properly and the double bed was very small. On the last day, we left our bags in the lobby. It would be nice if they had of been in a secure room. Having said that, the staff were pleasant and on duty all the time, the location next to Covent Garden in central London is perfect. We felt safe and considering this hotel as a central base only, we would return. We would like to note, it is not a place for luxury and service , but it is adequate and I'd like to mention the location is superb.

title: Simple, no frills hotel - great value for money!
text: This hotel was fantastic. I have stayed in a lot of different places in London (bottom and top end) and generally speaking, you get what you pay for. So I was a bit hesitant when I found Seven Dials at such a reasonable price. I was v pleasantly surprised. My friend and I stayed in the 'family room'. Double and a single bed with plenty of floor space (v unusual in London!) and a cosy ensuite : ) the room was fresh, clean and looked recently renovated. Located on 3rd floor (no lift and tight stairwell) made carting luggage tricky. Breakkie pretty basic. But otherwise, this place is in great location (esp if you intend to go to some shows). Would stay there again in a flash! Go to Bill's for breakkie and/or lunch! It's awesome!

title: GREAT location
text: I absolutely love Covent Garden, so this hotel was perfect for my recent stay in London with my brother. There was no air conditioning, which did prove to be a bit of an issue at night (thank God for the fan), but I was willing to put up with it because Covent Garden was literally right outside the door. If you're looking for an affordable hotel with a pretty decent free breakfast included, this hotel may just be for you. We walked all over from here, and never had a problem navigating the city.

title: Safe Friendly Hotel in the Best Location Ever
text: Have used this hotel for years. Not the smartest, no lift, and rooms could do with refurbish. But the best location. Clean rooms. Plentiful breakfast. Above all very nice staff, especially the lovely Hannah on reception. Runs the hotel with superb expertise, with a lovely smiley face.

title: Good choice for location, bad choice for comfort
text: We had an experience of two different rooms here. The first room we stayed in was exremely small. There was a small souble bed fitted within three walls and with two suitcases in the room there was no room at all, we had to climb over etg. The closet was also very small and you coundlt open it because the front of it was the only place where your suitcase could be sitting. It was located at the back with a small window, the room was dark, and the view was not appealing. The second room was entirely different, much more space, with a double and a single bed, a rpoper closet and room to move. It was located on the front side of the hotel and had large widows, bringing lots of light. We were really pleased with this room. The staff were very helpful. The breakfast is served in a small underground room and there is much to be desired. Some guests had nowhere to sit when they came down. The hotel is all about location and price. It is very near the metro station and the price is very good for such a location in London. I would only go back if i had the front room again and if I skipped breakfast alltogether.

title: Re-enjoying
text: When you go back to the same hotel within less than a year's time, that really indicates a satisfied customer. This time again, we had the nicest time in this middle-of-life situated small cosy hotel. Due to the crowded season, there was some misunderstanding in the type of the room we had requested for, and so the first night's sleep was almost all ruined owing to the wobbly soft bed for two

title: Do not stay
text: Horrible, hot, dated& noisy. The only plus point is the central location- don't go unless you're a very heavy sleeper or used to nighttime noise! Staff were friendly too. 70s decor, cramped - just horrible!

title: Yikes....
text: I booked a room here for two reasons: 1. it was very close to where I needed to be for the evening and 2. the reviews were decent (thirdly, at £115 for a single room, it was the cheapest I could find!) I haven't stayed in a hotel THIS basic for a long, long time. There wasn't even a shampoo/shower gel sachet. The shower was a little dribble - think 1970s-caravan - and the room was cold and noisy, despite being on the 4th floor. I did like the location, but I doubt I'll be back. However, if you want a proper Harry Potter (cupboard-under-the-stairs) experience, this is the place for you!

title: Probably worse than a British prison cell
text: This hotel is located 200 m from Covent Garden station. And this is absolutely the only - only – positive thing which can be said about it. The hotel is worn down completely. Dirty. No service at all. Lousy breakfast. Rooms the size of a shoe box. Our "double bed" was 125 cm wide! The toilet and bath was located in a kind of closet. The walls worn down and dirty just as the floors. The furniture all belonged in a dump. The staircase to the top floor was probably 60 cm wide, and in a lousy, hopeless condition. If (or when) a fire break out on this hotel I predict that no guests will get out in time and survive. I am surprised the fire department has not closed it long ago. We will never ever stay in this lousy, dirty hotel again.

title: Good hotel
text: This hotel is actually ok. The staff is very kind and always delivers a smile. The rooms are typical English. Not that big, but you really only need a bed and a bathroom. The beds were hard and nice. I slept really well. The room offered a good bathroom. The bathroom was small, but ok standard. The location of the hotel is really the heart of downtown. Good value for your money. I can recommend this hotel.

title: lovely!
text: I had my reservations about this property after reading some reviews but I was pleasantly surprised. Great value for the area. The seven dials area has a great atmosphere. The room was basic but clean and comfortable. The windows were very well sound proofed. The breakfast was a bit of a letdown but there are lots of places nearby to get breakfast. I will defiantly be staying again.

title: Small but well located
text: I can't on the basis of comfort and value for money bring myself to give this hotel any higher than 3 stars. The location is 10 minutes from Pic. Circus so location is perfect. Thats why it got the three stars! The rest is ..well... basic. Room is very small. Think, tripping over end of bed, nowhere to put luggage and furniture that can be moved with baby finger. Not exactly quality. Toilet is cubby hole. ...back to door whilst at sink. Nowhere for toilet roll to go apart from on floor, shelf 2 inches X 12 inches on which to place all your toileteries. Its a bit tedious after a while. The stairs is 2 feet wide and goes around in a spiral so its hard to walk down. Its an old house in London so its just the way it is. Its not really the owners/managers fault. However the price for London accommodation is just appauling in general. This place is rubbish value for money as is the whole of London. The breakfast is ok and is buffet style. I preferred this. On second day the beans and egg were cold. Two surly girls (looks like family run place) are in charge of breakfast. Other staff were fine particularly the lady of reception (looks like wife -you get picture?). I'm guessing Dad answers door when you ring doorbell. Its a small place for sure with low quality and a high price. Thank God the location is ok. Would I go back? Yes. I would be afraid the next hotel in London would be even worse..

title: Fabulous West End Location!
text: I loved staying in this location - to walk to many of Central London's attractions - or get the tube to others - (there are several underground stations nearby). The property itself reminds me of a seaside B&B - an older style house divided into a multitude of shoebox type rooms - my room was seriously TINY - what I thought was a wardrobe in fact housed a shower cubicle and toilet - however all very clean. I had a single room, and was pleased to get a really comfortable queen sized bed (room 16). Shame about the narrow, steep stairs - not for the faint hearted! If you value location, above space (as do I) , this is a great place to stay. Would stay here again.

title: All about location
text: Great place to visit Covent gardens, shows or excellent restaurants all within walking distance Actual hotel rooms reminded me if my university accommodation, small, bland and if on roadside slightly noisy

title: A perfect base for a Great theatre visit
text: We have just spent 2 days in London to watch a theatre show,we used the Seven Dials Hotel as our base. The Hotel was close to Covent Garden itself with covent garden tube was minutes away minutes away,the hotel is Clean, warm and although in the city quiet at night .we had a triple room with ensuite which although small was perfect for our needs tv free wifi and coffee making facilities and towels.The bed was comfy and clean.Staff were helpful and polite. Breakfast was served in the basement room although has no windows it was well lit and bright the cooked breakfast was hot and sufficient full english and 2 different cereals ,toast and tea and coffee plus juice served to order perfect for the price .would definitely used this Hotel again next time. not recommended if you have trouble with stairs they are typically steep and narrow .

title: Tiny basic rooms but excellent location...
text: Tiny basic rooms but excellent location for west end, theatreland, soho etc

title: Basic but good
text: Just returned from a two night stay in room 8,(compact but adequate with en suite) good service, room cleaned daily, free WIFI was offered by the management on arrival, after booking out of hotel was allowed to leave bags for later collection, breakfast was good and set you up for the day, the location was excellent for our trip .

title: Good location, average hotel
text: We really like the Seven Dials area of London, with its interesting shops, cafes and pubs. I have been so close so often and we have the hotel named after this charming corner of London to thank for discovering it . We took in two shows during our weekend away, and the hotel location was perfect for this. The hotel is clean and our room, though not large, was decorated in a light, neutral colour that helped to make up for the lack of light. It is run with a view to economy which may be sensible, but does take the edge off the welcome. The reception is supposed to be manned at all times, but when we arrived we couldn't get an answer and ended up going for a coffee across the road. The staff are mostly friendly, if busy, and if you mainly want a base handy for theatre land this is worth considering. Be warned, it's an old building. The stairs are steep and there's no lift.

title: Great Location
text: After reading a few reviews I wasn't sure what to expect, but what I found was perfect for a couple of nights stay in London. We were in room 10, which was street facing and had both a single and double bed in it. So plenty big enough for the two of us. As others have said there are no lifts, so climbing the 50 odd steps up to the room, with suitcases was interesting! It was also incredibly hot in London, but there was a fan in the room (which when you had the bathroom door opened whacked into it, LOL), which did the job. Breakfast was ok, usual fry up with choice of cereals. The best thing about this hotel though is location, a stones throw away from Covent Garden and Theatre land - perfect!!

title: Very Basic B&B, have very low expectations and you won't be disappointed.
text: It is amazing how an important location can help as business, no matter what the service. Business customers: Tottenham Crt Rd, Central Saint Giles, Covent Garden Tube are all a stone throw away. If you do not have an option and are forced to find something last minute or are going to any of the above offices, I would still find someplace else. If you are on a shoe-string budget then go for this place, if you are getting a cheap deal here. Tourists: if you are coming to visit London, but do not care if you get the English hospitality or not, then this is an ideal place for you, as it is right next to Neal Street, which is amazing for shopping. You have Starbucks, a nice place for Fish & Chips and Tottenham Court Rd & Covent Garden Tube Stations. Good: Full English Breakfast and proximity to tourist and business locations. Bad: Wireless is a joke, they should just say 'NO Wireless'. Claustrophobic, TV is like a 22 inch LCD, no shampoo. Bathroom had mold, broken doors (see pics) and were not taken care of. The rooms are very basic and one should have a low expectation when going to this B&B. Looked like the exhaust fan was cleaned few years ago. If you want to experience a true British B&B then this is not for you. On the other hand not sure how many true Brit B&B's are left. It is run by East European's who do not really understand the British Culture. Being a Brit myself, it was a bit disappointing for me.

title: Great place to stay for short break
text: This little hotel is a great place to stay if you are exploring London or going to the theatre. Near Covent Garden and 15 min walk from the Thames. Comfy, clean room. Welcoming, helpful staff and good breakfast.

title: Theatre Trip
text: We stayed just one night at this hotel, we didn't think we would want to spend more than that as it was very basic, the hotel overall needs some TLC, the furniture in our room was shabby with bits of the vaneer missing. The en-suite was very compact and bijou and it had a very unusual lock on the door. Saying that, it was clean and the bed was comfy, but the duvet covers were worn. The staff were friendly and helpful. Breakfast was full English and there was plenty of it although if we had gone a few minutes later the food would have been better as the bacon was dry and the eggs hard. A fresh batch appeared just after we had served ourselves. We chose this hotel for a) the price and b) the location - proximity to the theatre we were going to. Overall disappointed, but it was adequate for the one night stay.

title: new year eve
text: booked this hotel at short notice for new year eve 2012.lucky to get it pleased we did.excelent for all west end attractions.nice friendly staff.free wi fi.full english breakfast.would recommend this hotel and definately stay again next time we are in london.

title: Central London hotel
text: Perfectly located for sightseeing in London. Basic but clean and comfy. Surrounded by shops, eateries, theatres and things to do. Breakfast included for the price was a bonus. Staff all very friendly. Take your own milk!!

title: Mould heaven
text: Perfect place to culture some penicillin! Mould was all over the walls underneath the bubbling of the wallpaper! This hotel is amazingly situated right in the middle of west end, however definitely not worth the 105GBP a night that we paid. We paid less for hostels and got better livings while travelling over 5 weeks in the UK!!! After finding out we were on the 4th floor, we were offered no help in getting our 30kg luggage up the narrow winding stairs! We were advised that they would prefer if we paid a day before our check out! Breakfast on a weekday was at 7.00am-9.30am, after walking down to the breakfast part of the hotel (basement) were were greeted with a line of people waiting for tables. Once receiving a table at 9:15, we had to advise the waitresses that there was no food left. The condiments provided are also all out of date. On one morning, advising one of the reception staff of the mould, we were told that they were attending to other rooms first before the one we were in. After 3 nights in the incredibly small room were we definitely ready to leave. Expensive, not what the pictures show on the website and stay if only needing something close to West End.

title: its all about location
text: Found hotel very good, I had read reviews before going so I knew to expect small steps on stairs and no lift. Myself and my 7 year old son were on the third level, I was expecting it to be noisy at night but it wasn't at all, could be an advantage of lifting out suitcases all the way up to the third level without any assistance. Room was perfect for what we wanted, had a double and single bed in it. Everything very clean. Had a ceiling fan to keep us cool in the heat with tea making facilities. Location perfect to all theatres, Leicester square, close to Oxford St for shopping and just beside Covent gardens too, lots of restaurants around too. Would definitely stay again and would recommend on the basis that people know that reception do not help with luggage, stair steps small and no lift could be an issue for some. I also found receptionist could be more friendly and more helpful. We didn't stay around for breakfast so not sure what that was like.

title: Ask for streetview!
text: The location of the hotel couldn´t have been better, great atmosphere right outside the door. The room was small but not the worst I´ve seen in London. BUT! when booking ask for a room facing the street. Our only window opened to a brick wall 3 feet away which meant no air circulation, no daylight what so ever but also a nice peek at the offices located in the building behind the hotel :D The staff was friendly but needed some convincing to fix a clogged drain. Breakfast not impressive, go down the street instead at the local breakfast place for excellent toast and eggs. That said, the place was clean! the area was bursting with life and you felt safe though located in central area of town.

title: You get what you pay for
text: Me and my sisters chose this hotel because we needed a hotel close to Lyceum theatre (10 min walk away) a room for 3 people, our own bathroom, wifi and breakfast included. It's a very good place to stay if you're going to the theatre as its close to a lot of them and it's close to all the shops and restaurants. We didn't realise it's on a main road and it's very noisy on a night with cars driving past all night, the wifi is very good, the staff are very polite and let you keep your suitcases there after you check out (our coach home wasn't until 6pm and you have to check out at 11am) the breakfast was nice and you could get as much as you want because it was on a buffet, but could do with little improvements like having fresh orange instead of cordial orange, changing how they cook the eggs because they were like rubber eggs, they look like they need more staff to help out on breakfast because it was one girl rushed off her feet. The only thing putting me off staying here again is how noisy it was on a night but other than that I would probably come back to this hotel. ☺️

title: Very good!!!
text: Excellent position in the very heart of London. A few steps from Covent Garden and Shaftesbury Avenue. The rooms are small but clean and tidy, breakfast is good and satisfactory. Mind the steps! There is no lift, so it can be hard to carry your luggage to the top floor. However, it is a good hotel and one of the best I found in London.

title: Great little place to stay in london!
text: This place is close to all attractions in London. Plenty of pubs and stores around this hotel. The stairs leading to the rooms is a bit tight. Other than that this place is nice. Will probably stay again if we come back to London.

title: Great location
text: Fabulous location and staff very helpful. Receptionist saw we had a bit of luggage and upgraded our room to a bigger one for no extra charge. Good price for this rate in London and the rate included a cooked breakfast. Would recommend.

title: Absolutely lovely!
text: Me and my friend are just come back home (in Rome) after our stay in London. We stayed at the Seven Dials Hotel 4 nights...it was simply amazing! There are at least three optimal reasons to enjoy this hotel. FIRST: the location...the seven dials area is one of the most "glamour", lovely and lively in all London...it's just few steps from Covent Garden Tube Station...from Thottenam Court Tube Station... from Oxford Street, Soho, Trafalgar Sq., and so on... SECOND: the staff, absolutelly kindly, helpful, professional...and the breakfast is as good as at home! THIRD: the value! Are you able to find something similar in that area for less? It's a good three stars service and room but a cheap b&b price! They have 4 floor with few rooms, but they haven't lift, so if you have problems with the stairs, ask for a 1st floor room...
