title: Fabulous little Gem - Great Service
text: My husband and I stayed at the New Inn for 6 nights and we absolutely loved it. It's a great value, clean and in a great location. The Owner Jan was helpful and friendly from the time we made the reservations to the moment we left. I cannot praise her enough. The food at the Pub was great, both the Thai and traditional (we had Fish & Chips, Bangers & Mash). The St. John's Wood area is a wonderful neighborhood that we loved walking around and exploring the little shops and restaurants as well as the little church park, very safe and quiet. The Tube station is about a 5 min walk and will take you quickly anywhere you need to go in London. Would definitely stay here again.

title: Nice and cosy!
text: Tried this nice little pub recently with my wife. As we were new to the area, we looked this place up on TripAdvisor and thanks to the community who have given some great reviews we decided to try this pub. We wanted to have a pub grub and a drink and have a nice chat. The experience was good. We had cod and chips and beef burger along with a couple of drinks. Good was decent, service was good. They also have a beer garden which we will try out when it's a bit warmer (hopefully soon!) Will visit again.

title: Date 24 hours away
text: My husband & I had a date 24 hours away as we had tickets to see Simple Minds at The Roundhouse in Camden. I had done a search to find a bed for the night and I will be honest I booked another venue. My husband came home and said no way look at the reviews and cancelled. I was dubious about staying above a pub and had some misconceptions that it was going to be basic, noisy etc. I couldnt have been proven more wrong and was very pleasantly surprised. We arrived and the staff were very friendly and courteous. We were shown our room and it was clean, comfortable with a generous sized bed. Now it was February and it was 0' outside but the room was so hot we slept on top the bed clothes! Some people may find this unpleasant but for us it was fabulous. Again it was February and a Thursday night so I can not comment on the road noise or people drinking outside. When we got back from the concert we could hear the noise from downstairs but it wasnt at all load or disturb our sleep in any way. Throughly enjoyed our night's stay, thank you The New Inn

title: Mrmakeyoucry
text: Excellent place to stay with friends and family ,staff they are very good and polite exelent service ..................................................

title: Great Place !!!!
text: I first stayed at the new inn in January , when i was on a trip to London. I found the room really clean and the place very welcoming. The food in the restaurant was really tasty and well presented. When i moved back to London, in march, i was really happy to move to st john's wood. Since then,The New Inn is my canteen !! I eat there every time I'm too lazy to cook ! The fish and chips and burger are among the best you can find in London for this price. And the Sunday roast ! simple i don't eat at home on Sundays any more ! great portions, very reasonably priced, a good wine list, and for a few days, an outstanding cocktail list !! The staff is really friendly and professional, and the owner, Nick, is really close to his guests !! I recommend this place !

title: Avoid This Restaurant
text: It really pains me to have to write this review but our last night in London found Kristen, Scott(14) and Kate(12) wanting some more pub food. We searched Yelp/Open Table and yes TripAdvisor and based on Open Table reviews, it is a pub and they had 7:30 PM open, we decided to try the New Inn. I dont know what The Old Inn was like but you should really avoid this place for food. Drinks and beer are fine. Food, not so much. When we arrived at the pub it was very lively - great. looked like we caught them by surprise however. we were told by the bartender/hostess that they "...hadn't had a busy Friday night in forever..." should have been my cue to exit but we persevered. 3 of us had the fish and chips - the batter was almost a half an inch thick. sort of like an over done crusty waffle. the fish inside was moist and well cooked but the batter had some sort of cinnamon, ginger bread cookie flavor. not edible. the chips were fine - hard to mess them up. my daughter had a flatbread pizza. it was mostly tasteless - tasted like you were eating a loaf of bread. except for the balled up parts at the edges where the dough was raw and gushy. YUCK........ and to top things off, when my daughter went to the restroom, there was a drunk guy in the ladies room. Needless to say, this is a pub for drinks with friends only, eat at home or somewhere else in St John's Wood.

title: Brilliant and relaxing holiday stay
text: My wife and I booked two weeks at the New Inn in May when we visited London to catch up with our son who is doing his Masters at London Uni and is living just down the road with his girlfriend. From the minute we arrived when we were greeted by Jan we could not have asked for amore ideal location to stay. Although the accommodation was above the hotel and they had artists playing at the weekend we were not troubled in any way as the bar closed promptly and obviously the locals who patronise this old style hotel downstairs are very courteous and our sleep was not disrupted in any way and in fact it was quite pleasant to hear the music playing in the background. The rooms were clean and spacious and the bed was very comfortable. We cannot comment on breakfast as we were off on our travels immediately we woke which meant that because we could walk down Baker St into Oxford Street withing 40 minutes the location was ideal. Regents Park, Primrose Hill, Camden Markets and Lords Cricket ground where we attended a 40 over county game are within 10 minutes walk and the local St Johns Wood shopping centre has everything you would need including a Tescos and quite a number of shops and restaurants. There is also a laundry close as well which came in handy for us as travellers. The tube at St Johns Wood is very useful to return on and the Oyster Crd which we got when awe arrived and placed 50 Pounds on each card came in very handy for getting around. For overseas travellers please remember to keep your shopping receipts for large purchases as you can get a VAT tax receipt from the shop, we purchased clothing from Marks and Spencer, Debenhams and a new phone from Phone Warehouse and got a VAT tax receipt for these which we were able to redeem at Travel Ex at the airport to get our tax paid back to us in cash. All in all we cannot recommend the New Inn, Jan and her staff any more highly and would definitely return if we go back to London.

title: Decent pub near Lords
text: Very decent pub a short walk from Lords Cricket ground much better value than the pubs turned wine bars on the way. Good selection of beers and food. Burgers and fish and chips both good. Also a reasonable wine list.

title: The best little Inn
text: Ok I should have done this long ago and for this I am sorry because someone somewhere went to London and missed out on staying at this lovely Inn. The New Inn is the perfect place to stay the room was clean and neat the owner and staff make you feel right at home. The food is great and in the evening it is one of the best neighborhood watering holes. Walking distance to so many sights, The tube(train) is near and buses are also close to take you to all the other sights you may want to see. If you love dogs the cutest one greets you at The New Inn (if you don't London may not be the place for you) London is dog lover but the dogs are so well trained and the streets kept so clean you wouldn't know except to see them walking their masters.

title: Comfortable, friendly accommodation near Regent's Park
text: We stayed at the New Inn from March 15-21. The rooms are above a small but excellent pub. We had a few meals here and enjoyed them very much. The Thai food is really quite good. We didn't eat breakfast (you have to order the night before, and we were never able to do so) at the hotel but ate on the nearby High Street. Several good options there. We had to be moved during our stay so I can comment on two rooms. We stayed for five nights in a small but adequate sized double room. Quiet, good bed, very clean. On the last night we were moved to a twin room, which was larger but equally clean and comfortable. The noise from the pub never troubled us at all

title: Great day and night!
text: We arrived in London, very early on a bank holiday, thanks to favorable winds across the Atlantic. It was raining very hard (there were even regional flood alerts due to heavy rain that started the day before). We walked to The New Inn early, in hopes of leaving our bags for check in later in the day, but the owner saw us dripping wet outside and let us in. We were even able to check in early and dry off, leaving time to catch the local sights in St. John's Wood, including Abbey Road, and then conveniently catch the tube into London for a great (if not somewhat wet!) day in central London. We had Thai dinner in the pub, which was some of the best food we had on our 10 day UK trip. Bar was nice, people were friendly, and we sure wished we had planned to spend more time in London. But we will remember this one day for a long time, and we will definitely stay in The New Inn again on our next trip to London. Nice room in a great, and reasonably quiet location.

title: Our room at The New Inn was a fabulous oasis
text: Our room was large, clean, and comfortable. There were tea and coffee making supplies, the bathroom was also large for London, and I loved the heated towel rack. We ate splendid Thai food in the restaurant downstairs and drank all the real ale we wanted before going up to bed. The landlady, Jan, was friendly and helpful. Our room at the New Inn was a home away from home for us while we visited busy London.

title: Extremely disappointing
text: Have just read the review by Katie L and we could have written it. Had picked this place for the same reason, going to Wembley, We were met by the same girl who said we needed to pay even though we already had through the booking site. She didn't have a clue what she was doing. We went back down to have a meal before going to Wembley which was one of the reasons we'd booked here. The guy who served us again didn't seem to know what was going on. The chef is very good and food was lovely but when we asked for a dessert menu he just bought the normal one again so we gave up. Rooms are clean but dark and warm. A fan was provided. We were able to sleep with the window open (no flat roof net to our room) and I have to say it was surprisingly quiet. Like Katie L no explanation of keys, how we would get in late etc. Luckily another member of staff was outside when we got back and he opened the side doors for us that we didn't even know existed. Perhaps they have better staff in the evening. We didn't have breakfast and when we handed our key in the same woman from the night before took it off us without a word. Don't know if the staff were new but they are losing you customers. We decided not to have breakfast (went to The Ivy, superb) and had planned to book again for September but will be looking elsewhere.

title: Weekend visit to London
text: We chose this B&B as we needed easy access to Wembley Stadium and a simple B&B for the night. When searching the net we came across this quirky little B&B which was described in terms of friendliness, welcoming, a good music venue with good food and all close to our required area. However, what was meant to be a relaxed establishment turned out to be so laid back they were positively horizontal in a not very helpful way. When we arrived the young woman in the bar checked us in and told us that we had to pay in full on arrival (the reason for this fell into place as our stay unfolded). We were shown to a very small room which was hot and airless. It did have opening windows but with a flat roof immediately outside and thus access direct from the street we were reluctant to have the windows open. A small fan had been provided. The room was clean as was the bathroom with toiletries and nice towels. A tea/coffee tray was provided and was adequate. We then realised that as we would be out in the evening (they did arrange a cab for us) we might need to get back in after the pub had shut....the same young woman had no idea whether we could return after the pub shut at 12 midnight so we made sure we were back before....the same young lady could not tell us if breakfast was included but that they did start serving the public at 10am......when we went downstairs in the morning the same woman seemed surprised to see us appear in the bar as she had just opened the pub...made us wonder how we might have got out if needed due to an emergency or just needing to leave earlier (maybe payment taken on arrival and some people have to get themselves out before staff arrive).....We could only imagine that the staff on duty were new as clearly they knew nothing about guest management or their own establishment. Very bizarre. But it did a job - a bed for the night in the right part of town.

title: Wonderful hosts!
text: We stayed here for 4 nights. Staff very welcoming and helpful-drew us maps on napkins to get us to a great breakfast spot. The room was comfortable and had a nice, large fan. Loved the friendly downstairs pub, especially the 2 live in dogs. Great breakfast! Hosts Stephanie and Laura could not have been nicer. This was a fun and homey place to spend 4 nights in London. Close to Regents Park and several Tube stops. The neighborhood can be a bit noisy as many students seem to live nearby.

title: Noisy!
text: It's a pub with a few nice and clean rooms. If you like to party then this is your "hotel". Nice location near Regents Park but the loud partying is a bummer. Bathrooms clean and staff congenial. As write this, the noise from the partiers is overwhelming.

title: Great value, great location
text: This is a great little hotel in a great location- quiet tree-lined street, only 5 mins from shops & restaurants and 10 mins from the underground. Also only a pleasant 15-20 mins walk from Camden Market (which the owner kindly drew us a map to, when we asked for directions) The food in the pub restaurant was superb (Thai /traditional English pub grub) as was the breakfast. Room was comfortable and very quiet considering it is over a pub and there was live music on downstairs! Staff were friendly and helpful and we would not hesitate to recommend this hotel and will definitely stay there again whenever we next visit London.

title: Nice Quiet Inn
text: The hotel was in a great location, nice and quiet and beautiful. Basically across the street from Reagent's Park and within walking distance to Baker's Street tube station. Although it's above a bar we never heard a sound. The hallway up to the rooms is a bit skinny, so be prepared to carry your bags skillfully. :) The staff was very friendly and helpful. Stored our bags for us even though we checked out in the morning and didn't leave till the evening. Very pleased and would definitely stay here again! Free wireless and satellite tv were great extras.

title: A little gem
text: Lovely clean fresh room, comfortable beds with feather duvets and pillows. Lovely building, lovely atmosphere and very pleasant, helpful staff. Good food and really good cocktails to finish the day with. Will definitely be returning.

title: Comfort, convenience and cool cuisine.
text: My wife and I stayed here for a long weekend and it will be first on our list when we come to booking any further trips to London. It is situated in a very quiet area close to Regents Park. During our stay the weather was beautiful and we could enjoy a walk through the Park to Baker Street and on to Oxford Street and Central London. You can also walk along the canal to Camden where we enjoyed by far the biggest market we have ever seen. When the weather is less clement there is very convenient and cheap transport, tube and bus, nearby. The New Inn is very much a community pub and frequented by what we found to be very friendly and pleasant locals. The accommodation is not the most modern, but it is spacious and spotlessly clean. The pub serves European and Thai food which we found enjoyable and reasonably priced. The breakfast was great and well worth the money. It was great to return to the New Inn each evening after a busy day and have the convenience of enjoying a few drinks and something to eat under the one roof. The staff were efficient, friendly and helpful and we are already looking forward to our next trip.

title: Great food, nice ambiance, cutie dogs :)
text: Great food, nice ambiance, cutie dogs :) We ordered fish of the day & veggie delight and dessert of the day from the daily specialities, we loved them, seems very well done I would definitely recommend this place ! Thank you :)

title: Great little inn
text: Great staff, very good house keeping service and an extremely comfortable room for our stay in London in July 2012. Limited eating choices at the pub, but great choices for alcohol and a great hot English breakfast. Nice location too and very close to St. Johns Wood station. Will surely come back to our 'home' in London. :)

title: A night away in London
text: We were looking for something different and didn't want to stay in a big hotel chain. We like the pub atmosphere and wanted to run up Primrose Hill in the morning. The New Inn ticked all the boxes for us. The welcome we received was warm and friendly and the owner and his staff couldn't have been more helpful. The location was perfect for what we wanted to do and we walked in from and back to Paddington Station. The place was spotless and our evening meal was great. Didn't get time to try the silly hats or the Jazz but next time we will. Thank you for adding to our weekend.

title: Another comfortable stay
text: There are a couple of reasons why I have become a regular here: the staff are always friendly and the rooms are very comfortable. I think there are six rooms: all are very well decorated, clean and bright

title: Lovely English pub, good value, recommended
text: We stayed at the New Inn for a week in June 2011, and happily recommend it to others. It is different to standard hotels, just 5 rooms above the pub. It is well located in a very safe and attractive area. Handy to the tube, shops & restaurants. The Thai restaurant in the pub is very good value, and very good food. Staff at the pub and restaurant are welcoming and friendly. It is a much nicer visitor experience than a standard hotel. The room was a little dated, but very clean & comfortable. The floor in the bathroom creaked - but that just added to the character. We thought it good value for money. Unfortunately for two of the nights we were in London, they had a small heatwave, and the lack of air-con, and small windows mean't that it was difficult to cool off. Not withstanding that shortcoming we would happily stay there again for our next trip to London. When you do book, ask & they can arrange a very competitive cab to/from the airport.

title: Would go back there anytime!
text: Very nice food and lovely staff! Love this pub! We had a hock roast on a Sunday and it was really good! Atmosphere was relaxed and it was nice to spend a nice afternoon there. If you are in the area I recommend to pop in there to try their food or to just have a drink!

title: Wonderful inn and wonderful pub
text: My sister and I spent four days at the New Inn last week and we loved the whole experience. Jan and her whole staff were really delightful. The room was large, clean, and well appointed. The furnishings were not fancy but there was absolutely everything we needed and it was extremely comfortable. There was wireless internet which was very handy. It is about equidistant from various bus lines and the tube - not close, but not far either. We had the lovely breakfast several days and one evening had a Thai dinner in the pub. All the meals were delicious and good value for money - the dinner, I would say was exceptional value for the money. It was an easy walk to St John's Wood High Street which had many food and shopping options. The only problem we had was that a couple of evenings there was a lot of street noise which kept us awake for a while, but generally it was quiet and that was not a problem. We really loved the inn and would highly recommend it.

title: A lovely place and a warm welcome
text: I can't fault the New Inn. Unfortunately we didn't have time to eat there but we had drinks from a good wine list. Nick, the owner, as well as all of the staff made us feel so welcome. It's a charming pub and the rooms are extremely comfortable. Not huge, but fantastic comfy beds and smart modern bathrooms. A real find, and very handy for Primrose Hill, Regents Park and St John's Wood tube. So central, but in a quiet street. I'll be back!

title: A little gem
text: Set on the edge of Regents Park and Primrose Hill this wonderful B&B is a delight within the community of St. Johns Wood. Never have we had such a good nights sleep in the centre of London. Service with a smile, clean rooms and a very good value breakfast this B&B is ideally located on a good bus route and tube line for easy access to all the sights and flavours of London.

title: Prison-like rooms and terrible food
text: We had always wanted to stay at this hotel. It looked quite good on the web. We booked three double rooms originally at a certain price and when no confirmation came, called to confirm, only to be told the rooms had all been re-furbished to a high standard and the price had gone up quite considerably. I argued with the manager who relented by saying the full english breakfast could be included!!! The hotel was quite good in storing our luggage at the beginning of the day - that is where the "good" stopped!!! We were shown to our room or maybe you could call it a cell. You could just about get down the side of the bed to the bedside tables, there was an open fronted single wardrobe with hangers. A dressing table with tea/coffee and a huge fan. The bathroom adjoins the bedroom. A shower, basin, toilet and towel rail are in there. Ample space, in fact for two or three people to get in there (pity some of the room could have been made into the bedroom). The window was very small and once we had shut the windows to try to obliterate the noise we couldn't open it again. We put the fan onto the dressing table on full power (yes it was opressively hot) and had to leave it on all night. It was a toss up whether to leave the windows open and have throbbing music booming or the fan noise on - we chose the fan. We could still hear the music (if you can call it that) until way past midnight and on top of all this the lock on the door wouldn't lock. Whoever painted the rooms needs shooting as a three year old could have done a better job. We had had to book a time for breakfast the previous night so just before the alloted time we went down to the "restaurant" - basically it was up one step from the bar. It was a boiling hot morning and there were no windows open so even before the meal came we were already sweating. A lady came to ask if we wanted tea or coffee, came back with it, then returned almost straight away with the breakfast, she then went straight over to the door and continued to clean it with brasso!!! aarrgghh!!! We were not asked what we wanted and I have to say it may happen in America but it is the first time in my life that I have been served french fries for breakfast!!!! On our plates were: 2 fried eggs, 1 rasher of bacon, 1 sausage, baked beans, 2 small whole vine tomatoes, french fries and 4 halves of burnt toast. Personally I can't eat baked beans which almost covered half the plate but as I tried the burnt toast which just snapped like a crisp it tasted of mint, on top of which it was fairly obvious that this breakfast had not just been cooked but pre-cooked and left under a hot plate. I left the majority and had the aftertaste of mint in my mouth even after drinking the tea. I might have thought it was maybe just our breakfasts that were yuk but our relatives had their breakfasts an hour later and were exactly the same. I will never return and I would advise anyone who wants good food and a good night's sleep to do the same.

title: One Night in St Johns Wood
text: Booked accomodation for one night at this pub due to its proximity to Lords Cricket Ground which we were visiting the following day. Pleasantly surprised as the area was residential and quiet and first impressions of the pub were good and the staff courteous and helpful. Our room was spotlessly clean and had complimentary tea and coffee and sweets and everything you need for a short stay including a fan that would be welcome on a hot day. Bathroom was clean and modern with excellent shower. We had a meal at the hotel which was well cooked and reasonably priced and breakfast the following morning was excellent. Staff could not have been more friendly and helpful and we would recommend this accomodation for a short stay in London particularly at the price.

title: Great location and good value
text: We stayed here in June and were impressed with the location just a short walk from Primrose Hill, Lords and Regents Park. The tube is 10 minutes walk away through the interesting village of St Johns Wood withnits bistros, bakeries and pubs. An easy trip on the Jubilee line to Westminster. The room was cosy, clean and warm and the bathroom though not luxurious had a good shower and was quite big enough. Jan the landlady is great for recommendations and helpful advice. Terrific value for money and some fun entertainment in the pub if you want it - we would stay again

title: Great Value, and nice location
text: I would highly recommend this hotel to my fellow travelers. My room was clean and well equipped, and friendly staff. Also the food is very tasty. For London lodging options, the New Inn offers the great value, and the location can't be beat. It is in a friendly neighborhood (not too my tourists) with many restaurant options, and about 7 minutes walk to the St. John Woods Tube station. The noise from the pub downstairs is only loud when they have a band performing, otherwise, the chatter from the pub is not too bad, and on the weeknights the noise definitely cease once the bar closes, and it is pretty quiet.

title: Most excellent experience
text: The New Inn is a fabulous place to stay to get a neighbourhood experience within London. We enjoyed walking the canals to Camden Town, exploring the shops, etc. I cannot say enough about the lovely experience we had with Jan and the rest of the staff. Breakfast was superb, the pints were cold, the Thai food was authentic...the best part, a nice, quiet room with a spacious bath ensuite. We had a twin room and it was quite spacious by London standards. I am looking forward to another stay in 2012!

title: Hidden gem
text: Excellent food, relaxed atmosphere, friendly staff, welcoming to dogs and children, live guitar duo when we were there on a Sunday afternoon, squeaky clean bathrooms,... what's there not to like about the New Inn?

title: IT'S ALL ABOUT VALUE FOR MONEY!!
text: My wife & I have stayed at The New Inn on two occasions after using very expensive city centre London hotels and would in future always stay at the New Inn. Let’s be honest from the start, the New Inn is no fancy boutique B&B charging £200+ a night. It’s a very clean basic place that offers the traveller on a budget a decent room for the night. For me a B&B has to offer three things

title: Lovely little place with friendly staff
text: We really enjoyed our stay at the New Inn. All the staff were very friendly and accommodating. My husband contacted them before we visited to see if they would be able to provide a vegetarian breakfast (which they did and it was lovely, but it was so big I couldn't eat it all!). The room was clean and comfortable with everything needed in it. The only quibble we had was that there were a couple of things that could be improved aesthetically (toilet seat was well worn and bathroom could do with a lick of paint) but nothing that affected our overall stay. The room was a little noisy Friday night but you kind of expect that if you stay at a pub. The food was nice both in the evening and at breakfast. As for those moaning about dogs, there are signs everywhere. If you aren't a doggy person, move along there are plenty of places that don't allow dogs. I loved it, it was like home away from home and we loved their furry company! Thanks so much for a lovely stay!

title: Sunday roast
text: Living local we were hoping to find another nice restaurant to frequent, was not busy but the service was very slow,we both had roast beef I asked for medium and my husband wanted well done,we both got well done with a congealed gravy with over cooked vegables all was served cold,two waters and one glass of wine. Bill was £42 90 left hungry and would never returned. Good points live music and clean toilets.

title: Dogs!!
text: Visiting London with friends in 'summer'. Had a lovely time and then came across this pub. As soon as we saw the dogs we wanted to leave but thought we'd ask if we could sit and eat where dogs weren't allowed. Young staff member told us no as they are dog friendly (!) I like dogs but not around me when I'm eating. One quick drink and we were quickly outta there! Such a shame as it looked a great place but none of us would have eaten in a place where dogs are present. Not sure if there was a sign outside (if not, there should be).

title: Very comfortable stay
text: I have stayed here on a number of occasions in most of thier rooms and I have not yet been dissappointed. Each room is individually decorated and is very comfortable. The showers are good. Staff are friendly and helpful, and the food downstairs is excellent. Only complaint: I would prefer curtains to blinds!

title: Overpriced microwaved breakfast and irritating dogs
text: The New Inn touts itself as a gastro-pub presumably so it can justify its high prices. However, if you are going to call yourself a gastro-pub and charge high prices, your customers are going to expect something fairly special. This means good ingredients, hot, freshly prepared food, and a pleasant dining experience. Unfortunately, the New Inn does not deliver on any of these counts. We had decided to try the New Inn after receiving a flyer advertising that they were now serving breakfasts. Having never previously been to their and wanting to support a local business, we decided to give it a try. The pub has a fairly neat decor and lots of seating. The first thing we noticed however, was the strong smell of bleach in the air. Whilst this was quite off-putting, we thought we'd stay and ordered coffee and the traditional english breakfast. Coffee was ok and certainly better than some places up the road such as Richoux. The breakfast itself took 30 minutes to appear which is a little longer than I would have expected. When our food did finally arrive, we were a little perplexed why it had taken 30 minutes judging from what was on our plates. Whilst the plates were hot, the food itself was quite cold. The beans were served in a little pot but were dried out. The bacon and black-pudding were extremely dry and looked as though they had been cooked, refrigerated and then reheated in a microwave. The mushrooms also looked shrivelled and old so their freshness was questionable. And 'potato rosti' was a McCain frozen hash brown which didn't taste anything like a potato. The eggs, tomato and sausage were fine Considering how simple it is to prepare a traditional English breakfast for three customers in an empty restaurant, I'm unclear why our food was not only reheated, but also took 30 minutes to prepare and serve. Whilst the dogs at the New Inn are rather sweet, I did find them quite irritating. For starters, I don't think dogs belong in a restaurant and I probably wouldn't have minded them being there if they'd only kept away from our table. Unfortunately, as soon as our food arrived they spent the entire meal running under and out from our table and barked loudly and unexpectedly in an effort to try and get us to feed them. When I'm eating food in a restaurant, I really don't like being bothered by dogs begging to share my food with them. It would have been good if the restaurant owners had taken a bit more responsibility for their animals and perhaps fed them themselves or at least took the time to ensure that they don't bother customers. They occasionally trotted off and wandered behind the bar only for the waitress to shoo them out back which inevitably meant them headed straight back to our table. Their dog chews were also scattered around the restaurant which was also quite unpleasant. The smaller dog also kept eating the leaves and roots from an exotic-looking/possibly-toxic-to-dogs plant by the fireplace which I can't imagine would be good for it. Perhaps the strong smell of bleach was as a result of the owner having to clean up the poor blighters vomit from eating the plant!?! Overall, our experience of the New Inn was extremely disappointing and expensive. This is a real shame as St. John's Wood could do with another good restaurant.

title: LOVE this place!
text: I am only reviewing this place as a pub / restaurant. we didn't stay here overnight, but I would be happy to! What a pub! I knew from the moment I read the notice on the door that says "This is a dog friendly pub. If you do not like dogs, perhaps this is not the pub for you." I would like it. The room is very well decorated and maintained, but it in no way feels uncomfortable. It is exactly the kind of place you can relax. The bar is well laid out and easily accessible. The staff were attentive, friendly and polite. And cool. The menu is really extensive with a broad range of food types available. I asked the waiter for a recommendation and he unequivocally provided one. He was also correct. I had The Full Monty Burger. Wow!

title: Great food, great service
text: Ordered cesar salad. Very good bit pricey £12 but solid portion. Cheese board for dessert was incredible. Fantastic cheese and satisfying portion (is more than enough for two people). Decor is beautiful and other clientele very nice. Tucked away from St John's Wood and regents park a real find. Highly recommended and will return.

title: If you're looking for a cozy and lovely place, stay at The New Inn
text: Room:The rooms are small but super clean and exactly as shown on their website. Location: The location is perfect if you want to stay in a quiet residential area, away from the Oxford Street madness. It's perfectly well communicated via Jubille line underground (10 minute walk from the hotel) . 15min walk from Camden Town via Primrose Village, romantic walk.... Neighbourhood: charming! very british, no tourists and quiet streets. Wonderful cafes and restaurants in St Jonh's Wood Road. Much better than eating & having a drink around city centre! Staff: attention was perfect, they booked my cab back to the airport and were always available for any request. They aldo invited us for a live music concert at the Pub, sad we had other things planned that night. Definetely will stay again!

title: Simply Fabulous!
text: Arrived from Brighton a little bit weary. However the moment me and my lovely mum passed the threshold Nick was the perfect host. A relaxed and easy check in. Followed by a gigantic gin & tonic. Nick then showed us to our room No.1, which was splendid. We particularly loved the bed and bed linen. Especially the towels. Just like home from home. Would defiantly recommend this establishment any time. See you soon. Love Ems and Jen xx

title: Nice place for dog-lovers
text: My boyfriend and I spent a night here as it was conveniently close to London Zoo, which we were visiting the following day. The room was small but comfortable and very reasonably priced for London, though we did stay on a weekday so I can't comment on weekend prices. I've noticed several people complaining about noise - again, I can't comment on the noise level at weekends, but on the night we stayed there was no noise problem. We ate in the pub and found the food very tasty, though the 'salad' accompanying the meals was just a small heap of rocket. They also make some very nice, if somewhat pricey, cocktails - for some reason they do not do pina coladas, but there's a very nice banana-and-vodka cocktail called the Silky Banana. The pub is dog-friendly and the owners have two dogs themselves which wander freely around, so if you aren't keen on dogs or don't feel they should be allowed in an area where people are eating, this may not be the place for you. Personally, I enjoyed having the dogs around, they were very friendly and welcomed us as soon as we walked in. If you want a place you can bring your dog, or you just like dogs, this is a great place to come.

title: Great pub, Hotel and lovely dogs!!
text: We stayed at the New Inn for two nights as we were attending a wedding in the area. We found the staff to be mostly friendly during our stay. We arrived late on the Friday night and were welcomed to our room, which was decorated very nicely and was very clean. However, it did get very hot in the evening as we arrived during a spell of hot weather, this was obviously recognised as there was an air conditioning unit in the room, which we got a great deal of use out of it! Without it, things could have been quite uncomfortable! The only gripe about the room, would be the very small shower cubicle with the shower fitting that was just about hanging onto the wall... The pub itself is very nice and has a good atmosphere and also a really wide range of beers which was good to see. We ate at the pub during the first night of our stay and my pizza was fine, although was a little overcooked on the bottom. I ordered Chicken Ceasar Salad for my wife and although I was asked twice by the chap behind the bar to confirm that I wanted the chicken option of this salad, when it arrived it was inevitably the non-chicken option - essentially a plate of leaves and croutons . I'm sure that staff would have changed it had we informed them, but it had been a long day and it clearly have taken them a while to prepare a new one, so we just ate what arrived. Also had breakfast in the pub on our final morning and all of our breakfasts were excellent. By this time so friends of ours had also arrived at the hotel and all of our breakfasts were excellent. These ranged from the bacon and egg/Sausage and egg sandwiches to the American Breakfast and the pastry selection, which I think was the French option.... Overall a great place to stay in a fantastic part of London,

title: Wonderful stay!
text: Came here for a two night mid-week stay with my son. This B&B has recently been taken over but the new staff are friendly and welcoming and have made an excellent job of renovating the bar area. We were impressed by the size of the room, the location and the excellent quality of food served. If you want a nice, comfortable stay in a more relaxed area of London, this is the place to come. My only complaint would be that the room was way too hot so we had to open the windows overnight. Apart from this, a lovely stay, good size room and wonderful location (we walked to Primrose Hill and Camden Town from here). We highly recommend it!

title: Welcoming atmosphere
text: Thoroughly enjoyed our stay here, everything from the staff, service, room and food were of a fantastic standard. Just a short walk from regents park, enjoy the grounds or visit London Zoo. Close to Camden for a trip to the market. A nice high street with great cafés, bistros and shops. Qpark close by at reasonable rates. Would definitely go back and would certainly recommend.

title: Average
text: The atmosphere in the Pub is good. The food was nice. The area is very nice and not so far from City Center However, talking about the accommodation, not sure we should recommend it. First of all, the service wasn't good. The girl wasn't friendly. In addition, we booked a 2 nights stays but we had to change room after the 1st night due to a booking issue. We also add to pay everything at the check-inn, not during the check out. The rooms are ok for the price but the place is noisy until the pub close.

title: Very poor, smelly room - and very rude indeed.
text: I booked in here for one night and they insisted on payment in advance when I arrived. When I went to the room I saw why - they had given me a small room above the kitchens and it stank of food cooking. I could not open the window as this made the problem even worse. It was not cheap, either. They would not give me a refund and had no other room to offer - and the manager was rude and aggressive. As an older lady travelling alone, I felt quite intimidated and it seemed to me that they really took advantage of my situation. My honest advice to anyone thinking about booking this hotel is to go somewhere else.

title: Warm recommendation
text: I stayed at the New Inn for 7 nights 1-8th February 2008. The inn is in the quite St John's Wood area, very pleasnat and quite safe for a mother and her 10-year old. The pub on the ground floor was quiet at a reasonable time and the clientelle friendley and respectable. The owner and her staff really cared that we feek comfortable and have all we need. Our room was of a decent size, with twin beds, a desk, a sitting corner,and a large en-suite shower. Coffee tea and cookies were replenished every day by the kettle and the place was clean and warm. One morning we awoke to the sound of 20 horses marching down the street on their way toqfrom the barracks nearby. Both the full English and the "continental" breakfast were satisfying and prepared at our convinience. It is some 7-10 minutes to the St John's Wood underground station on the Jubillee line, an excellent place to start from wherever you head. There is a small Tesco on the way from the tube to the inn. open till midnight (maybe even later, I wouldn't know...). There are also restaurants, pubs, a Starbucks, a french bakery - a bank and more. the only one- minor- drawback is the narrow flight of stairs leading from the pub to the rooms abouve. it might be a bit difficult for challenged travellers.

title: Disappointing
text: We were excited to try this pub for Sunday lunch and had high hopes. The menu is very diverse - maybe too much so - there are pizzas and burgers and Spanish tapas and traditional Sunday lunch fare. One of our party's meal was missed off the order and turned up when the rest of us were almost finished. The garlic flatbread we ordered was not garlicky at all and the bread was tomato flavoured with some Parmesan and rocket on it. It was not the light pizza type bread we were expecting. My husband was disappointed with his roast beef as for the price there was little meat. My Caesar salad was not great - I had asked for chicken for an extra £4 and there was very little of it. The salad was overwhelmed with croutons and the dressing was average and not a usual Caesar dressing (from my experience). The service was good and friendly. There was live jazz playing which we found too loud for the space and meant it was very difficult to have a conversation. This place would be fine for a drink but I think the food is more pub grub than gastropub.

title: Great location, very clean room!
text: I was extremely happy with the New Inn. It is hard to find reasonably priced accomodation in London and even harder to find it in the neighborhood of St. John's Wood. The New Inn is an easy walk to St. John's Wood tube stop through a very pleasant, quiet and safe neighborhood and it is extremely close to Regent's Park. The location was fantastic. The other thing about The New Inn is that it was extremely clean. I am a big stickler on cleanliness and this place did not disappoint. The bedding and bathroom was clean and I found the beds to be comfy although my husband found the bed to be a little soft. We had the room at the front of the building with two twin beds and the room was very large. There is good cable TV in the rooms and free wireless internet access. The pub downstairs is very cute and nice as well. The staff were friendly and helpful and the room and hot water (in January, in England!) were nice and warm. There was no safe in the room but I really did not feel that I needed one there, frankly. There was no fridge in the room either but, again, since the pub is just downstairs, I did not find that to be a problem. My only complaints were that our room smelled quite musty when we first arrived. I am not sure if this was damp or water damage or what but there was definitely a smell of something like that. Once we aired out the room the smell did not bother me at all but my husband found he had trouble sleeping because whatever it was made him allergic on one night, so he was wheezing a bit. Also (this is common to hotels in England) after about 7 or 8 AM I found it to be extremely loud in the hallway as people were coming and going, the cleaning staff were bumping around, etc. etc. If you are jetlagged and trying to sleep in this might get a bit annoying - some earplugs might sort it out. Our room was directly next to the stairs so it was difficult to sleep once people were up and about for the day. The taxi driver had some trouble finding it -even though they are supposed to know how to get anywhere! :) - so you might want to bring a print out of a map the first time you go there. There's a one-way street system around there that threw him off a bit. All in all I was very happy with The New Inn. I will probably stay there again, mainly due to the location, cleanliness and price. There are lots of cute shops and restaurants right around there in the neighborhood as well as food shops, etc. It is all very convienient.

title: Fantastic Experience
text: Visited here on the back of a TravelZoo voucher, expecting the same old, same old. What a great surprise, welcoming owner as soon as we walked in, great beers on tap (approval from my father is testimony to this) and the food was all freshly cooked and enormous portions, remember this is using a voucher too! Our favourite part...pub dogs, we love a dog friendly pub and these dogs (both real characters) sitting in their leather basket watching all the activities go on and not being a nuisance is a pleasure to see. We will be revisiting, we've always loved this part of London, now there's another reason to visit, a great pub, serving great beer and great food hosted by a great landlord and friendly and helpful staff and 2 lovely dogs.

title: Great place to stay and eat
text: The staff were welcoming, friendly and helpful. The room was comfy with everything we needed and more. We had dinner and breakfast there, both of which were great. It's in a really good location, quiet but easy to get to the centre. The dogs were sweet too and caused no problems, in fact we prefer dogs in pubs, they tend to be more friendly and less pretentious places.

title: Love this place!
text: Food is great, very comfortable and inviting. Sitting on the soft leather couches with a pint of Guinness and two sweet puppies was exactly what I wanted after long flight from the states. This place felt like I'd been there millions of times before from the moment I walked in. I highly recommend this pub for anyone in search of a relaxing pint and good food.

title: Not what we had hoped.
text: Great service and food but this was unfortunately spoiled by pestering dogs running under our table and very noisy football crowd and TV's. Real shame as the staff were excellent but not as descibed on the Internet.

title: Excellent experience at the New Inn.
text: We stayed at the New Inn for five nights in May 2012. Even though we arrived early, Nick and the staff welcomed us warmly, offered us tea and hustled to get our room ready quickly. The room itself was very clean, spacious and comfortable. We had plenty of room to move around, do a little yoga on the floor and relax. Our room had a lovely view onto the residential street and trees in blossom. My husband had a work emergency early on, and Nick, particularly, as well as the staff were incredibly kind in accommodating him and changed what could have been a nightmare start to our holiday into a display of generosity that we won't forget. We had the continental breakfast, for us, tea and delicious warm pastries, which was VERY filling. I couldn't eat again until evening. We also had dinner and nibbles. All the food at the pub was excellent. We are vegetarians, and, again, they went out of their way to accommodate us. It's a comfortable pub, nicely decorated with a fun, varied, neighborhood clientele. The neighborhood is wonderful. The New Inn is a short walk to the St. John's Wood tube station and an even shorter walk to the High Street. It's away from much of the tourist madness, but only a short ride into the west end. Late one evening, we realized that we'd need a taxi early the next the morning to get to the train station for a day trip, and the staff arranged it perfectly. There is a narrow flight of stairs from the ground floor pub to the rooms, so if stairs are a problem, this isn't the place for you. It's also above a PUB, and not for the traveler who needs complete quiet early in the evening. The noise is muffled in the rooms, and was not an issue for us. It's happy pub noise, not car horns and helicopters. When the pub closes, it is quiet astonishingly quickly. All the staff were very friendly and welcoming. It was cool to be welcomed back every night --even by the dog! They stored our luggage on the last day as our flight was in the evening, carried our bags out to the car and bid us farewell like kind friends. We were very happy with our choice of The New Inn and had an excellent experience. We look forward to going back!

title: Rooms fine but dogs in restaurant are not
text: I stayed at this hotel recently. The rooms are clean and functional and good value for the price charged. Not luxurious but perfectly acceptable. Only criticism was that the wifi signal was weak and kept dropping out and the single beds in the twin room I was in are pretty narrow. What was not so nice was my experience in the restaurant. The owner's dog wandered round the restaurant and sat right alongside me, nudging my leg and begging for food. A few minutes later the owner appeared from behind the bar with a roll of paper and a spray bottle of disinfectant as the dog had had an 'accident' in the middle of the floor. A real shame as this is a lovely pub offering good value food and rooms in an excellent location. Without the dog situation I would have scored it at least a 4, possibly even a 5 but unfortunately given my experience I won't be going back.

title: No room at the Inn...again!!
text: Avoid at all costs!! Unfortunately I stayed here in 2013 and was treated extremely poorly. I decided to give the New Inn another go because I work locally and thought this may have been a one off. I tried to book a room and was told by Nick the owner that no rooms were available, fair enough, not a problem. I booked the Hilton in Kensington instead and thought nothing more of it. I was then contacted by Nick saying that he had a room available for me now if I would like to book. After a great deal of thought I thought why not because its very close to where I need to be for three days in July 2015. I made the booking and contacted Nick to say that I am away with work till later that evening and would send bank details through-which i did. I was told that this isn't a problem and all is fine with my booking. I then received an email the following afternoon to say that the room had gone and someone else had booked it??? My booking wouldn't be honoured, end of. What a shambles of an individual that Nick is and I wouldn't dream of staying here. The whole venue and management needs an overall and maybe Nick needs to attend a customer relations course...or two. FYI-rooms are very small and the venue is extremely noisy.

title: Surprise Birthday meal
text: My brother-in-law booked this restaurant for a joint birthday for Aimee and Edward (18 and 21 respectively) whilst we were in London for the weekend. He got to know this place from a TV programme he'd watched and then social media. He knew from this that they had an in-house puppy. The meal was very nice and the atmosphere and service were exceptional. We would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone staying in the area.

title: Great place
text: We really liked this place. We were going to Wembley arena twice in 3 days so decided to stay here as it was mid way between Wembley and the city centre. We were certainly not disappointed. Lovely pub situated 5/6 minutes walk from St Johns Wood underground which was 20 mins each way from where we wanted to go. The pub/rooms are in a lovely area with beautiful houses and lovely unique shops. We also had lunch on the first day and it was really nice. Ok, there was some noise in the room from the pub below on late Friday night but what do you expect? Especially like the pubs two puppies (and you too Nick) lol Would definitely consider staying here again when in the area.

title: Perfect !!
text: I stayed at the New Inn for 3 days and it truly exceeded my expectations. Set in a quit neighborhood but still close to St Johns Wood Tube station, Primrose Hill and Camden, with professional staff and exellent drink and food. In fact the food was so good I decided to have most of my meals there. Highly recommended....

title: Plenty of promise
text: Guess this is what happens when you take your time getting your review in! We arrived late September about a week after the new owner had taken over so there was no breakfast available during our stay, St.John's Wood High street was however only a five minute walk up the road. It is perfectly situated, close to Lord's cricket ground, Regents Park, Primrose Hill and the canal. On a quiet street so traffic was no problem and a short bus taxi or tube ride to Paddington for the Connect or Express to Heathrow. Judging from people who have stayed more recently the new owner is doing all the things he was telling us were planned. Would give it another go on our next London trip.

title: nice stay
text: The B&B is in the leafy St John's Wood area. I've previously lived in the same area for more than 5 years, and it is very pleasant to revisit. The inn has a very relaxing atmosphere, with spacious rooms (compared to most london hotels), helpful staff, and free Internet connection. It's 10 minutes to the metro station, 5 minutes to the high street, Regent's Park and Primrose Hill. The only problem during my 4-day stay is the breakdown of BT internet on the last night, but I guess that's more of the BT problem, than the hotel's problem. Overall, it's a pleasant journey.

title: Peace so near to the city
text: Just stayed for two nights here. Quirky in a good way. Nick Tyrie is a total dog worshiper and besotted with his new puppy! Clean and had two good night's sleeps as the traffic is barely around after about 11pm. If you don't mind walking half a mile, the Jubilee line takes you straight to Green Park and all the sights. We ate here both nights and had breakfast both mornings. The food is excellent -try the risotto and the pasta! Very friendly bar staff, too. Gorgeous neighbourhood.try not to gaze too hard at the houses and cars!

title: FANTASTIC place!!!
text: We could not have been happier than at the New Inn Pub = a total experience. The location is lovely and close to wherever you need to be. The staff - Flav and Jess - could not have been nicer. They all made you feel comfortable and at home. The rooms were exceptionally clean and updated. The pub is very classy as well as patrons - and honestly the only great cocktail I was able to get in all of Europe. The food was fantastic as well. There were 4 of us traveling and we all agreed it was the best place we stayed and it's the ONLY place we would stay in London. Kudos for Nick for such a super place. It will exceed your expectations!! XO see u soon!

title: WANT A NICE PLACE TO STAY IN LONDON. EXCEPTIONAL SERVICE & VALUE CAN BE FOUND AT THE NEW INN. OUTSTANDING
text: This is a place I will reccomend to all my family and friends going to London. Exceptional value for money, clean and good size room. Jan the landlady is a lovely person, always willing to help and ensured our stay was fantastic. The Inn is located in St John's Wood and is about a 10-15min walk to the underground station. St John's Wood High Street is only about 5mins away and has everything - cafe's, postoffice, banks, drycleaners....etc. Location is perfect. Premises is great - good meals! rooms good size and very clean. Wifi access is free as well. I will be staying here again, wouldn't stay anywhere else in London now. Thanks for a great stay Jan and staff! Sally

title: Great neighborhood, authentic London experience
text: Perfect location for a visit to London. Neighborhood Pub with rooms to rent above. Room was clean and updated. Beautiful view out the window into a courtyard. Great shower pressure in the tidy bathroom. Fun that neighbors and families hung out after school and work. Very good location for getting on the "Tube" to zip around the city and the train station is close. Just north of the London Zoo. Other ratings mention the narrow stairwell up to the rooms, but no big deal. Pub food was good, had the fish and chips and the thin crust pizza. best part of our trip was walking around this fantastic neighborhood after dinner and being able to peek in the beautiful homes. Felt very safe. We will stay at The New Inn again.

title: Wonderful B&B and Pub in St John's Wood!
text: We had the chance to stay here for 10 nights when we first moved to London this summer while we were searching for permanent housing. Nick and his staff were incredible, whether it was storing our extra luggage downstairs, providing us with excellent breakfasts and other meals along the way, and also having excellent accommodations with their new renovations. I am not sure what the rooms used to be like, but my wife and I could not have been happier to have the room we had, with an excellent bed and bathroom facilities, as well as enough space for 9 pieces of luggage which we had moved with to the UK! We have continued to go back to the pub since we moved elsewhere in the city, and hope to be loyal customers for as long as we are here. Thanks so much!

title: Great pub, good food
text: We ate on a Friday night, having come down on the train that evening. My friend had booked. Very welcoming owner and friendly staff. Stowed our bags in the back room for us. Had the house wine, which was lovely and reasonably priced. The food was great, good sized portions. Nothing to complain about. As I say the owner could not have been friendlier, even moved some guests of his to a different table as my friend fancied that one!

title: great location, good value for money
text: My wife and I stayed at The New Inn for 4 nights, and we loved it. Nice neighborhood, all you need is nearby. Room comfortable and cleen. Jan was friendly. Good value for money. We will come again.

title: Decent digs in great neighborhood
text: St. John's Wood is an upscale residential neighborhood (Paul McCartney lives there) on the Jubilee underground line. The New Inn is a 200 year old pub 2 short blocks off the busy neighborhood high street, the rooms are up above the pub. Our room was clean, spacious, and comfortable, unexciting decor, good water pressure in shower, zero noise from outside (though some from another room). Friendly by London standards. No phone, bring your own. Beer was good, we didn't try the food, opting instead to walk to some of the many cafes and restaurants nearby.

title: Nick Tyrie and his team made our stay very special!
text: My husband and I decided to stay here after seeing Nick Tyrie on 'Four In A Bed' and it was a lovely experience altogether! We were made to feel very welcome by Nick Tyrie and his staff. The food is great. The atmosphere is always warm and welcoming. And on Sunday we had an amazing Sunday Roast with very good live jazz band playing. We will definitely return to stay here. Highly recommended!!

title: Short trip to London
text: Fabulous hotel. Atmosphere is brilliant, rooms are clean, modern and very comfortable beds. And the all the staff made you feel very welcome. Not for those of you who want to sleep early as above the brilliant gastro pub so music on beneath. Highly recommended

title: Another great stay in London
text: This is the second time that we have stayed at The New Inn, and we enjoyed it even more than the first. Stayed this time for three nights. Breakfast choice and flexibility is superb. If you are looking for a place of style, with great standards in food, drink, and extremely good service, then this is all it promises. It's not trying to be all things to all people, but if you 'get' this sort of place then you'll love it. Nick and the staff are terrific hosts.The New Inn is now firmly set as our regular choice of stay when in London.

title: Great value in central London!
text: I've stayed here for two nights with my girlfriend mid Octobre. We wanted to see London so I looked for a nice place to stay relatively close to the city centre. I found this hotel on tripadvisor, it had really nice reviews so I decided to book a room for two nights there. The hotel really lived up to my expectations. The staff was really nice and friendly and the rooms were tidy and cozy. The location is also excellent. It's about a five minute walk to the nearest subway station (st. John's Wood) and you can get anywhere from there in a matter of minutes. The hotel seemed to be situated in a relatively wealthy neighbourhood and we could walk back to the hotel at night without having a feeling that it was not safe. It was also very nice to have a drink at the pub when you get back from a long day of city-seeing. It feels like getting home instead of arriving at "just a place to stay". I would advise anyone who's looking for a citytrip to London to stay here.

title: Very very noisy
text: If you want to sleep don't stay here. Although this is above a pub the room shook until 12 15 am and screaming and shouting was evident from the staff clearing up until 1 15am on complaining the following day the proprietress commentd that 1.15am was not late, he was extremely rude and impolite do not stay here I had to take a sleeping tablet also it's quite expensive, no warning of noise on website. Complaints procedure inadequate, I asked for a refund and was refused I'm very upset by their attitude

title: Loved this place and the area is fab.
text: I liked everything about this place: staff are super friendly and polite, they even take good care of their ever present spaniel. Room and bed were comfy and very clean, enough storage, bathroom looked tired but shower delivered with a punch! Has a dinner here on a Saturday night and both meals were good. For Breakfast we headed to the bakery on the main street (Illy coffes, and excellent non greasy croissants, pizzas and breads, some gluten free cakes too. After a night out we were given a warm welcome by the owner and we chilled on the sofa with a lovely glass of wine listening to good music whilst the locals are chatting and some dancing! Great way to chill out after a disappointing night out in Camden! Quiet neighbourhood at nightime (and day time), which was perfect for us. We explored the neighbourhood in the afternoon, residential and posh in parts. Lovely walks along Regent's park nearby and the canal, a bit of window shopping along St. John's Wood high street (lovely boutiques). Perfect way to kill a couple of hours on a sunny afternoon. Tube station St. Johns Wood, (Jubilee Line) its within an easy 5 minute walk. Nearby Abbey Road (The famous image of The Beatles crossing the road) can be fun fjust to see motorists getting upset over tourists taking ages doing silly poses in the middle of the road! PS Hampstead nearby its also very lovely and have some great Young's Pubs. Cheers!

title: A Real Find
text: Finding a decent and reasonably priced hotel in London is pretty tricky. The main brands all know how to charge and service and value for money can be hard to find. The New Inn in St. John's Wood is a Pub with rooms, a Hotel with a Pub, a Restaurant with a Pub/Hotel. You get the picture. I had the pleasure of all three. It's a good pub, a comfortable hotel (excellent large room) and my chosen New Inn Burger was one of the best I've had in a long time. I'll be back. Just need to persuade them to stock Carling.....

title: Overpriced for what you get
text: We recently stayed at the New Inn and it has varied good and bad points. Good points- Very friendly and overall good service. Great location. Bad points- Small and stuffy rooms. Noisey. Attention to detail. Breakfast. It was extremly hot when we stayed, i asked if there was aircon in the room and the lady said no but theirs windows. That would have been a good opportunity to tell us there was a fan in there which we only found the next morning when checking out. Breakfast is a joke. As a vegetarian it was an insult to be given a full english with meat included. Surely you should be asked what you would like? Clearly just heated up in the microwave by the cleaner. certainly not worth paying extra. If the rooms have been refurbished which i was told they have, i would hate to think what they were like before. They are very basic and small. Overall staff were extremley friendly and its a great location but for the standard, i think its overpriced. Really its a fab pub with a few rooms on the side that comes across as a second priority.

title: A little gem in London
text: Great location in a wonderful area. We have stayed here twice and enjoyed both visits. The new owner is doing much to upgrade the decor and while the rooms may be next and with that the price, We find the rooms adequate and clean. The localle is wonderful and convenient. The restaurant is fine for good pub food which we prefer in the larger cities.

title: Cosy Oasis in a beautiful part of London
text: Arriving at the New Inn and our cosy room was the ultimate reward for a 28 hour flight from Australia. We fell in to our spotlessly clean, comfy beds and slept for 12 hours. A lovely cooked breakfast in the very English pub set us up for a good day of work and sightseeing. The only comment would be that on Fridays and Saturdays there is live music until after midnight. Unless you are blind drunk or extremely jet-lagged (like we were) you will NOT sleep on these nights until the music has finished as it is like having a band in your room. However, for many this will not be an issue as it is very enjoyable to sit in the pub and enjoy the music. And the rest of the week is quiet and peaceful. It's close to a tube station and very accessible to the rest of inner city London. We loved it!

title: Excellent service, good beer, great food
text: Popped in for an evening meal with my family including two four year olds after a day at the zoo. Staff were welcoming and friendly, including giving free finger puppets to my kids. Food was excellent, the prawn and chilli risotto was the best risotto I have had and I have had a lot. Couldn't find a bad thing to say about it.

title: tip top
text: We ate here on Sunday night and had a wonderful meal, served by charming and efficient staff. Burgers are to die for, chips are superb and both food and drinls are reasonably priced (espeically for NW8). A fine time was had so AAA+ all round.

title: Enjoyed The New Inn
text: My wife and I made our first trip to London in late January and we stayed at the New Inn. We resrved our room last July after seing the reviews on Trip Adviser. I was apprehensive about this B&B because there were only a few reviews and all were so "over the top" in their praise. Found other reviews on other sites and they were also very positive. You can add our very positive experience to the others as we thoroughly enjoyed our stay. Best features are the cleanliness of the rooms and bathrooms. Second best is being able to come in after a hard day of walking and getting a drink in the pub to take to your room and enjoy after getting your shoes off. The pub food is very good. There is not a lot of hand holding as far as site seeing but Jan is helpful if you see her. The ten mnute walk to the Tube is enjoyable but not the walk back after a long day of walking. Taxis from the St. John's Wood station are available if you don't feel lke walking. The location away from main sites was not a problem for us as the tubes are easy to use and the small town feel is great. The worst features are the steep set of stairs going up to the rooms and if your windows are open, the noise on Friday nights as the pub customers are visiting on the street after closing time. The live band on Saturday night could be heard in the room, so light sleepers wll not enjoy their stay on the weekend. Since my wife and I are not light sleepers we had no problem. The beds are typical of those found in most European hotels, a little lumpy and the pillows are a little hard. No problem for us. We ate at two of the restauarants three blocks away on Allitsen Rd and they were both very good as was the Thai food at he pub -that's correct...excellent Thai food at an English pub! The two restaurants were Tino's and The Rotisserie.

title: LOVELY NIGHT'S SLEEP
text: Lovely leafy location, slept like a baby, staff extremely friendly and a really good hot and fierce shower- just what you need after a day trudging round the sights

title: A Gem
text: My husband and I stayed three nights at the New Inn in early December, 2008, and we had a wonderful time. I think the hotel's best quality is the inkeeper, Jan and the rest of the staff - they were all so welcoming, friendly, and helpful. The downstairs pub was charming and the locals at the bar were very friendly as well. Our room above the pub was clean and comfortable, and the daily attention to detail by the cleaning staff was impressive. The New Inn is located in a quiet suburban neighborhood. The 10-minute walk to the tube each day was actually quite peaceful and relaxing. In short, it would have been easy to book a room in a big chain hotel downtown, but I am so glad I did a little research and found the New Inn. Staying in a locally-owned establishment with lots of character made our visit to London truly memorable and enjoyable.

title: Food and service
text: We came to the new inn for a bite to eat the other day and were met by the owner Nick. We had a fish finger sandwich (to die for) and the tastiest seafood penne pasta we have had in years. The food was reasonably priced considering the quality. Great job guys, keep it up :-)

title: Not sure what the hype about this place is....
text: We havent stayed in a large amount of hotels in London, so I guess we dont know how bad it can get. But we stayed here in January for 4 nights and had the worst sleep ever. Outside the window in the apartment block next to us was constant noise from water running onto plastic (granted this is outside the control of the hotel). The rooms were really hot even in winter with all the heaters turned off, becuase the central heating pipes were too hot. We ended up sleeping with the window open, which meant the noise was even louder. The floor creaked whenever you moved, and we could hear other guests coming and going throughout the night. The thai food in the pub was shocking, though granted we come from Sydney where the thai food is amazing and really cheap. Some positive points though. The place was very clean with a comfortable bed. The area is very nice, safe and wealthy, close to the park and about 5-10 minutes walk from the train station.

title: Not what it was
text: Just returned from a long weekend and stayed at the New Inn for the Ashes Test. A regular for several years under the previous owner I had become used to the great ‘feel’ and atmosphere of the pub which has really changed under the new owners I’m afraid for the worst. So from the top here are personal thoughts Prices As a previous writer stated the prices have increased significantly. It used to be £75 a night and now its £130 a night. Yes it’s in a really nice area of London and within a short walk of Lords but at the end of the day it’s overpriced for what you get and the price does not include breakfast. Food We only tried the breakfast and at £12.95 it was expensive. If you stayed in the New Inn with the previous owner you will remember how good the breakfast was. Loads of choice with Fresh juice (not carton concentrate) Cereals, choice of white or brown toast and everything you would expect for a really good breakfast. By comparison at another £3 this was dreadful. It was clearly prepared and cooked the night before and re-heated in a microwave. Please do not try it, save your money. I did not try the evening food so cannot give an opinion but the menu looked OK and previous reviewers have praised it so maybe the breakfast is the only one not freshly made. The food would have to go some to beat the Thai food the pub used to serve when the kitchen was leased to them. It was outstanding and that was demonstrated by the difficulty in getting a table. No problem in getting a table now on a Friday or Saturday evening even during an Ashes test? Make up your own mind.. Noise This place has suddenly become very noisy which is fine if you like ‘repetitive’ music banging out live all night and into the early hours of the morning. Way to loud and unnecessary but I think its part of the ‘new image’ the place is trying to project, a new kind of ‘trendy’ pub. Way over the top and the constant ‘replay’ of the same old dance music drove me nuts particularly when I was trying to get to sleep at 1 on Sunday morning. Turn it down and give the local residents and guests paying £130 a night a break The other thing that seemed to be happening was a procession of glasses being dropped in the bar so the sound of breaking glass was pretty disconcerting. There were 4 in the hour and a half I was there! There were a lot of really drunk people and not just the cricket fans. Service Bit of attitude behind the bar from one of the staff when I had the ‘cheek’ to order another drink after he went to the till following serving me a beer without waiting to hear my next request or asking me if there was anything else? I really hate that. Not appreciated and necessary and you know, some people shouldn’t be in some jobs and this is not the job for him. Before then, when my lady arrived following a 3 hour car journey and walked to the bar to ask for the key, she was asked to pay up immediately even before she got to the key to the room? Not necessary, we booked months ago and they had my credit card details and given the event itself (ashes) and the scarcity of accommodation in the area, did they think we were going to turn around and walk out? She was pretty upset and told the guy to wait until she had at least got to the room and seen me when I got back a couple of hours later after the game? The owner got wind of this and apologised to her for this and suggested the man that had asked for the money had a ‘language problem’? He sounded Eastern European which is not a slant on his origins but its about training and understanding isn’t it? We checked out a day early at 6:00 pm when the game had finished and lost £130 which we did not expect to get back which was OK. As the breakfast was not paid for this was waived which was a nice gesture and appreciated. Thanks Nick. Atmosphere I didn’t really like it and it is nothing like it was before. Clearly there were people absolutely trashed and were continued to be served when they had drunk enough and shouldn’t really have been served, but to be fair to the new inn, this happens a lot in pubs in the UK so its not overly unusual just a bit worrying when these people cant even stand up?. What I didn’t like is the ‘short measures’ on the beer and lager the bar staff serve. ‘Big frothy continental Heads’ on flat real ale? I didn’t like the indignant look when I asked them to top it up which was done reluctantly and still not to the top of the glass (they, like most pubs do not serve in ‘oversized glasses) This is short measures and a blatant attempt to make extra money on the beer. No excuses. If you stayed at the New Inn in the past it was always packed on match days with cricket people, standing room only with good numbers outside. Now its nothing like this at the biggest game on the test calendar and the pub has resorted to ‘lure’ people in by getting young girls in black T-shirts, shorts and stiletto’s handing out flyers outside Lords itself to get people interested. That’s how the appeal of this place has declined I’m afraid and the bars around the corner are the really busy one’s after the game, not the New Inn. A sign of the times? Overall Not even close to what it was before and this article is not an attempt to tell a story about how good the old days were but I have the benefit of knowing what was and now what is. Nick, the owner has his work cut out here, he is a nice guy and will listen to you if you have any issues. He does have a potential goldmine that had a solid and reliable customer base but he has taken it in the wrong direction in my opinion and as a cricket favourite it is a shadow of its past glory. Before, unless you booked the day after the days of the test matches were announced, you had no chance of getting in. On Saturday morning I saw a couple checking out who clearly were tourists and not cricket followers? Customers other than cricket followers booking a night in the ‘New Inn’ during the busiest test in the cricket calendar around the corner from Lords. Unheard of?. OK that’s only a few days a year in the summer and the rest of the year is up for grabs but I think it is very average and I would not stay there again in or out of season (which I used to do) Gone is the brilliant Thai kitchen serving fantastic meals every evening, the band on a Saturday night playing ‘London Songs’ and the brilliant hostess (Jan) who really bothered and took time to get to know you and make sure your stay ‘worked’. Having read all of the last 2 years of Trip advisor reports on the New Inn, someone did mention their booking being cancelled 3 weeks before they arrived which caused them a lot of grief. The same happened to me shortly after the New Inn changed hands, but fortunately I was able to make alternative arrangements. Before I came down this time, I phoned a month before to make sure all was OK which was confirmed. If you book the New Inn and getting cancelled would cause you a lot of inconvenience, I would suggest you do the same just to be sure.

title: Great all round
text: The food was excellent - we had the bavette steaks - and the real ale was in top condition. We stayed in room 1, it was clean and comfortable. The location was ideal (close to the main shopping areas and 20 mins on the Jubilee line to Wembley for the show). Staff were all very friendly. A very good value place to stay.

title: Convenient location, helpful staff, excellent breakfast
