Having read previous reviews I concur that the rooms are small, however this is typical of London and for one night was not a problem for our needs...tea and coffee facilities in the room and superficially clean (the top of the wardrobe could do with a dusting once in a while). Luckily the air conditioning was functioning in our room, although I overheard other guests having issues with theirs. The main issue for me, from a hospitality point of view, is the service. I rang the hotel earlier in the day and the receptionist simply answered hello...introducing yourself and confirming the name of the property is a basic greeting when communicating with guests over the phone. Likewise our check in was not entirely welcoming. The staff here do need work on dealing with customers complaints and general communication with guests

title: DO NOT STAY HERE!!!
text: The Taxi driver had to go round the block twice as sign was so small. Wish he hadn’t of found it! On arrival the lady told us all about facilities. She told us Breakfast times (incorrectly!) Very tiny room. Claustrophobic almost. You had to step up into the shoebox of and ensuite. No Air Conditioning! The room was very hot and had problems opening the window. At one point we wedged it open with a bottle. Asked for a fan, which was delivered. No bottled water in the room. Asked for Ice, 1 small glass given! The power points were in an unexcessable area. We couldn’t charge our phones or my hearing aids. In the morning your woken up with the smell of cooking. We went down to Breakfast to be told it was finished, pointing to a card displayed. We had been given the wrong time for Breakfast. At this point the lady started speaking in a foreign language to another lady working there. Extremely rude. I went to reception to complain and he tried to make me look like a liar! Saying the reception lady wouldn’t give the wrong time. We were also told it was only complimentary breakfast anyway! Eventually we had cearials and toast in our room as staff seemed exceptionally unfriendly. I will NEVER return to this hotel again. It’s disgusting how they treat their guests. My advice STAY AWAY!

title: Missing property
text: Stayed here for one night. Left my necklace on the bedside table, a gift from my son. When I called them later that day they said nothing was found !? You don’t want to believe staff would be dishonest.

title: Acceptable business stay
text: This hotel is in a convenient area, close to several tube stops on useful lines. There's no real services here beyond the breakfast--you can't even get something to drink outside of the morning. I just needed a place to sleep and shower while working nearby, and this place can be fine for that. No lift, you'll be hauling your bags up stairs. The staff are friendly enough. My friend staying here left a bag (and his passport, which he didn't even realize) when heading to work, forgetting he was supposed to check out that day before heading to work. A phone call sorted that. They emptied the room, found all his items, and checked his bag, all with no charge for missing regular checkout. Rooms are small even by London standards

title: Great Location
text: Stayed here Oct 2013 for 3 nights. Would recommend asking for a room at the back as on a busy road and traffic noise and don't know why but the noise curfew between the hours of 11pm - 6am do not apply to this Area of London and many sirens could be heard. Room was comfortable and breakfast was great. Staff very polite and helpfull. The location was brilliant with a five minute walk to Goodge Street and 7-10 minutes to Oxford Street. Would stay here again.

title: You get what you pay for
text: The hotel is in a great location, especially for the West End. Staff were friendly enough, the room was a little tatty in places but overall acceptable. Only moan would be the poorly fitted door letting a lot of light through from the landing. Cheap accommodation for Central London.

title: Husbands Birthday
text: We visited London for my husbands birthday and wanted a hotel within walking distance of the theatres. The hotel was as expected for what we paid. The room & bathrooms were clean & tidy and well decorated. There was a mix up with our room when we arrived and there was confusion amongst the staff but it was eventually sorted and it didn't impede on our stay in any way. The only down side is that the hotel is located on 4 floors and there is no lift and as I am currently waiting surgery on my knee proved a little difficult. The breakfast was good and there was plenty of choice. The staff were friendly. We would definitely use this hotel again for a short break.

title: 5th June.
text: Dirty, located in room with thin window and lots of traffic outside. No sleep, freezing cold in a room where your name could be written in the dust. Staff were unhelpful and was told there in nothing they could do as the manager wasn't in. Would not recommend. Looked under the bed to find it covered in rubbish including 3 dirty teaspoons.

title: Ordinary hotel in great location
text: This hotel is in a fantastic and safe location. Hotel has great street appeal. I was traveling solo at the time and my room was no larger than a shoebox, room only for the bed and the suitcase. Basic cleanliness. There was nowhere in the hotel to go and sit to read, watch television or have a cup of tea. I stayed a week, but only ate breakfast there once. The breakfast room was in the basement and was hot and airless and too small for the number of people they were trying to service. Food not great either. The staff were reasonably helpful but not at all friendly.

title: Pretty misleading, CHECK ROOM BEFORE PAYING!! NOT 4 STAR!
text: I feel somewhat tricked staying at this hotel. Just shows you that you need to really check things out well. Booking.com shows it at 4 star hotel, which is completely misleading and in accurate. The hotel is for sure at the one start level. My room was under 2 meters wide, tiny and nothing like described. In the 20 years visiting London I have never seen such a small room, nor such minimal service for such a high price. For example, no room existed for my average size suitcase as it would prevent exiting the room. If you must stay here, the price level should be approx 50 sterling max, sub 100 dollars. Rooms are for ONE person max. ALSO, do not pay until you check the room! Check around

title: You get what you pay for!
text: Only paid £75 for a night with breakfast and considering the location it is hard to complain. I booked a 'small' single room and my god was it small. The tiniest room I've ever stayed in, no wardrobe and tiny ensuite but it was clean and for the money I guess I can't complain!!

title: Not as bad as I thought from seeing the reviews
text: Having seen some pretty awful reviews I was dreading my stay however I was pleasantly surprised. I had a tripe room (207) to myself which is probably why I am not complaining about the room space - I thought the room price was reasonable for London and also how central it was. Decor was nice. The bed was so comfortable - I slept like a log, no road traffic where I was. A little bit of dust, breakfast room was full and I ended up sitting with a stranger but it wasnt a prob. The full english breakfast was great. Yoghurts werent very nice. Staff were pleasant,

title: Bear grills for the weekend
text: Arrived here on Thursday, the reception by staff was quite rude. The window had no seal, & during the snow, staff left us with an extra sheet for warmth. Three attempts at securing a heater that worked were fruitless so we returned to our ice palace to sleep in hoodies and bottoms. If the receptionist could roll her eyes any more she would cause herself injury. Breakfast was abysmal. And found blood on the base of my bed! I would sooner camp in a field.

title: Totally useful, clean and comfortable.
text: I stayed for one night in the cheapest single room. Tiny, but perfectly adequate and comfortable. Clean, sparkling, compact shower room, and single bed, which fitted in to width of room. Hangers, TV. Everything needed for a £65 stay. Close to Goodge St, Euston and Tottenham Court Road stations, and a short walk to Oxford Street, Charing Cross Road and Soho. Would definitely stay again.

title: Theatre break
text: Staff Friendly location very good Definitely not a 4 star Hotel disappointed thought it would be a lot more luxurious no bar We only stayed for one night, the room was very hot and the bathroom very small Breakfast in the morning was good.

title: Not brilliant
text: We booked this hotel as it stated it was close to London picadilly however it was not as close as you would imagine and in fact was a taxi journey or the tube. The hotel is clean but very small and cramped, we struggled to get ready on a morning. The breakfast area was also really cramped. And the breakfast was tiny in comparison to what you get at other hotels. We will not be staying here again. But that is our personal opinion.

title: On balance, good value stay in a good location
text: There are thousands of 'budget' places like this in London, ranging from really terrible to pretty good. I've stayed in all kinds.The Bloomsbury Palace is at the higher end of the scale. I booked a single room, which admittedly was one of the smallest I've ever stayed in. But it was clean (recently refurbished), the bed was comfortable and the bathroom had plenty of hot water, towels and other essentials. Wifi was free and worked perfectly. There was even free tea, coffee and biscuits. No wardrobe, just a rail to hang things, but nothing to complain about unless you're the cat -swinging type. It was very noisy at night (room 106 is at the front of the building on the first floor, and Gower Street is busy all night.) But it's Central London - what do you expect? With a bus stop across the street, offering regular buses to the West End, and Goodge Street tube 5 mins walk away, it's well connected. Plenty of coffee shops, restaurants, pubs, shops nearby. The breakfast was freshly cooked and a pretty good Full English it was too - served by friendly and smiley staff. Finding a place to stay down town without paying an arm and two legs is never easy. This place was a pretty good compromise, and I will probably use it again.

title: Very good location but
text: Rooms are small and it is a very noisy stress even with the window shut. Staff are ok they did sort out the issues I had in the room. Breakfast was fine as I did get an English breakfast every day and coffee was drinkable. Wifi was ok except for one day when it was completely down. There is no lift so a bit hard when you are in teh 3rd floor!

title: Ummmm
text: So I almost cancelled this trip but it wasn't as bad. Let's start with the good things. The location is great and the staff are polite, breakfast was good with great staff. Now for the rest. The breakfast room was cramp with very little space. The building was dirty throughout and ran down, the room was not the biggest, it was a double, the bed sheets seemed fresh but the ensuit was small, tiered and the rest of the room was very warn, a unsecured window with no lock, a door that looked like it had recently been kicked in. The reception staff are where I get big concerns, they wondered off and left customers luggage in clear view and open to anyone to take. A front door with a security access card yet the door left open. If you want to save yourself from worry or stress then book elsewhere as there many better places.

title: OK hotel
text: Good location and pleasant hotel staff. The room was small, but nicely furnished. The door frame into the bathroom was full of marks and fingerprints. The bed was small and noisy. The breakfast staff were very short. The breakfast cook wore flip flops whilst cooking (!). I would not come back.

title: Stay away
text: Booked this hotel through booking.com sold to me as 4 star hotel. At best I would give it a 2. Rooms were small with no storage space. It was dirty, there was grime and dust, stains on the carpet and bed. The heat was unbearable. The breakfast was limited to either an awful english breakfast or cereals. Breakfast room was small and cramped, you could hardly move and at times there was a long wait to get a table. Staff were unfriendly and unhelpful and only our acknowledged our presence once, for payment. Internet was not working. Really disappointed and from now on will read reviews thoroughly even when booking a 4 star. Worst "hotel" ever!

title: Small rooms, overpriced, unhelpful staff but good location.
text: If the staff were better I would have given it another star, but for me there were too many negatives to outweigh the positives. Yes, it's a good location, I found it very easy to get around. Yes, it was neat, clean and comfy. BUT The rooms are literally tiny, once my suitcase was on the floor, I had no where to walk. The shower had a beautiful large rainfall shower head, but the shower was the same size as the head, so it was hard to shower. Once out of the shower I had to go out of the bathroom and shut the door to dry myself as there was no room in the bathroom. If you're doing lots of touristy things and just need a place to sleep - it's more than fine. I feel like I paid a lot to stay here but it was last minute and everywhere else was booked out so not sure how it usually compares. My big issue was the staff. On arrival I wasn't greeted with any pleasantries and was literally given the key and said 'its on the first floor, go up these stairs, there's no lift'. Okay. But I have over 30 kgs of luggage... It took about 10 minutes to get up the stairs and the two staff members could see me and no one helped. I had to ask for a map the next day and when asking about the area, the gentlemen at the desk had no clue. Again when I left and asked for the address to tell my cab, the lady at the desk said 'I don't know, google it'. RIDICULOUS. What would have been an average-good stay, turned bad because of this for me. Hospitality is your job. Be nice. Rant over.

title: Well located but with some negatives
text: Well-located Hotel, 10 mins by feet to Oxford Street, 3 mins to tube stations Euston Square and Googe Street, 5 mins to tube station Warrent Street - easy going everywhere! Booked a small single room which was really very small but nevertheless ok as I was just sleeping there. The room included shower and toilet, a big flatscreen, free WiFi, tea/coffee and cookies on the bedside table and a quite good English breakfast. It was nice furbished, 3 cushions, bed was quite wide and good, no cupboard. The staff was nice and helpful, storing the suitcase though checked-out was no problem. Unfortunately it was very very cold in the room though the heater was running all the time and the window seemed to be fine, I had to ask for additional blankets. And it could have been more clean, there was dust and dirt under the bed and also behind the bedside table. This is why only 3 stars finally.

title: Good Value - Great location
text: After reading some reviews on this hotel I was a little wary about staying here, however I was pleasantly surprised. I stayed here for 1 night with 2 friends last weekend. We had a triple room which had one double bed and a pull up bed. We had plenty of room and it was clean and tidy. I would give the bed 3/5 for comfort, it was a bit too hard for me. There was a slight gap in the door which meant a bright light from the hallway was shining in throughout the night, apart from the we experience no other problems. Our check in was simple and easy, I did email a week before to see if we could check in any earlier but no one got back to me! We didn’t spend much time in the room so for what we paid it was perfect for us. In a great location and luckily as it was bank holiday we could park within 1 minute walk away for free! Beware, this hotel has an early checkout of 10:30 am and the free breakfast finishes at 10!

title: SMALL ROOM AND TERRIBLE BREAKFAST AREA
text: Very disappointing stay at the Bloomsbury. The room, in the basement, was very cramped and far too hot. We didn't mind so much as we only went back to sleep but the next morning was a joke. The breakfast room is tiny and, like the other reviewers, we queued up for breakfast. he waitress did suggest we split up along the breakfast bar but we told her we'd prefer to enjoy our breakfast together. Eventually we got a table and just as we were sitting down we were asked if we wanted a cooked breakfast and if so what type of egg. After telling the waitress what we wanted we got up to get cereal and fruit and no longer had we sat down and the breakfasts arrived so we had to try and fit them on the side of the table until we'd finished! I also asked for HP sauce but was advised that they no longer provide it. Well as it's an ENGLISH breakfast I cannot understand why they don't provide it. Also my Husband ordered coffee and they must have just added water to a used coffee pot as it was disgusting and undrinkable. When I complained to the guy on reception he just shrugged his shoulders but I think this may have been because he didn't really understand me as he spoke broken English....never again!!

title: The worst hotel I have ever stayed
text: I stayed at "Bloomsbury Palace Hotel" between July 2 and 4, 2012. Originally I was going to stay 5 nights, but I cancelled it as soon as I found another much much better hotel nearby. I regretted choosing "Bloomsbury Palace Hotel" as soon as I saw the room (rm 304). The room is so small that the single bed inside occupies 60% of the space! There is no table, no chair, no fridge, and no place to even hang your cloths. Worst still, the bed is not flat (about 20 degrees inclined). But the worst among all is the room price. For a hotel with such a low quality, I was asked to pay 145 pounds per night (YES! 145 pounds for single use). July 2 and 4 are just normal week days!!! For your information, I came to London from Japan for an international conference at the University of London. So far I have stayed in nearly 300 different hotels around the world. "Bloomsbury Palace Hotel" is perhaps the worst I have ever stayed. You will regret choosing this hotel.

title: Very small rooms,especially the shower, basement rooms 🙈🙈🙈🙈
text: Location of hotel good for the sights, bare basic in the room. You really pay for what you get. Basement rooms very small, not noises once you shut the windows. Staff very polite, and helpful. Good English breakfast ,cereals, prunes,grapefruit, various juices, fresh fruit available, hot coffee on tap. Beds comfy .they kept the room tidy for us. They could do with an upgrade in rooms and a fresh coat of paint outside ,looking tired

title: Average hotel in great location
text: Great location. Booked when we couldn't get the hotel we wanted. A little pricey for what you get. Small and quirky but reasonably comfortable. We had room 5LG (lower ground cellar room which looked cave-like!) and booked the small single room for our 21-yr old daughter. Hers was basically a storage cupboard turned into a bedroom. Don't book if you're claustrophobic! Staff ARE friendly and helpful - especially the domestic staff and cooks. Breakfast was tasty. Photographs are very clever and suspect the place was "dressed" for them - or they're very old! Our bed space was well presented and quiet. Very hot, but two floor fans were provided. Shower a little tired and not very powerful, but did the job. Okay for a one-night stay in a very handy area. Keep your expectations realistic and you will be fine! Down side is definitely the limited 7-9 breakfast timing and 10.30am standard checkout, although they do look after your luggage for you if you want to wander.

title: Just DON' T
text: I knew London prices are very high, and when I booked this at a what I thought to be a reasonable price, assumed things would be just okay, I knew I'd be out and about most of the time. Well, if you're a big person, or overweight, or claustrophobic keep looking, at least DON'T choose the single room! I'm none of the above, but after tripping over myself for the umpteenth time just getting out of the shower, I decided to write this review. Firstly, you cannot sit on the toilet without bumping the sink, the shower is almost silly small, so try not to drop your soap. The head of the single bed is less than one foot from the only window. The NOISE of the busy street is overwhelming. I live in a big city, but never have I heard traffic like this. And , it's relentless, day and night. Even with the closed window, there's traffic. No matter what the temperature is outside, the room is hotter than Hades. There's no fan, no air conditioning, no circulation-- it's HOT. I can't even imagine being in here during the high summer. Got nowhere when I asked if there were other rooms available-- all the singles are in the front, and nothing else was available, even at a higher price

title: Don't go... just don't.
text: I stayed there for two nights for a conference despite the bad reviews thinking hmmm how bad can it be. I was wrong very very wrong. This place is really aweful to the point i can't even start. Just a few highlights. The rooms don't have aircondition but what is more the windows don't work properly. So you essentially need to just steam in the 28 degrees heat and of course you can't possibly sleep in that heat. You try at least to get some cold water from the tap only to realise that the tap only produces hot and luke warm water. The same goes for the trickling shower which you can't even regulate the temperature properly because the handle is broken. The water pressure is so low that it feels like a small dog is peeing on top of you. After all that you at least want something decent for breakfast and what you get is a terrible version of an "English breakfast" which makes airplane food look like a Michelin star restaurant. Need i say more? If you like torture maybe you'll enjoy your stay.

title: Get what you pay for place to stay
I expected more, but it's another average hotel
text: I booked this hotel for my mum, coming to visit me with a couple of friends. I choose it because I was looking for a nice place, easy to find and going around, so they could be slightly independent, with a decent size of rooms and a nice service. This was one of the cheapest, even if rather expensive, roughly around £55 each in a triple room, but I thought that it would be suitable for their needs. The room was nice, but nothing really amazing, standard double bedroom size, with an awful armchair bed instead of a proper bed fitted as the 3rd bed, looking awful and small. And the room was definitely small for three people. The bathroom was ok, again, nothing really exciting for the price (more than £150 per night). They didn't change the towels and tidy up the room, the carpet in the toilet stays there for all the 3 nights. The reception didn't help much, they were not the kind of service you're expecting. Not even saying 'Hi' or 'Bye' when you were coming/leaving. It sounded to me like "Please, don't disturb". We had to wait 10 minutes once for a person to arrive at the reception desk. We asked a map in two different times: the first time we got it, the second one we didn't. How is it possible? They said the maps were out of stock. Are you joking? Breakfast was average, jam and bread or English breakfast, not even possible to mix or having the sweet and sour as the continental breakfasts are in proper hotels. I wouldn't recommend to anyone. In other areas of the city, you have a better service for the half of the price.

title: What a shocker!!!
text: Paid £260 for a 2 night stay, arrived all looked ok & was told our room was no 5 on lower ground floor which rang alarm bells but we are always willing to give things a try. The hotel's name is Bloomsbury palace which is appropriate as all palaces have a dungeon & our room was it! Damp everywhere even directly above my pillow, dark as a coal mine, only a peg on the wall to hang our cloths on, a secondary door lock which didn't work (but the staff said that was ok because nobody was going to break in!) & a safe not even bolted down (see picture) but that was ok because it didn't work anyway. After a short discussion with the receptionist who said there were no other rooms we had to agree to stay there that night but we would be moved in the morning. The bed was the smallest double I have seen & hard as a board but no choice. Breakfast we were told by receptionist was up to 09.30 so we came down at 09.10 to be told by the waitress that yes breakfast was until 09.30 orders had to be placed by 09.00 so we could not have cooked food, the discussion which ensued lasted even less time than the one about the room, needless to say we got our breakfast but you should not have to fight for these things. True to her word we were moved next day & the room was ok, by chance our new room was directly over our old room, when you looked down out of the window it became clear why our previous room was so damp & dark as most of it was actually under the garden (see picture) hence the damp. NEVER AGAIN!!!! P.s no aircon or internet in dungeon.

title: Brilliant Hotel
text: We stayed here after a bad experience at another hotel and we loved it here. The room was spacious and comfy. Staff were so helpful and polite, there was a lovely woman working in the kitchen didn't say much but laughed a lot. They even allowed us to leave our bags after our stay for safe keeping and gave us space to get changed later when we collected our bags. The breakfast was also delicious we were very happy with our stay.

title: Surprisingly satisfying!
text: After reading some of the reviews on here I was a little apprehensive I have to say, but our stay here turned out to be very pleasant. We arrived a couple of hours before the check in time thanks to our early train. I expected to have to leave our bags in the reception area but the receptionist confirmed our room was ready early and we were welcome to use it. We were very thankful to be able to freshen up. We had a triple room as we were travelling with our young daughter and there was plenty of space. When I think back to some of the small hotel rooms we've stayed in when in London over the years this was a pleasant surprise. Bathroom was clean and shower nice and hot. Beds were also very clean and comfortable. Sleep was only disturbed by the return of some fellow guests talking loudly en route to their own room on the Saturday night. Breakfast was delicious with prompt service and the location was very handy for the west end, with some smaller restaurants nearby too. All in all, a great break away in London. I'd only avoid if you don't handle stairs well due to mobility as there's no lift in the hotel.

title: This is not 4*
text: You buy two old houses and you get 4 star hotel with small rooms, really steep stairs and breakfast room far too small for all guests. What you will get for breakfast you can smell long before you will get to breakfast room since kitchen was never meant to be here. On arrival our room was dirty (sticky floor in the bathroom, long black hair on the bed) and even after our complaint it was not much better. Double bed is very narrow and not big enough for 2 people. Wi Fi in the room is not working properly. We got a room in lower ground floor which meant we slept in basement. After I made complaint about that I was promise to get another room next day, but receptionist acted like he never see me before next day. In total real disaster!!!

title: Location and Value
text: Like many others great location, value for money and breakfast is included when we arrived check was quick and we were told we had been given a better room? That being the case not sure what the other room would have been like, it was clean really small bed and room but the bed was very uncomfortable and badly in need of decoration. Breakfast was ok and plentiful full english etc. If it is the location and value you are looking for then you’ll love it however, my wife and I would not stay here again and I could not recommend this hotel to a friend.

title: Disappointing
text: Quite an expensive hotel so very disappointed by the cramped little room (tv broken, blind broken, dusty). The breakfast was a long wait and they had run out of most items and had no clean glasses, bowls etc so had a mug with my fruit in. Appalling! Not satisfied with the response when we complained either.

title: good location, tiny room
text: tiny room, no lift, small reception/lounge. the single room (nr 304) had no table, no chair, no place to put the suitcase but the floor nice location, near regent's park. quite poor breakfast, awful coffee. i've been in better places, but the price was just OK for what I got

title: Clean and comfortable but very small
text: We stayed here after spending an evening at the theatre. The room was very small, imagine a small hallway with a double bed crammed in and you get the picture. Once you get over that, we had a good nights sleep, in the morning the breakfast was very nice but again the breakfast room is very small with not enough tables.. Tip.. Don't go down 15 minutes before finishing, everyone else had the same idea and a queue of disgruntled guests soon appears. I would stay here again but avoid room G5!

title: Great value for money
text: I stayed here two nights, paid £50 each per night with a friend! Pleasantly surprised by the modern rooms and they were so clean!! The hotel had an excellent location right next to googe street station and only 15 minutes walk from Oxford street! Hotel staff polite and very helpful, let us leave our suitcases in reception all day after checking out! Definitely recommend this small but pleasant hotel! Breakfast was delicious with a choice of full English, toast, cereal, fruit, coffee and juices!

title: Good Value for What it is.
text: Stayed at this hotel on 7th September following a late booking on late rooms, room rate including breakfast was £65.00 for a single. I have read the reviews prior to my visit but given that I was visiting for a meeting the following day, for this rate I thought would give it a try. Given that the location of this hotel is right in the heart of London, I found this hotel excellent value. The rooms are very small but ample room for a business traveller. The bed was comfortable, the bathroom whilst small was well equipped and modern and very good shower. The breakfast at the hotel was good choice, again compact but good value for money. Overall the hotel is average, but with extremely good value for Money and reasonable facilities. This is a fair and simple hotel, £65 for clean, good bed and breakfast for me hits the spot.

title: Great hotel,good value, amazing location
text: 5/10 min walk from Euston station, 4/5 mins from Goodge Street underground station! Amazing! Close by co op and pub too! Rooms comfortable, great shower and TV, good tea an coffee facilities with short bread biscuits! Breakfast was fine, good quality sausage in comparison with other central hotels at this price, reception helpful. Great for a touristy visit with room just used as a base, bed was comfy too, not luxurious but excellent for the price and bigger than other rooms in a similar area that I have stayed in!

title: Loved the place
text: Arrived on Saturday evening of 28th May .. Room was lovely and clean.. Ensuite was new and two types of shower.. 1 low 1 high .. The wife loved this as she doesn't like to get her hair wet once done.. Bed was superb.... Breakfast was filling and fine.. Coffee was lovely and always topped up.. Staff were friendly .. Room was 303. And tho it was top level I was not bothered bout the climb.. Price was brilliant for a bank holiday weekend .. So what if the windows and the skirting were not gleaming white painted.. It's London .. Added to character.. Free wifi and room was cleaned and bed made when asked ... Perfect for London walking and sights .. Will book again for sure .. James

title: Overrated on Booking.com
text: I booked this hotel for a family theatre outing as the location was pretty good - near Oxford street and Theatre land, on a bus route and it had a triple room. Booking.com rated it as a 4 and a half star. That is too high, I would say. We found it a reasonable place to stay - more like a 3 star. We arrived early and our room was ready was we checked in straight away. The room was fine and everything was clean and everything worked. The temperature was controllable and we got a good nights sleep. We had no traffic noise as we had a room on the lower ground floor. The breakfast room is obviously not big enough on a busy weekend as guests had to wait to get a table and there was not a great deal of room as tables were tight together. However the cooked breakfast was lovely and it was served up quickly despite being busy. The scrambled eggs I had were freshly cooked and delicious. The people waiting on us in the breakfast area worked hard and responded quickly to any requests. The reception staff were fine as far as we could see (unlike another reviewer) - one guy was very helpful in terms of directions in the area, and also getting us extra milk and sugar for the coffee maker. We were also allowed to leave our luggage there after checking out on the Sunday. All in all it was much better than expected after reading some of the awful recent reviews.

title: Great location
text: The hotel is super central in Soho district. Walking distance from Oxford street. The room was on the basement. The breakfast room is so small that you have to wait. It is clean and suggested only if you want to use it just for a sleep.

title: City break
text: Hotel is central and the cleanness is above average. Be careful that hotel has rooms on basement and does not offer intercontinental breakfast buffet. Only the typical English breakfast and the breakfast room is always full as it is small.

title: Don't listen to other reviews!
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel last weekend (9th and 10th August) we were bought a weekend in London as wedding present. After reading reviews on Trip Advisor, I was expecting an absolute shambles. But, we were pleasantly surprised with the hotel and it was much better than we were expecting, based on the reviews we'd read. We arrived at around 8pm on Friday, the gentleman on reception was very helpful and gave us information on breakfast times, wi-Fi codes etc (free wi-Fi is great, especially if you don't know where you're going in London!) The room was a strange shape, but perfectly big enough for what we needed. We had a quick shower and got changed (shower was hot and powerful - better than mine at home!) and shampoo, conditioner and shower gel, as well as towels were provided. We asked if there were any nice restaurants close by, the receptionist gave us clear directions to Covent Garden and was happy to help with any questions we had. Covent Garden is a 10 minute walk. Our room was on a main road so we had some noise from the traffic which can't be helped. But there was a fan supplied which was great as it allowed us to keep the window closed overnight, whilst keeping cool. Breakfast was ok, a selection of cereals and fruit, with an English breakfast choice too. 1 sausage, 1 bacon, beans, mushrooms, tomato and a choice of scrambled or fried eggs. Tea, coffee and fruit juices too. The breakfast staff were rushed off their feet, always busy and doing something so on one occasion, we gave her a hand by helping to clear our table. She was working really hard. Best thing about this hotel is the location, 10 mins from Covent garden, 5 mins from British museum, 10 mins from Tottenham Court Road. Perfect location for Central London. Would definitely use this hotel again!

title: Hostel not Hotel
text: If it is location, location, location you are looking for and not bothered by space, warmth, cleanliness and value for money then this is the hotel for you. I had a one night stay booked in a single room. Needed a place to stay overnight with no frills. I do expect at £65 to have a bed I can fit in with a level of warmth in the room. Considering the room was a box room (previously a store room in its original house stage) it can't be that hard to heat? Can it? Room was not clean and on the small shelves you could see the dust build up in the corners where a cuter had been waved over. Bed was firm and ok but I had trouble to sleep due to constant noise from the stairwell added in with the freshness of the air. The door did not dead lock from the inside which left me a little uneasy, I don't think security is on the priority list at this hotel. Front door open and 24/7 reception is great but they need to be attentive. I have not got a problem being challenged by staff at 1am on my reason for being in the hotel if I am the guest. The en suite was ok, however

title: Better read tripadvisor before booking
text: I went to London for a business trip and booked a couple of days at the Bloomsbury Palace Hotel. I don't know how they do it, but at booking.com they had a good rating when i booked a couple of months ago. However the single rooms are very, very small. Actually they are too small. I payed up front and that's the only reason why I stayed at the Hotel. Ok the WIFI is there and the location is good, but there a hundreds of similar Hotels around. London is just an expensive city and if you want to have the same standard than in other good Hotels, you'll have to pay the price.

title: Hotel room sizes
text: The hotel website features a blank page, headed 'Room Sizes'. I will provide you with the sizes for one room - 195 x 194 cms (6'5" x 5'1"). The bed is 172 x 80 cms (5'8" x 2'7"). The head of the bed (no headboard) is set against an outside glazed door, and the length of the room features a cold solid stone wall topped by full width window. It is a disgrace. Even knowing the room would be 'small', how small was a surprise, and how cold and uncomfortable the draft. The receptionist was clearly embarrassed but could do no more than offer a room heater and extra bed covers. Let's see if I am moved tomorrow night. I will update this review.

title: London weekend
text: Room 302 very small, bathroom tiny, the blind would not pull up the room needs a face-lift, bed uncomfortable and seems to droop to the left. Also on top floor so if you have difficulty with stairs don't have this room.The only good thing about the hotel was the breakfast but the breakfast room was too small.

title: Worst Nights Sleep Ever
text: Stayed here for one night on a visit to London for the cup final, booked a single room, it was very small and dusty, the window wouldn’t close and the blind was held in place with velcro so if you touch/moved or tried to do anything to it, it fell down, I asked reception twice for someone to sort out/close the window or move me to another room, no one was able to fix the window and no other rooms were available therefore I didn’t sleep a bit as the main road outside the hotel was busy with traffic all night. I asked to see the manager –and was told he was not available until the morning, I asked again in the morning and was told he was not in the hotel, I have given the hotel 2 stars as the location is good and the breakfast was good, But I would not stay here again or recommend if you want to sleep

title: bargain hotel in central London
text: I paid £65 for a room and breakfast - did n't eat breakfast - date elsewhere but the room was perfect. o.k! it was small but perfectly appointed, yep with the window open there was a bit of traffic noise - hey this is central London! Yes I walked up stairs to get to the room - this is what legs are for!

title: Surprisingly perfect
text: I often need an inexpensive hotel in Central London for one night between business meetings, and have had disappointing experiences. I tried the Bloomsbury Palace with scepticism but was rewarded with joy. Highlights were (1) really welcoming reception staff, (2) a tiny but beautifully appointed and comfortable room, (3) personal service for delicious breakfast (accommodating my vegetarian needs). Plus convenient location. Happy to recommend, and I hope to stay again.

title: Expensive but convenient
text: Stayed one night whilst on a business trip. Simple rooms but very clean. Breakfast was adequate and the staff took notice of my food allergies. Very small bathroom. Bed was very firm. Did feel more like a £60 room rather than the £80 I paid but I guess the extra charge is for location. Hotel would benefit from a refurbishment ..... Maybe include a bar and a lift!

title: Great Location
text: In general the place was lovely just a few things that can easily be changed would just make it so much better. Firstly every member of staff I came into contact with were lovely, very helpful and polite. breakfast was nice it just was very slow to get served and glasses etc to a while to get topped up to help yourself to juice. However staff again lovely and accommodating. Net curtains in our bedroom were black at the bottom, it just let it down a bit that a quick wash of the nets and it would leave a better over all opinion of the place instead of you feeling the place was dirty. Generally the place just needs a bit of TLC (remove the tape from the stairs etc) and it would be perfect. Location is excellent and they let us lave our bags as we checked out for a day of sightseeing

title: Disgrace
text: Booked a single room it was the same size as a dog kennel complained at reception to a chap called Abdl he didn't want to know I would never stay in this hotel again an absolute shocking hotel also breakfast and service was awful would never recommend this disgrace of a hotel

title: Great location for central London
text: Was a little worried having read some of the reviews, but we were not at all disappointed with our stay at the Bloomsbury Palace. Having shopped around I could not find anything close to the price I paid that offered such a good location, en suite and with breakfast. The hotel is a 2minute walk from Goodge Street tube station. From there you are 5 minutes from Leicester Square. This is a great hotel if you are visiting London for shows. The service was fine, breakfast was served promptly and set you up for the day. The room was tidy and cleaned during our 2 night stay. We were on the 3rd at the back of the hotel. We found the room quiet and being a triple with only the two of us, we had plenty of space. No lifts is a bit of a pain with cases but for the price I paid and the location I was willing to put up with climbing a few stairs.

title: A Friendly, Cheap, Clean Experience
text: Gosh, what a bargain! 1 Cracking location. 2 Very friendly staff 3 Clean room 4 Comfortable bed 5 Excellent breakfast - cooked to order 6 Very low price The only reason that 5 stars was not given was because the bedroom was unhelpfully small.

title: NO HOT WATER, ROOMS SMELL LIKE BACON
text: Well, what can I say about this Hotel,, The rooms are very small, no hot water in the shower, and when I complain about it they say that to many have taken a shower that morning. and that was that. the check in is first at 14:00 with was bad in our trip because we landed at 07:00, the checkout is 10:30 with is also bad because our flight out was 19:00. and they have no place to keep your luggage for you. The room smell like bacon from the kitchen, and the staff smokes outside our window. about breakfast the breakfast room is so small you have to wait in line each morning. The breakfast itself was very good, apart from the coffee. The location is good, the staff was friendly obviously not their fault that the facilities are very very bad. I do travel much and I do have standards when it comes to hotels, but not extreme ,, this hotel sucks,, sorry to say

title: Pleasantly surprised.
text: After reading the reviews I was a little apprehensive. I thought I have booked free cancellation but when I went to cancel I found I had not. I phoned the hotel to discussed my concerns as I was staying for my daughter's 21st birthday and the man I spoke to put my mind at rest. Yes the hotel is a little basic , the staff are mostly English as a second language but were all courteous and polite. I had sent banners ahead and also asked for a cake and bottle of prossecco if it was possible and all were in our room on check in at no charge to myself!. The room was clean to a passable standard, the bathroom was very small but modern and functionalable. The only negatives in the room were the mattresses were very hard and the room very hot but there was air con but we chose not to use it as the continuous fan keeps us awake. Breakfast was substantial and yes, the breakfast room is basic and small but the food , fresh coffee and juice was plentiful. I think the people posting negative reviews on this hotel need a reality check on what you get for £130 in the absolute West End of London. This hotel is a 5 minutes walk from a tube station, 10 minutes from Leicester Square and of a decent enough standard for one night. Come on people. You get what you pay for. Well done Bloomsbury Palace. You don't pretend to be anything other that what you are and you went over and above to make mine and my daughter's stay special .

title: Very clean, lovely polite, helpful staff
text: Was worried about all negative comments but lovely hotel, we had a room on 2nd floor, although it was warm we had air con and a fan. Had a safe in room. Stayed for 4 nights, towels changed everyday and tea/coffee/toiletries replenished. Hotel was full and had to wait about 10 mins to be seated (not a problem). I will definitely stay here again, very close to stTion and tubes. Staff very helpful and polite. Only downside was I informed them before I arrived that my daughter was a vegetarian but there was no veggie option for cooked breakfast - otherwise lovely, very quiet hotel.

title: Dirty room and unfriendly staff
text: Stayed here as close to the theatre that we were going to and central for shops but the hotel is dirty, the net curtains in the room were in need of a wash, the toilet seat was loose, the taps on the washbasin were loose and moved around. The staff just smiled at you when you tried get tell them anything. Breakfast, what can I say, not enough room. Cramped into a basement room, my wife has her foot in a pot and we stood in the doorway for 10 minutes with staff walking past us and they never made any effort to speak to or look at us. Worst hotel that I have ever stayed at. A lot of customer service training needed. Cleaners need to take a bit of time to get into the nooks and corners to at least made an effort. Overall a terrible hotel.

title: Good find for central London
text: A desire to see the Pompeii exhibition prompted a spontaneous trip to London over the Easter weekend with my wife. At very short notice we found the Bloomsbury Palace conveniently situated for the British Museum at under £100 B&B which for central London is a bit of a result. I stay in central London hotels all the time on business and room size is often an issue - even in the big brands (when someone else is paying!). We stayed in a basement room (No 4) and it was fine - far more spacious than some of their near rivals, very clean with a great ensuite shower. The door to the bathroom could be a little more private (see through glass). The staff in the hotel were very helpful, bringing extra towels swiftly when asked. The hotel was nice and quiet on Gower Street, but only a short walk to Goodge Street tube where there is all the life in terms of restaurants etc you would want. Breakfast was cooked to order (always a good sign in London) and was tasty - good quality bacon and sausage. We left our luggage at the hotel during the next day - there didn't appear to be a secure luggage room there, as the bag was just left in the lobby. So don't leave anything valuable in them (we didn't have a problem). A great stay in a part of town where hotels can be decidedly grotty - well done to the Bloomsbury Palace.

title: Great location
text: With easy walking access to central London. This hotel was great for my wife and I to enjoy a kid free weekend. Only criticism would be the breakfast room was far too small for the amount of rooms the hotel have to offer. But get past that and location is a winner.

title: Good for the price
text: A clean and decent central London hotel in the summer for under £100 - yes, it can be found. OK, my room (like single rooms everywhere) was small, but well-fitted - rather like a cabin on a boat. For one or two nights it was fine - with a very smart bathroom, comfy bed, good TV and coffee and tea-making facilities - which didn't skimp on the supplies. And a safe, which I didn't find till morning! The breakfast room is small and I can imagine it could get very crowded - certainly it would help if breakfast times were extended to 9.30 - one hell of a rush at 8.55 I noticed. The two waitresses were a bit rushed off their feet serving and getting extra crockeryy,etc. It would also help if the chairs would fit under the tables, but the legs are just that bit too wide, so everyone sits well away from the table, making it awkward to move around. Food was OK - but then I'm not one for a cooked breakfast and my scrambled egg was fine. The servings were more than enough. Summer in the city is always hot and noisy, and although there was a welcome fan in my room I made the mistake of not fully closing the window. So not the best night's sleep, but then I'm used to living where the noisiest sound is the sheep bleating in the field next door. But on the upside it meant I could walk to the British Museum, theatres, restaurants, etc and walk back again at night-time with no hassle. For the price (£75 b&b for a single) it beats a lot of the chain hotels (where I've queued for breakfast) even if the rooms are small.

title: Good for a 1 night stay
text: Stayed here for 1 night on the 7th of July in a triple room and was pretty happy with the overall standard, but wouldn't want to stay for more than a couple of nights. Yes, there are bad points to the hotel, but let's start with the positive things: The beds and carpets were very clean and the tea and coffee making facilities were of a good standard. The double bed was soft but perfectly ok for 1 night. The breakfast was fine. A full English if required with a choice of either fried or scrambled egg to accompany bacon, sausage, beans, mushrooms, half a tomato and toast. Cereals were available and there was enough tea or coffee to have as much as you liked along with plenty of juices and fruit to give a good choice. The bad points: Hot, hot, hot...We had to keep the fan (supplied) on all night as it was very, very hot. The single bed (for the 3rd member of our party) was in a separate part next to the bathroom and was apparently very uncomfortable. The bathroom is small with a sink, toilet and shower. The sink and toilet had been cleaned to a high standard, but the shower warranted much further attention to detail, but was usable if you are not over 6 foot tall. All in all it is ok if you are looking for a b&b that is in walking distance of stations serving the North and you want an easy walk into Covent garden and Leicester Square.

title: Small & friendly BUT...
text: This hotel is located in a very central location which is great, the rooms are clean and perfectly formed, the hotel staff are friendly and accommodating. We paid £95 for a dbl room, very cheep however the stairs are very steep with no lift. The breakfast room in the basement was very small and offputting, with a very inadequate breakfast. For a little bit extra on cost you could get a lot nicer hotel if you look around. Ps the scrambled eggs were rubbery!

title: Good location, poor service and bad attitudes
text: We stayed in this hotel for my birthday weekend with friends. The location is good and the rooms were nice but the service could have been much better. The receptionist watched us struggle with our luggage instead of offering help. My friend went to check in and finally agreed to paying on departure like every other hotel. On check out, it turned out they charged my card without y authorization and following agreement to pay on departure which I found to be very sly and unprofessional. For that reason we won't be staying again. Note: they only have one twin room in the entire hotel.

title: Perfect for our needs
text: Very convenient if visitingTate Modern. Fairly quiet street. The staff are what makes this Premier special, so sweet, polite and helpful and their relaxed and friendly attitudes make it feel very welcoming.

title: Premier Inn Disabled access room
text: Very large room, excellent for myself and my wife who is disabled and uses a wheelchair. Bed was large and comfortable. Again the bathroom was large and easy to use for my wife. Room was quiet and we both got a fantastic nights sleep.

title: Will stay here again! Lovely staff.
text: Stayed here for one night and the location and the staff were excellent. We walked to Southwark station which took about 3 mins to get to anywhere we wanted to go! Breakfast excellent. Will stay here again when next in London!

title: Great location for Tate Modern
text: A standard Premier Inn, clean and predictable, with friendly staff and good service. Had a lie in, a good breakfast and still got to Tate Modern just after it opened at 10am, which was exactly what we wanted.

title: 5 Star staff!
text: This Premier Inn is only 2 years old so everything is fresh and clean. Bathrooms sparkle. The Thyme Restaurant serves a really good breakfast and evening meal at value prices. The best thing about this Inn is the staff. They go out of their way to make sure you are cared for and deal with requests promptly. Jasmine on reception is a gem..she will go far!

title: Great location and excellent good value
text: The location for the hotel is excellent and you can access most of the main London attractions easily. It is outstanding value for money given the spot. You know what you are going to get with a Premier Inn, the rooms are clean, the staff are polite, the beds are comfortable, it's quiet at night and popular with British families. It isn't the Ritz and it doesn't pretend to be. If you want The Savoy go across the river and pay the money.

title: Spot on!
text: I've stayed in several Premier Inns so thought I knew what to expect but London Southwark really raised the bar. My little lad had been travel sick on the train from Manchester and so we were pretty stressed on arrival AND half an hour early so I was really pleasantly surprised when the receptionist double checked to see if a room was ready for us to check in early! It was a huge help, she made us feel very welcome and I have to say the staff were all lovely. The hotel was immaculate and our room was fantastic clean, warm and the best nights sleep in those dreamy beds!! We had breakfast which is great value if you're staying with kids I thoroughly recommend it. Yet again the staff were delightful, offering help, making sure we were all content, great with the kids. From start to finish it was an absolute pleasure, great location, great hotel but the staff were exceptional. Many thanks.

title: Great Stay!
text: Great location (Close to public transport and very close to the river, promoting pleasant walks). Impeccable service (Staff very available to help, extremely professional and fun). I would definitely recommend it!!

title: excellent
text: Very clean room and bathroom. Hotel was very well supervised ,staff friendly and most helpful. Decor was very good and above average for a budget hotel. Aircon worked well. A good location for travel around London.

title: Welcoming hotel in perfect location
text: Myself and my husband had a wonderful stay here for his 40th Birthday sightseeing weekend. Great location, lovely helpful, warm staff, comfortable rooms and delicious breakfast....what more could you want for a sightseeing stay! Opposite a sainsburys local and next door to a tesco express so perfect for forgotten items or drinks/snacks 5 mins walk from Southwark tube station.

title: london theatre break
text: the hotel is situated is really close to the south bank, with all of the attractions and restaurants you could ever wish for. one let down is that its not that easy to find and its not the greatest looking place from the outside. we were greeted by very friendly reception staff and our room was accessed really quickly. the room itself was really comfortable, couldn't open the windows and the view was shielded on the outside..... to stop you from looking into peoples apartments i guess! the hotel has an excellent restaurant on the ground floor and we had a great breakfast there even though we didn't have a reservation. a nice touch as some hotels aren't as accomodating. we thoroughly enjoyed our stay there and would definitely stay there again in the future. as far as London prices go, the price was very reasonable.

title: Good Hotel Good Location & Friendly Staff
text: Premier Inn is now my standard default for both business and leisure. Nice and comfortable big bed. Full English breakfast was very good and sets you up for the day. This Hotel was clean and bright, Staff were very friendly, helpful and efficient. Had a problem with noise during the night but didn't want to make too much fuss about it. Briefly mentioned about it during checkout and received a full refund for the night ! Already booked another stay.

title: Location, location, location
text: A good location from which to explore the south bank, and with the opportunity to walk over to St. Paul's into the city. It is within five minutes walk of Tate Modern and an easy walk to the Globe and the National Theatre for an evening performance, which is especially useful for visitors from elsewhere in the UK coming for one night

title: Comfortable central London hotel
text: Comfortable hotel well placed for Central London. Good value for money Despite being in busy area, no noise from street. Recommended highly . Breakfast can get busy in Premier Inns , good value for money breakfast but the buffet style service can be annoying when some of the trays empty and don't get refilled.

title: Excellent Stay
text: A fabulous stay at this Premier Inn. The rooms were immaculate and the staff were nothing less than amazing. So helpful, polite & friendly. A delicious breakfast was served with plenty of options to choose from. I cannot fault my stay and would visit again.

title: No Fresh Air Allowed!
text: dont stay in this new Premier Inn if you have any issues with claustrophobia because the Premier Inn Big Nanny has ruled that no windows are to be opened. Not only just the regulation 3 inches so you dont sully the nearby pavement by jumping out!! (why would you not go to the nearest car park and take a final leap there!) So you are incarcerated in your room with the deadly air conditioning for the whole duration of your stay - utterly ridiculous! if this rule is to stop idiots smoking out of the windows, such folks should be fined, not make me feel trapped I will make sure I telephone to ask about this rule for any Premier Inn booking spoilt my stay for the weekend the staff were lovely, very helpful, shame about the mad rules

title: Surprised how good....
text: Wow how good were the staff? Fantastic nothing was too much trouble so attentive what else can I say except give these people a pay raise. Room was spotless everything worked and so quite no noise inside hotel or from outside. I can recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Simple but effective
text: Hotel was very efficient, cheap and clean. I have a great stay. The checkin was quick and efficient. The location is prime close to the Tate Museum and very centrally located, I highly recommend it. Best deal in London.

title: Nice hotel
text: Conveniently located near Tate Modern, the Globe, St. Paul and the City. Affordable and quiet. Rooms are simple but clean. Breakfast was not included in the price but good value. This hotel is 5 minutes walk from Southward underground station. Nice restaurants nearby.

title: Not as good as the last time.
text: We stayed here in September for two nights during the Thames Festival and as we had enjoyed it so much we decided to spend three nights here over the period between Christmas and New Year. This time however we were not quite as impressed. The staff were just as pleasant as they had been previously, and the bed was just as comfortable as before, but we felt really let down by the restaurant experience. On the first morning we came down for breakfast between 9:45 and 10:00 and had to stand in a line for over half an hour before we were seated at a table. I realise that they have their busy periods but 35 minutes seemed excessive to us, and to other guests, some of whom had small children. The fault appeared to be too few staff to cope with the demand as tables were waiting up to 15 minutes after guests had left before being cleared. When we finally got seated there was another disappointment as the bacon and other breakfast items were cold. The following morning we went for breakfast at a similar time. There was no queue, but the bacon was still cold! The third morning we ate elsewhere. On the Friday evening one of us had the gammon. There should have been egg or pineapple with it - we got neither. Not a big deal really, but it just added to the disappointment. This hotel has so many good things going for it, but this time, at £90 a night we left feeling that our expectations had not been met this time.

title: Great
text: We had 2 rooms - 7 people . The rooms were comfortable with individual air con control - yay- something we'd missed everywhere else! Nice bathroom enough room, ample Buffett breakfast, great dinners, matre d was very helpful ( Morgan) arranged cabs for us @ gave us directions. Very happy. The Southwark stn was a few min walk away & there was an excellent fy pub around the corner!

title: Good hotel, great location, lovely staff
text: We spent 2 nights here - 2 adults and 2 kids. Its a comfortable, quiet hotel, with proper beds for the kids, good breakfast and located in a really nice area. Very close to the riverbank and all the action there. It's a 5 - 7 min walk from Blackfriars train & underground station with direct trains from there to Gatwick. Overall, a very good spot

title: Great night sleep
text: Good check in......Easy. lovely comfortable room with, although basic facilities, more than sufficient for our requirements. We had a room on the second floor and apart from the noise of doors closing in the early hours did not hear a sound. will stay here again if the opportunity presents itself.

title: Quiet and convenient
text: Stayed here to go to Old Vic theatre which was about ten minutes walk away. We were on 8th floor and found it very quiet. Breakfast was good

title: Perfect! Location, Staff, Resturant, Room etc
text: This review may seem quite long but I want others to know how good our experience was. Me and my sister have just got back from our first 'proper' stay in London! We last went when we were too little to remember it! So you can imagine how shocking it was to us when we arrived! However, this hotel is so easy to get to when you have no idea where you are and how to get around, It's a perfect location! The tube station is so close by and as our main reason for our trip was to see Robbie Williams at the o2! The Jubilee line got us straight there and back with no confusion or fuss! I would say that Southwark station is very central when it comes to tubes! Easy to access Madame Tussauds etc. As for the staff - you can't fault their welcoming, friendly and genuine attitude towards everyone! We were so impressed, they were always happy to help and seemed pleased to be working there. Resturant was very cosy! Very well priced and the food quality was brill! Seriously, we actually miss it! We booked a 'meal deal' with our stay for only £22.50 ish for a 3 course meal each! We were sceptical about the quality & choices in the meal deal before we got there, but we had nothing to worry about! Honestly, I have to say it's the best food I have had for a long time! And we aren't strangers to food/resturants! Room was perfect - very clean and had everything you'd want for a great nights sleep! We only spent 1 night but felt like we had stayed a week because we enjoyed it so much. So - basically, we had a lovely trip which at the heart of it was this premier inn! We were so impressed with the service and the food that we went back for dinner the 2nd night before we travelled home. The only thing we have to be disapointed in was the high price! We hadn't booked too far in advance so it was our fault. For the price we paid, to have the experience we had, I guess it was worth it, especially with the 2 meal deals included. We would definitely recommend it - please don't hestiate booking here if you're planning a similar trip etc. At the end of a very long day, we knew we had a comfy bed/room to get back to and a breakfast that finished at 11.30am! Bonus! I hope any future travellers share the same experience as us! :)

title: Perfect weekend
text: Enjoyed our stay immensely ,location not perfect but managed to travel around without difficulty. Especially liked the closeness to the Thames and Borough Market. Southwark underground only a couple of minutes away and plenty of eating places nearby.

title: Extremely happy with hotel
text: We are a family of 3 that stayed 4 nights in this hotel in August. We picked it over PI County Hall only for air conditioning. Originally, I thought that staying near London Eye was a preferred location, but I was more content in Southwark, away from the crowds. On a quite street with easy access to train and busses. Walking distance to Borough Market. Everything we wanted to see within 2 miles: Tower of London, Westminster Abbey, London Bridge, Picadilly Circus, Covent Garden, Trafalgar, Square, I think you get the picture. For those that have never stayed at PI, it is a very basic hotel. Although it has no frills, the customer service is exceptional, the food is good, and the rooms are very comfortable. If you like big pretty rooms, you won't get it here or at any PI (although the new one in Edinburgh on York Pl. is very modern). Although the air con is said by most to be unnecessary, I would say it depends on what you are used to. For me, turning it on after walking around the city for 8 miles on a warm and humid afternoon is not just a luxury, it's a necessity if you are used to it. So ask yourself if you have ever stayed in a hotel room without air con during summer. If you have, then you should know your tolerance. If you haven't, then you are flipping a coin between comfort and misery. Your call Thank you PI for a memorable stay for our first time in London.

title: Very good place to stay
text: We spend three nights in this hotel and it was very enjoyable time. Comfortable room for a family, very clean. Modern hotel, English breakfast and continental one, all you can eat and good quality food. Location not so far from Southwark Underground stop. 20 minutes walking far from Tower bridge. I will come back another time in the future. Suggested.

title: Great stay
text: I stayed here with my mum for an overnight getaway. It was perfect, quiet, comfortable and right near the Tate Modern. The location was a plus and the Tesco convenience store next door was a bonus for little things we needed and to top up supplies.

title: London Long Weekender
text: Have had a great 4 days in London. This is a great base for family sightseeing. 10 minute walk to the Thames Southside area where there is the London Eye and many great restaurants. Even shorter walk to get on the route for the Open Top Buses. Hotel is nice and modern. Very clean and the restaurant is excellent.

title: Great value at a great location
text: A well located and very comfortable hotel close to Tate Modern, Borough Market, Tower Bridge and The Tower of London. Be sure to try the Greasy Spoon opposite the hotel for a fantastic English breakfast

title: thanks for a great stat
text: We enjoyed our stay in this hotel very much.The room was clean and large for London standards, with a spacious bathroom.The basic internet connection was good, no need for us to upgrade it. We did not have breakfast in the hotel, because it was more convenient for us to just grab a coffee and snack in the coffee shop right across the street. So, we can't say anything about the hotel breakfast. We would definitely recommend the hotel and stay there again on a future trip to London.

title: cosy
text: A chain, but like family run. Extremely well situated, close to Shakespeare, close to the Thames, underground station just round the corner, conveniently close to the city centre, supermarkets and ATM at the doorstep. One thing is particularly welcoming, - so smoking allowed in the place, "not even out of this woindow", -which can't be opend anyway

title: Perfect stay!
text: We are a family of 4 and enjoyed our staying to this hotel. Everything was far above average and the price was perfect for the service. Breakfast was full English, very good quality food. Beds were very comfortable. Room was not big but was ok for the 4 of us. Very silent during our sleep. Very close to a lot o London attractions.

title: Wonderful short stay
text: This is a fantastic premier inn where the staff are so helpful and friendly. The rooms are spotless and the food is fresh and a good choice to suit everyone. It is in a really good position to the SouthBank. Only a few minutes walk and you are walking along the Thames.

title: Perfect base for city touring
text: I personally don't think you can go wrong with Premier inns when you are going to a city to sight see. They are above basic and you know what you get. We walked from Waterloo train station to the hotel and it took about 20 minutes. We left our luggage as we arrived early. Later we had a family room for 3 of us, it was clean and we had tea and coffee making facilities. It was central there is a tube station just around the corner but we chose to walk everywhere. 20 minutes to the tower of London and 20 minutes to the strand. Staff were friendly and helpful. I always think breakfast in hotels is overpriced but we did go for the hotel breakfast and we were really pleased with the quality and variety. The only thing I would say is that you have to pay for the Wi fi which I think is just wrong in this day and age.

title: Good Location - New Hotel
text: Stayed for four nights with two children. Staff very friendly and welcoming. Room large but not enough storage for a longer stay, just one drawer and a small open hanging area. Beds quite hard which caused a problem after two nights but was quickly sorted out by housekeeping who put more padding on the mattress. Very close to underground station and just a few minutes to Tate Modern and river bank walks. Food very good standard but let down by speed in kitchen. Waited 25 mins for starters and 30 mins for desserts. Manager recognised there were issues and resolved to our satisfaction. Overall, a great location in a modern, bright hotel so we will be staying again.

title: A lovely 5 day stay
text: Stayed at the Premier Inn, Tate Modern for five days in September and could not fault this hotel. Very clean, with friendly and efficient staff. Bed extremely comfortable and breakfast relaxing and good quality. Surprisingly quiet, even directly opposite the lift. Very good location. Would be happy to return here.

title: Nice Stay
text: This was our London home for 5 days, and it was an excellent choice. The staff were wonderful, exceptionally friendly and helpful. The room was very comfortable and clean. The location was good, an easy walk from the South Bank. There is a Sainsbury's right across the street for snacks and such (gin & tonic in a can!) and several ATMs. Don't miss the full English breakfast at Pickles across the street. Like other Premier Inns, there is only 30 minutes a day of free Wifi, though it is inexpensive to get it for the full 24 hours. Though the location is really good, it is about a 5-6 block walk to the nearest Tube or bus stop.

title: Birthday weekend
text: Superbly situated at the back of the Tate Modern, convenient for all the attractions we were visiting. Room was excellent value and comfortable as always with Premier Inn. Food deal with breakfast and evening meal with wine great value for London.

title: Great budget hotel for families
text: Just returned from our first trip to London with small children and this hotel was just what we needed / expect from premier inn with the added bonus of super friendly and helpful staff that made the stay very enjoyable. Close enough to walk into London city and few minutes from the tube. Will use again for future visits.

title: Excellent
text: We recently stayed here for a couple of nights as a family of four. Our room was ready when we arrived even though we were a little early. Room was clean and spacious. Staff were friendly and helpful. We didn't use the restaurant on this occasion but have in the past and it has always been lovely, especially breakfast.

title: Excellent
text: A really excellent hotel in a quiet location 5 minutes walk from the tube. We had a large room at the front on the 7th floor with cleverly designed windows which gave us a direct view up the street towards the shard. The room was clean with a large walk-in shower and a very comfortable bed. All the staff were very friendly & helpful from start to finish and we were able to leave our bags safely before check-in and after check-out so we didn't have to drag them around sight-seeing. Our only criticism was the dining room was far to small, and consequently there was a long wait for breakfast, so we bailed and ended up walking to a nearby Pret. Such a pity as I had been really looking forward to the Premier Inn breakfast as the last one I had was delicious. We'll have to get up earlier next time we stay.

title: Excellent location
text: Had been concerned about getting a room in London the weekend before the start of the Olympics. We had stayed at the Premier Inn on Park Street several years ago and in other Premier Inns at other points on this trip. It was a very clean room in a great location for a reasonable price. Southwark underground station is quite close, and Tesco Express next door makes for easy purchase of snacks and/or breakfast.

title: GREAT PREMIER INN
text: this was a new premier inn to us as we have stayed in the kings cross one usually. once again we were not disappointed. same great standard as before and we found this one an even handier location. within very east walking distance from southwark tube station on the jubilee line. it was also walking distance from the thames, which in turn takes you to wherever you want to go. the staff were great throughout our stay. always friendly and welcoming with out being over the top. we especially liked Jamie on reception, he was lovely, really friendly and cheerful. the restaurant staff were lovely as well but so was everyone. have to say though, the breakfasts are one of the highlights for us. we love those all you can eat breakfasts!!!

title: Thank you
text: I checked in here at 1015 at night having checked out of a terrible hotel not far away. Welcomed warmly and checked in quickly. Soon in room and settled. Perfect in every way. Quiet, cool and relaxing. Staff friendly and helpful.

title: Comfortable stay at Premier Inn Southwark
text: This hotel is well located to 5 mins walking distance to Tube station. Other attractions are short distant through Tube. Hospatiality and reception- Warm, courteous and helpful with a smile. One of them was Sasi( not sure if miss spelt ). They also help you guidance in travel or cab booking. Cechk-in, check-out was smooth. Room- Cozy, comfortable bed and compact. Bathroom was nice clean and with bathtub. House keeping was done properly. TV - channels for kids should be there..I didn't find animation channel for my son. Food- Their in-house restaurant was good even have meal for Indian taste bud. Outside of hotel - It is not a shopping area but you will get few departmental stores apart from other necessary things. Lot of cafes outside hotel but comparatively less numbers of Restaurants there. Overall had a good family stay and would recommend surely.

title: Good Experience
text: Stayed for one night, very clean, location fantastic for Tate Modern and Globe Theatre. Hotel staff, were very polite and friendly..they portrayed a true passion for their jobs, and appeared very genuine...well done and thankyou. Will recommend this hotel, plus use it again. Beats many other hotels in the area.😊

title: Great location, clean and would definitely return
text: Perfect location, friendly staff, spot on for a family weekend away. Lots of restaurants on the South Bank just a short walk away and easy to access most tourist spots with the boat and tube nearby (that said we walked to most places). A very reasonably priced hotel with a good size room for London, spotlessly clean. Highly recommend and will definitely use this again whenever we travel to London.

title: Perfect base
text: I stayed here for two nights with my granddaughters. If you like walking, access to all the sights couldn't be bettered, both North and South of the river at the same time having a quiet place to sleep. Locally there are plenty of restaurants (from street food to Gordon Ramsey)as well as The South Bank, Borough Market, The Old Operating Theatre, Clink Prison, Globe Theatre, Tate Modern etc. etc. - I could go on. Depending on which bridge you choose to cross The Thames, St. Pauls, Museum of London, Trafalgar Square, Westminster and Houses of Parliament are all walkable with great links from there courtesy of TFL. Waterloo Station is 10 minutes away from where Kew Gardens can be enjoyed for an excellent day out from the city. The hotel is clean and comfortable with lovely friendly staff and the excellent breakfasts set you up for the day. WiFi is free but we couldn't get mobile phone reception without going out into the street where incidentally there is both Tesco and Sainsbury's should you need any supplies. I would use this hotel again.

title: Central location, quiet night's sleep
text: This hotel is in a good location for accessing the typical sights in London. Despite its proximity to the main sights it was very quiet in the hotel and we did not hear any noise from outside at night. There are a couple of mini-supermarkets right next door which was handy for snacks / drinks. Easy walking distance (15 mins) from London Eye area.

title: Good location
text: Better than anticipated. Good, safe location, quiet and restful. Stayed on Friday and Saturday to visit Tate Modern, Globe Theatre, Millennium Bridge and St Pauls. Supermarkets outside for supplies. Good breakfast. Only a few minutes' walk from tube station.

title: New years stay.
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here new years eve and it were amazing. From the moment we walked in, we felt incredibly welcome and at ease. The food there is almost as amazing as the staff. Will definitely stay again!

title: Great cheap hotel
text: A stones throw from all the top attractions in London and walking distance with bags from Southwark tube station.
