Right at the back of Tate museum and Millennium bridge and easy to get cabs in the area. Very typical Premier Inn, awesome staff and very quiet hotel perfect for families and holiday makers.

title: Nice Premiere Inn but experienced better
text: Stayed here on a Saturday night. Very conveniently located to South Bank and 15 mins walk to nearest tube. Staff were helpful from the start. However, decor a bit tired and flimsy. I got the overall impression that it wasn't particularly clean throughout the public spaces. We have stayed in another Premier Inn north of the river and it was much better. I wouldn't opt to stay here again.

title: Fantastic staff
text: Fantastic helpful friendly staff. The staff were so helpful with all services. All offers in the dining room they used to help you save money. They couldn't do enough for you. Very nice clean and good size family room.

title: My lovely stay
text: I really had an excellent,beautiful, awesome, peaceful and Comfy stay. The staff within the facility were too welcoming and willing to assist at any given moment. Not withstanding other minute issues, the place is worth the value for your money and strategically located within central London. Kudos!

title: Excellent service and understanding
text: We gave the Premier Inn Southwark Tate Modern a real headache when we double booked our recent stay, to attend a family wedding. On top of that, we had booked the wrong Premier Inn

title: Not up to usual Premier Inn standards
text: I frequently stay in premier inns in London and have always had a great experience but not sure what's going on here. I suspect they are short on staff maybe? Problems on checking in did not bode well when they couldn't find 1 of the 2 family rooms we had booked online - and then told us we had been upgraded from a triple to a family room - how odd as that was what we booked. Door keys didn't work on either room and after fixing with reception they stopped working again by the morning. Breakfast was very busy with a lot of mess about and broken coffee machine - again I suspect this maybe due to not enough staff as they all looked very busy and tried to be friendly despite having to deal with a number of bewildered guests. Reception staff remarkably friendly - as always the case with premier and my youngest took great joy in wining a prize for finding a magic key. Good nights sleep was had ... until 6.30 when a loud boiler / high pressure noise was coming from the room next door (105). Won't rush to return sorry, despite your handy location and friendly smiles.

title: Good clean rooms. Excellent service makes up for some minor setbacks
text: Looking for a decently priced hotel in a decent location I ran into the PremierInn chain, which I've never heard of before. This was based on reviews here and the seemingly overall uniformity in a chain of hotels which I am so missing in Europe when comparing to the Hampton Inns and HolidayInn Expresses of the world. No Alarm and No Surprises

title: First time, very impressed
text: Absolutely superb hotel and location for a stay in London, stayed for 2 nights in a well equipped family room (2 single and 1 double bed which is a bonus) Staff all very polite and breakfast very good, certainly better than some for expensive premium type hotels we have stayed in before. One member of staff (Natalie?) at breakfast deserves special mention for her friendliness and professional manner (look after these people they are rare!) Will defiantly stay again next time we’re in London Borough Market not far away well worth a visit

title: Amazing stay in a fab location
text: We stayed just one night but were welcomed by a huge smile from the member of staff on the check-in desk. Had a fantastic meal for dinner in the restaurant, slept like a log and enjoyed the traditional full english breakfast. Just 4 minutes walk from the South Bank. Staff were very professional and friendly, we left our luggage with them for the day and they booked us a taxi in the morning.

title: Good location and helpful staff
text: Just back from a 2-night break. Good location - close to Millennium Bridge and Tate Modern and short walk to the South Bank area. Staff very friendly and helpful. Rooms typical Premier Inn - clean and quiet. Evening meal was fine and it's above a Tesco Express or there's an M&S Food within 100 yards. Would definitely stay here again

title: Perfect for theatre breaks!
text: First time in a premier inn, and everything was lovely! Room was lovely and clean, shower was brilliant and the beds were amazingly comfortable. Staff were chatty and really friendly, and we had a fantastic breakfast in the morning (cooked+croissants+cereal) delish! Couldn't find a single fault really!

title: I may regret this
text: I may regret writing this review next time I attempt to book the Premier Inn Southwark and find that it's already full. But to give it less than full praise would be greatly unfair. To begin, the hotel is well situated for a lot of South Bank locations as well as many just across the river, they are all well within walking distance for the fit. For those who are not then a good bus service at the end of the road will get you to Waterloo or London Bridge stations/underground in minutes. The hotel itself is new so clean, warm, comfortable and pretty sound-proof. The rooms are of good standard for the cost and the dining room provides excellent value meals. Add to this the friendly and helpful staff and prices that reflect reality as far as us 'out of towners' are concerned it is easy to see why I would be wanting to book again on our next visit to London - so long as too many others don't read reviews like this! A particular bonus was the great local pub thirty yards up the street andTesco and Sainsbury convenience stores (with cash points) almost on the doorstep. There are also several acceptable restaurants within five minutes walk. Top marks to Premier Inn for providing reasonably priced accommodation in the centre of London.

title: Superb
text: Just spent the weekend at this hotel with our family it was my daughters 40th Birthday. The hotel, as most premier inns was very clean and comfortable, with spacious rooms. The staff were really good and attentive to all our needs. With three young children we were made most welcome. My daughter was given some lovely flowers, a gesture from the staff. Thank you all very much and we will certainly be back.

title: Good location, clean rooms, pleasant staff
text: It's not frilly, it's not historic, but it's clean, close to the Underground, on a bus route, close to the Thames, and in a great little revitalized area. There's a small grocery next door which came in handy for dinner one night. If you like the after-work-pub-scene, then there's lots of apparent choices in the evening. The staff was extremely pleasant and helpful. The only complaint was that our bathroom door wouldn't close. They came to look at it but never quite followed through on fixing it. The restaurant downstairs was tasty and reasonably priced. All and all, it was a nice place to call "home" for three nights. The beds were comfy but the extra cot (rollaway) was ... well... less so. I'd certainly stay there again.

title: Great hotel for a city trip
text: Stayed at this hotel in december of 2013. We stayed 2 nights and enjoyed it very much. Good, clean room. Had a good sleep due to the no noise policy. Great breakfast buffet and nice and helpfull staff. Near subway and London Eye. It was very easy to travel from the hotel to the city for Some shopping.

title: Excelent location for the price
text: Excelent location, close to tube station. Compared to other hotels, very reasonable rates. The staff was very helpful . The rooms were clean and quit. Nice breakfast, although a bit pricey. There is also a tesco store right next door

title: Well intentioned but frustrating
text: A friend and I are staying here after a business trip just to have a weekend in London. What we found so far: - the night guy is nice enough, but not much help. We arrived at midnight and asked where we could eat

title: As good as a very expensive hotel !
text: We stayed at this hotel because it was close to a wedding we were attending,from the minute we checked in we could not have been happier. Whatever we asked for be it ice, extra tea bags even an iron and board for my mother! Nothing was too much trouble. The room felt more like an upmarket hotel than a Premier Inn, everyone in our party was very happy. Walking distance to the Globe, Tate Modern, and Borough Market, what more could we want! Having a Tesco right next door is helpful aswell. Will definitely go back to this hotel again.

title: Great room
text: I stayed here for 2 nights. It was about a 7 minutes walk from Southwark station.The hotel room had a double and a sofa, a bathtub.The room was clean. The receptionist was kind and friendly. There were some supermarkets and coffee shops around the hotel. It was very convenient.I was satisfied with all.I'll visit this hotel next time.

title: Poor room
text: We stayed in room 714 which was small in size which is not what i was expecting from a premier inn. The room would have been ideal for a single bed . The air conditioner stopped working during our first night sleep which woke me because the lack of air and stuffiness of the room. The hotel its self was in a good location and the staff were friendly

title: Another good purple palace
text: This is a centrally situated hotel, with good local facilities. Clean, quiet and comfortable rooms. Easy automated check-in. Secure lift access. There were staff available to let us in for our return at 0300hrs.

title: Good value
text: A good example of Premier Inn getting it right. Great location close to the Southbank. Spacious family room, clean and quiet. Fuss free check in. Friendly staff. Standard breakfasts. Very good value, would stay here again

title: Fantastic hotel for the price
text: Second time we have stayed at this hotel (me, husband and two little girls), as its the right price, rooms are great for children as they both get a single bed, modern, clean and its in the part of London we want to be in in the evening. This time we were arriving on my daughters fourth birthday. I called ahead just to ask if they could put a couple of balloons in our room and they did SO much more. We had banners, balloons with '4 today' on, a huge badge and a card from the staff. Honestly some of the 5 star hotels I have stayed in couldn't have done any better - and they would have put it on the bill!! My daughter thought it was magic!!

title: friendly and clean
text: Great hotel. lovely location. Nice bars and restaurants nearby> Breakfast at hotel very good. Staff fantastic! Had problem with guest bed and staff were amazing> Got full refund in morning. Was seeing show in west end so walked and tubed. Definitely stay again

title: Weekend Away
text: Third time at this hotel in just over a year and once again good service smiling faces and happy to help Breakfast time is busy but they tell you this beforehand if you want a quiet hotel 200mtrs from the south bank of the Thames with 2 convenience stores within 20 meters this is a great place to stay

title: Small hotel great find
text: Had 2 nights with family in 2 rooms. Very happy with all aspects from the reception desk, the cleanliness of the place and the food, breakfast very wide choice something for everyone and dinner which was enjoyed by us all. Would certainly recommend this place.

title: Great stay
text: Excellent location and exactly what we wanted for our stay in London! Friendly staff, clean room, good value for money, and a great breakfast! Our only criticism was that the pull out bed for one of the children wasn't that comfortable.

title: Great place to stay in Southwark
text: Good location 10 minutes from Southwark Tube, very close to Tate Modern and the Southbank. Nice cafes nearby. Rooms are clean and comfortable. The staff were courteous and helpful. A bit over priced for business stay mid week compared to other brand hotels nearby.

title: Great hotel
text: Really enjoyed my stay only problem they never changed my sheets even after 5 days so it wasn't very refreshing but over all it's was very great value for money. Great staff , very central and most of all not that expensive

title: Ideal Location
text: The hotel is situated close enough to the city so that most attractions are within walking distance, but far enough away to get away from the hustle and bustle. It was great to be able to go and see a show in the evening and stroll back to the hotel. The hotel itself is very clean and the staff are very friendly.

title: Weekend trip with friends
text: Very good location on Bankside near to Tate Modern, London Eye,etc. Lots of places to eat and drink nearby and close to tube and buses so very easy to get around. Good comfortable, quiet room. Helpful staff. Lovely breakfast. Would stay here again.

title: Lovely staff
text: No complaints It was a really nice room with a comfy bed and choice of pillows The bathroom was very clean bathroom All the staff were friendly staff The food in the restaurant was good too Joshua in the restaurant was so helpful and so happy :) He stood out for me

title: Lovely stay
text: My wife and two young kids had a wonderful stay at the Tate Southwark Premier Inn. The staff were absolutely brilliant especially with our kids making them feel very special and the food was great - very tasty.

title: Short stay for work
text: As usual, Premier Inn very clean and comfortable. Always feel totally at ease being a lone female as all staff are so helpful and friendly and security good. I love consistency because I never worry what the hotel will be like if I've booked with Premier Inn.

title: Location not the best
text: Very helpful staff , good clean rooms .Walked far too much this weekend to get to where it happens , too faraway from the river but if you have the time and are fit enough then its fine . Breakfast can be v busy between 8-45 and 9-30 as dining area is quite small .

title: Great location and friendly, helpful staff
text: Stayed Friday evening - arrived late at 10.45pm and collected room key quickly and hassle free from an automated machine (staff were on hand and happy to help if needed). The room was spacious, clean and comfortable with hairdryer included. Staff were very friendly and helpful, particularly at breakfast which was very relaxed and a great start to the day. The hotel is well positioned to the lovely Southbank area of London and is close to a tube station. The hotel would have got an excellent rating had both lifts been working!! I would definitely recommend this hotel and look forward to staying there again.

title: Top location and great value for our 9 night stay in London
text: The Hotel: We found the staff to be friendly and patient, all our requests were handled promptly, the rooms are clean, modern and a decent size, beds really big and comfy. We were on the 7th floor and didn't hear any noise from the street and minimal noise from adjacent rooms. The only negatives were a lack of ventilation fan in the bathroom which made it a bit of a steam fest when showering, and the inability to open the room window. Oh, and one day I had a towel that was long overdue for the rag bin. Location, location, location: We'd previously stayed in a Westminster apartment but agreed this hotel is actually BETTER located because Southwark is a fabulous place to be for outdoor eating, art, walking alongside the river, and for day and night views of the historical icons clustered across the river. Southwark tube station is an easy 5 minute walk from this hotel while in the opposite direction the Tate Modern and the Thames is an easy 5 minute walk, and Shakespeare's Globe a 10 minute walk. Simple navigation, and it felt very safe, night and day. With a Tesco supermarket next door to the hotel and a choice of cafes surrounding it, although we started out with the breakfast deal we soon located better coffee and better value brekky options nearby. We hated the coffee 'vending machine' at the Premier Inn's breakfast. Tip#1: Short walk to the Borough Market on a Thursday, Friday or Saturday for some REALLY amazing food experiences. Confit duck roll and glass of prosecco - yum! Tip#2: Tate Modern offers late openings on Friday and Saturday evenings. Door to your hotel door, 5 minute walk tops.

title: very happy
text: iI had never stayed in a Premier Inn before but had stayed in other chains. This is the best budget hotel I have stayed in, from the security of the hotel to cleanliness and comfort of the rooms and beds I was very happy. Will definitely Sta at one of these hotels again.

title: Excellent.
text: Let's face it, we all know what we get with a premier inn, a decent room to pop down your head. What makes this 5 stars for me was first of all, the location. Five minutes from the Globe theatre where we spent the evening. The price, we got an absolutely great deal. Last but not least, the fantastic staff, our welcome was bright, cheerful and generally fantastic.

title: Fantastic staff
text: My family and I stayed here for 1 night (22nd dec) the staff at this hotel could not do enough for you !! Love it when it's like this makes it a enjoyable stay. ( we Had the meal deal which was good value for money).

title: Brilliant
text: This hotel was a lovely surprise. Staff could not have been more helpful & courteous, from a call made before the visit to our departure. All had a friendly smile & made you feel genuinely welcome. All facilities were excellent & clean. Breakfast great!!

title: Great location for Tate Modern and the Globe
text: We chose this hotel as we wanted to visit the nearby attractions (including the London Eye). In our experience, Premier Inn staff are friendly and polite - and these were no exception - very well trained. The room was clean and big enough, with a view of the Shard from a side window. Mattresses are a little firm for my taste, but not too bad. Breakfast is reasonably priced, and you can eat as much as you like. The coffee machine was a bit slow, so could lead to (short) queues at times. We could leave our cases in the hotel after checking out, which allowed us the time to visit the Globe theatre (we mainly went to vist the Tate). Premier Inns are a consistently well managed budget chain, and we use them when no independent hotels fit the bill.

title: Very disappointed
text: I often stay at this hotel, my company's head office is nearby, and previously I've had no cause to complain. It's typical Premier Inn, however this time I felt like I was putting the staff out whenever I asked for something. First off the wifi wasn't working (in all fairness restarting my phone sorted that out), but my room phone wasn't working and was actually smashed - I could see all the internal workings from the side of the phone (room 812). So I had to go down to reception to ask for an iron and ironing board but had to ask again a couple of hours later (by phoning the 0333 number from my mobile as I wasn't taking another hike). Then when I went down for dinner I was told that there was a problem in the kitchen and there would be a long wait for my food

title: Perfect value for a visit to London
text: This hotel is such a great value. The location is great (5 minute walk from Southwark tube station, 15-20 minute walk to many of London's most popular attractions), the hotel clean and seemingly new. The internet was consistent and fast, and the bed was comfortable. There is a Sainsbury's directly across the street that is really convenient for picking up a snack or bottle of water before you head out for the day. My only advice for travelers would be to bring your own shampoo and conditioner--the hotel provides a combination body/hair soap that works fine on the body but wasn't so great for the hair. But overall, this hotel is a great bargain, and I wouldn't hesitate to return! I should also note that this hotel is, without doubt, the quietest hotel that I've ever stayed at in London. I stayed four nights and never once was I woken up by noise from the street (ever present in London) or from other guests. They really mean it when they say that they invested in soundproofing when they built the hotel.

title: Perfectly located!
text: This is a great hotel for a few reasons: (1) amazing night sleep (though the walls and doors are thin and carry most conversation, the beds just make you feel weightless and allow you a great sleep), (2) the check in process is super easy and via kiosk, with attendants that are super friendly, (3) the price for what you get and (4) the location is PERFECT! Both a Tesco Express and a Sainsbury Local within feet of the front door. Seemed to be a lot of families with kids, so if that bothers you then don't stay here. I also liked that you need your card to access both the stairs and the elevator. The breakfast was also really good - great variety and delicious. Fantastic coffee machine made every drink (and used Costa beans). I will definitely stay here again if I'm back!!

title: Super Clean and Comfy - Great Location, Great Stay
text: Nice and close to the tube station and lovely part of London, convenient for The Tate, St Pauls and places from Waterloo to Tower Bridge as roughly midway betwix both. Staff were friendly and helpful, check in was painless (completed on line before arriving) room was good side (twin room) and spotless, bed was very comfy and fresh and nice. Crisp linen, nice pillows . I had read reports of the Hotel being in a noisey location, we had room 216 this was quiet (I live in the Countryside only owls and foxes making any noise near me) The sleeping in a twin is one sofa bed and 1 giant double bed, absolutely fine for myself and my daughter. The breakfast was very nice (I had the continental) spotless clean, cutlery and tables - polite friendly staff, very quiet and enjoyable, loved the Costa coffee only disappointing thing, leaving as I had only booked 1 night - wish I had booked another night, pull your socks up Hilton and Holiday Inn's - this gem of a Hotel beat you by far in my books. There was a Tesco Express next door and very useful we found as I had forgotten tooth brush and toothpaste.

title: Premier not just by name
text: We stayed the night in this Premier Inn on the 5 September, after a day at the Paralympics. To say we couldn't be happier is an understatement. Very modern, very clean and very helpful staff. We ordered breakfast for the following morning, which my partner and I both felt was very good value for money. We will not be looking for any other hotel on our next stay in London.

title: DESPICABLE - ABSOLUTELY HORRENDOUS!!!
text: Even though I would have loved to be able to say something nice about this place, nothing can prepare you for the unacceptable customer service or the despicable room conditions. We were expecting a clean bed and shower, certainly no luxuries, but this was the ABSOLUTE WORST experience at a hotel that we’ve ever had! Lower cost in London should not mean: horrible service with an attitude, no heat, unbearable foul smells from the bathroom, disgusting bed sheets, or… OK, let me start at the beginning. Firstly, the horrible conditions of the rooms, particularly those on floors 1 and 2, are simply Shocking. You can look at pictures and read reviews, but opening the door to the tiniest, filthiest room…. And then the tiniest bathroom with a foul sewage smell that simply became intolerable after an hour! The shower curtain was VERY MOLDY (and I mean grey). Considering the *incredibly* small space, this thing will be touching you all throughout the length of your shower - simply appalling and totally unacceptable. Our friends staying at another room encountered the same exact situation unfortunately. Even the towels were dirty and smelled badly. We asked to speak to the manager and were told she would be in the following morning, but it then became obvious that this was misinformation also, as she is usually not on location. We requested transfer to another room, but there was only one other room available and even though we wanted to check out, we decided to wait until the following morning, as it was late at night. The next morning all of us started looking for another hotel in a convenient location for our work and returned to confirm our cancellation. After spending another half an hour in the “lobby” writing an email to confirm our cancellation request, as per Easy Hotel’s regulations, we were FINALLY told that there were other rooms on floors 3 and 4, which had been recently renovated. After checking those out (they were cleaner and the bathrooms somewhat more tolerable, even though shower curtain was still moldy and the bed was far from great), we decided to stay, in order to avoid losing more time from work. Additionally, I emailed EasyHotel prior to our arrival and asked whether blow-dryers were provided. The response was that the specific location at Old Street did not provide them, only to stand in the lobby and watch the staff hand them out to people requesting them! Then the HEAT WAS NEVER ON - even though the website clearly states that the rooms are fully air-conditioned and with heat. Every time we asked for it to be turned on, the response was “in 30 minutes” and then again and again, until my husband of 10 years watched me lose my patience for the FIRST TIME and raise my tone of voice to the intolerably rude person at the reception. UNACCEPTABLE! Needless to say the first evening there was no heat in the rooms and we were given some excuse of how it would automatically be activated later on, which was never. We’ve stayed at far cheaper places, which were far roomier and totally pleasant! No need for going through this upsetting and uncomfortable experience. Most times that we were walking in and out of the building there were people arguing with the staff anyway, which was no surprise, but still this was of little consolation. The manager was never there, except for once, on our last day. There is not a single phone number anywhere, “everything is web-based” we were told, so be aware of not being able to contact anyone if you need assistance. Needless to say we will NOT BE RETURNING! Only courteous person in reception was Kenneth O., the one star fully goes to him!

title: Terrible value
text: Paid extra for a room with a Window, which ended up being frosted glass right onto a busy (and noisy) road. I understand the hotel is aimed at the basic market, but would have been good to have a desk or TV, it felt more like a prison cell than a hotel. In fact I think prison cells these days are better equipped than this.

title: Would rate this 0 stars if it was possible
text: Not even the low budget price can justify just how basic and poor this hotel was to stay in. Zero windows meant that myself and my girlfriend found ourselves having to leave our door open throughout the night which left us both at risk. We stayed here for her sisters birthday, and the hairdyer having to be used didn't help matters! Our key decided to keep cutting out and not letting us in our own room every single time we tried to get in. Not ideal when you come back from a nightclub at 2am in the morning and want to just crawl in to bed. One slight positive however was the staff and that they helped us resolve the key issue promptly. No problems with them, just the hotel itself. Definitely needs to be sorted, and won't consider staying here again

title: compact and bijou but cheap, clean, and cheerful
text: The rooms are very compact and bijou but was very clean. The staff are lovely and were more than willing to help. Suitable for a one or two night visit but personally would go other places for long duration trips. My only comment/advice is some rooms do not have a window(s).

title: Malaysia
text: It is my 2nd time visit to this hotel. Well, it is a nice location as it situated near the city center. The price of the hotel is also reasonable, and cheap. The rooms are tidy, clean and comfort. I would recommend this hotel to everyone. Not to forget it is also location wise. Walking distance to Underground and bus stations.

title: Where do i even begin?
text: So i stayed here the end of April, not knowing what to expect. It was the first stop on the most amazing trip i ever been on. Lets say, my week started with this hotel, and thankfully, i didn't let it ruin the rest of my holiday. We started by being greeted with not being able to check in until 3 (got there at 2.15), fair enough, but then a few minutes later being told we can check in as there is a room available. However, not being told that we will be charged for early check in. Maybe being given the option, rather than being charged an extra £10, would have been nice. We then proceeded with a refund, for the simple fact, that we were a little annoyed at not being asked. Then when asked for a receipt we were told we can only have the receipt when we check out. Surely, it takes seconds to click a button to press print. Moving on, we entered our room, and holy mackerel. Yes, i get we didn't pay for a 4 star hotel, but i expected so much more. The air con didn't seem to work correctly. I woke up in the middle of the night, having to sit in the bathroom with my hands under the cold running water, just to cool down, and having lost about 4 stone in sweat. How i managed to sleep at all i do not know. The bed would howl every time i moved slightly. The sheets were dirty, The pillow (if i can call it that) was useless and i found someones hair on the bed. The bin needs replacing! As to why this would be left in the room i do not know. So as you can understand, overall, this is THE WORSE HOTEL I HAVE EVER STAYED IN.

title: Never again!!!
text: If this place was really cheap I could get the point

title: Very nice hotel
text: its a very nice hotel. clean rooms. we were able to check in earlier than possible. very nice staff. the price is very affordable and good for what you get. especially for short trips a nice hotel that has everything you need. i would stay here again.

title: One of the worst hotel experiences ever!
text: One of the worst hotel experiences ever! So ok, I know we paid £30 to stay here in the middle of trendy shoreditch but I don't think that makes up for what happened to us. We stayed here on a Tuesday night. A friend was visiting me from up north just before Christmas and we fancied dinner and drinks in London and a taxi home was approx £60. We saw this hotel and thought wowzer a brand we know, although budget, excellent for one night right?! WRONG!!! So first we get there at about 10pm after dinner and are greeted by a very lovely receptionist, she chats with us whilst she fumbles around and announces that no one has prepared a room for us but that's ok she can sort that immediately. She taps away at her keyboard and gives us a key and tells us to enjoy our stay. We go up to the room, open the door and there is literally a man BUTT NAKED in his bed! He screams....we scream...he screamed some more! We apologised and hastily closed the door. We instantly went back down and explained the problem. She apologised and gives us another key so we go back up. Open the door and guess what?! Someone else's room again!!!! Whilst the occupants were not there the bed looked like it had been slept in and there were empty take away boxes on the floor. Down we go again. Third time she gets us a room she says is "definitely vacant!" You can imagine we lost all trust by now.... ....we go up and the room is clean. It's not occupied and it's fine. We returned from our drinks at 1am and I awake at about 5am because it feels like I am sleeping in an underground bunker! It's so hot in here (it feels like I am in the fires of hell!) there is no window in the room to open. I can also hear the gentleman next door snoring so loudly it's as if he is lying right next to me. I am also laying here wondering if someone else may accidentally be given our key and wander into our room. This easy hotel is well known to be used by people who have had one too many and can't drive home or need a place to sleep off the alcohol. Are we safe as two girls on our own?! Also there is no mobile phone reception at all in here which is what brings me to writing this lengthy review....I am laying in my sweat soaked sheets typing this up in notes at 5:28am waiting for it to be a good time to leave :( Don't stay here folks, unless you want a cheap Way to lose a TONNE of water weight!

title: It was horrible.
text: The room and bed was so small, the light couldn’t turn off at night, there were mold on the walls, the bed was wet, the room was so cold and you couldn’t control the air conditioning, the floor was bumpy.

title: As basic as it gets!
text: This is beyond basic, no wardrobe no beside table, no lamps, just a very squeaky bed , a coat hook on the wall and a wet room, although it was air conditioned! It was clean but sheet didn't stay on bed and every time you turned the bed squeaked so much you woke up! My daughter referred to it as returning to the prison cell!

title: Thin walls. Overpriced for noisy night.
text: Checked into room 1.11, incredibly small room but thats not the problem, the problem is that the walls seem incredibly paper thin. People were talking quietly in rooms on either side, outside in the corridor and I could hear their voices as if they were standing in the room. This hotel appears to be a former office block and completely unfit as a hotel. You can hear noise travelling within the walls all around as if the walls reverberate the noise. Its not just voices but luggage moving and rustling is amplified also. There were no parties or gatherings, this was just normal talking. I went to the front desk to ask if I could be moved, I felt it was unreasonable to ask my neighbours to stop talking because they were not shouting or being antisocial. The desk clerk was honest and agreed that it was a very noisy hotel, the walls are very thin and they do have alot of complaints. I appreciated his honesty but that doesnt help me after paying £70.95 for the night so it's hugely overpriced and poor value when you cant even sleep, which is the minimum requirement of a hotel. He moved me to a ground floor room at the end of the corridor so I didnt have noise from both sides. It was quieter but still noisy at times with people using doors and stairs, I could even hear a person turning over in bed as if they were on the other side of the room, that is not acceptable. By this time I only had less than an hour sleep. The franchise structure of the brand is not customer friendly and leaves a lot to be desired. Its online booking only so an account setup in the small print means you cant get a refund but you get an account credit, yes, to stay at another Easyhotel. They are uncontactable, the head office contact is ignored and you have to play detective to get ahold of someone senior and site trade descriptions. I got a weak response from a manager saying the rooms adhere to soundproofing regulations, clearly inadequate if thats even true which I doubt and smells of business blurb nonsense. The website states 'simple comfort, great value' with both statements clearly incorrect. This is a problem prior known and they are only getting away with it by offering credit to those that persevere. These rooms need to be no greater than £20 a night and even then you'd have to consider the noisyness of the rooms. This hotel and business model make it a huge rip off.

title: HORRIBLE NOT RECOMMENDED AT ALL
text: absolutely not recommended!!! Dirty tiny rooms. Horrible unfriendly staff, tried calling never picked up, paid for a breakfast and received a lunch box with cornflakes a small milk carton an orange juice and a muffin you think that is a breakfast? Dirty walls which I don’t even want to know what they had, stayed in a room for disabled people which had no window, no ventilation, no air con, noisy and the toilet had a “chair” which was dirty and old (pic attached) DOnt stay here don’t spend your money here I paid £100 for the night absolutely waste of money !!!

title: Prisoners are treated with more dignity
text: Sadly my friend had booked this hotel for the group without reviewing trip adviser first. I can only compare this hotel to a prison cell, or a submarine. But if this was a prison cell l the prisoners would be treated with more dignity! I was already aware that this room did not have a window, but this will completely thrown out your body clock had you will not have a clue what time of day it is, all you would do is keep waking up for at the time checking the time The hotel is a five minute walk from Old Street tube station, which is not the best train station if you're planning to visit the centre of London, you would need to change at bank station in most cases which make traveling times awkward and lengthy. Reception staff were okay, but the reception was tatty, and dirty! I already had a low expectation for this hotel based on same of the reviews already written but I was still shocked by the appalling room. Between the group we had two rooms. The rooms were slightly bigger than I was expecting, but all you get is two beds and that is it. The mattresses in both rooms were uncomfortable, it didn't even come with a fitted sheet. So the sheets for all the bed become loose throughout the night and we were laying directly on the mattress. The mattresses laying directly on top of wooden box not a bed, my friend cut his leg on one of the corners of the bed! You do not get any bedside table or anywhere to hang your clothes. You have to store everything on the floor. The air-conditioning in one of the rooms was very noisy but worked, and the other room simply did not have a conditioning, which made the room unbearably hot! The bathroom is a totally different story. I have taken a photo of the shower, and uploaded this to trip advisor! Shower is too small to be practical, when you're having a shower you get the filthy shower curtain wrapping itself around you. I do not want to even consider how many people this shower curtain has been wrapped around! You was unable to sit on the toilet, as it is too close to the wall, knowhere to place your left leg and you have to remove the toilet roll before you even sit down as there is not room. The room is designed simply designed for quick cleaning, and there has simply been no consideration at all for the customers needs. You do not even get a plastic cup to have a drink of water with! Disposable cup must cost two pence and this is an essential item It's hotel must be owned by EasyJet group, but the advantage of a budget airline, is that your only on the plane for an hour or two! There are cheaper and better hotels in this, and I would certainly advise you not staying here. I will definitely not be visiting again and I would definitely not be recommending this hotel to anyone.

title: Quite good for a short stay
text: If you need only a place to sleep, easyHotel is a good choice (cheap and with own - not shared - bathroom). Barbrican easyHotel is very well communicated, we had clean room and the service was kind. However our bed was sunken a little bit and we had problems with ventilation in the bathroom. During the first night there was also strange smell in the bathroom.

title: A good stay in London :)
text: Good location, nice place, friendly atmosphere- everything the hotel needs to provide you with a good stay for a weekend. I was given free wi-fi. It is close to underground station. All types of cuisine can be easily found nearby. A nice choice for an economical trip.

title: Terrible
text: Worst worst worst hotel experience ever. After having a horrible airbnb experience we decided to move to this hotel. After calling the reception to see if there still were rooms available we hurried to there to check in. This was already late in the evening. When we arrived there a guy called Hasheed who helped us to check in. I repeated twice that we wanted the room from wednesday untill saturday. Check out saturday. After he filled out all the necessary stuff he gave us the key and told us that checkout TOMORROW is 10 o'clock. I looked at him and said, you mean saturday? Then he looked confused and seemed not to understand what I actually was saying. Then I asked him I paid untill saturday right? His answer was not a straight up yes. We were so tired that we decided to leave it like that. Today we arrived at the hotel late in the evening again and wanted to get in our room but our key was once again not working. Upon going to the reception the guy behind it told us that we only booked untill today. Unfortunately we didn't get any proof of confirmation, only a receipt that we paid. I explained the whole story but there was no compassionate answer. He said that we still need to pay for one extra night. I get that it's an human error. But an error made by the employee and not by me. I don't feel that I have to pay for his mistakes. I am not after a free night but a compensation would be very welcoming. Their customer service is absolutely the worst. Nothing is EASY about this hotel. I won't recommend this hotel to anybody. Educate your staff! Give them a course in customer service. Because this was super dissapointing! I have worked at the frontdesk of a hotel myself and this was not how we treated our guests.

title: Dirty room, not enough towels, rude staff
text: Only one bath towel for two guests, I informed the staff and they said I could ask for another towel later, when I did the employee said it could only be done the next day, when the cleaning staff arrived. There was also a problem with our shower water temperature, again we had to wait for hours until cleaning staff arrived so that the issue was finally solved and we could take a shower. Staff was unhelpfull and rude. Although bed linen was clean, the room was very dirty, we were sneezing all night from the dust.We also had stayed in Easyhotel Brussels a few days before and it was very nice. There seems to be a problem with the Old Street London branch.

title: Just don't, honestly don't. ....
text: The room was just shy of £90...I wasn't expecting much....and got less.... It's rather like sleeping in a down market prison cell I would imagine. The room stank of a mixture of fresh paint and sewage....not a nice combination. ...the key card kept refusing entry to the room resulting in a well trodden path backwards and forwards to reception. There is no ventilation and no way of opening the meagre window. The bed was uncomfortable. There was only one towel for two people...another trip to reception.. Doors slamming all night....left early never to return. ... a better nights sleep to be had upright in an easy jet seat....or on a park bench. ...

title: Cheap but cheerful
text: These are budget rooms ideal for a night out or if you are working a couple of days in London. You have to reset expectation when your staying in London. The price varies but I have never paid more than £50 and have had a room for £30 in this budget hotel. This is an exceptional price when you take in account the location. 10 minute walk to St Paul's and close to Old Street Station. The rooms are very small but contain the essentials, a double bed, sink, shower and toilet as well as a key card lock for the door. I have found them clean with one exception and to be fair when I complained I was refunded the cost of the room. They are also in the process of refurbishment and while they are still simple they are a significant improvement with less orange! The décor is garish but this doesn't bother me and I actually find I sleep better in a room without a window although it is easy to oversleep as there is no light to wake you up. So in summary great for a night out but maybe on your wedding anniversary!

title: Worst 2 nights ever
text: Room tiny. Heat unbearable. Not always have hot water. No windows or fan in room. Bathroom wasnt cleaned properly, stagnant water retained in holder under shower drain.Staff on desk not attentive as were on their mobile phone. Will never stay here again.

title: Budget meets a new level of low
text: It's very hard not to feel very emotional and have preconceptions about this place. Here are some of the good things about it. Firstly amazing location, Shoreditch is a stone's throw away, the City of London is next door and Old Street station is close enough to get you anywhere in the city. Secondly, this is the cheapest hotel I have found in this perimeter, even the hostels aren't much cheaper. If you are on a tight budget, this is affordable and not in zone 4 beyond. I got upgraded from a room without a window to one with the worlds most narrow window for free. Some people may grumble but at least I had sunshine. Bad things... Don't expect any customer service. Cleanliness of the rooms are as bad as any student dorm. My room and my friends rooms had sticky vinyl floors (bring slippers) and the bathrooms didn't fair better. My mother woke up with a rash from the linen and a friend found what we think is a thick pubic hair on top of her made bed. For your own piece of mind, I wouldn't want to use their towels either. Walls are incredible thin and the bathroom is very tiny. The ventilation and air conditioner do work despite what other reviews say. If anything they work a bit too well and my room was freezing from the air conditioning. Cannot say anybody can get a good night sleep but if you are going to spend most of the night in a bar at Shoreditch and essentially need a place to "stay" as such, this could be an option for you. If you are everybody else who needs a good night sleep and a clean room, please look elsewhere further afield or spend a bit more.

title: Confused..
text: So we wasn't expecting much as it was the cheapest room available in London, I think, with the best location to centre. But what a strange little place, it is the worst room I have ever been in. Who designed these things it's like a pod, must of taken half an hour to build this room. U dont want to spend much time in it. The smell and heating stories are true. Heating pointless doesn't work not even a heating system anywhere. Toilet flushes like an aeroplane one. The door even looks like its from the cockpit. Clean room and bed. Strange plug socket under the ceiling ?

title: Dreadful Place I Thought I Was In Prison
text: For £70 a night I would expect more than a cell with paper thin walls. A bed and a toilet/shower cubicle is NOT a hotel room. No table no telly no storage save for one hanger. It was bleak more a punishment than a short break. I was expecting comparable quality to the Easyjet brand. It is sadly nowhere near that quality. Shockingly bad and a complete rip off. They actually list toilet roll as a feature. Easyhotels have no idea how to meet customer expectations.

title: An interesting experience, but won't return
text: I am typically very pro-Easy and fly with them a lot without any complaints. My husband and I are not very demanding as long as our hotel room is clean and the bed is comfortable. I do believe EasyHotels are booked when on budget and therefore our expectations were non existing (we booked a double room without window). The receptionist seemed uninterested at check-in. We used the lift and some of the buttons were missing, but one can manage without. When we entered the room, we had a little giggle. It is extermely small, we thought of it as an airplane cabin meets office cubicle. There was literally no space to store our belongings and clothing, although there was a niche to put a chair or shelve. We managed fine living out of our suitcase. There are no other extras at all, having said that, I would not expect extras at a budget hotel and was fine with us. The bathroom was small but fitted everything, although you have to accept that your feet are in the shower when sat on the toilet. In our particular room the bathroom smelled really damp after having a shower and it wasn't clean in its entirety (curtain and I believe it was soapy residue). The door had to be closed taking a shower as it would otherwise trigger the smoke detector. Closing the door makes the experience a bit claustrophobic. There is no room to step aside the shower to wait until the water reaches temperature. I am not a light sleeper, but was bothered by sounds in the corridor during the night. At one point I even heard someone snore, which I can easily overcome normally. When we left at 5am, we discovered that there was not necessarily the guests fault, the floor would just creak. Regarding cleanliness, I did see a cleaner going through another room very thoroughly. Having said that, our room on the surface looked clean. I did see stains on the bedding, although I am convinced that they did put it through a washer. The floor was tidy, except there was a narrow space between the bed and wall which was very dirty and dusty. As said, the bathroom was damp and there was soapy residue. We stayed for two nights, but our bed wasn't made for the second night. The bed was quite comfortable though, no complaints there. I heard South Kensington & Earls Court are better, but we will definitely not return to the Old St/Barbican hotel.

title: Very disappointing stay
text: It is a shame that I have had to rate this hotel one star, but it is not without good reason. I stayed mid-week, sole traveller. There was a very bad issue with noise - due to doors that bang when they are opened/closed.(there was one strange chap who kept going in and out of his room) It is a shame, as this could easily have been rectified with soft close doors (common complaint in hotels!) I complained to the man on the front desk, who didn't care. He said that he isn't responsible for others' noise. This is fair enough, however I think it reasonable that he should have had a word with the chap in question, and also offered to move rooms. I know there was alternative space available as I phoned up afterwards to "enquire" about availability. i realise that the room was only £60 a night, however I still expect to get a reasonable nights' sleep if I am staying somewhere. I will not be back to this hotel.

title: Basic
text: The location of the Hotel is convenient, but extremely basic. The room Only has a bed not even a side table or chair. It does have ac. For what you pay and what you get its over priced. Had a fire Alarm but no announcements and nobody to check if all guests had vacated rooms.People were not sure what was going on. The Fire department arrived and Guests will still vacating the Hotel.The evacuation in case of an emergency definitely needs more work

title: Switzerland
text: Easy hotel in Old street is well located. The staff is very friendly and helpful. The rooms are very basic but just what we need for a few nights. Overall a very good stay. We would recommend it for short break in London

title: Good location but put a bench inside the bigger rooms
text: Good location, very poor speed in fixing broken things - maintenance. Also in bigger rooms they should try and put something that a man can put a thing or two on, like a small chair or a bench. You just get 2 beds and nothing more.

title: Great simple hotel
text: This place is great if you just need somewhere clean, quiet and safe to stay the night. Sheets were clean, towels and body wash are provided and check in was quick and easy. Will definitely stay again, only downside being the bed was a little hard.

title: Good budget hotel, windowless room not so bad as it might sound
text: I usually prefer more 'normal' hotels but booked this one following an advice from a friend, since the location of the hotel was perfect for my business trip. I have intentionally booked a 'no windows' room to try out such option for the first time in my life. To be honest, do not try this option if you plan to use the hotel for anything more than a sleep, or if you're a claustrophobic. But for my 3-day buiness trip it was perfect. The room and the bathroom were sterile and minimalistic, but I didn't need anything more. Lack of window makes the windowless room a perfect place for a solid sleep, so I would also recommend this option to party goers. When I am in London I will seriously consider going to this hotel again, as it just simply does the work.

title: Cold London but cosy room. Thank you very much Marius.
text: This hotel was exactly what I needed for this short business trip. When I arrived the room was very cold but this matter was easily resolved by speaking with Marius. There was no kettle in the room, but probably because there was no table to put it on either haha. I wouldn`t recommend this hotel for more than 3 days, but it was just fine for me.

title: It saved us alot of money... buuuuut....
text: ok me and my partner are not too fussy 25yo's we are slim & fit, we were looking to save on accommodation in London. We accidentally booked a 'twin' room with two single beds (thinking twin = for two people) - no biggie it gave us a bigger room. no window room, we stayed 7 nights.... walls are paper thin (not much exaggeration) buttons in elevator broken and automatic entrance door also broken aircon was good bathroom smelly and kept getting smellier ther is a nightlight that you cannot switch off that illuminates the whole room mattress and pillows are awful with springs poking into you etc (my back and neck were stuffed by day 3) IN SUMMARY wouldn't stay for longer than 2 nights here again. I would go to extra effort to save money before travelling so I could avoid staying here altogether.

title: Like a cell - but clean
text: You get what you pay for (literally). A bit like a clean police cell. Roller blinds didn't work, not so bad but the main wall was glass floor to roof and looked onto the main road. I wouldn't stay again purely because its too far to walk to either "nearby" tube stations

title: Never Again
text: Spend a bit more for a decent hotel. Our rooms has been put in the wrong thankfully we had the confirmation, no air con, no ventilation, rooms are beyond stuffy, not cleaned properly, staff were about as useful as a lead balloon. The place is basically a storage unit with a small bathroom Would never go back will never recommend this hellhole.

title: Should be called container, not hotel
text: Room was a windowless box with a dirty floor. The box contained: two hooks on the wall, a waste basquet size of pen holder, one ceiling lamp, two separate beds that weigh tonns (too heavy to move together) and A/C that didn´t work. Bathroom was 1 sqm with a mini-size sink, toilet bowl, a shower with low pressure, a shower curtain to separate it from the toilet bowl and one hook in the door. There was no cleaning in the room during our 2 night visit so already dirty floor kept on becoming dirtier and the waste "basket" was overflowing. Reception guys answered to hi´s and byes with a yawn or smothered mumbling. + Plusses: cheap less than 10min walk to tube - Minuses: dirty no hangers, no night table, not even one chair or puff to put your things on unfriendly staff totally mislead in its advertisement

title: Clean & Adequate
text: The room we had was small but sufficient. There is no storage but having read reviews we were aware of that. The shower room was adequate. It was all very clean and the staff helpful and polite. It is ideal if you just need a place to sleep and is a reasonable price.

title: incredible value
text: clean room, nicely made up bed, including mattress protector. easily accessible location and fantastic value. check in/out was simple and straightforward. for £10 this was perfect as i didn't need to catch the last train home, and could have a day wandering around the city

title: What a dump
text: The worst place I have ever stayed and I was charged over £160.00 for 1 night. This hotel takes budget to a whole new level. Whatever you do don't stay here. Other budget chains such as Ibis and Travelodge are like 5 star luxury compared to the easyhotel. The rooms have nothing but the bed and a wet room, no furniture not even bedside tables so you have to leave all your stuff on the floor. The bed felt like it would collapse any minute and the hotel was noisy.

title: Clean Place Nice staff manzoor
text: Very good location, very friendly staff, short way to the underground, nice and clean room, cheap booking, near to london Bridge and to other famous sights, good restaurants in the near of the hotel.1

title: Does what you expect and no more
text: if you get a good price, this place is fine for a one nighter. Wouldn't advise and extended stay though, small and the location is a bit out of it for those who don't work in the City &/or know London. Entrance area and location rather average. Lift has broken buttons! However, my room was very comfortable and unlike comments from some reviewers, clean. Shower area small, but works. I had a good nights sleep.

title: Surround sound
text: The hotel is located on Old Street, a very busy road. No matter where your room is you hear the noise from the road. Walls are paper thin so you hear your neighbours very clearly. Writing this right now at 1 am listening to rowdy neighbours next door. The hotel has been converted from typically badly built london office block, never designed for hospitality so you get to hear people above stomping around. If a good night sleep is low on your list of prioroties while in london then this is the hotel for you! Stayed at the earls court easyhotel and that was much quieter. On a more positive note the rooms are a decent size at barbican.

title: Brilliant hotel.
text: Great value for money, extremely helpful staff, especially tiago on the front desk. will be staying here again. Very clean and large rooms with a view over old street. Will recommend to anyone who is looking for a cheap nice place to get your head down so close to city center

title: Don't Stay Here - You'll Be Scarred For Life - Literally!
text: I stayed here for one night - Saturday 9th August 2014. I was bitten by bed bugs - 29 times!! We had a night in London and when I woke the next day I found a few bites on my leg, thought they were mozzie bites from the night before - we paid extra to have a window in our hotel room, but the window didn't open so the "mozzie" couldn't have come in from the window. The room was so hot, told the reception who said they would change the aircon - they didn't. Anyway, on the journey home I was becoming aware of more bites and when I got home I found I was covered in them - my back,legs, arms, hands and face. The bites were swelling and very painful, not how I react to mozzie bites at all. I couldn't sleep that night because of the pain and went to the doctors the next day. I tried going to work but driving was very difficult because of the bites on my leg. I had to buy a bag of ice to sit down! My work sent me home and I had to stay there for the week as I felt so awful, and by this time the bites had blistered and I couldn't even wear shoes. I contacted EasyHotel on Monday 11th August by email as there was no phone number to be found. I got an acknowledgement email and then nothing more. I chased them again about 10 days later and have still been ignored. The bites have just about healed now but I have a constant reminder not to stay at this hotel as I have 29 scars to remind me. I am disgusted by what happened to me when I stayed here, and disgusted by the fact that they have ignored me.

title: Don’t recommend to anyone...
text: Extremely small rooms, couldn’t even pass between the bed and the wall! Bathroom was also very small!! Room service was a 10£ extra and a small breakfast box for only 1 even though I made reservation for 2! Had no extra pillows neither blanket, so it was cold while sleeping... Made room reservation with window (more expensive) and it was underground with a small window on top just to get some light from the street... We demanded a proper room for what we paid so they changed our room, althoug it had window our view was to offices.

title: Hotel is as airline does
text: EasyJet are a no-frills, low cost airline that charges a low ticket price and then try to up their revenues by flogging extras. They don't do free drinks and premium seating. You don't fly EasyJet expecting a jet-set experience, but you do at least get to your destination - the skimping doesn't extend to servicing the engines as far as we know. EasyHotel is the exact accommodation equivalent of the airline. It's cheap (for London), it's got the basics that you need (a reasonably comfortable bed, a shower) and the wings don't fall off (it's clean). Just don't expect anymore. You get a room, a bed, a toilet and shower, and that's it. No TV, no wifi, no minibar, no sofas. As a place to sleep, it works. And it's not grubby like all-too-many cheap London hotels. Don't be put off by the location (it's a office block on Old Street) or the front desk (think security guard's desk in a multi-tenanted office block inhabited by downmarket accountants). Bring ear plugs (the walls are thin, and fellow guests can be - ahem - exuberant). Showering is a logistical exercise if you don't want to flood the "pod". In an ideal world, I'd fly scheduled business class every time, but only if someone else is paying. When it's on my dime, I don't mind EasyJet. Similarly, I'd have a sense-of-humour failure if an employer sent me here, but when I'm paying for it this is more than adequate. Tips: There's no wifi, but the surrounding offices haven't figured out how to secure their networks yet. The Co-op have a large mini supermarket across the street. Shoreditch is hipster central, so there is absolutely no excuse for drinking coffee from a chain. Try the artisan stuff available from places like Shoreditch Grind on the roundabout.

title: For one night and one night only....
text: when it says you pay for what you get, I could have been in a nicer hotel, with better facilities and a cooked breakfast for a tiny bit more. Room with windows is in fact windows that are obscured and cannot be opened.

title: Dismal
text: Solitary confinement prisoners get more luxury than you will here... And I think they purposely shield this place of any phone signal so you have to pay for wi-fi. But you get what you pay for. Cheapest thing around. Did the job for one night.

title: Long Weekend Away
text: Pre-med students came to London for a long weekend to sit our GAMSAT exam. Had a great stay, nice facilities and the hotel staff are very friendly and helpful. Saad is a top guy- great to banter with and made our stay a laugh! Great value, perfect place to crash if you're planning a busy weekend.

title: London on a budget
text: It wasn't the first time at the easyhotel, it's in a budget and clean, the rooms are very small but the location is nice and if you don't have to spend a lot of time in the room it is a valuble option.

title: Our family short trip to london
text: We used the EasyHotel due to the acceptable price, and service that fully match the pricing.. The rooms are small but if you are using it only for sleep and use All time in the City it is recomendabel... Dont use it for family vecation to relax in your hotel room.... It is simply to small... Close to caffes and restaurants...

title: Enjoyed
text: Had a lovely stay in easyhotel. Its very basic but you get what you pay for. Tube station is close and many food places around. Staff really helpful. All the restaurants i like are nearby it. Absolutely loved.

title: A disgrace
text: Simply the place is a dump Whilst I understood I was booking a budget 'hotel', this place was a disgrace. To be deemed a hotel, is totally inaccurate. A hostel would not even do this place justice- just a total and utter dive. Mattress- wafer thin and dirty Quilt- non existent Pillows- like plastic bags Window- looking out onto a roof and another office block Shower- unusable I'm not normally so passionate about things, but this place was a disgrace. Note this cost 90 on reservation, so not exactly a bargain place. Avoid at all costs!!! NOTE WE CHECKED OUT AFTER 20 MINS- we were not refunded!!

title: Bargain of a trip to the capital!
text: Me, husband & 17yr old daughter, 2 night stay in triple room which had a double & single bed in, no drawers, wardrobes or bedsides but who needs them, clean white bedding and towels, compact wet room/bathroom, shower worked slow but well as me and daughter have long hair!! We paid a bargain £108ish for the two nights, very basic which suited our needs, down for an audition & not a holiday! Islington is a great area, we walked from euston station to the hotel (receptionist was shocked!) we laughed.....in fact we walked everywhere, it's so close to the tube too. The reception staff were very pleasant & I would recommend this to people who want a really cheap, comfortable stay as it's 1/4 of the price of anywhere else :-)

title: Manzoov
text: Manzoov on reception is a lovely guy, helped me and my friend out with all our things, hotel is perfect for our stay, very happy here, room is spotless and a really good welcoming atmosphere on arrival

title: Cheap and very basic
text: Second stay here, less impressed than first time. Excellent value at £19 booked day before. Reception girl was friendly and check in fast. Room (as chosen) had no window, which was more claustrophobic than expected. No mobile phone coverage in room (3,O2). Floor was not clean, sheets and bathroom were. Bathroom is very small with shower gel provided. Apart from that, there's only a bed, a coat hanger and a bin. The room was very noisy due to neighbouring guests, so I suggest you take ear plugs if you are a light sleeper. It was also very cold in the room, and the thermostat didn't seem to work. Ideal for one night, if you need to be early somewhere. There is a Coop supermarket (which closes at 5 on Sunday) nearby, as well as several night shops.

title: Don’t do it
text: I’m all about giving praise where praise is due... but I struggle to find reasons as to why I’d enter this establishment ever again. There are plenty more affordable places to stay in London that aren’t this grotty. The receptionist seemed blasé and not bothered, we booked a room with a window but it faced an ugly rooftop and an office block, which although can’t be helped, it really was ugly. No air con. Considering we stayed during a time of blistering heat in London, the room was a bareable temperature, but it wasn’t nice not being able to alter the warmth/coolness accordingly. Walls are paper thin, we could hear people talking and listening to music very very clearly (but we were lucky that it was quiet by bed time. Mysterious dribbles down the wall beside the bed, dirty tissues behind the top of the mattress by the wall etc etc... a very small bathroom with a stained toilet. There was quiet clearly a leak under the floor because the laminate flooring was slightly ballooned and made a squelching noise when pressed. Maybe I’m picky, but it made me cringe constantly and it just generally didn’t feel like a nice place. We survived, and it wasn’t horrendous - but it also wasn’t enjoyable.

title: Basic
text: Rooms very basic, literally bed and shower which is what we were after . Working away , stayed close to site . Young gentleman assisted us with parking . Nice chap . Get what you pay for . Ideally located to Barbican area.

title: Alright hotel for low cost
text: The hotel was located close to London sentral and 2 different tube stations. The room was alright, though the bathroom was a bit small. For a trip to London where we dont spend too much time at the hotel, the room was satisfying. The personel were friendly and helpful.

title: good for the price
text: The hotel is really good for the price. My room was clean and it is located in a really good position. It is very minimal, the rooms are little and the space it is not much. Nothing is free, you must pay internet! Nevertheless for the price I think is a good deal.

title: 30th weekend
text: Were do I start on this place .... terrible no other words for it we came over for a few days for a friend's 30th when we arrive and got our keys for are room it was unbearable no TV no heating a bed that no harm you be better of sleeping in the street the hole toilet and shower thing in a cube is poor it's 2017 unreal ... worst hotel I have ever been in ... paid £169 for 3 nights and didn't even stay in the place more than 15mins had to pay another 300pound for a different apartment which is unreal amazing paying the extra def helps .. I advise anyone do not stay here there is better out there honestly there are hostels which are better...

title: Very basic
text: Clean but noisy and basic. Not a venue I would stay at again given a choice, better to pay a bit more and get some comfortable chair and bed. Walls too thin can hear everything said in adjacent rooms.

title: Great value for a London hotel
text: What is there to quibble about. Certainly can't complain on the price. Fantastic value. Clean, polite staff and best of all a very cheap price. Certainly can't be beaten for value. I would recommend this hotel for a cheap stop over. Easy hotel Barbican I will be a return customer.

title: Bedbug inflicted hot box
text: I really wanted to like this hotel. I loved the concept of just a bed and bathroom. That’s all I need when I travel. Price was great and it seemed clean enough. Seemed a bit better than hostel. But no, I woke up with bug bites all over my body. This hotel has bed bugs. When I told reception I just got an “oh ok.” Yeah, not oh ok. I fricking itch. Now I’m scared of taking it home. It’s an easy hotel for bed bugs apparently.

title: good for a weekend
text: We where arriving Friday night around midnight from Stansted Airport via StanstedExpress. It's a 20-25 minute walk from Liverpool Street Station to the "hotel", our checkin took around 10 seconds, so far pretty easy. We had booked a room without windows, but where "upgraded" to one with a huge Window facing the office building next door (Room 1.13). The room itself was just like expected, one big bed (two pillows one blanked), a trashcan, one hook, the bathroom door and thats it. There is literally no space left, so be advised don't bring any big luggage. There is an AC/Heating Controller in the room wich probably is ment to control the Air conditioning. At first it doesn't react in any way but then kicks on and locks a temperature when you wouldn't expect it. So be careful wich temperature you choose, as it's not getting warmer again. Not ever! In fact you can choose 3 states, smelly, cold and very cold. The bathroom is small but Okay. Toilet, a tiny Bassin and a shower corner. The shower corner didn't have curtains resulting in the hole bathroom getting wet, so we had to evacuate the toilet paper and any towels before taking a shower. In contrast to what's said in some other reviews our room was pretty clean and in good condition. There is free wifi in the lobby but that's dead slow and not worth staying down there. Some doors to the right of the hostel there is a 24/7 mini supermarket (open around 20hrs a day) where you can buy everything you might need. There are two tube stations nearby (barbican and old street), both are within a 5-10 minute walking distance.

title: Terrible hotel
text: It was just a bed,no side table or anything in the room.The bed the most uncomfortable as I ever slept in.There was no hot water in the shower just warm and the aircondition was on all night when was 9 degrees outside.It was very cold in the room and we couldn't change it.There is no free WiFi they charge £5 for it.It is a joke in 2018 I think.

title: Alright for 1 night
text: I stayed at the Old Street EasyHotel earlier this month as I was going to the theatre and couldn't get a train or coach home as they both stop running early. I wasn't expecting much from the hotel because of it being so cheap but the beds were actually quite comfortable - I had a good nights sleep. I had a twin room with no window (Room 114 I think) and I didn't find any problems with it. If you're claustrophobic I'd probably say to be safe pay extra for the window. My bathroom had a bit of a smell, not sure whether it was drains or from a previous occupant but I could have done with some air freshener. A couple of things about my room that I had problems were, was that the two plug sockets in the room were next to my bed only

title: Basic, clean accomodation in fantastic location
text: It is the 3rd time I have stayed here. The rooms are basic but clean with a small bathroom a bit like a ship's cabin! I love the area, near the hip Shoreditch with trendy independent shops, brunch options and an original crowd. Reception staff are friendly and ready to help if needed. Perfect place to stay if you don't want to break the bank on a short London trip.

title: Still no heating, shower floods the room, noisy doors
text: Cheap and reasonably clean but too d@mn cold to get a good night's sleep. Major design flaw: the shower floor is flat (why not angle slightly to assist water drainage?). Shower water builds up, runs into the toilet area and then into the room - covered half the floor in a puddle. Added to that the room doors are extremely noisy to close, so with neighbouring rooms coming and going at all hours it’s annoying and disturbing (sounds like they’re being slammed). I will definitely not be staying here again.

title: very poor
text: the hotel & room are clean and unexpensive (especially for a hotel in London) but: bothering loudspeakers noises in the room no window no table, no chair. a disabled room where you must kneel to wash hands.

title: Nice stay friendly staff saad
text: Came here to see the city. Find a good deal. Nice place and very friendly staff specially saad. Helped me to find places around here. Nice hotel. Basic room but clean and well maintained. Recommend to everyone. Will come back for sure.

title: Not worthy.
text: Just a bed with a really small bathroom. There is no place to store our clothes, no hair dryer, no control over the air-conditioning, no hot water. Almost as good as sleeping below a bridge. The breakfast box is a joke. Sorry.

title: Basic, but clean, great value, great location, friendly and helpful people.
text: I stay here every week, normally 2 nights, for work. It is very stripped back and basic, but every room has a private en-suite, and it's always clean. And the front desk people are always warm and do everything they can to help. I've also stayed in every other London EasyHotel. This is one of the 2 best (Paddington's the other).

title: Bare and basix
text: If you need just a place to sleep into and your own toilet and shower, then this might suffice. We stayed here for 6 nights, 2 adults and 2 kids on a twin room with no window. Compared with other hotels in an area which is in zone 1, the price is lower, and hence expectations and services would be lower. It is really very basic - bare room with twin beds and uncomfortable mattress, with 1 hanger, 3 hooks, 1 small trashbin and the bathroom, no windows to the point you may develop claustrophobia. That's it. It's just a good thing that we just need the room to sleep. They do not clean the room daily. They just agreed to do 1 cleaning of the room and change of sheets since I asked that we are billeted for 6 nights. And I wonder if they did clean it since when I had to fix the bed sheets (there is no holder so it gets removed easily), the floor underneath the beds are so dusty and dirty and I found 2 old socks probably left by previous guests! Please clean the room well including the floors underneath the beds! The good thing that's why I gave 2 stars - they provide towels daily, and location! It's about 5 minute walk to Old Street Underground, 10 minute walk to Barbican Underground, with bus stops, and there are lots of restaurants and grocery stores in the vicinity. If you are looking for a self service launderette, I found one in St. John's Street about 15 minutes walk from here. There is one in Barbican but the reviews in St. John is better. I stayed in a very good hotel cheaper than EasyHotel, in Heathrow, so I guess it is really the location that is paid for here. So if you are on a budget and with no frills, then this may suffice. I suggest to book it straight from their website ... I book mine in Booking.com and it came out more expensive. There is really much room for improvement here. Hope they do so.

title: completely ok for the price
text: The rooms are extremely small, they really did not waist any space but it is still functional. The room was clean, quiet, there are nice breakfast caffees around, it is quite near to the tube station... the only thing that disturbed us was the plastic mattress cover

title: Dirty. Run down. Does not meet basic needs.
text: Do not stay in this unsanitary, run down, rip off of a place. Appalling. Have asked for a full refund - no one has had the courtesy to even reply. Deplorable. Mattress uncomfortable. Pillows thin. Everywhere dirty. Shower disgusting. Light switches filthy. No personalised temperature control. No window. No fan. The room had a bed and a mirror on the wall. Stay in a hostel....way better than this disgrace.

title: Not as good as the usual easyhotels
text: Yes I know this is a budget hotel, having stayed in their sister hotels before I booked this for my husband and myself as we were attending some seminars I booked the windowless room( never again) not knowing what it would be like but felt like a coffin Pros Location Decent sized wet room Friendly staff Price Cons Uncomfortable bed Not very clean

title: Amazing service
text: Easyhotel is a very centrally located hotel very close, in walking distance, of shoreditch. Great service great location.. What more could you want! Would recommend to anyone looking to stay in the middle of London for a fantastic price.

title: There cheap and cheerful then there expensive and miserable
text: I stayed here on the 13th of March as I was running a course. The room was less than basic. There was nothing in it ecept a hook in the wall and a bed. The so called shower was a cubicle that resembled the toilet on a train. On the front door was sign saying “ please keep the shower door closed as the steam sets off the smoke alarm”. For that to happen there would have to be heat in the water and there wasn’t. The bed is a solid structure in the middle with a mattress . The bedding was clean though so that’s one good thing. On the way in I asked the taxi driver what the place was like and he said well it’s Easy you get what you pay for. But that is not true in this case. This hotel is more expensive that the Thistle around the corner and yet there is very little there. I will not stay here again .

title: The best budget hotel ever
text: We arrived at this hotel on February 20 early in the morning.The staff was very friendly (better than a five-star hotel). We left our luggage in a safe area until the time of check-in (arround 12).they gave us two electronic cards for the room when we checked in for a twin room on the second floor. The room was very spacious and clean,they provide us two bath towels and two face towels too! The bed was very comfy,the pillow too! The temperature of the room was nice and we had hot water every day.
