title: Wouldn't rate this hotel at all if I had the option!
text: DO NOT STAY HERE - Our experience with this hotel was appalling - they admitted to have over booked the hotel and had to transfer us to a sister hotel So Kings Cross - So Hyde Park then mainted there was a maintenance issue but clearly they had really overbooked as we were only two of up to 16-20 people that had to be relocated on this night. The conditions at the So Kings Cross can only be discribed at a building site with carpets being laid in reception as we arrived, and various dangerous electrical wires hanging at various heights from the ceiling and wall - no actual reception only a small dischevveled storage room with a desk and computer. I could go on giving more terrible details. They way we were treated was terrible, no customer service or consideration for the customer. Had to cancel the next three nights with this hotel and find another hotel in London. Ive never written a review like this before but I feel this needs to be said. Horrendous experience.

title: Good Value - Good Location
text: We stayed in Apartment 13 on the second floor. The property is worn and needed some upgrading. However, we found it clean. Somewhat noisy at night. The internet is spotty. We had to work with management to get it to at lest provide some reception. Towels were brought every day. The location is very good. The quality / price equation works well for this property.

title: Never Ever stay in this place.. It will spoil your whole London experience
text: I was deceived by the pictures they use on their listings. On arrival though, it was a very nasty surprise. They gave me the key to my room. When I entered the room, it stunk of sweat, and smoke. The smell was really disgusting and overpowering. The bed had hair all over it. The sheets were stained. Upon lifting the bed sheet, there were what appeared to be blood stains on the bed. The room itself was unclean and dirty... in fact filthy. The floor had crumbs on it and obviously hadn't been cleaned. The sofa in the room actually had dirt on it that had settled due to it not being cleaned. The table was dirty. The en-suite had plaster peeling off due to damp or God knows what. There was loose wiring, and the shower had mould growing. I could not even spend an hour in this filthy room, so went to the reception to complain. They offered another room which was disgusting. This one had ripped bed sheets, and a broken bed. A towel shoved in the window to keep it closed! Got my refund in the end and left. Found a much better place just round the corner.

title: Small, cold and no Wi-Fi and you get charged TWICE
text: Small and cold room with NO refrigerator or cooking facilities. If you like me need to work during your stay and need an internet connection you should choose another hotel. First day I had a very very weak signal and then the Wi-Fi was no more, I complained several times but I only got a shrug and a "sorry about that".Three days without Wi-Fi... Had to spend a lot time at coffee places with wi-fi. Checked my bank account today 6 days after I paid and realised I've been charged twice, something I'm going to have to deal with today. Spend your money somewhere else, apart from location this hotel is not worth the money.

title: If you stay here watch you bank statements!!!
text: After enjoying a very nice night at the SO hyde park hotel and giving them positive feedback. I was shocked to find that SO Quartier ltd their sister company had withdrawn £89 from my account twice. Once, as expected, on the 24th February and another time on the 4th March. I realised that this was probably a mistake and so rang the SO hyde park hotel that evening, speaking to the manager to try to resolve the issue. He explained that it was too late in the day to do anything so he would ring me the next day. The following day came and I was anxious to get my money back so I rang the hotel to be told that there were no records to show that the money had been debited from account even once and that I needed to prove that my money had been wrongfully taken by emailing my bank statements to their organisation. I refused to go along with this as I did not wish to share any more of my personal information with such a company. The upshot is still a week later I have not received my money back and my message to you is watch you bank statements if you do decide to stay at this hotel because once they've got your details you may find yourself in the situation that I'm in. It's not very pleasant and it's very time consuming.

title: For London, good value and great location
text: 3 best things about this hotel: - Great location two minutes from Lancaster Gate Underground Station - Good value and quality room/ hotel for London - Ensuite bathroom and kitchen facilities included When I arrived, the check-in was quick and I was pleased with the room. For this price in London, the room was a good size and had lots of facilities and features. The ensuite bathroom (with bathroom consumables provided) was a real plus. Though small (and a little bizarrely like a box in the room), it had everything we needed and the shower was good. Also in the room, there is a small kitchen area (tea & coffee provided) with microwave, hob, plates & utensils, and sink. The implementation was not quite right as the area was small, so the microwave was positioned on the hob (presumably, you would have to move the microwave to another part of the room to use the hob). The room was thus a bit quirky. There was even a standing fan in the room, despite it being November, which seemed strange. However, the room was warm with the heating on most of the time and the window did not seem to fix open, so I did use it on the last morning (partly for the fun of it!). The one major problem was traffic and other noise from outside. The window needs replacing with a more modern design or at least insulating to reduce the noise because it seemed as if the window was open when it was closed. The traffic and general background noise did disturb me when trying to sleep, relax, or watch the television. Although the room was quirky and not organised exactly right, I was very happy with it and liked it apart from the noise problem. Despite that noise problem, I would like to stay there again next time because the room is good and the hotel is well-located. No food is provided, as it is self-catering but it is good to have the kitchen facilities to use in the room and there are a few restaurants in the small road immediately to the right side of the hotel (when facing it) and more in the area. It is also very convenient for Paddington Station and Hyde Park. Overall, I did really enjoy the experience of this hotel.

title: Never stay here
text: Firstly I booked 10th November for the 30th November waited 20mins on the phone why they checked they had a triple room available. they confirm over the phone and by email. we got there in the morning dropped our bags off then later at 5pm came back to check in. taking in mind I have a 12year old which they asked on the phone at the time of booking. they gave us a single room and a double room two floors above saying there's nothing else they can do, after getting the email out they had sent me on the 10th confirming the triple the guy was stating I should of given them more notice at this point I said to my husband were just book in another hotel the guy replyed if we go else were he was still charging us full price because I was canceling the booking I pointout it's not what we booked there was no email nor phone call nor in the morning did they mention they had not got the room we booked we rang late rooms.com who took the booking and they said there's nothing they could do but take it up with the hotel. We paid the money and stayed as he was still charging if we stay or went the room was dirty no heating the blind held up by blue tack one dirty pillow and one really thin quilt the windows are single glazed and it sounds like the busses are in your room. I read the reviews before going so asked for a higher floor because of the traffic but never sleep all night because of the noise. This room cost £140 was not worth the £40 I was robbed

title: Do not stay here
text: Booked on late rooms and the photos made the hotel seem really nice, even better when we booked for £60 when it was supposedly cost £200. I feel robbed of my £60 photos are obviously not of this hotel, bed is broken and arrived to a lot if rubbish we had to move to get into our room. Toilet doesn't flush and we had to ring the hotel to see if we were in the right place as there are no signs outside. Thank god I'm only here 1 night!

title: Do not stay here
text: This is a horrid place. Firstly we to hike up quite a few stairs with all our luggage. My father is 72 and it was really hard work. The bathroom had the previous occupants wet towels hanging on the back of the door. There were bit all over the floor so definately hadn't been cleaned. Under the decorative bed throw were pubic hairs and other bits. The quilt inside the grubby cover was brown and stank. I woke to have bites in my legs. Once you have dealt with all that, we'll then there is the noise. It is horrendous. Yea this is a cheap place to stay and yes it's by Hyde park but honestly spend the extra money and stay somewhere better. I would never ever stay here again or recommend anyone should. I cannot believe that a place like this actually has the cheek to charge. They should be paying me!

title: Fine fir a solo traveller
text: I Stayed here for 5 night as a solo traveller, there was no real staff around to help if needed and no lift so had to carry suitcase all the way to forth floor. Small, although i did get a free upgrade from single to double so would hate to see what single looked like. a little street noise but clean and tidy.

title: Awful
text: We were moved to this hotel because we couldn't stay at it's sister property (so paddington) for which we had originally booked. I'm not sure how much a room at this place should be, but we paid the £90 a night for so paddington, there was no breakfast (we were told that we could eat at the other property (5 minute walk away)) the room was tiny and not the cleanest, and very noisy. I know London is a busy place but it sounded like we were sleeping at piccadilly circus. On the plus side the shower was good, however there was no maid service so the bed was never made and the towels not changed. Do not stay here even if it's for £25 a night.

title: assaha hyde park apartments
text: we stayed in room 7 on the first floor although we had to identify it as no numbers on outer doors!. Bed - very bad mattress and very low Sofa - very soft - we struggled to be able to get back up again kitchenette - clean, tidy and all utensils and pots as required, fridge was impecably clean bathroom - toilet was also very low tothe floor, toilet seat was loose and didnt fit, the shower cubilcle was very small but excellent water pressure - it was a true closet ensuite extras - all toiletries provided, towels, provided staff - the gent on reception at check in was very polite and helpful with info, lady on check out was also friendly and helpful room - overall was ok and better than expected after reading other reviews. it is fine for short stays but not more than 3 days max in our opinion great location , near all amenities - shops and restaurants

title: One night stay only..
text: I went to see The Stone Roses so I only wanted a cheap hotel just somewhere to rest our head for the night..that was after climbing 4 flights of stairs to then find out at 12.01am in the morning that there was no lights working in our room. The staff were very un-helpful and I wouldn't even class them as friendly. They didn't know I had even paid for my room and the room wasn't even ready upon arrival, there was a cleaner still there with the room swarmed in flies and a horrible mouldy smell. We were apparently staying in the more 'up-to-date' suite...'apparently'. Wouldn't spend more than £60 staying here, over-priced for what you get, certainly wouldn't class this as a 3star hotel. I've seen better!!

title: Awful hotel, great location
text: Rooms are very very small and basic. Although look nice on initial appearance, there are a number of flaws. Duvert much too thin, pillows too thin, bath room cramped, walls are paper thin and you can hear everything next to you, including the drunken teenager next door at 4am! Cooking apparatus is basic with no utensils and no reception apart from the odd hour during the evening. Only thing going for this hotel is the location, 3 mins from paddington and lancaster gate tube stations.

title: Quirky but functional
text: I'm working in London and staying in various budget hotels in the Paddington and Bayswater area. This is the first one that I've wanted to come back to, and having stayed here for a second week I'd happily come back again. The hotel seems to be part of the way through a refit. The 1st and 2nd floors look shabby, and as other guests have said you have to walk up the stairs as there is no lift. However both the rooms I've stayed in (No 19 on the 4th floor and 14 on the 3rd floor) have been newly fitted out and done to a really high quality. Compared to some places I've stayed the rooms feel really nice. Each time the rooms have been clean when I've arrived, although they are not serviced during your stay. For budget London hotels the rooms are quite spacious. Each room has had a little kitchen in it. In room 19 (double room) there was a hot plate as well as a microwave, kettle and toaster. In room 14 (single) there was no hot plate. Both had nice large fridges. Each room had plenty of storage space for clothes and bags although a few more clothes hangers would have been useful. Digital TV in each room and basic toiletries provided. Each room is a little quirky. In No. 19 the light in the bathroom switched itself off after a couple of minutes and then after a few more switched itself back on again. I've no idea why. In room 14 the bathroom light is on a sensor but it does not seem to be very well positioned. When you are in the shower it doesn't detect you so switches off the lights and when you're in the bed it does sense you so switches on the bathroom light unless you've shut the door. A bit more design could have gone into this. Similarly in room 19 there was a hole in the bathroom wall which you could see cables in. I'm not sure that this is good electrical practice or whether it's just temporary repairs... Likewise in room 14 it looked as though the smoke detector had been moved but the location it had come from had not been properly patched and painted and I don't even want to speculate as to what the mass of earth cable in the bathroom cupboard beneath the sink was meant to be doing. Each day the water from the cold tap has been very hot for about 10 minutes. It seems to be some odd plumbing is going on, but if you run the bathroom and kitchen cold taps for a while they do then start to produce cold water. Excellent location for Hyde Park and very friendly and efficient welcome. I would happily stay here again as it suits a budget traveller well.

title: value for money and nice location with good staff
text: I am a vegetarian from India and stayed here for 4 weeks at a stretch for a business trip. Alone. +ves: 1. Just opposite to Hyde Park and within few metres to Lancaster Gate Tube 2. Barclyas cycle hire station just outside the hotel 3. Rooms with fully functional kitchen, microwave, toaster, utensils

title: DO NOT STAY HERE!!!!!
text: I strongly recommend that people never book here. 2 of us were staying here, it was filthy, there was only 1 cup and 1 knife and fork, toilet seat was broken, the base of the shower filled up whilst showering so you had to have a really quick shower to avoid the overspill and flooding, there was a hole in the wardrobe, the tv didn't work. We spoke to the owner (who was asian) regarding the above and more and he was rude and was very racist saying that he is sick of 'us English people' we ended up contacting the police who came.. The owner wasn't to be seen. Photos will be uploaded shortly.

title: unclean room
text: want happy when we turned up to find the large apartment for 4 we booked we couldnt have was very dissapointing. we were first told we had to move to shephards bush and said give us 6 pound for a taxi when it would cost us around 20 pound. then said they wud give us 2 rooms whic were very small, dirty, carpets curtains black. light in bathroom was illegally fitted. fag ends behind curtain worst place ever stayef. noisey road no sleep. ruined our weekend was meant be at the proms in the park. they obviously had over booked. made out the lock was broken on the door. wouldnt stay here again.

title: Our room was like a furnace!!!!
text: Good points :- reception & staff lovely and friendly, clean, large communal areas good for meeting people, cheap prices. Bad points :- the room was just too hot!! For obvious reasons the window is only able to be opened a small amount, and it made no difference anyway. Had a very uncomfortable nights sleep due to the temperature in the room. Not sure if its the heating or pipes in the room that makes it so hot, but it wasn't pleasant! Other than than a good hostel at a cheap price!

title: if you are female, get a private room!!
text: My friend and I (two girls in our early 20's) stayed there for a few nights and we are very glad we had booked a private room. con's - There were a lot of creepy old men, like more than anyone else that just hung around the main rooms for a long time and it freaked us right out. I would not have been able to sleep in a 24-person room with them (just be careful). - The rooms were VERY small, but to be expected in London. - Our toilet didn't work during our stay which wasn't fun and the shower did not work either. - The wifi only works in the main room, and even at that, not really (it took me 40 minutes to connect to it at about 10pm). Pro's- - The people at the front desk were awesome - It was a good place to sleep and had comfy bedding though. - there is a kebab place basically across the street - you are really close to a lot of highlights so basically, if you get this place for a good deal, its worth it, but don't expect the ritz!

title: Nice and Clean!
text: Beautiful hostel, with great staff. All seemed really happy. Paid extra for breakfast - that was the only bad part of the stay, not worth it! Otherwise I had a private en-suite twin room, was worth every penny. So Cheap to say I was in Zone 1 of London.

title: I wouldn't recommend
text: The website and the photos make this hostel looks like a good place to stay but it's not a place I would stay again. I booked a private room with a private shower for my brother and I. The room was as expected since it is a hostel however, there was NO towels, wash cloth or bath soap, just room amenities. I went down to the service desk to inquire about the towels and the front desk guy said I've to pay for it. I would've been okay if that was communicated upon check-in or stated on the site but there are not. Room for improvement: They do need to work on their guest service skills and experience so the guest can feel welcome and home away from away. Inform the guests of any information needed so there's not element of surprise.

title: Worse living conditions than prisons
text: DO NOT STAY!! Awful awful awful rooms and bathrooms, communal areas are ok which give a false sense of security when you walk in. Hostel staff are really rude and unhelpful! We’d booked through lastminute.com for one type of room which was not available when we arrived, we were advised by reception to call them for a refund but when it’s actually come to getting a refund we have been told it’s not their problem. They are unbelievably rude and the hostel itself is disgusting. I can’t stress enough how bad this place is.

title: CHANGE OF ROOM AND OFFERD A SO CALLED CONTINENTAL BREAKFAST ....
text: Where do i start... first off we PREbooked a 4 bedded room for privacy online..we came all the way from birmingham U.K to london and when we got to the place at about 12:45, the guy at the desk (pedro) i beleve, took the information and double checked that the room was not ready and to come back and check in after 2pm (14:00) ok now when we came later on to check in the guy took the booking details again and THEN told me that the room we had booked can not be accessed and we had to go in a 18 bedded dormitry. the guy then said that it was a last minute change, then i asked him why he did not mention anything from when we came earlier and he then took my book in detials. he then said he cannot do anything as we came all the way from birmingham we had no choice but to take the new room..as we did not want to waste the time as we had a eent to go to to book another hotel.. then the charging of £3 EACH TIME you open and close the safe is ridiculous. and as for the shower, horrible and dirty. there were hair shavings on the floor and the shower head was broken,. as we were checking out, we noticed that people who were checking in next to us also had the same problem of prebooked a priate room but had to sleep in a 18 bed dormitry i wil not be coming here no matter what how cheap it is..

title: Weekend Break
text: My friend and I stayed in a private room, it was very clean and everything worked properly. The staff were absolutely brilliant! They took their time explaining the area and recommending transport/attractions to us. The whole hostel was very clean and the green area at the side was very well kept. It's a perfect place to stay for commuting in and out of London City. There was no air conditioning in the rooms so they get very hot during the day and early in the morning and the windows don't open fully, also the television room is locked at 12 o'clock which was a bit of a nuisance. Other than that it was fantastic, I would definitely recommend it.

title: It was denied i paid any deposit
text: I wanted to book in and the receptionist Lied in my face that not any deposit made, i need to pay for 5 night £40 because in the room i looked the beds are priced for £8. The receptionist don't even know how much a bed happen to cost.

title: Great location, place and staff
text: I spend there 2 nights as I was visiting London with my brother. This is the right place if you want a real English experience in the heart of London. I was surprised by the cleanliness of the place, it’s not just super stylish but it’s also kept greatly well! Have a look at my pictures to see what I mean! The reception guys were super nice, they gave us advises and tips while wee were staying there. There’s a breakfast service, vending machines and a pub in the building. This place is unbelievably cheap and great. I’ll definitely visit it again if I need to stay in London overnight. Thank you for the nice experience!

title: Adequate and did the job
text: The hotel was well located for the south bank- about a 20 min walk. The service was very good by the reception staff and they were very friendly. I think the hotel is best suited for international tourists looking for cheap London accommodation. We had a private room which was compact but clean and overall I'd say the price was ok- I'd possibly expect it a bit cheaper. We had a lot of noise from people walking past the room at night- not too much but just the noise of them walking was loud. I'd recommend it to someone wanting to crash in London for a night or two, but not a family.

title: Nice Hostel, bit far from the station
text: We had a nice stay at the RestUp. It was clean, we had all we need, people were nce,good breakfast, nice atmosphere. However, we expected it to be a bit closer to the Tube. Especially in the night it was a bit far to walk.

title: Very noisy but decent hostel, with a good location
text: First the good, the hostel had a good atmosphere in the communal areas, the staff were nice, it was clean and the showers worked and were warm. Mattress was firm , but fine. The bad is the noise level. You are right next to a dual carriageway and under the Heathrow flightpath (flights start coming in at 0600). At 0740 on a Sunday morning it was 45-50 decibels. That is beyond earplugs for me, but others might not have an issue. Plus it was the thinnest pillow ever. Even folded in half it felt like it wasn't there. I put my clothes underneath so I could lie on my side with my head supported. I suggest giving Rest UP a go if you can take the noise levels. If you can't, look at the hostels north of the Thames (Kings Cross, Paddington or Victoria). That way you will avoid the planes at least and the traffic tends to be travelling slower, so or is less noisy. But nowhere (cheap) will be really quiet in central London.

title: No sleep, no facilities
text: It was clean and the staff were nice. That's about all the positives of this place. Compared to other cheap, minimal, accommodation this is not a good choice. This place feels designed with only profit making in mind. I wish I has read more reviews on this place. Even with ear plugs the noise levels are terrible. Constant traffic outside, all hours of the night (and since I didn't sleep I can also attest to half a dozen emergency vehicles, with sirens blaring). The walls are also really thin, so any noise from the other rooms will wake you as well. The name 'rest up' really is a joke. There aren't any services or facilities except for toilets and showers. Breakfast is twice as expensive as anywhere else. Couldn't get dinner the kitchen was closed. No kitchen facilities available (not even a jug or toaster) so you can't make your own. Lounge is only open at certain hours. WiFi is only in limited places. The list goes on. Compared to other places you get very little for your money.

title: Good...the heatwave didn't help!
text: I stayed in a 4 bed dorm with friends for 3 nights in August. The rooms were small but each bed had 2 plugs (read other reviews where people were complaining about lack of power points) and a small light. The room also had a sink and a large mirror. I didn't sleep well as London was experiencing a heatwave so the room was very warm. This was not helped by the sound of traffic with the open windows (you can't win!). My advice is to bring ear plugs! I found the bed comfortable but I was sleeping with the duvet underneath me due to the heat. However the pillows were shockingly thin! I found the shower and toilet areas satisfactory. I brought flip flops as a precaution but there was no need really. Maybe we were blessed with our fellow guests. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful especially Sam. He had no problem organising excursions and taxis for us...he also acted as a cock block on occasion! Overall I was happy with the hostel. I mean where else would you get accommodation for €40 a night that close to central London. Not sure about the area itself but we got taxis (or ubers) straight to the door after nights out. We will be back!

title: Do NOT recommend
text: I stayed for three nights. The tiniest room I have ever stayed in. Uncomfortable. Before getting into the lifts, there was a terrible odor from the waste basket. Only wifi in the ground. The only relative acceptable thing is Location.

title: Great for a short stay
text: I think for a few nights or a week as somewhere to sleep in central London it's great, for a longer stay though I'd want a kitchen. Dorms are small but I only wanted to sleep. Busy road but earplugs worked fine. Location is great, just 10min walk to Elephant and Castle and from there you can get to any part of London very quickly and easily. Probably the second best bus hub in London. I lived in this area previously, I appreciate New Kent road is not it's best 'face' but there's so much going on here, a very well-known art college so lots of trendy caffs and bars- you just have to do your research people! The hostel staff I found really helpful as I extended my stay a couple of times and they went out of their way to make the room change easy. Hostel cafe is convenient but a bit pricey, for cheap coffee with wifi Wetherspoons & Pret are both up the road in E&C.

title: Clean and good value
text: 5-10 min walk to tube station 1-2 min walk to bus stops Nice and clean. Rooms are simple, beds, sink and a mirror. They are good value as well I think. We booked a 4 bed dorm and it was much cheaper than the 4 of us staying at a hotel. It's pretty big as well. So many rooms and so many people. Sometimes the queues are ridiculous and so the cacheck-in takes quite a while.

title: Basic but sufficient.
text: A cheap, basic hostel that is OK for a short stay. Located in a bit of a seedy area, though I wouldn't say we ever felt in danger or threatened or anything, just not the nicest spot in London. Having said that, it is very accessible and good links by bus and tube. There is a bus stop (Bricklayers Arms) quite literally at the door. A very good value. Our private room was clean and the bunk beds were ok. It was bright and the temperature was comfortable. We had an ensure sink and shower which we very clean but toilet facilities were down the hall and communal, and I did not find those toilets to be clean. This is why my review lost a star. They need to be cleaned more often. Also, be aware that there are many school groups that base themselves here so expect to be around loud and not always behaved children... but what can I say, it is a hostel after all. The front desk staff are extremely friendly and helpful and they are what upgraded the hostel from 3 stars to 4 in my opinion. One last tip, don't miss Borough Market. You can grab the bus just around the corner to the right on Old Kent Rd.

title: WARNING! MUST READ!!!
text: Staying here will ruin your vacation. Don’t be fooled by the photos, it’s a dump! Rooms are extremely small and cramped with no air. You will not sleep, as the temperature is like a sauna. Windows only open about an inch. I laid in a puddle of my own, and someone else’s sweat, on a thin, dirty plastic prison mattress three bunks high with almost no steps to get up with. UNSAFE! The pillow and linen weren’t laundered and smelled strongly of someone else’s armpits. Busy street right next to the place that has loud motorcycles racing up an down it at all hours of the day. No lockers in the room, but a locker room on the lobby floor which you pay $3 every time you open it. Breakfast was ok but $3.50-$5.00 depending on which one you get. $2.50 for a towel. WiFi only works in the lobby and not in the rooms. People going in and out all night turning on and off the lights and being loud. No privacy anywhere. Coed bathrooms and showers. Yes that’s right! Coed showers. The showers have no temperature control, so you get either ice cold or scolding hot water. Front desk clerk sold us a tour through golden tours and gave us totally wrong directions on how to find the pickup location. Almost missed the tour. They advertise being close to all main attractions but that’s another lie. You’ll find yourself navigating through a bunch of subway (tube) systems just to get anywhere. It amazes me that this place has been here so long and hasn’t fixed any of these issues. There are bad reviews going back quite a long time for this place. My impression is that they are only about making money and that’s all. I have only two positives: 1) I made a mistake booking and was given free breakfast one morning to compensate. 2) checking out early to go to a normal hotel. So, if you value your time and money on your vacation, save yourself a bad experience/headache and don’t stay here. YOU WILL REGRET IT IF YOU DO!!!

title: Great value for money accommodation in convenient London SE1 location
text: Everything that RestUp offer on your website became of real and tangible value on our nights spent there. One curiosity: the daily price are better, if the booking are not use the RestUp service online, the sites suggested here by tripadvisor showed better prices! The hostel building is so huge, with good service on the front desk,but it is so heterogeneo the level of information of the employees that work on the front desk, so other tip, take info from more than one employee before take decision. The bedroom for two are small and with bunk beds, with one basic shower room private, what is sufficient to nights of rest. There is one nice bar ten minutes walking from the hostel on the 50 Great Dover St, the bars and restaurants existing on the road on front the hostel are not attractive. Other nice place to go from the hostel is the The Shard building top lounge, free entrance but expensive drinks, 20 minutes walking froom the RestUp.

title: Pretty Poor and they screw you down
text: If there is a way to make a buck in a hostel these guys would have found it. You have to pay for absolutely everything. Towel-charge, baggage storage-charge, hot water-charge, laundry-charge and phone charge-yes, you guessed it CHARGE! The staff are pretty unfriendly to boot. Do yourself a favour and stay elsewhere.

title: Very good
text: This is simply likeable.there was lots of things its service greenery, rooms all were marvolous. Everyone should go there and experience it , my family got happy by my decision of booking that hotel. I hope you have got convinced to go there so what are you waiting for??

title: For £20 in London guess you can't go too wrong
text: For around £20 in London you can't really argue. It's pretty basic but if you're just looking for a room to stay in after a night out it suffices.. Also handy for a large group, especially if you need a bed after a long day drinking.

title: Just what we had been looking for
text: I went with my boyfriend for two nights, and I must admit I was scared about this place because it was new and there were just a couple of reviews of it, and after having read other place's reviews I didn't know what to expect. But finally it was just what I was looking for. What I was worried about overall was cleanliness, and I have to say I was really surprised this place was so clean! We booked a PRIVATE TWIN ROOM with private bathroom on the 2nd floor. Unfortunately, there were not double beds so that's not comfortable for couples... but we managed to sleep both in one bed. Also, we weren't lucky and our room was just next to the lift, so we could hear everyone going in and out at night. (If you are a heavy sleeper as me, this shouldn't be a problem: we both slept well) It DOES have a lift (there's a previous comment saying there's not, but they opened it the day we arrived) and they offer breakfast until 9.30 for.. I think 2.5 pounds. You can have towels for 2 pounds each (+ 3 pound deposit) You can ask for a hairdryer, they'll just ask for your ID card and keep it until you return it. Also they ask for a key deposit (I think it was 6 pounds) You can pay the room by card (not the towels) We had a private bathroom, so I cannot say much about the public ones... Also there was no heating in our room and the window was extremely thin, so at the beginning it was a bit cold.. but as the room was small, after a while inside it was warmer. There are many things to eat, p.e. pizza margherita for a fiver... not bad. Staff were OK, always trying to do their best. Its a 10min walk away from Elephant&Castle station, (Zone 1), so it takes just 20mins to get from the hotel to the city centre. - HOW OUR PRIVATE ROOM WAS: Don't expect a suite of it! There's just a tiny room with a 2-bed bunk, and then the bathroom. It was a kind of pre-fabricated toilet, the sink was small but the shower and the toilet were average size. It did have a mirror. There were many plugs at the room, and also many lights (one for the whole room, one for each bed and one for the toilet). The window was thin and there was no heating, but there were good duvets so it was fine. Ckeckout from 1pm, but safe locker room (with key). - WHAT I LIKED BEST: Amazingly clean--- This really convinced me to go there again next time. You get what you pay for, it's perfect for spending less than a week. Helpful staff. Very good location. Cheap breakfast, cheap private & public rooms. Lift. Drink & snack machines. Safe lockers (with key). Super duper decoration!!!(amazingly beautiful and modern hall, and very beautiful old historic building). Some kebab & chicken places around to eat, which are open till late at night (on the way from the station to the hostel). Supermarkets at less than 5mins (Tesco xpress and others, also on the way to the station) -WHAT I DIDN'T LIKE SO MUCH (BUT I DIDN'T REALLY CARE ABOUT): The mattress was a bit thin, although its OK if you stay less than a week. Same for the room size.. there's no place to put your stuff (just a couple of coat hangers) not even a chair or enough place to leave your suitcase opened... so if you have a lot of luggage you better look for a hostel with bigger rooms!. Also there was no heating and the window was thin, so take your winter pyjamas if you're going to stay a lot of time in the room (if not, your duvet will be more than fine and finally you'll even be boiling inside). So if you're planning to stay less than a week in London, I DEFINITELY RECOMMEND IT. To me it was perfect.

title: Hostel not a hotel
text: This is a hostel so for the price you can’t expect too much. I was here in my job as a coach driver My room was small with a on suite shower, it was clean with plain white walls, there is no TV or kettle. The school party that I took had 6 bedded rooms, they were not on suite. Both the evening meal and breakfast were quite adequate. Being close to the Elephant & Castle you can jump on the underground so you are in central London in minutes. If you don’t want the food at the hostel there are plenty of reasonably priced restaurants in the area.

title: Cheaper but constructive criticism
text: The place is really nice and tidy. But there is not plugs in the rooms. No wifi in the rooms. No curtains around the beds and no cages beneath the beds for baggage. If you want cabinets you have to pay for it and they are not in the rooms.

title: Excellent
text: Very good location. Clean, friendly. All thats needed. Near Elephant and Castle Tube. Has lockers and Laundry. Safe. Busy. Stayed 4 nights. Had a fabulous stay, Doors locked and had to use swipe cards to open them.

title: Cheap and Easy
text: Clean rooms with En suite. For the price this is as good as it gets. Everything you need if your out and about exploring London. If your used to 4 star hotels with TV and Pool move along.... if your looking for somewhere to leave your bags and have a good nights sleep at a good price for London then stay here.

title: Average
text: Staff was great and breakfast was fairly good. However, this was the smallest room I have been in. I stayed with a friend in a twin room. It consisted of a bunk bed and just the place to put our luggage: there was no wardrobe nor table where to put our things. Whenever we wanted to go out of the room, we had to move our luggage in order to open the door.

title: Go for something closer to the city centre
text: We had a double room with a private bathroom. Very small room, bed was pushed against the wall with very little room for luggage etc. but we managed to make the most of it. Bathroom was clean, glad to have our own as the hostel was busy. A big group of teenagers must have been occupying several rooms and were very noisy, using the hall way to gather and muck around. Towels are not provided, but linen is. Breakfast is available for 4 pounds, cereal, toast, tea, coffee, juices, boiled eggs, cheese, ham. Overall the hostel was okay, the distance from the city, which was walkable if you had the time and energy, was somewhat of a drawback, and in retrospect we would have booked accommodation closer to the city centre.

title: Fantastic Hostel
text: This is by far one of the better hostels I have stayed in anywhere in the world. It is new, has weather was great, there was a fantastic outside space with grass to seat on, they even had a bbq going with burgers and sausages to buy ( thought that was great). The rooms were decent, very clean, mine also had en suite shower and toilet which is an almost unheard of luxury in a hostel. Great chill out area including a room with a big TV, pool table and lots of comfortable sofas. The hostel was busy but staff were still very friendly and helpful. Location was good too, close distance to Elephant and Castle tube station ( zone 1) also loads of buses to anywhere in London just outside the hostel. I really enjoyed the stay and really recommend this place to anyone.

title: cheap and quick
text: for the 5 star traveller keep scrolling. for the backpackers and get through the UK on a budget travellers look no further. Rooms are small but perfect size for a few nights. bedding is supplied which is nice, most rooms are bunkbeds and come with a sink, some rooms have own bathrooms (I've heard). Towels cost 5 pounds but you get 3 pound back upon returning them. Showers and bathrooms(for the most part) are shared among the floor, males and females have separate ones. Cleanly for a hostel. I would recommend this place if youre traveling through london. only about a 10 minute walk to explore the back city of london and a very short bus ride to get to the main sites.

title: Basic and clean. Does what it says on the tin.
text: We were impressed by the atmosphere in this hostel

title: Clean enough
text: Stayed in a twin share room and it did have it's own shower but the plug in the sink was stuck down and there was dirty water left in the sink. The power outlets are right where the bar of the bunk bed is against the wall so some are unusable and the bed creaks like crazy everytime you or the person on the other bed moves a centimeter. The beds and shower were clean though

title: Location ir good, staff helpful
text: It is good price performance overall. Just wc/showers are common, small space, not comfortable. Water very hot in shower without possibility to change temperature. But in general everything is OK. staff is brilliant. Wi-fi works just in public spaces and sometimes signal was weak.

title: Moldy showers. Trash everywhere. Absolutely awful.
text: Do not stay here! Moldy showers. There’s not enough seating or outlets. Trash everywhere. People sitting in hallways to charge phones because there are no outlets in the rooms. No lockers in rooms for storage. Dingy lighting. Completely depressing. Do not give them your money.

title: A short but noisy stay.
text: Me and one of my classmate booked a room for 7 nights. The room was really small. The lockers that is provided costs 3-pound for every time that you need to unlock it. And you have to open the locker again inside a 24-hour period. This is a thing that makes planing and traveling a lot harder. The location is alright, its like 5-10mins walk away from Elephant and Castle metro stop. So its pretty central. The lobby was the only place to get Wifi, and it was often crowed with school classes. On the last night of our stay, did we experience some noise from the room beside us. And the noise was on for like an hour.

title: Cheap for a reason
text: Yes, so it was cheap. It's not the safest location. The one pub nearby was searching the people before allowing them entry. I had a younger friend with me and he was very worried for his safety, and said he could feel a lot of tension. "Why did you choose this hostel again?" I'm not as easily scared but it's very, very possible you will feel uncomfortable here. I was told there was someone stabbed on the street a few days before. The lady in the cornershop assured me that they "wouldn't touch tourists". This offered my friend little relief. Let's just say it's what could be described as "the real London"! I can only comment on my (4 person) room, I had two pleasant Italian fellas with us but the room was really very small. The beds literally couldn't be moved an inch any direction such was the lack of space. The overall appearance was a massive step down from the outside and lobby, the rooms seemed 50 years older. The people at the reception, especially late at night, left a lot to be desired. Far from helpful, the first night a rather intimidating man told me to "make this the last time you come to the desk" after I asked where I could get refillable drinking water. The second night I was there I saw a mouse in the kitchen area and when I informed them at the desk they suddenly seemed a lot friendlier and had some strange explanation about plumbing issues. They'd want to get them sorted ASAP then! Overall it's decent value, but if you're not a hardened backpacker travel with a friend.

title: Absolutely shocking, thieves!!
text: As you can probably tell by my title I'm not happy. When we arrived on the Saturday at around 2:00 pm we were greeted by one of the staff members, who check us in no problem, he then asked for a £10 deposit for the key, which we thought was fair enough, he said we would get it back when we checked out. So we check out on the Sunday morning and the women behind the counter just say thanks that's you all checked out, I then said "you've got our £10 for the key" she says "no there's nothing here" I said "I gave the guy £10 for the key deposit" she doesn't even say sorry, she just says "well if you haven't got a receipt... You should always ask for a receipt" so I'm standing in pure shock! "So your tell me that the other staff member stole my money?" She replies "I'm not saying that, you could be lying to me" Now she's accusing me of lying!!!!!!! It was getting embarrassing for everyone, they were not budging, if I thought it would have helped I would have called the police but for the sake of £10 I couldn't be bothered, it's just the principle!!! Terrible!!!! DO NOT STAY HERE

title: Good but not great
text: Room was very clean but basic, as one would expect from a hostel. There are lockers but they are £3 for every time they are opened. This seems like a bit of a rip off to me. Pretty good price and location for Central London. You have a nice view of the Shard when you leave. The room had one window which only opened a certain amount and our room was like a furnace, but it did also have a private en-suite bathroom so swings and roundabouts I guess. Staff in general are helpful, however the girl serving breakfast was rather rude. She told us that the breakfasts were closing soon and that we had to hurry up or go somewhere else. The manner in which it was said was an example of extremely poor customer service and we did then choose to go elsewhere. This was a small issue in what was otherwise a comfortable stay.

title: Cheap, so don't expect much...
text: Purpose of stay: two weeks work trip to London in November 2014 Room: 4-bed mixed dorm PRO: - cheap - clean - within walking distance of St. Thomas Hospital, London Eye, etc. - free WIFI (in the lounge area only!) - quiet on weekdays CON: - loud on weekends - lifts didn't work on 5 days (which is especially annoying if you have to walk up from -2 to 4) - no hot water on 3 days - showers are boiling hot - bathroom windows are always open, so it's freezing in the mornings - no kitchen facilities to cook or prepare your own food, not even a hot water jug - you can access all floors without access card which means safety is not the best - access cards are disabled on day of check-out, i.e. you have to go to the reception after taking a shower because you can't enter your room MIXED: - some staff is really friendly, but some is not

title: Perfect if you just want a bed for the night.
text: We stayed here for one night in a twin bunk room. The room was very basic, but was clean. We only wanted a place to leave our bags and a place to sleep and this was ideal. For the price you pay you can not expect too much. If you want the little luxuries then unfortunatley you have to pay for them. For the two of us for one night it was £60, the cheapest I could find in London on a Saturday evening. Its location is brilliant, a short walk for the elephant & castle tube and about a 25min walk to tower bridge. This place was just perfect for what we wanted. Would definatley stay again.

title: Don't do it.
text: I'm on a three week trip around Europe, and this is by far the worst experience I had. This place is a crap hole. Other reviewers have said the price is good, and I disagree. Maybe it's a good price for London, but $60 US dollars is not a good price for what we received. It's easily the most expensive room we stayed in after Berlin, Copenhagen and Prague, furthest away from the city and least amount of amenities. First of all, the rooms are ridiculously small and you pay a surcharge for EVERYTHING. £10 key deposit, £5 towel, £4 breakfast (which was a joke), £3 lockers. Also, when I went to check out and get my deposit back on the towel, the guy at the front gave me 50p pieces instead of pounds, knowing I wouldn't recognize the currency as a foreigner. Also, the checkout is at 10, an hour earlier than most places, and when we went to eat breakfast at 9, our key cards didn't work anymore. When I went to reception to ask, the lady told me to wait on the guy who was too busy making coffee to help me. So rude. No wifi in rooms, no computers, no soap. This is just a bare minimum hostel, and it was full of loud kids the whole time we were there. The neighborhood also sucks. I recommend trying AirBnB for a better deal, don't stay here.

title: Feel welcome
text: This Hostel has great staff, kind, helpful and very understanding. They went out of their way to sort out a few problems I had

title: Good but not perfect !!
text: The hostel is near "Elephant & Castle" Underground station. The London eye is a 20 to 30 mins walk from the hostel. There are plenty of shops and restaurants and a shopping mall nearby. There is a bus station in front of the hostel. The hostel is well designed and the receptionists are really helpful. However the WiFi gets really slow, when there are plenty of people connected.There is no kitchen, however there is a restaurant (which is expensive). There is only one bathroom with 2 toilets and 2 showers. which is not enough for the number of guests in the hostel. The rooms aren't spacious and the lockers cost from one to two pounds whenever you open them or per day. overall The hostel is secure, the location is good. but you should be ready to pay more money for extra services.

title: No air!
text: $22AUD /night beds-tiny, uncomfortable. No free towels, no shampoo Linen provided - DIY I confirmed my booking a couple of weeks ago prior to arriving, when I checked-in they told me I had to change room on my last night and only supplemented me a free breakfast for not having a room from 10-3pm! And will give me "free storage" for my luggage.. I would be OK to change rooms if it was immediately available but this was a real pain as I like to sleep in and go out at night. I was in a room 1 floor above the common area so wifi was able to reach there, but there was no ventilation and I was soo hot at night, it was VERY uncomfortable. The 3rd night I was there, I left the door open and that helped a little. The showers was a button and u had to keep pressing for water and you can't change the temperatures. It was SO hot I couldn't even stand in it. My last night I was in the rooms on ground floor and the showers there were a lot better! With space to put your things and a lock and I can finally have untimed water running with normal temperatures!!! Breakfast was good, cereal (cornflakes, rice bubbles and all bran?), toast, butter, jams, cheese, ham, cream cheese, cucumber and tomato. This dorm was huge, I felt like I was in a hospital. It was spooky. Silent. But I can hear everything when people walked/talked.

title: Not so good
text: The hostel is well located, a couple of tube stations away from Westminster. There is also the bus option on the stop right in front of the hostel. Shower is very small. There is no power socket near the beds. The staff is friendly and very helpful when it comes to buying tickets to attractions.

title: Individual room with a bunk bed
text: I spent one night in London on my way back home. I shared the individual room with a friend. The hostel is close to a bus stop from which there are several options to move around London. The check in process was quick and we could even get a room earlier than the official check in time. You have to bring your own towel or rent it by leaving a deposit. The room was quite small and really hot since the windows were set in a way to limit its opening (perhaps for security reasons). We stayed on the 2nd floor and the noise in the corridor was terrible. Also, we were next to a fire door in the middle of the corridor, and people opening it all night long didn't make it any easy to get to sleep. The shower plate was fine, but the sink was smaller than the ones found on the airplanes. The wifi signal is available only in the common areas, but it is advised on the website. The check in time is at 3 like most hotels, but the check out time is at 10. I had never been to a place where you had to leave the room at 10. It is most likely that I won't stay there again in the future. Despite the positive evaluation I saw when I was booking the room, the price/service/comfort relation is far from being optimal in my opinion.

title: just what we needed
text: We booked a double room as we were up early the next morning to recruit young adults for camp america then off home to Spain. The room and en-suite bathroom were extremly clean, bed was comfortable and the reception staff were nice and polite. We got what we payed for and was pleased (although the room was very hot ). The only thing that i wasn´t keen on (being a young adult female) was there were plenty of older foriegn men staying at Restup London, I thought the RestUp London catered more for young travelers/tourist..etc this being said it was not a problem, just merely an observation.

title: OK for a night
text: Shared a quad room with sink and shower. Nice looking reception and dining area. Beds were comfortable, but the room was a little dusty and could have been cleaner. Staff didn't seem very helpful. Wouldn't stay again.

title: Average
text: You will get for what you will pay. Small rooms, but very clean. Staff not much helpfull, especily that guy at the night shift which he wasn't british for sure. He wouldn't help me with my lost luggage at all. Good price and location not bad as well.

title: You get what you pay for, in a good way
text: Very decent hostel, clean and well maintained, helpful staff at the reception, warm showers, rooms were pretty standard but were warm and clean. Only things I'd complain about are pretty minimal, the beds were squeaky and that kind of stuff, showers were a bit annoying as well, you have to press the button every minute to keep it going but you can get used to that.

title: The Bag and Beyond
text: I had a perfect 2 night stay here, everyone was so accomodating and the bed was comfy. Only downside i would say is there wasnt enough activities for bags like myself to participate in. 10/10 - would definitely stay again, may even bring more bags with me! Kind Regards, The Black Bag.

title: My favourite Hostel in London
text: First of all, Sometimes I stay with friends in that leave in Zone 3 or 4 sometimes even 6 or 7 haha I dunno why is those Zones consider London, anyways, but because is quite difficult to get a ride on public transport after 12 midnight I book a hostel in central London. Every time that I visit London specially in weekends I used to stay here but tbh I never sleep there I usually come back to my room at 7am and at 9 am I'm up for breakfast lol. But the last time I stayed here it was ok. Some people might not like to share dorms but honestly I really don't mind, never had a problem with people staying there. In fact I had met people from other country and they join me for a pint or party in Soho. But if I need some privacy I will book an entire suite for me. Rooms are always clean and with clean linen, toilets and showrooms are ok. Is a cheap hostel I think I paid each night like £10. The perks of the Hostel is that's located in Elephant & Castle, Zone1 which is great because you are like 10 min away from Charing Cross, Embankment and 7 min away from Waterloo Train Station. Only a 5 min walk from the Hostel to the Tube Station and that's all. Very centric and cheap for a Hostel in London Zone 1. Highly recommended for solo traveller who are exploring The UK. Also you have a nice view of The Shard.

title: Good value
text: This hotel, while not the largest room, was CLEAN, shower was hot, wifi worked. My son & I stayed here for 5 nights. The price was right. We had more money to spend on other things in London. Not a bad walk from the Tube.

title: Average hostel
text: Stayed here for 1 night in an 8 bed mixed dorm. Place was reasonably clean and located quite centrally despite not being the best area. Bathroom in room was way too small. For the prices I would still recommend.

title: 2 showers later and I still feel dirty. Location a nightmare.
text: The shower was so dirty none of us could use it, and I have travelled South East Asia so I don't have stupidly high standards! Our window wouldn't shut which given the constant shouting from directly outside was not ideal. You have to pay £5 to use a towel, each! One of the bed sheets had what looked like a large blood stain on it. The vending machine stole our money and staff just shrugged and laughed. The room was so small that we could not all be off the bed at the same time. It was so claustrophobic, you couldn't fit any luggage in and there was no room to manoeuvre. There was no ventilation at all which meant that with that many people in the room it was unbearable. The tiny window did nothing. The noise went on until 5am, which was fine, but it then started again at 7am. I think we could have coped had it been dirt cheap, but we paid £81 for this when we could have got a reasonable hotel room for less if we had travelled a little, in future we would always do that. This seemed like an easy option but totally backfired. Perhaps if you are a hardened traveller then this is OK but for us it is definitely somewhere we will never return! 2 showers later and I still feel dirty. I wish I had taken photos but I just couldn't get out quick enough! Also it is not easy to get back here at night from lots of places, we had the option of 3 nightbuses or a £50 taxi.

title: The worst place ever
text: This place is complete rip off!!! We paid 84 Pounds a night (room for 2 people) for HORRIBLE hole, not a room. No carpet, no closet, no heater, no hangers. There is no other choice, you just have to leave all your staff on dirty floor. No towels, oh yeah!! You can lend them for 2 Pounds....And deposit for one key is 10 POUNDS (they won´t even bother to give you 2 keys). Tiny toilet with shower...Charges and rules for everything. The only luck was we just stayed there for 5 hours...I am working in hotel industry for years, went around many hotels, lived in hostel, but I´ve never seen something like this before. I honestly feel robbed. I expected something very, very basic, but not for this money.

title: Great hostel, but invest in an en-suite
text: Had a great couple of nights here. The receptionists were unfailingly helpful and friendly, despite it being very busy with hardly a moment to think. It's got a nice international atmosphere, although it's sad nowadays how people bury themselves in their phones and tablets as soon as they arrive. The surrounding area is --- how can I put it -- "interesting" but there's plenty of places to eat and drink if you don't fancy the very good value cafeteria in the hostel itself. It's on a main road so traffic noise is unavoidable. I'd also advise people to pay a bit more for an en-suite as the communal shower areas on my floor didn't look particularly inviting. One rather confusing thing is that this hostel is also called "Borough Rooms" on some websites. That's slightly misleading as it's definitely in Elephant and Castle, not Borough.

title: Lovely staff
text: A five star review goes to the lovely staff, in particular the night manager Alex, as I work night's it has been lovely to have someone so helpful and lovely to converse with very charming and he's made my stay pleasurable I've also seen his attentive positive attitude with all other guests.

title: Good spot
text: Spent 3 nights here and was quite happy with facilities - comfy/warm bed and hot showers. Wifi seemed to drop out frequently which was annoying. Great location meant lots of attractions within walking distance - if you had your walking shoes! Close to public transport too. Lots of school groups stayed here so was pretty hectic at times. Staff all friendly and I would stay here again.

title: Not good
text: Our experience at Rest Up was incredibly disappointing. We opted for a private room, sleeping two and with it's own en suite. Location, fantastic, so easy to get to.....but...located on a main road which attracts a huge number of flogs revving their engines all hours of the night. The room was clean...but....of course it was, it probably took 2 minutes to vacuum. It's the smallest room I've ever slept in, ever. And that includes the en suite. We had two carry on suitcases, and the room was so cramped, when we were getting ready in the mornings, we had to put our suitcases in the hallway to allow us enough room to move. We were up what felt like a dozen flights of stairs, and with the lift being broken the entire duration of our stay (despite assurances when we checked in that it would be fixed the next day). No stars to the staff, who, despite having half a dozen sitting around reception joking with each other, no offer to assist with our bags. We had to make our own beds when we got to our room (which considering the number of staff being paid to mull about, was a real shame). The mattress was plastic, like something you'd take camping. And fixed sheets wouldn't go amiss. Also, considering the price, it's mental the money grubbing. Arrive before check in, you have to pay to keep your stuff safe. First place I've ever stayed at that profiteered off a storage room. Then, 'rent a towel', when you're spending as much as we were on a bed, least they could do was throw one in with the sheets. Shower in the en suite had a defective shower head, which we alerted to reception day 1, again, assured they'd get someone to look into it right away...no sign of any fix by check out, no offer to be moved rooms, so despite having paid extra for an en suite, we showered in the communal bathroom. The decor was tacky, shoot the person(s) whose decision it was to buy 500 Banksy decals and slap them onto every possible surface. Expressed a few of my grievances to the reception on our way out, a shrug of the shoulders and we were out of there. Service, facilities and attitude towards guests = Poor.

title: Comfortable stay.
text: I stayed in a eight beds dorm and had shared bathrooms and toilets. The beding was clean and the double deck bed was a bit old so everytime I sat down on my bed made a noisy sound. My roommates were quiet so I was a bit awkward. There was a window but my first night was too warm and a window was not enough to cool down the air. The price was reasonable but the breakfast was a bit disappointed. I would suggest you have breakfast at the corner pub nearby the Elephant and Castle underground.

title: Lucky, if you don't have to share
text: We stayed here for one night in a shared dorm. No one showed up and we had the room for us. The elevator wasn't working though and the way the to the top floor is like climbing the mount everest. It's a very basic room with a very small sink and just the beds. It was alright for one night. I would like to mention that the staff is really friendly and really helpful. We went to the reception at 00.30 and a good spirited staff member helped us out.

title: Very, very basic...
text: We stayed for one night for work, as we needed to be as central to London as possible. After staying in hostels before, I was expecting a very basic room, but it was even more basic than I could imagine... The room was very tiny and uncomfortable.The bedsheets were damp (the bed was unmade) and covered in a thick soap. Staff at reception were very helpful in exchanging the sheets quickly, but the replacements were still covered in detergent and it was very irritating for your eyes at night time. Staff also spoke many languages and were very helpful to guests. There is a nice lounge area with wifi included. Overall, I would not recommend this hostel, unless you needed a very basic place to sleep at night.

title: Rubbish
text: It's quite rare that I have a bad hostel experience. Mainly because I've stayed in a lot of hostels around the world and tend to go with the attitude that it is just a room for the night - so i try not to expect too much. At the rest-up however it was more like a shed than a room, but with not even enough space to swing a cat. The only reason i booked here in the first place is not because i took no notice of all the rubbish reviews, but because my favourite hostels were fully booked and this was the only one left. It probably would have been more fun sleeping homeless for the night. Initial impressions - rubbish. Location is rubbish. Too far to walk from the nearest tube station, through a really grotty part of town, full of homeless people and tatty shops, so we ended up rocking it in an Uber because walking is rubbish. Building looks more like a prison and the inside is not much better. Staircase needs a few licks of paint. I find it hard to believe that this place has had a recent refurb... Only thing that can pass as new is the security gate outside that requires a passcode to get in. Not much help when you're trying to check in and are locked out. On check in staff were really miserable. Obviously everyone is entitled to have a bad day now and again but the chap on reception looked like he was on the verge of ending it all. No details given about the wifi. Got to the room and discovered this was because wifi is non-existent. Wifi only available in the downstairs communal area - which explains why half the hostel were sat on top of each other near reception. Before actually getting to the room we had to hike up six flights of stairs because the lift was broken along with everything else in the hostel. The room (we had a twin) - probably the smallest room in the world. Was also a boiling hot day - but no air conditioning in the room and the only window in there would only open by a crack due to the amount of security chains on it. So we had to wedge the door open with a shoe to get some air in there before we died of suffocation. Bathroom - rubbish. Not sure it can be called an en-suite as this sounds a bit pretentious for what it actually is. Take off the door and its just a loo and worlds smallest shower squashed into the worlds smallest room. No towels provided in the room. Not usually an issue however most hostels do offer free towels and those that don't are always offered to us by staff on reception. Not here... and I forgot to ask for them on our return back later in the evening and couldn't be bothered to take the pilgrimage to reception again in the morning, so had to just dry off with a shirt instead. Shower didn't even work properly. The hook that holds the shower head in place was broken, so it kept flopping down towards the wall. Had to try and wash my hair one handed whilst holding the shower head in place. Couldn't get the temperature right either, as to change it from hot to cold you have to press a button in, but due to it being chrome its slippy when wet making it impossible to function! Completely impractical. The worst bit of my stay here was the fire alarm that went off not once, not twice but THREE times between 04.15 and 04.30 in the morning, waking everyone up. Worst nights sleep ever. Check out was at 10, but i'd been awake since the fire alarmS going off at 04.15 - so that was my day ruined. On check out i thought it would be nice to go and sit out on the rooftop chairs and chill out for a bit - maybe get some sleep. But no. Reception stated the rooftop area was closed due to 'circumstances'. No explanation given. Didn't fancy breakfast here as it looked rubbish, so got a bottle of pop out of the vending machine which i needed to re-mortage my house for. Reception also kept hold of a tenner for the keycard to the room. You get this back if you don't lose it however a tenner to replace a bit of plastic is a bit extreme. Never had to do this before at any hostel I've stayed in. Possibly one of the worst hostels I've ever stayed in. Everything about it was rubbish. Won't be staying here again.

title: Budget Hostel in the centre of London
text: I actually booked 4 mixed dorm no breakfast but apparently no room for me so they gave me 6 mixed dorm with shared bathroom outside and free breakfast. That was OK as the 6 mixed room was bigger than 4 mixed room. The hostel has an elevator, lounge and nice lobby room with all UK Flags and red telephone box.

title: Dreadful. Broken bogs, failed wifi, wretched attitude
text: My feelings about this hostel weren't helped by the fact that 'single room, sleeps one' turned out to describe a bed in an eight-bed dorm. They need to get their advertising right. It was significantly more expensive than other places I've stayed in London which were much better, and considering the location (not particularly nice), isn't worth it. Trying to relieve myself in the morning was a challenge. One toilet was completely broken with water all over the floor. Another had no toilet paper. There weren't really enough toilets for the number of people, either. Many of the facilities were not clean. Attention to detail... well, my bed had a sheet. No pillow. What's that about? Getting about is a pain. The hostel has one lift. For about 400 people. That's dumb. The wifi is impossible to use

title: Recommended for its location
text: Bad service to guests. we had a double bed room. it was very small but clean. there wasn't any closet. - the locker room costs 3£ per day - towel costs 2£ + 3£ deposit - key card has a 10£ deposit the room is told to be en-suite but there were only a shower and a little washbasin - NO WC. TOO MUCH NOISE DURING THE NIGHT THANKS TO GERMAN GUESTS ON OUR FLOOR.

title: Noooooo. Not worth it
text: absolutely awful. Good location is what sold us. But we came back the second night and there were random people in our beds. The man checking us in made a mistake and overbooked our room so in the middle of the night we had to move all our stuff to another. Not only did they refuse to accept fault but they wouldn't even exchange us a cheap breakfast for our troubles. NOT WORTH IT.

title: Hot and sweaty rooms, wifi barely works
text: The rooms were poorly ventilated and very warm, was perspiring as soon as i got to bed. Wifi could not be received from my room and only works intermittently at the main area. But staff were friendly and helpful.

title: Very good and adequately accessible for wheelchairs.
text: Restup London was a very nice hostel. It's a very large hostel with what I believe was five stories. Outside looks very old and beautiful. Inside, there are contemporary touches. They have brightly colored sky light/windows in the checkin area. The lounge has a television and plenty of seats, which are often occupied. There's also a coffee bar with decent prices. One draw back for me is that the kitchen closes at 20:00. (I eat late). The dining area is a nod to Charlie Chaplin with huge images of him and was completed with bowler hat pendant shades. I use a wheelchair so accessibility is a huge concern. Upon my arrival, I discovered the lift was broken. The staff made sure that I found a mixed dorm on the first floor that was open enough for my chair. At the end of the day, it's a hostel. Rowdy tourist that make sleep difficult at times. Inexpensive rates ensure that it is very busy. They do have a proper accessible bathroom that has fully accessible toilet and shower. There was no additional charge for sheets, which was a nice change from other hostels who charge for everything. The breakfast was an additional charge. 2.99£ for cereal toast, coffee and juice. I think you could have a hard boiled egg as well. For 4.99£, you get an English Breakfast which include two sunny side up eggs, baked beans, sausage and bacon. Charges to be aware of are 5£ for a towel (2£ charge and 3£ deposit that is returned when the towel is returned) and a 10£ Room key deposit that must be in cash. Lockers are 2£ to 3£, depending on the size. My only complaint was that the wifi was hit or miss. It didn't work for me outside of the main lobby. Not by the vending machines, near the lockers or in my room. Overall I was very satisfied with my stay. It was the best hostel I've stayed in to date. I would recommend it to a friend.

title: Nice lounge, prison rooms
text: I stayed in the 8 bed mixed dorm and was not happy with the room whatsoever. The bathroom was not clean, and neither were the hallway bathrooms. The rooms felt extremely cramped and looked like a prison cell. The main area of the hostel was nice with some places to sit, but not enough. The wifi only reached to the lobby, so you couldn't even use it in rooms or the large cafeteria.

title: Nice and not expecive.
text: The hostel is almost in the center and is great for sightseeing. Had a room with bathroom and I was quite pleased. It was clean and comfortable. The bed was really comfy. The TV room was really nice, and the breakfast was ok. The only thing that I would change is more staff at the check in/out counter. That was a bit slow, but managable.

title: Stayed whilst site seeing London
text: My, my partner and two sons (17 &14) booked a quadruple here for our site-seeing weekend in London. When we arrived we were told that there had been a mix up with the rooms and we were instantly worried what we had walked into. However, we were delighted to find out that we had been upgraded to 2 double rooms, one on the second floor and one on the third. This was perfect for us as the boys were old enough to share and it meant we adults had a room to ourselves. The rooms themselves are very small! however, they were clean and comfortable enough for just the night. We were in bunk beds so not exactly built for a romantic stay (as we had expected) but perfect for a cheap stay over on a budget. Kind of like camping but in the warm and with beds.

title: Good Clean Hostal
text: I stayed with friends at the RestUp and was pleasantly surprised. We had two family rooms which were lovley and clean. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. My only gripe was that the thin windows made the room noisy at night.

title: The worst ever
text: Rooms were disgusting and REALLY smelly. The staff was not helpful at all. There were some sketchy people at the lounge and a couple had their notebook stolen. Not safe at all. No internet. No breakfast. AWFUL!

title: terrible atmosphere, I didnt even check in, even though i already paid a deposit
text: Hostel was full of 12 year olds, I would feel any self respecting hostel would deny booking by groups of children. Also you needed to pay for everything, adapters, lockers and as a cherry on top it is not allowed to drink alcohol inside the hostel. Since I was already waiting 30minutes to check in I decided this was the last drop and cancelled my booking.

title: Totally a mess!
text: One of the worst hostels i've ever been not because of the room or the accomodation, in general,the rooms were ok, the hostel has a nice atmosphere,very colourful and a nice decoration but because of the stuff especially the receptionists.One was worse than the other,the first one was really tired to help us the lady was really rude and aggresive and the third one was helpless. They charged us the double for the breakfast and they didn't gave our money back but they told us that we could have our breakfast for free the next day! (but what if we don't want to eat breakfast in your hotel?) my opinion:disorganised and unprofessional!

title: How to get sick
text: A terrible nightmare. First of all, it’s unbelievable that there wasn’t a heater in our room. We had to sleep wearing a vest, a t-shirt, pyjamas and a pullover to keep us alive. There wasn’t also space to hang up our coats after a very rainy day in London. Of course now we are sick. During the night it was impossible to sleep well: it seemed that thousands of people were screaming in our room. If you want to use the lift, you should wait for hours and hours. It’s not so comfortable when your room is on the 4th floor. It’s unbelievable that if you want to leave your luggage just for 2 hours before checking in, you should pay three or four pounds. We had to pay so much money (100€/70£ per night ) without any good facilities. Don’t choose this hostel unless you are a masochist. It is simply not worth it.

title: Average
text: Considering it's a hostel, and we gotta keep in mind that it involves noise, people coming in and out of the room at different hours it was comfortable, mostly clean and the staff was mostly friendly and helpfull. The cons were, every single day some people wrongly took a bed that was already taken, in a room that was supposed to be full, so when we came in to the reception to work it out they always ask the name to "verify the reservation" so considering that we did check in we shouldn't be doing this on a daily basis... The beds should be numbered or named to prevent this kind of thing from happening.

title: It was ok for one night
text: It was ok for one night and only for sleeping. Otherwise the place was quite dirty for me, and not very comfortable. The shower was warm and that was good thing. THe are where the hostel is is TERRIBLE. Check-in was after 3pm, which was awful to wait. I was tired and I wanted to go to the shower and then they told me that the check-in is like after 3 o clock.... -.-

title: Don't bother unless you're in a pinch.
text: We came to Restup London for 4 nights. We only ended up staying 3. We didn't care that we lost the money on the last day, we just wanted out. Why? Because as we entered, windows were boarded up (turns out to be a fire exit - not the main entrance), and the staff was very non helpful, they processed us in, gave us our key ( watch out 10 pound deposit) and told us that they had lockers that were available for 24 hours, single use only. The price, 3 pounds per use. No lockers in the room. And that can make you uncomfortable in the 20 person dorm. Another issue was the cleanliness, there was a total lack of it, I hesitated and procrastinated every time I had to go to the washroom, which apparently are unisex?! There where wads of hair stuck to the ground in the showers that did work. Now the most frustrating point

title: Good for value
text: Very nice location, 20 minutes walk to Big Ben. There are a few markets and fast food restaurants nearby. There are only 2 toilets for the whole floor. They are cleaned only once a day I guess so it stinks. Stinks a lot. There are only a few sockets so it could be a problem to find a free one in a 20 beds room. Wifi is overcrowded so do not expect it would work when you need it.

title: Small room and poor food!
