text: my husband and i arrived at this hotel and from the outside and location on norfolk square was quite impressed......however once we stepped inside we realised what a mistake we had made by booking this hotel, the smallest so called double room in the attic which had the smallest bed in it, a window that did not open, wet bed linnen and then......vermin poision boxes under the bed! but that was not the end of the horrors mouse/rat?? excrement on the bed and floor!!! we instantly complained to reception and asked to be moved so was then sent to the sister hotel "the metro" which is just down the road....nightmare number two!! was given a room with three single beds in, a t.v that did not work,a window that did not close with ripped and moth eaten curtains! breckfast is disgusting and our stay with theese hotels can only be described as a very expensive SQUAT!!! do not be fooled by the photos of the rooms!

title: The short walk from Paddington is NOT worth the savings
text: Room was old, tiny and dirty and scruffy- lots of mold in the bathroom. Light in the bathroom was so bad that my husband literally took his flashlight in there so that he could shave. Lots of train noise. Continental breakfast was basically four different bread rolls with two pats of butter and a box of apple juice. NOT worth any savings you may have - you leave feeling very grubby and in need of a shower and a good nights sleep.

title: So awful we didn't stay here!
text: This hotel was booked months ago, 2 double rooms and a triple room for a girlie weekend away. When we arrived we were told that there had been a leak which was in the process of being repaired and that were weren't able to have our original rooms. We asked to be shown the rooms we were now being allocated, before checking in. We were taken down a very narrow steep staircase and along a corridor strewn with mattresses etc. to a dark and dingy basement where we were shown a dark and dingy room with 3 double beds crammed in it! There was a workman in the 'ensuite bathroom' with a pot of paint, about to paint the extremely mouldy looking ceiling! 6 of us were expected to sleep in this room, the 7th was going to be given another room and it was suggested that some of us could share her bathroom! We were then told that the boiler was also undergoing repairs. Those of us who hadn't already fled the hotel in horror by this point were told that we would be given a very good discount on the price for the inconvenience. The discount was to be a reduction of £10 per night! The rest of us grabbed our bags and escaped too...

title: Its location is the only plus point
text: Located within a minutes walk of Paddington its ideal, but unfortunately that's pretty much all that's positive, the reception is a single desk in a broom cupboard, the decor is very outdated, dark and shabby as are all public areas and the room, the furniture being a miss match. The rooms are tiny and scruffy, bathroom was functional but again in need of updating. the Hotel is a 2 star and i suppose cheap but its pretty dreadful. The staff are scruffy and abrupt, check in wasn't too bad, at check out we were treated poorly almost to the point of being rude, best advice, pay a few extra pounds and go somewhere else

title: Complete negligence: DO NOT RISK IT
text: TLD: Nearly broke my ankle, no first aid, no staff, management deny any negligence, refused to refund. The small, hotel occupies an old worn out building and their narrow stairs are very uneven. On my way down these stairs the morning of my stay I seriously twisted my ankle (later diagnosed to be torn ligaments in my foot). While I was in shock my friend went to the staff to ask for some ice as I had 'fallen down the stairs'. He was offered a bandage and returned empty handed. The member of staff, who management have informed me are all first aid trained, never attended to me. He wasn't even at the desk when I finally limped out of the hotel. This negligence only continued when I contacted management to inform them of the incident and as for my money back. Over the course of a few emails his attitude changed from apologetic to denial. He stated no negligence occurred as an ambulance would have been called if it was required, although his staff were nowhere to be seen. If I had broken a bone I would have sued. Do not stay here, its overpriced, dangerous, and does not care for its clientele.

title: Can laugh it off as an 'experience' if staying 1 night
text: Positives: Paid less than £100 for 4 of us in one room (2 double beds) so got what you paid for. 5/10 minute walk from an underground station which got us to/from the centre of London very quickly. On suite bathroom - clean towels, everything seemed to be clean enough in the room. Staff were friendly. Beds comfortable. Negatives: They failed to tell us we had to climb 3/4 flights of stairs to get to our room which was a pain late at night with lots of luggage - there are no lifts. The room was very small and you barely had room to stand up in the bathroom. The flush mechanism for the toilet fell off after barely touching it. The shower head was broken and so we asked for it to be fixed and came back to find they had just positioned the shower head upright and ended up having to hold the head whilst showering. The mechanism to turn the heating off had broken so we couldn't sleep because we were so hot throughout the night as the heating wouldn't turn off. Not a brilliant location as there was a lot of shouting and possible gunshots heard late at night which was worrying. Basically if you're going on a one night stay to London and don't want to spend a lot of money then I would recommend the hotel as it is in a good location and is sufficiently clean. However wouldn't recommend if you're staying for more than 1 night and DEFINITELY NOT if you're looking for anything more than average in a hotel.

title: it was ok, except of the old floor!
text: I've stayed over here for a few days. I would say that the location is perfect (very near the tube) and the staff is very friendly! The breakfast is ok and enough. (they bring the breakfast to your room which is great. there probably isn't a restaurant over here) But the rooms aren't nice. Our room was clean, but the rooms (we've stayed upstairs) are way too old. The ceiling seems to fall down one time! We've seen the whole profile from the bed from the room above us through the ceiling! that was kind of scary:( The floors are too old and it makes a lot of noise if people were walking on it. So we haven't had a good night rest:(.

title: Awful
text: Small, cramped, dirty, smells. Find an alternative, best part of the stay was leaving! Check in staff very blunt, breakfast served to your room and mostly not edible! Needs updating and cleaning!! Rooms were disgusting not cleaned and dirty bedding, AVOID!!!

title: Average hotel at budget price
text: At a budget price this place is average but i think you can have better options at same price. Hotel is quiet old, Needs to do a lot with furniture,gates etc.Room was quiet ok. Bathroom was better. Got breakfast in room on very exact timing, Manager sitting downside was quiet helpful. Main problem is no lift and you have to take stairs and if you are likely of good area outside room then you will not find any, be to your room only. One postitve thing is it is near to tube station and many restaurants outside it.

title: No, no, no, no, NO! Find an alternative.
text: I am so relieved to be away from this hotel this morning. Though I will feel a whole lot better when I get home this evening and have a shower. I've tried to recall a worst hotel I have stayed in over the past 25 years of work travel and have drawn a blank. This is the worst. Let's start with the good points: Location and staff. - If you need to be near Paddington, this is close by, it is about 500 yards from the station. The hotel is across from a small green square that looked pleasant. The street itself looks nice from the outside with colonnades outside many whitewashed buildings. There are a number of hotels on Norfolk Square. - The staff are friendly. More apologetic than helpful, but friendly nonetheless. The bad points: Moving hotels, moving rooms, upfront payment, cleanliness, atmosphere, shower, bed, window, space, breakfast, reception availability, security safe, stairs and fire safety. - I booked this in a last-minute rush. 5pm on a Tuesday. Actually booked into the Metro Hotel on Craven Road. Upon arrival at the Metro Hotel my heart sank at the small doorway leading to a long flight of stairs with a tatty old wooden reception desk at the top. The person on reception was very friendly but could not find my reservation so called a colleague. He then said he was taking me to another hotel very close by that was better. He kindly took me to Tony's House Hotel which looked better from the outside. I was in a hurry so moving hotels was not ideal at this time for me. - Receptionist at Tony's House Hotel also friendly and seemed very on top of things. However told me they did not have a room available for 45 minutes. This was at around 6pm, so room would not be available until almost 7pm. Explained that I was immediately going out to see a friend and needed somewhere to drop my bags and freshen up. So he put me in a triple room and clearly explained that I would need to move the next day and explained that if I left my bag packed in the morning, they would move it for me. This was all done, so no complaints about doing what they said they would do, but I have an issue with rooms not being available in the hotel to which they have just moved me. - The hotel takes payment on arrival. It's been a while since I have done this. I am not surprised they do. I am sure I would have left earlier if my money had not already been taken. £198 for two nights. - The hotel is beyond tired. It is unclean. The carpets everywhere just look dirty. I am not convinced my bedsheets were washed. The sheets consist of two normal thin white sheets, one covering the mattress, the other to cover you, and then a thicker blanket on top. The thicker blanket was a brown affair and very old, something from the seventies, it may have been clean but everything about it said it was not. The white sheets looked clean but for the first time ever, I checked up close as I had visions of bedbugs... I found a black hair between the sheets. Could have simply been from the cleaner, but added to my growing discomfort at this point. - The shower in my first room (basement) worked well. However the second night I was on the top floor and not so lucky. Had a shower this morning and after getting the temperature right and stepping in the shower simply slowed to a stop after about one minute. It started up again after 30 seconds

title: Very nice and comfortable place to stay
text: The best advantage for us was location - center of London - and so then the price. We enjoyed our stay for one night. The green area in front of the hotel includes ping-pong table with free equipment.

title: Tony´s hotel
text: Good hotel on a good place with good price. Great location with Norfolk park and close to city centre. It is without restaurant so breakfast are delivered to your room, and mainly sweet only. But good restaurants are around too so not a big deal. Clean and quiet hotel with friendly stuff.

title: Stayed for Hyde Park Festival - great!
text: Staff were really friendly and helpful. Room was nice (room 9) with balcony, clean bathroom. Bed a little hard but would definitely stay here again. Great value for money.

title: Horrible
text: When we first got there the guy who worked in the reception wouldn't open the door for us even though he had monitors in his office showing him a family standing outside with their suitcases. The time was 6pm. We were five and got the smallest room possible. It was so small that we couldn't even place our suitcases anywhere. We had to take turns opening the suitcases and then place them on top of each other. It was not clean at all and there was dust all over the floor. When we got back to the hotel at night the room was literally like a sauna. It was nice of them to heat the rooms but not necessary at all. We asked for an extra towel to dry our hands with -didn't get one. The pillows were so hard that I had to sleep on my fluffy sweater. You can hear the vibrations of the tube so loud that it woke us up at 6am. The breakfast was served in plastic bags and were too sweet. The only good thing was the location and the staff. It was close to the Paddington Station, bus stations and restaurants. The guy who worked there was very polite and helpful. Wouldn't recommend this hotel if you're staying more than one night and with larger groups. There were a lot of things that happened that I just don't even have the time to write.

title: BEWARE OF THIS SCAM HOTEL
text: I booked a triple room for my family during our recent trip to London on this hotel through Expedia because it is the cheapest hotel I found near Paddington station. Good thing I did not avail of the prepaid lowest rate. Our nightmare began as soon as we arrived. We arrived early but since check in time is after 2 PM only, so we have to leave our luggage to have our lunch first. When we got back for check in, that is when the scam begins. First, the guy ( mediterranian guy) in the reception room told us that there is some problem with our room toilet so he needs to move us to another hotel which we need to walk again to get there. Second, he said that if I paid in Credit card, there will be a 10% charge on top of my original resevation rate but no charges if I paid cash. I questioned why there is no mention on the expedia site about that, he just said that is their policy. He even told me that he can walk me to the nearby ATM station to withdraw cash if i want. I just told him I will do it by myself. I actually saw other hotels neraby around northfolk square while looking for the hotel. So I know there are vacancies on teh other hotels, so I checked them out. I went to the nearby Belvedere hotel which is one of the first hotel I was considering and the reception guy, offered me a lower rate for their triple room. So I decided to go back to the hotel and told the receptionist that I am cancelling my reservation. He told me that I will be charged for one night for the room, which I argued with him that they have no available room for me on their hotel but on anothe hotel only. Anyway, I was not worried because the card I used for the reservation is a cancelled card already we left the hotel and moved to Belvedere hotel. Next time I would rather explore the place and get a better walk in rate on the other hotels nearby.

title: A pleasant stay...
text: Arrived here drained, but was happy with the friendliness of the staff and the cosiness of the hotel. Rooms: clean and comfortable, Location: outstanding. Perfect hotel for my short trip in London.

title: Value for money
text: I stayed here last night the cheq guy on reception was great couldn't do enough to help yes a bit of dust but 2 double beds your own shower toilet and continental breakfast servered what time you want tea and coffee for what worked out to £20 each it was great .People say you get what you pay for well in London for what I payed I'd say I got a lot more thank.

title: cheap and close to everything
text: This is basic and cheap hotel. A short walk from the center of London near Hyde Park. Czech helpful receptionist. Room small and pure. Breakfast served around nine hours consisting of: biscuits, croissants, yogurt, juice, cereal bar, cheese spread, butter.

title: Good price/value
text: In October 2011 we went with two adult and two kids to London. Great location, close to Paddington, quiet at night. Rooms not that big, but sufficient. Breakfast included and brought to the rooms at 8:00. Not a ***** hotel, but given the price, it is good. Would go there again. Only pity, was that we had a room at the 4th floor and there is no elevator, only a very tight stair.

title: Oh My God!!! Was that a big mouse or a rat??
text: That was one of the worst hotels I have ever seen! The only good thing about it is the location and the fact that all the day you are out because you don't want to be in that hotel. Very old and smelly furniture. The rooms are very small, the windows are not secured and you get to hear strange noices wondering if it is some kind of mouse or a rat trying to find food! I don't think the bed sheets were clean either.

title: Simply average.
text: We stayed for a few nights, and even though the first nights were cheap, the last nights were excessively expensive for such a basic hotel. The level of cleanliness left much to be desired. The bed however was comfortable. The breakfast was all industrial cakes and cookies, and the instant coffee was cheap and bad. Overall, average. Can't say much more.

title: Spotless
text: was originally booked into the Metro Hotel but when arrived was informed that our room had a leak and would have to go to their sister hotel. We were escorted there. First impressions when you walked in not very good and we were given a room right by reception. I must admit when we walked into our room I was pleasantly surprised, it was spotless, small but who needs a large room in London your out most of the time. Lovely white towels, tea and coffee facilities, fridge, iron and tv. Although the room was right by the reception noise didn't disturb us. Only the light rumble of the tube, which didn't disturb us either. Reakfast was provided the following morning which I also wasn't expecting much. 9 a.m as requested a tray was delivered to our door, 3 types of rolls, cheese spread, butter, orange juice, biscuits, pineapple, yogurt, cereal bar, for 2. I would stay here again.

title: dirty place with crazy staff
text: we've stayed here for a long weekend and luckily we did not spend much time in the hotel! our room was really dirty (with mice traps under the bed and hairs in the bed sheets). breakfast was good but being obliged to eat it in the room with no table nor chairs is not ideal at all. the staff was kind of crazy, trying to be funny but rather sounding creepy. the good point was surely the hotel location.

title: Very handy location
text: We stayed here because it was close to Paddington Station, The hop on hop off bus stop was at the corner of the street, about 100 meters, Paddinging station about another 100 more. Walking distance to Hyde park etc. Room was very comfortable, we had the room on the ground floor next to reception no problems at all. Breakfast was enough that we were able to pack half to have for lunch, friendly staff.

title: Fantastic
text: its in very good location...most important is the hotel and rooms are very clean...their staff are very helpful..everyday they gave room service which was great..i must say this is one of proper and pefect hotel in central london that gives everything in great value....

title: Pretty basic hotel
text: We booked at Tony's House just for a night's stop over as it seemed value for money. On the plus side is it's location. A few minutes from Paddigton station which in general is very convenient to travel around London. The staff was quite nice and helpful. Would I go back? Well, definitely not with children and only if I couldn't find something else. The inside needs attention and refurbishment, small spaces as almost everywhere in London, cleaning is not their top priority and they need to do something about the packed breakfast.

title: Our Tonys experience....
text: So..... As seems to be the norm, after now reading the reviews on tripadvisor, we checked into the metro hotel only to be told that there was a problem with our room. I say checked in, what actually happened is we walked up some stairs to find that a man had created a "shanty town style" reception atop a staircase... We told we would be moved and were guided on a tour of the sights of paddington before getting to Tony' House. We were checked into Tonys, given a key and sent on our way to find our room crystal maze style. Once we found our room, on the top floor, we did not find a crystal but we were horrified to find that us four blokes were to stay in two "double" (sort of) beds. We told Tony that we didnt really want double beds but he told us that there was nothing he could do other than offer us an extra set of bed sheets...... The room was no bigger than your average four man tent and there was filth decorating the surfaces. We dropped off our things and headed to Wembley regardless thinking it "is what it is..." Upon waking the next morning each of us experienced the "bi polar shower" mentioned in previous posts and the 3rd degree burns as a result. Having chance to have a look about we too discovered stains on the bed throws, grubby curtains and a manky net curtain at half mast loosely draped at the window. Some of the more irregular features of the room consisted and a boarded up radiator behind the beds and a pleasant canvas print of a lakeside scene on the wall literally hidden behind the wardrobe. Our final suprise was to come upon checking out. We headed to reception to find a note saying "leave your key on the chair," dropped the key and turned to see that concealed above the reception desk was, what can only be described, a big hole in the wall with two single mattresses, upon inspection this was either the truly crappest holtel room in London or a hideout where the manager/receptionist bunks down....... (See photo). Never to return again, a true Mickey Mouse establishment!!!

title: London break
text: We stayed at this b & b from mon 20th-wed 22nd Aug. We had the family room for 5 people which was based on the lower floor so no view but this did not bother us as we only used the room as a place to sleep. We found the room clean & the staff very friendly & helpful. The breakfast was brought to our room at the time we asked for,it consisted of bread rolls,jams,cakes,crackers/cheese,yoghurts & juices. There was a lot to eat so what we didnt have for breakfast we took to eat during the day while we were sightseeing. The room was quite small with 2 double beds & a single,but was fine for what we needed & the price we paid. Some nice pubs & restaurants right by which weren't over priced. Great location for seeing London & we will be using this hotel when we come next time. If you want 4/5* accomodation pay 4/5* prices,but if all you want is a clean friendly place to sleep dont hesitate to book here.

title: Bedbugs!
text: Room was small but clean (except the blanket) and the hotel was very close to Paddington. Since all we needed was a place to sleep, we were satisfied with the hotel UNTIL I found about 10 bites on my body that REALLY hurt. Since it has been below zero in temperature lately, I am pretty sure that they were BEDBUGS.

title: It is exactly what you pay for
text: The location of the Hotel is perfect, near from the Tube and a lot of buses stops. The breakfast is nice, it is not buffet. The receptionist is really friendly, we were very happy with the choice, it is exactly what you pay for.

title: No complaints at all
text: First of all let's remember we are in a prime location here - a stones throw from Paddington Station. Secondly let's remember we are in a prime location in London. Thirdly, let's manage our expectation when it comes to budget accommodation in a prime location in London....?! I wanted to stay close to Paddington, I wanted budget accommodation, I wanted a late checkout, and I wanted a single room price (i.e. less than a double as I was alone). I tried many direct approaches to hotel's in Norfolk Square and encountered many language issues (I am English), a couple of "we don't do single rooms, goodbye!" with no alternative suggestions, many "of course you cannot check out late unless you book for 2 nights!" - overall general unhelpfulness at worst and mediocraty at best. Tony's House made a very, very fair offer of a single room with private facilities and a 4 pm (repeat 4pm) check out for 65 pounds - and made the offer politely and efficiently. My expectations were set - tiny room, basic in every single respect and probably a heap of stairs to climb. I just prayed for cleanliness - but all I was to do there was sleep from late, til late after a lively Mayfair party. Upon arrival, check in was polite and with a smile - room not ready, but I was early, so no complaint. I was also told it would be worth my wait as I was getting a large room. I was further told just before i went to my room that any issue at all, no matter how small, to report it and all and any measures would be taken to rectify. He then told me I was on the 7th floor (I knew there was no elevator) which stopped me in my tracks - my look of dread did the trick and he guffawed delightedly and said "Not really, second floor!" - sense of humour as well!!! The room had 3 singles and a double bed - this was no single room - and there was still room to walk around! Decor plain but good, carpet fine, beds fine, bedding crisp and clean, and clean towels and basic toiletries on every bed. Bathroom was of the plastic pod variety but more spacious than others like this I have experienced mainly in French autoroute hotels. Window gave good light, and it opened and shut! Breakfast was delivered to room on a tray and was plentiful if not of the highest quality "continental fayre". But again - value for money. As I started the review, I will end - No complaints at all - well done Tony's House for the service and the great value for money in a superb location in London.

title: [--] / Una fogna
text: I was given Room 20, top floor, they said "double", continental breakfast included. First of all, it wasn't a double room, for obvious physical reasons. If I was able to penetrate the matter and walk through that filthy large single bed, or crawl up the ceilings like a spider, then ok, it'd be a double. But reality was that there wasn't even space to open the door to access it, unless the single chair was removed. What about this single chair? Well, this is one of the disgraces: the "breakfast" is served on a hospital tray at your door, as they don't have a breakfast room, there are no hot drinks served, there's no milk etc...They never state that, they don't say it in any of the hotel descriptions. Also, at the check in where they steal your money upfront, they ask you "at what time would you like the breakfast?" diverting the subject from the real scenario you will have to deal with: when you receive this tray (if you are lucky enough for nobody to have stamped their foot on it) you have to find a space in your room to eat the crap randomly laid on it. Hence the single chair (in a double room??) that you can't open if you have the bathroom door open. Oh, dear, the bathroom...but that's another story.... I'm sorry, I've already lost track of the appalling details of my staying in this [--] and in fact this description can't give justice to my immense effort in not pissing on the carpet (nobody would have noticed or cleaned it) after the manager refused to refund me the second night, which I decided to spend somewhere else.

title: Tony's House Hotel
text: Excellent location in Norfolk Square, very close to Paddington railway and tube stations. Staff very pleasant and always keen to help. Had a couple of minor inconveniences but nothing to make me complain. Decent enouhg continental-style breakfasts, delivered to my room each morning and a very comfortable bed. I will probably stay here again as I liked the good service and bustling area, plenty of places to eat and drink.

title: Ideal location, clean place, with a horrible breakfast
text: The hotel is located in a quiet and beautiful street near Paddington Station. The location is ideal for people on a short visit exploring London. Rooms are clean and staff helpful and polite. The breakfast, however, was a big disappointment. No dining room - the breakfast was delivered on the door and consisted of sweets and white, cold half baked bread rolls. With 5 people in the room and absolutely no extra place and no suitable table, eating breakfast became something next to painful gymnastics. We ate out.

title: Nice stay
text: We have been offered a room on the first floor. It was not big but clean. The bathroom was clean and new. The location is great, because it is just a few hundred metros from Hide Park. The breakfast is commercial but the quality is good. The stuff is helpful.

title: Family of five
text: If you are looking for a place to lay your head while doing a whirlwind tour of London with three kids and not much money, this is the place for you! We just wanted a roof over our heads, and a bed to sleep in, and thats what we got. The decor was not a factor for us, we got the family room which had its own adequate ensuite, with plenty of hot water. The beds were comfy and clean, and the TV worked. Breakfast was prompt, and had handy snack packs and juice boxes which we took with us on our sightseeing. The concierge Martin was fantastic. If you are looking for a laundrymat, there is one on just down the road, opens from 8 to 8. Lots of restaurants, the Hop on Hop off bus is literally just on the corner, the train station is 2 minutes from the front door, the cabs cost @ 12-15 pounds to get around to Oxford St, Notting Hill, Harrods, Kings Cross. The Tube was terrifying for this country Australian, but soon got used to it, unfortunately half the time it was closed!

title: Superb location + friendly stff
text: Superb location. Very friendly and helpful staff right from check in. Janos, one of the helpers, was extremely friendly and welcoming helping me carry my things to my room etc.Nice and comfortable room with comfortable bedding.

title: Perfect
text: Really lovely hotel, helpful staff, large comfy room (little kettle boils really quick). Would definitely stay here again, 5 min walk to tube, sainsbury and a lovely walk through sicilian place and a park on the way here.

title: Great value
text: I've stayed here twice now in April this year and November 2012 on a Sunday night deal from the Grange Hotel website and been really impressed both times. For a Central London hotel, it was very good value for money. I wouldnt say the staff go out of their way, exactly, but nobody is remotely rude, as described on other reviews. The Continental breakfast is absolutely brilliant. I'm not sure I would pay the full price for it, but when included in the deal, definitely worth it.

title: Decent room, good location
text: Needed a central location at a decent (for london) price 5 minutes walk from holborn tube. Secure parking 2 min walk. Not part of hotel so no idea on price. 15-20 walk to theatre land & loads of bars & restaurants. Quiet street & friendly staff. Room spacious & bathroom clean & well maintained. Its multiple converted townhouses so a myriad of fairly narrow corridors & a bit of a maze but no issues really. Room was stuffy when we arrived so left window open & was perfect. No AC that we could see so in summer may be an issue. Otherwise a perfectly acceptable stay. We didn’t have breakfast so can’t comment.

title: Very lovely
text: Very good! When we arrived there was building work across the street and our room was opposite so was really loud. We phoned reception to ask what time they started in the morning but the offered to move us straight away to the back overlooking the gardens! Very helpfully staff.

title: Aug-15
text: Nice hotel, good size family room. Very central location easy walking distance to British Museum, Covent Garden etc. Breakfast was expensive so didn't have this so can't comment, very enjoyable stay. We used as a base for theatre trip to Drury a Lane walked within 15 minutes, we would recommend to others to stay

title: Nice hotel, good rooms, good service
text: I stayed here for work & was pleasantly surprised. My room was really large and the staff were great. The bar in the hotel is tiny although they do have both an indoor & outdoor seating area to enjoy a drink. The continental breakfast was included in the room rate and had everything you would want. Overall a good value hotel for London.

title: nice and clean Hotel in the middle of town
text: The Hotel is in the middle of London and can be easily reached by the tube (Holborn) The people are very friendly and everything was prepared as agreed. The rooms ar quite big and comfortable with a huge bathroom. Everything seems to be very clean.

title: Clarendon't
text: "Who you gonna call?" No one. Our room phone didn't work and no one would come to repair or replace it during our three-night stay. I have read that similar travelers have suffered the same fate. I realize that this is certainly a "first-world problem", but after a long day of travel I like to be able to pick up a hotel room phone and call for food. Having to go downstairs to place the order in person is not convenient or desirable. I brought the matter to the attention of two receptionists, working on two different shifts, but to no avail. We paid approx. $130 US per night. The room was small but adequate, with a bathroom larger than the room might have suggested. The beds were severely uncomfortable. The breakfast was a standard Continental buffet affair: fruits, cereals, cheese, sliced meats, toast, etc. for an eye-popping 17-21 pounds (or approx. $35-40). There are many breakfast options withing walking distance that charge a fraction of the cost of the hotel. The hotel is located just around the corner from the British Museum, and Oxford Street is nearby to provide many shopping opportunities.

title: Great location but scorchingly hot inside
text: Stayed for 3 nights. Location is fantastic only a few mins walk from Covent Garden and theatreland and Oxford St and Regent St. Hotel was great value and the included conti breakfast was lovely. The room was small but clean and functional. The road outside was noisy at night with the window fully open to combat the blistering heat. Building work on a nearby property started at 7am and that was also a source of much noise (will only be mon - fri though and won't last forever). The main problem was that every radiator as on full and it must have been about 35 degrees C in the hotel and this would stop me from returning.

title: clarendon hotel
text: Average hotel, average price. Staff were friendly and helpful. Minor details let it down - bathroom sink plughole didn't drain properly therefore delayed the sink from draining and sink was scummy. Windowsills in the dining area coated in dust.The dining area was very cramped tables so close together that once husband was sat down I had to fetch anything he required from continental breakfast table. Food ok. The room was VERY warm requiring the window to be left fully open all the time which resulted in a disturbed sleep from all the sirens etc. It is in a very good location but I would be tempted to try somewhere different next time.

title: I was very impressed
text: Well situated, good sized room, efficient and well designed bathroom, comfortable bed. Polite and efficient staff, 24 hour room service and bar, the quality of breakfast fully justified the price. If you can get a good price then you won't go wrong with this hotel and whatever you pay you will be comfortable. Highly recommended.

title: Nice hotel with great rooms
text: nice hotel, lovely large room which a big bed, nice décor and lovely big bathroom, It is an ideal situation in London, round the corner is the British Museum and nice pubs and restaurants all in walking distance. We arrived early and our room was ready so didn't have to wait, we stopped 2 nights, and our train back was 3pm they kept our luggage safe most of the day, only issue was the receptionist(s) were frosty

title: Breakfast poor, ridiculous bedroom, not quite sure how they fed away with it
text: Was given room 13, it's in the basement underneath reception. So receptionist in high heels stomping around at 6am not helpful. Plus the delivery door and staircase is right outside the window. So door banging all night and delivery at 5.30 am that takes 30 minutes meant very little sleep was had. Quite how they can charge money for this room I have no idea. Staff have very basic language skills, breakfast , not sure if I could have a cooked breakfast or not, no one could tell me. Continental breakfast was very poor and did not look or taste fresh. All in all a poor hotel and would not recommend it.

title: Theatre break
text: Lovely hotel comfortable cleane and friendly always helpful didn't try the food but for London it seemed reasonably priced in a good location 20 minutes walk to shaftsbury for theatres and extra 15 to 20 mins to Buckingham palace and trafalgar square ect we felt quite at ease too walking round even at night some nice pubs and a witherspoons near by

title: Excellent Location & Wonderful Room
text: As boutique hotels in London go this one is pretty good. The hotel itself a restored Georgian town house is located very near the British Museum in the Bloomsbury area, with the museum not even 5 mins away. What was very surprising was the size of our room. Having stayed in London many times this was by far the largest room for the price. The facilities in general are limited with a small buffet breakfast area and small lobby. However considering the location there are numerous dining options available and quite a few good old fashioned London pubs all within walking distance either in the direction of Russell Square or the other way towards. A few little tips: - there is a great cafe come restaurant in the back corner of Russell Square which is a nice place to sit a people watch over a glass or bottle of wine. - British Museum is very close and best to go to as early as possible - see my review of the museum for more museum tips - if you are looking for more hotel type facilities you may need to manage your expectations, but I assure the hotel is very comfortable and the rooms are quite stunning for the style - it is a nice walk, with the right weather, to Covent Gardens, Tottenham Court Road & Soho, in general the location is quite good for exploring the West End.

title: Par boiled
text: Booked a " Double Superior Room" at £337 for 2 nights . Allocated one on the 3rd floor overlooking the street. The double superior room was very small. In my opinion it was very old fashioned and dated. I found the bed to be uncomfortable and the pillows floppy and of poor quality. There was just about enough space to move past the foot of the bed to get to the bathroom or door. I had to keep the bathroom light on all night so as not to hit and injure myself on the piece of shelf jutting out from above the fireplace which wouldn't be seen in the dark. Overall the room was clean enough but definitely needs a refurbishment and update. The shower and bath was accessible only by stepping over a very high siding. There was no air conditioning and we were absolutely sweltered even with the window wide open all night! There was a table top fan available but even when switched on to capacity it made little difference. I know it was high temperatures outside but there can be no justification for making people suffer these conditions. It felt like it was over 30 degrees. Even our chocolate bar which had been in our suitcase melted completely. To top it all the lift was out of order one of the days. The hotel is in a nice convenient location but not in my opinion, value for money. The continental breakfast was quite basic but the service at breakfast was good. We inadvertently left a charger in the room and contacted the hotel to ascertain if they would return it to us. This is their response "Should you wish for us to send it to you, please fax, or use the secure link below to send us a short description of the lost property items, a full postage address and your full credit card details with a note authorising us to charge your credit card for both postage cost and 20% service charge. If using the link, kindly put Lost Property in the Reference Number section. Please note there is a minimum charge of £5.00 for all credit card transactions". Well .... I think it might be cheaper to buy a new one! I was very disappointed in my overall experience here.

title: Distinctly average, but good location
text: The hotel itself is in a good location, close to lots of attractions, theatres, shops etc and this is really what you’re paying for. The rooms are small but functional, nothing special and comfortable enough to lay your head for the night. Breakfast was poor considering the small breakfast room was not busy. I seated myself and was ignored for almost half an hour, in the end I had to approach staff to ask for coffee. Cooked breakfast is extra and cooked to order, I opted for poached eggs on toast. I was presented with slightly over cooked unbuttered toast with two poached eggs that had clearly been thrown straight on the plate and were swimming with water. Who needs butter when your toast is soggy! It wasn’t a great experience, and the few other diners that came and went during the time I was there didn’t seem to have a great experience either. Shame considering how many staff there were for the number of guests, the service should have been much better.

title: A very good experience from beginning to end
text: The Receptionist was very helpful and efficient. He asked if we had stayed before, and on learning we had not, upgraded us to a Kings Size room. The room was large, very clean with a good range of facilities e.g. large TV, DVD player. It is a quiet hotel in a quiet area, but near attractions and the bus and tube network. The only disappointment was the price of breakfast (£17.25 per person) so we ate locally at one of the many cafes.

title: Overnight stop in Clarendon
text: A restful night in this small hotel. I had an executive room which was spacious and well equipped including sky sport for the football. Very clean and tidy with pleasant staff. The breakfast was served rather than buffet which was pleasant. The selection of hot and cold food was good.

title: Leaves a lot to be desired
text: I was booked into this hotel via the hotel reservation service at Victoria station, as I had arrived in London rather late (Around 8:30 or 9PM) and had no internet access. I paid £82 or so for the night in a single room, including breakfast. POSITIVES: + The location, in Russell Square, is fabulous + The building and its rooms are fairly well-presented + The price was pretty good, considering it was central London during the peak Xmas/New Year break NEGATIVES: - The exorbitant price for wifi access (!!) -- I'd stayed at a variety of hotels during my time in the UK & Europe, some more expensive than the Clarendon, some less so, ALL offered free wifi - The breakfast selection was quite limited, with very few choices. I had to order toast from a waitress, and when it eventually came (after about 15 mins of patiently waiting), it was not even close to toasted and too cold to even melt the butter. I gave up and walked out hungry at that point. Not a good start to the day :( - I stored my bags at the hotel after checking out, so I could enjoy a day of shopping. However, upon my return to collect them, I waited a good 15-20 mins after handing the reception staff my baggage ticket, while someone went to fetch my things. When the bags were FINALLY returned, I wasn't offered any form of explanation or apology for the delay. Very disappointing.

title: Very Classy Stay
text: We stayed as part of a larger party. Check in was a bit slow due to only 1 actually checking in and the other doing something else. The actual check in process was prolonged (despite payment on booking) and they asked for a lot of details but the signatures on the card was a good touch. The room was amazingly large and well set out. Lovely little touches including the hidden tea/coffee box. The only negative was the bathroom needs to be upgraded as the shower door was strangely in 3 parts. The concierge was called many times and was helpful and friendly every time. The breakfast was varied with many options with a choice of a full English or continental breakfast. The staff were very friendly and helpful and check out was much quicker than check in. They also offered a left luggage facility which we used before our room was ready and at the end of our stay. Location was walking distance to both Holborn Station, Russell Square and Tottenham Court Road. The British Museum is a stones throw away!

title: Service Extraordinaire
text: We have always enjoyed our stays at the Grange Hotels in London

title: Good location. NO FREE INTERNET.
text: Really good value in a great location. The room was very nice. The bathroom was especially nice, clean, with a big tub. There's no breakfast which is a little sad, but my main complaint was how much they charge for internet service! I'm used to hotels that provide free internet service and I believe that that's standard now in even the cheapest of hotels. There's a computer in the lobby that they supposedly charge you to use, but we just used it anyway to check our email now and then. The staff was so, so friendly and helpful! We'd return again.

title: Excellent Hotel
text: Stayed Aug 2014, we received a very professional and polite welcome upon arrival, the room was nicely appointed and very clean. We had breakfast included in the booking which was of a good quality and although only the cold breakfast was included, for me the additional 5 GPB per day for the cooked one was worth it. The hotel is in a good location and is within walking distance of Camden, Oxford St, the Thames and is a stones throw away from the British Museum. There are also 2 tube stations within walking distance being Holborn or Russell square both on the Piccadilly line which leaves from Heathrow. Overall it was a pleasant stay and we would certainly book again the next time we return to London.

title: Awful don’t bother !
text: Booked for a weekend in London with my boyfriend as we were planning a few trips to the theatre . The only good thing about this hotel is the staff and the location The staff were really professional and very friendly The location is short walking distance to plenty of theatres and great restaurants. However the room was so dated , the bathroom Was tiny and absolutely awful . The bath had a sort of weird box screen around it which made you feel like you were in a box ! It was so small you bashed yourself into it everytime you went in! The room smelt like an old people’s home and was so much smaller than on pictures! The tea and coffee cupboard stunk of must so we didn’t bother having them! At night it was around 7 degrees C and we had the window open all night it was that hot with no control over the temperature of the room ! I get this is a cheaper hotel for the area but it’s still Over £120 a night - and it is most definitely Not a four star !!! This hotel is most suitable For cheap business trips in cold Weather !

title: Possibly the WORST hotel I have ever stayed at!
text: Terrible terrible hotel! Do not stay at this place! It's a two star mascarading as a four star! Luring in gullible tourists. Dirty curtains, urine stained duvets and staff who don't understand English. Its Falling apart, old towels and smells. I changed rooms four times in one night, then when I tried to call down to reception the phone didn't work. Took an hour to get a duvet, as theirs are ancient and are paper thin,they then took it away again the next night,so had to go through whole rigmarole again. For your own sake, save your money and stay in a genuine 4 star or if not stay at a budget chain! AWFUL

title: Family weekend with outings planned in central London so the hotel is very well placed for that
text: We were disappointed, had been there before but found things rather tired looking this time. There was a smell of drains in our room and a broken toilet seat- worse for the men I am told!!! Breakfast was OK, the restaurant staff were really kind but the food was very expensive, so we went out round the corner the second day. There are good cafes close by. We had what I can only assume was a technical problem with our booking, and ended up having to pay twice for our room. I have not been able to understand exactly why. It made the weekend extremely expensive for me and the attitude to what had happened upset me and coloured my judgement. The front of house management staff said at the time they did not think we would be charged but it needed a senior managers decision. We were told a senior manager would ring on Monday

title: Great stay in quiet location with nice roooms
text: An old apartment building converted into a nice hotel. The neighborhood is nice and quiet, no traffic noise. The room we had was in the basement however this was not a problem what so ever. A big window provided enough daylight. Please be aware that the bathroom has the shower in the bathtub, with sliding glass door. Not a problem for us, but if your balance is not what it used to be it may be something to consider. The bathroom was clean and overall very nice. The room as well was clean and, good lights and all furnitures in very good condition. The double bed was hard which is something I prefer much versus a soft mushy bed. We arrived early and our luggage was smoothly handled by the staff while we were out shopping. The reception was staffed also in the evening. I would be happy to stay there again, found it to be of good value.

title: Do not stay at Grange Hotels - appallingly rude staff
text: I checked in with my family to 4 rooms on 3 December. Later, on our return from the theatre the night porter was incredibly rude to us. He told us that we MUST press the button when we come in and NEVER try to open the door because the locking system cost £5000. We arrived in three groups and he said the same thing to each group in a very aggressive and rude way which was very upsetting to our family, including my pregnant daughter-in-law. I complained to the manager in the morning but she, offered no refund on any of the £800+ I had spent. She promised her boss would call me the next day but this didn't happen and now I am just being fobbed off. Mistakes can be forgiven, but agressive and completely unnecessary rudeness like this cannot. And on top of this, Grange Hotels have absolutely no idea about how to deal with complaints. I will never, ever stay with them again.

title: Large bed
text: Centrally located hotel that I have stayed in several times when delivering training in Holborn. Always a warm welcome & they use an IPAD to register your arrival. Rooms are a good size for London & most have a comfortable large bed. The only thing to watch is getting in & out of the shower as it over a deep bath & then there is a shower rail on top. Might be difficult for some people

title: Could be great, but let down by important details
text: This hotel should be great. Bloomsbury is a fantastic location, close to the British Museum and a short stroll into the heart of Soho. The rooms are large and comfortable, and the staff are friendly and helpful. However, it doesn't live up to its four star billing. The shower gave out a trickle of lukewarm water, which turned cold after a few minutes. The temperature in the room couldn't be altered, and it was pretty chilly for most of our stay. The television was also set to a (quite loud) volume, and the remote was on the blink. If these details were sorted out, I'd be delighted to return. For the moment, the hotel needs a touch of tlc to make it a truly pleasant stay.

title: Basement Blues
text: Although booked into the Buckingham – a sister hotel down the road – we found ourselves shunted to The Clarendon. We were allocated a room on ‘the lower ground floor’, i.e. in the basement. The room itself was acceptable: reasonably-sized, with en suite, and in good decorative order. However, its location gave it several ‘special’ features. First, the metal staircase outside the window provided staff access (clang, clang, clang) to the door (creak) of the adjacent store room where essential early morning supplies (rattle, crash) could be retrieved. Second, the slightly-below-ground-level placement gave unrestricted acoustic access to the dawn arrival of delivery trucks reversing (beep-beep-beep) into position before lowering (whirr, clank) their tail-lifts and off-loading (clatter) trolleys to push (rumble, rumble) into the hotel. Third, directly above the room was the breakfast lounge. Here early rising guests (slow, slow, tramp, tramp, slow) and staff (trip, trip, cha-cha-cha) appeared to be rehearsing for an edition of Strictly Come Dancing. Insist on a higher floor!

title: Great place, at great value!
text: On our booking our aim was to find a hotel within the central London area that offered a middle to high standard room at a sensible rate. Believe me this wasn't easy for us to find! As a female I am somewhat fussy about where I stay. Is the bed big enough? Is there enough floor space? What about the towels! Are they fluffy?..... After much contemplation and literally a whole weeks worth of searching with every spare moment found we decided to stay at “The Grange Clarendon”. Now the Grange offer a range of 4 & 5 star accommodations spotted around some amazing parts of London, from Tower Bridge to Oxford Circus. Their website offers the client the experience to browse through each hotel before booking, giving you the opportunity to view just what your paying for. As a personal fan of boutique hotels, I thought The Grange Clarendon would be a perfect choice as it was part of their boutique range. At £86.40 we were able to book an executive room that offered a king size bed, Wi-Fi, private en-suite bathroom, digital TV,, toiletries, and a couple of little extras such as a safe and tea making facilities. Also lets not forget to mention the inclusive continental breakfast. Walking down Bedford Place, a beautiful quiet street in the heart of Central London filled with pretty Georgian town houses. Upon arrival we were greeted with an intercom system, some may find this as a negative, but it provided us with a sense of safety and security. On checking in we were met with a polite young lady at reception, friendly in manner making us feel more than welcome by offering us information regarding the Wi-Fi, room service and so forth. We were shocked to find out our room was on the lower ground but this added a little bit of mystery so we were more than happy. Walking through corridors with anticipation building the moment of truth arrived, would our room be as lovely as the professional photos teased it to be? Or would it be a big disappointment since the price was so wonderful? Stepping in behind my partner I felt a wash of dread but one glance around and that feeling subsided very quickly. The room was even more beautiful than the pictures had displayed, and it appeared to be much bigger in person. Our room was decorated in a soft cream colour complemented by teak and mahogany wood, complete with a sofa bed. If you get tired of him girls, you know where he can sleep! Looking around I almost couldn't believe this room to be just above £85.00 I went in search for the hidden issues and found myself wondering to the bathroom which was just as beautiful and immaculate as the room itself. There had to be something wrong surely?.... I was determined I opened every cupboard, every draw, and everything was perfect, even down to the wonderful selection of English and herbal teas supplied. Enjoying the room so much we didn't even notice the view until a little later, being on the lower ground I have to admit the view wasn't a feature, but who goes to a hotel just to stare out of a window? We settled down to watch the flat screen TV with it's selection of Freeview channels and the moment we hit the bed we were welcomed with pure comfort! The mattress soft but firm with soft bouncy pillows. At times we could hear people above and the noise could be distracting if this carried on for too long, fortunately this wasn't the case so we didn't mind. Around 8:pm we began to get peckish, rather than leave the comfort of our warm wonderful mattress we decided it would be nice to sample the food and room service on offer. Looking through the menu there was more than two vegetarian options on offer which was nice to see. And we had up until 10:pm to order food. Some items are one offer 24hr but not the main meals so look out for the * next to the items on the menu. I'm not one that's a fan of food arriving too quickly so when room service informed me it would be roughly 30 mins I was more than happy with this. On time as promised a knock at the door. Our meal was served on a little wooden tray under a silver platter, the meal was of a decent edible standard and was served with it's very own mustard, brown sauce, and ketchup in individual jars. The little touches really made the meal special. An hour or two passed and our bodies nor eyes could no longer take the comfort the bed provided and sleep came calling. Without much disturbance I awoke only once to readjust my pillows as they were a tad too soft for me but once I fell back to sleep I slept through which was lovely. Waking up at around 8:am it was nice to have the enjoyment of a lay in, the knowledge of rest without the worry of rushing to get our complimentary breakfast which is served daily till 10:am. Getting ourselves ready for the day ahead, we headed for the dinning room at 9:30am. At this point I would be lying if I said I wasn't worried that the continental breakfast would be limited due to the time. Arriving at the dining room we were pleasantly surprised by a busy but comfortable atmosphere, and there was plenty of selection still on offer from pastries, cereals, cheeses and more, also a number of juices and we were kindly offered tea and coffee. Our breakfast simple and pleasant we returned to our room to collect our items and to say one final goodbye to a beautiful room and experience. Down at reception we were kindly offered the option to leave our bags we denied as we would no longer be within the area but it was nice to have the option. Out of 10 an overall score of a 9½ has to be given, It would have been given a 10 but if there is too much noise this could be a distraction. Things to look out for: Good Points Good selection of teas. Comfy King size bed. 24hr room service. Bad Points Noise. Lack of view. Wrong instructions for shower use. Check in from 14:00 Check out 11:00

title: Good hotel, good location
text: We were originally booked at the Buckingham hotel, same group of hotels, but were 'upgraded' to the Clarendon just up the road. We were unsure what the upgrade meant until we saw room 108 - just about the biggest hotel room I have seen huge double bed, a pair of full size settees, plus other chairs and tables. chests and cupboards. Even wit all the furniture the room was not cluttered. Very good bathroom too, shower in bath, plus shampoo, conditioner etc. Good continental breakfast on offer but our deal included English breakfast and no complaints there re quality or quantity. Staff were very good and obliging too. No dining facility but there is room service dining, and there are plenty of restaurants nearby. Recommended and good value.

title: Great location
text: Stayed in this hotel as was going to Peacock Theatre to see a show. The theatre was a 10 min walk away. Holborn and Russell Square tube stations are 5 min walk away in opposite directions. Covent Garden was a 12 min walk away and the British Museum was round the corner. It also took me about 15 minutes to walk to St Pancras for my journey home. So hotel is ideally located for theatreland. Luckily I stayed in the lower ground floor which was cool in this hot weather. The room was large with 2 large double beds and ensuite. I've stayed in a few places in London and this was good value for money. Staff were friendly. I didn't try any other amenities but the wifi was good.

title: Not on my preferred list.
text: Far from the best stay I've enjoyed whilst stopping over on business in London. Pro's: Good location Con's: Poor facilities in room. No A/C, rubbish TV. In need of refurb Poor food, bland breakfasts and evening meals only served across the road in sister hotel. Service fairly average. Small rooms Not on my preferred list.

title: Sadly lacking in some areas but great in others!
text: Stayed one night. Upon check in we were told we had been upgraded due to a maintenance problem with our room and we were being sent to the Grange Tower. However we refused as we had booked for a theatre trip in Shaftsbury Ave. We were given an 'executive' room in the basement. It was huge I have to say and incredibly clean. Unfortunately it was very dark with no natural light due to so much garden furniture stacked above the wall level outside the window. we asked for a fan as it was so hot and was presented with an ancient rickety tower fan which switched itself on and off at will all night. The bathroom had a generous supply of shampoo but no shower gel. The kettle was in a box which was perched on a wall and hard wired in so you had to boil the kettle somewhat precariously in the pull down door of said cupboard. The fire escape plan is ridiculous and completely unreadable. The colour code for exit and lift was almost the same and the plan so small it was impossible to work out what direction to take. However, that all being said. The staff were polite and friendly, the location is fab and parking is 2 minutes away in Bloomsbury Sq. We paid £154 and there was no breakfast with that. so go off to local streets where there are plenty of options for breakfast, or of course The British Museum which is on your doorstep.

title: We love these Grange hotels on BedfordPlace
text: We always come to London just before Christmas for a long w/e, and do like the Grange Hotels along this street

title: Nice room but very expensive
text: Recently stayed for 2 nights at this hotel. The executive room was lovely and the bed comfortable,but oh so expensive. The room was so hot, no air conditioning and as it is classed as a 4star hotel I would have thought something would be done about this, even if was just putting fans in the rooms as we knew other guests had been complaining. The bar was not open whilst we were there and really it felt like a B&B where you had to be out during the day. And as for breakfast, well don't get me started, how on earth does anyone justify charging £23 per person per day for bacon and eggs !!!!!! So what we done, like a lot of other people was get up and go out and find a nice cafe to get something to eat. All in all very much a rip off hotel that could do so much better!

title: Huge room, good food, welcoming staff.
text: This hotel is in a great location, close to the British Museum, and Birkbeck University. We stayed in an executive room (311) on the third floor. This is probably the largest hotel room and bathroom I have ever had in the UK. The window, overlooking a tree lined view, could be opened all the way for fresh air, unusual in hotels now. Dinner was taken at a sister hotel 50 yards down the road and the food was good. The full English breakfast in the Clarendon's own restaurant was superb, and the service lightning quick, important ahead of a busy day. Staff were very pleasant, we would stay here again.

title: alright
text: We stayed for one night with 4 persons in one room in single beds (which were alright). The space was a little bit tight, but so was the price. Everything in the room was as decent as you may expect, but our bathroom was small. The breakfast was typical English. The location is great. Blackheath has atmoshpere, like a tiny village in a city (with a station around the corner) and Greenwich is a 15 minute walk away. Would return for a night at the same rate.

title: Good quality short-stay hotel
text: The hotel is situated just south of Russell Square and appears to have been renovated fairly recently – it’s a row of three comfortable nineteenth-century terraced houses converted into a hotel. As has been observed by other contributors, its rack rate is more costly than the hotel really justifies, but late bookings are much more reasonable (we paid £69 per night for bed and continental breakfast). The room, on the top floor, was small (a gap of about twelve inches between the foot of the bed and the opposite wall), but very comfortable. The only slightly worrying issue was a crack across the tiles on the bathroom floor coupled with an inability to shut the bathroom door, possibly indicating a structural problem caused during refurbishment. Breakfast was neutral in terms of quality, however the breakfast room was comfortable and relaxing. Staff are well-mannered and helpful. The street in which the hotel is situated is relatively quiet and free from excessive traffic noise, and is very close to the British Museum and a relatively short walk from Covent Garden Overall, an excellent value hotel for a short break – if you want a more individual experience it probably isn’t for you

title: Great Hotel
text: The staff are really friendly and extremely helpful ask for anything delivered in minutes . The rooms are very clean and in classic appearance with lots of space. Very handy for all main attractions and Holborn and soho and oxford st.

title: Noisy, small, not very good.
text: We paid £140 per night, which was supposed to include a 35% discount. We paid for a "superior room" through LastMinute. On arrival we were shown to a tiny little room. I said there must be a mistake as we were booked into a superior room, not a standard, and was told they don't have standard rooms - so "Superior rooms" are the worst kind of rooms they have!! They had advertised their rooms as "spacious" and "individually designed". THEY ARE NOT! Our room was so small, the tv wasn't on the wall at the end of the bed as you'd expect, because even though it was a flat screen there wasn't enough room for it there! The bathroom floor tiles were cracked, the wallpaper was very scuffed, it was a tiny room. We complained and were shown to 2 identical tiny rooms (not so individually designed then!) and eventually we were upgraded. The new room was much bigger, but was in the basement and close to the underground so ever 10 minutes or so we heard the train thundering past. Also we had booked a double but the upgrade was a twin and they had pushed the beds close together, but each was made up with single bedding on it. One of the cups was cracked (those stained cracks that let you know they've been cracked for ages and all the germs have got in), and when the room was cleaned the housekeeping staff spilled some water on my theatre programmes, so my only souvenir was soaked. The location was OK for us as we wanted walking distance to theatres, and there is a great cafe just round the corner that does a fabulous range of breakfasts for about £5.50 (English, veggie, Mediterranean...) The hotel was not a very pleasant experience. When we had booked (secret hotels) I thought we had got a bargain, but unfortunately I was very much mistaken.

title: Girly weekend 4 star
text: Myself and two friends stayed here in September 2015, I'd stayed here a year before with my husband and the return trip didn't fail to disappoint. A good sized room for the three of us, was slightly worried that the pull out bed might have been uncomfortable but I couldn't have enjoyed a better nights sleep. Clean friendly and such amazing value for money. We parked in NCP Woburn place which was a great deal if pre booked and breakfast in the amazing cafe in Russel park was the perfect end to a perfect weekend.

title: Lovely little hotel.
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here last weekend, our other hotels boiler broke and we had to book the Claredon last minute, however it turned out to be a blessing in disguise! The staff were friendly, rooms were clean and very comfortable! I loved the bathroom nice big bath! The hotel is in a great location near nice pubs, the British Museum and about a 5 minute walk to Halborn underground. The only thing I would say is that the checkout is a little too early at 11am and the WiFI is too expensive. Other then that I would highly recommend it!

title: Great location, shame about the rest
text: Stayed at hotel with husband for New Year celebrations in London. Arrived to a very frosty welcome from male duty manager. Felt like we were more of a nuisance. A smile would have been nice but he had no doubt undertaken a personality by-pass. Our double room was on the second floor and was really small. The heating was overpowering, in contrast to the bathroom which was freezing and only had a net curtain at the window, so that when the light was switched on, the world and his uncle had a birds eye view. We had booked another room for three members of our family who arrived the following day. This room, unlike ours, was enormous but very cold. It was on the lower ground floor, underneath the kitchen. Our daughters were disturbed very early by the general noise from above and woke in a panic when they smelt smoke. They realised that the locked door in their room led to an outer courtyard where the hotel staff had gathered, talking loudly and smoking. Breakfast was a disorganised affair. No one present to meet and greet and the staff, all foreign, displaying a distinct lack of customer service skills. Breakfast content poor and popular items like croissants quickly ran out, being replaced by cold toast.This hotel is not really 4 star quality. On a positive note, it is very clean and boasts an excellent location.

title: Great location, good rooms, good service.
text: My wife and I were in London for a long weekend - 3 nights, 4 days - for some sightseeing. After looking online, we found the Clarendon - which is part of the Grange Hotels group. The price was reasonable, the reviews were favorable, and although we didn't know the city too well, the location looked pretty good. The best part about this hotel is definately the location. It was a 2 minute walk from the Holburn Tube station which easily connects to the entire city, a 2 minute walk from the British Museum (which is great because since its free you can just pop in to check out some world treasures if you have an hour or two to spare), and a 5 minute walk to Soho and the heart of London. We booked directly through the Grange website which has the advantage of offering rooms at all of its hotels which are generally clustered right around the same part of town. Some are even on the same street. Check-in was easy and efficient as was the service from the reception staff for the duration of our stay. I had requested a room on one of the upper floors after reading about other's experiences where they were in the basement rooms which they didn't like too much. We got a room on the second floor. The room was pretty small but very clean. Since we didn't go to London to hang out in a hotel room, the size didn't bother us too much. The bathroom was nice and clean, the bed was decent, there was a desk and a tv. The walls/doors to the main hallway are a bit thin and you could hear people talking or opening doors outside your room, but that didn't bother us too much. We had the continental breakfast which was perfectly fine. We didn't order The English Breakfast. The people next to us one morning did and it looked fine but was probably a bit overpriced. We didn't really use the hotel bar or the restaurant except for breakfast. The bar had a small offering of liquor, beer, and wine. I don't know about the prices but it wasn't really a separate bar, rather an extension of the lobby/reception area. With so many great restaurants a short walk away, we had no desire to eat at the restaurant for lunch or dinner. It is definately not a 5 star hotel, however for the price it is a great deal and good value. Overall, we were very happy with this hotel and would definately go back there (or to another in the Grange Hotel group).

title: 7 Day Stay - Le Cordon Bleu
text: I have to say, the room was clean, bathroom was modern, what else can you expect from a hotel? Stayed in a single room (room 110) and the room was more than spacious, had a tea kettle, bath tub (lovely) and very short walking distance to British museum. Stayed here for a 4 day course at the cordon bleu (would DEFINITELY recommend it for anyone doing short courses there), very close to the school (2 minute walk) and not to mention, the staff was very helpful and kind.

title: Fabulous weekend
text: We stayed at the Clarendon for couple of nights to celebrate a friends special birthday. The rooms we had were really nice, they were spacious and well appointed with everything you could possibly need to be comfortable. The bathroom was large, clean and modern with plenty of luxury toiletries provided. The breakfast was delicious and plentiful and the staff extremely pleasant and helpful. For many years now we have always stayed in Grange Hotels in London and the Clarendon is up there with the best of them. The weather was atrocious but fortunately we had a great hotel, thank you for making our weekend so special. Why would we go elsewhere.

title: The clarendon (and the Grange hotel group) stinks
text: I've now stayed at this group of hotels quite a few times for business, but think I've reached the end of my patience with them. If you are a business traveller, you should read on. Even if you are a leisure traveller, you might want to take account of the problems that now occur regularly at this hotel (and other Grange hotels, from my experience). This used to be a really good hotel, with good, punctual service and a friendly attitude to customers. However, my experience of breakfast time (below) is indicative of what seems to be a serious downturn in their ability to delight (no, not even satisfy) customers. So why do I say this? -Breakfast, served from 7am onwards, is a joke. You arrive at , say 7.10am, to be greeted by the sight of a strapping young asian lad canoodling in the restaurant with a young waitress (no training or supervision needed in that department, but maybe in others). Once he's scarpered (without a word, or a thought of what you might want - he had other things on his mind), you are faced with a breakfast room with no fruit juice, no milk, no cutlery, no cereal, and no staff. That makes it difficult to eat breakfast then. Other staff arrive (after a while) treating the folding of napkins and chatting with each other as the key priority. You ask for a cup of tea, and some toast, giving them the benefit of the doubt, assuming that stocking the breakfast table was the job of the tall casanova and his young companion. This arrives, after ten minutes, cunningly disguised as a pot of hot water and two pieces of bread (and no, it's not one of those hotels where you make your own toast and tea). After two of three mornings of this over a two week period (as I said, I stayed there regularly), I mentioned this to the front desk, but as this continued to recur, I think I'll go elsewhere. This is just one example of the myriad of problems with what used to be a fine, friendly and cosy hotel. It is clearly now run by management who lack the basic competencies required to deliver a basic hotel service (even by London's dubious standards) so I would steer cleer of it - unless you aren't in a hurry aren't hungry at breakfast time, or have voyueristic tendencies!

title: 5 Star Location, 3 Star hotel
text: I was booked into this hotel through our London office, which I am working out of for the week. It was undoubtably arranged because the hotel is a lovely 4 minute walk across Russell Square to the office, making the commute undeniably convenient. Besides being close to my office (which none of you care about), the hotel is wonderfully situated in the city. You are within walking distance to the theater district, covenant gardens, leicster square, trafalger square, and the thames, not to mention tons of wonderful bars, pubs and restaurants. It's a good thing the location is so great, because the rest is nothing to write home about. Our double room is almost impossibly small for two people. My finance and I both have to get ready for work in the mornings and have to crawl over the bed just to get around. The itself, while FAR from ideal, would be managable, if it weren't for the ungodly temperature of the room. London is a cool 60 degrees this week, yet our room is nearing the high 80's. We have our window WIDE open, but because of the way the hotel is situated, we receive absolutely no air through that window. It really is stiffling - especially in contrast with the cool temps outside. It has made for a few miserable nights of sleep. In addition, there is a crusty, white stain on our decorative bedspread that I prefer not to think about, and when housekeeping came in, we were not given new towels (though the old ones were taken away) and our dirty coffee cups were not cleared. Sub-par hotel with a location that just MAY (?) make up for it.

title: Great Hotel
text: we have stayed in London many times and always stayed at Travelodges or Premier inns, although there is nothing wrong with these we wanted something a bit more georgian style, the hotel is very nice inside , not the best but clean and tidy, the rooms are small but more than enough room, location is excellent for the shops (oxford street) or the theaters in local covent garden with just a short walk away, it is also a short walk from euston station, breakfast is a little expensive, i would encourage the hotel to at least half the cost of this then that way more people would dine, overall i would stay here again and would recommend this hotel to anyone, the staff were great and helpfull and they even held onto our bags so we did not have to carry them around with us after we checked out, the spa is chargable

title: Great value and location
text: We stayed here for two nights at the end of September. It’s in a great location, very central but also in a quiet road. Check in was quick and efficient and the room we had was excellent. Yes, the hotel is in an old building so you’re going to hear creaks and squeaks but I would happily return, and it represents excellent value for a hotel in central London.

title: In London with young children
text: We arrived very early in the morning to London Heathrow on a Monday morning. We stopped at the tourist desk at the airport to ask some questions. Originally we had been booked into an Inn in Hampstead. The man at the desk was able to find us a room at the Clarendon for close to equivalent price and it was great! It was definitely much closer to the sights and made our trip in London much easier. He found us a very spacious room. We were very happy with our stay. The bar was nice as we could put the children to bed and come down for a drink. We would definitely return here again. We were able to store our luggage both the day we arrived and the day we left. This was very helpful especially since we were travelling with children. The only thing that was a little annoying was the cost of using the internet wi-fi. Any hotels I have travelled to in North America have wi-fi included in the price. This would be a nice addition, especially for travellers from abroad who don't have mobile phone usage.

title: Comfortable stay
