text: Stay here quite a bit for work. Exec rooms are large and spacious, with big comfortable bed. Was once put in a small room on 3rd floor and asked to be moved- more like an attic room and stairs to get there are really steep and shallow. Breakfast is quite limited and standard.

title: Pleasant stay in London
text: I stayed at the Clarendon for work and to be honest it's a nice hotel although if you get chance choose the Beauchamp as I found this far nicer. Breakfast is ok, they are ideally located near Holborn tube station and a minutes walk away is a host of shops, pubs and resteraunts. You can't really go wrong here for a short stay.

title: Lovely hotel in a good location
text: We stayed in a lovely room within the hotel, clean & spacious room with everything needed for a long weekend stay, friendly & helpful staff, good location for Euston station & attractions. Would stay again.

title: Noisy rooms in a London basement
text: Billed as a 4 star hotel, it didn't get off to a good start when the advertised price on their website did not include VAT so that was as extra surprise on the bill. Check in was swift and staff pleasant but I was a little dismayed to find they had deviated from convention to have a room number 13 which they had allocated to me. I was even more dismayed to find that I was on the euphemistically named lower ground floor - that's the basement to you and me. The room itself was very nice indeed which lovely decor and bedding and the bed was extremely comfortable. The room size was excellent for a London hotel. The bathroom had a lovely deep bath with lots of hot water but the fan did not stop running all night and even with the bathroom door shut it was loud enough to keep me awake for a little while. Also I could here lots of footsteps above me and moving furniture so the room was evidently not sound proofed fully. This was even more evident when early the next morning men delivering clean laundry to the hotel were very noisy outside my window which it transpired had the delightful view of the service entrance. They did shut up when asked but it had ruined my lovely lie in. The hotel position in Bloomsbury was very convenient but I did feel disappointed that their attention to the big details hadn't been carried through to things I considered important like sound proofing. And a free paper delivered to your room each morning doesn't make up for charging for use of wifi. For the price of a room I would like free wifi please.

title: My company was overcharged
text: Just noticing the last minute deals on this site when my Company actually paid a corporate rate of £140 for a room in the basement and I was only entitled to the buffet breakfast. I could hear people walking around the foyer upstairs until quite late and my room was next to a staff entry/exit so it was not the quietest of places. Room was compact with a massive bathroom but the shower door over the bath was a bit rickety. Buffet breakfast was ok - choices of fruit, cheeses, hams etc so I would not starve but I still think the rate was a bit pricey compared to the current mid week deals. I stay in London a fair bit but I am not sure that I would use this Grange Hotel again - the Rochester is far better.

title: Lovely stay.
text: Smoothly run hotel, staff were excellent, I asked for extra tea bags and a shaving kit and was swiftly given them. Room nicely decorated and very clean, shower was fabulous. Didn't eat or drink at hotel. Arrival and checking out was done efficiently. We were upgraded free of charge to an executive room which was added bonus. Very pleasant stay.

title: Central and comfortable
text: A very nice hotel centrally located with only a few minute walk to either the Russel Square or Holborne tube station. Very friendly staff and clean and comfortable rooms. Can only recommended this hotel!

title: Very good
text: Stayed here when attending an event in central London, so I didn't have worry about getting home. Overall my experience was good, hotel is very central, clean & comfortable. Only one thing - the breakfast is very expensive, so book room only. There are plenty of good cafes nearby.

title: Excellent service and location
text: We recently stayed at this hotel and we very happy with the service from the staff and the location. We were able to walk to Piccadilly and Trafalgar Square and down to the Thames. We would defiantly stay there again .

title: Great value hotel
text: Stayed here with my girlfriend for 2 nights for a bank holiday weekend. On Arrival they upgraded our room which was a great start. Very nice interior, clean and good size rooms. Great location in London, we caught a show in the west end and it only took us 10/15 mins to walk there - oxford street similar distance away as well. Plus the british museum was only a couple mins walk and there are plenty of subways nearby. Also had a baggage store room which was really useful upon checking out. Couldn't have asked for anything more really considering the price we payed. Would stay again without hesitation

title: Absolutely disgusting
text: I stumbled on an offer listed on the Lastminute.com web site during a search for 4 or 5 star hotels for a visit to London for my husband and I and my sister and her husband. The hotel was advertised as a Secret Hotel, luxury 4 star boutique hotel discounted by 45% supposedly. On receipt of our payment we were notified that the Clarendon Hotel, in Bloomsbury was our nominated hotel , on checking the negative reviews on trip advisor we became worried about the hotel. We notified lastminute.com that we were not happy and they asked us to report back following our visit, assuring us that the hotel would be ok. On arrival at the hotel we were checked in and made our way to our rooms and very quickly became very disappointed – the rooms were very small and in no way luxurious. The lace curtains where dirty and hanging down (see pics) The window paint was crumbling and in a terrible state of repair (see pics) The paintwork to the doors was very dirty and dusty and the bathroom door had dirty black hand marks on it – see pictures The wallpaper was very marked - See picture The bathroom was tired, cheaply and badly fitted out- the shower system could in no way be classed as luxurious. I could go on and on about how this room compared so badly to a four star hotel, but I think the pictures say it all. Determined not to spoil our trip away we left our bags and went out to explore London., however I made a quick visit to reception to check that we had been given ‘superior rooms’ and this was confirmed. We returned later that afternoon to quickly get ready for a show we were booked into see to find that a man repairing a window outside our door, on further investigation it was the window from our room which had been removed and was being repaired on the hallway floor directly outside our bedroom (picture enclosed). We only had an hour to freshen up, and had to return to the reception desk to ask that the repair man be removed whilst we used the room. The manager came up to our room, but the repair man was ignoring the manager whom was trying to gather up his tools and move him away from the window and out of the room. Eventually he was ushered out of the room and we began to unpack our things on to the bed – and at this point I cannot stipulate enough our disgust as we noticed the bed spread covering the bed was dirty, and the more we inspected the more stains we found – big black stains (see pic) and even more disgusting white stains all over – a stain every 8” squared. I am sure you can imagine as we did what the stains were, which was enough to make us nearly vomit and to our horror my sister and her husband where identifying the same problem in there room with the bed spread and they equally felt the room was dirty and not luxury four star. My husband asked that the bed spreads be replaced and that the room be cleaned up as there was putty and bits of wood all over the bedroom floor. The house maids then stood outside both rooms repeatedly harassing us for entry to sort the rooms out, again preventing us from getting ready

title: Impressed
text: The Clarendon is located very close to Holborn metro station. It's very conveniently located for sightseeing, dining, etc. Very central, several restaurants and cafes around. The area is nice. The staff was helpful, the room was clean and of a very good size. Was impressed by the fact, that herbal tea was available in my room, not just black english tea. Also I was lucky and they have upgraded my room! The only negative point that I can mention about this hotel is a ridiculously expensive breakfast. The selection of the buffet is good and it is tasty, but the price is just unbelievable. On my first morning I had my breakfast in the hotel, as I did not know the area yet, but on the second day went to a cafe nearby - same tasty breakfast, but 2.5 times cheaper! Would definetely recommend this hotel, but have your breakfst outside - will save a lot of money!

title: Brilliant Stay
text: We arrived after a very wet 10 minute walk from Euston Station to the news we had been upgraded to an Executive Suite. The room was wonderful and spacious with plenty of hanging space but a little short on drawer space. The bathroom was bright and airy with a good shower and a big bath. The step up into the bath was quite a tall one due to the fitted shower screen, but we managed this ok. As we were celebrating my husbands 50th birthday I had pre ordered a Champagne breakfast in the room. My husband was amazed at the quality of the full English breakfast, saying it was the best he had ever had. He can be quite fussy! The visit to The British Museum that followed was a very jolly one after enjoying the bottle of Champagne after breakfast. A brilliant start to our stay in London. We were centrally located for visits to Covent Garden, Leicester Square and Shaftsbury Avenue theatre land. The continental breakfast we had the following 2 mornings was ample with a good selection to choose from. We will definitely be back when visiting London again. Thank you.

title: Good trip spoilt by unhelpful receptionist
text: We had booked two double rooms here to treat my mother for her 60th birthday and arrived with our luggage in the morning and did all the admin before going off for the day, we were advised that check in was at 3pm. We returned at 5.15pm intending to get ready as we were going out for cocktails at Clairdges at 6pm. The receptionist, Agnes, advised one of our rooms was not ready, we expressed our dissatisfaction and she failed to even apologise but just smirked at us. In the end we requested to speak to her manager and lo and behold the room was ready almost immediately. I requested that she book us a taxi to Claridges at 6.15pm and we went to get ready, on returning to reception at the allotted time, she had failed to book us a taxi and again smirked when we noted our displeasure, another staff member went out and hailed us a taxi. All other staff were courteous and helpful but Agnes was non communicative and rude. The rooms were large and clean and if it hadn't been for her I would be providing a much better review.

title: Good location. Decent rooms. Good value.
text: The Claredon is one of five Grange hotels that were converted from a row of terrace houses originally built in 1815, and the architecture retains its splendid Georgian façade. Located in Bloomsbury, the hotel is short walk from the British Museum and the Domination Theatre, and within the same tube zone for Soho and a number of other theatres. Our room was clean, a good size, and complete with all the basics (TV, hair-dryer, safe, wifi, kettle for tea and coffee), however the wallpaper was coming loose in some places. The bed was a full-double, but the mattress was too hard to be comfortable. Although we were on the third floor at the end of the passage, there was still a bit of ambient noise that filtered into the room. The shower had good pressure, and plenty of hot water. The staff were exceptionally friendly, always welcoming and anxious to assist. We didn't eat at the hotel. In all, it was a very pleasant stay.

title: Fab location and lovely room
text: Stayed in room 209 which overlooks a garden , loved the fact I could open the windows wide and let air in . The room was spacious and clean with a large bathroom (access difficult to bath if a bit wobbly as the shower door could get in the way ) . Lots of products to use i.e. Shower gel etc . The kettle in the small cupboard made me slightly nervous but worked out ok , the bed very firm and comfortable . There is a safe in the wardrobe too . Breakfast plentiful and staff very attentive , good choices for a small hotel . A tiny criticism was that my tv remote didn't work when I was in bed as it was too far away but I survived . Excellent location but still quiet . Would definitely recommend it if for central London trips

title: good hotel
text: was a very good clean hotel the only problem was the heating in the room wouldn't turn off and the staff didn't seem to know how to solve the problem but they were very nice and this wouldn't put me off going back . very comfy bed and very clean

title: Great location but let down by basics
text: This hotel is well located in Bloomsbury and the building is lovely. The hotel has many strengths including friendly, welcoming staff. The atmosphere in the hotel is great and the architecture splendid. The room (overlooking the gardens) is a very good size and well appointed. It is a shame that basics are not so well sorted. The plumbing was poor - couldn't have a bath since hot water came out too slowly to fill the bath! Shower was seriously slow. Although not the fault of the hotel, we were kept awake from children running around and loud talking from a room above for several hours in the night. We heard every creaking floorboard! Did share these concerns with the reception staff who did apologise but nothing else. I say in many hotels and even Premier Inn give you a complete refund for less disturbance! All in all, it is a great hotel but really needs to address the basics.

title: Great location and quaint feel
text: The hotel is in a great location, 200 metres from the British Museum. I had an Executive room which was at the front of the building, with a high ceiling, plenty of windows and a view of the street. It's London so don't expect tranquility but I thought it was very acceptable. Hotel itself is quiet. Breakfast which seems to be included if you book direct was plentiful and reasonable quality. King size bed and plenty of space. Building only has three floors so if you like low rise it's a great choice. Only downsides: bathroom lighting wholly inadequate, windows in need of repair and some minor things like the phone just looked grim. However, very clean and seemed like fair value for price paid. Would stay again.

title: Great Location, good hotel
text: The location is terrific. British Museum is just around the corner. West End shows are a short walk away. Underground stations all around. Excellent restaurants just an easy walk away. It was set on a very nice road, which felt well lit and very safe. Hotel security is also good. Room was spacious (although I did got an upgrade so can't comment on regular rooms). The room looked out on a quiet square. The bed was very comfortable and the facilities and furnishings were good. Only small disappointment was that the hair dryer did not work. I reported this on the room survey provided by the hotel and they had emailed an apology before I got home. I would recommend this hotel to my friends.

title: Pleasant stay
text: I was lucky enough to end up in an executive room. Spacious, lovely decor and furniture, beautiful, spacious (again) and presumably recently renovated bathroom. I guess with this hotel group it depends essentially on the kind of room you end up in as they have everything from very low end to decent to nice. Breakfast was perfectly acceptable, I had wifi included (hate paying extra for such a basic amenity). The aircon didn't work at all (if it exists), so the room was variously hot or cold, depending on the day during a time in October when the weather was - shall we say - variable. The bar prices were very reasonable, and it is quite lovely to sit with a glass of wine in the little backyard/garden. It is apparent that management ships guests around their various properties, always under the guise of an 'upgrade'. So you shouldn't bet on staying where you have booked. A somewhat disturbing business practice. That is a worry as these properties really are not all of the same quality. Let the buyer beware, I guess. - There also is a bizarre policy where they charge your credit card on checking with 20 GBP that you will receive back on check-out. Anyone coming from overseas will be charged by their bank for these currency transactions. So, this hotel hobby costs the customer, while it truly serves no purpose (I haven't seen this in any other hotel I ever stayed in).

title: Great hotel, Large rooms, Good food, Excellent service. Will stay here again.
text: I stayed at this hotel for four nights in November 2017. My stay was very enjoyable. I was greeting by a helpful, friendly receptionist who was very efficient. She confirmed my booking and politely asked whether I would like to leave a deposit for incidentals. I declined which she said that was fine (Ignore the previous review about discrimination. I am white and was dressed very smartly and I still got asked for a deposit, very politely! This is quite normal in most hotels I stay at) There is a lift to each floor and my room was large and well furnished. Most of all it was very clean. The bathroom was modern and well fitted with good toiletries provided. Lots of soft clean towels. My Executive room had three very large windows overlooking the quiet street below. There is a small park at the end of the road. The heating in the room was excellent and easy to control. There was a kettle and plentiful supply of tea, coffee and milk with even a few biscuits. There was plenty of wardrobe and drawer space, a useful desk area and two armchairs. There is a very large safe in the room, big enough to fit a laptop in which is very useful. I did have a slight problem with the shower screen and, when I reported it to reception, the Duty Manager (Mwasa I think) gave it his immediate attention. This was then followed up by the General Manager, Mr Yash Rai, who made sure that the problem was solved quickly and to my satisfaction. All hotels have problems sometimes but the test of a good hotel is how they deal with a problem. In my case, the problem was dealt with correctly, quickly and efficiently. Full marks to Yash and Mwasa. Breakfast is buffet style with a wide selection of cereals, fresh fruit, yoghurts, pastries, meat, cheese, bread, etc. etc. Tea, coffee and hot toast is quickly brought to your table. You can eat as much as you like too! I didn't have the cooked breakfast but it looked good so I will try this next time. I have seen some other reviews and I have to disagree with the bad ones. The bed in my room was huge and very comfortable. The bathroom was spotless (which is very important). There was no noise problem. I have stayed at several of the Grange hotels in the same street and, in my view, this is the best. The others are good too but the service at this hotel is first class. I will certainly stay at this hotel whenever I am in London. I recommend it very highly.

title: Great hotel, good location - definitely recommended
text: This hotel was lovely, two couples stayed there for the weekend, there for the NFL Football at Wembley. We were there early and were still accommodated and just because we asked we were upgraded to king size beds and suite and couldnt be more comfortable. Staff friendly and very helpful - nothing too much trouble. Breakfast was continental and was all fresh and replenished before even trays finished, with as much toast as you wanted - Definitely a great start to the day. Great location, 6 min walk from tube and 20 mins from Trafalgar square walking. Told them we would be back :-)

title: London Weekend Treat
text: We booked to see a Musical and stayed one night at the Clarendon which is part of the Grange Group of hotels. It is conveniently situated with a secure car national car park very close by. The staff were extremely welcoming and polite and we had a lovely bedroom. Although the en suite was large, there was no heating in it, so no-where to dry towels and the floor tiles were freezing. The room and en suite were spotlessly clean. The only negative comment is that the breakfast room was too small for the number of guests which also seemed to cater for next door. Our table was so cramped into the corner that I had to disturb the next table guest every time I wanted to go to the buffet table. The buffet was average and because it was so busy, the staff did not have time to stock up regularly. There did not seem to be anyone in overall charge of the restaurant so the young girls, although very polite and willing, needed a guiding hand to be more efficient. The coffee was very strong and cold, despite a request for hot milk, which was cold milk just put into a warmed up jug! As we had a busy weekend booked, it did not ruin our stay, but if you wanted to linger and enjoy a leisurely breakfast, this would not be for you.

title: Nice Room - Shame we didn't book this hotel.
text: We actually booked a room at the Buckingham next door only to arrive and be told that we had been "allocated" a room in the Clarendon. We would have had a kitchenette at the Buckingham which we did not have at the Clarendon but accepted anyway. The room was fine although if the weather had been any better the lack of air conditioning would have been an issue and it could have done with a fridge or minibar. We discovered after our stay that we could in fact have booked the Clarendon for considerably less money than we had paid (thinking we would be staying at the Buckingham). We were not offered any refund of the difference in price and consequently feel deceived and cheated. Apparently, this booking practice is perfectly normal at this hotel. They obviously accept bookings for the Buckingham from various places like lastminute.com and once they have your money they simply "allocate" rooms at their other, presumably less desirable, hotels. We will not be booking any Grange hotels in the future but as long as you are aware of this booking practice and get a good rate this hotel would be ok.

title: Horrible! Stay away!
text: Family room is a double w/ a sad and flimsy pullout sofa. Management would not remedy the poor conditions although they nearly admitted that they wouldn't sleep on such a bed. No integrity. Stay away.

title: Lovely! Ignore the bad reviews!
text: Just got back from a 2 night stay in the Clarendon, and having read some bad reviews on here I was a little worried we would be dissapointed, but no! far from it! Our room was massive with a queen sized bed with the comfiest mattress I have ever slept on, at the back of the hotel overlooking the garden. Decor was nice, flat screen tv with freeview, and nice clean bathroom. Its in a great location on a quiet side street just off Russell Square - a stones throw from the British Museum and walking distance to Soho, Totenham Court Road, Oxford street etc. There are some nice cafe's near by for Breakfast. We also got room service which I thought was good quality and not *too* expensive, although bear in mind I had never got room service before so was highly excited about the whole experience! We had a paper left outside our door in the morning (all be it a business one so not my cup of tea). The staff are all really friendly. I would deffinately book this hotel again.

title: Very nice hotel in perfect location
text: Very nice hotel in perfect location in city center of London. I had very large room, with bath and toilet. There was coffe table with chairs, kettle, TV and radio. Few negative things: 1) I expected a fridge in room in the 4 stars hotel. 2) Noise on the street 3) In the morning it was quite cold in the room

title: 2 night stay
text: This is the second time we have stayed at The Clarendon, our room was on the 3rd Floor, lovely and quiet. We took advantage of an offer which included continental breakfast with the option of upgrading to a full English. Excellent breakfast. The staff were very helpful and we even managed to check in early. We have stayed other Grange Hotels and would stay here again. Close to Russell Square and Holborn Tube Stations and easy walking distance to Covent Gardens and Oxford Street.

title: Great Location
text: Just back from a one night stay mid week, Nice looking Hotel from Outside and just as good inside. Nice room(a little on the small side) but fine for the one night we were there, good staff and the whole place was very clean. On the down side , it was sooooooooooooo HOT ! we were in room 205 and had to sleep with the window open as it was so Hot, even after I turned the Radiator off, No Air Con in the room which a shame. We didn't have breakfast as we both thought that £23 for a Full English and £17 for the Continental was too expensive, I'd booked direct with the Hotel and a double room for one night was £166.00, which to me should have included Breakfast. On the Good side, the Staff were very Good, it was Very Clean and also very handy for Covent Garden etc, just a short walk away,We would stay there again.

title: Here for a concert at the o 2
text: In London to see Celine Dion at the O2.great little hotel staff were very helpful and very friendly.The rooms were clean and comfortable if a little hot tea and coffee were available in the room with a good bathroom.the location was in a quite street near two tube station and plenty of cafe's and restaurants it's different from the large chain hotel's but is perfect for a short stay in London we did not eat in the hotel but great eateries near by.It's a bit of a trail if you are going to the O2but great for shopping and the sites of London.

title: Good Cool Weather Hotel
text: We were there during a heat wave, so the lack of AC made sleeping tough sometimes. The rooms are well-appointed, and the bed was comfortable. Getting into and out of the bathtub is challenging. The lobby bar is insufficiently stocked and cramped in size. Employees are polite and helpful. The location is excellent. Bloomsbury Square is at one end of the block and Russell Square at the other end. British Museum is around the corner, and Russell Square tube station a short walk away. Some good restaurants and pubs are in the area. No free wifi.

title: Not really 4 stars
text: We booked this through Lastminute.com's Secret Hotels offer. It was described as a Luxurious Georgian Boutique 4* Hotel in Bloomsbury. It certainly was spotlessly clean and smartly decorated one of several such hotels in a listed terrace in Bedford Place. The staff were charming. The problem was everything was so petite - narrow corridors, small rooms - in contrast to the description 'spacious and luxurious' on the website. We were booked into a Superior Double Room but apparently we were upgraded to a De-luxe room but it was quite cramped and they might have left us wee biscuit to have with our tea in the room . The noise from the street was loud and at times boisterous most of the time, though I can't fault the hotel for that. The location was good and it's quite a pleasant hotel but 4 Stars? - I can't see why. I don't think we'll use Lastminute again for a hotel. Sorry!

title: near British museum
text: no air conditioning system, no bar in the room, uncomfortable pillows, poor insulation with other rooms ( can hear other talks, walking), too small double bed room, great location, friendly and helpful staff,

title: Nice and Comfortable
text: I stayed here with my daughter for 3 nights in February whilst seeing sights Was very clean and staff helpful We didnt take breakfast at the hotel but it did look nice a filling we chose to use the close cafes which were near by and reasonable A great base for sight seeing close to all amenities would definately return

title: Nice
text: Nice clean, quiet hotel right in the heart of London. Staff were very helpful and welcoming. Breakfast was nice too. Continental is included in the cost but you can have a cooked English breakfast for a few more pounds. Again it was nice and fresh and the staff were quick to help if you needed any extra coffee/toast etc. Safes in room are available so you can leave your valuables without worry. Would stay here again.

title: Nothing special
text: Booked a weekend break and wanted something a little more special than a Travelodge. Researched and found this hotel on lastminute. Photos looked good and price was reasonable but didn't include breakfast. Location is OK with Russel Square tube a short walk away but we decided to walk everywhere this weekend. Reception staff are pleasant enough. The room we are in is tiny with the end of the bed virtually touching the wall. Clean but not spotless. Large watermarks on bathroom taps, large crumbs near coffee/tea making area. White stain!! On the brown bedroom throw. Net curtains ripped. Bed was comfortable but noisy and squeaked every time you rolled over. Pillows were square and full of air!! TV has basic channels and nothing more. Shower was hot and reasonably powerful. In summary you can get better for your money. In hindsight a Travelodge at Covent Garden would have been cleaner, quieter, better located and better value for money. (I've stayed there many times before). Although this place isn't bad I wouldn't stay here again.

title: Weekend Break in London
text: My son booked this hotel for us as a present. So we had no idea about the place until our arrival. The staff were very welcoming and gave necessary information for our stay eg times of breakfast, location of bar and location of lift. Our room was lovely, large and scrupulously clean. It was at the back of the hotel and overlooked a lovely garden area separating the street running parallel to the rear. When I looked out of the window before going to bed I could see a man standing under one of the trees. He was still there the following morning standing in exactly the same position! I noticed that there were other 'people' in the park area which was a lovely place. The bathroom was beautifully clean and adequately equipped. The huge bed was very comfortable. The only problem was the hairdryer which was kept in a drawer and was the sort that you had to hold the button down to keep it going - very annoying. The bar was a peculiar little area adjacent to reception which had a few very uncomfortable chairs and not very attentive staff. Breakfast was a pleasant experience with a choice of continental or cooked. We were booked in for continental breakfast which was adequate but the price was £17.50! Perhaps I'm not use to London prices but that does seem extortionate. The location of the hotel was brilliant. Whilst there we were able to walk everywhere and is within easy reach of Covent Garden, Soho. We even walked from Westminster bridge. Checkout was a painless, quick process. I would certainly stay here again and would recommend it to anyone.

title: Garden View in Busy London
text: This small hotel is a reasonable value, especially over the weekends, for downtown London. It is on a fairly quiet street a block and a half from the British Museum. The back rooms face a small garden, but back up to a privately owned large garden that you can look at. So, even though you are in the middle of this huge city, it is peaceful. The double room was small, but had a desk in it. The bathroom, and shower were very narrow, and the step in and out of the tub was about 20 inches, which is really tall. No fridge, microwave or A/C, but there was a hot water kettle and tea bags. Staff was friendly. There is a small bar area downstairs and a lift. Continental breakfast was OK, but quite expensive - over 17 pounds

title: Not refined!
text: A bit disappointed. It seems the staff here struggle a little with English as it was hard to get the exact location of the hotel before arrival. When I arrived the receptionist couldn't advise me whether we were within the congestion zone or not (they are). The bar is shocking, basically 6 chairs around a table next to the reception area and the bar man is fingers and thumbs - don't expect a Whisky Sour here! The rooms are very comfortable BUT... at around 0545 a door kept banging from below (I stayed on the first floor) and it continued at around every minute. At around 0600 I called reception to ask it to stop and it did for about 20 mins and then it continued maybe every 30 secs. Clearly this is a health and safety issue which they have to adhere to but after a great night at the opera and a late night with my dad this is not what you expect from this calibre of hotel. I accidentally booked this hotel as my father wanted the Clarendon in Mayfair - clearly this exemplifies the difference! There was also an issue with breakfast. It would seem I had ordered breakfast for one room and not the other. When this was mentioned at breakfast they would not honour the mistake and charged me £25 for the extra breakfast rather that the additional £9 at the time of booking. Customer service? No - you are number here.

title: Excellent location
text: As the title says, this hotel is situated in an excellent location, just a few minutes' walk from Holborn tube (off Southampton Row). The hotel has been created from four adjoining Georgian London townhouses, so there are several staircases and corridors and I got lost once or twice! The receptionand bar areas are very appealing and comfortable. The 2nd floor room I was originally allocated (a nice double) had a completely dead TV, and as it couldn't be fixed I was immediately moved (and upgraded!) to a ground floor kingsize room with two sofas. As it was at the back of the hotel, it was nice and quiet. The decor was a little tired and the bathroom lighting somewhat dim, but it was spotlessly clean. My only criticism was that (for my taste) the mattress was very hard and I couldn't get comfortable at all. Breakfast was very good - plenty of choice, and the waiting staff were very attentive. There's a restaurant just along the road in a sister hotel, and plenty of cafes and restaurants in nearby Southampton Row - even a Tesco if all you want is a snack. Overall, I would be happy to stay here again and recommend it to others.

title: over rated!!
text: Charged far too much for what was on offer, customer service wasn't great. Considering how much I paid I would of expected breakfast with the room. I wouldn't recommend or stay there again. It didn't help that I had problems getting there due to snow, no one on the other side of the phone could even be bothered to help and kept trying to forward me on to someone else.

title: Enjoyed our stay
text: After 4 nights at a poor quality Paris hotel, Clarendon proved to be great value for the money. We had two rooms: A large executive corner room for my three children and a double room for me and my husband. Rooms are clean and comfortable. Location is not very central - it's not on the common hop on hop off bus route but if you and your children don't mind walking or taking the tube, this hotel is definitely a great value. Breakfast is not included and for almost GBP 18 per person, we opted out. Staff were friendly and helpful. This hotel is part of the Bloombury group of hotels. Never heard of them before this experience but would certainly look for their hotels as quality is quite good for money. (Maybe if they had a location closer to Trafalgar Square ...)

title: Nice hotel in a good location
text: We chose the Clarendon for it's location - very close to the British Museum and easy walk to the tube for access to the rest of London. It's a smaller hotel on a row of hotels all owned by Grange. The room was a decent size for London and it was clean. The biggest problem - no air conditioning. As a Texan where it would be insane for a hotel to not have air conditioning, it's not something I paid much attention to when booking hotels for our trip to the UK, but apparently its fairly common for hotels to have no AC. I'm assuming it typically isn't a problem as the UK is usually significantly cooler than Texas, but as luck would have it we were in London on the hottest day of the year (like, record-setting heat). The hotel staff provided us a fan and we opened up the window to get some air flow. Unfortunately, we still slept pretty poorly despite the comfortable bed due to the heat. The staff were courteous and helpful, so if we ever returned to London when it's not 90 degrees outside, we would stay here again.

title: Great location
text: This hotel has a great location, easy access to a tube station (Vauxhall) makes everything within reach. Walking distance to the Tate Britain. Picturesque views of Big Ben and Westminster. The staff are very friendly and helpful. Highly recommend.

title: Superb staff,hotel and location.
text: All staff were friendly and attentive without being overbearing.Special occasion even remembered by a much appreciated upgrade enhancing our stay.Great location we even walked to theatre land.Rooms spacious and clean.Breakfast buffet recommended.Will return!

title: Great value weekend break.
text: We stayed here for two nights in May, having booked with Omega Travel, Lancaster, and travelled down on Virgin Trains from Glasgow. Our room was clean comfortable and well equipped. The decor was modern, although we found dog in the mural a little odd. Breakfast was plentiful and tasty and the staff were efficient and friendly. The hotel is only 10 minutes walk from Vauxhall tube station, and the same in the other direction to Westminster Bridge. I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel.

title: Spectacularly spacious and clean
text: We booked this hotel last minute for a London trip and was more than happy with our stay. The staff were very happy and helpful. Our room was not overlooking the river but backed onto the railway line, however it was quiet with only a faint rumble heard in the morning. The room and especially the bathroom was probably the nicest i have stayed in. Very spacious, contemporary design, warm and comfortable. Bathroom was so clean and new looking and every thing modern and sparkling. Would certainly recommend.

title: for a London riverside hotel with close proximity to Waterloo railway station
text: I stayed at this hotel, for the purposes of a business trip. seminar and conference that I attended was run at this hotel. Staff are well presented and friendly amicable with a positive atmosphere. The bars and restaurants are on average pretty good. clean, comfortable and in the heart of the city.

title: Alarm System Failure - Again
text: It's the third time I (and the rest of the hotel guests) have been woken up at 2:45am by the alarm system. Having spent over 15k in the last 6 months between this and the sister hotel next door... This is my last night at this place. They claim it was a system failure and nothing could be done, its the third time in a month and they should get it fixed. The earlier review about bar staff ignoring you and not serving you for ten minutes is also true.

title: SMART
text: A very smart ,professional hotel overlooking the river thames and in good walking distance of some major tourist sites.I asked for a room witha view of the river thames and i did however my room also overlooked a noisey building site which i think could of been mentioned prior to booking. did not spoil our stay though.

title: Excellwnrn
text: Excellent in a very good location . The room had a fantastic view . Good service and very helpful staff always ready to help you . Gym with good machine and 4 tread mills . Breakfasrt was bit busy . Need to improve quality of food

title: Great hotel, reasonable rates
text: Very nice and clean hotel, all the modern amenities, nice to have the North American plugs in the rooms, well kept, good room service options. Check in/check out was easy and smooth with friendly staff. Concierge was very helpful and so were the staff at the entrance Very good location with a nice view

title: Great Stay :-)
text: Just a quick review to say that the stay at this hotel was very very good. Very helpful polite staff, great rooms, well equipped and nothing is too much trouble. One of the best in my opinion in this area. It is 5-10 mins walk from Vauxhall tube station and has a 24 hr garage and a convenience store nearby to buy snacks, soft drinks, nibbles etc.

title: We liked Lambeth
text: We ended up at this very classy hotel via a blind-booking site. Needless to say, the hotel was excellent, service impeccable, It introduced us to an area we were unfamiliar with, Lambeth, on the south side of the Thames. The pleasant riverside walk just across the street led to the more touristy areas of London Eye, Parliament, etc., so convenient to the main sites but out of the crowds. The surrounding area was quiet, tree-lined residential with just enough shops and restaurants to keep it interesting.

title: Building works
text: Disappointed with workmen outside my room every time we went to our room. Workmen noisy, especially first thing in the morning, plus the noise from drills etc. Dust sheets down outside our room, and a terrible smell of glue from where the workmen were working. If I had known this I wouldn’t have booked my stay at this hotel. Nice thing to remember for a first stay in London.

title: Very good
text: Good location just in front of thames river and very close to metro and bus station of vauxhall and close to big ben and parlamant houses , clean and convenient and sutable for family with very good staff

title: A great night's stay
text: Great location, room very clean, comfortable and quiet with a good view overlooking the river. A great welcome from the Bellhops on entering. Service was very good but I must call out the Concierge team and Mohammed in the Breakfast Club Lounge, a great friendly good morning welcome. Breakfast was plenty and a good quality. Easy walk across the River to House of Parliament or along the embankment to the London Eye. Buses stop outside and provide another good option for getting around. Would definitely come back again and recommend to others

title: On the Thames
text: A modern hotel that is clean, comfortable and spacious. Contemporary design with large bed. It's between Vauxhall and Westminister and you could walk along the river to major attractions like Big Ben, Houses of Parliament, Westminister Abbey etc. Vauxhall Tube was about a 8 minute walk.

title: All's well that ends well!!
text: We chose this hotel from quite an extensive list of higher priced (than is normal for us!) hotels in the center of London as we wanted a bit of a treat and a change from the usual Premier Inn type of hotel we stay in. Check in was handled extremely politely and efficiently and we were giveen a room on the 7th floor with quite a decent view of the south of London over the railway lines. The view of the balcony, however, was NOT nice. It was literally painted in bird poop. The room was advertised as a Superior room but to be honest it was tiny although very nicely decorated with a good modern bathroom. It was only after finding the previous occupant's hair in the bathroom that I finally asked to see the guest relations manager and invited him up to our room to show him the reasons for my disquiet. He duly visited and inspected the view and the hairs and although he told us the room was a standard room even though it is described as superior we really couldn't fault his desire and willingness to ensure the hotel guests are happy. Not only did he upgrade us TWICE he also, on learning the visit was to treat my girlfriend for her birthday, sent us a bottle of posh (for us!) fizz and a selection of lovely chocolates to our newer and bigger room. This kind of service and attention to guest desires is exactly the kind of treatment that will have us back again. The guest relations manager, James, deserves to be noted for his efforts. The hotel is lovely. Right on the Thames embankment and about a five to ten minute walk to Westminster bridge and the London eye. Door staff that are attentive, floor staff that are polite and welcoming and even cleaners that give lovely smiles when you say hello to them...which you should do! The restaurants are well maintained with a great selection of foods for all tastes although the mysterious vibrating tables in the lower one was funny!! Would I stay here again? Yes, I would, although I'd pay the little extra for a bigger room than the superior next time!! All in all, well done Park Plaza...well done James!

title: Great breakfast staff
text: Really enjoyed my stay at Plaza Riverbank over 3 weeks in August 2017, delighted by incredible breakfast staff aproach, fresh great food in the morning, warm atmosphere. ...special thank to Elena member of the breakfast team on the first floor. Overall great experience. .. Definitely will recommend. Razvan

title: Outstanding staff throughout
text: The room was clean, well furnished, aircon worked great, restaurant & bar were excellent with superb views over the river to the house of commons, but what really made this trip for me was the quality of the staff. I was working in, as well as staying at the hotel & from my first contact with the concierge to my departure, every single member of hotel staff I encountered was friendly, helpful, considerate & efficient from management right through to loading bay operatives & kitchen staff. I can honestly say I've never experienced such a high standard of organisation in any other hotel.

title: Miss chloe rigg
text: Amazing hotel great atmosphere very welcoming friendly staff very clean great amenities couldnt fault this hotel, great room with excellent views executive lounge very relaxing had the best stay here ever stayed here to celebrate my 21st birthday.

title: Absolutely freezing room. The heating is non existant.
text: The room is so cold, bathroom is shockingly freezing it's unbearable. Housekeeping have given me 1tiny fan heater, that's keeps cutting out because it overheat's. They are not able to provide a second heater. It's so cold I will have to sleep in the dressing gown. Totally unacceptable. I will never come here again.

title: Terrible
text: My friend and I got back to our hotel after an event, wanting to have a shower, when a horrendous smell came out of the shower when we opened the door, we were kindly moves to a suite as the smell was so bad, however there was still a bad smell in that shower too but not as strong. The windows of our suite had some hand prints, the carpet was very dirty. For breakfast we decided to have it in the hotel howev after waiting 10 minutes we had to re order our drinks to be told 20 minutes later that they don't have decaf. The staff were nice but the organisation of breakfast was terrible! The sausages and bacon were not replenished, we had to wait another 20 minutes to be able to fill out plates with the food. No one payed attention to us when we wanted a knife we had to find one on another table. Shame because the hotel has a lot of potential! But it was definitely not worth the money we spent and we are very disappointed

title: Good but hot and noisy
text: Rooms were clean, but were very hot, air conditioning was set to winter settings, hot air only? Isn't the reason you have air conditioning is to cool a hot room. Party in the next room went on all night from 0130 to about 0500, phoned reception to complain, it still went on, I asked in the morning but was told they could not here any party, funny there was empty wine bottles in the corridor should have been a clue. It was our 40th wedding anavercery so speciale, but spoilt because of no sleep for two nights.

title: Great Stay
text: Recently there with my sister for a few days. Great location close enough to the Metro but in a nice quiet area. Great experience from the start. Tony at the concierge desk was extremely helpful sending us to a wonderful tea house and pub not in a tourist area. Very local and wonderful food and atmosphere. He was also very helpful arranging tranfers to the airport. Highly recommend a stay there when in London.

title: Well located for having fun
text: This hotel is close to Vauxhall tube station for fast access to all London attractions (museums, shopping, theatres, etc.) It is also good for walks along the Thames, visting the Southbank Centre, restaurants, etc. Our room was an upgrade with a riverview which we found extremely comfortable. We enjoyed sitting in our room and watching the boats go by in the evening. Lovely stay!

title: Really a first-rate hotel!
text: I had the pleasure to stay at Riverbank Park Plaza Hotel for 3 nights, and I warmly recommend this excellent hotel with great service and hospitality.The room was very tasteful furnished and had a marvellous view of the river Thames, the Houses of Parliament and Big Ben. The bed was most comfortable and the "marble"-bath-room was equipped with bath as well as separate shower. All staff really made their best to make my stay as pleasant as possible. The Asian- inspired restaurant served a superb dinner.I would love to stay at this hotel again.

title: useful tourtis venue
text: good location for central tourist attractions. Classy building and facilities. comfortable bed and sheets. Tea and coffee facilities. Tower block with 15 floors, but very efficient lifts. Not all rooms have river views and some look out onto adjacent hotel windows

title: The cold shoulder..............
text: I booked this hotel via Hotwire and got a great price, i think it was circa £80 for the night. From a location point of view its not great. Its on the wrong side of the river for most tourist's. the nearest tube station is Vauxhall but i wouldn't want to make that walk too late at night or allow my wife to walk it late on her own. The hotel is very stylish with a great bar and the rooms are well appointed albeit slightly too close to the main railway line to Waterloo, but not too much noise. I had a major issue with my rooms air-conditioing in that it remained on all night at its lowest temperature, my stay was in December and it would have been warmer outside. I had to sleep with my head under the duvet, the shower was bliss but i hurriedly got dressed. My feet were still numb with cold as a stood at reception and asked, well demanded that they visit the room to validate my story......they didn't. If i was at a premier inn i would have received a refund, all i got was the offer of an coffee! I was told that the next time i booked i would be well looked after, had the email of the duty manager and we kept in touch. I emailed to book another room and bearing in mind i paid £80 last time.......£256!!!!! In summary not a great location, a good hotel with 1970's style customer service. If you get it at a great price go for it, if not then keep on looking.

title: Gets the job done with a nice touch
text: We booked this hotel using one of those features, pick the location, stars, pay a discounted rate, and then you find out the hotel name. The lobby and restaurants look great (we didn't eat there) and the rooms were nice and clean. Although a great view of Big Ben (because you are across the river) and London Eye, it's a bit removed from things. There is construction on either side. When leave the building, make sure you go right toward Big Ben, if you go left, it gets seedy, broken glass in the street, clubs open and people lining up in mini skirts even on Sunday at 10:30 am to get in. Over, if you are site seeing and just need a place to crash at night, this place is great. If you are honeymooning or looking for luxury, this is not the place.

title: Only a notch above a budget hotel
text: I realise the hotel has ongoing construction as it expands upwards by five storeys, but it is currently in a dire state. Staff are, as always, amazing

title: Very nice staff
text: The hotel staff very friendly and very accommodating. Location was good and we got a very fair price. There was construction outside our window, but I didn't mind it for the price since we didn't spend much time in the room.

title: Great location, and pretty cool design
text: My partner and I stayed in this hotel for our 4 day trip in London! Pros: good customer service. The rooms were great and I really loved the design and lighting. The beds were clean and comfortable. The carpet was kinda weird but it was carpet and it didn't feel dirty on my bare feet which is a big plus for me. The room was spacious and the bathroom was awesome! She could take a shower while I took a bath across from her. Close enough to walk to a lot of the sights but far enough away not to feel too guilty about eating everything in sight. 24 hour room service with really good food for late night munchies. A really nice restaurant and bar. It was my favorite hotel we stayed at out of the 3 on our adventure. Cons: there was a construction site outside our room window and you couldn't turn the air on since it was winter, I didn't mind opening the window though. I would stay here again.

title: Christmas
text: Well on arrival was so impressed, The hotel was so friendly and warm Was a great location we just had the best time ever... DON was lovely!!😘 Will return to this hotel for sure. It was close to the tube, lovely walk along the river just 20 minuets from thee eye 19/10 for me

title: Lovely Hotel
text: Lovely, modern luxury hotel well located for Westminster. Great facilities, excellent bar and restaurant, and fabulous views over the river and Big Ben. Also handy for the City. Short stroll from Vauxhall tube station.

title: A nice hotel ruined!
text: Stayed here for a night in February, not a location for holidaymakers although you can see the houses of Parliament the location is not great. Room was fine apart from the TV not working at first and the wardrobe not opening properly. Terrible outlook over the railway line! Was told I could upgrade to a river view for £40 but considering the room was £100 not worth it! The temperature was either arctic or desert - not ideal. Continuous noise alll through the night which sounded like someone was trying to rip apart the room with a wrecking ball, we phoned reception who said they would send someone up to investigate but they never materialised. Avoid - there are much better hotels available for the same price in better locations.

title: Surprise Location!!
text: Was worried about the location and getting around the city, traveling to Farnham, we were Happy with the location and the Rooms were great. We had a river view with one bedroom, which were very clean, we had trouble with drains, but they were taken care of right away. The staff were they to help!! Like that we were out of the craziness of the city but close enough to be in it too. Will go back!!

title: Great location
text: We recently spent two nights at the Park Plaza Riverbank in London. You can't beat the location! Just a short walk to Big Ben, The London Eye, and the Westminster Bridge. Can also walk to Buckingham Palace, Churchill War Rooms, Horse Guards, etc. Rooms seem spacious compared to other London hotels. Good breakfast buffet and service. The hotel Evan arranged our transportation to and from Heathrow for us and we were please with the chauffer service they had arranged.

title: Back to its best!
text: This is my go-to hotel when staying in London and my last stay in 2016 I was disappointed with the quality of the room......so its pleases me greatly to be able to say that when I visited in April 2017, it was back to its best!!! As always the check-in process is good, the front of house staff are always polite, efficient and helpful. We stayed in an Executive room this time and actually had a partial river view, which was kinda cool. The room itself was comfortable, huge bed, nice linens and plenty of pillows. The room controls worked a treat (they control the lights, A/C etc) and this time the curtains did the job of totally blocking out the window! Bathroom, clean with plenty of towels for the two of us and nice complimentary toiletries (Elemis - one of my favourites!). We didn't eat at the hotel but did have a nightcap in the Chino Latino lounge. You do need to bear in mind that your are in the central London when you get your bar-bill and also that the standard measure is a double! Waiting services at your seats (lots of comfy options plus stools at the bar) so ideal place to chill out before retiring for the night. Sleep quality good and check out process fuss free.

title: The only bad review I’ve ever left
text: So this was pretty disappointing . The pictures on the website showers a great view of Westminster , we had a room which didn’t even have a window , just curtains with a tacky picture of Westminster stuck to the wall. No natural light , couldn’t open anything for any air , we didn’t even realise when it was night and day as it was so dark. The heating was broken, we spent all night awake and boiling hot , the cold tap didn’t work so we couldn’t even have a drink of water which wasn’t hot . The doormen were also really confrontational and rude , really rude to our Uber driver- I didn’t realise we weren’t supposed to order an Uber to the front of the hotel , but that was my fault not the Uber drivers and the way he spoke to him was vile. Overall , don’t waste your money on what should be a pretty decent hotel - it wasn’t

title: Sightseeing trip to London
text: The hotel was perfectly situated for our trip to Hampton Court as Vauxhall mainline service is 5 mins away and goes directly to Hampton Court in 35mins. Also perfectly situated for a walk to the Southbank, Westminster and Buckingham Palace by tube to Green Park, all of which were on our agenda. The hotel was really good if somewhat corporate, beds were comfortable, great bathroom facilities although the artificial lighting was a bit depressing with no natural light coming through the rooms towards the centre of the hotel. Also the charge for breakfast at £22 per head was ridiculous it should have been included in the price of the room. There are plenty of cafes near Vauxhall that do a reasonable breakfast.

title: Great value for price
text: Stayed here for a couple of nights. This hotel was booked with Priceline and it was with a little trepidation I went to Tripadvisor after it was allocated. Based on these reviews I called the hotel and asked for a river facing room if possible. I was not disappointed. Views from the room are iconic - to say the least -the wide expanse of window made for quite a spectacle at night. My stay coincided with a heat wave but there was no problem with the a/c as the room remained pleasantly cool- I even had to turn it up a notch overnight. The concierge was helpful and provided tickets for the London Eye -a very popular attraction- thankfully saving me an additional queue. I walked there and back ~ 15 mins each way, in the balmy evening along the the Embankment - very nice. Good sized room,comfy bed, lovely bathroom, blackout blinds which worked, iron and board, free Wifi and free standard tv channels - all helped make my stay pleasant and glitch free. Added to that breakfast at Chinos was a sheer delight and the dinner, whilst a little pricey, did not disappoint. I asked for a cab at checkout, the valet stepped outside and a taxi was pulling up to the front entrance in 3 mins flat. For those who fancy a bit more energetic, eco friendly means of transport, there is a Barclays Cycle Hire (Boris Bike) rank a few steps from the hotel.

title: Birthday trip
text: Lovely hotel well situated.Rooms were spacious and very clean Beds very comfortable staff pleasant and helpful The hotel was having work undertaken at the front of the building but it did not impact on my stay

title: Very stylish hotel in an offices area on South Bank
text: My friend and I stayed one night in August having room 936. We had previously stayed at the Park Plaza Westminster Bridge and the Riverbank was in the same style : modern, spacious and quality. I would judge it is much smaller. It is further from any public transport (Vauxhall is the nearest Tube), is located in an area of office buildings and has few restaurants roundabout (though we had a pleasant Italian lunch at Sirena's in Black Prince Road - about 100 metres away). I arrived earlier than expected but was checked in at 11.00 by friendly Reception. The room had a huge double bed with one great duvet. Very comfy. Room was well equipped with iron etc and kettle though we did not use these). There was a flat screen TV. The remore control seemed not to be working so I switched the TV off at the wall socket as I could see no other switch. We loved the walkin shower. I wish more hotels had these for older guests (who can have difficulty climbing into bath tubs) and there was a plentiful supply of towels. The piece of soap provided though was tiny and it was fortunate we did not need to wash too often! The room had a certain "style" which we both liked. When we are in London we use a range of hotels in the Accor, InterContinental and Hilton Groups. I reckon Park Plaza is well up the league. We paid £136. This did not include breakfast but we left very early and did not have it there.

title: Top Stop
text: Stayed here overnight for business nearby. This modern well presented hotel is a short walk from nearby tube stations and the efficient staff have you booked in quickly with keen valets to deliver any larger luggage. The spacious rooms are serviced by quick lifts and the rooms are clean, comfortable and well equipped with a choice of pillows and good black out curtains. We didn't experience the evening meals available but breakfast was managed well with a huge choice from the hot and cold buffet and regular coffee top ups. Overall a very enjoyable stay. Recommended.

title: Wonderful Luxury Home Experience for Families
text: Stayed with my two sons. We all had our own bedrooms with lovely views of the Thames with balcony, dining room, kitchen and two bathrooms. More importantly each had our own large TV's. We had free cocktails in the bar and rented free dvd's and ordered pizza in. An impressive luxury hotel without the huge cost. We usually pay the same money to be all squashed up in one room.£248. inc vat and breakfast. The breakfast was a little disappointing as I ordered veggie cooked breakfast and the eggs were not cooked at all (see-through) however, the waiter was very good and did not charge for the (additional charge)pancakes my sons had ordered. Will always use this place now in preference to other 5* Hotels in london - more space for your money, especially if travelling with your family

title: Not a good experience
text: Good hotel. Nice room. The view “no-river” has a railroad view. Good wifi. Near underground (5 mins). Difficult to find. My problems happened with the reservation. Not good comunication. qwertyuioplkjhgfdsazxccvvbbnmmkjhgf

title: Fantastic hotel!!
text: Wow this is a fantastic hotel on the other side of the river offering a fantastic stay! We booked on the internet for a two night weekend break for a special birthday treat. On arrival we checked in and when we told the hotel it was a birthday weekend they gave us an upgrade to an executive room. This really made the break extra special. The room was generous in size and had a large well presented bathroom with separate shower and bath. The room was spotless and offered mini bar, hair drier, free Wifi and ironing board and iron. The view was an oblique river view. Breakfast was included in our rate and was continental with hot buffet option. Nothing was to much trouble and the food was hot and plentiful. The restaurant was well staffed and clean. The hotel public areas were well presented and very clean. We did find, however, that the hotel has building work going on both sides. It didn't cause many disruption though and we weren't disturbed. The other problem we encountered was with a noisy guest next door. At 03.00 we contacted the manager, who, came straight up and spoke to the guest and we had peace. The next day they moved us to the other side of the hotel and all was well once more. This hotel is perfect for a nice weekend away and I would recommend it to any of my friends or family.

title: Brilliant stay and breakfast
text: Dont be taken in by the photos, our three rooms overlooked train tracks. The rooms themselves were modern and clean. Tube stations could have been closer but would stay again. The breakfast was over subscribed so got sent somewhere else.

title: Noisy
text: Booked hotel as part of a lastmin.com package deal with theatre tickets. I booked this as a surprise few days in London for my partner’s birthday. Room was nice and the room service staffs were very friendly. The reception staffs were not very friendly they just seemed like they didn’t want to help you. The noise pollution was unreal both of us could not sleep properly for 2 nights! For the price of £249.00 it should have been stated before booking!!!!! The position of the hotel was good but as you only stay here to sleep not impressed.

title: Comfortable nights sleep in a friendy hotel
text: Great hotel, perfect combination of clean and comfortable rooms and friendly staff, with the added bonus of good wifi coverage Recommend for people and particularly women travelling on their own, feel very safe and not anonymous.

title: Great Hotel
text: This hotel is clean, well-presented, smart, and comfortable, with very friendly staff, who are willing to help you out with any queries or difficulties. Any problems raised to them were solved as a matter of urgency and the stay was as pleasant and trouble-free as possible. All possible amenities are available, as is a comprehensive breakfast and exceptional concierge service. Highly recommended.

title: GREAT LOCATION
text: Situated close to the River Thames and within easy walking distance of Westminster this hotel could not possibly go wrong. Indeed it does everything pretty well . The rooms are well appointed , food good and surprisingly competitively priced and the staff helpful even though always busy. I would go back.

title: Disappointing compared to previous visits to other London Park Plaza property
text: We had a large of people booking a block of >10 rooms for 5 to more than a week.... but when several of our group members arrived early one morning to check in, the hotel refused to provide even one room for them to check in to freshen up. Then, we were told that there was no operator in the hotel to switch an incoming phone call to our rooms. After complaint, we had to dial out and the hotel would credit our calls. Wow! That's an unheard of!

title: Highly recommend
text: Really lovely hotel. Glitzy but classy. Great room and good value. Service in all areas of the hotel was superb. Asian fusion restaurant - not cheap but extremely good and well worth the money. They serve a variety of Bento box courses available between 6-7. They are cheaper than the main menu items and absolutely delicious. Perhaps worth noting that breakfast (Sunday), was very busy indeed with quite a queue for the food. May have been just particularly busy day... We stay in a number of London hotels and would definitely put this up there with the best.

title: Quaint central London hotel
text: i found this hotel thru Priceline.com and it satisfies the location prerequisite. It is a ten minutes walk from vauxhall tube station, a ten minutes walk to Westminster abbey & the parliament buildings, so convenient that way. The room isn't anything special over the top so it's more a 3+star room. The bathroom is big with both a tub and stand up shower. The lobby is big and service is courteous. The restaurant food I've not tried but it appears pricy. There is a nice pub next door called the rose. I'd recommend a try for budget and location.

title: excellent!
text: I have been meaning to write this review since Jan 2012. My boyfriend proposed to me in this hotel. We had a beautiful room with a riverside view and staff were so helpful. The rooms was very clean and everything looked well presented. This hotel will remain very special to both of us and we are planning to go back for another celebration very soon.

title: Becoming a favourite.
text: I have stayed at the Riverbank on a number of occasions and can recommend it. A large modern hotel, the rooms are excellent - larger than most London hotel rooms and with large bathrooms. Very well equipped (including DVD player) and some rooms have great views. Breakfast is comprehensive though the cooked version can be a bit lacking in freshness if it has been on the hotplate too long. You will need a large bank loan if you want anything from the mini-bar so I recommend the little shop almost next door which stays open until 11.00 and stocks most things. The only real disadvantage for many people is the location - it is a fair distance from the nearest tube and there are only a limited range of eating places in the immediate vicinity.

title: Excellent Service Good Base
text: This is a very pleasant hotel close to Vauxhall station. I stayed at this hotel whilst on business and would not hesitate to return. Wifi was very easily accessed and did not " drop out" of signal. The staff are very helpful and the room was well equipped. I had a view of Big Ben and the London eye which was very nice. The restaurant for evening meal was very good, however, breakfast in the basement was disappointing due to lack of any natural light and slow service. On second morning I had breakfast at Chino Latino which was much more pleasant. I did not upgrade to "room with view" until,I checked in as I find this a much cheaper option. Rooms are spacious and clean

title: Great stay!
text: Booked for one night stay in March. Great location, friendly staff and a clean, spacious room. Easy to get into central London and some great views to be had. I would definitely book here again for a weekend in London.

title: Poor value for money
text: Room not ready on arrival. Room smelly, unfinished and bathroom poorly furnished. Breakfast poor quality and served in a windowless basement room. Good location, but poor value for money and not up to the standard of other international hotels.

title: Disappointed
text: Recently stayed for three nights during London's unusually warm weather. The room never got cool and the carpet needs to be replaced. The only restaurant in the hotel is not children friendly. This is a hotel for business men. We have stayed at the Park Plaza at Westminister and were disappointed by the location, price and lack of cleanliness at this hotel. The bell hop was the friendliest and most helpful of the staff.

title: Great location, below average interior
text: This is one of the hotels that you get excited about when you know you will be staying there. Who wouldn't? The Houses of Parliament and the London Eye are right across the road. MI6 is a few blocks away. Lambeth Palace, Waterloo Station - great location. But inside, the hotel is in need of a facelift. It is shabby. Cigarette burns in the faded carpets. TV screens in room wiped over with a damp cloth. Minibars with broken locks and handles. Grubby net curtains that look out on to the other side of the hotel (in my room, anyway). Room service consisted of soggy pub food. The shower attachment was hanging off the wall. At first glance, it kinda looks OK. But the more time you spend, the more you see needs a major overhaul. And no on-sight public parking. If you are driving in, you will need to partake of their valet service at approx £35/day. The public areas are OK. The concierge area was having some work done to it while I was there. Other than that, staff were polite and courteous. Stay here if you must, or if the company is paying for it. But if you want a location that is clean, modern, has good food, and where you are not afraid to walk around in bare feet, then look elsewhere.

title: Great location, good value for money
text: We stayed in the hotel in April. The location is fab, just 5 minutes walk from the Parliament and London Eye. Breakfast was descent, clean rooms, kind staff. Only negative is lack of car park in the hotel. They have a service they use but it is £42 a night?? In Novotel - just 2 minutes walk from the hotel, you can park for £24 per night.

title: Great hotel, great location!
text: We enjoyed staying at the Park Plaza Riverbank. It was clean and had a great view. There was construction next to the hotel but you could see the river just past the next lot. We left early for the airport and had asked for a boxed breakfast. Unfortunately it was left on the desk and never offered to us. Just before walking out the door to catch our taxi we did grab it...

title: Great hotel
text: Have stayed here before - always a smart, professional service, and the hotel facilities are very good. The only downside is the location, which is just a smidgin out of the way if you want local restaurants or bars - you'll need to make a short taxi ride.

title: One of the best views of London
text: I have stayed at this hotel at least five times over the past years. It is always a very pleasant experience to stay at Riverbank Plaza. Some of the best things about this hotel are: location, friendly staff, and, most of all, the view of the Thames and Parliament. The hotel restaurant is pretty good -the breakfast buffet is well served and relatively affordable considering that London is a very expensive city. The hotel gym is perfect for a quick workout before starting your day. The rooms are very bright and modern. Overall, this is a great hotel for the price and for the VIEW!

title: Good hotel, good location
text: I stayed at the Riverbank Park Plaza 13-15 February on a business trip, along with a colleague. I was very impressed with the hotel and would certainly recommend it. The location was ideal for our course in a building close to the houses of Parliament. We arrived early on the Wednesday and the hotel stored our baggage for us whilst we attended our course. When we returned in the evening check in was smooth and my colleague was able to request a smoking room. The room itself was lovely. It had everything required, including a safe and was kept clean and tidy. The bed was very comfortable and the shower was heavenly. Complimentary toiletries were replenished as I used them. We were lucky enough to have rooms that were not at the back of the building overlooking the railway line. Guests that stayed in these rooms complained of the constant noise. There was a variety of choice for breakfast (I believe we had the full breakfast option as opposed to the continental style). Fruit, yogurts, pastries, cereals, cooked breakfast etc. We did not eat at the restaurant as we had been warned the food was overpriced. Instead we walked both nights to the Leicester Square/China town/Piccadilly circus area. The walk was very pleasant along the river and passed some well known tourist attractions. Even for someone like me who does not like walking, it was within a reasonable distance. Overall, a very pleasant stay and I would certainly return.

title: Wonderful!
text: Wonderful room! I had the executive double king sized bed room. Well... the most delightful stay I’ve experienced thus far! The king sized luxury bed suite was offered to me, as an “upgrade” - all free of charge. The modern fixtures, plush pillows, free WiFi, deeply-set bathtub, (well worth a try) personally controlled air conditioning / mood lightning all have a wonderfully personally controlled relaxation experience. Couldn’t recommend more highly.

title: excellent customer service
text: Stayed here overnight on business in December, really nice hotel, good location for South West/Central London, comfortable room, modern bathroom & a great feel to it. The one exceptional aspect was the customer service.... I intended leaving my luggage with the concierge on the morning for a later collection. They suggested I could actually check in there & then & have my bags delivered to my/our room in readiness for our return from working. As it happens they only delivered one of the bags so had to ring down, but it was sorted in no time. I/we will be back.

title: Very good hotel - but lacking breakfast capacity!
text: Stayed here for 5 nights in August 2011 whilst working in Westminster, for which the hotel is very handy - 10 minutes walk across the Thames admiring iconic views of Big Ben, the Houses of Parliament and the London Eye. If you can, I would request a river view room - I didn't have one but wasn't there much of the time anyway - but the views would be spectacular. As other reviewers have noted the rooms are pretty good, with a large comfortable bed and walk in shower in addition to a bath. Other reviewers are right to note that there are few restaurants etc in the immediate vicinity - but in 10-15 minutes very pleasant walk along the Thames you can be at the very vibrant South Bank, where there are lots of options. The hotel was very busy when I stayed, which did put pressure on the breakfast room in the basement, which is too small to deal with peak times. Having said that I always managed to get a table but there were small queues at a couple of times. The range of the breakfast buffet was however very good.

title: Very good hotel
text: South riverbank hotel, near to tube stations and bus stops, with good views of Westminster if you have a river view room. 10 min walk to tube, 25 min drive to Victoria station by taxi, circa £10 dependent on traffic. Rooms werent ready when we arrived at 2, however they promised to dispatch staff to clean these right away. We went to Executive area on top floor for some free coffee/pastries. When ready after 30mins they had upgraded our room which was appreciated. Hotel is very modern which suits us fine. Bar area doubles as breakfast room. breakfast was ok, usual fare but limited. For example, only white and brown sliced breads are available, which is fine but seems limited for a hotel of this size and for what you pay for it. French toast and pancakes are available for example, but at extra charge of circa £8. 2 drinks in the evening were circa £20. Rooms were a good size, we had upgraded river suite and a double for our daughter. Suite has separate bedroom and was a joy to be in. Only slight issue was traffic noise at night. Decor was modern and had usual mod-cons. Breakfast could be improved but we really enjoyed our 3 night break, staff were on the whole excellent and hotel was great. Expensive overall, but London just is.

title: Great Hotel
text: This hotel was centrally located. Spacious and clean, Staff was prompt and helpful when needed. If I were to visit London again I would definitely stay at this hotel. Our room with a view of the Thames was fantastic. It was a short walk to many attractions.The only thing that could be improved was the quality of the mattress

title: Good location and easy to find
text: Nice hotel in a good location. Really easy to find. The room is nice and clean with good decor. My only issue is the building work going on around the place, it can be a bit noisy. Breakfast was good plenty of choice. I would definitely book again.
