text: Very nice and friendly staff both at the reception and breakfast room. The hotel room I stayed in is very clean and has all the facilities I needed including a good pressure shower and new towels as well as free tea and coffee facilities. Good value for money and I would stay here again.

title: 2 Star Room
text: I agree with the reviewer from Antwerp. I booked a triple room and was expecting a 3 star room. What I got was a two star room. The balcony window/door was flimsy and insecure, The bathroom had no toilet brush and 1 ply toilet roll. the soap was not replaced with new soap. The bathroom door was baddly fitted and stuck. The bedding was clean, the decor was basic, the flooring was cushioned vinyl rather than carpet. We were promised Satellite TV and Internet in the rooms...not likely! Didn't want to risk the inclusive breakfast given the overall ambience, which is more guest house than hotel really.

title: Not bad, not good
text: Very close to Paddington station, the location is very convienient. The street is full of small similar hotels. The building is a nice little house in a quiet area.the welcome was friendly and warm. Did not interact much with staff but what I had was ok. The room was small, but after all, a bed is enough. The room had acceptable cleaneness, but the bed cover could be reniewed. Bathroom was sufficient. The rest of the room facility like kettle and tv were useless. It is not a hotel you spend much time in. Just to sleep and go. The breakfast was dull. The so called english breakfast had nothing to it. With very simple choice of better products it can be greatly improved. Overall, not bad though. It changes a lot from those all look alike hotel brands.

title: Nice clean hotel but breakfast was disappointing.
text: On arrival the service was good. We arrived early and were allowed to leave our luggage while we went for lunch. The rooms were clean and beds comfortable. I had to ask for hairdryer which I collected from reception. The bathroom was clean. The only complaint I have is breakfast. As a vegetarian there really wasn't much on offer as part of a cooked breakfast - toast, eggs and beans. Some hash browns, mushrooms or veggie sausages are, surely, not too hard to come by. Good assortment of cereals. Coffee was average. Only orange juice an option. Service from staff was very good.

title: Convenient, clean & comfortable
text: This was a good last-minute choice. Advertised as a 3 star this hotel provided an excellent service. We did not expect 5 star facilities. All the staff were cheerful & helpful - especially Nicholas on the desk. The English Breakfast could have been hotter & the toaster does need adjusting but the food was okay. Very convenient for Paddington Station & our room was quiet, no traffic noise being in a square of large Georgian houses.

title: Fawlty Tower's in a good location.
text: Positives - Good Location, nice staff, good looking building Negatives - Cold, dirty, small rooms and London prices...Breakfast was horrific the coffee was foul, a greasy fried egg, cold beans, over cooked bacon, deep fried small sausage. The toast was in fact warm bread. The continental breakfast was 'photocopied' cheese, jam and warm bread. My tip is to go for the option without breakfast. Hotels like this are full tourists spending lots of money in the UK and hotels like this are a disgrace to us all.

title: Good location if going to Heathrow the next day
text: Picked this hotel because we had an early flight out of Heathrow and wanted an easy way to get there (i.e., the Heathrow Express). I thought it was a bit expensive for what you get, but given the price of staying anywhere in London, it was worth it. Our room was small but very clean and we had a nice bathtub/shower. A full English breakfast was included and it was good. And lots of ethnic restaurants in the area, so plenty of places to eat nearby if you stay for more than one day. And, of course, it is a short walk from the hotel to Paddington Station/Underground.

title: Booked for a week
text: Nicholas, the Manager was a fantastic guy who helped us with any query we had. Unfortunately when we arrived in our room - it was quite small, no fridge and no air-con which meant we left our window open 24/7. The room was immaculate and so was the bathroom and staff were amazing. They offer breakfast included and the girls in the breakfast room were so accommodating which brightened up our day each morning. The breakfast was either continental or English cooked - eggs, toast, sausage, bacon and beans. Lovely. I would probably upgrade next time and get a bigger room especially when you have to spread suitcases out. The staff made the trip a memorable one.

title: Heathrow to Chrysos in 25 minutes!
text: The hardest part about getting to the Chrysos Hotel was negotiating the stairs at Paddington Station with 'the luggage'! After a 24 hour flight from Australia, arriving at Hotel Chrysos to a warm friendly greeting was a great welcome. Our 5th floor room (serviced by an elevator) was honest, clean and looked out over the sweet Norfolk Square gardens. Each bedroom has an ensuite, yet another bonus. Complementary breakfast offered a full English or Continental with variety of cereals. All staff are friendly and courteous. If you want an affordable, clean, safe, quiet hotel literally 2 minutes from the hustle and bustle of Paddington, then this hotel offers excellent value for money.

title: not happy
text: Would not recommend this hotel.Sheets had not been changed from the previous guests. Rooms to small.Was on the fifth floor and the water pressure was terrible.Shower head was to close to the wall,not good,when you are trying to have a shower with very little water.Staff at the front desk spent most of their time on the computer watching movies or playing games.The only thing going for this place was the location.

title: The Perfect Hotel
text: I've been in Chrysos Hotel with my wife and my son of 9 years old in July 2008: I' had seen some reviews about this Hotel and I had chosen it for the cheap price (less than 600 pounds for a triple room for 7 days - breakfast aan taxes included), but when I arrived I was very surprised 'cause it was better than I could imagine

title: Avoid
text: My only explanation for the fact that other reviewers have given this hotel 5 stars is due to it's location. Literally a convenient five minute walk to Paddington Station, and close to bus routes. From there unfortunately it's all down hill... Upon arrival, the helpful chap behind the counter, helpfully watched me and my partner lug our cases up the entrance steps, before helpfully advising us check in was not for another 3 hours. Our cases could be left in the front foyer (no secure storage), and by the way they don't accept responsibility for our luggage being stolen. Welcome to the Chrysos! There are no maps of the local area or London supplied, and the staff did not appear to be interested in providing information. Further, the manager standing on the front entrance smoking a cigarette is not a good advertisement for a hotel in my opinion. The room was old and tired, with a hard, yet lumpy double bed that made "sproing" noises when you rolled over, and a single bed. The pillows were like bags of sand and well past replacement. Coffee/tea making facilities included, but no fridge. The bathroom had a shower/bath with no handrails, an obvious safety issue. The cleaners do not make the beds as such. They 'pull them up' in a way that a small child could make a better job of. Replacement of toilet rolls and tea bags is a hit and miss affair, as is cleaning of the toilet, and the room in general. On one occasion when we were out for the day, the cleaner had left the room unlocked after 'cleaning' it. The manager upon being advised was very apologetic and promised to speak to the cleaner about it. Dirty linen was left on the floor and stairs outside our room for two days by the cleaner. The walls are paper thin and you can hear noise from every room nearby. No fan or aircon is provided, only a radiator type heater. The only other means of ventilation is to attempt to open the sash type window which proved to be quite a feat. There is a nice, recently renovated common room on the ground floor, with a kitchette and coffee/tea making facilities, but no explanation was given as to it's use. Most patrons seemed to use the room to access the house wifi. We stayed here for 6 nights and can honestly say the hotel was the low point in what was a very enjoyable visit to London. It was only due to the fact we were prepaid and prebooked that we did not immediately seek accomodation elsewhere. And the final kicker? On the morning of our departure, the lift had been turned off. The manager did not know how to activate it again, so we were forced to drag our luggage down 4 flights of stairs. No assistance offered by the apologetic manager who stood there and watched us struggle. He was more interested in getting the room key back. I could not recommend this hotel. There are numerous other budget hotels in the Paddington area that I'm sure will provide a better experience for similar cost Footnote 1: Do not buy tickets for Golden Tours from this hotel as they get a commission from a tour company that provides lousy service. The Original Tour, or Big Bus Tours are a much better option.

title: Basic, but decent value
text: I had booked a single room for 2 nights. It was a tiny room on the 5th floor, but sufficient for my needs. Staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was clean. The bathroom, spacious (almost bigger than the bedroom). I slept well and can't grumble. Breakfast was fine: cereal, fruit juices, tea/ coffee, and a choice of a cooked English breakfast or toast with jam/ cheese. Very central location and good value at this price. If you're on a budget and are happy with standard accommodation, great place to stay. If you're looking for something fancy, you can pay for it elsewhere. It's London!

title: good value for money but...
text: At £85/night for 4 nights, you will struggle to find something that is as good a value for money in central London. My room was on the back of the hotel and was quiet, reasonably-sized for London (with a wardrobe and small desk), and the staff was friendly. I didn't try the breakfast. And here's the "but": I had a twin room, one of the beds was sub-standard but the other was passable for the price. The internet in the evening was completely unusable. The bathroom was visibly clean and had a good-sized shower but was not well-ventilated so there was a near-overpowering smell of mildew. Finally I will note that there was no air conditioning. Normally not an issue in London, but when it is 32C/90F you'd like to have something!

title: Customer Focus needs major improvement
text: This is the first hotel I have stayed where - 1. The staff at the front desk stay seated and give you the impression you are interrupting their personal phone calls. 2. Regularly smoke just outside the front door. 3. Offer no information about the hotel - There is no guest information booklets in the room - everything has be requested i.e hairdryer. 4. Not even a toilet roll holder in the bathroom. 5. Plastic disposal cups are supplied in the bathroom. 6. The bath is deep and slippery and very dangerous to get out - no safety rail. 7. No menu for breakfast - eggs will be served various ways on request. (The staff were very pleasant in the breakfast room) The rooms are small and need a thorough 'spring clean'. Whilst the lounge area is newly renovated it is sterile and it appeared the only time anyone sat in the area was to access wi-fi. We asked for a map of London - to be informed they had none. We needed to wash some clothes and were informed a laundromat was not far away - no exact directions. On checking out there was no interest shown regarding how we enjoyed our stay and we got the impression the staff thought they were doing us a favour by letting us stay at the Chrysos. The business card advises that the hotel is a superior 3 star - maybe in a third world country but we have stayed at better backpacking hostels. Apart from peak holiday times bookings are not needed and it would be worth allowing an hour to check out hotels in Norfolk Square as the renovated reception areas can be deceiving

title: Ok location, not that impressed
text: We only stayed here for a few days which we were glad about. We checked in and was asked to give our credit card details - i guess in case of damage? - we are travelling and neither of us have our credit card. So we had to hand over 20 pounds. This was quiet significant as we had budgeted for each day. We were given a huge door key (not a card). Im not sure how many floors the hotel had, but we were expecting to be on at least the 1st or 2nd. Wrong. We were less than 10 FEET from the reception. We walked past reception, we pushed open a swinging door near the stairs/lift and then there was the door to the room. The room was pokey. Old 90's TV. No kettle, no fridge. The bed was horrible. It sunk on one side and made noises every time you moved. The only upside was it was close to the Paddington Station. You could be at the underground or main one in less than a few minutes. There was some restuarants, take away places few minutes away too and supermarket about 10 minutes away. It had free internet, but played up a lot. You logged on and took ages to get anywhere and then if you leave it for a few minutes it'd go back to an advertising page and you'd have to wait ages for it to work again. It has a restuarnat, and we did have breakfast included but neither of us were gaim to try. If i go back, Convent Garden area seemed nice. They had markets, many shops. We travelled at Christmas so it may look different than other times of the year,.

title: Super friendly staff and location at night is nice and quiet for sleeping
text: What I expected modest hotel, rooms small. Yes carpet had a stain and the bedspread looked like it saw bleach... But it was very clean and bed was comfortable what I love is how quiet is was for sleeping with a window open no less! I don't like to sleep with AC , we had fan which made the room comfortable. However, no AC in 30 plus is not fun. I would not recommend to anyone who are bothered by this. Breakfast was fine, I did cereal and yogurt and toast.

title: We think they overbooked...
text: When we arrived at the Chrysos Hotel for our two night stay, we were told that our room was not available due to "water damage". We saw no evidence of water damage in the hotel or workmen repairing said damage. We were sent across the street to the Shakespeare Hotel for one night (see our TripAdvisor review of the Shakespeare Hotel). We were promised champagne and chocolates to compensate for our inconvenience. This did not happen. In our opinion, we think they overbooked and sent us across the street to a cheap hotel while we paid for a better quality room than was provided. We were able to check into our room the next day which was on the fifth floor. The elevator seemed shakey to me so I took the stairs if at all possible. Our room was supposed to be air-conditioned, it was not and we spent an uncomfortable night in the heat of the top floor. The only bright spot was that the bathroom had recently been renovated and was clean. The breakfast was just passable, nothing fancy. We would not stay here again because we could not be sure whether the room we PAID for would be available.

title: Good Hotel close to Paddington Station
text: Good hotel for a quick London stay. Located 2 1/2 blocks from Paddington station on a quaint block of hotels, it provides easy access to the metro, buses and direct trains to London Heathrow. The room itself was comfortable, spacious, though not incredibly modern and was fairly clean. Excellent heating! The bath had fresh fixtures, but could have been a little cleaner (tile grout & shower head were a bit questionable, but the sink, toilet were well scrubbed). Perks: breakfast is included in the rate as is wireless internet (just ask for the code at the front desk). Hyde park was a few blocks away and the city center was a quick ride or good walk away. Staff was nice. Note: I did not see a hair dryer or iron - they may have been available at the front desk or were well hidden. Also they were constructing a bar in the front of the hotel, which was a non-issue in April (they were just laying tile so noise-free). Should be nice once it's done, and for now just means you'd have to walk across a little area under construction. Tip: if you book through their website there may be a 10% discount off list rates.

title: Loved it!
text: We travelled to London on the 1st November 2008 and stayed for 7 nights at Chrysos. We checked the hotel's review in tripadvisor before we made the booking. I must say that the hotel and its service exceeded our expectations. Of course, one should not compare it to a 5 star hotel but it's good value for the money we paid. The service we received from the front desk was very good and friendly. The room we had was very clean. The size of the bathroom was alright compared to some other hotels which I have stayed. Also, the water pressure in the shower was good and heater in the room was adequately warm. Breakfast was the usual choice of English or continental breakfast. What we expecially like about the hotel is, it is located very closeby to paddington station, about 4 to 5 min walk away and its location is equally convenient for those who use the Heathrow Express from or to the airport, like we did. There are a few pubs and restaurants around the vicinity of the hotel, which made food easily available. Also, there is a convenient store located closeby the hotel. Overall we enjoyed our stay in this hotel and we will definitely go back there again in our next trip!

title: Good Location - Enjoyed Our Stay
text: We stayed at this hotel for 6 nights. It is situated on a quiet street with a lovely small park at the front. We found our room very clean (although small in size) and the bed comfortable. Found the staff very helpful with our requests. Breakfast each morning (was a choice of continental or full english) was very enjoyable. A short 5 minute walk to Paddington Station - what more could you want.

title: Good & Bad Points
text: Reception & downstairs bar area are fairly new with a clean modern look. Friendly reception staff. Upstairs it reverts to an old dated area. Bedroom was reasonable size with a good single bed and a very sloping double bed. Carpet was very dirty, bathroom needed a complete overhaul & bedroom was very tired & unkempt. A very basic cooked breakfast would have been better eating out. Paddington rail & tube station are only a few minutes walk away & plenty of eating places nearby. Would not stay here again better sticking to a Premier Inn or even a Travelodge.

title: Reasonable value & good location
text: For a one night stay in central London, this unassuming hotel fits the bill. It doesn't offer the elegance, fancy amenities, or attentive staff that you would get in a big-named hotel, but you get what you pay for ... and this hotel is reasonable value for London. All I needed on this occasion was somewhere clean, quiet, secure and close to Paddington. This hotel provided all of those things - and an okay breakfast too! It also had windows that opened which was a bonus!

title: Excellent location and service!
text: If you are looking for a fantastic location in London that is affordable and accessible via the Tube, then this is a great hotel! The rooms a pretty small, but they staff is pleasant and they have a great English breakfast every morning. The hotel is about one block from Paddington Station and located in quaint Norfolk Square. We loved our stay!

title: No air conditioning
text: We stayed here for 7 nights in July in hot summer weather. The hotel did not have air conditioning or a fan. Even having the window open did not help cool the room off at night. The bathroom had one small fan and after 3 people had showers the whole room was like a sauna. This is a good basic hotel with an average breakfast. I have never stayed in the Paddington area before. It is not convenient for an early morning departure from Gatwick airport.

title: Visit to London
text: I can not recommend the Chrysos Hotel for your stay in London, especially if you are on a budget, on arrival you will be faced with the beautiful frontage of the hotel and the very quaint garden at the front. The location of the hotel has close transportation links, with the very famous St Mary's Hospital close by. The very polite and welcoming staff of the front of house are very courteous and helpful, as are the staff at the restaurant, the location of the hotel gives you advantage of most of the historic and popular visiting locations. The room I found was adequate with complementary tea and coffee, nice clean towels and a very pleasant and powerful shower. The bed was very comfortable and the sheets were clean and fresh. The breakfast was plentiful for me any way those with a larger appetite probably would have cereal as well as a breakfast. I found the hotel was very well presented with beautiful tiled flooring on the ground floor and the small bar was very nicely fitted out. Overall I would give the hotel ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ it is a budget hotel with a very nice presentation. Again I would truly recommend.

title: Good Hotel
text: Good Hotel for the most part. Couteous staff. Rooms could be better taken care of better (More thorough cleaning required). Breakfast was limited (not buffet). Options given include english breakfast (one sausage, one egg, one rasher of bacon, a small amount of baked beans) or continental (toast, butter, jam, 2 slices of cheese), Tea or Coffee. Choice of 3 cereals.

title: Will book it again and again...
text: We booked Chrysos as it was a good deal and much more reasonably priced than any other hotel in the area. We found it to be clean and comfortable. Staff are friendly and polite. Rooms are nicely decorated and the bathrooms were very clean, and finally a hotel with working showers! Much nicer hotel then some others we have stayed in before. The Location is perfect with many surrounding pubs, restaurants and everything you would need. Transportation is so convinient, as the hotel is literally 1 minutes walk away from the subway. Our room overlooked the gardens which was lovely, id recommend anyone booking to pay a bit more and get these front facing rooms. We are definately booking this hotel when we return to London late this year. You get everything you need and no complaints!

title: Wonderful place to stay for value...
text: We had a wonderful stay ay Chrysos for 4 days. The location is wonderful for going down to see all the sites, the food nearby made finding a place to eat when we wanted it immediately easy. Overall would recommend this to anyone who asked. The front staff helped in getting us going in the right direction. Nicolas was of tremendous help. If your picky about the size of breakfast sure, it's not huge by American Standard but overall very good, the continental is just cereal but they don't hide that fact going in. The noise of the elevator in relation to our room was pretty minimal and caused us no concern. The bathrooms were very ample. Overall for a 3 star it was very very worthy of that rating. Great stay!

title: Excellent friendly hotel
text: I stayed 4 nights at this hotel. A very smart reception, and modern lounge area. The service was faultless, especially by the management! Rooms (and hotel in general) are spotlessly clean, well decorated, free wifi and free tea & coffee facilities - everything you need for a city break! Location is brilliant, and only 1 minutes walk from all train and bus connections. Beautiful front gardens, and even more so when it was sunny! Breakfast was ok, maybe a little more choice is needed for the Continental breakfast choice, but the full English was more than enough! Would definately book this hotel again, as it is the best one i have stayed in London.

title: Small & hot room
text: We had a really uncomfortable 2 nights here. Our room on the 5th floor (top floor) was tiny - supposed to be a double but was too small for two people, could only get in to the hard bed by climbing in from one side. Had to leave the window open the entire time as the room was hot (and we live in Qld Australia!). No water pressure, small bathroom, basic breakfast. Supposed to be free wi-fi but couldn't access on 5th floor. Only plus was we could walk to Paddington express to Heathrow. We won't be back.

title: Stay as far as you can!!
text: I really do not understand how some people have had rated this hotel as a good hotel? I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone. Better sleep on the streets of London rather than spending your money here! Absolutely frustrating! The room (located on the 5th floor) was soooo tiny it looked like a cabin on a boat (heading to creta!). Oh my god! No air condition, no safe, no refrigerator, a small window looking in a lovely park, but i would say no view from our room as we had to Climb on the bed to see outside. No locks on the window, no blinds, (slept at around 01:30a.m. and at around 5:00a.m. when the light came into the room I woke up!!! They mention in their site, free WiFi internet access. The only thing they forgot to mention is that you have to go to the lobby to use it!! Amenities in the bathroom: they probably must have thought that these should raise the standards of the hotel, so they bought these cheap soaps that cannot be used. There was no hair dryer in the bathroom but at the reception they gave me one. Oh and the bed was probably for dwarfs. My hight is 1,73 and I found my feet hanging off of the bed (imagine my husband who is 1,85). I would say that 129 euro per day (overpriced due to diamond jubilee) was a lot to spend on that hotel. Be careful of all this tricks they come up with, to raise their price. This room does not worth over than 50 euro and their breakfast is not worth at all. Breakfast was a big disappointment. What they call English breakfast (I forgot to take a picture!) was a few beans, a sausage, that looked really bad and an egg. Continental 2 slices of cheese, which I wouldn’t even give to my cat, salty butter and jam and toasted bread. That’s it and in a table some bad quality cereals, milk, ice tea, and orange juice. Very bad quality food, in a poor decorated room. You can give 2,50 pounds to grab a sandwich in a coffee shop and have some fruits too! Plus: Close to the tube and train station The lovely park outside

title: Very nice hotel at a cheap cost
text: The Hotel is at a very good location 1 min walk from Paddington, but in a alley with a small park, so there are no noise from cars. The rooms are clean with a nice bathroom and at an adequate size. The Staff is very nice and polite, and it was a nice surprise that we could get a nice full breakfast with out additional cost. We will for sure be back another time, hopefully in the summertime.

title: Perfect base
text: Great location, so near to paddington and it's restaurants etc. Hotel was a great base. Clean and warm. Breakfast included. So accommodating too, allowing us to leave our luggage there before check in and after check out which was much appreciated. Would definitely stay again.

title: Very nice place
text: Not the top one of course, but for tourism: wonderful. Nice and clean rooms, very good service, very well situated (close to railway and undergroud or tourist bus). One small remarque: try to repair some windows.

title: A warm place with Hospitality
text: I stayed in this property from Jan 22 to Jan 27,2016. First of all location of this Hotel is very good,near to Pedinton Railway Station and also have fast connection with Heathrow Airport by Heatrow Express. The staff/management are very good,specially ,the Delicious Breakfast,served by lovely faces in the morning.This place is in the heart of London and can sneak in to entire London through Tube.

title: Good location, Great Value
text: Stayed here in Jan 2010 while travelling through-out Europe. The location is fantastic being just a few minutes walk from Paddington Station where you can catch the tube to the local attractions. The staff were friendly and the included English breakfast was large and a nice way to start the day. Be aware that the elevator is old and can be quite noisy but due to the minimal amount of rooms on each floor it did not affect our sleep at all. Also the included WiFi will only work on the lower floors but there are comfortable lounges in the lobby where you can sit and make use of your own laptop computer. Overall great value as we got a discount on the room for booking online.

title: Clean and comfortable value for money
text: I booked this hotel thru a link on the BA website, I just wanted a reasonably priced place to stay for a couple of nights near Paddington where the Heathrow express arrives. This hotel is by no means the Ritz but it ticked all the right boxes for me, clean and comfortable, basically like a Premier Inn standard hotel in an older building. It was on a quiet square so no traffic noise, it had lifts which was good, plus they served cooked breakfasts as well as the usual continental. All in all very good value for money.

title: value for money!
text: Extremely friendly staff, excellent breakfast, good lift, room was small, but its an old building, and they have done the best they can in the circumstances. A bit of noise from the neighbouring rooms, but again, you can't blame the hotel for that. Very handy for buses and trains.

title: Great little b&b
text: My partner, our daughter, and I stayed here for 2 nights at the end of November, and we weren't sure what to expect as the prices were very reasonable. I am very glad we decided on the chrysos though. The location of it is brilliant, so close to paddington station (it's only a 2 minute walk from the station) and plenty of eateries and shops. The walk to hyde park is around 15 minutes. The room we stayed in was very clean, the bathroom was also a very good size, I can't comment on all rooms but ours was fairly large. The staff were all very friendly especially the men who manned the reception desk, evening and morning they were super helpful. The breakfast is the only thing that could really use some improvement, but in all honesty it is plenty. You either opt for continental which is the cereal on the side tables with toast, cheese and jam or a cooked English which is 1 bacon, 1 sausage, 1 fried egg, and a spoonful of beans. If you opt for the English breakfast you still get the toast and cheese so I would definately go for the English breakfast as you then get a decent selection of food! Obviously some people will complain about the breakfast but at the price we paid to stay we really couldn't fault it! Our weekend break was very enjoyable and we would definitely choose to go back to the chrysos!

title: Excellent
text: Being a regular for years after knowing one or two really awful hotels in london. This one is clean, friendly staff and even if prices can seems high, it is worthwile if you compare it to other 3 stars hotels in london..

title: perfect for Paddington - lots of options in the area
text: Stayed here the day before I flew out of Heathrow and it was perfect for what I wanted. A clean, well-located hotel within a three minute walk of the train to Heathrow, with lots of dining options in very close vicinity. It was quiet at night and the waitress served breakfast was perfectly acceptable. I would stay here again as I think its a better option than staying at the airport due to it's proximity to the Heathrow trains and there being more eating and drinking options.

title: london stop over
text: The hotel is very close to paddington station,underground and bus services.The check in process was hassle free and staff were helpfull and pleasant.Had breakfast one morning but didnt bother again not worth the bother it was tasteless.I would stay agai room only tho!!

title: Typical European Inn,
text: We were booked into this hotel for 7 nights by a travel agent. Before saying yes to it, we looked at the pictures on the website and even came to Tripadvisor to look at the reviews. I travel a great deal for my work so I know what I like in a hotel and this one didn't come close to meeting my standards. Here are my thoughts on the Chrysos Hotel. First the positive: - The hotel is in a great location, metro stops are very close and the buses are plentiful to take you anywhere you want to go. Also, taxis are always around the area because of it's proximity to Paddington Square. The Heathrow Express comes to Paddington Station, which is only a block or so away. - There are some great little shops in the area so you can get your morning breakfast there instead of the hotel "English" breakfast. There is also a Starbucks in the nearby Hilton Hotel if you want that. - The rooms were kept very clean. The cleaning staff did a great job and that was definitely appreciated by my group. - There is free Wi-fi but it only works in the lobby or close by there. The lobby is small and cold but it works if you need to get Wi-fi. There are only a couple of front desk people and they work very long hours. This can sometimes make them a little grumpy. Overall, they were very nice and accommodating. Now a few of the negatives: - The rooms are a typical European room. Very, very small! My wife and I had reserved a "Double" room, which by most European standards means a double or queen bed. Imagine our surprise when we got to our room and discovered we had 2 twin beds in a room barely big enough for 2 twin beds! We had a small desk, 2 beds and a small armoire in our room. You couldn't walk around the beds with the armoire doors open. We asked to get a room with just one bed(we were there on a romantic week away from the kids, after all) but we were told they only have a few of those in the hotel, even though our reservation clearly states that what we wanted. We were placed on the 4th floor and our room shared a common outer door with another suite. The people in that suite were very loud and we could hear everything they were doing in there(and vice versa, I'm sure). The 4th floor is very quiet though and I would definitely ask for that floor. - The mattresses and bedding need a serious upgrade. The mattress is very old and the coils are poking through in some spots. We pointed it out but got no response from the front desk. - Our bathroom was tiny but functional. On most days we had warm water in the shower and as I mentioned earlier, they kept it very, very clean. - As I mentioned before, there is no Wi-fi in the rooms so if you want to use the Wi-fi, off to the lobby you go. - I'm sure most people are like us and only used the room for sleeping in so the 2 beds weren't the end of the world, just a bit disappointing that they weren't at all willing to help us out. - The English Breakfast is very disappointing. We tried it the first morning we were there and the eggs were cold, the sausage was cold and tasted awful and the coffee was typical instant coffee. We went out to either the local coffee shop(2 minute walk) or to the Starbucks in the Hilton after that. Overall, I would rate this hotel on the bottom of the scale compared to some of the others in the same building or in the vicinity. If you can get a room for a low price and are assured of a newer mattress, consider this hotel. The reason I say that is because it is in a great location and it could function as a hub for your London adventure.

title: Okay Hotel
text: This hotel is okay and basic. The bathrooms need a desperate overhaul and the cleaning staff need to do serious dusting!! What saves the hotel is the area of Paddington and proximity to everything also the price.

title: Perfect London base for your London holiday
text: The first thing we noticed as we arrived was the friendly and helpful staff at the Reception. They allowed us to store my daughter's wheelchair in a very convenient place and helped us to make our way to the lift. The hotel itself is very attractively decorated, and despite being New Year's Eve, very peaceful. Everywhere was clean, warm and very comfortable. Our room was extremely nice. Twin beds with neat attractive covers. Ample storage space is provided, along with the very necessary kettle and tea/coffee making requirements. Often we are rather disappointed with bathrooms in hotels, but this was an absolutely lovely one. Clean, warm and bright with both bath and shower! The water ran hot at all times and we were both able to have a bath during the afternoon, and showers when we returned from the incredible firework displays on the Thames. Lovely fresh, soft towels and tiny soaps and shower gels were provided, and the toilet was not only spotless, but had a paper cover over it. The view was lovely, at the back we looked over the tops of the buildings to the awesome skyline of london. In the front you would have lovely views of the square, and its gardens. We slept perfectly and in the morning went downstairs to sample the breakfast. The room was a little bare, but clean and tidy. The food was really good, and our waitress was helpful. It would be nice if the room were more attractive but we could not fault the service. The position of the hotel is so convenient for transport with stations around the corner, bus stops only five minutes from the door, and plenty of good eating places and entertainment only a road or two away. We enjoyed our stay so much that we have already re-booked for the Queen's Jubilee weekend, and intend to use this hotel again and again. The only downside that we experienced was the steps at the front and the lack of a disabled entrance. This was, however, a small price to pay for such a lovely hotel, a really perfect base for your London holiday!

title: Very good hotel
text: We were very pleasantly surprised. This is a very basic hotel, but also very good. Beds comfortable, clean and the restaurant staff very pleasant. Could have been improved by a better view from the window but didn't spoil it. A stones throw from Paddington Station and Hyde Park so very conveniently positioned for us. Hopefully book again next year

title: Reasonable and centrally located
text: A friend and I stayed at this hotel 3 or 4 nights in mid July. The room was clean, perhaps a bit small, but the bed was very comfortable. The breakfast was substantial. The staff was helpful. Loved the location. Paddington Station was very close as was the bus stop. Several nice pubs nearby, too.

title: Great location!
text: Excellent location but very poor standard indeed. Room was very uninviting and looked like it had been furnished from a jumble sale. Dimly lit and cold. You are unable to turn the heating on or off and the room is very cold. Bathroom was ok. Great for Paddington station and lots of restaurants and cafes nearby. Breakfast was provided but cheap sausages and slow service. Wouldn't stay here again much nicer hotels very close by.

title: Great location, reasonable hotel
text: Stayed for three nights and enjoyed the location. A big plus is the friendly and helpful attitude of Nicholas, who greets you at the reception. The room was big with a large comfortable bed, we had access to a balcony overlooking the square. With Nicholas's help you should get parked just outside, whatever he tells you LISTEN TO HIM. Paddington station and underground is about 200yds away, worth a visit just to see the bear. Nice pubs and restaurants nearby. Have stayed in Russell square many times, but the atmosphere in and around The Chrysos Hotel is much nicer and much more relaxing.

title: An overnight in London before flying out.
text: Location great!! Really close to Paddington Stn. Taps in bathroom really tragic!!! No air con. Room stuffy even with windows open. Staff very pleasant. Location more a plus than other things were negatives. I'd use it again.

title: good hotel
text: i been at this hotel for a week. the staff was very nice and welcoming. the room was a little bit small bt the location of the hotel was excellent. the disadvantage was that the room was very hot with not aircondition at all. the breakfast was normal and the room cleaned every day/

title: Great location very poor customer service Glenda Australia
text: We arrived mid afternoon to be told our room was not ready. We were left sitting for over half an hour. Whilst we were waiting for our room a guest requested an iron, they couldn't be bothered to track one down so told her there wasn't any available. Another lady turned up for an interview which was held at the front desk for all to hear. Another guest booked in and was told there were no single rooms available and she had been upgraded to a family room. After sitting in reception for fourty five minutes I questioned the manager about our room only to be told it had been ready for some time and given a key to a grotty room out the back with old furniture and minimum facilities. It is a shame as the Hotel is in a great location in Paddington.

title: Convenient, but Cramped
text: The hotel is located very near Paddington Station. Our first room was so small that we had no place for our luggage with equally small bathroom. We were moved to double sized room the next day that had 3 single beds and a small seating area with a table. The bathroom was still small and had a shower instead of the small tub of the first room. Both rooms were equally warm and needed to have the window open to get adequate ventilation and cooling. The street can be noisy, especially a problem for front rooms. The breakfast was a disgrace.

title: Definitely the place to stay for a great London city experience
text: I am just back from a 5 night stay at this lovely little hotel, and I have to say I would have no hesitation in recommending it to anyone or returning to it the next time I want to visit London. It's location is perfect, with all restaurants, shops, pubs, bus stops and train and underground stations practically on your doorstep, yet a peaceful night's sleep was guaranteed from the comfortable beds and quiet rooms. The staff in the hotel are extremely helpful and friendly, a special mention to the guys on reception for their very kind assistance in providing maps and directions for buses and trains and which stops to take for each location. It really was much appreciated and very helpful to us.The only things preventing me giving this hotel a perfect 5 star rating was the bathroom facilities needing serious upgrading. The bath itself is too small to enjoy a proper bath, yet the shower head would not stay on the hook on the wall in order to enjoy a proper shower. Such a pity as the pressure in the shower was excellent, unlike the pressure in the cold tap in the sink, which was a mere trickle. Also the quality of the breakfast wasn't great, but quite sufficient to start off the day. We will be back!

title: Average
text: Dk not stay here: Room was very warm, no climate control. Breakfast best can be skipped. Stay here: Close to Paddington station: excellent for LHR travellers. Very helpfull receptionist. Plenty of restaurants closeby.

title: Do not stay here!
text: We knew we were in trouble when we arrived at the wrong Cavendish on Jermyn Street, London which we thought we had booked. It turned out we had booked the Cavendish Hotel on Gower Street. We knew we were in more trouble when we arrived at the Gower Street location and there were two potted plants that were very dead on the front steps, from lack of attention. The room was in disrepair! The door to the room looked like it had been damaged and repaired. The room was very small and needed serious updating! The mattress had protruding bed springs and the rugs were very stained. The amenities like milk and extra pillows can not be counted on. We had to ask for them! The best things about this place were the free wi-fi (strong, consistent signal) and the plumbing worked well. There was no air conditioning. The view from the room was of a very neglected garden full of weeds. The window would not stay open without propping with a coat hanger. We couldn't wait to leave!! Breakfast was ok.

title: Far from a 4 Star Hotel
text: Not a lot to recommend about this hotel except the location. Room facilities did not work, repair man could not repair the safe of the scorching hot water out of the shower. Changed rooms, again the safe did not work, and main light did not work, was promised both would be fixed, but neither were. Body wash and shampoo were half empty/used!!!! This time the shower was tepid (at best) Breakfast staff were absolutely rude. I came down for breakfast, the room was full, when I asked the waitress, whether I should wait or come back, she just shrugged.....eventually another diner offered their table as they were about to leave....shockingly rude. When I raised all of this with the reception staff, was promised a phone call and a part refund. HAVE RECEIVED NEITHER!!!!!!! Cannot give this hotel a low enough rating score for my stay Appalling, will NEVER return......

title: Could be better
text: The Hotel doesnt have a lift so its 50 plus stairs to the top floor. Room was tired. The shower did not drain quick enough so could not have a shower or the bathroom would have flooded. We told the staff and were offered to have a shower in another room, and were told it happens. As we were checking out having a shower then was not an option. The breakfast was alright. The hotel is positioned quite well for transport links. If this is 4 stars then something is wrong.

title: New low for tourist traps
text: There is simply no way this hotel is anywhere the 4-star rating it claims to be. I was stuck in a horrid "cabin" room with ripped out carpet. Breakfast was instant coffee and greasy spoon level substances.

title: Great Stay
text: We stayed at the Hotel Cavendish for a two night break at the beginning of December 2007. The London trip was a 40th birthday present from my husband and we took in the sights of London visited he Terracotta Army Exhibition and had a great meal at Fifteen - Jamie Oliver's. The Hotel was okay it had everything you needed it was clean airy and light. The bathroom looked as though it was a new suite. The room was a great size the bathroom was okay but a little small but both were very clean and well presented. Would we stay here again - yes we would. We were shocked to read the other reviews we did not have a bad experience at all. Our room did not look over the main road but to the back of the property so it was not as noisy. But what can you expect from London every street is a main steet traffic is continous as it is a big City. London is not the kind of place for a nice relaxing break it does not lend it self to that in my opinion. The breakfast was fine you could have a full english or anything from the buffet table. On the first morning I just wanted sonething light - poached eggs and tomatoe which was not a problem. The staff were very welcoming the receptionist even ordered us a taxi and gave us a call up to our room when it arrived. Our London trip was a great experience and we would definatley go back to the Hotel Cavendish. We stayed in room 208 that had a good view of the BT Tower with its colourful display of lights in the evening. Do not rule out this hotel for the price we paid and the great location only a ten - fifteen minute walk into Covent garden & The British Musuem we felt it was worth it .

title: Really good location and budget hotel
text: Lovely little hotel in the best part of London. Not jazzy and full of expensive frill. Just a basic clean budget hotel. Not sure what people are complaining about. Breakfast small basic but tasty and hot. Nice place nice staff.

title: Hotel Cavendish is a totally different hotel to Cavendish Hotel
text: I stayed at the Hotel Cavendish on Gower Street for a couple of days earlier this week. It’s cheap budget accommodation and you get what you pay for. The room was very small but functional. The bed was quite comfortable. The breakfast was ok but not brilliant. The staff were reasonably friendly. My main criticism is the name of the hotel. I made the booking through Booking.com after finding the hotel on Trivago. I did a Google search on Hotel Cavendish and the first hotel I was directed to was the Cavendish Hotel in Jermyn Street off Piccadilly. This is a totally different class of hotel. If I had read the information on Trivago more carefully I would have realised that they are two different hotels but it is a very easy mistake to make. When I was in London I called into the Cavendish Hotel on Jermyn Street and they confirmed that other guests have booked into the wrong hotel by mistake.

title: Just Awful
text: I was booked here by work and I think they got it mixed up with the 5 * Cavendish. DO NOT go here. I was wary as the reviews I had read were bad, but thought well, satisfied customers don't always give feedback. On arrival I gave my name to a man who was behind the desk with another man, to say their customer service skills were poor is an understatement. I asked if my room had been prepaid as I knew it had, he told me it hadn't so I stood outside looking for a different hotel on my phone, I would have moved away but it was pouring down. The filthy carpet that greeted me matched the reviews so I thought this was a great chance to change hotel, when suddenly the man came out and told me oh miss your room is paid for but if you don't check in it will get charged anyway. I did wonder if they were trying to get double payment from me. He asked me if I wanted a large room on the top floor or a small room on the bottom. I opted for the top. Walking up the 3 flights of stairs I saw an iron just left randomly on the landing, the carpet looked like it had never seen a vacuum cleaner in its life. When I walked in I immediately saw stains all over the carpet and on the bad base, my fears were fully confirmed. The bathroom was filthy and the curtains were that stained they must have been there for 20 years at least. The plug socket had scorch marks on the top which looked pretty dangerous and the wifi didn't work. This maybe because the router was plugged into the sockets with the scorch marks so I imagine they are not working. I felt grubby just sat in the room and knew I could not stay a minute longer. If it's cheap there is a reason it's cheap.

title: Shabby
text: Not affordable as we booked last minute. The entrance to the hotel is impressive but that's where it finishes. Once you go beyond reception you are into a maze of corridors. The walls in the hall ways are damp. Our room was the best out of the 2 rooms we booked but still it looked tired and dated and in need of TLC. This is not a hotel I will be returning too.

title: Cheap, good location, but ‘no frills’
text: Friendly staff, you get a decent breakfast, it’s in a great location near huge Waterstones bookshop and handy for UCL. The hotel has seen better days, and the rooms are small, but it’s functional and fine for a short stay.

title: Expensive for what you get.
text: I chose this hotel due to location and cost. The old adage of you get what you pay for springs to mind. The room was small but not as small as a colleagues in the same hotel. Negatives 1-Cracked pain in window 2-Windows not draught proof 3-Blinds dirty 4-Curtains dirty 5-Floor sloped so felt strange 6-Limescale on shower door 7-communicatiin problems with staff with English as a second language getting order wrong at breakfast. Positives 1-Clean bed sheets 2-Tea/coffee facilities 3-two packets of two fingers walkers shortbread fingers each day. 4-tv 5-shower was good. 6-sausage in morning was tasty Overall I would prefer to pay a little more for a better stay. £460 for 2 people for 2 nights not worth it.

title: fair value but disappointing
text: This hotel is not 4 star by my standards! It is convenient and our room was quiet (as requested) at the back. The front is on a main road. As for being re-furbished as claimed I saw no evidence as the public areas were worn and our room, although very clean, was tatty. The shower took 15 minutes to run even lukewarm and the hair dryer didn't work. The staff were helpful but when we needed breakfast early (7 am) to catch a train all we could get was cardboard toast. We booked this room late and with a deal it was just worth the money but I wouldn't want to pay full price for it!

title: Under the bridge is a better option
text: How on earth this one could claim 3 stars? This hotel is so below basic sanitary norms that I am surprised it still survives. The only explanation would be people confusing it with the other Cavendish (in Mayfair) and booking in this disgrace of a hotel service. No lift. This really should be written on their website in big bold red. Single room is not big enough to fit a suitcase. Obviously the personnel of this hotel thinks that suitcases are living beings, so they will walk upstairs on their own, and if you are travelling with a suitcase you should book a double. Audibility is great – you can hear everything your neighbors are doing! I certainly could appreciate traditional folk singing outside at 3 a.m. in the morning. It was too cold to sleep, anyway - the heater in my room was not working. To get it working, you should go to reception and ask – they will switch it on for you for a couple of hours. This is not something that I gladly do in the middle of the night. Blanket in the room had no changeable cover over it. It was DIRTY. The carpet on the floor was DIRTY. I was staying there for 6 nights and the room was not cleaned even once. I wonder if they know how to use a vacuum cleaner at all. Once I dropped something on the floor and had to look under the table to pick it up. I wish I had not. There was no hot water in the shower – only warm (kind of). It does take 10 minutes to rinse off shampoo from your hair because the water is barely streaming. Shower cabin is for S size people only. If you are wearing M – you will not fit in there. If you are L, you will not be able to make it to the bathroom at all. One brilliant morning reception called me to inform that the shower in my room is leaking on the floor below. I bet this happens with them on regular basis. On their website their advertise “free high speed wifi”. This does not exist. Computer detects variety of connections like HotelCavendish, Hotel Cavendish, HotelCavendish1, Hotel Cavendish 1a, HotelCavendish1a but none of them works. Don't ask me why I stayed there for that long, ok? Just do not repeat this mistake yourself. And price-wise: single room was 80 per night. In Travelodge Covent Garden (where I typically stay when coming on my own) you can get double for 70 if you book in advance.

title: Very Nice place to stay
text: We stayed in this brand new refurbished hotel beginning of May and really appreciated our stay here. It is very well located, in central but quiet area, near the underground and many bus stops. Our room was big and very nicely decorated, with all facilities, new design furniture, flat screen, free internet access. Buffet-breakfast was also very much appreciated. And most of all, welcome was very warmful and service really good. We will come back.

title: Certainly worth considering
text: I stayed with my son, and when I asked for a room with two separate beds, I was immediately upgraded at no extra cost. The room was warm and comfortable, plentiful supplies of tea bags/coffee/milk/biscuits, renewed daily. There was a good supply of clean towels, changed daily, and an excellent power shower. The room was cleaned daily and beds made. Breakfast was self service and cooked breakfast served by waitresses. There was more than enough food and plenty to drink. I would certainly return here.

title: Great B&B in a great location.
text: Only 10 mins walk from Euston station and 20 mins walk to the theatres in Leicester Square. Ideal location for us which meant we could walk to everywhere we needed to without having to squeeze onto the tube or get confused by the hundreds of bus routes. Room was a very decent size with kingsize bed (actually two singles fixed together), bedside tables and settee. Ensuite shower and toilet wasn't cramped either. Breakfast was standard help yourself to cereals, juice and fruit. Followed by any combination of fry-up you wanted and unlimited tea/coffee and toast. The only problem I could find was that the room was too warm, even with the radiator turned off, and we slept with the window open meaning the occasional noise from night buses etc.

title: Try another Gower Street B and B
text: I've stayed in a number of these B and Bs on Gower Street and this is not one I would particularly recommend. The building and gardens are not well maintained- the interior has been refurbished to an acceptable standard and appeared superficially clean. Staff in dining room are good ( thank you), Staff in reception hugely variable with some extremely unhelpful individuals. In a competetive world I suggest people vote with their feet and stay at an alternative b and b on Gower street.

title: Very Disappointing
text: My husband and i recently stayed here as an anniversary treat after a wedding in the area. I really wish we hadn't! We booked it through booking.com who advertised a rate of £15 which we thought was a bargain and snapped up! We then received a phone call to say this was a mistake and were offered a different rate which we reluctantly accepted as it was very short notice to find another hotel. The booking.com staff were quite rude and insinuated it was our problem that we hadn't checked the price but at no point was our booking queried until this phone call and surely the advertised price is the price you pay?! Anyway on arrival we found the reception with it's scruffy and dated decor then climbed all the stairs to our third floor room. It smelt very stale and the bathroom smelt of damp. The sash window was not properly fitted and wouldn't go up and down properly and looked out on to the guttering which was full of cigarette butts and rubbish. Breakfast was average. All in all grotty hotel that i wouldn't recommend, even for £15! Do yourself a favour and book a travelodge instead!

title: Horrible
text: Used booking.com who said this was a 4 Star hotel. It does not deserve even 1 Star! 1) No elevators, so if you are on the 3rd floor, you have to carry luggage up and down. 2)We booked a single and double room. The single room was the size of a prison cell. You have to sit at an angle on the toilet!! 3) Double room needed repairs. See pictures. 4) Poor Wifi. 5) It was stinking hot, and rooms and reception are not air-conditioned, so it was boiling hot. 6) No drinking glasses in the room, and tea cups were not replaced every night. 7) Reception resembled one for a back packer hostel rather than a 4 Star hotel. 8) Reception used to store luggage, so when we arrived early, it looked like an airport !! On the positive: 1) Centrally located, close to tube. 2) Staff were friendly. 3) Breakfast offered was not bad. From my perspective, avoid this hotel.

title: Ok but far from luxury!
text: My family and I stayed at this hotel for two nights. The rooms are an ok size but are quite shabby and in need of a redecorate. The skirting boards, walls and ceilings are all covered in scuffs and marks. However the bed linen and bathrooms are spotless. The full English breakfasts are very small although you could always ask for more. My room was at the bottom of the stairs near the breakfast room. One morning I was woken by someone falling from the top to the bottom of the stairs as at the top there is a door of which there is no sign saying that there are steps right on the other side so PLEASE be aware of this if you stay here. The stairs are quite narrow too. The staff were all friendly. This hotel has a good location and is not too bad for the price. It's not a too bad place to stay if you are spending most of your time exploring London.

title: Great base for central London
text: The Cavendish Hotel in Gower Street is a great base for so many central London attractions. It’s close to Euston (and the excellent Euston Tap pubs), Tottenham Court Road, Oxford Street shops, British Museum, the list goes on. We’ve stayed there twice, for the Great British Beer Festival last year, and a BBC audience recording this year. Buses and tube are within walking distance, so you can get anywhere. Bed comfy, breakfasts really good, price very reasonable for such a convenient location.

title: A little grotty
text: There are many similarly priced hotels in the same street. This one offers similarly sized rooms with similar basic facilities. However everything is a little run down and grotty. Walls are dirty, blinds don't work. It's a little grim. Bed was ok and clean but I wouldn't visit again.

title: "Warning Will Robinson" there are TWO Cavendish hotels!!
text: For a one night stay in London before joining a Crystal Cruise, a biz colleague told me to stay here...yes this one. So for one night I did not do my usual TA research (especially now that I have my Top Con Badge) LOCATION: Gower Street is wall to wall with converted old mansions turned hotels. It's in a terrific area and really walkable to lots (too bad a tube stop isn't one of those things close by) But alas, this one is a dismal excuse for their personal "4 star" rating. I am sure that most of the TA reviews you read are mostly true. We witnessed an entirely broken phone system, a guest arguing that she could not even get her suitcase in top floor "single" room and countless other complaints. Just don't put yourself through this. Keep researching. But in fairness, our ground floor room (or maybe below?) was very clean and of course hot...no A/C in August, but the bars on the windows gave one a certain......well you can decide. BTW...the REAL Cavendish? http://www.thecavendish-london.co.uk/

title: Great stay
text: After reading reviews of this hotel we were undecided on wether to cancel or not. Having been told if we cancelled we would still have to pay for the 1st nights stay,we decided to give it a try rather than loose money. The hotel is in a Fab location, reception staff were very helpful an always at hand wen we needed them, always happy to help regarding info on tubes, busses, and local food deliveries. 1st night we stayed in a 3 bed room which 3rd bed was a sofa bed. Not very spacious but it dis the job. Room was clean and had everything we needed, yes it wasnt LUXURY, but then what do you want for the price! It isnt exactly gonna be the ritz is it lol, we couldnt understand why people had moaned. 2nd night we was upgraded to a large 4 bed room with 2 dble beds. Was on street level but there wasnt much noise as u would expect being on a main road. The rest of our stay was great. Breakfast was great, lots of choice and very friendly staff. At the end of the day, this hotel does what it says. Its convenient, clean, and has all amenieties needed. If your looking for LUXURY then dont stay here simples! Go elsewhere and pay LUXURY PRICES. I cannot comment on the very small rooms(which seem to b the ones with bad reviews) but our stay was great. DONT LISTEN TO REVIEWS! GO SEE FOR YOURSELF.

title: Very good for what it is
text: For being a London-centre hotel, is not bad I think. The prices are good (London-wise) and the location is perfect. I will keep it on my list for quick solo or business visits in London, since I like Bloomsbury area. I wouldn't recommend it for couples as probably you would like to have something more romantic.

title: Rather go under a bridge
text: Tiny and dirty rooms. Worn out curtains, made from the same piece as the sheets. Stained walls. Cables hanging from the walls. Windows that did not close properly (in February!). Old low-quality matrassess. My bathroom was not cleaned in 3 days. I received a phone call at 3am from the reception desk asking me if I had been to a party that night and had not paid for a taxi (I even had to go downstairs wearing my pijama to explain the cop I had been in bed since 10pm!). Oh, yes, breakfast was suprisingly good!

title: OK BUT NOT WORTH A RETURN VISIT
text: The first impression was positive as the chap on reception was absolutely lovely and really helpful. We had the choice of a third floor room ( no lift ) or a room on the lower ground floor so opted for the latter. The outlook was of the hotel boiler room. The room seemed clean and adequate although very small and the carpet on the stairs to the room and to the dining rom was somewhat dangerous as it was threadbare. Breakfast was a huge disappointment. We had hardly sat down before the waitress pounced on us to take the order for our cooked breakfast and then it appeared before we had any time to eat any cereal, grapefruit etc or even get a hot drink. The breakfast was extremely poor. One very small sausage, one cold rasher of bacon, half a tomato and a fried egg...on cold plates too !! I stripped the beds before we left and really wished I hadn't because had I seen the stains on the mattress before I slept in the bed , I never would have. £105 for one night for two people. Very overpriced for what it was.

title: Cavendish Unsatisfactory
text: My husband and I were not informed at the time of booking with the Cavendish that they would be under extensive reconstruction(not redecorating). I am allergic to construction materials like fresh paint, sawdust,etc. We were initially given a room in an unsecured,adjacent building with no door staff and without a real lock on the door..imagine the door on a storage shed. We were moved to another room after we expressed concern about being placed in a construction site and having no working television, lock on door, etc. The new room was upstairs in the main hotel..also under construction. The workers were nice enough to move the ladders and paint and tools out of the way every time we needed to leave or return to the room. They were nice enough to refrain from sawing, drilling, etc. until after nine in the morning. The room was not the neatest.Apparently construction sites are a bit dusty. No dustbin to be found at all. No soap. The TV was still out of order.(Sounds petty but we live for our britcoms) The tea service was abysmal. Filthy cups and no teabags or sugar. The shower was best described by my husband as akin to being spat upon as the water pressure was missing(and we are familiar with european hotels and lower pressure, but this was just sad).The lowlight of this experience was the chambermaid asking my husband if he wouldn't mind leaving the door open while we were out, as the workers may need to get into our room!! (No, we were not on Candid Camera.)

title: Excellent
text: From booking in till departure very good. The staff all very polite professional and very helpful. The hotel is ideally placed for theatre shopping and tube.Breakfast great. Just a small change required - hotel information booklet and waste bin in bedroom would be nice. Would recommend 100%

title: Avoid. Seriously consider other options. At all cost.
text: Reminiscent of a school dormitory in a sad state of despair rather than a 4-star hotel. We were given a stuffy, dilapidated room at the basement, adjacent to the kitchen and were woken up at 6:30am every morning due to the clattering of cutlery and nauseating odor of fried food. Room dimensions were appalling and the third ‘bed’ consisted in an archaic, dusty sofa-bed with an uncomfortable mattress. WiFi was frustratingly nonfunctional, as was the bathroom’s water heating system. Photos on booking.com are deceptively misleading. This place is in dire need of a serious face lift. Avoid at all cost unless you’re planning to partake in a ghetto-experience

title: Hello sailor, fancy a night in a cabin?
text: This was my first experience for the latest London hotel euphemism for a really small room - a cabin. It was advertised as such and, with breakfast included, was a reasonable price (for London) at £75. The location is good - just 2 minutes walk from Goodge Street underground and very handy for the centre of London. The staff were friendly and helpful and the breakfast room was clean and the meal enjoyable with fast attentive service - but I was the first in and it might get a bit tighter for space later. Also a 7:30 start is a bit late for some of us business users. The public areas of the hotel appeared clean but a refurb wouldn't go amiss. The bedroom itself was the smallest I have been in with half of the single bed fitting exactly into a small alcove - the bed itself was quite comfortable. There is no chair, no rubbish bin, no kettle, no drinking glass or air conditioning provided. Bizarrely a thermos flask was placed by the bed but was half filled with cold water - strange! There was no plug in the sink and the pedestal for the wash basin protrudes in front of the toilet so you have to sit almost sideways! There was mould around the ceiling of the shower room and no air-conditioning. When the very small window was opened it let in a large amount of street noise. There was no bedside light switch. To turn out the bedroom light one has to go outside the bedroom door! For those with limited movement there are a lot of small windy stairs and no lift.

title: Not a good experience
text: On walking into my room I thought I had gone into the broom closet by accident. There was just room for a 6 foot bed no room for me and my bag in what little floor space was left. The shower stank of dampness and had the musky smell of a room left without any ventilation. The extractor was not working and found it had been switched off at the master switch. On turning it back on and using the bathroom at 4am found out why it had been switched off. If I woke my neighbour in the next rook I apologise. There was black mould on the wall of the shower, the cable for computer access was broken and had been like that for sometime as someone had repaired it was black masking tape and the repair was so old that the tape had lost all stickiness. The blinds in the room wear badly worn as was thread bear stair carpet. The hotel advertises cable television I could only find three channels which is less that you can get from free to air. Did report the faults and the receptionist on checking out was dismayed they had not been fixed. Would not recommend this hotel but have stayed in worse.

title: Bad management would not rate at all
text: Hi all, Fell ill a full two days before booking at this hotel. Cancelled booking directly with the hotel. Firstly they denied getting email even though I have proof it was sent. Secondly the mean management charged a full £125.00 on the basis we did not show up which was untrue! Draw your own conclusions as to what type of place this is. Sam and the manager rubbish! Alan B

title: Mixed Bag
text: Stayed at this hotel looking for budget accomodation in London. Booked two rooms as our party was my wife and myseld plus my 77 year old mother who has moblity issues. Hence a double room and a single room which give rise to slightly different experiences. The overall hotel is superbly positioned for the West End, particularly the British Museum and positioned directly between Euston Station and the Museum - easily walkable. It is an old substantial house which has been converted, hence there are a lot of stairs to reach rooms, but banisters allow impaired mobility access but not for someone who can not leave their wheel chair for short ditances. Reception is 24 hours and they were happy to have luggage left with them prior to checkout and after checkout, so that you can continue with your visit to London without dragging bags with you. The double room was clean and reasonably sized (room 103) at the front of the hotel. The small double bed was comfortable with clean sheets - I needed a second pillow as the ones on the bed were a little tired but this was supplied in the wardrobe complete with clean pillow case. Complimentry tea and coffee making facilites had plenty of supplies. The shower room had a high step to walk into it but it was again clean, plently of towels although they were a little thin together with bars of soap and shampoo were provided. It was a little noisy at times during the night as heavy traffic passed by. There was a small wall mounted flat screen TV with freeview diital channels and free wifi. Overall, for a £125 central London room, including a cooked breakfast - this room left a good impression. The single room was not as good. Room 104 had a single bed which covered the entire width of the room and was against the outside window wall. No curtains - just a pull down blind (in contrast with the nicly curtained 103). The flat screen TV had only an internal ariel in the room and was unwatchable. The bed occupied the room at its widest point and after a couple of feet into the room, the width narrowed to about half the length of the bed where it accomodated the ensuite shower room. This was perfectly adequate and of the same standard as the one in the double room. Overall, clean but very small, and with the bed pressed against the outside wall, quite noisy. The cooked breakfast was served in a room in the basement, not enough tables to accomodated everyone at once but turnover meant that this was not a real issue. the food quality was excellent with english breakfast consisting of bacon, sausage, tomato, beans and a choice of eggs. Cereal, fruit juices, fruit and yoghurt were vailable for self service. Toast was automatically brought to the table and the coffee cafetierre was refilled without needing to be asked. Staff were very good and friendly. Overall, had this reviewer only seen the double room, a strong review would have been given but I would not want that single one again although, in fairness it was a £105 cntral London one with breakfast included.

title: Just the job
text: Stayed here one night while visiting London for drinks with friends. Easy to find within walking distance from Euston station, easy to check in with polite pleasant staff, nice and clean with all the ameneties required. Had a single room (108) which was small but perfect for my needs, the only whinge is no double glazing which meant a bit of a draft from the window (bed right by window) but good heating meant that it wasn't really cold. Would definitely stay here again and recommend to anyone looking for a cheap London B&B for a stopover.

title: Nice cosy place
text: It is located at a very convenient spot. Was very clean and the lobby was lavender-scented. It might be tiny and there aren't any lifts (had a terrible time dragging my luggages up and down the stairs) but i find it rather cosy. Nice reception staff and breakfast was delicious. Although the price is a little steep for a b&b, i wld definitely come back to this b&b again.
