title: Horror Hotel - Can't be 4 Stars - Rip Off
text: I have to mention that this Hotel claims to be 4 stars,but has tiny rooms no minibar,no lift .... We got the tiny room(10 sq m(100 sq feet) including bathroom) that other customers mentioned as well in their reviews and they told us it's a double room. So besides having bad service they take paing customers for fools. The breakfast is also a joke and the breakfastrom is so small that at some times guests had to stand and wait for one of the 6-7 tabels to clear. We asked at the reception if it would be a 4 star hotel and wanted a proof of that and we were told that they wold not be authorised to give such a proof.

title: Excellent for the price
text: I worried after reading some of the reviews but booked the Cavendish because of the neighborhood and the price. My cabin single room was very small but clean and quite comfortable The staff was helpful, the breakfast was made to order (and better than the buffets at some more expensive hotels), the shower had good water pressure, and the room was quiet. A very pleasant surprise!

title: DON'T!
text: My partner and I stayed here for one night whilst visiting London to see a West End show as part of my 30th Birthday celebrations. The hotel is in a good location for the theatres and this is its ONLY positive point! This hotel is awful and essentially needs to be thoroughly investigated by Environmental Health! Genuinely surprised it had never appeared on Ramsey's Hotel Hell - ironically what we were watching on the TV the morning we checked out. When we arrived the man on the reception desk barely acknowledged we had arrived - there was no welcome or smile - it was a systematic request for name and then signing of the details. We were offered either a room on the third floor or a room on the lower ground floor - we opted for the third floor. There was no offer to help with the bags or showing us the way - just given directions and left to our own devices. On the third floor landing, there was an old mattress and two/three bags of laundry just left there - this was about 5 in the afternoon and they were still there after we had seen the show and when we left the next morning! When we entered the room (303), there was an awful smell of stale smoke in the room and when looking out of the window onto the ledge you could see the cigarette butts that had obviously been smoke out of the window to avoid going all the way downstairs again. Although would not be surprised if the smell was from back when people were allowed to smoke as it was clear it had not been redecorated for a good 20 years. Upon inspecting the bathroom, there were dirty, cracked floor tiles and disgusting mould on the bathroom ceiling. The water comes out either scolding hot or freezing cold - there was no in-between - hot was even coming out of the cold tap. The room was dated - the double bed was two singles put together and when we pulled back the duvet we found stained sheets and then only one of the singles had a mattress protector on it which was also stained with god only knows what and both mattresses had vile stains on them as well. We rang down to the reception and informed him and were offered the lower ground floor room instead. The receptionist showed us this room - I say room, it was more of a box - very narrow and small the 'double bed' was just a slightly larger single and it took over the room - you would have to climb on it as you couldn't walk around it. The receptionist peeled back the smallest corner of the duvet and seem annoyed when we requested to see more and the actual mattress which was still stained. We opted for the 3rd floor room and requested that some clean sheets were put on the bed - which again seem to frustrate the receptionist guy as he claimed that there were no housekeeping staff available to do it. We had to wait almost 20 minutes whilst he eventually found a maintenance man to do it for him and he only opted to take the bed sheets and didn't even bother with the disgusting mattress protector. He came back with sheets that were too small for the bed so this delayed us further. To say we chose to stay there anyway would be incorrect - we did not have much choice as we were on a time limit to get to the show - had we arrived earlier in the day, we would more than likely have opted to find a different place to stay. We both opted to sleep on top of the duvet as it was the cleanest 'dirty' thing in the room. The bed itself was uncomfortable and I couldn't get to sleep until gone 4 in the morning out of sheer exhaustion from lack of sleep. We had hoped that breakfast would be a small redeeming feature of our stay - we were very wrong! The breakfast room which was on the lower ground floor was cramped and uninviting. The waitress, with a strong foreign accent, did not so much ask what we wanted for the breakfast as told us what we were having. Aggressively talking at a rate of knots "Eggs - scrambled, boiled, fried!" and "Breakfast - beans, sausage, bacon, tomato!". Not great service at all. The breakfast itself was truly disappointing it came out within a minute of ordering (so pretty much cooked and kept warm rather than freshly done) - with a small chipolata size sausage, anaemic looking bacon and literally a tablespoon-sized portion of baked beans. Whilst there was other guests in the room as well it had an atmosphere that would make a mausoleum feel welcoming. My partner risked the shower in the morning but I opted to wait until I got home given the state of the bathroom. As we left, housekeeping was sorting out rooms on the 2nd floor but had just chucked the towels and sheets on the stairs which made it dangerous to walk down. Checking out was just as bad as checking in - no service, no hope you enjoyed your stay or hope to see you again or even a sorry about the room! Just handed the key-card over and left to leave in silence. Needless to say we are pursuing a full refund so far without much luck mostly because the 'manager' is constantly unavailable or coincidentally just left! Even being told that he would contact us back but never has. We were also told that in order to obtain a full refund we would have to email - which we did - but no response to it has been given despite when we phoned again they acknowledge they had received it. We will be pursuing it at a higher level as well. The hotel manager and staff should be ashamed of the cesspit they are running - lazy, uncaring, unmotivated and pride-less - avoid this hotel like the plague or risk catching it!

title: The noise from the road kept the bed bugs away
text: Good grief, I new I was in a bad hotel when they gave me my door key that was split and taped up. I was unfortunate enough to be allocated a lower ground floor. It was small, the carpet was stained but thankfully not as stained as the duvet......or the pillows. There was good mobile reception as I immediately tried to find another hotel but to my horror there was nothing avaiaqble close to Euston. i tried to have a shower but I could not get a decent flow of water, but to be honest if there had been decent pressure I think the shower head would have come off the wall. `it was in a bad way. i went to bed, fearing bed bugs. I did not see any, I think the noise of the road kept them at bay. I got through the night, had a small breakfast. I wont be back.

title: Terrible Hotel
text: The room is very very very small. There are no table, chair and rubbish provided in the room. Stains and smells were found on the bed sheets and matress. It was shame for it to claim as 4-star hotel. The condition is just a B&B accommodation rather than a hotel. It was the most terrible "hotel" I have seen so far.

title: Avoid
text: We Stayed here for one night and that was way too much-please avoid this 'hotel' at all costs.The rooms were awful and dirty and it is not a hotel experience-couldn't possibly stay for breakfast......

title: Decent, but I think there are better next door
text: There are several hotels of the same type nearby, even on the same block - a great location, and probably one of the better deals in London. (don't be shocked by small rooms, as it will be any decent part of central London for less than 150 quid/night) This place is decent for the non-picky. But I think I got better value for the money in the other hotels on the block I stayed at. Unfortunately, they seemed to have gone down since their review in Lonely Planet.

title: comfortable and convenient
text: We stayed here for 4 days in late June and found the hotel to be better than our expectations. It's proximity to the British Museum was a big plus for us. The rooms have all been recently refurbished and are bright and modern, and while not 100% done, we had everything we wanted. The beds are really comfortable and the flat screen tv was great for watching the world cup soccer matches. The in room safes were fitted during our stay. The staff were friendly and very efficient, especially the waitress at breakfast. We were given a tour of the new reception area which was almost complete and looks stunning. The narrow old stairs down to the breakfast room were the only negative for us. We would certainly stay here again.

title: Really great hotel and location
text: Booked through Lastminute and stayed for the weekend. Really liked the room and hotel location. Great bed, shower etc etc....in fact I cant find any faults. Would have liked to order breakfast in bed, but that sadly did seem to be very overpriced. So we had breakfast outside the hotel. Would def book again.

title: Avoid this hotel!
text: I would never recommend this hotel. The room was in a 2nd floor and no lift so I had to lift my lyggage and laptop myself. When I reached the room, I have no words to describe it. was not .....the size of a midget!!. I had to jump over my luggage to get to the tiny bed....head and feet in the wall, bathroom , tiny, and water poor. I had to get out of my bedroom as soon as possible as I felt absolutely claustraphobic. The towels with hole.....so quality in general very poor. Only the location is good but does not compensate! Overall it was an appaling hotel.

title: Make sure you use the safe in the corner of the wardrobe that you are not informed about upon arrival
text: The hotel appeared to offer all we wanted for our weekend in London until we returned back to our room on the Saturday after a full day of sightseeing to discover that my money had been stolen, passports and cards were left. As there was no evidence of a breakin I can only conclude it was stolen by somone with access to a key card! Two weeks later I am still awaiting a response from management.

title: Won't be back
text: The so-called double room we were allocated was smaller than a ship’s cabin with absolutely nowhere to put our luggage. The bed, which was not a double but a three-quarter, was crammed into the window recess with no room to move around it. The management insisted that this was a full-sized double which it most certainly was not I think it was what is commonly known as a three-quarter bed. There was no drawer space and the apology for a wardrobe was rendered inaccessible because our luggage blocked it. No bed light so had to switch off light at door and negotiate way back to bed in dark - not easy climbing over luggage etc. The “en suite” shower/toilet was also minute, the door skimmed the loo so that you had to flatten yourself against it or to climb over the toilet bowl to gain entrance, trying to get out again was another problem. On the whole the place was clean enough, the staff friendly, and the breakfast quite good, although the breakfast room is too small for the amount of guests they accommodate and people are queuing on the staircases waiting for others to finish. We won’t stay again. We do like that area and we had stayed at the Cavendish some time ago when the place was owned by two lovely Welsh ladies so we were very disappointed to find the service and amenities had declined to such an extent. There are plenty of other places on that stretch of road where the facilities are much better.

title: UNCLEAN
text: The room was not clean: showerhead was so gunked up, water sprayed every which way when the nozzle was turned on. Wiped down the bathroom counter with a napkin that I soaped up with the bar soap in the room, and the filth/dirt/dust that came up was utterly disgusting. The slight beginnings of mold were starting to form in the toilet, and when I checked over the mattress, I saw an old blood stain that was on the bottom side of the mattress. The mattress itself was long overdue for being replaced

title: Our over night at the Cavendish
text: First the Booking.com gave this hotel **** omg no way I will gave this * stars. The room very hot no AC, with window that will not stay open so I had to hold it open by putting a bin to wedge it open . Door to the room not locking , bathroom floor tiles loose , bathroom exractor didn't work as it was clogg up with fluff. If you like going up one lot of stair down an other with cases to get to your room then book this hotel. oh yes breakfast in the basement that it was ok. and the guy reception helpful . Location was good as it was only 10 minutes walk from places to eat and visit . Very rundown and need a good make over not only paint on the outside . Will I stay there again maybe in 10 years time when it refurb!!!! Not suitable for disable people or older people no Lift very narrow stairs .

title: Tired hotel. Find somewhere else even if on a budget.
text: Good stuff - Friendly staff, comfy and clean bed, great location (only 5 minutes to Goodge Street and two stops to Leicester Square. Bad stuff - No lift (and we were on the 3rd floor) so you need a certain level of fitness. Bedroom baking hot as no aircon and small windows. Bathroom poor and musty smelling. Broken bathroom fittings. Decor all round tired and dated. Breakfast was chaotic - we had to clear are own table as more guests than seats, all food was microwaved. Garden was overgrown so we were not allowed outside.

title: Good
text: Clean and comfortable rooms. Good Service. My room was particularily small but perfect for one. Definetly would recomend making sure you get a bigger room, if traveling with others. Great location.

title: awful
text: stayed here for 2 nights and it was terrible my room was minute, supposed to be a double, but the bed was far too small for a double. title: Average
text: Excellent location. Near the best of the best in London. Easy public transport everywhere. Nevertheles.....very,very,very small rooms. The baths are new and clean. There is no lifts. The brakefast is not good. Small place to have it so you have to wait. Fortunately the staff are kind

title: very good
text: great for cleanliness, v nice staff and really comfortable bed. Rooms were not huge but not overly cramped like some small London hotels.

title: dont bring a cat!
text: Flippant title but honestly the single bedroom i was alloted was not big enough to swing a cat in, you open the door and the bed is right there in front of you, not for people with claustrophobia, the room itself was clean enough and some effort had been made to fit a shelf (desk?) with a kettle and a selection of coffees but no room to supply a chair to sit on. To get in to the bathroom you literally have to fully open the bathroom door, step over the toilet and then close the door behind you, hot water supply was minimal.... Breakfast room was bright and quite modern, quality of the cooked full english breakfast was good, the waitresses all very friendly and helpfull and the guys working at the front desk pleasant, if only the bedroom had been bigger i might have swung for 4 stars.

title: Stayed here because of the location
text: Stayed here because of the location, but will probably not stay here it next time. Comfortable enough and the breakfast was lovely, but I suppose you get what you pay for. Worth it if you cant find anythingelse

title: Pleasant stay
text: I was a single traveller at the time and found the Cavendish a pleasant place to stay. The single room was tiny and the bath and shower were on different floors but just as others say I was in London for the sights not the room. The bed was comfortable, the owners friendly and helpful, and the breakfast was great. Cavendish Hotel is also so close to the sights I easily walked to the tube or a sight nearby.

title: Really not a 4 star property
text: I am sorry to say there's no way this hotel should be classed as 4 star. I'm not a moaner and this is the first review I've ever chosen to write. But if it helps one person avoid this hotel then my missions a success. The garden looked like a jungle. The windows wouldn't open and had a huge gap above it. The shower was falling to pieces and had no shelf for you to put your shampoo or shower gel on. The tv didn't work. We reported it the 1st night we were there and we're told somebody would be straight up to check it out . Well he must walk incredibly slowly because two days later he still hadn't arrived! Really not worth the price im my opinion. There must be better options than this for £250 for 2 nights

title: Theatre Break
text: Spent 2 nights below average hotel the sofa bed was a nightmare the springs stuck in my sons back all night. Great location staff present however the hotel is run down and could do with a good clean the breakfast was ok however the breakfast room is very small and in the basement all the tables are very close together

title: Small but good
text: We stayed for two nights in the weekend. Hotel is close to the metro and walking distance to city centre (trafalger square) which is nice. We had very a small room but very clean and it had everything we needed (nice bed and bathroom). Windows are a bit hard to open and when on the main road side there is some noise, but since you're in the city centre what do you expect. Decent English breakfast which you can order from the staff. Sometimes you have to wait a while for your breakfast due to the few tables. Reception is ok, but not really interested in you or if you have a good stay.

title: Hotel Cavendish on Bloomsbury is an IN-DECENT one
text: 1. They charged me twice on my credit card before I even checked-in 2. The room is small and the bedsheet is dirty 3. When I notified them of my checking-out the hotel a few days earlier than my original reservation 24 hours in advance, they charged me an extra night for that even if they told me earlier that no extra charge if it is notified 24 hours in advance 4. During my check-in, I saw a lady with 2 children were complaining about extra charge as well.

title: Horrific
text: Do not ever stay in this hotel.. It is not fit for humans to stay in. The walls were damp, the windows rattled. It was freezing with no heating. There were fittings missing everywhere. PLEASE DO NOT STAY HERE

title: Almost Perfect
text: I had a great experience. The staff was friendly, the area was quite while still close to everything, the room was clean, the breakfast was excellent. The only thing preventing me from rating this a perfect excellent is the false fire alarm going off 3 out of 6 mornings! Thank goodness I have a healthy heart, because the alarm nearly gave me a heart attack all 3 mornings.

title: 1st stay was ok
text: A bit tired but was clean and tidy with a decent room. Staff were friendly and efficient at reception and breakfast. I had a quiet room at the back of the hotel. The location is very good

title: Go find the city dump
text: Because you'll be more comfortable there. Oh, and make sure when you book to pay the extra to enable you to cancel after you back out of the hotel. If not they will keep your money for the whole time that you've booked. Poor communications and a manager who will avoid you at all costs. Rooms are not clean so be sure you're recent with your shots. Don't waste your time here.

title: Good Little Hotel with a great location
text: I don't understand whats so bad about this hotel. It's obviously not one of your overpriced major branded hotel chains but its perfect for a short stay in the capital. We stayed at this hotel in room 103, lovely warm room looking onto the main road. Most people wouldn't like being next to the road. But to say its a busy road there was minimal noise heard from the room. I've got to admit the whole hotel interior is quite old and tattered but that didn't bother us. As a hotel is a hotel and all you really do is sleep in it. The location is amazing too just a short walk from covent gardens and the big attractions. Anyway back to the room, the rooms are not modern however this gives it a more warm cosy feel. We was provided with towels and toiletries and a full coffee kit. The room was clean and bed was very comfy. I don't know how much this hotel usually is but the price we got it for was well worth the money.

title: Washing and sleeping are all you can hope to achieve in your room. Neither was a comfortable experience.
text: This hotel is generally tired and down-at-heel. All carpets are threadbare and paintwork scuffed. On a mild september day, the entire hotel was hot and humid. Seeing my single room, I assumed that I had been allocated a cabin room in error. I checked with reception and was told that, no cabin rooms are even smaller. I felt humbled by the thought that others must be suffering so much. The shower room was recently decorated but so lillipultian was its aspect that I could exit it only by pressing myself against the wall opposite the door: otherwise my body impeded its (inward) opening. The bedroom walls were a scuffed patchwork of soiled paint and unsanded filler. It was possible to view the TV only from the bed, which added unwelcome hours of exposure to its too-thin mattress and negligible pillow. I fled the room and spent the evening aimlessly walking the streets until tired enough to return and sleep. In the morning, Breakfast was well-cooked and the serving staff were polite and helpful. I would stay here again only if there were no conceivable alternative.

title: Beware
text: A truly dreadful hotel. The room was hardly bigger than the uncomfortable foam double bed. The temperature was sweltering - despite it not being particularly warm outside. The window could not be left open as the traffic noise was so loud. The trucks thundering past made the sash windows rattle. I have never been in a hotel room (despite back-packing around the world) that I have been afraid to close my eyes in. I implore you - STAY AWAY. Definately not worth the £145 that the company I work for, paid for my experience.

title: Charged twice for my room - no refund
text: Expensive for a tiny, dusty room with dirty, ripped sheets and a rusty shower. A maze to get to the top and while we were offered a lower floor room the customer service stopped there. I was CHARGED TWICE for my stay at this hotel! I assumed this was a mistake and would be corrected immediately but so far staff have been rude. My phone calls are being dodged and no one has replied to the 3 emails I have sent. I am £615 out of pocket now which is 3 weeks of work for me - and I get the feeling management couldn't care less.

title: good location and price
text: 2 minutes walk from the british museum and easy access to west end. so location is great. recent refurb by the look of things and the room was clean and bathroom newish. room was a triple i.e. twin with campbed so was a bit cramped. we paid £145 which seemed reasonable value for london! room however was stifling hot. on third floor with small sash window. unfortunately it was hottest weekend of trhe year. think carefully if you visit in summer. breakfast was mediocre. small portions even for us girls and service was questionable. would stay again though if i wanted cheap(ish) stay in good location and a small brekkie-maybe only in winter though!

title: Laptop got stolen, no hot water and unreliable Hotelmanager
text: I stayed in this hotel in May 2006 for two (2) weeks. I can absolutely sign and underline the former reviews. If you stay only for a weekend, you might not realise all the problems of think, it is just a temporay problem as the manager tries to explains it. BUT.. if you stay longer, you reckon, that the Hotelmanager keeps telling the same story to each complaining guest and acts as if this guest is the first one complaining about missing hot water. After a few nights my laptop got stolen and I found it hidden under the roof.

title: Lucky escape...well sort of
text: I booked this hotel for a business colleague and subsequently cancelled the room in accordance with their Cancellation/ booking terms. I was then suprised to find that the hotel had charged me the cost of the room for not showing up. I phoned the hotel to explain the problem and the reception member was rude and most unhelpful. I emailed the hotel my confirmation of the booking and confirmation of cancellation, however got no aknowledgement and had to chase 4 days later. I then spoke to what I can only assume was the same person who advised me I was charged because I booked and cancelled the room on the same day and said had I cancelled the room two days before the arrival date I would not have been charged for the room for not showing up. Suffice to say the logic was lost on me! given I cancelled the room 2 weeks in advance to when I was due to turn up. Whilst I can not comment on the hotel itself and the services it offers, I can only warn anyone planning to stay here whether booking with the hotel direct or via a site, to make sure you keep all correspondence you have and read the terms and conditions of the room you book, incase you need to cancel. It is only after the intervention of Late rooms.com, who agreed I had acted in accordance with the hotels Cancellation terms, has the hotel agreed to refund the money they took from my account. Fingers crossed they will, as they have still not ackowledged anything in writing to me

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: I decided to try this hotel in spite of mixed reviews because all the others nearby and of similar price had consistently bad reviews. I was cosy but not suffocated, comfortable and quiet. My single room had double glazing with blinds enclosed, so I never worked out how to look outside. Gower Street was reasonably close to St Pancras for the Eurostar. I took a taxi with my 2 suitcases, backpack and walking stick - tube or bus would have been easy without the baggage. When they saw me, they put me on the first floor thank goodness. The stairs are very steep. I had just enough room to move my suitcases around and repack. Breakfast was bountiful and early.

title: Good value, great location!
text: Our train arrived at St Pancras and the hotel was a 15 minute easy walk away. We went out in Covent Garden and Leicester Square which again was about a 15 minute walk. Felt the hotel was just perfectly placed! The room was very nicely presented and clean and the bathroom was spotless. The rooms are on the small side with no bath but that isn't a problem for a short break. Would definitely stay here again.

title: Book somewhere else!
text: Booked this hotel for a business trip, guest arrived after a long day / train journey to be allocated a "harry potter under the stairs" sized room with no carpe right next to the kitchen. Granted the description says "small cabin sized room" but this is definitely not worthy of 4 star rating - they are making £85/£100 a night out of a room that should be no more than a broom cupboard.

title: Friendly staff, shabby for the price
text: I stayed here one night this week for work and paid £155 for the privilege. At this price, the hotel was poorly maintained and with few facilities, as well as the inevitable small rooms for an older building that had been converted. staff were, however, friendly and there was WiFi.

title: Service? What service.
text: We stayed at the Hotel Cavendish for an anniversary theatre break. The location of the cavendish was superb and was in easy walking distance to theatreland. The hotel itself was clean and well presented. However, the problems started as soon as we arrived. The room was decorated to a good standard and was clean but this seemed to mask the poor amenities. Firstly, the new posh flatscreen lcd t.v was green and therefore unwatchable. We complained to the front desk and the receptionist came up to see for himself. He did not try to fix it apart from 'I'll let the manager know.' After arriving back from a great evening at the theatre I decided to have a shower only to find that it literally dribbled water. It would have taken an age to have washed. Again, I told the night receptionsit and he said, 'There is nothing I can do until the morning.' Fair Enough. The next morning we had to catch the early train and tried to check out. I complained that the t.v and shower did not work, the receptionist said there was nothing he could do as I did not pay full price for the room as I booked through Hotels.com. If I had known that getting a discount meant that I could not have used the t.v or shower, I would have paid full price! I asked if the manager would phone me, which he never did. I phoned again, no response, tried again, no response. In the end I called the Hotel 13 times over a ten day period! In the end the receptionist said that the manager did not want to speak to me. I found this absolutely disgusting. All I wanted was an apology, instead I was brushed off by the gutless manager. After writing to the managing director I received a brief phone call telling me I could have a 30 pound refund. This however, did little to change the bitter taste this whole episode left.

title: Good location and breakfast, but it ends there!
text: We stayed at the Hotel Cavendish on Monday night this week. We found it very easily and it's only a 5 minute walk from Goodge Street station, in a very nice area. We got checked in and out room was ready around 10 minutes later. We booked a triple room for ourselves and our 6 year old son. In the room was a super king sized bed and a single sofa bed, which the man on reception said someone would go in later on to set up. The small bathroom (which was basically built into a corner of the room) was clean and had a double sized shower. We were out and about in London all day and got back to the hotel around 8.30 to find the sofa bed had been set up. It was as hard as a rock with a 'mattress' that was around 2" thick, every single spring could be felt so our son said he would sleep in with us. It was extremely hot in the room with no ac or fan. When we pulled back the quilt the bottom sheet came with it, exposing the horribly stained mattress as there was no mattress protector fitted. When we checked the pillows they were flat and also stained and were a bit smelly. By now it was 9.30 and our little boy was so tired we had to go to sleep on top of the quilt. But I hardly slept due to the thoughts of the mattress and pillows 😖 Breakfast room was small but it was a very nice cooked breakfast, which was the only redeeming feature really. Complained to the man on reception who couldn't really have cared less to be frank. Wouldn't recommend this hotel.

title: Worst hotel that I have ever seen!
text: I booked 2 rooms here in July, for 3 nights. A double for me and my wife, and a single for my nephew. I was asked to pay the full amount (£630) when we arrived. I booked through Booking.com, as I always have done in recent years. We went to our rooms (carrying the cases up the stairs as there is no lift!!) and found that both rooms were dirty and looked shabby. They have not been decorated in a long time. The windows were dirty, the back was missing off the TV remote control, the carpet was badly worn. The bathrooms were not even clean.The towels were threadbare. I went downstairs and complained. I requested a refund as I didn't want to stay there. The hotel management refused.We left the hotel about 15 minutes after our arrival. I contacted Booking.com, and unfortunately they didn't help whatsoever. They just said that they have asked the hotel to refund my money, but the hotel doesn't want to!!!! Actually, I believe Booking.com are complicit in this scam, as they have this terrible hotel listed as a 4 star hotel, despite LOTS of negative comments on their own and other website. Booking.com seem to be happy to continue advertising this hotel, and taking their cut of the money, instead of looking after their own customers. I will not be using Booking.com again, despite using them over 70 times in the past. Beware, this 'hotel' is a rip off. Google it and you will find other reviews similar to this one.

title: Okay hotel with great location
text: This hotel was okay and it worked well the two nights we stayed there. Unfortunately me managed to time the hottest days in London and this hotel did not have air condition. We were given a room on the ground floor as this was said to be the coolest. It was still very hot but I suspect that in comparison with the other rooms, this was okay. It was nicely decorated and clean and the staff was very friendly. The breakfast was not very big but we were given the choice of a full English breakfast. The location was great with about a 30 minute walk to Camden town and a 10 minute walk down to Oxford street. This hotel was good for a few nights and apart from the lack of AC it was comfortable. I would consider this hotel in the future based on its great location.

title: The worst hotel I have ever stayed in.
text: This place, (calling it a hotel is not a proper description), is rubbish. It is listed as 4*, the Trades Description Act would list as a B & B hostel. The carpets are worn, my room had a hole in the ceiling and the window frame was absolutely rotten through and through and the net curtain had a hole in it. The shabby furniture was all marked and worn. The sink in the shower room had a large crack right across all of it, the Wifi was non existent as was any help from the staff. This place has no lift and as a solo OAP I could have done with at least an offer of help with my case up to the 3rd. floor. The stair carpets look as if they've never been vaccuumed and the artificial flowers are thick wih dust. Do avoid at all costs - if I hadn't paid in advance I would never have stayed here.

title: Poor customer service and small rooms
text: Arriving at the hotel I was asked to wait whilst the reception man sorted his papers. I did so patiently for 5 minutes. He then processed my check in details and asked me to wait. I waited, then 5 minutes later he thurst me a key and told me to go to the second floor. I had to ask how I got there, he pointed and watchede struggle with my bag up the narrow stairs . The double room had a very small bed and enough space for 2 people to stand up. I asked to change as I was with my friend and although we know each other this was pushing the boundaries!! The reception man was very unhelpful and told me that now I had been in the room it was mine and I could not change. I think the service was very poor and the room are very small. The location is good but still I feel that overall its is not value for money. Shame as I travel regularly to London.

title: Very good value for a cheap overnight stay in London
text: Paid £65 for a one night stay in a double room INCL a cooked breakfast. This is about as cheap as you can get for a decent nights stay in central London in a good area at fairly short notice. Forget how many stars it says it has - these are facts as experienced by me: Great location. 5 min walk from Euston, 15 min walk from St Pancras. 3 min walk to Goodge St tube station. The hotel has no lift so avoid if you don't want to lug your cases up stairs. It has three floors above ground and the breakfast room is one level below ground. Rooms are small yes but clean, and also quiet with good noise insulation from the traffic outside on Gower St. You can easily sleep without being distracted by outside noise. I stayed in double room 302 on the third floor. Small yes but nice and clean, tea and coffee making facilities, a narrow bathroom with shower cubicle and enough storage space either side of the sink. Nice big mirror too although fairly dimly lit. The bed is a small double so if you're over 6 foot tall you may overhang! Breakfast is nice - choice of tea, coffee, fruit juices, fresh fruit, cereals and the staff will also take your cooked breakfast order if you want one - on offer is bacon, eggs how you want, sausage, cooked tomato etc. For a great local place to eat dinner look behind Goodge St tube station (which is on Tottenham Court Road) on Charlotte Street which is the heart of the area known as 'Fitzrovia'. You'll find some great Italian, Greek, Mexican, Indian and Thai restaurants plus some decent London pubs. Check out time is 11am but they will happily look after your cases in reception if you want to come back later in the day to collect them before leaving London. If you don't want luxury but just a decent clean quiet place to stay in a nice and convenient area then you could do much worse than stay here.

title: Great Disaster
text: This is the most terrible hotel I have ever visited. First of all, no ventilation is available at the hotel, the smell is so disgusting that I can hardly breath well. When we entered the room, you can't believe that the floor is tilted by 20 degree, that means the floor is not flat land, but is a slope. I feel dizzy instantly. Then, I would like to take a rest on the bed, which lead us to another terrible part. The structure of the bed is so fragile and you won't dare to sleep on it. Of course, no need to mention that the single layer of the window will give yiou a feel that the double-deck buses are just next to you. It costs us 105 pounds per nite. But, I have to say that I won't enter this hotel again even if it's free of charge.
