title: Great experience if you are a borrower.
text: If you are looking for a noisy, small and unkempt hotel this is the best place in town. Stayed here for 5 nights and had about 10 hours sleep all week as the noise from all bedroom sides and the road is terrible. My room was so small you could not move around safely and had to keep moving my belonging from bed to floor. The absolute highlight was breakfast coffee ☕. Instant coffee in a cafetiere!!!!!! Unless you are desperate I would avoid.

title: A decent hotel
text: The Cavendish is in a great location, is clean, and satisfactory - it's just that there was nothing special about it at all. While our stay was pleasant enough, there isn't anything that would make me want to go back to that hotel. My only actual complaint was the wifi, which was costly, and did not even work. The rooms we had were small, but neat and clean. All in all, just a decent hotel.

title: nice place
text: close to underground, in a quiet street. near to many cafes, good to breakfast. You can go to almost places on foot.

title: Satisfactory hotel
text: This hotel is satisfactory if you are willing to trade prime location (for visiting University College London) and good breakfast for a microscopic room with limited amenities. In its favor are the excellent location for visitors to University College London (across Gower St from UCL) and excellent English breakfasts. The breakfast is cooked to order and includes eggs, grilled tomatoes, bacon or sausage, toast, fresh fruit, tea, juice, etc. The room was clean and the plumbing is modern and works. Although the bed was harder than I like, I slept well. The staff were pleasant and willing to help when asked. However, there are a number of disadvantages. While many American hotel rooms are unnecessarily large and most European rooms are smaller, my room at the Hotel Cavendish was smaller any I have stayed in and smaller than most cruise ship cabins I have stayed in. It was so small there was no good place to put my luggage. My carryon suitcase spent much of its time in the bathroom, and I literally do not know where one could put a suitcase too large to be carried onto a plane. There was no chair with a back although there was a bench type seat with the small desk/table. I did most of my sitting on the bed to use the headboard as back support. There was only one tiny trash container (with a lid that didn’t open when the foot pedal was depressed). The wifi is erratic, cutting in and out, and generally very poor. I was fortunate to have a room facing Gower St and thus was able to access the UCL network from the hotel

title: Compact and not 4 star
text: I booked this for a business trip and I guess it was cheaper than other 4 star hotels. Location was good as my venue was 10min walk away. Only took 10mins to walk from Euston station. Staff were friendly. The room was the tiniest I have ever stayed in. The double bed took up half the room and I had to place my case on the bed to access the wardrobe. Tiny desk that couldn't take A4 folder portrait way. Tea/coffee facility in the room was standard. The shower room was compact, but the shower had minimal flow. The toilet paper was reasonable and not the cheap newspaper stuff often used! There is no lift so if you had any disability or a heavy bag then you're stuffed. My room was roasting when I arrived as the radiator had been left on full with the window open! Even a few hours later with the heating off, the room was still hot and it was difficult to sleep. You can hear the street outside but then it is a city hotel. Breakfast was acceptable and service was efficient with pleasant staff. The wifi was very slow so I used my 4G as it was much much faster. For a business trip where I needed to bed down for the night, it served a purpose, but I won't plan to stay here again unfortunately.

title: Don't bother
text: I stayed here for one night. I chose it as it was close to Euston for an early train the following morning. The double room consisted of two single beds pushed together. Fine, but one was higher up than the other! The sheets didn't exactly smell fresh. The bedside light didn't work. Lighted flooded in from the hallway into the room. Unsurprisingly I didn't have a very good night's sleep! All this for a bargain £135 a night. My email of complaint was duly ignored. Never stay here.

title: Hotel Cavendish - great service & stay
text: We had a fantastic stay at Hotel Cavendish! The service from the staff was professional, warm and friendly! Location is fantastic - close to the Tube (Euston), British Museum, local high street, University and pubs!! Gower street is really lovely - the architecture is fantastic. The full english breakfast was delicious and all at a reasonable price. It is a converted house, so more a really nice B&B, but we had a really neat stay. Our room was a great size! Even though we looked out on the street, except for the sirens (which are mega loud in the UK), the rooms were noise free! Very comfortable nights sleep and free wireless! Happily stay again.

title: Dont Even Bother Booking
text: Stayed at this hotel 19.03 for one night. My Eurostar was delayed so rescheduled for the following day, so needed a hotel room for the night. On booking.com it rates 4star, So i trusted and booked. 4 stars i would struggle to give it 2 stars. On arrival around 8.30 - 9pm, one lady on the reception and man, Very unfriendly people and basically felt i was more of a nuisance wanting to have a room than a guest. I asked if they had a double room he just said no this is the only room left, A lie i know as rooms available on Booking.com but offered no discount for single traveler. So i thought ok nice attitude, Then breakfast is only from 7:30 - 9:30 really?? especially on a Sunday another let down, I asked the checkout time and he told me 10:30, but later when checking my confirmation in my room it says 11:00 so another lie he told me. I really felt uncomfortable and like i was more of a pain to him than a guest/ customer. On arrival to the room it was so small it was unbelievable, i had to have my suitcase in front of the door when i was in the room and then put it on the bed so i could leave the room. The whole room was just horrible, Shower moldy and hardly worked and im sure they turn the hot water off after a certain time, went to have a shower about 9.30 and it was just warm to say the least. The breakfast is ok in the morning, its free so you cant complain. Overall i would never ever stay at this hotel again unless like this time i was desperate but even then i would rather look for something else. And as for the man in reception he should either learn to give good service or find a new job your doing the hotel no favors in guest ratings.

title: Very basic hotel conveniently located
text: Well, the reason we stayed there is its location, conveniently located between St Pancras train station and the British Museum. It is also quite cheap compared to other hotels in central London. Apart from that, the room was tiny, smelly, very basic and would really need some renovation. Cleanliness could also be improved...

title: Good hotel for brief stay in central London
text: This is the kind of hotel where you will be neither disappointed nor delighted. It aims to be a good place to stay near London attractions and it does that just right. The room was small but it was modern, nicely furnished, bed fine, nice but small shower room and everything worked. Free wi-fi with a good signal, good TV, biscuits, and satisfactory breakfast (no decaff coffee though - just buy a jar - it's not difficult!). It's only about 5 minutes from the shops of Tottenham Court Road and the restaurants of Charlotte Street.

title: Warning - not a 4 star hotel!
text: Really disappointed with the hotel as I booked this for my girlfriend's birthday, paying a lot of money for what I was told was a 4-star hotel. The hotel was very dated and worn and our room was terrible. There were huge cracks in the plaster in the walls and ceiling, the main door looked very insecure and the lock was sitting in a crudely made hole in the door, the bedside lampshade looked like it had been trampled, the carpet and sideboard was dusty and the bathroom was an oddly constructed cabin structure in the bedroom. The bathroom itself wasn't too bad apart from being a bit worn and no hot water in the sink. Bitterly disappointed - I paid £450 for 2 nights and should have gone to a Travelodge/Holiday Inn/etc for a cheaper and better experience when all things considered.

title: do not stay here
text: The hotel as a hotel is nice as it's been refurbished but the service was horrible. When I arrived the owner attempted to put me in another hotel next door for one night that was horrible. Obviously he had overbooked. When I didn't agree he didn't know what to do with me until I finally had to stay at a friend's house. When I arrived the next day the I said, okay at least he gave me a double room for the week instead of a single at a really good price. To my surprise, there was no telephone, even though they advertise they do on the internet. This was something horrible for me as I spend the week in the cold on payphones. When I asked to use their phone, they were hesitant and they actually took two pounds from me for calling within London for 10 minutes. During the week people came into my room and hung up pictures without asking me, people came in for the satellite tv. I thought this was really rude as I didn't expect people to be running in and out of my room except for the cleaning ladies. My last night the owner again asked me to move into a single room... I just thought this hotel was very unprofessional and made my life difficult for no reason except to make more money for them. The rooms and the breakfast was fine but the service is what compels me to give it a terrible review. To be honest I did save money by staying there but I would have preferred to pay more and not have these problems. I was alone in London, doing business from 9-5 so I didn't have time to change hotels. I would never stay there again.

title: Not a 4 star
text: Very disappointing and definitely not a 4 star as advertised. I had a single room which was tiny even by London standards. The TV didn't work staff were OK. The hotel is very shabby. My room had a blind with mould on it. Location is central but I would not recommend this hotel particularly if you are looking for a 4 star.

title: Totally absurd that it's rated at 4 stars!
text: The tiny single rooms are more cramped than a prison cell. There's literally no legroom in the bathroom, the sink is just a bit larger than a cereal bowl and the shower is half-clogged. The overall cleanliness is unsatisfactory. The Wi-Fi connectivity fluctuates a lot. If this "hotel" is ranked 4 (four!!!) stars in London, then the accomodation standards in that city must be abysmal. Do yourself a big favour and avoid this place at all costs. The entire vicinity seems deplorable anyway, so avoid anything on the Gower street. There's no way you can't find better places at the same price or maybe even less in the nearby areas.

title: Judge for yourself
text: We stayed in room 101 on Sat 31st of Jan 2015. We only stayed 1 night but from check in to check out had no problems. The room was clean tidy and warm shower fine. Ok not the Ritz but also not the pits. For the price we paid excellent value for money. The breakfast was fine plenty of it and good quality.All staff including the waitresses very helpful and pleasant. So do as we did judge for yourself you may be surprised.

title: Location, Location, Location
text: I stayed there in April 2011 for two weeks and I definitely enjoyed it. My single room was large , clean sheets, new furniture, only the carpet was dirty and a bit old. The showers and toilets I used were brand new, and sparkling clean. Staff very friendly, I had a problem with my lock and they fixed in in a matter of minutes. And as bonus, I had someone playing the piano wonderfully just next door . Breakfast the same every day but it didn

title: Excellent value for money
text: Stayed for one night mid week in September. Halls of Residence with basic student rooms and shared bathrooms. Comfortable bed, clean and quiet. A massive hot and cold breakfast is provided and included in the price. The hostel is located near Saddler Wells on a main bus route less than 2 km from the West End and at £37.50 is outstanding value

title: Basic but good value
text: If you are looking for cheap accommodation in London during the student vacations then I can recommend the LSE halls of residence. This is the second one I have stayed in and would happily use them again. The room is basic (no tv/haridryer) and you share a bathroom with 3 other rooms. But the rooms are clean, towels are provided, wifi is free and they do a stonking good breakfast! We were located a few mins walk from Angel Tube with plenty of food shops/takeaways/pubs/restaurants nearby, and for London the traffic noise at night was very quiet.

title: Great value accommodation in LSE dorm.
text: The staff is friendly and helpful, the breakfast is fresh and plentiful, and the location is great. Roseberry Hall is a block from Exmouth market for a wide array of eating options or you can take advantage of the kitchenettes with fridge and microwave. The rooms are just dorm rooms but the bed was comfy. Toilets and showers are shared but clean and, unlike many uni holiday accommodation, all rooms are served by lifts. Bus to Waterloo outside the door and Angel tube station just up the road. Book ahead if you can.

title: An absolute dive but with good brekkie
text: I stayed at LSE before on Drury Lane which was perfection, so I booked this. Oh god I wish I hadn’t. It cost £95 which for London isn’t bad I guess but I’ve stayed at the 2 Grange Hiteks bear tower bridge for that price and it’s 5*. This was an actual hovel. We had a twin room, the beds were broken, the shared toilet had used paper hand towels all over the floor which hadn’t been cleared he next day and reeked of strong urine, and the shower looked unusable. The corridors look rough and univiting...I was ashamed to have gone here with my friend saying “I’m sure it’ll do us great” as my other experience was so good. I honestly don’t know how people live here throughout their studies, it’s disgusting. Literally the only reason this is 2* not 1 is because the breakfast was good. But the room itself was HORRIFIC and I literally could not be paid to come back here. Side note, reception staff were horrifically rude too, they had headphones in when we arrived and weren’t listening to us or each other. STAY AWAY. Book the one on Drury Lane instead, similar price if it’s available and way better, and the location is obviously amazing too. This wasn’t great for that.

title: Basic but cheap.
text: I stayed here in June for about £47 for one night which as London prices go for bed and breakfast I think is decent. Rooms are very basic student accommodation and a bit tired looking - that said the beds are comfortable and that’s all you need sometimes. Breakfast was good - a mixture of cereal, cooked and continental. You could have as much as you wanted.

title: Be very cautious
text: Room accceptable for price

title: Took some getting used to but on the whole a positive stay
text: I stayed with my daughter while she was attending an acting course. Check in was easy enough but a little friendlier would have been nice. The room smelled awful when we walked into it but we got used to it. Unisex bathrooms were unpleasant with broken toilet seats and as another reviewer has mentioned, plugs in the showers blocked with hairs etc. Kitchen was clean and I wouldn't have minded using it for tea, coffee or making a meal. The breakfast was really surprisingly good with plenty of hot drinks, toast and juice plus 6 other items from a wide selection. The room was small but adequate for our needs. The last night of a week was spoiled by the arrival of hundreds of spanish students who were blocking access to the stairs and lifts. The y then spent a good couple of hours in the evening runnning along the corridors and banging doors, also when I looked out one kid was going along trying all the door handles! Convenient for buses into the city centre and walkable as well. Cheap accomodation with good breakfast and good transport available but dont expect the Ritz!

title: So so
text: My wife and I stayed only for one night. The location is good and the price was very cheap. The rooms were very poorly decorated but the beds confortableand clean enough. Toilets and showers unisex (due to building work). The toilets were very urine smelling, quite unpleasant and in general not throurougly clean. Breakfast ok but staff were surly. Noisy all night. Staff on the telephone not very helpfull, but in person a lot worse. Ok it's cheap but lots of other cheap places.

title: Great value
text: What great value this place is. Do not expect five stars

title: It is good for the value but certainly needs simple improvement
text: I read most of the reviews on Rosebery Hall. I am an LSE student staying here until finding permanent accommodation. Let me start from the staff. The front desk people are quit moody, if you catch them in a bad mood they give you plenty of bad attitude. The breakfast is surprisingly great relative to the shabby rooms and horrible shower/toilets. The building is under construction so the bathroom on my floor was not working. I had to go upstairs or downstairs to use the bathroom. The shower was so dirty that I cringed every time I was taking a shower and I asked several other people and they said the same thing. the location is fantastic. Very close to Central London and King's Cross tube station (one stop over on the Northern line). the room I stayed in was smelly and that's because the carpet was from 1970's, no joke. the bed was also extremely uncomfortable. I could also feel every single spring. and the high light of my stay was when the African worker behind the hot food shouted at me because I was taking a banana on the way out. So I had to go and talk to the manager. This was not pleasant at all. all and all, it was not the best experience but I guess it could always be worse. as another reviewer said lower your expectations cuz this ain't Ritz!

title: The best value for money in London
text: An excellent value for money accommodation and well appointed for both tube & bus, my room was small but clean and well serviced, the breakfast was very good with lots of choice. The Ladies bathroom/shower room was uni sex due to repairs to Gents, which was a little awkward but led to some funny encounters. As a solo traveller I felt very safe and the walk to Old St tube was about 5mins if that. I will definately stay here again.

title: No internet for non-LSE students
text: My husband and I stayed in a twin en-suite for 10 days in August which cost around 70 bps/day including breakfast - certainly much cheaper than a hotel. The room and bathroom were bare-bones and dated but clean. The beds were horrible - could feel every bed spring. The majority of other residents were visiting summer school students so it got very loud at times. Our big disappointment was finding that we could not access the LSE wireless internet service or use the computer room. The front desk was not helpful at all. Breakfast was fairly good. Overall, our stay was adequate but I don't think I'd stay here again.

title: An uninhabitable room in a great location.
text: My room was on the 7th floor. The bathroom less than 50 feet away was being actively demolished and rebuilt while I was there, causing construction noise and traffic all day and dust at all hours. I had to use the dark, creepy and cramped "unisex" bath on the other side of the elevator lobby. I was told no other room was available. I was there to write a paper, but I could not work in my room during the day. On the day I checked out, there was no running water in the building. The dryers in the laundry room did not work. LSE student wifi was not made available

title: Avoid if possible!
text: A very good location, welcome and breakfast. However , having paid over £400 for a 5 night stay in a twin room with ensuite the accommodation was very very bad value for money. Dirty, airless incredibly noisy hot room which was not serviced even once during the whole of our stay. We requested towels which were handed to us, but bins , beds and bathrooms were just ignored as far as cleaning and changing were concerned. If you can , go somewhere else.

title: Terrible experience
text: One of the worst experiences I have had. Multiple floors of bathrooms out of order for months, drilling constantly throughout the day, multiple hot water disruptions every week and lack of prompt repair. Would not recommend AT ALL. Only thing half-decent was the reception and catering staff.

title: nightmare stay in worse student digs I have ever seen
text: I stayed here for a trainning weekend with 50 other women. It was hell, rooms were very poorly decorated with put you up type beds, Room smelt musty. Despite ensuite being booked none of our rooms were. Toilets and showers unisex (due to building work). Toilet seats broken and showers dirty. I was at uni 25 years ago and they were better halls then. Toilets long walk from room. Water in room not siutable for drinking, shared kitchens dirty. Confrence room boiling no windows or aircon, even the water in cooler was stale and smelt. Breakfast ok but staff were surly. Coffee machine in hall out of coffee and tea. Drunks in corridor. Noisy all night. Ok it's cheap but lots of other cheap places. Good location.

title: It may be halls of residence but we are still paying customers
text: I stayed here with friends and we had 4 rooms between us. I was well aware of what I was booking after being a student myself and after staying in halls of residence in other cities for a cheaper alternative. So I knew what to expect of the room etc. That did meet expectation, exactly what you would expect so thats all fine. A room with a bed a desk and a wardrobe - very basic but all that is needed for a short stay. This particular room had a shared bathroom - again this was advertised so no shock. However - underwear was left randomly in the bathroom by previous users. The cleaners went in that bathroom on at least 2 separate occasions and never removed these garments, they were just left there on the floor. Also after we checked in we left the bags etc in the room and headed out. After we returned late in the evening my friend went in her room and there was a mop and bucket in there that hadn't been there previously. So since checking in someone had been in the room and left behind this mop and bucket - god knows why! Like I say its a cheap alternative to hotel or normal b&b but we are still paying customers so some service is still expected and entering a room after check in shouldn't be happening and certainly not leaving cleaning things behind. The reception was very efficient on checking us in and the breakfast was very nice. The location was perfect for our night out in Angel.

title: Terrific location, terrific price.
text: Rosebery Hall Residence is a marvellously comfortable and pretty central experience. Where else can you bump into 40 very lively Dutch visitors and have a copy of Paionios' Nike next door? Seriously though, this is a terrific bargain.

title: Stay here to be near LSE and the Law Landmarks i.e Inner Temple
text: I payed more (80£ vs 64£) and stayed in the Postgraduate Middleton Wing which has nicerrecently refurbished rooms as compared to the undergraduate wing with older rooms. Whichever wing you all choose, do request for a courtyard facing room on a higher floor as they are quieter. Good breakfast spread. Just outside and to the left as you exit Rosebery Hall, you enter into Exmouth Market with a good coffee house called Gail's and if you are up for great small plates/tapas check out Lavender. Pizza Pilgrims make great yummylicious 10£ pizzas and I love their house beer and their young funky friendly staff.

title: Cheap well-located option, but too dirty
text: The only positive comments to this residence are about the staff - very friendly and ready to help in the reception, the breakfast, which is well served, and the reasonable location, nearby Angel. But, there are several negative points that make this residence too expensive for the price, including: - bedroom was really tiny, matresses were not comfotable, very used and smelly, and the room and corridor air was very saturated - mainly in the corridors/elevators, there was zero ventilation - bed sheets were not fresh cleaned and there was dust and smell in the wardrobes - hot water ends at about 23:00 - if you want a hot shower before sleeping, need to be before that time - vending machines not working, coffee machines not working too Therefore, I would only recommend such place if nothing around is available and if you just need a place to sleep a day - considering you have no allergies or problems with uncomfortable bed/bedroom.

title: Economic choice
text: I was on a course in the area and for economies sake, I stayed at the London School of Economics student accommodation on Roseberry Avenue. The staff were very helpful and friendly, looking up information online to help myself and a colleague, when we had slight emergencies. The room was clean, basic but perfectly suitable, and although the toilets and showers aren't en suite, they are clean and modern. The breakfast is included, and there is a pleasant choice for meat eaters and vegetarians. A colleague couldn't eat gluten and they provided gluten free bread, which I think she had made them aware of, prior to her stay. You don't walk away from breakfast hungry. It is only 200 yards to the Sadler's Wells Theatre, who have a pleasant café attached. Exmouth market is a food area, and again only about 200 years away, so there are plenty of places to eat and drink nearby. I will stay there another time, it really is a bargain. One of the colleagues on my course, also staying there was in her early 80s

title: Good location, friendly staff
text: This accom is clean with friendly staff and a great variety for breakfast. They have a computer room, laundrette, pool table and table tennis table. The staff are helpful if you have any questions. Only downside was our room faced a busy street so when it got a bit hot and you had to leave the window open, it was a bit noisy, but since you're knackered from the day exploring you'll fall straight to sleep anyway. Noise does travel down the corridor but I would definitely stay here again.

title: OK for one night if the price is right
text: Stayed for one night, I have stayed in student accommodation before so I knew what to expect but for £50 with cooked breakfast its OK but if they want more than £70 might be looking at some of the better tourists hotels in Earls Court or Paddington of Bayswater that offer En-suite , TV and a more homely feel.

title: Great location
text: The main reason I chose this accommodation was the excellent location. It's a short walk to the Angel tube station (one stop from Kings Cross). My room was basic with a single bed, desk and basin - shared bathroom facilities were a short walk along the corridor. A cafeteria style cooked breakfast was included. It was a little noisy at night as my room was close to the road but that's to be expected being close to the city.

title: Excellent loaction, good rooms
text: I stayed at Rosebery for 3 weeks on a study trip. The loaction is the first thing one would notice. It's situated in the heart of the city of London, with every major place of interest at a 10-15 min walk or a short bus ride away. The room are comfy. It's quiet during the day, while if you want to socialize at night you need to just head down to the pub on the ground floor. The common bathrooms are actually quite well maintained. Also, the kitchen at the end of each hall is very convenient. Definitely a "no worries" residence hall!

title: Decent value and convenient location for a short stay
text: Great central location, approx 15 minutes walk from Kings Cross, 5 minutes to Angel tube station. Breakfast very good and included in price. Some of the rooms (the 2 person in particular) are a bit small, so maybe not so good for longer stays - but excellent value for 2-3 night stay.

title: Great!
text: Great stay for price! Not to far from the underground or the city. In a student area which is fun. Comfortable and no complaints. I enjoyed my stay. I would recommend if you are traveling to London. :)

title: Great value for the money you pay
text: The staff was very friendly and helpful. It's a walking distance from "Angel" subway station. In the heart of London, just one station away from King cross. Rooms were very clean. The breakfast was delicious too :)

title: Basic but great value for money.
text: No frills here but basic, great budget accommodation. Very useful to have a kitchen available. Great location. Excellent transport links and a very handy supermarket a few yards away. Willd definitely book again.

title: Incredible value - I loved it
text: Pros: £50 a night including good breakfast Room is basic but clean and has big desk and wash basin WIFI Location is excellent - ten minutes walk/bus from Angel, twenty minutes bus from Piccadilly Circus Very helpful staff Cons: for this price it's not ensuite but the showers down the corridor are fine. (NB It isn't full at the moment - maybe it's less clean and quiet in the summer...)

title: While the students are away, the tourists play!
text: LSE Rosebery Hall is a modern student accommodation complex located on Rosebery Avenue in North London. This is a very handy location with frequent bus service into central London and a fifteen minute walk to Angel tube station and the restaurants, cafes, shops and pubs of Islington. During university holidays, rooms are available for visitors to rent. A full English breakfast, served in the complex' cafeteria is included in the price. We stayed in the newer extension called Middleton Hall. Our room was for married students, had a double bed, 2 study desks and en-suite toilet/shower. Very comfortable. Down the hall was a large eat-in kitchen equipped with stove, microwave, sink and frig, so we were able to buy pre-cooked meals at Sainsburys or Waitrose bring them home and cook them ours selves. Much easier on the budget.

title: Great location for those on a budget!
text: Rosebery Hall is a great deal for those who want to stay near central london, but want to save money. We booked through travelstay and it cost 156 pounds for 2 people for 4 nights (19.50 a person per night) We booked last minute and this place was great for us. It is about a ten minute walk from Angel metro station so it is very easy to get into the heart of london. The rooms were simple, but that is to be expected since it is a dorm. The halls smelled funky from people cooking, but the rooms were nice. There is a sink in each room and the beds were comfy. Also, the rooms are cleaned daily and you are provided with fresh towels and soap. There are two bathrooms/shower areas on each floor (one for men and the other for women) that were fine. Make sure to bring your own shampoo as that is not provided. We were on the top floor on the street side and we didnt hear any noise at night. If you ever stayed in a dorm room in college, the same standards can be expected of Rosebery hall. If i ever return to London, I would be pleased to stay at Rosebery Hall!!

title: Smelly corridors , dirty and dark
text: Ok, these are students halls, I understand, and I also understand the rate is quite cheap. However, they place still needs to be clean, right? Not so much! I can not possibly describe how horrible the corridors smell: like smell of curry combined with sweat and feet adore with a touch of urine and soya source for the top note!!! But the worse thing I saw was the mouse trap(attached to this review) in the room!!! They NEVER said I might meet some mice in the middle of the night. I didn't, but the view of having to put up with a mouse trap in the room was shocking. LSE has other halls round London with more or less same rate. The Bankside Hall is MUCH cleaner with much better access to central London. So, I'm very surprised why they didn't bring the level of hygiene up in this branch

title: Nice location
text: Had a few days here whilst watching the Rugby League Cup Final. Excellent location, away from the hustle and bustle of the city centre, opposite Sadlers Wells and close to the Angel, Islington. The #38 bus stops outside to Victoria, via Shaftsbury Ave. Piccadilly Circus and Marble Arch and are every few minutes. The rooms are small but clean and comfy and have free WiFi. There are toilets and showers on every floor and also a kitchen where you can make a meal. Sainsburys and Iceland are within walking distance. Breakfast is served every morning, cooked or continental, it's excellent. All in all, really good value

title: Perfect for my needs
text: I have stayed in an LSE halls previously behind the Tate Modern and went into Roseberry Hall with similar expectations. Let's get one thing straight- these are student halls, and if you didn't know that before you arrive, then you have seriously failed to do your research. They will be basic, but if you just need somewhere to lie your head after a busy day in the capital, they will do the job. My single room certainly did the job for me. Spacious, with a relatively comfortable single bed, desk and sink along with towels and toiletries. As I was in London for work, the speedy, free wifi was excellent. Reception staff were friendly, breakfast good (although I would steer clear of the ropey coffee machines!), and location to get around London via bus or tube was excellent. All in all, budget accommodation for those who just need something functional. For my £45, I don't think I could have done better.

title: Not my kind of accommodation.
text: Used TravelStay to find this accommodation. In spite of requesting a ground floor room due to my wife's fear of heights we were assigned a room on the 5th floor. The reception staff were sympathetic and reassigned us a room on a lower floor. There was no mention of it being student accommodation for the London School of Economics. Our block and entrance to assigned room smelled strongly (a sickly sweet smell) which permeated everything. It gave my wife a migraine. We complained and were offered another room. It was just as bad so we stayed put. It was raining hard and we had to exit reception to access our block and got soaked. We couldn't find the door to our block as it was poorly signed so we had to return to reception in the pouring rain then back through the rain to a well concealed door. We entered the block to encounter aforementioned smell and rodent trap (very reassuring). We unlocked the door to our room to find it was a disabled room for two students with notice boards (stained and marked) on the walls. The walls had stains and bare patches where plaster had been disrupted by the removal of some wall decoration. The beds were metal fold up style which rattled and moved around. The cupboards were plentiful but stained and dirty with heavy concentration of mould in one of them. The other had a hole in the door about the size of a tennis ball. The carpet tiles were old and in places badly fitted with gaps and tears. The toilet was the worst of all - it was a wet room style toilet with floor tiles which were grubby and grimy. The wash basin had a heavy line of black mould on the sealant, the shower head was so crusted with lime scale that it squirted water sideways past the inadequate shower curtain which fell off the rails when drawn. The ceiling tiles in the wet room were broken and sagging and the radiator was rusted and stained on the bottom right edge. Having complained about the smell we were offered another room but when we checked it we found no great improvement so stayed where we were. The windows to our room opened on to an external walkway and we were woken by returning guests at 1am. In summary it is way overpriced (£92 per night) for the grade of accommodation. In spite of being informed, on the web site of TravelStay, there were no tea making facilities in the rooms or available in the Kitchen and the bar was closed for the duration of our stay. There is no phone in the room and no TV or radio for entertainment. You have to go to the television room in the basement (another smelly sweaty room). Book here at your peril or be aware that it isn't all it is cracked up to be. The offer of a refund would be in order. ps I have photos to prove my assertions.

title: Good experience overall!! Breakfast rules :)
text: Stayed here for a night with friends. Room and beds were average but it was worth for the price. Staff were friendly and helpful. Shared bathroom and Kitchen was too modern and clean. Wifi speed was above average. 5-8 min walk from Angel Underground (Northern line). Highlight of the stay is massive, delicious breakfast we had got in our booking.

title: Excellent Accommodation for little money
text: I stayed at the Rosebery Hall over New Years 2009/2010. I really enjoyed the stay at the RH. The room (single room) was clean, with a washing basin, and it was big enough, with a table and two soft chairs. The basin and litter got cleaned every day. Bathroom facilities (toilet and shower) are in the hall, and I had to share it with only 3 other rooms, but never met anyone there or had to wait to get in. also those facilities were always clean and got cleaned as well every day. The accommodation is also very quiet, you don´t hear any noises from the streets or any other noises, except maybe footsteps when someone walks in the hall. The staff members have all been very nice and kind and also very helpful. You can store your luggage when arriving before 2pm. Security is very high in this accommodation. Only those who stay there are able to get in. Others need to ring to get in (Staff from reception needs to open) The breakfast was really good. They stick with the 6 items you can get, but that is actually a lot, as you have many choices from bread rolls to cornflakes, bacon, eggs etc. toast and marmelade/honey are for free. Same as the drinks. Another positive aspect is that you can book single rooms there, for all those who travel alone The next Underground station (Angel) is only 5 minutes walk. And it only takes about 15 minutes with the tube to Picadilly Circus, Leicester Square etc. The area (Islington) itself is also very nice with lots of shops, supermarkets, restaurants and cafes. I really enjoyed the stay at the Rosebery Hall, and i can highly recommend this accommodation to all those who are looking for a cheap but good stay in London! I would and will always go back there when staying in London!

title: awful
text: worst place i've ever stayed at -certainly would not go there again didn't get a wink of sleep all night,it would have been easier to sleep in the street like a tramp.desk staff were miserable and surly and presumably low paid sorry but nothing good to say-except stay clear

title: Awful stay, will never come back again
text: Encouraged by the reviews, I booked a single room at Rosebery during the summer. It was the worst decision I've made while traveling (and I've stayed at many youth hostels across Europe). The rooms and furniture are old, the walls yellow, the hallways smell strongly of urine esp. near the bathrooms (don't even get me started on the bathrooms - they stink so badly I try to go to public bathrooms before I return to my room.) You don't get to sleep past 7.30am because the management neglected to tell you that they are doing construction work on windows, bathrooms when you book, and only give you that information just before you arrive (so it's too late to change your booking). They also didn't tell me that workers will be coming in and out of my room from 8am, aka trying to unlock my door while I was changing, even after I yelled for them to 'give me a minute!' The last straw was when workers broke an expensive bottle of wine I had left in my room, and I got back at the end of the day to a carpet soaked in wine, the room reeking of alcohol (they didnt even bother to change my room for me), and a note saying they'll replace the bottle (they never did, and the management claimed no responsibility). Such blatant disrespect for their guests (no advance notice of construction work, no respect for private property, no sense of hospitality whatsoever) cancels out whatever redeeming features they have, like varied breakfast and proximity to the Angel tube station. You will be better off booking a room at any of the other LSE residences (I've stayed at Passefield Hall as well, and it is closer to the Euston tube station, much better quality rooms, and very very nice reception) - all for only 5 pounds more a night. This place is awful, and for your own sake, do not stay here.

title: great value for money
text: this is for the traveller on a budget. the rooms are small but neat and clean.shared bathroom breakfast is the highlight with a full breakfast with 6 choices. only 10 minutes walok to the tube station on a direct line to the city .

title: How broke are you?
text: I had spent a few nights at LSE's Passfield Hall and wanted to extend my stay, but they were booked up. The nice guy at the desk kindly called another LSE school and I was on my way, after (foolishly) putting down a nonrefundable deposit for 2 nights. There is nothing horribly wrong with Rosebery, if you are on a tight budget and don't mind Motel 6. The rooms were very clean, but things like the carpet and the furniture looked as thought they could've been replaced a number of years ago. My view was of the building behind, which looked more like a tenament than anything else. Also, as the cheapest of the LSE dorms, it seems to attract large groups of traveling students, and that's fine for them! Overall, too dingy, too old, too smelly, too depressing to feel like I'd want to come home even to spend a few hours here.

title: Everything Is Good But I Can't Handle With The Shower
text: Love it at Rosebery. All in perfect condition. BUT, I can't manage with the shower especially in gents toilet. THE SHOWER IS VERY HOT AND CAN NOT BE ADJUST AS THAT IS ONLY HOT WATER THAT THEY PROVIDE TO US. Could you imagine, I stay for 4 night on summer. The problem is when I get sweat after walking around in central London in warm weather and then return back to Rosebery for bath, I feel disappointed with the shower.

title: Good location - student hall of residence
text: This really is a student hall of residence, and feels like it, although much better furnished than in my day. It is built around a small garden, with a modest communal "pub" and a dining room below street level. Standard, nourishing, LSE breakfast - choice of six items from a range including fruit, yoghurt, cooked bacon eggs sausage etc. The location is ideal for Sadlers Wells, being about three minutes walk, and Islington - the Angel is less than 10 minutes walk. A major London bus route, the 19, goes down Roseberry. Although there did not seem to be much traffic at the weekend, the room on the third floor seemed to be noisy with traffic noise. And of course in a place like this one is at the mercy of fellow residents - if a group come back after midnight, you will probably wake up. Being a student hall, it is only available during holiday periods, but that includes the summer. The LSE website is very good and makes a booking an easy task. And you don't have to pay more than a small deposit up front.

title: Wonderful stay
text: I had a very satisfactory 5 night stay here. It’s probably a bit less “closer to the action” than other LSE residences, but still an easy 20 minute walk to Covent Garden, and literally across the road from Sadlers Wells theatre. I even had a nice view of St Paul’s Cathedral from my room. It’s in a more residential area and a lot quieter than the other student residences. I had a comfortable bed and felt very well rested by the end of my stay. Good shower and clean toilets. Housekeeping was very efficient and towels were changed as and when requested – something which didn’t happen in the other residences. Breakfast was excellent, good choices and plenty of space for guests in the dining hall. I was sorry to leave and am jealous of whichever student gets to spend the coming terms in “my” room! I would highly recommend staying here next Easter/summer.

title: Good value for money
text: I booked this for a 2 night stay

title: Very good value!
text: I stayed in the Rosebery Hall for 4 days alone (girl) while visited London. I was perfectly happy with everything and of course I knew that It's not the Ritz. I didn't regret the booking here. I felt absolutely safe. I arrived late night, the check in was fast and the lady on the reception was welcoming. The location is very good, the nearest metro stops (Angel, Farringdon) are only 5 min by walk. The nearest bus stop 1 min. I liked as well in the location that you can get easily to the center, but It's quite with gardens around. My room on the third floor looked to the street, and I like to leave the window open a bit, but also I'm sensitive with the noise in the morning especially - and there was some noise: kids go to school, workers singing while going to work etc- so I had ear plugs and I could sleep like a baby. The room was ok, you dont have to spend there all day...to go to sleep there it's good. In the neighbour rooms as I saw usually students stayed. They were absolutely okey as well and quite. You share the toilet and the shower with 3 more rooms (max. 6 more people - on my floor) I didn't have any problem with this, It was always clean. There is cleaning service every day in the room! At the breakfast you have choice to have 6 items + juice and coffee. I think if you choose wisely the 6 is enough. I was full everytime (bacon, cheese, scrambled eggs, croasaint, yoghurt, cereal...). I would recommend this place and I would come back again! :)

title: Well...
text: The accomodation was basic & rather cramped and the smell both inside & outside the room was horrific. It actually made me physically sick. They also tried to charge me twice for the stay.

title: You get what you pay for...
text: We stayed in a twin room. Rooms: they are puny, the walls are so thin that one hears everything, carpet wasn't clean, bedsheets and towels were though (thank god !), no soap at the sink in the room, terrible matress which needs to be changed. Our room was looking at the street, so it did get loud at times. Bathrooms/Showers: we had to cross two hallways to get to the ladies toilets/shower room. It was clean at times, and sometimes people just left it really nasty. The showers were ok, the only disturbing part was that there is only one hanger for clothes, so you have to use it smart, if you don't want to get your clothes soaked. Breakfast: was alright, can't complain. I am a vegetarian, and was happy that there where also no meat choices. You can only get 6 items from the "buffet", so use it wisely ! Location: Excellent. Close to the train station. There are markets, shops, restaurant, etc. when you continue the street.

title: Dissapointing
text: Bad: Room was a mess: there was a chair in the room with horrible marks and stains all over it. The Blind was dirty and so were the walls and the floor, just stains and marks. I have left my jacket in the room after i have checked out. I called them to send it back to me. They send they would- week later i had to call them ( 3 times to find out what is going on) , they said they have not found it and students have moved back in now- so there is no way its anywhere :( would not go there again- better to spend some more money and go place else Good: Breakfast included: from 7-10 that was good, not to early

title: Baaaaaaaaaaaaaad experience
text: Chunky old metal bar beds and too small. No closet hangers in the wardrobe????????????!!!!!!! No electric point near the mirror (shaving). Plastic curtains.... what the.... Breakfast is limited (to 6 pieces) 'Can I have some bacon please?' Yes, ONE piece. Friendly staff though - I feel for them to have to work there.

title: Definitely recommend
text: Stayed here for 1 night in August. Its location is what prompted us to book. No hassle, very friendly. Room was very comfortable and clean as was the attached bathroom. Breakfast was plentiful (6 items plus unlimited bread, tea and coffee). Ask for back of the building for more "peace". Staff, however, not aware that on-street parking is FREE right on their doorstep on weekends

title: Excellent value for money-Perfect B&B at a good location
text: Have stayed on several occassions at this accomodation. In my last visit it got renovated and the shared bathroom is very modernised and at high standard.Always enjoyed the heartful breakfast and the safe central location. In the night there is a bus going to town outside the hall.It's an excellent value for London and would recommend it to anyone who wants a basic clean accomodation at a very good and safe location.

title: Not all roses at Rosebery Hall Residence!
text: This was my 3rd visit to Rosebery and I must admit, I was somewhat disappointed. First let me list the positives. It is a very good location in Islington with access to Angel Station plus great bus service right out front. Lots of places to eat, drink and shop within a couple of blocks. Exmouth Market offers great variety as does the area around Angel Station. Can walk to St. Paul's Cathedral in 20 minutes. Theatre district is 15 minutes by bus at night....longer in daytime because of traffic. Rooms are basic and I shared a toilet and shower room with others on floor. They were always clean. Amenities Room (kitchen) on each floor. Cleaner when there aren't students around who make the same mess they do at home, but here there is no Mom here to clean up after them. Can store your food in the fridge. Now have WiFi access in the rooms, a plus. Showers should be much improved as they were doing renos while I was there. Had to search other floors to find one that worked...so be prepared to roam the halls in you basics!!! Be prepared for stairs as the elevator broke down while we were there and only one elevator goes to the top of Myddleton Tower - 7 floors. Generally reception has great young people who try to do their best for you. The noisy local young men who like to gather out behind the residence are still there, but when it rains, they don't come out, otherwise street noise can be loud in the late evenings.

title: Worst campus accommodation I have ever stayed in
text: I am used to staying in campus accomodation during the summer in London, it is usually, basic but cheap, safe, clean and central. I had thought that Rosebury Hall would be a safe bet - how sadly i was wrong. The hall is a 1970s building, attractive from the outside in leafy Islington and just across the road from Sadlers Wells. Angel is the nearest tube and Farrington described as close by is actually about a mile away with a hill to climb on the way. the lady on the desk was friendly enough and gave me (wrong) directions to my room. The room itself I had booked as being the cheapest en suite option available - the door opened into a dark and dismal small corridor with two cupboards ( I think) it was really too dark to tell. The aroma of the room was overpowering being a combination of adolescent male and stale tobacco smoke. The chip board ceiling tiles were all damaged and water stained and the damage was obviously old, the pipe casings on the wall had obviously been levered off at some stage and never put back properly, the bathroom floor had a good layer of dried in scum on it and the ceiling tiles suffered the same problems as those in the bedroom. The decor was that cream colour that was fashionable in the 80s which was probably when it was last painted judging by the state of it. The beds were essentially camp beds - there was no mirror in the bedroom, and although there was one in the bathroom, it was too dark to see anything in. The sink had a big sign warning against drinking the water ( this was in England for heaven sake). I arrived at midnight unfortunately - otherwise i would just have left to find somewhere else. On the plus side - the wifi was good, and the staff in the dining room at breakfast were very friendly. The breakfast was of a high standard for campus accommodation. LSE should be ashamed of itself for renting out rooms that have been neglected to this degree to students - and it is completely criminal to let out a room in this state at £84 to the tourist or conference trade. Students - if any of you read this, complain, loud and long if you recognise this room .

title: Do not rely on your booking
text: We booked an en suite room to stay in the night before I needed to attend an eye hospital appointment. We booked it 14 days before arrival and yet it took until the night before for them to call me to tell me they had overbooked and an en suite was no longer available. Not only this but they had already taken the money from my credit card for the booking. To make matters worse I discovered it was London Fashion Week and so now all hotel rooms near the eye hospital were either fully booked or charging nearly double the prices they were when I was researching somewhere to stay 14 days before. We did manage to find some alternative accommodation eventually and I can thoroughly recommend Accommodation London Bridge.

title: Sub-standard.
text: The rooms are prison like. Simple bed, cupboard and table (with no chair) combo. The one we originated in had cut chair and holes in the walls. Staff were standard. Friendly enough. No real positives that make it willing to stay. Standard canteen. Wouldn't recommend for any travel.

title: Does what it says on the tin
text: Mattresses were a bit lumpy and the en suite ceiling was falling apart, other than that, it was ok for what we wanted, a central location for a stag night in London. Breakfast was good, plenty of choice, with other options if you didn't want a fry up!!

title: Basic but great location
text: As l was taking my 86 year old mother to Sadlers Wells, l had to find accomodation that was very.close by, this was it. Ideally located with very helpful staff. It is fairly basic but the beds were comfortable and.the breakfast plentiful. The bathrooms were not too bad but unfortunately the toilets were blocked the whole time we were there and we had to walk to the next floor. Not ideal for an old person. Worth a look if you visit the theatre.

title: The international mans destinations
text: In London, one often observes the price of hotels to be obscenely expensive. The LSE Rosebery Halls are basic, clean with a great location close to Islington and not far from Kings Cross/Euston. Come one come all!

title: something beautiful
text: when I got to the hotel I noticed that it is very clean and nice, I got a room with a private bathroom also was clean and nice, the service was attentive and helpful, a good point is the location close to the city center is not far away and the area quiet and pleasant to rest, I would recommend because of the price.

title: Decent cheap accomodation
text: It all depends what you are looking for in your stay. I went with 3 mates and had a room each. We went for a lads weekend away and wanted somewhere to grab breakfast and just rest our heads after a bit of drinking. Comfy beds (although they were travel ones) and quiet enough to get some kip when needed. Breakfast was ok and hotel was close enough to tube stations. Great Greek restaurant down the road near the town hall (just cannot think of the name of it). Hotel was great value for what we used it for - only downsides were the shared toilets (Shared with rest of corridor - but clean enough) and the shared kitchen (The fridge has food that had been left and stunk the room out). Great to stay if your going to be out all day and all night !!!!

title: Convenient cheap accommodation
text: If you need a night's accommodation at bargain rate in London then this is a good choice. Admittedly it is student accommodation and a little spartan with a shared bathroom but was very comfortable and very good breakfast included 6 items off the menu and unlimited toast, tea and orange juice. Bus stops are right inside to get down to theatreland and West End easily.

title: Relatively cheap, but boy...
text: This place has a great (safe) location in London and is, relative to other places, pretty affordable. However, only visit this place if you're desperate to revisit your student hall experiences, because that's what you will get. Noisy corridors, dirty toilets, showers that cannot be locked and with doors that can be peeped over, unclear stains in the carpet, no tv, very small and stuffy rooms, creaky bed, extremely bad breakfast (limited to six items, and boy, do they check!) and so much more. So call it a 'lifestyle-experience' and you might enjoy it. Otherwise, pay a bit more and get a normal place to stay in.

title: Basic, clean, cheap, central - and a good breakfast make this a London bargain.
text: As many guests have said before, this is no frills accommodation! However it is clean, very well situated, and has the friendliest staff I've ever encountered in London. It's about a 10 minute walk to the nearest tubes (either Angel or Farringdon) and there is a bus stop directly outside.Don't stay if you're looking for hotel standard rooms and bathrooms, because you'll be disappointed. But if you are happy with clean, basic accommodation in a great location, and enjoy a good breakfast, then this should suit you fine.

title: Spartan but good for people looking for value & central location
text: The rooms are very spartan so if you plan on spending much time in your room whilst visiting London, this might not be the place for you. But if you're looking for a well-priced place in an excellent location. I have to say that I was a student at LSE several years ago so I enjoyed it with a sense of nostalgia.

title: basic, good value for money
text: stayed here whilst waiting for a eurostar connection. 5 mins taxi from Kings cross. Check in was easy, even at 0130 hrs! Room was very basic, but very clean and in good condition. Fresh linen and a comfy single bed was all we needed and we got that. There was a wardrobe and a set of drawers and a desk. Shared bathroom was spotless and modern, I was very surprised. Didn't stay for breakfast so cant comment. Was very quiet, didnt hear a thing (and Im a really light sleeper!) somehow managed to get lost in the lower floor of the building while trying to get out (some signs to reception would be handy!) If you're on a budget this is well recommended (as long as you are not expecting amazing things!)...better than a hostel? More privacy for sure...

title: great budget accomodation
text: I very much like staying there. The location is perfect, close to the East End as well as Holborn. The breakfast is first class, the rooms clean and usually quiet. Bathrooms are shared, but I have not had a cue yet.

title: Great value, very clean, safe and centrally located
text: Stayed here on six separate one night occasions over the summer of 2012

title: Basic but good value.
text: If you're after somewhere to stay for the night and a breakfast in the morning this is for you. Nothing fancy but if you want that you'll pay double! Decent location within walking distance of Angel tube or there's buses from right outside. It's only a 15 - 20 min walk from the City & St Pauls.

title: Good value for money
text: We stayed at Rosebery Hall in early September 2012. We didn't know what to expect and were pleasantly surprised! We rented a twin share with ensuite. The room was big, the bathroom sufficient, and everything was clean. The breakfast provided daily was good. You get a choice of 6 items, and if you take a yogurt and fruit, as two of your six items you have a snack for later in the day. This is not 5 star accommodation, but it is completely adequate, comfortable, and close to all amenities. I would recommend saying here if you are looking for a clean place to lay down your head at the end of a day of touring the city.

title: Cheap, clean and convenient
text: This is very modestly priced, basic accommodation. If you're simply looking for a bed and breakfast for a flying visit and/or don't have the £150+ for a room at a big-name hotel, this will do the job. The rooms are very basic, some en-suite but most with shared facilities. The single room I was in was of a good size, with a desk, hanging space and a sink for teeth-brushing. The bathroom on my stay was shared with 11 other rooms. The accommodation is organised into all same-sex wings - which isn't clear when you book but I found reassuring. The showers were modern, clean and efficient but the toilets didn't flush properly with predictable results... The room was quite noisy, but rooms on higher levels would probably be quieter. Wireless doesn't work. Don't expect any frills - there's no TV, hairdryer, toiletries etc. However, the towels and bedding were very clean and the room generally clean and tidy - no major maintenance issues. I checked in at almost midnight, this being the result of a project implementation over-running and requiring me to stay over. This was one of the few places still to have rooms. The night receptionist was friendly and helpful. Breakfast is served refectory-style. It was the highlight of the stay - varied, plentiful and good quality. I probably wouldn't stay there again unless I was really strapped for choice, but can see that this option offers travellers on a restricted budget good value for money for the location. I paid £39 for bed and breakfast via Laterooms. I've paid £160 and more for a much worse experience at supposedly upmarket London hotels so this place is worth a shot. One final comment: LSE has sister accommodation in other London locations. I subsequently stayed at the LSE Bankside residence (another unplanned overnighter) and can strongly advise against it (see previous review). LSE Rosebery is much cleaner.

title: very good value basic accommodation
text: We stayed in a twin room with ensuite on the 6th floor. The rooms in LSE halls are basic, but then you expect that since it is student accommodation after all, but they are fine for our needs. The staff are very helpful and, when the heating did not work, they came up with extra duvets. Our room could have done with some touching-up and re-painting as it looked a bit tired after a year of use by students. The hall is just a few minutes from the Angel tube station and there are many bars, pubs, cafes and restaurants nearby in Islington or on Exmouth Market. The breakfast is not haute cuisine but OK and plentiful (we skipped lunch most days)! Overall excellent value for money.

title: Good value for money accomodation
text: I stayed for two nights. The room was rather small but clean and tidy. The bed was comfortable and I had a good nights rest. With a window to the court yard it was also very quiet as soon as the bar closed - and also ok before. The bathroom was rather far from my room, but also very clean. I would have wished for a dry place to store your clothes while taking the shower. But alltogether I was quite happy with my stay - especially for this price.

title: Go for a stable!
text: The people at reception were reasonably helpful and friendly however that platform of acceptance was soon to disappear. The smell of the corridors was foul and on entering the room, it was clear that no care had been given to it. There were stains on the walls and carpets, no nearby drinking-water facilities, uncomfortable beds and damaged furniture. Stay clear unless desperate.

title: Great value for money for a short stay
text: Rosebery Hall is perfect for a short stay. We stayed for 2 nights with a baby and a toddler and found the rooms and the kitchen to be very clean and comfortable. We were out all day and inly used the halls for sleeping. The breakfast was excellent. However the bathrooms were dirty and unpleasant to use (too many people to one bathroom). One disadvantage for a young family is that students come in late at night and make noise. Perhaps we were unlucky as we were there at the same time as a large group of young people who partied every night until the early hours. On the good side, the staff were friendly and helpful. The location is excellent (including good public transport links). The price is very good for the area. I would definitely stay there again.

title: Fond memories
text: This place is wonderful for the money. If you have places to visit and there are plenty in London and not bothered about fancy hotels then this the place for you. All the staff are a delight and always ready to help with a smile. The accommodation is basic but everything is clean and tidy. It reminded me of my time as a student in the 60s. Lovely for the not too fussy! Great location and the walk to ANGEL tube station is just close enough to work off some of the wonderful breakfast. I cannot speak too highly of this place.

title: Easter 2012 in London
text: Good, clean, inexpensive, centrally located accommodation. Very very good!!!!

title: Superb value for money
text: Do you know what? This was incredible value for money. For sure, it was basic - and felt a little like stepping back ten years in a timewarp since I lived in a hall of residence - but as a bed for the night it did the trick. Pleasant and supportive reception staff gave a good first impression. I was in the older wing on the eighth floor

title: Value for money
text: Good, clean, inexpensive, centrally located accommodation. Baked beans were good! Pleasing to discover free wifi in the dining hall (although I didn't notice it until the last morning).

title: a home from home in North London !
text: Charming, friendly place to stay when in London. The accomodation is simple and spotlessly clean.Breakfast is copious from full English to Continental: the choice is yours.Lovely aroma of freshly brewed coffee welcomed residents in the restaurant every morning.All served by friendly staff with a bright smile.Reception staff always happy to help and advise.There is a kitchen on each floor.Very useful for preparing a meal if wanted. It is easy to reach the hall by bus and buses stop just outside the entrance. There are several shops,coffeee bars & restaurants in the immediate area ranging from Italian to Chinese and Indian.All up to your taste but rather expensive.There is a supermarket close by where I bought some food and cooked in the kitchen in the hall.

title: GREAT value for money, but ...
text: Cheap stay in London, near Sadlers Wells. A university hall of residence, functioning as a hostel. Basic rooms. (Mine, at least, wasn't en suite) A rather jaded feeling to everything. The rooms and facilities are tired. The computer for guests' use is frustratingly old-fashioned. Reception is good - efficient Room service is minimal, and the rooms themselves ar .,0e a little depressing.

title: Good locatoin, clean, great value, very nice breakfast
text: It is a quite simple accomodation, but great value for the price, rooms are clean and comfortable. Amazing for the price we paid and very near central london. The breakfast is a typical English one, very rich and with many options.

title: The cheapest residences of the LSE
text: Alright, Im a student of Summer School and I chose to live here as it is the cheapest amongst all LSE halls. It is an average, 2 star kind of accommodation. You'd definately get the best sleep here, the rooms are cleaned everyday. The rooms are small, but that's how student accommodations are. It is good residence and I can spend my time living here. Amenities are okay. The location is okay. It is 20 minute walk from LSE, but trust me you will enjoy the walk every day and there are numerous students who chose to walk every morning. It is fun. It is also location near Angel station and is in Islington, which has maximum concentration of Bars in London.

title: Great value for money
text: Student accommodation. Basic, cheap, clean & really good value for money. It's basically halls of residence but was very quiet and in an excellent location. Five minute walk from Angel underground, but stop right outside. Breakfast is excellent!

title: I shall be back - very soon
text: This is a great price, and obviously a certain basic nature has to be expected, but everything is clean and there's enough space. I spent five nights here, and shall return in a few months with my partner: it's difficult to imagine such quality at a price like this anywhere else. As a vegetarian I'm very picky about food, but a full breakfast is guaranteed with no problems. Vegetarian sausages, potato waffles or hash browns, scrambled eggs, baked beans, pain au chocolat, then some bread with cheese, washed down with orange juice and coffee or whatever? Fine for me. This is a very short walk from the Angel/Islington, and I only used the bus service as I wanted to see where I was going: everywhere is a dob of a wallet (containing your Oyster card (£18.80 for a week's travel plus £5 for the forever reusable Oyster)) away. As a literary nut, I spent almost a whole day in Kensal Green Cemetery, went to Horace Walpole's Strawberry Hill House near Twickenham (£8), Abney Park Cemetery in Stoke Newington, Iain Sinclair's Haggerston and the borough of Hackney in general, Old Ford's Victoria Park etc, Spitalfields and Whitechapel, parts of the City, and on and on. McDonalds (Chapel Market) is great for free wifi, although it's probably also as good at Wetherspoon's The Angel, where I only sampled the beer. Negatives: First things first: the men's bathroom is really hidden away! I could have done without the huge bunch of (exclusively male) schoolkids on the last two nights, as they made a hell of a noise way after 2300 hours. It took me a time to work out how many plastic bags I needed to have a good shower and come out dry. NB If the above are really negatives, then I can live with them.

title: Budget Stay......good breakfast
text: The rooms were clean, and beds were nice. Best was the Breakfast. Staff were nice and friendly, and they even allowed us to keep our luggage for extra time, without extra cost. Budget accommodation, so don't expect much.

title: Shaabby and uncared for.
text: My wife and I stayed in the LSE’s Rosebury Avenue property for one night 13/04/12. We knew that for £59.95 it would be pretty basic so we were’nt expected anything special. The building was nice from the outside and well located for the Angel Islington. Staff on reception were friendly and professional. Then we opened the door to room 515. We were immediately greeted by a damp musty smell. Inside the tiny room there were two very small single beds. A shabby little wardrobe, the door handle came off in my hand when I tried to open it

title: Good value central but hostel type accommodation
text: Staying in a student hall brought back many memories - it felt quite lonely to be one amongst groups of school children, foreigh tourists and resident students. It is very basic accommodation and feels like staying in a hostel with an odour of testosterone. However, my room was clean, there was a very good choice of breakfast items in the refrectory dinning hall, the security staff were very friendly and above all other factors it was extremley good value for London accommodation and in a very central location - 5 minutes bus journey from Kings Cross, 25mins from London Bridge and 30 from Waterloo. On my first night my key turned constantly and didn't work but when I told the secuity staff he moved me to another room. The biggest negative is sharing communal toilets and showers but if available some rooms are ensuite and the whole block is being renovated. If you want a bargain stay here but if you want any sort of luxury stay in a hotel.

title: Excellent budget stay
text: At £36 per head for a twin, en-suite room with full English breakfast how can you go wrong? Well, we didn't. It is student accommodation, so you shouldn't expect luxury: but the room was clean and perfectly adequate for our needs. The staff were very helpful,the area was safe and secure and the Clerkenwell area seemed to be a pleasant one, even at midnight on Saturday. The breakfast was more than adequate, and the serving staff much more helpful than top price hotels we have used in the city centre.

title: good value for money
text: stayed her for a few nights in march 2012. THe accomodation is basic, but fine. I had a twin room alone. For me it was fine, it would have been a little crowed if you stay her with 2 people. Bathroom and toilets are in the hallway. These were kept clean. Breakfast was really good. Toast, coffee and such were unlimited. There was yoghurt, (good) croissants, fruit, egs and such, you could choose six of the unlimited items. Friendly staff, restaurants, tube station and cafe's nearby.

title: Don't be fooled by the name, but worth a try if only once
text: Ok, Rosebery Hall sounds nice, and belonging to LSE which is quite a prestigious establishment would set you up to expect at least medium - high standards in terms of the condition of the place.... We stayed for 2 nights (me and wife) and our twin room was on the 7th floor, the halls reminded me of my own Uni halls from a few years ago.... tatty, unpleasant smelling corridors, painted 'exposed' brickwork, a bit prison like! The room itself was fine, bed linen smelled fresh, and towels and soap were provided although the walk to the gents bathroom was right at the end of the corridor, a little further than I'd hoped. However the showers were fine, and hot. Where the place let me down was when it came to sleep quality. Being on the 7th floor there was still a lot of traffic noise from the window (which was shut!), the room was generally hot, and there was constant noise throughout the night of doors banging which meant I had the most disruptive couple of nights sleep I've had in a long time. Breakfast was included and service was good although seemed a little authoritative in that guests can have upto 6 items from the breakfast list, no more than 2 of each and no return visits! Now I don't like wasting food and had to make a judgement as to how hungry I was before going back for that extra croissant/yoghurt/banana for fear of being 'spoken to' ! What the place lacks in sleep quality, it makes up for in location, about 5 minutes walk from Angel tube station, and about 20 minutes walk from Kings Cross St Pancras, but although the money is going to a good cause (subsidising students accommodation fees) I don't think I'd return in the near future unless I was by myself.

title: Good Value Budget Accomodation
text: We stayed during the Uni Easter holidays so on our corridor there were a few students left which was was a little noisy on Saturday night. Our room was a twin, which had two firm but comfortable beds, two desks, and a small shower/toilet room and overall was clean and tidy. At the end of the corridor there was a toilet with bath and a separate kitchen area (bring your own crokery/cutlery/pans as these are not provided). Also bring a hairdryer if you need one. We had breakfast included in our rate which allowed 6 items from cooked/continental breakfasts plus tea, coffee, juice and toast and this represented excellent value for money. There are very good transport links including bus and tube connections closeby. The people on reception were very friendly too.

title: Good value for money
text: Rosebery Hall is a great place to stay in London if you're on a budget. It is located in a good area with easy links to the West-End and only a five-minute walk to the Angel tube station. This is a student accommodation, so rooms are basic but clean. The staff were extremely helpful and welcoming. The only problem is the Wi-Fi in the dining hall, which is very, very slow and does not work most of the times.

title: Cool location, great value and a very substantial breakfast included
text: A really good location that is very close to central London and served by an excellent bus service. The facilities although basic were clean and the breakfast included in the price was extremely good value. The only snag we encountered was that we arrived very early in the morning and we were given a room already occupied which was rather embarrassing plus there were no towels available so we had to share. Other than that, we would definitely recommend the LSE as exceptionally good value accommodation.

title: Good value
text: Accomodation though basic was clean and tidy. All the staff were helpful, Kitchen staff were lovely one even remembered I was going to be a Grandma :)) Excellent value for City Centre location. Well located to get around, plenty of activity and things going on. Only complaint were curtains were hard to pull to keep night light out, blinds helped though

title: Great Value, but it IS a student hall of Residence. Good parking !
text: I've stayed at this hall of residence a couple of times, and it is pretty good value for money. Rooms are basic but clean, but the standard of the rooms and bathrooms does vary a lot between different buildings and floors. I've been frustrated trying to book a single room, on both occasions I've had to book a twin room just for myself, even at short notice they will not let you have a twin room at single price. The best thing about this location is the parking. The street to the side of the hall has free parking from the evening until 8 in the morning, and it always seems easy to find a space. This for me is a huge bonus. It's also possible to reach the Hall without going into the congestion Zone, by travelling down the City road - which is right on the edge of the zone. For those that have to bring their car into town, thus is an ideal place to stay

title: Okay for the price
text: Nice location near Angel station. Room functionally furnished, comfortable beds. Both shared facilities (toilet and shower) were very clean, and shared only with 3 (?) other guests. The shower drain was clogged, but it was not really a problem. No free internet.

title: Unbelievable value for money stay in London
text: As a former student of the LSE I had thought that the accomodation would have improved since my student days in the 80s. Evidently not! However, though the accomodation is very functional (no ensuite, basic bed, desk and chair) it does represent great value for money. We paid approximately £70 for a double and a single with a full breakfast. We have also stayed at Passfield Hall which has a better feel to it (less utilitarian) and more central location and I would recommend this hall as well. Staff are very friendly and helpful.

title: Great service, value for money, especially for London area!
text: Don't be put off by the area, yes a residential area but on street metered parking available nearby, and you don't have to go far for a pizza and/or a drink. Friendly staff and prompt service. The price was good and although we had booked a twin, we were given a triple which was a double and a single bed. I think the only real disturbance was from the fridge.
