title: Small but perfectly formed
text: We were going to the Ealing comedy festival so this was perfectly situated for us. We were upgraded to a garden room, I was pleased to find windows that actually open so we could get fresh air although there was air con for quick cooling. We had no problems with noise or light. Kettle and nespresso machine available along with water. Shower good and little molton brown toiletries left each day. Breakfast was fine, natural yogurt and fruit available, as well as cheese and ham and mini croissants. There's a garden outside too which is lovely for London. Staff very helpful, even charging my phone when I'd forgotten my charger. For the price this was a great hotel and we'd stay even if we were wanting to go more centrally in London, about half an hour away on Piccadilly line.

title: Nice hotel, nice location
text: I stayed here last December with my partner. Lovely hotel and room and amenities. But the room made me feel rather enclosed! It was a lovely but a small room. The bed was very comfy and and the deco was nice! I loved the shampoo etc in the bathroom! Also had a sewing kit, very convenient! A minute walk away from the station, and staff were friendly! Only thing I would say is the price was slightly a bit too much for what you get, but over all, nice hotel!

title: Lovely hotel, perfect location
text: Just returned home from a two night stay at Hotel 55. I booked the hotel before reading the reviews, which put me off a little, but so glad that I didn't cancel. The hotel is by traffic lights on a busy road so anyone not used to traffic noise may find difficulty sleeping but it was not a problem for us (we were in a front room too). Rooms are lovely, very trendy. Hairdryer, tea/coffee facilities, water included. It was lovely to be able to open windows wide and get some air overnight, waking up feeling refreshed. Beds are lovely and comfy and shower was great. No lift but staff helped us up the stairs with buggy/baby stuff so not really a problem. Lovely room to eat continental breakfast which overlooked a great garden, plus a bar but we didn't get time to have a drink in it! There's limited parking but wouldn't have wanted to park outside anyway as the hotel is at traffic lights and no one would let the taxi out when we went out one evening! We parked in an NCP which is 2 min walk around the corner (safe and only cost £5.50 for 3 days) and the station is next to the car park, so a very convenient location, we were in central london within 20 mins and family ticket cost approx £12. We will definitely return to this hotel as planning to see a show soon....without baby!

title: Lovely Small Hotel
text: Came to London for the weekend, lovely small hotel, Staff are fantastic. From the outside just looks like a normal house, but once you get in its very nicely decorated nice area to eat. Well located, Liked the little details that went into our room, The coffee machine was a great idea and the nice magazines in the draws to read. Will defo reccomend and use again! Oh and breakfast is continental but very nice with lots of choices!

title: Perfect Stay
text: My partner and I stayed here recently and we had a great stay. Our room was clean and lovely right at the back of the hotel so it was lovely and quiet which is great as I'm such a light sleeper. The breakfast was continental which involved pastries, fruit, toast and cereal but for an extra price you can have cooked breakfast, both were really good and filling. The staff were friendly and willing to help. The car park was full (only offers 5 spaces) when we arrived on the Friday evening we arrived but the receptionist said there was free parking on the road at weekend just arrived the cornor so we parked there and on Saturday morning when a space became available we moved the car. The tube station is a 2 minute walk around the corner which is perfect. You get complementary tea, coffee and bottled water in your room, as well as a mini fridge with food and drink which is an additional price. We really enjoyed our stay and will be looking to stay here again when we come to London in February. Definitely worth staying at if you want to get away from the busy London centre.

title: Great spot to stay
text: Stayed here for two nights in mid-May. Directly behind North Ealing underground station (once you walk up the steps and out, continue along the street...you'll see a white building through the trees on the right infront of you). Loved that it was near underground. Loved that it was outside core of busy London. The staff behind the desk were all very friendly, polite & helpful. Carried our bags (and wouldn't even accept a tip!), and arranged our early taxi ride. Hotel is clean and has cute, modern decor. Breakfast was lovely...continental includes fresh fruit cups, cups of granola and yogurt, croissants and pastries, toast, cereal, other apples/bananas. Other reviews have complained about the lack of breakfast, but perhaps they woke up late. It was lovely - freshly brewed coffee too. Would recommend this to anyone! Super affordable compared to any other place we looked at in London.

title: Perfect romantic getaway in London
text: We had a lovely 3-night romantic getaway and we couldn't be happier that we chose to stay here. First, we were worried because it's not centrally located but the area is just charming and quiet. The hotel is actually close to the city center and to the airport as well. It was really nice to arrive back to the quiet hotel after a long day walking around in museums and shopping. The staff is lovely, the rooms are comfy and beautiful and we also had a couple of nice cocktails before dinner. We will return for sure!

title: Nice little find
text: A little gem of a hotel tucked away in the corner of North Ealing, just a hundred yards from the tube station. My girlfriend and I stayed at the hotel during our trip to see The Woman In Black on stage. The room was a bit small but very tidy and modern, with a view of the Japanese style garden, for which we paid extra. The bathroom was excellent, and perks included a safe, a Nespresso machine and some high end complimentary toiletries. Customer service was top notch, the staff were friendly and helpful. The Japanese restaurant downstairs seemed nice, but we never ate there, although we did drink at the bar. The place seems like more of a business hotel but served well for a short couple trip away. Parking is very limited so go there by train or find a backup car park, but I recommend this hotel to anyone.

title: Nice hotel in the 'burbs
text: My husband and I stayed at Hotel 55 for 4 nights in May during a warm spell in London. When we entered our Garden facing room it was super hot, but cooled down quickly with the air con. The room was clean and modern and had tea and coffee making facilities which was nice after a long day of traveling. The bathroom was tiny but the shower was nice sized and everything is new/updated. Hand soap, shower gel, shower cap and shampoo were provided. The bed was decent (I have definitely slept in worse) and the continental breakfast was yummy. The staff was super nice and always willing to help out when needed. The hotel is about a 2 minute walk to the nearest tube station and there is a bus station literally right outside the front door which will take you to Ealing Broadway for lots of restaurant/pub choices and shopping. Cons: -Loud, especially with the windows open. -30 minute tube ride to downtown

title: Great location
text: We had a 2 day stopover during Rugby World Cup and so finding accommodation was a bit of a challenge however this boutique style hotel served us very well. The hotel is basically a large repurposed house with a good Japanese Restauarnt at night which flips to the breakfast room in the morning. The place is very easy to find and is literally a 3 minute walk from North Ealing station making easy connections to Heathrow and Central London. The neighbourhood is filled with pubs and restaurants and theres a couple of small grocery stores close by for supplies. Our room was tiny by north american standards but everything was well appointed and clean. Great for a stopover where you just need a comfortable place to sleep

title: Lovely stay
text: Had a very nice stay during my visit to London. Staff were nice and the rooms is comfortable. Cannot complain, loved the huge shower. Car parking is limited, however there is a large car park only two minutes walk away. Really important to me to have reliable wifi connection and Hotel 55 did not let me down. I would recommend 203, it was a lovely spacious room with a back facing window so I had a good sleep.

title: Handy hotel for the tube into the city.
text: We enjoyed our one night stay at this hotel. it is clean and comfortable and a reasonable price for London. Our room was a little dark and could have done with a bit more light but not really a problem for one night though. We didn't stay for breakfast but the restaurant looked really nice and modern. The gentleman who checked us in was very friendly and Tiberias who checked us out was lovely too. It is within easy walking distance of the tube station for our trip into London to see 'War of the Worlds' at the Dominion Theatre. We arrived quite early and our room was ready for us , it was fortunate that we did as there are only 4 parking spaces in front of the hotel and we got one.

title: Better offer for short stay
text: 2 times I have stayed this hotel, at least reasonable offer compare to London center. Rooms are clean, but sometimes beams of the roof disturb your comfort and bit narrow for long stay. Water pressure of shower is strong enough, however difficult to adjust heat. Bed mat is too soft for me. They have Japanese restaurant in same location, and offering Japanese breakfast also. All in all, nothing is dissatisfaction but also not enough reason for becoming repeater.

title: Well Located
text: Came here for an overnighter, was well received and efficiently given my card to my room, there is only 4 maybe 5 car parking places at the front of the hotel, I believe there is some around the back end of the hotel but not sure. Room was cosy Air Con was switched off, I switched on to get some air and even tho it was on 18 it was blowing really warm, so I switched off and opened a window. Obviously that let in traffic noise as it’s right on the main road. The tube is literally 2 mins away. If you need somewhere to park on a weekend the stations car park is only 2 quid all day Saturday and I think Sunday. It’s just past the hotel and turn right, then it’s slightly to the right I think. Hotel was good a bit pricey for what it was but it’s location mainly, I didn’t eat there so can’t tell you about momo the Japanese restaurant. The tea, coffee and water where free in the room so extra bonus for serving fruit tea too. All in all I would go again especially if you want to visit London.

title: Disappointing & noisy stay
text: The photos of this hotel online looked beautiful but our room (111) was very much a standard boxy hotel room with little space and very dark. The so described 'garden view' was also infact a view of a building site as I presume the hotel were currently building an extension. As a result we were woken up at 7am by the non-stop building work and drilling, and pretty abruptly left the hotel afterwards. Potential for a nice stay if you got the right room but the hotel should warn guests of building work (and lack of supposed garden view) on the website. Will not be staying again.

title: London's Best Kept Secret
text: We stayed at Hotel 55 for our honeymoon in London. Yes, it was a tube ride of about 25 minutes to the city center, but the tube station was only 2 minutes from the hotel (we really didnt feel the time). It was beautiful, especially breakfast in the conservatory. The staff was friendly and helpful. I considered this a very trendy hotel, in a peaceful neighbourhood. The bath products were Molton Brown, which were very chic and upscale. The bedding was soft and welcoming . Our bedroom was on the second floor and overlooked the garden, it was small but perfect. I am going to stay there again on my next trip to visit the Queen.

title: Tiny boxy room with thin walls but...
text: I find myself a little ambivalent while writing this review. The room was too small and too dark (not enough lights) for my comfort and we could hear our neighbour's television but the compact room is also laced with a nespresso machine and loccitane toiletries which I totally approve. What I do like about the hotel, is Momo Japanese restaurant. It is set in a little garden oasis. Have lunch there and you will forget you are lodged in a boxy room that is hopefully not facing the A406. Another plus for this boutique hotel is that it is only a stone's throw to North Ealing tube station.

title: Quirky but fun
text: First the traffic in this part of London is horrible. The hotel has very limited car parking space so the best bet is the NCP near the nearby tube station. The room was more than adequate ours was on the 2nd floor so if you are carrying heavy luggage and have a room on the top floor it could be a struggle. There is a full bar and a good dining area plus a rather attractive and unexpected garden. The staff were very helpful The wi fi crashed which was a problem since I had some papers to work on. They were deeply apologetic and allowed me to use the PC on the receptionist desk and gave my wife a drink on the house. What could have been a major inconvenience they dealt with well with no fuss. The tube station is literally a few minutes walk There was a continental breakfast which was good. A hot breakfast cost an additional £5. Coffee was very good. My wife said if we had occasion to visit London again she would stay again a rare compliment.

title: Just what I needed
text: Staying here for our 2nd visit to London for an NFL game this year and it was nice and easy. Flying in to Heathrow it was only 2 tube journeys away with a changeover which was nice and quick. Same for getting to and from Wembley. Tube station, as stated in other reviews is only 2 minutes walk away. We arrived about half 11 and even though check in was meant to be at 2pm we were in our room by 12. Good sleep even with a street facing room.

title: What a hotel should be
text: Staff always helpful. Room always very nice. Lovely little guest samples in room e.g wash gel, sewing kit, shower cap. Breakfast a bit basic but nice. Very comfy

title: Great Location
text: Stayed here for the weekend of the challenge cup game at Wembley. Bus goes from outside the hotel straight to the stadium so really handy but also easy to walk - about 35 mins & we did this coming back. Hotel room was small but clean, comfy bed & well equipped with water & nice coffee machine. We were in Room 7 ground floor & it was a bit noisy during the night with other hotel guests coming & going & sound of TV in the room next door but to be expected in a small hotel. We parked on Ealing station car park behind the hotel Saturday morning until Sunday lunch £3.90 so great for London & found a lovely little Italian right behind the hotel where we ate on the Saturday evening. All in all a nice stay. The hotel itself has a small front - room for 4/5 cars only. Pictures on website is a bit deceiving & was full all the time we were there! Plenty parking behind the hotel.

title: Excellent location and helpful staff but...
text: Our stay at the Hotel 55 proved to be very good in the whole with a couple of caveats. Plus points first. The staff were very helpful and responded positively to us and our requests. The bed was comfy and there was tea and a kettle, and a pod style coffee machine. The location was ideal with a tube station with 4 minutes and Ealing Broadway about 20 minutes walk. Locally there's an Italian and a couple of small supermarkets but we went for supper and sport (rugby semi final followed by the Arsenal match) at the Wheatcheaf about 10 minute walk away and breakfasted at the local Wetherspoons so we can't comment on the food in the Hotel, apart from the fact the full breakfast cost £11 each. The rooms have a safe and chiller, but we couldn't see a price list for the mini bar. Minus points, we initially were put into room 103, which apparently we'd asked for, but as it was at the front we asked to move the next day. This was for a number of reasons, firstly it overlooked Hangar Lane and the traffic noise was too much. Secondly it was very dark. The lighting was so dim in the bathroom when we came to go out we struggled to use the mirror for the basics i.e. shaving/putting on make up. Thirdly the shower in within a bath tub, but the side of the tub was so high, we struggled to get in and out safely. BTW room 104 that we moved into was much better with lighting and not bath tub, but 105 does have the same shower/bath arrangement. We also found that the hot water ran out in both rooms if one has a long shower, which I do tend to do. We did mention these issues to the staff and they are already working on improving the lighting in the rooms and, had we mentioned the water, a back up hot after system is available.

title: Room = Convereted Attic Small Cramped clean room, super craamped Bathroom
text: Beware , the Rooms are small, Very small. Staff is polite, but they cant help change the room. The marketing was misleading, may lead you to think otherwise. This property is a old house which has been badly modernised.??Issue is that the description could be better. ?? I booked a family room as we had our 11 year old child , we were told family room is available. And that there is free parking.??When I reached there I realised the house ( sorry hotel ) oh !! Sorry the house .. had 4 parking bays for 28 guests..so I went hunting road side parking .??The family room was a small converted ATIC and the SO CALLED GARDEN view was a view of a half grass patch !! And yes while you can shuffle from point A to Point B in the room, in the bathroom you would be lucky to move you hand to brush your teeth.??The only saving grace, it was clean. ??And yes the continental cold breakfast was NOT arranged properly for humans and the flies that were tasting the food made me get up hungry.??So try at your risk.??One good thing worth mentioning though is that the staff was polite and smiling. The breakfast was not impressive.

title: Reasonable for a short stay
text: I've just returned from a 2 night stay at Hotel 55. I travelled alone to attend a course / conference near the hotel. I stayed in a "cosy room", the smallest room type. It cost £70/night B&B, booked direct with the hotel. My room was ready when I arrived, located on the ground floor. It was very small - probably about 3 square metres, and almost all the floorspace was taken up by the very comfortable double bed. It is, after all, a "cosy" room. They make reasonable use of what room there is

title: Affordable Prices and Access to Metro
text: Hotel 55 is a really warm and friendly hotel in London. We stayed there for three nights and we loved the spacious room, the Nespresso coffee maker and the modern design of the hotel. Plus, there is the Japanese restaurant downstairs, which is really awesome. Sushi is fantastic and the prices are pretty decent, considering London!

title: Short Break
text: This time last year our son moved to London for his year out. I booked to stay in Hotel 55 as it was near to where he moved. I was so impressed that my husband and I went back this year when visiting our son. The hotel is small which gives it a family friendliness which is lacking in bigger chains. It is spotlessly clean and the rooms have everything for a short stay. The restaurant is Japanese and very good quality. The staff are all very friendly and accommodating. It is close to a couple of different tube stations and within walking distance of Ealing town centre. I highly recommend Hotel 55.

title: Number 1 London Hotel :)
text: What a great hotel to stay if you want to visit London!! My sister and brother-in-law came to spend a few days, with my partner and I, from Spain. We decided to spent a couple of days in London and the fact of booking a couple of hotel rooms was very hard for me due to previous bad experiencies in London Hotels. But we all agreed that Hotel 55 ticked all the boxes and every box!!! Cleanliness is my priority and this hotel is spot on, honestly. From bedroom, bathroom, public areas and breakfast service...We were really impressed. The location of the hotel is great. Just 20 mins. to the centre by tube. One piece of advise, please get an Oyster Card because you can save some money in travelling. And finally, I would like to make a special mention: Tiberius at reception desk, he is a great person, extremly helpful, polite, kind and he can speak perfect Spanish!!! (which was very helpful for my sister). Thanks Tiberius for your attention to detail, you make our stay very comfortable.

title: Small but sweet
text: My partner and I stayed here for one night whilst going to see a show at Wembley. We could have stayed closer but for double the price! The hotel was easy to find and there were a couple of parking spaces in the forecourt, however we chose to park down a residential road round the corner (free all day at weekends). We paid extra for a garden view room, thinking it would be quieter as the hotel is on quite a busy road. It was peaceful, however we could only see the conservatory roof from our window! The room was quite small but was perfect for 1 or 2 nights. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was lovely. The shower was so hot and powerful too!! We didn't eat breakfast or at the hotel within the hotel so can't comment on that. Check in and out was easy, and the one staff member we saw on the front desk was friendly enough. It is about 3-4 miles away from Wembley Stadium and it cost us £11-£15 in an Uber taxi to get there/back. I would recommend this hotel for a short break.

title: Overnight stay
text: We stayed in Room 007, towards the back of the property. Comfortable with some nice quality touches. Great shower, coffee machine in room and comfortable bed. Staff were excellent and extremely helpful. We would definitely stay here again.

title: Great value for the money
text: This hotel was completely renovated 9 month ago so everything seems brand new. I'll try not to duplicate the posts before me because they were all accurate. Free internet access was important as I needed to book show tickets and such. Some hotels charge up to 14 quid per 24 hour period for this. There is a laundry with bundle service, two small grocery stores and a great pub(Greystoke?) less than a block away. The phones are VOIP and it only cost .15 per minute to call back to the US. That was cheaper than my mobile phone. Some rooms are larger than others so if room size is important then check the floor plan. We chose a garden facing room (less noise) but they are smaller.

title: Second time stayed, great hotel 55
text: Wow! This is my second time stayed in hotel 55. I like this hotel so much during my first time visit London in 2010. Thus, my friend and I decided to stay in hotel 55 again during our second time visit in London 2014. Location, although is bit far away from London downtown, but i personally feel that hanger lane is a peaceful side and is totally difference from the bustling city center. You need to get down from North Ealing underground station and walking distance within 7 minutes. Easy to find with a map. The room (street facing)for this visit, has being arrange in a corner side. Thus, there will be a bit smaller compare to the year 2010 room. But still good with conformable bed and pillow. Also, nice shower as well. However, the mineral water has changed to a normal brand/ packing :( I still remember, they provided the Hotel 55 sparking with a nice bottle in year of 2010. I found that the breakfast has became limited selection .. just some croissant, bread and corn flakes. But during my first time stayed was better breakfast. Staff, as usual, friendly and helpful. One of the morning shift staff, i cant recall his name but he still can remember us for way back to 2010 :)

title: Hidden Gem!!
text: My daughter and I booked an accessible room for the night of Ed Sheeran's concert at Wembley. The hotel was easy to find and a disabled parking space had been reserved for us. Front desk were wonderful and helpful and the room itself was beautiful as was the ensuite bathroom. If you are travelling to Wembley forget Uber or taxi services - its easy enough to either catch a tube or, like us, catch the 483 bus just outside the hotel! It was the best night's sleep I've had for a while at Hotel 55! The beds are fantastic! If you want to book this hotel, book it direct with Hotel 55 as they include a continental breakfast which was delicious! We will definitely be booking again for our next trip to Wembley!

title: Small, professional business hotel
text: As with other reviewers, do not be fooled by the exterior. The interior has been thoughtfully designed, with an eye for detail. The things that I look out for are as follows - a comfortable bed, air conditioning, powershower, decent wifi, and a quality cup of coffee in my room. Hotel 55 ticked all of these boxes. And Tiberius at reception ticks the box as well. This is not the Ritz, and is certainly no Travel Lodge. All in all, my 5 star rating is for what you get and value for money. Highly recommend

title: Lovely little Hotel - Becky & Mark from Hull
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here recently. We stayed in one of the appartment style rooms. It was clean, spacious, modern and the bed was very compfy. The continental style breakfast was lovely and there was plenty of choice. For those who fancy a full english breakfast in the morning, this was also available for an additional fee. The staff were very friendly and helpful and the hotel is in a great location to get into central London as North Ealing tube station was just a 2 minute walk away. The only negative some could find is that hotel carpark is very small. Luckily we managed to get a space, but all the same there did seem to be plenty of on street parking around the back of the hotel. Many thanks to the Hotel 55 staff team for a great stay. We will definitely be back.

title: A friendly place to stay
text: my husband and I had a wonderful stay in this small and personal hotel. The room (type cozy) was very very small. Barely any room to walk around the bed so we felt lucky for not being tall or big and travelling light. However the room was clean, decorated with a lot of taste and quiet. Also the bathroom was modern with lovely and luxurious products such as the complementary shampoo and soap. Most importantly the service was excellent. We were greeted upon our late arrival (after midnight) by a friendly night porter. The next morning breakfast service was also pleasant and friendly and again in a lovely setting. On our second day we got down to the breakfast room after 10. We thought the night porter had told us breakfast was until 10:30. It wasn't. We figured we would be sent away without breakfast. But no, we were offered coffee, some croissants and some fruit and yogurt. This was such a lovely surprise. We were extremely pleased with the level of service and would definitely stay here again. The hotel is a bit further away from the center of London. Approximately 30 minutes on the tube from covent garden, a popular attraction. It wasn't a big deal for us as the tube station North Ealing is just around the corner. I can highly recommend this small, cozy hotel with its friendly staff. If you are tall, travel with a lot of luggage or just want more space, book a slightly pricier and bigger room. If you are like us and travel light than a cozy type room is ok.

title: Expensive for an hotel with so many cons!
text: We stayed at this hotel for four nights in October. It’s far from the center but with an underground stop just 2 minutes away we are 30 minutes away from the main attractions. The neighbourhood is nice but the road in front of the hotel is quite noisy. Upon arrival we were given a smoking room that smelled terribly and had views to a wall just one meter away from the window. During the night we could hear a very disturbing noise every eight minutes… yes, I timed it because the smell and the noisy didn’t let me sleep! In the morning, I asked to be changed to another room which was more pleasant but extremely tiny - we could hardly pass between the bed and the wall. Also, wireless Internet didn’t work in that room so I had to go to the hallway or to the restaurant to download emails and use the Internet. The design of the hotel is nice, although not spectacular as some of the reviews say, and the staff is very friendly and helpful. We exchanged several emails before the stay and they were all answered quite promptly. Breakfast was fine but tables are very uncomfortable. It seems like we are having a picnic instead of a meal in a restaurant. So, the restaurant is nice if you don’t plan to eat… Nevertheless, the garden and beer garden are beautiful and quiet. I wish we could have enjoyed it more.

title: Small but ticks a lot of boxes
text: Hotel is quite handy to reach by tube from Heathrow, which was a plus. There's not much going on in Ealing (apart from a nice Indian restaurant across the road which another reviewer mentioned) but it's a two minute walk from the tube stop and is on the Picadilly line which made city centre very accessible, though it takes about 30 mins to get there. My first reaction when I saw my room was displeasure - really small. Two of us couldn't pass each other at the foot of the bed. And the 'garden view' I'd paid for was blocked by the roof of the parking lot below. There was a mere glimpse of garden in the distance so this is something they need to look at as it is most certainly false advertising. And it was really expensive for the size and location - exchange rate wasn't good which didn't help those of us who normally use euros. But on closer inspection I was really pleased at the attention to detail. The bed was super comfy with great pillows and good linen and I slept like a log every night. The room had a Nespresso machine and wine glasses, which was a nice touch (no corkscrew though :) ) and every day two bottles of water were left in the room, which is always appreciated. The bathroom was tiny but spotless with l'Occitane products, which were replenished every day which was also impressive. Not much space or shelves to put our stuff but not a massive deal in the overall scheme of things. Breakfast was really really good. Continental was included in our room price but for an extra £4 per person each day you could get a hot breakfast. I thought this was a really good deal and surprised more hotels don't operate on this basis. Food was really nice - fresh fruit, little pots with yoghurt, granola and berries with honey, pastries and excellent coffee, served in individual cafetieres. We ordered hot food every day and it did not disappoint. Really buttery scrambled eggs and yummy mushrooms. - made with love I think. Really high standard. And the breakfast room is gorgeous Really bright and modern. Loved it. Bar is very Japanese-y cool though their wines by the glass were not good. I had a glass of Sicilian red and it was dire. I couldn't drink it. And not cheap either. Would stick to beer next time. And one other small gripe. There is free Wi-Fi but you need a code from reception. But you need to log-in every single time you use your phone or iPad. Very annoying. But overall I really liked it but travelling in and out by train every day was a little tiring. Next time I'd probably pay more and stay somewhere more central.

title: Cozy and clean room!
text: The hotel is in a quiet place 20min outside of London and the tube is 2minutes away! Has a great interior and our room was small but cozy and clean ! Clean towels every day and bottles of water (really happy for the water!! ) Yammy Breakfast !! Helpful reception Nice pub 2 minutes on foot and you can find mini markets , pharmacy and restaurants near by ! I really recommend it if you are not a fun of big city noise ! I am definitely going back there on my next trip !

title: Homey.
text: Got lost looking for this hotel due to the chaotic roads in London and my sat nav being tempermental and not finding it......but a quick call to the hotel reception and they were able to quickly guide me to the right location. spent 2 nights here and was given a room with a garden view, although small it was perfect for the job of just a place to rest the mind from the hectic london life , a true haven for the tired body and being in the back of the hotel outside noise was minimal except when it rained heavy on the first night where the rain lashed onto the conservatory roof. The coffee machine was a godsend, just what I needed in the morning especially when I skipped on the breakfast as I found it hard to wake from a lovely nights snooze. The hotel is conviently located and only just a couple mins walk from north ealing tube station which took you directly into the heart of London quickly and being not far from chiswick gave me the opportunity to dine out in decent restaurants. gutted didn't get the chance to try out momo, will have to next time.

title: Individual hotel in busy area
text: Very clean, well furnished room with all you could want inside. Didn't try the restaurant so can't comment on that but it does Japanese food. There's free parking outside But only four spaces and no way of reserving one, so I booked parking nearby privately.

title: Stylish boutique hotel. definitely stay again.
text: Drove to watch take that at wembley. such a convenient location. bus stop right outside. 20 mins to wembley stadium. room very nicely decorated. VERY comfy bed. Breakfast was lovely. when they say limited parking there are 4 spaces out front. however right behind hotel is NCP car park by ealing tube station.

title: September stay!
text: Stayed here back in September just never gotten round to writing a review! Lovely place with super friendly staff, booked me and my friend taxis constantly as we had never been to London before and got a bit confused trying to make our way back to the hotel one night after a gig. If I'm ever in London again I'll definitely be staying here. :)

title: The spirit of England.. Good Manner Services , boutique choice
text: Represent the spirit of England , Good Services and warm greeting.. Apparently provide multi languages in the reception , good recommendation for nearby community facilities and shops.. You will quite enjoy your short journey in Western London for take a break as a British as well.

title: What Trip Advisor is for
text: Excellent room, spacious and very well equipped with a bath, a minibar, a Nespresso machine, kettle, iron and ironing board. My only complaint was the noise because it overlooked Hangar Lane. If you get the chance, a room on the other side of the building would be worth paying a bit extra for. Whole place has comfortable and relaxing decor and the bar has a desktop computer which customers can use (there is also free wif-fi). Note: although the address is Hangar Lane, the hotel is a long way from Hangar Lane tube station (I know because I walked it) but is very close to North Ealing which is just round the corner. All in all, just the sort of value for money out-of-the-way gem of a hotel that you hope to find with Trip Advisor.

title: Great
text: Very nice and friendly hotel at a good rate ! 24h open bar which is great ! Rooms are very cosy , comfortable and modern, with excellent amenities! Shy ( shylander, the Brazilian receptionist) is amazing ! Super friendly and hard worker ! See potential to be a good manager !

title: Hotel 55 - Cozy
text: Small room, but nonetheless, the bed is so comfortable I had trouble waking up in the morning! Amenities were basic, but complete, and toiletries were from Molton Brown! Good location, near the airport, within 30 mins for taxi journey and costs less than 25 pounds! Very near the tube also! Good when you're here purely for shopping!

title: Great hotel.
text: We stayed here for the first time recently and had a lovely room with a view of the garden at the back of the hotel. The hotel has a small car park and we managed to find a space but as the tube station is just round the corner we didn't need to use the car after that. The hotel has a bar lounge and a Japanese restaurant. We had a lovely meal there ,which was the first time we had eaten Japanese food ,but the staff were very helpful when choosing what to eat. The restaurant was full and the food was amazing. The hotel staff were also excellent and we thoroughly enjoyed our stay.

title: Above Expectations
text: We stayed at the Hotel 55 for several nights in late November. Our room faced the garden so it was away from the road noise. Although the rooms are tiny, the bathrooms are first rate, the beds and bedding are very good

title: "Loved this hotel"
text: From the moment we got to this hotel, I knew our stay was going to be perfect! We picked this hotel because we were seeing MUSE at Wembley stadium and because we liked the look from the photo's. This hotel is modern, stylish, clean and inviting. Our room and bathroom was lovely, comfortable bed. We had drinks in the garden until the Japanese restaurant opened at 6pm. The food was gorgeous. Better still, we hopped on a number 83 bus outside the petrol station straight to Wembley (£2.00 each) and got the bus back at nearly 1am, which stopped right outside the front door of the hotel. Really enjoyed our breakfast, lovely coffee too, I will definitely be staying here again!!

title: Weekend Break in London for BST Hyde Park 9 -11 July 2016
text: This is an excellent hotel located within 5 min. walk of the Piccadilly Line with direct links to the City centre. Hotel is spotlessly clean, staff are very friendly with excellent service. Nothing was too much trouble. Room was compact but extremely well fitted and had everything you need and was exceptionally clean. Could not fault it. Parking is limited but we were able to park outside off road. Would definitely stay here again.

title: I liked it and it did the job
text: I liked this hotel and it did the job for me. Yes, it is not in a central city centre location, which may be a minus for a lot of people. For me it is important to have clean rooms, good breakfast, friendly staff and reasonable prices. Hotel 55 had all that. It takes 20 minuted by tube to reach London city centre and the tube station is literally round the corner from the hotel. The Ealing area is quiet, green and tranquil. If you take a walk around, you will see beautiful english houses, lovely gardens and get a feeling of a real residential part of the city. No hustle and bustle, rather quiet and peace. Breakfast is full and high quality: juices from real fruit juice, cereals, toasts and fruit. The room we had was a little tiny, but very clean. Internet connection worked perfect and it's free. All in all, I liked this place and will return.

title: Nice and clean but noisy.
text: Stayed here with friends last week. Originally booked for 3 nights but decided to check out after 2. I paid extra for a garden room and to be fair there was no traffic noise, however we were awoken at 6am by an alarm coming from an upstairs room which did not go off. I also managed to hear the news in detail from next door rooms tv and I don't think they even had it on that loud. Would I stay there again? Probably not.

title: Great place!
text: Me and my partner have stayed here twice and have not been disappointed on either occasion! The staff are friendly and welcoming, there is great parking spaces available either at the front of the hotel or round the corner near the station which is reasonably priced! The rooms are beautiful, comfortable beds and modern! There is even a coffee machine which for me makes this room top! I don't think I will go elsewhere as it is great value for money and I have stayed in various Hilton hotels and 5 start hotels!

title: Very nice indeed!
text: Just got back from a long weekend at Hotel 55 for my boyfriend's birthday and we were really impressed! Booked through their website and got 3 nights (Friday-Sunday) B&B for £220 which was a bargain compared to similar options I'd looked at. Our room was on the top floor overlooking the garden and was spacious enough - although it did get very warm at night and we couldn't get the air con to go any cooler! Nicely decorated room, comfy bed and small bathroom with very powerful shower! I think I'd recommend getting a garden facing room on the first floor - these seem to be the more spacious, quieter and cooler rooms. The Wi-fi worked no problem. Breakfast is perfectly adequate and the service at the reception was excellent. They were very helpful and one member of staff even offered us his umbrella when we were going out to a restaurant one evening in the rain! It's really close to North Ealing station, and the trip to Oxford Circus (fairly central) takes about 45mins. We'd also recommend the little Italian restaurant round the corner (near the tube station) - massive portions and great service at a very reasonable price. All in all, a really good place to stay, we enjoyed being a little further out of London and will definitely be going back!

title: Excellent Hotel
text: Stayed here for only the one night however wish it was longer! Originally booked for a garden view room, and arranged an early check in of 1pm. When we arrived at the hotel at around 1:20pm we were informed that our room wasn't quite ready, the staff quickly rectified this by offering us a complementry drink in the bar, which was nice of them. When the room was ready around 15-20 minutes later, the guy who took us to our room, which I believe was the manager, informed us that we had been upgraded to a suite, which was a pleasent surprise! The room was amazing! separate bedroom and living area, mini barv and even a small kictchenette! The bathroom was equally as nice with a lovely rain shower. The hotel isn't in the city centre however it is very easy to travel to and from the hotel by the tube, the nearest station (North Ealing) is about a 2 minute walk away, and the piccadilly line takes you right to the heart of the city. Takes around 30 minutes to Knightsbridge, where you can find Harrods, which my partner loved, at my expense! Travelling to Wembley couldn't be easier, as there is a bus stop just across the road. However we opted for a taxi, which costs £16 one way and took around 30 minutes due to the traffic, as it was an England International game. Overall our stay at Hotel 55 was excellent and wouldn't hesitate staying here again when i'm next in london.

title: Not what you would imagine from the outside
text: I needed a hotel close to Ealing Broadway for 2 nights. I was welcomed at reception and handed the key to my 'cozy' room. cozy because of the size. However, the bed was comfortable and the bathroom fully equipped. Complimentary wifi and bottled water. And a bonus was the efficient air conditioning and inclusive continental breakfast. All at a reasonable price. On one of the nights of my stay I ate in the Japanese restaurant. Good food, good service, at a reasonable price. I would definitely stay here again.

title: Great Little Hotel
text: We stayed at Hotel 55 for one night on 16 June. On arrival we managed to bag one of the free parking spaces located at the front of the hotel, there are only 4 spaces available so we were very lucky. Check-in was very easy and straightforward and we were given room 204 on the top floor. The room was a good size with a comfortable double bed, wardrobe, easy chair, flat screen tv, safe, tea & coffee facilities and airconditioning. We had a view of the large well-kept garden at the rear of the hotel. The ensuite was lovely, very contemporary with a large power shower. Molton Brown toiletries were a nice touch. The room was very quiet due to it being at the back of the building, away from the road. The hotel's main eating area is great, with a bar and separate lounge area. Breakfast is continental only (no full english) but it was very nice with a good selection of food, cereals, fruit etc. The train station is literally a 2 minute walk around the corner of the hotel, and there's a selection of little shops plus a pub which does food in the same vicinity. Our stay was to visit a concert at Wembley Stadium. The hotel is approx. 3.5 miles away. We had taxi to get us to the stadium which cost £13 (the hotel reception arranged this for us), and we walked back afterwards, which was quite a trek and took about an hour! We would definately stay at this hotel again for both visiting Wembley and visiting Central London (20 minutes away). A lovely hotel with very helpful staff.

title: A gem of a small hotel not far from central London
text: We had a great stay at this hotel, which is contemporary on the inside and tastefully furnished. Our room was a very comfortable suite, the cupboard had lots of space for folded or hanging clothes, skylights gave the room lots of natural sunlight, big screen TV's, modern furniture and lighting fixtures, fruit bowl, good quality coffee machine too and small fridge: the bathroom was also fabulous,,spacious with underfloor heating and heated towel rack, and the good shower and bathtub made for a relaxing time. The breakfast buffet was also very tasty with a nice variety to choose from, the mark of a more up-scale hotel, including very good cappuccino. We had dinner once at their Japanese restaurant, MoMo, which was also very good and popular we heard among the local residents in that area. The staff were also very friendly and helpful at all times. Can't think of any complaints during our stay there. Highly recommended for anyone who's looking for a pleasant stay in the London area but without paying two to three times more than they have to. The hotel is conveniently located near the North Ealing station, so getting into the center was quite straightforward. Great value for money, we'll stay there again next time we go to London.

title: Lovely hotel, but not quite worth the money.
text: My boyfriend and I stayed here for three nights, and it was a very pleasant stay except for a few minor hiccoughs here and there! We arrived mid-afternoon and were given the key-card to our room with little to no fuss at the reception desk. We asked for a garden view - unfortunately, the restaurant below our first-floor room blocked the vast majority of the garden, which was a shame considering we'd paid extra. The room is a bit on the small side and is probably not ideal for those staying for a long time with a lot of luggage, but other than that it was a very good little room! Very modern and tastefully-decorated, and with some really lovely mood lighting, too. The room has the usual complimentary stuff like a kettle, teabags, and a hairdryer, but I was surprised to see an espresso machine on the desk, too! Useful for those who need motivation to catch the morning tube! The bed was very comfortable, but I believe there was something wrong with one of the wheels, because it would suddenly shift forwards every time we leaned against the wall. Unfortunately, whilst nudging the bed back to its original position, we saw that the floor underneath was absolutely covered in dust and old bits of food. Not quite what we wanted to see on our first night! I understand that it's difficult to vacuum underneath furniture, but it really was an extremely unpleasant sight. Other than that, there was no other fault with the bedroom! I'd recommend sleeping with the window closed and the air-con switched on - even though our room was facing away from the main road, we could still occasionally hear sirens during the night when the window was open! The air-con works very well - slightly noisy at times, but much better than sleeping in a stuffy room! The bathroom was pleasant enough. The shower door was a little bit stiff, but the power shower more than made up for any other issue! Bloody loved that shower. The sink was a little bit on the small side - be careful when running the tap at full blast, because there's a very good chance you'll accidentally soak your crotch and/or the entire bathroom. Bit unfortunate, that. My only gripe with reception was when we went down to tell them that our safe didn't lock. The receptionist told us it would be fixed soon (according to my locksmith boyfriend, all it needed was a reset code) but it remained broken for the rest of our stay. Not a massive problem, but it would've been nice to have somewhere to keep our valuables. Oh! Before I forget: I absolutely loved the complimentary L'Occitane toiletries! Even when we accidentally forgot to remove the 'do not disturb' sign from our door after leaving for the day, the maids left a little bag of clean towels and toiletries outside our door. Very considerate! Location wise, the hotel is in a relatively quiet and green area compare with the rest of London. The underground station (North Ealing) is literally just a minute's walk 'round the corner. Get yourself an Oyster card, and - boom! You're sorted for your entire trip! Ideal. It takes about twenty to thirty minutes to reach the more central areas of London, but the station is so quiet it's usually very easy to get a seat on the tube when it arrives. Unless it's rush hour, of course. Top tip: avoid commuters like the plague. Due to not being much of a breakfast person, I never actually tried any of the hotel's food, but we did dine at Momo, the Japanese restaurant adjacent to Hotel 55. Let me tell you now that Momo is the absolute best Japanese food I've ever had, and this comes from the self-proclaimed queen of sushi. The staff was very friendly, and the food was beyond delicious! Absolutely loved it. If you find yourself with a free evening, definitely eat at Momo! (I recommend the chef's selection of sushi!) We checked-out on Saturday morning, and the receptionist was lovely and very efficient. He seemed a bit bemused by the fact that we hadn't eaten anything from the mini-bar ("Are you sure you had nothing at all?"), but who on earth would ever pay two quid for a Kit-Kat? Go to the garage down the road. Beat the system and buy four Kit-Kats for the price of one hotel Kit-Kat. Hell yeah. I genuinely enjoyed my stay, but the hotel didn't quite feel like it was worth the money we paid for it, even if it was in the most expensive city in Britain. Good thing we got a cheaper deal than most! I hope my review doesn't put anyone off! Also: free wi-fi! Awesome.

title: Saved us
text: After needing to find a hotel room after chaos at Heathrow airport and flights for our family of 4 being cancelled at midnight, and having been told by the airline to find our own accommodation, the night staff Hotel 55 saved our faith in humanity by being very helpful and understanding (beyond just finding us a room) after I found them online.

title: A Haven of Peace in the Traffic Madness of London
text: When compared to similarly priced hotels in the Ealing and Acton area this is a gem. Conveniently placed for the tube and an NCP car park, Hotel 55 was exactly what we needed. Whilst the rooms are not all spacious, and some a touch gloomy, they are of a high spec and the hotel has some very attentive and efficient, well trained staff. Of particular note is the high standard of continental breakfast with an excellent choice of cereal, pastries and fruit. I would definetely use Hotel 55 again and fully recommend it.

title: Garden Room
text: Lovely hotel, within 10 min walk to Ealing Broadway. The hotel has a beautiful bar area which opens into a peaceful and well keep garden, which is a real bonus in busy London, and the drinks from the bar were reasonably priced. Will definitely be back again. xx

title: As Advertised
text: For a change, I went down the laterooms option - found that the hotel was acutally as advertised - did not delivery more than what was promised, but at least it was not less. Friendly staff and actually interested in making your stay comfortable. Be daring and try the new garden room, but definately try and negotiate the rate down. Would come back

title: Good for Wembley location and tube access
text: We booked 2 nights at this hotel and chose it due to it proximity to a tube station and Wembley. We couldn't have got much closer to North Ealing tube station and it was a 2 min walk round the corner the only downside was that it took 30 to get to central London for the rest of the trip. For Wembley it was great on the way as there was regular buses right opposite the hotel and took us directly to the arena. Allow plenty of time as the traffic is slow and took us 45 mins to get there. On the way back no buses arrived at all and we struggled to get a taxi. The bus service was supposed to be a 24 hour service but we waiting a long time and not one showed. We paid £25 for a taxi back. Our room was 002 which was on the ground floor and an adapted room. The noise from the street wasn't too noticeable however we had more noise from Reception as our room was right next door. I would suggest a garden facing room or one away from Reception. You can tell the have tried to reduce the sound delivery as it had two doors to the room - a heavy duty fire door and an additional internal door. The room was clean, modern and had all necessary requirement with the exception of milk. We couldn't have a hot drink! There was complimentary bottles of water. The bathroom was spacious however a little dark. The lighting could be a lot better. The beds and pillows were comfy and the rooms were made up whilst we were out. The cupboard space was good and could hang up all our things and put the suitcases in the cupboard which kept the room clear. As it isn't a central hotel it was a very quiet and relaxing hotel but lacked a buzz that I like. There was very little around therefore you needed to be more central for busy restaurants and bars. The staff were great and friendly and helpful. Good little hotel but just not busy enough for me.

title: Small but excellent
text: If you want large rooms then this hotel is not for you. But on the plus side, very clean, great staff very helpful, the garden is pretty in a zen kind of way. Breakfast was very good and only a few minutes away from the tube. If you fancy some pub food just pop to the Greystoke a few minutes away

title: Fantastic staff and handy location
text: I stayed here for a weekend having driven down from Manchester. Access to the hotel is perfect - easily accessible from the A40 and easy to find on Hanger Lane. Parking wasn't a problem even though there were no spaces left at the hotel. We parked in North Ealing tube station (£1 for 24 hours!!) without a problem. The room was smallish but adequate and decor was lovely - the place was spotless. Bathroom was also really well thought out with a fantastic shower!! I was concerned that there would be road noise but I slept like a log with no noise whatsoever. Breakfast was continental with a good choice and really friendly, efficient staff. We didn't have dinner there or use the bar - Ealing is within walking distance with a wider selection of eateries and bars. A real find I think!!

title: Hidden Gem..
text: What a fantastic hotel this is.. Modern, Spotlessly clean with Friendly helpful staff.. North Ealing station is a 2 minute walk away and the town centre of Ealing is 5 minutes away on foot. The Japanese restaurant on site serves lovely food for a reasonable price. The hotel serves continental Breakfast which can be eaten on the patio area in the garden. Bar serving alcohol on site but pubs and restaurants around the corner if you want to venture out. Would highly recommend staying in this hotel.

title: Convenient and a good value for the money
text: My wife and I recently visited the UK and this is the place where we stayed during the fifth night of our trip. Once we found the place, the biggest issue was finding parking. The hotel has no onsite parking but being London we expected parking to be an issue. Luckily the East Ealing tube station is pretty close to the hotel so we were able to park there for the duration of our stay without any problems. It was also very convenient to stay somewhere that is so close to a tube station. The hotel’s décor is very modern and trendy which made it attractive. Check-in was easy and the desk clerk was very friendly and was kind enough to give me change for the parking meter. Walking to our room was quite difficult however because there where large stacks of bags of towels all thought the halls which had to be climbed over at times. I thought to myself at first that they were probably just doing their rounds cleaning the rooms, but the bags were there during our whole visit, so I guess that is just where they store them which we thought was kinda odd. The Room was VERY small and essentially had just enough room for the King sized bed in it so you had to climb over it to get to the bathroom and there was no room at all to put your luggage. Still, my wife and I agreed that it was good that they didn’t sacrifice the quality and size of the bed for more walking space because the bed was the most amazingly comfortable bed that I’ve ever slept in. It had both a feather down mattress and comforter. The bathroom was small too and the sink didn’t work very well, but the shower was nice with great water pressure. The hotel includes breakfast which is nice and convenient. It wasn’t too fancy but it was perfect for our needs. Checkout was quick and easy and the desk clerk in the morning was just as friendly as the one the day before. All in all a pretty good place to stay.

title: Great boutique hotel!
text: I have stayed at this hotel many times, it is situated just outside central london and so is very easy to get to and excellent value for money. If you are lucky yo may get a free parking space on the front of the hotel…. there are only a few, four I think. If not then there is plenty of parking just round the corner at the train station. It is small, yet nicely furnished and a lovely place to stay.

title: Excellent base for a city weekend
text: My girlfriend and I stayed here for two nights whilst down in London for a weekend break. Unfortunately due to prior commitments we were not able to arrive at the hotel until around 1am. Having known this in advance I emailed the hotel who were prompt to respond, asking if parking could be reserved and would reception still be open. I was notified that unfortunately due to the limited parking (there are only 4 spaces) that if one was not available upon arrival I would have to use a pay car park around the corner, but that checking in at around 1am was not an issue. Upon arrival (bang on 1am) I was pleased to see that there was a parking space available, which I proceeded to leave my car in all weekend until we left, though we did find out shortly after that the pay and display car park is literally a 2 minute walk around the corner, at North Ealing Tube station, and is also very reasonable priced - around £3.50 for 24 hours if I remember rightly. Sure enough the reception was also open ready for us to check in. My only complaint at this point is that with it being a boutique hotel in what is essentially a converted house, there are rooms right next to reception. I wasn't aware of this and was told quite abrubtly to keep my voice down - I feel signage on the front door may have been useful, or simply a more polite request to keep the noise down. I have to say the room was very tastefully decorated. Space wasn't exactly in abundance, especially with me being 6ft4, but that said it is a boutique hotel, and it wasn't particularly cramped either. The room was exceptionally clean and the temperature control was very good to ensure a good nights sleep. I do not like hotel beds, but I must say the bed here was very comfortable indeed and I had no issue sleeping. Our room was situated on the back of the hotel - with the front being on a main road I assume there would be some traffic noise, but it was perfectly quiet being at the back for a good nights sleep. The bathroom was again small, but very nicely fitted out and very clean. Most importantly the shower was powerful and didn't fluctuate in temperature at all which was pleasing. There was even a nice coffee machine in the room with complimentary shots/pouches to use and these were replaced the following day if used. We didn't use the restaurant or have breakfast as the hotel was simply somewhere to sleep for us, so I can't comment on those aspects. The hotel itself is in a superb location right round the corner from North Ealing tube station which is only a few stops away from the main stations in London on the Piccadilly line - within half an hour maximum we were at Knightsbridge. I would definitely use this hotel again for a weekend break. It is easy to get to in the car, convenient for parking even if you have to pay and display around the corner, and is reasonably priced in comparison to the competition.

title: Lovely boutique hotel
text: Stayed here for three nights, its a lovely hotel, clean and chic with comfortable beds and great shower, the staff are very friendly, we asked to change rooms because our shower was cold and we had a room on the busy main road and the traffic noise kept us awake, but they moved us to a room at the rear with no problem. Only a 2 minute walk from north ealing station and about 25 minutes into central London. There is a lovely italian restaurant near the station called Vila Toscana, the food is excellent.

title: what a find
text: We stayed in this hotel at the week-end and booked a garden view. I have to say although the room was quite small it was very very clean, the shower was heaven (after miles of walking) with lots of clean soft towels. Slept like a log in the lovely comfortable bed. A really good choice of breakfast. All the staff were very polite and attentive especially the gentleman on the front desk nothing was to much trouble. Good old fashioned service.When in london we will always stay here from now on. Thank-you.

title: Very clean friendly hotel
text: I stayed here with my Mother for 5 nights. It was around a 20 minute tube ride into London, but the subway was literally 5 minutes away. We had booked a street-side room, and there were 2 available when we checked in, so they let us picked with one. There was one that was sunny and faced the street - and one that faced a side of another building. We picked the one that faced another building due to noise complaints others had made about the street. We had no problems with the noise, but the room always seemed dark. They could do with brighter light bulbs. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I used the free Wi-Fi everyday and had no problems. There are not a lot of choices of restaurants around the area - but you can take a 15 minute walk to Ealing/Broadway and have plenty of choices.

title: cosy, good, convenient hotel
text: Stopped here one night after I located a £90 deal on Laterooms. It did the job. Only 4/5 car parking spaces - there is an NCP at the North Ealing tube station (£2.20/day). Picadilly line about 30 minutes to Picadilly Circus, but quite infrequent trains in the morning (could have walked 10 minutes to the central line though). Location for car was OK - right on the North Circular. If you're coming by car, you MUST approach from the north (A40, hangar lane gyratory) or you'll find it impossible to turn in. Room was v cosy indeed - not comfortable for anything other than sleeping - extremely minimal working space for business travellers. There was free wi-fi which was great since the Vodafone signal strength was zero. Overall rating - good, but not great for the business traveller.

title: Excellent hotel right where I needed it.
text: The tiniest room I've ever had, but all was there! We shared a small double room, and in this case the price and location was what we needed, in addition, there is an excellent japanese restaurant in the house.

title: Great stay
text: We booked over the internet from Australia and did not know what to expect. Place was great. Bed was first class comfortable. Breakfast excellent and great selection. Staff were more than helpful. Only drawback would be that the bathroom was a little squeezy but as we spent all day sightseeing it didn't matter. The comfort of the bed and inclusive breakfast more than made up for it. Would stay there again.

title: Lovely
text: We stayed here for one night. Wanting somewhere close to Wembley and also easy to get into London. The staff were friendly and helpful. We really enjoyed our stay and will recommend to others. Will return in the future.

title: Great for Wembley
text: We were looking for a reasonably-priced but decent hotel within reach of Wembley stadium, when we were seeing a concert. We were lucky to come across Hotel 55.The hotel is on a bus route that stops directly outside the stadium although the return journey, when that bus stop was closed, was a bit more tricky and required the use of an Uber taxi (about £12 journey, I seem to recall). It doesn't look much from the outside but once you enter, the modern decor gives this boutique property a contemporary feel of quality. The room itself was a good size and had everything we needed but was not quite the same standard as the bar and restaurant area (some of the furniture was a bit dated). Still decent though and the bed was comfortable so overall I think it was great value for money and a decent place to stay. We hit the bar once we got back too, which was happy to serve us until we headed up to the room around 2ish, I think(!!). Would recommend it if you are going to Wembley and we would stay there again.

title: Pleasant stay
text: Good hotel. Good location. Good value for money. Very helpful staff. Comfortable bed and clean bathroom. Nice perks like l'occitane en Provence toiletries and nespresso coffee machine. Free parking available but very limited i.e. 4 spaces in the front of the property. Would definitely recommend and I'd stay here in london again if the price were right.

title: Clean, compact, generally pleasant hotel and amazing for the price
text: Our primary reason for staying here was proximity to a friend we were visiting but we were pleasantly surprised by the place. It is right on the main road (north circular) so handy for getting in and out of London by road and also close to North Ealing tube station on the Piccadilly line for getting into the centre. There is as you might expect some traffic noise as a result, so if you can book a room at the back of the property as we did. It didn't disturb our sleep in any event. The hotel is very clean and neat, with modern decor and artwork throughout the corridors and rooms. This gives it a nice homey feel, and the friendly staff help reinforce this. Our bedroom was quite compact but we did have just about the cheapest room. The bathroom in particular was bijou shall we say. But the shower was spacious and as I said everything was spotless so no complaints there. Breakfast was pretty standard - continental included as a default which is cereal, pastries, fruit salad, juice, yoghurt, etc. and an extra fiver for cooked food which could be a full English, omelette or whatever as you request. Which was very good for the price. Dinner was excellent as there is a Japanese restaurant which has been there for years but has I'm told merged with the hotel more recently. It is well worth trying that out one night - or indeed lunch if you get up late! One other nice touch was getting free bottles of water in the room. Which helped counteract the usual astronomical prices of anything from the fridge, if you had wanted a mini bottle of wine for example. You will be able to find better hotels in the centre of London but I challenge you to find many, or indeed any, that are as good for the price. It worked out as something like £100 and a bit per night for the two of us which is very unusual for anywhere within this distance of central London. Give it a try, you won't be disappointed.

title: GREAT VALUE, FRIENDLY PEOPLE
text: I stay at the Picton on a weekly basis as my work regularly brings me to central London. I can't fault this place for location, price or service. Gary & Dwight can't do enough for you & go way beyond the call of duty to help their guests (they see you more as a new friend). Plenty of bars, coffee shops & a variety of restaurants - all within walking distance. Hyde Park is 5 mins walk & a 40 minute stroll will take you right into the heart of the city. The area is served well by 2 tube stations & a mainline station. I have colleagues who stay in a nearby "chain" @ more than twice the price & whilst their decor is better, they all complain about the impersonal aspect. London is a lonely city if you're on your own, at the Picton you've always got a friend. The number of return guests are a testament to the warmth displayed at the hotel. Re the decore - it's a mad mix of traditional & 70's modern but it's quite quirky so I like it. everyone I recommend this palce to loves it. give it a try - you won't be disappointed.

title: A nice hotell perfect situated in London
text: Nice hotell with a good athmosphere. The personell are very friendly, serviceminded and also positiv. The breakfast was very good! We will come back later when we are visiting London again. Elin and Geir from Norway

title: Made London Experience Great
text: Found the Hotel listed on the internet and chose it because it was near the tube and Hyde Park. We arrived early in the morning and were allowed to check in early. We had booked tickets to a show the first night and Gary whipped out a map and drew our route to the theater on it. We spent the next 4 nights there and enjoyed it all. We checked out and then the snow began to fall. We made it to the airport only to be sent back to a different hotel in London by the airline. We spent one night in the other hotel and then I decided that if I was going to be stuck in London that I wanted to be in a place more hospitable then some big sterile hotel. I called the Mandalay and they said they had a room so we made our way back. We spent 4 more nights in the Mandalay and every day was nice and warm and comfortable. They even helped us get tickets on the ferry out of England so we could make it home in time for Christmas. My daughter is already planning on returning there in the summer. oh....and the food at the restaurant is wonderful as well! Order the coconut chicken dish!

title: exceptionally good value for central London
text: I spent 8 nights at this B&B in March/April this year. I chose Mandalay Picton House, as I was searching for a B&B or budget hotel walking distance from my daughter's flat in Paddington, and I was impressed by the Tripadvisor reviews I found here. I actually had 2 stays (6 nights, then away for 4 nights, then back for another 2), and after I'd found myself feeling quite at home and relaxed there during the first stay I was very pleased to be coming back. My single room had a little balcony and a nice view over the street (Sussex Gardens). It was comfy, nothing flash, but not at all dreary. Breakfast was simple, but filling (I had toast, egg, baked beans cooked with tomato, cold cheese and cucumber, jam, & a pot tea, every morning!) - not at all gourmet but it did the trick to get me out the door, and there is plenty of exciting eating to be done in London over the rest of the day. The family who run the B&B are very friendly, and it felt very safe there - I left my luggage in the tiny reception area on my last day, and this was fine (you can't walk in from the street without being buzzed in or without a key, and one of the staff is always sitting at reception or not far away). Paddington also always felt very safe to walk around when I was on my own, daytime or very late at night - it's an all night kind of place, and well lit up. The main reason for going back would be for value for money. This B&B cost less than the equivalent of $85 (Australian) per night, including breakfast, which is remarkable, considering it's in central London.

title: Very friendly
text: I booked this hotel because of it's location close to Paddington, because it claimed quieter rooms and because it was within my budget. We were staying one night and were visiting the theatre that night, so it was just a place to sleep and have breakfast. I found the room clean, and while basic, it had all you needed. I had booked a room at the back of the building as it was quieter, and it was quiet enough for a good night's sleep. The main positive for me was the friendly service throughout our visit. There was gluten free toast provided for a special diet, and they even gave a small gift and a big Happy Birthday to my little girl on her special day. It was those little things that made the difference.

title: Interesting
text: As long as all you need is somewhere to sleep, this hotel is fine. The owner was lovely (I think he was the owner!), He was friendly and helpful. The hotel is very tired and shabby. The socket fell out when I unplugged my charger! The bathroom is the smallest I have ever seen. I'm short so it was fine, but my husband wouldn't have a hope of fitting in it. TV worked occasionally, but not every time we tried. Wifi was only available in certain locations. Breakfast was average, though I'm not sure about curried beans and curried sausage that early in the morning. Leaving bags was just behind a screen, albeit, only staff could let you in. Location is perfect for Paddington. We were surprised how quiet it was (apart from the drains outside).

title: Service, safety and central
text: I first came in contact with hotel owners through their small, budget but excellent restaurant Mandalay on Edgeware Rd. Since then I have stayed at Mandalay Picton House Hotel several times and have always been satisfied. The small rooms and lack of lift are more than compensated for by the first class service and location. The breakfast is hearty, if somewhat greasy, and clean towels are provided daily. I have always felt very safe and comfortable at this friendly, quiet family hotel. Colleen

title: Don't stay here
text: When we came to our room (we just got the keys and walked alone to the last floor) we realized that the room wasn't cleaned from the guests before us, but we coudn't find any of the staff because it was late. Worst experience ever and I traveled the whole world. The smell was unbearable. There is no wi-fi in the rooms or at the reception.

title: A bit odd
text: This hotel was recommended to us by some friends in Norway. The area is nice and quiet and with Edgware Road close by, you get to see parts of London one would not have seen staying at more central hotels. The staff is very friendly, and the prices are not too bad. I did not like the room at all. Fabric filled with dust and the strangest lavatory ever. It's like a spaceship cubicle in the wall. Hard to describe really, and might as an oddity be worth a stay in itself. Never seen this before. But very small and poorly ventilated. As soon as it gets wet in there your room will smell like a wet dog. Breakfast was interesting. Not what I was expecting, but very tasty nonetheless.

title: Friendly but old fashioned
text: There is a warm and friendly welcome at the hotel but it is a little old fashioned and needs some updating. Everything is clean and tidy. My room with its wooden wall panelling was a bit gloomy but it served its purpose. Windows are single glazed so you may need to leave the radiator switched on if you like it warm. My room backed onto the back of the hotel so was reasonably quiet. Bedding was interesting and a bit like staying at your grandmothers in the 70s with sheets blankets and an eiderdown. I think progression to duvets might be a step forward. nonetheless the bed was comfortable. You step up into the caravan style shower room which was reasonably cramped. The sink was missing a plug which is not helpful if like me you wet shave. The water from the shower is hot and plentiful but the shower curtain seemed to have a life off its own and (one of my pet hates) stuck to me constantly as i showered. Tea making facilities are available but are not topped up daily (cups are cleaned though). If you need more tea bags, milk etc these are available at the bottom of the staircase by reception. Breakfast is in the basement from 7 till 9 (good for those who prefer a little earlier start). The lady of the house is welcoming. Breakfast is basic but at least it is provided if you need it. Keys have to be left at the hotel and the front door is locked but there is usually someone to open the front door and you don't have to wait too long. Cheap and cheerful for those just wanting somewhere to rest their head and very convenient for Paddington Station but could probably do with a bit of an update.

title: I love this hotel!
text: I have been traveling to London for many years now. The first years i stayed at many different kinds of hotels. Than about five or six years ago i was recomended this hotel from a friend. I travel to London many times evrey year, and than i always at this hotel. I am from Norway, so i was suprised when i learned that some of the staff spoke Norwegian as fluentley as if they were born in Norway. The service and helpfullness from the owners and the staff is the best i have experienced in a hotel anywhere in the world, it feels bit like my second home in England. Whatever i ask about the staff are always willing to help. The breakfast is good, and the rates are reasonable. Usually when i stay in a hotel with this kind of rates, i usually will get no breakfast, or just toast and marmelade, not so here! The rooms are good, and they are always kept clean. The location of the hotel is also perfect. Just 3 minutes to walk to Paddington underground or rail. I have stayed in this hotel maybe 10- 15 times, alone or with friends and the service, breakfast, and rooms has always got the same standard. I will in the future always stay in this hotel when i am in London. The top rating from me is not because it is a luxury hotel, cause it is not, but because all in all it is perfect! By the way the owners have a Burmeese resturant about 10 minutes to walk from the hotel. The food there is fantastic. The staff at the hotel will make a reservation at the resturant for you. You wont regret it!

title: Awesome
text: This is our second time staying here. We love this hotel. It’s affordable, it’s clean, staff is so friendly and the neighborhood is lovely. Close to Paddington, close to Hyde Park, close to pubs and restaurants Thanks for having us-see you soon. Next stay, you may want us to keep our key 😉#coyg

title: Cheap and cheerful
text: This hotel is convenient for Paddington Station, the underground and a short walk from Hyde Park. Staff are very helpful and friendly. The room was very clean with twin beds but the bathroom was very small, it had a sink, toilet and shower which was manageable because we are both small. It is very secure and safety of everyone seems paramount. There is a good selection for breakfast especially as it's included in the price. This is very cheap for somewhere so close to the centre of London.

title: Affordable hotel close to Paddington Station
