title: Fantastic apartment
text: Beautiful spacious apartment, very centrally located with Kilburn High Road and Kilburn Park stations right next door. Couldn't have found a better place with such a great location and a very reasonable price!

title: Value for Money - with everything within 5 minutes reach
text: Initially I was bit hesitant about being at SOQ (based on some of the not so good reviews), but based on my friend's (who was at SOQ) feedback - went ahead with the reservation. I got a room at 4th Floor - which had 1 Bed Room, 1 Hall - with TV-Sofa at left & Kitchen on right, and a table with couple of chairs in the center. Kitchen was fully furnished - with 4 burners, oven, griller, fridge, dish washer and a washing machine as well. It also had cutleries - good enough for a small family. Bed room had a king size bed with a cupboard & bed side table. Also, a 3 drawer chest. Washroom was spacious enough & had all modern amenities one could ask for. Localities: Tesco Express is downstairs - so you get more or less everything. Kilburn Park Tube (Underground) is 3 minutes walk, and overground (Kilburn High) is hardly a minute away. You have multiple cash machines around the place - with one just next to Tesco. Just the other side of the road - you have multiple food joints, Mobile card/recharge stores, grocery/breakfast/electronics/bags/shoes/fruits - you name it & you have it here. Finally - the Hotel Staff: What I liked best about this place is the friendliness of the staff here. Absolutely friendly to the T. And always ready to help. :) Do I recommend this place? You best! Of course yes!!! Special Points/Tips: (1) The rooms with road side view are more airy - and I felt more comfortable. But they are also bit noisy! (2) Rooms on the inside are more quiet. But you may feel bit hotter (even without the heaters). (3) Wifi at hotel is good enough (you need to collect the voucher from reception)

title: Nightmare on Kilburn Highroad
text: I booked this Hotel with another company they had a different name for it.. SO London this was with Travelstay...... I booked a 1bed Superior apartment with a bed settee in the lounge.. wot i did get was a dirty run down small room with a bedroom and bathroom.. Oh my god i was disgusted smelt like it had just been cleaned but the table had breadcrumbs and bits of food left on it cooker was filthy ground in food round the eliments bedding very white sheets but pillows grubby duvet old with holes in it carpets stained.. so i complained and was moved to another room of the same standard BUT this 1 was a little better or worse depending on what we saw ie carpet rail was stuck down with electric tape no screws the bed settee was taped up with the same electric tape you couldnt put it down because of a lack of space so i had to sleep on the top not it was only 3'6" wide i'm 5'6" with no covers for the full 4 nights of our stay this was due to not being any!! we got fed up with asking for utensils and crockery none came so we went to the local £ shop and bought our own.... Won't ever ever go back to this hotel i'm in a battle with Travestay and the onbudsman at the minute due to false advertising.... please don't book this hotel because you wont get what you pay for... The one good thing about our stay was the Hotel staff they were so friendly that is till we were ready to leave then they don't give a dam .........

title: Never book this accommodation!
text: Arrived here for a 2 night stay only to discover our 2 bedroom apartment had a maintenance problem. No hot water!! Was offered a 1 bedroom apartment for 5 and only agreed as receptionist said we would get room at half the cost. We clarified this point on several occasions to ensure we were hearing correctly and was assured that part of the deposit we had already paid would be refunded to our account later that day. Not a great start to our stay in London but although the room looked shabby and would be crammed we felt we could put up with it for the discount offered. Bad mistake!! The next morning the receptionist back tracked and said she had made an error and the discount was only 10%!!!!!!! Spent the next 2 days trying to speak to management without success. On checking out we still had no refund and the poor receptionist even offered to pay the money to us out of her own pocket ( seemed like she was scared of management) Which makes me wonder how they treat their staff ?? I believe she made a genuine mistake but the management should have stood by the original offer. Funnily enough a party of 6 arrived directly after us and were given a 2 bedroom apartment. Obviously they felt it was easier to fob us off with a smaller room. As regards our apartment it was far from its description as a luxury apartment, looks nothing like the photos online. Pillows were lumpy, blinds ripped to bits,view disgusting( rooftop covered in cigarette butts) mugs in kitchen smelt of disinfectant and tainted the taste of anything put in them. Shortage of towels and lack of information such as hairdryer had to be requested at reception if required etc. Only reason this place gets one star is its location to underground. Would never book this accommodation again. Wrote to management on my return only to be offered 10% off my next stay....not likely will never be back!!

title: spacious and clean DON'T be put off by other reviews!!!
text: People tend to only want to moan on reviews, but we are having a great time. When we arrived the lovely gentleman on the desk, upgraded us to a double bedroom apartment due to a slight misunderstanding on our booking :-) the kids loved having their own room and it felt like we were very much at home...beds comfortable and clean, heating all in working order,so lovely warm and cosy, bathroom nice and clean with plenty of towels and all kitchen appliances in working order (bring cutlery as this is not provided) but cups,plates and bowls are :-) the location is very good and locals are nice and friendly. Parking was full but we managed to park the car on the street close by for free(weekends only). We would definitely stay here again and will recommend to friends and family. when I read the reviews I was very worried about staying but then I realised that people who moan about a blind being broken are probably a jobsworth and moan about everything so please don't be put off! :-)

title: Not too bad
text: This is an "alright" place to stay, a little bit run down but clean and the staff were "mixed" in their english and service. We didn't have any issues with the lady on reception mentioned elsewhere here (she's Polish BTW) she always smiled and was helpful. Rooms were quite large and reasonably tidy and clean, be careful which room you get though because the ones facing the High Rd are noisy, very noisy!

title: Noisy
text: We went to So quartier wanting to stay for 11 days. The noise coming from the pub/club downstairs was so loud that we didnt sleep until 4 in the morning. Then at 6:30 when the shops (Tesco) opened below it was noisy again! The stuff i must say was friendly although I never got a wheelchair seat for the disabled shower eventhough i called and asked for it 5 days before arriving! Unless they put triple windows i dont think anyone will be able to stay there without earplugs! Good location, friendly eager to help stuff but extremely NOISY... I left on day 2. Alexis (disabled) with wife and son

title: Great option rather than a family room in a hotel
text: Excellent location 5 minutes from Kilburn Park tube station on Bakerloo line, 20mins from Kings Cross. Tesco express below so you can get provisions for breakfast, sandwiches for days out or food for an evening. First time in a Serviced Apartment , chosen because it was the same price as a family room in a hotel, a bargain really. Put the kids in the bedroom on the first night so we could watch tv. This meant we slept on the sofa bed, was a little bit uncomfy as the mattress is quite thin so swapped for the second night. We have 2 children aged 4 and 7 and took a blow up Noddy bed for the youngest as its only a double bed in the bedroom and a double sofa bed in the lounge. Staff friendly and helpful, all in all a pleasant stay at a reasonable rate. (£110 per night).

title: It costs a lot. It's not bad but could be better
text: The apartment was fundametally dirty. thay have moquette on floor and this doesn't help the idea of a clean place. the window was broken, few forks, knives and pots to cook. And they have the [--] "franch bed" (queen size). to sleep in two persons on it it is bad. good connection to the tube but bad area. Nothing against balck or poor people but sometimes where there' s poor life conditions there are crimes. and one day seiing the "police line Don't cross" on the street gives you the idea.

title: Far, far away from luxory!
text: We were transferred from So sienna, in which we booked the room for our 5 night stay. SO Sienna had problem with water (which apperes to be common according to the staff). The So Quartier apartment was small, oldish and worn with many problems. For example the bathroom smelled mould (had to use my asthma pipe), the bathroom lock got stucked all the time and the tap in the "kitchen" was leaking. There were not enough dishes for four people. The windows were blurred (which made the apartment dark), but when I opened the window, I could see the reason why. Luckily we did not spend much time in this appartment! Pros: the stuff was friendly and close to underground and overground stations. Nice restaurant (Raw Brick) nearby with good pizza and pasta!

title: Don't listen to bad reviews!
text: After booking to stay here I found lots of negative reviews so much so that I was dreading turning up here with my family! I was so relieved and pleasantly surprised when we opened the door and found a perfectly decent apartment much bigger and cleaner than expected. Nothing was old or broken as some reviews claimed and it was more than adequate for a theatre break with my partner and two boys. 2 mins walk from Kilburn Park tube station which is so handy with children after a long day of walking around! Only thing I would suggest is having a proper storage room for luggage to make you feel slightly more at ease when leaving belongings there as we had to leave ours in reception, the reception is manned 24 hrs a day so it is secure and our bags were left there all day before checking in and prior to checking out and were fine. All in all perfect stay, good service and no complaints what so ever. Would definitely stay here again :)

title: This place is SO bad I don't know where to begin...
text: This place is bad on every front. 1. The location is a constant struggle against noise, both in terms of traffic (cars, buses, trains) as well as noise from residents and visitors of the shops and pubs/restaurants nearby. 2. The staff are at best clueless and possibly ignorant. Despite speaking to hotel staff at the premises at time of reservation, one month prior to arrival and even a day prior to arrival, when my family checked in, they were not assigned a quiet room at the back of the building as agreed with the staff 3 times! 3. Most importantly, the state and cleanliness of this place is appalling. The general areas are dirty, smelly and run down, but unfortunately the rooms are worse. The furniture is worn down and some of it is even broken. The room smelled so bad that even a few mega-doses of Febreze could not deal with it. The kitchen had not been cleaned at all after the previous occupiers checked out (or possibly many months prior to that), so I ended up cleaning the entire kitchen myself while my sister tried to clean egg white from the water cooker that someone had tried to boil an egg in. When it was time to retire for the night, the discovery of used sheets on the sofa bed was the straw that broke the camel's back. I have spoken to hotel staff and have requested to speak to management upon discovery of each issue, but neither seemed at all interested in actually providing customer service or caring about customer satisfaction. After all, the money's in the bag, so why care?

title: Probably wouldn't return
text: Check-in was easy, great reception guy who upgraded us from a 1 bedroom/sofa bed apartment to a 2 bedroom apartment free of charge, we paid £165. But walking into the apartment it smelled and the laminated floor was awful - basically reminded me of uni halls but in a poorer condition. It wasn't dirty or unliveable for one night but it had seen better days. Area was ok but nothing special. If anything I would've paid abit more to stay somewhere better.

title: Fantastic apartments
text: My husband booked a one night stay for us without reading any reviews, if we had read them prior to booking we would never have had the pleasure of these fantastic apartments. The reviews we read after booking were awful but as we had made a non refundable booking there was not much we could do about it. We travelled with heavy hearts and arrived at So quartier 2 hours earlier than check in which is 2pm. We had informed them half an hour previous to our arrival that we would be there early and the receptionist was more than helpful offering the apartment to us on arrival. We could not have been more amazed with the size, quality and cleanliness of the apartment and couldn't believe that people had reviewed it so badly. I am very particular about bathrooms but I honestly could not fault it. The bed so extremely comfortable and the sheets were crisp and whiter than white. The kitchen area was also immaculate and fully functional. The smoke alarm in the living room was running low on battery life and was bleeping so we mentioned it to the receptionist on our way out for lunch, she assured us she would deal with it while we were away. On our return she apologised and said that the maintenance man was at lunch and would we mind moving to another room opposite (108) she offered to help us move our luggage but as we only had an overnight bag this was not needed. The second room was even better, only in that the sofa was bigger and more colourful and the lounge area was larger, all other rooms were exactly to the same high standard. Reading the previous reviews regarding noise, I opened the window only to hear noise any city would have. I found the tesco shop underneath a god send not a hinder due to it being a self catering apartment, it literally took 5 mins to buy my essentials. There is also a very handy cash point to the side of the shop. The two pubs either side of the apartment block offer food which again was a plus, together with a small cafe next door to the reception if you wanted a breakfast. I can honestly say having stayed in many so called 3 and 4 star hotels and apartments this definitely does what it says on the tin. So much so we are going to book again for May this year and stay 2 or three nights not for business purposes this time but for pleasure.

title: Adequate but not luxury!
text: We stayed here while my daughter was at the nearby hospital as price was reasonable. The apartment was clean but basic, not a luxury apartment as advertised. There were a couple of minor issues such as no plug in the kitchen sink making washing up difficult and a big crack in the bathroom sink. The shower was poor, Luke warm the first day and cold the second! The main issue was a health & safety issue, both windows in the apartment opened fully and as we were on the third floor this would be dangerous for children.

title: We enjoyed ourselves!
text: Are you on a budget and traveling to London? This is the BEST choice! Just a tunnel or bus ride up from the central heart of London you'll LOVE this area if you are an adventurer. It's a 2 minute walk to the tunnel and the bus is right there. TONS of shops are right out the door for supplies or restaurants. These spacious rooms add a nice place to relax. Most have a kitchen area. Is it a 5 star hotel? No...but we would never go any where else again! If you're super uptight then keep looking but I'll tell you by the looks of it, even the classic list of hotels looked shabby in comparison and feature TINY, tiny bedrooms without a kitchen. We had breakfast in our rooms and went out for dinner. We chatted around a bottle of wine and cheese and could play card games while taking a break. I loved the people at the desk and all of the near by places....I actually miss them...

title: Went for the Avios, but won't go back....
text: It's a little out of the way to start with, but that's no great shakes as it's easy to find from Kilburn Park station - out the station turn left walk straight up the road, crossover, next door to the gym down the side road by Tesco. I couldn't find this information anywhere I looked though, and I couldn't get through to reception. On arrival, I was given my room on the 3rd floor. It's not an inviting lobby and after dark when I got back, I didn't feel that safe. the room was very warm, so I had to sleep with all the windows open, subsequently very loud. The kitchen was pretty sparse, no dishcloth, nothing to get the trays out of the oven. No wine glasses..... I DO know hardship

title: Friendly Helpful Staff
text: Turned down the first apartment on the 1st floor that we were given, terrible smell of takeaway food coming through the window. Asked for a high floor apartment, as I'd originally asked for when booking. This proved no problem for Radville, the desk manager on duty. Check-in was smooth and simple. Our new apartment was very spacious and comfortable, the kitchen was well stocked with equipment, the bedroom was large and clean, as was the bathroom, although there was a noticeable lack of sink plugs in the bathroom and kitchen. Our stay was very comfortable, despite the dubious looking young women that visited the building, not quite knowing the way to "their own" rooms........ Good area for reasonably priced eateries, the apartments sit right above a Tesco, very handy for a morning danish, newspaper etc! Public transport was very handy, with an overground station just a minutes walk away and an underground around 7 minutes away aswell as plenty of buses. A good array of shops up Kilburn High Road took care of a rainy afternoon. All in all we had a good stay, but I don't know if I'd rush back, as the apartments seemed a little on the seedy side.

title: HUGE
text: Stayed here after the Marriott down the street and actually had a better experience overall even though the quality was way lower I booked a $185 rate which I saw later increased to $800+ in the day (!) They put me in a huge 2 bedroom apartment The carpet was stained and worn and the couch could have used cleaning but otherwise the value was amazing Personally, I prefer stained carpet and a huge apartment to clean new carpet and tiny London-standard room The front desk girl was very, very nice Location is also great If you're not too uppity and can deal with worn furnishings, I highly recommend this place

title: If you're happy with very basic, this is it.
text: We booked a 'luxury' apartment & although we weren't expecting 5 stars we were horrified to be led to a basement apartment that smelt of damp. We had to repeatedly ask for basic items - eg: a fry-pan, plug for the sink, teatowels and to get the TV working. The kitchen/living room were REALLY TINY and the bedroom was huge and there were 2 bathrooms!!!! It wasn't fun eating breakfast looking out on people's dropped cigarette butts. There was no security so the place had to be completely locked when going out, thus the damp dank smell never left the place. We didn't feel comfortable sleeping with opened windows, but with no fans there was little choice. At least it was close to the tube & a bus stop - both very convenient.

title: Luxury?????????????????
text: Advertised as luxury apartments So Quartier must have misunderstood the word. The carpets are absolutely threadbare and very badly stained. The blinds in the apartment were bent and twisted and there is no shaver point in the bathrooms! What hotel / apartment does not have a shaver point in the bathroom ??? Our request for a non smoking bedroom was ignored as the room 412 wreaked of tobacco> Whilst the staff are pleasant enough it is obvious that any issues raised have been heard before as they are met with a wearied expression of 'I know , I know, you're not the first and won't be the last '

title: The absolute filthiest hotel I have ever stayed
text: I have traveled a fair amount in my 47 years. I like to think that I have reasonable expectations. My travel experience has varied from budget to luxury depending on the occasion and our personal budget. We adust our expectations accordingly. In otherwords don't stay at a Days Inn and expect J.W. Marriott ammenties. However, common expectations of all hotels regardless of budget would be cleanliness and in good repair. This hotel was truly the dirtiest room I have ever stayed. My wife and I were traveling Europe for two weeks. We had reservations in London for 2 nights at a sister property the So Sienna, which apon arrival informed us that the had a bad electrical short and moved us to the So Quartier. They said it would be an equal or better grade room! The carpet was so dirty my wife or I would not take off our shoes or flip flops to walk around. Additionally the carpent was completely worn out. The furniture too was unattractive and in need of replacement. our matress was so uncomfortable, it was like a poor grade, worn out futton matress. The accomodations were so bad, that we left our second night with no refund or reimbursement. It was that gross. We have never, ever left a hotel before. Save your money and stay somewhere else. I don't know why anyone would stay in this area anyway, unless it's a matter of cost, but there is a Quality Hotel across the street that seems much cleaner.

title: Not 4*!
text: Advertised as luxury - certainly not. Only positive was the bathroom - very clean and 4*! Rest of apartment only 2*, floor filthy, broken blinds etc. good location though. Close to underground. Staff friendly.

title: It is what it is
text: I did not pay for this hotel stay so I am not sure how much the rates are. I paid the rate for a mother hotel that had to transfer us here because the room was "out of order' (see my review for So Sienna for details). The staff at the desk when we arrived at the So Quartier were friendly enough, but distracted. I think they were in the middle of a shift change and the phone was ringing. The space inside the lobby was very crowded and not at all welcoming - it was very dark. When I placed my luggage on the floor at the end of the desk I was startled by someone sitting in the darkened room just past the desk. She was on her phone and appeared to maybe be a staff member waiting for her ride at the end of her shift. I waited patiently until the clerk was off the phone )she did greet me right away though - so I was not irritated by the wait) and gave her our name. She seemed a little disorganized, as I said before, and it took her a long time to prep our room keys and complete the paperwork. Once in the room though, the real disappointment began. the room was very large - I was impressed by that. And the kitchen was adequate. But the furniture was lacking. The pull out sofa was already pulled out and made up which was helpful but there was only one small TV on the wall with unsightly cables running down to a DVR player that took some time to figure out. That was okay though for us, as we really didn't have a lot of time planned for the room anyway - but the bedroom had no TV...just the connections. And no furniture other then the bed, a desk built into the wall and a white plastic folding chair that felt too flimsy to sit in. The bed was very firm and the next day I had a very bad backache as a result. After a few hours of walking around and ibuprofen though, it loosened up and it was not a problem the day after that for some reason. The bathroom though....there was NO counter space. And with four people sharing ONE bathroom...this was going to be a problem. There was a sink, a tub/shower, and a toilet. There was a medicine cabinet above the sink that did provide SOME storage space. The shower curtain was moldy along the bottom edge and from the shower you could see the top of the medicine cabinet...and the little slivers of left over soap that had been left there to...I guess melt? The hot water lasted about 35 seconds before running out to luke warm and there was no water pressure to speak of. The shower head looked okay, but just did not provide the power needed. For four people, even staggering our showers out, it meant two people would be taking cold showers. Our stay was only two nights, so we did not say anything. I'm not sure how the hotel would have responded. The room was noisy, both from the pub across the street (we were on the third floor of four) but also from the family staying in the room at the end of the hall. Not everyone travels well, or quietly. The room upstairs provided some noise as well our second evening there from an over-amorous couple, but quieted down rather quickly. Overall, you have to know what you are getting with this type of hotel. London is an expensive city to visit, but it is one of the greatest cities in the world. To visit on o budget you have to be willing to accept some lack of luxury. I would not likely stay here again, but would considered their sister property, the So Sienna.

title: So-So So Quartier.....
text: Myself and 10 friends stayed in two apartments for a hen party. First impressions were nice modern spacious apartments but both had hideous rotten suage smells and on close inspection were quite dirty and obviously uncleaned from the previous guests. Once we'd overcome those issues, we were horrified to find that one apartment had no hot water!!!!!! Reception quickly sent somebody to fix it, but they couldn't....so offered us a different smaller room which was too late anyway as the hen party was in full swing. The beds were comfortable, kitchen well stocked and bathroom modern. Location good access for central London. Good price when split between a few of you....otherwise probably not.

title: Cheap, convenient, no frills
text: Stayed here at the weekend. We weren't after anything fancy and this suited our needs. The location was very handy for both the underground and overground. There was a Tesco Express and a cash machine underneath the apartments, which again was very handy! We had booked a two bedroom apartment with sofa bed- one of the bedrooms was really just part of the living area partitioned off with sliding doors. This didn't bother us but I expect it might some people. The apartment was clean but showed signs of wear and tear. Our apartment didn't have a kettle and the TV didn't work. However, when we mentioned this to the reception they came and fixed it straight away and brought up a kettle. The cooking facilities were limited- only one very small pan and there were no cloths or sponges to wash up with. We booked at a really good rate and didn't plan to be in the apartment much so it was fine for us and we had a great weekend. I would recommend for groups of friends after something cheap and handy. If you're after something more luxurious then I wouldn't necessarily recommend these apartments for you.

title: just ok
text: Wasn't really impressed with this place. Only stayed for one night to go to a show in London and then on to Brighton next day. We arrived at 2pm, pulled up outside to ask where we could park? Receptionist, although friendly was not really that helpful? Their car park was full and so were spaces at the back of the apartments? Finally found a space a few streets away but as we're not from the area had no idea if we had to pay to park there or not? Told receptionist what the sign said, she had no idea either?? Asked a local who assured us it was free at weekends. Apartment was clean but very small and very basic and furniture had seen better days. Living area consisted of a single bed, a kitchenette, a table and 3 chairs and a TV that you couldn't really watch as it kept freezing?? There was also no complimentary tea/coffee supplied but we had brought our own, unfortunately no cutlery anywhere ?? So made drinks but couldn't stir them ?? The bedroom had a double bed a side table with lamp and wardrobe, only one mirror in the whole place above bathroom basin. Our bedroom overlooked the pub next door and the busy high street so was very noisy well into the night and ambulance sirens going off continually. There is a Starbucks and a Tesco next door which is convenient. It's not a very nice area, lots of run down, boarded up shop fronts and dirty high street. We stayed here because it was close to Abbey Road, on our list of places to visit and it was just a short taxi ride to the West End to see a show, It was ok for one night, although not cheap! £165 for a one bed apartment for one night! Considering the next night we stayed at The Grand Hotel Brighton which was complete luxury and had 2 rooms including breakfast for £198, it was definitely not worth the money. I would not stay here again and wouldn't recommend - sorry

title: Great accommodation!!
text: We have stayed at So London Apartments in March for 4 nights. Lounge room and bathroom were so spacious and heater worked so well (helped us a lot as it was snowing!), we loved it! For the price we paid (70 pounds per night - Rates to Go), it was amazing, almost like too good to be true. As the previous review, there are many shops around the place, it took only 5 min from the station, everything was quite convenient. The receptionist was really nice. She always told us the way to get to anywhere. As I read so many helpful reviews from tripadvisor before we went on holiday, I'd like to recommend this apartment without any hesitation!

title: Lovely apartment, great location!
text: We stayed here as a group of 3 for a weekend trip to visit family. Having read the reviews I was a little worried but I am so pleased we chose this place! We had a one bedroom apartment (No.213 one double and one pull out bed) which was clean and spacious and had everything we needed for a 2 night stay - cutlery, plates, glasses pots and pans included - although some wine glasses would have been nice! it seemed to have been recently decorated, or well cared for. There is an overground station a 30 second walk from the apartment which was great for us going to Euston - only 2 stops, and a Tesco express underneath which was handy for carrying things back. Most of the staff seemed friendly. The only downside is that someone (probably housekeeping) had been in our room during the day and left the door wide open behind them, which was quite worrying. All in all was a great stay and I'd definitely come back next time I'm in London.

title: Fled After Check-In
text: I should have known there was going to be a problem when the National Express--an airport-to-hotel bus service--never heard of the So Quartiers and did not travel there. The tube ride from Heathrow is long! The address, as others have noted, is not accurate. The hotel entrance is not located on the Kilburn High Rd, but on an alley of the main drag. It sits above a Tesco market. My "luxury" one-bedroom was, in a word, depressing. One opens the door to an enclosed space with three more doors--one to the br, one to the bath and one to the lr/kitchen. The doors would not stay open by themselves, so any room one entered would be an enclosed and stifling space. It all looked clean, and there is a flat-screen tv and free wi-fi--both nice amenities, but this hotel is far from central London. It is in what I would call a "transitional neighborhood"--lots of empty store fronts and "going-out-of-business" signs in others

title: Large rooms, nice location
text: Even if I live in London...I had to find out a temporary place. I was impress from the size of the apartment and everything new refurbish!! The staff is friendly and the areas clean. Most of the hotel in central London, they don't have such large rooms!The location is very good because with one bus only, in 15-20 minutes you are in Marble Arch! Internet is complementary. The price is still ok....flat for 2 will be around 100 GBP per night. I always recommend this place to friends and tourist.

title: not 4 star
text: really not impressed with this, boiler made so much noise it woke me up, matteress very hard and could feel the springs,all very shabby. on the plus it was clean! dont bother going lady in reception kept spraying air freasener around the guests, not pleasent and rude

title: Avoid like the plague!!!!!
text: Double booked us and refused to give refund!!! Finally did through badgering MD. Totally ruined my handicapped brothers birthday weekend as we got back at 11.30 only to find nowhere to stay. Booked through booking.com and they were equally unimpressed with the hotel. Horrendous experience with equally horrendous receptionist who refused to contact a duty manager. Compensation offered was 15% off another stay!!! Fawlty Towers moment. Avoid, avoid, avoid.

title: Reasonable value for money
text: We stayed here for four nights in June, 2011. I had spent considerable time searching for a place in central London for our trip. My criteria were: family friendly (we have two kids), close to underground, relatively spacious accommodation

title: Just average
text: I stayed here three nights with my wife and 8 month old son. After reading the reviews I knew that we would either have a pleasant stay or unpleasant stay. As it turned it out, it was not bad but just average. We stayed in apartment 411, which was quite fine, clean and quiet. However, I could see that other apartments may not be so fortunate. What really stood out was that this place could be nicer if they cared enough to make an investment to provide a better experience. The plates, utensils and kitchenware provided were a mixed match of styles and nothing uniform. The bathroom could have some extra amenities that would make a positive difference. One can feel that the owners just provided the bare minimum and nothing more. As for location, the local neighborhood is nothing spectacular but does provide the shops needed to stock your apartment. It´s not a neighborhood that you will want to spend much time in but the plus is the access to the tube station and buses. Paddington Station is three stops away. I do want to recognize the friendly staff, who try their best. As for a baby cot, we called ahead to reserve one and also ask for a quiet room. We got the quiet room but upon arrival were informed all baby cots were taken. They found another one in the basement--fortunately...otherwise it could have been a real nightmare. BTW: Although the Wifi access is free, it was not always reliable. I would say if you choose to stay here...it´s a gamble what you may get and thus i really understand why the reviews are so mixed.

title: Felt like home
text: Apartment The apartment was very nice, clean and spaceous. It was very warm and cozy although it was snowing heavily. The decoration was lovely and the kitchen was new, well equipped and very practical. The stuff was more than helpfull. Generally speaking, it felt like home and and all that for about 68 pounds per night /per room cause I got a special offer. Up to 90 euros pn/pr I stay there anytime without doing any more hotel searching. Location It is not very far from the center and the tube station is nearby but you have to use two lines for most of the popular destinations and if you want to go out for a drink late at night then you will need to take a taxi on your way back.

title: Would rather have paid that little extra and stayed somewhere else.
text: Very tired and basic apartment looking nothing like the advertised on Hoteldirect.com. Wallpaper ripped and peeling, stained carpets, missing lamps and broken blinds. Beds are uncomfortable and someone had smoked in the room previous. We asked for a hair dryer and they sent up a broken one which was obvious from the plug. The entire building is in need of a major redecoration. It is pretty much a hike also to and from central London - no immediate tube - overhead to Euston. Buses are frequent but please get an oyster card otherwise it will soon become expensive. Taxi even more so. Tesco direct is underneath and whilst we stayed a major refurb was underway - drilling at 04:30am. A lot of money spent. Wouldn't stay again if the last place on earth.

title: Nice accommodation, good value for money
text: We ended up in this serviced self-catering accommodation having been double booked into So Paddington. Leaving the double booking aside, I have to say that this was a great place to stay. Lots of space in the room and upon arrival we found that everything was clean and in place. We were based in Central London but were able to get to/from this accommodation in less than 30 minutes on the tube so convenient also. A good range of shops including a Tesco Express underneath to collect supplies was also useful. Only downside was that we had to wait for 5 minutes at reception on arrival for anyone to turn up but credit to Ashlee on the front desk who was very helpful indeed and very friendly. We would certainly stay here again despite it not having been our original first choice.

title: Avoid at all costs!
text: Wow! This place is a shocker! It's very Noisy, the staff are rude, incompetent and a disgrace to the service industry. I would NOT recommend this place to anyone if you want somewhere friendly, clean and professional. This business is neither of these and it's a disgrace for the price you pay. The staff were shocking, it's a miracle any of them work in an industry that is supposed to welcome guests and show a degree of proffesionalism. Avoid at all costs.

title: Rubbish place
text: That hotel was a the worst hotel I have ever been in my entire life! I think it doesn't worth 4 stars to rate. When I arrived to London I thought I can recharge my batteries but actually I couldn't because the bed was uncomfortable. Even when I wanted to dry my hair after shower, I found out it doesn't have any hair dryer. In addition, the floor was awful and it turned me off cause it was soooooo dirty. If I were you, I wouldn't book this disgusting and chaotic hotel. And please don't pay attention to that beautiful photos that had been taken in that hotel. That pics are taken for fooling you. So please don't book this terrible place and don't repeat my mistake!

title: HIDEOUS -DO NOT STAY HERE
text: Reading through the reviews I see that others also experienced what happened to us. We were told our apartment was not available whilst we were on the way to them - their attempts to contact us were pitiful. We were sent to Shepherds Bush which was close to useless as we wanted to be near Wembley hence booking Kilburn. I tried to speak to the sender of the email on the telephone but was brushed off and left with the receptionist. The attitude of the employees was disgusting for a company charging £225 for a night. Upon arrival at Shepherds Bush we met 2 girls who had also been bumped from Kiburn and they had had to wait 4 hours for someone to let them in to their apartment........ Once inside the apartment building we were disgusted at light fittings hanging out of walls, stains on the carpets, an empty water bottle on the floor - I could go on. I am not sure what the company understands by the word luxury but it is certainly not the same as mine. The whole outfit is shoddy, unprofessional and blatantly a rip off. Do not even consider using them. If I was allowed to give them a minus rating I would but you have to give a score.

title: Quirky and relaxed
text: We visited the hotel whilst visiting London to watch a gig at electric Brixton and we were not disappointed. The parking was hard to find on the sat nav but once at the hotel we were pleasantly surprised by the beautiful decor and theme. Staff were helpful and the room was perfect. The bed was comfy and the honesty bar full of good quality alcohol. Everywhere was clean and the complementary green and black chocolate delicious! Thanks for a lovely stay and we will be back 😊

title: Beautiful stay
text: I was looking round all these different websites for a decent hotel to stay in for a night and was almost at the brink of giving in to Premier Inn, Ibis or Travelodge, which isn't great if you're celebrating an anniversary. Found this place on lastminute.com and when I looked at the rooms I thought to myself it couldn't be real! But I fell in love through the pictures and when forwarding the details onto my better half, we needed to book it! We got ourselves the Superior King Size double standard room. The receptionist was friendly when she greeted us and helped us find our room as well as the living space where they had a huge selection of DVDs and complimentary teas. There are so many corridors it's easy to find yourself lost and trying to remember the painting on the wall that was near your room, which is all part of the fun. The room was beautiful. A little bit smaller than we thought, but beautiful nonetheless. It was clean, the chocolates and books were a lovely little touch and the toiletries were really cool. I admired the tiling in the bathroom, the way the room was painted and the soft lighting. We both live in a noisy area so we didn't feel it was noisy during our stay. The location is a bit strange and hard to find if you don't know which direction you're going in, but the buses that ran through went through Central London which is convenient. Only thing stopping me from giving it a full 5 is I think there was a loose wire in the DVD player so we couldn't get to watch any film properly. But, this isn't a hotel you should be comparing to with other ones, you found this one, you go here and you won't regret it

title: Soul, colour and warmth in a london hotel!
text: A splash of latino colour in the drab world of mid price london hotels. Quirky and beautiful. Well worth venturing off the tube map.

title: Hot Sauce Wow
text: I was a bit apprehensive on getting the taxi from waterloo whre my friends where staying not knowing what to expect but when i got there how my thoughts changed i was greeted with a quirky reception and a friendly receptionist who put me at ease ,i was even offered if i wanted my bag carried up to my room a nice touch ,when got to my room that too had loads of character may be a bit bright but loved it ,the bed was really comfy i had a great quiet sleep ,nice and quiet ,then instead of the usual tea/coffee which was free anyway downstairs ,there was a small hot sauce and some chocolate just something really different i loved my stay and would definatley recommend a stay couples would love the cosiness of the whole room excellent !!

title: Characterful hotel with excellent food
text: We booked several rooms for a wedding party and there was a bit of a glitch with the booking, but the owner worked to sort this out quickly to everyone's satisfaction. Rooms are lovely, very different from the bog standard rooms of a chain. Standard rooms quite small, however. Breakfast is superb, good continental with lovely smoothies, cereals, eggs etc. for a very reasonable £5 and cooked breakfasts at reasonable prices. Everything is home made, not bought in. Some of our party also ate there in the evening and thoroughly enjoyed the tapas. Very friendly, helpful staff. No tea/coffee making in the rooms but a very comfortable lounge open 24 hours with complimentary DIY fresh ground coffee, a wide selection of teas and an honesty bar for alcohol. There are several storeys and no lift, so if the stairs might be a problem, ask about this when booking - staff happy to help with bags. Would have given top rating except for the mix-up, although this got sorted, and the stairs. Everything else excellent, would happily stay again.

title: A unique hotel with lots of personal touches
text: I stayed here last October as I was celebrating my 30th birthday in Camberwell - it was a wonderful experience from start to finish. The rooms are spacious and comfortable, with lots of colourful flourishes and personal touches. They come with free L'Occitane toiletries, chocolate, notepads and chilli sauce made in-house! There is a well-stocked honesty bar (and freezer for late night ice-cream cravings!), and a great breakfast with Monmouth coffee and lots of local produce. The reception staff were super helpful and friendly, and we were able to store our bags at the hotel until we had to catch our train. The only downside is that there is some noise from the busy road outside but, overall, this is a real hidden gem and makes a change from soulless chain hotels.

title: Warmth
text: Despite looking very average from the outside as the Tapas Bar is not open at present, the desk service in the evening and morning was very welcoming/ The free drink and DVD facilities were also shown and the arrangement was laid back. Room was a bit tight but well provided for including organic chocolate! Great to have solid pillows and a firm mattress. More than made up for the view of wasteland out the back (temporary it has to be said)! I'd certainly recommend it to anyone. Buses straight to KX and Esuton

title: Best Hotel to find in London!!!
text: We stayed there for 4 nights and had a real great time there. Really clean rooms, very good breakfasts, and a phenomenal Angels & Gypsies restaurant around the corner. The staff was extremly friendly and helpful. If we will come back to London one day, we surely book the Church Street Hotel again!

title: Fantastic service
text: The Church Street Hotel is located between Clapham and Brixton and easy to find by bus from Waterloo (how I arrived) and car (how he arrived). Camberwell isn't a beautiful area but we if you're looking for somewhere of good value to check out the London sites, this is it. The bedroom was cosy (but not small) with flat screen TV and great shower. We didn't have the breakfast but made use of the extensive DVD library and now regret we didn't make use of the bar....where you can practice your Tom Cruise cocktail shaking to make your own drinks. The best thing about this hotel was the service. I left a pair of earrings in the room and they called to tell me the day after I left. They then posted the earrings to me all packaged up free of charge. They arrived 2 days later.....fantastic! I'd definitely recommend this hotel. My advice...get a paper from the shop across the road and sit on a bus for the half hour ride to the London Eye and South Bank and enjoy the fact you haven't spent all your budget on accommodation!

title: Brilliant
text: Stayed here on Sunday 26th as my husband had an appointment at King's Hospital at 9am and we couldn't face the commuter train. What a gem we have found. Immaculately clean rooms, gorgeous linen and soft, large towels. Honesty bar with complimentary tea and coffee is a gem and the pastries were delicious. Will return.

title: Good but not great
text: We stayed at the CST for one night and have decided it was ok. Good things: the complimentary bits are nice, hotel looks nice from outside, room size good. Bad things: lumpy uncomfortable pillows, shower could do with an update, so many stairs and most importantly, no drinks-making facilities in the room. This makes no sense to me, as first thing when we woke up all we wanted was a cup of tea in our bed clothes. The hotel should provision for both in-room and lounge-area drinks. The cost seemed pricey too. Also 2 further things that have resulted in this ranking. One is that when we left for the night reception asked that we leave the key with them.... I have never heard of that before! Seemed very odd! The other is that the staff could be more willing in terms of offering to phone a taxi for you... They weren't particularly hot on customer service.

title: This hotel is a must visit for a quirky delightful experience!
text: From the outside it doesn't look much, but inside you come into a Mexican / Spanish experience, with Mexican religious artifacts everywhere, from paintings to stained glass. The service was excellent and all the staff friendly. Quite the best breakfast I have ever had, and the evening meal was very well presented and excellent too. Although the building has an old world charm it was spotlessly clean. You must visit the Communion Bar in the basement - with the illuminated stained glass even on the front of the bar, depicting bible stories - and the cocktails were superb!

title: Church Street Style
text: Really loved the style of this hotel. South American Catholic. Rather like something from Madonna's "Like a prayer" video. Rooms are small but perfectly formed and brilliantly styled. Web site is a perfect presentaion of the hotel. There is also an honesty bar in the hotel so you can get a beer whenever. Breakfast was simple but good. This hotel was a great surprise and we would definitely recommend it.

title: Quirky.
text: Booked this place off of the back of other reviews, and, to be honest, was not at all disappointed. A quirky well run hotel located in a busy vibrant area of London. Well located for the city and West End, and surrounded by great local bars, pubs and restaurants. A very decent find indeed.

title: Lovely unique hotel
text: We stayed at the Church Street hotel while visiting friends in the local area. The main positives are (1) it's unique and has a lot of character, (2) the staff are very friendly and helpful, (3) it is very clean, (4) breakfast with fresh pastries was good, and (4) there are a few nice pubs and restaurants in the local area but it's also very easy to get into town by bus. The only negatives are that the road is very busy and we struggled to sleep with the noise of the traffic and sirens.

title: Visited four times
text: A quirky and interesting hotel, comfortable with lovely friendly staff. Ask for a top floor room to minimise noise. There is a continental breakfast which is fine. My first two weekend stays were even better as the restaurant was open. Cooked breakfasts and tapas meals were delicious so I didn't bother looking for a meal elsewhere. Not sure why it is shut, but hope for future guests it re-opens soon. Would certainly recommend it.

title: A real city break hotel
text: An interesting hotel near Camberwell Green that provides good value for money by London standards. We were upgraded to a room at the rear of the property at no extra cost. This meant we were not subject to traffic noise from the main road, which on a Saturday night was frequently used by police and ambulances with sirens. The room was quite large and nicely decorated. The en-suite was rather tight but with all you would require including body was and shampoo. A nice touch is the two complementary chocolate bars. Breakfast is a communal affair with tables arranged in two rows. This was rather hectic as most people staying at the hotel chose to have breakfast at the same time! However service was friendly and the continental breakfast more than adequate, chunky toast, boiled eggs and french pastries with a selection of jams. The only minor point is that the rooms do not have tea facilities these have to be accessed from the honesty bar but once breakfast service has started this is not very convenient for an early morning cupper.

title: once upon a time.........
text: i have'nt seen this hotel,although i have been travel in the whole Europe.this is a wonderful time in my life and i want to come here again and again. i want to tell everybody about its facilities and services.I like the cleanness of the hotel. The staff was very friendly and helpful. please come here once and feel the adventurous trip.

title: So friendly and helpful staff
text: They could not do enough to make us feel welcome . The unlimited tea and coffee and honesty bar wonderful... Such a treat although we did not need it. But late at night to have a cup of tea and a pastry .... Delightful. Could not fault the room, so much better than chain hotel. Just need to be able to do stairs... But our room was quiet at the top of the house.

title: A little "carrot" in the heart of Camberwell
text: Stayed for 2 nights while attending a conference at Kings College. Ideal location, fab rooms, helpful, friendly staff. Nice extra touches in the rooms and plenty of places for food and drink nearby. Didn't have breakfast but colleagues said very good. Would consider staying here when visiting London despite being further out of City.

title: Terrific out-of-the-way boutique hotel
text: You have to know your way around London to get there but its worth the trip. All the desk staff are terrific, very helpful, and genuinely nice people. Good breakfast- lovely fresh breads. Very comfortable rooms, wonderful decor, quiet if requested. Nice safe neighborhood with fruit stand across the street. Restaurant next door has great food but is super noisy.

title: Nice Hotel with charm
text: The Hotel is very clean and cozy and has a lot of charm. The Breakfast was very good and is served courteous. I would book this hotel again for a short stay in London either for business or leisure. There seem to be a lot of nice restaurants around but I did not have a chance to try one.

title: Really original and quirky. Great change...
text: Really original and quirky. Great change from corporate hotel UK. Love the complementary chocolate and hot sauce. Food in the new restaurant downstairs is fantastic too.

title: Different and nice...
text: Very good rates, excellent continental breakfast, nice decoration and atmosphere. Nice pubs around. Not luxury but comfortable and sympathetic service. No elevators. Good location close to centre and public transport.

title: Quirky, but great
text: A great hotel if you are looking for something a bit different to the run-of-the-mill premier lodge offering. This place has character in spades: My room was bright red and had some really "interesting" art on the walls! It was a bit small, but the bed was comfy and it was quiet. Thanks for the Green & Blacks chocs and the pot of Papa's Hot Sauce! Would stay here again to try out the honesty bar as I didn't get a chance before. Right in the middle of loads of shops and amenities, so very handy too.

title: Really nice hotel
text: We arrived late for a brief one night stay. Our daughter was in labor as we arrived from US and wanted us out of the house! (Baby born while we slept.) In spite of the hour (11pm), the clerk was cheerful and helpful. The room was large and had wifi (since our UK phones were not active, this was very helpful to find out that the baby had been born so we could go back to our daughter's house!). The bed was solid. The bathroom was huge! We did not use the tub/shower but everything was clean and the towels were soft and fluffy. Each room is different and the decorations are different in each one. The room had everything one expects from a hotel and more! The next morning, we ate breakfast at the restuarant downstairs which had a nice cold breakfast for 5 pounds and hot breakfast for 9 pounds. We were able to top up our phones and take the bus home rested and refreshed.

title: Great hotel! Well worth the journey
text: I spotted this hotel 2 years ago and hadn't had chance to use it but I am so glad I have finally stayed there. Beautifully decorated eclectic hotel with great service and attention to detail. I stayed with my husband for our 15th wedding anniversary and it was fantastic. Room spotless, breakfast great so much better than a chain hotel In central London. Thank-you. Also made me use the London buses on my travel card instead of the tube and it is so much better.

title: A little gem in south london
text: i stayed at the churchstreet Hotel for 6 nights and was thrilled from the cleanliness, comfort and uniqueness. Everythink appears just as beautiful in front of you as shown on the website with a cheeky-mexican flair and a lovely eye for detail in decoration and room arrangement. The set up of the breakfast room was charming and cozy.The buffet(is included) comprised healthy choices of organic based food and the breakfast Lady's have been very relaxed and helpful. I stayed for a further education course and it was always superb to be welcomed by the friendly staff and the most impeccable clean room with little choci bars and home made chilly sauce as a treat.L'Occitane toiletries with an enticing scent and the very fluffy Bed linen and towels don't let you cool either. The honesty bar on the second floor turns out to be a good concept too, since you have the opportunity to make yourself drinks with putting name and room number down, another plus for having trust in your guests and reinforces that feeling of being home once again. Wifi is for free by the way. The nice corresponding restaurant next to the Hotel the 'Gypsies & Angels' has to offer a superb assortment of food and wine and as soon as you walk into the Restaurant you feel transferred into a latin atmosphere with it's interior, decoration, concept of food and wine(Tapas, sherrys, south-american wine). Location might make you a bit insecure, especially if you never have been to camberwell and don't know what to expect but this is just initially and dwindles away as soon as you walk through the part and you're interested in people and different cultures who retaining their roots which looks like a big battle of colours if you see the afro african people running around in their traditional costumes. Good puplic transport to the city is provided which takes you max. 20 min. to get to london bridge. All in all the Hotel offers superb value for money and i've been a bit around. i'd say that the concept is perfect and you would not regret it. it is also not easy to find Establisments with such an enthusiastic Team of Staff members who all very knowledgeable, so warm hearted and who are expressing their personalities in a way which is delightfull and not over the top or fake. Just very warm and open paired with knowledge is unbeatable. My next trip to london is soon approaching and the church street hotel can certainly count on me that i will be back.

title: Quirky and friendly
text: I stayed for two nights at the Church Street Hotel and found the accommodation to be just what I had expected. There is no tea or coffee in he room but it is available in the bar for free and is far higher quality than you would normally get. There is an honesty bar and DVDs available for the rooms. My only complaint was the floor above was so loud and woke us up at 6am on the second night but it's an old building and as long as you can deal with that its not a problem. If I visited again I would use this hotel for sure!

title: Characterful!
text: Our second stay here- its a bit of a rabbit warren, lots of stairs, takes a bit of practise not to get lost, but friendly, warm & clean. Oliver F complains about the noise which was true on our first visit, but the room we had has now been fitted with secondary double glazing and its a huge difference- mind you as we used to live nearby maybe we are used to London traffic noise.

title: Unique hotel- ideal location for kings college hospital
text: We had to stay near kings college hospital and we found this beautiful hotel on the hospital accommodation list. The room was light and airy - bright and cheery. The complimentary chocolates and water obviously went down well!! The honesty bar was great idea- meant that we could have free tea/coffee 24/7 and also alcoholic or soft drinks as we pleased. Breakfast was simple but lovely- huge pastries which were lovely. Service was lovely at breakfast and from reception staff- was lovely to be taken up to our room on arrival rather than just being directed. As we had hospital appointment at 12.30- we were really appreciative of a late check out that we weren't charged for. Additional bonus is free DVD hire- we didnt use but lovely idea. I'Occitane toiletries were nice too - would definitely recommend

title: Saturday stay before the London Marathin
text: Room was clean but bed was uncomfortable, washbasin was cracked & wallcovering needed attention. Good shower & L'Occitane toiletries. The highly rated( 10/10 Times reviewer) cooked & continental breakfast was disappointing - the only cooked items being very hard boiled eggs & DIY toast. Staff were pleasant, welcoming & helpful but our stay was definitely not worth £135 - suspect prices were hiked because of the marathon. Not too much disturbance from street noise but creaking floorboards above & outside the room combined with the uncomfortable bed didn't make for a restful night.

title: Lovely place
text: I love the theme of this hotel. We had a top floor room so had to climb many stairs to get to it. The room was lovely with complimentary bottled water, chocolate and a jar of chilli. Would recommend to anyone wanting to stay in the area. We had a lovely visit.

title: South American charm
text: What a surprise in the middle of Camberwell! A very charming little hotel, friendly if a bit like a Rabbit warren. The room was very clean and well maintained. There was even a couple of bars of high quality chocolate and a sample of their own hot sauce to take away. The bed could have been a little more comfortable but for 1 night it was fine. Just up the stairs a little is an open lounge where guests were encouraged to help themselves to the fresh coffee and tea. There are pastries and alcoholic beverages available too which are paid for using an honesty box system. An extensive array of DVDs available in the lounge, just choose a title and take it down to reception for them to give you the actual DVD to play in the room. All in all a very pleasant stay, and very handy for Kings College Hospital. We will be using again when we're in London to watch a show.

title: My new favourite hotel in London
text: I stayed at the CST last night and it was fantastic. Superb service, great food (all sourced from quality producers), great atmosphere and lovely rooms with funky decor. The complimentary hot sauce and Green and Blacks chocolate is a fab touch. The L'Occitaine toiletries demonstrate the understated quality of the place.There is a relaxed atmosphere, which makes a pleasant change, and the honesty bar is an automatic winner with me! I have stayed in many hotels, for work, and this is my new number one which I will selfishly keep a secret! I was upgraded to a deluxe room which came as a lovely surprise. If you like something a bit different then you can't go wrong with the CST. I will be returning very soon.

title: A little Gem
text: Wasn't quite sure on arrival. There for two nights on business. A hotel that has a quirky identity, one that it struggles with, I couldn't quite figure it out! The facilities are basic, book a room with an en suite. Breakfast is fantastic and so too the tapas in the next door/connected establishment. Staff are very friendly. Prices are good too. Will stay again for sure!

title: A great place
text: We booked this in January this year with very short notice and we couldn't believe our luck. Its a great place for a flexible London holiday - 24 hour access, with access to an honesty bar in their beautiful dining room. It was and exciting place to stay - it has the character of a small family run hotel with modern comforts and a blend of aesthetics. We felt very well looked after while also totally independent. Will definitely stay again. Thanks!

title: One of the best hotels we have stayed in
text: We stayed here one Saturday night while helping our daughter settle in to a new home nearby. The hotel has a Spanish theme and is full of intricate and interesting decor and artwork. There is a lot of attention to detail. Our room was excellent with welcome extras that make the difference - facecloths, bottled water, a fan (no air con) and organic chocolate. The reception staff were extremely friendly and helpful. The hotel has an adjoining Spanish restaurant which was wonderful. It also has a private lounge where guests can have free tea/coffee and a honesty book for alcoholic drinks. Breakfast was a delicious organic selection of cereals, pastries, boiled eggs and jams. Parking at weekends is on street with no restrictions and we were able to park in a side road a short walk from the hotel. There is an excellent pub over the road. The area itself is not exactly salubrious but we cannot fault the hotel.

title: Fantastic Boutique Hotel
text: I can't say enough about this little hotel. I stopped in a single en suite room 11. The service and staff are fantastic. The decor is homely and very cool. It feels like a home from home. I love the little touches like chocolate in the room and free teas and coffees in the library. Really nice touches. The breakfast in the morning was a delight. I invited my daughter and her boyfriends as I was visiting them at Uni and paid £5 each for a lovely continental breakfast each. The sour dough toast was so yummy as was the home made porridge and preserves. Sadly we suffered an incident and my daughters boyfriend badly hurt his foot and I needed to get back to Lancashire. Even though we had checked out of the hotel were fantastic and so helpful in our hour of need. I arranged it so we could email our new train tickets to them and they printed them off. I can't say enough good things about Church street hotel except for I am coming back again on 15th June. if you want a friendly welcoming experience in London 30 mins from all major attractions and you want to pay half the price of the big hotels then give Church Street hotel a try. I won't be stopping anywhere else in London. Also top tip the Grand Union pub round the corner does the most amazing burgers with sweet potato chips at very reasonable prices.

title: Perfect
text: With Brixton Academy a short £5/6 Uber ride away this was the perfect location for me and my wife to stay after a concert, when checking in we were welcomed by a really friendly woman who made us feel at home straight away. Really nice clean hotel quirky decor, nice small details from a small jar of home made hot sauce to complimentary chocolate. Free fast WiFi, good breakfast couldn’t ask for more. The next time we’re staying in the area we won’t even look elsewhere we know where we’ll be staying! Very impressed.

title: Just what we needed a perfect distraction!
text: Our single night stay at the Church Street Hotel was due to a close family member being treated at Kings College Hospital so our stay was rushed and a hotel was urgently required. After searching for hotels close to KCH (within walking distance) this popped up and we booked it not knowing the style/theme of the place, but it provided the perfect distraction from the reason we were in London. Although it was slightly more expense that what we wanted to spend we had no other option. The moment we arrived at reception the staff were very helpful and friendly. Not knowing the area very well at all the parking provided by the hotel at St Marys church (a 5min walk) was great value and the car was safe and secure off the road. The room was warm cosy and the bed was surprisingly comfortable. The bathroom was clean & the L'occitane toiletries were a pleasure, i suppose the only issue with the room was the bath being a bit small but then i am 6ft 3ins tall. The food in the restaurant was fantastic, healthy and great value with 10% discount as we were staying & the honesty bar had a wide selection of branded spirits which my fiance and i enjoyed in the evening after visiting hours were up. Plus free tea and coffee which was a really nice touch. All in all it was a great stay and I'd recommend to anyone.

title: Surprised
text: Stayed locally many times and this place is the best by far. Ok, you will get lost on the myriad of staircases, and maybe the bathroom could do with a bit of TLC(room 13).Overall though, a lovely place to stay. Usual London mix of restaurants in the area from kebab/chicken/pizza places to upper end dining. Transport to central London will always involve a bus journey, unless you get a cab or like walking. Very comfortable and excellent staff. Would not have a problem recommending this hotel.

title: Perfect, very friendly
text: The staff is wonderful, I loved the honesty bar, the decoration...

title: Fun, individual hotel.
text: Good value boutique hotel, friendly staff, lovely rooms and the tapas next door is definitely recommended! Would happily go back again. The honesty bar is a nice touch & the nearby parking is handy too.

title: Charming hotel with friendly staff, unique rooms and relaxed atmosphere
text: I decided on Church Street hotel in the first instance for its relatively close proximity to Brixton Academy. The phographs of the hotel looked interesting and quirky (in a good way) and were a good representation of the room we stayed in. The room was clean and comfortable. I particularly liked the bright coloured tiled bathroom and recessed alcoves. The staff were very friendly and the continental breakfast included organic cereals, delicious local jams and pastries and a vast range of teas. A nice touch was an extensive DVD library that all guests had access to if desired. Would definitely return to this hotel as it was a great base, particularly for Brixton Academy. A unique find.

title: Quality
text: Pros - location, near to lots of shops and 10 minutes walk from the station - clean - decor - friendly staff - reasonably priced - facilities Cons - bit of a trek from Central London Overall a very nice hotel with interesting decor. Bar and resteraunt downstairs make it a perfect place to stay for a few days. I stayed in a room with a shared bathroom which was clean and never seemed to be in use. Recommend.

title: Wonderful stay
text: Church street is a wonderful hotel in London. Rooms are big and confortable, bathroom is fantastic, the breakfast was really good and the location was perfect, with nice reastaurants and bars within a walking distance and only 15 minutes by bus to waterloo tube station
