title: Good value stay in central London
text: We just needed a place to stay for one night in London, and we wanted something near the Kings Cross Station as we needed to take train the next morning. The fact that the bathrooms and toilets are communal did make me hesitate to stay here at first, but as it was just for one night, the price was inclusive of cooked breakfasts and the triple room was available, I decided to go for Passfield Hall. The rooms are clean, and very spacious for London standards, and the location is very central and boasts great transport links as it is within 10 to 15-minute walk from Euston, Kings Cross, Goodge Street and Warren Street stations, the British Library, and the British Museum. Showers and toilets are functional but nothing fancy as it is used as student hall of residence. There was plenty to choose from in breakfast options - you are allowed to choose seven items in addition to coffee/juice, such as bacon, eggs, tomatoes, baked beans, yoghurt, toasts, cereal, etc etc, and when all was added, it provided filling start to the day. There are too many shabby, run-down, and extremely cramped hotel rooms in London, and I think Passfield Hall is a sensible choice for people who want clean and efficient rooms in central location in London but do not mind the issue of shared bathroom too much.

title: A good no-frills option
text: The location is superb, very close to Euston Station and British Library, plus it's a pleasant walk to the British Musuem and even Covent Garden. The building is one of a row of stately Georgian terrarces surrounding a shady square. The area is quiet and there are no nightspots nor busy traffic (but not many good pubs or shops either). A room with breakfast this close to the West End at this price is a bargain. The rooms themselves are spartan with absolutely no 'extras': no telly, no phone, no kettle. Just a bed or two, a desk, wardrobe and sink. Toilets and private showers down the hall are basic but clean, plenty of hot water. We were invited to drop our bags off before the room was ready on arrival, plus could leave our heavy bags behind the next day after checking out. Breakfast in the self-serve cafeteria is hearty, but again nothing fancy. You are allowed generous portions of cereal, fruit, toast, bacon and all the other usual fare. Windows only open an inch or two and the rooms can be very warm on the south side in summer (no A/C or fans). When we first stepped into our room there was a damp smell and on returning late that evening we noticed a wet spot in the carpet (a leaking pipe?). It was too late to move rooms that time of night. It does feel like going back to uni all over again (some of the students don't leave, so you might be rubbing elbows with them in the common areas). The carpets are tired, the decor is plain, but you're not here for your honeymoon!

title: This is a dump
text: I was booked into this dump by an employer. Peeling wallpaper, damp stains on the ceiling, carpets so stained that who had to wear shoes at all times and terrible shared shower and toilets. This property is sub standard student accommodation that reflects badly on the LSE and Tripadvisor who apparently gave it some sort of award. I strongly advise any visitor to London to steer well clear of this appalling dump. However the staff were pleasant.

title: It's like being in high school again.
text: The only that is good about this place is the location. It's close to about three different Metro stations. The hall itself is in need of a bit of a revamp. Water doesn't clear properly in the showers so they flood as you're showering, toilets don't flush properly and the carpets, well, they cleaned them while I was here but I think that just made them muddier because it didn't dry quick enough. The laundry facilities were quite dirty. There's no AC (not even a fan) in the rooms which can make some summer nights quite unbearable. Kitchen facilities are available but the condition of the utensils is not good. The communal bar fridges tends to be too full and I don't think there is communal crockery. Breakfast is included. It's a decent selection of hot and cold foods but it's very much like a high school cafeteria in atmosphere. Rooms are very well equipped with furniture which probably reflects that the hall is normally a student residence. The hall isn't in a particularly noisy area, unless guests start to congregate in droves (in excess of ten persons) outside your window till 3am in the morning. Noise is quite significant under those conditions because the windows can't be shut because that is the sole source of airflow. I recommend bringing a pair of ear plugs.

title: Excellent value
text: This is a great place to stay if you only need somewhere to put your head down for a few nights. Stayed 2 nights in a single room - nice staff, place is clean, the bed comfortable, decent breakfast and, above everything - amazing location. You're within walking distance of Oxford Street and with great transport links nearby to get you anywhere you need to go. And for £40/night. Could not fault it for what it is, would definitely stay again.

title: Good Budget Option If Available
text: My wife & I just spent a weekend at Passfield Hall, and doubt if we could have found better accommodation in London for anywhere near this price. Everywhere, from the rooms, communal areas like showers, and the dining areas were clean and well maintained. The showers were good, and there was always plenty hot water, and clean towels provided. The choice and quality of the breakfast was good with more than enough selection of both cooked items and cereals/fruit etc to suit us. They do get a bit off if you dont take all your breakfast items at once. The location is great too - handy for Euston, Euston Square, Russell Square and not too far from Kings Cross - plus the many restaurants in the area, and attractions such as the British Museum and Foundling Museum. If you don't mind the fact that rooms are not en suite, don't have double beds or televisions this is great accommodation at a great price.

title: Great budget place
text: Stayed in a single room for one night with shared facilities (bathroom and kitchen) in early July, 2018. Pros: Conveniently located next to two Underground stations (Euston and Euston Square, depending on the line that you want to take) Clean shower stalls and toilets Cheap (I booked around a month beforehand and it cost me around £51) Buffet breakfast with sufficient choices Towels and basic toiletries provided Cons: Dirty stained carpet (remember to wear shoes/slippers) Window can only be opened slightly and the hot weather wasn't helping either Broken fan (only a small breeze came out from the sides!) Wifi is free but slightly slow Would recommend, especially to solo travellers.

title: Perfect for our needs: affordable, safe, convenient, clean and wifi!
text: I found out about booking university rooms by total accident. I am so glad I did. Our accommodations were awesome for our needs. We felt secure and safe. The room and bathrooms were clean and tidy. The staff was friendly and helpful. Our breakfast was an added perk, that we would not have gotten with any similarly economic options. We were in a great launching point to see the sites, being so close to many bus stops and Euston Station. We were also within walking distance to many sites, most exciting to me, The British Museum. We plan to return in the next year or two, and LSE Vacations is where we hope to book!

title: Fresh brewed coffee for breakfast
text: That was really great: Freshly brewed coffee for breakfast instead of machine stuff. The room was a bit worn and my stay would have been most enjoyable had I known the advice I give at the end (i.e. garden side). The staff was polite and helpful, even giving ideas for future stays in town. A Boris bike station close by with easy access to the sights around (get yourself the newest "cycling in Central London" and docking stations maps before going bonkers in the oneway system). The WLAN was free at my stay though the registration process was a bit cumbersome. Worth a try.

title: Love it!
text: I have stayed here a number of times over several years. Rooms are basic, compact, clean. Cost is affordable, staff is helpful, breakfast is tasty and generous. Refurbishment 3 years ago installed reliable lift, although it moved the laundry to an annex and wiped out ironing boards, but maintained a basic kitchen on each floor for stashing in refrig, boiling water for coffee, etc. Locale is so convenient for me, with bus just 2-1/2 blocks away and perfect for where I want to go most, tube about 5. Delis, restaurants, shops, post office and internet cafe within 5 blocks. I'm always on working vacation. The one thing that ticked me off this time was that in contrast to 2 years ago, internet has just one computer at one pound per 20 minutes, w/queues forming

title: ONE OF THE WORST
text: One of the worst accommodation I have ever stayed. This place needs to change the carpets they have also breakfast is awful. Everything is cold even if the duration is 2 hours(8 am-10am). Also the staff is very rude, once I forgot my key, the receptionist is like going to kill me for that. I’m a human-being I can forget my keys right?

title: Excellent location, good breafast
text: This is student accommodation and so don't expect luxury, but for the price I paid and for the location, I was very pleased. The check-in was easy, I had a large ground floor bedroom with ensuite shower room. It was clean and functional. No luxuries like a TV or even a bedside light, but if all you want for the night is a bed in a great location, look no further. The breakfast was especially good, huge choice, proper coffee machine and all included, this was far better than I have had in many much more expensive hotels.

title: Not for me
text: Stayed here overnight recently. For the price I paid, I wasn't expecting The Ritz but, even though it was only a place to sleep for one night, it was still pretty disappointing. Entry to the place is through an office/reception area. Staff I dealt with there were pleasant enough, but you almost feel that they still think they're dealing with the young students from the term time lets, and not paying overnight customers. I was on the top floor (4th) of one of the 2 annexe buildings with no lift. I was given directions on how to get there, but it was a bit of a job finding it. Once inside, the stairs were really narrow and steep. On our floor there were 2 rooms, a kitchen area and a shared bathroom. The bathroom was pretty big with a decent sized shower, but you had to keep turning the water back on as it went off every 30 secs or so. There was nowhere to put your clothes either. The rooms were basic. Really basic. No tv or aircon or even double glazed windows! The breakfast wasn't the best either. And they weren't exactly polite when asking for your breakfast card. Breakfast consisted of Some cheap and nasty cereals, some tinned grapefruit segments, a massive bowl of yoghurt to help yourself to and a cooked selection, but you can only choose 6 items. Fried eggs were overcooked, beans were cold, bacon and sausages pretty dried out. There was some bread and a toast machine to make toast, but you'll need to put it through around 3 times if you don't want just warm bread. I only booked here because everywhere else seemed really expensive to what i would normally expect to pay - even the Travelodge's were asking over £140 for that night. I don't think I'd stay again.

title: Bargain gem in central London
text: The high points - location location location, extremely friendly & helpful staff, and great price. Rooms are spartan but comfortable, breakfast is plentiful but uninspired. Access to a kitchen is great - microwave, stove, kettle. All in all, this is the perfect place to stay for those who enjoy simple things and don't need to be pampered. Only down side- the limited available dates they offer rooms to the public.

title: Brilliant for a Budget!
text: This accommodation is in a fantastic location, a very easy walk from either Euston or St Pancras. I stayed in a single room with a shared bathroom, and cannot fault the value. The room was simple but clean, with a lovely view and everything I could have needed, including a sink in the room itself. The bathrooms were also well-kept and I didn't once see anybody else whilst I was using them - although my one complaint is that the nearest bathroom was quite a distance from my room! The staff were friendly and very helpful, and a cooked breakfast was included - all in all, excellent value accommodation and I would stay here again!

title: Amazing location for a budget stay, with a great breakfast buffet
text: This is a budget accommodation in a university housing facility. As such, you should expect the amenities to be humble and modest, and to share space with large groups of (often noisy) students. But if you're fine with that, this is an amazing deal in a perfect location (just minutes from Euston and St Pancras stations, making it easily accessible to the airports). The British Museum and Petrie Egyptian Museum are within easy walking distance, as are tons of other museums, cafes, pubs, pretty much anything you want. And the breakfast buffet is really, really good, too! For the money, this is one of the best budget deals I've found in London. I wouldn't really recommend it for couples looking for a romantic setting, though.

title: Good value! Bring your earplugs....
text: These dorms are a good bet if you don’t mind a college dorm experience. Our corner room w/two beds was the largest college dorm I’ve seen – has a wardrobe w/drawers, desk and sink. Because a double room was not available one night we were there, we had two single rooms and they are SMALL. It did have a sink & the standard wardrobe & desk, but the room is very small. There are a few things to know: Phones: Each room has one phone per bed, but in order to use them you need to purchase a LSE phone card. I attempted to do this each of the 5 nights we were there, but they never had any. If people need to contact you at the LSE, they need to know your room number as there is an automatic system that requires an extension. Alternatively, there is a phone booth a few steps away from the entrance to the right across the street. I had no trouble using a calling card from the US. Wireless: none. Starbuck’s a block & a half away. I'd like to see them charge a bit more to cover the cost of having wireless. The lack of wireless is a deal breaker for me. Internet café: a few blocks away - ask staff for directions. Computer w/Internet: one in the dining hall. Cost is 1 pound for 30 minutes Noise: bring your ear plugs. The door slamming is amazing

title: Long weekend
text: I've just had a long weekend in London to watch the Rugby League Challenge Cup Final with some friends. One of the other guys booked it for us on a budget as we needed nothing special and I was therefore expecting a real no frills accommodation. Well I must say I was pleasantly surprised

title: Great Place for a Base!
text: I stayed here while in London sitting exams and was pleasantly surprised. It’s a short walk from Euston Station and the British Museum, it’s clean and comfortable and I felt very secure. And it was a fraction of the cost of a hotel in peak holiday season!

title: Good and nice location
text: I stayed here for 9 nights. My room was very small but clean and the bed was fairly comfortable. Breakfast was great. For the price I was paying, I couldn't ask for better food. The staff was friendly. I was told that if I used their postcard, the staff would mail it for free, so I wrote one and gave it to the staff. No sure what happened to it as my friend never received my card. The bathroom and shower could be kept in a better condition. The light bulb in the toilet near my room went dead the second day I got there and no one replaced it for the entire time I was there. And the sink was not working in a different place and no one fixed it even on the day of my departure. Someone put up a note which says that it would be fixed soon but nothing happened. Of the entire time I was there, I did not once a staff person cleaning the facilities. Do they expect the guests to do all the cleaning? Even though there are signs everywhere telling guests to keep these facilities clean, but after all, some staff member should clean the showers and the toilet regularly. Very often, you find these facilities such a mess, as not everyone has the same habit. Every toilet has a sign telling the guests to put the trash in the trash bin but not every toilet has one. What are supposed to do?If no one cleans these places, you should tell the guests that no one will do the cleaning, so we do keep walking into such a mess and keep hoping that someone is going to do some clean. If you are not a picky person and can put up with sharing not well-kept bathrooms, then I would stay here. The location is great. By the way, what happened to the TV remote? Did anyone take it?

title: Great Location & Breakfast
text: Stayed here last Saturday night for one night stay. Hotel is across the road from Euston station so location is great. Staff very helpful. However, stayed on the the first floor whose toilets and showere were out of order due to construction work, meaning you had to use the shared facilities on either the ground or second floor. Also, my window wouldn't close which in the City means you hear everything. Having said that, the price of staying is really cheap and ideal if you plan to be out and about all day. And the breakfasts served were great. This is the second LSE property that I've stayed in and I would stay again but would maybe contact them in advance to ensure the bathrooms were in working order on the floor you are staying on.

title: Solid Stay
text: My sister and I stayed here for two nights in a room with two twin beds (no en suite). The rooms were MUCH bigger than any of my college dorm rooms. The sinks in the room are great. Bathrooms down the hall are small and co-ed. The shower doors lock (again, an upgrade from my own recent college experience). We arrived prior to the official check in time so left our luggage in an unlocked, unattended luggage room. The room was very crowded and luggage was piled high. There should be a better system in place for early arrivals if the room is ready. Breakfast was great - there is a limit to how much you can take from certain categories of food - but it was very filling and there was a good variety. I am gluten free and asked for assistance choosing food. The kitchen staff were not knowledgeable but then the head chef walked me through everything and read labels on all - including the canned tomatoes. Bravo! No major complaints about our stay (other than the luggage room - but nothing was taken). The hotel was a solid stay. We chose it based on its price and location to the Eurostar station for a very early train out to Paris. St. Pancras and metro stations are very close by and we felt safe walking around the area after dark.

title: Bargain Price In A Good Location.
text: We had difficulty finding it in the first place as it's just a small plaque saying LSE Passfield Hall, not in any way like a hotel sign (which it isn't of course). We were on the second floor at the back of the building so was very quiet, except that the radiator made the most horrendous noise at about midnight on our first night there. It was actually turned off and I had to turn it on to stop the noise (which was like pneumatic drill). Consequently, for the rest of our stay, we had to leave the radiator on, which did make it a bit warm in the middle of the night. The room was quite large and basic with many stains on the carpet, which was a bit off putting but I don't think it was actually dirty, probably tea and coffee stains. Knowing what to expect, we took a travel kettle and some tea and coffee so could make ourselves a drink if required, I also took a hairdryer as they aren't provided either. The toilets and showers on our floor were closed, so we had to go either up or down a flight of stairs whenever we needed to 'go' which was a bit of a bind, but even having to 'double up' with the other floors, I only saw someone else on two occasions. The breakfast is superb and really set us up for the day. There are lots of buses into the West End, and it's a steady walk to Oxford Street. An absolute bargain if you're on a budget and we will definitely stay here the next time we visit London.

title: Terrible experience. Avoid at all costs.
text: Price seemed reasonable, perfect location, and nice pictures. Stayed for 8 nights and could not sleep at all. Being a student hall, I expected silent rooms to be able to study and rest, but I got coughing noises from the neighbor, the entrance doorbell, foot traffic by reception inside a room with a bed, desk and washbin. What they did not mention in the website at all is that windows don't shut properly, all the noise from the street comes in, as well as a nearby A/C unit which made it impossible to sleep. Staff at reception are not qualified to deal with customers or any issue outside standard check-in/check-out procedure. There is no elevator, so be sure to pack lightly or have someone carry your suitcases up the stairs..

title: Very basic student accommodation but cheap for London
text: We stayed overnight as we wanted to be close to London attractions. It's 45 years since I was in a Hall of Residence (University of Exeter) and I have to say my accommodation then was of a higher standard than Passfield Hall. I think the Travelodge would be a safer and more comfortable overnight stay than Passfield Hall, but at least they provide breakfast and a coffee or tea (if they have any mugs available and we had to share one!). Sorry, Passfield Hall, but you're OK for backpackers and students, but those of us wanting some creature comforts would want a little more.

title: Excellent accomodation, exceed my expectations!
text: My and my friend stayed in Passfield hall for 3 nights in July and one night in August. Our room was spacious with comfortable bed and the sink in our room made all the difference! We had to share the bathroom with 2 other guests, but the bathroom is just next to our room and is always clean. The neighbourhood is quiet at night, but only a short walk (about 5 minutes) from Euston Station, and it is safe and not scary for girls to walk at night. The breakfast is great, a range of food to choose from and the portion is enough to last until lunch or even tea time! REMEMBER to request a room on the ground floor if you are travelling with large luggages, me and my friend had to drag our luggages (30kg each!) to the 4th floor! Also, wifi is not free, had to queue up to use the computer in the dining room or pay for the wifi plan.

title: Fab accommodation for a good price
text: My husband, daughter and I stayed for 2 nights. Although the communal toilet and showers was a bit of a put off, the rest of the facilities are great. The breakfast was abundant and tasty. The games room was a definite hit, we played table tennis, table football and pool. We also had games of monololy, chess, draughts and dominoes. When you have a small child it's difficult entertaining them at night so this was a nice change. The rooms are big and the beds comfy. We were next door to the loos so that was fine. All in all a good deal. We'll be back.

title: Why pay more?
text: Passfield Hall was so hospitable - way more than I expected from what is a student hall most of the time. The bathrooms are shared but you get your own little set of free toiletries, clean towels, and there's coffee mugs in the kitchen. This was my first experience of shared-bathroom holiday accommodation and I was really impressed at the clean, quiet shower rooms and toilets. My bedroom was also generously sized, with a wash basin and writing desk, and as it was a hot August I appreciated the desk fan. You get 24 hour access to the building with your key card. There is also use of a luggage room, just ask at the front desk. That was very useful for me as it meant I didn't have to carry my bag around London on the last day of my trip. They do breakfast but I was too busy to try it. And oh yeah, the wifi's free and REALLY fast.

title: Will be back
text: This is basic clean accommodation, some rooms have shared bathroom and toilets (which are kept very clean) Reception staff excellent Rooms very comfortable To lift to third floor Breakfast was amazing and the choice fantastic Location central Thank you

title: Excellent value for money!
text: We stayed here for one night to attend 'Open Garden Squares' weekend. My review reflects the cost of £69.60 for two people including breakfast. The location is brilliant, just across the road from Euston Station. The rooms although sparse, as cited on its website, are spacious and clean and include towels, soap and free WiFi. We had a shared bathroom and despite many people staying there the bathroom was empty every time I wanted to use it. The shower was clean and hot with good water pressure. However I personally thought the bathroom facilities could do with a lick of paint to freshen them up. Breakfast was excellent and included all the items you'd expect for a full English including vegetarian sausages, cereals, fresh fruit, tinned fruit, yogurt, cheese, ham, pain au chocolat, croissants, toast, jam etc. There was coffee machine for a range of coffees and also regular filter coffee in a jug. Outside the dining room was a garden terrace where you could take your breakfast. Passfield Hall attracts a range of customers of different ages and we noticed single travellers, couples, families and larger groups. We stayed in an annex across the courtyard and noticed a launderette in a building which would be great if you were staying for a week. I would highly recommend this accommodation if you are looking for great value for money in a safe location. We will certainly be booking again and I would happily stay here if I travelled alone.

title: Ideal location for visiting the British Library on a budget
text: This is student accommodation and very basic. The single rooms have a bed, hand wash basin, wardrobe, desk and some drawers. The cost is exceptional low and only available in the vacations. My high rating is for value, not luxury. The reception appears to be staffed by students and the ones I met were cheerful and helpful. The breakfast was generous. It starts at 7.30am to 10am. and you select up to 6 items from the self service counter, plus any amount of coffee/tea and toast. Hot dishes such as sausages and bacon are available from about 7.45am. There are three floors with a lift up to floor 2. Each floor has a kitchen and bathrooms. It is about a ten minutes walk to the British Library and five to the Wellcome Institute.

title: Excellent for a cheap convenient stay in central London
text: The student rooms are clean and spacious (beds a bit hard an institutional). Brekky excellent, wifi fast, staff friendly. Will definitely book again if come through to St Pancras/Kings X - highly recommended of you want a reliable, clean, convenient stay at a great price which you'd be hard pushed to find elsewhere in London

title: Few faults - truly excellent !
text: Must concur entirely with recent reviewers ! - unfettered wifi access is needed if they're serious about marketing to non-student inmates - and so is a more user-friendly approach to running the evening bar and provision of meals, etc However, these are minor niggles - overall, cannot recommend this place too highly, for a pleasant, and inexpensive and exceedingly well-located stay in London Many thanks indeed, Passfield Hall !

title: Beautiful mature trees in the interior courtyard. Fairy lights at night!
text: This was the second time I stayed at LSE Passfield Hall, this time in the main building. I like the closeness to Euston station. I feel safe in this neighbourhood. I like being within walking distance of Covent Garden and the British Museum. Even Westminster is less than 1 hour walk away.I saw An American in Paris and felt reasonably safe walking briskly back alone after the performance. The reception staff are friendly and helpful. The shower rooms are clean. I don't like having to walk down the corridor for the toilet at night, but the inexpensive room price helps! I kept a small cloth wallet looped over my room door handle with my room key card in. It made it easy to remember to take it with me. The big breakfasts were varied and nicely cooked with medium quality ingredients. This is not the place to go to for outdoor bred specialty sausages.

title: A not unpleasant experience
text: Good for what you pay for considering its location, but be prepared for a different type of stay than your average B&B or hotel. For some reason I had in my head that the typical resident would be mature students and old professors, but it was obvious when I checked in that the oppsite was the case - I was back in student land! I stayed in student residencies in the 70's and this place had a certain amount of nostalgia. The room was basic with a single bed and a wash-hand basin and was amazingly quiet considering the age of my neighbours who must have been very well behaved. The showers and toilets were communal at the end of the corridor but were exceptionally clean. Towels and basic toiletries were provided. The piece de resistance was the breakfast. Refectory style, but superb quality which surpassed many many fry-ups I've had at more salubrious establishments. All in all good value for money and i would go again if in the area.

title: Great Fun !!
text: I truly enjoyed the 10 days I stayed at Passfield Hall. Staff was friendly and helpful. My room was small but comfortable. No problems sharing the bathrooms or showers. Only a two block walk to several bus routes. Met several amazing travelers from all over the world. And....had a great breakfast to start each and every day. Would definitely stay there again !!

title: Great place for a short stay!!
text: Hotel was perfect if you need to lay your head down for the night. I was only staying one night doubt I could have stayed longer. The room was very basic but catered to everything we needed. Only downsides were our room wasn't in the main building we spent 15 minutes luggin bags around and ended up not finding our room, we had to go all the way back to reception to get someone to show us to our room. It was difficult to find your way around, small corridors leading off into different areas. After a few hours though we knew where we were going. Beds were so cumfy had such a great nights sleep! Breakfast wasn't to my taste, tried the cooked breakfast and everything look uncooked. The pan au chocolat was nice and the coffee. Overall its ok for a short stop over but for a longer stay maybe invest in somewere better.

title: Awesome location and value
text: I would recommend this to just about anyone - it's a shame more hostels can't run themselves like a university dormitory! Passfield was clean, quiet and in an unbeatable location in Bloomsbury, very central to tube lines and London's attractions. The rooms are comfortable and the shared bathrooms are surprisingly private, with plenty of hot water to go around. The value is fantastic. All the double were booked so we took a triple and just didn't use the extra bed and it was STILL cheaper and nicer than anything else we looked at before booking. There is a breakfast every morning, and as a vegetarian I appreciated the fact that there was plenty for me to eat. Fruit and boxes of cereal are provided for those travelers who can't sit down for a full breakfast. My only complaints were that we got there early and had to store our luggage in a unused dorm room. It was packed with bags and it didn't seem particularly secure. There was also one grumpy desk person who wasn't very helpful when asked for directions or other help. These are really really small things in comparison to the complaints one could potentially have when staying in a hostel! I wish I could stay here every time I go to London!

title: worth its price!
text: Our double room with lavatory was big, the furniture rather old, but everything very clean. There were enough bathrooms in the hallway, so it was no problem having no private bath. Towels were exchanged regularly. We just loved to take the abundant breakfast (extremely friendly kitchen staff!) to the inner courtyard and eat there. The neigbourhood is pleasant and calm, Euston Station as well as several bus stops and tube stations are at walking distace (as well as the British Museum).

title: Great Value - Great Location - Good Breakfast - Bring Earplugs
text: My first trip to London on a serious budget. I got a single room. It was fairly clean but well worn. I did sleep under sheets I had packed and my sink and phone jack had issues while I was there. I was on the 4th floor which was fine for me

title: Good on the budget!
text: I was there between Sept 7 to 10. The experience of staying at LSE Passfield was generally positive. Like many who have reviewed, the breakfast was great and the location really good, since I was there to attend to my academic work at UCL. The only grouse i had was with the heat in the room. There was no ventilation (or fan) and the windows couldn't be opened beyond the 30cm gap, hence no way for the air outside to cool the room. Perhaps this would be ideal for late spring/winter situation where a warm room would be welcome.

title: Great location, great value.
text: Put aside any concerns you may have over Uni type accommodation. This is clean, well maintained accommodation in an excellent location, close to Euston station and in the lovely leafy Bloomsbury area. Staff are excellent and very helpful. Breakfast is buffet style though reasonably enough, given the low cost, you are limited to the number of cooked items that you can have. Unlimited toast, coffee, tea, juice though. If the weather is good, the dining room has a nice terrace leading off. So far I have gone only for a room with shared bathroom but have not found this a problem, never had to queue to shower. All rooms have a handbags in. The kitchens are well equipped with white goods though cutlery and crockery and pans limited. You can collect a mug, tea bags, coffee and sugar from reception for free so you can brew up any time.

title: Rund-down, smelly and only cold shower.
text: I didn't expect muh rom this accommodation as it was fairly cheap compare to other hotels in the area. I was however still taken aback by the rooms with tiny single student/children-style single beds, without even as much as a bedside lamp, a dated and worn equipment which would have resembled a dual-occupancy boarding school type of room. No TV, no fridge, nothing at all. The worst were the showers: Only cold water - and not because the water heater was defect but it only has a cold tab. The missing warm water is intentional! Simply below all acceptable standards at that price, I recommend looking somewhere else. I only award two points because it was reasonably priced.

title: Excellent location, awesome breakfasts and it's cheap! Good value for money!
text: We have stayed in a private twin room. It was spacious, clean and warm (been there in Jan 09). One of the shared showers had problems with hot water, the other was fine and ALWAYS had hot water in any quantity :) The location is superb, quiet and yet in the centre. But the best thing about this place are the breakfasts! Free breakfasts with great selection, really worth every penny.

title: Good value
text: Booked in for three nights. When I arrived they had put me on the 3rd floor but as the lift only goes up to the second I asked to change rooms. The helpful reception staff sorted this quickly and I was given a room on the ground floor opposite a shower. Room was a decent size, typical student accommodation, was clean and comfortable, Although no aircon (I was there on the three hottest days of the year) there was a fan in my room which was much appreciated. The shower was fine but the toilet didn't flush very easily so twice had to flush it again before I could use it. Room was cleaned and towels changed after two days so no complaints there. The breakfast was as good as some I've had in more expensive hotels and it set me up for the day. Had an afternoon free so sat in a deckchair in the enclosed garden under a tree and read my book - a relaxing space.The big plus for Passfield Hall is its location - close to the tube and bus routes - very convenient. It is what it is and represents excellent value for money.

title: Value for Money
text: The hostel is really good and is good value for money. It's walking distance from Euston and Euston Square station. It's really close to the Russel Square station too. There's a park with a Mahatma Gandhi Statue just opposite the park. It's a good option to stay.

title: Super value
text: What a find. Had three nights here with family - what a bargain. Staff were friendly - especially those downstairs on breakfast who were so nice. Room was good for pice we paid. Only issues were the heat - room was so hot and he fact no one changed towels or emptied bins the whole time. If it are driving parking is an issue plus it is in congestion zone. Would definitely stay again. Breakfast was delicious.

title: nice, clean and good location.
text: In general it is a good hotel with clean toilets, bathrooms, bedrooms and linens were changed regularly. Breakfast is also good, but it would be great if there could be more options. The room i stayed is facing the street, so it was a bit noisy and with some very energetic neighbours next door, i was woken up a few times in the middle of the night. May consider: - giving free wi-fi - giving free internet services - more change of towels instead of bed linen - providing regular dinner and lunch (not to be booked)

title: ask for low floor
text: I booked this room for location (near to Euston station for a 6am train) and budget/safety and on all those criteria it was fine. HOWEVER there was no alternative but to pay for a breakfast i couldn't have (I emailed asking for packed breakfast, simple breakfast available at 5.15 or a discount and none was possible.) My room was on the 4th floor up EIGHT flights of stairs with no lift and I had heavy luggage for an all-weather trip to Scotland. Use of a kitchen was allegedly included but that was on the second floor and i had to return to reception (stairs again) to get the kitchen coded onto my key: and then the fridge was switched off and there were no cups, or any other crockery - I'd brought tea bags and wanted to heat porridge in the morning but didn't bother in the end. My room was small and clean but half of the ceiling sloped right down (attic) . Tiny shower en suite- I'm a size 12. wouldn't fancy your chances at size 18! Toilet outside the bedroom door. My verdict: if I'm going by train to Scotland again I'll stay en route, not near Euston for the first train. Could have been worse, but I'm not doing this again.

title: Excellent budget accommodation....plus breakfast!
text: I have stayed here twice now and highly recommend it. Previously we have stayed in the Central Yha but Passfield is cheaper, has more space per room and includes a very good breakfast. The location is in Bayswater with 2 gardens opposite. It is a short walk from Euston or St Pancreas. Check in was friendly and efficient. We stayed in a triple room which was very spacious - three single beds, three wardrobes and three desks. The beds all had bedding which was fresh and the room was clean. The rooms have a wash basin but are not en suite. There are plenty of toilets and showers on each floor and we never had to queue and they were kept clean. There are kitchens but they are poorly equiped unlike the YHA ones. This was a disappontment as i was hoping to cook our own meals to save money. Just a kettle for a cuppa would be good, however i can imagine they may have had problems with people not clearing up after themselves. Loads of places to eat out in London though. A bonus for the summer is a garden out the back with tables and chairs. The breakfast is lovely. You are limited to 6 items but this is not a problem as it is a bonus to have it included. There are cooked items, cereals, yoghurts, muffins etc. Very good. It is student halls so don't expect any luxury but it is clean and spacious and a great location too.

title: Good Value
text: Staff on reception were helpful and friendly The rooms are clean warm and the bed is comfortable. It was warm so i had the window open and there was some road noise No TV or Internet but if you want a cheap basic room in a good location for Kings Cross, St Pancras or Euston stations then i can reccomend Passfield Hall I had to be up early so cannot comment on the breakfast.

title: Economic & Location
text: Situated very close to both London Euston and Euston Square Stations, LSE Passfield Hall is a good choice for travelling in / out of London. The Rooms and the Breakfast was very good and the shared toilets/showers are sufficient and very well maintained.

title: Good value, but know ahead what you're getting
text: I stayed one night at Passfield Hall, choosing it because of its proximity to Euston Station. I paid 38 pounds for a simple, perfectly acceptable single room with ensuite shower. I had requested a quiet room on an upper floor. I got the top floor, but there was no elevator - older, less able customers should beware the stairs. Check-in went smoothly, the student part-timers on the desk were polite, friendly and efficient. Hot water was fine, and the toilet was conveniently located right outside the door. My student neighbour returned at 11:00 PM and though she wasn't particularly noisy, the paper-thin walls meant I could hear every noise of her attempted seduction of a classmate. I had a B&B package but as my train to Glasgow was at 5:30 AM, I had to sacrifice breakfast. The location is great, shops and pubs minutes away. I spent the night watching football in a cosy little place round the corner from Russell Square underground. It is not for those looking for frills or who want great service. I'd go back, for the price, the location, the lack of hassle. If you pack earplugs, you'll be fine.

title: Value for Money
text: Only paid £30 per night so in the middle of London this was cheap. Shared showers and toilets. Not very comfortable, the bed I had felt like it was almost worn down to the springs and the blanket was barely big enough to me. The breakfast offered a decent range was hot( I had one at 9.40 and one at 7.45)

title: Do not stay here under any circumstance!
text: OMG we had nothing but problems with this place. Check in was at 3 and we arrived at 3:30 to get our room. We had just got into London after traveling and flying for 24 hours. All I wanted to do was get into my room and take a shower. They said our room was ready and gave us our keys. We get up to the 3rd floor where our room was and it was a disaster zone. I was in utter shock. I have never seen such a mess. I really should have taken pictures for you all to see but I was in such shock I didn't think of it. Cleaning supplies, dirty rags, dirty paper towels, and all sorts of other garbage and half eaten food products were strewn all over the place in the hallway and in my room! The door to my room was wide open and the mess was all over the floor in my room. Dirt and hairs were on the desks in my room. The mirrors and sink were disgusting. All 3 mattresses were up in the air on their sides and out of their bed frames. No sheets or towels or anything were on them. It was literally a disaster zone. And this was supposed to be where I was staying. I immediately went back down to the desk again, hauling all my luggage down 3 or 4 flights of stairs again because the lifts don't go all the way up to the 3rd floor. I was really upset and there happened to be a long queue I had to wait in again to tell the staff about this situation. By the time they finally got around to me it was probably close to 4 and they said they would have the cleaning staff do my room right away. I asked if I could just switch to a different room but they said all rooms were already assigned. I said "why can't you just assign me to a room that is ready that belongs to someone else who hasn't checked in yet? And then when that person comes hours from now they can have the room I was supposed to have since it will be clean then?" You would think this would be a simple concept but it was not for the staff at this place. They eventually gave me a key to a room on the first floor. I thought this would be my new room but I think they thought it would only be a temporary room. I go to that room and a man is in the hallway and is like "what are you doing trying to enter that room? That's my room!". So ugh, they gave me a room that someone else was already checked into! I go back to the desk again and am clearly frustrated. They walkie talkie the cleaning staff and tell them to clean up our original room right away. We just had to sit there and wait. We were supposed to be able to get into that room an hour earlier but they were not ready for us. They wouldn't give us another triple room that was already cleaned and that no one had checked into. They just made us wait and wait and wait. When we finally did go back up to the 3rd floor our room was moderately clean, but the hallway was still a mess. It was very awkward walking to the shower in the hallway past all the male cleaning workers. I felt disgusted with my room the whole stay, having seen what it had looked like just a short while before. Also, we were supposed to have a triple room for only two people. We should have been given 3 breakfast vouchers since the room was for 3 people but they only gave us 2 vouchers. They limit you on the amount of breakfast food you get per voucher. It would have been nice to have the extra voucher that we paid for since we could have got more food at breakfast then. Or they should have given us some money back. I would stay away from this place if I were you. The staff is incompetent. They were unapologetic about the check-in situation. I tried to be nice to them and understanding and they never even said "sorry". They didn't offer a refund or anything. At the very least they should have gave us some money back after this whole ordeal, especially since we were only 2 people and had to pay for 3 people to stay in this crappy room. Stay far away from Passfield Hall! Also, I am willing to be contacted if the hotel would like to give us a refund still!

title: Passfield Hall is great!
text: I recently stayed at passfield hall for a week with my sisters. We got a triple room that was clean and comfortable - (remember these are dorm rooms) at a great price. The breakfast is fantastic, the service (from front desk to kitchen hall) was professional) and the location can't be beat. It's quiet and safe which are key for me. They provide maps with bus routes and food/restaurant locations - you are right by the tube or numerous buses that cater to tourist sites (the 14 and 24). There is a little garden in the back to have tea and read - and laundry and kitchen facilities. We used the shared bathroom in the hall - but it was always well serviced and clean. If you need a place to stay while sightseeing in London - this is a great place. In my travels I've stayed at a variety of 4 star hotels and all types of hostels and passfield hall was a great find! I would definitely go back and would recommend it to all!

title: Good for a short stay
text: This is basically a student dorm, and as a student myself I find this a good accommodation for me! I've spent two nights here. There is a bit of a draft in the room but I didn't mind this. Toilets were always clean which was nice. Nice breakfast but very bad coffee, but that's just me :)

title: A good stay for the price
text: Ideal location for me and the service on front desk and in refectory was good. I particularly liked being able to obtain free tea/coffee/milk from reception.

title: Great location and value!
text: The rooms were what you expect for a dorm -- bigger than we thought they'd be. Location is great -- two tube stops just a couple of blocks away (Euston Square and Euston), and Russell Square is pretty close too. There are three buildings, we stayed there at both the beginning and end of our trip, once at Tavistock (no elevator, beware) and Passfield. It caters to a younger crowd so as you'd expect there was some late night noise, though much less than a much more expensive hotel in Bath we stayed at too. Dorm food breakfast had lots of choices

title: great location great price
text: we asked for a room on the ground floor as we were bringing my mum who is 83 our room was overlooking the back but the other room was facing the road as the windows had to be left open all nite it can be noisey. Great location and a great breaksfast - staff were nice -

title: Good value for money!
text: I've stayed in both Twin Room and Single Room during my trip in London. The Twin Room was big comparing to a normal B&B room, but the Single Room was just fit. Anyway, both rooms were neat. For the breakfast, it's quite good with enough choices. The only problem was one of the staff serving the breakfast was a bit rude. One suggestion for adding more value to young travellers like us, please provide free internet connection, either via wifi or cable. It's a very common facility in hostels nowadays.

title: Absolutely terrific.
text: One of my favorite accommodations ever. If you're looking for luxury, you obviously need to search elsewhere, but for the price this exceeded all my expectations and hopes. The location is ideal, overlooking Tavistock Square, and really just a street or 2 from both Euston and Euston Square tube stations. Plus, there's a 24-hour Portland's (convenience store) three blocks away or so, in case you're lacking any essentials. It's a safe neighborhood, with plenty of attractions, restaurants and lovely places to walk. Plus, having a sink in the room was really neat. I would absolutely time my future visits to coincide with LSE student holidays so I can stay at Passfield again.

title: Better than average Hostel accommodation
text: As long as you understand and accept its student hostel accommodation you won't be disappointed and it has a lot going for it! Rooms are perfectly adequate, with working heating, opening windows, desk, wardrobe etc - only drawback might be a very poor mattress comfort-wise but it's not purporting to be a Premier Inn. It is in a quieter part of Euston/Kings Cross and you feel pretty safe in the surrounding streets. The building security is positive too and there is 24 hr reception. Free wi-fi, decent breakfast, decent showers, kitchen facilities, and a games area/tv room make up the positives. For £35/£45 a night if you don't want or need the frills it's good value for money.

title: Hidden but central place, good value for money
text: It was not a piece of cake to find this hotel. It is in fact a central one (close to the Euston railwaystation) but without a proper map and during night you can have a serious problem. So study your way in advance. Other LSE places is much easier to find. My room was tidy and small, but with a comfortable bed and pleasant room temperature. The night was quiet and I slept really well. Breakfast was served in a basement, containing cereals, full English style breakfast, milk, juice, fruits and tea. I liked the view from a dining hall to a backyard with big maples. The only shortcoming of the stay were separate toilets and showers, but they were quite clean (toilets cleaner than showers, take your flip-flops to the shower). Overall, no doubt good value for money, but I have slept in better LSE hotels yet.

title: Nice and comfortable place. Good value for money
text: My boyfriend and I stayed at Passfield Hall in September 2011 for 4 nights. It is a nice and cheap accomodation, very convenient in my opinion. The most important thing to say is that the room was large and clean, and the shower and the toilet were clean, too

title: Nice place, terrible staff
text: The college has been refurbished and it's nice. Good breakfast and good location are the best features. But if you are in need of anything, cross your fingers! My experience was bad. The male staff was useless and very lazy. There were four toilets near my room. The first was closed (Why? They didn't know!). The second was dirty and awful. They promised to clean it. Their way of cleaning it was: stick a piece of paper on the door saying: "Do not enter!". In the third one the light was off, and it remained off during all my stay. So there was only a toilet for a lot of rooms. Please, refuse if they give you the 109 room: it's hotter than all the others (remember that in the college you can't open the windows if not for ten centimeters, no matter the weather outside)

title: Cheap, clean small rooms
text: Booked a cheap single room, and that's what I got. The rooms are clean, and the hotel is ideally located for Kings Cross, and going into the west end. Not the fanciest of accomodation, but if you're after a place to lay your head, then this works great. The toilets / showers are shared but clean

title: Very Friendly and Clean Place to Stay
text: I have stayed at Passfield twice, and both times found the staff and check-in process very friendly and co-operative. Rooms, toilets and showers are very clean

title: Great Location, Well Above Average, Secure
text: I have just returned from a eleven night stay at Passfield Hall, London. This was an excellent base for me as I did daily train travel in and out of London. It is a seven minute walk to Euston Station, here you can catch the underground or trains. Most important issue for me when booking was the security. I give this 100%. Every hall is electronically keyed, as was each room, kitchen, computer room, laundry room and main entrance door. The room was comfortable, good size, clean except for slightly soiled carpet, daily towel change. The mattress could have been a better quality though. Also had a telephone that could be used with phone cards, a wash basin and a window that I could open as I was on the 1st floor and felt safe with it kept open as it openened from the top. Having a computer room was great. Although only three were working when I was there. The breakfast was excellent, many choices and I noticed that most "tourist" were able to make sandwiches for their lunches and take a piece of fruit. Many healthy choices available. I did not use the TV lounge, it seemed their was always sports being watched. Huge TV screen. Did laundry which was great and not too expensive. Staff helpful and pleasant. Easy check-in and departure. Offered to call the cab. Great having the kitchen on each floor. Nothing of mine was taken from the fridge except my milk. You must date and put your name on ll items in fridge. There is a Tesco Express opposite the Russel Square Underground. All train stations have a Marks and Spencers with ready made meals that can be heated in micro. Overall, WELL ABOVE AVERAGE

title: Excellent value for money with a central location
text: We stayed here for one night in December 2011. The rooms are relatively basic, but comfortable. The twin room was very spacious and contained a sink. Towels and soap were provided and their was plenty of tourist information in the reception of the hall. The bathrooms were down the corridor, but were clean enought and there was also a kitchen where you could make hot drinks and snacks. The breakfast was a highlight of the stay. Plenty of food with a wide choice from hot or cold breakfast items along with as much tea/coffee as you like. In some places in London you'd almost pay more for a breakfast like this than we did for the room!! The position of the hall was excellent. We could walk to pretty much everywhere we needed to go. It is based in a nice area, which felt safe to walk back to at night and is only a few minutes away from the nearest tube stop. I think that the website makes it clear that it is a student hall of residence and not a hotel, therefore as long as you don't expect luxury then I think this is a great place to stay. I will definitely be staying again and would recommend it to friends and family without hesitation.

title: Perfect for the weekend!
text: I went to London as a group of 4 and stayed here in two twins for the night and it was perfect! The service was friendly and helpful, especially for clueless 18 year olds, the rooms were big and spacious, very light and the toilet facilities were adequate (I'm told the shower is good too). It was also surprisingly peaceful for so close to the centre of London, so sleep was great on comfy beds. The breakfast was amazingly huge, didn't manage to finish with full English, unlimited toast and tea, but the best part of this place is the location, 5 minute walk from Euston meaning you can get anywhere quickly. There are lovely, affordable restaurants nearby and you are a short tube ride from...well everything! :D Oh and they have a luggage room so you can leave your things there instead of dragging them around London so you can go home that night! Fab! Would highly recommend and will definitely use this next time I do a trip like this!

title: Inexpensive and very central
text: Myself and friends stayed at lse halls of residence August Bank holiday for 2 nights.. staff are so helpful.. as you can imagine it's basic but very clean and friendly staff.. and close to the heart of London... comes with a full cooked breakfast.. absolute bargin.. This was my 5th year of staying there..

title: Very very poor!!!!
text: I were there for 03 nights(17-20 april 2015) Room not in main Building No Lift Poor Breakfast( max 06 items!!!) In the room dirty carpet and very dirty Tapestry on chair!!!! In 3 days never one time a hot water for a shower!!! My first and my last time here!!! Probably right for very young people!! I don't suggest it!

title: I've stayed twice
text: I've stayed twice, my first in a single and second in a double. My first impressions were good as it is very close to the centre of London and a 5 minute walk from Euston station. The front of the building is nice and the neighbourhood is also pleasant. Reception staff were friendly enough although they are clearly not hotel staff (remembering that this is a university accommodation!). The first stay was certainly better as it was in the front building and on the first floor. However, on my second visit I had to weave through the first building, up and down stairs, across the courtyard and to the second building, up stairs to the second floor. If you tire easily, beware! The rooms are very basic. My first stay had a floor-length window with a view of the park which was nice. The windows aren't the newest so you can hear outside clearly but it's a fairly quiet place, especially at night. The second stay had a much smaller window with a view of the courtyard, which is just as good as any other. The courtyard also requests silence between 7 and 11 so nights are peaceful. I was provided with towels and toiletries, and a drinking cup. As fair as cleanliness goes, this is where the budget shows. The carpets are fairly grotty, as are the shared bathrooms and showers. I recommend you bring flip flops. The beds were comfy enough, but I was very tired and am usually not very picky either! Breakfast was very nice, with a decent spread. I went up for seconds without realising I wasn't meant to, but the Jamaican lady was very friendly when she let me know (no croissant snatching!) Overall impression: VERY GOOD VALUE FOR MONEY! If you aren't staying for long, or if you don't mind slightly sub par standards, this is a great place to stay. I challenge you to find anywhere this close to central London as cheap as this, with a free breakfast. If you find it, let me know. I'll stay here every time I visit London until you do.

title: still has good
text: clean rooms safe enviorment excellent breakfast lovely garden clean toilet and shower areas staff polite in lovely quite area close to tube and buses about 15 minute walk to oxford street theatre land

title: nice Hotel
text: Stayed at Passfield Hall for two night,nice Hotel, near Russel Square, 5 minutes walk of British museum. I had a single room with no ensuite and it was clean. There was a sink Had to pay a 88£ in September.

title: Great value, clean and comfortable
text: We stayed with our three adult children. Their triple room was huge! The rooms are warm, the beds comfortable and their is a lovely view outside the French windows. Very handy to Euston station and within walking distance to Covent garden etc. The buffet breakfast is great. Reception staff very welcoming and informative. Great alternative to hotel accommodation.

title: Budget stay, excellent dorm facilities, can almost (not completely) believe it is a hotel.
text: I'm backpacking around Europe and chose Passfield Hall as I wanted a single room in a convenient location on a budget. I was quite impressed and overall had a great stay. Similar to another reviewer I got in at 8am but no check in until 3pm, so they have a luggage storage room which I used. I spent the day at the nearby British museum (which was amazing enough to only just keep me awake after 28hours of travel and jet lag from Australia). The room was on the ground floor and near several bathrooms. I rarely encountered other people in the bathroom/shower, even though at breakfast time it was clear that plenty of guests were staying. The shower water is not very hot at peak showering time in the evenings so I switched to 5:30am-6am in the morning to shower and the temperature was much better then. They also need to schedule more frequent sanitary bin pick ups as there was an almost overflow in 2 bathrooms in the 4 nights I stayed, so ladies beware. Breakfast was very filling - 6 main choices, unlimited toast, juice, tea and coffee. Just be aware they are very strict and you are treated like a student. I had an early tour bus to catch around the corner, so popped down at 7:20am (breakfast is at 7:30am) and asked if I could take a banana. The lady was very strict and said no. I repeated and said "so I'm not allowed to touch anything before 7:30am?" And she again said "no", even though taking a banana10 mins early would have made no difference to dirty dishes and people get cups of tea at 7:25am all the time. It was very strange. The reception were very friendly and helpful, I bought a train ticket and asked about printing or Internet cafés, they said just email the document to them and reception printed it out for me. I also heard reception being very helpful to tourists who needed directions or assisting with minicab bookings. I didn't use the kitchen but apparently there was one available. WiFi available too, but a 10 MB limit so be aware and register for it on as many WiFi devices that you own as you can. There is a single computer for guests at reception, so I could upload photos. My room was tidied and rubbish emptied daily. Location wise, I could walk to Covent Garden in under 40 minutes so I explored on foot quite conveniently. It was easy to find from the tube provided you have a map of the local area as the streets in the neighbourhood are logical and arranged in rectangle blocks. I caught the Piccadilly line from Heathrow direct to Russell Sq station. It is only a 10 minute walk from Euston station if you are booking long distance trains. Overall a convenient and budget stay in London. Some parts mentioned above remind you that you are in a dorm, not a hotel or hostel. But overall it should meet very well the needs of the average traveller.

title: A real find - very happy to have found L.S.E Vacations @ Passfield Hall
text: This is the most important thing to know about staying at Passfield Hall: Staying here is excellent value for money, and generally very, very pleasant. I can't fault the rates at all considering all these things: 1. The facilities are very clean and easily accessible, with showers & toilets on each floor. 2. You get a really delicious breakfast for free. It is DELICIOUS and varied! Continental or full English... Pain au chocolat, croissants, waffles or pancakes, fresh fruit, fruit salad of grapefruit & orange, prunes, cereals, yogurt, muesli or bacon, eggs, tomatoes, toast... and strong, hot black coffee or fruit juice! You are allowed at least 6 items for breakfast & unlimited toast & drinks! 3. The location is excellent: you are right in the middle of Bloomsbury facing Tavistock Square. If, as someone going to stay in London, you want to feel comfortable and that you are in a really lovely part of this amazing city with historical buildings, this is it. Bloomsbury is beautiful with it's rows of Georgian [?] town houses and peaceful, leafy green parks. Plus, it's a short walk away from Covent Garden, the British Museum, China Town, Trafalgar Square & the galleries, Buckingham Palace... within 20 minutes you are in the cultural heart of the city & the many places to eat & sights to see. 4. The staff are really friendly & helpful. For example, the first time I stayed here I was having a dilemma with my phone and stupidly had forgot to bring my charger with me. I was relying on it but it was about to lose battery! The lady at reception let me use a charger they had behind the counter & I was able to leave my phone charging for almost a couple of hours for no extra charge. This was such a massive help! [Thank you!!] 5. The rooms are yes basic, but absolutely fine! I stayed in one of the single rooms & you have everything you need: theres a basin & taps [always hot water, which is great!], towels, wardrobe, chair & desk with lamp & fan, single bed with really warm snuggly duvet... AND when you check in you'll find a welcome gift on your bed of sweets & biscuits & wash pouches [shower gel and shampoo/conditioner]! 6. It's very secure with 24 hour reception & electronic cards for each room So, all the above for £45 is brilliant. Most places in central London, even a basic b&b are a similar price or more. I think L.S.E are an excellent choice for anyone looking for somewhere to stay that's both affordable and with high standards. I'm really happy to have discovered L.S.E vacations & will certainly be staying here again. But, I do have just two things to point out: Firstly, when I stayed there was building work being done. This never, ever disturbed me - It was very, very quiet and there was nothing intrusive going on at all. My only issue is that it meant I couldn't open the curtains and I was advised to keep the window shut. It's a shame because the whole building was covered in green sheets so there would be no point in having the curtains open and you can't look out at the view. It's not the nicest thing to see when approaching to check in either ... But, that can't be helped. If the building needs work, it needs work, and it has to be done

title: Very good value for money
text: I visit London 2 or 3 times a year and whenever I happen to be there in the summer I book a room at Passfield Hall, which is incredibly good value for money. The hall is centrally located and very convenient for public transport (tube from Euston, Euston Sq and Russell Sq and various buses

title: Lunch Lady needs to be replaced!
text: Great location and decent room for a student dorm but if they are going to rent out rooms they should advise their staff to treat guests with respect. The women serving the breakfast buffet is rude and one might think she was the inspiration for a Seinfeld episode.

title: Good value, warmth of welcome, very helpful
text: I have graded this at five stars because it more than fulfils reasonable expectations of budget accommodation in central London. I stayed for two nights in a single room - non-ensuite - my error. I thought I had booked en-suite so was a bit wary but I needn't have been. The facilities were opposite my room (317) and I never encountered anyone else there. They were also very clean. The kitchen was just down the hall. I used it for making coffee (mugs, coffee, sugar etc available at reception) and it was fine. Recycling facilites took care of my overblown salad and there was all the rest of the stuff that I didn't use - microwave, cooker, toaster, fridges - more than enough. The room was on the third floor of the main building - the lift went to the second floor so that was fine. The room was small - but clean and equipped with what I needed - good lighting, lots of sockets, wardrobe with hangers, desk, wash basin, mirror etc. The free internet access was easy to register to and quick in operation. Building work was going on but there had been warnings about this. It caused me no problem as I was out early and back after they had finished. Room temperature was dealt with by opening the window - my view was onto the street but it was high enough up to be private - curtains didn't need to be closed at night which was fine by me. I'd like to say a particular good word for the reception staff - they were friendly, accommodating and efficient. Lovely. I was able to leave my bag in a locked room after I had booked out. I can see why there might be some concern about security(another group had parked their stuff in the interim so two bags turned into thirty-ish) but, on balance, I value the facility and can ensure that anything I might worry about stays with me. Breakfast was very good. It is clear about what can be taken without limit and wha is limited. For those who are inclined, an entire day's calorie load could easily be consumed. Clean surroundings, pleasant servery staff, good coffee. Overall, this accommodation is really good value, does what it said on the tin and I would go back there in a trice.

title: Passfield Hall Student residence central and comfy
text: We found Passfield Hall in the London Lonely Planet guide book and I'm so glad we did. It is very central

title: Excellent accomodation for the price
text: I stayed at Passfield Hall last night after going to see Kate Bush at the Hammersmith Apollo. I was looking for something cheap and basic, and Passfield Hall more than fitted the bill. It's very well positioned, 10 minutes walk from Kings Cross St Pancras, and even quicker from Euston, so if you're travelling in from outside London to those stations, you don't need to worry about any additional tube journeys or bus rides. It's a bit difficult to find though - it's tucked away behind Euston Road, and at the moment it's covered with scaffolding. I walked past it 3 times before I realised where it was, but I found it eventually. The rooms are small and basic, as you'd expect for the price, but they are immaculately clean, bright and very comfortable. The bed is more comfortable than you'd find in chain budget hotels. There's a bathroom area with 3 separate toilets and 3 separate shower units, so there's never any issue with waiting to take a shower. The breakfast is also much appreciated - a good buffet selection of bacon, sausages, eggs, beans, hash browns etc, with the additional options of cereal and toast. It's also really tasty! The only issues I'd say is that if you have a room on the top floor (as I did), be prepared to climb several flights of stairs - no problem for me as I was only staying for one night so I was travelling light, but I wouldn't fancy lugging big suitcases up those stairs. Also, the walls are pretty thin, and the guest in the next room to me played his music throughout the night, and I could also hear him snoring! That's not Passfield Hall's fault though, and I'd hope for a quieter neighbour next time around! Finally, it's in a very nice area and the added security of having to buzz through to separate areas of the residence puts your mind at rest. The reception is staffed 24 hours a day and the staff seemed friendly enough (I didn't really have much opportunity to interact with them though). I'm not sure if there's wi-fi, but I didn't have time to use it if so. Overall, if you're in London outside of term-time, and need a place to crash for a night or two, this is a very good choice.

title: Excellent Value for Money
text: The halls are in a excellent location. As soon as you arrive you are made to feel welcome, every thing is explained clearly. The rooms are clean and tidy. Breakfast was very good, overall exceptional expeirence. I will use the halls again.

title: Excellent budget alternative
text: I stayed in these student halls for 12 nights during August and was very satisfied with my stay. All was as described on the website, smallish basic room with handbasin. There are three floors on the building but no lift to the third, so it was a bit tough hauling my luggage up an extra flight of stairs. There were sufficient toilets/showers for each floor, and all were kept clean. Wifi was fast and reliable. Breakfast really was excellent – not just for the price, but actually better than a lot of hotels I’ve stayed in. Nice vegetarian choices and as much drinks refills/toast as you want. The only complaint I’d have is 7.30am/8.00am start is too late, during the week I often had to forego breakfast as I had to leave before it started! Overall a pleasant stay in a pleasant, safe area close to many attractions and public transport links. I would have no hesitation in recommending.

title: don't bother unless you can't afford anything else
text: nothing seemed to run smoothly here. It was hot in London and even hotter in the building. There are many fire doors which stop the air circulating inside. Coupled with this the floor was damp (maybe a flood or students messing around was the suggestion) but in the heat it was humid and smelled like wet dogs. There was a lovely Georgian sash window in my room - which overlooked the courtyard. This was nice but the windows we locked so that I would not open more than four inches. I asked if this could be unlocked so I could open the window and let some air in. Apparently, their insurance policy would not allow the radical act of opening window. This also made me uneasy about an escape route in the event of a fire. As I was being told this I noticed the window in the reception area was open wide. Their suggestion was that I should buy a fan for the room - but another staff member stepped in and offered a spare fan for loan - "cos I looked nice". Water in the shared showers was always cold in the morning. One day, I had been out and about until late - when I returned, the carpets were wet, and my bedroom door had been left open - not just unlocked, but ajar. Luckily, nothing was nicked - and when I reported it they were rather non-plussed. Positive side: cheap, and plenty to choose from for breakfast if you are on a budget. And it was interesting to watch everyone nicking the food for their lunch too. I guess you cannot help but take on an institutional mentality in this 'nannified' environment. Location was handy for Euston, and the British Library if that lights your candle. I couldn't escape quick enough on check out day, and wish I would have left as soon as heard their window 'policy'. Never again.

title: Great value, budget B&B/dorm with excellent breakfast
brillant
text: forgot how many times ive been i feel safe here rooms are basic clean toilet and bathrooms always pleanty of hot water breakfast very good always hot and fresh pleanty of seats outside to sit in courtyard and also this year deckchairs they are upgrading the front with scaffolding up so it will look lovely when done

title: OK but no WiFi as promised
text: We stayed here for 6 nights, my partner studied law here for three years in the 60's. We had room 25 which is a long walk from reception. Checking in was painless and we went to our room. The room was quite large with two windows, beds are very basic and weren't very comfortable. We could get no WiFi signal in room 25 despite the website boasting of a Signal in every room. I asked at reception and they said oh yes room 25 is a problem for WiFi but this would be fixed. It wasn't and in fact the student WiFi signal went off all over the building and the login poster was removed from reception, we could log into the Cloud WiFi in public areas. Our room wasn't serviced on one day and we had to ask for dry towels to shower with. The grouting round the bath is a three dimensional work of art - never seen such a bad job as this in my life as a maintenance engineer! The breakfast is excellent, full selection of hot food, great coffee and great service by the catering staff. In considering all of the above comments, you need to keep in mind that this is Central London and what you pay to stay here wouldn't get you a park bench to sleep on in the world of hotels! We would stay here again but not in room 25. We have stayed in most of the LSE Halls and this one has the best breakfast.

title: Basic but convenient and friendly
text: The room was comfortable if small, and clean - rather like a cell in an open prison in an enlightened country. If I stayed again I would bring some form of portable entertainment, a radio or CD player. Had problems with the telephone service, which assured me that no such number existed when I tried to contact family and close friends, also with the shower - the gate did not close properly and water flooded the bathroom floor. How to turn it on to the required temperature without getting an icy drenching eluded me. The breakfast was exceptional - almost worth staying for that alone. As a disabled guest I appreciated the lift and found all the personnel with whom I dealt very helpful and sympathetic. The location could not have been better for proximity to transport. Unfortunately I had underestimated my own ability to cope with London and had to leave earlier than planned- no fault of Passfield Hall's.

title: Location Great, Staff Great 😀👍
text: Hello we stayed for a period of two nights at The Ibis Styles London Kensington and were suitably impressed. The location was in easy walking distance to Earls Court Tube Station and local pubs and restaurants. The room whilst small had a comfortable bed and adequate shower/toilet, the view from the bedroom was quite quaint. Breakfast was provided and had a nice continental selection. However what really made this stay special was the attentive staff especially Diana and Shade who went out of their way to help with an airline luggage problem and who were always happy to help any way they could. For that alone, to meet two special staff members who went above and beyond will never be forgotten. Again I would reccomend this hotel to any traveller seeking a central location with possibly the nicest staff one could wish to meet. I will see you my next visit.

title: Good value and very nice
text: This is excellent value. The hotel is not as expensive as the many others in the area and it does the job. It is clean and comfortable and the decor is stylish and distinctive. There is a gym hurrah! The location is good - the museum district is 15 minutes walk, as is Imperial College, Hyde Park, and the Albert Hall. If you don't have much time locally then do go to the V&A museum. It's inspiring and free, and the queues are nothing in comparison to the Natural History or Science Museums.
