It isn't a place I would recommend as a base for a holiday either as it's not the best area for seeing London from. I stopped over here for one night when working South of the River. The area is not great, Old Kent Road is pretty run down. Parking was reasonably secure, clean and comfortable-ish rooms, reception OK, polite enough staff but not brimming with enthusiasm. The shower was OK but I agree with what others have said about it not draining quickly enough. Quite a bit of noise from the street, sirens were the main thing (I was on the top floor) but acceptable bearing in mind it's location (it was a Tuesday, not a weekend). Rooms at the back are much quieter, my colleague stayed in one and had a quiet night, so see if you can request one. The Chinese attached to the hotel Shu Castle, was pukka - really great food not your normal Cantonese fayre - proper Szechuan food, a real adventure. We were going to trek off for a curry but in the end went to the chinese and it was a great decision. We then wandered out to look for a nice little pub and decided after 3 or 4 mins walk that a 'nice pub' on Old Kent Road was probably wishful thinking and walked back (maybe we went the wrong way?)- the hotel has a little bar in reception anyway.

title: Spacious rooms, good value
text: This hotel is good value for money. We went with our 2 children and the rooms were very spacious. The staff are friendly and relaxed. The hotel itself is a 30 minute walk from Tower Bridge although there are buses every 12 minutes (nearest tube Elephant and Castle). There are 2 restaurants next door, both Latin, both serve enormous portions. We went to both on different nights. The one further away from the hotel is the better one (they are literally next door to each other). This hotel is a great option if you want to avoid the expensive hotels nearer the sights and are prepared to either walk or take buses/tubes.

title: Pleasant place to stay.
text: Premier by Eurotraveller hotel is quite a pleasant place to stay. The staff are nice and very friendly. The rooms are big and convenient. Will love to be here again.

title: Basic but clean but not safe for small children
text: Stayed for one night recently, location is ideal for east London although the immediate neighbourhood isn't great! The rooms are basic but very clean and they are making efforts to make the hotel look nice. Biggest complaint would be the beds...they have sharp metal corners that are just at the right level to leave a nasty dent in your leg! Not ideal when you have a toddler, I would for that not recommend it being the safest place for small children.

title: Good value for mney
text: Very modern, spotless and with friendly staff. Room was large, well furnished, cleaned and decorated. Much better than we expected and very convenient for public transport. Would definitely stay again.

title: Maggots!
text: This hotel has a good location and is fairly reasonably priced. However, during our stay we found two maggots on the bed which was quite an unpleasant experience as you can imagine. We were given another room but upon trying to complain further were sent a most unsatisfactory letter which seemed to be implying that the presence of the maggots was not the fault of the hotel.

title: A real gem
text: We stayed one night in June 2017. We were very pleasantly surprised as some mixed reviews. We had requested a quiet room and got one on third floor at back of hotel, No road noise. The room was clean, a good size and had tea making facility, safe, fridge and air con. The bar area and dining room were pleasant and modern, lifts to all floors, and the staff were friendly and helpful. The car park is behind the hotel, easy to find and has designated spaces, very secure. The cost of car park was £25 for 24 hours which I think is reasonable.I would definitely return as it is in a good location too.

title: excellent hotel
text: The Premier hotel was great! I highly recommend booking there because transportation wise it is very convenient, the service is welcoming, the rooms are great and very clean. total value for your money!

title: A Good Budget Hotel
text: A little further from the City centre than we would have liked but clean and comfortable. The staff were helpful but the surrounding area was a little run down. We stayed for three nights and travelled around on buses, the tube and the DLR. Buy an Oyster card as soon as you arrive - makes travel much cheaper.

title: Comfy and clean for a one night stay
text: Stayed here with friends. There was 3 of us in a triple room. The reception area was clean and tidy as were the corridors and room. Comfy bed, with extra pillows available. Room was well equipped with a hairdryer and ironing board with iron available on request. Complementary small toiletries in the bathroom and also towels. Easy to use heating in the room. Although it is situated on a main road the room (ours was at the back of the hotel) was quiet.It is easy access from Elephant & Castle tube, just over a mile with a taxi costing about £5.00 although we did walk mostly which took around half hour. A pleasant stay.

title: Social meet up
text: FIRST. Please do not mix this hotel up with a Premier Inn as it is far from it. It is not a hotel from that well known chain nor is it a premier standard hotel. It is a basic cheap hotel and you get what you pay for or even less. Check in was easy, breakfast explained and we were pointed in the direction of the lifts. The room was clean . Towels provided were clean and toiletries provided consisted of 3 mini bars of soap and some plastic cups on the sink. The staff at check in were helpful and provided a sheet of paper with bus numbers and routes which was very useful - the bus stop is not far. The cover on the quilt was ripped and the sheets did not properly fit the mattress. They kept moving on the ill fitting mattress protector and ended up in a pile on the bed. We had a disturbed night on the first night, not because of traffic noise but because of a naked man running around knocking loudly on room doors and trying the handles...... a call to reception and the said gentleman was whisked away with a pillow to cover his modesty. The hotel staff were very not at all forthcoming the next morning regarding what had happened and different stories from different members of staff. Apparently there was meant to be security cctv...... my question : how did night staff miss a naked man walking around the hotel for about an hour. We received no adequate explanation for what had happened and no apology. Second night sleep was fine but I was awakened on the Sunday morning by the sound of somebody vomiting outside in the hotel corridor. Sad to say the vomit was still there a couple of hours later !!! This hotel is what it is meant to be cheap and cheerful however I would not recommend it to any lone female travellers. £5.00 at Ozzi's cafe ( just two doors up) does get you a full English with a mug of tea, pleasant service and very nice it is too

title: Great stay
text: We recently stayed on Halloween for a gig at the 02 academy in Brixton and the hotel by large was very good. The staff were friendly and helpful, the rooms were clean and a decent size. Some of the furniture had stains on and the 'drinking water' tap in the bathroom leaked which was what stopped it getting 5/5. It had very secure parking around the back of the hotel which is worth paying for in my opinion. The beds were very comfy but the sofa bed was like a rock so I'm glad none of us had to sleep on that! Overall we had a pleasant stay and compared to the hotels close by it was good value too. The taxi from the hotel to the 02 academy was £15 each way.

title: Really dirty but good service... see pictures
text: Service was good and noise complaint was dealt with efficiently. Breakfast was OK and all you can eat. Yes the traffic can be noisy but it is on a main road so to be expected. Unfortunately the general cleanliness let's it down along with the thin walls. We also had a loose plug socket which didn't work. Also... I couldn't have drunk from the drinking water tap in the room... it's disgusting. The mattress and bedding was stained. Also some of the crockery was dirty and cracked. See pics for examples of lack of cleanliness in our room.

title: Okay rooms. Terrible service.
text: We had help booking this hotel as we were traveling with Children and needed beds for four. Buses run past front door and take you to tube station. Although if you're energetic tube is just 15 to 20 minute walk. Wouldn't walk area late at night though. Our Taxi driver told us the area is up and comming. Not a bad description. But still has a long way to come. The room was very small for a family. No facilities except a kettle. But at least they were clean. No Free WiFi. They charge £2 for an hour and you can't stop the time once you start. Biggest disappointment was on our morning of check out I was picking up a hire car. There is no on street parking so I asked concierge if I could use car park for half an hour whilst we loaded our bags. The answer was yes but I would need to pay £15 for the privilege. Must say the staff weren't rude but they were not helpful in any way. Felt like if they could get a quid out of you they would try their best. Only stay there if you are on a tight budget and don't need the extras.

title: Ok for the price but an item of clothes went 'missing'
text: I stayed here for 2 weeks whilst my flat was being readied. It's a decent hotel for the for price but I lost trust in them when a shirt that I had in my room went missing. I told management and they said they asked the cleaning staff but couldn't find it. I'm 100% sure it was in the room and somehow was gone. It made me weary of leaving other things in my room whilst I was out.

title: Deliver what it says on the box
text: Party of 2, for one night. Experienced Traveller. The hotel offer exactly what's on the box. It is located within close proximity of Elephant and Castle and Tower Bridge. Parking is at the best of time difficult, and the hotel charges a fortune for parking on their premises Some rooms will be on the front of the hotel, overlooking the Old Kent Road. This could be interpreted as noisy but thanks to triple glazing not much noise gets inside. The staff do their job properly but do not expect a warm open arm welcome. You will be given your cards, details of your room and off you go. The hotel has a bar and is surrounded by small take away restaurant. The room was clean, spacious, but nothing magical about it. Overall an experience that was within the parameters of our expectations.

title: Lovely hotel
text: Best we have stayed in. Free WiFi..safe.. 3 mins from bus stop. Friendly will definitely be going back.. breakfast ok but would of liked bacon on the menu..tho everything was nice. Would recommend to anyone

title: Basic and Noisey
text: If you are going to stay at this hotel i would ask for a room away from the Old Kent Road. There is constant noise from traffic, all through the night. There are numerous sirens every hour. The staff were not over friendly and the air con/ heating didnt work properly and was noisey. The shower was awful the head didnt work properly. We couldnt get any hot water out of the sink tap.

title: Decent for the price
text: This hotel offers decent accommodation for the price listed in one of the most expensive cities. The big plus is that it is located close to the Tower Bridge and has excellent bus links to all major sites. Bedsheets and bathroom are clean and the staff was very helpful. Tip: ask for a room facing the back of the hotel, of you don't like street noise and if you want your windows to open. Overall good value for money for 2 max 3 nights.

title: Great Location, and value for money.
text: Stayed here for a week, I really liked the hotel because of the location it's close to the bus line, and not so far from everywhere. The rooms are clean, the staff are so-so. On a good day they are very nice, friendly and helpful. (i noticed the night staff are the cranky ones always) I had a view of old Kent road, which was nice to just look out and see London wake up and go to sleep. You only get free internet if you book on their web site, otherwise you pay. Didn't get to eat breakfast, but there are lots of reastuaunts and eateries around the hotel, all walking distance and supermarkets close by also. Will I stay here again, YES, for sure.

title: Weird hotel experience - won't stay again
text: Run by Indian owners - the hotel has that feel of being abroad in a low quality hotel yet it's newly decorated. The style would match that of temperatures outside of 80degrees but in cold London - tiles on the floor, lino as flooring in the room, air conditioning which doesn't heat the room well doens't match the requirements for this country. Taps in the bathrrom only pore water if you bend over and are close enough will automatically come on and you get soaked. The shower is small and an issue for anyone trying to have a wash! No bar - well it's part of reception and not inviting. The dining area is not comfortable and cold and bland in the morning. The walk from Elephant and Castle is long around 20 mintues and with a bag not good. Also, the hotel is not in a nice area. The hotel doesn't have an evening restaurant and will invite pizza and chinese companies to deliver take aways. There are no local restaurants I would feel comfortable in - carribean run restaurants, I saw gangs on the streets and went swiftly back to the hotel. Traffic is a huge issue in the morning and delays if you have meetings. The bed was comfortable and have flat screens but feel they have cut corners all over the place to save money and has had a detrimental feeling to comfort and a relaxing ambience. Asked to leave as soon as I checked in but I had paid and no refunds. Stayed for 3 nights. Will NEVER stay here again.

title: Nice clean rooms
text: A group of us stayed here during our trip to London , it was the best price and good location, rooms were clean and seemed to be recently refurbished , staff were friendly too, we would definitely come back ,

title: Not good at all
text: Hotel staff were surly and spoke very little English, couldn't find my reservation so check in took a while. Our room was clean but one bed was partly held together with duct tape, the space to hang clothes was above the desk which had the cups and kettle on. Noisy guests and staff could be heard at all hours due to thin walls and tiled floors, tiled floors also in the rooms, would expect carpet. I booked the hotel for access to room service and a restaurant and they didn't have either. What they call room service is a couple of drink choices and mints. It is not the type of neighbourhood that i would feel comfortable going out in the dark to look for somewhere to eat, during the day it was fine. Someone from the front desk rang our hotel phone a couple of times at midnight one night, no idea why. Check out was quick but staff didn't even ask if we enjoyed our stay.

title: Dont understand the bad reviews it's anexcellant budget hotel and will stay again.
text: My friend booked this hotel for us for a night out in Brixton so I looked it up myself to see where we were staying and was teriffied by the reviews. However ignore all the bad reviews I do not understand where these people where staying and wish I had taken pictures for proof of how nice is it. It is easy to find and about a 15 mins walk from the Elephant and Castle tube station. The entrance lobby is large with a really nice bar/ lounge area with TVs. The bar is open most of the time it seems where you can purchase a range of drinks and snacks at your convenience. When we arrived the staff couldnt have been friendlier, we planned to just drop our bags and explore for the day as we arived early but they let us check in and go to our rooms no problem. The decor is modern and clean and we were really suprised after reading the reviews and expected the worst when walking to the room/ cabin. When we went in our twin room we were amazed, we had two large, comfy double beds, the room was spotless. The room was alot bigger than expected much larger than you standard premiere inn for example. In the room there was, tea and coffee facilities, iron and ironing board, plenty of spotless towels, soap, safe, fridge, free wifi, TV and even slippers. What more could you want seriously. The staff are also really helpful and knowledgable, we wanted to go to Borough Market and the guy at reception directed us and told us bus routes with no hesistation. The reviews about showers being too small myth me.... We had a double (door) shower than was fine for pressure. By no means a power shower or anything fancy but a decent, plesent, clean shower. The only fault I will say is you cannot open the window for safety and smoking etc. The rooms temp is meant to be controlled by a panel on the wall which we just could not work out. However a quick mention at reception the staff member showed us and set it to how we wanted and also sorted a fan. Please ignore the bad reviews I am so glad we did and can't wait to stay again. The Eurotraveller excels itself especially considering it is a budget hotel. 10x better than any Premiere Inn or Travel lodge.

title: my daughters birthday weekend would defo use this hotel again
text: i can not complain the staff were nice and polite nothing was any problem would recommend to anyone price is fab for london short bus ride city centre they could help with the local transport info staff were polite wich is a massive plus in my book

title: Premier - Eurotraveller -old Kent road London
text: Stayed at this hotel for one night The room was good no problem very spacious But the reception area ,Lounge area very poor standard. The Bar area very poor standard service poor felt the bar assistant did not want to sell me wine as I was a female I asked for 2 glasses of white wine and he only served me with one glass . Had to ask again after few moments he served me the second glass Thankful we did not have breakfast, breakfast area did not look welcoming at all. It seemed as a run down cafe. Staff and management need more training Sad to right this but felt need share my experience.

title: Okay
text: Well after reading some reviews was slightly concerned but found the staff helpful and answered all questions we asked answered well. Explained bus links and tube links well to us. Bar well stocked. And reasonable price for London. Hotel is clean and okay. We had a room on second floor. Beds fine and bathroom fine. Room was clean and tidy. Beds made daily and cannot fault the hotel. It's a basic budget hotel. We needed a room for a week and this did just what we needed yes it's away from the centre but it's on a main bus link into London and local tube station is approx 15 minute walk or you can get a bus. Yes I would visit again for the price we paid. And the area I felt safe in. Myself and my daughter didn't have any worries walking from tube to hotel. All in all a good visit for a basic price.

title: A budget hotel near Central London but on terrible road...
text: When you first arrive, you ask yourself why anyone would put a hotel on this road? The area is terrible. My initial view of the hotel itself was good. The room was clean and there is a large TV with all the freeview channels. However, when you look closely around the room, it has obviously been built on the cheap. The bathroom door didn’t close (so wouldn’t lock), wires hung down under the sink, the shower was held to the wall by sellotape, the shower tray was leaving the wall, skirting board broken, holes in walls etc. The corridors have cheap wooden floors so you hear everyone walking about and leaving early in a morning. To say this is a fairly new hotel, it is in need of a big renovation. All the staff are Indian and were polite towards me - no problems. The room was on the 3rd floor, I asked for a quiet room and was given a room near the rear - very glad I did - Old Kent Road is just a constant stream of sirens from emergency vehicles and very busy traffic. Nearby is a Tesco, cash machines and lots and lots of takeaways. It is a 15 min walk to Elephant & Castle tube station, but if you get a 21 bus from outside hotel, it is about 10 - 15 mins to London Bridge. I didn't have the breakfast at £10 - better to get one from somewhere else and save money. Overall, a half decent hotel in the middle of a dump, but a short journey to Central London.

title: Extended weekend in London
text: This hotel is great option for travellers who want to stay at hotel just for sleeping. Room floors were quite cold, breakfast was average but little too expensive. Bathrooms were old and showers worked poorly, but there was always hot water. Service was great and receptionists were friendly. Location of the hotel was great transition-vise. Overall experiense was good, but would not come again.

title: Basic - Clean, nice staff, too far from tube, poor breakfast
text: Bookied via Booking.Com at reasonable price considering it is London. However, if I had paid full price, I would have cried. This is a basic hotel clean and reception staff are kind and helpful. That is the end of the good news. Although there are good bus connections from the stop just a few metres away, the nearest tube station is 20 minutes walk although I have to say a walk down Bermondsey Street to the Shard is lovely, especially on a friday when Bermondsey Market is in full swing or you stop for one of the best coffees in the world at the superb Watch House.There are several reasonable eating places next door, Chinese, Mexican and a gold old Cafe who serve an freshly cooked English Breakfast, bread and mug of builders tea for 5 pounds, brilliant! I recommend against eating breakfast in the hotel, it is dreadful and costs 8 pounds. Watery scrambled eggs made I think from powder and microwaved plus tiny cardboard sausages make this possibly the worst breakfast possible. The coffee is hideous. Simply no effort on this point and this hotel should seriously sort this out. There are also some mediterranean/middle eastern carry outs and shops. This is a multi culti area and I never had one issue even though I walked a lot, lovely locals.

title: Nice hotel, worth the money
text: We stayed here for 2 nights and I enjoyed the hotel. Although a bit far from main attractions there is an easy bus route that you can use. The room was nice and cosy and the staff helpful. Breakfast was also good. I was impressed they had European sockets for tourist. You can't see that very often. Definitely worth the money we paid!

title: Parking Fiasco
text: Well what an absolute horrible experience this was. I arrived to this hotel after 10pm after what was an extremely long working day, all i wanted was my room key and perhaps a bite too eat. It was too late for food which was fine, I asked about the getting a drink and charging it to my room but was told that wasn't available and that I had to pay there and then for the drinks. I decided I'd just head straight to my room. So I'm just finishing checking in and the lady asks if I have a car..... I said yes and told her I had it parked out in the back car park to which she replied ok I'll add that to the bill. I asked how much it was and she said £20.00, to which I replied that it was only £10.00 on the website when I booked it. So i said I was not paying £20.00 to park my car, she then called for the duty manager who was as useful as an ashtray on a motorcycle. He said it was £20.00 for parking end of the story, so I asked where it said that on their website??? He had no answer, then replied that the car park was actually full. I also upon booking this hotel emailed them asking to book a car space for me.....I got no reply and presumed all was well. I was willing to pay the £10.00 for parking but felt totally ripped off at the thought of them trying to charge me £20.00 when I had booked in good faith. Out of principle I stood my ground and refused to pay that fee and said I wanted to cancel my booking. That is when this duty manager laughed and said "we will still charge your card for the room" This just made me even more angry, so i asked to speak with the manager. The duty manager rang him and said he was unavailable but he said he would cancel my booking and would NOT charge my room. I stay in hotels nearly every single week and I have never had an experience like this in my life.

title: Perfect As Always
text: I stay here on a very regular basis - and often for months at a time. The reception desk is open 24 hours a day- the staff are always extremely helpful and pleasant- The bar is open basically 24 hours a day and is very well stocked. I often sit there to watch TV even though there is a TV in every room. Wifi was recently completely re - installed and is not just free but also fast with no blind spots. Breakfast - buffet style with toaster & selection of breads. Hot - Scrambled Eggs, baked beans & sausages + cold meats, cheese, jams & honey. Assorted pastries, muffins and cake-fresh fruits both cut and whole. Coffee, Teas and juices- cereals Much as you can eat for under £8!!! The rooms are very adequate in size well-equipped – all on suite of course and very clean – And probably the best rooms you can find at the price within reach of the city and West End of London – that is my experience anyway.

title: Very disappointing
text: I was very disappointed by this hotel. It reminded me of a run down Travel Lodge with inflated prices. The rooms were spotless and adequate. However the Reception and Bar area was very shabby. The staff's behaviour ranged from downright rude to surly. The day I departed I intended to leave very early. However when switching on the bathroom light, all the lights fused. I had to go to reception to get someone to check it out. The receptionist came to my room and on entering accused me of overloading the system. All I had plugged in was my phone charger ! It was resolved in a few minutes but the delay made me late for my meeting. This hotel is OK if all you need is somewhere to put your head down for the night but the staff certainly need some Customer relations training

title: Weekend to London :)
text: I have always wanted to go to London to do some sight seeing. So for my Birthday my boyfriend book this for me form 21/02/14 to 23/02/14. Due to seeing some bad reviews on this Hotel I started to worried a couple of days before. When we arrived at the Hotel the surrounding area look a little dodge, but the Hotel stood out and looked well percented. To get into the hotel either you have to wait for someone on the reception to open the doors or you could swipe your room card key. This inpressed me becuase I knew it was safe. When we enterend it was very clean and friendly, the checking in process was very fast and they took a scan of you ID. We were placed in room 107 of the first floor, The coridors and lift was very clean. We found it a little difficult to get into the door using the key cards but ones we knew how to do it, it was fine and had no problems with the door. The room was very clean and offered a lot which I was not expectining for this type of hotel, such as - A nice TV with lots of good channels which was located up on the wall infrount of the bed - Big floor Lenth Mirro perfect for me to do my hair and makeup. - A hair dryer - Ironing board and we had to ask for an iron at no exter charge - Cloth storge and hangers behind the main door - There was a little shampoo and two hand soaps in the bathroom - Kettle and cups with tea, coffee and suger - A seperent tap for drinking warter with 4 plactic cups - Due to there being two of us there were two bath towels, one hand towel and bath mat. - The shower was amazing it was really powerfull and easy to use - The clean came round and changed the towels which we placed in the shower and also made the bed. - They also supply you on arrivel with bus times - The staff were nice and my Boyfirend was happy because a pint of fosters was only £2.50 and you can either drink this in the reception area or in the room. - The BUS STOP in just a two min walk and they are very reliable. There are only two things I would suggest to the Hotel which are: - Whiles the bathroom is clean it could do with a make over - Window in room needs repairing as there is a slight gap in the hinge area We did not eat in the place so we can not comment on the food or restuarnt. Apart from this we both hand a lovely time and would defently stay with this hotel and again along with recommending it to other who want to visit London.

title: Spoilt our weekend
text: During my one night stay with my 12 year old daughter, I had approx £600 worth of property stolen from the room. I called the Police at half past midnight and they came out to the scene. They are still investigating. Apparnetly, a Hotel exmployee allowed strangers into the room and lett them there unattended whilst we were out at the theatre. The Hotel is not communicating with me and have, so far, refused to even refund my room tariff. I suggest this hotel is removed from the Vist London website. I would not want any other traveller - especially from overseas to have such a stressful experience as we have. It gives London a bad name!

title: If you want a very clean and comfortable room and don't mind a dreadful location, this is the hotel to choose.
text: I shared a double room with my teenage son. I've stayed in tiny, overpriced rooms in Bayswater, and so I appreciated the really spacious and comfortable modern room that we got here. The bathroom was spotless and, incredibly, everything worked well. Even the hairdryer was good! We got an excellent deal on Booking.com so no matter how dire the hotel might be, we weren't complaining. Even at the standard rates displayed in the lobby (GBP 99 per night for a double) it would have been ok. BUT: the hotel is really far away from Tower Bridge and you can't walk from the nearest tube (Elephant and Castle) because it's not a nice stroll through pretty streets, it's a long walk through absolutely miserable and honestly spooky areas. This is not a nice area of town. We had to take a taxi to the tube station every time, so if you stay here, only do it because you've got such an amazing deal that you can splash out on taxis all the time. We paid GBP 39 per night for our room, so we could get away with it, but deals like that are rare, and we were very lucky. The staff were reserved and quiet, but did help us with small things that we asked for

title: Clean, quiet, basic but does what it says on the tin
text: I was visitng an Aunt who lives on the Old Kent Road and this hotel was 5 mins walk from her home. Perfect location for me - but knew ahead the area is quite down market so had no expectations about the location. Ideal for me - great price £79 for a Saturday night in London! Had a ground floor room with a double and single bed - large space. Clean bed linen and towels - took my slippers as read no carpet so could be cold underfoot - shower clean and warm though pressure a little lacking. Friendly staff.

title: Great budget hotel
text: Our friend whom we visited in London recommended this hotel. We are a family of four and usually book two rooms so price is important. We had two clean, quiet good sized rooms. The hotel provided some extras you don't normally find in a budget hotel such as an iron and coffee pot. As far as location I would describe the neighborhood as very ethnic and similar to Queens, New York if that helps. I felt very safe walking alone with my 9 year old daughter and bought things in the local shops. As far as getting around from the hotel we were able to reach all the sights we wanted to visit easily by bus or tube. My friend who lived locally was guiding us but since we were always on a bus or tube anyway it seemed fine. The hotel is about an 8 minute bus ride from Tower of London. The front desk was very accommodating. I did notice they weren't warm and fuzzy but they were very polite and helpful. We ordered the English hotel breakfast for 10 pounds per person per day. I enjoyed being able to eat breakfast and return to the hotel room then shower since we were not totally adjusted to London time. The breakfast room was sunny and clean and they gave us a lot of food. In summary if you are looking for a clean, convenient, budget hotel. Go for it!

title: Great value for money, clean rooms and helpful staff
text: We booked our hotel in London fairly last minute so were low on choices which fell under our budget (we wanted to stay quite central). The photos didn't look particulary inviting but we took our chances and were pleasantly surprised! The room was very clean and kitted with a hairdryer, towers, tv, iron board etc. The snacks and drinks sold at reception were very cheap too - not the usual triple price you normally see at hotels! It was nice and quiet and we slept like babies! There was great bus links and is about a 20min to the Elephant and Castle tube station. There were a lot of supermarkets nearby but no coffee shops / restaurnts so we walked / travelled nearer the centre most days. One more great thing - the view from our hotel room was amazing! From the third floor we could see Canary Wharf and the Shard. Very impressed! For the price we paid and the location, I would reccomned this hotel

title: Pleasantly Surprised
text: We used to live in London so knew the area. We were aware that it is a 15 minute walk to London Bridge tube or a bus ride to Elephant and Castle. We have stayed in many hotels in London previously (some reasonable expensive) and chose this one due to it's location close to family and the fact that our teenage boys and a friend were also staying for the weekend (not spending a fortune on hotels for teenage boys who don't appreciate their surroundings). We were pleasantly surprised at how clean the hotel was and how efficient the staff were. Our sons friend decided to come at the last minute and the hotel changed the twin to a family room at no extra charge. The rooms were clean and spacious and had everything we needed. I would definitely stay here again and recommend it to family and friends. The only criticism I have is that the iron sent to our room had slightly exposed wires in the cord. For £30 or so to replace it versus a pricey compensation claim if someone electrocutes themselves, I would replace any dodgy irons.

title: Great service and welcome
text: Guys on reception were friendly and welcoming. Room was clean and spacious. Breakfast was disappointing - hot food was luke warm and toaster wouldn't work because it wasn't turned on early enough to heat up in time. Plenty of cakes and croissants if you like that for breakfast.

title: Mugging Central
text: AVOID - firstly I am a local and run a theatre a few miles away and was shocked when discovered they call themselves Tower Bridge - it is nowhere near Tower Bridge, it is on the Old Kent Road. 2 miles away in one of the most crime ridden areas of London. My experience was that I was booking a hotel for some of my actors, our usual hotel in Greenwich was full, so search internet and this one came up. Thought £99 for a douible in TOWER BRIDGE was great value and and called to book the room for that evening. The reservation clark said I had to confirm the booking with a email, which I did as paying with our company card. I tried t give him the card details but he said, I has to come in person and pay as they will not confirm with cards (I wanted to make the full payment at the time). Tried to tell them that I was a business and the customers will not actually be me so cannnot just travel to them to make a payment in person. They said they must do it this way. So I ended up giving the clients the money in cash and told them to pay for the hotel when they arrived. Once at the hotel, they called to say that the hotel is no where near Tower Bridge and not near any tube or train and had to get there from the actual bridge by taxi. It was then I looked up the actual venue address and knew what a bad area it was in. Worst, they had accepted the cash but the hotel still insisited on a credit card which they did not have so made me drive to them to give them mine. Which I had to do, to. Stupid rules and no parking outside.

title: Budget, not a good area, but actually was fine.
text: Reasonably modern, clean, fairly comfortable, nice staff. Bit of a walk from the nearest tube, and at night I would take a taxi. Breakfast was fairly basic, but again, you know, fine. I suppose the word that comes to mind is: serviceable.

title: Good location for visiting London
text: Recently stayed here whilst on business for 1 Week, hotel room was clean, had a comfortable bed and en-suite bathroom with shower. The hotel is around a 30 minute walk from London Bridge, otherwise there are a few tube stations within 20 minutes. For the price per night (Booked via Laterooms.com) and for the location I would definitely stay here again whether on business or holiday.

title: Surprised for London
text: I was pleasantly surprised with the hotel room considering Old Kent Road location. It's biggest disadvantage is it is slightly outside the tourist zone if you want to easily walk to places and minimize tube and taxi. But this is London, you have to expect to take transport most places you go unless your like me, a walker. It was coming off the royal wedding when all hotels rooms were overpriced, and so paid as much as for a 4 star a week later. Having said that, it was priced better than the rest. Rooms were very clean and functional, and while not splashy, were modern in design, and slightly larger than comparable London hotels in this price range. Wifi is available at a fee. Front desk staff were very helpful, and their simple bus guide to access to the city was useful . Breakfast for the price was adequate and comparable to other places - not fine dining, but gets you going for the day. Be warned though, closest tube, is Elephant and Castle. With luggage, it is one to be missed, and trying to get a taxi outside is awkward. I found it better to get off at Waterloo and take a 10-12 GBP taxi ride to hotel, especially at night, or with bags. While the hotel would not be my first choice in London, if priced right, I would stay here again as it was not a bad experience as I have had with other places.

title: Fine in the Med
text: WWas double booked elsewhere o had to find a hotel sharpish south of the Thames. Intenret led me here. Next dor to a very appealing chinese on the very mixed economy Old Kent Road. Good reception and service. Room the TV did not work so free Wifi was offered instead. My only real gripe was as the rooms having no carpet was very cold on the feet. Tiled floors are fine in the heat of the mediterreanean, but less so in the cool Autumn of England. Take some warm socks. Was abit noisy, but then this is London and somoene s busy building something somewhere.

title: Good location and value for money
text: The room and bathroom were basic but clean. Was pleased with the secured car parking area behind the hotel. The staff were extremely helpful and friendly. Public transportation was in easy reach - absolutely no complaints and will not hesitate to go back.

title: Good hotel, shame about location
text: Was quite happy with most things about this hotel. The rooms were clean and modern looking with adequate facilities (including plenty of sockets!)and a lovely comfortable bed. The bathroom was nice and large and included a roomy shower. Although it was located on a main road the noise wasn't too bad thanks to triple glazing on the windows. The only drawback for us was the location, with it being quite a walk from the nearest tube station (Elephant & Castle) although we did become acquainted with the bus routes and there were plenty of buses to central London.

title: Disappointing
text: Despite the not-so-low-price, the hotel service is disappointing. The hotel is clean and the room was unfailingly tidied up, but the breakfast is expensive and unsatisfactory, the receptionists didn't satisfy no one from my (absolutely reasonable) requests, and no one seemed to see me as a customer to make somehow satisfied. Never ever again.

title: A Good Hotel
text: Stayed one night having flown in late to Stanstead. The hotel was clean and comfortable and a reasonable price. The staff were friendly when checking in. Its not the Ritz but for the price we paid and its location it was good enough. One word of caution it can be a little difficult to find. You have to drive through the services but it is there.

title: pleasantly surprised
text: Stayed for 3 nights, Reception staff were very welcoming and gave us a slightly bigger room as we were staying for 3 nights. Room was at the back of the hotel, so very quiet. We had a lovely comfy bed with white linen, room and bathroom were very clean. Plenty of towels and the shower was a good size. There was a fridge, ironing board and hairdryer. Also there was a safe in the room at no extra charge. Staff were very helpful, and gave us lots of good advice. Buses stopped a few doors away, they take you into the city if you don't want to walk. The bar area could be a little less like a waiting room, but I think they are working on that. We would definitely stay here again, great value for money.

title: Better out there
text: We stayed here for business location was easy for London Bridge. The hotel is clean and had all the basics in the room but the location is not particularly nice and I felt unsafe on a evening walking around. I wouldn't pay full price either this is often offer nearer the time if you need a place to stay.

title: Good enough
text: My husband and I stayed here whilst working in London as it was the cheapest accommodation we could find. We were not expecting much but we were pleasantly surprised. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable although the pillows were a bit hard. There were plenty of storage, sockets and lighting options. I imagine it could get quite cold in the chillier months with the uncarpeted floors. The downsides were the shower head which had a horizontal spurt so, on the first morning, I got a face full of water when I turned it on, the television reception was intermittent and the room (at the front) was the traffic noise was noticeable, particularly the frequent sirens. Also our towels, damp from our morning showers, were folded and placed back on the rails meaning that they were still damp when we used them I the evening. We had no problems with the wifi.

title: Good
text: A nice hotel, clean a tidy from what we saw And the staff were helpful when checking in. Ok for what we wanted, a base!! A little too far from tube for our liking but there are good bus links to get you closer to the action if you don't want to use a taxi.

title: Never again
text: This hotel, despite it seems located in the centre, is in a very dodgy area of London. It is also VERY far from the Tower Bridge (it takes 20 mins to get to the bridge). They gave me a room at the first floor, facing Old Kent Road. That road is traffic congested and sleeping at night was practically impossible. At late night, I was in bed, with my barred eyes, repeating "never again!" to myself. Moreover my room was not very clean. Bed and bathroom were okay however and that's the only reason why I am giving 2 points and not 1.

title: Oh dear
text: I suppose for a budget hotel, we shouldn't expect too much but there was just too much to overlook. The power in the room works off the door card which means that when we landed, the room was very, very cold. We tried to relax for a short while before getting ready for a night out but not easy when you're sat in a coat. The shower in the evening was fine. Decent power and hot water but the towels are really small. The inadequate hot air heating eventually warmed it up just enough for us to go out but by the time we returned it was freezing again. We whacked the heating to full and jumped straight into bed. We only had 3 pillows between 2 of us so not enough. The noise coming from outside was terrible and I'm sure the windows weren't fitted right as the room just didn't warm up all night. In the morning, there was literally no water to shower with... No water at all! Turned the shower on and it dribbled slightly like an old man with a prostrate problem before giving up altogether. Had to make do with a wash at the sink (cold water) and a quick escape because we had really spent enough time in the place. We didn't bother with breakfast as it smelt pretty awful. I suppose if you are on a very tight budget and the usual budget chains are full, this place would do the job but please make it your last resort.

title: Mixed feelings about this one
text: I stayed here earlier this year, having got a late booking at a lower than normal rate. I would not want to stay here at the published prices. The location is in a fairly downtrodden bit of south London and whilst there are good bus services almost outside the door, it is not a great spot if you aren't visiting the area specifically. At first glance the hotel seems modern with stylish decor and purple floor lighting in the corridors. But you don't have to look hard to see the place is actually fairly basic. The staff were polite to me but not very well trained. I skipped the breakfast so can't comment on that. The bar turned out to be a can of beer from the reception fridge, which was a bit of a disappointment. If you want to eat in the evening, there is no dining room but the hotel has an entrance directly into the Chinese restaurant next door. It, too, is basic and expensive for where it is and what it provides. I'd stay again but only if the price was low and I really couldn't find somewhere better.

title: Betsan Williams
text: We stayed here in an apartment as have three teenagers so 1 room wasn't big enough. It was nice and clean, cooking facilities, lovely shower and comfy beds. Kids loved it. Staff were charming and happy to help. Easy access to buses and tube station. Lots of shops and takeaways near by. Would definitely visit again for price and easy access to city.

title: Clean, but !!!
text: Stayed in this hotel for one night clean but also pretty basic and a bit overpriced pay £109 for one night not including breakfast , Plus parking for one night at The back of the hotel was £25 which I think is outrageous considering the car pk had that in unsafe feeling about it which was shared by the Chinese restaurant with rubbish everywhere . now here comes the but the Showerhead was encrusted with limescale, water quality poor plus took good 10 minutes for the hot water which wasn't really hot , brown ring around sinkhole , told a member of staff about it all they could say was sorry, Think the staff need to have a little bit of customer care training. Would not recommend this hotel.

title: Cheap and relatively cheerful
text: Not that cheap considering how basic the place is, we paid around 120 for the double (two weeks in advance) room on booking.com but considering its in London it's to be expected. The room was clean and bed was comfortable, there were plenty of clean towels and shampoos/soaps, about all you can ask for in a budget hotel like this. It was ideal for us as we had business in elephant and castle but otherwise, it's a bit out of the way. My one complaint is this - upon returning to the hotel lobby, parched, at 4:30 am, there was absolutely no danger of the staff opening the bar for refreshments, disappointing, but not a deal breaker. Would stay here again if we needed to.

title: Excellent service very clean .
text: We stayed for 2 days for a wedding we were attending. There were quite a few of us so we had nearly 9 rooms. Rooms were all clean and tidy. Hotel is in a great location near shops etc. I would definitely recommend this Travel lodge.

title: Avoid the Breakfast
text: We came for a single overnight stay and found that the room was hot, its not really possible to open the window as the place faces onto a busy road. We paid £15 for two breakfast options next morning - I wish we had spent the money in the waitrose opposite! There was no orange juice, a really poor selection of undercooked bacon and no sausages. The mushrooms were dry and the staff rushed off their feet. I think that the coffee machine had seen better day - as the Lavazza coffee was very poor... If you get a cheap rate its worth a try but not at the £105 we were charged.

title: Another good stay at Raynes Park
text: On arrival there was some confusion about the room we were to stay in, having confirmed this by phone to Raynes Park TL two weeks before arrival. However, Tom on reception was determined to get the issue resolved and pulled out the stops to do so. Having gone back to my car, Tom was waiting for me as he had sorted out the room and everything was resolved. Well done Tom, yet another staff member with customer service as number one concern for customers. You WILL hear the trains at Raynes Park station but you can't have it both ways. Having that station so close is an asset for access to London. Lots of food options on the doorstep and a good Wetherspoons for a drink and breakfast. Overall, a great location, staff very helpful (particularly Tom on this occasion) and comfy clean rooms.

title: A fairly basic hotel, but has helpful staff and everything you need
text: Stayed here whilst visiting a relative in Raynes Park, but also wanted to get into Central London easily. Hotel is fairly basic but very clean and with decent size rooms. Breakfast was very good, but we didn't try any other meals, although the restaurant menu seemed good and reasonably priced. Staff very friendly and helpful. Didn't use the car park but it seemed to have plenty of spaces. Location (above the co-op) is very handy for the shops, pubs and eateries of Raynes Park. It is very close to the station, which has frequent trains to London. Wimbledon Common and Windmill a few km away - worth a visit if you have time to kill. Very happy with visit

title: Very enjoyable two night stay
text: This was my first ever stay in a Travel Lodge, and on the strength of this experience I would feel confident to book one again. We were staying for a family visit, and arrived from Wales after a long drive. Great to find the car park had spaces, and this remained the case throughout our stay. Check in was swift and pleasant. No wait, friendly receptionist. We had opted for an early check in, a worthwhile choice as we arrived soon after twelve noon, the start of the early check in. Our room was warm and comfortable. We slept well. Bathroom small, reminded me of a cross channel ferry! Plenty of room for make up , not always the case in much more expensive hotels. Excellent shower. Couple of negatives: duvet cover and pillow cases too small for their contents. Pillow and duvet poking out by morning. My husband would have liked a comfy chair, but there wasn't room for more furniture. Breakfast was very nice, plenty of choice. We had a couple of beers in the bar/ dining room one evening, and sat comfortably on a couch there. Very secure. From 10pm needed to use room key to enter hotel. At all times, corridor entry was by room card. Never before seen a bottle opener attached to the room desk. Would be happy to stay again. Thank you to all the very pleasant staff who cheerfully made us feel welcome.

title: Noisey but nice
text: I have stayed in numerous Travelodge's but has the smallest room I have known, and apart from the large double bed, there wasn't much room for anything else. It wasn't an issue for my wife and I, as we didn't spend much time in the room, but it could be for others The only other drawback is the noise from the trains, and this isn't an issue if you close the room window, but this would be a problem in warm weather, especially as there's no air conditioning On a positive note, the hotel is 2 minutes walk from Raynes Park station, there is a Weatherspoon's pub nearby selling cheap drinks and food, and there are 2 supermarkets round the corner. I must also mention the polish girl on reception who was kind enough to lend me a phone charger during our stay. We had left ours at home, and she went out of her way to find one we could use.

title: London Raynes park Travel lodge hotel
text: Situated in the central area of raynes park just a short walk away from the bars & restaurants just few metres away from the hotel there is the bus stop every bus that arrives takes you to the centre of Wimbledon which takes about 6to10 minutes the train station is also walking distance from the hotel which goes directly to London

title: Friendly staff making all the difference
text: I stayed here with a friend during Wimbledon fortnight and this hotel was really good, inexpensive and very handy for the train station. Many travelodges are the same but this one stood out for its very friendly and helpful staff. They had walking, train and bus options for the hotel to the tennis and gave good advice not to take a taxi from the station but to let them order one at a cheaper fixed rate. Breakfast was really nice. And it's right next to a mid-sized co-op which was handy.

title: Good new hotel
text: Good location, excellent transport connection, new fresh hotel, clean new bathroom, comfortable bed, helpful staff, spacious convenient room , nearby shops, free car parking , a children's play area in nearby park.

title: Brilliant place to stay
text: This travel lodge is so convenient for getting into central London 10 mins on the train . The free parking is a real bonus the place is extremely clean and the staff really friendly and helpful the breakfast was good

title: Good business hotel
text: The hotel is in a very convenient location, a minutes walk from Raynes Park train station so very accessible from Gatwick airport and close to the centre of London. The rooms are clean and fresh looking with comfortable beds and a bright light in the bathroom which is handy for getting ready in the morning. Body wash is provided in the bathroom but the dispenser in my room wasnt working unfortuantely. Hairdryers can be borrowed from reception free of charge. Breakfast is pretty decent with a selection of hot and cold options, coffee and juice. There is also a vendine machine by reception but it was out of order during my stay. There is a co-op attached to the hotel but it was closed by the time I got there. Overall I would stay here here again, it was comfortable and clean. Hope this helps!

title: Raynes Park
text: The Travelodge had comfortable beds, and a clean bathroom. Wifi was extra with a limit of two devices, would have liked it to be free, or unlimited devices. The room was cold when we arrived, and had trouble getting the heating to work. The reception desk helped us get the heat working.

title: Very friendly staff. Very clean room, but too hot. There is a fan provided. Good location opposite the train station.
text: The only negative was the wifi wasn't free. Staff very friendly. Room very clean. Good shower. Good location. Good amenities in the area. Room was too hot but a fan is provided. Very comfortable, clean room

title: Great for Chessington
text: We stayed here for one night so we could get to Chessington World of Adventure for opening. The hotel is clean and feels very welcoming. The staff (gentleman I saw on check-in and another I spoke to regarding my Wifi code that I hadn't received) were very polite & helpful. Impressed that the car park had normal sized spaces, not the extra narrow ones Travelodges normally have so I could actually get the kids out of the car, The room was a great size (had a large double bed and two single beds out for our family but still plenty of room to move about and for the kids to play). As others have said, you could hear doors banging (we were on the 5th floor, marked as the quiet floor) but they didn't keep us awake, just woke us up in the morning as many people were obviously leaving early. The tea station was well stocked and the kettle was clean. We were very happy that there were large mugs instead of the silly little cups you normally get. The shower was powerful and everything in the bathroom was spotless. The taps for the bath were very slow and you couldn't have water out of the sink tap and bath tap at once but not a problem at all. The room was rather hot and we had the fan on all night but we had 2 adults and 2 toddlers in one room so it was bound to be! We could hear the trains throughout the night but again, didn't particularly keep us awake. Took us about 15 minutes to get to Chessington in the morning. We would certainly stay here again and were very impressed, especially when compared with other travelodges (used to stay in a lot for work)..

title: Good value for money
text: I stayed here for two weeks. There is nothing to complain about. My room was big, the bathroom was clean and spacious and the beds are very comfortable. I really enjoyed the cozy duvet. Easy checkin and checkout and extremely friendly stuff. Thanks Miruna for your help and your hospitality. I’d definitely come back.

title: DISGUSTING, DIRTY, NOISY AND RUDE
text: Staff not helpful, if they deign to speak to you at all. Room dirty and smelly with wet carpets! Bathroom unfit for use by this disabled person, it was a "disabled" room, fitting insecure and dangerous and unclean. We were kept awake by the sound of running water, as the water riser was in a cupboard in our room! Design flaws throughout the room. Staff INVISIBLE. Noisy. Stayed here one year ago and everything was great! How things have changed in that time.

title: Raynes Park Travel Lodge
text: I use the Raynes Park Travelodge every month for business stays when I come to London. It is excellent value for money. The rooms are well equipped, modern and the beds extremely comfortable. The staff are all extremely friendly and helpful, and always available. The location is fantastic, being just opposite the British Rail station, and there are frequent buses to Wimbledon town center (only about ten minutes away). The train service is frequent, and you can get to central London in about 25 minutes from Raynes Park, or you can take the underground from Wimbledon. There are at least half a dozen decent restaurants within walking distance of the hotel. Wimbledon Village and town center are a short bus ride away (or a 20 minute walk), where there is an incredible variety of restaurants and pubs.

title: excellent leisure break
text: A friendly staff team at all times. The check in was smooth and efficient. Rooms were clean and fresh. The shower worked well. The hotel was well placed for the station so it was easy to get to central London and there were plenty of places to eat around the hotel as well as the hotel dining area.

title: Clean and bijou..
text: Wonderful helpful staff, within a small but well formed hotel! The atmosphere was very cheerful created by attention to detail in design and care!!! For a town center location this was an oasis of peace and tranquility!!!!

title: Another Good Travelodge
text: Opposite Raynes Park station and it also has parking! Trains every 5 mins to Waterloo station taking 22 minutes. Excellent location and a cheaper alternative to staying in central London. Cafe bar on site but there are also several good restaurants and three pubs in the immediate vicinity. Co-op on ground floor and a large Waitrose opposite. Hotel is modern, clean, comfortable and quiet. You can get some noise from the VERY busy railway but we got used to it very quickly. The trains virtually stop during the night. They caused us no problems at all even with the window open. Just remember that Travelodge is a budget hotel so not many frills nor air con, but you do get en-suit, TV, tea making and a very comfy bed! A thoroughly enjoyable trouble-free 2-night stay!

title: Average
text: Rooms are clean. Hotel is very convenient. Check-in staff were friendly but did not need to interact much during stay as we arrived quiet late at night. Room was on 4th floor overlooking the side road. Room shower holder was broken meaning shower would drop down all the time and had to be held to use it. Quite a bit of noise from corridors, closing doors etc. Also quite hot. Overall an average stay. Little things like adding soft closes to the room doors would really improve the stay.

title: Clean but a bit noisy
text: Rooms are clean and reception friendly, bathroom a decent size. I had a room facing road and train station which was a bit noisy . Overall a good experience and I would probably book again in the future if needed.

title: Room
text: 1st class in all areas ,breakfast was was good 8 out 10 for hotness . Staff were without exception friendly ,polite and looked after you .Parking was adequate and plenty . Shops were close and the area felt safe to explore safely

title: Excellent
text: Staff at Raynes park couldn't do enough to help the staff were very friendly the breakfast were lovely and the building was clean and tidy, we would definitely stay here again, the train links just outside of the hotel were brilliant, very central for everything.

title: Great Hotel
text: Very good hotel, well kept, comfortable rooms, fast Wi-Fi, co-op around the corner, and just across the road from Raynes Park train station with regular trains to Wimbledon and London Waterloo - Perfect when working in the area. The hotel staff were friendly and helpful. Breakfast was superb. Would definitely recommend to anyone looking to stay in the area.

title: Great stay in a great location
text: We stayed to visit Wimbledon and its a great location for that, but the location would be good for a visit to London itself, the station is only a few mins away with very frequent fast trains. We will be coming back

title: Low price yet excelled our expectations
text: We stopped here for 1 saturday night visiting the local area. Took 38 minutes from Kings Cross (change at Vauxhall for overground rail and hotel is 2 minutes walk from Raynes Park station). Polite staff. Ask for another set of towels as they only give you 1. Two pillow each and a fan in the room. Might get noisy in summer if you need to leave the windows open. Rooms were clean. TV had all the Freeview HD channels. Breakfast was great and resaonably priced.We booked the stay in advance for around £35. Would highly recommend if in the area and only a short journey to central London or Kingston (also worth a visit). Curry Leaves Indian nearby was also excellent and incredibly cheap.

title: Good location but poor breakfast
text: The hotel is relatively new and the room was clean, the bed comfortable and the bathroom was clean too. Stayed here for two nights on the 5th floor and because the weather was warm we had to have the window open which meant there was noise from the trains nearby. Booked a 'light breakfast' on the first morning which was good. We decided to repeat this on the second morning but the breakfast was very poor - the dregs of granola, no natural yogurt, fruit juice that was like coloured water, no fresh fruit at all, so we basically had tea and toast and a bit of granola. Tables were also not cleared quickly too. After a complaint from us, the management did refund us as they did not want us to be dissatisfied with our stay in any way. Good parking by the hotel for our stay.

title: Awful smell in rooms
text: Overpowering smell of cleaning chemicals in the room. Did not dissipate when opening the window. Woke up feeling sick with a headache it was so strong, it was still lingering on my clothes when I got home.

title: Great location and service
text: Got this room as a £20 bargain with a discount code. Quick check in by helpful staff and room was immaculate with a comfy bed. Because of its proximity to the train station you do hear train noise (it is London after all) but I didn’t see (or more importantly hear) any other residents during my stay.

title: a short stay
text: not bad on average WiFi iffy would stay again food breakfast good didn't have meals ideal for drop off to visit other places nice area clean out side as well as inside bar wasn't to bad with enough variety

title: Very pleased
text: Only stayed one night and really didn’t expect much as previous stays in travel lodges have been grim but Raynes Park was great for what I paid, no whistles or bells but everything you need. Rooms and restaurant extremely clean and welcoming. Staff seemed very helpful. Breakfast was very nice all in all a very pleasant stay

title: Lovely
text: We only stayed two nights but we slept really well, not too far from shops and the train station isn't far either. Clean tidy room, lovely staff and car park. What more can you ask for. We could have had breakfast for a bit extra, but we don't normally have much so decided not to have any from the hotel. There is also free wi-fi for 30 minutes or £3 for 24 hours which isn't too bad. Would go again.

title: Perfect location
text: We visited London to see 2 West End shows. This hotel was perfect. Free parking and very near the train station, 20 mins to Waterloo. Clean, good beds and nice breakfast. All the staff were polite and helpful. Will stay here again.

title: Very good value for money
text: We stayed here for a long week end visiting family in the area. Our room was clean and comfortable, it was also cleaned every morning. The Travel Lodge is conveniently situated for the train station , there is a Co -op underneath, Waitrose across the road and a range of small restaurants and cafes in the same street. Our room was hot but we used the fan which did help considerably. Staff were extremely helpful and obliging. We did not eat at the Travel Lodge but the restaurant area did look very clean. It is an easy (2 mile approximate) walk from Raynes Park to Wimbledon Common although if you do not know the area you will need a map. This we did and visited a Country Fair which made a nice change.

title: Excellent stay
text: Stayed in Travelodge Raynes Park and rooms were excellent and spotless. Very comfortable beds. Buffet breakfast very good, great selection to suit every type of eater. Would have no hesitation in recommending.

title: Great stay , great service.
text: Lovely hotel , great location and the staff are 2nd to none. Couldn't fault the place at all. Lovely spacious room very clean and tidy. Breakfast at hotel was great again with great staff. Booked early check in room not quite ready on arrival but was quickly resolved. It'

title: Great hotel location for london trips
text: A great hotel location for trips into London as it was only a 2 minute walk to the overground station. The Hotel was clean and tidy with all the things you would need. It had free parking on a first come first served basis. There was a bar which served all types of drinks and a restaurant that served breakfast dinner, tea and nightly pizzas. The Hotel staff were very friendly.

title: Handily placed for Wimbledon
text: This a good Travelodge, fairly new and located right in the centre of Raynes Park a few yards from the station and 10 minutes drive from Wimbledon.It has a cafe/bar and there are plenty of eating places just around the corner from the hotel. There is a large car park at the rear accessed from the next road from the entrance to the hotel. Comfortable rooms, everything worked.Reasonable rates for outer London. Has two lifts.

title: Noisy, lack of parking
text: The hotel is next to the railway station and although the room was far too hot we couldn’t open the window due to the noise. The family room has fold out single beds which were very uncomfortable. There is a terrible lack of parking and the paid breakfast buffet was not refilled unless you asked. We will not be back

title: Excellent value for money
text: This was our first stay at this Travelodege and after a particularly bad stay at one a few years ago I was at best apprehensive. The hotel is brand new so sparkles like a diamond. The receptionist was charming and check in was swift. Our room was a double so compact and comfortable for an overnight stay. It was very clean and the bed was very comfortable. As it was a hot night we had the window open and the only thing that disturbed our sleep was the noise from the road and trains but once everything went quiet we both slept very well. The bathroom is of a high standard and was very clean. The all you can eat breakfast was good value as it included cereals, fruit salad, yoghurts, bacon, scrambled eggs, sausages, fresh mushrooms, tomatoes and hash browns all cooked very nicely. In short a very pleasant stay and we will be staying here again!

title: Excellent, Comfortable, Efficient Staff
text: Very efficient from booking through to staff on hand at The Raynes Park Travelodge! Excellent rate of stay, Clean, Comfortable Rooms and Dining/Reception area! Accomidating staff! Free parking and Enjoyable Breakfast! Recommend!

title: Great stay and excellent team!
text: I visited Raynes Park with my wife on the weekend 5 August 2016 They have a great front of house team and I cannot compliment them enough. Good approach and attitude to any enquiry or request Rooms small but clean and practical and the breakfast was ideal as was the location to the train station If you want to eat and drink, it was on the doorstep without any problem at all Free parking was available should it be wanted but the train was so handy Well done the team at Travelodge Raynes Park, we want more of you!!

title: New favourite Travelodge
text: Chose the hotel for location and parking as a stop over between family visit in Cambridgeshire with 2 London shows. The hotel was in a great location very close to a station with a regular service into Waterloo.

title: Great value and location
text: Booked here for our trip to Wimbledon tennis (only a 10 min taxi ride away). Typical travelodge - fairly basic but clean. Rooms are quite small but that's London for you. Great location, near the railway station (so expect noise), with plenty of places to eat and drink, plus a waitrose and co-op for any 'bits' you might need. The staff we met were very friendly and helpful, including giving us all the info on various options to get to Wimbledon. Thank you Travelodge for a good value stay in London.

title: Great customer service
text: Paid for early check in, was too early for that but let me check in an hour early. The staff were very friendly. The location was good, just across from the train station and on top of shops and a post office

title: Great new Travelodge
text: Stayed at this new Travelodge in the last week. It is a newly opened Travelodge and is situated on the corner of Amity Grove approximately 2 minutes walking distance from Raynes Park Railway Station. A Car Park is also available for those driving to the hotel. The room was as you would expect from Travelodge, ideal for what we wanted, this being a comfortable bed, clean, great shower room and value for money. Travelodge recruit the most friendly and helpful staff and their customer service is by far the best I have ever come across, this one is equally as good. We didn't have breakfast at the hotel as chose to eat at Wetherspoons which is 2 minutes walk from the hotel. Other amenities serve the vicinity so it was just perfect. There are frequent train services for inner and suburban London destinations and It is approximately 30 minutes walk from Raynes Park to Wimbledon. Absolutely ideal for short break travellers who want to experience suburban London and business travellers. Will definitely be returning,

title: Staying in South London
text: The Raynes Park Travellodge is a 2 minute walk from the railway station making it easily accessed from either Waterloo Railway station or Victoria Coach and Railway stations (via Clapham Junction).Trains run about every 10 minutes so no need to use expensive taxis.

title: Great location for a quiter London experience
text: Got a bus to the door from Heathrow Airport just one bus change. There was a train station also across the road.Good location - short trip on train to Hampton Court Palace . We didn't need to go to city centre but would have been a short trip on the train. Hotel was bright, clean and breakfast was good. Would recommend this hotel.

title: VERY HOT ROOM
text: The room was very hot with NO air conditioning. I assume this is a known problem as there was a desk fan in the room. We were unable to open a window due to train noise from the nearby railway. No table near the mirror which made it difficult for my wife.

title: Great location
text: As I was going to be working in Wimbledon the day after I decided to book into this place so I can spend some time with friends in London I don't get to see often. The staff on arrival were warm and friendly and even thought I was a tad early let me book in. The room is a normal standard Travelodge room. But as its suposed to be very clean. The only problem I encountered is the delivery for the hotel and surrounding shops started very early. So if you want a quiet lay in maybe try getting one on the front

title: Great value for money in London
text: I have not been a fan of Travelodge in the past, but we were attending a party in the area and needed somewhere to stay.The hotel is relatively new, I understand, and it was everything we needed for a one night stay. The reception team were friendly and helpful, free parking was a bonus and the proximity to the station (1 minute walk) and therefore the centre of London (about 20 minutes) can't be faulted.The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. The room and bathroom weren't huge, but perfectly adequate for our needs.We didn't use the restaurant, so can't comment on that.If you're looking for somewhere to stay in London and don't mind being a little bit out of the centre, I would highly recommend this hotel.

title: 2 night stay
text: Came here for the Saturday, Sunday stay on the august bank holiday. Had the early check in which is a bonus and when we checked out on the Monday we could keep our car in the car park while we headed back into London for the day. There is a railway over the road and yes you can hear the trains but in fairness its so handy to have the station so near by. The one thing I notice here is the rooms can get very hot. There is a fan provided but if its a really hot day this could be a problem. Nice size bed although I found the mattress very hard , this however is down to personal choice of liking soft or hard mattress. A good supply of tea and coffee , milk in the room which was topped up. You can pick up more tea or coffee at reception. We asked to borrow a hair dryer which was obtained at reception. A nice size tv which has freeview . Wi-Fi is half hour free and then 3£ for 2 devices. Didn't take the Wi-Fi so can't comment on its speed. Breakfast. Saturday we went to Wetherspoons which was awful so Sunday tried the hotel breakfast. We found this so much better plus kids eat free. No fried eggs but the scrambled eggs were delicious. Would have this breakfast again. The staff we found very helpful and polite. A good team run this hotel and keep it clean. In summary this is good value and ideal for going into London on the train. Such a easy location to get to. Good size room and good facilities. It's right above a coop so handy for any bits needed. We will be back soon for our 3rd stay.

title: Mr &mrs g
text: Rooms are basic but clean and tidy. Bed comfy. Friendly staff, breakfast good but not outstanding. Convenient to train and buses. Some noise from traffic and trains but to be expected being so near central London.

title: Very good Hotel
text: We stayed 10 days in this hotel in Raynes Park, coming from Italy.The hotel is good, very clean and at the reception you find very accurate and kind persons. A very large parking is available for cars, and the railway station is at less than 100 mt. with very frequent connections to central London. Clapham Junction is at 10-15 minutes by train. Buses are very frequent to Wimbledon,Kingston or any other direction. The hotel is above a post office and a Cooperative market open up to 23,30. Many nice restaurants on the road. Rooms are clean and not noisy. Prices are more than reasonable compared with the service. Only one remark. If you stay for several days, there is not so much space organized for the luggage and clothes. We will certainly use again this hotel in the future.

title: Comfortable and clean hotel, always good standards
text: Hotel was very clean, room had everything we needed and the bed was super comfy, king-sized and gave us a great sleep. Our only issue was having a room across from a noisy railway line, but I guess that's just being in a city! Staff were very friendly and extra helpful and the buffet breakfasts were great value for money. This hotel is very close to Raynes Park station, there's a Co-op food store below, a Waitrose nearby, plenty bus services, restaurants and cafes galore - it's very well located. Can't complain about anything!

title: Travelodge, you know what to expect.
text: This is a fairly typical Travelodge, they're all much the same so you know what to expect. Th room was clean and comfy although the pillows were a it hard for me. The breakfast wasn't fancy but it was good all-you-can-eat fare. It was a little pricey but I suppose you should expect that in the London area. A good base for trips out.

title: Raynes Park Travelodge
text: Receptionists a bit snooty and blunt. Not that friendly, seemed to be An inconvenience to answer a simple question, too concerned with doing her own thing . shower was a bit grubby. Overall Average stay

title: Another nice stay
text: Once again a nice stay with good polite staff who are approachable and will help you out. The Travelodge has had some work done and it does show in that the carpets looked grubby with some staining and had lifted in places. Lift flooring had also lifted and didn't look to welcoming. Bedroom was clean and tidy, bathroom and shower was clean. This is a good place to stay as you are a short train journey from Central London

title: New hotel tiny room
text: The staff were excellent but there was no storage in the room or place to put suitcase. Hardly enough room for suitcase even on the floor. Absolutely brainless design. Would not recommend 'new' style Travelodge rooms. Crazy. New breakfast was good.

title: disappointed
text: best thing about this hotel is the staff, they were lovely, all very helpful and courteous. The room was clean and we slept well. There isn't any air conditioning and it was very warm when we were there but the room did have a fan which we used constantly. The worst thing is the food. we pre-paid for a full english breakfast, the hot food was luke warm, not great for pork items!The 'fresh' orange juice was anything but, it was quite unpleasant and the bread was green mouldy. The evening meal wasn't great either, frozen fish and chips. I would stay here again but I would never eat here again.

title: Visit to family
text: Very handy location for visiting family. Very close to public transport and places to eat near by. Good value for money. Bed comfortable but furniture in short supply. Heater in room so could control room temperature. Fan in bathroom not working.

title: Perfect
text: We stayed 1 night here and it was more than what we expected from a Travelodge. We were greeted by the assistant manager who was very polite and helpful.
