title: Be very wary unsecure site with automated entry system with no back-up.....
text: After a long few days of travelling arrived at hotel around 7pm with thousands of people heading to the fireworks.. Tried to register with the self-service machine which didn't recognise my surname, rang house keeping number no reply, started to feel quite scared alone in London with all these people around. Tried ringing the bell which was answered and then immediately cut-off, after 45 mins of trying to enter the hotel I decided to go and try some other hotels in the area. Fortunetly I found a bed for the night but as I was supposed to have been staying at onesixtwo for three nights for the tennis at O2 and had confirmed before leaving it was a very frightening experience. Around two hours later I was called to be advised that someone would come and let me in !!! I advised that I had made alternative arrangements and wished to cancel my entire booking whereupon I was told I would be charged for the Saturday night !!! I have not checked my visa yet but will be putting a formal complaint in re this accomodation. I would certainly not advise anyone to arrive at the hotel without ensuring someone will be there to meet you, my understanding from others around that my experience is a frequent occurence for travellers to this hotel. I would never have booked it over 6 months ago if I had realised it was an unattended building as I am a single woman who was travelling alone.

title: Nightmare on Westcome Hill 6th november 2012
text: Arrived around 8.30-9.00pm after spending a lovely day at the O2 tennis. My daughter had booked and confirmed twice that we would have a twin bedded room, this was not so, my daughter rang the owner who is in Brighton on a mobile to ask for a twin-bedded room, unfortunately we could not be moved so he arranged for the bed to be divided and the room rearranged. This was arranged after about an hour, but we were itching to have a shower and relax. TV didn't work. Room was also smelly, so windows were opened. My shower was fine but unfortunately for my daughter whilst she was showering the water got so hot she burnt herself and then it suddenly went cold. Not the end of the story, we went to bed, dozing off and around 11.30-midnight someone knocked on our door asking if we had a double room, this was very unnerving as we felt very uncomfortable knowing no-one was on site and obviously not knowing who was knocking on our door, this put us on edge all night hearing whoever going up and down the stairs, so no sleep, we were pleased to see daylight in the morning, I cannot believe that we were charged £140 for 1 night, a complete RIP OFF. Recommend look for alternative accommodation.

title: Never stay here!!
text: We booked a nights stay here after watching the tennis at the 02 arena. All other hotels nearby were full, and it looked lovely on the website. Saw the other trip advisor reviews the day before we went and thought it can't be that bad can it? Well actually it's worse. From the outside it looked like a hostel, inside wasn't any better. Check in system is electronic so there isn't even anybody to complain too. We were given the ground floor room which contained the boiler lovely and noisey!! The cleanliness of the room was like nothing I had ever seen, it was filthy. Everything seemed to be broke or loose. We really didn't want to stay but weren't left with much of an option as it was late on an evening. We didn't even make it to breakfast, we daren't to be honest looking at everywhere else! The worst thing is the price! I'm not sure how they dare charge £100!! I advise anybody who is considering staying not too, it's absolutely disgusting.

title: Horrendous - don't stay here
text: I booked a room for 12 and 13 October (room 6 for the night before my wedding, and the wedding night), and a room for 12 October (room 11 for the night before my wedding for my two bridesmaids). My friend booked a room for 13 October (room 11 for the wedding night). We also recommended other friends to stay. On 12 October, room 6 was very cold. I could not get the radiators to work and so rang the number on their website at about 10.15pm. We were told that he would be at the hotel in around 20 minutes to come and find out what the problem was, so I spent the evening upstairs in room 11 with the bridesmaids and waited for him. An hour and a half later he still hadn't turned up, so we rang and his phone was switched off! I spent a very chilly night in room 6, and was understandably quite upset that the night before my wedding I had to stay up past midnight to try and get the heating sorted, and then spent the night shivering. On the morning of 13 October (my wedding day) there was no hot water to shower, so I had to wait and use the shower in room 11. I complained to one of the staff about the heating and hot water, and she kindly found a heater to plug in to warm up room 6. It's unfortunate that she put the heater directly under my wedding dress. Luckily I came back to room 6 in time to cool the dress down before it set on fire. I had a hairdresser, other bridesmaids and family arriving. With the heat of the hairdryer, we decided to open the patio doors in room 11. I was quite distressed to find out that the doors do not unlock, even though they are linked to the fire escape. That has to be a serious heath and safety issue. Two of the staff also tried to open them but could not, and said that the hotel was already aware of this. My friends then took over room 11 and got ready for the wedding. They were unable to lock the door to room 11 from the outside, so they had to leave the room open for the whole day and night. Again, the staff advised that the hotel was aware of this. This is absolutely not acceptable, especially as one of my bridesmaids left her ipod in room 11 and it is now missing. When my new husband and I returned to the hotel in the evening on 13 October, there was still no heating (expect for the portable plug in heater). In the morning of the 14th, just before heading off on honeymoon, we could not even shower because the water was once again freezing cold. Once back from honeymoon I sent an email to the owner requesting a response to my comments and nothing was forthcoming. Terrible place, nothing like the website. The only good feedback I can give is to the hotel worker who served breakfast, she was lovely and seemed quite embarrassed by all the problems we encountered.

title: Rooms okay but breakfast poor not family friendly
text: Found this hotel on the website and thought would try a smallish place with the hope of a more personnal service. However, check-in is via a computer screen and there was no-one around to talk to or ask questions. Our room was on the top floor via 4 flights of stairs and the door to the room was smaller than a average room, the stairs were steep and tight. There was a patio style door which was locked and could not get it open even with the keyl However view from the room of London was spectacular. When went to breakfast on Tuesday morning was extremely disappointed as there was no cooked breakfast, the fruit looked as if it had been left over night and there was not much of it. The girl who served the tea told us that the patio had been broke for a while and even though she had informed the manager, nothing had been done. The toaster was not working properly and about an hour after breakfast, we had to have something to eat. However the girl who served us breakfast on the Wednesday morning was extremely helpful and seemed to have things, like the toaster working well.

title: Soulless
text: Yes this place is not a friendly B and B because there is nobody on site. Yes it is an absolute rip off. It is in a row of pretty grotty shops and hard to find. You have to check in via a screen which eventually worked for us. The room was so small one person had to sit on the bed so you could move around. For breakfast and cleaning there is a sweet girl who is holding the whole thing together. The room was clean but various things in the shower room were not working. The walls are not insulated so you can hear every movement from the rooms next door!!!! We were going to Eltham Palace so location was OK.

title: Awful guesthouse, nothing contemporary about it
text: I booked a 3 night stay at this 'hotel' that describes itself as a contemporary guesthouse. We were not expecting the Ritz, a semi-decent B&B would have been just fine - on arrival there was nobody there. No check-in desk let alone a 24 hour check-in desk. We eventually found a touchscreen machine in the very small foyer that allowed us to check in electronically and deposited keys to the room (incidentally all you need is a booking surname to get some keys, no further identification is required which poses serious security concerns). Once we got the keys we had to negotiate going up some small, narrow, steep stairs (no lift / elevator on-site) to a room on the top floor with our luggage. After recovering at the top we entered the room and found a TV covered in dust on the floor and a wire hanging out of the wall. Worried that the hotel may think this damage was caused during our stay we tried to contact them. After four missed calls, someone eventually picked up and told us that TV should have been taken away earlier.. (this is the only nice part) they offered to swap us into another room. This other room happened to be in the basement with very little natural light, contained many unwelcomed eight legged friends and had an insecure handrail leading down to it. After a first uncomfortable night we decided enough was enough. One the first morning, we left and cancelled. We called the hotel to ask for a refund of the remainder of the stay based on safety grounds (no one there and only two keys separating you from the outside world). Initially they said that would be OK and then after thinking about it for a few hours decided to refuse and stick to the cancellation policy. I would recommend this hotel to absolutely noone, unless you're travelling Europe on a shoestring budget and even then this there is no value for money in staying here. There is a very nice Clarendon just down the road in the village which you should pick instead.

title: So unnecessarily disappointing
text: We (I was with a friend) were expecting a cosy and friendly welcome from an establishment which calls itself a 'bed and breakfast' but, on arrival to a very tiny foyer, we were confronted with a touchscreen welcome. Actually, we didnot initially even notice the screen and had to negotiate with a voice on the entrance phone pad. The first thing this person did was to try to put the price up from 99 pounds per night to 120. (I had booked on Late Rooms). When we eventually managed to get booked in we had to trudge up a very steep, but nice and clean, stairway with our luggage as no lift was installed. The room was very small but clean and practical. The bed was comfy but let down by such lumpy pillows that we both used cushions instead. It wasn't a room to look forward to getting back to for a relax. We were both really looking foreward to breakfast as we were doing a lot of travelling. The breakfast room looked very inviting with nicely set tables, big plates and bowls. Unfortunately, there was very little to put in/on them. 3 different cereals, seeds, currents, tinned fruit ( no serving spoons), a wrapped bit of a loaf, a couple of flat cruissants, 2 pieces of insipid looking cheese and a slice of some sort of meat. After being served a very nice cup of tea my friend asked if we could order breakfast. She was told that the establishment had stopped offering a cooked breakfast since 2009 to which she replied, 'Well why have we got such big plates and knives and forks?' The answer was, 'Good question Some people make themselves a little sandwich'. I don't eat bread or meat. We were advised by someone else of a good place to eat breakfast so we went there. (Good review will follow). There was no one to take our grievances to and we felt very wary that we would be overcharged. As it happens, the price stayed at 99 pounds per night but, as breakfast was not really an option, we still felt overcharged, disappointed and that we'd had a dodgy experiene. We won't be going there again. EVER.

title: A rip-off. Might be OK at non-Olympics prices if they fix the showers
text: I booked this to go to Paralympic events at Greenwich as I needed to be within walking distance, so it fitted that bill. First the positivies: The room was well decorated, the bed was comfy, everything was scrupulously clean, and there were the usual decent toiletries, biscuits, tea etc., TV worked fine, and the heating was fine. The breakfast is a small buffet but has a good choice inc. fresh fruit but as others have said, you do have to work it all out yourself, including searching a bit for some items. So all that was fine, but for me there were a couple of significant downers that left me feeling like a mug: -the shower simply did NOT work properly. It took about 10 minutes for ANY warm water to come through. Not hot, just warm. Once it did come through I jumped in to try for a quick shower and shampoo as I didn't trust the water to last - but it wasn't even long enough for the quickest shower. After maybe 2 minutes it went freezing cold again. I tried jumping out and waiting for it to heat up - I tentatively tried to boost the temperature with the shower dials, but I only got another 2 minutes of warm before it went back to freezing. The shower unit looked new and is the same one my parents have so I knew this wasn't normal for the unit or that I wasn't using it properly. There was a notice telling you not to switch off the shower switch by the bathroom door but it SAID it was on. I needed to catch a pre-booked train and didn't have time to waste waiting for the shower to stop having a nervous breakdown, so I ended up having a cold shower. Not acceptable for a £150 B&B one night stay. - Of course (!) there are NO staff in this hotel. I was lucky enough to bump into a friendly chambermaid on arrival who fetched my key, but otherwise you're on your own. The girl putting the breakfasts out was in and out in a flash. I phoned the hotel number and explained the shower issue but the man who answered wasn't at the hotel and said he'd have to look later. He never called me back and for all I know never looked at the shower and all subsequent guests have caught pneumonia. - the room was a standard double but there was very little room and storage. Just enough space to squeeze round the bed and a bit more space by the door and bathroom. I'm used to travelling in Europe and smaller rooms as a rule, but this was definitely my limit of smallness for a double. - As others have said, the entrance is not brilliantly signposted, and is, quite unexpectedly, in the middle of a row of newsagents, hairdressers etc. The website is definitely rather misleading. OneSixTwo - you need to provide better on-site service, and you have to sort out the showers. Also, if somebody calls you to complain about something, the least you can do is return the call later on. I was really polite and made a reasonable complaint. You left me feeling like you didn't care at all, which is a shame. This kind of seemingly small thing goes a long way.

title: Trip to o2 to see Jesus Chris Superstar
text: Had problems finding a hotel as London Triathlon was on at the Excel, so eventually book onesixtwo even though some reports were not so good. I have to say I disagree and can not fault them. Excellent location (all though slightly suspect from out-side). They even helped us to check in early. Will use the hotel again, when next go to the o2.

title: Pleasant surprise!
text: My partner and I booked Onesixtwo last minute as we had planned a day at the O2 and decided at the last moment it would be more suitable to stop over. The hotel had very mixed reviews so we didn't expect much from it. We booked the superior room as many reviews said the rooms were too cramped. The superior room is their largest room and for the extra £20 I would recommend booking it as it was very spacious, comfortable and thoughtfully furnished. I work in the hotel trade myself and gave the room a thorough inspection, apart from behind the television, it was very, very clean. I had such a good night's sleep, the bed was very comfy. If you go with low expectations, you may find your stay more enjoyable. We completely missed it when we first drove up the road, it looks like the front of a shop. I found the room very boutique like, even though the rest of the building doesn't reflect this. I found that perhaps the price of the room was a little high when you are only offered a continental breakfast. I have stayed at cheaper hotels with the most fabulous full english breakfasts. Also reception is a automated machine, so their is no personal touch there either. We felt a bit like being in a big brother house. There was no sign of any staff until we had finished out breakfast two women with onesixtwo tunics came in poured themselves coffee and said if we needed anything, they would be on the terrace. It really is ideal for short stays, especially if you're planning a day at the O2. It really is only ten minutes away and is pleasant enough for short stays. Its easy to get to, you just really need to keep your eyes peeled once you're on Westcombe Hill. I wouldn't advise it for families, it is quite noisy at night, and I don't think it is roomy enough for more than a couple of people. It is a nice intimate setting, my partner and I enjoyed the boutique style room. I believe the website appears to be an accurate representation, allthough "easy free parking" isn't quite what I would call it. I had to park in a residential space and ensure we were gone by 10 or I could have got a ticket. We never saw the managers 'Kevin' or 'Tony', that other reviewers have mentioned. It was pleasant if a little pricey for what the service really was.

title: Not what I expected!!
text: Stayed here last week while at Paralympics. From reviews I expected a boutique B+B - not converted upper floors of a shop in a shopping parade. The entry is a narrow doorway sandwiched between a hair dresser and takeaway. Totally faceless - inside the narrow hall is an intercom and an automatic check in machine. The machine would not accept my reservation and after buzzing on the intercom for some time I was told that they had completely misspelled my name. Eventually I got in. The room, which I had been told was not a small double, had just enough room at the bottom of the bed to walk round - so goodness nows what a small double would have been like!!! Only good thing was that the bed was comfortable and the decor was ok - well so it should be in 2012. Other guests I met were similarly confused by what this place had turned out to be. Worst thing was I chose it because there was suposed to be free parking on the street within 2 minutes walk - there was none - it was all restricted 2 hour and a tow away zone. This caused a great problem as I had tickets for the Paralympics the following day - eventually got someone on the intercom again I was told about a carpark - so I had to get out there at 7am the next morning to make sure I had a space and it did mean I had to return earlier than I wished so I missed seeing a gold medal in the equestrian event. Somewhere I had read breakfast was "fantastic" - not so - myself and other guests had to search in cupboard for coffee - Kingsmill bread packets and cheap sliced cheese and ham straight out of the packet does not constitute a good breakfast . My advice don't stay here even though there is a bus stop outside the door. This is the first time I have ever felt moved to write a negative review.

title: Never again - nothing like the website
text: The Hotel looks very "boutique" on the website. in reality the fittings are of low quality, table wobbles, towel rail and shelf in the bathroom is loose. we were unaware that the hotel would not be manned (normally Hotels with "Do it yourself check in are MUCH cheaper eg £50-£80 not £240. On arrival the automatic check in machine did not have a record of our booking. We telephoned the chap who tried to check us in, finally acknowledging that the machine could not let us in. we waited 10 minutes for a charming young lady to arrive and attend to another guest who was concerned about parking. The young lady spent 10 minutes with her showing her the Marks and Spencer Car Park. After 20 minutes we were shown in to room 3 (not our room) then into room 1. the shower did not work. I telephoned the chap again and explained that we were tired and so far our experience of onesixtwo was terrible and i felt like leaving! He told me to do just that! finally getting the shower to work we left to walk to Blackheath. We dcided to check the front door key. It did not work. We called the chap again who was most unhelpful. Fortunately at this point your sister in law arrived and told the chap that the key did not work. She tried her best to recover the terrible situation. In summary 1) The hotel is * star in reality and it is represented as **** on the internet and in price (The Clarendon hotel in Blackheath had vacancies at the same price with a car park/ staff/ quality fixtures and keys and showers that work, my error of judgement to choose 162 over the Clarendon) 2) The check in procedure was akin to a Travel lodge @ £80 ish not £240.00. It took 20 minutes to get to our room 3) the man at the end of the phone is short, rude and unhelpful. 4)your sister in law was very charming and tried her best to recover the situation. All in all it was the most horrific and disappointing Hotel experience I have ever had and i have spent the last 30 years travelling both at home and internationally on all budget levels *** to ***** star.

title: Average hotel in good area of Greenwich
text: We always use Trip Advisor when booking and usually only select hotels with excellent ratings. This hotel had received mixed reviews but we had to book somewhere at short notice and there was limited availabilty in this area. There was no-one on check in when we arrived but there was an electronic check in machine which dispensed the keys. We were told there was unrestricted parking nearby in Mycenae Road but there were signs restricting parking to 2 hours from 0830-1900. We were told this was because of the Olympics so may revert back to unrestricted when they are over. Fortunately, we did not need to leave the car there during the day, otherwise not sure where we would have parked.The room was a small double and was ok - clean and comfortable apart from someone else's hair in the shower drain hole and a leaking shower head. There is no air con so slept with window open and in the morning there was a dawn chorus of pigeons, which some people may not appreciate. The breakfast was continental buffet - limited choice but ok. There is a good pub at end of road. The price of £79 is reasonable for London, so can't complain too much. London is totally overpriced - it's not the capital of rip off Britain without good reason. If you want value for money, go elswehere.

title: A hotel that bends over backwards...
text: My new wife and I spent our wedding night at OneSixTwo after our wedding. It might seem an unconventional choice for a wedding night but our wedding was filmed for a reality TV show in the local area and we wanted something different for us and our guests. We virtually took over the hotel with 8 of the 10 rooms being taken up by wedding guests and from the second we arrived (a very late check in of midnight!) to the second we left (a generously offered extended check out) we were treated like royalty. Breakfast in bed offers (and an extended breakfast time), rose petals on our bed, the extended check out were all things we wouldn't have expected. Dawn, who was amazing, even gave us a wedding card and was helpful and polite throughout. If you're staying in London, and want a stay in a contemporary, comfortable and relaxed environment we seriously cannot recommend this place any higher. Fabulous!

title: False Advertising, not so much of a bed-room more just a bed!
text: I stayed here (room 2) for a weekend in London and trip to the O2, due to the location and decent reviews. After my two nights here I had many gripes about this hotel and definitely wouldn't stay here again. The room:- You can't even walk round the beds without touching the wall and the air con unit (which you can't have on if you want to sleep as they are so noisy) makes it even worse as it's so big - when I complained they said 'all our rooms are small!' The shower you had to wait for hot water for up to 3-4 mins. As for the fixtures and fittings, they might of been nice at one point however its a shame you can't do simple things like put a drink on your bedside shelf (I tried this and it fell off due to it not being level!) The shower rail and bathroom door handle both fell off. I complained to the staff and they came back with 'sorry I am not a handyman but we will let the management know' (surprise surprise I have heard nothing) Noise/Terrace:- Other reviewers have mentioned the pigeons, I think its quite obvious there is a problem with them if you cover the whole of the yard and the bathroom terrace with a net. Oh yeah and no hot breakfast and they don't keep it stocked up, I had to ask for tea bags both mornings! (i am aware that on the website it now says continental breakfast however I am sure when I booked it was a full English) So to sum up, if you want to stay in a bedroom with no room and fixtures that aren't fitted, with a massive air con unit that is so loud you can't have it on (they turn it on and leave it on all day when you are out - nice energy saving guys!) then this is the place for you. Oh and if you want to sleep after 5am (when the pigeons wake up) then bring heavy duty earplugs (or turn the air con to block out the noise) As an aside, there is free parking and bed was comfy.

title: Never again
text: We stayed for 1 night & that was enough. We booked in expecting the place to be how it's portrayed on the web site- how misleading. The room was clean apart from the dirt in the bath and the live moth in the bed and the tv didn't work. The worst £120 we've ever spent!

title: Lovely place.
text: This is the forth time we have stayed in this hotel, we have had a different room every time. The room this time was number 1, it was lovely, bed was comfy, tea and coffe were in the room, t v, some where to hang your clothers, breakfast was nice. This time we went by bus to the o2, which was recommended by the hotel which was alot better than going by taxi and cheaper. Would i go back, yes.

title: Very average place to stay
text: We were not expecting much anyway given the decent price me and my partner paid for the nights stay. We booked it because we were to attend the Jay-Z & Kanye West Watch The Throne Tour at the O2 Arena, which was very close by and only 6 quid by cab. We only stayed one night and it had everything we required besides an ice bucket which I very kindly requested from downstairs but there was "nothing we can do" due to the manager being absent from the building, not the hardest of tasks but oh well.. Swiftly moving on. The so called 'Hotel' lacked a somewhat personal touch however the bed was comfy, breakfast was averagely pleasant and if we ever attend an event at the O2 again, I'm sure this would be our preferred choice of stay!

title: Great hotel for a one night stay
text: Stayed at this hotel when my husband and son went to an event at O2. Yes the rooms are small but you are told that on their website, which is great for 1 night but I think would be a problem if you were staying for a longer period. When we arrived we saw the kebab shop etc and were quite concerned but when we went inside and met the Manager who is v. pleasant and he showed us to our rooms these concerns were proved unfounded, you would never know you were in a busy London high street from inside. The Manager made us very welcome and could not do enough for us in giving advice on how to get to the O2, where to eat locally etc. In the morning we had breakfast in a very light and airy dining room where we had a continental breakfast which was more than adequate, you could eat as much or as little as you wanted. My only warning would be that I was told I could park on the street outside but this is after 6pm and before 8am and would suggest that you park around the corner in a residential street but this was not a problem as it is quite a nice area, I only wish I had been aware of this before the £63parking ticket! Would recommend this hotel unreservedly.

title: Very standard and a little disappointing
text: Paid £89 for one night stay in room 1 (Most basic room I think). The B&B is right next door to a Kebab house but being that we stayed on a Saturday night and our room was at the front of the building, I must say we weren't kept awake by any noise. You have to ring a buzzer before you can enter the building. Given the access code to let yourself in & you are told what room number you are in. Found the right door but with no light bulb in the landing light this made it a little tricky! Door is unlocked for you to go in & our key was in the room. It's a nice enough looking room but leaky shower with more water coming out of the unit than the actual shower head. Dual tap on sink was very woobly. No light bulb in bedside lamp on one side of the bed. Bed appeared comfy but it was just an old mattress with temper topper. The radiator wasn't even attached to the wall and was just resting on the boxed skirting. The whole building was unbelievably hot during the night. Infact we couldn't sleep due to the temperature. Had windows open, radiator turned right down and there is a air con unit in the room which despite the loud noise of it we just had to turn it on. Come the moring we were wondering about the breakfast we had paid for. Without investiating the building it is not really obvious where the breakfast room was and there is no one on site to assist you. I ended up phoning the mobile number we were provided in a guest manual just to ask about breakfast. The room was nice enough, very cramped if they were ever fully booked. Nice but basic breakfast. We even cleared our own table as it seemed to be expected of you. We saw one person who worked there very briefly and as we felt she didn't even say goodbye or thank you for staying. I must mention about the parking. Basically we couldn't find anything without a long walk back with our luggage. We ended up parking in a residential area which requests a permit. We took the chance & lucky no parking fine. But that was very risky and wouldn't recommend it. Overall fine but little disappointed.

title: Comfortable and clean, great for O2 visits
text: Stayed here for a concert at the O2. Cannot fault the place. Lovely clean room with an extremely comfortable bed. We stayed in Room 11 and was great space for a 1 night stay. Room had free wi-fi which is always useful! The bathroom was clean and well taking care of. No bad words about the room whatsoever. Excellent location if you need to visit here. Good bus links to get to the O2 which stop directly outside the hotel and North Greenwich station. If you are looking to travel there by taxi use the service the onesixtwo recommend – they charge a set rate and not a meter, so if you’re stuck in traffic it’s not a huge worry! The gentleman who greeted us on check in was very friendly, he also served us at breakfast the next morning and was still as chirpy as the day before. The breakfast was plentiful. Continental was on offer, breads, cereals, meats and cheese available, tea and coffee, orange and apple juice. Pretty much all you require! Overall had a lovely stay here – usually book chain hotels but will most likely be using the Onesixtwo for my next stop at the O2.

title: Great location and very clean
text: I stayed here with a friend in Mar 2010 and went see Lily Allen at the O2. The location of the hotel location is BRILLIANT, its 5 mins from the O2 Arena. The location may be great but our room was a little on the small side to say the least...we stayed in room 5 I think. The sheets and beds are soooooooo comfy, the bathroom is tiny but very very clean and there was The White Company toiletries. We only stayed one night and I slept like a baby. Their website is a little misleading, we didnt have breakfast so i cannot comment on that but the hotel is a converted shop? i think....... and is in the middle of several houses/shops and is next is to a kebab shop. This was handy as we needed a can of coke or two (there is a minibar in the room, which you can leave cash for!) The window did'nt close properly which meant when the heating cut off in the early hours the bedroom was freezing by 6am and that was with the curtains closed. All in a great time and we would stay again!

title: Some good, some not so good
text: As we had read on these reviews, the key was dispensed through a machine which is slightly weird. Also our key got stuck but it was easily remedied as a staff member was on call out, and they were very apologetic and trying their best. The room was ok, but the furniture is starting to show a little wear and tear. The bed was very comfy with nice sheets and it's a great location. The breakfast was fine with a good selection, and a very friendly woman welcomed us and served us tea and coffee. It's not a luxurious place, and could do with a few replacements but fine overall.

title: Great Place
text: I have stayed at this place and its excellent, its near to the O2 and other local attractions namely the Olympics 2012. The rooms are clean, great breakfast! The host Ken deserves a special mention, hes a fantastic guy and nothing is a problem!!

title: Small Hotel, nice room with comfy bed - great for O2
text: Easy to get to after gig at O2. Rang ahead as we would be booking in late (about 11.30pm) not a problem, great checking-in service which just required entering name and other details then our key dropped into a secure box - ingenious! Room was small, but perfect for what we needed - we had a complimentary bottle of wine in our room, which was a lovely touch for our wedding anniversary. The bed scored a 10/10 for comfort, lovely big bathroom with White Company shower gel and shampoo. Don't be put off by the street outside, this hotel is great inside. The kebab shop next door was perfect for a late night 'apres' gig 'snack'. We rang the hotel to let them know we'd be late checking in as we would be going straight to the O2 and they recommended getting the 422 or 108 bus instead of a taxi - we did this and were dropped off just down the street from the hotel - saving a small fortune in taxi fares and a long wait at the taxi queue at the O2. Breakfast was lovely -M&S bread and pastries etc, very friendly chap made us coffee and the lay out was very sociable to chat to other guests. Would definitely use again if going to O2.

title: Brilliant Place
text: Me and my boyfriend (young couple) stayed here for the night after watching the football at The Valley. The place was immaculately clean and really well decorated. We stayed in what was described as a "small double". The room was indeed small, however for one night it was fine. The en suite bathroom was still of decent size and, like the room, was immaculately clean and well fitted out. We only saw 1 member of staff when we stayed there, which was at breakfast. We had to check in electronically and although was very easy to use, felt a little odd as sometimes I think you just want to see a friendly face that can answer any questions or concerns you may have. Having said this there was a welcome pack on the bed that answered any questions we might have had. My one slight disappoint is that there was not a cooked breakfast: just a range of cereals, meats and bread. I would 100% recommend anyone to stay here if you are just going to the Greenwich area for a night. If it is London where you want to mainly visit then this hotel would still be OK if you wanted to save on money but not necessarily the quality of the hotel. It took us about 20 minutes to get into the city centre (via bus and tube).

title: Dirty and Dated!
text: To be honest with you we were very disappointed with the hotel. As we have small children a night away is luxury. When we booked the hotel it sounded very nice. To turn up and see it was in a parade of shops and next to a kebab shop wasn't very impressive. The service was good on arrival. But again when going into the room we found lots of body hair on the bed which was vial. The overall cleanliness of the room was poor. We felt it hadn't been cleaned and the carpets were dirty. We decided immediately we wouldn't be staying for breakfast and slept with our clothes on. For the room cost of £100 we feel badly ripped off and felt the website is very misleading.

title: ICE COLD WATER IN SHOWER!
text: In the morning when I woke up and went to have a shower the water was ICE COLD! The staff advised that there is one boiler per floor and it happens when the hotel is full - we have to wait for the water to heat up! I would hate to be there in Winter! On a positive site the one staff member that we met was very nice and very friendly, but that is not enought to make up for NOT having HOT WATER! The breakfast was very minimal.

title: Small, cheap, impersonal.
text: The hotel OneSixTwo in Westcombe Hill, Greenwich, is advertised as a “boutique hotel”, which to me gives the impression of a fashionable, cosy, and a delightfully intimate alternative to the large impersonal hotel chains

title: Brick wall of rudeness
text: Having booked to stay a night at OneSixTwo from the lush looking website, I wish I had stuck to what I know! The position was disappointing but the room seemed fine when I went in, though a bit small for my 6ft 3 rugby frame. The evening started badly when the bathroom smelled of damp - the TV freeview signal was pixelating all evening so viewing was imposible. The bed was excellent though. In the morning when I went down, I complained about the shower and the TV and said I would forget breakfast (I wanted a cooked brekie and they only had continental on offer) I also made a comment about putting something on the trip advisor website hoping I would get some form of compensation for the sub standard room for a four star establishment. The lady was very apologetic and said she would let me know. They got back to me and told me that there was a problem with the water and the shower and they would refund the £7 breakfast - no mention of the water and TV - to cut a long story short - I spoke to possibly the most rude and aggressive manager I have ever come across who has refused to give me his name and told me that if we were face to face we wouldn't have a problem!!!! The accusation that I verbally assaulted a member of staff and threatened to shop them on the internet (this is the first time I have reviewed) was blown up - the first conversation with Mr Tough Guy ended in him ranting and then [--] you and then put the phone down! Call 2 was only answered when I used a different phone and a complete refusal to give me any details to complain - hence this review - Customer service is alive and well in Blackheath!

title: Clean, cosy and friendly!
text: We stayed here for two weeks on a vacation to London and basically to watch the ATP tennis finals at the O2. It was only 15 mins per bus to the arena so very convenient. As for our stay we found the place cosy, clean and the manager (Kevin) and the staff very help and friendly. Breakfast was a feast of fruit, breads, etc.

title: Good nights sleep
text: I stayed with my daughter for one night to watch tennis at the 02. The now legendary Keven was just as described! As soon as I got off the train at St Pancras he rang to ask if I needed directions and on arrival gave us a sheet with very detailed instructions on how to get to the 02 by bus and how to get home, which really helped. We also had the attic room and it was just as described, with 2 comfy double beds in alcoves, which gives you a bit of privacy. The breakfast was very good for a cold buffet and nothing was too much trouble. I know this sounds pernickity, but there was just a couple of things that would have made a good stay into a great one. The central heating didnt work and there was a noisy electric fan heater that blew out hot air, which i didnt fancy using overnight so it was a bit nippy. There was also limited tea/milk etc, and when we came back at about 23.00 there were no shops open anywhere around the area (which did surprise us). It would have been nice to have access to extra supplies or been able to use the breakfast room to make a cup of tea and have a biscuit. There was also an empty tissue box in the bathroom ( I told you it was pernickity!) All in all though, I do hope to return next year. It was very clean, comfortable and very convenient for the 02.

title: Misleading website and reviews
text: Cannot understand the good reviews on here. Ruined a romantic weekend. Room was tiny, noisy and dirty, up steep stairs. Bathroom tiny with peeling paint. No reception area. Looked more like a dentists from the front. Will not be returning.

title: Completely agree with previous reviews
text: My wife and I tried to book this hotel about a week ago but it was fully booked. We settled for the nearby and much larger Clarendon. Having booked in to the Clarendon we were told that they had no recollection of our specific booking request and recieved a very "computer says no" attitude from the reception staff. On the off chance we tried ringing 162 and by luck they had had a cancellation. How lucky we were. As in previous reviews, the rooms are very tastefully decorated, the shower spacious, modern, powerful and easy to adjust (just don't run the cold tap in the sink whilst someone is in the shower as it makes that water very hot). The bed was easily the most comfortable I have ever slept in and Kevin, the Manager, could'nt do enough for us. We only live in Margate but like to visit London now and then and having found this little gem we will go more often.

title: A Gem
text: What a fabulous find! It is a small guesthouse with comtemporary furnished rooms, spotlessly clean. The continental breakfast was varied and plentiful. The manager made us feel extremely welcome and was well informed on transport and local attractions. Can't recommend highly enough we will certainly be returning!

title: Pleasant Suprise
text: I booked OneSixTwo as a stop over for a long weekend to attend a wedding. The day before I was due to stay I looked up the location just to confirm and thought 'Oh No!' when I saw the photo on google street map. The website for the B&B cleverly photographs the upstairs windows and does not show that it is located on a busy street squeezed between a kebab shop and a newsagent - but don't let that put you off! The B&B is conveniently situated about a 10 min walk from Blackheath Village in one direction and Greenwich park in the other. Westcombe Park rail station is about a 5 minute walk away and takes you to central London in about 10 minutes. We were greeted (2 hours early) and allowed to drop off luggage even though the room wasn't quite ready and were given a key to return at our leisure - great service! The room (room 3) was very small but nicely furnished and very comfortable with a great shower and nice toiletries. It was suprisingly quiet given the location with the exeption of the pigeons nesting outside the window and what I believe was a boiler in a cupboard in the room which struck up a number of times throughout the night!! There is a small fridge with drinks and snacks in the room, but all at additional cost. Tea and coffee facilities were complimentry and most wlecome after a 4 hour journey. We stayed for 3 nights and stocks were replenished daily. Breakfast was served from 8am to 10am over the weekend which was very sociable. A lovely spread of fresh & dried fruit, cereals, nuts, pastries, lovely bread for toasting and a variety of jams, spreads, cheese, ham, eggs etc as well as the ususal breakfast beverages. I was slighlty disappointed that the 'full english' was no longer available but did feel better for it! Breakfast was a 'help yourself' affair which was perfect to relax and take your time over with no pressure to hurry and freedom to have as much or as little as you fancy. The room was reasonably priced for London. An added bonus was the FREE parking just round the corner - unheard of in London! I wouldn't stay here again for a relaxing break but it is an ideal for a place to stay whilst enjoying a sociable weekend in London.

title: Cute
text: I stayed here with my partner as we went to the O2 to see Peter Kay. When we arrived it isnt in the most glamorous location but the gentleman that greeted us was really lovely and couldn't do more to help. We had a room on the top floor (up some quite steep stairs) which was lovely and had two double beds, a lounge area, small balcony, and a great bathroom with a jacuzzi bath! My partner and I slept in 1 of the doubles, but it was nice to have the choice as we do both quite enjoy our space haha. Before we went out to the O2 the hot water stopped working, but the gentleman there fixed it straight away and it was fine when we got back. We were also told all the information we needed about buses, taxis and restaurants. We chose to get a taxi ordered for us. All in all, i would say don't judge a book by its cover, this is a lovely little place with great personal service. Would definately recommend.

title: Sorry, almost but not quite!
text: Stayed overnight after a show at the O2, about a 10mins taxi ride away don't walk - the hotel room book suggests half an hour, but in reality more like 45minutes on not very pedestrian friendly roads! Set among and in a row of shops, so doesn't look like a guest house from the outside. Clean rooms, noisy portable air con unit that kept cut tting in and out during the night (covered the noise from the street though). We had booked on the internet and were given a room (room 1) at the front - very noisy! Get a room at the rear of the hotel if you want a better nights sleep. Several problems - awful, lumpy sinthetic duvet on the bed, the hand basin tap in the bathroom was loose, the shower was really small and the water turned ice cold after a few minutes, the towel rail had been replaced a few times, shame nobody had filled the holes behind it. White towels, yes, fluffy? not so sure about. And what about bathrobes? looked hard couldn't see any, glad nobody knocked on my room door!. On the plus side, a double room with two armchairs, that doesn't happen in a lot of hotels. Staff on duty only at certain times of the day, and then they are usually out in the street, drinking tea and talking with delivery drivers. Continental breakfast is only OK. Why? although the pastries and bread seemed fresh, the platter of sliced meats and cheeses had been in and out of the refrigerator several times and had a film of moisture all over it. The milk for the cereals and beverages wasn't chilled (and it was during the time of 25C temperatures! Mmmmm! ) Reasonable selection of teas, but the coffee was disgusting. It had been made in one of those drip, drip filter machines early in the morning, and was still sitting on it's hot plate nearly two hours later and burnt and bitter. There was a hot water urn, so why not supply one cup cafitieres and coffee in pouches so that guests can make fresh coffee as well as fresh tea? The website says it has a "boutique feel" but I think that , although it tries very hard, it doesn't quite make it! But at the price, it's an OK place to stay if you need to overnight in the area.

title: STAY WELL CLEAR !!!
text: This Hotel is not what it shows on there website !!! Worst Hotel we have ever stayed in and will not be returning !! Would like to ad the staff who were at the hotel were very friendly and so helpfull. but the staff we spoke to either on the intercom or phone were so rude. It seems a very money grabbing hotel and no customer care !!!

title: Overpriced, not like pictures, wouldn't recommend
text: Tiny rooms, no storage, 3 coat hangers. Shower in first room was electric and went from scalding to cold and was unuseable. We phoned and were moved to another room, the shower was not electric in there but just as bad (seemingly the water board were working on the water which reduced pressure) so 2 nights without a decent shower. Radiator did not work in bathroom, had stone tiles so was absolutely freezing. Mould on bathroom ceiling and loose tap. Service was very helpful, breakfast was fine and beds were very comfortable and clean. Probably was beautifully decorated 5 years ago but no way is this of "Boutique" quality.

title: Great welcome and hospitality
text: Recently stayed at onesixtwo and would definitely stay again. Kevin, the receptionist was extremely helpful and welcoming. Breakfast was very good too. Bathroom was very clean, large shower and nice White Company products. Thank you.

title: A hidden gem.
text: Booked to stay here when attending an event at the O2 and it certainly is ideally positioned for this. Onesixtwo looks like nothing from the outside but once through the door this is as good as any boutique hotel you'll find. The attention to detail in the rooms is 5* without a doubt. Excellent quality beds, immaculate decor, spotlessly clean, well equipped and deep fluffy towels. The proprietor seems genuinely delighted to see you and will do everything he can to make your stay perfect. Breakfast is a superb continental buffet. Situated close to Greenwich and with excellent transport links this is an oasis of calm away from the busy, often rude, city centre. Very strongly recommended

title: Generally good a few minor glitches. Kevin was the hotel's best asset!
text: Generally good overall. My partner and I stayed here for one night this weekend when we went to watch Lee Evans at the O2 and it was ideal for what we needed: contemporary accommodation near to the O2. Our room was fairly small and the bathroom needed a bit of a cosmetic touch-up as the floor tiles were wobbly and the sealant in the shower was very worn along with the paint work on ceiling. The decor was lovely modern with minor wear and tear. Bed was perfectly comfortable and the room had plenty of facilities: tv, hairdryer, tea and coffee etc. The location is ideal! Frequent buses practically on the doorstop to the O2. Just what we wanted! But I have to say the hotel's best asset is Kevin the manager! Very friendly, knowledgable and welcoming! Overall a good stay! Ideal if you just need somewhere to stay when visiting the O2!

title: Quiet,residential area Sharon G
text: We stayed one night at this hotel and will recommend highly to family and friends. The small double ensuite was very pleasant, a very comfortable bed,with a quiet location overlooking beautiful gardens. There is small terrace at the back if you want to smoke or have a quiet drink. Kevin the MC was very helpful and went the extra mile to make us welcome. He was very knowledgable about the area.....which was a great help. We had a very good continental breakfast.....healthy options, lovely fruit salad. Lots of tea/coffee. Terrific value with good transport links to O2, Greenwich,Tower Bridge, CanaryWharf

title: A hidden gem
text: We stayed at Onesixtwo while my son was taking part in a half marathon in Greenwich and I'm so glad that we chose this B & B. Our room was small but the bed was very comfortable.We had an en-suite shower room, TV, hospitality tray and a mini safe. Breakfast was lovely. So much choice and lovely quality. Kevin, the manager, was so helpful and obliging. Nothing was a bother for him. We asked him if he could recommend a nice Italian Restaurant close by and he not only recommended it, he tried it out too!! And so, we had a fabulous meal at Bella Vista Cuccina. Thanks Kevin. Regular buses ran from just outside of the hotel down to North Greenwich Tube and the O2 (every 5-10 minutes). There is a nice pub very close by which also serves food and a chinese restaurant a few hundred yards away. Nearby Blackheath Village has a bigger selection of eating places and some lovely shops. Although not ideally placed for City Centre shopping, we would stay at Onesixtwo again now that we know how easy it is to commute into the City and because its a good location if you're visiting the Greenwich area. If you want the City Centre, big luxury hotel with impersonal service and a full English breakfast, then Onesixtwo wont be for you, but if you want a really comfortable bed and a personal yet professional service in a quieter location, then try it out. We would stay there again without hesitation. If you're travelling by car, there is free parking very close by.

title: Though I fully paid for it, I opted last minute for not going because of the 300 pounds deposit
text: As a due and fair premise, I have not been in this structure as last minute I was too scared to go there, and I decided not to show up and book another place. So, my review has nothing to do with the place itself but surely it has to do with the policy and the customer service of this place. I had no idea of the fact I had to pay 300pounds cash deposit on the check in and, when I wrote to them a very long email almost two weeks before my stay telling (and literally begging) that I did not had the money for the deposit, they just replied with one line saying "it's not my problem, booking is not refundable". After another email in which I was insisting, they told me it was ok not to pay but, as alternative, I should have left my passport for three days of my stay. Anyone I told about that advised me not to go to this place, as it is pretty weird and uncommon to leave a passport for so long (especially, as it can be read in many reviews, there is no one at the reception). Furthermore, many reviews, here and booking as well, mention the unsafety of the place in the night (especially over weekends), with drunk people partying in the apartments, and this put a further red flag for me not going there, given that I was a female solo traveller. In sum, I would advice everyone to read carefully all the rules for going to this place, including 300 pounds cash deposit (never heard in my life for such a short stay) and not making my mistake. Perhaps I was just unlucky, as I also read many positive opinions and reviews about this place, but this was my experience with them and i think it is fair to share it with other customers, as this whole thing with them created so much stress for me.

title: Very comfortable stay in London
text: I spent several days with a group of friends in this apartment complex on a recent visit to London. We had a three double-bedroom apartment with en-suite bathrooms. The apartment was very clean, the rooms quite spacious, and the location is great for trips to central London and also extremely convenient for Heathrow as the Tube Station (a few minutes' walk from the complex) is on the Piccadilly Line. Supermarkets and lots of shops open until late in the area and I had a lovely view of the park from my window. I wasn't the one who booked the apartment but had read reviews here and was ambivalent about what to expect. Thankfully, we did not have a bad experience, particularly with staff or beds. The bed was very comfortable and it wasn't a sofa bed. It was a proper double bed with clean linens made available on arrival (sheets, duvet, pillows, and two towels per person). The heating is under-floor and is monitored by two panels (one each for bathroom and bedroom). It was freezing when we arrived but, once switched on, the rooms quickly became toasty! The kitchen is equipped with microwave, electric stove, kettle, fridge, washer/dryer, and dishwasher as well as with plenty of cupboard space and pots, pans, plates, glasses, cutlery, and basic kitchen gadgets. There are also basic washing supplies (tablets for the washer/dishwasher, liquid soap, etc.). It is a self-service apartment meaning that there is no cleaner and one has to re-stock supplies if they run out or maybe ask staff. We didn't stay long enough to find out (5 days in total and we still had plenty of supplies by the end of it). Each room, including kitchen, was equipped with a big flatscreen TV and there is free wifi throughout although it can be patchy at times and you have to sign up initially. Apart from the kitchen, there is no other communal area but we didn't mind as we were out and about most days. Things I loved: location, rooms (reminiscent of high-quality student en suite rooms), bed, heat, hair dryer and alarm clock in bedroom, cleanliness, code security entrance, and locks on each room. Things that could be improved - drawbacks: absence of lift which makes it very difficult to lug heavy suitcases up stairs if you happen to be above ground floor (which we were) and is also tiring for elderly people and returning with heavy shopping. - water pressure in the bathroom. It could be better, especially for such a fancy shower head and mechanism, which is electronic. Maybe it was because we were on the top floor. In one room, we had a problem with the temperature the second day but the staff were great and sent people to fix it within an hour of calling them. - small bathroom size, especially sink size. Very hard to wash or brush teeth without some maneuvering if you want to avoid spitting toothpaste or water on the floor. Okay for one person but pretty crowded if two are sharing. - check-in and check-out times. Instead of the standard noon check out, one has to be out by 10 am and check-in is between 2-4 pm on the day of arrival. Seems pretty unfair and inconvenient. We were lucky because we arrived on a very early flight but had friends to stay at until we could check in but other visitors to London obviously will be inconvenienced by this. - Area is a bit rough but we experienced no problems despite going out and returning late at night. All in all, we were pretty pleased by our stay and have no major complaints. I think it is ideal for both short and long-term stays, especially if the price is low and you don't mind doing basic cleaning up after yourself.

title: Very disappointing, poor customer service
text: I requested check in at 1.00 which was accepted by Elizabeth, on arrival at 1.15, however, we had to wait outside 20 mins as she said 'check in is 2.00'. When a woman came to show us our apartment she was unaware we were in the wrong building and we then had to walk to another 5 minutes away. In this building there is also a gym so we were met with a distinct smell of sweat. The rooms on the website look great but ours bore no resmblance to any of those so beware. We booked a 2 bed apartment for the 4 of us, the second bed was a sofa bed in a small room which served as kitchen/dining/lounge/bedroom! When I again spoke to Elizabeth about this she said simply that we knew exactly which apartment we would get as we had received a 'gallery' of pictures in an email. This is totally untrue - I cannot see one picture of our room anywhere on their website or any other site showing room photos and certainly never had a 'gallery' sent. The apartment was further cluttered with a cot and high chair which were dragged out and just left on the landing in front of the fire escape!! When the woman was leaving I had to ask where the door key was - 'on the table' I was told. There was no key and had I not asked we would have been unable to lock the door when we left. Neither TV was tuned in and one had no batteries in the remote so no chance of doing so myself. There were 4 in our party but only 3 mugs and glasses. Whilst checking the website regarding the 'gallery' I noticed there was supposed to be 'chocolates or biscuits' - do not expect those either. I messaged Eizabeth (again) and got not reply but some time later a man did arrive at the door unannounced, luckily we were still in and showed him the problems. He left, as we did, and upon our return there was 1 mug, 1 glass, batteries in the remote - and a bottle of wine and chocolates by way of an apology. I would have much prefered a more understanding manner from Elizabeth who needs to learn these are her problems to deal with and not the paying customers. These apartments have been done cheaply and are fine if you're prepared to 'make do' and don't mind a stressful time arguing with staff.

Excellent location for access to Piccadilly line & lots of nice cafes & places to eat nearby.

title: Super value top accommodation in London
text: Having been to London many times and staying in central london we decided to look further afield to beat the rising over the top prices in central london. Linton Apartments certainly filled the bill cost wise and looked really good in the pix on their listing so we took a punt and booked. So glad we did. This place is as good as the pictures portray on the website and we were mightily impressed with the finish of this lovely apartment. Real tradesmen were involved in this apartment and it to their credit it is superb. Crisp and fresh as a new building it was a pleasure to stay here. Security is no concern as the access is controlled by two different points where you have to enter security codes to proceed. The location is great being less than a minute to the Turnpike Lane underground and a stroll down the High St to a large and very interesting selection of shops. Surrounded by cafes and restaurants with an eclectic range of food from everywhere it really is a great location. Using the underground you can be in Central London in under 20 minutes. Finally the staff of the real estate company below the apartment are involved in the management of the apartments and are lovely people to deal with. Nothing is too much trouble and they are only too happy to help with answers to questions and in our case a hand down the road with our luggage when the taxi would not park close to the pick up point. They also undertook to post our postcards the day we were leaving London. Cable TV, free WIFI, Great heating/air con, Nice kitchen and facilities, wooden floors, very secure. I really do recommend this accommodation in London. You will not be disappointed. We will be back for sure.

title: Perfect for Family Stay
text: Stayed there for 6 nights with my family of 4. It is located in North London and right next to Turnpike Lane Underground Station. It took about 1 hour from Heathrow to there. You will need to bring your luggage to the ground by stairs. They are not very long but still be prepared. The location is well sign-posted, and check in was quite fast. However be reminded that they did not have 24-hour front desk so you may need to contact them in advance in case you arrive out of office hour. The interior of the apartment was so great. Everything was in order, and my mother especially enjoyed using the kitchen and the washing machine. The air-con worked quite well in heating but if you need cooling it may take a while. The decorations were modern. Remember to bring yourself the bathroom amenities or you can buy in the nearby supermarkets. There are quite a lot of shops and eateries around so you don't need to worry about it. With such a group size, I can't think of any other choice for its price, location and quality in London. Highly recommended for family stay.

title: Very comfortable, modern flat.
text: The aparatment we stayed in was very clean, comfortable and spacious enough for 3 adults. The well equipped kitchen worked well for our needs, breakfast, night snacks, etc. The washer/dryer combo was small and took quite a while to do our laundry, but saved us going out to a laundromat. The area was a bit removed from the center of London, but very near a subway stop. We really enjoyed one particular restaurant, Tarshish, our last night in London that was minutes away. I would highly recommend these apartments to anyone who is visiting London and doesn't want to live in the busy city center.

title: A NEW, MODERN STUDIO IN A WONDERFUL POSITION
text: It is a nice place to stay, with new and clean apartments. The people at the reception are helpful and friendly. The area is safe, with several restaurants, shops and supermarkets. The tube station and the bus stops to the city centre are very close. It is at the beginning of zone 3 in London, a 20 minutes ride to Piccadilly Circus by tube.

title: Excellent
text: I stayed in the Single studio room.Everything was perfect.Bed was comfortable.Market,Underground train station and bus station is near just 2 min walk from the property. Property is well maintained and everything is in perfect condition.

title: Fantastic
text: Everything was good. The room was clean. Its located in a friendly neighbourhood that feels safe. everything worked. A lot of shops in the area. Not too far away from central london. The staff is also really friendly. We had a great time!

title: Perfect for a short stay in London
text: Brand new studio with fully fitted kitchen and modern facilities a stone's throw from the tube station (Piccadilly line).Extremely helpful and kind staff . Good value for the price we paid. We are very happy with our choice and we will surely come back there if we decide to visit London again!

title: Awesome Stay
text: Place was wonderful. Staff were all really helpful and accomodating when we had any questions or doubts to anything we might have during our stay. The place is so conveniently close to the tube, and has plenty to offer in terms of food or places to get groceries nearby. The apartment is new, clean, fresh and spacious and definitely a nice place to retreat to, after a day of endless shopping or packed sightseeing schedule. The apartment also offers everything you need at home and it was a joyful home away from home for us. London was such a joy to visit and Linton Apartments made us feel so much at home and no doubt made our trip so much more memorable and enjoyable.

title: Great value, great location
text: Highly recommend this place. A home away from home. Great value, friendly and helpful staff, great location on the Piccadilly line within easy reach of central London. I shall be staying here for any future visits to London.

title: Very good
text: I like it! Clean, tidy, close to underground station and very good facilities! But I would like a curtain... :) Last year we were in a Classic Studio, I liked it better, because the bathroom was bigger.

title: Very good choice for accommodation
text: It's very clean and good looking. Very professional organized. It is situated in very good neighborhood. The underground is really close so it is not so far from centre, it's really good connected so you can go anywhere.

title: Beautifull days
text: Very good apartments situeted in 3 zone of london but very near to the underground station (called "turnpike lane") The apartments are completely new and endowed with every confort. We have spent splendid days. Indeed recommended!

title: Average
text: Me and a friend decided to book the deluxe studio for our 4 night stay in London. Booking the apartment was relatively easy however when we got there it wasn't as big as it was portrayed in the images online. We didn't complain though, it was smaller than we thought but still comfortable for the 2 of us. The apartment was heavily furnished with Ikea products, from the bed down to the cutlery which I had no issue with. We found the mirror on the wardrobe was cracked on the bottom corner and the bedside lamp had broken and been glued back together- not a great impression. The bathroom was almost claustrophobic if you spent longer than 3 minutes in there and the smell of damp from the huge patch of mould visible from underneath the sink didn't help. The apartment description on the website promised us a garden view which in reality was a view of the park located opposite us. On the day we arrived our host showed us how to connect to the Wi-Fi and who to call if we needed anything. We immediately connected our phones and my phone (an Android device) wouldn't connect but my friend's iPhone connected easily. I rang reception at around 4.15pm to ask why my phone wouldn't connect and also to request another pillow as I usually sleep on 2 pillows. The man on the phone told me to restart my phone and that housekeeping would send a pillow up to my room ASAP. It was around 7.30pm and I still had no pillow and no Wi-Fi connection. I decided to call the reception again only to find they are off duty after 6pm. The next day at around noon- still no Wi-Fi or pillow- my friend and I decided to go to speak to someone face to face. On the way out I spotted the housekeeping ladies and asked them if they'd forgotten to put the pillow in my room but it turns out they were never told in the first place. When we got to reception we were told that the Wi-Fi was having issued and virgin media were dealing with the issue and we would have internet access by 5pm. 5pm came and we were finally able to connect to the Wi-Fi only to find you would be logged out of it after a certain period of time of inactivity which is rather annoying. The apartments are definitely not sound-proof as it says on the website which again was a let down. The only good thing about the apartment was the location.
