Me and my sister in law came to see Taylor Swift, and found it was a 10 minuet walk to Kilburn Station, 4 stops, then you’re at Wembley Park Station, where you have a further 5 minuets walk to the stadium! There is a small, very tight car park at the back of the hotel, costing £10 per night, which you almost don’t have much choice other than to use it, as there are no other car parks around, and on street parking is Permit Holders only, or Pay and Display. The one star is only for the guy on reception and the location. Would only stay again if I seen they’d updated their hotel

title: Perfect for a short stay when on business
text: This place, albeit slightly dated, it’s perfectly clean and the bathrooms are modern and with good showers. Nothing is worse than having a shower that is rubbish and barely runs! The lodge vibe is very much present throughout, but I quite liked it. The only downer is there is a distinct scent around the corridors that I can’t quite put my finger on, but nothing that would put me off going back. Definitely a good business trip hotel, especially if you can get a good deal on the cost.

title: Decent base for Wembley
text: We booked one night as a cheap hotel near Wembley. As we really needed very little from it, it didn't disappoint. Wembley is a 15 minute walk to Kilburn tube station then 4 stops north on the Jubilee line and another 15 minute walk from Wembley Park tube station. Rooms were basic but clean. We booked the family room on the ground floor and had the penthouse suite room 29. I assume this was the penthouse as it came with a balcony which came in very handy for pre show and post show drinks. Couldn't get any hot water from the shower late afternoon but it was fine the following morning. Plenty of tea, coffee and biscuits. TV on the wall and a decent night's sleep. Very happy for the price.

title: Nice little place
text: My husband, best mate and her husband stayed in this hotel whilst we were at a concert in Wembley. Although our room was a little dated, it was clean and tidy and the bed was super comfy. I would deffo stay again next time I am in London x

title: Short stay
text: A very friendly, comfortable + clean hotel, staff could not have been any more helpful, great location within walking distance to both train station and tube station, lots of restaurant and shop's within walking distance

title: Ariel
text: The staff was nice and the room was cheap- but the room was very small, and very cold too. The bathroom was freezing and the water was cold. The bed was comfy and there was a flat tv, and a pretty view of a snowy road in london

title: Not recommended at all.
text: If I could I would give this hotel no stars. I am very dissapointed in the way I was treated at this hotel. My friend made a booking here to stay for 10 days and after he had travelled on the plane for 6 hours and from the airport to the "hotel" for one and a half hours, we finally arrived. we were waiting outside for 10 minutes trying to open the door, we were pressing the buzzer. the door wouldn't open as it was very stiff so we thought it was closed because the check in is at 2pm and we arrived 1:40pm. I called the hotel to check and Sean the supervisor at the hotel said push the door it is easy and shut the phone in my face. I went back and pushed the door really hard and the door opened. Sean was standing at reception the whole time and could see that we were struggling with the door and did not get up to help us. As soon as we walked in he said ' are you stupid do you not know how to open the door?' I was shocked and said we tried very hard but it wouldn't open. I said he should have a sign on the door at least to say there is problem with it. He then told me that I am rude and need to shut my mouth and stop talking and called me stupid once again. I then told him he is very rude and shouldn't talk to me like that. He called and cancelled the booking within 30 seconds of us being there. he didn't even tell us what was happening and just walked inside into the office. I then pressed the buzzer at the reception to ask if he had cancelled it and how it would be processed. He was rude again and I told him I would report him. As we stood outside others tried to go in and they struggled to open the door. I was shaking the whole time because I have never been verbally abused like this. If the manager sees this could you please email me so I could explain the situation, as Sean would not inform me of your name. I have reported Sean to the website we used to book from because I will never accept someone talking to me like that.

title: Not recommended
text: I was hoping this would be a good base to stay at during a training course but it wasn’t. I’ve stayed in many 2 star hotels and this was by far the worst. Positives: friendly reception. Reasonably near tube (10 min walk). Good shower pressure. Negatives: Incredibly strong smell of smoke the moment you walk in the door. Room wasn’t clean. Kettle had a fault so kept cutting out and wasn’t usable. Room and especially pillows smelled of smoke. Hot water in shower took a very long time to come. Radiator on very high with no control so windows had to be open but anyone smoking outside was then an issue. Room looked straight out onto road so anyone walking past looks in. Two guests next door were having an incredibly loud breakup until 3am, screaming, shouting and crying. Lots of doors slamming. Blackout curtains but a lot of light came around sides so very hard to sleep. Bed didn’t have a proper cover so seemed very unhygienic. Etc. I assume it’s also the worst room in the hotel as room photos show MUCH nicer rooms than the one I was in. It’s a shame as it has the potential to be a good hotel.

title: The excellent service makes up for minor inconveniences
text: The hotel offers very warm and hospitable service and allowed us to check in at 11 am even though check-in time was 2 pm. This meant that they had to rush to get the room ready for us but they did so without any fuss. In fact we woke the manager up with our early arrival but he was nice about it. The only thing that we were inconvenienced with was that the hot water took a long time to get hot (almost 15 minutes) and even then it was mostly lukewarm only. We had to do without a shower for the both nights we were there because it was too cold to take lukewarm showers. Imma who was in housekeeping was always very helpful and attentive and took care of our requests for towels and to clean up a clogged shower drain.

title: Unexpected refund and lovely room
text: I was due here for 2 nights but weather conditions meant my flight was cancelled, so I called the hotel to let them know I would be a day late. I was calling simply to let them know, but was amazed to be told that I would get a refund for the first night (I pre-paid). I thought this was incredible customer service as I cancelled at short notice. It was a completely unexpected and kind gesture - impressive. The room was spacious and incredibly clean, WiFi strong, good shower and lovely bed. Due to facilities, room, price and customer service, I will absolutely be back.

title: DOES WHAT IT SAYS ON THE TIN
text: Whilst I only stayed for one night, this no breakfast hotel, located at the Cricklewood end of Shoot Up Hill on the Edgware Road (at the junction with Walm Lane), provides a clean resonably cheap option for Central London. It is close to the buses and does what you would expect. No complaints and would happily use it again if I needed to be in the area.

title: a weekend in London
text: The room clean and comfortable . Tea and coffee making facilities. Not far from any transport. Very helpful information at reception. No lift rooms on three floors. Would go back if visiting London . Price good

title: Rested
text: It was an ok stay but for the same price I have stayed central London. It was a bit embarrassing when I went for breakfast with my wife as we were told that we we not entitled to breakfast as this had not been paid for. This happened on the 2 mornings that we stayed so we sat there in the dining area whilst the waiting staff confirmed with reception that we had paid

title: Short stay
text: We visited whist attending a concert in Wembley. Very friendly and helpful gentleman on reception. Rooms were clean and tidy a little dated but did the job perfectly. Great location for Wembley and central London. Would stay again.

title: Good little hotel
text: Easy to find. 10 min walk from Kilburn tube station. Easy to get to Wembley. Room was clean, bathroom too. Plenty of coffee etc. Receptionist was very helpful and polite. Basic but good. Bedside tables with plug sockets. Few local shops on the high st. Cheap and cheerful Wetherspoons 2 mins away too! Will be back when we have other events at Wembley!

title: Not a bad little hotel
text: Checked in for 1 night for gig at Wembley, tube just a 10 min walk and close enough to Wembley to warrant not paying extortionate prices when a big gig is playing, room was small but comfortable enough, small double bed was a squeeze, clean and check in staff really helpful and friendly

title: Brilliant!
text: Spent the weekend here. Shaun, the owner, went above and beyond making sure our weekend went smoothly. what a fabulous place and location. Ask for room 17! what a quirky room, the mirrored ceiling made us giggle. lovely and clean, great shower and comfy bed. The hotel is on a high street with lots of interesting shops, we had oyster cards and found it easy to get into the centre of London, probably took around 30mins. Our initial reason for choosing the Cricklewood was its position to the Wembley stadium, this didn't disappoint, two stops on the tube and we were there, also no hitches coming back late on the tube and bus. We would certainly return and use the hotel as a base whenever we visit London, as long as we got room 17! Thank you Shaun.

title: Don't expect the Ritz!!!
text: Good standard budget hotel close to the jubilee line and 10 minute tube from Wembley Park....clean good shower....close to a very diverse selection of restaurants and a couple of pubs. All in all good value.....no food!!!!

title: Comfortable stay
text: Stayed for one night last weekend primarily for a gig at Wembley. Was met by a friendly, helpful receptionist and later met the manager who was very friendly and welcoming. The lodge is only 10 minutes walk to the tube and 4 stops to Wembley so would definitely recommend a stay here if you're staying for that purpose. The room was a good size, bathroom was quite small but didn't matter for one night. Had tv and tea/coffee making facilities which is always welcome. Thanks!

title: Reasonable budget accommodation
text: My room was small, with no bedside table or lamp. Comfortable bed. The bathroom was very small but clean, with lots of hot water. Good TV. You have to go out for breakfast - cafes limited on Cricklewood Broadway. For London, this is budget accommodation.

title: good budget hotell
text: Clean,little bit small rooms but big enough, good enviroment, supermarkets and different little restaurants and bubs nearby, wifi is not working all the time, very good and helpfull staff, good location.

title: Great stay
text: Lovely hotel, currently undergoing renovation but doesn't affect guests (we weren't affected anyway). Nice sized and clean room with good facilities. Really good location with lots of amenities nearby. A 10 minute walk from Kilburn tube station and around a 7 minute walk to Cricklewood station where you can get the Thameslink into central London. Very attentive staff who were on hand to make sure you had a great stay. I would definitely stay here again, fab location and very reasonably priced. Thanks guys xx

title: Very Pleasant Stay
text: The staff at Cricklewood Lodge were very attentive and did everything they could to ensure we had a pleasant stay. The room was clean and newly decorated and we had a very nice time. Thanks to Cricklewood Lodge.

title: Hotel to be avoided - Rude and helpless Staff
text: The hotel is old and not very good preserved. However, the worst part is the staff: extremely rude, unpolite and heartless. I tried to comunicate with them but the answer was confusing and not clear at all. They didn't help us and they were cruel with their attitude. In all my traveling experience, I've never been treated this way.

title: Clean hotel, with small but functional rooms, very friendly and helpfull staff.
text: Clean hotel, with small but functional rooms, very friendly and helpfull staff. Arrived at the hotel to drop our bags off on our way to wembley stadium. Needed to be a quick turn around, the friendly member of staff booked us in, and ordered us a taxi for six and we on our way within ten minutes. Great.

title: What a find this is!
text: This is a good little hotel run by a fantastic guy called Shaun. The hotel is located right on the bus route straight into Marylebone or Paddington - quick trips - and is next to shops, pubs, restaurants - all within comfortable walking distance, so although there isn't a restaurant in the hotel, you have a range of choices just outside the door. The hotel is currently being refurbished which is nice and the rooms are comfortable, clean and well maintained. A great supply of coffee,tea,milk sugar and orange juice is on hand. Nice view into the trees from my window which opened, a good telly and really you don't need much more. My bathroom was lovely. I can't say enough about Shaun who runs the hotel. He is THE most helpful person! Welcoming, friendly, thoughtful, practical and just a lovely guy. The other staff there are lovely too. This hotel may not have 5 stars on the outside, but it has 5 stars from me as far as what's going on inside - people who are there to help when you need it and a place to stay where you feel really welcomed and looked after. Thank you - I will return and I will recommend your hotel whenever I get the chance to. ***** Oh, and it's great value too! And no - I didn't know Shaun or anyone else at the hotel prior to staying there!!

title: Comfortable, clean and cheap
text: The walls are maybe too thin... sometimes you could hear other people talking, but it is very quiet at night. The room I stayed in was extremely small (which I already expected since this happens in most of the hotels I've been to in London), but had everything I needed. It is a bit away from the city center but Killburn station is 10 minutes away on foot, so you can expect to be in the city center 15-20 minutes later. The politeness and kindness of the staff was absolutely exceptional and the cleanliness of the hotel was outstanding. I usually have allergy problems with carpeted places, but this hotel was spotless. The price of the single room (when I booked it) was way below average considering London standards. So if you don't mind to stay in a very small room I would totally recommend this hotel. And let's face it, cheap hotels in London are terrible, this one isn't. I don't think it's the best hotel to stay in, however I've given the best score to this hotel (which I usually don't do) because because it exceeded my expectations. It's very difficult to find something like this clean, quiet and cheap in London.

title: Basic but good...........
text: We have just returned from a long weekend away in London and as a base we booked to stay at the Cricklewood Lodge Hotel mainly due to price as hotels closer to the centre were very expensive and we didn't want to spend lots when we would be out most of the time. The hotel is currently having it's rooms renovated but we didn't experience any noise or disturbance whilst we were there. We were put in one of the completed rooms which was lovely and a nice size with an amazing shower. We were on the main road and it was busy so if you are a light sleeper ask for a room towards the back but to be honest we were that shattered after sight seeing all day that nothing would have disturbed us :-) It was room only but there was ample places to eat nearby including a good old Wetherspoons less than 2 minutes away. The nearest tube station (Kilburn) was a 10 minute walk away and didn't take long to get into the centre of London. If you are after a good, clean base for exploring the city then you can't go wrong with this hotel.

title: FA cup final weekend
text: Stayed here on the weekend of the FA cup final, booked as a late deal, was extremely pleased with the accommodation, also very friendly staff (Sean couldn't do enough for us). Quiet location, clean room, with two bathrooms!! Not far from train station. Had a great sleep in a comfy bed. Well worth the price we paid! What more could you ask for :-)

title: Neat well maintained rooms
text: I stayed at this hotel for 6 nights and found it to be very good. It is well maintained and clean. My room had been newly renovated. The hotel is close to shops, pubs and Kilburn underground station. All reports you read about the manager being a friendly helpful person are true. He is one of those people that is exceptional at his job. Each room has it's own shower and toilet. The only downside was that the room had no bar fridge, but this seems to be a fairly common thing amongst budget hotels in London. I would definitely recommend staying here. However, I probably wouldn't select this hotel to take my family to. Not because of anything bad, but it really is just a hotel. No family spaces

title: Good one night stay
text: We stayed here on a one night stay to attend a family party. The reception staff were super efficient. We had a family room, which was very spacious and clean, plenty of room for the three of us. This hotel had a bar which was a bonus, we got served quickly and the prices weren't too bad either. We had breakfast which was self serve and very adequate. A pleasant stay over all.

title: Amazing place
text: I stayed here for 5 nights. The manager Shaun was amazing. He was very friendly and helpful. The room was very tidy and clean. There are biscuits, juices, tea and coffee in the room and also a kettle. The room was cleaned everyday and they put new juices and biscuits. The hotel is very close to Kilburn Underground Station. I really enjoyed my stay here and would recommend to anybody. I'll definitely stay again.

title: Saturday night stay
text: Me and my friend stayed here on Saturday 2nd of July as we were attending a concert at Wembley. We were greeted by the manager who was very friendly and gave us the information we needed. The location was great about a 10 minute walk to the tube station and just round the corner from a wetherspoons and shops. We had a problem with a broken shower head however once it was reported to reception it was dealt with within minutes. The bathroom door was also very noisy when opening and shutting. The rooms were quite small but that wasn't much of a problem as we were out most of the day and there was everything you needed. This hotel is value for money and would recommend for a short stay whilst visiting Wembley/London

title: Top of the Hill!
text: Sean (Manager) was ace, very helpful & friendly. Was moved from a single to a double on the lower ground floor as they were re-furbishing and although the room was facing the main road, the windows were double glazed so no problem there.The only problem I did have was that I had to sit sideways on the loo as it was too close to the wall, but apart from that a good stay & very reasonably priced for London. The bus stops were close by with loads of buses up & down Shoot Up Hill to Kilburn. There was The Beaten Docket (Wetherspoons) across from the hotel which had great breakfasts for £3.25, & Kilburn has some great restaurants & cafes as well as the Tricycle theatre & cinema.

title: Nice and cozy
text: I stayed three nights in the end of April and I was very pleased with my stay. The manager was very welcoming and pleasant, and made sure that everything was good with my stay. He was maybe one of the nicest hotel workers I've ever met during my holidays! Also other members of the staff who helped me during my stay were absolutely pleasant. I had reserved a single room but got an upgrade to a double room, which was great. The room was clean and bed was nice, and bathroom rather spacious, at least on London standards. Only minus thing was that I didn't find a hairdyer but because I didn't necessarily need it, I did not went to ask if they had one. There were pleanty of coffee, tea, biscuits and juices ready in the room. The wifi worked well during the whole stay. The closest tube station is about 10 minutes walk away, but you can also take a bus from a very close bus stop to the station or straight to Oxford street, for example. That's handy if it's raining, like it was during my stay. It is a bit far from the center, the tube takes about 10minutes to Bond street station, but it is still in the zone 2. However, the neighbourhood seemed fine and even though my window was facing to the street, it was very quiet. They were also renewing something at the hotel, but even though I slept rather late, I didn't hear any noises. I could stay here again!:)

title: Surprisingly Nice
text: The hospitality industry in the UK leaves a lot to be desired when it comes to value for money and treatment of guests so my expectations are never high, however this particular establishment renewed my faith. Very clean in both public areas and room, tea and coffee facilities with very generous amount of supplies in the room, daily room service and a very warm and friendly welcome on arrival and throughout my stay by Sean. My room was a bit smaller than expected and in some area's practicalities were lacking but they are undergoing a refurbishment (which does not infringe on stay) so availability was limited and the fact that I was given a reasonable explanation with the offer of improvement the negative was turned in to a positive. Just because we opt for a more reasonably priced B&B instead of the ludicrously priced hotels does not mean that we should be treated in accordance with our spending power like so many do, This little gem of a place has a standard that should be followed by a few more hotels and guest houses.

title: London Museum visit
text: Very helpful & friendly. Great to have the cheap on site parking. Clean & tidy family room. Not enough cloths storage. Needs some drawers. Light over desk didn't work. They did drop in another chair without asking as there was only one for the four of us. The security/fire door to our floor broke so no one could get in so it was propped open over night. Food was ok with a fair choice. Double bed was not level so not a great nights sleep. Very helpful with directions. Would stay again but would request a different room if the bed was the same. Half hour free wifi

title: Excellent value, excellent service
text: I had a 5 day conference and needed somewhere nearby to stay. I arrived and was greeted by the friendliest man Shaun, the owner. A pleasant welcome on a miserable and rainy day. The room (which he upgraded for free) was newly refurbished, clean and spacious. The refreshment tray was very generous and refilled ever day. I would highly recommend this hotel. Shaun went above and beyond during my stay and he deserves a medal!

title: Excellent Value and good service
text: I was looking for somewhere for two nights, while a went to concerts and met people over two days. So I wanted someone clean and easy to reach, quiet, and I was not concerned about a large room. Cricklewood Lodge met all this. A very helpful manager booked me in. The room was small but very pleasant, with en-suite, TV and as much coffee and biscuits as one could possibly want. It's only ten minutes walk from Kilburn underground station. And although they don't provide breakfast, the Wetherspoons pub just 100 yards down the road does provide it from 8.00am, and for £4. I'll definitely stay there again.

title: Excellent Hotel
text: This was the 2nd time I have stayed at this hotel, the newly refurbished rooms are extremely well finished and you really can't fault this hotel for the price. The manager Sean is really friendly and goes out of his way to make you feel welcome. Next time in Cricklewood will definatly book again!

title: Third time at Lodge. Never disappointed
text: Really great place this. Booked a single room for £50 and upon arrival was given a double. Room spacious, warm and airy. Bed was very comfortable and shower very good. Unbelievable amout of tea, coffee, biscuits and juice. Always very well looked after. Will definitely be returning.

title: Good hotel, friendly manager
text: We booked a twin room, and we got a gigantic room with two double beds and two bathrooms. They were refurbishing, and the manager apologized for the inconvenience, but we never experienced any inconveniences. The only thing I missed was a closet for our clothes...

title: Lovely little hotel
text: I booked this hotel last minute to go and watch a recent England game at Wembley, I was pleasantly surprised at how friendly the staff were towards me,which is very rare in London, my room was clean as was the rest of the hotel, it was a short 10 minute walk to the tube station or a 2 minute bus journey, about 5 minute walk to the town area where you have a wide choice of food and drink to chose from, all in all I would stay at this hotel when I make another trip to Wembley

title: Great value.
text: Having read some earlier reviews we were pleasantly surprised to find the lodge spotlessly clean and comfy, if a little small. Will be booking again when visiting London . Friendly and helpful staff, perfect if you're planning a trip to Wembley as it's only a couple of stations away on the tube.

title: enjoyable stay
text: We stayed for the England match 8th September. The rooms were lovely and clean, lovely comfy bed and nice pillows.Made to feel very welcome even thou we were 2 hours early for check-in. Plenty of shops around, Wetherspoons down the road, easy travel access for train/tube Such a good price.Will definitely be staying here again.

title: Clean , helpful staff, reasonable price
text: Stayed there for one week. Comfortable bathroom, fresh sheets duvet. Biscuits, tea, orange juice supplemented every day in the room. Almost fully refurbished place. The manager of the hotel is a kind man, genius of knowledge, ask him for anything , for instance he will tell you how to get to Greenwich by ferry instead of boring tube or will give you a map with directions and bus/tube numbers

title: Comfortable position - clean - Owner extremely kind - Near a good pub
text: Hotel set in a comfortable position, due to the fact which is located at few hundreds of meters from the Kilburn stop of the Jubilee tube, with which is possible to reach the center in approximately 15/20 minutes (Embankment). Is also possible to use the buses which pass frequently heading to the center. Small but clean rooms with tea, water boiler, coffee, biscuits and sugar. Owner extremely kind and available. If you need any kind of transfer by car ask directly to him, who will prompt you a fine service with lower fares compared to classic taxis. Really near to the hotel is located a pub in which we dined well, with good food and beers.

title: It was lovely!
text: Went there for one night only for Ed Sheeran concert! Stayed there on 12th July! Got there, nice welcome from a nice man! We stayed in a family room and it is small but it was nice, 2 single and one double and toilet and shower separately with also a tv! Bed was comfortable and when we arrived there was cups with biscuits and coffee sachets etc and orange juice! Very kind.. Thank you!

title: Quite good for the price
text: It’s always a risky business booking a low-price (for London) hotel in London, and this time my gamble paid off. I chose this because of the location (on the bus route I needed), and was pleased with my choice. Certainly it’s fairly basic, but fine for a short stay — my room was tiny but clean, comfortable, quiet and well equipped

title: great value
text: A good value otel 5 mins from jublee line clean rooms and comfortable bed with brewing facilities in the room ideal for us attending a concert at wembly staff were helpful and friendly would stop again

title: Pleasant and Clean
text: Stayed at the Crincklewood Lodge Hotel for three nights with friends was idle for a weekend in London was on main bus route and easy train access (about 10 min walk away) Into the city staff were very helpful rooms were clean and comfy towels were changed daily,The hotel is easy to find being on the main route there is a few good bars and restaurants within ten min walk from hotel would go back next time we are down in London for the price it's Excellent value.

title: So helpful!
text: Me and my friend stayed in this hotel this weekend just gone and had a really lovely stay. The room was small but cute and had everything you need from a hotel room. It was a good location to get the tube to Wembley stadium and not too far from London city centre itself. The manager of the hotel was so lovely and helpful, me and my friend have never met such a nice manager before! He helped us find our way around London and we cannot thank him enough! Thank you for a lovely stay and for helping us so much, we would have gotten lost otherwise. Naomi and Danielle x

title: Good value for money
text: The room was very small, but comfortable and clean. The walls, however, are paper-thin and the sound of traffic starts quite early in the morning. But the hotel is very well located

title: Great decent priced hotel
text: Stayed here for a weekend away. It's a few mins walk from Cricklewood train station and bus stops. It was a kind of lads weekend so we were just looking for a place to sleep and didn't plan to spend a whole lot of time in the room. We looked at other hotels in the area and picked this one purely on price. I was very surprised that the room was spotless and spacious with lots of tea and coffee The staff were friendly and helpful and Sean the manager is a lovely down to earth guy. I have no hesitation in recommending it for a stay. It is not Claridges or the Ritz, but doesn't claim to be. I will definitely stay here again on my next trip to London

title: Great hotel. Good value.
text: I stayed here for a couple of nights on a weekend. The first night I was in what was supposed to be a double room for single occupancy. To my great surprise the room was massive. There was enough room to sleep four if needed with a double bed in the middle and two singles either side. Being a rather large chap I slept in the double bed which was super comfy. The room and everything in it was very clean and well maintained. Absolutely gangs of tea and coffeee and even biccies! The second night I moved into a twin room with a mate. While obviously it wasn't as big as the other room it was still comfortable enough. I'm probably going to stay here in a single room for four nights in June and am really looking forward to that. The cost and everything else comapred very favourable to the Travelodge up the road. I would definitely recommend this. Well done Sean and co.

title: NOT the Travelodge.
text: First to note that a lot of the reviews below are for the Travelodge, which this is not. Not being a Travelodge meant that the guy on reception (sorry I didn't get his name) was able to be totally flexible, and use his initiative when we pitched up before "check in" opened. Rooms were allocated, parking fee was waived, in no time at all we were in our rooms. In fact I'd go so far to say that the guy on reception was probably the best receptionist/duty manager I have come across. The rooms were plenty large enough for a short stay, although the bathroom in the room I stayed in was a little on the small size. The curtains aren't thick enough to cut out the morning sun, and the noise from the road is fairly constant through the night. Overall I'd rate the hotel somewhere between average and very good, but Tripadvisor doesn't seem to think there's a category in between the two.

title: recent stay
text: i stayed for 11 nights and found the place comfortable safe practical and was located central to three major areas. plenty of towels and the om tea and coffee was great .shower gel was nice and plentiful.staff are very friendly and the general manager Sean is helpful and great to deal with.

title: Friendly staff but dirty bedsheets
text: I stayed in a single room overnight. The reception staff were very friendly and helpful. The room was basic, as you would expect for the price, and the location was handy with regular buses. My one (fairly significant) complaint was that the duvet cover was not clean. When I went to bed, I thought the sheets smelled a bit stale - like they'd been stored for a while before they were used. The next morning, I found grease and smears of curry on the duvet cover. These weren't just stains that hadn't come out in the wash - the cover hadn't been washed at all. When I mentioned this as I was checking out, I didn't even get an apology. Yes, this place is basic and would probably be okay to crash out in (which is all I wanted), but there's no excuse not to provide clean linen.

title: Comfortable
text: Does what it says on the tin I suppose! A little out of London but only 15 minutes walk from Kilburn underground. There are plenty of buses that pass the hotel too. There are plenty of places to eat nearby too, including a Wetherspoons. My main gripe is the check-in time being as late as 3pm and there doesn't seem to be a lot of leeway given with regards to this unless you pay extra! We bought a drink and this seemed to get the room ready a little quicker (about 1440)! The room was comfortable and clean and the price reasonable for London so I'd stay again.

title: Really good lodge
text: Contrary to the reviews i've seen here, its a really good hotel,turns out its been remodeld this year and looks really good, rooms are comfy and the breakfast its really rich and tasty

title: Mixed feelings
text: Stayed in the "hotel" on New Years Eve. Cost was £40, so was not expecting much to be honest. Asked for a rear facing view as wanted to avoid traffic noise from main road. Room was very basic both in terms of amenities and space. Box room would be an apt description. However, room was reasonably clean and levels of general cleanliness not too bad at all. Shower was efficient but sink tap was wonky. Radiator not working in bedroom but was not that bothered as don't like heat in bedrooms generally. Bed was adequate but curtain was flimsy with no net curtains. I have read some exceedingly bad reviews re this hotel, particularly re customer service from the Management. Well I can say I was greeted very well and the Manager was courteous and polite. Further remarks re hotel being used as a "knocking shop", I really take with a pinch of salt. Flimsy walls and partitions mean that noise does carry unfortunately. Coupled with a very long stand up row in the street made it difficult to sleep (it was New Years Eve after all) I wont put anyone off staying here but take heed of the maxim "you get what you pay for" as this is particularly apposite at this establishment. However, if you need to stay a night or two in a decent spot re travel connections to town or to Wembley then this is an option

title: short stay in London
text: Stayed in the travel lodge 18th-19th October 2013. Its roughly what you expect for £40 a night. Bus route right outside the hotel which leads on to Kilburn underground about a mile from the hotel. The room was relatively clean with a nice flat screen television. The bathroom again was clean however a little cramped and steamed up very easily. The bedding seemed ok however towels were grey and no bath mat was included, so the wet floor in the bathroom was a bit of a pain. From reading other reviews it seemed as though i got lucky and had a room situated away from the main road. The view from my window looked out onto a roof and car park below, however the room was just for sleeping in so if I wanted a better view I would have stayed closer to the city center. Another downside to the stay was the frequent fire alarm which literally went off several times during my stay. One being 4pm in the afternoon and another nearer 4am in the morning. Never seen any members of staff apart from on arrival and leaving. All in all not a bad hotel. Easy access to the tube and has a tesco express just next door which was handy as an alternative breakfast or quick lunch. Would stay here again.

title: Unclean low standard of care
text: Very unclean room. Bed and room was very much below what you expect. Yes it's cheep but simple cleaning standards should still be met. Walls are very thin was kept awake by man snoring in next room. This hotel has very low standards please don't expect much

title: Weekend in London
text: Good attempt on decoration but not worth the cost and very disappointed that the only breakfast available was a "Continental breakfast" in the room which comprised of a muffin bun and a biscuit despite booking bed and breakfast accommodation Would'ant recommend this "Hotel" and would not stay here again !!

title: Not totally crap
text: For the pricing I guess you shouldnt have too high expextations, but... I made my booking online, payed a deposit. Got no confirmation, had to call long distance to check if I had a room, they receptionist hardly understood english or the concept "online". after three reminding emails I got a confirmation, just before I left for London. I asked for a receipt but they refused to include the deposit. Internet was extra charge and didnt work. The room was nice and clean when we came but wasnt cleaned every day. Shower sewage worked for a two minute shower, then it was full. Breakfast was a joke. Powder coffee and biscuits on a sticky tray in the room, though there was a sign with bed and breakfast outside. Anyway we managed to sleep and they wasnt rude or anything.

title: You have the option of staying 3 hours here...
text: The place I was booked into let me down so my husband booked me into this place via Laterooms. On the plus side it was cheap -£83 for two nights, the ensuite room was clean and the TV was a decent size flatscreen. On the minus: 1.Parking was an issue. There is a tiny car park dominated by big white vans with very little manoevring space, odd when there is a huge unused forecourt -so I parked on the road. Note that on the opposite side of the A5, the hours for free parking are more reasonable. 2. Every time I went in the hotel there were workmen sitting on the steps at the entrance smoking. 3.The reception area was protected by a grille (the type to keep bank robbers out). In spite of this, it was often unstaffed, allowing anyone to just walk into the areas where the bedrooms were. I was not comforted by the fact I was informed that the Reception (and presumably the front door) was open 24 hours. 4. A sign indicated "Minimum stay -3 hours for £30". Charming. 5. No breakfast was available. I was promised croissants to go with the tea/coffee facilities in the room (which were fine). However these never turned up on either morning. 6. There was a large vending machine in the hallway with nothing in it. However, it did advertise Durex on the side. To be fair, the room was reasonably comfortable although lacking in natural daylight due to being in the basement. There was just enough light to see the huge pile of cigarette dog-ends on the shelf outside. In spite of all this it was surprisingly quiet as I had been expecting loud raucous parties involving ladies of the night due to the indications I mentioned. By the way, there are some nice places in Cricklewood - The Windmill, just up the road, is much better.

title: Difficult to Say
text: My Daughter and my Grandson stayed here when attending the Robbie Williams Concert. She was offered a double when she had requested two singles and it was sorted out. The rooms were clean but she was concerned about the reception at night and the fact that there was a sign to say that the rooms could be rented by the hour !!

title: Clean and basic, good value, but disappointing in some areas
text: Four of us stayed in a large family room in Cricklewood Lodge on a Friday night. The hotel was easy to find, but then the trouble started! The area is a little rough around the edges, not normally a problem for us but could be concerning to some. The car park only has room for around 7/8 cars and on this occasion 3 of those spaces were taken up by a work van! We had to ask the work man himself to move the van as the hotel staff weren't keen to help. The nearby roads are residents' permit only.. Worth noting! Check in time is 2pm according to the booking, we arrived at 3.15pm and were told our room wasn't ready and to come back in 15mins! We loaded the car back up and went for a drink for an hour and when we got back the maids were just finishing. The staff were not very apologetic at the room not being ready for over two hours! We were not offered anything in compensation of the car park and room issues... Our request for a discount was adamantly refused. When we got back from our concert at around midnight the noise outside was pretty bad! Screeching cars, horns, backfiring, police sirens just to name a few! Definitely an inner city backdrop, worth noting for light sleepers. Unfortunately we had to keep a window open as it was so hot. If you overlook the aspects which are only specific to our stay the hotel is basic but very clean, the maids did a great job. It is cheap and cheerful and kind of does what it says on the tin. The area may be of a concern to smaller groups, particularly women, as we seemed to attract unwanted attention from the locals! Very close to buses and tube with a variety of pubs and restaurants.

title: Awful Experience
text: I stayed mid week and I was astounded by the quality of the experience. I. Whilst it was cheap, I did not expect the room to smell of stale cigarette smoke and be grubby. 2. The owner charges extra for the use of debit cards. He did not say this until after he had started putting the transaction through, and then tried to blame me for not reading a sign, that I could barely see for all of the metal bars across the window. He was then grumpy when I offered to go and get cash 3. When I asked for a receipt he got even grumpier, and started ranting about Muslims on benefits wanting receipts for the council as they were all immigrants wanting hand outs from the state. I explained mine was for my employer, but by this point he was in mid rant. 4. The owner is clearly an immigrant which made the last rant even more offensive. 5. The was lots of traffic going past, which made sleeping impossible

title: accommodation at hotel
text: I liked the accommodation and breakfast. good hotel cleanliness. without disturbance of noise from other rooms. good service. I had no problems with hot or cold water. TV worked but was not compatible with the TV remote. I stayed in the basement but it was no problem with this as everything was ok. I sat between 08/07/2011 and 12/08/2011

title: It appears they have sorted this place out...
text: I booked this as an emergency place to stay, and booked the double room. I arrived at the caged reception area, and paid my money, the chap seemed kind of ok, maybe I caught him on a good day. I was given room No10, and as I headed through a maze of corridors, and mattresses in the hall, I expected very little as I put the key in the door and peeped into the room. To my surprise, the room was spacious, with two big double windows, it was clean and airy and the bed was super comfy. The bathroom was compact and tiny, but clean.. the flat screen tv had a multitude of tv channels, and there was even some buscuits to go with my brew. We decided to sleep in and skip breakfast, so cannot coment if it was of any quality or not.

title: Dreadful
text: I booked nearly 3 weeks in advance. There were 3 of us that required a single and a twin room. It was booked, paid on debit card, and confirmed. When we arrived at 6pm we presumed the rooms would be ready for us. They wasn't. The owner said that someone had paid extra to have the rooms for longer as they'd missed their flight or train. We needed these rooms to get showered and changed as we'd gone to London for a friend's birthday party. The owner said we'd need to give him more time for the twin room & suggested he upgrade the single into a double at no extra cost so at least we could all get washed and ready. He reassured us that on our return the twin room would be sorted. The double room was split into bad points and one good point. The good point being it seemed clean. The bad points

title: Hell
text: what a dump, should b closed down, lots of noise going on early hrs like furniture being moved, reception person very rude, did'nt bother with breakfast did'nt want to risk food poisoning,

title: Poor digs, expensive cost!
text: I personaly thought this hotel was a lot of money for what it was. I was given a room that was supposed to be a family room as no single or doubles available, this was tiny, so dread to think what the other rooms were like. No windows in the room, or should I say cell! Breakfast was a farce Also if you parked in the small car park early you would be blocked in and no way of getting out until the owner of the car in front eventually turned up Asking ar reception before 8 in the morning was met with a guy who was sleeping behind the counter and no help when woken up!

title: Health warning!
text: Cheapness is not an excuse not to be clean. One star is too much for this hotel. There was filth everywhere in the room, shower was broken, little to no pressure, tile missing. There was undescribable dirt in the room, skirting board, windows, carpet. Very strong smell of urine on the carpet, hidden by a rug. Discusting!

title: When are you coming back to give me my keys for the room ?
text: I stay at this hotel once about 4 years ago . At 1st it was ok . We stay in room number 2 at the bottom floor with a en suite bathroom . The room was old with the owner friend bed bugs . An old TV and a little dark room . As this hotel is close to brent cross and it near the word cheap 60 pound ( but not worth the 60 pound) an emergency happen where we had to stay again .At around 8pm I rang the bell no one answer so I rang again still no answer then a tired old man open the door and shout what do you want . I looked up thinking I was in the wrong place . This man was so RUDE ! I asked if they was any rooms left he said yes and he walked off . I am still waiting for him to come back ! Please you need to close this place down

title: Took 1 look at room and left
text: This hotel was booked for me by a London-based company that I was visiting though I can't imagine why this hotel would be on the list of preferred places for business visitors. Admittedly the travel budget was tight - under 70 pounds per night. I was booked into a double room. The gentleman manning reception was rude, unhelpful, and quite frankly, needed a good wash. The hotel could have done with a good wash too. I left shortly after seeing the room I'd been given because it was grimy and I couldn't imagine spending a night in its cramped confines. Avoid this hotel if you can afford to.

title: NEVER STAY HERE
text: Me and my family were put here as our flat flooded and we had no hot water. It seemed ok at first but then we discovered they had bed bugs, we left as soon as we found out but bed bugs hide in your clothes and luggage and we didnt even realise we'd transported them to our own house! This hotel is disguisting, never stay there!!

title: IT IS BEING REFURBISHED AND WAS QUITE COMFORTABLE
text: I was apprehensive to book this hotel but was pleasantly surprised.It is being refurbished and the corridors have new carpet.We had a twin bed room which had been refurbished. The walls had been painted, the carpet was new and the twin beds were super comfy. It was not perfect but i would go again. Breakfast was excellent.

title: SHOULD BE ADVERTISED WITH A HEALTH WARNING
text: I am mortified to have booked my husband and sister and I into this filthy hotel. The location suited our needs and for this we were prepared for basic standards. But one could never be prepared for the dirt! It was filthy. The floors were filthy. The paintwork was filthy. The windows were filthy. The ensuites were filthy. As for the smell...a mixture of gas and sewerage. This was definitely our worst experience of accomodation in fifty years. Advertising should carry a health warning

title: Never stay at this "hotel" - avoid at all costs
text: Stayed at this hotel with family and we could not believe that this "hotel" had been allowed to open. We arrived to a building which looked terrible on the outside with a broken stair rail to the door. Then were greeted with a caged reception desk - it should have said it all!! One of the rooms had a door to the shower room which was hanging off and you had to be quick or the shower base would fill up and flood the floor. As for the smell - there are no words to describe it - a sewage smell was the closest we can get. The "penthouse" on the top floor was even worse. We could not bring ourselves to walk on the carpet it was that dirty and kept shoes/slippers on our feet at all times. The wallpaper was flithly and hanging off. The window was so dirty you could not see out of it and the handle to open and close the window was handing off, the second night it did break and we had to sleep with the window open. The shower/toilet was really small and again the wallpaper was hanging off. The toilet handle was hight above your head was again broken. The smell again was seeping under the door and we tried to spray perfume on the pillows at night to cover the continual smell. There were continuous banging of doors throughtout the night and we really got very little sleep over the 2 nights. I would never suggest to anyone to stay there ever - not unless dramatic changes were made.

title: Just an awful palce top stay
text: From the arrival to a "caged" reception area, to the inadequate 4' bed for two people, the cold shower room, with a broken w.c and a broken cystern handle, just one dull light, the filthy carpet, the night time fight/argument which continued twice for periods of around 45 minute during the night, (and we did not go to bed until 2.30 am) the whole experience reminded us of the "Bates Motel" but worse from Psycho. A truly awful experience. The small car park was full too, My tip is to avoid this awful hotel.

title: Lovely Hotel
text: Me and my boyfriend recently stayed in Cricklewood Lodge for few nights, this hotel is good and the receptionist and an elderly man were so helpful, they give us all the information and direction that we need (like bus and tube) after fill in the form the receptionist show me where my room is and told me about the key for the room, for the front door in case we come back late at night (as the door is locked for security reason), and where's the breakfast room too. We had booked a double ensuite room from their website, and we were very pleased with it, its just exactly same as the photo shown on the web. i think they had been renovated as the carpet were new and clean, and the bed was so confortable, we really had a nice sleep over there. In the morning, we had a lovely english breakfast, the staff were friendly and helpful and the dining room was so beautiful and modern. I think i will visit this hotel again on my next trip, and i would recommend this hotel to friends, this area is very convenience and the transport links are very good too.

title: Avoid - Staff robbed our room
text: AVOID THIS HOTEL LIKE THE PLAGUE. IT IS OLD, DIRTY, SMELLY, RUN DOWN AND THE STAFF ARE THIEVES. My self and my partner stayed in this hotel because it convenient location when we for flat hunting in the area. We found the hotel to be of low standard but were not alarmed as it was CHEAP and suited our budget. However, returning to the hotel after our first days flat hunting we discovered that while our room had been tidied - a spare mobile phone and charger of mine along with my girlfriends purse with drivers license, an old bank cards, sim cards and travel doc's had gone missing from our bags left in the room!! My girlfriends bank later called her to say that the bank card had been tried with wrong PIN twice and the thieves then had the check to call her bank and demand the pin number from them using details from the stolen drivers license!! We confronted the cleaners (also breakfast cooks) the following morning and they flatly denied any wrong doing - with no proof but the fact that our belongings were gone we quietly awaited the end of our stay. AVOID THIS HOTEL LIKE THE PLAGUE. IT IS OLD, DIRTY, SMELLY, RUN DOWN AND THE STAFF ARE THIEVES.

title: Give it a chance
text: We stayed for one night at the Cricklewood Hotel. It was pretty poor from the parking point of view with a very small car park for a thirty roomed hotel. On arrival the reception were very helpful, keys handed over and asked if we needed anything. The room was very basic and the cleaning was still being done even though we did tell them what time we would be arriving. The only downside to the room is that they are not en-suite and we had to walk down a flight of stairs for a shower or the toilet and to be honest they were clean but could do with modernising. There is some storage space but not a lot however we were only there for just one night so didn't take a lot anyway. Our bed was really comfortable and we slept very well to wake up with a quite nice breakfast although a very small dining room, again not big enough for a 30 roomed hotel. I would stay here again but after a good renovation could be a very nice place to stay.

title: Terrible, avoid at all costs!
text: I booked a room in the Cricklewood Lodge for a friend who was staying in London for a few days. I went to pick up the keys for him and was greeted by an incredibly rude man in the reception, which immediately set alarm bells ringing. As soon as I walked I could see the hotel was shabby, and had a dank, horrible atmosphere to it so I asked if I could see the room before paying. The receptionist wasn't too happy about this, and I can see why he didn't want me to see it. The room turned out to be disgustingly dirty, it was smelly, full of ugly, rickety furniture, the bed was really uncomfortable . How could I let my friend stay there? I went back to the reception to let the man know I didn't want the room. He was on the phone for ages and totally ignored me. So I left the key on the counter and walked out. Later on he called me with a torrent of verbal abuse. I had the right to cancel my reservation and I don't feel I should have been subjected to this. Please avoid this hotel.

title: awful time at the Cricklewood
text: Theres nothing good to say about this hotel. It is in desperate need of renovation (it looks nothing like the pictures on the website). Our room (8) was dirty and shabby. The furniture was a mix of rickety old tables and a dirty desk. The tv didnt work properly and there was no remote control. The over bed light was a rusty desk lamp screwed to the wall. The sink in the bedroom was dirty and rusty and covered in fag burns. Our double bed was awful due to the fact it was made up of 2 doors which nicely stuck out from under the mattress! Now for the best bit, the shower room. It was filthy. The toilet would not flush, the bowl was black, as was the floor. The shower was no better, it was covered in mould. You had to lift the whole door up to get it to close ( that is if you were brave enough to get in it ). The window also would not shut and to stop people looking in, it was covered with newspaper. Unfortunately the breakfast wasn`t any better. It was run by 3 girls who could not speak very good english, and they didn`t think twice about arguing in front of the guests. The food was very poor, i could only recommend the toast. Overall i can not give this hotel more than 1 out of 10. Please think carefully before booking a stay at the Cricklewood.

title: nice hotel
text: I have recently stayed at this hotel, I was able to check in late at night, it was no problem, and shown to my room. My partner and I had booked a double room with an ensuite over their website, and I was very pleased with our room. It was spacious and had been renovated, you could tell them carpets and fittings were new. At breakfast we had a huge english breakfast, the dining room was big and modern, and also the staff were friendly. I needed a hairdryer and extra pillows that night, so the night receptionist brought it up, no problems. Overall I would recommend this hotel to any guests coming to london, transport links are very good too.

title: Avoid this hotel at all cost
text: We visited London for 3 days to see my son before moving on to Paris. He found this "little gem" for us and I guess being a backbacker, hostel, budget traveller he felt it was good value and it was definitely close to his flat. We found the family staff disinterested and had no sense of customer service whatsoever. The room we were given was in the basement...well if we had not not been exhausted from our very long day we would have walked right back out. It was grimey, dank and dark. The overall level of the hotel was poor to very poor. We stayed because we were barely in the room other than to sleep and we know it would be over soon. Finally, breakfast (included with the room) was just passable served with the same "I really don't care" level of service we had come to expect. We were supposed to stay on our last night before our flight home but instead stayed at The Crown Morin Hotel just up the street, what luxury!
