title: Great for Fleet Street, Temple, Strand, if a little compact
text: Only a quick stopover to attend a party in the area, but for the price paid this proved a great find, with excellent modern amenities and staff who couldn't have been more helpful. OK, fair to mention the room I had, whilst well put together, was compact and without a window, (other choices available) but was perfect for my needs and great value, compared to better known competitors in the area. Everything worked perfectly, from power points to air conditioning, brand new fittings, great shower, comfy large bed, dimmer switch lighting and an absolutely stunning tv with all Sky channels. Complimentary wine and food (yes really) was a lovely touch specially given it was nearly midnight on a Saturday (!) Superb all round, would definitely stay again if in London but I'd recommend checking room size (and window situation) specially if staying as a couple. Breakfast in Zest cafe adjoining was good as well, a healthy emphasis and again all very well done at a good price.

title: Great value, small but perfectly formed room
text: The rooms are compact. This is made very clear when you book so it shouldn't be a surprise. For a city break when you are out and about all day and evening it's the perfect place to stay. It's great value. The compact rooms don't waste space and they have everything you need. The beds are comfortable. The bed linen is lovely. The towels are huge and fluffy. The shower is great. We did struggle to get the plug to work in the sink, but that was a minor issue. Kettle with tea, coffee and chocolate and a bottle of water. And don't forget the complimentary wine and cheese. The selection of cheeses was much better than we were expecting. It's worth a visit for this alone. Our room was at the back with a view of Temple Church, so no street noise and a window which opened for fresh air was an unexpected benefit as most city centre hotels seem to be sealed boxes relying on air conditioning only.

title: Great London hotel
text: Really enjoyed our stay! Warm welcome, easy check in and out, room small but comfortable, had all the amenities and it was IMMACULATE. Location was ok, we walked to all the London attractions only using the tube to and from Kings Cross. Would highly recommend and would definitely return!

title: Thumbs up
text: We knew that rooms were going to be small, but were still a bit surprised by the size of the one we stayed in. If your tv is about the size of the bed, you know that there's something wrong. Bathroom was clean, sheets were so-so and there were some stains on the wall of which we don't want to know the origin... However, staff is very friendly and helpful and the hotel is located in the middle of Fleet Street so the location is very good. Would we go back? Probably not. But I would recommend it to anyone seeking an affordable, modern hotel in the middle of London.

title: Trust the trip!
text: Teeny tiny room but for one night in the big city it was great. Small but beautifully proportioned the room has all you need for one night and it's spotlessly clean and with complimentary tea, coffe, chocolate and toiletries. But the main attraction is the location. On Fleet street within walking distance Trafalgar Square,it couldn't be better. Would recommend.

title: Excellent business stay in compact room
text: First stay at a Z Hotel, for business on a weekday in the City. Pros: Very comfy bed, big TV, excellent en suite and shower, staff very welcoming and helpful on front desk. My room had a second queen sized bed on a mezzanine over the floor level bed: could be fun for families for a one night novelty. Complementary wine and cheese 6-8pm is a good idea. It's a slightly bigger bedroom than Bloc Hotel, Birmingham - I haven't tried Premier Inn's Hub format yet, but am keen to. Cons: It's not the sort of bedroom you would want to spend much waking time in, particularly if there is more than one of you: if you want that sort of room, book a Premier Inn or other hotel with conventional larger rooms. Breakfast was in a cafe next door (run by Z Hotel) - not as good as PI, but still not bad. I will return for business trips.

title: Incredible small room but really cool !!
text: I booked a room for one night for a business trip and I asked for a no-window room because I was curious. Incredible experience, every single space optimized, nice and modern bathroom, great shower, comfortable bed and pillows, huge HD TV. The queen size bed is perfect for single traveller. The complimentary drinks and the location are an additional value for price. I will be back in the future.

title: Room without room at all
text: We are talking about a clean modern well located hotel BUT there is not room in the bedroom. Seriously claustrophobic. Three sides of the double size bed are against walls. One of which is window, so in desperation you can jump. The bathroom is made of glass walls. It does not have a proper door but one of those rolling doors which never closes. Therefore, the person who is in bed, turns the head to the right and can see you in your intimate moments. Moreover, there is no wardrobe. Do you travel alone? Ok, go for it. Do you travel with someone else? Go somewhere else. Ups! I almost forgot: The entrance to the hotel and its hall smell as if you are in the kitchen of a fast-food restaurant. Sticky. You wear a rain-cover or any kind of protection or your clothes will smell. Anyway, the staff is nice.

title: Perfect
text: First time using this chain of hotels. Amazed how lovely our room was. Compact clean and cozy with everything you would need. Staff exceptionally helpful and friendly. Good location. So many little extras that we would have taken advantage of if we were staying longer. We did receive an upgrade to a queen room, many thanks for that as me and my hubby were celebrating our wedding anniversary. Will definitely be using again when we visit London.

title: Such a tidy and cute place
text: I stayed in the z hotel in fleet street with my mum for three nights and we both really enjoyed it. The area is amazing and so many important sights are in walking distance. The smallest museum - the twinings tea museum with shop - is basically next door. We booked a room "without window" and didn't know what to expect but what we found was particularly cute and comfortable. Our room was tiny and only had a really comfy bed, a small desk, a massive TV and a bathroom. Not having a window wasn't a problem at all because there is a really modern air-conditioning system and light system installed. And when I say tiny, I really mean it

title: Unexpected surprise
text: Booked for one night not expecting much after reading reviews - was pleasantly surprised upon arrival. Rooms were extremely small but modern & clean - enough for one night. Complimentary cheese & wine was a nice touch too - very friendly staff. Would definitely come back again if visiting London again.

title: Clean and compact
text: I recently stayed overnight with friends as we were celebrating a birthday and going to the Tina Turner show which is only a 10 minute walk away. There were 5 of us in total and we had booked 2 family rooms. The beds are like bunk style. The rooms were quite compact and one of the rooms only had a window which you could see out. However they were super modern and clean with lots of towels and shower gel/soap and Coffee/tea facilities. Breakfast wasn’t included but we pre booked for under £10 each and had a small buffet breakfast in the adjoining z cafe. Perfect! We would definitely recommend for a one night stay.

title: A place to lay your head
text: I only bother to review places that I'm prepared to give 5 stars and I hesitated at Z Hotel in Fleet Street because the room was so very small. Too small even to take a photo. But I decided I would and this is why. Pricing is on a par with Travelodge and Premier Inns, but these tend to be in slightly edgier locations, and Z Hotel City really is in a fantastic location - almost right opposite the Courts - and I felt really safe walking there late at night. I would say it is higher spec too. Everything in my room was of reasonable quality, very clean and good condition - the bed was comfortable with a crisp white duvet, it was very quiet and I had a good nights sleep. The frosted glass bathroom cubicle had a good shower and nice towels. There was a tray with brightly coloured mugs, coffee, tea, hot chocolate and a big bottle of water. It had a good TV and is manned 24 hours - there were two friendly people greeting me even though I checked in at 11pm on a Sunday night. Something to be careful of when booking is that I almost booked a room without a window which I would have hated, but fortunately I just realised in time and paid an extra £5 to have a room with a window. I would certainly book here again, but only if I was alone. Unless you are on a really tight budget, when I guess you might accept being cramped and with little privacy for lower cost, I would say the basic double room is too small for two people. Equally you might struggle if you are a big person who likes some space. For just me though, and for one or two nights max as a business traveller more concerned with location and a place to lay your head without paying the earth, it definitely delivered and I enjoyed staying there.

title: Perfect for the price!
text: We paid for a standard double with no window but we’re lucky enough to get a family room with two double beds stacked on top of each other, we didn’t need the extra bed but it was nice. Having sky tv was a really good addition! The room was just big enough for 2 and the shower was great and the room was clean and comfy. Complimentary coffees and tea was fabulous. Really central location and about 7 mins walk from temple, would definitely stay again for the night!

title: Quiet hotel
text: Stayed here for easy access to work while i was away from my normal working office. Room was clean and of a reasonable size, the staff were friendly and helpful by taking my bags to my room. The cafe where you get breakfast was good. There wasn't a huge amount of variety but i managed to always find something i wanted. You don't really here the street noise and there are many pubs and restaurants near by for dinner choices.

title: Compact luxury
text: The only reason I have given this hotel 4 instead of 5 stars is due to the size of the room. The location was superb and considering how central this hotel is, it was incredibly quiet and I had a great night’s sleep! Sky TV was a great bonus as was the complimentary water and hot drinks. The room was spotless and a real luxury to have fluffy towels in the bathroom! By far the nicest hotel I have ever stayed in in London for business. The only downside is the size of the room and if you are claustrophobic this is not the hotel for you. However if you are looking for luxury at a reasonable price and just looking for somewhere to spend a couple of hours at the end of a long day then I thoroughly recommend! The staff were also extremely pleasant at the front desk.

title: Great at what it is
text: Stayed here in April for one night on business and thought it was great. Really cost effective way to stay in the city - right on the Strand/Fleet Street. Rooms really are small - so if you're looking for loads of space then look elsewhere. However, they make this clear from the outset, and the rooms are well equipped - wet room is good (and a nice powerful shower!) - tea, coffee etc - and full Sky TV including BT Sport and Sky Movies. Free internet also although that's pretty standard. One thing the room did lack was a desk - this didn't cause me a massive issue as I just worked on the bed, but worth flagging. For the money though, really really good value!

title: Not quite as cool as Premier Inn Hub
text: This hotel is in a great location on Fleet Street, near the Strand and not far from Covent Garden and Theatreland. It's a very small reception area and unfortunately, the check-in process (if you haven't stayed there before) is a little painful as you're asked to use the ipad to register...zzzz. Once you're in the room though, its very similar to the Premier Inn Hub hotels, just less funky (never through I'd find myself saying that!) The room itself whilst small is well balanced, the bed was comfy and the bathroom was sufficient with plenty of towels provided and everything at your fingertips. The huge TV at the end of the bed was probably a little too close for my liking but you don't have to watch it! The wi-fi is free once you register too. The complimentary cheese and wine downstairs in the adjacent bar area early evening was a nice touch and service was professional London standard.

title: Very small and claustrophobic - no amenities.
text: First and last visit - it tries to be like Citizen M hotels I.e small and chic cubicle rooms, but instead it is more like Stalag 17. I was put down in the basement - claustrophobic and gloomy. Does not have, drawers, wardrobes, Bath, biscuits, iron, laundry, safe, phone etc etc etc - I guess that it’s like ‘doing time’ at Ford Open Prison. All kinds of moaning and groaning from pipes, aircon etc, plus can hear the neighbours movie on their tv. Positives: nice staff, free wine (OK) and cheese (good), good location - these are the only reasons that I could consider giving a second star. I’m typing this at night, hoping that the neighbour’s movie will finish soon and that I might sleep. Torture! A Last Minute secret hotel will usually give you a Grange hotel for £50 less - better/proper hotels in decent locations. Over £200 for room and brekkie - not worth it!

title: Perfect spot
text: Stayed here 27-30 May via a booking.com reservation as it was near to an event I was attending just across the river. Travelled from Cornwall to Paddington, jumped on the Circle line tube to Temple and then a 5 minute walk. Piotr who checked me in was hot! Great smile and great customer service. Swift checkin and up to my room. The room was one without a window but very clean with modern facilities and a huge tv on the wall. For two people sharing it was a little cramped but it was quiet and the aircon is superb and very quiet also. We borrowed an ironing board but had to iron clothes out in the corridor! Very limited hanging space in the room. No room service but tea/coffee and a kettle available and Ye Olde Cock Tavern next door serves food up to 11pm. I would absolutely stay here again.

title: The Z Hotel City of London
text: Overall our stay at the Z hotel in the city of London was great. The rooms were clean and the staff was very friendly. When we arrived and checked in we were just in time for their wine and cheese "happy hour" which was amazing. Basically all you could drink for 3 hours with a selection of cheeses and chocolates. Be warned though- the rooms are tiny!!!!!!! They are very nice but very small which made our stay (with my husbands parents) a little awkward and required some time management between couples. I would recommend staying here again as long as you are with people that you are fully comfortable being very close with or as long as its just one couple in a room. The most surprising was the see through bathroom and shower- no privacy there and full view for anyone else in the room. The beds were very comfortable as well. The hotel was about a 10-15 min walk to the major sites and very close to the Thames river. We did a pub crawl one night and walked the whole time so it was a great location. Highly recommend!

title: Smallest Rooms Ever
text: As a traveller who has visited more than 60 countries, I have stayed in many hotels. The Z Hotel wins the award for the smallest rooms I have ever seen. A queen room had a small corridor, the width of the door and perhaps 2 meters in length, leading to the bed, which was effectively taking up the only other space in the room (apart from the bathroom). We had to crawl into bed via the only access point... about 1 meter wide. Breakfast was good, location was good, cheese and wine was nice. It's a shame the rooms are so tiny.

title: Night out in London crash pad
text: Great value. Clean and modern. Cost was good considering in the centre of London and it was 20th Dec. Our room was on the ground floor. Large with a walk in shower. Water pipe were a little noisy but all in all a bargain. Go for it.

title: Modern, Great Location, Clever Design
text: My partner and i travelled here as part of a birthday/anniversary trip to London. I Can honestly say after planning this trip and constantly scanning for hotel deals this was by far the best for the price. In central London, two seconds from temple station and a stones throw away from St Pauls. Definitely great value for money! Our Hotel room was immaculate, cosy and modern. We had a double room with a window, yes it is small but if you're only sleeping in it, you don't miss the extra space.. It does take you back a bit but once you're used to it, you forget about the size. The design of the room is well thought through for space and storage, even down to the lighting which gave the room a really comfortable feel. The shower was huge and could easily fit two people in. The room is a really clever design! We loved it. I would say this type of hotel is great for a weekend in the city or a couple of nights away? Anything longer would desire a bigger bedroom. The staff were really lovely and even gave us complimentary chocolates for our anniversary, we had no problems with this hotel and will definitely be back again. Loved it!

title: Late Valentines
text: The hotel was what we expected and more, the staff were really friendly and helpful. We had complimentary wine on arrival for our late Valentine's celebrations. Also as we entered in our room there was a box of chocolates from the hotel staff left on the bed for us.. I agree when people say the rooms are small which they are, but me and my boyfriend are small anyways so we fit in well lol. I do recommend this hotel 😊😊

title: Bijou but managed to fit everything in
text: So I knew when I booked that this was going to be a really small room - the website doesn't try and hide the fact. Even so, when I opened the door to my bedroom, I actually burst out laughing at how tiny it was. Having said that, it was absolutely fine for one person for one night and I would stay there again, but I think a couple with any amount of luggage would really struggle. There were lots of plus points to this hotel. The reception staff were friendly and welcoming

title: Compact but adequate
text: Z Hotels are consistent, good locations, exceptionally clean, well presented, functional but rooms are compact - no room for extras - glad i was a solo traveller in a double room. Had a drink in the bar and prices were reasonable for a central London hotel. Will use this chain again.

title: Pretty, affortable stay!
text: Me and my mother stayed here for the 1 night as we were seeing a show in the West End. This hotel was well within walking distance and also a 10 min short walk to Covent Garden. The staff were exceptionally friendly and very welcoming. Rooms were a bit on the small side. But fine as we were basically only sleeping in it. Lovely comfortable bed and TV came with Sky. Comes with tea/coffee facilities. Amazing complementary cheese and wine was served between 5-8pm. Overall a lovely stay. Right in the heart of the city and very affordable.

title: Brilliant!
text: We decided on a last minute weekend in London, we didn't have plans to spend much time in the room, we simply wanted somewhere to wash and put our head down. The room was air conditioned which was heavenly after a long day exploring. It was spotlessly clean, facilities were great and the bed was extremely comfortable. A couple of small points which I don't expect the hotel can actually do much about, so more for guest awareness

title: Mixed feelings but great location and clean modern room
text: We had a negative start to our stay here as we had booked via Priceline (which in turn went through Agoda in this case) and had thought based on our booking that we were booking a queen room with a window (we had triple-checked this at the time of booking as we knew we did not want an inside queen). However, we were told at check-in that we were getting an inside queen (i.e., queen with no window), despite the fact that even our email confirmation stated "queen room" (not inside queen) and that we had been led to believe that we had booked a queen room with window. We were not happy with the way that the guy checking us in handled the whole issue, but in the end paid an extra 20 pounds for the two night's of our stay to ensure we got a queen room with a window. The extra kicker was that the guy checking us in then said he was giving us a room with a great view (which, honestly, we didn't care one way or the other about, we just wanted a window), and when we went to the room, we found there was not in fact a great view at all. We just laughed about it. It didn't give us a lot of confidence or respect for the staff there though. The room itself was nice - small, but not as small as we thought it might be based on the other reviews here - and very modern and clean and functional. Bed was very comfortable. As others have noted, it's a little awkward with the toilet area having only frosted glass and being so close to the bed, where you can essentially hear and see everything going on when someone's in there, but if you don't get stressed about those things, as we don't, it's not a big deal. Location of the hotel is great - walking distance to many attractions, and close to two tube stops as well (note that the Temple station that is listed on the hotel website as being the stop to get off at, we found to be sometimes closed, so we tended to use the Blackfriars stop instead). The hotel is surrounded by lots of small eateries and pubs. Overall, the stay was nice, we would just advise if you book through Priceline or Agoda to screencap any web pages that indicate the room type. Not sure if we'd stay here again just based on our experience with staff at check-in.

title: Gem
text: Excellent hotel on Fleet St close to everything. Small but comfortable rooms ideal for 1 or 2 nights. Staff are always helpful and cheerful. Excellent choice of breakfast. Free cheese and wine from 5pm - 8pm for residents. Will stay again

title: Superb rooms, very well-situated
text: Everything about this hotel is perfect. I was there for work, so didn

title: Small and almost perfectly formed
text: It was a bit of a surprise how small the rooms are but to be candid that's not a big problem for an overnight stay. Only gripe was that the air conditioning refused point blank to function. Breakfast was a highlight. Freshly cooked, healthy and filling. Would definitely stay again if only one night is required.

title: Book now- fantastic!
text: I booked this fir two nights- £60 Per night for a double with a window. I arrived and was told I'd been upgraded and I was welcome to have complimentary cheese and wine between 5-8pm every night. The staff were warm and friendly. Arrived in the room- compact but everything you need- fantastic shower and shower room, really confirms this bed with a huge tv at the end of it showing sky.... Cannot recommend highly enough- central location was awesome.... fabulous! Will book again if in London without hesitation

title: A tiny expensive box.
text: These rooms are tiny, but well equipped, very smartly laid out rooms. However, I do have to say that you can get hotel room within the 3 zones in London (a weekly pass on the tube/bus to those zones is round 30£) OR a great private AirBnB--for round the same money--AND you won't feel like you're living in a very clean tomb. Also, the staff is great.

title: Very impressed
text: We were not expecting much as this is not a pricey hotel and is obviously small and meant for shorter trips. Traveled with a friend and reserved two rooms, the staff was great, very friendly and accommodating. The rooms are very small but this is be expected when reserving single rooms. Both of our rooms were very clean, well decorated, cozy and considering the small space were laid out quite well, plenty of storage and hanging space. We only stayed 3 nights so for short trips and traveling solo I would definitely recommend this hotel. The location was perfect and very accessible to all of the great sites in London. I will absolutely stay here again and have zero complaints.

title: Highly recommended for a night or two in the city!
text: A friend and I booked a room at the Z Hotel on Fleet Street for one night in February. We were going to a gig and out for drinks in Central London afterwards, and this was a perfect location for us while in town. The room itself was brilliant and had a great view overlooking Temple Church. A brilliant location and it was great waking up (albeit with a hangover!) to the church bells. The room was compact but had everything you needed, including tea and coffee making facilities, a flatscreen TV and Sky. The bed was comfy and all bedding fresh and new. The only thing I wasn't overly keen on was the toilet/shower pod which had no walls only frosted glass seperating the pod from the room. So when someone is using the shower or the toilet you can see them from the room. I found this a bit of a weird concept, personally I think a bathroom should be more private, but only a small point! We were also delighted with the offer of complimentary cheese and wine in the dining area, which the hotel kindly puts on every night. I thought this may just be a small selection of cheeses and a glass of wine, but to my surprise the cheese was plentiful and so was the wine - we were offered at least three refills - it's a shame we had to leave for the gig we were going to! All in all I cannot fault this hotel - if you're in London for a few days and need somewhere central then this is the place to come. Great value, great rooms and the staff were all very friendly and welcoming. Would stay here again tomorrow!

title: Really lovely visit
text: I was most delighted with my recent stay the Z Hotel City, perfect location for my business needs and very welcoming. On my early arrival I was kindly advised that I had a room upgrade which is always a super nice way to start. My room was beautifully compact and well designed. My allocated room was on the second floor in room 210 which was a double family room - it has really cool bunk beds, however I did sleep on the bottom bunk. The beds were a three quarter bed so lots of room for 1 person, a very neat wet room and a little table with plenty of mugs with tea, coffee and hot chocolate. I arrived at 2.10 and put my bags in the room and went for a walk for a couple of hours - a very wet day to say the least. I arrived back and sat in the cafe to prepare for the following workday, Monday. At 5.00 I was delightfully impressed at the Cheese and wine buffet - it was truly first class quality with incredible cheese, breads, olives, grapes and a selection of wines. Totally enjoyed despite the heavy rain causing a minor disruption (professionally managed to resolve). Lovely cheery staff who are eager to make everyone happy. I will definitely be back and thank you to the Z Hotel City!!

title: Tiny - in a good way
text: This has to be the smallest hotel room I've ever stayed in, and yet that didn't matter. The space was designed to be incredibly functional, so it had a double bed, a small desk, some hanging space, and an en suite shower room, all packed into an area marginally larger than two double beds. Opening the door took up most of the available floor space, but the room was designed that way - and as it was just me and an overnight bag that wasn't a problem. I was more interested in a comfortable bed (yes), clean (yes), reasonably quiet (yes) and location (yes - right on Fleet Street). If you're in town for a short business stay, definitely book it. If you're here for longer on holiday, or travelling as a couple, the room I had might be a challenge, but worth checking whether they have anything bigger available.

title: Mr
text: Stayed for five days with a friend , service was fantastic , cheese and a few glasses of wine daily free was fantastic bonus. Room was very small for two people and not really any privacy, but overall a great stay

title: Fantastic hotel - a great find
text: Just stepping into the lobby I could tell this would be an interesting stay

title: Exactly what was needed.
text: We stayed on Friday for one night on business. We arrived late and the staff on the desk (Anna and Greg) could not have done more for us, thank you! Rooms were great and all you need for a great sleep.

title: Comfy room, efficient and courteous staff
text: Two nights in a family room. Found the room's facilities to be of a high standard and the beds were very comfortable. Was concerned about noise in a city centre location, but as we overslept on the first night then clearly noise was not an issue! Staff were very efficient and courteous. Will definitely use this hotel again.

title: Ideal for discovering London
text: Hotel is very clean, up to date and the staff is very kind. The rooms are very small, when you need a lot of space, this might not be the place of choice. We stayed 4 nights in 2 rooms, that worked perfectly for us. Attached to the hotel you'll find a small shop for healthy breakfast and the hotel invites guest for wine and cheese from 5 to 8pm. The hotel is ideally located. Getting around with a travel pass or a daily Oyster card is very easy. In front of the door, you'll find a bus stop and some 400m you'll find the Temple Underground station. I would recommend this hotel.

title: Fun Stay in London
text: I totally love this hotel! It had good atmosphere, staff was friendly and helpful, rooms a bit small but well designed with place for everything. Rooms were clean, modern, nice. Great location, and breakfast facility on the grown floor.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text: Such a lovely economy hotel, paid £80 for a clean comfortable room with huge bathroom & huge wide screen to with Sky television access to all channels . From 5-8pm all guests are welcome to sample free cheese and wine in the reception bar which was a lovely treat and saved having to get starters for our evening meal. Will defiantly stay here again, great value for money, ideal location, no fuss & great freebies, including breakfast (free toast/muffins/tea & coffee. Staff were lovely & polite

title: A Pleasant Surprise
text: I was one of the rare visitors of this boutique hotel as very few would stay for more than one week. I have chosen this hotel because of the location which was 16 mins walk from my daily destination of meeting which was near St Paul’s Cathedral. My first choice was the nearby Crown Plaza Hotel but Crown was fully booked. Z Hotel turned out to be very suitable for me as the location was perfect for a business cum leisure solo person with restaurants, breakfast take away stores, London tube station, drug store, corner shop, law firm, etc conveniently located nearby. The room was extremely small and tight but clean and perfectly decorated with good quality materials. The air conditioning temperature was accurately adjustable individually within the room. The hotel provided a free 5 to 7pm unlimited wine and cheese for its customers. The smoked cheese was delicious. For me, serving the same five types of cheese every day was a bit tough to adjust. The Riesling wine served was very smooth and blended well with the cheese. I will not rule out to stay in this hotel again for my next solo visit to the City of London.

title: Well designed, compact and comfortable
text: The cost of my single room was £110 for the night including breakfast. Given the incredibly central location, I felt this was very reasonable. The room was extremely clean and quiet, with a comfortable bed and nice touches (a bottle of water in the room, some toiletries, etc). It was incredibly small but absolutely fine for what I needed (and was advertised as such), and had effective air con. Customer service was very good, and I was given a complimentary glass of wine which was an unexpected bonus! They were happy to store my suitcase for the day once I'd checked out, too. The breakfast was fine - quite tasty scrambled eggs - though I hadn't realised it was essentially in a cafe that's open to the public, which meant it was rather busy. I would definitely stay there again if I needed to be in that location and it was still the best deal on offer at the time.

title: Snug but groovy !
text: Stayed here for JUST one night at the end of a trip, and loved it.. VERY compact rooms, so pack light !, but once you're in the groove of the small design, you'll love it. There are rooms without a window, but that could be very claustrophobic, so suggest opting for a windowed room. covent garden is about 15 mins walk, and on a weekend, you'll feel that its a bit quiet here, but dont worry about that, just wear comfy shoes.

title: Annual London theatre weekend
text: Booked Z Hotel not expecting much as we had booked on price. First location was perfect for walking to theatres, Adelphi, theatre royal etc. Next we checked in an hour early and staff were really friendly and helpful - not the falling over you friendliness you often see. It was a genuine warmth that they wanted you to to enjoy your stay. The room. Yes it was very small but it had everything you need for a couple of nights stay. The biggest positive is that everything is spotlessly clean. Not even dust in the unreachable corners. Shower powerful with lots of hot water. For once I can think of nothing to complain about.

title: Excellent Stay.
text: My Wife and I stayed here for 2 nights room 125,We were greeted by a Staff member named Pioter with a smile and very professional,he explained to us all the rules of the hotel in a polite and professional manner,We were then showed to our room by a young lady who was again polite and professional.. The hotel was remarkably clean and has everything you need.. No fault found,the room was serviced while we were out,fresh towels and fresh linen.. I do highly recommend Z hotel and will definitely be back. Thank you for making our stay comfortable and especially to my wife who had a broken foot. Keep up the good work. Room 125.

title: Overall just what I needed ...Great location Great place to stay
text: This hotel is almost opposite the famous Courts of Justice . The hotel is modern and extremely well situated .The staff are most welcoming extremely professional courteous helpful and friendly . The rooms are serviced daily to a standard that one cannot fault, Couple this with great free internet connection, air conditioning multi channel smart TV in the room and superb breakfast ( to mention just some of the attributes) and I can only suggest why would you consider staying anywhere else . I booked for 5 nights and have slept very well indeed (queen room with windows) I have no hesitation in making this my preferred choice next time I am working in the capital The rooms are not huge neither is the cost you pay ... but you are in a prime area of central londo

title: One night stay
text: Stayed overnight for business reasons. My room was compact but comfortable. Great facilities including a wide range of teas & coffees, water, smart TV & hairdryer. Was welcomed with a glass of wine which is always good in my book! Great night's sleep with minimum noise. Will stay again. Thank you.

title: New Hotel - Lovely Staff
text: I managed to get a good deal at Z Hotel's new branch in Fleet Street. The location was great for me and I was pleased with the price (£130) although sad that breakfast wasn't included. I expected the standard to be similar to Premier Hub Hotels or perhaps even up to CitizenM standards. I felt a bit disappointed. The hotel is located by Ye Old Cock Inn just about opposite the Royal Courts of Justice. You enter the hotel up a corridor to a reception desk in an alcove. This space saving entrance would be typical of my experience of the hotel - this is not a place to find wide expansive rooms and the luxury of open space. The reception was warm and friendly, if a bit overbearing. I was given a room on the first floor and invited to pay for breakfast in advance - £9.50 - as opposed to £12 on the day. More about breakfast later. The room turned out to have the feeling of a conservatory bolted onto the building - lots of windows overlooking the back of office buildings (see photo). Nice but because of the overlook, I tended to have the blinds down. There is an annoying skylight covered by a white blind but this lets lots of day light in early in the morning - waking up to bright white light above you... The room was small and tiled with slippy laminate flooring. But it was OK - good bed, swish shower, everything you really need in a room as long as you are OK to wend and weave your way around the tight corners and make sure you don't bash yourself on the TV or other fittings. There was nowhere to put any clothes of course or to rest the suitcase while I was unpacking. There is storage space under the bed. There was a free wine and cheese reception in the cafe at 6-8 - this was OK - nice glass of Malbec and some nice cheeses. A few people in, all very quiet and British, everyone on their phones. I felt it lacked in atmosphere in the small elongated, corridor like cafe. Breakfast was "served" here next morning: cereals, juices, coffee (staff regulated the machine), and then a kind of buffet with cheese, boiled eggs, salmon, ham, mini pastries and white bread which you sliced yourself. OK but compared with other hotels charging the same price, breakfast was pretty lame! Go to CitizenM and get a cooked breakfast for this. Go to Premier and get the same cheaper. Go to many places and get much more for your money! So a good hotel. Nice staff. But I think the pokiness of the room and the lack of space means that this doesn't have the feel of the other new tech hotels which are popping up. And as for the breakfast, I'd recommend going elsewhere - perhaps to the pub next door?

title: Excellent location
text: Hi. Area is convenient for metro and St.Pauls Cathedral. Nice place. Not very big and bathroom is visible through glass frosted doors to the entire room. Lots of pubs with good food and character nearby.

title: Great hotel in the central, but still not too busy area..
text: I booked here by mistake, but ended up very pleased with my "mistake". (I meant to book the Z hotel Soho to be at the same hotel as some colleges, since we were attending the same congress). Comfortable room, very friendly staff and even complementary cheese and wine every afternoon! The price was very satisfactory too.. Absolutely recommended! Supert hotell! Veldig sentralt, men fortsatt fredelig område. Gangavstand til Trafalgar Square og Covent Garden etc og god bussforbindelse til ulike steder + Temple underground station i nærheten.. Fantastisk ost og vin servering hver kveld(!) og kjempehyggelig betjening! Anbefales!!

title: Hotel Z city London
text: Lovely small hotel very well situated for sightseeing and theatres. Rooms minute,but very modern and clean and well stocked. Staff and management outstanding. Would recommend highly if not wanting to spend too much time in a tiny space.

title: Great value hotel for a short stay
text: Arrived at Waterloo and walked to the hotel via the South Bank, visit to the Tate Modern, crossing the Millennium Bridge, taking in St. Paul's and viewing some of the grand old press buildings of Fleet Street. In short, great location. Warm, friendly and helpful welcome from Agnes on arrival who was lovely throughout my visit. Hotel was modern with clean line design. I stayed in a single room on the second floor. You have the option of a lift or a walk up a spiral staircase. As many have noted the room is compact and if you are claustrophobic this is not the hotel for you. However, the room had everything I needed. Space for my bag under the bed. Controllable heating. Toiletries. Comfy bed, flat screen TV. Small desk and stool. No wardrobe rather hooks on a wall with hangers which was perfectly adequate for me and made best use of the space. The shower and loo are screened off by glass panels. Liked the design and the shower was great. Hairdryer provided in room. I took advantage of the cheese and wine (offered between 5 and 8). A welcome and very tasty touch. Again staff very hospitable in the bar/ seating area. Free and strong WiFi throughout hotel. The room was quiet and I slept extremely well. From the hotel, it is only a short walk to the Strand, Drury Lane and Covent Garden but the hotel does have bus and tube links very close by. For an overnight stay I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again especially for the price. Great value.

title: Great value and service
text: Z Hotel has everything you need for a short stay. Small well designed capsule rooms with all amenities you need: quality bed linen and towels, toiletries, hair dryer, sky tv and catch up channels, tea and coffee, black out blinds, all for superb value. Surprise treat was the early evening offering of free cheese and wine in the bar. Will definitely be back.

title: Tiny but perfect!
text: Centrally located hotel with excellent service from the young staffs. Got to London earlier than expected and was able to leave our bags at the front desk before check in. Check in was a breeze and to my temporarily disappointment, the hotel did not grant my special request. However, the next day after housekeeping, my request was granted as shown in the picture below. Me and my partner were ecstatic to be able to have Tim Roth sleep next to us on the bed side. Free wine and cheese tasting was very nice as well. The selection of both wines and cheese were really good. The staff were very professional. Be warned though, the rooms are tiny and may not be ideal for everyone but for me and my partner, it was perfect. Will come back to stay at the Z Hotel again for sure.

title: Weekend away
text: Weekend away for our anniversary. Staff very friendly, welcoming and responsive. Room very clean but very small, I cannot believe the room allocated to us was a double, the ensuite came right against the bed, 2 people could not pass in the small space between the ensuite and table to get to the bed. When in bed had to climb over each other to get out to go to the toilet. No storage other than hanging against the wall. We stayed 3 nights, maybe okay for a one night stay. I did make enquiries at reception but told all rooms were much about the same. We did read they were compact but did t think they meant so small. On the positive it was very conveniently located for many attractions and theatres.

title: different - room without a view
text: easy to book through a booking site. easy to find - 10 minute walk from temple tube station, no big entrance into hotel so could easy be missed, on the opposite side of the road to the courts of justice so when I passed that I just kept an eye on for it. Check in/out ok. The bit I wasn't sure about at check in was that they get you to fill in details on touch screen which also then makes you a member of the Z-Hotels club where they offer you further discount if you book through them direct. Very friendly staff. luggage storage and lift. We booked a room without a window, which doesn't bother me and actually made a change from being woken up with light coming through the window or noise coming from outside the window. Yes the room was compact and bathroom kind of not that private and it was a glass wall, but it was very modern, smart and clean. Bed was really comfy (not too far off Premier Inn standard), large screen TV at end of bed, bed was basically build into a square space so could only get out of it from one side (but not the first hotel I've stayed in like this so didn't bother me as it would others). Good shower.Tea/coffee/bottled water in rooms, no fridge, did provide hair dryer. Didn't hear any noise from corridors. Evenings were 5 until 8pm free wine and cheese for guests staying at hotel ... and good cheeses by the way so I've planned all this into my next trip to London when I take mum. Breakfast was presented in a slightly different style by way of it was more like a café style where you get your breakfast from a counter like you would walking into a regular café ... you order your cooked stuff at the till and take your cool items from the fridges. For what I paid I thought it was good value for money (people seem to get different rates) and as I said I'm already planning to use the hotel again. My sized room was ok for one or two nights stay. Just an added bit .... I would love to see what the other rooms are like because I get the impression from my room that they are trying to utilise every bit of space they can with how the bed was and how they designed the bathroom while making it modern and practical. And they even had umbrella's to take out if it rains - a nice little touch.

title: Great hotel
text: Honestly can't fault this hotel. Stylish, clean & compact. Very friendly & obliging staff. Walking distance to everything or local tube stations. Really nice touch free wine & cheese at 3-5 every day. Enjoyed every minute of my weekend stay. Will be back. Recommend to anyone!

title: Excellent Breckie in cafe Z!
text: Modern with a twist, smiley helpful staff, speedy service and keen prices. Less than £7 for coffee and scrambled eggs with smoked salmon, plus a potato scone for scooping. Rather good! Free wifi from the hotel.

title: A litte Gem...
text: Exceeded all expectations... seriously... I was a bit worried as I had only paid £49 for my nights stay, however I was on business and the photo's looked ok so I went ahead... I was greeted with a beautiful smell when I walked through the door and was immediately greeted at the small yet chic reception by one of the staff, she checked me in efficiently went on to explain that I had just missed the complimentary snacks and wine and although she couldn't do snacks, she asked what wine I would like... she returned with a large glass of white wine for me to take to my room... I was already in shock, never in the UK have I ever been greeted with wine, even in some of the most expensive hotels I have stayed in... So off I totter to my room... Corridors where light and airy and room numbers/directions where clear to follow... I entered the room to find a bijou but ultra modern room which had everything from fluffy towels to Cadburys hot chocolate to drink... or from the beautifully crisp bed linen to the large flat screen TV at the end of the bed with full SkyTV (including sport) or the complimentary toiletries to the Babyliss hairdryer... everything about this hotel impressed me and I would most certainly return - WELL DONE Z Hotels... xxx

title: Small rooms
text: Having read some of the reviews I thought this hotel would be OK as it is fairly close to Covent Garden. I wasn't prepared for how small the rooms actually are. It may be ok if you are fairly young and are used to sleeping in a cupboard but my husband and I are not. We booked a queen room expecting more room but no, the bed was under the window with only one side accessible so one of us had to clamber across to get to the other side. The en suite is part of the room so if you're sharing a room make sure you know them very well! On the positive side, there is free wifi, soft towels, tea and coffee, and the room is clean. I won't be staying there again.

title: Fantastic price for a central hotel
text: We needed a hotel for a single night in London as we were going to a concert and this hotel was a gem of a find! The hotel is about a 5-10 minute walk to Temple underground station and is situated in a really nice part of London. The entrance to the hotel is done really nicely and the staff couldn't have been more welcoming and helpful. I had booked the most basic of rooms but the receptionist confirmed to me that it didn't have a window which didn't bother me at all. She then proceeded to tell me about the wine and cheese offer to guest in the café, which was amazing! The room itself I loved, you could argue it was basic but it had a huge tv with sky, hairdryer, tea and coffee making facilities, air con and a really nice modern bathroom which some top hotels don't offer! The only thing I would say is that the shower area is right next to the bed and although is frosted glass, I'm glad I was staying with my partner as anyone else you'd have to be very familiar with to have a shower :)!! We didn't hear any noise from rooms around us when we got back and slept well, all in all I really cant fault this hotel and would definitely stay here again. Fantastic rooms at a great price and great staff to match, a rarity in some major city hotels these days

title: Incredible value
text: For a place that is pretty much as central to London as you can get I was unsure of what I was getting into at the cost of £85 per night. To be honest I had all the facilities I needed and it was clean. I probably had the best night sleep I have ever had at this hotel as there is no noise between rooms and is air conditioned. Probably not one for a romantic weekend break but I will definitely be using it for all business trips.

title: Great Location, great staff
text: This hotel is in a great location on Fleet Street and we felt happy and safe to be walking about the area. When we arrived the reception staff were very welcoming.Our room was a compact, inside, Queen bed room. It was very clean and amazingly quiet. The bathroom was in a frosted glass box, it had a great shower, complimentary toiletries & white fluffy towels. The bathroom was not very private, fine for a long married couple like us - not sure how it would be for just friends? A cheese and wine complimentary buffet was served in the adjoining cafe each evening. The wine and cheese were excellent and the staff working there were delightful. We had breakfast in the cafe each morning this was also very good. We were only leaving London on the day of our departure at 10 pm, the hotel stored our luggage for us which was very helpful. We will definitely stay in this hotel when we come to London again.

title: Excellent relation between price and quality
text: Simply awesome! Great comunication with tube, train stations, Gatwick and Heathrow Airports. Located in "City of London". Perfect to see the city by walk. Very quiet. Nice staff. I recommend It absolutely!

title: Very good location very small room
text: Quiet and clean and good for a very short stay in the centre of the City. Not great for more than one person - and we had booked an upgraded room so goodness knows how small the standard is. Don't take any luggage other than really small bag! If I was on my own and wanted somewhere in this location where I could get a good night's sleep I would go back but not for anything longer or with anyone else!

title: Business trip in London
text: Attending a 3 day conference at the ExCeL again, but decided to have a hotel closer to heart of the city this time. Location: Near a subway station (Temple Station) and busstop, at walking distance (15 min) from Covent Garden and St Pauls Atmosphere: Modern Rooms: Small, you have to literally live out of your suitcase as there is no wardrobe. Good firm mattress, nice shower, quiet room. Cleanliness: Spotless Staff: Very friendly and helpful Extra's: Complimentary acces to the wine bar next door. Value for money: Fair Conclusion: Nice clean modern hotel with cosy complementary wine bar, nice staff and conveniently located. I would certainly come back

title: Efficient pied a terre in central London
text: Spread out across several properties on the same street, the rooms are v=everything you need as a traveler and nothing more. Minimal, practical and clean. Do not go with five suitcases, though. Ask for a big room, because if not, the small ones are for solo travelers. Great wine treats / happy hour at five in the breakfast room. Very hip and chosen by the Mad Men crowd. Close to public transportation. Walking distance to great Chinese restaurants, Oxford str. Etc.

title: A Gem....
text: Absolutely delighted with our choice of staying at the Z Hotel City.A clean ,comfortable and cosy room ..a location so central that it is in the walking distance to Covent Garden and beyond...a very friendly and welcoming staff..amazing value for money.Would definitely stay there again.

title: Excellent at the introductory price and winning location
text: Spent a weekend visiting London and the sales and the Z Hotel City turned out to be the perfect place to stay - nestled in a quiet part of town at the weekend but right on the edge of the shopping, eating and theatre action. Staff were very friendly, helpful and accommodating and seemed genuinely pleased to have us there. Two of us arrived late and were immediately offered a large glass of red at reception to take the edge off a day's travelling. The room was small (as expected - the concept explains as much) but the bed really comfortable, the bathroom well-designed and there was just enough room for the two of us to move about and stow our shopping. Overall a great experience. Get in there while they still have an introductory price (early 2016). Can't wait to see what the true tariff turns out to be as I'd love to return - and often.

title: Clean, convenient and comfortable to a point
text: Anyone who books here and then moans it is small should really do a bit of research. It is small, the concept is small, the photo shows its small. Family room is really only suitable for kids that are younger- 13 and under I suggest. Beds are comfortable and rooms clean. Due to their size really only suitable for one or two night stays. After two we were glad to be on our way. Free wine and cheese is nice touch for the adults at 5-7pm. Thing letting it down for us, mentioned loads on here is the glass doored bathroom. Kids wouldn't shower because of it and a lot of singing had to take place at other times. Even as a close family- there's a line!! Plus points- great location and decent rates.

title: Good Location, Good Service
text: Adequate space that satisfies all needs. Great location, situated near tram, bus routes, St Pauls cathedral and other tourist spots. Full sky tv bouquet Friendly and warm staff Cafe situated next door Clean, neat and tidy

title: Small but perfectly formed.
text: I may be wrong, but surely the USP of this place is that it's stones throw from everything and the compromise of that is that the rooms are small? I know not, but the rooms are bijou, rather than small. Small feels like an ugly word to describe them. Anyway, the rooms are teeny but very cute and just what you want. When I go to That There London, as we call it in the North, I tend to spend as little time as possibly in the hotel as, well, there are things to do, people to see et cetera et cetera. Cleaned to a very high standard, the rooms are immaculate and we'll formatted. The televisions are rather large, but give one an IMAX experience without having to pay the entrance fee at the Science Museum which is a real boon. The frosted glass I will admit leaves little to the imagination when using the facilities for any extended period of time but with your significant half, such boundaries shouldn't be taboo, surely? My advice: turn the bathroom light out. Your silhouette will no longer be visible, unless you are particularly reflective. A lovely hotel, I would definitely recommend it and we will be staying there again: 7.5% discount for return custom. Thank you Z Hotels, we very much enjoyed our stay.

title: Unique concept which works (almost)
text: Rooms are small - but that's not unusual in London. However the design is such that everything fits and works well, without feeling too cramped. No phone in the room is a mistake - you can't phone down to reception for anything - you have to physically go to reception. Wine and cheese reception each evening is a nice touch for guests. Breakfast is good and not expensive. Good fixtures in room with big screen TV showing sky channels, excellent shower and comfortable bed (standard double though rather than queen or king).

title: Great stay once again at this hotel
text: I use this hotel often when staying in London as it is close to our head office and the prices are reasonable, the staff are so friendly and helpful and its represents great value for money especially with the free cheese and wine included between 5 and 8 pm. Last night Agnes in the cafe area was more then helpful and very chatty. It was interesting speaking with her and she really looked after us. Thank you and will be back :)

title: Awesome
text: Really friendly staff a First time ive had a good nights sleep in a hotel bed Really quiet location Staff were really friendly and accomadating to our every need Recommend u stay here The free wine n cheese every night between 5pm n 8pm was an unexpected bonus

title: Quality micro rooms & great staff
text: If you've never stayed at a hotel micro room - then you need to research thoroughly before booking. Myself, I've stayed in micro rooms at other chain hotels, so upon opening my hotel room door was not a surprise. Unlike a person whom I accidentally overhead at the front desk complaining while I was checking in. These rooms are very small, yet quality, modern, and spotless. If you only need a great, somewhat inexpensive, at a very convenient part of the city - then this nice hotel is worth researching. The staff are super friendly, polite, and responsive to customer's requests. Many frequent bus routes service the hotel every few minutes, within a 1 block walk from the lobby. If you find my review and advice helpful, please click the helpful button below.

title: Small but Effective
text: Booked months in advance and took a punt on this hotel in Fleet St London. Only a doorway with a Z on the column to give you any idea of its location. Room very small (door hit bed when opened and only access to bed from one side as is against the wall) but ensuite even smaller had to open door to dry my back and get dressed. But all this forgotten when you realise just how good the location is. So central to everything and afterall you only want to sleep in your room. Staff friendly and room clean.

title: Was OK
text: Although my second email and it's reminder prior check-in got ignored for some reason, the check-in was smooth and quick. We found 4 of the personal standing behind the very small reception when we arrived, if just one of them had answered our email :) Rooms are tiny but clean. Every day fresh towels are getting exchanged. There's a very good babyliss hair dryer which I appreciated. Rooms where pretty cold at the beginning. It was rainy the first day too so would have appreciated to not come into such a cold room. We where 3 adults, 4 would have been to much. In general: clean and modern furnished. One bed is just next to the toilet and segregated only by a glass door that is not completely closed. This I didn't find convenient at all for any party that's in that room because of potential smell. So we had to coordinate that somehow. We paid extra 80 punds/3people/3days for breakfast, was ok, got scrambled eggs or naan-bacon, porridge or yoghurt, one of them also could be compensated with a croissant and you get a soft and hot drink. Only one girl was confused, thought she brought us twice a croissant while she forgot each time. In the end we didn't have to pay so was ok. Other girls there the next two days where great. In the end the price/service level was OK. Some stuff are helpful and very nice while others are less. One guy almost run into us in front of the hotel, was probably late. But still, we where guests. Not even a sorry. There is no clear mission. Many Spanish speaking stuff there. Neverthenless, rooms were quite cheap for London but Hotel is not that central since we preferred shopping streets such as Regent-, Picadilly-, Oxford- and Bondstreet. I would probably consider this hotel again or check for a more central one at an upcharge. But can recommend this hotel for a short and cheap stay.

title: Prime location and brand new... but tiny rooms!
text: Prime location yet very quiet (10 min walk from St Paul, 15 min from Covent Garden and less than 5 from Temple metro station). The hotel is new (or fully refurbished), very well equipped, space is perfectly optimized. Staff was friendly and professional, very pleasant. I enjoyed the breakfast taken in the bar/restaurant/snack (whatever you call it) next to the hotel (you access it from the hotel, no need to put on your jacket). Rooms in large cities are never big. This hotel comply with the "rule". My room was barely 8m2 which makes the bed touching the shower. Being alone made it very acceptable. Just bear in mind the toilets are also, technically, by the bed (just in case you wish for a bit of intimacy if you travel with your partner...). Also pay attention to the fact some rooms are without windows. You are well informed at the time of the booking. Room for improvement: the breakfast voucher sold at the reception isn't worth it. By taking it you will hardly save a pound from the price tag. And you will only if you take a full breakfast (large yogurt + eggs + coffee + juice). Anything less and the voucher costs you more.

title: Perfect
text: Really impressed with this little hotel, yes the rooms are very small but we knew that on booking , they were pod type rooms, I think this adds to the feel of the hotel , the rooms themselves are still impressive really modern with great decor, reminded me of the rooms On my recent trip to the mgm grand in Vegas. The rooms are spotlessly clean and the beds comfortable. The complimentary cheese and wine was gorgeous, there is no resteraunt but they have an offer with the interlinking cage next door for 10% off we didn't eat here so can't comment on the food here. The location was brilliant just 5 mins walk from temple tube, 10-15 min walk to trafalger square or 5 mins on the 15 bus which stops right outside the hotel. 5 mins walk to the Lyceum theatre and Covent Garden There is a left luggage facility to leave your bags in. All in all we really enjoyed our stay here

title: Great experience and we’ll be back!
text: Me and my friends went to The Hotel Z City for the unlimited cheese and wine the other day and Michał made the whole experience so much fun! Thank you, we’ll be definitely coming back with more friends! :-)

title: Perfect for a couple of nights
text: Clean and compact, serves a purpose. Rooms are small, but value for money. Very close to the Aldwych theatre, so a good choice if staying for one night, and don't want to pay London prices. Free cheese and wine is also a bonus, and friendly staff.

title: Great location and place, but pushing new tinyness frontiers!
text: The absolute smallest room I have ever stayed in! Smaller than I have ever imagined.... However, this is done with great thought as all the pieces and parts interlock, and there are creative ways of dealing with the lack of space. We did not take advantage of the add on breakfast, but when eating at the Z cafe, the food was fresh, delicious, and a little creative. I was asked when booking about windows and did not upgrade to a windowed room. I guess I had never had the experience of staying in a windowless room..... The have a very sophisticated lighting schema that has lots of different levels and moods. However, I DO NOT recommend a windowless room for anyone with jet lag or otherwise sleep-disordered!!

title: Compact
text: Great room clean, but you do need to know your partner well as it has a glass bathroom that does not leave much to the imagination. No wardrobe just somewhere to hang your clothes so if staying don't expect somewhere to hang your clothes for the duration

title: OMG a clean comfortable hotel I can afford in the heart of London
text: I run a charity so when I have to go to meetings in London it's been impossible to find a decent, central hotel that I can afford to stay at. So I either travel home on stupidly late trains or go 40+ mins out of London to stay somewhere affordable. Not any more - this hotel is perfect. Right on Fleet Street, the rooms are very clean with all the comforts I could want (kettle, tea, TV, hairdryer and a great shower). I was lucky to be upgraded to a Queen room which was a good size. Great concept, friendly staff too. Love it - I'll be back.

title: Leanne brogan
text: Me and my son stayed here for two nights last week for the bank holiday and we loved our stay hotel was Spotlessly clean the staff were really helpful and friendly especially zavier he was a life saver! It's in a great location we will definitely be going back soon.

title: Perfect
text: This is the second occasion my wife and I have stayed at the Z Hotel in Fleet Street. It is in a great location within walking distance to most areas of interest in London. The hotel rooms are equipped with all the amenities that you need and the beds are extremely comfortable and the bathroom/shower more than adequate. Some rooms are quite small but at this price you cannot complain. They also have large wall mounted TVs which show ALL Sky programmes. This hotel offers very nice compact rooms in a great location and the service provided by the staff is first class. Perfect for a short break to London.

title: Small but Adequate
text: Right in the thick of it, in the centre of London, on busy Fleet Street. Great for going to the Adelphi Theatre, as just a short walk down the road. Small doorway entrance. Greeted in reception at small checking in desk. We paid for an inward room with no window. Very small - reflected in the price we paid. Air conditioning. Just enough room to get into bed and use the frosted glass en-suite. It was a bit of a squeeze to get ready the next morning. Clean and tidy through out. We paid for the breakfast in the attached café next door. That was good value, which included a cooked breakfast, coffee/tea, yoghurt fruit drink and juice. I would stay again but only for one night at a time.

title: A Brilliant Location
text: This hotel is in a fantastic location to allow for access to the varied attractions in London. It is in a safe area and there are a number of different bus routes that can be accessed directly out side the Hotel. The rooms are small, however I do not stay in a hotel to spent the day in my room, I'm out exploring. The room is a place to sleep. The beds are comfortable, amenities are more than adequate. A word of warning the bathroom in behind frosted glass so if you are sharing with someone you aren't very close to, this isn't a place to share! We enjoyed our stay and would most certainly return here.

title: Just Excellent
text: The location was great, the rooms, although small, were well designed and set up. But more importantly, three nights through a four night stay this week, the customer service has been exceptional. At check in, it was smiley, warm and friendly, and service in the evening was equally so. One massive "gold star" goes to Agnes (spelling probably incorrect), who has the most unusual ability to make people fell comfortable, welcomed, and important. She is someone who any organisation would be both proud and privileged to have working for them. Superstar.

title: Compact but excellent value
text: Yes the rooms are small and i had climb over my husband to go to the toilet as the bed was against the wall. But the room was spotless, staff reslly friendly. And where else can you get a hotel room in london for such a good price and have free muffins for breakfast, fruit and iced tea at the reception desk. And cheese and wine every evening from 5 to 8pm. And right in the heart of the city of london with lots to do. Brilliant!

title: Does what it says on the tin - modern and friendly
text: We stayed overnight here after a theatre visit in London. The staff are very friendly and helpful and the rooms and facilities are modern and chic. Free wine and cheese evening must be taken advantage of! Showers are fantastic and we got a remarkably quiet nights sleep considering the location. Obviously the small rooms are tiny, but you know that upon booking as this is the urbanite feel. Just be aware that there is little left to the imagination when using the facilities in your room if you’re attending with a new partner. 😂

title: Tiny Rooms
text: The Good: The rooms were very clean and decorated in a modern style. The staff was amazing, very warm and welcoming. The internet was fast, and didn't drop. The location was perfect, right in the middle of everything, and close to the river. The towels are perhaps the biggest I have ever seen in a hotel room, and housekeeping was excellent. The Bad: This is a micro-hotel, the rooms are ridiculously tiny. There is no place to put your luggage except on valuable floor space, and if your luggage is bigger than a carry-on bag, you're in trouble. The bathroom and shower are separated by a glass wall, and sliding glass door. The glass is somewhat frosted, but you can still see too much. The door doesn't seal shut, so be prepared to hear things you wish you hadn't. Apparently there is complimentary wine and cheese at a certain time, we weren't offered this on check-in. It took 3 requests on 2 different days to finally get maintenance to fix our broken TV. The "family suite" may work if you have a child under 12, but isn't suitable for anyone over that age.

title: Lovely staff and comfortable room
text: I only spent a night as I traveled for business. I was slightly worried that the booking I had was for a room without window, but it turned out the room was comfortable enough for the type of stay I had and there was everything I needed (towels, hair dryer, Tv, free wifi)... The staff is really welcoming and loved the fact that I was offered free cheese and wine on my arrival, that really made my day and the waiter at the bar was really kind and happy to help on deciding what cheese to eat with what wine. Great location as well and in general a ver good place for a short stay, if you want to stay longer than a day or two I would upgrade to a slightly bigger room.
